She also followed up with Swissport regarding my bag, and informed me as soon as it arrived. The hotel was very nice, and the staff, especially Berit and Celine in the front desk, were very friendly, welcoming, and caring. I enjoyed my stay at this hotel very much and would recommend it to anyone who is visiting the Basel area, but prefers to stay a bit away from the city centre. It is very well connected to Basel by bus, tram or train. It is also next door to Aqua Basilea, a water park, for those who are interested. I have two suggestions for improvement: The day I left, I had ordered a taxi, which arrived several minutes late, after repeated calls from the front desk. What had happened apparently, is that my 7:00 a.m. taxi had arrived on time, but was taken by someone else. Taxi drivers should link the time to the hotel room number and/or the customer name, so this does not happen. Secondly, the taxi driver charged me a flat fee of 50 CHF, without using the meter, stating that it is standard fare from the hotel to Basel downtown. I had no way of confirming, but this was not transparent as it should have been. The hotel should only deal with honest and transparent taxi companies.

author: FunWithDaFam
title: I will stay here again! I loved it.
text: I used Marriott e-certificates to book two rooms for one night (Saturday night) for our family of seven (2 adults and 5 kids) to stay here on our trip up to northern Europe. Check-in was quick and easy - and the staff was very friendly. At check-in, they provided me with a voucher for our family to use at the waterpark next door (I wasn't expecting this - I thought I would still have to pay something to use the waterpark (which would have cost our family about $150); it may have been inlcuded as this was a weekend - or because I have status with Marriott - or maybe every guest gets it - I'm not sure). Whatever the reason, the waterpark was great (it was the highlight of the entire trip for our kids). The rooms themselves were fabulous. We had two connecting rooms; both clean and comfortable. Beds were great! Interenet was fast and I had no issues. Parking was 29 Swiss Francs - and the parking garage was incredible (I'm usually not impressed by parking garages - but this one was great)! We did not eat the hotel restaurant (18 Francs per person for breakfast was a bit steep for us). We opted for some bread/pasteries at the Coop/gas station up the street. The location of the hotel was great for us. It is outside of Basel - so don't expect to be able to walk out of the hotel and see the city. However, the hotel did provide us with free transit passes to use during our stay (the train station is right by the hotel - and it's an easy ride into Basel). Will I stay here again .... hands-down YES. The Marriott Brand has never let us down and it exceeded our expectations once again here in Basel!

author: Holiday-Mum-9
title: Overpriced and disappointing
text: People kept telling us Switzerland is expensive, but this was our last stop in Switzerland and we had found it reasonable until arriving at this hotel. We often stay at Mariotts in the UK and Europe to break up our camping holidays. I booked through Travel Republic and chose this hotel because it was nextdoor to a watermark and the marriot website advertised free entry to guests at a weekend. Disapointment No1. Daughter was given a rubber duck on arrival as a gift, although there was no bath in our room (you can have a bath if you forego cuddles and have a twin-bedded room). We had been travelling around Europe in a campervan for 3 weeks and really wanted a soak. Disappointment No 2. The receptionist informed me that as I had not booked direct with the hotel, I was not entitled to free entry into the aqua baselia but could have discounted entry of 75 chf for three people. (I've always used Travel Republic and this is the first time I've come across this.). Disappointment No 3. The shower is a wet room. The floor was slippy and took ages (and a couple of towels) to dry. Disappointment No 4. The car park is about 35 chf for 24 hours - charged by the hour. However, the beds are comfy and everywhere was very clean. Just not my usual perfect experience at this chain.

author: SwissFrenchBrit
title: A long way to walk ....
text: Let´s be clear .... this hotel is not - despite the name Marriott Basel - in Basel. It´s in Pratteln, which is a fair way out of town. Nevertheless, if you´ve got a car and you´re on a tourism trip rather than working, then this might be for you. However, be aware that there is (with the exception of the swimming pool complex) nothing to see in Pratteln (unless you´re into Ikea-flat pack furniture). Didn´t think so. No mistake: This hotel is only 3 years old (date of writing 2013) and still looks brand new. There is a bar and a restaurant, but I guess is that it´s more for visiting on business, as there are a number of international companies in the near vicinity. The rooms are new, light and nice to be in. Beds are good. Decoration is .... err ... American. Perhaps they should have taken a trip to Ikea. All in all, though a good place to stay, if you need to be here. But be careful if it´s the sights of Basel that interest you.

author: AlisonJCowan
title: Great hotel and make time to visit the Aquabasilica!
text: We arrived early evening, tired, hot and sticky after a long drive from Italy. We felt truly rejuvenated by the time we left, but here is my usual review of good and not so good bits. Here's what we really liked: Plenty of onsite parking under cover or above with easy access from the hotel, new-looking, modern hotel but with homely, sympathetic decor, very friendly and helpful staff (although the hotel was very quiet so they had plenty of time to provide a good service), great, large rooms, free Wifi in the lobby, in-room safe, very pleasant bar and restaurant, with the opportunity to sit outside (just far enough away from the carpark and road), good choice of food for the continental breakfast, with a clear understanding that the hot food 'American breakfast' was extra (but it wasn't clear how much extra), large, firm mattress but soft, plentiful bedding and unusual blinds outside the bedroom window. We also had a problem with our TV, which was fixed within 5 minutes - great service. The hotel appears to be mainly geared towards business travellers, and we noted the first floor with meeting rooms and breakout areas looked very nice. However, the best bit was the Aquabasilica, which came at no extra cost (apart from Spa treatments) on top of the room charge and is accessed from within the hotel. We decided to have an hour or so in there on Saturday morning, but were amazed by its size, the amazing range of wonderfully-heated pools, water jets, outdoor pool, plenty of sunbeds (which looked brand new), and oh happy days, a fantastic range of water slides! We ended up spending much longer there than planned and had a fantastic time. The few not-so-good bits, more like things to be aware of: The changing rooms in the Aquabasilica were pretty much unisex. There were areas identified for men and women, but all in the same area. There wasn't a huge selection in the restaurant for dinner (although the food was great), and parking still cost CH29 for one night! As mentioned, it was not clear how much extra that hot 'American breakfast' cost, although small cards were placed on all breakfast tables to be filled in by guests, clearly stating which breakfast they had paid for. Had we wanted to have a hot breakfast it wasn't clear how much exta a spoonful of bacon and eggs would cost. The blinds in the room were very effective to filter the sun, but the controls were not easily found. A call to Reception revealed they were by the entrance door, which seemed like totally the wrong place for them but finally the room was flooded with light when we worked them out. Overall we arrived tired, hot and a bit fed up after 8 hours in the car, and left the next morning feeling relaxed, chilled and happy. What more can you ask for! We would definitely stay there again and would do everything to make time to visit the Aquabasilica.

author: Stevie390
title: Immaculate but be careful of the expensive extras
text: The Courtyard hotel is in an industrial suburb to the east of Basel. It is part of a complex that includes a waterpark and shops. It was handy as a stopover for me, but I wouldn’t suggest using it for seeing the sights of Basel city. As far as I can tell, there is no direct bus or tram link between the hotel and the city centre. Nevertheless, the Courtyard is a modern and high quality facility. My room was a good size with all amenities provided including coffee, tea, safe, iron, etc. It was spotlessly clean, in super condition and with comfortable and practical furnishings. The bathroom was also a good size with walk-in shower. The hotel offers good quality accommodation for its room rates. However, there are annoying “extras” including CHF29 for overnight car parking and no free internet. Indeed, wifi access to The Cloud costs a crazy CHF7 for 30 minutes, CHF14 for 120 minutes or CHF28 for 24 hours. All these prices seem extortionate. There is a good on-site restaurant that offered well-presented meals and drinks at a good range of prices. Room service is a little inconvenient – there is no in-room menu, but you can go downstairs to the restaurant, make your choice and come down and collect it when ready. If you don’t fancy going up-and-down, it can be delivered for an extra CHF5. The breakfast cost CHF28, so again quite expensive, but was wide-ranging and good quality. The staff were friendly and helpful.

author: petersouth
title: Great hotel, great waterpark, terrible location
text: The Courtyard by Marriott is not located in Basel but in the Pratteln industrial suburb. Upon arrival you are met with a sterile factory-like building, but the moment you enter the lobby you are greeted with the warm and elegant Marriott atmosphere. POSITIVE ASPECTS Arriving by car is easy and the hotel has a large parking lot. The staff is always friendly and helpful, and the rooms have a charming modern elegance. Hotel guests are offered discounted entry to the in-house waterpark Basilea, an amazing complex of pools, waterslides and wellness activities. NEGATIVE ASPECTS Located far out of town in a rather unpleasant industrial area. Arriving on foot is absolutely not recommended. BREAKFAST A large buffet breakfast with hot and cold choices is served in a spacy dining hall. An outdoor terrace is also available during the warmer season. PUBLIC TRANSPORT Reaching the Pratteln station for local trains between Basel and Olten requires a 15 minute walk. Next to the station is a stop for tram line 14 to downtown Basel. IN CONCLUSION Recommended for all kinds of travellers. The hotel is equipped for large tourist groups aswell as for business travellers. Families with small children will appreciate the in-house waterpark Basilea. Arriving by car is strongly recommended!

author: olivercarey
title: no bar, zero service, stony beach and 5 euros to wash clothes!!
text: my partner and I visited Corsica as part of a cruise and were very excited to return. We booked with easyjet to save over £1,000 by travelling with Corsican places, the flight was fine both ways, despite some very relaxed parents, storms, torrential rain and delays. We got a taxi from the airport, priced by the (very corsican) 'tariff' ..£70 euros. The resorts bar was open on our arrival, but only served water, fizzy drinks and martini. We stayed for 2 weeks and only was the bar open another 2 times after this, families with children taking their own water to the pool, no service on the beach at all so be aware. The hotels on a very busy main road which leads to the village with a few bars and restaurants, nothing to warrant dressing up but certainly to warrant euros on drinks, our drinks were the same usually altho the bills would be different each visit, varying up to 10 euros. guess the bill became a popular game! The food was average, amazing moules and generous servings but nothing as nice as the food in the larger towns. The bars are all tatty, except one that had been built during our stay, it faces the beach and was clean and new. The Hotel offers excellent self catering facilties, all cooking equipments, altho the washing mahcine is 5 euros for one wash and another 5 if you require the dryer. no maid service and only one set of towels for 2 weeks, unless you want to buy extra! the complex is very echo-ey, if that makes sense, the French are very quiet, as are we, altho when some noisy people turned up it disturbes eveyone, a lot!!! the bedroom faced the corridor so if anyone walked past the noise is loud, also the bedroom was small and stuffy. Given the choice this is not a good 'resort' to visit, the other towns are more central and busier, the walk along the main road to get anywhere isn't a pleasant one. The butchers was excellent although we were charged £11 euros for a slice of quiche, it was lovely but no way worth that price. The car hire was £400 euros for one week (renault clio) and it is to be returned washed and hoovered, strictly! Restaurants outside the resort were good, some of the loveliest food was at a northern village which name escapes me, but its north west by a large marina. Some beautiful beaches are south of the resort but at least an hours drive, perhaps more, for pure sand beaches. Don't expect smiley service, you won't get it.

author: halenhelen
title: Personal service
text: I have travelled across the world for nice resorts and this is a really special one. Thanks Wilfried and the team for making our honeymoon a really special one. I won’t forget how the staff and even the guests congratulated us - how cute!! The Resort is small enough to provide you with really personal service and special experience. The resort is secluded (but with good WiFi) so be prepared to be disconnected from the world. We took the plane to Congo Town airport and the hotel arranged a pick up (taxi + boat) for us. We are really glad that Wilfried offered us an early check in so we can start enjoying the pool villa earlier. The villa is really comfortable with good shower. Soft drinks in the mini bar are also complimentary. I also glad that there are mosquito spray and coconut oil in the cool to help us stay away from the flies and mosquitos that are unavoidable on such an outlying island surrounded by greeneries. Finally I also want to mention the food which was great! Every lunch/dinner we have 2 main courses to choose from, all of them are surprisingly delicious (I had no expectation on food in resorts given my experience in Bora Bora...). Overall it was a lovely stay. Really glad to meet Wilfried and the team at Tiamo. I wish to go back one day!

author: P3624DPdavidm
title: We had a very nice time here
text: We stayed four nights for a quiet warm weather, warm water break. The place is small, the staff is simply wonderful, all of them. The food was actually remarkable for the small size of the place. The short snorkel trips at high tide (this was late afternoon when we were there) were truly excellent. We have been snorkeling in many place and this was one of the best. It helps that the places to visit are close by, perhaps 10 minutes in a boat. We had a pool villa which was nice, private, but a bit worn. The bed was comfortable. The screened porch was nice. My suggestion to Wilfred, the manager is that the place needs some spending on maintenance. The boat motors need work. The sails on the small boats need replacing. To be fair, they're working on it. The docks are new, for example. Then again they don't claim to be a 5 star place. As a guest experience it is close to perfect. We went in early February and there were only 2 other couples there. I'm sure we will return to Timao. FYI we used Watermaker Air from Fort Lauderdale to get there and it was a very nice way to travel.

author: JackieOdm
title: Tiamo Resort is wonderful!
text: We spent 9 nights at Tiamo Resort and wished we could have stayed another 9 nights! We loved the Resort. The food was excellent....a limited menu but great choices. The chef did a great job and came out to meet us. The staff are excellent.....from Wilfred to Nicolas to Miss Audrey, Miss Pinkie and Miss Koko. All our needs were met. We stayed in Villa 10 and loved it....extra room, 2 bathrooms, large, heated plunge pool and wonderful views of the spectacular sunsets each night. Housekeeping was also good and attentive. The pool was cleaned each day. There was a screened porch and we used it. We also had a very private portion of the lovely beach. We scuba dived with an excellent dive master at the resort. The diving was very good with sharks seen on every dive along with good, recovering coral and a lot of different fish. We are experienced divers and we enjoyed the laid back, easy diving. We each had a massage with Pollyanna who did a great job. We will return!

author: KullyP
title: Exclusive & Luxurious
text: We wanted to end our visit to the Bahamas with a bit of luxury, and chose Tiamo after the reviews. The resort didn't disappoint! We stayed in a Villa- the room was on the smaller side, but with a walk in closet, the room wasn't cluttered with luggage, so it worked. The bathroom, though joint to the room, had it's own entrance. For the first few nights, it took some getting used to leaving the bedroom to use the bathroom- especially in the dark. For the time of year we went, it was extremely quiet, with only 2 other couples at a time, so for the most part, it felt like we had exclusive use- without the price tag! The staff, including the chef, are the an asset to the resort, as they made every effort to ensure we had a wonderful trip. The food was the best we had throughout our Bahamian trip of 2 weeks. In terms of inclusive activities as part of our stay at Tiamo- canoes, fishing, sail boats, scuba diving etc, this was plenty to keep the OH entertained whilst I was happy indulging in books. They have a cute little library/study where you can pick up a read should you get through yours. Ethan, who runs the dive shop, and the various captains were all lovely during our snorkelling trips which go out once a day. As mentioned by previous reviews, the sand flies are a literal pain, and whilst the each room is equipped with repellant and oils, they're a determined bug. This is just part and parcel of nature, so the resort can only do so much. One thing my husband did bring to the managements attention was discolouration of water that came out from our bathroom taps and shower- a little bit concerning, however we were reassured that this was a result of the purification chemicals used. I wouldn't rate this resort below 5 stars- it was a blissful end to what had been a beautiful 2 weeks in the Bahamas

author: ANYCUrbanAngler
title: As Close to Perfect As You Can Get
text: So I never submit reviews of properties because frankly I am lazy and would rather spend my time with other things. However, with all of that said, I find myself writing a review of Tiamo. My wife and I booked this hotel so that I could go fishing while she enjoyed the beach and other non-fishing activities. The resort is an absolute home run. The service, even though it was a little laid back for this New York-er, was great, the food outstanding and the fishing even better. The only issue that we had was with the bugs. Just remember to always spray yourself with bug spray. The room was very comfortable. We chose villa 10, which was the most private and most spacious villa on the property. Also, we asked a lot of the staff with respect to food requests etc, and everyone always accommodated us with everything. We asked for an extra serving of prawns, and we got them. We asked for a fruit and cheese plate for a late night snack, and we got one. We asked for conch to be served at one meal, and what do you know it was on the menu the next day. We told the staff that we loved stone crab, and it was served for lunch the very next day. Even in spite of all of our bug bites, my wife and I are looking forward to going back soon. This is a very special resort.

author: Singerred
title: A beautiful and quiet place to relax!
text: I was here with my family (two teenagers) during the week of Christmas. The first night we stayed in two of the villas, and the rest of our stay was in the Bird's Nest. The villas are terrific. One had a private pool, and each one had two rooms, and two bathrooms. Both villas had a lovely view of the ocean. The Bird's Nest was beautiful and spacious. There is a nice kitchen, but there is nowhere to buy food, and they didn't supply food, so the kitchen was useless to us. The food at the resort was delicious, and the Chef was willing to accommodate some requests. The dining staff was also friendly and attentive. The highlight was Lee and Nic in the dive shop. They really made our trip! They were both very attentive to my teenage children. My son was able to get his PADI certification while we were there. We loved that the resort is small, and luxurious. There was no fight for a chaise lounge, no loud music, no wild parties. It was peaceful and restful, and it was fun talking to the other guests. The only negative was the sand flies. They provide oil and spray, but we were all bitten, and we all reacted to varying degrees. I recommend bringing a lot of antihistamine with you, because you don't know how sensitive you will be to the bites..

author: ReelBuddies
title: Depends what you want
text: Tiamo without doubt may be the most beautiful property on Andros but... If you are coming to Andros purely to fish I would recommend Mangrove Cay Club where we stayed before coming to Tiamo for a few days. If your agenda is a little fishing and a little beaching then Tiamo may be a better option. We thought the accommodations were top notch, I don't understand why some reviewers mention an open air walk to the bathroom...crazy, there is all the privacy you could ever want. The pool outside the room is really nice, good ambience and good fun after a day wading the flats. Yes, the bonefishing wading the flats in front of the lodge was fantastic. My wife and I hiked miles of flats and even found a blue hole we heard about and found after searching on a long hike (had to dive in when we found it!). We were perplexed by some of the small things however such as the old/dirty cushions in the common area of the property...the daily rack rate is such that everything should be in top notch condition. I have to also report that the place was a little up tight. At least for my wife and I we like to yuk it up with the locals when we stay at a place so we can learn about the place. The ownership here kept too tight control of their staff to the point where it was a little bit uncomfortable. The vibe at night didn't fit a high end (fishing) lodge in the Carribean. You can do both high end and a tad Jimmy Buffet...loosen up a little and go see Liz over at Mangrove Cay for some lessons on creating a warm, friendly and inviting atmosphere. The ethos of Tiamo is more European than American if you will. I wanted to jump in the main pool at night during dinner to liven the place up but didn't only because it probable would have made things hard for the local staff who we became friendly with. Would I go back?... Maybe? Would I go back if all I wanted to do was fish..no.

author: julieatallah
title: Perfect isolation in paradise
text: There are few gems like Tiamo in Caribbean, small, private--the perfect getaway for a stressed couple. Island isolation, beauty, and comfort. My husband and I were long overdue for a vacation and searched for a small, completely pampering experience. Tiamo fit the bill with it's small size and location. Only accessibly by boat, you will feel like you're on your own private island. The rooms are well-appointed with soft sheets, comfortable beds. Chef Keith's food is excellent and fresh daily if there's a good catch by the sea fishermen. The service is excellent from the managers, Wilfred and Julien, to the staff people (special thanks to Pinky and Briana)--fun and friendly. They're there if you need them, but will stay out of your way if you need privacy. Casual and quiet, there's no need for fuss at Tiamo. Pack your comfy clothes. Bring swim gear for snorkeling by the blue holes or in the shallow, clear waters right off the beach. While there are plenty of activities to do, we rather enjoyed doing nothing, reading books, listening to the waves, the birds, and general quiet. Do use the bug spray provided, the sand flies are brutal. Our only disappointment was the spa. Service was fine, but really not as top-notch as the rest of the resort. We would have liked that to be a more pampering experience. Overall, we loved Tiamo and will definitely return!

author: tincup305
title: Private Paradise!
text: My family and I just returned from a week stay at Tiamo Resort. I booked this through luxury link which I was a little nervous about as this was the first time I had done that, but everything from the booking to the vacation was seamless. We have traveled extensively esp in the Caribbean, vacationing at between 18-20 different islands, and Tiamo is the most beautiful resort we have visited. We stayed in the Exclusive Pool Villa for some extra privacy. Service was exceptional! Delta lost my luggage on the way down, and when we arrived Julian the manager took the baggage claim information contacted Delta and the bag was on the front porch of our villa before I woke up the next morning. He even opened the gift shop for me upon arrival so I could raid it to get me by. So a big thanks to him! We traveled with our son who is 13, and the staff was very accommodating to him, offering to make him any meal he wanted. Although it wasn't necessary because the food was amazing! They served lobster one night which made our son very happy as that is his favorite food. We were a little nervous since it was all inclusive. We typically don't frequent all inclusive resorts as we are all about luxury and good food, which you do not find at most all inclusives, but Tiamo was five stars all the way from food to service to accommodations. I read the reviews prior to going and packed sunscreen with bug spray so the bugs were not an issue. I know other reviews commented on the cost of alcoholic drinks, and I did not think price was out of line for a resort, not to mention the drinks were amazing. Their mixologists have to be well trained bc we always received a perfectly mixed drink. There were tons of marine activities although we did not take advantage of them it appeared many guests did, and there was always staff on the dock to assist you. We wanted a week break from work, school, sports schedules, etc to relax and spend time as a family and we certainly got to do that. A huge thanks to the entire staff for a great spring break! I hope someday they expand and add two bedroom villas for families.

author: annekey2014
title: paradise island
text: My husband found this place because Andros island is one of the capitals of bone fishing. He caught his biggest bone fish ever and needless to say he was in sevent heaven, which is something only a real fisherman can understand..... I thought theplace was beautiful too. The water is great, and the grounds were beautiful. The food was five star and so was the service. The only reason I could not give this resort a five star overall was because of the bugs. There were these sandflies that were absolutely insatiable. They all seemed to feast on my blood. There was insect repellent available in the bathroom, but I do not like to put that on my skin. there was also 'skin so soft' available, which can work, but is not totally full proof. Infact, by the time I realized how bad it was, it was already too late, and I was covered with bites. My dream of sitting in one of the comfortable lounge chairs under the mangrove trees, overlooking the aqua sea was quickly scattered. I could not really be outside, unless I was on the water. I know that mangament sprays regularly, but it is clearly not enough to keep these little pesks away. Using very strong chemicals is obviously very toxic and not very desirable either, thus, for those who are easy targets for the bugs this is not a great place. It is really too bad, because if it were not for the sand flies I could have easily stayed there for a month. The private villa was charming with its plantation like decor; it had a very comfortbal bed with luxurious bedding and air conditioing; it had a nice little porch and a private pool as well as a great view of the lovely beach. We met the loveliest people among the guests as well as among the friendly and helpful staff. The weather was great and the sunsets were to die for!

author: 563jamess
title: wonderful visit 08/12/13
text: my wife and I had our first visit to Tiamo and found it charming. The "rooms" are individual cabins and while we had a pool cabin with A/C we seldom used the pool or the A/C but I would still recommend both as the pool lit at night is very nice and the A/C is useful for drying both the room and clothes.ful for drying clothes and cooling on hot days. Not enough can be said about the staff. Nothing is too much for them....Audry, Carolyn, Pinkie, and the other ladies will serve your every need with a smile......add to that Lee on the "big" boat and BJ for the "Bone" boat, Allen and his mates for water activities and maintenence, Makia for booking assistance, Keith in the kitchen followed by the ladies ( we ended our stay with TuTu)....all are terrific at their tasks and attentive to every need. Julien oversaw our stay and was also always on hand for a chat or advice. In short, we have visited over the years the Bahamas from Columbus Island to Nassau to Long Is and the Iguanas and Tiamo is best of all in every respect. I enjoy bone fishing and have done so from Christmas Island to Alphonse island and found the bones in the Bight near Tiamo (and indeed on the eastern end of the Tiamo beach walking) to be in the best condition I have ever seen. The ecology of the Bight provides abudant food and a bone the same size as a 3lb bone anywhere else weighs 4lbs at Tiamo or more! They are incredibly strong as a result and don't tire easily. And BJ knows where they are....... One word describes the food: superb!....but you could add imaginitive, varied, perfect proportions, and beautifully presented...... Visitors should realize that you are visiting a tropical enviornment and be prepared for the beasties that will welcome your visit (and your warm blood!).....take some precautionary defensive sprays and something to relieve the effects. A small price to pay for the experience....such as going into the "bush" and visitng with the giant iguanas who share your space!! Tiamo has many repeat visitors and they just got two more!! e. stebbins

author: sunshinegirl1964
title: Wonderful, but a few things you need to know.....
text: We visited Tiamo as a brief get away in August for 6 nights after purchasing on Luxury Link at a discount. The staff at Tiamo are beyond compare, Brenda, Carolann, Kay and all of the behind the scenes people are so friendly and willing to do anything to make your stay more comfortable. The villa was lovely and extremely clean but be prepared that the bathroom/shower area is outside of the bedroom with the airconditioning. It was a horrible experience in August with the heat and humidity. May not be such a bad problem in the cooler months but the humidity was so bad that several mornings, the mirror was so clouded with condensation you couldn't see into it. We LOVED having the private pool but as we were the only ones on the beach, we didn't have neighbors. I am sure when the resort is full, I wouldn't have enjoyed the proximity of the neighbors with either the bathroom situation, or the pool. Dining was wonderful and every meal was a treat! Drinks, however, are not included in the room rate and in my opinion were very overpriced. $17 for a cocktail, $7 for a beer. I realize costs are high in the outer islands but this seemed a little much. Activities were also very expensive. The beach is not perfect and to go to another area on the West side of the island was $650 minimum, again, I realize how costly gas is but seems very pricey and wish I would have known these prices before booking. There were no daily "activities" as is advertised on the Tiamo Website. I don't know if this was because of the low season, low # of guests or just because we didn't really inquire. The french family that were at the resort at the same time seemed a bit dismayed at the lack of offered, included activities. It is a lovely resort but you definitely need to have an idea of the actual costs of the things not included. For us, a bit expensive for what we experienced. And definitely keep in mind, the open air bathroom situation, it was a bit too open for a conservative, mid-western lady.

author: beachbum555
title: Isn't it great when the stars align?
text: My hubby and I like to fish the flats. And eat like royalty. And dive/snorkel. We appreciate attentive service, especially when it's warm and genuine. If lots of people go there, then we don't. So I told him staying married 20 years was worth a special trip that included all these things, and apparently when you google luxury and flats fishing, you get Tiamo! Everything that we look for in a vacation is here. Even better, the kind of travelers that like to get off the beaten path were here. Liberal, conservative, city, country, sailor, fisher, didn't matter. It was a blast to hang out with some of the most interesting and entertaining folks a person could ever want to know. Staff is gracious, anticipating every need or want. Food is off the charts good. Beautifully presented, fresh ingredients, fantastic sauces. Far exceeded my expectations. Can't wait to go back!

author: AlistairC727
title: Relaxed elegance
text: I was referred to Tiamo by my fly fishing outfitter. Because of its unique location in S. Andros Tiamo has pole position access to some of the most iconic bonefish flats in the world. Tiamo set me up with phenomenal guide Cpn Marvin Miller. The bone fishing did not disappoint, even tho I was fishing in the Aug low season at times the flat was a traffic jam of bones. On one day I had caught 10+ bones and then stopped counting. Also these are Androvian bones and on average the biggest bones in all the destinations I have fished. My GF accompanied me on the trip and she is an underwater photographer. There are a myriad of blue holes to dive, and Tiamo have a great boat and dive staff. She was the only diver that week so she was treated like a princess. Now for the resort. The pricing may seem on the high side but this is easily a 5 star resort with a European dynamic. Makia took care of all bookings and transfers with efficiency and seamless service. The accommodations are impeccable. But the hi light folks is the FOOD. Chef Keith's food was exemplary, every meal was simply superb. So much so my GF took a cooking lesson with Keith..he is a master Chef. Wilfried the GM brings a Paris flair to the property which is uniquely refreshing. We shall return.

author: thezaz
title: Peaceful and remote but expected more for the money
text: We took a weekend 'getaway' to Tiamo because it was remote and we were looking for a peaceful and romantic location. It was remote (we took the WesternAir flight from nassau to get there) and quiet in that very few guests were there when we were, but they were doing construction during our visit (which they did not tell us about) so we did have to listen to the sound of construction throughout the day instead of the sound of waves on the shore. The location is generally very beautiful with great snorkeling that's easy to get to. We didn't fish but lots of other guests enjoyed the fishing and had good success. The staff is real friendly (Colyn, the manager and 'Sam' the bartender are especially fantastic) and they seemed eager to make us happy. The atmosphere was relaxed and the food was probably the best resort food we're ever had. The cottages were charming and we generally enjoyed our time there. There are a few things though, that Tiamo could do to align the experience with the price tag. First, due to a design flaw, the bathrooms flood terribly when you shower and remain soaked until the room is serviced. If they were to put a small ledge between the shower and the toilet, it would contain the flooding. OR if they provided a long squeegee in the bathroom, guests could manage the flooding on their own after their showers. Secondly, they told us that they were going to refresh our room refrigerator daily - including the milk . Though during our stay, they never did that and the milk in our refrigerator just got more and more rancid over the course of 4 days. I'm sure they would have refreshed it if we had asked, but there's no way to ask them without going up to the club house and we never remembered to ask when we went up there for dinner. The 'spa' is nothing more than a single small room and the massage I received was not very good. They advertise their 'walking trails' as one of the resort features but they are so overgrown as to be barely passable (and you have to walk past the resort garbage dump on your way to 'nature'). We enjoyed the non-motorized water sports but it was hard to get any assistance with them since it was frequently difficult to find any staff around. So yes, romantic and charming with a lovely staff and we did have a nice time. But we also found it expensive for the experience and we feel that with a little bit of effort, they could make it more worthy of the price tag.

author: jmcvey13
title: Tiamo hits it right on
text: My wife and I had the distinct pleasure of having 5 days at Tiamo over the last days of June through July 4th. When we booked the trip we had reservations about traveling to Andros in July. Boy were we wrong. We arrived the first day and were the only guest but were made to feel right at home as Moraq and Matt layed out the red carpet. Over the next 4 night there were two other couple that were both pleasant and entertaining. Over the 5 nights, I am not sure which meal I enjoyed the most, because the chef made each one a total delight. Meals ranged from, lamb, duck, fresh tuna fresh snapper and his chilled soups were off the charts. All in all I felt like I was in a 5 star dining experience from the beginning. As far as the activities at Tiamo: I really like to fish and have a hard time siting still. My wife on the other hand is active but doesn't mind sitting on the beach and relaxing. Tiamo was a perfect compliment of both. I spent 3 half days with guides bonefishing and the rest of the time catching fish from the shore. I will report that my wife did catch a bigger fish than I did, I believe it was a 7 pound bonefish. When they tell you that there are fish right there, believe them as it was a very common event to see tailing fish daily during high tides. We also snorkeled, kayaked and fish for tuna with the owner one day. The accomodations very delightful, with well decorated rooms and some of the most comfortable beds we have sleeped in. When we left on the Sea Plane from Safari Sea Planes, my wife tapped me on the shoulder and didn't asked but demanded that we come back. Rest assure we will.

author: laxmigoddess12
title: pinch me, I'm in heaven
text: If you are looking for a superior 5 star resort without the crowds and noise, this is your spot. We stayed for 3 days, piggybacking this getaway with a business trip in Nassau. Even though the stay was short, it took me no time at all to completely relax and forget about the outside world. The setting is private and everything and more that one could hope to find in the Bahamas. The only way to arrive is by boat and from the time you are met at the dock to when you depart; every detail is looked after by the capable and friendly staff. Matt and Morag, the management team, are professional and friendly. We were lucky enough to be there when the owners were present which was a bonus as well. The food rivals that of fine dining in any city. Hats off to Chef Keith. We had notified the resort that one of us is a strict vegetarian and at every meal there were delicious vegetarian options. Snorkeling in one of the area's blue holes was a highlight. The beach is clean, white sand and the water very calm due to the Bight. Alex, the Nature Concierge, was knowledgable and planned activities based on guest's interests. A big plus is that there is a wonderful spa so if one person wants to be out bonefishing or deep sea fishing for the day, there are always spa treatments, diving, snorkeling, kayaking or nature activities to choose from. Captain DJ took me on a boat tour around one side of the island and pointed out several private beaches that could be visited and noted that the resort would pack a picnic lunch to bring if so desired. I was perfectly happy dividing my time between the infinity pool and the beach with a massage or two thrown in for good measure. The cottages provide privacy and are beautifully appointed. The top quality mattresses and bedding were much appreciated at the end of the day. Given the intimacy of the resort, I could envision reserving the entire resort for exclusive use such as a wedding or private group getaway. We will be back!

author: Kathy1053
title: Wow. Our Private Paradise!
text: This resort is on a remote section of Andros, Bahamas. Accessible only by boat or seaplane, it's a perfect private getaway. With only 10 bungalows, it's very quiet and that's a good thing. No other resorts are in the area. Boat traffic is limited to only those that come to the resort and your personal fishing guides. No jet skiis and speed boats mean that time on the beach is for peace and quiet and listening to nature and the small waves lapping on the shore. The minute we arrived we were met by a friendly face. Staff remembered all our preferences. The manager and Ellie, the owner, met us at the end of each day and were attentive to our needs and loved to hear about our day's adventures. They made it our home away from home. The food was wonderful. Being that it's your only option considering you would have to take a boat back to town for something else, we were nervous about what we would encounter. The chef did a fantastic job and coming from New York with our many 4 star restaurants, we are a tough crowd to please. We were there for an after Christmas vacation with our teenage kids. The hotel arranged many private excursions for us and at our leisure. Scuba, fishing and island exploration. The water is crystal clear and the beach sand very white. We were there for New Years and the hotel brought in a live band. Considering that at most they have 20 guests in house, that was a wonderful and quite unexpected treat!. I would recommend this resort highly for anyone wanting a private getaway with wonderful food, staff and accommodations.

author: ERM24
title: A little slice of paradise
text: This was my first trip to the Bahamas and I was NOT disappointed! From the moment of arrival, I was struck with the beauty and tranquility of the resort. This was particularly highlighted with the attention to detail from the guest boat pick up which saw my partner and I arriving in just as the sun was setting. Visually it exceeded all my expectations! We were staying in one of the 'Breeze Cottages'. From the intimate setting of the cottage set slightly back from the beach among the tress this truly felt like we were on our own little Island. Having never been fishing before, I was keen to give it a go, particularly as my boyfriend was an experienced fisherman. There was ample opportunity to not only go out deep sea fishing but also to have one of the boat men take you out and show you the best bone fishing spots. We never wanted for any equipment, advice or technique tips from the staff. I found this very useful as I was able to have a casting lesson off the jetty prior to our trip. It was this attention to detail and pre-empting any expectation/help that the guest might need that left me feeling like nothing was too much for the staff which I have never experienced at any other resort. Little can be said about the menu without singing its praises. The food was of the highest quality, with a wide and varied menu choice throughout our entire stay. I particularly loved the fact that the red snapper I caught the morning of our fishing trip was then used on the menu that evening. This was truly fantastic!! There was never a moment when I was idle while at Tiamo, unless it was by choice preferring to catch up on some reading that day while taking in the view looking out onto the sea from one of the beach loungers. From the moment we arrived, the staff and owners were nothing short of fantastic! I can't think of Tiamo without a smile spreading across my face. Truly one of the best Christmases I have ever had and I have been singing its praises ever since!

author: runningmomma
title: The BEST trip you will EVER take....unplug, relax and just be!
text: WE can't say enough about Tiamo. This was the most amazing trip that my husband and I have ever taken...and we've been to some great places! We need a quick get-a-way from the kids and my husband loves to bonefish. So, in searching the internet, I found Tiamo. Didn't really know what to expect, but the pictures looked nice, so we booked our four days and were NOT disappointed. Bill has the most fantastic staff....courteous, friendly and extremely attentive. Our bungalow was beautiful! My favorite part was the "outside" shower....hearing the birds, frogs, etc was simply amazing! It was the end of season (they close up for the main part of hurricane season) and we were one of the last guests to enjoy this hidden gem! We even had the place to ourselves for two of the four days.....can you say heaven??? Don't come here expecting some ritzy, hoity-toity resort...it is anything but that! There's lots to do outdoors....catch bonefish from the beach (my husband was in heaven), snorkel the blue holes (crazy amounts of fish, even on a windy day!), find beautiful red starfish two feet in diameter (just off the beach), dive the reefs, relax in the negative edge pool, or just BE under the lush palms on your own cushy teak lounge chair. With no clocks (there's a really small one next to the bed), no phones (no cell service...love it!) and no real TV (there's a flat screen in the library, but who needs that???) you feel a million miles away from anything!!! We didn't even see another boat on the water while we were there! It is understated luxury at it's best. Keith, the chef, is a culinary genius!! Let's just say our stay started with lobster eggs benedict when we arrived on the docks at Tiamo....need I say more??? It just got better from there! They'll accomodate any requests you have, but trust me, the menu has NO flaws! We are already planning our return to paradise next April....this will be a trip we take for many years to come!!!

author: hb212
title: The perfect honeymoon!
text: When we were planning our honeymoon, we had a fairly strong sense of what we were looking for -- since, after all, this was a once-in-a-lifetime occasion. Our list included a pristine beach, luxurious amenities, sophisticated food, and complete privacy: no kids, no gimmicky restaurants, no touristy bars. Tiamo, a hidden gem in the rather unlikely venue of the Bahamas, turned out to be the answer. It was slightly complicated to get there (though probably no more so than getting to any other Caribbean island that's worth seeing). Flying to Nassau, which is a straight shot from New York, was easy enough -- but the resort itself is accessible only by taking a 15 minute puddle-jumper, which departs once a day. An easier, though more expensive option, is flying into Fort Lauderdale, and then booking an hour-long flight on a private airline; this way, you won't end up losing a day to travel. And when you do arrive, it's all worth it. The natural beauty is breathtaking -- white sand, clear green water, a tangle of nature trails, and no commercial buildup anywhere (the resort is accessible only by boat). Many of our photos resembled screensavers, and the beach reminded us of some we've seen in Thailand (which, in our opinion, are some of the most beautiful in the world). The setting is perfectly complemented by the relaxed but ultra-sophisticated decor of the hotel: sky-blue cushions on elegant wooden beach beds, flowing white drapes, matte tiles, ceiling fans, and a shimmering, mother-of-pearl hanging sculpture above the communal bar. We also loved the food (included in the price of admission), which far surpassed any we've had in the Caribbean: an important feature at a resort where there are no other options for dining out. The chef prepared a series of inventive dishes that were varied, reflective of the local culture, and served in such reasonable portions that no matter how much we ate, we never felt stuffed. The meals, served beachside, were one of the highlights of our trip. We also enjoyed the pace of daily life at Tiamo. While I lounged by the infinity pool or had a dreamy massage at the small, jewel-like spa, my husband enjoyed the sailing, fishing and snorkeling activities, often led by the hotel's genial owner (who is an accomplished deep sea fisherman in his own right). There's also a state-of-the-art fitness center with a view of the water (though I, sadly, did not partake). But what appealed to us most of all about this hotel was the scale: intimate, elegant, and a far cry from the monolithic corporate feel of many luxury beach resorts. Our cottage -- one of only ten, which comprised the total room count -- featured white wooden beams, a private beach, a screened-in porch, and an indoor/outdoor shower (though, unfortunately, no internet access). The whole effect was rather like being on our own private island, which is about as good as it gets on a honeymoon. So if you're looking to splurge on the perfect romantic beach holiday -- or simply want to retreat and recharge -- Tiamo is the place to go!

author: Ebury090
title: The most wonderful stay - we will be back Tiamo !
text: My husband and I recently visited Tiamo in early March and had the most wonderful stay. The island is simply beautiful and just as you would imagine a desert island to be with swaying tropical palms and white sand. I kicked my shoes off as the sea plane landed and didn’t put them back on until it came to pick us up. It is so perfectly formed; you feel as if you are the only two there and the privacy and luxury cocoons you into a totally relaxed state. The food was sublime with fresh fish, salads and fusion cooking on the menu everyday. We have stayed in many luxury locations around the globe and Tiamo is up there amongst the best. I love to snorkel and the swimming and snorkelling were superb with its clear crystal azure blue waters. My husband enjoyed some boating and of course fishing all in one of their beautiful new boats. I enjoyed the spa and had some excellent massages with their resident therapist. The resort has been recently upgraded and has been beautifully designed with so much attention to detail. No corporate furniture and fabrics here. It is wonderfully styled and has the feeling of a large relaxed country house but with all the luxuries you need from Frette towels and linens to the latest NYT gold medal wining wine. The staff were amazing with nothing too much trouble. This is rare in the Bahamas and quite unique to Tiamo - having stayed in different resorts there and in the Turks & Cacaos we know this! We felt a wonderful sense of freedom on the island which is so safe and private. There can be few places in the world you can go where you can leave your door wide open and know the only thing that will have been disturbed is the ice cooler which is filled up daily and the mini bar replenished with your favorite tipple. We will be back Tiamo.!

author: flyfisher7777
title: Great fishing, great food, great service, great location
text: Having been to both the old Tiamo (five years ago), and the updated version (this month), I would have to say the new owners have preserved the best of old and found significant ways of adding to it. The resort location and basic set up is fantastic. The beauty, peace and solitude of Tiamo sets it apart from other places. Having miles of beach you can walk every day is simply an amazing experience. Combined with the small number of possible guests means you feel like you have the place to yourself. The service is amazing as the staff and new owner constantly look for ways to make you feel special and cared for. The renovations are beautful, and the pool is a refreshing addition. The beds are new and amazingly comfortable. The bathrooms are redone and the decor of the rooms is beautiful. Amentities at the main building like Wifi access allowed me to connect to work the few times it was required. We also watched some of the Masters golf tournament on the Sunday and enjoyed an air conditioned and comfortable room created for reading and watching TV. The food was one of the draws for us and we were not disappointed. The chef is wonderful, offering a varied menu with creative and delicious meals. We craved fresh seafood, and certainly had our fill while we were there. The bonefishing was the primary draw for me, and while the weather was not the most cooperative, the fishing opportunities in Andros are simply some of the best you will find. I has shots as some large bones (6 lbs plus) and while I only landed one in that size range, I could only blame my casting ability for lack of greater success. I caught planty of average size (2lb-3lb) fish to keep me happy.

author: chelseyLondonUK_
title: "A week in heaven"
text: My newlywed wife and I, decided to go to Tiamo on a friends recommendation. We were not disappointed!!. It offered everything we wanted, it was secluded, beautiful, hot and most importantly all the staff were lovely and willing to go out of their way to make out holiday as enjoyable as possible. As an enthusiastic but armature fly fisherman Andros stood out as a great location as I could sneak in a couple of day’s bone fishing. My guide Marvin was very patient with both me and Ruth, he took us all around the island looking for the perfect locations to catch the fish. Just being out on the water was fabulous an added bonus was that Ruth caught her first bone fish, annoyingly the biggest of the day. The resort itself had recently been done up. the rooms had everything that was needed and immaculatly presented. The honeymoon suit had a brilliant view and lovely decking to sit on and watch the sun go down. I want to congratulate the chef for producing five star food, which is even more an incredible achievement considering how far mush of the ingredients came. Most nights he would cook Snapper, Wahoo or whatever else had been caught that day. In my opinion there is nothing better than catching blue water fish and eating them. There were a large amount of activities to take part in if you were that way inclined but we were happy just to sit back and relax. I would advise this as a great place to go on your honeymoon. As you can get as involved with the other guest as you like but when you want you can get away and find your own space. We could not have asked for a better week We will be back. Thanks Tiamo Alan and Ruth

author: androsdonna
title: Got engaged in paradise
text: Wonderful Engagement Surprise! My fiance chose this resort because it is on Andros, where I grew up on the US Navy Base on the North End of the island. He also knew I would like the eco-tourism aspects of the hotel. It was so wonderful we asked for a behind the scenes tour, so we could learn how they operated. The beach was wonderful, very private with great warm blue water. There are only 11 bungalows, so at any time the most guests there will be is 22. Every day the Nature Concierge team leads an excursion, some days a kayak trip, some days bonefishing. We chose to skip the first day's excursion and spend the day at the beach. We were the only ones there all day! The next day we went on the snorkeling trip, and got to swim over several underwater blue holes, and a sunken boat. The staff could not have been friendlier. Chef Joanne's meals were amazing, and the service staff was so friendly. Sandy was a great and fun bartender. Our bungalow was really special. It felt very secluded and private, even though it opened out to the elements on all sides. Though it was VERY hot while we were there, the bungalow was always comfortable. And we loved the huge exposed shower. Of course the trip was extra special because my boyfriend proposed to me on our last day there, our second anniversary. When the staff found out, they were very happy for us, and all of the staff and guests cheered for us at dinner. We will definitely be back, and are even considering having our wedding or honeymoon at Tiamo next summer!

author: TSouthwest
title: Sublime Tiamo
text: It’s difficult to find words to convey what one experiences at Tiamo Resorts on the island of South Andros, but I feel the need to try! There is a sublime quality that begins once you leave the dock and head out into the South Bight and it continues when you walk up to your own private bungalow as the sun slowly sets in front of you. No cars, no TV’s, no radios, no newspapers, no interference from the outside world to intrude into an atmosphere of elegant simplicity with every building carefully constructed to maximize one’s immersion into a natural world, while still providing a comfortable experience. This is one resort that means what it says about sustainability and concern for the environment. Every stage in the conception, planning, and construction of Tiamo was carefully worked out to minimize the impact on the environment and the ecosystem. The demonstration of this lies in the overall design of the facility. But beyond the physical presence of the resort, the heart of the resort lies in the intentions of the staff and the owners, which radiates warmth, acceptance, and a sense of community we have not experienced anywhere else. You truly feel at home here. You may be isolated from the troubles and worries of the world, but you are treated to level of service and quality of food that is unsurpassed. The wait staff and the bar staff provide a congenial setting for a happy hour which is followed by a shared meal with all guests arranged at one long table. So here you are, far away but sharing with newly found friends the joys of the day whether bone fishing, snorkeling, sailing, swimming, hiking, or just lying peacefully in your own hammock in from of your bungalow. And at night the perfectly constructed bungalows, allow the evening breezes to flow through the screened porches, while keeping out all the bugs so you hear only the sounds of the ocean, and the wind in the trees. In fact, you can’t even see your neighbors, only the dense trees outside. Someday more resorts like Tiamo will be constructed with such care and concern for the environment. But until then, Tiamo leads the way proving that you can have world class service attending to the needs of your clients, while at the same time attending to the needs of the planet. Thank you Tiamo, thank you Mike and Petagay, thank you staff and management of Tiamo for showing the world how it should be done.

author: Nomad20234
title: Great Week At Tiamo
text: Firstly, anyone who has given Tiamo a negative review obviously did little or no research into what the place offers and is all about. I can't believe that anyone would come here and be surprised by aything that they found. We stayed for a week in June and had an absolutely wonderful time. The only negative thing about the whole week were the mosquitos which is hardly the fault of Tiamo! The bungalows are lovely. The beach is fine. The water is crystal clear. The food was fantastic. Eating with the other guests every night was very enjoyable. Maybe we were just lucky and had nice people there that week (thankfully not some of the people who have left reviews recently). The staff are all great. The locals were extremely pleasant all the time and Adam, Tamara and Graham were simply fantastic. They are enthusiastic, knowledgable and accomodating. I cannot praise them highly enough. If you are looking for a big resort hotel with HBO, A/C, wireless internet then this is not the place for you. If you are looking for real desert island, away from it all rustic beauty with a personal touch then you should certainly consider Tiamo. We had a wonderful week as did all the other guests we stayed with and spoke to and we cannot wait to go back.

author: Nomad9953
title: Speechless!!!
text: My husband and I stayed at Tiamo January 7-12th 2006. We even got married there!! Sometimes the thought of a Destination Wedding is more like a nightmare...but not at Tiamo. Tiamo exceeded our expectations and made us the happiest newlyweds in the world. I could not have wished for anything more, they made a little girl's life long dream come true. Everything was taken care of ahead of time and everything from arrival, to the ceremony and honeymoon, to departure was a breeze!! The food was excellent, service was great and the atmosphere.....Well.... you have to be there to understand how truly unique, relaxing, and beautiful it is. The only, and I do mean only, negative thing I could possibly say is...sand fleas. They bite, and if you forgot your Deep Woods Deet (only brand that works) you'll be itching. BUT, I think those kinds of things come with the territory. I also think the efforts and values that Tiamo stands for are great. Their eco-friendly style was something I have never experienced and it was wonderful. We are planning to return in a few years for a wedding anniversay. See you all soon.

author: Road20235
title: Perfect balance
text: Tiamo is an amazing achievement. Mike and Petagay have created an exceptional resort that perfectly blends comfort and relaxation with the unspoiled natural beauty of Andros Island. I had visited Andros several times for fishing, but never considered bringing my wife based on the rough accommodations and that travel to Andros was difficult and unpredictable. Not any more. NY to Ft. Lauderdale, then Lynx Air, a new service, right into Congo Town. I got a kick out of going through customs at the tiny airport with my 6 fellow travelers. A 5 minute taxi ride to the South Bight, and a short and beautiful boat ride to Tiamo. I had excellent bonefishing with local guide Marvin Miller, who took me to the west side of Andros to places that have never been fished. He really knew his stuff. Tiamo works with several guides like Marvin, with nice new flats skiffs. There is also snorkeling at several blue holes or hiking inland trails with Tiamo's knowledgeable nature staff. At dinner, Mike would toast returning couples with champagne. This happened every night the week we stayed at Tiamo. I can see why. We will be back too.

author: talover
title: rustic luxury...
text: Tiamo is as described by others before me....secluded, blissfully quiet, stunningly beautiful with its deserted beaches, turquoise waters and thriving barrier reef. On landing, the bungalows and main lodge are not visible...yet as you lie in your most comfortable bed ('open air' surrounded by screened in porch) you can see down a pathway to the sand and sea. The bungalows epitomize the nature of this small resort....simple in design (featuring wood, native stone), finely screened for protection yet wonderfully connected to its beautiful surroundings, private yet seconds from the beach and a minute or two from the main lodge building, comfortably luxurious (great bed and nice linens!)...and all of this with an 'eco friendly', environmentally respectful approach. Additional comments... ...We encountered ZERO bugs, mosquitos,'noseeums'at this time of the year. ...Temperatures (early March) were ideal (of course we are from the north!)....daytime high 70's and low 60's at night, which was perfect for sleeping under the duvet. ...Water temperatures were a little cool, but wetsuits are available for long snorkelling expeditions (which are a MUST) ...Sightings of large sea turtles, leaping tarpon, small sharks and barracuda were thrilling....not to mention the breathtaking aquatic life in general. All of this is accessible and comes to life as a result of the very knowledgeable staff of 3 young students employed by Tiamo....BRAVO! ...We enjoyed some of the best "dinner parties" ever, as we gathered around a long table with all the resort guests in the evening (all 20 of them!). As noted by others, there is a definite international flavour and a fun, interesting mix of people. ...As dinner "wound down" a bonfire was started on the beach and those wishing to sit and chat, view the stars, have a "nitecap" were welcome. ...Lastly, we found this to be a very "easy" getaway in general. With just four or five days to "escape' at this time, we found the direct flight to Nassau (available commonly in the east) and seaplane trip of less than half an hour ideal. Once on the shore, bags were taken, a drink and light lunch were prepared for us just steps away and within an hour we were walking down the beach! Tiamo is truly a special place...a rare find and the sort of secluded and peaceful retreat that is becoming more and more difficult to find.

author: Alan1231
title: Everytime I think of Tiamo...(smile)
text: It's really hard to write about a place you want to keep for yourself. Not tell anyone about it and hope it never changes. As the seaplane took off from the fresh water lake in Nassau and slowly climbed into the sky, you new right then that this adventure was going to be a breath taking experience. Just the sight of the water was breath taking. The staff waited on the beach to meet our plane as it glided up to the beach and we jumped into the water without our shoes on. Paradise, Paradise and more Paradise. The staff is great. From Cheif Eric whom shaves his head and makes wonderful dishes, to Grahm and Nature Boy Eric whom both really try to make your experince here a lasting impression. Maxine and Mellisa know how to shake the grove thing behinde the bar at night, so bring some of your own music. Dance a little, Drink some of the best tequilla and get to know a few people from all over the World. Besides the staff, we were the only American's there. We meet wonderful people from Germany, the Bahamas and Sweden. If you want a life time experience you need to go here. Warning - Bring Good strong bug spray 100% Deet, but do not let a few biting insects scare you off. Just be prepared.

author: RONBRONB
title: Just what the doctor ordered
text: When our seaplane landed on the beach at Tiamo Resorts, we had to take our shoes off as to not get them wet. The next time we put them back on was when we left for Nassau Airport. In between we experienced total relaxation, exquisite dining, pristine beaches, and the finest snorkling we ever experienced. Initially the whole ecotourism, no tv, no a/c thing scared me. It turned out to be "just what the doctor ordered". We take our vacations very seriously, normally staying at 5 star resorts. Tiamo exceeded all of our expectations. The food was excellent,{Kudos to Chef Eric}, I gained 5 lbs. Everything was made to order and fresh. They were also very sensitive to my wifes many food allergies. The beach was pristine. On many occasions our footprints were the only ones all day. Lying in a hammock with a good book is something everyone should experience. The snorkling was superb.Our guides Grahm and Nature boy Eric were informative and helpful. The water was warm and clear. I swear you could see 100ft to the bottom. We had the pleasure to have dinner with our host Mike on a few evenings. He is a very unique individual with interesting views on almost everything. In conclusion, we have nothing but great things to say about Tiamo Resorts and would highly reccommend going there. We will be back!

author: Journey34977
title: It's like landing in a postcard.
text: As our seaplane touched down in the water off of Tiamo(an experience that should not be missed), our pilot, Paul Harding of Safari Seaplanes, turned to me and my wife and gave the perfect description of the resort: "It's like landing in a postcard." The beauty of Tiamo is more than you can accurately describe. Paradise is as close as you can come. You can't help but forget about the hectic pace of the real world while you relax at Tiamo. While laying on a hammock under a coconut palm listening to Kenny Chesney's "Songs from the Old Blue Chair" CD, I decided that this was the perfect soundtrack to Tiamo. The staff goes above and beyond the call of duty to ensure your stay is perfect. Chef Eric's culinary creations are amazing. The daily announcement of the dinner menu is always one of the day's highlights. The sea life is so abundant. Whether viewing it from the shore, a boat, or snorkeling at one of the amazing dive sites, it is hard to believe you can be that close to these amazing creatures. Snorkeling at the blue holes is just like being in an aquarium. The bonefishing is unbelievable. Our guide, Shine, is a master. I don't know how he saw all of the fish, but we kept catching them, one right after another. For the perfect spot to forget about the hustle and bustle of the real world, book a trip to Tiamo. The rustic luxury of this island paradise will put your mind at ease.

author: Passport7252
title: A Paradise - and hard to believe
text: Nothing is perfect but Tiamo comes close. Not wanting to repeat what others have said before, it may just help to confirm that Tiamo is close to a paradise. You will be pampered by the staff and there are at least one and half of them to one of you and often more. There are a maximum of 21 guests. The chef and sous chef present menus that are carefully chosen, cooked and beautifully presented. The beach is of fine white coral sand. Sailing across the water for the first time in the boats that can't capsize was wonderful. I could go on and on. We loved it. That said it might not suit everybody. It doesn't have all the facilities of the busy resort. There is no swimming pool or TV for example, but that is what makes it so totally relaxing. It is ideal for honeymooners. There was one marriage while we were there and one due for the following week. We have seen more numerous and more colourful marine fish while snorkelling elsewhere in the world, but the coral gardens are absolutely stunning. If you want to spoil yourself then Tiamo is to splash out on!

author: Roving37266
title: An Amazing Adventure
text: My husband and I visited Tiamo in March 2005. From our first emails with the owners to the end of our stay, the experience was perfect. If you want to know what to expect on your stay........just look through the website. Their website is accurate and there are no exaggerations. It really is that amazing. We wanted a relaxing vacation away from the hustle and bustle of the everyday world and Tiamo gave it to us. We felt as if we dropped off the planet for a week and we loved every minute of it. Tiamo is what an eco resort should be. They run the resort on solar power, they minimize their energy and water usage and they are active in preserving the nature habitat of South Andros Island. As a result, each guest gets the experience of being on a natural island with gourmet meals, awesome activities and a friendly staff. The activities are all included and they were a blast. We went snorkeling to a different site every day we were there. The fish and coral were breath taking and the guides added even more fun with their explanations of what we were seeing. The staff was very accomodating throughout our stay. They talked with all the guests at breakfast and decided what activities to do each day. They also made special meal arrangements to accomodate my food preferences (i.e something other than fish). For our anniversary, they even facilitated a special secluded picnic just for us. Overall, we would reccommend Tiamo to anyone that wants to leave the normal world behind. There will be no TV, no phone and no clocks to distract you. All you will have is a beautiful beach, the crisp ocean air and plenty of time to share it with someone special and the new friends you will meet.

author: Inspire14642
title: The perfect Honeymoon
text: Wow, what a great vacation. We went for our honeymoon, and it was absolutely what we wanted, and more. We arrived on a beautiful sunny day to Tiamo, via a terrific boat ride with captain Butter, a dreadlocked local who looked like something out of a movie. When we came to Tiamo, we were met by Petergay, and her daughter Bella at the dock, and the staff took our luggage right to our room. Check-in was as simple as can be, and we had the freedom here to do whatever we wanted. The best thing about Tiamo is the nature. My wife was a bit scared to go snorkelling out in the open water, but John and Justin, the two nature guides, were so helpful and supportive. Although we were on our honeymoon, we learned way more that I thought we would about the local ecology and environment from the guides, and although we were not expecting an educational vacation, we were pleasantly surprised to have had one. The bungalows were beautiful, and we could hear the waves on the beach from our bed. The place is deserted, it's like gilligan's island, except we got to the the best food imaginable. Chef Anna was the bomb! We loved the dinners and lunches (although the breakfasts were not quite at the level we were expecting for 600 dollars a night :( ). The only drawback was there was one rude bartender named Marcy, but all of the other staff were so kind, they made me feel like we were at home. Thank you Tiamo. We don't know when we will be able to come back, but we definitely will be coming soon!

author: Flyer9948
title: blissful nature experience
text: When I booked a trip to Tiamo Resort solely on the basis of their wonderful website, I was concerned that the reality might not live up to the website. What I found at Tiamo, though, was even better! Tiamo is a remote, quiet, relaxing place to spend a few days or a week. With individual bungalows nestled amongst the palms trees and vegetation along a private beach, you can't get much more serene than this. Throw in 3 tasty meals a day, including a gourmet dinner, and your taste buds will be happy too. The owners and staff were all very friendly and welcoming. As I was preparing to leave, the groundskeeper insisted on stopping what he was doing to find and cut up a coconut from the beach for me, since I mentioned I was disappointed I had forgotten to do that. Tiamo is an eco-resort, but they don't seem to throw that term around lightly. Composting toilets look just like the real thing, but use a pint of water and drain to tank for composting (and they're not stinky!). All power for the resort is solar (they do have a generator for backup, but rarely use it). They have motorboats for getting to the resort, fishing, travelling to the reefs and blue holes to snorkel, etc. Other than that, no power toys = blissful quiet! Sailboats, kayaks, snorkeling equipment and trips, and hikes are included in your stay and were incredible adventures. The reefs and blue holes had plenty of beautiful fish and other creatures easily visible while snorkeling. Even the snorkeling right in front of the beach was interesting - fish, rays, eels, starfish, etc right from the dock. There were bonefish on the flats a short walk or kayak from our Tiamo bungalow, which and boat for a day of flyfishing for bonefish (cost extra). Those looking for loud or flashy won't like Tiamo (which is fine with me!). There are no jetskis, no casinos, no shopping...so come prepared to relax and enjoy the natural surroundings. Those looking for tranquility and beautiful marine surroundings will be well rewarded.

author: TeamMan
title: Convenient to Longwood Gardens and . . .
text: . . . Value priced. The Gardens are just about a mile or so down the road. If that's your destination, then this place is a perfect. If you're looking for a comparable hotel, think Hampton Inn. Mendenhall is a rural country version of a Hampton. The rooms are modern and very clean, something that is an absolute must for me. The basic room has all the amenities you might expect plus an extended area with a comfortable overstuffed chair and ottoman. Our room was on the second floor giving us easy access to a lounge area overlooking the lobby (see photo). It was a great value, too. We paid something like $145 plus tax for the night My suggestion is to ask for a room on the second or third floor in the rear. I have a feeling that the lobby and hallways can get noisy when there is a big weekend event (e.g., wedding) at the hotel. As for the "free" breakfast this is where the Mendenhall falls short of most Hamptons. Without going into all the problems let's just say it needs a makeover and upgrade. There is very nice (clean) but small fitness center with treadmill, stationary bike and elliptical along with a rack of weights. It could use a couple of yoga mats. I plan to visit the Gardens again and the Wyeth Chadds Ford Museum. I will most certainly stay at the Mendenhall.

author: jctravel4fun
title: Guests watch your step!
text: Stayed at Mendenhall for a family wedding. Be sure to request early check-in or no room until 4p. Upon receiving our key we crossed the parking lot from the main lobby to reach our room. The elevator was very small and barely large enough for our family of 4 and bags which included 2 kids under 14. Upon arrival at our assigned room their was a step UP to enter. Signs are posted to watch your step. Inside, the rooms were dated and could use a remodel given the price per night. Carpeting felt old, lighting was dim. Inside there is a reminder to watch your step when leaving...because you need to come down that step again. My in-laws stayed in another room and my mother in law wasn't as lucky. She fell due to the step and hurt her foot which required x-rays and a walking boot to heal. Aside from ice the hotel didn't offer much to compensate for the situation as they felt the signs are warning enough. A step in and out of a door way is a risk and it's a decent step up. Take caution if staying at the hotel. Wedding food was ok and bar staff at the event were pleasant. It was an average experience.

author: AuntieFlo
title: Alexander's Lounge at the Hotel
text: I didn't want to eat at the hotel, but it was snowing and I didn't want to drive anywhere. I walked up to the reception desk for the lounge and the formal restaurant. I said I was alone and I wanted to eat in the lounge. The gentleman there said to sit where ever I wanted and HE would bring me a menu. Fifteen minutes later I went back out to the reception desk to ask when he was bringing the menu. He remarked that he told someone else to bring me a menu, no apology. I took my seat and about 5 minutes later a waitress brought a menu. I ordered a glass of wine. There were 15-20 wines on the list of by the glass wines and the one I wanted was not available. I chose another one. I was not really hungry so I ordered a greek salad and I added a portion of grilled maple citrus salmon to it.
