For some odd reason, the salmon came out on a separate plate, not on the salad. It was also not maple citrus flavored. It was just grilled salmon. The salad was tasty with lots of crumbled feta cheese. However, it came with two huge chunks of tasteless hothouse tomatoes. A few grape tomatoes would have been so much more flavorful. There are so many better restaurants in nearby Kennett Square, don't bother eating here unless you have to.

author: gypsy5961
title: Christmas getaway
text: We stopped without reservations on a Thursday late afternoon . We had Friday night booked at a local B&B but were winging it for this day. We were going that evening to Longwood Gardens for the Christmas light show. The hotel was on the way with less than 3 miles to go. I had read good reviews so we decided to check for availability . The desk staff was very curtious . We decided to do for the King Suite . The newly remodeled lobby is beautifully done . The quest rooms are still being transformed but we found our room to be very nice and question the need for a remodel . Clean and spacious with nice toiletries . The bed was very comfortable and the room quiet. Breakfast was beyond expectations . Hot and cold food with everything anyone could want . A very nice staff in the breakfast room and good tasting food . The restaurant on premise has 2 choices . A casual bar or a more formal restaurant. We had a drink and small plate at the bar after our trip to Longwood Gardens . It was perfect to just walk on up to our room . A fair deal all the way around and convenient to most attractions . I would highly recommend a stay here .

author: Marcia1435
title: Thanksgiving 2017
text: We arrived at the Mendenhall Inn around 2:00pm. Our room was not ready, so we headed to the restaurant bar. Out server, Tiffany mixed up wonderful martinis and mimosas. She even gave me a pumpkin martini the bar was going to feature. It was delicious. We asked for a little snack and she supplied it, too. What really impressed me was her concern about a patron. She called a cab to make sure he got home safely and made sure he got into it. Sharp, friendly and competent! Great experience. Our room was on the second floor and had a king bed. We enjoyed our stay and the complimentary breakfast. I wasn’t crazy about the oatmeal dispenser. Loved the coffee in the lobby and the friendly service. Thanksgiving dinner was in the Golden building. There was plenty of food, servers kept the table and buffet stations tidy. It was a great meal with lots of choices for diners of every age.

author: jdalles
title: Enjoyed our Stay Near Longwood Gardens
text: This is a well known hotel, with an equally well known restaurant on site. We chose to stay here because of past visits, and enjoyed our stay. There were three of us traveling, a couple and a single (Mom), so we booked two rooms. When we checked in, the couple (us) was given the Presidential Suite, which looks just as you see it in the photos posted here. But renovations are coming. The room was lovely, with a "hunt country" kind of a theme, a big jetted tub (the reason we were in the room we were in), a sitting area, kitchenette, separate bathroom with shower, and an entry hall. Plenty of room for 2 and we invited Mom over to have some appetizers and relax before we went across the drive to dinner. The room had big windows that looked across the property to distant trees which were in good fall color, nice to see. The style of the room had a period look to it, and the colors were dark green and muted dark red. While quite appropriate for the setting, we think if renovations are done a brighter color scheme would give the suite a boost. The lighting needs more wattage, and more lamps in the suite, especially on grey days or at night. The bed was comfy, the TV and fridge worked fine, the bathroom was clean, we did get a chuckle out of the push button wall mounted phone between the toilet and the shower (I guess if you are the President you have to be in constant contact no matter what you are doing...!) Others have mentioned the renovations underway. We were getting an early start, so we were not overly troubled by the renovations happening in the room next door (which the workers told us will serve as the prototype room for all the future renovations), nor by the daring roofers on the steeply pitched roof over the restaurant building. Yes, they all started work at 8 a.m., which would have been a bit much had we not already gotten up. The breakfast which was included in the lodging price was good as far as selections and the room was comfortable. You could have hot items, cold items, or make your own waffles. No reason to go away hungry. Longwood and the other marvelous places to visit are very nearby. All in all it was just right for our needs.

author: tbridges126
title: Almost perfect....
text: So my wife and I stayed here a few days ago, on a Saturday. We had requested early check-in for our room. The young lady at the desk, Katelyn I believe, was most helpful. The room wasn't ready yet, but we were headed to Longwood anyway. When we arrived back around 9ish, the young man at the desk, Steven, was exceedingly rude to us. He barely spoke above a whisper and repeatedly cut my wife off. We figured this is not typical so we just left it be. When we got up to the room, it was quite nicely decorated and the bed was very comfortable. We had an issue turning on the shower, so we called down and Steven answered the phone very curtly, without so much as a friendly inflection to his voice. Again, it must just be him. Later that evening, around 12am, we went to the lobby to make use of the sundry shop. Marjorie was an angel I tell ya. We kept going in and out of the shop but she smiled and made polite conversation the entire time. The rest of the night was uneventful. At breakfast the following morning, Dee was very helpful, describing everything we asked about and even helping us find some ice for our water. I highly recommend MOST of this hotel. The only sore spot of the trip was Steven.

author: missybrown
title: Not The Best!
text: Arrived on a very rainy evening with advance reservation. Had written a request for a quiet king bed room. I was traveling alone and had close to six hours of preparation for a business meeting in Philadelphia. Due to Draft Week this was the closest hotel to the city that was available. Was given a room on first floor near the elevator with 2 beds in the main building. I called the front desk to request another room and was given keys to the older building ---- arrived to room and it was occupied. Went back to front desk and was given an eye roll and then escorted to another room. The building smelled musty, the carpet was worn and dirty and the shower curtain had mold on it. The restaurant affiliated with the hotel no longer allows one to charge meals to their room- new policy. When asking the front desk to look up my Choice Rewards number I was told it was not possible. I have stayed at many Ascend hotels including the Ascend Century House in Latham NY( a stellar property in every way) and they had no problem pulling up my number. I will say the bed was very comfortable and the coffee was delicious. I ate no breakfast so I can not comment on that. Perhaps the fact that this room was booked on HotelTonight a third party was why I received a sub par room I am not sure. And I knew I was not entitled to points for my stay---- although I guess it really made no difference as my dinner could not be charged to the room! I will not return!!!!!!

author: thetraveler002
title: Exceptional Stay
text: We chose this Inn after staying at an Ascend Hotel in California. Stayed here two nights and the quality of this Inn was on par with our excellent experience in California. I had requested an early check-in, if at all possible and when we arrived the room was ready for us. The front desk personnel were both attentive. The room itself was nicely decorated, clean and comfortable. Loved the shower head, the best ever. Breakfast was included and it was a full breakfast. There was nothing else we would have asked for. The breakfast attendant was so accommodating, even looked up nearby museums for us on his smart phone. After a long day at Longwood Gardens we were too tired to go to the restaurant for dinner. Called for room service, placed our order and it arrived timely and well presented. The only thing missing on the tray, which was wrapped in a table linen, was a candle and a vase with flowers. A really nice and relaxing experience. We would definitely stay here again. Have got to see those DuPont museums.

author: KMA_Adventures
title: A Lovely Spot in Historic Chadds Ford
text: I previously attended a wedding and reception at the Mendenhall and wanted to experience the hotel at the inn. A friend of mine was visiting from out of town so I decided to take this opportunity. I stayed on a Thursday night and the value was excellent. The lobby is lovely and a Keurig awaits you there in addition to lemon water. The inn has 3 floors and was easy to move about. The room was standard, but was very clean. A desk and a lounge chair complete the decor. The view from my room (#319) was of the trees, was private, and would probably be very lovely when the fall leaves turn. The room was comfortable, particularly the beds. The robes were a nice touch. I had no issues with noice, or any other things for that matter. The staff were very pleasant and helpful. The breakfast was a genuine full, hot breakfast, and the variety was quite impressive. The dining area was quite expansive. As a Choice Hotels member I was granted a very generous late check-out time that was greatly appreciated, and particularly helpful due to a later than expected check-in. Although I was not visiting in the immediate area, this would be a great option for those who are, and nice place to get away from it all. My friend was very impressed with the property, and I would definitely stay again.

author: LucyB56
title: Close to Longwood Gardens and Wintertur
text: This hotel is better than average. The #1 requirement is cleanliness. The Inn was clean. The bathroom is not fancy with tiling, etc. but it was immaculate. The beds had mattresses that a person sinks into a little. I prefer a firmer one but that's not a problem. The sheets were clean and of a higher quality grade than many other rooms in this price range. Television was a large flat screen with HBO. The WiFi was spotty. Not the strongest signal. Reading the poor and terrible reviews, it seems that most of the problems are related to "blocked" rooms. We had no problem at all with noise during the night. This hotel is less than 10 minutes away from Longwood and Wintertur. Very conveniently located. Would recommend to others.

author: Sarge1996
title: Quiet and Cozy Rooms
text: We stayed at the Mendenhall Inn enroute to a shopping excursion the next day but mostly to celebrate our 39th Anniversary. The room was very clean and orderly. Although the view was the back side of the inn with a parking lot and garbage area, it was not too bad since we weren't there that long. I would have preferred the front side. Perhaps there should be a form to complete upon arrival to ask for a preference. It seemed that all occupants that night were on the back side of the inn. The room was quiet despite a family next to us. Breakfast the next morning was good and there were many choices, however, the coffee was a little weak. The selection of items was better than most hotels that offer breakfast with the room. The scambled eggs, biscuits, and waffles were very good. Bacon was a bit undercooked but still very tasty. The only downside of the stay was that in my reservation request I indicated we were staying for our anniversary and no one acknowledged it. The Inn did have a package for Anniversaries but I didn't see it when I reserved online and when I tried to change to request it, I was not able to do so. It would have been nice to have a little something welcome us in our room. The restaurant had a flower centerpiece when we dined there.

author: BrinsleySchwartz
title: Location, Location, Location...
text: We had stayed at the Mendenhall a number of years ago and found it to be just what we were looking for. A small quiet private hotel where we could relax and enjoy the nearby attractions. This time was different. We booked the two dinner package, one dinner at Mendenhall and the other at the Concordville Inn, with tickets to Winterthur, Longwood Gardens and The Brandywine Museum. All in all, not a bad package, however the Mendenhall is no longer quaint. There were two weddings each of the nights we stayed, this made the place a little frantic at times. Coming back to the hotel after touring the area, there were very few places to park because of all the wedding guests. The rooms at Mendenhall were somewhat dated but clean and neat. We found the staff to be extremely friendly and helpful. We had dinner (limited menu for package guests) our first night at the Mendenhall Restaurant, the food was well prepared and tasty, classic american dinner. The restaurant was well appointed and quiet. Our second night was at the Concoirdville Inn (where again there was a wedding and no parking) with a menu for package guests very similar to the one at the Mendenhall. Not so well appointed and not so quiet. The tickets for the attractions appear to be good for a least a year, we visited Winterthur which we found to be somewhat confusing but non-the-less interesting. Next time we come however, we will find a different hotel.

author: NanciK_11
title: Mostly Good - But Big Beware
text: We stayed here two nights for a wedding. It is a small, older hotel but we enjoyed our stay there. The folks at the front desk were very nice and helpful. We got lucky as we were on the third floor on the back hallway, overlooking the woods. Our room was quiet and decorated nicely. The shower had been recently renovated and was great. Rate was $139 a night and I thought that was reasonable. We did not dine at the restaurant or go to the bar. The wedding venue was very nice. Food was also very good. Staff was okay. Not over the top friendly for hosting a wedding. My big beware is if you have a basket for gift envelopes, make sure it is locked so only cards can be put in and not taken out. Someone came in and stole a half dozen cards out of the basket. It was caught on tape but staff has not been overly helpful in trying to resolve. Police were contacted next day and report filed and I guess this has happened before there.

author: Lulubelle1212
title: Lovely Hotel
text: Last Saturday night we attended a wedding at the Inn at Mendenhall. Since we live an hour away, we decided to get a room so we didn’t have to worry about driving home late at night. For years I have been hearing about how beautiful the Mendenhall Inn is, so I was excited to finally stay at the hotel. I was a little disappointed. The Inn is very nice, but not at all “grand” as it is usually described. Out room was in the South Building and was in the basement. Not at all what I expected. The elevator and hallway in the South Building was a little dingy. Our room, however, was very nice, it was spacious and had a “colonial” feel to it. Our room had two double beds which were extremely comfortable. The room was spotless. The staff at the hotel was efficient and friendly. The hotel provided a free breakfast which consisted of scrambled eggs, premade omelets, sausage, make your own waffles, muffins, biscuits and gravy, oatmeal, and cereal. The hotel has a bar and a fine dining restaurant (one of the best restaurants in the area). The hotel is close to Longwood Gardens and the Brandywine Battlefields. All in all, it was an enjoyable stay and if I were to attend another wedding there, I would definitely stay again.

author: MMACM
title: What A Deal!!
text: We did the Brandywine I package which includes Longwood Gardens. The value, room quality, front desk courtesy, and service were impressive. This was a great deal. The only negative I experienced was something that I observed with the breakfast staff members. A guest asked if an item was going to be refilled and the staff replied "Just wait lady"... as if to say hold your horses. Now, I could've seen only part of that exchange and she could have been a difficult guest, but I didn't see anything to prompt that short response. I would stay here again and would recommend this place to my friends and family. And by the way... we arrived close to 9p. Every place to eat in the area closed at 9p except the hotel tavern. I hadn't eaten yet, so I ordered a burger and fries. Whoa! A half pound burger with mushrooms, onions, swiss, and bacon for $12 bucks. I took it to my room and slept happy.

author: knudah1
title: Friendly staff, great amience, quiet location
text: Bottom line: The hotel is quite and rural and the staff is friendly. The other amenities are pretty standard or nothing special, but this is a good hotel. Rooms: Clean and comfortable. Oddly enough there was a phone in the bathroom. Service: The staff was incredibly friendly. The ones I talked to always had a smile and were very helpful. Value: Pretty reasonable price. You get a good room, standard amenities and friendly staff for a decent price. The restaurant is a little pricy to me, but the food is really good for the money. Location: This place is pretty rural. If you like quite, you will probably find it here. As some who likes to run there were not many places to go for a run outside around here. Highway 52 has a small shoulder, but fast traffic. The side roads are beautiful and low traffic, but have no shoulders. Amenities: While it does have a business center the printer there was constantly broken. I did not try their exercise center, but it does have one. The rooms have free internet and the free breakfast has a good rotating selection of hot items (eggs, sausage, etc.) as well as a good and standard selection of cold items (cereal, fruit, etc.)

author: mievan
title: Nice Hotel
text: I usually stay at a Hilton or Marriott. Everything was booked for the night I requested so I looked at the reviews and saw this hotel. It is part of the Choice Hotel "Ascend Collection". Ascend Collection hotels must embody one of three distinct categories - Historic, Boutique or Unique and show a commitment to service excellence. I was very please with the location (near Longwood Gardens and Winterthur). It was located off a quite road, so there was no road noise. It is an older hotel/Inn - 1990, but very well maintained. I stayed in room 124 which was across the parking lot from the main building. It was very quiet. The room was very clean and the linens and beds were great! The staff at the hotel is friendly and very service oriented. Complimentary breakfast is included in the price of the room. This type of self serve breakfast is offered at many hotels, but it is usually served on paper and plastic. This breakfast was on china and real silverware. There was also an omlette/eggs cooked to order station. The day I was there there was a selection of eggs, ham, bacon and home fries. It also offered the usual cold cereal, muffins, bagels, waffels, fresh fruit, etc. I would stary here again and recommend to family and friends.

author: 918mjw
title: Nice property, despite no power. Staff not overly helpful.
text: The hotel itself was quite clean and well-decorated. When we arrived, the employee checked us in, took my credit card for incidentals and even directed us to the elevator, but failed to mention that there was no electricity throughout the property. When we got to our room, our keys didn't work so I went back down. Instead of giving me new keys, she needed to come up to verify I was using them right. After waiting to get new keys, we finally got into our room. When we went in, we realized there was no power. I expressed my frustration that the hotel could have notified us in advance of our arrival. She claimed she had no contact information for me. We asked for candles or flashlights and they said they couldn't provide anything. Unfortunately, we had prepaid for this hotel and they were not willing to refund our money or help us since we had booked the room through a third-party. Lesson learned! Book hotels directly irregardless of the $$$ saved! The free breakfast was quite basic since they had no power, but they had gone out and brought back Duncan Donuts coffee and donuts. They also had a hot plate where they were making custom omelets which was a nice touch. When we checked out, they could not print a receipt, but promised they would email it. I left my email address but never received the receipt from the property.

author: latavalozzo
title: Highly recommended
text: Actually, I did not stay at the Mendenhall, my son and his wife did. This is one of many stays for my out of town family, friends and business associates. Through the years the Inn has only gotten better. Being a long time resident in the area, I am familiar with the local Hotels and restaurants, when having to accomodate out of town guests our experience has been that Mendenhall Inn was by far the best. Not only do they have an excellent restaurant that provides a wonderful cuisine, there is a friendly tavern and an incredible Sunday Brunch. The atmosphere is lovely with rates, restuarant offerings very affordable. The Sunday Brunch is the best value in Chester County. I have recommended the Inn to friends and business associates for years. There has never been any disappointments. Our family enjoys gatherings for Brunch and dinner for special occasions or just getting together. We even had a large family reunion there. In the many years we have visited the Inn we enjoy it like it was our first. The service is excellent from the hotel to the waitstaff. This is the other restaurant of the two that I enjoy going to, from those special times to just stopping in for a light fare and the New York cheesecake to "die for" in the tavern. P.S. Mendenhall has Buckley's beaten hands down. If you live in the area and are just looking for fine dining at a very reasonable cost, stop in, you will be pleasantly surprised.

author: IcebergSlim06
title: Great Hotel but Noisy!
text: We were in town for an overnight trip. The staff was extremely friendly the entire time we were there. I did not realize that the parking fee was $8 per night but it's expected for a "close to downtown" location. The rooms are spacious and comfortable. The kitchen comes well equipped. The only noticeable issue is the white appliances. Most other properties have upgraded to stainless steel (no biggie). The only negative worth mentioning is the noise from outside. As soon as we were settled in and off to sleep... the 11pm train (not DART) outside come by with all the bells and whistles blaring!!! I'm not sure if this can be heard on the other side of the property. Once sound asleep... the 7am garbage truck comes by with beeps and banging the dumpster on the truck. I would definitely recommend requesting a room away from the railroad tracks and dumpster side of the hotel. Overall it was a great stay. We will probably stay here again when in the area but definitely on the other side of the property.

author: givings
title: Decent accommodations but unprofessional staff
text: Great location and reasonably updated rooms are the reason for two stars. But... Upon checking in, I asked about a room upgrade since we are Marriott Gold. I was told NO, the hotel is completely sold out. After pulling up the online availability which showed upgrades WERE available, I was told that the online content is wrong. "Really?" I asked, "but why can I pay for this room online right now but you say it is not available?" He's not sure. "Okay," I say, "may I speak to the manager?" All of a sudden an upgrade materializes. I hate fighting over reward program benefits. AND being lied to. The room was fine, but the table/chairs combo on the balcony was missing one of the chairs. I immediately called the front desk and asked for the missing chair; was told housekeeping would bring one by. We waited. And waited. And waited. The moment was lost. Husband and I would have enjoyed sitting on the balcony in the evening or with our coffee the next morning, but no chair was provided. At 8:38 am, housekeeping knocked on the door and started letting herself in. Seems awfully early on a Saturday morning to clean my room. Fortunately I was awake and dressed, but she opened the door before I could actually let her in. We will not stay here again, and will let our friends know they should find a different hotel.

author: anr131
title: Convenient and Pleasant Stay
text: I spent two nights here. The check in was quick and easy. Our room was very comfortable. The bed was soft and even the couch was so comfortable I probably could have slept there. The ceiling were high and the room spacious, which made me feel right at home. We didn't use the kitchen much, but it was fully stocked if we had needed it. (There was also an option of leaving a grocery list for them to shop for you that would be useful if you had a long stay). The staff was all very friendly and gave me a complimentary razor and can of shaving cream when I realized I forgot mine. Breakfast was fantastic. There was a wide variety of hot and cold items. The breakfast and dining area was very clean, and employees took the trash from our table for us. One afternoon there was strawberry water in the lobby; that was a nice refreshment as we were leaving. The location is great, right off of West 7th and only a $5 Uber ride to downtown. Even so, it's set back between condos, so it was very quiet. I highly recommend, and I plan to stay here again.

author: NorthbridgeRich
title: Clean and convenient
text: I stayed here for two nights. It's conveniently located off 7th Ave in the Cultural District. Check in wasn't as smooth as I would have hoped. I checked in online the day before arrival to expedite my arrival as I just wanted to be able to change and head to my appointment. The front desk was staffed by one and she was helping someone make a reservation. That took about 5 minutes. Once she was off the phone she quickly checked me in and the room was available. The rooms have all the amenities you expect out of a Residence Inn. I however was just staying 2 nights so I didn't use the kitchen area. The bed was comfortable but a bit hard. The bathroom was clean and neat. Basic toiletries were provided. Morning breakfast was served in the lobby area. Assorted pastries and bakery items are available as well as hot food including French toast, bacon, scrambled eggs, and self service waffles. Juices and water are also provided. The only issue I encountered was a full parking lot and confusion on where the lobby entrance was. I saw many people try and use the back door as the first turn for the hotel is actually the back parking area.

author: Coach_Clark
title: Underwelming
text: This may sound nitpicky, but afterall it is an average rating and not a poor rating. These are the reasons I found this Residence Inn to be considered Average: My wife and I did a short get-away for our Anniversary, to the Fort Worth location. We wanted to be by the Kimbell and have a relaxing, quiet stay in the area. The room was quiet enough (even the occasional train nearby did not disturb our sleep). However, there were a few nagging things that took away from the experience. The hot tub/jacuzzi was out of order. We had brough our swim trunks and were disappointed to find this out. No night lights in the room. I know this is petty, but the room was pitch dark, and any lamps were too bright to leave on, plus the fan was automatically on with the light switch for the bathroom, so leaving the door cracked with the light on was not an option. Adding a few nightlights would help navigate those late night bathroom trips. There was a used bar of soap in the shower - Kind of grossed us out. There were several panhandlers around the area, so if you are walking just be prepared to deal wit that (not the hotel's fault of course). The restaurant area nearby was more of a strip mall with the ubiquitous Starbucks and other chain options. We ate at Pho District Vietnamese restaurant which was closer to the hotel and had a good meal there. Lastly, it says it is pet-friendly, but a $100 non-refundable deposit is a pretty steep charge for bringing a small dog. On the positive side, the hotel is very close to the Kimbell and the Fort Worth Arboretum, which we both visited. The Desk Staff was very courteous and helpful. Breakfast options were pretty decent. The room seemed clean enough except for a few stains on the floor and a slight must smell. For a Residence Inn I expected a little better, but I can't give this one more than an average rating.

author: 673darcyt
title: Lies are Prevalent
text: Hotel was clean. Breakfast fine. HOWEVER, I chose to stay at this hotel for 6 nights because, while it was a bit more expensive, it had a free shuttle that could get me to/from my class at TCU. I called twice during the month before my arrival to verify the shuttle. "I need to be at class by 8am and leave at 4:30". I was told those would not be a problem. Upon arrival, I learned the people I'd spoken to had lied. The shuttle had been booked for four weeks (and was booked for more) by two companies for those times. I'd have to take a cab or use an Uber driver. My Uber driver (more reliable than a cab) has been wonderful, but I'm having to pay $20 plus tip each way, twice a day. If the Residence Inn had not lied to me SEVERAL times, I could have stayed at a cheaper hotel and walked to class or rented a car. After all $50 a day times 4 days is $200. When I expressed my concern about the lies, the assistant managers basically said, "Sorry" or "The shuttle is booked 90% of the time by those companies anyway" (really?! and no one mentioned that when I called?!). One did refer me to a manager who "Gets in between 7:30 and 8 and who leaves between 4:30 and 5". Would not stay here again. Trust is not there for me and who knows what else they might be lying about.

author: Koakoakoa
title: Nice location, uncomfortable beds
text: The bad: The major problems with this place were the beds and pillows. The mattresses are saggy and uncomfortable, while the pillows are over stuffed, making it impossible to sleep well. I did not get one good night's sleep while we were there and my back hurt every morning (and I'm only 28 and in good shape). Also, the linens were bumpy- obviously worn out poly-blend. I had to go down to the desk to get a different sheet, which was replaced a few days later with ANOTHER pilled, scratchy sheet. This makes me think that it is probably a constant issue. My advice to the manager/ owner would be to update your bedding and mattresses- they are obviously cheap and worn out. We were considering this place for a family reunion next summer but the beds would have to be updated. Also, the water temperature in the shower would randomly switch between scalding hot and freezing which was really weird. The good: The location for this hotel was great. It was easy to walk to different restaurants and there is a nice park across the street. Additionally, they have a shuttle service that will take a group to specific locations (restaurants or the stockyard, wherever) BUT it only lasts until 8pm. We were there for a wedding and the staff was very welcoming and accommodating. The rooms were nice, I actually preferred our studio to our friends' suites that we saw. The only difference is that there is a wall separating the living area from the bedroom and there is an extra TV in the suite. It would be good for people traveling with kids. It was nice to have a full kitchen available in the room. The free wireless worked well and it was fun to play on the basketball court outside. Breakfast was decent, but they need a microwave in the breakfast area for those of us who prefer our eggs, bacon, etc hot instead of lukewarm. Bottom line: great location and friendly staff but the beds and sheets are only 1 or 2 star quality.

author: Iyer_vijay
title: Loved my stay here at the Residence Inn
text: I first stayed here in Feb 2013 and was impressed by the service they provided . And on my next trip from Aug 2013 to Oct 2013 . I insisted on getting myself accomodated in this hotel. The rooms are spacious , breakfast was good enough . . . But more importantly . . it is in very close proximity to lots of other diners . . . Very close to downtown . They also provide a free shuttle to places within a 5 mile radius .. . Which is really helpful for people like me who dont prefer to drive around in the US. Have a great time . And I prefer to stay here in my every trip to Fort Worth.

author: CCTraveler56
title: Wish I had found this one sooner.
text: My family stayed here for my youngest daughter's graduation from TCU. We booked a total of three rooms for the event, with me staying an entire week. I didn't realize they offered a "cocktail hour" and dinner Monday thru Wednesday. Each night has a different meal but always a salad, beer and wine, and soft drinks which is included in your hotel cost. It's not gourmet food but quite good, especially if you don't want to go out. Breakfast is also included. It's a typical breakfast but there's always plenty of it. Though I wish they would have a different cut up fruit other than honey do melon. Everyone that I death with at the front desk were pleasant and helpful. One late afternoon when we got back to the hotel, our neighbor across the hall had their door open and was cooking Indian food. Boy, that smell is strong! It hadn't been bad the previous evenings and didn't permeate into our room. This time it did! The front desk took care of it and their door was quickly shut. I guess this can be the drawback to having a kitchen in each room. This was also the least expensive hotel I found for the busy graduation weekend. Ask for a TCU discount when reserving a room. It saves you a little bit of money!

author: CaribeGirl_8
title: Not impressed.
text: Yeah, yeah. It's a nice property and the location is good. But there is an abundant amount of thoughtlessness when it comes to the details. In other words, there were way too many corners cut for my liking. Here are some examples: -The bedside lamps don't have outlets in them so you have to move the large nightstands/dressers to plug something in. -The hotel internet not secured. I'm sure apartment dwellers use it and take up bandwidth because it was very slow. -Beds very low (think IKEA beds). -There was nothing in the shower to provide traction at the bottom of the tub, making it VERY slippery and quite hazardous. -Brian, the GM, didn't ask me a floor preference upon check in. The people in front of me got asked, but I guess I wasn't afforded that luxury, being the lowly state employee I am, on the government rate. Brian, you really shouldn't put young, single females on the ground floor next to a construction site. -The fitness room was tiny for a hotel of this size and there were no sanitizing wipes. So gross. Do you see what I mean? I travel a lot for my job so the details matter. Needless to say, I don't think I'll stay here again

author: heeler1
title: Enormous suites, friendly staff
text: Stayed here for a business trip and for a friendly, clean, business trip kinda place it is a good choice. Nothing new or special but the staff were exceptionally friendly to say the least. Check in was a breeze. I got in late and was hungry and its important to know the hotel does not have its own food options in the evening. Breakfast in the morning is buffet style (my experience) and adequate but not exorbitant. Serviceable is a good word. The suites are ENORMOUS. Full kitchen, microwave, coffee maker, sitting room. Good TVs in both the living area and in the bedroom. Bathrooms are a little dated but lots of hot water. The bed was comfortable enough and linens of adequate quality. Ktichen has all you need to make your own dinners, etc, although it is not very far to a great part of downtown for really good food. There was a bit of traffic noise due to construction going on next door. For late night snacking, there are cold drinks and chips and snacks at the front desk and the prices are very inexpensive. No gouging. all in all a decent place to stay for business with room to stretch out and feel like you might not exactly be in a hotel...

author: Father0f6
title: Great for a getaway
text: We stayed just one night on a short weekend getaway. I got one room for my wife and I and another for the teenage kids. The staff was very helpful. They knew we were there to have fun and made sure they told us about all that they offered. The location is great, very close to Sundance Square and the Mongtomery area. There is also the Trinity river trail right there. The rooms were clean and nice. We had one studio king room which was quite a bit larger than the one bedroom queen room. The kids stayed in the larger room. We used the heated pool and the hot tub. The breakfast had hot and cold options, the kids especially liked the Texas shaped waffles. After breakfast we used the bicycles that the hotel lends out at no cost and rode the Trinity river trail. I wish we would have had more time to stay another night. They also offer tennis rackets and balls to play on their tennis court and lots of pool toys. The next time we want a weekend getaway with the family we will go back.

author: anniefield
title: Good location
text: Had previously stayed here a couple of years ago. Husband, son and myself were in the area for the Giants/Cowboys game so thought we would check in here again. Last time as a couple we stayed in a studio suite. This visit we chose the 1 bedroom suite which has a separate lounge/kitchen area so son could sleep on the sofa bed. The hotel had not changed apart from the fact that there is now another new development of apartments on one side. It was nice to have the separate bedroom though the bathroom could only be accessed through it. The bed was only a queen size whereas on our previous stay in the studio suite it was a king. There was a small kitchen area with a full size dishwasher, fridge/freezer and microwave but only two rings to cook on and no oven. The aircon was efficient though quite loud going on and off during the night. It did not bother me too much but as the bedroom is very small I could see it annoying very light sleepers. There were tvs in the lounge and bedroom. Wardrobe was a double and there were several drawers in the room for belongings. There was a hairdryer, iron and board but no safe. Toiletries supplied were not sufficient for three people. Towels were not very large but the shower was good and powerful. We did not have any breakfasts in the hotel this trip. For a couple of days it was fine but if we were to come again as a couple we would probably choose the studio with the larger bed and kitchen area. There are even more bars and restaurants within walking distance since our previous visit so that is always a plus. Free parking and free breakfast .All staff were friendly and polite.

author: 127_Hill_Country
title: Ouch, I hurt from sleeping on the bed
text: I was impressed when I arrived at this Resident Inn. I am a Marriott Rewards Platinum member and have stayed at a lot of Residence Inns. The lobby at this hotel was above what I normally find at a Residence Inn. The carpet and tile was what you would find at a more expensive hotel. The check in went well...the clerk was efficient and friendly. We got to the room and I found the furnishings again slightly better than other Residents Inn. The one bedroom suite was about 30% smaller, though. Sine it was just my husband and I it wasn't that big a deal but I missed having a place to open up my suitcase that was out of the way. The big draw back on this hotel was the bed. The sheets and blankets were nice. The issue is that my husband and I both kept waking up because we were uncomfortable. As the night wore on I had to keep switching sides because I was getting pains on the side I was sleeping on. I just got up and I am now sore all over. I looked at the brand of mattress out of curiosity... It is a hotel line called Englander specifically made for hotels. A Sealy or Simmons would be so much better. Overall good looking hotel in a good location to the Fort Worth museums but the bed is very uncomfortable.

author: marilynb133
title: Very comfortable stay
text: We used our Marriott Rewards points to stay in this clean, centrally located property while back in Fort Worth visiting family. We loved being so close to some of the best art museum which we took advantage of while there. The 1 bedroom suite was comfortable. Our granddaughter slept on the pull out couch in the living room area. With this third person the placement of the bathroom (located in the bedroom) was a little awkward.The kitchen, though small and without an oven, was well supplied with everything one could need to prepare simple meals. The breakfast was great. There was plenty to chose from and always hot and tasty. We were there for only one afternoon reception offering snacks and drinks. The pool was our granddaughter's favorite place! It was clean with plenty of towels. Toys were available to use while in the pool. There is a great deal of construction in the area but it was quiet indoors. We never heard any noise from outdoors while in our room. We did have a snag the evening before check-out that took a little time to sort out. We were informed that we would have to pay for our final night. There was confusion as to our award benefit but it was cleared up by the front desk and Marriott's Customer Service Department. The staff's assistance continued days after we left Fort Worth when we discovered that my husband had left behind a pair of shoes. Fortunately they were located and the staff sent them to us. We'll be back in Fort Worth again and certainly will plan on staying at this Residence Inn.

author: WhitneyF593
title: AWESOME! AWESOME! AWESOME!!!
text: We reserved 2 rooms. We requested the top floor with both of our rooms close- The front desk at check in around 7-8pm was GREAT!!! He went WAYYYY out of his way to make sure our rooms were great. One of the rooms had an odor, and he immediately switched our room and upgraded it a bit. The hallway had a bit of an odor. The hotel is super close- within walking distance to a strip of restaraunts. We ate at Gloria's which was really good. The rooms were clean. The breakfast was perfect. Service was amazing. The pool was clean and warm because it is "heated". I loved our mini vacay here! WE WILL BE BACK. This hotel is also super close to the Fort Worth Zoo, which we visited the following day. :o)

author: lucycan
title: Great hotel with a few small caveats
text: Ive stayed here before. About 5 years ago when it first opened. So I wanted to submit a follow up review. I needed a quick 1 night stay somewhere close to downtown Ft Worth. I spent over an hour on this site looking at all the Marriott properties (there are quite a few) within 10 miles of town. They all have, at best, average reviews. Except this property. I checked in fairly late, about 10pm. I asked for a room in a quiet location and was given room 401, in a corner at the end of the hall. The room was nice, clean, and large. Only a few small issues. Old style TVs, but I don't watch much. Old style Marriott bedding which was mentioned in another review. No big deal. It was soft and clean. The shower water was only mildy warm in the morning but I think this was a rare issue, at least according to the front desk. The property is nice, the staff was friendly, and its in a good location. I got a decent rate. I would stay again.

author: ladinks
title: Over priced
text: Given the location of this hotel, the price is too high. Paid $214 per night with AAA. Walking distance to a shopping Center with a Super Target and a few restaurants. Gloria's (Mexican food), Pei Wie(Asian food) and a rowdy, noisy sports bar. Exchange Ave and Sundance Square are not walking distance. We arrived 20 minutes after check-in but when we got to our room it was still being cleaned. Front desk apologized and upgraded us to a balcony room. Balcony was very large and had a partial skyline view. Complementary hot breakfast was substantial and served daily. Happy hour was beer and wine with chicken wings, green beans and salad. Note: Happy hour is Mon-Thursday only! Nice park next to hotel with a duck pond. Keep in mind this is a residence in with long term guests. During our stay, the hotel was pretty much taken over by FEMA employees. On Sunday night (10/5/08) the BBQ area that is supposedly open to all hotel guests was completely monopolized by the FEMA group. Overall a good stay but not a good value. PS. Front desk was clueless on airport directions, got better directions from a hotel guest.

author: TNTColorado
title: Going home ... again :-)
text: If you are going to be in northeastern Italy and want to enjoy history, culture, and simply a great environment ... Portogruaro is the place to go. Yep ... Pisa has a leaning tower ... big deal ... so does Portogruaro! And Antico Albergo Spessotto (also known as Hotel Spessotto) is THE place to stay. In the heart of the old city, right next to the canal and leaning tower (not to worry ... it leans the other way), great accommodations, very clean and great food. The staff is great ... from the friendly folks in the food/bar area, to the behind the scenes folks who do a great job ... to our absolutely favorite ELISABETTA. A great mom, wife, front desk expert ... and after staying here for seven years in a row, a charming lady we consider to be a friend. This place is a truly a home away from home.

author: Limotrav
title: Old hotel close to everything
text: We were told by a young couple that this was a fabulous quaint hotel, and it is indeed 'quaintish'. The decor is dark timber, very dated, but okay if you don't mind it a little dreary. It was clean, and the bathroom had a modern shower set-up. The hotel is situated in the old part of Istanbul called the Sultanahmet which is an intriguing and interesting part of town - close to the Blue and Pink Mosques. We had a Double Standard room, and all we wanted from our one-night stay was a comfortable bed, which we sadly didn't get. This was possibly the hardest bed I've ever slept on, and certainly the pillow definitely was. Our room was at the front of the building on the first floor. Traffic noise may be an issue for some in the front rooms, but as it's not a very busy street, it didn't bother us too much. The building is 6 storeys high, with a lift to the 5th floor, then a spiral staircase with no handrail to the roof where the bar and restaurant are. Hence, this wouldn't be good for people with mobility problems. The view from the roof is fantastic. The included breakfast did not appeal to us Aussies. It consisted of basic cold cuts, cheeses, breads, fruit, eggs, olives, tea, coffee and juice. This breakfast area is also the restaurant and bar. We had a toasted ham and cheese sandwich for lunch there - and it really was basic. We went out for dinner. I hesitate to give a negative review of Burckin Hotel as the staff are very helpful, but would we stay there again? No - mainly because of the hard bed.

author: Vistaowner
title: Hotel OK but not wheelchair accessible as advertised
text: The stars are because of the accessibility misinformation. This hotel showed to be wheelchair accessible and path of travel. I requested an accessible room when booking. It was NOT. From the street to the lobby was 13 stairs down without a railing! They said 'these are the only stairs'. When you can't walk that is not accessible. In the end we stayed and two workers helped my husband down and carried our scooter, wheelchair, 4 suitcases (from cruise) down. The elevator was just big enough for his normal size manual wheelchair. The room itself was an upgrade and although small was quite nice and clean with renovated bath and small balcony with chairs and table. Once we were settled, they kept our luggage and scooter downstairs, it was ok. The view was of Blue Mosque, water and other way to city. I took a walk and found that it was very close to Grand Bazaar too. The staff on hand for that day and night were exemplary. They were there immediately when I called about the AC. They helped us leave at 3 AM for our flight as everything had to be lugged up to the street including my husband and that made a huge difference. I would say that most rooms do not have a balcony, only the 6th floor. Thank God for these employees. No stars to whoever took the reservation in the first place and for the listing that showed it accessible.

author: junglyhh
title: Pretty decent hotel with a great location
text: This is our second trip to the glorious city of Istanbul. If you are a first-time visitor, you should definitely stay in the Old town-Sultanahmet area. What can be better than comfortably sitting in a terrace, staring blankly at the Hagia Sophia and Blue mosque while sipping some Turkish tea and enjoying a great breakfast buffet? The Burckin hotel seems to provide all of these, and its location is hard to beat. If you are from the Istanbul airport, you can take M1 to Zeytinburnu, and then T1 to Cemberlitas, the hotel is a short walk from the tram stop. From the main otogar (bayrampasha), you can hop on a servis shuttle provided by your bus company and get off at Aksaray, then walk to Yusufpasha tram stop and take the tram. The hotel also provides private transfer to the IST airport which costs 70lira or 30euro. The lobby and common area of the hotel is well decorated. The staffs in the front desk speak very good English and can help with most common requests. There is an elevator but our room is on the first floor so we never used it. The room is a little small, but is indeed quite cozy and clean. So if your main task in Istanbul is sightseeing, it is a decent base for a few nights. The only reason that I cannot give 5-star is because of the shower. There is a music player embedded in the walls of the shower room. Once you turn it on and also turn on the water, its touchscreen is locked, perhaps relying on some humidity sensor. It would take quite a while to be able to change the settings again. So if unfortunately you set the speakers very loud, you won't be able to turn if off later and have to bear the noise. Maybe I don't know the right way to use it. This is certainly a very nice perk but a brief user's manual attached next to it would be very helpful.

author: FabGlobetrotter03
title: I liked staying here
text: This hotel is in a great location; very close to the Hagia Sophia, Blue Mosque, Grand Bazaar, City trams and transportation. We stayed in a room on the sixth floor with a balcony that has views of the Blue Mosque. We stayed in a room on the sixth floor with a balcony that had a view of the Blue Mosque. The room was small but clean. There was hardly any space for our suitcases but the balcony made up for the space. The hotel paid attention to the fact that we were two ladies staying in the room and provided us with two shower caps, dental packages, nail files; which is really good. The hotel staff were very attentive and assisted us with our requests. Wifi was very good in both the room and the lobby. Breakfast was served at the Rooftop Terrace of the hotel and the views from the terrace were lovely. You could see the Bosphorus and it’s the two bridges, the Blue Mosque and Aya Sophia. I am always open to new food, so I tried some food that I was not used to, and liked it. There was cereal, cheeses, cold cuts, yogurt, cakes and decent choices at breakfast. We also had dinner at the hotel restaurant and liked it. It has good choices on its menu at reasonable prices. In the evenings, I would go up to the terrace for some wine, relax and enjoy the view. I enjoyed staying at this hotel. It was not very luxurious but it was nice.

author: lwa3
title: Burckin luxury!
text: Lovely hotel. Very nice and clean and friendly staff. Breakfast basic but it is included in the price, so not bad. And lovely to see the city from the rooftop view. They offer transport to airport - price can be negotiated too - so we were happy overall. Stunning rooms with everything you need. TV in our room didn't work but they only had Turkish channels so no loss, as we didn't use it. Amazing location, literally 2 minutes walk from the tram. And about 10 minutes walk to the Grand Bazaar! Lovely area to be located in. Close by to lovely restaurants, shops etc. And free wifi...the strength is brilliant! Recommended! This review would have been 5 stars if they hadn't have tried to overcharge on the mini bar - we did not use any yet they tried to insist in making us pay for 3 cans that we'd apparently had. We argued it and insisted we hadn't! Eventually backed down, but spoilt our experience overall, as the staff had been so friendly and accomodating!

author: SLBM
title: Good for sightseeing
text: It is a very nice and small hotel dedicated for tourists. For the "default sightseeing programme" location could not possibly be better - it's just a couple of minutes from the Sultanahmet Square, where the key sights (Sultanahmet Mosque, Hagia Sophia, Basilica Cistern, Topkapı Palace, Arecheological Museum) are concentrated. Also the Grand Bazaar is not far away, easily within walking distance. Should you need to go to modern parts of Istanbul, a tram stop is just around a corner, allowing you to reach Taksim within something like 20 minutes (tram to Kabataş and then F1 funicular). Hotel itself is very nice and clean, although the rooms are relatively small. I visited this hotel once before, and then I got a larger room, this time it was smaller, but still enough for a tourist (I did not come to Istanbul to linger in the hotel after all). Bathroom was nice and fuctional and so was air-conditioning, although its control was a bit complicated without a manual and it did switch for heating-only mode couple of times - be aware that this can happen. What could definitely be better, is the soundproofing, so be prepared to hear some noise from your neighbours and to be heard as well. Staff of the hotel was friendly and helpful and resolved all our requests without any problems. Internet access is fully functional and free of charge. Breakfast is nice, although for some it might lack variety (depending on what kind of breakfast you are used to). It is served on the roof terrace, which during winters is now closed. It offers a perfect view towards Haghia Sophia, Golden Horn and Bosphorus, although the Blue Mosque, which is partially obscured by a quite ugly residential building. Be aware that to get there you will need to climb a flight of steps, elevator does not reach the terrace. Upon bookig hotel emailed me with an airport pickup offer, which we did use. The cost was EUR 25, paid in cash upon departure (although it could be, and actually was, paid with Turkish lira converted at a rate of 3:1), although according to the information on the hotel website one way transfer is free of charge if you book through that website instead of using some agent. Transport provided was fast and comfortable, and I think it was worth some extra money over a standard taxi. All in all I am very happy about my stay at Burckin Hotel and I can recommend it for tourists, perhaps a bit less for business travellers, mainly due to lack of comfortable workplace in the room (but if you don't have any work to do at the hotel, you may well go for it and take an opportunity to see the main sights which are very close).

author: FROOOM
title: comfortable, upscale, central, friendly
text: i am an experienced world traveler of mature years, picky on hotels (but not overly so), who does much advance research on my travels, including the accommodations, and therefore is rarely really disappointed in them. i have stayed here a couple of times, returning because of several reasons. it is a great location in sultanahmet between the blue mosque and the bazzar. perfect location half a block from the tram line between the two stations. walk everywhere or take the tram down to the ferry port/rr station and over to the newer city. no hills to climb to anything on this side of the bridge. it is a friendly place and they will help you with your siteseeing plans and projects with "how to get there" and "what to see" info if you are nice and personalble to them. breakfst up on the penthouse is very nice and cheerful and a good meal. the rooms have all the "mod cons", but they are really laughably small. ok for a single, but for two people??: get real !! last time i had a "view room" near the top with a lovely balcony which made ALL the difference. there is a computer 24 hours off the lobby. no dinners, but lots of restaurants and a minimarket nearby. quiet location. nice decor in the rooms and super clean, of course. it feels like home, and i look forward to staying here.

author: Academic_SLO
title: Excellent stay at Burckin hotel
text: It was really hard to pick a good hotel in Istanbul, since there are so many to choose from and once you start reading reviews on Tripadvisor it is even harder to decide. Our stay at Burckin was great. The location is excellent, literally 1 minute from the Sultanahmet tram station which makes it very easy to access the hotel from the Ataturk airport. The hotel offers and excellent view of Agia Sofia and the Blue mosque. Topkapi palace is 3 minutes away. The staff is super friendly. Rooms are of decent size, very nicely furnished. The top floor offers rooms with balconies. There is free WiFI all over the hotel and in the rooms as well. The breakfast/restaurant area is on the roof with a truly breath taking view of Agia Sofia and the Blue mosque. Breakfast offers a nice variety of continental-style breakfast essentials, but the emphasis is on Turkish dishes which are very well prepared. ILKE, the waitor is especially friendly. All in all, I would highly recommend this hotel for business and personal travel, especially for couples or singles. Maybe it is not adequate for very young children, but for children above the age of 6-7 years it should be fine. I highly recommend this hotel, since it offers a good quality-for-value choice.

author: machita75
title: Small and elegant
text: We stayed several nights here. The location is great located on a street perpendicular to the tram line. If you ever get lost, just find the tram and follow it. Our room was TINY (had to jump over our suitcases to get in bed!) but very well appointed. All of the furnishings, finishes and decor were well selected in the design of this hotel. The room was clean and smelled nice and you can tell the cleaning staff work very hard. Everyone at the front desk was friendly and knowledgable about things in the area. The terrace has a great view of the mosques and the water. However, it can get crowded up there for breakfast and the staff cannot keep up, piles of dishes sitting around. Its also lovely to sit up there at night when the weather is nice. The AC in the room works really well (in fact one night I had to get up to turn it off because I was freezing). My one complaint is that all the prices for the hotel and bar are in Euros. WHY!? This hotel is in Turkey. I guess they assume that most of their guests are from the EU, but for those who aren't, it is confusing. We ordered drinks and the poor bartender had to get out a calculator to convert the prices to Turkish Lira. This seems unnecessary.

author: J9094AYstevens
title: Another dark and generally miserable Turkish hotel
text: A while ago I ate in an average restaurant that was gaining terrific reviews on trip advisor. It had so many good reviews that is was ranking above many michelin starred establishments. Being a geek, I analysed the reviews and found that nearly 30% were from people who had never written more than two reviews. Its a bit odd to visit a mediocre restaurant and feel the need to open a trip advisor account and write a rave review about it. Now in Turkey, I am amazed at how awful the hotels I am staying in are. They both had very good reviews, but the reality is that they have both been gloomy unfriendly and generally not very nice places. A quick look through past reviews reveals a high number of reviews from first time reviewers. So the Burckin hotel. When i arrived there were two guessed at reception demanding to be found another hotel. They were very cross and from a phone conversation to an agent I understood they were willing to lose money just to be taken away from the hotel. The room I am staying in cost 100 pounds a night. It is the size of a college dorm, without any of the accompanying charm. The room is perpetually dark and the decoration is abysmal. There is a single light in the room and a broken table lamp. The bed is hard and uncomfortable. The walls are paper thin so you can hear people showering, talking, the cleaning going on outside the rooms The staff are generally miserable and seem disinterested. Nobody says hello. In the breakfast room, nobody greats me, explains the buffet (which is stocked with many foods I'm unfamiliar with, nobody brings coffee or explains where to get it from). The situation of the hotel is good, but that is all it has going for it. There must be good hotels in this area, but they are more than likely begin drowned out on trip advisor by hotels like this where people (and this could be genuine) feel the need to write their one and only review to say how amazing this place is - even though my experience tells me different.

author: ViajerodelUniverso
title: Winter at Burckin Hotel in Istanbul
text: I wanted to feel the character of Istanbul in winter. I reserved a longer stay at the Burckin Hotel than last summer. This time a nine nights stay. Included a one way transfer from the airport. They were at the airport with my name waiting for my arrival. A bigger room was asigned (obviously a double) facing the charming small park in front of the hotel, but the small room I had last summer was comfortable enough to Europe standards and for a single. The holiday decorations were the most elegant on the street. This time I walked from the hotel to the Grand Bazaar which last time I did not visit. The Dolmabahce palace and the Spice Bazaar were also included in this visit. The location of this hotel is just great, close to the Sultanahmet tram station, but you could walk to many of the most important monument and museums to see in Istanbul. A second visit to Hagia Sophia was almost at sunset and the lamps were also on, just magical. For two days after some warm days when even roses were blooming there was heavy snow, so having the breakfast included kept me comfortably warm at the hotel going out only to have dinner. The breakfast buffet is offered at the library during winter, not at the spectacular terrace they open in summer time but the tables at the library were very well set. The book on Turkey I donated to the hotel library last summer was labeled and available to myself as a reference. There was fast and friendly response to every request I made. I am most grateful for all their attentions. If you doubt going to Istanbul in winter, do not hesitate. The city is not crowded but lively. The Burkin Hotel is my home in Istanbul which I hope to visit again. Fantastic city and hotel.

author: marcopolo111
title: Excellent location, quality, service and value
text: It has all I need when traveling for pleasure: location, quality and comfort, quietness, service and value. The location is ideal for a few nights as it is in walking distance from most of the must-see attraction in Istanbul. It is also very close to the light rail and you can go effortlessly and expeditiously everywhere. If you were to stay for a week or so, you may consider other parts of town less touristic. Although my room was a little small, it had everything I needed. It was beautifully and tastefully decorated, with solid wood floors, double panel windows, efficient and quite air conditioning. Great bathroom with bathrobes, wonderful towels, multijets shower and a great spread of toiletries. Everything was spotless clean. The terrace on the seven floor serves as bar and breakfast room. Beautifully decorated with a marine theme. And the view is to dy for... The quality of selection of breakfast was superb, with dozen different cheeses, vegetables, breads, fresh fruit, etc. Although it is in a busy area, the location in a small street, the double glazed windows and thick walls provided perfect quiet. Although some reviewers had concern about service and staff, I found all of them knowledgeable and, in a Turkish way, very kind and helpful. I would not necessarily trust their restaurant recommendation: other than that as great staff as you will find anywhere. My price for a single was less than hundred euros for night: that include taxes, Internet, great breakfast even parking. In my opinion and outstanding value.

author: vvara
title: Great location, otherwise pretty spotty
text: We went to Istanbul on our honeymoon and stayed four nights at Burckin. Over email, they were very nice, promised us a high-floor room with view and an airport pickup. When we arrived in the airport no one was waiting - we called, and Abdul was extremely rude to us, said it was "impossible" that we had been promised a pickup. We actually forwarded him the email we had received (from someone named Hassan) WHILE WE WERE ON THE PHONE and he still refused to send a car, said we would have to discuss it with Hassan. We asked if the hotel would reimburse our taxi and he refused to answer the question, just kept saying it was "impossible" and someone else's problem. When we arrived, after a $20 taxi ride, Abdul said he had spoken to Hassan and that we would get a return airport transfer as compensation. Nevertheless, he didn't apologize and continued to give us dirty looks for four days and put us in the worst room in the hotel - a minuscule low, corner room that was obviously a single. Hassan and everyone else in the hotel were very nice to us. The next day Hassan moved us to a much better room (though still not a high floor). The hotel was very clean and the location is absolutely perfect - a five minute walk from the Blue Mosque, and one block from the Sultanahment tramway stop to go to Beyoglu. The rooftop terrace has spectacular views, and the breakfast they served up there was pretty good - though they could open some more umbrellas, as it was over 90 degrees by 9am and only a few tables were in shade. And even though the breakfast is "included" in room price, if you want a glass of juice you have to pay TWO EUROS extra! The rooms are quite small - though we knew that going in. More problematic, they have no shelves or drawers to put things away, only a small closet. And the bathrooms, while clean, have a lot of broken fixtures - the showers in both rooms were broken, with water flooding the floors and the spray heads not staying upright when put in their brackets; TP holder kept falling off the wall. Small details, but not that hard to fix if the hotel were paying attention. We would have given Burckin a 4-rating, if not for Abdul and his lousy attitude.

author: AhmedD331
title: Not a good choice
text: This hotel is located in a very good area. Very near from Blue Mosque and Aya Sofia. Lobby is narrow but nicely arranged. The room with Balcony is very very small. Extremely narrow and crowded. It is almost occupied by the bed. TV screen is small and was not working. AC is good. Bathroom is not bad. It is not good for a family as every floor is smelly with cigarrettes smell. It was so strong in my room in the sixth floor and my family room in the second floor. We opened the windows and sprayed perfume but the small was so bad. Reception staff was not smiling and tough as if giving orders when talking. Really not professional for this type of service expected from such a hotel. Other staff including administrators where more nice. Breakfast was simple and of limited varieties but was enough. I would not recommend this hotel for family stay and definitely will avoid it next time!

author: tulapa
title: Pleasant Experience
text: Got to know about this hotel via tripadvisor. After reading the reviews, i booked through booking.com. I want to commend the staff for their excellent customer service, they were nery accomodating and nice. my first night was a room on the first floor which was next to street, it was a bit noisy sincy i love to open my windows for fresh air instead of A/C. I complained and it was changed the following day to a better room on another floor. The breakfast was great, but could become boring after a couple of days. I particularly want to thank Ercan who made me a great breakfast despite coming 2 hours after breakfast ended free of charge without requesting for it. Eating at the roof terrace was good. the views were great. The location of this hotel is great, depending on what you came for. It was too close to the the street though. bout never mind, the windows are really good with locking out noise. what else can i say, thanks for the free drinks in your mini bar. i will definetly come back. thanks to you all, God bless

author: helenayusof1601
title: Beautiful Riad But Needs Better Management
text: We stayed for 4 nights. At the beginning it was quite hard to find the place. Spent in the taxi for about an hour and paid 300 DH for it. Few kids showed us direction but had to to pay 50 DH for them. When we got there we were amazed by the authenticity of the Moroccan decorations that they kept. We booked for 4 night but stayed only for 3 nights as we went for a night trip in the desert. The room was cold especially through the night. We couldn't switch off the lights as it would switched off the entire power in the room. So either sleep with a bright room or dark with no power (which mean we couldn't charge our phone or iPad). We were not explained how thing works (lights, shower, safe, door has no lock) On the last night we we told to pay a service charge which was not told at the beginning of the visit. There was not set price for this. They would charge you with whatever suits them. We told them that we would need an early breakfast at 7 as we needed to be at the airport early. Waited for about 20 mins next morning but no signs of anyone. We decided to leave as we have to catch out flight. So we didn't get out last breakfast.

author: 373lynneh
title: Trade description query?
text: We made our booking for this hotel several weeks before our intended visit. My husband and I were on a driving holiday incorporating Morocco and chose this romantic Riad to meet up with friends staying in the city, and spend the new year. Our choice was based on reviews that we had read and that it advertised free parking. How wrong could we be? We made several phone calls (at added expense) to the 'owner' asking for directions, to be told that the signal was too bad and he could not hear us. We had no difficulty making other calls, so assume that this was not down to our phone. We finally gave up by paying a guide (more expense)to direct us. It took approximately two hours from the time of our first call, to the time of arrival, which included finding parking (yet further added cost)which was not available. We then had to make the extensive journey through both the market and the souk. When we presented at Riad Dar Eliane, my husband and I were met by the 'owner' and given tea whilst we admired our luxurious surroundings and made note of the framed reviews scattered around the building. Tea finished, we were then advised that we would not be staying at the Riad of our choice or indeed on our booking, but in one of the owners other properties, we were finally marched back through the Souk to the Riad Oulaya, where we were handed over like some kind of trading commodity. The Riad Oulaya, was a very tired little Riad, not entirely unpleasant, but not quite the luxury we had signed up for. The decor in the room was not dissimilar in style to our orginal choice of Riad, but appeared to be some kind of budget version. I do not wish to be unpleasant about our new host nor the surroundings in which We found ourselves ( after all- where else would one go at 8.30pm on New Years Eve?!) However, a little honesty on behalf of the businesses might have been a more appropriate route to take and most certainly not acceptable practice in the UK With regards to the Riad itself, yes, it was tired and shabby. On the plus side we were served bread, coffee and some of the best orange juice in Marrakesch for breakfast. The Riad served its purpose for 2 of the 3 nights that I had booked for ( I checked out before the third due to my disappointment at the deception) In summary, had we have been advised that our choice of accommodation was fully booked, we would at least have had the option of booking elsewhere. Had we been made aware of the difficulties that we might encounter and the additional costs incurred, we would likely have chosen to spend the money on a hotel and saved ourselves the hassle. All in all, I am aware that I am reviewing a property in which I did not stay, but would like to warn other travellers of the deception that occurs.

author: 7MichaelD7
title: Good location
text: I write this review still as a guest at this hotel. We arrived from our stay at Essaouira on rather cold and rainy day in Marrakech so we were looking forward to getting to the hotel and unwinding. After walking for almost 10 minutes navigating the labyrinth of motorcycles, carts, bicycles we finally arrived at our riad. Our first reaction was mixed as our host Bouchra seemed a little unwelcoming. After the customary mint tea we were shown our room. I was looking forward to seeing the room as I was impressed with a framed article from Vogue with an editorial featuring the Riad. Room - we had a room on the ground floor which which opened out onto the courtyard. The room is long and narrow. The doorway is very low so we had to constantly remember to keep our heads bent to avoid getting a head injury. Lights in the toilet did not turn on. The bed linens looked like they had seen a great deal of use and needed to be thrown away. The hot water from the shower stayed hot for a few minutes and gradually got colder. The courtyard had birds nesting in a tree so we went to bed and woke up with the sound of birds which became annoying. Breakfast is basic. Coffee, breads and jams. The food at the hotel is expensive compared to other restaurants in the main square. Location - the riad is located within about 8 mins walk from the main square. We were provided with a helpful map to direct us to the square. The only redeeming part of this hotel is the roof terrace with views of the atlas mountain and Marrakech. I will definitely avoid this hotel if ever I'm in Marrakech again

author: JessMcP
title: Perfect
text: My boyfriend and I stayed at Riad Dar Elaine for three nights in February. We were unable to find any fault and the whole experience was perfect! We had arranged a transfer from the airport through Dar Elaine which was a smooth and easy way of arrival. Unfortunately we had not yet had a chance to get Moroccan Dirhams and Bouchra kindly had no problem paying for our taxi and porter. We instantly felt welcomed and the mint tea was the best we had in Morocco. Our room was gorgeous and cosy. There was a heater and plenty of blankets. The bed was cosy and we slept extremely well. Dar Elaine provided us with maps and directions, helped us to organise our sahara expedition, arranged taxis and had no problem storing out luggage while we were elsewhere for two nights. Upon arrival John took us around the medina and to the main square ensuring that we got our bearings and would not get lost. They provided number that we could call at any time. The breakfast wa delicious each morning. The terrace was a lovely spot to read a book in the afternoon with a glass of local wine! The riad is peaceful and quiet which is a nice escape from the hectic medina streets below! The service was wonderful and I got the impression that the staff were always willing to help. For example, I washed some clothes in our sink and returned later in the day to find the items had been hung up to dry in the sun, a very thoughtful touch. The location is excellent and very close to the main square. I would highly recommend Dar Elaine to everyone visiting Marrakech as it was an all round wonderful experience which I am unable to fault. Thank you to John, Bouchra and the team for making our stay in Marrakech so memorable!

author: AggieCornwall
title: Well recommended
text: Booked in for 2 nights at the start of our 11 day trip in Morocco. Everything done online and John was most efficient at email contact. A beautiful riad and the food - which we pre-booked - was the best we had in the whole of our trip. He and his team organised Mustafa - guide for the medina. Well worth the 200 MAD per person as we got a lot of information about the people and the place. We would not have found our way around as easily without this orientation tour. Highly recommend this if you are only staying for a night or two. As I said, the food was absolutely wonderful and the chance to unwind with a drink after a long flight was most welcome. Breakfast great - wonderful fresh orange juice and croissants, etc. Rooms are delightful and the roof terrace a great place to unwind. Tip - organise the taxi to riad with John - you will never find it without. The taxi takes you to outskirt of medina [no cars allowed inside]. Then a porter meets you to take you and your bags to the riad. Good map at the riad which is essential! Highly recommended.

author: ShanIn
title: Awful Service, no original features in the house- charmless.
text: We were looking forward to staying in Dar Eliane, having read the wonderful and glowing reviews here. The stay started off on the wrong foot- we were met in D'jaamaa el Fna by a porter- who tipped our backpacks into a cart and pushed it to the street the Riad was on. He then dragged our bags upside down the last ten meters or so to the house. Upon entry we were informed we owed this man 30 dirhams (not much money to us- but it was what we paid for a taxi ride from the station to the middle of the medina, so for a 5 minute walk we felt it was a bit much, especially when you take into account the excellent treatment our things got in the final few meters to the house!) The house itself is utalitarian- clean enough, comfortable enough. But its completely lacking in charm. All the old features- the tiled floors, the fountain in the middle, are now destroyed. You could be anywhere in the world inside this riad- which is sad. It must have once been a beautiful home. The service went further downhill from there. We were told by John (the owner)in his initial email confirming our reservation that he preferred credit card payment. When we asked we were told that the credit card machine did not work and we had to pay by cash. When we asked if we could pay by Euros rather than Pounds- Bouchara tried to cheat us on the exchange rate twice- by converting Pounds to Dirhams at a terrible rate, and then Dirhams to Euros at another terrible rate. We asked to speak to John at this juncture.
