She refused to allow us to (though we said we were happy to call from our mobile and incur the cost) and walked into another room where she threw her calculator against a wall and uttered what sounded to me like expletives. Finally, after the credit card machine began to work miraculously she tried to charge us a 'fee' for using the credit card- According to Bouchara this is common through out Morocco (its not, don't believe her.) We refused to pay this, and ended up paying exactly what we owed and not a single penny more. The house is ok, the rest of the team (Steve etc) were nice enough. But we carried our valuables with us whenever we went out. We didn't feel safe in the house, and we felt like Bouchara was trying to cheat us wherever possible. Not recommended.

author: fredic
title: Very disappointing
text: We arrived in Marrakech after having a fantastic time in Essaouira in a great ryad. We came down to earth with a crash when we got to Dar Eliane. First impressions and the welcome you receive when you first get to a place count for a lot. We were met by a young lady, Bouchra who gave us the impression she was just going through the motions - repeating the information she had done countless times before. We asked about getting to the Menari gardens which were met with a dismissive - get a taxi, we had to probe to find out from where. The second day we got back to the hotel and after sitting in the courtyard realised I could hear other people talking. I checked the details of the ryad our travel agent had given us and realised that there was a roof terrace. Bouchra hadn't shown us that or another lounge area we could use not even told us they were there. The other member of staff we met - Slimane - is a lovely young man - more limited english than Bouchra but always friendly and willing to help. I think your experience of the place may also be influenced by whether you are in a downstairs or upstairs room. We had one of the downstairs ones which opens out to the courtyard. So if you want a window open say to have a shower, if people are outside having their breakfasts , they would hear. The first morning we opened the window by our bed to find another couple having breakfast only yards away. We therefore kept our windows shut but that made the room quite claustrophobic. The bathroom smelled of damp too, We were very disappointed - the place looks so great from the website.

author: Headington_Boy
title: Far from the madding crowd
text: Dar Elaine is a great place and fantastic value for money. It is amazingly tranquil, especially given the hustle and bustle of the city that goes on around it, and the roof terrace is a highlight. We arranged a taxi transfer from the airport via the Riad, and there were no problems with this. It cost us 100 MAD. Be aware, however, that the taxi can only get as far as a nearby square, and then its a 5 minute walk through narrow streets to the Riad with a porter. We ate at the Riad on the first night and the food was great. A few things worth mentioning 1. despite the fact that you are given a map, we got lost on the first moring trying to get to Djemaa el Fna (easily done !), so might be worth asking someone to show you the way first time 2. as previously noted, the staff leave around 9 p.m. The owner (John - quite a character !) said that if we wanted beer or wine in the evening that we could help ourselves from the kitchen and just leave a note so that they could add it to our bill - definitely i good thing if you like a cold one in the evening ! 3. You can settle your bill by credit card or cash, but it seemed like cash was the preferred option. We were also asked to pay a 50% deposit on our first day, but there were no problems with this. There is a cashpoint a few minutes away (next to Cafe Des Epices) and loads down in Djemaa el Fna. Did an excursion out to Imlil with dalilatransports.com which was great and also arranged transport to and from Essaouira with the same company. All in all a great trip ! p.s. one more thing - Preston and Chantelle (from Big Brother, if you are sad enough to know who they are !) stayed here and there is a photo of them up in the dining room !

author: sammikins74
title: It is stunning, welcoming, affordable - and well worth the 'mini-adventure' through the souk to get there.
text: We were in Marrakech for 4 nights and stayed in this riad for the remaining 2 nights as it was not available for the whole 4. Well, what can I say-I think for once I was dumbstruck and just said ' wow ' on first arrival. This stunning riad with it's vibrant colours, fantastic finishing touches of Moroccan artefacts on the wall and welcome atmosphere take your breath away. The riad is in the souks, and I would say the best thing to do is to ask a local how to get there (we ended up paying a local boy the equivalent of a pound to find this gorgeous place-and it's well worth it when you see the maze of souks ahead of you). Once we arrived the hosts couldn't do enough for us, and everything is just so stunning we seemed to take pictures of every corner of the place from the plants, furnishings, ornaments, carved pillars and even the shower! The roof terrace is relaxed and stylish with sunbeds and great views - and so peaceful which is amazing considering how near the bustle of the souks you are. Once you are orientated the riad is easy to find if you get to the small square that is the 'spice market' and then go past the local vegetable market area-I have no sense of direction and even I got the hang of it , and we were only here for 2 nights. The room was gorgeous and had everything we needed. Towels were soft, beds were comfortable and gorgeous, the bathroom was stunning and the breakfast area in the downstairs open-air courtyard was full of stunning architecture and gorgeous touches. I would come here again in a flash. The photos on the website are stunning but still nothing but being here would capture it's beauty and ambience- but it still remains cosy and homely too. The riad is only 10-15mins walk from the main square. I love the hectic atmosphere of the main square and love Moroccan food and enjoy listening to the calls to prayer from all the surrounding mosques, and I also enjoy having fun haggling in the souks. We visited the Marjorelle gardens which are well worth it, as is the museum within it -we took a horse and carriage there on Valentines Day and it was stunning. We shopped in the souks, and had an impromptu drumming lesson in a shop! We ate in the main square at the food stalls that get set up in the evening (the prices are so low it's amazing) and the entire time we were not disapppointed with any food we had anywhere. If the hectic nature of the square or souks gets on top of you then get out to the gardens, the 'new town', or further afield to the waterfalls (Cascades d'Ouzoud) or Essouaira for a day trip. I had been to Marrakech before just briefly and loved it. This trip I discovered a lot more of it, and I feel that this city will have another surprise for me hidden away somewhere each time I visit. I will be back again and again (hopefully to the Dar Eliane), as will my partner who had not visited a place with such a different culture before and he said he 'fell in love' with it.

author: Maybus
title: Cosy base in the heart of the Medina
text: Our stay at Dar Eliane got off to a bit of a rough start, when our flight was delayed. We called ahead when we found out to change the time of our taxi pick up, but when the flight arrival time changed again and we arrived at 4am instead of 6am, there was no way to get a hold of anyone and get in to get some much needed rest. We made our own way to the riad but no one answered the doorbell or the phone. In the end we had to go back to the airport and wait for our designated pick up. Although this change in plan is in no way the riad's fault, it simply isn't like a hotel where you can show up at any hour and get access to your room. Other than this, our stay was truly excellent. The rooms are as beautiful and comfortable as the pictures suggest, with the sunny but cool courtyard a great escape after a busy afternoon in the Medina. I especially loved our room decor and felt it was definitely perfect for a romantic trip with my boyfriend. We especially liked the common room where there was loads of entertainment provided - DVDs, chess, cards, great for those that aren't into being out all hours of the night and would like to retire to the riad and still be able to find entertainment. Because there are only 4 rooms, it also felt very cosy, as you recognized all the guests that were staying there. It can get a little noisy as the riad's rooms are all surrounding the open courtyard, so you can clearly hear other guests' conversations going on, but no one was inconsiderate and everyone quieted down once it got late. We had made note that some reviewers described the location as daunting, and while it is tucked away behind several narrow alleyways, it did not feel any more dangerous than any other part of the city. It also was not hard to get back to the hotel at all, you could not miss it if you came through the souks. Also a good location because of the proxmity to the souks and Jemma El Fna. Badr the hotel manager was also very helpful in arranging tours and making a reservation for us at Chez Ali. Although there did seem to be a lack of communication to us about the details, the plans were always already made after an initial request.

author: Percyhenry
title: Budget Hotel
text: When I read the reviews I thought, yes, this seems good. Easy parking and a bit out of town. I anticipated a slight country feel and a place to exercise our dog. We had read it was not so easy to find, so we did our home work. But even so we thought the Hotel could have helped a bit. When we were on the round about and could see it, they might have put a sign up to indicate which of the exits we needed to take. There were two that were possible. Unfortunately we took the last exit and it was wrong. So we had to double back and go round again. They missed another opportunity to help as there was no sign to say this way, yes, go pass this office building and car park to our Hotel. When we, somewhat gingerly had, we had to tinker around with a key pad to open the automatic barrier. Not that easy and not that welcoming either, and incidentally, necessary as the hotel is not manned by staff after a certain hour and you are given the code to let yourself in and out. I can see I am going on a bit so to be briefer now I will say that this hotel is lacking charm, it is too expensive for the budget type of accommodation it provides. The staff seem to know this and so lack the pride to be charming themselves. They gave us the wi fi code but it didn't work and there was no one to help as the desk was deserted. The grounds were just left like a building sight. It reminded me of a school. But the bed was comfortable. Even so I would not return or recommend it.

author: bc370
title: Short ski break
text: The good 1. location is perfect - right across the road from lifts and ski school including piou piou (quite steep hill tho!). Intersport is next door and esf and ski lift offices are a minute walk. Quite a few restaurants close by too as well as boulangerie. Petit casino is a 5 min walk. 2. Some kids toys available in reception 3. Room was clean and warm. Water was hot but beware no shower curtain! Towels were good. Nice views over the valley (room 26) 4. We checked in around midday which was handy. 5. You can park in a private carpark at the back The not so good 1. Price - When we checked in the lady charged us full price even tho there was a 20% discount due to family week. She explained that when we booked (via booking.com) the offer wasn't on but we didn't pay until the day of arrival so felt a bit cheated. It's quite pricey but then it's in a ski resort and was fully booked... 2. Limited kitchen equipment - no tea pot or cafatiere or cleaning equipment (sponge or tea towel etc) 3. No ski boots in hotel is a bit of a pain (but understandable) as ski lockers are downstairs

author: HilaryfromMonaco
title: Very basic accomodations
text: Positive: very central location, staff (although somewhat inexperienced - or was it just a language barrier - spoke little French, some English) obviously wanting to please. Negative: where do I start... We had a studio and although informed it may not be possible to have a proper bed, it was quite difficult to appreciate the fold-out sofa. Once open, could not move around the room and very uncomfortable. The kitchinette was fonctional but cutlery etc VERY limited. The bathroom was small but worst of all the tiny bathtub which really needs at least a shower curtain (water all the way into the living area every time we took a shower). The biggest inconvenience was that there was absolutely no closet, chest of drawers, or coat hangers.... Absolutely nothing; we had to leave all our clothes in our suitcases! For winter holidays (with parkas etc) a total hassle. Others have stated but worthwhile repeating that the hotel is very badly indicated. We know Valberg very well and therefore had no problem. Someone arriving from elsewhere may certainly have a hard time finding the entrance. Access to the ski lockers is not convenient at all which means everyone trapses through reception - using the one very slow elevator - with ski equipment to get to their lockers. Once in the locker-room, there are no benches making it very difficult to change. The lockers are very small (barely enough space to the ski equipment of one person!). Although most people have breakfast in their apartments, it was nice to have the possibility of having breakfast in the dining room. However, the quality was poor. Typical French continental: coffee/tea, croissants, baguette, orange juice. It would have been nice to have a choice of bread (maybe some wholewheat?) and a basket of fresh fruit...

author: Mashariki
title: A lot of room for improvement!
text: There are only two positive things that can be said about this place: a fairly good location, with easy access to walking routes and a good, easy, free WiFi connection. All the rest needs a serious improvement. There are no signs, apart one tiny logo on the door that this is a hotel. One, looking very bored, receptionist/manager, who is not available during the day. We found the main entrance locked during the day so make sure you take the key with you! The room equipment quite bizarre: for a studio for two people, two plates, two soup bowls, some cuttlery, one frying pan and a saucepan there is a HUGE dishwasher! NO CUPS AND NO KETTLE. A manager, asked for two cups, looked very surprised and suggested drinking coffee from the bowls. Apparently they don't have cups. I didn't use or even see the restaurant but I wonder what they use to serve drinks. Bed comfortable but you need to unfold it yourself from a sofa-bed mode. Bathroom could do with a shower curtain and at least one hook. No hooks in the room so I don't envy the skiers who have to deal with wet ski suits. Quite poor space usage: there is a boiler (quite noisy at times) on a floor level with completely unusable space above! There was no cleaning over the two days I was there, the rubbish was not taken out, the bathroom mat was changed but not the towels. The corridors and the staircase painted gray and very dimly-lit- they don't make the great impression. The hotel is OK for a 2-3 nights stay (in summer) but I wouldn't be rushing back!

author: pigeon33
title: Great place to stay when visiting this area!
text: What's wonderful about The Butterfly Garden Inn is that it's away from the town of Sedona and close to many of the natural areas we wanted to visit. You're just down the street from the trailhead for the popular West Fork Trail and other national forest stops. And it takes only minutes to get to some great trail heads in town if you leave your cabin before 9:00. (Driving home in the afternoon is another matter--lots of afternoon traffic in Sedona.) Our cabin was one of the ones furthest from the road. It was very clean, quiet, quaint, yes, don't expect fancy. We loved it! We like to cook our meals when we travel so a fully equipped kitchen is high on our list. This kitchen had limits, though, as the supplies were minimal--no salt and pepper and not a lot of pots and pans. But when we needed something, they supplied it. We were surprised by the Keurig single cup coffee maker. We came with our own coffee fully prepared to make our own pot of drip coffee each morning. But that was not to be. We got used to the Keurig, and they do give you as many cups as you'd like, but I would have preferred making our own coffee. (Keurig cups are not environmentally friendly, either. A hotel in Phoenix provided biodegradable ones -- with excellent coffee BTW -- and we thought that was great. Maybe Butterfly could do the same?) We had a wonderful time in Sedona and would definitely stay here again! Thank you, Butterfly Inn!

author: BandB-1508
title: Great place, wonderful people, easy access to area
text: This is a cabin experience, not a resort experience, so my rating is in that context. We rented two cabins (3 bedroom + 2 bedroom) for five nights the end of February just after the huge snowstorm. The cabins were cozy. Frank and Kent were very helpful in figuring out what trails were good, given the weather, and all sorts of other advice. There were four of us older adults in the Blue Eyed Sailor (15). Great space. The kitchen worked well (full size fridge and stove, good sized table and counter space, microwave, Keurig coffee maker) though the cooking utensils were a bit sparse. The bedrooms were comfortable though distributing the heat evenly was a bit of a challenge. We liked the third bedroom as a "go to" option when snoring got too much.The gas fireplace was fantastic. Our daughter and her two teenage sons were in a two bedroom (14A Linda). It worked well. We were able to have separate space but could also all hang out in the Blue Eyed Sailor. It was great being off-the-grid in the cabins, yet have the opportunity to hang out in the Lounge with WiFi access to connect as needed. The Lounge is very comfortable. For most of our stay we had the place to ourselves. Great location for access to Sedona and environs, Flagstaff, and the Grand Canyon (an easy day trip). Because of the snow fall, we did not have access to the great spots that are very handy to BGI. The store is well stocked. "Ruby" the espresso machine is brilliant. Easy access to major food stores in Sedona.

author: MarcusStarling
title: People AND Dog-Friendly
text: A coworker had been raving about The Butterfly Garden Inn for months before I finally had a chance to experience it for myself. Ironically, I was there the same weekend as another coworker and her husband but didn’t find out until we returned to work the following week. The fact that all of us thoroughly enjoyed our stay, yet didn’t even run into each other while there, says a few things about the Inn. It is truly cozy and comfortable. Tranquil and serene. You’re surrounded by nature, but for the most part have the amenities of a traditional hotel. And it’s all well-maintained cabins. There’s a grassy courtyard that truly does have an assortment of butterflies milling around. And several of the cabins are dog-friendly, so expect to see a fur baby or two frolicking about as well. Again, didn’t even see my coworker and her husband (and dog) although I was in a cabin not far away with my girlfriend (and her dog). And we’d visited the courtyard several times that weekend, which was directly across from their cabin. Point is, there is a communal sense to the property, yet everyone has a good amount of privacy as well. Also, the communal part is one of the highlights, because it is family-owned and the owners are truly some of the nicest people you’ll ever meet. They are genuinely warm and friendly and, as a special amenity, provide a breakfast basket each morning, discreetly hung right outside each cabin door. Apparently they make the goods themselves, which include yogurt, warm croissants, chocolate chip muffins, boiled eggs, cranberry scones, etc., depending on the day, and even a mason jar of dog biscuits for your furry critter(s). They also have 27 acres of land you can explore, once you cross the road and navigate the rocks and brush along the creek to the north and south. But if you’re not feeling that adventurous, like us, there’s an old-fashioned two-seater swing in the courtyard along with a couple of hammocks, grills, a market and the comfort of your personal cabin to enjoy. At first I was a little put off by how far north the property is from downtown Sedona (about 10 mins). But after getting settled in I soon realized I was enjoying staying at the Inn more than leaving it.

author: 2kwaldo
title: Stopped for Lunch
text: I've been meaning to visit this place for some time and finally made it for lunch with a friend. I had their burger and fries. Very tasty. Fries were excellent. Remember to tell them how you want your burger cooked. They didn't ask, and I was distracted talking to my friend. I typically prefer medium rare and if you don't tell them, they serve the burgers medium well. Who does that? Medium should be the standard. Anyway, the burger was kind of tasty, but a big disappointment as it was over cooked. I can't blame them, but make sure to tell them. The seating outside faces the roadway. Hard to call it a highway, but it is only one of two ways to get to and from Flagstaff to Sedona, so it is busy. Still it was relaxing and I highly recommend a stop here. The cabins are all behind the lobby/store/restaurant so would guess it is quiet back there in the pines. I only gave a 3 for service because they didn't ask how I wanted my burger done. That is a standard question in food service. But they were very nice.

author: hippiegran
title: Amazing & peaceful
text: The Butterfly Inn is the perfect place for relaxation, beauty, rest and food. The cabins are so quaint and decorated so nicely. There is a old timer fire place that goes on when the heater kicks on. The kitchen area is perfect and I am telling you- those beds are ultra comfortable. Breakfast is delivered to your door each morning and it is a continental homemade delicious pastries and fresh fruit,. There is also an excellent restaurant if you want a hearty breakfast or you can cook your own. The owners own property across the street that you can hike on. I loved the stream and running water. The grounds are very pretty. The owners are so delightful. They are kind, giving , loving people who really want to make your stay heAvenly. You just love them instantly. Browse the gift shop and they have local items to sell. I loved the soap and body lotion. Do not leave without buying them. I could go on & on but really you must take the opportunity to stay here. You will keep coming back to this magical place. I know I will.

author: kathryna640
title: Nice get away
text: We stayed here for two nights, we were in cabin 17 Cabbage White. For us this Cabin was perfect we had two adults and three kids. ( It's a big 2 bedroom. )There is a playscape located right next to the cabin, although the kids had a blast just playing around the cabin. Our Cabin also had a Propane grill which was great to make dinner on. There is NO tv, air conditioning or cell service here, the owners do have a telephone booth on the property that you can use to call anywhere in the US if need be. You can go to the main lounge on the property to access internet if need be, or to borrow a book or board game. If you get too warm in your Cabin you can sit outside in one of the chairs or the hammocks. The owners are super nice and you can tell they love what they do! They have thought about everything. Each morning the breakfast basket that they deliver to your door has plenty of Yummy food, I found that I could not wait to see what was going to be for breakfast :). There is a great creek across the main road if you bring your swimsuit. You will need to traverse some of the landscape to get there. The store that's located on the property really does sell everything. We will have to go back and visit in the winter months :)

author: BrassNuck
title: Peaceful spot in Oak Creek
text: First of all, Frank was a very pleasant, accommodating host. If you are looking at cabins closer to Sedona in the summer, it is several degrees cooler up here. We slept with our windows open at night and loved the temperature. We spent 2 nights in the Purple King Shoemaker. It was very quiet at the back of the property. The king-sized bed was very comfortable, and we are older folks, so that is important to us. The bathroom is small, but was quite adequate for our needs. The linens of both were very nice. The living area has a coffee table that doesn't show up in the pictures and a Keurig coffee maker. There's also a small refrigerator with wine glasses, water glasses, coffee cups, and a corkscrew on top. If we had been staying longer, a cabin with a kitchen would have been nice. Since we are early risers, we were sitting out in the adirondack chairs reading the first morning when Frank delivered our breakfast. It consisted of delicious warm cheesy biscuits, yogurt, homemade granola, fresh fruit, and juice. It arrives at your door before 7 AM. While we were here, we ate all of our meals from their cafe; everything was delicious and the portions were generous. We even bought some of the wonderful fresh-baked cookies to bring home with us. The setting and grounds are very nice. We liked the location because we could walk across the road and swim in deep (cool) pools in Oak Creek. The West Fork hiking trail is just about a mile down the road, and that is a beautiful hike.

author: lksully
title: Wonderful Retreat
text: A breath of fresh air! Stayed recently with our family of five... 2 adults, 16, 15 & 11 yr. old kids. Wanted to get away for a few days and escape the Phoenix summer heat and this was just the place. Well appointed cabins with kitchen, 3 bedrooms and double beds in each. Nice mattress and bedding. One bathroom which was a decent size. The best part was the breakfast basket that was delivered each morning to our cabin. Wonderful pastries, yogurt, fruit, etc. More than enough food for our family! Wifi and TV available in the lounge area, an area off the office. Though loved that we did not watch TV! Excellent food at the restaurant! The marketplace is SO convenient and serves cappuccinos and lattes. In order to get to the creek you have to cross 89A which was not difficult. Honestly would have preferred to be creek side but wasn't a deterrent. Property is well maintained and loved. Very friendly owners and staff. Very close to Slide Rock State Park and just North of Sedona to escape the bustling tourist shops.

author: nb147c
title: WOW!!! The best place I have EVER stayed at!!! Must book now
text: I so lucked out when booking this beautiful spot. It was booked online so I thought I would call and double check. Frank got back with me shortly and told me he had 1 cabin available so I booked it! We hurried from Mesa to Sedona excited about our spur of the moment trip. Upon arriving we were welcomed graciously and given detailed instructions about our stay. We then headed to our adorable cabin which was all ready for us. It was absolutely the neatest little cabin I have ever been in. with a little kitchen, fireplace, puzzles, books, etc. We met some of our neighbors and ended up playing dominoes all night which was so fun. The next morning I went on the deck to find a basket hanging, I looked inside to find a homemade breakfast. Fresh homemade yogurt with granola, fresh fruit, homemade cheesy onion biscuit, muffins, and fresh juice!!! This made our day! The owners were beyond fabulous! The cabin was incredible. I want to come every month and I think I will, this place has become our home away from home!!! Thanks so much for an amazing trip!

author: Ge0rgeaT
title: Tranquility nestled in the pines.
text: The Butterfly Garden Inn is the most peaceful place I have ever stayed. Frank graciously checked us in and showed us exactly where to go and filled us in on breakfast delivery. We filled up on midnight snacks in the general store which has just about everything you would need. Walking into the cabin is like coming home from a long trip. It's calm and cozy. We stayed in the two bedroom Monarch Cabin #8. The cabin had a sofa, coffee table, fireplace, dining table, full kitchen, and more importantly a Kuerig coffee brewer. The dining table was fully set and had a welcome note. With three beds there was plenty of room for my two teens and my husband and I. The beds and pillows were very comfortable. My favorite part of our stay was the breakfast basket that was delivered to our cabin. It was full goodies including fresh fruit, yogurt, granola, milk, cereal, muffins, biscuits, apple juice, and orange juice. While enjoying breakfast you can hear the birds chirping and the wind in the trees but what you can't hear is people stomping down the hall, doors slamming, or traffic like you would at a normal hotel. The Garrisons do such a great job of making you feel welcome and at home. There is so much more to the Butterfly Garden Inn such as the lounge area where you can relax and read or play a board game, the cafe where you can get real homecooked food, and the creek that is just across the street. We only had one night to stay but I have already started planning a return trip. The Butterfly Garden Inn will become a family tradition for us.

author: raingurl
title: Amazing Destination Wedding Venue
text: My new wife and I were married @ The Butterfly Garden in last weekend and it couldn't have been anymore perfect. We chose to get married at The Butterfly Garden Inn because of the fantastic experience we'd had with family two years previously. Choosing to have a destination wedding was a bit scary but proprietors Frank and Nichole made the experience worry-free. There were always on-hand for phone calls, emails and an in-person visit to plan. From the moment we arrived, we knew the experience had begun. The came out to greet us with hugs and had a Congratulations notice posted at the front desk. When we checked into our cabin the Cuban Crescent) there was a basket with cookies, chocolates and champagne, along with a card from the staff. Each morning, we woke up to a basket of wonderful breakfast items like croissants, scones, yogurt and granola, etc. - something they provide to all guests, not just those getting married! Between family and friends we rented 6 cabins and and said our vows on the lawn under the pine trees and mountainside with the carriage house from 1890 as our back drop. After the wedding, we headed to the Canyon Room for our reception where Frank and the staff had prepared a Mexican food fiesta with absolutely delicious enchiladas, quesadillas, chips and guacamole, and an awesome taco bar for 30 of our closest family and friends. Not a rubber chicken dinner in sight. After the wedding, we moved back to the lawn area where brother set up a variety of games for the adults to compete at and the children could use the playground next to it. Our guests were also able to enjoy Sedona, heading off to visit Oak Creek (right at the Inn), Slide Rock Park, and take a Jeep tour of the area. Overall, The Butterfly Garden Inn was the perfect choice for our destination wedding, and we're already planning our first anniversary party there!

author: wilburismycat
title: Weekend Getaway
text: 4 of us stayed at the Butterfly Garden Inn in June of 2014. It was such a quaint little place to stay. The cabins are adorable and actually quite private. We loved bbqing and sitting in the Adirondack chairs in the evening. Popular Slide Rock was closed due to the fire that had taken over a weeks prior, however we walked across the street to the water and had a little fun. the water was COLD but refreshing and very clear. The restaurant on site was very good and reasonable. Also the coffee was delicious. Perhaps the best thing was the special basket of goodies that is left by your door every morning. What a treat! The only items of complaint were 1. the beds are ROCK hard. and 2. the sitting area is extremely small and we all 4 were a little cramped. Minor things but something you should be aware of. We would love to come back and spend a few more nights!

author: JohnM708
title: An Absolute Gem in Red Rock country
text: We spent a lovely, snowy New Year's Eve in beautiful Oak Creek Canyon. The setting was wonderfully enhanced by our choice of The Butterfly Garden Inn to spend two nights. The inn is a set of carefully restored and nicely spaced apart cabins. Our cabin was a cozy one room with a gas fireplace providing warmth and a romantic glow. The cabin was tastefully decorated with Warren Kimble prints and rustic furnishings. The bed was as comfortable as sleeping on a cloud. However the highlight has to be the freshly made continental breakfast, left on a hook on the porch of the cabin, in a picnic basket each morning around 7. We enjoyed savory scones, fresh apple turnovers, homemade granola and bowls of fresh fruit. What a treat! There is a small store onsite with everything from the usual necessities through to a nice selection of wine and Arizona crafts. They also sport a nice cafe and coffee service. Frank and Nicole, our innkeepers (and bakers :)), were gracious to a fault. When we arrived late in the afternoon on New Year's Eve, a bit worn out from our flight from California and the subsequent drive from Phoenix, and facing the prospect of a late dinner reservation in Sedona, Frank was quick to help us find a fine meal just down the road from his inn. They were there to help with suggestions and answers to any of our questions. Our trip to the Red Rock Country and Oak Creek Canyon was very much a last minute, spontaneous choice. We cannot believe our good fortune in finding The Butterfly Garden Inn. We cannot wait to return.

author: HRKCI
title: Beautiful Cabins and Owners Wanting to Make Your Stay Perfect
text: Eighteen months ago, I booked 3 cabins for a small reunion group. The Garrisons, a young, energetic, married couple from day one only wanted to make our stay perfect. They understood changes in the reservations over the past few months and asked repeatedly if we had any special needs, including dietary restrictions and/or allergies. One of our group has significant medical needs requiring dietary restrictions. Since they provide homemade daily breakfast baskets, they immediately responded to my request on behalf of this individual. When she cancelled in the last 24 hours, they understood, even though they had already made the dietary arrangement! The cabins are immaculate, updated with comfortable and attractive linens, dishes and an overall attractive appearance. The grounds are beautiful and well maintained. Cabins have outside sitting areas, picnic tables and gas barbecues. The breakfast baskets are fresh, hot, yummy and more than plentiful! Couldn't wait to see what was in them and they did vary over the 2 days. The store/cafe on the property has everything you might need or just want. We cooked both nights as we didn't want to leave such a comfy, cozy environment. Lunch was bought from the cafe and was delicious with reasonable prices. My reunion group (from Portland, Oregon, Seattle, Washington, Houston, Texas and Washington, DC) could not stop raving about the arrangements I had made. They loved the Butterfly Garden Inn. Lastly, Frank Garrison couldn't have been more helpful in guiding us to the right time to hike the most spectacular hiking trail a mile from the cabins called West Fork. The parking lot fills early and quickly. With his guidance, we got parking spaces before the lot filled. Since I returned yesterday, I have been recommending the Butterfly Garden Inn to everyone I see!

author: TravelMawith2kids
title: Home away from home! Great for families of all ages.
text: Our family of five stayed in a two bedroom that was situated under the pines all alone near the playground. The master bedroom was huge with a king size bed and a gas burning stove for chilly nights. We loved it, it was soo peaceful and the young couple was great and informative. We were about 15 minutes from Sedona, which was nice to get away from the hustle and bustle of the tourist area. Each morning we were greated by a Yogi the Bear type basket of breakfast goodies! We never had to go out and pay for breakfast. It was jam packed with fresh pastries, fruit, juice, cereal and yogurt. Most morning we had left overs for treats in the afternoon. There is a full kitchen with basic utensils for cooking a full meal. There are hiking trails with a stream right behind the cabins. It was affordable and a wonderful trip for my nature loving kids (14&12) and the playground worked well for my 13 month old niece. **** If you get the tourist coupon book, there is a coupon in it for 15% off your stay. The owners honored the coupon eventhough I hadn't purchased it until after I arrived. The coupon saved me $150!!! Wonderful experience, would stay again!

author: 4forMelissaC
title: "mom" camping!
text: This place was wonderful! Very clean and I am a huge clean freak! The grounds were beautiful. The creek across the road was picturesque and fun to explore with the kids. We have 4 children (1,3,5 & 7) and we felt right at home. Breakfast in the morning was wonderful. Our first morning there we requested that our breakfast be "to go", it was perfect for driving! The cranberry orange scones were the best I have ever had. I wanted to buy more the next day, but they were all out, no surprise there!! The cabin was romantic and family friendly at the same time. My husband and I woke up to look out our window at the rock wall of the canyon, it was beautiful! Second morning breakfast was again great, from the adorable picnic basket left by the door! I could only find two caveats, first is there is no A/C, which usually isn't a problem unless its a little too warm. Half way through the night, if you leave the windows open, it cools down. Which brings me to #2, security. There isn't any so guests are free to come and go as the please, but so is anyone else. We didn't have any issues.

author: Desert_Kat
title: This place does it RIGHT!
text: This place just does everything right. I don’t have a single complaint, to be honest...and that's a first. My husband and I wanted a quiet get-away for a few days this past December before the holidays and after some searching found this lovely place in Oak Creek Canyon. The property is charming, not-too-rustic, but still gives you that "in the woods" feeling as each cabin is separate and nestled among the grounds. Very private, but only a minute or two walk to the main lobby/office and on-site general store. Property is well located along the highway, and only about a 10 minute drive into the main town of Sedona. Owners Frank and Nicole are the most gracious hosts - accommodations were made for our late arrival and they even planned a special surprise for our anniversary - how thoughtful. Their hospitality and attention to detail as business owners really makes a difference. We stayed in the "Aaron's Skipper" cabin, however as we walked around the grounds, we didn't think there was a bad one we could have stayed in. They all seemed great and well-located. Some awesome things to mention: - Daily breakfast provided via picnic basket at your door! Expect yummy and FRESH foods. - Cabin stayed nice and warm even when it was snowing outside! - Property IS plowed during snow season - The hot apple cider they make/serve at their store is amazing! My husband and I have been searching for a place to call "ours" for when we want to get away, and The Butterfly Garden Inn has met what we are looking for. We have nothing but positive memories from our stay here and really can't wait to stay here again this fall/winter.

author: 582charmaineb
title: Absolutely Lovely in Every Way
text: My family of five (inc. kids aged 3, 6 and 9) stayed in the Sonoran Blue cabin no. 6, and traveled with another family of five (inc. kids aged 5, 9 and 12), who stayed in cabin no. 8, for a two day stay at the Butterfly Garden Inn after a three-day railway tour of the Grand Canyon. Spending time at the cabins and on the grounds of this lovely place was such a relaxing way to end our vacation. The weather fluctuated, but was nice enough to take advantage of the gas grills and eat outside both nights and make full use of the picnic tables, which seem to be a feature of every cabin on the premises. During our stay it was sunny and breezy, in the high 70's low 80's. At night the temps dropped to the high 30s and low 40s, so we loved the thermostat controlled fireplaces. On the day we checked out the weather plunged into the 30's, and it snowed! The cabins were exactly what I pictured and wanted: cozy, clean, comfortable, slightly rustic, very charming, no televisions and hardly any mobile service (there is free wifi, which works better the closer you get to the lobby and lounge). We spent most of one day across the road wading in the creek, and also spent some time in Sedona looking around. We otherwise took advantage of the playground and the decent selection of card and board games from the lounge. The proprietors are wonderful and friendly. My children are peanut and tree nut allergic, and I was super impressed with the way our hosts accommodated us. The really lovely breakfast basket we found outside our front door each morning was full of plentiful, carefully packaged, peanut and tree nut free homemade items. I can't imagine returning to Sedona and staying anywhere else. Highly recommend, particularly if you are looking for a cozy and personal resort alternative.

author: RiteshB_11
title: Fantastic place to stay.
text: My wife and I stayed here for a weekend getaway. We had a great time and enjoyed our stay very much. The owners are very nice and run a great Inn. We stayed in cabin #16. It was very cozy. The full kitchen was great. We had most meals at home. The morning breakfast basket was great. My wife doesn't eat eggs and we were given a vegan breakfast baked good with each basket. That was so thoughtful. The grounds were quiet, located in Oak Creek Canyon, in the Coconino National Forest. We were very close to the very popular West Fork Trail head. There is no TV in the cabin. There is a very weak and intermittent cell signal. There is decent Wi-Fi. That was plenty enough tech for us to fit the kind of weekend that we were planning. It's a great place and we would easily come back if we return to Sedona.

author: pawsompooch47
title: Not for everyone
text: I spent three nights here in October in the Painted Lady Cabin. I can see why this would be a great place to stay in the summer to beat the heat of more Southern Arizona. That seems to be the majority of their business, according to the guest book in my cabin. But in October, the temperatures in the mountains are quite cool, dipping into the 30's at night. The cabin has a singular heating unit in the kitchen, which kept the cabin fairly warm, once I figured it out. Except the bathroom, where there is no heat and it was FREEZING. There is a single metal stall shower. The lighting in the kitchen needs improvement. And the refrigerator froze everything. $175 a night is a little steep. The Painted Lady cabin was very close to the cabin above it, and that cabin's picnic table and Adirondack chairs were right outside the bedroom window. I certainly could hear my neighbor's every word as the walls and windows are pretty thin. Also, I was very surprised that so high in the mountains, the traffic noise was loud and the traffic was heavy. Because of the previous great reviews, I had originally booked a nine day stay here, and am very glad I chose to move down into the town of Sedona after three days. According to my car thermometer there is a 20 degree difference in air temperature when you get down into town and I was toasty warm the rest of the trip, and had cell phone service and a TV and a gas fireplace and pool and QUIET for less $$$. I think the lack of TV and cell phone at the Butterfly Garden are a novelty, good for busy families and city people who want to get reacquainted without interruption. But I'm from New England, where rustic cabins in the woods are a dime a dozen. I did very much enjoy the breakfast basket. It was like waiting in bed in the morning for Santa to come! And the bed was very comfortable.

author: Loucardsfan
title: Perfection
text: We stayed at the Butterfly Garden Inn for two nights in late September. The setting is absolutely lovely. Our cabin was the Painted Lady was perfect for two people. The place is very comfortable and extremely clean. The breakfast service was a great way to start our mornings. Yogurt, granola, muffins, fresh fruit and juices all brought to our cabin in a lovely picnic basket. Now I know why Yogi always got so excited when he saw one! The grocery was very well stocked and we found everything we needed to make a light supper in our cabin. They even had hiking supplies, toiletries and snacks. I had heard about Franks cookies, so I had to get one. They did not disappoint! At Frank's suggestion we took the hike at the West Fork of Oak Creek. The apple trees were chock full of fruit and we were able to pick a few apples to enjoy after we finished the hike. Beautiful scenery along the way. We started out at about 7:30am and had the place to ourselves, the hike back along the trail later in the morning was a different story, but it was fun to chat with others along the trail. I would and will highly recommend The Butterfly Garden. Nothing fancy about this place but it is absolute perfection.

author: JivaD
title: Fantastic. But don't tell anyone or it'll be spoiled!
text: We had an absolutely delightful experience here. The cabins are basic but lovely. The hosts are tremendously friendly and helpful, and the area is perhaps one of the most beautiful places in United States. I saw another reviewer who said that the breakfast was a little too basic for their tastes. I have to say that our breakfast was perfect. It consisted of fruit, bread, coffee, and juice as well as cereal and milk for the kids. It had just the right mix of carbs and fruit to give us the perfect start for the day of hiking that we had planned. We've stayed at hotels where the "Continental breakfast" left something to be desired, but this breakfast was ideal and it was a true joy to sit outside under the pine trees and munch quietly. The Wi-Fi was a little shaky as one gets away from the lobby, and cellular service is nonexistent. But these two foibles simply add to the perfect disconnected retreat that these cabins provide. The hosts provide a tremendous variety of boardgames which you are welcome to take back to your cabin and play. We selected one and plead with our children. The lack of Internet and cellular enabled us to do this amazing thing called "talking". It was a lot of fun. If you're looking for a perfect getaway that takes you away from all of the distractions of the everyday world and transports you into a beautiful Woodland Garden of Eden, this place is for you.

author: Alchemies65
title: Eden!
text: My beau and I spent five days here, in the Oak Creek Canyon, and absolutely, unequivocably, fell in love with the place! Frank and Nicole (and Gabby!) are superb, top-notch hosts. Their friendly care, easy rapport and welcoming spirit set the tone for us. We stayed in the Cuban Cresent cabin (the best one, I'm certain!) and things could not have been more perfect - cozy, comfortable, and wonderful nesting spot from which to launch out and explore the Canyon and surrounding Sedona area. One of the favourite things about the stay was the morning breakfast basket that was hung outside our door every morning at 7am -- incredibly delicious homemade pastries and breads and fresh fruit, and plenty of it! We loved those morning baskets. And! Be sure to go to the Market store to get your morning coffee. Frank (or Terri!) brew up a mean latte or Americano! Also very cool: they have a love-lock gate for couples who want to commemorate their stay at the BGI - we happily added ours, are delighted to be one of the first locks on the gate! This place is an awesome spot for a romantic getaway! We are definitely planning a trip back to stay -- looking to book during the monsoon season... we want to see the high waters flowing through the Canyon, and do alot more hiking! Cannot recommended the BGI - and Frank and Nicole! - highly enough. Thank you, Frank and Nicole!

author: tekirisma
title: Getaway from your vacation
text: This is a wonderful place to have Two Vacations in One. Located 9 mi. outside Sedona (up Oak Creek Canyon toward Flagstaff) it's quite close to all the attractions of Sedona & environs, but when you're done there for the day, a quick and quite scenic drive later you're out in the woods among the trees where you can grill dinner outside & eat sitting at the picnic table, enjoy the sound of the breeze through the trees while you relax on the oh-so-comfortable Adirondack chairs and enjoy a good book, watch the blue jays, or whatever! So relaxing!!! & a totally different vacation from your time spent "in town". There's a wonderful looking swimming hole( or two!) in Oak Creek located just across the road (& across a small island of land) and a beautiful set of waterfalls there. (Too bad the water was too cold, and the weather not hot enough, to swim in mid-October: but on the other hand, the leaves were just starting to turn beautiful yellow & red!). My cabin #11 was nicely decorated, the king bed very comfortable; the bathroom is very small but very clean & adequate for one's needs. The breakfast, included in the price, is hung in a little basket outside your door each morning and is it DELICIOUS !..... and big, and different every morning. On weekend nights they had a community gathering (of guests) around the campfire at 6pm, but I was always still in town with other plans at that time. There is no TV, phone, (or phone reception),or WiFi in your cabin, , but a very nice large living room area available 24/7 in the lobby building where you can use the computer. There is also a nice little market there where they can 'store' items for you in the refrigerator. I hiked the very popular West Fork Trail (esp. popular at this leaves-turning time of year) which is just 1 mi. up the road. The young owners are extremely friendly and helpful. I would return often but the price is a bit much, even though it was their 'Grand Opening" prices (they just opened in July '12, I think, though their cabins have been there a long time, now freshly refurbished.) I hope they don't raise the prices out of my reach!!!

author: neegmosest
title: Close to St Lazare station
text: Hotel is well located close to St. Lazare station. Walking distance to Galleries Lafayette (15~20mins walk). Rooms are too small, we asked for an xtra bed & then had no place to move around. Breakfast is just ok. They had just the same BF for our 5 days stay (pretty boring). Wifi is complimentary (ask the hotel for password). The hotel helps arrange for any shows or sightseeing you wish for. Paris is well connected by their Metro & hence we never took a taxi. Everything was so reachable. THe hotel is about 45mins from the CDG airport. the hotel has no restaurant of its own, they don't even provide with drinking water (I guess they just want all to have water from the tap). We carried a water bottle from home & kept refilling it. Bottled Water in Paris is so expensive. There are plenty restaurants near St. Lazare station, including Starbucks & several fast food joint incl a Mac D. Food in Paris is expensive - even a burger or a coffee.

author: DebrianTravels
title: Glad I found this hotel!
text: I recently stayed three nights in Paris. I found this hotel by comparing many properties on online booking and review sites. I had heard the horror stories of Parisian hotels. I am glad to say, they do not apply to the ATN. For Paris, the rate was reasonable, the room was small but not so small you could not move. I had a full size bed that was very comfortable. With windows that opened, you could wake to fresh air yet not too much noise from outside. Be advised, the bed is low to the floor, so if you have issues with your knees or getting up from low places, this might not be the best fit for you. The hotel provides WiFi that was great in a city where I had difficulties finding WiFi. The staff was friendly and there is good access to both the Metro (Liege or Saint Lazare stations), RER (Saint Lazare) and regional rail (Saint Lazare). You are only a few blocks north of the Au Printemps department stores and the Paris Opera is a reasonable walk if you want to experience the streets of Paris. The cafe at the corner of Athens and Amsterdam streets is good for a convenient dinner on a sidewalk cafe. I would note that this is not a bustling district late into the evening. For Americans, this might be off-putting but I never felt unsafe and I returned to the hotel late each night, walking from the Saint Lazare metro station. I definitely recommend this property and I would absolutely consider it in the future should I return to Paris!

author: Nadine-blumarine
title: very good hotel!
text: The hotel is disigned for people who want to spend good time in Paris city centre, but not overpaying for location and comfort. Very nice, cozy, comfortable and clean. The place is not noisy. The hotel is quiet and neighbors does not hear each other. The rooms are cozy and nice with unsual color and interior. The windows are big: from the ceiling down to the floor. TV, fridge, bath with shower, very cute glass table and chair. Turquoise walls cheered us up. The hotel located in Paris city centre, 7 min walk from Opera Garnier, 2 min from Sent-Lazar railway station, in quiet bystreet, around the corner from noisy city life. One disadvantage - room service. 1 shower gel for 2 of us. We left tips but no changes. Even went to the reception because we do not have any gel to take a shower. Breakfasts are good, tasty with a good choice: sausages, omelette, porridge, yogurt, buns, croissants, jam, nutella, tea, coffee, orange and grapefruit juices, flakes, 2 kinds of cheese. If I am coming to Paris again, I will stay in ATN hotel. It's nice to see Opera every day.

author: davidSs333
title: Well Presented Budget hotel
text: I choose this hotel originally from great rate that they offered for my quick stopover in Paris. For those who doesn't know, the name ATN actually come from the name of the street which is Rue d'Athens. The hotel close to the main shopping district, I'd say 5-10 minute walk, there's plenty of restaurant close by, and two metro station just on the other block which was Saint Lazare and Europa with 5 minute walking-distance. I would like to highlight the productivity of their staff, and the way they work. I rarely see the staff that work during one shift, the single staff on the desk literally just work. This guy is the multi tasked as a manager, receptionist, and also security. He always act like a security ask question to new person who want to access the lift. The room was small but clean. The bathroom was perfectly comfortable. The ameneties were just lotion, shower gel and shampoo. There are minibar with 4 euro for each item. However, I could recommend you to buy elsewhere, theres plenty supermarket nearby. You can get 1 litter water for 1 euro or less. ATN also offered free wifi internet, ticket code can be obtained from reception, one code valid for one device only, so if you carry your laptop, ipad, smartphone etc, you might need several code. The room hallway can be intimidating if you carry large suitcaseby yourself, some assistance might needed. The lift also could barely fit for three person. However, there a stairs on the side, the hotel only 7-8 story tall, you can access the stairs easily.The last but not least, smoking area is available, little nice patio downstair on the lobby, just walk pass the lift. So my tip would be: Mini bar can be overpriced, Dont forget for one internet code for one device only.

author: PR272
title: Brilliant Marco!
text: We used the hotel for 3 nights. There was a bar area and a great breakfast menu! It was a short walk to the Opera and the big department stores on the Boulevard Haussmann. A nice patisserie was steps away. The bar which is just next to this hotel has a great atmosphere, and great food and drinks for a good price. The staff are lovely too. The room was not as small as some 3 star hotels often are, and the room was absolutely spotless!! The hotel is great money for value! The best part is Marco, on the front desk. He is amazing! He has excellent english, humour and all the knowledge you need if you want to get the most from your trip in Paris. All the staff were friendly and happy to help. The rooms have free wifi, and a free safety deposit box. Well furnished and quaint. Will be booking for more in the years to come! Thanks Marco for all your help! Tips for Paris, get taxi numbers, and preferably a hotel (like this one) which will call a taxi for you. We found it very hard to get taxis .

author: jwylam
title: Good value for cheap but clean, boutique looking hotel in paris!
text: Stayed here for 2 nights with my family, 2 rooms. The twin bed rooms are bigger than the double bed rooms, so we took two twin bed rooms. Size is okay, enough space to open suitcase and theres a small desk for you to work on. Small flat screen tv, underground parking available from hotel with extra cost. Deco of the room is modern-ish . but you can tell from the ceiling that its kind of breaking down. but overall is okay, so despite the ceiling. Hotel is very close to the St. Lazare train station ( which is also where the Metro station is Several pastry and cafe round the corner for breakfast. There's a church near by the hotel but nothing much to see. Pretty convenient and good priced , the only disadvantage is that its not located within walking distance to champs elysee & etc. But by metro its quick. If you are driving there, becareful cause a lot of the roads are only one way, it took us a good 15 mins driving around to find the correct road to get through. Receptionist was really helpful, there's paris map and she was very nice telling us where to go for sightseeing and etc. Internet connection was so-so... signal wasn't too strong, always had to reconnect. Would definately recommend everybody who wishes to spend not too much on hotels but also would like to stay in a nice and safe place. ( oh theres, no deposit in rooms!)

author: murduk
title: Just Excellent
text: This is the first time writing a review. I travel a lot for my work and travel to Ankara frequently to see my kids. I have probably stayed in all high-end hotels in Ankara with my 2 kids. This hotel is so comfortable, since it is a somehow a historic/renovated building, it doesn't feel like a hotel. It's very relaxing. Hotel is all very nicely decorated, rooms are spacious and have a high ceiling. I booked the breakfast included option. Breakfast is open buffet only on Sundays. Which I liked a lot, they serve you a nice breakfast in the restaurant on weekdays. There is a small library inside the hotel with some cool books. I recommend Rahmi Koc's book about his world tour with his sailing boat Nazenin IV. The hotel is next to a museum, which you can enter free without getting outside. Staff was so helpful and nice. Since I was jetlagged I have interacted with both day and night shift staff. They were all so nice, helpful. This is a great hotel.

author: Tedstravelblogs
title: A modern Ottoman caravanserai
text: This is a premium hotel located in the heart of historic Ankara. On first arrival it seems more like a misplaced African hunting lodge than a 400 year-old Ottoman caravanserai, but then the Empire did reach into Africa in its heyday. Whatever, the hotel has been immaculately restored and very tastefully decorated with plenty of character – be it Out of Africa or Silk Road. This is a very good hotel which would be excellent save for a few easily-remedied flaws. The good: Comfortable, stylishly decorated and reasonably spacious guest rooms. The same can be said of the bathroom. Everything expected of premium lodgings was provided and it mostly worked as expected. Everything worth seeing in old Ankara is within a short walk or a very short ride. Included parking at the front of the property. The included wifi worked fine on our devices. The TV has a few English language channels – mostly news. The agreeable hotel restaurant is in the adjoining Rahmi M Koҫ Museum (a 500 year-old caravanserai - Ҫengelhan) where you can dine amongst the exhibits. Breakfast is a very pleasant a la carte affair taken in the delightful roofed-over courtyard under the vacant gaze of a collection of mounted animal heads. The not so good: In our room the very functional work desk had but one power outlet anywhere nearby and it was already occupied by the light – doh! The rainfall showerhead was defective and was more like a waterfall which rendered it irritating rather than comfortable – inexcusable in a hotel of this standard. Front desk and breakfast service is efficient but a little peremptory. No fault of the hotel but if you are driving here the roads in the heart of historic Ankara were laid down at least a millennium before the well-laid-out modern city so be prepared. We’d come back.

author: lchellingworth
title: A really nice hotel...shame it was so empty.
text: We stayed here for two nights. We were given Room 205, a lovely corner room with views over Ankara and the museum building site next door. The noise from the construction did not greatly trouble us as it started after we awoke. The double glazing helped too. The room was a good size with a sofa seating area, large and well appointed bathroom, coffee and tea making facilities. There isn't a fridge with mini bar but there is room service if required. The bed was comfortable with excellent linen and pillows. Although we did see one other guest at breakfast on our second morning, it did feel like we had the hotel to ourselves most of the time. This is a shame as it is a really lovely hotel in a good location for sight seeing. We walked down to the wonderful Museum of Anatolian Civilisation and then took a taxi to the Ataturk Mausoleum. The taxi ride cost a reasonable 15 YTL. The Ankara Citadel is opposite the hotel and like many ruins in Turkey, needs some love and attention. Some of the houses within the castle walls are being restored but the ruins themselves need some sign posts so you understand what you're looking at. We would certainly recommend the hotel if you are visiting Ankara for sightseeing or business. The breakfast was excellent, the public areas beautifully done and the service excellent. The staff do speak some English but perhaps not as proficient as staff we have encountered at large hotels in Istanbul. We will have to practice our Turkish! Highly recommended.

author: Magalan100
title: Very Disappointing
text: The building is beautiful and has been fully restored to well beyond its former glory, but the level of service in the hotel falls way below that expected after reading reviews. Firstly we had booked a transfer from the airport to the hotel and it had been confirmed by email, sadly the taxi did not arrive, after waiting for 30 minutes we telephoned the hotel and were told that they would send one and it would be about 40 minutes, we told them to forget it and we took a taxi from the taxi rank at the airport. On arrival at the hotel they did apologise and offered to pay the fare we said no but you can do the return trip when we leave. They said they would send complimentary wine and fruit to our room immediately, and the time is now 16.30, but by 19.30 as we were leaving to go out to eat we asked if the wine was really going to arrive and were told yes; it was in the room when we came back at 21.30. It is mainly housekeeping that is letting the hotel down for instance we used the wine glasses in our room the first night and left the next morning early to go sight seeing, on our return to our room at 15.00 the room had not been cleaned, so we asked front of house if this could be done. When we left for our evening meal the room had still not been cleaned, but when we returned at 21.00 it had been cleaned, but the dirty glasses were still there, and the coffee machine had not been emptied. 48 hours later and after another cleaning team had been in the dirty glasses still remained in the room, we went into the resturant asked staff to come to the room and take them away. There was a large stain on the carpet in our room (The Colonial Suite), we asked for a topsheet for the bed instead of the duvet - this never happened despite several requests. The toilet seat was broken when we arrived we asked for it to be mended or replaced and we were told it would be done when we left the hotel in 5 days time, we asked to change room and were told they could only offer us a lower grade room. After asking every day about the toilet seat, it was replaced on the third day . There is no fridge in the room so it is impossible to keep water or drinks cold, it would not be acceptable in the heat of summer. The tablecloths on the breakfast tables are well past their best and many have holes over which staff try to place baskets of (dead) plants top to hide the holes.. These dead plants are removed everyday and put back the next morning, why would you even bother with the dying plants - throw them out. There is massive construction work next door which will continue for some time, so you will be woken up early with drilling and do not expect to take a nap in the afternoon as it is impossible with the noise. The lack of English we did not find a problem because you can always find a way to make yourself understood, but the lack of professional service is unacceptable in 2013. They have a pillow menu, what a brilliant idea but before this hotel gets to that level it has to get the basics right please, as you have a beautiful building that the staff and systems are letting down.

author: MarkusW220
title: Beautiful Hotel - Excellent service!
text: We just came back from a long weekend in Ankara. We were there for a wedding and booked the hotel based on the excellent reviews it got on tripadvisor. I am happy to say that the reviews were spot on. The hotel is beautiful! Its is located right in front of the historic Ankara castle, with small antique stores and bazar streets just around the corner. The area around the hotel is obviously going through gentrification right now and one can still find run down houses and bumpy roads. More importantly though, they people are helpful, friendly and nice. We did not have a single negative experience during our 4 day stay and always felt welcomed and safe. A normal taxi drive downtown (e.g. Maltepe, Kicilay, Bahcelevieler) will cost you about 8-12 TL. As we were busy with the wedding during the day/evening we decided to only eat breakfast at the hotel. The food was excellent and it was more than enough. As other reviewers have pointed out the rooms are charming and are equipped with luxurious material. Overall we were nearly a little sad that we did not have more time to spend in the hotel. The most positive experience for me though was the service. People went out of their way to make your stay as pleasant as possible. For example when we left our phone in the cab that drove us to the airport, one call to the hotel was enough to make sure the driver is coming back to the airport with our phone. Again as Dean-Traveller said it is almost worth a flight to Ankara just to stay there.

author: Dean-Traveller
title: History alive, a special experience
text: The renovation of the caravanaserie in the old town of Ankara has been exemplary. Modern amenities blend into the old building in a seamless way. The building is very special and the high service levels contribute to this feeling. Service and attention to detail started at the complimentary airport pick up and continued throughout our stay. The caravanaserie is next to the citadel in the old part of Ankera with the old shopping streets next to it and the Museum of Anatolian Life nearby. There are views across the city from this high point. Breakfast is served in the central atrium under a modern roof which protects the ancient structure. It is cool and airy. Food was good and service attentive. Dinner in the brasserie in the adjoining building was of the same high standard. This is within the museum, so you are surrounded by artefacts. Rooms are individually decorated and each has a different theme. There are antiques throughout the hotel including in the rooms. The air on is high tech and excellent. The bathrooms are huge with bath and shower. Linen is luxurious as are the Molten Brown toiletries. It felt a privilege to stay here. We could not believe the value for money. It is almost worth a flight to Ankara just to stay here!

author: azan
title: Unique Experience
text: If you look for a unique hotel experience in Ankara that's the hotel to stay at. Converted from an old caravanserai, it has all modern amenities but also atmosphere of the past time. A lot of care was invested in the design to create a quiet refuge. When I heard that each room has a different theme, I was a bit apprehensive. (I stayed in the Tibetan room.) But it turned out that theme decor was discreet and tasteful. The hotel is located at the entrance to Ankara's miniature Old Town (and several good restaurants) and close to the Museum of Anatolian Civilizations, the only worth seeing in the capitol. The hotel manager Sylwia Dal and her staff couldn't be more helpful. I bugged Ms. Dal about this and that well before my arrival and she would always answer email promptly (she and her staff helped me to get a bus ticket to Cappadocia.) I asked for airport pickup and a driver was waiting for me despite the flight being late. The breakfast is served in a lovely covered inner court. And my only (minor) complaint is related to breakfast - it is not served, it's celebrated as if it was a 5-course dinner. First, the plate of cheese arrives, then coffee or tea, then your order a hot dish from the menu and in between a good looking waitress moves slowly and majestically as a 19tht century steamship on the ocean. And when you want more coffee, you have to ask for it and wait until she sails back to you. Fortunately, there was a Nespresso machine in the room so on the 2nd day I gave up on having coffee with breakfast and had it in the room. But overall, a fantastic hotel!

author: JoParis10
title: What you see is not what you get
text: Last summer I searched for a remote hotel in the heart of the Pyrenees mountains. I came across the website of the hotel Os de Civis which is in Spain, but reachable only via Andorra and all seamed perfectly allied which what I was looking for. I was a bit surprised by the price which seamed very reasonable for such a good place, all seamed perfect in the start and I was not requested to give any more detail of credit card nor anything else but my name... We reached in the summer, had spent already some days on the french side in a charming small village in the mountains, with only 11 permanent inhabitants and beautiful, traditional houses and I was looking forward to the lovely trekking tours which I found online in and around Andorra... Already when crossing the border from France to Andorra I was shocked to see that this small country is more of a shopping paradise in the middle of the mountains where you get cheap cigarettes, alcohol and petrol at each corner of the road and in monster buildings... Reaching finally the road to Os de Civis which is supposed to be very remote, we followed a huge bus and about 3 huge tourist buses were coming our way... we reached the hotel with it's enormous parking, the large tourist shop inside... so I understood that the photos of the website were so well taken, that you surely did not suspect any of that.... Os de Civis is maybe a charming old village, but nothing like the beautiful remote place calm and peaceful I was looking for and expected by reading the website of the hotel. After a quick tour of the hotel and the area we decided not to stay there and it's the first time I stepped out of a hotel without spending the night there, disappointed by the deceiving images of their website. Basically this is the reproach which I have to make to this hotel. Since I did not stay there, I can not tell about the service in the hotel but it's already a deficient service to false the information on what you get in the first place. It still might be the ideal hotel for a large group of 100 people looking for a place to stay all together. But it's certainly not the place if you look for something remote and charming. Andorra and the region in Spain which we drove through is unfortunately devastated by too many monster buildings hoping to attract a large number of tourists in summer and winter. But it creates phantom villages which destroy the natural charm of this region. Much more interesting with historic places and a grown culture is the area of Luchon de Bangneres on the French side a few hours from there, there you'll find more beautiful remote villages which are still alive with an existing culture, beautiful trekking tours.. and great French cuisine!

author: B8206WFjulier
title: Oh dear NO!
text: I have written a lot of reviews and always try to be objective, so here we go; On driving through the village we went past the place, we turned around and as we entered the driveway our first words were “Oh dear NO!” We were greeted nicely and taken to our room- and I have to say that the employed staff - a mother and her daughter - were very nice and friendly and did the best with what they had to work with. The ‘Lodge ‘ room 11, a twin was in reality a run down rotting wooden building. On opening the door there was a musty smell. The furniture was shabby, the divan beds looked like they had been rescued from a refuse skip, with rips and stains. The bedding was white and clean though. The bathroom was tiny, the toilet flushed only when it wanted to and the shower - now this is another story - we were contacted the day before and told that due to a leak in the village the water pressure was very low and the shower would not work. We were given the option to cancel, but at such short notice I could not get anywhere else, so really we had no option. I have since found out that this last minute problem has been going on for about a month! We sought solace in the on site pub and restaurant. It’s tired and shabby too, but as I said, the staff were friendly and the WiFi free. The evening meal was average price but below average quality. A free desert was offered as compensation for having no shower. I didn’t feel safe or secure in the room so slept badly, not helped by noise from the road and the dripping toilet systern. Breakfast is from 8 TIL 9am, except today when she forgot to open the door, leaving us waiting for 10mins in the rain. Breakfast was exactly what we expected by now- dreadful. Cold, cheap. If you are looking at this one, bear in mind our first reaction - “Oh dear NO!”

author: Mrs_D01
title: Cracking stay.!
text: My hubby n 2 friends stayed here for one Saturday night after running a section of the West Highland Way. Ok let's get the basics out the way.. It could do with a lick of paint and a bit of tlc but it has as accommodation everything you need/want. After mailing to see if an early check in was possible, a prompt response informed me that it should be no problem. As it turned out we got 1 but that was fine as we had some runners still out so getting one later turned out ok. So after getting warmed we headed to the bar with the intention of chilling out eating early and off to bed after a long day. Boy did that turn out badly! The beer is probably the best pint in Crianlarich and they have a good selection. A mini pub crawl later we were back at the lodge for something to eat. Cullen skink and haggis was lovely. A game of killer on the pool table we retired to the bar for a final drink at about 8ish before bed. Cue resident entertainment in the form of the chef and a guy who could only be described as Billy Connellys dad had us n most of the bar up dancing n singing to traditional Scottish songs and stuff from the 60s So much for the early night! Eventually packing up at 11pm we trundled back to the room. Back at 8.30 for a cracking brekkie with as much tea n toast as you can shake a stick at. So as a final word would I stay here again? You bet! Next time I'll take my own maracas

author: HBomb1
title: Friendly staff, good food but better showers required
text: The perfect stop for walkers, bikers, cyclists and travellers on route to wherever. Not where you would choose to stay for a longer holiday. Good position on the main road (South) out of Crianlarich. We stayed in the lodges which were acceptable but in need of a bit of a clean up and revamp. Each had a nice porch, which was great for sitting out on and for bikes, but the rooms were a bit tired and smelt of too many wet clothes dried indoors. i.e a bit damp. Bed was quite comfortable and there wasn't much noise from around or next door. Don't expect fridge, hairdryer etc but there is a kettle and tea/coffee making facilities. Shower room was a weak point. Accepting issues with water pressure etc most people staying here are likely to need/want a good wash/shower at the end of a tough day walking or travelling. Our shower room was tiny, a bit grubby, the shower pathetic and the experience would be almost unpleasant if it wasn't for the pure need at the end of a long day. Bar and restaurant were fine. Service pretty good, staff friendly and the menu traditional but varied. Fish and chips, Lamb Shanks, Fish Pie, sticky toffee pudding, burgers.. etc Breakfast was excellent. Cereals, juice and traditional fry but the staff made up toasted bacon sandwiches on request (and for takeaway) which were great. We would stay again though.

author: mairim886
title: Mistake by management, please leave.
text: My friend and myself stayed here at the begining of June. We had booked to stay 3 nights from the 1st to 3rd June. When we arrived we decided to have dinner in the restuarant, The dish I had was good but my friend's was of poor quailty. We were asked to move to the bar to finish our drinks immidately after our meal. A table of German and Canadian tourists were still eating when they were asked to move. We had been told there would be music on the 1st night there wasn't(musician tuned up stayed 10 minutes at most and left) 2nd night we knew there would be no music.We were in the middle of finishing our drinks when the management started to varnish the tables they said they were 'laid back' but thats rude. It says leave.We had a day trip to Oban (2/6) and had our dinner in Oban came back to the lodge but went to the village for a drink it was ok. We decided to go on another day trip the following day.
