It was an unforgettable experience. Both thumbs up for the braai (barbeque) area. My partner had so much fun doing the braai. Overall I am extremely happy and satisfied with mosaic private sanctuary and that my partner and I had the opportunity to spend a romantic weekend at this venue. In retrospect we wish we could have stayed a bit longer. Thank you to everyone at Mosaic Private Sanctuary! Daniel & Brian

author: hrs5704
title: Relaxing Retreat
text: Just returned from a relaxing stay at Mosaic, and absolutely loved it! The staff was very accommodating and the property is so beautiful. The atmosphere is very peaceful, and there are plenty of activities to keep you busy if you so choose. My favorite was taking quad bikes down to a beautiful secluded beach. My boyfriend and I stayed at one of the self catering cottages for 2 nights and at the lodge for one evening. We had a wonderful experience at both! The cottage was very spacious and equipped with everything we needed and more. The cottages would be a great option for families or for couples wanting a full kitchen and extra space. The lodge was really unforgettable. So tranquil and private. Our room was fantastic and included a large bed, nice porch with a sitting area, mini fridge, huge bath tub, and private outdoor shower. Everything down to the bath products were top notch. The food was really amazing and exceeded our already high expectations. The chef at the lodge is so talented! After returning from a delicious meal, we came back to our room to find the bed turned down and a lovely bath drawn. I can't say enough wonderful things about Mosaic's location, accommodations and staff. Suitable for a romantic couples getaway or a family affair. Would absolutely recommend!

author: CapeTownHasen
title: A true gem
text: We just came back from this most wonderful weekend getaway for a family with kids. We stayed in the milkwood cottage 3, which was perfect for us (2 adults and 3 small kids). The cottage was very spacious and well equipped and very good value for money. A cot for our baby was also provided. After we checked in we had a relaxing picnick by the lagoon (with a delicious cheese, cold meats, olives, homebaked bread etc. platter - also very good value for money as far as I am concerend). The kids could run around freely and climb rocks and trees, they absolutely loved it. In the late afternoon we took a boat-trip onto the lagoon and were spoilt with drinks and snack and the staff was really wonderful and very friendly. Sometime during the day my son spotted the "safari" vehicle and wanted to take a ride, so for the next morning a driver (sorry forgot his name) took us through the reserve onto the beach. The kids climbed the sanddunes and got hot chocolate and biscuits, what a treat! These activities are free for people who stay at the lodge, but understandably we had to pay for them. In the morning we discovered that the gas had run out (no hot water in the shower and no gas in stove) but his was sorted out very efficiently by the staff after we reported it. This morning I got a call from them saying we forgot one of the kids jackets in the cottage and that they will post it to us. How nice is that! On the way out we also had a look at the lodge, which is beautiful as well, not as much free area to run around for the kids as the area by the Spookhuis, but a pool that is heated all year round! The family suit can fit two adults and two kids on matresses as well as a baby in a cot. After seeing the family suite the kids insited, that we should try the lodge next time. We really love this place and will be back with some friends this winter still !

author: bigdadwangchung
title: A Very Special Place
text: We stayed at Mosaic Sanctuary for 3 days 2 nights last week. It is a very special place. First, the drive down the coast to get there is an indication of what you will find. Beautiful mountains on one side and gorgeous untouched beach on the other. Mosaic in nestled in the bush with a lagoon and the mountains as the back drop. As for the service and meals they were super. The food prepared by Yuri, the chef, shows the feeling he puts into his cooking. Good local dishes complemented with fine South African wine. The Malva pudding was to die for. The service is almost one to one. We were dropped off at the beach and toured the caves and walked 5km on the beach passing 2 fisherman and one other , that was it. We were met by the staff and 4 other guests for sun downer one the beach. The other guests did the Shark cage which they said was awesome. We would like to come back during whale season sometime to relax and enjoy. The accommodations were excellent and the outdoor shower refreshing. All of our need were attended to. Oh. The Spook House. What a beautiful renovation by the owner and serving wonderful lunch outside watching the unique birds.

author: 3sisters3
title: Paradise in every way.
text: My family stayed here for a night before Christmas. The location was easy to find and the road easily navigable in an ordinary car. On arrival our breath was taken away by the view and peace and quiet and everyone was extremely welcoming. The main area is charming and wooden with thatched roof, full of character and in keeping with the local area. Of all the hotels we stayed at in South Africa the attention to detail in the bedrooms and bathrooms was the best. Shawls for cold evenings, swimming towels, night lights by the huge bath, flowers on the basin, powerful and hot outside shower....all done with huge thought and planning. The staff were all delightful and helpful. Johann took us down to the dunes in his land rover and was extremely knowledgeable and amusing about the plant and wildlife en route. It was a fabulous way to see the sunset sitting on the beach with a glass of wine watching the seals. We could only imagine how spectacular it must be in whale season. Once back at the lodge Jurie had prepared an amazing dinner for us with many choices and I find it hard to believe an earlier review that the food wasn't up to scratch. For us it was one of the best meals we had in South Africa and prepared with true dedication and skill. Octavio was extremely helpful and interesting and Amber very efficient too. The staff were absolutely top rate and the location, lodge, bedrooms and bathrooms out of this world. There is a super plunge pool looking out on to the lagoon and a wonderful terrace for breakfast and drinks. We could not fault this lovely place and I would thoroughly recommend it to everyone.

author: Umberto-Huby
title: A perfect oasis to close off a perfect three weeks journey
text: Reaching Mozaic Farm was a bit of a challenge. 7 km of dirt road to finally find an "off-road" which happened to be in a very bad state due to heavy rainfall in the past weeks. However, our hosts picked us up on the road and took us through a parallel improvised off-road to the lodge. The lodge is perfectly built into the landscape: it is 'one with nature'. The cabins stand separately but make a perfect unity with the main building. You smell and sense nature all over the place. From our room (Flycatcher) we had fantastic views on the lagoon with hundreds of flamingos and herons. A wonderful oasis to live from a nice terrace. The room is spacious and very well equipped with bath and outside shower (a great experience !!!). Free WIFI available, which is a bonus! Great dinner next to the fireplace in a cosy restaurant area. The lady of the house allowed us to order a limited edition bottle of wine, which we have highly appreciated!! This lodge does have indeed a famous wine cellar! Breakfast in the same area or outside under the milkwood tree was a nice buffet with english breakfast if wanted. A walk through the fynbos, a tour on the lagoon (not really added value) and a tour by 4x4 through the fynbos and dunes to the ocean were all included. The place has an outside heated pool with lagoon view. This is a perfect place if you look for peace and quiet in a great nature setting. It is less well located if you come to Hermanus for whale watching. It takes you at least 30 minutes driving to reach the Hermanus beachfront.

author: JaredW504
title: Two weeks in an African Paradise
text: If you're looking for somewhere that is both relaxing and full of entertainment and activities then Mosaic Farm is the place to stay. I heard about it from a friend and thought I would give it a try. First off the service was excellent. Everyone there is very kind and helpful, they are more than willing to go out of their way for anything you need. Graeme was the guide for most of the activities and he made sure I had the best experience I could, cheers to him. The lagoon lodge is tucked in some trees and has a beautiful view of the lagoon and the mountains in the background. The rooms were very clean and spacious and I especially liked how the shower was set outside the room (with cover of course) so you could see all the amazing scenery. There are plenty of activities to do as well. I took a quad bike tour in the morning that takes you all around the farm with amazing views and in the evening we took a ride to their beautiful beach (which had some great dunes and the whitest sand I've seen) where we had appetizers and drinks. I would just like to add that we rode a unimog to the beach and if you don't know what that is I'll just say it's one of the COOLEST things I've ever ridden on. You can also rent kayaks and go around the lagoon or take the more relaxing route and take a sunset cruise on the pontoon with food and drinks. If you are a wine connoisseur then you will be more than pleased with the wines Mosaic offers or you can always go to a wine tasting at one of the many vineyards in the area. The cook there is fabulous and the food is very fresh (their vegetables are grown right on the farm), I was never disappointed with a meal. There are a few towns in the area with the closest being Stanford which was only a 10-15 minute drive. It is a very small but cultural town with a grocery store and a few restaurants. Hermanus is the big town you pass through before you get to Mosaic and is only a 30-40 minute drive. There are plenty of places to go there and the night life is fantastic. Gansbaai is the town past Mosaic and there is one main reason I went there: great white shark cage diving. It was one of the best experiences of my life and words can't describe the feelings you have when you're in the cage and maybe a foot away from a great white. I can't thank my friend enough for suggesting Mosaic Farm to me, it was truly the best trip I've ever been on.

author: passportstampjunkie
title: Southern hospitality takes on new meaning at Mosaic Farms
text: We love Mosaic Farms! The setting itself is captivating, especially if you are in to birding. The raised walkway that takes you to your individual bungalow is reminicent of Montana to us, with the gorgeous scenery right outside your door, it really feels like you have the place to yourselves (even if you really do). While we were there, the weather was not very cooperative for outdoor adventures, but we still had a very memorable and wonderful time. Our arrival was greeted with Craig and Warren showing us to our room-with deep soaking tub, outside shower, huge king size mosquito netted bed-and views for ages. We were hustled into the Land Rover for a sundowner out on Walker Bay-even with the 40 knot gales, it was breathtaking. We saw whales very close to shore while dining on fabulous gourmet hours'douvers. Next was dinner in the beautifully restored Spookhuis-if you want a romantic dinner, bring nice clothes, this is the chance! All food is organic, local or grown on the property, Chef Craig comes out and tells you what the entrees are, and everything c'est magnifique. The presentation is style worthy, and the flavors are delectable. We had a great time at dinner, and even saw an Owl on the way home to our cottage. The main room is cozy and wonderful to sit and read in, or look through the telescope at the many birds on the lagoon. The level of care given to preservation of the environment is commendable, as well as the extensive knowledge of the local flora and fauna by Craig. Paula is also extremely hospitable, and we had a wonderful time speaking with her about things to do and see in the region. This is not the touristy area of Hermanus, but 45 mins by car to both Hermanus or Gansbaii, so you can do all the whale watch or shark diving easily from Mosaic. The only difference is, you get to come home and soak in the pool or your own private soaking tub at a 5 star spot! Advice if you are going on a walking tour or hike, would be to bring long pants and socks, as there were quite a few ticks (most likely conditions and season was just right). None of us got bit, they're easy to spot, but just a word of precaution. We highly recommend Mosaic to fellow travelers, and the staff make it what it is-relaxing, fantastic, beautiful, and educational. Thank you to Craig, Chef Craig, Paula, and Warren for making our stay memorable!

author: ChristyLee56
title: Good value for location
text: We picked this place because we were on a tight budget and this place was the closest to the center of town for a reasonable price. It wasn't amazing, but we were happy with it overall. The location was the best thing. From the hotel walking it takes about 15 minutes to get into the center of town. There is a busy and nicely groomed walking area down into town with a great view over the city. Just note however, this part of town including the hotel is on a high hill over the main part of Lyon. To get back to the hotel from town it's a steep uphill climb for about 10 minutes. We are in our 20s though so this was fine for us. The hotel itself was nice enough. The staff was very friendly and spent time giving us directions to various places in town. They were happy to print out directions or maps for us too, which helped a lot. Our first night the room was okay but every time we walked in there was this smell that I can only describe as sewage. The room was clean and there was no obvious source of the smell. When we opened the window and aired it out it was okay, but the smell would come back. Because of this we asked to change rooms the second night, and they were very nice and let us change rooms. That room smelled fine and was a slight upgrade from our previous room. Both nights our window faced the street and had a nice view of Lyon.

author: K9076WEcindyh
title: My expierence
text: when arriving to the hotel we had reservations for a weekend stay. I requested a room on first floor received a room on second. ( no big deal). Walking into my room my coffee pot was dirty my bed spread was dirty with BLOOD stains, and the room smelled like dogs. ( the smell wasn't too big of a deal due to me bringing my 2 small dogs with me). The first night was ok, we swam and just hung out in our room( we had to rotate who went with the kids to swim due to one of my dogs barking when left alone front desk complained so we immediately dealt with it). got up the next morning enjoyed the very good breakfast they offer, left for the wedding. we took the dogs to avoid any issues with the barking. returned to the hotel around 8ish the same night. swam some more and went to sleep it was a long day. that night ( Saturday) i was lucky to get 2 hours of sleep( which was a concern of mine due to the fact i am epileptic). people above us were fighting sounded like a wrestling match i initially woke up thinking some one broke into our room. I informed the front desk Sunday morning on our way to breakfast of the disturbance. while eating breakfast one of the hotel employees came and whispered to my adopted kids about their biological mother.( which was not to be knowledgeable of our location or supposed to have contact with kids) My kids were all confused and scared. I informed the front desk, and until i checked out the worker still circulated the area we were in and glared at us. Never in my life did i think i had to worry about a staff member at the hotel disclosing MY PERSONAL information to others. very VERY DISAPPOINTED i have since then had on going problems due to my personal information being released. tried contacting gm several times in regards to this and now a month later The GM Kathy's way of fixing this is to offer me a free 1 night stay at the hotel! and mind you the employee who violated my AMENDMANT RIGHTS TO PRIVACY AND THE STATE OF OHIO PRIVACY CLAUSE FOR PRIVACY AND PERSONAL INFO IS STILL EMPLOYED!

author: /undefined
title: Such a disappointment!!
text: We were VERY disappointed with the lack of quality customer service. the front desk ladies were rude and inconsiderate & often times not even at the front desk when we had questions. As a matter of fact, the one woman rudely stated that we cannot check in any earlier than the 3:00 time. While I understand this, she made us wait until 5 minutes after 3 to even be willing to check on the availability of our room. She also did this to 2 other customers that we observed while we waited in the lobby area. We were also disappointed in not finding food/restaurant/pizza/tourist attractions in our room & I had to go to the front desk twice to get this info. The lady told me that Country Inn doesn't allow this to be placed in the room. We also were frustrated when there were no tv listings anywhere. We found the pool to be nice & comfortable, however, there weren't any towels any time we went there & since there was no clock, we were rudely told at midnight that it was time to leave. While we gathered our things, the woman very rudely stared at us & continued to tap her foot. However, it was nice to see her bringing towels, which she did not offer to us. Our room was nice & comfortable, except for the bathroom door that was difficult and very loud to open & close. We thoroughly enjoyed the breakfast & the woman tending to it on Sun. morning was friendly, efficient & nice. She and the one cleaning person were the only ones at the hotel with our experience that were friendly and smiled at us. Overall, we did not feel welcome or valued and were highly disappointed in our experience, which is why I stated I would not stay at this hotel again nor recommend it. & when we checked out, the woman didn't even ask about our stay & didn't wish us well.

author: sandrac161
title: Very Nice:)
text: This hotel was a very pleasant surprise! Did not realize we would have a microwave & refrigerator. The beds and pillows in this room are probably the best Ive slept on in a hotel room ever. It was very clean, more towels than usual, and actual name brand products. The hair dryer was great! They had a nice heated indoor pool & hot tub. They also had fitness room but I didn't have time to check it out. Breakfast smelled delicious though we slept so well we missed it lol..I wonder if all Country Inns are like this?? Also many restaurants are right there. They are in the midst of remodeling half of the hotel but was no bother in any way. I know this sounds like a rave and just to assure you, I know nobody connected with this hotel.. I was just so happy with it I wanted to let people know. I always check these reviews and they have many times stopped me from going somewhere based on negative reviews. By the same token I choose my rooms by this so wanted to give this place the 5 stars for my experience:):) Oh, my one small complaint is that they do not have the little area with bars and hangers that every hotel has to hang your clothes on and they do not provide you with a dirty clothes bag which I always use. I really needed it this time as we had wet bathing suits & dirty clothes from exploring Ohio Caverns and parks:)

author: countdowntovacation
title: You can't go wrong with Country Inn and Suites
text: We stayed in room 215 (suite) for one night on our way back to Michigan. The room was $125.00 + tax. There was a sitting area with a couch, high back chair, desk with a chair and a TV. The bedroom had a king size bed and TV. There was a door so that one person could sleep while the other watched TV. The room had a small refrigerator and microwave. There was a one cup coffee maker also. The bathroom was clean. The toilet didn't flush that well. I did inform the girl when we checked out the next morning. The carpet in the sitting area was stained. The bed was very comfy. We had a good night's sleep. If you are a light sleeper this room is not for you. It is at the top of the stairs and you could hear the hotel phone ring. We did not use the pool or fitness room. Breakfast was a standard County Inn & Suites breakfast. The dining area was kept clean.

author: FlabbergastedGuest
title: Bed Bugs
text: Checked in very late with my husband and infant. Paid in cash for the room, service was acceptable but unfortunately not as amazing as Holiday Inn, who was booked solid. Came in the room and the first thing that hit me was the smell of...something. It was supposed to be non-smoking, and didn't smell like smoke, more like a mold or the air conditioner leaked through the carpet. Bathroom was immaculate but the carpet was dirty, as shown by my now-black socks--either way, I find this problem at a lot of hotels. The worst of all this is that I awoke at 6 a.m. with bed bug bites. I have a very specific allergy to them [as known from a previous hotel stay several months ago] where my skin swells in welts where I've been bitten. I did not bring them with me, as the hotel manager, Kathy, attempted to imply--after I stayed at the prior hotel I laundered every item of clothing I have, and steamed even my shoes and luggage, per the advice of the exterminator I called. I was not offered any sort of solution, but was given a story about how they launder all the bedding [including the *down* comforter and *down* pillows--which is highly doubtful] and are checked monthly for them. It could be a housekeeping oversight, or another guest might have recently brought a few with them. I would never ask for a refund, or for my stay to be comped [obviously I was prepared to pay for my stay since I paid upfront in cash] but the fact that she didn't so much as offer to do so was really disheartening. I wont stay here again, or at any other branch of this hotel. Now I have to go through the added time and expense [all while traveling with an infant] of bagging and laundering/steaming my things before I go home. What a shame!

author: lahlah57
title: Home away from home
text: Family from California as well as myself stay here regulary when visiting relatives. It is truly a home away from home. From the time you step into the lobby and see the fireplace glowing to the time whan you leave for the day and the front desk says to have a very nice day. We travel frequently around the world and this is truly a very comfortable establishment! Our favorite was the morning breakfast that no one else can beat for it is included with your stay. It's not dried up danish and maybe a few sad bagels but is well rounded for adults and children as well! A cereal variety, eggs, gravy, bacon, sausage, bagels, danish, belgian waffles that you make, coffees, juices, skim and regular milk, english muffins and regular bread! Condiments that add variety and it is greatly appreciated that they had Sugarfree syrups and a few different sweeteners for the diabetics as well as the weight conscience. What a wonderful way to start the day with a cup of coffee and a newspaper in their quaint dining room. After breakfast in may be necessary to go the the workout room to burn off what was eaten. Elliptical, recumbant bike and treadmill......that work!!!! Imagine that, they work and so does the satellite tv that can be watched while working out! So many places claim they have a gym but half of it does not work. Thy also have an indoor pool and jacuzzi for those who wish to swim. As you can tell, we were impressed! This is and will be our home away from home!!!!

author: SanG778
title: Beyond our expectations!!!
text: My husband and I were on our honeymoon just a week ago. Nice, France was our 5th stop of our very long holiday. We got to Nice from Verona, Italy by train. When we arrive at the train station, we called the hotel to find out the best way to get there. The very kind man on the phone explained to us exactly how to get to the hotel. We had to walk to the tram from the train station which was literally a min walk. We were so glad because all the places we had been visiting, required us to walk quite a bit from the train station, and that was tiring with our luggage etc. It was only a 2 stop tram ride and then a 3 minute walk to the hotel. The hotel is located just a 2 minute walk from the beach, Promenade De Anglais. Restaurants, Cafes, Massena Square and the shopping street is right behind the hotel, barely a walk at all. We were very pleased with the location of the hotel. It is a small hotel, but definitely with big rooms. Our room was spacious and a comfortable size. Plenty of space for our bags and all my shopping! The staff were very friendly and assisted us and told us all the it places to go to. All in all we were very pleased and would definitely stay at this hotel again if we visit Nice in the future.

author: Ross81UK
title: Good room , great location
text: Stayed here for 6 nights very recently. Hotel is located pretty much a block behind Place Massena / Galeries Lafayete, really central and easy to get to - 3 min walk from Alberti bus stop on the 98 airport bus route. Upon arrival we were too early to check in but they were happy to store luggage for us and after we had used the bathroom to freshen up after our flight the guy on reception had a map waiting for us with all the main areas highlighted (although this wasn't our first time in town) - very welcoming! We returned to check in later, this was done in seconds by a friendly lady. Up to the room on the 3rd floor via the stairs (the lift is classic cage style, my partner didn't fancy it - looked a great period feature to me). Wow - our superior room was huge by French hotel standards. Nice fresh furnishings and a huge shower in the clean bathroom (toiletries supplied too). I'm pretty sure the bed was queen size, massive. Big flat screen TV on the wall too - French TV only though. Aircon unit and a fridge as well - everything you need. The room was cleaned daily even weekends and public holidays with fresh towels etc. Staff were very friendly throughout our stay. Check out was even quicker than check in, very efficient. As previous reviews state the walls are pretty thin and we heard ahem ahem 'noises' from the room next door several times but that's hardly the hotel's fault really. So overall - great location, friendly staff and a lovely big room. Putting that all info perspective of the good room rate we got...highly recommended! We may well be back in 2016 or 2017 :-)

author: travellerjim2015
title: Wow. We were impressed.
text: We wanted a short get away to Niagara Pennisula but looking for a change from "cookie cutter" accommodation. This hotel surpasses our expectations. The off season price was very reasonable. The room was large, with high ceilings, two lovely sofas with two very comfortable double beds. Although a bit hard to find the GPS took us right to the front door. We were met by the hostess who personally escorted us to our room. My wife uses a walker so she got her own key for the lift to the second floor. That was very much appreciated. The restaurant is across the street but the street is not busy so getting there is not a problem. If it happens to be raining, the hotel will provide an umberella that you can leave at the restaurant and pick up another one for the return trip. The free parking is close. The free Wi Fi is easy to access and quite fast. I personally enjoyed a soak in the jetted tub after a day of walking around @Niagara On The Lake. Included were passes for complementary wine tasting at local vineyards. (One is right across the street next to the restaurant). We were also given a pass for a cheese tasting at a cheese shop about 1km away. We will be staying there again on our next off season visit to the area.

author: spicemom3
title: Lovely night at the Inn
text: We stayed for a night for our anniversary. We haven't been to Jordan Station for many years. The Inn on the Twenty and the staff were great. We were welcomed genuinely at the front desk and after detailed explanations of the inn and our stay, she waked us up to our suite (nice touch). Suite 17 in the Inn was really nice. A good sized living room with gas fireplace love seat and coffee table & chair...King sized bed with a beautiful arched wall and view of the fireplace. There were beautiful wood beams incorporated into the ceiling, which reminded us of the history of the building and Jordan Station. The large bathroom with a jetted tub and separate shower, were 'traditional' but clean. Nice towels, robes and bath amenities. A very cozy place for a fall getaway. We wandered around in the shops & galleries & did a wine tasting & some shopping across from the Inn. We had dinner at our favorite vineyard restaurant... (a 10 min drive from the Inn) at Vineland Estates Winery. We have never been disappointed there - and the dinner was spectacular as always. The next day we both had massages at the Spa on the Twenty (the spa beside the Inn). We both really enjoyed our deep tissue massages. Sometimes spa massages don't live up to the term "deep tissue" - but these were just what we asked for. We had a perfect quick overnight fall getaway in the lovely, quiet Inn.

author: Rayzor_Sharp_Reviews
title: Wonderful, just wish we had more time.
text: Stayed at this Inn after hearing great things from other couples who had stayed there. There was four of us in total and all of us stayed in the Vintage house. It is separate from the main inn located above the spa. You get your own driveway, own entrance and patio. Its directly next to the inn and across from cave springs winery. While it worked out very well for us two couples this setup might not be for everyone. If you have trouble walking stairs this isn't for you. Once in the door at the ground level you have to walk up about 20 stairs which might be troublesome for older guests or those with ailments. For us it was no problem at all and the couple we were travelling with had no complaints. The setup is at the top of the stairs, one room turns to the left and has a queen size bed, bathroom and view of the street. It also has a door that closes and locks from the stairway. The other room at the top of the stairs is on the right and has a living room seating area with fireplace as well as a fridge with coffee bar and a second bathroom which (on request will be unlocked for use). In the sitting area is a pull out couch which is where my wife and i slept. While the area is cozy the mattress was very uncomfortable. We didn't have high expectations for a pull out couch but it sufficed for one night. If you think this is going to be an issue for you then this might not be the room for you. Over all we enjoyed the inn, the staff had our room ready early for us and the accommodations we lovely. I would recommend this place if you were going winery touring or antiquing in the area. I would recommend two nights however to see all the sights around the surrounding area.

author: Suzie0724
title: Wedding in the vineyard
text: My husband and I got married August 19, 2018 at the Inn on the Twenty and had the ceremony at Cave Springs. Grace was our special events manager and was exceptional. I had so many questions from the time we booked until the wedding date and she answered each and every email quickly. If she was unavailable someone else would respond also very fast. They have a list of recommended vendors and each person we chose was awesome. The Officiant Paul Fletcher from Cathy Davis and Company was fantastic, Tom from Sound Obsession had the guests rocking all night, Shawn from Shawn Taylor Photography stayed with us all day and we are so excited waiting to see the pictures to come, Carol from Vinifera did a lovely job on the flowers. Stacey was the onsite restaurant manager for the day and she was superb. She was like the secret service, always in the background taking care of things and only showed up when needed. She made sure everything was running smoothly so I didn't have to worry. It was the perfect day, perfect weather and perfect venue! If you are thinking of booking here then just do it and you won't be disappointed. We had the windows room for the reception and it was beautiful. We booked it prior to the merger of the Inn and Vintage hotels so it was renovated prior to our wedding and we were so happy to see how beautiful it turned out. Most of our guests said it was the best wedding they have attended and the most beautiful. They also noticed the great service and we all know how important that is. We also had our rehearsal dinner at Jordan House and that was also amazing, wonderful food and service. Many guests were from out of town so we pretty much took over the village for the weekend which made it a lot of fun. We had had breakfast each morning included for guests so it was nice to see everyone each morning. Overall could not be happier with our choice and especially having a dedicated person like Grace helping me every step of the way. Suzette and Allain

author: mjl601
title: Things are changing
text: My husband and I have stayed at the Inn many times over the years - it is a perfect getaway spot within an easy drive of Toronto. Jordan is delightful, Cave Spring winery produces wonderful high-quality wines, the Inn on the Twenty restaurant has a great chef, all the staff are warm and welcoming. We have always enjoyed our stays. However, on our last stay in the first week of January, we learned that the Inn and the restaurant had been acquired by new owners, Vintage Inns. Previously it had all been owned by the family who started Cave Spring. It was a rude surprise to find that while in the past breakfast had always been included, now it no longer was part of the room price. Room prices have not been reduced, btw. Now we were simply informed that the restaurant would be open for breakfast, at a charge of $12 - $20pp. We opted to go elsewhere. I have to wonder if this is not only a move to improve profits on the rooms, but if the breakfast service will be phased out entirely going forward if demand drops - resulting in fewer staff? The restaurant has always focused on well-prepared delicious local ingredients - will this continue? The employees and local people I spoke to admitted to being very nervous about the direction the new owners would be going in. Breakfast may seem like a small matter, but it was part of what made our stays truly feel like a fantastic getaway. Doubts have been raised now. Hoping my fears will be allayed.

author: JAL0001
title: Perfect Getaway!
text: I have stayed at this amazing Inn several times, but have never left a review. This is a fantastic place to stay. The rooms are beautifully decorated, very spacious, and comfortable. The Team that works here go out of their way to make your stay enjoyable and make you feel welcome. They are so engaging and friendly. The village of Jordan, where this is situated is calm and serene place that makes you feel like you have arrived somewhere that you don't need or want to look at your phone, check your emails.... etc. The food at their restaurants are absolutely delicious. Even the breakfast, which is typically included with the stay, is top quality. I had a delicious smoked salmon, eggs, cream cheese, great coffee, ad again, great and friendly service. The wine store, (not actually owned by the Inn anymore, but still connected) is a welcoming place as well. Didi, Meg and Pat are so nice, and passionate about the Cave Springs wine. They are also passionate about the people that come into the store and make sure they have a wonderful visit. Look forward to seeing you all again soon! Thanks for a special stay!

author: Sunseeker990
title: Picture Perfect Wedding Venue
text: We stayed at Inn on the Twenty, where our friends were married. The wedding venue was lovely and the service was excellent! Upon check in to the hotel, the young lady at the front desk was very warm and welcoming and showed us all around our room, advised that there were fresh baked cookies and fresh coffee etc. She looked up the wedding details to ensure we were in the right place at the right time. Our room at the inn was incredible - well appointed, extremely comfortable, very roomy, quiet - overall just wonderful. I wanted to bring the bed and pillows home! We had a gas fireplace, a small sofa, two comfy chairs, a desk, dressers and more. The bathroom had a Jacuzzi tub and a separate walk in shower. There were high end toiletries and even robes! Overall, just lovely. Breakfast was included in our price and this is the only reason I did not give a 5. The breakfast service was very slow - we sat for almost 10 minutes after being seated before someone came. The hot breakfast we ordered took a while to come and when it did, everything was cold. We had to ask more than once for milk for the coffee and for refills. It was not very busy with only about 6 tables occupied when we were having breakfast. Other than that, I highly recommend Inn on the Twenty for an overnight (or longer) stay.

author: RetiredWoodturner
title: Very good but not as exceptional as in the past
text: We stayed for 2 nights. Everything was verry good and the food itself was exeptional. I noticed even on the first day that the level of quality had deteriorated slightly. Liquid soap containers instead of bars of soap. I have no problems with that except the pumps in the soap dispenser did not work properly. Coat hooks on doors not attached properly. In the dining room there were flies. Also at breakfast there was only one server who seemed to be run off her feet. Service was very slow. I realise that these are all relatively minor issues however having stayed at this facility several times over the years the change was noticable. In the past everything was always outstanding. This time however there was a noticable drop in quality. For the prices charged and reputation I expected more. Staff were as helpfull and friendly as always. In chatting with staff and vendors in the area we heard that the Inn was recently sold. New owners/cost savings??? Its a pity as this Inn used to be really outstanding in all aspects. Now albeit still very good, the cutting edge of quality experienced in the past was somewhat dulled.

author: 319jy
title: Comfortable
text: The room was gorgeous. Beds super comfortable, pillows , sheets and blankets perfect ! Sitting area was also enjoyed . The bathroom was huge and spectacular. One thing we noticed that the shower water pressure was so strong and fantastic. Felt like a massage.. Clean and comfortable in the whole room . Quiet and peaceful. We faced the courtyard and the view was so nice.. We were greeted by a very friendly woman who personally took us up to our room and explained everything. We really appreciated her hospitality towards us.. The inn is a 5 star in my opinion. Although it could do with some drinks and snack service for late night enjoyment. Now that would of made it PERFECT ! But still all in all a very good stay for the night..

author: estrag
title: Almost perfect
text: There is much to love about Inn on the Twenty. The common areas and landscaping are lovely. The included breakfast is outstanding. Service was warm and attentive, the baked goods tasted fresh-out-of-the-oven homemade, and the portion sizes were just right. Everything we had, including the coffee, was delicious. Mixed review on the room experience. Our first night was in our reserved room. It was big and very clean, with a comfortable bed and great shower and jacuzzi. However, the furnishings were dated and our request for turn down service was ignored twice. We were given incomplete directions for a hike that was recommeded, which was frustrating. Also, we had an issue with the room and called the front desk a couple of times with no answer. To the Inn's credit, when they learned about our issue, they immediately offered us an upgrade to a beautiful suite. They put us into The Vintner's suite, and that was amazing. Beautiful, up to date, very comfortable. We ended our visit on a high note!

author: 408eva
title: Romantic One-Night Stay
text: What a beautiful inn and such welcoming and attentive staff! We had a premium garden suite with a walkout to a small garden. The patio furniture hadn't been set up yet but it was convenient to exit through our garden to the parking lot. Our room was gorgeous, super clean with a sofa in front of the fire place, Jacuzzi tub and separate shower in bathroom. Romantic, comfy bed. We did a wine tasting across the street at Cave Springs and then toured the main street. Such a pretty neighbourhood. When we came back warm cider and cookies were available. The cider was so delicious! Dinner, however, was a disappointment. We had booked a special all-inclusive spring meal pkg and we both wished we had ordered off the menu instead. Our server was lovely but the food so bland. Even our dessert was disappointing. A strawberry tart whose crust just crumbled into dust. After dinner we went for music at the Jordan House Tavern. A very good trio was playing light rock. The next morning we had a very tasty breakfast. Again, our server was just lovely! We will definitely return and hopefully have a better dinner experience. The only reason I can't rate this wonderful and unique place excellent is due to our disappointing dinner.

author: 354pauliner
title: Vintage House at Inn On The Twenty
text: We stayed at the Inn On The Twenty just for the one night as we attended a wedding on February 4th 2017. Check in took about 3 minutes and that was with us even having a few questions. We stayed in the Vintage House and had no idea what to expect. The room was in a cottage at the side of the main building and on the second floor. The minute we opened the door we knew we were in for a little treat. The foyer was bright and well lit. We went up the stairs and were pleasantly surprised with the décor as well as the size of the room itself. To the right of the stairs was the doorway into the living room area which had a couch, two arm chairs, a flat screen tv, stereo and electric fireplace. To the left of the staircase was the bedroom and bathroom. Not only was the bedroom quite large the bed and linens were one of the most comfortable I have slept in. Then there was the bathroom which was about the size of most second bedrooms. It was quite spacious with a vintage style sink and accents throughout. The Inn has kept an old world charm and feel with this room. From the accents, to the peeling paint on the window grilles to the wide plank wood flooring. I definitely felt like I was staying at an old country manor. Just the feeling I hoped for. I will definitely be returning in the spring/summer in order to enjoy what the town of Jordan has to offer.

author: Mr_Garcon
title: Wonderful Get Away Highly Recommended
text: We spent the weekend in Jordan attending the seasonal wine and food festival, weekend of January 14th. Had stumbled across this lovely hamlet several years ago while researching wedding locations and did a brief tour of Inn On The Twenty. This year my wife and I booked a few months in advance (this Inn books up quickly and is in high demand) and headed down to have a relaxing weekend. The Inn did not disappoint in the slightest! We booked two alcove rooms for ourselves and my wife's sister and husband. The Inn's rooms are very spacious and with a large "ever so comfortable' bed and fireplace is just what the doctor ordered on those long afternoons of walking around at a festival. The sitting areas were perfect for an additional glass of wine and some cheese and fresh bread from the local bakery. The package that we purchased included an enhanced continental breakfast at the Inn's restaurant, which by many standards was better then several full breakfasts we have experienced in our travels. Your choice of eggs benedict, French toast, or eggs and bacon (with home fries) was the "enhancement" and was paired with lots of fresh pastries, fruit, granola, hard boiled eggs and breads. The most amazing thing we found about this wayfarer's paradise was the beds!!! We have been hunting to find the same mattress locally as it was the BEST sleep we have had in years!! Now, I am an early riser by most accounts, normally getting my first coffee around 7am, but during our stay I had a (very) tough time getting up in time to meet our family for breakfast before the 10:00am cut off. I wonder if they have put extra insulation in the walls because we heard very little once we retired in the evenings. And we slept so soundly one would wonder if there was something in our home baked night time cookies (found in the lobby!). The staff were exceptional in there ability to attend to anything we needed, as well as assist us in finding out who made the mattress and where one might acquire one (yes it was THAT good of a sleep!!). We have thought we may need to go back sooner than expected to "relax" in room 16 !! Definitely will recommend this anytime someone wants a nice get away in a very relaxing environment. And a personal shout out to Beverly for all her hard work in tracking down items!!

author: FancyfreeToronto
title: It could be great and it's just good
text: My daughter and I spent a two night post-Christmas getaway here and did it all - spa, dinner at the restaurant, wine tastings and purchases. There were some wonderful moments, but on the whole Inn on the Twenty was not as special as it could be. It was just a nice place to stay. Customer service was really the missing ingredient - the front desk was generally empty and there was just no sense of welcome. We had issues at both the spa and restaurant. Though we spoke with staff at each, and there was just no generous-spirited response to acknowledge these. The best news - Cave Spring is a great winery and the tastings were fun. The common spaces at the Inn are very nice and our room was pleasant. The bad news - the spa and the restaurant need improvement. There are better choices in the region for both. We booked our room early in December, but wanted to decide on spa treatments so left that for later. Staff did not tell us that spa spots should be booked as early as possible. Yes, we should have known but thought they would proactively advise us. When we tried to book about a week before our arrival, virtually no times were open. Something was finally arranged after way too many calls. The restaurant felt tired. We had two appetizers and two entrees, with wine with each course and coffee. Everything was just OK and the carrot soup was disappointing. No one seemed particularly interested when I mentioned it. Our dinner the next night at Two Sisters Winery, on the other hand, was the exact opposite -- wonderful kitchen, great vibe, and excellent service.

author: FraserM311
title: Beautiful 3 day getaway
text: The tiny village of Jordan is home to Cave Spring Winery which operates the Inn & Spa as well as a wine store / tasting venue and an extremely nice restaurant which overlooks a beautiful woodland valley. We booked two rooms as we were meeting old friends that we hadn't seen in over a year. When you are arranging a getaway for friends there is always a bit of pressure to find something they will enjoy. This Inn didn't disappoint. It is off season and the beginning of the week so there were only a few guests in the hotel. We arrived early and as there were two side by side top tier suites immediately available we were upgraded. A very nice treat! Our room was nicely decorated in a traditional style befitting the building and the area. It included a large living area with sofa, chairs, fireplace and desk. The adjoining bedroom featured a very comfortable king bed. We also had a beautiful private garden with table and chairs beyond the french doors, overhung at this time of year by a scarlet leafed Japanese Maple tree. The huge bathroom contained a jetted tub and small shower. This was the only small deficiency. The bathrooms which seemed to be of 1980's vintage are a bit past their due date and had it been new and up to 21st century standards of design, finish and efficiency, I would have rated the hotel excellent. The staff that we encountered everywhere, Reception, Housekeeping and Restaurant were all wonderful, pleasant and efficient. We will certainly return the next time we feel like a getaway!

author: 919lolam
title: ABSOLUTELY AMAZING
text: I don't know where to begin for an absolutely beautiful couple of days. My sister organized a small vacation for a couple of nights to share with two other beautiful friends. Its was for one of our friends special birthdays. From the second that our feet hit the entrance of this absolutely stunning hotel, we knew we were in heaven. Checked in rather quickly, and a young gentleman helped us to our rooms (even carried our luggage) we couldn't get over this. We settled into our rooms and the got acquainted with the cute shops across the street. Had an absolutely amazing supper which was part of our package across the street and had a wonderful server Cathy entertain us over supper. The food was magnificent, chefs specials were displayed beautifully on our places. The view from our table was magical cascading for many miles of vines and hills and beautiful rolling land. Breakfast we couldn't wait to get back with Cathy waiting on us, good food, great choices, nice buffet of some sweet breads, fruits granola and yogurt to get us started. Coffee was always hot and flowed often to the table. The hotel and restaurant should be commended on the team work of their staff. They have been employed by many years and that is obvious with each and every one of them. Thank you for making our stay in JORDAN, truly the most memorable. We will be back!!

author: waynegm54
title: Very Relaxing
text: It was our 29th anniversary so we decided to stay at the Inn on the Twenty, have dinner at their restaurant and visit some wineries. We have been there several times before and every time has been very enjoyable and relaxing. This time was no exception. We decided to do this only a few days before we wanted to go so were a bit concerned about availability. However, booking our room was no problem using their online reservation system. We also booked the restaurant using Open Table. We typically visit the Niagara Wine country every year but alternate between Jordan (and Inn on the Twenty) and Niagara-on-the Lake (usually the Prince of Wales). During the summer peak season we prefer Jordan (and Inn on the Twenty) as the area is less busy and therefore more relaxing. We usually stay in Niagara on the Lake in either the Spring or Fall before the summer tourists show up. Our room was very comfortable and dinner was great. We do not typically use the Spa. The rooms have that country inn feel yet have all the modern conveniences. The village of Jordan does not really have that much so we spent the morning visiting wineries (including lunch at one of them). Once back in the Village we walked around the stores, went to Cave Spring Cellars to taste some wine and buy a case (Inn of the Twenty offers a $20 credit for your room if you buy a case of wine, which you create a mix with different ones, at Cave Springs), and then stopped at the Inn on the Twenty Restaurant for a couple of afternoon drinks. Before dinner, we went back to our room for a bit of a nap. An excellent and relaxing way to spend our anniversary.

author: 2013Wren
title: Such Luxury and Tranquility in a Sweet, Interesting Village
text: My mother and I just returned from a 2-night stay at Inn on the Twenty. The Inn is wonderful - so luxurious and tranquil. The quality of the rooms, grounds and common spaces is exceptional - clean, comfortable, quiet, well appointed, lots of amenities . . . And the hospitable attitude and professionalism of the staff is outstanding! They made our short visit even more pleasant! My mother's main floor room with a private patio was a great feature. Would love to return again. There is no shortage of things to do in the village without ever leaving (not to mention all the local area attractions if you do feel like some short drives) . . . interesting shops, so much nature to appreciate, good food and drinks . . . and just people watching from the patios. All the staff in the stores and restaurants were so friendly and so accommodating. It was a wonderful 2-day get away not too far from home.

author: GratefulinDundas
title: A Lovely Get-away
text: We were given the gift of a Life Experience card (those Shoppers Drug Mart ones!) as a wedding present and booked in during a particularly intense and busy time in our lives. We chose a Sunday night and it was absolutely perfect! We checked in easily and enjoyed some very tasty homemade cookies in the lobby. The gift card included wine tastings (4 each or 8 if we shared). We shared! We bought some icewine to take home and some tasty wine to have in our room with a picnic lunch we'd prepared. How lovely it was to settle in and sit by the fire in comfy chairs sipping, chatting and nibbling before a restful nap. The beautiful decor and spacious room was a delight! We wandered down the street to the Jordan Tavern for dinner as we weren't really in the mood for a fancy dinner. The menu was diverse and the cocktails were fun. My snake in the grass was quite tasty, and my partner enjoyed the caesar special. We marvelled at the size of the roast beast special the man across the room ordered! Back to the beautiful room at the Inn for a lovely, deep sleep - this time with the windows open enjoying fresh air. The enhanced continental breakfast completed the package and we re-entered the world 24 hours later, convinced that it was a wonderful gift we'd offer to others! Iif we'd had the time and energy, we're sure we'd have enjoyed visiting more of the shops and galleries in Jordan - likely staying two nights next time, rather than one.

author: DVJjvd
title: A great place on a cold winter day
text: I decided to go here on Family Day rather than suffer the crowds on Valentines Day and was very pleasantly rewarded. The inn was not crowded and the restaurant associated with the inn was not crowded for supper on the night we arrived/. Since we were the first in fro breakfast the next morning @ 8 am we got the best table in the house and were treated to a lovely view of the valley behind the inn while we enjoyed some tasty buckwheat pancakes and a fruit cup. The night before we luxuriated in the Hadley Room which was one a several they have that has a jet tub. The room was beautifully decorated and the fireplace kept the room cozy. The heat does not transfer easily to the washroom and the tile floor is not heated so be prepared to have cold feet or bring extra slippers for the washroom experience. The king bed did wonders for the back of "she who must be obeyed". The service both at the restaurant and the inn was top drawer. We also had a chance to visit Cave Springs winery across the road from the inn. We didn't know it at the time but it closes at 5 and we only had a few minutes to enjoy some of the samples. Recommend the Estate bottled Reisling which we both enjoyed and purchased. Did not enjoy the Cab/Merlot Dolomite...but tastes are very personal. We both booked massages the next morning and came away feeling better for it. They do have WiFi but I couldn't get it to work. No biggy. In all it was a wonderful stay and I'd return.

author: Chopstick105
title: Almost forgot to review this very special place
text: In my January review I said we would be back for a wedding in August. The stay was everything we expected it to be and we heard similar comments from the many guests. There were three weddings the same weekend but we weren’t tripping over each other. We took the Cooper’s Suite, an almost stand alone cottage on the other side of the parking lot from the main hotel. The other half of the building was another cottage occupied by our daughter and her husband. We had an adjoining door in the cottages and an adjoining gate brought the two quiet and comfortable patios together. They were surrounded by greenery which made them very private with no intrusion from the parking lot or the streets. Another bonus was a private driveway for parking right beside the front door. Our suite was two-level with a nice bedroom and a very large sitting room. We used it and the patios as the hospitality suite on the night before the wedding. Being away from the main building and having family in both cottages made us less nervous about noise. We are used to great service and excellent accommodation here and this was no exception. A bit pricy but an excellent example of getting what you pay for. Our American friends would find it a bargain at the moment with the exchange rate. But don’t reserve it during the Icewine Festival because we want it.

author: HeatherH781
title: More Than We Imagined!
text: We stayed in the Laura Secord Room. Beautiful spacious room with fireplace and jacuzzi. We dined at the Jordan House for Lunch. Great pub grub. Place was packed with locals. Beautiful day for mid November. Lots of crafts and winery tours in nearby locations. Upper Canada Cheese Factory also a must visit. Dined at the Main Restaurant across the road. Food & view excellent. Service great. Loved our server, Brian. Gave us tips for visiting places in the area. Surrounded by great wineries. Our room came with breakfast which was also excellent. Bought some of the homemade granola to take home with us. Will definitely go back. There is a spa on site but we did not have time to take advantage of this amenity.

author: Chouster
title: Luxurious room
text: We stayed at the hotel for a wedding and the room did not disappoint. The inn is located on a quaint street in Jordan, Ontario near shops and wineries. It's easily accessible and close to the highway and there is a lot of parking nearby. The rooms themselves are spacious with tall ceilings. The rooms came equipped with a Keurig coffee machine with plenty of pods. There's no milk or cream in the room but you can easily call the front desk for this. There's a TV with DVD player and the beds are large and comfy. The temperature in the room is easy to control except the curtains cover the air vents which is a bit of a design flaw. The other other complaint is that our room didn't have much of a view but that wasn't really an issue for us. The bathrooms are large and spacious. The jacuzzi easily fits two people. The bathroom is also well equipped with bath salts, close-up mirrors, shower caps etc. Included in the package was breakfast across the street featuring a hot dish, fresh fruits, tea/coffee and a continental buffet (with yogurt, pastries, granola, toast). The food was pretty good though nothing mind-blowing. Overall, a really romantic getaway and a place I would definitely return to.

author: christinebV3413OZ
title: A Very Nice Stay
text: We stayed at the Inn on the Twenty from the evening of June 2-June 5, 2015 in a private garden suite. Years ago, we had visited the area before to taste wine and stayed at the Jordan Inn. We loved the small town feeling and we wanted to return to the wine area and stay at the Inn. We were welcomed by the front desk clerk and then proceeded to our very pretty garden suite. The suite, next to the parking lot, was spacious and very clean with a small entry room containing a couch, desk, chairs, a refrigerator and a fireplace. This backed up to bedding area with a very comfortable king bed. The bath was large with a jetted bathtub and sufficient lighting. Internet was also included and fairly quick. The garden area was secluded and charming with a small table and chairs. We thought the staff at the hotel was professional, helpful and pleasant. On the first night, we ate at the hotel's fine restaurant, located across the street from the Inn and enjoyed the food very much. During the following days, we had the included breakfast at the restaurant and found it good and the staff very accommodating and efficient. The only suggestions I have involve the shower and the refrigerator. Although the bath in that suite is quite large, the shower stall is very small and dark with no light. Either remove the shower curtain in the shower and replace it with a door or make the shower larger since the bathtub is so large. The second is about the refrigerator. In reading one of the Trip Advisor’s comments about the Inn, the person remarked that not all rooms had one. When he/she asked for one, he/she paid a fee. I asked for one when I booked and was not charged a fee. All in all, the stay was extremely pleasant, the Inn was lovely and the restaurant excellent.

author: Jedavan
title: Decent Experience
text: I should start with a disclaimer as I was at the Inn on the Twenty for a corporate retreat and normally I would not stay at this type of hotel property. Generally it's a great spot and I would imagine in the summer and during wine season the town and hotel would be robust with energy. The best part of this hotel is the staff as the service is excellent and their willingness to help with any detail is outstanding. I'll admit I struggled a bit the physical property as there were four "misses" that think the hotel could tackle differently: 1. The rooms are huge but difficult to keep cool. A few of my colleagues commented on how hot their rooms were and the wall mounted air conditioning units couldn't keep up. 2. My room had two queen beds and both need mattress tops or replacing as the mattress quality was akin to a college dorm experience (they felt thin, old and were not comfortable). 3. The bathrooms are fairly dark which is particularly noticeable when you are in the shower with the curtain drawn. I appreciate it's an older inn, but the lack of light made the bathroom feel smaller and older than it actually was. 4. While the bathroom overall was extremely clean, there was a massive twine wreath on the wall that desperately needed to be vacuumed as months of thick dust had accumulated on the wreath and wall. Overall it was a nice spot and I can see why couples would love the property given the focus on the quaint feel. Loved the bottle of wine they leave in the room for you when you arrive (would like it better if they put it on ice) and as I mentioned the staff are outstanding. Definitely worth recommending and hopefully there are some new mattresses on order as the bed quality didn't match the Inn experience.

author: GasbarNut
title: Absolutely Fabulous Mini-Getaway! More time needed!
text: Hubby and I needed a last minute getaway so opted for this lovely little town on one of the coldest nights of the year. The cold didn't matter much to us, except to strengthen our resolve to return to this incredible little hamlet when the blossoms are in full bloom! Inn On the Twenty is awesome! We absolutely loved every facet of the Inn, our room, and John from the front desk is a genuinely great gentleman (and funny! We have a new inside joke regarding our license plate thanks to John!). The small town is so nicely appointed, much like the Inn itself and the rooms. We adored the fireplace being on most of the night, loved the tub for two in the room, and had a really great wine tour as part of our stay over at Cave Spring. For Niagara wine lovers, you NEED to head to Jordan if you don't already know how influencial the Pennachetti family has been in this region and to wine-making in Ontario in general. It was fascinating learning more about the various regions-within-the-region, so much so that we bought the fantastic Map to put up in our home. Pat was not only truly knowledgeable at Cave Spring Cellars, she was personable and a real treat. She's definitely an asset! We had a midday snack at Jordan House Tavern and will return there again too for their Fish Tacos. The breakfast at the On The Twenty restaurant on the Saturday morning was SO LOVELY, and we just sat and enjoyed the offerings (the scones - you can't have just one! - and the homemade granola are eclipsed BARELY by the gorgeous smoked salmon hash with poached egg!!!) and coffee with the spectacular view for over an hour. We did get a last minute deal via the Ontarios Finest Inns website to be able to afford our stay, but we are determined to do it again because it was that special for us, and next time we will go in the nicer weather so we can go to the Jordan Museum and explore some of the awesome trails nearby too. If you are looking at this, you're already considering it. Go. You won't regret it!!!

author: Chopstick105
title: Deserves an Excellent rating despite a few idiosyncrasies!!
text: Oxford dictionary defines idiosyncrasy as 'a distinctive or peculiar characteristic of a place of thing'. Inn-on-the-Twenty abounds in them and yet we came away thinking we had an almost perfect stay. When you enter there is a fairly steep stairway to the reception on the second floor. There is no regular elevator but the receptionist offered us a key to the elevator the makes the hotel accessible for wheelchairs; it is kind of hidden in the back. We had a two level suite. The TV was on the second level in an armoire that doesn't face the bed so the TV is pulled out and you view it at an angle. Downstairs in the very nice sitting room with a fireplace there is no TV which might be a blessing. The fireplace is another one of the idiosyncrasies, it doubles as the heating system so when the set temperature is reached the fireplace goes off. Since we were sitting with low lights and sipping wine I partially opened the window to force the temperature down and the fireplace on. Don't go here if you are expecting sterile chrome and glass but all these little things were actually charming rather than annoying. There were really good things as well. The bathroom was huge and beautiful. The whirlpool tub easily accommodated two with a nice ledge for the wine glasses. It was also easy to get in and out of which is a plus since we are both in our seventies. The decor was reminiscent of the 1800 and very comforting. The included breakfast in the restaurant across the street was one of the best included ones we have had. This summer we are back in the area for a wedding. We immediately booked one of the detached cottages with a patio where we will host a drop-in hospitality suite. We have probably told 20 people they should go her to unwind and we have written reviews of the local restaurants as well. Don't miss the Jordan House Pub.

author: Lili-Fairfeather
title: Perfect!
text: I stayed at the Inn on the Twenty September 19th before my wedding with three of my girlfriends, and the night of the 20th with my new husband! We were promptly checked in by John and Sandie who then assisted me into my suite. I had reserved a two storey loft suite, with a pullout sofa which gave us plenty of room! Upon returning from the rehearsal, our room had been “turned down” with chocolates left for us! The pullout sofa was a bit tricky to get out (I think because it's new), but according to my two girlfriends, it was very comfortable – not like any sofa bed they’ve ever slept on! The next morning, we all went over for breakfast. There was a buffet of whole fruits, some pastries, cereals, yogurt, granola as well as bread and jams for toast. Our server brought each of us a fresh fruit cup as well as coffee/tea or juice if we preferred. We all had the “eggs how you like it” feature and it was just the right amount of food! After breakfast, we went to the hair and makeup room in the Inn to get beautified by Rebecca, Holly and Porsche. (thanks ladies!!) And then off to get married!! The suite was quiet, cool and the bed was so heavenly to sleep in after a long day and night of dancing and socializing! Everyone at the Inn was so helpful, kind and accommodating! We will definitely be back!! Thank you for everything! :)

author: 685melaniec
title: Already planning to go back
text: My partner and I visited Inn on the Twenty on August 4th and 5th at the beginning of a few days' getaway. We were interested in visiting Niagara on the Lake but wanted to stay away from the summer busy-ness of NOTL. We chose Jordan for it's proximity and to experience something a little off the beaten path and are very glad we did. We stayed in a beautiful alcove suite with a private enclosed garden (the Moyer Suite). It was spacious, beautifully decorated, exceptionally clean and had a lovely, large bathroom. There were many thoughtful little amenities provided and the staff was very friendly and helpful (the young woman behind the desk quickly offered up a large umbrella on our first morning when it was raining as we were departing the inn for breakfast across the street. We kept it for our day trip into NOTL and were very grateful for it). The rooms and inn are very quiet, which means a great sleep. We added breakfast onto our room rate for $20.00 (for 2), plus tax & gratuities and it was excellent value. The dining room across from the inn is beautiful. Be warned that Jordan is a very quiet little place, but if you are looking to relax and recharge, it is an excellent choice. Although dining choices in the village itself are very limited, there are interesting and decent quality choices within a few minutes drive. Don't miss Kenneth Walsh's incredible photographic art gallery across from the inn and the young woman at the Jordan Historical Museum gave a great tour and insight into the Mennonite history of the area. The young man behind the tasting counter at Cave Spring Cellars across the road from the inn was friendly and knowledgeable (you receive a complimentary pass for tasting a few wines when you check in at the inn). A special thanks to John in customer relations at the inn. I had booked and prepaid our reservation through Ontario's Finest Inns just a few days before we were leaving and while I got a confirmation from them, I did not receive a confirmation directly from Inn on the Twenty, as Ontario's Finest had indicated that I would. As I was a little concerned, I emailed the Inn directly just a couple of days before we were due to arrive and John answered promptly that they had not received anything from OFI, but assured me that they were putting a lovely room aside and requested that I simply forward my confirmation from OFI. Although we had booked on a last minute discount through OFI, the room we received was a actually an upgrade from the one that we had reserved and at no point were we made to feel that we were treated with any less than the utmost hospitality and professionalism, even though it was a discounted rate. We are planning to return to the inn this Fall or at Christmas.

author: Campfiver
title: Lovely place
text: We decided to stay here and make a weekend out of it to celebrate our anniversary. I had made the reservation and was lucky to get a lovely loft room. The Inn gets busy with weddings. Check in I found a bit strange, there was a small sign stating that reception was on the 2nd floor. No elevator in sight. Check in was friendly and fast and we were escorted to our room. Sitting area with fireplace is on the main floor with a small washroom. up the stairs to the loft is the bed with a big bathroom. There is a wardrobe which houses the TV and the Keurig coffee machine. the whole set up was very nice, however personally we would have preferred to have the TV in the sitting room as we don't watch TV in bed at all. Also we don't like to sit on the bed to watch. Anyway we had to go to the car to get the luggage up, and that is where by chance we discovered the elevator. I went to the reception and asked about the elevator as I find it very difficult to manage stairs. We received a special key for the elevator, which made it a lot easier. We also mentioned it to another couple as he had challenges going up and down stairs as well. They received a key as well and were very grateful. It is an older building so AC was installed per room. We had to turn AC off as it was very noisy. But all in all we loved our stay at the Inn.

author: msginthevillage
title: Nice, but exorbitantly overpriced
text: My wife, son, and I spent a night at the Inn en route to the Muskoka Lakes of Ontario. We wanted a comfortable place to rest in the middle of a long road trip. We stayed in a duplex suite room and had dinner and breakfast at the restaurant across the street. Jordan is a very small village that seems to be owned by the Inn and Cave Springs winery. It's a block full of shops, the inn, a tasting room, and the restaurant. I reluctantly agreed to pay approximately $300 for the room. The inn staff were efficient, but without any style, and offered us no assistance. Our impression was rescued by the wonderful dinner we had across the street. The wines from the winery were very marked-up (200% of retail, from what I can tell). I am used to paying for wine at restaurants, but there is something very annoying to me about paying so much for Ontario wine grown next door. Somehow, Ontario (my birthplace) has confused making good wines with charging as if they came from France. I always imagine shipping is included in a good bottle of French wine, but this can't be the case here. Anyway, breakfast the next morning was a shameful affair of lousy canned fruit, a small hot entree, and a small, poorly composed breakfast bar. Here we are sitting in the fruit basket of Ontario, a province renowned for excellent produce, and we are given a highway hotel breakfast. I had a similar experience at Huff Estates in Prince Edward County, Ontario (see review), so maybe there is a virus going around... All and all, a large room, decently furnished, but not nearly worth the cost.

author: urbainedesbois
title: Oooh so nice !
text: Spent two memorable days at the Inn on the Twenty in Jordan. Our room (no. 14) was on the second floor, just by the garden exit. What a nice view ! Extra high ceiling, oversized room with a full sized lounging area by the fireplace and an enormous bathroom ... I was a very happy camper! Breakfast was served in the very chic restaurant across the street, again with a beautiful view. Friendly staff and quiet surroundings ... what can one ask for more ? ... Well, there is one little thing that could be changed : I booked through Expedia at a price 25% lower than the one advertised on the Inn's website. The catch is that the breakfast was NOT included, something that wasn't clearly noted in the Expedia advertising. So much so that I called the Inn to clear this out before my arrival. I was told that all the Inn's guests had breakfast included in their room rate. Not true. Oh well, just a minor disappointment in an otherwise perfect stay.

author: Frank-TJ
title: The lovely Inn...
text: Just arrived back in the UK after an amazing 10 days spend in Ontario, with a very special 3 of those days spend in Jordan Village at the lovely Inn on the Twenty. After a long 3 hours on the road driving from North Ontario, the Inn was truly an oasis in the sweltering heat wave of last week in the area! We entered into a very relaxed atmosphere with very welcoming and helpful reception desk staff who led us to our room. The room we had (Room 1) was very nice indeed, high ceilings, good quality fittings and a very comfy bed. The bathroom too was immaculate with a whirlpool bath, standalone shower along with a large sink area. All in all the accommodation was the perfect space to kick back and cool off after a day spent touring the local wineries in the 37 degree heat we had last week! The Inn is set in the wonderful Jordan Village which was so peaceful and very quiet with hardly a soul on the street, maybe something to do with the heat again! My wife and I very much enjoyed the 5 minute stroll through the village down to the Jordan House Tavern which is also owned by the Inn, this place is your typical North American bar with a wide selection of beers and decent Canadian/American style pub grub should you not be eating at the more formal restaurant directly across from the inn, which I will review separately. The Jordan House Tavern had some excellent chicken wings and sweet potato fries, which we washed down with some great local beers and ales! This place would definitely be my local pub/bar if I lived in the area! Only one thing stopped the Inn getting the full 5 stars from us. Due to the extremely hot and humid weather during our stay, air conditioning was essential at all times in our room. Unfortunately the AC unit in room 1 was pretty loud and not ideal if you are a light sleeper like me! Maybe it needed some maintenance or tuning. Also, the ceiling fan didn’t work but can’t complain too much about that because a maintenance call was offered and we declined as we knew we had the air conditioning. A heavier sleeper would have been fine I’m sure, but I found the noise from the AC unit a bit disruptive at night. Maybe I am nit-picking! But all in all, I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend the Inn to anyone thinking of visiting the region to tour the wineries, it is the perfect haven to relax after a hard day sipping back the ole grape juice!

author: 881andreap881
title: Fabulous food and service at the Inn and Spa!
text: My mom and I go at least once a year to the Spa on the Twenty and we love it, so for my 40th birthday we decided to take a girls' trip to the Spa and stay overnight in the Inn. We had an absolutely fabulous time. We ate dinner at the Inn the night we arrived and it was beyond excellent. I have dietary issues (gluten and dairy) and not only were there many items on the menu that I could eat that didn't require any modification, but also they made it clear they were very happy to modify any dish so it was gluten/dairy free. My mom even spoke to General Manager before we arrived and ordered a gluten/dairy free birthday cake. It was delicious! (Thank you to Don and the pastry chef!) That night we stayed in the 2 Queen bed room at the Inn and it's a beautiful room - very tastfully decorated and comfortable. We then had another wonderful meal at the Inn the next morning, and again they accommodated my gluten and dairy issues. Breakfast was fantastic. We then went to the spa and enjoyed several treatments and lunch there. The spa staff are great and we left feeling very pampered and relaxed. Overall it couldn't have been a better getaway. The food and service at the Inn and the Spa are superb and we highly recommend it! Thank you to everyone who made our trip so memorable. Customer service that exceeds your expectations doesn't happen very often these days, and everyone at the Spa and Inn did just that. We will certainly be back! Andrea P - Burlington, ON

author: JennyAWK26
title: Close but far away
text: On a friend's recommendation I booked a Loft Suite for Friday night. I have driven past the exit to Jordan on the QEW many times but have never been in this area. Very happy we decided to go. As soon as you get into Jordan you feel your a long way from the city and really on vacation (40 mins from home!). The inn was quiet when we arrived and the receptionist took us straight to our loft room.
