The room was very large, high ceilings , comfortable living room downstairs with a fire place (not needed!) and stairs up to a big loft area with a king bed , cabinet with tv, coffee maker etc.... Washrooms are downstairs and upstairs and the upstairs bathroom has a shower and jacuzzi tub. Really like a small apartment - extremly comfortable and relaxing.. Took a short wander around the town before dinner - peeked in the store windows and took a look a the heritage area complete with old mennonite graveyard. We did not book the inclusive dinner as we wanted to keep our plans open but ate at the Inn on Twenty anyway. Had a great window table with a view over the valley - everything was excellent, we chose a bin-end wine at a reasonable price, we had wonderful salad starters, and trout and lamb as main courses. Great service, little extras that you expect for fine dining were all there.. Saturday morning we went back for our included breakfast and then after checking out we hiked out to Balls Falls from the bottom of the hill. This is a lovely walk by the river, we saw turtles,a grass snake, no beavers but a lot teeth marks (!) , turkey vultures, hawks and large trout..as well as lots of native flowers. After the walk we came back in to Jordan and spent the afternoon pottering around the stores and had a nice outside lunch .... This was a surprise getaway for my boyfriend and I and it was worth the cost as we really felt that we got away and had a mini 24 hour vacation. We will definitely go back, besides we didn't get around to doing our wine tour!

author: MikeM277
title: Nice little Getaway!!
text: This was my first time staying at the Inn. I've visited the Restaurant on quite a few times in the past and have always enjoyed the food and service there. The hotel itself was very nice and charming. My wife and I were their celebrating my birthday. We stayed in a Loft Suite. The room was very nice overall.. Modern and lot's of room to move around. The only complaints I had was: 1) We found a few hairs in the bed and noticed a few more in the washroom. Felt a little grossed out by that. They could have done a better job cleaning the room. 2) Fireplace wasn't working. 3) They keep the coffee and tea in the washroom. Don't really think that is the best place to keep those sort of things right beside the toilet and washroom sink. Otherwise, we enjoyed the fact the bed was on a seperate floor (it made the place feel bigger). They also left chocolates on our pillows in the evening (nice touch). Another thing I liked about the Inn was that had cookies near the front desk. Nice cute touch!! Unfortunately, the rating I'm giving it is average just because of those points I mentioned above, otherwise I would have gave it a very good score.

author: YorkshiremanOntario
title: Another great new year.
text: This Inn is a real gem. We booked an overnight package for new year's eve. The room was fantastic, It was a loft suite and was one of the nicest rooms we have booked on any of our trips. The room was clean, was well furnished and the bed was very comfortable. The bathroom was clean and modern it also had as seperate jacuzzi tub and a large shower. There is also a powder room on the main floor which is a great extra. The staff are efficient and polite and happy to help in any way they can. The public areas reflect the very high standard for quality and cleanliness that is evident througout the whole inn. We ate at the restuarant both new years eve and the follwing morning. The food was very good and the wine pairings are excellent, breakfast was also very good but I would recommend they add a few items for guests that like a more standard breakfast. The dining room is well laid out and has a great view. The restaurant staff are top notch and even though it was new years we felt like the service was very personal and the staff were not spread thin. We didn't get much time to enjoy the village but it is a nice clean street with some interesting shops and galleries and must look amazing in the summer when everything is in bloom. We plan on returning just to enjoy this and take some walk's along the river. I would highly recomend a stay at this Inn and a must vist area to explore.

author: heregoes
title: Lovely town, great restaurant, nice spa but just "okay" inn.
text: Jordan is a lovely little town with quaint shops. The Inn is right on this lovely street. The Inn is separate from its restaurant and its spa, which is a little inconvenient. However, the restaurant is top notch and the spa was lovely--great service, lovely amenities and I enjoyed a beautiful facial. Our room in the inn was a lovely two-storey loft, beautifully furnished with a lavish bathroom. The reason I say the Inn was only "okay" is that it lacks a central lobby and doesn't have a "warm" feeling. The thing we disliked most was the fact that all four of us (we were travelling as two couples) had spa appointments at 11 a.m. and we had asked for a late check-out since the spa only had one shower. It was a Sunday so we figured that there probably wouldn't be a guest arriving for a Monday. They refused us this request. We were very disappointed as we were spending money in their spa and they couldn't accommodate us. Even if they had given us another room to shower in....any kind of accommodation would have been appreciated. We paid a pretty penny for one night in the Inn with a wine-pairings dinner so we thought they were nickle and diming us. The breakfast was included but there was only one option available which was Eggs Benedict and pastry. I cannot eat wheat so I requested oatmeal and was shocked when they brought me instant oatmeal! In a restaurant of this quality, I had expected they would either make it from scratch or not offer it. It's small details like this that keep the Inn on the Twenty from rating a 5, in my opinion.

author: abour
title: Great Girls' Getaway
text: I spent one night at Inn on the Twenty with 2 girlfriends. We shared one of the 2 rooms at the Inn that have 2 queen beds. I really enjoyed everything about the Inn and will definitely be back. Our room was really spacious, with beautiful high ceilings and a fantastic washroom with both jacuzzi tub and a walk in shower. We also really appreciated that the room was prepared for three people on our arrival. There were three bathrobes, coffee cups, wine glasses, and extra towels. It was great to have everything we needed for a relaxing mini-vacation. We had dinner and breakfast at the restaurant and really enjoyed both meals. The restaurant setting is beautiful, the food is very good, and our server at dinner was fantastic. The breakfast was a nice treat, with fresh breads, fruit, granola and a daily hot item, all complimentary. A great way to start a day of wine touring. I had the hydrating facial at the spa and it was the best facial I have had. I was a bit sad that the spa doesn't have a hot tub to relax in before or after the services, but the ambience was very nice, and the quality of the service more than made up for that. Overall, the Inn exceeded my expectations. It has the right balance of relaxed luxury. I think it is truly excellent value for the area and a perfect setting to enjoy Ontario's fantastic wine country.

author: SummerTravellers
title: Top Class Room, Top Class Service
text: We stayed as a couple here on the evenings of November 30 and December 1, 2012. We have stayed in the Niagara region at similar lodging, including Harbour House, but would rank this Inn as at least equal, if not slightly superior. We booked well ahead of time to reserve our desired room, Suite #9, which is located on the cozy northwest corner of the inn. This suite is spacious in terms of square footage, with ceiling heights to match, which vary between 16' to 9'. Three very large windows bring in incredible natural light, even on dreary grey Nov/Dec days. The firepalce is situated in a sitting area, and made a comfortable setting for reading and/or having a glass of wine. No issues with the bedroom or bathroom areas. All areas seemed very well kept, very clean upon our arrival. Little touches added to our enjoyment of our room, including a Keurig in the bedroom, comfortable rug and blanket/throw in the sitting area, and a selection of local themed books, and nature books, among other genre books, in the mini in-room book collection. The rooms here seem competitively priced (for this upper-end price point) with simlar properties in the Niagara region. Include a two night package that includes a dinner at the Inn on the Twenty Restaurant (across the road), a great breakfast in the restaurant both mornings, and a free wine tasting session at Cave Spring Cellars (also across the road), as we did, and you have a recommended weekend experience. Not to mention the numerous small, excellent wineries within 10 minute drive of the inn, for wine lovers. In addition, the reception staff were extremely pleasant, willingly helpful with questions, seemed genuinely appreciative of our patronage, and even gave us a complimentary bottle of Cave Spring 2011 reisling upon check-out. For those looking for a quiet, up-scale mini-vacation locale, I would recommend Inn on the Twenty. A

author: FamfromVancouver
title: Quaint inn offering delicious breakfasts!
text: We stayed at the inn for three nights in early October. We were travelling with our five year old daughter and the room we were booked into was more than enough room for our family. There was a lovely sitting area with a corner fireplace and two queen sized beds. The bathroom was very spacious and included a jacuzzi tub. The inn has a lovely feel to it, very warm and inviting. In the afternoons, warm baked goods and apple cider were put out in the reception area. As another reviewer remarked, some of the furnishings in the reception area are in need of some updating. The bathroom fixtures in our bathroom were also quite dated, which surprised me for an inn of this standard. The furnishings in our room however were quite contemporary and comfortable. The breakfast, which was included with our room, was absolutely divine. The breakfast is served at the restaurant across the street. We were greeted with juice and coffee and a basket of warm freshly baked pastries. The chef also prepares one hot meal item, and there is also a cereal/granola buffet. My daughter and I are vegetarian, and this was easily accommodated. There is not too much in Jordan, and a car is definitely required if you are planning on touring the wineries around the area. There is a great little gift shop selling luxe soaps, bath products, etc. across the way called Beauty Safari. We ate supper a couple of times at the pub attached to Jordan House, the Inn on the Twenty's sister property, about a ten minute walk away. Overall, a great choice and we would return without question.

author: PeskyCanadians
title: Overpriced. All the charm of a nursing home.
text: When we first walked in the door, the lower floor of the hotel was cordoned off with a chain. We walked upstairs to the charmless reception. It looked like a nursing home. Tired chairs in the lobby. The art and lighting was reminiscent of a Howard Johnson. Our room had used magazines, a Jacuzzi and shower stall straight from Home Depot. The bathroom was decorated with grapevine wreaths covered in a layer of dust. You had to call the front desk to get the wifi code. I was asked if I wanted turn down service, I said yes. It never happened. The fixtures were cheap. The bedspread was cheap. Oh, but breakfast was included. The fruit in the morning had been poorly trimmed, so pineapple and melon had green rind still attached. The lattes were lukewarm. The oatmeal was Quaker's finest instant. I could go on and on, but I won't. It was utterly disappointing. ESPECIALLY given the price.

author: RHFamilyof4
title: Have gone for 3 years in a row, great little get away!
text: My husband and I stayed here a few weeks ago for our third time. We went with a group of about a dozen other couples and singles. We had a pre-set dinner arranged at Cave Springs across the street and it was divine. We had wine paired up with each course (there were about 7 courses), each was just great. Before dinner we were given a tour and had wine tasting. After dinner we all gathered at our suite, which was located on the ground floor so had a nice patio area. Room was quite clean and comfortable, bathroom was large and accommodating. We love that there isn't much to do there! We shopped for a bit on the main drag, drove through the area and just relaxed. Would be nice if there were a pool, just to lounge by to have something additional to do. Hubby golfed one day, I went to Buffalo and it was a quick drive. Front desk staff were always available and helpful, even checked the border wait times for me. Breakfast at the CSV for 2 mornings were very good, simple. We opted to have dinner at the Jordan House Tavern and it was good as well, for a pub, friendly staff, nice location. Free wifi but we didn't have any luck with getting good reception. We let them know about this little annoyance. Not really suitable for a family with kids as there really isn't anything to do, but we love it and will go back again next year. Maybe they'll have put a pool in! : )

author: Dear_Penelope
title: Why go to Venice for a romantic getaway trip?
text: Jordan ON, Inn on the Twenty, 3845 Main Street, Jordan, Ontario, Canada L0R 1S0 Inn on the Twenty is one of the best small resorts in the Southwestern Ontario, Canada. We found this place on the Ontario Finest Inns website and went back several times. I would highly recommend it. Located in a small and sleepy town of Jordan, Ontario, in the heart of the Wine Country, Inn on the Twenty offers a little bit of everything for everyone. In my heart, it holds a special spot and it will always be the most romantic getaway place I can imagine. Forget a romantic and expensive trip to Venice – go to Jordan, Ontario :-) The accommodations are superb. The rooms are located in the original, century old Vintage House with high ceiling rooms, comfortable furniture and a corner whirlpool tub in the specious bathroom. The place has a lot to offer, with a fabulous SPA just next door to the inn (or should I say, a romantic walk under the pergola). The staff at the SPA is extremely courteous and remembered our names from the previous visits. The place offers couple massages which was my favourite. On the Twenty Restaurant is this year’s Diners' Choice Winner with a fabulous breakfast menu and gourmet lunches and dinners. The view from the main dining room is just breathtaking. We stayed at the Inn on the Twenty several times, mostly in summer, but one year we decided to celebrate New Year’s Eve there. What a treat! The place is even more special with vintage Christmas ornaments everywhere and snow on the ground. And last but not least - the wine tasting. You can taste the local wine to your heart’s desire in the renovated Cave Spring Cellars Winery. My vote goes to the Cave Spring Riesling and Gewürztraminer wine. The reds are OK, but nothing extraordinary.

author: D_Marchioni
title: I wish all Weddings were held here
text: Awesome! That just about says it all. My son and my new daughter-in-law were married here in June 2011. Everything was picture perfect. The rooms were lovely. I loved the king-sized beds. The room service was quick, efficient and discreet. The food was fabulous. The gnocchi was to die for. The venue was beautiful and overlooked a marvelous ravine/forest area. Everyone commented on how wonderful the place was. And what can I say about the staff! They bent over backwards to accomodate all of our last-minute requests with a courteous smile and quick response. I will definitely stay here again at some time in the near future. An amazing weekend! Dave Marchioni

author: 155019Frank
title: "Great room, friendly staff, superb food"
text: This is our 3rd year of spending a weekend in May or June at Inn on the Twenty. We played 2 rounds of golf at nearby Peninsula Lakes, wonderful golf course, 27 holes, as friendly a staff as you could meet on a golf course anywhere. Golf was arranged for us by the hotel. Our room and the private garden behind it with parking right next to our accommodation has always been outstanding. The staff are very friendly. The ambiance is very good since the hotel is in a quaint little village street type setting. We had all our meals at the hotel (except one lunch at the golf course) which involved a lunch on arrival, 2 breakfasts and 2 dinners which were included in our package. On Saturday evening we ordered the chef's 7 course tasting menu with wine pairings which were almost all from the adjacent and presumably co-owned Cave Spring cellars which also offers tastings and wine tours. I would have preferred some international wines as part of the pairings but the selection of wines offered were surprisingly good including a Gamay, Pinot Noir, Cabernet, Merlot Cabernet, Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay and late harvest Riesling all from Cave Spring Cellars. My wife and I both found the food for the tasting menu to be outstanding and included a sturgeon dish which I have never tasted as a fish before. My wife's tastes were more oriented to vegetarian which the executive chef Mr. Kevin Maniaci was happy to arrange for us. A nice touch was the individually prepared menus printed and sitting on our table with the family name at the top and our individual christian names heading each half of the menu. Service throughout the weekend was excellent. We will most certainly be returning for our 4th year next May or June.

author: dissatisfied96
title: Extremely overpriced
text: Unfortunately started off badly , when I made the inquiry about features on the phone, the attendant was very short and rude. Luckily when I phoned back and am not sure why ,( only because the photos on the website were pretty ), the attendant was very nice. We stayed in a loft suite . It was lovely however very stuffy. The best feature of the loft was the bathroom. The spa as spas go was subpar.. Very cut up , overpriced , attendents expecting a large tip. The breakfast in the morning over at the Inn was not good. The eggs very runny and a very small and poor selection of other items. We were very glad we cancelled our dinner reservations the night before and went to the Lake House which was excellent. The best part about the weekend was the mini wine tour over at Cave Springs. The lady giving the talk was excellent. She was very informative and friendly. It was an extremely expensive overnight and unless you have money to burn there are better value spas and inns. If the quality was there it would be fine but it wasn't.

author: cheshiremackat
title: Third time back... again lovely.
text: My wife and I stayed again for the Valentines Day / Family day long weekend. Again, we had a spectacular time! We booked the "chocolate fantasy" package, which included dinner at On the Twenty restaurant. Dinner was excellent (I had the duck, my wife the trout). Dessert was served in our room. We had quite the assortment of sweets for dessert, it was a very nice experience. The room was clean and large. Bedding was warm and comfortable. The gas fireplace threw off incredible amounts of heat, so continuous use is not recommended, but it did help keep things warm when necessary. If I had to think of a flaw, it would be minor and humourous, but the Innkeeper needs a new dictionary... the "chocolate fantasy" is described as including a "risque" gift from cupid... well our gift was two small mugs for hot chocolate and some truffles... not exactly my definition of "risque". All-in-all an relaxing and warm weekend spent in a lovely inn... we will be back.

author: BeckyAylmer
title: very unique spot to stay-good food-good wine-good rooms
text: My husband and i just returned from a 2 night stay at the Inn. We enjoyed ourselves. The main strip in Jordan when the Inn, restaurant and Cave Spring winery is quite unique with an interesting history. We had the "As YouLIke It" package which included our dinners-one being a dinner designed just for us The food was excellent and the service was professional in every way. The Inn was nice but I have to agree with other visitors-it is more like a hotel. We have been to an Inn before and it was completely different type of experience. It felt a little cold and yes there was no where to sit and enjoy a drink except for a patio outside. Because the restaurant was across the street we needed to go there to eat which was ok I suppose. The spa was wonderful. I want to say the lady who did my massage was Malina or Marina-she was excellent and professional. It was the nicest spa experience I have had. Certainly the most personable. Ihave been to a top rated Spa in the city and you were just another VISA card. This spa does not make you feel this way. Another thing worth mentioning-it has been noted before by fellow travellers-the hotel rooms are hot. It was not warm when we were there but yes-we had the air running the entire time-strange. Overall it was a nice visit. If we were to return we would probably stay at the vintage house next door (part of the Inn) It appeared to have a bit more charm to it.

author: thematriarch08
title: Relaxing Stay at Inn On The Twenty
text: Jordan, Ontario - Inn On The Twenty Date - Nov. 3, 2008 Reviewer - Nora and Dave On a recent trip to Niagara wine country, we spent a night at Inn On The Twenty in Jordan, Ontario. The Inn is located in the quaint small town of Jordan, Ontario and is affiliated with the well known Cave Spring Cellars which I believe is one of the first wineries established in the Niagara Peninsula. The Inn is beautifully appointed with a lovely fireplace in the reception area and a number of quiet sitting areas scattered throughout the building. Our 'alcove' suite was very spacious and included a gas fireplace and a large jacuzzi whirlpool tub. We had purchased the Carpe Diem package which included a complimentary wine tasting at the Cave Spring Cellars across the street from the Inn so after checking in, we strolled over to the winery. The staff were very knowledgeable and poured us tastings of virtually every wine on the list! We decided we had better skip the complimentary wine tasting later in the afternoon at the Inn! The package also included dinner at the On The Twenty restaurant. The meal was absolutely outstanding as was the service and the wine recommendations. The next morning we had breakfast at the restaurant which was also spectacular....freshly baked pastries, waffles with fresh fruit and great coffee....not that we really needed this after our fabulous dinner from the night before! The relaxing atmosphere of the Inn, the culinary delights of the On The Twenty restaurant and the time spent at Cave Spring Cellars made this a great overnight getaway but the secret ingredient to this stay was really the people we met at the Inn, the restaurant and the winery. Everyone was exceptionally nice and nothing was too much trouble. The service was outstanding. We will definitely be returning to Inn on the Twenty!

author: samsmom2006
title: A spectacular small inn with fantastic dining!!!
text: I highly recommend this lovely, high end Inn for a couples getaway. We drove from Columbus Ohio (5 1/2 hours). Had booked a one night with dinner and breakfast included based on TripAdvisor.com reviews. This was our launching spot for a day of biking and vineyard tours out of Niagara-on-the-Lake (with Niagara Wine Tours Int'l). We wanted to save a little bit of money and booked a room in the 2 room Vintage House, a restored 19th century building adjacent to the main inn. Jordan is a beautiful little village. The Inn's gardens were gorgeous. Our room was in excellent condition- very spacious- nice, clean bathroom- comfortable queen size bed. Staff was very courteous and helpful. Dinner was amazing- there were no restrictions as to what we ordered off the menu (often with meal plans they keep you to a short list- not here!). The emphasis was on fresh and native... we had Alberta Bison Tenderloin. The interior of the restaurant was lovely. Lots of older guests and young financial types from Toronto. The Inn's wines (the Inn owns a vineyard) were very good- but of course alcohol was not included in the room rate. We hiked a trail near the Inn. And, finally, breakfast was delicious. I hope this review was helpful.

author: kalliopy
title: Fabulous!
text: My husband and I celebrated our wedding anniversary at Inn on the Twenty and we were not disappointed. We booked the "As you like it" package which included 2 nights stay, 3 course dinner one night, 7 course tasting menu the next and breakfast for both mornings. We also booked massages. The room was absolutely beautiful and dispite what others say, it was very cool in the room and yet is was very hot outside. It was extremely clean and looked beautiful. The spa was amazing. The massage was worth every penny! I can't even begin to say how wonderful the food was at On the Twenty. The 7 course tasting menu was the best idea that anyone had ever come up with. I got a call from the chef, Kevin, the day before we left and we went through a list of things we all liked and disliked. As there were 4 of us for dinner that would be 28 different plates. We had 21 different meals and it was great as we all tried each plate. They are not big but that is the whole point as you have to make it to the end. We had individual menus set up for us and it was fantastic. He couldn't have done a better job. I would recommend this to anyone who is looking to eat some great food, sit back and relax!

author: limecat1
title: Tasteful and tastings!
text: I just returned from the Inn on the Twenty for a "girls' get-away." We had a wonderful experience at the Inn. Upon arrival, we were treated to some delicious shortbread cookies and soon after had a wine tasting in the lovely appointed lobby with other guests. We were personally escorted to our rooms which were in the Vintage House. We had both rooms in the upstairs so it was like our own private house. There was a box of chocolate ice wine truffles waiting for us at the door. We had a private parking spot next the house and a private courtyard with lush flowers and a table and chairs. Breakfast was included with the room and was across the street in the main restaurant. The restaurant was beautifully decorated with an orchid on each table. The food was fresh with locally grown fruit and ingredients. The pastries were light and tastey. The bathroom was spacious and spotless with a small recycling bin and a basket for the dirty towels. The robes in the closets matched the color of the respective rooms. Everything in this small area was within walking distance. It was almost like our own private village. Very quiet. Cave Springs winery across the street had a nice "walk the vines" tour onsite at the vines and a wine tasting afterwards. The second night in the lobby was a plate of chocolate brownies which somehow the lady at the desk insisted that we take the remainder to our room which we gladly obliged. I almost forgot the Spa - book ahead it fills up fast, but we did manage to get massages which were wonderful and relaxing. The cleanliness of the properties and friendliness of the staff were excellent.

author: terridvm
title: the staff is wonderful!!
text: We were quite impressed with this property, and especially the staff. We had booked the Fresh Start package, which includes a suite with fireplace and jacuzzi tub. Unfortunately, we were told at booking that there was a convention there, and there were only 2 small rooms left. We were disappointed, but booked the smaller room anyway. However, when we arrived, they had upgraded us into the Vintner's Suite, a much larger suite, at no additional charge. And this was our experience through the entire stay--the staff continually went above and beyond to make us feel special. The property itself is very small, nice, and clean. If you are looking for nightlife--this is not the place. But it is a quiet, romantic getaway. The food at the restaurant is also wonderful--lots of wild game. Be sure to try the caribou appetizer. As for the area, I cannot say enough good things. I had no idea that Canada even had a wine country, but they have hundreds of little wineries all around this area, many which are every bit as good as the ones in Napa. Once again, the staff at all of the wineries were extremely friendly and helpful. If you are an wine enthusiast, I highly recommend visiting!

author: Coastal23081880866
title: Good service but big problem with the Kitchen
text: I had the opportunity to spend few days at Sofitel West Lake with my wife and kids. We had a very mixed feeling about our stay in your hotel. Initially I sent you a private but since you did not answer, I decided to write this comment on Tripadvisor. First of all we would like to say that receptionnists, barman, maids and waitress/ter are all very professionnals. But unfortunately, there is a problem with the Kitchen which offered to my wife rotten or spoiled food and small piece of rope. During the first breakfast she had palm heart with her salad, unfortunately she realized after eating one palm heart that there were spoiled (green/dark color). We did not expect a 4 or 5 stars hotel to serve rotten food. Furthermore my wife is breastfeeding our last kid and it could have lead to food poisonning for both of them. We reported it to the manager who decided to offer us a bottle of wine, we appreciated the gesture even if we do not drink but at the end it does not solve the problem for your hotel. On the second day she discovered a little cord/string in her food. No risk of food poisonning this time, but still it does not match our expectations of what you should get from a Sofitel Hôtel. It was reported to your manager too. To be honest we are very disappointed by this experience. The reason why we often go to Accor group hotel is because we expect to get high standard services and food safety guarantee. Up to us this experience did not meet the required standards.

author: Pearlfect
title: Convenient location
text: Sofitel Hangzhou Westlake is conveniently located within 5 minutes’ walk to the side of Westlake where the food places are. E.g. near to highly rated 外婆家, Starbucks, secret recipe and some other cafes. Hotel provides car/driver booking for 50RMB/hr, which i thought was pretty reasonable. Driver was polite, friendly and helpful. He even advised us not to buy some stuff at certain touristy places, which he shared that they were overpriced. I thought that was pretty honest if him. Rooms were clean. Daily cleaning and turndown Service. Pillows were TOO SOFT, it’s as good as no pillows even though they gave two pillows per twin bed. Only downside was the room service. Food wasn’t nice. The western food wasn’t nice at all. Fish and chips was so oily, the batter was soggy. Hot chocolate tasted more like chocolate milk. Other food were all very oily and there was little variety on the menu.

author: KevinKSY
title: Total Turnoff That I Wanted To Leave Immediately at Daybreak
text: I stayed at the Sofitel Westlake Hangzhou in July 2018 for business. Pros: • Near the Westlake, a renowed tourist attraction. • It is also near dining and drinking locations • Short distance by taxi to the Hangzhou and Hangzhou East train stations. • Room is generally acceptable. • Staff were helpful and courteous during the check-in, check-out and arranging transport from the hotel. Failure: • One of the pillows in the room had a yellow stain. It was a turnoff. • During the night, I suspected a guest from a neighbouring room was smoking, despite it being a non-smoking room. The smell of cigarette can be smelt in my room and toilet. It was suspected that the cigarette smell was likely to be from the central air conditioning. This caused me to have a bad headache the entire night and the next day. It disrupted my work. In addition, my clothes smelt of cigarette smell. • Inflexible management: I had booked a wrong date on a hotel booking platform. I informed the platform and they got in touch with the hotel. I was told the hotel refused to allow the change to the correct date. In my opinion, I rate the hotel based on various considerations including service, location, comfort and cleanliness of the hotel as well as other aspects of customer service. While the hotel was satisfactory in its location and staff service, the key failures in its cleanliness, the smell of cigarette smoke from a neighbouring room through the central air conditioning and the lack of flexibility would lead to feel that my recent experience warranted a two-star rating. Personally, I would not return to this hotel given my experience.

author: 44ScottZ
title: Tired Queen at The Lake
text: I bet this was a Grand property a few years or decade ago. It Does have a great location, but so sorry ownership doesn't invest in upkeep. The room was very quiet at night. Kudos! I tried speaking English with Bar staff (3), Conceirge (2) and found help only at front desk. Tried the 5th floor lounge, but they wanted to charge 180RMB for the final 20minutes of F&B. Yikes!! I was hoping to relax, not race. The last Sofi I stayed at was in Miami, Fl. Remember it was exactly the modern French Impressionistic this property is NOT. When entering the room on second floor, hit was an aweful smell from bad plumbing, or lack of a vent pipe. The carpet was decades old by appearance, curled and pulled up along the walls. This reservation was booked through Hotels dot Com. IMHO, think Mngt is trying to lure in guests with discounts to fill empty rooms, when they should think about luring through Renuvation. Too Bad, disappointment with such potential.

author: uybenedictec
title: One of the best in Hangzhou in terms of location
text: It is my first time to stay at Sofitel Hangzhou Westlake. As the name suggests, the world-famous West Lake is just across this hotel. The hotel’s facade is old, but the interiors are kept clean which is the most important thing. During check in, I was offered a welcome drink, apart from the welcome drink Accor members get. The check in was a breeze and the front desk officers unsurprisingly knows how to speak in English. My room has been upgraded and I am assigned to stay at the 5th floor. This hotel has 6 floors only. My room is in between the elevator and the lounge, and offers me a partial view of the lake and surrounding areas. The room itself is big and there is a separate toilet and bath and shower. What I probably didn’t expect was the bed to be a bit hard. I was hoping it would be softer for better comfort. I tried to make use of the facilities and they only have sauna at the men’s changing areas. It is rather small for an upscale hotel. During my visit, the pool is under renovation. As my room was upgraded, the room includes free breakfast at the Club Lounge. They pretty much serve anything there, the lady will provide you a menu, but cooking time may reach 20 minutes. Of course, there are fruits and breads ready at the buffet table for those who cannot wait. If you are visiting Hangzhou for business or leisure, this hotel has probably one of the best locations downtown.

author: vtnz
title: Best experience when compare to Sofitel hotels in Australia
text: We have stayed in a number of Accor Hotels. Being an Accor Plus member and with the latest stay included we would have clocked up 18 nights in Sofitel hotels alone. My experience with this hotel chain has been poor previously and hence I have kept my expectation low when I booked Sofitel Hangzhou. We have upgraded ourselves to Sofitel Executive Club floor this time round. My recent experience is a stark contrast to my other experiences in Sofitel Wentworth Sydney, Sofitel Brisbane and Sofitel Gold Coast at Broadbeach. My whole family were blown away to the attentive service given to us by Yuna - Sofitel HangZhou Guest Relation Officer. We were guided all the way from reception to our rooms. What exciting place to visit around HangZhou and what services and benefits we can enjoy during our stay here. The buffet breakfast and lunch at the Kwee Zeen was also of very high quality. We have found that every staffs that we have come across are polite and helpful. A special credit is also given to Robin at the concierge who recommended two fantastic restaurants and which we had a fantastic experience at the local cuisine. My only slight disappointment is with the internet speed at this hotel. It seems rather slow in the era of digital age. We could hardly browse foreign news using its WIFI. In terms of locations, we are glad to have chosen this hotel as it is right opposite west lake and convenient to other eateries and shops nearby. I would recommend this place to holiday makers again.

author: EnLeung
title: Great staff, good location but disappointing buffet
text: Stayed at the hotel for a short break with family. The hotel is easy to get to by taxi and is close to metro and rail stations. There are a number of public buses stopping close by. The hotel is right next to the Westlake which means an evening stroll after dinner is possible. The rooftop bar is a nice place to chill and trust the view of the sunset would be nice though the weather during my stay did not offer me a chance to prove it. The staffs of all kind are very helpful and kind. May be too kind in the first morning of my stay that the lady was banging on the door for over a minute when I was hoping to have a lay-in forcing me to get the door, just to be asked if I have any laundry! I learnt my lesson and switch on the do not disturb for the rest of my stay. The one thing I am really disappointed is the quality of food and the availability of orange juice at the buffet in the western restaurant on the ground floor. We arrived there around 8pm, a few dishes were empty and were not refilled for the time we were having dinner. The is a whole fish that half is gone while the other half was being tortured. The other vegetable dish with the gravy being dried and burnt. My girl got her first glass of orange juice and cannot have a second one because there is no orange juice left for the whole hotel! Unbelievable! Though, I must say the grill to order lamb chop was really nice to be fair. Given the price at RMB250+ per head for hotel guest and the brand name of the hotel, I was expecting the food and drinks are much better quality. So my suggestion would be stay for the location but avoid the buffet. Will I ever stay there again? Likely, but definitely will need a lot of tempting to get me into the restaurant again.

author: lauramF0YR
title: Fabulous location and great service
text: We stayed at Sofitel Hangzhou Westlake for five nights during our 3-week trip to China. We are a family of four and booked two delux rooms with club access and were very lucky to be upgraded to a suite. The rooms were lovely - well appointed and very clean. The in-room Illy espresso machine was outstanding - we were missing good coffee by then! I reckon the machine is way superior to Nespresso (sorry George...). We also enjoyed the club - fun to go for a glass of wine before dinner (although the wine was not great but hey it was free). The breakfast selection was great but the restaurant was quite busy. We never tried the breakfast at the club that clearly would have been more quiet - my kids were worried about not getting all the choice that was available downstairs! We also ate at Kwee Zeen. My daughter insisted on doing the (quite expensive) buffet and being only 10 she did not have much to eat. I was a bit shocked that they did not have a kids' price for it but oh well. We all enjoyed our western meals after 2 weeks in Yunnan and then were ready for more Chinese food again. The service at the hotel was impeccable. Most staff that we saw spoke good English. Because we traveled with kids they had put a kids' bathrobe and a toy in the room, and while my 10-year-old was a bit too old for it she appreciated the gesture. Lovely! We spent a lot of time at the swimming pool because we have kids. The pool is a bit dark and small but it did the trick. The location of the hotel is just amazing - right next to the lake and a walking distance from Hefang Old Street and western malls. We will definitely stay here again next time we are in Hangzhou.

author: /undefined
title: Poor Service
text: I stayed five nights. I reserved superior room with Le Goter afternoon tea once. However, I don't think my room was upgraded even I am platinum member. My room number is 617. My friend is not member, her room is 619 which is as same as my room. Moreover, the so-called La Goter afternoon tea is I could enjoy tea time in the executive lounge. Since I am platinum member, I can access to executive lounge any time. Moreover, the check out service is poor. Only one staff worked in the member counter but 3 staff worked in normal reception counter. The waiting time is longer than normal guest. The staff did not do the check out for me initiatively even they knew I had waited more than 15 minutes. The breakfast time is until 10:30am. I tried twice at 10am. Some of foods are packed and returned back to kitchen. No one prepared the fired egg or noodle in their counter. Moreover, I stayed five nights from 13 April to 18 April. I checked in very late on 14 April early morning because of flight delay; but it does not mean they counted me stay 4 nights only. I just wonder whether they calculate my reward points correctly.

author: SleekVoyageur
title: Great service / Great location.
text: We stayed here twice during our recent China trip. The first check in was just one night stay on the day we arrived at late evening. With prior arrangement, managers/staffs of Sofitel had kindly helped me to receive our train tickets from tour operators for us to catch a train first thing in the morning to Tunxi. Great service. Thank you. Check-in/check out twice were smooth and easy. Staffs were polite and helpful. Rooms(We had 2 rooms): Clean eventhough the decor and furnitures looked a bit aged. Breakfast: buffet style breakfast came with our room package. Delicious with a good selection of food. Coffee was aromatic after drinking some mediocre coffee served in our Chinese hotels. We didnot use their facilities at all, as there were plenty to see at Westlake. One could walk, jog, run or cycle at Westlake. What a beautiful lake. This hotel is a stone throw away from Westlake at Xihutiandi area. The underpath entrance to cross the road is just next to the hotel. There are plenty of restaurants from posh to affordable at the area near by. Carrefour supermarket is round the corner. We would stay here again if visiting Hangzhou next time

author: 878faym
title: Non-smoking request
text: The location is unbeatable. West Lake is just across the street. The facility was standard of a 4-star hotel. I took a star off facility because the indoor pool was closed for maintenance. It was quite a disappointment as swimming is the only workout I do. The only major problem I encountered was the assignment of a smoking room when I had requested for a non-smoking room. The room itself didn't smell like a smoking room. I guess housekeeping did an excellent job in freshen the room. But the bedding, pillows, and mattress was filled with smoke. Unfortunately I did not realize it until I went to bed and as kept up all night coughing due to sensitivity to second hand smoking. When I brought up the problem with the hotel at 5:00am, they quickly rectified the situation and moved me to a true non-smoking room. I just didn't understand why didn't they assign me into a non-smoking room in the first place when I clearly requested at the time of reservation. Most staff are fluent in English. They were courteous, attentive and very helpful. Tim the bellmen especially deserved recognition. I arranged an airport shuttle but didn't realize the luggage capacity was limited and had to take up the last row of seats for storage. My brother and I had to take a separate vehicle when the shuttle could only accommodate my other family members. Tim was assisting us in loading the suitcases when we realized our situation, he reacted quickly by arranging a taxi for us to catch up to the shuttle so we wouldn't have to miss our flight. If we are visiting the West Lake again, I will consider the Sofitel because of its great staff.

author: chrismD2896YF
title: Decent, but a bit disappointing...
text: Hm. Basically a decent place to stay. The location at the Westlake is absolutely supreme. Staff was friendly and efficient. Room large and clean. Dinner in the Hotel Restaurant okay. What was my problem? Expectation Management. I booked the Hotel to get a bit of "luxury" at the end of a family vacation at quite a pricy rate. The Hotel is also highly recommended on trip asvisor...but my room (460) was quite old and run down. Not even a picture at the wall. No view at all. Hotel also has a small footprint, small lobby, no real outside area (apart from rooftop), no shops etc. Hotel could also use a facelift from outside... So overall well managed, but falling behind compared to other international chains. Good for a short business stay, but does not make you want to extend your stay...

author: oliviayooo
title: Not Recommending AT ALL
text: I am writing a long story to share my very upset experience with Sofitel. My flight on 10/Sep to Hangzhou was delayed to 23:00. While the take-off time was confirmed by airline, I called to hotel around 21:30 to inform my arrival might be after mid-night. To my big surprise, I was told my room was cancelled. I was totally shocked since there was no any notification to me before the cancellation. A lady manager Hu claimed 1, The booking was cancelled at 8pm as no credit card guaranteed. 2, The only assistance I could have from her was to book another hotel nearby. 3, In the second call she updated me that hotel tried to pre-charge the room charge from my card but failed since I have pin code with my card, then they cancelled my booking; 4, my booking was through Booking.com, there no direct contact left with hotel so that no one confirmed with me before the cancellation. I rejected her option of assisting me to find another place to settle me down since I have already lost my trust on her. Here are something I could not understand, 1, hotel tried to pre-charge me from my card but failed, was this called " a booking without credit card guarantee"? 2, I used Booking.com for years and my full contact was left with them, every time I could receive confirmation letters from other hotels directly after reserving room, how come that it turned to no valid contact in your hotel. 3, I sent a email on 5/Sep to Sofitel official generic email address and explained the purpose of the stay and inquired some information, all of my booking information was provided in that email. Unfortunately, until today, there was no reply from Sofitel, not even a auto-response. My flight touched down in Hangzhou at 1:40, I was finally checked in to a hotel at 3:00 in the morning. I have never expected the trip was started with a nightmare like this. The hotel is the powerful side in the whole process, pleas show more care to your customers.

author: bobcentreroad
title: excellent location and reasonably prompt service
text: this hotel has a Chinese five star status, at a very convenient location, after crossing a street called Nanshan road, you are in a major part of west lake where tourist crowds flow endlessly. it is so easy for one to walk into that lakeside paved path to watch sunset and have a morning stroll. at nearby bike rental spots, you can hire a bike for a day of casual trip around the entire lake for a mere 30 RMB yuan. on the other side, it is a casual walk to the two streets Hangzhou offers to visitors, Gaoyin street for lots of restaurants of authentic Hangzhou cruizine, and Hefang street, which offers hundreds of local varieties, basically a busy, noisy tourist attraction. to the end of these two streets, it is the famous north-south Yu street, a name for a Song dynasty royal street, now a remodelled commercial and tourist street. for location alone, this hotel is truly worth of being selected. the counter staff speak English to international visitors, but i am not sure of that for other staff members. Anyway, service provided by them are quite reasonably prompt and in various forms, if you ask for it. the room is large, and bathroom amazing, with separate shower (comfortable) and toilet, and a large bath tub, in which you can watch a bathroom TV. more interestingly, there are his and hers basins for two people, most convenient of all. the carpet is relatively new, soft and comfy, TV set also a relatively new model. the hotel is a low building with five floors, not a skyscraper, as city regulations set a height limit for buildings around the lake, so you would not see large crowds in and out of the hotel at one time, a quite relaxed environment, making it possible for staff to pay more attention to you. we had a bay window for a city view, and the window glass lowers noise from the street, Westlake avenue, so it is quite quiet at night. but because of road work for G20 summit, you hear machine noise sometimes. we enjoyed the stay immensely, even quite satisfied about hotel Chinese restaurant food, and might book it again in future. But i have to say that we stayed in an executive room (not suite), so our impressions may be different from others who did not.

author: isimpo
title: Superb Location , Room Needs Improvement
text: I specifically booked the Sofitel West Lake for its location. West Lake was literally across the road and the hotel was perfect for discovering the area by foot. It was a leisurely walk from the hotel to the West Lake Museum where one could get the bearings right and learn a bit about the place. I also stopped by the Pan Tianshou Memorial Museum just down the road to take in some beautiful art. The hotel was also very close to one of the top ten scenes of West Lake, "Orioles Singing in the Willows". From there, my husband and I walked leisurely by the lakeside to the Lei Feng Pagoda and Su Causeway. Then we took a boat to Xiao Ying Zhou island in the middle of the lake, and then took another boat to Gushan Island and had late lunch at the Lou Wai Lou Restaurant. We were so tired we took a taxi from there back to the hotel. If you have more energy, you can actually walk to the Bai Causeway. At night, we walked to Yan'an Road, just east of the hotel to the Yintai Department Store Complex and had a delicious dinner at the very popular Grandma's Kitchen. There are many restaurants within walking distance of the hotel. We also discovered a small store across the back entrance of the hotel selling cheap but very delicious buns for breakfast. I would have given the hotel 5 stars had it not been the faulty central air conditioning in our room. We called for service because it was very warm and musty. Even after servicing, the central temperature control or the fan still did not work properly, and the room was very hot even though it was very cool outside. It was so hot and uncomfortable that I kept waking up at night. Other than that, the service at the front desk as well as the business centre was wonderful, and it was a memorable stay.

author: /undefined
title: wonderul
text: I spent a wonderful and comfortable times, it is the second time I visit the hotel, because of the best hotels in .Sofitel hangzhou West Lake through my experience. I think, general manager of a very clever way of his administration and organization of the hotel, has the coach a team on a large capacity rapid and high-quality work,. The reception was a welcome and fast, Wonderful, clean room, beautiful decor, excellent lighting distribution differs from some hotels. The only thing which I felt a difference is the Wi-Fi is slow. Perhaps because my house I have a speed of 14 MB, This time, used all their restaurants, the food was very delicious, providing a wonderful, thank all the staff at the restaurant. It has a swimming pool perhaps too much but it is very slim and orderly. Hospitality lounge on the fifth floor quiet place to take a break sometimes do, workers in training and activity summit. Finally, I like to: I thank the Director-General so much, it really special work. I thank Ms. / Leona received wonderful to us and asked about our needs. I thank Ms. / Seoul brilliant guidance of our service daily. I thank Ms. / Anna which they ask us and that was lacking something. I thank all the staff at the concierge service to help them always Gemayel them they always ask if something bothers us or the hotel there is nothing negative to be corrected Are we comfortable with, and when I think of one thing and look up I see that everything is wonderful in this hotel fact, I felt like I was with my family. Thank you to all the hotel staff. I'll see you again.

author: davirena
title: Does not meet the expected Sofitel 5-star standard.
text: Despite the convenient location, the hotel is old and need refurbishment. I booked an upgraded room, but was put into a very old and worn room upon check in. Luckily the front desk staff was able to help me move to a newly renovated corner room, which was beautiful. However, the quality control of the housekeeping was lacking. The bathmat was really dirty and disgusting. We ordered in-room breakfast which taste was great, and the juice is really fresh. However, the design of the room was a miss, because the room service table cannot even fit the entrance in between the wardrobe closet and the luggage table. So my husband had to help the server to lift up the whole room service table to get pass through that. What a service by ourselves. And this happened both times on the 2 days we stayed there. On the first day of arrival, we tried to book a tour guide to accompany us tour the city the next day with the concierge. The concierge told us to go the Level 2 to the business center where they can help us to arrange. The business center staff had no clue, so we went back to complain at the concierge. Only then, they helped us and they were finally able to sort out for us a very nice tour guide for the next day. Accor management definitely needs to step in to get things fixed in this hotel.

author: adaraymond
title: Great location. Nice rooms. But don't expect westlake view from your room....
text: Spent 2 nights there on a business trip. Chose this hotel because of (a) location, (b) relatively less expensive and (c) Sofitel brand. Sure that is an old building but Sofitel has got it properly managed. Looks like it has got a refurbishing not long ago. Got upgrade to executive floor. The hotel's just 3 min walk away from a main entrance to the shore of westlake which is still very beautiful despite of the always hazy weather - an excellent (in Chinese standard) job of the management authority. Another 10 min walk will bring you to a major shopping area in which a big Apple Store situates. Hotel lobby is pretty good. Lobby lounge is also good. Staff is friendly and helpful. Room is proper-sized and nicely Sofitel-style fitted. Really like the sealed packets of tea leaves, not tea bags. The only drawback (which is immaterial to me) is you don't have any nice view from the window - either your room is facing a busy street which could be noisy (I don't really know) or the back of a residential block which you can see people cooking in their kitchens at night. Breakfast at lobby cafe is not very appetizing although the variety is not bad... Overall a good choice to stay in Hangzhou.

author: GeekRockChick24
title: Close to both West Lake & the city makes a great experience
text: I stayed here for two nights with my husband and my dad, booking two separate rooms. My husband and I were upgraded to a king-size room, which was incredibly large and luxurious and faced the street, whereas my dad's standard twin room was far smaller and your standard hotel room, which faced the back side of the hotel. The rooms were on the same floor but not next to each other, which was fine, thought it would've been nicer to be next to each other. Our room had both a shower, a separate bath tub, two sinks, and the toilet separated off, which was very practical. The location of the hotel itself is very convenient. It is within 10-minutes walking distance of a quiet part of the West Lake that isn't overrun with tourists. I found this part of the lake to be nicer than the western and northern parts of the lake which had lots of tourists and tourist cars that would just make everyone else get out of the way. It is also within 15 to 20-minutes' walking distance of the downtown area where you can go shopping and go out to eat. Breakfast was also worth the add-on. Food ranged from continental breakfast (bread, cheese, croissants, etc.) to American-style breakfast (eggs, bacon, potato) to Chinese-style (Hong Kong-style noodle, dim sum, you tiao, congee), and included a really nice range of fruit (bananas, oranges, dragonfruit, apples). We were full enough from breakfast that we only needed a small snack during the day. My only minor complaint was the concierge. When we asked if there were any good restaurants nearby that served local Hangzhou cuisine, he looked at us blankly and suggested the hotel restaurant. However, he didn't really try selling it; he just said, "The hotel restaurant is very good," and when asked more specifically about the menu, he just shrugged. This could've been due to a language barrier, but at a five-star hotel in a place like Hangzhou that has many tourists from everywhere and not just China, I would've expected slightly better service. Then again, the concierge was very helpful in getting us a taxi to go out to the Longjing tea fields and Lingyin Temple. I definitely recommend this hotel if it's your first time in Hangzhou. It made for a lovely stay, especially after a long day of walking around the West Lake.

author: sherrysers
title: nice stay
text: location.great and convenient. near to west lake. staff. friendly and helpful. service. great. very welcoming and up to par room. big spacious. clean . comfortable. value. reasonable. valued for money. sleep. quiet and sleep soundly.

author: ChuckL_Seattle
title: Wonderful weekend at West Lake
text: Planned to spend the weekend in Shanghai but ended up in Hangzhou on short notice. Was stressing out about lodging because it was a busy weekend. Ended up at Sofitel West Lake and my problem was solved. It's China so I was prepared to be put thru the ringer for last second booking. After some negotiation, their ***extremely charming*** front desk manager Linda found me a room at a reasonable price. Linda even threw in free breakfast. Was prepared to proposed at this point, but sadly all I had was a bag of Jelly Belly. Did not experienced the renovation problems staff mentioned. No construction noise, AC was ice cold. Room had great city view with a slice of the lake. The fresh fruits and cookies were nice touch. Can't complaint about the location. walk thru the underpass the lakeside mall greets you with Starbucks and Haagendazs. After the familiar, venture out to the scenic West Lake and blend in with the gracious locals. Here's a pro tip - take the island ferry, two hops get you far. Walk as much as you want, then take the taxi back. One of the best "change of plan" ever.

author: cindy_vsc
title: Beautiful luxury hotel though staff assistance should be improved
text: I believe the hotel is very good however the staff should be less passive in communicating and be more trained. The ladies at the check-in desk were wonderful and helped us very kindly to check in. As a platinum card holder we got upgraded, complimentary drinks, breakfast and access to the executive lounge. The hotel's location is great, fantastic breakfast with a wide selection of Western and Asian food, the room was fantastic, great bed, comfortable bathroom, nice toiletries and fast service from housekeeping. Unfortunately the room temperature was way to high however the air conditioning was not working which made it quite uncomfortable to sleep though the bed was great. My partner booked a special spa package which turned out to be great however we had to inform ourselves instead of the staff informing us. This communication issue came back during our entire 3 day stay. Staff is very kind and patient however a bit helpless as they are seem clueless about most issues. Also, while we were arranging our treatments it was hard while there were so many staff we talked to and we were not assisted by one person. This also caused us to follow up a bunch of times to handle things. As well when asking if someone could fix the air conditioning we were told the first time that it would be fixed. Upon returning back to the room at night it was not fixed yet and after another call it turned out that it has been disable trough out the entire hotel (as this is obliged by law while it is not hot enough yet). It would have been better if we would have been told this the first time. On our last day we made sure to inform the front desk we wanted to book a taxi which was no problem. We confirmed this another 2 times afterwards. Once we checked out and sat down to wait for our taxi the general manager told us it is not possible for the hotel to book a taxi. This gave us a some stress as we had to catch our train. The congiere managed to get one on the phone which was in the neighborhood and showed up after 10 minutes.

author: LoyaltyLobby
title: Extremely Poor Service & Staff Beyond Unhelpful
text: Was supposed to stay at the Sofitel Hanzghou for a Sunday night but..... 1. Made prepaid booking on Orbitz.com because hotel was not available on Accor's own website. 2. Arrived to hotel using a taxi and no bellboys in sight. Had to get luggage by myself from the trunk and carry them to the lobby. 3. Le Club Accorhotels check in desk was unmanned (I am Platinum member). 4. Hotel unable to find the prepaid reservation that I had made on Orbitz because hotels own reservation center is closed on sundays and they apparently manually type in reservations that come in. 5. I requested General Managers business card so that I could let him/her know about the issues with the attempted check in. Staff cannot provide me with a business card. 6. While waiting in the lobby, I decided to book another hotel. No bellboy again to help getting a cab and loading my bags to the trunk. I cannot understand how Accor allows this hotel to carry their flagship Sofitel brand considering all the service shortcoming from missing bellboys to trying to locate a reservation. There are many other far better options in Hangzhou and you should really avoid this disastrous hotel.

author: /undefined
title: Acceptable only
text: I booked the room thru Accor. Then according to my profile, they should notice I need a non-smoking room. Yet when I checked-in, the staff told me that non-smoking room was all sold-out. I said I can't live in smoking room (because of my trachea problem). Then the staff suddenly could arrange me another room. I felt strange, didn't she say non-smoking room are sold out? When I came to the room, I noticed it was a trick. They arranged me the smallest room I ever lived in Sofitel. I wonder whether this was the room I booked. But I came there for business, so I just reluctantly accepted it. Room is facing the street so it's kind of noisy. Plus, the upper floor is being renovated. I couldn't sleep well everyday in the morning. Friends in Hangzhou told me that the given price can find a better hotel there. Thus I think improvement is needed, as this is Sofitel!

author: 22Raffles
title: Fantastic, warm staff and great location !
text: We stayed here for 3 nights from March 25 to 28. Our first time in Hangzhou and couldn't have picked a better location. Our room on the 5th floor was larger than expected and in good condition. Enjoyed the walk and the bike rides around the lake ! Although the weather was somewhat cold and drizzly on two of the days, we were encouraged by the warmth of the folks at the hotel. There are too many individuals to name ! All good folks. No bad service experience to speak off. The few individuals who stool out: James and Burning(Club level), and Yuna, the Assistant Front Desk Manager. The housekeepers, and the boys at the concierge went out of their way to please us. These folks did not let the language barrier get in the way of great service(by China standard). The breakfast restaurant was understaffed for sure. We felt sorry for the waiters and waitresses. Selection at breakfast at both the restaurant and the Club lounge was average at best but the bubbly made up for it ! Overall, a great stay and will look forward to returning hopefully soon.

author: 1-Around-World
title: Excellent service, older hotel, good location
text: Sofitel Hangzhou Westlake is situated in a good location directly across the street from beautiful West Lake. To get to the lake, one would need to use the underground pedestrian pathway (looks like stairs access to a subway). There is a high-end restaurant inside the hotel and a few others within walking distance. There are also some silk shops nearby. Hotel seems older but is still clean - and parts were under construction, so may be undergoing renovation. Lobby is clean and airy. Rooms have high ceilings, so makes for a more spacious feel and bathrooms are clean with nice L'Occitane toiletries. As a business traveller, what was inconvenient was poor internet wi-fi signal in the rooms. Amenities: There is a gym, but it is smaller and a bit dated. There is a club lounge which is very nicely decorated and provides a relaxing atmosphere especially for happy hour in the evening. It is also worth it to pay for the breakfast buffet for one day - the spread is excellent (try the bread pudding!). Service is excellent - hotel staff are very polite and helpful. Taxis were never a problem because the staff would help me to arrange beforehand. As mentioned in my other reviews, don't forget to ask for a hotel business card which includes locations/sites in both Mandarin and English (easy to point to when in a taxi). In summary, it is a nice hotel with great service and location. It fits the bill for the price point.

author: smel_98
title: Old and Rundown - not a Sofitel
text: Just as others have mentioned, this is not a Sofitel. There is nothing 5 star about it. The location is good, right across the road from the Westlake, but that’s where the positive ends. We stayed on the club floor due to the bad reviews, as we thought that by paying a little extra we might get a decent room. We were wrong. The room, the lobby, and the restaurant were all as worn out as one another. As for the Club Lounge, I felt like I had to have a shower after sitting on those chairs for the five minutes we were in there for evening drinks. I don't know why they bothered since when we arrived for breakfast it was closed. We enquired at reception only to be told Club Guests should proceed to the restaurant for breakfast today. Breakfast; we were shown to our table only to come back to it to find someone else had also been seated there. Then we had to wait, holding our plates of food whilst they set another table for us. We had to get our own coffee and clear our own table. To top it all off, one of the staff standing around doing very little, was leaning up against the side wall with his finger planted firmly up his nose - although by this stage I was not at all surprised by his behaviour. It sums up the morale and work ethic on display by all, and the dilapidated state of the hotel in general. Its not only expensive for China, but you would get better than that for the same price in Europe. If it was the first Sofitel I had ever stayed in, I wouldn't bother with any of them ever again. Mr Sofitel should really take a look at this one. I could go on, but all you really need to know is just don't do it.

author: thequeeeen
title: Smokitel
text: Sofitel is located right by Westlake and is literally a 3-5 minute walk from Westlake. The hotel has a somewhat awkwardly positioned entrance and not many taxis are willing to drive right to the door. They'd stop 20-30m away or along the main road, those with unwieldy luggage in tow should note the slight inconvenience. There's a convenience store about 1 minute away, Carrefour and McDonalds are about a 8 minute walk away. There are also plenty of cafes at Westlake, for those looking for the comforts of home, there's Starbucks, Costa and Haagen Dazs too! It's location is its main selling point. The hotel lobby is smokey, having the cigar bar nestled in the corner of the lobby doesn't help. We were allocated a non-smoking room, but the corridors reeked of smoke. We could see our neighbour smoking in his room. Surely there should be non-smoking floors? Rooms were a decent size, decor and design was dated, not something I'd say would live up to it's "luxury hotel" branding. Beds were hard and there was no air-conditioning in the room. I think the hotel is centrally heated and the rooms were overly warm, there was nothing housekeeping could do about this. Customers are largely local, expatriates are few and far between. The command of English of the staff was poor to mediocre, likewise about the service. We had asked the lady at the business centre to assist with a restaurant reservation, she rudely told us that our rooms had phones which we could use! Sofitel serves its purpose as a clean hotel to retire to at the end of the day, location wise it's great.

author: mjc1959
title: Just how old is the carpet? Where is the lake?
text: They upgraded me to a club level room which is nice ... er, I guess. Like the other two sofitels I stayed in, things just look grubby. Why is that? I don't feel like walking barefoot in my room. The view from the window is straight into an apartment complex. Maybe they put the curtains on the windows here to stop the view from coming in. Basically I would take a smaller room which looked like it had been updated in the last 15 years or so. And the room was very expensive. After reading the reviews again, I wondered if I had come to the wrong sofitel. I just stayed in an ok mediocre best western in nanning and it was better then this. I'm paying four times as much. And it's not exactly lakeside. I'm thinking I may as well have just stayed in the city center where hotels are cheaper and more appealing. This will be the last sofitel for me. Big thumbs down on this place.

author: jennwong
title: Not Worth the Cost
text: I've stayed at numerous Sofitel Hotels around the world, and can say with honesty that the Hangzhou Westlake is the worst. For the prices we were paying, we could have just as easily stayed at the Hyatt, which from what we hear is fantastic all around. Our problems started with check-in. The site that we booked through mistakenly booked us into a 2 twin bed room instead of a single king size. The receptionist insisted that there were no other rooms available in the entire hotel, which seemed doubtful as it wasn't supposed to be an especially busy weekend. After discussing our options with her and getting nowhere, we asked to see the manager - it turned out that the manager had been standing at the reception area that entire time and despite our obvious distress, didn't even bother coming to see what the problem was until she was specifically requested. She told us that if we wanted to book a room with a king sized bed, we would have to pay for the upgrade. She also said there were rooms available - cost aside, why wouldn't the hotel automatically upgrade us without the hassle and cost? If there are rooms available, it just seems like good customer service. Instead of offering this, she immediately told us there would be an additional charge, and then called the travel agency we booked through to validate that there was a mistake in the booking. In the end, and about a 20 minute wait, we were given the upgrade. Once we got to the rooms, it was another disappointment. We booked a deluxe suite and were upgraded to god knows what, because the room we were given was dingy and completely outdated. The carpet looked stained and old, and the walls were dirty without any paintings or decoration. The TV was about 5 years old and dirty, like something you would see in a budget hotel, and to top it off, the sound tracking was off for all the channels so there was a 5 second delay from when someone on the television would say something to when you would actually hear it. The bathroom was also a bit of a disappointment - a shower stall that leaked on the floor, a bathtub with no shower curtain, a hair dryer that looked like it was from the 90s and blew out hot air that smelled like burning hair. The final complaint we had was with the lobby cafe - advertised as a 'magnificent lobby cafe with huge windows that look out onto the lake' is a ridiculous lie, the cafe is just as dirty and dingy as the rest of the damn hotel. The carpets were seriously stained and the couches were falling apart - on top of that, the morning of check out time, I waited in the cafe while my boyfriend was checking out and a staff member came over and told me I couldn't sit there unless I ordered something, even though I was the ONLY person in there. All in all - if we were paying budget prices for a budget hotel, all my above complaints would be invalid. However, for a 'world class hotel', the Sofitel simply doesn't meet up, and is definitely not anywhere close to a 5 star hotel.

author: FeltonS
title: Impeccable service and a superb location.
text: The location simply can't be beat: right on West Lake, across from the restaurants and walking paths of Xi Hu Tiandi. The building is a bit dated, but very, very well maintained. The service staff is excellent. My request for a power adapter was fulfilled immediately. Room service was quick and friendly. Some of the best trained and most polite staff I've found in China. My only complaint with service concerns the concierge desk. This is extremely important to foreigners who stay in their hotel, and so I was disappointed to have trouble with one of the members of the concierge staff. When I asked for a taxi, rather than get me one with a meter, he negotiated a flat-rate price for me. Obviously, as a business traveler, this is unacceptable - I need a receipt! I ate in the Western-style buffet, and it's one of the best that I've encountered in china (and I've encountered many). Worth visiting. Superb! However, the gym facilities are comically bad. The locker room is dingy and not acceptable for a five star facility. It doesn't feel clean or maintained. The gym itself is a joke: two old treadmills, a stair climber, and some weights. It's the sort of gym maintained because they need to say that they have one, not because they want the best one. If you are a business traveler who wants a quality gym experience, this hotel is NOT for you. But otherwise, it's first rate and highly recommended.

author: jamesbond_ppk
title: Best service ever.
text: This hotel offered the best service I have seen in a really long time. Simply amazing. Again, being a frequent Sofitel customer, I was upgraded at check in. I spent the first night on the street side. The view is ok, but isolation towards the street is bad, so beware, it can be noisy. On the second day, I was joined by my girlfriend. Before her arrival I asked the concierge for a vase to put her flowers in when we'd get back. From that moment on, a strange machine started. The assistant manager with a staff of 4 decided to help me making this stay memorable. They worked for about an hour to do their utmost, just for us... I was upgraded, again (this time from the quiet side, but the view is quite poor), and they invaded my room with red roses. We got special bath robes, and everything I asked for was done at once, perfectly. It was so much I had to warn my gf of the over "cheesy" reception that was waiting for her... Basically, amazing service, everything was done so that our stay would be fantastic. And it was. Thank you, Sofitel Westlake :)

author: MR-Meijer
title: Nice hotel witha beautiful view!
text: As businessman I’m often in Asia. Hong Kong, Taipei, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Xiamen, Hangzhou, etc., etc.. Mostly I choose Sofitel. In Hangzhou I always choose the Sofitel West Lake Hotel. It is a nice, good and not to big hotel with a beautiful view over the West Lake. Almost everything is like a good Sofitel standard. In the lobby and by registration desk every one is very friendly. As special the relation officer Iris is very cooperating. Whit an American boyfriend is her English not only perfect, but she also try’s to make your stay as pleasant as possible. Train tickets, a taxi on time, or arrange a bottle of wine from one of the restaurants to your room. Nothing is too much for her. She is very professional and knows the meaning of service. Only the telephonist from the room service was not so professional and spoke very bat English. They must also tell me the different between Club or non Club room, excepting the price. Also when you want to make a reservation by e-mail to [--] , they always refer to the website, and than you must make a reservation by the website and that cost me a lot of time. The Sofitel in Shanghai is than more professional. One simple e-mail or fax, and a confirmation are enough. But the rest is very good.

author: Claiyee
title: Five-star service
text: My friend and I stayed at the Sofitel Westlake for 2 nights. We were very happy overall. Here are the pros: 1. Location - It's very central and close to Westlake, Hefang St (full of shops) and "Orioles singing in the willows" (a gorgeous garden near Westlake). It's a short taxi ride to everything else. I felt the Shangri-la had a more scenic location but I wasn't prepared to pay almost double for a room with a lake view and no breakfast. 2. Staff - I had no problems with the staff's English language ability. They were excellent, polite and efficient. Through them we managed to book a fantastic day tour of Hangzhou (with a cruise on Westlake and visits to Peak Flying from Afar, Lingyin Temple, Dragon Tea Well village, Silk Museum to name a few places) and they handled our airport transfers and suggested places to eat. 3. Breakfast and room service - The buffet breakfast is fantastic with a very wide selection (e.g. hot English provisions, pastries, porridge, noodles, cheese plate, cured meats plate, yoghurt and fruit, cereal ...etc). The room service prices are so reasonable and the dessert (creme brulee, cheesecake) is very tasty. Cons: 1. Pool - This needs an upgrade. It's beginning to look a little old. However, sauna is great.

author: kristyb562
title: Pass on this hotel.
text: I had to stay at the Sofitel because my work booked the hotel. I had a nice room that overlooked part of the lake and a busy intersection at the front of the hotel. The street noise was very loud and when I asked to switch to another room they moved me to a room that faced an apartment building. I could literally reach out and touch them. It wasn't any quieter so I made them move me back to my orignal room. After 11pm the street noise dies down. The walls are paper thin. I could hear every single person walking down the halls.
