Next door I could hear a couple loudly enjoying their night....it was very uncomfortable to say the least. Don't eat at the buffet near the lobby. The food is questionable and the service is horrible. The restaurant at the club level was good and the view is pretty. The food was limited, but good. Try the noodles. If you have to stay here request a room that faces the lake on the club level and bring some earplugs. The bathroom is very nice and I loved the toiletries.

author: barolobrain
title: Nice hotel with a great location
text: It's all about location. The Shangri La is the choice for many and indeed it has a beautiful location although it's bit of a walk to downtown and Qinghefang. The Hyatt, also on the lake is a very large hotel, located downtown. For us, the Sofitel was perfect. A 10 minute walk to the Qinghefang Neighborhood of Hangzhou, near 3 boat launches and about a 20 minute walk to downtown, situated on the lake. We had room 401, located on the NE corner of the building. Room was nice, quiet and comfortable. Broadband was free and the hotel has decent drinking and eating facilities. The 5th floor is the club floor and has access to food and drink exclusive to people on that floor. We tried to book but with only 5 days notice and the fact that it was the last week of the Hangzhou expo, we were out of luck but ultimately, it did not matter. Staff are helpful with a decent command of English if needed. Breakfast buffet was decent, a mix of Chinese and Western and the cigar bar was comfortable and relaxing. We had easy access to Qinghefang, Leifeng Pagoda, boats to Xiaoyingzhou Island and downtown and Xihu Tiandi. We only stayed two nights but would recommend at least three nights to see most of the sights and get a good sample of the fine food that Hangzhou has to offer. We will be going back and will definitely book thit hotel again.

author: BlueSkyChina
title: Feeling almost like home !
text: Just arrived in Hangzhou with family (2 kids) we really have been enjoying the professional and nice service during our 6 weeks stay at this hotel !!! Nice location: direct on the lake, walk distance from shops (for foreigners too!) Good breakfast and flexibility for food preparation: The staff was really kind to help us with adjustments (custom made menu for supper served on time, snacks preparation for schoolkids...). Each time that we had something to suggest somebody was hearing, understanding and TAKING ACTION ! Waow ! The breakfast buffet is furnished with good bread (French people telling you !) and they keep improving the choice. We met with others guests who were happy there too. Some were staying for months and even years ! Don't forget to try their cocktail buffet at the end of the day ! Funny and colorful things to taste ! Big and cosy rooms with huge suite: We did several stays at this Sofitel, so we tried different rooms too. All of them were ok. We appreciated the fresh flowers and the fresh fruits plate. The suite should be recommanded to every family ! Huge compared to other ones we have tried ! What else ? We liked it soooo much that we went back during one of the last typhon !!!

author: Kaustria
title: Serene oasis next to Westlake
text: We recently took the train from the brand-new and ultra-modern Shanghai South railway station to Hangzhou. The train station itself was an architectural marvel to behold and the two hour train ride to Hangzhou was easy and pleasant. Soft seat train tickets were RMB (13$) for the roundtrip journey. We took a taxi to the Sofitel, located at at big traffic intersection but with excellent view of the lake and you can reach the lakeside promenade by crossing the square. The hotel lobby is modern, calm and soothing with a a sleek koy-fish stocked pond, elegant and stunning floral arrangements and a very pleasant seating area and daytime coffee-house bar. There was plenty of extremely helpful staff at the reception, concierge as well as in the stores and bars. We had a room on the Executive Level on the 7th flor which also provided access to a gorgeous lounge/bar restaurant with sleek and elegant oriental design features, international newspapers, a fully stocked bar, and coffee and tea available all day long. Our room was not very large but beautifully appointed, all color-coordinated in deep burgundy, gold and matching shades and it had a big bay window overlooking the intersection and lake. The room came fully equipped with an internet ready laptop plus the usual niceties of thick white bathrobes, umbrellas, all sorts of scented toilet accessories, safe etc. A bowl of fruit was brought to us right after check-in (which we did with a special receptionist on the executive floor) and happily settled into our room. A lavish breakfast buffett with full service (included in the roomprice) was served on the Executive floor and in the late afternoon there is a Happy Hour on the open-air grass terrace outside of the bar with a generous sampling of small delicacies and complimentary drinks. We enjoyed our camparis as we plotted our sightseeing route for the next day. The staff could not have been more helpful a lovely woman from Holland gave us several tips on which tea plantation to go to and some other tourist advice and we felt we had absolutely chosen the right place for our 2 days in Hangzhou. It is not cheap but it is worth the money. Bike rental in the hotel is available and my only " complaint" would be that the rental bikes were really old and shabby and in very poor condition. A one-hour a day free rental is included in your room and every hour after that is Y20. I would suggest to management that they upgrade to a few new bikes it is possible to take a leisurly ride around the lake without returning with a backache. Other than that, everything was perfect! Karin Will post some pictures after I get back to the US.

author: SaltheFatFish
title: Not a good choice at all...
text: This hotel suffers from a poor design and use of its location advantage, so much so that what it's supposed to be have, it lacks. First, its location right next the West Lake is supposed to be a great plus, but the hotel rooms face the streets instead. Construction of a subway (which is expected to take at least 2-3 years) right in front of the hotel means whatever nice view is marred. Second, the restaurant which faces the Lake is supposed to have a beautiful deck. But it's a Chinese restaurant which serves loud crowds (there are no quiet Chinese reataurants). It's meaingless trying to sit at the deck to get a view of the Lake, as you won't be allowed in unless u eat the restaurant. The place also closes at 9 pm, which means sipping coffee or tea or a drink or two at the deck is not possible in afterhours. Also, this hotel is meant for leisure visitors. Its business facilities are not meant to be used. Its business centre staff does not know how to operate the photocopy machine properly. Any incorrect prints must be charged, something not usual in 5-start establishments. The internet speed is also excruciatingly slow. It's free, that's why, you may say. But even if you are willing to pay more in order to get your work done, it's not possible. Finally, the non-smoking rooms are not really cigarette smell free. Maybe because some guests are simply incosiderate, but I have to sleep with cigarette small for 4 nights even though I asked for a non-smoking room. Any attempts to spray freshener in the room are also useless. For the amount of money I paid (RMB 880/night), I think I am much better off staying at the Hyatt (RMB 1080/night), which includes breakfast! The Sofitel may be new and near the bars and coffee houses, but no thanks, I don't think I will stay here again.

author: RayTopple
title: Not 5star but very good all round hotel
text: Firstly no idea why 5 star appears. It’s not. What is 5 star are the staff. Attentive, friendly and efficient. The rooms are ok, the shower is ok, the bed is ok, the view is to die for. It is a good all round hotel. Nice pool area and pool bar. All inclusive from 10-22. The food is always hot and there is generally a selection. A lot of comments moan about the food. Look at what you are paying per night and then judge. Not had an inedible meal not had to go out for food and we are fussy. My moans? Great coffee at breakfast but only instant available after. Packed lunch- nice they offer but not really worth carrying around. No kettle in rooms. Apart from that very pleased with the hotel, the weather and the area. We have a pool view and yes it noisy until 23-30 but the payoff is - the view. I would recommend Golden Sands for a cheap break in wonderful Corfu.

author: amyhensman87
title: Great friendly hotel
text: I don’t normally write reviews but on reading some bad ones, we thought the record needed setting straight! We arrived and were greeted by a very friendly receptionist whom every morning greeted our 18 month old son. The room was small and yes dated but it had everything we needed and was very clean. Fresh towels were given daily and the beds and floors were always made and clean. I will add that the mattresses were a little firm but we still managed to sleep ok. The pool areas were spotless and the day beds were a great addition. The food was fine. Yes I’ve had better, by myself, my husband and our toddler always managed to find something to eat. Some of the veg was sometimes undercooked. The young men who cleared the tables were very friendly and always made an effort to speak to our son. The all inclusive drinks were ok. The wine and beer was fine but the cocktails should be avoided. Our stay was very pleasant and we would go back. Considering what we paid for our honeymoon, I think it was fantastic. Thankyou Golden Sands Hotel

author: Taresa24
title: Shocking !
text: We have just arrived home after a week at The Golden Sands . We arrived & the room was very dusty it was late so we went to bed . Got up for breakfast , the food was cold & under cooked . Utensils dirty . People going down with sickness. All inclusive - yet guest were eating out all meals due to the under cooked meat & Luke warm /cold food . Trying to get a Thomas Cook rep to visit to see the food was impossible . Told no rep in the area all week explained the food was unedible but still wasn’t interested . Lots of complaints from other guest . The hotel reception staff , bar staff were very friendly & polite . But the food let it down which is such as shame as the scenery is beautiful & the whole holiday experience would’ve been great if they could just get the food & cleaniless sorted . First time visiting Corfu & it put a dampener on the holiday . We had to eat all our meals out when we had paid for all inclusive . We were told by another restaurant that the problem had been in that hotel for 3 years yet still not been sorted . Even people at the other end of the resort said what hotel you in we told them they said poor you we’ve all heard about how bad the food is there under coooked . So it got around resort pretty fast ! Would I go back , no . Thomas Cook let us down big time in resort - they failed in their duty of care .

author: L8800TRdavidh
title: Amazing Time
text: Just spent 7 nights at this hotel and can't fault it.. yes the rooms are slightly dated, could do with a freshen up but towels and bedding changed daily.. bathroom and main room moped daily. Food was ok, plenty of choices to suit everyone, you get what you pay for and for what we paid we where more than happy. All inclusive Bar open till 10 at night.. beer on tap is a good beer and all cocktails made with house spirits but no complaints with us. Now for the barman Thanos.. this guy is an asset to the hotel. Friendly, lively allways got a smile on his face.. Rented bikes from spiros next door. I had a moped for 15 Euro for the day.. 5 Euro petrol and away we went.. explored the mountains and had a fun day riding around on these. Couple of evenings popped into a bar called Easy Busy.. very friendly in there and had a good laugh as he tries to sing along to English songs and dance. So you've probably read some bad reviews on this hotel but what people think there gonna get for as such a cheap holiday for 7 nights all inclusive is beyond me. Would definitely recommend and would definitely go back. Thanks Golden Sands for an amazing week in Corfu.

author: KasiaS1710
title: We loved our stay in that hotel!
text: I was there with my boyfriend. We knew that this is only *** hotel so didnt expect luxury, modern rooms. Honestly, we went there for a chicken feed and I thought I would be regret that choice. However it was a perfect time with my partner! The pool was big enough, room was not „new” but it was cleaned every day and the towels were changed. It was really clean and tidy. One beach is 3-5 minutes from the hotel (I can recommend it) and the other „Issos” beach is 15-20 minutes from the hotel and it”s excellent! Sandy beach and beautiful, cristal water... Unfortunatelly you have to pay 7€ for two sunbeds and umbrella but this is for all day. Finally, the staff of the hotel is awesome! They are so kind and helpful that I cant even find words to describe them. If you want to go sightseeing you can hire a quad from the kind Man next to the hotel. We visited Chlomos, Marathias and a lot more. The views were breathtaking.. I came back home today morning and I miss that place so much! I would definitely go there again. (Sorry for any mistakes, this is not my first language).

author: 42jillc
title: Some good,some bad
text: We booked this hotel at the start of the year for a week from 2nd August - 9th August 2018. We were going to give the Greek islands a miss this year but my wife got itchy feet so we were offered this hotel for a week for a price much cheaper than what we normally pay. Reading Trip Advisor reviews we went with an open mind, We arrived to be met by a very friendly receptionist and a clean looking hotel so initial thoughts were quite good,the room we were allocated was dated but clean, we had none of the problems other guests have complained about such as ants (funnily enough we get ants in our house in wales during the summer). The bathroom was clean although some of the fittings were dated but working and as some reviews complain of water rising up through the drain you will find this to be a common problem throughout Greece as we have found in 5* and 4* hotels we have stayed in. There is no safe in the room but you have the option of using a hotel safe in reception for a small charge, however we used our flight suitcases with a padlock which was suffice. The food is decent enough, some complain of ham for breakfast instead of bacon but i quite enjoyed the ham and eggs (how can 3 billion Americans be wrong, ham and eggs is good enough for them), plenty of choice on display as i consider a decent breakfast the most important meal on holiday as you can eat out the rest of the day. Lunch and evening meal was ok but we did struggle with our 12 year old with rabbit and liver. The hotel grounds are in good condition although the white sunbeds are in a very sorry state with cracks and sharp edges which can cause nasty cuts and the pool itself is in very good condition and cleaned daily. There is no beach towel hire at this hotel - you can take your room towels down to the pool but not down to the beach - we bought towels from the local supermarket which costs us 7.70 euros per towel, but these were nice to bring home as a souvenir. The local area offers a decent amount of bars and restaurants within a short distance but for any younger parties thinking of going to this place it is definitely not for you as its more family orientated. The beaches are ok but they are mostly stone but if you use the beaches to the left of the hotel we did find some areas of sandy beach where we went most mornings. The sea is stunning and you can go out for a long distance as its very shallow, plenty of fish to snorkel around. The drinks in the hotel are ok, ive read comments about the cocktails which I agree with as they are not the best but the beer is lovely,even better than mythos and I thought the white local wine was nice and certainly the best ive tasted in Greece (5th time). The barstaff were my biggest disappointment on the holiday, i dont think ive ever had such rubbish barstaff on holiday, slow,ignorant and i found it disgusting to see them handling bar snacks with a cigarette hanging out of their mouth, they were more than happy to mess around most of the time and a few times we saw the Manager deliver them a telling off. The drinks come in plastic beakers which i think are to do with cost and there seemed to be a lack of them at times and the bar snacks were pretty basic but ok if you intended staying by the pool. All inclusive drinks finish at 22:00hrs but you can purchase drinks up to midnight but be prepared for the bar staff to make their own prices up. During our stay we did three day trips, the Grand Island tour, Paxos/ Antipaxos boat trip (which is highly recommended) and a day at the water park for my my 2 boys, you can book these at Storks Tours Travel Agency, turn right out of the hotel and just up the road, booking with Thomas Cook costs considerably more. I would definitely come back to this hotel but please sort the few problems i have highlighted .A big thank you to the reception staff, cleaners, chefs and kitchen staff. Barstaff,,,,find another job as your ruining a decent enough hotel.

author: jackiekitty06
title: Holiday from hell.
text: When we booked this hotel it was getting excellent reviews but by the time we went they were terrible and I understand why. The first indication of how our all inclusive holiday was going to go was about 20 mins after we arrived. Check in wasn't till 2 so we left our luggage and went to have lunch and a drink. The lunch was just about edible. Little choice and we had to fight the wasps to get it. Then we went to the bar and things got worse. All inclusive local spirits consisted of brandy, vodka and ouzo or undrinkable wine or beer (no diet juice so too bad if you are diabetic) served in plastic glasses which were reused. When we got to our room there was a piece of glass lying in the corner, it was still there when we left 2 weeks later. 2 days into the holiday I was taken to hospital with diahorrea and sickness. We were told this was a virus that was going around. Strangely it seemed confined to our hotel. My husband also became ill and many other guests. When we stopped eating at the hotel we got better immediately. Our cleaner didn't seem to know that there was a balcony so it never got cleaned but that might have been because the rail was loose and we were on the second floor! The reception staff were lovely and that is the only reason this hotel got any score at all. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone but if you do go make sure you have travel insurance.

author: elaine955
title: If you are thinking of booking here DONT
text: We booked this hotel a year ago when the majority of reviews seemed pretty good. we are regular all inclusive guests at hotels and we go away 4 times a year so we know what to expect and were not very fussy! However, breakfast is the only time you can help yourself to tea, coffee and juice. Lunchtime only water available on help yourself basis unless you queue at The pool bar as there is no other bar/ drinks service available and this is all day every day. Dinner time we were unable to get a coffee and were informed coffee stops with snacks at 6pm! So after this time you cannot get a hot drink! We are not drinkers and rarely touch alcohol and I cannot have sugar drinks and NO diet/sugar free drinks are available. I complained and they gave me Coke Zero for a day out of glass bottles which you have to pay for usually and then they bought a 2ltr bottle of Coke light which was very welcomed but then the same bottle kept appearing with the same amount in it and tasted like the soda stream Coke that was being served at the bar. As if this was the case it would make me ill I didn't dare chance it so stuck to water and coffee which meant after 6pm I could only have water. I complained about the coffee and was met with complete disinterest. The food is not good at all and is catered towards Eastern Europeans taste who appear to be the majority of guests. My husband and granddaughter were ignored at the bar and the Eastern European were served first even tho they had been waiting. If you like vodka and orange at 10.30 am then you'll love it here. If you like a nice dinner finished with a coffee then go elsewhere as you definitely won't get that here! A kettle and tea/coffee making facilities in your room would make a huge difference. Overall I would never return as we are not fussy and have ate out almost every meal since our 2nd day! Hugely disappointed both by the hotel and reaction of staff when complained.

author: annasK7280UZ
title: Holiday from hell
text: Never again! I am an experienced travel but this holiday was worse I ever had! 1.We been promised Sandy beach?!-rocks instead! The beach is 15 minutes walking distance. 2.I asked for a town location and we had this hotel in a middle of nowhere-5 km from the centre of the village centre! 5 of 6 buildings surrounding the hotel are abounded-there is nothing to do at all! As a result I had to spent a fortune to entertain my son and myself as there were nothing to do at all! 3. First night!Conditioner didn't work and I had to open the balcony because it was very hot in a room as a result my little son got badly bitten by mosquitoes and it's a reason why we couldn't sleep second night. 4.Second night Conditioner was repaired but it is so very old and switches on every 15-20 minutes with a horrible roar. I spent in this hotel 7 nights and didn't sleep even once!!! Is this a holiday ?! 5.All inclusive! It's the most basic all inclusive I have ever seen! Minimum food selection! I am a healthy eater and there is nothing at all I could have between the meals as they offer only fries and pies ,no fruit or ice creams for kids even coffee you can get only the instant one or pay for a distant one! So we end up eating out and buying our own fruits,ice creams and drinks. 6.Beds had dirty sheets 7.Bathroom tap was green with rust 8.Toilet basin was filthy 9.No entertainment during the day and boring evenings ! I don't know who gave them 3* but it's a horrible mistake 1,maximum 2 stars. Only one good point is a personal who are trying their best!It's hard to imagine someone who would enjoy this holiday!

author: JennyW2342
title: Avoid at all cost!
text: This isn't a hotel its a dump! Within 5 minutes of arriving I was on the phone to my travel agent to be moved to another hotel..... Beds had dirty sheets..... Bathroom tap was green with rust..... Toilet basin was filthy and had not been cleaned..... Damp on the walls..... Filthy dirty and grime on radiator brackets.... Food was a disgrace totally inedible and as for the all inclusive package thats a complete joke!! Tea or coffee was available but as for soft drinks the coke was more like Covonia cough medicine mixed with flat soda water and the fizzy orange tasted like it was out of date and very bitter! The alcoholic beverages were very limited and they then charge you extra for any cocktails you want! My children ages 5&6 wanted to go in the pool while we waited to be moved but were stared at by the other guests so much that we're scared to go in and hid behind me instead. When they did go to the playground well a dirty patch pf grass with a couple of swings that were about 30 years old, my youngest was scratched by a dog that had got out of the property next door! Even the fire escape is damaged and to get down the staircase you have to make sure that you dont get your foot caught in the hole in the floor! Once i had complained to the front desk I was followed around by a member of staff at all times which made me feel really intimidated..... couldn't wait to get out of that hell hole! When my son asked for the code to ring out from the phone in the room, the receptionist refused to give it to him 5 times.... great customer service eh!!! Avoid this place at all costs 😡😡😡😡

author: _ubom255
title: Family vacation
text: This hotel has two sides. So lets start with postive - staff is great. Friendly and helpful when we asked for something they always deliver/fix(for example not working AC) Balcony is quite big and nice. Pool area is nice. Negative side - rooms are old. Matraces are terrible! Never slept on something worst. Bathroom small, old and not looking very nice. At evening there were lot of mosquitos. We had all inclusive but food wasnt very good(and now im trying to be positive). Hotel is at least 10min walking to normal beaches(they are really nice, especially on left side). Be aware that kids pool is deep and not suitable for very little kids. Also there is nothing at all for kids so keep this in mind when you have family. Surroundings of hotel is quite and for young couples/people there isnt really much to do but I was with my little son so for us it was positive side. Its 3 star hotel so not really that bad for the price(however ive seen better 3* hotels) but i wouldnt choose this hotel again. If you are old couple and want budget vacation I would recommend otherwise look for something else.

author: TraceyB627
title: Dated budget hotel. Friendly staff. Poor food.
text: Just got back from a week here. On first appearance looks nice but once inside very dated. Bedrooms basic Bathroom even more basic. Beds okay but no mattress protector, pillows mouldy. We're swapped but to a rock hard unusable pillow. Had to use a towel. Staff very friendly Food repetitive and boring with minimum choice. Breakfast- cereal, cake, cheese,ham, bread with 2 small slow domestic toasters, croissants, tinned fruit. Lunch- soup,salad, chicken,pork casserole,rice,chips was typical and always cold. Deserts was either a mousse and apples or jelly and apples another day. Evening meal pretty much the same. Never labelled so often guess work as to what you were eating. We ended up eating out locally. Location- main beach 20 mins walk Plenty of water sports , tavernas etc Nearest beach 3 mins walk although access down steep concrete path. Free sun beds if you are buying drinks etc from taverna. A few tavernas near by. Two supermarkets. Bus stop outside hotel for Corfu town. Leaves 10.30 every day 2.90 euros each way. Overall If you are on a budget then this hotel gives you a basic base but would consider b & b as tavernas offer better value and quality food.

author: TLCRC
title: A nice hotel.
text: We arrived in the early hours and were greeted by George. He was really friendly and helpful and despite the early time, was very cheery! Our rooms were nearby, as requested, and we had stunning sea views. The rooms were clean and spacious with plenty of hanging space for clothes. The bathroom was rather small and dated but was ok. Rather dark and the shower head had to be hand held as there wasn't anything to fix it to the wall, but ok. We had opted to stay half board. Breakfast was pleasant enough and George greeted us everyday-he even remembered our names which we thought was quite sweet. The evening meal wasn't so good. The food wasn't very hot and there wasn't a great choice for veggies. After the first meal, we decided to go into the town for meals. The pool area is nice. Clean and plenty of sunbeds. The pool bar is well stocked and very reasonably priced too. Overall, we were pleased with our stay. Friendly staff, clean rooms and a good location. If we return to corfu, we'd be happy to stay here again.

author: 540petarm
title: Just what we wanted and a lot more
text: My girlfriend and me have just returned from a 10 night stay at the Golden Sands Hotel. I'd like to highly recommend this hotel, with so friendly and accommodating staff, from reception to the cleaning staff. They made our stay here wonderful, never felt so welcomed before, just like home. The rooms were comfortable and clean, there was everything we needed, air conditioning, TV, free WiFi etc. Cleaners cleaned the room every day, with fresh clean towels changed daily. The food was great, with variety of meals for every taste. Really great selection of food. The pool area is well kept with great bar, comfortable hammocks and sunbeds, and there were big area for kids and sports, tennis court, and free on-site parking. Also they had few themed nights in hotel (Greek night, Latin night, Pool party...), but truth is that there was great atmosphere every night around the pool area, with Ioanis, Spiros and Alex, with whom we had a lot of fun and laugh. Mix of great music, little fireworks and their party attitude made every night memorable for us. Just outside hotel is excellent XL beach, where we spent most of our time, but little further (10-15 mins of walking) there were more great beaches, like Issos beach, Chalkiounas beach, Marathias beach etc. This is a small place, but i think that it has more great beaches, than any other place in Corfu. And this hotel is in the best position in Agios Georgios. If you want you can drive away from the AG to the other places and beaches, because everything is near in Corfu. We spent some time in Paleocastritsa, Glyfada beach, Sunset beach, Corfu town (bus is only 2 or 3 euros in one way), Kanoni (great experience, drinking frappe while airplanes landed/took off on short distance from you), Achileon etc. I forgot to mention that near hotel there are great number of restaurants and bars with excellent food and friendly staff. Summa summarum, great hotel, great staff, great beaches, the GREATEST holiday ever. Thank you Ioanis for a great time and everything that you and your team did for us. We felt like home and we wish to spend our holidays in your hotel for many many years to come. We had FANTASTIC holiday.

author: 172emmaw
title: Did not live up to our expectations
text: I visited Golden Sands 1 week with my boyfriend in september 2013. We were really disapointed of the hotel and the location of the beach. The description told us that the beach would be 50 meters from the hotel. Totally a lie. Where the beach was supposed to be there were just a big scarp which you could not walk down from and there was definately a beach down there. The beach that actually were really nice was approximately 20-25 min walk from the hotel which was fine because we like to exercise, but when I think about all people who are disabled, children, elderly people... Not a fun distance to walk everyday when the informations said the beach was 50 meters away. The other thing that we were really disapointed about was the breakfast. It was actually so bad we bought our breakfast at a supermarket each day and ate it at our balcony because we don't let the small things ruin our trip. And how bad can i breakfast be? Well.... really bad. Anyways, I guess it might be a nice stay for people who like to walk a bit, because it took almost 20 min to walk to the village where there were nice restaurants. Especially The Balcony, we went there 2 times. Wonderful place and really nice staff. Otherwise, The Golden Sands is not anything I would recommend. Corfu is beautiful, nice weather and Korfu Town is really nice. But not Golden Sands.

author: Zuzkazuz
title: Nive, quiet place to stay
text: The hotel is located in the quiet part of Agios Georgios, therefore if you are looking for a quiet place to relax, it is a good choice. The pool looked nice and clean, however I have not tried it, as I spent my time travelling or bathing at the sea. The beach which is closest I did not like, it was very narrow with stones in the water. I preferred Issos beach which is about 10mins walking distance. Clean, sandy and safe for children and nonswimmers. The connection to Kerkyra is ok, bus 2x/day, enough to explore the city center (old/new fortress) + boat trip from the old port. There are many beautiful places to explore in Corfu, I recommend to rent a car for 2 days, it is worth it. The rooms - we had one room into the pool direction (sea view) and one oriented to the hills. Definitelly I recommend to pay for the sea view room, as that room had newer furniture, bathtub and overall looked cleaner and better. The other room was quite outdated and needs a rennovation, not too nice, but ok for sleep. The rooms were quiet, equipped with aircon, small TV and small fridge. Good size of balkony, 2 chairs, small table. The food was the subject of my biggest concerns, but I am happy to say it was wonderful. Breakfast was simple, but tasty and for dinner you could select from several options, there was always something "typical Greek", so we did not eat out. The last but not least was the staff, always friendly, trying to help.

author: NataliaBE
title: Good place to stay if you're looking for escape from city
text: Really good overall. Next to big sandy beach. Towels always clean. Bed folded. Only 1 moment would mention - sand was everywhere on the floor (you can't avoid bringing it on your shoes) and I think it wasn't removed properly in whole week. Only from bathroom. Otherwise all was fine. Really good walls between rooms, you can not hear your neighbours at all (!). Really enjoyed quietness, this is away from any city, so there is no noise, all is calm. Within 2 minutes walk there is a good supermarket and a bit further 1 more. Also few very nice cafes at the same distance. We had a car rented - always had place to park, no problem. We had half-board and I must say we were happy with it. Quality of food was good, always fresh salads and hot meals, quite good choise of meals and all well cooked. Definetly worth the money you spend. (P.S.: Fitness and Spa did not try - had no time as we were travelling around every day, so it remains not rated. Saw a swimming pool there though, seem people quite liked it. Didn't try myself.)

author: 718dianag
title: Simply awesome!
text: First of all we would like to thank you for beautiful holidays ! We really enjoyed it ! If you want to enjoy familiar atmosphere, it is really great choice! I have never stayed in such good hotel. Staff is extremely hospitable, with smile on their faces every day. Everyone here is doing a great job . The atmosphere they spread ...unforgettable . Breakfast and dinner- wide selection of everything :))) Dinner - everytime a Greek speciality - we really aprecciated it. The rooms were clean , pools maintained every morning , I cannot say an unsatisfying word ! The hotel prepared for us programme every evening, where you could even participate . What we really loved was Greek night ! The performance of dancers showing the part of their culture ,was amazing. You could sit in the outside bar where a sympathic bartender takes care about you, you can enjoy their homemade wine or cocktail if you want and just relax or watch the programme. I strongly recommend this hotel ! :))) Alex & Ioannis - thank you for everything ;))))

author: g0rdanak
title: GOLDEN SANDS – FOR GOLDEN HOLIDAY
text: If you want to enjoy every minute of your (one and the only in a year) holiday, than I warmly recommend you to stay in this hotel. It is really nice and cozy. Situated near beautiful town of Corfu, but far enough to feel that you are on the lonely island. You can forget all noise and crowd, and sleep well. This does not mean that you will be board in the little village of Agios Georgios. On the contrary, in the evening you can have a nice long walk through the main street, and have drink or good meal in many bars and taverns. But let’s go back to hotel. It is a stone throw from a magnificent beach. You don’t need to walk to other beaches or rent a car. Also you can enjoy near the pool having some of the fresh drinks or cocktails. Food is more than excellent (especially dinner). Always something different, but with special Greek taste. Rooms are very good and very clan. Stuff is story on its own. I can only say that friendly is weak word to describe theirs hospitality. Best regards to George. And what more to say, except that last summer I was third time there. I will surely go again in near future. Many thanks to manager Petros, he made the best of this hotel. Gordana K.

author: sandyatgrove
title: good value hotel apart from the food.
text: Booked last minute as B&B but free upgrade to half board. Lovely view from our balcony over the sea and well kept gardens and pool, Rooms a little dated but comfortable. There is a small lift. Staff friendly. Situated in a quiet bay with the sea across a small road, Access to the beach is quiet steep. If you go further left out of hotel and access the beach next to the restaurant, they offer free sunbeds if you eat and drink their food, They come and take your order and deliver, great service.There are two well stocked supermarkets to the left of the hotel. There are a lot of small restaurants to choose from. We ate in the hotel but this is the first time that I have ever encountered a restaurant without any choice.They just serve a very basic meal, which was very disappointing. The breakfast was basic.The highlight of the holiday was the quad bikes. The place next to the hotel offers a discount. They let you try in the car park opposite and I would encourage you to have a go! We are mature,larger ladies and for three days we had a fantastic time going over the mountains and stopping at all the hidden beaches. We also took the bus into Corfu town which stops just across the road. Just great for shopping! I would recommend this hotel but not if you intend to eat on the premises.

author: TDT67
title: Friendly Welcoming Hotel
text: Our stay at Golden Sands was very enjoyable. We were warmly welcomed by Ioannis and throughout our stay, all the staff were fantastic. A particular thank you to Ioannis and Aspa, who were so helpful and friendly on reception, to Alex and Magelis who looked after us so well in the restaurant and of course to George, whose hospitality is second to none. We stayed in room 219. The room was very nice, but would benefit from some updating, particularly in the bathroom. However, the room was spacious with plenty of storage, clean with very comfortable beds and good air conditioning. Breakfast was plentiful with a good selection. Continental with a warm dish each morning. Our one criticism would be the evening meal. We were surprised that there was no choice at all and the quality/combination of food could be improved greatly. It would also be preferable to eat more Greek dishes when in Greece! However, overall, we had a great stay and would certainly consider returning to the hotel. The hotel is in a quiet area of the resort. St Georges South is very low key with some excellent restaurants and lovely sandy beaches. We would recommended the resort for couples and families.

author: 31tony_m31
title: not impessed at all
text: it promised kettles and tea making facilaties in each room. when i went to reception to ask where our kettle was i was told they didnt supply them, after a lot of needless arguements they finally gave me one. we were half board but the food was disgusting. we expected the continental breakfast and were prepaired to try it once and see how it was. once was enough after that we ate our breakfast elsewhere. the evening meals were a joke, on our 1st evening we were given a large bowl of beetroot each topped with a very thin yogurt, we asked what this was and were told it was a popular greek dish.i have been to corfu many times before and never come across this dish before and i hope i never do again it was disgusting. the main couses consisted of large brown beans in a red sauce,not forgeting the stale bread which accompanied every meal. another night we were served smash potato, pork burger stuffed with cheese and mushy peas {no visible peas just green mush} we went down every evening to look at the meals, we sat and waited to see if anything decent was about to be served but it never was so we ate out every night. i am an an ordinary working class man but i would not have given that food to a starving dog. the rooms wer very small and basic. the bathroom was even smaller and the shower was very antiquated with a small shower basin with a dirty shower curtain and was so small you couldnt turn round in it. also there was nowhere to put the shower head as it was broken. on 2 occasions the hot water went off for several hours. our bathroom never had a plug for the sink which made it difficult for me to have a shave. when i went to ask at reception for a plug i was told it would take 3 days for them to get one from corfu town. everyone we spoke to in the hotel complained of the food and the bathrooms. i cant understand why trip advisor issued a 4 star rating to this hotel, unbelievable. the receptionist never told the truth about anything we ever asked them about.i would never ever use this hotrl again. a.mulloy, hull, yorkshire

author: Tenila
title: Oh Dear......
text: Well, it's a little bit difficult to write anything very encouraging about our stay here..... Except the rooms are kept very clean and the housekeepers work very hard. Rooms cleaned and towels replaced every single day, beds comfy and as the rooms generally have a fabulous sea view then sleep quality is pretty good. The staff were accommodating and pleasant but my oh my the food was absolutely appauling! I stayed with a friend and we booked half board - total waste of money... We ate two (well actually one and a bit in my case - my friend braved it out for the two) evening meals. The first was basically chicken and chips and on the second night what was supposed to be a pork chop with green beans and greek style potatoes. Mine was stone cold and the meat was tough to put it mildly. When I complained to the staff the only option given to me was 'would you like some bread and butter'... The breakfast isn't much better either and for me the cleanliness of the dining area is questionable. Now for the good bit....the pool is a good size for relaxing by. The hotel is a little bit remote from the few bars and restaurants that are available. We would highly recommned staying in this resort but not at this hotel. Its a fair walk to the main beach, which again is beautiful. It is 'golden sand', very clean and a couple of areas outside the beach front restaurants where you can lie in the sun on loungers that are removed from the main area outside the large All Inclusive hotel at the end of the beach. There are water sports available for the energetic holidaymaker. The sea is very shallow for quite some distance, so safe for children, but not much there overall to amuse or entertain the younger ones. Overall I would not recommend this hotel other than on a bed and breakfast basis, but the resort as a whole is fabulous...like going back in time to the Greek experience of the 1990's.....

author: danshkayamb
title: Very Nice. Would go back .
text: We have just come back from 2 weeks stay here.Having read reveiws before we went was not good, but we got there with open minds as some people write negative reviews and have enjoyed there stay which is not fair to the hotel. On arrival we were greeted by a lovely lady at reception. Of which I would like to thank for all her help. We had a lovely sea view room which overlooked the front and the pool and bar area. Yes the rooms need a little updating on the inside and the lift is out of the stone age. And really needs a new one. But you need only use it for your cases. Yanis the manager is really nice and will help you out with whatever you need,but he is no mind reader and cannot help if you don't ask. Goerge at the poolside bar is a case. He too is really nice and very helpful. St. George is a really nice place to go, Lovely and quiet, away from the hussle and noise of other Towns. The People are equally nice and will help you with anything.But thats the Greecians for you. [Brilliant people]We were there for 2 wks and enjoyed it. We ate out and were not disatified anywhere. and real value for money. So all in all we really enjoyed our stay at this hotel.Would go back. 11/6/2012-25/6/2012 phil/sue manchester

author: Rhiannee
title: Nice quiet hotel
text: We came here for the last few days of May. The hotel itself is nice, good size rooms, air con for us was free! They supplied us with travel adaptor, there was a small TV, small hairdryer-not really any good though lol. Unfortunately, there were 1 or 2 marks on the sheets/pillows. We didn't bother saying anything, but I'm sure they would have been really helpful if we had. We just didn't use them and they changed them the next day. Very friendly staff- they were always on hand for advice or just to greet you and make you feel really welcome. It is in a very quiet area, not alot to do, which is perfect for us but we rented a car so we got to see Corfu town, Cavos, and just found little beaches along the coast. But you can rent quad bikes etc from right next to the hotel anyway. TIP: if u do have a car, and you use GPS, do not turn left out of the hotel to go somewhere far. Turn right, and let it guide you from there. (If you go left it brings you through a village with some horrible tiny roads-you will mess up your car!) The hotel is also right next to the beach, don't use the 1st footpath you find to go to the beach, walk down to the left and you will find proper steps. We had breakfast here, not the best...some bread, cheese, ham, boiled eggs, sausages, fruit, cornflakes, and cake. I don't eat pork or dairy ! so quite limited really haha bread and eggs for me! We didn't eat dinner here, but there are alot of restaurants around the hotel. All in all, it was so good for the price, would definitely stay here again, and recommend it!

author: TrueNat
title: Funny holidays
text: Stayed there 12 days. We were 4 girls and we got all that we expected from that hotel. 3* as well: tolerable rooms, just there is a strange problems with towels: you got every day 1 less :) , swimming pool, enough place for parking and a little area for children with swing. All territory is cleaned, with nice palms and flowers. The sand beach is 5 mins walking, if i could advice, you'd go a bit more to the left and you'd find wider and more comfortable beach, with sunbeds and umbrellas (6 euros per a day, but after 5 p.m. they are free! ;)) The special thanks to the stuff! George is a very kind man, with nice sense of humour, thank you for the warm atmosphere in the restaurant and an extra ice-cream;) Ioannis, the great manager, arranges all your problems and dance latina better than sirtaki, thank u for your smile and waiting for you in Moscow! We rented Fiat Panda in George car rental (walking about 500 m. to the center of the village and you'll see that office), say hi to Kostas! We had a wonderful round-trip, saw the great views of Corfu, enjoyed frappe and retsina, sorry for ouzo:) but we didnt like it, met some donkeys, lost the way sometimes and felt very happy! Finally you'd ask why 4 points and not 5? Honestly we were not satisfied with food: poor breakfast and dinner for menu, which was not so variable, meat is too spicy, fried potatoes is almost every day, all dishes are not so tasty, strange.. with so nice ingredients! But one of my friend is ready to do master-class for your chief;) And it means we'll be back! From Russia with love!

author: funshinebear11
title: What a gem!
text: We just returned from a week's stay at AGIOS GEORGIOS, We feel so lucky to have discovered this hidden little secret of a gem. Golden Sands was great- what you'd expect from a 3 star hotel, plus a little more. Rooms were fine- clean and spacious enough, lots of storage space and a very handy little fridge! you can get a safe and AC for 5 euros a day, or so. Decor was a bit old-fashioned but if like us you only spend time in the hotel to sleep and shower, it really doesn't matter. nice big pool with a bar but you'd be a fool to stay there instead of bathing in the beautiful, clear, clean Mediterranean right across the street! The hotel offered some night-time entertainment like traditional Greek dancing and costumes- fun! Very friendly and helpful staff. Loads of tavernas and bars but non too crowded. We highly recommend Le Bistrot- best food in the area, so fresh, real respect for food and ingredients and really really lovely family who owns it. The perfect gettaway for a family or couples, relaxing calm with enough buzz to keep you going at night (try Mad Mike's!). Also recommend renting a quad to tour the island and going on the boat tour to Paxos, Antipaxos and the caves (only 28 euros!). Only bummer was that there was nowhere to get cash out but most places only take cash!! So bring plenty with you. Absolutely amazing! Can't wait to go back!

author: YoungTraveler50
title: Beautiful Area
text: Hotel is situated on the Adriatic Sea. Surrounded by the most beautfiul sandy beaches of the island. You can walk for hours in either direction. Nice area. Many bars/restaurants. Situated about 35 minutes away from Corfu Town by car or 1 hour by bus (Green bus- 2/day 10AM and 4:30PM). The hotel itself is kept clean. Reception/Lobby and restaurant have been recently renovated. The rooms are a decent size, clean but dated furniture. Breakfast and dinner can be included. The restaurant offers a fixed menu from a variety of traditional greek specialities (Souvlaki, Pastistada, Moussaka, Pasticio,etc). The pool area has a bar and lunch menu as well as a kids pool and a playground. Also has a Tennis court. What made my experience memorable at this hotel is the staff. From the restaurant to the reception you will find lovely attentive people doing their best to make your stay as perfect as possible

author: Zizz08
title: The worst hotel I've ever seen
text: My problems are: - Some rooms are noisy, there is some kind of machinery for the pool at one side of the hotel. You must close the balcony door if you want to sleep. - There were killed mosquitos on the walls and on the curtain. It was disgusting, there were cleaning every day, but no one removed them. - The food: that is the main problem. I've been some *** hotels in Greece, and other countries, but this one was ridiculous. For breakfast: one type of "salami" (cheapest), 1 type of cheese and jam. (of course butter too) The bread is usually at least one day old, not fresh. The coffee tastes like water, the orange juice is usually undrinkable. No vegs, we bought some in a shop. Others bought nescafe and orange juice too. Some guests made sandwiches for themselves (stealing food), the solution: a fellow started to distribute the cheese and the salami, two or three slices / person. The dinner was better, but you cannot sit where you want, your room number was signed on a piece of paper on your table. -The positive part: usually the staff was helpful, except the kitchen fellow, who guard the food. Jorgos, the receptionist is a funny guy .- Location is ok, the beach is nearby, the pool is ok.

author: roadrun50
title: Within easy walking distance to the mosaics
text: A very short walk to the see the mosaics. Hotel provides parking pass to a public parking lot, less than one block away. If you park close to the wall, you can unload your car before taking it to the parking lot. I believe it is a one-way street. There are three or four steps up to the lobby from the street. There is a chair lift for disabled guest. Front desk personnel very helpful. Room was very comfortable. I was on the fourth floor. Only window a skylight. The night I was there, there was trouble logging onto the free wifi on the fourth floor. A call went into the vendor but problem not corrected while I was there. Used connection in the lobby. At check-out, elevator had a glitch and continually cycled between the fourth and second floor. Eventually corrected. Breakfast ok but nothing special

author: SaubleisBest
title: The BEST
text: Having spent a month travelling in Europe, my daughter and I were delighted by Hotel Diana because it is an easy walk from the train station with rolling luggage, is located very close to San Vitale and Galla Placidia -- 2 of the best sites for Byzantine mosaics, and has very friendly and helpful personnel. For instance, the friendly man at the desk saw our half empty water bottles, and offered to fill them up with cold fresh water from the water dispenser near the front desk. Next, he suggested an itinerary for seeing the mosaic sites in and around Ravenna-- beginning with Sant' Apollinare in Classe because each church has specific times when it is open to the public. Rather than taking the train to this site 3 km away, he said we could use the bicycles of Hotel Diana instead- at no charge, and that we could follow a bike path to the church. An assistant immediately brought up the bicycles and we were given a lesson on how to use the 2 lock system and how to store our bags safely in the front baskets so as to deter thieves from snatching our possessions while riding. Our room was comfortable-- and yes the shower stall is very small as other guests have commented, and the toilet is located right in front of the tiny shower stall making it a bit uncomfortable for use. You have to have a slim build to fit through the opening into the shower-- so beware. No big beer bellies would be able to get into our shower stall. But otherwise, we were very pleased. Finally, check the times ahead of time for trains to your next destination and purchase your ticket the day before. We were heading for Rome and the "direct" Frecciarossa train leaves Ravenna at 6:22 a.m. We asked if we could have a couple of "doggy bags" for breakfast and found them in the morning on the front desk all neatly laid out with croissants, yogurt, apples, baby Gouda cheese, and complimentary new bottles of water. If you are Canadian you are lucky-- because you will be directed to visit a gelato place a few minutes away that is owned by a Canadian from Montreal. We were treated so well all in all during our 2-night stay to see the beautiful mosaics of Ravenna, that there is no question of us returning to Hotel Diana in the future. Compared to the atrocious cost of staying in Venice, Hotel Diana is a bargain. And Ravenna was a nice change from the tourist and traffic-clogged streets of Venice, Florence, Pisa, and Rome. Ciao.

author: FoodWineSFBayArea
title: Very good value, comfortable and clean in a town that is often overlooked by Americans.
text: Hotel Diana has good value for the money. Rooms are clean. Beds are above average for Italian hotels 'tho not as good as standard American one can get a decent night's sleep (doubles are typical Italian, twins pushed together). The breakfast spread is excellent - good fresh fruit, fresh fruit juices, yogurt, rolls, cheese, cured meats, etc. One of us is a morning coffee drinker who loves his espresso and reports that theirs is good. Parking was convenient. The staff was very friendly and helpful. Restaurant recommendations were excellent. The day we were leaving, during check out the desk clerk asked where we were going next. When I told him we were heading toward Venice, he recommended stopping at the Pomposa Abbey and restaurants for lunch if we wanted to stop along the way. We visited the Abbey but passed on lunch, choosing instead to go to Venice. This was our second stay at this hotel. We first stayed here fourteen years ago and decided that it was a good hotel and a great town in which to recover from jetlag. It was as great to recover from jetlag here as we thought. We were happy that the GPS kicked in and was working when we arrived as the hotel is close to the center of town so it would not have otherwise been easy to find (fine if not tired from a transAtlantic trip but not great if one is tired). Because Ravenna is a vacation spot for Italians, although we were there on Halloween and All Saints Day, restaurants were open to accommodate Italians enjoying their long weekend. If you have never visited Ravenna, it is fine to be without a car. Having a car makes it easy to see everything there is to see. All sights can be seen in a single day. Restaurants are very good both in the center of town and outside of it.

author: EurobMalaga
title: Much better than average
text: Travellers arriving by car can park in the secure basement parking with its entrance immediately next to the hotel. The ramp is rather steep, which will make longer vehicles 'touch-bottom'. The hotel is within a short and pleasant walk from the city centre. Don't forget to visit the stunning cathedral. Big oldfashioned typical Spanish hotel with beautiful marmor floors. The friendly and very helpful gentleman at the reception made us feel most welcome. This hotel feels somewhat dated, but renovation is in progress. The breakfast lounge was already in ‘new-style’ (could not order breakfast in the room). A nice and lively bistro-type restaurant next door, belonging to the hotel, serves excellent meals, with very accommodating and friendly staff. Nice sized and very clean room, with marmor floor and typical Spanish wood wall paneling. One large cupboard. The oldfashioned CRT TV will be replaced as part of the renovation and a minibar will be fitted in its (presently empty) cupboard. There are enough electricity power outlets. A practical sized bathroom with a decent sized shower, which (exceptionally) did not leak. The morning of our departure we could leave our car in the basement parking until well after the checkout time, for the duration of our visit to the beautiful Cathedral.

author: stevensA5026VD
title: Last Option Hotel unless you smoke weed!
text: I to this hotel for business and this location was convenient to the meeting location. Let me start with a positive the room was very clean but everything thing else needs major improvements. Check in was hurrible. No sympathy or empathy for guests.customer service was poor. After making wait an hour to check in, I ask for a quiet room away from the elevators. The guy put right next to it and i heard the elevator, the ice machine and people talking and laughing. Not cool. Most hotels has complementary toothbrushes and toothpaste and combs. You guessed it this one don’t. On top of that I reported that the third floor smelled like weed and smoke filled the halls. The lady brushed me off and did nothing about it. Now the hotel is supposed to be smoke free. The food for breakfast was terrible, so bad I had to eat cereal each day. I tried dinner and the wings were good but the Mac and cheese was hurrendous. It was basically pasta with melted cheese on top. The bar tender was cool though.

author: buhoDallas
title: Rough around the edges in some areas.
text: I was aware that this was an economical place to stay in Portland. It is owned and operated by Portland State University. I stayed here for 6 days. I had stayed for the previous 6 days at a Hilton in Denver. No comparison. The pluses: warm daily breakfast, an orange line train is right across the street which gives access to most all of Portland, plenty of staff that are giving their best efforts to clean, organize, etc. The negatives: my room’s (avoid #191) carpeting was so stained, worn and generally gross that I always wore shoes when in the room. I thought this was the norm with all rooms but I was able to look into other rooms when housekeeping was present and saw carpeting that was in like new condition. Another negative: you feel like you are staying more at a motel than at at hotel. #191 opened into a corridor which looked out into a parking lot. Also card keys stopped operating on two occasions. Kudos to staff. They made great efforts to clean as well as they could and be professional. I think that this stay is a perfect example of you get what you pay for. So have realistic expectations.

author: fourdeps
title: Great price and above nice accommodations
text: We stayed at University Place for 5 nights and had a great experience. Our room was on the first floor right by the pool. Request these rooms if you can - they are convenient and updated. The room had a great King Bed and everything was very clean and well-maintained. The pool area is very lovely - we used the pool and the patio chairs to rest and relax each day. The breakfast was very above average and included in the price. While the choices were pretty much the same each day, there was plenty of variety. We loved the potatoes and the granola cereal. The room is large and busy but well-organized except by the juice and bread which was a bit crowded. The parking is an extra fee, but well worth it to have a spot. The room rates are far lower than almost all the Portland hotels, so the parking fee is almost irrelevant. The location is ultra convenient to transportation, the waterfront, and many restaurants. Walking is preferred in Portland and the location makes it so easy. I did have to wait in line about 10 minutes to check-in and some people were cranky about that, but it really was not a problem. I would definitely return to this hotel - it is a good value, a good location, and a nice place.

author: ddbleu
title: 2+ Overall
text: The staff was very helpful and friendly. But the property is rather tired and run down. We stayed in the mid-range room, not the best and not the economy. It was clean and beds were comfortable, but there was a very loud machine outside our window. Maybe a huge air conditioning unit for common areas. Not sure but it ran all the time and was so loud we couldn't keep our slider open. Other than that, we didn't hear a lot of noise from the hallway or neighboring rooms. The in-room small frig was a plus. Our bathroom fan didn't work and we reported it, but it seemed the same after maintenance came. TV didn't work for the first day. The layout of the property is rather confusing, on two different levels. Breakfast was OK, scrambled eggs, bacon, etc. same every morning. It is close to the light rail train, and a block from the streetcar line. I did not like the fact that they slapped a $780 charge onto my credit card upon check in for "incidentals". It wasn't taken off until we checked out.

author: 585matthewh
title: Generous breakfast buffet, good location
text: Pretty good value, and a big breakfast buffet is included. Free coffee available in the lobby as well in the morning. It's an old hotel, but well maintained and clean. Some rooms are being upgraded, but I got a regular old one. Bed is a little firmer than I'm used to, but not too much of an issue. TV didn't work at first, but someone came up and reset it. There is an overnight parking charge of $15.00. One issue I did have is the layout of the place. If you look at the building map, the sections look like a bunch of randomly scattered dominoes. It took a while to figure out how to get to my room from different entrances. Stairs and elevators aren't where you might expect to find them. I was able to navigate the place by the second day. There is a transit station right in front of the building. Nice college neighborhood. I'd probably stay here again.

author: RoadTrippersWA
title: Most Reasonably Priced Hotel in Portland
text: As those of you who have booked hotels in Portland know, it isn't cheap. This is true in most downtown parts of major metropolitan areas. Portland is a small city by many standards, but is still an expensive place to spend the night. We found the University Place Hotel, did our research on TripAdvisor and other sites, noted the good and bad reviews, saw the extremely reasonable rates and determined it was worth a shot. This place (according to its own website) is "Owned, Operated and Located on the campus of Portland State University and Open to the Public", so I was not expecting a lot. I am guessing that the front desk is staffed with Hospitality majors, as they were mostly young and very polite and helpful. The place has a dated feel to it, although there is quite a bit of renovation going on. Our room (as many do) faced the central courtyard and swimming pool. Room was quiet and comfortable. Breakfast was pretty good, though this is one of those places that check your room number as you enter, and cannot take food out to your room or otherwise. That felt a little heavy-handed, but experience tells me they must have had more than a few non-guests dropping in for breakfast (students, perhaps?). The hotel is right on a MAX line, and across the street from two north/south pedestrian walkways towards the heart of downtown. We went to a show at the Keller Auditorium, 5 blocks away directly down one of these paths - very convenient. There is a - sort of - restaurant on site. But there are lots of food truck-type places a block north on 4th, a Hawaiian food restaurant, and everything else a walk or short MAX ride away. It's not perfect, but if I have the need to stay in Downtown Portland, I am coming back here.

author: miketI4448AP
title: Affordable and Clean Accomodation near U of Portland
text: The hotel bills itself as a modest hotel with modest prices - as it says in the hotel guide. I had a pleasant experience checking in with the cordial staff. The room was very roomy especially for one person and a good size for two. The bed was very large and comfortable with about 8 pillows on it. The bathroom was on the small side; but plenty big enough for it's purpose. Amenities included a hi-def TV, microwave, fridge, coffee/tea maker, and hair dryer. Everything was clean and I didn't have one thing to complain about. Oh maybe one thing the view of the parking lot wasn't the greatest; but because of the hotel's location I don't think any room had a good view. The hotel is located near Portland University and in a location with plenty of condo buildings. No restaurants or shops in the immediate area; but not too far away. A light rail and bus stop is located in front of the hotel and they run on a regular basis with a screen informing when the next 2 scheduled trips are arriving. The complimentary breakfast has a large selection with scrambled eggs, bacon, sausages, cereal, muffins, toast, juices, coffee/tea, and anything else you would desire for a hearty breakfast. The dining area is also very large with plenty of tables. Very impressive for a complimentary breakfast. The desk staff are helpful with all requests, the housekeeping staff are efficient and friendly, and in conclusion I enjoyed my stay. If you're looking for clean and affordable accommodation this is the place.

author: CaseyluvsSophie
title: Great Location, Great Breakfast, Great Pool & Courtyard, Rooms underwhelming
text: Recently stayed here for the Little League Softball World Series that my daughter and her team representing Canada were playing in. The location is excellent on campus of Portland State University with Go Train station right in front of the hotel. Also a ton of food trucks, restaurants and pubs within walking distance. Downtown within walking distance and easy access to the nearby freeway. The courtyard pool and patio are also excellent with a number of tables and chairs for socializing, hanging out and having beverages. The breakfast buffet that is included with the room price was very good as well with excellent quality bacon, sausages, hasbrowns, waffles and eggs. Juices were less than superb and seemed to be made from powdered mixes, Tang? Coffee was good. The negative aspects of this hotel include: old dingy dark small cave like rooms in desperate need of renovation and new furnishings; newspapers for purchase only and parking an extra $15 per day. Notwithstanding the negatives, given our outstanding room rate of $95 per, it's hard to complain. Rooms had tiny fridges and microwaves which was a nice touch. Bathrooms were small. Management advises that the hotel will be doing extensive renovations in the near future. I would stay here again after the renovation, assuming the room rate is decent. Good place for families on a budget who want a good location in Portland.

author: keriw699
title: 70's run-down
text: Pictures make it look nicer than it is. The upsides: linens on the bed were clean and nicer than the rest of the room, towels were pretty decent (as mentioned in another review), employees are pleasant and helpful. Housecleaning staff gave a friendly greeting whenever they saw us, our room was clean - considering how aged the place is. That's it. We paid $108 a night, so were not expecting anything fancy at all, and an in general run-down would have been fine for us. This hotel is really run down, pretty sure the only maintenance it's seen since the early 70's is emergency maintenance . Ceiling above bathroom sink had seen water damage a few times, half the lights in our room would not turn on, carpet was pretty gross; rippled in many places, bathroom light plate was barely screwed on, and didn't fit- possibly replaced for the umpteenth time.Something was going on down the hall - looks like water damage or so, perhaps the remodeling that other reviews mentioned, but there was an emergency plumbing truck outside for the time we were there (2 days). It felt like what I'd expect from a Motel 6 on the side of the road. Walls were pretty thin. We are serious deep sleepers and nothing kept us awake, we also go to bed pretty late as well - hearing others staying up late is not a bother for us at all. That said, we could hear the tv in the room on one side, and the loud conversation and laughing on the other side. Though obnoxious, this didn't bother us at all for the reasons above. But could be a problem for anyone who sleeps early and light. While affordable you pay for other things- $15 for parking, you pay for a newspaper if you want one, etc. That sort of affordable. Plus we came back very late at night (11:30) and took the last available parking space. I paid for a space, I'm assuming they would have made sure I got one (looks like anyone can park in their lot as there are pay boxes as well - so I wondered how they control that as I circled to find a space) , but I'm pretty happy I didn't have to carry in my sleeping kid at 11:30 at night to argue for a space. We did not chose this place for location, but it looks like it is a good place for location - with light rail out front - we saw many people heading to a game, and proximity to the college. We had a car and spent most of our time downtown, from that point of view, it was a good location. Everything was 15 minutes away; the zoo, OSMI, Powell's, etc.

author: ElleN350
title: DISGUSTING DUMP !
text: We were caught searching for a place to stay at the last minute, and boy did we regret booking a room there over the phone! It's in a shady part of town & almost impossible to find on crazy dead-end one-way streets. That in itself should have been a forewarning to us. Having pre-paid a small fortune made it impossible to get a refund, but if we could have, we'd have left 2 minutes after walking in the room. The condition of the room was disgusting - a real dump!!!...dark with broken lamps, old furnishings, and everything FILTHY DIRTY. Crud & burn marks were on the indoor-outdoor type carpet, with torn drapes, scrapes, scratches, nicks, scuffs on every surface. Naturally, the beds were old, and very uncomfortable with cheap shabby linens. And the BATHROOM was HORRIBLE: MOLD everywhere! Plus a broken mirror, bashed doorframe, no fan, old noisy toilet, no counter....just ICK. We were afraid to turn out the lights anywhere fearing critters would appear. The check-in service was bad, too. Two surly girls didn't so much as say 'Hello' to people as they walked in. Then the room charge was increased while we stood there with a "take it or leave it" response. The biggest joke is they make you sign & pay for a "damage deposit" ....ridiculous. Fair warning: Don't waste a penny on such an awful place!!!!

author: Dolphinlove70
title: Frustration at Poor Service
text: When we checked in we noticed that the non slip coating on the bath was coming loose but did not really look closely. That night when I had a bath I ended up covered in old adhesive. later I was doing my back exercises on the floor when I discovered a long pin like a hat pin on the carpet beside the bed. In the morning we went down to the front desk and advised them of the bath situation and went to breakfast. When we came back just about to leave for our conference we were advised we would need to change rooms right away. They sent a young man with a luggage trolley and we expected him to offer to help us. It was not until we asked him for help he actually lifted a finger to help us. after a very rushed relocation we set off late for our conference. The new room was definitely cleaner and nicer than the first. Next day we went off to our conference first thing in the morning. We returned to our room at 6.00 PM to find that it had not been serviced. Bed not made, towels on the floor, coffee cups and glasses unwashed and of course the room and bathroom had not been cleaned. We advised the front desk of the situation and left to have dinner. When we got back to the room at 10.30 PM absolutely nothing had been done to the room. My husband went down to the front desk and insisted the senior clerk on duty come and observe first hand the state of our room. This he did and took many notes. It was our intention to stay on another night but after our experiences with the service or lack thereof we decided to move to another hotel. I will say in the interest of fairness when my husband spoke to the duty manager the next morning he advised us we would not be charged for our stay and he refunded all monies we had paid. Even so I would not recommend this hotel to anyone.

author: WandaP977
title: Near OHSU
text: Great place to stay if you need to be near OHSU. Older but clean hotel - very large with lots of rooms. Staff was friendly. they have Keurig's in the rooms with K-cups, very nice! Micro and fridges also. Limited choice on TV channels. If you are a particular about the comfort of your bed....you probably won't appreciate this location. Too firm for me. The only big complaint I had was the lack of maid service while we were gone for an entire day. They had obviously been in the room. Coffee was restocked, but our beds had not been touched. This was very upsetting as we were so tired and had to make our bed before going to bed. With my bad back - this was not good. They have a pool but I can't comment on it as we did not use it. They do offer a bit of a discount rate for family of patients at OHSU and they provide a warm and heart breakfast every morning. Parking is a premium everywhere in Portland and they do charge for parking. Bonus is the city transit runs right in front of the hotel.

author: catherineb962
title: For heaven's sake, a perfectly fine hotel
text: Truth be told, I was scared to stay here after reading all the terrible reviews. Guess what-- it's perfectly fine!! Is it a luxury 5-star accommodation? No, but that's not what you're paying for. During my stay, it proved to be a clean, quiet, convenient place to rest my bones after touring around Portland all day. The staff was friendly, the free breakfast a huge bonus, and this is as close as you can get to downtown for the money. An easy 20-minute walk or short tram ride IMMEDIATELY OUTSIDE THE DOORS OF THE HOTEL will bring you straight downtown. Head in the other direction and you're a 25-minute ride across the river from some of the best craft breweries Portland has to offer. I didn't swim in the pool, but it looked clean and well-cared for. The only slight disappointment was the lack of wifi in the rooms, but we were so busy all day, I didn't miss it. If you bring a laptop, the ethernet cable works great, or spring the extra $10 for the more expensive room with wifi. I asked about a AAA discount and checkout and saved 15% on my 5-night stay. We got fresh cookies at check-in. I slept like a baby. I'm a happy traveler and relieved the negative reviews proved not to be true for me. Yes, I did say FRESH COOKIES.

author: DianeB112
title: Smelly beds
text: I needed a place to stay that I could return to on many occasions to visit my son in college. It needed to be reasonably priced, convenient to the college and at least to be acceptable by my lowest standards but it wasn't. I booked my stay back in July when my son had orientation. I wasn't able to look at a room because they were booked at that time. I decided to take the risk and book it for our September stay when we returned to bring him to stay at college. When we first walked into the room it didn't smell bad at all. Actually, the room itself never smelled bad at all. However, when I went to sit up and read that night on top of the covers I noticed a very strong dirty hair smell coming from the bed. After sniffing around a bit I discovered it was coming from the pillows. They looked clean but smelled so horrible I was afraid to sleep in the bed. My son had a roll-away which it and the pillow that came with it was fine. Fortunately he had brought his sleeping bag which I ended up using that first night. The next morning I told the front desk the problem and told them they must change the entire bed including replacing the pillows. They did but it was very slightly better but still not acceptable. I continued to sleep with the sleeping bag and his camp pillow. Also, we were in room 192 which had a HUGE swath of carpeting as you enter the room that had been cleaned with bleach. It looked like a crime scene. I won't be staying here again.

author: 966colinh
title: More for your buck
text: The check in was pleasant. They give you the best chocolate chip cookies! The room was just fine. And the gardens surrounding the pool were well kept. The Grill was fantastic! I had one of the best burgers! It was also a bar which was nice. The help was always pleasant. They refreshed the room sending us into our second night. Ice machine and pop machine worked. The location was close to the MAX. This was how we saw the town and ate out. There was a Starbucks just up the street. They did have coffee in the room as well. I really enjoyed myself here. You get a lot for your buck, not to mention the absolutely best hot breakfast!

author: Karolpdx
title: Fantastic Location
text: This hotel is very conveniently located in the downtown area adjacent to campus of Portland State University. There is an ample parking lot. In the inner courtyard there is beautiful pool with adequate seating and tables. The complementary breakfast buffet in the large dining room includes a variety of hot and cold items. If you are gluten intolerant you can have scrambled eggs, bacon, fruit, juices, yogurt, coffee and tea. Rental cars are available on site. One block away is a group of food carts/trucks serving mostly inexpensive Asian fare. You can easily catch the Max light rail in front of the hotel or stroll down to the Riverplace area. As I said the location is very good. Front desk service was very satisfactory with one exception. I tried to call from outside without knowing the guest's room number, and a female clerk refused to put me through. Oddly enough, on the previous day a male clerk was very helpful with the same issue. A family member stayed here and mentioned an early morning disturbance when a group of unsupervised pre-teens apparently had a field day slamming doors and talking loudly in the rooms on both sides of his at 4 in the morning. On reporting the issue to management, he was asked to inform the desk clerk if there was a recurrence of the problem so that security would see that it stopped. Fortunately this proved unnecessary. Other than that his stay was pleasant.
