author: TFigel
title: Convenient to Portland center but that's about all
text: Anyone looking for little close to the downtown center of Portland will find plenty of little at the University Place Hotel and Conference Center. There is little except the fundamental bed(s) and bathroom. Our family and a family friend had booked rooms during the July, 2015 time of a daughter's wedding. The promised swimming pool so attractive to grandchildren? Closed for cleaning. Wi-fi? Only available in tiny areas of the whole complex. Working keys to the room? So erratic that our friend had his replaced four or five times over the stay. The breakfast? This was fine, a decent array provided for a big room full of guests. The hotel is owned by a local university and seems to run as a neglected class project. A young staff buffeted by the same complaints each day - no working room key, no wi-fi, etc. - has no apparent help from a management dedicated to solving the problems. A young staff member helped us learn about the narrow seams of wi-fi availabililty and, more important, helped us cancel one of our rooms so that people could move to a real hotel. We had booked the hotel through Priceline, a mistake that left us dealing with a third party when help was already scant in face-to-face dealings with the suffering low-level hotel personnel. Among Portland hotel prices we saw, this hotel had a modest cost. But "modest" is a standard the hotel does not achieve.

author: hundertwasser
title: could not be any more mediocre!
text: So astoundingly mediocre in every way that they should come up with a new word for it. The only things to recommend it are very competent maids (who should be running the place!) and, well, that's all I got. Maybe the low price? But then, you do get what you pay for. The front desk has NO IDEA what is around the hotel. They say there are no restaurants nearby, when there was a decent Thai place just a block away that is open late at night. They don't know about delivery restaurants. They don't know the MAX schedule. They don't know what line train services the hotel (the yellow and the green, btw - it's the PSU campus, duh). The elevator works sporadically, and there's only one; parking is insanely expensive and there is no security guard - broken glass in two places in the parking lot showed that it's not a safe place to park overnight. The rooms smell like cigarette smoke, the sliding glass door to the deck wouldn't latch closed, the pool is full but always chained and marked "closed," and our entire floor was full of athletes who left their doors wide open and partied loudly for much of the night. Don't even think about going to their "restaurant." It was NASTY. Pre-frozen chicken sandwich, salmon burger, and hamburger patties, which the waitress couldn't even identify; they stop serving super early because management is too cheap to keep a cook on at night (10 people came in after 9:30 and were turned away). The bar closes really early, and isn't very impressive anyway... drinking here is nothing but a sign of severe depression and possibly suicidal thinking. The tartar sauce in a packet was a nice touch, too. In short: management is clueless. I really hope this is not related to some kind of hospitality or service program at PSU, because if it is, this does NOT recommend any of their graduates.

author: retiredt_13
title: Only in Desperation
text: We only picked this place because of its proximity to our destination. We knew the reviews were awful and we were not disappointed. It really is an old, mostly dirty, run down hotel. Carpet in the room was so dirty you definitely didn't want to go barefooted. Bathroom (tub & toilet) was surprisingly clean. Well, except for the 3 places the grout was starting to crumble that were filled with black mold. Front desk staff were personable upon entry, but the four times we went through the lobby to get to the 'restaurant' they made no acknowledgement of our presence. Breakfast was the same as every other hotel/motel that is serving with the exception of no waffles or pancakes. Parking fee is a joke. Towels were ample, but not very new. Sheets were clean. Pillowcases were not double and not king size like the pillows were. It worked in a pinch----but we will try to avoid it in the future. As always the beds were extremely FIRM. Because of negative comments before we didn't even try the 'free wifi'.

author: gary053
title: Two new stays in April and May / close to OHSU
text: It looks that staying in a deluxe room makes the difference, according to the reviews. We stayed three nights in the middle of April and three more on April 30 and May 1 and 2. Hospital rate during these stays was $109. Includes breakfast and wifi. Parking is an additional $15 per night. First room had a microwave with outlets on it, so it was easy to power the laptop and cell phone. Second room did not have an adjustable office chair, so that was missed (in addition to the outlets on the m/w). Second room had a slight amount of mold around the tub and some tiles. I noticed, Shelley did not. Both rooms had flat-screen tv's and Keurig coffee makers. Both were clean, other than fingerprints on the slider--but not bad enough to call for housekeeping. Breakfast has a nice selection, and that's good: the food offered has been the same each time we've stayed. Restaurant and lounge need an update in decor, but staff is prompt and food is tasty. There were four staff behind the desk when we checked in; later in the day, there was only one staff and a large number waiting to be checked-in. What's with this? Guests were waiting and the poor desk clerk was harried ! Management needs to pay closer attention...this has happened more than twice that I've observed.

author: DonH207
title: Cheap, safe, quiet, and convenient, but . . .
text: Cheap, close to the city center, quiet, and safe (I guess). Decent, free breakfast (real scrambled eggs!). Helpful staff, too. But I'm not sure that I would stay here again. I can deal with the weirdly worn and discolored carpets, the door locks that require esoteric wisdom to operate, and the police arresting someone in the parking lot as my friend checked in. What I can't deal with is the dysfunctional internet, which tantalizes one by working for a few minutes and then disappears. If you need to *work* while in Portland (as I did), this is not the place for you. On checkout, I asked at the desk about the feeble internet. The answer was that the place is owned by Portland State University, so the internet is managed by PSU IT, and they just don't care, in spite of tons of complaints from guests. C'mon PSU. Have some pride! Is anyone in a position of authority paying any attention to the many guest complaints???? It should also be noted that many of the staff are, in fact, students in PSU's hotel management program. They were nice, and they tried hard, in my experience. Still, they're just students. Given the many problems with the place, and the many complaints online, one wonders what lesson their teachers are trying to convey. One last point - the web site claims a restaurant on site. Well, I suppose so. But what that really means is that, at the poorly stocked bar, you can also get a hamburger or a salad. It's not a real restaurant.

author: SDH_2_8
title: Unable to give a rating of 2.4, so I will lean toward the lower in order to make a couple of points.
text: The good news items are price and location. The bad news—aside from the fact that parking went up $3 since last year, with no such notice at the time of booking— is that when you book a deluxe room, you don't necessarily get one. When I asked about this at the front desk, they told me that I was in an even-numbered room, and that the deluxe rooms were all odd-numbered. Huh? I said "I booked a room with fridge, microwave, larger TV, 'updated' furnishings ... and I got the same dated-but-clean non-deluxe room I had the year before, and the year before that" (I did mention it's conveniently located, right?). "Oh," said the front desk staff. "If you want those things you have to ask at check-in." "Really?" sez I. "I thought I 'asked' when I booked a deluxe room—on your website, no less." "No, we have to wheel those items into the rooms upon request." No "Sorry, our bad," or "Sorry for the confusion." Just an dull attitude. I did not know what to say. If you're a TV junkie, the reception will drive you mad. Want 'free' wi-fi? Prepare to 'activate' the service daily. This activation link expires 10 minutes after access is requested. If the link has expired, you will need to request access again. Seriously? As for the free breakfast, it's pretty much low-grade. I recommend you walk a block to the food trucks and get a breakfast burrito. Yum!!!

author: Rochester1969
title: Ok for family.
text: Staff great and accomodating. Rooms Clean. Breakfast excellent. Hotel is a bit dated. Great value. Outside of Building and hallways needs a good powerwash and paint job to brighten it up. Ask for a room around the swimming pool. as the rest of the hallways are dark and enough lighting due to layout of building. Wi-Fi is not strong, intermittent. 5-10min walk to starbucks, pizza, food trucks and public transit. Not much to do in area as University district and business area. Hotel located opposite side of downtown (10min with tram). We stayed for 4 days. We would buy the daily bus pass a few times. I would stay here again.

author: Allergictraveller
title: Asthma attack in great location
text: The good: * Good price for location. Downtown is about 1-3 miles walk; tram is within a couple of blocks. * Plenty of food trucks and small restaurants within a 10 minute walk. * Small convenience store within 10 minute walk. * Fridge and microwave in room. The bad: * Old, dilapitated, gloomy with rudimentary bedding. * Allergens! I had an asthma attack within an hour being in the room and I do not easily get an attack. * Very noisy. Highway is close and all rooms have window ac/heating units. All these noises stream through glass doors that do not close well. Ask for a room facing the pool to reduce noise from highway. Luckily I visited outside student season so neighbors were no problem. * Strange personnel. They were more concerned about me trashing the room (really a 40+ yr old?) than me being comfortable (no reaction to my complaint about asthma attack-not even an 'are you okay'). Unless you are a student and used to living in dirty, noisy places-I would avoid this hotel.

author: DoctorM
title: Don't expect much and you won't be disappointed.
text: The University Place hotel is part of the Portland State University and appears to be staffed by students. It is located within 10 minutes walking distance of the campus center in the Park Blocks but it is isolated from the sights and activities of downtown Portland. There was been construction for a new mass transit line and bridge in front of this hotel for more than a year, so you may find restricted access. This hotel was probably built in the late 70s or early 80s and definitely shows it age. The rooms are perfectly ordinary with foam pillows, reasonable bed, and the AC unit in your window. My room on the top floor never cooled down on a 90 degree day in Portland. The room itself was clean and every thing worked except wireless internet. Wireless has better connectivity in the lobby. The breakfast area is just plain sad: located in a dark , mostly empty space with a few steam tables set off to one side, most of the bakery items wrapped in cellophane, large urns of coffee, and with a large screen TV dominating the space. Throw your breakfast voucher in the un-attended basket and help yourself to the uninspired scrambled eggs , sausage, and bacon. You probably won't be spending a lot of time here. I put out a "please clean up my room early" sign on my door at 7:30 am. When I returned at 4pm, my room was not clean. So service is not a high priority here. (or perhaps the staff thought it was a 'do not disturb sign"?) This is a budget hotel for downtown Portland and is an acceptable choice if you are just passing through or visiting the University. Parking is $12 per night. Easy walking distance to campus bars and restaurants.

author: JanW670
title: Not what I expected
text: We ended up at this hotel when we arrived in Portland and found that our condo had been double booked. The hotel lobby is nice and the desk clerks were very helpful. The rooms were clean (we had 2 rooms for 7 days) but pretty basic. Our rooms overlooked the pool which could be very noisy since the windows did not seal very well when shut. There was no way you could take a nap in the afternoon or go to sleep early because of the pool noise. Also, at the time of our visit there was a major construction project going on in front of the hotel which began early in the morning and continued on into the early evening hours. They are reconstructing a road or running the public transportation line through there so it doesn't appear that it will be done any time soon. The hallways to the rooms was very smelly - I almost turned around and went back to the desk to check out but once in the room I did not notice any smell. Also, be aware that this is called the "University Place" for a reason. A lot of student athletes, etc., stay at this hotel when they are traveling to Portland State University for meets and games, etc. That being said, the location of the hotel was great. We were able to walk into town with no problem. The area felt safe (once you crossed the construction zone) and there were some small parks nearby to sit and read. The river was just a couple of blocks away - easy to walk to. The best part for us was that it was available when our other accommodations fell through. The free breakfast was very good - hot food every morning (eggs, bacon, sausage, potatoes) as well as pastries, coffee, bagels, toast, cereal, etc. Plenty of room to sit down and enjoy a meal.

author: OregonProud7
title: Loved The Cookies
text: Spent the night here on Monday September 10, 2012. The hotel was recommended to me by Portland State University, as my son was having an Orientation the next day. The hotel offered a cheaper price for parents of PSU students which was $119.00/night plus an overnight parking fee- $12.00 (ouch!), local taxes etc, grand total $145.88. Pretty steep for such a basic hotel. The nicest feature of the hotel were the warm chocolate chip cookies upon arrival and the morning breakfast. The rest of the hotel was just "okay". It looked like one of the hotels that had seen better days. The road leading to the hotel was bumpy and being completely torn up. The hallways were dingy and dark - a little scary. The outside appeared old, lightbulbs were missing on walkways etc. One nice thing, my bathroom didn't have a working lightbulb, I called the front desk and the service department arrived promptly and replaced the bulb. The front desk was friendly. Worse feature? Our room was overlooking the highway and the noise level was terrible. We heard the traffic all night. Would I recommend this place? Probably. But if it wasn't for the discounted price, I would have stayed somewhere else cleaner and nicer overall.,,

author: Nancy_Bob_WA
title: Accomodating, comfortable, convenient hotel
text: We chose this hotel for a family reunion celebrating a graduation from Portland State in mid-August. There were 17 of us in 7 rooms, including a suite that we used for evening gatherings. Some were there for 2 nights, others up to 5 nights. All the rooms (kings with rollaways, doubles, adjoining king and double and of course the suite) were deluxe, which meant they were upgraded and had a microwave, refrig, flat screen tv and balcony - well worth the extra $10. Because we were here for university commencement, there was an even lower rate from what was already very reasonable. Wi-fi worked just fine. Kids as well as adults enjoyed the pool, and there were lots of tables around it for us to gather. Free breakfast was very nice with eggs, bacon and sausage, potatoes, sweet rolls and muffins, variety of juices, etc. I was impressed that all the breakfast utensils as well as paper plates and cups were compostable. We didn't hear any of the construction noise. This was convenient for public transportation or for walking to destinations, and those with cars didn't fuss about the parking fee. Staff was very courteous and helpful with all our questions. We had take-out from the hotel's Lincoln Station Grill two nights around the pool, and that worked out very well. Everyone in our party said they thought the hotel was perfect for our family reunion and thought that having a suite also had been a very good idea. And the large yummy chocolate chip cookie when we checked in was a plus, too!

author: JelkaD
title: It's ok.
text: I stayed there with my husband for a weekend. We were out walking the city most of the day, Came to the hotel to change and leave again to go out at night. It's ok. I foundthe location good because it gave us opportunity to travel teh city from north to south. The train stop is a couple of blocks away -which was a great advantage. The price is perfect for what we needed. The bed was comfortable, good water heater, good air conditioning. TV- Cable. No fridge. I do have sugestions though, the linens and bed spread where very outdated and worn. I was concerned and went thorugh everything before sleeping there, and asked that they be changed. The new ones were the same. I guessed they were clean- no strange smells or anything, just shabby- cheap. If they would dress the room up a bit it would've been much nicer. A fridge wouldve also helped.

author: lynnwayneg
title: Cheap, comfortable, clean and close to PSU
text: After reading some of the negative reviews about University Place, I checked in with some trepidation. It is hard to believe that those reviewers stayed at the same place that I did! Reservations and check-in were very efficient and friendly. The room was large, comfortable and clean. The beds were fine and had fluffy pillows. Nice amenities like free high-speed Internet, a microwave, a Keurig coffee maker with free coffee and tea pods, and a refrigerator that was empty and actually had room for something besides outlandishly-priced mini-bar items! Ice and beverage machines just down the hall. I also appreciated the availability of the hotel restaurant when my son slept through various meals. We had a room facing the interior that was quiet. We heard the occasional voice in the hall or next door, but nothing bothersome. Besides the extremely reasonable price, the really great thing was the hotel's close proximity to Portland State University and the downtown. PSU is only a few blocks away, as are MAX and streetcar stops. It was a cinch to get to and from the airport and the hotel using MAX. There's really no need for a car (and the $12 daily parking fee) if you're just going to be checking out Portland for a few days. Honestly, maybe the hotel has had a complete makeover since the negative reviews, but I would highly recommend it to someone looking for a reasonably-priced hotel close to downtown.

author: flycake99
title: A dirty, dumpy place
text: I booked a room for my sister and her husband who came visit us in downtown Portland. I read some bad review about this hotel but I thought maybe those people were just having too picky. However, I was wrong. This stay for my sister and her husband turned out to be a nightmare. First, the hotel is old and outdated. The room is dirty and worn. There were some strange bugs crawling on the bathroom floor. The front desk people were rude and did not provide any help at all. The management of this hotel was a big joke. We had to clean the room ourselves before my families can stay for the night. Second, the bed is horrible. My sister and my brother-in-law both had backache on the next day. My sister even got some bug bites on her legs when she was sleeping. OMG! This stay was just totally horrible! What a terrible hotel with zero service and ridiculous price! I will suggest you take your $120 and stay somewhere else. However, if you dislike your in-law, this can be a good place for you to put them in.

author: weezrows
title: Just adequate conference facility
text: I stayed at the University Place as part of a conference being taught by Portland State University (PSU). The hotel room, meeting room, and catering (same fare all week-sliced fruit, mediocre Danish, juice, coffee) were adequate, but nothing worth noting. In Portland, there is a far better selection, even for those on a budget. Most everyone in my meeting complained about the hotel. The room was large, but very basic and in dire need of a renovation. My ceiling was covered with stains and the carpet was in poor shape. The A/C ran constantly with no thermostat. There are no movie channels on the hotel television. One good feature is that a refrigerator was available for $25/stay. Also, another plus was very nice Neutrogena bath products. There is no complimentary computer as in other hotel chains. A computer was available for charge in the small hotel lobby store. It is located within a few blocks of the PSU which is likely the reason for its selection for my conference. It is possible to walk to the more interesting downtown and the Portland trolley is very close. Parking is available for $12/day. PSU appears to be taking advantage of the location and ties to the PSU instead of marketing it to the vacationing public. I would not stay there if I were going to Portland on vacation.

author: blamar
title: Good and fair but not much bad
text: We stayed at the University Center as part of a Conference being held by Portland University. On those terms, everything was very good, the meeting rooms, catering, location, all were just what was required. The room was also adequate. Comfortable but way overdue for renovation and a new decoration scheme. The place felt like it was trapped in the seventies of brown and tan colours. The room its self was large and comfortable. Getting to it was a sojourn worthy of going through a mouse going through a maze. The reception area and front desk was adequately staffed by awesomely uniformed people. In truth, that was one of my big issues. The hotel appears to be run by students and it has the same egalitarian qualities as a student union or student paper. That means there is a refreshing view of attitude but there is little in the way of professional service. The pool is outside and as such was not open, neither was the apparently adequately serviced fitness room. It was never open when I tried to get into it. The location is very easy to drive to but I did get lost a couple of times in Portland's map of one way streets. We like walking and it was a very nice walk to some pizza places, corner pubs, and a great thai restaurant. Also, the Portland trolley is very close (within a couple of blocks) and it provides very good access to the interesting sections of downtown Portland. I would stay there if I were in town for another conference, but it would not be my first choice if I were going to Portland on vacation. The conference price was also very good but that still would not change my mind on where I would stay.

author: Wabe1816
title: Terrible customer service and far
text: The best thing about this hotel is the view of the Bosporus Straight. The sub par customer service and distance from sites motivate me to give this hotel one star. The front desk workers lack human warmth and follow- through. During my stay, neither the front desk personnel nor the concierge took the initiative to greet customers. In fact, I observed the concierge ignore guests who approached his desk. Instead he focused on surfing the web. I noticed excessive mold in the shower in my bathroom, which made me very uncomfortable. When I requested facilities rid the shower of mold, the front desk said they would fix the problem but they neither fixed the problem nor followed up to ensure my satisfaction. During breakfast, it was apparent that the restaurant lacked staff as the tables often lacked basics, like cutlery. It took shouting and persistence, sometimes, to get one of the scarce wait staff to serve customers. The hotel is not located close to public transportation that takes you directly to the tourist sites, like the metro or tram. Instead you have to walk up a hill. While this is fun at first, don’t attempt this walk if you have problems with your bones or joints. Moreover, do not even think of taking this walk at night unaccompanied because the surrounding streets and large swaths of the corniche are dark. The safest, quickest, and most comfortable method of visiting sites or getting to the marmaray sirkeci is via taxi. Buses are tricky if you do not speak the language and are unfamiliar with the city. If you expect to receive a warm welcome, use meticulously clean bathrooms, observes attention to detail and exploit close proximity to the tourist sites without climbing steep inclines, then this place is not for you. Perhaps you should investigate hotels on the tram line, near Gulhane park, instead.

author: SteveAdamson62
title: good location
text: The location of this hotel is perfect for accessing the Sultanahmet by foot. It is was a shame and a scam that this wasn't explained to us our first night there. We arrived around 7pm. Upon check in we asked where we could go for a short, 10-15 minute walk and find some nice place to eat. We were told that there was only one place and that we would need a reservation. Well I thought if that is the only place then yes please make the reservation, which the concierge did with a smile. The restaurant was not at all busy when we arrived. Trust me no reservations were needed. Now the meal was fine don't get me wrong but it wasn't exactly what we were hoping for. And as we found out the next day this was far from our only choice. Had the "concierge" directed us to turn left instead of right upon exiting the hotel we would have found the exact area/ambiance that we were looking for. Instead this fellow directed us to a high priced restaurant that gives kickbacks to those who send customers their way. Soooo not cool. Oh ya and there is no terrace area. That is what through us off in the first place for our dinner choice. We thought we would have dinner and drinks on this supposed terrace. When we asked we were told that there is not a terrace only the glassed in patio out by the road. And so the scam began. Now the rest of the staff were pretty nice. But all it takes is one bad apple to ruin an otherwise good experience.

author: 71hm
title: Great view, Exceptional Location, Great Value
text: The selling point of this place is the location and the view. You get a view on the Marmara sea (but I think you need to specify that while booking, otherwise, you may get a view on the old, little streets of Sultanahmet which isn't nearly as charming as it sounds, but rather claustrophobia-inducing). The Blue Mosque, Hagia Sofia and Topkapi Sarayi are all less than a 10 minute walk away. The Grand Bazaar is an 18 minute walk away or so. You can always cab to the tourist attractions which are on the other side of the Bosphorus or take a bus tour to cover all the more distant bases: eg Galata Sarayi, Dolmabahce sarayi, Beyoglu, Suleymaniyah mosque. You can easily walk to Cemberlitas Hamam/turkish baths, which is a real treat. You can also easily walk to Galata bridge and have a famous balik ekmek under the bridge in one of the restaurants there, a la Anthony Bourdain, and on your way back to Hotel Kalyon you can pick up some wonderful swets from Hafiz Mustafa for dessert. Being so close to so many tourist attractions you are close to convenience stores and restaurants (I recommend A la Turka on Akbiyik Caddesi about 5 nutes away, where we were randomly served by Gordon Ramsay one evening. Keep in mind that you need to make a reservation there and that there is a standard time you need to show up to be served. The food is sublime and it's a great value). Ahirikapi balikcisi, one of the best Fish restaurants in Istanbul is 2 minutes from the hotel (use the back door. Don't be shy to keep asking the staff to open the back doors for you whenever you come and go. They are the ultimate short cut to everything). Loved this hotel. I have no idea whether it has a pool or a gym and honestly I don't care.

author: Scrippsmater
title: Great location, not so great room
text: Our travel agent in Turkey (Sojourn Turkey) told us that we had been 'upgraded' to this hotel since it was much better than our earlier selection. We took the agent's word for it. It is located on the Sea of Marmara. The location cannot be beat. Our room on the other hand was at the back of the hotel overlooking a rear alleyway. The room was small but that was not a problem in and of itself. It was well appointed and had all the amenities that we needed. Since we were busy sightseeing we did not spend a lot of time in this room. The staff was consistently polite with the exception of the gent who runs the restaurant. He was mostly dour and grumpy. The breakfast spread was very good and the restaurant with a beautiful view of the Sea of Marmara was a great place to eat. The one dinner we ate at this restaurant was adequate and will do in a pinch. The lady concierge was very good and efficient. She was able to help us with all our reservations and tickets for the Mevlevi Sema ceremony at the Hodgapasha center. Without an ocean view room this was a wasted 'upgrade'. Would have been better off staying someplace with out a view. I admit it was my fault for not making this clear to the travel agent.

author: AdiH562
title: Mediocre, Over priced
text: The only thing going for this hotle is its location, really. But there are many more hotels in this location... I spent three nights in this hotel on business. I got the classic room which is a simple queen (or full?) bed room for 92Euros, not including VAT, nor breakfast. (Breakfast is additional 14Euros, if you so choose.) The good: Location, AC, free WiFi in room. Helpful staff. The not so good: Hotel is getting older, and is somewhat rundown. I was going to say that it is clean, until I walked into the shower and found myself staring at too much black mold in the grout between the tiles. Room is small, and there is not much beside a bed. There is a tiny desk, but if you are here on business, or a traveler who wants to do some computer work, this desk is not really sufficient for that. There is a small bench in the room, which your luggage will be placed on. Thus, really, there is the bed and not much space around it. The safe in the room is not bolted down and can be simply hauled away with your money and passports in it. So if you were thinking about placing them there, think again. The (moldy) shower is also very tiny, and you are likely to hit each wall, and each of the half-round doors while trying to take a shower. Be careful when stepping out of the shower with wet feet, as the step down to the bathrrom floor is unusually and dangerously high. While everything in my room worked fine, at a colleagues room, only one light bulb worked and his room was dark. All in all, for that price, you can do better elswhere.

author: HinaR_13
title: Beautiful hotel and great location
text: Me and my husband stayed in this hotel in April 2013. The location of the hotel is great, it is just a 5 minute walk to the Sultanahmet square. the walk is very uphill and the roads are cobbly but the trek is worth it. I found the small roads almost magical. We always entered and left from the back door, which staff kindly opened up for us, and we never had to wait for them they were very efficient. The hotel decor is very modern and i cant get over the lovely smell in the hotel overall, it was amazing. We stayed in the classic room, which was very clean and had modern decor. The AC system was fantastic, each day housekeeping left us chocolates and a weather forecast card for the next day. We only ever ordered a chicken sandwich, the sandwich was nice but was needed some sort sauce. The room service was great, I ordered ice cream which was not on the 24 hours menu and it tasted great and was delivered very fast. overall i would say that this is a fantastic hotel with a great location, you can walk to everywhere and do not need to waste money on taxis. the staff are very friendly and make your stay very comfortable. we would love to come back to Turkey and stay in Kalyon Hotel. Mrs. Zahid.

author: Mewithac
title: Great location - friendly staff
text: I recently stayed here on business as part of a larger working party. The trip from the airport was hassle free and relatively short, 15 minutes maybe. Received a warm welcome upon arrival. Reception is modern, spacious with an airy feel. Was struck by the lovely scent but couldn't work out if this was down to the large floral display or some other air freshner. My room was overlooking the old walls and sea at front of property. Room has all you need and again in keeping with the decor elsewhere in the hotel was clean, modern and spacious. The only negative being the walls are a little thin and it meant I could hear my 'neighbouring' colleague rather too well. Also, being woken by the local praying at dawn takes a little getting used too but in many ways added to the cultural aspect . Breakfast was a buffet affair. Attentive staff at all times. No problem with check in or check out. In fact upon arrival I discovered my room was a smoking room. As a non smoker I rang down to reception and they immediately moved me and my colleague. A great hotel, ideally placed for sight seeing, with friendly attentive staff.

author: R0002
title: Great Service, Great Location
text: My girlfriend and I stayed 5 nights, originally it was supposed to be 6 nights but we missed a flight. The hotel were very understanding and didn't charge us the penalty. The rooms are clean but small especially the shower area. Service by the staff is very good, the front desk offer great advice and assistance. The hotel is in a very good location, you are within 10 -15 minute walking distance from the Hagia Sophia, Basilica Cistern, Blue Mosque. Also the Grand Bazaar is a short taxi ride. Other sites such as the bosphorus cruise, egypt bazaar and Kopkapi Palace are all a short taxi ride. For the Bosphorus cruise take the IDO local ferry for 25TL and spend a total of up to 6 hours (including 2-3hr stop over). Also the Kopkapi Palace and Museum can take a full day if you see everything. All the sights I have mentioned are a must. The bazaars are good as well. We used tripadvisor for some restaurants including Pasazade Restaurant,(try to get a table on the roof top), Fuego Restaurant and Raymond Restaurant (near by Pasazade) all were very good and moderately priced. The hotel is about 30 minutes by taxi from the airport for approx 35TL and all the other locations were around 10TL. Just make sure you ask them to use the meter. I highly recommend the Kalyon Hotel for service and location, the rooms are just a bit small. We loved Istanbul and it starts with where you stay!

author: ShaliS83
title: Perfectly located
text: Stayed for 3 nights in April. Unfortunately the days we stayed in Istanbul it rained heavily and was cold! But we still enjoyed our stay at the hotel. It is located in the old town and our room looked out to the sea. The view was great and if you wake up early enough you get to see dolphins swimming about! It was a great sight to see :) The hotel itself is very clean and has a lovely reception area. Staff were very friendly and provided us with brochures and maps of the surrounding area. We stayed in the seaview room which was nice, although the beds weren't the most comfortable we've slept in. Also we didn't have one duvet between us but 2 single duvets but not a big problem. We loved the door at the back of the hotel which was a shortcut into town. We got to walk up the cobbled streets towards the town. The hotel is located very close to the Blue Mosque, Hagia Sophia and Topkapi Palace, also the Grand Bazaar isn't too far either. The cobbled streets leading up to the town are quite steep so ladies bring flat comfortable shoes or trainers!! I had to buy a pair of trainers from the Bazaar the day I arrived! We ate at the restaurant on the first night, I had the gnocchi and my husband had a cheeseburger, enjoyed it very much! There are many restaurants located very close to the hotel so you are spoilt for choice and Turkish food is delicious! Because of the proximity to the main sights, we would definitely stay here again if we were to return to Istanbul

author: aminn_11
title: Just great
text: Take a look at the photo I uploaded. No need to say much! I had a 3 night stay at Kalyon hotel. My room had a sea-view. Through the big wall-size window I had a unique view of the marmar sea. The reflection of sun rays on the sea was just wonderful. I used to sit in the sun in my room looking at the sea for hours. The room was clean. The reception staff were really very very helpful and very friendly. I could easily exchange money in euro with an exchange rate better than the airport. The location of the hotel is really really close to the blue mosque and it was even closer to a sema dance place. I had a nice breakfast. I strongly recommend everyone to try its restaurant. I had a dinner once. The food quality was just great and the price was very reasonable considering the quality. I had no problem using the wireless internet and the speed was good. For sure this hotel will be the only place I consider in my next stay in Istanbul and I have already recommended it to all my friends who might travel to Turkey at some point.

author: Esty666
title: Ladies first
text: I stayed there for two nights on a business trip, so the hotel was booked by the organizers of the trip, but it was an excellent choice. The greatest thing about it is location. You look right across the Sea of Marmora, an unimpeded view, and you can watch all the tankers and cruise ships sailing out of the Bosporus. You can also walk to the old city center with Hagia Sophia, etc. In about ten minutes. Along the way you pass bars, small local and larger restaurants. The staff at the hotel was nice and friendly and accommodating, and the room was clean and, well, very modern. What was funny was when we were checking in. Each of us was handed his key to his room, and when it was my turn the front desk clerk had already taken the next key off the hook and then turned and saw me. He checked his name list, gave me another look and put the key back, getting a different one. Oh yeah? What now? I have to say here that I was just one of two women in a group of almost twenty, and the guy had obviously not recognized my first name as female. Later we realized that practically everybody else in my group had rooms to the back – and they were all moaning the following morning about being awoken VERY early by the muezzin who seemed to be right on their balconies. I had been given a room to the front – absolutely quiet and overlooking the sea. Heehee … oh yes, the food at the hotel was good as well, not outstanding, but good.

author: EternalSunshine78
title: Excellent location - average hotel
text: If you prefer to enjoy the most relevant historical attractions in Instabul, this is the right one choice due to Its location (it is 5-10 min walking distance from Blue Mosque, Hagia Sophia and Basilica Cisterna and not too far away from Topkapi Palace). Having in mind how huge is Istanbul in order to save money and time to reach historical sites, this is more than great advantage that adds value to this hotel. Other advantages: The reception staff and guest relations desk are very friendly, positive and at service all the time. The sea view is very nice. Superior Rooms and Suites are furnished recently, quite spacious including bathrooms. The bar is very nice in terms of atmosphere, view and staff. Lobby area is modern, elegant and spacious. Disadvantages: Cleaning standards are not so high (I noticed a lot of dust in the room, especially in the corners). We booked Classic Room which is TOO SMALL including the "king size" bad which is hardly for two persons (so we had to pay extra for Superior room which is normal size). There is huge traffic noise due to its location (especially if you keep the window opened). The breakfast is too expensive for the quality they offer - it is the same breakfast every day, it is poor choice especially sweat pastry and the coffee is awfull. There is no gym, turkish bath, pool or some additional values that are expected from 4 stars hotel. Sleeping quality is not so high, I find the mattress pretty tough. Summa summarum - This is the great choice for touristic visiting due to Its location but a little bit expansive for the quality and content they offer i.e. the ratio price/quality is bad.

author: gal_tash
title: Trendy & Fantastic Location!
text: Our family (2 adults and 2 young children) stayed here for 5 nights. The location is perfect walking distance to many of the touristic sites & lots of little shops nearby. It also has lovely views of the water. Our kids had fun watching several boats pass by our hotel window. I would definitely recommend this hotel. The staff were friendly. Only down side was no free airport shuttle. The airport is fairly close (about 15 min drive); however, it cost us $60 Euros to take a shuttle one way. If you can manage to take a taxi, it's about $30. With the amount of luggage we had, we required a larger vehicle. The hotel was pretty quiet. The cleaning staff did an excellent job! They cleaned our room everyday and it was spotless! One day they left chocolates on our pillows and one day they left a piece of paper informing us of the weather for the following day. Great TVs in the rooms, but it went to waste because there was no channels in English (no satellite TV). Our only purpose was for our 4-year-old to watch cartoons....which he watched in Turkish language. If you don't care about TV, then it won't be an issue. Satellite would of been appreciated though since we couldn't spend much time out in the evening since the kids were sleeping. Laptop came in handy for this :)

author: Memis1982
title: You feel very welcome, very important and very very...good!
text: Hallo to all! While I was in Istanbul, my company has booked for me at first three days, then extended it to four days. So four days in Istanbul...four days at Kalyon! At my first entrnce of this hotel I could see it belongs to the turkisch modern and historic culture. It has got an uncompareabel flair, also beause of its location. Weh you leave it you can see the other side of Istanbul und this fantzastic see. You can go for a walk hours and hours and at the end you will forget the time but not your space. It took only a few minutes to reach the great, and I mean great, Sultan Ahmet Mosque and the Hagia Sophia. Kalyon Hotel has a very central location from where you can reach the railway system in Istanbuk, which is very comfortable und cheap. And when you come back to your hotel, the Kalyon team will welcome you again, like it is your first visit...with a warm and helpful smile. After your first night and your great sleep, take a shower and go downstairs to the bright und luxury dining room to get your tasteful breakfast, which can be turkish or also european. It is up to you, but one thing is sure; you will enjoy. And I think that a day with a perfekt breakfast will be a perfekt day, so you will always have a great day...in Kalyon Hotel Istanbul! I swear! Memis

author: DianaFilistine
title: Prime location, beautiful view!
text: I stayed at the Kalyon for a week in June 2010. From the minute that I was picked up from the airport by the car service that the Kalyon provided until I was dropped back off at the airport a week later, I was satisfied. I booked two sea view rooms and was so pleased by cleanliness and the view of the Marmara Sea that I had from both rooms. The Old City of Sultanahmet is a short, easy 5 minute walk from the back door of the hotel, with restaurants, cafes and small shops lining the streets on the way up. Late at night there are night guards that are lining the back street, and there is always a greeter in the front of the hotel. I don't speak Turkish and I am a young female but I felt completely safe in and around our hotel day and night. The staff of the hotel provided us with impeccable service and we were always greeted with a smile. The day before I flew in to Istanbul, I received an email telling me that my hotel reservation was cancelled, I called the hotel and they worked the issue out immediately. I had no issues with anything at this hotel. Food in the onsite restaurant is expensive, but a short walk out the front of the hotel to the left or to the right will bring you to restaurants that are open from about 8 am until about 1030 pm, after 1030 pm, the Armada hotel serves light sandwiches until midnight, but for the best food in the city, it is definitely worth the walk up to Sultanahmet. Each morning, the maid service will leave the weather report on your pillow as well as a signed card from the maid asking you to contact her if there are any issues. Internet access is controlled via your room and passport numbers, and it is free and unlimited for the entirety of your stay. The hotel is clean, well appointed, and in a perfect location, the staff is fantastic, and the price is right. The Kalyon Hotel is one that I will definitely be staying at again when I return to Istanbul. If you have any further questions about details of my stay, feel free to email me at ein_il_qamar@hotmail.com

author: Dilber_10
title: Kalyon is worth to stay!
text: Finally it is my turn to write a review about Kalyon Hotel in Istanbul. Let me first mention that I have read a lot of reviews in booking.com and in tripadvisor about many hotels before my travel. I had couple of hotels in my list to choose and Kalyon was one of them. I was not sure that Kalyon would really proof my expectation. Now about the hotel. it is near to airport located in old city, near Sultanahmet mosque, Topkapi palace, Al-Sofia and other historic places about 5 min walk. Breakfast is super with wonderful view to the Marmara sea. You can see dolphines swimming in the sea in the morning, while having your breakfast. Rooms are newly refurbished , clean, no carpet on floor. LCD TV monitor. Generally i would rate it good +. You may order one of 3 types pillows free of charge to your room, they are feather, ortopdeic and hard ortopedic. In rooms and in the hotel wi-fi free of charge. I recommend this hotel to everyone and if i come to Istanbul ever again, i will choose this hotel. Apart from center Taksim square, this place is very quite. I also recommend "Mesale" restorant which is near Sultanahmet. The restorant has a very good menu and life music and "dervish"( men in white clothes) dansing. Staff is very welcome and friendly. I will attach photos soon.

author: Coffe_N
title: Ok business hotel with hard beds
text: I stayed at Kanyon hotel for three nights in October 2009 and paid 92 Euros per night inclusive of breakfast. The hotel is located in the Sultanahmet area where many of the tourist attractions are but from the hotel there are some quite steep roads leading up to the Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia. There are several bars, restaurants, and minimarkets close to the hotel so you will not have to go without food and drink. If you take the regular train, there is a stop, Cankurtaran, almost next to the hotel. But altogether the location is so-so, especially when considering there is a big road just outside the hotel and traffic in Istanbul is noisy. The hotel seems to be very business-oriented so the staff is somewhat “cold” but very polite. Checking in was quite fast and I got a room on the 2nd floor facing the street. The room was fairly big but somewhat worn and the bathroom was not in that great shape with some visible stains and a crack in the sink. But altogether an OK experience EXCEPT for the bed which was hard as a rock! And I am not just saying hard – I mean HARD and my colleague in another room was of the exact same opinion. Internet was for free and there was some problems logging on but a trip to the reception provided me with a user name and password. There were some problems with internet, especially late in the evening when I just didn’t manage to use the internet. Breakfast was OK though annoying things as staff not letting you pour your own coffee and so did occur. The hotel was a fair value but compared to the other 4-star hotel I stayed at (Marmara Sisli), the Marmara was far better. I honestly think you can find better hotels in Istanbul for this money and the bed almost killed my back.

author: /undefined
title: Disgusting
text: Booked a smoking room as we did at other hotels. In which at other hotels you couldn't even smell the smoke. When you walked down the hallway it was horrendous n the room was worse. The blankets are stained. Dust behind the bed was half inch thick the smoke alarm was hanging off the ceiling. Carpet was crusty. We changed rooms to non smoking blankets still stained toilet has rust stains from bolts on seat shower handle grungy with mold n mildew. Dust still half inch thick. Couldn't sleep well due to paranoia of possible bed bugs. I left my luggage outside for the night when we got home. Then threw it in washer with boiling hot water with amonia. Outside garbages should be bigger as they overflow fast? Won't be staying there ever again. Worst I have ever seen. I will say the staff was very friendly and courteous. Worst I have ever stayed at 😞

author: /undefined
title: Friendly staff, nice play to stay if you want to save
text: It's my family's first time overnight stay at Super 8. We love the hospitality of the staff at the Rogers Minnesota branch -starting with the guy in the front desk (I forgot his name-if it's Scott) and the friendly lady in the dining room. During our week long trip, we stayed in 3 diff hotels because we had to move places. Aside from the low price (having given a discount because of booking early), we love the fact that we had a free breakfast in Super 8= a deal that wasn't part of the accommodation from the other two more expensive places (double and triple rate than Super 8) where we also stayed in. Great starter! Even for my two toddlers who had cereals and bagel---which left me worry free scrumbling for something they could eat. Place was also accessible to groceries (a nearby Target store) as we had to buy immediate needs like water and milk, and fast food as well. Spacious parking. Location was nice peaceful. I was able to go around and jog early morning in the nearby neighborhood and commercial area without having to worry about safety. I just noticed though, that the bath tub in our bedroom wasn't that clean. However, I love the fact that we were given free soap and shampoo as well--for that price rate. My husband and I agree to go back and try considering Super 8 again the next time we travel and had to hop different places again. I was actually discouraged by a friend to book at SUper 8 because she had an unpleasant experience with a room that smelled like cigarette. I am glad we didn't have that concern at all. Will come back again.

author: /undefined
title: We were put in a smoking room only because that is all that...
text: We were put in a smoking room only because that is all that was left. Not Super 8's fault we had to take a smoking room, but we did not anticipate the condition to be so poor. The room did not have any fan running and it smelled just terrible in the room. The comforters, blankets and the sheets all had stained and BURN HOLES from cigarrettes through them. The blankets were so badly worn out and old and should have been replaced years ago. Likewise with the mattresses. You could feel the springs they were so old and worn. There was no shampoo or conditioner set out. Worst was that there was no additonal toilet paper or any soap in the room. No one was at the front desk when we went down to see about new blankets and soap, so had to have my kids cover up with towels for the night. No one would sleep under the blankets. I would have rather slept in car. Gross and very disappointing. I typically go for non-smoking rooms. Now that I have had to stay in a smoking room, im actually afraid to stay in a hotel that offers them period. If there are burn holes in the blankets.....i know there are sprinklers but come on. That is a safety hazard for everyone in the hotel.

author: StaceyW788
title: I will NEVER stay at this Super 8 again!
text: I stayed at this hotel on June 30, 2012. The guy at the front desk was blunt and rude. He quoted us a price for the room which we thought was unreasonable since my in-laws always stay at this hotel every 4-6 weeks. The quote was almost double the price. My husband told the guy that his parents have stayed here for years all of the time and they have never paid that much. He looked up my father in-laws name in the computer and said...yep he does get a cheaper rate and I don't know why and I cannot give it to you. We should of left but we didn't. Stupid mistake on our part. The hallway and room smelled like cigarette smoke. (I had a non-smoking room) The beds were "very" uncomfortable, the rooms are small and no refrigerator. The air conditioner was louder that a 747 jettaking off. We couldn't sleep because of the hard as ever beds and the air conditioner noise, so we got up early and were at breakfast @ 6:00am. Which was horrible!!!! Frozen waffles that you put into the toaster and they were paper thin....really! There was cereal, yogurt, bagels, juice and coffee. That is why I did at least gave it a 1 star.

author: TravelerSpeaks
title: Good location, avg service, poor management
text: It is the end of March 2015 and I'm here at this hotel for a business conference in the beautiful city of Cuernavaca. The hotel is picturesque, located at a nice location not too far from the city center, has a small swimming pool with a bar nearby as well as an outdoor restaurant. The rooms are well-maintained, but upon my arrival I did find mosquitoes in my room which I reported to the reception and they took care of it. Service, in general, at this hotel is mediocre. While at the restaurant they forget things like giving you cutlery or napkins. They forget placing salt-and-pepper on your table and take on an average 15 minutes to get you the check. But these are still inconveniences one can deal with. I got the shock of my life when I was at the gym this evening. The gym basically has six machines and two air conditioners. However at the time of this writing the treadmill wasn't well oiled so it was quite slippery and hence a health hazard, the exercise bike was broken, the stepper was not calibrated and was working in a very weird way, none of the two air-conditioners were working: one was not even turning on while the other was not cooling at all. So I went down to the reception to report this to the manager on duty and I asked her a simple question that when was the last inspection done for the gym. She had no answer for me and that was shocking. She even said that I go visit the gym at the holiday in express Hotel situated nearby and she said their gym was fully functional and this was surprising to me because normally in my experience the express hotels ranked lower in services than the full service holiday inn hotels. However, this hotel has an excellent breakfast buffet, much more food than you can deal with in the morning. I hope the hotel management can get their act together as soon as possible and improve the service at this hotel and take care of the maintenance issues on site. This is one of the very few decent hotels in this remote town of Cuernavaca.

author: Viewfr0mtheHill
title: Great Value for Paradise
text: We came here on business and chose this place for its price and reputation. Boy, were we not disappointed. I would come back for vacation if I chose to come. The valet took the bags and the car quite quickly. Check in was smooth without issue. We got what we asked for (king non-smoking). In fact they put us in rooms where they had just put new carpeting (nice). I was impressed that they had put motion activated lighting in the hallway but chuckled at how long they took to turn on (they turned on just as i was getting to my door). The room was beautiful, modern and spacious. The bed was comfortable and I got a great nights sleep. No problems with the internet (included). Actually sat at the bar by the pool that evening checking my e-mails (very relaxing). Breakfast was the buffet (we had this added to our room rate) outside by the pool. What a selection! The scrambled eggs with salsa was amazing and so was the service. Felt like we had three waiters to ourselves. Great stay and actually looking forward to coming back.

author: DannyM134
title: 4-star in Mexico, 2-star in Arkansas
text: While the courtyard and pool (although I never used it) are quite nice, and the overall property is well maintained and manicured, that's where the pro's end. First, you get killed with the exchange rate. As of today, their rate was 11/1 but the published rate is well over 14/1. I'd definitely suggest booking through a travel site rather than through Holiday Inn. Second, this is a Holiday Inn, NOT a luxury hotel. Every service person wants/expects a tip and will basically wait for it until you either cave in or walk/drive away or shut the door. I'm sorry but I can park my car on my own. If you don't let me, that's fine, but I'm not going to tip just because you won't let me do things on my own. Third, pack enough to where you won't have to do laundry. It's $35 pesos per shirt, $45 pesos for pants and $25 for miscellaneous items. That's just for laundering... not dry cleaning. There are no self serve facilities available. Fourth, don't attempt to extend your stay as they tend to only honor the original reservation and that's it. It happened to me today and now I'm stuck looking for a new place for 2 more nights. I told them that I'd need to extend my stay at least until Wednesday but to keep it reserved until Friday. I got the friendly head nod and signed a new sheet and got a new key. I should have had someone who was bilingual to clarify with them. Well, aside from that, the room service is quick, but don't order the pizza as their cooks have yet to master the art of sauce. I'd suggest walking 2 blocks and getting Domino's for better quality and at a lower cost.

author: 233perec
title: So cosy and welcoming!
text: This is the very first Parador of them all, the beginning of a great saga of iconic hotels all over Spain. Being inaugurated more than 80 years ago, I must admit that I was a bit suspicious about its conservation state. But the whole Parador is quite well-kept, even better than other oldie Paradores with a similar rate indeed. The landscape was also a great surprise; located in a forest in a mountain range not too far away from Madrid, you will be able to enjoy excellent views in your way to the hotel and, of course, if you decide to use it as basecamp for hiking around the area. Gredos is like a palace-proportioned hunting hut, that means a spacious Hotel meticulously decorated with plenty of animalistic and hunt-related things here and there. I found it so cosy and enchanting and I totally loved the numerous fireplaces toped with deer horns and other pieces of taxidermy, the old maps depicting the mountain range or the shotguns and ammo bags exhibited to create that wild countryside atmosphere; but of course, some people might not find it so appealing. It's just my taste. What you would definitely enjoy regardless of your sensibility for animals are the numerous saloons, lounges and terraces available which make this Parador a really comfortable place to spend your time, more than just sleep and carry on. Not surprisingly, Spain's leading politicians meet here to write down the current Spanish Constitution in 1978. In my particular case, I got "trapped" there because of an unexpected snowstorm (don't underestimate the weather there in wintertime) and I enjoyed one of the most charming evenings I can remember having a wonderful dinner and then reading a good book by the fireplace while I could see through the window the snowflakes falling down. A kind of postcard picture you might expect in a Swiss shelter but not really in a Spanish Hotel two hours by car from the capital. If you decide to sit down at the table here, don't miss the El Barco beans and a good sirloin of beef from Avila, which are the regional delights. As usual, the traditional menu was the wise choice here. There's not much to say about service and the general quality of the rooms a part from being as good as expected, which in the case of a Parador is always a good thing. Definitely an interesting place to stop at and a unmissable landmark for a Parador fan -like me ;D

author: JBeckers
title: Vintage hotel that captures the essence of Brasilia
text: As a tourist, you are probably going to visit Brasilia for its architecture and city design. You are only doing this if you are interested in architecture. For example, I did not want to visit Brasilia first but my wife insisted so we went for 2 days. I am glad I did because it is a side of Brasil that is worth seeing in my opinion. It gives some insight in the visionary development of the country in the 1950s-60s. Just to say: because you are probably visiting Brasilia as a tourist interested in architecture, you should book this hotel, since it is a part of the history of the city. Niemeyer himself had a hand in the design of this hotel. Moreover, it is in a very silent and beautiful location at the lake a little bit outside the centro. A taxi ride to the central axis of the city is about 30 reais. You can also take a bus just outside the hotel that will take you to the central bus station, for 3 reais. What we did, is to take the bus to the city, and then take a taxi back. Breakfast is nice. Swimming pool also very nice. Diner in the restaurant, called Oscar, is fine but not the most refined Italian food we have eaten in Brazil. Interior of the hotel is vintage. Very modern in its own way. It also smells nice upon entering, somehow this is important to me. The reception staff was very friendly and helpful.

author: Stenhouse_1
title: Beautiful building
text: This is a beautiful building that has been sympathetically restored. The rooms are very clean and quite spacious but the nice balconies have no furniture on them, which is a pity. Reception staff are pleasant and efficient and appear to speak a range of languages (a relief given how dreadfully my non-Portuguese pointing combination works). Breakfast is great & included in the price. All in all a great place to stay in Brasilia. A couple of niggles: A real lack of hot water for the shower. Get up early or be taken back to memories of your school days! The second issue is the restaurant, which I'd generously call mediocre. The room is beautiful, but the service is ponderous and the food a little dull. I totally understand that some people don't like being a waiter, but really that's no excuse for looking miserable and being bad at it. Frankly, either get some training done or get a better team. As it stands, Oscars is letting the business down. Lastly, cappuccinos / lattes etc. are on the menu, but nobody will actually serve you one. Odd to say the least. Niggles aside, come for the building and enjoy.

author: rafkam
title: A must for design enthusiasts
text: In a city where all hotels are clustered together, I jumped at the occasion of staying out at the “out of the action” Brasilia Palace. Its lakeside setting made for a quiet alternative, and the opportunity to stay in a Niemeyer original is an added bonus for those interested in architecture. The hotel is set in the “North Hotel Zone”, which is right next to the Alvorada Presidential Palace, but quite far from everything else. Therefore, if staying here, renting a car is recommended (as is a GPS, since navigating the city’s complicated airplane-shaped geography is quite complex). Apart from Oscar, the pretty-good onsite restaurant, the only other option within walking distance is a German bar-restaurant “Bar do Alemao”, also on the lake. The lobby décor makes for a great first impression, although the hallways and rooms quickly erase those in favour of a mid-70s institutional (yet clean and functional) feel. Check in is swift, and all rates include breakfast, which is a very good buffet served at the Oscar restaurant, with a nice outdoor area by the pool. The rooms are all laid out along one side of the rectangular building, facing east, and the building itself is “divided” between the north and south wings. North wing rooms apparently feature a lake view from its balconies, although they are directly above the function room, which featured a wedding on every night of our weekend stay (the place looks like a popular wedding venue), so it might not be recommended for light sleepers. Our room, in the south wing was very quiet, but the view from our balcony facing the hotel’s kitchen/service entrance was less than desirable. Rooms are spacious, and have all mod cons, but are generally soulless. No complaints regarding comfort. The main point for staying here is to admire the design, the murals, and to relax by the very nice and quiet pool. We did not see any kids during our stay, so can’t comment on whether it would be kid-friendly. Other facilities include a gym, although few would want to venture in the 5 x 5 aquarium just outside reception. Check out was quick and painless. Probably would not stay again as the novelty factor is now gone, preferring the convenience of a more “central” hotel, but I would still urge first time tourists to stay here, if only for one night as it is a truly unique place.

author: midmodman
title: Living in a Niemeyer
text: We chose the Brasilia Palace in order to experience living in a Niemeyer building. On that level, it did not disappoint. It's a well-maintained modernist hotel. The rooms are small, clean, and efficient. Each room has a nice balcony. The service is friendly and attentive, though few staff speak English, as was our experience throughout Brasilia. The breakfasts were very good - a wide array of hot and cold items, fresh fruits, juices, and baked goods. There is a nice, large pool area. In all, a really good value. We had a very disappointing experience in the hotel's restaurant, Oscar. They were clearly understaffed and overwhelmed the night we dined there - we only saw four waiters for the entire, completely full restaurant. No busboys, no hostess. Our waiter appeared never to have eaten in a restaurant, let alone work in one - he seemed flummoxed by how to place silverware on the table and went in search of a corkscrew for a screwtop bottle of wine. The food, once it finally came, was fine. Some downsides to know about - the fitness center is small and the universal machine was broken when we were there. The location is isolated and cabs need to be called specially to the hotel, which adds a surcharge to your fare. (It's about R$20 from the hotel to the major landmarks.) Even though the hotel is right on the lake, there are no recreational opportunities right there - not even a path near the water - because you are in a secure zone near the presidential palace (which you can walk to). We were happy we stayed here, but you need to weigh your desire for modernist authenticity with your need for convenience.

author: RonaldoDaSilva
title: A Masterpiece
text: This place was amazing. Thank you TripAdvisor for allowing me to read all the original reviews and be able to get a real feel for this hotel before getting there. I simply loved it! Perfect location - 10 minutes from all the major sites in Brasila - and close to the Brazilian President's residence. Friendly staff (they could be a little friendlier), and excellent in-house restaurant (Oscar)... a MASTERPIECE in modern architecture. I couldn't get over the architectural lines, glass, concrete, tiles, mid-century furniture and expansive views. The grounds are peaceful and very zen. The rooms are simple but comfortable and an extension of the whole architectural experience. The gym was tiny but worked for me. I really enjoyed the gym’s location in relation to the other common areas of the hotel and, most importantly, its views. A little history I learned... this was one of the 1st buildings to be built in Brasilia in 1958. It caught on fire in the 70s and supposedly it took a few decades to be remodeled. Great job remodeling it, great place, amazing experience... a Masterpiece if you are into it. Otherwise, I am sure there is always a Marriot or Sheraton around for an "Americana" experience. Boooo!

author: travelhappytraveler
title: Classic building, nice stay
text: My husband, an architect, was thrilled to stay in this Oscar Niedermeyer building. It lived up to his expectations. It was equally nice to see that they have maintained it so well. It is a beautiful property. The rooms are simple and clean. Not the most comfortable bed for me, it was firm. So, if you like that style, you'll be content. The bathroom is clean and seems to be fairly new. The location is okay, you will want to have a car though. I can't imagine touring from this location without a car. Plenty of free parking. The staff is pleasant. They don't all speak English, but we never had an issue communicating our needs. We did have problems with the air conditioning which they fixed the next day. The halls are long and we were at the very end. only issue is the layout is strange - they really only use the center elevators which is inefficient. The breakfast is abundant and great. Oscar the attached restaurant has good food, it is expensive though. it isn't particularly a tourist hotel, seemed to be a business hotel primarily. I would recommend it for a couple of nights if you are an architecture buff, it not, I'd just take a peek at it.

author: ZoBlu
title: Great for architecture buffs
text: I really struggled with my rating of this hotel, as there was nothing particularly wrong with it, but nothing particularly great about it either. I really wanted to give it four stars, but in the end all I can say is that it is 'fine'. I recommend the hotel with some reservation - I would make sure you get a good rate, otherwise I'm not sure that there are extremely compelling reasons to stay here. Overall, the environment is a bit sterile, so maybe it's only really best for business travellers. The negative: - It's true, the location is not great and you absolutely have to take a taxi to get anywhere (there is a bus apparently, but the hotel staff discourage you from taking it), although the hotel say that they will offer cycle hire next year, which would be great. - The rooms; they are, again, 'fine', but nothing very special. I was bemused by the non-flatscreen television in the room. Not a big deal at all, of course, but in this day and age and at these rates, I was surprised at this 'non-modern' touch. On a serious note, though, the rooms were actually quite a bit loud. I could hear the person in the next room banging around in the morning. The questionable: - The service. The front desk staff were very helpful, and the maids were cheerful, but the latter did seem to want to hurry us out of our room in the mornings. The staff in the restaurant were more apathetic, failing to clean tables or lay new place settings. The last morning, we ate at a dirty table and then were locked in the restaurant once breakfast time officially ended! The positive: - Architecturally stunning. My partner loves photographing interesting buildings and spent a lot of time here outside taking pictures. Of course, one could do that without actually staying here.

author: doc_hapi
title: Location is not enough
text: Attended a convention at Kochi Japan and was booked by a travel agency for my 5 days stay at Nishitetsu Inn. Looked at the previous reviews and was told that it was clean and the location was ideal for a tourist. Pros: Staff was courteous. Location was good. Plenty of nearby restaurants. Cons: I was given a smoking room and I am allergic to smoke. The odor was so strong it is as if I am the one smoking. (Must be the central ventilation). I requested if I can be transferred on a later time or date but to no avail. Was told it was fully booked even if I can see guests leaving (checking out) on the succeeding dates. A day or two does matter. Room was small around 3.5x5m (includes the bathroom) with a very small window. Not ideal if you are a bit claustrophobic. Was given a meal ticket for breakfast. On the last day, I noticed that I lacked 1 stub. Told the front desk of my concern and was initially being asked to pay. They eventually gave one after saying that I will just write something about it.

author: everlong1
title: Good location to walk around the center of Kochi city
text: The hotel is located in the center of Kochi city. From the hotel, Kochi castle and Kochi castle history museum, shopping streets, Ryoma's birth place, good local restaurants are all walking distance. You can take trams to go to the castle if you are tired of walking, the tram stop is just 30 sec away from the hotel. If you want to go to Katsurahama and Ryoma museum, you will need to take a bus. The bus station to Katsurahama is also 30 sec walk. Even though the hotel is located in the center of the city, you don't hear noise in the night. Ah, yes you are not in Manhattan NY, so the city is not busy in the night. After 9PM, there are few cars outside. The room is small, just like NY hotels, you don't have space to open your suite case on the floor, but i could manage it. Breakfast area is also small and it gets crowded if you want to take it at 6:30, but they don't stay long, so you will find a seat if you wait 5-10 minutes, while you are taking food from buffet area. I think there is an option not to include breakfast in your plan. There are not so many breakfast alternatives around the hotel, but you can just buy bread and coffee at the convenience store in the first floor. The best thing in this hotel is that they offer FREE smartphone during your stay. Yes, it is free of charge. You can even call international. you can take the smartphone outside and look up maps, search interesting points, and restaurants. it is just 10 minutes Kochi station, if you have a big suite case, you might want to take a cab or a tram, but if you have only carry-on bags, it is easy flat walk from the station. This hotel is better than the hotels in front of Kochi station. very conveniently located.

author: MunichEricJ
title: Great location, nice, new property
text: Nishitetsu has impressed with a line of business hotels which offer just a bit more flair than the usual business hotel Spartan drabness. The Kochi branch continues that flair. I had a friendly and quick check- in and was given Room 1223, a double bed room looking north towards the main train station. The room was clean, bright and well- organized. There were not so many amenities in the room, since they put them in the lobby and between check- in and elevator, you can choose what you want to use from a wide range, a good idea. The bed was comfortable and the room was very quiet, no noise from the outside or from neighbors. The bathroom was a bit smaller than usual, even for a business hotel, and the tub was so small that I could not have sat upright with my legs stretched forward. But it was spotlessly clean and everything worked well. Breakfast is in the back of a Lawson conbini adjacent to the lobby. It’s an excellent buffet, with the traditional Japanese items and additionally fried noodles with cabbage, fried eggs, and a really good battered fried fish. The fried fish didn’t look like much but the taste reminded me of my fave Cambridge chippie on Mill Road. And yes, it’s great for breakfast ;-) I had to hold back or I would have stuffed myself. The setting is along the restored canal. The bridge which gives the hotel and neighborhood its name is also adjacent to the hotel. There is an arcade just a wink north, but even on a Saturday evening there was not much going on – it has seen better days, and hopefully the Nishitetsu , canal restoration along its modest length and other projects will help revive the arcade, too. There is a wonderful Bonito restaurant in the arcade. The hotel is also at the cross of a couple of tram lines, and very near the airport limo bus. If you want to walk from the main train station, it’s 800m, not so far and a straight path from the station, very easy. All in all, it’s an excellent value, great location and worth considering.

author: joebbb
title: Convenient, good value
text: So on our recent visit to Shikoku, we stayed here a couple of nights during our visit to Kochi. Upon arrival at the train station, we hopped on a tram, and 2 stops later, were at the hotel. Do not attempt this with suitcases, but with smaller backpacks, it worked well. The hotel is centrally located at the intersection of two major streets. The famous Harimayabashi (bridge) is right behind the hotel in a cute little park. There is a convenience store connected to the hotel. The room we had was small by western standards but spacious enough. It was quiet, comfortable, and clean. Extra amenities were located in the lobby. Staff were helpful and friendly, and although English is limited, we had no trouble communicating. When we came back to the hotel at 2:00 PM the second day, the room had not yet been made up. After making a request at the front desk, we waited about 20 minutes, and it was done. I suppose we should have put the "make up the room" sign on the door, but we would assume they would make up the occupied rooms first. Anyway, it was a minor inconvenience, if that. We walked to Kochi Castle, and there is a long, covered shopping arcade that pretty much runs from near the castle all the way to this hotel. There is a huge variety of shops and restaurants, including the Hirome Food Mall, which has the best katsuo tataki I have ever had, among many other local delicacies.

author: 284leandror
title: Not a Family option in LA
text: I’ve been to several Intercontinental in different places. In general, they are very good and with excellent service. Maybe, I had a bad luck this time. Arriving at the hotel, reserved room were not available. They blamed “third party agency” (hotel.com). After some discussion, they found a king bed room in another floor (imagine yourself, a floor away from your kids). Then, another long discussion and the “found a handicap room in the same floor. Bad start. Next day we tried to use the pool and it was not available due to an external event. Next day my room was not made at 18:00. Next day breakfast took 1 hour to be served and it was cold, wrong, etc. Disaster (Manager didn’t charge as it was really bad). To get into your room, one need to take at least two elevator (3 if you park). 1st day looked cool, next ones...not a good idea. Downtown LA has nice stuffs, but not appropriate for families. In summary, don’t go with your family to this hotel. It does not worth what they will charge for.

author: Lorrdb
title: Beautiful Hotel
