text: This is a beautiful hotel with stunning views! The lobby is on the 70th floor so it takes some time getting used to going up to go down to your room to go back up to come down and exit. Staff are very friendly and helpful. My room was lovely and clean. The bathroom sink drained slow but other than that, it was great. The rooftop bar on floor 73 is pretty but the $25 cover for non-hotel guests is steep considering the view gets blocked by the tall red chairs that are along the windows. Bring your own jacket on a windy night as they seemed to run out of blankets every night we were there. Lobby bar is nice with a great view too. More servers would have been helpful as we were seated in the lobby for 20 min without anyone approaching. We went elsewhere for cocktails. I called pre-arrival and needed to ask for a refrigerator for my medication. I was on hold for 20 min and disconnected 3 times but on my 4th call back, Gerald Bratton answered and he was a superstar!!! He said he could hear the frustration in my voice and he would take care of my request and make sure I had a fridge even though he couldn't reach anyone in housekeeping at that time. Sure enough, I checked into my room and there it was!! Thank you Gerald from making my check in smooth and easy!

author: BGT_NV
title: THE SERVICE MATCHES THE VIEWS
text: Stunning views are a draw whether you live in a high rise building or just get an upper floor when traveling on holiday or business. My sanctuary in this 73-story hotel was on level 34. I refer to the cocoon-like experience I had for a 2-night stay. Beyond the stunning lobby and views out from floor 70, I was impressed in the quiet elegance from the Porte-cochère entry off 7th Street whilst being whisked to the lobby in a high speed lift. The elevator ride was swift, smooth, and quiet. All the attributes needed for the forthcoming great guest experience. Check-in was efficient and I didn’t mind the 90-minute wait for my room. An avid explorer, I took a late lunch in Dekkadance the 69th floor restaurant. More about that later. My room was the pinnacle of the experience. Spotless. Everything worked. The elegant bath and sexy obscure glass wall that borrowed light from the bedroom all added to my relaxed privacy. Myriad lighting options all centrally controlled at bedside and by the door; a great shower, beautiful bath and bedroom finishes led to an overall great value for my visit. The service exceeded my expectations. A late night dinner in the aforementioned Dekkadance [clever spelling aside, it still delivered a pleasurable indulgence in luxury dining] proved to be an even greater surprise. Manager, Larry Katchen made a casual dinner a memorable experience for me and my guest. A private tour of roof top bar on Level 73 capped off the evening. I will return. Thanks to all the staff.

author: Travelandshop2019
title: A week stay
text: This hotel is very luxury and big, the staffs there is very polite and friendly, i do admit they have the best staff and workers there so far i went to so many hotels. But one thing made me really disappointed is , i requested a refrigerator to put my toodler milk and food on first day. Few days later when i came to my hotel room, the refrigerator got unplug, from the morning i left till night all the stuff inside is not frozen, everything need to be throw away. I was so mad so i contacted the lobby about this. It was night around 9:30. The lady said will let her manager know. And i waited no one call me back. So i call down again , finally someone heres me. I said my toodler needs the milk inorder to sleep, now what can i do? Should i go out late night to buy milk? They said will bring me milk and say sorry. I waited almost 40 mins for the milk. After this i thought someone will call me back about what have happen but no follow up and the next day check out, they seem like nothing happen. Everything in the fridge cant be eat or drink, what they do is give me few glass of milk. Should there be a good apologize, should someone follow up us back after. I mean they have the great staff but the costumer service can be much better.

author: andresr61
title: Spectacular hotel overlooking all of Los Angeles
text: I was lucky to have stayed here for a long weekend for work. I was almost sad to leave my room on the 64th floor that overlooked the city! Pros: -Great location in downtown L.A. which offers easy access to other parts of the city. -The design/feel of the hotel spaces and rooms is modern and feels luxurious, not cheesy or if it's trying too hard. Very well done. -The room I got was large for a standard room and the design is perfection. There are plenty of lights, electrical outlets/USB ports and surfaces. The floor to ceiling windows with blackout drapes allow you to open one panel to let in fresh air. The bathroom and closet were both large. The bathroom had separate shower and tub. Product are Le Labo. -The gym on the 7th floor is probably the nicest gym I've been to in a long time. It has friendly staff and the most current equipment. -There is bar in the lobby in addition to one on the rooftop. I recommend being at one of them for both sunset and sunrise. -The staff at the front desk, in the lobby and housekeeping were simply wonderful - could not ask for friendlier or more helpful people. Cons: - If I HAD to pick a con, I would say that the bed was just "meh". The mattress, bedding and pillows didn't meet the high expectations that were set by the amazingness of this hotel.

author: kramsitruc
title: Great (except the elevator system)
text: Upscale, convenient, efficient and friendly service. Spotless, new, luxurious with incredible views. Superb gym, fab pool. The only issue has been mentioned in many reviews. The lift system is just weird! Appreciate their speed, but we stayed on the 57th floor. Going to or from the room from street level you have to go through the lobby on the 70th floor. We didn’t find queueing to be an issue. However, security is a concern. You can get to any floor without a room key! Secondly, is it realistic to expect customers to be happy to travel ‘up’ the hotel in the event of a fire alarm? And thirdly, the issue we rated the single biggest flaw, the gym and pool are on the 7th floor. You have to go through the lobby and past the gorgeous bar of fully dressed people in your gym kit or swimming towel. It’s just a little disconcerting! You need to have a certain level of body confidence to do so!

author: NBDad
title: Sleek business hotel in downtown LA but awful service
text: On a recent business trip to LA I was looking forward to staying at the Intercontinental Hotel atop the new Korea Air tower. While there is much to like about this modern hotel, including a sky lobby on the 70th floor, expansive views of the city and a stylish super cool open air bar on the 73rd floor with firepits, cozy seating and endless televisions, the service was just bad. At check-in around 5:30 p.m., lines of would be guests glumly stood in line waiting for the couple of clerks who were processing them slowly and a concierge just looked on. Note to Intercontinental and other "luxury" brands: customers paying premium rates don't want to stand in line on arrival as if they are checking into a roadside motel for a transaction that should take minutes with their credit cards numbers on the reservations. Hire more desk clerks at peak times and what about outfitting them with ipads so they can walk among the customers so the guests can be comfortable? After 30 minutes I finally arrived at my room on the 37th floor -- and surprise -- the key didn't work! A call to the front desk rang and rang so back up to the lobby I went. The hotel is also underserved with elevators, which are surprisingly slow for such a modern building, so expect to wait. An engineer was sent after another 30 minute wait and I finally got into my room an hour after arrival. The guest rooms are perfectly fine in tones of beige and gray with comfortable beds, adequate lighting and a capacious bathroom with standalone shower. While there were was very little street noise despite close proximity to the freeway, there was a lot of noise room to room, with very audible and loud arguments and crying babies happening in a nearby room. In the morning, another wait in line to check out and to leave my bag while I went to a meeting. In the garage there was a long wait for my checked back and a line of irritated guests trying to drop off bags or get cars but who couldn't get the attention of the apparently only one bellman on duty. Great views and nice finishes are very nice but a hotel rises and falls on service. By all means next time you are in LA take a ride up to the sky lobby to look around or visit the Spire 73 rooftop bar ($25 cover for non hotel guests) but save your money and stay at a place that will make you feel like a valued customer whose time is valuable.

author: 764karync
title: Birds eye view of LA
text: Rising above the city like a giant gateway to the future is the Intercontinental Hotel Downtown Los Angeles. My boyfriend arranged for a birthday weekend here. The entrance seems a little industrial/office like at first blush but that quickly fades away. You exit the valet and walk straight to the elevators and you are swept up on an express ride to the lobby perched on the 70th floor. You see the lobby bar to your left, and straight ahead what looks like a stylized airport terminal check in like you are ready to fly away. This building is one of the tallest west of the Mississippi; that provides perspective on the views. Our room was a corner unit on the 39th floor and to say the sunset and city lights are spectacular is an understatement. The room has state of the are lighting and climate control and the bath and bed were very comfortable and well appointed. We got ready for the nightlife at Spire 73; the rooftop bar on the 73rd floor. To get there you have to take a glass elevator that isn't for those afraid of height. The rooftop has a bar that stretches almost the full length of the deck. Its outfitted with cozy semi private and romantic seating on the perimeter and funky benches with different colors and textures. They did have inventive heaters to keep the crowd warm on chilly nights. The crowd was very eclectic; great for people watching. I would recommend a stay here just for the shear novelty of it.

author: DrSDahlan
title: The best view but.....
text: I stayed at this hotel for a week with my oldest daughter. I was there to set my girl for schooling in LA. This is my first time in this hotel. The view is the best. The price is good. The room is very clean and the food was not bad. The roof top bar is a wow with great service. I enjoyed my stay at this hotel in general. I did talk to 2 managers about my concerns and they both tried to buy me out by waving a fee or give me a coupon. Very silly attitude and I will say it to your fave again. Fix your problems at the spot. Your in room phone service team are not professional and they don’t follow up on orders. Your luggage storing fees must be said up front to the customer before you store it. Small silly things like this will always make your ratings go down. I hope you both care about what I said to your face and what I am saying here. I loved this hotel and will visit my daughter in la again this year. I hope all above problems will not be repeated to me or to other customers. Best regards. Dr SD 2019.

author: BizTraveller168
title: Great hotel and views BUT lousy elevator system
text: Let's start with the positives. Great lobby. Located on the 70th floor of one of the tallest buildings in the US, the view is unbelievable, from sunrise to sunset The rooms are big and bright, bathrooms have both a toilet and bath, and location in downtown LA is near to shopping (7th Street) and entertainment (LA Live and Staples Center) The lobby lounge on the 70th floor also offers a good pour, from champagne to whisky, they don't shortchange you The bad? The elevator system. There's an elevator that takes you from street level to the 70th floor lobby. Then a separate elevator that takes you to your guest room BELOW the lobby. There are many disadvantages to this setup. Imagine my room on the 35th floor. To leave my room, I have to go up to the 70th floor, then take a separate elevator from the 70th to Street access. Imagine having to go through 105 floors instead of 35 All hotels I've stayed at with this kind of setup have a common problem: the elevators from the lobby to the street will be the bottleneck. And as expected, there are lines to these level 1-70 elevators. To make matters worse, the hotel does not have service elevator for luggage from level 1-70. So the bell desk competes for elevator space in a crowded elevator. This oversight in design is simply unforgivable So is the Intercontinental a good hotel? YES! Is it a practical hotel? NO

author: MaryannS60101
title: Ultramodern and ultra aggravating
text: This hotel's style is very modern - cold might be a better description. It was beyond aggravating to have to wait EVERY TIME for the elevators. The lines for the elevators were ridiculous. Our room was on the 59th floor. We had to stand in line to go from the ground floor up to 70 and then walk across the entire lobby to get to the bank of elevators that would go down to 59. Then take the elevator up to 70, stand in line again to get out of the hotel. This is just stupid. Our room was not fully stocked with toiletries when we arrived. The next day, our beds were made and we got toiletries, but no towels and our room was not vacuumed. We asked for more towels and that our room be vacuumed, but that did not happen. We had to call down a second time for towels. The bathroom was not really cleaned very well. This is a 5 star hotel? Not in my book. That being said, the breakfast buffet was wonderful, although some of the food could have been warmer.

author: bl0ndie72
title: Shame about the lifts
text: The Intercontinental Downtown is a stunning hotel without a doubt. It offers far stretching views right cross LA to the beaches at Santa Monica & Huntingdon Beach & to the Hollywood Hills. It was easy to get to from LAX. A short taxi ride. Reception is on the 70th floor. Wherever you go & what ever you do in the hotel, you have to go via floor 70 & change lifts to get to your floor, any of the restaurants, the pool ,the gym etc. To begin with this was fine. But after the first day & several visits to & from the hotel, it becomes a real chore. We were staying at the hotel whilst the Rose Bowl was on. The hotel was so crowded - which meant the lifts were even slower & the queues to catch a lift stretched for miles.... (slight exaggeration). Our room was an executive suite on 53 rd floor. It occupied the left corner of the hotel with views to the coast & also inland. The room was huge, with a big tv, nespresso machine, safe, ironing board, hairdryer & mini bar. There was a seating area with a comfy sofa & arm chairs. The bathroom had a a bathtub, a separate shower, wc & just one sink. The water pressure in the shower was awful. It came out not much more than a dribble. The bed was really comfy & there were low level lights that came on if you got out of bed in the dark. All in all the hotel was lovely & I did enjoy our stay there - but the lift situation really lets it down.

author: ltravel2016
title: Beautiful hotel with major elevator issues
text: The hotel is beautiful. The lobby is on the 70th floor so the views are fabulous! The lobby is a wonderful place to gather. The rooms are a good size and very modern. The hotel has some major flow isssues with the elevators. We often had to wait in line to get up or down. We would have to leave our room 10 minutes early just to make sure we got to the ground floor in time. You have to switch elevator banks to get to the top or bottom. The room design has a flaw too. The bathroom has a glass wall so if someone uses the bathroom and wants the lights on in the middle of the night the other guests in the room get a bright light in their space too. The best part of the hotel is their concierge service! Charles was wonderful! He was able to get us dinner reservations for New Year’s Eve! He also helped us find a church to attend and gave us many great suggestions! Charles was excellent! He helped make our trip special. We wanted to go to the rooftop bar but both nights we tried they had a private party so it was closed to other guests.😐 Lastly we were traveling with a large party and had requested our 4 rooms be close together. They had three of our rooms next together which was great but the other room was on a different floor and with the elevator issues it was a problem. Overall we were happy with our experience but hope they work out their elevator issues soon.

author: 502dukec
title: Comfortable beds, goofy lighting, goofy faucets, troublesome elevators
text: Stayed here for the 2019 Rose Bowl. Room was on 45th floor, and hotel lobby is on 70th floor. To get to our floor we had to either ride to the 31st or the 70th floor, switch elevator banks, then go to the 45th. Ohio State players and coaches were staying on floors near ours and, when they all needed to be at practice or team meetings, every elevator was too packed to get into, so we'd have to wait for the next one, or the one after that. As for the rooms, lights are MOSTLY controlled by a pad at the door or one on the nightstand. There is an All Off/On option or a Mood Lights option that seems close to all on, and not much in-between. You can turn the bathroom lights on with separate switches. Same with bedside reading lights. But none of the other lights can be separately controlled. Faucets are hard to figure out - odd way to turn the water on, and then no way to indicate hot versus cold. Took a good long time for the sink to begin running hot, so it took a while to learn which was hot & which was cold Maid service was frustrating. Once we were left short on towels and twice with NO washclothes. Our beds had sheets over the mattress, but no top sheet. Talking with other guests we leanred that some had top sheets and some didn't. We guessed that there was little to no room checks by supervisors or else there'd have been more consistency. On the positive side, the rooms were very quiet and the beds were quite comfortable

author: Cassiecatt
title: Beautiful Hotel! Management really cares about customer satisfaction
text: I wrote a review about this hotel after a 2 week business stay here recently. There were lots of hiccups for myself and some of my colleagues during the stay, mostly regarding the reception desk and security staff. I got a message from the hotel manager who wanted to make it up to me, and invited me to enjoy the rooftop bar, Spire 73. I decided to take him up on the offer, as I was going to be in the area soon. I was sure glad I did. Everything was beyond excellent. He and the food/beverage director both came to greet me and wanted to ensure they care a lot about their level of service. Everyone there went above and beyond to prove me wrong in my initial impression of the service. The chef even came out to greet us and answer questions about the menu. All of the food we had was amazing, and they even got my husband to try tofu which he normally wouldn't do. The view is of course spectacular, but having that level of service makes it all complete. I may not need to stay in the hotel rooms again soon since I do live in the area, but I will definitely be back to Spire 73 or maybe even try one of their other restaurants. For anyone staying in the rooms, they are really nice and comfortable with great views. The gym, pool and jacuzzi are wonderful. The lobby staff who direct you are very friendly. The elevator situation can take some getting used to, but if you're staying on certain floors like 31-52 I believe, you can take a shortcut elevator to save time. I had some Korean food to-go in the lobby cafe and it was pretty tasty for a quick easy meal!

author: DforDan
title: 5 stars satisfaction
text: Prime location: right next to a small shopping center and 15-20 mins walk to convention center. The view: Is it weird they set up the lobby on 70th floor and then you have to take a different elevator back down to your room level? Yes. But is the view of the entire downtown worth the ride? YES. EVERY SINGLE TIME The Bars and restaurants: Definitely go to the roof top bar on 73rd floor. The food is good and the drink is well made (cue shishito peppers and a good old fashioned). You have a nice crowd and good music, every one is energized there. Dress nicely for the pics to downtown. (Or if you want to be more quiet, then stay at the lobby bar on 70th) Stay fit and enjoy some sun bathing at the gym and the pool on 7th floor. The gym is pretty much on the top tier in terms of the equipment (the machine counts your reps for god sake). The sun does go down early and gets blocked by another building. So go early. The room: Since the hotel just opened last year. All the furniture is in very good shape with no visible signs of tear and wear. I am very happy with the room size, the tub and the magnificent view from my room. Definitely will come back again

author: DesireeG509
title: Modern decor, stunning views, quiet and great sushi
text: From the concrete walls to the wood paneling throughout, this is one of the most contemporary designs I have seen at this price point. You can see the views that include the cityscape, mountains and ocean. Wow! We haven’t heard any of our neighbors so this place must have been built with noise proofing in mind. Sora has incredibly fresh sushi. The spicy tuna rice appetizer is the best I’ve ever had. The issue with the dual elevators is overstated. They run so quickly and there are pleasant hosts that help with the elevators. The greeters in the lobby are so positive, happy and helpful. They give off good vibes. The only drawback was the buffet breakfast. The temperature of the hot foods were lukewarm and therefore average tasting. I’ve eaten at the Intercontinental Hotels in London and San Francisco, and these places were next level. Also, there were multiple people eating food with their hands while they were getting or waiting for food at the buffet. While not the fault of the hotel, maybe there should be a sign? I’d stay here again, but would skip the hotel breakfast buffet.

author: georgesY7264SW
title: Costly and Unnecessary
text: I guess if you're choosing this hotel, money is no object for you. On a business trip, the room rate was $300+taxes. The service throughout the property was excellent, as it should be. My room was very clean and well-stocked. The rooftop bar on the 73rd floor was cool. The gym was huge. All good. Not good: Price. The lobby is on the 70th floor, apparently just for the cool-factor of that concept and thus, a lobby bar with great views. Lame, but it's LA, fine. What's not fine is the ridiculous elevator shuffle, having to go up to the 70th floor to cross into different banks of elevators to get to your room, or vice-versa, down to the ground. The elevators are efficient, but it's an unnecessary design. Dining - the only place to watch the football game one night was at restaurant bar on the 69th floor, where the cheapest meal was a $42 buffet that was a joke. There are no TVs in the lobby bar. The only reasons I'd stay there again are if a stay was booked for business on my behalf, or if someone paid me.

author: Susanlynn53
title: This hotel bills itself as 5 star and is lacking
text: Im trying to think of a positive thing to say about this hotel to start off the review and it is really difficult. The views of LA are great. However, this hotel does not have a business center and it is near the convention center and has business travelers. Very inconvenient. They told me to go to the concierge and they would print out my info, I did send them an email and I did go there and it took 45 minutes for her to come to the desk with my forms. She was very helpful when she did arrive but the wait was extremely inconvientient. It was confusing for some to go to floor 70 for the lobby and then to your floor. Every day at ground level there were crowds trying to get to floor 70 and when you got to the elevators there was a wait and people who were a tad confused about the elevators. I stayed 5 days in this hotel and asked for turn down service when I checked in. I received that service 2 days of my stay. When I called they stated they were so sorry they didn't have any idea why I did not get that service. Big issue if you are a light sleeper - the wall between the bathroom and the bedroom is glass and if you turn on the lights in the bathroom it lights up the bedroom. The beds were average, we got a room with two beds. Mine had a ridge in the middle and i rolled to the right hand side. Lights switches are high tech. This hotel was very crowded and it might have been they were overwhelmed. My friends were in a hotel nearer the Convention Center and they had great service and room. Might have been a better choice.

author: Boscaverde86
title: Great hotel with spectacular views
text: We stayed at the InterContinental for one night during a California trip. We really enjoyed the stay. As soon as you get to the 70th floor lobby, you are presented with a gorgeous view of LA. It's a little weird (and spectacular) to see airplanes flying at your level as they are landing at LAX. Since we are IHG Platinum members, we received an upgrade to a corner room on the 46th floor. It had amazing views from both the bedroom and the bathrooom. The bedroom was reasonably sized, while the bathroom was quite large for downtown LA, and included a separate tub and shower. To no surprise, the room has a minibar, but unfortunately no separate refrigerator where you can actually put any of your own things. The rooftop bar, Spire 73, is amazing. There is no cost to visit the bar if you are a hotel guest. The drinks are a little pricey, but reasonable for LA and for the setting. (Most beers were $9, mixed drinks around $17-18.) It seems to be where the "pretty people" go to hang out. We visited the lobby bar after going to dinner and it was packed and loud at 10pm. We had one drink, and then moved on. The valet parking was convenient. It was a little pricey ($48), but I guess that is to be expected for the location. It's really a great experience.

author: dagoose9500
title: Lobby Lounge has a VIEW
text: A local mentioned to me that this hotel had a unique lobby (and bar) located 70 floors up. I visited this hotel to check out the view. The building is beautiful! The security staff is very cordial. The elevator quickly whisked you to the lobby level. At lobby level guests can check. The bar was my destination. It did not disappoint! Expansive view (with many pricey cocktails to accompany your view). Well worth a visit. At 5 pm there is an outdoor lounge that opens a few floors ip. It is another short ride up. I took a quick view of it. Definitely an ‘A’ List Zone. Might as well have been in Las Vegas! A very cool place to be seen (or impress a date). Enjoy!

author: iaccess
title: Modern luxury hotel with spectacular city views
text: We absolutely enjoyed the modern vibe and luxurious interiors of Intercontinental LA Downtown. There were amazing views of the city from the floor to ceiling windows in our room. The bed was very comfortable and the bathroom was large and luxurious with lots of sink space and a separate shower and bathtub. Lots of power outlets and USB ports for charging devices and centrally controlled lights to quickly turn lights on/off or set some mood lighting. We found the maze of elevators to be a bit confusing, having to transfer multiple times to get to the room, lobby, roof top, parking, etc. Not much the staff can do to change that, but it does take away from the enjoyable stay at the hotel. We only gave the hotel 4 stars because of the less desirable experiences we had: 1. Finding the entrance to the hotel is confusing when you're driving a car. Our GPS took us to the front of the hotel which doesn't have a driveway for cars to enter in. We had to call and were directed to look for the "Parking" sign and use that entrance. We ended up having to drive 2 blocks down to go around because of one way streets 2. Where you drop off your car for valet and where you pick it up are two different locations. Had to ask around where we needed to go to get our car. 3. Service at the Lobby Lounge was very poor on the Friday night that we were there- tables were not wiped and we had to look for someone to get our order. Our food came at a reasonable time, but we saw the couple in the table next to ours leave because they were waiting almost 40 min for their food. Overall, we enjoyed our stay in this luxury hotel - it was very well maintained with modern amenities, had comfortable interiors and good food.

author: Viennetta2017
title: I can't wait to go back again to Intercontinental
text: Unfortunately I spent just one night in this wonderful hotel. Once you get in, you don't want to leave! The room was really confortable and large on 48th floor, the swimming pool was perfect and the rooftop just amazing. The view on Los Angeles is just breathless! I had dinner with a friend at the Lobby Lounge. Very nice. One thing that could be improved consists in the bread. I asked for some bread but the waitress told me they had any. For breakfast there is an amazing choice of sweet and salt things, fresh fruits, gluten free muffins, pancakes, and whatever you like. Regarding the area, Downtown is not nice and safe at all. It is the center of LA but there is nothing to see or to visit. Too dirty. I am a little bit disappointed. I also asked at the reception if they had an adaptor (for my EU pc) available. They didn't have any. I think this is something the hotel could improve since it has 5 stars. Generally speaking, I recommend this hotel for its confort, the friendly people working there and its good atmosphere. Uber is really easy to use in Los Angeles. You can always take this hotel in Downtown and then move to visit LA.

author: ROLANDOMD
title: Business with PLEASURE
text: Steven at the front desk is respectful and provided the services expected. Able to modify the reservations accommodating the evolving changes that we have as clients. Emeli and Israel -was quick in apologizing for the needs for repairs or fix ups in the club suites, without listening to my plea, quick to hand a complimentary drink at the bar, and did not really act on the issues that I have in the club level room floor... which might be minor to some, but not for us...clogged drain and non functional soaker tub( later found out from maintenance Roy that there was a work order already in place ) since day one, as soon as we return at the end of the day and was about to shower at midnight before we go to bed, I was asked by Israel if this should wait in the morning or have someone be sent ASAP, I explained to Israel I would choose ASAP since we don’t sleep until we shower. The maintenance guy arrived at 0730 a.m. and he said that the tub is beyond him and has to be another person. Explained to Emeli and Israel as well- linens appeared clean but stains are all over, housekeepers mane should retire those linens and not return to circulation. The bidet that is not working was reset and fixed after 12 hours. Called for water as part of the amenities ambassador platinum- spoke with Ingrid, twice and one time with Rosa, no water ever arrived. But when I called the answer was “ right away sir “. Jacques - from room service for the welcome savory option was very professional and apologetic for the room not being ready Chef - Carlos Cuevas was excellent in explaining the food he prepped and they were truly delicious The AIR PURIFIER EXCHANGER - was a amazing and you won’t smell the smog and other pollution elements in downtown LOS ANGELES. Compared to my recent stay at the Ritz in downtown LOS ANGELES, where the hotel was covered up with scent diffusers, InterCon was real working air purifiers The the pool, gym and the gym personnel where very polite and knowledgeable. The attendants at the lobby level was very on top of things and were ready to help when I got out of the service limousine on crutches, I was properly and appropriately accompanied to the IHG Ambassador lounge after being recognized. Kessia and Sarah from the lounge were hard working and carries the day with a smile. I just wish that on real busy times at the club lounge the other “big shots” that just walks around and tell the other people what to do, would help instead since we, the guests can see that the staff they are manning were overwhelmed. We do understand that they have their own job descriptions, but there were three actual supervisors telling two other staffers what to do in a very busy afternoon weekend influx of guests. The restaurants were pleasers...

author: Lizardia
title: Wedding visit
text: Went to a wedding with two couples, the father of the bride his pal, my husband and I and found the hotel to be more than we expected! 70th floor lobby was fantastic. What a view. We stayed on the concierge floor our rooms were divine and had free breakfast that was perfect. It's buffet style with great coffee machines for what ever kind of freshly ground coffee you want! They will special make egg orders if you want. They made a scramble eggs with cream cheese version for 4 of us that was melt in your mouth good!!!! Also enough to share with the room! Yummy! The service was over the top all 3 mornings we were there. We stopped for drinks 2 evenings and the bar. The highest in the Western Hemisphere!!!! Gotta go....great service and drinks!!!! We ate a birthday dinner at the restaurant and it was fantastic as was the service and what a view!!!! Gotta go. It's a must!!!! It's a great location!

author: TWonderlust
title: Sky High!
text: A anniversary getaway with my wife to this modern luxury hotel was superb! The required valet parking was no shocker in Downtown LA, rather convenient and quick. We were shocked to find that check-in to the hotel lobby was on the 70th floor. The day was clear and the scenic views spectacular! Granted an early check-in and upgrade to a higher floor corner room suite (Thanks Jessica). The room had updated amenities, plush comfort, and a modern look with the newest technology in hospitality. During our stay, we were able to experience the huge state-of-the-art fitness center, large pool complex, and multiple amazing F&B outlets. The most impressive was our elegant dinner at La Boucherie. We splurged one night and were blown away with the excellent food, exceptional service, and sophisticated atmosphere. After dinner we returned to our room to a complementary chocolate truffle plate and bottle of champagne to continue our celebration. This is the above and beyond attention to detail service Intercontinental hotels has become known for. Awesome memories! Views were stunning throughout. If you are afraid of heights beware, be wary of the elevators which are fast and can cause vertigo (I was told). Overall, this Intercontinental was truly unreal!

author: chivas7113
title: Nice Hotel , good customer service
text: We stayed here from Sunday through Wednesday. Upon arrival their customer service was great. Valet parking helps/ directs you to elevator that takes you to the Sky Lobby on the 70th floor. Front Desk were efficient and helped explain basics of hotel and elevator use (which was not too bad) Elevators from ground floor to 70th was fast and amazingly quiet, I can hardly tell it was moving. Our room was on the 49th floor. From our room we just take elevator to 31st floor then walk around to another set of elevators to take us to ground floor. From there we go to P1 to get our car from valet. (Before getting your car , call ext 7212 and give the last 4 digits of your valet card. When we did that, our car was always ready for us). Valet was $48+ a night with taxes. Breakfast buffet at Dekkadence was $35 for adults and $20 for my 12 yr old and free for my 4 year old. Breakfast was ok. Good views of city while eating. The pool was awesome, if you have kids , it’s a must to go swimming on the 7th floor, our kids loved it. Water is heated and so inviting. Overall a great experience, EVERYONE working there are so helpful when help is needed. We used our Korean Airlines mileage for the rooms , normally it would have been $260/night for the 2 queen bed room we had. (About the mini bar, be careful and don’t move anything or else the sensor might detect it as an item being removed and your credit card will get charged, this happened to me and a call to front desk resolved the issue and after mini bar attendant verified we never used the mini bar, the charge to my card was overturned) Some photos of a informative card about hotel elevators and where amenities are located. Also photos of sky lobby and night shot from 49th floor.

author: DustinKane
title: Views!
text: The Intercontinental is a beautiful hotel with amazing views that span from the mountains to the ocean. Virtually every room has a premium view. The lobby is bright and takes full advantage of the views. It’s a pretty new hotel so everything is pristine and fresh. The rooftop bar is a highlight as well. My room was quite large. In LA I have come to learn that a spacious room is a luxury. I had an amazing view that included the “Hollywood” sign. The bed was a bit on the firm side for my liking but it was not uncomfortable at all. The elevators are a drawback. I didn’t mind that it takes 2 to get to the room. I understand the reasons for that. The problem was that it took sooooo long for the elevators to arrive. Frequently there would be large groups gathering waiting for what seemed like an eternity. The elevators have to span a lot of floors (70 to the top) so it seems like there should be more or they should move quicker

author: KiwiTravellers
title: Top Notch!!
text: We stayed for 4 nights in July 2018, being Ambassador members helped with a room upgrade to the 60th floor. I notice numerous folks complain about the lift system - we thought it was fabulous - cuts out rif raf having a tour around the hotel, also provides a sense of security. The hotel is well located in downtown but unfortunately with the extremely high temperatures while we were in LA this prevented us from walking around the city. We spent our time visiting the Getty Centre, air conditioned!! and another day to a ride to the Beverley Centre, a little disappointing, lacking the WOW factor. Charles the concierge recommended a bistro to eat at while at the Beverley Centre, it was awesome!! The hotel room was spacious, we had 2 large beds, really comfortable especially after a long flight from Venice, Italy. The room was so quiet, clean & really well appointed. The bathroom was fabulous, a nicely tiled shower with clean grouting. I try to chose hotels which are relatively new, therefore presentation is Top Notch! We paid US$60.00 each per day to use the club lounge, this was beneficial, Breakfast, tea & coffee available throughout the day. Also 5pm drinks!! This made sense when we weren't going to be out in the heat finding somewhere to eat & drink. Also had a couple of meals (casual) at the lobby bar, the food was great - just what we expected. We have only one grip - when checking in they take a deposit on the room, unfortunately my husband presentated a cash card, instead of using a Credit Card. The funds are with drawn straight out of the cash card, hence using your travel cash facilities. We are aware of these sort of things but being tired on check in & not having a clear mind ... This is the price you pay, still I am waiting for the refund of the cash, after realising what we had done & presented a credit card to resolve the issue. Yes I would recommend to anyone wanting to visit Downtown LA. Intercontinental stands by its brand.

author: josebelman
title: Worst Hospitality we have experience ! !
text: So.. we stay normally at 4-5 star hotels and we heard about this hotel as the newest hotel in Los Angeles, CA - It is beautiful, but here is the issues we had, these reviews personally have helped me to choose hotels and now I am doing my part to others. We where suppose to check in at 4:00 pm but said it would be approx 30-45 min wait . We. where fine w/ that, it was not big deal. However here is when things started falling apart. The lady called us to tell us our room was ready 45 min later ( Great) We did let them know we wanted a fridge in order to store our small snacks from (Whole Foods) she said, just move the items around the current refrigerator therefore we can make room for our snacks. We did that Exactly ! We get to the room and it was an amazing View however the bathroom was not clean ( We did not complain ) we where told the hotel was at its fullest capacity and I am assuming the cleaning crew was doing their best to clean fast to let us Inside ! - We always tip the cleaning crew when we leave, but this time we did not- The floor had lots of dust, as we walked, the pillows also where not fresh, they smelled- We requested new pillows and took 30 min , in the middle of the night . AS we checked out - we got our invoice as we expected, however they charged us ALL items in the Refrigerator - which it was very evident, they where all there and we never ate. We requested a refund and said they would but now it has been close to 3 weeks and no refund. They gave us the run-around to talk to his person, or this person blah blah blah ! It was a nightmare. Good Luck to everyone , If you do stay learn from my experience and enforce it ! Tip the people.

author: SoCal_Worldtraveller
title: Great hotel, but how much was two hamburgers?
text: Well, let me first say this hotel is beautiful and the views from the 70th floor lobby bar are spectacular. The rooms a modern and are a very nice size – no complaints there. We will return. However, we arrived back to the hotel after all the restaurants were closed and we were starving. We ordered two hamburgers and one beer from room service. It took a little over an hour to arrive, but that was not the issue. We were so hungry that I just signed the bill and handed the guy $15 tip. I go to check out on the TV the next morning and bill was totally confusing with taxes and fees, adds and deducts, etc. So before checking out I went to the check-in lobby to have the billed explained to me. So get this. The room service menu states the hamburgers were $29 each and $7 for the beer. OK, I know its expensive for two burgers, but it was late and it was room service. But wait. The total bill for the two burgers and the single beer, with all the taxes and service charges was $107.32!!!! I’m serious, $107.32 for two burgers and a beer. The hotel is really nice and you will get charged $50/night for valet parking, but I wasn’t expecting to pay over $100 for two burgers. Be forewarned. I like the place and we will be back, but we won’t ever order room service again.

author: Erickg123
title: Something different
text: We stayed here during our family trip to see a couple different museums in the LA area. First off, this is the tallest building west of the Mississippi with the highest floor being a rooftop bar on the 73rd floor. On arrival, the building is something that grabs your attention and when the valet welcomes you, they direct you to the check-in lobby on the 70th floor. Parking Unless we missed the self parking. The only parking available at this property is valet and will run you about $48 per day. On check-in, we traveled up the 70th floor where we received our room assignment and keys. We then had to take a separate elevator down to our room. This proved to be a major inconvenience as anytime we wanted to leave the property we had to travel up to the 70th floor then switch to a separate group of elevators and take one of those down to the ground floor. Everyone seemed confused by this. The room was great. Very clean and used modern technology. The beds and pillows were extremely comfortable and the room was well stocked. The views were amazing from our room and could only imagine they are from every room. The staff was friendly and helpful. A couple of downfalls. There are no vending machines in site but there is a 7-11 down the street. The hot tub could have been a little hotter as everyone commented on this not just us. The thing with having to switch elevators was also a pain but the hotel was great.

author: 92mirandaf
title: Does not meet brands level of service
text: My family and I first stayed in this IHG property last July when it first opened. At that time ther were kinks in the quality of service that I chalked up to the newness of the property, staff and their lack of training. Welp, we recently stayed here again a whole year later and I was even more disappointed. The reception staff dropped the ball from the moment of arrival. My Husband and I are Spire Elite members in the rewards program. I was the second name on the reservation and upon check in (without my husband present) was told my name was not on the reservation (which we confirmed various times with the customer service agent prior to my arrival). Instead of being gracious and trying to figure out what may have gone wrong to mix up the reservation, I was grilled for my personal info and then finally told “as a one time courtesy” I will be added to the very reservation that was suppose to be in place prior to my arrival. Further, I was not informed of the club lounge location, hours or offerings. All Spire Elite members should be advised of this information at time of check in for their personal and business needs. Our room was not ready at time of check in, fine, we went to eat and pass some time. I was told that a text or call would be sent to notify us of its availability. Neither occurred, so after a few of hours we returned with the hope it would be. I found the club lounge (after I asked) I utilized it most morning and afternoons. I found most of the staff members were not welcoming, friendly and their helpfulness lacked with simple requests. Again, the level of service expected of staff attending the lounge for loyalty members did not meet expectation. The saving grace of this hotel property is its beautiful views and aesthetic. However, just these two things can maintain the property. The service does not meet this IHG brand. The staffs addition to this [cool vibe] aesthetic is not a positive contribution but stereotypical LA ‘tude with any simple request or service enacted as if they are doing a favor for the client and not taking into account that clients are consciously paying for minute details and attentions with their stay. We will be looking to other properties outside the brand that offer a higher quality of service in the LA area for our subsequent visits.

author: brendal519
title: Great Location Downtown, perhaps not the best choice with young kids
text: Great location for discovering downtown LA. Right on 7th street. Lots of restaurants and shopping. Across the street from various bus stops and metro station and the visitors center is just downstairs. We travelled with our two kids, age 4 and 8. As others have mentionned, it is a bit annoying having to transit by the 70th floor lobby before going out, going to the pool or going back to the room. There were pool floats in fun shapes that our kids loved. The views are spectacular and the room was very nice and big enough. Service was okay. A bit distant and stiff. We felt as though we were bothering the concierge when we asked for information. If you want friendly service, ask the doorman on Wilshire or the bellhop. I think his name is Jameel, he was friendly wish and seemed to like working there. Wish we had met him at the beginning of our stay. This hotel is about 45min from LAX in traffic.

author: collector
title: Great staff. Beautiful view
text: The view is great and the rooms are wonderful. As a RA we recieved a upgrade to a corner suite. The pool was packed for the 4th of July, but I reserved one of the cabanas at the pool and it was well worth the money. However, I think that one of the keys to a successful hotel especially a IC is the staff. It is up to the management of the hotel to retain those outstanding professional employees. I stayed in this hotel the first month it was opened in 2017. I returned this summer for a 2 night stay. Prior to checking in, I called the hotel and was connected to the club lounge and was so excited that the person answering the phone was a person that had been at the hotel when it opened and she remembered me! I was even more excited when I learned that almost every employee that I got to know during my stay in 2017 was still an employee of the hotel! That says something for the management of this hotel. The staff at the club lounge was the same as a year ago. Several individuals of the food and beverage department were still employed, but had been promoted. This hotel management must be doing things correctly because they are keeping their excellent professional employees. The staff in the club lounge are superb! The management of the IC Downtown LA should commend the professional staff of the club lounge. hope that the management of this IC will recognize these professional individuals. I look forward to a future visit to this hotel, I hope that we will be welcomed by these same employees. I would recommend this hotel to anyone that wants a great experience when visiting Los Angeles.

author: fairmont2016
title: Very good five star hotel but...
text: The hotel itself is wonderful, with the lobby over the roofs of LA (70th floor) it's just stunning arriving there. The interior is stylish and fits perfekt. The room was spacious and clean. I really loved the gym, since it was equipped with everything you need. After dinner we went as well to the rooftop bar at 73rd floor, which was the best thing you could do to take a few cocktails in a nice atmosphere (except for the music, felt like they played a cheap radio channel) So now to the reason I just give the hotel three points: the service. I don't know whether this is an American thing that everyone is just annoyed, unfriendly and definitely don't cares about guests. I always thought Germany was the unfriendliest hospitality nation but since my first time in the US a few years ago I know better now. For this time my opinion didn't change. For a five star hotel there should be done much more concerning guest service and guest experience in that topic. Examples for this stay: unfriendly and rude valet parking, check in without a smile and with the first words: "to early for the check in", bored answers when I had some questions etc. etc. A further point was that the maid service didn't changed the bath amenities. Of course, that point isn't as important as the former one, but still important enough for that kind of hotel category. When I complained about everything to the guy at the reception it didn't seem that any of those information would ever get to the higher management. Because of that I decided to do it here as well. Finally, I would come again, but only because I liked the hotel so much. You should definitely change something with that staff attitude.

author: CoCoCounty
title: One night stay just for the views
text: New building and hotel that opened in the heart of DTLA June 2017. The prices for their basic rooms average over $409 per night and rarely appear on third party sites like hotels.com. When they do appear, it’s usually at last minute, starting at $216, which is why I booked a one night stay to see the views of LA. I selected the Deluxe Room as it’s an end corner room with ceiling to floor windows on two sides. After checking in at the lobby on the 70th floor, I was placed in a room on the 51st floor. The room rate is a bit outrages for the IKEA decor and furniture. Little frills other than a large separate tub. The rooms lack refrigerators and microwaves, even though there is a dedicated fridge for the mini bar..super annoying!! The other annoyance is that when leaving your room or returning to your room, you must always travel all the way to the 70th floor, walk through the lobby and go down a separate elevator. That got old quick! The beds were hard. Hotel security was like secret service walking around everywhere you go. The rooftop bar on the 73rd floor is free to enter for hotel guests and offers the highest views, but the drinks and service are just “ok.” Pool and staffed gym located on the 7th floor. There seemed to be a glitch when checking out on the TV so I called and was told that the only way to check out at the moment would be to visit the lobby or just leave if I didn’t need a receipt. There was a long line in the lobby due to the check-out “glitch.” No outdoor smoking areas anywhere other than leaving the building to walk to the busy street. Overall, the views this hotel offers are amazing. The price for accommodation and service on the other hand is why I would never come back unless it’s on a special as it was this time. Cleaning staff did a wonderful job.

author: AdrianPBaker
title: Oh dear!!
text: I was so looking forward to another stay in an Intercontinental hotel, in preference, I thought, to the normal Marriott or Hilton nonsense. Silly me!!! This is a relatively new hotel and whoever designed it must have had a rather strange sense of humour. To say it is bland would be an understatement. The reception is on the 70th floor!!! Which means that to get to and from your room to anywhere you have to go up to the 70th floor and then another lift to your room. The rooms are decidedly sparse. Mine didn’t even have a desk. The restaurant has a breakfast buffet which costs $38 for a bowl of oatmeal and some fruit.!!!!!! Go back for dinner in the evening and you have a great choice on the buffet if you want to self serve or have the “A la cart” menu which would be at home in the local McDonald’s. The only high point is the gym which I must say is fabulously equipped and massive. With a fabulous steam room and sauna. The staff are very polite and doing there best to appease the rather dreadful mess. All this for $420 per night!!!!!! So, save your money and go to the Marriott, at least your expectations won’t be shattered. Such a shame, Intercontinental used to be so good.

author: SonofBen
title: Elevators make a Great Experience not so Great
text: I recently spent 3 nights in the hotel while attending a Conference. I loved many things in the hotel but not the elevators. The most frustrating thing is that when you are on your floor (say the 50th) and quickly want to exit the hotel, you first need to go up to the 70th floor, change elevator (unit), and only then can you go down to the 1st floor. The best thing in the rooms is the shower; it is a separate unit and you do not have to stand in the bath with a shower curtain sticking to you. The water pressure was also excellent. Beds were also a pleasure to sleep in. As a hotel guest you have full access to the pool, gym and sauna. You also do not have to pay for access to the brilliant open bar on the 73rd floor (that opens daily at 4pm). If you are not a guest of the hotel you have to pay $25 after 8pm. The gym has good equipment and I had a great work out there. Afterwards I hit the pool and the Jacuzzi. Between 6-7pm there were just 2 of us in the pool area on the 7th floor! When it is cold at the bar on the 73rd floor they give you blankets. Or you can go down to the bar on the 70th floor where you also have great views of the city. Someone said that this is the 2nd highest building west of Chicago. Everyone who worked at the hotel was extremely helpful and friendly.

author: log24
title: Comfortable, modern design with aggressive cleaning service
text: Enjoyed a recent two day stay at the Intercontinental in downtown Los Angeles. It was my second stay, with the first occurring not long after the hotel opened. I was struck by the lack of long lines for elevators that I found during my first visit. It appears that not only has the novelty of the Spire 73 open air bar worn off, but now non-guests pay $25 for the privilege of evening access. On the second night I upgraded to a room that included lounge access. Really enjoyed the food and beverage options. Still not as good as most international lounges but complimentary alcoholic beverages are a rarity among US lounges these days. I guess that's why IHG doesn't permit free access to VIP members of the IHG rewards program. Nice touch as the lounge was much less crowded than a typical Marriott or Hilton lounge and the patrons were better behaved. One service miss was the aggressive cleaning personnel on the last day. Was told I would receive a 2 PM late checkout thanks to Platinum status with IHG. The first unwelcome knock and opening of the door by a cleaner, in spite of the do not disturb sign, was at noon. Then a second followed at 1 PM. I also find the hotel's weekend parking fees are expensive compared to other downtown structures. I park elsewhere and walk to the property.

author: Marcelotavares
title: Like a nightmare, my door was open at 1:30 am and a security man with another staff broke into my room!
text: Like a nightmare, my door was open at 1:30 am and a security man with another staff broke into my room! They turned all the lights on and went in the direction of my bed! I was sleeping with my son, and woke up completely confused, without understanding anything! They asked me: "What are you doing here?" and continued "This room was supposed to be vacant!' I told then that I arrived on Tuesday, this happened on Friday, and that I booked that room until Sunday. But they didn't believe me, they continued to ask me a lot of questions. "Did you change your room?" But I was really sleeping in the middle of the night! They continued asking if my son went to the lobby among other dozens of questions, like an interrogation. They also canceled my keys, asked me for my Passport, and spent around 15-20 minutes inside my room, without any call before, they didn't use the bell, I felt completely unsafe. That was the worst experience that I have ever had in a hotel. And as a frequent traveler, that previously booked rooms at other Intercontinental hotels and as an ambassador, I was really disappointed with this bizarre situation. In the morning I went to the front desk to talk with a manager and she told me that on the system was registered that an engineer entered the wrong room to repair a bulb! they registered a false information, this was not what happened! To complete the poor service, the manager said that she apologizes for the inconvenience! When you book a hotel, at first you are paying to have a good night, not to have this kind of nightmare. I paid and didn't get the service that I expected!

author: CJL61
title: LA on business
text: I visit LA around once a month for business, and since this hotel opened around a year ago, I have stayed here several times. The obvious highlights are the newness of the place, incredible views (especially from the rooftop bar on the 73rd floor), etc. While all these things are fine, there are a couple of factors which prevent me from giving 5 stars. One is the fact that when checking in on the 70th floor, you then are sent to your room by one of three elevator banks; this would be fine, except for the fact that when you want to go to street level, you must return to the 70th floor first and then go down. The same holds true just to go to the 7th floor health center. Speaking if the health center, I find it disappointing that in such a nice and new club, there is only one standard stationary bike (also one or two recumbent bikes). A hotel of this caliber should have more choices, and even one or two Peloton bikes. The other slight issue has to do with room service. While I understand that a hotel likes to make money on this, I find it hard to swallow that a $5.00 delivery fee in addition to 22% service fee is added to the check. Of course, the person who delivers also is hoping for a gratuity, so by the time you are done, a $30 light snack/drink has turned into a $50 expense. Again, many hotels charge extra, but this is on the high end. A $12 bowl of oatmeal ended up being over $25 when everything was included, which is really hard to stomach when I can go downstairs (after 2 elevator rides) and get a good bowl at Starbucks for under $5.00. Lastly, the $20 wine by the glass with dinner had a very stingy pour compared to other pours by the glass around town, so that added fuel to the fire. Finally, the complimentary fruit basket upon arrival was removed the next morning after I had left for work, and I hadn't even touched it. The last thing that really got me was a call from room service at 10:30pm, which was 1:30am for me since I was coming from NY. He told me my charge didn't go through, then asked if I was with Korean Air, and when I replied "no" he just hung up without apologizing. As a side note, the hotel must have a deal with Korean Air, because there were flight attendants coming and going at all hours. Overall this is a nice, new, clean hotel with great views, but not much more. Considering I have been here several times and hold an Ambassador membership with IHG, the level of service I receive seems no different than any place else.

author: teresaw353
title: Get A view Of The City At The Lobby Lounge
text: Haven't stayed at this hotel like the President yet. Just wanted to check out the lounge one evening after a hard week's work. The Lobby Lounge is on the 70th floor. What a beautiful view of my city!!! Pretty good service but the drinks are not cheap! $15 for the wine. Interesting décor. Very busy! The restaurant is on the top floor. We went up just to take a look. My co-worker got dizzy so we didn't stay. Found a parking lot across from a mall nearby. Or below the hotel of course. And, right in the middle of town. So, take public transportation! Take a break from shopping or from your L.A. trip and enjoy the view!

author: 506CW
title: Won't be returning
text: I had two stays at this hotel and both were not good. The service leaves much to be desired and the layout is just downright confusing with the crazy elevator system. The hotel lists the address as Wilshire but in fact the main entrance is on 7th St. This means your Uber is likely to leave you at the top of a staircase with your luggage to lug down to the actual entrance and then you must figure out that reception is on the 70th floor. My experience at other hotels with upper floor reception is that you are greeted at the ground floor level, your name is called ahead to reception and they are expecting you when you exit the elevator. Not here. No one is in the entrance lobby greeting guests. The rooms are okay - modern, clean and perfectly fine but nothing to write home about (one deluxe room stay, one hospitality suite stay). The staff is ill-informed. We asked on our first stay about a restaurant for dinner and were directed to the CLOSED sushi restaurant in the hotel. Finally had dinner at the steak house which was nice but very expensive. For breakfast your only option is the buffet. There is a coffee bar on the ground floor that is not run by the hotel. At check in and check out the reception staff seemed bewildered as to how to proceed on both of my visits. The pool area is small but not too crowded, no great shakes but the pricing on the empty cabanas was absurd. Never saw one in use during either stay. We returned for the second visit only because it was the site of a conference we were attending. If given a choice, I will stay at the JW or the Ritz next time or better yet - the Intercontinental in Century City where the staff is unfailingly friendly and welcoming. Bottom line, this location is still experiencing growing pains. I really value the friendliness and competency of staff and this hotel needs work in that area.

author: Out_of_valley
title: High Tech, Great Views
text: The hotel elevator system is a little complicated. First, in order to register, you have to take an elevator to the 70th floor. Then you take an elevator down to your room. If you want to leave the hotel, and your room is on floors 32 to 52, you must take an elevator down to the 31st floor, then walk a short way to another bank of elevators to get to the 1st floor. If your room is above above the 52nd floor, you have to take an elevator to the 70th floor, then another one to the 1st floor, or so I have heard. The lighting system in the room is also complicated. You have to put your room key card in a slot in order to turn on the lights, which increases the risk that you will walk out of the room without it. Plus, it seems like you can turn on all the lights or none, but it is not clear how to turn on only the one or ones you want. The water control in the sink was also a little hard to figure out. One thing that was very low tech but annoying was the bedside clock - instead of a digital clock with a lighted display so if you wake up in the middle of the night, you can see what time it is, they have a small clock with no lights. The views from the rooms and the upper floors are fantastic. If you eat at the restaurant on the 69th floor and have a table by the window, it is jaw-dropping. The decor in the rooms is very nice - clean, modern style with blond wood, etc. The room had a safe, bathrobe and slippers, a long shoehorn, etc. If it weren't for the tech hassles, it would be a great hotel. It is in a great location - right in the heart of downtown and right near the subway and two DASH shuttle bus lines, restaurants etc.

author: lisaw197
title: Outstanding Property!, Not InterContiental Service
text: My husband & I are Ambassador members, upon arrival from San DIego. We were greeted & escorted very warmly to the 70th floor to check in. The front desk Mgr check us in and was very, very rude unprofessional. This was our first time to this property and we only knew what we had read. She did not give us a break down of any of the amenities of the property. The property was so georgous, my husband & I had our own tour after we checked into the room on the 43rd floor. Great room, wonderful view. We dine at the lobby bar - service was horrible as if we were invisible. We waited 45min before someone even ask if we were be8ng help. The restaurant Mgr.also walked by us several time. My husband enjoyed the fitness facility 💯%, the staff in the fitness was very informative. The rooftop & view are amazing. The entire view in the building is outstanding. The staff needs a lot more training w/ InterContinental service and the clientele base. The staff was very much judgmental and the color of your skins make a difference at this location. It’s sad that a beautiful property has service of this level. We will look to re visit again .

author: Socalicouple
title: Look out LA, a new downtown experience has begun!
text: I had three friends in town for Easter weekend, so we decamped to the InterContinental's new shimmering tower in rejuvenating downtown LA. The hotel is new and still getting it's footing, but it already represents and impressive addition to the Los Angeles hotel scene. Upon arrival we dropped our car off at valet, and shot up to the lobby on the 70th floor, and immediately upon stepping out of the hotel you are knocked over by the staggering views of Los Angeles sprawled out in front of you. Floor to ceiling windows surround you. From the ocean to the mountains, it is an awesome sight to behold. Our room was on the 34th floor, so you quickly realize elevators are going to be a key part of the experience. Fortunately the technology seems to have been worked out to avoid what could become a tiresome dance of going up 70 floors to get to the lobby, and down 36 floors to get to your room, and back up 36 floors to get to the lobby, to go down 70 floors to get out of the hotel. The rooms are very modern and spacious. The views from my room were outstanding of some classic old LA buildings sprinkled in with new towers downtown. The cherry on top of all of this technology and service is literally on top at the 73rd floor, which is Spire 73, the highest open air rooftop bar in the western hemisphere. We made it up there after a Dodger game for drinks. With the hotel being new and word still making it out, go now before the crowds show up, because this will be a must see bar scene as the weather warms. I'll review Spire 73 separately, but suffice to say I've never been in a bar like it, and I've been lucky to frequent some great rooftop bars in NYC and Asia. Another gem is the lobby bar on the 70th floor. Great service, small, intimate and great craft drink makers. The views are obviously spectacular. Views aren't enough to make a great hotel, and time will tell how the service, the elevators, and large crowds test this property. That said, the views are truly incredible, and the rest of the elements seem to be on track at this early point in time. This is a place to get in early and enjoy the view!

author: soojik216
title: Beautiful rooms & views but lacking service
text: We spent two nights at the Intercontinental in DTLA. The views are spectacular, and our room was absolutely beautiful. The hotel definitely delivers on those fronts. If you want a luxurious, modern experience in the heart of DTLA, you can definitely get it here. It's also extremely well located and is across the street from the 7th Street/Metro Center Station, which is a hub for the LA metro. We found this to be very convenient when visiting other parts of LA, as we didn't have to deal with parking. Unfortunately, we found the service somewhat lacking. Before our arrival, the staff was very helpful in merging two separate reservations I had into one and ensuring that we'd stay in the same room both nights. However, the service went downhill from there. When we initially arrived, we checked in to our room only to find that the bed had not been made. The duvet was strewn on the floor, and the pillows were all over the room. The rest of the room had been cleaned, so it was somewhat bizarre. We called the front desk right away, and it took them 2 calls over a 30 minute span (they had promised to call back with a solution after the 1st...they never did), for them to finally tell us to go back down to the front desk to get a resolution. Thankfully, the woman who helped check us in also helped find a new room and upgraded us to a suite. Unfortunately, I did not get her name, but I give many props to her! We also experienced a few other minor service mishaps during our stay: (1) the line for the front desk was always very long, (2) our room key stopped working after the first night so we had to go back to the front desk to get this resolved, (3) we called the front desk about a potential charge on the mini bar, and had to call three separate times to get a resolution. Overall, I'd say there were no major deal breakers but many small inconveniences. We did love our room and the hotel's location, but we're not sure if we'll stay here again, given all the other great options in LA.

author: 306lynnw
title: Great first stay!
text: This was our first stay at this Intercontinental. It's lovely, and once we figured out the elevators, we were fine. When you enter the lobby, you take the A bank elevators to the lobby on the 70th floor. To access the guest rooms, you use the C bank elevators. You key in your room number on the key pad in between the elevators. There are no buttons to push in the elevators. It's actually pretty cool. I initially tried to get into my room and didn't think the key card worked. I went back to the lobby, and talked w/Karla. She was so nice, and upgraded us to a corner junior suite. That was so nice of her! It was fabulous, and we thoroughly enjoyed it. I would definitely stay here again; it's close to the Central Market, the Last Bookstore, and numerous restaurants. Since it was raining, we had drinks and apps in the lobby. One small complaint; the chairs are definitely more for looks than comfort. However, with some judicious rearrangements of pillows, I managed to make my chair comfortable. Staff is great, the rooms are beautifully appointed, beds comfortable, and the shower is fantastic. Who could ask for more?

author: Chaig33
title: Bartender 'Patrick' from La Boucherie
text: I will really skip all the miserable & series of below par experiences and interactions I had as soon as I walked in to this Beautiful Property. The Best awesome part of this stay when we went to La Boucherie. WELL??!!. It was empty at 6:10pm on a Saturday evening , We did Not have a reservation BECAUSE when we called the Concierge prior, he said it was all booked for the night. Hmmm.. ok?.. So! We walked in and the Hostess said, theyre booked & we will have to be in a wait - list. We decided to be JUST seated in th3 Bar & we can STILL have the FULL menu. So.. we did! The entire great SERVICE experience from 6:15pm- 8pm >> will be all for Patrick the Bartender & all the team who worked with HIM . All the staffs WHO was all smiles & took time to explain & present our entree , appetizers & cocktail drinks down to desserts was 5 stars!!!!⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐. Yes!!!!, for $350.00 , you didnt CARE to put us on a nice small table. Good job on how u treat your IHG Member. Patrick, if NOT FOR you. THIS Beautiful Million Dollar property is not worth any. Thanks for the wonderful experience!! I wish u more and more loyal guests.

author: samsI2779EF
title: Incredible Views and Hospitality
text: I booked this as an Ambassador Platinum reward night. They reward desk booked the wrong night so contacted the hotel directly , n was resolved quickly and professionally . Upon checking the line was long but moved rapidly . FYI the lobby is located on the 70th floor with Breath taking 360* views and mountains to ocean . I was greeted as a Platinum ambassador and advised they had given me a complimentary upgrade , even though on a reward night , to an executive corner suite on 47th floor . The suite was approx 600 sq ft 60m2 and boosted views of the Hollywood hills , BHills, LAX and downtown as well as Ocean . The amenities were fantastic and frette linens . The brunch buffet is well worth the $35/person with endless food and views . Everything went well and the service 5 Star . The only draw back to this hotel is the elevators. You must go through the 70th floor lobby for everything which can be annoying with long reception lines and the main bar . But the elevators are fast and reliable ! The front desk is fast and friendly as well as the staff at the breakfast buffet. The pool is excellent and great hang out spots all over the hotel . Truly one of the best IcH in the system .

author: 5glamtravelers
title: Stay at a different hotel
text: We went to an LA Clippers game and this hotel seemed to be a reasonable nearby option (although not quite walking distance). For a family of 5 (3 kids under age 9), we booked two connecting rooms through hotels.com. We confirmed the connecting rooms by calling the hotel the day before which also took close to 30 minutes because this hotel is busy and clearly understaffed. At check-in, at 10:00 pm with 3 kids asleep on the couch in the busy lounge area, we were told there were no connecting rooms. The option? An upgrade to a room with only 1 king bed and several roll aways, or two rooms down the hall from each other. And, the hotel staff said they couldn't refund the second room. It's our problem to figure it out. The main problem with this hotel is the complete lack of customer service and the we just don't care attitude. We asked for a supervisor and he didn't even make eye contact. Just pointed to the computer screen and told his staff that we could take it or leave it. In the future, we will never stay here. The icing on the cake? When we were told on the phone last night by a second manager that it is not the hotel's responsibility to provide connecting rooms to families with minor children. Take note families with young kids like us, this hotel doesn't care if you have to split your family and stay down the hall from each other. It's not their problem. Hmmm...there are too many wonderful hotels in Los Angeles to ever stay here again. Take note families.

author: Curiosity665683
title: The Most Spectacular Hotel I’ve ever Stayed in
text: I stayed at the InterContinental Downtown Los Angeles on 28th January - it was my first visit to L.A. and it definitely won’t be my last. You enter, where you’d expect the lobby to be but it’s in fact on the 70th floor, so you then get into the lifts, where you’re sent up to the 70th floor. The views from the lobby are breathtaking. My check in experience was fabulous with the hotel staff member politely enquiring about my stay in L.A. and giving me complimentary drinks vouchers! I was allocated a beautiful room on the 51st floor, looking out upon the whole of L.A. - I didn’t need to go to the Griffith Observatory! The beds were so comfy, helping me get over my jet lag and the rooms are extremely modern. The bathroom had a separate shower unit and the hugest bath, which I took advantage of using both. I went to the rooftop bar, using my complimentary vouchers and again the views were breathtaking - I was informed it was the tallest open top bar in the Western Hemisphere. The bar had an amazing atmosphere, the staff were again lovely and the drinks selection was fantastic. I woke up the next day, with the Hollywood Hills to my right, astonished by how incredible my room was. I used the hotel’s gym the next day, where you’re working out, surrounded by Los Angeles’ downtown skyscrapers. The equipment again was pristine and brand new and there were complimentary towels and fruit infused water. There were a variety of channels to watch on the built in screens on the exercise machines such as: Netflix and overall it was an extremely pleasant work out. I wish my stay could have been longer but I would without a doubt stay here again, if I were to return to L.A. The best hotel I’ve ever stayed in! Thank you so much for such a fabulous stay, I can’t wait to come back!

author: redeyetraveller
title: Modern, comfortable rooms in Los Angeles' tallest building
text: For our car-free weekend in Los Angeles, we decided to spent the night at the 73-story Intercontinental Los Angeles and could not have been happier with our stay. We found service to be friendly, the room to be modern and comfortable, and the views from the lobby exceptional. Moreover, located at the corner of 7th and Figueroa, the hotel is in easy walking distance to most downtown locations and just across the street from the downtown transit center with connections to the metro and recently opened Expo line to Santa Monica. A Lyft to LAX on Sunday afternoon took about 35 minutes and cost just $30, while the Expo line to Santa Monica took about 50 minutes and just $1.75. Check-in takes place on the 70th floor lobby (the Wilshire Center is currently the tallest building on the west coast and the 10th tallest in the US) and was quick and efficient. We were pleased to have been upgraded from a superior room to an executive room, which primarily offered a corner view with extra space to relax. Rooms are located starting from the 31st floor, meaning that from the lobby you will need to take a second set of elevators down to your room.
