Our 34th floor room offered impressive views over DTLA and almost everything you could need – large, comfortable bed, good workspace, large TV, and a comfortable bathroom with both shower and bath (toiletries were from Agraria in San Francisco). The room also featured a chaise and small table, as well as plenty of sunlight from windows on two sides. The only minor downsides to the room was the automatic minibar (meaning there was no room to store the cake we purchased from Bottega Louie), lower end Keurig coffee maker, and no electronic control over the curtains. With the large amount of windows in the room, it was some what awkward having to go behind the long work desk to manually open and close the shades. While we didn't have breakfast at the hotel, we did enjoy drinks at the lobby lounge over sunset. Drinks were reasonably priced for a hotel bar (approx. $9 for beer, $14 for wine, $17 for cocktails) and we found service to be friendly and quick. For those looking for a more trendy destination, the hotel also has a 73rd floor SkyBar. Guests of the hotel have waived cover charge, although semi-formal attire is needed. The hotel also offers a very large and modern fitness center on the 7th floor. Having stayed at many hotels, this was probably the best fitness center I'd come across, especially as equipment was all brand new. There is also an outdoor pool, although from the looks of it, it is less a lap pool and more a destination to relax at. All in all, we were very pleased with our stay and would definitely consider returning.

author: JamesE339
title: I wanted to give this hotel 5 stars, but.....
text: I was so excited to enter this hotel. It makes a great FIRST impression. I booked a standard room for my first visit, and was told i was upgraded as an ambassador member. Apparently, I was upgraded to the smallest room. Several friends, who had booked at the same time...at the same rate...had MUCH larger rooms. Oh well.... I also booked the Club rate. The Club was large, and had a variety of offerings. The staff was great but the food offerings were underwhelming. (OK, the desserts were old, and stale!). Sorry....but this was true both days! On a positive note, the staff was amazing. The building has a great health club. I was excited to see it. Unfortunately, the design of the hotel dictates that you must go in one elevator to the lobby, TRANSFER across the lobby to another elevator to get to the health club. So....working out in the evening, you must walk 'sweaty' and in 'work out' gear through a trendy lobby area/bar FILLED with 'A List' or wannabe patrons while looking like a bum. HATED THAT! I didn't go to the health club the next day.... Room was comfortable, clean....nothing extraordinary. I left with a very average review of what should be an amazing new Intercontinental property....

author: W5450ZYjuliec
title: Modern, chic, indulging experience (except for housekeeping)
text: I came here for to check out Universal Studios while taking advantage of my Ambassador free night. We got upgraded to a corner suit and our bathroom had a view of Hollywood hill. We checked out the gorgeous open bar Friday night then indulged our welcome drinks at the lobby lounge. We were there before 9 so it wasn't crazy busy. The only downside is that the hostess does not seat you (I think they are just placed to greet you) so the servers don't know that you are a new guest and you need to flag their attention to get any service. As for the hotel, I do plan to send a formal review. I had the worst housekeeping experience ever. I accidentally left the privacy sign up and when I came back, my room was not made. I asked for the room to be made, scheduled a time and made sure I left a decent tip as it was already past 8:30pm. When I returned I was disappointed to find: no fresh towels, old towels still in the tub, bathroom sink not wiped down, bathroom amenities not replenished, coffee not replenished, my coffee mugs left in the hallway and no clean replacements, floor not vacuumed (it seems new debris was left behind). Only the bed was made. And there was a random empty hairdryer bag left on the desk. I'd like to think that the room was not cleaned by the standard crew due to the odd hour, but I think a SOP or checklist count have prevented this mishap. All in all, I still enjoyed my stay. I will come back and will look the other way for housekeeping. I do expect some corrective actions so other guesses would not have to endure this.

author: Gsl_9292013
title: High-Rise High-tech Hotel
text: Stayed here for 4 nights last December since hubby has work in LA. This is an Ultra modern hotel with the lobby located on the 70F. The view from the lobby is very impressive. We stayed at the 35F where there is also a very good view since they have floor to ceiling windows and like semi corner room view. The room is big and spacious. Everything is operated with the touch of the button i.e just press the option by the door for housekeeping or privacy same thing with the lights. The bathroom is also big. I love that they have a separate shower and a full size tub ! The only thing is there is no microwave and the refrigerator is full of their drinks and snacks but there is a coffee maker which is replenished daily. The location is perfect since its walking distance to Staples center and places to eat and shop. The only thing is the elevator can get confusing since you have to transfer as there are two sets of elevators. Just make sure to remember the instructions by the receptionist and you'll be fine. Parking is valet only at $45/night if i remember right or you can use the parking structures close by. Service at the reception and housekeeping was also good. We would definitely book here again the next time we're in LA.

author: Goodfoodperson
title: Not the warmest hotel I have ever stayed at!
text: I have stated at several Intercontinental hotels in Europe and understand they set up the hotels to cater to Americans who were used to the comforts of home that the European hotels did not. This Intercontinental in LA is both cool and rather strange. It is located in the tallest building west of Chicago so the Concierge told me. That is kind of neat and the view is spectacular. What is weird is the lobby is on the 70th Floor and you check in through the garage and almost have to let the bellman take your bags to your room. Their is a really neat open air bar on the 73rd floor. Also the lobby has these lighted chains hanging down that look art deco but again the Concierge told me they are really chains that hold the building together in case of an earth quake and can stretch up to 19 feet. What's also strange is that the elevator from the ground floor only takes you to the lobby on the 70th and then you have to take different banks of elevators down to your room. I went with a corner sweet for a little more money and the view was great but the room was high tech, grey/white color scheme, a little cold for my taste and not inviting. The Concierge was very friendly and informative. I wanted to print a document and although the hotel has been open for over 6 months I was told the business center is still not open and held up the city of LA. When I went to check in there was a rain storm and the hotel lost its connection and they asked me to wait. They did give me a free drink coupon for the lobby bar but after 10 hours working I was in no mood to sit in the lobby and cool my heels with a drink and wanted to go to my room and get a shower, change clothes and go get some dinner. Luckily the wait time was fairly short less than 10 minutes and the desk staff was very friendly. Morton's steak house is literally across the street. The food court across the street by Morton's has some great lunch selections. It was fairly cool when I stayed and I went to the open air bar on the 73rd floor and it was cold despite the heaters and fire pits. I ended up taking my glass of wine back to my room although I was offered a blanket. I doubt I would go back but if your into the high tech modern design and chic this would be a great place. Don't take the kids as this seems to have young business travelers primarily.

author: roncW2332AY
title: Staying in downtown LA
text: Downtown Los Angeles used to be a no go zone in LA but its changing and is fast becoming hip and interesting. IT hasn't been completely gentrified so its an interesting electric mix of what was and what is to come. The hotel is (technically) the tallest building in LA. It's new and hence very modern and the rooms, though not huge, feel large because of the floor to ceiling glass windows and jaw dropping views. This alone makes it worth a stay... to say nothing of the "roof" bar. The rooms have everything you can want. Great towels, linen, beds and shower, light and desk space. A few reviews carry on about the need to travel to the 70th floor to the "lobby check in" and then travel down to your floor somewhere between 35 and, I presume, 69. Is this really a problem? If you can operate a smartphone you should be able to get your head around this it's not too difficult. The check in process was less than friendly. I thought I had prepaid (which it turned out I hadn't) and was told that quite assertively. I was given no information about facilities or anything other that where the elevators to my room were to be found. I wasn't asked if I wanted to know anything except if I wanted my status rewards as a drink or points. Nothing too serious about all of this but not a welcoming experience. I suspect it will be sorted with more training over time. Overall a great new "business" hotel (i.e. It's not a quaint boutique hotel) but you will get a great nights sleep and wake up to an unbelievable view in a fascinating and exciting go to part of LA.

author: MVaughan99
title: Amazing treat of a luxury hotel!
text: We happened to try out this brand-new hotel over Christmas Eve, and so glad we did! It was deluxe and sumptuous throughout. Though some services and features were closed for this specific holiday time (like Spire73) the rest of the hotel was busy and exciting and gorgeous. The lobby on the 70th (accessed by lightning-speed elevators) is marvelous - though the lobby lounge area was very busy (a bit of a surprise for during Christmas!) our check-in was quick and personable and unrushed. It is a bit odd and clunky to have to then take a different elevator to get to one's room - especially once checked in and when coming and going from the hotel, via the lobby each time and therefore having to take two elevators - nevertheless it proved to be no problem, and certainly no huge delay since all the elevators are remarkably quick. Interesting/new manner of using the elevators, where one chooses your floor on a general keypad first and then you are directed to which elevator to take. we read a sign in one elevator that indicated as a warning that if one does not choose their chosen floor first before getting in a random elevator then you could get stuck! We never fell into this circumstance, but were also unwilling to try too. Our room was stunningly huge and plush, with a huge bathroom too. Fun concept to have a half-frosted window from bathroom to the rest of the room, as a hint/tease! The views, from our room or from the lobby or from elsewhere around the hotel, are superb and panoramic over the whole city. As mentioned, a number of venues and services were not available to us over Christmas, but we were not at all disappointed in this or by any aspect of the hotel. It is difficult to imagine what might have caused some of the negative reviews of this hotel on TripAdvisor - unless it was from when the hotel first opened (back in the summer) and perhaps some kinks needed to be worked out then? Our stay and the service was terrific and top-notch. One extra novelty and recommendation: Make sure (gents, anyway) to use the Men's Restroom off the lobby near the elevator to Spire73 - best, and most interesting, view from any bathroom anywhere!! :-) It was indeed a thrill to stay at this hotel. Only for one night, and wish it were longer - but we'll be back. And once again I can't say enough about the superb and attentive service as well. Gorgeous property and for a luxury hotel, really quite affordable as well. An outstanding value!

author: cz75guy
title: Bizarre logistics
text: When you arrive by car at the listed address, 900 Wilshire Blvd., you are on the wrong side of the building... Just a set of double doors with the address and the word "Hotel" above the door. Fortunately, a staff member inside the doors told me the checkin area was on 7th Street. Do not look for the usual semi-circle where you are met by the bell staff and valet. You appear to be driving into a loading dock area. Reception is interesting as well. You take an express elevator to the 70th floor, which is the lobby, where you check in. Beautiful views, excellent service. You the take a different elevator bank to floor where your room is located, which was the 49th in our case. Very new, modern and fresh, with a comfortable bed and a very nice bathroom. Good wifi too. Back to the logistics. In order to leave the hotel, you had to take the elevator back to the 70th floor lobby, switch elevator banks and go down to the ground floor. That's if you are walking. If you need your car, you must take another elevator bank, stairs, or escalator down one more floor to the valet pickup area. All of this was confusing enough that the hotel has associates stationed all over pointing you in the right direction. It was really a distraction to an otherwise excellent property. We didn't try any of the onsite restaurants or bars as we had commitments outside the hotel.

author: M7758LRolgam
title: Beautiful hotel with great staff
text: Amazing new hotel with incredible views and moderately priced. Rooms are very spacious, with modern decor. Everything is brand new, and it's a pleasure to be in the room and using hotel facilities. Staff is very friendly and accommodating. The lobby is beautiful; nice furniture, a hip bar that also serves food, and did I mention the views? You can see up to the coast; Hollywood sign is right there; perfect location for pics and selfies. The outside bar on 73rd floor is also excellent, although seats by the windows get filled up rather quickly. Couple of minor annoyances that still do not diminish the fact that the hotel is excellent: 1. Lobby on 70th floor, and all transfers between your room and outside have to go through that. Not a huge deal, but if you are staying for a few days, this becomes a journey you have to do several times. 2. Dekkadence buffet is average; the high price tag of $65 per person is because they serve king crab legs and other seafood in all-you-can-eat style. Other food is just OK. Unless you going for that, then not worth it. 3. There was a rather unpleasant disturbance on our floor at 5am, and it took security almost an hour to handle it. Not hotel's fault that it took place, but would've hoped that hotel security is a top priority nowadays, and this could've been handled quicker. However, hotel staff was more than accommodating, and covered our dinner and parking for the inconvenience. Special thanks to David, Jean Baptiste, Patrick, and Adriana for their hospitable approach and generosity. Would love to come back to this hotel when in LA, and would definitely recommend to anyone staying in downtown.

author: love2travel79
title: Amazing View but underwhelming experience
text: My husband and kids (ages 7 and 9) stayed at this new hotel during the Holiday Season as a staycation. I have to rate this hotel a 4 stars because I did expect EVERYTHING to be perfect, given its hype….and it was not. First the positive, the views ARE unbelievable! From any window the views are capturing. The clean lines and decor made the space feel very upscale and serene. The room size is very comfortable, with plush robes and a large soaking tub. However, having the lobby in the 70th floor is a bit of a hassle. You have to take two elevators to your room. First up to the lobby, switch elevators and then down to your room. Second, the room lights operate with the room key being inserted in a slot by the entrance. But this too can be a hassle. One night I was the only person who remained in the room while taking a shower, when my husband and kids stepped out of the room and took the key, the lights turned off, leaving me to get out quickly and scrambled to find the second key! Finally, breakfast room service too over 1 hr for delivery without explanation. These are all small things that can be overlooked, but having a 5 star view, I expected a 5 star experience. Overall, I would recommend this hotel and return, but lower my expectations.

author: silverm0623
title: Pleasant Improvement
text: Stayed here in July after they opened so this is a sort of follow-up review. Overall, definite improvement and operations seem to have improved greatly. Was upgraded at check-in to a corner room per Ambassador benefit which was quite nice. They also include little maps in the key card holder which is nice. Staff was plentiful all over the property if you had questions or were lost. Corner room was great but definitely missed the huge suite I had last time. Turn down service was very nice and they give you water and ice. Ambassador welcome amenity was great with a huge bottle of Evian, fruit, and chocolates. You are also allowed to help yourself to the Evian water in the min fridge as a benefit which was an awesome perk. Kinda wish they had two bathrobes and not just one but that was the only negative of the room. Greatest part is that the gym was recently finished and was likely the nicest gym I’ve ever been to in a hotel. A few things like the locker room are still being finished but the equipment was the most high-tech I’ve ever seen. Watching Netflix on the treadmill screen? Yes please! The ladies staffing the gym were amazingly nice and professional and asked if we had any feedback of the gym as we left. A+++ Was given drink coupons at check-in and we used them at the rooftop bar which was amazing, although the windows looking out up there are truly getting quite filthy to be honest. At checkout the lovely agent Tunisia proactively removed all charges that were complimentary per my Ambassador benefits which was nice since I hate having to fight for things to be removed so A+ on that. Random parking charge had shown up on my bill but she quickly removed it when I explained it was definitely a mistake. Will definitely be back

author: 167ianj
title: Delayed Luggage, Horrible Security Check at Lobby, Poor Feedback Management
text: 1. we checked in at roughly 20:40, and then we went out for dinner. However, we hadn’t received our luggage at 23:30 when we returned, until we gave a call to concierge. It seemed like there must be some miscommunication. 2. approximately 23:00 when we waited for the elevator from 70th floor to 73rd floor, we encountered a drunken gentleman in blue shirts and his friend. We got frightened due to his language assault on us and punched on window. And he even made threatening gesture to us and approached us, when he noticed that we tried to leave him alone. At the end, a concierge lady asked him to leave with her. This accident really ruined our mood to enjoy our drinks on 73th floor, and I thought such a modern and luxurious hotel bar should improve the security check at the lobby. 3. Tomorrow the front desk representative sent an email to promise a talk with us "at our convenience". However, she didn't reply the email, which we stated we want to meet her when checked out. Then when we checked out, she didn't show up. Even when we asked to see her, the front desk staff replied that, she is not available to talk at that time, so we should come back later. Thus, we stayed in LA downtown to wait her for 2 more hours to talk to her. We finally had a chance to talk to her, and she simply apologized like a robot, and offered a 10% discount for next time. She didn't talk about the reason of luggage delay, the personal safety incidence, and the reason we have to WAIT HER 2 HOURS to get an explanation. At that moment, I believed the best compensation is to ask back for my IHG rewards points.

author: SimoneM764
title: nice but many things to fix
text: The hotel is very nice, it doesn't have very big suites, the biggest is about 85mq, I got a King Executive room 60mq that was very pleasant. As Spire Ambassador member I have tried to early check in at 12 but the room was not available, that's ok but unfortunately also at 2pm the room was not ready, I finally got it at 3pm with still the minibar almost empty and no complimentary waters. I got a water from the minibar that supposed to be free as ambassador or at least to cover the absence of complimentary waters but I have been charged for it. I had lunch there at the bar, I had Prime New York Strip that was delicious! I spent some time at the Spire Bar with 2 friends we got 3 Old Fashioned, they were the most horrible of my life we talked about that with the manager and we had our drinks changed with 3 different ones that were horrible too. We couldn't drink them and we left them almost full and nobody came to ask us how were our new drinks, it was embarrassing for me to do that because the bartenders and the staff are very friendly and cool and the all ambience is very nice but really the quality of the drinks are embarrassing, that's a pity. We moved down to the bar at 70th floor and we got 3more drinks that were good. In general I could say I had good time, the vibes are very good and the staff is amazing but it's a pity that we cannot have a decent drink at the Spire that is the reason why I opted to stay at this IC. They day after I had some major inconvents. I communicated to them my need to use the late check out at 4pm. At 12pm the housekeeper knocked my door and woke me up, asking me the time of check out and I told me I requested late check-out, at 14pm they came back and asked me again, and I specified I want to check out at 4pm. Around 2.20pm I went to have lunch and when I got back on my room the card was not working, so I came back to the 70th floor and unfortunately I had to queue almost 25min to get my card reactivated. There were only 2people at the counter nobody at the Elite Benefits Counter and no Ambassador spot. This was very annoyed but the big surprised was that when I asked to reactivate my card, they told me the card was deactivated automatically after 12.00 because is the check-out time. I explained for the fourth time that as Ambassador member I decided to use my late check out benefit!! The staff is very friendly despite some misunderstanding and embarrassing situation I have felt welcome. there are many things to fix, I'll probably be back and give it a second chance

author: NilsLDK
title: One of the best City hotels I ever have been at
text: We stayed at Intercontinental Downtown LA for 2 night. The hotel is brand new, and it is located downtown LA, where you can find great bars and restaurants. Downtown you can also find some shopping. The hotels is located next to the metro, why you easily can go to places such as Hollywood and Santa Monica. The check in was fast and the staff was really kind. The lobby is located at 70th floor, where you have a great view at the city. We checked in early and the room was ready. We got an executive room at the 57th floor, where we also had a great view at Hollywood and Beverly Hills. The room was huge, if I compare the I compare with other city hotels. The room was clean and WiFi worked perfect. We had access to the club lounge - one of the best I have been at. The service was great, the food was amazing and they served great cocktails. Also the breakfast in lounge was one of the best, I have got in a lounge. The hotel also has a great clean pool area at the 7th floor with full bar service. 73th you will find the roof top bar, but it is crowded. This hotel os one of the best city hotels, I have ever been at - we will be back. The only negative thing about the hotels is the elevators. There is often a huge line, where you need to wait at least 10 min.

author: isaacmiz
title: Best hotel experience I had in the U.S.
text: I enjoyed every minute of my 3-night stay at the new Intercontinental Downtown. My suite on the 65th floor (got an upgrade because my room was not ready) was simply unbelievable. What else can you ask for when surrounded with such amazing L.A. views? It was quiet, beautifully decorated and had a comfy king-size bed. On the low side, it was challenging to enjoy a hot bath, as the water were cold most of the time (perhaps it has to do with the high floor?). No issues with the shower though. Service was fantastic - from reception to the elevator assistants (yes, they have it there because the whole thing can be a bit confusing at the beginning). I would like to mention Michael the concierge as a fine example for hospitality service at its best. Michael built a walking itinerary in downtown L.A. for me that was very fun to do, and also helped me getting a ticket to The Broad Museum (highly recommended). He is an asset to this hotel and to the tourism industry in general. The pool is lovely, with a nice bar that serves some good cocktails. The gym will be open soon (I was told), but meanwhile they have an agreement with the nearby branch of Gold's Gym, which I found to be very convenient. Also nearby are a few restaurants and some stores (including Zara and Target). Overall, good location to explore DTLA and a wonderful hotel to enjoy.

author: jco32552
title: Good choice for downtown LA
text: I just spent three nights at the Intercontinental. The views from the 70th floor lobby and my 55th floor room were spectacular. The room was small, but thoughtfully appointed with a very comfortable platform bed and good bathroom facilities. It's brand new, which of course goes far. They must have state of the art windows because there was no noise from outside at all. One logistical downside is the elevator configuration. Lobby is on 70, guest rooms below accessible by various elevator banks. To go downstairs from my guest room I had to go up to the lobby, and then down a different bank. In the morning, I had to wait on a line to get onto the elevator to go down; I found this a bit claustrophobic. Worst choice made by the hotel was restricting access to the roof bar. There is a 73rd floor open air bar that is pretty spectacular. Unlike the bar in the lobby, it is spacious with a long bar. Unfortunately, the hotel is treating it like it's a nightclub; what I mean by that is that I had to wait 20 minutes to be permitted upstairs to join my friends (I was alone), while a line of ~35 hotel guests built up behind me. Non-guests were sent downstairs to the second floor to wait on another line. The guard said that the bar was "at capacity", but this was not true (as the friends I was texting with confirmed). When I got upstairs, the bar was about half capacity with most seating at the bar and in the lounge space unoccupied. I feel that it is rude to create false demand as if we were tweens waiting on a sidewalk, with paying hotel guests who are trying to go to their hotel's bar. It's really not a very nice way to treat hotel guests. When I got back downstairs from the half empty bar maybe 45 minutes later, the guard had made people wait again, and there was a long line of people who were hotel guests waiting in the lobby. Shortsighted, thoughtless and frankly not very welcoming.

author: lalaearmuffs
title: Amazing views, but something felt off...
text: I just returned from a 2-night stay at this new hotel. The 70th floor lobby is indeed very cool and I spent as much time as possible enjoying that one-of-a-kind view. My room on the 46th floor was spacious. But something about the experience felt off. Some of the amenities within the room were not user friendly. The in-room coffee was poor and I'm pretty sure that the creamer was expired. Nonetheless, I was disappointed that it was not restocked the next day. I was not impressed with the service at various establishments: pool side, the restaurant where they serve brunch, the spire bar on the roof. I found the service plainly rude. The security was also lacking- a lot of people are in and out of that building, especially due to the rooftop bar. Yet there is no validation required to access the hotel room floors. There are many greeters on the premises, but they did not help me feel any safer. In addition, various parts of the hotel are still under construction, including the gym. The alternative was to use the Gold's Gym across the street. I did not end up partaking, but this is definitely an inconvenience, especially when you consider how difficult it is to get to/from your room/to the lobby/downstairs (basically, you can't leave the building until you go up to the lobby and then you take another set of elevators down to the first floor of the building).

author: SapphireButterfly
title: It's the little things that make the difference - excellent event hotel
text: I went to a banquet at this hotel attended by 500 people and this review is based solely on the evening. Valet upon arrival was fast and efficient, no issues there. The dinner menu was surprisingly tasty for a 500 people event. It was as good as if I were having dinner at an upscale restaurant downtown. I cleaned my plate completely, it was that good. The only problem was I had no room for dessert, so at the end of the banquet program, I asked the server for my table, Marcelo M. for a take-out box to take the dessert home with me, honestly I was kind of embarrassed... But the dessert looked so good, I wasn't about to let it go to waste. This is an unusual request and hassle so I was expecting either a no, or a long wait for it. And of course I was expecting just an empty box to pack my own. Shout-out to Marcelo M. - THANK YOU, you're amazing! Much to my delight, my take-out box, complete with the banquets choice dessert already beautifully packed inside it, came within minutes of the request. I could not tell you how surprised and happy I was to see this level of service for a mere banquet guest. And I wasn't even staying at this hotel! Down at the valet for a 500 people event I was expecting a zoo and long wait. Again, I don't know how the valet service retrieve cars so quickly, my car came within 5 minutes. I literally only had time to put my dessert down on the bench, take a quick pic for my friends and there was my car! Needless to say, my first impression for this hotel is excellent and I will definitely keep it in mind for any events my friends and I may be hosting in the future.

author: kgoil
title: The New Intercontinental Downtown is a Five Star Hotel
text: We stayed at the New Intercontinental Hotel in Downtown Los Angeles from September 15-17. The InterContinental was recommended by our middle son who is a senior at USC and a Medical Assistant on the USC Football team. We were impressed by the Hotel and the quality of service. Room 3805 had great views as does every other room in the hotel. The room was very clean, the bed was very comfortable and the bathroom was awesome. The only complaint would be the sink drain was partially clogged. The Lobby is on the 70th floor which sets the tone for the entire Hotel because of the incredible views of Los Angeles. We arrived in LA from Denver at 8am. We had breakfast/lunch at the lobby restaurant which was excellent. We were able to check into our room at 9 am. We have never been able to check in to a hotel that early. A young lady named Angel checked us in and she was wonderful. Very pleasant and personable. We tried to get a reservation in La Boucherie but were not able to because of its popularity. The Intercontinental has excellent security 24 hours per day. They do not have a fitness center as of now but we were directed to Golds Gym across the street. The pool area is incredible. It is very neat and clean as well as having great service. I would recommend the Intercontinental Downtown Los Angeles to anyone looking for an excellent hotel at a very reasonable price in comparison to other Los Angeles area hotels.

author: DavidY601
title: Fantastic hotel in great location...but lifts are a pain!
text: Stayed for one night at the recently opened Intercontinental Los Angeles. As a regular business traveller I look for 5 things - a clean room, comfortable bed, good shower, decent WiFi and good location. This hotel scores strongly on 3 out of 5. It’s a very modern hotel with contemporary decor - on the positive side, it’s in a great downtown location, the rooms are clean and spacious and the beds are extremely comfortable. However the water pressure in the shower wasn’t great and neither was the WiFi connection (although they do allow multiple devices to be connected). The only issue with the rooms being so high up is that the mobile phone signal isn’t the best. My only other complaint is that the reception is on the 70th floor and my room was on 43rd - accessed by a different set of lifts. This mean that, by some bizarre arrangement, having to get in the lift to go up to floor 70 in order to access the lift down to street level. If I had stayed any longer than 1 night, this would have been an irritation. A real positive is the attitude of the staff - from the warm welcome on the ground floor, to reception to concierge- everyone was helpful and friendly. A real highlight was having a late breakfast at Dekkadance on the 69th floor. I had arrived after the buffet had finished so ordered from the a la carte menu. I ordered the “Opulence Benedict” - an upmarket take on Eggs Benedict made up of Parma ham and poached crab instead of ham/Canadian bacon, dressed in rich hollandaise sauce with the perfect hint of horseradish atop perfectly poached eggs. It’s simply the best benedict I have ever eaten (and I have had many...!). Coupled with a fantastic view of Los Angeles and a cold glass of OJ it was the perfect breakfast! A generous portion, I thought I would not finish it. In the end I ate the whole lot!

author: Molliebclyde
title: Good and Not-so-Much, but Memorable Nonetheless
text: The hotel is certainly physically impressive—the architecture, design, and furnishings are all on point—and there’s nothing any reviewer can further say about the views. And while there may be a learning curve with the staff, I found them to be excellent, especially in the Club Lounge. But what bothered me was that the hotel seemed like “tourist central”. The lobby was always packed with people off the street looking around, crowding the bar and making it difficult to navigate. I suppose you need to expect some of that, but it got a bit much. Speaking of the Club Lounge, this is one of the better ones: a good food spread, much variety, cocktails, etc. As for the rooms, beware of the “Deluxe Room” which they tout as a corner room. Well, it’s a corner room if you count about less the 2 feet a “corner”, which is blocked by a column and curtains that cover half of that. But the room is quite nice, although we had some trouble getting enough hot water. The fitness center isn’t yet open, but you can walk across the street and use Gold’s Gym, which is probably better anyway! Everybody complains about the elevator set-up. It’s true that it takes one extra step in the process (to go up to the 70th before going down to your room), but it’s not that bad, and it’s a set-up used all over the world. The valet is odd: to get to and from, you need to walk through an industrial sterile white hallway like you’re in some sort of service entrance. A bit creepy and quite jarring from the great design of the rest of the hotel. Despite the ups and downs, I enjoyed staying here. It really is quite a memorable place.

author: MadridClydo
title: Striking hotel trying to work out the kinks after opening
text: The hotel is tall, with great views, nice rooms and 73rd (or 74th) floor rooftop bar. I was here with a conference and it was nice but there are some kinks and strange things the hotel needs to work through. First, my Uber driver could not figure out where to enter. The valet and taxi drop off is on 7th Street. Walking into the lobby, I immediately went up the escalator and half way up someone told me I needed to take the elevator to the 70th floor for check in. It is kind of a grand entry, but the elevator is not very visible and people needed to direct me. They hit the mark with the great views while checking in. The elevators were another story. From the 70th floor, you can take one set of elevators to any floor (not marked) and the other set of elevators only to 5 and 1. My room was on 46. Once there, if I wanted to got to 5 or 7 where the conference was, I had to take the elevator back up to 70, transition to another set and then go down. If you are below the 41st floor (I think), you can go to 31 to transition to other floors. Needless to say, fairly complicated and you have to figure it out or get help from employees who inevitably have to stand near the elevators to direct you because it is too confusing. The rooms were nice and all seem to have a view. All the food served was good. As a recently opened hotel, there are lots of little things they are trying to get right. My first day, two of us had burgers and coke on the 70th floor for almost $70. On the 69th floor we found a cheaper restaurant for next time.

title: High in the Sky
text: This hotel has a unique 70th floor reception area. Was very clean and the staff was friendly. Loved the view and the outside bar on the 73rd floor. Children were welcomed to see the bar and view up till 8 pm at night. We visited the bar around 530 pm when we were treated to the LA Police Helicopter doing a fly by and waving to everyone there. Rooms were clean and spacious. Only thing wrong with the room was the lighting in the bathroom. If you turned the light on in the middle of the night it would light up the whole room and woke up the kids a couple of times. Being a new Hotel it needs to work out a few things. Upon arrival we were not told about the restaurants and the bar on the 73rd floor. No directory in the room about what the hotel had to offer. Staff was new and a lot had just moved to LA and were unable to assist when we had questions on directions or the use of the Metro system. Conveniently located downtown and near the Staples Centre and the Metro was just across the street. Numerous restaurants from cheap to expensive in the area. The Security staff we amazing and very friendly.

author: stevebT4762EY
title: Great hotel, pity about front desk staff
text: Hotel dominates the skyline. Unique 70th floor reception was fun for the first time. Having to go up to get down every time you want to go or leave your room becomes tiresome. On arrival, check in was a nightmare. Two rooms booked, neither ready. Just completed 36 hours of travel, can you at least prioritize one room. No problem, we'll get on that. Other room will be ready at 3pm which is normal check in time. 2 hours later, at 2:45, neither room is ready. We need 10 more minutes. Guess what, 15 minutes later still not ready. We've given you a free upgrade to the room you previously booked, great! Just send luggage do we can freshen up for the ,extinguish at 5pm. Two cases delivered, one not. 45 minutes later and several calls and up and down visits later, the case arrives. Sorry, it was in storage! Receptionist gives the eye toll and head shake to communicate how stressed she is! Apart from that, and the go up to go down, the hotel is clean, fresh and pleasant. But sort out the front of office staff cause if they duck, so does the experience. All in all, worth a visit and stay but just not sure we would repeat the experience.

author: stevewR4112KO
title: Work needed to make it amazing...
text: Have stayed here 2x on biz in a corner room...the last one was stunning w/amazing views. This hotel has a long way to go before the service and experience is as awesome as the property appears. Staff is friendly...yet disorganized. Seemingly none of them are empowered to make a decision to better a guest's experience...it's always, "let me check with my Manager" or "you'll have to talk to the Concierge who's with a guest right now" and pointed to an empty Concierge desk where I stood for 15 mins. The elevator situation is, in a word, intolerable. With reception on the 70th floor, I get that you must travel there from the 1st floor to check in and the double-decker express elevator (upper & lower cabs) does that just fine. It's after you check in that's intolerable. From 1st floor, you can get to the 31st floor or 70th floor. 31st floor has access to another bank of elevators to "crossover" to some, but not all, upper floors. Some of us were on 52nd floor and were able to do crossover. I was on 54th floor and wandered 31st floor aimlessly before discovering that there is no crossover for floors above 52. In order to get to those floors, you must go to 70, go to a different bank of elevators then go down. Confused? Just wait until you're a guest there. Higher end valve in showers has a hard time delivering consistently warm/hot water, so you're constantly readjusting it. La Boucherie on 71 is their high-end steak house. Front desk had the reservation noted at the wrong time in the name of my Staff and not mine--despite that we'd gotten a confirmation email with the correct info/name. Again, no one empowered to fix it without calling a Manager...and making the guest wait. Definitely a long way to go before guests can enjoy the same experience as in other InterContinental properties.

author: marshalex
title: Seamlessly smooth and totally worth it glam
text: This is a new hotel in downtown LA and stayed here for 2 nights recently. The location is good with Macy's a block away and a fair amount of eating / shopping places within 10 minutes walking distance. The hotel is in the tallest building of LA and the reception at 70th floor prepares you for all the glam and glitz this place is. I was upgraded to Executive Room with Club Lounge access due to my Royal Ambassador status. It is a large room at the corner with stunning views. See attached pics for a better idea of the room. Needless to say the room is very tastefully furnished like the rest of the hotel and all modern nuances abound in the room. The Club Lounge has a good (by American standards) breakfast spread and has a very friendly staff. Its 70th floor views are really brilliant. Sone pics are attached. The entire hotel is shiny and new and has modern (sometimes tastefully quirky) decor. Feels very classy and enjoyable. The elevators are super confusing with no buttons inside and one has to come to the top floor from lower room floor to go to the street level. Might be a cumbersome thing for people with limited time or mobility. Overall a great stay and totally worth it.

author: pizarrofiction
title: All The Right Ingredients...
text: The hotel itself is impressive, dominating the skyline and brand-new as it is. The rooms are lovely with excellent views over Los Angeles. Every member of staff is eager to help and chat, no matter the time of day. The hotel lobby on the 70th floor has a great chill-out vibe with art books and comfy sofas. The rooftop bar is worth a visit even though it gets pretty busy. The coffee shop on the ground floor is great for some quiet time or if you need to get some work done, the vanilla honey iced latte is very tasty. The pool area is gorgeous, with attentive staff on hand to provide you with towels and drinks. However, it's obvious this hotel has some teething problems and poor design choices. Hopefully these can be sorted out. The first issue are the elevators. You need to get on one elevator to get to the 70th floor, then another to get to your room. If you're going to the pool or bar it gets a little crazy. Despite there being staff on the ground floor to direct you, you can still see guests wandering around lost and frustrated. It also seems they haven't finished building the hotel yet. The gym on the pool level is under construction, so if you walk out of the elevator you are greeted by builders and ladders, which seems unprofessional and confusing. The rooms also suffer a little from the systems in place. You have to actively press a "service" button by the door if you want your room made up, otherwise they won't come. The TV kept blacking out, and there's an app that allows you to Chromecast from your tablet, except it doesn't work. If all these minor issues were fixed, this would definitely be a five star hotel.

author: 742jillv
title: Beautiful views, amazing hotel
text: From the moment you walk into this hotel, you know your in for a treat. I love that the entrance is off the street, so there is no rushed drop off in traffic, or bottle neck where your in a rush. Check in is on the 70 floor and the views of the city are spectacular. We were upgraded to a junior suite. The room was beautiful with so many little upgrades. When you got out of bed at night, the floor beneath the bed would illuminate, no there was no tripping or hitting your shins on your way to the restroom. The bed was very comfortable, we could see the Hollywood sign from our room. Everyone was very nice and helpful. There are 3 restaurants on property Dekkadence where we ate had an all you can eat buffet for $55.00 per person. But this is not your typical buffet, the food was gourmet all delicious with the chefs there to help you make your choices. The food was delicious. The other 2 restaurants were Sora (a Sushi Restaurant) and La Boucherie on 71. Reservations are needed for the latter and they enforce a strict dress code, so if you plan to dine there call in advance. They also have several bar options Spire 73 is a fun trendy bar on the 73 floor, beautiful views from the tallest building in LA. They have a DJ, they were pretty busy that night, so we went down to the lobby bar, where the bartenders (both Christopher's) made excellent drinks and were fun to talk to. Great place to stay, I only wish we had more then one night to visit.

author: SouBru
title: top place to stay ..... soon
text: The brand new intercontinental downtown LA has all the trappings of a great luxury hotel from the architecture to the views to the amazing roof top bar. This property has real appeal. The rooms are well appointed with modern, sleek features and luxury bedding. The lobby and restaurants are beautiful and food quality is tops. But the honest and candid reality is that the details and kinks need a little more time to get worked out. As with any large hotel opening things are not always smooth and this is no exception. Check in was slow and the line to check in extended into the elevator bank about 20 guests long. The frustration was palpable among the guests and no one from the hotel worked the line to apologize or organize the seeming chaos. The room turnover was clearly slow as numerous guests waited in the lobby to be assigned a room. You could overhear the negative commentary of guests being told their rooms would be ready in 30 minutes or an hour only to wait for hours for their rooms. The Ambassador lounge is very nice but the staff are still in need of training and access is not controlled. Guests just wandered in to gawk at the views even though they did not have lounge access. I look forward to going back in a few weeks. And I am certain service will Improve quickly. This will be the top place to stay in downtown LA. Just needs a little more time.

author: japangeles
title: Staff needs training, elevators need signage (today).
text: This hotel is new and has a lot to work out. The first obvious fix that should have been done yesterday since nearly every guest has experienced a problem is the elevator signage. In order to transfer to common floors on the hotel (the bars, restaurants, supposed gym that doesn't exist yet, and lobby), you need to use one set of elevators from the 31st floor. That means that from any other floor, you have to first transfer from a core set of elevators to 31, and attempting to transfer anywhere else results in "ACCESS DENIED" on their lovely LEDs. As a millennial I found this interface puzzling, but since much of the clientelle is in their 50s and foreign, I can only imagine. Service. The staff is generally friendly but extremely green. Asking for a toothbrush kit means a several minute hold for consultation. Also, when I called regarding the elevator situation from the core when I was trapped, the person didn't know what to tell me and hung up, then allowed the phone to ring for 2 minutes before picking up again to transfer me to someone that could help ("Oh, go to 31 first, then transfer." - Thanks!) Finally, Spire 73. Yes, it's a rooftop bar. As a guest we should not only have priority but there should really be no hustle. This is not Hollywood Blvd. The bouncers need to understand that I am not dying to get my freak on in a mini skirt and Forever 21 heels. I want to see the view and have a cocktail, so politely grant access and offer us a good night, nothing more. The rooms themselves are beautiful with fantastic views and floor-to-ceiling glass. The TV channels don't work and the Keurig is placed next to an outlet in which all the plugs are filled, requiring disconnecting the mini-fridge power to make a cup of coffee. These matters will be worked out over time, but when you open, there should be experienced staff all over this day-in, day-out before the whole billion dollar investment flops because of sheer inattention to detail. On a less optimistic note, Elevate Lounge is across the way from the rooms and the glass is not double-paned enough, the degree of noise pollution is fairly substantial.

author: KarenCityinMountains
title: First To Stay, Not Ready
text: I stayed here on a business trip 6/22/2017 - 6/25/2017 and we were the first people to stay. The hotel was not ready to open to the public. First the elevators are confusing and hard to figure which ones and how to get where you are going. To add to the confusion there are no signs and no directions. The staff are friendly and eager to help but being so new they may not be sure of the correct answer to questions. There were no ice machines as they were there but still in the box next to the ice machine room. The room was nice and comfortable. The shower was very nice spacious and the towels were thick and of course brand new. The AC worked great as well. The issues we had with the room were, there was no trash cans in the room yet and took over 24 hours to get one. To get the TV, lights, and AC working you have to first put the key card to the room into a slot next to the front door! It would have been nice if the front desk told you or if there was a note on the desk telling you how to operate the room. Left room at 10am Saturday and housekeeping never cleaned our room service light was on as well. There was no cell service in the hotel either and I have T-Mobile and in Los Angeles I get service Everywhere. The pool was nice there are cool cabanas and a big bar. We had a great day at the pool. The hotel was gorgeous and I hope they can get this stuff together for their future success.

author: Melicin
title: Amazing place
text: My girlfriend and I stayed at this hotel for the second half of our Bali trip. Our jaws were dropped when we were taken to our villa. This is definitely one of the best places we stayed so far. Living room and bedroom are in separate huts. They both are quite large. The bathroom is outdoors. There is a good sized private pool. Everything is super clean and new. Breakfast was included and you can either have it at the restaurant or brought to your room. The service is amazing, they are very friendly and accommodating. They even paid our taxi fare when they didn’t have the car to pick us up from jimbaran. There is a private beach, however it’s nothing special. The beaches in that area are not good for swimming. Plus, in Bali, there is so much to see, you don’t want to waste your time lying on the beach. Overall, this is a great hotel, 100% recommended.

author: dianahuntley
title: Perfect mix of traditional Balinese vibes and modern minimalism
text: We were here for a few days at the beginning of November and had an incredible experience with Kayumanis. It's hard to describe, but everything about the spacious villa exuded privacy and relaxation. Loved that the check-in and welcome drinks took place in our villa, especially as we were tired from a long commute. The music was a great touch. One of my favorite quirks about this hotel is that they leave a positive quote each night on a parchment during turn down service. Another thing is the jars of ginger cookies and nuts that are refilled every day - very tempting, especially as a late night snack. The rooms were clean and comfortable. The bathroom is outdoors and I personally love that about properties in Bali. The hotel provides organic bug spray which is a life saver! We opted to have a private dinner on the beach our second night there, and it was one of the most beautiful dinner experiences i've had, with a secluded spot on the beach, and a 7 course seafood menu we pre-approved at check-in. You have 3 options for breakfast - in villa, at the restaurant or a sunrise breakfast on the beach which they only do for a limited number of guests each morning. We tried the sunrise one which we really enjoyed. The staff were wonderful. Our butler was very helpful with trying to book activities and also walked us to our massage because it is easy to get lost in the labyrinth of walkways when you first arrive. It's a part of the magic of the place, the high walls and the beautiful landscaping. P.S. the massage was amazing. 10/10 - we would definitely return. Thank you to the entire team at Kayumanis.

author: mohsinhussain2018
title: Kayumanis is the place to be!
text: I had the privilege of staying at Kayumanis for 5 days and must say it is probably the best place I have ever stayed! The privacy in the villas is perfect for a couples holiday/honeymoon and the service from the staff is impeccable. If you call reception for any kind of assistance in anything they will Immediately send someone to assist you. They also have a free shuttle service which honestly saved us a lot of money as we could get around the area without having to pay a penny for taxis. We stayed at another villa after our 5 days at Kayumanis and the difference was huge. If I have any regrets, I wish we would have stayed at Kayumanis for the full duration of our stay in Bali. The difference between Kayumanis and other hotels/villas is huge! We even visited the Mulia resort (one of Kayumanis’ main competitors) and that also did not come close to Kayumanis. We didn’t just feel like guests, we felt as though we were part of the Kayumanis family and one of the people that went the extra mile for us was the driver called Beny. This man made the whole holiday more enjoyable for us. Whenever we needed any advice on where to visit in Bali, he would point out all the best places to go, places to eat and so on. We feel as though we have a friend for life in Beny and this is how the staff make you feel part of the Kayumanis family. If anyone is planning on going to Kayumanis (you would be silly not to!) then please find Beny and you will not regret it. He is a credit to Kayumanis and represents everything they stand for, they are lucky to have him! I genuinely felt sad when saying our goodbyes and he even went out of his way to buy us a gift before we left! Gestures like this show that everyone MUST stay at Kayumanis and trust me there will be no regrets! Thank you for everything Kayumanis, especially Beny. Will hopefully see you all in the near future! Mohsin

author: GBoox
title: Good experience and an enjoyable stay but the villas need some renovation.
text: During our stay in Nusa Dua, we chose the Kayumanis Private Villa & Spa for 6 nights. I think that all in all, the net experience would have been overwhelmingly positive if it wasn't for some small things adding up. Starting with the pros. The settings is great, the traditional villa layout feels very private and there is a lot of space. The bed was very comfortable, the always full minibar (complimentary) was great and I liked the twice a day housekeeping. Staff was always helpful (however some more knowledgeable and willing than others admittedly), always available and attentive. High tea with local Balinese snacks was a thing to look forward to every afternoon as well. The most important thing is that even though we felt isolated in our villa, we were only a 7-10 minute walk away from the beach and if we wanted to go anywhere else, the shuttle service was available to drop us anywhere in Nusa Dua. Another nice gesture was the free transport from Kayumanis Nusa Dua to Kayumanis Ubud where we continued our holidays. Moving on to the cons which are mostly related to the room. When we checked in and went to the villa, I tried to raise the blinds that were covering the main windows but the mechanism was broken and so were some of the wooden parts. The staff immediately (and I really do mean immediately) sent someone who replaced them. Then in the living room only one of the floor plugs was working, with the other one not having any power going through it (it was not the one connected to a switch). In the living room area I think there was also some kind of smell which I would associate with a closed space and that is odd. Other than that, I think the breakfast could use more variety or some flexibility in modifying your order. If you are looking for a private villa, I would recommend Kayumanis provided that they do some kind of refurbish soon as small things can leave a sour taste if they pile up. If you don't think that the cons I mentioned are important at all, then by all means book your next stay here. This level of privacy and attentiveness cannot really be found in normal hotels.

author: ArumPuri
title: Best Decision!
text: We stayed here for 4 nights and it was one of the best decisions we ever made. Nusa Dua has always been our accommodation choice location. Private, pristine white sands beach. We stayed in a hotel the last few trips to Bali, this time we decided we want to stay in a Villa and just chill. I must stay, best decision! You can request for a driver to pick you up to and from the airport or anywhere in the local area. The service is first class. All the staff was friendly and helpful. Every day, they serve you afternoon tea in your villa (or they will just leave it in your villa for when you return). The breakfast can be inside delivered to your villa or at their restaurant. Food was always excellent. Breakfast and snacks were included in our room price. There is a beach that is a 10-minute walk through an alleyway of sorts. You can take their bikes if you wish (free). The villa itself was amazing. We had a private pool, a bedroom, and a living room. The rooms were in two separate small buildings. Oh and outdoor shower is amazing! I would highly recommend this villa to anyone who is thinking of staying in Bali.

author: lisasH712UQ
title: An amazing and first class luxery resort
text: My family and I cannot say enough about Kayumanis Nusa Dua resort. We have travelled as a family all over this world and on first sight of our villa I had tears in my eyes. The staff, although that is a poor word for it as they are wonderful and professional individuals that take your comfort and vacation experience to the next level are, over the top wonderful. There is never a quesion or request that does not go answered. You are always made to feel welcome by everyone and your experience and relaxation is paramount. The restaurant is simple the best and we travelled to a few places around Bali and there was no better food that the Indonisian and Italian at the hotel. It was simply outstanding, and we are foodie snots so trust us on this one. We took the cooking class and market tour and loved it, the meal and the experience was a first for us and we learned some interesting skills. Chef Wayan Merta Astawa was a delight to be with that day. We hired a car a couple of days to see more of the country, although Bali traffic is awful. Mayo took good care of us and got us back and forth in record time. Even keeping cold cloths and beer in the back, perfect! It was sad to leave and after seeing a lot of this world I would still go back and stay again and again. Indonisia is simple a beautiful country with beautiful people and the resort is a reflectioin of that. The Smith Family

author: armie_2015
title: Best honeymoon ever
text: We stayed at kayumanis for 12 days for our honeymoon, and what a great honeymoon we had!! Amazing resort, with only 18 Villa’s. Very small and quit between the big resorts. You dont hear the other villas. Breakfast at the restaurant or at you villa at any time! It didn’t matter what time it is. Afternoon high tea from 15:30 to 17:30. And then two restaurants where you can choose from. Two cleaning moments per day. Complementary mini bar. A very quit and clean beach. Free car drive to 15 min distance. We had a private beach dinner 7 courses. They go all the way for you at kayumanis. There is not much to do around the resort in nusa dua, but we had tours arranged to ubud and and the other higlights in bali. So if you want to go out and have a busy nightlife, this area isn’t for uou. Very very nice people. I have never seen this service level anywhere. I would reccomend kayumanis to everyone who wants a quite and nice honeymoon! Thank you kayumanis for everything.

author: U6161ITsamanthaw
title: Lovely little relaxing hideaway
text: Very relaxing and private villa. Villa is surrounded by hidden concrete walls so extremely private. You have two villas, a sleeping bathing area and living, eating area. Both were really luxury and had a Balinese feel to it. Lovely to sleep in a king size canopied bed and mattress was very comfortable. Was strange having an outside bathroom, but the mosquito coils at night did a great job. Tub was very relaxing would have been better if it was a spa bath. Air conditioning in both rooms worked very well, was a little weird walking from one villa to the other and venturing out into heat to do so. Fridge was in the bedroom, and probably should have been in the living area, or another one in the living area. Private pool was great and bigger than I expected. Facilities were very well maintained and all of the staff were friendly and always said hello. High tea every day was delightful and was great to have Balinese deserts included in the assortment for us to try. Breakfast was also delicious and there was always an abundance of food. Friendly and efficient staff. Only downside was that there was no air conditioned space available if eating breakfast in the restaurant. Long walk down to the beach club, so we only did it later in the evening. Complimentary 30 minute spa was nice, a little bit hard at some points. Welcome me drink of lemongrass tea was nice and refreshing after a long flight. Fruit, nuts and biscuits along with cold drinks available daily in room was also a very nice touch. We also enjoyed the no young kids policy as an escape from it all.

author: 398janau
title: An amazing holiday
text: We arrived at this hotel spoiled and pampered by a high-level quality of other hotels all around the world. Photos and reviews already gave us a hint, that the hotel is going to be beautiful but with the first sunrise ( which seemed like it was meant to be especially just for Kayumanis that day) we knew it is going to be also very unique, therefore you deserve the first star for the location and setting. It is a paradise, an oasis of calm, where you have anything you could ever wish for right at your fingertips. The second star goes for the design and architecture. Architects were very smart and thought of everything - a sufficient amount of light in the interiors as well as exteriors, a functionality of the furniture and also enough greenery to connect the hotel with nature. We were very impressed by all those small details which made us feel like home even after the very first day. We would give the third star to your brilliant restaurant. Your chefs belong to those who are creative and who see gastronomy not just as their profession, but also as their passion. Thank you for all those amazing meals we had the opportunity to taste (from the chicken soup just like from grandma to Kayumanis toast which I feel like we can't live without). The great forth star belongs to loyal, fast and professional staff. They take care of us with love, especially Tri, Novi and Eka! Our only complaint is that we can't put them in our suitcases and take them home with us. The last star is for the perfect atmosphere and overall impression. With my husband, we wish you from now on just the guests, which will have a heart in the right place and won't come just to try finding issues. As people working in the same industry ( even at the other end of the world), I must say I couldn't have any negative attitudes towards you like rivalry or competition, only a gratitude, respect and the sense of belonging as you are people who manage to do their job with love and to the best of their knowledge and belief. We would highly recommend this place to anyone who is thinking about to visit! Thank you for making our holiday unforgettable!Vila Gamal/J&S

author: N2643HPbrianl
title: In a single word - AMAZING!
text: My friend and I spent 10 days at Kayumanis Nusa Dua, and it tore us up we had to leave when our holiday was over. The staff is simply quite amazing! My friend just wanted to go Kelingking Beach, and the front office staff were able to make the private tour arrangements at the last minute and it was something they had never done before. The excursion went very very well! The Take With You breakfast was greatly appreciated on the excursions where we left so early in the morning. The food here is very very good - never had a bad meal whether dining in or going to the restaurant. High Tea is something you are going to want to do everyday here. The tray of food is great, and I love the Iced Green Tea! The amount of privacy we had here is something we will never experience anywhere else as we did not see other guests and we could do what we want inside the villa. A couple of items I would like to see be made better. Breakfast on the beach in order to see the sunrise is nice but what would really make it fantastic is if the breakfast is ready upon arrival at our lounge chairs. I feel by doing this we could watch the sunrise without interruption. The other item is maybe curtains or shades for the living room windows. When the sun shines in even for a little bit it can get a little uncomfortable in there. Everything here is top rate and we cannot wait to come back! Thank you Eka, Nedy, Tri (in the restaurant), and everyone at Kayumanis Nusa Dua for making this an unbelievable stay!

author: Pathfinder300052
title: Amazing private villa
text: We visited this place at the end of February. It is an amazing hotel but what really makes it stand out is the service. Everyone at the property is so friendly. Initially you might think that the property is more expensive than the surrounding resorts. However, you get so much value for what you pay. The room rate included private airport pickup, daily afternoon tea, mini fridge, fruit, snacks, 30 min massage, daily breakfast on beach, restaurant, or in villa. Every villa comes with a private pool which is not just a tiny plunge pool. It's a full size pool! I didn't see anyone swimming in the resort pool (although it looked amazing) because everyone was enjoying their private pool. The outdoor bathroom and shower is pretty unique as well. The villa is completely private and huge. The private beach club is a short walk away. They also have feee bike rentals so you can ride the bikes on the beach boardwalk. Afternoon tea and breakfast served in your own private villa is amazing! Finally, the service is out of this world. If you are on the fence about booking this property, just do it. There is a reason this is the number 1 property in the area. Thank you for an unforgettable experience.

author: 865juheeb
title: Fantastic service and a great great place!
text: Right from the time we got here, the staff was super super friendly and helpful. The property itself is beautiful, relaxing and very luxurious. Our villa was super cosy, it really felt like home. Food is good - must have the Nasi Bubuh at breakfast. It was yum :) We also did something called the Sunrise breakfast which was a breathtaking view of the sunrise on a nice beach bed laid out on the private beach. Highly recommended for everyone who wants a luxurious five star like experience. We were well taken care of and we can't wait to visit this place again. P. S. Special callout for honeymoon couples - our room was set up for the occasion. Great place for your special trip. A lot of small small things were done to make us feel special. Won't say more. The rest you should experience once you are there. Can't wait to visit them again. Special call out to Erna, Devi and Benny for being wonderful and kind.

author: nonevent666-666
title: "Welcome home!"
text: There's not much I can add to the review I wrote of Kayumanis Nusa Dua in April 2017. That we chose to return for another stay, seven months after our first, speaks volumes for the quality of the resort. When we booked, we requested to stay in Villa Akasia, where we were last time. It's a great villa, and the pool area is in full sun for many hours each day. As anticipated, the villa was spotlessly clean. We did have one minor problem with one of the entrance doors, but the engineering crew dealt with it on the same morning we reported the issue. Service. A welcome addition to the villa was the power board with three international plugs and four USB outlets. Brilliant! One measure of staff satisfaction at any business is turnover, and Kayumanis Nusa Dua obviously has very low staff turnover. It was great to see the same friendly faces whom we met on our first stay. The staff are all so gracious and obviously pleased to be of service to their guests. It's probably unfair to name exceptional staff individually, since they're all excellent, but I really must give a special mention to Susi, Ebi, Yuda, and butler Bayu. Thanks guys - you're the very best of the very best. As I said, though, all the staff are fantastic, which reflects the generous spirit of the Balinese people. We were pleased to be greeted with a "Welcome home!" when we first checked-in, and when we returned after an outing. If only home was this good! Breakfast at Tetaring was very good, as expected, and we dined at Piasen on New Years Eve, where the food and the service were excellent. It was a shame that Nusa Dua seemed so quiet, due to Mt Agung threatening to erupt, but if there was a place I had to be marooned because of an erupting volcano, it would be Kayumanis Nusa Dua. It's simply excellent, and we hope to be welcomed "home" again very soon!

author: SuSuSuSu87
title: Nice quiet resort but beware of the mosquitos
text: We have arranged for airport transfer prior to the trip , the staff was there early to pick us up however, we didn't manage to spot him due to the huge crowd when we were on the way out to the arrival area. We approached the information counter (i.e near the arrival area where the group of hotel staffs were there to pick up their guest) for the staff to make an announcement, however, our butler didn't manage to catch that announcement too. We managed to meet our butler only after we made a phone call to the resort. While the initial experience weren't too good, the butler provided good service once he picked us up. The cold drinks, towel and nice cookies during our trip to resort were good. The duration from the airport to the resort was about 25 min. The resort offers free transport to anywhere in nusa dua and jimbarang, and airport transfer, however on some occasions, the driver was late (15-20 min late) in picking us up on the stipulated timing that we have agreed on previously. The breakfast and complimentary afternoon tea was good and in good quality. I love the vegetarian nasi goreng and kayumanis toast. Free mini bar, snacks (biscuit and peanuts) and daily fruits. There's also a separate menu for vegetarian and food can be send to the villa. In general, the service standard was good and I remember that service staff provided for 2 bottle of 1.5 litre water when we asked for 1 bottle which we find that they were pro active in meeting our demands. This is a quiet resort with lots of privacy. Free bicycle for loan which we utilised to ride to the nearby attraction "waterblow" and I enjoyed very much, its a pity that the hotel don't provide lock for the bike though. We stayed in Dadap, overall the environment and cleanliness was alright except for the 1) mosquitos (which does not seemed to be afraid of repellent or the mosquito coil) , the mosquito most active during the evening to night time and it keeps us busy at night, 2) facilities at the bathroom seemed to be a bit wear out (i.e rusting at the bath tube sink hole, rusting at the shower head), faulty tap (which was fixed after the first housekeeping), i also observed a gush of brownish water that flows out of the tap for about 5 sec when I first turned it on , 3) the stone decors near the outdoor shower and before the entrance to bedroom prone to collection of water which = more place for mosquito breeding, while i understand it is inevitable for mosquito to be around in nature place, such decor could be removed to avoid more breeding place for mosquito. Besides that , water from the taps in bali is non drinkable, do take note however it not a issue as resort staff are more than happy to assist and provide more water when required. Overall still a good experience, however It will be better if the staff is able to share with guest of what are the stuff to do within the areas and local attractions during the first meet up and to update their maps accordingly.

author: welltravelledToronto
title: The perfect retreat
text: My husband and I stayed here for 6 nights in May. We had some difficulty initially trying to pay at the website and had to resort to using our banker to help arrange a money transfer. That was frustrating and did make us wonder about whether we made to right choice but once we arrived we realized we had. Kurnia, who picked us up at the airport and took us back was also available for drives throughout our stay. His kind and thoughtful care set the tome for our stay. All the staff were pleasant and respectful - from the moment we checked in to the time of our departure. My heart smiled at seeing everyone content from groundskeeper to restaurant staff, to room, pool and beach attendants and spa therapists. This atmosphere of contentment was good for the soul :). Our villa was perfect! The sleeping area was perfect - the mosquito netting around the bed helped to diffuse the air conditioning that could have created a bit of a chill. The bed was amazingly comfortable. We slept so well that our internal clock was reset after one night. The breakfasts were delicious with a number of interesting dishes from which to choose. We could have had our butler bring it to our room but the idea of going to the open air restaurant appealed to us.We did have tea brought to our room most days to enjoy after a day of exploring or just walking the beach. The hotel's walkway to the beach closed at 7 but we found a lovely route to the beach through the property pf the next door hotel's grounds.Our habit was to eat out by the beach each night and then enjoy a leisurely walk back to our villa. We also made use of the spa the day before we left which was the perfect way to draw our holiday to a close.

author: sixamigos
title: Very enjoyable holiday. Excellent Villa
text: From the minute we were picked up at the airport by our Butler, we were supplied with cold water, cold towel and cookies and a very comfortable drive to our villa for four nights which was villa Pinus. We had a magnificent crystal clear pool, lovely bedroom and family room of a very high quality which was stocked with free drinks in mini bar, bowl of fruit, jar of cookies and jar of the most delicious peanuts. Our toilet was indoors but our shower was outside. What an amazing experience waking early to shower outside with birds singing, blue sky and squirrels running along the fence, something we will never forget. All the staff at Kayumanis could not do enough for us. For example we mentioned to the cleaners that it was a little bit dark in the bedroom for makeup, hair etc and within two minutes they had the electrician in our room with a portable desk lamp which was perfect. Being able to have your breakfast any time within 24 hours is a huge plus with a very large variety and they are very flexible with the menu and you also can have your afternoon tea in your villa which is free. A very big thanks to Yuda who looked after us. We dined at their restaurant Tetaring on the first night and the lobster stir fry was delicious and of high quality. We had cocktails on their private beach and the bar staff were outstanding in setting up our lounge chairs and offering to spray us with their insect spray. Every time we left our villa even to dine at the restaurant for breakfast or dinner our room was cleaned and restocked, even after a walk to the beach or a morning out. We decided to go to Bumbu Bali restaurant and the hotel staff booked and organised for the restaurant to pick us up and return us after dinner. We are very grateful that the staff were only too eager to drive us to Bali Collection and pick us up any time we decided to return. We are also grateful that we were given the use of their office computer and printer to checkin for our flight home. You are also given a 30 minute neck and back massage each as part of your stay which was very relaxing. Take the guess work out of deciding where to stay!!! If you want to spoil yourself and meet some of the nicest people in the world you MUST stay at Kayumanis Nusa Dua for a very relaxing and romantic stay. Suk Sama to all at Kayumanis, we shall return.

author: TravellerNL010
title: Enjoyed our stay
text: We looked forward to coming back to this place, since our first stay two years ago was absolutely wonderful. The staff is still very friendly and helpful. They will do everything to make you feel at home. We were given the villa Cengkeh, which is the first villa on the complex when you walk out from the lobby. This villa is smaller than the villa we were given two years ago (Merbau), but still of a good size for two people. We noticed that the maintenance of the villa could be improved. The wallpaper in the living room started to come off on certain places and the colour of the paint in the bathroom was already worn off. Some of the wooden blinds in the bedroom could not be closed properly, which can be a problem in the morning when the daylight breaks in. Housekeeping tried their best to solve this, but when something is broken it simply needs to be repaired or changed. These are little things, but when you pay around 300 USD per night the villa (one of the highest priced accommodations in the area) should be in an excellent condition.
