In the end after a long day of being a tourist it was great to come back to the villa for some fine dining. We recommend Kayumanis Nusa Dua without reservation to anyone who wants to experience the magic of Bali. We would come to the Kaumanis Villa and Spa at Nusa Dua in a flash.

author: FatboyRed
title: Bespoke service that exceeded expectation
text: We stayed for 4 nights at Kayumanis Nusa Dua. It was our first stay with Kayumanis. Their service is one of the best we have experienced. Our butler Bagus picked us up at the airport and was very attentive to our needs. Though his shift was 7am to 3pm, he was with us at 9pm one of the nights to make sure that our dinner at the beach was perfect. Bagus also sent us to the airport when we left. This is the only resort we have stayed where every staff knew our names. You can have breakfast any time you wish. The sunrise breakfast at the beach, which was complementary, was lovely. The resort offers free transport to anywhere in Jimbaran. We were most impressed when our driver who picked us up at the crowded Ayana resort recognised us immediately at the lobby without us having to look for the car. Perhaps the only negative point is the distance from the beach. Despite being in Nusa Dua, the resort is about 7 minutes' walk to the beach. Kayumanjs provides free bicycles for guests to cycle to the beach. That said, we thoroughly enjoyed our stay at Kayumanis. The level of service provided by its staff really made a difference. When we left, we had a farewell gift in the form of a luggage tag with our names and address pre-printed. We met a French couple who has been staying with Kayumanis for the past 4 years, each stay lasting a month. With the exceptional service provided by Kayumanis, I can understand why. This resort is highly recommended for those who like a quiet stay at a boutique resort with excellent service.

author: Achatina
title: I Will Definitely Stay Here Again! Highly Recommended for Honeymoon
text: I stayed at Kayu Manis Nusa Dua for 3 days and 2 nights. And I regretedi it,,why I didn't stay there longer..... :( Me and my husband went there last week for our honeymoon, and both of us are very satisfied! They (Kayu Manis) begin their service by pick us up at the airport and welcome us with Cinnamon cookies and cold drinks in the car. When I arrived at the villa, I was surprised with the place that truly offered 'private place'. I booked one bedroom villa with honeymoon package. In the room, there were two rooms in the villa. One room with kitchen, dining room for two and sofa complete with CD player+CDs. The other room is bed room and an outdoor bathtub+shower+toilet. Pretty awkward in the beginning but since the villa is very private I could feel comfortable. In addition, they put flower petals on bath tub :) The villa also has a private pool. Big enough for two people. With wooden deck and a douche. Thing that made me and my husband impressed as the hospitality from the staffs, especially the butler. They made us feel like royals! Seems 'No' wouldn't be an answer from them. They will provide you things you request the best they can.. All in all,, Kayu Manis is a very recommended place especially for you who want to spend their honeymoon in Bali.

author: Shnazio
title: Excelent service, friendly staff and great food in a beautiful environment
text: My wife and i stayed at the Kayumanis in Nusa Dua in the one bedroom poolvilla 'Cemara' from july 17th until july 29th . Right from the start we had a feeling that our stay would be something special. After spending three excruciating ours in line for immigration at the Denpasar airport, we were awaited by our friendly Kayumanis butler Agus. In the car we received cold towels, mineral water and freshly baked cookies. At the hotel we were received in the lobby, which is in an open area and where no computer is used. I think that is to give the guests a feeling of complete relaxiation. Our butler Agus, checked us in and after giving us a tour of the resort, guided us to our villa. The villa consists of a seperate bedroom and livingroom area and a swimmingpool. The villa also has two outside showers and a bath which were on the back side of the villa. Our twelve days were spent in this beautiful villa with typical balinese archirtecture, where our butler Agus and staff did absolutely everything to make our stay unforgettable. We also received a lot of benefits like daily afternoon tea (including sweets), 2,5 hour spa treatment and an in villa barbeque. There is a 24 hour butler service and they have one of the best breakfasts that i ever had at a hotel. Everything is so fresh and tasty. The banana jam for example is an absolute treat. I definitely recommend the Kayumanis Nusa Dua to anyone who likes privacy and to be pampered during his or her holiday. We absolutely loved our stay and would definitely reconsider going back there again.

author: JanneJ
title: excellent hide away experience
text: We stayed in this resort 4 nights after we been in Ubud 4 nights, we wanted to find a villa near a beach. It's rather dificult to find a pool villa at the beach, so this with a short walk was what we find, and the walk was ok. We talked to 3 hotels for getting a nice price and Kayumanis gave us a good offer. First we didn't think this was as good as we thought, more like a prison with grey walls... but after 4 nights in a plung pool villa we loved it. This resort is really for a hide away stay. You can stay in the villa 24/7 and get all service you want. Actually they want to serve breakfast and other meals in the villa, there is no extra charge for this (But it makes the restaurant rather empty...). The breakfast is excellent. For a romantic stay this hotel is excellent, we loved to be able to naked take a dip in the own pool whenever we wanted. The pool was actually 1,2 meter from the bed... Our experience is based on a good price, if we should pay full price I think there is better places. WiFi was included and worked good. We toke a nice bikeride one day. A short walk there is some restaurants. the hotel provide you with free transfer to restaurants, that worked good.

author: ZsophistiKate1
title: Fantastic service!
text: My husband and I stayed at Kayumanis in Nusa Dua for four nights during our two week honeymoon in Bali. Kayumanis was just fantastic, the staff especially. They really made us feel welcomed and cared for from the moment we stepped on the premises. They even had a "sunset cocktail" gathering for all the guests and the staff to interact and get to know one another, which we thought was really nice. The whole staff knew our names and were all made aware of any needs, requests, and special accommodations. I have an intolerance to gluten so I am really used to avoiding a lot of foods and accommodating for myself, but everyone from the waitstaff to the management went out of their way to make sure I was take care of, making special foods for me and even alerting restaurants outside of the hotel ahead of time without me asking them to. Nothing was ever too much trouble. They were all so great, especially our "butler" Endy, I just can't say enough nice things about the experience. We had stayed in Seminyak the previous four nights and it was such a relief to be away from the traffic and construction and arrive somewhere peaceful and relaxing. Our villa was beautiful. The outdoor shower is really fantastic! Breakfast in the villa each morning was delicious. We went on a fishing trip through Kayumanis which was so much fun. We began the day at sunrise on the water in an traditional catamaran, fishing around Jimbaran. We stopped and had lunch on a small quiet beach and then got back on to snorkel and fish some more. Then, we were cooked a delicious BBQ seafood dinner in our villa that night, which included some our day's catch. It was really great. I would definitely recommend staying at Kayumanis if you are planning to spend time in Nusa Dua. A truly wonderful experience!

author: Mystie
title: Perfect Place to pamper yourself!
text: We stayed at the Oriental-themed L-shape villa. This basically means that the Bedroom is separate from the Living Area. I highly recommend the L-shaped villas! We relaxed in the Living Area during the turn-down service every night. High commendations have to be given to the staff. Everyone we encountered, from booking the hotel to being sent to the airport at the end of our stay; all our requests were handled professionally, and we felt marvelously pampered! The bed's very comfortable, the villa's very spacious. The private pool is actually big enough for a swim! Food is excellent as well, although the appetizers and main courses are much better than the desserts. I highly recommend the local cuisine, and the omelette is delicious for breakfast! The candlelight dinner have to be tried! We hired the butler (our butler's name is Arya) for a full day's tour. And whilst he took us to some popular art galleries (as per our request), the 'Semar Kuning' art gallery in Ubud which he recommended turned out to be our favourite! The choices were varied, and the prices were way more reasonable (and negotiable). There were few disappointments, and one would have to be the private beach connected to this villa. It's not exactly the sandy white beaches that's connected to the bigger hotels. The bathtubs is on the small side- will only fit 1 person, which is surprising, since this resort caters to couples. The desserts need to be improved. Other than that, our stay here was close to perfection!

author: iheartbangkok
title: hmmm...maybe I am a little young for this place...
text: I was planning on staying at The Bale and wish I had stuck to my original plan. I booked Kayumanis and cancelled The bale at the last minute because I read the reviews on trip advisor and they were glowing! I also logged onto their website and the place looked incredibly modern and beautiful- and we were looking for somewhere special to get engaged. On arrival the grounds are breathtaking , very cleverly designed and the staff were very knowledgable + attentive. We arrived a little early and so decided to have lunch in the restaurant. The food was good, but I ordered a Capiroska and I cant remember exactly how much it was ($15 AUD maybe) ,but it was really bad and super sweet with lumps of brown sugar in it and the glass was only half full.. I am happy to pay 15 dollars for a cocktail if its good... We were shown to our villa by our butler and as he was showing us the bathroom there was a giant lizard and its poo in the bath. He got on his walky talky and ushered us out . We offered to flick it out with a towel and asked them not to kill it ( we are australian and are used to such situations) along came the maintenance man with a large backpack can of poison and as we were checked in we heard the spray sound and he carried the dead lizard out in his hands...we felt responsible for its death and very guilty. The villa ,which was actually 2 rooms didnt really fit in with the rest of the place and were quite traditional in style.I actually found it a bit frustrating having the two pavillions.one with bedroom and bathroom and the other with kitchen /living.The aircond in our room seemed to be really slow , but was super efficient in the living room part.It was really hot in the night and i contemplated sleeping on the sofa so I could be cool- not what you would expect to have to do for $500 a night! We had organised a candlelit dinner and the setup was beautiful! I asked for an indonesian menu (as you would being in indonesia) , but had to settle with a modern italian menu -no choice set menu. I thought for the price it was very disappointing and the tira mi su at then end didnt 'pick me up' as tira mi su should -it just let me down... On the plus side the pool and outside area was lovely and very refreshing.The breakfast was fantastic- what choice! We also had a great massage and scrub in the spa. I am sorry that I didnt have a very good time and cant rave about the place as others have. We were recovering from a stomach parasite that came from eating some dodgy chicken on jalan legian and so we probably werent as relaxed + accomodating as normal. I could possibly go into more detail about other things that were a bit off or annoying, but shall spare you anymore torrents in case I change your mind.One persons experience can depend on so many different factors.. I am a bit of an avid Asian boutique hotel visitor and feel that I have had better value for money in other places that I have stayed..

author: 322jackiet
title: Great place to stay on Route 66
text: The rooms are comfortable and clean. The decorations are cute and fit with the theme of the town. One of the first things I noticed was they had two luggage racks already available in the room which is awesome! I never understood why hotels don't provide more then one when they know more then one person with a suitcase is coming. Great little details, we will definitely recommend this place to our friends. I only have two "negative" comments but they aren't enough negative to stop me from coming again and I will still suggests the hotel to my friends: 1) My self and my friends in another room, all 4 (two for my room and two for my friends room) of our keys randomly stopped working. Thankfully we got back to our room before the main office closed down for the night (I believe it shuts down at 10pm). If we had gotten back after the person in the front left I think it would have been a big hassle to get into our room. They provide after hours numbers to call if needed, but all of those were inside our hotel room and we didn't think to copy it down/bring it with us. So if you plan on getting back to the hotel after hours I would copy down the after hours phone number. 2) There were 3 couples in our group so 3 separate room reservations. We all booked through TripAdvisor/Booking.com on the same day within the same hour for the same type of room. Both of the other couples were upgraded to suites with kitchens at no extra charge. One of the couples didn't even ask to be upgraded and they were surprised with the upgrade when they checked in. I called and asked for a mini fridge for the room because I have meds that need to be kept cold. The lady who answered basically said most likely no but she would see. I'm used to traveling with an ice chest to keep my meds cold it just would have been easier not to need it in the room. I'm not sure why I didn't get a mini fridge for my meds when my friend was upgraded without asking and didn't need it.

author: 113marcil
title: Poor customer service and small rooms
text: We arrived at the hotel only to be told our reservation was cancelled. That is a problem I will take up with booking.com. My issue with the Lodge was the customer service. The lady at reception just kept stating that we had cancelled even though I had confirmation from 3 days before. She was totally unsympathetic and did nothing to try to rectify the problem. I had to ask if there might be two rooms available that she could rent to our group. She checked and advised they were available so I asked if we could please just get those rooms. She completed the check in and said we could not have the keys even one minute before 4pm check in time. I have never experienced this before. Always in past travels if room was ready we were able to check in. The time was about 2pm. I said OK but as we have been traveling for hours could I use the ladies room. I was advised I could go across the street to a laundromat as they had no public restrooms. I did not consider myself as "public" as I had just paid her $160. for a room. At that point I was a quest. When we finally got to the room it was clean but very small, no closet and little floor space to place luggage. It is a cute, quaint building right on Rte 66 which is what drew us to the location initially. I have left a message for the manager to call me but as of yet have not gotten a response. There were 4 of us and anyone of them will confirm the truth of this exchange.

author: 658JS
title: Grand Canyon visit with 3 kids
text: We really enjoyed our stay at The Lodge on Route 66! Great location and proximity to the Grand Canyon. The town is so cute and quaint! There were many dining options within walking distance. The most important thing is IT'S ON HISTORIC ROUTE 66!! My youngest was so excited to stay on Route 66! The hotel has been renovated and is very nice on the inside! We stayed in a king suite (sofa sleeper in living area). There is a refrigerator and microwave in the room...speaking of the refrigerator, we ate one night and had leftovers, too bad we didn't know the refrigerator was not automatically left on...so we lost our expensive leftovers 😢. The Wifi is not good at all! With that said, who comes to Williams to use Wifi? We were on a two week roadtrip and the goal was to relax and unplug from our everyday...spotty wifi ensured that happened, lol! The breakfast was good! Typical continental fare: waffle maker, sausage, bagels, toast, juices, coffee, yogurt, etc. Breakfast is included with your room rate. Amberlee and Jamie worked the front desk and were super sweet and helpful! Overall, we would definitely stay here again!

author: NP1951
title: Convenient to Grand Canyon
text: We stayed a few nights based on location and charm. Read good reviews on TA prior to booking. Grand Canyon train available just two blocks away from motel. If you are train enthusiast, consider riding instead of driving. Cutest town on our Route 66 drive from California. We think value offered was good. Our room was a small suite-tiny living room w sofa, pub table, microwave. Queen bedroom very tight but we were ok. Good sized TVs in both living and bedroom. Good space in bath area. Bed comfortable. Perfect space while we toured Grand Canyon and Painted Desert. Nearby restaurants (steak houses, pubs, Italian, country) are totally walkable. We found each to be very good. 50 mile drive to GC is on a good road. Great laundromat directly across street should you need it. Breakfast at Lodge simple but well laid out. We recommend instead of chain hotels in and near GC Park.

author: countryguylawrence
title: Great nostalgia
text: We stayed here two nights while visiting the Grand Canyon. The room we had was a suite with a king bedroom and a living area. Everything was very clean and very quiet. The room was updated very nicely and without losing the old school charm. Although we were just one door from the main drag, the road noise was not noticeable nor was there any noise from the neighboring units. Bed was extremely comfortable. HD tv's in living area and bedroom. Refrigerator/freezer with microwave and kitchen table and chairs. Very nice tub/shower with toilet. Double sink with over-sized vanity. Nice luxurious towels. In the center of the courtyard was a covered patio with two fireplaces and drop curtains to enclose the area if needed for weather. This was a great unexpected feature. Continental breakfast was a little better than you would expect from a retro motel. Two waffle irons, sausage patties, and the normal fruits, bagels, muffins, etc. Price was fair. Our only reason for not giving this a 5 star rating was the lack of good power outlets for the tech stuff and low lighting in the living room area. Overall we were very happy with the Lodge and would certainly stay here again.

author: cutebamagirl
title: Grand Canyon Day Trip
text: We chose to stay at The Lodge on Route 66 because it was close to the Grand Canyon and the reviews on TripAdvisor were good. We rented a king suite, but only because it was the only king size bed available. The suite had a full size sofa which I think was also a sofa bed. There was a partial kitchen with a microwave and a very small refrigerator. It also had a Keurig one cup coffee maker with enough coffee for two cups. They charge you $1.00 for each additional cup. The good thing about the room is that it was very clean and had a very comfortable bed and wonderful linens. The negative thing with the room is that the kitchen table was very uncomfortable, there weren't any glasses or cups in the bathroom, and the blinds were messed up preventing us from having total privacy. We packed our belongings and loaded them into the car before going to the Lodge to get some breakfast. It was a least an hour before check out time and we'd planned to go back to our room after breakfast. When we got back to our room the housekeeping staff was already cleaning and she didn't offer to come back later. She didn't say anything to us, just looked at us kinda funny and kept cleaning. I'm not sure she spoke English anyway. Needless to say, we checked out sooner than we had intended to. Overall, our stay at The Lodge on Route 66 was pretty good.

author: BrownBalto
title: Odd variety of rooms
text: We stayed at the Lodge on Route 66 for one night on our way from the Grand Canyon to Las Vegas. The staff there is very friendly. The location is fine. We were first put in a room with one queen bed. The room was tiny. There was only about one or two feet to move around on each of the three open sides of the bed. The air conditioning unit blew right on the bed. There was a window that could be opened, but the window in the bathroom was glass block and couldn't be opened so there wasn't any cross ventilation. Because my husband is claustrophobic, we asked for a larger room. We paid more and got a suite with bedroom, living room and kitchen. The area was much larger but most of the windows were glass block and couldn't be opened. The kitchen had a window that opened, but the way it was configured, you had to stand on a chair or something to get to it (and we are tall people). There was also a door that could be opened that looked onto a UHaul lot. That couldn't be kept open at night so we were forced to use the air conditioning which was loud. There is a free breakfast but it wasn't much to my liking. And perhaps this is particular to me, but it was served on styrofoam which is a negative for me. Also, the refrigerator in our room didn't appear to cool, although the light in it worked.

author: stephanieh31
title: It's all about location and experience!
text: My family stayed in two standard queen rooms at The Lodge for one night on our way to the Grand Canyon. Overall, the rooms we got were sufficient, but nothing spectacular. They were very small, but we were warned of that when booking, as the square footage of all rooms is listed on the website. There is no refrigerator or microwave, which was an inconvenience. We had to use a styrofoam cooler to keep things cold, and made due without a microwave. The bathrooms were very small, and could be difficult for a larger person to move around in. The beds were outdated. The air conditioners were a little annoying, as they turned off and on quite often. We tried adjusting the temperature to see if that would help, but it didn't. The angle that the cold air blows out will freeze the unlucky soul that has to sleep in the bed right next to it. In our case, it was my husband, who is normally very hot blooded. He even complained that he was freezing most of the night. Our son, who slept in the other bed further from the air conditioner, complained that he got hot during the night, so the temperature in the room can vary greatly depending on where you're sleeping. We did not get to try any amenities due to our early morning schedule, so I cannot comment on how those were. The upside of this motel is that it's centrally located and you can walk to most nearby restaurants and shops from there. Overall, now that we've had the "experience" of staying on Route 66, I doubt we will spring for the cost of these mediocre rooms again. If it weren't for the location of this motel, they would NEVER get away with the rates they charge.

author: SantaFeSister
title: What's not to like?
text: We spent three nights in suite #3 and enjoyed the experience. Extremely clean. Two comfy queen-size beds. Quality toiletries, towels and bed linens. Two sinks in the bathroom. Kitchenette with micro, fridge, and full-size sink. Sofa and two chairs in living room. Large flat-screen TVs in both the living room and bedroom. Windows on both sides of each room, so lots of natural light. Free wifi that worked. Nice breakfast… we loved having raisin toast! Parking right outside our door. Shady portal in front of the lobby where you can sit and watch the world go by. Short walk down the street to good restaurants and bars. Easy hour's drive to the Grand Canyon. As for staff, Audrey the receptionist is a delight, and the housekeepers did a fine job. Only two minor niggles: the light over the tub in our bathroom was barely bright enough to see anything. And the breakfast area of the lobby was so crowded that it was hard to move around the tables. But those issues were not enough to spoil our stay.

author: aksharp1
title: Love it!
text: Stayed here for 2 nights on a larger queen room. Absolutely loved it! The staff at the front desk are very nice. The room was very nice and clean. Loved that they had extra coffee and cups for guests in the room so you don't run out on your first day. Loved having an electric fireplace. Just made the ambiance even more lovely. The bed was very plush and comfy. Many different type of pillows, not just feather pillows (which I hate). Bathroom had plenty of counter space for all of my stuff. Breakfast was small but sufficient. It filled me up. Had waffles, sausage, english muffins, breads, fruits. Location is awesome, can walk every where. I highly recommend this place.

author: curiousl8y
title: Pick The Lodge for its Comfort and Continental Breakfast!
text: We stayed in Williams for 1 night on the way to Santa Fe. We chose it on impulse, because it stood out from the usual chain motels in that area of town. Quick and easy check-in, friendly staff, good service. If you pick a 1 bed room, be aware it's going to be small. That being said, it was more than adequate and comfortable for a night's stay. Rooms are very clean and well maintained. The bed was comfortable, with several pillows ranging from fluffy to dense, so you can take your choice. The bath was modern and comfortable. The heater/air conditioner was quiet and worked efficiently. The TV is a good-sized flat screen with HDMI cable channels, very nice. The rooms all have cute names, and you park right outside your door. Off the lobby is a nice room for Continental Breakfast. It has the usual assortment, plus several waffle-makers, with waffle batter ready for use in the correct portions in individual plastic cups. Good waffles, and fun to make! All in all, an enjoyable stay.

author: CleveandKat
title: Love this little gem!
text: On old Route 66, the main attraction in Williams is it's convenient proximity to (about an hour’s drive via Hwy 64) The Grand Canyon and the Rail Road that can take you there. We booked a suite, as the rooms looked small in picks. The Lodge was clean and charmingly cozy. VERY comfy bed! We would stay here again. We got in at dusk, and Christmas lights were already lighting the streets and some restaurants. Check in was quick and friendly. The Red Raven was recommended for dinner. A short block and a half walk away. Excellent recommendation! The food was divine, the service warm and friendly, and the price surprisingly affordable . The next morning, free breakfast had a nice variety of pastries, waffles, fruit and yogurt. I’m gluten free by necessity, so grateful for the yogurt and fruit. It was uncrowded, but we were later than folks taking the train. Check-out was quick and painless too.

author: PalmTreeSeeker4ever
title: Cozy but clean...
text: We stayed here on our Route 66 trip after seeing the Grand Canyon. Of all the little towns that we stayed in, Williams was our favorite! Our hotel room (#11) was very small but clean. I appreciated not having the overwhelming smell of carpet fresh trying to cover up a musty smell, as we have experienced in some of the vintage hotels along 66. The bathroom was very clean with good water pressure. The toilet and shower were a separate room, with the sink being right off the bedroom. We sat out in the covered terrace and played cards which was very relaxing. The two fireplaces were not on, but it was too hot anyway. We had 3 items that bothered us just a little. 1- the tv remote did not have a "sleep" function . 2- If you were laying on the left side of the bed, the street light perfectly hit the pillow so that an orange light was in your eyes all night. A simple curtain on the sides of the blinds would fix that. 3- The right side side of the mattress was broken down I think and my husband kept feeling like he was rolling out. The office staff were all very nice and helpful. We did not use the breakfast, as we wanted a full breakfast before we hit the road. We would most definitely stay here again!

author: travellinjenna
title: Clean, Comfortable, Convenient
text: While this is an older property, it has been updated quite nicely. I had one of the lower priced rooms, #7 which is a basic motel room with 2 queen beds. Unlike the suites, this room doesn't have a fridge or microwave, just a coffee maker. If you are planning on staying more than one night you may consider upgrading to a larger room with more amenities. For me, the regular room suited my one night stay. The room was very clean (this is a no pets/no smoking property), although there was some dust behind the beds and furniture. The sink area is separate from the shower and toilet room. This makes your dressing area fairly large but your bathing area will feel cramped. The shower rod is one of those curved ones that extends quite a distance out. This wasn't a problem for me, but I would estimate that if you are on the tall side (around 6 feet) you will find the rod hits your head when you use the toilet. just fyi I am a light sleeper but did not notice much noise from either the adjoining rooms or the road. I did run the air-con all night so that helped with supplying white-noise. Breakfast was listed as continental but it was much more: Waffles, eggs, sausage, yogurt and a variety of breads to toast. The dining area is located off of the check-in desk. It is not especially large and could get very crowded as their sister motels also share the breakfast room. I would guess that the earlier breakfast time is the busiest as people head out early for the Grand Canyon (?) Despite being fully booked during my stay I did not have a problem with finding a table. My only "complaint" is the price. At about $150 a night it is probably the most expensive motel I've ever stayed at.

author: PalmSpringsVisitors
title: Lots of pluses, a few minuses
text: This was our first stop driving from the central coast of CA to OK. We love older, Route 66-type motels and so chose the Lodge. It is far enough away from the center of Williams to be quiet but not so far that you can't walk into town. The grounds and hotel are attractive, well kept, and very clean. After reading the reviews, we chose a room with 2 queen beds since reviewers thought the room with 1 queen was very small. Our room was fine; we slept on one bed and put our luggage on the other. The bed was comfortable, the sink area was spacious, and the shower/tub was adequate. The staff checking us in and out were friendly and professional. There were a few minuses. When checking in, I asked whether a king bed was available at an additional cost. Apparently, the king suite was available, but after trying for a few minutes, the staff member could not change our reservation (really?), so we stayed with our original room. The next morning I washed my hair, but the hair dryer didn't work. Since the office didn't open until 7am, we decided to pack the car and so took our luggage out. Unfortunately, our room keys didn't work so we couldn't get back in the room, and I was outside with wet hair! This would have been fine except it was cold and snowy on that May morning, so I waited in the cold car. At 7am, we went to the office to get a hair dryer and breakfast. The coffee was very good (we're Starbucks fans), and there was a nice assortment of breads and cereals. Unfortunately, the scrambled eggs were terrible--very dry and cold--and they had just been put out. We ended up going somewhere else for breakfast.

author: rcmal
title: Cozy and comfortable stay
text: Stopped over for one night on Easter Sunday prior to Grand Canyon. We arrived quite early at The Lodge, before 1pm and the front desk staff was so kind to check and see if the room was ready. It was and so we parked in front of our two queen room suite 400sq ft. It was small but a good layout. First room you enter has one queen bed, TV and a very small sitting area with a table, two chairs, counter area with fridge and microwave. My two teenage boys do not like to share a bed and so we brought with us a twin air mattress and it fit perfectly in the sitting area. There was no extra space to walk around with the twin bed inflated. The next room you enter is another queen bed with it's own TV. They have double sinks in a separate area which is nice as you could use the sink/vanity area while someone was in the bathroom. They have a very nice outdoor area with a fireplace and heat air curtains above that you can control by a timer switch. It was very quiet and somewhat like a ghost town due to the holiday. Very limited selection of stores and restaurants open. We went to Red Raven for dinner which was good. Wifi was spotty. Breakfast was included and was decent. They have two waffle makers. Would definitely recommend to family and friends.

author: scottb211
title: Better than I even expected
text: My wife and I wanted to get out of town for the weekend. It had been a few years since we'd been in Williams. After doing some research, we were really impressed with the reviews for the Lodge, it looked like the rooms had been remodeled and weren't your run-of-the-mill motel fare. We ended up with room # 19 ("Chicago"), which was a Queen suite. I was really surprised at how nice it was. It wasn't huge, but it was very nicely decorated. The bed was comfortable, both the sleeping area and the "living room" had flat screen TV's with DirecTV service, and there were two separate heaters. Plus, it's within a block or two of everything, so you don't need your car to get around. There's a nice continental breakfast (including waffles), and chairs out front if you want to watch the traffic roll slowly by. Tips: - Our room (19) was the closest to the street, so there is some traffic noise as cars rolled by. - As other people have mentioned, Williams is a town with trains. So if that is the kind of thing that will wake you up, bring earplugs. - Our room had two heaters. I retrospect, we should have used the heater in the main room at night to heat the room and NOT the one next to the bed. Because it works. Very well. So much so when it would come on we felt like we were next to a blast furnace. It would have been better to just use the comfy sleeping bag comforter they provided. In any case, we were exhausted from walking around (and a couple draft beers here and there) so we slept well regardless.

author: cared_12
title: Cute, Clean, and Affordable
text: My family of five recently stayed two nights at the Lodge in Williams. Our experience was great. We spoke with three desk clerks during our stay, each one more cheery and helpful than the last. Our room was cute and clean, but on the small side. This is, after all, a relic from the 1950's when a bed and a toilet were all one was looking for in a motel. But that is part of the fun of staying on Route 66! The breakfast area was clean and well stocked with the expected items, including fresh scrambled eggs and sausage. The outside area, which included a seating area around a fireplace, looked comfy. I'm sad to say it was too cold on the nights were there to even sit out by a fire. I would have liked to have spent some of our evening there. A word to the wise, be sure to have a cell phone, there are no phones in the room. Also, the train runs very near by and sounds it's horn at night; I wish I had thought to bring ear plugs. And a word to hotel management, a lock on the bathroom doors would be nice. In such tight quarters, you would not think that "hey, I'm in here" would be necessary, bit surprisingly it is! As for the town of Williams itself, we had fun walking the main street and poking around the little shops. Maybe it was because we visited in the off-season, or maybe because of the impending storm, but many of the shops were closed when we passed by, which was at about 7pm on Friday and Saturday nights. All restaurants were open, however. About an hour in the car is all it takes to place you in front of The Grand Canyon. We will return, and when we do, I will be sure to book a room at The Lodge.

author: R2NAZ
title: This place is so adorable
text: We are so happy we stayed here, so much so that we are planning a trip back soon. We were only in town for one night to ride the Polar Express with our son. I booked this little gem 6 months ago because we wanted something quaint and comfortable at a reasonable price. This place did not disapoint! We traveled from PHX the morning of our scheduled train ride and arrived a bit earlier than normal check in. No problem, everything was ready & waiting for us. We had a spacious 2 room suite. The bed & bath are in one room with a closeable door & the kitchen & couch/bed are in the other room. Both rooms had a tv with satalite and lots of channels. The kitchenette had a mini fridge & microwave plus a bar height table & chairs. There was plenty of space to spread out & relax. The king bed was mostly comfortable (every time someone moves you can feel it) and the lighting was adequate. One suggestion would be to bring a sleep mask if lights keep you awake. The parking lot lights come right through the blinds so it makes it a bit hard to sleep. We didn’t have time to enjoy the outdoor fireplaces but love the idea of them for our next visit. Breakfast was yummy with normal continental plus waffles, sausage and eggs. This hotel & the one directly across from it are owned by the same people and both have a well loved & well taken care of appearance.

author: diamondking64
title: Needs a few tweaks
text: We've been here three times now and make it our place to stay in Williams. A few things could be improved: Wi-Fi was weak in our room. My iPhone found the network, the password was entered but the connection was lost a few seconds after. Also, the bathroom soaps could be upgraded to better smelling varieties. They also feel rough on the skin. For showering, the water pressure got very weak sometimes, almost to a trickle. Another suggestion is switch to better in-room coffee. The cup I had was maybe the worst ever. All-in-all though, the Lodge is terrific. We stayed in a two BR suite this time and loved it. DirecTV is a great add. The beds are very comfortable and the rooms were quiet. There is some talking from the outside courtyard but nothing too rowdy or after 11pm. We truly believe this is the best place to stay in this quaint little town on old Route 66. New amenities with an old-time feel. We'll be back.

author: 358joelb
title: Nice Motel, Good Location
text: I was hesitant to stay here at first being that I never have stayed in a motel before. I will say I am pleased with the rooms at this location. I stayed in room 3, named "Newberry Springs"; it was a decently sized suite with a sofa bed, kitchenette, two queen beds and enough space to accommodate three toddlers and two adults. The price was good especially being that the rooms seemed modern, not to mention that the rooms were VERY clean. The staff was very friendly and helpful as well. Breakfast is provided in the mornings and it is just as good as the Garden Inn, or Best Western. While I ate breakfast here I found it easier to take my family of five to the Pine Country restaurant a few blocks away. The location is extremely convenient; for the price of a basic room at the Grand Canyon hotel which I believe is over-rated I had a suite that was within a few blocks walking distance from the Polar Express and other shops/restaurants/bars in the town. -The only things I can point out that annoyed me are thin walls (occupants of the adjacent room decided to have a drunken argument at 0200 until one finally decided to storm out), however I can say that about all of the hotels [thin walls] I have stayed at, in the late evenings every noise can be heard. - Lack of privacy; the doors to the bedroom or bathroom had no way of locking them. I also maintained the blinds closed because the units faced parking lots, so everyone walking/driving by can see into your room. - There are not phones or an iron/ironing board in the rooms. Any phone calls to the hotel staff were to be made via your cell phone or you can walk to the office. The things I pointed out above are relatively minor observances that I think others would like to know about (which had deterred me from staying in similar places in the past). Overall I enjoyed my stay, it was a first for me, and I will surely return here if I need a place to stay when passing by.

author: FyF_13
title: Motel OK. Will return
text: In Williams there is a lot of motels. The Lodge at Route 66 is an OK place too stay. Rooms are small but quality is good. It is clean and beds good. The rates may be at the high end compared to the competitors. Location is OK if Route 66 and/or Grand canyon is the goal. No fridge though. WIFI in rooms with OK quality. Parking good and free. No Swimming pool. Good free Breakfast included. Room and motel is clean. Location is Good. Service level is OK. Surrounding area is fine and fairly safe. Take a stroll. Will I return? Yes.

author: OCBluejay
title: The Lodge...a GREAT stay for touring Grand Canyon.
text: This little gem of a motel in Williams gave a us a perfect home base for touring the Grand Canyon and Meteor Crater this past week. Williams is a quaint little town that has no outside "big" chain eateries or coffee houses (save for the fast food places that are visible from the I-40). As you drive under their welcoming signage, you instantly feel the classic, nostalgic essence of this small, railroad town. They do have family/resident owned business who pride themselves on making your stay pleasant. The restaurants are unique and accessible by foot. The Lodge was comfortably redone and modernized. It is a quite motel as I only heard the train whistles when I opened the door. We stayed for 2 nights in a double Queen room and then moved to a King suite for our third and final night (our double Queen was already spoken for the weekend) The dQueen room will remind you of the throw back motel set up with no closet but a rack to hang your clothes....very Route 66!! My husband kept reminiscing about his childhood days and how his dad would drive back and forth on the Route to Alabama from Cali.....driving until he was tired in the night to pull into "VACANCY" signed motel like this one. He loved that I picked this motel!!! The beds do take up a lot of the room but you are not there to ballroom dance but to sleep. Then we moved to the King suite. The room was a corner room and had a lot of space with an ample Kitchenette, Kerig coffee maker and table. The bedroom was separated by French doors. I asked my daughter which did she prefer, her own Queen bed or the pull out with the living room and large flat screen to herself. She liked having her own space in the King suite. So if you are looking for more space go for the suites.

author: AZFamilyman
title: The front is 66 historic, the rooms modern appointed!!
text: The lodge on Route 66 in Williams AZ is a total score that I found on TripAdviser. It has the old historic Route 66 classic front and parking. Williams is safe so the door to the outside is a plus. You literally park in front of your room. There is no hallway noise; in fact this is the quietest hotel in town. It is at the east end of the Route 66 shops and restaurants so it is walking distance to all the fun. We stayed in a King Suite (450 sq. ft.) that was totally demo’d and remodeled with modern appointments and was extremely clean. They took 2 standard rooms closed off an outside door and put a pair of doors leading into the bedroom and master bath section. The bed is a pillow top. The bath has a travertine double basin vanity with hot water and good pressure. The toilet and shower are in a separate room. There is a refrigerator, microwave, Keurig, kitchen sink and cabinets. There are 2 big screen TVs with DirecTV and Wi-Fi for guests only. It is a long way from I-40 so there is no highway noise and the only train noise is the Grand Canyon Railroad horn in the morning before they leave. The continental breakfast is top quality with self-cooked Belgium waffles, percolator coffee, sausage patties, various toasts, pastries, fruits, yogurt, OJ and plenty of seating. There is a cool patio area in the center of the courtyard. The staff is very friendly and helpful. The only gripe I have is the lack of blackout blinds in the master bedroom.

author: rlpack1956
title: Could have been a "5" but.....
text: This is a really great place! The property is well maintained and neat as a pin. The room was nice, clean and amazingly comfortable. The bed was very luxurious and had wonderful linens. There is a nice covered patio with two fireplaces just outside the rooms. Check in was seamless and professional. The place is surprisingly quiet for being on old 66. The Lodge on Route 66 would have gotten a solid, no questions "5" except for one thing. The breakfast they offer has no milk. No milk?!? Who has no milk for breakfast?! There were 2 quarts of Coffee Mate (one original, one some God-awful flavor) on the counter. Thinking they might just be out, I asked the Guest Assistant if they had any milk. She replied, "We don't carry milk". SO if you like milk in your coffee or like a glass in the morning, stop by a Kwik-Stop and buy a quart before you check in.

author: ChurchMouse2010
title: Quaint updated motel
text: We had little idea what to expect. We usually stay in a chain hotel. We found this place to be a quaint motor court motel. We had a queen room. It was small, but that's the way they used to be. It was well maintained, seemed to be recently painted and carpeted. There is a nice patio area with two gas log fireplaces and overhead heaters, with little gardens on both ends of the patio. We would have rather had a desk in the room than the dresser. It is a short walk into the downtown area, which is very easy to walk. The train station is about 4 short blocks away. They offer a continental breakfast. On the day we stayed there was a waffle station, sausages, bread, Danish, oatmeal, yogurt, OJ and of course coffee. There were no cold cereals if that is what you prefer. The motel across the street is affiliated with this hotel, and they share the continental breakfast. Overall, it was a nice place to stay, feel a bit of nostalgia from the motor court days, and the patio was a great place to spend the evening after dining out in town.

author: SWMKerman
title: Great stay....Did not disappoint us.
text: This was our third year in a row to Williams. We love the area and it is a break in the day when we are traveling 10 hours. We have stayed in some dumps over the last couple years in Williams, and we spent a little bit more money to stay in this place. We were not disappointed. The gals in the front office, Cindy and Audrey were kind,courteous, friendly and very helpful. They were quick yo get us checked in and recommended a couple places to go. Since we were in on a Saturday, the rate was a little bit higher than i would have liked to spend, but it was a very comfortable room. The bed was just right and it was clean. They even finished polishing the furniture. IT JUST FELT CLEAN. The bathroom was in good condition, and you did not feel like you had to walk around in shoes. We were in walking distance to what ever you had your heart on. We had 4 people in our party, but the room with 2 queens was the biggest that they had. No big deal. I wished i could have been bigger. The continental breakfast wasn't fancy, but it was good for us. We enjoyed the furniture on the outside of the office to sit and lounge and read. All in all, i would come back here again and would highly recommend this hotel to all.Just see the girls there and they will take care of you.

author: Californian2
title: Perfection on Route 66
text: I don't know what the sourpuss from Norway or the fuss budget from Houston (reviews from July 1 and 2, 2013) are complaining about; this place is a great find! I chose to make a reservation here after seeing reviews on Trip Advisor and also thanks to the motel's own website. I liked the photos, and am happy to report that they do not misrepresent. The room descriptions were clear, including square footage, so it was easy to choose the right one for our needs (if you're not from Norway!). I won't tell you which room we reserved, because I don't want to spoil our chances of finding it available next time! Suffice it to say that when designing the rooms, the owners thought of everything to make their guests comfortable. We were only in town for two nights, but agreed that we'd have been comfortable there for months. Our room had French doors closing off the bedroom from a cozy living room and eat-in kitchenette. The bedroom had its own seating area with additional television, and we enjoyed watching an old movie from bed one evening. Oh, and the bed was extremely comfortable! Much more so than that at the $500/night hotel we'd just stayed in the night before! Our bathroom had two separate vanities with sinks, a nice soaking/whirlpool tub, and a double shower. There were plush bathrobes, and I didn't have to call the front desk for an extra luggage rack, as I do everywhere else, because they already had two in the room! We don't rise before ten, so I can't include breakfast in my review. I'm sure it would have been nice. The staff are friendly and caring, and there is plenty of information in the front office to guide you to local attractions.

author: TobyK643
title: Impeccable, quaint, and small.
text: As everybody says, the rooms are small. Two of us had to do a bit of dancing around each other in the bathroom area in the morning, and there isn't any desk or sitting area besides the bed. Not for the business traveler who wants to get some work done. BUT, the room was wonderfully decorated, from the towel hooks to the appropriately sized TV for the room. They make the best use of the space that is available and the interior design was pretty great. Even the room door was fancied up. Now for the important stuff...the bed was the most comfortable hotel bed we have ever slept in, with the softest sheets also. Also, the room was very quiet, even though we had folks in the rooms adjacent to ours. Most importantly,they had a button on the air conditioner unit for constant fan. No longer do you have to choose between a cool sleeping temperature and soothing white noise. The evening desk staff person was great and check in was fast. I would gladly stay here again when in williams. I wasn't a fan of the instant oatmeal packets, most places have an urn of warmed oatmeal and some jars of brown sugar and raisins. The orange juice was plentiful, but no eggs, sausage, nor bacon...true continental. The danishes were fresh and very soft. We not big on breakfast anyway, so it didn't ruin our experience. 4 out of 5 due to room size.

author: BenGruda
title: Nice, but more of the same
text: My wife and I stayed here for 2 nights while we explored the Grand Canyon. The location is great, and you are within walking distance to basically all of downtown Williams. Other Tripadvisors seem to really like this place. Well, it is nice. We had two queens in our room, one wooden chair, TV, and you pretty much had to squeeze past everything when you got around. A coat rack with hangers were the only storage, so we used the other bed to lay our clothes, etc. on. Pretty tight quarters, so if you plan on relaxing in your room, except in the bed, forget about it! Beds were comfortable, and decor was tasteful, but the wood made the room really dark. Continental breakfast was just that. A waffle maker, toast, muffins, instant oatmeal, cereal, etc. You know the drill. No real hot entrees except waffles and the hot water you added to your oatmeal. Coffee was just barely passable for me, and I drink a lot of java! In short, unless all the other places in town are horrible which could very well be possible, I just don't get what all the hype is about. Would I stay there again? Sure, but don't expect much more than you get at any other decent drive up motel.

author: mdrich11
title: Warm, Comfortable, Inviting....
text: This was our third stop on our recent Route 66 adventure. We decided to stay here based on the reviews we read on Tripadvisor and MAN were we not disappointed! Upon pulling into the parking lot, one immediately feels the 'old, nostalgic' vibe of the classic Route 66 motor inn.All the rooms are named after iconic towns located on the Mother Road and we were placed in the 'Seligman' room. I was expecting to walk into the room and be greeted with the old musty smell that goes with staying in one of these old classic motels.and boy was I ever wrong!!. The rooms seem to have been recently remodeled as mine was arguably the NICEST and CLEANEST room I have EVER stayed in. Everything in the room seemed to be new, including furniture, mattress, plumbing fixtures, tile, carpet, etc. .And the mattress was VERY comfortable. The room had a rustic decor that fit the area perfectly and gave the room a warm, pleasant feel. It felt very inviting. The room was a tad bit small, but so were all rooms in the motor inns of olden days. Not small enough to be a problem though....just a TAD bit. The wife and I were traveling alone and the place had a really nice nostalgic/romantic feel to it. It would also make a perfect place for the vacationing family. The atmosphere is PERFECT. I am not one to usually inform the staff of how nice of a place they have, but I made it a point to stop by the lobby before I left to tell them thanks for the wonderful experience. And speaking of the staff.....they were as frendly and welcoming as one could ever wish for. We asked the front dest attendant to recommend a place to eat, and the place they recommended was exceptional! The wife and I have only one regret about this stay.......it wasn't long enough. If we're ever in the Williams, AZ area again, you can bet this is the place we will stay. I give it an A++.THANKS!!!

author: Bob1949
title: A good option for Williams
text: We enjoyed our two night stay at The Lodge in Williams prior to the train to the Grand Canyon. Williams is an ideal stop over if the Grand Canyon is your aim, particularly by train. We booked one of their larger rooms and it was spacious with a separate sitting room, bedroom with large and very comfortable king sized bed and separate bath/shower room. Strangely the washbasin was part of the bedroom and the toilet had a very noisy fan whenever the light was switched on which caused a few problems in the middle of the night! There is probably too much bulky furniture in the sitting area but is was fine and the integral kitchen area was useful. The heating system was very efficient. Wifi was fast and easy to use. The Lodge is well located for getting to the train depot and the restaurants/bars on the main street. We ate at the Singing Pig (bar area adjoining) and food and atmosphere were OK, see separate review. We also ate at the Red Raven and this was much more of an occasion and not particularly expensive. Car parking at The Lodge is very convenient right outside your room. My one criticism would be with regard to the breakfasts. Part of the Lodge seems to be across the street and the one morning we were there it was sold out and breakfast was totally chaotic and an unpleasant experience. The next day it was quieter but still unpleasant in a dining area off Reception that is cluttered with a basic range of food and insufficient toasters etc. All in all, a convenient and comfortable stay to visit the Grand Canyon and it represented fair value for money. However, if you want a peaceful location as a couple, be aware that it seemed to attract families with very young children, at least whilst we were there.

author: DaisyChain1968
title: Cute and Comfortable
text: We stayed here for 2 nights in June 2012 as a pit stop for the Grand Canyon. I chose it due to the mainly positive reviews from Trip Advisor. Rooms are quite small, basic but tastefully decorated. We were four in a room with two very high and sturdy larger than average Queen beds so the room felt smaller as we filled it ourselves. You are able to park your vehicle right outside the door so we kept much of our clutter in the trunk of the car to give us more space. Also, the fact that you can open the door and sit outside on patio chairs does give you a bit more room. The sink/ wash area of the bathroom is outside of the bathroom so it's handy if somebody is in the shower and you need the mirror, basin or hairdryer. Free Breakfast is served just off the reception area in a pleasant room. Much of the usual continental style menu is served and is quite nice- it starts at 8am which is a little bit late if you want to make an early start for the Grand Canyon like we did. Internet is free which is good. Williams is a very small town, very quaint and delightful. This motel is on the main street of it and everything is within walking distance. Our only complaint would be that the air conditioning unit is under the window very close to one of the beds and is very tough on the person sleeping nearest to it. We tried opening the window but they are bolted shut and even covering the 'blast' with towels to make the cool air less fierce but my husband still managed to catch a nasty cold. Without it the room was very stuffy at the end of June. Grand Canyon is around an hours drive away.

author: zimaaaaah
title: Great stay on Route 66
text: Stayed here for one night before heading to Grand Canyon with family. Hotel was exactly as pictured on website. Furnished and decorated nicely with a "lodge" touch. Room had Queen bed in one room and a sofa bed in another with the kitchenette/living area. Plenty of space for the four of us. The beds and pillows were super comfy. Extremely clean and well kept property. Loved that we literally parked outside the door of the room. Location was very convenient to the historic part of Williams. We did hear the trains a few times at night, but I think you would have that any where in Williams. The breakfast was very light; a little too light for our taste. Check-in was easy and quick. Kind of neat that you get real keys; not a plastic card. Check out was a breeze and they even let us leave our car there the next day while we were touring with Marvelous Marv's Grand Canyon Tours. (review coming soon) All in all, great stay for family and would be perfect for a couples getaway.

author: geezersgirl
title: Simply Great!
text: I booked one night at the Lodge on Route 66 based on the reviews here on Trip Advisor. We were just beginning our long road trip from California to points in the midwest. We checked in around 3 and were given the Oklahoma room, This is one of the smallest rooms on the property which was fine with us since we were only there for one night. The room was perfect. Southwest in design and really cute. There was a queen bed & bath with separate vanity area. It was a scorcher of a day but the a/c in this room was a beast and kept the room downright chilly. The property is located smack dab in the middle of downtown where all the action is, After getting settled in we decided to check out the town and grab some dinner. The front desk pointed us in the right direction to the Red Raven just down the block. Dinner there was absolutely delicious! It was all I could do to not lick the plate. Headed back to our room and settled in for the night, One thing missing in this room is any sort of closet. That was not a problem for us but if I was stayng more than one night I would want one. The bed was really comfy and my hubby liked the flat screen tv. We were up bright and early to get on the road. They do serve a free continental breakfast but do not set it up until 7:30. So we headed across the street to the coffee bar to get our caffeine fix. I would deifinitely stay here again, The staff is super friendly and helpful, in fact 400 miles down the road we discovered that we had left our memory phone pillows in our room. We called the front desk and they had already bagged them up and had them ready to send to us. We had them hold them and picked them up on our way home 12 days later.

author: travelpatty22
title: Lovely little gem...
text: Thanks to TA reviews we made reservations to stay here the night before we went to the Grand Canyon. It was a good choice! The room was charming--not the typical chain hotel decor. It was clean and the bed was wonderful. Nice large bath/dressing area, but small room. It was fine as we just wanted a place to sleep. It was too cool to enjoy the gazebo and firepit area. The owners were delightful and helpful. The breakfast was amazing for the small area they have. Very simple, but adequate--cereal, oatmeal, pastries, toast, fruit, juice, etc. Everything was presented so nicely--almost felt like guests at a B&B. We had had a big, yummy lunch at In & Out Burgers in Las Vegas, where we flew in, so wanted something light for dinner. Went to the Safeway to pick up stuff for lunches the next few days and were pleasantly surprised...it is a lovely store. They had a great selection of salads, soups and sandwiches at lunch time, but deli not open at dinner. They do have some salads and stuff prepackaged there and the ones we had were delicious and just what we wanted. Our stay in Williams was very nice, except for the cold weather!

author: wskungfuclub
title: williams doesn't have a lot of choices, but this place ain't bad...
text: went to williams to do the polar express thing with the whole family and my sister's whole family. she booked the whole trip so i had no clue about the hotel before hand. on the outside the lodge on route 66 looked like a run down motel--but it fit right in with the whole rustic route 66 scenery. we got 3 rooms. 2 basic ones for parents and a suite for the grandparents and kids to stay in. the basic room was tiny and no frills. the bed was comfortable and everything was very clean. the heater worked great. the suite was actually pretty nice. it had a table large enough to play cards on, and a small kitchenette. the living room area had a fold out sofa and it was very comfortable. the lodge is great for what it was. this isn't a luxury 5 star hotel with spa, gym, and business center. this is a nice comfortable place where you can get a good night's sleep and enjoy the rest of what williams, az has to offer. there's plenty to do for a few days with the grand canyon and the train rides nearby. overall our whole family enjoyed our stay there. we had no issues and no complaints.

author: TrainMikeJ
title: Definitely the Best on Route 66!
text: My girlfriend and I stayed one night before taking the Grand Canyon Railway the following morning (also a worthwhile stop in Williams!). We arrived at around 9pm after a long drive from Phoenix, AZ. The gentleman on the desk was very pleasant and quick to check us in. We had pre-booked our room months ahead of time and got a standard room with a Queen sized bed for $79. The bed was incredibly comfortable! Our room was right beside the ice maker room but I didn't hear anything all night. The room had a nice assortment of channels available on DirectTV. Not all channels were enabled, but enough to be able to pass the time away before bed. The room had a standard 27" TV. Breakfast consisted of prepackaged donuts/danishes, hot cereal, coffee, and juice. It was more than enough to wait the couple of hours for the train departure and the included breakfast in our ticket. My only minor complaint is that the room heater is a little touchy on the temperature setting but not enough to change the 5 rating I have given. Whomever was complaining about room size, you can clearly see on the motel's website what the room looks like. True, the standard rooms do not have a lot of extra room around the bed, but there is lots of space under the bathroom counter and a suitcase stand was in our room. Would I come back here? DEFINITELY! When you look at the "lower standard" motels along the route, this one is a no brainer. I went to Williams for the train, not for the hotel/motel. Stay here if you're riding the train, not the train's overpriced hotel in WIlliams. Much better bang for your dollar.

author: humbus
title: Wonderful!
text: I found this hotel on the internet, read the reviews and thought we would give it a try. My family went to Williams to go on the Polar Express, so we only needed one night. I decided to splerge and stay in the executive suite since we had 2 children with us. It was fabulous! Very cozy, decorated very nicely, great attention to detail. The bathroom had a jacuzzi tub, which was nice, but a bit small. The shower was very large and had two shower heads. The only complaint I had would be, the towels were rather thin, could have been a bit more luxurious. The bedroom was nice with a fireplace and the bed was very comfortable. There were french doors that lead into the living area with a sofa sleeper for the kids. The staff was very friendly and helpful. They offered a continental breakfast, which I would have to say was very limited. Maybe it was the time of year, but they only offered packaged doughnuts and danishes, packaged oatmeal and coffee. No juices or cereals or anything fresh. A little dissapointing compared to everything else. However I would definalty stay here again and just go somewhere else for breakfast.

author: BillyRay31
title: Upscale, Renovated Motor Lodge from Yesterday. First Class.
text: A great, great Stay. This a a motor lodge on old Route 66, that has been renovated and made very, very nice. My wife and I are very picky, and we loved this place. On the outside, it is a beautiful, adobe-stucco motor lodge. On the inside, it is renovated and and upscale. We rented a suite, which was two rooms made into one big unit. We had two queen beds, with very nice linens, as well as a full sized pull out sofa bed. We had 2 adults and 3 kids (8, 10, and 12). We had plenty of room. Williams, Az. is a good alternative for visits to the Grand Canyon. It is a very nice, small town in the mountains of Arizona. There are numerious shops. The Grand Canyon Railway is right accross the street from the Lodge. We chose to drive to Flagstaff and on to the south rim, to drive the entire 27 mile rim road. That was quite fun, ending the day at the Village to eat dinner and watch the sunset. Williams is close enough (60 miles) to use it as a base for multi day trips. The Lodge on Route 66 has much nicer accomodations than anything at the Park or even outside the park closeby. If we ever make this trip again, this motel will be where we will stay. Billy Ray Lawerenceville, Georgia

author: N8642MCamyr
title: Definitely luxurious and affordable
text: My husband and I booked a king suite during our recent vacation to Arizona. When I spoke to Theresa on the phone I mentioned that we were coming out for our 20th anniversary. Sure enough, when we entered our suite we found a bottle of champagne on ice with two fancy glasses! What a nice surprise! Although The Lodge doesn't offer any AAA discount, we were able to use our AARP card to take 5% off the rate. For about $125 per night we had a nice-sized two room suite with an extremely comfortable king-sized bed. The living room had a wonderful couch, and there was a kitchen area with a fridge and microwave. The bath area was huge, with two sinks in one area and the tub and toilet in a separate room. All fixtures were beautiful and of high quality. We were especially impressed with the comfort of the bed and the lack of noise in the suite. Check-in and check-out were a breeze, and it's very convenient that you can park the car right outside your door! As others have said, breakfast is served in a little patio area in the center of the motel complex. Although the food provided was mainly packaged fare, the coffee and decaf were excellent. We were very impressed with the way Theresa went out of her way to make our stay comfortable. She has a wonderful personality and is fun to talk to. I would definitely recommend the Lodge to anyone looking for more than just the standard motel room in Williams.

author: grahamkuk
title: Our best accommodation along Route 66
text: I booked this refurbished motel based upon trip advisor reviews and the information at the Lodge's own website. The suite we booked had extremely comfortable twin queens beds in a bedroom off the lounge/kitchen. The bedroom had a small dressing area with twin wash basins and off that there was the shower room (good strong shower too) and w/c. The lounge featured a comfortable sofabed, armchairs, TV, a dining table + 4 chairs and a kitchen area with all the mod cons. A complimentary breakfast was served in the covered area shared by all of the rooms - a good selection and more than enough to feed all 5 of us. (See the photos at their website). Reception is in the nice little shop at the front of the property. Booking at the moment is by e-mail but online direct booking will be available soon according to the owners - I think that when this is available this wonderful motel will be booked out quickly. The property is a typical small single storey motel completely refurbished by the owners just over two years ago and what a marvellous job they have done. Across the road the owners are now busy refurbishing another old motel which will feature lots of neon when it opens in 2007. The location is on the main street in Williams so you can walk to everything in town. This is our third visit to Williams and the town gets better every time. Williams is the only place along Route 66 where the whole town is being regenerated on the back of the Route 66 thing. Keep up the great work. We stayed here as part of our drive along the whole of Route 66 and we all agreed that this is our favourite of all of the hotels/motels we stayed in. Our only negative comment and easily fixed is the door to the w/c shower didn't have a lock. Highly recommended and this is where we would stay again next time we are in Williams.

author: ccm404ds
title: Really nice place to stay - close to bottom of slope & all amenities.
text: We had accommodation set for five but as there were two of us so it was perfect. The self catering equipment was adequate and the dishwasher was great. Fridge even had a freezer section and didn't expect a 4 ring electric hob. Microwave was handy. Note that you have to lock the main door with the key - 2 supplied. Each room has a ski locker room and was great - may be tight for 5 pairs though. Our only complaint was the smell in the kitchen and toilet, possibly due to the extractor fans. Our room overlooked the rear of the skiing resort but was fine for us as no traffic or noisy people at road level. Couldn't get TV to work and heating controls are fiddly but warmed the room up no problem. They provided towels, bedding covers, etc, dishwasher tablets, washing up soap, cloth and drying cloths. The pillows aren't great. There are two supermarkets nearby: a Spar, with a bakery nearby for the fresh bread, croissants, etc.) is up the road about 200m on the left. The other is in the Forum area down the lift. Ski lifts and slopes were great and the nearest chair/ magic carpet is 200m down the road. Food and drink was quite expensive but expected. The small cafe/restaurant, Sucre Sale, was excellent and we all (group of 8 adults) loved it. There are several to chose from. We would happily go back but, as we prefer to try other resorts, it may not happen for a few years. Gave it a 4 but it was close to a 5. Highly recommended.

author: GlenB885
title: JUST RIGHT
text: We had accommodation set for five. This would be cramped but for two or three, perfect. The self catering equipment was adequate and dishwasher was an useful addition. Fridge even froze the ice cubes and the electric four ring cooker did its job and even on a very low simmer. Tip: you have to lock the main door, it does not self lock! Ski locker room available and useful. Only complaint is that the kitchen and bathroom extractor fans didn't work so cooking smells and steam stayed around. We had a room over looking the rear of the skiing resort but not unpleasant as it was a quiet road and a little used button lift dragging past. TV and heating controls need playing with but fine once you know what button to press and when. Failed on the microwave/grill oven even with the instructions. They provided us with towels, bedding covers etc, dishwasher tablets, washing up soap, cloth and drying cloths. There are two supermarkets near by. Spar (this also has the bakery for the fresh bread, croissants and sugary stuff you just dont say no to) is out the apartment, turn right and up the road about 200m. Another is out of the apartment, cross the road and down the steps in front of you and cross the next road to a passenger lift to the base of Flaine skiing start point, turn left and a small shopping center is ahead of you. Ski lifts and slopes are great and only about 200m from the apartment. Food and drink is quite expensive but to be expected and there are enough to chose from. For us this apartment was just right and no real complaints and happily go back or recommend.

author: phoebes582
title: Skiing holiday - recommend
text: We recently stayed at Res La Foret for a week skiing holiday from 7-14 January 2017. We were pleasantly surprised with the hotel, welcomed by polite and friendly reception staff who spoke very good English. The reception area was spacious, warm and nicely furnished with plenty of seating, the reception hours are slightly odd and vary but as long as you check times beforehand you should be fine. We arrived at approx 4pm and were advised the rooms are usually ready at 5pm for new guests, the lady on reception made a phone call however and confirmed our apartment was ready so we could head up early and unpack. It wouldn't have been a problem if we had had to wait however as the free wifi in the hotel was good and reception allow you to leave luggage with them if you want to explore a bit. The 2 of us headed up the lift to a type D apartment, 5th floor, that sleeps up to 5 people. Having been to self catering apartments for skiing before we were happy that Res La Foret apartments were a generous size, a separate toilet to the bathroom was handy as well meaning there was no arguing over using the loo/shower. The apartment was clean and practical, all necessities supplied, a bonus that there was a small kitchen cleaning kit (washing up liquid, sponge, cloth etc) toilet roll and bin bags supplied, it's always hit and miss how far a hotel takes the phrase self catering! As a couple we used the double sofa bed in the living area for the week and left the bedroom for our suitcases, clothes and kit. The apartment would have been slightly cramped I imagine with 5 people sleeping in it and all ski/boarding kit for each person. The TV has English channels if you search, the wifi is good, kitchen supplying pots, pans, cutlery, glasses etc and decent sized mugs (used to these type of hotels offering espresso sized mugs and having to take our own). The locker rooms are large and warm, some apartments seemed to have 2 lockers assigned to them whereas ours only had the one, again this would have been cramped with more than 2 sets of kits in there. There was a water leak above our locker room but this was fixed within 24 hours of appearing. We had the fuse blow all electrics in our apartment on our last night and my partner went to reception,despite the lady working just closing at the end of her shift she came to our room and ensured maintenance were on their way to fix it before going home. Overall very satisfied with the hotel and we had a very comfortable stay. There is a ski rental shop right next door (25% off for hotel residents, don't forget a credit/debit card if renting kit) the shops 5 minute walk to the right of the hotel, a lift to the lower level directly in front of the hotel and the piste was a 5 minute walk to the left of the hotel so perfect location. We were worried about the skiing conditions as the snow report had been dismal and not all runs or lifts open, the risk you take booking early January. The first day we were again surprised with how well maintained the open slopes were and that night welcomed a dumping of snow, this lasted us comfortably until Thursday when we had continual snow for 24-48 hours and there was powder everywhere, brilliant conditions for skiers and snowboarders alike, more and more runs were opening the longer we stayed and all staff involved diligently maintained the already open slopes. We did not have a bad run all week and couldn't have been happier, we left flaine very happy and would definitely return in the future to hopefully ski the whole grand massif area as opposed to just the flaine area and will look to book at res la foret again when we do.

author: W9387YPdanm
title: Ok. Could be loads better
text: If you want location and aren't bothered about luxuries, this is the place for you! I booked a room for 7 of us and paid extra for guaranteed sofa beds??? The apartment layout is quite user friendly with two bedrooms (1xdbl bed) (3x single) and a living room with two single sofa beds. Then there's two bathrooms one with a bath and basin and one with a shower and a loo. Then an additional toilet separate. The kitchen is small and basic which tends to be the case with these places. NO OVEN but does have a microwave oven and dishwasher. The views are awesome if you get a south facing room with views of the facing mountings and most of the pistes. Parking is at the rear of the hotel (give yourself plenty of time to dig your way out of the snow as it isn't covered). We had a few gripes while we were there which I'm sure you wouldn't get in other hotels if you're prepared to pay a little more. -shower heads held on by last occupants shoe lace -beds aren't comfortable to most people over 10st -eggy drainage smell on occasions -room for 7 adults but only space for 5 boots on boot heater locker. -reception is closed throughout the day on most days -receptionist was friendly at check in, but when you ask for help, just fix it yourself. -wifi didn't work for 4 days. I think if they just changed their attitude as A hotel on the whole and raised their game a little bit, this would be a great hotel in a premium location. Unfortunately it's big and I'm sure they get the turnover with little overheads so they are happy. If I were to return, I'd try the newer Pierre Vacances d'Eos just slightly up the hill. For £100pp more you get much nicer rooms, elevated situation, pool, free shuttles anywhere in Flaine. It looks good.

author: AmsterdamSusie
title: Worst service, billed us for EVERYTHING
