text: First of all, DON'T go here!!!!!! We stayed here with friends during our ski-holiday. It started when we arrived at 8 o'clock, the room would be ready at 4 but the manager was really unreasonble and they helped us at 5. We waited in the lobby and the manager again asked us if we could be quiet because they were 'working'. The toilet and the reception was closed. The rooms were fine but not special. And the showers were cold. During our stay the manager did not first warn us of noise complaints but she just gave us a fine of 200€ per room. There was not a possibility to discuss this with her. We could not make any sound after ten o'clock anymore and there was security walking in our aisle. We whispered in our room and walked without shoes because we would be kicked out otherwise. Then the worst part, the check-out, a really unfriendly women came to check the room and everything was our fault. She billed us for the following things: - trash can with a tiny scratch €72,50 - lost key 85€ - little chair with broken leg €120 - smoking fine 200€ - extra bed that was not placed in our room but should have been there, manager told us we lost the bed?? €120 - broken door €220 There was again no possibility for a discussion and we were not taken seriously. We have never met such unfriendly staff!! Our holiday has ended in a very expensive way due to this weird way of handling. DON'T go to this residence!!

author: richardhP8952US
title: could be better...
text: Checked in well before the normal 5pm time and avoided the scrum, but no key available until well after 5pm. The room was still being mopped when we arrived at it. The apartment (301) was very small for the Superior 6/7*booked –smaller than our 2015 6/7* apartment (524) and only 1 wc instead of the quoted 2 wcs, the kitchen was very small – again, smaller than last years. Shower head was broken and with no curtain, the floor got wet with every use. On day 2 queried with reception if we were in fact in the correct type of accommodation, but she could not say and said she’d refer it to the manager. Never got answer. Somebody came quite promptly to look at the shower, but only bodged it badly to keep the handset on the wall. Bedroom, storage and lounge were all clean and comfortable. In fact, the rooms were very quiet and there were minimal disturbances from the other residents in the full-up block. The lifts were a bit hit and miss – some call buttons not illuminating. Quite busy too; I suppose because it was a busy week and nobody wants to walk much in a ski resort. Ski lockers were adequate – boot warmers didn’t always work. Block is quite close (100m) to the Grand Vans lift and not too far from the long stay car park. Very good checkout process – just hand over the key and go! Overall, it was ok, but I could have done without the smaller apartment and the shower problems.

author: AntsHarrison
title: Poor overall but please read the review
text: I have just returned from a ski trip to Flaine staying at the here and I need to apologise to the god "Trip Advisor", I have sinned and booked a stay with out consulting the Oracle and trusted what was on booking.com. Lesson 101, read this first. To summarise. The positives 1.25 hours from Geneva 5 min walk from ski lift Decent space in apartment and lockable ski locker Great skiing Reasonably priced shop on site Staff were very good The negatives The apartment was a disgrace - see pictures, do not unpack until you have carefully inspected it. I cannot begin to describe just how bad it was, and to compound things our apartment was next to the bins and the stench that greeted us is still with me now. According to the reception staff they are due a refurbishment and the owners are considering their options, net result a complete lack of investment in the essentials. This is a self catering resort with limited choice of bars/restaurants and very spread out. Due to point above there is no soul or feel/vibe to the resort. What food was available out was both very average and very very expensive as was the alcohol. Our view overlooked a road which was popular with dogs/owners, and it was always a delight to have breakfast in watching various dogs defecating whilst looking in on us. Boy it is an ugly child of the 60's. So to sum up. If you want a ski break, just to ski, are not worried about eating out or staying in luxury but are prepared to pay a small fortune for everything this is the place for you. And the strange thing is with the exception of the accommodation it ticks a lot of my boxes so will probably go again. I have complained to booking.com as what they advertise and what is delivered is a long long way apart as we paid £140 a night and it was more 1 star and £50 a night. Email me with any questions.

author: Simon2009
title: Good value for money. Wifi poor. Not ski in/out.
text: Stayed 17-24th Jan. 1 bed apartment fine for us and 2 kids - living room sofa easy to make up if a bit firm. Pillows were old & stained. Was quiet enough on the 4th floor with a balcony facing the street/resort. The complex is about a 300m level walk from the main lifts (eg Grand Vans) and beginners area. It's not ski in/ski out. Apartment was clean and functional. Plenty of heat and hot water. As stated elsewhere there's a hob & microwave with grill (no oven). The local supermarkets (Spar in Foret, Sherpa in Forum) have a limited range and are about 50% more expensive than usual. 3 cafes/restaurants in the building/adjacent and one also runs a small supermarket with an entrance on the ground floor of the complex. The Flying Dutchman pub/cafe next door does take-out pizza/burgers/chicken/chips. Restaurants are usually 14-25€ for mains courses. Wifi was 15€ per week but very slow - measured at 0.2Mbps. Ok for light browsing/email but you're not going to be watching tv online or using Skype. Irritatingly you have to sign in on a web page every time you connect. Overall I thought it was comfortable and good value for money. Would go again.

author: LiamSteer
title: Great location and views but tatty and dated apartments...
text: I have just come back from a weeks break in the Pierre & Vacances Residence La Foret in Flaine. I traveled with my wife and 2 friends. We were looking for a nice self catering apartment so Pierre & Vacances Residence La Foret looked the business! The apartment that we had was very very tatty with extremely stained carpets, walls and in general. We had the largest apartment that they offer and I have to say that the living area and kitchen was tight with 4 of us. The beds were unbarebly hard and I resorted to using one of the spare duvets folded in half to enable me to get some sleep. Also, we paid the 15 euros for the wifi, had trouble logging on from time to time the speed was shocking, 0.02KB's for most of the day. You would be better off paying the roaming charges on your mobile. Please don't be fooled by the photo's, these apartments look nothing like the promotional photo's, they may have done when they were first built but things have changes allot since. The kitchen was equipped with Microwave, hobs, coffee machine and some utensils but the knives were extremely blunt and the utensils limited. With all this in mind though they are in a great location in relation to the ski area and it's a short 100m walk to the nursery slope and lifts. The apartments are also close to all the amenities including pubs, shops and the lift to the forum section of Flaine. Lots of people have said about the noise but we have to say that this was not too much of a problem for us and we had a 1st level apartment. We had an amazing holiday and the apartment did not spoil it for us but if you are looking for a quality finish and plenty of space i would look else where. We felt that the price of this apartment was not on par with the quality of the place but then you pay for location i suppose and this place has that sorted!

author: LarssonDK
title: Good accommodation with a few exceptions
text: Went skiing in Flaine for a week in January 2012. We did order the 2 bedroom apartment with two separate double rooms and a living room/kitchen. It was very nice for 4 people but advertised to accommodate 6/7 people (2-3 people in the living room). Bed linen, bath towels and kitchen kit (dishwasher tabs, cloth, dish soap, towels) was all included in the rental. So was end of stay cleaning (with exception of the kitchen area). This service was very good and helped us save weight in our traveling bags. The interior was in general tidy, but bed rooms was missing some storage space (only a small cabinet in each) and the bed was rock hard (way too hard). On the plus side the beds included real duvets not the normal french blankets. Wireless Internet was 15€ for a week. During our stay, they were doing maintenance from 15:00 to 18:00. It was so loud that we couldn't have a normal conversation in the apartment. We went to the reception to complain about this and it stopped for the day. But next day it started again. This happened 3 days in a row. There was no warning about this when we booked the room. If no maintenance was going on during our stay, I would probably have rated this better, but apparently you can't be sure when they have scheduled the work. They won't tell you.

author: DOM_1183
title: Dirty & noisy. FInd somewhere else.
text: You don't go to Flaine for the architecture but this place is poorly built and poorly maintained. We went for a long weekend. This was the second time that I have stayed at La Foret and have resolved not to return. When we got to our apartment, we wanted some water but the glasses were filthy. When we looked at the plates and bowls, there were the remains of someone's spaghetti in one and other food remains in others (all stacked on top of each other under cleaner crockery). Missing light bulbs, dingy bathrooms and ingrained dirt everywhere. This apartment needed to be take out of service and given a deep clean/refurb. What made it worse is that we paid for a premium apartment. This was on the side of the building. South facing? Well part of one room was. The bedrooms were North facing. I have stayed at P&V in Flaine and Les Arc. In Les Arc we got bed bugs. At the time I thought that it was a one off but now I think that cleanliness is way down the list of priorities for P&V. (P&V will send you a feedback form but not respond.) If you stay on a Friday night take earplugs as you are likely to be kept awake by partying neighbours. On the plus side, the staff are pleasant and the apartments are near to the slopes but that is not enough to justify the price or the quality of the accommodation.

author: theweather
title: hopeless service
text: My partner and I stayed here for 3nights. First impression of the (standard) room booked was that it was dark and small. The shower had a dank smell about it. There is no ventilation in the room at all. You cannot open windows. The shower alcove is completely transparent hence no privacy. I had emailed the hotel prior to staying to ask after their facilities, the email was never answered. We were disappointed to discover that the rooftop bar was closed due to a private party, this was not conveyed to us prior. We ordered room service breakfast one morning, I asked whether one of the meals was vegetarian as it was not clear on the menu, I was told it was., however it arrived soggy, in a box with plastic utensils complete with ham. It was on par with airline food. I also rang reception to enquire whether I could purchase an item from the room, the staff member had no idea and said they would call me back...they never did. The housekeeping dept did not clean the rooms until very late in the afternoon, we came back from one day at 3pm and the room had still not been cleaned and we had to wait downstairs until it had. The room never smelt fresh and the floors not particularly clean. I found long hairs on the blanket provided and on my last night I developed a red itchy rash from the bed linen. Obviously house keeping use some very harsh chemicals with washing their bed linen. On the whole I found the staff very amateur and in dire need of training... They just didn't seem to care.

author: brittanybathgate
title: Disappointing and doesn’t live up to the photos
text: I booked this hotel as a treat for my boyfriend and I before heading home to the U.K. From the photos on the website The Old Clare looks amazing so I was super excited to stay, but as soon as I stepped in to our room I was really disappointed. The first thing I noticed was how dark the room was, nothing like those bright and airy photos on their website. It’s so dark we had to have all the lights switched on during the day. Secondly, we were placed in a room on the first floor right next to the main road. I wouldn’t have minded had I not specifically requested a quiet room when I made the booking. I made the booking quite far in advanced so that the hotel would have plenty of time to accommodate my request. The room was so noisy, all I could hear was the traffic day and night. I could also hear the water running very loudly every time the room above me had a shower or flushed the toilet. And thirdly, the pool looks nothing like the images on the website. From my understanding it’s recently been refurbished, but there’s no sun loungers or seats by the pool, so if you do go for a swim you’ve got nowhere to sit after or leave your stuff. You can sit at the bar, but I’d prefer not to in a wet bikini. Massive shame because it would be awesome if there were sun loungers like shown in the image on their website, but they are nowhere to be seen anymore. Other cons: - Breakfast room service was delivered in a paper bag. No tray or plate. How am I supposed to eat my breakfast when I’ve got nothing to put it on. - No turn down service? Just got back to our room at 5pm to find the bed hasn’t been made, room service leftovers are still in the room and fridge hasn’t been replenished. We’re actually still here with two more night lefts of our stay, and I’m seriously considering moving to another hotel...especially as I can now hear a pneumatic drill outside.

author: quevara
title: Room 301 small and claustrophobic
text: Perhaps I was just really unlucky with the room I was given. I found it very small and it didn't have high ceilings! It had a narrow strip of window with an internal view overlooking the top of the lobby atrium. Bathroom shower was large. Towels were thick and fluffy. Double basins. Check in at night was cool and polite, not unfriendly but I wouldn't say it was welcoming either. During the day I found reception staff always said hello and were very friendly. Even though you needed a swipe card to get to your floor in the elevator, the open and public staircase accessible to all from the lobby means anyone can climb it to any level at any time! Room service was speedy and delicious (flatbread and broccoli) Street noise inevitable. Not the place to go if you want a super quiet room. Close to Spice Alley. Shopping complex next door including a cinema. I probably wouldn't stay here again. For a more comfortable stay I would return to QT Sydney.

author: itsmardizzle
title: It’s lovely but you need to be very close to your travelling companion
text: I hate glass bathrooms. I know they make the room look more spacious, they are super trendy, blah blah blah. But if you are sharing your room with anyone other than a VERY significant other, really, who wants to see someone else in the shower, or worse, on the toilet? In the room I had at The Old Clare, I was fortunately on my own, but you could see very clearly through the clear glass shower box to the toilet, even though the toilet cubicle itself had frosted glass. Not frosted enough, people! Having said that, the building is great, location is brilliant, close to Central Station and other public transport, plus lots of eating options. The room was nice, not small, the bed huge, but way too soft. It was spotlessly clean. Nice amenities in the coffee machine, plus kettle and mugs for tea, and nice bath wash, shampoo and conditioner. Only one large bath towel, the other one provided was small. Weird. If there had been two of us in the room, one would have had to make do with a small towel. Kensington Social provides breakfast and room service, but when I rang the room service number on the menu, I got an answering machine message saying they were too busy to answer the phone, please leave a message and they would call back. Erm, no. Called reception instead, and was VERY happy with the food when it arrived, it was excellent. Breakfast is good, the menu is small but there are sufficient choices to keep most people happy. Service in the hotel and the restaurant is lovely. So, recommended, I would stay there again, but I would like to know if there are rooms with less revealing toilet walls.

author: MtHD74
title: Excellent location, nice hotel but some improvements necessary
text: Overall, a nice hotel but didn't quite live up to the hype. Excellent location adjacent to Kensington Street which is filled with excellent restaurants and bars. Stayed in a Clare Room which had one of the best beds I have ever slept in. Nice amenities. Housekeeping always did a great job in the room too. My only gripe was the front of house staff. When ringing to confirm location en route, the fellow was quite unprofessional on the phone and abrupt. Upon check-in, the woman was quite brusque, had to remind her breakfast was included in the room rate and when I went to leave to go to the room after check in she gave me such a look of such disdain it was quite affronting. There were issues with the iron during the stay which caused the electricity to trip and leave the room without power. By the 4th time this had happened, I visited the front desk personally, told the woman that I would be heading out and could it be fixed, only to come back 2.5 hrs later to find the room still without power. Visiting the front desk again I was told it had been fixed and when I said it hadn't, her reply was "Gimme, gimme, gimme, umm, an hour and we'll get it fixed". Luckily Spice Alley was in full swing so I was able to enjoy some nice dumplings before coming back to the hotel hoping the electricity problem had been rectified. It had been and I was very appreciative that the manager had left a voucher for complimentary drinks in the Clare Bar and he personally visited later that afternoon to check if the electricity was working and if all was fine. I appreciated his personalised touch and follow through after the issues with the front desk. I would stay at the Clare again, merely due to it's location to Kensington Street and the super comfortable bed. I don't think the staff are very good ambassadors for the hotel though.

author: DrBK
title: industrial chic, a great luxury staycation
text: Stayed in an Abercrombie room as a couple with a 5mo infant. Sorting out valet parking slightly confusing given entrances are on narrow roads, however no major issues. Reception small but well-staffed and welcoming. Hotel from entrance to room modern and pays homage to the previous industrial site. Bed was luxurious and soft. Deep freestanding bathtub and large shower were standouts. Airconditioning worked well, and all the little amenities available in the room to ensure a comfortable stay. Free cot for the little one was an appreciated touch. Toiletries not single use (so no take-away goodies here), and nothing else to take away apart from good memories without an extra cost. Gym has basic equipment, suitable for those looking to keep in shape whilst on business. Outdoor heated pool a delight, and certainly feels like an escape in the middle of the city, poolside bar not available during our stay. Free wifi fast and reliable from room to poolside (tested, NBN speeds). Bar hipster, dark and sleezy - perhaps a nod to it's past history but not particularly welcoming. Easy access to CBD, Central train station, etc. Although given we are Sydneysiders the main attraction for our staycation was the Kensington Street restaurants - will be back to explore more!

author: BUMPYWelwyn
title: Almost Perfect!
text: Loved this hotel, great location - be sure to visit Spice Alley (area full of Chinese, Korean and Malaysian Street food restaurants ) and Eastside Kitchen and Bar, some of the best food we ate in Sydney - 1 minute walk from hotel . Quirky hotel, fabulous room ( had one with free standing bath in room). High ceilings which gives an airy feel and gorgeous toiletries. Loved the free bag on arrival ! I gave it 4 stars for two reasons instead of 5. Kensington Street Social, restaurant within hotel is closed Sundays and Mondays. We wanted to eat there but we were there whilst they were shut . Anyone staying those nights would miss out. Minor point as there are fab choices nearby . Biggest gripe was hotel pool which was fabulous but not nearly enough beds to accommodate those wanting to relax by pool in the really hot temperatures . I counted 6 couples in the space of an hour come to the pool and leave because there were no beds . Think they have 6. There are plenty of chairs and tables up on the pool terrace (very few being used ) so would be better to have fewer tables and more beds. Also there are two umbrellas only for all beds - I actually had a couple ask if they could lay at the foot of my bed for the shade which of course I said yes as it was a really hot morning . That aside I would def stay there again and highly recommend this hotel .

author: DeniseGarcia100
title: The place to be in Sydney!
text: I have the fondest memories of The Old Clare where I lived for a month when I was last in Sydney. It is my favorite city in the world and this is the hotel I would like to go back to every time! The people are so lovely: Martin and Alice, Anna and so many others that really made me feel welcome and at home. Alice made sure that I had everything for every meeting, every visit. She was a jewel! The Old Clare hotel is luxuriously appointed even if you stay in the least expensive room (my case!). The bed is one of the best, the bathroom is so wonderful....everything about from the door, to the items in the mini-bar: every aspect is thought out with distinction and charm. There is really no place like it. Martin, the super concierge, is the most handsome man alive and he is also the most caring, warm and thoughtful person to assist you. The swimming pool on top terrace is a heavenly retreat at every time of the day or evening. This is the place to relax and sip a drink with a gorgeous view of Sydney. The restaurant has two wonderful restaurants / bar. The most extraordinarily unique asset is the pedestrian street across where I had the best breakfast in the world every day at Anthony x Glider, a Thai-Japanese place that had the most unusual and healthy offerings ever! Please open one in Boston!! Behind this pedestrian street, you will find another one full of Asian eateries that are to die for. You never have to leave that street! I recommend this hotel to everyone and to owners of other hotels that I visit around the world as a model of what hospitality - a blend of elegance and casual luxury - must be ! I would love to be back at the Old Clare hotel.

author: maw11
title: Amazing Hotel and Area
text: We moved hotels from the Sheraton Parkside as it was not as we expected. We are so happy we did. The Old Clair hotel turned our trip around. The staff is great; the hotel design and location are much more suitable for our family. We stayed 5 nights in a loft style room. Our 10-year-old slept on the sofa on the first floor, giving my wife and I a little privacy. the bathroom was perfect, functional, with a tub, shower and private toilet. The hotel has great Wi-Fi, and a nice rooftop pool area to cool off in our lounge. The location is fantastic. A short walk to central station, close to several shopping centers, (one directly across the street with a Woolworth grocery store, liquor store, pharmacy, and movie theatre). Chinatown is close, As is the university with its great architecture and Dr Chau Chak Wing Building designed by Frank Gehry. The Broadway Shopping centre is just down the street, across from it a park with beautiful old university grounds and buildings. All around this area you will find small restaurants, nail salons, shopping, grocery stores, etc. Directly beside the hotel is a narrow street the houses many interesting international restaurants, another wine shop, Handpicked Cellar Door, and Koi Dessert Bar, (make sure you check out the fantastic desserts). we were visiting family nightly and only got to experience The Kensington Street Social. It was great although a little expensive. We will stay at The Old Clair the next time we are in Sydney.

author: 660GaryC
title: Fine Hotel in Chippendale
text: My wife and I just spent 4 nights at this charmingly renovated hotel. We enjoyed the mix of old and new. Our room was comfortable, clean and reasonably quiet (there were drivers who zoomed down the street at night, but the soundproofing in our room dealt with this pretty well). Our room also had a glass shower - a new experience. The only thing I would change is it would have been nice to light up the toilet closet separately from the rest of the bathroom area (glass walls let a lot of light thru) , but this is a minor complaint. The staff was friendly and helpful. Kensington St. Social restaurant was a good place for breakfast - as I noted in a separate review, it offered choices with cereals (muesli and granola) no other breakfast places we visited did that. Very good breakfast at a reasonable price given the setting. We never stopped in at The Clare bar - it was either packed and noisy or closed when we tried to go there. Simiarly, we didn't eat at Automata, but it always seemed lively and busy when we passed by. Another real positive was the location of the Old Clare: across Kensington St. are a lot of good to great restaurants: Spice Alley, Bistrot Gavroche and a very nice wine tasting bar (Handmade Wines). The Central train station is a few minutes walk away and many buses pass close by. Sydney Opera House is 3.6 km (about 2 miles) away, about a 45 minute walk, and the central shopping district is somewhat closer. Darling Harbor 1.4 km (a little over a mile) and less than 20 minutes. Hyde Park is also 1.4 km away. Neighborhoods like Surrey Hills (1.2 km) and Paddington (2.8 km - 30 minutes) are similarly nice walks from the Old Clare. Put it all together, a good location for visiting a lot of Sydney. We will definitely stay here again on future trips.

author: WilciSelf
title: Great Location
text: My wife and I spent 1 night at the Old Clare last weekend and we very much enjoyed it. The room was reminiscent of the Little National in Canberra , but larger and very satisfactory, however the bed was far to soft for my wife. If you have a back problem , be careful to ask if they have firmer beds. The staff were great and very helpful as a was a 1pm checkout at our request on Sunday. We had some drinks in the Old Clare Bar, and enjoyed the atmosphere . We didn't find it overcrowded and noisy as many reviewers did. It was a tad slow, this was because they make so many cocktails, kinda slows things down a bit. We also had breakfast at Kensington Street Social, which was fine , but I have had better breakfasts, servings a little on the light side , but a good atmosphere. Most of all we enjoyed the location, surrounded by many restaurants, bars and cafes and a great Cinema at Palace Cinemas, next door... if you haven't seen Bladerunner 2049 yet make sure you do. My major disappointment was that the Hotel charges a credit card fee..... maybe in all the literature it states they do ... but didn't see it .. I have stayed at a lot of hotels across the world and this is the first time I have seen it. ..Its a tacky money grab , that does not fit with the hotels vibe... so I gave it 4 stars instead of 5!

author: 0809Dragonfly
title: Look up...Look down....Look all around!
text: Intrigued by the photographs of an industrial styled renovation I made a booking for three nights at the Old Clare Hotel. I was a bit confused about breakfast arrangements so I rang the hotel. My first impression was of excellent customer service and I have Ryan to thank for that. He explained that while the Hotel was ideally situated to a number of excellent cafes, Kensington Street Social, located within the Hotel precinct, collaborated to cater for Hotel guests. An excellent recommendation and we were pleased to we took his advice. On my (early) arrival I was advised, by the very helpful Georgina, that a Heritage Room was not yet available but that she would contact me directly. Armed with a map, walking directions to my shopping destination and recommendations for shopping in Surry Hills and a fabulous cafe, Alimentari, for lunch, I was on my way. A courtesy text later and I was soon ensconced in the Mary O' suite. What a marvellous upgrade! My husband and I loved the separate sitting/dining room, the three way bathroom (with separate shower and toilet) was luxurious. The only downside was getting up in the morning after a great sleep in the fabulous King Size bed. The Hotel is ideally situated in Kensington Street, home to Spice Alley which serves all manner of asian street food delights and more upmarket restaurants. Dine early to avoid the crowds on the week-end. Many thanks to Martin Bray, the 'Super Concierge' for being so personable in dealing with a minor room service issue and then delivering two very dry martinis, just the way we like them, in chic old style martini glasses. They certainly beat the cup of tea I'd made! Attention to detail is key in this quirky, stylish renovation which features classic decor from the original buildings juxtaposed superbly with modern design. Remember to look in all directions so that you don't miss anything. A big tick to all the staff, who without doubt are the friendliest and most helpful we've met in a long time travelling and thanks again Old Clare for a wonderful stay!

author: siuhang
title: Nothing short of stunning
text: At first I was worried that the hotel would be overly punk, but I was relieved when I entered my room. The first thing that hit me was the open bathroom and those "cult" shampoo, shower gel and hand wash from Triumph & Disaster. Nothing of the sort of chemical stuff you get. The transparent shower was right next to the bed (with no curtain) and I was thinking, this hotel is not suitable for kids and strangers. The next thing that wowed me was the high ceiling, high windows and designer light. It really helped to make the room feel more spacious and made me feel more relaxed. And 2 washing basins! Everything was classy, from the Le Creuset cups to the antique chairs. The bed and pillows gave me perfect few nights of sleep. The hotel is conveniently situated near Central Station where you can catch a train or tram to Fish Market. Chinatown is within walking distance, so is Darling Harbour if you follow The Goods Line. Surry Hills is just on the other side of the Station and you can cut through the underpass. Next to the hotel is Central Park Mall where Woolworths opens till midnight. Our room faced the line of restaurants on Kensington Street but the sound proofing was exceptionally good. The room did not include breakfast but Kensington Street Social has a package for hotel guest and the restaurant was stunning as well. The only findings I have are that the hotel did not provide toothbrush and bottled water but you can always get them in the Woolworths next door. The magazines in the room was quite backdated. I also find the towel rack a little inconvenient as it was on the back of the glass panel of the shower. Would go back to the Old Clare anytime.

author: julieaW9926TY
title: Wonderful ambience
text: Love this beautiful old building, so sympathetically renovated and refurbished to a high standard. The mattress was perfect. Room was lovely and unusual in it's layout. Staff were friendly and helpful. The bar was super noisy, but once away from it, it was quiet. We ate in the restaurant downstairs, and that was a good meal. I would add that the champagne serve was ludicrous. Paying $19 for about 100 mls was just plain rip off stuff. I did ask the, to fill my glass, and they did. But this annoys me. Champagne is not supposed to be served like that! Not even in France! The one thing that really bugged both my partner and I was the pillows. They were so huge and puffy, that we couldn't use them. Uckily I was able to borrow a pillow from my daughter, but otherwise it was a problem.

author: 875susanp
title: Avante-garde respite
text: After a day of lengthy weather related flight delays and sweltering heat, we arrived late at night. Walking into this room with its sumptuous bed and large modern bathroom after a very efficient check in was restorative. This hotel is stunning, and one gets the feeling that every pierce of furniture down to the chaises at the pool was chosen with an artistic eye. The hotel is also outfitted with a clear concern for guests' comfort. In the rooms, this was exhibited by the private toilet, multiple shower heads, separate sinks, comfy bed and linens, among other things. The loft layout of the room gives such a sense of spaciousness. The location was great for us as it was only blocks away from the University of Sydney where our son was starting as an exchange student. Given how late at night we arrived, he was not able to check into his apartment the day we arrived. The rollaway (which we had not ordered) was there within minutes of checking into the hotel. The concierge helped us rent a car on a Sunday (when many rental companies are closed or have limited hours) which was promptly delivered to the hotel. She permitted us to turn in the car at the hotel after the rental company closed. The hotel took care of returning the car from there and did not charge us for overnight parking. The assortment of furniture throughout the common areas and in the room is stunning. The wifi works well. The rooftop pool is lovely, though we didn't have enough time to enjoy it, and the pool bar was not open at the times we went to the pool. Even if you don't have time to spend at the pool, at least go up and take a look at the views from the pool. This is not your run of the mill luxury hotel.

author: OliveP523
title: More of a mixed bag than I expected
text: The actual renovation is pretty wonderful in how they have blended the old and the new. But it's not double glazed so there is street noise. The showers in the double rooms are see through which is embarrassing if one of you brings people back to the room while the other showers. The pillows are ridiculously thick, making my first night's sleep uncomfortable but we got slightly lower ones after that. All of our party had trouble with them.The bedding was lovely and the room was really well appointed. Breakfast has no buffet but the menu items are delicious. The bar was billed as having craft beer but had only 3 brews on tap. We ordered food twice in the bar and both times the orders were screwed up. The staff were generally very helpful and polite, especially at reception. The pool bar was also oversold in that the bar was not open once during our stay of a week. There were only 6 pool loungers, which were full on several days but also there was no real shade because the umbrellas couldn't deal with the wind. There is a gym which I generally had to myself. It has 3 treadmill type things, a bench and free weights, none over 10 kg. Rather less than the website shows. So pretty limited. All in all I would stay there again but would bear in mind that two of the features we went there for: the craft beer and the pool bar were not actually as advertised.

author: tantone1
title: Fantastic Boutique Hotel for a long weekend
text: This boutique hotel was the location for a friend's birthday at the co-located Automata restaurant. We took the kids and had interconnedting rooms. The rooms were very clean and funky and worked well for all 4 of us. The beds were amazingly comfy. The location is brilliant; walking distance to Central Station and in a part of town full of amazing eating options. The Old Clare has a bright lounge bar and has two world class restaurants within its walls - Automata and Kengsington St Local. We ate at both and were blown away. Spice Alley is next door. We found it took 5 mins by taxi to get to the Rocks and the CBD shopping (although there is shopping next door and a shopping centre 3 blocks along Broadway). But the real reason this was a fantastic stay was the service. The reception team made everything easy, from check in to organising and chasing up our taxi when we left. They went above and beyond our expectations, including posting us some clothing our kids left in the room the week after we returned to Perth. This is a small luxury hotel that is designed for adults but is happy to accommodate kids (they loved the pool on the roof), is well located, has amazing food and very high quality service. We are grateful to our friends for finding this gem. We will definately go back and highly recommend the stay.

author: LucyB2238
title: Rude staff ruined the stay
text: I always leave reviews because I use them when booking places. My partner booked this hotel for the night of my birthday, being a Friday he was still at work and I had the day off so he suggested I check in early and he will meet me there when he finished work. I went to check in and instead of politely telling me that I had to get his written confirmation, I was made feel stupid and ignorant in front of other guests that I wasn't allowed to check in without him. I was made to sit by the side for 10 minutes and then I asked if there were any way to check in without him and only then did the lady tell me I had to get him to send a confirmation email to them saying he gave them permission. I have no issue with that for security reasons, but the way the staff handled it was rude and unprofessional. After that I was sent to my room, which was not the room my partner had booked. He especially booked a room with a bath, and this room had no bath. I called the reception straight away and the same lady sighed and said she would get back to me. So here I was, sitting in a room, with no explanation and not sure what to do as I wasn't in the right room. After 15 minutes of waiting, I decided to call reception again and the same lady (with the same foul attitude) told me I had to wait til 5 (it was now 2:30) until they could move me to the correct room. So I thought, stuff this and I had a shower while I waited. Not at any point did she apologise for the mix up, or offer any explanation. At 5:30 I was then moved to the correct room, still no explanation, no apology and no acknowledgement from any of the staff that they had made me feel a lot less than welcome. After that, thankfully I didn't have much to do with the staff again. But this really took away from a stay that should've been nice and relaxing. I felt for my partner who had paid $450 for the night - when paying that much for one night you'd expect to be treated well. After this stay I wrote to management and they apologised for the incident but I would NEVER recommend this place to anyone. I often travel for work and my partner and I stay in hotels often, so I like to leave reviews - unless they have completely re-trained their staff I would never stay at this place again.

author: Lyssiant
title: Legitimately bespoke, a touch fancy.. and oh just so cool!
text: So yeah.. bespoke / original heritage restorations are massively in right now. The Old Clare does it all and does it all right, but it's just so refreshing to see that they are still able to maintain their own individual charm in a market where trying to be different is "the new black", It's got the cool factor of the QT, but with more homage to the originality of the Carlton United Brewery building it is based off.. There's just something magestic about walking down the freshly restored but original corridors and seeing the photos of what the building was during it's original recreation stages.. We were booked into a Connell Room (advertised as the "impeccable standard") and by gosh they were right (refer to photos).. Just amazing.. the photos speak for themselves.. This hotel has single-handedly started somewhat of a cultural revolution in the Chippendale area as all of the laneways around the building are Melbourning-up into fashionable little spots. Between enjoying the room and enjoying the surrounds, there's a plenty to do just in the precinct for a short trip and Central Station is just a stone-throw away too. Service is a delight with the staff seemingly hand-picked from the cotton fields.. they are all super well-presented, knowledgable, friendly and down-to-earth.. just like what you'd expect from a classy bar or something.. They will treat you how you should be treated.. and i guess that would be different depending on who you are XD Loved spending time with them all, from Georgina the all-star to Martin the super-concierge to Alice the commander-on-duty, to the glorious hiccup girl who literally hicced her way all through my check-out, luggage, valet etc. with a big smile =] Loved my stay and will definitely be back next time i'm around this area. Thanks!

author: Jemmacamille
title: Unfortunately a disappointing experience
text: I was disappointed with the level of experience and service for a boutique hotel. As a traveler for business I have seen what other boutique hotels around the world can offer and their attention to detail is far superior to The Old Clare Hotel. It makes Sydney look a bit behind the rest of the world. Rooms on the ground floor while big have no insulation - I was able to hear every sound in the corridor, every person walking past, every door closing. I could hear the toilet flushing and the shower draining on the floor above me. The interior design is nice but its not clever - where is the attention to detail? There is so much potential to make the rooms more comfortable - a lot of the space is wasted. Where are the little luxuries that make your stay just that little more special. For a bathroom to have a huge bathtub you would expect bath salts or bubble bath for a more enjoyable experience. A good quality doona for the bed wouldnt go astray. Down lights in general are outdated not to mention down lights in the bathroom which only provide harsh and unflattering lighting. Many boutique hotels provide an iphone free of charge for the duration of the guests stay so they can find their way around the city and make calls free of charge - amazing! The Old Clare doesnt have any perks. I thought the level of professionalism from the staff also let the hotel down - poorly presented with an attitude that was possibly too casual for the standard the hotel is trying to promote. Sydney is over priced and outdated - it would be great to see hotels, restaurants and bars move with the rest of the world.

author: ben46k
title: Hidden Gem
text: A quick 1 night stay for business in Sydney. I required a hotel close to UTS where I was attending a conference. I drove in early and to my surprise my room was ready at 7am. This gave me an opportunity to freshen up before my meeting, whilst my car was valet parked without a fuss. The decor and atmosphere of the hotel was fantastic. A great fusion of its past as well as modern ammenities. My room, (Clare room) was huge. Free standing bath, beautiful floorboards and a bed that I could sleep on either vertically or horizontally! Room was quiet, modern and probably nicer than many upscale hotels I have stayed in. I dined for dinner and breakfast at Kensington St Social. Great vibe, excellent food. Service was polite, knowledgeable and fast even though they were busy. I had the swordfish and my beer was served in a pewter mug to add to the funky nature of this pub/hotel/fine dining/ complex! The pub had a dj and was pretty loud in and around reception but for me, it added to the atmosphere of this hotel. Crowd was professional and aged between 25-40. I can't really fault my stay and I would stay here again to sample a part of the city that is somewhat unknown to me. Now need an excuse to come back!

author: jasonh2015
title: Beyond Perfect - Thank you!
text: WOW.. this place is fantastic. Was left in a bit of pickle when the hotel booked for my wife's birthday let us down. Called Alex at the front desk at the Old Clare and he worked his magic and got us a fantastic room. Martin, the SUPER concierge is a Super Hero. He not only looked after us but really went above and beyond to make our stay unforgettable. Such a good guy and really is the heart of the place. He even managed to swing a table for dinner at Automata on a Saturday night with 1 hours notice. That is impossible. PS... fantastic place and must go with the matching drinks.. the Sake is an experience! Thank you again! The hotel is the perfect mix of design and comfort. The rooms just feel right and the attention to detail is fantastic. My wife is a successful interior designer and even she was blown away with what they have done with the place. I am not usually on for a 10/10 but this place turns it up to 11! A must stay.

author: AustMat
title: Nice Stay
text: A Friday night break. The foyer and check in is relatively casual for a 5 star hotel. We were upgraded a room category which was nice - the room was spacious with high ceilings, lounge area and open bathroom with bath. Nice design and furniture - loved the hallway carpet - shame the rug in the room isn't as cool. We stayed one night so it's hard to get a really good feel for the place, but the service we received was attentive and friendly. Location worked well for what we needed, though somewhat pricey if you consider that it isn't in the CBD. We had the power short out while getting ready to go out - had to have someone come up to the room to reset. The large searchlight style lamp didn't work, which as unfortunate as it would have been nice to just keep this and the bed light on. Lastly, if you are a light sleeper maybe request one of the 'new' rooms, or a room facing away from footpath/road as much as possible. I was woken a few times during the night by rowdy party goers and sirens. I understand this is a heritage building - but for a 5 star hotel, sleep quality is a key issue. If they were able to modify the windows / entry for the restaurant downstairs, surely something could have been done to introduce double glazed windows to hotel rooms. We had breakfast elsewhere - I found the menu a little convoluted and lacking the basics. Overall, we did enjoy this hotel. We are just hesitant to return given sleep quality.

author: RulyTruly
title: Beautiful design but noisy
text: I stayed two nights in a Clare Room (with separate bath and shower) on level one, overlooking a little laneway. On arrival my room was immaculately clean, with stunning decor which highlights the building’s industrial heritage, huge windows and high ceilings. The open-plan bedroom/bathroom featuring a pristine white tub looks beautiful, but its minimal privacy may not suit some guests. Hotel paraphenalia such as menus and laundry bags contain cheeky quips that raise a smile. The room also has a separate area with a long bar-style desk, a sink above the mini-bar (which holds interesting snacks like beetroot and sweet potato crisps) and an espresso maker. The air conditioning system was quiet and efficient. Room service is provided by the hip restaurant downstairs Kensington Social, and is a far cry from the mainstream being personable, flexible and unusual. Disappointingly, my room wasn’t serviced at all during my two-night stay. The first morning I left early and arrived back in the room at about 2pm to find that housekeeping had not cleaned the room. As I went out for the evening at 4pm I spoke to reception about getting my room serviced and a cabinet door fixed (it had fallen off). I was curtly informed that it was too late to clean the room, but that they would replace used towels and fix the door. On my return at 10pm the dirty towels remained on the bathroom floor, as did the broken door. I rang reception again and a couple of clean towels were delivered. More problematic was the amount of street noise which disrupted sleep both nights of my stay. The hotel is situated in a vibrant area above bars and restaurants and the room’s closed windows aren’t sealed to stop the noise of party-goers, revving motor cycles and delivery trucks. The second morning was worse, I was woken at 4am by something that sounded like masses of heavy furniture being shifted and beer kegs being rolled about. On check-out I asked that at a copy of my bill be forwarded by email (rather than paper). Reception happily agreed, but three days later it still hasn’t arrived.

author: Bloggers_Boyfriend
title: unbelievably bad!
text: So we checked in at the Old Clare Hotel in room 113 which is the 'Show Room Suite'. All the other shortfalls of this hotel might have been forgiven if only the customer service was somewhere passable. The reception to put it mildly did not make us feel welcome at all. We were rushed through as though our arrival was an inconvenience, and when I was asking what was on this weekend in Sydney the answer was a very short "I have no idea - please follow me to your room." At any other 'luxury hotel' I might have expected the reception staff to recommend some activities in town! The hotel reservation actually called us earlier that week to ask if we would like to upgrade to the 113 suite for an extra charge and we specifically said that we would rather not as we preferred the room we actually booked. But when we arrived, they announced that they took the liberty of upgrading us anyway (free of charge, granted), explaining that the room we originally booked was taken. The hotel staff's one redeeming gesture might have been the 'personal welcome note' which was left for us in the room. It was written nicely in hand... on the back of a cardboard coaster. A fitting cherry on the top, for one of the worst customer service we have probably ever experienced at a hotel. So many hard to ignore details are displeasing about the hotel and the room (which I mentioned earlier is their 'Show Room'). As for accessing the narrow laneway entrance to this hotel, our poor taxi driver was stuck on Kensington Street for 10 minutes because the street is only wide enough for one vehicle, one of the hotel guests had parked their car blocking the street. As for our room, the first thing we notice is that on this Thursday night, we could hear all the loud goings on of the bar right down stairs - the windows were single glazed, and provided no sound proofing at all. Going to fill up the bathtub, we were wondering why the water wasn't heating up, and we discover that the hot/cold indicator was installed backwards! Again I am emphasising that this is a $1000 per night 'Show Room Suite'. It was nice of the hotel to include a Nespresso machine in the room, but unfortunately they placed it inside a tiny shelf that required you to take the whole machine out to be able to put a capsule in - in their defence I understand that the reason for this was because the cabinet was restored from an antique, but I wonder that there was no other solution for this. Conclusion: The only pleasant takeaway we have from The Old Clare Hotel is its nice decorations, which unfortunately does not make up for its poor attention to important details and its nonexistent customer service. Does not come close to justifying its overpriced rates.

author: nzphotog
title: Fabulous renovation and really large rooms
text: Stayed at the Old Clare Hotel for 3 nights, book-edging a yoga retreat in the Blue Mountains. I was able to stay in 2 rooms...can't remember the other one's name, but the Abercrombie room was definitely fab. The location: a few minutes walk to Central Station...so easy to get to the airport. Across from the alley was a whole set of Asian restaurants (a Sydney hidden gem), where the food was reasonably priced and tasty. The neighbourhood Chippendale was trendy and there was a mall nearby where I found the things that I wanted (a bicycle pump, lol). As to the hotel itself, the admin and restaurant and bar sections were in the Old Clare Hotel. The reception staff was very friendly I arrived early in the morning, and was told the guaranteed check-in time was 3pm, and that they would have my room cleaned on an urgent basis. However I only got a call about 230pm that my room was ready. The room itself was spacious. I thought it would be noisy in the morning, but the sounds were only of the construction across the alley, and not of the traffic. The windows of the room are a storey high. The decor was industrial. Amenities came in large bottles...I wonder how these were topped up. The doors to the bathroom were clear glass and I stupidly hit my head 2x in trying to enter. The second room I stayed in was the Abercrombie room, which had a bathtub outside the bathroom area. Didn't have time to play around in that, but the idea is sexy. There was an outdoor lap pool by a bar in the roof, with some great views. However the pool was not open late. All in all, an exceptional experience and worth the money. I will return to stay in this hotel.

author: amitna1r
title: Highly recommended!
text: We stayed at Azure for a night, and during our short stay were left impressed with the quality of the hotel and service. Two things that stood out: 1. Quality of room: Very well maintained and clean. 2. Service: They communicated via SMS and answered questions. The service was great, since it allowed us to get quick answers easily. The staff were also very responsive, friendly and considerate. Even at 1:30am the person at the desk was friendly, jovial and upbeat. Apart from above, below is great too. - The hotel is at an excellent location. It has great views! - There is a park close by for kids. - The hotel is electric car friendly. It has two electrical charging points with free electric charging. - There is a nice cafe right beside which serves good food.

author: 40somethingsurfer
title: Ideal Hotel Especially if you have a Dog
text: This property went beyond our expectations. Our executive suite was well worth the extra money. Nice modern mountain decor. Large bedroom. Large sitting area with sleeper sofa (which our daughter used). Good sized refrigerator and microwave. Two large flat screen TV's. Two vanities and large dressing/closet area in bathroom. Room and property was exceptionally clean. We and many other guests had a dog and there was no evidence of pets anywhere. They had a nice pet relief area right outside the back door. Gym was well equipped and clean with a beautiful lake view. It's right in the middle of town and on the main highway. We took nice walks along the bike path to Stateline. Supermarket is 2 minutes away. The restaurant on the property is the perfect diner - good service, good food. Rate the hotel a 10!

author: michelledQ2585TR
title: 3 night stay
text: We absolutely loved this hotel. Great location in South Lake Tahoe. Close to restaurants, grocery stores, entertainment, casinos. Our room had the perfect view of the lake. There was also lake access right across the street. We did go to the restaurant for breakfast twice. It was very good and they had a nice view of the lake as well. There are bicycles to use as well. Big hot tub. The room was nice and maintained well. The bathroom was very clean. The room was very nicely decorated. Coffee maker, microwave, and fridge. Wish it had a bigger fridge though, it was very had to store leftovers in. Overall, it was wonderful. I cannot wait to come back!!

author: lynnh139
title: Can't go wrong if you love beauty
text: We stayed in a double queen room on the first floor with a view of the lake and had a beautiful view through the trees. Lake Tahoe Boulevard runs between you and the view but the room is soundproof. Even with the small patio door open and the fresh air wafting in it's still not too loud. The beds are extremely comfortable, soft sheets multiple pillows. Very clean, very nicely decorated.microwave and small fridge included. A beautiful double Decker Jacuzzi with the swimming pool below and a nice view from the Jacuzzi. The best part is they give you free bicycles for 2 to 3 hours and the bike path along The lake provides hours of fun. Within walking distance is Freschies and sprouts café for delicious and inexpensive fresh food. Also, you can't miss the boat house for drinks at sunset. I think it has the best view of the lake anywhere. This is also within walking distance. If you're a sports enthusiastt there is jet skiing, paddle boarding, boat tours, mountain bikes etc. to rent very nearby. Everything is within walking distance or bicycle distance. You can get a 30 minute reflexology massage for $40 for 30 minutes nearby. Our favorite was 'healing touch massage'. Go in September after the kids are back in school and the crowds die down. There will be less traffic.

author: Csnchz423
title: Good choice
text: I just got back from a weekend in South Lake Tahoe. We booked two standard rooms at Hotel Azure and found them to be quite comfortable. The hotel is located across the road from the lake in California. Its about a 10 min drive to state line. The rooms are small but very comfortable. We had a room in the lake side building on the 3rd floor. Our balcony had a view of the parking lot but I imagine the front facing rooms are quite nice. There is a pool on site though I never really saw anyone in it. There are free bikes available and lawn games/outdoor seating. Overall the hotel is simple, cute, and quaint. I booked this trip with short notice so there was a limited availability of accommodations. I enjoyed my stay and would recommend it to others but if I were to go back I would probably look into other places first. There was one day where our room did not get serviced by house keeping until after 2pm, which was a little strange. One of the girls at the front desk was not very friendly but luckily others working that shift were. The day of checkout I asked if I could extend to late check out since I had a late flight out and wanted to still enjoy the lake. I was told if I extended to 12pm the charge would be half a nights stay, and if I extended to 2pm it would be a full nights charge. Needless to say I booked a room at the Hard Rock for $50 and saved myself the trouble.

author: pamgoes
title: Almost a 5 star.....
text: We booked this hotel based on TA reviews and found them to be fairly accurate. We had booked a King Great room and were kindly upgraded to an executive suite with separate living area on the third floor of the building next to the pool. The room had a view of Lake Tahoe, albeit across the street and back a considerable distance from the main (and busy) road through South Lake Tahoe. Check in was efficient and seamless. (Note: The hotel will add a $50/night authorization fee to your credit card but refund that upon check out provided you have not billed items to your room. Also, the billing on your cc appears as Inn By the Lake as that is the former name of the hotel.) WiFi is included and works quite well. All rooms include a mini fridge, microwave, balcony, TV, Coffee machine (not Kurig), supplies for one regular, one decaf four-cup pot. The separate living area had a pull out sofa bed, work area and work desk, TV. The king bedded room had two end tables, closet, sink area with mirror, separate bathroom with an additional sink, toilet, and shower. Our room overlooked the hot tubs which were used a great deal during our stay. I did note that there was a lot of debris in one hot tub during our entire stay. Our only other minor issue was that the room was not well lighted. We did mention this to the front desk on departure. It seemed the bulbs in most of the lamps were either low wattage or needed replaced. Also, even though the hotel states they were recently upgraded and remodeled, the carpet in our unit (number 350) appeared to need a good cleaning. The hotel is pet friendly. Overall a good stay, prices were right, service at front desk was friendly and efficient.

author: EuniceLM
title: No sleep / Checking out
text: The hotel is nicely located across from the lake. The lobby where I checked in was pretty small, they had no restrooms inside, but across the way in their event center 😒. We were accommodated earlier than the check in which was nice. I had reserved the great room which included a king size bed and a sofa bed. The room was fairly modern, huge and we had 2 sinks. Also, the bed was ok, it was fairly bouncy but their pillows were amazing. The thermostat in the room is was got me. I can deal with the bed being bouncy but the noise when the air comes out of the vent was awfully NOISY and plus is was just a fan. The thermostat did not have an option for an air conditioning or heater. Basically it was just a very noisy air fan, which kept me and husband up all night. The next morning we were getting ready to check out at 11am. It was around 10:50am when I heard a knock from housekeeping??? I opened the door and he said we needed to check out. It seemed like we were being kicked out. This was the very first time ever in my whole life that housekeeping came before the check out time?? Wow...!! When we had the “No Disturb” sign on our door. Anyway, I will not be back that’s for sure.

author: SassyMamaErica
title: Great customer service, very clean
text: We planned the first day of our road trip to be very long. Seattle to Tahoe with 3&5 year old boys, crazy, we know. The drive actually went well. However, we didn't make it to Tahoe till 2:30am. We arrived at our Airbnb and the door code would not work. The owner did not respond within 5-10 min, so I just decided to find a hotel. This one was close with great reviews. It was 330 by the time I was asking for a room. The gentleman man was so very kind! We planned to stay that night (3am check in, and the next). He had already done his banking for the night and said we could just stay for free. We were given a lake front room, which was a perfect view for drinking our coffee from our French press. I used their pot to make the hot water. It was very clean and updated. Plenty of linens, pillows, and towels. Beds were comfortable and the black out curtains worked well. Parking lot is well lit and I heard it was patrolled by local law enforcement. We didn't have any problems with a loaded down truck.

author: barbarawU9662NI
title: Our stay at the Azure
text: We stayed at the Azure from Tuesday to Friday, leaving Friday. We were booked to have a lake view which I would call it a peek-a-boo view. We had a balcony which had an iron railing, then outside of the iron railing were 3 boards going across blocking a lot of the view of the pool, and what view there was of the lake. The noise from the traffic on Hwy 50 was bothersome. We had a hard time getting into our room due to the card and lock. Half the time we couldn't get into our room and had to keep trying. This was a PITA. It was nice to have a frig, microwave and coffee maker in the room which we used during our stay. It was also nice to have the hotel within walking distance of Safeway. We bought snacks and things for breakfast since we don't like to eat out that often. Safeway fit the bill for us. We found the restaurants expensive and the food not appealing. The Bear restaurant was okay, we had breakfast there on our way home. No complaints there. Wifi was great and was free! All in all, I don't know if we would stay at the Azure again.

author: 267lawrenceb
title: Basecamp Hotel for grownups
text: I'm a huge fan of the ACE Hotel chain and I liked the idea of the Basecamp Hotel but after reading through the reviews a couple times, I realized I needed something a bit more grown up.... Cold rooms - Thin walls! I found the Azure on trip advisor... The rooms looked cool and the price was actually very reasonable. I was also traveling with my dog and they were more than accommodating. Checkin was easy and the room wasn't a second rate pet owners room like some places, the room was beautiful. Really contemporary with just enough reclaimed wood to be on trend without looking dated. The bath was all new and overall the place still had a light new carpet smell. For my dog they supplied a huge fluffy bed and had onsite pet areas when the time came... Very together. The room was lakeside (which means street side) but the place was super quiet. We had neighbors next door but aside from hearing them in the hall, we wouldn't had known they were there. Overall great experience. The only issue we had that we had to call to find out the pet fee and notify them we were bringing our buddy along. You can add a note if you book on their website, but because we booked through Tripadvisor (getaroom) we didn't have that option. I'm sure something that can be improved in the future.

author: biggrumpybadger
title: Lovely rooms
text: I stayed at Hotel Azure recently for 10 days on a solo snowboarding holiday. I have stayed here before (over 10 years ago) and the rooms have been renovated and look very nice. Staff were very helpful. I would book this hotel again without a moment's thought. I did have a few very minor whinges though.. * There's an outdoor hot tub and whilst gowns are provided, slippers are not so bring your own. Slippers had been provided on my previous visit so I hadn't thought to bring any. * On my previous visit, a continental breakfast was provided. This is no longer the case. The Beach Bear restaurant is right next door, which is handy, but adds a little extra expense to your visit. * My room, despite having been refurbished well, had a ridiculously small bath, too short and shallow for a proper soak after a day on the slopes. This, I hear, is common to American bathtubs though. The shower was very nice but the poor size of the tub made it seem like the presence of the bath was more of a box-ticking exercise and not thought-through. * Despite the name change to Hotel Azure, the only place this name appears seems to be on the website. The sign outside the hotel still bears the old name as does the printed card on the phone, the champagne flutes, etc. Not really a big issue but the lack of consistency, I feel, seems a little unprofessional and not in keeping with a quality contemporary hotel. * Common areas such as corridors don't seem to have received the same refurbishment as the rooms. They were clean and looked-after but could do with a bit of an update so that they reflect the same contemporary feel as the rooms. As I said, these are all minor gripes and next time I visit Tahoe, I will have no qualms about staying here again. The refrigerator and coffee machine in the rooms are good touches and the bed was large, firm and comfortable.

author: mommyreeze
title: Snow Trip
text: We stayed this past weekend for 2 nights and enjoyed our stay very much. Hotel staff are great and friendly, despite having minor issues with both check in/out. Not quite sure what happened, but the front desk's demeanor in handling was great. We took advantage of the free shuttle to Sierra At Tahoe, and have to say it's such a great way to go. It was great not having to deal with driving back down 50, parking, navigating traffic, etc. The shuttle picks up across the street, a little bit past the Bear Beach Cafe. Drop off was a little bit further past Yama Noodles but still convenient. We had the King Great Room on the 3rd floor, facing the lake. The room is a great size, with a king bed, pull out couch, table, fridge, and microwave. There was a lot of room to spread out, and I liked that the bathroom was separated from the main space. And this may sound like such a little thing, but the shower was great. The pool and sauna are heated, and it's very enticing to see steam billowing from the area when the temps are single digit, but the thought of freezing in between getting your clothes off and into the water nixed any thought of using the sauna (though that didn't stop others at all!). Overall it was a great stay. The room was quiet, the bed and pillows were comfortable, and the property appears exactly like the photos. I did overhear others complain but they had ground floor rooms in high traffic areas. Not much can be done about that besides making sure you get a room on a high floor. Would definitely stay here again.

author: saf7670
title: Stuck in the 70’s
text: This hotel like the Heritage next door, a reminiscent of what was a very good hotel in Manila in the 1970’s, and does have a certain charm. Check in was fine, quick and efficient and I was given a room on the 11th floor. Which is ok but the lift only goes to the 10th floor, you then take to the stairs. Room is spacious, clean and has a comfortable bed. The aircon was excellent, I turned it down to low cool, but then had to get up in the night to turn off as I was freezing!! Edsa noise can be heard 24 hrs which can be annoying, and takes a little getting used to. The aircraft noise however is bad! The hotel is right on the flight path from MNL, the end of the runway is only a few hundred metres away! in fact you can watch the planes take off from the corridor windows, and see them go overhead a few seconds later. And Manila has flights 24 hours a day! Breakfast is basic, a choice of American which is bacon, egg, toast, or Filipino porridge. You get a choice of coffee or fruit juice. The pool looks big in the online booking sites, but is actually quite small, but looks clean and inviting on a hot Manila day. Hotel requests a deposit of 2000php, which can be an issue for some who have just arrived at MNL, and have yet to exchange currency. They will accept credit card deposit. The big big negative for this hotel, apart from the outside noise. Is the lack of free WiFi. You can pay for WiFi but at an extortionate rate. I stayed here because I was watching a band at the nearby bluebay walk, and didn’t fancy a long walk afterwards.

author: kommandantl
title: A nice place for a 3-Star !
text: The hotel was neat. The room was big with toilet, dining place, seating area, kitchen and balcony. They provided kitchen facilities and toiletries. The bed/pillows were all comfortable. The AC was good. Overall it was a great place. The staff was helpful. The security was tight. I would definitely come back. The restaurant had great food and great view of the pool. I didn't really like the location. It is right at the highway and walking at night does not feel safe. Always wise to catch a cab or grab at the hotel to go near by places. SM MOA is the closest mall some 10 mins ride away and is a great place to hang out. I also didn't like that the toilet sink is outside the toilet and the toilet does not have a bidet but not at all a deal breaker. The internet is paid but didn't bother me since I always use pre-paid internet. Don't expect posh luxury look for a 3-star hotel. So those who are used to high class lifestyle, you'd certainly feel the backwardness of this hotel but again, you get what you pay for. We enjoyed our stay.

author: BalikpapanRain
title: You get what you pay for
text: This is the third time I stayed in this place. This time was the longest. I was there for four days. It is just so cheap. I was street side but on the top floor which was a little quieter. I requested a room in the back so I would be away from the constant 24/7 sound of honking and traffic, but apparently, it was not available. I hoped to swim, but the pool is always full of screaming kids. It would be nice if hotels would make like a 9-11 ADULTS ONLY swim time, for people who want to relax in a pool without selfish, poorly raised kids yelling everywhere. The hotel still does not have hot water. You do not really NEED hot water in the Philippines, but it does take a minute to adjust to in the shower. My biggest complaint, is they absolutely KILL you on internet. Every day, having to PURCHASE internet cards, wonder when they are going to expire, etc. What a headache in a time when free wifi is in practically every hotel in the world. I needed to stay one more day, but I went to a nearby hotel for the sole reason that I was sick of paying to use wifi. Copacabana also charges a very high rate on items in the mini bar. The other hotels I stayed in were literally charging HALF of what I got charged at Copacabana. I never leave that place happy that I stayed, but again, it is cheap to stay there for a good location.

author: Fabulousniki
title: First time in the Philippines as an Adult .....
text: So I was a tad bid nervous with the entire ordeal. Arrived late and followed my cousin's suggestion to stay at this apartment/hotel. The price was right, staff accommodating, clean spacious room and mini bar. My room consisted of two rooms - the living area with living room (no TV) 4 seat table and kitchen and an Air Conditioned bed room with two twin beds, bathroom, safe (so important) and TV. The hotel is situated on a busy highway and is surrounded by other hotels, entertainment complex (for those interested in a "adult activities), chain restaurants, and Mall of Asia. It's also 3 kilometers from the NAI Airport, which could mean a 15 min trip or 6 hour trip, depending on how crazy Manila traffic wants to be. Seriously. On my two night stay - I was able to go to a few restaurants, visit MOA, and entertain family comfortably. Room service food was delicious. It was not a difficult choice to stay here again before my trip back home. A few tips for westerners - the mini bar is hand counted at check out. So if you are in a rush - make sure to allow yourself an extra 20 minutes for an attendant to count out your fridge. Make sure you do your own count. Don't be alarmed by the armed guards outside. You want them there! Although they ask you to sign in guests, do not be alarmed to see older western men walking into the hotel at early hours with very young female friends. You are across the street from the EDSA entertainment complex. So those with impressionable young children should take note of this. I think this will be my go to place between flights in/out and around the Philippines. I would probably stay in a hotel in Makati if Manila was my main destination.

author: CharityCupidMon
title: Exceeded Expectations
text: Wow! I booked this one when me and my 5yr old nephew were still in Baguio. We were coming down to Manila to get our flight to Bacolod the next day. Upon arrival, I had problems with my bank and couldn't withdraw some cash so my sis sent some via LBC. Unfortunately, LBC was close at 5PM. So I asked the hotel if we can stay for without deposit of 2k ( which is refundable) and I'll just pay half of it and get back first thing in the morning when I catch the LBC open. I even asked them for the child's sake, to let us in. And so the attendant respectfully said, "yes, mam, so your baby can rest. He looks tired." And assisted us to our room. Who could've done than better? I truly was so thankful for being o considerate. Room was so spacious and the outside view was excellent. Near the airport, MOA, Starcity and almost the tourist spots around Pasay. Accessible as it lays just beside Manila Heritage and the national highway :) Price is right. In fact, affordable. They have a pool too :) <3 Definitely gonna stay here again. PS: I knew this hotel apartment because in my college years we stayed here for our industrial tour :) The only prob is that you have to pay another for their wifi :|

author: kelapa44
title: Very clean, not an apartment, beware of minibar cheats, no free wifi
text: Very clean hotel. From the airport to the hotel which was a 10 minute drive, the taxi cost was 750 pesos. But the hotel can book cheap taxis to the airport at about half the price – 350 or 450 pesos. As it says apartment hotel and the pictures showed a stove, pots – I expected such items but we only had a kettle. Beware of drinks from the mini-bar taken by others. We arrived to the hotel room with the bell-boy but we did not notice an empty mango juice can. It was just after the bell-boy left that we noticed it on the table. Since we were to tired we just went to bed. Next day we told the hotel management about it but they did not believe us. (we read other reviews that someone even had the whole mini-bar charged to them). Lifts were a bit weird. They go only to the 10th floor then you have to walk up a flight of stairs (if you get rooms on the 11th floor). But the bell-boy can carry heavy bags if you have any. Air-con was a bit on the warm side. Sink is outside the toilet. Wifi is not free.

author: Nyree75
title: Studio and 1br on top floors not great but others are immaculate!
text: A large group of us booked rooms here; a family of 11 booked a 4br apartment, a couple booked a 1br apartment and I had a studio apartment. After booking, I was advised there was no elevator to my floor, the 11th and when I went to my room, I could ask them to help me take up my suitcase. We went to the couple's 1br apt which was basically painted black with a red feature wall. The room had an aircon and tv which looked like they time jumped straight out of the 80s! We decided then that I should just get a portable bed there and look for something better in the morning. But they wouldn't refund us for my room. So, my studio apt was painted in the same dark and dank colors and I too had electrics from the 80s. It was ok, I wasn't bothered too much but then I went to have a shower which the bathroom smelled like a urinal and had a few ants on the floor. I really needed sleep so was super quick. I cdidnt get much sleep; when I turned the aircon off which was blowing in my face, all I could here was the traffic do I got up at 5, had another shower and went outside on the balcony to watch an amazing sunrise! Wifi isn't free, I paid 100php for 1 hour. There's no breakfast, no offers on anything which I thought was pretty bad as the room was certainly not worth the money. So why do I give them 3 stars?! Well, in the morning, I went down to family of 11 to see how they were doing and their room was immaculate! It was modern, new tv, air con, decked out with nice furniture. It was really homely and like a completely different hotel. I'm sure not all the rooms were as bad as mine and perhaps they're renovating from the bottom up so, for convenience, I'd stay there again but would be requesting one of the more modern rooms!

author: 349karenn
title: Well I wanted to be close to the airport
text: My family just needed an overnight close to the airport, as we flew in from sydney and the next day flying on to El Nido. 1. Close to airport? Check. 20 mins from international, and in monday am peak 15 mins to ITI Hanger (they told us to allow an hour though) 2. 24 hour reception? Check. 3. Restaurant in case flight delayed and you dont want to go out? Check. If thats all you need then its adequate. Don't go out though, its a scary area. Pool is nice. Just what you need after a long flight. 2 bedroom apartment actually had 3 rooms and was quit large. We were on the 4th floor and it was noisy all night with traffic beeping.

author: Mangereman
title: Value for price
text: My wife and I stayed for 2 nights on arriving in Manila until we moved on to longer term Condo accommodation at MOA.
