The spa is a joke and dont even expect to take a shower before your flight if you have been at the beach all day and already checked out. They have no towels and no hairdryer available in the spa. I had to blowdry my hair at the front desk in front of all the guests. People complain about walking up the hill but it is not bad. We are in our 30's and walked it quite a few times. King Dee at the excursions desk was sweet and helpful, we rented a scooter for a day trip and it was well worth it. The team at breakfast was good and many staff there took the time to chat and smile. Next time we come to Thailand we will skip Phuket alltogether and go straight to Khao Lak. It is much more natural and less touristy.

author: 734rachelv
title: Don't want to leave!
text: We are here for my husbands birthday. It's the first time we have been to Nook Dee and we will definitely return. For my husbands birthday I asked if they had any balloons and they said they had already ordered a cake for him- so sweet! We are in a corner room (301) and the views are amazing. It's a little bit small for the 3 of us as our daughter is a teenager. The only complaint I have is that there is not enough wardrobe space/drawers for clothes. The pictures don't lie on the website. Our room is exactly the same as photos. Every evening there is happy hour 5-7 on roof top (weather permitting) the bean bags are very cool and super comfy! The staff are exceptional! From housekeeping, front office to Food and Beverage. Alex is our favorite, so friendly!! Even though he was in the bar he asked us how our room was, asked if everything was ok. I mentioned that the self closing door wasn't closing properly and by the time we got back to our room it was fixed😃 The breakfast buffet is great- a wide range to choose from. Caters for all nationalities. We still have another 4 days here and are looking forward to the Friday night BBQ. Love this place!

author: BjornWilliamo
title: One of the best hotels I have been to!
text: This is one of the absolute best hotels I have been to. First of, the hotel and building it self is very fresh and clean. It's a pretty new hotel so that's what to expect I guess. The rooms are very nice as well. What is really good about this hotel is the location. It's located between Kata Beach and Kata Noi. And Kata Noi is one of the better "big" beaches I have been to in Phuket. As there are not many hotels near Kata Noi, this Is a great option. Do note that the hotel is located on a hill. It got an amazing view over Kata Noi but it can be a bit enoying to walk up and down the hill everyday if you plan to be at the beach everyday. They do offer a shuttle service for free which is great. I recommend renting a motorcycle though. What was even better was the staff. They where extremely friendly and helpful. My girlfriend got sick while we where staying there. When she was sick they brought us a lot of extra water and did everything they could to help us. If you plan on going to the southern part of Phuket I really recommend this hotel!

author: melc13
title: Fantastic hotel with amazing views
text: We stayed for 4 nights in room 311. On arrival we were given a welcome drink & cold towel. The staff are amazing - so friendly & nothing was too much trouble. The manager frequently came round to check that everything was ok. The room was lovely & adorned with elephants. Bathroom had a bath & separate walk in shower. The piece de resistance is the infinity pool with amazing views over Kata Noi beach. There are plenty of loungers but to be honest it was never that busy. Breakfast was pretty special too. Everything you could ask for - fresh fruit, cereals. pastries & an egg station. The omelettes were to die for made by a lovely chef who supported Arsenal! They seemed to cater for the Chinese market quite a lot too. The hotel offer a courtesy shuttle to Kata Noi & Kata beach which is quite useful but its only a 10 min walk down the hill to Kata if you are feeling energetic. There is a rooftop bar which is open from 5-7pm which offers amazing sunset views. Definitely worth a visit where you can sip your sundowners! I would certainly recommend this hotel for its unique location & lovely staff.

author: 3inthesun
title: Absolutely loved it.
text: Nook Dee in Kata Beach was one of the pricier hotels we stayed in while in Thailand and if was well worth it. Stunning view when you arrive of the infinity pool and blue waters at Kata Noi beach below and the hillside greenery of Kata. Very kind staff who try to get to know you was a plus. Location: yes, like other reviews state, the hotel is up on a hill. But to us, totally worth the unobstructed view from our panoramic deluxe room and from the pool. We did thr walk up and down at least once daily but there is an hourly shuttle but I think the first one into 'town' is at 10am and the last shuttle up is at 9 or 10pm. It's only during peak sun/heat hours that the walk up the hill is brutal. But we were used to walking a ton every day having come from Bangkok and Chiang Mai. Room:clean, modern, comfy bed and linen, very nice bathroom and balcony with great view of sunset! (We had a panoramic deluxe, worth it!). I think I asked for the top floor so that probably helped with our view. Food: we had dinner once at the hotel resto our first night when we were too tired to go out. We had massaman curry and chicken satay, both were pretty good. Pricey but fair. Breakfast buffet was delightful! Made to order coffee (aka cappuccinos or whatever you wanted), eggs, bacon, omelette plus Asian and American breakfast staples like noodles, fruit, meats, croissants, toast etc. Wait staff knew us by name and were so kind. Infinity pool was awesome and we took advantage and treated ourselves with the 2 for 1 drinks at happy hour. Some were made strong, others not so much but still delicious.

author: 278leahs
title: Excellent Gem on a hill above Kata Beach
text: Overall the Nook Dee is a great hotel. The rooms are clean and modern and include fridges, beach bags, flipflops, towels & a safe. The pool area is spotless and absolutely beautiful on a hot day or at night when it is lit up. This is a great hotel for people who want to be away from the chaos of Kata Beach. That being said, this is NOT a hotel for people who want to walk outside and be next to all of the shops / restaurants / beach. The Nook Dee sits on a very steep hill which adds to its charm and the view, however, while it is relatively easy to walk down to the beach (10 minutes), it is extremely steep to walk back up. There are a lot of blind corners and many tourists who rent mopeds who have no idea how to drive them up and down steep hills. The Nook Dee provides a shuttle service to and from the beach, but unfortunately the times are lacking as you can't get down to Kata until 9am and there is a gap in pickup/ drop off from 5pm- 9pm at night. Kata is bustling until at least 11 pm every night, so this is a bit disappointing. Otherwise, I have no complaints. It was a great choice at a reasonable price by western hotel standards. They also provided a comprehensive breakfast that appealed to their client base - mainly eastern and western Europeans & Chinese. There is something for everyone. My suggestion is to spend the money on breakfast & on a room that faces outward towards the ocean. It is a bit quieter as it is away from the pool / deck / lawn area.

author: jlbmpms
title: Beautiful hotel, peaceful location, great stay
text: We were very happy with our stay at Nook Dee. The rooms were immaculately clean, spacious, and had a beautiful view over the sea. The pool was amazing with a gorgeous view and ample lounge chairs to sit in with umbrellas. Staff were very friendly and accomodating. Breakfast every morning had a huge variety of food and drink and staff were very welcoming. This hotel is around 700m from the main street so it has a peaceful and relaxing vibe away from the noise. It takes around 10 minutes to walk down the hill to the main street which is an easy walk but there is an hourly shuttle if walking is not for you. The walk home is up the hill but we found this very achievable and walked everywhere we went. Very accessible location. Wifi was decent, required regular sign-ins but was a sufficient speed for calling overseas and loading the internet. The only area for improvement here is the gym. The gym has 1 bike, 1 cross trainer (which doesn't switch on properly) and 1 treadmill. There is 1 multi-functional weights machine and some hand weights. This really only accommodates one couple at a time. My boyfriend and I had to alternate turns on the treadmill which was frustrating when we both incorporate running in our workouts. Aside from this we still used the gym everyday and found the equipment to be sufficient. Overall, we loved Nook Dee! The views from the hotel are absolutely gorgeous and the relaxing vibe was exactly what we needed. Thank you to the staff for being so helpful and welcoming!

author: johnwoodhall
title: Great hotel fab staff
text: Just returned from an eleven night stay at Nook Dee. We seemed to have stayed longer than most as it would appear many travelers visit various locations in Thailand and hop from one location to another after a few days. Overall our stay at the Nook Dee was an enjoyable experience. The hotel is beautiful and offers its guests fantastic views over the bays of kata and beyond. The facilities at the hotel are excellent but by far the hotels best quality is it's staff who are from the security guy outside to its manager the friendliest and most polite hotel staff that I've ever experienced in my travels. The pool area is superb, the pool bar and restaurant areas are well ran and immaculately looked after. Breakfast was great with the views over the bays stunning. Plenty of choice to suit all breakfast needs and freshly cooked bacon sausage and eggs on request. The rooms all offer sea views We were on a low floor but could still see out over the kata bay area and the surrounding hills. The rooms are well kept and presented with high quality fixtures and fittings and very large comfortable beds. We found the hill up which the hotel is located up very steep but without the hill you'd lose the super views, personally I'd endure the hill to get the views. We walked down but after a couple of sweltering walks back up we resorted to tuk tuk journeys to get us back to the hotel. These are pricey given the short journey but you can barter them down. We used to pay 140baht but far better than walking back up in the humidity. Would definitely recommend this hotel to others and gladly return should we return to phuket. Great staff make this hotel stand out from the others they're a credit to the owners and management.

author: NeleW127
title: Nice but too expensive
text: Nice new resort but too expensive. It's next to Foto Hotel. Room is clean but the shower is unreliable. I could not let my son (7 years) alone in the shower because it went from cold to very hot and visa versa. The pressure of the water was realy good so the bath filled quickly with water. (you can wath TV from inside your bath) You get 2 bottles of free water but if you leave it in your fridge they don't give new one. Happy hour from 17pm - 19pm on cocktails, mocktails and beer. A small chang is 120 bath and cocktails 200-240 bath. Free shuttle to the beach at 10am, 13pm, 15pm and 18pm. It is only 5-10 minutes walking to the restaurants at Kata beach. It's a really steap hill but for young people no problem. There is also a restaurant just next door and if you go to the street and turn right, you find also a couple restaurants. Very large pool with a nice view. We went in july and the sun was gone at 16pm at the pool. We expected more at breakfast. You have all the basic but nothing special. Toast, eggs, cake, yoghurt, 2 hot dishes, fruits, noodle bar,... They serve really good coffee at breakfast (jura machine). The daybed is big enough for an adult or child.

author: 891ammarh
title: great view, excellent service-5 star
text: me and my wife stayed there for 5 nights. Our first impression of the place? splendid!! ...the decor of the room, the whole theme of the hotel, the colours, the people, the view, the pool...all were top class and one of a kind. Not very crowded and guests staying there were all nice. We booked a sea facing room on the third floor and woke up every morning to a beautiful view of the beach and hill side forest. All amenities were new and found no issues with anything at all. Breakfast was amazing with soo many options along with the view of ocean if u choose to sit outside. loved the waffles and coconut puddings. The only issue is that it is located on a steep hill. Easy to walk down to the market (a 5 min walk) and further 5 min walk to the beach. Problem is coming back up. a 5 min walk on a steep hill will take u 20 mins and a lot of stamina. time yourself to use hotel shuttle or just take a taxi from market to climb up (should charge 150 Baht if u negotiate). Overall, excellent value for money.

author: man7drake
title: A pleasant hotel to chill and relax
text: For those who did not know, this hotel is located about an hour's drive from the airport. We used metered taxi and it costs about 900. This hotel is located on a hill, overlooking the beautiful Andaman sea. I stayed at the deluxe room which is on 3rd floor and the view is absolutely stunning especially during the sunset. You can always go up to the rooftop for better views. The room is large enough with king size bed and very tastefully decorated. There are few minor problems though. First the hot water from the shower is inconsistent. Second, for unknown reasons, there are quite a number of small ants on the dressing table. Not sure if this only happens to my room. I didn't see these as big issues so I didn't complain but hope the management can take note of that. Breakfast is included throughout our stay. There's only slight variation on the breakfast spread which I managed to observe. While the spread isn't that impressive, their bircher muesli tastes good. There is a gym next to the spa which they advertise it opens 24 hours but when we were there in the morning it was closed. Access-wise, we spent quite substantial amount on taxi and tuktuk just to get around the town. The hotel provides shuttle service but with the last trip is at 6pm, we didn't have choice but to take taxi or tuktuk back after our dinner. The fares are more or less like below: Hotel to Patong - 400 Baht by taxi Hotel to Kata town (near Kata night market) - 150 Baht by taxi Patong to Hotel - 500 Baht by taxi Kata town to hotel - 150 Baht by tuktuk We even tried walking back once. I wouldn't say it's a pleasant walk because it's hilly and dangerous and the area is not very well lit at night. All in all, if you are looking for a pure relaxation, this might be a good choice for you.

author: Chase42
title: Great hotel with a few caveats
text: This is a new hotel and luxurious for the price we paid. The staff were all very kind and professional. A few things of note: we had some issues with the cards not staying in the reader and thus turning off the electricity; the staff remedied this with thicker cards. That said, the fact that the electricity (including the fridge) turned off when you left the room did not fit with the luxury angle Nook Dee is going for. Pretty inconvenient if you ask me. Secondly, the showers were amazing but water temperature was very inconsistent and made showers unpredictably hot or cold. The staff compensated us for that which was appreciated. Fitness center was lacking a bit. One treadmill, one elliptical, and one stationary bike. The machines were unplugged when I entered, the lights were off, and the AC was off too making the room really hot. It seemed like they were trying to cut costs everywhere with respect to electricity. Lastly, the hill, as everyone mentions is frustrating to climb. I consider myself to be in decent shape and broke a sweat every time I climbed up it. I don't think the shuttle service taking guests down and back up four times per day is adequate, it should really be every 90 minutes at least. All in all, loved the decor of the hotel, really enjoyed the service of the staff, but there are a few things that need to be tweaked before it can go all the way.

author: 6aishwaryas
title: Panoramic Sea View Room
text: Had an excellent stay at Nook Dee Resort. It was by far the best hotel/resort I've ever stayed in. Staff service was excellent (interacted with two of the staffs mainly, Pearl Dee and King Dee and they both were great, friendly, gave us information and tips, gave us as much discounts as they could for transport etc) The other staffs were also very nice. Outdoor view from the breakfast area was beyond amazing. There was good warm and cold water shower. Room was extremely clean and the aircon temperature was just right, not too cold and not too hot. View was so breathtaking. The breakfast was also good. Had a mix of Thai and international buffet. The hotel could improve on the transport. There were only about 4 timings every few hours to the beach. Maybe there could be one every hour to the main road as well. The road is very steep and hence it was very inconvinient to walk up and down to main road. If we took a cab it would be about $8 for a journey less than 5 minutes. Besides that everything else was great. I would advice you to take the speedboat tour from the hotel itself as they offer a variety and the prices are negotiable because the staffs really go all out to satisfy their customers. The lobby and outdoor infinity pool was very beautiful and the rooftop had a 360 degree view of the Kata beach and hills.

author: 156yuh
title: Adequate but a lot could be improved
text: I am a pretty picky traveller so this review is meant to give constructive criticism because when it comes to hospitality detail is everything. I booked this hotel purely for the panoramic view advertised on the website. The room with the best view was supposed to be the corner rooms and that was what I reserved. Issues upon arrival - There was no bell boy to receive me and direct me to the reception. Though it was a little pass 8pm, it is not that late to have no one stationed at the entrance Check in was relatively smooth but the staff were a little distracted and kept talking to each other I was shown to my room but it was very hot. Rooms should always be pre-air conditioned before the guest arrive. Despite being the night time I could tell my room did not have the same panorama view as advertised on the website. I called and realized that there are two different sides for the corner rooms. Unfortunately, my side faced the roads and mountains with construction more. Issues during the stay - The water temperature is very inconsistent, it's either too hot or too cold. The front desk manager and her team tried very hard to fix it but was not very successful. I was later informed that they will update the piping system soon to fix this issue. There was no tissue paper, only toilet paper. The toiletry is also pretty basic. There were flies in my room but the room cleaning managed to fix that problem later on. Overall, I had a good stay and that is because of the stunning sunset and ocean view in the room. The experience and service can be greatly improved. It needs more attention to detail. The staff sometimes seem too causal and relaxed. If you just want to be a basic hotel, you can ignore my comments but a hotel with such amazing view and interesting decor, it would be a waste.

author: AMKH123
title: 3 nights at Nook Dee Kata beach resort
text: We visited Phuket earlier last month and stayed in Nook Dee from 10th-13th May, 2016. I don't have enough nice words to say about this hotel. The vibe of this hotel is so positive and friendly. As soon as you enter, you are welcomed by wonderful smiles and hospitality plus breathtaking views of the ocean from the hotel. Not to forget the stunning infinity pool facing the sea and the bar just outside the lobby. I loved the staff of the hotel, they were very sweet and tried their absolute best to make your stay enjoyable. We got an upgrade to a beautiful room with gorgeous views of the sea - the Lub Dee room on 2nd floor. It was nicely cleaned on a daily basis. The rooftop of the lobby also offers great views and is a relaxing spot to enjoy your time with your partner. The hotel was sparkling clean. The only thing I would like to point out is that people who may have trouble walking up and down the hill (10-15 mins to downtown roughly by walk) could rent a scooter from the hotel (450 baht a day) or from downtown (300 baht a day). The hotel does offer a shuttle service 4 times a day to the beach so that may also be used to go to downtown. The massages around the area are superb, two chefs was a great restaurant and there are other nice places in this area to visit as well. Goodluck to all planning to stay at this fabulous resort. I already miss it, hope to be back soon again 😊

author: Catherine079
title: Just perfect
text: The resort is very new and it clearly shows. We thoroughly enjoyed the pool in the afternoon, the magical view and sunset from our room (we booked the Deluxe Panoramic Sea View), the nice hipster decoration of the rooms and the view from the bathroom. The restaurant is very nice with plenty of choices. We also had a dinner which was also very nice. They also offer some buffet dinner options which I think are very good (we didn't have it since it was Italian night and we preferred to continue discovering Thai cuisine). Cocktails were nice, although not the best we had in Thailand. There is a free mini bar in the room and coffee making facilities which is also very helpful, along with the bucket of ice brought by a nice lady each afternoon. In the mornings we preferred Kata Noi beach that was more peaceful than Kata. I will agree with the rest of the reviewers that the only downside is the absence of more frequent transfer to the village. It's only a 1 minute drive by car, so why don't they add more? We strolled down by foot in the afternoon, and it was ok. But then, at night after dinner, you either have to take a taxi or go up by foot. The thing is that the taxi drivers tell you that they need 200 baht to take you up, and we talk about a 50 second drive. It's not the amount of money that is significant, but it's the real "steal" that bothers you. The hotel could help the visitors avoid this experience by adding a couple more mini-shuttles. I think we have met the owner of the place ? not sure, but he was the most kind Thai man we met during our trip.Back to the resort now, the check in was good, but really, the receptionists must really understand that they should first say "Welcome" and then say "Passports please".... Believe me this was the first thing the receptionist said when we entered the hotel after a 5 hour trip. After, they gave us tea and fresh towels, but again, I would prefer a smile and a "Welcome" than these. But apart from this, it was overall a very nice experience and I would choose the same hotel again.

author: astra
title: Great stay
text: Stayed here for four nights in a room on second level with a balcony which looked to Kata and Karon. Room was a good size. Bed was quite hard so I asked them to put a quilt under the sheet which made it softer. Pillows were good too. TV channels were decent. HBO and sport channels. Bathroom was lovely however the lighting was dark over the sink. Breakfast was very good. Pool was lovely but it was so hot that it was like a huge bath. This is a small hotel so not a ton of people to fight for the sunbeds. We ate lunch and had room service one night. Food was quite good. The staff are amazing. The manager is a lovely guy...sorry I can't recall his name. The shuttle bus was a blessing as the walk back up Heartbreak Hill is exhausting. The taxi fare is a set 200THB so can get a bit expensive if you don't take the shuttle back. This hotel is up the hill so not very close to the beach. Overall a very pleasant stay.

author: Istok
title: Really good, but not perfect
text: We like trying out new hotels, that is why we booked 4 nights here. The good thing about new hotels is that they are usually clean, the furnitures are not worn out and the staff is (usually) were helpful and taking care. On the opposite, you can often find things which can or even must be improved. We had similar experience at Nook Dee. All-in-all, it is a superb hotel with a great location and nice design, but there are a few things that needs some attention from the management. We knew about the location, so we were not surprised that it is on a hill. And it was not a big issue because we rented a motorbike. This is where we got disappointed first: the hotel asks for 450 baht per day, which is a rip off. Especially because only 20 meters from the hotel you can get the same for 300 baht. Secondly, many of the staff members can hardly speaks English. The third negative thing is the water pressure in the shower and that you cannot really regulate the temperature. Another thing that bothered me a bit was that our room (109) had a door to the adjacent one. Of course, it was closed, but it was not sound-proof; I could hear the television and the conversation from the other room. What I also missed was a television from the gym and some comfortable chairs from the top terrace. Ok, enough of the negative things. There are a lot of things that we liked: the design of the rooms, the pool, the bar next to it, the view from the pool/room/top terrace. We ate at the restaurant once (as the rain was pouring cats and dogs outside) and it was really delicious. The hotel manager was present and he had kind words to the guests. Altogether, we had a nice stay at Nook Dee. Tips for restaurant: go to Chai Thai restaurant or Kitchen, which look simple (or even dirty) but deliver excellent food for very cheap.

author: fraans
title: Nice modern hotel. Friendly staff.
text: My family and I had a good stay at this new hotel. Rooms are really nice. Spacious and well decorated. View of Kata and Kata noi beach. 200THB to go back and forth to Kata by tuktuk. Shutlle is 4x a day. Staff is really friendly but not all speak English very well. Breakfast was ok, just ok. Good coffee. Possible to eat outside with great view of the beach. There is a small bar outside at the pool, but when raining you cannot have a drink anywhere inside. We ate at the restaurant once. This was bad experience. Dirty salad. The didn't charge me though.

author: DoctorButt
title: Awesome, everything we wanted
text: We had a fantastic stay at Nook Dee. The atmosphere is much more relaxed than other hotels we've visited, and the staff have a great knack of making you feel comfortable and well looked-after without being all over you. We were lucky enough to get an upgrade for our first night, so we experienced two different rooms: Lub Dee and Fun Dee. Both were beautifully appointed, very quiet and peaceful. Fun Dee (with the outdoor jacuzzi) was especially nice. We didn't have dinner in the restaurant but the the breakfast was very good. There are millions of dining options along Kata Beach, where we walked most days - it's uphill on the way back but not bad at all! The pool and pool bar were lovely too, with an incredible view. The gym facilities were a welcome bonus... Small but well-equipped with complimentary water and towels. Wifi was PERFECT throughout hotel. Take note: taxis are much more expensive when ordered from the hotel (I think this is a standard thing). Much cheaper if you can to go down to Kata and negotiate a price - for us it meant the difference between 1200 and 600 THB for trips to Phuket Town. The only things I'd change: - More information in the in-room compendium about the surrounding area, hotel facilities (i.e. restaurant/bar and room service menus) and available tours - More snack/light options on the daytime menus - Longer room service hours (ends at 10pm) Otherwise, no complaints! I'd stay again.

author: U1118WFalanc
title: An absolutely "AMAZING" Retreat
text: During a 4 night stay in Patong, we decided that we wanted to venture a short distance South for an evening and visit the beautiful resorts of Kata and Kata Noi. We looked several properties and almost discounted the nook dee as it was nestled on a hilltop between resorts, it's location actually proved to be an incredible bonus as it offer stunning views of both resorts and sunset. To the nook dee! We arrived to a warmth of smiles that were worn by every member of staff throughout our stay. We were humbled by the Thai hospitality. The hotel has a trendy vibe but does not forget it's Thai roots with vibrant silks and authentic features. The rooms (ours was a Lub Dee) were incredible! Clean and tastefully decorated with all the amenities you could wish for and more. The infinity pool sells itself with stylish loungers by the bar. Please try the mango with sticky rice, a revelation! Evening dinner was poolside amongst beautiful lights and the food was simply delicious. Buffet breakfast offered an extensive range of western and Asian (hot/cold) options and the coffee was fresh and wonderful! Do not be put off by the location being nestled hillside between these beautiful and vibrant beaches (it's a massive selling point). A beach shuttle is offered, taxis are cheap and we found many guests chose to stay at the nook dee in the evening due to its setting and amenities. We were both very sad to leave this beautiful property and its people and will always look back with fond memories. Thank you so very much!

author: alconan
title: Pleasant Stay
text: Nice stay at the Nook Dee Kata Beach. Sadly we stayed to long, a fortnight here is far to long. It is not a luxurious pamper fest of a tropical island super hotel. It is a drop in move on Motel. It has great features, the pool is divine, the rooms are lovely ( on the small side) and generally the staff are pleasant. The food, which could be more of a feature at the Hotel was very good. Our problem was two fold, we spent too long at Nook Dee, it is not somewhere to spend a fortnights holiday. It is a very nice drop in Motel to spend one, two, or three nights, and this is how it is set up to be. It was our first visit to Thailand so didn't know what to expect. Next time we will do things very differently. Whilst checking out we were accused of taking a plate and a pair of flip-flops from the room, on both counts not guilty, the cleaner had both the plate and had thrown one pair of flip-flops away. Be Aware!!!!! Overall the hotel is new and very pleasant, the food is good, the pool divine, not for children though, location and views terrific, rooms very nice but small. It does sit on a hill and each journey via tuk-tuk will cost 200Baht (£4.00) so can prove expensive. We hired a Moped, but its not for everyone. Thank you Thailand we hopefully will return one day.

author: fabulousmoments
title: Lovely stay!
text: My fiance and I stayed 4 nights at this hotel in very end of December, and we loved our stay! This new boutique hotel is located in the hill of Kata beach. Our room - Lub Dee Room had a great view and the room decoration was absolutely lovely. The infinity pool was exactly what we expected and enjoyed it so much. The selection of breakfast might be limited but for us it was good enough. Also, I'd like to note that this hotel has a way to make every guest feel special. For us, our flight arrived very early and got to the hotel way before the check in time. They managed to prepare the room in an hour or so and even invited us to the breakfast. It will of course depend on the room / seat availability, however, I could feel their efforts to satisfy their guests. And the manager was welcoming all the guests at the lobby, restaurant, and poolside, which gave us a kind of at home atmosphere. Here are a few things they can improve: -More frequent shuttle bus to the Kata beach will be nice. -Our room came with free mini bar but they forgot to fill the tea bags and coffee on both the 3rd day and 4th day. Also, they did not leave extra toilet paper roll on the 3rd day, even after leaving a note to make sure; but probably they did not read English. -I didn't have the opportunity to try their spa, but the menu seemed limited. Wish they had a full 3 hour spa course. Well, this is a new hotel, so I hope they keep up their good management and will We'd like to come back!

author: Ksim31
title: Absolutely Faultless!
text: This hotel is the best we have ever stayed in! From the moment you arrive you are blown away by the views from reception! Our room was so beautiful on the third floor with amazing views over Kata beach, the decor in the rooms was perfect and complete luxury. We loved that there was a cafetière so that we could enjoy a proper coffee in the morning. The pool area was beautiful never crowded and the infinity pool was the best I've ever seen we loved the jacuzzi and the views looking out to the ocean! The staff were wonderful so friendly and treated us like royalty the whole time they are a credit to the hotel. The manager was also super friendly and would often walk around talking to guests with a big smile, we felt really comfortable staying here. The location is perfect! Yes it's up a steep hill but the walk down is nice and a tuk tuk up is only 150 baht, the hotel also has a shuttle several times a day. We loved that we could go to kata noi beach which is the best in Phuket in our opinion and also walk to the nightlife of kata if we wanted a livelier atmosphere. The best part of our stay was most definitely the food! The hotel chefs are so talented we ate the best Thai food we have ever had! The menu is original and had some wonderful Thai dishes that we had never tried before, the fried chicken wings with cucumber salad was to die for! Thank you so much for a wonderful stay, we hope to return to stay with you for longer next time! 😃

author: MilindaD
title: Best stay ever in Thailand!
text: Service was excellent from day 1 till the very end. The hotel is beautifully designed on a hilltop with magnificent views of both the evergreen mountain and the two beaches karon and kata noi. The rooms are excellent, free mini bar includes beer and are refilled daily. The bed is nice and soft, the shower and bath are well placed and are of 5 star standard. The pool has all the views you need. A bar next to it, a water sofa with jacuzzi. What else can you ask for. Pool towels and attendants at your dispense at all times. Breakfast was at Roy Dee restaurant overlooking the sea with the morning sun. Can't explain how beautiful it is. Downside : Phuket has a taxi mafia and the hotel is not immune to it. The best beach (least crowded, clean and decent waves) is kata noi and to get there you have get a taxi from the appointed taxi mafia at 200 baht ( sgd 8 / usd 6). The distance is less than 1 km but as its down a steep slope walking it down is not easy and not recommended on a relaxing holiday. Hotel should increase shuttle or on demand shuttle for guests who are paying usd 200 a night to stay here! Airport drop is again by the taxi mafia. If you book with hotel it's baht 1300, if you book with the mafia counter right outside he hotel it's 1200. I called a internet company and am in a fortuna 4wd as I write for baht 700. Do not book taxi rides or tours with the hotel. We wanted to book similan island which was quoted at baht 3,800 by hotel and we got the exact tour down by kata noi beach for baht 2500 without even bargaining! I would definitely return to this hotel but I will bring my own hoverboard / skate board to save the many baht 200 I paid to go up and down the hotel to the beach!

author: pawandhatt
title: Really enjoyable stay at Nook Dee!
text: We stayed here for about 4 nights in November and overall this place was great - from the moment we arrived, the staff were very friendly and so accommodating! We arrived late in the evening and there's an amazing pool that overlooks the city and beach - we wanted to take a dip in the pool and the staff were willing to keep the pool open past its closing time for us. We actually spent quite a bit of time at this hotel lounging by the pool which we usually don't do. They also provide a shuttle to karon beach - this beach was clean, relaxing, and not overcrowded. We were able to rent umbrellas and enjoy the sun and water. The hotel also provides complimentary beach towels and bamboo mats for the beach which was really nice. With regards to the food, we don't usually eat at the hotel but decided to have lunch here one day and the restaurant food was really good. Breakfast was included with our stay and was great as well - the menu is a bit limited but the food was really enjoyable nonetheless. The breakfast area also has a great view of the city/beach area! My only criticism of this hotel is the fact that its situated at the top of a pretty steep hill...my husband and I are pretty fit and active and it was a difficult trek up the hill when we chose to walk it. But I also have to admit that part of what we loved about the hotel was the views and that's also due to the fact that the hotel is situated on a high hill allowing you to have that view. We tried a few times to get a tuk tuk to just take us up the hill but the prices they charge for doing that are a rip off. My suggestion to management would be to provide more shuttles or some kind of transport to at least go up and down this hill. The rooms were lovely and the decor had a really nice Thai style theme. We also had a great view from our room. I struggled with whether to give this hotel an excellent or very good rating just because of the hill! Decided on Excellent :) I think this was my favourite hotel while we were in Thailand. Thanks to the staff and and in particularly "A" for a great stay!

author: Nalini1095
title: Beautiful views, excellent service!
text: We stayed at this new boutique hotel for 3 nights (wish we could stay longer!) and absolutely loved every bit of it. We got a warm welcome from the manager and staff and were given some delicious drinks. We especially loved the infinity pool that looks over the ocean and the jungle. Furthermore, the hotel has a nice rooftop terrace from where we could see the sunset. Breakfast is very elaborate (warm food, cold food, fresh bread, fruits, good coffee etc.) and delicious (BEST brownies I ever had). The room was so beautiful because of the mix between modern and Asian designs and the view. You could also see the ocean from the bathroom which was really relaxing. The staff is extremely helpful and nice and rooms are cleaned every day. With regards to the location, we rented a scooter because the hotel is located on a hill which is quite steep. This way we could explore the area without worrying about walking up the hill all the time. Shuttle buses to the beach are provided tough, 3 times a day. One point of constructive feedback: there are (outdoor) movies played every night but these were Thai movies. I think the hotel could get more audience for the movies if these were Hollywood movies since these are applicable to a larger audience (or 2 movies every night, one Thai, one Hollywood). We didn’t mind because we went out every night but if movies were played that we liked, we would probably stay in one night and have dinner + movie at the hotel since the atmosphere is just great (excellent view, relaxed couches, good food, outdoor etc.). We literally have nothing negative to say about Nook-dee and can’t wait to come back! I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone who wants to relax and wants to have a (romantic) getaway.

author: pand71
title: Pros and Cons
text: Stayed at Nook Dee from 16 to 17 Dec 2015. Pros - 1. nice pool that overlooks the sea at the end 2. Manager was friendly 3. Room was clean Cons - 1. Shuttle services only operates on 3 timings.. 10am, 2pm and 6pm. Thereafter you got to make your own way back either by tuk tuk ( 150 baht) or walk up the steep hill. 2. They did not refill the toileteries on the 2nd day. 3. Even in breakfast area, they only allow those with sea view to sit out to view the scenery. First time i have seen such practices at breakfast. 4. Rooms were not bright.. 5. You have got to pay more for sea view from room. ( 3rd floor). even though I paid for sea view, it was blocked.(1st floor) If i had a choice, would have picked a hotel room nearer land.

author: Ultima-Forsan
title: Few points away from being perfect
text: I really liked my stay at Nook Dee hotel. It is by no means the most beautiful hotel I've been to in Thailand and I think the manager really tries to make it perfect but there are some points that needs to be improved. Pros: The views The pool Rooms with Balconies Free daily minibar with the right room Hospitality of the reception Hospitality from the manager Food,dinner or breakfast is at the top. Dinner portions are small tho. Two times per day house keeping. At 5pm someone would come inside to prepare our bed for sleep, never seen that before. Cons: Hotel is still in construction and has no fitness center yet. Some parts of the hotel seems to be unfinished but rooms are top notch👌🏻. Staff at the restaurant was not the best. On our second day breakfast we went to serve ourselves at the bar and one of the servers took all our beverages from our tables and left with them. I told him that we were still eating and he didn't really understood. I had to take our stuff back from his plate to continue our breakfast. I've seen him for the next 3 days and he seemed rude with us. After that we waited 30 minutes to get our main food to arrive but they simply forgot to serve us. Apparently topless sunbathing is allowed and might not be advisable for families. Final: None of the cons would stop us to go back to this hotel. It's truly a gem and it deserves more attention.

author: L-ECAEP
title: A VERY SPECIAL PLACE!
text: This resort is EXCELLENT on so many levels! The resort itself is built on the side of a big hill with wonderful views of Kata Noi to the south and the Kata/Karon coastline to the north with the Andaman sea stretched out in front and the green lush hills behind. It is brand new (still under some construction), I arrived on the 3rd opening day.The design & decor are artisan inspired, thoughtful with a warm and whimsical Thai touch. The features & fixtures in the rooms are modern, the bed and pillows are like a dream (turn down service at night has a sweet touch), nice ammenities in the room and a conscious concern for the environment by not using little plastic bottles of shampoo etc. The pool is so cool (just look at the pictures) wth a jacuzzi and comfortable deck. I can't emphasize enough how good the food is (you have to try it!) and the presentation just made it taste so much more delicious. Last but not least the staff and management are the key that makes this place a winner! I left feeling like I was saying goodbye to dear friends. They are always there to give you top notch service, but you can tell they do it from their hearts ... so genuinely! The location is not on the beach but there is a shuttle to take you there. I could hear the waves on Kata Noi beach at night from my balcony. I would recommend this resort to everyone. It is an excellent value and a beautiful Thai experience! I will definitely visit again!

author: puengt2015
title: The best boutique hotel, Perfect stay, Great food, Can't fault anything, Definitely will be back
text: Nook Dee = Very Sanook = Very Fun = Happy Stay This hotel is on top of a hill that over looking Kata beach, Katanoi beach, and Karon beach. I can actually see all these three beach from the hotel. Which make it so special coz all the rooms have sea view in different angle and they all very beautiful and it take less than 5 minutes to go to the beach. I stay with a group of family with young children. All the kids are very happy with the swimming pool especially the big black jacuzzi in the middle of the pool. At the edge of the pool there is a clear acrylic that allow you to dive and still see a beautiful view of andaman sea. Room is very well design inspire by Thai culture and lifestyle. Bed is super comfortable. Room amenities are so cute especially the purple and green Silk bathrobe, never seen this anywhere. Kids also love elephant doll who is a mascot of nook dee. Roy Dee restaurant is definitely need to be mention. Breakfast is much better than many 5 stars hotel. Dinner is even better. They offer variety of Thai and international food. Since we come in a large group, we try and share several dishes. I would have to say that everything we order are so good and the price is even cheaper than many restaurant around here. Even though you are not staying here, I would recommend everyone to come for lunch or dinner. Last but not least, rooftop of Nook Dee will take your breath away. This is the best spot to watch sunset in Phuket. You have to see it with your own eyes.

author: yellowsubmarine117
title: Not suitable for winter guests!
text: I will first mention the disappointments: Off season during our November visit therefore their pub was very quiet and we counted on ambiance during the evening...generally the neighbourhood was VERY quiet. the first night I requested beef and ale pie and the beef was so hard I could not put my fork in it nor eat it properly.. I did not complain ..it was a nostalgic item I was waiting to have after more than 20 years of absence from the U K. Following night we sat for diner , anyway, after choosing what to eat, the lady kindly informed us that they no longer served diner because of lack of clients ...therefore the next two days we ate at the babacombe inn which was cheaper and great taste and which had quiet a few clients Every night for our 3 nights stay the radiators were turned off in the middle of the night , and it was chilly , and put back on around 7 am. The breakfast for 10 GBP was not buffet and the English breakfast was a rip off . Some nearby hotels and cafeterias were giving a decent breakfast for around half the price.We had asked if they had yogurt or patisseries or croissants or hash browns but the answer was no they don't provide these items. The breakfast is at an odd time of 9.00to 9.30 ...we usually have our breakfast around 7-8 am...British breakfast is about 1 hr, cooking-waiting-eating etc ...so if one goes at 9.30 and finishes at 10.30 it is like brunch....and our 3 meals timetable is messed up!! Last day had to catch the train at 10 am, they kindly accepted to serve breakfast at 8.30 ...we ordered a simple porridge and 2 toasts each and guess the quantity of porridge presented on a miniature cereal bowl ?? about 3 table spoons of the stuff that could fit WITOUT EXAGERATION on a tea saucer!!! I wish I had taken a photo of this . The SPRING bed was uncomfortable ( I have not slept on a spring bed in my last 20 years and more than 30 hotels since). First night the wind from the sea was strong and the door n windows were rattling all night ...had to use my earplugs and some wine to sleep! THE GOOD. Points : we were well received by Jane! The location is beautiful and 5 mins walk to the miniature village, And railway cafe (great place for cakes and tea etc..) The Babacombe theatre was also 5 mins walk and play great fun. Good for stroll in a quiet area... The kingsize bedroom was spacious.

author: janice1969
title: Lovely Hotel :)
text: I have just returned home from this wonderful part of the world and what a lovely place to stay. The room we stayed in (room 6) had the most beautiful view of the bay. Now coming from a famous seaside resort myself you would think I couldn't be blown away from a sea view but I have to say it was gorgeous. The hotel room was very well equipped, the king size bed was fantastic and very comfortable. The room itself is a large, spacious room with excellent natural light. There are only 8 rooms within this hotel but in my opinion that's a plus as its nice and quiet. The bathroom was very modern with a double shower and it was all so clean. No dirt or mould to be seen anywhere. The 32 inch T.V was great and having brought my own hairdryer I was surprised to see they supplied a decent one themselves, there was also a fan in the room, I nearly brought my own, glad I didn't. There was plenty of space with a double built in wardrobe which would comfortably fit a couple of suitcases and shoes! and also plenty of drawers for storage around the room. All the staff were very friendly and approachable, the food was lovely and the steak was cooked exactly how we liked it. The only down side I found (as a few others had brought my attention to on trip advisor), were the tight parking spaces but they are limited with no extra area to extend on and no parking on the seafront road as the road is too narrow. We did however, after walking around the area, find there were some parking spaces on the road nearby and there were about 3 or 4 spaces at the side of the hotel on the road. I will definitely stay at this hotel in the future and hopefully in the near future too :)

author: puddinlover
title: COULD BE A 5 NOT A 4
text: My wife and I booked in here for 4 nights on Friday 14/09. Our first contact was with the manageress I think her name was Jan, she was very helpful and very friendly. We stayed in room 8 which is very roomy and has fantastic views across the bay, you can even see the sea whilst sat in bed . Everything so far was great, however, we both had a shower before going out for the evening and found the water pressure was very low, my wife had a real problem getting the soap out of her hair. Then it became a bit chilly so I attempted to switch the radiators on, without success. Then the following morning we both went for a shower but found that the towels were still wet due to the elaborate heated towel rail not being switched on. We are not the sort to complain so we persevered. We carried on like this for a couple of days, when I received a phone call from my local hospital with regards to pending surgery. This meant that we had to leave a day early. We informed a member of staff the day before and asked if they could let the owners know. We had seen the owners a few times who while friendly appeared to be a bit stand-off. We saw one of the owners at breakfast on our final morning. We spoke to the manageress about having to leave early and offered our regrets all this took place in front of the owner and he never offered one word. We had paid for everything a month in advance including 8 breakfasts (very tasty) that have to be booked seperately. There wasn't one mention of any potential refund not even for the 2 breakfasts that we wouldn't be needing. I have left writing this review pending a possible e-mail, non have been sent. It is for this reason we can only give 4 and not 5 stars. This place could be great but for the penny pinching.

author: cathtiger
title: Excellent hotel. Lovely staff, super location, great bar, good value.
text: I would highly recommend the Royal. We stayed for one night (Saturday). I only booked there as we were attending a function but will definitely choose the same hotel when I visit the area again. The staff really make this hotel stand out. All are friendly, helpful and courteous but without being over-bearing. We had booked room 4 which looked great but were 'upgraded' to room 8 which was even bigger. The room appeared recently decorated, had a wonderful view of the bay and the bathroom was immaculate with bath and shower. Lots of really useful hotel and local area information is provided in the room too. There is also plenty of (free) parking. We had a great evening at our function which was in the back room of the bar. The drinks are reasonably priced for a hotel (around £6.50 for a pint and a gin and tonic) and several local real ales are available. We had a buffet laid on too which was excellent quality and good value. Breakfast is only £7.95 and although restricted to between 9am and 9.30am is defintely worth having as is freshly cooked to order. The full breakfast is huge with really good quality ingredients and a dining room overlooking the bay. This hotel knocks spots off some of the big chain hotels and for £59 is great value too.

author: pitrf
title: Important to read!!
text: I travelled in past 15 years a lot, basically almost every continent. When I travelled alone usually slept in hostels. Found this El Misti place so I booked it for 2 nights, that was the maximum I was able to stay in Rio for now. The location of the property is just fantastic, very safe neighborhood of Ipanema, beach is just 100meters away, there are numerous dining and shopping opportunities in nearby. Slept in 8 bed dorm, they came to clean it every single day. There is fast WiFi in whole property. As well as AC on every single room. Usually during the daytime they turn off the AC in the room, but you can ask reception and they will kindly turn it on for you, if you wish. Common area near reception is nice,there are large LCDs so You can watch whatever You want. There is a bar downstairs, with tasty caipirinhas and supercool breakfast for just BRL15. On nightly basis multiple guests are chilling down at the bar. Very cool. All in all I love this hostel. Staff is just fabulous!! On my list of 50+ hostels I have been to, this is definitely in top 3. Highly recommended.

author: T2808OWdavidg
title: Misti added DOPE value to a conference in Rio
text: All around great spot. Traveling for Fulbright conference. Met a ton of very interesting and passionate people passing through El Misti Ipanema. The ambiance was on point. The environment was relaxed. The staff was a 5 Star Dream Team. Well what's his face was kinda... nah, im jk. Rodrigo, Thay (sorry if i misspelled that), Danny, they were all exceptional. Definitely found my spot whenever in Rio. Top it all off with a great location one block from the beach and one block from the central park of the neighborhood. Price was righteous as well. If you're not getting it yet, I could go on and on. It was great. Go. You should go. Just go.

author: junnegrajales
title: Good breakfast and near the beach but staff were on and off and poor wi-fi
text: The breakfast was really good--plenty of options: juice, cakes, coffee, cereal, fruits, and eggs. It's not for free, though, which was uncommon. Good AC. It's near the beach. Party hostel with free Caipirinhas every night. Spacious bathroom. Clean and modern enough. The wi-fi was really poor when I was there, though. The staff were on and off, one of them decided to play Creed's greatest hits at 2 in the morning really loudly. And they have the infamous 3 bunk beds. The beds' height were so low, you can't sit upright. It was really uncomfortable, I hit my head all the time, and I'm not even tall. Apparently, I was put in that room because I was only staying for one night (I was thinking of extending my stay to a week, but because of the terrible beds and the inconsiderate staff with the terrible taste in music, I hastily left). It wasn't a very good first impression. The hostel didn't have much English speakers when I was there (which isn't the hostel's fault), but it didn't have an international backpacker vibe. Apparently it's a hostel franchise, but honestly, there are better options elsewhere.

author: JannedeBeer
title: Janne de Beer
text: It was a treat to firstly be in the beautifully clean and safe city of Kigali Rwanda. Secondly, what a huge treat to have stayed at the Radisson Blu Hotel and Convention Centre. I felt pampered from wake up to good night time! The entire staff are unbelievably friendly and gracious. Nothing was too much trouble. The room and ablution facility in the room were immaculate. Not to mention the uncapped WiFi. Now for matters most important to me.. The Food! (I am a big girl you see who loves food) The sumptious breakfast offering daily was delicious. Ample hot and cold options with a wide variety of other traditional offerings like smoothies, pastries(to die for) and many other tempting treats. Lunch offerings were just as delcious with special mention of the biryani and curries, roti etc. Tastes were unbelievable and more-ish. Again tempting pastries (by the brilliant Chef Negi) that teased my taste-buds. Exexutive Chef Rickard and Sous Chef Jose your daily culinary offerings made all my resistance crumble! Last but not least, I had the BEST Burger EVA in the Lounge with handcut chips and guacamole. OMG Delicious. Overall the attention to detail and overtly positive attitude from everyone I met was way beyond any regular Hotel Offering. Mr Denault, Francois , Chef Rickard, Jose, Negi, Anwar, Bobson, and many many more THANK YOU to you all.

author: stephenalexander1124
title: My first choice of hotel - The Radisson Kigali - visited 3 times in the past 7 months.
text: The hotel is an attractive building set in excellent grounds. The amenities are good but the most over riding feature is the hotel staff. So welcoming and pleasant from the door man who helps with the baggage from the car to reception to the cleaning staff. A good hotel needs good well trained staff and this is where the Radisson Blu in Kigali really scores. On my recent visit I was particularly impressed by two members of staff. The first was Umariya Gotter in the business class lounge. The service was as kind,courteous and classy as on a Business class airline flight. Perfect attention to detail and forward thinking for the customers needs.Very impressive. The second member of staff was Claudette on the Reception. I was checking out and paid my bill by Visa card.I went to the airport for my flight to Doha. My business colleague from the US called the hotel and gave his card to pay my hotel bill. Claudette arranged for the amount on my card to be refunded immediately and sent me a personal email advising me of her actions which I received as soon as my flight landed in Doha.That was good business efficiency and I really appreciated it. As I said - a good hotel becomes an excellent hotel when you have good staff. I must also add a thank you to the very helpful member of staff that was looking after the business centre. He was just so cheerful and helpful. Thank you Radisson Blu Kigali - I'll be back. Stephen Alexander

author: Bill1andBill2
title: Best business hotel in Kigali perfect for the conference center
text: The hotel is only a few years old; it’s modern, bright, cheerfully appointed and well maintained. The Kigali convention center is 20 m across the entry drive. Room size is like most Radissons and the basics are excellent with high quality beds, bedding, lighting, desk, international power outlets convenient to desk top and bedside, and good AC control. WiFi was usually OK but sometimes finicky, for example, requiring signing in again after an hour. The bathroom is large but shower only, with bath amenities typical of a Radisson - lots of big towels, a terry bathrobe, iron, etc. The rooms facing the pool have a pleasant little balcony. The pool and exercise facilities are inviting and excellent. Staff are friendly and accommodating, handling several special requests very quickly in reasonable ways. When the hotel is not expected to be full at 8 pm, late checkout is 6 pm. Although the breakfast is among the better hotel breakfasts in Kigali, the baked goods are unusually tasteless and dry. The poolside bar has the expresso machine, which we enjoyed. The lunch and dinner buffets seem over-priced but the Italian restaurant a few m across the entry in the convention center is better. The bar serves a crisp Mutzip light draft and several decent wines. Bar food servings are a short list of standards and over-ample - it would have been nice to get just a tray of roasted peanuts like we find everywhere in Uganda. There are several good options for food nearby. We had a great cheap burrito at the Meze Fresh, a 600 m walk mostly through the convention center parking lot, but the Radisson has an electric shuttle that will take you most of the way. We had a fabulous dinner at the Brachetto - a 2 km 5 minute taxi trip.

author: moyerthibaut
title: Excellent hotel
text: I stayed one month in the Radisson. Certainly very central and luxurious. One of the best in town if not the best Rooms are modern and great. The lobby is fantastic. The swimming pool area is enjoyable but a bit empty. the bar and the restaurant are great. Central situation in Kigali. Mostly populated by consultants and conference participants. Single travelers with laptops. Special thanks to: Justin, the tennis coach, for his professionalism and amazing lifted bankhand Claudette and Eric, at reception, for their welcoming smile Goret at the bar for her kind smile and attention Janvier and Jean-Paul at the bar, because they both have the skills of French Parisian waiters without any arrogance Gentile at the restaurant for her smile James, at the laundry, for his incredible kindness and attention The ladies from the spa, especially the one who just arrived from South-Africa To be improved The main negative point is security. I can understand careful security measures when events are on-going but this is less understandable when the conference center next door is empty. Generally I wouldn’t advise to stay at the Radisson when a VIP/head of state is also staying because Radisson quickly switches to prison break mode. Last point on pricing policy for non-guests. I would certainly enjoy coming back for brunches if it wouldn’t be so expensive. Who is willing to pay 15$/person also for children just for a dive? Whoever is in charge of pricing policy in Radisson should reconsider.

author: 890fangs
title: be mindful of how much you pay when check out
text: We were a small team and had a few rooms. As a few left earlier, we checked two rooms out earlier but confirmed with reception that it's fine. On check-out day, we were in a hurry for our flights so I paid, got the receipt without much checking, and left. Later, I found that the hotel had charged us for the remaining nights of the two rooms we checked out earlier. Plus, they failed to book a $840 cash we paid into the master receipt. So together, they overcharged us for close to $1200. I called the hotel and later emailed a manager, confident that it would be looked into and the fact would prevail. It came as a shock about the hotel's response to this. First, they didn't respond at all for quite a while, though I called and emailed several times explaining the situation. Finally the manager emailed back briefly that I did NOT have the rooms checked out at the reception. I'm outraged. I remember clearly that i had the room checked out at reception, confirming again and again with the receptionist that it's fine and the rooms were checked out. AT THE SAME TIME, i booked a limo from the reception to send the guests to the airport. SO I CANNOT REMEMBER IT WRONG AND I'M 100% SURE. When a guest is checking in a 5-star like this, he/she could only trust the hotel and the people working there. We were told it's the best and represents the city and its service. We liked the city (Kigali) so much and its people. But I must say, this is a very bad experience.

author: Ishuheri
title: Intimidating Welcome
text: Years ago, I went for a tour of this place as it was being built, and I've watched it go from building site to local landmark, lighting up the night's sky in Kigali. This week, a friend was holding an event there, and it was my first time to go inside. The moto dropped me at what looked like the main entrance, just off a roundabout. As I walked towards it, a security guard appeared and told me that the entrance was actually at the other side of the building. With a furtive glance at the gathering rain clouds, I set off on a fifteen-minute walk. The whole road is cordoned off so that no one can drive past. There's another big entrance with Convention Centre written across the top, but as I approached, five extremely serious-looking policemen with very big guns started waving me to cross the street. Not only can't you drive past it, you can't even walk past it. In total, I had to stop to ask directions three times before I found the actual entrance, tucked around the back. I braved road barricades and armed guards. It felt extremely intimidating, more like finding your way into a fort than being welcomed into a hotel. When I finally found the event, I was charged FRW 11,500 for a G&T, which is an extortionate price. The staff were friendly enough, but I had to specifically ask for ice and lemon (something that should come as standard with all G&Ts - especially for that amount of money). The event was being held in the lobby. There were a lot of people there, but it was hard to hear what the speakers were saying as the acoustics were extremely echoey. I appreciate the need for safety at one of Africa's most expensive buildings, but I think it's been taken to an extreme. You'd expect it of a parliamentary building, but not a convention centre. The overbearing security and the high price of drinks has put me off going back. I'm glad I had a look inside, it's pretty enough and does have that wow factor, but it's not somewhere I'd choose to relax.

author: 904lindak904
title: Business Class Room, well worth it
text: Regular rooms were sold out so I took the business class room while at the Kigali Convention Center for a conference. The room was spacious and the amenities in the room were plentiful. I didn't realize it when I booked, but the Business Lounge is MUCH better than any I've seen elsewhere. It's across a short 2nd story bridge and set up like a combination restaurant and upscale comfortable lounge. They have NICE food and drinks from 6:30 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. at no extra charge. The deck on the back side is furnished beautifully and has an amazing view of the city while being perfectly serene and private. Many have written about the breakfast buffet, which is included in the price of the room. Don't miss it, or the "tree tomato" juice, which tastes like passion fruit, only better. The staff will do anything for you -- I asked the chambermaid if they had mint tea. He'd never heard of it but asked me to write down so that he could go the catering dept. to check. Shortly after, there was a plate with mint tea bags in my room. And so it went from an international charger to anything at all. Security is extremely tight to get into the convention center campus and accordingly the hotel is very, very safe.

author: seguno303
title: Great combo of hospitality and aesthetics
text: The first impression of the building is aesthetically inspiring. The exterior reminds me of China's Olympic stadium the bird's nest. Surprisingly, the impressiveness of the design was matched by the hospitality of the staff. Whether it was upon entering and always being met with a smile and helping hand by Jean-Pierre. Or the Guest relations team run by Mr. Oumar. I remember when I needed to get a SIM and airtime after a long day of conferencing, and the staff was willing and ready to help solve my problem -- i had no idea, nor energy to figure out how to do that. Special thank you to Jocelyn and Shekina in guest relations for their help with that. The food and amenities were also of note. The spa is well appointed, though totally indoors ( I would prefer some more natural lighting). Lillian was engaging and thorough. I recommend you ask for her. There are several distinct spaces to dine. With two restaurants and three bars/lounges. This allows for some nice variation esp. when on an extended stay. Again, a note of gratitude, to Grace in the Larder restaurant, who noted my fondness for a local bracelet she wore and had one made for my kids. As you can see just by the fact that I know names reminds me of just how different an experience the hospitality was here. Kudos to the team, and to the country for such a splendid representation.

author: Rasdok
title: Rwandan Swank?
text: Welcome to the swanky part of town, smack in the middle of Kigali and right at the new convention centre. Welcome, also, to an African replica of European style. I’m not sure whether I should be impressed or disappointed. Yes, it did feel like any Radisson in any European city, but is that what it should be? Maybe the outside decoration of the hotel was supposed to reflect a calabash or a mud-and-wattle abode, ie African roots. But it doesn’t reach that. The inside is very stylish and reminiscent of a procurement manager who asked some plastics company to pour pre-designed moulds for cupboards, desks and TV cabinets. Either way, it is a modern hotel, and maybe that speaks more to what Rwanda has achieved in general than a misplaced reminiscence for dark, wooden African style. I liked the subtle touches of interior decorating and I think one should look at this hotel as a singular achievement. For the price though, it should’ve had a better breakfast. TV – Another one of those OS pre-programmed jobs that doesn’t allow you to connect HDMI and USB. It’s also very far from the table, so no working on it. There is a fancy screen sharing option for your laptop, but having a corporate PC, that software is not installed (please take note hotel staff) Pillows – Very very very soft. But as I took the 3am flight into town and straight into meetings I didn’t even notice so tired was I Room-service burger – Now this is a proper burger! Very juicy and with crispy fries. One of the best I’ve had. Gym – Didn’t have time to use it, but it looked very well stocked. WiFi – Excellent wifi reception everywhere in the hotel. I could even have a 2hour Webex session without hiccups.

author: rachelbN6363IC
title: Beware airport transfers that don't happen
text: Room and hotel building was generally nice, but the service at the front desk was disorganized. They need to work on one guest at a time, as mentioned by other reviewers. It took about 20 minutes for me to check out because of various issues. When I tried calling the front desk I often got no answer. The worst part was that I had reserved an airport transfer as I was arriving alone just after midnight and it was the end of 17 hours of travel for me. Unfortunately, no one was there to get me and no one answered any of the phone numbers I had for the hotel. I even had some local people standing outside at the airport try to call the Radisson for me, in case my phone wasn't on the network. I waited for a while and then I finally got a ride with another group on a bus. It was 2 AM when I got to the hotel and the front desk did not seem surprised when I said I was not picked up as promised. Why was this such a problem? Well, there were no taxis, perhaps because it was 1AM. The next day, I emailed the staff member, Julian, who had "confirmed" my airport pickup and she offered no explanation as to why I was forgotten. She did offer me a free trip back to the airport. "Um..... No thanks!" If you are woman traveling alone, you may want to take extra steps to ensure that you are picked up. I travel a lot, and this was a first for me. It didn't put me in a good mood with this hotel.

author: 483antonv
title: Not quite there (yet?).
text: room 408 Exactly one year ago, this modern looking hotel opened its doors for the first time. It is a stylish complex, with a very large and grand reception area. The only access to the hotel rooms via the elevator is with a key card holding a RFID chip. Same counts for the access to the various floors and individual rooms. Watch out for it to be all mixed up in the neighbourhood of electronic equipment. It may fail on you. Rooms are large spacy and have all amanities one may expect from a hotel like this. Yet, the large shower head was not working properly and it needs plumbing. The drainage of the shower is not working fast enough to consume all the water, when showering. Thus you risk water seeping into the whole bathroom area. WiFi was a headache and did not work well, which should not happen in a hotel like this!. Gym was in perfect shape. Nice outside pool. Breakfast offered all one can think of and was well presented. Watch out for an unexpectedly high bill, when having a drink at the bar. Cost for the taxi service provided as rather high, compared to the distance. Security overall and at entrance was reasonably good. ] Organisation/staff, was not very efficient and needs upgrading quite a bit. This may have an effect on the overall experience,

author: JoeRugby
title: Luxury and Lavish Dining in Rwanda
text: While working in beautiful Rwanda, I try to take a moment every now and then to enjoy the culinary fair that Rwanda has begun to develop in recent years. Undoubtedly, one of the most beautiful and safest countries in Africa, Rwanda has recently opened some exquisite new hotels and restaurants. The Radisson Blu is certainly the top of the hotel restaurants. We came for Sunday brunch. Truly a well planned event with culinary masterpieces from around the world at your fingertips. From potato cucumber salad to prawns and beet, chicken and goat skewers, to local fish and a plethora of dessert options, this restaurant really tries to impress. The service is comparable to New York, London or Rome. Food flavors are still being refined but are good. I especially liked the beef skewer and the many many salad choices. The apple pie was very different but a punch of good flavors. The fish was "so so". The restaurant is overly pricey but as they say, "you get what you pay for." As a respite in a busy travel time I would recommend the Radisson Blu Restaurant. Truly a new and fresh take on traditional foods in a wonderfully beautiful setting. Wow, Rwanda is on the move up! The luxuriousness of this restaurant is trend setting.

author: Safariafficionado
title: A new landmark for Kigali and absolutely worth a visit
text: Conference visitors will no doubt appreciate the closeness of the Radisson Blu Kigali to the adjoining Kigali Convention Centre, just a few steps across either a footbridge on mezzanine level or on ground level. The new Radisson is already a landmark due to the dome over the main conference centre auditorium and when lit up at night can be seen from many parts of the city. My check in was very professional, all data at hand, leaving me to just hand over my passport - now a requirement everywhere in Eastern Africa - and sign the check in form. The porter service was equally swift and my bags arrived at the same time as one of the front office staff showed me my room to point out the various features available. Being new was everything in pristine condition and the room lived up to my expectation of what a new Radisson Blu ought to be like. A fresh crisp colour scheme in the rooms and very complete furnishings gave way to brightly coloured corridors with matching carpets. I had enough space on the working desk to spread out my laptop and other gadgets with enough sockets to charge all of them on the desk and not need to seek other wall sockets. Internet access does not require complicated sign in procedures as it is an open network available to all Radisson Blu guests while in the hotel premises. The bathroom was very generously spaced too and I loved the large fluffy towels. I enjoyed two breakfasts and one dinner at the main hotel restaurant called The Larder. All meals offered a mix of buffet set up and food cooked to order and quality as well as presentation left nothing for wanting. Staff attention in the restaurant can best be described as 'keen' and at the turn of my head a staff was at my side. I also greatly enjoyed the Club Lounge of the Radisson Blu in Kigali which is located across from the hotel in the conference centre, a floor up from the new Italian restaurant which I plan to sample at my next visit. In the Club Lounge can guests enjoy some light breakfast, snacks for lunch and later a selection of finger food around dinner time or simply have a cup of tea or coffee during the day. The staff were most attentive and while I only had tea and water for drinks was a wide selection of beers, wines and even spirits available for guests entitled to the use of the lounge through their booked room type or by holding a Carlson Rezidor loyalty card. First time visitors to Kigali should not fret over the very thorough security checks at the main entrance to the hotel and conference centre, something now the norm everywhere in Kigali but also across the Eastern African region and aimed to ensure safety and security of guests. It was an all round positive experience and the arrival of Radisson Blu has added options for visitors to Kigali in the five star hotel segment. Comes highly recommended.

author: 591lawrencem
title: Exceptional Staff and Service
text: I stayed at the Radisson Blu with a number of coworkers for two weeks while attending a conference. The hotel accommodations, conference center, and business services were all top-notch, but the highlight by far was the friendly, helpful, and attentive staff. Without a doubt the best customer service experience I've ever had at a hotel. While everyone on the hotel staff was excellent, there were a few employees that deserve special mention. First, Germaine, one of the hostesses at the Lounge bar and restaurant, was exceptional. Friendly, very attentive, and with a great sense of humor, she made us feel welcome and at home while traveling. Eddy, one of the managers, and Fabrice from the Lounge were also excellent. Papy, one of the porters, was very friendly and always ready to help with whatever we needed during our time at the Radisson. Honestly can't say enough good things about these employees and the experience they created for us. Aside from the phenomenal staff, the rooms, food, and accommodations also deserve top ratings. The rooms were clean, comfortable, and modern, and housekeeping kept them immaculate. The food at the Lounge and buffet at the Larder were very good. All accommodations and requirements while traveling for work were met, and the internet was fast and reliable. The only negative experience during the visit involved security at the gate. On the second to last day of our two-week stay, my team ordered food from a local restaurant to be delivered to us at our meeting. We were unaware that prior authorization was required to have food delivered, and security would not allow the food past the gate. After nearly three hours of dealing with security, we were finally allowed to bring the food into the property. Not only was this an excessive amount of time to resolve the issue, but some consideration should have been provided to us after spending two weeks at the hotel and purchasing nearly all of our meals from the hotel. Overall, the experience was excellent and I would highly recommend the hotel to anyone traveling to Kigali.

author: nickbN5838AT
title: Serious Issues
text: On first sight this is indeed a beautiful hotel, however the actual experience fell well short of expectations, especially given the cost. On check in, the receptionist was not aware that they do not accept American Express so we wasted time repeatedly trying to get my credit card approved. When I was shown around my room and bathroom, the toilet looked as though it had been used. So I flushed the toilet but the flush water was yellow. I complained at the desk next morning but in the afternoon it was still the same. When I asked at the desk I was told this was due to using recycled water. It looked very unpleasant.
