First evening there, the guest lifts were not working. I could not find any alternatives to the stairs. Again I complained and they then put up some signs, but the alternative lifts were behind doors marked private so not immediately obvious. On check out there were incorrect charges on my room bill. It took forever to sort this out and they were incapable of printing a receipt. It took 20 minutes to check out which delayed our departure to the airport. One last point, the acoustics of the corridors of the hotel guest rooms is really poor with every door closing or conversation echoing and reverberating down the corridor, similar to a prison. Unfortunately, the rooms are not well insulated from this and its possible to hear every noise and conversation from inside the rooms.

author: Marco_Polo499
title: It could be a comfortable hotel, if they let air conditioning work when needed.
text: The historical Mardin (destination of tourism) is perched on the side of a high and steep mountain, at the altitude of 1100 metres. Several hundred metres below there is the modern Mardin, and the hotel is located there. The location is quiet and pleasant, and there are amazing views to the surrounding extraordinary landscape. The hotel is quite new, and complies with the good standards of the Garden Inn chain. Rooms are very comfortable and whatever is expected in a Garden Inn is provided: pleasant and effective furnishing, large and good beds, an armchair and a tea table, a functional working table, a wide TV screen , pressing and coffee-making facilities, a safe, complimentary drinking water, and so on. The bathroom is well equipped and comfortable, although the fixtures already show signs of fatigue (the temperature of the shower could not be controlled; the sink drain was blocked and not working). The staff tries to be helpful, but English is understood only by a few staff members; communication with the others was practically impossible: I tried to use various major European languages, I tried to explain myself by making drawings and I even used a gestured language, but always to no avail. Deeply frustrating. A positive note deserves the business centre, which is efficient and well maintained (a very rare feature elsewhere); it is located in a dedicated room, there are two computers and one printer, the keyboards are of the standard international type (a lucky choice; to be praised) and the system is managed by an external provider: in this way Internet navigation is efficient. The buffet breakfast is fairly basic. The main hot dish is boiled eggs, and little else seems available; the customers have to prepare their own coffee by mixing industrial soluble powder and hot water (in Turkey, the home of coffee !); there are no milk, no decaffeinated coffee, no infusions (except a big bin of previously prepared tea). The weakest point of this hotel is the air conditioning, whose temperature is set by the management of the hotel; the controls in the rooms are disabled and the hotel circulates air at the temperature they decide (generally very high); if you want a milder temperature you have to make a specific request (and this may prove very difficult if the employee who speaks English is off-duty); the hotel will activate the A/C in your room, and the activation will last until the next morning; if you stay more than one night, you have to repeat your request every day. One day I omitted to make my request, and I waked up in the night with a suffocating temperature of 26 degrees Celsius in the room (although the external temperature was rather cool); I immediately asked for air conditioning, but I was told that it was impossible to activate it at that time of the night: consequently I was obliged to sleep for the rest of the night on a sofa of the hall, the only place of the hotel where the temperature was bearable. The bad management of the air conditioning makes this hotel quite unattractive. The distance between the hotel and the "old Mardin" is not great, but the tangled topography of the area makes the journey very long: there are cañons and mountain walls everywhere, and it takes many kilometres to get around them; in May 2018 the price of a taxi ride from the hotel to “old Mardin” was 20-25 Liras (4-5 Euro).

author: Isabella628
title: No Air Con, Cold Food, Faulty Internet, Lost Laundry, Toilet Extractor Fans Not Working
text: Stayed here several times now due to business, so I had no say in where I would be staying as this was booked by my employer every time for business. If it were up to me, I would not have returned here after my first stay! Stayed during the peak of summer and then several times again up to winter. NO AIR CON: So everyday I would return from work, get into my room and the room would be boiling hot, after turning the air con on and realising it made no difference at all to the room temperature (only the fan spins, it's not actually air conditioning), I contacted the reception several times and told them about this, each time I was told "I send my friend", and then sometimes after a long wait, someone would come up and tell me to leave the air con on for 15 mins and it will get cooler, this annoyed me everytime as I always waited at least 30 mins with it turned on before calling them and waiting made no difference. After complaining several times, I was told that the air con in the hotel has been turned off to save electricity??? MIXED/LOST LAUNDRY: The in-room leaflet states that laundry will be returned within 24 hours - average time for me over the course of several trips was around 4, 5 sometimes even 7 days before I'd get my laundry back. Sometimes you'll receive it back with items missing and twice they even mixed my laundry up with other guests. COLD FOOD: This is guaranteed!, order some food and it'll arrive nice and cold, this is not a joke. For some reason the food never arrived hot. So I ended up going elsewhere for food when I had time and if I didn't I just had to put up with it. NO INTERNET: So several times the internet would not work, when this would happen, it would last for days at a time. I'd understand if it was the whole of the hotel which lost internet access but this was not the case. I would complain to the reception and they'd tell me that they don't know and so can't help me??? They gave me the number of the internet service provider for the hotel and I was told to call the provider directly, myself?? and to top it all off, I was charged for making the calls to get the internet sorted out. TOILET EXTRACTOR FAN NOT WORKING: The extractor fan in the toilets do not work, can't say if this is the case for all the rooms but I stayed in 4 different rooms so far and the toilets have extractor fans but they do not work. And you can guess that pointing this out to the hotel staff makes no difference at all. At this point I had given up on customer service anyway. Thank you for taking the time to read my review, hopefully it can prepare you for your stay if it's unavoidable.

author: sumavax
title: A very good choice in Mardin
text: The Hilton Garden Inn in Mardin is a large building with 4 floors, which is still very new. Sufficient free parking is available in front of the house. Coming from Kiziltepe the hotel can be seen from afar because of its dominant position on a rock at the outskirts of the city. It takes a vehicle to get to the city centre. The staff were friendly but their English was poor and thus communication somewhat difficult. So e.g. we were assigned a smoking room first in spite of our request for a non-smoking room. Breakfast was of good quality. The hotel has a very nice indoor pool and hot tub. Both were of pleasant temperature. We got a spacious room with a view of the expressway. All home furnishing items worked without problems. There was a big TV set, a fridge and a kettle. The air conditioner cooled perfectly. We also liked the equipment of the bathroom. The free Wi-Fi in the room worked flawlessly, the login with the passport number was awkward though. We would choose this hotel again on another stay in Mardin.

author: C130driver
title: Comfortable, safe, good standard for the city, customer-service oriented
text: - The staff was extremely friendly and accommodating – from the front desk to the IT guy. Turkish, Arabic, Kurdish were widely used while several hotel personnel also spoke English. The Front Office Manager, Murat, was absolutely invaluable in us enjoying our stay. He was fluent in English and made several suggestions that we enjoyed. - Breakfast was a nice buffet - Restaurant and bar prices were reasonable and staff was terrific. 23TL for a mixed drink, whereas in Ankara we paid 40 TL for the same mixed drink at the Ankara Hilton. - The property is two years old, and not located in the downtown or old-town areas; well-appointed and about 3 miles from the “old town” shopping area, Mardin Museum and restaurants – an easy taxi ride – 15TL. - Typical wait time for a taxi was about 10 min and even though we called the front desk in advance, hotel staff would not call for taxi in advance until you came downstairs and showed up in front lobby. - It has all the services of Hilton: indoor pool, a small fitness room, business center, silver shop, snack shop, etc. The restaurant has a nice view. The rooms are very nice and clean; you can adjust your bed from soft to firm. - We experienced 6 power failures in 2 days, lasting about 1 minute each time - One front desk staff member suggested we use one particular taxi driver to take us to the Museum, the monastery and other sights; unfortunately, the driver ended up not speaking any English. We paid 150TL for the day; however, with the exception of having him wait at the Monastery, it probably would have been less expensive/ easier to take separate taxis; it did simplify our lives and he was pleasant! - If sight-seeing, pre-plan your trip so you know what you want to look at. Hotel staff were very nice, but are not equipped to help you plan your day-trips. - Hotel rooms have only semi-individual air conditioning/heating controls. You could make it warmer but couldn’t individually cool the room. Even with our unit off and the window open (in December), the room was rather warm. - Overall, very nice hotel stay…we would return.

author: Joe_33
title: A new hotel with stylish and comfortable public areas & good food
text: Positives: • A new hotel with good design. • Well appointed public spaces: a stylish bar, a large and very pleasant lounge area and a large terrace with views. • Plenty of free parking immediately in front of the hotel • An interesting view down the valley from each of the rooms • Good air conditioning • Internet fast and reliable. • A very good price for the room. • An iron and ironing board in the room – enabled me to get on top of my laundry. • Staff friendly, spoke English and helpful with local knowledge. They found my reservation in seconds (a rare experience for me in Turkey). Negatives: • Not that close (around 2km) to the new or old parts of Mardin – both a little too far to walk – so your car needs to be driven. The old part of town is up a steep hill and parking can be difficult in the narrow streets of the old town. I parked on a wide road below the old town and had a very pleasant walk up through the alleys to the top (hard to get lost in the maze of alleys – you just keep going up hill). There is one good restaurant in walking distance of the hotel (it is the first one you reach walking away from the hotel) and a shop selling alcohol. • The “extras” at the hotel are pricey – breakfast was $12 and the shop charges about 3 times what local stores charge. • The hotel is on a new street that doesn’t show on my GPS – worth finding the hotel on Google maps before you set out. • People arriving by intercity bus would need a taxi from the otogar. Overall A very good place to stay – a little bit of the USA in eastern Turkey. Not very ethnic but I enjoyed 2 days break from Turkish hotels (and some of their interesting quirks).

author: TrishHWashington_DC
title: Hilton Haven
text: I'm coming from a sister Hilton Garden Inn in Sanliurfa with exact same decor and lay-out. If you're looking for local color, this is not the place to stay. But if you're like me and experience local color all day and appreciate a modern, well-lit, comfortable room with amenities like wi-fi, then this new hotel is perfect for the weary traveller. Hilton did a great job furnishing the rooms with space-efficient furniture and an ergonomic desk chair. The rooms are very well-lit for reading ( a bugaboo for me in hotels) with plenty of plugs (another hotel annoyance) for computers, i-Pads, phones, and such. Terrific bathrooms, small but very efficient and amenities abound (except shower caps). The king beds are comfortable with good side tables and two bedside lights on the wall-- one is general lighting and one is goose-necked for night reading. Climate control is excellent. No complaints there. The staff are friendly and I assume just learning the ropes of a hotel chain. The hotel is situated just out of town-- taxi or bus needed-- on a hill. This is the first built of what will be a hotel area, for a Sheraton and another major chain hotel will soon break ground. The restaurant for breakfast is lovely, offering a buffet with wide variety of foods and outdoor seating. A Precor gym is on the lower level as well as an indoor pool and Jaccuzzi and a laundry room for guests staying a while. For an area which is just beginning to see more tourism, this hotel is a welcomed respite and much nicer than the older Hiltons in the U.S.

author: Cartercook01
title: Wonderful Stay - great staff and location!
text: My husband and I stayed at the Hotel Tahiti for 6 nights. The hotel staff was amazing and did everything and more to make our stay perfect. The hotel feels more like a 4 star. Great central location for exploring the island and restaurants in walking distance at night. Several things worth mentioning: - The hotel staff made all the dinner reservations I requested prior to our arrival. Reception staff walked us personally to where to park our scooter. Very friendly and always helpful. - We arrived a day early. The corner room we had reserved was occupied that night. The next day the staff insisted on moving all our belongings while we enjoyed time at the beach. - Breakfast is exceptional and included a wide variety of foods and champagne with attentive staff. I have no idea how the staff found out it was my husband’s birthday, but the servers brought him a small cake w champagne and strawberries while singing Happy Birthday. - Corner room had a good view of the sea (see pics from room) very comfortable bed. Lobby was nicely decorated. Entire hotel is cleaned and tended to constantly. - Lobby bar staff was awesome. Helped us with ice for our small beach cooler each day. Made after dinner drinks for us (even if they were closed). Pool bar was also equally has accommodating. Can’t wait to go back!

author: bierre1
title: Good service and great location
text: Third time in Formentera and this year we decided to stay at the Tahiti for our 8 days long vacay. What we liked: - Location: in the heart of the most lively town of the island, Es Pujols, and steps from the beach. I have to say that my favorite town is Sant Francesc but still, you can't beat the sea views over the Mediterranean. Also, some great restaurants are around the corner. - Staff: literally everyone is super kind and friendly. - Bed: so comfy, we slept like babies! - Breakfast: delicious buffet with a lot of choices, from charcuterie to pastries to fresh fruit, bottle of iced Cava included. What we didn't like: - Room: just average and overpriced for what it was. We stayed in a Best Superior with partial sea view and it was tiny. Really tiny. Pack light because otherwise you will have a lot of difficulties on opening your luggage as there's limited space in the room. The bathroom was also very little, and looked a little tired even after the remodeling. - Value for money: Formentera still lacks in luxury accommodations and everything is generally very pricey (and we all know that). Tahiti is no exception. Priced like a 5* hotel but it's basically a 3* who went under a cheap renovation in order to get another star. The outside area is pretty and so is the lobby, but you can definitely notice that the building is old.. if you come here, don't expect anything luxurious. It's all about the location and the service. Overall we had a good stay but for what we we paid I was expecting a little more in terms of comfort and rooms.

author: beebobBrighton
title: Stunning, beautiful hotel!!😘😘
text: Just got back from 9 days of staying with partner and 3 grown up kids at this truly gorgeous hotel. From the moment we arrived we're taken for complimentary drinks and nibbles on the seating area overlooking the beach for amazing sunset and views..Robert the manager extremely welcoming as was lovely Manu the bar tender.. couldn't do enough during our stay to always greet us with smiles and to see if we were enjoying our stay. Also a big shout for Frank at the pool bar.. lovely chap.. always on hand with smiles and chats. All staff very welcoming. The gorgeous aroma of Tahiti reed diffusers filled the whole hotel like a fresh clean enveloping hug..and they gave you miniature bottle to take home. Breakfast buffet amazing..superb choice and everything so fresh.. including freshly baked pastries and bread. Lovely new clean contemporary hotel.. amazing location on the beach and 5min walk into Es Pujols that had a great mix of restaurants and bars and shops.. including array of craft stalls along seafront..nice relaxed vibe in town. Thank you so much Robert to you and your wonderful staff for making our stay such a pleasurable stay😊..it is truly up there on favourite hotels list and would love to come back some day. Room Tip: 108..most definitely best in hotel. 1st floor left hand corner spot.. AMAZING views of beach and Ibiza in background..and get both sunrise and sunsets.. glorious.

author: seaclick
title: Highly recommend this hotel
text: We stayed at Tahiti Hotel for 4 nights. We had a room with no sea view. The room size was perfect and addionally we had a balcony which was perfect. When I made the reservation I thought the room was going to be smaller but exceeded my expectations. Very quiet room. Neat and clean. I loved the decoration of the whole hotel. Modern with style, loved the lights it had. All the staff was extremely nice and friendly. The manager was after each detail and was waiting us when we arrived. This is great customer service! It has a pool that is nice although it doesnt have sea view. Nevertheless we scarcely used it as we prefer the sea. The hotel has a great location , many restaurants nearby. At the same time you have the possibility of walking to all the other beaches without taking a car. The hotel has no parking but we didn’t need it. If you need beach chairs or beach umbrella this has to be payed in the beach. The hotel does not include beach service. The breakfast is wonderful they had everything I liked and even more. I highly recommend this hotel

author: Ambisholiday
title: Rubbish WiFi and breakfast rules
text: I need to work when I am away, so good WiFi is vital to me. The Tahiti WiFi makes you log in every time you use the device, this irriated me intensely. But the speed of the WiFi is crap. So I couldn't actually do my work. The staff knew about this and could do nothing. I think it is pathetic in a decent hotel, very poor indeed. The breakfast...the food is great, good spread lots of variety. But the room has the acoustics of a school dining hall, every noise is amplified and it is loud. You are not allowed to eat outside on the nice decking area they have. NOT ALLOWED. My wife wanted to take her coffee outside and the breakfast Gestapo (see picture) told her she needed to buy a coffee from the bar and to drink outside. The manager was very happy to tell me "Yes those are the rules". We left 4 days early. What sort of hotel dictates where in the hotel you can drink your breakfast coffee?Does it really matter to them? Ask for the school rules when you arrive or you might get a detention.

author: djpe
title: Lovely hotel & superb service
text: A 2 week stay as a Thompson package from UK. A lovely modern hotel whose staff are exceptionally pleasant and helpful, offering efficient, attentive but not intrusive service at all times. Room on first floor with a pleasant verandah & nice sea view. Air conditioning works well. Good wardrobe space & safe provided at no extra cost. Small fridge and coffee making facilities - soft drinks/milk/coffee replaced daily as part of the package. Fresh towels for swimming pool or beach provided each day. (Beach is very near indeed - along hotel's own path of maybe 30 yards or so to the promenade). Pool crystal clear and incredibly well maintained. Plenty of loungers and huge parasols. Poolside bar - a great range of drinks, coffee, snacks with a lady who could not have been more pleasant and helpful, an absolute asset ! Breakfast - superb. A huge range of hot and cold items with daily variations up until midday! Lounge areas inside and out well attended by pleasant staff and good service. Great selection of restaurants (walkable) In the area. Highly recommended - we wil be back!

author: LeeBakerLegion
title: First Class
text: Wow! Just WOW. This hotel has (almost!) it all. The breakfast selection is truly phenomenal. Never seen anything like it before and it out-did most 5 star hotels. The service from all staff was perfect. The rooms were immaculate and the cleaning was excellent. Maid service was on a daily basis. Pool was amazing and the towels supplied were of the best quality. The room minibar was restocked daily for free. Reception staff were very welcoming and helpful. Beautiful position on the beachfront with fantastic views. Why 'almost'? The free wi-fi. Appalling. Very slow indeed even right in front of the reception area. A first class, four-star hotel should have a free wi-fi service better than was provided. The only minor issue with such a truly fantastic hotel.

author: SophieT68
title: Amazing premises, top-notch service, fabulous hotel
text: We needed a place to REST after an exhausting year, so we chose the quiet island of Formentera. On Tripadvisor we saw excellent reviews for this hotel so we chose to stay there. THAT WAS THE BEST DECISION THIS SUMMER! We arrived late by the last ferry and were nonetheless greeted very warmly by Eduardo who very rapidly grew on us. Always attentive, friendly and professional, his caring manners were the personal touch every guest dreams of. Overall the staff is extremely friendly, helpful and makes you feel like you're part of a big well-wishing family. The room (superior - well worth it) was extremely comfortable, serviced when WE needed it to be, and stocked with the mod cons everyone needs. The bedding was very comfortable, the air conditioning was efficient and noiseless, the view fabulous. The next day we went for breakfast and WHAT A SPREAD THEY HAD!!!! A great variety of dishes superbly presented suited every known kind of picky eater. The service was efficient and rapid, fresh squeezed orange juice brought included in the room rate... Perfect. In the afternoon after a good swim, we chose to sit at the beautiful terrace overlooking the beach and were brought the ULTIMATE sangría one can wish for. Pure heaven... The hotel is located near the village of Pujols, where there are a lot of eateries and where we had fabulous tapas one evening, at a very affordable price. Car rentals up the road offer a discount to Hotel Tahiti patrons and we visited the entire island for less than 80Euros (one day) including petrol!! Overall our stay was beyond our expectations and we encourage those of you considering making that trip to book it NOW!

author: elviscafe
title: Superb service, excellent food, great location
text: Finally found what we have been looking for on Formentera...! The website doesn't say much and in no way extols the fabulous hotel that this is. I had read the few English reviews on tripadvisor which helped to make the decision, but also know Formentera reasonably well. We couldn't get a main hotel room for our full stay, so stayed in the pool studio to start off with - given it was half the price of the main hotel, we were very pleasantly surprised. Room was fine and you can still just about see the sea. Main hotel room was bigger, nice balcony and more amenities, but to be honest, I would be happy enough with a pool studio again. The breakfast - which is truly impossible to describe - is literally amazing. Six stations of just about every kind of food imaginable and all to an excellent quality. served from 8am to midday, they have played an absolute blinder here! Food - we didn't eat there but wish we had now. They have a pop up restaurant twice a week for a fixed price of €40 for 5 courses - the menus looked very good. The snacks form the main bar are amazing (try the empanada de carne) and the pool bar are also good quality. Location - about a 5 minute walk along the sea front from the main high street in es pujols, lined with bars and restaurants (and the market stalls in the evening) all the way. Beach - about 10 yards form the front of the hotel through the hotels private entrance (nice touch). There are nicer beached on formentera, but it is a pretty good one. Lovely big fluffy beach towels free every day form the hotel too! Cleanliness - perfect Downsides - not that I can think of! Maybe only that the Italians are all so immaculately turned out at all times...!

author: notrag07
title: Tremendous
text: Hotel Tahiti is located within a five minutes walk of the center of Es Pujols. My wife and I have now returned for our fifth stay here. We tend to go at the beginning of June when Es Pujols is still relatively quiet as it is described as a "lively resort". Es Pujols is a good place with a reasonable number of shops and plenty of small restaurants for evening meals. The Hotel Tahiti offers most things that anyone could want for a relaxing time. Clean rooms including a fridge with free soft drinks and TV but with only CNN in English. Worth paying the extra money for sea view rooms as the turquoise colored sea is less than 50 yards from the hotel. The hotel is not cheap for a 2 star hotel but is worth the money as the classification does not do the hotel justice. The swimming pool is well maintained with free sun beds and shades. There is a drinks and light refreshment area by the pool. Breakfast is served up to 12.00pm and offers the widest selection of both hot and cold foods which are unlikely to be bettered in a 5 star hotel. New this year is the ability to take a set course evening meal for 40 euros which will appeal to some but we like trying out the many restaurants that are available in Es Pujols. The staff at reception are helpful and speak reasonable English. The majority of the guests staying here are Italian, then Spanish & German. English are in the minority which also reflects the number that visit the island. If you want fish and chips and other English delights then don't bother to take the 30 minute boat trip from Ibiza! Do take time to visit the various beaches, each one has it's own character. It is possible to rent a car but on an island of 50 square miles is a bit of a waste. Many people rent bikes, scooters or Quad bikes to get around and they are ideal for traveling down the rough unadapted tracks to beaches which are difficult to access by car and definitely are not on a bus route. Discover a deserted beach with a small restaurant and it will make your stay at Hotel Tahiti even more memorable.

author: Buttinhams
title: Could so easily be a five star hotel
text: We spent the first two weeks in September at the Hotel Tahiti and will certainly return again. Hotel positive points (1) The reception area / bar / outside terrace are immaculate. (2) The breakfast / brunch buffet served between 8am & 12pm is superb with daily variations to a very high standard. (3) The pool and pool area is maintained very well with comfortable, adjustable sun loungers with deep cushions and large umbrellas. The pool staff are very friendly and eager to help. (4) The rooms are claned daily to a very good standard. (5) 10 bottled soft drinks are added to your fridge each day, free of charge. (6) Free WiFi access is provided for the duration of your stay. (7) The location of the hotel is excellent, virtually on the beach and within minutes walk of bars and restaurants Hotel negative point (1) We booked through Thomson and were given a "standard room" as there was no option to upgrade. Although the room was comfortable enough, it was pretty basic,and the bathroom was very small with a tiny bath and limited space to store toiletries etc. We also had a room overlooking the ca rpark, which seemed the norm for people booking through Thomson. When we enquired about room upgrades we were told that there were "Superior Rooms with sea views" but these had to be booked directly through the hotel. We will book directly with the hotel next year and make our own arrangements for fights / transfers etc. The supplement for a "superior room" is 30 euros per night. The Resort of Es Pujols is quite small and caters predominantly for the large numbers of Italian tourists coming to the island. The restaurants are generally excellent ranging from cafe type eateries to high class steak and seafood reataurants. Typically the restaurants do not start serving food until 8.30pm, although there are a few exceptions that open around 7.30pm. Recommended Restaurants: Chez Fred - Basic pizza / pasta / meat / fish El Gaucho - Argentinian steak house - unbelievable steaks Sa Varadero - Spanish food to a very high standard Pizza Pazza - Authentic Italian pizzas Sa Palmera - A huge menu, ranging from local rabbit dishes, fish & meat to pizzas & pastas. Excellent and very reasonable Bocasalina - High Class Tapas, Meat & Fish dishes Capri - Outstanding seafood restaurant The local beach is white sand with warm waters, ideal for swimmimg. The sunloungers are 6 euros a day each as is a parasol.

author: anna69wallo
title: perfect - the best holiday we've ever had!
text: This hotel is superb, the position is incredible right next to the most amazing white sandy beach. The sea is clear blue which always took out breath away. The hotel itself has been modernised and is now very contemporary, clean and the service is excellent. The staff are really excellent and are desperate for you to enjoy your stay with them. This hotel only offers B&B but the breakfast is served from 0800-1200 which is basically a brunch and the menu reflects this - I wont spoil the experience for you but safe to say the choices are excellent and breakfast really is a treat. The swimming pool is just lovely, nice and clean, when we were there very few people used the pool so we really had it to ourselves - it was bliss. There is also a lovely selection of complimentary soft drinks left for you to enjoy every day in the fridge in your room - this will save you a fortune as food and drink are really expensive all around the resort Es-pujols where this hotel is based as its the tourist capital. As the hotel is only B&B you have to find your own lunch and evening meal - there are so many places to eat, the quality is very high but its not cheap - the cheapest meal we had was a Chez Fred (2 pizza's and a bottle of house wine) which cost 21 Euro's. The most expensive was a meal at Valadero which is a grill/streak house on the seafront which cost 79 euro's for two of us. There is plenty of italian restaurants to try as so many italians go to this resort for their holidays but there is also a new Italian Tapas bar down one of the side streets off the seafront which only opened this season - it is stunning and the food will stay with me forever - the restaurant needs peoples support cos its the new kid on the block so please give is a try its called Formosa Tapas and is opposite a burger bar...There is plenty to do on formentera, there is a great bus service that gets you around the island but remember alot of places including the capital san franciso close up their business's at 2pm for a 4 hour siesta so go to these place in the morning. The best way to see the island is either by moped, bicycle or electric bike - you dont really need a car. The island is big on preserving the enviroment, its very green and you are expected to respect it. There are some great walks all around the island and several nudist beaches. All in all we had the most wonderful holiday, we found formentera the most wonderful place, stunning etc...its only just over 2 hours from the UK with a 30 minute ferry journey to get to the Island. My only advice is leave your kids at home unless they are under 5 they'll probably get quite board, this is an island for the grown ups with people visiting year after year - we have now joined that gang cos we think we've found our special place....enjoy!! its a holiday we will never forget and feel so fortunate to have been able to find a carribean island in the med!!!

author: Bruce0604
title: Proabably the best little hotel in the world... for total relaxation
text: We don't want too many people to know about this little gem of a hotel and we'd like to keep it a secret as much as possible. However we shouldn't be so selfish and the management and staff deserve to be praised as much as possible. I fear more and more people are getting to hear about it anyway, so why hold back? This was the second time we've stayed at the Hostal Tahiti, having previously been there in September 2007, and I'd have to say it's just go better! The hotel and the rooms are kept spotless and it has everything you need for a complete chillout. As ever the staff were all very friendly and welcoming, and ensured our stay was a complete pleasure from check-in to check-out! Like last time we hired bikes for 5 days so we could travel to some of the nearby beaches and other places of interest with relative ease, much more relaxing (and environmentally friendly) than the scooters which the hordes of Italians seem to prefer. It's also a cheap way to get about, at 40 euros for the both of us, and most places can be accessed easily as the island is small and flat enough (in most places) for leisurely cyclists like us. We visited more places last time - San Francisco, Cala Seona, La Mola, etc - but we only used the bikes to get to our favourite spots on the beaches at Les Illetes and Levant quicker. It was too hot to travel too far anyway! We also discovered more, and better, places to eat than last time - and on our last night we found even more down a wee side street... so that gives us another reason to go back soon! Our favourite was Casanita, just down the street from the hotel, where the dishes were delicious but very reasonably priced. The most expensive meal was at the Caminito, an Argentinian restaurant, and the setting was very beautiful and romantic. I'd have to say our steaks were probably worth the hefty price paid. We also had a very lovely meal at Chez Gered, in another lovely setting round by the boardwalk on the beachfront, although communication was a bit of a problem as none of the staff spoke any english and it was mostly geared to the Italian clientele. I think we'll just need to take Italian lessons (not spanish funnily enough) to make our next trip to Formentera a little easier. This little island off the coast of Ibiza is proving to be our own little bit of paradise, and without the hassle of a long haul trip, and if Carlsberg did hotels then I'm certain the Tahiti would be high up the chain.

author: howardfh
title: Superb accommodation on a glorious island
text: Let's start with "Hostal Tahiti". This phrase must be some kind of Spanish anagram of the term "Luxury hotel", no way is this a 2* hostal. Many of the rooms have balconys overlooking the sea, and have (wait for it) fridge, kettle, tea/coffee, flatscreen TV, airconditioning, cutlery, free safe, bath/shower with enough shampoo to keep a supermodel happy, and, as I had booked with the excellent Astbury Formentera, complimentary fruit and a fridge-full of drinks (all kept being topped up!). Oh, such nice touches! One usually associates this sort of service in 'normal' hotels with a "oh, so you expect to breathe, sir? That will be an extra £3.50/night + VAT" Add the brilliant breakfast buffet, comfy lounge sofas, well-stocked bar inside, a cracking outdoor pool/jaccusi and a smaller pool for toddlers, plus direct access to the beach, I'm looking under every pillow to find a fault. Surely the staff must be a bit off and disinterested? Nope, they get an A+ in being helpful and cheery. The cleaners, then? Nope again, they're also very thorough. Ah, found a disappointment - the pool bar was shut when I was there in late September! That means having to leave the hostel... ....to visit Es Pujols and Formentera. The village has a great night-life, not, ahem, thousands of drunken youths out to drink more beer than they can swim in, but genuine holiday-makers, many senior, who just want to eat out and have a quiet drink in the classy establishments. Es Pujols has two fine beaches (spotlessly clean and safe to swim in) itself, but travel a few miles north by bus or bike (or walk through the dunes) to the best beaches in the world. White sand, turquoise sea, and no building development whatsoever, save for some quaint beach bars/resturants. I hate writing all this as it means more people will go, and I don't want Formentera spoiled. Safe roads, very little crime, no pollution, and, on many of the beaches, no need for costumes. "Formentera" is definitely an anagram of "Paradise, Do Not Spoil". I'll be back, and back, and back......

author: Passenger96252
title: The Pipe’s Annual foreign jaunt
text: Well where do I start? Arrived at 11am only to be told that I couldn’t book in until 4pm. Booked in at 4pm didn’t get into our room until 5:15pm as we were told that we were on the 1st floor, then the 3rd floor, then the 1st floor again, then told that the barrel in the door was broken and the handyman was en route to our room on the 3rd floor, no sign of the said handyman who apparently had gone to the 1st floor while we were on the 3rd floor... After going back to reception and losing my temper (which I have never done on holiday) was told by another receptionist that we were actually on the 13th floor! Got into the room at 5:15pm, bearing in mind that when I booked this hotel with Travel Republic it was cheap and cheerful.... I have booked cheap and cheerful on a few occasions and up until this point have never, ever had to clean a room (allegedly the cleaners had been into the room and had cleaned it) there was splashes of tomato soup inside the microwave, food debris on the worktops in the kitchen area, the fridge was absolutely manking, the list goes on.... and to top it all off didn’t have enough crockery and glasses for 4 adults.... asked for more.... was promptly told no way and would have to manage with what I had!!! The pool area.... on arrival in the afternoon I spotted something very odd... there were lots of sunbeds but people were putting towels on the floor... turns out that you had to pay for sunbeds and parasols (per day)... also I had to pay for the hire of a kettle, toaster and a tv remote (tv was bloody useless as didn’t pick up any channels at all)... have only ever paid for tv remote at all other hotels I’ve stayed at... the only thing I’m really thankful for is that we were Self Catering as speaking to a few other Brits at the hotel said the food was shocking.... people on AI couldn’t get a drink after 6 at the pool bar as she’d shut up shop at 5:45pm!!! The resort itself is beautiful and well worth a holiday but please don’t stay here.... absolutely shocking and I’m no Mrs Bucket by any stretch of the imagination as I’ve said prior I’ve paid similar to stay in hotels in the Canaries and the Balearics and they’ve been far far better than the one we ended up in!!!! You have been warned!!!!

author: Colley10
title: Decent hotel at a very decent price
text: I have stayed at this hotel twice in the last two years and whilst it may be a bit dated in places, it is a very decent hotel in a good location. I have read numerous negative reviews about this hotel, yes the sheets only get changed once a week which isn't great but the food is ok without being anything special... but for the very very reasonable price you can book this all inclusive holiday for you can hardly be expecting Gordon Ramsay to be making your breakfast?! The pool is nice, staff were pleasant, drinks were good. The All Inclusive includes 3 meals per day and there is also a snack bar, I have read a bad review that it is only open for less than 3 hours a day but the wait time between the three main meal times isnt long so I feel the snack bar is primarily there for people who maybe missed a meal! Basically you get what you pay for with this hotel, but really it isnt as bad as some of these reviews... No double beds... of course there isnt what happens when two friends stay in these rooms... they cant be changing the beds can they... no shampoo or shower gel in the rooms... of course there isnt man, its a cheap hotel. The pool is salty... its a saltwater pool which is advertised... oh and there is wifi, but it doesnt reach all the rooms... dont believe the lies, lower them Hilton Hotel expectations at Budget Hostel prices and have a great holiday

author: foodiewaitress22
title: The most rude staff, horrible place avoid!
text: Now I have avoided writing this review as we returned from our holiday here almost a month ago because I didn’t want to be completely horrible as I was one of the people who were putting my faith in the positive reviews. Maybe, just maybe, if you are placed in one of the main blocks things could be differently however we were not. We booked this hotel 8 months before travelling so therefore gave plenty of notice of our “block 1/2” review. (Keeping in mind it’s not as cheap as everyone claims unless you go for all inclusive). Despite this we arrived late & low & behold were couriered over to block 3. We had to get a van to pick us up & drop us there as mentioned before it is placed across a dual carriage way. We spent the first 4 days of our holiday in hell, being told time & time again we would be transferred to a better room only to have each day ruined by the disappointment of not being moved but however being spoken to like an absolute dog by receptionist Juan. The most rude man I’ve ever met! I sat one day & cried uncontrollably in the lobby of the main building because of a completely unnecessary argument which was held. On the 4th day in we eventually spoke to a much nicer man who I can only imagine to be some sort of manager & he explained that we weren’t in fact moving at all so we spent the first 4 days waking up every morning in preparation to be moved. You can see how this really angered us. Once we knew we weren’t being moved we tried our best to enjoy the time we did have. I have no problem whatsoever with dated rooms, I’ve been to Portugal many times & I know this is the norm, however rude staff & dirty rooms, I am not okay with. Just see the pictures attached. Balcony door did not lock no security all situated in main hotel, sockets were stuck behind headboards which didn’t move, mouldy presses, dirty walls, our “pool view” which consisted of an empty unused pool, & a dual carriage way we had to cross to get to the main building. Anyone who decides to hope for the best & trust the positive reviews, the tips I will give you is if you want your towels changed they need to be on the floor as if they’re hanging up they’re assumed as clean, pool is saltwater & is €1.50 per sunbed & parasol (which is one thing I didn’t mind as your guaranteed them). Don’t take the risk with the thought that you’ve requested the main blocks because early August they facilitate mainly Portuguese people travelling English & Irish seem to be thrown over the third block & as I was told by one of the horrible staff “you’re just a number”.

author: fatdrummer
title: Better as self catering
text: Used this hotel about 20 years ago. We went all inclusive this time. Check in is around 4pm. Was straight forward and not too long a wait. The hotel rooms are needing a refurbishment. No air-conditioning but a wall mounted fan in the living area and in the bedroom. No light out on the balcony.we were in block 2, there was 4 lifts and were working most of the time. There was not a lot of choice at mealtimes and we ate out a couple of times. Had to queue a few times but not for long. The pool was cold and salt water, just perfect in the very hot weather. Hiring sun beds was a great idea. Pool cleaned before opening every day, cleaners in the room every day. Hotel was clean enough. Pool staff, cleaning staff, restaurant staff all good. Entertainment team and lifeguards all good fun. Would use again, but not all inclusive.

author: Y947TPrachelk
title: Don’t believe all the terrible reviews!
text: I’ve just returned from 10 nights here with my 2 children and although I never normally leave reviews, I felt compelled to leave one to try and balance some of the extremely negatives ones. This isn’t a 5* hotel but it doesn’t profess to be. It is very large and as you would expect, loud. We never experienced the queues that others have complained of and always found plenty to eat both in the main restaurant and snack bar. Likewise, we never had an issue getting served for drinks. The times for the serving of spirits are clearly stated so I’m not sure why people complain about this after the event. This goes for the hiring of sun beds too. I did initially think this was a bad idea but after going and being able to get sun beds at any time of the day, I think I’m actually a convert to this system rather than the normal towels being strewn over empty sun beds from those who’ve reserved them, “just in case”. It’s 1.50 Euros a day so budget for this. The rooms are basic but ours was very large and clean. The beds were changed 3 times during our 10 night stay which was more than adequate for us and more often than I’d have changed ours at home! I found all the staff friendly and the reception staff were very helpful. They all seem to work very hard servicing such a large hotel but did so with good grace. The pools are fabulous and well maintained. The resort itself is also lovely and the beach is gorgeous and clean. I found the sun beds very expensive to hire here though (6 euros each). We had a fabulous holiday here and I’m personally glad I read all the negative reviews before I went because I was very pleasantly surprised. Tip; request a room on a low floor in either block one or two.

author: jades794
title: Nothing to worry about
text: If I’m honest I was a little concerned about staying at the hotel purely based off the reviews. However I’m really happy with the value for money I got for my stay. It was our first time visiting Portugal in general and I would definitely go back. The location is great. There is so much to do around the area and the hotel was always clean, the the staff where always helpful. The pool was always cleaned , safe and you never have to fight for a sun lounger because of the 1Euro charge for the day. I personally completely understand the logic in it. All four of us always had something we could eat (even if it’s not the largest range of food, but I think people forget they didn’t pay for a 5* holiday). Our room was also cleaned daily unless we asked for it not to be because we was in it and the room had supplies for eating in if we wanted and various items for the beach tucked away - like beach chairs, floats that we could use. The only downsides for us personally as a family is there is no free ice cream/ice lollies but the ice cream wasn’t overpriced elsewhere lucky. Also maybe for others is that even if all inclusive you pay for spirits (very cheap) before 8- free afterwards but other alcohol like local beer and wine is free. The pool is also cold but again really not a big deal, once your in you get over it. In fact my kids didn’t even seem to notice. There is two bars, a video(entertainment bar) and a games room that would keep us entertained when we decided to stay in the hotel In the evenings. I wanted to make a point of when I came home of making an honest review to help others when reading all the Reviews and the truth is I really enjoyed my stay and so did my young family.

author: 665hopem
title: Amazing! Ignore all the complaints!
text: The staff are so nice and understanding. My family and I were given 2 rooms because there were 5 of us, but my dad and brother only used one for sleeping, so we talked to the manager about it and we gave up the room, they gave us 2 more beds and agreed to bump us up to all inclusive instead of giving us a refund! The food is hit and miss but most of it is really good. There are 2 decent sized restaurants and both have the same food. Lunch can be repetitive but it still tastes really good. The pool is amazing, it's so big and it's a good thing that it is saltwater. You get used to how cold it is at first and get used to how salty it is. You have to pay for sunbeds and parasols but that's fine because they aren't that expensive and they put it where you want it to go. There is a supermarket and a souvenir shop right beside the front entrance, some things are a bit expensive, but it's still really good. The maids clean everything every day so it is cleaner than what people say. The rooms are very good and the beds are quite comfortable. The beach is only a 15 minute walk up a hill and it is beautiful. The all inclusive isn't the best as you have to pay for slushies and cocktails, and for an ice cream you have to go to the supermarket, and I understand because it is a budget hotel, but you get free meals, soft drinks and juice, and free spirits from 8:00-11:00pm. The entertainment is brilliant, they do aqua fitness at the pool every day and then they go to the bar every night and do dances for the kids and then go on to the main thing. While I was there it was bingo, parrots, karaoke, dancing, lizards, guess the song, and then quizigo (a cross between a quiz and bingo). Their names are Patricia, Mikaela and Enrique and they are all lovely. We went to ZooMarine while we were there and they provide transport and everything. Ignore the reviews, this hotel is lovely!

author: katieo168
title: People need to lightgen up
text: Arrived 2 days ago- staying 10 days. Reception staff were 2 lovely girls. Obviously had my paperwork (why wouldn’t I?) They said we could leave our bags and come back in 2x hours as the room wasn’t ready which is fine. They even offered us free lunch for the inconvenience. We are only on a b&b basis. Got back and room was ready. Clean tidy and massive apartment. A bit dated but we weren’t expecting much. Pushed the 2x single beds together which wasn’t an inconvenience really. Breakfast wasn’t the best selection but there’s so many places round about to try. Pools nice- just the sunbed thing but it means people aren’t running down at 7 then going away all day-smart idea. So far so good. Would defo recommend for the price I don’t know why people complain about little things. I felt I needed to post this review because of all the negativity. We are in block 1 also.

author: paulcots35
title: Not bad at all
text: I am here at the moment with my wife and 2 kids. I was worried after reading the reviews over how the holiday would go. Luckily we’re having a great time. We are staying in block 2. The rooms are dated but big, bright and clean. The cleaners have been in everyday except last Sunday. We are all inclusive and would certainly choose this option again in the future. The food is hit and miss, but you’ll definitely find something you’ll eat. You won’t go hungry. The drinks are plentiful, and yes, at times the queueing can be irritating but relax, grab a beer and sit in queue, your on holiday. The pool area is fantastic and the staff around the pool are brilliant. Fabritzio the lifeguard, a genuinely nice guy, thanks so much for keeping an eye on everyone in and around the pool as well as the entertainment you are bringing to my children. If I ask my children, who’s the nicest staff, after fabritzio, they would say scarlet. Thanks to scarlet at the pool bar, no matter how busy it is, she will meet you with a smile. I had one issue, the water was completely gone in the room. I went to reception, met a very pleasant lad and informed him of what was wrong, we went for a walk for an hour and on return the issue was fixed. We can’t complain. And we will probably come back in the future.

author: laurajM813DX
title: Do not go!!!
text: Just arrived back from here today, absolute shambles of a hotel! All inclusive? Defo not! No spirits until 8pm at night, cues of people outside restaurants every night before doors open and waiting over an hour to even get a foot in ththe door. Snack bar that opens when it feels like. Asked to see a manager twice and not once did he show face he sent some maintence manager to speak to 3 irate guests who tried to fob us off. Food is terrible very few options great if your a rabbit and eat lots of salad kids nuggets that are solid I wouldn’t feed my dogs half the things they served. Rooms terrible and old with a toilet that constantly runs during the night bath that leaks and tiles all cracked, tiny lifts that for 3 people, 2 massive blocks of apartments and one across a busy road over a bridge with steps away from a pool. You have to rent a tv remote pay €1.50 per day for each an umbrella and sun lounger you also have to pay €1.50 for them to tell you when your transfer is coming for you. Anything to make a buck here and they really don’t care. The fear on the receptions face when anyone walks towards them. Never in my life have I ever stayed in such a bad place it’s like a hostel. We spent most of our holiday quing for food how bad is that! We were all inclusive but by the 3rd day we were too hungry and started eating out costing a lot more. Portugal is beautiful itself but I will never be back I’m afraid it’s put me right off the country it’s that bad!

author: J8049SUrebeccas
title: OMG!!!!
text: So eventually checked in AFTER 16:00 having arrived at 12pm, hotel looked ok tbh, then it starts.. collected the key, reception said a car will take us to our room?? A CAR??? anyway off we went, tower block j, floor 7, not even manned, no pool no restaurant nothing.. guy says it’s ok u can save ur legs by going through the garage but ignore the mess?? Ok, so room at first glance was ok tbh, IF YOUR SELF CATERING, we was ALL INCLUSIVE, and having to walk everyday over the bridge to the main complex where we had paid to stay.. totally gutted, on the phone to get it sorted as I am not staying here!! Got in contact with the hotel manager, lovely bloke tbh, ( when we actually got to see him due to long queues of folks complaining too ) those who were half board got upgraded to ALL INCLUSIVE as a good will gesture however you had to queue for almost an hour to eat and this was at every meal time, then when u did finally get seated there was no food so again you had to wait,.. sat down ate your well below average food quickly as you knew there was a long line of hungry guests still waiting.. so what on earth were they gonna do for us, feeling like an outcast due to Brexit we planned our strategy.. the manager said her can move us but not until Sunday?? It’s now Thursday?? Nope not good enough, holiday company are in contact and we are all working together ( HALE TRAVEL REPUBLIC ) so we decide to stay where we are in “ zombie towers “ and down grade to self catering and get a tidy sum back, and eat out, there is plenty of restaurants and bars to eat a short walk away, it made more sense, now I am no way one to complain and never have, until now, so if u do stay here go self catering trust me it’s easier, I’m not letting this ruin my holiday as the place is fantastic but just be mindful please and look for alternative hotels in the area, the pics are genuine and real.. btw u gotta pay for ur sun beds at €1.50 a day?? Jeeeees, all inclusive includes ur meals, beer, wine, squash and that’s about it, oh and look out for the pink wrist band there for the Spanish, they get priority here?? Anyway.. pls read and take this in, I don’t want anyone feeling like we did!!!

author: S630OGdavidt
title: Clube Praia da Rocha
text: Arrived at 9.30pm 15th May by . 10.30 we decided we were not spending a week here. In 48 years of Marriage I have never taken my Wife to such a dreadful hotel. Our apartment needed a complete refurb. Furniture at least 40 years old. Paint missing from walls, unsafe electrics, dirty bathroom. You have to pay for sunbeds. The bars are like bus station waiting areas. Arrogant and unhelpful reception manager.Hotel is too big for swimming pool area in my opinion. 12 inch CRT TV at least 25 years old. Terrible reception. You would have to be desperate to stay here. Inside . Dining room like a 3rd rate cafeteria. Only had breakfast and lunch, poor quality, then booked out. The reviews of very poor are correct. Love holidays should remove it from their website. Local restaurants told us that they serve a lot of customers who will not eat at the hotel. I could go on forever but i think you must have the gist of my opinions David UK

author: 876gemmaj
title: don't panic
text: honestly I think we all just need to step back and review our expectations of what a 3* in Portugal will be like. my sister and I (both in our 30s)are partial to a cheap break away and we've ended up in some very questionable places but reading the reviews even we were concerned. needlessly..I'm writing this by the pool and I'm having a lovely time. pool area - large and clean, yes you have to pay for loungers but as we read the description before we booked we knew this and if we hadn't it's not the end of the world. someone complained the pool is cold, of course it is it's a body of water outside. staff- couldn't fault them food - we only really go all inclusive for the drinks. the food was ok, average. I really don't know what the people giving scathing reviews are expecting? I'm a picky eater but come on for breakfast cereal, breads, croissants, fruit, yoghurt, eggs beans and bacon. lunch -soup, pasta, meatballs, salad fish, chicken. if I didn't like anything I had a salad and thank god for it and my waistline. we went out in the evening accommodation. the place is tired. you're heading back into the 70s. our room was very very tired but clean and functional which is all we want for somewhere to sleep. definitely zero wow factor. all in all I pronounce our trip a win.

author: 874kayas
title: Awful! Avoid
text: On artival at the hotel we arrived around half 11 in the evening the receptionist we checked in was very on arriveal the greeting that we had was rude and caused unessasary problems for myself and the family. When we arrived we explained we had a booking of 7 people confirmed the name the booking was made under to be told that we needed the “voucher” that we booked with, as we were unaware of this “voucher” we explained we did not have it but we had all the proof to show that the booking was ours including the invoice. The unhelpful member of staff would NOT stop going on about this voucher and I was made to go into our booking online (using my own data) to find what he was asking for, when we found what he wanted it was not even a voucher it was just the comformation of the booking that we had made, I also had email him the link to it but that was not good enought then I had to take screenshots and email them! When talking about the issue he was fully aware that the website we booked with had not sent us any form of “voucher” or told us to bring one with us and then he even admitted that it happened previously then tried to go back on himself and say it doesn’t happen at all. Many times we asked to speak to a manager but he was not responding, only 50mins later did he claim he would speak to the manager in the back but just walked in and straight back out and said “the manager said don’t worry about the voucher”. As we had travelled all day and arrived at the hotel by 11:30pm the 3younger children we had were getting restless. When we finally got our keys we had two rooms next to each other which weren’t the greatest, 1 room had cracks in the shower so it kept leaking, we found silverfish in the rooms and the water boiler was just a joke! 1 of the rooms had heating and 1 did not so we went to the desk to ask if it could be sorted and the same rude staff member replied “you shouldn’t have it you never paid for it” so the next day we spoke to another member and they sorted it out straight away. Every morning I was woken up early as there was banging coming from the upstairs and downstairs rooms to only find out people actually LIVE in the hotel and they were refurbishing. Also you have to pay for everything such as sunbeds, umbrellas, tv remotes, shouldn’t that already be included? Also as walk into block 1 there is a very strong fishy smell walking towards block 2 which I guess is the restaurant. Pool is not that great either, the weather was not the best whilst I was there but the pool could do with a bit of heating as it was freezing cold, I only went in to assist the children on the slide (the only thing I could not fault) and we all came out shivering! Location is good and a few decent clubs around and few places, as a teenager wouldn’t say there is much to do it does get boring. Beds are also uncomfortable and now that I am home me and a family member have both somehow got rashes which seemed to appear on the last day of our holiday. Other members of staff were friendly including the cleaner for our room so thank you

author: angelawithers66
title: AVOID AVOID AVOID
text: We have just arrived back from this dreadful place. I really don't know where to start. I wasn't expecting too much for the £450 a week (all inclusive) (what a joke) that we paid but was expecting the hotel and the room to be clean however basic it was. Our twin room was filthy, bathroom had footprints across the floor where it was clear that it had not been cleaned when the previous occupiers vacated. Bath was worn and shower attachments disgusting. Door was a disgrace and full of dirt etc. Twin room, one bed sheet was changed on the only occasion the so called cleaners came in, other bed was untouched along with the towels for the whole week. Electrics were dangerous, walls filthy and balcony rusty. Patio door didn't lock. We paid for self catering facilities which we were hoping it would include a kettle! nope had to pay for it and the sunbeds and umbrellas were charged on a daily basis around the pool area. All inclusive but everything had an extra charge. Sheets of glass were covering the tables in the sports bar which really is not appropriate with children about, only knocked my knee against it slightly and it moved. Please do not book this hotel,food was horrendous, ate out for the week, nothing suitable for the kiddies to eat or adults for that matter.I cannot stress enough, avoid this hotel , it shouldn't even be 2 star! Everyone we spoke to all agreed. Alex and Angela. Wales.

author: Vinnie0000
title: Trust me do not take your family to this hotel.
text: Hi Everyone, So sorry if you have booked here and if you have your family please make sure you have bought extra money to pay for meals out if you are all inclusive. Well where do I start. Upon arrival all looks good. Rooms you could get away with 3 star just. The maid never visited room even if you leave the sign hanging on the door knob to say clean room. Towels filthy even clean ones that where handed to us in corridor. Like I said earlier food inedible and repetitive, Badly ill. Who ever put a cockerel up on the roof that woke you up then the seagulls then the dog every morning???? Some apartments are privately owned so can everybody not make a noise please when departing fast. I can say that the only real good thing about this hotel was its position to the Squash club next door where you will find a great service for breakfast and drinks, Maybe the hotel chef should pop in there to pass on Knowledge to the owner of the hotel. It was a real shame because the area is great with a beautiful beach and surroundings. Staff nice people but please stand up for your holiday makers which are effectively your income. Hard work always pays off. I would visit area again as great value but I am sorry to say--Not at the Clube Praia Da Rocha. Seriously folks pleased be warned.

author: L6817DLlouisem
title: Worst holiday ever
text: Myself and my partner stayed here for a week mid May. We wanted a cheap and cheerful getaway in the sun for a few days but my god was it horrendous! The hotel itself was horrible, the beds are like sleeping on concrete, the pillows were as if they were stuffed with cotton balls! I read a few reviews before booking and thought maybe people were over exaggerating a little but no, they really weren’t! Some people say you get what you pay for but in this case I don’t believe that! The staff were extremely rude. They had stupid rules down by the pool, there was a lot of complaints from various other guest , I could write a book! The worst part was every morning between 9am & 9:15 am there was Work’s going on in the apartment directly underneath us, a jack hammer going all day until late that evening! Hammering, banging nailing etc! When we checked in there was no mention of these works, when we checked out there was no questions if we enjoyed or stay etc! I looked for fresh towels on day 2 to which I was told by a grumpy rude member of staff that they only change the towels every 3 days! That can’t be hygienic! I demanded fresh ones there and then so he gave me 1 lrg & 1 small! Between 2 of us that was fun sharing those! The bed sheets were never changed the whole week, the apartments were supposed to be cleaned every day but suprise suprise this didn’t happen!! We thought if everything was this bad we wouldn’t even try the food here so we never ate here!! It is safe to say I will never go back to that hotel and to be honest it would almost put me off Portugal all together!

author: Shaza0707
title: Very Very Disappointing
text: We have recently returned from Clube Praia da Rocha, and to say it was awful is an understatement it was a dump. On arrival the receptionist was not welcoming at all he gave us little information on the hotel, there was no smile or courteous in his manner. The most informative piece of information he gave us, was that we could have dinner and place out luggage in the hold cupboard as dinner was ending at 21.30 hrs. as we arrived at 19.45 hrs. The shock was when we went to our room and observed that it was very much a dormitory, there were very low twin beds, with lumpy pillows. It was a struggle to get in and out of bed, due to it being so low. In the living room area there was a sofa bed and a very old fashioned portable television, which we were not aware that you needed to hire the remote, to be able to watch the television. In addition to this you are limited to English channels as there is no cable t.v. In the kitchen area as we had an apartment you have a jug which is used as your kettle and a small electric hob. The bathroom was dirty the tiles on the walls needing cleaning, the bath was very stained. There were no towels in the room when we arrived I had to go down and request them. When I did speak to the receptionist and asked about a double room, I was told none of the rooms in the hotel had double rooms, which was very surprising especially for a hotel of this size. There was no wifi in the rooms and again there is a cost of 3 euros per day, again misleading as this is not stated clearly in the hotels description. Although this is an all inclusive hotel the food is limited and there needs to be a much more wider choice of dishes. The hotel is very dated and requires modernisation in furnishing and decor. If you require cheap this is the place to go. I will not be staying in this hotel ever again. It was our first wedding anniversary and I was REALLY, REALLY DISAPPOINTED. Try to avoid if you can,

author: clairesW8306YR
title: Really Disappointed
text: We had stayed here last year and as we knew what to expect we decided to book again. There have been a few changes since last year. The kitchen staff have all been replaced and new suppliers for the food have been sourced. The food was terrible. The choices were very limited and unless you were at the restaurant for the time of opening the food was usually cold. Last year the food was enjoyable and there was lots of options. The glass on the table tops had chunks missing and my little boy nearly cut himself on it. The worst part of the holiday was the group of students that had been allowed to book,, We were told that there were 200 students booked in on the Thursday with a further 150 booking in the following day. The last of the students checked out late on Sunday. Due to amount of students getting drunk around the pool and the chanting and music we did not feel that it was a safe place to take a three year old so ended up having to book trips away from the hotel. You also could not get to the pool bar thanks to the students congregating there - they had been given kegs of beer so had no intention of going anywhere else. We spoke to the Director of the hotel who assured us that that the university had provided security and so had the hotel, but there were not enough. On an evening they were either having round in large groups on the ground floor of the hotel block and refusing to move for anyone, or they were running up and down the fire escapes and banging the fire doors throughout the night. At 1.30 am we had them banging on our door, sitting outside the apartment shouting, singing, blowing whistles. This went on to 2 am when they went out and started up again at 5 am when they returned, The hotel had seen fit to put the students in amongst families with young children and simply told us to be patient when we were calling down to reception at 1am . We asked the University security to do something and their response was that they were trying to but no one was listening to them. On the Saturday night the hotel did let us move to a different block where there were no students staying, but we still were unable to get to the pool etc for drunks. Most of the staff at this hotel are lovely and it wasn't their decision to allow the students to stay, most of them were trying their best to help. Needless to say that we wont be returning for a third time to this hotel

author: sazzel88
title: Hit or miss
text: Came here with my partner and sister in law, for 3nights. So where do I begin, this is my second time to Praia da rocha and first to this hotel. This is a low cost hotel and if you want 5* then don’t visit there. We went self catering so can not comment on food. But our transfer driver said “your lucky you didn’t go all inclusive” entering the hotel I felt like I was stepping back in time. There was a group of college kids there about 100 of them, singing, drunk and loud. We spent all our time down the beautiful beach and used the cockroach room just to place our heads at night. If I was a family there then I would not have been happy with all these students they out ran the hotel. Do think the hotel should have warned the families. I didn’t pay for the tv or kettle As I don’t watch tv while on holiday so don’t know what channels they had. Didn’t spend much time in the hotel as it’s not the best, I would advise to blow the hotel up and start again. But like I said if you want low cost and don’t want to pay much this is the perfect place. The beach is amazing and we hire the sun beds and get service straight to us. Amazing views. Lovely weather. Was a little quiet but this is the first time we have been in may. I would go back to Praia da rocha but would not visit this hotel. This is the first time I have been to a low cost hotel and can say it will be the last.

author: 188stellap
title: good BUT
text: Have a family holiday at Clube Praia da Rocha on the 11th April to the 18th April 2018. Pros: 1. Hotel have a pool for kids which good for family member. 2. Friendly staff. 3.Closed to the bar street,restaurant, supermarket etc (5 minute walk) 4. Taxi is about average price eg. 10-12 euro Aqua shopping centre and continente supermarket 5 minute walk from Aqua, Portimao is 5-6 euro with a taxi for 6 people. We used taxi because we have 3 kids, if you walk maybe 30 minute walk. Cons 1. Everything from kettle, sunbed, wifi etc you've to paid. Note there NO WIFI IN THE ROOM. ONLY IN THE RECEPTION OR POOL AREA. DONT WASTE YOUR TIME with WIFI. 2.Its a family resort but unfortunately, there a people offer sale cannabis in the hotel and my husband offer one. There plenty outside as well. Be careful Recommend place to eat is chinese and japanese restaurant on the bar street praia da rocha centre. its worst for money and family with kids.

author: Jamiethatcher
title: CHILD ABDUCTION ATTEMPT NO SECURITY.
text: We arrived at the hotel and i will start with a plus. The hotel room was big and up to a better then average standard, the staff were good here very happy to help. bad points now. food: we tryed breakfast. was only offered eggs bacon and beans. (no sausages mushrooms or much more) food was awful and im not a fussy eater i still aet it. we then tryed dinner there was soup looked like someone had left a plate outside to collect rain water. ontop of this there was only 4 options for hot food being: chips fish meatball and rice. that is it... no variety and looked awful, we walked out. On our third night a male with and orange shirt and curly hair tryed to break into our room from the roof as we were in room 1306, top corner. he jumped in the lift. we said to ourselves we should report him. as we got downstairs we saw 3 males holding this male and a lady with marks all over her body from an attack in which this male tryed to shut her in a room and take her baby. this lady was an emotional wreck and when we said this guy tryed to break into our room the hotel said the police are coming. this is not an attack on the hotel.. BUT WHY IN A COUNTRY WHERE child abduction is so high..can anyone freely walk into this massive hotel without being checked...he would have had no wrist band on. it is very lucky that the male did not get away with the child but i feel this needs to be made public as the portugese news will not publicise child abduction attempts like the british tv will. other then this cheap place to stay close to the strip where the best place is THE IRISH ROVER great food drinks entertainment. we stayed in this place till 3am then moved on to the clubs till 7am.

author: karenhutch
title: Needs an overhaul
text: Rooms very dated,overlooking a derelict car park & very noisy over the weekend with locals rallying in their cars. Radiator hanging off wall, cracked tiles in bathroom & kitchen area. OLD 14" portable TV, which you have to pay for the remote control to watch. No lock on safe. My 2 daughters (age 16 & 11) slept on a sofa bed with a small pull out tray (suitable for 4-6 year olds!). Had to pay for the use of the sunbeds round the pool. Indoor pool was closed/derelict as they said it was too expensive to run. Food very repetitive and luke warm. Snack bar served same food twice a day everyday. Only one member of bar staff to serve over 700 guests, and only allowed 2 drinks per person in small plastic cups - expect to queue! Only beer, wine & soft drinks are served during the day. Spirits are served after 8pm. Bars close at 11pm SHARP. Reception staff not bothered about anything and just say "its normal!". On our final morning we had a cockroach in the bathroom and I took photos to show the reception staff, again - nothing was done, except our wristbands taken off so we could not eat or drink as part of the all inclusive all day ( we left at 6pm). I would not recommend this hotel.. SunMaster need to review this hotel and remove from their website!

author: drcarta59
title: You Get What You Pay For.
text: There are many reviews of this place that make out it's hell on earth and even say it's a prison, these reviews must be done by complete pansies. Yes the rooms are pretty dated and have an old 90s TV in them but who comes on holiday to sit in their room and watch TV? The rooms are spacious and the maids gave us fresh towels and made our beds daily. The food isn't great but it gets you by if you are on a budget, the only thing I was disappointed enough to complain about is the fact they wouldn't even allow us to take a sandwich out of the restaurant area to take to our son who was ill up in the room, really jobsworth staff acting like we might smuggle out a bit of bread and a slice of ham for someone without an all inclusive wrist band. Our next issue was noise, our room is situated overlooking the pool so it's pretty loud, we understand this can't be helped but getting woken up at 7/8am every morning by loud maids preparing other rooms and moving furniture isn't on. We also got woke up by drilling several times. We are on holiday and want to relax and enjoy a lay in, not be woken every morning earlier than we would back home for work. It's hard to enjoy a late night and a few drinks the night before as we know we are going to awoken the following morning by staff whether it be preparing rooms or doing repairs. The staff in general are pretty moody, but I have been to Portugal a few times and found most of the local people are pretty rude unless you are buying something from them. The location of the hotel is decent, only about 5 minutes walk from all the restaurants and beach. I am not sure what it's like in other areas but here we have been put off going to the beach as you cannot just relax without people offering you items to sell and they don't take no for an answer. Also, getting offered to buy drugs 5 times every time you walk down the strip gets annoying especially when I am walking down the street holding the hand of my 3 year old son. All in all you get what you pay for, this isn't a luxury hotel, it's dated, the staff look tired and can be quite snappy, the food isn't great. But for the price you can't complain, some reviews on here are paying £400 pound to go on holiday and expect a modern luxury hotel and act shocked when they arrive at a very basic hotel that's stuck in the 90's. I would of voted this hotel average but the early morning wake up calls made the holiday a lot less enjoyable as feeling tired all day and wanting to go to bed by 10pm really does make things a lot less enjoyable, especially when you need the energy to be running after a young child.

author: joxx1986
title: Do not be put off by reviews!!
text: Have just returned after an absolutely brilliant 7 days away at this hotel. I had read the reviews before we left and was dreading arriving at this location! We landed late and got to the hotel well after midnight, on arrival the reception staff were very friendly and very helpful, we found our room which yes is very dated but was huge!
