We intend to visit again this year outside of the summer months as we really enjoyed having all the walks to ourselves.

author: Nerakb
title: Good value, slightly slow dinner service
text: Stayed on nights of 2/3 august 2014. Stayed in room 2 with my daughter and 2 dogs. Room was large enough with a double bed and bunk beds, to put up the two dog crates. Bathroom was clean with lots of shower gel/conditioner. It overlooked the garden at the rear of the building. One single gripe. My daughter and I ate there Saturday night, booking a table for 8.30pm. We were seated at 8.30, our meal order taken ( which was simple as we both had the same items) and we waited and waited for about 40 minutes for the stater to appear. My daughter did complain and the food appeared. I will not fault the food it really was very tasty but with the wait we were too tired to enjoy it. This was the only reason we did not eat there the second night of our stay. We ate one breakfast during our stay which was a buffet help yourself with more than adequate food quality and choice. Again one single moan. The mixed toast we ordered was pretty burnt, so much so that we managed a single piece each out of about 8 pieces offered. The coffee was hot and strong, so was the tea. Please if there is going to be a delay in service please advise at the table before the client comes looking to moan at you

author: mar1942
title: Dissappointing
text: We were visiting our family who were holidaying nearby and chose The Kings Arms because it had been recommended. The owner of The Kings Arms was very keen to know what we thought of the room, which had just been refurbished and looked good. Although the shower needed updating and was also very small. The breakfast was a fiasco. We were told to move from where we were sitting because' it would be easier to manage everyone in the same area'! I refused and she set up the table which had only been half prepared. We had to ask for tea twice and when it came to the breakfast itself, there was only cereal, no fruit or even tinned fruit. The selection at the counter was dismal. Bullet proof fried eggs, cheap sausages, bacon uncooked. I asked to speak to the chef, but he was busy. He brought out scrambled eggs which he had in an old ice cream container! The toast had only looked at the toaster. To say we were disappointed is an understatement. Customer service does not exist in that establishment. Beautiful surrounds but staff and pub need to be refurbished!

author: mrtenpercent
title: Pleasant BUT!!!
text: On our arrival at our destination Otterton, Devon, the village was a pleasant surprise as we looked for The Kings Arms, our accomodation for the next three nights. On arriving at the good sized car park of the Inn we were pleased to stretch our legs after a four hour drive. On entering the Kings Arms foyer we were greeted by one of the bar staff who asked us to sign in and gave us our room key. The pub has twelve letting rooms of which some are allocated as pet friendly which is why we choose this accomodation and were able to bring our small dog who is after all part of our family and loves his holidays also. On finding our room we found it clean but plain, the bathroom was adequate with shower. The first evening we decided to have a ride out and investigate the surrounding area. After finding several lovely villages within a short drive we decided to eat out at a village called East Budleigh, at the Walter Raleigh pub also pet friendly where we had a most pleasant evening with a good food selection and a most pleasant welcoming landlord and staff, locals included. As it was our first night we decided to return to Otterton and retire a little earlier than usual after our long drive. On returning to our room approx, 10.15 pm, we realised we had neighbours, noisy neighbours. TV blasting out and them having to shout to talk over the tv. We soon realised the walls were as thin as paper as we struggled to ease into a kind of what we would have liked, a stress free night, but not until 12.45 am! The next day we found our room tv with only one station with a intermittent signal. The English breakfast was of good quality with generous portions and the waiting staff friendly. Part of the bench seating in the pub was ready for a re vamp. Although we could have dined in the evening at the Kings Arms, we were spoilt for choice with the surrounding village pubs so missed out on this treat but the evening meals we saw being served looked plentiful and tasty. On the night of the opening of The Olympics we returned to the Kings Arms hoping the large two TVs in the pub would be on and we would participate in a drink while watching this event. This was not to be ,no TVs were on. I asked one of the staff if we would be able to watch the opening of the Olympics in the bar to which she replied yes but you can`t have the sound on only the picture? We retired to our room and watched what we could on our one channel intermittent TV. As a plus the surrounding coast and villages in this area are certainly worth a visit and we found that a great deal of the cafes and shops were very pet friendly.

author: WalesHolscrazy
title: A disappointing stay
text: Found the pub on the "I know Devon" website & booked a 3 night weekend stay at the last minute. Normally I reveiw thoroughly, any place we plan to visit - this time I only managed a quick look at the pub website - the photos seemed fine so off we went. The pub describes itself as "child & dog friendly" - there were so many dogs, it appeared almost obligatory to take one, some people had 2. Our room was small but clean. uncomfortable bed, wafer thin pillows( we asked for 2 more) & the shower was a trickle, very hard to get wet. Food - breakfast was delicious & our first evening meal (fillet of cod & gammon) excellent. We had planned to spend our days touring the area,returning for a pleasant evening meal & a few drinks, however on Saturday evening at 7.45pm there was little choice left on the menu and, after waitng 45 mins we complained. We were told that most of the food had gone at lunchtime & there was a shotage of chefs ?? My husband managed a ribeye, I had pea soup & a side order of chips! On Sunday after a day out, during which we enjoyed a carvery elsewhere, we returned, hoping for a light snack around 8 or 9pm. We asked for a sandwich or baguette etc - no chance! They suggested a starter from the "specials board" - have to say that the items on the board on Frid renained unchanged on Sun, apart from those which had been removed. Pretty disgusted, we drove to a caravan site a mile away & got a snack from their shop - which says it all. We are an easygoing couple with simple needs,not given to complaining & relatively small appetites, I have left a lot unsaid, please read between the lines & don't stay here. One last point, we don't take a laptop on holiday but there is no Wifi & no mobile signals in the village or surrounding area.

author: TheYoungMonk
title: Worst hotel stay of my life. Regretting the decision.
text: This property justifies the adage "Never judge a book by its cover". I was misled into booking a studio apartment here going by the pictures put up on the website. It looked like THE dream apartment. It was my birthday eve and I thought I could enjoy in a nice big place, sitting out on the roomy balcony and having the comforts of a kitchenette etc. ALL of the above turned out to be a far-fetched dream. The property is located in the middle of a crowded street and it took a lot of time to get here (thankfully the parking lot is a secure place). Upon seeing the room, I actually thought I have reached the wrong hotel because it was NOWHERE near the photos I saw. The bed was small, bathroom was very basic, and the balcony had a view of the opposite room and corridor. The room was not cleaned properly and it was a very very basic fit out. The AC was not working (you couldnt go below 22 degrees) and I had the worst sleep of my life here. I requested the reception staff to move me to a ground floor room, as shown in the photo but they declined. Or probably they didnt understand as they were challenged to speak English. Needless to say, my stay was already looking ruined. The entire property was filled with rowdy teenagers and students who were creating ruckus till late at night. Some guys even banged violently at my door at midnight and ran away (despite me having put up a Do Not Disturb sign on the door). I was so disturbed that I cut short my stay and moved out of this place the next morning. Even when I stepped out of the hotel, the town center was a good 10-15 minutes walk (nowhere close to 2-min walk as advertised and believed by me). Really regretting the decision to stay here, and will NEVER recommend it to anyone.

author: 173keren
title: In Petite France- it in NOT.
text: it's a basic hotel. and it's 15 min walk from Little France. not 5. it' might be 5 if you are a tall adult walking very fast. We unfortunately for us were with two kids (2,4). I think calling something "little France" when it's really 5 streets away in a borderline dodgy neighborhood- is not ok. As for the hotel you get what you pay for. Basic. Our air con didn't work. we called the man from reception who told me there was nothing to do. so we were very hot. it the morning when we were checking out I told the new person at the desk the the aircon is off, and he said- well maybe you had a window open somewhere? because they don't work if the windows are open. The night man didn't know that. fun. It's not horrible, in general they were kind, the room was clean, there are some kids toys in the lobby and that's nice. BUT in petite France- it is not.

author: lakewhatcom
title: Nice apartment
text: We travel frequently for business/pleasure and generally rent private apartments. The booking process is streamlined, the rates reasonable but VERY inflated for seasonal purposes (recent Fete de Luminaire). We always recommend apartments to travelers and if you prefer a hotel type that has support services, Adagio Access is a decent choice. It is exceptionally clean-but double check the recently painted status (I had read before); our unit was and we should have moved because of the smell. I didn't ask so take responsibility. The amenities are perfectly fine, everything was in working order, the security was great but I recommend unit safes. The internet is free but slooooow. You can pay to upgrade. It is 2014 - and this is a requirement regardless of the Adagio 'Ryan Air' pay as you go approach. The reported great service was prompt, but younger staff in a group behind the desk were openly judgmental of my poor French, and us as Americans. We are older (60's) but savvy and acutely aware of Euro / American impressions. It isn't appropriate and older customer service would never consider this (even if they think it). I did write a review on the auto generated EM and promptly heard from the manager who stated she would address this. I really appreciate this as 99% of the time reviews are completed without acknowledgement. The location is great with easy walking access from the Central gare and into the City Center. Go for it and try an apartment - it makes all the difference and this is a good place to start. Strasbourg is exceptionally beautiful.

author: 288aleksandarp
title: Avoid the attic rooms!
text: Adagio Access Aparthotels are usually great, with clean rooms, excellent small kitchen and good bathroom. This was our third Adagio Access hotel and we had always reserved "standard apartment", not superior. However, Adagio Access Petite France in Strasbourg has three extra floors under the curved metal roof (sixth and seventh floor have exact the same layout of the rooms as the floors below, with 11 rooms, 8th is different, with 6 rooms). There was no Wi-Fi in the room, only in the lobby. We had a room on the 7th floor, smaller than 20m2, with angled wall and the double bed 130cm wide (we have measured it precisely with A4 paper :) )! Can you imagine how two people, one very tall and strongly built, can fit in that bed? Hardly. When you get out of bed, don't jump, because you can knock your head easily (angled wall, window which, when opened, reaches the bed). Temperature outside was about 15C during the night, but we needed only the sheets. But, if it's warm outside, room is hot like an oven. The greatest disappointment was, however, attitude of one women receptionist, who was so unpleasant and adamantly stated that our room was 20m2 and that "all the beds in the hotel are the same size, 140cm", which simply, wasn't the truth! Why act like this with the guests is beyond my understanding. We have never had such experience. To cut the long story short, avoid the "attic rooms", unless you are solo traveler and don't mind the summer heat. We are sure that other rooms (floors 1.-5.) are spacious enough with normal beds, because we know how the "standard apartment" in Adagio Access should look like.

author: alohashar
title: Comfortable surprise
text: The hotel was more than we expected. New, comfortable, spacious. It is similar to the American Extended Stay, but nicer. Good staff. We had breakfast in our room with some bananas and croissants we bought in town. Brought our coffee from home premeasured in filter and plastic bag...ready for the pot. With fridge, you can have your wine and snacks in the room before dinner and keep your bottled water cold. Petite France (10-15 mins) ok to see, but downtown Strasbourg by the Cathedral is a must (take the tram). 2 blocks away at the Ibis hotel is a very good restaurant, Courtepaille. Check their combination dinners that include beverage or dessert. Excellent quality. Location...we walked from train station...about 15-20 mins. with baggage; 10 mins. without. A bit seedy looking until we got to the hotel. From there forward, looked good. Close to tram and buses. 15 mins walk to Petite France.

author: tempt78
title: Wonderful stay
text: We had a wonderful stay at this place and booked into their apartment for 4 persons. Very clean modern room and kitchenette facilities, friendly staff, private parking at reasonable price and well situated. Not much of a view but still its in the city, we were not expecting a birds eye view form the 8th floor. We didn't have their b'fast as for what they are charging, and our normal b'fast routine, not really worth it. And since we are already booked in a room with full kitchen utensils, pots/pans, coffee maker, water boiler and a microwave oven, there is no need. Only complaint is that there is no toaster and no kitchen wipe cloth. Please beware that you need to clean the kitchen items and its countertop yourself, otherwise you'll be charged 20€. And also since the room is on the last floor (8th), it is pretty cold in the night, even with the blanket they have. Wish they would provide a thicker type of blanket for autumn/winter months? Parking is at 8€ per day and it is important to pre-book it as there is limited space available. Although you may find public parking along the road, we feel safer to park our car in their private parking. And also it seems that reception does not open on Saturday nights. Guess this is due to not having enough staff? As far as Internet connection goes, free WIFI connection in the reception area only. While in the room you'll get LAN connection, cable are provided. As this place is situated in a residential area, you'd need to walk about 15-20 minutes to get to restaurants, bar etc. There is however a couple of food delivery restaurant, pizza and Chinese food. Very quite area, good for a peaceful night sleep. Highly recommended and will stay there again the next time we go to Strasbourg.

author: Chris_8000
title: No Ritz but good Value for the money you spend
text: We stayed for two nights (4 adults, one child) and had reserved two studios. The staff at reception upon arrival was cheerful, friendly and helpful. There was enough parking in a locked compound as well as underground parking (max. height in the underground garage = 1.80 m) and at 8 Euro very reasonable. The rooms are very clean and new. The double bed was narrower than expected (140 cm), so the child sleeping with the parents was a bit of a challenge. If you are travelling with a child, make sure to reserve a triple room or apartment instead. The studios are ok for short stays but don't offer much comfort: there are only two hard plastic chairs in each room. The kitchenette with the fridge is a definite plus. TV has a vast number of French channels, several German channels but non in English or Italian. There is a free internet connection in the room (connection cord supplied) but no WiFi. The bathroom is spacious but the shower with its shower curtain is not very well made: the curtain is too thin; too long and therefore constantly sticking to places it should not. It was hard to shower without flooding the bathroom. On the plus side: The rooms are well insulated and hardly any noise penetrates. The air condition was in perfect working order and not as noisy as some. As we enjoy a good breakfast, we were a bit disappointed: there were no breakfast meats and not even a hard boiled egg in sight. Also, only white bread and only canned fruit were available. Also, the coffee pot (while upgraded to two – probably due to the customer complaints) could have been replenished more often. All in all, we had a pleasant stay and the proximity to the old town is a definitive plus. If you are looking for a place that is fairly central, quiet and reasonably price as well as clean, this is it!

author: ZedAbdn
title: Nice place but a but dissapointed
text: It was a clean hotel. Well located. Warm welcome when checking in. Great breakfast and very attentive service at breakfast. Room was clean, well provisioned and warm. Looking through the online photos of the hotel again however, none of the rooms seem to resemble the tiny tiny room I was in. I now feel that the stay was not value for money. The walls were so thin. I heard every word of the couple next door. Every word. Everything. And they both seemed to individually keep leaving the room for a few minutes to then return. At one point there were three people in there with one speaking Russian. Weird. And the toilet self flushed every five minutes. Upon check out, I was going to make them aware of the toilet and that I barely slept due to the thin walls but no one was at reception. I waited and waited. In the end I left the key on the desk and left.

author: 697gilbertj
title: Quaint and Charming, breakfast amazing!
text: Booked by our travel agent, so we had no idea. Very quaint, peaceful and clean. Front Desk lady very wonderful. Immediately felt welcome. Got us a ironing board right away. Rooms are tight but cosy. If you were tall, shower could be an issue. Great access to everything and easy to find. The best was breakfast. Wow. The restaurant is picturesque with old world charm. They even have an outside garden sitting area if it wasn’t raining. Food selection and quality was fresh and tasty! Comparing price to Canadian hotels, it’s higher. But the breakfast included with the ambience of the room made our day! Thanks.

author: Colonel-Chris
title: Great location- friendly team
text: Three is a difficult number - do you take 2 rooms or look for a family room? 3 adults though not 2 plus a child !... So I expected a pull out bed with poor mattress (Stansted Holiday Inn !) but we were shown to a beautiful suite. A huge Extra king sized double and a separate room with a single bed leading to a terrace. Ok Storm Doris was here so we didn't get out day 1 but the next day the sun was out and I had 20 mins in the sun! The rooms were beautifully decorated. Bottled water, plenty towels, kettle etc, good wifi. Only downside is the walls are thin - we could hear the people above getting in / out of bed and the guy snoring next door. Small lounge area with well stocked bar but some great bars full of life and draft beers just a few mins walk away We arrived early in a taxi from the station though at that time there were parking slots outside. very friendly welcome and help finding our meeting location. Excellent breakfast. Great location. Cathedral ruins say 5 mins and most of the central university buildings 5-10 mins walk. All the team we met were very friendly and helpful. Very close to getting an excellent but I don't give many out. One in the last 4 years and I spend 15-20% of my time in hotels. Overall I can strongly recommend this hotel . Great staff, good value (Feb) and well located.

author: laiseinm
title: Good value, for a cosy and friendly place to stay
text: I arrived in the evening and met Ellen. She was absolutely welcoming and even helped carry my large suitcase up the stairs to my room on the first level. This was indeed a great help/ relief as I was weary from having travelled the whole day from London to Edinburgh and then onward to St. Andrews. The single room I was put in was facing the front of the hotel and it was rather small. I had a difficult time opening my large luggage to retrieve and repack my things. That aside, it was cosily decorated and felt like home for the 6 nights I was there. The bathroom was also compact and there was a water pump system that made me jump when I first heard it. I was informed that this was to help the water pressure. Regardless, the water pressure at the shower was so weak that it took a long time to finish my shower daily. The sink had 2 taps, with only the water from the cold tap flowing; it'd have been good to have warm water to brush my teeth and wash my face with. The breakfast was fairly reasonable, though I found the mushrooms a little oily one day. I enjoyed the daily availability of fresh fruits, especially the grape fruit. The hotel is tucked away from the main area in town, and Market street is just a short walk down a side road. It is closer to the the St. Andrews Cathedral, the Pier and the Scores, leading to a very pleasant walk towards the Old Course and West Sands. It snowed lightly the weekend I was there, which made for wonderful photos to be taken. Overall, this hotel is definitely value for money, and I would return. A round of thanks to Ellen who was wonderful in helping me secure a taxi to Edinburgh Airport and to Paula who gave me information on the other rooms in the hotel. It's the people who make the place.

author: Bangonscot
title: Disappointing to say the least.
text: Arrived to find a small, old, dank room with a shabby lock and what seemed to be a 100 year old mattress. The first 4 things I can handle. The mattress is where I draw the line. After arriving late at night from overseas I wasn't looking to change hotels but this one wasn't going to suffice. As politely as I could, I explained to the attendant that the room was not suitable. She said they had no others available and wasn't authorized to make a decision on charges. She added that this had never happened before - hard to believe since there are at least 11 other "terrible" ratings on TripAdvisor alone. Anyway - no manager was available on location or by phone so I left my mobile number and was assured of a call back in the morning to discuss the situation. No call ever came - just an obscure charge on my CC that I will now be disputing. It's not as if I no showed and tried to get out of the room. In my opinion the quality is just extremely poor and this is just another hotel that coat tails off of its location to charge exorbitant amounts to unsuspecting visitors excited to be at the Home of Golf. I visit Scotland often so I know better. Do yourself a favor and avoid this establishment. There are so many better places to stay in and around St. Andrews.

author: floodbug
title: Wonderful small hotel & fantastic staff
text: I stayed at the Albany for 3 nights recently, on my first trip to St Andrews. I was on my own but had booked a double so I could spread out a bit. The room was 'bijou', extremely comfortable, and well-appointed with intelligently placed electrical sockets, a bugbear of mine. Check-in was quick and the staff/owners incredibly helpful. We had really high winds while I was there, but I slept like a baby and the bed was marvellous. Because of the lay-out (converted townhouse), I imagine it might get a little noisy, but I used earplugs and wasn't bothered. Breakfast was a big and very pleasant surprise: lots of choice, both cold (buffet-style) and cooked to order, and it was all good quality. The breakfast room was quite spacious for a small hotel, so you never felt as though you were being scrutinized, as can happen in some establishments. It was all very relaxed but professional at the same time. I'm not a fan of over-heated hotel rooms, and fortunately the wall heater was easily adjustable and did the job - warm (when I came in soaked), and cooler when needed. If there's a criticism, it would be the inconsistent temperature of the shower which was more drizzle than shower, but kept me clean. I really liked the toiletries. There's also a cosy little lounge with a corner bar and, at the beginning of December, a roaring log fire. This was a godsend when I came in like a drowned rat one day and couldn't find my room key at the bottom of my bag. I'd definitely stay there again. Nothing was too much trouble for the staff, and the whole feel of the place was spot on.

author: patricialC8558OB
title: Look no further!
text: I stayed at the Albany last Friday and Saturday as I was attending a wedding in St Andrews. Before extolling its many virtues, I'll get my two minor quibbles out the way:- I was checked in by a very pleasant young man who unfortunately did not ask if I needed any help with my heavy case. As my room (4) was at the top of a 35 steps spiral staircase - and I am no spring chicken - this would have been very welcome had it been offered. On checking out, the same chap checked me out efficiently and courteously, but failed to ask for my key. I didn't realise it was still in a pocket until I got home to Glasgow. Admittedly, it was ultimately MY fault, but I would have been spared the bother of having to return it had I been asked for it. A gentle reminder to the young man might be helpful. Mini moans over I must now praise the Albany for its many good points. Room 4 was very small - and is advertised as such - but more than adequate for my needs. It reminded me of a cabin in its cosiness. It was spotlessly clean, as was the shower-room. I usually find difficulty in initially using a strange shower, but this one was simplicity itself, and performed perfectly. I also liked the presence of a "real" hairdryer in a drawer, as opposed to those weak efforts attached to the bathroom wall. Much appreciated! Breakfast was excellent as was the service. I must also praise the location which is very handy for the shops etc. It was also very convenient for its proximity to the Old Course Hotel where the wedding was - taxis there and back costing less than ten pounds with tips. Most importantly, the staff (including the young man on reception) were all very helpful and friendly. I would have no hesitation in returning to the Albany Hotel in the future and highly recommend it for a very happy stay in St Andrews.

author: feebak
title: Brilliant hotel!!
text: Where to start!!! Great hotel in centre of St. Andrews- free parking outside - if you don't get a free space there are usually some pay and display ones further along north street ( £2 for 2 hours) and the free ones clear a bit after 4 so you can move your car then. We had booked the garden suite for one night as a last minute end to a lovely weekend break at kilconquhar estate. We booked direct and the staff were very helpful. The garden suite is massive!!! A large L shaped room with 2 singles and a king size bed- the singles are made private by two opaque glass doors. There are two settees in the main part of the room with the king size bed and there's still loads of space!!! Two large bow windows look out onto the terraced garden and a door leads up a couple of steps to a large terrace with tables and chairs ( cushions for which are provided in the room). Wesat outside for a couple of hours in the sun ( I know - in OCTOBER ) it was lovely!!! As mentioned before there is a lovely lounge with small bar ( bottled beers and spirits etc). The gentleman who owns/ runs it is charming and the breakfast was fantastic! Loads of choice from continental to full blown traditional cooked breakfast ( including tattie scones) made with good quality ingredients- you won't need lunch!!! The staff are all friendly and helpful- hope to go back again soon!!! Some reviews state they felt it was expensive- but I doubt you can get a hotel room of this size,with breakfast, much cheaper elsewhere in St andrews( <£50 a head)!

author: 692kennyh
title: Not the best and be sure to avoid Room 11!!!
text: We stayed one night while visiting St Andrews and will be back soon but won't be staying here. Greeting on arrival was good and hotel generally looks ok. Unfortunately we were put in a room downstairs which was very, very poor in so many ways. It's called a small double but even that is misleading. You feel like you're in a dungeon room. Room temperature either sauna or a fridge. Bed soft and you will trip over the lone chair trying to get into the toilet!! Shower was terrible. All these things are poor but worst of all was the noise from every angle. The noise of footsteps from above, the stairs outside, the staff arriving etc etc was incredible and it started at 6am and never abated. I am a very sound sleeper but there is no chance of sleeping past dawn in that room. This room should not be used for paying guests. The rest of the rooms may be ok, I don't know, so I will not make an overall judgement. Service was pleasant at all times and breakfast was ok. I was disappointed that when I was leaving and handed in my key the reception staff didn't ask me about my stay. If they had bothered to look up and ask I wouldn't have bothered with this review.

author: AlisonH2522
title: Upgrade your plumbing
text: My husband and I stayed at the Albany for 5 nights the third week in June. I wanted to give a better rating as we liked the location, handy for everything, and the breakfast was good, waitresses very friendly. However, the very minimum I expect of a 3 star hotel, especially one that charges £140 a night, is a good bed and a decent shower. The Albany failed on both these requirements. The bed was uncomfortable and the springs were noisy. It took me 4 days to work out how to get the trickle of water that came out of the inner circle of the shower to a temperature that my body could cope with. We felt we were fobbed off when we spoke to reception staff about this. They know this room (no 18) is sub standard and don't want to get involved. The toilet has a sani-flow unit which is very noisy and churns all the time water is running in the basin and the shower. The room itself was fine, clean but a bit tired. Old cream curtains let in full daylight at 4.30am. I probably would not have given a poor review if we had only stayed one night but 5 days was just too long to cope with the shower. I found myself panicking about how I would wash my hair and ended up hanging over the bath and using cold water to avoid scalding my scalp. From reading other reviews, most of the other rooms must be of a much higher standard. A bit of investment is required in room 18 to make it worth it's high price tag.

author: BarryRD
title: Spoiled Weekend
text: My family and I decided to spend the weekend in st Andrews, and after a great stay last year we decided to stay at the Albany Hotel again. I wish we'd tried somewhere else. It all started off well: pleasant and fast check-in, the room was clean and the beds were comfortable. Things started to go wrong around 2.30 in the morning for at least the next 90 minutes. My young children and I were woken up by a lads party returning from a night out, who were not really considering their neighbours. Now I understand the management can't have much control over their guests, but why they would place a family next door to a group of lads does escape me. I tried on a couple of occasions to call the night reception but it kept ringing out. So with no other option I had to speak to the group myself. Not impressed on having to do it but the kids were quite upset. Despite the lack of sleep the kids were up at 7am so plenty of time for breakfast. This too started off well but the scrambled eggs with the smoked salmon was so cooked it could have bounced off the floor. Despite the majority of my breakfast left I was only asked if my plate could be taken away. There was no query of something was wrong, which there obviously was. Check out was quick, but again no query about the stay. It seems when all goes well in this hotel the staff are great. However, there seems to be as lack of ability of dealing with problems: either through avoiding the issue or not noticing. This is a nice little hotel that could be great.

author: nigel_duthie
title: Late Booking Success ... But Don't Mention The Seagulls
text: I booked this hotel only a few days before my wife's birthday - the price and location were the attraction. Despite living locally, we'd never noticed the place on previous visits to St Andrews, and almost drove past it. Parking was a little difficult initially (Saturday afternoon when the weather is nice, not unexpected), but we eventually got a free place directly across the road. We received a very nice welcome from the charming receptionist, and we had a double room on the ground floor. The room itself was fine, very clean and with a comfy bed, good TV and a nice view out the back. The only disappointment was the en-suite which was effectively just a partitioned area of the room. the shower made gurgling noises for quite a lot of the time we were in the room, but nothing in comparison to the seagulls ... After a lovely evening wandering round the town, we enjoyed a nightcap in the small lounge where we had a nice chat with another couple, regular stayers by the sound of it. My wife is a light sleeper at the best of times, but even I was woken by the seabirds who started at the crack of dawn and kept going until it was nearly time to get up. Obviously nothing the hotel can do about that, it's a hazard of staying at a seaside town, but it did mean that we were a bit less than bright and breezy when we went down for breakfast. As noted by other reviewers, the breakfast was outstanding. The male and female serving us were very busy as every table was taken, but their service was impeccable, attentive to your every request. The food itself (traditional cooked breakfast) was fantastic, as was the coffee. Nowadays, you're often charged extra for breakfast and it's not worth the money, but the Albany came up trumps ! Just a pity it's a relatively early meal time (7.15 to 9.15 on a Sunday), but probably due to the early check-out time (10). Which in turn is probably due to the early check-in time (1). How about slipping everything by an hour at the weekend ? We thoroughly enjoyed our stay in St Andrews and felt the amount we paid was a fair price for the experience. We'd definitely come back, but hopefully to a slightly better room and when the seagulls are hibernating !!!!!!!!!!!

author: CindyR3325
title: We will be back
text: LOVED The Albany Hotel. The Staff, Sean, the manager, Sophie, Johanna, Katie, Liz, Rose and Rick the chef, and the housekeeping staff are the ones that make The Albany Hotel the wonderful place it is. They make each and every visitor feel like royalty. The rooms are small but quaint. Breakfast is outstanding. Everything is fresh and most mornings you can find Sean waiting on tables or busing tables right along side Liz and Rose. The rooms and the entire property are always spotlessly clean. The lounge is quaint and a great place to read, have evening cocktails and visit with everyone staying in the hotel. Our last night in St. Andrews, Cecilia the owner had cocktails with everyone. In all our travels we have never had an owner and a staff make us feel the way we were made to feel at The Albany Hotel. The location is perfect. Most of our group were golfers. They had no problems getting to courses to play. For the sightseers and shoppers in our group most everything was within walking distance or the busstop was right across the street. I look forward to our return trip to stay at The Albany House.

author: t10bosma
title: Nice and friendly admosphere
text: I just wanted to post a respond on this review, as there are so many negative stories about the hotel. Of course it is not the luxury of a standard hotel like Ramada and no mini-bar (oh the drama.), but it has so much more character. It is just a very small traditional hotel you would expect in the neighbourhood of such a friendly little, but famous village as St Andrews. When we came in there was a small cosy living room just near the reception. There was a nice fireplace with warm fire where you could sit and have a nice drink. The hotel staff was more than friendly to us, and the breakfast was great. The room we had was on the street side and you would expect a lot of noise, but in fact it was very quiet, we slept with the window open. The rooms were clean and fine. Very much Scottish traditional decorated. Small but comfortable. Although I can imagine that the beds would be too small and uncomfortable for bigger people and people with back problems. All the basics were there. The only thing what I can think of for criticism is that because the walls of the rooms are very thin, that this could cause a lot of trouble, but that would be just bad luck. Location is perfect, not in the busiest part of the street, close to the beaches and town centre. Definitely recommend it for couples!!

author: Sarah2018S
title: Great to stay and see Dubrovnik
text: A lovely guest house you are actually being welcomed into Toni' s family home. Self contained studio we had with en suite and kitchen facilities. Rooms were cleaned every day and towels changed when you want. Fab air conditioning. Buffet breakfast served every morning from 8. Pool and grounds were fantasic and very well kept. You would often see Tonis relatives watering the garden and the little ginger cat walk by. There is a vending machine for drinks and a toilet near the pool. All staff are friendly and helpful if you need anything. I went with my 16 and 13 year old and they went for late night swims where the pool was lit up. One night we had a treat of a real croatian family meal...well worth the money (250kn each) for starter, main pudding and carafs of wine did not stop...a fab night. Its in thebport of Gruz. Lapad is a 20min walk away and Old town prob 30 mins on foot. I would recommend this accomodation. Thank you to all the staff at the Bokun!

author: jessdbromley
title: Perfection!!!
text: We have just returned from an 11 night stay at Bokun Guesthouse with Jet2 Holidays. We have always gone for big & luxurious hotels on previous holidays but this year we fancied something different - when I saw the pictures of Bokun on Jet 2, I instantly fell in love and when I arrived here, it did not disappoint! We were greeted by Toni as soon as we got off our coach who helped us with our cases and invited us for a free welcome beer whilst having a chat about all the vital information we needed to know about Dubrovnik. He made us feel right at ease straight away! We are not the type of couple who tends to mix with other people & instead like to keep ourselves to ourselves and we found that we were able to do that at Bokun despite it being a small Guesthouse. However, if mixing with other people is your thing then Bokun is perfect for that too! We had a double room and it was fabulous. No, it's not huge but why do you need a huge room? It was the cleanest room I've ever come across in all my times of staying in hotels etc and the air con was also probably the best I've encountered on a holiday. What's more is that the Guesthouse is secured with a large iron gate that is locked (each guest has a key to gain access in and out) so all your belongings are more than safe in the room. I thought the room was just stunning - there have been reviews on here which have been negative towards the room but personally I thought it was beautiful - the exposed brick work especially! We are very active walkers and spent a lot of the holiday exploring and walking miles each day. However, we did not walk into the old town as it was a very steep hill and too hot for that so we caught the bus there and back each time we went (12kn per person) and they were very reliable. I've got to say, I was a little reluctant to staying in such a small Guesthouse at first but Bokun, you have completely changed my perspective on small and friendly hotels - i don't think I could return to a large hotel again after my stay here. If you have booked a stay at Bokun then you are in for a real treat. Thank you Toni and Christina for making our holiday the best holiday we've had so far. Perfection!!

author: Sipoges
title: A faultless stay in Dubrovs thanks to Bokun guesthouse!
text: Sipoges were lucky enough to stumble upon the Bokun guesthouse on booking.com whilst planning their Croatian adventure. Dubrovnik was our first stop and we arrived at this little beauty around midday. We regretted declining the offer from Tony of the 200kn ride from the airport to the guesthouse as a taxi cost us 300kn :( but Sipoges live and learn and we would encourage other travellers not to make our foolish mistake of declining this stunning offer! Upon our arrival we were greeted by Tony, the man of the guesthouse. Straightaway we knew that we were in the right place! Sip can be quite anxious and he began asking about payment but Tony rightly told him to relax and just enjoy our stay :). Our room was perfect - great size and it reminded Sipoges of a little cave due to the stone walls and blue lights. We miss the cave! :( We headed straight for the pool area for a nice cold beer from the vending machine. We had some vending machine chaos and Sip beer got stuck but on of the guesthouse owners quickly came to our rescue to retrieve the beer and clean up the mess we had made. Breakfast was a real treat - continental style (which Sipoges don't usually go for) but the fresh bread, cold meats and cheeses and selection of spreads really set us up for the day! There was even enough for Sipoges to take a couple of spreads back to our room ;). Location was fantastic and Sipoges enjoyed walking the 20minute journey to the old town every day. The guesthouse is also only about 5 minute walk from the ferry which was very handy for our Onward journey to Hvar. Sipoges would like to thank Tony and family for our stay and we would definately love to return!

author: sharlancashire
title: Dubrovnik's special hideaway
text: Visited with my partner for 7 nights. What a fantastic guesthouse 2 minutes from the harbour. But you would never have guessed with the location. It was so peaceful and had lovely grounds. Toni was great. He was very friendly, knowledgable and helpful. He arranged 2 trips to Montenegro and Elafite islands and couldn't do enough to make our stay memorable. His family and the staff were great too. Friendly and helpful who work really hard. The breakfast was yummy :- freshly picked fruit from the garden, bread, fruit juice, yogurt, ham, cheese, pastries, boiled eggs and tea. The room was bright with a very comfy bed and the bathroom was extremely clean with a powerful shower. Twenty five minutes walk to the old town but 5 mins on the bus. Toni recommended 2 restaurants, peppers and otto. Make sure you reserve a table at peppers as it's very popular and would recommend the tuna steak which was tasty. Dubrovnik old town is stunning. It's like going back in time and you must take a guided tour and walk the walls also. Overall the food everywhere is delicious and the people are extremely respectful which made our holiday a fantastic experience. Thank you Toni and all.

author: Littlebex
title: Amazing, beautiful, relaxing!!!
text: I cannot recommend this place enough! Toni runs a beautiful guesthouse! He and his family make you feel so welcome.... The rooms are spotless and comfortable.... If you're looking for a huge room then this isn't for you - but with the lovely terrace and pool area I can guarantee you won't spend too much time in your room! On the day we left he was getting sky installed which might appeal to some people! The gardens in the guesthouse are stunning! Lots of fruit trees and other beautiful plants lovingly tended by Toni's parents... And the pool area is large and definitely needed on those hot Croatian days! In terms of the location we loved it! The old town is a short walk or bus ride away. In the local vicinity are some great restaurants, I can recommend peppers, amphora or ottos nearby... Slightly further in Lepad is restaurant Lepad which serves great food too!! The way the guesthouse is run and set up means you get to meet fellow travellers on the terrace and round the pool so you can share ideas for adventures and places to eat... Seriously - you should book this place and you will not be disappointed... We can't thank Toni enough for making our stay so good.. His knowledge of the local area and its history as well as that of Croatia in general means you'll get a lot more out of a visit than you would staying in a large hotel that will lack the personality of the Bokun guesthouse..

author: sunnypdx
title: Not my favorite place to stay
text: Based on the other reviewers I must have had a one off experience. The room itself was ok. It was fairly clean, although the shared bathroom shower did not drain and was therefore always dirty. The location is very close to the bus station, and a pleasant 20 minute walk to the downtown area, which is the location I preferred. The host was quite condescending and rude though. I let him know what time I was arriving, which was midnight. In his email, he sounded friendly and stated it was no problem- he would leave the front gate unlocked and I could knock on the door. The gate was not unlocked, and no one answered the bell. I finally called him on my cell (international call), and he came to the gate extremely annoyed. I thought it was just a one off, since it was late. In the morning he was friendly, but just hours later, he completely ignored me when I had a question. The following morning I got a tirade for asking if I could still order breakfast. I left after two days, as I did not want want to deal with his behavior anymore, so I left. I really did not ask many questions or favors and kept to myself, so I was surprised at his behavior. I cannot recommend this place.

author: SamGorchuk
title: Average budget accomodation
text: Bokun is considered a Sobe in Croatia. This means you get a room and typically not a breakfast. The room we had was small. The rooms could use a good scrubbing. The shaded garden terrace was nice to sit in during the heat of the day. It is located in the middle of Dubrovnik but, in Dubrovnik the sights are at the edge of the city; ie the old city and the beaches. There is a bus stop close by which provides good local transportation to other areas of Dubrovnik. It is close to the bus terminal if you are arriving by bus from Split. If I were to go to Dubrovnik again I would stay closer to the old city or to one of the beach areas, ie Lapad. Toni was very helpful.Bokun is considered a Sobe in Croatia. This means you get a room and typically not a breakfast. The room we had was small. The rooms could use a good scrubbing. The shaded garden terrace was nice to sit in during the heat of the day. It is located in the middle of Dubrovnik but, in Dubrovnik the sights are at the edge of the city; ie the old city and the beaches. There is a bus stop close by which provides good local transportation to other areas of Dubrovnik. It is close to the bus terminal if you are arriving by bus from Split. If I were to go to Dubrovnik again I would stay closer to the old city or to one of the beach areas, ie Lapad. Toni was very helpful.

author: krazylegs
title: Charming guesthouse within reach of so much
text: This is a lovely family house (the family still live there), set back from the harbour, which has been converted into guest rooms and apartments. The family have a baby, a toddler (whom I saw very little of) and very placid labrador. We were travelling with our toddler so the baby-swing and toys in the beautiful, peaceful garden were a handy addition! Tony's homemade wine and liquers are worth a try on a relaxing evening on the terrace. We stayed there twice in two weeks. Initially for three nights and then for five nights (we visited Bosnia and Montenegro by car). The apartment we stayed in was clean, adequately decorated and air-con'd but we lived in the lovely garden. Tony was generally helpful but the was a misunderstanding over a double-booked cot... he ultimately came up with the goods and continued to be very hospitable. The old town is unmissable (a cheap 5 minute bus ride). A walk around the city walls is a must (recommend you don't do it in the heat of the day). The Buza bar at sunset is blissful. A boat from the old town to the island of Lokrum is lovely. Our fave thing was the tranquil Island of Lopud. Car free and a 25 minute stroll to a quiet sandy beach. The guesthouse is right next to the harbour and the handy Jadrolina ferry.

author: TerryAReviewer
title: Pretty Good - Let's improve a couple things in the bathroom!
text: Hampton Inn - generally one of my favorite budget weekend stay hotels. Usually my first choice if the price is equal. This is my first stay in this Hampton. All of the usual great things about the Hampton were as expected: Room Size - Enormous Plenty of seating, desk, storage, Fridge, Microwave Excellent, Extremely friendly staff Carpet Looks dirty Heater/AC moderate noise - digital temp, cycles on and off as needed No tablet at the desk Bathroom: Terrible odor in the bathroom upon entry of the room. Musty, I suppose. Ventilation inadequate. Can you upgrade the fan? Can you add a heater? While the room was warm, the bathroom was very cool. Tub Shower: Water temperature was only adequately hot. Bathtub looked dirty. How about a hand sprayer as the next investment? Water Pressure was very good?. Bow out shower curtain. Plenty of shelf space in the shower tub. Your designer went off the rails with the faucet that comes out of the wall - it is ugly and I had to make a lot of effort not to spit on it when I was brushing my teeth! Breakfast: As expected for this hotel type. Well stocked. Plenty of seating. Room 228 Quiet

author: RedThunder99
title: Disappointing front desk judgement call!
text: Veronica was the service desk's name representing the business and general manager! A box of cereal (small to go type of box) was requested during checking in and she responded with.... I'm uncomfortable with that, I would need to ask my manager for permission! She made the judgement call to spare one to me. Her response was an embarrassment! Folks, its not Pilet Mignon! For the customers who are gold or diamond members or really...any paying customers!.... that sure reflects on us as customers no matter the amount of money spent on Hilton! I have spent between 15-22K dollars per year on Hilton for business related travels. THE CUSTOMER WHO WROTE A REVIEW IN REGARDS THAT THE CUSTOMERS ARE RIGHT.....IS CORRECT (read his review below) AND CORPORATIONS AND MANAGEMENT NEEDS TO BE REMINDED THAT THEY DID NOT GET THERE WITHOUT US CUSTOMERS! REMEMBER YOU ARE SUBJECT TO CONSUMER AFFAIRS. Change your way of business practice. Some of the best customer service I have encountered with for Hilton- Hampton is in Ukiah and Arcata, CA. General Managers ask how they treat their customers! They are Great!

author: Garrison98370
title: A Poor First Impression Followed By.....
text: All it takes is for one employee to ruin your stay right? That's what happened when my wife and I checked into this hotel last week. As a 6 time Diamond member and now a Gold member of Hiltons Honors program, I have stayed and am very familiar with Hilton properties and service all over the world. This was going to be a short overnight stay for a road trip between Seattle and LA. Arrived at 9:45 PM and the lobby was empty except for two desk clerks. I stood there in front of them while they worked away on their computers without any "welcome" greeting and so then wandered about the lobby for a bit and then came back. Finally I said "can you please check me in? Its been a long day". It seems that Veronica was training the other and they were too busy and wanted me to wait. After telling her that guests and customers should come first she explained to me that that was my opinion and got argumentative with me. There was no offer of water bottles or any of the Honors perks that one comes to expect. I was embarrassed and disappointed and after finally getting my room key we settled in and experienced what we have come to expect with Hilton properties. Clean and well maintained rooms in a comfortable atmosphere. Breakfast and check out were fine in the morning and I asked if the GM was available to let them know of what happened. She was not so I called later that afternoon to the GM Bhavini [-] and left a message asking her to call me back. She did not call me back so I have to conclude that this hotel is not interested in good customer service and I will take this property off my list.

author: Markpicc
title: Ok visit - ok service
text: As a precursor- I’m a Diamond member - and obviously stay very frequently at Hilton Properties. This place was convenient to Sacramento international airport and close to downtown Woodland. Incidentally, downtown Woodland has some good eateries. We arrived around noon on a Wednesday from a cross country flight and of course our room wasn’t ready. It wouldn’t be ready for 3 hours...per “policy”... weak. Rooms were ok. Bathrooms were ok. Water pressure good. Towels poor quality and old. Bedding was very comfortable. Air conditioning worked pretty well. Front desk staff not incredibly helpful. Pool was out of service. It was 100 degrees. Nice to know when booking? Breakfast, average. Overall, nothing to write home about. Grade = C

author: J1775BMgaryc
title: Convenient to Sacramento Airport
text: Spent one night in order to catch a flight out of SMF. The hotel is only an easy 10 minute drive to the airport and cheaper than Sacramento Hampton’s. Positive: Room was ready at check inn. Clean and serviced. New decor was tasteful. Room darkening window shades helped muffle the sound of the freeway. Shower was hot and water pressure good. Negatives: Hotel right on the freeway off ramp. Half the rooms were under renovation on the floor we were staying. This could’ve been a major problem staying over several days. Not all accessory outlets (USB) were hooked up and live. In room iron was broken. Bathroom sink slow to drain. Bed mattress was thin and uncomfortable. Only one slow elevator. Did save $50 from a Hampton room in Natomas. Not sure it was worth it.

author: NorCal4169
title: Some good, some not so good.
text: We had to pick up a family member in nearby Davis, Ca and decided to check out Woodland. We have stayed at another Hampton Inn closer to home and liked it a lot. This one was one notch lower. First the good things. The location is good. It's close to some good chain store shopping and eating. It's not far from the fun downtown area of Woodland, probably a 5-10 minute drive depending on traffic. We were pleasantly surprised by the great stores and restaurants downtown. The king room we had was a good size and value and the all the staff we encountered were pleasant. The free breakfast was just average and better than a continental breakfast. Now for some downsides. The carpets were really dirty and stained in spots. Both inside the rooms and in the hallways. The walls looked liked they had many spots that were damaged or had wall paper separating from the walls. The pool area seemed a lot older than the hotel. The tile work had seen better days and the hot tub was really small and dirty. The also ran out of towels that night and the previous night according to another guest at the pool. Overall the hotel is pretty decent and if the price was better than other hotels nearby, I would stay there again. It just seemed like they had been cutting a few corners on cleaning and upkeep.

author: terrysO5716SB
title: Going Downhill
text: Please Note: This feedback is NOT to receive any comps or any points, but wanted to share my experience. In regards to our Independence Weekend Holiday Stay at the Woodland location: -Front desk acknowledged us as gold members only towards the end of check-in. I felt as if she did not believe we were actually Terry and Cher checking in. Unsure if there was anything wrong, but she checked both of our I.D.'s and credit cards. -We requested extra washcloths and towels...Did not receive. When asking the front desk for washcloths, the gentleman working there continuously brought out the wrong item. It was almost as if he was pretending not to know what washcloths/facecloths were. After 10 minutes we were advised there were no clean/spare washcloths in the entire hotel. -We requested laundry service and turned in a shirt to be laundered on Sunday, July 2nd. The shirt was held for 24hrs before being notified that the laundry service would not be available for the next 5 days. Unfortunately, many of the Hampton Inns and Garden Inns across the United States have gone downhill in level of service. The following are my observations: 1. The decor is becoming "worn around the edges"...Carpeting, bedskirt and furniture tends to be stained. 2. More frequency of strange hair being found in the bath towels. The bathroom wallpaper is dirty-looking.

author: G6297PBdavel
title: The problem is management not the peopke
text: I paid for three rooms, 2 queen beds, 1 king bed. We could not get in early because rooms were not cleaned. I understand, but I left my card and paid for all rooms. We had wedding to go to and needed to be there at 4pm. My son arrived and he had got his room. When he returned his wife and children sat outside the room siting on the floor while he tried to talk w/ the front desk. they said the card was not accepted. Before I left I made sure all rooms were paid and my card was accepted. I was told late that night after returning to the hotel, that the day staff did not save the information!?? So my son and his wife with children, was demoralized for a mistake that your policies not your employees made. Until you let the employess that you hired,'make decessions for the customers you will continue loosing good paying individuals. Change your policies. don't hold your employees accountable for making decisions when they see an injustice and a simplistic decision is to allow them to speak for the management. they see the injustice and they can not make the right call because they fear you will fire them. Shame on you for putting them in that position.

author: Maryannestravel
title: Great Place To Stay
text: This last stay was my third, and once again it was a lovely stay. Of the Hampton Inns that I have stayed at, this particular property is the most consistently excellent in all aspects. We arrived late in the evening and had checked in electronically. (I am always a little worried with late check-ins, having walked into lobbies with unoccupied front desks or, in some cases, told that the hotel was sold out and walked to a nearby property.) Upon entering the lobby, a polite gentleman promptly provided us our keys and made the quick transaction pleasant (appreciated after a long drive and a late night). We were concerned with the parking as the lot seemed full, but there was an available stall that was large enough to accomodate our full size pickup truck. It was very nice to see that the lot had a security guard patrolling the property as well. Our room was clean, the beds comfortable and the bathroom large and well appointed with plenty of towels and all the necessities. It was quiet and we slept well, which was appreciated as we had a long drive ahead of us the following day. We have come to accept that complimentary breakfasts are usually lacklusture at these genres of hotels but this property had a well stocked breakfast that was tasty, hot and provided variety. We happened to arrive in the dining area with just 15 minutes to spare before the breakfast was closing and thought that it would be sparse and the food cold, but not so at all! Again, we appreciated the thoughfulness of the hotel to provide quality right up to the end of breakfast service. The staff in the dining room were professional, friendly and helpful! Checkout was easy and took less than a minute. The gentleman at the front desk was friendly and very professional. This is becoming our "go-to" property when travelling through the Woodland area and we look forward to our next stay.

author: RokLov
title: Nice Place in a Small City
text: Having stayed at other hotels of this chain, I expected an above average experience, and was not disappointed. Check-in was easy and efficient. Connie, the Front Desk person was also friendly and very helpful. At check-in, I was given a 15% discount card for the best restaurant in town. The lobby is comfortable, well lighted, and airy. I liked it. The bathroom was neat and clean, and the amenities were above average. The towel supply was more than ample. The Fitness Room was a little on the weak side. Just two machines, treadmill & eliptical, and a 65 CM Fitness Ball. The good news is that both machines worked. The bad news is that there was nothing for Abs, Arms, Chest, or Shoulders. A really outstanding point, is the free breakfast. A nice variety, to include bacon, omelets, 6 different types of cereal, waffles, juice, hard boiled eggs, coffee, and more. The food is nicely prepared, hot, not greasy, and tasty. The dining room is well laid out, clean, and airy. If you are in a hurry, the front desk has 'to go' bags. I rate it as one of the top two hotels in the city.

author: km_thompson78
title: Decent place close to the airport
text: Booked this hotel as we needed someplace close to the airport and usually stay at Hampton in the Bay Area. We got a 2-queen room. The price was a bit higher than we pay for the same room near the Oakland Airport location. This room was slightly larger, however, with a small sitting room, and kitchenette. A little dated, and my sheets were either dirty or stained on one corner, but okay. Proximity to the airport was ideal - only about a 15 minute drive. Our biggest complaint - we arrived in the evening as planned, around 8pm. Upon check in the receptionist told my husband she had been trying to get ahold of us and that we "almost didn't have a room." Apparently they only hold the room until 4pm and, "lucky for us", it was a slow week. Nice. Most places you can't even check in until 4! She said if we'd had a credit card on file it wouldn't be a big deal. Ummm...okay. I made the reservation through our Hampton Inn account which keeps all of our information on file, including the credit card. I spoke to the receptionist myself and explained how I had booked. Apparently they have been having trouble with their reservation system for "over a year" so she wasn't surprised. Maybe it's time to get that fixed? Also had trouble with our room keys not working. Receptionist stated they have been having trouble with those, too.

author: Stuffinmama
title: Good for a one-night stop over
text: After touring Sacramento, my adult daughter and I spent one night at the Hampton Inn & Suites in Woodland. We chose this location because we have friends who are living in Woodland. The location is very good, there are convenient stores and restaurants in the vicinity such as Target and Starbucks. The room was clean and well appointed. The feature I appreciated the most was the comfortable chair and ottoman. So often in hotel rooms you end up sitting on the bed, and can never get comfortable. So for me the chair was a welcome surprise. A lap desk was also provided - nice touch. There was a wide selection of channels available on television. The A/C worked well and there was ice available on our floor. The wi-fi worked well, and the desk chair was comfortable. It would have been convenient to have had more outlets available in the desk area. Lastly, the breakfast. It was not especially tasty. There was some sort of quiche-tart egg selection and what appeared to be French toast sticks, as well as a waffle iron. The service area itself had several items that needed refilling such as silverware, the oatmeal, bagels. Perhaps we had just arrived after a large group. It would also have been nice to have had a breakfast meat of some type. Lastly, as I review other hotels in chains such as the Hampton Inn, I continue to suggest that complimentary bottles of water upon arrival, especially in hot climates, would be most inviting.

author: Tobys_view
title: Soft Toilet paper
text: Hampton Inn For context purposes I need to indicate that I spent a week (Nov 2-10) in California travelling around the San Francisco area. During this week I stayed in 4 different hotels/chains. As a result, some of my comment will be in comparison to the other three hotels (which I have not named in this review). I arrived late evening; however the reception staff member was very curious and efficient. Everything was ready and waiting for me to arrive. The process went quickly. Like the other three hotels, I stayed in a room with a king bed. This one did not face any traffic so I did not hear any traffic noise. Unfortunately, I could hear every movement of the person on the floor directly above me. I couldn’t get to sleep until 1am as a result. The room was clean and spacious. The bed was firm, but soft enough to be relaxing. It also had the most comfortable sheet and duvet. In addition, this hotel had the softest toilet paper of the four. The continental breakfast was what I was expecting, simple but ok. There were both hot and cold items. The staff member was very friendly and kept everything well stocked. All in all, it is a nice hotel and I’d stay there again. For the price and the quality, it was a good value.

author: Maryannestravel
title: Very Nice Stay
text: This property is typical of a Hampton Inn and exactly what you would expect from the brand. The room was very clean, the bed comfortable and the sheets were exsquisite! They were probably the softest sheets I have ever experienced in a hotel of this genre. It was quiet and very easy to access from highway. I was in room 109, which is located right next to what I think was a water pump room and there was constant white noise. This is not a detriment in my opinion as it sounded just like one of those noise machines that some hotels put in their room to mask ambient noise. I actually liked it, but if you are one of those people who need absolute quiet you may not want this room. Another point to note is that the water pressure is a bit odd as it alternates from a decent normal pressure to a "hold on to your hats & glasses" uber pressure. Again it didn't bother me at all once I got used to it as the water tempuratures maintained, it was just something unexpected. The staff was courteous and efficient, although they were not as overly friendly as I have seen at other Hampton Inn properties. They got the job done, which works fine for me. The breakfast was your typical "breakfast included" faire and everything was clean and well stocked. I do want to emphasize that the housekeeping staff was outstanding! They were quiet, efficient and the room was sparkling clean each day of my stay. Very impressive! Overall this is a great property if you are in the area - I would definitely stay here if business brings me back to Woodland.

author: norcalhummingbirds
title: Reliable and clean
text: We were heading north to visit family. It was getting late and I found this hotel in a TA search. I called ahead and the friendly gentleman on the phone saved us a room. The hotel is easy to find, just north of the airport and south of the 20 connection. Our room was spacious and clean. It had a convenient coffee bar. They have a nicely stocked mini-mart in the lobby. I like the electrical outlets right on the bedside tables. Don't have to climb under the bed to charge phones etc. Nice big tub, but the shower head is so high up I couldn't reach it even standing on the edge of the tub! The pillows were soft and the bed very comfortable. Our AC, heater was quiet. We too had trouble with the wifi, very slow. But I've seen worse! We had the breakfast, waffles, bagels, fruit etc. I suggest they serve some eggs without ham. Coffee was good. It is a good place to spend a restful night.

author: tglink97
title: We'll be back!
text: Our family stayed for the week and our stay here at the Hampton Inn was excellent. We know where to stay when we come back. We were lucky to have Ricardo, who was especially helpful through our entire stay. We checked in early from our trip and he immediately helped us. He answered all of our questions about the local community and was friendly through and through. Ray was also helpful and friendly. Our room was nicely clean and we couldn't find any faults with it. They have an outdoor pool and jacuzzi. The pool at the time wasn't heated, but we didn't care. They had an array of Hot & Cold breakfast items, which changed everyday. Hot chocolate, Hot water, Coffee available all night long. Cookies served in afternoons. The cleaning staff was very respectful and cleaned our rooms when we requested. They also provided us with extra towels and forgotten items without any hassles. Overall, we'll consider coming back and consider Hampton Inn for future travels elsewhere. Thankyou for a wonderful stay. :)

author: Tre_Landrum
title: Good stay
text: We only got one night here, and not much of that. The price the quoted on the phone was about $30 cheaper than listed on their web page. It took this place from a nice place, but more than we really wanted to pay, to a great room at a great price. The beds were very comfortable, and the TV was a nice flat panel. My wife was disappointed we couldn't stay one more night so we would have time to watch a move in our hotel room. The front desk was very helpful. I had a business internet meeting I had to take at 1, but check in was not till 3, and when I called at noon our room was not ready. I told them I need a private place to take an internet meeting and they said they had a business area. When I got there at 5 till 1 they had my room cleaned, and key ready with the internet password written on the back of the key envelope. They gave me the option of taking call in my room or the business office. My room worked out perfect. The comforter on the bed was lumpy. I am really not sure if this was a design feature, or a result of them washing the comforter. I am going with the latter option; I like to use any excuse to think the comforters get washed in a hotel. Either way it was on top and really didn't matter. In the end a very nice room at a great price.

author: Ruddstar
title: Beautiful Figeac
text: Hi Folks, If you find the review of help, please click the helpful green tab at the end. THANKS. My Wife and I stayed here on Saturday 13th June, for one night only. The fee was 90 euros, without breakfast. We enjoyed a lovely drive down from Saumur, mainly on D roads. We found the hotel with ease and parked for free, in the hotels car park, some 20 meters down the road, opposite reception, on the other side of the road. All staff that we encountered, spoke really good English and on arriving, were allocated room 113. Everything was clean and tidy, everything worked just fine. There were tea/coffee making facilities and most important of all, the a/c was brilliant. Unfortunately, we did not have a river view, but for 90 euros, we felt it was a good deal. The hotel also has a lovely snug bar, which we both thought looked very English looking. The restaurant terrace looked a very special place to be dining, but unfortunately it was raining, so we took the short walk over the bridge, into the very quaint town. It was our first visit here and we both loved it. Some lovely bars / restaurant to be enjoyed, along with the odd square or plaza, with limited shopping. A very nice, relaxed atmosphere. Would return to both hotel and town without hesitation. Many Thanks Gary.

author: scottishtravellers2
title: great hotel
text: We have just got back from an 11 night stay in the Pont D'or in Figeac. which we booked through Brittany Ferries. I would definately recommend the Pont D'or and Figeac. We are a couple with 4 teenagers(12-17) and we had 3 rooms. This is the 5th holiday we have booked in french hotels and it's the first time all our requests and expectations have been met. We needed 1 double and 2 twin rooms one with bath and balcony and all 3 rooms together, this was all waiting for us when we arrived. The hotel is very well placed with a lovely view overlooking the river. The breakfast/dining room looks out on to the terrace and we had breakfast every morning in the sunshine on the river terrace. A stroll over the bridge took us to the tabac for our morning paper and into the town where there are lots of restaurants and bars to choose from. the town is busy but has a good mix of tourists and locals. We saw very few British visitors. Drive an hour in any direction from Figeac and there is an interesting town to visit from the very comercialised Roccamandour to the beautiful Martel. The hotel is spotless and the rooms very comfy, we paid extra for a river balcony in one room which was really worth it. The bar was pleasantly busy in the evenings until after 11pm but there isn't much noise as it was mainly couples sitting enjoying a drink and the view. The pool is not large but it's spotlessly clean and although it's not heated it was warm enough. We spent every afternoon there with the children and it made our holiday. The staff at the hotel are all very friendly and helpful and advised us on local places to eat and visit.

author: like2travel1
title: An excellent hotel in a fantastic location
text: My wife and I spent one hight here, and found the hotel excellent in every way. Not only is the hotel very nice, the location is outstanding, right in the center of this small town, along the Cele River. The old city is directly across the bridge on the river. The hotel is quite new and has been very well maintained. Our room, which overlooked the river, was very modern, adequately large, and was very nicely decorated and furnished. Our beds were extremely comfortable. Our bath area also was large and modern. Everything was outstandingly clean. All of the staff were very friendly and helpful. The hotel has an enclosed outdoor parking lot directly across the street. The hotel also has a deck area bar overlooking the river, which is a very pleasant setting. The Best Western web site is very accurate in its description of the hotel, except that "coffee/tea makers" are only in suites. Some rooms also have a balcony that overlook the river and old town, but we don't know if these are standard rooms or suites. The hotel has a 3-star rating and it fully meets this standard. It is one of the best in town, and we very definitely would stay here again.

author: 872sarahm872
title: Great little hotel in the heart of it all
text: I took my mother to Paris for her birthday and even after living there for a year finding the right hotel in the right area for a good price is hard. I ended up settling on Hotel B Square and I'm so glad I did. We arrived past midnight but the concierge was still very helpful and friendly. The room was relatively small however most rooms in paris are. There was more than enough room for luggage and to be comfortable. We even had a balcony which was fab. The bed was comfy, the room was had good curtains so in the morning we could lay in a little. There was a fridge and a kettle in the room which was also helpful. The bathroom was nice with a rainfall shower as well as a wand. The only issue we had was a cracked toilet seat which wasn't replaced when we told reception however it didn't matter as I didn't really affect us. We didn't eat there so not sure on breakfast but there is plenty around and we managed to stumble on the markets before they closed on Saturday which was great! More than anything I was impressed by the location for the price. Place de clichy was a 5 minute walk which is full of cafes and resturant, cinema and of course the moulin rouge. Montmartre is just around the corner (one of my personal favourites) and access to Metro and buses. I recommend this hotel for short stays in a great location at a brilliant price in Paris!

author: Logan780
title: Great location, clean rooms, small bathroom
text: 5 of us had three rooms for 5 nights in June. The hotel is on a quiet, tree-lined street and was recently remodeled. For our first trip to Paris we were prepared for small rooms but were surprised just how small they were. Having said that, this was one of the cleanest rooms I have ever stayed in. While the rooms were small, they were comfortable with clean white linens, a bar fridge, a safe (I never did get mine to work), air conditioning and flat screen tv. Two of the three rooms we had on the fourth floor faced each other across a small central courtyard so didn't have a view. The third room had a nice view of the street. The bathroom in my room was miniscule and one of the shower doors wouldn't open because the sink got in the way which was an issue because I'm a big guy. I did, however, manage to get in and out of the shower. The hotel is about equal distance from Place de Clichy and Rome Metro stations which makes it convenient to get to wherever you need to go in the city. The hotel was also a short walk from Moulin Rouge which we attended on a Friday night. There are cafes (Augustin/Terasse 17) and shops nearby and you can get anything you need within a couple of minutes. We tended to head towards Place de Clichy to catch the Metro The staff were, for the most part, friendly and if you tried a little bit of French they would work with you. The young girl working our first night was very helpful getting us 2 cabs in a downpour. We all had issues with our room safes but the staff got them sorted out. I was the only one that tried the breakfast which was okay. It was just as easy to stop on the way to the Metro in the morning and pick up a croissant and a cup of coffee for half the cost. For the most part, we were in our room only to sleep and change clothes before dinner or a show. If you're looking for spacious, this is not the hotel for you but if you're looking for a comfortable, clean room at a reasonable price (for Paris) then I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone travelling to Paris.

author: /undefined
title: Cute Place
text: Loved the bathroom. So modern! The room was Art Deco, I guess. KPurple chandeliers! And thank God for the elevator. Down side for us was that it was a long haul from the train station with luggage, the WiFi was not working, and we were there on a Saturday night so the cafes out front were still active.
