Once we got to sleep, we were not disturbed by any noise, though. It was comfortable. The breakfast is nice. The consierge was very pleasant but not too helpful about the WiFi. Also, we asked for the airport shuttle service. He wanted 16 Euro up front and then we had to pay the shuttle guy another 20. We doh't understand the 16 part. The consierge would not add it to our room bill, it was separate and had to be cash. ??? His breath was pretty bad, too. But the hotel itself was nice, just not as conveniently located as we thought.

author: H1878TZclaireh
title: Good value for money
text: We are staying here now. For £30 a night I don’t think you can complain. Clean,if a bit rough around the edges. Good shower, plenty of hot water, comfy bed & pillows, quiet on a night, plenty of plug points...even near the mirror 🙂 We’re in apt 80 overlooking the pool which is a great spot but this is the pool that has now started major construction work. Not ideal as drilling been going on all day upto 6pm...but we’ve been out all day so not too bad for us. There are another 2 pools in the complex with more than enough sunbeds. Clean pool areas and no saving beds required or allowed. Zanzibar on sight is fab, friendly staff & good value. Pool snack bar is as needed, nothing fancy but adequate. Large supermarket 2 minutes from Reception with everything you could need & reasonable prices. Nestors Restaurant on site. Eaten there once and going again tonight as the food was amazing! Sirloin steak was gorgeous, as were the mussels & seafood pasta All in all, good value for money. Once the pool upgrade is finished, 1 bedroomed apts 80 - 85 are spot on. For the other pool very close by I’d try apts 62 -65. We would definately return. £30 a night? Couldn’t get a half decent B&B on the UK coast for that!

author: clairebG3197OG
title: Excellent accommodation
text: As usual previous reviews on here would suggest it is a dump - couldn't be more wrong. I was wary as we got it cheap. The apartment is spacious with everything you could ask for - microwave , kettle, toaster, hob, fridge and enough cooking utensils to make a basic meal. TV with English channels and WiFi throughout. Good sized pool with enough space for sunbeds without been cramped. Pool bar serving good meals all day . Supermarket nearby and British shop for everyones needs. Handful of bars behind supermarket to keep you going . It is a good 10min walk downhill to market - Tues and sat and a further 10 mins to beach, shops and bars. Caleta is a quiet resort. Past marketplace is the big indoor shopping center. Nice for a mornings walk. Already planning to come back, enjoyed it. Staff we met were helpful. Couldn't fault this place.

author: MrsP1073
title: Certainly not 3 Star, it’s hard to give it 1!
text: We booked a one week stay here with a 2 bedroom apartment. We arrived late evening to a room with sheets with hairs on, hairs on the floor, no coat hangers in the wardrobes, cigarette burns in the sheets and coackroaches running over the cooking area. The maid visited the room once during the whole week and replaced one single towel so I had to return the others to reception for replacement as they had begun to smell. She did not mop the floors and I had to again ask for this to be done. One of the pillows had no cover which again I had to go to reception and ask for. Beds had no mattress protectors on and were so well worn they were like hammocks. The duvet type covers were smelly and damp. The TV in the room is not a TV rather just a radio. The bathroom has a hot water tank so hot water is limited when 4 people need to shower, invariably if your last you get a cold shower! Communal areas were filthy and every conceivable gap in the wall had a cigarette butt stuffed into it. There were more tiles missing from the pool than were in it. The reception has shower rooms below which again were filthy with settees in with the foam hanging out and filthy floors. On our final day we had a lot of rain which poured into the wardrobe through a hole in the roof and soaked our daughters clothes. The rain also came in through the windows. Also when it rains the WiFi didn’t work! Overall this complex is very poor and requires a lot of investment to bring it up to standard. I would recommend spending more and staying elsewhere. It does appear that some rooms have been renovated from the outside but there was no evidence to suggest that the renovation work was ongoing to the majority of the rooms. Very disappointed and would never return.

author: Julie081
title: Quirky apartments
text: My husband and I stayed here after exchanging my timeshare to do so. Our apartment 65 was lovely. It is quite old and dated and was a bit fusty when we opened the door but I liked it. it was comfortable with a great shower in the bathroom but very limited cooking facilities. We found it to be adequate as we like to eat out each evening. However is was fine for making breakfast and lunch. It overlooked the refurbished pool and was very quiet at night, which we like. I was dreading the bed but found it to be really comfortable. The only one problem was it was very hot once the windows were closed and the ceiling fan in the bedroom was too slow. There is no air con, You also could not leave your windows, open so the place had to be shut up during the night - we would not risk leaving them open even though the area seems to be safe. The supermarket, 5 minutes walk away, was great and the prices reasonable. The newly refurbished pool, which we overlooked from our apartment was lovely and clean. There was always plenty of sunbeds. There are plenty of places to eat, all within walking distance. The town is not too far either. I found the staff to be pleasant and helpful. The restaurant on the complex is well worth a visit (we went 4 times in 7 nights) The food, service and staff were all excellent at a sensible price.

author: Jessdjess
title: Cheap and cheerful, relaxing week.
text: I was a bit worried after reading the bad reviews but was pleasantly surprised when we arrived. The reception staff were lovely and friendly. The bungalow (6) was basic but clean. The bed could have been better. Two single beds which were slightly different heights pushed together. The kitchen was adequate for cooking basic meals, breakfast etc which is all we wanted. Fridge, cooker, kettle, microwave, coffee maker, pots, cutler etc. TV had English channels. We had a garden view patio with table and chairs outside and clothes horse for drying clothes. We used the Elite pool which was nice with a bar to get drinks and snacks. It’s wasn’t too busy and we could always get a sun lounger. Plenty of great restaurants down the hill in the town. Bollywood spices in the Montecasillo centre is 2 minutes away and is gorgeous Indian food. Considering I paid €270 for 2 people for a week I think it was fine. If you expect luxury for that price then you will be disappointed.

author: richardiwatson1969
title: A very basic 2 weeks
text: Stayed 16-30 July. If you are looking for a beautiful apartment, with stylish decor and furniture then don't stay here. The rooms were old and tatty, The beds were the worst. No real sleep for 2 weeks. That being said when I pointed things out to the staff, they were changed that day. The cleaning service was poor. Only cleaned 2 times in 2 weeks. I think it depends on your apartment allocation. If offered 10-13 then avoid. The larger pool area was scruffy. Lots of broken tiles, daughter suffered gash to her knee. The smaller pool area was better and quieter. Avoid food and drink from the pool bar, expensive and not very good. Supermarket offered better and cheaper choices. The area was OK, a little run down. In need of a clean up. Not a lot of entertainment on site, unless you like darts or bad karaoke. We walked into town most nights..lots of bars and food places. Average price for a meal for 4 was 45-50 euros.

author: RichardB809
title: Plenty to keep coming back
text: We visited the Elite Fuerteventura Club for the first time at the end of June 2018. Our first impression was a good one. The reception was very welcoming and although we arrived at about 11am everything was ready and we had access. The apartment was a bit tired but had all we needed. It also smelt a little musty which was quickly dealt with by housekeeping. It was not very well equipped for anyone wishing to truly self caterer but for just breakfast it was fine. The landscaping is well cared for and the two pools are clean and monitored by the life guard every day. Elite has a very nice club house with drinks at very reasonable prices and Nestors restaurant is fabulous. Beautifully prepared food and very generous portions. Mains could easily be shared. The supermarket was well stocked despite being refitted and there is a Brit Store on site. This is expensive but convenient. The walk to town is a gentle downhill stroll, about 20 mins and passes the market area which is twice a week on Sats and Tuesdays.The town itself is ok and family orientated with a huge beach of golden sand. Two Sun beds and an umbrella was E10.50 per day. Atlantic’s shopping centre is a very pleasant strol along the front and has a number of well known brand outlets. We had a lovely week and will be going back again next year

author: 541claireh
title: Great value stay.
text: Thoroughly enjoyed our 1 week stay here... exactly that !..you get what you pay for and have travelled all over the world with holidaypirates from whom we bought this deal ! On arrival with Ryanair we were through passport control collecting our hand luggage off the Carousel and into the taxi within 12 minutes !! seriously smooth... The apartment was clean and spacious beds were comfy we loved our little Terrace where we had lunch everyday. Self catering facilities were sufficient all appliances working and room cleaned and towels changed once in the week which was plenty for us. It's clear the complex is being updated and Improvements are being made. We had friends who were staying the same week at a very expensive all-inclusive resort in Caleta on the seafront.. our experience far surpassed there's ! The receptionist was extremely helpful and knowledgeable about things to do and places to go locally we stood and chatted many times. She advised us to take the free tues/sat bus to Puerto del Rosario which we did.. and fetched a couple of bags of self catering shopping from the (far cheaper) supermarket in the city. We also enjoyed the free tour of Caleta and the views of the mountains on the free bus journey!. We loved the pool area for it calm quiet relaxed atmosphere I swam every day in the pool which was clean and quiet. we walked over 10 kilometres during the week up and down the hill into caleta, which we enjoyed. We saw the cat cafes😂 snapshots of local life and enjoyed seeing the resort on foot. We ate out every night searching out the best deals as we were on a real tight budget . we found three-course meals for €10 each in the resort, €5 lunch specials at the Trafalgar and happy hour drinks early evening were plenty. We would definitely return... there are some fantastic deals to be had out of the main season

author: butlinsbabe58
title: Home from home
text: My first solo holiday and my first visit to Fuertaventura. They say you get what you pay for and I was a bit dubious due to the reviews and low price. The bungalows themselves were ok it was just the furniture inside was very dated. I never had a problem with cleanliness or creatures in the week I was there. Would've preferred more than 1 visit from the housekeeping. My bed was not very comfortable and the kitchen equipment could've been a bit better but all in all I can't really complain! The bungalow was well equipped apart from decent glasses and mugs, and after reading about the lack of cereal bowls I took my own! I didn't get around to going in the pool as it was never really hot enough to tempt me but it looked ok...just in need of a bit of tlc. The whole complex was friendly and welcoming...Nestors restaurant was lovely and Zanzibar was the only place to be for me in the evenings...sitting at the bar on a stool chatting to the lovey staff. I tried walking in to town one evening but didn't enjoy the food and didn't feel as comfortable as when I was sat in Zanzibar! Being on my own I didn't venture far but didn't really need to as it's all there on site... the restaurant, the bar, the shop, the people. A special mention has to be for the staff in Zanzibar who worked non stop but still had time to chat and make me feel welcome... Martina... Susan.. Judy and Redoiun. I'd love go back and maybe look into buying a holiday place there in the future. I can see why so many people love and return to Caleta de Fuste. This place was lovely!

author: 564elaj
title: Lovely holiday, little warning for guests staying at the hotel.
text: We recently stayed here for 4 nights. We were in apartment 13, which was near the main road (no balcony), this was not an issue for us! The apartment was nice, had kitchen/sitting area, bedroom and bathroom. Upon arriving, the staff were very welcoming, gave us leaflets to have a read through, some about the hotel - saying we should lock all doors and windows each time we leave the apartment, which we did. On the last night of our holiday, we went to the restaurant at the hotel and then to the bar until early hours in the morning. When we got back to our apartment, our bedroom window was broken and open, and our stuff was everywhere, someone had broken in and gone through everything possible. Luckily for us, all our valuable stuff (money, passports etc) were in my partners case which had a lock on it. Baring in mind, this was only a hand luggage case, they could have easily taken it with them. We rushed back to the bar and told the member of staff working there what had happened, he got hold of the hotel security and he got to us right away. He then brought us back to the apartment to get the rest of our stuff, where more security had got there. They were brilliant, as they stayed with us while we got the rest of our stuff, then sorted out a new room for us which was near the reception, and had a balcony. They told us that whenever we are on holiday we should always have the curtains closed with a light or tv on, so that it looks like someone is there. We had the curtains closed everyday except that night. Also if the window had not been locked, it would not have counted as a break in. We did not let this ruin our holiday as we were very lucky that nothing was taken. The point of this review is just a heads up to use the safe in the room, it does cost more but it’s worth it, and we will be using it from now on. Do not let this put you off staying here, we loved it there, and an incident like that could happen at anytime, anywhere. Stay safe wherever you go, and enjoy your holiday.

author: fapjje
title: Ok stay. Not heaven but not hell.
text: This place is alright. Don't no what 'hell-hole' reviewers expect, including the previous reviewer who didn't even stay here. We are here now and will be here for 4 weeks. Very spacious bungalow, as big as any one-bedroom place we've ever stayed in. Very well equipped with kettle, toaster, coffee-maker, microwave and TV with some English channels. We would never be bothered about the TV anyway. There aren't any Soanish channels on UK TV! Also has iron and ironing board. Never had them anywhere else we've stayed. Wi-fi is free and always works. Very close to lots of bars and places to eat. Many more of them in Caleta centre which is 15 minutes walk away or 3.50 euros by taxi. Reviewers who don't like the complex being up the hill should have done more research before coming. Plenty of information available about anywhere you want to go on the internet. Perhaps needs a bit of touching up here and there but so does everybody's house at home. Generally very clean premises. Reception very helpful and friendly. Recommend staying here to anybody who's not a miserable moaner.

author: Luke1307
title: Absolute Hell Hole!!
text: I was worried about this place after seeing reviews and rightly so! We paid for a cheap holiday but this was taking the mick, we did not expect 5* but we did expect at least 1! Where to start - the room was filthy with dirt and grime everywhere. The sofa bed was an absolute state and didn't look like it had been replaced since the 90's. The floor and kitchen tiles were all cracked and dangerous and the bath was black with grit and dirt! Surprisingly, the toilet was rather clean. A lot of bulbs need replacing and the place needs a general re vamp! It seems that there is a good side and a bad side. We were to the right of the Nestor's restaurant if you were stood on the abandoned stage in apartment 75. If we were on the left, it seems everyone in those apartments were part of a time share and had lovely rooms, the rest had been left to rot. There are 2 pools, both of which are not heated and freezing along with 1 pool bar which is barely ever open. The reception is clean and tidy with helpful staff! We even had a local rep knock our door during the holiday and re assure us that we would be the last people staying in our apartment before renovation, however after a recent re visit to Fuerteventura and a walk up the hill, i can assure you this is not true! There are some lovely bars in the area, look out for the Red Lion and the Sizzling Pig, both of which are very accommodating and in great spots! To summarize, avoid this hotel and stay down the hill in Puerto Caleta.

author: stevev548
title: Honest Review
text: We have stayed here three times in three different apartments (58 - good, 13 - not so good and currently number 30 - good and has been updated). Taxi from airport €13. It is a big complex with 3 pools and some areas are a little tired but you can see maintenance going on. Rooms are a little musty so on arrival open all the doors and windows. If you need anything towels, irons etc - pop up to reception and you will get them in 15 mins. There is a bar on site (Zanzibar), very cheesy and very British. That said we pop in there before going to bed for a quick drink. Each room has a TV, safe (€2 a day), kettle, microwave, fridge and a small job. Supermarket is 2 mins away and has good freshly made bread and pastries. We paid just over £8 per person per night to stay here. Is it worth £8 - absolutely. Is it value for money - absolutely. Would we stay again - absolutely. If you want a base and a place to sleep then stay here. If you are looking to spend time in your room and hotel then look elsewhere

author: Carlisle_Eater
title: Great location - bit grubby
text: We have just returned after a week here. Overall the complex has a great deal of potential. It is a good location with three pools and lots of restaurants and bars nearby. There's also a couple of supermarkets on site. It's a walk down a steep hill to get into the main town but taxis back are only 3 euros so it's worth while. The town itself is lovely and has a lot to offer. There's also a good local market on each Tuesday and Saturday which sells bags and jewellery. The reason I have given this 3 stars and not 5 is the state of the apartment itself. Whilst it was a good size and centrally located, it was a bit grotty and in desperate need of a good clean. We had the cleaners round twice during the week. Not entirely sure what they did as the bed being made consisted of the bed spread being straightened over the still crumpled sheets. Neither time was any of the table tops of other surfaces wiped as not a single thing on them had been moved. There were also a few stains on the floor and walls which look like they had been there a while and would have come off with a good scrub! As I say, it did have a lot of potential though. The pools themselves are good and well kept. And the pool bars offer decent food at good prices. We are likely to return to Caleta de Fuste but will probably stay at another complex.

author: MrsTupo
title: get what you pay for
text: So after reading the reviews i was quite worried, but when we got there it wasn't that bad we paid £187 for 11 nights so couldn't crumble. The rooms are basic, when we got there there was no kettle or toaster or microwave (but didn't need a microwave as we ate out) so went and told reception and they brought us kettle and toaster so wasn't to bad then it started to go down hill a bit. after 3 days i went and asked when we would be getting clean towels and sheets the receptionist rang through to the maid. then came back and said it had been done today!!! that was a total lie the lady then gave me clean sheets and towels so i now had to do it myself. on day six we someone came in and changed our sheets but only the tops sheets of the beds but i couldn't be bothered to argue so let it slide. then on day 9 no clean towels or sheets yet again so i went to reception and greeted by a very rude man who just kept shrugging his shoulders. eventually someone came and changed the sheets but said she had no towels so by this point i was getting pretty annoyed. i later went back to reception to ask for some to again be shrugged at and given 4 hand towels. and the dirty towels that gathered up where left in a pile as the cleaner never took them with her. so the next day i went and asked for some lager clean towels to be greeted by the same rude man shrugging saying there were none. fortunately the manager was there and i explained everything and I said had the cleaner took the towels yesterday maybe they'd have some clean. and with in minutes he came with clean ones!! that's towel gate!! fridge was crap all rusty we had a leak in the toilet late evening and sent some one in the morning and they just silicone it so no doubt will leak again other then that pool was great was a short walk to the town up hill tho so would suggest taxi back. elite bar was fab for breakfast 3.50 euro WiFi was pretty crap only worked in the early hours of the morning.. if it wasn't for the rude male staff and the non existent cleaning service it would be an OK place to stay. Id maybe stay again if i was looking for a last minute cheap holiday its not as bad as some people make out but it is budget hotel so you get what you pay for.

author: rebeccal162
title: Exceeded My Expectations.
text: When we booked most of the reviews looked ok for the apartments. We were looking for a cheap week away in the sun and weren't expecting high end luxury. However, prior to travelling I read the recent reviews and dread set in with reports of cockroaches and difficult staff not addressing problems with rooms etc. General advice was to ask for a refurbished room, which we did through our booking agent. On arrival we were fobbed off and told the hotel was very busy and it wasn't possible to change our room - yet after being here a few days that doesn't appear to be the case. The apartment is tired and needs some maintenance, a lot of the floor tiles are cracked and the kitchen area isn't really functional, the worktop is severely damaged and I wouldn't want to prepare a meal in it and the kettle turns clear water from the tap brown!! The bed is comfortable and the apartment is clean. Housekeeper has been in every other day so far, although a towel disappeared and we had to get another from reception. This was replaced without hesitation. Internet access is available but you can only access one device at a time, so for a couple it is a bit tricky and we have had to take turns. Our apartment is no.19 and is directly by one of the pool's and the Elite Bar. Therefore, tea and coffee have been cheaply available and the kettle hasn't been a problem. Although I say there is a bar a stone's throw away it is only open until 7.00pm - so no disturbed sleep. The pool area is lovely with plenty of sun loungers and umbrellas. The apartments are under the flight path but everywhere is on the east side of the island. There hasn't been any flights in the evenings and the usual pattern is two or three in 5 minutes and then nothing for an hour or so - So perfectly bearable. The complex is a 10 minutes walk out of town and slightly uphill but again this should be perfectly manageable for most people. We did have a problem with a smoke alarm battery being low and the alarm bleeping but within 1/2 an hour of my husband raising the issue with reception it was fixed. The hotel represents good value for money - it is not luxurious but as other reviewers have said 'you get what you pay for'.

author: songbird68
title: Not as bad as previous reviews implied
text: As with previous reviews, yes this place was tired and dated but it was clean. We were situated adjacent to Zanzibar's and Nestors it was relatively quiet except for the kids bouncing their footballs late in the evening. Again as other reviewers have said, in January you don't expect there to be any kids around, obviously our schools need to fine the parents more for taking their kids out of school especially when they have just had 2 weeks off for Christmas. Our apartment had a fridge with ice box, a kettle, microwave, toaster and electric juicer. It had plenty of plates, cutlery etc and we were pleased to find a corkscrew (I had packed one just in case). We were there for 2 weeks, Saturday to Saturday, the maid came in Thursday, Monday and Thursday. Sheets were changed and so were towels. We had a problem with ants the first two times we turned the shower on as they were coming out of the taps on the wall but after that it was fine. In the 2 weeks we had a total of 7 cockroaches but that is to be expected in the Canaries. Zanzibar's offered free Wifi but the signal wasn't great. We had sangria twice which was nice but felt that the brandy and gin that we had tasted watered down. We never went into Nestors as we like to sit outside and smoke after our dinner and every night the 3 tables that were outside had a reserved sign on them but we never saw anyone sat there at various times of the evening, plus we thought it was quite expensive. Staff at Fuerteventura Beach Club were friendly and unlike other reviews I have seen on here, there was a man cleaning the pool daily. It is a bit of a trek into Caleta itself but the train runs every half an hour and costs 2 euros per person. Taxis were between 2.50 and 4.00 depending on what time you got one. The best places we found to eat were, Slow Boat Chinese buffet which was 8.95 for all you can eat but on Wednesdays you get 30% off so it was 6.25 and there was a lot of choice. Gambrinus was another really good restaurant. Kobi Steak House ribs were really good and a decent price at 12.50 and if you have a massive appetite at breakfast try their big breakfast for 4 euros which you get 3 eggs, 3 bacon, 3 sausage, beans, tomatoes, hashbrown, black pudding and toast, a coffee cost 1 euro if you have a breakfast. All in all a good holiday for an astonishing £231 each for 2 weeks.

author: MCPK
title: ELITE FUERTEVENTUA BEACH CLUB - VERY GOOD
text: I had read a lot of reviews and did not know what to expect. However the complex is made out of several apartments which differ in comfort and state I believe. The best are the Elite Suites (only 3 or 4 of them) and we were in the category below, the best in the apartments section. It was spotlessly clean, very comfortable beds, great shower with jets, change of towels and cleaned every day, very well furnished, own patio. The location was perfect, close to the salt water pool. Very quiet and relaxing. We did not use the other 2 pools as far busier, noisier, both with bars. The salt water pool was brilliant, cleaned every day and very big. Plenty of sun beds. Most of the time we were at the most half a dozen people and it was great to pop into our apartment for lunch and drinks. There was a restaurant on the premises, a "Brit" supermarket which we didn't use as we usually avoid anything British as in our opinion that defeats the purpose of travelling abroad and is also more expensive. Just across the road there was a local Supermarket "Dino" which was brilliant and very cheap - fresh numerous types of bread, pastries etc..., every morning and throughout the day. Close by a shopping centre, restaurants, bars. Easy 15 mns or so walk down to the centre of Caleta de Fuste and the beach. Lots of restaurants, market, very busy at night.. Anyone not wishing to walk, taxis are very cheap - only 3 to 4 Euros. The staff in the reception of the complex were very helpful, friendly and couldn't do enough for you, especially Madi. For a peaceful, restful with lovely surroundings and gardens I would recommend it. We certainly would happily go back.

author: fionaf938
title: 3* Prices for 3* Accommodation
text: My friend and I have just got back from a week at these apartments. For the money we paid, it was as expected. The apartment was clean but the smell when we first entered was pretty foul! This was easily resolved with a good airing and some scented candles. The kitchen was a little strange; the microwave was sat on a chair, but everything worked and was clean. The pool areas are great (there are three) and the sunloungers are really comfortable. The only disappointment was that our apartment was not serviced at all in the seven days we were there. I did approach the receptionist about the bins because they were, naturally, attracting the attention of insects. We were told to empty it ourselves and given insect spray. I do believe that they should address this promptly because it wouldn't take a great deal of time for them to arrange a refuse collection and replace towels, even if they don't bother cleaning. There are two supermarkets really close by and it's not too far from the beach. The restaurant on site, Nestors, is absolutely disgusting and extortionately priced, so do take a walk to the town. There's a lovely restaurant called Cafe Nero there that serves a wide range of gorgeous food! Anyway, you get what you pay for. If you're expecting 5*, you should have paid for 5*

author: 556holliec
title: Great stay, would come back
text: My friend and I stayed here for 4 nights at the end of June and had a great time. The complex was easy to get to from the airport - ten minutes in a taxi which cost around 11 euros. Considering some of the reviews other people have left, we were pleasantly surprised when we arrived. The apartment was basic but clean and was better than we had expected. The cooking facilities are fine for making breakfast or lunch. Our apartment overlooked one of the smaller pools and was very quiet most of the time. The resort had more facilities than we expected - 3 pools, reception, bars, restaurants and it was close to the supermarket. The receptionists were always very helpful. The electrics tripped in our apartment and someone was sent round within 5 minutes to sort it out. One small issue we did have was a few ants on the kitchen floor. However they are obviously aware of this as a can of ant spray was left under the sink which got rid of them. Also, there was wifi but it wasn't working while we were there. Caleta de Fuste is a lovely quiet area. The beach and shopping centre is about a 10 minute walk down the hill from the resort. There is a fantastic restaurant near the supermarket called the Pickled Palm which is run by a lovely couple who were very accommodating for two vegetarians. We ate there three evenings out of the four we were there, which says it all really! Overall, we found the Fuerteventura Beach Club great value for money - it was perfect for our budget sunshine break - and we would be quite happy to return.

author: harribarker
title: Cheap so you need to make allowances!
text: Stayed here tues-fri mid may. The price we paid (£242 flights, s/c accommodation & airport xfers), was reflected in the accommodation. It is in dire need of updating. We stayed in no.20 right on top of the 'noisy' pool. People tend to ignore the swimming from 10am-6pm rule and stay out quite late and no one seems to move them on. Nice pools and no shortage of new sunloungers. The fridge was rusty on the outside but clean inside. Only used that, kettle & toaster. Reception staff v helpful. Large supermarket across the road, very reasonable. We spent a grand total of £170 on everything when there so all was good. Went into town each eve for dinner, 15 mins downhill there, and steep uphill back. For a cheap getaway, short term break it is ideal for a base but for longer, I would have ibnsisted on moving or trying to upgrade. Only one standard was available thru On The Beach. Would return but stay in better accommodation.

author: gembob234
title: Excellent value for money
text: Stayed here on two occasions and you do very much get what you pay for. The rooms are outdated and basic but serve their purpose. Two ring hob, fridge freezer, fry pan and pot, plates, glasses and cutlery, microwave and toaster all in the apartment. You may have an iron and ironing board, i found my friends had the board and we had the iron, never had a hairdryer. Living room/diner has pull out sofa bed, dining table, coffee table and old style TV - english channels are the news and true movies. Bedroom had two twin bed very hard mattress with bedside table, dressing table/mirror and wardrobes. Maid service twice a week. We had a pool view room with terrace. Staff are really helpful reception couldn't do enough for us even contacted places for us we wanted to visit to make communication easier over the phone for us. Called taxis as and when we needed - they are about 3 euros in to town. Parking is available we was able to park outside our apartment and most of the island is free parking. The restaurant serves huge portions, a bit pricey but you do need a reservation which was new to me but they will bring your food in to the bar as take away. The meals are big enough to share between 2! Zanzibar is the onsite bar and has free wifi to connect to and they had entertainment on - as young people it didn't really cater for us but the beer was reasonable priced and the cocktails good :) Location is up an hill however there are shops and supermarkets within a few minutes walk and the market is on twice a week in this area. Its a great base to discover the island from, puerto rosario is 10 mins drive, airport 10 mins, corralejo (sand dunes) 30-40 mins, el cotillo (great surf) 45 mins, horse riding (finca julie) 40 mins, go karts (gran karting) 10 mins, costa calma 45 mins and jandia (morro jable/national park) about 1 hour 15 minutes. Pools are fabulous and there are three with two having bar and snacks near, never used the gym and don't think anyone else has either in a long time. For a self cater holiday cheap as chips with a good base to explore the island this hote is fab! definitely would go back

author: Debbie187053
title: Great holiday
text: This place is a little gem for the price. Apartment basic but everything you need including iron and hairdryer. The pool has plenty of sunbeds and the pool bar is a must. The owners are lovely and the staff really friendly, the food is good and the prices are to. 3 euro for full English and 2 euros a pint. A couple of minutes walk and there's a square of bars. The Bell pub has all the sports on and owner a nice chap. 10 mins walk into main town. El capitano is a good night. 2 for 1 till 10. Pily serving behind the bar is hilarious. Food is good and it always has live entertainment on of good standard. Legends bar has live entertainment on. Staff really friendly and it's great for a dance to 60s and 70s till late. Zanzibar on the complex itself is open till one and that to is a lovely bar. Hyper Dino supermarket 2 minutes walk. We are on our second visit here.

author: MargaretC463
title: A nice week away
text: Exchanged into this complex with timeshare. This resort is formed by three separate areas. Club Elite, Club Fuerteventura and Club Montecastillo. We were in a two bedroomed apartment on the Elite Section. After reading previous reviews we were rather concerned. However although in need of TLC we were satisfied with our stay but understand that this part of the complex is for timeshare owners are are of a better standard. There were three pools all unheated two having poolside bar. There were plenty of sunbeds. We arrived early and was allowed straight into our apartment and the reception staff were very efficient with this and throughout our whole stay. There was a complimentary welcome pack. Pool towels and bathrobes were supplied. Beds were comfortable, but some of the furniture could do with replacing. Room was cleaned 5 times, towels and bed linen also changed during our stay. The evenings were quite chilly and we found the bedrooms rather cold, but could hire heaters if we wanted to. Was within walking distances of several nice restaurants including steak houses and fish. Nestors Restaurant on the complex was especially good. There is a market twice a week near the complex. There were supermarkets within walking distance. We hired a car which allowed us tour around the island. There was free wifi but very difficult to get a connection, but was available in the bar on site.

author: 1MCW
title: very different from reviews
text: Stayed here 19/08/14 for a week, read the reviews and did wonder what we had booked. Got there and there was no need to worry. The resort was lovely, admittedly it's not brand spanking new, though it is all functional and clean. Yes there is rust on the bottom of the fridge door, it gets wet from when they mop the floor, it still does the job it is designed to do!! and seriously how long are you going to sit there looking at it!!! The apartment we stayed in was clean and secure. I asked for a thicker curtain for the bedroom window and within 15mins a maid came with a blackout curtain. There are three pools, we stayed at the one by our apartment. Plenty of modern comfortable sunbeds, the other two pools did have limited beds this is because they want them to be quieter. It was a very quiet resort, ideal for relaxing. We had a working kettle and toaster. You really don't need to eat in as it' s so cheap to eat out. We really liked the resort. There is a 10-15 min walk to the main centre depending on your pace. Restaurants to go to is Le Patio, Dorado Le Garden de Pescario, The restaurant on the pier on the beach, Le Capitan and also Los Caracolitos in Salinas del Carmen,(2miles in the next village) where they will provide transport, well worth the visit.

author: Manhuwa
title: YOU GET WHAT YOU PAY FOR
text: Well unless you are really on a very tight budget then perhaps its better to avoid. I styayed here for 2 weeks from Aug 7th to 21st and having paid only £225 for a family of 4, maybe i expected too much. The amount which is equivalent to £4 a day per person says it all. It would be folly to expect a decent place for such a fee. The apartments are in need of a makeover, definately need new furniture and refurbishment. The bedroom had 2 single beds put side by side to make what they call a double, the sitting room had a sofa bed with terrible linen, well worn out. we asked them to change it and the replacement sofa bed linen was no better. the bathroom had paint peeling of the bath tub, its one you couldnt sit in, luckily there was an overhead shower. whilst i can forgive the state of rooms based on the amount i paid, i was dismayed by the lack of cleaning of the swimming pools and given that they use salty water in the pools, all the tiling around the pools would become dirty with dried salt residue from water drippimg from swimmers and in my 2 weeks there, they cleaned the pool surrounds once. The pools you could see residue at the bottom. all apartments have nowhere to place an oven and kettle, you end up using one of wooden chairs in the corner. the rooms are not air conditioned and it gets very hot i had to sleep with doors open. i would say the apartments are probably worse off than Pontins or Butlins in the UK. the workers try their hardest but there is definately need to invest and re-touch the apartments. location is great, on site stores, pubs and a restaurent plus three big pools. ants are in issue i guess in the whole island, any tiny bit of food they accumulate, overally i wouldnt book again, even on the tiniest of budgets. the accomodation provided by Travelodge UK is by far better snd top class than what i witnessed here. anyway you get what you pay for, having paid 225 pounds for 4 people over 2 weeks it would be too much to expect a 5 star hotel type of apartment. therefore YOU GET WHAT YOU PAY FOR.

author: gemnicholson
title: Amazing for what you pay!
text: We stayed here for a week at the start of August.. Upon reading previous reviews I was quite worried that there would be some issues upon our arrival but I was extremely surprised and relieved within minutes of being here. We paid £109 for three of us for a week in the middle of summer which is just amazing. Don't get me the wrong the rooms are basic but they have everything you need - large bedroom with lots of storage, a tv, full kitchenette including fridge, microwave, toaster and even a coffee maker! The rooms were clean and the maid came three times during the week we were there! We got ants near the door once but immediately were offered any spray and it worked a treat and they never returned! We had apartment 87 which lead right onto the pool area. The pool area was by far the greatest pool and the pool next to the elite bar is by far the best for families. My daughter made many friends who she will be keeping in touch with and loved playing round the pool with the other children. You could easily get sunbeds if you go down before 11am and these were great quality with lovely straw parasols available. The elite bar/cafe was great value and the food tasted lovely, the three of us eat here for lunch everyday for around 10 euros and the service was brilliant, the two ladies would happily bring your food and drinks to you around the pool. The hotel was up a steep hill and we did catch a taxi for 3 euros back from the centre a couple of times, but if you like to walk it is only around ten minutes to all the bars and restaurants. A taxi from the airport is 13 euros. Much cheaper than transfers! PLEASE do not be put off by any bad comments about this place, we will definately return next time we wish to have a cheap week away!!!

author: 490AnthonyM
title: Do not believe negative reviews
text: Just arrived back from a week in Fuerteventura, in which we stayed in the Fuerteventura Beach Club in early august. It is only 5 minutes from the airport by taxi. I was a bit nervous at first after reading the reviews but after we got our room i was much relieved. It was basic however it was clean and done the job. It was cleaned every two days. The staff were very helpful and there was no bother with us checking in. One negative comment about my room was that there was only one air conditioner and it was situated in the living room part and didn't really cool down the room. The pool is big and lovely, however there is not that many sun loungers and you can't reserve them or your towels will be taken. There is a bar called the Zanzibar on site and it is great value and there is even bingo there i won €130 there so i was very happy with myself. There are bars, restaurants and shops on site and the town centre is about a 10 minute walk where there are more shops and restaurants. You can get a taxi for €3 or there is a little train from the Zanzibar. Not five stars by any means but deserves a better rating. Would definitely return because it is a lovely place. This place is NOT FOR YOUNG CHILDREN though because there is nothing for them to do. Very cheap holiday. Loved it

author: OzYorkshire
title: Pull it down and start again.
text: What can I say about this place? Why is it called The Beach Club, it is at least a mile from the nearest beach? If you read my other numerous reviews you will see I am quite subjective and don’t criticise for the sake of it but this place is so bad it’s unbelievable. The accommodation we had was not really fit for human habitation until we had cleaned it, and the last thing you want to do on holiday is start cleaning. We had “chalet” 21 which was access via 2 steps onto a patio which was filthy with cigarette butts and general dirt, then in to the living area where there was a fold down type bed settee thing which was made up of 2 pieces of old foam on a base covered with a filthy cover, in this area was also a small kitchen, the kettle was on a shelf above the cooker, very safe? the cooker hob consisted of 2 rings, these worked fine, there was also a microwave sat on a chair in a corner, this was filthy, by this time we had decided that we had cleaned enough so never used it, there was a fridge that must have been sourced from a second hand shop, the door did not close unless slammed hard. The bathroom was another dirty room, the towels provided were so thin and worn they were pointless, the shower was adequate but 2 people could not get a shower consecutively or there would not be enough hot water. In the bedroom to ¾ beds were pushed together, needless to say they did not stay together, slightest movement and they became two separate beds, the bedding was clean but grey, not white, we asked for another pillow as there was only 3 in the room. There is a safe in the wardrobe which costs 10 Euro, recommended to use it. The pool is a cold sea water affair, there are tiles missing, we saw a cleaner once spend an hour cleaning the pool, the dead leafs and vegetation were an interesting addition, oh and don’t forget the rats that comes out to play between 4 and 5 on an afternoon, there is more than one living in the wall near the pool and bar area, with all the cats that are around they take a chance!! The bar area (Zanzibar) is OK but tends to cater for the long term residents and the time share owners than package holiday visitors, the time share areas were immaculate. The reception area was helpful when we used it, we spoke to the “customer service” chap and we mentioned our concerns about the place, we highlighted the possibly unsafe and dirty conditions and with a shrug of the shoulders he said you get what you pay for and walked off, some customer service. There is a little train that stops outside the reception area and for 3 Euros 2 people can have a ride to the beach, quite a pleasant short ride through the island. Because the hotel is on the flight path there is no lack of noise from the plentiful aircraft landing at the airport 5 miles away. The onsite restaurant, Nestors, is quite good and Emma and Nestor go out of their way to provide a great service with good food, the portions are huge and well cooked. Would I go back to this place NO.

author: jaythehammer
title: so good for the money
text: ok here is our honest review for the fuerteventura beach club, firstly i guess we got an amazing deal we had a two bedroom apt and we paid less than £200 each including flights and transfers. thought the apt was great for what we paid, yes the fridge had some rust on the outside but hey it kept our beers cold so no problems and it was plenty big enough. We had everything we needed for self catering all of the cooking utensils were of good quality and condition the hob looked fairly new and we had a kettle and toaster. There was a hot water tank in the bathroom (electric) so we had constant hot water and the pressure in the shower was excellent probably the best ever. Plenty of towels as well as extra blankets maid came twice during our week and there was a broom dustpan mop and bucket there so all good. didn't encounter any bugs or insects room was very clean. Balcony was of a good size but we spent most of our time outside the front door, in the walled front garden as this was a little sun trap and out of the very strong wind. Didn't use any of the hotel amenities i.e. bars etc but the pool outside our apt looked amazingly clean and the sun loungers were new and great quality much better than normal white plastic. Check in and out was excellent the lady on reception was english and very very helpful. Also the changing/shower area below reception was amazing. Plenty of hairdryers, mirrors,sinks,individual shower cubicles and toilets all kept really clean. The only bad points i can think of are that the beds were the usual two singles pushed together instead of a double and as we now have memory foam at home i really don't find sprung mattresses that comfortable but thats personal preference although both bedrooms were great sizes excellent wardrobe space and bedside cabinets and both had big dressing tables with mirror and chairs. It was in a good location 3 supermarkets in the immediate area including 2 selling british foods only if that floats your boat on holiday also numerous bars serving food and restaurants and a couple offering a takeaway service. It was a leisurely 10 minute walk into the centre of town and the beach, Downhill on the way uphill back however didn't find it to steep and there is a land train that runs right outside the reception down through town to the harbour and back didn't get a price but wouldn't think it was too expensive. All in all, Find it really hard to pick faults at that price would definitely return i have stayed in worse places in caletta for a lot more money really really enjoyed our stay would definitely recommend it is really very good for a budget stay

author: BicinViaggio
title: Horrible - Stay away!
text: As soon as we arrived we noticed the following: 1. The rooms were very dirty (body hair everywhere). The kitchen was very dirty and very run-down. 2. There were ants crawling in the kitchen and all around the apartment. 3. The patio door was damaged with clear signs of breaking-in. By the door there were gnawed bones, also full of ants. 4. Bed sheets were used, with hair and - again- ants! 5. The place was stinking of mold and beds were humid. We booked through Otel.com. Despite I patiently provided any information and pictures stating my assertions, we have not been refunded yet. Given this, I would recommend people to book through websites that do not request upfront payment.

author: davidtracey09
title: Relaxing Break
text: Back yesterday. We stayed on a Self Catering Basis. Really great time. So relaxing. Yes the place is tired, but have stayed in worse places and payed a lot more. We will be going back. Staff were really helpfull and nothing was a problem. Bravo!!!!! Get a bus from the airport, 1.50c or a taxi at 12 euro. Just outside the front look right and there is supermarket there. Great value. A little further along there is a small square and there is a pub called The Bell. Call in and say hello - great guy. Also in the square there is a place called The Ranch with a large breakfast @ 4.90c is great value. Great place to start the day!!! In town please try Fado Rock and Nestors. You will thank me!!!! The Slowboat buffet is also very good value. Overall a great place to holiday - roll on next year.

author: frazercoglan
title: Internet bookings beware!!!
text: Stayed here with wife and two kids last two weeks in August. Were allocated room 68 first impression what a dump!! bed settee ready for the tip, kitchen old fashioned with a grotty old rusty fridge but there was better to come. On unlocking the rear patio doors we discovered that the previous evening somebody had attempted to burgle the apartment by forcing a screwdriver into the frame damaging the frame and at some point slipped and cut themselves which had left a puddle of blood on the floor. The damage was reported to reception and the maintainance man attended and informed us that a new frame was needed then the manager arrived. He totally denied that it was a burglary and informed us that it wasnt blood and was infact red paint lol!! We asked for a change of room and were informed if we did move it would be to one of a WORSE standard at which point we pointed out there were plenty of refurbished apartments standing empty. We were told they were reserved for timeshare swop holidaymakers and we noticed any Spanish holidaymakers and he could not allocate these apartments. The new door frame turned into a small metal plate covering the screwdiver damage and the so called paint was mopped up by the cleaner clearly showing it was in fact blood!! Also after denying they had a problem with burglaries the manager did admit the apartments facing the road did suffer from break-ins as the security guard couldnt cover this area so beware if you get one of these. We decided to stay but they would of found it difficult to find an apartment worse than this dump so i slept on the disgusting, damaged flea bitten sofa bed ( stunk of sweat) by the patio window just so the wife and kids felt safe at night. Over the next few days we watched all the refurbished apartments being let to timeshare and spaniards where nothing was to much to trouble whilst all the Brit cattle were given a key to there very own dilapidated dumps. Every time we walked into Reception there was always an internet booking complaining about their accom being given the brush off too full etc.. and at one point the girl was giving out the refurbs to timeshare and Spaniards whilst virtually ignoring the poor sod complaining. The Resort itself we really enjoyed but this accomodation is the pitts, if you book over the net dont say i didnt warn you if you get allocated your very own dump.

author: Fuerteventurasno1fan
title: You can tell Spain is broke......
text: This was our 3rd stay at the FBC (returned 5th Aug 12) and it's been our worse one so far as regards to the accommodation. Our room was nice enough (we always request a room in block 35-46) with good self-catering facilities. Only problem, the beds were like concrete!! Plus the room was baking hot and the ceiling fans were worse than useless! The maid visited everyday apart from Wednesday and Saturday (main change over day) and if we wanted clean towels we just left the dirty ones in the bottom of the shower. The one thing that really upset us this year was the state of the pools. The swimming pool at the Elite bar was by far the cleanest and the other two pools were filthy! The pool outside our room, number 44, wasn't cleaned for the whole two weeks we were there. This meant a green slime built up around the edge of the pool and what with the bits of trees that had been blown in by the wind made a big congealed mess at one end of the pool. Plus it meant the edge of the pool was very slippery and a few of the children playing in the pool were slipping over, even when walking! Also, the tiles around the pool were never washed down as you could see where the pool water dried overnight and left 'salt patterns' on the floor. Please note that the three pools on FBC are salt water! We never ate at the Elite pool bar because we met a guy who lives in Caleta and told us that their kitchen is right next to a sewer!! Kind of put us off a bit! Instead we went over to the Montecastillo centre and had breakfast from Bar El Nido where we met Iain, Janey and Catherine who do some of the nicest and best value food in Caleta!! All in all we had a fabulous holiday and yes we'll be back. It's just such a shame that they are letting this place go a bit!

author: neilludgate
title: think its a postcode lottery on the standard of accommodation
text: Just got back from 2 weeks at the FBC (25-07-12). Just read the 3 previous reviews, and our experience was the opposite. You pay for what you get, we didn't raise our expectations after the price we paid and previous reviews, but got a pleasant surprise. Although we had no air con, we hired a fan!, our apartment was one of the best we have stayed in. We had a 4 ringed hob, microwave, kettle, toaster and even an iron, and to top it off a fridge that worked (we had experienced broken fridges in the past). Maids came in twice weekly. We had booked a 2 bedroomed apt, got (no.47), we viewed the sea from our front door and pool from our balcony. Never had to fight for sunbeds, always available. I was informed that upgrades of the rooms is taking place, the upgraded rooms have the mod cons ( a family leaving the same day as us even had an oven), the unupgradedrooms not, that's why its a lottery as to the standard of your room. Downside is its not for kids, as Neil the rep told us, its for the older generation, there is nothing for kids to do. The walk down to the centre is pleasant, but coming back can be a struggle. The whole area needs a revamp, the fiesta centre is struggling. Chaplins is good for fish and chips! For the drinkers, great happy hours everywhere in the main centre, Windmill, el capitans, Lord Nelson. San Miguel 1.50 in some places. Recommend Meson Gallery (by kings arms) for Spanish food, sports tavern for Sunday roast, 6.90 with drink and ocean view in Atlantico centre for general food. Caleta has not changed since we first went their 5 years ago, and needs some money spent on it, still can't believe they have not extended promenade from main beach to the Sheraton hotel. All in all good holiday, but if went back would try and stay more central rather than up the hill.

author: RobOwen
title: Sooooo Peaceful!
text: First time I have stayed ‘up the hill’ in Caleta De Fuste. The good points. Well it was the cheapest on offer so good value. How peaceful. So quiet. No fighting over sun beds. The pool area so inviting and well designed. The on site pub the Zanzibar always seem to have some form of entertainment so no need to move far of an evening and the draught lager Amstel was the real McCoy, packed a punch. A nice clean and well run venue. We also took full advantage of the onsite restaurant Chez Moi very nice setting and good service. We stayed in the Beach Club which seemed to merge with the Elite Club. Our room overlooked the pool and had good sun you could see the sea from it, albeit a way off.. Rooms 50 to 80 seem to have a good outlook. The room seemed quite secure with double locks on the door. Not a bad size room and balcony. The only down side to it was it was in need of refurbishment regarding bath and kitchen area’s. Everything worked but tatty. However at the price we paid we didn’t let it bother us too much

author: Discover809647
title: Lovely holiday - would return!
text: After getting a really good deal and subsequently reading some dubious reviews, was a bit nervous about what to expect. However, no need to panic. The complex (Elite) Fuerteventura Beach Club/ Montecastillo were fine. Reception and Montecastillo was on one side of a road and Elite Fuerteventura Beach Club was on the other side, although facilities was available to use for all. Apartments on Montecastillo side were of slightly better quality (ceiling fans, really paintings – as apposed to faded Monte prints, and really wooden kitchen instead of MDF) – however none of this really mattered as it is all cosmetic –and seriously how much time do you spend in your apartment admiring the art…? Our apartment in Elite Fuerteventura Beach Club was in an excellent location – our patio was right next to the pool, which was great until we came back from the beach one afternoon to find an ignorant Spanish family sitting on it, who were quite put out we wanted to use our apartment and patio(!) Anyway, the apartment was equipped with iron, ironing board, kettle, toaster, coffee machine, hairdryer, fridge and 2 electric hobs. Pool towels were provided and anything you needed the hotel would do their best to accommodate. Cleaners came every 3 days or so. Cleaning just really making of the beds, empting the bathroom bin and cleaning of the floors. Hotel provided their own ‘welcome meeting’ and were very helpful and well informed. Overall there were 3 pools on site to use (cleaned every other morning), (Jacuzzi’s drained, sauna locked and gym chargeable), there were two pool bars (one in Beach Club, one in Monte Castillo), restaurant – Pizzas were amazing! Local supermarket just in front of the restaurant on the road, open until late (although not very well stocked) and a SuperDino chain supermarket across the road. There is a bar at the hotel that has live music and Kareoke. On the final day of your holiday, you are able to retain your pool towels to use the facilities until you leave. Reception will hold your luggage and you can shower downstairs (under reception) – they will give you clean towels – although they are hand towels, very much appreciated. Overall we were very happy with the accommodation and the price we paid. We would return without a hesitation. NB - check out reviews for Monte Castillio as this is the same complex (across the road) - so info on the complex (NOT ROOMS) may be useful!

author: mynosehurts
title: Cheap & comfy
text: Decent fully equiped apartments,abit rusty but cant complain due to price.electric hob,fridge,toaster,kettle. we didnt have a microwave but that is availuable. Lovely pool area (3 large pools around),staff,good zanzibar 1min away.Close to supermarket,nice short 10-15min walk to town where nice resturants,bars and shops can be found. The place is very peaceful and quite,good place for relaxing, but not for partyin! No near clubs whats so ever, better off staying in corralejo if thats what you want. Good excursions availuable,can be booked at reception or excursion shop in town but be sure to ask about facilities and shopping areas and where to go as you wont be told unless you ask. Downsides are: Twin beds are given for a couple,me n my partner put them together but stil managed to fall through! Blankets way too thin to sleep with as it gets cold at night and apartments have no heating!, Headboard hits the wall n makes noise with every breath or movement! really annoying! Had to resort to stuffing a sheet between wall n headboard and turning beds sideways! Very fustrating! Also pool not heated, way too cold! hardly any1 uses it! such a waste as its a beautiful pool! Also when we stayed the sauna and jacuzzi were switched off! :( All in all, a decent stay, only paid £100 for 2 ppl for 7days so cant complain. Not really for the young though, not enough entertainment and kinda gets boring in the evening...also not enough english channels on telly!.

author: craignotts1
title: Careful...!
text: Stayed for 3 nights of a 7 night holiday. Friendly reception staff. Pointed out on check in we wanted a quiet holiday. Was put about 7 meters away from Zanzibar night club,, its started at 11.30 - 2.30 am..! KARAOKE..! The bass was so much the glass was vibrating in the windows.. WARNING..! DO NOT take an apartment near that pub/club. We did get moved the next day however.. The apartments are VERY tired, rusty baths,loose wires, stained sofas, rusty fridge, the list goes on... oh!.. AWFUL beds Ask for extra blankets to pad them out a bit) The location is a 10 min walk from the center.. 15 mins back as its UP hill.. need to be fit.! HOWEVER... its cheap, pools are great with tons of sunbeds ect. When you check in, look at the site map and take NOTHING near the club..!

author: ge0rge2
title: Give it a miss, watch out for theft of money in your locked safe!
text: Room worse than basically equipped. Doors falling apart, locks missing. Beds stinking. Cockroaches. Fixtures and fittings worn out and in bad state of repair. Time share accomodation, stalked by rep at a welcome meeting. Safe has habit of opening and emptying itself whilst you're out and locking itself up afterwards! Pool has missing tiles. Jacuzzi not working through 2 weeks we were resident. If you like sleep ... forget it. Karaoke until about 3am - very loud and planes fly all night overhead (100 ft). Rooms only cleaned 3 times in 2 week stay. Pavements very dangerous with wooden planks dotted round to cover craters! Good fun if you like hopscotch but no good for kids or elderly. Place full of locals using facilities as open to anyone. No lifeguard or security guard. Staff friendly but when challenged about the state of the room they repeatedly reiterated you can get a better room if you pay more. Would not recommend or ever return there.

author: maddad55
title: Dont expect too much
text: The staff were really friendly and helpful but the resort, even the Elite part where we were booked, is very dated. When we arrived the occupants of our allocated room had not checked out so we could not get into the room! We were given another room but that was in a part of the resort that was being renovated. The room was fine but outside there were paving slabs missing and lots of digging going on to replace water pipes. I suppose an all year complex must get renovated at some time and we were just unfortunate to experience that. After 3 days however our plumbing in the bathroom started to come through the shower drain! Every time the toilet was flushed or the sink used it came up through the shower drain. To cap that off the electricity then failed when the shower was turned on which is apparently a common problem. We were moved to the next door room which was much better and survived the remaining holiday with no further problems. The complex has 2 pools and one was being renovated during our 2 week stay. They used sun loungers to block off the pool which meant there were not enough to use around the second pool. The Elite pool bar is supposed to be open until 9pm but it closed every day at around 5.30. The onsite restaurant, Chez Moi, is the worst place we ate during our fortnight. When you hear the pinging of a microwave shortly followed by the delivery of your food you know you are in trouble. Much better food is available in town. Our favourite was “El Patio” who cook fantastic steaks and paella and very generous sized complementary liquor after the meal. In short Caletta de Fuste is OK but the Elite Club leaves a lot to be desired. On a drive south to Jandia we found some fantastic beaches and should we ever go back to Fuerteventura then Jandia would be the place to go.

author: CATMONAS
title: Wouldnt go again !!
text: The resort looked great on arrival. 3 pools to use, the Elite being the best one. 3 bars in the resort - the Zanzibar has entertainment, the Elite Club has the Elite bar by the pool and the Secret Garden is a sunken underground bar with karaoke and discos most nights. This was the best, the staff and owners were friendly. Those are the good bits. When we arrived they had no record of our booking for 3 people. As we had all our paperwork they put us in an apartment which was great, 3 steps from the pools edge !!! But as the first of our 2 week holiday progressed, problems arose. No patio table or clothes dryer, broken toilet seat, split shower hose, no pots and pans, broken cutlery draw, mains plug socket stopped working after 2 days and ants everywhere - all around the loo, in the bath, kitchen - you name it !! We found out we were staying in the reps quarters !! We complained so many times, they moved us for our second week to the Elite Club part. On arrival much better, pool view again and gorgeous pool all lit up at night and from our balcony we had the view of the Zanizbar and stage so we could watch entertainment from there. But unfortunately the cockroaches in my bed freaked me badly and I ended up sleeping in the bedroom with my 2 friends on the last 2 nights. There were timeshare reps everywhere but we managed to escape their clutches and stray cats which were very friendly which I loved and had my favourite that visited me each day. The Chef lived next door to us and was lovely and treated us very well when he did a BBQ. All in all the Island is fantastic and this resort could be equally fantastic as all the staff were very helpful, the accommodation has let it down which is such a shame. I loved the way most of the bungalows over looked the pools it was beautiful. I would definitely return to Fuerteventura but probably not here.

author: Neil_Ellis
title: For £98 quid for a weeks rental, can you complain?
text: Went with a couple of mates for a chilled out week as needed to recharge the batteries!! Busy Summer!! Booked the flights, mytravel.com and appartment seperately, appartmentsabroad.com, paid £98 for the appartment for a week, Bargain!! 10 mins in a taxi from airport, 9 euros!! Would reccomend that instead of doing the package deals, check out the seperate things first.... Reception staff, bunch of ill trained, ignorant and down right unprofessional people. As we were not there on a timeshare as owners, we were treated as second class. Made to wait while they served 'owners' first. Billy the sales rep for the timeshare is pretty cool, for a scouser! and in no way did we feel there was a hard sell, We were asked if we wanted the tour, but kindly refused, end of! The appartment, was very, very tired, poor state of repair, broken patio door, broken bed, ants all over the bathroom and the odd cockroach or 4 descended during the week. Maybe leaving the patio doors open isnt a good idea!! Maid service, twice a week, not enough i would suggest. Pool is okay, even if its a tad salty, but the best thing is the MALIBU bar by the main pool. Katherin and her mother, Manchu are brilliant... looked after us brilliantly.. Free BBQ on a Friday, Free Paella on a Sunday, and happy hour from 3-7pm everyday!! PS, if you go tell them they need a new set of darts!! Overall, what can i say except, for £98 take the rough with the smooth!!

author: patrikoskarg
title: On the edge between 3 and 4
text: Room: The room was quite standard with comfortable bed, TV, 2 chairs, kettle, gratis tea and no carpets on the floor. The room was not so large but it had a huge chair that filled quite a bit of space. Not so many electrical contacts, I found just 3 of them. The room had a small fridge and safe. Bathroom was also not so spacious. The shower curtain was not clean (discolored). Soap, which was called "Prestige", had an intriguing (certainly not good) fragrance. Breakfast: Standard breakfast with cheese, ham, eggs etc. The french toasts with maple syrup was highlights at the breakfast. The good thing was a lot of space in the breakfast area. Location: Not far from tourist attractions like Latrabjarg, Raudisandur beach or Dynjandi waterfall. Right next to Patreksfjordur. The gas station is 100 meters from the hotel. Personnel: Nice and no complaints Overall experience: The hotel and room were clean, the last one maybe a bit too small, a bit less clean bathroom (shower curtain) and odd scent of the soap. Breakfast was absolutely OK. Pretty average experience. Price/what you get is slightly below average, a bit too pricey in terms of quality you get. Would I recommend this hotel? There are basically not many things that speak for or against this hotel. A fair alternative if you are close by.

author: MycroftAllan
title: Superior Room - great fjord view; restaurant excellent, good value for Iceland
text: Loved the location of this hotel in the small town of Patreksfjordur. We picked it for a two night stay to put us near to the Latrabjarg cliffs and it's a natural stopping off point on the way up to the Dynjandi falls and Isafjordur. Room and facilities were great - we had a lovely view of the fjords (there's the main road into Patreksfjordur just outside but it's not a through route). We ate in the hotel both nights. The hotel was very full (July) and the restaurant appeared full both nights, it was advisable to book when we got back each evening to make sure we had a table. I can understand non-residents not being able to dine if they just turn up in summer as has been mentioned elsewhere. The staff were very friendly and efficiently professional from reception to restaurant. Hotel tariff included free breakfast which was a good buffet. This is quite often a very expensive extra in Iceland so was a welcome help to our budget. Latrabjarg cliffs were about an hour away (most on an interesting gravel road - cliff hugging and mountain climbing and descending, very glad we had a good 4x4). The cliffs lived up to their reputation (calm sunny day) with puffins just standing around a couple of metres from you. From here we went to Red Sands beach (slightly more up and down grave road) which was a lovely relaxing beach with a great café on the front. All this could be done in a day and then you move on but it was quite nice to have a relaxing day and head back to the same hotel late afternoon for a chill out in the "small town". There's a very small supermarket less than a minutes walk from the hotel with limited products for re-supply if necessary (if you're heading to Isafjordur there are two big supermarkets there). Loved Patreksfjordur and the hotel for the peace and quiet and really gentle feel to being at the end of a road at the end of a peninsula. There's not a lot to do in town in the evening but walk down the side of the road next to the fjord - which was lovely. Other things we did in the area - Flókalundur - on our drive north we stopped here and walked up to Helluvatn, Quite steep climb but opportunity for a good couple of hours walking if you're passing that way (equally it's not far from the ferry port).

author: DaZ407
title: A rather disappointing experience
text: We traveled in Iceland for 2 weeks, and most of the accommodation we took was guesthouses or apartments. We did want, however, to stay once in a nicer hotel, and were willing to pay more for it - and therefore chose the Fosshotel, which according to the pictures and reviews seemed superb. It began with misunderstanding regarding the payment method - we asked them via e-mail before our stay if we can pay in cash in Euros, and we understood their answer as "yes" - but eventually we could just pay in ISK or credit card. Never mind. Then we got to our room. It turned out we were just in front of the laundry room, which was noisy and there were always things around it. Why such a new hotel can not make the laundry room in a place that will NOT disturb the guests? It is quite in the middle of the floor, so maybe other rooms can be also disturbed by it. Next, it turned out the shower was not sealed, so it was quite flooded after each shower, and also the faucet was problematic and you either had cold or very hot water. After all that we went a bit disappointed to bed, which was comfy. But then we saw the green light. Not Aurora Borealis, unfortunately it was a very cloudy night. Instead, there was sort of an emergency lamp in the room, which we couldn't turn off, that illuminated the room with a weak kind of UFOish-AuroraBorealish green light. It was quite a nuisance, as we like to sleep in a dark room. Was the abovementioned a "disaster"? surely not. But as the most expansive and new hotel we stayed at we had high expectations, which were not met (while other guesthouse and rental apartments met them easily) - so it was quite a disappointment. Some positive words must be also said, so: The hotel is very nicely decorated, there is an elevator (not something we saw a lot in Iceland), the breakfast was good, and we also ate there dinner at the 1 night we stayed and it was also quite good.

author: sifnartn
title: Good addition to hotels in the Westfjörds but not up to speed on several accounts
text: It is good to have an additional hotel option in the Patreksfjördur, ideal as a basis for exploring the south-west of the Westfjörds. The hotel offers good quality rooms but fails to deliver in some respects: - rooms are functional and modern but too small for a newly built hotel. A problem for many hotels in Iceland. - the overal cleanness of the rooms needs to be urgently improved. We found many hairs from other persons on the bedcovers, and the floors were not well cleaned - we had to request new covers and a decent vacuum cleaning. - dining in the restaurant is good quality but not cheap (though sadly in line with most in Iceland) - we recommend booking the half board option to save a bit on the price. - breakfast is of good quality and constantly refilled. - some of the hotel's furniture shows already signs of usage though the hotel was only recently opened. - demeanor of the staff varies wildly: some were very helpful and friendly, others could not be bothered or had a too high esteem of themselves and failed to deliver on the first rule of hospitality, which is to serve the customer well. - the wireless internet was very spotty and on of the slowest we have ever had in Iceland - when it worked. Full stop. Complained to the staff and they replied they were aware of it but could not solve the issue. - "parking" means a plot next to the hotel, which is partly unpaved and thus full of water in rain. It seems like the money run out to tarmac the parking after the hotel's construction. In short, some improvements are needed but should certainly be possbile. Fosshotel could look up to the Icelandair chain of hotels for some pointers as to how to improve.

author: Colin-Poole
title: As you'd expect for a Fosshotel
text: A modern Fosshotel on the edge of Patriksfjordur. You get the good standard you'd expect from a Fosshotel ... nice room, good food and a particularly good breakfast. My room was at the front with panoramic views over the fjord. However, being SW casing it was very hot from the sun. Opening the window was the obvious solution ... but the room was almost above the front door ... where the smokers gather ... resulting in an unpleasent odour from their fags. Later in the evening "smokers corner" was more anoying as they would tend to gather in two's or more and speak/shout !! A great hotel I'd be pleased to stay in again but I'd want a room at the back. I stayed for 2 nights ... on the first night a big coach party meant the getting breakfast before 08:30 was difficult. On the second night it was half full with independent travellers. There's a fuel station right next door to the hotel which is located on the (main) road into Parteksfjorder.

author: heron48
title: Very modern, very clean hotel
text: We toured the island over a 10-day period. And of all the places we stayed (different lodging everynight except one 2-night stay), this was the most modern and upscale facility. Everything in chrome and black. I see where other reviewers used the term "sterile" to describe the decor, I can see where they might say that, but for us it was more of a "modern" look and definitely more of a professional look. The dining room was fully booked so we could not have dinner there, but the receptonist did refer us to a great little restaurant that was an easy drive. We did have breakfast and had a great variety of hot and cold plates, typical Islandic/European. We were quite pleased with our rooms. Patreksfjordur is a great litte town to drive around, cited on a beautiful harbor. We had destroyed a tire on Road #612 due to all the pot holes and the receptionist provided great advice on a local Michelin dealer to get a new tire installed. In addition, you are about 30 miles from the Latrabjarg Cliffs, which were quite amazing, albeit quite wet and a bit chilly when we were there. If you do go that way, do allow for plenty of time and caution on Road #612 as we did ruin a tire due to the potholes. It's no fun changing a flat on that road in the rain! I did not enter a "value" as our stay was part of an awesome pre-paid package we purchased through Icelandic Tours. However, based on the other faciities we stayed, I'd guess this was probably the more pricey location. Not to say it was't worth it, as we were quite happy, and after roughing it a bit the previous two days at the Latrabjarg cliffs, the added comfort of this Fosshotel was appreciated.
