author: Rochester_NYTrunkman
title: A great new hotel in an area that needs more lodging.
text: This was the nicest hotel we stayed in in Iceland. The staff is wonderful. The rooms are modern, clean and very comfortable. The bathroom was the best one we had in Iceland. No leaky shower like most other places we stayed! They even have an elevator. Dinner was delicious and high quality. The waiter was excellent. It was on the expensive side though. However there aren't many choices in town. Breakfast was very good. Getting back to the staff, the guy at the front desk is a great. We asked him if there was a chance we might see northern lights and he said it was possible, but not likely. At 11:30 at night he rang our room and told us to go out front and see the northern lights. He apologized for disturbing us, but he noticed our room lights were still on so he figured we were up. THAT WAS SO NICE OF HIM! We got in our car drove just outside the town and away from the lights and were treated to an amazing aurora show. Thanks again.

author: TheQuietTravellerToo
title: New, clean lines, simple yet elegant.
text: We are on a one month Iceland tour, having been here two years ago for two weeks. All our arrangements were made by Nordic Visitor as part of a self drive tour, so, we don't know the specific prices for accommodation. Nordic Visitor, in their tour packages offer three types of accommodation and we booked comfort accommodation (private bathroom, "nice" hotels & guesthouses), breakfast is always included. This will be one of many reviews for this trip. COMPLAINT FIRST. They charge for Wifi. The front desk clerks are obviously uncomfortable with this since they probably get complaints from everyone. It is ludicrous that hotels in high tourist areas, where there is competition to charge for Wifi. Only Fosshotels do this. OK, now the good. Lovely new hotel, tastefully designed and built. Clean rooms. Not tiny. Generous breakfast. Chocolate in a bowl at the front desk. Overall very nice. Would have scored 5 if not for internet.

author: LvtrvlLA
title: Modern, efficient, corporate-like minus local charm and a few opening pains to work out
text: Pros: -Hotel is new (thus clean) and modern -Room space is well utilized -Cable tv -Great breakfast buffet included in our room rate. The breakfast staff are wonderful; personable, and professional. Too bad the front desk staff is the opposite. -The restaurant and small bar is compact, relaxed and modern looking. With cocktails going for USD $16 and food quite pricey (yes, everything is expensive in Iceland) we opted to dine out which resulted in one of the highlights of Patreksfjordur - discovering Stúkuhúsið café/restaurant. A short drive away from the hotel, it offers charm, ocean views and homemade cooking from a gregarious female proprietor. Definitely worth a visit whether to use the internet, have a great cup of coffee with desert or for a relaxing homemade dinner. -Parking is free and directly next to building -Great views -Good base location for exploring area including Latrabjarg bird cliffs and hot pools Concessions: -Newly opened, the front desk staff is in dire need of hospitality training (greeting guests properly, smiling, sufficiently answering questions & responding with more than a one word yes/no, etc.) Ditto housekeeping staff - nothing was replenished, including the towels we had left on the floor, nor cleaned, only slightly tidied & bed made. I'm confident all the kinks will be worked out in time. -Charges for internet. This was the only hotel we stayed at in Iceland that charged for internet. There is one complimentary guest computer in the lobby where you may access the internet but you are competing with all other guests for usage. Despite booking through booking.com we were not offered free Wifi so search for specials. -We were given a handicapped room, which was fine, however as there was no shower bay, the shower leaked all over the floor creating a mini swimming pool we tried to alleviate with towels (which weren't replenished) vs. tracking water throughout the room. -Expensive, as are all hotels in this area, & not sure value is in line with cost -What most stood out with us is while nice & new, overall we found the design and accommodations of this chain hotel lacking the charm of the area. Without looking out the windows, this hotel could have been in any major city in the U.S. It did not convey Iceland, or Westfjords. Being a chain, I'm not sure there is much that can be done to alleviate this however, it is a shame that this area got a new hotel which does not properly reflect all the beauty, culture & charm it has to offer.

author: Cal_TheHotelLover
title: Terrible 4 Stars Hotel with a decent rooftop pool
text: Booked this place over the NYE weekend for one night. From the photos the place looks decent with a great rooftop pool. However, the hotel looks run down from outside and my predictions were all true. I was appointed with a room that has a chipped ceiling, chipped cabinets and it comes together with a damp odor as well. Requested to change the room immediately and they able to appoint me with another within 30 minutes. The other room were “perfumed”. But at least the ceiling aren’t chipped. Nothing much to mention about the room. There’s no minibar, it’s a very ordinary hotel room with the basic amenities. The wifi isn’t working but I couldn’t be bother with it anymore. There aren’t any restaurant at the hotel for lunch and dinner. Only for breakfast. Only thing to mention about this property is the rooftop pool. The exactly term for “a pool with a view”. I will not come back again though, you can definitely get somewhere better with the rates they are asking. Bear in mind, this isn’t 2/3 stars Hotel.

author: AnaLaine
title: NO TOWELS 😳 And when do they change the bins??
text: The asset of this hotel is definitely the infinity pool. I must admit, I booked because of how good it looks in the photos. But yes, it is very pretty during the day and of course it's stunning at night! However, the service is bit ugghh. I booked a request of having a king size bed but what I got during the day was a twin bed 😳. So much for a special request. They offer me to come back the next day and ask the receptionist to get me a new room with a king size bed. What a hassle. Setting that aside, my first night, there were NO TOWELS! I had to ask and ask and ask for them to get me new towels. You would expect them to give you new towels everyday but I guess you have to remind them everyday 🙄. Anyway moving on, the location is okay, not too good but not too bad either. It's near Pudu Station which is about 6-8 minutes walk from the hotel. And from pudu you can pretty much go anywhere you want go. If you go for a walk just behind the hotel, you'll find a market where you can do grocery shopping if u need to. But there's also a lot of street foods located just in corner. Overall, if you want to see the infinity pool then go for it! Booked it! It's very pretty, but if u want the service, I suggest you stay somewhere else.

author: Worldtraveler1305
title: Self service hotel
text: Where do I start? From check -in until check - out the whole experience was traumatic, something I wouldn't wish upon my worst enemy. When we arrived at the hotel 2 receptionists were playing on their phones, completely ignoring us. After getting the receptionists attention I was giving my room key. The room was filthy. Towels, bed sheets and rubbish all over the floor. We were giving another room which had no toiletries, I went down to reception to ask for some basics. I was told be the receptionist that someone would bring toilet roll and some shampoo/body wash asap. After 90 mins of waiting I decided I couldn't waste any longer and so went out for the day. When I returned to the hotel almost 6 hours later we still had no toiletries, I phoned reception twice before someone finally gave me a toilet roll and a hand soap at reception. I had to ask every day of our stay for toiletries to be replaced, they weren't. I asked reception on day 2 for some shampoo and he laughed at me and told me that they don't provide any. Our room was also not serviced/cleaned once during our 4 day stay and so I found myself going to the local 7/11 to by some shampoo, as well as taking out the bins. I raised concerns about the lack of toiletries to reception several times until one receptionist told me his job was to manage reception, not to deal with guests complaints. The security guard who works by the pool is the only positive point about this hotel. The rest of the staff that I had the misfortune of meeting were extremely uninterested, inept and simply didn't care. I have emailed the manger of the hotel to express my concerns about the lack of service (none) which are offered by D'majestic Place by swiss garden but she has yet to reply to me. Avoid at all costs unless you want to spend most of your holiday asking for basics such as toilet roll. 4 star? not a chance.

author: whatevermeandyou
title: First Timer
text: New chic hotel in town you need to visit, worth the money tho. It might quite far to walk to main center, but who care? Just get uber or grab, right? The room design is good with new modern minimalist style. The problem is one of my pillow stink so bad, i put it on the floor anyway to void the smell. The main problem is the one who checked us in at the reception. I couldn't remember his name. Indian guy with specs. He is not even greets us? He was busy with his phone, even on checking in process. I need to remind him about my credit card, since he is busy with his whatsapp. Its 6pm there is no queueing guest. Why don't just put your phone for awhile and finished the process?? Big NO for his attitude. You should hire better person with better attitude for your service standard, seriously.

author: 114ievau
title: What a fantastic place to stay in KL with a fantastic view!!!
text: Wow! This is the right place to stay to enjoy your time in KL!!! BIG thanks to Mrs. Paula and her team (specially Sharon at the reception). Mrs. Paula knows what real hospitality is all about!!! So friendly and helpful!! I got upgraded to a studio room which is simply amazing! It was like mini apartment. Wow! The view from my window was worth 10 points as well as the view from the roof top infinity swimming pool! The gym is very well equipped, pool clean and well maintained. Location is great, easy to reach the center, as well lots of local life restaurants and shops just behind the building. In a conclusion this place is highly recommended!!! If I ever will be back to KL I would stay only in D'Majestic Place by Swiss Garden!!! THANK YOU!!!

author: hazrulhussin
title: A Marvellous Unplanned Last Minute Trip
text: The price we paid and the room we had was Excellent! It was a clean and beautiful room with a touch of modern design but it was a bit small which was fine since we need it just to stay for a night after a long travel from east coast. The toilets are only covered by tempered glass walls which was nice and sexy. But not if you are sharing with a guy (lol). It was a cozy night sleep. The beakfast does area does not have any view as it is surrounded by guests room at level 6. however, there is an open deck at the same level which was nice. The choice of food for breakfast was very minimal though but luckily it wasn't that bad on the taste. The view on the infinity pool was awesome mostly on KL city. The staff was very friendly and will greet you with smile all the time. The setback was that, if you drive an MPV or any big car, be sure to be very careful as you go by the parking lot as it has a very (very very) narrow turn to go up or down. Our room was on the 9th floor. we did request for much higher floors but sadly it was a full house. The view we had from the room also not so good one as it was facing the other side of the city. Be sure to request higher level rooms with a view facing the KLCC / KL Tower. Overall, we had a nice stay and wouldn't mind to come again next time to try out other amenities which we didn't have the time to do so on our previous trip. It would be a pleasant stay for those who wants to go to the KWC (Kenanga Wholesale City as it is a walking distance of 5-7 minutes away and the LRT is only 5 minutes away from the hotel.

author: patilprasanna2003
title: Luxury hotel best priced... Infinity pool... Awesome
text: Hotel is close to berjaya times Square. D'Majestic is new hotel all modern amenities... Furniture neat and tidy... It's ditto same what is shown in their pics. I got a hotel chic room had a great view from room. The room has all amenities microwave washing machine fridge all stuff... The room has partition door also if you are 2 couples you can share the hotel chic room. Good for family. Hotel has Infinity pool on roof top. It's an heaven for sun bathing people and people like who loves pool and great open view... I was deciding between berjaya hotel and this one... And glad I choose D'Majestic... I was out for 12 nights stayed here for 2 nights... This hotel was top in neat and tidy with modern furniture. Hotel is near to all the places. Superb.

author: ykh_malaysia
title: Excellent modern hotel in old KL area
text: Other than the slow check-in process, the overall stay had been excellent. We stayed in a 2-bedroom suite which actually comprises of a Junior Suite connected to a separate studio suite room. Both bedrooms are very spacious, and the beds are big and comfortable. Both rooms have kitchenettes, and the sitting room is large and the dining area is big to fit 6 people comfortably. Rooms at the higher floor provide good views. The open swimming pool on the top most 20th flr is certainly a must-go. It is large, clean and the views are just fantastic! The gym at the side of the pool is open 24-hrs and is large and clean, and the equipment are new and function efficiently. There are many security personnel around to make you feel safe staying there. The area around the hotel is a complete opposite of the modern-feel of the hotel. It still is the old KL of the late 80 to 90s. You can find plenty of good and cheap local foods, especially Chinese. Forget about eating in the hotel, instead explore and try different authentic local foods everyday for your breakfast, lunch, dinner and supper, even morning and afternoon coffee/tea. There is also a hawkers' food lane nearby which is about 5 mins walk away. It is open daily from 6pm till late night. It is also about 15 mins walk to KL's main shopping area, Bukit Bintang.

author: thamy629
title: Amazing Stay
text: Prior booking with this hotel, we are already aware of its surroundings and what to expect from it so while some travelers may think is old, not tidy or clean enough but we felt that is what makes the area 'unique'! A lot of local, authentic delicacies can be found there (regardless you are looking for breakfast, lunch, dinner or supper) + a really old-school huge wet market is nearby (within waling distance of 10~15mins). We are a group of 4 and stayed there for 3 nights. From the moment we check-in till check-out, we are a very happy + almost 100% satisfied group of people. The staffs there are very good, helpful, friendly and almost very efficient. Why almost efficient? Well, the housekeeping can reacted a bit more faster when we needed something but that is just a small matter since we are not in a hurry (luckily) when we made those requests to them. Other problems we faced would be the aircon in room 1909 (where these is a huge living room + dining room + kitchen) is not working well as the room isn't cool enough especially in the day time even we had adjust high speed + cool air + lowest temperature mode. Next cons will be the WIFI in the whole apartment as it is not only slow but always lost connection - hope that can be improved. We have no such such WIFI issues when we stay in other Kuala Lumpur hotels. Now the positive things to look out for - the 20th level's gym (24 hours), pool (7am to 10pm daily) + the complimentary steam bath and sauna (both were located inside the washrooms - not sure of the operating hours and the staffs there can help to switch them on for you when you need to use it)....all very good functionally and that level has awesome views too! You may also bring your own drinks + snacks to enjoy the night views there. Not to be missed! The 2-bedroom apartment we had styed is spacious, clean and tidy with some modern features in it. Basic utensils are provided in the kitchen area and there is a microwave + a washing machine there too. A stove is provided too but no pots & pans are placed there though. In general, the hotel is full of positive vibe to me and i guess also due to it's still new (just 1 year or so since it's opening). Surely I will be back when the next family gathering trip to the same city next year! Keep up the good work and hope the management can do their best to maintain the hotel well + improve in areas being highlighted by guests too. Cheers!

author: garydP9229MY
title: Booked Private Residence
text: Currently staying at this property. This is a mixed hotel/private investors development which majoritarily operates as a hotel by the Swiss Garden group. We booked a private residence through AirBNB as we are having an extended stay at the property which worked out to be more cost effective. Its a relatively new and therefore modern hotel offering the usual facilities. Please note that I cannot comment on the hotel facilities in the main as we do not use housekeeping, front office or restaurant facilities at all. The highlight of the property is undoubtedly the rooftop infinity pool and deck on level 20. A very nice clean snd good sized pool which affords a great view over the surrounding area of Pudu, The Golden Triangle and KLCC. Shame there is no bar facility as yet on this level. Particularly nice view at nightime. Gym facilities also seem to be good and are popular. Having had a good look around it appears that other than minor personalised modifications by our owner, the rooms are all of the same style and standard. Ours is a one bed unit and is a very good size. Only complaint in our room is the bed! It is very hard and a perhaps suits the Asian clientele more than us. Overall, this hotel does attract a majoritary of Asian residents. Its in a good location and walkable to Berjaya Times Square and the other malls and attractions of The Golden Triangle. Lots of restaurants and food options, shopping and massage around and about and a 15 minute walk to Ikea Cheras. Uber rides are good value and readily available in this area if you use the app.

author: MelvinFoong
title: Wonderful
text: Beware of this hotel. Once you stepped in, you would not want to go home. I stayed here with my partner for a week. It is a new trendy. Check in process by the front office staff was brisk. We stayed in the Studio Chiq, a moderately big room for both of us. Facade of the building was a tad mediocre but stepping into the hotel lobby was a totally different. A total Swiss Garden's signature. The scent in the hotel lobby was soothing and relaxing, and not too over powering. Room decor was modern and chiq. Very comfortable bedding and furniture. Breakfast was norm, but dinner is to die for. In the vicinity, there are abundance of hawker's delight and street food to indulge your palate. If you prefer shopping, the hotel also provide scheduled shuttle services to the famous Bukit Bintang, or you can always take the scenic route of Malaysians public transportation. Bus station is right in front of the hotel. Pool in the evening to watch the sun set is to die for, but if you are a morning person and not afraid of the cold, a morning swim with Petronas Twin Tower in the background would be the ultimate Instagram'worthy picture. All in all, I do not want to go back!

author: tingt206
title: Bad service ever!!! Won't come again
text: Book for 5 night at studio chic type. When we arrive they give a room which is not as we expect as seen on photo in their website. They give us one part bedroom of "suite with two bedroom" type. Of course it is not as big as "studio chic" type. Later they give change to studio chic. But very angry I have to see that condition of room. Not even have a sofa in the room, but full of table and chair where you can put yout computer to work. I came to kualalumpur with family. This is not room for family, this room is like for working. I ask for change again. But what they said : " we're very sorry right now all of staff in the middle of meeting with director, so nobody can help to prepare for your room" WHAT??? I wait again for 5 hours, they didn't give any respond yet. So very DISAPPOINTED. Don't ever came to sleep here. So Fake with their photo.

author: Lone_journey
title: Far from expectation
text: Could really do better. Stayed at Luxe room for two nights. The mattress was too hard and no way near comfortable. Rooms at 6th floor are too noisy because they are facing the Pudu Road, which is famous for its super heavy traffics. Hot water supply unstable. Water pressure low at certain time. WIFI? What WIFI? It never work for me. Room was not very clean even after the housekeeping works. Pipe music outside the room through the night was really a nuisance. Car park entrance and its ramps are too narrow and difficult to negotiate, especially at the corners. However, a plus point for its very friendly and helpful staff. From the reception to the housekeeping. Obviously they are being well trained by Swiss Garden. All in all, this hotel, with its premium rate, is not up to the Swiss Garden standard. I can easily find a better one with half the price in this area.

author: kons168
title: Near to train, near to great food, noisy and small room
text: We reached the hotel around evening 6 pm, there were only one front desk staff who were busy on the phone. So we were forced to wait close to 15 minutes, before he managed to entertain us. Considering we are the only one trying to check-in at that time, the waiting time is not tolerable at all. The hotel rooms seems all facing outside, so you will not get a room with no window view. The bed is on the hard side and the pillow is just nice. The bathroom shower only comes with overhead rainshower type and not hand shower option. The WC is located separately from the bath area which is great. The hot water is very consistent and it will be good if they can keep this up. 2 bottles of complimentary water is given daily. Car parking is complimentary for hotel guest for now, could be chargeable in the future as I can see security boom gates being constructed. WIFI internet is provided complimentary (need to get login from the front desk). Not much TV channel choices provided and the working desk located directly beneath the air cond vent so working on the desk for a long time gets really cold. Location wise, nearby you can get a lot of food courts with many food choice available. Walk a bit further and you can reach the famous street food in Pudu (Wai Sek Kai). The train station is located opposite the street, which is behind the shops. At night the area will be a bit dark so have to be careful. Distance to nearest Mall (Berjaya Times Square) will be a bit far, so it is either you can take a cab there or take the train to another station nearer to the mall. As this time we got a room facing the main road, there are traffic noise late at night or early in the morning. Not sure if higher floor will face the issue but we are staying on the 8th floor.

author: CYS001
title: New hotel at Pudu
text: I stayed for 2 nites in D'Majestic. The hotel is located about 100m walking distance from Pudu LRT station. The walking alley to the hotel is dark at nite. Check in was fast and friendly. Staff are keen to help and efficient. Corridor to the room is non-aircond. The room is modern and clean. Toilet washing area is open concept which is unusual for Asian. Can felt very cold after coming out of the shower. Toilet rack design was out of reach as the rack is fitted at the end of the washing area counter. Swimming pool area is uncovered and not guarded. Therefore, I did not try the pool. Breakfast area was deserted and we ventured out to the shops behind the hotel, which are aplenty with Chinese, Malay and Indian eateries. Sometimes can hear loud music at night from the shops below. Overall, I enjoyed my stay at the hotel. Get to go to my designated places using the LRT. However, I felt that the room should be valued at less than RM180/nite.

author: PatrickChai
title: A bit waste , disappointed
text: I saw a New Hotel and a very special rate , decide by Urself after staying, Rm50, Rm100, Rm 150 and Rm 278. This is very good marketing strategy and I decided to try! 1st impression so good and nice, location ok , parking perfect with good security guard. Customer service with good smile, I ready to pay Rm278 coz can get a free stay for next visit. But after check in I found that , all not ready yet for launching , maybe next time will be better but already waste this marketing strategy coz I just pay Rm50 and I think I better choose others hotel for my next visit . 1st - Customer Services , smiling is good but not enough experience to handle. 2nd - Room problem (No electri) I have been change 3 times to get my room and I need to take from ground to 10 th floor , then 10th floor to ground, repeat and repeat to get my room card. 3rd - lift .. Why they need to scan card to get to hotel floor since the card can't be use, lift totally hanged! finally take a lift without card scanner at behind, but wat purpose their apply this ?? If say security they got special lift, !!! Waste 4th - Rooftop -- view is perfect , nice swimming pool , perfect bar, but nothing can use coz nobody there- WASTE 5th - dining 6 floor , another Waste -- no food and even no ppl over they, wat is called restaurant?? Guest need go outside to find some food, then the lift can't even use , haha funny. Really wasted , should be improve and can be improve, coz room is nice, rooftop is relaxing, location is good , staff can be train. Maintenance and be upgraded.. Overall can stay is pay Rm50 - Rm150 But the publish rate is Rm630 for Luxe Room. At this moment the price is over and not this rate. Finally hope Swiss garden can see my review and upgraded for others Guest, coz every journey is important for our traveller. Good luck

author: PeterHillsLewes
title: Adequate and clean
text: Stayed here three nights as part of a tour from UK. As a single I expect smaller rooms on tour. The size of this room (201) was fairly average compared to others I have stayed in but I found the bed was very low and was placed on a frame or similar which was larger than the mattress. See picture. The bed also has a large shelf at the head (see picture) meaning it was extending well into the room leaving little room to get past. The bed side tables were set back too meaning they had to be pulled out from a small alcove to access them. Bedside lights were also at the back of this alcove meaning you couldn't turn lights on/off without getting out of bed. The oversized frame presented a real hazard for stubbing toes. Speaking to other tour members it seemed that these things weren't an issue so guess it is just this particular room and is one to be avoided. The room itself was clean and comfortable and the bed (whilst too low) have a good night's sleep. This particular room looked out onto the main road but I wasn't overly troubled by traffic noise with the double glazing. Air conditioning worked well and was reasonably quiet meaning it could be left on overnight. Evening meals were included on tour and this was a fixed menu served in the basement restaurant. Food was adequate but nothing took get excited about. Service was quick and efficient. Breakfast was in a separate room on first floor and was of a buffet type with a reasonable selection of cold meats, cereals, rolls, sweet pastries and also bacon and scrambled egg which were fine but virtually cold despite being in what appeared to be heated containers. Overall an adequate hotel, but based on my particular room not worthy of four stars.

author: 315krishac
title: Excellent hotel - would definitely recommend
text: We stayed at this hotel for a week. We wanted something out of the hustle and bustle of Barcelona but something which wasn't completely isolated, and this was definitely the place. Great location, only about a 20 minute walk to Badalona beach and a 10 minute walk from the metro station- where you can grab a train which run often until midnight everyday apart from Saturdays where it runs all night. Extremely handy if you're heading for a night out in Barcelona. We purchased t10 tickets which cost us €9.95 and allows for 10 journeys. Even gets you to the airport! Hotel was clean and staff were extremely helpful and friendly. We were very tired the night we arrived and ordered room service. Food was superb and very reasonable for what we got! Roof top terrace is not all it made out to be but it didn't bother us too much as we spent most of our time exploring Barcelona. The breakfast in the morning offered a nice selection of cereals, juices, pastries, cakes, cold meats, cheese and fruits. Even had hot breakfast food including mushrooms, bacon, sausages and eggs. What more could you ask for. This is hotel is great for a short break away from the hustle and bustle of Barcelona or even if you want to stay and explore Badalona. The beach was clean and not too crowded and the city centre was a pleasure to walk around. Would definitely come back again. Thank you

author: Isla9876
title: Good hotel
text: We stayed at this hotel for 6 nights from 29/4/17. Really good hotel with a lovely room. The hotel is a 15 minute walk from the metro and the L2 line takes you straight into the middle of Barcelona, which takes around 20 minutes. Our room was cleaned with fresh bedding and towels daily - which was nice to come back to after a long day out exploring Barcelona. Our room had a mini fridge (excellent as kept water and juice very cool) along with a safe too. Only disappointment was the bar/terraced area. We were under the impression the bar was on the terrace however there is not one up there, only one on the ground floor which is very small, limited and quite expensive. This was a shame as due to the times the metro closes at and if you didn't want to pay for a taxi from Barcelona, you'd be back at your hotel by around 11.30pm each night. So a drink on the terrace would have been enjoyable. All the staff were friendly apart from the one staff member that dealt with us whilst checking out. Barely spoke to us and didn't even ask if we had a nice stay. We were then charged a fee for 'room tax' which I now understand is something that was introduced by the government. We don't mind paying for this however a warning when booking or at the beginning of the stay would have been nice to know that we would have to pay 12 euros at the end of our holiday. I know this is not much but when you only keep a small amount of euros for the airport this wasn't great. If we had been advised of this at the beginning of our stay we could have made sure we kept this aside. Other than these small issues, a pleasant stay at Rafaelhoteles Badalona!

author: 215rianaj
title: Best Badalona hotel with some limitations
text: This hotel is NOT in Barcelona. That could be a positive if you are trying to avoid crowds and value your sleep quality. It is about a 10-15 minute walk to the train station that takes you to the Center of Barcelona. Badalona, however, is a very charming place with lots of good quality restaurants, lots of ambiance, shopping, beach, running, biking, roller blading... in general, a nice town to walk around. The hotel itself is nice and modern. The rooms are basic but comfortable. The sheets and towels are always clean. When you look at the wallsame you can see signs that the hotel is a bit Old, with wall paper starting to come off at the very edges or some old dirt in the corners of the bathrooms ceiling. That been said, it is still the best hotel in Badalona. The fodder at the restaurant is excellent. The restaurant and hotel personal are polite and helpful...although sometimes a bit slow. For example I asked for a hair dryer as the one in the room wasn't working. 2 hours later they still had not delivered the item. There is a wonderful deck with chairs and a view on the 14th floor. I don't think most people know about this as it was always empty while I was there. I had it all to myself!

author: kushi1963
title: Great hotel. A bit far from Barcelona.
text: The hotel is located in Badalona so if you want to visit Barcelona you have to use public transportation. The most recommended transportation is the Metro. It taked 30 minutes to get to the center of Barcelona. There is a train leaving every few minutes. The hotel is approximately 15 minutes walk from the Metro. The hotel looks nice. The reception people are polite most of the time and willing to help. The rooms are not too big but very clean and with a modern look. We stayed in the 7th floor. The noise from the street can be heard specially in the morning. If you have a rented car take into account that the hotel parking is very expensive. In terms of restaurants nearby don't expect too much. Most of the time they are closed and when they are open the food quality is not very good. Breakfast is great! Good variety and quality of food served in a clean and big space capable of accomodating many people at once. We had a surprise with the bathroom door that is made of glass and you don't have too much privacy.. Overall we enjoyed our staying and recommend this hotel.

author: Londongirl50423
title: What a hotel, it made the whole trip worthwhile. Fantastic!!
text: We were allocated this hotel as part of a groupon deal, and at first was dubious because of the distance from Barcelona. However from the moment we arrived, we realised that we were onto a winner and everything would be fine after all. The hotel is extremely nice and very contemporary in style. The staff all know what they are doing and nothing seems too much trouble. Our room was high but we could see the sea, also quiet. Lots of nice toiletries, the bed was high and very comfortable. It came with black out curtains, a nice touch we thought. The restaurant was down a flight of marble steps below the reception floor and was tastefully decorated. There was just a sense of calm and tranquility that evaded everywhere and helped you to de-stress and relax comepletly. The breakfasts came as part of our package and were delicious with many choices. We also ate in the restaurant in the evening and were not disappointed. The beach was about a 20 minute walk and the metro station approx. 30mins. It was all signposted well and we found our way around very easily. When we returned to the hotel after a busy day, we sat on comfy sofas while a lovely waiter brought us large glasses of wine and nibbles. We felt extremely pampered and didn't want to leave on the last day. You will not go wrong with this hotel. They cater for your every need.

author: 486JohnO
title: Excellent
text: What a wonderful surprise this hotel was. We decided to try Badalona, so that we were close to Barcelona, but also near a beach. We usually stay in Eixample area of Barcelona. It was a great decision as the metro was only 10 minutes from the hotel, and the beach 15 minutes. The metro to Psg de Gracia took a mere 15 minutes direct. The hotel is modern, spotlessly clean and very welcoming. The staff were without exception charming and very helpful. We had a junior suite booked, and it was wonderful, with a separate sitting room, and a shower room, and also a further large room with a wonderful spa bath. There were always ample towels, and good toiletries, and the sheets were changed every day. The minibar was super efficient, and the bar was always happy to supply ice if required.The breakfast was very good, with a great choice of cold and hot items and a very efficient coffee machine. Don't let the hotels position close to the motorway put you off. Try to get a room on the higher floors, and you will hear no noise ( we were on 15th ). I simply could not find one fault in this hotel. It was fantastic, and it will be our favoured hotel on return trips to Barcelona. Can't wait for the next time!!

author: CathB360
title: Modern hotel, great location
text: Stayed here in May 2013. Decor is modern, very clean and comfortable. Location is brilliant if you are happy to use the metro/hire car. Lots of excellent restaurants on the sea front within a short walk away, as well as cafes, food and clothes shops. The Catalunian mountains are a short drive away. Barcelona is about 15 minutes by car. I would recommend Badalona as a good base for exploring the area is transport is great, bar/restaurant prices in were cheaper than Barcelona and it wasn't as touristy at all. The room was really good, nice big window, not much of a view but kept all the traffic noise out. Minibar was handy to remove all the hotel stock and use it to store our own food for picnics. TV had a few English channels. Hair-drier was a bit lacking in power but did the job. Shower was amazing! Staff were really friendly and helpful. Car parking is expensive but secure. Can't review food as we didn't eat there but all in all, a great hotel, would visit again.

author: honador
title: Would not recommend this hotel to anyone...
text: Me and my partner stayed in this hotel from the 13th to the 20th, due to its location outside of the city and having read numerous reviews about its overall look and feel. My suggestion to anyone considering staying here is simply, don't. Our room was broken into on our first night and the room safe was smashed into pieces with the intention of stealing all our money. I had exchanged money at the hotel reception and we were either being watched by another guest or someone not staying and the hotel, however, our conclusion was that this must have been an inside job. Luckily they got away with nothing as we (luckily) did not leave our money in the room safe and my suggestion to anyone considering leaving valuables in your room is don't, having seen how easy it was for someone to break into the room safe. The hotel was unable to explain how someone may have been able to break into the room and made us feel like WE had intentionally done this. WE were made to feel like the guilty party, with their only response being "This have never happended before...". The police were called, but we were never consulted and were not provided with any updates throughout the rest of our stay. We were offered an upgrade, which we accepted, as we did not want to cut our stay short, nor could we afford to find alternative accomodation. Housekeeping left our room door open on 2 seperate occasions and even left the bedroom window open, not such an issue as our new room was on the 15th floor. Following the incident, the staff were rude, unhelpful and generally looked down on us as I can only assume they still thought we had something to do with the break-in. There is no security at the hotel, pizza delivery people are given free roam of the hotel and we generally felt un-safe for the rest of our stay as the hotel were unable to provide an explanation in regards to the break-in. I requested the details of the general manager to make a formal complaint, which weren't provided to me. I have issued a complaint letter to head office which as yet has not even been acknowledged. Badalona itself is a lovely town, full of lovely friendly people, lovely restaurants and bars and the beach itself is a lot nicer than Barcelona beach. If you are considering staying in Badalona, find an alternative hotel to this one...the Hotel Miramar on the sea front looked quite nice, for a 3*.

author: Zeppo11uk
title: Good base for out of town travellers
text: We stayed for a long weekend 17-19 August. Transfer from Airport to Passieg de Gracia is approx 20 mins via Renfe train. Buy the 2 day green travel pass from tourist info at airport upon arrival. Change at PDG onto the purple L2 metro, lots of stairs, escalators up and down, long corridors, can be a bit confusing but Metro punctual. Travel from PDG to L2 Badalona terminus is another 20-25 mins. If you take the tram it also shows that it stops at Badalona but this is much further away than the metro Badalona- be warned if you have heavy bags as it would be a half hour walk to hotel. From the metro its 10 mins max. ** Check you are looking at the correct Badalona stop on the underground style map, you need the purple line for the hotel. Due to holidays no restaurant which we previously knew about but also no bar. "closed for holidays" said reception but it wouldn`t have been a major task for them to pull 2 San Miguels into a glass.!! Rooms are very modern, no complaints but other comments about water coming out of shower are correct but not a biblical flood as some have said. Breakfast is continental and while not advertised as "all you can eat", you can stuff yourself. Hams, pastries, toast etc etc . Reception quoted a taxi as costing about €20 to get to central Barcelona but we got from there to La Sagrada for €13. Loads of places to eat and local bars when you walk down towards Badalona beach, theres two Frankfurter shops, a pizza place but then at the beachfront a goddamn Macdonalds. You can drink at the seafront bars inside but they all have their own seating area on the promenade. Its waitress service and you need to wave at them to get their attention otherwise you will wait for an eternity as tables are packed in tight. Avoid the Austrian taverna at all costs as they don`t have enough staff, they forget your order and you`ll never get served - awful. If you want a cheap-ish out of town hotel with good travel connections this is ideal.The motorway noise is not really noticeable, you are looking at approx half an hour to the main Barcelona centre and all you need is nearby - bars, pharmacy, cafes, restaurants

author: SJMO1
title: A Great Stay in Badalona
text: Stayed here July 28th - Aug 4th booked at short notice having read all the reviews - which were very accurate and useful! Whole holiday worked really well for us. Loved 'feel' of Badalona, particularly the promenade and narrow shopping streets. If you don't mind a few 10-15 min walks to beach, shops, Metro or mainline station then hotel position is fine. Hotel was clean and comfortable. Found the reception staff friendly and v helpful. Room was average size on 7th floor. Wardrobe space fairly limited. Our bathroom was enclosed not one of the glass partition ones (which I would not have liked!). Motorway noise was not a problem. Thought buffet breakfast was really good 7.30 - 10.30 daily. Tended to use the Metro to get into Barcelona rather than mainline train, but you could use either. Found both v easy and safe to use. Def buy T10 ticket as it's excellent value. Spent time on beach at Badalona - busy but great and on several Barcelona beaches. Would recommend both the hotel and Badalona as excellent value for money. From airport caught mainline train R2 to Clot and then Metro (purple line L2 i think?) to Pompeu Fabra in Badalona - v easy and covered by T10 ticket.

author: LeeR846
title: Pleasant enough
text: Stayed 4 nights at this hotel as we went to the moto GP in Catalunya. The hotel is relatively new and stands 15 floors high. Situated next to a motorway in a residential area of Badalona, 20 mins away from Barcelona to the west. The view is not the best, we were on the 14th floor and could just about make out the coast. The motorway is constantly busy until the early hours, although surprisingly noise from the motorway was not really a problem. We stayed in a double room which was well furnished. Big bed, decent shower and toilet all seperated by smoked glass partitions. The mini bar is outrageously over priced, as to be expected really, so we did not go any where near it. (€3.50 for a packet of chewing gum). Breakfast is a continental style buffet serving sliced local meat, salami, cheese, fresh fruit, pastries, toast, yoghurt, fruit juice, tea, coffee and a spanish spin on the english breakfast were all available between 0700-1030 hrs during the week. Parking was probably my biggest gripe with this hotel. Charging €15.00 (Inc 8% tax) a day, it cost me €60.00 to park for 4 nights. so just be aware of that when budgeting. Overall, a pleasant hotel, clean rooms with comfy beds, serving a good breakfast. The centre of Badalona is only a 10 minute walk away to the sea front, restaurants and shops. No pool and no Spa.

author: mirnaaa87
title: Great hotel
text: We stayed from 19th till 26th May, it is a very good hotel located in Badalona. We were a group of 7 girls so we have 2 twin rooms and 1 triple room. The triple room was identical to the twin room but had an extra folding bed in it which made it very tight for space. There was not much privacy regarding the bathroom.. we called it the 'see through' bathroom it was not a separate bathroom and literally a class door before the actual bedroom and the only privacy you had was a curtain to separate them. I am not sure if this is a European thing but this was not ideal for us. Despite that, these are the only things I could really fault and that is me being critical! The shower was great, the hair-dryer was great. I know some people were saying it is not strong.. I would have to disagree with that. The room was cleaned on a daily basis and was left in a great state, our clothes were even folded and put on our beds! We did not have a kettle facility in our room but we ended up buying a small one and that served us fine. The breakfast was probably the highlight, it was a buffet and had different things nearly everyday. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The staff at reception were extremely helpful and patient with us. It was great to know that there was free use of computer and also free printing facilities which I know a lot of hotels would jump at the chance of charging you an arm and a leg for that. The hotel itself is a short walk from the Underground station, we got the 5 day pass which served us perfectly. If you do not want to walk from the underground station to the hotel, there is a taxi rank near the hospital and it costs around 3 euros for a journey there. I would definitely recommend this hotel as it had everything we were looking for and more!

author: bexindevon
title: Great hotel!
text: Me and my boyfriend stayed in this hotel last week for 4 nights. We did ask for a double room, but got twin beds - but this is pretty much the norm in Europe anyway! We got this hotel for approx. £60 a night including breakfast, so for what we paid, we were very happy. Our room was on the 15th floor and had amazing views over Barcelona, we oculd even see the Sagrada Familia in the distance! The hotel is well appointed (although, their hairdryer is rubbish, bring your own if you are used to a powerful hairdryer!), and spotlessly clean. The rooms are cleaned and made up every day, and you can choose if you want fresh towels every day or not. The breakfast was very good with a variety of meats, cheeses, fruits, cereal, toast and a few cooked options every day (as well as tea/coffee/water/juices etc.!) The hotel is about a 10-15 minute walk from the Metro station, which takes you right into the centre of Barcelona. We bought a 3 day ticket which cost about £15 which covered all of our transport for the time we were there - well worth the money! Not only the Metro a fast reliable method of transport, it is also very regular (only having to wait a couple of minutes for any train), and very clean. Badalona is at the end of L2, which meant that in the mornings you were guaranteed a seat on the metro! Badalona itself is a nice town, it seemed very friendly, and although we travelled at the beginning of May it did seem that it was still slightly out of season. But as the Metro runs until something like 5am, you can stay in Barcelona for the nightlife! The beach at Badalona is nice too, is it a bit grainy, but I think that is pretty typical of The Med's beaches! Overall I'd highly recommend this hotel, friendly English speaking staff, and good quality rooms, go and have fun in Barcelona!!

author: JamesD85
title: 'local' area with a short walk to Metro and 10 minutes from the coastline
text: Rafaeleshoteles is a quirky contemporary hotel with friendly and helpful staff. The location is average, depending on the room you may get mountains, buildings, sea view or all 3! The hotel appears to be directed at businessman but don't be put off, although the rooms are not overly big it is clean and comfortable. The bathroom joins the bedroom and maybe not private enough for some but turn the tv up and you'll be fine ha ha!! Shower is lovely and big. Just check your mini bar when you arrive, if you don't intend to use it just be aware what's there; hotel tried to charge for nuts... Only one pack on arrival and then another pack appeared! The hotel is in Badalona... Quite a local Spanish area, supermarkets near by, coast 10 mins walk away through the streets and metro is easy to find... 10/15 mins walk. Metro is the best way to get about and needed from Badalona to visit anywhere... 2 x adult 3 day pass 37EUR. However, Restaurants/cafe's left to be desired.... In Badalona restaurants don't open until 7.30-8pm so don't be heading out at 6 wanting a big feed! Get a city map and head off out, Jaume and villa olimpica are worth a look on a sunny day (cathedral, beach and la Ramblas). If you want to visit Parc De Guell (Gaudi's park) get off at Vallarca on green line....you will need at least half a day, and decent shoes... Alot of walking but well worth a visit! All in all a good little trip but you will be on the move a fair bit! Finally... Value you for money - 0, unfortunately prices are just as expected.

author: georgebaz
title: Regret that I'm not an oiler
text: Proximity to oil drives hotel rates upwards and Hilton Garden Inn Perm is not an exception. It's built for oilers (and probably by oilers, not architects, judging from its façade) - on a wide thoroughfare near a large Lukoil headquarters and not that far from a humongous oil refinery. When I stayed there I regretted that I am not an oiler with a fat expense account, the rate was so high. I travelled with my better half and we both liked the interior and overall freshness of this property. The staff were friendly and professional, our little room clean and the smallish bathroom was supplied with Crabtree & Evelyn® amenities. The bathtub was of a smaller size and water pressure quite economical - not a trickle of course but boring if you know what I mean. Equally boring was the assortment of TV channels, mainly Russian state-sanctioned programmes with an addition of the BBC World Service, CNN, Euronews and Deutche Welle. Wireless internet was included in the room price, the bandwidth was high. The mattress was comfortable but not the synthetic pillows. We did not use the AC because it was possible to move the window pane four or six inches and let the street air in. The room was quiet and conducive to good night's rest. There was no in-room safe box and no mini-bar, but plenty of tea- and coffee-bags, sugar, some bottled water and an electric kettle. The room was equipped with an iron and ironing board. Buffet breakfast was served from 6.30 and their espresso machine was great! We also liked (but did not use) the generous offer of 'coffee to go' which was available for every guest leaving the restaurant in the morning. This was a nice touch, I have seen a hotel where they confiscated any food or drink that guests were trying to smuggle out of the restaurant. Great move Hilton! We will hardly return to Hilton Garden Inn Perm because we have nothing to do in that part of the city. Tourists who come for the sake of Perm's world-class Opera and Ballet Theatre and the city's art museums had better try more central locations.

author: minniedaisy
title: Good Value and Good Place to Stay
text: This hotel in Perm, Russia is a good place to stay. It is clean and the staff is friendly. The front desk clerks spoke English. A great breakfast buffet was included in the rate. It has decent free wifi in the room so you do not have to go to the lobby. It also has a business center. We needed two rooms and there were no connecting rooms available so we had to split up into two rooms but this was just a minor inconvenience. There is a market across the street from the hotel that sells a wide variety of snacks and groceries. There is a McDonald's, a shopping mall with a food court, and an aquatic center with a very nice pool next door. Be aware that they require guys that swim to wear a speedo-type suit and women to wear a bathing cap. There is an ATM in the lobby so you can change your money as you will need rubles at all of the places mentioned. We walked around the neighborhood and it felt safe. There were a lot of families out walking with children. There was a place where you could rent bikes, and there were kids riding bikes and skating. I recommend this hotel if you are traveling to Perm.

author: buyandsell2011
title: Great pics, not so great in reality
text: I and a friend were booked to stay here for 4 nights in Dec 2016 as part a trip visiting Barcelona and Granada. We booked through Booking.com and were really impressed by the pictures on the website of their spacious rooms and lovely balconies overlooking the street. The room we booked, was (supposed to be) a 3 person room with a balcony as we wanted a bit of extra space in the room. After a great few nights in Barcelona and an amazing drive though Spain to Granada, we arrived and checked in. The lobby of the hotel is fantastic and looks nice however the same cannot be said for the rooms. We were given a room (in the next building it would seem) which was extremely small and with a window which looked out into the shaft of space in the interior of the building (some sort of ventilation shaft)! Naturally, we were horrified and very surprised as it looked absolutely nothing like the pics we had seen. As we were staying for 4 nights, we felt it would be impossible for us to stay in this room for such a period. We immediately went to the desk to ask for another room which was more like that which we had booked. After a discussion with the staff and showing them the booking website and room we had booked, they agreed to move us to another room in the morning. The new room was slightly bigger but did have the balcony overlooking the street so we were happier as a result. In general, the rooms were very small, the beds and bedding were sub-standard and the bathroom facilities were terrible! A concrete floor in the shower and a very dirty and dark bathroom! In general, I would say this hostel is for very low budget travel (despite how the pictures look) and I would not recommend staying here for longer than ½ nights at most. Not suitable for families with children. The only saving grace of this hostel is its location. Smack bang in the heart of Calle Gran Via De Colon and literally next to the historic district of Albaicin and very close to the Alhambra (10 mins by bus).

author: apackham
title: Left my bedroom door open
text: I will start with the positives before the negatives.. Firstly location wise it is pretty central. Quicker to walk to Plaza Nueva on Calle Elvira rather than on Gran Via. The room we had (103) was a simple twin room with ensuite. Very basic with just a tv and no safe. Dont expect any shampoo! Testament to the people who take rooms there, when coming back to the hotel after a long day out (from 10am til 8pm) when walking to our bedroom door we noticed in the distance our bedroom door was wide open. We obviously expected the worst - everything taken. Now, fortunately, nothing was. Our passports were still there and our beds freshly made. This was the proof that we hadnt left the door open ourselves but the cleaning person. Reception and manager put up a fuss before even saying the word "sorry". They claimed that the cleaner only "shuts the door and doesnt push it to double check it is lost". My trust with the hotel was gone after this point. They didnt offer us anything (we were just lucky we had our passports!) and still no over the top apology. They actually didnt really care. Our trip to Granada was excellent. The hotel was the only negative.

author: SeanQ
title: A Cheap Base in the Centre of Granada
text: We booked Hostal Atenas on the recommendation of a friend who lives in Granada. Booking online was easy. The web site is excellent. We drove there for a mid-week visit. There were lots of yellow road signs to the Hostal around the city centre which helped us to find it easily and we were able to get a space in their underground parking (at the top of the street which runs alongside the Hostal). They had declined to book us a parking space in advance, but we got one OK when we arrived, 15 Euros for 24 hours. They actually let us park for longer without extra charge, which enabled us to visit the Alhambra next day. Staff spoke English and the cost for each double room (all our rooms had 3 single beds) was 30 Euros per night. Can't be bad ! The sheets on my bed were, I thought, a little grubby and I felt itchy all night, so didn't sleep well, but it may have been psychological. The beds were hard too. General room cleanliness was very good. Any staff we met were friendly and helpful and although there is no on-house catering, there are plenty of bars/cafes/restaurants close by. As an easily accessible, cheap base right in the centre of Granada, Hostal Atenas can't be beaten. NB Spanish Hostals, in our experience, are not like the "Hostels" used by backpackers which you find in many European countries. A Hostal is really more like a no-frills hotel and in some cases they are actually motels - generally clean and very good value, some with in-house catering, some with eateries nearby. Recommended.

author: bestyman
title: cheap, clean ,good location, parking but read on
text: Review posted jan 2006 but stayed there a couple of years ago so things may have changed. The reason I am writing this review now is that we are going to Granada again and I was looking on TA when I saw this hotel. The wife and I had a debate as to whether or not to stay there again, our points are. £36 GBP ( about 50US$) for 3 nights! If your on a budget this is the one for you. I doubt you will find cheaper Good location, very short walk to shops bars etc. Car Parking , not many hotels have this Air con, the air con really worked. Clean, not spotless but no complaints. From reading the above you would think the place was what dreams were made of but read on. Its like going back in time, an iron lift in the stairwell like you see in old american scary movies. The room is like a whitewashed cave . The room is bare with 2 simple beds with clean yet tatty linen. It did have a tele but only in spanish and remote was optional extra with deposit required. It reminded me of a youth hostel I stayed at once. View from balcony was a grubby brick wall about 10 foot away Food and drink not available , staff were nice enough. When we go to granada again we will not be stopping there . We are going over valantines and this place is not romantic in the slightest. We will probably stay at the carmen which is 5 times the cost so its unfair to compare. If you are on a tight budget and want a cool place to sleep then stay here. Mark

author: LincolnG770
title: It is just another Ibis.
text: I was glad when I got knowledge that I was going to stay on a Ibis in Rio de Janeiro. This way I could expect a pattern service, no surprises and a safe place. Regarding the Rio de Janeiro downtown , these characteristics make a hotel like Ibis a special place. LOCATION: Located in Rio de Janeiro downtown, it's close to Lapa and the main church of city, but pay attention to your belongings cause this neighborhood is not a safe place. You are on a easy way to anywhere and at night a taxi is totally recommended. ROOM: Is a pattern Ibis room, fair enough for a business visit, but a little small for a family trip. The bed is comfortable, the room is quiet and the bathroom is ok, but the shower is too weak. SERVICES: Ibis has a honest service, the cleaning is ok and the staff are gentle. The breakfast is one of the best things of this hotel and has a very attractive price. The WI-FI is good enough to work and do not require extra charge! OVERALL: Ibis is always a Ibis. Perfect for business, ok for a couple, but too small for a family. On the same building you have a Ibis Budget, but regarding the night rate, Ibis is better option. If you stay on Ibis Budget, I totally recommend have the breakfast on Ibis. Is on the same building and a better option.

author: DRLuxury
title: Worst of the Worst ..... Noisy and dirty
text: Being an Accor Platinum Member believe me I know their brands very well. Ibis even in Australia or Europe will give you teamaker, freezer, big screen tv and quiet rooms. Not so this pitiful excuse of an ibis. Nobody care to work or to smile at the reception desk (not my problem when you hate your job, stay at home!!!), room was not made at 3.30 pm !!!!, Wifi never working , avoid week-end because there is a club bladting the whole neighbourhood for the whole night til 8 am !!! Not joking. Dirty rooms, 1 shampoo for 2 person, no hand towels. Miserable place. Would give it -5 points. Never ever again. Worst nightmare of a hotel. Just the view was nice. Don't go out with ipads or iphones in that neighbourhood, full of shady characters, homeless and worse. Terrible hotel. Just the view to the church was nice. Nothing to do with this gulag.

author: Alexinmelbourne
title: great location and good value
text: I have stayed at the Ibis Rio Centro on two occasions - once in August 2014 and again in June 2015. Firstly, the hotel is in a really good location for tourists. Although it is away from the beaches, it is walking distance to some of the best tourist attractions in Rio. It is close to the Theatro Municipal, Catedral Metropolitana, Museu Nacional de Belas Artes, Lapa, Selaron Steps, Santos Dumount Airport, ferry terminal to Niteroi, and Metro and bus transportation. The rooms are basic, but modern and comfortable. This is not a luxury hotel but a value hotel. The hotel is very busy but functions efficiently. Wifi was fast and reliable. Breakfast was basic, but inexpensive. The rooms have mini-fridges which are not standard at Ibis. The only issue I had was when I asked reception for a laundry recommendation. I thought this would be a fairly common questions. I had a suitcase full of laundry and had I organised this through the hotel it would have cost over 300 reais which is absolutely outrageous (to put that in perspective the minimum wage in Brazil is about 4 reais per hour). When I asked for a recommendation near the hotel I was told that there were no laundry options in the neighbourhood. After searching for two hours I eventually found a place that charged 100 reais for just a few items of clothing. Even in the most expensive European or American cities there are coin laundry options for under 15 reais. Please provide a better options for in-house laundry or a better recommendation for a local laundry business because not only did I waste several hours, but the pricing only adds to the reputation that Rio is a tourist trap city.

author: RDGROULX
title: Bare minimum indeed
text: Rooms are ok if you considered the "budget" naming but other Ibis Budget are better (yes Zurich, i'm looking at you) and with a cleaner/fresher feel. Nothing shoddy here, but it's ok. This area is particularly noisy and smells of diesel all day however; I felt like I was sleeping next to bus diesel engines and fumes and opening the window was a no for me. Breakfast not included, we got charged for it but the problems was really that it was the very lowest strict minimum to have the right to call it a breakfast. Basically some small bread buns with sliced ham and cheese, some coffee and a few fruits. No eggs, no cereals, no bacon, nothing else. The breakfast room feels like a hostel: full with large round tables shared by everyone. I asked the staff if that was it as I was a bit letdown and she flat-out told me "if you don't like it go somewhere else". That's exactly what we did the next day. The internet was an irritant of particular interest of mine. When travelling abroad this is a must-have nowadays in iPhone/Android age and a decent internet is as essential as decent clean water in my opinion. The internet service was bordering on marketing misrepresentation as the bandwidth was so overloaded you'd swear a denial-of-service attack was underway. It took about 2 min to load a simple Gmail account on my laptop so you can imagine the rest. A simple white page from Google had a loading time!! In 2014 Rio de Janeiro this is not accceptable, even on a budget. Otherwise the hotel is fine. I felt like we were in a processing factory churning people but otherwise you can sleep if you leave the window closed. Next time i'll be staying a bit more outside the city.

author: NigelC730
title: Not what I had expected
text: After paying more reals cos of the Revillion i found out that Ibis Hotel in the centre very disappointing. I was there to expect for few things. 1. access to the Internet so i can check e mails and flight bookings. theirs was not working. 2. Secondly i expect a decent meal in one of their restuarants but it turned out to be buffet only at 27 reals in their cafe, The area is bit rough(seedy area) in rundown Lapa area surrounded with prostitutes. It is unsafe walking there from the metro Caricoa. It also took me nearly three hours to get back to hotel after the revillion. taxi cost 45 reals to get back. 3. Thirdly Kitchen staff bit grumpy. 4. room, bed duvet bit old and bit worn out, some tears on edges...5. After checking out they charged me for breakfast that I did not order. So Tried another Ibis hotel this time at Santos Dumont, few days later, theirs was great and much better, Internet access great and restuarant on the second floor where I finally had my decent meal and wine. the staff were so helpful. better bedding in room. Area much better and easy eaccess to domestic airport and centre. Anyone who want to stay for the revillion or the Carnival, it is best to stay at Copacablana or Ipanema so you get less hassle of getting back to the hotel and the sight of homeless tramps sleeping on streets in downtown Rio.

author: jmallmann
title: New Ibis Hotel, good value
text: I stayed at the Ibis for New Years Eve. The Hotel is just one year old and so in a very good shape. It´s central location in the old center of Rio is excellent by daytime. a lot of little shops, bars, restaurants, historic buildings are around the hotel. disadvantage is nighttime when everything is closed. locals warned me that it is unsafe to walk there by your own in the area - get a taxi!!! a metro/subway station (Carioca) is about 5-7 min. walk away with quick access to copacabana, but see above great during business hours but not an advisible walk at night. the room was quiet and had everything we needed, a comfortable bed, nice shower, tv (cnn/fox news). In almost the same building is another hotel of accor hotels (formule one). New Year´s Eve all the Rio hotels ask for unbelievable prices so the ibis (booked via www.hrs.com) was a great choice. The journey via metro to copacabana was easy and quick (you must get a special ticket for this day in advance, showing you the specific time to board your metro to copacabana. we got it very overpriced from a guy at the reception. coming back in the night was not problem at all, the trains were not overcrowded, very well organized and there were people having the same way to the hotel from the metro station - we were very glad about -but there are always taxis.... ). We payed about 50 Real from the hotel to the Int. Airport, about 30 minutes drive. e )

author: J5201DZstevenr
title: Forget manners at the manor, go to a theater.
text: My wife is from the area and had always talked about how cool it would be to stay at the Movie Manor. We stayed here and were very disappointed with the visit. The place was not packed by any means, but we were given a room that didn't exactly face the screen. Of course it didn't help that the night we were there, the main screen didn't work, at ALL. When I called about the main screen, I was told there was a power outage in the morning but they were hoping it was going to work (which they decided in about 30-minutes to give up for the night). Funny thing is, no one mentioned this at check-in time, but at 915 at night, they had no problem telling us the truth. I then asked if we could switch the sound to the secondary screen (which was working) and were told that that was not an option, as only the main screen is piped into the room. You'd think as long as this place has been around, you'd have the option of screen 1 or 2, but I guess technology hasn't caught up in this hotel. I asked what our options were and the "customer service representative" informed me that we could drive around and PAY for the second screen, which at this point was 1/4 of the way into the film. What a lousy way to spend the night, watching "Deadpool 2" from a chair in silence. I totally understand that technology doesn't always work, but why not tell us at check-in that there is a chance the main screen isn't working and offer a "free pass" to see the secondary screen. Do something other than hoping that the main screen will work. At least the movie-goers in the drive-in were given the option to head to screen 2 or get their money back, those of us in the hotel were offered zilch for the technical troubles. In the future, I'll spend a little less for a more modern hotel in the area and just pay to go and see a movie at the theater. Best Western showed nothing but total disappointment and an absolute disregard for any customer service.

author: Gilbert0
title: A destination all it's own
text: This was just a one night stop on a road trip to the Four Corners area. But in the end it could have been a destination in and of itself. While we were there, I scoured the internet to see if I could find another hotel that over looked a drive in, and this is the only one. It's incredibly unique. Put it on your bucket list and tell your friends, there isn't another one like this on the planet. Ask for a room on the second floor, and let them know which movie you want to see. The lady at front desk was very kind and helpful. The rooms do have a microwave and fridge. You can go to the concessions stand and get pop corn and cokes. We brought a bottle of wine. Chairs can be pulled over to watch the movie close to the windows. Don't miss the sunset out the front side of the hotel at dusk. Breakfast was great! Biscuits and gravy, sausage, eggs, waffles, toast and more. Clean and friendly. This is a must stop destination that is unlike anything you've seen. All of my friends were envious of the pictures on Facebook. Go to this hotel!

author: 91michellew
title: I would rate less if possible!!
text: DO NOT STAY HERE if you value quiet, security, comfort, and guest service. Upon arrival front desk clerk aka General Manager's wife, struggled to process my Best Western Travel cards, with check-in taking (30) minutes. Upon finally completing that lengthy process, I drove my RV to back lot by storage bins as instructed. At the base of the stairs to my 2nd floor room was a truck complete with (3) male construction workers who happened to be laying flooring in a room just down from mine. I had to navigate my way around debris and yellow tape to access my room and then listen to hammering/ staple gun for two hours before they finally cleared out. That evening was very busy and quite loud, but that is not unexpected fir a Friday night. What was unexpected was the uncomfortably hard bed which is very rare at a Best Western. I resorted to grabbing two blankets from my rig and laying them down for some padding.... to no avail. Suffice it to say, it was a VERY lovely long night:( Very early the next morning having not slept, I went to breakfast and requested a late check out from the ONE kind woman behind the desk, telling her of my struggle with the bed and of my desire to rest before hitting the road later that day. This request was granted. A shirt time later I went out to my rig to grab a personal belongings no and noted the white truck from the day before complete with barking dogs. I looked up towards my room just as one of three men opened my door with a master key and began to enter my room. I yelled " what are you doing" and he shut the door and said " oops wrong room." I was very upset and told all three men that they should not be entering rooms with a master key and called the front desk. The General mangers wife answered and told me to " just relax". I promptly gathered my belongings and my dog and went to check out. I again spoke to her of my distress and she argued with me. I fled and within a half hour the General manager Mike called and left a voicemail expressing his "disappointment" in me for being rude to his front desk clerk (his wife) and his maintenance men. I filed a complaint with Best Western. Take heed and stay elsewhere!!

author: Z4Jones
title: A real experience not to be missed
text: We stayed here recently on the way to thru Colorado to Colorado Springs. The proprietors were friendly and accommodating. The room, fairly standard but clean and comfortable and less expensive than most we have stayed at on our road trip. (Ours was the "Audrey Hepburn" room). But ... what a treat! Shortly after checking in and getting comfortable, we sat side by side, watching the drive-in movie through our room's picture window! (the movie, "Sully", was pretty good as well and, 1 hr 36 min, just the right length). One of the best, most novel experiences of our whole trip. Catch it if you can. (But note that the season for drive-in movies ends at the end of Sept.). Other notes: > breakfast is included, and "ok" but could include more fresh fruit. > workout room has standard treadmill, bike and elliptical and a universal but no free weights. > don't miss Fernandez Taqueria -- for some of the best, authentic Mexican food you've ever tasted! and prices very reasonable! (See separate review). Just a few miles on the other side of Monte Vista but note that the restaurant closes at 6:30 pm.

author: serinecho
title: What a cool place!
text: I loved this place, it's so cool! I travel from Boulder to Farmington NM at least once a yr, and take 285/Wolf Creek pass way. A friend recommended this place, and I am so happy we stopped here! It's close to the Sand Dunes, so excellent idea to stay one night on the way. My 7yr old LOVED it! It's basically a drive-in theater which you can see through your hotel window, with the speakers in your room. Kid friendly movies. Clean and nice and affordable. The manager Mike and his wife were so super awesome too! They had some technical difficulties and the movie started a little late, but they dealt with the situation promptly. They were so friendly too!! Free continental breakfast in morning, nice area to eat, or you can just take back to room. Smaller place so close to car from room. Get a room on the 2nd level if you can. Play ground in from of screens for kids too. You can also park in front of screen if you want also. We will definitely be back and will tell all of our friends!!

author: M211ITalanc
title: Living on their uniqueness and name. Ought to consider updating
text: We first stayed at the Movie Manor Motor Inn in 1989 as part of a cross-country family vacation. We selected this motel due to the uniqueness of being able to watch the drive-in movie from your room and have the sound piped into your room. Very cool. Amazingly, our daughter married someone from Monte Vista, thus we have repeatedly stayed here over the last several years. Each visit is more disappointing than the last. When we stayed there in July 2016, the room was not very clean. The previous guest's ear ring was on the table. Clearly, there was not a wipe down or even dusting between guests. Not good in fighting colds and flu. Also, in July the in-room refrig had the food from the previous guest. We thought we would give this place one more chance and stayed here this month, August, 2016. Continued disappointment. Neither one of the end table lamps worked nor the alarm clock due to not being plugged in. There was only one outlet on that side of the room and it was directly behind the bed. The two maintenance guys had to move the bed out and plug in an extension cord behind the bed to get the lamps and clock working. How in the world could this have happened?? Does not housekeeping at least turn on the lights in the room when they clean and would have noticed this issue? The toilet sounded like a high pitched whistle when it flushed and did not always shut off. Loud enough to wake up not only any guests in our room but probably next door and downstairs as well. The wall air conditioning unit made so much noise that it was useable at night.

author: hanierene
title: Total Disappointment
text: When I found this place, I could not have been more excited. I mean, you can watch a drive-in movie from your room! Not only that, but they play current movies! I didn't think it could be better than that. I was wrong. When we got there, they had just changed the movies from two that we would have liked to see, to two that we couldn't care less about. We tried our best to deal with this disappointment, only to discover that the quality from your room is seriously lacking. We would have had to sit in the dark just to get rid of the glare from the lights in our room. Also, we could only see the screen from one of the two beds in the room; and it was like watching a big screen TV from REALLY far away. We ended up trying to find something less disappointing on the TV inside the room. As far as the room itself, it is clearly in need of a remodel. The beds weren't at all comfortable (I had trouble sleeping). The shower had limited water pressure. I did appreciate all of the space available in the sink area of the bathroom. The only thing I didn't like about that, was that the outside door opened straight into the bathroom area. Seriously? One thing that did redeem the experience is that they do put on an amazing breakfast spread. Unfortunately it wasn't enough to keep us from going elsewhere for our other night in the area. Next time, I'll research more fully when planning my vacation.

author: grantw983
title: Unique...loved it!
text: This has got to be one of the best experiences I have had at a best western. I typically stay in Comfort Inn's, Holiday Inn's, or A Loft/Element hotels, but the quirkiness of The Movie Manor had me driving 3 hours from home to just experience the place. The rooms were clean, the staff was super friendly. Sangita was an absolutely amazing hostess and very helpful with recommending a place to eat. One of my favorite things I saw here was the wall paper and the décor in general. The movie theme is just so friggen fun! Arnold Schwarzenegger Exercise Room? How is that not a winner! I stayed in room 213 (Richard Gere) and the view to the drive in theater was perfect.
