I laid back in my queen bed, turned up the sound and enjoyed Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles in a way you can only experience here. I can't believe that anyone would want to change the décor, the atmosphere, or just the overall feel of the place. Breakfast was much more than I expected for a free hot breakfast at a best western. Coffee was actually good and I there was plenty to choose from. I have recommended this place to everyone since I have been back home. It's little places that are tucked away that make road trips worth the drive vs dealing with airport security and the headaches of screaming babies on flights.

author: julias21
title: Like staying with friends
text: It's always nice to walk into a hotel lobby and have the desk staff greet you pleasantly. At the Movie Manor, not only is the greeting warm and friendly, so is the entire service experience. Sangita and Mike are two of the nicest people ever. When I realized I forgot my phone charger, Mike loaned me one of his. The internet was down when I got there because of a community-wide service interruption, and Sangita promised to call me as soon as it was restored. I've stayed with friends who didn't treat me as well as they did. The motel itself is old, but in impeccable shape. The lobby is inviting, with fresh cookies and plenty of coffee and water. The breakfast room looks out over an open space and the mountains, and is a perfect place to start the day with a hot breakfast. My room was recently updated, spotlessly clean, and comfortable. It was a little small -- for one person it was fine, for two people it would be cozy, for any more, it would be crowded. Of course, the view from the window is of the movie screen at the drive-in, and when I stayed they were screening Batman v Superman. You flip a switch in the room to get the sound, which comes from a speaker in the ceiling. Just like being at the movies. Even without the movie experience, however, this is a great place to stay. It's little far from town so you have to drive for dinner or the grocery store (the room has a fridge and microwave), but it's quiet and pleasant. I wouldn't hesitate to stay here again next time I'm in that part of the state.

author: 563lawrences
title: The pinnacle of a 60's motel.
text: We come to this Best Western every few years. It never seems to show any wear. The room was perfect. We needed a handicap room and asked for a walk-in shower. Perfect with hand rails at the right location. Very clean and no issues. Perfect. The customer service has been great. In years past there were problems. They have added a breakfast room and have a continental breakfast that match the best I’ve had from Hamden Inn. And the view while you have your breakfast is a vista of mountains and solitude. If only it wasn’t a 5 hr. drive we would come more often. Can I think of a motel I’d rather stay at? Nope

author: Jjackson75165
title: Amazing!
text: This has got to be by far the Best experience we've had while traveling...and we travel a lot! When we arrived at 11pm we were greeted by the owners who are very passionate about hospitality! Our room was heated already when we arrived and it was already 9 degrees outside. The room was immaculate and up to date. The restroom was extremely clean no mold or mildew and the shower curtains were clean! Everyday when we left for the day we always returned to a clean and fresh room! There is plenty of breakfast options and kept stocked so there wasn't any running out and the food was great! None of the food tasted like rubber or sponge. It was delish! If you go in the summer there is a drive in movie apart of it and your room looks out to the screen and can watch the movie inside your room while laying on the bed. It's awesome! This location is about 30 min away from ski locations. The owners are amazing and it's locally owned..you'll more than likely be greeted by one of them and I Love that! Pets are welcomed! Hands down best place!

author: NorthernMNfamily
title: Kitschy, Quirky Family Fun!
text: Ever since I read about Movie Manor in the book "Weird Colorado", I've wanted to stay here! I wasn't expecting much for the hotel and rooms themselves because for me it was primarily about the drive in experience. I. Was. Wrong. The room was spacious...really spacious...plenty of room for a family of 4. Normally when we stay in a hotel, I am VERY wary of letting my baby crawl and play on the floor. Not the case. The room was spotless. Really immaculate. (They shampoo the carpets every few months and all the bed linens smelled freshly washed.) The beds were super comfy. There were 2 easy chairs and a desk chair, mini fridge and a microwave, and the room still felt spacious. The marble topped bench in the entryway was great!! Introducing my kids to a drive in movie was awesome. Being able to do it from our hotel room so the baby could go to bed on time was fabulous. Good choices and prices at the concession stand, and the volume of the movie speaker in your room is great. Breakfast the next morning in the lobby building was great (nicely updated!) and the food was delicious with a nice variety. We are SO already planning our trip for next time!!! It is worth the trip!!!!!

author: chrchgrlmis
title: Free Drive-in Movie with a good night's sleep
text: This hotel is so unique and a great experience! I've stayed here a half dozen times over the last 14 years (whenever we are in the area) and the experience has improved. The rooms have been updated and feel fresher. They are very comfortable. We had a terrific view of the main movie screen and slightly obstructed view of second screen. It was Memorial Day weekend and they were showing X-Men and Godzilla --both viewable from our room. Sound for the main screen is piped into the room and the other screen you just have to tune in by radio. The hotel has a free breakfast which was quite tasty. Generally, the same as other places: waffles (although 2 flavors! original & strawberry), hard boiled eggs, cereal, yogurt, pastries, sausage, etc; but what the others don't have is a great view of the area. The breakfast room is a large windowed area with views of the surrounding area. lovely! Helpful hint for parents: The sound for the screen is for the entire room so if the movie is not appropriate for your little ones you may not be able to listen as there is no way (that I know of) to isolate the sound. Note: You do NOT have to have the sound on in your room unless you choose to. Helpful hint for those who just want to sleep: When a lot of guests are watching the movie and you are not you can hear some of the movie sounds from their rooms. Just turn the room's AC to high fan and it drowns it right out.

author: patrickglen
title: Great Hotel - Restaurant needs to stop pretending.
text: We went to the Movie Manor for the advertised Mothers Day Lunch. I am torn between 'unbelieveable' or 'WTF' as my choices to describe our experience. First off was the Salad Bar, which consisted of a bowl of salad, pudding, coleslaw and some type of potato salad. No salad toppings at all! They should of just brought us a little plate of dinner salad instead of offering a poor excuse of a salad bar. Then when our dinner arrived some of the poor souls in our party ordered the shrimp dinner. I kid you not there was six small shrimps that they probably purchased from long john silvers the day before. For that the charged close to $20.00. I had the Prime rib which was cold and below average and was complimented with something that resembled rubber green beans and a cold baked potato. Our waitress informed us that they were out of sour cream and didn't have any other toppings for the baked potato. What is sad is that the place wasn't even close to full. Then dessert appeared which consisted of strawberry shortcake but unfortunately they had run out of strawberry's so only a few of our desserts had that topping. The best part about dessert was that instead of removing our dinner plates and then asking if we were ready for dessert she just brought it out. We had to move our dinner plates to the side to make room for our dessert. In the end I really wondered if they were putting on a show for a hidden camera for a new reality show 'America's Worst Restaurant' or if they really were that incompetent.

author: 207danw
title: Excellent Family Fun on the High Plains
text: I recently stayed here while exploring the Creede, CO area. It was professional, very clean, up to date and charming. I can't fathom why anyone would call this place dated! It is a piece of Americana operated by Mike and his wife who have over 30 years experience. It is a family run motel run by caring folks. The Cast of "the Lone Ranger" including Johnny Depp stayed here for 2 months during filming in Creede, CO and I can see why. The bed was very comfortable and the "Drive in Movie" from your hotel room was great fun! I was surprised at how good both the sound and picture were given the limitations of the distance from the screen. The projector produced enough light and was of sufficient resolution so that it was easy to enjoy the movie looking out over a sea of cars gathered for family fun. Mike and his wife are very detail oriented - even the garden hoses were neatly coiled! I must admit that my wife and I moved the bed in front of the window (we moved it back in the morning) to watch the show but this was no big deal. There are treats and popcorn available and a restaurant is also either on the property or near by. The included breakfast was similar to other such fair at Best Westerns - but with excellent freshness and quality of ingredients. The fruit was attractive and fresh, the coffee was HOT and FRESH! The view from the dining room is Stunning! The individual creamers for the coffee were COLD and FRESH - as a coffee addict I particularly appreciated this. There is just something special about sharing an experience with others in this way, it is wholesome and harkens back to a time in America that was full of hope and promise. Don't expect the Ritz Carlton but do expect Quality - 50's Style The location is in the middle of the San Louis Valley between the Great Sand Dunes National Park, the amazing Mountains surrounding Creede, Lake City, South Fork and Pagosa Springs. It is near Wolf Creek for Skiing and it is near an amazing Colorado Train journey to Chauma, NM which starts south of Alamosa, CO. You won't be disappointed.

author: timetoride
title: Woops almost missed this
text: We were heading towards the Great Sand Dunes, Colorado on motorcycles. I saw this hotel on the internet and new it was on our rout, to our surprise it was terrific. It looked a bit questionable for the price (60's dated motel style) when we got there, although the grounds were immaculate. We pulled in and the staff greeted us very warmly. They happily changed our room so we had a better view to watch the DRIVE INN movie from our room. Yes, it’s a drive inn movie theater motel, just like the name implies. It’s decorated with movie memorabilia. Our room (The Richard Gere) was immaculate, completely updated with nice linins, lots of pillows, comfy beds, and spotless WHITE bathroom. We had lots of room to store our suitcases and riding gear with out crowding the bedroom. The huge picture window framed the drive in screen; the speaker was in the ceiling. Attached to the motel is a restaurant. Serves breakfast, lunch & dinner. We parked the bikes, had dinner and a few beers (they have a full bar) food was good and portions were as well...Then up to the room to watch the cars drive into their spaces and then settled into watch Batman...It was easy to see and hear...In the morning we had a great omelet, more than filling and took off. We will go back there every time we plan a trip in the Monte Vista area, you should NOT miss this!! PS this first time I wrote this review, I mistakenly hit the wrong stars...Its excellent!!

author: mogulman
title: I love this place
text: We came here about 5 years ago. During this road trip I planned this place as a stop on our way to Mesa Verde from the Denver area. We weren't disappointed. We had some mexican food in town before it got dark and stopped at a nearby grocery store for some snacks. Then we settled in for the movie. I was with my son (10). We walked our to the playground by the movie screen. It has a lot of retro playground equipment (teeter totters, etc). My son had fun. We watched Ice Age 4 from our room. My son loved watching in our room with the sound pumped into the room. I noticed that the rooms are very sound proof. This helps when you are watching the movie from the room, but also afterwards. You don't hear a lot of noise from other rooms. It looks like they redid the rooms a few years ago. Our room was very clean and comfortable. I think the only con was the restaurant that is on the property. We were going to eat there, but we stopped by and it didn't look great. One table of people. The menu didn't look that appetizing either.

author: midcenturystylemag
title: Best Western Movie manor is retro and great for families!
text: Part of the Best Western chain, the Best Western Movie Manor is located on the same property as a historic drive-in movie theater, which means guests can watch G rated – family-friendly movies on the big screen from the comfort of most rooms every mid-May to mid-September, while enjoying fantastic mountain views. George Kelloff, as a young man, saw a wonderful drive in movie theater in Brownsville, Texas, in the 50s and decided he needed to own one himself. In 1955, George and wife, Edna Mae, built the Star Drive-in Theater on the site of an old airport on Rt. 160 just west of Monte Vista, Colorado. View slideshow: Movie Manor in Monte Vista Colorado is a mid-century treasure! While running the box office, George dreamed of a motel that would wrap around the drive-in theater. With large windows that faced the outdoor screen and sound piped into the rooms, motel guests could see the movie from their rooms if they chose. Fourteen units of the Movie Manor Motel were completed in 1964. Thirty years later, room capacity has more than doubled as a Best Western motel. A second outdoor screen was added in 2003. The drive-in theater includes a snack bar, and a restaurant is next door to the motel. George and Edna Mae have now retired, but the property is still run by their son, George Jr, and his wife Judy. Families with young kids will especially love seeing movies that are always family friendly on the big screen from the comfort of their own room, the sound is available with a switch and a volume control. The slightly over $100 a night price may not seem inexpensive, however, if you factor in getting to see a first run movie and the clean and well furnished rooms – it’s a bargain! The rooms all have a movie theme with pictures of famous actors and actresses. Each room is named after a movie star (new and old) and my favorite is the Arnold Schwarzenegger workout room! If you’re afraid Monte Vista is a dead end for activities, be sure to check out this review of the available sightseeing down in the area! Monte Vista also has a little something for everyone. Just outside the Movie Manor, guests will find plenty to do, like visiting Great Sand Dunes National Park, experiencing the National Wildlife Refuge, attending the annual Crane Festival and witnessing the thrills of the Ski Hi Stampede Rodeo, one of the oldest in Colorado. There’s more information on what to do in the area on this review on Denver Parent.

author: SiriusBlackDog
title: Very nice.
text: The pet rooms are in a small separate building they refer to as the "Annex." The Annex rooms do not have a view of the movie screens. It seems that the Annex building was probably renovated from a snack bar or something when there were more screens at the drive in, and the walls in the room give away the age of the building. They weren't in bad shape, just clearly not new. I stayed two different times at this hotel on the same trip. Rooms were well-appointed, including a flat-screen TV (although the cable service had a limited channel selection). A few bugs and spiders had managed to get into the rooms, possibly due to the exterior doors (rather than interior hallway doors), but despite the invaders the rooms were quite clean. My room for my first stay was on the back of the building, and on the front for my second stay. It made quite a difference for road noise. Bed and bath linens were nice. Everything worked and wi-fi connection was fine. The light switch near the door controlled the light over the sink and vanity area, which was fine on first arriving in the room, but didn't make practical sense when actually using the sink area. Staff was friendly, helpful, and accommodating to my requests. Huge field behind the buildings is great for exercising dogs. The location was a very convenient five minutes from my destination, but I give it three stars for value because the price seems a bit high for the area, even despite the nicely-appointed room. I would stay again but would attempt to negotiate a better rate, especially if I was staying more than one night.

author: FTAList
title: Fun, unique experience. Nice motel, too.
text: My family has been visiting the Movie Manor for over 15 years now. If anything, it's a little better than it used to be. It's an older motel, but well renovated. All rooms point toward the main drive-in theater screen, and they all have speakers to hear the show. What we found out this trip is that you can also see the second screen if you look sideways out the window, and the second screen uses FM for its audio, so the clock radio in our room worked great. The exercise room is a just a converted guest room, but its equipment is surprisingly modern. It was a great way to work up a little sweat after a long drive. For little kids, there's still a playground at the base of the main drive-in screen. The WiFi was surprisingly strong, and the cable TV included HBO this time. (The Movie Manor had held out for a long time, which isn't so strange considering the free first-run movies available out the window every night.) However, the cable lineup was actually a little sparse. The adjacent restaurant is a godsend, especially in the morning, even though breakfast isn't free. (Try the Kibbie beef sausage patties.) In evenings during drive-in season, walk straight over to the snack bar for hamburgers and true drive-in food to take back to your room. This is a destination, which is good because it's not very close to anything else. It's a good mile outside the small town of Monte Vista. Each room's door opens to a spectacular, sweeping view of scrub brush and semi-desert. But if you can work a one-night stay here into your cross-Colorado plans, you'll have good memories to talk about for years to come.

author: lovesNC
title: Average Stay
text: This is a unique motel. You can watch a movie from your motel room. Open the curtains, pull up a chair & adjust the sound. Wish the room had a microwave, as we had microwave popcorn with us. I know they wanted you to buy their popcorn. The room was a decent size & comfortable. There is a good sized ledge for your suitcases near the door. A plus. The toilet & tub/shower are in a separate room. Nice shower. Sink is outside. TV in cabinet. Desk & phone; 2 chairs; 2 double beds. No frig or microwave. There is a restaurant on the property, but you have to walk there. Not attached to the motel. Ordered a grilled cheese & soup. The grilled cheese wasn't cooked; soup was good. If you are looking for a different motel experience, this is the place.

author: tranquilblue96
title: Good but nothing special...
text: I brought my family on a side trip to the San Luis Valley as I grew up there. I always wondered what the hotel was like, so we decided to stay there after a fun day the Great Sand Dunes. The room (they are all named after movie stars) was okay but very dated. It had comfortable beds, but the bathroom had lots of spiders. Overall, it was clean, but showing wear and tear. We didn't eat dinner at the resturant, but we into the city, where there is not much of a selection. We were excited to see the movie and had a good room to see it. The sound was a bit loud in the room and hard to adjust. We were able to walk to the concessions and get popcorn...yum. The movie was okay, but we were far away so it was not quite a movie experience. Before the movie we took our toddler to the little playground in front of the movie screen. It was 50 years old! Very cute, but not all that safe anymore. In the morning we ate breakfast at the resturant. It was really good but expensive. We spent $37 for 4 and one was a kids breakfast..Overall it was okay but nothing special. You would probably have just as good of a time watching a movie on HBO or pay per view at the comfort inn.

author: jillg221
title: Be forewarned
text: Scotia Grand is a property management office with limited office hours representing various rental apartments scattered over a large urban development called Quartermile. The concierge office in Quartermile is not directly associated with Scotia Grand and will give you the after-hours phone number of Scotia Grand if you have any issues. We had several issues. #1 - We booked a premier 1-bedroom apartment for one week during the Edinburgh Fringe Festival. We were assigned to a small dark apartment on the bottom floor of an office/apartment building next to the noisy loading bay of the local Sainsbury's grocery store. The bed was tiny and uncomfortable. There was no Wi-Fi, no hairdryer and no instructions for the ultra-modern hob/stovetop/microwave. When we complained we were given a modem and a hairdryer. #2 - Then we compared photos on the SG website to our small apartment and saw that our very bedroom was pictured on the website as a standard 1-bedroom unit. Yet we were being charged for the premier apartment. When we complained about this we were told to pack our suitcases the next day and they would be moved for us to a larger apartment. Since we were paying over $300 per night, we expected the larger apartment to have some sort of wow factor. While it was large and well appointed with a comfortable king-size bed, we were shocked to find that our floor-to-ceiling windows were approximately 30 feet away from a massive, busy high-rise construction site. (We were on the third floor of a tall building.) There was complete lack of privacy unless we pulled the blinds. Once construction is complete that fishbowl apartment will be looking right into another fishbowl apartment. #3 - We were also told that our apartment would be serviced once halfway through our stay, and when we requested this we were told that "the girls" were too busy that day, but they could manage to drop off some toilet paper and a fresh set of towels. By this time we were desperate for toilet paper. #4 - The worst thing by far is that we were promised a reduction in our bill since we had to spend our first night in the wrong apartment (without a sincere apology), and when we got our credit card bill, we had been charged the full original booking price as if we had stayed 7 nights in a penthouse. We will never stay here again and do not recommend it to others, including our friends in UK who attend the fabulous Fringe Festival.

author: audrey_mandy
title: Modern apartment in a great location
text: Accommodation: The apartment was 2 bedrooms overlooking a beautiful park. Bedrooms were large and we had 2 bathrooms. Beds were very comfortable. The apartment had very large windows. It was well maintained and clean. Cooking facilities were great. It was the 1st opportunity where we had time and space to have home cooked meals. Transport: Drove to the apartments. Instructions provided are good. During our stay there was a lot of construction which can be confusing. Drive to he airport was not difficult, approx 20 - 25 mins. Paid parking @ £16 per day. I expect this would be costly if you were paying an hourly rate. Convenience: Sainsbury's supermarket is on the Square (3 mins) towards Middle Meadow Walk, eateries are 5 - 10 mins walk towards Lauriston Place and towards the right down Forest Place on to George IV Bridge. Laundry - Apartment was equipped with a washer. We did not use this as we were only there for 3 nights so time was short. I would be useful to have a dryer when you are traveling and only have short stays. Nevertheless a washing machine is great. Negatives: I was prepared for this, but the office location to check in once we had parked our car was very difficult to find. Eventually after waking up and down I finally located the office which is separate from the apartments.

author: becaface90
title: Disappointing - one thing after another.
text: First thing's first, Grand Scotia probably know I am going to write this as I think they know our experience wasn't a great one. (No.1) I got a call the morning we were due to arrive to advise there was a flood in our room and we were getting moved. As they were fully booked we were going to another property in the West End not run by themselves which was not in the old town where we had booked. This made me extremely worried as it was a surprise for my boyfriend's birthday and I didn't know where we were going nor was I sure this would be of the same calibre that we had paid for. (No.2) Upon speaking with the new hotel I was meant to be going to they advised they needed payment from Scotia Grand, I then called Scotia Grand to tell them and they advised they had magically had a cancellation and we now had what we had originally booked. I was somewhat dubious as why had they not called me in the first place to tell me the good news? So after much worrying and stress we were setting off an hour late. (No.3) Upon arrival, the check in was some what disorganised however they apologised and said we were not going to be charged for the parking we had requested which was nice. (No.4) Off we go finally to get the room, then the parking pass doesn't work, we have to reverse out, go back to the Office and one of the owners/Managers follows us round and gets us in after phoning the NCP Office. He advised we could have a drink on them a bar round the corner so we thought ok surely nothing else can go wrong. Low and behold... (No.5) We get to the apartment, lovely bathroom, nice spacious bedroom, good sized living room and kitchen. Then I see the view. A building site, with teams of builders at eye height to us. Absolutely no privacy whatsoever. They started banging at 7.40am every morning on the dot so this meant not a great sleep. There is no main mirror in the room and the plugs don't stretch to the bathroom which resulted in me doing my hair in the camera of my tablet. Now realistically in a year or two time this will be a lovely apartment once the work is finished and it is in a great location however for me the whole thing was so shambolic and unorganised I wouldn't risk booking here again. May I also mention this was mid-week not a busy weekend nor a busy period during any Festivals. Steer clear.

author: Annie_P_2862
title: Good location near the Universtiy
text: We stayed at the apartments for one night for our visit to Edinburgh University. The directions etc were very good and we collected the key to our apartment with no problem. After parking in the car park we found the door to our block very easily and located our apartment on the top floor. We did book a 2 bedroomed apartment and were very surprised to be in a very large 4 bedroomed apartment. We love lots of space so this was great. The apartment was hot but that wasn't a problem because we could open the windows and there were several fans to use. The apartment was contemporary in style and had everything we needed. We easily logged onto the WIFI which for us is really important. The beds were slightly hard but this is down to personal preference. Another moan of mine is not enough hangers in wardrobes but we were only there for one night so didn't affect us. There was plenty of hot water and fresh towels. The only negative we could find was the apartment information booklet, although professional, was not very comprehensive for example, we tried to watch a DVD but there were no instructions for this. We eventually worked out which channel to set the TV on etc. Also we had to plug the DVD into the TV! There were also no instructions for the microwave and as there are many different makes and models it took some time to work out exactly how to use it. Other than that a very nice apartment in a lovely location. We would definitely use the apartments again.

author: travellister
title: Great apartment but reception lacking
text: Firstly the apartment was great. Really convenient location only a 10 - 15 minute walk to the Castle. Very clean, spacious, great bathroom. The laundry facilities an absolute godsend when you are travelling for a number of weeks. Lots of great bars and restaurants nearby. OK that is the positives. The only thing that really let this place down was the reception. After pulling into the layside as instructed, I spent 10 minutes trying to find the reception. No signage whatsoever! I had to ask people for directions. Finally I found it. Very basic reception. Their excuse for no signage was that it was too windy to put out the sign. That didn't help me! They supplied me with keys and that was it. No map of the city, no local info on bars, restaurants, local attractions, taxis, nothing. There was no folder of information in the apartment except for checkout information. No instructions on how to use the combined washer/dryer. I did work it out for myself but it would ha be been nice to have some instructions. So, yes the apartment was great but they really need to get their act together to provide a basic service for tourists.

author: Eno89
title: Birthday Treat gone wrong
text: This was mine and my partners first holiday, and it was his birthday during the trip. I had arranged 4 nights at the apartments with its central location and views. I booked a Premier one bed (open plan lounge, all cooking appliances a variety of pots pan and other essentials), due to the extra square foot and appliances (I have previously stayed here so I know the standards of the rooms and its facilities). The morning after we arrived the extractor fan feel off while my partner was cooking breakfast, we rang the office and they sent someone over immediately (which was great), upon his arrival (lovely man) he explained it was something in most of the apartments but he will get someone to come and fit it (we were out for the day and gave consent for them to come in and fit the issue) and there was also a sign on the window in the living room saying not to open the windows, meaning the only window that could be opened was in the bedroom (we planned on cooking dinner everyday including breakfast before our planned trips out). This was a big blow and not very good especially for what we paid. After out lovely day out we came back to the apartment which seemed untouched, further more I had no correspondence with an update all day. I sent an email that evening and within an hour we were offered a move... Thinking it would be a room similar we were downgraded to a standard one bed, and the next day the washing machine didn't work. Baring in mind this is my partners birthday and we had to stay in all day, and the bell rang SIX times with people trying to fix it, eventually the owner came and got on his hands and knees and fixed it. The facilities in the apartment were half the standard and condition, which again was very unsatisfying and rather unpleasant. Although the staff were attentive. It does not stray from the fact that we paid nearly close to £400 and had quite a disruptive and impersonal trip. Upon my return home I contacted the manager directly thanking then for there assistance during the stay, but highlighted that the experience was not what we expected and paid for (in regards to room size and facilities), I got a response asking to highlight all the issues which I did, then I received a message that he will be returning to the office on Friday (27th Feb 2015) and I have heard no reply since. I am truly saddened that this has happened and that I have to leave a negative review but I wouldn't wish this trip on anyone. Very disappointed and we will not be returning. It is a shame because the location is very central and easily accessible

author: Doyounoah
title: Average accomodation in wonderful location
text: We stayed at the Grand Residence Quartermile Apartments last week for two nights. We were met by a helpful member of staff who showed us to the apartment and went over key information and instructions. First impressions the apartment was clean, a good size, lovely open plan kitchen/living room and double bedroom with separate toilet and shower. The location is really fantastic. It is right in the heart of the old town and ideal for exploring this side of Edinburgh so I would definitely recommend staying here if you’re looking for accommodation within this area. Overall I was satisfied with my stay at Scotia. I would have given it four out of five but there were some areas that needed improvement. It was clear the apartment had been “lived in”, of course you would expect that in an apartment flat that is rented out however there were a few things we noticed that reinforced this feeling. There were quite a few marks and scuffs on the white walls and the white chair in the bedroom had brown marks all over it so perhaps staff need to update the apartment with a lick of paint and new furniture. Unfortunately, the curtain railing in the living room was broken and was on the floor, leaving an unsightly view of workmen on a building site. The member of staff did try temporary fix it back and said she would get someone to come and repair it but no one ever came. I find things like this annoying. Yes, sometimes there are problems with accommodation but if there is a promise to fix/resolve the issue, then staff should go out of their way to do this. Unfortunately, this never happened for us and left me feeling annoyed as the view from our bedroom and living room was of the construction site and builders – hardly captivating! Maybe on this occasion we were unlucky with our apartment, but I do feel that if you are looking for average accommodation this would be suitable, but for special accommodation, try elsewhere.

author: Wolfsontherun
title: Old and New
text: The apartment was part of an block with permanent residents we assume. It was relatively easy to get to and easy walking distance to most attractions. Nice and quiet at night. The apartment was spacious with a nice view, though in one direction it looks into an office block. The area used to be an old hospital which has been converted to apartments and office blocks. Nearby restaurants were not busy, it is off the main tourist track, though the supermarket was pretty busy every time we went there. It services the local student population I think. Not a huge variety of stock but adequate for our needs for our short stay. The kitchen was the least well appointed of the serviced apartments we stayed in during our month in UK and Europe. Pots and pans and utensils were not in good condition. It would also be good to be given some written instructions as to how to use the washer/dryer. Bathroom wasn't well ventilated and has a big step into and out of the bath/shower. Lounge seating was inadequate if you have other guests. It was a small 2-seater plus one single seat. I suppose it was just to accommodate two people in the apartment, but nice to have a bigger couch. Plenty of room for it. Bed was quite soft but a good size and the bedroom was spacious with room for two suitcases on the floor. We were there in winter but the heating was good so having heavy quilt bedding was not necessary. It would have been good to be provided with blankets as an alternative.

author: MOBilise
title: Great apartment in handy location
text: This apartment has recently had a change of name to Scotia Grand Apartments. The place is handy to the Royal Mile and Edinburgh Castle attractions and also to the train and bus stations etc. On arrival the office staff was simply superb and nothing is too hard for them. The apartment is furnished really well and has all the mod cons. Has its own modem router that provides a good wifi reception. Also has an ADSL connection if needed. Stayed there for 3 days the first time , headed west for a few days then came back for one more night The first time around would have appreciated the operation manuals for some of the electrical items. Confused initially with the cook top when turned on, which is all glass and works on conduction when a pot is on it and turns off immediately when taken off. The place is very modern and supplied with a large fridge, a freezer, dishwasher, microwave oven, cook top and a washing machine and dryer , TV , DVD player, pots and pan, plates, cutlery etc etc. It really is superbly fitted out. Have a gripe about the low glass coffee table which I kicked seven times, maybe I'm just a slow learner . Lol . The place is spotless and the bed is very comfortable. There is great heating in the place. Sainsbury shop is only two minutes walk away and provides most things for one to purchase and cook for themselves in the apartment. This really is a home away from away and would definitely return.

author: mcmicken
title: Lovely Flat
text: My girlfriend and I were looking for an apartment to stay in central Edinburgh, these came up very reasonably priced so we thought we'd give them a shot. The most important thing is that the flat itself was fantastic! We especially enjoyed the huge bath in our apartment. The decor was nice and modern and we had a nice view from the living room. We were only staying overnight so we didn't get to take advantage of the well equipped kitchen (had both a fridge AND freezer which was a nice touch). The lady who showed us to our apartment was very nice, didn't catch her name unfortunately. It seemed like it was a busy day for people arriving but she handled it well. I do feel directions could have been a little clearer in the complex. We got into the complex no problem but reception wasn't obvious and took us a few minutes to find. A minor frustration, as it appears to be a work in progress, but a frustration nevertheless. The booking site that we used claimed there was free parking with a pass but when we arrived we were informed that we had to register for this before arriving. There is an NCP nearby but that added to the cost of our stay and, again, was a little frustrating. Not to mention there was a pipe leak so the car park floor was covered in what smelled like urine. Not the fault of Thistle Residence but left a sour taste in the mouth. We both felt that these could be really amazing holiday apartments and we'd certainly stay here again, but maybe give it a little time to iron out a few kinks first. So much of it could have been a 5 star review for me but little annoyances got in the way. Definitely worth checking out though!

author: WelshFromNottingham
title: Luxury in the heart of Edinburgh
text: Six of us came from Surrey, Notts and Western Australia, to meet and spend a night in Edinburgh en route to a wedding on the isle of Skye. We could not have wished for a more luxurious and comfortable place to stay...and at a very realistic price. The apartment is in a converted wing of the old hospital building, on the edge of the Edinburgh University campus. It is within easy walking distance of the Old Town, and George Street is no more than 20 minutes' walk away. Parking is secure and close by. It's hard to find the first time...ask a traffic warden! Once we reached the reception office, the extremely helpful man on duty gave us our passes and guided us on foot into the car park...descending floor by floor to give us directions to our reserved spaces. He then walked with us to the apartment and showed us around and how everything worked, handed out keys and left, refusing a tip. The flat is lovely...3 good-sized bedrooms and two bathrooms, one en suite. Power showers with "rainfall" heads are sublime after a hard day's walking, and the living area has views across the Meadows. Coffee, tea and milk were provided (9 or 10 helpings of each) in the kitchen. We didn't test the cooking equipment as we were eating out. The beds were large and comfortable, and there were plenty of bedside sockets for phones, ipad etc. Wifi is free and of adequate speed. Only two negatives: the rooms were hot, and we couldn't find a way to turn down the heating; and it is quite hard to find Nightingale Way because of current construction work and road closures. Otherwise a perfect place to stay...we will definitely be back.

author: MWalsh-Erding
title: Excellent Apartment
text: My family stayed in a 3-bedroom Thistle Residence apartment (13 Simpson Loan) last week for four nights. Both the quality of the apartment and the location were excellent. The Sainsbury shop just a 100 metres away was also very handy! A couple of small issues ... like the fact that a fully-equipped kitchen for six people had exactly six knifes, six plates, six glasses. So, despite the presence of a dishwasher, this was an inconvenience that could have been avoided (and was rectified the next day when we mentioned it). It's also a bit of a challenge figuring out the heating system ... doubtless very logical if you want to sit down with a handbook, but a quick-guide would have been useful, as would a short explanation of some of the electrical switches (ie: the heated handrail in the bathroom is controlled by a switch outside the bathroom at floor level ... and it took us a while to figure out which switch controlled the high window). Finally, just a warning that the 3-bed apartment had two beautiful large bedrooms, but the third one was very small and presumably intended for children. That's fine if you have children with you, but mine are all in their twenties ... so it was a little bit of a shock ... and the "kids" needed to toss a coin to see who had to be in the small room. Despite those points, I think that the apartment was very clean and beautifully equipped ... and I wouldn't hesitate to use Thistle again ... so it still deserves 5-stars.

author: TimNG
title: Smart & Central; Noisy and lacking privacy
text: Beautifully done modern apartment in a fantastic location. Clean and well furnished with all the facilities in the flat that we wanted. Thoughtful extras included like tea bags and some milk and an array of multi-media gizmos. The welcome was efficient, friendly and helpful. Two big downsides though for the flat we stayed in: noise and lack of privacy. Our flat was at the back above the industrial bins & public bottle bank (about 12 large ones) and the rear of Sainsburys. This meant that from early in the morning there was a lot of protracted lorry noise, crashing of bottles being deposited, and loud beeping/warning messages as lorries reversed. These flats are also fitted with floor-to-ceiling windows. This creates a lovely amount of natural light. There are roller-blinds in the bedroom, but they let the light in and there are no curtains, so a lot of light still comes in. This (plus the lorries and bins) means you are guaranteed an early wake-up, whether you want it or not. We didn't want it. It also means that wandering in to the kitchen in the morning to make a cup of tea with no clothes on is not to be advised: since your neighbour, just 15m across the road in a similar flat, may well be admiring the interior of your flat at the time. Not much privacy here. Finally, the internal sound-proofing is not great: people opening and closing their doors in the corridor sounds like they are coming into your own flat. This is no big deal in itself, but added to the issues above just makes this feel like too much of goldfish-bowl for me to want to come back again. Which is a shame, since it is a great flat in a great location. Some attention to the windows dressings would solve the light issue: blackout curtains/blinds in the bedroom and some form of optional muslin style curtain in the living room. Ensuring that you get a flat that is not above the bins and Sainsburys loading bay would solve the noise issue.

author: WideEyedTraveler
title: Wow! We so enjoyed spreading out in our "pad"
text: We two tired travelers arrived at Thistle and discovered a spacious apartment-just like the website! We had a comfortable living room, a working kitchen with a table, and two bedrooms and two bathrooms! The apartment looked over a lovely green park called "the Meadows," and it was beautifully quiet at night. What a find for Edinburgh. We took baths (yes, there was a full bathtub) and did laundry (washer-dryer provided) and cooked at our place for a couple of days. We discovered a Starbucks and a small Salisbury grocery store less than a block away. We ventured out to do tourist things like visiting the Castle, then came back to take a nap and "process." When we arrived, we took a taxi from the airport, and I recommend this, as it's not the easiest place to find if you're tired and unfamiliar with the city. Later we discovered we were about a 20 minute walk from Victoria Bridge where the shuttle bus goes. We were close to the Elephant (the cafe where Harry Potter was conjured), about 10 minutes to the Royal Mile. The location was great. The manager was very nice. He printed up some tickets for us on his office printer. He goes off duty at 7 p.m., so this place is set up for travelers who arrive before that time. If you are a furniture snob, be aware that it's Ikea quality. But the space and tranquility were worth it to us.

author: Oldcodger2011
title: Great new apartments - still some snagging
text: I believe that Thistle Residence have about 40 apartments in this brand new desirable development "Quartermile" on the site of a an old hospital. Most of the other apartments are owned by (wealthy) Edinburgh citizens. Their apartments are in separate blocks from the Thistle reception which unless special requests are made closes at 7pm - so not so good for those arriving and departing late evening. The one bed apartments are either on the ground or 1st floor - ours was on the ground floor. The developer has equipped these apartments to a high standard, best quality built in oven, hob, dishwasher and fridge. However some functionality has been overlooked - no cutlery drawer at waist height & wall cupboards for 6' 6" basketball players. A separate utility room contained washing machine and drying rack. There were no hooks for hanging coats in any room or hall - since other flats may have been occupied by their owners before being let through Thistle this may not be universally true. The bedroom had nice fitted cupboards and a functional queen bed (Ikea?) If you are looking for soft mattress toppers, Egyptian cotton sheets, fluffy dressing gowns, slippers you will be disappointed. Fluffy white towels and a power shower are provided and by request a non slip bathmat. The sink in the toilet / shower room had the most awkward mixing tap with very little clearance to the sink - it looked good but like the kitchen was low on functionality. The dining / kitchen had a large sliding door that did not have any means of locking except in the totally shut position - this may be a problem on the ground floor in a hot summer. There is a blinding fast internet connection and good TiVo package for the flat screen TV but no phone. A nice settee to sit on while relaxing and a functional ikea table and chairs. So in summary the apartment offers comfort away from home but some negotiation with the helpful staff during office hours may be required - so bring your own phone or laptop to communicate.

author: regtravel2014
title: Poor Service
text: These apartments are good for single business travelers, but for couples or families we wouldn't recommend. First night, Booked the thistle residence on booking.com at the last minute. We were arriving late in Edinburgh, and since check in is only open between 2pm and 7pm, we asked if we could get a late check. The response from Thistle was that we had to book their airport pick up service for £35 to be able to check in late. When we queried it, they said the late check in fee was £15 which we will have to pay to pick up the keys. We eventually arranged the pick up service and arrived at the hotel late.The apartment was adequate, quite spacious two bedroom. More of a business type apartments than for vacations or getaways. We were only staying one night, and so checked out the day after. However due to confusion regarding check out times we were awoken by the sound of the maid coming in at 10am sharp to clean the apartment. Once the confusion was resolved, check out time is indeed 10am!, we expected her to let us shower and pack to leave, but she stood around waiting for us to leave. We felt forced out of the room, which made us very uncomfortable. Second night, we stayed at the Thistle residence a couple of days later, since we couldnt cancel the booking. This time check in was completed on time, but the service from the receptionist was poor, and seemed unwilling to help us find the room. This time the apartment was a one bed room which is significantly smaller than the other apartment. But it was adequate for the stay. The cleanliness of the bathroom left a lot to be desired. The was a hand print on the bathroom door or some description, we shuddered to think what it could be. Also there was mould growing in the bath/shower.

author: UpAndUp
title: Perfect for a romantic weekend
text: New apartment, clean and comfortable, with all the facilities and kitchenware for a romantic stay, great location near the Royal Mile. Good area (supermarket, Starbucks, University..). Nice for a romantic weekend. My only comments are: 1. The bedroom is small. (although the rest of the apartment is big) 2. When we arrived the hotel entrance (office) was closed. We had to wait 10 minutes for staff to arrive (we freezed) 3. Neighbours can be heard banging doors and talking in the hallway 4. Ask for more bathroom towels (one each for the duration of the stay is not enough). The area is safe and quiet, Local supermarket, cake shop and Starbucks next door. 5 minutes walking distance to pubs and shops. 10 minutes walking distance to city centre. Really nice. We enjoyed the stay. Perfect for a romantic weekend.

author: jalogs
title: Good apartment. Good location.
text: We stayed in a one bedroom apartment. Living area comfortable and well equipped compact kitchen. Bedroom a little small but bed comfortable and plenty wardrobe space. Bathroom consisted of walk in shower, basin, toilet. and heating rail, Have to say that shower water ran onto the floor which in the long run could rot the floor if it seeps between the tiles. Apartment could have been warmer. Radiators were turned up but just cool. Having said that the apartment was clean and well furnished. Situation brilliant. Close to restaurants and small Sainsburys just a few minutes walk. Buses into city centre very close. Try Peter's Yard for breakfast, almost opposite. Coffee and cinnamon bun....yum. Huge choice of breads, cakes etc. We will certainly return with family.

author: hobbes2220
title: A place to relax and call home
text: I was supposed to return to my father's roots (Scotland) with him this year but he became ill and could not join me. He suggested an apartment and found the Thistle apartments online for me. The location is very central: a 10 minute walk to the Royal Mile and a few minutes more to Princess Street, easy bus access to just about anywhere, in a community with loads of coffee shops, pubs and restaurants near by, and a small grocery store on the ground level. The apartments themselves are spotless and exactly as the pictures online show. having a stove top for a quick breakfast and a cup of coffee / tea is great, and having a washer meant I could travel with less clothes (though there was no dryer in my apartment). Scott, the manager, and his team were absolutely fantastic. They just couldn't do enough for you. The ONLY two things I would caution people about are the height of the tub/shower and the noise level outside. Unless you are 6 foot, you have to sit on the edge of the bath and swing your legs over to get in there really isn't any way you can safely or easily step out. If you have any mobility issues it might be a bit of a challenge for you. Other apartments may be entirely different and all in all it wasn't an issue for me (though would have been for my 85 year old father). Secondly, the quartermile is being built on the old hospital grounds and there are many more sites to go, so construction is ongoing. It's not horrible. Just noticeable in the background. There is so much construction in Edinburgh itself that it probably wouldn't matter where you stayed. I couldn't imagine staying in a hotel room for a week when you could stay here. I would absolutely return to this location the next time I am here.

author: DnagsCrew
title: They Make Bumps in the Road FUN!
text: Spent a family weekend at Hyatt House in King of Prussia to precharge for the holidays and do some shopping. Arrived at the hotel at 3:45pm for check in with my wife and three children. A young lady by the name of Vanessa greeted us and gave us the news that our room wasn't ready. She stated that it would be at least an hour in a very apologetic and sincere way. In a moment of shear stupidity, my next comment was, "Are you going to let me check out late on Monday?" Not my best moment and Vanessa without missing a step stated, "I can make that happen." We didn't take her up on her offer, but I was again impressed by her sincerity. We were invited to stay in the lobby why we waited and began watching a college football game on the lobby T.V. While I was getting something out of the car, a man by the name of Joe, Hotel Chef, approached my wife and kids and offered them snacks and drinks. He also offered to fix them something to eat if they wanted. I nice gesture that didn't end that night. Joe went out of his way the entire weekend to ensure my family was comfortable and lacked nothing. When I returned to the front desk an hour later, Vanessa was not there. Another women stated that she would be right back as she had to go upstairs to help clean a room. Within five minutes Vanessa returned somewhat out of breath. When I asked why she was out of breath, she just smiled. I was never more impressed traveling by the way these two people went out of their way to accommodate us. Now you can say they should have had our room ready and blah, blah, blah. I rather look at it as two people bending over backwards to fix a problem, but the problem king of faded away by these folks showing themselves to be two of the most dedicated, honest, and sincere people I’ve ever met. My wife always says, “People are not perfect, but perfect for us!” These people were perfect in trying to help us. I strongly recommend this hotel as they get it right. Thank you so much for making our stay a great one and my entire family looks forwarded to seeing you soon.

author: lucy1038
title: Overall a good option in the area
text: So overall we had a good stay here. We were on vacation and choose the hotel for it's convenient location to the mall and easy access to the Pennsylvania Dutch area. I have broken my review down into pro's and con's. Pros: Excellent location, unlike most of the hotels in this area you can actually walk to the mall very easily (5 mins) on footpaths. The room was great (we had a king suite with a kitchenette), very spacious, clean and all amenities we could need. The staff were very friendly and helpful. Plentiful free parking. Con's: These are small but annoying little things that I have to mention. At check in we were told breakfast Mon-Fri was until 9.30am. When we came down Tuesday at 9.01am it was nearly all cleared away and the staff member on duty said they only ever do breakfast until 9am. This mis-communication was super annoying and meant we only got to grab a small amount of what was still left out. Equally when we went to the pool for a swim at 9,30am there were no towels at all, so we had to go to reception to ask these to be restocked. Finally the air-con in the room cannot be switched off or the fan strength changed, the only control possible is the temperature that you want it to be at. This is annoying for night time noise. Overall we had a good stay and would probably stay here again, although it is expensive compared with other local properties. I would highly recommend asking for a room on the mall side as the rear of the property is right beside the highway.

author: 329tashae
title: Nice stay
text: I stayed here for 2 nights on a back to school shopping trip. When I checked in, the guy was NOT friendly. It was only this one employee as all others were nice. I’m from the south and I’m used to better hospitality. He did allow us to check in an hour early which was nice. Other than that, the room was nice and served it’s purpose. We had the one bedroom suite. It was clean. The lobby area is really nice. We used the pool and hot tub. It was clean and what you expect for a hotel pool. I didn’t use the gym, but it was a nice added extra. Breakfast was good. I enjoyed the selection. All in all, I thought the hotel was a good value in a great location.

author: amandamN2035KN
title: Insanely overpriced for what you get!
text: I decided to pay a little more for this place because it looked nice online and the reviews were pretty good. Bad move. It looks very nice when you walk in but beyond that, not so much. The first thing that annoyed me was that we were staying there for a few days for a dance competition. I was there by myself with two young girls, we were carrying lots and lots of bags, I asked for a luggage carrier and there were none. They didn't know where to find one, they only had a few, I'd just have to wait until one came back down. Meanwhile, there were 3 people JUST STANDING THERE telling me this. Not one of them offered to help in any way. The room...I think we got a handicapped room. Everything was very low to the ground which wasn't too bad except for the bed in the main bedroom. It was literally on the floor and was not comfortable at all!! The blinds were broken, the bathroom smelled super moldy. And I had a pair of shoes that I wore there, we left the next morning to go to breakfast and when we came back my shoes were GONE! Gone. Never saw them again. The following day, we tried going to the VERY SMALL pool in the VERY SMALL pool room. We had to leave after 15 minutes, the concentrated chlorine smell was actually making my eyes water as I was trying to relax and read a book while my girls swam and then we all got headaches. I have to say, they only reason I gave a 3 star was because the breakfast was fantastic!!!! They have made to order omelettes and a variety of things, there was something for each of us. But I would never stay there again!!

author: sweettrip4
title: Mini Vacation!
text: We chose this hotel for its distance to Philadelphia, approx. 30 minutes away give or take depending on traffic. We are glad we did, when we arrived, around 3pm our room was ready for us and all my preferences were met, ie: away from elevators and on the top floor. The woman working at the front desk was friendly and did her job accordingly, nothing special really. Our room was clean and spacious, we loved the mini kitchen since we were there 3 nights it worked out perfectly, it was like having a small apartment. There was only one thing really about the hotel/room that was not so great and that was the proximity to the highway, its very close to a major highway and so if you like us, get a room facing the highway, you will hear plenty of motor vehicle noise, not so great if your a light sleeper which I am (I hear everything) but in saying that we walked so much during the day shopping/sight seeing that when it was time for sleep I was out cold in a matter of minutes! The bed itself and pillows were very comfortable,and the maids did and excellent job at cleaning. One of the highlights of this hotel is the amazing buffet breakfast, we have stayed at plenty of hotels that offer a buffet breakfast, but this one was a step above, so many selections of hot and cold items, not to mention an egg chef ready to prepare omelets how ever you like. In the 3 nights we were there they changed up the breakfast items every day! that's amazing! bravo Hyatt House! I must also mention the staff working the buffet area were all very attentive and helpful always making sure everything was kept clean and stocked. The area in which you eat was fabulous too, very spacious with plenty of places to sit that were spread around quit nicely, with two large TV Screens. This hotel was also within walking distance to King of Prussia mall and plenty of restaurants. We would defiantly stay here again without hesitation, 100% recommended!

author: LLCoolDaveTravel
title: Really Nice Property
text: I was staying at this location for 2 weeks on business. And with the exception on one housekeeping issue (that was resolved)....this is a great property. It is very modern, the rooms are spacious and very clean. The staff is exceptional. The beds are very comfortable and quiet rooms. My room was a king room with living area and kitchen area. This place had all the comforts of home. The gym, I felt, was well equipped. They had a nice indoor pool area, hot tub and I think it had a sauna too but didn't go in there. The daily breakfast buffet was excellent including made to order omelets. It appeared they had a restaurant as well but I did not use that. Had a nice full service bar area too...I can speak of it but my friends say it was fun. Property also has two really nice fire pits that is fun to sit around and socialize. There is a small business center with computers and printer and the property sits right across one of the biggest (if not the biggest) mall in the USA. I really like this place, I think any one would.

author: VirginiaN192
title: Awesome Weekend in PA
text: This was my first time in a Hyatt House and I found it to be an awesome facility with all the amenities. I will definitely seek out more of your "Houses" in the future. Very beautifully done aesthetically. Love the fire pit area outside, the fireplace in the wall in the lobby with the added pool table - family friendly touch. Breakfast staff was pleasant as well as the young lady at the bar Friday and Saturday. Trev and other man at the front desk Friday evening were very nice and helpful. Your location is ideal as we were able to take your shuttle to area restaurants, mall and casino. I would definitely stay here again while visiting my aunt who turned 95 this weekend! On another note - prior to my arrival, I inquired about getting a shuttle/ride from the airport to the hotel and was referred (by a staff woman) to a very nice gentleman Sammy. This was a SUV pick up at the airport to hotel and cost $85 + tip. Sammy was prompt, professional and a friendly gentleman. Not being familiar with the area and possible bad weather kept me from renting a vehicle. When I checked in at 9PM I asked the staff about Uber cost and they informed me it would be about $40. I actually left from my relative's home (8 minutes away) and by choosing "Pool Ride" with Uber, the total cost was only $27. and there were no other riders. I definitely recommend the staff be educated to recommend Uber from the airport for the lower cost!

author: Annaandfam
title: Wow!
text: I am so sorry to be so late on this review. We stayed here a few months ago and were so impressed that I had to make sure I did. First of all, thanks to Laughlin and Baye. These guys were amazing. Helpful, funny, and real! No robots here. They had everything we needed, covered. I wish all hotel staff was more like them. The hotel itself is beautiful, clean and comfortable. Our room with the fully stocked kitchen, glass enclosed shower and giant plushy bed blew me away! And the price was great. Their breakfast is phenomenal and they make omelettes to order. (And they don't give you dirty looks if you put in for another one. I loved this place. I will never stay anywhere else in King of Prussia. Oh, and we didn't use it but they have a shuttle to take you where you want to go! Thanks guys, you made it great! Oh, I almost forgot, we didn't use the pool either but they have a hot tub too and a lift so handicapped people can use the pool and spa. So great!

author: nativenewyorker9
title: Disappointed
text: I have stayed in this hotel many times and have always had great experiences. This stay began mostly the same. Friendly check in and efficiently all feather bedding had been removed and replaced as per my profile and request. I went down for breakfast in the morning and could not find any non-dairy creamer for coffee. I asked the kitchen staff who said they do not have anything non-dairy on weekends. This made no sense. On my way back to my room, without coffee, I inquired at the desk why they no longer have coffee mate or even something else non dairy such as soy or almond milk. She said they did and called the kitchen and asked them to find it for me. It was brought out and I could now have coffee. My question is why was all that effort necessary. I had never had an issue at this hotel before. I have stayed over 100 nights in hotels this year across several different chains. None of which presented this issue. Failure to change this one small issue will cause me and probably several other readers who need non dairy creamer to consider other options for hotels when in the area. I have always liked this hotel so I hope they change back to offering what they had for years.

author: 170shiral
title: Great Hotel
text: The pictures on the site does it no justice! It's nice and cozy here! Staff was awesome the minute we walked in! Hyatt offers mobile check in and check out! Continental breakfast is the best! Staff is great! Rooms are nice and clean! Didn't get a chance to get in the pool because it was undergoing maintenance. I wish we had a better outside view of something other than the highway. Also our room only had a shower and I love baths, but there was no tub! But the water pressure was great! The Hbar offers a small selection of drinks and light menu. I'm sure I will return to this hotel whenever I plan another trip to KOP. And the Mall is directly across the street, supermarket is about 5 minutes away. It's great here.

author: chris13209
title: Very nice hotel
text: This is a very nice place to stay. The whole facility is clean and very well kept. The staff was very friendly and helpful. They have a bar that is open to I think 10pm and they let you take your drinks to your room if you want too. The breakfast they have is great. It changes a little bit every day so it not the same old thing. They will make you an omelette if you want one. The coffee was very good too. Our room was excellent. We got a one bedroom and it was very spacious and clean. It seems like this is a newer hotel, it is modern and well decorated. The hotel is across the street from the king of Prussia mall. It has a joes crab shake next door but it is a mile or less away from some very nice restaurants. It is located just off the highway so it is pretty easy to find. Well kind of. It sits back in off the road and I drove by it once. There are signs for the hotel but there are also signs for joes and babies r us too. They all share the same main entrance. We would definitely stay there again. The price of the hotel was very reasonable too.

author: thirawitl
title: Great hospitality
text: This was my first experience of Hyatt House. I usually stay at Park Hyatt, Grand Hyatt and Regency Hyatt. I was not expecting much. Hyatt House has everything but room service. The bar opens at 5pm and you can order food to take to your room. The bar has a limited offering but it does cover a fairly wide range, the wines are somewhat disappointing. After spending 3 nights, I can say that it was quite enjoyable because the staff were friendly and helpful. For instance, my colleague was staying a a near by hotel. After dinner at Capitol Grille, a great restaurant within walking distance of Hyatt House, we used the courtesy Hyatt bus to drop my colleague off at her hotel. Nice! The next day after attending customer meetings together, my colleague again asked to use the courtesy Hyatt bus to drop her off. The bus was out, but the hostess said we could have a drink at the bar, which not yet official open! When the bus came back, the driver fetched us and my colleague went back to her hotel. Nice touch! Breakfast was included in my room charge. The offer the basics and have an omelete station, again a lovely touch.

author: healthcarestocks
title: Nice Property; Response to Issue was Lacking
text: I stayed one night on a business trip at Hyatt House. The hotel is right next to the King of Prussia Mall so I wouldn't call it a scenic location. That wasn't an issue. The building is actually quite nice and check in was smooth. I had a king bed suite with a small kitchen area. The room (435) had a vaulted ceiling with power operated shades and curtains for the top section. Unfortunately, the lights from the parking lot still come through a bit at night, but that wasn't the issue. Around 4AM, there was a noise coming from the storage closet outside of my room. It sounded like a cat, but i had no idea what it was. I told the front desk when i went for breakfast (included) that it woke me up. Noted it and looked at me like i was crazy. Mentioned it again at check out and the same look. Front desk staff made no attempt to make me happy. A small credit toward the bill would have sufficed, since i was woken up at 4AM. Unlikely to stay here again.

author: D352VJjayh
title: Make sure you put the do not disturb on the door
text: Let me start by saying the primary reason most people pay for a hotel like this is SLEEP. This is a business hotel so when I want to sleep in I dont need a loud knock at 8 AM saying housekeeping. I know you are trying to get your job done early so you can go home but I am trying to SLEEP. Then I get oh sorry I'll tell them to stop from the front desk. First of all, manage your people and tell the housekeeping staff SLEEP is the primary goal of a hotel and knocking on doors before check out time is acceptable. Secondly you cant give me back my SLEEP that I paid for so offer some other comp if you ever want me to come back. Back to the front desk as I walked by this AM the same dour woman who was there and dimissive of me when I checked in was still there in the AM so I guess she was crabby at the beginning and end of her shift. Not a good way to greet your guests in a hotel that cost $229 a nite. Nice looking woman to so probaly unhappy someone who looks like her has to work the front desk at a hotel. Now lets go to the reservation experience. I messed up in my rush and booked the King of Prussia Hyatt Place vs Hyatt House. I called Hyatt Place and the woman Jas was nice enough to agree to cancel the reservation but guided me to make a new one with points before she did . I called Hyatt reservations and spoke to Odyssy who made the reservation at Hyatt House after she told me the points requirement for both were the same. I was later told by the front desk at Hyatt House that was not true and Hyatt House was 8k points vs 6k points for Hyatt Place. I then called back the Hyatt Place and Jas proceeded in error to cancel my second reservation. I then had to call Hyatt reservations again and spoke to Jamie who had to cancel the first reservation I made with $ while putting me on old for a long time to get the hotels permission which I already had and gettig her manager to do the cancellation. The complete lack of respect that Hyatt has for their customers time who have busy lives is terrible. I will use up my Hyatt points and avoid them going forward. I have to say the Westin beds are much nicer anyhow

author: 714megans
title: Great service, large rooms
text: We stayed at Hyatt House King of Prussia for one night before an early flight out of Philadelphia. It was me and two friends, and the room with 2 queen beds was large enough for us all to be comfortable. The room was great, has a good sized tv, a couch, and even a full kitchen with utensils, glasses and cooking supplies. The bathroom was clean and the shower was nice. The beds and pillows were comfortable. As soon as we arrived, there was a lightning storm and an electrical fire down the road, so the whole area was out of power for about an hour. The staff was very good during the event and did everything they could to make everyone comfortable. The pool area is nice. Basic, but still an indoor pool with hot tub and rinsing shower. There is a gym that I didn't use but it looked nice. The complimentary breakfast was fantastic, way better than expected. It was a full buffet with lots of options and an omelet station. I would definitely recommend this hotel and stay there again if I'm in the area. Didn't get to try Joe's Crab Shack right next door due to the power outage. The hotel is across the street from a large mall which is convenient.

author: RDH4U
title: Will definitely stay again!
text: This is the quietest hotel in which I've ever stayed. It's right next to the PA Turnpike, but I never heard the traffic. I also never heard any doors slam, toilets flush or water of any kind from another room and I was on the first floor. The breakfast area was very nice without any plastic (utensils, cups, plates, etc.). Nice selection of hot and cold foods plus someone fulfilling custom omelet orders. The tables are kept clean; salt, pepper, ketchup and tabasco are on each table. My family and I were warmly greeted by Bill. He described the hotels ameneties and gave us good directions to our destination. Comfortable bed, fill size fridge, 2-burner stove, dishwasher, no plastic in the room. Our shower was the size of a bathtub -- nice! We ate dinner at Joe's Crab House, across the parking lot from the hotel. Not too bad. WARNING: DO NOT DEPEND ON YOUR GPS TO GET YOU TO THIS HOTEL. CALL THE HOTEL NUMBER AND WRITE DOWN THE DIRECTIONS GIVEN BY THEM!! The GPS will get you close, but puts you on the PA Turnpike which you don't want, if you're coming from the south.

author: 590colleenh
title: Clean. Classy. Relaxing.
text: Just left our one night stay at Hyatt House, and I'm sad that we can't stay longer! It's clear that attention to detail is something they take seriously here. Check in was quick, and our room wasn't too much of a hike. I'm that person who checks the sheets, towels, and whole room in general for cleanliness, and I was extremely pleased. The room was huge and extremely comfortable. I honestly feel so relaxed like I have just returned from a spa! The staff is courteous and attentive. AND THE BREAKFAST! Breakfast was so delicious, I had three plates! I was looking for a clean and modern place to come after celebrating my fiancé's birthday, and this selection was perfect. I can't say enough wonderful things about Hyatt House Philadelphia/KOP. WE WILL DEFINITELY BE BACK, NO QUESTION! P.S. If they ask you a preference for a room, tell them "away from the elevator!" We were right near the elevator, AND the front desk so we heard dings and rings all day. But it certainly didn't hurt our stay!

author: friedricha2015
title: Really great hotel deal
text: If you are in the swank King of Prussia area of Philadelphia and don't want to shell out 250 dollars a night, this is the place. Because its an easy walking distance to the big mall and about 100 yards either the Capital Grill or Joe's crab shack, this place has you covered. It has a great lobby with 24 hr coffee and a pool table, a small bar, and a great exercise room. The exercise has really good quality ellipticals and treadmills and there are 3 of each plus exercise mats and free weights and a few machines. The pool is shallow but the hot tub is huge. The stay includes a cook to order omelette breakfast. The smallest room is big, with a kitchenette, functioning refrigerator, modern furniture, modern finishes and TV with actual HD. The kitchenette was well stocked with any kitchen utensils, cylinders, pots pans, corkscrews, etc. The corner rooms are cool because they have 16 foot ceilings. If you're light sensitive, opt for the the standard height room as the second floor windows leak light. The bed was firm and comfortable, not just a cheap mattress thrown over a board. In the past year I have seen many of the same faces at the check in counter and they're nice and helpful. For a little extra you can opt for the 1 bedroom and put the kids in the living room on the pull out. The only minor issues I've had were the fake fruit in the lobby, a shortage of towels in the pool area and that the breakfast ends somewhat early. It ended at 9 am on Columbus day, which they didn't consider a hotel holiday. There aren't kids running up and down the halls here, as this caters to the business crowd. Between the ideal location and the great value, this is the only place I stay now when I visit the Philadelphia area.

author: luvWDW
title: Next door to King of Prussia Mall and Valley Forge Historical Park!
text: Another great stay at a Hyatt property hotel! Our room was spacious, clean, modern and the staff were very welcoming and professional. The hot free breakfast (made to order omelets) is always a nice perk! We were only here one night, so we didn't utilize all the amenities available. During breakfast, we were able to play a game of pool. Ask the front desk to check out billiard balls and cues. Nice touch! I have not seen that at any other Hyatt House as of yet. If you like shopping, the hotel is adjacent to the King of Prussia Mall (one of the largest in the US). It's also near the Valley Forge Historical National Park. Before we flew out of the Philadelphia airport, we made a stop here. It's definitely worth a look. It's free to park there. Set aside a couple of hours to view this large park by foot, car, or bike. We chose to bike. A must do, since we were limited on time. We were able to stop at many of the historical landmarks and enjoy the vast views of autumn trees.

author: leroncita
title: Wow!
text: My husband and I were visiting Philadelphia and Lancaster, and decided to search for a hotel deal through Groupon when we found this amazing gem. A cautionary note - there are two Hyatt properties within close proximity of each other in King of Prussia. We went to the wrong property first. The two hotels have a very different feel, and I could tell immediately that I was either in the wrong hotel, or that the lovely lobby pictures on the site were lies. Thankfully, we were in the wrong hotel. Hyatt House is amazing! I am extremely particular when it comes to hotels, and after my stay here, I am a converted Hyatt supporter. The lobby is beautiful. The check-in process was very smooth and within 5 minutes of walking through the entrance, we were on our way to our room. We considered going to the mall to grab something to eat, but after traveling a great distance for the day, we decided to check out the hotel offerings. Our meal was delicious, and our server/bar tender was very pleasant and accommodating. Breakfast in the morning was the best I have ever had at a hotel.
