text: back home a week now. We just wanted to share our experiences abroad in the wonderful patong thailand. Im glad when we booked that we picked such an awesome accomodating address to stay " absolute bangla suites" extending our stay an extra duration we enjoyed it so much. "Location" great! so central to everything, a short walk to shopping, beach and bars. Cleanliness of rooms prestine, kudos to the staff who take care of the upkeep so pleasant and wonderful to talk to an always with a smile, thanks 'Tip' and the decor was 'amazing' with added bonus of the jacuzzi =). we stayed in 2 rooms at absolute bangla ' the studio and the junior suite' and will definitley return in a few months for more. The in-house food was amazing and well priced, your taste buds will agree. We included breakfast in our stay and would strongly suggest the same, a great way to start your day with a beautiful view from the rooftop, some great food and some cool OJ. To get you ready for everything thailand has to offer. Go for a swim on the rooftop pool and laze about sipping cocktails , mixers or beers what ever tickles your fancy. Climax nightclub bar and restaurant competitively priced soooo lean on the wallet, great if you want to catch up on some live sports , listen to music and converse with other holiday goers. 'Grab a bite to eat here people" " a drink" and throw your watch away. Big hello to the team upstairs 'Simon Dave Fong and Pang for the great laughs and quality service it's you guys who add to the atmosphere of the rooftop. Keep it up, Sam and i'll be back for more.

author: LizzyLill
title: Horrible Hotel - extremely noisy and dirty!
text: The Absolute Bangla Suits is well located if you like to be close to bars, discotheques, restaurants etc. It is only 500 to 600 metres away from the beach. The rooms are classy, well equipped and offer a feeling of comfort and high class. However this is all positive that can be said. The hotel is in very close neighbourhood of a very noisy night club (just 15 metres to the left of the hotel) and an even noisier discotheque (20 metres to the right of the hotel). The night club and the discotheque both stop playing the very loud music at 5.30 in the morning only! Sleeping without ear plugs is simply impossible! Occasional hotel parties on the upper floor (next to the pool) add to the noise! We stayed 14 days in the hotel. During 7 of these 14 days the lift was out of order. The staff did not clean the apartement properly. When the bed linen and bed sheets were changed the new ones were covered with lots of large dirt spots etc. We did not receive new shampoo, soap etc. on a daily basis. The floors were not well sweaped, so that quite a bit of sand (from the beach) was still on the floor every day. The garbage was not removed daily! The food in the restaurant is not cheap and not really tasty. We met seven couples that all moved to another hotel because of the ploblems discribed above. Absolute also wanted to move us to one of their other hotels (the Nakalay) which however was located outside of Patong Beach with no beach access and no restaurants, entertainment etc.in their neighbourhood - the complete opposite of the Bangla Suits, but boring.

author: AmsterdamEscape
title: Nice places
text: Staying here at present. Places are nice and different but are not being kept up to their original standard. Decor lovely with red and black as the main colors but getting a little frayed at the edges. Torn bedsheets, holes in towels, chipped and broekn floor tiles and we have an ant invasion in the kitchen. But nothing we cannot handle. We were given a junior suite with no balcony, view is terrible, a sort of back alley. The ones with balcony look a lot better. Bathroom has a rain shower and a super Jacuzzi bath suitable for 2 (nice for couple) . Lovely touches like the blue neon around bed and all around living room. Air-Co good. Fast complimentary internet. Staff friendly and helpful enough. Location perfect. Down a side street (cul de sac) right in the middle of the madness but we can hear zero noise at night as we are located at the back, suites with balconies may hear some noise but the places seems well sound proofed. Beds excellent. All in all excellent I guess.

author: Xarthus
title: Heaven at a price
text: This hotel was simply amazing. We splashed out a little bit as it was our honeymoon and got an upgraded room to ensure we would have a spa though it seems we needn't have worried - all the rooms appeared to have spas (they should make this more obvious on their website!). When we got there, we DID have a problem with the new Tiger bar being built next door - we opened the curtains to find a man with a jackhammer, 2 stories up within arm's reach of our bedroom window... we went right downstairs and I prepared myself for a grand fight when initially we were told the whole hotel was booked out... though within 10 minutes they had us set up in a identical room well away from the noise so we were happy. The rest of the stay I am glad to say was magnificent - the room was VERY spacious with a full sized kitchen (and fridge!) 2 massive TVs, 2 DVD players (one in the main room, one in the bedroom) a nice big bed, wonderfully comfortable couches and a fantastic, roomy spa! The room was always clean and service was prompt. The rooftop bar was nice (if a little pricy) and the pool was nice (if a little small). Best of all, this hotel is RIGHT on the main strip, close to the major shopping centre end - no taxis needed, everything is within walking distance. My only complaints would have been the elevator - it was CONSTANTLY full of service people... we only managed to catch it once or twice the whole time we were there - thankfully we were only on the second floor but it might be worth checking which one you are on as this place is in SORE need of a service lift. The second thing would be the time-share groups... I don't think one day went by where we didn't see at least 10 groups go through... they really seem to push the whole time-share thing though luckily not on us (we have heard others weren't so lucky though). If you want a hotel that is close to the action, comfortable as hell and you don't mind paying for it - this is the place!

author: Mel2309
title: Great staff, clean, perfect for couples, would not recommend for families.
text: We bought a very cheap 'spreets' voucher for a 7 day stay and were very impressed. Staff were wonderful, as a few have said their English isn't great but neither is my Thai... Room was clean, has everything you need. White couch grubby, but this must have been a design choice as who in their right mind would put a white couch in a rental? The restaurant, pool and bar area on the 5th floor is impressive. We had our breakfast up there each day and it was lovely. We didn't eat at the restaurant, however we did have room service one night which was average. This place us in a perfect spot for couples wanting to party, it's in a side street 50m from Bangla road, 150m from the beach. We had our 8 year old with us and made sure we were home before the action started at around 10pm each night, Bangla rd isn't for littlens!! Part of our deal was that we'd sit through a 2 hour sales pitch by the 'ABSOLUTE' crew.... That's 5.5 hours I'll never get back.... Please read reviews on the absolute group before going through their sales pitch, the reviews are scathing. And although our sales guy didn't earn his commission from us on the day, he was nice enough. You do see them throughout the day showing perspective clients through the hotel, but they keep to themselves. All in all a very comfortable stay.

author: Binhar
title: Families Beware!
text: We had stayed in Thailand last June/July and whilst there scratched an Absolute ticket and won 7 nights free accommodation. We chose to come back in March and as we had stayed about 8kms out of Patong, wanted to stay in the heart of Patong. We chose to stay at Absolute Bangla Suites with two children. The week before going I did check tripadvisor and saw some not great reviews, but had high hopes that we were staying in 5 star accommodation as we were promised. When we finally arrived at 8:30 at night after flying all day, we arrived to busy, wonderful Bangla Rd. When we checked in the first thing was that they didn't know our accomm was for 2A & 2C, thankfully I had taken all my confirmation emails. The beds for the kids had to be made up in the living area, so not much room, and then we found out the air-conditioner in the main bedroom was not working and was blowing out hot air. Looking around the two rooms the accomm was 3 star at best with patchy paintwork, the rangehood nearly falling out of the ceiling, furniture chipped and looking old and the cream couch was very grotty and dirty. They sent engineering to look at the air-conditioner and as my hubby is one himself, helped diagnose it needed a new compressor, this was fixed up the next day. We were offered to move rooms for 1 night, but it was so late and the kids were already asleep that we declined and said we would stay where we were. Then the nightclub started in the alley and went until early hours of the morning. I cried for most of the night. On a positive note the pool on the roof is great, the staff and security guards were very friendly. The resort is very busy during the day as prospective buyers of Absolute Destinations were shown a room next to ours so you were always passing people in the corridor. The room next to ours must have been pristine and I thought if only they knew what was next door. We did have an opportunity to share our experience with Absolute sales personnel and were given an apology and they did their best to appease us. I would not recommend this accomm for families. For young couples it is perfect as it is so central to the Patong nightlife.

author: mimio86
title: .....dirty linen/ see through showers
text: ewwww.. My pillow case had dirty grey marks (appears 2 b dust stains) on them - BOTH SIDES! bed sheets had these red stains along with the same dirty grey.. Towels had dark black dots on them, lucky I brought my own towel!! As I walked past a room which was being cleaned, I peered in.. 3 staff was in the room; 1x staff was cleaning, where the other 2 were sitting on the couch talking, 1 of which was also picking her nose!! The shower includes a window with a partially white snowed look.. If ure taking a shower u can c outside.. My friend stayed in room 105 where the shower over looks the front entrance where 2 security guards sit.. I peered through the glass once jus 2 investigate the view frm the shower the security guards were already looking up @ me! We asked reception 2 change our rooms 2 a higer level as we questioned the shower.. The hotel was full n the staff member said they will call the building engineer as the staff stated people frm outside cannot c in.. She called me back m said the engineer confirmed outside camnot c in.. Sooooo.. Who/ what was the security guard looking @? I can even c in frm the entrance!! Its not tinted nor mirror finished.. Siiigh!! Was truly disappointed..

author: kellie177
title: Would never stay here again
text: All we had were problems, i dont know if they even check rooms before putting you in them. We booked the Junior Suite, we were led to beleieve that this room had a spa on balconey which it didn't as the spa was in the bathroom. After 28 hours and 2 hours of arguing they moved us to the penthouse for 1 night (Penthouse is a little bigger and has spa on balconey that is the only difference although the view from the balconey is a brick wall) and then moved us again for the ramaining nights to the executive suite, so 3 moves in 4 days! We tried to cancel reservation and get our money back but they said no. We called the hotel prior to arriving asking them if they could pick us up, the answer was no, although when checking in other stayers arrived in one of their cars. They did allow us to check in early after telling us on the phone we couldn't. We checked in, air-con didnt work, they came and fixed it. Bathroom door to bedroom didnt close. They only gave us 1 card for entry to our room when we asked for another they said no you can leave it at reception with us if you go out although that doesnt always work out as at the moment by partner is in the room asleep as he is sick which means if i go out and take the card he will have no air con, if i dont take the card i will need to wake him to let me back in. Lift didn't work when we arrived, we were on the 2nd floor so it didn't really matter but the pool is on 5th floor which did make it annoying, this was fixed after a few hours. Internet didn't work for the first 5 hours of our stay. Tv reception and internet cuts out at times. Hotel is right in the heart of the nightlife so it is extremely nosiy at times, people screaming fire works ect, construction in also going on next door to hotel which is very very noisy at all times. It was compolsury we had to pay for a christmas eve dinner 1500 baht p/p, food was terriable and not much of it. We tried to have a spa although it didnt have any hot water, they came and fixed within 15 mins, when spa did work we didn't have any water pressure, then the spa leaked from the bottom onto the bathroom floor (luckily there was a drain in the bathroom) When we eventually fall asleep we woke up in a sweat as the power had gone out in our room so we had no air-con, they came and fixed within 30 mins The pool is small and only has about 8 banana lounges ialso think it is open to the public if you are using the restruant. Overall most of our issues were sorted but with difficultly, i dont feel for $350.00 AUS a night we should have any problems!

author: /undefined
title: Just Wow
text: This was the first time we took a long road trip with the family. It was my wife, my mom, my three kids (age 10, 8, 2), and myself. We made it to the hotel on Friday 9/16/16 after a 10 hour trip. We were coming up for the NASCAR race and went to the Lincoln Park Zoo in Chicago. When we got there checking in was easy. We got to our room and there were 3 towels in the bathroom so we went down to the desk to ask for more. We were told just to reuse the ones we have. We said there are 6 of us and only 3 towels, then he gave us 3 more. When we went to take a shower the tub would not drain. After 2 minutes the water was above our ankles every time and rising. It would not drain until 15 minutes after our showers were finished. When you would start the water and then pull up on the faucet to make the water come out of the shower head, it would only push 1/2 of the water threw the head. The toilet would clog almost every time, even just number 1. The lights under water in the pool came out and cut my foot and was floating with exposed wires. When telling the front desk person he just said okay. The only good things I can say about the hotel was it was pretty clean and in a good location. Will not be coming back to this hotel next time we come up to that area.

author: megeg9
title: So disappointed!!
text: First of all I booked this reservation like 2 months in advance and requested the first floor because we have kids and it'd just be easier coming and going. We were told at check-in they weren't able to give us a first floor room because of renovations...which I never saw anything that looked like renovations were happening. Our first room was on the second floor which reeked of cigarette smoke...the whole floor. The room was absolutely disgusting. There was a big wad of chewing gum on the head board of one of the beds, big stains on the floor and walls, scuff marks all over the walls, the window looked like it had not been cleaned...ever, a huge brown/red stain on one of the box springs, smoke detector was dangling by the wires from the ceiling, and the vanity in the bathroom was literally falling apart! There was also a sitting chair in the corner that looked like it had been ripped up by a dog. We took photos of all the issues. We complained...obviously...and was told whoever stayed there before stayed for a couple months. So, I guess they never cleaned the room after?! A maintenance man showed up as we were wheeling our luggage out and he looked disgusted and said "we're gonna have to shut this room down!" I was disgusted that they put a family with kids in a room that awful. They gave us another room on the 3rd floor which was much better, but still not great. Bathroom vanity was broken and the blankets on the beds had holes in them. I have stayed here a few times before and we seem to always have issues. We won't be staying there again. The Comfort Inn next door is more pricey, but much cleaner!

author: Q7264MLrobertw
title: Worst hotel ever!!
text: There was mold around the window, the heating and ac unit also in the fridge. They tried to charge me for my service dog even after I showed them his ID card. The toilet was not anchored to the floor, it had pee and poop all over it. The bed had puke (I believe) down the one side. We had to sleep with a window open bc the mold was so bad. I got the the room for 3 days with my husbands points, contacted Corp and sent pictures of the conditions. I was told I would get a total refund that I still have not received. I am 6 mos pregnant which they were well aware of, and still put us in a room filled with mold. At one point there was nasty bed box springs and other unknown bed parts in the hallway. The lock on the door was broken off as if the door had gotten kicked in. My husband took 3 sips of coffee and violently vomited. The breakfast, well I would not call that breakfast. We left early the next morning. We had driven over 15 hrs to get there then became sick for a few days from the conditions. I have emailed and contacted Corp still with no final resolution.

author: BirdBrainStevensPoin
title: Gross
text: Front Desk Clerk - Unfriendly, rude and NOT helpful at all. He and another worked stood in the lobby and watched as I struggled negotiating my luggage through the two sets of manual entry doors...nice gentlemen! No directions to my room, no information concerning hotel amenities, just give me your money and go away. My Room - This is where it got really scary. Stinky, dirty, dark, and just overall gross. I was completely afraid to take off my shoes and come close to touching the carpet. Ugh, now the bed. Let's see, cigarette burns all over the 1960's bedspread and blanket, stains all over the sheets and a thick layer of dust and crud on top of the headboard. Really, I have to sleep here and pay for the privilege? I would have happily paid the man to leave his hotel had I anywhere else to go at 10:30 pm. From my experience with the bed and the carpet, you can imagine my continued disappointment in the bathroom that didn't look to have been cleaned in quite some time, the dirty walls, door and curtains that were half hanging over the window. You sir, should be absolutely ashamed to charging money for people to stay in this complete sh*& hole. Days Inn & Suites - what in the hell have happened to your standards? Do you even have standards? Wow, complete disappointment and my LAST stay with Days Inn

author: tamimcoats
title: Family Funeral
text: While the Days Inn chain is typically a lower cost hotel, this one is an exception. At over $80 for a standard room with 2 queen beds, I would have expected things to be a little higher quality. There was a distinct moldy smell in the lobby and our room was no different. We turned the fan on constant high and even opened the window while we were physically in the room. That was a positive, that we were able to open the window, but we were on the first floor. My entire family was staying at this hotel, and they all said the same thing, each of the rooms were a bit smelly. One was so bad that he had to change rooms. The smell goes away (or you get used to it). The beds were a bit soft for me, but clean. Single sheeted, which is no longer the norm. The decor is ancient, so is the carpet. There was a spot on the carpet that was so sticky, it took my flip-flop off of my foot when I walked on it! The bathroom floor was sticky, like it was mopped but not rinsed. The service at the front desk was satisfactory. I didn't spend much time checking in, so I don't have an opinion. The exterior is inviting and well lit. Free wi-fi and continental breakfast. The wi-fi is fast and ready when you check in, that's a huge plus in the eyes of my teenage daughter. We didn't partake in the breakfast, so I have no opinion.

author: Old-Socialist
title: There are nicer places, for less
text: After checking in, I went to my room. Upon opening the door, I discovered it was already occupied. How can a motel check someone into a room that is already occupied? I was reassigned another room. The room, itself, was clean and comfortable. But, the corridor was trashed, and the elevator worn and slow, with a damaged control panel. When I did settle into my room, I turned on my computer and connected the the wifi. The wifi kept slamming me with way too many advertisements and pop-up ads. ie: The headline ad alone would display 4 copies of each of the 5 ads. I must assume the local IP has a reputation for searching for online sex because many of the ads were sex ads. The next morning I went down for my "continental breakfast" at 6:10:AM. Although the advertised start time was 5:00:AM, nothing was prepared. And, the clerk just sat and stared; he seemed bewildered that I had the audacity to disturb him while he played with his personal laptop. When the manager arrived at 6:35:AM, I complained about the lack of a breakfast, to which he quickly made up just a small amount of very runny and lumpy waffle batter, then put out a meager collection of white and wheat bread slices to top-off his selection of breakfast items. I felt compelled to call the customer service line to express my opinion about the motel. A few days later the manager called to make amends - by offering me a room at half price the next time I come through the area. The next time I am through that area, I plan to pass-up his offer.

author: KParker_12
title: NEVER stay here!!
text: Please, think before you book! This hotel has a history of bed bugs. When I pulled back the covers to get in bed a huge silverfish ran across the sheets. I also came in contact with 5 roaches during my 5 day stay. I should have known to leave when I checked into my room and the toilet was filled with some else's feces...the bathroom reeked of old urine. Who knows how long it had been sitting there?? When I contacted the front desk about this, they offered no apology, after being firm in the fact that I was not going to stay in a room that smelled like someone else's fecal matter, they rudely told me I could change rooms. The rooms have a horrible odor and feel damp. The staff is HORRIBLE. I stayed there while on a business trip, I was working nights and I told the staff my schedule so the cleaning people would not disturb me during the day. A cleaning woman walked in on me while I was sleeping, right after I had informed them several times of my schedule. Once I went to the front desk, called out "HELLO" loudly, no one answered. I then proceeded to call the hotel from the phone in the lobby.....SURPRISE SURPRISE, someone answered who had OBVIOUSLY heard me call for assistance. Such a rude and inconsiderate staff. The Indian man who owns it is blatantly rude and sarcastic. Moral of the story.....DON'T STAY HERE!!

author: JJJ2003
title: Rudest staff I have ever experienced
text: Was relocating to Ohio from Utah and stopped here along the way. My wife and I were each driving a car, along with our son and dog (a Yorkshire Terrier.) We had planned where we were going to stay beforehand as not all places accept dogs. When we arrived out our planned hotel we were informed that they no longer accepted dogs, leaving us looking for another hotel at about 9 at night (I don't blame the first hotel by the way. If I owned a hotel I probably wouldn't take dogs either). We got online and searched for dog-friendly hotels nearby and found Days Inn. We then called their 800 number and checked for availability and rates. Since my truckbed was full of moving items we were preferably looking for a room with an outside door so that I could keep a close eye on my vehicle, this hotel is not one of those. When I told the operator that I was going to try to find something else she began making deals, she slashed the price once and I was not yet sold, so she slashed the price again and I booked the room for much less than advertised (I can't remember exactly what it was now). So great, we finally found a place to stay. We arrive at the hotel, dead tired of course since we had been driving all day and it was now 10pm or so, and begin gathering our things to head inside. We brought our most valuable items with us instead of putting them in the moving truck, so each night we would take these items to our room with us so that they would be safe. So picture this, my wife and I are dead tired, hauling in a heap of bags and things along with a little dog tucked under my arm and a now screaming three year old in tow. I come to the door and am obviously struggling to get it open, have to set down a suitcase that then falls over, and as I reach down to pick it up one of the hotel workers zips by me, talking on his cellphone the entire time, and basically slams the door in my face. I manage to juggle the door open and check in at the counter. I am now a bit irked of course, especially since the worker that slammed the door in my face is sitting in the lobby having what looks like coffee and a snack with another worker, so when the man checking me in seemed a bit offish I at first assumed it was just me being sensitive. Then the man sees the price that I had paid for the room and begins openly complaining about the franchise and "how do they expect him to stay in business at these rates." The, what I now assume is the owner, then realizes that they had failed to charge me the fee for the dog, at which point he asks me accusingly if I had neglected to tell them that I had a dog. I told him that I had told them about the dog and they must have made a mistake, he then shakes his head, hands me my keys, and grunts my room number. For the remainder of my stay each time I saw him, or what now appeared to be his family members that worked there, I would be drawn into a glaring contest until we were out of eye contact. I am normally quite thick-skinned, and things generally roll right off my back. But the service I received at this hotel really, really, rubbed me the wrong way.

author: travlin4u
title: Great Staff- But not the Cleanest Rooms...
text: The Days Inn in Morris ,Il was very nice, but NOT the cleanest! We had booked a Jacuzzi Suite, ,,,,as the price was right. However,,,,upon check in--- the Jacuzzi Tub was horrible, with scum around the tub- definately noticable, and it had filthy, spotted, mirrors surrounding it! Now this is not to say that this is a dirty hotel! We just feel that the housekeepers could have done a much better job on cleaning the jacuzzi tub and surrounding mirrors. We did notice that the mirrors in the bathroom was also very spotted, and just feel that they could have done a better jobs on mirrors, as well as the building entrance doors... Other than that, the hotel itself was very nice,---and affordable! The beds were comfortable and clean, as well as the rooms! The suite had a microwave and refrigerator. And we felt this was a very nice hotel..... The staff was very accomodating! They also had a free morning buffet, which included beverages, donuts, cereal, and fresh fruits. However,,, We wish that they had fresh bananas instead of spotted, ones.... If the management could* perfect * these few errors in the hotel, We could surely recommend more patrons! Until then...

author: pollyannapoptart
title: A Wonderful boutique hotel.
text: On March 5,2019 I stayed at the lovely Le Royal Hotel in Paris. I traveled to this beautiful hotel with nine of my friends from Chicago. Le Royal is in a great location and there are plenty of restaurant's, shopping, and ATM machines all within walking distance. Le Royal offers a delicious breakfast with cheerful staff. The ladies at the front desk Leticia and Ann were so accommodating and gracious. We had an incident with lost baggage at the airport and Leticia was so helpful. She helped my friend navigate the Internet as well as the forms that were needed in order to retrieve her missing bag. She was kind enough to get my friend an Uber to the airport and help her navigate the Metro back to the hotel. Leticia also gave wonderful suggestions for various restaurant's, sightseeing, and shopping which we all loved. Thank you Leticia for your hospitality!! I'd also like to give a shout out to the gentleman on the overnight shift. The morning we left he made us coffee for our trip back to the airport. Unfortunately, we were not able to see everything Paris has to offer but just enough to make our trip memorable. Merci beaucoup Le Royal! Marianne P. Elburn, IL

author: brenist
title: Lovely little hotel!!
text: We recently stayed here, and we were a bit unsure before arriving, how it would be! We were greeted warmly, and treated with the kindest respect even though I know we looked worse for wear when we walked in! 😂 Long flight + rain + train +rain +metro + getting lost to find the hotel all while dragging our luggage! 😂😂😂 (I wish I could remember all the names of the people that helped us, but I know I will mess them up!) But seriously, Le Royal, your people are your best asset! They were soo kind, and sooo helpful, and so tolerable of my very rusty and very bad French! Our room was adorable, the bed was incredibly comfortable, the bathroom was awesome! Lots of counter space, and the shower was great!! They are located just across the street from an adorable boulangerie, very close to two metro stations, and you walk out the door and can find pretty much anything you need! So a great location! I was VERY thankful for cafe being available whenever you needed it! (Jet lag ensures you will! Ha!) And I was also quite thankful for the breakfast they provided in the morning. It was a lovely little spread of delicious fresh breads, cheeses, meats, yoghurts and fruits, and juices. Perfect to get a start on a full day of walking and sightseeing! We will definitely be coming back to this adorable hotel on our next return trip to Paris! And I would highly recommend it to anyone that is looking for a great place to stay! Thank you again for your kind service to my daughter and I while we were there! ❤️

author: AndyS931
title: the hotel is on decline
text: I stayed at this place about five years ago, and can definitely say that it is on decline. What remains good about the hotel is - the location - easy access from the Charles de Gaulle airport by train, a lot of restaurants in the neighborhood; - rooms that are sufficiently sound-proof. The mattresses are also not bad. The hotel is located in a building that does not seem to be designed as a hotel, so it has rooms of various sizes and shapes. By paying a bit extra, one can get a room that is larger than tiny rooms that dominate the Paris market. I also had a room with a bathtub instead of a shower, which is nice. Negative side: - Not clean or well-maintained at all. The towel drying rack in my bathroom did not work and was covered in rust (see the picture). You can also see about a quarter-inch layer of dust on it. I am a male who travelled alone for business, so I could live with it. No way would I stay there with my wife. - Bathroom amenities were also very scarce. - The breakfast. It was unbelievably meager. Very limited selection of food. Only two types of meat as cold cut. No cheese at all (and this is France!) Stale bread - again, how did the hotel manage to obtain stale bread to serve it? This is France, where bread is always fresh and tastes fantastically. I will not consider staying there again.

author: thomascG3170XP
title: Coffee Anyone?
text: Regardless of your age, if you want to be treated like a child, this hotel is where you want to stay. At Hotel Le Royal Rive Gauche, you are just another incompetent traveler that cannot be trusted to drink a cup of coffee in your room or carry your room key in your pocket when you go outside. I am a retired, 65 year old, Vietnam veteran with 28 years of active service and 15 years as a traveling sales professional. This is the first time I’ve experienced such disregard for my comfort and well being by a hotel which is in business to provide their customers that very thing. The room is nicely appointed, but, there is no coffee, no water, no mini fridge. There are 2 wrapped plastic cups on the sink. Forget the vending machine. So, regardless of when you wake up, you have to get dressed and take an elevator down 4 floors to sit, like a child, in a uncomfortable room, with strangers, so you can be observed drinking a 2.0 ounce cup of Nespresso! We traveled in Italy for 2 weeks, 3 cities, 3 hotels from Amalfi to Siena. Each day, in each one of these hotels, we could make and enjoy coffee in our room. It is one of the pleasures of vacation travel. We could also take our key, which was not attached to a heavy metal paperweight! For our last 4 days of our dream vacation in Europe we chose Paris. When you check in and unpack, you don’t notice everything right away. Being booked through an agency, you cannot easily change hotels. We have enjoyed Paris and the nice French people who make us feel welcome. We did not enjoy this hotel. “Hotel Le Royal Rive Gauche, our CARPET comes first!”

author: B1632LRhannahw
title: Really Good Experience
text: We had a really good experience at this hotel. We stayed here six nights on our first trip to Paris as a couple. It’s located near everything, including restaurants, cafes, Luxembourg Gardens, and it is a short can ride away from the Eiffel Tower and many more monuments and sights. The staff were all friendly and efficient. The bed was very comfortable and I have a bad back so I’m picky. The room is small but we didn’t come to Paris to stay inside a hotel room! The breakfast is charming, nothing fancy but completely adequate. The loungey area near reception is stylish and very nice for reading. The only tiny drawback was the faint urine smell in our room’s toilet area from a toilet bowl brush that wasn’t properly rinsed out. It wasn’t overpowering and in fact my wife couldn’t smell it but I can because I have a sensitive nose. The shower head was a bit tricky to get used to but after a couple times it was fine. The AC was strong. The view charming. The whole experience was very good. I recommend it if you’re looking for an affordable, convenient location!

author: paigeoliverw
title: Everything we needed, and great location!
text: For our first trip to Paris, we used go-today.com and upgraded to Hotel Le Royal in the Montparnasse district of Paris. It could not have been any more perfect. The accommodations: We were in room 23, which is actually the third floor, overlooking Boulevard Raspail. The room was very spacious for Paris, although from the floorplan it looks like other rooms in the hotel are slightly smaller. It was clean and beautiful and had a gorgeous view. The bed was comfortable, there was a bathtub(!), and there was plenty of room for our belongings. We were surprised there was a minibar in the room -- which was great for bringing home cheese. :) The location: We were close to several metro stations, as well as plenty of shops and restaurants (our favorite was Le Bistrot des Champagnes at 6 Rue Léopold Robert, 75014 Paris, France.) We were in a residential section near Saint-Germaine, and the walk to the big attractions along the left bank was fairly easy on days we chose not to use the Metro. We also caught a hop-on, hop-off bus not far from the hotel. The hotel offered most amenities, including wifi, send-out laundry and dry-cleaning, and good deals on a few tourist options (including the dinner cruise on the Seine). If you don't want to pay for send-out laundry, there is a laundromat a couple of blocks from the hotel. We LOVED the area and would stay here again. It's less touristy, but still has everything you need to get to the touristy areas. The staff: I can't say enough positive things about the staff here. For starters, we wound up arriving early in the morning because of a last-minute flight change related to an Air France strike. Though the hotel was completely full the night before, the staff worked to get a room ready shortly after another guest left. They didn't have to do that, so we were SO grateful they could accommodate us. The team was wonderful in every way. Just really lovely, kind (even though our French was horrible) and helpful.

author: Yuki626
title: Perfect Introduction to Paris
text: My boyfriend selected this hotel for our first trip to Paris together. Usually he and I have very different tastes when it comes to hotels, but I must say that Le Royal Rive Gauche was an excellent choice and I was impressed with his selection. The location of the hotel is hard to beat - taxi, bus, metro, and train are all easily accessible. Just being in the Montparnasse district is quite "romantic" and the neighborhood is filled with history and beauty at every turn. The hotel itself has been recently renovated yet has retained its historic character and charm. There is an elevator for guests but 2 people plus luggage is the maximum that can be accommodated. Our room was a junior suite on the 6th floor which had every amenity that we needed. The queen bed was amazingly comfortable and the linens smelled of lavender which was simply divine. Our room was very quiet and we slept soundly each night. The large bathroom had gleaming double sinks, a separate glass enclosed shower, and bathtub. Breakfast was included in our room rate. The selection offered was vast for a continental breakfast - fruit salad, juices, coffee, yogurt, fresh pastries, various cold meats, and really good, piping hot scrambled eggs. We did not leave hungry. The staff at breakfast were always very friendly and greeted us with a smile. It was a pleasure to see them each morning. I would certainly recommend this hotel and would love to return one day myself.

author: M2He
title: Wonderful customer service, excellent hotel
text: We just returned from a 6 night stay at the Hotel Le Royal, and it was delightful. The staff was fantastic, knowledgeable, and helpful. We had 2 rooms on the 4th floor, there is an elevator, but it was small, no problem 2 trips! The room was a very nice size for Paris. The bathroom was very large. There was a fridge, you just needed to ask for the key. I had a room with 2 standard beds pushed together (typical European) and a twin bed for a child. On line pictures are very accurate. Our package included breakfast. Again, very standard Parisian breakfast. They had yogurt, breads, jams, eggs (scrambled and hard boiled) croissants, chocolate and plain, an apple turnover, ham, a salami, cheeses, etc. There was also cereal, milk, juice and coffee. Actually, you could get coffee all day long, bonus! I would certainly return to this hotel. It was 3 block walk (maybe 5 minutes) to 2 different Metro stops, and a 10 minute walk to another. These 3 stops practically covered all of Paris with little transfers. I am a big fan of the subway.

author: cardamomss
title: Spacious hotel, helpful staff, great value for money
text: My husband and I visited for 4 nights with our 17 month old daughter. We had a really comfortable stay that met all our needs. We stayed in a junior suite which not only had plenty of space for a crib and but also extra room to run around for the baby. The room was also 'L' shaped which allowed us to have a small light on that did not disrupt the baby while she was sleeping! The bathroom was large with two sinks and a tub. This is the most spacious hotel room we have stayed in in Paris. We were delighted to find all of this at what, for Paris, was a reasonable price. The bed was comfortable and the room was clean. A few more amenities, like conditioner or curtains that blocked out all window light, would have been much appreciated. But, these are quibbles. Breakfast was served daily. It was fine - scrambled and hardboiled eggs, a selection of fruits, cheeses, breads, and pastries. As well as cereals and juices. The staff were super accommodating and helpful. Someone helped us heat up our daughters dinner in a microwave and we were allowed to use the in room mini-bar to store our daughter's milk. Location is excellent. The hotel is very close to both Montparnasse cemetary and the Luxembourg Gardens, as well as two metro stations that connect you directly to most areas of tourist interest in the city. We were the only family with a small child at this hotel, but we would absolutely return again. We had a great trip and felt very comfortable at Hotel Le Royal.

author: GretchenH174
title: Wonderful Staff, Great Hotel!
text: We went to Paris last month (May 2016). My family had stayed in the same hotel previously and highly recommended the hotel to us. The cleanliness and modern look of the property was impressive for a boutique hotel. But be aware the elevator is VERY small-- which can be typical of European hotels. Every room had its own safe, which was a Godsend with passports and valuables. We paid a bit more and got a room with a balcony-- Deluxe room. It was worth the view! The only down side, was I couldn't plug in my hair appliances into bathroom outlet (even with converter) -worked in bedroom, but mirror was over the bed. We went in May, so no AC until May 16th. The location was so nice- within walking distance to Metro stations and many wonderful cafes. The neighborhood felt safe, as we were 4 women traveling together. We wouldn't have made it without their AMAZING front office staff! Every morning they patiently showed us which Metro to jump on to get to our destination. We were SO grateful for their help!! When we go back to Paris- we would stay in Hotel Le Royal again! As a side note-- we booked through GoToday.com which bundled our flight, transportation to/from airport and hotel in one package. They recommended this hotel originally. Great job everyone! We LOVED PARIS!

author: travel4lifeMinnesota
title: Very small room!
text: The hotel is very close to a variety of metro lines. One which brings you right from the airport. There are also a couple other lines close by. The neighborhood was nice, we found a couple little nice restaurants and places to go to late for drinks. The morning breakfast was ok. Scramble eggs, deli meats, cereals, breads of many assortments. The women who works in the morning was pleasant and very hard working. By the varied reviews there must be a variety of rooms. We must have received the mouse sized room. You could barely stand up straight and walk around the bed . The bed and pillows were not comfortable. The bathroom had been updated, but as others have said it is a tub (which they ask you to shower in) and have only a partial cover so you have to be careful not to get water on the floor. We thought the staff was fine. Last time we were in Paris we rented an apartment in Montmartre which is maybe I had such a difficult time with our small room. We booked through Go-today package, small room?? We were on the 6th floor and the elevator was as big as a phone booth.

author: LHSnow
title: Accessible location, nice neighborhood, friendly staff
text: This hotel is in a great location in terms of the Paris Metro. It was only a few minutes away from the Vavin station, and a short walk to a number of other stations. We traveled to Paris from London via the Eurostar, so it made it easy getting to the hotel. Upon leaving though, our flight to Rome left at 7 am so it was too early for the Metro to be running and get us to the airport in time. One of the hotel staff arranged transportation for us to the airport (CDG) at a fixed cost of 80 euros (total cost for 2 people), which seems quite high. If you need to get to the airport, I would inquire about the cost of a taxi instead for comparison. In addition, the gentleman at the front desk our last night was kind enough to open the breakfast area (extremely) early for us to grab something on our way out. Very friendly staff who were always willing to provide recommendations and answer questions. The rooms were nice, bathrooms were updated, and amenities provided were nice. There were some areas of the bathroom ceiling that were ajar and a little unsettling though. We also had some trouble with the shower as it is a tub with a showerhead, but there is a half plexiglass type door. We had difficulties keeping the water in, so just take note as to try and not make a water mess as we did. There is free breakfast included, but just note that it is a small selection. There are hot scrambled eggs, hard boiled eggs, an assortment of breads, pastries, and croissants, a few cold cut plates, cheese, cereals, milk, orange juice, water, and a hot coffee machine. This selection is not unusual for European hotel breakfasts, so just be aware that if you are looking for more, grab something small here and then eat out later. We did come down late to breakfast right before breakfast closes, but the kind kitchen staff still always made sure there were enough hot scrambled eggs. I might add that some serving utensils for the cold cut meats would be useful, even if just a fork were provided - I noticed several other guests using their hands to grab things, which robbed me of my appetite. There is no hotel restaurant, but there are many restaurants and cafes in the surrounding areas. All in all, we enjoyed our stay very much and wouldn't hesitate to stay here again should we return to Paris.

author: OneTanMomma
title: great location
text: a nice hotel in Paris and conveniently located between two metro stops (within 3 minutes walking distance). Very close to Montparsse Tower and the Catacombs if those are places that are of interest to you. Room was quaint and clean, bathroom was top notch for a Parisian hotel. Our biggest compaint was the wifi signal in our room. Not sure if being on the 4th floor made a difference - but the signal was patchy and intermittent in our room (46). We had to use the lobby for making calls using the wifi and for facetiming families back home. Overall not a huge problem, but inconvenient. The breakfast was filling and standard. Was tired of it by the 3rd day. Would have appreciated a change in the offerings from day to day. The "free" Nespresso machine in the lobby never had any coffee inserts throughout our stay. Finally, there is one particular man on the night shift at the desk. He is mean and miserable and very intimidating. He was less than helpful when we asked some questions regarding the area and metro stops. He make a couple of unsavory remarks to my friend. Other than him, everyone we encountered at the hotel was very pleasant and very accomodating. Overall a fine stay at your hotel.

author: GlenSJ
title: Clean, friendly and modern hotel
text: My fiancée and I stayed here for three nights over August for a quick birthday getaway, booking with airmiles accrued with BA. We flew into CDG and found getting to the hotel very convenient. Hotel le Royal is about 5 minutes walk from Gare de Pont Royal which itself is on the same line as Gare du Nord, on 'RER ligne B' taking about 45 minutes. First impressions were good, the reception is tastefully decorated in a contemporary style, the adjoining breakfast area is under a glass roof and features a mirrored wall which helps make the room feel bright and airy. The receptionist was pleasant and after hearing my best GCSE level 'bonjour' switched to fluent English to check us in. We were given keys to room 52 on the fifth floor and directed to possibly the smallest lift I've ever seen! As our room was booked with airmiles we were given a 'standard' room and had little expectations (it was free after all!) The room was on the small side, with a smaller than double bed. I'm 5ft11 and my fiancée is 6ft3 and both of us were dangling over the edge of the bed. It was however comfortable :) The decor echoed the rest of the hotel and was quite modern and tasteful, the large window looked out over the rear of the building and provided a good amount of light. The bathroom didn't have a bath but the shower was tall friendly and had good water pressure. Location for our stay was very convenient with Montparnasse full of places to eat and drink in the evening. When journeying into Paris the Metro stop Vavin is a minute walk away. Breakfast was included in our stay and served between 7.30 - 10am. Very standard continental fare, croissants, cold meats and boiled eggs etc. Selection could be a bit more varied if I'm honest but what was available was tasty. Overall we enjoyed our stay immensely, the hotel is clean, modern and well positioned. When we do come back to Paris we'll not hesitate to stay here again.

author: Ilovetopraise
title: Good Location and Reasonably Priced!
text: We really liked the Hotel Le Royal in Montparnasse. We had never been to Paris, but were celebrating our 40th, so consulted a friend who had been more than 30 times...our concerns were safety, cost, and central location. We selected this hotel because it was recommended and the pictures looked great. We felt and were safe our whole trip. As matter of fact, the neighborhood people are friendly. We used public transportation for everything and the Metro is only one block away on either side of the hotel. There is someone at the front desk all of the time to assist you with your needs- even metro questions. The cost for a pleasant little hotel is reasonable....probably a three-star by most standards. Remember in Europe, the rooms are very tiny! The pictures made everything look larger- not the case, teenie- tiny by U.S. Standards, but it worked. We traveled with two other couples and our room was bigger than theirs. Very convenient. Right next door (a door away) is an Italian restaurant with good food and reasonable prices. After this are several restaurants and cafes within walking distance. There is an ATM machine on the same block for Euro and lots of stores and bakeries for fresh pastries, even a pharmacy. Pros: Very helpful front desk staff They all speak English- at least enough to do business Small business area for boarding passes, etc. Diverse people from all parts of the world Very neat and clean - rooms and food area Vacuumed daily Great, safe location- we sat on the bench out front at 11:00 p.m., no worries Breakfast included Cons: TV only has 3 English speaking channels- but we didn't come to Paris to watch TV NO WASH CLOTHES (I understand it's not customary in Europe) I really had to get picky to find cons, we liked the hotel a lot.

author: neenee95
title: 3 girls in paris with 3 friends
text: I was impressed with Hotel Le Royal so I decided to finally write a review. My two friends and I really enjoyed our 3 day stay at hotel le royal march 2015. It is a nice clean hotel, close to many restaurants but the streets did not disturb us. Our room had 3 twin size beds and as 3 american sized girls, there was adequate space for our luggage and accessories. The bathroom was also quite large. The hotel is close to 3 metro stations vavin is the closest, raspail, and montparnasse-bienvenue. montparnasse-bienvenue station has a couple of connecting lines and is only 5 minutes away. We never ate at the hotel because there were so many restaurants outside that were nice and the prices were reasonable. We were especially glad once the USD became stronger. I would also suggest bringing cash and changing money near monparnasse tower. It was easy to find and they did not charge a convience fee. Also going up manparnasse tower is a great way to start out your trip. There were practically no lines and no tourist trap craziness when we got there. There is also a roof top where you can see the expanse or paris including the Eiffel Tower. We were also able to walk to the catacombs from the hotel. The staff at the hotel get an A+ in customer service and was very helpful and kind. At the end of our stay we were able to put our luggage in the luggage room since our flight was a couple hours after check out time. I have been in hotels around the world and this is the 1st time I am writing a review for one because I didn't have to pay a fortune for a great time.

author: sirx
title: Affordable and high quality hotel in Paris
text: This hotel exceeded my expectations and I would recommend it to anyone visiting Paris. We stayed for two nights in a twin room paying 140 euros per night. The prices for hotels in Paris are very high, and it is hard to find good hotels for less than 125 euros/night. This one was excellent, the room was big, very clean and nicely decorated. We had a large window facing the main street, but with the windows closed we couldn't hear any noise and the curtains were dark enough so the sleep quality was perfect. In the room there was a safe, mini-bar, hairdryer and free Wi-Fi (with a strong signal and fast). All the staff members, from the reception to the breakfast service and cleaning staff were very friendly and helpful. The reception and waiting area are very nicely decorated. Additionally we were able to leave our luggage in the hotel's luggage-room after check-out. The breakfast is not included in the room price (as in most hotels in Paris), and costs 13 euros/person per night. We had breakfast at the hotel and recommend it, the choice is wide, with bread, croissants, pastries, scrambled eggs, ham, cheese, yogurts, fruit and a large selection of drinks. In terms of the price and quality, it is worth it, the restaurants close to the hotel offer a breakfast of coffee, a croissant and orange juice for 7 euros. The location of the hotel is very convenient. There are two metro stops within a 3-min walk and the area seems safe. There is also a large variety of restaurants and bakeries 3 min away. Overall I think this hotel is much better than a typical 3-star, I would compare it with the best 4-star hotels in which I have stayed. Excellent experience, definitely recommended.

author: Catherine97
title: Great base for Paris with a tween
text: My 12-year old daughter and I stayed here on a recent trip to Paris and found it a very good place to base ourselves. Low key, friendly atmosphere. We paid a little extra for a superior room with a view of the avenue. This was decorated neutrally but nicely, and was of adequate size with a very decent bathroom. The beds were great: super comfortable. We slept extremely well; and the street is not noisy. Air conditioning worked. WiFi did not, which was an irritant when trying to plan the next day. I liked the area. Some historic old cafes, wide boulevards, a neighbourhood supermarket. Not thronged with tourists. Excellent transport options here with Vavin metro stop almost outside the door and the RER Port Royal stop very close at hand (you can get here directly from CdG airport). The hotel is close to the intersection of Boulevard Raspail with Montparnasse, and if you look around the area you find diverse restaurants, shops and cinemas showing some original language (ie English) movies. We had a delicious breakfast with fresh juice and good hot chocolate every day in a cafe a few steps from the hotel (didnt opt for the one in the hotel, largely to save some money!). 15 minutes walk to the ever-lovely Luxembourg gardens, you are close to Rue de Rennes and all its shops. If you prefer to stay on foot, half an hour's stroll gets you to the bank of the Seine and many of the main touristy bits of Paris. Staff were pretty friendly and very accommodating about things like leaving your luggage. There's a nice area to hang about, close to reception with free coffee - this was the only place you could get online we found. I would probably stay here again, despite the Wifi.

author: SuBu16
title: Pleasant Stay
text: Myself and my husband stayed here for my 30th birthday, having stayed here previously in 2012. Location The hotel is next to a couple of Metro stops; we always seemed to use Vavin, which is seconds away from the hotel. There are plenty of places to eat and drink nearby. Staff All of the staff were very pleasant and the receptionist spoke very good English. Room Our room was comfortable and very clean. Unfortunately our window faced a brick wall and so it was very dark. There were toiletries provided in the bathroom. The big downside for us was that there was no tea/coffee making facilities in the room. I realise you can get tea/coffee in the lobby but first thing in the morning or last thing at night, the last thing we wanted to do was wander down to reception in our night clothes! Breakfast Breakfast was lovely. There were teas, coffees, fruit juices, yoghurts, fruit, cheese, cooked meats, bread, croissants, pain au chocolat and eggs. WiFi/Email communication The Wifi in the hotel was terrible. We could not get access in our room and when we did get access down in the lobby, it was very slow. My husband had emailed the hotel about something (I assume relating to my 30th birthday) but he received no response, nor was any mention of it made during our stay, which he was disappointed about. Overall, we were very pleased with our stay and would return again.

author: 127Phil
title: Le Royal Montparnasse "Better Late Than Never"!
text: "Better Late Than Never"! - This is because this review is of our stay at Hotel Le Royal in August 2013 which is 5 months ago! We travelled to Paris by Eurostar on Friday 16th August to celebrate my wife's 60th birthday on the Saturday and travelled back on Eurostar Monday 19th. Our trip was booked with Avios using 17,300 points plus £280.00. Then I spoke to Joe of Domestic Rail 01233 617913 and got return rail tickets from our local station Biggleswade to King's Cross to connect with Eurostar from St Pancras for just £11.00 each. Although not directly related to the review of the hotel anyone travelling on Eurostar might find the following information useful. It seems it is not a good idea to buy your Metro tickets at Gare du Nord because of the potentially long queues. We bought a carnet of 10 Metro tickets at St Pancras for £15.00 although they were £11.90 on the Eurostar train. From Gare du Nord we took the Metro Line 4 to Vavin on Boulevard du Montparnasse and it was a very short walk across the street and around the corner to the right into Boulevard Raspail and we were right on the hotel. We arrived at the hotel at 10.45 in the morning. Check in was not until 2.30pm although Candy on reception was extremely friendly and helpful and allowed us to store our luggage while we made good use of the wait by strolling through the nearby Jardins du Luxembourg. We also visited Le Pantheon (15 euros pp) and had a lovely meal at Aux Charpentiers, Rue Mabillon which is very close to St Sulpice (where you can see the Rose Line) which was our final stop before getting back to the hotel at 3.45. Eric was on duty by that time and I'm not sure if it was because we were celebrating my wife's birthday but he allocated an excellent room (13) just up one short flight of stairs. The room is at the front of the hotel overlooking Boulevard Raspail and I must say we were not bothered in the least by any traffic noise. It was a lovely touch next morning when in honour of my wife's birthday; Eric and a member of staff came to our breakfast table with a brioche with a candle in it. As I am a singer by profession the natural thing to do was to launch into "Happy Birthday" which everyone joined in on. All in all we can thoroughly recommend Le Royal Montparnasse. All of the staff are extremely helpful and speak good English. We were very happy with the breakfast menu, the overall service, the room and facilities. We hope to return soon.

author: /undefined
title: Short break
text: Nice friendly hotel. All reception staff could not have been more helpful. No coffee facilities in room but was available in the lounge area. No tea, but one staff member did find some tea for my husband one of the evenings. This was greatly appreciated after trekking around Paris all day. Family room for four was adequate. Had everything we needed. Had breakfast on the first morning. Was very basic, and at 12 euros each we found this to be an expense we could reduce. The following 2 mornings we went to a local boulangerie where we bought croissants, drops, pain aux raisins for about 10 euros and had breakfast in Luxembourg Gardens enjoying the surroundings. Location was good. Lots of restaurants nearby. You could walk to everything in Paris but you do need your walking legs on. Metro is easy to use, and at 1.70 for a single trip this is quite cheap to do. Would definitely use this hotel again.

author: skierpro
title: Wonderful stay at Le Royal
text: This wonderful small hotel is an excellent place to stay while in Paris. In terms of the pros it has many! Firstly, the rooms were spacious (we were 3 adults and stayed in a triple room with 3 single beds). The rooms have a very luxurious feeling to them and are very well kept and clean! The location of the hotel itself comes with pros and cons of its own. It's located near 2 metro stops which are very convenient but for someone like myself who enjoys speaking english, it was difficult to eat in this area as most of the restaurants and cafes don't expect too many tourists in this area (it's outside of the tourist area perhaps). As a result it was difficult to communicate with the waiters in the many cafes on Montparnasse. Nevertheless, some did make a great effort to find a common ground. Back at the hotel- it was very quiet and sleeping was great. The room we had (58 i believe), had doors (which open completely to let in that breathtaking Parisian air and view) which opened to a yard for school children- however that was never a problem. They were never loud and even if they're too loud for your liking, you can close the doors and turn on the A/C. Now in terms of cons, it has one or two. Firstly, a WARNING TO THOSE WHO NEED WI-FI. Chances are you won't be able to access the free wi-fi on the 4th floor and up (unless it was just me). It was kind of disappointing and i had to count my blessings that i didn't rely on the wi-fi for my communication/directional needs. The second con is more of a caution. Don't buy the breakfast that's included with the hotel. The cafes in the area (especially on Montparnasse) offer great filling breakfasts for the same value- sometimes even less. Eat and enjoy Paris but not in the hotel. It is quite expensive but so are most things in Paris.

author: KirstenPeach
title: Made our trip!
text: My mom and I stayed at Hotel Le Royal for 6 nights with a deal from Go-Today and could not have been happier with our stay. The staff, one gentleman in particular, was so friendly and helpful. Everyone spoke good English and gave us directions on the best way to get to the Louvre/Opera Garnier/etc whenever we needed it. The location of the hotel was absolutely perfect, especially for two women traveling alone. The neighborhood is adorable with several cute sidewalk cafés open well after midnight. This made us feel a lot safer walking home late. While we were originally concerned that our street would be noisy, it didn't reach the inside of the hotel and didn't affect us whatsoever. The breakfast was wonderful! We fully enjoyed walking down every morning to the very cute dining room. Breakfast was an assortment of meats and cheeses, yogurt, fruit salad, apple sauce, boiled eggs, chocolate and plain croissants, french baguettes, orange juice, tea, hot chocolate, coffee, and warm milk. We loved everything! I especially enjoyed the chocolate croissants :) Our room was very comfortable; it was small but that was to be expected from a European hotel, and really cute! Another thing about the location of this hotel: it was so convenient and close to everything! It took 10 minutes to get to the Louvre, 20 minutes to walk to the Eiffel Tower, and for anything further out there were Metro stations just a block away. We also very much appreciated the espresso machine in the lobby! I do not understand any negative feedback, our experience was 100% positive. My mom and I both agreed that there is nowhere we would rather stay than Le Royal for our next visit to Paris :)

author: lbugher
title: Beautiful hotel in Paris!
text: I loved my stay at Hotel Le Royal and I'll definitely seek this place out again when I take my next trip to Paris. The room was really comfortable and not nearly as small as others made it sound like it would be. The location was fabulous. We were able to get around really easily from our hotel and see all the sites. The breakfast was good, but I wasn't prepared. As you know, when you get breakfast in America at a hotel it's kind of a free for all. You can go in your pajamas and no one's going to bat an eye. You grab your styrofoam plate and fill it up with biscuits, gravy, soggy eggs, a couple sausages, and you can take it to your room or sit in the little lobby area with everyone else. You can get your coffee to go on a styrofoam cup. Big cups for drinks. A perfunctory meal to get you started for the day but hardly a culinary experience. I went to breakfast looking like a mess because I thought I could just grab a couple things and take them to my room (I was in a hurry because we only had 2 days and I wanted to make the most of it and not waste my time lingering over coffee in the lobby). To my surprise, all the tables had place settings and there were no napkins of paper plates to take your food out. I broke etiquette and still took some food and got some peevish stares from other patrons. Next time I'll remember to get up on time and not be that trashy American who stuffs food in her purse and takes it to her room. Oops! Otherwise, great place! The staff was nice to me despite taking the food to go upstairs. They didn't seem to mind. But apparently its a faux pas (look at me using my French!) to take your breakfast to go so be a good sport and try not to pretend you're at the Comfort Inn like me ;)

author: Lawrence3178
title: lovely little hotel in a great location
text: stayed at Le Royal for just one night on the 2nd Jan but i wish it had been longer. locating the hotel is very easy - the Metro station is less than 1 min walk away and the hotel is very obvious from the outside. it is located in the busy Latin quarter there are a lot of bars and bistros within a 3 min walk. Once you enter, you notice that everything is spotlessly clean. Reception is fast and efficient and the staff speak perfect English. We stayed on the 2nd floor so took the lift up - as is the case with a lot of hotels in Paris, the lift is very small with just enough room for 2 people. The rooms are very comfortable however ours was very warm...... we opened the windows and i was amazed at how they shut out the noise - the room went from silent to very noisy is the matter of one second! the TV has good reception and there are one or two English speaking channels. the in room safe is very simple to use. The Hotel WiFi is good with decent speeds. The bathroom facilities were good - even though small the shower was amazing! especially after getting in from a long day of walking the city! Breakfast was a typical French breakfast - bread, ham, eggs, preserves, and pastries. Served between 7 and 10am, it was of the buffet style so basically 'all you can eat'! I would suggest you eat a lot if you have a busy day ahead of you.the food quality is good although the water for tea and coffee was warm rather than hot. i will defiantly be staying here again and i would recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a nice well located hotel in the heart of Paris.

author: CharlotteM822
title: Lovely little hotel
text: Brilliant hotel, would definitely recommend. Only 25-40 mins drive from both Orly and Charles de Gaulle airports, and three minutes away from a metro station so the location is perfect. Very nice, safe-feeling area, and near to a four-way crossroads, all of which are heavily populated with great restaurants! This didn't affect the noise level in the room either; there was some construction noise but no street noise like people or cars. We walked most everywhere we went, the hotel is ideally situated to get around if you'd like to see Paris rather than spend all your time on transport! The staff are impeccably polite and very very helpful. The rooms are clean, comfortable and pretty, with lovely furnishings and decorating. The only downside is that the rooms, or ours at least, are/was very small. The bathroom was therefore also small, but the shower was a good size so no real complaints. Air conditioning is available, there was a switch in the room to turn it on and off as we pleased, and the free internet was a real bonus; no fuss to connect, and great speed. A complimentary continental buffet breakfast was also included. The lift is quite small, and wouldn't fit more than two people with luggage, which might be a slight issue if you were a larger group and staying on one of the upper floors, but only really for your first and last day. It was also slightly annoying that you were not allowed an iron in the room, but you could go down to the laundry room at any time and use the one there, just had to ask at the front desk. Check-in and out was smooth and simple, which was particularly notable for us as we were using airmiles vouchers and thought this might be a little more complicated to process, but not at all. On our check-out day, the staff held our luggage for us as check-out time was 11 and our flight was not until the evening, and also booked our taxi to the airport for us. Overall, I would definitely stay at this hotel again and would absolutely recommend it!

author: 51richardm51
title: Great hotel in great location
text: We stayed here between 6-9th April 2012. The hotel has ~ 60 rooms on 6 floors with lift and stair access. We stayed in very nice dluxe rooms on 5th floor with balcony and views over Boulevard Raspail. The hotel is a 20 minute ride from Gare du Nord on tube line 4 with no changes required. It is then 100 metres from either Raspail or Vavin tube stations. The hotel is in a relatively quiet residential area (Montparnasse) with lots of shops, restaurants, cinemas and good transport links to the main sights. The local attractions include Tour Montparnasse with views over Paris from the 59th floor, the Montparnasse cemetery and the Catacoombs. We loved staying in this hotel. Nice rooms, no noise, friendly staff and nice buffet breakfast. There is no restaurant as such. There is wifi and free computer access. Coffee and papers are provided in the small lounge. The staff are very friendly and helpful. We will definately stay here again as we like the hotel and it's location. We can't wait to come back. Perhaps without the children next time !

author: jvmoney
title: Great Location but very small Rooms
text: We stayed here for a few days and the place was beautiful. Very moderately priced, and in such a convenient location (minutes from the metro, with tons of restaurants, etc all within walking distance). The lobby was very modern looking and check in was a breeze. The front desk spoke english and they offered a free morning breakfast (if you woke up early enough). Overall Rooms were very small, and the bathrooms were even smaller. I personally loved the decor throughout, but be careful if you have lots of luggage bc the elevators are small and the stairs were winding. During your stay in France, I highly recommend you try the Crepes, get an expresso at the various cafes, and if you enjoy beers from around the world, I highly recommend the "Desperado". I've traveled quite a bit and have tried tons of beers from all over, and this may have to be my favorite to date. Unfortunately I've been unable to find any west of the atlantic so its something that I look forward to when i travel back to europe. Prices for food was pretty fair, but drinks can get expensive except for wine so be prepared if you're a heavy drinker like myself. Highly recommend you visit Champs Elysees if you like to shop, and get a credit card that doesn't charge international conversion fees (i.e. Capital One offers a free one). The girlfriend bought a few things from LV, and when they offer you the option to convert it to US dollars real time, ask to pay in euros bc you'll get a better exchange rate. I learned the hard way after my first purchase so my loss is your gain. Overall, I would highly recommend this Hotel!

author: Asiana14
title: Very nice hotel with small rooms
text: The hotel is located in a nice neighbourhood. Just walk aroud the corner and there are some nice restaurants. ( a litle bit further there are also some nice pancake restaurants too) Metro station is nearby. The hotel has got a good ambiance and the decoration is very nice. It all looks very well maintained. Breakfast is simple but perfect. Rooms are nice but tiny. You just have enough space to walk around the bed. Also a very small bathroom. Only possible to accomodate one person at a time. Wireless internet acces in the room was good. Tip: Don't want to do all the things you find in a common city guide? In bookstores in Paris you can buy Time Out Paris. It's is an english guide that gives you information about the common tourist attractions but also the hottest spots to go to. I bought the 2011 version and found it very helpfull to spot places a local would know of, but is not mentioned in a typical common guide.

author: Foxy304
title: Cozy and charming, would love to come back
text: We loved our 3-day stay at the Le Royal in April. The hotel is very clean and neat, nicely decorated and cozy. The location is great - lots and lots of little Parisian cafes and restaurants are just around the corner. "Vavin" or Raspail Metro stations are about 3-5 min walk. Reception staff is very friendly and courteous. Our special thanks to Eric, who was very helpful and aided us in finding restaurants, giving advice on attractions, transportation, etc.. Back to the hotel review. We've stayed at the triple room and it was roomy and clean. Nice updates. Large bathroom is modern and convenient - we've had a stall shower and a tub, which was very much enjoyed by my husband and 8 yo son after a day-long walks on the streets of a magnificent city! We liked the breakfast too. It was just perfect for our little family. Teas, coffee, juices, croissants, yogurts, eggs, cheese, cereals, etc. Everything was fresh and tasty :) Summing all up - for the price we've paid - it was SUPERB. Will stay there again and recommend to our friends.

author: MarianSouthYorkshire
title: Would stay here again!
text: Just been recently refurbished ( still painting while we were there) in lovely modern colours chocolate, gold, purple & silver. Booked this from the reviews on this site and it was well worth it. Our 4 night stay was worth every penny. Our friends had a double room, very clean but very small!!, the bathroom had no bath and a VERY small shower. Fresh towels and sheets every day. Beds were very comfortable.Our room was classed as deluxe. A bit larger with a bath. The only critic of this was the shower was very narrow. It was sometimes difficult to not bang either the shower taps or the shower screen. Very nice, however the room was on the front, main road was very noisy. It was quite warm but we couldn't open the windows because of the noise. The staff were great! The continental breakfast was fresh and tasty.But PLEASE tea/coffee making facilities in our room were greatly missed and the coffee machine downstairs was usually out of milk. Plenty of bars /restaurants nearby and the Metro station of Vavin was 5 mins walk away. The Metro system is great and easy to use. Check the prices at restaurants before you eat, some charge more for sitting outside in the sun rather than inside! One thing about the Metro is that it isn't very disabled or pushchair friendly, there are few or no escalators mainly steps & lots of them! This is sometimes difficult with a suitcase. Other than a nice cup of tea being availble when we woke up the hotel was great and we would stay here again but would definitely request a deluxe room!.

author: TeeJayGee74
title: A wonderful experience
text: We stayed at the Le Royal Hotel in Montparnasse for 4 nights in late September after booking online after reading some reviews on this site. We landed at Orly airport and had to catch a bus to Montparnasse, which cost 8 euro each. Sadly the bus ride took longer than anticipated due to protest marches through Paris, so the trip took about an hour, usually though, we were told, it takes 30 minutes. We had to then walk about 3 blocks to the hotel because as we later found out, most maps in Paris are not to scale!!!! The hotel was very nice. The manager was fantastic upon our arrival (and throughout our stay), giving us information on where and how to travel through the busy Parisien streets. The hotel room was very nice, but small, although apparently, by Paris standards it was about average. The room itself was extremely quiet and peaceful. The hotel was also very quiet and peaceful, which was appreciated after a day of sightseeing around Paris. The buffet breakfast costs 11 euro extra per person/per day, its a little bit pricey for what you get, its basically a continental brekkie, but it is all you can eat, so my advice, is to eat up!!! Wonderful restaurants around the corner in Montparnasse Boulevard. The hop on, hop off bus departs a block up the road on Raspail Boulevard, which is very handy. Directly across the road from the hotel there is a bus which will take you directly into the heart of Paris, again, very handy. Free wifi in the rooms is a huge bonus, although at times it can be a bit slow. For the price, I would recommend a stay here, it is money well spent!!

author: MrsFussbags
title: Lovely little quiet hotel
text: Spent only one night here sadly, as I thought this hotel was great. I booked a freebie with airmiles so fully expected to be in a tiny room over looking the bins... but our room was big and front facing. Very clean, nicely decorated. Polite and helpful staff. Our room was quiet, no complaints there. Breakfast was perfectly reasonable for me, but if you are looking for a belly busting english or with masses of choice then you might be a bit disappointed. However top marks for serving on white china (not those dreadful mugs) and the room was very clean and well presented. There are lots of cafes within a tiny distance from the hotel so you wont have to go far if you are pooped after a day sightseeing. Very near Metro for all the sights. I thought the area was fine, we did not feel uncomfortable walking back from the metro at about ten thirty pm. Free wi fii (ask at desk for your code) which had my other half jumping around like he had frogs legs with his iPhone... he could get the football results which kept him quiet while I had a bath. Sadly though, now most frenchmen call me "madame". No longer am I "madamoiselle", which was my only complaint about the trip!!! Good little hotel says madame le Sac de fuss.

author: Ex-Buffalonian
title: Idyllic, small hotel in one of the most atmospheric parts of Paris
