You will need a golf cart to get into town which is only about a 15 minute ride but it's worth it. You can enjoy the "city" at night and go back to peace and quiet. I will definitely be going back!

author: JFiddler
title: Excellent
text: Our family of four (two adults, two grown adult children) stayed at Athen's Gate for 16 days over Christmas and New Years. It was wonderful! E and Ruth were both fabulous, as was Javier. Our three bedroom condo was awesome, with great furniture and good beds. The only small issue for us was realizing that there was no king bed and that the master opened (through bi-fold closet doors) to the living room. For us, with older kids (19 and 20), they couldn't really spend time in the living room after our bedtime as there was little privacy. But, other than that, the condo was fabulous! Clean, spacious, well appointed (could use salt, pepper and some oil) and quiet. The pool was lovely and the drinks, made by Ruth, were great! One thing...around the pool it would be useful to have a sign letting people know to be quiet, respectful...no splashing, etc. There were some instances where it may, or may not, have been helpful. E arranged for us to rent paddle boards for the week, which was a great way to check out the beach and coast. He also helped organize various snorkelling trips. The resort had bikes so we could bike into town, but we also rented a cart, which is nice to have on the really hot days. We would definitely be back!

author: U4196PGdons
title: AWESOME TRIP!!!!
text: Athens Gate is by far one of the nicest places to stay on Ambergris Caye. The facility itself is extremely clean and well equipped if you want to cook yourself. Direct TV in each bedroom provides all of the television amenities of the U.S. The Wi-Fi is adequate but not state of the art. We had 4 people in the Condo and sometimes it worked well and others it did not. The condo has a washer and dryer set that works well and also daily maid service. The location is perfect. The condo is a 15 minute golf cart ride from downtown San Pedro. Far enough away to be secluded but close enough to be convenient. There is a small grocery store right around the corner for last minute items. The property is maintained extremely well by "E". He is there and willing to help for anything at all you may need from booking excursions to teaching you about fishing from the pier to getting the bikes ready for you to ride. He is a fantastic property manager who seems to foresee your every need. If staying at Athens Gate we would highly recommend booking any excursions through "E". All in all we would highly recommend a trip to Belize and staying at Athens Gate.

author: jenr760
title: The best vacation ever!
text: My husband and I recently took a trip with another couple and stayed at Athens Gate. The moment we landed and told the airport attendant we were staying at Athens Gate, we learned that Carlos was on his way to pick us up (without us asking!). When we arrived at Athens Gate (about 3 miles from the airport/town), "E", the operations manager of the property, was there to greet us, let us into our condo, and had a welcome drink ready for us at the bar after we settled in. It took us about a day to adjust to island life (with the help of some locals that we met at the bar), which means that you relax and do what you want to do, when you want to do it, and if you don't get around to it then that's ok! The view from the property is absolutely gorgeous. The pictures on the website are gorgeous and are extremely accurate. There is no reason to ever leave the property (I would have been content sitting on the beach the entire time soaking up the sun and the view), but if you want to and aren't sure what to do during your vacation, just ask E! During our stay, E set us up with 2 tandem kayaks and snorkeling equipment (both supplied by Athens Gate). They also had a golf cart for us to rent so we could get to and from town. We were able to get some good recommendations from E and the locals on what to do in town on any given day. E also chartered a boat for us for a very reasonable price on the last day of our stay. Our knowledgeable boat captain (Dave) took us to 3 local snorkeling locations and to Caye Caulker for lunch. What an amazing way to wrap up the trip. All excursions, bar tabs, and cab rides were conveniently added to our bill to settle up at the end of the trip. Leaving the condo, our bags were taken to the cab for us and cab scheduled to pick us up (again, without asking!) based on our flight times. The condo itself was fully furnished, very clean, with every amenity you could need. If there was something it didn't have, E got it for us personally, or he told us where to get it. What sets Athens Gate apart (and why we will stay here every time we come back) is the service and the care that is taken to make sure guests have the best experience possible on Ambergris Caye. Best vacation ever...we will be back!

author: N1910JNrobertm
title: Unbeliezeable
text: All reviews are so true! Dad with two kids, 24 yr old son and 20 year old daughter on family vacation. We had the BEST time. We've traveled extensively in the past, and Athens Gate is the top of the top. Kudos to E and James. San Pedro, once you get acclimated, is great. Kids met lots of nice people in town at friendly bars. Contact Manny at Manuel's Bar on the Beach for personalized snorkeling, fishing or just to be on his boat to go across to Caye Caulker for the day or half day. A very nice guy. E recommended the Reef Restaurant, a "locals" place. Best fish, etc. Reasonably priced. If you can't be happy on Ambergris Caye, you can't be happy. ... Especially at Athens Gate... it is a gem. We hope to be able to go back soon.

author: Seoul2013
title: After 2 visits to Belize this is my favorite property in Ambergris Caye
text: We live in San Diego. This is our return trip to Belize. We came a couple years ago (also during July) and stayed at Pelican Reef Villas, which was amazing; I have to say it is a hard choice between the 2 properties. Our stay at Pelican was our first experience, Lori the manager, gave me so much information from the first phone call and everything she said was dead on. The things that I think people do not realize looking at retouched pictures and clever angles are things like the beach. Most properties North of Pelican and Athens Gate have a seawall and although the sand is beautiful you cannot access the water by just walking into it. There is very little foot traffic on your beach compared to others, as it is not a thoroughfare like they are in the middle of San Pedro. When you sit on the beach with a cup of coffee early in the morning you really get to experience paradise, it is so quiet and peaceful. The staff checks on you literally every time you glance in their direction. The amazing part is that they treat you the same whether you walk up to the bar with a beer from your fridge or a beer from theirs. They just don't act like they are trying to sell you something they act like they are trying to fulfill your every need. They will help to book activities and although it is probably slightly more expensive than booking your own, they use top-notch tour operators and lets face it do you really want to take a chance that you picked the right one? "E" and James could both work at the Ritz Carlton and be customer service employees of the month, but I'm glad they work here. We stayed in a 2 bedroom ON the beach at Pelican and a 3 bedroom ON the beach at Athens Gate, Amazing rooms, very modern, very home-like. Here is some of my Belize advice...Spend at least one day in the pool swimming laps up to the swim-up bar. Jump off the pier and swim at night, Spend one day with Oliver for the beach BBQ (this is the absolute best day, and that includes ALL of the trips we did in 14 days of hard vacationing), Get up early even if you don't get up early, you are not invincible put on sunscreen and bug spray, Take a whole day and a golf cart and resort hop as far north as Portofino (make sure you stop at Palapa Bar). This time when we went we really paid attention to the top 20 properties on the island listed on Trip Advisor in case we found something better for next time; and hands down I don't think you will find a better location coupled with a better property and a better experience. My suggestion to you is stay at Athens Gate if this is you first trip, you definitely wont be disappointed and i doubt you will move for your second trip, you can't go wrong at Pelican Reef either. This will be a yearly destination for us and i have nothing but great memories.

author: TaraB765
title: Paradise- Truly a Home away from Home
text: This was one of the best vacations I have had in such a long time. Belize- Ambergris Caye and the surrounding islands were so beautiful. I can see why it is voted #1. I was traveling with one of girl on a girls getaway from the busy cities and chillax and go on little adventures. Athens Gate was the best place on the island in my opinion, as far as resorts. The property is very new and well kept grounds. I loved the view with the docks running out to the ocean with huts and Athens Gate has these huge pilars and a lighthouse-- well it's really bathrooms. It was a boutique spot and lovely. The staff 'E' and James were awesome. Even the little dog J-Lo, she was my dog away from home. I highly recommend this hotel/resort. They have everything, we went kayaking and we rented a golf cart for the week and rode to town. The only complaints I have were the mosquitoes were out of control at night---pretty much all over outside of town. And we didn't realize how close the jungle was and never made it there... I want to go back all the time and I wish I lived here... it was so sad leaving. Such a memorable experience.

author: Snuzuluz
title: Very attentive staff!
text: My wife, daughter and I spent a week at Athens Gate in Belize. We had never been to Belize before, didn't know what to expect, but the staff at this place made it very easy. "E", as the resort manager goes by, is great....very helpful, and just a good human being. His sidekick, James, is also a good person and by the end of our week, we referred to him as "mini me"! James was very helpful, personable, great bar tender, and really cared about our well being. (The staff, including Pamela, really makes this place special!) The rooms were very nice....large, nicely equipped, and always kept clean. The sister property, Pelican Reef, down the way, appeared to be nice as well. We had breakfast there a couple of times which was only about a 5 minute walk. Athens Gate is very nice....great pool, on the beach, decent bar, keg of Belikin beer, and good people. We felt like we were the only people staying there with all the attention given to us. E and James helped arrange all trips including zip lining on the main land, cave tubing, snorkeling, and dinners. All were first class with no issues. They picked us up at the airport on time and had our golf cart ready to go when we arrived. Although there is no restaurant on the grounds, there is an excellent Tex-Mex place right across the street with very good service. We happened to be there during the rainy season which attracts numerous mosquitoes. James and E were always there to help with bug spray and a drink. We will come back to Belize and stay again at Athens Gate.

author: Z5706DRlisaw
title: Been everywhere and one of my favorites!!
text: I feel bad it has taken me so long to write this review!! I tell everyone that will listen what an amazing time we had at Athens Gate. From the booking phone call Rhonda was so sweet! Took extra time explaining everything we should do it Belize and what information I would need. I instantly felt comfortable with our decision to not only go to Belize but to stay at Athens Gate. We ended up missing the flight to San Pedro and needing to take a different flight. I was worried how I was going to get a hold of the resort to let them know, I didn't have great phone service. We landed in San Pedro, it was pouring rain and there was E waiting for us :) I said I think you are picking up someone else because I never go ahold of you to tell you what out travel plans were. He said nope I'm her for you. Come to find out they had been on the phone for hours calling our last resort, tracking down the person that took us to the airport and found out what flight we took just so they could be there for us when we landed. In a foreign country it was such a comforting feeling knowing that they were taking care of us. They booked our tours, make our dinner reservations, served us drinks. We were spoiled rotten! The rooms are enormous!! Like a 2 bd suite. Brand new. Huge verandas that we sat at for breakfast every morning. They also have an amazing Tex-Mex restaurant across the street. It will always be one of my very favorite and most memorable vacations. Can't wait to go back!

author: synergii1
title: The most incredible vacation spot in the world!
text: The resort is pretty much brand new. Athens gate is the sister property of Pelican Reef and about 800 meters away from each other. I was really upset when we tried to book Pelican Reef and was told we would have to move rooms in the middle of the week due to a wedding happening that weekend. After a few calls, Greg suggested that we stay at their other resort Athens Gate and assured us that we would love it just as much. This was probably the BEST decision that was made on our part by booking a whole week on a whim. When we got to Athens Gate we were blown away by the immaculate condition it was in. The pool was so sparking clean and had a waterfall that trickled down to the pool from the "lighthouse". We had an ocean view facing out and it was perfect! I felt like my friend and I were the only ones on the whole property. Not many people know about this gem, and most people perfect to stay in town they are wrong! This was ultimate luxury being only 2 miles from town. Everyday we had housekeeping clean our rooms, wash our dishes from our cooking, and stock up on new Eco-Fresh body products. I felt like we were staying in a timeshare resort! Everything in the kitchen was brand new including use of a blender to make your own fresh fruit drinks from town. They had all Frigidaire appliances that also looked brand new. "E" and James and the rest of the staff including "J-Lo" the little Chihuahua were the most friendly and warm staff I've ever encountered. Seriously after a week they felt like family. "E" was always so quick to make great suggestions for us in town, and book anything we needed for activities, and even went deep in the water dragging a kayak for us to use on the ocean. I really wished we owned a little piece of Athens Gate because I hope to return back once a year and enjoy relaxation at its finest.

author: joec264
title: Conchy Joe
text: As a person that travels for a living, I thought I had experienced everything that was possible.That was until I stayed at Athens Gate. The owners have risen the bar on excellence. Yes, the condos are perfect, spotless and with all the amenities that is expected from a five star location. It is the staff and the attention to detail that far exceeds anything that I have experienced. You can find no better a staff that is willing and eager to make sure your stay is enjoyable. I was a quarter mile away on the beach when James appeared with a towel. He noticed that I needed one and ran one to me. E has a knack of knowing what you want before you do. In setting up tours, sailing, etc. E gets you what you want-not steering you towards just a few. No inside deals here. It is what is best for the customer! The grounds are beautiful. I made a game out of trying to find one leaf out of place and never found one. The beach seemed to be constantly raked. Nothing but white sand. I found paradise.

author: bagswife
title: Beyond perfect.
text: This is our 3rd trip to Athens Gate and I can say that it is always perfection. This place is truly our home away from home. Rhonda and Mr Joe are gracious hosts and will do anything to make you feel comfortable. The accommodations are nothing less than spectacular. If that we're not enough the rest of the staff is nothing less than wonderful. Eliazar "E" is there to handle everything for you from excursions to drinks. He can get you a catamaran or search the island for cinnamon bread. Anything you need he is there. Plus he is one heck of a nice guy. He has become an honorary member of our family and we are glad to have him. James is a newer addition to this group and he is pretty great as well and makes a mean dirty banana! John keeps the ground well maintained and provided my daughter with as many coconuts as her heart desired. San Pedro is a special place and Athens Gate is no exception. Truly I don't understand why Athens gate is ranked any less than #1 EVER! We've been to the island 5 times in 5 years and the last 3 have been spent here (once at the sister property Pelican Reef). The other properties only try to duplicate the perfection that is Athen's Gate.

author: Yourluckyday
title: Great Choice
text: The people at Athens Gate were wonderful. They were very helpful in making reservations for all activities on the island. It didn't matter if it was dinner, diving, snorkel trips, golf carts, cabs they would do it. E, the concierge, was awesome and helpful. The property itself is beautiful. The rooms are very spacious and nice, clean, and decorated tastefully. The kitchens are nice with brand new appliances and full refrigerators, granite counters and plenty of seating. The televisions are a little small, okay a lot small, but I can give that up for a week when you think of all the other things you can do here. The pool is nice and the common areas are very welcoming. My only complaint is that the wireless internet would not work in our room. I had to go down by the pool to log into the internet, which isn't all bad but we thought the internet would be accesible in our condo and it was not. I would stay here again and would recommend it to anyone going to San Pedro for vacation. They also have a restaurant next to the property which was very good also. They are located south of town so you will either need to rent a golf cart or pay a small fee for taxis everytime you want to go in and out of town. We did the golf cart and were glad because we had freedom of movement. There are many good restaurants in close proximity to Athens Gate and would take 10-15 minutes in the golf cart to reach. They are actually closer than you think its just that roads are pretty bad and you cannot drive as fast as you would in the states. We liked going into town and we used the golf cart to go to a local grocery store for supplies for our kitchen.

author: shellier_12
title: Should be renamed HEavEn's GatE....
text: What I found was a little piece of Heaven when I arrived at Athen's Gate. After the easy communication and booking process by Rhonda, she offered to also book our hopper plane from BZE airport to San Pedro. She also took care of the taxi to/from the airport/condo. They even have their own golf carts for rent. The cost was simply added to our credit card upon arrival! When we arrived, we were greeted by a big smile from a man named "E". I capitalized the letter "E" in the title, because without the owners capitalizing on this rare gem, it would just be another beautiful condo. "E" definitely makes this resort a treasure. "E" gave us valuable info, a map of the city with recommendations, booked all of our excursions, cleaned and bbq'd food for guests, bartended, arranged transportation, got fresh coconuts from trees to use for our tropical drinks, washed our dirty golf cart, and the list goes on! No matter what your desire, "E" graciously handled it with a smile. "E's" two assistant staff were exceptionally helpful and as nice as they come! Rhonda and Joe were on site, and would always ask how our accommodations were and if we needed anything. At the same time, they kept their distance so that we felt as if the place was ours. Wonderfully nice and helpful people. Their property is immaculate, including the sand freshly raked every morning. They have housekeeping and it is a full amenity property. It was so refreshing to stay in a location where people have an older set of values: trust, communication, and respect. My friend stayed at Xanadu the year before (for a higher $$$ and less space/conditions) & said this was WAY better and one of the best vacations she has EVER had (and she has traveled the world). I have recommended this property to everyone & I am saving my money for my next vacation to HEavEn's GatE.......THANK YOU TO ALL!!!!!!

author: DustinB363
title: Athens Gate Resort-Best in San Pedro, Belize
text: I had a fabulous trip to Athens Gate Resort in San Pedro, Belize. When I flew into the airport I was taken back in times quite a few years to a much more peaceful time, people on golf carts, very few cars and everyone was so friendly. When I arrived at Athens Gate Resort by prearranged transportation by Rhonda at Athens Gate I was greeted by the ever so friendly and helpful driver Alberto. When Arriving at Athens Gate I was greeted by Mr. Joe and Rhonda, they both were so sweet and kind and let me know if there was anything at all that I needed to please let them know. They also sent me to their wonderful pool bartender to lineup any snorkel/dive trips which i did. Everything in the rooms looked brand new, the 2 building are engineered to absolute perfection and beauty!! I felt like the "King Of The Island" staying here. The furnishings were amazing and the view was even more amazing. I also lined up a dive trip through Eliazar (E) with Rico's Tuff Enough Dive Center, did my first intro to dive, it was amazing swimming alongside horse eyed jacks, enormous grouper, sea turtles nurse sharks and sting rays. Also was able to catch a few Kelly McGuire shows while on the island, he is a Belize favorite and from time to time flies in from Texas for some R and R and to do a few shows in San Pedro. Most of his music is written about San Pedro Island, Athens Gate is even mentioned in some of his songs and Ambergris Caye, all of his cd's are a must have for San Pedro visitors and troprock fans as well!!! Anyway, I will never stay anywhere except Athens Gate Resort and would recommend it to anyone that was planning a trip to San Pedro, Belize!!! Make sure you check out Mr. Joe's Lonestar Tex-Mex Cantina directly across from the resort, it is amazing food and the best Chicken Fried Texas Steak in all of Belize I assure you!! Thanks again to everyone at Athens Gate Resort, Mr Joe, Rhonda, Eliazar, John, James,Josh, Rebel and Chino for making my stay unbelievable and unforgettable, I hope to be back very soon!!!

author: SharonD270
title: Best place to stay, excellent service,
text: We stayed Decemeber 14 - 21st and had an excellent vacation. The condo exceeded expectations and we have stayed at 5 star hotels in the past. The tap water was reverse osmosis and there was a full kitchen plus washer/dryer. The view was incredible. We fished and snorkeled right off the dock and caught barracuda, snapper and a crab. The restaurant across the street, Joe's Lone Star Grill, had the best Grouper meal on the island as well as the best chicken fried steak anywhere! The concierge service was stellar. All we had to do is ask "E" and he would deliver the best boats on the island. If you love fishing, we caught snapper until our hands had blisters. We enjoyed a private night snorkel with Barbar that was unbelievable. If you haven't seen a green moray eel at night with flashlights, you really should! The picnic all day excursion with Oliver and Brian was an adventure that included fishing, snorkeling and a delicious meal. Make sure you book with your room because all of the above trips helped to make this the best vacation I have ever taken (including vacations in Europe and Hawaii). You can use the bikes and kayaks from the resort and should. We rented a golf cart and ate at some very good restaurants. Wild Mango had great small plates and excellent ceviche. Carolines was freshly prepared and one of the best places to eat.

author: DennisD963
title: Couldn't be better
text: Just got back last night. Couple points worth mentioning: - The complex owners, Joe and Rhonda, were excellent hosts. I travel abroad fairly frequently and have experienced none better. - The units themselves are top of the line everything. From the artwork to the kitchens, all premium. - The staff. The best part of the complex. Everything written about "E" the concierge is true. This guy works magic. The support staff that works with E is great as well. Housekeeping staff was great and Johnathon was helpful and friendly. I talked to people staying in other resorts, they did not have this same experience. Fishing off the pier was pretty good, bring your own poles, but spend most of your time in the morning and night. Snorkeling off the pier was great, but you need to go to Hol Chan during the day and also for a night snorkel (just ask E). This is my first review on TripAdvisor, but I felt compelled to write it based on the 'couldn't have been better experience' I had. I would not stay anywhere else, and I am contemplating having my destination wedding down there. Ps. Have E set you up with the Oliver day trip.. with the spear fishing and private lobster cookout!

author: Kristy_DC
title: Loved it!
text: My husband and I stayed at Athens Gate with another couple in late May / early June. Upon arrival, we were met by the infamous E, who greeted us by name and brought us to the bar to get us checked in. We had booked a 2 bedroom unit, but were upgraded to a larger 3 bedroom unit because it was available. E met our every need, from moving our luggage to the new unit to scheduling our excursions (Mayan ruins, zip lining, and fishing), to recommending restaurants. He was a wealth of knowledge, and we wound up hanging out with him by the pool for hours. The owners, Mr. Joe and his wife, Rhonda, were always on the property, and were very nice and accommodating. They own the Tex-Mex restaurant right across the street, where we ate several delicious breakfasts and dinners. The pool was immaculate, and the beach was beautiful. Both of our units were clean, beautifully furnished, and afforded wonderful views of the pool and beach. The 3 bedroom unit was closer to the beach, which we loved. We caught a lot of fish on our fishing trip, which we brought over to Pelican Reef. The cook there prepared the fish for us while we hung out with the two bartenders, and had a relaxing afternoon. After a week at Athens Gate, I was NOT ready to leave. I am looking forward to going back, and wouldn't hesitate to recommend it to anyone.

author: BeachFanLis
title: Amazing staff, luxury residences, excellent atmosphere
text: My boyfriend and I, plus our friends who are also a couple, split a two bedroom at Athen's Gate for an 8 day trip. We came with other friends who split other 2 and three bedroom condos. Our trip was wonderful, and we owe our amazing experience to the staff at Athen's Gate, specifically the bartender/organizer/knower of all "E." E met us when we first arrived, mixed us a rum punch to welcome us, called us a taxi whenever we needed one, recommended the best restaurants in town, set up scuba and snorkeling trips for us, arranged for a yoga instructor to teach us yoga by the pool, called a masseuse to massage us on the beach, and was overall just a joy to talk to and hang out with. Along with the great staff at Athen's Gate, the condos were absolutely beautiful. The builders paid very close attention to detail, and everything has a luxurious feel to it (my one friend loved the kitchen so much she said she wanted to recreate it in her house at home). The only thing to be aware of is that while the master bedroom is huge, the second bedroom is pretty small. However, the living areas (living room, kitchen, even the patio) are also huge , so if you're not worried about spending a lot of time in the second bedroom, then it's not a big deal. The pool is awesome, with a great view of the beach, and concrete stools in the water next to the pool bar. The lighthouse structure at the pool houses the bar and two restrooms (so you don't have to run back up to your room). The beach is quiet and serene, with white sand and crystal blue water. There is a lot of sea grass in the water, so we didn't do much wading out into it. But the sea grass does also mean that there's a lot of life in the water (hermit crabs and fish). The pier next to Athen's Gate has a platform on the end with lounge chairs. There are also steps down to the water so you can easily get in and swim or snorkel. We snorkeled under the pier and saw a huge school of fish, two angel fish, and a ray. Athen's Gate has free bikes, kayaks, and a small catamaran that you can check out whenever you'd like. We biked into town a few times and also took out the kayaks. I would absolutely recommend Athen's Gate to any of my friends, and we'd definitely consider returning. We had a wonderful trip.

author: yukoncanada
title: A slice of paradise
text: Stayed at Athen's Gate for 2 weeks in March, 2011 in a 2 bed/2 bath condo. These units are large and comfortable. The central air makes them great to come home to on those hot humid days. The decks are large and all have wonderful views. The location of Athen's Gate is in my view perfect. Away from the hustle & bustle of San Pedro but only a 10 minute ride by golf cart (renting a golf cart is worth every penny). You can wander down the beach to Pelican Reef for breakfast or lunch if you don't want to prepare your own meal. Many restaurants to choose from in town. I would recommend Hidden Treasures or Blue Water Grill as my top choices. The owner Mr. Joe and wife live on site and make you feel very welcome. "E" runs the bar and is the "go to guy". He is so very helpful and is a fountain of information about what to see and do. If you wish he will arrange your tours for you with reputable agencies that have a proven track record. I strongly recommend that you do so as there are too many agencies to chose from. During our stay in San Pedro we did visit the other resorts and not once did I see one that I would prefer over Athen's Gate. I recommend it without hesitation.

author: ndser
title: Elegant Base For Exploring Durban
text: We stayed at Essenwood House in Durban for 4-nights in late Oct ($87). The Essenwood is located in the chic suburb of Berea on a ridge overlooking downtown Durban. You entered the property through a security gate and down a steep, narrow driveway to a parking area with the house to the right. The 2-storey house retains the appearance of the mansion (circa 1929) it once was, a stately building with shutters, verandas and patios, with a garage to the side, that faces a nicely landscaped lawn and garden around a large pool (nice seating area around the pool, with views of the monkeys in the trees). The 1st floor housed the office, parlour and seating area, and the restaurant and kitchen; the guest rooms were on both floors (all with a patio of deck) and above the garage. Our room, over the garage, was huge with a spacious sitting area (wicker chairs, table, antique desk and chair, cabinet with mini-fridge and TV) in front of the 2 twin beds pushed together to form a king and fronted by a bench. There were 2 huge clothes cabinets in an alcove by the door, a modern AC unit (no overhead fan), and 19th century paintings on the walls; 2 windows provided good light. There was a view only of the parking lot, and it was the only room without a deck or patio. The room did show its age, though, with unscreened double-sash windows that made mosquitoes an issue (they had to be kept closed most of the time) and scuffed and dated wood trim and furnishings. The bathroom was huge, with a vanity with double sinks, a 6' long bathtub, a large shower (unfortunately, the water temperature fluctuated constantly) and heated towel racks. Breakfast was not extensive but was quite good – fruit salad, yogurt and cheese and a full English hot breakfast – choice of eggs, bacon, mushrooms and tomatoes. Essenwood was close to the many good restaurants on Florida Ave – a 5-min taxi drive (R25) that avoided the issue of having wine or beer with the meal. Most of downtown Durban was also close, - Shaka Marine World was only a 15-min drive away. In summary, Essenwood House provided comfortable and spacious accommodations in an elegant setting close to downtown Durban. It served as a good base for exploring the area.

author: travelplansr
title: Fantastic place to stay. Service from the heart
text: Stayed 3-nights at Essenwood House and wow what a great place. From pre-booking via email to my arrival, and the stay itself, the owners John and Paddy made me feel very welcome. I totally felt at home immediately. The room was a large, very spacious, high ceiling property with a huge bathroom (separate tub and shower) and a wonderful balcony with views of the Durban seaside area. It has a well stocked mini-bar with very reasonable prices and a nice tea service as well. The property is immaculate and well taken care of. It has a warm homey feel to it vs. an impersonal hotel like atmosphere. It is well located, very quiet, and has excellent security. It is just a short downhill walk to a Florida Street with tons of restaurants and pubs. If the property was excellent, the service was even better and truly heartfelt. I had a punishing schedule, leaving early in the mornings and back late each day. John gave up his fish and chips one night so I could eat, and Paddy thoughtfully and proactively had a home cooked meal prepared for me when she realized I might be dead tired after a long trip to the game reserve. I felt so guilty for not being able to eat it as I had made other plans, but THANK YOU Paddy. I was really touched by your thoughtfulness and care. I would happily recommend Essenwood House to anyone visiting the Durban area. John and Paddy just know how to do it right and will take good care of you.

author: bigles
title: Wonderful Olde Worlde Service. Perfect location & a personal approach
text: We have just returned from 11 nights at Essenwood House. I cannot recommend this accomodation highly enough. John, the 4th generation owner and his excellent staff could not do enough for us. Fabulous huge rooms with a bathroom larger than many hotel rooms we have stayed in. Fresh cotton sheets daily and a view of Durban to the Indian Ocean. Paradise. The breakfast is to die for. Fresh fruit salads, yogurts, evertthing cooked frest to order, delicious warm croisants and fresh squeezed orange juice, Yum ! We ate outside when we were able to listening to the exotic birds and watching for cheeky wild monkeys who raided our fruit bowl one day when we left the window ajar. Essenwood House is a safe haven only 10 minutes to the beaches and night life by hire car or taxi. Totally recommended. Durban is wonderful city and South Africa a destination we shall return to again and again. Do take time to do a proper Safari. We took 3 days with a personal guide who treated us like royalty. Do hire a car. Driving is safe, easy and on the left. Restaurents are half the price of the UK and service is great.

author: Cookingaround
title: The worst Hotel that I have been in.
text: I reserved this place at the last minute and I did not really go through the reviews. It stated with RUDE cold stone-faced receptionists that had a hard time speaking English. The main elevator did not work and we had to go way into the back and use the staff elevator, ( this has been broken for months ). One of our beds were the worst I have ever seen, under the cover sheet was covers with hair, dirt, dead insects and the mattress was stained. We slept in the other bed that was not so bad. The place was a sauna, topped off with the outside roof ventilators running all night kept us awake. The one (only) pillow was flat and the cheap curtains would not keep out the light in the morning. The towels in the washroom were washed but badly stained. On the walls and side wooden areas of the wooding bed frames had (looked like) nose goblins and blood spots. As for breakfast, we had no salt, peppers, knives, forks napkins on the tables, water downed juices, and only the good sausages and bacon was served halfway through the breakfast time (talk about cheap). I noticed this as we were leaving back to the suite. After reading the reviews (to late) we decided not to complain and just stay the night and transfer to another hotel. This has to be the WORST HOTEL I have ever stayed in. All in all, this place should be shut down. Now Mr. Administrator you can add your "cut and paste" comments

author: mp66
title: Average but great location
text: Stayed at the Gromada recently in a group of ten for three nights, celebrating a mates birthday. Chose the hotel mainly because of the bed situation - lots of twins available, and the free breakfast - easier to all meet up in a morning. Had read the location was good, but not having visited the city before, couldn't really judge initially. Check-in (arrived around 8pm) was handled efficiently, and all booked in within a few minutes. Not exactly over the top with the welcome, but certainly not rude, but offered only the bear minimum of information - breakfast times and the direction to to rooms. It's said the hotel is dated - and is - a bit stuck in the 80s, although it's clean. The bathrooms seemed to be much more up-to-date than the bed areas. Beds were a little uncomfortable, but nothing to complain about - just not up to modern standards. There was a good choice for breakfast - especially if you like sausages. Not sure of the quality of the food - I stuck to toast, but none of the party complained and all seemed satisfied. In terms of location - it is in a great place. Old Town (where we spent most of the time) is a 25 minute walk away - the Palace of Culture just 10 minutes or so. There are quite a few Metro stations within easy walk too, but we just stuck to walking to ensure we saw more of the city. There are lots of bars and restaurants within easy walking distance too. We got a good price for the 10 of us and so the Gromada proved to be very economical - something we needed to consider for all our group's different budgets. Overall, the Gromada is an average hotel, with an average price tag - but in a great location. If you're working to a budget, but still want a central location, I'd be happy to recommend, but don't expect it to be of the quality and standards of the larger chain hotels. Would I stay again - well I'd certainly consider it...

author: OperaBeginner
title: Central and budget-priced but this year, with added mosquitoes!
text: I’ve stayed for the weekend at this hotel five times in the last six years, at the same time of the year, i.e. late September. It is centrally located – less than a five minute walk from the Palace of Culture – and budget-priced for an ensuite room: £35 / 203zl a night, including breakfast The hotel looks like a car park that’s been turned into a hotel and is very big: there is an annexe and I had to walk down an endless corridor to get to my room. It has the slowest hotel lift in the world which is no joke when you are tired and don’t want to face the stairs. The breakfast is good but will never win awards: there is a large selection of hot and cold food (three varieties of sausage) ice-cold boiled eggs but also hot scrambled eggs, meat, cheese, fish, vegetable dishes, machine made coffee and miserable Lipton’s ‘tea’. The cereal is coco pops or bird seed-type muesli. There are only two rooms for breakfast and the hotel is large, the weekend I stayed the Warsaw marathon was on and the hotel was full. This means that if you have breakfast at a peak time, you will have to hunt for somewhere to sit and hold on to your table when you go to get some more food – difficult if you are on your own like me. On the Saturday, I arrived when the dining rooms were not too busy but on the Sunday, I had to move tables twice, finding that ‘my’ table had been taken when I had got up to get some more food. There were also some youth tour groups of the brat kind which I could have done without so early in the day. But. This year, it was mosquito hell for me. I was bitten severely, on my ears, face, arms and legs. I tried to kill the ones I could see, leaving bloody stains on the curtains and walls, which I then tried to wash off but I couldn’t get them all. I tried to close the window but it just would not close tight. I didn’t know that mosquitoes in Warsaw in September were a problem and, this is the first time it has happened to me in five years at this hotel. So, I don’t know about returning next year.

author: LudekL
title: Gromada - Central Warsaw
text: Having read many negative reviews, I was worried that maybe I should have booked elsewhere. However my fears turned out to be groundless. The location is superb, within walking distance of just about anywhere a tourist may go, There are very many restaurants and bars in the near vicinity, including a superb Wedel hot chocolate and coffee shop next door - try their chocolate marzipan tart! My room was in the old part, and for some reason I was allocated accommodation with disabled facilities - an extra large bathroom. My only minor gripe was that the bed was just right for me, I'm 6ft 2ins and would have liked something slightly larger. The room was clean and serviced daily. Service was pleasant, prompt and cheerful. In reception and foyer bar. Breakfasts were a little chaotic, due to the large number of guests milling around. But the food selection was adequate, with scrambled eggs, sausages, as well as a selection of cold food, Bread was fresh and tasty. The elevator/lift looks modern. Don't be fooled and walk. It's much quicker. The heat wave had passed when I arrived so I can't comment on cooling and air -conditioning. All in all a much better experience than expected. Very good value. Recommended.

author: JohnB7987
title: A Dump to Say the Least
text: The lobby fools you upon entrance. It has been updated. However, the entire hotel is old, so expect everything to follow along the same path. The only elevator takes forever to come to the lobby and move from floor to floor. It is faster to walk up and down the stairs. The elevator sometimes does not work at all. The rooms are as old as the hotel. The rooms have never been refurbished. The bed mattress was sinking to the floor as it was never changed. The room was never painted and had marks all over the wall. The room was dimly lit. The internet did not work in the room my entire stay. The phone in the room did not work as well. You can call the lobby but no one ever picks up. Overall, the hotel calls itself a 3 to 4 star property when in fact it is a 1 star property; basically it is a dump. However, the price is inexpensive and the location is centrally located. The also serve a buffet breakfast which is fine. Only stay here if you are desperate; you can find better hotels nearby that are much better for the same price.

author: A_Jorge_Leite
title: Only on a budget
text: I stayed in this hotel 4 days on a business trip to Warsaw on October 2014. It is superbly located, close to the main monuments and historic sites (what's left of them, since this city was leveled when the Nazis left it in 1944/45). It´s quite a large Hotel with long corridors, old style. Clean as you would expect. I was somewhat disapointed with the breakfast, though..Poor, not well presented, no care for detail. Sausages were greasy, the eggs soggy, looking like it was cooked in the early hours of the morning or the day before...One of the days the bread wasn't even fresh... And the room...Be aware that I have nothing to complain as far as cleanliness is concerned,but everything else was mediocre. I was in a 2-bed room. Both beds squeaked and the sheets were not smooth to the touch. The furniture was quite old and the same goes for the bathroom. Evrything worked with ease although the towels were too rough. The decor was lousy and the carpet floor all stained. And someone smoked there before I arrived.. All in all, not a pleasant place to be. Only if you are really on a budget

author: FrancescoCrn
title: Good, old-fashioned hotel with amazing location
text: We stayed at Gromada Dom Chłopa for one night only, as we had a stopover in Warszawa. With the help of GPS, and our previous knowledge of the city, we managed to reach it late in the evening without any particular problem, even if there are roadworks everywhere in the surroundings. Unfortunately, they didn't have any free non-smoker room, but the room we got assigned to (1st floor, older part of the building) didn't really smell of smoke. I am very sensitive to it, but it didn't bother me at all in this case. The room was big, and the bathroom as well. The furniture was old-fashioned, but in good condition, and very functional. It remembered me of People's Republic of Poland times! There was even dedicated space to put our suitcase. Complimentary water included. The TV was a comfortably big CRT set. I was interested only in Polish channels, so I cannot comment on the full array of channels. The beds were old, but it didn't affect my sleep quality (being a heavy sleeper helps). OK buffet breakfast, but the choice wasn't the biggest. There could have been more fresh vegetables. Personally, I didn't like their twaróg cheese. Besides, it was pretty standard, in a positive meaning. I would return again to this properly, if they keep competitive prices.

author: sedasek
title: Business trip
text: I spent there one week. The location of the hotel is quite good, personnel itself was just fine, can't complain about them. From the other things, I think i can find just rather negative ones: * The hotel is not so small. There is just one lift though, which is unbelievably slow, so almost of no use. * Breakfast room and its organization not really good enough for the amount of people (overcrowded, hard to move around, personnel often not managing re-supply missing food). * Though I stayed for a week, they gave me every time wifi password valid for 24 hours only, so one had to ask for a new one every day. * The hotel was not as clean as I'd expected on a similar kind of hotel. The corridor walls were quite dirty, the same the carpets in the corridors or in the room. * The furniture (at least in my room) looked like it still remembers the time of USSR : ). * The mattresses looked like rather some cheap ones. For me personally, not much comfortable. And noisy : ) * The desk was just enough for one person, not possible to sit two people with two laptops at it. * No electric plug close to the desk where one could connect e.g. his/her laptop. * Not able to provide more than one key from the room (though we were officially two of us at the room). * No aircon. The room was quite hot even during the time we were there (May), good luck during the hot summer... * No fridge / minibar / hot water kettle in the room. * No hotel slippers / comb / toothpaste / toothbrush / body lotion / shampoo (only available some shower gel).

author: Prosiakowski
title: Hotel Gromada Center Warsaw (staying end of Nov-Dec 2013)
text: This hotel is an epic reincarnation of the Soviet misery. It's unsurprising that half of their visitors are actually Belarusians, Russians & other folks from the post-USSR space. Arrogant, pretentious and lazy service at the reception, poor and noisy breakfast, metal (!) mattresses in some rooms, unreliable Internet, awkward restaurant inside the hotel. But most importantly it stinks...You feel that poisoning smell already from the elevator. At some floors it becomes unbearable. They use some cleaning detergent which caused me allergy, minor eye infection and insomnia. Half of the rooms are deprived of the tea facilities and refrigerators. The elevators are hell slow. And if you are lucky to be in their newer corpus (the one with slightly better rooms and some catering facilities inside the rooms, but often deprived of WiFi instead...) be sure that it will take you 10-12 minutes just to reach your room by two elevators. This hotel also hits my record with laundry delivery - 2,5 days after I handled it to the reception...Obviously nothing like fitness center, sauna or swimming pool - but that's of course expected. A ridiculous aspect is that they do live both a gas and non-gas water in the rooms as a courtesy: fine! but when you open the non-gas bottle you realize that it is still mildly gas-ed. Therefore, for someone who drinks only natural water, that "generosity" of the hotel virtually does not make sense. The only truly positive thing about this hotel is its location, right in between the main railway station with its shopping centers and the central and cutest street of Warsaw, ul. Nowy Swiat. Shame that they abuse that luxurious position to offer such a terrible service. Warsaw is a great city and it's for sure has much more to offer!

author: Tfl1
title: Should rename this place The GRIMada!
text: I stayed here for 5 nites during a recent business visit to Warsaw. The hotel was booked by my client so I had no say - but they were nice and booked me a suite. Or so the booking said. I wrote to them in advance, asking for a few things but I never got a reply to the email and there was no sign of it in my folio when I checked in. Also at check in, all knowledge of suites vanished - I was assigned a double bed room - the checkin staff seemed incapable of understanding that I had expected a suite, not a double room so I gave up on that bit of luxury. As others have noted, this hotel is in two buildings connected by a walkway on the 1st floor and served by one of the slowest lifts on the planet. From reception to the room was as long as 10 minutes (especially as the other wing had only one lift working). The staff at reception and in the bar seemed largely devoid of humour or any sort of personality - although this did get better on the last two days for some reason. Breakfast was mediocre, the scrambled eggs very watery on 2 occasions, the bread rolls a bit stale over the weekend and the whole atmosphere less than cheerful. The bed itself was comfortable but a new mattress would be useful as it was quite worn (W-shaped if you know what I mean). The wired internet never worked (despite my writing in advance and asking for a room with good access) and the wireless was often very, very slow and on a few occasions non-existent. On the plus side, the room was very quiet with the windows shut, and the shower was excellent - loads of hot water and good pressure. The location was good for my work, and there was a wealth of small places to eat just a stone's throw form the place. If required, I'd stay here again for the convenient location and quiet room, but I'd prefer to stay in a better place if at all possible. All in all, it was a pretty grim place.

author: InternationBroomball
title: Good Value to a Degree
text: An older but very spacious and large hotel in downtown Warsaw that has seen better days. This is the classic “you get what you paid for”, and if you have a low budget it is an excellent buy for a couple of nights. Rooms are older but clean. There is a unique circular elevator in the main lobby, however, if you are in a hurry...take the stairs! Front desk Staff are very courteous and will help with all your needs and directions around the city. WiFi is available but inconsistent in the rooms, but then again...its free. Excellent reception in the lobby area. Breakfast was included and I would recommend it. Good selection and very much a cultural experience. The down side was our room location compared to the outside activities. We had a street view with every activity imaginable within 200 meters of the hotel. Everything from blaring disco night club music to motor bikes testing the loudest exhaust systems in the world were all part of the hotel experience (until 3-4 am). Sleep was not on the agenda! Highly recommend taking the rooms on the courtyard side. Less noise I’m told. The up side is the location. It’s walking distance to “the remarkable Old Town”. A must see for any traveler and also close to the many pre and post war museums as well as the central train station. The hotel also has some great amenities pertaining to the lounge area and the courtyard which is under used for the location. Bottom line...Not bad for bargain basement pricing

author: LeszekS_11
title: Center location, but average hotel
text: Gromada Hotel is located in the heart of the city. But meant geografically and by attractions of night live. Unfortunatelly it is not smoothly communicated from airport, train or even public transport. You have to walk for a while, and "enjoy" noises of Your wheel-suitcase on the sidewalks. This is a big hotel, which means two minor things for U: - queues at the check-in, especially 6-8 P.M. (only 2 persons in service) - crowdy breakfast room Rooms. All is depending on the part of the hotel. New - is quite OK. Old - nightmare, old beds with sprigs attacking Your back. I think that reservations are distingushing thoose, so avoid "tourist" rooms. Anyway - the rooms are average, nothing special but it is still 3* hotel so no luxury expected. You have a large room with a bathroom with shower (general amenities provided). The breakfast - as I said is crowdy, sometimes You will spot an empty containers, but it is filled up quickly. Just sit up to anybody with smile. Breakfast is really nice, even better to some network 4* chains. Scramble eggs are real, not from powder, and You will find a nice choice of polish meats. I'll say - more that you'll expect from 3* hotel.

author: Jade97
title: Clean basic hotel and good location, expect no more than that.
text: I was in a standard room in the 'new' wing which has two single beds. The room, towels and linen were clean. The room is decent sized but very basic. Location is 2 minutes walk from Nowy Swiat and busstops, very convenient. In the 'new' wing there is no wi-fi in room. There is wired internet in room which was free. So, bring your own router for wi-fi devices, or you could sit in the lobby or a nearby Starbucks for wi-fi. Breakfast was included in the room rate I paid. There were both cold and hot selections for breakfast, but if you arrive after 8:30am, hot food was basically cold food. Other than that, expect nothing more. Not good value for money. The front desk is perpetually too busy to answer phone calls if you call for service from your room. As a couple of other reviewers have said, it took a long time to check in/check out or to get anything from the front desk. You have to go to the front desk to get even a hairdryer. The room rate is overall reasonable compared to other pricier hotels. If you are after a very basic, centrally located hotel, this is an ok option.

author: LongJohnSliver
title: Convenient hotel spoiled by poor services
text: I am hoping to write a review of this hotel's restaurant under a separate heading. It deserves special mention for the excellence of its traditional Polish cooking, better, and better value, than many of the well-known chains and cafes in the city. The hotel itself is a mixed bag. Built in the 1930s, it's a big place with memories of former glories pervading the reception hall, ghosts of the Comintern years when the Dom Chlopa no doubt hosted conferences of middle ranking Party bureaucrats. It boasts a central hydraulic lift that is itself a museum piece, a Futuristic tube of glass and steel, glacially slow and reeking of motor lubricant. The rooms are adequately comfortable, the breakfasts OK, reception staff friendly, the location central and convenient. But I'm determined to do what little I can to expose the wi-fi ripoff that plagues so many mid-range and budget hotels. As long as hotels install a wi-fi router of some kind they think they can advertise internet access in every room. But the temptation to cut corners by using a cheaper, weak, possibly domestic style router must be huge. In so many places the wi-fi signal in rooms is simply not strong enough to carry a busy hotel's-worth of internet traffic. It was farcically bad at the Gromada and the hotel's IT operative openly admitted as much to me. So the promise of wi-fi in every room was frustratingly meaningless because it hardly ever worked, despite complaint after complaint. It is just an empty promise to travellers working abroad who these days rely on the internet for business and, even more, that crucial contact with home. I hope other Tripadvisor reviewers highlight this annoyance. Because, failure to provide a service promised in the price, amounts to ripping off the guests.

author: stanj
title: Seeing the reviews, I had to double check if we had the right hotel
text: I was unexpectedly in Warsaw for a week starting August 29 2012 and from the airport for a few nights at the Radisson and was surprised by the very good price(under $70) for a last minute reservation. I did not know my duration because it was a trip interruption getting a visa to another country corrected by their embassy in Warsaw. After very pleasant 2 days I found that I would be there a week so decided to book a different hotel close into the Old Town so I could be a tourist and walk, outdoor dine and visit museums within walking distance. I found the Gromada Dom Chlopa for about the same price but well situated near where I wanted to explore. When I say it I knew it looked familiar with layout and construction as being like dozens of old Soviet style hotels in Eastern Europe. My room did nothing to change that impression, even the smell of the old carpets and hard center sagging single beds reminded me of USSR 1975. It did have some things going for it, a nice central courtyard beer garden, a good location near cafes, music bars, Old Town etc. The rooms in the main section were anything but nice, in furnishings, bedding, common areas etc. It is not all bad, the cafe/bar had low cost beer, there is an attached restaurant which I did not try and it had wireless internet which required getting a new password at the front desk ever 24 hours. Although there were no bad experiences, the lobby staff was pleasant enough but not what would be called "friendly" it only amplified what a super deal I got from the prior hotel. Compared to my prior trips to Poland, which is a friendly easy-going place this hotel was the only let down on the trip. It does not take much to please me but I would never bring a partner or family member. My main goal was to be out during the day until late at night walking or socializing so having a less comfortable room with bad beds and linen did not cause problems. My suggestion would be to look for something a little better and stay in close to Old Town if you are a tourist or want the night life of that area. If the weather is hot, forget it, no air conditioning although windows did open onto the courtyard. There are some nice hotels in the area and many nice apartment/BB and residency houses that are very attractive and clean. Midweek rates in the higher end hotels are very reasonable in Warsaw, $100 gets a very nice place from M-F

author: susiern
title: Pleasant Stay
text: This was my first trip to Poland & being of Polish decent, I was very excited to finally be there. I stayed with family, but a week we traveled around staying in hotels to visit the sites. The Gromada was a good place to stay because it was close to the Old Town & New Town, within walking distance. My room was a very good size, some USA hotels have smaller rooms. It had 2 big windows that allowed a lot of fresh air in. I love to sleep with the windows open. There wasn't much of a view, but I wasn't in my room other than for sleeping. There were 2 single beds with great pillows & comforters. The bathroom was modern with a shower, clean & offered small soaps, which some hotels do not in Poland. I was on the 3rd floor so the elevator was important to me as I have bad arthritic knees. The breakfast was great & plentiful with a big variety of things to choose from from breads, cheeses, eggs, sausage, fruit, cereals, pastry, tea, coffee, juice, etc. This was included in the price of the room which was nice. The price was great too compared to USA standards. It only cost ~$60 I think, don't exactly remember. The hotel staff was helpful & offered some suggestions for dinner & maps of the city. There is a gift shop that was nice, since I wasn't able to find everything I wanted in the city center. I only have 1 negative thing to say & that is there are no blow dryers in the bathrooms & you have to ask for one at the front desk & they were all out when I did. So bring your own.

author: Polskamom1
title: Free internet
text: Gromada Dom Chlopa (center of the city) I booked in the new section of the hote. I reserved a Standard Plus Twin room in order to get into the new section which supposedly has air conditioning. In order to get to the room we had to take the elevator from the lobby up to the second floor, get off the elevator, cross the "bridge" to the other building, get on that elevator and take it up to our floor. Not a big deal but you should allow extra time to get from room to the lobby or vice versa. The room was not air conditioned (though it had a thermostat) and the window only opened from the top. Our room was on the side of the hotel that overlooked the older section (including lobby) and the driveway. Tour buses coming and going at all hours and loud people were an issue if the window was open. The beds were OK. Only English station on the TV was Al-Jezeera! Free internet in the room and in the lobby is nice. Can't understand why more expensive hotels charge for internet. Bathroom with shower was a good size and included a towel warmer which can also be used to dry items you've had to launder in the sink. No shampoo or bar soap in the room. Like many Polish hotels, Gromada Dom Chlopa (center of the city) uses liquid hand and bath soap. Shower drain was a bit slow but turning down the water pressure prevented a problem. Breakfast buffet was included in the price of the room but it was pretty bad. I've eaten breakfasts in a lot of Polish hotels (all over Poland) and this was one of the worst. Desk clerks speak English and are very helpful when it comes to calling taxis, giving directions and the like. Old town is within walking distance - we did it and I'm 60.

author: W5145NIjulied
title: Bargain price for Lake George - Excellent Service
text: If you're looking for a clean place to lay your head at night after a full day of Lake George or Adirondack activities, then you can't beat the "bang for your buck" of the Studio Motel. First of all - It's a motel. You're paying for a motel. It is not going to be the Crowne Plaza or the Marriott. So, when you come in expecting a motel, you will NOT be disappointed. The place is clean, well run, and located just about one mile from Lake George's main drag. We have stayed here four times, and will stay here again. The staff are excellent, the cleaning crew does an excellent job, and you get a few decent perks for a motel (fridge and pool). We always had excellent interactions with the staff with cheerful greetings and wishes for a good day. Be aware that this is NOT a winter hotel. We visited in mid-October and heater had to run overtime to keep our room warm with chill of the early fall nights. The restroom was pretty much always cool. If you're visiting in the fall and are on the cold natured side, you might want to bring an extra blanket for the bed. We would have been too chilly without ours. But, again, we knew what we were paying for. So, there was no complaint from us. For $64 per night, we consider this a find. We'll be back. It suits our needs as we go hiking in the Adirondack's daily and just need a place to sleep between adventures.

author: ekimpj08
title: Great Stay, great vacation!
text: We stayed at the studio motel in late august 2016, for a short family get away. I booked 4 rooms personally with an additional room booked separately. I want to start by saying that everyone that works there are so nice and are willing to help you. I had my in laws with us and needed a disabled access room which was no problem. We also had to have oxygen delivered for a member of our group, which again no problem at all. They stored it there before we arrived and after we left awaiting pick up. This hotel is within walking distance (5-10 minute walk) from million dollar beach and the village of Lake George.The hotel was clean and modern but we stayed in the rooms over looking the pool, which i believe is newer than other parts. The rooms were clean and in good repair and cleaned daily. The beds were two full size in the room with a small kitchenette with sofa and table. I will say that the beds were not the most comfortable but were OK. The only problem we really had was keep the covers on the bed while sleeping, they kept sliding off all night. Sheets and covers had no weight to them. The pool and grounds were very clean and well maintained, which from talking to the owners they took pride in that. Great stay, great vacation... Value for your money... We will be back to stay again...

author: ffhal58
title: Quick get away
text: From the outside this place looks promising. It has a pool and the grounds are kept up nicely. But looks are deceiving. We were put in a cottage in the back of the property down a hill behind other taller buildings. Paint was peeling off the cottage. Lighting outside was very dim in parking area. Inside, the bed was horrible. I could of slept on crates and it would of felt better. It was 2 nights of back pain. It had i ceiling light and no lamp in the corner where there was 2 chairs and a table. The bathroom was way to small you could hit your head on the door frame while on the toilet. When you stepped out of the shower you hit the toilet. It was like a closet not a bathroom. It had a flat screen tv and a small fridge with an in wall air unit. I don't think I'd ever go here again.

author: DZsmom
title: A little better than average but i can't give it very good
text: Just stayed at the Studio Motel for a few days with my older grandchildren. Check in was quick and pleasant. If you are looking for clean, decent rooms at a moderate price, this is a nice place. The room was large and had a back door to a shared balcony. The pool was clean and nice and the pool area had plenty of places to sit and be comfortable. Overall, a nice place but with a few caveats. We had a first floor room and it was very noisy from the guests above. They had children who ran and jumped a lot and the noise was disturbing. If I stayed there again, it definitely would not be in a first floor room. I thought the pool was supposed to be heated but I found it to be cooler than if heated. The room had queen beds but mattresses were noisy and only moderate quality. The bottom sheets did not fit the bed properly and came off the corners several times. Smoking is allowed on the decks but the smell does travel and drove me back inside. Be sure to bring pool/beach towels. There were three of us in the room and we got three towels. I picked this hotel rather quickly based on the reviews and the prices. However, with all of the hotels in Lake George, I might do a little more research the next time.

author: SarahS1972
title: Love this little, out of the way motel
text: I booked Studio Motel based on the decent reviews on Trip Advisor and because the price was reasonable for Lake George on an August weekend. I didn't have much expectations especially since the place I stayed last year was a little too rustic for my tastes. I was pleasantly surprised. We had room #1 which was perfect for us. I believe this is their "Disabled" persons room, which we are not, yet it still worked out just right for us. The room contains one double or queen sized bed. I think they said it was a double but it slept like a queen. It also has a sofa, TV, bureau, low table and two chairs, a small refrigerator, and a microwave. Outside the room is a long railing along the walkway which was great for us. We're SCUBA divers and this was a perfect place to hang some our wet stuff. The room is around the side of the building by the housekeeping facilities so not many people go there. Some quirks: - Only one side of the bed has a night table and lamp. - Because the front door is right next to the dryer vents, lint from the dryer comes into the room. - The shower doesn't have a shower stool or seat of any kind so if someone has problems standing, this room isn't really adequate. - Also regarding a disabled person, the toilet is at the normal height -- nor raised. All that said, I would stay here again.

author: RoadRabbitTC
title: Comfortable Stay! Great Low Price
text: I cannot come up with one negative to this place, other than no jacuzzi in room. Room is clean, bedding is clean and not stained like many other low cost motels. Free Wifi and plenty of parking. Stayed here for one night during Six Flags Great Escape opening weekend and needed a comfortable low priced place to sleep. Check in was quick and efficient. Room I had came with two beds, a couch, fridge, microwave, and table. Bathroom and linen was clean. Shower temp and pressure is fine. A/C worked great, kept room cool. Friends had a room for same price with fridge, microwave, stove, kitchen sink. We all loved this place. Tucked in alongside RT 9L on a main road but off the main strip into Lake George. 6 Flags is about 5 miles right down rt 9 and the action of Lake George is the other way down RT 9. A ton of restaurants, stores, outlet stores, etc in the Lake George area. The lake is a great visit as well, beautiful scenery. Definitely will stay here again when in the area

author: WCLamb
title: A first time guest -- it won't be my last stay.
text: Stayed at the Studio Motel for Americade this year after finding it at the end of last year's Americade. It was exactly what I was looking for, and a much closer commute to the village than either Saratoga Springs (1/2 hour away) or Queensbury. The Studio met all my needs and exceeded my expectations. Preferring a motel where my cycle can be parked right outside my door for easy loading in the morning and unloading after a day's ride, there seems to be fewer and fewer motels available in that configuration. Most are modelling after the center-hall hotels where one must lug their bags to a inside room, and a smoker must walk 1/4 mile to get outside and have a cigarette with the morning's coffee, whereas the Studio Motel has direct access to the outdoors from all rooms, and a covered seating area for relaxing -- rain or shine. The owner is a fine gentleman and is looking forward to our return next year. I'll be happy - happy - happy to accommodate his wishes when he accommodates mine. I've already requested the same room... my son will probably come with his wife next year and we'll book TWO adjacent rooms. We spent a good bit of time poolside on Saturday... a first for me during Americade week... but it was a great way to wind down after a busy, busy week. Everything wanted or needed was there! I can't believe I didn't find this place years ago (I've been coming to A'cade since 1999) and think it's because the current guests keep it a secret. I can understand why! It's a treasure!

author: 52cindya
title: Disappointed
text: Ok so we stayed here 3 years ago & loved it. So we decided to go back this year August 2013 which we told the owner we stayed there before & we received a little discount. (which was very kind of him) He is a very nice person. We stayed in the back in the effiecencies to save money on meals, plus we dont mind cooking. We checked the room before we paid seemed fine. No bedbugs, shower curtain was moldy (which we asked for a new one & received) . (I had brought our own cleaning supplies since we had the effiecency -thank godness. Bathroom smelled like urine & bathtub was filthy(i really didnt notice when we checked the shower curtain) Took me an hour to clean bathroom, kitchen area, inside of refrigerator.Needless to say after i cleaned it was better (bathroom still smelled like urine though) but the point is I shouldn't of have to. I was so disappointed. What I noticed is that the boy who cleaned our room only took the garbage out & made the beds & put in toilet paper & vacum. He never once never cleaned the inside of the toilet because there was a stain in it from day 1 & we stayed there for 5 night. (this was my test to see if he did clean it) Things that I love about this hotel is having the room in the back facing the woods & play area close for our little one. Private as well in the back, its quiet & everyone there is super nice. We loved the pool & went in it everyday - super clean. The grounds of the hotel are beautiful well maintained & super clean. Love the fact its off of the main Rt9 & in the mountain area & still only 2 minutes from everything. My boyfriend says he wants to stay here again next year & that its okay we have to clean it first. He likes the Studio Motel (which i do too, but needs to get better quality help to make sure rooms are squeeky clean) I told him I think this would be the last time I stay here. Oh also beds are very uncomfortable!

author: davews6
title: Great place, beds in old building not good
text: Been to Lake George probably 40 times over the years. Decided to stay here based on reviews from others. The location is fabulous. The pool is extremely clean with salt water filtraiton, very nice and warm. At check in we were given room in old building (closest to road) as we reserved room with 2 double beds to accomodate our little one. Don't really like to have to pay entire amount in advance but ok... The room itsself was very clean, stand up shower only which is not the preference for the missus but ok. Bathroom very small. Refrig. was a nice touch so we could buy food to keep some vacation costs down. The grounds were emaculate with a play area. Housekeeping did a good job on the 1 day we allowed the room to be cleaned. There are 2 buildings near the rear of the property that seem to be much newer. We did notice that those 2 buildings are essentially 3 stories with the lowest level underground with only rear facing rooms. The beds in the old building were very uncomfortable and slightly canted toward head being lower, and the pillows were about as thick as three paper towels. Don't misunderstand, for the price we would definitely stay there again, and plan to, but would get a room in one of the newer buildings and would request a forward (pool) facing room.

author: GaryD433
title: Best Place In Lake George
text: We have been coming to Lake George for Americade for the last 10 years. After staying at a few other places in the area we found this gem in the woods. The owners have been most accomodating to us, offering as much a room for free just to stay around are friends for the last night of our stay, when we were booked in at another motel. The rooms are very spacious, and clean. If something is needed to be attended to, they will FIX it . The motel is located just out of all the noise, and close enough to all the amenities for the event of Americade. The grounds are immaculate, with the pool available, and the newly paved parking lot with enough spaces for everyone. As we come for a motorcyle event, at times some tools are needed to add a few new items to our bikes. They offer up tools, also as the bikes get dirty, he provides an area to clean them. We have met alot of people and became friends at this motel, and most of them have been coming back year after year with no complaints. The rooms all have chairs and tables to relax out front of your room. This is definitley the best place in Lake George We will definitely be speed dialing this motel for our next stay. As another review said, the worst thing about this place, is these reviews will keep this place full, that we might not get a room when we need it. Thanks to the owners Naeem and Tania for another great stay. Gary D

author: LisaP98
title: Tucked away just far enough from the busy village of Lake George, we loved it!
text: I loved the location in more ways than one! Felt like a local and still minutes from the action. The owner couldn't have been kinder or more accomodating. We stayed in the older section of the motel, by choice. A little dated with knotty pine walls and an old fashioned bathroom, so if it's modern decor and a cookie cutter room you are looking for, you won't find it here in any of these older rooms. There are newly renovated rooms which look more like small apts from the outside if that is more to your liking. Personally, I liked the old nostaglic feel to our room just fine. My daughter had one room with a dble bed and I had the other, each had a TV. The bathroom was in the middle but could be reached two ways. The tub was short but the water pressure was excellent and the shower head was a perfect height. I couldn't find an outlet in the BR though, so had to use the hairdryer in the room itself, near the mirror. Be sure to bring a hairdryer with you too, as they do not provide you with one. There was a small frig in bedroom number 2 and AC|HEAT access as well. Serta products to sleep on and everything was clean. The price was right and I was very happy with everything! I will definately come back here!

author: gouldme
title: Terrible, not worth a penny
text: Do not recommend this place. I made reservations to stay here 7 months ago. When i showed up they had no record of my reservation, luckily I kept the e-mail. I booked directly through the motel's website but supposedly the "company" went out of business. Needless to say, the price that I reserved the room for $58/night was irrelevant and if I wanted to stay I would have to pay the current rate of $120. This hotel is not worth that price, not even if it was within walking distance from the ocean would it be worth that price. They should have validated the price I paid considering I had proof. We had a king size bed with 3 square pillows. The hallways carpets were filthy. And the two nights we stayed there, we were awoken to people talking and shouting. One night some radnom dude started banging on people's doors. There were no card-access entries, no security. People were able to come and go at all times. When we went for breakfast the little area was dirty as if the Tazmanian Devil blew through. There was no bread left to toast. There were no cups for coffee. And this was an hour before breakfast was stopped. And this isn't a safe area. I was there for a race and according to some cops we spoke with, we should have never left anything in the rooms when we weren't there or in the car overnight.

author: rachelles434
title: Worth it?
text: We found this hotel with booking.com and were excited for a much needed beach get away. We arrived to check in to our pre-paid stay of 4 nights and the girl at the desk was unprofessional right away. She just kept shaking her head and saying how Expedia makes them overbook. They didn't have our room. No acknowledgment of how devastating that must be to feel like you are going to have to try to sleep in your car with 4 small children in an unfamiliar place.
