Meanwhile my 1 year old cries with daddy in the car and 3 other tired little girls. Tyler, the other employee was the absolute rudest front desk employee I have ever experienced. He was rude and lacked compassion. He told us flippantly that we could find a room elsewhere. We spent half an hour scouring the internet and calling hotel after hotel that was full. They offered 1 bed for the 6 of us as the best they could do. I asked if they were going to compensate us for not getting what we needed the 1st night, compensate us for the people that would be attempting to sleep on the floor. He became angry and told me I should just cancel my stay. I did and we found a kind front desk agent at Comfort Suites with one last room and the 2 beds we needed. I worked for Marriott for a few years and my husband worked in hotel management with Marriott and Hilton and this place needs employees who care about people. I would like to think management wouldn't like their employees to act in such a disrespectful, cold manner. THE worst customer care experience I have ever had. Worth it to pay a little more for a decent human interaction and a guaranteed bed ANYWHERE ELSE.

author: palomad964
title: Lots of bumps in the road
text: First when I arrived many people had complaints about their room and another couple was complaining about being overcharged. It gave me a bad feeling. We checked in and I left the deposit in CASH so I would get it back the next day. When we got in the room automatically there was an overwhelming wet smell coming from the bathroom but it smelled the whole room. We tried to ignore it but it worried us because it seemed like a mold smell. The staff was very nice about our request to switch rooms. So we did. The next morning, I went to check out and there were 3 other parties waiting that looked upset. I checked out and asked for my deposit. The woman said they were " low on money and have to wait for the manager to come " she gave me no time frame for when that would be happening. Now I understood why everyone was waiting angrily. I explained that this was cutting into my vacation time before I have to catch a train. Someone also came and they had to leave without their deposit because they we're catching a flight ! After 30 min of waiting with no answers. She told me that the owners were going to come in with money in 30 min. They came 30 min later and no one apologized . Not even the owner. They just stared at me as the girl at the desk was giving me the money . It was so uncomfortable as well as annoying. It cut into my personal time and I was already checked out, I couldn't even relax in the room since I had to wait an hour.

author: /undefined
title: Nice people, terrible property
text: Our check in was easy and the clerk was very nice and helpful the room was another story. We checked in at 10pm and went straight to our room. It was hot and stuffy so we decided to turn on the a/c. The frame around the unit was broken and barely hanging on and it sounded like a leaf blower. Since the a/c was so loud, we thought opening the window would be a better idea. No screen so back to the a/c. After we were able to get the lights lit, we noticed the peeling paint and graffiti. (Some of it obscene) We turned on the TV but were unable to control the volume using the remote because it was broken. The people next door, 4 young men, talked all night long. They were still partying and laughing when we left at 6am. The bathroom sink clogged and we ended up using the tub to brush our teeth. Thank goodness the toilet worked! The complementary breakfast was about what you would expect. Watery coffee and stale breads. I didn't feel safe staying here. If I have to visit Oceanside again, I will spend the extra $20 or $30 to stay up the street.

author: /undefined
title: If I could give this less than 1 I would
text: There were so many problems. First, incompetency with the staff. We were assigned our room, got there, and other people were in it. Turned out they had been moved from another room and no one marked it in the system. Then we get a new room and the TV doesn't work at all. Next morning, we head to breakfast which ends at 9:30, it is 8:45 and everything is gone and no one cares at all to refill anything. There's cereal but no milk. There was only enough waffle mix for one waffle but no butter. Syrup was pretty much out too. Luckily we got the last 3 cinnamon rolls. The OJ was brownish colored. There was no hot water available but there was tea and hot cocoa (had there been hot water I'm sure those would've been out too). I shouldn't have to get up at 6:30am, so I can be guaranteed one of the amenities that drew me to this hotel. The daytime desk staff was there yapping about something but no one cared about lack of breakfast choices or even that the trash cans were overflowing. Then when I checked out, I told the daytime desk guy that the cable was out in my room and he was like "oh ok". Not "I'm sorry" which would have been nice at least. I do want to say the towels were nice and fluffy, and the night guy, Tyler, was very apologetic about the room mishap. The Internet worked so that was at least a positive.

author: 1baggo
title: Perfect for what we wanted
text: They have three buildings. 1 is for pets and smokers. 2 and 3 are where we stayed. they are a lot newer. For the price you can not beat it. The workers were all really nice and full of information. lots of parking even for a trailer or motor home. The place was clean and well kept except for the pool area. The pool itself was clean but the area around was not. The room was clean. It had a frig and microwave. AND A VERY COMFORTABLE BED! The breakfast was ok. Nothing special. Next to everything. About 5 minutes to ocean. It was a nice get away for my wife and I.

author: Travel1111111
title: RUN AWAY FROM THIS PLACE
text: Booked this Labor Day weekend stay through Hotwire. Paid additional $15 per night pet fee totalling an additional $60, no problem. We walk up that dirty, crooked stairs to the second floor ( why is the pet room on the second floor???) making our way through cigarette butts and a junkie on a bike, asking for cash. The room stunk so bad I wanted to gag & was sooooo hot! We tuned on the A/C & brought our things in and sat down and looked around. Phone unplugged on the floor, TV didn't turn on, fridge on the dirty carpet and completely rusted at the base. The bathroom had a burned toilet seat and hair on the "clean towels". The room stayed hot and we sat and looked at each other. I went down to the desk to see if there was a non smoking room as my daughter has asthma and I got an instant headache from the stink. The girl at the desk said I booked through Hotwire and so I should call them if I had an issue. I asked if a non smoking room was available and she said for $50 more per night I could get a queen room with 1 bed....2 adults, 2 dogs and 1 child......This hotel is not worth $50 per week! I called Hotwire who called the hotel directly and didn't get any further than I got. Horrible customer service! RUN, Don't walk!!!!!! I have washed our clothes and duffle bags twice since returning home and they still smell like we've been on a Vegas bender for the last month. I'll spare you the boring details of the constant smell of people smoking pot and the high number of people riding their bikes near our cars asking for money..... At least the owner got a safe parking space in the front of the hotel, under the lights, so his Lexus would be safe........

author: /undefined
title: It's not how it used to be. ..
text: So dissapointed, I guess there's new management? Horrible. I used to stay here all the time when my husband was stationed at Camp Pendleton the management was amazing and nice. I used to check in and they already new.I needed extra pillows and towels this time they wouldn't give me extra pillows and when I went up to my room there was nothing but hand towels no shower towels. They only.remodeled like half of the hotel I believe because last time I stayed the room was nice and clean. The one I got this time was dirty. Spider webs... horrible. I've known this place for about 6years and this the worse management they've had. Rude ladies at he front desk also. Talking bad out other people staying there while I'm trying to check in. Definitely will not be staying there anymore. breakfast: breakfast used to be much better... all they had was waffles, cereal, milk coffee, some honey buns. They used to do eggs bacon, sausage. This place has gone down hill.

author: K4494NObarbarab
title: "Room 103"
text: When reading other reviews remember this, its a "Budget Motel". With that being said, I was completely satisfied and got what I expected. The Staff evening and day were wonderful. The woman showed me 3 rooms to allow me to decide! Who does that now a days? Room was clean, all bathroom fixtures in working order. The tub is slippery, I just put a hand towel down so my grandkids wouldn't slip. No biggie people.Little musty in the bathroom, and one desk lamp light bulb out. Bed was comfortable. Pool area is fantastic! Had a fridge and microwave and coffee maker which I did not expect. Sufficient breakfast, but there was only fruit one day (of 3). Cant blame them though, people just steal that kind of thing. Get your waffle early! When they are gone they are gone I think. Orange juice is great! I think the rooms are mostly nonsmoking, therefore there are a lot of cig butts on the grounds, maybe a couple ashtrays would be nice. That's probably my biggest complaint.

author: helenbC2683PG
title: Unsatisfactory
text: This location was not the best of places I have stayed. As a matter of fact it was the worst experience I have ever had. The desk services was okay, but the room was not so good. At registration I was not asked if I was a Wyndham Rewards Member, I had my number ready. When I walked in the room, it was freezing. I tried to get the heater going so when time for bed I would be comfortable. The room never warmed up. I mentioned it to someone, but I wanted to allow time to pass for the room to warm up and it never did. Secondly, the building my room was in, it was under construction. Men were working on the problem and was an inconvenience. They were working in the same area of the stairway I would need to use to access the floor to me room. There were people a couple of doors down from me, that looks shady, were loud most of the night. I was afraid for my safety, and was uneasy all night long. I ended up checking out because I was not happy now did I enjoy the time there. I just wanted to leave. It definitely was not worth the cost of the room, even if it was less expensive, I should have been reimbursed. Not my best experiences.

author: 667MichaelF
title: worst wyndham motel i have ever stayed at .
text: reserved a room for two days and had to check out a day early . the motel charged me extra money for checking out at 12.00 noon instead of 11.00 am. dissapointed with that because the office was packed at 11.00 am anyway . the room itself was pretty dirty, bedding not the best, furniture literally falling apart. the bathroom was the worst however,the tub was about to cave in on me and had very little water pressure. the room i had did have cockroaches and fleas probably from the pets allowed policy. i checked in around 3 pm on sat afternoon and noise did not quit until around 3.00 am! i got no sleep at all! it gets worse , i was the victim of a crime, grand theft at about 3.30 am and caught the culprits! the motel did nothing! neither did the oceanside police dept. i did recover some of my property but had to take matters into my own hands to do so . it was my next door neighbors that did the deed . smoking meth outside and openly dealing drugs! i wont be staying here again. bad trip!

author: kimmers70
title: Seedy- not for a single gal-
text: Although clean and quiet, this hotel has "extended stay" guests. Lots of questionable activity, especially after dark. Unit 327- the door would open only after 3-4 times of trying. The door has settled and the holes do not match up. The dead bolt would not work. Could not plug the bathtub- had to borrow a screwdriver to take apart the drain cover and shoved a wash cloth in the hole to plug. Internet router had to be reset 4 times in order for the building to receive wifi. Staff- POOR GALS! Only one person staffed at the desk. Could not get anyone to answer the phone at the desk (if they are busy, they WON'T answer). God forbid someone were to have an emergency! If I needed something, I would have to walk down to the office. One time the phone was ringing off the hook and the gal ignored it. A bit scary to have to do that after dark. No maintenance after 4pm. What's that about? Breakfast? What a disaster! Small area and appeared people were just walking in off the street and helping themselves.

author: /undefined
title: Several concerns
text: Room assigned was unclean. Towel on floor in bathroom, dirty garbage and sink. I was assigned another room. Went to front desk next day to have my stay extended a week. This time, I used my corporate credit card. The woman made an error and charged me for the two nights I paid already on my personal card and the extra nights. I tried to get this corrected, however, even though she and the manager stated it was corrected, by bank statement shows that it is still on hold. I had to call them, and then my bank. I am waiting for the charges to be removed. Please contact them to insure it has been done. The woman there (Diamond), stated we might need a three way conference call, but my bank stated they needed a letter faxed with the letter head. This is very concerning. I would like this corrected asap, as it is taking up my time. You also have a problem with the pipes and hot water in the room I was in. The faucet would not go off and the water is scalding! Unfortunately, I did like this place and the conference area, but I find it needs updating and better computer knowledge or training to staff.

author: sonias836
title: Luckily the staff is nice
text: Luckily, the staff is nice or this hotel would have received 1 star. Check in was easy. The room had a musty smell, but it wasn't horrible. After 20 minutes, I would get used to it. The bed...wow...it was like sleeping on plywood! I stayed for two nights (only because it was already paid for.) I seriously considered eating the cost of it and going elsewhere. But I stayed. The hotel is rundown. The carpets are loose and pulling up in some places; old, stained sinks and yellow tinted toilets and tubs. Walls are paper thin...you could hear the neighbors conversations. There is ample parking but it must have been a packed weekend because it was a full house. The parking was filled with people who looked like bums, but probably weren't. You had to drive through the ghetto to get to Starbucks. The beach is about 7 minutes away. Not bad, I guess. For the price, considering I spent $250 and didn't get an ounce of sleep because it felt like I was sleeping on the floor, was not worth it. The breakfast was waffles, two choices of cereal, or 1 choice of pastry. Really disappointed. The reviews seemed better than all this. This really should be a 1 star Hotel.

author: 793mariamc
title: Lots of Bed bugs in the room!
text: Lots of bed bugs in the room. We woke up around 1 am to find our bodies swollen and covered with bites. My husband caught two in a paper cup and brought it to the front desk, and got the response "well, what do you want me to do about it?". We asked to get moved to another room in a different building. When we asked for any medicine for the swelling from the bites, we were told to drive 5 min down the road to Walgreens to get anti-histamine. Upon returning to the room, we turned over pillows to find and catch 7 more in total on both beds, with fresh blood stains from their feeding on us. After googling, we found out we had to wash all our clothes in high heat. So we basically spent the night in the laundry room washing and bagging up our clothes so as to not bring them with us anywhere. Super 8 wouldn't even offer to pay for the laundry (let alone the dry cleaning that a number of clothes would require). We didn't get to sleep till 5:30 am, and when we asked about extending our stay so we could get some sleep in the new room, the night staff told us to talk to the manager, Sam Patel, in the morning. To our surprise, he decided to not show up and told the front desk staff to tell us that (a) they wouldn't charge us for the room and (b) we would have to check out by 12 pm or pay $10 per hour extra if we were there any longer. The response we kept getting was "well, we're not charging you for the room". I wouldn't expect to pay for the room, since (a) we barely used the room as we spent most of the night in the laundry room (b) didn't get much sleep which ruined the next day (c) had to wash brand new clothes that were gifts that we can't give anymore (d) had to get several articles dry cleaned. The cost of the room doesn't make up for all of the above. We had only stayed there for the night on our way to LA, and by the time we checked out at 12 pm, they still hadn't called the exterminator. The attitude of the acting manager and manager was of complete indifference.

author: Cathi65Mesa_AZ
title: Worst Stay I have EVER Had anywhere
text: Upon arrival, I was told that my request for two beds had not been met nor would be accomodated. It was prepaid, so I had no choice but to take the room. There was no sympathy whatsoever that this affected my plans(Ino longer had enough beds for my grandkids who were counting on a sleepover with Grandma). She just plain didnt care. The parking lot had several balconies of people that I would call shady just staring at my car and the grounds were just plain old and dirty. I have never made such a comment, by the way, but there just isn't any other way to say it. I felt scared and felt the need to double check the locks on my car. My husband will tell you I normally forget to lock everything but the stares from the guests from the balcony made me fear for my belongings in my car. The room itself was reasonable and seemed clean enough. That is the nicest thing I can say. The next day, I was leaving in a hurry with my grandson, and left my best pair of jeans and Tee shirt behind. I called the same day. Do I need to event tell you???? Of course the maid took them. 150 bucks worth of clothing. If you can't trust the help, than you can't afford to stay here. Period. I have a long history of reviews on this site and NEVER have I given a poor one. If I could give minus five stars I would.

author: Yu-JinC
title: Cheap, and you get what you pay for
text: This was the cheapest hotel anywhere in the region, so we went for it- staying for 6 nights. I'm not a picky guy and I've stayed in a lot of motels, so I know what to expect from one of these places. This Super 8 has decent service and is relatively convenient as far as location goes (though it's not in walking distance of anything) and has a pool and free breakfast. The breakfast is pretty lackluster- we only bothered once, then opted for fast food instead (yeah... that was an upgrade). Service is decent, nothing special though which is to be expected. The biggest gripes I had with the hotel are its design and layout. It's got really thin walls which is kind of typical of a motel, but what is not typical is the interior corridor design. Each building is a double story with doors on the INSIDE, on a corridor- kind of like a real hotel. At first I thought it was kind of nice, but that was until I realized how that corridor amplified sound and carried it. If someone closes a door on the far end of the building, you can HEAR it through the walls all the way down. If someone yells in the hallway, it sounds like they're talking in your room even if you're on the far end! Additionally, it's pretty clear the place is old- including everything in it. The carpet was in bad shape, pillows were small and almost all the towels had stains. The faucet wouldn't stay on- kept dropping closed. To put it simply, this place is in need of a refresh.

author: RobbnMandaM
title: Noisy Hotel
text: Front desk is very friendly. Neighborhood is not the best. Rooms were clean. Light in bathroom worked for about 5 min. Flickered on and off for the rest of the stay which means it's not a bulb it is a wiring issue. Even with a small bathroom window it's hard taking showers in the dark. Or just uncomfortable leaving the bathroom door open to get light from the vanity area. The pool was nice, but the rules weren't enforced in the slightest. The hot tub was tiny and impossible to get into when there are kids constantly jumping in and out. It was supposed to close at 9 but guests remained in it long after. We had a room at the end of the hall by the door and heard a constant slamming sound that kept waking us up. We thought it was the hall door slamming so the second night we made sure it was open. We then realized it wasn't the hall door but the doors to the rooms slam so loudly that the walls shake. impossible to sleep past 6am. They advertise a hot breakfast which means they have 1 waffle iron and a typical continental breakfast. The first morning we spent 20 minutes waiting for the waffle iron and our family had to eat in shifts becuase the sitting area can only accomdate around 10 people. We didn't eat there the rest of our trip. Overall it is an inexpensive hotel, but very noisy. probably would not stay here again.

author: us7879
title: Would be back!!!
text: Well after a long day at Legoland, We wanted to stay at a hotel close to Oceanside beach at Rubys restaurant on the pier which was this one.... Overall, we enjoyed our stay & had no problems at this hotel, but a few slight inconvenience occurs... Employees - Very nice, friendly... GREAT Customer Service skills Con. Breakfast - Was not available due to state license not issued to them or something, But they more then made up with it by certificates to the donut shop next door to the hotel, who had wonderful fresh bagels, donuts & include juice, milk coffee etc. Rooms - Thank goodness we got to stay in the closed area aka "Conference building" as the other part of the hotel area on the other side was not enclosed & looked trashy... But the "conference building" was great like your at another hotel avoiding the outside ;) Hotel property it self - There's 3 areas basically where rooms are at the hotel 1. The Conference building area 2. an area where your hotel door is outside for anyone to be able to come to on the streets or where ever & 3. an simi closed area... That said the 2 & 3 area looks trashy the 1 area conference was nice & clean but very small room... Beds were comfy but small also (they were double size beds, but to me thats small considering our home bed is a Ca. King... I was hoping for atleast a queen)... The hotel property was quiet throughout the night till about 7am in the morning a car alarm was going off for almost 2 hours & the staff did nothing of the disturbance (although the lady was out there with her car)... That said - Although the rooms are small, the 7am disturbance & only 1 nice area at the hotel property to stay which is the "Conference building" Due to the great friendly customer service we received we will be back!!!

author: Katleary
title: Box spring mattress-Woke up with a sore back!
text: My associate and I spent one night at this hotel, having business with a client in the area. The hotel has a conference center on the premises, but when we asked for a wine opener (you’d think that a hotel with a conference center would have a wine opener), I was told that the only one they had was broken and it was never replaced. Ok...so we had to get creative to open our bottle of wine. We had to call the front desk after dinner, as we hadn't noticed when we checked in, there wasn't an extra roll of toilet paper left in the bathroom and we had less than a sixteenth of a roll available to us upon check-in (not enough to go around for 2 people). The remodeled bathroom was nice though and the showerhead and water pressure good. No amenities to speak of other than a bar of soap a small shampoo. There was an in room coffee maker, but no coffee. The TV was old and had limited channels and needed the wiring checked to correct the static and lack of focus. The beds were a different story all together!! Both beds felt like box springs with no mattress! Both of us woke up the next morning, having tossed and turned all night due to the uncomfortable “box spring only beds” with upper & lower back pain which lasted all day!!! It was a terrible nights rest for both of us. This hotel really needs to invest in new beds and TV’s. I’m a Best Western Rewards member and have stayed in many BW Hotels around the country for years. I was very disappointed in this hotel meeting what I consider to be minimum BW requirement standards.

author: Fremont_Dude
title: A very motel like Best Western
text: We chose this hotel because it was a best western that was close to Escondidi Wild Animal Park and the photo on the internet looked good. But upon arrival the hotel looked any thing but like the photo on internet. It had more of motel feel to it. the check in took longer as there was only one person taking care of front desk. The room up on stepping in was hot and it took quite a bit of time for AC to kick in. The room carpet has some stains and over all the room looked like it needed some serious upgrade. Breakfast had cornflaked with 2% milk,some packaged danish, granola bars, apples and Oranges ( one of the already rotten ). The fruits need less to say were not appealing at all. Coffee was pretty bad like a coffee at a car dealer. But i was thankful for the cereal at least it saved some time for us. The comforters in the room looked pretty old too. Barth room was clean, but again pretty old. The Hotel advertised free WIFI, but it was not working for us. I got a feeling that this was probably some old Motel converted into Best Western. Overall it is not up to other best westerns we stayed.

author: Tank002
title: Great hotel, good price.
text: I read all the negative reviews and doubted about staying here. But I was wrong. This is a great hotel. My wife has MS and I requested a ground floor handicap accessible room and was given room 114 right off the lobby. Loved it. The room was fresh, clean and looked as if it had been recently remodeled. The bed was good, and the room and bathroom was clean. No problems whatsoever. The only thing I wondered about was if it is handicap accessible, why did it have a tub instead of a walk-in shower? It didn't matter to us, but I wondered about if someone had a wheelchair. The lobby was always clean and you could smell the freshness when you walked in the front door. The breakfast was good. Eggs, sausage, and biscuits and gravy. Plus many other food items. The only thing I didn't like was the entrance to the hotel was potholed. But, it shared a drive with a strip mall, so there is a lot of traffic. Outback steakhouse is right beside it, and within walking distance are Steak-n-Shake, Fat Patties, and across the street - Cracker Barrel. Will definitely stay here again.

author: 918hattieb
title: My July 2017 visit.
text: We had stayed at this Motel before and therefore we knew about where we were. Greatly enjoyed being here again. Our room was great for us. HANDY-CAPABLE! Roll-in shower as I cannot get into a tub. What a blessing and so many people willing to help was incredible. The bed and bedding was clean and soft. Bathroom linens were too. The breakfast room was clean and the personnel here were very helpful too. They have a good variety of breakfast foods. Seven days I had nothing to do but enjoy being alive in Huntington, WVA. As we were leaving they gave us a "to-go-bag". Contained granola bars, Apples, Bananas, Oranges and Water. Sure came in handy at the Airport. Many thanks to all who made our stay in Huntington, WVA. memorable. Will try to stay here on our next trip to W.VA. . Thank you to all who made our stay here memorable.

author: WHISKEYTIM
title: WONDERFUL EXPERIENCE
text: My wife and I stopped here for one night on our way to KY. We are Diamond Members and used points. I had reached out before to request quieter room. Anna the GM responded personally. We arrived later. Check in was easy, efficient. Room was in pretty quiet wing (on edge by main highway but didn't really hear traffic). Plentiful parking etc. Room was clean, great AC, nice fridge/micro. LOVED the shower. Pretty good breakfast for quick hit before moving on. Good coffee. Everyone I encountered was helpful, pleasant etc. Overall would definitely recommend and no question stay here again!!! Thanks for a super night's sleep.

author: tah52
title: If you don't mind the sounds of a submarine, then go ahead and stay here.
text: We booked this hotel for 4 nights but only stayed 2. I was so angry because the walls in this place were paper thin. You could hear the people in the next room eating popcorn. It was ridiculous. Also, when they people in the next room turned on the water, it sounded as though we were about to experience what the people on board the Ark must have experienced. It was so loud I could hear it through my ear plugs. They also had a big group of kids and chaperones in for a sporting event. The chaperones should have been smacked because they were not supervising the kids. I called the front desk staff to complain and they apologized profusely. I felt satisfied for that night. But then it happened again the next night. I called the front desk staff and told them we were checking out because I had had enough of the noise. The staff apologized again and I told them it was not their fault. It was the fault of the owners and they were not to blame. They refunded 1 night and we went on our way. I will never stay at a Best Western again.

author: SINBADNOBLE
title: Good overnighter.
text: This hotel was clean. Bathroom clean . whole place looked a little worn. This place is just off I64 and in the heart of a large shopping and entertainment area. Had a room at the rear so no noise problem. Strange parking rules. You must park only in spaces that belone to the hotel. They are well marked. Signage is quite clear about this. Parking for nearby shops overlap in the lot. Good free breakfast. Lots of working men at breakfast. Looks like they may be weekly. Had to walk up stairs to 2nd. Floor. No sure but I don't think there was an elevator. If that makes a difference. Over all not that bad for an overnighter. Price under$ 100.00. Lotst of food nearby.

author: 821sallyc
title: Very nice room, not so great customer service
text: My husband and I were on a road trip and spent a night at this hotel. The room was very clean and quiet, perfect for sleeping peacefully. Bed was comfy. I really enjoyed our night here. The only downside was the check out process in the AM. This took a total of 45 minutes. Apparently there was a soccer tournament nearby, so they were overwhelmed at the desk with people checking in and out. The problem I had was the lack of organization. There was no order to the line at all. Everyone was scattered all around the desk, waiting to be seen by the single front desk lady, who kept hiding in the back room, despite the heavy crowd of people waiting. Now, call this idea crazy, but at the very least have a second person to take over the front desk rather than make us wait. To top it off, when the lady finally acknowledged us, she was rude. She didn't smile or say have a nice day, nothing. Just checked us out and didn't even say we were good to go, just moved on to the next person. I've worked in customer service myself. Even on my worst days I was still required to be polite. Anyway, despite this check out process I still give it 4 stars due to the nice, clean room it provided.

author: judyw969
title: Noise + Noise = Little sleep
text: We went to Huntington yesterday to attend the State Gymnastics Meet. When we decided to go, this was the only motel that still had rooms available since there was also a volleyball tournament there.. Pros: The room was large and clean. There was a good variety for the breakfast with several hot choices and different protein choices besides the usual waffles. It is very convenient to the Interstate and right across the parking lot from an Outback where we enjoyed dinner. Parking was easily available. Minor Annoyances: There was a popcorn machine in the lobby but there was never any popcorn available. Small soft pillows - we usually bring our own, but forgot. Major Annoyances: Our room was located just off the front lobby and was very noisy. We could hear the phone ringing all night long. There were loud conversations - one happened at 5:00 this morning to wake us up for the day. It is a pet friendly hotel and we had a dog in the room next to us. It barked on and off during the afternoon - we had arrived at 3:00 and wanted to relax before dinner. Got back from dinner at 8:30 and it was barking continuously until 9:45. It was barking at 7:00 this morning, while it was tied to the door of the Breakfast Room and you had to get by the barking dog to enter the room. Hope that no one was allergic or uncomfortable around dogs. After the tournament we had a 3 1/2 hour drive to get back home after spending the day enjoying the meet. It was difficult for both of us to stay awake after a night of little sleep. We probably would not try to stay here again or recommend it to anyone. If you have to stay here, do not get a room near the lobby and find out where any pets are staying and stay far away.

author: 997DanielB
title: AVERAGE AT BEST, POOR AT WORST
text: As for my stay, everything was fine. Great bed for sleeping. A/C worked well. No noise. Friendly staff. Close to mall. No complaints. As I read a book in the common area, I got to hear what others had to say. This gave me a very different feel. Several Strip Clubs nearby. TV remotes that did not function. Alarms in neighboring rooms that were blaring. A/C units that did not function properly. Side doors that did not work with the room keys. Small pool. Thus, I would not bring a family to this hotel, but if it is just adults (and you do not mind the atmosphere around the hotel) then it is an ok place to stay.

author: BBGRL
title: Nice stay
text: I enjoyed my stay here for the weekend. I stayed here for a week 7 years ago, and I would stay here again when I am in town. The staff were all friendly and helpful. The room was quite comfortable for 3 people. The bed was not as soft as some beds. The walls were a little thin, one night when I was trying to fall asleep I could hear the bed in the next room over squeaking, and children screaming and crying (come to find out the kids were 2 rooms away from us). I used the gym equipment around 11 at night I didn't want to stay too long because it was very noisy and next to a guest room. The breakfast was ok. The hard boiled eggs were freshly put out cold, there was plain (no flavor variety) instant oatmeal and the hot water was warm-ish, and of course the make your own waffle. The best food available was the popcorn in the lobby! Overall, I enjoyed my stay and would stay here again. Even though all the rooms around me were non smoking, the smell of cigarette smoke was very strong in the hallway, but thankfully not in the room! There is a bbq grill and pavilion in the parking lot. Across from the hotel in the same parking lot there is an outback steakhouse. The mall is really close, it is a great mall- if you like to shop, make sure to go to the Huntington mall!

author: Marinda08
title: Great Stay!! Would Stay Again!!
text: I stayed at this hotel on a Friday and Saturday night recently when I helped a relative move. Friday night was a bit noisy, as the hotel was sold out, due to several wrestling teams staying there for a championship tournament. One of the teams members donned their wrestling uniforms and found great pleasure in running up and down the hallways upstairs as well as downstairs, where I was. This wasn't the hotel's fault, and it did eventually stop. My room was perfect, in the perfect location for me, as I had my dog with me, and was on the ground floor, directly next to the outside door, in the rear of the hotel. If you are seeking quiet, request a room away from the outside doors, as the hotel does not have an elevator, and the doors stay very busy. My room was clean, and I had everything I needed, except for bar soap, which the housekeeping staff cheerfully gave me when I asked. The room had a fridge, and in room coffee pot, which I greatly appreciated, due to dietary needs and having to pack food. The breakfast in the morning was much appreciated as well. The shower was hot and great water pressure. My room faced the rear of the hotel, which backs up to I-64. This was not an issue for me, but may be for some. The heater in the room worked fantastic and was very quiet. Pets are welcome, which is also a great amenity. A special thank you to Deana, a staff member who was tending the breakfast area on Sunday morning. You were very cheerful and friendly!! There is an Outback Steakhouse in the shared parking lot, which is very convenient. I would definitely stay here again.

author: dshaver
title: Are the rest of these reviews real? Smoke-filled, loud hotel.
text: If this had been sold as 1* hotel at Motel 6 or Super 8 prices, I'd be happy. However, it is not rated nor priced like the quality it represents. Be vary careful -- the star ranking on this hotel is all over the map: 1* at Priceline, 2* at Kayak.com, 2.5* at Expedia.com, 2.5* at Hotels.com, and (shockingly) 3* at Hotwire. The condition of the hotel was "OK" but there was certainly lots of deferred maintenance -- lose handrails, carpet seams ripped open, windows that didn't close, stained ceilings, cigarette burns on the desk, sink, chair, etc. The Internet connection was free but uselessly slow; attempting to download a 10M document failed dozens of times and I gave up after an hour of effort at night and again the next morning. Warning: More than half this hotel is smoking. I was stuck in one of these nasty smoking rooms for the first night of my two night stay and it was ugly. The halls and rooms near the smoking rooms smell really bad -- like a bingo parlor on a Saturday night. I'm not a super sensitive person re: smoke; just shocked how everything was so smelly. Generally, this is a loud hotel as there are lots of late night and early morning hallway noise. During my stay, the hotel seemed to be about 50% construction crews that are coming and going at all hours. They park diesel trucks in the parking lot and start them up at 4am and then need to idle them for five minutes to warm them up. In short, thin walls, cruddy doors, and cheap windows lead to lots of noise everywhere. There is no quiet side of the building -- on the north is the Interstate and the south the highway and (much worse) double train track that has much overnight action. Breakfast was reasonable; waffle machine, a few cereal choices, hard boiled eggs, etc. Bright spots: Outback shares the parking lot and service there was great; a few good microbrews on tap. There is a Cracker Barrell walking distance across the road. Fat Patty's is just a bit further walk -- amazing hamburgers in this very local, four-location chain.

author: /undefined
title: Noise in bathroom
text: At 10 PM I heard a loud noise from our bathroom. It was coming from the drain in the bathtub. I heard it over the TV. I called the desk at about 11 PM and the desk person was nice and said that she could move us. Who wants to gather everything up and move at that hour. I said no and she said to close the bathroom door. That certainly didn't do any good. I woke my husband and he checked out the hallway and you could hear that noise out there. We decided to just go back to bed and he, of course, went back to sleep.He could sleep through the Atomic Bomb. I don't know how long it took but I finally did go to sleep. When I awoke in the morning the noise was gone. I listened when a neighbor used the shower. The noise was not the same. We have family in Hurricane and we have recently been using your motel. In the past we were using the Red Roof. Thank you for letting me vent. Joanne Rea P.S. The ladies in your morning buffet are very helpful and very nice.

author: maybjc
title: average
text: My family stayed here for one night. The check in was smooth. I believe the rooms could be updated. The shower curtain needed to be changed or atleast washed. The shower made a very loud noise. When I called the front desk, they offered to switch our room but said that some room's pipes are louder than others. There was a strange smell in the room as well. The WiFi was good. No mattress pads on the beds. It was very noisy. We could hear talking around us. Breakfast was ok. The lady tending to the breakfast did not seem happy to be there, more annoyed. She was not friendly to those eating. Usually the breakfast attendant is friendly and more interested in the guests. Ok for one night but would not choose for a longer stay. No elevator either.

author: Ridem1953
title: Never Again!
text: We stay 30+ nights per year in chain hotels,mostly Best Westerns, while traveling on business. The Barboursville property was full with work crews when we arrived with reservations. We were given no choice of rooms. The first room reeked of urine-we got the housekeeping supervisor to inspect the room,she agreed about the stench. Spraying with air-freshner couldn't cover it. One of the housekeepers seemed well aware of the problem,and said that some of the air conditioners dripped on the carpets,and turning on the heat released the smell of mold and fungus. (SO...obviously not a newly discovered problem,but certainly not corrected by maintanence or management either) The hapless individual "Rodney" working the desk had 5+ guests waiting for check in,seemed overwhelmed,and was having problems with his computers skillsHe was abrupt to the point of rudeness. We did finally get another room,a few doors from the front desk that smelled a bit better. However while the Lobby has 5-bar wifi reception, room 108,less than 30 feet from the front desk has 1 bar,making it impossible to connect to the hotel wifi. When this was brought to Rodney's attention,he shrugged and walked away,and said "I can't help you". Beds were good-,room was quiet except for the plumbin gnoise from adjacent rooms from other rooms is very audible. Breakfast is basic,a waffle iron and biscuits&gravy constituting the hot items. The blue- berry muffins are GREAT! But with employees like him,and poor service to boot for $80 USD..I'll be staying at the Holiday Inn Express next time I need to stop in Huntington/Barboursville WV. This,by far,was the worst experience we've had at a BW,over the course of several hundred stays over the past 5 years. Inspect a room prior to renting..and let's hope Rodney finds another job where he will be happy.

author: Evelynliu625
title: Clean room and good breakfast
text: We came here for the summer holiday with our 2 year old kid. We asked for a parking space (needs to call the hotel in advance) and a crib. 1. The location is 5 mins walking distance to the beach. But is a bit far from the center, it takes 20mins by walk to reach the center. 2. The room is clean and with enough space for three of us. 3. We have a balcony facing the river and seaside on our left, it becomes a little problem during the night when some hotels and restaurant hosting the concert celebrating the summer festival. 4. The bathroom is a bit old but clean with quite powerful hairdryer (very important for my long hair and kid that can never stay still for more than 5 mins). The shower room is big enough to keep an adult and a kid inside. (But the floor is very slippery so be careful when your kid is inside) 5. The breakfast is very good, bread, sweet pastry, salty choices (piadina, salami, prosciutto, eggs and sausage), fruits, yogurt and a bar providing fresh coffee. Only drawback is the ac. The wind goes directly toward the bed and was a bit noisy when it switch on and off to adjust the temperature by itself. In general we enjoyed the stay and would definitely think about it when we come back to Cattolica in the future.

author: SoCalOregonian
title: A VERY NICE STAY
text: We stayed at this property one night on 01/17. Upon arrival was warmly greeted by; I hope I get her name right, Lysheila. She was able to accommodate my requests of a top floor away from the elevator. We had reserved a Queen suite, which was furnished with 2 queen beds and a sleeper sofa. Also in the room were an easy chair, coffee table, reefer, microwave, kuerig machine, but no room safe. There are also air pots of coffee available 24 hours a day in the breakfast room. Our room faced the parking lot of the adjoining home improvement store and the main road. The room got a little noisy in the morning from the increase in traffic on the road. From the room we were able to see the rail yard, but heard no train horns through the night. Breakfast was the standard HIE fare. Total for one night in the queen suite was $145.54. All the staff I had contact with was very friendly and helpful. Located adjacent to the hotel is a Sizzlers steakhouse, also close by is a Bi-Mart store. When in K. Falls again, would stay at this property.

author: jeancE2088AX
title: Great stay
text: We booked a King suite. It had plenty of room and was very comfortable. The little kitchen area was more than adequate for us. It included a fridge, microwave, Keurig coffee maker and there were plastic (reusable) glasses and paper plates in the cabinet. Check in was easy and clerk was friendly. We got there before regular check in time and room of our reserved type happened to be available so she let us check in early. The bathroom was big enough for us both to get ready at the same time. The provided breakfast was fine. It has enough variety to please most people. It began at 6:30 am and we were there by 7. It wasn't crowded, but I can see how it might be if we had been there at 8:30 or 9. The breakfast prep lady kept everything well stocked & hot. The pool is indoors and is clean and a comfortable temp. Though it's pretty small. As we were exiting 2 small families (4 adults & 5 young kids) got in and pretty much filled the pool.

author: Guest0814
title: Paper-thin walls
text: Service is friendly. The room was clean. The bed was comfortable. Everything was operational including responsive Wi-Fi, and I thought the second sink outside the bathroom was a nice touch. The location's not bad; it's easy to get to and find, and Fred Meyer and other establishments are within short walking distance. Parking may be an issue; there's another hotel directly adjacent to this one which shares a parking lot. The lot also has a Sizzler. I got here around 6:30 PM, and open spaces were extremely limited. I got lucky and found a spot, but other drivers were wandering around in circles waiting for someone to leave. Noise could be better. I barely heard anything at all from outside the hotel. However, the interior walls are paper thin. I could hear people in neighboring rooms coughing, talking, etc. Around 8 AM the cleaning crew started coming around, and doors to the other rooms were opening and slamming shut so often that at first I thought some kids in a larger group of guests was playing hide and seek or something. Since the AC/heater unit doesn't have a fan-only setting, options to drown out the noise are limited at best. If you're hoping to sleep in you should consider staying elsewhere. The shower wall seems to have some water damage; this could become an issue later.

author: lie2me
title: Very nice
text: Asked for top floor room and got it. Rooms are not large but functional. Two queen beds which by far are the some of the most comfortable beds I've slept in. I travel a lot and I recall the beds at the Westin Hotel in Portland as being the best--these are comparable. Bathroom has tub shower combination and counter top is marble built into a free standing cabinet, which was very attractive. Closet a little awkward since it had one large mirrored door that swung open for access and tends to block access to the rest of the room. Desk and nice office type chair. There was also an occasional chair in corner with an ottoman. Unfortunately both were hard as a rock and essentially not usable. Flat screen tv with HD signal. This is newer property compared to the life of most hotels so things are in pretty good shape. The breakfast buffet was extremely well prepared and flavorful--better than any other properties where you go get your own food. The choices were extensive with offerings such as actual cheese omelettes, regular and turkey sausage, scrambled eggs, sausage gravy with many bread and muffin choices. They have a pancake 'machine', milk products, hot and cold cereals, juices, yogurts, fresh fruit and a vast array of other things to include their renowned cinnamon rolls. The only downside to all this is you eat off styrofoam plates, plastic knives and forks (ok in size though) and paper cups.

author: Nickels9895
title: Well Above Average Holiday Inn Express
text: Not your typical HEI, this location is above average. Either a newer facility, very well maintained or both. We were in the area to visit Crater Lake National Park which is about an hour away and this location was perfect. Nice lobby, breakfast area and rooms. Very clean room and bathroom, housekeeping did a good job. Ample outlets for charging electronics. Typical HEI breakfast with one exception and that exception wasn't the food but the employee working in this area,. This individual was absolutely outstanding. Due to a bus load of college athletes staying at the facility, which they kept segregated in the event they they were noisy which they were not, the breakfast area was crowded in the morning. She ran around herself making sure everything was fully stocked, fresh and clean. In addition, she visited each table providing a morning greeting, cleared and washed tables, and took out trash. There were times she actually appeared to be running. Kudos to her, she should be promoted to corporate trainer as many many other locations could benefit from the skills this lady possesses. I apologize I did not get her name to provide her with the recognition she deserves. Ample seating area for breakfast is available and they offered the conference room for breakfast due to the large crowd. Very well kept and maintained facility. Would absolutely recommend and return to this facility when in the area. Room cleanliness: excellent Bed: comfortable and not saggy Pillows: comfortable with a choice of firm or soft Bathroom cleanliness: excellent Towels: nice and soft WiFi: good Television: good selection Refrigerator: yes Microwave: yes Staff: friendly and helpful with outstanding breakfast serving individual

author: Illinois_John
title: Decent Hotel with Friendly Staff
text: My wife and I stayed here for two nights while visiting Crater Lake (about an hour's drive away). The hotel is located in an area with a Bi-Mart, a hardware store and a Sizzler Steak House next door. There are a number of other restaurants and stores within walking distance of the hotel. One night we chose to walk to Nibbley's Café, about a 1/2 mile walk. I recommend this restaurant for a good dinner. The check-in and checkout process went very smoothly. The breakfast is your standard HIE fare. The breakfast staff is very friendly and there is plenty of seating space. We appreciated that there was an ample supply of bananas each day. The room was clean and quiet. The blackout curtains worked very well. The bed was comfortable and we got a good night's sleep. The bathroom has a tub/shower with a grab bar to assist with getting in & out. In addition to the shower curtain, there is a triangular plastic piece on the wall and edge of the tub to keep the water off of the floor...an excellent idea. There is a powerful exhaust fan on a separate switch from the bathroom light. Unfortunately, the bathroom light is not very good for shaving. The towels are soft and absorbent. The shower spray was strong, but the shower head appeared to be clogged on one of the settings such that we had to use a narrower spray. I did have some issues with the Wi-Fi cutting in and out on both nights we were there.

author: anameineed
title: Seemed really understaffed
text: I'm afraid we had a negative experience from the moment we checked in. There was a long line at the front desk and only one person working. After waiting twenty minutes to check in, we couldn't believe when we got off the elevator and were looking directly at our room. I have written in my online preferences that we like to be as far away from the elevator as possible. I tried calling down to the desk three times and nobody answered. So I went back to the desk to ask in person why we were given this room. First he said "I thought it was far enough away". When I asked how the closest room to the elevator was "far enough away" he pulled up my account and then admitted that he hadn't actually seen my preferences. Then he went on to show me a stack of bookings and to tell me that he was just too busy that day to deal with personal preferences. So we ended up staying in the room where we got to listen to the elevator "dinging" with each guest who came and went. Next we tried to use the business center. Only one computer would turn on so we went out to the front desk to ask for assistance and were told, "Oh yes, it doesn't work, we really need to get that fixed." Um yes, that would be a good idea to fix something you know is broken. The pool and hot tub were the tiniest we've ever seen in a hotel. It was so crowded that there was no swimming possible, so we gave up on that idea. The air conditioning also did not work in our room, it cycled on and off continuously despite whatever we set the thermostat to. To add to the noise from the a/c, we could hear TV from neighbors and even their personal conversations were so clear that we felt like they were in our room...very uncomfortable situation. I would like to make one positive comment-- The next morning we had a good breakfast, and the woman who was working in the dining room was delightful. She was running around like crazy trying to keep everything refilled, and she still took time to greet everyone and ask if there was anything we needed. She was by far the best part of this otherwise disappointing hotel experience. Needless to say, this will not be the hotel we select on our next visit.

author: nowincolorado
title: One of my favorite hotels
text: This is a wonderful hotel! The staff were very helpful, friendly, and kind. The common areas and hallways were spotless clean. The room was immaculate. It came with a mid size frig, microwave and sink area outside the bathroom. We had two very comfortable beds. I got the best night sleep here – I slept 9 hours straight! The heating/AC kept the room the right temperature and was not too loud. We did not hear any noise from other rooms or outside. I could live here it was so nice! If you need anything at all, do not hesitate to ask the front desk staff – they are more than eager and willing to help with anything you need. This is an outstanding hotel! The breakfast was superb! The bacon was crisp, the omelets were hot with plenty of melted cheese and the made to order pancakes were filling - every thing was very good!! The breakfast hostess made sure everyone at every table was taken care of. She put people first in her job! The management and staff are top notch here! It would be a privilege to stay here again! Love, love, love this excellent hotel!

author: Allison_Hua
title: Visit the Redwoods
text: This hotel is attached to a very cute little casino that offers slot machines (no live card games or roulette, just slot machines). DO NOT eat at the casino restaurant or the gas station around the corner that sells fried chicken. Overpriced at best, food poisoning at worst. Our room was clean and quiet. The staff went out of their way to help my husband who is gluten intolerant have breakfast every morning. The best option for gluten free people there is yogurt with nuts and fresh fruit. You will have no cell service here, (at least not with AT&T) and the wifi they have available does not work well so this would not be a good place to get business done. Perfect for someone trying to minimize their screen time though like we were. Not every room has a bathtub, if that is important to you you must ask. The only tub available to us was in an accessible room with a low shower head. If you book in the late winter the rates are very cheap and you can have the parks and the hotel mostly to yourself which is a huge plus in my book. They say the pool is heated but it was much too cold for my husband and I to swim in comfortably when we visited in February. This hotel is perfectly situated to visit the redwoods right outside crescent city as well as the longer drive past Eureka to drive the Avenue of the Giants. We stayed for 4 nights and were able to see both parks comfortably. Definitely go to the Klamath River Overlook, the drive thru tree, and trees of mystery.

author: kathleens361
title: Worth staying here for the beds!
text: Stayed at the Holiday Inn Express in Klamath Falls a few years ago. It was a good stay then and it was this time too. We were on the 3rd floor (there are 4 floors) and staying two nights. The first night was Ok as far as noise, a real quiet Sunday night. Had a really good dinner meal at Sizzler Sunday night, which is in the same parking lot as the hotel. The beds were so comfy! Best beds on our trip so far, not hard as a rock but with some give and a pillow top. Nice breakfast setup. I had pancakes (machine made and a little tough), milk and either sausage (Monday) or bacon (Tuesday) along with a cinnamon roll and banana. The only complaint and improvement - too flimsy, cheap & small of knives, forks and spoons. I could hardly cut the pancake much less the sausage patty. They charged different rates for Sunday and Monday with Sunday being cheaper. Monday night at the hotel someone above us checked in about 8:00 pm and had a child that ran back and forth for over an hour. I called the front desk to ask if they had "quiet" hours, she said they did not. When I asked about the child above us, she didn't even know there was a child in that room (shouldn't you know about all your guests?). In any case, she handled my complaint very well and was nice enough to call the room above us once I told her the problem we were having. The noise did die down, thankfully.

author: Karina_In_Melbourne
title: I love this hotel!
text: Visiting Crater Lake without a car is the reason I wound up in Klamath Falls this September. Holiday Inn had an agreement with a local taxi company where they arrange for complimentary pick up and drop off at the Amtrak Station, which was a major selling point for me. And sure enough the taxi driver was waiting to meet me off the morning Coast Starlight train. The hotel was also happy to store my bags while I headed out to the lake for the day – something I had assumed was standard at all hotels but at least one other motel I contacted in Klamath Falls told me they could not offer this service. I had emailed Holiday Inn prior to booking to ensure they fitted my particular requirements and their response was prompt and thorough. The staff were very friendly and helpful via email, over the phone and in person. Once I returned from my trolley ride out to Crater Lake, check in was a breeze and I went up to my room. The hotel was clean and new, and the room was spacious with a street view. The wifi was free (great for web browsing but not strong enough to sustain a Google Hangouts phone call), the shower had a great flow and temperature, and best of all they had toiletries by Bath and Body Works which are one of my favourite brands. Sizzler was right next door and was my dinner choice. There was a big drug store across the road, and on the next block (maybe a 5 minute walk away) were several stores including Safeway and Ross. I spent my evening shopping then used the hotel’s coin laundry room (two washers and two dryers). There was also a gym and pool that I had no time to use, unfortunately. Buffet breakfast was included in the stay, served in the downstairs breakfast room. It included omelettes, pancakes, muffins and cereal. They also offered an express option for those who needed to eat on the road. The taxi was ready and waiting for me to head back to the Amtrak station at the time I had requested. There were no problems with checkout and I would happily recommend this property to anyone planning a stay in Klamath Falls.

author: rhansen7
title: Just what I needed
text: Two nights at HI Express and I'm refreshed. This hotel is perfect for any traveler. My room was 212 with a king sized bed, mini-kitchen/wet bar, couch, chair & ottoman, small dining table and separate desk with office chair. The decor is current and lovely, everything felt new and fresh. My bed was sooo comfortable. Internet connection was strong. Seriously loved it here; they have paid close attention to detail. I love the nite light on the blow dryer in the bathroom! I have 2 comments, not really complaints, but I didn't care for the shower head...one of the rain-kind, its really hard to rinse the soap out of your hair when the water softly falls like that...and the faucet handle was hard to turn. There is a "save the environment" hanger in the bathroom with a spotted owl on it. Considering how the spotted owl episode nearly destroyed Oregon's economy, I think maybe a picture of a waterfall or something would be more appropriate. The elevators must have recently had belts changed because it screaches to a halt when it reaches your floor. But there are 2 elevators so you don't have to wait long. Staff is friendly and helpful. I will stay here again, no doubt.

author: kandjOregon
title: Average stay
text: I stayed at the Holiday Inn Express while in town on business. I had moved over from the Best Western to meet up with co-workers in town. I should have stayed at the Best Western. The rooms are nicely appointed; however, the walls are paper thin. This is to be expected in a hotel, however the facility is a newer one and could have been built with this in mind. You get used to hearing the shower next door, but when you can hear the water running in the sink, telephone conversations, the clock radio and television, this is just too loud. There also seemed to be a lot of light in the room when you try to sleep. Green lights on the microwave that faces the full length mirror, making it shine throughout the room, the light coming in from under the door, the light from the clock - lots of towels were used to darken the room. They have a nice indoor pool area, but the unfortunately the spa was out of service for my entire week's stay. The breakfast room is clean, but I was bothered by all of the paper products used to eat on. Plastic silverware, foam plates, paper coffee cups. It seemed not only environmentally unfriendly, but low class. The food was decent, quite a few selections and a fun pancake machine. The breakfast room staff was excellent and very attentive. Other reviews were correct in the lack of parking due to the parking lot being shared by another hotel and a Sizzler restaurant. Many times I had to park quite a way from the hotel and when going out in the morning to leave for work, it was obvious that the parking is mainly used by the Sizzler crowd, because the parking is plentiful in the morning when Sizzler is closed. I went home for the weekend and returned to town again for work the following week but made my reservation at the Best Western Olympic Inn. I recommend it over this Holiday Inn Express.

author: cavejeff
title: Very good HI Express
text: This is a newer one, and way better than the smelly and tired HI Express I stayed at in Eugene OR (the one by the regular Hilton in Eugene). The room was great, and the woman at the front desk staff was also helpful, maybe her name was Yolanda. She fixed the exercise bike for me in the workout room and later got me a spoon. I think the only thing weird about this hotel is the room numbers. For some inexplicable reason, at least on the 3rd and 4th floors, the numbers jump around and the orientation signs on the walls are wrong. I was in room 420, and the sign pointed me to the left. Well, I went left, and the rooms started at 423 and went down from there but across from 421 where I expected to find 420, I found 419. Had I passed my room? Was it by the ice machine? What the heck? I went a bit further and the room numbers inexplicably jump from, say 412 to 415. So I decided to ignore the orientation sign and go the other way and was watching the numbers on the left side go up 423, 425, and then on the right they started at 418 again. So 425 is across from 418, and I kept going and found my room across from 427. How strange. I also noticed that there seemed to be glue on the wall by some of the signs, so I am wondering if they found out that someone had coded the locks wrong so they switched the room signs, or...well...I don't know. This really isn't a big deal, but it is awkward and they should fix it. But not fix anything else because everything else is quite nice. Although they could extend the pool hours to 24 hours/day like some other HIEs.

author: SKPeterson
title: A Jewel Amid the Gravel
text: My wife and I traveled to Klamath Falls, Oregon, for the 2013 USBC bowling tournament. I decided to give the Holiday Inn a try, as I had good luck with them in Europe, and the other hotels, from my web searches, seemed to be mostly junk. We arrived at about 5pm, and the check-in was effortless. The desk person only gave us one key, so I had to go back for another (maybe she asked me and I was just distracted by something else). The room was very clean and generally well maintained, but there were a couple of little glitches: 1) The bathroom door handle was loose; 2) The towel hook in the bathroom wall, next to the shower, was pulling out of the wall; 3) The A/C was VERY noisy. Since it was nice and cool at night we decided to sleep with the window open (they only allow them to be opened about 4 inches) - we were on the 4th floor, so no worries about security. TV quality was a bit iffy - seems we had a hi-def TV, but no hi-def TV signal. Bed was exceptionally comfortable, but I like them on the soft side...not everyone does. Breakfast was very good, for a hotel without a restaurant - milk, yogurt, cereal, scrambled eggs, sausage, biscuits/gravy, pancakes. I don't drink coffee, but according to my wife, it wasn't so great. Didn't have a chance to try the pool or the other facilities (pool / fitness). They've got a nice little business center just off the lobby. Ice and vending is in the elevator lobby on each floor. For a short building (only 4 floors), the elevators are kind of slow, but, oh, well. Plenty of places to eat within a 5 minute drive. Next time I'm in Klamath Falls, this is definitely where I'll stay.

author: Leisure_Traveler045
title: Clean and comfortable
text: I did not reserve ahead and found that getting a room mid-week was not as easy as I expected. Fortunately I snagged the last room here. Paid more than I would have liked but it was a nice stay. Large room with seating area. 32" HD TV. Bed comfortable and clean. Pretty much what you expect from this chain. Typical HIExpress breakfast food. The negatives are nit-picks but.... the room was hot and stuffy when I arrived. I turned on the A/C and went to dinner, but the A/C shuts off when no one is in the room, so I returned to a hot, stuffy room. Also the A/C is loud-ish and turns completely off/on when the temp needs adjusting, so expect to wake up frequently if you are a light sleeper. The bathroom door shuts itself and is not air conditioned, so if you want any fresh air in there, you'll need to prop the door open so that there is some air exchange with the room. The shower soaked the floor of the bathroom despite my best efforts to make a seal with the shower curtain. So I used extra towels to sop up the mess. The management said they were aware of this problem and trying out different solutions.

author: Substrata23
title: Superb Customer Experience & Spacious Rooms
text: I don't give out to many 5 star ratings, saving them for the experiences that really stand out. Our stay here was one of those. First off, we arrived at 1:30 PM exhausted and hot from a day of motorcycling and asked if we could check in early. Even though they had sold out the night before, they found us the 3rd floor room I requested (I thought this was the top floor.) Grateful, we got in the elevator only to realize their was a 4th floor. So we went back, head in hands asking if they could switch us to the 4th. Again, they came through despite how busy they obviously were. So thanks for that, Michael. Then we walked into the room and were immediately impressed with it's layout. Two beds, plus a sofa, plus a kitchenette -- all for $108. After 10 nights of different hotels/motels I can tell you this was a great deal. Since the facility was built in 2008 it has lots of outlets for recharging various devices. The wifi worked great for our laptops, not so great with our iPhones, but that has happened frequently. The shower had good water pressure and impressively fluffy towels. The A/C kept the room well cooled as well as providing a nice "hum" throughout the night to maks noise. We slept well on the firm bed and did find a couple of "soft" pillows among the 8 in the room. The location is in the busy outskirts of town; there are lots of eating and shopping choices including a large Safeway with a Starbucks only half a block away. The street stayed busy through the late night, so ear plugs are advised if you sleep light. All in all a great night's stay.

author: TZK
title: Suites are very spacious
text: This is an updated Holiday Inn Express. The hotel is not real large but does have 4 stories with 2 elevators. The parking lot seemed kind of small but we had no trouble finding a parking spot. The parking lot is adjacent to the parking lot of a Sizzler Restaurant. We stayed in a suite, which was very spacious. Suites differ from regular rooms because they have a sofa, coffee table & a table with 2 chairs which can be used for eating. All rooms, I believe, have microwaves & refrigerators. The fridge in our room was decent sized with a tiny freezer. 4 sets of plastic utensils & 4 styrofoam plates & bowls were in the cabinet by the microwave. Furnishing were very nice & the room was very clean. Wi-Fi in the room was very good. Beds & pillows, as in all Holiday Inn Express hotels, were very good. The bathroom counter top was quite high, which might be a problem for young children. Initially, it was difficult to figure out how to get the shower water temperature regulated but, once you figure it out, it's not hard. Near the lobby, there is a business center with 2 computers. The hotel only provided a small local newspaper - no USA Today papers. Breakfast was the same as at other Holiday Inn Express hotels but it wasn't quite as good the morning we were there. Eggs that were just put out were not hot & the coffee wasn't very good. Overall, it's a very nice hotel & I would definitely stay there again if I was in the area.

author: Spwilson13
title: New Years celebration
text: Stayed here for 3 nights over New Years. Excellent location central to the city and central shopping area. Staff is excellent and does a wonderful job. In particular Mr Hassan is a great employee who deserves special recognition. He is always attentive and no little detail goes unnoticed by him. His fixture is in the lobby and he eagerly awaits to help arriving and departing guests. In between he is found organizing the snack pantry, ensuring tables and chairs in the lobby and lunge are clean. All in all a great employee. Rooms are nice, clean and housekeeping went out of their way to make our stay enjoyable. We enjoyed room 241 (photos from balcony posted) which is a deluxe river view room. Although not that spacious, it does offer first rate views and on New Year’s Eve we had a front row seat to the numerous firework displays. Highly recommend this room for anyone who wants a first rate show without the hassle of crowds and cold. Breakfast is done well, with vast assortment of hot offerings, breads, and fresh juice. The sekt for mimosas is a welcome touch. Some minor irritations, but the excellent and very friendly staff did a great job and we thoroughly enjoyed our experience. HHonors Diamond

author: Pro-Flyer
title: It is what it is
text: Location is right by the Rhine. Hotel looks a bit like an old school or hospital. There appear to be a lot of Arabian guests attending medical facilities in Bonn. First impression was fairly Arabic and ailments. Reception was friendly and jolly. Corridors had a bit of an old Holiday Inn feel. A/C smelt a little bit, but managed to drop the temperature somewhat. Most disappointing was breakfast. What an unloved affair. Sour looking wait staff, buffet did not look fresh and appealing. There were a lot of Dutch people, many of them blatantly made sandwiches to wrap and take away. Wouldn't expect that at a Hilton. Finally, the garage charge was outrageous. Overnight parking in the hotel car park was in my opinion too expensive. Will I return? Maybe ... if in the area, it ain't a "go to" destination.

author: joekrueger
title: Nice Staff - Old Building - Excellent Location
text: Location: At Rhein Shoreline, View to Rhein, Walking Distance to City with many Restaurants and Bars ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Room: good size, very clean, fully equipped ⭐️⭐️⭐️ Breakfast: not enough stuff, used tables remain uncleaned, loud but dark room, no fresh made cooking station, lots of choices, normal quality of products ⭐️⭐️⭐️ Service: overall very friendly, asking the typical phrases, very good but not really personal. ⭐️⭐️⭐️ Wellness: Fitness. Sauna. Pool. Below Average. Needs state of the art improvement. No music. Almost no LED lighting. Small. ⭐️⭐️ Building: needs refurbishment. 90s look. Clean. Big. But old. ⭐️ Overall: one can see in every corner, that the owner safes money on renovation. The stuff does its best. Author: Hilton Diamond. SPG Platinum. GHA Black. Very frequent traveler.

author: ceedaworld1
title: #HiltonBonn
text: Travel is like reading a book. Turn the pages and the story keeps on going. Sometimes one has to bookmark a certain part. On my travels, I bookmark the Hilton Bonn. I hope the experience is the same as I remembered it from before. Yes the fresh look of the lobby and the easy check in and short walk to the rooms. My body has been on the go for hours and all I want to have is a clean and quiet place to recharge. A quiet sip of tea in a chair and a run of the international tv channels numbs my mind. Slowly, I will shower and slip into the plush robes and one size fits all slippers and jump into my dreams. Morning comes too quick and the river view is spectacular. I rush down to breakfast and find a cornucopia of fresh food and drink to start the day. Listening to the international chatter in the room, reminds me this could be any hotel in the world. But the German punctuality of service and flair of service set it aside from other places. My stay was over several days and each one brought new insights into the "Make it Right" motto. The Hilton Bonn is a destination for one to enjoy. It pleased me to stay here and I would bookmark it again.

author: NDawbneyFisher
title: Superb Christmas stay
text: We decided to come as a family over Christmas - my husband and I had been once before but just for one night, and wanted to return as the previous stay was not long enough. I had booked a deluxe room and junior suite, and a couple of days before I rang the hotel about allocating next to each other, possibly with connecting doors. I spoke to Thomas, front of house manager, and as a diamond member he upgraded the junior suite to a suite, then gave us a deluxe room with a connecting door, so in effect allocated us a two bedroom suite - excellent customer service. We had also inquired and booked the Christmas eve and Christmas day meal packages - Rachel had sorted it all out very efficiently. Got to the hotel, concierge parked the car securely in the garage, check in quick and efficient, went to the suite - superb it was. Large, comfortable beds, powerful showers, dining table, lovely sofa and chairs, and a sofa also in each bedroom, with a view of the Rhine. We had driven and decorated the lounge with our small Christmas tree, stockings, battery candles, and nativity - made it very homely. The Christmas eve dinner began with a champagne reception, and Rachel came to greet us, took us to our table, and her colleague Svenjia also came to greet us. The Goose, and Beef with an expresso crust were both superb, and there was a large selection of starters, and a delicious soup. Our package included wines, beer, soft drinks and water - we had some white and red wines, still and sparkling water - all very nice. I then went to Midnight Mass in the Basilica which was only a 10 minute walk. On Christmas day we had a leisurely breakfast and a superb buffet lunch, with the drinks package again, with Svenija lookng after all the guests well. The meal package prices were excellent value - what was also nice is that there weren't sittings - the table was yours for the whole evening/lunch, so there was no rush - we didn't stay the whole evening, but could have done. During our stay we also made use of the pool and sauna areas - nice and relaxing. The weather was fine, so we had some lovely walks along the river, and we also visited the main Christmas market and Beethoven House. It was our first Christmas away and it was superb - not least because of the excellent customer service we received before and during our stay. The hotel is great, and the location perfect - next to the Rhine, quieter than the city centre, but less than 10 minutes walk to the centre. Had a large selection of English tv channels, so we spent some time watching Christmas movies and relaxing. I'd highly recommend this hotel.

author: Daniel_NL
title: Good hotel, but average Hilton
text: In the recent years I have visited multiple Hilton properties, but this wasn't an impressive one. The hotel is 50% renovated. Strangely enough this relates to the lower 2 floors. I paid extra for a river view room, but this isn't worth the money. It's not like you have a view of the Petronas Towers, the Giza Pyramids or something so don't bother in my humble opinion. If you choose a room in the center of the courtyard you don't have a problem with street noise. Breakfast: it was so crowded there was a queue in front of the area. I think it is a bit sad if you serve cheap sekt with a plastic cap from a Louise Pommery Champagne cooler. You were able to order eggs but this isn't displayed anywhere (clearly). Parking: how can the hotel charge EUR 26,- per night if the parking 50 meters away charges EUR 12,-? For lazy guests? You can only pay cash at the other parking but there is an ATM in the hotel.
