Staff: very attentive. Location: on the edge of the center. Easy to walk down town. Spa: pool is very small but the sauna area is nice. Looks a bit tired though.

author: scottsitner
title: predictable and pleasant
text: I mean the above in a nice way. This was my first stop on two weeks in europe. I wanted something i could count on, with no weird european things to start with. I know I would get clean, comfortable, friendly and consistency. The room was renovated so very nice, although I could not get either thermostat to do anything, but the wndow open and it was fine. Nice towels(really) bed was comfortable, tv bored but for english speaking there were maybe ten channels and basically all news. The location is perfect. I walked everywhere with my son. just steps from the City center, the river, and Bonn U, it was a great location, could not have been better. I would stay here again for this. Staff was very nice, english speaking and ridiculously attractive. I ate lunch and breakfast. Lunch was a burger and tomato soup and was ordinary. Not bad, but nothing memorable. The breakfast buffet was very nice, good and fresh, and relaxing. The room overlooks the river so was pretty all in all, I am a loyal Hilton person. I know what I am getting. maybe it lacks local character but that is not always a good thing. I would stay here again.

author: aivarsd2016
title: Be careful with Hilton!
text: I book hotel through booking.com. The price was acceptable. When I returned home and found that the hotel blocked my credit card for a much larger amount. In addition to still blocked me an unknown amount. Although the hotel bill I signed for the amount on the reservation. For two days I can not get a response, and money on the card is not released. Is Hilton robbers? P.S. Breakfast is served burnt meat. Shame on Hilton! It was a very unpleasant surprise. In room water small buttle is for 4,50 EUR!!! "Hilton"?!?!? P.P.S. No-one room cleaner understands English!

author: albertg267
title: Laid-back stay in Bonn
text: A very nice location, just at the bank of Rhine. A short walk to the city centre, no need for the public transport. In general, a nice hotel, but most of the personnel is sort of undertrained (?). I saw mostly one person at the reception, therefore it took longer than usual for the check-in/check-out. A person during check-in behaved like a first-day trainee - didn't greet properly, didn't recognise the status, didn't explain anything. Had to come back some time later and talk to another person, he was knowledgeable and helpful, did an upgrade and issued vouchers for a bar (they don't have an executive lounge unfortunately). The breakfast was good enough, not extraordinary, but will suit most of people. However the service was again odd - the really puzzling thing for me was when the waiter asked whether I wanted a cup of coffee, I said yes and she started pouring it. However there was very little left in a coffee pot, she said 'oops', put the empty coffee pot on our table and never come back. There is a grill restaurant and a snack bar, and also the bar (good choice of cocktails). There is a pool, that was not crowded, however whenever we went there, there was a lady saying that they were going to have aqua fitness or whatever in 30 min. They really should put a schedule about these activities! There is also a sauna, and as quite common in Germany it is nude. Parking is extremely expensive, so we parked a car in the Opera parking, just a minute walk from the hotel, but much cheaper. In general, we enjoyed the stay, but the management should invest more in the personnel training.

author: thomassB9298KV
title: Average Business Hotel
text: Very central located next to the river and good reachable with public transportation. Rooms located next to the main road are a bit loud. Clean, but the rooms interior was a bit old. Our Chinese guest demanded a smoker's room, which was very smelly, way beyond a normal smokers room. We were very disappointed with the service. This was our first stay in a Hilton hotel so we expected more. Many small things are annoying. If you want to use the rooms wifi you need to register to Hilton's customer loyalty program. If you join this program and you reach a specific level, you will get a free bottle of water on the room and small snacks in the lobby. Otherwise you need to pay for that which I personally think is very silly and a sign of bad service. The minibar was empty which didn't bother us. Due to changes to our schedule we needed to checkout a day more early. They didn't want to refund us for the rooms even we told this to the reception in advance. Even the breakfast for the next day we had to pay. I expected more fairness. Fitness area and the pool are nice. Breakfast was also very good with the possibility to sit outside if the weather is nice.

author: fourcourt
title: Perfectly Acceptable International-style Hotel
text: I'm not quite sure why this is the Number 1 hotel for Bonn on Tripadvisor, the competition must not be trying very hard. There's nothing wrong with the property, I consider it to be perfectly acceptable, but overpriced. Positives: Good location within walking distance of the City Centre, Close to tram station, and to boat stations for trips on the river. Excellent breakfast facilities. Friendly and helpful staff. Spacious Hallways & good-sized, adequately-appointed rooms. Very clean. Negatives: Bar poorly stocked. Layout of Gym/Pool/Sauna area is odd. Many facilities appeared to cost extra. A room with a view of the river? - 'extra', Wi-Fi in the room? - 'extra', (unless you join the Hilton HHonours club so they can pester you with junk e-mails) - I've already paid near €200 a night, thanks - the least I'd expect is Wi-Fi. Bottled water in the room? - 'extra'. City tax should be factored into the initial price offering, not charged on checkout.

author: zeus-san-diego
title: I gave it 5 stars because of the service by the front desk staff alone.
text: I totally understand why some would give this a star less as it is more of traditional Hilton but I received excellent service and support from the front desk staff and that raises up the entire hotel. I had been traveling for over a week of business when I got to the Hilton and asked for some ideas on places to eat that were not at the Hilton or tourist laden. One of the front desk people jumped on the computer and did some quick research, asked about if I wanted a nice walk and about any other preferences. Once I was done, I had a nice place chosen, a mile or so walk through beautiful neighborhoods and along a park. Exactly what I wanted. I ended up walking into the wrong restaurant, haha, totally my fault, and it turned out even better than what I had planned. Back to the hotel. The front desk folks also helped me figure out where a few stores were for various types of needs after I lost a few things over the prior week. The hotel overall seemed clean, well kept, and well managed. They took care of little things like replacing my sparkling water with still water, and they delivered on everything I was looking for. They have a spa with two saunas, a pool, a reflection room, and a workout area. All very well kept. I was surprised they actually had such a nice spa as it is a smaller Hilton. They have a huge breakfast buffet, and it is a bit pricey, so make sure you are hungry. My room was good size, facing the courtyard and seemed updated, no signs of wear and tear. The rooms facing the main road coming over the river might be noisy, don't know, but it is a busy road so I would recommend a courtyard facing room, north facing room, river facing room. While not cheap, I was able to walk everywhere I wanted to go from the hotel so that made it a "value" from my perspective.

author: katherineannelee
title: Typical Hilton Home in Bonn
text: I stayed in Bonn for one night on business. Bonn didn't seem to have too many nice looking hotels I found. So I went with the classic Hilton as you can normally know what to expect with these kind of chains. And so it was. It's a typical, ageing, Hilton. It is very clean and the staff where nice. The room was classic and had all I needed. A minus point is that you need to pay for a bottle of water for the night. One bottle should be in the price, I think. They have two restaurants, the Grill and a bistro style restaurant and a bar. I had a quick dinner at arrival in the bistro and it was nice. What I liked was the fitness area that was perfect for a workout in the morning. What confused me is that you only get internet if you are a Hilton club member. Else you can only use the internet in the reception. This kind of service I find very strange in this time and age. It is not the hotel I would like to spend a vacation in but it was good and convenient.

author: nldogbert
title: Good hotel close to center of Bonn and the Rhine river
text: Check-in: Fast and efficient with all relevant information provided. Room: Was given a deluxe room with a partial view of the river. Room has a small balcony which is nice in the summer and warn nights. Other than that, a simple room as expected from Hilton hotels in Germany. Typical amenities in the room. Internet: Free internet provided as a HHonors member, only too bad as a mid-tier elite member you still have to share the basic internet with other guests. Speed was ok, did not experience any drop in signal. Bar/Lounge: A small area, and due to the Christmas market surge in guests, it was crowded and for guests arriving late, no further place was available. On normal days it would most probably be sufficient. Breakfast: This must be the highlight of the stay. Great spread and the best is that it is a champange breakfast - this is getting rare in Germany/Switzerland. The quality of the food here is very good and service very efficient even though there was a crowd. This in my opinion is the best among the Hiltons I have stayed in Germany. Staff: Just your usual German efficiency, nothing more nothing less. Generic: A reasonable hotel in the area - if it was not for the good breakfast, than I would say the value for money at this property is on a low side - since there is nothing else that is spectacular provided.

author: dadsasdasd
title: Good Hotel by the River
text: Nicely located hotel offering good if not über-luxury service. Review based on a one night stay in June (background of spending 80+ nights per year in different hotels around the globe). Location: A very good location with just a stone’s throw away from Rhine, next to the Kennedybrücke. Walking distance to the city center. Immediate neighborhood an interesting mix of residential area, shisha shops and the Opera. Tram & subway station a bit over 100 meters away, distance to the main railway station roughly 1km. Biergarten Am alten Zoll perhaps 300m south of the hotel was a nice place to enjoy a beer (or three) while watching the traffic on the river. Room: Room at 3rd floor with a view towards the courtyard, Rhine just about visible. Room was big enough for us, though it was not especially roomy as such. Décor was rather calm, the room was very clean with no signs of usage anywhere. Few minor details where the hotel is beginning to show its age, for example the elevator buttons were not always working as they should, but nothing really to complain about as such. Little noise from the corridor, did not notice any noise from the other rooms or street. Etc: Breakfast was very good, plenty of warm & cold choices including also some local Sekt (sparkling wine). Did not try the restaurant/bar otherwise, so no comment there. Check-in & out was fast and friendly. Two bottles of water received as complimentary. Parking garage was somewhat tight to navigate as well as expensive. Would I return there? Sure, a good hotel in a nice location

author: davidtrandal
title: Christmas in Bonn
text: Historically we have spent our winter vacations in warmer climates (e.g., Hawaii). This year we decided to spend some time in Bonn and it went very well. Given the cold we figured we would need to spend a larger portion of our time indoors. Thus, we splurged and stayed at the Hilton in Bonn. This is an excellent hotel. The rooms are spacious, very clean, large windows, and brightly lit. Most important, the rooms are very quiet. While we loved heading out to the Christmas markets during the day and early evening, it was awesome having some down time in our cozy room. I have stayed here before and will continue to stay here on future visits to Bonn. Some of the other key advantages of staying at the Hilton Bonn. It is only a couple of blocks from the city center. It is on the Rhine. You can grab the tram right next to the hotel. There is a McDonald’s a couple of blocks away if you want a quick soda (with ice) or an egg McMuffin. The room had a mini-fridge for leftovers and/or to store your soda. The hotel has a nice pool and sauna which we went to every morning. We also joined a water aerobics class on one of the mornings (no charge). Ice machine on each floor. Again, excellent hotel!!

author: 351premk
title: BASIC HOTEL AT GREAT LOCATION!
text: Last weekend I traveled to Austria by car from Blackpool. On my way I took a stop over at this Hilton Bonn. I stayed one night here. Hotel situated overlooking River Rhine, very near to main Bonn city attractions specially Beethovan haus. On my arrival welcome by friendly reception staff. As a diamond member, upgraded to deluxe room. Originally I booked king guest room for 73.03 euro. As per my wish, they allocated my room. Room at the top floor (fourth floor), near to the elevator (room number 402). Clean room with good view of the River Rhine from the private balcony, comfortable bed, TV with lots of channels etc made my stay enjoyable. Attentive staff help me every way. Great breakfast. Now the odds, hotel don't have executive lounge. Small size bath tub. Parking expensive - 26 euros. Over all I enjoyed the stay.

author: robertaA3859QN
title: Nice place with some flaws!
text: Overall the stay was pleasant. Rooms are nice and are spacious but could have used a dab of paint here and there. I assume last renovation was a while ago. The bathroom door had also seen better days. Would expect higher quality from a Hilton hotel. Only annoying fact is that one has to pay a ridiculous high fee for parking. 26€ for the day is a rip off. Of course they know that it's hard to find a spot nearby. The opera is next door and the places outside are reserved for the people that live there. I could live with the fact that if I'm not a guest at the hotel that I would have to pay a higher price but this is a rip off and a lack of service. Also free internet via WiFi is only available in the lobby. If you want to connect to the internet in your room you need to pay. Again an example of terrible service. As we only stayed a night the missing internet did not impact us that badly. Mobile reception was very good so it was no issue to use that instead.

author: glewbel
title: Standard conference hotel in a great location, and with nice staff
text: The Hilton Bonn faces the Rhine, and is a couple of blocks from the historic central district. There are lots of restaurants within a few minutes' walk, and the tram from the main train station stops a block away from the hotel. Some of the rooms have a view of the river, although most of them look into a courtyard that has more of a "peek" at the river. However, if you're not likely to sit in your room watching the water, don't spend a lot extra on a river view room since there are benches on the riverbank just across the street. We stayed at the Hilton Bonn in August 2014 and it was mostly packed with an odd mix of business travelers and large (very large) Middle Eastern families with lots of kids racing around the lobby. The hotel staff was excellent--friendly and helpful--and our room was clean and functional with one exception. There was a massive, thick layer of fuzzy dust on the vanes for the air conditioner vent above our heads when we checked in. It looked as if it had been there for months. We called that to their attention and they took care of it. I guess housekeeping doesn't regularly vacuum much above the floor level. I would not describe the Hilton Bonn as luxurious or even "trendy" (per TripAdvisor's standard review questions) or "romantic," it's just a comfortable, somewhat elderly conference hotel. Breakfasts were very good so it's worth trying for a rate that includes them. Quite a few websites rate this property as 4 stars out of 5. I think 3 stars would be more realistic. It feels like an older hotel with a comfort level similar to a Hilton Garden Inn, though with a nicer lobby, better restaurant, and a nicer bar.

author: MichaelA496
title: One of the best Hiltons ever
text: Stay sometimes at Hiltons but never been motivated to review a large chain business hotel before. This place is however exceptional. Seems to be staffed entirely by kids (or am I just getting old) who are happy and motivated to make your stay perfect. Rooms very modern, and soundproofing tops. The tramline passes by the hotel but you would not know unless you look out the window. Breakfast buffet extensive covering everything from fresh croissants, fresh fruit to eggs'n'bacon, with an amazing fresh cheese selection. Health centre in basement looks spotless. free wifi in lobby but room wifi costs bless Hilton Honours member of high standing. Hotel restaurant too expensive for my wallet but menu looks very traditional with a few nice touches so if you are on an expense account go for it. Now, the hotel does not push the location but this place is perfect for walking along the Rhein as it is literally only metres away from the front door. Across the road is the Bonn theatre and around the corner the Beethoven concert hall. Location location location. The aforementioned tramline takes you straight into the town centre but you will enjoy a stroll through the cafe quarter more, its starts at the next block. My tip is look first at this place when planning on staying in Bonn, if there is a block booking for a conference the price skyrockets so go elsewhere, but if you can get a good deal it is by far the best place in Bonn. they have great advance booking deals so watch out for them if you know your travel dates. If the closet light comes on when you open the door don't worry, it extinguishes itself after 4 minutes.

author: 737daveg
title: Comfortable Hotel
text: I have stayed here often on business. The building may not be impressive but the rooms are large, impeccably clean and the beds are large and comfortable. No need for a car as it is an easy walk to anywhere in Bonn or a nice walk along the Rhine. The breakfast in the morning is large and provides many options including individually cooked eggs to your liking. The staff at the front desk is some of the best I have ever encountered and is a reason why I love this hotel. No request seems too large or too small. And always a warm welcome when you arrive. The fresh fruit at the desk is nice as well as the small knosh in the room upon arrival. Also free English language newspapers everyday (for those of us who lack fluency in German). Many restaurants nearby. I would recommend Hotel Pastis restaurant around the corner and avoid the Thai place across the street. The hotel bar is nice in the evenings after a long day. The bar food is good if you are too lazy to go out for dinner. My chair was by the window. Treat it well.

author: KingDaniel911
title: Shaky start, but all issues resolved and we had a great stay!
text: We recently stayed in the hotel and selected the hotel based on parking and location, and the general quality level of the Hilton chain. Price: the room rate was rather high, reflecting the July high-season. Also Internet was rather high at 20 Euro per day, considering T-Mobile offer a 4.95 rate for their 24hr Wifi hitspots in Germany. Quality: excellent, but. We initially had a number of minor issues which combined became a significant problem. However, all of these were resolved and the management team did an exceptional job of communicating with us. Service: following on from the previous comments. The service at the hotel was really excellent, from the check-in staff, housekeeping, restaurant and general management, they all seemed extremely concerned that our stay was initially poor due to a number of minor issues. These were all resolved and we were given a number of complimentary items that more than resolved our initial disappointment. Facilities: the restaurant is good, breakfast was excellent and it was great to be greeted by your name upon arrival each morning. The gym was well maintained, my only issue was a lack of air-conditioning but this is in the process of being resolved. There is a pool, it looks nice, but I did not use it. There is underground parking which is also excellent, very secure and plenty of space. We arrived in a sports car with low suspension and had no trouble getting in and out of the garage, which can be a problem at some hotel locations in major cities. Overall I can highly recommend the Hilton Bonn hotel. Simply from the attitude of the staff alone, but combined with the excellent location and faculties it was well worth the visit. We will definitely stay again at the hotel.

author: RebellenA
title: Reduced Hilton Honour benefits
text: I visited this hotel two years ago and then in would have received the grade from me but for my last visit it only receives three. Mainly to the reduced benefits for Hilton Honour members. Last time I visited you were given one bottle of water for free and they also delivered a plate of cakes to your room. Now the free bottle of water is away (about 5€ in the minibar menu). In our room was awaiting some free muffins, but the muffins were very old and hard, also the chocolate bars that were offered had expired six months ago. I hope this was a bad joke from the hotels side, otherwise I do not understand why you give expired food to your regular customers. Next time you find old things in your cupboard, please throw it away instead of "rewarding" your customers with that. Also there is free internet for one hour in the lobby, it might be free but would be nice if you could connect to the network as well, after 30 minutes trial and error we ended up with going to a cafe for some wifi access instead. Also the cozy bathrobes and slippers have disappeared. The gym when visiting it (20 Jan 2013) smelled of oil, maybe there had been some maintenance to the machines, but when I came there it was empty and I can understand why as in that smell nobody would do exercise. The sauna and pool were good, although would be nicer to change in the room and use the bathrobe to go down. Now also the body lotion from the sauna has been removed away. the room was okay, one of the newly renovated rooms on 1st floor, I hope the chairs will be renovated aswell, our armrests felt apart when we sat on that. The TV channel selection is good, but you need to do something with the login system for the TV, everytime we turned it on, we had to select what languages for the menus etc. this you should only do once. Also there is an annoying delay when you change channels, everytime it takes 5-10 seconds before the sound and pictures appears. The bed was good and comfortable, the toiletries ok, but would have appreciated more of them if there are two guests. The breakfast was really good. I hope that the Hilton honours downgrading benefits are only temporary and that the hotel does not make jokes on other guests by serving already expired food to them. But after my bad experience I need to start looking for another hotel for my upcoming trips to Bonn.

author: Masahisa
title: Quiet hotel by the Rhine River
text: Location: we walked from Bonn Hauptbahnhof to the hotel and it took about 15 minutes. The hotel is on a big street and it was easy to find it. There is a tram station near the hotel (just a few blocks away), but it was fun to walk because we walked through the downtown and got to see pretty shopping streets and beautiful city hall. The area it locates is very quiet with no shops and restaurants around it. The back of the hotel is facing the Rhine River. Check In/Out: It was not busy hour when we checked in and out, so checking in and out was quick, it took only a few minutes to check in, and only a minute to check out. The lady at the front desk was good and very efficient. Room: It was modern and clean, big enough for two of us. I did not have any problem with opening my suites case on the floor, and still I could walk freely in the room. The chair in the room was very comfortable. Our room was facing inner courtyard, so it was very quiet during our stay in this hotel. The only disappointment is that we did not have nice river view. Bathroom: It was a little bit smaller than I expected but I liked it because of the modern design and it was clean. There were nice shampoo and soap! Overall: The hotel is good value for money. If the hotel was a little closer to downtown, it was perfect. I would come back here if I have a chance again!

author: starflyergold
title: The great WiFi rip off - rooms ok
text: I stayed two nights at the Hilton Bonn. All in all it is a comfortable hotel though not what I would call luxury. The room was not particularly large but functional. The king bed was comfortable though the duvet covers (2 separate ones which was strange) were a bit flimsy. The bathroom was acceptable and functional. Toiletries are Peter Thomas Roth. The mini bar was not restocked after the first night which was just as well considering the prices. Housekeeping was superficial and missed cleaning the room properly. The air conditioning was not very powerful. A growing annoyance with Hilton (not just this property) is that they insist on charging exorbitant amounts for WiFi. There are 2 options to choose from: leisure and business. The former an outrageous €13 for a slow service or the latter for an eye watering €18. That is per device! So if you like me travel with laptop, iPhone and iPad you pay €13 for each device for each day. Surely that can't be right. It is this sort of rip off which makes me choose Hilton less and less. While I was staying some construction work was going on with occasional drilling noises (the website did not mention this at time of booking). The staff were friendly and nice.

author: Ingermany
title: This should be a Fairfield Inn
text: It seems that I am always critical, or at least when it comes to Hilton Hotels. I love to travel and stay in the boutique hotels of Paris or the B&B's in the UK, but when I am traveling for business I just want a little piece of Americana. I think more so because I live in Germany, I feel Hilton should be a great American experience. I also think others who stay at a Hilton judge America by how they are treated at the Hilton. I found the Bonn Hilton to not be up to the standards it should. It is clean, and ordred as you would think any place run by Germans would be, but the Hilton experience ended there. Part of the day I had to work in my room at the hotel. There was a jack hammer going on for hours, this was crazy for a business hotel. I am finally a Diamond Club Member with Hilton, yeah! It took years to get to that level and the Bonn Hilton I was to stay as such. Not one mention of my level with Hilton, I will admit I was just excited about it, and really do enjoy the privileges. I will tell you that the executive lounge was nonexistent! Instead, we were all given a bag in the lobby, one item for Blue, two for Gold and I got the privilege of having three items which were just horrible. I was checked off the list with perfect German efficiency to ensure I would not get anything else. I also have to mention the food, it was horrible and room service was a joke. Interent was bad and parking was 25 Euros per day, in Bonn, not Berlin or Hamberg.

author: Insightful
title: The service is superb
text: The staff in this hotel are young and of a high calibre. The receptionists evinced an alluring combination of suave professionalism and genuine warmth which instantly made us feel at home in the hotel. Though we arrived there at about 10.30 p.m., the downstairs restaurant (which was empty at the time) immediately rustled us up a couple of very tasty pasta dishes (washed down with German beer so real that you could taste the hops! ). The hot food was very welcome given the sub-zero temperatures outside. We had a similarly positive experience with the hotel breakfast. There's an extensive smorsgabord of both hot and cold dishes and - if you're travelling somewhere early in the morning - the generous breakfast certainly sets you up for most of the day. The bedrooms are warm and comfortable. The bathrooms are bright with highly effective showers. But, in common with one of the other posters on this thread, I would put the rooms into the 'very good' as opposed to 'great' category. They're fine for a night's sleep ; but there's nothing much to differentiate them from thousands of other hotel rooms in thousands of other business-oriented hotels throughout the world. The hotel is about as central as you can get. It is literally a six or seven minute walk away from all the central attractions of Bonn (including the house in which Beethoven was born : a 'must see' in my opinion). I would definitely return to this hotel. But mainly because the staff are youthful in outlook and lively and obviously enjoy the hospitality business. Genuinely great people.

author: Maxesparents
title: By far the best hotel in Bonn - and great staff
text: My second stay at the Hilton Bonn, and it surpassed previous experiences. I got exactly the room location I had requested. Everything was extremly clean and quiet. TV and internet working without a flaw. A bed from heaven. Good location, everything you might need in walking distance. Allowed early checkin and an extended checkout. The staff was extremly helpful (corrected a minor internet charge problem without hesitation). If you like good food, the hotel restaurant is the place to go. I had the best "Wienerschnitzel" I can remember and a wonderful appetizer, and all dishes were presented and executed very professionally - and surprisingly affordable. Great breakfast choices. Nice pool and well maintained fitness area. You cannot go wrong here. F. Diederichs

author: dcl80
title: Small and Useful Hilton
text: This hotel is a nice Hilton right on the Rein River. Next to the Kennedy bridge. Quick walk to the town center. I did not have very high expectations... but I have to say I was very wrong this hotel is small but very cute. I like the fell of a small hotel, but i think they still have like 200 rooms. The lobby is small with a nice open bar. My check in was very quick, and the lady checking me in was nice, helpful and welcoming. As a Diamond member.. I got an upgrade to a Deluxe room with a balcony over looking the courtyard and the river. I got a free welcome drink at the bar, and a fruit plate in my room. Two bottles of water also in my room. I also was provided the Hilton breakfast, very good... the staff in my seating area was not as helpful, This was the only down point in my stay. Room was a nice size flat LCD TV, good bathroom...clean.. and bed was nice also... Also was given a late check out.. over all happy with my stay...

author: IndianaMichigander
title: Best B&B I've ever experienced - hands down.
text: I had the recent occasion to stay at short notice in Kport. The Captain Jefferds Inn was recommended by a friend who has stayed here exclusively in Kport for over 10 years. Sarah, the innkeeper along with her husband, Erik, could not have been more accommodating. Due to the chaos of organizing many friends and family to all stay together for an unexpected event, numerous phone calls for additions, subtractions, and then more additions had to be made. Sarah, and her assistant, Rachel, were amazingly flexible and understanding. We had a group of 8 people total, and we were all made to feel welcomed and at home. The rooms are beautifully appointed, comfortable, clean, and cozy. The breakfasts were delicious, all freshly made, and set the tone for good days. The sun room has delicious snacks and drinks. Checkout times were flexible, and that was much appreciated. Sarah and Erik generously upgraded our room and were incredibly kind at a time that was most appreciated. The Captain Jefferds Inn is a gem. I would recommend it to anyone. Knowing now that it's there, I wouldn't stay anywhere else when I return to Kport. Thank you for a memorable experience.

author: keithm368
title: Flying Visit
text: My wife and I love Kennebunkport. During previous visits we stayed in a nearby establishment and wrote a nice report on trip advisor. However it had lost its appeal. This time we wanted something different. We found it and what an amazing place Captain Jefferd’s is. We were welcomed warmly and shown around the house. Lots of lovely personal touches which are delicious and generous. Our room was perfect. It was comfortable and cosy, containing all expected amenities. The Inn was busy with lots of guests yet there was plenty of space to be private. The food served was to die for. Sarah and Erik along with their housekeepers made each individual feel valued. Chatting the right amount of time, being courteous and helpful. Visits to the States are made as frequently as we can but this is one place we will return to. It really is a place to stay and be looked after. Thank you!

author: traveler6257
title: Excellent Anniversary Stay at Captain Jefferds Inn
text: We stayed at the Captain Jefferds for our 30 anniversary long weekend and absolutely loved it! The property was warm, welcoming, and well maintained. There were nice common rooms as well as outside areas to sit and relax. The porch was amazing. Bright and comfortable. The breakfast was incredible. It was a 3 course breakfast each morning and we ended up not really eating much for lunch. The staff was wonderful as well which is what really topped it off. They were helpful with suggestions and so accommodating when we asked if they would take our picture prior to dinner on our anniversary. She walked us all around the property taking various shots! Amazing. Location was convenient. Just a couple of blocks to the center of town with restaurants and shops. Arundle Wharf restaurant was at the end of the road which was really good as well. Highly recommend Captain Jefferds and would stay there again!

author: Janet3471
title: Perfect!
text: My husband and I make an annual trip to Maine every summer and stay at the Capt. Jefferds. I've titled this review "Perfect" because I can't think of any part of our stay that is less than that. We have stayed in the Wiscasset room recently but other years have stayed in different rooms. The rooms are spacious, clean, filled with light and so comfortable. They are beautifully decorated. The breakfasts are incredible. The 3 course meal leaves everyone happy and ready for the day! The location of the inn can't be beat. A walk into town and shopping or a walk to the ocean is such an amazing choice. Either way you are never disappointed! Finally, the innkeepers and staff are wonderful!! They make you feel so welcome every year and are so helpful with any questions you may have. They do so many personal and thoughtful things like leaving granola bars for our early departure, a candle in my "birthday" muffin and Prosecco in the room to celebrate. It all adds up to a "perfect" stay!

author: scdm
title: Lovely Inn with lots of amenities
text: This is our second visit, but it's been a long time in between. We came back because it was a gracious and pretty setting at that time and nothing has changed since then. We were escorted to a corner room with two comfortable chairs, large bed with smooth, soft sheets and fluffy feather pillows! The AC is regulated by temperature for precise cooling. The staff is delightful. They have two porches for guests to enjoy and a very pretty inside sitting room. The Inn provides free wi-fi and there is also a desktop for guests to use if they wish. On the sun porch (with beautiful sea breezes) guests can enjoy cold water or soft drinks any time of day. You can also have some wine for a small fee. At 3:00 PM, the staff provides cheese, crackers and homemade cookies. (Try the almond ones--really delicious!) There is coffee and tea during the day and in the early morning (when it is really appreciated). There are daily newspapers put out for guests to read. I'm sure there are more amenities that I am missing because they have thought of everything. Oh yes, they provide beach chairs, umbrellas and bicycles! This Inn is conveniently located to the town--very easily walked--and close by to the beaches. Can't wait to come back!

author: CarolanD111
title: The Best!
text: From the moment you walk into the Inn, you are warmly greeted and catered to! The rooms are immaculate...each one is different. The sheets are silky and divine. The towels soft and lush. The products smell wonderful. Even the special touches like a washcloth just for makeup. No detail isn't thought of. Each afternoon homemade treats are put out in the sunroom. Magazines and books to avail yourself of. Self service tea station that rivals any tea house. Shops and restaurants are a short walk. Sarah will have terrific recommendations for you. Wonderful to escape there in the winter....bundle up and walk on the beach or to town. Come back and put your feet up in front of a roaring fire. Oh, and the three course breakfast...each one was unique and delicious! We were pampered!

author: stephaniecD3323NW
title: Fantastic stay in a wonderful town!
text: We stayed in 3 different rooms (Wyeth, Arundel, and Baxter) during our extended stay over the New Year's holiday. This could not have been a more wonderful experience! Each room had its own unique charms. The Wyeth is in the front of the main house and offers a fantastic bathroom with standing jets in the shower and a great view from the front of the house. The Arundel room is in the back of the main house and has a spa tub and gas fireplace with 2 very comfortable armchairs. The Baxter room is in the Carriage House, and has the feel of a cabin, with a beautiful painted mural around the 2-person spa tub. The gas fireplace adds to the cabin-y feel, and a screened in porch would be wonderful in the summer. The staff was exceptionally friendly and always willing to go the extra mile for their guests, providing wonderful conversation, excellent recommendations for activities, and anything guests might request no matter the time of day. The rooms were clean, comfortable, and beautifully decorated, with some of the nicest linens I've ever seen or felt. Each room has 2 plush bathrobes. Many of the rooms have gas fireplaces which were perfect for those cold Maine winter nights, and the spa tubs were so relaxing. Special mention goes to the chef and staff for the amazing 3-course breakfast prepared every morning! During an 8 day stay, I never had something I didn't enjoy immensely. The staff was very happy to accommodate any food allergies, preparing individual special dishes for select guests. I can not recommend the Captain Jefferds Inn enough! I will most certainly come stay again, hopefully with more family so I can share the experience of this wonderful place!

author: K5048MErichardh
title: Could not have been better ... Seriously!
text: My wife and I were in New England as a couple for the first time in 35 years. We searched all over websites like you're doing right now. Our eyes seemed to go cross-eyed. I came across Captain Jeffereds Inn in Kennebunkport, Maine while we were deciding where we would stay in MA, VT, NY or ME. We booked nothing at that time. Then the day of the trip we were on the search again and came across very good references of Captain Jefferds Inn. We called the owner of the Inn. She was delightful to talk with and we choose to spend our only two vacation nights with them. Best decision ever. Off-the-charts! I wish we could have stayed a week. This place had it all; charm, romance, fair price, great breakfast and wonderful staff. I recommend it without reservation. In fact, we are going to South Central Massachusetts in February and I'm thinking we will forgo looking at other B&Bs in MA and make the two and a half hour trek to Kennebunkport just to be with these wonderful new friends and their outstanding home. Your search is over. Take the plunge and book it. I don't write reviews but Captain Jefferds was that good that I've opted to write this one. Hope it helps you! Dick

author: travelmutter
title: Spacious B&B, dog friendly, free bikes, in historic area, walk to restaurants
text: Large, gracious historic home with gracious innkeepers but keep in mind that it is a B&B so if having breakfast (2 seating times) at a common table with other guests is not your thing, then look for something else. Spacious common areas throughout the ground floor for relaxing and coffee/tea available all day and cookies/cheese etc available in the afternoon. They also have wine available for a nominal fee ($7-$8/glass). Not all of the rooms are located in the main house. I was in the HIdeaway room (compact room up an exterior flight of steps with a small duck your head entrance). It is a dog-friendly room and it seems that the dog-friendly rooms are located outside of the main house and have exterior entrances. All rooms equipped with hair dryer, lotion, shampoo and crème rinse). I am an early riser and was able to enter the main house and have coffee and read the paper (NY Times, Wall Street Journal and the Portland, ME paper were available) in the sunroom. Free Wi-Fi is also available. No TV's. Walked into town at night to eat. The reason I chose the Inn was because they indicated they had free bicycles available to use. although they had put them away for the winter, they graciously found one for me and I was able to explore the area by bike. Bottom line, would I stay there again? Yes, most definitely. The location is excellent.

author: octoberlady33
title: If only the innkeepers cared about guests' comfort as much as the decor
text: My husband and I went for a short birthday getaway. First, the good: The inn is beautiful with large gorgeous common rooms on the first floor - a large living room, dining room and sun room. Erik the innkeeper was very friendly when he checked us in and helped with reservations for dinner at a local restaurant. We were on the third floor in the Katahdin Room, 3rd floor. It rained and stormed all night. The wind rattled the windows, and I mean all three windows sounded like doors slamming non-stop! After a sleepless few hours we stuffed some paper between the frames and that helped a lot. I can't believe that the owners don't know of this problem and that for a few dollars you can put foam tape between the frames and prevent it! The WORST part was at checkout when the owner, Sarah, asked if it was windy up there during the night, and when I said yes, and told her about the banging of the windows, she SMILED and said, "well, it's an old house, old windows". Really?!!! Also, the mattress was awful - soft and the springs were shot. The inn is a beautiful place but it would be nice if the owners put some effort and money into the features that allow their guests to be comfortable during their stay. Breakfast was nice - fresh fruit, a scone and pancakes. We enjoyed it until at the end, Sarah came out and announced that the cook had had to go home sick, and the housekeeper had taken over and should be congratulated. OMG - the cook who prepared most of our food went home SICK?! Thanks for the info. Sarah - next time at least just say the regular cook was "unable to come in today"! A beautiful place, but I would not recommend it to a friend.

author: hollyhill29
title: Charming to Boot!
text: My husband and I thoroughly enjoyed our stay in the Wyeth Room on the Second Floor. Generous in size with a lovely mantled fireplace! The inn keepers maintain this property meticulously. Great attention to detail. The king bed was very comfortable with lovely linens and fluffy pillows. Great shower! Very nice toiletries. There is always hot tea, coffee and hot chocolate available. Fresh baked cookies in the cookie jar. Lovely afternoon treats set out. The breakfast is served quite formally in the dining room. Full service. There is an early seating and a later seating. We chose the later, which was 9:30. Worked out great for us. I would highly recommend this Inn. Walking distance to town where all the great little shops and restaurants are located. Lovely all the way around!

author: osesu96
title: Very Pleasant Stay
text: We selected this B&B based upon other reviews found on Tripadvisor. We booked and made our way to the Inn. We were impressed with the upkeep of the Inn and the grounds. We walked into the Inn and were immediately met by one of the innkeepers who took us on a brief tour before showing us to our room. The room we had was called "The Hideaway". Overall, a very comfortable room that has its own charm. It had an outside entrance which is good for those who may be out late and a little door in which to enter the room. The room size was roughly the size of an inside cabin on a cruise ship, same would apply to the bathroom. All was comfortable and clean for the 3 days we were in town. The Inn also boasts electric car hook-ups for those of you on the cutting edge of vehicle technology. The breakfasts were superb. Two seatings, so make sure you confirm with the Innkeeper which one you are assigned. The breakfasts included a fruit dish to start followed by the main course which was like a quiche or french toast with fresh berries, etc. Afternoon tea, snacks were typically cheese and grapes, cookies in the late evening. The Inn also had 2 patios, plenty of access to the mini-kitchen, bikes you could borrow, etc. Overall, we are extremely happy with this Inn and will definitely return.

author: J1914RZdouglass
title: Outstanding Visit at a 5 Star Property
text: This was our first time to stay in a B & B/Inn. We didn't know what to expect and were a little reticent. What a surprise we received. We made the reservation over the phone and it was like talking to a new best friend. Everything was explained / discussed - including the fact that we would be arriving late - the key would be waiting for us and we were given the code for the front door. The room was much more than we expected. It was large, comfortable and VERY clean. The AC worked great. The bathroom was very large, had a tub and shower ( separate) and plenty of room for two and VERY clean. Sara sat at breakfast every day and joined in the conversation. The 3 course breakfast was delicious and different each day. There was always coffee, tea, homemade cookies available. Just can't say enough about the frioendliness of the staff, the care which was taken to ensure our stay was perfect and the attention to every detail that was very evident. Location for the area is great - very walkable - or you can use the bikes to explore. Sara knows the area well - great suggestions for exploring, baeching and eating.This inn would be equivalent to a 5 Star hotel ( in our opinion) and we would highly recommend this property.

author: joshmom
title: Absolutely wonderful!!
text: You feel at home from the minute you enter the B&B! I can't rave enough about the Capt. Jefferds. The staff is so professional, warm and gracious - they truly want you to have he best stay and are there to help you make that happen! Every detail is covered from lovely snacks in the afternoon to water bottles and espresso coffee all day to the beautiful grounds... We stayed in The Chatham Room, which is right off the entry foyer. Normally we wouldn't chose that location as it is next to the front door, but it was great. The room is charming and we felt as if we were the only guests. We came and went as if it were our own home! I would definitely recommend the Chatham Room. The breakfast is delicious and they accommodate any issues. It's service with a smile and a huge desire to please. The location is fabulous. The Inn is on a quiet street just a few blocks from the center of town, you park when you first arrive and can walk everywhere. We took full advantage of the beach! You sign out the parking permit, chairs and towels, which is a lovely feature. Every effort is made here to have the best stay. We look forward to our next stay!

author: 390susanf
title: Beautiful Inn
text: My husband and I were given a gift certificate for Captain Jefferds Inn from our son a year ago Christmas. I called to make reservations and was told there was a two night minimum. Since my husband and I were going to be married 45 years on a weekend they had available we booked for two nights. Reservations and email notifications were done very efficiently. The day we arrived we were greeted by Steve who was extremely friendly and gave us the tour. We were very impressed with the amenities afforded to the guests but when we were taken to our room we were disappointed. We were assigned to River Green, which was a room in the roofline. Therefore it was small and the ceiling over the bed was slanted so if you got up from the bed too quickly and forgot about the ceiling, you hit your head. There was a skylight in the roofline over the bed which had a retractable shade however the side window and door were partially covered with sheer curtains. We had a hard time sleeping especially in the early morning when too much light came into the room. We asked to be moved but were told all the rooms were booked. It was disappointing that the room was also the same price as the others which were probably more spacious. Other than that, the staff was great, the owner lovely, the breakfast and snacks delicious and the inn was kept immaculate. Wouldn't hesitate to stay there again but would request not to be put in the River Green room. By the way, I told the owner it was our 45th anniversary when we booked months ago and she had a bottle of champagne on ice waiting for us with a congratulatory note. Also lovely music was playing in the room! Very thoughtful!

author: TravelWriterDB
title: Awesome suite - hated to leave
text: Even in winter, this large coastal home projects a feeling of comfort. Without even seeing the fireplace going, you know you’re about to be warmed and welcomed inside. As we walked up the steps and made our way inside, our feelings were confirmed. Innkeepers Erik & Sarah Lindblom have expertly restored the home, which exudes charm and character from its wonderful wallcoverings to its brilliant white woodwork. Just about every room has a touch of spring with cut flowers. We stayed in the Arundel room – quietly located at the end of a private hallway. We had seen pictures on their website before we arrived, but the brain was spinning trying to take in all that lay before us. Directly in front of us was a massive bed with uber-large comforter. Scanning starboard revealed the wonderfully done bath with warm-toned marble tiles, golden fixtures and corner shower. Turning to the port, a sitting area by a three-sided fireplace and an inviting whirlpool tub beckoned us. Within minutes, my wife had deposited her bags, grabbed her book and was curled up in one of the two large arm chairs. The chair and ottoman suited her perfectly. Wrapped in a blanket, with the fireplace glowing, I could tell it was going to take an act of Congress to get her out of that chair. I opted for the whirlpool tub and relaxed with a glass of wine. The world was at peace, at least in our small corner of it. If we hadn’t already had dinner reservations, we might both still be there.

author: DrMeg315
title: A Perfect Birthday Weekend
text: My husband booked us two nights at Captain Jefferds as a birthday surprise. I couldn't have had a more wonderful weekend!! From the moment we arrived, everyone was bending over backwards to ensure we had a wonderful time. There was champagne in our upgraded room, candles in my breakfast scone, so many cute little touches! No detail has been overlooked here. I am a converted tea drinker, and I adored the assortment of loose leaf teas to brew in my own little tea pot 24 hours a day. The mugs were even pre-warmed! My husband loved the coffee and espresso too. Breakfast was amazing! I am a fairly accomplished cook and baker, so I tend to be picky. The meals and treats at Captain Jefferds surpassed my expectations. Our room (Camden) was stunning! So elegantly decorated and comfortable! The sheets and linens were like nothing I've ever felt. I spent hours reading next to the fireplace and didn't even want to leave to see the area! In short, everything from the service to the food to the linens was top notch! The only downside to staying here is the rough adjustment to arriving home.

author: VeronaWater
title: Cozy winter get-away with outstanding attention to detail
text: We've stayed here twice, both for romantic get-aways. The first time, we were in one of the less expensive rooms, with low ceilings and a very small bathroom. This was fine at that time, since we were on more of a budget. For a little more money, we were far happier in one of the rooms in the main house, which is where were stayed during our more recent visit, in March 2014, and that's where we'd stay again in the future. The Camden Room was cozy, with tasteful decor, interesting furniture (possibly antique) a gas fireplace, soft towels, good linens, feather duvet, comfortable bathroom, and a real wood four poster bed. Although I would tend to prefer to eat my breakfast in private or more anonymously, as in a cafe, we did sit down with some of the other guests for the very tasty and fresh homemade breakfast. I appreciated that everyone was considerate and essentially kept to themselves, which meant that my fiance and I could have our own conversation without being distracted by others. This is a place for couples, or it was when we visited, and that meant that the whole atmosphere was restful and quiet. We slept well and felt we had a real getaway at a time of year when we needed some R&R, even if it was snowing outside. We felt we were extremely well looked after by the staff which seems to pay close attention to all of the small details. We also loved that a real fire was lit (and roaring) in one of the downstairs sitting rooms when we came back from dinner on our first night. We had the room to ourselves and enjoyed a taste of complimentary port on the comfortable couch by the flames. A nice touch. This is one of the nicest places we've ever stayed. Not many properties are this well kept, and well managed these days. So many are going to falter in some way, whether it's the taste of the decor, or the quality of the food, or the housekeeping. This Inn is spotless and it's clear that they aspire to the highest level of hospitality. The places is full of antiques and real art; a true New England inn and far more interesting than a hotel.

author: NancyG-818
title: Great Place to Recharge Your Batteries
text: We recently spent two wonderful nights at The Captain Jefferds Inn. The CJI is our "go-to" place when we need to get away and recharge our batteries. This time we went with friends who had also been there before. We love the staff there ... everyone is so warm and friendly and can't do enough for you. There were brownies, cookies and cheese & crackers waiting for us upon arrival. They also have coffee, tea and hot cider (the best!) We love sitting in the sun room and watching people come and go while we relax with our afternoon treats. This year we stay two nights so we could have one full day in the middle ... which we used to drive up to Freeport (L.L. Bean) Another favorite thing that we love about the Captain Jeffereds Inn is having breakfast with the other guests in the beautiful dining room. This time around, there were so many people staying at the Inn (full capacity is approximately 15 rooms). The first day we were able to snag seats at the main table (our favorite). The second day we ended up sitting at a table for 4 (still in the dining room, but not the same). The breakfasts are always so good ... whether it's the Warm Pears, or the piping hot Popovers, or the delicious homemade Quiche. The rooms at CJI range from $215 to $429, We usually get a "deal" ... the best deal of all is the half priced rooms if you make a $35 donation to Habitat For Humanity (a Spring time deal). Deal or no deal, the Captain Jefferds Inn is the place you want to go when you need a little get-away. We always return to the Real World charged up and ready to go! Alreayd making plans to go back again.

author: NJ-314
title: Captain Jefferds Inn – The Class of Kennebunkport
text: Among many features that separates the Captain Jefferds Inn from other Kennebunkport properties is the staff. They care about their guests – they are “connected” to the Inn. The Innkeepers – Sarah and Eric – set a relaxed atmosphere with a clear focus on extraordinary comfort and service. Breakfast is a great experience. It is the perfect start to a day in Kennebunkport and the southern Maine coast. The dining room is large and beautifully decorated – the food is outstanding (usually three courses). While the sun room and patio are comfortable and welcoming all through the day, it is a special treat to get an early cup of coffee (before breakfast) and sit back to enjoy the garden or check the morning newspapers. Each guest room is different and each is decorated beautifully. The bed linens and towels are soft and luxurious. The beds are large and comfortable. The Inn grounds and gardens are well tended and beautiful. It is a short walk to Dock Square and a quick ride to any of the beaches in the area. The Inn provides parking passes for the local beaches that require them. You simply cannot go wrong staying at the Captain Jefferds Inn. We have stayed at the Inn at least once a year since 2006 and will certainly return

author: runningonq
title: Very nice inn, great location
text: My wife and I stayed her in the 4th week of July; 3 nights. Overall this is a very good inn. Excellent location to dock square, close to a number of good and very good restaurants, 45 minutes to Portland and a little bit less to Portsmouth, NH. The staff was excellent, very helpful and accommodating. The inn itself is in good condition and very picturesque. The one complaint I do have is the air conditioning. 90% of the time AC will not be needed but when it is required, our window unit was horribly noisy. This is certainly not am economic inn and therefore the AC issue should be remedied. This is a great location to spend a couple of days sightseeing, spending time at one of the many local beaches, walking, bike riding, kayaking, etc. Our room was large, comfortable, clean, very nicely furnished. We stayed in the Adare room which has a large main room with king size bed, a large bath with tub and separate shower with a gas fireplace separating the bedroom and bath. The large bed was extremely comfortable. Breakfasts were fine; traditional New England breakfast. Overall great stay, would definitely go back in non-summer months. The load AC would be a deal breaker for me in summer months.

author: cpennnh
title: Wonderful Gardens and Pet Friendly Rooms
text: We happened upon this great B&B a few days ago when looking for a pet friendly room, and they were very accommodating on short notice. We were lucky to find one room left. It was in the carriage house portion, and it was large enough for three people (or two people and a pup in our case). The best selling feature of the Inn is the location. You are walking distance to everything and they have beautiful gardens that back up to a gorgeous public garden. This works out fantastically if you brought a dog because you will see other dogs playing there all day long. The owners of the Inn are extremely nice and even make sure the dog visitors are taken care of with special treats and a toy. They leave dog bowls and extra towels for them too! Their pet program is well thought out. The human features are great too! You can order glasses of wine to your room for a very reasonable small charge. My only suggestion is that we were not warned that our breakfast time, which was set for us, would lead us into the dining room to sit at one large table with 8 other people that we didn't know. We would have skipped breakfast had we known that (even though it was absolutely fabulous and delicious). No one seemed to be too keen about sitting with 4 other couples while being served. No one said a word! Most of the B&Bs we've stayed at have several cafe tables inside and out and you sit with your own party. If you are shy or on a romantic getaway, this eating situation will not suit. We felt that we should have at least been told how it was set up or given some sort of buffet option if we didn't want to join in. Not sure if it was because we arrived last minute or if they just don't tell you. Otherwise, I would have given it 5 stars.

author: AmyMcGowen
title: The Perfect place to stay in Kennebunkport!
text: For my first stop on my first trip to Maine, I chose the Captain Jefferds Inn and boy did I pick the perfect spot! The Innkeepers (and Rachel) are just so sweet and helpful!!! The room (The Arundel Room) was huge, gorgeous, well decorated, with an oversized jacuzzi tub, fireplace and lots of room. King size bed and mini fridge added to the luxury. The bed was so comfortable, the room was so quiet, and the view of the neighborhood was quaint. The location is perfect..... just one block from the port (and restaurants), and 3 blocks to town. If you want a pet friendly place, this is your spot, as they have rooms designated for pets in the Carriage House. If you are not a fan of pets, not to worry.... they are not allowed in the main house. (I didn't hear a peep out of the dogs staying there ). The Inn is immaculate! The 3 course breakfast was gourmet and delicious! .... simply perfect!! I will go back, for sure!!!! No place else to stay in this town!

author: 845donnag
title: A wonderful Bed Breakfast Inn
text: Myself, my husband and my son were there 2 nights. This was my husband and my first time in Kennebunkport. The whole staff was pleasant and accommodating. The rooms and grounds were clean and beautiful. Our was room was large, warm and pleasant with a large bathroom. One sitting room was a sunroom with coffee, tea and snacks was inviting and provided a nice social time. The larger sitting room was beautifully finished with sofas and paintings which was more for quiet time and reading. The breakfast was great in a beautiful dining room on a large dining room table that invited socialization with others in the Inn. I was running in the Maine seacoast marathon and had to follow a breakfast diet which they accommodated. They are very accommodating for people with dogs. They provided sheets, bowls and a treat for the dog which he loved. In fact they had a hose and provided towels for after the dog went swimming. Shops were within walking distance. The atmosphere was friendly and less business like. We loved our stay so much we booked another night in 2 weeks and are planning to go back next April and May as well.

author: George_P_NewYork
title: Adding my 'Excellent' review to the other 400
text: The Southern Maine Coast has plenty of charming destinations, and Kennebunkport is at the top, in my opinion. High-end without being stuffy, appealing to the tourist without being tacky, it's a beautiful place. Adjacent to the small shopping district is a lovely residential neighborhood, where inn after quaint inn is located. And it's there where Captain Jefferds stands out, possibly for its sheer size. It's big. It also has lots of curb appeal. Sarah and the staff greeted us and gave us a quick tour; it didn't take long for me to see that, just like the town itself, the Inn is beautiful, manicured and comfortable. The room in which we stayed was great... huge for two people, with a gas fireplace that warmed things up in a hurry. I think it's a bit of a balancing act when it comes to decorating B&B guest rooms: convey the local flavor, the personality of the house, or both; in a way that isn't knick-knack-y or overdone. Captain Jefferds succeeds here. Cozy doesn't begin to describe the bed experience, which envelops the slumberer in an extraordinary pillow-top experience. I happen to be more of a firm mattress kind of guy, but I did get a good night's sleep. Breakfast was innovative and tasty; and the service was very attentive. We chatted briefly with Sarah as we left; she is well-suited for this business, as she was very engaging and welcoming. I can't imagine that there's a reason to stay anywhere else in town.

author: robyno350
title: Absolutely wonderful
text: Our much needed, romantic getaway weekend to Kennebunkport started with arriving at another inn, which we had booked months in advance, only to be told they mixed up our dates and booked us for a month later. Fortunately for us, that inn was full and sent us to the Captain Jefferds Inn. I am so thankful that a mistake brought us to The Captain Jefferds. I cannot say enough good things about our stay there. Upon arrival, it was late, and we were tired, hungry, and frustrated. From the minute we stepped through the doors, the staff (and other guests) went out of their way to make us feel welcome and comfortable (Thank You Amily and Ann-Marie). We stayed in the Baxter room our first night and moved to the Chatham room our second night because the Baxter was already booked. Sarah took the time to sit and chat with us and ensure we were properly welcomed and Eric took us on a tour after most of the other guests had checked out on Sunday. All of the rooms are lovely to say the very least. I'd be happy staying in any of them. The house is absolutely beautiful and there has been incredible attention to detail in its renovation and maintenance. The snacks and coffee/tea/cider in the sunroom were a great touch. The breakfasts were wonderful--we were included in their family-style breakfast even even after showing up at the last minute. Sarah, Eric, and all of the staff were extremely friendly and helpful, and truly made us feel like part of the family. We are eager to return, and are also planning to book a weekend there for my parents as a birthday getaway.

author: NancyG-818
title: Relaxing, Friendly and Fun ...
text: That is how I would describe each and every visit to Captain Jefferds Inn. I've been there with my husband several times over the years, and we've introduced friends to CJI who also have gone back. Just recently, however, I was at Captain Jefferds Inn for a weekend get-away with my four sisters. Some of us had been there before, some had not ... and for those who had not been before, they agreed that would not be their last visit. Sarah and Erik are friendly, warm and welcoming. The Inn is immaculate. I've stayed in many of the differently decorated rooms, all are great. The breakfasts are to-die-for good. We enjoy sitting and talking with the other guests before heading out for the day. Later on the in the afternoon, it is fun to return to the "sun room" for tea, coffee, hot apple cider and homemade cookies ... and find out how everyone's day went. The Inn is located just a short (convenient) walk to the downtown area. We did a little shopping, had some great light bite dinner within walking distance, and even spent one afternoon at a spa just down the road (yes, we did walk in spite of some pretty brisk winds!) I have been to Captain Jefferds all four seasons now, and I honestly think each and every one has its own charm. This most recent visit, we met people who have been driving up from Virginia every year for the last 15 years ... what does that tell you?! I think it speaks volumes. :D

author: thedavidperez
title: Very Nice Stay
text: My wife and I visited for one night recently. Everything about our experience was perfect. The booking process was easy. Check-in was smooth. The house itself has lots of character and is in great shape. Makes for a very romantic setting. The rooms were nice and spacious. Our bathroom was ok, but we were explained going in that the bigger room had a less nice bathroom. Lots of very nice small details all over the room even under the bed! The breakfast was included and very good. I really enjoyed the cider in the afternoon. The location was perfect as it was walking distance to town. The owner and her staff were very friendly. Price was fair. Really enjoyed the place!

author: montyj1138
title: Home Away from Home in Kennebunkport
text: As we drove up to Captain Jefferds, I immediately felt confident that we had booked the right place. The beautifully manicured lawn, outdoor patios surrounded by flower gardens made my husband and I feel like we were at a special retreat. The manager greeted us by name as we walked in the door for the first time, and made us feel at home. The rooms are just as they are shown online, if not better, and very clean. The sheets are incredibly soft. Each morning they provide a delicious, homemade, and very creative 3-course meal. My favorite meal was the apricot stuffed french toast and sweet and spicy bacon. They also provide bottled water, sodas, and snacks, which was an added bonus as we were coming and going throughout the day. One of my favorite experiences of the stay was taking 2 of the available Captain Jeffers bikes down to Mother's beach for the afternoon. The staff packed us towels in a backpack so it made traveling easy, and we didn't have to deal with parking. But if you prefer to drive to the local beaches, they will provide you with passes that cover the cost of parking. Oh! And don't leave kennebunkport without trying Rococo ice cream at the end of Spring Street downtown... we went there every evening to see what new flavors they had created thanks to a recommendation by one of the other guests. Captain Jefferds made our time in Kennebunkport much more special than if we had stayed anywhere else. I am already looking forward to when we can return again.

author: jmarsha9
title: All around excellence
text: My wife and I stayed at the Captain Jefferd's recently for a long weekend. We were able to bring our Shih-tzu, Shelby because the Capt. Jefferd's is one of the few B&B's in the area that allows dogs. We stayed in the Hideaway which is tucked back behind the main house, accessible by its own private staircase. The door to the room is about 5 feet tall which was funny, as I am 6'3". The room was comfortable, clean, and small. It lacked TV which was nice. The staff had a little pet package prepared when we arrived which included doggy dishes, a towel, a throw to put at the foot of the bed (where Shelby happens to sleep), a tennis ball, and a homemade dog treat shaped like a moose with her name in icing on it. Nice touch. Breakfast was served in three courses each morning and was delicious every day. All the other guests we talked to at breakfasts were repeat visitors to the Capt. Jefferds, making it a point every year to come back. The B&B has been beautifully restored. The sitting area had very comfortable sofas and a fire to relax by in the evenings. The location was perfect as it was only a few blocks to downtown, shopping, and dining. We will definitely make it a point to visit again next year!

author: DrDANT
title: Not worth the exorbitant prices
text: Captain Jefferds Inn sits in a quiet and charming neighborhood in Kennebunkport. The main inn is very charming, breakfasts are good (a bit over the top for some reason), the staff friendly and the place clean. We booked the Baxter "carriage house" because we had our dog--it was rather expensive (close to 400 a night) and the pet fee high. But the pictures and innkeeper description assured us it was very large and roomy and luxury. It was anything but. First, what they DIDNT mention was that we were right below another room--and the people had 2 big dogs. So we heard the thumping, walking, creaking, and all the bathroom sounds (UGHHHH) above us for both nights and both mornings. Asking the asst. innkeeper to mention there were people below did not help--the place is very old and very creaky and the noise woke us up many times. It was unplesant. In addition, the room was not luxury-the toilet seat was cheap plastic and came loose, the shower fixture was loose and leaking, and overall, the room was small and the bathroom tiny. Theres a huge soaking tub right in the room--rather odd. The TV cables all came loose, and we had to figure out how to put them back so it would work. Overall, for the price, the room was very substandard and certainly not a "luxury room", as advertised. I estimate the room should have gone more for 200 a night to match what we got and we felt the innkeeper should have let us know it was right below others and the floors noisy. I asked other guests about their rooms--many liked theirs, but I did hear some complaints from other guests. We would not return.

author: JTFV
title: A Great Stay
text: Nothing new to report here other than to say we had a great experience at the Captain Jefferds Inn. When I called to make the reservation, the only room available was the "Hideaway" room. They warned me it was a tiny room with a tiny bathroom. I booked anyway and took my chances. Yes, the room was small, but it was as neat as a pin. If traveling with kids, this room would be perfect for them. (Not sure if they allow kids...) I dropped a vitamin and crouched down to find it and noticed that there wasn't a speck of dust anywhere either under the bed or under the dresser. Unusual in an old house. There are a few rooms that have their own screened porches, so if you enjoy a morning or evening with some seclusion, I'd recommend asking about those rooms. They also had well maintained bikes that we took out for a few hours. There is a 7 mile ride that takes you out along the water and loops you back into town in a hour and a half. Always a great way to see a town. Breakfast is served at a large table with half the guests at one seating and the other half an hour later. If you prefer to eat early you may want to tell them that when you book as it seemed the early seating filled up first, but that may just have been the crowd's preference while I was there. My only constructive criticism would be that breakfast was very sweet. Fruit with sweetened cream or yogurt, pancakes, scones, et cetera. I'm more of a savory breakfast eater. That being said, I never requested anything else, so in all fairness I'm sure they would have made accommodations for me had I asked. Overall a very good experience. Would definitely stay here again.

author: MEKMOM
title: Wonderful Weekend!
text: We have stayed at many inns and this is one of the most delightful we've ever enjoyed! These are some of the many amenities that have been thoughtfully provided, many varieties of coffee & tea available all day, cookies, water bottles, soda, afternoon snacks, umbrellas, bikes, sherry, newspapers and in each room fresh flowers, wine glasses, a cork screw and mint candies. We stayed in the Assisi room. It is on the 3rd floor, with many stairs to reach it but it is a huge room, with a king bed, love seat and chair, fireplace and a small section of the room that was made into an indoor garden. The bathroom has a double headed shower and it also quite large for an inn. The 3-4 course breakfasts were excellent without being too much. The owners and staff were all very friendly and helpful. They even had a camera charger they let me borrow when my battery went dead.The inn is a very short walk to the town, shops and restaurants. My only advice is ask if the fireplace isn't working since they don't light the pilot if they haven't taken the air conditioners out (which they do when they consider it too cold to use them) even if the nights are cool. They gladly did this when we asked. Also there is a large window in the garden area of the room which has no shade or curtain of any kind on it and the sun shines in that window in the early morning. If this would bother you beware before you book it, ask if anything can be done or bring your own sheet or blanket to cover it. We took the curtain off another window, that also had a shade, and rigged it to cover the window. I had mentioned my concern to the gentleman that showed us to our room and he didn't seem interested in trying to change it so we just dealt with it ourselves. Overall we truly enjoyed this inn and would recommend it without hesitation!

author: Juliana_John
title: A truely special place
text: I have so many wonderful things to say about this Inn. We booked our trip just a couple days beforehand and they were so accommodating! We were worried about finding a place right after July 4th but were thrilled to find this little, quaint inn was still available. From the start we received wonderful service, a tour of the inn, our bags quickly brought to our room. The first two nights we stayed in the Florida room, perfectly clean and just the right size. The room wasn't available for the 3rd night so Sarah kindly upgraded us to a room well outside our price range! The afternoon cookies and tea were wonderful, not to mention the lovely 3 course breakfast every morning! You may choose to eat at either 8:15 or 9:30. Every bite was to die for. They have 4 bikes available so you may ride around town. In addition they have chairs, towels, sunblock, etc for you to borrow. The inn was also great at offering dinner recommendations. The grounds were well maintained with flowers galore. It is in the perfect location, just a few blocks from downtown Kennebunkport. On the Saturday during our stay they had a craft fair going on right behind the inn which was a fun surprise. I am already dreaming of our vacation back to Captin Jefferds Inn and we haven't even made it home yet!

author: diablonyc2
title: Another great stay at CJI
text: We originally stayed at CJI in December for the Xmas Prelude and had such a wonderful time; we decided to spend our anniversary there this past week. Once again, our expectations were exceeded! Prior to booking, we spoke with Steve (an assistant inn-keeper) who assisted me in identifying great places to have dinner. He also helped with check-in arrangements since we had a last minute change and arrived late at night. We chose the Baxter room (again) and just love the way it is decorated, from the fire place to the painting on the wall over the Jacuzzi. On arrival, our dog in the darkness remembered his way back to the room and beat us there. He feasted on the personalized treat and played with the little tennis ball. They also surprised us with a nice bottle of sparkling wine and chocolate for our anniversary! Perfect after a LONG drive. At CJI, you can expect a fantastic breakfast. While on vacation, I love to sleep late....but not when in Maine. Each breakfast is a work of art! From baked grapefruit to spinach Florentine, you cannot go wrong. CJI is located walking distance from the town. For us it is perfect as the Baxter room door is located by a park ground where my dog loves to walk in the early morning, and then head into town to check out the stores and any interesting trees or fire hydrants.
