Bottom line, to be able to stay at a high quality bed and breakfast with your pet is a wonderful treat for us (In addition, you would never know other pets have stayed in the room...A+++ for cleaning). Plus its location is perfect for people who like to relax by the water (via walking or biking) and enjoy fine dining. If planning on traveling to Kennebunkport, check out the CJI. We have tried a few others in the past, but now are hooked on this place!

author: ACG_MA
title: STAY AT THE CAPTAIN JEFFERDS - YOU WILL LOVE IT!!
text: My husband and I have traveled to Kennebunkport for a stay at the Captain Jefferds Inn annually for the past 6 years - we have loved EVERY visit! Generally we travel there in the winter months for a get-together with friends. The Capt Jefferds in the perfect setting for this mini college reunion for so many reasons. They have a wide variety of rooms featuring luxury amenities. There is a lovely 4 season porch that is perfect for gathering for coffee/tea, or a glass of wine. The main living room is a great place for a group to gather to discuss each day/night's agenda. The staff there could NOT be more wonderful - they are friendly, accommodating and personable. Breakfasts are always an amazing 3-course event with both sweet and savory elements - something for everyone! We also stayed at the Capt Jefferds for a spring-time wedding and intend to do the same this coming labor day weekend. We've loved our time at the Capt Jefferds so much that we've given my parents gift cards to go and visit, as well over the years. My parents have so enjoyed their time there that they have, in turn started giving gift cards for stays at the Inn to other family members and friends! It is so accessible from Boston! Finally, I'd like to add that the Innkeepers, Erik and Sarah have done a beautiful job updating many of the rooms since assuming ownership! We will continue to go back for years to come!! (I have literally never written a review for Trip Advisor before, but feel so strongly about the wonderful experiences that I've had at the Capt Jefferds that I simply had to share!)

author: BeantownGirlMA
title: Great Anniversary Weekend
text: We stayed at the Captain Jefferds Inn in Kennebunkport for our anniversary. We were in the Wyeth room, which has a king sized bed, fireplace and remodeled bathroom. The room was very nicely appointed. The fireplace was fantastic -- we lit a fire each night and it was so nice to sit in the comfortable chairs in the room, drink wine and read. I can't rave enough about the sheets that they had on the bed -- they were so comfortable that we actually bought a set when we got home! The newly remodeled bathroom was quite nice -- great water pressure in the multi-head shower. The bedroom windows also had wooden shutters, which kept out the light in the morning -- much appreciated. The breakfasts are amazing and the staff is very accommodating of food allergies. There are two seatings for breakfast. We spent each morning chatting with the other guests, which was fun. There is a pantry that is accessible 24/7 with sodas, waters, etc. The staff also puts out mulled cider, hot chocolate, coffee and cookies in the afternoons. There is a fire lit in the fireplace in the living room all of the time and a basket of menus for all of the local restaurants. It's the little details that made our stay so enjoyable. The location is great -- it's about a 10 minute walk into town. There was plenty of parking at the inn, even when they were fully booked. The only drawback is the lack of (noise) privacy. The inn is a beautiful historic building, but every night, we could hear other people's conversations, drawers opening and closing, footsteps from the rooms above and flushing of toilets in other rooms. It's a bit unnerving to realize that you have so little privacy. Not sure how (or if) that can be fixed, but it was the only drawback of the whole weekend.

author: diablonyc2
title: Cannot believe I have never stayed here before! (that's about to change)
text: We just returned from a wonderful weekend/partial week at the Captain Jefferds Inn. I have stayed in Kennebunkport, ME before and was extremely impressed at the level of service we received at the Inn. For the first time, we traveled with our dog. They made this as pain free as possible. Of course there are rules which are to be expected (as the rooms look untouched by canine teeth), but they go out of their way to make man's best friend as welcome as possible! He LOVED the cookie that awaited him at arrival! From the staff, to the owners...they are all pet lovers! This has opened my eyes to a new way of traveling! Our stay was in the Baxter room...which is simply amazing. It has a rustic/cabin feel (which is different from the overall feel of the house). The fireplace, furnishing, whirlpool tub....all magnificent. As for the breakfast......wow! I am ready to drive 5 hours back for the eggs florentine alone! Eric did an outstandning job each day. Pros: - Location: large grounds for dogs to run (on leash), steps from town - Food: amazing...and I originally went just for lobster - Room: sheets that were amazing and just a great place to relax - House: wonderfully maintained and decorated for Xmas - Staff: Bradon/Steve and the rest were outstanding. Helped with dinner choices, where to travel to w the dog, and Brandon even got a chance to play with the pup (who loved him). Cons: - Cannot think of any at the time except that I can't visit more often. If you are traveling and looking for a high-end B&B that accepts and loves pets, give them a try. It is a great town to visit in the summer and winter (expecially if you like peace and quiet in the winter).

author: LadybugNH
title: Terrible Customer Service!
text: Twice we received very, very poor customer service...The first time was last December 2010. We saw the rooms all have a DVD player online. When we got to the Inn there was no player in the room so we asked for one. We were there for a "Girl's Christmas Weekend" and we traditionally every year all watch the Polar Express movie while we open gifts at an Inn. The innkeeper's assistant told us that was not possible and we would have to watch it in the family room downstairs. So that was ruined. I was not going to bring my guests and all the gifts down there where all the other guests were. So I made a complaint to the Innkeepers and they gave us a discount off a room to try them again at another time. So I booked a room this year for November 5th, 2011 to stay again, with my Mother, who cannot climb stairs. I was called by the Innkeeper three days before my arrival only to be told the room we requested (the only room on the first floor level) was now occupied by a family member who lost power and we would have to reschedule for another weekend. They offered us another room upstairs which will not work if my Mother cannot climb stairs and they knew that. I thanked them for ruining my weekend a second time. I told the innkeepers I will never stay at their inn ever again. My 80 year old Mother was heart broken to find out we were not going to this Inn this weekend. This was very cruel of the innkeepers. Then they have the nerve to call me and tell me they moved the family member to another place. If they were able to do that in the first palce why did they call and ruin our weekend?? These Innkeeper's should not be in the hospitality business at all. They do not care about their guests!

author: DanielGiannavola
title: We absolutely loved it and we'll come back again and again!
text: This was the first trip to Maine for my wife and I. As a kid I watched President George Bush and Barbara vacation to Kennebunkport, Maine. It's always been my dream to go there. My dream came true and it was more beautiful than I could've ever imagined. The Captain Jefferd's Inn is so quaint and beautiful. If you've ever dreamed of going to Maine and staying in a historical Bed and Breakfast, this is the place! The Bed and Breakfast is like taking a trip back to the 18th Century, yet, with modern conveniences. The rooms are so quaint with attention to detail. The staff is so courteous and absolutely charming. And they all welcomed our little mini-daschund, Abby, to stay with us! When we entered the room, there was a little doggie welcome basket to include a personally made doggie cookie with her name on it! That's not only awesome, but made us feel that she was truly welcomed. The grounds are so gorgeous and there are so many beautiful homes right around the block. You can walk to the shops of Kennebunkport and the area is heaven if you like to antique. The morning breakfast was also wonderful and in the afternoons, there is tea, coffee, Vermont Cheeses, Cookies, and other homemade snacks! This is the place! Thanks for a great vacation Captain Jefferds Inn.

author: averycak
title: Captain Jefferds Inn, our home away from home!
text: We absolutely love Captain Jefferds Inn! We have stayed there many times often staying in the Baxter Room, which offers its own private screened in porch with views of the water. We could come and go without disturbing any other guests because of its private entrance. The room has a spa tub with river rock stonework, and a hand painted mural on the wall, that gives the impression of a relaxing ride down a Maine river. Even the faucet was like a little waterfall. It’s so relaxing after a day of walking around Kennebunkport. The elegance of the dining room, the great food, and meeting new people is a plus. We got to hear some interesting stories, and make new friends. We have never walked away from the table unsatisfied or disappointed. The innkeepers are very gracious, and we are always made to feel right at home. We will sometimes stay in one, or another, of the other rooms, since there is a room for every taste, and style. We love the rustic cabin feel of the Baxter room, making it feel like a lodge on Moosehead Lake, but with all the amenities. Anyone could choose one more formal if they wanted to. We only wish we could have stayed longer. Thank you so much Erik and Sarah, for the lovely stay, yet again. We can't wait to come back this month! Sincerely, Cheryl and Allen K.

author: skush2
title: The Best Medicine Money Can Buy!
text: We both have really busy work schedules and hadn't taken a "real" vacation in six years. Although the photos of the Captain Jefferds Inn that were on the net were lovely, they did not do the inn justice. It was far more beautiful than we expected. The grounds are meticulous, the decoration is warm and inviting and the rooms are more comfortable than a five star hotel. The beds are plush and cradle you with their pouffy featherbeds and egyptian cotton sheets. The bathrooms are stocked with your every need right down to the soft and thick towels, the perfumed wildflower soap and the "his" and "hers" robes. The innkeepers leave no stone unturned, right down to the sewing kit and scissors tucked away in a drawer in the desk and the tiny nibbles of fudge bagged and tied ever so carefully and left on the bed stand. They are always available and there to serve your every need. Breakfast is formal in its setting and menu but laid back in that you eat at a long table with all of the other guests. The food is wonderful and tasty. Everything is home made and every morsel melts in your mouth. DId I mention that the inn is immaculate ....and I have very high standards. I looked for dust in hidden places that even I rarely get to in my own home...and guess what, I couldn't find one dust bunny. I could go on but if I did you would know everything and might not visit. There are still many surprises that await you at the Captain Jefferds Inn. I can't wait to go back...three days just wasn't enough!

author: terryan
title: Beyond all our expectations
text: My husband and I only stayed one night, but wished we had spent our whole vacation here! We toured the coast of Maine, ending in Kennebunkport. A perfect ending, but we hated to leave the Captain Jefferd's Inn. The inn is beautiful, lovely authentic furnishings, lovingly tended gardens with lush flowers and water flowing, large, expansive green lawns with chairs and benches, even a furnished patio with umbrellas to enjoy a glass of wine in the evening. We stayed in the Vermont Suite and had a very large suite, with a huge bathroom with soaking tub and a shower, a high queen bed with feather bed, sitting room with tv and a twin day bed, all with a huge screened in porch with chairs for enjoying the evening. We were welcomed with fresh lemonade and an always full cookie jar, bottled water and sodas, all complimentary. Our room was already air conditioned as it was very hot out, but we did not really need it due to the wonderful breeze off the water. The inn was just a block from the water and a lovely restaurant, the Arundel Wharf. We parked our car and walked everywhere, which is a great bonus as Kennebunkport streets are jammed with cars midday. Our breakfast was served promptly and we enjoyed the company of the other guests in the lovely formal dining room. One plus was that the internet was fast and a good connection, especially for an old house! This was our favorite stay on our trip, and we can't wait to go back for a color tour in the fall. We consider ourselves somewhat picky travellers, but the Captain Jefferds exceeded all our expectations, even providing a special breakfast to accomodate my husband's food allergies. We cannot find a single thing to criticize! Thank you for a great stay and see you soon!

author: ceyda79
title: A mini getaway with our 4 mos old
text: I really needed a break before heading back to work post maternity leave and heard great things about CGI so we decided to give it a try. Our 4 mos old is very well tempered but being first time parents we figured that we'd test it out with a one night stay. We arrived early and asked for early check-in and were told that they would do the best they could to clean up from the guests prior. Normal check-in is 3pm and they were able to get us in at 1pm which was fantastic, not to mention great for the baby. The lady was extremely accodomating which was greatly appreciated. The Inn was cozy and our room was clean. The location was fantastic, within walking distance to some great restaurants and shops. It allowed us to go back and forth for our child's naps during the day. That evening we slept well except the walls are quite thin so we were able to hear everything that occured in the room next door. The next morning the Inn guests greeted us with smiles wanting to interact with our child. We came in with our stroller and were slightly dissapointed at the way we were told to move it. We expected a smile and a nice request to move it to the next room however instead we were told that it needed to move with zero smiles. This was a bit hurtful because she was being very good and we felt at that point that maybe CGI isn't that kid friendly after all. I immediately noticed that the Inn guests felt our discomfort but we proceeded with breakfast anyway. Other than that I would say that this is the perfect little place for a NE getaway. I would recommend it for couples.

author: robbyjh
title: Fantastic and wonderful place to relax and enjoy eastern seaside
text: The owners truly want their guests to relax and enjoy. The breakfasts were incredible. Everyone went out of their way to meet our needs and wants. They are very knowledgeable about the area and did not steer us wrong at any point. Our room was on the third floor. It had a skylight that opened and let the fresh sea air flow into the room. It was spacious and comfortable with a king sized bed, a love seat, a couple of comfortable reading chairs, a separate bath, a large closet for clothes, etc. We truly enjoyed the sunroom and the patio. Fresh coffee and juice was available each morning before the wonderful breakfasts. There were 2 seatings for breakfast ( when enough guests were there). We took the later one and enjoyed our lazy mornings. The inn is a couple of blocks from the unique and fun shops that line the main street in town. There were 4 or 5 very nice resturants within walking distance also. You can do as much or as little as you want. There is no pressure to anything --- it was wonderful!!!! We have been on multiple luxury cruises and beetn to a couple of all inclusive resorts. The inn surpassed any of those experiences. This is one place a person should try to get to. We had a ball.

author: MRT2KB
title: Nice Stay
text: My husband and I chose to stay at Captain Jefferd's Inn on Saturday, June 27 for our 12th wedding anniversary. We stayed in the Monticello room. The room was nice, spacious, and very clean. We arrived later than we had expected and had dinner reservations for 6:00 p.m at Grissini's. Steve, who was the Inn's host for the evening, checked us in promptly, gave us a little tour, and took our bag to our room. He was very friendly and personable. When we returned after dinner, we were looking to purchase a bottle of wine or champagne to take back to our room for the night. Since it was our anniversary, Steve was very generous and gave us a bottle, rather than have us purchase one. We were very grateful. We had a working gas fireplace in our room, so it was nice to sit by the fire and enjoy our champagne. The Inn was very quiet during the night, as opposed to the noise you hear outside your room at a hotel. Breakfast the next morning was very good and is included in your stay. They also offer complimentary beverages, homemade cookies and light snacks in the afternoon into the evening, and they also have a refrigerator with complimentary bottled water, juice, and soda in the pantry, as well. The only complaint that I had were the pillows on the bed. It's not the Inn's fault. I like a firm pillow and their pillows were very thin and flimsy. I probably could have asked for a different pillow, but it was late when we went to bed and I did not want to disturb anyone. The location is a short walk to all the shops in Dock Square, as well as the restaurants, boat cruises, etc. We would highly recommend this B&B.

author: ThatWouldBeMeSc_Usa
title: July 2008 - Excellent Hospitality
text: Room was clean and fresh. Staff was courteous and warm. They welcomed us like old friends and anticipated arrivals! The only problem we had the entire 3 days was that we asked that our air conditioner unit be left on while we were out so that when we returned from shopping, etc., our room would be cool. It was turned off when we returned. Other than this small oversight, which was easily remedied, we couldn't be more pleased with our stay. The owners are very friendly and eager to please. We mentioned we were from the south, so they made a special effort to cook us grits for breakfast! That's going the extra mile, since they don't serve them on their menu. The inn is quite lovely and the gardens beautiful. Well-kept lawns and everything was in bloom! Shopping and restaurants close enough to walk even for the four of us slightly out-of-shape types. I've never slept in a more comfortable bed in my life (the Manhattan Room). We were very satisfied with our accommodations and will visit again soon! Thank you for a lovely getaway weekend!

author: TubbyTankers
title: Adorable B&B, Good Price, Good Location
text: Captain Jeffers Inn provides comfortable rooms, great location, great service and great food all at an affordable price. There are about 10 rooms done in traditional American style. They are spacious and clean,with even a sign under the beds saying "yes, we do clean under the beds too." The beds are very comfortable and feature 650 count sheets and fluffy pillows. We stayed in the Terrace room, and were very happy. There remainder of the B&B was clean and neat. This adorable B&B is located just off the Kennebunkport downtown area. You are within walking distance of Kennebunkport and Kennbunk shops and restaurants and Walker's Point (the Bush estate). There are also several spas located near by too. There is a side walk in front of the B&B that takes you to Walker's point (1 1/2 mile) and the shops. The staff was very friendly, but reserved as to not annoy anyone. Free water, diet cokes, coffee, tea and regular coke were provided. They also provided recommendations on where to eat and shop. The breaksfast was INSANELY good. Each breakfast was three courses including coffee, juice, or tea. The first course was fruit or oatmeal followed by a muffin, danish, or other bread item. The last course was usually a meat served with an egg based dish. I consider this B&B a great deal for the quality service, food, and rooms. The only possible down side (as with all B&Bs) is that you are staying in an almost 200 year old house. There are some creaks, the walls maybe a little thin, and a slight "old" house smell, but nothing you wouldn't expect with an old New England B&B.

author: Goldie_Mack
title: Outstanding B&B
text: My wife and I were looking to celebrate our wedding anniversary someplace special that was still relatively close to our home in MA. We like Kennebunkport and decided that a B&B there would be a great way to go - since we started visiting in 2001 we've stayed at several well-regarded B&Bs in the area (Cape Arundel Inn, Captain Fairfield Inn, etc) but based on our recent stay, the Captain Jefferds Inn is now our favorite. It exceeded our expectations in every way. Upon check-in, we found a bottle of chilled champagne and a handwritten note for our anniversary, and the happiness of that initial moment typified our two night stay. We stayed in the Monticello room, a spacious room at the corner of the second floor nearest the main entrance. As you can see from the photos, the room had a Thomas Jefferson theme, tasteful classic decor, and plenty of natural light. The bed and chairs were very comfortable, and the bathroom was nicely appointed. The staff were courteous and the breakfasts during our stay were delicious. The grounds of the B&B are pretty and abut an open green space (not sure if the B&B owns this or if it's a small park) which makes for a pleasant stroll around the property. All of the unoccupied rooms were open for inspection as part of an art event/inn tour in which the Captain Jefferds was participating, so we looked around in several of the other rooms. While I think the website gives an accurate depiction of the rooms, I actually thought the rooms were even more attractive in person than on the web site. Overall, we were delighted with the Captain Jefferds Inn. Beyond the Inn, we took side trips during our stay to Cape Porpoise (the Inn provided us a sticker for Goose Rocks Beach at no additional charge) as well as up to Portland (about 30 min drive). We dined at the White Barn Inn (exquisite!) and Grissini. To summarize our impressions: -Spacious, clean rooms, nicely decorated in an attractive, well-maintained inn -Excellent proximity to Dock Square (<5min walk) -Walkable to ocean front (~20 min walk) -Excellent service and attention to detail When we return to Kennebunkport, we will stay at the Captain Jefferds Inn.

author: chessiesailor
title: Beautiful Inn, Great Experience
text: We were warmly greeted by Sarah and part-time resident inn dog, Emily (?) and from our initial meeting we felt right at home. It was very clear from our two night stay that the innkeepers and staff pay close attention to the details. Our room was spotless and had many warm touches. As we were the first to arrive for the day, and at our request, were afforded a quick tour of the entire Inn. We would have been comfortable in any room we visited but very much liked our Monticello room with fireplace and queen bed that put me to sleep the second my head hit the pillow (thanks in part to the satin soft sheets and pillow cases). As our stay occured early in the season, the quaint town of Kennebunkport was very quiet but still very open and welcoming. The business district is a short couple of blocks away with several options for dinner. Our favorite was Bandaloops. We very much appreciated the absolute quiet respite provided by the Inn and this location though would also like to come back in high season to experience the area in a new way. The breakfasts were fabulous. Erik obviously works very hard to prepare meals that are special and unique. The service both at breakfast and throughout the day was just amazing. Again, lots of small details that add up to a great experience. Sarah and Erik provided just enough interaction to make you feel you are in a special place without being overbearing. We felt that we were in a very special place but not intruding on someones personal space. Hope those who are considering B&B options understand that unique ability of these innkeepers. If we are ever back in the southern coast region of Maine we will definitely plan to stay at the Captain Jefferds Inn. In fact, we may plan to explore the coast of Maine again because of the Captain Jefferds Inn. Great Inn. Great stay.

author: omaopatravellers
title: We ALWAYS stay here!
text: About 10 years ago, we discovered Kennebunkport as a destination. We have stayed in many of the bed and breakfasts and hotels in the area and enjoyed most of them. However, four years ago, we stayed at the Captain Jefferds Inn and fell in love. We try to never go anywhere else. Over the years, we have stayed in several of the rooms and all have been immaculate and comfortable. The ammenities of the inn from the wonderful and varied breakfasts to the afternon tea complete with homemade cookies and delicious cheese/crackers provide quiet respite to our hurried world. Recently, innkeepers Eric and Sara have also set out wine in the evening for our enjoyment. (And enjoy we did!) We especially like the sun room in which one can read several newspapers provided, talk with other guests, or just watch the birds fliting about outside the many windows. Our hosts obviously love what they do. They strive to make each of their guests feel as if they are home. They provide accurate information of local eating establishments or the areas nearby attractions. This past visit, Eric told us of a wonderful way to walk to the beach in Wells. We stomped through pathways of snow in a beautiful reserve until we arrived at the beach and it made out day! Summer, winter, fall or spring, this is where we want to end up when we getaway. However, we live in Houston, Texas so we have to plan our visits. We regularly save our money to spend at this wonderful retreat. Thank you Eric and Sara for making a trip to the Captain Jefferds Inn so wonderful!

author: diver1
title: A Perfect Week-end
text: My husband and I just spent a perfectly serene week-end at the Captain Jefferds Inn. The inn's attention to detail was superb. Highlights include the soft classical music playing in our room as we entered, the chocolates by our bed and the fresh cut flowers in the sitting room. Breakfast was perfect. The setting, complete with flowers and candles, was beautiful. During the first day, we were served fresh fruit, pound cake and blueberry stuffed pancakes. During the second day, we were served brandied bread pudding, muffins and a fritatta. All of this was homemade, all accompanied by fresh squeezed orange juice and fresh delicious coffee. Another highlight was the homemade cranberry oatmeal cookies the innkeepers served with afternoon tea. The Captain Jefferds is a short stroll away from Dock Square, the heart of Kennebunkport. It is a very short drive away from beaches and Walker Point, the site of the George Bush estate. I cannot say enough positive things about the inn. My husband and I will definitely be back. (Also, the best lobster in town is at Nunan's Lobster Hut in Cape Porpoise. They only take cash and checks. They are only open for dinner - after 5 pm.) Enjoy Kennebunkport!

author: VAChuck
title: A real gem of a place to stay and dog friendly
text: The Captain Jefferds Inn is a real fine. The guest rooms, common areas in the main mansion, and the grounds are meticulously maintained. We stayed in the Brandywine room. The room was spotless and spacious. The furnishings were elegant and yet comfortable. There is a very comfortable king size bed. The bathroom was very large and well laid out. We had our two Bichons with us and we were delighted at the special treatment they received. There was a nice doggie welcome sack in the room upon our arrival. Our dogs were permitted to sit under the elegant dining room table during our morning breakfasts. The Inn's owner is a retired vet and he was able to recommend a very capable vet when one of our dogs had an ear problem. The rooms of the inn are very elegantly appointed. Each of these has comfortable areas for reading or just enjoying the paper with morning coffee. Breakfast is served in two sittings. The first one tends to be in the dining room and the second is outside if the weather permits. We enjoyed this place immensely and hope to stay at the Inn again.

author: luvubecks
title: Silver Wedding Anniversary
text: We received a voucher from daughter for a stay for our silver wedding anniversary. We got engaged in the hotel 28 years ago. We were looking forward to going back. Reception was clean and modern receptionist was lovely checked us giving us an upgraded room. Room was a good size bathroom also a good size. Stunning sea view as well. Downside to room was very noisy heating system which we ended up switching off to try get some sleep also large bed was 2 singles pushed together wasn’t very comfortable. Also shower wasn’t great no water pressure made it very difficult to rinse hair after washing. Our dinner was from a set menu I had soup to start which came with normal brown sliced bread. Husband had the bruschetta. For main I had ribeye of beef and he had black pudding and haggis olives. Desert was apple crumble and bannoffee gatueux. Drinks were ok it’s not the best looking French Martini. The young lad who served us was very pleasant. Breakfast was a bit all over the place limited options of continental and tea and coffee out a pump flask is not what I would expect from a hotel like this. Cooked options were ordered from very young waitress who was wearing nail varnish. I had poached eggs which were overdone and husband was looking forward to his full cooked breakfast but is still waiting on his fried egg. We were disappointed with our stay after looking forward to going back for a special occasion. For the price a night costs here you would expect better. We have stayed in much cheaper places and had better stays.

author: markowenblakey
title: No Security / No Help / No Cleaners
text: It is frustrating when you stay in Hotels all overs the world, that you can cop attitude from staff in a hotel in Largs. I had already lost faith in this hotel before I had checked in.... We arrived at the hotel at 9am realising our room would not be ready. I asked if there was somewhere secure to leave our cases. There is NOT. You can just leave them in lobby. I asked what time we might be able to check in. The girl said 2pm (the only I’ve it seems). So we left our cases in a hotel lobby with a girl who couldn’t even be bothered to check we were even guests..... As the keys here are kept on enormous key rings it makes sense to leave them at reception. The bizarre thing is when you back in, and ask for your key, they just hand it over, with no idea who you are. Given there is no safe in these rooms I ended taking my passport with me, cos I don’t consider the rooms safe. There is no house keeping process in place. The first morning we couldn’t find a hair dryer, but did find a cupboard (see photo) of old wine bottles. While this may be the best hotel in Largs.... it exists for weddings. The brekkie was okay.

author: smartie1968
title: Drive by - please
text: Well, what can one say. Sat nav took us to the back of the hotel which was revolting. We were there to attend a wedding, but that's another story. Receptionist was rude to the point of dismissive. The general cleanliness was poor; cobwebs, spiders, brass banister rail filthy. Wedding coordinator dirty and unhelpful. Food atrocious. Had to go to the chippy for a fish supper. Drink extortionate. £3.50 for a tiny bottle of diet coke. Rooms at the height of summer boiling. No fans offered. Shower pressure worse than an oldie with a UTI. Honestly, body swerve this place. Horrible.

author: paulbayley
title: Victorian Plumbing
text: Firstly, I was staying here on business so relied on the wifi. Numerous times it just didn't work and everytime I complained the reception staff told me there was nothing wrong with it. They offered to let me use the office internet which still didn't work in my room! When it did work it was fine, just unreliable. Staff were really nice and helpful and breakfast was a treat each morning. Weddings from hell were the feature of my stay. They served wedding guests until 4am and little sleep, with banging doors and conversations that left little to the imagination through the paper thin walls of my room 112. The plumbing was awful. If I turned on the hot tap I had to run for my life until the permanent air lock had calmed down to avoid being spat at and scalded. The shower was a drizzle which I complained about and was told basically "It is what it is". I couldn't move room as the hotel was full. This astonished me as there was only about ten cars in the car park at best except when the weddings were taking place. A bonus feature was the bathroom radiator playing the theme to Chitty Chitty Bang Bang.I quickly learned to turn both radiators in the room off to get some semblance of quiet. To be fair the main hotel was ok but could do with a refresh and the staff were great but sorry bathroom not acceptable in 2018. Owners should be ashamed!

author: Sunshinemama
title: Night of luxury
text: Looked at hotels in Largs and The Brisbane House Hotel definitely captured my interest. We arrived at the hotel which offered good parking, upon arriving at the reception we were met with the lovely Francesca who could not have been anymore helpful... She booked us in, giving us a personal feeling of VIP guests, polite, cheerful, lovely smile and attentive, a real ambassador for the hotel. The room was on the second floor with easy accessibility. The refit is wonderful, the hotel stunning... I can see why so many weddings are held there. Francesca check on us to see if everything was to our liking.. And of course it was and more. We decided not to venture out, had a few drinks and then ate in the restaurant "Oscars"... The food was delicious, prices we thought reasonable... The only thing that could be improved in the restaurant was... For the staff to be a little more aware and to smile... As they are representing the Brisbane. But we would recommend here and would like to thank Francesca very much for making a our stay so nice.. Thank you xx

author: Con42
title: Nice hotel
text: Went here on an Itison deal. The hotel was nice in a great position right on the seafront with great views. It has recently been done up and the rooms are pleasantly decorated. We were upgraded to a seafront room which was a great surprise. The room was large and had everything you need. It was comfortable and very clean. Think they do need to do some snagging in the rooms as there were a few small things needing fixed such as the push button on the toilet but nothing major. It was very windy and wild outside and there was a draught from the windows. The radiators were roasting hot but as they were below the windows and behind the curtain it left the room a bit cool. I fully understand the trials of being seafront but maybe secondary glazing would be an option that would be cost effective as the heating bill must be high. The staff were very pleasant and helpful and couldn't do enough for you. Part of the deal was dinner , B& B. The restaurant was lovely and the menu had a good choice and was very tasty. Breakfast was also very good and the Irish lady who appeared to be on her own was very nice, very helpful and pleasant. A credit to the hotel. I would recommend a stay here as its a lovely hotel within walking distance of the seafront and shops. Well worth a visit.

author: Snapperkev
title: Nice food, Clean but poor service
text: Stayed at the Brisbane for 2 night's near end of February. Set on the coast the Hotel is in a great location and is only 45 mins by train from Glasgow. On arrival we where met by renovation work at reception. Not ideal but check in was quick. The rooms are small but adequate and very clean. The staff are very polite and friendly. The food was of a good standard and very tasty. Where they let themselves down is the service. Probably the worst I've had in a hotel in years. Now don't get me wrong, when they did serve you it was courteous and polite..When they did!!!!!. The service (and I use that term loosely) was way below what should be expected. At times you could be waiting up to 10 mins to get served at the bar or longer if you where waiting to catch the attention if a food waitress. I should point out that it was not busy and we where the only ppl looking to get service. Used glasses etc where not being removed from our table and at times they didn't have the drinks you ordered in one bar but had it across the hotel in another. They didn't offer to go and get it for you. 👀 It was so obvious that the hotel has a staffing problem and it it made our stay less enjoyable for it. Its a pity, if they could sort the staff issue out the hotel and Largs would be a lovely place to spend a few nights.

author: 287silverfox
title: Disappointed
text: First visit via an Itison voucher. Outside, looked impressive, so had high hopes for our one night stay. Room.......very small but tastefully furnished. Bed, a bit lumpy. Only 2 hangers in the (open) wardrobe ! Woken at 5.00am by extraction fan , literally just outside the window , starting up from ? the kitchen area .Necessitated closing window to reduce the noise level, (but only slightly). Staff, friendly and well meaning , (some of whom looked considerably under 21 !)! Dinner previous evening in pleasant surroundings but comprehensive menu drastically reduced to 'Itison' menu, down to only 7 items, (and 2 of those were "unavailable") ! For the first time in my life , the Prawn Cocktail was served on a flat plate , consisting of a spoonful of prawns mixed in some insipid mayonnaise and dumped on 2 small lettuce leaves with a slice of fresh supermarket (white) bread cut in half and lying either side on the same plate. No butter, which had to be requested ! (A touch of salt and pepper did nothing for the mayo, by the way). Main course, Daun (?) of beef in red wine Jus with veg , which included a barely cooked cauliflower floret . The meat although tender , was very 'stringy' and way too salty . My wife had the fish (battered cod) which included a slice of somewhat brown coloured lemon , which , on suggesting the chef found the rest of it so it could be binned , passed his apologies back via the waitress. Barely Disabled-friendly , (there was a ramp up the side of the building) , no lifts , and stairs everywhere else. Surely, the idea of using an Itison voucher is to 'Showcase' an establishment , informing would be guests of the delights and facilities it contained ? In truth, we were left with the distinct impression of being 'second class citizens' and the idea that management were trying to 'claw back' some of the costs of an eight month old refurbishment. Please tell me I am wrong ?

author: carronbrae
title: Great position in Largs but let down by everything else
text: Had an Itison voucher for 1 night and added on an extra couple of nights. Room was very hot despite turning the heating off, the window was frosted to the outside so no view and above the kitchen so extractor fan was noisy from 6.30am to 10.30pm. Hot and cold on the tap was the wrong way round. Shower door leaked. 4 hangers for 2 people for 3 nights! shower attachment had a mind of it's own and was about to fall off. Unable to read using the bedside lights. Room service haphazard.Food mediocre. Staff mediocre and could do with more training/management. Breakfast okay apart from the hot water that tasted as though it had come from an urn that had been boiled dry. Wifi in room was obviously being hogged by someone as could only seem to get it spasmodically even though it said it was a strong signal. Room noisy from banging doors as guests went upstairs. Felt as though the hotel was totally geared up for weddings at weekend and any trade during the week was incidental. Enjoyed Largs and despite the rain we still managed to get out walking and complete the Ayrshire coastal path which was our aim. Wouldn't come back to the hotel though.

author: aldomartini
title: Modern Comfort
text: Bought an Itison deal for an overnight stay with dinner and breakfast. The hotel has been extensively modernised since my last visit. Paid a supplement of £10 for a bigger room with a sea view which was only visible with a walk to a small window. A glass of prosecco was delivered to the room after check in. A 2 course dinner was the deal. We opted for haggis pakora and tempura prawns, both with sauce. Warm, well served but never home made. Mains was fish and chips for both of us. Again, nothing home made. Bought a bottle of wine which was well priced. Service at dinner and the following morning at breakfast was excellent. Good choices on the breakfast menu which was hot. Overall a very nice stay. Room was modern, and very clean and comfortable. Recommended and we'll go back.

author: harbro114
title: Brilliant
text: This was a last minute weekend break. Like the other reviewer read the reviews and took the chance. On approach beautiful looking hotel ample parking and great location. Was greeted at reception by Fran what a diamond! Warm friendly and exceptionally helpful. Helped is upstairs with luggage too. The room was lovely on the second floor. Very modern. Fresh and very comfortable. The end suite was excellent. Went for dinner in Henry's and was greeted by the charming Eca . The service was first class. The food was outstanding. The prawn and crayfish starter was the best I ever tasted. Over all this hotel is a winner. Will highly recommend to all.

author: Nataliecameron
title: Glen Room (family room)
text: So I was here for my friends wedding. I stayed in the glen room with my 3 children and partner. Room was what looked like the "clearers room" old dirty brown door unlike the gorgeous white doors for the other rooms. When I walked in I was greeted by a musky smell as if the room hadn't been cleaned recently. The furniture was old and deep brown wood. The bed looked stunning tho a old wooden four poster bed. I thought maybe this wasn't as bad as I thought then I sat on the bed. It started! This bed was the most noisiest squeaky beds I have even hear in my life. It honestly kept me awake through the night. Every move I made the bed had a noise for it. The wardrobe had no handle and the tiles in the bathroom had black masking tape on the. Because the tiles were lifting. Do not stay in the glen room!!! I went to visit my friends room and her was stunning. Huge kings size bed with high head board and the bathroom was stunning. No musky smell nice clean and tidy room. I cannot fault the staff they were lovely and friendly. Room service was always on time and food was delicious.

author: theadeofspades
title: What was that?
text: Okay... So i was invited to a wedding here and decided why not eh? Firstly.. Who laid our your car park? I may or may not have parked in a disabled space but it was particularly poorly signed if I'm being honest. Secondly... Who doesn't use Key Cards to enter rooms? Welcome to 2016 el Brisbano - get your act together! Thirdly - sitting through a ceremony on your chair was one of the most painful experiences of my life - please splurge out a little and buy comfy seats, yeah? Next up - CARD AT THE BAR! Once again, this is 2016 - chip and pin is a major factor in (statistically) 78% of our lives! Yet, your staff refuse to serve us. I blame you, Mr Brisbane; catch a grip! After this, imagine my horror when I could not buy my four year old some blackcurrant squash without having to fund the Fruit Shoot agenda. Disgusting. Continuing from this statement, how dare you allow drug dealings to go on in your very restrooms? This question is not rhetorical, no sirree, so please take on the burden of what this means - you have allowed illicit dealings to occur on your property and you are quite fortunate that I have decided against alerting the authorities! My last point concerns brekkie: who in this blessed world has decided that the complimentary breakfast with an (overpriced) £100 room should actually end at 9.30am? THE AUDACITY! As much as I have been dismayed by the Brisbane House Hotel this eve, I thoroughly enjoyed myself and would recommend it to my well-established peers nonetheless - I still had a "slammin" night!

author: RobinKABZ
title: Good location, poor accommodation
text: Initial impressions were good as we arrived in reception, however we were brought down to earth on arriving in our room. There is no lift, but as we were on the first floor this was not a major inconvenience. The room itself was quite tired looking and small. There was nowhere to put luggage. The lower half of the window was opaque, presumably so we could not see whatever was on the other side of the window. There was the constant sound of some piece of machinery on the outside, possibly air conditioning for the kitchen. The room itself has no air conditioning. As we later found out the mattress was lumpy. The bathroom, also quite small, was well beyond tired, it was in serious need of refurbishment. It looked quite dingy and old. The lounge, bar and dining area is modern, bright and west facing with a nice view of the sunset. The seating is not very comfortable for a prolonged stay. The dinner menu is acceptable and the quality also acceptable as are the prices. Breakfast is a little unimpressive from a presentational point of view. There is an outdoor terrace area in front of the bar which we did not get to use due to the weather. The location is ideal for visiting Largs and is close to the ferry terminal and town centre. The hotel has adequate parking facilities at the front of the hotel. The staff on reception and in the lounge area were very pleasant and helpful. This could be a nice hotel but it is in serious need of refurbishment. I felt it was grossly over priced considering the condition of the accommodation.

author: rrrosielee
title: Must do better....
text: Positives...location, parking, OK food, nice bar, amenable staff. Negatives...(considering £110 a night) Tiny double room, very very hot and noisy. Kitchen ventilation fan right outside bedroom window (room 107) No air conditioning Rickety staircase held together with gaffer tape, wet paint signs where there was no wet paint! Fire extinguishers holding doors open!!!!! No lift Very rough decoration, mouldy bathroom, plugs not attached to sink, paint peeling off the ceiling. Room not cleaned properly, bin not emptied, nappies in bin from Saturday until we left on Monday. Tea and coffee not replenished. Staff should advise when booking that it's not just a wedding taking place but very very loud music until 11.30, very difficult when trying to get a 19 month old toddler to sleep! Breakfast....no rolls on the first day, no mushrooms on the second day. Not a good idea to have your staff eating and drinking in the restaurant area during breakfast. You would not find this in other 4 star hotels. I hope our comments allow you to address these issues for future guests. Remember hotels survive on repeat business. We did voice our concerns on departure on 1-8-2016. Had a missed call from the hotel on the same day but since then no effort has been made to contact us again.

author: Lynne0481
title: Had a good time
text: My partner and I arrived at the hotel on 5th April having taken advantage of a itison voucher and also paying for an extra night & sea view. I was worried before I arrived as I had read previous reviews on trip advisor. The entrance to the hotel is lovely and the receptionist was very welcoming and told us to let her know if there were any problems with the room. We stayed in room 206. The room was clean and had a massive big window with a gorgeous view on to the sea . There were a few little things wrong with the room but I would just put this down to it being a bit tired but I personally am happy as long as I have a clean bed to sleep in as I am not planning on spending a lot of time in the room, there was nothing that I would have went out of my way to complain about. The bathroom looked as though it had been done and was very nice. There was obviously a lot of renovation work going on in the hotel and I am sure once complete it will be lovely. We had dinner in the hotel on the first night, I have no complaints with the food, we had different meals and were both very happy with what we had eaten, I would have eaten there again if we hadn't made other plans. Breakfast both mornings was also lovely, we were those annoying people who come in two mins before breakfast finished but nothing was said to us and we were greeted with a smile. We both had the full breakfast on the first day and a smaller breakfast the second day, I had asked for black pudding to be added on to this and this was no problem for them. Overall I have no complaints, we had a nice wee break away including a trip over to Millport where we hired bikes for a few hours. I would recommend getting Fish and Chips from the Fish & Chicken Bar in the town near to the Thomas Cook. The fish was cooked fresh and I can honestly say it was delicious. I would also recommend paying a visit to the Waterside Bar, the barmaid there, Izzy was really friendly and welcoming.

author: Overnyter
title: Failed
text: Booked in for b n b. Was told I had a four poster, very grand thinks I - not at all was the truth. A very basic looking frame and the hard lumpy mattress does not fill the base. There is a periodic humming noise throughout the night which came from the heating or the fan units just below my room. So constant disturbance through the night. The Windows were manky both inside and out and the chair very stained. Nice big TVs on wall but remote missing! When ever a TVs chef cooks poached eggs they cut into them and the golden yolk oozes. So I assume that is the way a poached egg should be cooked and served. It's certainly how I enjoy them. Mine was done and served hard so I did not eat. I noticed another's that also looked hard. At no point was I asked if everything was ok not even by the receptionist who was sat in a chair that looks like it's been rescued from the tip! I believe I got a deal on this room but it's worth nothing if the basics are not satisfied. So avoid the Glen room. I would give them another chance but I won't be rushing back. The bathroom was nice see pics

author: 442cameronm
title: Dingy room, poor restaurant service
text: Booked for 1 night business trip. From the road the car park and hotel look modern and sleek. All glass and steel. Reception was efficient and was expecting me. Room was tiny and a bit dingy. Window overlooking back yard where the staff use to smoke. Bed was a double but all but colapsed. It bowed into the middle from all sides. Bedside lamp did not work. Mirror light did not work. Bathroom vent fan clogged with fluff. Damage on wall was roughly patched up with plaster. Went for dinner, unfortunately as a single dinner was made to sit at a table in the middle of the room. Had to ask for a menu, then for cutlery. Food was decent. Service was poor though I had to ask for everything I needed. Young staff generally were we're polite but inexperienced. The manager was mostly outside socialising with others. Pity inside does not reflect outside.

author: craigb260
title: The Worst Room I Have Ever Been Given in a Hotel
text: I think my review title says it all..... We had booked here in Feb 2016 for a one night stay. The general feel I got of the hotel after passing reception was that it was a bit run down and tired looking. There are scrapes on the wallpaper and scuffs going up the stairs etc. The room, 201, didn't have WiFi because the signal strength was too poor. The room smelled strongly of paint, so much so that my wife was starting to get a headache, and she had only arrived at the hotel half an hour before me. The wardrobes had no doors on them and were unfinished, no bath, there was a large mirror left on the floor. The drawer unit was chipped and some of the drawers were broken and didn't close. This was all I noticed because I left the room after about 3 minutes and asked to be changed to a different rooms. The gentleman at reception explained that unfortunately he couldn't change our room because they were fully booked. He went on to explain that they have been having this problem for 'the last 5-6 weeks' because everyone that gets room 201 wants to change rooms. I'm sure that the Brisbane must have nice rooms because if they were all like room 201 then the hotel would have no customers and have to close. The receptionist did offer us a stay at another time but we won't be going back. We cancelled our dinner reservation, checked out and left. The whole process took around 17 minutes. The shortest stay at a hotel in my life. Can't really think of a positive......eh.....the reception staff could speak English so that was good....and the room did have 4 walls....and the windows had glass in them. So slightly better that a mud hut.......I should have made that the title of this review.

author: 864joannef
title: A mixed bag
text: Well this place is a complete mixed bag..... We stayed on an ITISON deal. The hotel from the outside and the car park looks lovely and has a great spot overlooking the sea. Reception was lovely also and check-in was fine. The restaurant has been fitted out very nicely and the food was good however think the staff have to explain better what the deal includes and what other option is on offer as we were a bit mislead and only fully understood when overhearing staff explaining to the table next to us. This part of the hotel I would have given 5 stars. Now for the big let-down.... the corridors upstairs and the rooms are like a 1 star hotel. The place is very run down and really I was glad we were only staying one night. Stayed in what we were told was an upgrade room so I feel for anyone in a standard room. I also feel sorry for the people below us as the floorboards were extremely noisy. The only good think about the room was large window with the view, the curtain however had seen better days. The staff seemed to not bother about putting away cleaning supplies etc. and we seen this lying about several times when passing through corridor. I can see a real future for this place if all the corridors and rooms are fully renovated and I mean fully, unless this is done I have to say sadly I would not stay here again and wouldn’t recommend it in its current state.

author: bennyg690
title: Great location, accommodation lacked quality.
text: The nature of our trip was a family wedding so the hotel was merely a place to lay our heads over a very busy weekend. The location was great on the seafront of Largs just a stones throw all the local amenities. The frontage and restaurant had an initial wow factor but unfortunately the rest of the hotel didn't follow suit. The hallways and carpets were well worn and shabby. The room was on the top floor and had a great view out to sea. It was very clean but the decor was tired to say the least and needed extended refurbishment. Curtains, wallpaper and towels were ripped and furniture was damaged. These seemed fixes that were inexpensive and easily picked up during an inspection from hotel management. The wifi that was complimentary didn't work at all during all of the stay. The shower was no more than a Luke warm dribble. Our family members were also in the hotel and had far worse rooms than mine with tiny rooms, hard beds and awful views. Double occupancy at the hotel was over a hundred pounds per night which is a lot more than a decent travel lodge or premier inn. Despite the shortcomings the room was quiet and comfortable. The staff were friendly and breakfast was of a reasonable quality. Would not stay again as it a lot of money for low quality .

author: RetiredBrewer
title: Excellent location let down by shabby rooms and communal areas.
text: The staff were friendly and helpful. The breakfast was adequate and catered for my wife's gluten intolerance. The location is excellent. The parking was easy. The reception area was very nice. The good news stops there. Once you climb the stairs you enter another world. The communal areas are not just tired but shabby. The first room we were offered was unacceptable with torn curtains, wallpaper hanging off the walls and a part eaten pack of biscuits on the tea tray. The second room we were offered was better but had a substantial list of faults some of which were remedied by the staff. An attempt had been made to upgrade the bathroom, but the standard of finish was very poor. The water pressure for the shower was very poor and anyone with long hair would need to invest considerable time in rinsing shampoo out of it. The soundproofing between the rooms is apalling. Pray that your neighbour hasn't been for a curry and is not feeling amorous. The floorboards in both the rooms and the landings on the second floor don't squeak they shout. I used to visit this hotel on business regularly years ago as it was justly famed for it's hospitality and cuisine. This stay let our visit down. We did not try the resaurant apart from breakfast so cannot comment. We used Lounge at Largs and Nardinis. Overall this visit was like visiting an elderly relative in a care home when your last memory of them was of a vibrant young person.

author: Scottish21
title: Impressed
text: Stayed here for 1 night with 5 other couples to go to the hotels Christmas night. Hotel entrance and bar area is very light and modern. We paid a bit extra for a room upgrade and were allocated a massive room overlooking the sea. It had a four poster bed with an ensuite bathroom with walk in shower and jacuzzi bath. The room was lovely until you started looking at the detall. Carpet was stained in a few places with what looked like the residue of either red wine or coffee, one of the bedside lampshades was stained and there were what looked like water warks on the ceiling.As this was a Christmas night we paid for dinner and breakfast. Bar prices were reasonable by hotel standards and the traditional Christmas meal was one of the best i have had in many years. Portion sizes were enormous and the quality and presentation of the food was second to none. As i have some health problems i couldnt eat the desserts on offer as part of the fixed Christmas menu. I explained this to the waitress and asked for cheese and biscuits instead. Given that most hotels dont deviate from fixed menus i was absolutely delighted when the waitress advised i could have an alternative dessert without question ! The "full monty" cooked breakfast the following morning was delicious and the staff during the whole stay were friendly and engaging. It was during breakfast that one of the staff advised us that the hotel rooms would shortly be geting refurbished. As it already has elements of a trendy boutique hotel, i cant wait to see what it looks like once its refurbished ! To the management and staff of the Brisbane Hotel, my personal thanks for making this a lovely stay. Myself, my wife and all our friends will definitely be back !

author: susansN5615ZQ
title: top hotel for weddings, maybe, but not for overnight guests
text: the outside of this hotel looks impressive. the lobby looks like the top class hotel its supposed to be. It is such a shame about the rooms. The room we stayed in was in need of refurbishment, now. The paintwork is in need of a new coat, the ceiling had a large watermark on it from the room above. the furniture was in need of replacement. There was bits of paper underneath the legs of the wardrobe to stop it falling forward. The mattress on my bed (we had twin beds) was so hard and uncomfortable that I thought about sleeping on the floor, but the carpet was not very clean !!!!! The sheets and duvets were of good quality, and very white. We heard every noise from the room above, all through the night. Floorboards creaked as they walked about, beds groaned etc etc, not nice to listen to. The bathroom was nice, very modern, although there were cracked tiles by the door. Nice white fluffy towels. Breakfast was only OK. Tea and coffee were help yourself from the flasks on the table. There was no yoghurt and no tongues for handling the bread.The cooked breakfast was greasy and not of a high standard, ie; sausages were cheap, gristly, bacon was very fatty. We didn't have a main meal here so cannot comment on the food at dinner. Staff were very friendly. Personally we will not stay here again, and we do intend to visit the area a lot, as our daughter is moving there.

author: Aly252014
title: Not too shabby
text: We stayed here on the 10th of October so we could attend the Boat show in Inver Kip marina. We did not arrive to quite late in the evening after having a scout about for other hotels. I looked at the website and it looked quite nice. The receptionist was wonderful and very welcoming, we were allocated a room to the front but it only had a small sea view so it was on the lower end of the price range, which was ok as it was only for one night. I think the rooms over all could do with an upgrade, although its not the worst I have been in. I do not know about the rooms at the higher end of the scale but if it was similar the finish I would of not been happy paying that. The paper was peeling, chipped paint shoddy furniture but over all it was very clean. The bathroom was spotless. The shower was not great but I can not fault the cleaners. We ate in the restaurant which was very quiet considering it was a friday night. The menu was good, and very good prices although the food was average. I ordered the fish and chips, and out comes a massive portion crammed onto a small plate. I asked the male server for a side plate and he brought me another dinner plate which is a bit odd. Anyhow I think my fish was a little undercooked but over all it was ok. My husband enjoyed his lasagne. The puddings were to die for, I had the sticky toffee and it was amazing. Good night sleep, the bed was comfortable but I felt the rooms to be quite hot. Breakfast was good, but again the breakfast room was a little underwhelming. Overall I think if i was paying the higher end of the scale Id of been a bit more disappointed but for one night it did the job. The highlights were the staff, the lobby and the dessert :) I would go back for a one night stay but not more than that.

author: Arnold_Layne_13
title: Big on presentation, lacking in substance, pub grub in plush surroundings
text: I went for dinner with 9 work colleagues, it wasn't a special occassion. The youthful and perhaps inexperienced waiter spilt a pint of lager over one of our party. The same waiter got the starter order wrong because he didn't write anything down but the beer soaked diner gracefully accepted the chicken strips that had arrived at the table in error. My prawn and crayfish salad was nicely presented but tasteless. For my main course I had Chicken Paremessanio which lay nestled in an oblique shaped bowl, a nice touch but again the food was tasteless. My compadre on the other side of the table had a fillet steak which looked tasty. His chips were served in a small tin bucket... are you getting it yet? The Brisbane takes presentation seriously which is obvious as you approach the establishment from the High St... all nicely lit glass facade and trimmed bushes. But... the food and service was a let down. This is pub grub served in a hotel. It has to be said though that at £8.99 for 2 courses it represents decent value. The spilt beer and the incorrect starter appeared on the bill and we were even dumb enough to leave a tip, generous folk that we are.

author: CazaGlasgow
title: Rooms need some work...still!!!
text: This was my second stay at this hotel, both times for a wedding. The wedding was lovely & was a nice setting with the function rooms being very good, food at the wedding was lovely & service was good. You can't fault the wedding side. However the same can't be said for the rooms, I previously didn't rate the rooms so I new what to expect. We had a small rear facing room which I new when we booked for £90. The room size itself & bathroom were fine in size, I didn't expect big as of how size was described but I would same size was fine. The room I think had been decorated maybe a year or so ago but paint on walls dirty & window sill very marked, their is no view from the window as glazed out to hide extractor fans, which they fail to mention when booking, we had to sleep with window shut to not hear noise, which meant room was very hot, it was hot I room constantly. The bed was comfy but missing a mattress protector, sheet straight on to mattress not very hygienic!!! The bed side light didn't work, these are things that should be checked by housekeeping. The bathroom was awful, I read a review from over a year ago where someone complained about the bathroom & the manager said it was being upgraded but still not, the tiles & bathroom seal are black & bath stained, shower through dirty taps that need a good clean. The bathroom is not up to standard. We ordered breakfast to the room for an extra £3 each & I would say that is a good price & worth it, tho order came wrong, we ordered white toast & got brown & asked for no beans on one but came with it. I did fill in my comments card with all these details but she I handed it to reception she ripped it up. I would of said something & about the room but the bride & groom were their & I didn't want them to hear any negative comments, I would say the rooms are over priced & they make their money knowing that wedding guests want a room as a wedding can be a long day. I think the hotel needs to sort their rooms out & listen to the feedback customers leave on here,

author: Scottaw3
title: A lovely bash at the Brisbane
text: I stayed in this hotel midweek in October to attend a wedding. I stayed 2 nights but only paid for one (the first night was paid for me; a few of us staying in the Glen Room, unsure how much this was. The second night cost me ₤60, room 108). I found it lovely. Nice view of the sea, reception staff very helpful and friendly, they didn't mind when I asked if I could print off a speech I'd written! And I know that this is at their discretion so thank you. The rooms were nicely furnished, decorated, clean. The housekeeping did a good job especially since they have organise their cleaning around a tidal rhythm of daily wedding parties arriving and leaving. The wedding (130 people) went along without a hitch, people were organised well and the food was nice. The manager is a character, I found him very amusing. Some of the reviews on here I feel are a bit unfair about him! My impression was that he enjoyed working there and took pride both in his hotel and in providing good guest service. NB they also provide a small bus service which I believe will drop off/pick up within small distances - something that was very useful at midnight for some girls attending the wedding who had had to book in a BnB up the road (I'm not sure if this needs to be arranged in advance or not, sorry). With regards to the 2nd bar, we checked in the night before the wedding we were attending and used this other bar to have some quiet drinks and a catch up. Quite right that it shouldn't be an overspill for the rather more inebriated wedding guests who have their own bar! I'm giving this hotel the full 5 stars because I had a fantastic time, and it was value for money for me because I didn't have to pay for the first night. I will note that there were a couple of plumbing issues (shower drained very slowly in the Glen Room leading to some floor flooding - fixed with some plunging by reception, and the bridal suite toilet had blocked, which again I believe was fixed promptly however these didn't really affect me directly, or spoil my stay).

author: Marty_240679
title: Fantastic Hotel. Location, Location, Location!
text: I stayed in the hotel with my wife on Saturday 16th March as I was attending a friend’s wedding there. Location: Excellent, right on the front of Largs’ seaside with the town centre in close proximity. Parking: Plenty of room for all hotel guests. Check-in: No fuss at all – No queues, very pleasant reception staff – was in the room within a couple of minutes of arrival. Room: Suite Room 101 – Very spacious room. Included a nice 4-poster bed, with a nice leather couch to relax on and look out across the water across the road. There was also tea & coffee facilities, a makeup table for the ladies, and plenty of drawers and hanging space for those who don’t travel light. The bathroom was excellent – with a spacious Jacuzzi bath and a walk-in shower. The view from this room is stunning. Hotel facilities: My evening meal was as part of the wedding, so I didn’t use the normal restaurant facilities that were available for anything other than breakfast on Sunday morning - but if it was anything like the standard of everything else in the hotel I am sure it would have been excellent. The breakfast was really nice – continental breakfast etc available and the waitress taking orders for anyone preferring a cooked breakfast to cereal / toast / yoghurts / fruit juices etc. There was also tea and coffee available. I went for the full monty – very nice, black pudding with a fry-up is always a nice touch. Check-out: A very short wait due to a lot of people checking out at the same time, but completely hassle-free. Again, reception staff very pleasant. Will definitely stay here again.

author: Leigh_AnnR21
title: A get away.... Glad to come home
text: My husband and I have just spent three days in Largs, which we loved. It is a shame that we cannot say the same for this hotel. Yes, this hotel is aesthetically pleasing from the outside and at the reception area, however the room which we paid £168 in total to stay in for two nights, left a lot to be desired. On arrival, the staff were accommodating and informed us that they had complementary upgraded us to a sea view room. To be honest I would have loved to see the room that we were originally going to stay in if the room we got was an upgrade. Within the two days we stayed in this room we noticed… - The two bedside lamps were plugged in but did not work. - The decorative cushions on the bed had stains on them. - The heater in the toilet was up at maximum but the knob to turn it off was broken. - The black leather headboard on the bed had slash marks on it. - The walls of the room were dirty and marked. When we checked out of this hotel today I just wanted to get out and I know I will never go back. I filled in the feed-back form stating that the room was very poor, but reading some of the reviews on this page, even if I said that we didn’t have a good stay, I don’t think anything would have been done. Upon reading the manager’s response on one persons review on this site, I feel that if someone posting as a manager cannot spell and use grammar properly makes me realise that the people running this hotel take your money and don’t care about customer opinion and feed back. I believe the weddings and other functions which this hotel provide would be top notch as I cannot fault the hotel staff or restaurant staff, but all of their hard work is being put down with the state of the rooms. If I know of anyone going to this hotel I would definitely tell them otherwise.

author: Hazelnutineverybite
title: Great spot for an overnight stop.
text: My first stop at the Brisbane House Hotel for an overnight stop whilst on business, I was pleasantly surprised. I would normally stop in Gourock or Greenock but thought I would give it a try. Check-in was very efficient, lovely receptionist, first impressions are very good. The earlier review of the squeaky floor boards is accurate and although there is an historic explanation I did find it annoying. For an overnight stop I was happy to put up with it as the hotel has a lot to offer. I had a double room situated on the first floor at the front, the view of the Clyde front which was obscured by the back of the heightened front entrance (watch that one). However, I was tired, it was one night so I put up with it rather than make a fuss. The room was a double with en-suite, the shower was a walk in self-contained unit, excellent. Bed was comfortable and there is a TV and coffee making facilities. I guess in some ways I was fortunate, the weather was superb so after a walk down to one of the nearby bar's I sat out on the front patio of the hotel for dinner. The front of the hotel is protected by glass so even with a cool breeze you can happily stop out there until quite late in the evening. Dinner menu has enough variety and the food was splendid. The hotel is in a great position on the beach front and there are bars and restaurants nearby in walking distance so enough variety for a short stop. Breakfast is taken in the hotel bar/restaurant, again friendly welcoming staff and I enjoyed tucking in to the Brisbane House Special. As a businessman it ticked all the boxes for a short stop, quiet despite road outside, nice location, enough to see outside the hotel and enough within if you just wanted to stop there and chill out! I would definitely return.

author: StuartM35
title: Do the basics better...
text: My wife and I stayed over for a nioght as we attended a family wedding in Largs. We chose the Brisbane as the last time we stayed there we had a fantastic river view room oerlooking the firth of Clyde. This time we weren't so lucky - maybe he vagaries of booking on line but we were facing out the back and next to the fire door on the first floor. Our room was nicely decorated but basic, all we needed really for a single night stay and judging bythe noise the wedding party that was going on was obviously having a very good time... While the rom was good the bathroom was in pieces - a hole in the ceiling had blu tack in to stop plaster dust falling, the shower was a mixer-nightmare tap, if you flushed the toilet the seat came flying down at you... (Rm 115). When eating at night the girl cleaning the table next to us in the restaurant simply swept the food crumbs onto the floor!! The chap serving us was very good - Jordan - and he apologised but for a hotel of this size and decor the wine list was poor - about 8 of each plus Rose and champagne. On serving the white wine was way above room temp and so needed an ice bucket and 10 mins to cool down. The meal was very good - we both had steak, cooked just as we asked - and with the extras we asked for too. Breakfast was good, service a bit slow but there was only one person serving and it was fairly fiull - if you've a wedding on and foks staing don't you make provision for that? On leaving neither Alli or I were asked if we'd enjoyed the stay... That's juts poor, basic customer service. If we'd been staying more than a single night we'd have made some noise about the above but would anyone have cared? Overall I'd say the BHH needs to do more of the basics better - don't sweept crumbs onto the floor, keep the wine cooled, close the office door (throughout the stay you see into the office that was littered with paperwork and extremely untidy), ask your customers how they are, how the stay was and so on.

author: grumpyoldgunner
title: Don't Judge A Hotel By Its Reception
text: I and my fellow ship mates stopped off in Largs as part of our Easter Cruise. We were really looking forward to our stay at the Brisbane. First impressions were admirable. A lovely contemporary lobby and a very charming receptionist. At this point we couldn’t wait to see our rooms. Then the very charming receptionist directed us to our rooms. We knew something was wrong when she told us we were out the back. I got to my room, initially things looked good, and then I closed the door. My god the heat hit me, it was hotter than the sun. Great I thought I have air conditioning. Yes I had air conditioning, but no way to control it. Ok I open the window, no can’t do that because of the kitchen noise. The longer I stayed in the room, the more I saw that wasn’t up to the same standard as the lobby. Some of the following are defects I can report: Random screws sticking out of the wall, stains on the ceiling and a random hole in the ceiling. The bed was very uncomfortable and with a classy plastic cover. The wi-fi could not be picked up in the room, I was only on the first floor. I’m sad to report all my ship mates had the same sort of shoddy standards. I just wish our rooms were up to the same standard as their lobby and staff. Some of the rooms look really nice but, be warned some are not.

author: LPTES
title: THIS IS ONE SERIOUSLY HOT HOTEL
text: I booked this hotel to celebrate a special occasion. We had two rooms, 106 and 107. My mother could not bear either the heat in her room nor tolerate the endless noise from the hotel kitchen area outside the window which had to be left open in an attempt to ventilate the room. She was grudgingly moved to a shoe box sized room at 11pm when she contacted reception. This room did benefit from air conditioning but suffered from an offensive smell from the bathroom. Rooms 106 and 107 are both at the back and the lower part of the windows is opaque glass so you have virtually no outlook at all. The replacement room was to the side and had no outlook either. The valance on the bed in my room was very dirty and stained in a number of places and the overall rating of this small room would have to be below average. We are regular hotel guests and are used to so much better than this at a much more favourable price! Some hotels are anxious to ensure their guests have a good time while others only want your money. The owner of this hotel only wants your money, so be warned. We will not stay here again and would strongly advise others to give the hotel a wide berth as the suffocating heat could well aggravate health problems. We are talking the sort of temperatures that kill dogs in cars. We were given a small reduction of £10 per night for the replacement shoe box sized room but I can honestly say we've stayed at the Hilton for less money and will be doing so again shortly. This badly run hotel is the best advertisement for other accommodation providers in Largs. If you want to be comfortable go somewhere else.

author: khutch7
title: don't book a "small double" room!
text: We booked a room because our friend was getting married there. The wedding itself was lovely. The service and wedding meal were lovely too. The room was a shock. It was a more like a small single room with a small double bed. The furnature, curtains and carpet were very old fashioned. There was a very small tv with four channels and an airconditioning unit that only seemed to generate hot air. The bathroom had an unattractive green suite.
