The shower was every old and only had a curtain rather than any cubical. This resulted in the toilet roll getting wet when the shower was on! The trouser press didn't work and wasn't secured properly on the wall. On checking out I told the member of staff I felt the room was not up to standard. She was very cold and unhelpful - asking 'were you not told it was a small doubleroom when you booked'. I told her i was but that wasn't the only problem and I would be taking matters further with the manager when the wedding party had left. I presume there are nice rooms at the front of the hotel but I will never be back to find out. This is probably the worst hotel room i have ever stayed in!

author: ClearExcutiveSearch
title: Hotel Brisbane is good but will be great!
text: My wife , 14 year old son and I stayed at the Brisbane Hotel for two nights, one before our motor cruising course and one after the course. At the time the Hotel was going through a very large up grading project with the builders in. There was very little noise and the staff were so efficient and polite and the service was excellent, we didn’t notice the ongoing works.. I don’t want to use the stereo type for the “Scots” but the hotel food was being sold for £9.99 for two courses and the food was so good that the place was heaving from the rafters with locals who knew a good deal when they saw one. The rooms were large and airy but our sons single room albeit very well presented had an awful view of the air conditioning units. On our second night we up graded to what they call the executive/honeymoon suite and for the extra £30 was well worth it. Great views of Largs through the windows, huge bedrooms that were well appointed and all mod cons. The bed was a king size and was so comfortable. The only thing missing from the room was a telephone. It had the flat screen and free standing cupboards and ward robes that were in keeping with the hotel. The bathroom was wonderful with all new accessories, a Jacuzzi bath, and an all around shower. The only down side is that the executive rooms were above their conference room come party room and you could here all of the noise from these rooms. If there is a party beneath you will have to endure the party until they finish. Might be worth a quick call to see if there are any party’s on during your stay. Overall this was an excellent stay and the hotel will be fantastic when finished. A big thank you to all of the staff who made our stay an excellent one!

author: miaNairn
title: An outstanding hotel
text: Just returned from Brisbane House and never before have I thought a hotel worthy of taking a few moments of my time to pass comment. . We found ourselves at Brisbane House at midnight, following a change of route from our own plans. Brisbane having one room left and grateful of it. As late as it was the receptionist gave us a warm welcome and insisted on leading us to our room on the second floor carrying our suitcase. A real YES person, nothing is too much. The following day the weather was too poor for paragliding on Arran and decided to spend that night at Brisbane again as it was such a treasure of a place. That night we dined in the restaurant and were amazed at the quality of the food, an eclectic range of taste and style and very good value. Second morning we were late for breakfast and immediately offered cereal and toast. Happy to accept as we were the ones that were late. Two minutes later without any prompting the waitress returned to say the chef was still there, we could have a cooked breakfast if we wished which we accepted. We noted that the staff were what made this hotel the best I've stayed in as they were always looking to make sure our stay was comfortable, putting the guest first. Something that all hotels and businesses in general strive to do but unfortunately rarely equal. We also noted that 'locals' were employed,most refreshing! The location is beautiful, the rooms well maintained and spacious. Now that we've found the place, will return to stay as we regularly go to Arran for paragliding.

author: BerryJ446
title: Slowly going down hill.
text: We have been staying at the Holiday Inn Express for at least 10 years. We thought it was the only good hotel in town and maybe it is one of the best of a poor group. First, the room had no coffee and one cup for coffee in the morning. I asked and was told, they do not put more than one cup and or coffee in each room since some travelers are single! You have to ask, she said. This not a normal occurrence in most hotels. When trying to find the front desk person, I found her on the phone watching TV in the breakfast lounge! She was not happy to get me the coffee or explain why it was missing. The room was clean. Outside the entrance there were used cups, food in containers, etc. when we arrived in the afternoon and it was still there the next morning. When asked for a street front room, we were given a back room facing the gravel bank. We stay here regularly an expect they would know we want a front facing room. (Once on the backside, we faced a load of caskets on a truck. Okay, that was just interesting luck.) We checked-out the Best Western Plus after this poor stay and think we will make the move. Our phone reservations direct to the hotel have also been challenging.

author: PamelaS3700
title: Great place!
text: Holiday Inn Express is a very nice, consistent, quality stay. The lobby looked and smelled clean. The room was clean and neat with plenty of room for my sister and me. The bathroom had a nice size counter for all of our things. There was a pool and and hot tub but since we were there only for one night we did not use them. Beds were comfortable and plenty of pillows to find the one most comfortable for me. We also had a refrigerator and microwave if we needed it. Our room was quiet. We were on the 3rd (top) floor so we did not hear upstairs neighbors but did not hear next door neighbors either. We requested to be far from the elevator so we did not hear to those sounds. Ice machine was near elevator so we did not its noise either. Check in and check out was swift and efficient. There is a restaurant next door easily accessible through interior doors so we did not need to go outside to get dinner. My only complaint is that the furnace/cooler is noisy. I had to keep it off at night to sleep.

author: nymetsfanz
title: Had a great experience.
text: Maybe our stay was an anomaly, but if other hotels would follow this one they would get so much more business. Room was HUGE with plenty of room for 5 of us. I couldn't believe how quiet it was..and the hotel was booked full. No doors, no one in hallway, no car noise. I read reviews about the truck stop across the street. First, it isn't directly across the street. Second, we were in the back and maybe that was a difference but we heard nothing all night. The beds were super comfortable. Plenty of linen and towels for our clan. They also figured out the breakfast options: omelettes, biscuits and gravy, pancakes, etc. Much better then most other hotels. And they have 1 person assigned to the breakfast so they can keep up with it and keep it clean. It isn't a front desk person doing 10 jobs at once. The only down side was the attached restaurant got no so great reviews so we left to eat dinner. There is a casino attached but you wouldn't know it staying in the hotel. Even in the lobby we heard and smelled nothing. I read these reviews again and again about the noise but seriously this was probably the quietest hotel I have EVER stayed at. This is our 4th hotel in the last 2 weeks and they ain't all been gems. I'm pretty critical of places I'm paying quite a bit of money for and I felt comfortable paying for this one. We would definitely recommend this hotel to others and will stay there again when passing through.

author: ChoctawCharli
title: Superior front desk, super clean, comfortable room!
text: Arriving at this hotel in severe pain after a bad fall at a previous hotel. I was greeted by a delightful front desk receptionist by the name of Liliana Mendez. She was sweet, kind, and EXTREMELY helpful. The service, the attractiveness and cleanliness of the lobby should have prepared me for the room. I had a standard double queen room. However, it was large, well appointed and the beds extremely comfortable. When I asked for an extra blanket, I got a QUILT! The toiletries provided are from Bath & Body! OH! And I don't want want to forget the little gift bag of a snack and bottle of water when I checked i as a Rewards member! I am a rare visitor to Nevada. But, this Holiday Inn in Winnimucca sure made it worth my time! Mexican restaurant (a few American sandwiches and a small kids menu) and small Casino are attatched. Coffee pot is a Keurig. Terrific water pressure in the shower!

author: 415nealb
title: Clean, efficient and friendly
text: I had never heard of Winnemucca, NV until recently. I'm still not entirely convinced how to pronounce it. But it is a friendly stop-- one of the only stops-- in the heart of Northern Nevada. This particular Holiday Inn Express fits the mold: the branding is everywhere. The front staff is very chipper (they even called before bedtime to ask if I needed anything). As members of the points program, we were treated to little baggies with chips and bottled waters. My kids used and loved the pool and hot tub. The hot tub was certainly "hot"-- with several patrons remarking that the temperature was surprisingly high. They have the usual diverse options in their FREE breakfast. I was impressed at the organization of said breakfast area. Even the sugar packets were filed neatly. As for nitpicks: no human could fit in the chairs as they are staged at the desk in your room. You have to wiggle the chair out if you want to sit and type a review of said hotel. The outlets that part of the nightstand come with 2 plug-ins and 2 usb plug-ins. I was quite excited when I saw this, since I have a lot of devices to charge. The usb plug-ins flat-out don't work. And the regular plug-ins are so "worn" that your devices won't stay plugged-in. We're getting way in the weeds-- but some might wonder why I didn't fill-in the 5th bubble. Overall a very nice compliment to the Holiday Inn Express cadre of hotels.

author: spacegrover
title: vomit in the pool-disappointed and disgusted
text: I am at this moment making reservations to pass through Winnemucca again very soon. I wanted to take this opportunity to leave a review I meant to do (and should have done) 6 months ago when my family stayed at the Holiday Inn Express Winnemucca. We have chosen this hotel several times in the past because the indoor pool is ideal for letting our young kids get some exercise after being in the car for 5 hours. In December when we arrived, I asked about the pool hours (we were checking in at 8pm) and was informed by the front desk that the pool was closed as someone had just vomited in it. They were now waiting as they had just called someone to come empty and clean the pool. We were disappointed and grossed out but glad that they were addressing this health and sanitation issue correctly. The next morning at 7am there were children and people swimming in the pool. I asked the front desk how it's possible to drain, clean, refill and re-heat the pool in 11 hours. The girl at the desk said she didn't know, she had not even been told that someone had vomited in the pool and she went on duty last night. She looked in the window at the pool and said that it looked alright. I ask to speak with the manager. The front desk clerk said that all the staff had been at the company Christmas (or New Years Eve party- I can't remember which), last night and she didn't think her boss would be happy about being woken up so early. She called and the supervisor didn't seem to have any information to add to explain it. She was apologetic and gave a significant discount on the room for the night, which was appreciated, but didn't correct or explain the problem. I know mistakes can be made, and nobody is perfect but when you are dealing with allowing unsuspecting children and adults get into a pool that has had vomit in it you are possibly compromising the health and safety of your guests. Ultimately I have no trust that this Holiday Inn Express has it's guests best interests in mind. I will not be staying here again for this reason. I will now go make my reservation at another hotel.

author: StaceyQM
title: over priced
text: In a word, adequate. This was the 3rd Holiday Inn we stayed at in as many days and it was interesting to see the changes. Pros- Nice, helpful staff. Acceptable hot breakfast Nice pool and hot tub. Nice, comfy Bed linens Clean bathroom. CONS- not so comfortable beds that really sway and wobble as any one moves around. very spotty wifi that requires repeated loggin in. You could feel people walking by the room. LIterlly the bed would sway as someone passed by. Odd. Very noisy AC. We were fortunate that we had no loud neighbors but I can easily see how this would be a noisy hotel. Vending machine on third floor did not work. Had to go to lobby for next one. It was the most expensive hotel in the small road town but I'm not sure it was worth it. I felt bit ripped off by the price considering the HI we stayed at the night before was $10 cheaper and worlds better. There are other, typical cheaper choices in the town. If I were to stay again I think I would investigate them more carefully.

author: 441duanem
title: Hope Marriott will come to town!
text: Winnemucca is the only decent stop enroute from southern OR wine country to SLC. We chose this over the Candlewood because of the pool and gym. Both were filthy w/ cans and bottles in the gym along w/ sticky seats and handles/mirrors/windows. The pool is inside but had dried bird poop on the table along with fresh grape soda rings and feces under a chair. When notifying the holding company (Hilton Honors,)the next morning - after requesting a quiet room and getting one across from the elevator, then changed to across from the ice machine and right next to the off ramp where trucks throttled down all night, having to get key cards 3 times as the first two did not work, on follow-up, I was told the case was closed as I had not ask for a refund!? I asked to re-open the case since I was still receiving "How was your stay" and closing bill information from this hotel. No deal. Customer relations goes no higher than hitting their internal buttons to fob a customer off. To top this one off: the hotel replied that we argued about the amount of the stay as we checked in. In fact, we had called the hotel to ensure our quiet room and let them know our 4pm arrival would be delayed a bit due to a severe storm. The rate eat check in was the same as our confirmation and we were greeted with the customary bottles and peanuts shoved in to a sack. So this hotel lied(s) about guests!! Really! Not staying at another HIE - ever. Marriott never disappoints. -Stay in approx. 60 hotel rooms each summer but never a Holiday Inn Express again

author: Washed
title: Solid Good Place, Could Use Some Polishing
text: So, Winnemucca is a small town with just a few choices, relatively speaking, this is a good pick. No bed bugs, or major flaws. The free breakfast is quite passable. I do recommend the cinnamon rolls, as others have, I recommend them to my wife too, but when went down together with over an hour of breakfast time to go, and they were out with no more coming! The mini omelets are usually good, but in this case the cheese tasted too phony, plasticy. The executive suite we got was good sized, with actually an OK view. It works. However the cable is like they are stealing it from the neighbors! I even made sure the connection was tight, didn't help, most channels were washed out and bad looking. The WiFi however worked great, so that helped balance that out. The young lady at the front desk was very pleasant, even at our 11pm check in, and the lemon water is a nice touch. The place is spendy, the AAA discount did seem to be the best deal if you can do that. One easy fix the hotel should make--clean or replace those luggage carts! The carpet is really dirty, though the carts work well, either replace that carpet or give it a good scrubbing. That's part of the first impression, also, thanks for having them, but please clean!

author: Cococath
title: Great Expectations, Lousy results
text: My husband and I are travelling across country and stayed at another Holiday Inn Express in another state. It was a wonderful motel so we were looking forward to staying here. I should have known this one would be bad news when I saw a small suitcase in the lobby with a sign attached to it which read " give us a 10 and win this bag!" They must know how poorly this place is run. We have to flush the toilet three times every time we use it. The TV is supposed to have 20 channels but only four come in. The internet goes out every five minutes and all the front desk can do is restart it so that it works for three minutes. We can hear everyone walking down the hall. The air conditioner doesn't work right. The room is clean but dumpy. The decor belongs in a far away decade. The restaurant gives you a lot of food but the food is awful. The vending machines are sold out of everything. The supposed pet-friendly motel has no place outside for pets to relieve themselves. I cannot wait to check out and will never be back. All this for a mere $160 per night. Holiday Inn should be ashamed, their reputation is much better. If you need to stay in Winnemucca, go anywhere else and spend less.

author: Eddie114
title: Won't stay here again.
text: Well let's see. Have to book a room with these guys. Had to repeat my information to the guy 10 different times over the phone. Took me a hour to book a room. When I got there the lady that was working then. Didn't have any customer service at all. Rude. My stuff still wasnt in the computer right at all. I'm a rewards member and gave her my card. Along with my credit card. When it was all said and done asked if my membership number was on there. She said no. Well what was the point of me giving you my card if you aren't going to look are put it on it. Also the guy ahead of me is a reward member also. She made sure he got his reward stuff when checking in. But sure forgot to make sure I got mine after checking in. Also the beds wasn't that comfortable at all.

author: Funfuninthesun
title: An ok... but might be one of the "best" hotels in town
text: We stayed one night in this hotel on our way out to Montana. We did some research on Trip advisor before we left, and it looked like this was one of the nicer hotels in town. The outside is clean and the lobby was clean and over looked the pool. There was only one person behind the desk to check us in. We were the only ones at checked in at this time... but as we were making trips out to the car... the line grew and grew. The room was clean and had a good size fridge. The mattresses were comfortable, however the pillows were marked “ Hard / Soft “... but every pillow case had the same type of pillow in it... so it defeated the purpose. The bathroom was average. They have an indoor pool and hot tub. They both were nice One thing we noticed all night… was that this is a pet friendly hotel, which we understand pets need a place to sleep too. But some of the dogs barked all night. After being in the car all day and then having another long day in the car the next day… the last thing you want is to hear dogs barking all night. The amount of $$ we paid a night for this place, was a little steep. We stayed at a few other places along our trip and got much more for less $$$

author: 4ChristinaD
title: Very nice accomodations, could be upkept better.
text: We stayed one night at the Holiday Inn Express in Winnemucca, Nevada for one night. The hotel was very nice for the most part. The woman at the front desk was very nice and helpful with whatever we needed. We stayed in one of their double queen suites. It was extreamly spacious! The quality of everything was really well chosen and well placed. However, the sink on the livingroom counter did not work and the extra blanket in the closet for the pull out couch had someblood stains. I have to add that it looked like it had been washed but that the stains had not come out. So, with that said, I wasn't too bothered by it. The staff replaced it right away. The breakfast in the morning was very good. Like I said, the quality of things were good. The only real down side was the crime rate and the price. It is very conveniently located, but you cannot forget to lock your car because things have happened there. Once again, the price was a bit outrageous, but all-in-all, a nice place.

author: hepb
title: Fine for a stop over
text: Arriving at the hotel you find a standard, reletively new looking hotel. Go into reception and you feel a little like you've come into the workers entrance. Basic and badly designed. The staff are pleasent and quickly gave us the room. The room was not good, it felt tired, a little shabby and through the thin wall was a screaming child. We went back to reception and, mainly using the screaming child as an excuse, got moved to an upstairs room. This was much better. A standard hotel room which was perfectly fine for an overnight stop. Clean and quiet, facing the back away from the carpark. Next morning I planned to go elsewhere as therebwas a complimentary breakfast, but in a small bit of a room just round from reception. However it was free so I gave it a look. What a pleasent surprise! A full selection of cooked food, an automatic pancake maker, a fridge full of goodies including yoghurts and milks, and as much tea or coffee as you. We enjoyed it a lot. So, not special, but good value, entirely what you need (providing you get the right room) and a very good complimentary breakfast. We arrived too late and left too early to try the pool, but many families seemed to be enjoying it.

author: Maricara
title: Not up to the HIE standard
text: This hotel was not at all what we expected for HIE. I'll start with what was good-- the room had a microwave and refrigerator. Check in was smooth and easy. The bed was comfortable. That is about all I can come up with- now for the bad. From the outside, this hotel looks fairly new, but once inside our room it was clear that it was a cosmetic touch up on the exterior. The room was small, dated and dingy. While some furniture was new- it felt chintzy. The microwave overheated, the toilet wouldn't properly flush, the AC unit belted out smokey smelling heat at one point, the noise on our ceiling from the 3rd floor was irritating. The worst part was the noise outside-- there was a constant engine revving or racing noise all night long. Even with windows closed it was disturbing. The WIFI was nearly non-existent- it took 5 mn to load a page. The room felt unclean-- I was worried about bugs and didn't go barefoot on the carpet. This was our most expensive hotel on a cross country trip (over 160 per night) and not worth it at all. We haven't had breakfast yet- but I'm not anticipating a great experience based on the small size of the dining area. An additional note- this hotel is attached to a casino and Mexican restaurant. Can't wait to check out!

author: lulubelle0
title: Disappointing
text: First let me state that we took a three week driving holiday and travelled 9000. km. So we stayed in our share of Holiday Inn Express Hotels. Most of them were just great. This one was the worst. We waited 20 minutes to check in, because there was only one person working and she was already with a custormer together with the fact that her telephone keep ringing and she was answering it as well. Secondly the hotel is suppose to be smoke free, but the first room we got stank of smoke, so we requested another. Thirdly no towels at the pool. We told the front desk person and she informed us that none were available as they needed to be washed. ??? So that afternoon, in the evening and in the morning before we left, no pool towels. Fourth the breakfast bar is below usually Holiday Inn standards. They dont' have any proper space so all the tables are all jammed together. In the morning your bumping elbows with the other guest. Finally and ironincally it was the most expensive Holiday Inn we stayed in between North Dakota and California. Maybe because you're in Nevada and there is not many cities.

author: sybilgirl
title: Dirrrty!!!!!
text: We had stayed at this hotel a year ago and it was okay at that time...not great, but okay. This time it was disgusting. I pulled back the bed spread and there was a bug there. The blanket was grossly dirty with "some kind" of crusty stains. Yuck! Our feet were black from walking on the carpets in the room. There were cobwebs in the stairwells and the stairs themselves looked like they hadn't been vacuumed in a week. The desk girl was worthless. She did not seem either surprised or sorry that the bedding was dirty. She said that there wasn't anything she could do because there was no clean bedding. When she didn't have customers, she was on the internet available for guests. Will never stay here again...and this is the most expensive of the Winnemucca hotels! Definitely not worth the money. Also, my husband either got food poisoning from their breakfast or from the Basque Restaurant at the Martin Inn. Beware!

author: latrecel2018
title: A very beautiful hotel in a central location
text: Pros: •the island has the most beautiful beaches I’ve seen in my life!! •The hotel is situated on the ocean! •there’s a restaurant/bar on the premises. •The staff was extremely friendly (Tearsa was my favorite). •We rented an entire apartment. The apartment was spacious, clean and had updated everything. •The location was in walking distance to downtown and 10 minute drive from Mambo beach. •Staff arranged transportation and arranged a rental car pick up. •there’s a pharmacy in walking distance and restaurants all around. •WiFi was good. •my room had an apartment with a view of the city in front and a gorgeous ocean view from the veranda. Cons: •the neighborhood doesn’t feel the safest at night (however there is a security guard that sits outside the resort until about 2am). •Food wasn’t the greatest in Curacao overall. •The hotel menu was super limited. •The hotel room doesnt contain a phone. •There’s a pool at the hotel but i think the limited water supply in the country prohibits the use of the pool because it was blocked off. •The taxi cab rates were expensive. You’re better off renting a car.

author: Pig47
title: Wonderful place to stay
text: This is a very lovely, comfortable and pleasant small hotel. Our room was spacious with a private balcony. The room and the entire hotel are kept exceptionally clean. When the windows were open there was a lovely breeze in our light, sunny room. The restaurant is on the ocean so we ate breakfast outside looking at the sea. The food in the restaurant was excellent with good variety. They even made modifications to meals when requested. The location of Bij Blauw is perfect, easy walking distance to shopping, restaurants and interesting sites. The best part of Bij Blauw is the staff. Everyone is friendly, helpful and cheerful. They offer a welcome introduction with information and maps. They are helpful in arranging tours, taxis and walking directions. Everyone on the staff was a delight to talk to. If I could give them more than 5 stars, I would. Excellent place to stay

author: Kedwardsmd
title: Just Nice Enough
text: Importantly, the staff was extremely kind and hard-working. Often there were female employees lifting their weight in luggage or buckets of water, always with a smile on their face. The only interaction we had that was somewhat puzzling was when we gave our feedback directly to the employee after asking how our stay was, to which he replied by blankly staring at my face and saying nothing. If it wasn't a hollow question, we probably wouldn't have bothered with the review. Being objective, staying here was actually a little frustrating. Most notably, for 6 nights here we barely slept because the "king bed" is actually two twins haphazardly jammed together, consequently I landed in the crevice between the two mattresses most of the time. None of the other rooms (there are 9 total), so we were stuck. From the time you walk in, you are a second-rate guest to the customers at the restaurant. THERE IS NO POOL, this shouldn't be advertised as such because you literally cannot use it (it is in the middle of the restaurant with no barrier or accessory chairs). Our waitress, who was the only unfriendly employee we encountered during our visit, laughed when we asked if anyone ever uses the pool. There is street parking, but this is also tedious as most of the spots are taken up by THE MENUS (it is as unnecessary as it sounds) for the restaurant. Your soundtrack in your room is a seemingly impossible and endless chatter of silverware. We were aggressively referred to a car-rental place that was significantly more expensive than nearby Savannah Rental, which was easily in walking distance from the hotel. Finally, at all hours of the day (weekdays, weekends, days/nights) the staff inconveniently locks the front door, often even if they are sitting at the front desk. Walking underdressed through the eating area into a narrow side-door to the hotel grew annoying over time. It is a nice enough hotel if you need a clean/safe place to stay, but it certainly has no amenities you couldn't get elsewhere.

author: 31Tripper40
title: Value for money and delicious restaurant
text: We stayed recently one week at Bijblauw. When first arriving in Curaçao we were a bit disappointed - we had a sort of well organised and clean "Netherlands in the tropics" in mind but it is more like any other country in the tropics we have visited before. Having realised this Bijblauw stands out well. The location at Pietermaai is nice, but it still needs a lot of redecorating. Completely dilapidated houses stand next to nicely redecorated ones. Having said that Bijblauw is a nice example of what can be done. We had one of the small rooms which was just fine - during daytime you are out and about anyway - but we found the bathroom a bit smallish. Especially with a walk in shower water is sprayed everywhere in the cramped bathroom . Some kind of swing door would be a good idea. Air-conditioning and fan worked fine. Staff friendly but all of the young Dutch apprentice type: eager but sometimes lacking experience. Now the very best part for me is the food. We went out eating several times but we have to admit, Bijblauw was probably the best. Absolutely delicious. Not fatty but pure, genuine. We also liked the terrace and view, especially in the morning at breakfast. The Swimming pool is very small and appears to be more decorative than anything else. For us, the (small) rooms were absolutely value for money!

author: chinapple
title: Great location and welcoming energy
text: My friend and I had wonderful stay at BijBlauw! Our room was very clean, comfortable and charming. The staff is very friendly, helpful, and also proficient. Their dining area is outdoor, right next to the ocean, so it was amazing feeling during a breakfast every morning. The menu is very simple but food is so fresh and delightful. I really enjoyed perfect flaky croissant, yogurt, granola, fruits and a great cup of coffee with ocean breeze. Our waiter at morning, he was very sweet and wonderful! This is great location. We could walk to The downtown, museums, and local restaurants within 10 minutes! Additionally, It was my birthday as our last day at Bibjlauw. All of the staff remembered my birthday. They decorated our dinner table very pretty, and surprised me twice with delicious dessert and candles for a breakfast and a dinner! They are absolutely lovely people, and they made my trip very special. Thank you so much, Bibjlauw!! I would love to come back again :))

author: Chit0wnTransplant
title: Excellent stay at BijBlauw!
text: In planning my second trip to Curaçao for a week of shore diving, I researched different hotel options and considered booking again with one of the larger hotels on the east side of the island. However, I wanted to have a different experience this time and decided against. BijBlauw came up in search results as one of the higher rated hotels, so I considered it further. I had a favorable impression Pietermaai from my last visit: its distinct architecture, seaside views, excellent location with great dining and shopping options, and Punda only a short walk away. In addition to location, I selected BijBlauw because of its small size, positive TripAdvisor reviews, and relative cost when compared to similar options in Pietermaai. While I expected a comfortable stay, I was impressed with the level of service and attention I received from all staff, the thoughtful room features, and the overall ambience of the hotel. The hotel staff were all friendly and hospitable, taking time to ensure I was enjoying my stay and offering any assistance needed to ensure my holiday was as worry-free as possible. In particular, Nina and Amber went above and beyond to help resolve a baggage issue I experienced with the airline upon arrival to Curaçao, communicating with local airline staff to coordinate transport of my bag when it finally arrived to the island and helping me to find locally any needed items in the interim. I am grateful for their assistance early on to ensure my trip moved forward as planned. My room was quite spacious, quiet, clean, and comfortable. The design was soothing, yet unexpected. I appreciated the temperature-controlled air conditioning, rain shower, and sleep-inducing bed after a day of diving. The excellent food at the hotel restaurant was a real bonus (more on that in a separate review). The reliable wifi helped me to keep in touch with friends and family during my trip without using my mobile data plan. Even with all of the amenities, the staff made my stay special and memorable. I routinely observed any one of them tending to the needs of other guests, and appreciated the team effort demonstrated by all. I've stayed in boutique hotels around the world, and my experience at BijBlauw is among the top. Thank you to all of the staff. I look forward to seeing you again, soon!

author: EU4
title: Beautiful Boutique Hotel, perfectly placed
text: We chose to divide our trip to Curacao between staying at a boutique hotel: BijBlauw and another resort hotel. Bijblauw consists of two historic houses with a large sea view terrace behind. We were recommended a 'Comfortable Small' room on the ground floor as my wife has mobility issues. While not an 'accessible room' in the usual definition, it had a wet-room style shower. Step-free access is via the passageway leading to the restaurant terrace area, although the doorway is narrow and there is a single step in the corridor. Access to the bar and restaurant terrace is all step free, with plenty of space to manoeuvre a wheelchair. We were made very welcome by Nina and Amber upon our arrival, and were keen to ensure that we had all the help and everything we needed. Dining at BijBlauw all happens on the sea view terrace, where the service is attentive and friendly. The food is all freshly prepared and delicious. The restaurant is open to all so it may be prudent to book a table for dinner at busy times (Weekends). BijBlauw is situated in the up & coming area of Petermaai, which has many beautiful painted historic buildings. It is about 10 minutes walk from Punda - the heart of Willemstad and Nina very helpfully suggested a route to the centre along a route with a pavement/sidewalk (Nieuwestraat), which made pushing a wheelchair much easier. (Not all streets in Willemstad have pavements). The most impressive feature of this hotel is it's staff. Nothing was too much trouble and everyone did everything they could to make our stay perfect.

author: Candyplatz
title: An unexpected delight!
text: We stayed at BijBlauw because of an unexpected change in flights necessitated an overnight in Curacao. We chose it based on Trip Advisor ratings, and we were not misled. Very fun, interesting and beautiful little hotel. The seaside setting is lovely, the decor innovative and attractive and the staff as welcoming as possible. There were a few glitches with our stay, hence not a full five star rating but I'm confident that next time these will not be a problem. The restaurant was fabulous. Dinner was the best fish I have ever had in the Caribbean in 20 years, except for fresh tiny tuna just off the boat in Bonaire. Nothing beats that... Glitches: AM watchman was supposed to collect our bags and accompany us to front steps for taxi. That did not happen, and even the cab drive was surprised. We managed. The pins which hold the shutter slats closed were missing. So we couldn't close all the shuttered windows, which made it less private (we overlooked the restaurant and were at eye level with the neighboring balcony, which was not ideal). Pillows were large and hard. I am little, and prefer softer, smaller pillows. Good think I travel with my own. No blankets on beds, just sheets (very clean) and linen throws. I prefer blankets. But that might just be me!

author: jernej1000
title: Pre Christmas Relaxation
text: Before heading home to Europe for the holidays we decided to take a couple of days in Curacao. Read great things about BijBlauw and I have to say - the hotel, the staff and the restaurant exceed every single expectation. The room - we had the suite above the main entrance (room number 4) was awesome. Huge high ceilings. Amazing bed. Great rainfall shower head. A balcony where we would relax and drink wine. The staff - I have never encountered a friendlier staff. Whether working the front desk or the restaurant everyone was always smiling and genuinely happy to see you and help you out. The restaurant - the food was amazing. Loved breakfast the most. Nothing better than coffee (incredible coffee) a croisant and that view... perfect. The rest of the meals were just as great. Like everywhere else in Curacao they have amazing french fries. Like I said, the experience could not have been better and would immediately book it again should we ever take another trip to Curacao.

author: LoulaGod
title: Nothing too much trouble
text: We stayed for a few nights here in the heart of Pietermaii. Not knowing anything about the island before, we were happy with our choice. Several very good restaurants within walking distance in a topsy turvy world of chic, renovated historic buildings painted all colors of the rainbow and run-down buildings where the very poor huddle behind pinned up sheets. The chic people are winning out, with nearly every unoccupied building in the process of being converted to a hotel. Bij Blauw is owned by a Dutch family who are professional hoteliers. However, it is more a vocation than profession in their case, and they have the genial, outgoing personality to make them ideally suited for the role. No matter what we asked for, nothing was too much trouble. Butter? A big slab arrived in a glass dish. Tea? A whole selection on a piece of wood fashioned into a tray. With tourists revolving through this place like the ocean breeze, how wonderful that they seem genuinely interested in meeting new people and making them feel at home. The rooms are decorated very tastefully - think Robinson Crusoe with a subscription to House Beautiful. The overall effect is a boutique hotel in Amsterdam that just happens to have an open air restaurant with an ocean view. For those sensitive to noise, be sure to ask for a room upstairs since you can hear the clinking of dishes from the kitchen and the arrival of the morning cleaning staff if you are in the downstairs rooms. I hate noise, but somehow the fact that this felt like being in someone's home, it didn't worry me. It reminded me of being a child and hearing the activity of my parents once I had gone to bed. If you are more interested in rolling out of bed and onto the beach, then maybe a resort is better for you, but if you don't mind a more urban feel and appreciate a kind of Soho vibe you won't do better than Bij Blauw.

author: billd427
title: Perfect Honeymoon
text: Bijblauw provided my wife and I with a wonderful honeymoon. Unfortunately Hurricane Matthew had put a damper on part of the trip and for our safety we had to move rooms. That being said, we stayed or visited several of the hotel rooms and they’re all great! The owner, Ruud and his wife generously gave us a “Hurricane Survival” kit which included snacks and a couple cans of wine. Fortunately the Hurricane did not hit us and we got to camp out in the hotel and enjoy the delicious snacks. Ruud and his wife are fantastic and so is the rest of the staff that we met especially Diane and Diana. They were so helpful arranging activities and providing recommendations for the area and accommodating to all of our needs. They certainly went above and beyond for making our stay special. The hotel restaurant and bar is excellent. I had every cocktail on their cocktail menu and they were all great. We had breakfast there every morning and we did have dinner at the restaurant. The food was incredible. I had a cod dish with the native Curaçaoan funchi which was incredible. Breakfast was fantastic also. The only suggestion I would have for the breakfast is perhaps switch it up a little. The sweet and savory (pancakes and bacon) is fantastic but every other option on the breakfast menu seems like variants of bread, which was all delicious but mixing it around a little bit I think would improve the menu slightly. The location is also great! BijBlauw is a short walk away from downtown Willemstad and some cool bars in Petermaai. I love Curaçao and I’d definitely stay here again.

author: wilfly
title: Home Away from Home
text: I spent a week at the BijBlauw. My kids and I felt like we were at a home away from home. It was our first time traveling without my husband. We felt really safe and at ease. The staff assisted us daily with any questions we had about day trips. My ids practically lived in the pool. each day we were given a fresh jug of water to drink by the poolside. The pool is not heat but I think this is typical of most hotels on he island. The rooms were amazing this was my favorite part. Very quaint and beachy. I especially loved the curtains that the owner sewed from Linen. I loved the clothing in the store. A bit on the high end, however they offer a sale rack. Great safe location. Con If you like well seasoned and spicy food the food served is not for you. The restaurant has a live band some nights the downside to that the music kept me up and loud conversations when on late hours.

author: MariaNewport_NC
title: Poor hotel , good staff
text: When we talked over the phone with one of the receptionists , we were told we would have a room with a terrace . When we got there , he said it was a mistake . Our room was smelly (mildew ) , small , dark , no view and uncomfortable . It says it has a courtyard view , but actually you cannot open the windows because people walks to and from the restaurant by the courtyard . There was very limited space for your clothe . A kind of shelf so high that we had to use the chair to grab our clothe . In the bathroom , no curtain shower , 2 containers with hand soap and body wash , no shampoo , no facial soap , no space for your toiletries , and you have to be 6 feet tall to be able to see yourself in the mirror . They offered to upgrade us to a bigger room upstairs for extra $50 dollars a day ,but it was not worth it . I think this hotel maybe good for backpackers or young people who only want the room to sleep and don' to care about comfort . The only good thing about this hotel is the staff . They were really great , kind , friendly and very useful when my husband got sick . The restaurant is also nice , with water view and good food . The location is also very good , which was one of the main reasons we picked this hotel , at least with that we were not disappointed . So , if you don't care about a dark room with no view at all , but want good location, this is the right hotel. Renting a car is a must , so we were really sorry not to have booked a hotel in the west side of the island , a nice lighted and spacious room with a balcony facing the Caribbean Sea ,like many of the resorts offer .

author: 136sharonc
title: Perfectly located boutique hotel
text: We spent one week at Bijblauw and our room was located on the main floor, actually right on the open terrace. Noise was not an issue once we closed our windows. The hotel is perfectly located for a 5 minute walk into Punda and a block away from bars, restaurants and clubs. It is located in the re-gentrified area of Pietermaai, so there are some buildings still in ruin but that did not detract from the beauty of the area. We were also able to walk 35 mins to Mambo beach on a daily basis as part of our exercise routine. Parking could be an issue on nights when there is a lot of activity in the area, but the security guard, Peter, was nice enough to tell us two ladies when he thought a more secure park would become available, so we could scoot back out to move our car. The front staff, especially Marleen, Anneroes,Britt, Edward were very friendly and helpful. There was a water main break on the day we were going to a wedding so they called a nearby hotel to get us a room where we could shower and change. Luckily the water came back on in due time to get ready. The ambiance at the Bijblauw restaurant was excellent. The sound of the ocean crashing on the rocks and the view of the ocean while we dined was wonderful. Note: you do not need to be a guest at Bijblauw hotel to dine at the Bijblauw restaurant. The service at the restaurant does need some improvement (being used to North American style service) but we put that down to a need for training for one staff member. However, Jacqueline, who was one of our servers at the restaurant, was very attentive to our needs. The front staff, Marleen, Anneroos, Britt & Edward were all very friendly and helpful. There were a couple little issues here and there but those were promptly resolved. I intend to return to Curaçao for a visit and will stay at Bijblauw on my return.

author: Snana81
title: Our favorite spot on Curacao - our own terrace with a sunset view at BijBlauw!
text: We visited Curacao and Bonaire in November 2015 and started our Caribbean holiday at Hotel BijBlauw. Arriving at the hotel after long flights was lovely: we were shown around the Seaside Rendez-vous room with its own, huge, very private terrace (and a private entrance), received welcoming drinks and were able to admire the fabulous sunset before going for dinner at the hotel's own restaurant downstairs by the sea. Couldn't have had a more perfect start to our stay on Curacao! The best part of the Seaside Rendez-Vous room was definitely the terrace - wow! Not short from 30 m2, right next to the ocean with an unobstructed view, and perfectly secluded. A couple of times we ordered the BijBlauw breakfast from the restaurant downstairs, and it was brought to us on our own terrace (pure luxury). It costs about 30 $ (for two), but it's huge! Totally worth the money, the only problem being that one won't get hungry again for lunch time...! The room itself was very nicely furnished and beautiful. To be honest, we preferred Bonaire to Curacao, but that was probably partly due to the fact that in Curacao we mainly stayed in Pietermaai and rented a car for only one day. If it wasn't for BijBlauw, we might have been even a bit disappointed, but luckily the Seaside Rendez-vous was a perfect getaway for five days! When my boyfriend went diving with Scuba Lodge Divers a couple of times, I had no problems spending my time just reading and relaxing at the beautiful terrace. The room had a small fridge, which was very convenient for storing drinks and snacks. The service was super: the staff was very helpful with helping us rent a car, gave us restaurant tips and I head them arrange snorkeling trips to other guests. And all this with a smile :) The location was OK - within a walking distance from some of the restaurants, Queen Emma Pontoon Bridge and Handelskade. If you're staying on Curacao for longer than just a couple of days and actually want to see the island, renting a car is a must. If you just want to relax in beautiful and calm surroundings, have some wine and eat in nearby restaurants, BijBlauw is definitely the right place to stay. Pay some extra for the Seaside Rendez-vous room; it's totally worth it!

author: wmsc
title: Great Hotel, great restaurant
text: The staff here is awesome. They make sure every need is met. The facility is two old remodeled houses, one with most of the hotel rooms and the other with the concept store and one other room. Many of the rooms are small, we stayed in a larger one. With a portrait of Diderot staring at us, we settled into a large comfortable room. Unfortunately this room is at the front of the hotel. It is a very noisy room. Apparently riding around town on a noisy motorcycle, revving the engine to set off car alarms, is a national sport played in the Pietermaai section of Wilemstad. Additionally, during the remodel, in laying the upper floor, a 2" extra top step was created. It can be a little awkward to traverse going down what are steep stairs. There are no do not disturb signs and housekeeping comes at 10:00. One housekeeper seemed perturbed at the news we were sleeping in until 11:00 and rolled her eyes at the news of our plans. On the other hand did I mention the restaurant? It's fantastic! All the restaurants in Willemstad require a reservation, BijBlauw is no different, don't hesitate. If you like smaller hotels, with a staff who gets to know you, you will enjoy BijBlauw.

author: richardmL3078HQ
title: A boutique hotel...that will make you jealous!
text: I chose "BijBlauw" because of it's central location and excellent reviews. Prior to arriving I was concerned about the size of my comfortable small room since I needed a corner where I could set up a work area. The room with King size bed was more than large enough to accommodate my needs, had a perfect table and bench to function as a makeshift desk for my set-up and left enough space for me to exercise as well. Plenty of closet space for storage. A gorgeous bathroom with a single french door and a rain shower head to die for and many windows equipped with french shutters letting through that magnificent Caribbean light from the south west. BijBlauw is the epitome of a boutique hotel. The design is delightful, the colors, the lighting, everything is just right. The managing staff is friendly, attentive and concerned about your needs. The workers are helpful and accommodating. The hotel is immaculately clean. They have done a wonderful job in what once was a neglected and dilapidated old down-town area. I would consider "BijBlauw" a barometer for the on-going Willemstad renaissance. You don't have to look for authentic nightlife because you're already in it. But if you choose to step away from BijBlauw's cozy restaurant and bar you will find plenty of upscale restaurants and lounges along the coastline strip. Or just around the corner, "Miles", one of the coziest Jazz cafe's you'll ever set foot in. An 8 minute walk west will have you in the downtown heart of Punda on "het Koningin Wilhelmina Park". And the famed playa "Mambo Beach" is just an 10 minute straight-line drive away towards the east. And when you get back, park your car right in front of the Hotel, that easy! BijBlauw was an experience worth remembering and repeating.

author: Hanna_KIviniemi
title: Did not live up to our expectations
text: We read about BijBlauw on the internet before we decided and everything looked really nice and good reviews too, so we decided to book. The hotel has a good location if you like to be near the city and restaurants. It is located in a cool neigbourhood, right by the sea and has beautiful view, specially from the restaurant. But for closest beach and swimming you need to take the bus or car. The hotel is small and cosy and the staff are friendly and helpful. The managers swished by, but did not really make an impression. We stayed in a small cosy room on the second floor and it had an OK size and even a bit of seaview. The beds were comfortable for us (not too soft), but I guess that differs from person to person. There are a few details where the hotel could improve; put soap- and shampoo holders in the shower, fix the holes in the wall and put a full size mirror in the room, there was also lacking a hair dryer. So far so good....BUT our stay was made pretty uncomfortable by the small cockroaches that we found in our room. We spoke to the hotel staff about the problem and they asked us to pack our things and empty the room and then they cleaned it from top to bottom, but it didn't help. In a day they were back. This is not acceptable for a hotel of this standard. We were never offered to change rooms, neither did the staff ask if the problem was solved. They compensated us with a bottle of wine. Another thing to know is that the noise from the restaurant can be loud, so if you are a light sleeper that could be a problem.

author: activeboomeradv
title: Cozy room means cozy
text: This is a small boutique hotel that has very friendly service, comfortable beds and pillows. It is in an area of town that is still transitional, but we felt safe and we were able to easily walk to most places..including some nice nearby restaurants. “Downtown” is a short 10 minute walk. While the price was reasonable and the room clean, the rooms (they call them cozy) are very small and you risk running into the TV mounted on the wall on your way to the bathroom if you are not careful. We had a problem finding a place to put our 2 pieces of 22” luggage (one piece ended up in the bathroom). Don’t expect Kleenex or a hair dryer as this is a very basic place in terms of room amenities. They are ecologically friendly and put shampoo and conditioner in little open (and unlabeled) jars. I guess you are to use the shampoo as body soap as that was all there was. The nice rain shower (no tub) did not have any shelving to put any unlabeled jars for use in the shower. They do have an in-room espresso machine, a safe and refrigerator. While the wifi is free, we had issues trying to access any secured (https) site. Normal http sites were fine. The restaurant was very good, with service being a little slower than in other places we ate but remember you are on island time. The rooms could use more soundproofing but the hum from the air conditioner drowns out the noise from your neighbors. The air conditioner takes time to cool down the room and doesn’t feel like it cool it to the temperature you set it at. Still, once it does cool down, it keeps the humidity down and you can shut your windows to keep out the mosquitos. Between that and the overhead fan, you can sleep comfortably. While this is a good price/value place. You just need to know what you will be getting. And, you may want to upgrade to a larger room.

author: miri242
title: Stylish location & lovely staff contributed to great stay
text: BijBlauw is a boutique hotel in the trendy Pietermaai district. We've been staying in their big apartment, the "Yellow Brick Suite", for five days as part of our honeymoon in September 2014. The apartment is only nine months old and is in perfect condition. The decor is stylish and very modern, yet cozy with much attention to detail. The apartment also has a big terrace facing the patio and the sea which we enjoyed a lot. What we liked best at BijBlauw was the friendly atmosphere. The owner as well as everybody working there were extremely friendly and helpful and we felt very much "at home" from the minute we arrived until the late check-out (which we appreciated very much). We have also tried breakfast, lunch and dinner and thought that it was very good and fresh - it felt like it was made with love ;-). Prices are on European level. The situation in the Pietermaai district is great if you want to be within walking distance to the city (10 minutes). Also if you want to explore the island by car it is a good starting point (we rented a duck from "ducks united" and had a lot of fun with it). As Pietermaai is rather hip, there also is some nightlife nearby, especially on Fridays and Saturdays. And BijBlauw has its own restaurant. So this might be something to consider if you are a very light sleeper. Also if you are looking for your typical beach hotel, that it is not. While you can't be any closer to the sea (you can have your breakfast in the restaurant literally 50 centimeters from the water), there is no beach directly at the hotel. However, all the nice beaches are within comfortable driving distances. All in all I can highly recommend BijBlauw for travellers who like a boutique style hotel in a trendy location. Thanks to all the team who made our stay special.

author: Suzy737
title: Location!
text: I was pointed at BijBlauw by their neighbours Scuba Lodge who were fully booked during my stay. BijBlauw opened mid-December 2013 and therefore is brand new. The rooms are located in the green building, the apartment, shop and children's restaurant are located in the yellow building. It is located in Pietermaaij which is an upcoming neighbourhood with so much good restaurants that you can easily fill one week with another restaurant every day without having to walk more than 3 minutes. I think that that is a big plus of the area. I felt like being in a real Curacao area instead of the standard hotel areas. I stayed at BijBlauw for 5 nights and didn't need a car. You're at walking distance of Punda and Otrabanda and there is a bus stop in front of the guest house where you can take the bus to Jan Thiel and many other places at the Island. I traveled alone but felt very safe even in the dark as the restaurants and hotels in the Pietermaaij area have arranged for their our security guys. I stayed in the Rendez vous room which has the best view of all rooms. It has a big balcony with a wonderful sea view. You can see the cruise ships come and leave and have a nice sunset view as well. Wifi was working good. Because the guest house had recently opened after an extensive renovation my room was missing some details to make it meet its price (e.g. a large mirror, enough space to layout your suitcase, loungers on the terrace, a place to dry your swimsuit, amenities such as tissues and soap). Furthermore not all electricity holes in the wall were finished yet and the cleaning ladies obviously hadn't found here routine yet (bin not emptied one day, no toilet paper other day, no replacement of used cups). But the owners were around each day and confirmed me that they are working hard to finish all these details. They are so enthousiastic and nice and I'm sure they will make the house to a big success. I found breakfast overpriced so I only tried it once, but the restaurant is wonderful and has a nice ocean view. If you're travelling to Curacao and want to be in a central location with a hip feeling and a nice view, I would definately recommend BijBlauw.

author: Ronboy_EK
title: Excellent stay. Very friendly staff, super location, great food. We will return.
text: My wife and I stayed at the Dionysos Central Hotel in March 2019 as part of a 14 night package with Jet 2 Holidays. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay. From the outset, Valentina, Olga and Nadia on reception were a delight - extremely friendly, chatty and couldn't do enough for us. The restaurant staff were also very pleasant and efficient. The hotel suited us to a tee - not too big, nicely decorated with a good sized pool and sunbathing area. Our room was very comfortable. The hotel is one of the older hotels in Paphos and is in a great location - very handy for the promenade and harbour, supermarket, bars and restaurants. It lives up to its claim to be 'Central'. Our favourite eateries for lunch were the Grill Garage and Hondros Taverna - both within easy walking distance. The food, prepared by Executive Chef Pambi and his team, was buffet style with lots of choice - some dishes with a definite Cypriot cuisine, others general European style. We enjoyed all of our meals. The food was very tasty. Typically, at dinner, there would be soup, extensive salad bar, 5 main dishes plus a vegetarian option and a pasta option. Also a choice of desserts. One or more chefs would stand beside the buffet in case guests had any questions about the food. There was a small but adequate car park for our hire car. The layout of the hotel does involve steps, so not really suited to wheelchair users. We intend to return next year. Our room was overlooking a taverna which had traditional dancing several nights a week - this could be a little noisy. We would ask for a room with a sea view (more expensive) or pool view when returning to the hotel as these rooms are quieter.

author: 962sarahd
title: Christmas treat
text: Great hotel in a brilliant location. We felt well looked after from our first contact (I booked direct) until we left. We took the local bus from the airport which stops less than a 5 min walk away (if you don't miss it like we did) and cost 1.5 Euro each. The receptionists were friendly and smiley every time we passed. We only had a couple of queries and they answered these well. The room was a good size (deluxe 308) even with 3 adults in it. The main bed was huge and the extra was serviceable for an adult man. We didn't make full use of the extras (wine, fruit slippers etc) but they are a nice touch. We had no problem with storage as there is masses. The room was clean and stayed that way with daily service. The shower room was spacious and the water always hot and of good power. We did have an issue with wet floor as the screen isn't long and had to be aware that there was only a frosted glass door for the area. The other down side of the room was the small balcony and being at the back of the hotel but the weather wasn't really warm enough for this to be an issue we just sat by the pool when we were on site and it was warm enough. We stayed on a half board basis and the food was good for buffet provision. Plenty of choice and fresh. Restaurant staff were great especially Demetris, Mario and Sofia. There is a good amount of comfy chairs for sitting around in the evenings, too cool out in December. We hope to return.

author: scotos
title: November holiday
text: Arrived in Pathos on 31st October the last date of the season we were told on arrival. On arrival at Dionysas hotel we found that the kitchens were closed and there was no food available. Our room was in the newer part of the hotel and was modern. Our only comments were the glass door in the bathroom. No light on the balcony, The was a kettle etc but the power was at the other end of the room. On arrival the aircondition was working and needed as the temperture was in the 30s. By the weekend the air condition did not seem to work and when we ask we were told that as it was now November the air condtion was switched to a heater. The hotel is not suitable for people with mobility problems. There are varoius sets of short steps in reception. Reception looks very nice with variuos comfortable sofas and seats but especially at night it is very dark. The meals ar all buffet. The indoor area is very small but there is a larger outdoor area. Breakast was the same food everyday and the coffee machine made horrible coffee. We took the coffee from the room and asked for hot water..Evening meal looked good on the menu but unfortuately was usually tasteless. If you are vegitarian for get it. With the reception area and outside being ill lit where were a few falls requirng medical help.With one lady staying overnight in hospital after a fall There was no evening entertainment. We enjoyed our stay in Pathos but would not return to Dionysos Hotel

author: N3611EVjohnb
title: Don't do half board.
text: Positives - Great location. Great staff. Good size room & bathroom. Plenty of sunbeds. If you want to swap books they keep them behind the reception desk & the staff are very happy to get them out for you. Inside the hotel is very clean and tidy. Negatives - Awful food. Hot puddings had no custard, cream or ice-cream. Pancakes at breakfast had nothing to go with them. HAD to sit outside for evening meal (which started at 7pm) with stuff falling off the trees & loads of ants & cats about so go bitten a lot. We went half board but ate out most of the time. The pool had a steep bank/slope that was gravelly which scraped toes & knees. Small pool looked dirty. Rooms were dark. Balcony had no light so didn't bother sitting there and the 'garden' view just wasn't a view atall. There was nowhere to hang wet washing, swimwear etc. And the daftest thing of all is a glass, see-through bathroom door!

author: GoonerA
title: Great Hotel
text: Great hotel. We booked our holiday with only 4 weeks in advance and this was the only hotel available in the centre within our budget. I was a little worried before arriving as some of the reviews were a bit off. We arrived around 1130pm at night and had obviously missed dinner so the next morning were given a voucher for lunch. When we got into the room there was a bottle of complimentary wine (albeit a bit sour) and a bowl of fruit which was a lovely touch. The rooms were clean and up to date and the maids were great. We asked for a sea view room on the top floor prior to arrival and we were given this free of charge. There was always plenty of beds around the pool and it was never crowded in the pool so you could happily swim up and down. The only issue we had here was the food. We booked half board (breakfast and dinner) - we tried both once and was not impressed. There was not much choice and to be honest, everyone rushing to the buffet and filling plates and plates up was off putting so we ended up spending £500 more eating out. Other than the food, the hotel was amazing. The staff were always friendly and able to help and the rooms were great. Special thanks to the chap who is the night receptionist. He was always chatty and it was great to come home from a long day and see him happy. Ignore the other negative reviews on here. It’s a 3 Star Hotel and if it wasn’t for our disappointment with the food, I’d say it was a 4 Star. Will definitely recommend this hotel and we would definitely stay again. Location is perfect and for its location, hardly any noise. Thanks again for a great holiday!

author: juliecC5491YF
title: Friendly hotel in a great location
text: Brilliantly located right in the middle of Paphos resort area, surrounded by shops, bars and restaurants, two minutes walk to the coast, five to ten minutes walk to the archaeology park, thirty minutes to Tombs of the Kings ( or take a bus from the bus station nearby). We were in a deluxe garden view room, very clean, adequate size, comfortable double bed, newly refurbished shower room en suite. Nice touches such as dressing gowns and slippers and fruit and a bottle of wine on arrival. There is a safe (free), small fridge and a kettle, The wardrobe is on the small side and not many hangers, we bought some cheap plastic ones in Jumbo in the mall. Balcony with table and chairs, ours overlooked the garden, Small flat screen TV with only BBC World and Bloomberg business channel in English, no USB slot, The wifi was poor in the room for the first few days there, then was upgraded and certainly on the first floor where we were, worked well from that time onwards, It was always fine in the reception area. No entertainment at all in the hotel. There is a pool which is not enormous and may get congested in high season plus a kiddie pool, plenty of sunbeds and a nice little garden, (complete with the ubiquitous cats you find in Cyprus). The hotel does have a car park which is quite small and fills up also somewhat tight to manoeuvre, there is however free municipal car parking behind the church opposite which acts as overflow. We were half board, Breakfast is good, full English style cooked items, cold meats and cheese, pancakes and waffles, fruit salad, yoghurt, cereals, bread and jam, cake etc serve yourself buffet style.. Dinner we found to be fine despite some adverse reviews on here. The food was not fancy but wholesome and plentiful with lots of choice. Basically soup, a selection of salads, a carvery meat and several other hot choices, some Cypriot, some international, even shepherds pie and fish and chips. The hot desserts were usually the best on the dessert table,, bread and butter pudding, chocolate pudding, strudel, banana fritters etc, whilst the cakes and mousses tended to contain or be based on artificial cream or something tasting like Angel Delight. The menu tended to repeat itself on a weekly basis, You could order wine or beer but there was no problem in just ordering water at a nominal fee, Though there was a pasta choice most nights, there was not a real childrens menu. The dining room staff were lovely, friendly and really hard working and speedy, your plates just disappear as soon as you finish. In fact all the staff were really nice including the reception staff. All in all, this is a town centre hotel, not a resort style hotel, but really deserves more than its current 3 stars because of the friendliness of the staff and its fantastic location which could not be bettered,

author: getawaykent
title: Good Quality Hotel & a Very Efficient Team
text: My wife & myself have recently returned from a week's half board stay at the Dionysos! We chose the hotel because of its close proximity to the sea front which is less than a minute’s walk, & some of the more positive reviews we had read! My wife had emailed the hotel prior to our arrival & requested a high floor with a sunny balcony, & that is exactly what we were given. Our check in was very efficient as we were the only guests arriving on the Wednesday afternoon. Room Card, safe key, Fridge Key, TV Remote, Internet Log In Codes & a voucher for a complimentary drink in the La Place Royale Restaurant handed over in a couple of minutes. Reception staff throughout our stay were genuinely very friendly & always acknowledged our presence when in the hotel. We stayed in room 210 on the second floor at the rear to the hotel. Overlooking some foliage & the La Place Royale restaurant, our balcony was sunny up to around noon each day. The room was well appointed with twin beds, walk in shower, sufficient wardrobe & drawer space for our week's stay, safe deposit box, wall mounted TV, hair dryer and tea & coffee making facilities. Complimentary towelling robes, slippers, wine & fruit were awaiting our arrival. Improvement opportunities however would be the addition of hooks in the bathroom for the towelling robes & the provision of an electrical socket on or near the dressing table to plug the kettle in! As mentioned in other reviews the food at the Dionysos is described as average, but on the evenings we ate in, we were always able to find something that met our requirements, & there was always a Cypriot dish on the menu. In my opinion the price of wine was fine with a bottle of reasonable white wine priced between 13 & 14 euros. A carafe (litre) of house wine was 11.50 euros. Unfortunately the hotel was quiet during the week we stayed & as a result the restaurant lacked an atmosphere in the evenings, however they tried their best with the playing of some festive tunes on the sound system! There was always a very good selection of hot & cold food at breakfast, and the coffee & juice machines provided good quality drinks. The weather in Paphos during the week of our stay was excellent for the time of year & this added to our overall enjoyment, particularly as we were able to lay on the sunbeds around the pool area for a few hours on one of the days & relaxed on our balcony for several of the others. Overall we were impressed with the Dionysos & particularly the friendliness & efficiency of all the staff we met. Would we return to the Dionysos in the future; absolutely!

author: goatgirls
title: September Break
text: Arrived after delayed flight. Hotel clean and serviced well throughout the stay. Had booked a quiet garden view room to ensure we had a quiet stay but allocated a room opposite the bars. Noise on a couple of nights was awful. However, manager did try to address this appropriately and all in all it was fine and most of the time the noise had stopped by 12 Ish. Wi-if is poor though and I can't understand why all the bars and restaurants and bars have accessible free access where here you have to log on every time and only use if one at a time. Food at breakfast was good but would have liked so low fat options like low fat yoghurt etc. Coffee machine at breakfast not great and was also poor at the pool. Pool was great and always room to sit. However, sun loungers are not comfortable at all and need replacing really. Ended up going to the harbour and paying to use those instead. Staff were all really great. Attentive and kind and helpful and I couldn't fault them. I know some of this sounds negative but we had a great time and the hotel was generally good, just a couple of small niggles that have quick fixes that would elevate the experience. I would go again and it's so central and accessible.

author: bengi1623
title: Brilliant, relaxing and perfectly located. Ideal Hotel.
text: My wife and I have being staying at the Dionysos hotel for many years and I am not a little bit bias by giving this brilliant hotel a very good and truthful review. Over the years we have seen the changes to the hotel, by improving the bedrooms, the dining areas and other parts of the hotel. All of the changes are for the better of the guests , we have spoken to many new guests and return guests over the years and they all agree that the hotel is improving for the best. As other people have mentioned in there reviews, you arrive at the hotel and your check in is usually done in no time by the pleasant and very polite reception staff. On entering your room you are welcomed with a bottle of wine, a bowl of fruit and a dressing gown and slippers, for him and her. You would also have been given the keys to the fridge, the safe deposit box and a TV remote all free. The bathroom is very well equipped and spacious, clean towels are provided every day, ( remember to put them on the floor to be sure they get changed ) The maids are very polite and most of them do speak a little English but do like you to wish them a good morning in Greek ( Kalimera ) Overall, your room is very clean and spacious, you also have a reasonably sized balcony to just sit and have a drink or watch the world go by. One thing I will mention, is people ask , which area would I like my room to be in , well, I have stayed in most areas and find them all alright but you will pay more for a pool view, if that's what you want. Any noise from the surrounding areas can be usually blocked out by just closing your room balcony door. Once again, as other reviews have said, breakfast is very, very good, it would take to much time to mention everything available but you will enjoy your breakfast, believe me. The evening meals are also very, very good and I am sure that you will enjoy them as well, maybe with a few glasses of wine or a beer. The staff at breakfast, the pool bar and for your evening meal are all very pleasant and polite and will help you in any way they can. There is a front bar called the Cafe Royal , this is situated on the main road through Paphos and is part of the hotel. You can enter it from the hotel pool area or from the main road . The hotel is situated in a very good location, only a few minutes from many restaurants,bars, the beach and the harbour. In my opinion, you will not find a better 3 *** hotel in Paphos with so much to offer and with such a very helpful General manager,called Costas and his amazing staff. The manager and his staff have helped many people we have spoken to, enjoy their stay at the Dionysos by sorting their problems out in a very professional way and that makes a big difference. Each year we have gone back to the Dionysos, we have met a lot of old friends that have returned, simply because they have enjoyed their stay at the hotel. This must tell you something about this brilliant hotel, so don't hesitate ,give this hotel a try. My wife and I would like to say a big thank you to the General Manager , Costas and all his amazing staff for two wonderful weeks stay at the Dionysos Hotel.

author: borntotravel59
title: Nice Summer Break
text: Hotel very well situated in Paphos. Staff very friendly and helpful. Room ok with plenty of storage and a hospitality tray replenished daily. Air con and ceiling fan to stay cool. Found the bed mattress a bit on the firm side, took a couple of days to get used to it. Shower was brilliant with plenty of pressure and choice of standard shower head or rainforest head.Was a garden view room but could not see much of the said garden as the balcony looked on to a massive plant! Breakfast quite good with hot and/or continental. Evening meals were good although a bit repetitive, Pork and chicken etc, but with the salad/pasta buffet as well it made a good selection overall. The pool area and sun terrace were kept clean with plenty of loungers and parasols. The pool bar had reasonable selection of drinks but must point out that it is cashless, and if not AI, cost is signed against your room as is drinks at the evening meal. Room bill is paid on vacating. From the hotel it is a short stroll to the harbour passing plenty of restaurants and a few bars. Plenty to see out and about, we used the public transport which was efficient and cheap with friendly drivers as a bonus. The weather was very hot, August, just the right excuse to go for a drink. Would definitely think about a return visit.

author: EugeniAblogina
title: Blissful vacation spot
text: Having been to Dionysos 5 years ago, I was happy to find it as peaceful, relaxing and comfortable as I remembered it. Even better than that, I can see that the hotel is developing (the rooms and lobby areas have been redesigned since), while the staff remains very friendly and proactive, everyone operates very smoothly on all levels. I was made very welcome there. Initially, I had a Standard land-view Room 515, then a sea-view Room 205. Though some would say the initial room is somewhat oldish in style, I found it very lovely with all natural wooden handmade furniture and such cosy and homey atmosphere. Besides, it was never too hot or noisy in there, I could sleep with my balcony door open (that's a big bonus for light sleepers) and didn't have to use the air-conditioner at all since the temperature inside was comfortable even in the afternoon time (NB it was mid to late August, probably in July I would have had to). The other room I would characterise as a modern and spotless one (looks like it has recently been redecorated) with a gorgeous sea view (facing the pool area as well), it is equipped similarly but with some extras like a hospitality tray. Since I'm a tea-person I found an extra pleasure in having tea on my balcony. This being said, I found both rooms equally comfortable and nice.
