I always feel cheated when you are charged a fortune for cheap drinks in the mini-bar after paying so much already! I made good use of the free shuttle service, with awesome friendly drivers who know all the hot spots.. just let them know when you want to be picked up and they were there! What i especially loved was being able to feel as though i could spend all day in the hotel without having to leave. I used the spa there alot, and only went out really to get food (i wasn't a fan of the resto - very basic). I would have the music playing from my ipod in the background and be reading a magazine by the pool while i'd been abandoned by my boyfriend, who took off every day to Sanur for kitesurfing). From here we stayed in another similar set up hotel just down the road, which was alot more expensive - and other than having bigger private pool - i was far more impressed with the design, quiet, internet quality, staff and set up at Kayana. Would stay there again over anywhere else in Seminyak!

author: 241klarag
title: Romantic gem
text: Stayed for 4 nights in room 19 with my boyfriend. Gian met us at the train station and carried my bag to the guesthouse. As people have said there are quite a few steps to get to La Mala but we found that part of the charm! The town gets VERY busy during the day and it was lovely to be able to get away from it all :) Gian gave us a short tour of town on the way back from the train station which was very helpful. The room was spotlessly cleaned, towels and bed linen crisp and fresh. The room was cleaned and made up in a nice manner every day. The room was lovely, a little bit small but nice and minimalist decor (which we liked!) and the bathroom was super good, shower one of the best during our travels. The room is among other things equipped with a bottle opener and wine glasses so we bought some wine in town and enjoyed it on the wonderful patio/balcony that is shared between the rooms. We hardly never met anybody there, as it is a small guest house and people are busy exploring, but when we did it was lovely to have a chat with fellow travelers. I also did my short work-out in the balcony in the morning/evening and I can not think of a better place to work out! The balcony overlooks the ocean and is away from the noise of town, you can observe birds, boats and swimmers :) There are two places in town you can have breakfast at, which is included in the room. We liked the one by the Harbour (Bar Ananasso) for the views in the early morning but other one was also nice. If you are going to hike between towns we recommend to wake up early! It gets really hot during the day and trails also busy but if you are an early riser you will have the trails for you and without the heat. La Mala is highly recommended by us, we had lovely days there, thank you Gian and team!

author: T4516EIsusank
title: Exceeded our very high expectations! Book early!
text: We stayed here for two nights and arrived with very high expectations after reading reviews. Our expectations were exceeded! La Mala is beautiful - we were in room 20 and it was perfect. The entire property (4 rooms) and our room were incredibly clean, full of light, and fresh sea air (great windows for fresh air and good views)! Our room had coffee service for early morning. We bought wine at a cute shop in town and used the wine glasses and cork screw in our room to allow an enjoyable time on the terrace with our wine and incredible views. Generous breakfast included with your room at a cafe nearby La Mala - very convenient and delicious! We also ate at very good restaurants (recommended by Gian) and had fun watching the children play in the main plaza area. Nice touches throughout the room - good lighting, outlets, bathroom well appointed with clean, fluffy towels and nice toiletries. Great shower and very comfortable bed. Housekeeping services provided daily. The space is well-situated in Vernazza - right above the main village area. There are many steps, but not at all a deterrent to the stay. Gian is a great host - met us at the train station and carried our bags all the way to La Mala and again to the station when we had to leave. He is very responsive and gracious. We plan to return - we feel we found a little slice of paradise! Grazie, Gian!

author: jonchaley
title: Phenomenal view, some suggested improvements
text: I stayed in room 31 for 5 nights. The view looks exactly like the pictures. There are a few small issues, but great stay overall. Gian met us at the train station as promised and helped with the luggage both coming and going. You will want the help...it is a LOT of steps up to the room. He was very helpful during our stay with reservations/info, etc. The room is clean and quite spacious. You share a veranda with the other rooms, which was fine. It gave us a chance to meet some nice folks and enjoy a glass of wine as the sun went down. I would go again, but hope Gian reads this, as I would like to see hime continue in his success: >The room furnishings are a bit spartan for this price point. Un-cushioned chairs, hard bedding, very simple, uncomfortable couch >During a 2 or 3 night stay, I can understand not changing the sheets. But 5 nights? Yes, it is expected at least once. Again, high price point for this to be considered an extra frill. >Unlike other reviewers, I found the breakfast to be quite good at both of the locations Gian has arranged for. However, it is a long hike down the stairs to get to breakfast, and a long hike back up if, as we always do, you'd like to freshen up a bit before going out for the day. A better option for guests IMO would be something very simple out on the veranda...coffee/juice, and some croissants/fruit. Again, at this price point it's kind of expected. All that said, it was a pleasant experience, just hoping for some improvements.

author: rhinotsk63
title: Research Pays Off
text: Last summer we decided we wanted to return to the Cinque Terre. We had previously visited in 2008. After lengthy research mainly on Trip Advisor we decided to stay at La Mala for 3 nights. This proved to be an awesome choice. The booking process was relatively easy and Gian was prompt to respond by email. Upon arrival in Vernazza by train we called Gian and within 5 minutes he met us at the station and carried our bags up to our room and gave us a quick orientation to Vernazza. As many have mentioned there are quite a few stairs up to the room but that is just one of the many charms of La Mala. Once at the room you seem far removed from all the hustle and bustle of the town below. We stayed in Room 31 which has 2 windows which overlooked the sea. It was awesome to crack the windows at night and hear the sound of the ocean below. The hotel provides vouchers for breakfast for 2 different establishments, Blue Marlin, which is close to the train station and Ananasso Bar, which is on the harbor. We tried both of these and they both were very good. Having breakfast on the harbor before all the day trippers invade is highly recommended. Gian also helped us make a dinner reservation one evening which was very helpful. I hope to return to Vernazza again in the not too distant future and I will definitely stay at La Mala again!

author: 800marissas
title: Stop Looking and BOOK NOW!!
text: If you are still looking for a hotel in Vernazza, look no further. Seriously, this location was our favorite of our entire Italy trip. Gian is so professional and kind. He met us at the train station to help carry our bags up. There is no way you could find the place on your own. You can tell he has been in this business for awhile because he took care of everything and offered his cell phone just in case. The hotel is breathtaking and room 31 has unforgettable views over the communal balcony. The hotel has been owned since his grandfather and he takes great pride in his property. And it really shows. I can't say enough good things. Breakfast was included and we went to the Blue Marlin which was good. Gian is a LIFESAVER because the train station was not holding bags and we had to check out at 10:30 AM but were not leaving Vernazza until that afternoon. Normally they will hold them at the train station but since it was early March, they were not offering it yet. Gian offered to take care of them in his personal house for no charge! After our hike, he met us with the bags at the train station. Such a nice guy. Seriously, just book this hotel and you will not regret it.

author: valbar2015
title: Beautiful!
text: My husband and I arrived by train and Gian met us at the station to show us around and help with our bags. La Mala was one of the highlights of our trip. We stayed in room 26 which has views of the sea. The room actually consists of two rooms on two levels. The bottom level has a day bed, closet (with small frig) and private view of the sea. The top main level has two windows that look out over the terrace and sea. We loved the room and views however just be aware that you will need to keep the main windows covered for privacy since the terrace is shared by all the rooms. Since the other rooms were not occupied yet on our second day we took a peak at all the other rooms. Room 31 is probably the best because of the size and views but all the rooms (even those without views) are really very lovely. I would stay in any of them. Room 26 is best for more than 2 people due to the extra room on the second level. The other rooms also have more bathroom counter space. I really enjoyed the simplicity of the décor. With all our travel items strewn about who needs more clutter? Plus it's all about the views. Breakfast also comes with the room. 2 tickets are provided each morning to be used at one of two cafes. We enjoyed the Ananaso Café over the Blue Marlin. We highly recommend La Mala and would definitely stay here again. Great service, spotless, excellent!

author: 73edl
title: A nice stay
text: We had originally planned to stay in Monterosso, but our first choices were full. So, we decided to try La Mala. We ended up staying in two different rooms due to availability. It was a bit inconvenient, but everything worked out pretty well. The place is near the train station, and Gian met us there to help with luggage and show us around. Vernazza, like most of the towns in Cinque Terre are not that big, but we would not have ever found the place without him. But be prepared to walk up a lot of stairs. The rooms were very clean and comfortable. We started in room 19, which is a bit small but OK for two people. We moved to room 26 the next night, and this room was much larger. I would recommend rooms 26 or 31, if available. A small breakfast is included at two of the local cafes. Both are pretty basic but still pretty good to start the day. The view from the patio is beautiful, especially at sunset. We had a very nice but short stay, and we would definitely return.

author: AaronK782
title: La Mala! Listen up: Perfection!
text: So La Mala, where to even start... just stop reading now and see if they have a room for you while you are in Vernazza! I'm sure there are many nice places to stay in Vernazza, but none better than little La Mala... La Mala is 4 precious rooms perched atop one side of the town. The rooms are white and comfortable and clean and modern and just so... magical! The absolute BEST part of La Mala is the shared terrace overlooking the sea! seriously the terrace is to die for. We were at La Mala for three days two nights in August... this terrace has you situated right above the sea, overlooking the waves and the little hidden beach to the east of vernazza. Gian is an AMAZING host. Since La Mala is so small of course there is no staff to speak of and certainly no front desk like at a hotel... when you arrive Gian meets you and walks you up to his little establishment, shows you around. Very handsome (man crush) and charming. All you need to know is that at the end of our wonderful Italian vacation when i asked my wife 'what was your favorite part our our trip' she said 'the terrace at La Mala'! Enjoy!

author: carmenor5989
title: Beautiful stay in Vernazza
text: We booked room 20 at La Mala for our honeymoon, it was the only room available at the time (around 4 months prior to my stay). Gian was a great host and was easily contactable. He met us at the station and helped us with our luggage which was incredibly helpful with those steps in Vernazza! It was a short 5 minute walk to the station (if you don't have heavy luggage). It's not easy to find the hotel the first time round if not guided but it's pretty easy after that! The house is beautifully decorated and new, there is a flight of stairs to get to our room. Although there is no view in our room (we were aware of this when we booked), the room and bathroom were new, spacious and clean! There is adjustable aircon and safe in the room, mini bar can be a bit colder but overall the room was very very nice. There is a common terrace which is perfect to relax with a beautiful view of the ocean. Sound proofing is great from room to room. We had the chance to see room 31 which was amazing! It was very big and had the best view of the ocean! It was just above the terrace so can potentially be a bit noisy if the terrace is occupied. We will definitely try to book this room when we return next time (I heard this was booked almost a year in advance)! We also went to Riomaggiore and Manarola during our stay but loved Vernazza the most! We would highly recommend La Mala if you choose to stay in Vernazza!

author: jandmus
title: A Gem in Vernazza
text: My husband and I spent 3 nights at La Mala while visiting the Cinque Terre with friends. We stayed in room 20 with a great view of the tower in Vernazza. We were met at the train station by Gian who carried our bags up many steep stairs to the hotel. This in and of itself was worth the price of admission! If you have never been there, you can't possibly appreciate how steep and narrow the stairs are! The hotel was beautifully done in white on white. It was a great contrast to the vibrancy of the colors of the town of Vernazza. The room, although small was well laid out and comfortable. The bathroom was done in white marble with grey slate floors and a roomey shower by European standards. It had all the amenities. We loved the communal terrace over looking the sea for afternoon cocktails with friends. Although rooms 19 and 20 do not have a sea view, they do have the benefit of not looking into the terrace which provides privacy. I can't say enough about the service and friendliness of Gian and his mother. They made us feel like friends of the family! We would definitely recommend this hotel and would stay there again in a heartbeat! It's a 12 on a scale of one to ten.

author: Stena
title: Great stay at La Mala
text: Gian met us at the railway station and took us to La Mala. The hotel would be impossible to find amongst the winding streets and alleyways. The hotel is located some 70+ steps off the main square. The hotel (really 4 rooms) is perched on the top of the cliff. The outside communal terrace is stunning. Wonderful view (we had room 31) over the ocean and the terrace. It was lovely to lie in bed and listen to the ocean. Room was very spacious, very clean and modern - in fact we really liked it. Lovely crisp good quality linens and a comfortable bed. The bathroom had a rain shower and marble finish. The breakfast is served in two cafes - one which had no indoor seating (which was not good as the weather was poor) and another with a rude owner. So not great. Vernazza is a cute village, if a little overrun during the day with tourists. When the tourists depart (c. 5.30pm), the village returns to quiet peace.

author: C4397DEjenniferl
title: Please Stay Here!
text: I really wish I could just live here! Gian is the best host I've ever encountered! He met us at the train station and then walked us to the apartment. Unfortunately, we could only stay in Vernazza for 2 nights, but we are already planning out next trip back to Vernazza and we're definitely going to stay at Gian's place again. We stayed in Unit 19 and it had an amazing view of all the colorful homes and ocean. It is an immaculate unit, all new fixtures and very modern and white! They clean your room daily which is much appreciated. The area is close enough to everything walking distance, but far enough away to have some quiet time in the evenings. There is also a terrace that is available for everyone to use. Beautiful view of the ocean and castle. It's right off the cliff! Originally, we had booked a different room but because there was a storm coming in the next day, Gian bumped us up to a nicer room with a view so that we could enjoy our stay indoors. He was so accommodating and very easy to communicate with. He gave us restaurant suggestions, is quick at responding to texts, and his English is great! Gian's THE guy in Vernazza, he had a walkie talkie during the storm and was communicating with a bunch of other people to get the power back on, and as you roam around the town you constantly see Gian everywhere with a group of friends! He's like the go-to guy! You will not be disappointed if you stay here!

author: BabetteU2013
title: Love Love Love!
text: Ahhhh La Mala!.. My partner and I stayed in room 19 in September when we visited Vernazza and the Cinque Terre and we loved it! Gianni came to get our bags from the train station when we arrived and gave us a talking tour of the town on the way to the hotel. He settled us in and recommended some great restaurants for us to eat at. He was uber friendly and he was so casual that we instantly relaxed as well. Our room was amazingly clean, it was modern and it was comfortable. The bathroom had the best shower and the best water pressure I have ever had.. I wanted to stay in there all day.. and the terrace.. need I go on? the views.. the views.. the views... it was quiet and a great place to go for a wine and catch up with other guests in the evenings after days of hiking and sightseeing before going out for dinner. The servicing of the room during the visit was also particularly impressive; whoever serviced the room took care and the attention paid was the best I have seen. La Mala and Vernazza was one of the highlights of our Italian trip and I would definitely recommend. It is great value for money.

author: RobertY773
title: A little slice of paradise
text: Wonderful, quaint little place. I highly recommend it! First, it is in a great location, and in the great town of Vernazza. A reservation is a must. And while you are making a reservation for this place, be sure to make a reservation for dinner at Belforte. La Mala is small, white, simple, and a little reminiscent of Santorini, of all places. La Mala blends beautifully with the simple charm of Vernazza. We had room 19, and loved it. Ah, Gian, our host. Gian Baptiste to be exact, but just call him Gian. Why do I love him? Well, because he carried by 25 kg suitcase, and my wife's 25 kg suitcase from the Vernazza train station, up the steep stairs, to the lovely room 19 at La Mala. Thank you Gian! Grazie mille! We shall return here, and hope Gian is still here in 5 to 7 years, when we do return. Caio Gian, and do stay at La Mala! Oh, and travel much lighter then my wife and I. Bring more Euro's, and Less Clothes.

author: SOCIAWG
title: Very Nice Boutique Hotel
text: This is not a true B&B in that breakfast is not served in the residence. Guests are given tickets that they can use at two restaurants in Vernazza for breakfast, including the Blue Marlin. I would label La Mala as a boutique hotel with four rooms and is located near the town's harbor on the plaza. We stayed in Room 26. Room 26 is on two levels. The upper level consists of a bedroom with a queen bed and a modern bathroom (shower, sink, toilet and bidet). In the upper level are two windows with sea views. Down a flight of stairs, the lower level has a single bed, closet and small refrigerator. Unfortunately, the refrigerator was not working and, because of the five-day Easter holiday, it could not be repaired or replaced. The lower level also has a window that looks out on the sea. We opened the windows at night and feel asleep listening to the sounds of the surf hitting the cliff and beach below. Room 26 is suitable for three adults. La Mala has a common area patio overlooking the Mediterranean. The free wifi worked great in our room. A hot water pot and supplies for instant coffee and tea were in the room. La Mala is not for those who cannot climb stairs. There were approximately 75 relatively steep steps from the plaza to our room. Fortunately, upon arrival the owner met us at the train station and toted our two suitcases from the train station to the room and upon checking out, carried them back to the train station. Also, La Mala still accepts credit cards for payment.

author: dlr1953
title: Great Experience!
text: We stayed at La Mala for 3 nights the last week in September and loved it! John met us at the train station and carried our two heaviest pieces of luggage (50 lbs. each) up the steep, narrow staircase all at once! The four of us checked in the same time as another couple, but he took time to talk through details with each of us. We were in Room 31, which was amazing! Room 20 was nice but without much view. We discussed the best places to eat and John recommended 3 great places for us, each night in a different village. He made the reservations and each place gave us an excellent table. We ate at Belforte in Vernazza, Billy's in Manarola, and Miky's in Monterosso. There are lots of steps to La Mala but there are everywhere in Cinque Terre. I have back problems and the bed was a little hard for me, but I asked for extra pillows to help and had them in my room right away! We actually enjoyed the eggs and focaccia for breakfast at the Blue Marlin. They also made up a nice to go bag for us the morning we left as it was early (7:00). The other place was a bit of a problem because they told us that we could only have a pastry, but the other couple got savory focaccia and a pastry. So that needs to be worked out. Would definitely plan to stay here again.

author: 915katec
title: Best place we stayed in Italy!
text: What can I say that hasn't already been said? The La Mala is extraordinary. The majority of our trip through Italy was spent staying in modest accommodation, but I decided to splurge in Vernazza and stay in Room 31 of the La Mala - and I'm so glad I did. The decor and views from this room were incredible. The bathroom was spacious, modern and beautiful (the rain shower . . . heaven!). Our bags were taken up the (many) stairs to the room for us which was very much appreciated! The room was crisp white with amazing views of blue sky and ocean out the window. The La Mala is an excellent choice if you want to sit back and relax in your room, enjoying a sea breeze and a gelato. The township of Vernazza is delightful, particularly in the late afternoon after most of the day trippers have left. We were provided with some great suggestions for restaurants in the town and we weren't disappointed! We spent one day trekking between Vernazza, Monterosso and Corniglia and I felt we made the right choice staying in Vernazza as it wasn't too big or too small and had a particular charm about it. Staying at the La Mala made the stay absolute perfection.

author: AM-TOR
title: Lovely experience
text: We stayed for two nights in room 31 in March. The room is absolutely lovely with clean whites everywhere and a spectacular view of the sea. The room was spotless, spacious and welcoming. The bed was comfortable and the bathroom large, modern and pristine. This is likely the nicest place to stay in Vernazza...modern, clean and spacious. We also felt after visiting the four other towns that Vernazza was the nicest. Vernazza is quaint and has a special charm. The proprieter was very helpful. He met us at the train station, helped with luggage and helped orient us with the town, information on trails, restaurants, and even potential train delays on our departure day, etc...As we were coming during some rainy weather, he was proactive in contacting us prior to our arrival to note that the roads were closed and we had best come by train. Breakfast is available at one of three little bars each morning. Two serve only a pastry and beverages, one includes hot options. There are over a hundred steps to get up to La Mala which are to be expected in this sort of town. They were easy to navigate and not a bother. Though the prices may be a little higher versus other hotels, the quality and views are worth it. There is a terrace accessible by all guests which is perfect to share a few drinks while you watch the sun set. I would absolutely recommend to others and stay here again on our next visit.

author: Craiger9929
title: spectacular view
text: La Mala is a clean, modern plave to stay in Vernazza. Views from the terrace overlooking the Ligurian Sea are amazing. Good place to sit and have a vino rosso after it cooled off in the evening. Its tricky to find. Rooms were crisp and clean with modern furnishings. Bathrooms were nice. Rooms were of average size. AC worked great! Breakfast is included but not on site. You get to eat in a couple of restaurants in the town. Our only issue with La Mala was feeling rushed out the door as we were leaving on our last day. I didn't like the early check-out policy of 1030 am and they started cleaning rooms and making noise well before 8 am. Not conducive to sleeping in and having a quiet morning. Other than this operational hiccup, no other major issues with this property. Rooms are on the pricey side but you are paying for the terrace view and the modern rooms.

author: MLRobertson
title: Somewhat disappointing, given the price
text: Don't get me wrong, the rooms are beautiful and finished to a very high standard, but as a frequent traveller I've come to expect a lot, especially when putting down 160 Euros a night! On a couple of occasions we had cool/cold water from the shower. The first time it happened, I was already in the shower and battled through. The second time it happened, the water was freezing cold, so had to call the owner (I'll elaborate later...) to come and tend to the shower. He brought a gas canister, and 10 mins later the water was warm. However, the whole rigmarole took around 30 mins to sort - not ideal when you've just finished a 2-hour hike and are rushing out to catch one of the (infrequent) trains! Coming back to 'calling the owner'... I wasn't aware of this set-up; there is no reception or dining area in the 'hotel'. The 'hotel' is a series of rooms, with a terrace, and a phone to call the owner, should there be any problems. Breakfast is served in one of the cafes, on the square. This wasn't a problem at all - in fact the breakfast location is lovely! However, I was disappointed with breakfast only including: one glass of juice, one coffee, one focaccia and one brioche. Not a great amount given the room's pricetag. To top it off, on the first day, we weren't offered all of the breakfast items, and had to constantly ask for each one. The room and location is beautiful, but my main bug bear would be with the value for money: small amount of breakfast and hotwater for the price. NB. Vernazza was hit in a flash flood last October, and is currently undergoing refurb work. Be aware that it doesn't look like it did in the photos this time last year. Nonetheless, it's still beautiful.

author: pauline12325
title: A little place in Paradise
text: My husband and I stayed in La Mala for three nights. I had reviewed La Mala on Trip Advisor and decided to book as the reviews were very good. La Mala exceeded all our expectations. It was exactly as I expected and more. We rang the rooms when we arrived at the train station and the lovely owner was there to get us within 5 minutes, carried our luggage up several steep flights of steps...expect this if you go the the Cinque Terre!! and showed us our room. Well what can I say, our room was amazing. Beautiful clean white linen, shutter windows which opened out onto a terrace below with views of the ocean as far as the eye could see. We slept with the windows open every night and listened to the sea below...paradise. We were given breakfast vouchers with a choice of three different restaurants to choose from. We chose the one near the bay with the yellow umbrellas, great service and really good food. Everyday when we returned to our room it had been cleaned and tidied and was so detailed that we didn't want to move anything to spoil the effort taken by the cleaner. Honestly, this was the hightlight of our three weeks in Italy. La Mala Rooms are amazing, staff fabulous and the views to die for. The Cinque Terre is gorgeous, I cried when I had to leave our beautiful La Mala in Vernaza and will definately return again. Don't think about it, just book this amazing place, you won't be sorry.

author: janicetj
title: Hope to stay longer next time!
text: We spent two nights with friendsat La Mala in early October and it wasn't enough either to enjoy this lovely guest house, with its spectacular terrace, or to explore the nearby villages. If I had to do it over again I would certainly book at La Mala, but I would extend our stay by at least another night. Everything about the booking process was crisp, professional, and efficient. As we had reserved two rooms in January for a stay nine months later, I reconfirmed by e-mail a few weeks before our trip. Within three days or so Gian wrote back to say that the booking was reconfirmed. He met us at the train station as promised and was extremely helpful and informative (he helped us make reservations at Belforte, where we had one of the most memorable meals of our lives, and also recommended several other excellent restaurants in town). He works on the premises beginning at 10 a.m.every day, and is always reachable at other times by cell phone. We stayed in room 19 and our friends (another couple) in room 20. Of the two I would say that room 19 is the best - it's slightly larger, has a nice stone wall accent, has a slightly nicer bathroom, and has a really beautiful view that takes in the main street of the town, the village, the terraced hillside, and the church and harbor (complete with bobbing boats and waves crashing against the rocks). But of course all rooms have access to the very dramatic views from the terrace. The location of the guest house, above the harbor and close to the castle, is excellent, and after we had done it once we didn't find the twisting stairways up to it to be much of a problem. In the light of hindsight I would have allowed two days just to do the hike,which affords more incredible views. The route from Vernazza to Corniglia involves two hours of really strenuous climbing on narrow rocky paths, and the same is true of the route from Vernazza to Monterosso. Both paths were challenging for us (a yoga practitioner, a karate brown belt, and two four-mile-a-day runners). Trying to do both in the same day would be difficult and would allow little time to explore the villages themselves, which really are very charming. And you need time just to kick back and enjoy the lovely laidback lifestyle. All in all I have only the best to say about La Mala. We will certainly make it our home away from home if we have the good fortune to return to the Cinque Terre.

author: kmarie_711
title: Lovely hotel with an AMAZING (shared) terrace viewing the Mediterranean.
text: Yep, I hate to sway you, but I think this is probably the best hotel to stay at in Cinque Terre. The town is incredible and this hotel is modern, clean & lovely! La Mala is a gorgeous little hotel. It's not like 'hotels' like we're used to in the US with a front desk & staff on hand... you need to call them when you get there so they can come & open the place up for you & give you your key. It's more like renting a furnished, super clean one room apartment (without a kitchen). The guy who let us in was SUPER helpful, he gave us some vouchers to use for breakfast at a few restaurants around town. (we usually went to the Blue Marlin - food was really good & the staff was SO nice) The room itself is not huge, but it's SO clean. The sparse decor comes off as elegant and modern - and allows the color from the town & sea to flood into your windows. There is a shared terrace out back overlooking the Mediterranean. AMAZING panoramic views, we took probably 50 photos on that terrace alone. Getting to this hotel could be a bit tough for people that may have knee/leg/hip problems and have difficulty climbing stairs. (To be fair, individuals with those ailments may have a tough time in any Cinque Terre town...) It takes a LOT of stairs to get to this hotel & it's very confusing to find. We were fortunate enough to have some super friendly townspeople help us on our way - because we could not figure out the pay phones in town to make the appropriate call for the owners to let us in. (Totally our fault - and yes, I feel ridiculous for not realizing the dial tone is different in Italy!) All in all, a GREAT hotel. We WILL be visiting again! 5 stars all the way!

author: HoodedBanoonigan
title: Modern Room and Perfect Location outweigh Dud Service
text: This is all about a modern, clean room in a great location. If you are hoping for 5-star service and someone to roll out a kilometre of red carpet for you every time you leave your abode, my advice is to keep on looking. Here's what you need to know: 85 steps to your room, so prepare yourself for some quality thigh-blasting. Email correspondence before your arrival will be characterised by confusion, despair and profound regret in equal parts. But fear not, for all works out well in the end for those with the nerve to perservere. The staff at Vernazza train will station will call La Mala on your behalf when you first arrive, they will meet you at the station, and transport your luggage to your room. Check-out aside, this could be the last time you see your friends from La Mala, so make the most of it. The eating is very good in Vernazza and the locals friendly, so no need to ask for recommendations from La Mala nor have them make reservations for you (my advice is to stick to the restaurants identified as typical vernazzan cuisine and dont just go looking for the restaurant with the best seaview). Breakfast is off-site, good quality but limited range. Safe and bar fridge in room for those with something to hide. We stayed in Room 19. A clean, modern, white, well-lit affair, bedroom small but sufficient, generous bathroom, great view of town and of the inlet, private and tucked away, with shutters on the windows for those who like to touch things. The shared terrace offers a spectacular view of the ligurian sea. At night, a comfortable bed and quiet room await (quiet once the locals below retreat after a night of music and revellry). In short, La Mala was everything we expected (we didnt expect good service so were comfortable with what was offered).

author: 4willtravel
title: Loved it!
text: We stayed at La Mala with our two children (8, 11) at the end of July. Based on reviews below and the fact that there were 4 of us we booked room #31. It was so beautiful. Clean. A/C. Amazing view of the sea. We loved the shared balcony, although we never saw anyone else on it. Gian suggested Beleforte restaurant our first night. He called ahead and we were seated at the best table in the restaurant, on a terrace literally hanging over the ocean. Because we loved La Mala and Vernazza so much we wanted to stay an extra night and miraculously the room was available. Gian was terrific. He phoned ahead to location of our next stay to let them know we'd be coming one day later. Given the language differences I was very thankful that he made that call for us. He also helped us figure out the train schedule for our departure. Let us leave our bags in the hotel after we checked out so we could continue to sightsee before our train arrived. Every recommendation he made to us was terrific. I cannot recommend La Mala enough.

author: aeverett003
title: Fantastic!!
text: This was our favorite part of our 10 day trip to Italy!! Cinque Terre was amazing (especially Vernazza) and La Mala did not disappoint. This was not the most expensive place we stayed while in Italy, however, turned out to be our favorite. We called the guy when we got off of the train and he was there to pick us up within minutes. He carried all of our bags up flights and flights of stairs! When we got to our room it was clean, hip, and very comfortable. We quickly grabbed a bottle of wine and went out onto the deck overlooking the water. It was a "community" deck, which I had read about in reviews. I was a bit skeptical about it, however, it was not an issue at all. 2 times we were on it alone. Another time we met a really nice couple who we shared a bottle of wine with. It was so relaxing! If you are looking for a modern hotel with charm and wonderful views, I would highly recommend La Mala! We visited all of the towns and found Vernazza to be the most charming. We sat in the square and drank, ate, and people watched one afternoon. It was so much fun. We were so sad to leave La Mala and Cinque Terre. I almost talked my husband into extending our stay!

author: justkate8382
title: Fabulous location and view worth the splurge
text: We stayed in the amazing Room 26 (under room 31) and absolutely loved it! This room totally made our stay in Vernazza and was one of the highlights of our trip to Italy. Room was clean, well-lit and beautifully appointed in white. Room 26 also features a "below-decks" sitting room down a small flight of stairs and has a small, porthole window that looks out over the sea. I spend many happy hours reading and relaxing on the sofa down there, just staring out at the ocean. GianBa, son of the owner and manager of the property, was incredibly helpful when we first arrived in Vernazza. He came to the station to help with our bags and then gave us excellent recommendations for restaurants in Vernazza. There is no reception site at La Mala, so if you are NOT an independent traveler or require a lot of reception services, this place is not for you. One warning to potential guests: The terrace is shared by all guests at La Mala! Room 26 has windows that overlook the terrace and it may feel less "private" in the room while other folks are using the terrace. If you are using the terrace, be aware that folks in Room 31 and 26 can pretty much hear your every word if the windows are open. La Mala also has an agreement with one of the local bars in the main square to provide breakfast for their guests. Get the free cappuccino with your ticket, but skip the pastries at the bar. There are fresher ones at the bakery just up the street on the Via Roma. You'll have to pay for them, but it's worth it.

author: mpetersen74
title: Gorgeous room with a breathtaking view - perfect for a honeymoon!
text: For three nights of our honeymoon in September 2009, my husband and I splurged on La Mala's room 31 in Vernazza. While the hotel itself is clean and lovely, the room's view was hands-down spectacular. With a thunderstorm one night (a novelty to us native San Diegans), this was definitely worth the few-night splurge to us. (We stayed in more budget-minded rooms on the rest of our trip). While I'm not sure that I can add much to the many previous reviews for La Mala, I will share our experiences compared to those of other reviewers: * Breakfast: We did not receive juice with our breakfasts, but as coffee drinkers, we completely forgot that this was included. We did receive our foccaccia, pastry, and a capuccino without issue, though. I didn't find the folks at the bar to be particularly un-friendly, either. One tip, though: Skip the included breakfast at least one morning and treat yourself to the pastries up at Il Pirata--they're amazing. * La Mala staff: Giamba was friendly and helpful. He met us just below the train station and helped us with our bags. Other guests commented that they didn't see any staff after checking in. This was not our experience. Giamba told us when he'd be around and where he'd be, and when we did have questions, we always found him without a problem. * The stairs: Yes, there are a lot of stairs to get up to La Mala, but don't let that frighten you. We were prepared for a Duomo-esque hike after reading some of the reviews, but it really wasn't that bad. Many of the flights of stairs are broken up with walkways, so it's not like it's a constant climb. Our hike up four flights of stairs to reach the Bellevue House (in Florence) was more strenuous than this. *The towels: We actually liked the microfiber towels. They may have been thin, but they were very absorbent and did their job. In summary, this was a great place to spend a few days on our honeymoon, and we'd recommend it to others on a romantic vacation.

author: bel80
title: Stunning views in Room 31
text: We stayed in Cinque Terre for 2 nights, and chose Vernazza based on reviews of the area and of La Mala. And we were not wrong at all! The first thing we did when we stepped into Room 31 was admire the view. We couldn't believe how beautiful it was to see the sea outside our windows, or to hear the slight calming sound of the waves. The room was clean, very white, modern and simple. There was plenty of room for luggage, it had a sofa, a table with 2 chairs if you wanted to have breakfast there, a wardrobe, aircon and a flat screen tv. Sheets and blankets were very crisp and clean, as well as bath towels. They also provide you with slippers, a couple bottles of water and fruit juice. Only one thing to note is that there are ants in this region of Italy, you can't escape it, and you might be lucky and not see any. Also, make sure you shut the windows at night, as a lot of mosquitoes and bugs can and do come into the room at night. The location of the hotel is on top of the west side of Vernazza. You do need to go up a number of sets of stairs, as it is quite high up. So if you cannot walk, it may be a struggle. The good thing is that the owner of the B&B, Jamba, does greet you at the train/ferry to help you with the suitcases up the stairs. Vernazza really isn't that big, so it is in a really good position (5-10 min walk to train station, 5 min walk to ferry). Breakfast is provided at one of the cafes down in the piazza - you get a coffee, cold drink and pastry. In regards to restaurants, I would recommend Gambero Rossa and Belforte, owned by the same people, Belforte has amazing views at the tower, whereas Gambero Rossa has really good food (try the lemon marinated anchovies, it's a local dish, and the best we had at this restaurant).

author: gm7hj
title: a pleasant place to stay
text: My husband and I stayed at La Mala for three nights in May. We had been told to ring the owner when we arrived at the train station and he would help us with our bags - which we did and he arrived quickly and helped us up the stairs to La Mala. Our room was number 20 which didn't have an ocean view - which we new. It was extremely clean and very nice. We enjoyed sitting on the balcony overlooking the ocean in the late afternoon - the view is incredible. Apart from meeting the owner when he carried our rooms to La Mala and showing us our room we didn't see anyone who runs the place again. We contacted them to pay for our three nights accommodation and were told to leave the money in our room - we found this very strange. We had been very excited about staying at La Mala and felt a little disappointed mainly because: 1. We had chosen a B&B as it is nice to meet local people in a different country - this didn't happen as we basically didn't see the owners except for five minutes. 2. La Mala is extremely expensive and I don't know if the prices are really justified. 3. The breakfasts at the local cafe on the town square were very basic and the owners very unfriendly and obviously didn't want to give us the breakfast we were entitled to - we had to ask for each thing we were told we would get and it was begrudgingly given to us. I feel they are doing the owners of La Mala a big disservice. 4. On our last morning we had to leave early. We told the owner when we arrived and he just said we would have to miss breakfast then -we felt the decent thing for him to do would have been to have reduced the price of the room a little - this wasn't offered. All in all we enjoyed our stay at La Mala it just didn't quite meet our expectations.

author: lorelle71
title: Drawbacks When Staying at La Mala
text: My daughter and I stayed at La Mala in early April of 2009. The view was great and the room was very nice. However, no one so far has pointed out the drawbacks of La Mala. First of all there is no reception, so if you need something, you have to use a cell phone (do you have one with you in Europe?) to try to run down John, the young man who acts as a receptionist, but who is often down in the village hanging out with buddies. Secondly, since there is no reception, you have to eat breakfast down in the town at a bar. The bar owners are on their own time schedule and, even though they are supposed to open at 8:00 am, you may have to wait until 8:30 or later for them to arrive and begrudgingly offer up the scanty breakfast you qualify for. The service here is almost surly and lacking in friendliness. The owners seem tired, and burned out. The last day we stayed at La Mala, we spoke to John about the fact that our train to Genoa would leave shortly after 8:00 the next morning, and since we had paid for breakfast, could we get our breakfast served a little early. I mean, this is 8 o'clock and that is not early. He assured us, after calling the bar owners, that they would be there early and we would get our breakfast. Well, as we suspected, no one showed and we sat there for as long as we could, then raced off to catch our train. After we arrived home, I emailed John to get some kind of compensation for the breakfast we never got. He acted as if it was nothing ("the breakfast was just 9 Euros") and has not refunded our money thus far. La Mala is pricey (!) and certainly a decent breakfast needs to be assured, I would think. You may want to consider these drawbacks before booking a room at La Mala.

author: CaWino
title: Is This Heaven? No, It's La Mala
text: We stayed four days here in September 2008. La Mala is an excellent little B & B. It is very contemporary with white walls and accents. Clean, too. Breakfast, consisting of coffee and croissant, was provided in the bar at ground level. There as a very nice public terrace with a sea-view. The windows of our room looked out on to the terrace, and visa versa - See photo #5 - a little odd. Two of us stayed in room #26, which is their biggest. If I had it to do over again, I would pick a smaller room. #26 is intended for at least three people. It was a split level room. The upstairs had a double bed, TV, and bathroom. The downstairs had a single bed, closet, and frig with mini-bar. The mini-bar, stocked, with beer and mineral water, was free. The biggest downside was the trek up to La Mala - 69 grueling steps. The price of the room was more than other places. Jamba was the owner and a great guy - See last photo.

author: Renoir184
title: Great experience at La Mala
text: We recently stayed at La Mala in Vernazza and had an excellent stay. Despite the relatively high price of the rooms, our stay was very comfortable and we enjoyed the attention to detail. Like many of the accommodations in Vernazza and Cinque Terre, this is just a collection of bedrooms in town, so there is no front desk or anyone "on duty". We made a phone call, and someone magically arrived to take us to the room and explain everything. The rooms are decorated entirely in white, so the lines are very clean and modern. The bathrooms are adorned with the finest fixtures possible and everything is ultra clean and ultra modern. The beds are very comfortable and the views ... well, unparalleled. We stayed in Room 20 for the first night and then in Room 19 for the next two nights. Our preference likely was Room 20, but they are pretty much equally excellent. There were only two minor negatives to the stay ... the many stairs to climb at the end of a busy hiking day (pray that you don't forget anything in the morning and have to walk back up) and the checkout procedures which were basically nil. We happened to see the owner on the street as we were leaving and confirmed that we left the key in the room and that our credit card would be billed. Otherwise, we really weren't sure of the procedures. Despite these two very minor points, La Mala is a first-class place to stay in this tiny, enchanting and beautiful place on the Italian Riviera.

author: rainycity123
title: Magical...
text: Yes, Vernazza and the Cinque Terre is swarming with tourists, yes, the streets, trains and hiking trails are crowded, but to miss the magic of the Cinque Terre because of this would be unthinkable to me. La Mala was wonderfully clean, the view was amazing, the room small, but with all the amenities. We arrived in Vernazza very late because of a train strike in France (surprise!) and it was pouring rain and very dark, no-one around except two slightly scary looking young people huddled under cover. We approached them for help with the phone, and immediately they wanted to help. Yes, they knew Gianba, and within minutes, he was there, carrying our heavy cases up all those stairs, (unknown to him my husband was packing 8! bottles of wine in his case, but Gianba carried it up like a bag of groceries), and arranging for us to eat supper even though it was closing time. Nice intro. The Cinque Terre is amazingly beautiful. Staying in Vernazza was great, because the vast majority of the tourists would be gone by about 5 pm. We thought our meals of freshly made pasta and pesto, mussels cooked in wine and spices, and fresh fish were some of the best in Italy,enhanced by the cheap but good white wine. You will be privileged if you are there during a storm, because it's so impressive to watch the waves flying over the buildings, and crashing into the little harbor. And during the night in La Mala, you can maybe hear the waves just outside your window. You must at least hike the easy part of the trail, Via dell'Amore. The views are breathtaking. The memories, hopefully, forever.

author: theadventureseeker
title: The only place to stay in Cinque Terre!
text: What you see is what you get! The pictures on it's website don't lie....you get that and more. A contemporary, sparkling clean gem of an inn with great attention to detail located in the charming town of Vernazza. All this wrapped up in a traditional Ligurian house with a gorgeous stone terrace looking out to the sea. We loved our room #26....completely private with no adjoining walls (to the other rooms) and a bonus room downstairs (complete with daybed) and window in the stone wall that overlooked the sea. From our main room which had 3 large windows with crisp white roman shades that flooded the room with sunlight, you could crawl out the windows onto the terrace. The room and modern bathroom were both very spacious and all white which gave a nice backdrop to the azure sea and sky. The elements used in this inn spared no expense. The windows closed airtight for privacy and opened 2 ways (swung open and cracked open at the top) so you can hear the ocean at night. The bathroom fixtures and water pressure were excellent. We were given a tour by the owner Mama Giamba and all 4 rooms were just incredible with their own character...#19 & #20 were smaller, but boasted gorgeous views of the village. #31 was the largest of all and sat above #26 with 2 windows overlooking the sea and terrace below. A highlight is the breakfasts which are served in the charming Burgus Cafe' & bar on the harbor (a very short walk away). We enjoyed having our tea and freshly baked pastries in this gem of a arty filled cafe' complete with great tunes and design elements: teak, stone, glass. Vernazza was our absolute favorite of all Cinque Terre. Very picturesque and small. The locals were incredibly friendly. We loved our meals at Saldarno's, Da Piva's and Il Baretto. Stay for entertainment at Da Piva's (just below the stairs to La Mala) for a real treat of music with the locals. Yes, La Mala isn't the cheapest place in Cinque Terre, but you'll get your money's worth and more!

author: lanaimike
title: La Mala--Best stay of our entire trip!
text: My wife and I have just completed a five-night stay at La Mala, and we heartily recommend the property if your travels bring you to the Cinque Terre. We stayed in Room 31, and it was as wonderful as other posters have mentioned. The property is run by Armanda and her son, Gianba, who are extremely friendly--and La Mala has that same sense of welcoming. The room is "white-on-white"--not the typical "over the top with the heavy fabrics" style that we saw elsewhere in Italy--but a very clean, almost Scandanavian design with crisp bedding, hardwood floors, comfortable wooden chairs and a small couch. The bathroom was pristine and of ample size with a marble shower--great water pressure, too. The room measures aproximately 12'x18' (the outer wall angles in so it's not a perfect rectangle), and two large windows look out onto a terrace and the ocean below. The terrace has two cushioned benches and two cushioned cubes to sit on as you enjoy the view...and what a view it is! And as great as the vista is in the day, the moon reflecting on the water and the string of bobbing lights from the fishing boats at night was magical. Your morning will start at the cafe on the square next to the stairs leading up to La Mala. Guiliano will serve you slices of buttered focaccia, orange juice, a choice of pastries, and cappucini that put Starbucks to shame. And watching the regualrs come in and talk babytalk to Guiiano's daughter is guaranteed to put a smile on your face. Enjoy the quiet of the morning, because tourists flock into Vernazza throughout the day--but then at 5PM or so, the harbor area empties out, and the town is yours for the evening. One morning we talked to "Mama" (Armanda), Gianba, and the young architect who collaborated with them to renovate the property--you could tell they were proud of what they had accomplished, and they should be. Of all the places we stayed in Italy during our 3-week vacation (Hotel Splendide in Rome, Palazzo Sant'Angelo in Venice, Grand Continental in Siena, and Hotel Noblesse in Lucca), we agree that La Mala stands out as the only place we would book again without a moment's hesitation. I'm attaching photos of the Room 31, the bathroom, and a couple of views. The shot from the ferry shows the windows of Room 31 (with shutters above terrace) as well as those of Room 26. The window in the wall below the terrace is the small study of Room 26.

author: HawkaZulu
title: High Design, Immaculately Clean and new
text: Good: Wow. Beautiful, impeccably clean (and everything is white so you¹d know), and feels brand new in the midst of a very old place in the world. Breakfast vouchers (pastry/juice/cappuccino) at downstairs hip coffee bar was a great system. Perks like free beers, juice and water in your mini fridge that are included in the price... Amazing view from Room 19 (and the others I imagine). From the corner room (19), one double window opens to a wide city view on the mountainside in front of you, and you can hang your head out and see the harbor/water. On the other wall, the window gives a view of the castle (probably about 200 yards away?) and the sea on the other side of the town of Vernazza. Did I mention everything was clean and white and new? Try a musty room first if you want, but I felt like being spoiled at this point in my trip. Nice touches like glassed in marble shower with 8² wide high volume spraying showerhead/or euro wand style head. Bad: The high-tech modern building (automatic lights, smart chip in a card in your keys etc) were cool, but it had doors that were a bit thin. Footsteps/conversations in the hallway could be easily heard bouncing off the carpetless floors. Great place, well designed, WAY cool patio that I¹d love to hang out on during a warm night (a bit chilly when we were there). Their website IS reflective of what you¹ll find there. People who understand what Americans and/or sophisticates like when they travel and who are into a place with style. They even meet you at your train and help lug your bags up all the stairs to get to the room

author: I_Tarabishi
title: Amazing Geographical Spot & Smart Management
text: Actually we have thousands or millions of beautiful locations around the glob but the challenge is how to use and manage such resource to be a perfect getaway for people from around the world. Robinson Club combines both, the perfect sunset bay view with smart management. I am sure there is someone genius behind this entertaining, luxurious, beautiful, clean Resort. I would like to share my experience with you to give the full credit to the people who made me, my friends & my family spent an amazing vacation not once or twice but triple times in less than 2 months. It started 2 months ago with my childhood friend living in NY for the last 5 years asking me to find a nice place to spend his annual vacation with me and whoever interested from our old friends. I recommend some hotels in Sahl Hasheesh that I visited before, but after he reviewed those hotels he asked me to look for more hotels with clubs or nightlife, so we decided to visit Robinson on the 5th of August as a 4 single adults. We booked 2 double rooms for 4 nights. We had an amazing vacation, water sports, beach volley, parties at night, delicious food,.......everything you think of. 17th of August, one week after my return I decided to take my wife and my 3 kids again to Robinson Club Somay Bay!! They've spent a vacation to remember I figured out that there were another dimension I didn't know which is the kids club (kids programs) all day long. Beautiful teenage girls, polite, well trained and speaks different languages take care of the kids in the amazing Roby's Club. One month later, 13th of September I decided to visit Robinson Club for the 3rd time as we have a long national holiday. I recommended the hotel to other close friends of mine and guess what they also spent the vacation with us and couldn't believe how amazing this place is. Robinson Club In Words + Entertainment (different program and dress code everyday) + Staff ( great hospitality ) + Cleanliness ( everything ) + Food ( very delicious ) + Beach ( amazing ) + Rooms ( very spacious ) + kids Activities - Robinson Time ( actually this is the worst thing about the place) the club has an hour plus than Egyptian local time, which is very confusing to us and the working staff alike. Should be reconsidered from management Thanks to Mr. Essam Aly (Reservation Manager) Mr. Abd Allah ( Front Office Manager) Mr. Kareem ( Front Office) Everyone working at this place. Great work Really

author: ManuelaRonald
title: Good average vacation - nothing too impressive
text: In short: Mid November 2014 we spent 11 days at the Robinson Club in Egypt; we travelled with our 9 months old and had a good relaxing time but were not too impressed. Note that we chose the Robinson as in 2013 we had been to the Robinson on the Maldives, which we loved. Unfortunately, the Club in Egypt didn’t not live up to those standards - from an overall quality and experience perspective. The Egypt Club is a decent place and still for sure has seen better days: the facilities, the décor, the rooms look very used and cleanliness is not always highest priority. We had booked a suite in house D which is located furthest away from the “happening” to enjoy a more quiet vacation – then again the sound travels along the beach so no matter how far off you believe your room is, if there is party and music at the beach you are part of it. We were onsite for their DEEP RED week which is a party and activity week – not really for families with small kids. Hence, if you want more peace and quiet stay away from these DEEP RED weeks that happen 2x a year. Generally, if you are a “club person” you will enjoy this setting – the club offers loads of activities and happenings, for young and older. If you are not the “club type” then better look for something else. The club can host 700 people, if you like it smaller then do not go there. Its crowd is German, that means everything is German led and instructed. The food is decent and they make the effort of theme evenings, which is nice. They gym and sport session offerings are good too. Unfortunately the breakfast and dinners are served “upstairs” and there is only an elevator for emergencies, hence we ended up carrying our stroller over the stairs up and down. There is also a shortage on highchairs, so often you will need to take your baby on your lap or race for a highchair as soon as the “doors open”. Also, mind you that it is quite windy in Egypt, in the winter season this might be too much for your baby/kids so consider bringing warmer clothes and a hat. All in all we had a good time and would recommend the Club Robinson in Egypt if you are ok with what we stated above.

author: Rocky_Barrito
title: Such a stunning experiance
text: Actually, you should keep secret tips for yourself, so it is somewhat difficult for me to write this review. I loved this place. It is a little boutique resort divided into two properties in one street. The rooms are wonderful. I stayed in one of the penthouses. They are new, stylish, well equipped and furnished. Everything in the hotel is well maintained and clean. The breakfast and other food was excellent and the barman did a perfect job, too. The management and all of the staff were the most welcoming of the trips in my last years. Everybody had a smile on the face and was charming. The hotel is gay friendly. The location is great. It is in walking distance of many of the actractions in Siem Reap. There are a lot of returning guests. For me it will be not my last visit, too.

author: Tominthailand
title: Cute little botique hotel in the middle of the city...
text: Just returned from a 4 night stay at one of their villas and we were more than pleased with the accommodation and service. The staff were amazing and really bent over backwards to make us comfortable and welcome. The resort itself is just lovely with such rich character and ambience. Our room was nicely decorated and clean. Plus the treats and beverages in the minibar were reasonably priced (something you don't often see in hotels). The electricity in the rooms works on a key card system, so the AC shuts off once you leave the rooms. Our villa had a very high ceiling in the loft bedroom, so the AC really struggled to cool the room down once we returned from trekking around Angkor. We had to wait about an hour for the room to cool down enough to sleep comfortably upstairs. Also, the stairs going up to the bedroom loft were VERY steep with short steps. We had to turn sideways and creep slowly up and down every time we wanted to go up or down the stairs. I definitely would stay again, but perhaps not use one of the villas, as the rooms on the ground floor looked just as lovely. However, these were very minor inconveniences and we still loved our stay. I love that the breakfast runs till noon and the food we had was delicious! They even packed up a breakfast box for us on the last day because we had to leave for the airport extra early. The free pickup from the airport was super nice and the initial ride through the city on the little resort tuk tuk was a charming introduction to the city. Also, we found that the saltwater pool was super refreshing after touring the temples all day. The location is fantastic and it's just a short 5-10 minute walk to the night markets and pub street. Do your self a favor and stay here on your trip to Siem Reap.

author: AmandaW257
title: The perfect resort in Siem Reap
text: We were on a field trip in Siem Reap for a week, with 10 female travellers. We had booked single occupancy rooms at the Rambutan Resort for the duration of our stay, and were not disappointed. The resort has a beautiful blend of colonial style in a tropical setting, which was perfect for us. Our rooms were all well appointed, and I made the most of my balcony for early morning tea and meditation. We spent a few hours most afternoons back at the resort, enjoying the pool, having a massage of enjoying a drink. It was so relaxing and enjoyable. We had dinner at the Rambutan one evening which was very good, and a good range of Khmer and western dishes were on offer. Very tasty. Breakfast was included in our room rate, and was an a-la carte menu. Most of us tried different dishes most days, and all were terrific. The standout was the 'french toast' - order it with banana. Even the cappucino was ok :-) The absolute highlight and the stand-out feature of the Rambutan Resort, however, is their staff. The are enthusiastic, warm, helpful and couldn't do enough to ensure we had a wonderful stay. A huge and heartfelt thanks to Tommy and his team . I have no hesitation recommending the Rambutan Resort and I will certainly be back!

author: John_from_Cottonwood
title: Our Escape in The City
text: Stayed at this hotel for 5 nights. Enjoyed it immensely. It was great to return to after a tour our touring Angkor Wat and surrounding area. Our room was extremely quiet, comfortable, spacious, with great A/C. Enjoyed the pool in the afternoon and evening. There is a happy hour from 5 -7 every night and usually took advantage of it before going out for dinner. Breakfast was tasty and cooked to order. Had lunch and a couple of dinners at the restaurant which was good as anything we had out. It was way too easy to hang around here and I felt a bit guilty about it. The staff could not have been friendlier and more accommodating. We toured on our own, but used a tuk tuk with driver furnished by the hotel. Great value and we really enjoyed the driver. We were told the owner also has a bar/restaurant called Miss Wong's. Don't miss it. they serve proper cocktails and Chinese cuisine. We had some dim sum with our cocktails which were tasty.

author: ClaudioZucchelli
title: We loved it here
text: We had a beautiful suite at the hotel with a huge bed, a very lovely bathroom, plus an upstairs area which was a large terrace with sun loungers and even a big stone bath and shower, with a view over the pool. Stunning design throughout. Photos struggle to show how pretty the hotel is. The pool is in a courtyard with rooms and the bar surrounding it. The whole place is densely planted and authentic Kmer features abound. The food and cocktails were very good and breakfast, which is included, was made fresh from a lengthy menu which has western and Cambodian options. I also greatly enjoyed a free thirty minute foot massage. The staff were outstanding, always going out of their way to be helpful and friendly and ensure that our day ran smoothly. The price included pickup from the hotel, which also ran smoothly. They got us transport to and from meals and a show at Pharé. They found a superb guide and driver to show us the Angkor site. They even let us use a room after we had checked out but came back from an activity soaking wet, and needed to change. This is an LGBT friendly resort, and my husband and I felt very comfortable. It's not a gay party resort, but rather a peaceful and friendly type of place. I can certainly recommend it to both gay and straight couples and families. Kids seemed to love the pool and exploring the outdoor space. Thanks for a great stay!

author: Rivergirl100
title: Great service, great location. Just what I was looking for.
text: The hotel is in a great location - close to the night market and restaurants, but not in the thick of the tourist activity. The staff were helpful and friendly. For example, when we had trouble finding a specific restaurant, the desk clerk looked it up online, then called to confirm, and then gave us specific directions to the restaurant. The breakfast was included, with a variety of western and Asian options (although some of the western options were perhaps not quite perfectly replicated, but that's the joy of international travel, right?), all of which were quite tasty. The room spanned two levels with a large bed and bath on the first floor. The second floor had a sitting area with a day bed / couch, a TV, minibar and a small balcony. This meant that my teen age nephew had some privacy on the second floor without me needing to rent a second room. The pool takes up almost the entire courtyard area and is literally steps away from the front door. While it wasn't crystal clear, I saw it cleaned daily, and there were often happy bathers in the pool. That said, if you are coming to Cambodia for the swimming pool, this may not be the hotel for you. The room was well conditioned, and had a safe, and was equipped with all the basic amenities you'd need - shower gel, shampoo, bottled water, etc. Sheets were clean and fresh. Beds were comfortable with no head/foot boards so they should fit all sizes. Sufficient outlets and lights. Room didn't smell at all. In other words, none of things that you might fear in a mid-priced hotel were present. During a severe down pour, we did get some water coming in under the front door, but that was the only downside at all to the room. Coming back, I would definitely stay here.

author: HarryTM
title: Down a side street is a hidden gem - not far from the town centre
text: I say this because from the rather narrow side street (room for tuk tuk but not much more) the unimposing exterior does not really give a fair impression of the peaceful and comfortable rooms that lie within. Nor does it give an accurate impression of the exceptional warm and friendly staff who went out of their way to be warm, friendly and helpful. In fact nothing was too much trouble. This applied from my arrival at the airport where I was met by the tuk tuk driver to take me to the hotel. Such was the value of the tuk tuk and the skill/knowledge of this driver I used him to take me to Angkor Wat and elsewhere throughout the weekend. Having heard the hotel described as “home from home” (and of course assuming this was exaggeration) I was so pleased to note that this really was the case. My room was large with a good sized bathroom. It was a clean and well equipped with all the amenities that one needed or could expect. The only problem for me - was that it was a up a steep set of stairs - but when I got there it was so peaceful and with its own balcony overlooking the pool. So peaceful that after a busy day as a tourist I was able to fall asleep without any noise - and this despite being so close to the centre. The hotel bar/restaurant was very good. An extremely good value menu with a choice of western or Khmer food options. The included breakfast was more than adequate and there was an in-built flexibility which ensured that if something else was wanted - if they had it - you got it. If I have a criticism - it is that the bed frame had a wooden ledge going around it - all this way. This was wonderful for accessories like spectacles, remote control and phone - but meant I had to be a bit of a contortionist to get in and out of bed. So, the ultimate question : would I return if coming back to Siem Reap - without a doubt.

author: PeterS6
title: The best hotel in Siem Reap
text: If you want to experience an intimate resort & hotel in Siem Reap instead of the 5 star coldness you must stay at Rambutan Resort & hotel. Firstly the location is right across from the centre of Siem Reap. You do not need to take a tuk tuk to get anywhere if you are prepared to walk. It is only about 3 minutes across the river through the night art market to get to the old market, Pub Street, numerous food places or to go for a massage. The resort (and hotel) are built around a swimming pool so after a morning touring the temples with the crowds it is pleasing to come back to the resort and relax by the swimming pool with a Kampot Pepper martini made by either Mr Tong and Mr Ratha. These two barmen will get you into trouble - they are so obliging and make the best cocktails - and the price of cocktails here are USD4.50 compared to around USD18 where I come from!!!!!!!!!! So it is the place to indulge a little. Now the staff - Mr Sea, Mr Piseth, Mr Bunthat and all of them are the best. They make you feel at home and nothing is too much trouble to them to help your stay be a memorable one. The rooms are great and a very good price for the standard. If you want to indulge yourself upgrade to the Urban Residences attached to the resort. They are incredible so if you are staying more than a few days do this. They are large apartments with full kitchen so if you feel like cooking - why would you when there is so much good food around you incredibly cheap - you can do that. They are fully serviced and well worth the few extra dollars. I cannot speak highly enough of this place - I usually stay a couple times a year and it's like going home - you are welcomed as one of them. I've introduced a number of friends here and everybody has raved about the resort so try it - you will not regret it.

author: failim2018
title: Home Away From Home
text: Stayed there for 7 nights. Place is extremely well located. Walking distance to the night market and pub street but yet it is so peaceful. When you are back from long day tours and the Cambodian heat, Rambutan is a welcoming respite and you just can cozy up in bed or soak in the pool. Rooms are always well cleaned. Had the breakfast there every morning I was there. Food is good. Since I was in Cambodia, I tried their variety of local dishes. Their Coconut Fish Amok dish was just heavenly. Loved the Rambutan Tart, which was unique. What makes Rambutan even a greater place is the team who looks after the nature inspired boutique hotel. They are always friendly and warm. Give you advise of the places to go and are always helpful.Thank you, Tommy, Sea, Mayom, Tong, Long, Bunthat and all the team! You really made my stay in Siem Reap so memorable. Realized that I did not take much photos of the hotel itself as the hotel was too cozy and made so lazy and dreamy to whip out my camera and take pictures. haha! Managed to capture the amazing team on my camera phone. Lots of Love, Faili

author: PtheTraveler
title: Perfect location, even better place
text: I spent many a nights researching where to stay in Siem Reap. After all, you want to be near the thick of it but you need to rest to be refreshed for all your day time templing activity. I am sooo glad that I chose Rambutan. Location couldn't be better. Quiet side street yet just a short five minute walk to the "thick" of it. Mind you, Siem Reap, can be a bit underwhelming when it comes to things to do at night, but that you cannot change, where you stay, you can. The rooms are perfect, I had an upstairs one with a second floor consisting of a terrace with lovely full moon views, outdoor bathtub and charm to make the hike up the steep stairs more than worthwhile. The well trained staff was attentive, courteous, and most importantly, genuinely, concerned. Tommy the manager went out of his way to make you feel welcomed. He is a true professional that not only made sure I got the most out of Siem Reap but gave invaluable tips for the rest of my journey. If for no other reason come for this, but there is more, so much more. To name a few, perfectly made rooms, three bottles of water a day, a smiling,attentive, concerned staff and the COCKTAILS, expertly crafted, some home brewed, ask about the 'secret' pepper steeped vocka. It only gets better. While Siem Reap is one of those "been there, done that" places, Rambutan keeps you wanting to go back. Thank YOU, for a great stay.

author: NapaCasual
title: A lovely spot! A wonderful refuge. Stay here!
text: We were greeted by a wonderful man, wish I could remember his name! So polite and wonderful. We received complimentary foot massages. Lovely! Our room was on the second floor - Bluebell perhaps? It was up a staircase near the office on the second floor. The room was lovely and well appointed. In the end, it was a tad small but that was fine. We didn't spend much time in the hotel, which is unfortunate because it was really nice and the pool was beautiful! We ordered room service a couple of times - so tired from all the temple-hopping and the food was lovely. An AMAZING complimentary breakfast and good cocktails. The bathtub on the balcony was a wonderful touch. I was so excited about it. However, the warm water flow was insufficient to provide a hot or even warm bath, which was very disappointing. If not for the tepid and uncomfortable bath and low water pressure, this would be a 5 star review.

author: HJP1972
title: Amazing service, like their sister in Phnom Penh!
text: Everyone comes to Siem Reap to visit some or all of the 300 temples dotted around this little bustling city. So when something else takes your attention it’s unexpected, but oh so devine when it makes your experience even better. At Rambutan SR(like their sister, Rambutan PP) service is exceptional. I’m always impressed when I receive fabulous service, doubly impressed when it is by two different properties, same company. This tells me the Rambutan group are doing something right. Hiring great people, training and investing in them. Whatever the reason, as I customer I thank you! Yes the resort has great rooms. Ours with a roof terrace with outdoor shower and bath. Loungers and a great private area overlooking the main pool. Super comfy bed and bedding. Fantastic food, some of the best we had in Siem Reap, served by some of the most friendly staff we encountered in all of Cambodia. Thanks Mr Rotha and Mr Tong (great cocktails)and the girls serving breakfast. Front desk organised everything we needed efficiently with big smiles!!! Thanks Mr Tomi for the restaurant recommendations we are steadily working through them. Can’t wait to share our experience with anyone who will listen! P.S the complimentary foot and leg massages we received were amazing!!

author: D7482QBkarenb
title: More than met our wishes
text: Rambutan Resort was an excellent location for our vacation. The staff were all amazing. They more than exceeded our expectations. We stayed at this wonderful resort from November 18 through November 24th. Our room was lovely with a very modern feel. We stayed in the Urban A room which was tucked away in the rear corner. I was worried it would be very noisy due to the Resort being sold out and a large party was being held there but we were never bothered by any noise from the party. The manager did anticipate the crowd and noise and said we could use the pool and dinning area at the neighboring rambutan location next door. It was never an issue but I did go over to look at their very nice pool. They arranged all our tours, transportation, dinner reservations and spa treatment reservations. I had 4 spa treatments at the resort and my husband had 2. Each massage was better than the last. The pool was great! It was a beautiful location to cool off and relax. The bar and wait staff were wonderful. I suggest the Rambutan Mojito. They have a large selection of made to order breakfast and a really nice dinner menu.
