The breakfast starts at 6am but goes until much later than we expected which was perfect for us because we are not early people. Thank you very much to the wonderful people at Rambutan Resort! You all made our dream vacation amazing and unforgettable.

author: H1287DGbenjaminc
title: Best hotel in Cambodia, if not Asia.
text: Well this review is a bit overdue, however I have booked a return visit to Siem Reap (an Rambutan) which prompted me to realise I never left a review from my first stay. This Resort truly is the best in SR. As others have mentioned, it is located on a very quite and cute alley/lane, but only minutes walk from the centre of SR, the river and markets. Also, really close to the Made in Cambodia market which is a must visit - beautiful handmade products. The staff here are next level amazing. From initial booking via email, no request was too hard or bothersome. The bar staff are great and let me tell you they can make an unbelievably good cocktail and I have extremely high standards - the Rambutan Mojito....OMG - so good!! What I also really liek about the staff is that they are polite, friendly, but also great to chat and have a laugh with. The hotel itself is beautiful and the rooms extremely comfortable and styligh. I love the fact that it has charm and character. Yes, there are some steeps stairs but there's on one or two flights to deal with. My partner and I both had massages and other treatments whilst there and they were great - just as good as Bodia Spa which is the most prestigious in SR. But probably what was the icing on the cake was our final day. Our flight wasn't leaving until 8pm, and we checked out at 12 midday.Despite being very busy as it was the hieght of peak season (between Christmas and NY), the hotel staff said that we could leave our bags with them, then before we need to go to the airport they would give us access to a room to have a shower, relax and refreshen up before our 13 hr journey back to Australia. I have never experienced such amazinvg service in a hotel before, and I have stayed in some extremely expensive hotels before such as Browns London. Don't hesitate - just book this place. We will be returning in Feb next year and our decision to come back to Siem Reap was mostly based on this hotel.

author: PeterS6
title: Fabulous Resort ....... the place to stay at in Siem Reap
text: This is not the first time we have stayed at Rambutan and it will not be the last. Rambutan is in a fantastic location - easy walking into the Old Central Market / restaurant / Pub Street for dinner or a drink or two late at night. It is located down Rambutan Lane and although in the middle of Siem Reap it is very quiet. A lot of the restaurants have moved from the other side of the river to the same side as Rambutan so it is very easy to get to really nice Khmer food done by the NGO Training restaurants from Rambutan. The rooms are fabulous and we just spent 10 days staying in the Urban Penthouse and it was even better than living at home. The Urban Residences are well the extra if you are staying for an extended period ....... the rooms are great but I think we were spoiled staying in the Penthouse. The staff are beyond words - they remember your name - they make a real effort to remember our Western names and greet us each time we see them. Nothing is too much trouble and particularly the bar staff in the evening. One in particular stands out - we call him trouble but he is a fantastic barman, makes the best Khmer Martini or Passionfruit Martini imaginable ........ and the most wonderful smile - thank you Mr Tong ....... We booked the whole resort and had 40 of our closest friends for a significant birthday party and is was the best party ever. The staff, the food, the ambience they created and the music all contributed to everyone having a fantastic time. They managed a large crowd and party with ease and aplomb. I cannot recommend this resort highly enough. You will not be sorry you stayed at Rambutan Resort ...... it is a special place if you want to stay in a small boutique hotel where the staff fuss over you ......

author: russypooh
title: Wonderful Experience
text: First let me say Thank You for the wonderful staff. They went above and beyond from the moment we arrived to the day we left. Special Thanks to Mr. Bunthat and Mr. Soun for your warm hospitality, your attention to details was extraordinary. To our tuk tuk driver Kouen for his professionalism and expertise during our temple tour made our stay memorable. And to the rest of the staff members from housekeeping, maintenance, to the restaurant staff, you guys are Awesome! The hotel is beautiful. We stayed at the villa with a pool view. The room was charming, very chic and modern. Downstairs was a large bedroom and bathroom and upstairs is with a sitting area and a balcony perfect to lounge around. Very well designed hotel/resorts. The restaurant serves delicious food. Good variety from local Khmer dishes to western cuisine. Cocktails are very good as well. Location was very quiet but it is still very central within walking distance to everything including The Night Market and Pub Street. Overall experience was wonderful and looking forward to staying here again.

author: johncH4065WG
title: Charm. Hospitality. Location. Style
text: What more could you want in a hotel. That feels far more charming than a hotel. A variety of uniquely decorated and configured rooms. Some more traditional in flavour and others very modern incorporating wood, concrete and metal with traditional crafts and style. My room had an upstairs open air balcony with outdoor shower, bath and lounge. Really charming. Downstairs was a richly decorated room with all the facilities needed and generous bathroom. The rooms are arranged around a central pool and lounge area and the open air restaurant and bar. Wonderful cocktails. Must try the Khamer martini. The service here is so charming. From the management who obviously are respected by the staff to everyone you deal with. Front desk, restaurant, bar, security. They do their jobs very smoothly and efficiently, with smiles and authentic hospitality. Location is a short walk from pub street through the tourist market and across the river. Very handy and convenient. The hotel is in a small lane so is quiet and away from traffic and any noise. Highly highly recommended.

author: Kikizinho
title: A beautiful and central place
text: Of all my stays in Siem Reap, Rambutan Hotel is, by far, the best place where I have been accommodated. The first thing I'll remember, because the most obvious, is the quality of the reception. Staff clearly respect specifications extremely well put together. Always smiling, friendly without being intrusive, full of attention at every moment: glasses of iced water are served while you are at the pool, even cups of fruits salad with delicious vanilla ice cream, breakfast in a doggy bag given to me by the night watchman one very early morning I'd gone to visit the temples... all these attentions in a spontaneous way, without ever soliciting anything! A half-hour foot massage is offered during your stay. Mine was very good and efficient, after exhausting sightseeing. Breakfast is also included in the price of the rooms. Varied and intercultural (from pancakes to Khmer dish, through eggs of all kinds, French toast, or simple butter jam baguette with croissants...). Very good and plentiful. A transfer from/to Siem Reap airport is included in the room fare. A tuktuk was waiting for me at the airport (I had sent my flight details by email prior to arrival): no stress, you feel already welcome upon arrival! The pool is lovely, and you can enjoy also the facility of the neighbour's hotel (same managers), the Rambutan resort & spa, which is 10 metres away in the same alleyway. I mention this because it offers more sunny spots than the other more shaded one. The hotel is beautiful, tastefully decorated, well maintained. Clean and spacious, the rooms have got small terraces. Mine was equipped with an air conditioner and a fan fixed on the ceiling. I am very excited about my six night stay at this hotel, since I now have found my "base camp" in Angkor! Looking forward to coming back indeed!

author: chirsl2015
title: Unreal
text: The only thing i dont like about this resort is the kitchen staff and their breakfast menu, Breakfast selection are little and small, bacon and butter must be really expensive ? Or just stingy i dont know. The kithen are really really slow... it can take about 30 min for 2 eggs and toast. Just hope when you having you breakfast youre the only one there if not it can takes awhile for food to arrive. Lets start... Me and my partner booked rambutan resort months ahead, there are many options to choose from when picking a room, at the end we picked the villa, the villa itself is not bad...the villa itself are 2 levels which is really cool you get a bath tub and a water fall style outdoor shower, it look exactly like the photo but we not feeling it. So we decided to see what other rooms looks like, the resort are very kind to show us all the other options, they showed us he newly finish apartment, loft and the penthouse. All i can say about it Oh my god. Apartment, loft and the penthouse are absolutely stunning it is beyond word how beautiful they are. 3 of them are modern/ concrete finish look very very nice, the loft have a bridge build into it truly a surprise for us. It just something you are nit expecting it in the resort. We end up taking the apartment that comes with your own wifi (great bonus ) smart tv with Netflix installed ready for chill and a JBl portable wireless speaker for use, for us that was unrealistic, all the little things was just wow. Hotel staff are really really friendly and engaging specially Mr. tong he is very smart. Location are great 👍 close to pub street and markets.

author: PnA63
title: A very individual experience !
text: We thought this hotel a great experience of Cambodian hospitality. The staff are superb, very accommodating and attentive. Special mention to Mr Piseth who remembers all guests names and greets you as a friend. Indeed all the staff are absolutely delightful and the most smiley people we have come across. . As said before the hotel is located down a small alley but is located within easy walking distance of Pub Street and an array of restaurants and other bars. There are Tuk Tuks outside the hotel doors should you want to ride into town at a $2 cost. Everything here in Cambodia is priced in US dollars, I'm sure there are exchange places and banks but we didn't see any while walking around so I would bring plenty of US dollars in cash to make life easy. The hotel itself is small, with a small pool surrounded by lush vegetation. A quiet little open bar and eating area to one side of the pool. The rooms are spacious but there are mosquitoes patrolling the area looking for tasty tourists so definitely use repellent ! The doors and windows of our room had lots of gaps that wouldn't stop mosquitoes, in all honesty wouldn't stop a dog from entering they were so large but the rooms are sprayed with repellent on a regular basis according to the brochure ! The air con isn't bad and there is a ceiling fan to keep you cool. There is also an outside stone bath and shower should you want to use it as well as an inside shower. We only used the inside shower as showering with the local insect population didn't appeal to me. The stairs to the rooms here are huge. Very steep and intimidating and if you have any walking or leg problems I would recommend a ground floor room or another hotel. Breakfast was OK. Nothing special and I thought that charging for extras such as sausage , various coffees and juice was somewhat distasteful, an inclusive breakfast means an inclusive breakfast, not specific items and we'll charge for the others we know you'll want. We enjoyed staying here and enjoyed all the attractions this town has to offer, on the whole the hotel is good.

author: TilleyMan
title: Slightly off the beaten track... a stylish comfortable base in Siem Reap.
text: We were very happy during our 5 night stay at the Rambutan... staff very attentive and helpful, food great... and the bespoke cocktails are sensational! Happy hour is well worth building into your evening schedule... Our upstairs Deluxe Suite had a large Queen sized bed, and was tastefully decorated with whitewashed walls and natural timber furnishings. Bathroom was large, finished in contemporary style polished concrete with good privacy for the toilet (don't really want to share everything with your partner!). While the outside verandah looked very inviting, in June it was just too hot to enjoy sitting out there so we tended to just collapse for a nap in the late afternoons with the AC on max! Not so sure whether the outside terrazzo bathtub would ever get much use... but it looks good! The pool is a little smaller than it looks in the online images, but still a great place to cool off from the heat of the day... and it does get REALLY hot in Cambodia in summer! We had a couple of in-house massages while were there, one session very good and one session almost comically bad with two youngsters who obviously would have preferred to be somewhere else. Quality control should be better monitored by the hotel's management. We found the reception staff very knowledgeable about good restaurants nearby... and were very happy with one recommendation for our special dinner on the last night. Do try the Chanrey Tree! Staff are readily able to book you a tuk-tuk or arrange tours of the various ruins... one thing we very much enjoyed was getting up very early to see dawn over Angkor Wat... absolutely stunning! A lovely, serene and cool base to explore all that Siem Reap has to offer...

author: Steph_Surdeau
title: Pure Heaven
text: I genuinely don't know where to start rating this resort. It was beyond anything my husband and I could have expected! The resort itself was absolutely stunning. A beautiful, tropical pool surrounded by gorgeous plants. A gentle waterfall cascading down creating the ultimate feeling of relaxation. Our room was amazing - large and extremely luxurious. One thing I'm going to mention (despite it being a bit odd) is how nice everything smelt. Never something I've commented on before or probably even noticed before, but there I've said it. It's a nice smelling hotel. The staff at this resort are beyond lovely. All good fun and SO SO kind and friendly! They went above and beyond throughout the holiday to help us. Definately take them up on their offers to arrange transport to/from tourist sites as they know everything about going and help advise when to go and what to take. Don't get me started on the food! I tried almost everything on the menu and enjoyed every meal. If you do decide to go here, then prepare yourself to enjoy the holiday of a lifetime!

author: 981michaelt
title: Better than I could have ever hoped for.
text: I've traveled the world and enjoyed this hotel more than any other. The Staff make this Hotel 24/7/365. This is a mid range boutique property. It has a Wonderful Bar, Good quality Restaurant that serves up wonderful food at very competitive prices. The pool is refreshing after a long hot day of sight seeing. I traveled in the high season and even with the property full, I was made to feel like the only guest. They saw to my every need, and I put them through their paces. Laundry, dry cleaning, private tour guide, private car, massages, night clubs, tuk tuk drivers,food, beverage, welcome platter and events. The staff are creative and open minded. My friend and I each had separate rooms, both were large ,clean, well maintained. Maid service worked around my schedule and the room was always made up when I got back. No knocking on doors. It is well located withing walking distance to most things but far enough away that at night it's very quiet. Most rooms require the use of stairs. In the day time life does happen so if you are needing a hotel for lite sleepers taking long day naps might not be the perfect fit. I managed naps though with no problem. The area felt safe at all times inside and outside the hotel. Stayed 9 nights, would loved to have stayed 90... The staff are a perfect 10. 5 stars.

author: PrincessYuna
title: Amazing place - very much recommended
text: We stayed 3 nights in December and spent New Year. After a trip to the beaches in the south, we came back for one more night. The Rambutan Resort is wonderful. We have stayed in two different rooms and they were both very good. Everything is well taken care of and with much style. Everyone at the hotel is extremely friendly and helpful. We really felt welcomed back after a few days away. Check in was perfect and they explained what we could do and how to go around the city. Everything we asked, they were very accomodating. Location is perfect, because it is out of the craziness but in a couple of minutes you are in the markets and Pub Street. It is a very quite place. We ate several times in the hotel and food is very good. Breakfast is a la carte and you can choose between a good variety of options. For people with mobility difficulties, make sure that you ask for a room in the ground floor. We had a wonderful stay!

author: ftsnyc
title: Charming, well-appointed boutique resort in Siem Reap
text: This was my second stay at the Rambutan Resort in four years. The place itself is a lovely oasis; aesthetically pleasing, well-maintained and very comfortable. The salt-water (chlorine-free) pool and sweet little bar and restaurant are a welcome respite after a hot day exploring the temples. The food is delicious and inexpensive. Try the fish amok. I loved the hearty included breakfast with both western and Cambodian choices (try the bor bor) and good strong french-press coffee or espresso. The room was immaculate with cool clean tile floors, a big comfortable bed, rainwater shower, original artwork on the walls and all the usual amenities; ceiling fan, a/c, safety deposit box, tea kettle, mini bar (stocked with affordable wines as well as other treats). I really enjoyed the balcony with lounge chairs, table and an outdoor bathtub which I soaked in a few blissful mornings. You can have your breakfast (or any meal) delivered to your room and enjoy it on the balcony surrounded by flowers and overlooking the pool.. You can arrange all of your trips to temples (and other excursions) or reserve circus tickets or make restaurant bookings at the front desk. It couldn't be easier. I made good use of the reasonably priced laundry service. The best thing about the Rambutan Resort as I have said before, is the endearing staff; they are intelligent, charming, thoroughly professional as well as friendly and really, in the end, inspiring as they grow and develop their careers. There is another aspect to the Rambutan Resort that appeals to me in that it benefits the local community and there are education opportunities for the staff. As you can tell, I really like this place, intend to return and recommend it heartily.

author: 951gregorym
title: Charming tropical oasis
text: I've spent a while reading the negative reviews and it makes me genuinely sad that, what we valued as charming and authentic, other travellers viewed as dirty and substandard. Please don't be put off by the negative reviews: this place is an absolute delight! Many of the criticisms seem to have be out of date: we had no trouble getting towels by the pool, our room cleaned or recommendations for restaurants/bars and day trips to temples. Yes, it takes patience at times to be understood by the staff, but I'm always humbled that the rest of the world makes such effort to speak English and don't take this for granted. The staff were so friendly and genuinely eager to help that the odd miscommunication only adds to the charm and authenticity. The setting here was gorgeous: the pool and tropical plants are beautiful and tranquil. And yes you might find a friendly gecko in your room, but what do people expect?! This is Cambodia, not some sterile western city centre. Surely one comes here to experience Asian culture and environment? :) I'm hoping some of the reviewers don't go to Angkor Wat expecting handrails up stairs! Sheesh! I must also praise the food, which was speedy, fresh and delicious. And such good value. We went to Khmer Kitchen after reading such glowing reviews, but we honestly found the food, service and setting to be MUCH better at Rambutan. In summary a fantastic stay, definitely recommended. Thank you! Chris and Greg

author: 892iand
title: A home away from home
text: This is my 4th stay here. So coming back here IS like coming back home especially seeing some of the staffs from my past stays here. It is located across the river from the old market and pub street. You can enjoy the convenience of 5 minutes walk to the crowds but also able to enjoy the quietness of being away from all the hustle and bustle. The breakfast is good. You can have the choices of western or traiditonal Khmer food. If you want a combination of both, they will be very generous to give you both for your breakfast. The room itself is nice and spacious, housecleaning is efficient. TV in our room was not connected but I assume it wouldn't take a minute to just hook it up. Plus we didn't feel a need to turn on TV when there are so many around to see. The pool has salt water, so better for skin and eyes and not attractive to mosquitos. Pool bar provides various drinks including cocktails and mixed fruitshake. The hotel restaurant has an excellent menu of both Khmer and western food. I had one of the best Amok here and even the cheese burger we ordered for room service was exceptionally good. The staff there are very knowlegable about where to go and what to do so you can simply ask them to give you advices on your stay there. It is a gay friendly hotel although there seems to be more straight guests. But that doesn't pose any problem. We felt very welcomed and extrememly comfortable staying here. The only minor problem we had was on the second last day 2 of our towels were taken away after house cleaning and no new ones were refilled. Again I am sure they are only a phone call away but we were just too lazy and also didn't want to bother the staff.

author: A_and_BBrighton
title: Great location to explore the city!
text: We stayed in the hotel for four short days at the beginning of August 2015. Technically the rainy season and it did rain for a while most days but this was fine for us. The hotel is set back away from the main road, a 10 minute walk from the main tourist type roads where most of the bars and restaurants reside. Its a great location to explore Siem Reap by foot or via one of the many Tuk Tuk, that will try to get your business at every possible occasion. The hotel has a small courtyard pool, which is shaded for the majority of the day. Being able to cool off after a hard day exploring is a great benefit! The restaurant / bar is situated next to it, open air but sheltered for when it occasionally rained. This is also the best place to obtain a wifi signal (it didn't reach as far as our bedroom) over a particularly good Ginger Mojito. Breakfast is basic but filling and set us up nicely for a day of touring. Our room was basic, a little on the small side but clean, located on the 1st floor, furthest away from bar / restaurant. We booked our trip very last minute so options were very limited but the room was more than adequate for our needs. All the staff are very friendly and helpful, the reception organised a Tuk Tuk driver to take us around the Ankor Watt for a morning, and also gave us directions to get to eateries with the best local food. We had arranged a number of things to do ourselves, prior to arrival (a Vespa food tour and a Cambodian cookery class) but the hotel seemed to have a wide set of activities that could be arrange, if you wanted them. Overall, we think the hotel is great value for money has the great benefit of being in the centre of town and being a great base to explore the city on foot (most of the larger hotels are located out of town and shuttle their guests into Siem Reap and out to the Ankor Watt in buses). We would definitely recommend this hotel if you prefer (like us) a hotel with a bit of soul, somewhere close to everything that matters but also far enough away from the noise, hustle and bustle of a very busy city and nightlife.

author: Eddyp01
title: Little Oasis - Attentive Staff & Great Location
text: We travelled as a large group and booked the entire hotel. So I can only draw my conclusions from a large group in-house - 4 nights. Staff: During my stay I found the staff to be warm, caring, attentive and always willing to assist and help out. We were a little crazy at times due to the nature of the celebration but nothing was too much trouble. Security is always important during my stay anywhere and I always felt safe and secure through out my stay. Room: I was allocated Moke (M) room. It was very contemporary, clean, with all the modern facilities and amenities - Strong AC, room ceiling fan, well stocked mini bar, rain shower, signature bathroom products, TV/DVD, outdoor Zen bathtub, lounge chairs on my balcony and near black-out curtains. Issues: Construction was occurring outside my room during my stay, which was a slight dampener after a heavy night out on Pub Street. Not something the hotel could control or manage, but something to think about when it comes to room allocation. Menu - The menu was very well thought out and planned to cater for a wide variety of tastes. It was predominantly a Khmer flavour but with a western infusion. All dishes I encountered packed flavour and punch. Issues: My only feedback would be that the Eggs Benedict needs some attention. The toast varied from rock hard/crunchy to sloppy from the poaching water. I'm am not one to complain about food, especially given the environment/location. But somedays were better than others - with Chefs creations. Facilities - The pool is situated in the main centre of the hotel - like a Moroccan Riad - which creates a sense of community for the guests. There are ponds of tropical fish scattered through out the property, large green frond/tropical plants which enhances the feeling of a secret oasis. I observed the pool being cleaned daily and the staff did their best at garden maintenance through out my stay. I would return to Rambutan again, most definitely.

author: Charley6666
title: Excellent hidden resort in center district
text: -Nice Staff. Everyone is extremely friendly there! there was sth wrong wiz my credit card and the guy there helped me to solve it patiently. I went back to Rambutan 8 days after my first stay. Everyone recognize me and chatted with me, feeling just like old friends reunion. -Good facilities. The Swimming pool is surrounded by ensuites. Bed is soft. FREE WIFI is ok. Yet sometimes there are many mosquitos. But it would be better if you choose the Deluxe Suite. -And the breakfast is awesome,traditional khmer cuisine! Location is ideal. Just a 2-mins walk to night market. I would say it is one of the best choices in Siemreap.

author: U5096QPstevef
title: Excellent Stay
text: We do not normally provide feedback on hotel stays but thought we would this time following an exceptional stay at the Rambutan Resort in Siem Reap. From the beginning the quality of service was truly excellent. The hotel helped with advice and booking for transport and a guide for touring the temples. They also arranged a car to meet us at the airport and for our onward journey to Phnom Penh (also a Rambutan hotel), all of which were arranged with minimal fuss and complete reliability. (If touring the temples, I would definitely recommend a private driver / guide. For minimal cost it allowed us to get the most out of our time in Siem Reap.) The hotel / resort is quite central and a short 10 minute walk to the centre (markets and Pub Street). It is less than 5 minutes ride in a Tuk Tuk. As it is quite central, it is in what is best described as a “working area” down a small-ish lane. Despite not being located with the large international hotels in a more “manicured” area of Siem Reap, we had no issues walking around and felt perfectly safe. In fact being in a more “genuine” area of Siem Reap, added to our Cambodia experience. The Resort, whilst small is clean and has all the facilities you need including: a pool, bar and restaurant (shared with the related hotel just down the lane). The room was comfortable (with air-conditioning), quirky and much more interesting than staying at a larger international hotel chain, where frankly you could be anywhere in the world. Whilst the hotel was very good, it was the helpfulness of the staff that made the stay exceptional and memorable. They were always courteous, helpful and willing to offer advice aspects of staying in Siem Reap. If you are looking for small boutique hotel that is more memorable than a large chain hotel, we would certainly recommend this one.

author: abundy
title: Great Staff, location and facilities
text: After a snafu with a booking, we were given the Mimosa room, with a bath tub on the balcony. First the negatives. This room is on the top floor, and is accessed by 2 sets of stairs. The first set of stairs is steep, so if you have difficulties in negotiating stairs then this room is not for you. The second set of stairs are not so bad, but they are a bit longer. All of the sliding locks on either the bathroom door or the balcony door and shutters don't actually line up so they don't really lock. While this is no problem as this room s on the top floor an only really accessible from the stairs, it was a little dissapointing detail. Now the positives - Staff excellent. Facilities excellent. Pool excellent. The guys at reception will organise anything you need. Trips to the temples can be charged to the hotel room. The driver we had was excellent. Just organise what you want the day before and he will be there. there seems to be some organisation from these tuk tuk guys as there was a menu of what prices were for the circuits you wanted to do around the temples. We organised to have breakfast made for us to take on our early morning temple visits, but they were nothing much. Just a small baguette, which was nice and a croissant and some pineapple jam. All in all a great place to stay and a great location to the town (just across the river). Oh and the beds were comfortable as well, not like the usual asian type rock hard beds.

author: PeterS6
title: R&R in the middle of it !!!!!!!1
text: Down an paved laneway in the middle of busy Siem Reap is this oasis. You will be surprised. I had one of the rooms on the 2nd floor overlooking the salt water swimming pool and it was great. The room was large, well laid out with a desk, mini bar and safe. The shower was massive and no worries about water pressure as in other places in Cambodia. The room was clean and had a balcony overlooking the pool with a stone bath (there was a curtain you could pull around for some privacy). I am not sure how many people use the bath but for a romantic weekend could be nice. Beside the swimming pool is their bar and cafe - breakfast goes until midday and the selection was either some western style breakfast or Khmer food - I chose the Khmer and it was very nice. Great way to start the day before walking to The Hive for coffee. The staff were plentiful, very helpful and friendly. Service was good without being intrusive. They were happy to arrange tours or tuk tuks for you at a moments notice. Just remember in Cambodia everybody (well nearly everybody) goes to bed early (just after sunset) but they get up at the crack of dawn so be prepared for this if you plan a late night. It was not a problem in the resort but with the noise from surrounding houses. However, wherever you go in Cambodia this happens. It just means an early start with an afternoon nap by the pool. What could be nicer. Thoroughly recommend any of the Rambutan (Golden Banana) Resorts or Hotels - I'll definitely be staying there next time I'm in Siem Reap - which is likely to be soon. I had a fabulous time and thoroughly enjoyed the resort - cannot recommend it enough. Enjoy.

author: JohnH616
title: Amazing Intimate Resort
text: Spent three days touring the Angkor temple complex but one of the highlights was staying at this amazing, intimate “resort.” From the moment you arrive at Rambutan Siem Reap you are surrounded by comfort. The staff is - to a person - professional, friendly and helpful. The rooms and pool areas are well equipped for comfort but not stuffy. I had a two-level unit with a deck that was the perfect place to chill after days exploring Angkor. I also recommend the restaurant at the hotel. There are countless options in Siem Reap but the food at Rambutan was among the best I had on my trip. The drinks too! The hotel is also in a nice location – a good distance from the hectic but fun pub-street night market but close enough so you can access that area with a $2 taxi ride or a very easy and safe 15 minute walk. As I said, all of the staff are excellent without exception. I’ll mention Svay Kouen specifically because he was managing the front desk most of the time I was there and arranged amazing things for me – including one of the best oil massages I have ever had. He also set up a tour guide and driver for me that immeasurably enhanced my trip. My guide was perfect - he knew everything from the history of each site to the type of rock they used to build it. But he also knew when to send me on my way to wander through the ruins alone, taking pictures, meeting up with him later with my questions and observations. In case you want to use the same one (full of knowledge and energy) have the hotel book him for you in advance: Be Sokong Kear, kear0204@yahoo.com I should also mention Sokham who is one of the drivers the hotel recommends. Spent three fun days zipping around the area with Sokham and Kear - an experience I will never forget. I’m already looking at flights to return early next year!

author: ChinaKent
title: A stylish place to stay in a great location.
text: I was picked up at the airport by a driver in a car and taken to The Golden Banana Resort, the welcome was great, with very friendly and helpful staff. The rooms surround the small but adequate pool; mine was located on the ground floor. My room had a 2nd floor with access up a stepped staircase, upstairs is a sitting room, a little sparsely furnished, a bar size fridge, a smallish TV and a nice balcony. The upstairs only has a fan for cooling so at times was quite warm. Downstairs had an air conditioner and ceiling fan which kept the room nicely cool and the bed has a mosquito net but I did not use it or even see any mosquitoes. The bathroom was a good size, the water flow n the shower was adequate and the whole place stylish. The room service was good but the size of the meals was a bit small for the price. The quality of the breakfast was excellent, with a good range of options. The location is very good, close to the Old Market and Pub Street, I walked the 10minutes but you can get a tuktuk or motorbike if you want. I organized my tuktuk driver through the front office which was the same price advertised everywhere else to explore Angkor Wat. It was good to take the tour by tuktuk, the driver was friendly but did not offer any information about Angkor Wat, which others do. The 2nd day price was different the 1st day, so make sure to ask about the prices before you go, it did not break the bank but it would be a lot nicer to have been told of the price change upfront, we all only need nice surprises. I enjoyed my stay and it was good but the inconvenience of having to go upstairs to watch TV while usually not a problem was as the World Cup was on and it was very inconvenient. While I was there it was quiet and relaxing until the last day when a family with children arrived, now normally people are out exploring during the day but I had a rest day and the children in the pool were a bit loud, however you can’t have everything. I caught a tuktuk to the airport and that was fine, you don’t need a car. Overall, a good stylist boutique resort (I don’t think it is big enough to be called a resort), great friendly helpful staff, with a great location. Make sure you visit Miss Wong’s for the classiest cocktails and venue going around.

author: katehoole
title: My Golden Banana stay
text: I booked myself in for 2 nights in April and arrived with a friend who had booked into the b&b next door. By comparison, she paid about 35SGD through another online outfit and I paid 78USD per night direct. My place had 2 floors and was luxurious by comparison. She knew that a bed and shower was necessary, not much else. I loved my room which led straight out by a cool, tranquil swimming pool, with bougainvillaea draped over balconies and banana leaves keeping the area cool. Staff were more than nice, they were extremely helpful and keen to make sure I was comfortable - I am a divorced woman in my forties. Staff organised a tuk-tuk the first day for 5am, We negotiated a rate and settled on $17US for the day. Everyone was helpful, kind, smiling and we were satisfied. The following morning I arranged to have a motorcycle take me around on the back. I paid $11US and really enjoyed the relative freedom of being on the back of a bike going around Angkor Wat. The breakfast was excellent and part of the deal (I chose the Cambodian noodles). The coffee was less good, but hey ho there was excellent coffee in any of the many coffee bars around Siem Reap. Really recommend the Golden Banana. I could have gone cheaper and there are plenty of options to do so, however, this place came recommended and I would recommend it to others. I hope this is useful.

author: Ecrad
title: Just perfect
text: Every now and then, you stumble across a place that meets your needs perfectly. Golden Banana was one of these rare finds for me. I arrived after an exhausting bus journey from Phnom Penh, after staying at GB's sister resort, Rambutan. A warm greeting, a cold towel, and a friendly check-in had me already feeling at home. The room was right on point - clean and spacious room, comfortable bed, great shower, balcony with outdoor bath overlooking the pool. The pool was great not only for swimming both day and night, and catching some sun, but also for meeting other guests and sharing conversation and a drink between temple visits and other activities. The restaurant served surprisingly good food, and the service was warm and friendly. Tea and coffee facilities in the room might be nice for a late night craving when the bar is closed, but otherwise unnecessary as the staff will bring you whatever you need. And then there's those staff. What a wonderful crew! The reception staff were efficient and organised, always sorting any request or query with quiet professionalism, ensuring that everything ran smoothly, whether it was a driver, a massage, a flight or a change to my booking. The bar and restaurant staff made me feel right at home, and felt like friends by the time I had to leave. The manager, Tommy, is equally friendly and does a superb job of keeping the ship on course. I had such a wonderful time here that I extended and ended up staying for around 10 days. And I've already booked to return for a quick holiday during the year. Thanks, Bananas!

author: ferris1985
title: Wonderful, intimate and friendly hotel
text: My wife and I spent 3 nights in Siem Reap and stayed at this lovely hotel. It was an excellent choice. The hotel is in an ideal location- its close to some nice restaurants and bars and the fantastic night market and also a perfect base for seeing temples. This is a must in Siem Reap. The staff were very friendly, courteous and very well-trained. From the moment we arrived they went out of their way to assist us and make us feel at home. We were on honeymoon and they really did make it special for us. I spent a lot of time chatting to the staff at the bar and around the hotel and they were very pleasant. I also liked the fact that the owner is constantly around talking to guests which I doubt you would see in the bigger hotel chains. The hotel is pretty small but this is one of its main qualities. The setting is intimate and inclusive- it attracts young and old couples, straight and gay and this really sets it apart from a lot of alternatives. It has a lot of charm and personality and the rooms are simply beautiful ( I highly recommend a cocktail or two in the bath on the balcony) Additionally the food, drinks and spa treatments were of a high standard. If you stay here you must hire the tuktuk driver Tiger who is employed through the hotel. He took us temple trekking two days and he was a lovely, friendly young man. All in all I would recommend the Golden Banana to anyone looking for a relaxing, comfortable stay in Siem Reap. We will definitely be back soon.

author: SusaninMadison
title: Stay here - you'll find comfort, location & hospitality
text: I spent three nights at the Golden Banana Boutique Resort and felt both like I was home and on vacation the whole time. If I return to Siem Reap, this is where I will stay. As others have said, the Golden Banana is centrally located, but it's across the river from the downtown attractions. This means you can easily walk to the Old Market - and then walk back again to blissful quiet. The rooms and resort are decorated with an eye to simplicity and continuity. You'll enjoy the art work by Ter. You'll enjoy the open space in your room, the rattan, the louvered wooden shutters onto your balcony if you have a second floor room, the thought that has gone into the smallest detail - like the traditionally carved ibis on the desk in my room. The restaurant serves meals all day. I came down each morning to sit at a table next to the waterfall and salt water pool (salt water doesn't attract mosquitoes). Seriously - a salt water pool just across the river from the Old Market. Coffee always came quickly, and so as I waited for my meal I could wake up looking at and hearing water. A wonderful start to the day. And the staff was incredible - a rare treat to find people so friendly and engaged. From Toeu my constant, kind and attentive waiter who talked to me about the education he had received from an NGO to Thol Hong, the manager, who made sure details were taken care of and was a ready resource in talking about Cambodia. I was there consulting for a favorite NGO, and Thol asked thoughtful questions about it and made clear how important it was to him to give back to his country as he continued his career. Staff respect your privacy, so you will need to initiate conversations if you want to engage with them. But if you do, you'll go deeper into a what a jewel this place is. Thank you once again, Thol and Toeu. It was a delightful stay.

author: traveldayne
title: We had joy we had fun...
text: Tucked away at the corner of a small quiet alley . Don't be confused by several other hotel resort by the same name next door. Most probably by same management. We were greeted with a warm and helpful staff who welcomed us with cold drinks & towels. Our room which was large enough for both of us located just above the restaurant . Comfy bed , nice power shower with a balcony & bath tub outside overlooking the pool And most importantly free WIFI ! There is no lift to the upper floor . If you can't carry those heavy luggage with you , do not be despair, the staff will be more then happy to help you with that. The stairs can be slippery though especially after the heavy pours most afternoons . My travel partner accidentally slipped from the staircase that leads to the restaurant. Luckily it was nothing serious. A sudden 20 mins power failure for 2 nights in a row was a little bizarre I must say. The hotel massage service was quite good but not cheap. I believe you can find many around town with affordable prices . Breakfast was simple but good enough to start your day. We only had lunch once at the restaurant during our 4 nights stay. Curious glares I've been getting from a waiter while having my meal can make one feel a little awkward. Despite all that we had a really good laughs with the staff who've made our stay very enjoyable.

author: stayfrostysparky
title: Your own little village in Siem Reap
text: Located down its own lantern-lit lane, "Golden Banana Alley", the Golden Banana is like having your own little village away from the dusty streets of Siem Reap. From the pickup at the bus station to the send off at the airport, the sense of community is immediately there. It's the same friendly staff who greet you with a smile each morning at breakfast, serve you drinks at the pool each afternoon, and hand you your key each evening! They also know all the extremely professional tuktuk and taxi drivers that they recommend, and took care of arranging our three-day exploration of the temples, including a very worthwhile recommendation to journey out to Koh Ker (ask for Keat Din as a driver, he knows even the far-flung temples well). Location is fantastic, only a 5 minute walk across the river from the Old Market, Pub Street and the main town area. The road along the way is very lively with plenty of eateries full of locals, so we never had to take a tuktuk, and we never felt unsafe. We had a Deluxe Villa room, which was lovely and very spacious with a big covered terrace upstairs to relax on during hot, stormy afternoons. Never had a problem with the water pressure in either the bathroom shower or outdoor shower, in fact the water pressure was amazing! Toilet did have issues flushing a couple of times, but it got there in the end. Also great was the 10pm curfew on noise in the pool and bar area, really helpful for trying to get an early night before sunrise at Angkor Wat! Breakfast offered lots of choices and it was all made fresh and served poolside, or in your room, or practically anywhere else you want. The GB is gay-friendly as well, and my partner and I felt completely welcome, but there were plenty of straight couples and families staying here as well, and it was never in-your-face. Overall, would not hesitate to recommend this resort. Considering going again at the end of the year! Really friendly spot with the best staff and rooms and an environment that make you really feel like home.

author: arch_c
title: Great location with excellent food, nice rooms
text: We (family of 3) stayed here for 5 nights in May 2013 and regret not staying longer. We had booked the Deluxe Villa - although the room was a good size (300 odd square feet + an equal sized rooftop), the room itself was smaller than I expected from looking at the photos on the website. That said, it was adequate for us, and we didn't feel crowded. Our villa came with a private rooftop terrace with a fabulous stone tub and loungers. We didn't really make the best use of the terrace because of the heat. But I did have a long soak in the tub after a hot day touring the temples. And we spent a couple of hours late one evening just relaxing on the terrace and watching the stars and geckos! The stairs to the rooftop are steep but were not a problem for us. The pool is fabulous and my daughter made a dash for it every chance she got. I especially loved the tropical garden feel of the pool and hotel. The hotel has 16 rooms, about half of which were unoccupied during our stay. So it wasn't too crowded, and not too deserted either. We loved the food so much we hardly ate out much. The menu is limited - just a page long, so between the three of us, we managed to try almost everything on it during our stay. There are quite a few local dishes on the menu - these are a must try for the fresh ingredients and subtle flavors - absolutely delicious! I especially loved the mee cha, amok, and Khmer curry. The staff is very welcoming and friendly and will tell you about local customs, etc. Another great thing about the hotel is its location - it's less than a five minute walk across the river to the Old Market and Pub Street. And it's just a minute's walk to the Siem Reap Art Centre where you can shop for locally made souvenirs and paintings. To summarize, this hotel is excellent value for money and we had a wonderful stay.

author: FerretingOutTheFun
title: An Oasis in Siem Reap
text: We absolutely loved our stay at the Golden Banana! We were in the GB II Villa property, with a standard room on an upper floor. The GB II Villa is comprised of four buildings that surround a central pool, which we learned was filled with salt water as a mosquito deterrent. We managed to work in some pool time every day, washing off the dust from the temples and enjoying delicious – and potent – cocktails as the sun set. The room was decorated with simple wood furnishings and a queen bed with a firm-but-standard-for-Asia mattress. An extra twin bed in the corner meant that three people could share the space. The bathroom was industrial chic and would have been wonderful had the water been at all reliable. After repeated calls to the front desk we were told that there just wasn’t a lot of water in the region and we learned to regulate our usage. All rooms have balconies overlooking the pool and feature giant bathtubs that must only get filled during the rainy season. The resort was fully booked during out stay, but we didn’t hear a peep from the other guests past 10pm. That was left to the Hip Hop club down the street which pumped out music late into the night. Breakfast was served in the open-air restaurant and was included in our room rate. Choices included eggs, bagels with a variety of toppings, Asian noodle dishes and scrumptious banana pancakes. Dinner at the hotel was also tasty if you're too tired to go out. We loved the location, which wasn't too far of a walk from the bustling Pub Street area. Even walking back at night, we never felt unsafe. And if you need to hire a tuk-tuk driver, ask the hotel to call Namo (sp)! He lives nearby and was an absolute joy!

author: Zion51
title: I will definitely come back
text: We stayed there 4 days and had a very good time there. The rooms are clean and spacious. Every room has a terrace with a bath tube outside and a couple of chairs to relax in the evening after visiting the stunning temples of Angkor Wat. It is very close to the night market and the Pub Street meaning that you can walk there at night to grab a drink and get something to eat. If you dont feel like going out after a long day, well don't! The food is very good (and the chef is always smiling! Great guy!) in the resort and in line with the city prices so there is no surprise and no overcharge linked to the place. Service is great, there are some hickups once in a while but nothing major and everything is always dealt with with a nice smile and a lot of calm. I really have nothing mean to say about the place, only compliments! Works for couples, families and friends. On the previous comments I read. Yes, the swimming pool is not made for a tri athlete but for a relaxing time after a long day of walking, its perfect! Also, I have read that some people where complaining about the waterfall sound but to be honest that didn't disturb me at all as it is shut off after 10 pm (or maybe earlier) and doesnt start until late in the morning. I actually felt it gave a very peaceful feel to the place (zen attitude). Oh one last thing, they can provide the tuck tuck and the guide so dont worry too much about this. For the visit the first day, just make sure you have 40USD per adult to get access to the site. All in a wonderful experience in the GB, if I come back (which I am planing to for the rainy season), will definitely go there again.

author: kamiak
title: Nice staff!
text: Stayed 5 nights at the Golden Banana Resort in Mid-March. We had a room just off the pool, with a terrace upstairs. My favorite thing about the hotel was the staff - particularly in the bar/restaurant. They were very nice and always smiling. One afternoon I was at the pool, and the GM was having a staff meeting. I could hear lots of kudos and lots of applause. They seem to have a sense of teamwork and community there. the sign of great management. The quality of food was quite good and the price more than reasonable. My only feedback is the bed. To truly experience the sights of Cambodia. you must climb stone stairs, walk miles, and really push yourself. The bed is firm, like most Asian hotels, and while I can deal with that, it also features a wood ledge around the mattress. Some nights I was so sore and tired that getting up to get some water or use the restroom was painful, because I had to traverse the bed ledge. While it was useful for my alarm clock, and attractive to look at, the ledge at times caused me some pains. A small thing really. I miss the smiles at the Golden Banana. thank you for a great stay

author: EllenorNewcastle
title: Friendly,good location.
text: We had to laugh. First morning at breakfast we were the oldest, straightest couple at breakfast, although we did know it is advertised as gay friendly. Some people may be put off by this but don't be as you will miss out on a great little boutique hotel. And yes, it is very family friendly. Our room was on the top floor which was great exercise up the fairly steep steps,so those that aren't so agile should maybe request a ground floor room. Our room was quite large and I loved the outside bath that I used of an afternoon when there were too many at the pool. The owner is always around and seems to have a great rapport with his staff. This is probably why they are so happy and efficient. Breakfast was good and pretty large serves. We had lunch a few days as well and can recommend the bruschetta, yummy! Also the iced lemon tea is to die for. The most refreshing drink after a long hot day. Location is walking distance to everything central. Markets, restaurants and museum. We loved our stay here and would definitely stay again.

author: lennybruce
title: Wonderful stay in every way
text: We just had a wonderful 3 night stay at this great place. Everything was just as it should be. A large room, nicely appointed with a very comfortable bed, very nice bathroom, laptop size room safe, minibar fridge, flatscreen TV, great channel choice and very good wifi. My favorite treat regarding the room was the quite private balcony with retan loungers, outdoor stone bathtub and shower. We bought some nice bath salts at one of the boutiques in towns and enjoyed a relaxing outdoor soak every evening after our busy and hot days. One night I got to enjoy a fantastic thunder and lightning storm from the warm comfort of the tub (my partner who is a bit shy of lightning passed up the bath that evening). The staff was very friendly and engaging giving us an additional opportunity to learn some more about their lives in Cambodia. The barman could make nice cocktails and the food, which we enjoyed a couple of times since we just didn't want to leave the place, was also very good (the Cambodian dishes and the french fries also!). With a nice pool and relax beds around the pool area our stay was complete. The management was also very nice and helpful and from what I heard from the staff, they care about their staff and their development. Always nice to see. And since the city was experiencing some flooding when we were there, the manager was totally prepared to give us any assistance necessary if the water was causing movement problems on the morning we had to go to the airport (in the end was not needed). But we sure felt good the night before that he was so involved and prepared to do whatever (thanks Tommy!). I do have one note that I don't want to leave out for those who may stay here in the near future partially based on my review. In September, 2011, when we stayed, they were doing some construction work on expansion. This causes some minor unavoidable noise but for 99% it wasn't anything that really disturbed us. The hotel is doing their best to minimize the disturbance by planning the work as much as possible at times when it will be least disturbing and trying to get it mostly done before the high season starts and the occupancy rates go up. And they are doing their best to put people in rooms that are further away from the work. And since the work is being done during the day when one is mostly off touring, it's really not much of an issue. And this fact did not diminish at all the feeling we left with - this is a great place that has all their ducks in a row!

author: Dr_Drew2
title: Can't wait to return
text: This was my first time visiting Cambodia. Most of the other reviews say it all. The location is down an alley and about a 5 minute walk from the old market. The hotel itself is incredibly charming and a complete open-air design, as is much of everything in Siem Reap. We were in a villa that had the terrace on the second floor. Everything is very comfortable and extremely relaxing. The staff are all very friendly and so is the dog, Blackie. All of the food is fresh and quite good. We ate several meals there and they were all good. The coffee is wonderful. The bartenders make lots of different drinks and the prices are very affordable. We spent a couple of evenings sitting at the bar talking with the staff. The free wifi is a great benefit too. The hotel staff arranged our airport pick-up with a car and was able to arrange our temple tour with a car, the same driver, and tour guide. They were all wonderfully friendly local people who I would recommend to anyone. We took our driver and guide to lunch with us and it was great to have local perspectives on the food and culture. Supporting this local hotel and these local people has such an impact on their lives, especially during the low season. Staying at this hotel was one of the best decisions we made regarding our trip to Siem Reap. Had we stayed at the Raffles or De La Paix, we would not have had the same attentive, personal, and local culture experience that we had. We look forward to returning.

author: neige8
title: Beautiful place with warm, friendly people!
text: We are so glad we stayed here. Everyone who works at this hotel is so incredibly nice. They work really hard to make sure all their guests have a wonderful stay. Our room was great – super clean, big bed, tile floors, nice bathroom and we loved the balcony with the outdoor bathtub. Breakfast was good (the eggs were the best choice). We looked forward to the fresh juice & tropical fruit every morning. The salt-water pool was wonderful! It was so nice to come back after a long day of temple climbing and cool off with a drink by the pool. Their mixed drinks and the Amock are sooooo good! The GB is the perfect distance to the middle of town (pub street etc.) 12 min walk or 5 min via tuk-tuk. The center of town can get a bit hectic, so it was great to stay in a place that was not directly in the middle of it all. The GB hotels are located down a cute little alley. The main street before the alley has a few small restaurants that mostly locals go to. We liked the fact that we were not totally surrounded by tourists. We often walked home at night and felt safe (but females coming back alone at night should take a tuk-tuk - it is only $3 USD) We arranged all the tours and airport transportation through the hotel- totally easy, and the drivers and guides were great. My advice is not to do back to back temple exploration days. We took a day off between our tours and stayed by the pool, had massages and checked out the town, it is smart to pace yourself. Remember – it’s a vacation! If you are looking for friendly, mini-tropical oasis in the middle of Siem Reap – this is your place.

author: LookStranger
title: Can I get the Fish Amok recipe?
text: Reading reviews on TripAdvisor is so dangerous. You see litanies of mind-numbing, scrappy moans, and you wonder nervously (bearing in mind you have no way to know, and are likely booking from a distance) whether there's veracity in this nit-picking; it sows seeds of doubt. What you don't get to see (or hear) is the people who are complaining. If you did you might gain perspective. I've never written a review before, but felt compelled on this occasion. It's roughly like this: if you're a low-key, normal, cheerful sort of person looking to have a delightful time in a beautiful place, not looking to antagonize anybody or establish your superior guest credentials, not looking for reasons to gripe ... then you'll have a wonderful time at the Golden Banana. It's completely lovely. The staff could not be more sunny and sweet, the rooms are spotless, spacious, the pool salty, clean and refreshing. It's a shining little oasis. However, if you're miserable and wear your misery like sackcloth and ashes wherever you go, then you'll probably find cause for some complaint or other. But that likely has more to do with you than anything else; perhaps the cost of the hotel would be better spent on therapy? Or (if you have the money) stick to Mandarin Orientals, where the entire modus operandi is geared to mollifying misanthropes and curmudgeons. Everybody else? Go to The Golden Banana, I think you'll be very happy.

author: BigSis2112
title: OK, a few problems
text: Golden Banana is a nice little hotel situated down a lane the other side of the river from the Old Market. The area is OK, a bit dark at night (GB have their own street lighting as Siem Reap don't provide much street lighting outside of the main town area). The road to the GB is paved up to a point and then it's like a dirt track so it's a bit tricky after heavy rain (lots of mud and puddles). The day we arrived we got two rooms one above the other (M and L), but the air con in M wasn't working so they moved us to a ground floor room (C) which was near the pool. As it turned out, we might as well have stayed in M because there was a storm around midnight and the power to that part of the town went off until about 9am next day so no lights, no a/c and worst of all for us, the drains backed up and the bathroom in C got flooded. In the morning when the power came back on, there were thousands of little wriggling things on the bathroom floor in the mud - tadpoles? tiny fish? I don't know what they were, but wasn't keen to stay in that room again after that in case there was another storm. Please be aware if you go there, C isn't the best room - it's dark and dingy and if possible get a higher up room as you'll have a nicer time. Anyway, the a/c man came out and fixed the a/c in M and we moved back there and were much happier after that. The GB staff assured everyone that the power going out like that was very rare but as it happened again during a storm 2 days later, I think they were stretching the truth slightly! The rooms were clean and well looked after, the breakfasts were OK (3 choices, all vegetarian). We ate lunch there and that was fairly average - they mentioned in their room info that their chef was one of the best, but I can only assume he doesn't start work until the evening - we didn't eat there in the evening so I don't know what the food was like then. The pool is small but that's all you need really - just a quick dip to cool off. The prices in the restaurant and bar were similar to most mid-range restaurants in the town and the staff were happy to help out with organising tuk-tuks, temple visits, horse riding trips etc. I would mention that as it's dark and badly lit around that part of town, solo female travellers might be best to think about getting a tuk-tuk home (even though it's walking distance from town). I walked back with my teenage daughter one evening (about 9.30pm) and we had strange groups of guys calling to us, one group offering us drugs.......nothing too threatening but it did seem quite seedy, especially around the riverside area on that side. People with mobility problems would have to go for a ground floor room I think as the stairs to the upper rooms were quite steep. It's not very stroller friendly either. To sum up - it was a nice looking hotel but I think they need to invest in a generator and for that reason I'd probably stay elsewhere if I went back to Siem Reap.

author: Mastemah
title: Wonderful stay - full recommendation
text: I was having a trip through southeast Asia with my wife and from several hotels we stayed in, this was definitely one of the best. Location: The hotel is located on the other side of the river opposite the center of Siem Reap, approx. a 5-10 minute walk to the center. The hotel is located in a charming side road, which is very quiet. If you want to go to the Angkor Tempels, it will be an approx. 15-20 minute drive, the airport is approx. 20 minutes from the hotel. Overall, the location is very good. The Golden Banana Boutique Hotel is adjacent to the Boutique Resort. The following are things we liked the most about the hotel: *) staff extremly (!) helpful and nice.. just wonderful *) clean and comfortable rooms with A/C and satellite TV *) stylish decor *) very clean and cosy bathrooms *) the room named "ylang", which we had, had a great terrasse overviewing the pool. The terrasse featured own bathtub and shower, as well as two chairs for relaxing *) great fruit drinks and milkshakes Compared to other hotels in Siem Reap, you might find this place a bit expensive, however, you will get value for your money (our deluxe room was 90 USD/night incl. breakfast). The swimming pool is a salt water pool and was to my feeling a bit too fresh even for the hot temperatures in Siem Reap. Although the hotel informs about a lot of frogs and gekkos generally in Siem Reap, we never saw a frog and only some gekkos in the hotel area. The place is a gay friendly place and during our stay about 50% of the couples staying were gay. To summarize: The hotel is really great and I can hardly think that there are many places out there that could beat it. We loved our stay and there is nothing negative I can say about the place, everything was just perfect. I would definitely recommend this hotel for your next trip to Siem Reap (which is a great place to go to... don't stay less than 4 days for Angkor and surrounding, you will definitely regret if you do so!)

author: Cocojeanne
title: Quaint boutique hotel in the middle of the city - loved the style
text: My husband and I stayed here for 3 days, 2 nights. We didn't arrange for a pick up but when we got to the airport, we were pleasantly surprised to find a driver waiting for us! Soka was the most polite, kind and humble driver ever. He picked us up with his car but took us around the city with his tuk tuk. He brought us to the best food joints there and we enjoyed his company so much, we had him sit down to lunch with us one of the days. When we got to the hotel, a quiet oasis and a friendly receptionist greeted us. The pool and the decor were so welcoming and I can't say enough about the 2 story villa that we got. The French colonial house was spacious and tastefully decorated. The location was very central and great for walking. Breakfast was more than adequate and the staff were really friendly. They also helped us book our bus tickets to Phnom Penh and helped us with our itinerary. When we needed to access the internet, they brought us to another part of the GB where we were able to go online for free. They also arranged spa treatments on site and these were done in a tasteful hut. The only negative points were the steps going up to our door and the steps going up to the bedroom were kinda of steep and really tiring after a day at Angkor Wat. The shower stall was also poorly designed because the water kept flooding the rest of the bathroom. The hot water ran out during long showers so wasn't that great...the other thing was that there were many mosquitoes in the rooms that came in through the cracks of the doors and windows. Not a biggie since insect repellent kept us free of bites. At night, we were kept awake by the cat and dog symphony but were so tired from our treks at Angkor Wat that we fell asleep again quickly. No fault of the hotel. Overall, I would recommend this hotel to everyone looking for a boutique hotel or bed & breakfast kinda accomodation.

author: newyork2626
title: One of the best budget hotels I've stayed in
text: I ended up staying in a superior room at the b&b. When I booked they quoted me a room in their boutique hotel. So make sure you are aware this is a 3 in 1: b&b, hotel and resort. I opted for the superior room in the b&B $28 instead of of $21 for regular and it was a great choice. The gay shines through: clean sheets (though matress very hard), hot rainfall shower, tv, balcony, and clean. The only real disappointment were the towels: they were stained, ragged and smelled lightly of mold - so just bring your own (along with toiletries). Also bring a tissue box should you need it. The all male cutoff tshirt wearing staff were extremly helpful, albeit their English was not great. Calls cannot be tranferred to the room, so they will walk you over a phone, kind of Inconvenient. Wi fi in most rooms, the closer your room is to or above reception, the better it is, book accordingly. I booked tuk tuks through them. They are slightly more expensive but i didnt mind. My tour guide was very friendly but not super knowledgable on the Hindu texts and temples. Granted, I am an advanced scholar in the area. So if you want an in depth tour, I'd recommend booking your own guide elsewhere. Overall, i wasn't blown away by the guide's English or knowledge. I don't recommend the laundry - my clothes came back dirtier with hair and dirt I didn't have on there before and the material (cotton/polyester) was ruined!

author: irenemalone
title: always perfect
text: We have stayed here twice now. I always travel with my young son and this time some friends joined us with their teenage children. The service is top notch and the facilities are wonderful. I cannot recommend it highly enough, the rest of the reviews give plenty of detail. I have also stayed in the cheaper rooms and while plain, the same excellent service was extended and I was never once given the impression my lower budget made me 'second class' in any way. The resort rooms are a delight. The Golden Banana is one of the best, if not the best, boutique hotels I have ever stayed in. They do encourage you to use their drivers, and it seems one traveler felt pressured. but it's important to keep in mind that not only do they vet the drivers they use, so you can be sure they are safe and honest, they also have a large extended 'family' of workers. These drivers cost no more than any others you might use, and they have the correct licence as well. The police are checking more often and a driver without the proper paperwork will get refused entry to the Angkor Wat park areas, which would put a serious kink in temple plans. Cambodia is an extremely poor country and there is no welfare of any kind, so the extended network of helpers is a normal facet of life. I would just go with the flow with these things and not let it spoil your stay. The food is excellent and there are many restaurants worth checking out. Don't miss a trip to The Sugar Palm for an excellent meal, and go to Dr Feet for a miracle of foot restoration after climbing those temple steps! The hotel itself is very quiet and keeps a relaxing atmosphere going. It is super close to nightspots like Miss Wongs, so no-one misses out.

author: KandJ44
title: Excellent rooms, service and staff
text: My husband and I stayed here for about 6 days on our honeymoon. The room was wonderful, very roomy, high ceilings, great bathroom and balcony. The style of the room was great and the shower was huge with an awesome rain style shower head. The tub on the balcony was also really nice, although it could of used a larger shower curtain. The staff was wonderful. They were all very kind and helpful. The service was excellent, the menu was limited, but very delicious. Breakfast was really filling and good quality. The breakfast was eggs and assorted local fruit, fresh juice, coffee/tea, bread and yogurt. We received a very nice welcome when we arrived and the treatment remained the same throughout our stay. We booked our tuk-tuk driver through the hotel and we loved him! You can pay for everything on a credit card which makes it more hassle free. The driver was excellent, very flexible, friendly and knowledgeable. My husband had the unfortunate experience of needing to go to the hospital for a stomach bug. The staff at the Golden Banana was extremely helpful. They found us a driver right away, helped call the hospital and were very flexible when we had to extend our stay because of my husband's illness. This is a great place. I HIGHLY recommend staying at the Golden Banana.

author: goldengirl217
title: Great hotel and a great value, just outside of the main area of town
text: We stayed at the Golden Banana Boutique Resort for 3 nights in June, 2010. We paid 60 USD per night for a Suite room. We were a little worried before we came because the hotel was mentioned in a NY Times Article on gay destinations in Cambodia, and we almost cancelled our reservation (not that we are afraid of gays, but we were worried it would be more of a "party" atmosphere than we were looking for). We were so glad we didn't cancel! Golden Banana was a great little boutique hotel a 5 minute walk away from town. Our room was really great - all rooms overlook the pool and have a balcony and private outdoor tub along with an indoor bathroom. It was air conditioned with a TV and had everything we needed. Our rate also included breakfast which was very basic but did the trick to get us going in the morning. The hotel was very clean and had modern amenities. The saltwater pool was great, probably the best pool of our entire 3 week trip. The hotel is located on a side street just outside of town and is easily walkable whatever time of day (it's dark at night walking home but we still felt safe). We hired a Tuk-Tuk to bring us from the airport and for an 8-hour temple tour (for $13). We had the same driver the whole time (Mr CNN) and were really happy. The hotel did a great job of arranging all our plans. We couldn't have been happier with the Golden Banana. I would highly recommend this hotel for singles, couples, and families. It's a great deal and a really great hotel.

author: Lizarazu20
title: Fantastic Room, With Great Pool Area
text: Room: Great room. Clean, and well decorated, captures the feel of the place. Modern amenities, plus free wifi. Had a rooftop balcony, with outdoor bath tub and shower, which were nice. Rating: (4/5) Staff/Service: Work needs to be done in this department. Was a struggle to re-confirm reservation. Had to place many calls, as well as e-mails before it was sorted. Some were great and knowledagable, unfortunately it seems like there were only of them in the 15 or so personel that we dealt with. Seems like only a few people on staff are able to make decisions or do things and if they are occupied it can be annoying waiting to talk to them. Took follow- ups to get things at times. On two minor issues had to ask three times in order to have something refilled or placed in room. One extremely postive note; tuk-tuks can be charged to the room, which is a benefit to someone like me who relies on plastic more than cash. Rating: (2.5/5) Location: Only a 5 minute walk from were all the action is happening, in a nice quiet area. However, the walk is a little odd, as the road to the main street is either dirt or half completed. At night, it could be a little disconerning as it is not really lit until you are about 15 metres from the hotel. Rating: (4/5)

author: A_Mac2010
title: fantastic place to stay
text: Siem Reap was my final stop on a round the world trip and the Golden Banana boutique resort was the icing on the cake! I initially had only booked 3 nights but ended up staying for an extra 2 nights. The location is perfect- 5 minute walk to centre of Siem Reap down a quiet street- so you are near everything but yet can escape the hustle and bustle of the town. I stayed in one of their suites- gorgeous room which was really bright and spacious. My balcony (which came complete with an outdoor stone bath) overlooked the pool. Overall the decor is pretty cool. The staff were very friendly, they really made you feel welcome and nothing was ever a problem. They organised a great tuk-tuk driver to take me to the temples at Angkor on 3 different days. The lovely pool is a very welcome break from the temples and the 40+C temperatures. I actually ended up eating lunch most days by the pool- the food was really tasty and good value. They make great cocktails too! The included breakfast ,which was more than adequate, is also served beside the pool. Another handy feature is that they add everything including the cost of tuk-tuk/taxis etc to your final bill so you don't have to negotiate prices. Overall I thought the GB resort was good value and definitely worth $54/night. I really enjoyed my stay and will definitely be recommending the Golden Banana to my friends.

author: Gillian44
title: Perfect in every way
text: Siem Reap was our last stop of a 6 week holiday and we decided to splurge on the accommadation (we usually spend AUS $10-$35.) We emailed ahead and were lucky enough to get a room for $54. Their driver was waiting at the airport for us and delivered us to the Banana. We were greeted warmly and instantly knew the extra money was very well spent. The room was just beautiful and air con a real winner. The pool was a huge bonus and meals were tasty and well priced. THE STAFF. They are all just so happy which makes the experience memorable. Nothing was too much trouble and I believe they love being there. Of course we wanted to visit the temples and decided to take a guide. Good decision. Without one you can wonder around and admire the structures but with a knowledgable guide you can begin to understand ssssoooo much more. We were lucky enough to have a very kind gentleman by the name of Khen Yon. He was so much more than the average guide. He was willing to chat about sensative topics eg. Pol Pot , genocide, civil war etc. and how this effected himself and his family. I feel I experienced more with this particular guide than other travellers I spoke to. I feel the Golden Banana chooses their staff very carefully. Would love to visit again and again

author: sypanda
title: Paradise in Siem Reap
text: I can only echo what many people here are saying about Golden Banana Boutique Resort. I was a bit concerned about the price ($74 USD for villa), but figured the splurge would be worth it from all the reviews here. We had requested airport pick-up and were met promptly there. Upon arrival, we received welcome drinks and had a brief "orientation" of the resort and were able to ask questions about getting around/tours, etc. The staff (all men) were incredibly friendly and helpful at all hours! We took the villa - a beautiful 2-floored bit of luxury. (Upstairs we had our private outdoor bathtub, shower, lounge chairs. Very romantic!) The pool was a very welcome retreat during the inevitably HOT hours during the day. We opted to go out early to see the sunrise (5am), return around 9/10ish and go out again around 3pm. Location-wise - Golden Banana is PERFECTLy located - not in the midst of all the noise/action of Pub Street/Market, but within a 5-7 minute walk.
