We did not have to get tuk tuk's to-from our hotel at all! It was perfect! I was traveling with my fiance and his parents (from Belgium - first time in Asia). This was definitely our favourite accommodation in Cambodia!!! HIGHLY HIGHLY recommended for the location, the service, the luxury!

author: ghekko62
title: Never Felt more welcome
text: I had a great time at the golden banana resort. Great service, Very friendly staff and great laughs. However I would caution travelers. I did ask the hotel to book 2 seats for me on the bus to Phnom Penh (I have a larger build and the bus seats are small) but the hotel only booked one seat which made for a very uncomfortable trip for 6 hours by bus. the second thing was that I shared my email address with staff to keep in touch. One friendly staff member wrote to me and asked whether he could join me further on during my trip to Sihanoukville. I was surprised and unsure what exactly he was proposing. Was I to pay for his trip? It seemed forward for someone I didn't know very well. When I wrote and told him he couldn't join me he was not very impressed. This left a sour taste in my mouth after such friendly times. I booked this hotel off the internet and as a result did not get the cheapest price. Whilst this resort is a wonderful place to stay, there are much cheaper to be found in Siem Reap or you can get a better price just showing up without a booking. I thought it a little unfair that I booked 3 months in advance and paid $69 per night PLUS 10% which seemed to be the highest rate when others turned up with no booking and received a substantial discount. Having said all that, if money is no object this place is a great place to stay. Check that the staff get your onward bookings correct and be careful who you give your email address to, and you should have a great stay.

author: CharmSoh
title: Home of the best tuk tuk driver in town!
text: Cosy little boutique resort set in a fantastic location only minutes walk to the main food and shopping area (including Pub street and the night market). Here you will find lots of local and international food options as well as a convenient supermarket, pharmacy, spas/massage etc. Unfortunately the villas were full when we stayed, but the suite had everything we needed. The rooms were clean and comfortable with queen size bed, fan and a/c, big rain shower (including hot water) in the bathroom with really nice smelling liquid soap. Outside we had a semi secluded patio looking onto the pool with deck chair, small table and outdoor bath/shower. Unfortunately because our room was on the ground floor (W room) and right next to the pool, it attracted a lot of mosquitoes. We dealt with this by spraying our room each night before we left for dinner and returning to only one or two mozzies that still managed to eat me and my bf. My suggestion is to ask for a room on the 2nd floor as there may be less there. Note: the resort will spray your room for you each afternoon. It was great to have a pool to come home to for a cool down or just to chill out after an exhausting day in the heat. The complimentary breakfast was healthy and tasty – fresh seasonal fruit with yogurt, fresh OJ plus eggs with toast and butter, coffee/tea - perfect way to start off our busy temple sight seeing days. One day we had to wake up very early to reach Angkor Wat before sunrise and the resort arranged for us to have our breakfast earlier than their usual time. By the way, the Amok on the lunch time menu is delicious! I think the best part of the resort was the service. Everyone working here is very polite and helpful, especially our tuk tuk driver Kimyin. Definitely recommend you ask him to take you out to the temples. He is a very friendly guy, can share knowledge about the temple history and most importantly has the coolest green and hot pink tuk tuk in Siem Reap, the envy of all tuk tuk drivers! The Golden Banana Resort is an excellent choice for Siem Reap accommodation, highly recommend it!

author: blwright
title: Golden Banana is GOLDEN!
text: We booked five nights at the Golden Banana Resort based on the positive reviews on TA. Once here we extended our stay to TEN – just couldn’t bear to leave such a lovely, tranquil oasis in Siem Reap. We loved this resort and highly recommend it! The rooms are comfortable: Big bed, TV with many int’l channels, WFIF, mini-bar, large safety deposit box, excellent bathroom, balcony with lounge chairs and tub and shower!! The only minor complaint about the room would be that the lighting at night is a bit dim for old folks like us with weak eyes. The pool and garden setting is just ideal after a hot tour of the wats. The restaurant serves breakfast all morning – such a thoughtful gesture which accommodates various schedules for the guests. The breakfast is delicious and you have a couple of options. We always chose the “egg” option which included: a large bowl of fruit, freshly squeezed orange juice, freshly pressed coffee, eggs to order, and whole wheat toast. The staff is polite and attentive. We also ate a few dinner meals at the restaurant. It has a limited menu, but the food was excellent and no more expensive than walking into the restaurant section in town. The front desk staff is very helpful and can book a guide or tuk-tuk driver for you. You can rent a bike which is a fun way to get around town or the Angkor Archeological Sites if you have enough time and want a leisurely tour with some exercise. Our tour guide, Mr. Vuthy, arranged through the hotel, was excellent. He knew the best times to be at certain wats for the best light and fewer tourists. He also knew all the bet places for photo and took some wonderful photos of us. Best of all, he took us to places “off the beaten track” and helped us organize donating a well for a local village. If you are in Siem Reap over the weekend, you should be sure to go to the free Beatocello concert in support of the Kantha Bopha hospital which offers free health care to Cambodian children and pregnant mothers.

author: Dogma
title: Friendly staff, Excellent Location, Lovely pool and room, Good food and drink
text: Title pretty much says it all. It was a pleasure to stay at GB. The staff was always smiling, happy, and so helpful. The location couldn't be any closer to Old Market- just walk out alleyway, a little up the street, and cross the bridge (and walking past the BBQ restaurants when they're grilling makes the mouth water!). The atmosphere at GB is quiet and relaxing. Even when kids are swimming and playing noisily in pool, there's a nice calm and contentment to the whole atmosphere. We stayed in a villa and it was lovely with a nice king bed, free wifi, a great bathroom rain shower and very steep steps to a wonderful balcony with a stone soaking tub, outdoor shower, and lounge chairs. It was literally one step to the pool. Breakfast was very good and the Cambodian coffee extraordinaire. We ate dinner of Cambodian BBQ one night (served 18:00-19:00h only) and it was superb. In addition to the nice bar and the bartender who was quite skilled at his craft, we were happy, well fed, and slightly tipsy- what a great day after temple trekking. The stone tub makes a great bubble bath (provided) for soaking except note the privacy curtain is more a warning for others on opposite balconies to practice their skills of averting their eyes. We thoroughly enjoyed the range of people staying at GB(young, old, single, families, couples, gay, straight, blonde, brunette, etc.) and everyone looked relaxed and happy. Do not hesitate to stay here. One note to the management is to remove the downright ugly and slightly creepy painting on the wall in the villa opposite the bed (a prior review mentioned it too). It's seems out of place with the decor and rather forced in design and intent. Our next visit to Siem Reap will find us staying here again.

author: KierSF
title: simply stunning
text: From the moment I arrived in Siem Reap until the second i left The Golden Banana resort (TGBR) took care of everything. I was met at the airport by a Tuk Tuk driver which had been pre-arranged by TGBR. I managed to get a slightly earlier flight from BKK so i shot off an email from bangkok airport letting them know and as if by magic they had arranged the pick up with less than 1 hour notice. The hotel is maybe 30 minutes from the airport. it is about a 5 minute walk to the main drag of Siem Reap. The hotel is gorgeous, all designed around a beautiful salt water pool ( fresh water attracts mosquitoes). I had charming room/suite on the ground level. Comfy bed, high end bathroom with rainforest like shower. Patio overlooks pool with outdoor stone (?granite) bath for that all important al fresco bathing experience. Pool was really nice temperature and spotless. The service was flawless with really friendly staff. Breakfast was included which was pretty good. The hotel arranged slight seeing tour to Angkor Wat which was predictably spectacular. The only slight downer was that I was traveling alone and this would of been a wonderful place to share. I am working on that front and will come back with a beautiful man next time :-)

author: jrcw75th
title: Wish We Could Have Stayed Longer
text: I went to Siem Reap/Angkor Wat with a friend. We stayed in a room on the top floor. While the room was a bit on the small side. It was still very nice. The shower in the bathroom was wonderful as was the private stone tub and shower on the balcony. The bartender Sima made us some wonderful Mojitos. It is a very quick walk into the old section of town. We ate at the Blue Pumkin and Khmer Kitchen and both were outstanding. I was sorry we didn't have more time to shop. Our tuk tuk driver was Natt and he was provided by the hotel. He was always super punctual and even picked us up from the airport and took us back to the airport at a very early hour. We were also able to get a very early check in to the hotel. The salt water pool is very nice, and is the centerpiece of the hotel. You can get laundry done at very minimal cost, and the mini bar features $2 Angkor beers. One night one of the staff walked myself and another guest into town to Linga, which was very nice and fun - and also super inexpensive.

author: ChilliGarlic
title: Golden Find!
text: I was recommended to stay at the Golden Banana by a friend after mentioning I was going to see Angkor Wat. And I'm so glad I followed his advice! It's a beautiful hotel - a lot of thought went into the design and the attention to detail is quite wonderful. Nestled in a quiet lane, only a few minutes walk or tuk tuk ride to the centre of town, and just 30 minutes from the temples by tuk tuk (transport and perfect guide arranged by the hotel.) I loved the things written in the in-room directory and the menus regarding the resort and staff. Modern, witty, and completely genuine. Not your standard corporate prattle that means nothing. Even the reproduction Yun Min Jun artworks around the resort are contemporary and witty - something a larger place would be terrified of! The staff were totally friendly and helpful and knew their jobs. They seemed very appreciative of their jobs and that reflected in how they treated customers. A wonderful vibe. The bar staff explained to me that they are also able to study because their fees are paid by the hotel, which has trained them as well, giving them a career and a future. It's impressive to make such an effort with staff - they really repay it with loyalty and a genuine desire for the success of the hotel. The pool is a gem, and the food is delicious and served anywhere you want, from your balcony to the poolside. Free wifi was a great bonus as well. This was a genuinely delightful experience. Oh. And the coffee is GREAT!

author: Spacex
title: the BEST !!!!!
text: My partner & i stayed at this little piece of paradise only last month ( November,08 ). It was truly a wonderful experience and a peaceful place to be. Our room was called BUTTERFLY PEE ..........hehe. Only just a few minutes from the dust heat & bustle that Siem Reap township can be on most days & only a short US $1 Tuk Tuk ride from the old market area. But a really easy 5 minute walk through the local village to all the food , foot massages and shopping you might require from the stunning Cambodian people. Every food you can imagine can be found here in Siem Reap. We stayed in the new resort which was just beautiful !!! Although not complete then....I am sure it would be by now as it was all systems go and we noticed the developing changes in the short 5 days we were there. We had a quiet room overlooking the pool and the room was clean , lovely furnished and serviced impecably daily. Mind you this room was BRAND NEW . It was air conditioned , an outside bathtub on the verandah for that cool evening soak , a safe, flat screen TV , a mini bar fridge , a great bed, fantastik bathroom, views over the pool and across the local village roof tops. All you need can be found here. This hotel is NOT ... a big concrete structure of a hotel like the many big ones you will see in Siem Reap. The GOLDEN BANANA is small enough to offer each guest one on one service & you will find it mostly quiet and peaceful. I see no reason at all why you would not be satisfied with this hotel which offers wonderful Cambodian staff at your service. Truly friendly and there to assist. Thankyou again to the great staff & management of the Golden Banana...... we can not wait to get back there sometime very soon....................... Conway & John X AUSTRALIA

author: Navalator
title: Surprise at the end of the path
text: The place had all the appearance of studied deferred maintenance causing it to resemble a resort that might be described in a W. Somerset Maugham novel. I fully expected to breach upon a dining table by the pool populated by Maugham, Hemingway, John Dos Passos, E. E. Cummings, Frederick Gerald Haxton and other intellectual gay expats chain-dragging on Gauloises, sipping scotch neats and commenting on the bubble butt belonging to Ahmed the pool boy and the bulge in pants of the young Cambodian waiter: A place where Dorothy Parker would love to sit and develop insults of the rich, famous and decadent. The hosts were nonplused, gracious, informative and solicitous: Perfect for the atmosphere of the place. Staff friendly, charming and professional. And, the food was outstanding. There is a house specialty called ”Amok” described as a traditional Khmer dish, Mekong/Tonle Sap River fish fillet wrapped & steamed in banana leaf with Khmer herbs. It comes in a small package but is rich and filling. Be hungry before you order this dish. Another dish to die for is the house Vegetable Soup, a mixture of potato, cabbage, carrot, Chinese cabbage & cauliflower soaking in a broth of secret herbs and spices. You just cannot get enough of this very tasty dish. All the other items we ordered of the menu were first-rate and complimentary to the milieu. The rack rate is within reason and well worth the stay. Access to the venue is through a rather seedy series of paths, prime examples of the neglect of the Cambodian civic infrastructure by the corrupt government, that might startle the unwary traveler but the risk is worth the reward.

author: raocardio2
title: Recent stay
text: my husband and I checked into the hotel less than 2 weeks ago. The service is not good at all. No complimentary bottle water , when we requested more Nespresso capsules , there was just one, we were informed that the evening staff will take care of it. And they did not . The rooms are below par, the windows open to the outside, very dark and dingy, the location is not central . The front desk is not courteous. TV did not work properly. We checked in only at 3.30 or so in the evening. I informed them that same night we would be checking out in the morning. And we did so at 10 AM. We were charged over over 1000 dollars for our stay . The front desk informed us we will be penalized for not staying the 4 days we had booked. They refused to understand the reasons for our unhappiness. We are very dissatisfied and disappointed with the Hotel and staff. I would like to be reimbursed fully . I do not recommend this hotel. We checked in to the Intercontinental and loved it. Wonderful hotel and staff, very good concierge service.

author: shaneinsweden
title: Quirky, quiet and very private - good location for airport and shopping
text: We had booked the secret room, which I think is one of the cheaper rooms in the hotel - down in the cellar. It had its own lovely patio and the decor was really nice and quite quirky. Although there was a laundromat/detergent smell outside the room - perhaps there is a laundry room nearby? Not at all unpleasant just unusual, The whole hotel in fact has a fairly unique and quirky character, from the staff who were really very friendly and helpful to the his-and-hers bath robes. A couple of things really stand out with this hotel that aren't probably apparent from the description: 1. I don't think I have ever been on a quieter city street. There was literally no-one on the whole street when we came back to the hotel in the evening. If you are looking for some peace and quiet then I can really recommend this hotel. 2. Your door key doesn't open the front door in the evening and you have to be let in by one of the staff (who opened the door very promptly after we rang the bell). There is no chance of any non guest wandering around this hotel. If you value your privacy this might well be an important point. 3. The hotel is really handy for the airport, the Marionneau bus stop is about 10 minutes walk away on the nr 1 line to the airport. 4. The hotel is also pretty handy for shopping in and around the golden triangle

author: rjrLeeds
title: Absolute bliss
text: Where do you start when you try to review a place like Yndo. It's not just the beautiful bedrooms with every attention to detail. Nor is it the beautiful towels and towelling robes or the equisite Hermes toileteries. It's not just the sublimely comfortable beds with duck down pillows. Nor the wonderful breakfast of breads and home made jams, great coffee, fruit salad and yoghurt. Nor is it just the great style of every aspect of the hotel. No, it's the wonderful staff who make you feel so special. They can't do enough for you. Even down to offering to collect you from a local restaurant. They sorted out a lost passport. They just want you to enjoy your stay. It's surrounded by some wonderful restaurants too. The Garopapilles is 200yds down the street and is a great dining experience (the best meal I've had in France for many years). We had rooms 100 and 102 (Cosy rooms) on the ground floor with their own private terrace. Great bathroom with wonderful shower. Everything well thought out. This is as good as a hotel gets. Immense attention to detail and it really shows.

author: KPH5
title: Best place to stay in Bordeaux!
text: We arrived exhausted minus one suitcase early on Friday morning after a transatlantic flight and a very stressful transfer in Madrid. From the moment we arrived in Bordeaux, Yndohotel started taking care of us! We had arranged for a transfer from the airport through the hotel, more expensive than a regular taxi, but he waited for us as we made a claim for the suitcase and then informed the hotel that we were on our way. The transfer was easy and very pleasant. By the time we arrived at the hotel, they had already contacted our airline to track down our bag and they informed us it would be delivered that night! With some fantastic coffee and snacks to fortify us, we went for a walk around town to get some fresh air. By the time we got back to the hotel, they had made sure that our room was ready early for us - much appreciated! We stayed in a 'crazy' room - which was modern, comfortable, stylish and spacious. We loved every aspect of it! We had contacted them via email to arrange a dinner reservation for that night at Les Miles - set 'surprise' menu which was fantastic! When we returned we had a glass of wine on their peaceful terrace overlooking the courtyard and one of their homemade Bordeaux specialities - cannelés -delicious! They suggested we take the two bikes they have in the hotel (old but perfect for cycling around town - everyone bikes in Bordeaux) and cycle around town and go to the new wine museum the next morning. Great idea - saw so much. Again, they had great suggestions for dinner and made reservations for us. From start to finish every single person at Yndohotel made us feel at home and like one of the family. I cannot wait to come back to Bordeaux and to stay here again!

author: bebeminion
title: Chic boutique hotel in Bordeaux
text: One would have never thought there's such a cool, art-deco, modern type hotel (and looks brand new too!) in Bordeaux so when we saw the raving we quickly booked ourselves 2 nights at Yndo as well. As the Cosy room was sold out the second night, we had to switch rooms. Normally we don't like that but we figured why not. And am so glad we did cos the second night in the Crazy room was really amazing. The room was huge and has a large sitting area and coffee table so feels like you just walked into some designer's apartment. There's also a 4-poster bed with funky "drapes" around it which made you feel like you're in the jungle a bit (probably cos of the color...) and the mattress is super comfortable. Every piece of furniture in this room (as well as the Cosy room) are all like designer pieces. My only complaint is the shower. The shower in the Cosy room has no door but just a small piece of glass so all the water flooded the bathroom floor quickly and we had to ask for another floor mat. Also the water is a bit weak at times. But other than that, all the staff at Yndo are all very friendly and everything is very new! We also love the paintings that are being exhibited at the hotel when we were there. Really great work by this artist whom I've forgotten the name. Would highly recommend this hotel to anyone who is in for something cool and NEW! The hotel is also a short walk (about 10 mins) from the "city center".

author: ketel_always
title: Better than we imagined
text: We visited the Bordeaux area for four days in early July with some day trips exploring nearby areas such as Cap Ferret and St Emillion. We couldn't have asked for a better experience than the Yndo. Every time we returned home from a great day, the Yndo was there waiting with a very comfortable and very clean room in an ideal setting. The room was updated in a modern style that somehow didn't over power the traditional style of the building. It has an A/C system that could get it as cold as we wanted. It was 99 degrees one day so that was very important. It's in the center but just far enough away from the epicenter to be very quiet. no more than a 15 minute walk to most sites and restaurants. The staff to guest ratio was better than I thought existed. If we wanted something, we just asked and several staff members would be there to help. The first day there, we were tired from the early train ride over from Paris so we just said feed us. Out came fresh melon and Iberico ham plus some delicious veggie lasagna and a great wine paring. They were always attentive and helpful with dinner recommendations and reservations. They went the extra mile to get an extremely difficult lunch reservation for a place that has really odd hours and days that they just aren't there. The cost per night was reasonable for a 5 star hotel but I will say, be prepared to pay for this level of service for the food and drink. Breakfast is 30 euro for example but everything is high quality. I have no problem with paying more when the service and food meet the high levels they have at the Yndo.

author: GalleryGirl64
title: Modern Art meets the Belle Epoque in Bordeaux
text: I recently visited Bordeaux for a couple of nights. Not somewhere I had particularly chosen to visit, it was just the nearest place of interest to stay on a trip to watch my son during his England Counties rugby international which was taking place nearby. The hotel was fantastic. A really clever combination of modern art, subtle and sophisticated interior design and real comfort. Everything was high quality and had clearly been put together by somebody with electic - but brilliant - taste. Our room although more or less 'standard' as described by the hotel's website was large and airy with a wonderful skylight with electronic shutters and a fabulous huge egg shaped bath. The staff were really helpful and very, very sweet. Nothing was too much trouble and before we left we were shown around some of the other rooms of the hotel by the receptionist, as I had mentioned how much I liked the decor. All of the rooms were different to one another - and all of them were fabulously proportioned and beautifully designed. Breakfast was served in a gorgeous little room which had a pretty outdoor terrace set within a courtyard. The hotel was in a great location. Just a 5-10 minute walk into the very centre of town where there are many nice bars, brasseries and a surprisingly high quality array of shops. If I was in the vicinity again I would certainly stay here. It was a breath of fresh air, relaxing, beautiful - and had staff who really cared about their guests. Well done YNDO. A wonderful short break. An unexpected delight.

author: annpK7508VK
title: MU Hotel
text: Arrived in the afternoon. Didn't know we could arrange for hotel pickup. Looking around for transport when we chanced upon the Hotel's mini van. Waited a while for driver and we were fortunate for all 4 of us to hop on. Ride was 10 minutes from airport. Driver was very friendly and helpful. We couldn't check in until 3 pm. However driver volunteered to drop us off at Old Town. Hotel lobby is modern. Breakfast spread was modest and they changed an item or 2 as the 3 days went by. Rooms were clean and service excellent. Location wise relatively convenient. We could walk to church (Catholic) and Ipoh Parade (Shopping Mall). Hotel also provide shuttle services at 9 am, 12 pm, 3 pm and 6 pm to nearby places of interest. Our only disappointment came on our last day when we had booked our transport to the airport only to be told that the driver had to proceed to the airport urgently to pick up guest and leaving us stranded. There was another couple who were also supposed to be on same pickup and they were not too pleased. In the end, we booked a Grab that was RM7 to the airport. Didn't want to wait only to miss our flight. On the whole a pleasant stay. Will stay again next time.

author: Merlin0921
title: Comfortable and Secure
text: I spent two nights in the Mu. The room was spacious but spartanly furnished. (I had the second cheapest room; I understand there is a slightly smaller cheaper option available.) The bed was OK. Chairs were small. There was one small round table, and a small desk built into the wall. Bathroom was fine, shower good. Staff was friendly and efficient. Breakfast options were predominantly Asian and were kept well-supplied. Apple juice was the only juice available during my time, and the only fruit offered was watermelon and a green melon. The hotel seems to cater to Chinese tour groups, which resulted in a very full dining area the two mornings I was there. You must pay double to get your laundry back before 2:00PM the following day even if you turn it in before 10:00AM. Most hotels can do better than that, and can offer same-day service without extra charge if you turn things in early in the morning. The hotel is very secure. Both the elevator, your floor hallway, and your room require your room key card to open. It was quiet and I slept well.

author: gmsgms2016
title: Clean and adequate.
text: Stayed 3 nights. The lobby is well designed with colorful and arty circular cushions. A self served dispenser for welcome drinks. 3 computer terminals for internet. Stairs, or lift, leads up to the breakfast area. The selection is modest but adequate. There is a small play area for children on the second floor next to the restaurant. The rooms are clean and new. Has all the amenities. Toothbrushes, shavers and etc provided. Water pressure slightly low but usable. The temperature control was not working well - it was either too cold or hot. Can’t get anything in between. Our room had a nice view of the sun rise. We even saw a short burst of fireworks on one of the nights in the distance. There are some coffee shops and a dim sum restaurant within a min of walking of the hotel. Many small shops around. Overall clean and new. Will stay again. The

author: didie36
title: Enjoyable Stay
text: Check in from 17-19 Dec 2017. Nice 3 star hotel located in town center. Reception was good and no problem checking in and out which was smooth. They collect RM50 if pay by cash and RM00 by credit card for deposit which is refundable upon check out. Standard room was a little small but adequate for 2 adult and 1 child. Rooms has all the essential needs including complete toiletries (2 sets toothbrush, shaver set, shower cap, sanitary bag & cotton buds), torchlight, iron and iron-board provide in the closet, safe-box & minibar that sometimes not all in 4/5* provide. Breakfast has tasty & adequate meal choices and children from 12 years and below can eat with free of charge. The hotel is walking distances to town attractions and Ipoh Parade will take about 20 mins walk. Every night, there is a Chinese hawker next to hotel that you can enjoy Ipoh food. Infront of hotel, there is also a mamak stall open for 24hrs. Basically to find food is all within reach walking 5-10mins. We also tried the Gym, air-conditioned but small and not many equipment's. However it's enough to sweat out and we could move around comfortably besides they also provide mineral water. Overall, very satisfied for the price paid. Will definitely return back and recommend this hotel to anyone who wish stay in Ipoh. Thumbs up & keep up the good work!

author: bezdtravellor
title: Best bang for buck hotel
text: When you first pull up near this hotel, you will notice certain things missing. The first being the absence of the humble bellhop and another being the absence of fauna surrounding the hotel. The first is a real bother for people with a lot of luggage. You would be provided a trolley if you ask so that's nice to know. When you step in, there's a completely contrasting vibe to the hotel. It looks modern, well lit and feels luxurious, in a 2017 way. Checking in is something you have to wait for a while because most of the time this hotel is fully booked. Once we did, we stepped in one of the most compact rooms we have ever been into. Luggage storage is not an issue even in that small space and the wardrobe is among the most tightly packed I have ever seen in my entire life with an ironing board and iron and space to hold at least 3 camping bags. If you are feeling tired after admiring the rooms, the beds are incredibly soft and comfortable. We got a room with twin beds and the only thing I have to complain is the placement of the plug. It's not in the middle so at any one time only the person sleeping near the plug has access to it. The food is above average which is something I have come to expect in recent times. The staff are friendly and are doing great even if there is only one attendant at any one time. This is also rather affordable coming in at RM167+.

author: JoanneHoSL
title: A bolster in the room - enough said!
text: I would normally pack my bolster along when I'm on a road trip - but I had forgotten this time. Guess what- the rooms come with bolsters! I have never been to a hotel which provided bolsters - so this was a pretty awesome addition - and for that, I give them an excellent rating. However, the hotel has the weirdest policy, especially being in the service industry. We had book 2 standard rooms over Agoda as there wasn't an option for a Family room when we put in 2 adults + 2 kids. We requested for interconnecting rooms. We found out that they didn't have interconnecting rooms. Called up the hotel to request for us to change from the 2 rooms to the Family room instead (which they had available) but apparently, instead of just paying the difference (probably around RM70) - they wanted us to pay RM150 for the switch. When I asked them why, they just kept insisting it was hotel policy. If I pay RM150 extra (double the actual difference), I would essentially be paying for 3 rooms. I don't mind topping up the difference, but I've never heard of paying such a premium for the change. They couldn't explain WHY - stating it was just policy. Was it administrative charges? No, it was just hotel policy. This was the message conveyed over the phone prior to us arriving. By the time I got there, I didn't want to press further. But it was a disappointing start to the stay. Thank goodness they had bolsters to save the day.

author: greatserpent
title: Good hotel with only a few negatives
text: Cons:- 1. on one of the days the breakfast was limited because even the noodles were spicy, i didn't really understand why they have spicy food as not everyone can eat that but in general breakfast was pretty decent although strictly at 10:30am they really pack everything up. 2. housekeeping problems, we stayed 6 nights...on 4 of the days there were minor problems that were a bit annoying such as cotton buds not replaced, a replacement toilet paper when the toilet paper was clearly near the end would of been nice, towels not replaced on one day, shower gel not refilled on one of the days, one of the twin beds the duvet they replaced had a bad smell but my duvet was fine, only two out of the 6 days the housekeeping did a good job and i believe it's because there was a different cleaner on those 2 days i think it was day 3 and 4 that was good, the rest had small issues. 3. location was pretty decent but if you don't have a car it's not in the old town so it's quite a walk but they do provide shuttle bus at specific times. 4. pillow was above average i'd say but it wasn't a really great one, after the 2nd day when i woke up in the morning my lower neck would hurt just a little bit but it's definitely pretty alright, there's a lot worse pillows out there. this is always personal preference though. Pros:- 1. reasonable speed wifi (not the greatest but at least you can stream youtube at 360p without it stopping unlike a lot of other hotels), 2. reasonable amount of parking space, 3. good reception staff, 4. spacious room, table and chair in the room, tv was pretty alright, bed mattress was super comfortable, loved the shower (it's separated from the toilet so that was great), water pressure was good, hot water was good, shower gel and shampoo dispenser provided loved the setup of that, hairdryer provided, big sink and bench to put your stuff in the bathroom, mini fridge provided 5. nice view over some part of Ipoh from the 5th floor. I would stay here again though, it was quite comfortable.

author: SimranG130
title: Perfect for family stay.
text: My family & I total 4 people, stayed here for 2 nights. Upon arriving we were greeted by friendly frontdesk lady. We were not really sure on continuing our stay for the next night so we booked a family deluxe room only for one night. We asked the front desk lady to reserve a room for us for the next day and we particularly suggested if we could remain in the same room however, we were told that we might have to change our room the next day as it is booked under other family. The following day, another frontdesk lady named Jing Chi was in charge. when we were about to move into a different room, the friendly smiling frontlady desk named Jing Chi tried her best and made us remain to stay in our hotel room. We were so relieved upon hearing that as shifting rooms meant that we had to shift our luggages as well. So overwhelmed by the service provided. Overall the staffs were very friendly & welcoming. The whole working staff were friendly, but I could only note the names of the frontdesk ladies, Farhanis & Jing Chi. The best part I love is that, there are many sockets to plug in my gadgets. The only thing I look in hotel rooms. Also, the fact that they provide shampoo in big dispensars. Overall 5stars rating for this hotel. Perfect for a family stay. Definitely one of the best in Ipoh.

author: vn06
title: We will be back!
text: We were very lucky to be picked up from the airport in a spanking new Starex. Luxurious and most comfortable. The General Manager, Kenneth Perreau, was very thoughtful from the start; he went through great lengths to find us a room configuration with enough shower arrangements that would fit our family size. I liked that the shower gel and shampoo are in big dispensers. not in little bottles. I read the previous reviews and it is evident that the hotel is taking all constructive comments seriously and improving wherever possible. Kudos to the management! There was a very pleasant bellhop who helped us with our bags, both at check in and check out. Rooms were of a good size. More than enough plugs in the rooms to charge our multiple gadgets, something I look out for in a hotel room! Nice to have an iron and ironing board in the room too. All the amenities one needs in a room.. good enough even for a business traveller. We were at the Mu Bar practically every night. We enjoyed the nasi lemak at breakfast spread (the sambal is nicely spicy!). We were met with courteous and very friendly staff at all the outlets. This has been a lovely family vacation and we will surely be back.

author: JoNunis
title: Modern clean rooms
text: Booked 2 rooms for my family of five. It's our first time at this hotel and was pleasantly surprised by its clean, modern chic rooms. Love the fresh zesty colours within the hotel. When we entered the rooms it had fresh clean smell. Very comfy beds including the extra bed we requested. Bathroom was also clean with modern design. Basic amenities were provided in each of our rooms e.g. Coffee/tea, fridge & ironing board. One of our rooms had a spacious balcony. Buffet breakfast was really value for money. It had a mixture of western & Asian dishes. Love the nasi lemak! Another plus point the hotel is a walking distance to the famous food shops in Ipoh. We took about 10mins to those areas. And there are few Chinese shops around the hotel as well. The MU roofbar was one of the highlights where my family had a great time with the scenery of Ipoh at night and good music and affordable drinks and delicious finger food. Would definitely return to stay in this hotel

author: Natinbali
title: Best Hotel in Ipoh
text: Among many hotels in Ipoh, I chose MU Hotel (formerly Ibis Styles Ipoh) for my 2-nights stay in Ipoh with my family. My main reason is because its Ibis brand and their location. The location of MU Hotel is perfect since it is located at Jalan Sultan Iskandar. You can reach many tourist attractions and eateries in a walking distance from the hotel. We arrived quite early (about 11.00 pm), but the receptionist Ms. Felicia allowed us to check-in early. We got 2 Standard Queen Rooms on 6th floor. The room was surprisingly very spacious. Even the bathroom is so big. No complain at all for the room since it was very clean and comfy. They even provide hairdryer, iron + desk, flashlight, something that we rarely find in other hotels. For such an affordable price, we also got a complimentary breakfast. The breakfast is good. Limited options but all is delicious. I personally love their Nasi Lemak. For those who driving, MU Hotel also provides an indoor and outdoor parking space. I will recommend this hotel to everyone who will visit Ipoh. Definitely will stay here again if I got chance to visit Ipoh in the future.

author: flooly
title: No longer the Ibis that I know
text: I am a regular at this hotel. This time I am booked for 3 nights. Upon checked in, I found out that from 1 April 2017, it is no longer under Ibis but renamed MU hotel. We needed to re-register as they were using a new system. First day, room was not made until 5pm when the house-keeping came knocking on the door. We told him it is not necessary any more. The worse was there is major renovations going on which was not informed on the website. The signage at the hotel was barely noticeable and was also not informed to the guests upon check in. Drilling and knocking sound which is so near to our room. After going down to the reception to complain about the renovation noise, we could not take it and decided to check out. I needed to go back to the room to pack my things. I could not use the card key to open my room door, so I went down again. There was a guy supposedly manager insisted that there is nothing wrong with the card and went up to the room with me. He could not open the room either and he went down with the card while I waited at the room door. After a long wait, I went downstairs to find that he was in his office. I asked him why he did not come back with the key and he said he is doing something to reformat the card. I was very angry and said that he is punishing me for complaining and deliberately left me standing outside the room. He then reformat the card at the reception which took less than a few seconds. Without the backings of international chain like Ibis, I expected the service/condition to deteriorate but this is very soon and very disappointing.

author: doaks80
title: Nice hotel in a fairly slummy area
text: This hotel is a block or so across the main road from the area with the night markets that most tourists will be interested in. The surroundings of this hotel actually feel very poor and run down, which stands in contrast to the Hotel itself which is 4 to 5 star, and looks very modern both inside and out. I booked through an online booking website, and was given a free upgrade to a deluxe suite room with another TV. I was very impressed with the room - it had a large bedroom and another large lounge area, and a modern and nice bathroom with decent included bathroom disposables. I was most impressed with the view to the East of Ipoh which was basically a vista of limestone cliffs and mountains. Beautiful. The rooftop bar was basic but nice, with more beautiful views of Ipoh and surrounds (the hotel is by far the tallest building in the immediate area). Breakfast was average (but included in the room cost), standard continental fare. I found the staff average. Check-in was slow, and they struggled to book a taxi for me when I was leaving. They were also not very knowledgeable of the area - I asked about the location of an ATM as I had little cash with me, and the suggested a mall 30 minutes walk away, when in fact I found not one, but a whole string of foreign-supporting ATMs and banks along Jalan Yang Kalsom about a 2 minute stroll just to the west of the hotel. Around the hotel there are quite a number of eateries, including a food court literally at the base of the hotel. It is all very local and while probably very authentic, not very nice. If you stay here, it is about a 10 minute stroll North-West across the main street Jalan Sultan Iskander and into the night-market district where there is a much better range of restaurants and quality street food, much more tourist friendly, but still filled with local Chinese eating out too. All in all I really enjoyed my stay in Ipoh, and found this hotel to be a very nice place to explore it from. The only real downside is the location is at the fringe of what I would consider walking distance to the old-town area, which was fine for me but if you were not so fit and wanted to explore the old-town area every day you might want to look at somewhere closer.

author: Dav_Goh
title: SImple & Nice, Value for Money
text: For those who drive, free parking is available at the basement which as I observed, can park around 20 cars. Yes its very limited. Before the entrance to the basement there is parking lot which can park 6 cars. If both places are full, you can still park at the roadside, but remember to buy and put the parking coupon from 8am-6pm. The room & bathroom are both in good condition, tidy & clean, no weird smell. Not too spacious but good enough for us who just stayed 1 night with 1 big luggage bag. Refrigerator, iron, hair dryer & other basic things are available. The bed is queen size, so not to expect a big bed. Breakfast was included with the booking I made. Not the most varieties you would hoping for but is good enough if not too picky. Local food like fried noodles, nasi lemak, toast, coffee, fruits, noodle with soups are available on the day we stay. There are few PCs located at the lobby floor but I didn't use it. Not sure is it free to access to Internet, but should be. Free Wifi is available and yet because I didn't use it, no comment on the connection quality. There are 2 chinese restaurants nearby the hotel which are available for lunch & dinner time. But not those famous place in Ipoh you would have want to go.

author: /undefined
title: Comfortable and clean... Great staff
text: Stayed 4D3N in the Deluxe Room. Within walking distance to new town area and Ipoh Parade. Tucked in a quiet corner away from the areas with main activities - which is great. Bedroom was clean. Bed was comfortable. Toilet and shower facilities were clean. Living room was cosy with sofa. Great ambiance in the room. Although my room preference was room away from elevator, I was okay with the room next to elevator because I didn't experience any disturbance throughout the day. Like the ambiance of the breakfast. Sufficient spread for a 3 star hotel. While the food items can be greasy at times, it was manageable for me due to the presence of the noodle/soup section and the bread section. Rooftop bar was a great idea, but the fans were insufficient to maintain a cool environment in the evening. Otherwise, I would not mind getting a drink there in the evening. Can consider installing air cooler units instead of fans. Can consider air-conditioning a section of the rooftop bar. Overall, hotel staff have been friendly and helpful. Attentive to the need of the hotel guests.

author: amiel99
title: Still good
text: My first stay was 2 years ago when it was newly opened just before Chinese New Year. Not as spanking clean now but no issues at all with cleanliness in the room. Free buffet breakfast was adequate for me. I really don't need an extensive spread but food must be edible aka tasty. There's an egg counter but no ham or bacon just eggs, cheese, onions, red chillies. Delicious nasi lemak with sambal and chicken rendang (yum) and condiments. There's also chicken sausage, baked beans, salad, fresh fruits, mee goreng. Clear soup and laksa with bee hoon and yellow noodles. Coffee, tea and chilled juices. All these kept me going till lunch. In-room wifi was strong and stable. There's free basement parking for guests but I reckon anyone can just park their cars there as the gantry was lifted (where's the security?) If you are a night owl and looking for supper before 12am there are a few eateries within 100m. Else, Ibis' MU Bar opens till 1am daily and comes with a beautiful night view. If you just want a place to rest for the night (we checked in at 8pm) and have an edible breakfast at the hotel in the morning, Ibis does the job pretty well. Else there are a few new and recently renovated hotels around. Make your pick but for me it will still be this whenever I'm in Ipoh.

author: lavendydream
title: An alright hotel, clean & no frills
text: Stayed at the Ibis Styles Ipoh hotel over the last weekend for one night. It was a first time visit, chose this hotel as it was part of the Accor hotel groups, so just to try it out. Hotel design and architecture was nice, chic and colorful, with the ibis styles feel to it, especially for common areas like the lobby, first floor sitting area and restaurant. It was especially quiet during my visit, seems due to school holidays ending and hotel was not crowded. So check in was a breeze for me, I was the only one guest at the counter. Service was okay, friendly, but felt much training needed as most staff seems inexperienced, to match the Accor standard. A first impression of the rooms, clean but very small. I booked the standard room (which was supposed to be 25 sq m but looked much smaller), felt it too claustrophobic so had it upgraded to a Deluxe room, which had a living area and a dressing table corner (bathroom was the same). It was much more decent and breathable space. I also took a glance at the other room categories while considering the upgrade; there are also standard courtyard room (smoking floors) and a Deluxe Suite (the only one suite room in the hotel). For those who do not mind room space and just needed a bed, standard room will do fine, since it's still more value for money. Other facilities in the hotel include a business centre (two PC terminals with some cordial welcome drink at the lobby floor) and a Mu Bar (mini rooftop bar on 7th floor), no gym nor pool though. Breakfast served was decent (for an ibis), taste was fine but rather limited variety of choice. Hotel car park is at the basement level, parking space was limited but there are also roadside parking available beside the hotel (chargeable fee during weekdays). Overall, for my first visit, I find the ibis styles Ipoh an alright hotel (decent, clean, no frills), not bad for a choice in Ipoh, but not as value for money if comparing to the many other choices around, i.e. local hotels nearby offering lower rate, bigger rooms, and more facilities. May try out other hotels next time.

author: traveggie
title: Staff must improve
text: We like Ibis hotels and stay in them a lot all over the world. The room in this hotel is good, comfortable bed, nice shower, nothing wrong with it. But in the six days we stayed here, nothing seemed to go smooth. The bathroom of the first room they gave us had a bad drain smell, so we asked for a different room. We are entitled to an upgrade, because of our gold Accor card, but the only better rooms are on the second floor, which is the smoking floor ??? We ended up on the sixth floor, great room, great view, but in the evening, when the bar, right above it, opens up, you have to put up with some noise, you can hear people walking on the wooden floor. From about 10 till after midnight the noise, gets a lot worse, when the bar moves the furnature ? The rooftop bar looks nice, good views, cool. Not many people seem to use the bar and we found one of the waiters so cocky and obviously seeking a tip that we stopped using it, which is a shame. The other waiters were nice enough. The room door cards we were given needed to be changed about 6 times over the days, because they stopped working. Same thing happened numerous times with the wifi code. Breakfast is a bit sad and not much choice at all. Most off the staff at reception seem indifferent, they have no P R skills and can only answer standard questions. Not very professional at all. The room for me is worth 5 stars, but the hotel staff brought my rating down to 3. Lots of room for the staff to improve.

author: malaichai
title: Good Value Ibis Styles
text: Had a one night weekend stay recently with my family. Hotel is still looking new and is strategically located downtown. Hubs of Ipoh old town and night market are both conveniently within 25 min walking distance away. The Deluxe room that we had was very clean and roomy. Comfortable for a family of 4 grown up persons. It however consists of only 1 queen size bed. Extra bed is optional and is chargeable at MYR70 a night. The room comes with a separate shower and toilet cubicles one each. It is also equipped with 2 wall mounted LCD TVs. One in the sofa furnished common hall and one in the bedroom. Ironing and tea & coffee making facilities are provided as well. Breakfast spread and the coffee served in the cafe was good though there are rooms for further enhancements. Quality of staffs that we encountered were generally service oriented and polite. Though our stay had some initial hiccups due to miscommunications, the hotel staffs nevertheless did a fine recovery job... Would certainly recommend this place for a comfortable clean interior!

author: pivoine86
title: Wonderful stay!
text: It's was a family trips with my 2 kids for 3D 2N. The check in process is pretty fast in the check in counter. But there is no bell boy to help u collect your luggage but is OK we do it yourself since we don't have large lugage. And we stay in level 4. The room is clean and the water heater is function well, can consider a modern type design room. The air-conditioning is slow to getting cold even the temperature setting to the coolest. As its take time to cool up the room. There is a welcome drinks voucher given that u can claims your drinks at Level M. Same floor Cafe where u having breakfast for tomorrow. The breakfast fast is seem OK if u are not the type of fussy. Or u have an option to eat outside of hote. At the hotel entrance turn to your left there is a famous food stall name "Upper hill" in Cantonese which is operate day and night. And u can had a local food for breakfast or dinner which is a most convenient by walking distance. In the hotel level roof there is a bar for chill at night but please don't go during rainy days. It's will spoil your mood. And there also not allow kids below 18yrs old to enter. Please take note! I will come back again to stay in this hotel in Ipoh.

author: travelbugvee
title: Impressive hotel, strategically located and very comfortable
text: Our first stay in an ibis Styles hotel and boy, are we impressed. We took a Deluxe Room on Level 5 and it was HUGE with a super comfortable bed and an equally big living room, 2 flatscreen TVs, a safe deposit box, a fridge, ironing board, hair dryer, torchlight, sofa with 3 additional chairs, and a lovely view of Ipoh. The bed comes with a thick mattress pad on top with fantastic linen and 2 bolsters (first time I've had bolsters in a hotel room). It was so comfortable, I had to rip off the bedsheet to get the brand of the mattress (and the other time I had to do that was for the Westin's Heavenly Bed). We took advantage of Accor's recent sale where the room rate was 40% off for members. Did not expect much from the breakfast but we were pleasantly surprised with the range on offer. It's not big but the main items are covered - cornflakes, bread, fruits, drinks, porridge, local snacks, nasi lemak, sausages, scrambled eggs, bread pudding, baked beans, a noodle station, and a coffee machine churning out good coffee. A pity that there's no egg station but I'm not complaining especially when Accor allows 2 children to access the buffet breakfast for free. We got welcome drinks and there is a free flow of drinks (hot and cold) for guests from the Streats Restaurant. Access to rooms is via your keycard and you are only able to access public floors and your specific floor. There are 3 computer terminals on the ground floor for guests to use and WIFI signal is strong throughout the hotel. Newspapers are provided in the lobby and in the restaurant. The hotel is a tad understaffed so checking in and out took longer than usual but the service standards are good. There is a single level basement parking and lots may be full if you return late at night and if the hotel is full. In any event, there is plenty of roadside parking outside the hotel but you will need parking coupons if you park Mondays till Saturdays. The hotel is located just outside the city area and everything is within walking distance from the hotel. Super location. Love the design of the hotel and the smart use of colours throughout. We will return.

author: lila08
title: last minute plan turned out fine - awesome modern design
text: we were less than 2 hours to reach Ipoh when we got to know we had to stay in a hotel during festive season (Eid). managed to secure a booking on the way to Ipoh via phone call after browsing thru the internet in the journey. we were thinking to stay for 1 night only, but after checked in & saw the room, we decided to stay for 2 nights. the modern design & decoration of the hotel, room even furniture caught our attentions. plus point - covered car park (even though limited). free wifi for 2 users. clean & complete bathrooms with towels and hair dryer. steam iron & ironing board provided. friendly helpful staff. good breakfast but not so satisfied with the quality of cereals. good housekeeping. bonus point - kids play area near the restaurant with flat screen tv showing cartoons & some toys and books. provides bicycle rentals as well. front desk called our room when our McDelivery arrived. minus point - no room service for food.

author: zuluwarriors1879
title: Enjoyable ambience and friendly staff
text: Ibis Styles Ipoh appears to be the first hotel belonging to an international chain in the area. It is a very new hotel and the maintenance is very good. We found the design of the hotel very refreshing and cheerful, based on citrus fruit colours that Ipoh is well known for. The registration process was very efficient; the young Chinese lady manning the counter was very helpful and provided us with useful information. At the hotel, we felt a good sense of security. Each level could only be reached using a keycard and there were many security cameras. We had two rooms; a little small but equipped with everything we needed. The beds were very firm though the pillows were on the soft side. The rooms had a lot of lighting points which could be individually controlled.There were also many electrical sockets - even USB ones. The bathroom had a inner sliding door which divided the shower area, the toilet and the wash basin area. It was helpful as it kept the area dry. The aircon could be individually controlled so that was not a problem. Breakfast in the well lit cafe was relatively simple but tasty. Service could have been a little faster in replenishing the food but that was not a major issue. There is a bar at the rooftop - pity we did not use it to enjoy the night scene because children were not allowed. But, it would have been a good place to chill out. In the end, a good hotel for families - reinforced by friendly and helpful staff.

author: atomm2015
title: Basic concept and good location
text: Its relatively new hotel and very neat concept. Styles, minimalist and promoting green. Very cosy feel and family style. Love the setting, the room decor and the bath. The reception area is nice with free pc use and internet access. Check in was a breeze. Front desk was helpful when seeking information. Security wise is good with cameras in and around the hotel. Even the lift accessible with key card only. Parking space a bit limited but plenty of parking around the hotel. Located within the walking distance to the famous chicken rice area. Again in and around plenty of small eatery from malay to chinese street food. The streets are a bit dark though, therefore the front reception forewarning us on security. This happens anywhere around the world as long as you excercise a bit of caution, you should be ok. Otherwise driving out is good. Its value for money and even better then some boutique hotel. Free Internet access, coffee and tea making, iron board, plenty of charging points. My choice of hotel and will be back when im in Ipoh.

author: BrownLovesCony
title: Very good choice of hotel
text: We stayed in Ibis for 3 nights during our road trip to Ipoh. We were greeted by a big lobby and welcome drink. Check in was fast and smooth but I think the check-in staff could smile more and show her friendliness. We love our room at first sight! The design is refreshing and modern. Bathroom is unique with a common sliding door and a large mirror. There are 2 bolsters provided and it feels right at home. Room is not very spacious but comfortable enough for couple. Only downside is the room was facing a row of dilapidated shophouses with zero worthy view. The location of the hotel is very good. All famous eateries and mall are within 5 - 10 mins walking distance. Parking space somehow is limited but is not a problem for us since we walked to almost everywhere. Breakfast choice is limited and the cafe packed with people during weekend. We noticed that Ibis do not provide toothbrush and toothpaste. At first, we found that unacceptable. When we enquired with the staff, she explained that toothbrush and toothpaste are only provided upon request. This is because Ibis Style is grouped under 'Economic' among Accor group hotel and this is also to prevent wastage as most people bring their own.. Point taken! :) Ibis has a rooftop bar which is high enough to have a bird-eye view of Ipoh at night. Overall we're satisfied with our stay at Ibis and will definitely recommend this hotel to all.

author: aslimversgwm
title: A very modern hotel with good views of the Cameron Highlands
text: This is a super, contemporary hotel in a good location with views of the Cameron Highland mountains from the upper floors. The reception area is very spacious and modernistic staffed by efficient receptionists. I had requested a room high up and was given a very large suite on their top 6th floor with lovely views of the highland, limestone mountains in the distance. The room included a lounge area which included a comfortable sofa, armchairs, table and dining chairs, a big flat screen tv with BBC World News and several English language movie channels. There was an alcove for coffee/tea making - included + an efficient safe. The room's lobby area also included a desk, chair and reading light with power points for writing and computing needs. The bedroom was well sized with a king size, double bed, as requested, table, chairs, flat screen tv and a double fitted wardrobe. Both the lounge and bedroom had separate air con units with large windows to admire the mountain views over the rooftops tiles of nearby traditional houses. The bathroom was also well sized with a good shower - hand held + rain shower. Toiletries included shampoo, shower gel, toothbrush/paste set, comb and cotton buds. The 7th floor contained a bar lounge with great night skyline views and a full cocktail menu enjoyed from comfortable, modern designed chairs. Live music on some evenings, or disco type on others. Breakfast was buffet style served on the mezzanine floor with Western and Asian selections. Coffee was good being freshly brewed from a self-service espresso machine. Eggs cooked to order with a bread selection for toasting. All told an excellent, modern hotel to stay with little, or nothing to criticize. Perhaps the breakfast could include more Western selections.

author: urbanguy1974
title: Very satisfied with my stay
text: Recent 1-night stay as a tourist. Positives (1) Room compared favorably in terms of size, decor and facilities vs other hotels of the same category (Ibis, Four Points by Sheraton, Holiday Inn Express, etc.) I have stayed at worldwide. Room was clean with fresh and modern decor. Relatively spacious bathroom. An example of when "budget" does not equal cheap. (2) Good value for rate paid. Free wi-fi, breakfast and parking. Coffee/tea making facilities, bottled water and iron/ironing board in room. Separate bottles of shampoo and shower gel (not all-in-one). (3) Nice partially open-air bar on the roof. Good place for drinks around sunset or at night. Issues (1) Limited basement parking. Even on a weekday night, while I managed to find parking, the basement was full. There may not be enough parking during holidays. (2) Bed and pillows were a bit soft. Could be a matter of personal preference. (3) Bar ran out of pomelo juice (a relative of grapefruit grown around Ipoh), so could not make any of its local specialty cocktails.

author: Zoula
title: New and good staff
text: Hello, We have decided to escape from Kuala Lumpur for an overnight trip to Ipoh. My wife booked two rooms at the hotel. The hotel is located in a district full of local restaurants at a walking distance. I would probably say that you will have ample choice of local food within 1.5 km of the place. The hotel is very new and very clean. The rooms' size is just nice and comes with the normal amenities. Internet is available throughout the hotel (WiFi) and it is free. Price is reasonable too. There was a small issue though; the speakers at the corridor was right at my door and I found it too loud. I made the remark to the management; the manager on duty came to check it out and fixed the issue. thank you Mr. Shaiful for your prompt action. You are what makes hotels real hotels. Breakfast was included, there is free flow of coffee from a real espresso machine and there is just enough food to please any taste. I will surely go back to this hotel if I need to spend a night in Ipoh. Keep up the good work.

author: john_gpjm
title: Huge rooms for ibis styles!
text: Its located right in the heart of Ipoh city and most conveniently accessed by car. Lots of eateries nearby. Parking is available at the basement. Can be very quiet at night and there is no security post there at moment. Hotel is very new (was told it only started operations in January 2014). Thus, the set-up is modern like of all Ibis styles around the world. The honor complimentary room upgrades for those on Platinum with Accor. Rooms are spacious for any ibis styles! And being a styles concept, it comes with breakfast which contains a variety of local (nasi lemak etc) and the usual international cuisines (sausages, backed beans, bread). Fresh orange juice available. Breakfast needs are met for a typical person here on business. Room is clean with huge bathrooms and balcony (standard room with balcony) which at first was amazingly odd as my balcony is as large as the bedroom (perhaps more space could have been used for the room instead). Room is not typically designed for 3 beds; when the 3rd bed goes it, it will fit but it is really cramp! Safe available. Pillows need improvement (They only provide single pillows and a weird sausage shape pillow). Wifi is also complimentary in rooms. In the lobby, there are three computers which are internet ready to meet the needs of those staying here. Speeds are acceptable. Service, certainly better than many other hotels in Malaysia. They have received training and i'm satisfied with the customer service.

author: SaketG31
title: Ibis Ipoh: Aaha in some areas & oh oh in some!
text: I booked this hotel online for 2 night stay. This was the best international budget hotel preferred by my local colleagues. Front desk staff was very helpful and resourceful. The room was small, with more area for bathroom, and less of working area. There was only zero dial option that connects to front desk. A/C cools the room in few minutes and you need to switch it on separately. Dental kit and shaving kit not available in room. Wi-Fi is strong. In breakfast, baked beans, bread and fruits were the only veg menu. Lot of ice added to juice containers to make it chilled, but it makes them very diluted. For dinner, as in house guests, I got 20% discount and aloo gobi as the only veg menu. Bed was soft and got good night's sleep. The hotel forgot to clean my room, and when this was available. After waiting half an hour, i just checked corridor and found one guy from house keeping cleaning rooms with walkie talkie. I requested him to clean my room and thankfully he did - but is this really my job? Everything else was okay.

author: /undefined
title: potentially the best in Ipoh if only...
text: I have stayed in most of the Ipoh hotel over the past 10 yrs and Ibis could potentially be my favourite. It was a comfortable stay for my family of 4. I strongly recommend the deluxe room if you don't mind to spare a little more budget. The room is in good size with a living hall and a separate room. there is a sofa in the living hall and there are rooms for 2 extra single bed. The bed is the best that i have experienced thus far in Ipoh hotel. The decor of the hotel is vibrant. Staffs are polite and patience. But there is certainly room for improvements. The lobby is extremely dirty when i checked in. The tiles are full of shoe mark and the carpet at the lobby are filled with mud and dust. The carpark does not have any security guard. I have a deluxe room with courtyard balcony but the courtyard has not been cleaned. the floors are full of mud too. the head board of the bed has not been cleaned properly too. In summary, i think the management needs to look into the housekeeping. the hotel is still very new, thus maintenance is the main task to make sure the hotel can excel in the long run. Breakfast is simple which is expected but reasonable quality for this range of hotel. Location is good which is in the centre of the old town.

author: IJR86
title: very nice hotel, good location.
text: the good: the room was very nice and clean. but it definitely requires a good maintenance to ensure that the carpet remains clean in the long run. love the vibrant colored interior and staff are friendly and efficient. location was great, in the middle of everything. the bar in the roof top is a cool place to chill, love the chairs and the ambiance but the staff were a bit slow. had to ask for the bill twice. overall, a satisfactory stay for the price we paid. would definitely stay here again. and the bad: unfortunately about 4 days before my arrival, i received a call from ibis hotel to inform that there was a system glitch and my booking did not actually go through. there were no more rooms available, and they offered to make reservations at syuen hotel at the same rate. however after i insisted and refused to be moved to syuen hotel, they made necessary arrangement and i managed to stay at ibis anyway. they should have called earlier to inform that there are no rooms, and i find it funny that there are no available rooms. i even entered ibis hotel and booking.com websites few days before my arrival, and it stated that rooms are still available. if you know there are no more rooms, the management should ensure that the system reflects the same. but no issue with this since they prepared a room for me anyway. so when we entered our room, it took about 30 to 45 mins before we could feel the aircon. we were too exhausted we weren't bothered to call the reception. biggest mistake ever, it took longer than 2 hours before we could feel the aircon at night. and of cos it was too late to call anyone at that hour (about 1.30am), we were thinking of our safety as we were 2 girls travelling. but if our aircon was working, there would be no issue with the hotel at all, seriously.

author: Raymondetc
title: Sleep with style.
text: When back to Ipoh to attend a wedding dinner. As the dinner starts at 7.30 pm and expected to end at 10.00 pm, decided to book a room for a night. Did an on-line booking in the morning, drove to Ipoh in the afternoon and check in about 4.00 pm. Checking -in was a breeze. Car park is free. Just walk across the street and it's "little Genting", a food court style eating shop. Walk across the other side, there is a mamak store, cooking nice food. Walk to town and you'll get endless eating shops. Superb location. Our room was very new, Large restroom. Would personally prefer a smaller restroom and a bigger sleeping area. Even though the sleeping area was rather small (to my liking) it's laid out was great. Lots of power point to charge up our gadgets The bed offers quality sleep. Highly recommended. If you sleep late, remember to pull on the curtain.

author: travelfeet
title: Walk to some of the best food restaurants nearby
text: The purpose of staying at Ibis was so that we could explore the streets nearby for some of the best food in Ipoh & it was terrific that we could just walk there. Besides that, the room was clean, bright, reliable Wifi in the room, safe deposit box, fridge, kettle, hair dryer, multi sockets ... And a plus plus point, 2 long towel racks to hang damp towels to dry (Room 422). Ibis, you did well here. Breakfast came with the room but I chose to eat out. I did take a look of what was available: Malay, Chinese, Indian & International Breakfast with a Coffee Maker on site. How do you walk to the food streets nearby? Turn Left as you Exit the main lobby, walk towards Restaurant Impressive to the main road which is visible from where you'd be. At the traffic lights, cross diagonally, walk along the main road then walk down the streets on your left. ( all opposite) the Police Station. Ipoh Tuck Kee Restaurant since 1963 for Kueh Teow with the raw egg. Chicken Rice just further down. Curry Noodles at Xin Quan Fang Coffee, open 7.30am to Noon. Closes by 11am during public holidays. From Restaurant Impressive, head to the main road, walk straight down & pass the traffic lights. At the double storey Shoplot, probably 5 shop. I'd stay here again next. On the downside: Check-in was slow. I arrived at 4pm & even with confirmed booking, they had to find me a room.

author: FrenchRemix
title: Maybe one of the best in Ipoh
text: Spent 1 night stay here and my review as follows: 1) Location: in Central Ipoh Town, very near to Ipoh Parade, local food, 7-11. Very good location 2) Lobby: Nice design and very clean. Check in was also fast. 3) Rooms: Room is compact but very nice design. Matress and pillow are of good quality - not the typical ibis pillow quality. Everything looks very modern. Bathroom is very nice and spacious. No complains and totally worth the price it charges. 4) Wifi: SIgnals are strong throughout the hotel 5) Buffet Breakfast: Maybe the best ibis hotel buffet breakfast in Malaysia. Quite a variety, nice atmosphere. 6) Parking: They have underground parking but maybe can accommodate up to 30 cars only. However, the surrounding of the hotel is safe to park and there are ample of space to park. No issue with parking in my opinion. 7) Roof top bar: Surprisingly the atmosphere is very nice. Drinks are priced reasonably. Overall, this is a good new hotel in Ipoh. As opposed to the older 4 stars in Ipoh, in my opinion, it is more worth it to stay the new ibis styles.

author: hassy12
title: How could I not like the hotel ? Its wonderful.
text: For the price i paid, the room is more than a value for money. I was accompanying my husband on his business trip and this hotel is just perfect. The room is clean, spacious. The toilet is modern, separate toilet and shower cubicle. The bed is more than a comfort at home. Hotel was decorated with vibratnt colour. Got kid space, reading lounge and an impressive rooftop bar. The bar is a must try. Friendly staff, good place just to chill and let the night pass by. We tried having dinner at sTreats as well as they were having 20% off total bill during our stay. Food was ok. For breakfast, the spread is good. Variety. From nasi lemak to porridge, toast, cereal, laksa, mix fruits, salads. Just name it. Overall i would definitely return to this hotel and highly recommended.

author: rcmcg
title: Three star hotel with five star quality
text: Good points: 1. Large, well lit underground car park. 2. Welcoming receptionist who checked me in efficiently 3. Well designed quiet rooms with good quality fittings and comfortable beds. 4. Very pleasant roof top bar which overlooks traditional Ipoh shop houses and distant hills. 5. Good food served in roof top bar. 6. Excellent buffet breakfast served in nicely designed coffee shop with outside area for smokers. Bad points: 1. Porters not well trained on lift operation. 2. Roof top bar waiter did not serve the correct food order. 3. Not all food available until 20 minutes after time breakfast should have started. 4. Tables not cleaned after guests left the breakfast room. Overall: I would have rated this hotel 'Excellent' if staff training had been better.

author: lukasg88
title: New hotel with poor customer service
text: Stayed for one night in late March. The good: This is a brand new hotel with nice, stylish decor and good amenities for the price (except for the internet speed, which is capped at 512kbps - perhaps slightly too low in this day and age). The room's size was adequate for a budget hotel. The bad: Customer service left a lot to be desired. Check-in was slow and inefficient - we arrived around 4pm and had to wait for nearly 40 minutes to get into our room. The receptionist did not smile, communicated in commands ("You can sit", etc.) and noticed my Platinum status only after I pointed it out to her on the reservation form (which resulted into an upgrade to a "Studio" room). We were given a voucher that promised a 50% reduction in the restaurant *and* the rooftop bar (on a bill of over 100MYR), which we decided to split between some light refreshments downstairs and drinks upstairs. The mains we ordered arrived with a 10 minute gap between each other and I have every reason to believe that the prawns in the "prawn paprik" were far from fresh. After presenting the voucher after receiving our bill we were informed that it could only be used in the restaurant or in the bar (since their billing systems were not connected, despite belonging to the same owner/hotel), despite the fact that it explicitly stated "redeemable in the restaurant *and* the Mu bar" (not "or" - the staff member called this a "mistake" on their behalf). Afterwards we decided to order some fruit, which arrived warm (!) and a club sandwich, which arrived without some key ingredients that featured in its description. To sum up - stay away from the restaurant, the service offered and the food served were both well below average. The last nail in the coffin of customer service was a 10pm call from the reception - I was informed that Ibis Styles Ipoh had not received my payment (should have been forwarded by Accor) and demanded booking confirmations, etc. Surely this is something that should have been pointed out to us and resolved as soon as we checked-in. No apology was given for this intrusion. Unfortunately, Ibis Styles Ipoh was the weakest link during our stay in Malaysia and this was only due to its poor customer service standards - staff and management have a lot of work to do before catching up with the rest of Accor family.

author: TheonlyRyanT
title: Satisfied
text: Not what I expected from the photos. The design is modern and unique. The courtyard is almost as big as the room, enough space to relax. But i think the room space is not big enough. The toilet is big too. And I like the Sky Bar at the Roof Top. It is very relaxing and you will have a mountain view. The service is good. The bed is very comfortable. Had a nice sleep and very peaceful around here. There's a coffee shop with nice foods next to the hotel, so it's very convenient. Pity there is no swimming pool. I stayed in a Standard+Courtyard Room. It was on the 3rd floor (With Courtyard Room only available on 2nd & 3rd floor). The view was disappointing - old rooftops...

author: michellesH8318YN
title: Nice location, other than slow wifi and bathroom a little disappointed, still an okay stay.
text: Husband and I Stayed at a Standard Double room for 3 nights in April 2018. Let’s talk about the good stuff first: Location is convenient, short walk to all tourist attractions. 2 mins walk to supermarket and some restaurants. Reception staff are nice and helpful on calling taxi. The room itself is okay, room and bathroom are spacious in size. The bed is very comfortable for me, the sheets are one of the softest one I’ve slept on. But the double bed are two twin beds with separate sheets and blankets pushed together.
