title: A wonderful place where it feels like staying with old friends
text: Your B&B is beautiful and very homely, so much space and we loved the clean, new and stylish furnishing, the huge suites (that could easily sleep a small army), the lovely bathrooms, the balconies overlooking orange and lemon groves and being serenaded by the inevitable cockerel with laryngitis. Breakfasts were always fresh and delicious with a new surprise for every day - seasonal cakes (it was Easter), local versions of croissants etc. Always plenty of choice and really only someone terribly greedy could eat something of everything! It is a bit of a cliche to say someone couldn't have done more for us but in Antonio's case that was literally the case. From showing us where to eat, catch the train (and drive us to the station once), what to ask for on our trips, how to get around the region and hiring us a large people carrier, his cheerful attention made us feel very special. Thanks also to both Antonio and Mrs. Antonio for coming in person to the airport to collect us and for taking us on our return trip at an unearthly hour - well beyond the call of duty (again). As for Romeo we all loved him from our 17 year old down to the 8 year old. He's a lovely placid dog always ready to play and be gentle with everyone. On a more practical note, there is a super shop next door for anyone wishing to stock up for the day's excursion and the walk into town is only a leisurely 10 - 15 minutes. There are two train stations in Pompeii. Make sure you understand which is which. Don't be put off by the shabbiness of the trains they are very functional and convenient. The train is very cheap and there is a local line that shuttles along the coast between Naples (didn't enjoy much) and Sorrento. Get yourselves a roaming ticket.You can walk to the ruins which is a wonderful way to spend the day - no transport needed. It's on your doorstep, well about a kilometer away. A day driving along the Amalfi coast is magical (driving was actually quite fun) so do make sure you schedule this in to your itinerary. Again our heartfelt thanks to Antonio and Iona (?) who are excellent hosts and now friends. If you are thinking of a stay in the region, I can fully recommend staying at Certe Notti. Ross, Lis, Adam and Peter

author: TominZurich
title: Friendly and Spacious
text: Antonio and Ione make you feel welcome and at home--but you have your own, spacious apartment with a small balcony overlooking a garden. The bed was most comfortable, and the bathroom clean and nice (though the shower was clearly for people of slimmer builds). Antonio is the most helpful of hosts, and gives excellent "quick and dirty" explanations of how best to benefit from Pompeii and the other archaeological sites. The B&B is very close to things. It is about 500 m.to the Circumvesuviana railroad stop, from which you can easily go to Naples, Herculaneum, Salerno, Sorrento, etc. It is about 1.2 Km from the less-used entrance to the Pompeii ruins at the amphitheater, and about 2.5 Km from the main entrance at Porta Marina. So it's extremely convenient. Antonio also recommended Zi Caterina restaurant (as well as others), which we found superb (see our review). The Certe Notti has free SKY TV (big flatscreen) and free WiFi, both unexpected in a small, three apartment B&B like this. Most of the channels are in Italian, although there's a way of switching to English for many dubbed US and British shows, of which there are a lot. Because of the pull out sofa beds (our apartment could have slept up to six), there are no tables--neither writing nor coffee--and no chairs. And the sofa beds are not particularly comfortable to sit on. During better weather you can sit out at the table on the balcony, but we were there in the winter, when it was too cold. Also, you may wish to bring earplugs--the street in front is busy during the day, and there seemed to have been a whole bunch of roosters anxious to make sure we were up well before dawn. Any shortfall in this regard, however, is made up by Antonio, who is the most genial and helpful of hosts. There is secure, off-street parking. This is a charming place, with a great host. We can't recommend it too highly.

author: Belfastgirl23
title: Excellent choice in Pompei
text: We stayed in Certe Notti for a couple of nights at the start of September. The best thing about it was the space - we were a group of three, which can be difficult to accommodate, and the arrangement of having two separate but interconnected rooms was perfect for us. We had advised ahead that we were arriving late at night and the sofa was already made into a bed which saved a lot of trouble. It was pretty quiet by Italian standards which we really appreciated given how late we arrived. We also ran into a little trouble with not being able to get in but it did resolve itself pretty quickly. The breakfast was also very nice and informal. The place is also just a nice size and feels very cosy - if your teenage daughter decided she wanted to go to pompei alone this would definitely be the place for her to stay, it felt very safe and secure even to leave valuables in. The balconies to front and back were also great because we were all able to feel we had enough space. The B&B was also nice and close to the ruins and had a couple of very good and cheap local shops right outside the door. I would recommend the mozzarella di bufala from the little minimarket right next door, together with their fresh bread it made a delicious picnic lunch. The people were very nice too as others have said but I have to also say a special word for Romeo, the owners' dog, who also gave us a very warm welcome! The only slight down side was that the air conditioning wasn't great. It was very hot when we arrived and it felt like the aircon wasn't up to the job of cooling both rooms. But that's a minor grumble in an otherwise great stay. I would heartily recommend this place!

author: aaronandholly
title: Couldn't ask for more!
text: We planned two nights in Pompei but booked four nights there based on the great ratings for Certe Notti. We were not disappointed. It's a small building tucked away on a somewhat busy street up the road from the Circumvesuviana Pompei (green line) stop. The ampitheater entrance to the Pompei ruins are also within walking distance. As soon as you step into Certe Notti's courtyard, you'll feel like the chaos of Pompei has been left behind. Our room included a patio overlooking an orchard, a spotless and spacious bath, and a separate sitting room. Breakfast was excellent every morning, including our last morning when the wonderful owners came an hour early to make sure we had breakfast before leaving on an early train. The coffee was great - like having your own personal barrista! Others' comments about the owners are 100% accurate. Antonio and his wife want your visit to be outstanding, and they'll do everything they can to make sure it is. They gave us an excellent overview of the area, including helpful restaurant info, and offered to take us to the train when we departed. We couldn't ask for more gracious and enjoyable hosts. When you reserve, you should try to tell them when to expect you. We arrived mid-afternoon and had some trouble getting a response at the gate (the courtyard is securely locked and not accessible without a key). That's really the only thing we'd do differently - Pompei itself is underwhelming but the ruins are amazing and Certe Notti makes Pompei a fantastic home base to explore the ruins, Amalfi Coast, Vesuvius, and the surrounding area.

author: mypsuedonym
title: A simply brilliant place to stay!
text: I stayed here with a friend in September for three nights - it was simply brilliant place - the accommodation was superb and the hosts were so helpful and friendly we could barely believe our luck! We booked an apartment with two separate bedrooms and a shared bathroom. Technically it was a one bedroom apartment but the front living room had been prepared as a second bedroom. The apartment was lovely, clean, dry, etc and the furnishings and fittings seemed all fairly new. It was very nicely presented. As a bonus - this was the cheapest accommodation by far that we had during our four and a half weeks in italy. If readers are wondering if the accommodation sounds a bit of a squeeze - fear not: We had no need for a living room during our stay - we were out and about for most of the day and by time we got back to the apartment we had usually seen many so much, walked for miles, eaten at some wonderful places and were quite simply (and very happily) exhausted. Our hosts were so good, and seemed almost not to be able to do enough for us. [Antonio - if you read this: I suggest you can do less for your guests and they will still be more than happy!] Serving us great breakfasts, even better coffee, and providing us with good, clear, information on how to get around the many sites nearby. There is a lot to do in this area - and the train makes visits to many of the locations a breeze. And where it didn't go, we used the local buses instead. Antonio was full of hints on which restaurants were the best for different types of food, and the difference in the dining experience they offered (small family-run restaurants to large restaurants on the main street). He was also helpful regarding how to avoid being caught out by local scams designed to part the unwary from their money. I simply couldn't recommend Certe Notti highly enough. If I am ever back over that way again, I would definitely stay here.

author: 2Luvn2Travel
title: Never known better service
text: My wife and I had expected to have a woderful time in Pompeii but we would never have imagined... We arrived in Naples but sadly picked the wrong train. Instead of going to "Pompeii" we went to "Pompeii Scavi". Not knowing how far off track we had gotten I called the B&B for directions. Before we knew it, Antonio drove and picked us up at the train station. Before we got to the B&B he gave us a quick tour showing us a church (that couild be seen from just about anywere in Pompeii) and where it was in relation to the train stations, ruins, resteraunts, and the B&B. This was just the start of an amazing time. The B&B was emaculate and our spacious room had a living room, bedroom, and a terrace with an amazing view of the garden and Mt. Vasuvious. The bed was literally the most comfortable we had slept on in our two weeks in Europe and Antonio and his wife were helpful, kind, and gracious hosts. As an example, my wife and I had gone for a walk and returned with some Gilato well after dark. Without hasitation they offered us spoons, bowls, and some napkins so that we could enjoy our dessert on the terrace. We were only there one night and there are to many good things to mention here. Suffice it to say "Unbelievable Service". The only regret that we have about our stay was that we were only there for one night. We left Certe Notti wishing we could have changed plans and stayed a few more days. They were amazing!! Thank you both. You are the best.

author: BFAmberL
title: Really old, outdated- but OK
text: I have stayed at this place 3 or 4 times now over the last couple of years on my trips back and forth from Idaho to Minnesota. Everytime we have stayed in a room that was a carbon copy of the others- Each having a table with broken legs (the tables all sway quite a bit) the bedding is old, the carpeting is old and stained. This trip was no different. My kids ate the breakfast provided (fruit loops) but I was unable to eat anything as they didn't have any protein options such as eggs or yogurt.. It was fine, but unexpected to have so little, as we have never tried to eat breakfast at this location before.. but typically do at other places. The thing that this place really has going for it is it's staff.. I have been greeted and checked in/out with nothing but sweet ladies. I with this place was a bit more updated- but it is what it is. We had dealt with some loud music all night the last time we stayed there- but I am unsure whether the front desk was aware. I did not bring it up as I forgot. Somebody in the building close to where we were was listening to some TV or music pretty loud throughout the night. The thing that this place really has going for it is it's staff and the location right across from the Thai food place which has great food- and being so close to t he freeway. It it weren't for those reasons, I'd go somewhere else. We may actually head to another place next time just for comparison.. there's gotta be something better than this.

author: Eyeteach1
title: The better of the two "name brand" hotels
text: Deer Lodge is not a large town, but it does have many wonderful attractions to visit. There are only a handful of accommodations and the Travelodge is the better of the two name brand establishments. The front desk staff was great. . .though there was a line up to register and some who had no reservations were out of luck as there was a rodeo in town. Even though she was stressed to the max, when it was your turn she was very friendly, accommodating and knowledgable. The facility does need a few updates. The carpet was stained and the linens were a little old, but all was very clean. We had a handicapped room where the staff had put a recliner for my husband (again the staff is very accommodating). The bathroom had a walk in shower which was great, but no place to put toiletries. The sink area was in the bedroom, but it still would have been nice to have a place to put some things in the bathroom. The room had a mini fridge and a microwave. A continental breakfast was offered in the morning which we chose to forgo as it was sparse and there was not much seating area. During the night we could hear people in the hallway, but it wasn't bad. We had a good nights rest. Knowing some of the other accommodations in town, I would probably stay here rather than some of the other places. It was quiet, comfortable, and clean, and the staff were very pleasant and accommodating.

author: 7377ml
title: Two night stay and was disappointed, used to so much more at a Wyndham motel
text: When I arrived the clerk was nice enough, she even stated since I was Rewards card member she was going to upgrade me to a king size bed. When I got to the room it was apparent that this place had been remodeled in years. The TV an old 19 inch model, not a flat screen but a really old TV. The room had almost no outlets for plugging in anything. One on the wall on the right side of the room, with an extension cord running under the bed for the lamp left side. I use a C-Pat machine so I had to pull the bed out to find one left plug in on the extension cord. Didn't seem all that safe but it worked, well at least for a while. When it was time to go to bed, the light switch turned off all the lamps and the ceiling light and of course my C-pat machine. The only way to get it to work was to stand on the table take the ceiling light cover off and unscrew the light bulb and then manually turn off both table lamps. Beside the lamps there was also a alarm clock plugged in to this one outlet. Behind the TV there was one outlet and plugged into it was the refrig, Micowave and TV. Not sure this is all safe or not. The next morning went down to the free breakfast and was very disappointed, no yogurt, no bagels, no eggs or anything hot except you could make a waffle or pancake and there was some bread to toast. The second morning we just went to a cafe across the street. After the first night my wife went down to get a cup of coffee and the house keeper meet her in the hall and stated I see your staying two nights do you need anything? Now assuming (wrong) that our room would be cleaned, nope the maid put two towels on the sink and didn't do anything else. The second night we did the same thing with the ceiling light and checked out as soon as we could the next morning. We plan on staying again in Deer Lodge but unless this place is made more modern it won't be at the Travel Lodge. However the town of Deer Lodge is a wonderful place and the people are very friendly and welcoming.

author: JennyW337
title: Is this whole motel broken?
text: We stayed last night at the Deer Lodge Travelodge, renting two rooms to accommodate 3 adults and three teenagers. The room rate was very low, and booking was simple over an online reservation site. We paid $112 for two double rooms. That was about the best part of the experience and things went down hill from there. Available parking was very limited, and the end of the building we parked at was completely dark- all the lights were out, which made unloading difficult. In one of the rooms the TV was broken, one of the main lights was out, and the window was broken- it couldn't be closed the last couple of inches on a 30 degree night. Not good. On top of that, the door was wide open on our arrival, propped open with a wet towel. What was that about? In the other room, there was dirt/gravel between the sheets on one bed as well as what looked like pet hairs, a big stain on the carpet, and the outlet we plugged our phones was busted, as we found out in the morning when our phones weren't charged. The beds are hard and uncomfortable. The hallway floor is so loud that you sound like a giant even if you step light, and getting to hear another motel guest clear his throat and cough up plegm like he was in our room was quite the treat. We were told that Apple devices were having a hard time connecting to the Internet, but the lady at the desk didn't seem concerned at all. The Travelodge offers a continental breakfast with toast, pancakes, a waffle maker to make your own waffles, cereals, a few juices and coffee. There were some oatmeal packets, which were much appreciated by our gluten free family members. The desk people were very pleasant, other than the lack of concern over Internet connectivity, however, that doesn't really change our overall opinion of the motel. When we left, the teenagers commented that it was "pretty ghetto".

author: 303oweno
title: Great place
text: Extremely clean!!! Very friendly good value. It is an older hotel, many of the fixtures and furniture (including the TV) are from the 80's but it appears that is because the owners care for them greatly. It is by no means run down, they just maintained the hotel very very well and they lasted. I have traveled quite a bit and notice small things that show how well a room is cleaned. They take care of them all. Example... The vent in the bathroom was immaculate( a rarity), the lamp shade clean as if they were brand new and the "brass" wall fixtures looked like a they were shined by a cadet with brasso, yet it is obvious they are older fixtures. Nothing was in disrepair, truly impressed. The staff were extremely friendly and knowledgeable. Beds were comfortable (one draw back was the pillows were flat but we traveled with our own so not a big deal)and breakfast was done well. It is limited but adequate for a free breakfast. Two flavors of waffles, breads, fruits and 4 choices of cold cereal as well as various hot cereal. OJ and apple juice. Well done. You can hear early travelers leave and will hear loud voices in the hall but that is more from inconsiderate people than a knock on the facility. It by far is the best hotel in its price range and up to the top in the next price range as well. A must stay!!!!

author: /undefined
title: Everything cheap, but the price.
text: We stayed here because this was the only national chain motel in town, and mom and pop motels usually are poorly constructed with few amenities. No offense to the fine community of Deerlodge, MT, it's a very nice town and I'm sure the quiet is a draw for some. But how on earth can this motel charge over $80 for a room that Motel 6 charges $40 is beyond all comprehension. Everything was shabby, cheap, and poorly done. One swipe of the TV top with my hand said it all, dirty! (FYI, flat screen TV's have evidently not arrived to this part of the world). Pubic hairs in the shower--YUK! and cheap construction so that every step on the OSB floors resounds throughout the structure. Greeted upon entering the motel was a pleasant but scantily dressed woman, which left to the imagination wide open as to what additional services were being offered here. (Maybe this is a positive for some, but my wife did not appreciate such an open bosom welcome.) Overall I got a 20% discount which brought the price down. Was I suppose to feel like I got a bargain? Deerlodge is not a tourist destination, but a nice town to pass through. Save your money and drive a few more miles and stay at the next small town motel, else opt for one of the mom and pop motels in town. You will likely save some money. TIP - GET SOME LIGHTING IN THE BATHROOM. YOU CAN'T CLEAN THE PUBIC HAIRS ON THE WALL UNLESS YOU CAN SEE THEM! TIP- TAKE SOME OF THE MONEY YOU TOOK FROM ME AN FIX YOUR ICE MACHINE.

author: Fuzzworth
title: Clean but flawed and somewhat overpriced for the season
text: The young woman at the front desk was personable and polite. She didn't show any irritation at being interrupted on her dinner break, even though she had a bag of French fries cooling while she checked us in. I had registered on line, though, and didn't know until I moved some of our luggage into the room that it did not have the fridge and mic that I'd requested in the "special requests" panel of the application. I was too tired to drag stuff back out and work through the switch to another room. Beds were comfortable, bedding clean. The usual "rubber" pillows, but from long experience we've learned to bring our own, so the pillows weren't a problem. The breakfast was a bit sparse -- the usual flip-over waffle iron and a couple kinds of dry cereal, white, whole-wheat and raisin bread for toast, with the standard little sealed units of marmalade, grape jelly and peanut butter. Only two tables in the tiny, inadequate breakfast area, which is ridiculous for a 30 or 40-room (didn't count them) motel. I can't imagine hauling a flimsy bowl of cereal and milk upstairs and along a hallway. The cramped little nook must be a madhouse when the place is full -- there were only a couple of guests the night we were there. There were few guests that night, and, to her immense credit, the clerk did not give us a room immediately adjacent to another occupied room. Excellent! A pet peeve of mine is that motels often assign adjacent rooms to all guests, even on slow nights, making your chances of a noisy neighbor more probable. Of course a busy night will necessitate packing 'em in, but when there are only a half-dozen guests in a multi-room facility, it's ridiculous to stack them next to each other. So brava! to the desk clerk at Travel Lodge in Deer Lodge MT. That alone might bring me back there again, but I'd count on going elsewhere for breakfast if the place was even fractionally full.

author: sierrapup
title: Great motel, getting better!
text: We stayed at this hotel on our way through Deer Lodge. It was formerly a Super 8 and recently was taken over by Rodeway Inn (part of Choice Hotels). We payed $71 total with AAA. We were pleasantly surprised when we cheked in at the size of the room. It had a kitchen with table, couch and tv in one room, then the bed and another tv in a seperate room. The front desk was cheery and helpful even though it was late at night when we arrived. The hotel was very clean. It is an older hotel and some of the furnishings are dated. But they are clean and show little wear. While we were there, they were preparing to install all new carpeting. The bed was very comfortable and the shower was strong with plenty of hot water. They have a complementary continantal breakfast which included pastries, hard boiled eggs. waffles (yes, waffles!) orange juice, coffee, tea and fresh fruit. I would definately recommend this hotel. It was nice when we stayed and it appears that Rodeway hs plans to make even more improvements.

author: busterandtilley
title: We will never return
text: We have stayed here five times, this stay was our sixth. We have always had a suite on either floor 3 or 4. Unfortunately we were given room 113 on the first floor. I firmly believe that this floor is reserved for short lets and such. We were booked in for ten nights and it was awful- the noise in the early morning is unbearable, but that isn’t the fault of the hotel. Secondly the safe in this room will trip out, leaving you no other alternative than to call maintenance- which we did three times in two days. In the end we resorted to using our cards. The cleaning staff are not quite so thorough and our room wasn’t swept for two days. The sheets and towels remained unchanged for four days despite the request notice being place directly on the bed!! There was only one cleaner who was exceptionally good, but we only got her one day-when the linens were changed. The fridge was dirty, stained and remained unused except for bottles of water. On a more lighter note The foyer is welcoming as well as being cool, a welcome respite from the heat outside. The breakfasts are legendary, and every thing previously mentioned in my reviews still stand, although Cristina could do with more help. Most days she had to work 30 covers singlehanded- what a star!! and always so happy too! The pastries are quite good too. The rooftop swimming pool is compact and doesn’t ever, not whilst we have been there, become overcrowded. But the birds were a real problem If you fancy a drink or snack someone will gladly get it for you. We will not be returning, preferring to stay elsewhere, and bitterly disappointed that our continued patronage wasn’t appreciated.

author: N6472FJmatts
title: Decent hotel, but slept badly due to noise outside
text: There are a lot of good things about the Reveron Plaza (see below), however with my low rating I want to draw attention to a serious problem. On two of the five nights I stayed, I was woken at around 6:30am by someone using a high-pressure spray to clean the square outside the hotel. This uses a loud machine, which sounds a bit like a drill used for roadworks. This has previously been noted by other reviewers (see e.g. mick74uk3's Nov 2018 review), but as of March 2019 is still an issue, despite the hotel apparently trying to address this. I hope the hotel again confronts whoever is responsible for this, and I am happy for them to use this review as evidence to the disturbance it is causing to their guests (and, presumably, many of the other people in other places around the square), and the negative impact on the experience of tourists. Other than the above, here are my thoughts of the hotel: Pros: -Great location (1 min walk from taxi rank, a few mins from the beach, bars, shops, and restaurants) -Friendly, helpful staff -Decent breakfast selection (cooked, pastries, fruit, cereals etc) -Nice rooftop pool. Some other reviewers said the pool temperature was too cold for them. While I would not describe it as warm, I found it very comfortable for swimming once you give your body 30 seconds to get used to it! Note that this was in March. -Very comfortable bed and pillows -Clean -Nice decor -Free wifi, which worked perfectly Cons: -Early morning noise, as discussed above. -Pigeons by the pool. At times it felt like a scene from The Birds. The pool seemed very clean and well maintained, but I was somewhat concerned about the risk of disease being spread to swimmers! I expect this is very low risk as long as the pool has adequate levels of chlorine, but it was still somewhat annoying. Overall, I would be happy to return - but only if the early morning noise is resolved.

author: Beckywall_uk
title: Finally got to stay here .......
text: Decided to splash out a little extra and stay here as every time I walk past it, something about this hotel mesmerises me. Not sure whether it’s the look, it’s wonderful location or the beautiful Spanish/colonial decor throughout. However 10 lovely days were spent here over the Xmas period; THE GOOD The staff are some of the most polite and attentive I have ever met. Under the leadership of the hotel manageress all seem so happy in their work and with such a small team - probably only 15 in all, you get to know some of them quite well Cristina always had a smile to greet us! A beautiful buffet breakfast served every morning until 10.30 so even the longest of lie-ins were not disturbed. Good choice of breads and cereals and hot food cooked to your choice. A Stealth cleaning team who seemed to manage to make our beds every single day despite us arriving and leaving at various times! Christmas Day saw a lovely intimate drinks reception for all guests which to be honest made my day. It was lovely to see staff and guest all mingling wishing each other best wishes for the festive season. A request to change rooms half way through our staff was dealt with quickly and efficiently within 15 minutes without issue or undue delay. THE BAD I always add a bad section to any review to give you both sides, but I am struggling with this hotel as there is very little bad to report. The water in the bathroom can vary in temperature depending on the time of day you choose to shower or bathe if I was being really picky, there are chairs in the room but a sofa would be lovely to relax on at the end of a busy day. But these are just picky things (and I mean picky!!) apart from that - I can’t honestly think of anything else that the hotel can improve upon. Things outside of their control - it’s in a very busy area, great for people watching but noisy with tourists and the church bells (chiming between 8am and 11pm) and the balconies are fairly small and don’t provide much privacy. Other than that a beautiful quaint hotel that I will be sure to return to one day.

author: tc00ps
title: Wonderful holiday
text: We stayed on the third floor overlooking the church. The room was great, it was really spacious with lots of storage. Cleaned daily. Towels changed when we asked. Tea, coffee and milk supplies and a fridge with a bottle of water included. The location of the Hotel is amazing. Everything is within an easy walking distance. The Pool area is lovely. No issues getting a sunbed and lovely and clean. Our lifeguard had to assist a person taken ill and he did a fantastic job. The breakfasts were really tasty. Cooked to order so a short wait and they were so fresh and nothing too much trouble. Lots to choose from if you didn’t want a cooked breakfast or omelette and never an issue getting a table. Coffee machine amazing. All in all we had a wonderful holiday at this hotel and I would not hesitate to go back and to recommend it to anyone. Thank you to all the staff !

author: goddessIsleOfMan
title: Lovely quaint hotel with very friendly staff
text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel the last week of August. We were extremely happy with our choice of hotel from the minute we walked in until the minute we left. We had always wanted to try here and were definitely not disappointed. Upon arrival we were greeted with a very welcome glass of cava while the check in process was completed quickly by a very friendly gentleman on reception (I can't remember his name but he was outstanding during our visit). All the staff we came across were very friendly and nothing was too much trouble for them. I was particularly impressed with the lovely lady who used to do the Happy Hour service at the poolside every afternoon. She tirelessly took orders and delivered the drinks up to the pool with a friendly smile and chat. The breakfasts were good. There was plenty of choice from Continental to Full English and you could stipulate exactly what you wanted and how you would like it cooked. The hotel appeared to be busy but the waiting time for breakfast was minimal. We had a top floor room overlooking the square and church. I would definitely recommend this if you are looking for an opportunity to watch the world go by and soak up the general atmosphere of a town square where the locals meet up. Our room was very nice. It had a huge very comfortable bed and the air conditioning was working perfectly (just what we needed as it was extremely hot when we were there). It was cleaned daily to a very high standard. The hotel is not modern by any stretch of the imagine but it is maintained very well. We enjoyed our stay so much that we can't wait to go back in October!

author: liamk490
title: Well run central Hotel
text: Stayed here for 11 nights August/September 2017. It is a quaint hotel, full of character. All staff were helpful and friendly. The rooms were comfortable. They were cleaned daily. The Hotel was spotless throughout. Breakfast was excellent with plenty variety, both hot and cold. My wife enjoyed the top floor pool with the happy hour cocktails. The only small downside was that the bedroom balcony seating needs upgrading or at least some cushions as we ruined our clothing with rust stains. Overall we enjoyed our stay and will come again. If staying here, make sure you call to the Fortuna Nova restaurant just 2 minutes away. We dined out for 11 nights in Los Cristianos and would have to rate the Fortuna Nova by far the best. It was outstanding. We received excellent osteopathic treatments directly across the road from the Hotel in the small shopping center passed the flower and tatoo shop. He was very professional and generous with his time. Would strongly recommend for those back or body aches.

author: Tiggerlinda56
title: Return visit disappointing
text: We have stayed at this hotel for a number of years when visiting Tenerife, and have always affectionately called it Faulty towers because of the things that are wrong, i.e. Sink plunges not working, fridges not working. However the staff were always helpful and efficient under Delores leadership. Delores is unfortunately on long term sick leave and the new staff are not a patch on her. Myself and my friend drink decaffeinated coffee, the first morning was fine we got our coffee, from there things went down hill; the second day we asked for decaf coffee which seemed to be in short supply, but eventually got a sachet each. The third day we expected that the coffee would have been replenished but no, the unhelpful non smiling waitress said they didn't have any, after requesting she source some, guess what she found a whole box full! Why didn't she check her supplies before breakfast was served knowing she had customers who drank decaf coffee, and having been asked for some why didn't she source it quickly and apologise? Because she couldn't be bothered. Then the sitcom broke down for 3 days making the temperatures in the room unbearable. We were told many things about the progress of the repair when we asked ' it will be fixed this afternoon, we are awaiting a part from England, we are awaiting a part from the other side of the island'. We asked for a fan only to be told they didn't have any and they would contact management, but nothing happened until we contacted the Jet2 rep and then we got a fan. We also were given a bottle of fizzy wine in an ice bucket, but no apology. Then notices started appearing around the lifts saying the air conditioning was broken and they were awaiting a part from main land Spain, eventually the air con was fixed on the fourth day in the afternoon. Communication on the matter was sadly lacking. We asked for ice from the bar to have a drink on the balcony in our room to be told abruptly 'we don't have any!' That's funny as we had received an ice bucket full of ice with our complimentary wine! The quality of the breakfast and staff had diminished sine our last visit and I am seriously considering making this my last visit!

author: padwad12
title: Friendly Hotel with Character
text: We arrived at Reveron Plaza in August 3 adults 1 teenager on a room only basis . It was alternative accommodation as our other accommodation had shut for refurbishment. Had to walk a short distance from the bus drop off point as the large bus can't get down to the Hotel. Lovely friendly greeting at reception and soon had us booked in for the 2 rooms on the 4th floor . One room was facing the church the other was around the corner facing the street and an area under development . The hotel dates back to 1949 the receptionist was telling us and it is full of wood and glass decorative features & paneling. It is well maintained and all the staff keep it in excellent condition.Rooms are well kept and good size with ensuite. All the usual facilities you would expect including Air Con, safe, tv, mini bar fridge and kettle including switch console units at the side of the comfortable beds. Rooms were cleaned thoroughly daily towels changed & tea/coffee sachets restocked where necessary. We were facing the church and the clock would start chiming from 8 am onwards which we actually enjoyed as it added to the character of the place.Every so often when there was a mass the bells would ring out for longer which we also enjoyed. Early evening we would sit on the balcony watching all the kids playing on the square.The rooftop pool was a nice chilled out place ( Nobody running around trying to reserve beds as it's not allowed) and provided a waiter/waitress service to relax even more with a beer or cocktail . There is a reading room on the 4th floor that my children used a lot as they said it was so relaxing and chilled them out. Location is excellent as you are a very small walk down to the beach front where there are absolutely loads of restaurants/ bars etc. Every member of staff we came into contact with was genuinely friendly helpful and everyone made us feel welcome. There are several places to eat and most have similar menus but places we returned to were Linares II and Me Gusta for quality food & friendly service. First time in Los Cristianos but would definitely stay here again in the future. A Hotel with character & friendly staff helped us have a great holiday . Thank you

author: debrae454
title: Excellent choice
text: Stayed here in August. Got a taxi from the airport just €25, so we could be dropped off directly at the hotel as busses cannot get to the narrow road outside. Check in was easy and we were shown to our lovely room, spacious and clean. Plenty of space for your clothes and everything, nice size bathroom, and a little area with a small fridge and a kettle, supermarket just up the road to get milk, beer, wine etc (€2.25 bottle of cava, about €O.65 for a can of lager). Room was cleaned daily. Our room was overlooking the church square and we didn't find it loud at all, yes the square is always busy but not an issue. Breakfast was really good, choices of the usual pastries and croissants, toast, fruit, cheeses, cereals etc, or choose your own freshly cooked hot breakfast. The full English was very good, waitresses on the breakfast shift were very overworked, it worked better when there were 2 on than just 1, but excellent service every day. Rooftop pool nice and quiet with good views. All staff at hotel were friendly and welcoming at all times of the day and night, they clearly put customers first. On our first night the electrics tripped in our room, this was about 10.30 in the night, someone came up within minutes to rectify this. The hotel itself is old and it was lovely to see that it had not been overly modernised and had most of the original features intact, truly beautiful. The location is superb, minutes from the beach and in the centre of as many types of restaurant you could wish for. All round good choice. I would not now stay in any other hotel in Los Christianos, as this one could not be beaten.

author: alant271
title: Great traditional hotel
text: My wife and I spend a great week here at the beginning of July. We were welcomed with a drink by a very friendly and helpful receptionist. In fact, all staff without exception were very pleasant. Our room was spacious, spotless and cleaned thoroughly daily, if a little dated. The water was always hot, and there's a safe in the room but it's €3 daily plus a €20 refundable deposit. The WiFi is free, and strong enough to stream TV shows. Breakfast was delicious, and food is cooked to order so you can have as much or as little as you like, plus the continental selection is buffet-style. I believe the same lady worked every day at breakfast and done a fantastic job. We never had a problem getting a table. The pool area is lovely and quiet, with great rooftop views; the sunbeds are available early but you can't swim until 11am as that's when the lifeguard comes on duty. There aren't many beds, but only once did we ever see all beds taken and people seemed quite good not to reserve them without being present. The hotel is situated in a great location, surrounded by restaurants, cafes, bakeries and supermarkets, plus a short walk from the beach. There is also a taxi rank just across the street. For those less mobile I would recommend against a coach transfer, as the surrounding streets are too small for the coach to get close so there's a good 800 metre or so walk with your cases! Much easier just to taxi. In summary, this hotel is perfect for couples looking for a quiet, laid-back place to stay while still have easy access to amenities.

author: Sen72_13
title: Short break
text: My good lady and I had a week at this hotel. What a little gem of a hotel. A little dated and perhaps due a spruce up but a great find. Rooms are spacious and comfortable very clean and a large bathroom. My only gripe is the bath had a shower curtain which stuck to you in that horrible way they do. Plus the bath was fairly narrow which made it worse. This is why the hotel didn't get 5 stars. Breakfast were hand cooked to order, plentifull and good quality. Staff also very good. We had a room facing the square and church, which was the busier side. We liked this as we like to people watch. The church has a bell tower that chimes the hour and half hour between 8 am and 10 pm. We didn't find this issue at all. There is a pool on the roof which has a life guard but not a great many sunbeds. Again we never saw it full. Loads of small bars and restaurants near by and beaches 10 minute stroll away. Bus station just up the street again 10 minute walk. We highly recommend la Perla Italian restaurant just 5 minutes down past the church the pizza are incredible. Also the steak restaurant at the side of the church was good quality and service. We will definitely use this hotel again when we visit Tenerife.

author: corneliaGalway
title: Lovely Hotel
text: my husband and I stayed here from April 23rd to 30th. On arrival we were greeted by an efficient courteous receptionist who offered us prosecco while he processed our documents. Our room was on the second floor to the side of the hotel with a partial sea view. The room was large and nicely furnished. It had a fridge, safe ,TV, kettle with a hairdryer in the bathroom. The balcony had a table and two chairs. There were no facilities for drying wet towels etc. on the balcony. Breakfast was all the usual fruit, cereal, pastries, cold meats, cheese, and hot dishes were cooked freshly to order. It was really tasty. The pool area, on the fifth floor is quite small .However when we were there we never had a problem getting a sun bed or umbrella. A lot of the guests didn't go to the pool. Also it was heated which was divine . The hotel is located a short walk from the beach ,right in the centre of things. There are numerous restaurants nearby. We enjoyed our stay at the Reveron Plaza. It isn't really suitable for children or those wanting a lively time but for people of a certain age its great.

author: 160glynisl
title: Just beautiful
text: Stayed here for my birthday in March. The hotel is charming and the staff are amazing. Andres on reception was superb and very funny, joining in with us with the fun of carnival antics. Maria on the bar and later in the breakfast room was a delight as were the other ladies at breakfast. Francisco ( I think how you spell his name ) was also a super smiley helpful guy, finding out details of the misleading pick up service issued by Jet 2. In fact everyone from the cleaners to the lifeguard were great. Now the Hotel. It's oldie worldy and fabulous. It's position is perfect, right in the midst of things overlooking the square. We had breakfast here and were offered everything and more that you could wish for. The room we had 101 was enormous with loads of storage space as was the bathroom. Toiletries were supplied. They will hire towels for the pool too if you need. Coffee and tea making facilities, small fridge. In fact one of the nicest rooms we have had. Please put a plug socket near the mirror, I'm not sure of using straighteners in a steamy bathroom!! Pay for a safe but that was expected. I would thoroughly recommend this beautiful hotel to anyone and should we return to Los christianos I would stay again without hesitation. Thank you for a great birthday , I really enjoyed the bubbly you gave me to enjoy in our room. xx

author: grahambF5304HP
title: Authentic Spanish hotel in town centre
text: Really enjoyed our recent stay here. Hotel very clean inside and central for all activities in Los Cristianos. Very pleasant staff who are helpful at all times. Full English breakfast cooked to order. Items can be varied according to taste. Loved the swimming pool area. Water nice and warm. Great views from 5th floor bar area. Nice view of church from bedroom. Large room with neat area for making tea/coffee. Big bathroom with a bath/shower and good towels. A bit noisy sometimes outside early morning from street cleaning and in the evenings from kids playing football in the square. Need to ask for Sky News and CNN to be installed on bedroom TV. Screen a bit small but got used to it. All in all an excellent hotel in a great position with wonderful staff who always go the extra mile for their guests.

author: rupertb737
title: Small excellent Hotel
text: My wife and I stayed in September,flying with Easyjet from Edinburgh. The hotel is in the centre of Los Christianos in an area full of restaurants/shops amid small pedestrianised streets.It is very near the sea front-only about 150 metres-with easy access to the beach and promenade.The whole area is very well maintained with palm fringed street gardens--spotless and quiet considering its busy location. As the hotel is B/B only, the proximity of good restaurants is a real bonus and the prices are cheap vis-a-vis U.K.prices--a really good steak+ chicken dish with 4 glasses of wine for 30 Euros---lager 1.50 Euros a pint. The hotel itself is intimate--only 40+rooms with breakfast freshly cooked to order.Rooms are cleaned thoroughly, with clean towels daily andthe reception staff are very pleasant and helpful.The roof-top pool has loungers and is accessed from your room.There are toilets but you need to change before going up---it is not really suitable for children as there is no shallow end, The gym equipment downstairs would be a credit to any club/private gym and is the best I've ever seen in a hotel--modern and comprehensive with weights/ etc etc--it is free of charge. All in all then, an excellent central hotel. However,our experience with Easyjet transfer arrangements was potentially a disaster, as the drop off point specified on their voucher from the airport--the Reveron Plaza, is not where you are dropped off as it is inaccessible for coaches due to the narrow streets..We were told to get off the transfer bus at the Trype Tenerife Hotel, which is about a kilometre away across a warren of streets at 10.30 at night in the dark without any indication of where to go by the driver who just pointed in the general direction of downtown Los Christianos.He has previously tried to let us off at the Reveron Apartments even further out of town .This had a neon sign, so we knew it was wrong, but the Reveron Plaza has no such sign being invisible amongst the high rise buildings around it. We just stood on the pavement on the main road outside the Trype with no idea where to go. We were "rescued" by a couple of passing tourists who knew where it was and they actually took us there---a ten minute walk across various streets and steps. I would not recommend Easyjets arrangements, as there is no indication that the delivery point is not actually at the Reveron Plaza as it states on the voucher .We decided to take a taxi back to the airport on our return journey as the pick-up point was at the Trype too and we had several suitcases. Also we are both pensioners!!! Jet2 customers at the Reveron were delivered by private transfer after being let off the bus. The hotel charges 3 Euros a day for the safe---a courtesy room is free of charge for post 12 o'clock room vacation with a safe room for keeping luggage. To extend a room stay costs 27 Euros if available. I hope this is of some help. Mr Booth.

author: /undefined
title: Good hotel and location
text: We booked this hotel as part of a Jet2 package. When we arrived we were given a nice cold glass of Cava each whilst we waited to be checked in. The hotel has a relaxed atmosphere and one of the quietest, if not the fastest, lifts I have ever encountered. We asked for a quiet room and chose one on the second floor overlooking the church square, which was a nicer view than the third floor one at the front. Only a few rooms have some sea view and they are more expensive. The square is quiet at night and the church clock doesn’t sound between 10pm and 8 am. Local children tend to play there in the afternoon and evening. One picture of the hotel seems to show it in a pedestrian area, but a moderately busy road forks left and right in front of it, though it seems reasonably quiet at night. The room was a good size with a fridge, safe (extra cost) and a nice big, firm, bed. The bathroom was also good and actually had a bath! There was plenty of hot water in the mornings. The TV had no English language channels. There was a good selection of food for breakfast. Cooked food mostly involved eggs and fried ones tended to be overcooked. Real orange juice is 2 Euros extra. It is possible to see the sea from some of the tables.

author: TheTallFella
title: A Great little hotel
text: Check-in friendly and efficient Nice foyer and bar area Only single lift which can get busy as shared by hotel staff, but taking the stairs wasn't too hard going. Mainly an older clientele which we liked adding to the peace and quiet yet buzzy with the square, restaurants, bars and beach near by Clean and airy public areas all tiled Best floor for us was the fourth overlooking the square having spent one night on the east side overlooking Amalia street and a big hole. However, it did benefit from the early morning sun Over looking the square is north west facing, but we did get the late evening sun for an hour or so and watching the world go by was very relaxing. The Church bells chime between 8AM and 10PM and add to the charm in our opinion. Fourth floor is also where the breakfast room is Breakfast was good with friendly staff in the restaurant. Selection of meats, cheeses, Danishes, fruit, cereals etc plus a good Coke breakfast. One floor up on the 5th is the swimming pool and sun deck / lite lunch area The swimming pool on the top of the hotel overlooking Cristianos is a great place to relax and read. It can get busy but in fairness we always just managed to get a lounger although people had a nasty habit of leaving towels and books on them for several hours despite hotel policy. The rooms are nice and clean, but nothing to write home about. Suffers occasionally from lack of hot water, being warm rather than hot, but not quite cold enough to stop us showering. The shower is set at a single height ~7ft! Great for myself but not my 5ft wife! Bathrooms could do with an overhaul although they are cleaned and serviced well. Beds are comfortable, but two singles together rather than a proper double. There are two superior rooms in the hotel rooms 301 and 302, these have large balconies and sea views, but can only be booked through the hotel at a €40 to € 80 supplement depending on the room. Given the hotel is reasonably priced, especially if you book on line I think it offers value for money and a different city option to the other hotel complexes in the area. We have stayed in nicer rooms but the hotel is unique and many people were booking their return visit on departure. So on this basis a 5 star rating

author: Eat1Drink2Travel3
title: Such a shame it was a let down
text: We had booked two nights here before our onward travel to La Palma. The building and architecture of the hotel is beautiful, the location is great, especially for the port. When we talked to the staff (when we could locate any), they were generally friendly. The breakfast is good. But, and I'm sure you knew one was coming: We got a corner room on the first floor with a balcony facing the square. It felt like we were in the square as it was very close to it and noisy. The big clock in the square strikes loudly and often and from 8am. As we were there in the Good Friday, there was a party going on til the early hours in the morning. Although the hotel couldn't do anything about the noise in the square, once the mayhem in the square finished, we realised there was a loud generator in the room next to us. The first time I went to have a shower, I found that there was no hot water. Instead it was tepid and ran out after a couple of minutes. We went to alert the reception but he just shrugged and said as it was Good Friday they don't have a mechanic to fix it. The shower was tepid for two days running. The beds are hard and pillows uncomfortable. The rooms are tired looking and need an update. The bathroom has no window and not sufficient light. Having paid nearly £400 for two nights, and expecting a 4 star hotel (which it clearly isn't), I am disappointed and will not return.

author: hellybell14
title: What a gem!
text: This is a delightful hotel,takes you back in time! The decor is superb,so oldy worldly. I felt I was back in the 1930's! I requested an upper floor over the church square based on trip advisor reviews. I wasn't disappointed! We were on the 4th floor (407). The balcony was lovely to sit on and listening to the hustle & bustle in the square was great. No swearing or drunken arguments just children playing and people chatting. The church bells were literally opposite! But they were not annoying. They rang every hour from 8am til 10pm so not intrusive. The roof top pool was peaceful and quiet, great for an afternoon siesta or dip. There was even a lifeguard on duty! Breakfast had a good selection of fresh fruit,pastries,cold meats,cheeses and cooked breakfast. No complaints!

author: ColinN139
title: One star too many...
text: We booked 9 nights on the strength of the hotel description and reviews. The hotel is well located with a choice of restaurants, shops and bars close by in a pedestrianised area leading to a beach and the small port serving La Gomera - 32 Kms and 40 minutes by swift ferry. The hotel is tired and rather gloomy with dark wood and coloured glasswork in the wide staircase giving an impression of an old French city hotel. Our room was comfortable with a decent bed and small balcony with table and 2 chairs. There was another table and chairs in the room by a wall hung 13 inch TV offering few programmes. There is a safe in the wardrobe needing a key to activate the digital keypad - €20 deposit from Reception. Wifi reception was free but very poor. To use it in the room, you had to stand by the door or go down to the reception area where the was an unattended bar with no charm. We had booked half board - meals are taken in the single restaurant and only in the evening. After 3 meals with few or no other diners, poor choice and food, we ate in local restaurants. So overall, the hotel needs a makeover or to go down a star. There is a large gym complex on the basement, used by non-residents and with lots of equipment, much of which is out of service. There is a sauna and steam room on the top floor but it is closed for much of the time when you want to use it - weekends and between 11.00-16.00. The heated pool is on the roof - towels from Reception are €20 deposit - with views over the town and to the sea and sun loungers, but unattractive other than for a quick swim. To offset the negatives, the staff were helpful and friendly but if ever we returned to Los Cristianos, we would stay elsewhere.

author: JLS1959
title: Disappointed !!!!!
text: Returning guest to this Hotel for 8 night stay with my husband. Oh how I wish we hadn't. Had contacted hotel before arrival requesting room looking onto plaza and high floor. Had lovely reply stating how delighted to have returning guests and yes request would be arranged. On checking into hotel we were allocated room on 1st floor at rear of Hotel....... I explained situation and was advised maybe possible to move later in week. We declined offer. Rooms were exactly as previous visit. Fabric worn to threads on chairs. Pillows were awful.I am convinced floor had not been cleaned. Soles of new slippers ( thank goodness I had taken a pair) were filthy within 30 mins of wearing them. Positive note. Pool area immaculate. Nice and quiet. Breakfast very poor. Won't be back until hotel is renovated. Sorry.

author: 373katiep
title: Average
text: I personally feel this hotel is over rated. I had a wonderful 4 nights in Los Cristianos but I can't say the hotel played a huge impact. First of all, the buffet breakfast is ok. Juice, pastries and hot drinks - nothing tantalising. We didn't eat lunch or dinner at the hotel because of this. Very noisy in the mornings! Road sweepers and traffic pass by the hotel at 5am! (Do try to get a room at the back - despite others reviews saying face the church). I could only people watch for so long.. and I'm very nosey! Besides.. room at the back faces the ocean and what a breath taking view it is. On this note, I recommend booking a boat excursion in the local town. I saw dolphins and whales with their young. I probably wouldn't revisit this hotel, purely because you can rent a private villa in Los cristianos for almost the same price. If I had to favour one thing about this hotel is would be the room top pool. Which is heated. And very peaceful and serene.

author: Paulajane1964
title: Central Hotel very nice
text: Booked with Asda, all went smoothly, This hotel is very central to everything you need, e.g.. shopping, food, beach. Ask for a room overlooking the " Church Square" otherwise you will be overlooking a rubble site on the pop side of hotel ! looks like a building was demolished. Over looking the square is great for "people watching" you can sit on your balcony even get evening sun. It is very noisy when you have your balcony windows open,but thats the price to pay for people watching !! Also, the Church Bell goes off every half hour from 8am to 10pm, this you get used to !! Hotel is quite old looking,could do with maybe a re-vamp, but is clean and all staff are very friendly. The Pool on the roof is ok but there were far too many sun beds and not enough umbrellas for shade. Also it was a bit of a fight to get one as people put books and towels on them, there is a sign up saying NOT to do this, but it happened. But for us, there were far too many sunbeams crammed around the pool. Breakfast is nice with a choice of continental or full english , but you could have anything really . Be aware of ordering a boiled egg ! they say 5 mins, we usually do one for 3, when it came it wasn't cooked ! so make sure you say 5 mins !!!! big eggs i guess. ! Beds a bit uncomfortable could do with new mattresses really, but overall hotel is nice.

author: 1mairead
title: Not what we expected!!
text: Just returned from a week in Reveron Plaza. We were most disappointed, having read the reviews we expected to have a lovely holiday. To be fair the location is fabulous, walking distance to restaurant's etc, the roof top pool was equally pleasing. However breakfast was a total let down, one waitress only so service very slow, also eggs pretty much your option on menu!! The 'fresh fruit' was tinned, the pastries were hard, but the rolls were nice. On arrival we paid 20€ for the WiFi for the week. The receptionist told us we could use it anywhere in hotel. WRONG. WiFi will not work past the 2nd floor. It's a 5 story hotel!!!!!! Also you can only connect one device at a time, ridiculous. When my partner explained this to the MANAGER he laughed and said "your on holiday". Felt this was rather strange behaviour for a manager. My advice to people is be careful when going on the opinions on tripartite and maybe check things out a little in advance. We certainly have learnt our lesson and have had a holiday with lots of unnecessary disappointments.

author: 250dianec
title: Enjoyable stay
text: My husband and I stayed for a short break in September. Having read previous reviews we requested a balcony room overlooking the square and that is exactly what was allocated. The hotel is very traditionally decorated and exceptionally clean throughout. Our room was of a good size and comfortable. We took our own travel kettle as there isn't one provided (surprisingly for a 4 star hotel) but not a real problem. We hired a room safe which we tend to do at most hotels. The rooftop pool was lovely and when we were there it was fairly quiet, at no time was there an issue with towels on sunbeds. We paid a deposit for pool towels which is refunded on return of towels. On arrival there appeared to be some confusion with the computer system, we were slightly concerned that there was an issue with our passports but later found out that they have a new system which causes some confusion. The staff were pleasant and helpful, in particular the housekeeper who looked after the 3rd floor who was always smiling. Do not arrange coach transfer from the airport as the coach cannot access the area close to the hotel and you have to wait for some time at the airport before being dealt with. It is not that far so better to travel by taxi. There are a number of restaurants close by which are good but don't bother with the coffee shop opposite. If you ask for an ice cream they serve it in a dish and charge a fortune. The man who served us was exceptionally rude. I would definitely return the this hotel, it was a very relaxing experience. I must mention though that it is better suited to adults without children.

author: steve2702
title: Nice Stay
text: Hotel right by the Church square and 5 mins walk to the Harbour. Plenty of restaurants within walking distance in town. or along the prom. The hotel itself is typically spanish in style with tiled floors and I liked the decor. Could be a bit noisy as furniture is dragged across the floor but not a real problem. Room was spacious with a small balcony and very clean. Bathroom was also ok with shower over the bed. Room was a double room with two single beds. As with many Spanish hotels I have stayed in there is no tea making facilities in the room this being at extra cost. Also at the time I stayed the room safe you had to hire at 30 Euros for my 9 night stay and Wifi is also an additional cost of 20 Euros per week. The pool area on the roof is a nice relaxed area and the pool is well maintained. Snacks such as Sandwiches and Pitza can also be had there via a telephone call to the Restaurant who will deliver to that area. The hotel Gym is one of the better equipped hotel gyms I see with enough equipment a free weights to get a good workout. There is also a Spa which I did not try. The hotel bar is reasonably priced so have a return drink will not empty your pockets. All in All quiet hotel for Sole travellers, friends and couples. I wouldn't consider it as a hotel for children and young families. I enjoyed my stay and if I returned to Los Christianos I would more than likely stay again.

author: MPeterson67
title: Standards seem to have slipped since our last stay
text: We stayed here after Christmas 2012, and found the Reveron Plaza Hotel excellent. As a result we booked again for the recent school half term. On arrival we were booked in by a gentleman who clearly wished he were elsewhere. He went through the motions, but there was no smile and no welcome. When we asked for use of the safe he looked as though we were wasting his time. The room was the same as last time we visited. It was clean, with all the facilities you would expect of a mid range hotel. Unfortunately breakfast was not as good as last time we visited. Ingredients were the same, but obviously cheaper. The sausages were like cheap Tesco rubbish - mushy in the middle. The bacon was thin and tasteless. The best was the scrambled egg, which was lovely. The breakfast staff were the same as before - friendly and efficient. However, the hotel was obviously economising on ingredients. The hotel has the advantage of an excellent location, right in the centre of town, within suitcase-trundling distance of the bus station, (111 bus to or from the airport), and near the sea front and the ferries. There are plenty of cafes in the town, selling all kinds of food. Sadly, when we left, the person who checked us out was just as unpleasant and miserable as the person who checked us in.

author: joeyw346
title: Bugs,bad food and no internet...
text: I went to this hotel and I was terrified.. I could not get breakfast so they brought some "food" for me in my room.. Well food is ok if you wasn't eating for like 8 days.. Sangwich was like plain cheapest ham with cheese..Bread was about 3 days old.. 1 banana, water and yogurt..If you can call that thing a yogurt.. So food was very very bad when you pay 75 euros for 1 night.. But wait, worst is comming.. I had to wake up very early to catch my flight.. After I woke up I heard some weird noise coming from my bag which I left on the floor.. So I turned on my room's lights and 1 big bug just ran under my bed from my bag! Well atleast I didn't need to wait till my alarm went off because I just jumped from that bed! Internet was very poor, no signal in my room and plus you had to pay 5 euros for 1 day! So whole amount for hotel was 80 euros.. Very bad.. Disappointed...

author: quinny817069
title: Nice ,But stuck in a time warp
text: Stayed here for a week Dec 2013. The hotel is nicely furnished and the rooms are a fair size and spotless. The bathroom shower was the worst shower i have ever experienced in a hotel i would have been better just having a wash-down. The dining room is old fashioned looking and badly laid out. The routine is that you sit at a table and staff ask if you want Tea/Coffee. you then help yourself to cereal or cold meats, cheese bread etc. (only problem is they don't put out enough and you end up trying to find a member of staff to replenish it ) However if you want a cooked breakfast then you have to order it. I got the impression that everything was geared to save money, even to the discomfort of the guests. The pool area on the roof is lovely. Clean with plenty of sunbeds ,however if you want a snack or a drink from the pool bar you have to pick up the phone and dial a given number and a member of staff will come up from the kitchen ,take your order and go and prepare it. Its the same at night with the main hotel bar. most times there was no member of staff present and the receptionist had to phone the dining room to get the member of bar staff who was doubling as wine waiter in the restaurant come down and prepare drinks. There is nothing here to encourage guests to remain in the hotel and there is absolutely no atmosphere present. Bar staff are lovely and attentive but its obvious that management are cutting corners when it comes to paying staff The hotel charge you for Wi-Fi when small restaurants round the corner provide it for free. Drink prices in the hotel bar are on par with the area. The hotel is in a great location with bars restaurants nearby, and its only a 8 min stroll to the playa . I was informed this is a family run hotel. Well, it could be a superb hotel with the right team running it. As I said in my title "stuck in a time warp ". just about sums it up

author: yanto68
title: Shame about the pigeons
text: My wife and I stayed at the Reveron Plaza for 3 nights from 31st August. Having been to Tenerife every year for many years we always said we would like to stay at this hotel, so we added 3 nights onto our usual three weeks self catering holiday to spoil ourselves. The location is ideal in the centre of Los Cristianos close to all shops, restaurants and a very short walk from the beach. The hotel is clean and spacious although not a large hotel, the room and bathroom were of a decent size and again very clean. The downside with the room was that is was on the 4th floor overlooking the large hole in the ground mentioned by other reviewers (see photo). The balcony was very small with a cast iron table and 2 matching chairs. This didn't bother us too much as we were only there for 3 days. However the balcony and the handrails and to some extent the table and chairs were thick with pigeon droppings, it didn't look as though any attempt had been made to clean it for several days (disgusting). I know they have problems with pigeons but a daily clean should be a priority. After complaining it was cleaned a little but no where near enough to encourage us to sit out there. The hotel has a roof pool and good views from the roof but there again when we went to check it out we were put of by the pigeons in the pool and droppings in several areas. The breakfast was a buffet with a served cooked breakfast, the selection was very limited but being a bacon sarny man I enjoyed the 4 lovely rashes of bacon and bread roll with HP sauce each morning. The waitress on the first morning was a very pleasant young lady who greeted us with a smile and advised us where things were. The next two days however we were greeted (or not) by an elderly lady with a miserable face who didn't manage to raise a smile at all and in fact gave us the impression we were an inconvenience to her. Reception staff were very pleasant and helpful, would we stay there again? well maybe but we would ask for a room facing the church and perhaps on level 2 where the pigeons didn't seem so active.

author: Hibeeslass
title: Lovely Hotel
text: We have stayed in Los Cristianos many times but usually high end self catering and away from the town center. As we love this island so much we decided to try a hotel for a change. We found and booked the Reveron. We were delighted with it. All the staff were super helpful and friendly.The cleanliness of the hotel is evident throughout. Our room looked overlooked the square the view is delightful. The only downside (and it's my downside, might not be yours) is the little church, the bells go off every hour till ten at night from 8 in the morning, despite the triple glazing in the room, it still woke me every morning - earplugs would have done the trick. We were on the 3rd Floor and despite the bells would say we had the best room. If you want away from the sounds of the bells then you are compromising the view. The breakfast was nice full English and continental available for you every day however ideal as the times are 7.30 - 10.30 we noticed that they were not quick at replenishing the items within the last hour of service. Wifi is not free I took 3 days for 10 euros but sadly found myself sitting in the hallway to get a signal as it did not reach my room. Almost every eatery/coffee shop/bar in Los Cris have free wifi yet this huge classy hotel charge you. The hotel has a rooftop pool with great views. It was never busy when we were there so had no problem getting sunbeds. There are the odd pigeons that pop over for a dip but they are not intrusive and most of the other guests like me enjoyed watching them. There was a day where the hotel had hired a bird of prey handler and sat this big eagle on the roof to scare the pigeons off but once it had gone they were back at least the hotel are doing their best to address this.What I also loved about this hotel is the location it's slap bang in the centre of Los Cris so handy for everything. Shops the beach, bus stop, taxi rank lots of lovely bakeries and coffee shops wee bars, Spanish Tapas nice gift shops not usual tat everything is just brilliant!! (I so wanna be there right now).We would have a wee nightcap downstairs in the hotel the night staff were so friendly and nothing was too much trouble. Although the Taxi rank is 50 meters away from the hotel it is handy to book and pay for a taxi at reception before hand 22 euros hotel give you a slip and you give that to the driver when they pick you up from the front door!! Would stay here again.

author: LEllen12
title: A good choice for the money
text: This is a safe and clean hotel. The breakfasts were nice and served in a very sunny room. The location is close to the beach and shopping. The wifi is terrible. It was not free and we often had to sign in several times an hour. We came for a wedding so we didn't spend a lot of time in the hotel. Our bill for five nights was 374 Euros. It was a good deal for the money. However, we did not have any hot water for the bath at night, it worked in the morning but not at night. We did find a dead cockroach on the floor in the bathroom so we just put a glass over it and the housekeepers cleaned it up. Some of the front desk staff were extremely helpful and others not as much. There were two woman working in the morning, I asked them about the breakfast. They told me that I had missed it and it was over but I still had a few minutes. I ran upstairs anyway and was able to get a nice meal. I am not sure if we will be back to Tenerife and I am not sure if we would stay there again. Our friends stayed at a much fancier place which cost 100 euros more a night and they spent their days by the pool and really used their hotel. We went to the zoo and all the wedding parties so we didn't need any ambiance or amenities.

author: Bowwow2
title: Nice people, tired hotel.
text: Having just returned from a week at the Reveron Plaza we would not rate it as a 4 star. In its day it must have been the place to be but alas not to day. Its not all bad, the staff are great and so helpful. But the bathroom and room was very tired and in need of an up grade as most of the hotel. But having said that the pool area on top was good. Breakfast more than ample. Wi fi was an extra, no kettle in the room. While you could hire a kettle, if its 4 star should one not be in the room as the Wi Fi. It is in a good location but the downer is that no matter who you do a transfer with from the Airport they drop you off about 1/2 a mile away telling you that its 200 mtrs. You have to wak through a park that had what looked like the homless and drug users paradise. Not a good place to be at 3 am in the morning with all your bags etc. Especialy if the people are old and frail or with young kids and lots of baggage. The paperwork states that they will drop you off at reception but the only thing they say is the bus is to big. Is that my problem or are anm I being unreasonable to expect them to do what the contract states and what I have paid for. Thats my rant over but disapointed. Over all a little TLC and money spet on the place and it could be back to its former glry,

author: ArnoldMark
title: Great HOTEL, Great location!!!
text: We stayed here 6 night in June. We were in room 112, facing church. Room was very clean with decent balcony. Tv has I think only 4 English channels, I think it's only channels they have. I knew it before coming in, so I took my leptop, I thought I would be able to watch my NBA finals. How wrong I was, my leptop became a brick !! WiFi is HORIBLE !!!! €5 for a day...mmmmm....are you bludy JOKING!!!! I had another issue, which was ice! Outside is like +30 and you are dreaming about nice cold Gin and Tonic with you in the balcony....and guess what? No ice machin!! I thought ok, no worries I will ask reception, the look I have got for that unreal and they gave me 4 cubes, because they don't have enough for them self!!! So next time I went I gave a guy €5 tip to get rid of all that hassle after that he was without any troble supplying me with ice!!! Breakfast, don't let me start!!! Thanks God waitress was great, she was on her own and she did a great job!! Anyway, great Hotel with few issues! I will, come back, but without leptop.

author: mlscott1970
title: hotel reveron plaza tenerife
text: my wife & i stayed at the hotel reveron plaza from 7/06/2012 until 21/06/2013.having visited los cristianos on many occasions over the last 15 years we had walked past the reveron many times & frequently commented on how attractive the hotel looked & that we would dearly like to stay there some day.well on a visit to los cristianos in november 2012 we finally plucked up the courage to walk in & take a look around.its fair to say we liked what we saw & especially liked the rooftop pool.when we returned to the uk. we dicussed staying there for our summer holiday 2013.we booked in november for the dates in june. we booked bed & breakfast. we also asked for a high floor ( there are only4 floors & the rooftop pool).upon our arrival we were greeted by a very cheerful receptionist who swiftly booked us in. we wer in our 4th floor room within 10 minutes of arriving.the room was very clean & spacious with plenty of room for moving around & plenty of space for hanging clothes in the wardrobe.our room faed the church & square it was a great place for people watching from the small but comfortable balcony. the following morning we went to breakfast in the dining room. (served from 0730 until 1030 on the 4th floor) we found this to be ok. my wife enjoyed an omlette or english breakfast everyday along with several of the pastries that were on offer.i opted for either toast or cereal of which there are several available.the rooms were clean & tidy as was the whole hotel in general. there are a few negatives with this hotel but nothing that should ruin your holiday with a bit of thought.1.wifi is not cheap (around 25 euro for the fortnight ) and its a bit hit & miss. 2.if you dont like noise then the rooms overlooking the square may not be for youas the church bells ring every 30 minutes from 0800 until 2100.3. if you in a northeast facing room the view isnt that pretty there a large empty hole opposite the hotel. 4.i felt that bathmats would be of great benefit to people that may not be steady on their feet as the bathroom is very slippery when wet. so in summary a very nice hotel in a fantastic location with wonderful staff. but a few minor wrinkles to iron out. highly recomended.

author: holidayqueen3
title: Small Hotel, great location
text: We stayed at this Hotel for a week in May, following recommendation from my parents who stayed in March. It is a small Hotel but has attentive staff and a fantastic location, being right in centre of Los cristianos. Bars, restaurants and shops right on the doorstep and the beach is only 5 mins walk away. We had room 201 which was lovely, with 2 balconies, large room with double wardrobes, plenty of hangers, fridge, settee & table & chairs which we did use as a couple of evenings it was quite cool. The bed was comfortable, room cleaned well and breakfast was good though could have done with extra help at times as during busy time, had to wait a while for coffee and breakfast order.
