There was cereal, juice, fruit salad, pastries and bread as well as eggs or omelettes cooked to order. We did go to the pool a couple of times and it was fine but we spent time on the beach. We found the other beach Playa de las Vistas better as was quieter, being further away form the activity at the port. The sunbeds were 12 euros for 2 & parasol whereas the main beach was cheaper at 9 euros. The sea was freezing though! Plenty of choice of restaurants for the evening, we liked La Fortuna, San Luis & El Burgado but there is something for everyone. Lots of walking opportunities along the promenades. The worst bit of hotel was the shower which was very weak and would not cost much to buy new shower heads which would make a big difference! However I am sure we will be back! Our room was at the back which was very quiet.

author: 24AnnM
title: Nice hotel, good location
text: Have just returned from a week stay at this hotel. We stayed here four years ago and did notice that the quality of the food at breakfast was not as good as it was previously, no bowl of fresh fruit anymore. However, the hot food is cooked to order and not pre-cooked as in some hotels. Fruit juice was more like squash and no choice other than orange. Rooms are clean and comfortable although beds are quite hard. Towels are changed everyday. Shower not very efficient and no height adjustment, also no rubber shower mats available so be very careful as bath becomes quite slippery when wet. Fridge in room needed replacing as it didn't keep water or drinks chilled. Our room was on 2nd floor overlooking square. Church clock, opposite, does chime but only between hours of 8 a.m. and 10 p.m. so not a problem. Although we booked transfers between airport and hotel, (with A to B company), we were dropped off about 1/4 mile away and told coaches not able to get near hotel. Not impressed as we had to wheel our cases quite a distance. Had we been aware we would have not booked. On our previous visit to this hotel, we were transfered by taxi right to hotel. Didn't bother with return transfer as we knew we would have to drag cases to pick up point. Instead, we took a taxi from just up the street, (taxis always available there). Cost to airport was 22 euros. All in all, enjoyed our stay and would recommend this hotel as it is in a very convenient location, beach and restaurants all within 5 minute walk and on the flat.

author: mandurahholiday
title: Old Tom Morris Cottage
text: We spent five nights in the Old Tom Morris Cottage in the middle of the Golf Estate. Well firstly, there is nothing 'old' about it. The cottage is more like a modern house and is absolutely stunning. There are four large identical ensuite bedrooms (that can be either king or twin bedded), a large open plan kitchen, dining (table for 8) and lounge area with a huge fire place, then a conservatory style room with another dining table (for 12), lounge and TV and views to die for. The backyard is large enough for kids to play in, with a weber and outdoor setting. We stayed in winter and house is cosy and warm. There is underfloor heating in some areas and column heaters as well, but the house stayed beautifully warm. There is a washer, dryer and dishwasher, and the house is serviced daily. There are glass doors that open up between the two living areas and to the lawned areas so in summer you could open this all up. The house would suit two families, four couples or a mix. Having two living areas is great for kids and adults. It is on a small side road of the estate so safe for kids to ride bikes, scooters, walking etc. The house is at the top end of the golf course with views down the golf course and the rolling hills. Absolutely stunning. It says there is wifi in the house and you can connect, but it doesn't work.

author: Incredul0us
title: Well equipped and spacious cottage
text: The cottage was very well equipped. Everything is provided for- even heaps of firewood and charcoal. The daily cleaning service was an absolute bonus- even the dishes were washed. The little touch of a chocolate on each pillow was definitely a nice surprise. Spacious bedrooms.The cottage is easy to get to and is private, even though it has a view onto one of the golf course holes. 3 families stayed and it was good that kids had a separate area to watch TV and play. When it was windy the roof was very noisy, making it difficult to sleep. It was cold when we visited but the cottage was warm with underfloor heating and a big fireplace. Some comments to assist Kwa Jabu going forward- provide more communication closer to the time as to where to collect the keys and to remind the guests what was included etc. The oven door is broken so to close it you have to use a little latch and nail. Can be tricky when trying to get stuff out the oven when the latch is hot (too fiddly for oven gloves).The temperatures and grill/baking indicators have worn off- please write them on. The washing machine doesn't work properly. When washing requiring a cold temperature was washed using the cold wash setting- the washing took 2 hours and when it came out it was steaming hot! Needless to say some items of clothing from the wash are not what they used to be. Fridge can be on the small side for stocking food, drinks etc. Perhaps have a small bar fridge to complement, but not crucial.

author: reginafug
title: A very nice stay
text: We had the pleasure of staying in the Ballinderry four nights. The hosts, Luc and Hilde are very nice and warm. They really want you to have a good time in their guesthouse. And, then, there is Paris, the host doggie, and she loves all guests. ❤️ Our room was super spacious and very comfortable. The air conditioning was very much appreciated. The breakfast is plentiful and fresh. We really enjoyed our breakfasts, to include one glass of bubbly with breakfast. One evening we took dinner in the guest house and it was expertly prepared by Hilde. We really enjoyed our meal and thought it was delicious. Choice of wines is good. Overall, we are glad to have stayed here. One day we were stuck in the middle of nowhere, and the hosts were very kind to assist us, which we greatly appreciated. Thank you Luc! We recommend this guest house without hesitation.

author: pvc0012015
title: See you next Year
text: It starts to become a habit. I think we have visited Ballinderry for the 6th time now. It all started when we needed a place to stay and my grandparents looked at a brochure for Robertson. We did not even know they were Belgian. From the first moment we felt comfortable. since that moment, we have stayed there every time we were around, we even based our travel plans this time, based upon their availability. When you arrive, they will make you feel welcome, they explain everything and take care of you. They also give you some tips on what to visit. At night, you have the option to eat there (guests only), they discuss the menu with you and they even record what you don't like (for next time). The food is fantastic. After the food, you go to sleep, in a fantastic room. Luc and Hilde take pride in keeping their B&B updated and they update rooms all the time. Everything is always extremely clean and you can notice their eye for details. I have never seen a B&B or hotel (even my own house) so well maintained. The garden is very nice to sit in as well. We hope to visit them next year again.

author: r0man53
title: Absolutely wonderful experience
text: We stayed at Ballinderry for two nights and were allocated a wonderful large room which opened onto the gardens close to the swimming pool. The bedroom had everything you could need with huge extremely comfortable bed and massive well-equipped bathroom. There was copious storage for clothes and comfortable seating. You could make fresh real coffee and tea. We slept extremely well on both nights. On leaving the bedroom you enter the beautiful gardens with excellent swimming pool and long interesting, lawn and flower beds. Beside this is the house with options of patio area or undercover room for evening dining or breakfast. There is a large sitting room for general usage with large selection of books and TV. The guest house is close to the centre of the town and has plenty of secure parking (though security doesn't seem to be a big problem in Robertson). The owners - Hilde and Luc - are charming and do everything they can to help. Breakfast is varied, fresh and delicious. A real treat is dinner which is optional but not to be missed. Hilde plans and prepares this for a large proportion of each day and the courses are all extremely interesting and absolutely wonderful. The wine list is carefully chosen and excellent. We only ate there on our second night and bitterly regret not eating on both nights! Our stay at Ballinderry was a real highlight of our holiday in South Africa and we cannot adequately describe how much we enjoyed it and how grateful we are to Luc and Hilde for their hospitality. No wonder that so many guests there had returned after previous stays. We would love to stay there again!

author: Rohinarora
title: A Nice stopover
text: We had planned to stay at Montagu ( we were coming from Knysna and going towards Cape Town) but didn't like anything there and as it was still daylight thought of continuing on. It soon became dark and we tried finding a place to stay. We were lucky to find Ballinderry at Robertson. We had looked at 'Robertson Small hotel' (looked very nice) before this but it was a bit expensive for us and in any case it was full. The lady there helped us in contacting Luc at Ballinderry. We weren't too keen on 'grand hotel. ' Luc helped us out by giving us discount as we were staying just for the night . We were 2 couples with total of 3 kids . The kids shared a room. So we had 3 rooms in total. Rooms were nice and spacious with good bathrooms. As it was night-time, Luc suggested a nice restaurant where we could have dinner. Hilde made some very nice breakfast for us which we had by the fireplace. My wife Devicka and I went for a walk in the morning and to see what Robertson was all about. It appeared to be a nice and peaceful place. Luc and Hilde seemed to be good people and I hope they continue to do well.

author: RuthExpat
title: Just OK
text: We spent a week in the hotel: the rooms are very clean and the beds are good. The single rooms are very small. We had booked breakfast, but it was awful (coffee horrible, food thrown at the buffet, juice yucky and waiter VERY unfriendly), so we went out for breakfast everyday instead. The other staff - apart from the grumpy night porter - were friendly and spoke some English, the barman speaks German. What the main problem was was the noise within the hotel: I had the first room on the first floor directly over the lobby and dining room. I called it the room from hell, especially on Monday and Thursday when there was the most awful, loud one-man-with-keyboard dance "music" going on. The music stops promptly at 23:30, so by 24:00 when the guests have disperced to their rooms, you are lulled into thinking you might get some sleep. No chance! At 24:30 the staff rearranges all the lobby furniture and you get to hear the screeching of the sofas being pushed back into place. So when you finally drop off around one and think you'll sleep in, you're foiled again: at 07:00 all the breakfast preparation noises start and by 07:30 the mostly Italian guests (lovely people, but famously loud) are babbling again in the dining hall. The room from hell! My daughter was luckier, her room was at the back and she didn't get the dining hall din. I must say though, that we loved Ischia. The people living there not just friendly, but helpful. In May the flowers are amazing, the Island is not too busy and the food delicious. We'll go back, but sorry Punta del Sole, not to you. Shame.

author: EvgeniaP
title: Fabulously!
text: Dear all, I spent nice time in this hotel! Location: It have very suitable location (near center of Forio, 10 min to the beach). Near hotel you can find a lot of different shops. Staff & Service: I don't speak Italian but all staff from hotel tried to help me. They took care me. It's so important! All staff were attentive to my needs. Inside hotel: Hotel have thermal swimming-pool, Jacuzzi and gym. It’s suits to use both possibilities. Also I had therapeutic massage and it helped to relax. Outside hotel: Near hotel you visited open swimming-pools and Jacuzzi. And also you can used a lot of beach chairs with umbrellas. Restaurant: I tasted a lot of delicious Italian food and drank homemade white vine. I advise to choose good hotel for you rest as Hotel Punta del Sole. Evgenia

author: Padlocke
title: WOW! Seven days of fun and relaxation on this island in paradise!
text: The one thing that we liked the most about this resort is that we weren't put into a "group". We enjoyed meeting and chatting with fellow visitors, management and the friendly and wonderful staff. At our age (70 and above:-), we did not feel out of place. In other words, we fit. We did as much or as little as we wanted. There were many adventures to choose from and we kayaked, swam in the pool and ocean and picked a trip to go on each day. In addition to all of the activities, the meals were amazing! There were so many choices for each meal that is was hard to decide. All of it was over the top in flavors, quantity and quality. The Toberua Serenaders played at lunch and dinner. Their music was fun and very nice to listen to. When they weren't playing you would see them around the resort doing a multitude of other things. The management, Robyn and Warren, were always busy but made time in the evening to chat with everyone. We enjoyed all of the staff. They were always available when needed and were very warm and friendly.

author: GaryH977
title: Incredible value
text: Just got back from a short but wonderful stay at Toberua. Once here, you really wont want to leave. First of all, the value of this place in Fiji and even comparatively in the world cannot be beat, a private island paradise with minimal villas, with personalized service, clean and comfortable rooms, and private beaches at a fraction of what it would cost otherwise in Fiji or elsewhere (looking at you Maldives)! Speaking of value, do the full board meal plan, its worth it and the food is excellent, also how great is it to have the friendly staff locate your whereabouts on the island to take your next meal order?! The staff here are exceptional. Welcoming, friendly, willing to assist with anything and also very calm and laid back, all aspects of Fijian hospitality. Miri, Zach, Epele and the rest of the crew were all incredible. Once they all learn your name, that how you will be addressed! Not once was I asked what room I was in either, which I normally only find in the best of 5 star hotels! Diving is incredible in Fiji and Everett runs a great shop with Epele, and prices are excellent. Spa is great, Vita is excellent and super friendly as well. The range of complimentary activities are also great, and snorkeling off the island is pretty great already if you dont dive! Robyn and Warren run a great place, surprised its only 3 stars, as the service levels here are better than some 5 star places ive been to! Truly an Aman or Six Senses of the 3 star hotels ive been at! Truly enjoyed our stay here. 100% would recommend it to friends, solo travelers, families or couples as it has things for all types of travelers looking for an island getaway. I shall return one day and spend longer than a night!

author: 366cristis
title: Truly Paradise!
text: Absolutely amazing trip! This is a top notch place. Plenty to do on the island and plenty of space just to be still and relax as well. All the staff is very welcoming from the moment you arrive for the boat transport. They never stop smiling! It certainly feels like family very quickly. Food is fresh, local and prepared very well. Wallu in particular was scrumptious! The island offers a nice breeze and plenty of places to escape the sun if you need to. Freddy is helpful with tips on how to try any of the watercraft and Jone is the most patient and knowledgeable of scuba instructors. We were so thankful they offer the PADI diving course right there! What a treat to get certified in such amazing waters! Every night after a fun filled day it was great to have a cocktail and enjoy the sound of the Fijian musicians as they came to each table to sing for us. Such great hospitality. We absolutely loved our time here and would cherish a return trip!

author: vialegirl
title: Best week ever!
text: Recently my daughter and I spent a week on Toberua Island. It was one of the most relaxing, rejuvenating and inspiring vacation weeks we have ever experienced. The island is a paradise. It is truly a barefoot resort, and that is just what we wanted. Having never traveled to this part of the world before, we wanted to really see what Fiji was like. We loved everything from the boat ride to the island, the day trips to the Picninc Island, the amazingly professional, caring and lovely staff, to the fresh wonderful meals. The accomodations were confortable and fun! Our bure opened out on to the ocean, and we spent every evening and every morning enjoying the ocean breeze. The island is so tiny and yet it had everything we wanted. I would return in a heartbeat! Our last day in Fiji was spent touring Suva before our flight. The resort manager arranged for us to have our taxi driver take us around, store our bags and get us to the airport at the end of the day. It was perfect. Every person we encountered in Fiji, and especially on Toberua, was was friendly and helpful. It is a beautiful part of the world.

author: Colleen545
title: Best Hut on the Island
text: My husband and I celebrated our 35th anniversary at Toberua Island, we were welcomed by the staff and management upon our arrival which was a lovely touch making us feel welcome from the start. The service from the staff was absolutely amazing they accommodated us with everything we needed. Balle serviced our room most days and have a little chat such a lovely lady. Sam and Zac made our cocktails each evening and kept us entertained and yes Sam makes an awesome cappuccino! Massi and the serenaders what can I say they are incredible, up for the challenge each evening going from table to table singing a song of your choice, and they never failed to please. They are such an asset to the Island, not only do they sing and play instruments they do many activities. Thanks Massi for my coconut you sourced out, it was the best. My husband in particular loved the staff he had so much fun with them giving them nicknames which I think a few like Kawasaki and Salvatore are sure to stick as there fellow workmates loved and started using. Volley ball each evening at 5pm with staff and visitors is so much fun, just another activity that involves everyone. The meals are great, the only negative is that its a lot of food, set menus for lunch and dinner. Would be nice maybe for a bigger selection of snacks that you can order from the bar area for lunch eg. sandwiches, pizza, toasted sandwiches, pastas, nuts, chips. I know we cannot control the weather, we went to picnic island it was a horrible day we left Toberau it was windy and the water a little choppy, we were told it should calm down in about hour to hour and a half, exact opposite it was absolutely horrible it was so windy and poured with rain. I only thought when we arrived back home it would have been nice if we had been offered to have the trip rescheduled at no cost, something to think about. We stayed in Bure 2 right on the beach fantastic location THE BEST! Thank you to all the staff and management for having my loud fun loving husband and me for the week

author: Chikaby
title: The most awesomest of small island resorts in Fiji
text: If you need a massive chill out , need relaxation, want to do nothing but nothing, and want only total rest and rejuvenation, this beautiful little gem is the place to go - you can go swimming, fishing , deep sea diving, snorkelling, day trips to Picnic island , kayaking, paddle-boarding too , but if you just want to indulge in eating, sleeping and reading with the occasional massage and a pedicure or a manicure, you can do this too. Don't go here if all you want to do is party - its not that type of place. The island ambience is gracious and gentle, quiet and peaceful and it is this tranquility that eases one to a deep sleep each evening. The trees flutter their leaves all day and bird song is tropical in its chitter and most delightful. It can be windy and it can be gentle and calm - the veritable range of weather is just as changeable and interesting as watching a match at Wimbledon. It sure beats watching TV any day. Did we mention the food ! OMG Mala the chef and his crew are pretty awesome - they give you a choice each day of menu and you choose what you want to eat. The crab appetisers and local spinach soups are superb. The fresh fish is to die for - and I totally died and went to heaven each day. We particularly liked the use of fresh local ingredients on the menu - food we would certainly not get back home so we appreciated the chance to experience Fijian cuisine at its finest. Management Sandy, Max, Sameer, Lenni and staff are so personable, friendly, obliging, graceful and beautiful people. They took the time to ensure we , and other guests on the island were happy and made sure we did not want for anything . The care and consideration given to every guest from arrival to departure was especially outstanding. We note from our own extensive travels that this feature on its own often distinguishes great accommodation from the ordinary. It is no wonder than that Toberua continues to receive the fabulous accolades that it deserves. We were thankful of the opportunity of spending time here , loved every minute and would travel back again soon if we could. Vinaka !

author: TexasDadWaco
title: 5 days of near perfection!
text: Ok, near perfection. Why well no selves, drawers for clothes but two twin beds to leave suitcases open on. No anti fog for masks, but you always have spit, and third, well that was it only two lame complaints. The stay was fantastic. The snorkeling great. The people great. Hats off to Max and Sandy for a great resort well staffed! The good. OMG is just kept getting better every day! I have learned not to eat beef in such locations, but the bar b que night had tenderloins and they were as good as any I gave had in the states! Lunch the next day featured this same beef on salads! Fantastic. Bar drinks were always fresh made and Zack was great! Always a smile but hey he works on an island, how bad can it be! We took a behind the scenes tour and saw just what it takes to be self sufficient out in the sea! Pretty cool stuff. Grab a book, or borrow one, hop a plane ride, only 11 hours from LA and just go! Dead of their winter, water was warm enough days were pleasant and night were cool for sleeping. Great time to go.

author: shylyriley
title: A Fijian home away from home
text: I recently stayed on Toberua Island for 5 nights with my husband. We stayed in Bure 12A. We booked Toberua as we needed to totally relax and disconnect from our hectic lives. We were slightly taken aback by the taxi transfer....we assumed we would get our island vibe on when greeted at the airport...but we were not spoken to, just herded into an old style vehicle without fully functioning seat belts and driven in silence to the boat launch. Once we arrived on the island the famous Fijian greeting was in full swing. I must say we loved the communal volleyball game every night at 5pm...so much fun to watch and participate in...it created a terrific sense of community. We opted for the inclusive dining package. We were fed 3 times a day at set times with a delicious variety of local foods...all tastes were catered for. I found some of the food slightly rich for my palette, however I just chose what I wanted from the 3 to 4 courses offered and was always satisfied. We snorkelled, kayaked around the island many times, fished and swam and swam and then swam some more. The staff....oh the staff...they are just delightful....I must say however I had a very strong affinity to the wonderful Zack...he was just delightful...if I could take Zack home I would..he is a true gentleman!!! There are so many lovely things to say about our experience on Toberua Island. If you want an off the grid, community minded, relaxed holiday...then book now! I must also thank Masi and his melodic sidekick for their wonderful western and Fijian tunes every night. We were sad to say goodbye to Toberua...however we carry this tiny little Fijian island in our hearts forever!!! Thank you!

author: SheilaXOS
title: Be aware of extra costs
text: Beautiful island resort. Helpful staff but female of couple management team could use some better customer service tips. Transport to the resort was not fully ironed out prior to holiday and resort could have handled transfer options much better. Miscommunication cost me a full day lost in enjoying resort and also cost me a lot more money than when I left resort. Issue was cleared up but only because I keep immaculate records in correspondence. No apology was made however regarding miscommunication. Manager was quite defensive when I was only trying to help her as several other reviewers have complained about hidden costs. I.e., if you know it's an issue with third parties make sure the transfer and meal options are brought to light. Go above and beyond. Customer service is everything. Wifi is spotty which is fine but there should be no charge for it then. Excursions were nice and reasonably priced. Food was good but overpriced as there are no other options. Staff was friendly and Lini was extremely helpful! Nice resort of you want off the grid but be aware of all costs to be incurred.

author: yasminc215
title: A slice of true paradise
text: Thank you to Sandy & Max and the staff for a wonderful stay at Toberua! My husband and I recently visited Toberua to get away from the NZ winter and it truely lived up to our expectations, offering plenty of rest, relaxation and sunshine! From the greeting from the staff when we first arrived on the island to the sad farewell when we departed, we loved every moment. We stayed in an Ocean Front Bure, the room was absolutely huge and we had many peaceful nights listening to the waves out the front. The outdoor shower was fantastic and our room was kept clean and tidy daily. The staff and food were probably what made our trip though. Fijians are known for being very welcoming and friendly and Toberua did not disappoint. Every night we headed to the bar for a sunset cocktail, where we enjoyed the company of the staff and their singing. We joined them to play volleyball and went out snorkelling every afternoon to the most amazing spots. Every meal we got to choose an option, always three courses and the food was so fresh and delicious. We were particularly fond of the fresh bread. One thing that was new to us was the wildlife on the island, lots of birds everywhere, a few bats and the odd black and white snake! We got used to it though and nothing bothered us too much. We actually did a day trip to bird island and also kayaked the mangroves, which we highly recommend. Oh and the massage, also great! All in all, a perfect trip and we can't wait to come back the same time next year!

author: MiniMantis
title: Absolute paradise - take me back!
text: I hardly know where to start - to rave about the pristine water and breath-taking snorkelling, the gorgeous white sandy beaches, the delectable and varied food, or the numerous luscious napping spots I found to sleep off said-delectable meals? I think that starting point has to be the people - the staff at Toberua, in the restaurant and bar, the housekeeping crew, the spa ladies, the boatmen and gardeners, the amazing managers, Max and Sandy, and everyone else there - are really what make this place incredible and utterly unique. And that is saying a lot, because it's an idyllic tropical paradise, so one might ask how you could improve on that! But Fiji is famous for its people's hospitality, and everyone that works at Toberua typifies that. My boyfriend and I were embraced as family - he even got to play bass with the band! Mixed in with the bird call and lapping of gentle waves, there is always someone having a giggle. I think it's that that really stole my heart. In saying that, Toberua won our affections instantly in many other ways too. It somehow strikes that magical balance between having an atmosphere in which you can totally relax and do nothing except swing in a hammock, and having lots to offer if you do feel like doing an activity or two. We did the kayaking trip in the mangroves which I definitely recommend - it was like exploring somewhere no one had ever been. We also went to Picnic Island which - well there's no describing it - you just have to go. It is the castaway island of postcards. We also snorkelled a lot and used the catamaran which was exhilarating! The rooms are wonderful - I loved the open-air shower where you can shower under the sun each morning (don't worry, no one can see in!), and our balcony that looked straight onto the Pacific. The rooms are traditional structures, but with all the luxury you could want (I could lie horizontally across the bed and not touch the sides!) which we really liked. Being in some apartment-like shoebox is not our idea of a tropical holiday, so Toberua's rooms were perfect. Just writing this is making me homesick for Toberua - and it's saying a lot that you can be homesick for somewhere other than home! Big lolomas to all the staff and the managers - we'll be back! xo

author: AM029
title: Left speechless, well rested and with our tummies full.
text: Toberua is beautiful! The island is what you would see on a postcard...blue clear waters, colorful fish, coconut trees, hammocks, huge spacious bure styled rooms...its paradise! Having been to Fiji once before, I really wanted to experience what it would be like to stay on an outer island so I watched a few YouTube videos and Toberua was recommended as one of the top 10 (but also within my price range). It was worth every cent. Not only is the resort beautiful, the hospitality received by the staff makes for a welcoming atmosphere. The attention to detail, staff coming to your room personally and taking your order for breakfast, lunch and dinner, chefs being aware of my food allergies and catering around that and making such delicious meals, the quick efficient responses to my emails about transport and food packages, staff welcoming you at the dock and waving goodbye to you as you leave, meeting the wonderful hosts..all this and more made us feel special and truly looked after. I have to mention, that having hotel hopped around a few different hotels on the mainland (Suva, Coral Coast, Nadi)...Toberua gives you something totally different, an Fijian/Island experience worth having. I found rest/peace/zen/whatever you like to call it..I found it at Toberua!!!! With no TV, limited WiFi that is only available at the bar area (my own data worked fine on my phone), its almost like your forced to disconnect from technology and focus on spending quality time with traveling companions, focus on the beautiful surroundings, focus on yourself...the things/people that matter. With the opportuntity to focus on myself LOL...I found time to book in for a hot stone massage and mini facial in the most ideal location for a spa; getting pampered listening to the waves crashing just outside (not through the speakers) was amazing. So amazing I dozed off a few times.(apologies for any snoring). Haha If we had stayed more than one night we would have found time to participate and do some of the activities on offer. Next time we will be staying for longer, that's for sure. Talking from my own experience, when Im on holiday theres a little bit of guilt that comes with not occupying your time with sightseeing and activities because maybe I feel like im not making the most of my trip or Im missing out on experiencing what Fiji has to offer. You don't have any of these worries staying at Toberua. You are there to relax. Find some zen. And you will find it easily here in paradise with the most beautiful staff looking after you. Thank you to all the staff for the wonderful experience. Vinaka.

author: viajeraloca2090
title: Little piece of paradise ❤️
text: This lovely island has been recomended to us by two separate couples. Since we have newer visited the Suva side of Fiji we said why not! " it's only 30 minutes with a boat from the main land. It is a tiny island resort with only 15 bures. It has a lovely swimming pool under the palm trees and modest facilities of lots of things to do if you decided not to swim or snorkel for the day. One of the most special think for the resort is the management and the staff has a lovely welcoming, friendly and happy -typical Fijian attitude. " which I found it's disappearing at many resorts as they get bigger and more crowded". They made us feel special. Even there is quite a bit to snorkel for around the island, they took us to complimentary snorkeling trips every second day. Also the food was very different then any other Fijian resort I have ever been. Creative menus daily with local ingredients. Was fresh and delicious. Every lunch and dinner there was a guitar music which tick another box. For families, I guess any time of the year wold be nice but for couples who likes to have a quite, peaceful and romantic holiday...I recommend them to choose the dates out of Australian school holidays period. If you like to have a peace of paradise I highly recommend this lovely, well looked after green island with beautiful sunshine and sea.

author: LindaS698
title: Hidden Gem, Oceanfront Bures, Live Music, Wonderful People!
text: My 7 year old son and I booked a one week holiday here in January 2017. We chose the resort based on our Travel Agent’s recommendation and would not hesitate to return. It’s perfect for families with young or older children, as well as couples or singles – there was a mix on our trip and everyone we met were return guests – some had been 7 times! This is a tranquil spot 25 mins by boat from Nasouri which has 15 beautiful Bures right on the ocean front. No garish bed spreads here! Think Pure Fiji products in the bathroom, swinging chairs and sunbeds on the deck. My son absolutely loved the snorkling trips where he saw Nemo and Blue Star Fish. The dive school is great with the most reassuring and experienced instructor – Sirello. The live music at lunch and dinner sets the scene beautifully and Max and Sandy are wonderful hosts. The resident musician Masi doubles as the pied piper with kids so don’t be concerned there is no kids club - they are guaranteed to be entertained with kite flying, fishing, crab races and water sports. Did I mention the food is delicious? The staff here go above and beyond in a genuine way – especially Bale. We stayed in Bure 5 which was lovely. We’ve got our eye on Bure 3 for next time – next to water sports and with a sandy access to the water straight from the room. I also had a lovely massage in the Spa. We’ll be back – for longer!

author: givilomitour
title: Perfect place to spend relaxing holidays
text: We spent 7 nights on Toberua and it was perfect. - Perfect from beginning : pick-up at the airport with private boat transfer as we where the only family to arrive at this time. Greetings by Max and Sandy who manage this island. - Beautiful bure : we liked the bathroom with its outdoor space, the room is quite large and you can enjoy the sound of the ocean while falling asleep, true luxury ! You have your own outdoor furniture with hammock, sun lounge and swing. The view from the deluxe oceanfront bure is quite stunning. - Fine food : full of flavours ! When you ear the drums, you know it’s time for meal. Cooked breakfast, 3 course lunch, 4 course dinner. Everything is perfect. - Snorkel : snorkel off the beach is good but you have to swim a bit further (not easy for young kids). There are complimentary daily boat trips to different locations (sand bar, double tree) where snorkel is very good. I truly recommend the trip to ‘picnic island’ where you’ll find amazing snorkel. Clams, Angelfish, Damsel-fish, Anemone-fish, Cuttlefish, Surgeon-fish, Octopus, Butterfly, Parrot, Goatfish, Trigger-fish, ... Lovely staff ! A small island with lush vegetation and stunning scenery. Only negative point : we didn’t want to leave.

author: eillae
title: Family holiday on the lovely Toberua Island
text: We have just come back from spending a very relaxing week on the lovely Toberua Island Fiji. Toberua Island is very small with only 15 bures. If you want to get away from everything then this is the place to go. The bures are spacious with an amazing outlook only meters from the water. We spent our time kayaking, paddle boarding & swimming around the island. There is no TV(which was great) so take a good book or two. The food was good, though a bit hit & miss at times. I think there is room for some improvement here but overall nothing to complain about. There was definitely a lot of food so you won't go hungry. What really makes the island is the staff. The staff are all amazing. So helpfully & friendly. All staff know you by name. A special mention to Asa & Pita our amazing bar staff. You were awesome. I would definitely recommend Toberua Island Resort though my one word of advise would be if you can avoid Australian school holidays then do so as the island did get a bit overrun by young children on our last couple of days.

author: SallyBell6
title: Fifth visit, been home one week, desperately want to plan my sixth!
text: My parents first took me to Toberua in 1980, and again in 1983 and 1988. After a 26 year gap I took my children in 2014, and, I've just come back from the most wonderful visit with my partner. The trip was meant to "get it out of my system", but all it did was get it into HIS system! It was so wonderful to show him first-hand a little place that has stolen my heart and is an irrefutable part of my life. He "got it" immediately. The bures, the food, but more importantly the genuine warmth of the hosts and staff make this place so special. The wonderful balance between luxury and service / barefoot and unpretentious is something that you can't manufacture... it just "is". Big resorts or exclusive adult-only luxury retreats just cannot provide what Toberua does. It also provides wonderful opportunity to make new friends, or you can simply enjoy privacy if that's what you prefer. On this trip, too, we really found out how fabulous the snorkelling can be, if you ask the guys to take you just a little bit further out... there was a section of reef drop-off which provided some of the best snorkelling I've done in my life. And the Village Trip is so genuine, heartwarming and uplifting. Fijians are the happiest people in the world. Just read all the other reviews (how many destinations AVERAGE just a whisker below 5 stars?), and GO. Just GO. You will not regret it. I only wish the lali drum was calling me for another meal, right now. *SIGH*

author: sonjam758
title: I didn't want to leave!
text: My friend and I are mid twenties and have just returned from an utterly blissful week on Toberua. I HIGHLY recommend it. There's not much I can say that hasn't already been said... We stayed in Bure 8 which was on the "windier" side of the island and was delightful! A beautiful breeze nearly 24/7 and we could sleep with the doors wide open! It was peaceful, you would think you were the only ones on the island! We also got the food package (which whilst expensive) is highly recommended! The food was delightful, varied and fresh! The best thing is the staff come and find you throughout the day to take your order for your next meal. Bliss. Great activities.. The snorkelling was out of this world! Do it as much as you can! And endless kayaking, SUPing, swimming, sailing... The staff are beautiful. They remember your name and are such caring and kind people, they make this island! In summary, GO HERE! A blissful week of relaxation and fun. Thanks Toberua for making my first visit to Fiji so memorable, I'm sure it won't be my last!

author: RenuB
title: Enjoyed our stay on our very own “Gilligan’s Island”!
text: We just spent 7 nights on Toberau Island Resort. It was my first time to Fiji and Toberau. I loved that it felt like we were staying on our own “private” island. The best part of the trip was the staff. From the owners (Glen & Joann), to the managers (Max & Sandy), to Wise in the dining room, to Asa at the bar, to Lennie in the office, to countless others, you felt like they treated us like their family. The lodging and food were wonderful. We requested the bures on the windy side of the island and enjoyed the tropical cool breeze while sleeping with the doors wide open. The food was fresh and plentiful. My only suggestion would be a few more options on the bar menu for those that want to eat a light lunch. We only did 3 excursions through the resort and wish we had done more. The Mangrove kayak trip was enjoyable. The city tour of Suva did not work out as we planned but Max/Sandy handled it fairly. The village tour is a must because it provides a peek inside the Fijians daily life. The rest of the time we spent at the beach, pool, paddleboarding, kayaking, snorkeling and just unplugging from our electronic life at home. The musicians they had daily for us were great. They sang just about everything; even learned Deep in the Heart of Texas for us! I would highly recommend Toberua Island Resort!

author: raftus88
title: Solitude, quiet and relaxing
text: This place is a secluded upmarket village/island, very relaxing. We visited in early December before the tropical cyclone season and its taken some months to fully consider our stay here. Reservations system for international payments was very confusing, best just to use a credit card. The transfers were very easy and well organised by reservations from Suva (Nausori) airport and Nakelo Landing for your boat transfer. Most international flights land into Nadi and the small aircraft over to Suva is quite expensive with Fiji Air. Arrival upon the island was great, we had a deluxe Bure which suited our family of 2A2C. People said Fiji in December was very hot but I guess coming from Brisbane we found it very nice with the sea breezes. It was right on the beach and you are living in a small village of bures, so it is quite special. You wander over to meals when the village drum sounds, ordering a drink from the bar enroute. Our teenage girls didn't eat three full meals per day so the value in the meal package (which didn't seem to be negotiable) for some families is questionable. Housekeeping and the village staff were all excellent without fault. Loved the open bathroom with sea views. The catamaran sail tore while we were there and they didn't seem to have a spare but there was paddle boarding and kayaks and the sea was quite calm. The dive team are nothing short of sensational, very calm instructors and for those that wish to do the intro, start early in your stay as its the ideal place to learn in the pool and then transition to the ocean. For advanced divers the vis was good, the reefs and marine life great, the gear well maintained and you can run through whichever advanced course you want to. Various dive boats that were well maintained. Great to go out and do a boat dive at 10.00am, back for lunch and a few cold beers and chill the rest of the day. I would certainly go back.

author: TravelBugin415
title: WOW - this is the place to stay in Fiji
text: This was truly a special place to stay for 5 nights this November. The only negative is that we didn't stay longer! I think the Island has 13 bures, a "14th" for the talking, jalapeno eating parrot, Jack. We stayed in bure 12, which was lovely but a bit strange that while in the shower, you can see directly into the windows of the second floor of one of the staff houses. We arrived and departed to the staff singing at the dock. They also serenade each of the tables at dinner nightly. The whole island was quite musically talented it really added to the island's ambiance. The staff choir performed on Sunday which was a special treat. There was plenty of time to relax and enjoy a phenomenal setting but there were also a lot of options for entertainment each day. The kayaking trip through the mangrove was a great adventure. We also had a fantastic dive at Sacred Reef. The dive masters were great guides and helped to make me, a sometimes nervous diver, quite at ease. 5 stars all around, the food, the setting, and the people. We definitely would love the chance to return here. One note - the transfer cost to be picked up/returned to the dock or Suva is about $215 (U.S.) per person.

author: 560neshk
title: Tranquil Wonderland!
text: My family and I (consists of 2 toddlers under 4 and my wife and I) stayed here mid November for 5 nights. We were really looking forward to getting away and spending some quality time with our children. We were not disappointed! We were quite late to arrive at the jetty for the launch to the island, and the staff that were waiting for us were very polite and understanding (consider a flight direct to Suva if you are coming from Nadi, we drove, not a good idea with toddlers!!!). Once we got to the island, all of what we expected we experienced within the first few minutes. Staff were wonderful, location simply beautiful and accommodation on the mark. I know many people talk about food and other things, but for my family and I, the friendliness of staff is most important. Toberua Island Resort cannot be faulted for this. The staff were great, always willing to set time aside for a quick chat with us, or to play with our children. It was an awesome experience that our toddlers are still talking about (especially being a part of the band during dinner!!!!) Food was great, with varying menu's throughout the stay. Though some may find the cost pricey, it is well worth it considering some of the other places we went to later in our trip (this place was our highlight, did I mention that!). We will definitely be looking to come back to visit again very soon. It was the perfect place to spend good quality time with family without the digital distractions. All I can say is do it. Go there, it is well worth it and you will not regret it.

author: FogHat13
title: Words will not do this place justice, you have to see it for yourself!
text: BULA!! This was our first time to Fiji, and we will never forget it! We were in shock after setting foot on the island, the weather was perfect, the water warm and inviting, the employees on the island singing and smiling, you can’t help but feel bliss. The island is a perfect get away, it’s quiet but with lots to do and the staff are some of the friendly people I have ever had the pleasure of meeting, AND THE FOOD!!!!!!!!! The food was outstanding, they give you a bit to choose from and there was not one thing that I didn’t like and I am somewhat of a picky eater. The music what a great touch, there is nothing like eating a great dinner watching the sun go down and having live music. All of the activities were great, one of my favorites was Picnic Island, and it is completely under sold. We almost passed it up just because it sounded ok, but we were already on an island did we really need to pay to go see another island? It is a MUST I am so happy we went!! I will admit I was worried about the snakes after reading some of the reviews on here, but they are blowing it way way way out of proportion, we only saw 3 and they stand out very well and they want nothing to do with you. My only regret is that we did not stay long, 5 days is not enough I wish we would have done 7 or more. There were a lot of thing that we missed out on doing (including the BBQ) because we didn’t stay all 7 days. Vinaka! Vinaka! Vinaka! Thank you so much for the unforgettable time and memories, we will be back!!

author: W2165TGscottm
title: Our Island Home
text: We had Toberua recommended to us by several friends and they couldn't say enough nice things about it, now we know why. My partner and I booked the holiday almost 18 months ago so it was a long wait, but the trip exceeded our expectations. Renee who handles all the internet enquiries was amazing to deal with as I was planning a proposal on our trip and had some specific requirements, all of these were met with a professional touch. We stayed in Bure 2 one of the premium Bure's on the less windy side of the island (for this time of year) and it was spectacular, two steps of your verandah at high tide and you are in the ocean with a spectacular small coral reef about 2 metres out from the shore which we snorkelled above daily, lots of fish and star fish and some very pretty corals. Because tou are inside the main reef, there are no big waves, it's more like swimming in the calmest ocean everyday, at low tide your can walk around the island and check out all the crabs, starfish etc and gain a different view of the place. The food was sensational, hot breakfasts if you wanted, or fruits, cereal and toast. 3 course lunches, 4 course dinners and BBQ night on Saturday was just great. Day trips are great to do or you can just relax, the trip to the local village (when a lot of the staff are from) is a must, bird island was amazing, and there are plenty of diving and snorkelling trips available. We both work in by busy and stressful jobs, so the ability to be cut off from the world was much needed and quite novel. The staff managers Max and Sandy were lovely and very knowledgable, and the way they moved among all guests during their stay to make them feel welcome was very nice and now to their staff. The staff at Toberua are why you will come back, they make you feel like family members and their level of attentiveness was something we've never experienced before, the bar boys Zak, Asa and Pita are true ambassadors of Fiji and they mix a mean cocktail. The serenaders especially Mase, Ronnie and Georgie have voices and harmonies that make the hairs on your neck stand up, and having them play at lunch and dinner just further ads to the magic, the wait staff are so friendly and Ledua runs the kitchen staff like a well oiled team. My partner went to the day spa and raved about her massage whilst I went fishing with Pelli and had a great time, even out the fish were not really biting. I've tried not to gush in this review, but it's hard not to, Toberua is our new home away from home and we are planning our return soon, we've even talked the in laws into coming as well. We made many happy memories in Fiji and Toberua Island, just book now, you will not be disappointed,

author: wesley5
title: We love it
text: It was our fourth visit back to Toberua... after spending our honeymoon there in 1999. We love the atmosphere of the island.The bures are spacious with the wonderful inside / outside bathroom. The island is relaxing, with enough activities to keep everyone happy.... if you want to go for a sail or paddle board, just wander down to the beach and there they are ! Fishing trips are held every couple of days for a small cost. Once a day ( weather permitting) there are trips out to various snorkelling sites for any one who wants to go. Most days, there could be additional activities such as a picnic on a sandy island 30 mins away, a village trip, a staff church service , kayaking in the coastal mangroves...these are all special experiences. The food is excellent ( the best we have eaten in our travels in Fiji)with beautiful fresh meals, served in a lovely location, with beautiful Fijian singing at lunch and dinner . We always find some interesting people to chat to from around the world and our 13 year daughter loves the island too. The staff are outstanding and we will return to Toberua again ! We know that it a special place that we leave each time relaxed and feeling as if we had a holiday. Wifi is available for a small cost in the bar area ( just enough to check emails ) No TVs ! Small mini library, mini gym. A special place for those people who don't want a big resort !

author: Cheezel
title: Left under Clouds
text: We have returned to this special place many times. This visit was under grey skies and night time rain. But even then we left relaxed and with regret. Toberua Island has an attraction that draws people from all over the world back again and again. It leaves people refreshed, and happy to pass on a recommendation for this little gem. It is as unspoilt as any place could be while providing for the tourist market. Apart from the weather I think most people would be hard to please if they found reason to complain. The food is as good as anything we have experienced in the South Pacific. It is an interesting mix of European and local, but Malakai never loses the thread to fresh Fijian produce and taste. And the best thing, the quality is consistent. Anyone that was left hungry would be very to hard to please! Zac at the bar mixes any cocktail you desire with an endless and genuine smile. The band will happily play or learn a song for you if requested, and the managers, Sandy and Max, go beyond the call of duty to insure Toberua, for every guest, is memorable. From the smile at the front desk to the friendly "Bula" of the grounds man it would be hard to find another small, intimate resort with more to offer. The weather, as I mentioned was inclement, (not exclusively at Toberua). But there are still numerous off island activities included (free), board games, a small library, pool and table tennis, volleyball, gym, spa and optional trips are offered at a competitive rate. This island doesn't fail to deliver. There have been upgrades since our last visit but the essence of Toberua remains unchanged. We are already planning another visit back and what higher recommendation could I give?

author: 152keithh
title: Excellent resort - will definitely return!
text: After planning a long dive trip in Australia I planned to go to Fiji to chill out before my long trip back to the UK and this was the perfect place to do it. From the moment you arrive in Suva everything is made easy - a taxi takes you to the boat (only a ten minute taxi ride) and then you have a great 30 minute boat ride out along a river then out to the island. You get a real sense of how small it is when you are approaching it from the mainland. On arrival there is a welcome party on the jetty and you are greeted so warmly by the staff. My 'bure' was excellent - open and spacious and well equipped. That said, I did not spend a great deal of time there. The pool area is generous for the size of the island and I spend many hours lazing around reading by the pool with the occasional dip to cool down. The dive centre is great - I the island has a dive instructor and dive master and they know the dive sites exceptionally well and give really good guided dives. They really look after you too which is reassuring when you are travelling alone with no 'buddy'. Several guests were doing their Open Water PADI on the island whilst I was there. The food is exceptional - you are never hungry! Breakfast, lunch and dinner are generous and delicious and you will be hard pressed to find high end restaurants which could beat this place. There is regular tea, coffee and cookies laid out in the bar area during the mornings and afternoons. The staff are superb - so attentive, remembering your name after only one introduction but making you feel special and like you're party of the island family. The entertainment they provide is also fantastic - taking song requests from guests over dinner which creates an intimate but inclusive are atmosphere. I would thoroughly recommend Toberua - as a solo traveller I found I could be as involved or not involved as I wanted to be as the staff draw you in when you are there alone. Families and couples will also find there to be plenty to do throughout a trip. I will definitely return one day!

author: SallyBell6
title: Everything I'd remembered and more
text: Toberua is part of me and always will be. I want to be back there right now and I only left just over a week ago. I first stayed on this unique island in 1980, and then twice more in that decade, with my parents, when I was in my late teens and early 20s. When I returned this year with my two mid-teenage children - 26 years since my last visit - I was completely mesmerised by the place once more. It is exactly as it has always been, only better - the warmth and inclusivity is incomparable. I don't believe there's anywhere else where you will find as genuine a welcome from the delightful hosts Max and Sandy, and such true friendship and warmth from the staff (Pita, Ratu, Zachariah, Masi, Ledua... everyone really!). I felt so at home in the beautiful hand-crafted bures with their remodelled patios and bathrooms; I loved walking barefoot down the shaded sandy pathways to the beautiful bar and restaurant; the meals were amazing with huge variety and choice across the week (can I have some kokoda and some chargrilled fresh tuna NOW please?); and the activities on offer were all delightful. The "included" snorkelling trip every day was a highlight, and we also loved the must-do village trip and the mangrove paddling. I wondered if my older teenagers would "get it" or whether I'd left it too long... I needn't have worried, they want to go back as soon as possible. And along with all this, we made some amazing friends who I miss already. Just go. Soon. Although don't let everyone in on the secret. :-)

author: ricke85
title: Honeymooners paradise
text: My new wife and I.... Yes I said new.... Both been married before but that's a different review!!.... enjoyed 8 amazing nights... That's a review not for publication!... on this island paradise. The accommodation is top notch, comfortable and traditional. Whether you're there to relax by the pool drinking cocktails.. Which we did plenty of, Enjoy a massage.... Which my wife did plenty of!!.. partake in a wide range of water based activities, a boozy afternoon fishing with the boys... Which I did a little of!!.. or a breath taking trip to picnic Island, followed by a twilight kava fuelled friendly game of volleyball with the locals. That'll build your appetite for an amazing meal under the stars. But what really makes this resort so special is that as soon as you're serenaded off the boat on arrival the staff make you feel like you're the most important person there. Their friendliness, warmth and humour is infectious. My advice is enjoy the luxury this place has to offer... Its hard to beat.... But experience the local culture the staff are eager to share also.. Very special

author: 240emmaa
title: Perfect family holiday
text: A belated post but one I've been meaning to write. Our family of five (children 5,7,9) visited this island resort for Easter 2013. We also celebrated our son's 7th birthday during our stay. The people were exceptionally kind and friendly and made the experience so much fun for the kids with snorkelling, fishing and mini golf. The chef took great delight in cooking the big fish our kids caught off the pier .. Staff also took our children paddle boarding when they didn't want to come on a boat ride with the rest of us. We were concerned that such a small island would have its limits in terms of activities to keep the kids happy but, on the contrary, there was so much to do in simply enjoying the simple things. The highlight for us was Saturday night hermit crab racing which raised $$$ which we took to the nearby village the next day to present to the local school .. This is a paradise where families and honeymooners can co-exist with ease. It's tranquil, relaxing and good fun for all and the place is small enough such that you can let the kids roam free with no fear of stranger danger .. The wonderfully cheerful Fijian staff are the real treasure on this island. We couldn't recommend it more highly .. One note .. Ask for the rooms numbered 1,2 or 3. The others on the other side are a little dark and windy

author: Cheezel
title: Returnee's Still Impressed
text: We have just returned from another trip to Toberua. This time we have revisited with our children who both spent many holidays on the island while growing up. Each time we return we worry the quality will have lessened. The staff will have changed or new staff may not give the same open, honest and friendly service or that the food may not be up to the standard that Mala and Manu provide. This certainly was not the case. In our opinion Toberua is unsurpassed as a place to kick back and relax. The food is as good as anything we have experienced in the South Pacific. The variety and mix or European/Fijian ingredients make the meals both interesting and delicious. Between fresh fruits, muffins pastries and anything cooked you desire for breakfast to three course lunches and four course evening meals (plus morning/afternoon tea and evening bar snacks) you are spoilt for choice and never left hungry or disappointed. The bures are excellent. As always the house keeping was great. A friendly smile and spotless room. Toberua is tiny, only around four acres - but there are many trips off the island to suit all tastes. They include village trips, mangrove tours, bird island and a picnic on a pure white sandy beach only a short boat trip away. On the island there is also much to entertain guests or a nice small pool and loungers if you simply want to relax. Toberua is not the most convenient island to access but it is well worth the effort. The management are doing a great job of keeping this special place at a standard that keeps so many people returning time and time again. Soon there will be a larger bure (three bedrooms) for anyone wanting to visit in a larger group or family. Our thanks go out to the wonderful friends we have at Toberua and Sandy and Max the managers. We are already planning another trip.

author: gaiteiro
title: Our new favourite spot in Fiji
text: The main advantage of Toberua is that it is so small - only 15 bures. This means that all the staff know your name within hours of arrival (including the gardeners). We felt really welcome from the moment we set foot on the island, and that feeling lasted the whole time - it was a real wrench when our time on the island was up. The bures are very spacious and done in a fairly traditional style with great logs for the support timbers and a high steeply pitched ceiling. One very useful feature is the "scullery" yard which connects the beachside verandah to the bathroom - ideal for washing the sand of the feet and leaving all the swimming/snorkelling/diving gear to rinse and dry. The food was excellent, and although the FJ$150 per day seemed a bit dear, in reality it was not. Your $150 includes buffet breakfast, morning tea, three course lunch, afternoon tea and a four course dinner, with lunch and dinner having a choice of three main courses - fish, meat or vegetarian. The staff will come round the island to find you to take your order in advance of the meal, which might seem a bit odd to some people, but does have the advantage of meaning there is a lot less food wastage in the kitchen. The Saturday evening barbecue was perfectly catered - everyone had plenty to eat, and the only meat left at the end of the evening was one sausage and a small piece of steak. What to do on the island? Despite the small size of the island there are plenty of things to keep you occupied both on and off the water - daily snorkelling trips to amazing nearby reefs, diving, sport fishing, hand-line fishing, sailing, kayaking, paddle-boarding, reef golf, path putting, tabletennis, pool, croquet, beach volleyball, and some excellent half day and day trips - visiting local villages, mangrove kayaking, visiting the local bird sanctuary island, picnic Island trip, Levuka day trip, shopping trips to Suva..... Except for the daily snorkelling trips any activity involving a power boat incurs a charge, but these are not excessive, and the non-powered water activities are all free - my wife and elder son spent most of our week sailing and paddle-boarding. The whole friendly attitude of the island begins with the managers, Max and Sandy who are always to be seen around the island, asking everyone how they are, what they've enjoyed, suggesting stuff to do, chatting with guests at the bar, and generally making sure that every single guest is as happy as they could be. The resort can have no better recommendation than in the number of returning guests they have - one American couple were on their 10th visit, and an Australian couple had been coming since 1983! And on the day we left there was a palpable excitement among the staff that arriving as we were leaving was a woman with her young baby who had first visited when she was a baby (and there were still staff who remember looking after her then). We're definitely going to be returning.

author: bbaker71
title: An amazing holiday
text: I write this review a bit hesitantly. I love sharing great experiences, and without trip advisor we wouldn't have found toberua, but you really don't want everyone knowing how amazing this place is. My family with two teenage kids spent five nights on the island recently - i wish it was more. It's hard to list all the highlights but lets start with the absolute number one - the staff. It's a pretty special place as it is, but compared to other parts of Fiji, they really do set it apart. Snorkelling and fishing with Charles, epelli and asao, having a few quite drinks at the bar with ratu, peta and Zach. Meree turning our messy room into a haven again everyday or Frances with her fantastic massages and facials at the islands spa. And the band, who can forget the band. As for the island itself its stunning. Small enough to get around, big enough to have your own space whenever you wanted it. We were located on the windy side of the island but it didn't matter, we loved the breeze. The snorkelling was fantastic. The village trip a must and yes, picnic island is unforgettable. Just don't forget the sun cream... The food was excellent and I'm very sad to have to wear shoes again. Very sad. Teenage kids can be hard work sometimes, but I haven't seen my kids so relaxed and happy for years. We all agreed its the best break we have had, and we will become regular visitors to toberua as so many of the people we met on the island were. Thank you sandy and max for allowing us to spend some time on your wonderful island. See you next year.

author: 844MichaelF
title: If only there were 6 stars!
text: I cannot say this enough, you HAVE to go here. Yes, it will take you a little longer to get to this idyllic location but it is worth the wait. Yes, you will pay a little more than you might at other Fiji locations but for what you get, you will want for nothing. To put it out there. You will pay three packages: for the rooms, for transfer to and from the island, for the food package and then you'll pay for incidentals if you want them (alcohol, scuba, the spa facilities etc). None of these are super cheap but none of them are going to break the bank either and listen to what you get. Paradise. 16 bures, no locks, no phones, no TVs, (internet if you want it...why?) and staff that will bend over backwards to help you and get to know you. The snorkeling, fishing, kayaking, and catamaran-ing is all included. The meals are incredible and staff will find you through the day to ask what you'd like for lunch and dinner so that you can just sit and have it brought to you. It is both couple and family friendly and you can choose to make friends with the guests or have your own private hide-away with outdoor showers and private hammocks. The day trip to the local village is a must. You will relax like you have never relaxed before, I promise you this. You will never want to leave. My wife and kids were in tears when we left because we felt like we had just left family behind. We will return as soon as we can. Go find your warm, happy place.

author: facie60
title: This bed and breakfast beats all!
text: The Brookside Mountain Mist Inn is perfectly lovely. We've been going there annually for almost 10 years.The Inn is so spotless, you could practically eat off the floors.The location is perfect with a gorgeous view of the mountains. What makes this B&B extraordinary is the hosts; they are extremely inviting and friendly but also respect their guests' privacy. They are helpful without being intrusive. The breakfasts are to die for, and we have not felt much of a need to eat again until dinner. During our recent stay, we decided to enjoy the "romantic dinner for two." Once again, the food was succulent, and the best part was being able to stay right there in the Inn enjoying lovely music, dimmed lighting, and an evening of quiet romance. We'd highly recommend this offering by the hosts! Dina and Carolyn made a terrific decision to use their extensive property to build 2 cottages for those who may want to have a longer stay in the mountains. On our visit, we were able to get a sneak peak of the building under construction. The cottages are opposite to the large ranch B&B. We could see the workers there but did not hear any noise at all. It was probably the neatest construction site I've ever seen. The builders parked their trucks/vans in a location that made it easy for us "house guests" to park in the usual spot. We heard no hammering, loud voices...nothing! I was incredibly impressed by the respectfulness of the crew for those of us staying in the Inn. Love, love, love this place!

author: Eleni1973
title: Beautiful Friendly Island Paradise - Bulla!!!
text: We stayed in June 2012 for a week and from the moment we got there, the staff welcomed us with open arms. They were so friendly and made us feel like we were one big family. The food was so beautiful and they always serenaded us with their beautiful voices. The staff always had a smile on their faces. We went with my sister and her family. A total of 8 of us. 4 adults, 2 10 year old boys and 2 12 year old boys. The boys loved it so much. They would sit at the bar and order their drinks and there was plenty for them to do. The staff made them feel special. We visited one of the villages which was so well organised. It was great to see their culture. We visited the school and they did a special song for us followed by a welcome ceremony in the hall. We will definitely visit Toberua again and we loved that it was so private and we felt like we were the only ones there. It was sad to leave. My sister and I even shed some tears when we said our goodbyes!!!!! See you again and hopefully soon. BULLA!!!!!

author: Shabalicious
title: Toberua Dreaming......
text: We have found our little slice of heaven! We booked this place after reading such good things on here and we are glad that we did. We decided on Fiji as we needed a week to relax and spend some quality time together and Toberua was perfect for just that! From the moment you arrive on the Island you feel relaxed and I did worry that I would not be able to switch off in just a week but I did after about 10 mins. I turned my phone off and did not know what was going on in the outside world! The place has a wonderful ‘home away from home’ feel and when we asked one of the housekeepers if it was ok for us to move our sun loungers down onto the sand, they responded with ‘you can do what you like, it’s your home’ That made me smile! The food was lovely, home cooked and we did not eat the same meal twice, the staff were all so friendly and remembered our names from day 1 and I LOVED the fact that we did not have to worry about keys, money or security for the week. We left everything open all of the time and the only thing that I had to worry about was the fact that my book fell apart. We also loved the inside/outside bathroom and the hammocks, perfect for some afternoon reading when you have had too much sun. We stayed in Bure 12A and we think that it was the best one, you can sunbathe right outside and it is very private. My boyfriend and I loved it so much that we have said that we would love to get married there, you can book the entire island out for $4,000 AUD a night. We met some lovely people who we are going to stay in touch with and I cannot recommend this place enough! Toberua Dreaming, I can’t wait to book it again! The only thing that I would suggest is getting the domestic flight from Nadi to Suva. We got a taxi as the flight had sold out but it took about 4 hours so made the journey quite long. We did get to see some more of Fiji though so that was a plus. If you are thinking of going to Fiji then this is the place……

author: JulieD409
title: Toberua put the 'family' in our family holiday
text: It has taken me a few weeks to write this as I wasn't certain I could right the review Toberua island deserves. Our first trip to Fiji but from the moment we stepped off the boat it was like being home with family. A small resort where both staff and other guests can get to know each other easily. Genuine and friendly staff, we now consider our friends. The changeover of management festivities also included the guests which was a privilege to be a part of. Never a dull moment the kids were entertained the whole time - snorkelling (from the beach or the daily boat trip to a reef), kayaking, swimming, golf, volleyball with the staff, pool, table tennis, eating, finding coconuts or hermit crabs, or just chilling with one of the staff at the bar. My 11 year old also did the intro diving course and went scuba diving off picnic island (the island trip an extra cost but a must), Armini was fantastic and very encouraging which made for a wonderful experience for my son. Food package was brilliant - loved the choices from a menu rather than a smorgasbord. Yes there were some sea snakes after bad weather but these were quickly removed by staff - and we're not an issue. I was not concerned as I took my queue from the staff who were not concerned - I just wore something on my feet at night. However these would never deter me from returning to this wonderful place. Some families had been there 9, 13 and almost 30 times such is the allure of Toberua. Thanks to all the staff especially Emori and Pita whose personalities were so much like our families it was like having two extra brothers. If you want a holiday without worrying about hotel keys, knowing your children are safe and secure, beautiful food, relaxing, beautiful location and meeting other people Toberua is your destination. We will be back!

author: SLH1111
title: No keys, no cash, no worries
text: Just had a thoroughly relaxing and enjoyable 7 night visit on Toberua. Don't let getting there deter you from this jewel - the tiny atr42 flight from Nadi to Suva & the subsequent boat trip to the island (with views that I can only compare to the Indian backwaters) are half the fun. From the minute you're greeted on the island by the wonderful staff, you'll realize why the guests return time after time (some there had visited the island 8 times). Facilities: Mostly impeccable. It's not 5star luxury, but it's what I would call island luxury. The pool was always perfectly maintained, and there is a real effort to use natural materials all throughout to maintain the island aesthetic - and it's pulled off brilliantly down to the details. We were in bure 12 which seemed to be amoung the best in terms of privacy as it borders the staff village wall on one side. Very comfortable and spacious. The oceanfront garden was brilliant, with two sun loungers and a hammock. The Staff: Can't say enough good things. They are the kind of warm & friendly that automatically makes Westerners skeptical, but you quickly dispell any doubts of their genuineness. For me that happened as soon as I heard Pita's laugh :) In general, the island works like a well-oiled machine, which is particularly evident in the planning and execution of the meals, which were flawless nearly every single time. (There is a meal plan that came out to about $1000 AUD pp/pw, but after eating out in Denarau, you'll appreciate what a bargain this is, esp considering the effort it must take in getting ingredients out there.) The benefits of being on this small island abound. Amoung them, not having to worry about keys (or security in general, doesn't get safer than this), not having to carry cash (only one bar, one restaurant and everything goes on your bure tab), no tv to distract you from actually relaxing, and the personal attention. It also facilitates a lot of interaction amoung guests (and staff alike), which I noticed that not all guests were particularly comfortable with, but the bure's provide reasonable privacy to spend alone time on your own beach if you aren't up to chatting. For a small island it also packs a pretty big punch - array of spa treatments (recommend the Island Journey), food options, wine menu etc. Left yesterday and missing it already. You can't go wrong with this one.

author: 543taliae
title: The most relaxing week of my life!
text: Due to unforeseen circumstances, I ended up traveling to Toberua on my own instead of with my brother. I was quite apprehensive about a week on my own, but it ended up being perfect. Toberua is the kind of place where you can do as much or as little as you like, and interact with others or keep completely to yourself. The staff were so kind and friendly. There are only 15 bures on the island so it is nice and intimate. The bathrooms and rooms were lovely, though you will most certainly encounter some geckos in each. A fellow guest who had been in the travel industry for many years said it was the best food he'd ever seen at a Fiji resort, and they are also flexible with dietary requirements. The reservations team was very accommodating when I had to leave a night early. There were only a couple of downsides: the wifi was down due to a cyclone (no fault of theirs), but they charged for use of their office computer. The beach directly surrounding the island was not mind-blowing in terms of clear water/white sand, but it was still really really lovely and they do a day trip out to postcard-worthy waters. Occasionally the heat in the bures made it hard to fall asleep. The few encounters with sea snakes were a little unnerving, but the staff were really swift in throwing them back in to the ocean, and I just kept the doors to my bure closed to make sure no snakes snuck in... Apart from that, everything was beyond perfect. The diving was incredible, the staff were magnificent, the isolation was beautiful, and I left happy and relaxed. Thank you for a WONDERFUL week. Will be back and will stay longer!

author: Clare_On_Holidays
title: Most relaxed I've felt in years
text: I've just returned from a 6 night stay at Toberua over Christmas and had an absolutely wonderful time. I went alone, which can sometimes a be a bit daunting, but the manager Shelley and all of the staff were extremely welcoming and made me feel right at home straight away. Many of the other guests were also fantastic and the resort layout, activities and set meal times encourages people to make new friends. Toberua is a small resort on a reasonably isolated small island which makes it perfect for getting away from the hustle and bustle of life.
