To get there you have to get a taxi and then a boat from Suva airport, but the resort will organise that for if you purchase a transfer and it only takes about 45 minutes. If you are looking for a resort where you can just spend the days reading books, swimming, snorkelling (there's a free trip each day), getting massages and drinking cocktails then this is the place. If you want to use it as a base for sight seeing then it's probably not the best choice, but they do run day trips for diving, fishing and to visit the local villages. The trip to the local village was probably one of the highlights for me. The poverty, compared to the western world, is pretty confronting but the villagers could not have been more welcoming. They put on an afternoon tea for us, showed us around, conducted a Kava ceremony and we all had a good old dance. There's the opportunity to buy handicrafts from the women and to donate to a community fund for improving the village facilities. I encourage anyone who goes to give generously. The accommodation itself was clean, modern and spacious. There's no air con (only fans) but I didn't miss it. Even though it was the height of summer, the sea breezes kept the place cool. The food could also not be faulted. It was fresh and varied and super yummy. I really hope to head back there again sometime soon.

author: SteveW226
title: My home away from home
text: We arrived at Toberua Island Resort at night following a drive up from Vudu Marina (sth of Nadi). Its a drive I would recommend if you have not seen the island, with its plethera of villages and rugged beauty. It will certainly add to your appreciation of Fiji. Upon arrival we were greated at the jetty with a song, friendly smile and a cold drink; and a 'welcome home' from the staff. We were definately off to a good start. We were quicky booked in, taken to our rooms to freshen up and off to dinner, where we met 'Maggie' the stand in manager. Maggie was a delight and immediately made us feel like we were the only ones there. Having read the other reviews I must agree that the rooms are very comfortable, the food is good and the staff are fantastic, they really make you feel like you are part of the family. I would recommend getting to know them, they are always happy to have chat and many have very interesting backgrounds or family history. The must dos for the island are: 1. snorkelling (which is free) or diving (dive team are great with kids); 2. visit the local village and join in the dancing; 3. play volleyball with the staff (they will make you feel like part of the team). One suggestion though don't play volleyball after drinking 'kava', it can be very embarrassing but the staff do get a laugh. To summarise Toberua Island is a place you go to relax and have a good time. The resort is ideal for couples and families who want to spend quality time together but if you are after party games, disco and drinking to the wee hours of the morning then Toburua Island it is not for you. Finally I would like to say a big hello to my friends Masi, Peta and Ratu. It was an absolute pleasure getting to know you 'Gentlemen' and I look forward seeing you again......Vinaka.

author: Rizwandean
title: Our Toberua Experience
text: My wife and I arrived at Toberua on November 3rd and left on November 7th. To really describe Toberua and the experience in words is somewhat difficult because one has to be there to experience the sheer peace and tranquility surrounding the place. When we got to the island, we were warmly greeted by the team and they all introduced themselves to us in order to get to know us. Shelly was also there to greet us and we got some really lovely welcome drinks to kick start the vacation. We were then taken to our room which has the best view of the ocean we've ever seen during our time in many different resorts and hotels. I truly loved the way the staff all took their time to meet up with us and Google definitely isn't lying when it says that you've simply got to try the cocktails made by Ratu - they're truly unique and refreshing. The best part about Toberua is that each of the staff go the extra mile to ensure you're comfortable and they're always willing to assist you no matter what time you need help - we found that out quickly when my wife felt a little ill and the kitchen staff lovingly prepared some hot vegetable soup for her and continuously asked us how we were doing and if there was anything they could do to help us. We really appreciated this. Another lovely aspect about Toberua is the food - it is truly to die for and each meal is so unique that you never get tired so you should really be prepared to put on a few extra pounds while you're there!!! Meals are served on a sandy terrace overlooking the beach and the ocean so the ambiance is really good and helps you relax while you eat and the staff usually sing songs and play a guitar. The pool is beautiful and if you're a fan of the ocean, then you really don't need to look any further because the ocean is right outside your villa (each villa is situated in front of the ocean) and they have outdoor showers as well. Toberua really wants its guests to relax so don't expect to find clocks, radios, TV's or Internet access in your villa and if you're looking for all that, don't go to Toberua because the idea is to get away from all the stresses of you daily life and just let the world pass you by, which is exactly what my wife and I did. I suppose the hardest part is leaving Toberua because you know you're leaving a truly magical place and the team make you feel like a part of their family so parting can be a little difficult. I would recommend Toberua to anyone looking for the true meaning of a "Pacific lifestyle" because Toberua is by far the best resort we've been to and we're looking forward to returning there as soon as we can. You have to try it to believe it.

author: RaphS686
title: Fantastic Week
text: Exactly what we wanted! Small, quiet, clean and beautiful island! Took a bit to get to from Nadi, but it was so worth it! Once we stepped on the island, everything was perfect! Had sun every single day! The staff took the trouble to know us personally and they were really the star attraction. The entire atmosphere was like being at "home" with friends around! Friendly, courteous and always with a smile! Other than breakfast, which you can't vary much, the meals were fabulous! Continental/a little fusion cuisine. Went home as cargo not passengers! The bure was big and nicely set out. Outdoor shower/toilet took a bit to get used to. They cleaned the bure twice a day! Waterview and hammock outside sets the scene. My only disappointment (not sure if this is valid as I have not been to other Fijian Islands) are the corals aren't as many and colourful as I hoped. Our first Fiji Trip and it will not be the last. We look forward to going back!

author: DBSSuva
title: This is what a resort should be.
text: Toberua was absolutely wonderful. If you are looking for a quiet, charming, great service, upscale resort, this is the place. This is our 4th resort since we arrived in Fiji 2 months ago. It exceeded our expectations. At first, I was worried about the size of the island but we found ourselves entertained with the available activities or just relaxing on the hammock. The rooms are very clean and all have breathtaking views. The staff makes it a point to know you and your family by name and are very attentive to any of the guests need. The service is what was most impressive. Since I been in Fiji, that's the one thing that I find resorts lack - good service. Toberua does not. The staffs warm, friendly smiles made requests easy. We also liked the fact that our kids can run around the island free and not worry about them getting lost or taken or anything like that. My son, who is a very picky eater, LOVED the food and we did too. I couldn't believe he was actually eating with joy. He usually sits around complains then cries about having to eat. The Toberua chefs made it so easy by cooking delicious meals. A huge VINAKA to all the staff members for their service. Congratulations Shelley on a well ran resort. We will definitely be back and will be recommending Toberua to others. Diana S.

author: Pesto242
title: Quiete and Intimate Resort
text: To summarize the resort is one of the best I have ever been and any improvements are limited to island location. We were there for our honeymoon and both my wife and I left with lasting memories and a few new friendships. Pros: The resort has the most amazing staff I have ever had the pleasure to meet. Even though this resort only had a handful of guests, the staff knew everyone names and made you feel like family. The island is very nice and the burés are up to date and beautiful. Food was amazing (I do not use this word often in my vocabulary) the chef is Fijian and trained in multiple other resorts outside of Fiji. Even though the island is small we were able to easily separate ourselves and find intimate things to do. In addition we were able to spend time with other guests in the bar/lounge area and interact in a family oriented setting. It really does not feel at all like a hotel that you are just a visitor passing through. Cons: (You can always improve and everyone has different ideas) The island is on the Suva side which gets more rainy weather than the Nani side. This can cause the weather to be a little cooler, more cloudy and more tropical rains. Since we spent 2 weeks prior on the Nani side we did notice a 2-2 1/2 degree Celsius difference but no issues with rain. When I thought of Fiji I expected the most amazing beaches and water. The island does have a good beach, but not what I was expecting coming from the Mamanuca islands. I can not say thank you enough to all of the staff on the island for truly making our trip one of the best They alone allowed for multiple of these stars.

author: ElleNZ2502
title: A little piece of paradise
text: We made a last minute decision to go away and booked for ten days on Toberua Island Resort. We hadn't researched the resort except a quick look at trip advisor which was positive, and so it was really pot luck. Well, we struck gold. From the moment we arrived until we left, the staff were absolutely amazing. Ten days flew by and we seemed to be occupied most of the time. We did the open water diving course (PADI) and can very highly recommend this. Our 11 year old daughter did it too and she was very well looked after and we felt safe at all times thanks to our instructor Isareli. The water was beautiful and warm and some lovely coral and aquatic life. The food was nice, but a bit limited in choice at times, with only a few varieties of fruit available throughout our stay. Breakfasts are limited with an option of one hot dish per day and 2 cereals, toast and muffins. We had the meal plan which i think is good value for money. The rooms are very spacious and well appointed, bathrooms are recently renovated and very nice. It is a fantastic place to take kids as they all mix and form their own "kids club" and the staff are always ready to help out. The island is only 4 acres so the kids just run around to there hearts content. Zac, the barman can make a mean cocktail, so 6 0'clock drinks become a ritual! We enjoyed our stay so much that before we left, we booked to return next year.

author: ALLISONA502
title: Paradise found!
text: My husband and I just returned from what was supposed to be a 9 night stay on Toberua Island. Sometime around the 4th day we started fretting that we should have booked for a longer stay because we were enjoying ourselves and the company of the lovely guests and darling staff so much. At our farewell dinner we jumped-up at the last possible moment as the Toberua Serenaders were about to sing our farewell song and said STOP! We didn't care that we just lost all our flight refunds - we just couldn't bare to leave. We still agree that it was the best decision we made for a long time. The extra time gave us more oportunities to carry-on relaxing, laughing, eating, snorkling on the magnificent reefs, dancing and enjoying the company of wonderful new friends while the staff spoilt us with their kindness and happy ways. If you are looking for high-end chic sophistication - don't go to Toberua. If you are looking for a holiday that totally relaxes you and makes you long for your next stay - this is the place. You won't find 3000 thread count Egyptian cotton sheets but you will find pristine clean rooms, comfortable beds, wholesome fresh and tasty food and a beautifully stocked bar that reveals incredible stories of visits from international stars that have enjoyed the beauty of the island and surrounding views. An example - we didn't know that Billy Connolly had married there or that Sir Edmund Hillary regularly brought his family for holidays! One of the two couples that we met were on their thirtieth+ trip which they had done over a period of 30 years - even had their sons wedding there! Another couple were only on their 5th trip - their first was their 25th wedding aniversary some 20 years ago. My husband and I have travelled to some exotic places over the years and stayed in some extremely high-end hotels as well as home stays with locals. There have been some good experiences and some bad. This one, I am delighted to report was 'all good'. We have never felt so relaxed and so sad to leave. We even thought of keeping it a secret - selfish huh! Aching to go back to our new second home, Toberua, we will see you in our dreams.

author: smc810
title: Toberua - My island home - Fantastic family destination
text: We completely loved our stay on Toberua Island. If you have active, busy children don't be afraid to book your holiday here. We only booked for a week because we thought that maybe our boys, 8 and 10, might get bored - the island is only 4 acres and there's no tv or computers. We were delighted to be wrong. They had the best, best time. There is so much to do on this island, or if you prefer to chill then you're every whim is catered for. Without a doubt the highest recommendation goes to the staff who are all just so, so delightful. The staff make this island and deserve the highest recognition for their endless endeavours to spoil and luxuriate. What did we like the most? It would be easier to list the things we didn't enjoy. So, here they are ..... zero - zilch - nothing. Truly, truly everything was a divine as it looks on the toberua.com website and the information we gleaned from travellers reviews. Interestingly the island resort operates an 'education scholarship' for local village children to attend high school. Guests are able to contribute to this fund, which helps local village families send their children to high school and would otherwise be difficult given the subsistence living that many fijian workers and villages eek out. We can't wait to return - it feels like our island home. In the words of our 10 year old son - "Even I had tears in my eyes when we left because I loved it so much" Vinaka vaka levu Toberua.

author: MaryS649
title: Wedding bliss
text: My husband and I eloped to Toberua - just the two of us, no family or guests at all. We purchased their basic wedding package and I was really impressed with what we received for it. We arrived on the Friday and sat down that afternoon with Mere to go over the details of what we wanted (rainy day options, what music we wanted the band to play - also the choice of island band or choir), what flowers I wanted, etc. and she was most accommodating - I asked for extra frangipanis for my hair and received a beautiful hairpiece - no extra charge. On the day, the celebrant/minister came a couple of hours early to confirm the kind of ceremony we wanted - he does both secular and religious - and then one of the staff came to help me get dressed. The staff had dressed the beach where the ceremony was held beautifully - the trunks of the palm trees were plaited with leaves and there were a dozen or more (no kidding) flower arrangements of tropical flowers lining the aisle - I was blown away. The ceremony was short and sweet and a huge number of staff and most of the other guests turned up to watch the show! It was a truly romantic day and a completely stress-free wedding. If I had the money and the time (we did this all on three weeks' notice) I would have loved to have booked the whole island out for family and friends. It's a beautiful spot and well worth a visit. We snorkeled the morning of our wedding and I also found time to fit in a massage before the event - I may have been the most relaxed bride ever! My only regret is not engaging a professional photographer. We took a great quality, easy to use SLR camera with us and one of the staff happily took pictures for us but they were nearly all out of focus. The other key feature of Toberua that I have to mention is the quality of the food - it was delicious. I'm a big seafood lover so chose that option nearly every meal and it was all excellent - lots of spicy Asian influence, ranging from Thai to Indian. My hubby is the steak eating manly-man type and he was impressed with his food choices too. The staff on Toberua are numerous and very friendly and I'd definitely recommend it for a relaxing, chilled out holiday.

author: TeeGee81
title: So relaxing - Toberua staff are wonderful!
text: We stayed at Toberua for 5 nights in September and we absolutely loved it. There was enough to do that we werent bored, but there wasnt too much do so we still had plenty of time to relax. This was our first visit to Fiji and I researched extensively in the hope that we would choose the right place to stay and we were definately not disappointed! The staff at the island are what makes the place so special, by the time we left it was like we were part of the family. We went fishing with Mini which was fun. A couple of times we did the daily snorkelling trip which was nice. And we also did the village trip. The food (meal plan) was fabulous and well worth it, we enjoyed a cooked breakfast daily and 3 course lunch / 4 course dinner. We didnt have morning or afternoon tea once during our stay as we were still full from breakfast / lunch and didnt need it. The double hammock was amazing for an afternoon siesta and for reading books! We stayed in one of the big resorts in Denarau (Nadi) for 2 nights before heading to Toberua for 5 nights and then went back to Denarau for 2 nights, however we wished we had of spent the last 2 nights on the island rather than going back to Denarau, we truley were sad to leave. We stayed in Bure 1 which was on the not-so-windy side of the island (which we were very pleased about) and it suited the two of us perfectly. Thanks again and we hope to come back and visit one day. Getting to Toberua: You can Fly to Suva however we took a bus from Nadi Town to Suva (they drop you at the Holiday Inn Suva). We booked the bus through Tourism Transport Fiji (TTF) at Nadi airport when we first arrived. The cost was $22 Fijian Dollars per person, and it was comfortable enough. It took 4 hours on the bus to the Holiday Inn Suva) - where we were met by the Toberua organised transfer to take us to the landing and then on the boat to the island.

author: MargarettaG
title: Just perfect
text: My husband and I stayed at Toberua Is. Resort end of July into August. In the time we were there the manager went on leave and a replacement manager took over. I have to congratulate Maggie as there was no change in management style and the staff all seemed very happy about the arrangement. Of course the staff are wonderful never forgetting our names or our favourite cocktails. The band boys are to die for at night dulring cocktail hour and dinner. They played all the songs we knew so we were very relaxed. The food was delicious, with lots of fresh vegetables and melt in the mouth steaks. We had a wonderful time, loved chatting with the other guests from many different countries. The rooms were large, airy and cool. Well serviced twice daily. Outside dinner was so romantic under the stars on the edge of the water. Value for money although we were too relaxed to do too many trips. Maggie was a delight gently circulating during cocktail hour and dinner making sure everyone was ok but also being unobtrusive. Well done Toberura Island Resort. The owners must be very happy with their two managers - good choices. We will return in the not too distant future.

author: rambler07
title: Just what we needed!
text: Sorry for the late review, we actually stayed in Toberua Island Resort last year for my birthday. It was just fantastic and exactly what we were looking for. Saying that we were extremely lucky with the mix of customers there, who were really nice and funny people. Adults only, so we had a great time! While the island is extremely small, we were never bored and did something different every day like scuba diving, snorkeling, kayaking, hobie-catting (that was awesome!) and of course my husband participating in the daily staff volleyball competition. He even had a few golf shot on the beach when the tide was low! The owners also said that they will add a 'gym' bure for the cardio-exercise freaks that may visit the place, so there is plenty to do there! The accommodation was very impressive and we believe we had the best bure of the island. Traditional Fijian decoration with a whole glass wall opening onto the sea (literally 3 meters from the beach or sea depending on the tide, but perfect for those midnight dips!). Amazing view from every bure I would say. Half open-air bathroom accessible from the back of your bure, which was extremely handy when coming back from the beach, as you are able to wash the sand of your feet before spreading it all over the floor of your room. Huge hammock was just perfect for relaxation such as arvo siesta or read a good book. This island was bugs free at that period, so that was a +, considering that mosquitoes just love my blood! The food was lovely and we have no complaints there. On the contrary, we felt like we had too much to eat (definitely take fullboard, it is worth it!), but because the food was healthy I didn't even put on weight! They call you for each meal with the sound of drums, which was a nice touch. The staff was just amazing and so friendly, they really made it hard for us to leave and of course a few tears were shed when we left, with them singing to us on the pier! Would definitely recommend it to anyone who are after a relaxing time with water based activities. We certainly would like to return anyway.

author: Olympia58
title: The most idealic holiday spot ever
text: Toberua is a beautiful island off the Fiji coast near Suva. My husband and I and 30 of our closest friends and family booked out the island for a week of birthday festivities. The entire island (which is only about 800m x 500m) is occupied by one resort with 15 bures. Each bure can sleep up to four people. They all face out to sea so all have perfect views. All bures are spacious, clean, cool and have modern well appointed bathrooms. They each have a balcony with lounge chairs, a swing chair and hammock. And all are quite private. There is a central swimming pool that guests can share and a shop with essentials. A single restaurant accomodates all visitors for all meals. Tables may be set up in groups, individually, inside or outsided, depending on guest requirements and the weather. Food is fabulous, varied and plentiful. Also a great wine list. There is also a bar and games area with pool table, table tennis and suitable for board games, cards or just chatting. Staff are friendly, capable, professional, warm and welcoming. Management is involved but not intrusive - offer suggestions but under no obligations. Activities are there for those who wish to partake - experienced and careful dive masters, snorkelling, hobbycat sailing, kayaking, fishing, reef golf, putt putt golf, village tours, picnics on other islands, or just laze by the pool. Spa treatments also available - a big hit with all our friends on the trip. In short, one of the best holidays ever and I couldnt recommend Toberua highly enough

author: jmurphnc
title: Babymoon/Engagement
text: I surprised my wife for her birthday with a mountain getaway. We stayed for 4 nights in March. Neither of us had been to a B&B before, so we didn't really know what to expect. As soon as we arrived we were very impressed with the grounds and the interior of the inn! Carolyn met us at the door with a friendly smile and made us feel right at home! Dina was in the kitchen and was about to come out and meet us with a smile as well! I bought the Babymoon package and my wife enjoyed it so much! On our third day there we went to see waterfalls. We drove to Dry Falls in Highlands, NC. This was such a unique waterfall because you are able to walk behind it. It was there underneath/behind Dry Falls that I asked my wife to marry me! To make a long story short, we had such a wonderful experience and will definitely be back! Carolyn and Dina you spoiled us and it was worth every dime we spent! Thank you for making our first B&B experience one we will never forget! Your hospitality, kindness, friendly atmosphere and let's not forget the delicious breakfast, made our trip one we will never forget! Can't wait to come back!!! James and Raven Murphy

author: GreySkinnedBoy
title: more than fantastic place with lovely friendly people!
text: Stayed on Toberua Island for 8 days and did not want to leave! Well organized holiday experience from the pick up at the airport to drop off at the airport ....nothing to fault! Staff are friendly, helpful and genuinely happy. They don't expect a tip and are still full of smiles and laughter! Our bure (bungalow) was fantastic, traditional with a very modern twist, well appointed, very clean and comfortable with the convenience of your own semi-open air bathroom, large deck overlooking the sea just steps away from water, with your own hammock, sunlougers and deckchairs. The pool is small but refreshing... Overall a very small island with only 15 bure's (so no overcrowding) gives a nice family feeling, and the staff the opportunity to get to know you by name. The food was plenty with a good breakfast, 10 o'clock tea, 3 course lunch, 4 pm tea and 4 course dinner under the stars.... All food was delicious and freshly cooked by a very accomplished chef! The food was of high standard, lovely flavour and high quality. Because there is nothing to do on the island but relax , sun, sleep and eat...the staff put on daily activities which if you whish you can take part in free off charge...snorkel trips are arranged daily free of charge...you 0nly have to pay for diving courses or your tank if you are a padi diver and day trips away from the island...but all is affordable! We enjoyed the island very much and would recommend this resort to anybody.... We brought a laptop and videos etc...because there is no TV but we did not feel inclined to take it out once! You will leave the island tanned, relaxed, a few pounds heavier but with a smile on your face and in your heart! If the world was not so big and if there were not soo many places to see I would definitely come back..... Shelley the manager (who has only been there for 2 months!) is doing an amazing job to keep it all organized and to your liking...she is always around to make the stay even more comfortable and to keep you safe ( she makes sure life jackets are on board etc. when the staff take you out etc...not that they were needed! The staff know the area really well and look after you as if you were one of their own!) Vinaka Vaka Levu ...Toberua staff.!

author: GeorgiaTripp
title: Home sweet home!
text: Sorry for the delay in writing our review. Lots of things going on. Never the less the best was visiting our favorite getaway. As usual everything was perfect. Dina did a great job alone while Carolyn was recuperating. But we did get a glimpse of her. And are sure Dina is glad to have her back and running!! We love our room Pinehurst. Beautiful views and so quiet and cozy. As usual the breakfasts were fabulous. Prepared AND served by Dina. Also so enjoyed our cocktail hour on the terrace with Dina. We are counting the days til Sept. for our return. Love to the two best innkeepers we consider great friends!!

author: southweststeak
title: Nice introduction to Fiji but expected more
text: June is actually Fiji's winter and our first 2 days was clouded by rain and cool weather. The accommodations and staff are truly excellent but we found the food lacking-the same commercial vanilla ice cream offered for dessert and no exciting seafood was served (no crab, scallops, lobster, etc. Mushy shrimp was served one night out of 5 and overcooked mahi mahi frequented the menu although the beef, lamb and chicken were of good quality). Great place for families-our visit was shared with 10 children from families in Australia-we happen to love children so not a problem for us-lots of games, pool table, books, some activities and a pool to keep kids occupied.....Resort is all inclusive in terms of meals except for juices and drinks at the bar. Boxed or canned juice is offered complimentary only at breakfast. Cheese plate was a disaster-same fruit from breakfast and 2 cheeses: white cheddar and cream cheese and 3 Ritz crackers. I am only mentioning the food because on the return trip home, a Burger King Whopper and Odwalla's Superfood juice tasted like the best food we ate all week. And don't buy anything from Suva's airport cafe past security-worst food EVER. Back to resort: View from Bure's are spectacular-teeny tiny island-literally stroll around in less than 20 mins, no waterfall and no hiking opportunities. Picnic island ($) is a must-lots of coral, small shells and colorful fish. Village visit ($) was sullied by chief's constant plug for donations-highlight was the watered down Kava drink. Recommend coconut demonstration. Passed on scuba ($$)-maybe try next time? Daily snorkel trips are recommended-visits to Shark rock, secret garden, sacred garden, and sand banks were fun. Saw lots of harmless reef shark, a puffer fish, ubiquitous blue starfish, loads of colorful reef fish and thick black and white sea snakes (think broom handle thick). The kids at the resort had a blast collecting discarded sea snake skin (shedding) at night. Recommend the inclusive non-motorized water sports-kayaks, Hobie cat, etc great way to exercise if swimming is not your forte. Finished 2 books in 5 days but that's was ok as goal was to lie in a hammock everyday. Next visit will shell out even more money for supersoft sand beach and better food. Oh yes and the massage was nice but was not Shiatsu or Swedish-more like lots of oil and some rubbing.

author: TheVonJohnstons
title: Good quality family holiday... " and no Kids Club!!!"
text: My family of five (8,11 & 13 year olds) stayed on Toberua Island for 10 nights over Christmas & New Year. This was our childrens first trip overseas, so this was 'big' for them! We found the Fijians to be genuinely beautiful & kind people, and we were looked after by some fabulous men and women who worked on the island and come from two neighboring island villages - so its a good relationship Toberua Resort has, employing them. We visited one of these villages and found that to be a major highlight of our stay in Fiji. We were presented with flower neckpieces and enjoyed the kava ceremony, whilst dancing with them. Their children of course were running around and really were just the most gorgeous kids. Three lovely young girls came up to my daughters wanting photos taken, smiling and laughing all the while. The Resort itself is more like a bed & breakfast with only 15 bures, its not busy, but runs at an organsied steady pace. They offer snorkelling trips out everyday, scuba diving, fishing (which our 8 year old son did everyday off the jetty), trolling, kayaks which we easily paddled right around the island. We did the Day trip to Levuka, a BBQ lunch on Picnic Island was also great fun (wear thongs as there is lots of old bits of sharp coral, I found out). A lovely pool, the tropical grounds & gardens are raked are groomed daily and are of a botanical garden standard. Beware the black & white sea snakes, they're all over the place, mostly at dusk and into the evening but we were told they're harmless - my son counted 64 of them in total, and he loved running around with his torch spotting them! They have a pool table, bar, pingpong, tidal golf, the staff play guitars and sing during lunch and dinner whilst enjoying some kava which you're more than welcome to sample. Theres a lovely avairy with 3 quirky parrots which we enjoyed feeding our 'leftovers' from brekky! All in all a great holiday, and we would dearly love to go back someday. It is expensive especially if you drink cocktails everynight, but overall we found it was worth it and have NO regrets. All the people who work there are happy, polite and fun, always willing to help you in any way. Thanks for some great memories guys. The Johnstons

author: Dacs8
title: My best holiday ever !
text: I recently went to Toberua Island with my family, and I'll admit I was a bit worried before we went that it might not be that great for me as a 17 year old on a small island. However I couldn't have been more wrong. We have been fortunate enough to have had quite a few overseas holidays, and in particular several others in Fiji. Toberua Island was by far the best ! From the moment we arrived on the island we were greeted by the wonderful Fijian Staff and the new Kiwi managers, who throughout our entire 8 days worked tirelessly to ensure we had the best holiday ever. They always greeted us by name and went out of their way to ask how our day was etc. Marty the manager and his staff even farewelled us at 5.30am on the day we had to reluctantly go home ( Mum had to be nearly dragged off the island - she wanted to stay forever !) The best parts for me were not only the people and the food but the awesome diving, fishing and day trips. I completed my Padi diving course which was the most amazing diving ever . Joe the instructor was fantastic and i can't wait to get back there and dive with him again. Other highlights were - -learning to windsurf - perfect conditions to learn in the warm water temperatures. - The trip to the local village was an absolute must for anyone staying on Toberua. I am studying yr 12 Geography and one of the topics is Disparities so this was amazing to actually see and experience everything we had been learning about. -The picnic island trip - This was a long way from the island a good 30-40 min boat ride each way , so was very good value, and for anyone who is not that much of a water baby, you could snorkle and see some of the most amazing fish, coral etc in just over waist depth water ! - meeting one of our Kiwi heroes on his way home to NZ to show off his 1500m Bronze Medal from the recent Olympics ! Nic Wallis and his lovely wife Sierra arrived a day or so after us and we enjoyed many a game of Toberua Golf, pool and table tennis - and Yes he is good at all those sports too !! We had such a good time that we are remaining in contact via emails. I could keep writing forever about this wonderful place, but better get back to my studies. Mum and Dad are already planning our next holiday there, hopefully next year. Provided my brothers and I keep behaving - so yes back to studying !!

author: Bubbles088
title: AN AWESOME EXPERIENCE
text: If you are looking for a special Fiji Island experience, then we can recommend you make Toberua Island Resort your next destination. We have just spent 10 wonderful days there. This is a very pretty island and the real treasures here, are the exceptional Island staff with their beautiful smile, friendliness & willingness to please. They knew us by our first names within hours of arriving. The Island musicians serenaded us at our bure before dinner, then played throughout the evening while we dined, we then joined in with singing & dancing. The new owners were on the Island, while we were there, busy up-grading & fine tuning their new enterprise. The managers, Marty & Lisa are an outstanding, caring & consiencious couple, dedicated to their job. They & their staff go out of their way to make sure your holiday is just perfect. A highlight not to be missed is Wednesdays daytrip to Picinic Island. The swimming & snorkelling amongst beautiful colourful coral & fish is incredible, as is the BBQ lunch. Mondays afternoon trip to the neighbouring Island Village is another worthwhile experience. Our days were fun-filled with swimming in the lovely pool, playing putting golf, reef golf, reef walks, glassbottom boat, fishing, canoeing, diving, snorkelling, evening volleyball with the staff, dancing,singing, laughter & eating the delicious food. We even managed to fit in the occasional afternoon nap. This is a great place for families or just a peaceful Island Retreat. Our memories of this wonderful place will linger long & the laughter of these lovely Toberua Island people will continue to echo in our ears.

author: Cheezel
title: Long Term Returnee Guests disappointed
text: For several years our family have chosen Toberua as our favourite destination for a relaxing break. We have visited the Island as returnee guests many times, always finding the service, food and accomodation of high and consistent quality. Toberua's biggest asset is its staff, many of whom have come to be considered friends and all of whom seem genuinely proud of their Island. Our last visit to Toberua was in June 2007. Since this time there has been a change of Manager and I believe it will be followed shortly by a change in Ownership. We have in the past had no hesitation in recommending Toberua as a destination for anyone wanting to relax and unwind. However, I would strongly advise guests booking directly through Toberua's flamboyant Reservations Clerk to insure their details of arrival are noted and fully understood (we have personally been left at Suva Airport on three occasions), all requirements and arrangements are in writting, details are written in the reservations diary, and even if not requested, a deposit is paid at the time of reserving your holiday. As Toberua is slightly limited in actual beach frontage we have always made sure to prebook our preferred bure well ahead of time. Despite having spoken to the Reservations Clerk in person 11 months ago, despite having corresponded via email regularily regarding our annual booking, despite having email confirmation of our specified bure being available pending our definate dates of arrival, our 2008 booking has been disregarded. Obviously it was not entered in the reservations diary at anytime and our bure has subsequently been allocated to another guest. Our family is now in the process of organising an alternative Island on the Nadi side of Fiji. I look forward to following up with a review and comparison. Would we still recommend Toberua? Yes it is a wonderful destination which generally provides great service, food and atmosphere. Unfortunately this incident and the total lack of effort to rectify a botched booking, the lack of concern, and total lack of any acceptance of responsibility has left a sour taste in the mouths of these returnee guests. We can only hope the new Owner takes measures to insure he retains valuable business rather than allowing this great little resort to be jeopardized by Incompetence and lack of concern.

author: Travelwriter63
title: Shhh! Don't tell anyone how good it is!
text: It is hard to say anything which has not already been said in previous reviews. Hudson, the reservation manager is very efficient in organising your stay before arriving on the island. Hudson also especially loves kids on the island, so if you have kids they will really be looked after by Hudson. From the second you arrive you feel you are a million miles away from home with the staff welcoming you with beautiful singing and some local hospitality. This was our second stay and it was as every bit enjoyable as the first. The best thing about the island is the staff. They are so warm, friendly and good natured. Anything you want to do, they will accommodate at a moment's notice - maybe some fishing, crabbing, a boat ride around the island and other traditional customs like weaving and coconut demonstrations. They get to know you by name very quickly which is really nice. Lala is known as King of the Kids and whilst we were on the island there were many kids who were entertained by Lala with some great activities including the hilarious watermelon cracking game. It was great fun to see the staff have a crack - Bale was very funny and Luse was spot on everytime at getting to the watermelon and cracking it! After the staff, the next best thing is the food. Great breakfasts with a different 'special' every day, a three course lunch and a four course different. We were there 7 nights and not one dish was ever duplicated during the time we were there. The staff will find you wherever you may be to take your selections from the lunch and dinner menus - mid-morning for the lunch menu and mid-afternoon for dinner. And if by some remote chance you would prefer something not on the menu, the staff will accommodate your request. So here is a typical day: Wake up and head off to breakfast, then lie by the pool, head off for some morning tea, then lie by the pool and read a book, head off to lunch, have a nice afternoon siesta, head off for pre-dinner drinks before dinner and finally a few drinks at the bar to finish off a great day in paradise before heading off to bed. If you want to be a little more active there are plenty of activities to participate in if you want. You even have the opportunity of playing volleyball with the staff each afternoon - but be warned - they are very good players, especially Long Joe! We can't wait to return - we love Toberua.

author: pinacoladafan
title: Our new Favorite Place in Fiji
text: As promised here is my review on Toberua Island. In one word MAGNIFICENT!. I have to agree with everyone who writes a review about this place that it is so special that you really need to visit for yourself. We were met at the wharf (after travelling by their launch for around 25 mins) by the manager Brendon and some of the staff who were singing and playing guitars. First thought is Wow, isn't this nice and everyone calls you by your name so they know you as you set foot on the island. We were taken to the dining area for lunch while the luggage was taken to our Bure. While walking to lunch we were also shown around the island and then we had our first taste of the excellent meals we were going to experience for the next 7 days. Lunch is 3 course and dinner 4 courses (if you can fit it all in) had to cut back most days but nothing is too much trouble for them so if you don't fancy what is on the menu they will prepare something you may like (which they did for our son who is not too adventurous). We settled in and felt at home straight away and certainly went onto Fiji Time.Very relaxing. Our 13 year old daughter asked "Did we ever have to leave"? and the 11 year old son asked "when are we coming back"? All this in the first hour!!!! The next 7 days were pure bliss. Sleeping,reading,eating,drinking. Pure relaxation. The first few days we just relaxed then there was New Years Eve which was really good and a lot of fun. Hudson had done a wonderful job of organising everything. A brilliant night of socialising and mixing with the staff.Then unfortuately New Years Day it started to rain in the afternoon and then continued for the rest of our trip,(on and off) so we didn't get to do the activities we wanted but that didn't worry us as we had already decided to book again for Christmas and New Year this year so hopefully we will be able to do the things we couldn't because of the rain and windy overcast conditions. (But who can predict the weather). And before we new it,it was time to leave which was very sad but we left knowing we had found a little piece of paradise which has now become our new favourite place in Fiji.

author: clicker
title: Bliss!
text: Choosing a holiday destination off the internet can be an anxiety inducing experience; will it live up the photos? will the food be ok? have we booked the right accommodation? So it's often a slightly nervous time as we approach our never-been-before holiday resort. No need for nerves when heading to Toberua Island. Even though it was dark when my husband and three-year-old arrived by boat I knew we had made the right choice. From the warm welcome on the wharf to the cake and Fijian hymns generously given to farewell our family, our Toberua experience was unforgettable. This small but perfectly formed island has 15 traditional, spacious bures all lapped by the turquoise Pacific. However, most of the time it feels like your own private island. It is hard not to feel completely relaxed here, whether it's gazing out to sea from your palm-shaded hammock or snorkelling in the clear blue Fijian waters. Real lives are quickly forgotten and the most pressing thing usually involves wondering what delicious treats will be served at the next meal. The meal plan is fantastic. The food, classic 80's fare but using all the best Fijian ingredients, (coconut, fresh fish, spices, pineapples etc) is a continuous delight. We never ate the same thing twice and always looked forward to the sound of the drums heralding the start of what was usually a three-course affair. Cilla, our daughter, was very well catered for. The staff were a joy and played a huge part in making our holiday an incredibly memorable and warm experience. Toberua Island has the highest return rate of any accommodation in Fiji and it's not hard to see why. It was with much sadness we left the island but with definite plans to return we know without a doubt those lei's did end up on the beach!

author: BC001
title: Dream holiday
text: We recently visited Toberua for what can only be described as ten days of bliss!! Toberua is a small island with only 15 bures, which means that guests are limited. Despite the size, there is plenty to do on the island including swimming, snorkelling, trips to nearby islands etc. Alternatively you can choose to do nothing except sit on the beach or in a hammock and feast on the delicious meals. Lunches are 3 courses and dinners are 4, supplemented with morning and afternoon tea as well as a buffet breakfast. Unfortunately after day 2 my medium-sized stomach had to cut back to a maximum of two courses - bummer!! The menu will always have one seafood dish, and without exception the food is tremendous. As I said my only regret is that I couldn't eat all of it! Our 3 year old son had an absolute blast. The water on the beach is very shallow and so great for small kiddies. The fish swim around you and will even feed out of your hand. He basically roamed the island (a parent behind of course) and was quite happy exploring the various nooks and crannies as well as the resident parrots. The bures are lovely and well-appointed, and the indoor-outdoor bathrooms are gorgeous. Toberua was very special mainly due to the friendliness of the staff. I can't remember going to any other place where the staff made such an impression. Because they live on the island you get a chance to know them, and for them to know you. This made a big difference especially to our son who felt like he had a whole lot of new friends. I was impressed by how many repeat visitors come to the island - we met a family who had been there 12 times, and a couple whose parents had been there over 30 times!! I would certainly go back and would recommend it to couples and famlies with small children.

author: aussie_angel82
title: Another fantastic stay at our favourite resort in Fiji!!
text: We have recently returned from our 3rd trip to Toberua....and can say for certain it will not be our last!! This is the perfect place to unwind. You can relax here, secure in the knowledge that you will be well looked after. The staff and management at Toberua genuinely care about making your holiday in Fiji as memorable and positive an experience as possible, and will go out of their way to ensure that any requests from guests are promptly attended to. Everyone greets you by name from the moment you arrive, making you feel truly welcome. Indeed, even the resident parrot Jack will often take the time to say 'Bula' or 'Hello' as you walk past! It is interesting that other resorts sometimes claim that lower quality food is an unavoidable part of staying on an island - clearly, anyone who believes this has never been to Toberua! The food here is absolutely amazing. Three or four course lunches and dinners are the norm, and every dish is always superb. This is the one restaurant in which I have dined where I will try each and every dish with absolute confidence that it will be delicious. The live Fijian music each night during dinner, courtesy of the Toberua Serenaders, further enhances the dining experience. As you sit at your candlelit table, listening to their beautiful singing whilst looking out at the many stars, with the soft sound of the ocean in the background, I can guarantee you will never want to leave. Apart from eating (look forward to breakfast, morning tea, lunch, afternoon tea and dinner)there are also lots of other activities available! Snorkelling trips are organised most days, and also offered are excursions to different nearby islands, village visits, daytrips to Suva or Levuka, Diving and fishing expeditions, and daily reef golf. Plus if theres ever something you want to do that does not seem to be listed, just ask and you can rest assured that management will do all they can to accomodate your request. Vinaka vakalevu to all the team at Toberua for another wonderful holiday - we will be back!!

author: 426yvonnew
title: Fantastic Fiji Destination
text: From what I had read, I was expecting Toberua to be fantastic - and it was! We spent the last 5 nights of our 3-week holiday here and couldn't have picked a better place. Toberua is easy to get to from Nousori Airport. You are collected from the airport, taken to Toberua's river landing, and then taken by boat to Toberua (about half an hour trip down out the river mouth to the open sea and Toberua Island Jetty). There is no small boat transfers or wading through water! We loved our private ocean-front bure - the huge towering ceiling, large covered verandahs, indoor/outdoor shower, hammock in the shade, water lapping close by, etc. The food was excellent and the staff and service unfaultable. The Island itself is interesting and beautiful with sandy paths, towering shady coconut palms, and changing scenery with high and low tide. One soon gets used to the banded sea snakes sleeping in cool hollows quite oblivious to the coming and goings of guests. There is plenty to do if you can raise the energy - from reef golf to water sports - lazing around the pool, table tennis, village visit, Bird Island visit, fishing, etc. Don't miss the bbq on Picnic Island. The staff pack everything you can think of (including beach umbrellas) A beautiful little island with white powdery sand, and exceptionally good snorkelling. While you're in the water, staff are preparing the most wonderful bbq. Everything about our Toberua experience was a joy - the staff were just so friendly and helpful. We were sorry to leave and hope to go back again one day. If you only have a chance to visit one place in Fiji go to Toberua - you won't be disappointed.

author: gangin
title: Immaculate!
text: “Immaculate” is the word that pops to mind when thinking of our stay at the Brookside. From the moment we turned into the entrance to when we left, we found no fault with the grounds, accommodations, or the hosts. The very first thought I had when I pulled into the graveled parking area was “How do they keep the gravel off the paved drive?” I still do not know, but the same care is seen throughout the property and the Inn. We stayed in the Palms with a king bed, 2 comfortable recliners, TV, DVD, wi-fi, mini-fridge and remote controlled fireplace. The individual heating/cooling unit was operated by a remote control and was so quiet that I had to put my hand near it to see if it was working! During our stay we were able to keep our windows open for the cool breezes. The outside sitting area had a view of the mountains as did the common area and dining space. Everything Dina and Carolyn did was for the comfort of their guests including great breakfasts to start the days. We left breakfasts with empty plates and no need for lunch on the two days we stayed! We also left with the Brookside cookbook. One interesting comment made by Carolyn was that they keep a menu of breakfast during your stays and would try not to repeat them during repeat visits. Just another example of their attention to detail! A large supply of visitor info on the area and menus of local restaurants were available in the lobby. Dina and Carolyn were a great source of information also. There was a "rainy day" room with many DVDs and books available. Downtown Waynesville is less than 1 ½ mile and five minutes away. We enjoyed browsing in the shops and galleries and have eaten dinner in several of the very good restaurants there. The entrance to the Blue Ridge Parkway is about 7 miles away and both directions on the parkway quickly rise to heights that give great views of the area. We enjoy our visits to the Waynesville area and have added the Brookside as a preferred accommodation for future stays!

author: Julianne65
title: Very pretty Inn with very friendly and knowledgeable staff
text: My husband and I visited Brookside Mountain Mist Inn for our first wedding anniversary. I had seen the Inn on a website, and since it looked very nice, I decided to book a room. The place is very pretty, inside and out, and pretty much, what you see is what you get. Carolyn and Dina, the owners, are very welcoming, and they have helpful recommendations about things to do in the area. Plus, Dina is a great cook, so breakfasts are worth getting up for. My husband and I stayed in the Plantation Room, which has a walk-in shower and a 2 person jacuzzi tub. The shower was great, and the jacuzzi tub bath salts were fantastic. While my husband and I went here for a romantic getaway, it is also a nice place for couples to stay as an alternative to a hotel, and for adults with older children or even friends. Waynesville is about 30 minutes outside of Asheville and has a cute downtown area with lots of fun and different shops and restaurants. It makes for a great way to spend an afternoon. And then there is Asheville, with the shops, restaurants and of course Biltmore. It makes a great day trip. Also, there are plenty of outdoor activities, such as white water rafting, kayaking and horseback riding, as well as a number of other types of attractions in the area. There is something for just about everyone. My husband and I very much enjoyed our stay and are planning to go back! And Brookside Mountain Mist Inn offer discounts for returning guests. :)

author: wmtip
title: Great Breakfast, even better hospitality
text: We had the greatest time staying with Carolyn and Dina. The warm hospitality was refreshing and genuine. For breakfast we had 3 courses each morning (muffins, fresh fruit, and major entree). Some of the wonderful things Dina made were Sweet Potato pancakes, sausage casserole, blueberry cream cheese muffins, parfait, strawberry lemonade muffins and cheesy hashbrown casserole. They have thought of everything here. From wine glasses, refrigerator in the rooms, cork screws, evening snacks (i.e. ooey gooey chocolate chip cookies and pistachio cake), game closet, water, coke and hot chocolate available 24/7. The inn is super clean and quiet. The inn was fully booked during and our stay and we didn't hear a peep from the other rooms. Great room with a roomy bathroom and shower. Hot water was not a problem at all. The inn is located close enough to Asheville to be convenient, but also far enough away (about 30 minutes) to be quiet and relaxing. Located about 5 minutes from Downtown Waynesville, dinner selections are varied. There is also free wi-fi and a laptop in the common area that is available for use while visiting. I can't wait to book my next trip. If you are looking for a quiet, warm, and relaxing place to stay, then look no further.

author: SOBELLE1
title: PLUSH, PAMPERING, PLUS!!!
text: My husband and I were also introduced to this magical place through a Living Social Deal. This was the most relaxing, stress-free mini vacation we have had in years. From the moment we arrived, the cordial hostesses, Dina and Carolym made us feel special and pampered. We received a little introductory tour showing us the "rainy day closet," stocked with a good variety of free movies, games, and books; then the refreshment nook where guests could help themselves to complimentary hot or cold beverages 24 /7. We appreciated this, since we were just at an upscale hotel that charged $4 for a bottle of water. We were taken to our quarters, the Palm Room, which lived up to its name...all kinds of tasteful, tropical-themed items including a fake palm tree. A fruit and cheese platter, as well as an afternoon snack of oatmeal cranberry cookies awaited us. We enjoyed the comfy leather recliners and electric fireplace. Each morning we were treated to fabulous 3-course breakfasts. These gals can do amazing things with yogurt, fresh fruit, and their creativity! We just HAD to purchase their cookbook. From the large common parlor's panoramic windows, we viewed birds, squirrels, and the spectacular sunset behind the Smokies while enjoying wine. The Inn is conveniently located, close to a variety of activities and restaurants. It is a beautiful, spotlessly clean establishment, which is even more appealing in reality than in pictures. We definitely hope to return soon.

author: lori_and_matt
title: Friendly Hosts, Comfy B&B
text: My husband and I just got back from a weekend stay at Brookside Mountain Mist. We were in the Hickory Hills room, which was incredibly spacious. The bed was huge and comfy, and the room had a gas fireplace which we took advantage of quite a bit. We were celebrating my husband’s birthday, and I worked with Carolyn to add some special treats to our room every day; she was happy to honor all of my requests. We also took advantage of breakfast in our room one morning; that was definitely a plus. The food was yummy and plentiful. I especially enjoyed Dina’s baked goods. (If I had regular access to them I’m sure my skinny jeans would never fit again.) The living room area also had a gas fireplace and comfy couch, and offered lovely mountain views. The landscaping was beautiful; it’s obvious they’ve taken great care with it. We were hoping to be able to take advantage of the fireplace deck one night, but the weather wasn’t very cooperative – we picked a rainy weekend. The location is convenient to downtown Waynesville. There are a couple of restaurants within walking distance, and more a short drive away. Unfortunately some of them were closed since it’s the slow season. But that just gives us an excuse to come back later and explore some more. We spent a good deal of our time in Asheville, which was an easy 30 minute drive away. Overall we had a pleasant stay. We felt comfortable and at home at Brookside. Carolyn and Dina are friendly down-to-earth hosts, and I hope we get to see them again soon!

author: KateB983
title: What a great find!
text: This was our first visit to Brookside, and we just loved it! When Carolyn greeted us at the door, we knew this was going to be a great place to stay. The Inn is warm, cozy, clean, and comfortable, with nice amenities and special options, like Biltmore Estate, golf, wine, and spa packages. They also have discounts available at local restaurants. We stayed three nights in the Hickory Hills room, which is large with a remote control fireplace and a nice sized bathroom. Dina's breakfasts were fabulous, and her afternoon goodies in our room were a nice welcome home after a day out. We appreciate the in-room refrigerator to keep our own drinks in. There is also a common area to "serve yourself" cold drinks, tea, hot chocolate, and coffee. They have interesting books and movies (with popcorn!) and wonderful outside areas, including a fireplace deck, for your enjoyment and relaxation. The landscaping is such that you almost forget you are in a residential neighborhood; very relaxing to just sit and watch the birds and squirrels. The living room is like going over to a friend's house - not at all stuffy, very welcoming, and comfortable furniture. Carolyn and Dina have done a fantastic job at making their Inn a splendid place to stay, offering genuine hospitality and excellent service. We enjoyed spending time with them and we look forward to our next stay...very soon! Check out their website to see all the details, pictures, and things to do in the area. If you're planning a trip to the Asheville or Smoky Mountains area, try the Brookside - you'll be glad you did!

author: DianeW655
title: Great Place to Stay!!!
text: My husband and I just returned from a 3 day 2 night visit. It wasn't long enough. I loved my visit to the Brookside Mountain Mist Inn. The owners/inkeepers have obviously taken great measures to ensure they have a quality B & B. The rooms and the inn are so very clean and comfortable. It is truly the perfect combination of down home feel and luxary accommodations. So much attention to detail is paid. I have stayed in many B & B's over the years and this one was an absolute remarkable find. The Inn is everything it promises and so much more. Caroline and Dina are wonderful hostesses. The breakfast and baked goods alone are enough to command a return trip. There is so much to do in the area and Caroline and Dina could not have been more helpful in guiding us. The views from the inn and the grounds of the inn are breathtaking. The inn is very well kept both inside and outside. I highly recommend The Brookside Mountain Mist Inn. A visit to this inn would be a wonderful experiance.

author: mountainlover225
title: Perfect Mountain Getaway!!
text: My husband and I just recently stayed at Brookside Mountain Mist Inn for our Anniversary. What a special place this is! We did our research and checked the on-line reviews before booking. They all were right on target! From the moment we were greeted to the time we checked out we knew we picked the perfect place. This bed and breakfast is unlike any we've ever stayed in. It's not one of those stuffy, Victorian B & B's with antiques you're afraid to sit on. This B & B feels more like coming home and the hosts, Carolyn and Dina, are warm and welcoming. There are a variety of places to sit around the property, each with a spectacular view of the mountains. Our favorite thing to do was sipping a glass of wine on the back patio watching the sunset behind the mountains at the end of the day. The only thing we regret is we didn't stay longer. There is so much to do in the Waynesville area and we ran out of time. The quaint shops and restaurants are top notch and the locals are very friendly and helpful. Be sure you check out the waterfalls that Carolyn suggests, she knows the best places to go. Overall this was the best vacation we've ever had, and certainly the most memorable anniversary. I highly recommend this bed and breakfast to anyone looking for a comfortable, relaxing place to stay in the mountains.

author: ssockalingam
title: Clean hotel in a great location
text: We stayed at the Athen Cypria for 3 nights. This is a 3 star hotel in terms of amenities. Its very clean. The rooms are a small in size. Do not expect any views from the windows! The window is small and you need to keep it closed for privacy. Ours had a view of a uninhabited building which you feel you can almost touch!! The hotel, as many in that area has a very nice view of the Acropolis from the bar on the top floor. Get there for drink after sunset and enjoy the view. The buffet breakfast has a reasonable amount of choice though its average in quality. The hotel is in a great location. You can actually walk to the Ancient Agoras and if physically able, even up to the Acropolis. Lots of shops just outside the hotel. A 15 minute walk will get you to the Monastiraki Flea market. This is an amazing place to browse in, especially if you enjoy picking up collectibles. Couple of nice restaurants in the neighbourhood. and its a 5 minute walk to the Blue line Hop-on-Hop-Off buses. This was really convenient as we took a 2 day pass and used the buses to visit most of the museums and sites. The reception did not have the latest maps for the hop-on buses so you should also check with the clerk at the pick up points. But they are helpful and made a couple of calls to check on the hop-on buses and other tours.

author: B8976BKkellys
title: A wonderful European hotel
text: A Greek travel agent suggested Hotel Cypria for two stays recently. The hotel staff were very accommodating and friendly. My husband and I got adjoining rooms for our teenage kids and ourselves. The location is good for tourists - walking distance to the Agora, Parthenon, airport bus, and two metro stops. As many with US flight arrivals, we arrived way before check-in time. I expected to store our luggage and hang out somewhere for a couple of hours. Instead they offered our rooms to us. The room and bathroom are spacious by European standards and it has all the amenities of a 4-star with a room safe, air conditioning controlled with an individual remote, good wifi, etc. I see other reviews about the tiny elevators; hey that’s Europe. Our rooms were in the new wing so there’s a funny pathway of stairs and elevators but “hey that’s Europe.” Breakfast was everything I wanted. I saw another recent review criticizing the lack of milk for cold cereal. It was in a dispenser by the juices and water every morning for us. We let the staff know about our early arrival for our second stay and headed out to the rest of Greece. I had visited with a couple of bellmen about the rest of our trip. When we returned for our second stay, one of them remembered where we had been and asked about it. We were so early in the day that I expected to store our luggage but again, they were ready for us. Everything was clean and well maintained. Along the way they booked a couple of taxis for us, advised us on movie theaters (open air theaters is a thing there, try it!), and so forth. No problems at all. Ask for the new wing.

author: clemcd
title: Haven for Shoppers
text: Stayed here for a few days before going on an island cruise.. This stay we were given a room at the back of the reception. The room was beside the elevator , small and dark . The shower area drainage was not effective. The holes to drain the water were small and unable to drain the water making the bathroom floor all wet and unsafe. On our return from the cruise we checked in again at Cypria. This time we got a beautiful new room.. The bathroom so nice.. It had a tub and nice shower area.. Breakfast in the hotel was included. The food choices were good.. I loved their breakfast.. Value for money. The location is a haven for shoppers.. A short walk ( 1min) you are in the shopping area. So shops, churches and restaurants are accessible.. Transportation available after a 3 min walk ..

author: POLINA2006
title: AN OTHER GREAT STAY AT ATHENS CYPRIA
text: This is the second time we visited Athens Cypria Hotel. Great location. In the center of everything. Syntagma sq. 5 minutes walking distance. Ermou street 1 minute on foot. Monastiraki 10 minutes on foot. You can find everything around the hotel. Restaurants, cafe, shops, bars. Metro and bus station 5 minutes away. Station to airport next to Syntagma. Ideally located for someone who wants to explore Athens. Reception people very polite. Fast check in and check out. Reception area very nice too. Room was spacious, clean and bright. Breakfast was really nice. We had our luggage stored when we checked out. Overall we had a fantastic stay and surely this is the hotel we'll choose next time.

author: Percussionmom12
title: Small rooms
text: This hotel is in a great location. Close to shopping, museums, main square, subway. The staff is friendly and the hotel is clean. Breakfast has something for everyone. The Greeks don't really know how to make eggs but they weren't too bad. As long as you don't want your bacon extra crispy you will be good there as well. My only suggestion is to upgrade to a larger room in the new section. Our room was in the old building right across from the elevator. I have had larger rooms in NYC if you can believe that. My husband and I couldn't even get ready at the same time. I would get ready and then sit in the lobby while he got ready. Also if you want air conditioning let them know at the front desk when you arrive. They need to turn it on there. You will also need your key card to then turn it on in your room along with the lights. We couldn't figure out how to turn on the lights in our room. It would have been nice had they told us that when we checked in. The blow dryer wasn't too bad but was in the bedroom instead of the bathroom. My only real complaint was the room size so again make sure you upgrade to a larger room. Also the WiFi worked throughout the hotel and in the sitting area outside.

author: trevord646
title: 2 nights pre cruise in Athens
text: Stayed here for 2 nights before a cruise. We booked a superior room. Not sure it was very superior but it had a spa bath. Did not really match the rooms in the photos. The bed was very very hard and we could clearly hear people piddling in the bathroom above Thats the downside. The upside is that it is in the Plaka. We took the bus from the airport to Syntagma Square and walked about 200m to the Cypria. Check in was easy. Accessing the wing with the room in it was a little different but no issue. down a floor, cross to another lift and back up to the same level but with no direct link other than lift or stairs. without bags we always used the stairs. Helped burn off the excellent breakfast. Was probably the best breakfast we had in Europe. When we left we walked back the Syntagma Square and caught bus X80 to the cruise terminal. While others talked off long walks from the metro and taxi fares we were deposited about 50m from the embarkation point. Excellent.

author: MarcC
title: Great customer service - Mediocre mainenance
text: This review is a little complicated. It covers 2 different stays over a period of 2 weeks. Our first stay was for a single night. We had booked a superior room. We were given a lovely room with a terrace on the top floor at the back of the hotel. After a couple of hours, water began pouring out of the air conditioner onto the floor. The AC had to be turned off. The staff could not fix the problem or move us to another room. So we stayed overnight without AC. It was not all that bad and they gave use a bottle of wine and a credit for our inconvenience. A week later, we came back for a 5 night stay. Once again we had booked a superior room with twin beds. This time we were shown a dark and dismal room with damaged furniture and a double bed. When we complained, they moved us the next day to a perfectly acceptable standard room but they never even offered to credit the cost difference between a standard and a superior room. The hotel is well located just of of Syntagma square in the pedestrian area. A five minute walk to the metro, near lots of restaurants and clubs. Breakfast was good if a little repetitive. I might book this hotel again if I could reserve the first room we had with working AC at the price I paid but paying extra to end up in a standard room did not impress me very much.

author: 781amandam
title: Dirty room, good central location
text: This hotel is older and needs updates. Our room had a nasty carpet with stains on it. The bathroom had mold all over it and the comforters both had stains on them. We didn't realize that breakfast wasn't included in our room rate so they charge an extra 10 euro per person. We got a complimentary fruit basket of 2 oranges that were inedible and 2 peaches. The one peach I ate was good but the next day the maid had stolen the other one... Such a random thing to take especially when we left tip out and she didn't take it. The bed was rock hard like sleeping on a piece of ply wood. No view at all but you can leave the hotel for that. The ac worked really well, our room was like a freezer. The location is perfect to explore Athens. 5 minutes walk to the metro and like 15 minutes to the Acropolis. Stay here to explore and not expect to be in your room much and you'll be fine. I saw other rooms that looked newer, with not carpet on the floors. Guess we just got unlucky with our crappy room for our honeymoon. Athens was fun to visit though but 4 days was more then enough for us.

author: henry024
title: Very good location
text: This is a very good hotel, and a good place to make your headquarters in Athens. It is reasonably near the places you want to go: Parthenon, shopping districts, National Archaeology Museum, Agora, temple of Zeus, subway. None of these places are "next door"; all are a moderate walk or else a ride by public transportation. Just to the east there is a major subway station, Syntagma Square (this is also where the tomb of the unknown soldier is). Two lines meet here. One stop south is the Acropolis and temple of Zeus. One stop to the west is the Agora. The subway is very nice, and very inexpensive. To get to the National Museum of Archaeology, go to Syntagma Square and take a trolley north. The hotel itself is very good and has an excellent free breakfast. Our room was very nice, seemed new. Our room was in the west wing, for which you must walk down a floor (or take an elevator), walk across an otherwise unused lobby, then go up in an elevator. It's slightly inconvenient, but no problem. The only real negative, and it is a VERY common one in Greece, is the terrible WiFi. It's like going back to 1995 and having a dial-up. We met that problem everywhere in Greece.

author: dmcmug
title: Great location for budget travellers
text: Before we arrived the hotel, I have emailed them a couple of times about choosing the room and checking on the amenities provided. They have been friendly and patient to my confirmation of getting an Acropolis view room which is 10 Euro extra (but is definitely worth the deal). They even gave me the highest floor. The Acropolis view room has a small balcony with two white chairs and a small table, and it is nice to stand outside and look at the Acropolis, especially during the night. The room has basic amenities and hair dryer. I need hot water but they do not have water kettle, but I can easily call the bar and they will bring me a jar of hot water. The room is reasonably sized with flat TV and there is enough space for two large luggage to be placed side by side. The wifi is excellent. They even brought us fruit on the first day as welcome treat. The location of the hotel is superb, about 5 minutes from the airport bus stop near Syntagma Square. The hotel is located on a tiny street with three or four restaurants opposite, so even on a Sunday when many shops are closed it is easy to find food. On the corner of the tiny street one finds Ermou Street with many shops, mostly clothing and shoes. It is within walking distance to the Acropolis and Monastiraki Flea Market. Both check-in and check-out has been easy. The lobby is small but we do not need it anyway. We kept our luggage at the front desk as our flight was later on a Sunday afternoon. Then we hopped to Syntagma Square for the National Guard ceremony around 11am before we grabbed our luggage to take airport bus. The hotel is definitely one great reason which has made our journey unforgettable!

author: Phil_from_perth
title: Good location with mixed experiences
text: We stayed at this hotel on 2 occasions, 2 weeks apart. On the first stay the room we were given was very small so much so that there was only enough room for 1 bedside table. The balcony was good but our view was an ugly office building and a derelict rooftop. The bathroom was so small that the shower curtain smothered you as you attempted to wash yourself because the rail holding it was too far inside the bath. The mattress was old and collapsed on 1 side so that when laying on it, you were laying in a trough, causing my wife to have back pain in the morning. We requested a room change and the hotel obliged without a fuss and upgraded us to a nice Superior room without a balcony in the second building. This room was very spacious, comfortable and served our needs very well. Our 2nd stay was only a single night in transit and we booked a family room because that was all that was available. It had 2 single beds with virtually no room for a 3rd bed for a child. It appears that if you book a family room, you do not get a double bed. Be warned there are many different configurations of rooms in this hotel within the room types, so much so that the Internet photos are very misleading. We would suggest that there will be only a handful of rooms with limited Acrolpolis views. Overall be prepared to take what you get and don't expect a lot. The location to the Plaka and restaurants is the saving grace of this hotel. The staff were helpful and friendly and the breakfast was limited in some areas.

author: bytchnyc
title: The staff and the location made this hotel.
text: This is definitely a 3 star hotel. Rooms are a bit dated. Beds are decent. Bathrooms are clean but also on the older side. Only soap, shampoo and body wash. So ladies if you need conditioner, carry a small one. Wifi was strong in the rooms. The staff is what's makes this place a four star. Our flight came in really late due to cancellations and delays. And the overnight guy, Andreas was absolutely wonderful. In the day there was a lady (forgot her name) that helped us so much with recommendations. The location to this hotel is really convenient. We took a taxi because of the time, but one could easily take the metro from the airport here. Also, it's one stop from the Acropolis. There are fantastic restaurants and coffee shops close by. Breakfast has a great variety. Options for all dietary needs. Stay here for location and a knowledgable staff.

author: Carlym81uk2014
title: It was ok- but that's it
text: When I booked this hotel through Booking.com they put a hold on my room of 70 euros without telling me. When I asked what this was for, they emailed me to say that they would give it back when I arrived, as a guarantee for them. But the thing is when booking through Booking.com, this is not supposed to happen. Not that we had a real problem with it, I wasn't planning on not turning up anyway. Check in was fine and the guy at the desk was friendly enough, but our room was a bit of a shock. It wasn't like it was a budget hotel, it is supposed to be 3 star. My room however, was definitely a budget room, it was absolutely tiny and the air con unit was fixed together with sellotape. The shower head was all worn with the silver coming off and there was nothing to fix it to the wall (there was, but it needs repaired).
