The staff knock and open your door and caught me a couple of times with no clothes on, really early in the morning at 10am! Do they really expect you to be out by that time every day?! No breakfast included in the price, which considering we paid 280 euros for 4 nights was a bit mean. There was a lot of banging and drilling going on during our stay and nothing was said to us about this upon arrival. Even though it started before 9 most days. No one ever said hello to you when you came past the reception desk, either leaving or coming in, which I have never experienced ever. Very odd. The bar next door which is part of the hotel, Annabelle Cafe, was nice. Just a pity you could never get served! I think this hotel is fine, but it's definitely NOT 3 star.

author: Mazuza2
title: Good Location, Comfortable Rooms
text: This is a fairly good hotel. Rooms are small, a little worn, but very clean. It could be noisy at times from other rooms. We stayed for three days. The room was a king bed suite in the new wing. It was cold and rainy during our stay and it was a little chilly in the room. The breakfast buffet was very good with a big selection of items. The WiFi was strong and there was an in room safe. The location is excellent, right in the Plaka district. It is near the Acropolis and Syntagma Square. We spent New Years in several bars within walking distance and had a good time. The Metro to and from the airport is in the square about a five minute walk from the hotel. The front desk staff was helpful with directions and advice. House keeping was good. I would recommend this hotel as a good value, but if you are fussy, I could see where you might have problems here, the décor was kind of grim.

author: adrian-globe-trekker
title: Good location, 2 star hotel
text: The hotel is well located. Walking distance (15 min slow pace walk) to most attractions. Walking distance (a few steps) to restaurants, bars, shopping. Overall, the decor is minimalistic and outdated. Carpets inside and outside the room are stained and need a much needed update. TV, AC also really old, but still work. Bathroom was clean and had relative good space. The room itself is ok for someone visiting solo, perhaps a couple. If there are 3 or more travelers it's going to feel crowded. May work if you are on a tight budget, but not going to be impressed. The lobby, is pretty much a good preview of what you are going to get ( outdated, minimalistic and with a feeling that a bunch of frat boys worked on this together with a 10 minute time limit) If you are traveling with children, there's nothing for their entertainment (other than the old TV set. Entertainment can certainly be found outside) Metro and bus stations that go to the airport are about a 5-10 min walk at a slow pace ( syntagma square) and the fare is 8€ and 5€, respectively. It's about 45 mins using either one. A cab ride is about 35-40€. Had difficulty finding the hotel when I first arrived. Make sure you have the address in Greek, otherwise no one can help you. Had the address in English and bilingual locals were not able to help me. I was able to find it using apple maps. I'm giving it 3 stars because of the location. It'd give 2 stars to the place itself.

author: bintu_e
title: Average
text: The hotel's location is very close to all central attractions. Rooms are OK. I had a knee injury before checking in to the hotel and I occasionally needed ice as a part of my treatment. When I called the reception to request ice they directed me to the bar where I had to explain my issue again to the female bar employee. Now's the funny part, the lady actually told me that she was busy and couldn't provide me with ice and that I could come to the bar and take the ice myself. When I told her about my condition she said yes... A few minutes later she came to the room, brought me a cup filled with ice to serve with drinks. I asked for 2 bags of ice which was very easy to procure, of course if she had listened carefully what I had to say in the first place. Furthermore, I didn't find the staff very charming in general. We were not greeted with smiling faces instead some standard procedure and standard talking. We were provided with drink tickets as a courtesy of the hotel but another lady in the bar asked us to leave the tables so that she could clean the place... Wasn't she suppose to wait until we finish enjoying our drinks? I guess you can always find a better place to stay than Athens Cypria. That's all I have to say. I loved Athens, I'll definitely be back, but not to Athens Cypria, they missed that chance.

author: sonia-doctor-hedonis
title: if you got room 421
text: i am just returned from Athens. I was at World appac congres of psychiatry and neurology that happen in Hilton Athens. I cant afford myself hilton or caravel Divani.. Hotel Cypria is in the little (even not a street) near shopping zone.. So, if you want shopping , it could be ok.BUT even , if you got the first wing or part of hotel Cypria. Unfortunately i got second wing. far away from the main building byt next to elevetaro with view to a dirty noisy stupid corner of hotel...I can see good balcons( oh some rooms at part o ne have balcons) and i can hhear awfull sounds. Beacuse of my purpose(attending Congres of psychaitrist) i was not interesintg and didnt have any time for shopping. and during llasr week happen demostrations at Syntagma square...So. every morning , at first i have to walk from hotel lavrint to exit , than to walking miles to Hilton Congres center.. Several night i was returend to Safe parto of Syntagma by police car from Hilton.. So. I do like greece ,i do like Athens but please avoid Cypria hotel and AVOID ROOM 421.. taxi drivers from syntagma usually didnt speak englisfs or deutch or italian .. and extapaod cause demostration happeing.... ps. they didnt have hair dryer, its was hard to shower in that stupid room, On booking com they got 8 ..What a mistake... Its 1

author: hollydc13
title: Fantastic Location, AC, Clean nice sized bathrooms, Yummy Breakfast
text: The title pretty much says it all. Located about 5 minutes walking from Syntagma square Metro and about 10 minutes from Manastraki Metro. About a 15- 20 minute walk to the Acropolis. We were strolling though so maybe its quicker then that. Right next to Ermou street (big shopping street) there is always something going on near the hotel (in a good way) The room was really nice sized. They added a cot bed for our 2 1/2 year old daughter for no extra charge. All 3 beds fit well with some extra space still leftover. The AC was a dream (it got quite hot walking around outside) The bathroom was very large and had a tub! (important when you have a child who hates showers) The balcony is dinky and we had no view (except of an old falling apart building) We were on floor 2 so I'm sure that had something to do with it. The breakfast was very lovely with a ton of choices, Greek Coffee as well as American, teas, cereals, tomatoes, eggs, sausage, bacon, potatoes, fruit, yogurt, cereal, lots of breads with different spreads. More dishes too, but I can't think of what right now. You will for sure have something to choose from. The lobby was really pretty, as was the dining room. We were given a voucher for 3 free drinks so My husband and I got some cappuccino freddos and my daughter had an orange juice at the restaurant next door. A very nice gesture on their part. This hotel had all the necessities and went above and beyond that. It's not a 5 star hotel as far as luxury goes but it is a very comfortable 3+. If you want a nice place to stay that doesn't break the bank, but still feels like a vacation, this is the place for you.

author: Arijit_26
title: Great Hotel close to all the historical sites
text: I and my wife stayed in this hotel for 5 nights during our stay in Athens in October 2012. This is centrally located off Ermou street, which is one of the better shopping areas in Athens. We had a great welcome with coupons for complimentary drinks from the adjacent cafe. The staff was very helpful and cooperative . Since this was our first trip to Athens, the help from the reception staff was very helpful in planning our travel. The rooms were spacious and very clean. The break fast was awesome. Being centrally located, it is very easy to reach from the airport. Take the Airport line Metro, line 3 and get down at the Syntagma station. Cross the road and walk down Ermou street. The hotel is on the third lane on the right. Travelling to Piraeus port also is easy ( we had taken the ferry to Santorini early morning). Just walk down Ermou street to Metro station Monastiraki and take the line 1 metro . It takes about 20 mins. The only issue one may have is that the rooms donot have a great view, but given the various other advantages of the hotel and at the price, this can be compromised with. The hotels biggest attraction is its proximity to most of the important sights and markets of Athens, while it being in an absolutely safe area. One can literally walk to Acropolis, Ancient Agora, etc while the Psyri and Thissio and Monastiraki are also fairly near. Also a large number of good taverns nearby. Overall, great value for money . We were very satisfied with our stay.

author: LindaK420
title: Safe and handy location
text: We stayed with our family of four (2 adults and 2 teenagers) in 2 bedroom inter-connecting rooms. (429 & 430). Although the rooms were not very big, we were nevertheless comfortable. The daily breakfasts were delicious and plentiful. The hotel itself is in a very very safe location just off Ermou street with numerous tavernas, supermarkets. pharmacies, fashion shops etc nearby. (even Mcdonald's !) There was plenty of police presence and this made it very safe indeed. We walked to Syntagma square, Plaka and Monastiraki several times and the "Happy Train" just on top of Ermou St. took us on wonderful sightseeing rides around Athens. This was a very cheap, (6 euros for adults), convenient and handy way of seeing all the sights. You can hop on and off the train to visit the Acropolis, the museum, plaka shopping district etc. it comes around approx. every 45 minutes and you have about 5 hours to complete the whole journey. The Monastiraki train station is within walking distance where we caught the train to Piraeus Port where all the boats leave from for the Greek Islands ) The hotel staff were really very nice and helpful to us and nothing was too much trouble. Be aware though, there are no shops open on Sundays and on Saturday nights the blasting music from the disco nearby is a bit too much, but this is not something the hotel can do anything about. All in all wonderful and safe location and plenty to do around.

author: olerofe
title: Agree with others: good location, poorly maintained and deteriorating
text: we were a family of three . we were placed in the old wing, in a room so small that we had to put our suitcases (carry on bag size suitcases) in the bathroom for the three of us to move about the room. with the third bed, cot really, we could not open the closet door. this part of the hotel is in poor shape. hall carpets stained and buckling, easy to trip over. dirty, grimey, ugh! it is obvious that it is just ignored from a maintenance perspective. the staff was very accomodating, and we were upgraded to a larger room in the newer section at no cost. (we booked thru fantasy travel, a large agency, so that may have helped ). the new room was larger and newer, but the maintenance philosophy is the same. tv cable frayed and didnt work. large bath tub but be careful getting in and out because rusted screws protruded from the side of the basin. air conditioner worked but the plastic louvers used to circulate the air was, of course broken. .hall carpet needs replacement etc...also, beds very hard even for european standards. breakfast ok. location is where you want to be. only hotel that i couldnt connect to free wireless internet. somehow i was not surprised. this hotel was not our first choice, but in fairness to fantasy travel, we booke d late, and the special olympics were in town also. would not stay again.

author: roxylass
title: Awesome location, subpar hotel
text: Cypria is in a perfect location - 10 minute walk to Acropolis and all other major sites in Athens. It's also a three minute walk from the Syntagma Square metro, which goes directly to the airport. Beware of political situation though, because it is also in the heart of where protests are taking place. We didn't feel scared or have any issues from the protestors, but we also actively avoided the area so just be aware of what's going on. The hotel is self has two wings, and we were in the older wing, so I can't speak of the new wing. Our room was very small with two twin beds pushed together and the tv did not work. There is a safe that we did not have issues with. Bathroom is spacious and they provided shampoo, soap and body wash. Our major issue with this hotel is that during our first night, someone walked into our bedroom through the sliding door attaching the adjacent room to ours. Our door had not been properly locked by the hotel, allowing a man to come in... twice. The hotel responded in the morning and though at first they claimed it was fine as long as it was locked on one side, I was able to convince them to quickly come fix the problem. The problem is this should never happen. The default position should always be locked (from both sides) unless specifically requested. In the end, you aren't staying in Athens to spend time in your hotel, so this is a perfectly fine place and literally could not be in a better location.

author: walter6504
title: Hotel in decline
text: Good points: High ceiling. Clean, spacious room. New tile work on bathroom walls. Bad points: Internet did not work. Shower head holder broken. Room safe broken. Shower stall leaks onto bathroom floor. Mildew on bathroom floor tiles. No ability to make tea or coffee in room. Had a poster that promoted in-room pornography beside 19” television. Light bulb burned out. Poor room lighting. A lot of noise from inside the hotel made the room noisy. Overall impression: A hotel on the decline. I would choose another hotel next time.

author: needtogetaway2
title: Good location but couldn't stand the room.
text: We visited Athens Cypria when we arrived with our adult daughter. We had to wait for our room to be ready (till about 1:00 although they had said it would be earlier) so we had some coffee and looked around the area which was good with lots of shops and taverns/restaurants. What was disappointing was when we did get our room it was dark, dingy and very small. I want to clarify that we have traveled enough to know small is normal in many places and that was not the issue. We had trouble moving around each other once the 3 bags were in the room. It had 2 twins pushed together (not unusual in europe) but that was it for the 3 of us. The hotel had been booked through an agency that knew we were 3 adults and the hotel also knew this. Our reservation said a double room with an extra bed. When we inquired about the situation they said this was all they had available and that an extra bed would be brought up. I asked where it would be put because there did not appear to be enough floor space for another bed. They said they would fit it in and I further asked if we would be able to walk around it which they had no answer for. I assume they expected us to crawl over it to reach the WC. We would have been ok with 3 twins had there been real space for them. After noticing the stained bed cover and the alley view of the garbage we decided to find another hotel. We did spend more because of the last minute change but don't regret leaving the Cypria. The hotel/travel agency did refund our $.

author: travelerfromsocal9
title: service was wonderful!
text: 4.5 stars. We stayed in the older side of the hotel. It isn't all that bad. I got a peek into the newer rooms and they do look nicer, but I am told that they do not get the free WIFI that we get in the older side of the hotel because service is unable to reach the other side of the building. One of their front receptionist, Andreas, was amazing. He answered all of our questions and was always providing superb service. This hotel is lucky to have him. Guests also receive one free drink from their sister restaurant next door, the Aphrodite. The bartender and the waitress that worked there were really great as well. I've been feeling a bit under the weather and asked for some water with lemon juice, and the bartender juiced an entire lemon for me with the electronic juicer. The hospitality in Greece (esp. this hotel) is just amazing. The room was really clean. Location is superb. We were within walking distance to all the historical sites (Acropolis, Temple of Zeus, Agora, etc.), and to Plaka and Monastiraki (both of which are great places to eat and shop.) It is also very close to the metro station. This hotel is a great value for your money. I would highly recommend this hotel, and would definitely come back if I return to Athens.

author: JerseyJean
title: Great value at the heart of Athens
text: Athens Cypria is a traditional European 3-star hotel, with simply furnished rooms, not very large, but clean and functional. It is also one of the few reputable hotels that can accommodate 4 full-sized people (here, 2 parents, 2 teens) in one room, which has a great cost advantage over taking 2 rooms in a comparable hotel elsewhere. The distinguishing feature of Cypria is its location, just a few short blocks (barely one US city block) from Syntagma (Consititution) Square, close to the Metro and buses, and only a few minutes walk from the Acropolis, Plaka, Monastiraki, Lykavittos, and lots of other places of interest. Because it is on a pedestrian street with lots of inner-facing rooms, it's mostly very quiet despite this central location. So don't go there for the view, but for what you can see when you leave the room. Beds were very firm, linens spotless, bathroom functioned fine with plentiful amenities. The room had free wireless internet, hair dryer, and a safe. The hotel has been non-smoking since July, and (considering what a huge cultural change that is) there was seldom a scent of smoke. A full breakfast was included in the price, generous enough to hold you till dinner. The food was tasty, though basically the same every day for the week we stayed. The staff was helpful and friendly, though the wait staff was spread thin in the restaurant, leading to a few forgotten requests and slow coffee refills. The online reservation interface and the hotel's follow-up e-mails all worked very well. The front desk staffers were all comfortable in English. Clientele is mostly European. In summary, this was a simple and positive European-style experience, best if you are using the hotel as your "home base," a great place to sleep, rest and regroup, rather than as a resort experience in itself. BTW, we selected this hotel based on others' reviews at TripAdvisor, and our experience was consistent with most of those reviews.

author: Auset
title: GREAT HOTEL - WOULD STAY HERE AGAIN
text: I traveled to Athens with a friend from 9/9- 9/16. The hotel was close to the Syntagma metro stop ( around a 3 minute walk). The hotel staff was wonderful. We were asked if we wanted a room with a balcony at no extra charge. At first we declined but later our room was switched with no problem. The room had adequate space and the bathroom had a tub, which was not the case with our first room. Ask for a room in the new wing. The hotel is also close to all of the attractions (Acropolis, Temple of Zeus and museums). They are all within walking distance. The Hotel is also on a very quiet street. At one point I got up early morning to sit on the balcony and read a book and barely heard any sounds. It is also located around the corner from Ermou street which is a buslting shopping district. The breakfast was good and plentiful. My only complaint is that the carpet is a bit worn. Other than that this hotel is a great find. I would recommend it to anyone.

author: Gayleonthemove
title: Great Home Base and Location
text: Stayed w group of 8, four adults, four teens. Close to everything and most of the TA reviews as correct. Nice clean rooms, small but normal for europe, good value. Booked 2 "family rooms" but they gave us 4 doubles instead at no xtra charge so that was great! Clean and comfortable. Alley bar is fun and has good people watching. A few things they could improve on: 1. Staff is bilingual but not overly helpful or friendly. Some are down right rude (is this a greek thing?) Check in could have been smoother if they had told us that there were two elevators to take to our room instead of hauling our luggage through the two level lobby and then up more stairs. Also, the AC and lights do not work unless your room key is in the slot when you walk in so you always walk into a dark room. 2. The free drink cards are only good for a few drinks (non acloholic) and be sure to show them when you order or they will charge you and then tell you they cannot fix and to use it another time. 3. No receipts for currency change but their rates are better than the local bank. It was VERY HOT when we were in athens and we had pre arranged for a private day tour with AC cars to see all the sites in one day 8am to 5pm. It was the best things we could have done and was enjoyable for the teens too since they got historical information as well as info about what it's like to live in athens today. I could not imagine doing a whole day of sites in the 100 degree weather we had so we made the most of the day with the tour and then had another day to do museums and meandering, Buses are easy to use too and cheap if you have more time in the city.

author: kiwienvy
title: Location, Location, Location...
text: We were travelling with 4 small chn and grandparents. Location was important everything had to be within walking distance. The hotel is on a little side street(pedestrian and scooters), It linked to a main shopping street that was busy and full of things to buy! At one end is Parliament Buliding and Syntagma Sq. 5min max. At the other is Monstraski Sq VERY good for cheaper eating and flea market shopping approx. 15min walk. Not far from there you have access to little trains that can take you straight to the acropolis for a reasonable price. Shopping for basics (little supermarkets) are minutes away. We even walked to the Temple of Zeus and the Gardens (can't remember name but very good for tired chn (grandparents and parents) to relax in. Has chn's playground. It was further though approx. 20min, 30min at a stroll. The rooms were very small but this may be typical of Athens, the only thing that bugged us was the unfriendly female staff on the desk (usually during the day) not once did she smile, welcome us, at times we felt we were inconveniencing her by asking for help or directions. That aside breakfast buffet as excellent hot bacon, eggs, sausage/ fruit/yoghurt/cake/cereal/bread/toast etc yum! Overall, would stay there again more positives than negatives.

author: TexanBornTravelers
title: Highly recommend, great staff, service and location
text: We spent several nights post cruise here. Upon arriving at the port early morning, we took a taxi to Hotel Cypria expecting to ask them to stow our luggage until check in time. We were pleasantly surprised to find that our room was available and that the staff allowed us to check in early. Our reservations were through an internet site, but by direct email I had requested a room with a view of Acropolis and received a room on the sixth floor with a great view. The staff was friendly and extremely helpful. They helped us make tour reservations, arrange for transfers and taxis and also provided wake up calls as requested. At any time we had a question or asked for a recommendation the staff responded in a friendly, supportive manner. The room was large enough with sufficient closet and drawer space for our stay. We had just returned from a 12 night cruise, so we did have more luggage than we normally would take on any trip. Our room had 2 twin beds pushed side by side. The beds were on the firm side, but comfortable enough. In our room there was a desk, an arm chair and a welcome basket with oranges, apples and peaches. I was so happy to see a bathtub in the bathroom! The room and bathroom were clean and the air conditioning worked well. The buffet breakfast was exceptional, with a large variety of hot and cold dishes. We were able to use our laptop with wireless access at no charge. The connection was excellent and very easy to establish. The location is the main reason we picked this hotel, and we are happy with our choice. The Athens Cypria is close to Syntagma Square, many restaurants, shops, tourist attractions and museums. I would definitely recommend this hotel to others and will stay here on my next trip to Athens.

author: krnworld
title: Great Location
text: I recenlty stayed at Hotel Cypria for 3 nights. Staff spoke good English but weren't very friendly. A bit of problem with check-in. Booked a single room with a view through www.HRS.de in 3 weeks advance but the receptionists could not locate the reservation on my arrival. The staff blamed the HRS for the error. All the rooms with a view were booked so I was given a dark room on the second floor. As I was settling in, the receptionist called saying she's found my reservation and I could move to the room with a view. The new room on the 6th floor had a view of Acropolis and a balcony. The room was spacious, clean, quiet and air-conditioning in working order. Bathroom was small but clean. On arrival, fruit bowl and a complementary drink voucher at the hotel bar were provided. Location is superb- 5 minutes walking distance from 'Syntagma Square'. Easy access to the airport by either Metro or Airport Express bus (50 minutes journey). The hotel is located just off a main shopping street. Major tourists attractions are within 20 minutes walking distance. Breakfast included in the rate was average. Hot food (scrambled eggs, sausages, potato), cold meats, cheese, bread, watermelon, cereals were offered- not exaclty high quality. Overall, Good value for money. Hotel Cypria provided excellent location and comfortable room but nothing special. When booking, ask for a room on the 6th floor with a view (top floor).

author: Angspar
title: Location Location Location and a Great Hotel Too
text: We chose the Cypria based on its location and were not disappointed. Located off Ermou Street the main shopping drag in Athens, the Cypria is within walking distance of the Plaka, Monistriaki and Syntagama Square. The Acropolis and Agora are within a five minute walk as well. We were a party of 6 adults, two couples and two single travelers. We were offered tree Acropolis view rooms, but since those rooms only had twin beds, the single travelers were the only ones to take advantage. Their view was nice during the day and outstanding at night. A small balcony allowed them to sit outside in the evening and gaze upon the lighted Acropolis. The cost for the Acropolis view room was 10E per night. Both travelers thought it was a good value. The other two rooms were 'Standard rooms'. Our 'Standard' room was located in the new wing and featured a wardrobe, a desk, two built in nightstands, a mini bar fridge and a tv. The bathroom was a pleasant surprise as it was large and spacious. The room while clean and comfortable was nothing special, it reminded me of a Holiday Inn. The staff was friendly and helpful. The breakfast buffet was outstanding with lots of different items. If you are looking for a good value with a fantastic location, the Cypria is for you.

author: Pink_Buddha
title: Short and sweet stay at the Cypria...
text: I stayed at the Cypria for only six hours at the end of October 2007 - but thought I would share my experience!!! I had booked the hotel thinking I would be arriving at around 3 a.m. as my flight was due to arrive at 2:00 a.m. - but a 2 hour delay of my plane meant I didn't arrive until 5:30 a.m.!!! I chose this hotel for its location vis a vis the drop off point of the X95 airport bus at Syntagma Square - and using some great directions given by an earlier reviewer (thanks!!!) found the hotel no problem - and had no concerns for my safety despite the late hour as it is in a really nice area. The staff were friendly - they said a late checkout was fine!!! The room was clean and well furnished and stocked with everything you would need - extra pillows and blankets, etc. There were also excellent dark curtains!!! It was very quiet as well. The decor was a bit dated but it sort of added to the old fashioned charm of the hotel. I unfortunately missed breakfast - so can not comment on the food, however I was given a voucher for a free welcome drink to use at the bar which was next door and was very pleasant with outdoor seating on to a nice street. Also - there was a basket of fruit in the room which was a nice touch!!! The location of the hotel is really excellent - it is right in the middle of all of the action - off Ermou street which is one of the main shopping streets in athens and is very pleasant (and is pedestrianised - so less traffic noise). You are within easy walking distance of Plaka and the Acropolis, etc... Overall I think this hotel is really good value and I would recommend it.

author: PVTraveller
title: Great hotel
text: Stayed here at the beginning and end of a 3 week trip to Greece. Stayed here for 2 nights at the beginning of our trip and 1 night at the end. Check in was smooth and pleasant both times and the staff are very good and helpful. We had booked a family room and for the first 2 nights were pleasantly surprised to get a large room and a half (almost like two rooms) with large bathroom in the new building. The bathroom had a jacuzzi tub which our kids enjoyed. Everything worked well, including the a/c. By contrast, my sister had also booked a family room and they got a small room in the old building which was in need up updating. On our last night in Greece we were again in the new building, but the room was smaller, but more freshly decorated with a similar great bathroom as before. The only negative this time was that the a/c was not working and our room was an oven the whole night long. It was extremely unpleasant, but had to be endured as we had checked in fairly late and we only discovered it wasn't working at around 1:15 am when we couldn't sleep because of the heat. This was truly the only negative. If anybody checks into room 125 anytime soon, ask them if it's been fixed! Breakfast is very good with plenty of choices, and the staff are excellent here as well. Location is wonderful, within walking distance to everything and very close to Syntagma square metro station. Would definitely stay here again next time we're in Athens.

author: DorisDayqld
title: Great location
text: My husband and I stayed at the Athens Cypria on 3 different occasions over a 2 week holiday to Greece. On each occasion, we were not disappointed with the service and cleanliness of the hotel. We had 3 different rooms. The first was room No 122 - a queen bed with a smallish bathroom (shower/bath), no balcony, a view to other rooms, air con, hair dryer, shower gel, shampoo, small fridge, tv, fruit. The second room was No 230 - king bed, shower/spa, shower gel, shampoo, air con, hair dryer, small fridge, tv, fruit, electric jug, coffee, sugar, milk, no balcony, a view over a street. The third room was No ? - queen bed, bath/shower, small balcony, view to other rooms, air con, hair dryer, shower gel, shampoo, small fridge, tv, fruit. Breakfast was a buffet with a substantial variety of juice, cereal, breads, hot food (scrambled eggs, sausages, bacon,potatoe), cold food (cold meats, tomato, cheese etc), fresh fruit, coffee. This hotel is centrally located and is within walking distance to Syntagma Square, Plaka, Monastiraki Square, Acropolis, other ancient sites and public transport (bus, tram, rail and the tourist bus). The front desk reception staff were very helpful offering directions for locating public transport and a map of Athens. The day we checked out, we were able to leave our luggage at reception while we went off sightseeing. The luggage is in view of the staff but is not secure. Each time we stayed we received a voucher which entitled us each to a free coffee, orange juice or ouzo at the cafe next to the hotel. Nice touch we thought! You can access the internet for 3 euro an hour. We would recommend this hotel for the average tourist travelling on a budget and we would stay there again.

author: Simpv21
title: Good moderate hotel
text: Overall, the Cypria was a decent hotel located in the heart of Athens. It is a clean and modern moderate hotel. While it lacked some luxuries, it was an extremely good priced accommodation. The best quality is its location- just two blocks off Syntagma Square and a few blocks from the Plaka and other shopping, the hotel provided an excellent base to explore the city by foot and mass transportation. The staff was friendly and helpful. The rooms were very clean and everything in both of our rooms was in good working order. The disadvantages- like most places in Greece, the hotel was very smoky. Our first room was infused with a permanent smoke smell, a problem furthered by the less than perfect ventilation (our first room overlooked an interior courtyard of approximately 1 square meter). It's central location does have one drawback- narrow streets. Our tour bus was unable to drive close, so when we were picked up/dropped off, it was always in Syntagma Square. Finally, the breakfast was mediocre at best. The selection was limited and bland, but the staff always friendly. To avoid large crowds in the small dining area, go early (and you also beat the plumes of smokes from cigarettes). One last tip- there are two wings to the Cypria. The first time we stayed in the older wing. Down the stairs from the main lobby are the elevators to the newer wing. If you can, try to stay in the newer wing- the rooms are larger and more modern. Overall, the Cypria is a great moderate hotel with one of the best locations in Athens!

author: scoobydoobie
title: A Modern, Pleasant, and Convenient Hotel
text: We stayed at the Athens Cypria Hotel for two nights at the front end of our honeymoon and on the last night of the honeymoon after returning from Santorini before the flight back to the United States. We stayed in early May. The front desk staff was courteous and helpful, the hotel clean and very conveniently located just off of Syntagma square, very close to the Plaka, Kolonaki, and the Acropolis. We had a "superior room". King size bed, jacuzzi tub. The bathrooms were very nice and modern, the shower good and strong. Beds nice and comfortable. Not so much of a view but in Athens, who really cares about a view? The hotel was in easy walking distance of everything we wanted to see during our brief stay in Athens. Some of the rooms reportedly have a view of the Acropolis, I believe rooms 603-607, but they are more expensive than the superior room we had and when I asked the clerks one time to see if we could change to an acropolis view room from the superior room, they laughed at me. Our rooms were very clean and cofmortable. And the ceilings were mad high! I'm 5'10", and even with jumping on the bed as high as I could, I couldn't touch the ceiling. The breakfast that the hotel offers is not bad at all. It's sort of geared towards Germans and Brits so some of the breakfast items seem a bit unsavory to a dumb American like me, but it's not bad. Also, the cabbie from the airport had a very hard time finding the place, since the street it's on is a tiny sidestreet. Personally , we preferred the metro from the airport to Syntagma station, from which it's a 4-5 minute very easy walk to the hotel. Remember, your hotel in Athens is simply a place to keep your stuff and sleep and bathe. The Cypria was very welcoming and seemed to be a popular place from the amount of business they had. Though we might be curious to try another hotel if we go back to Athens simply for the sake of variety, we'd stay again at the Cypria in a heartbeat.

author: GreekamericanMom
title: Athens Cypria perfect for families
text: We just returned from 3 weeks in Greece. It was our 1st trip for our kids, ages 7 and 5. My husband and I haven't been for 11 years, although I have been 5 times total. Usually we stay with family, but since there were 10 of us traveling from the US, we stayed in hotels. I chose the Athens Cypria based on a review in Frommer's Greece and because of all the positive reviews on Trip Advisor. The Athen's Cypria did not dissappoint. We had one room for our family of 4 and one for my sister's family of 4. The location was great, walking distance to many areas and a very short walk to the Metro. The breakfast in the morning was also excellent to have--just eat and go sightseeing. We also appreciated the drink coupon we received at check in. I am not sure we got it just because our room was not quite ready, but it was nice to have a Frappe and relax for a bit. The hotel staff was so nice and always helpful. The AC worked well--I have to admit, just because a hotel says it has ac, it may not work. I also enjoyed having Ermou street so close, just a block up. It is fun to shop/window shop on Ermou. Just a suggestion--write down the location of the hotel with cross streets. Not one taxi driver knew of this little gem. Our Athenian family also had not heard of it. (Take Karayioryi Servias out of Syntagma Sq;Diomias is on the left, after Lekka).

author: Me5492
title: Cypria Surprise
text: We stayed at the Cypria on our last night in Athens before heading to the airport. It was a nice surprise. The lobby was charming and the staff was helpful. There are plenty of coffee shops and shoe/clothing stores right outside the lobby door. The room was adequate and clean (a cot was brought in to accomodate the 3 of us). We were able to get a room on the 6th floor with a good view of the Acropolis. Yes, you could see the unattractive rooftops of other buildings but there was an unobstructed view of the Acropolis from our small balcony. Room 607 looked like it had the best view from all of the 6th floor rooms. Definitely request a room with a view if you can because it was the same price for a room without a view. Upon arrival we were given a free drink coupon (coffee or ouzo) and the buffet breakfast was good. If you plan on going from the airport to your hotel via metro, the Cypria would be a great choice. The hotel is an easy 3 minute walk from the Syntagma metro station. Having 3 large suitcases, this was a major plus for us. After you get out of the metro, head to Ermou Street (opposite direction from the Parliament). There is a Mc Donalds on the corner of Ermou. Go down the street (I think 2 blocks) until you see the Berto Lucci store sign and make a right. Athens Cypria is within walking distance to the major attractions. It was safe to walk around the area, even late at night. If you're looking for a clean hotel with decent rooms as your home base for shopping, strolling to major sites, and close to the metro, this is it. I highly recommend Athens Cypria.

author: MaestraM
title: Great small hotel near but not in the Plaka
text: We booked the Athens Cypria Hotel through Dolphin Hellas travel agency in Athens. It was actually about our fourth choice because the other hotels we requested were full that weekend. What a pleasant surprise it was! The hotel is simple, not luxurious, but very comfortable and with many of the amenities of more expensive hotels. The staff were friendly and helpful. (I can't imagine which hotel the two negative reviewers visited, but it doesn't sound like the Cypria.) The buffet breakfast was just right--approved by my husband, who really likes a full meal in the morning. We stayed at the Cypria twice during our time in Greece. Our first room was comfortable and quiet but looked into a light well. It was fine for recovering from jet lag. For our return from a trip out to the islands, we asked for a view room, a request that was granted with a smile. We got a room on the 6th floor that had a spectacular view of the Acropolis over the nearby rooftops. It also had a little balcony where we enjoyed a simple takeout meal and watched the sunset. The Cypria is not in the Plaka, which we considered a plus. It's on a walking street just off the main shopping Street, Emou (also a walking street) and very close to Syntagma Square. Athenians come to the is area to shop and congregate in the sidewalk cafes. The Plaka is a short (4 or 5 blocks) walk away, and it's an easy walk to the Acropolis, the Roman Agora, and the Greek Agora. This hotel is a very good base for a visit to Athens.

author: luvroma2
title: Great value and Location
text: My husband and I stayed at the Athens Cypria hotel for a total of 5 nights in May 2005. We stayed one night before travelling to Rhodes and the Peloponnese and an additional four nights upon our return. During both stays we had views of the Acropolis (rooms #603 and #604). The rooms were nice sized and very clean. There was a basket of fruit in our room both times, as well as "welcome" drink coupons. The breakfast was a full buffet with fresh juice, tea and coffee (even made to order Greek coffee), hot items such as eggs, bacon and sausage, cereals, Greek salad "fixings", cold cuts and cheese, yogurt and honey, cake and several types of bread and rolls. It's hard to imagine what else you could want for breakfast. The location of the hotel is ideal. You can walk to all of the major sights in Athens or if you prefer, the Metro is two short blocks away. The Metro goes directly to the airport in 40 minutes at a price of 10 euros for two people travelling together, one way. (Be sure to purchase and validate your ticket. We saw several people being fined for not having valid tickets). The rooms with the Acropolis view are really special. It's wonderful to look out first thing in the morning and see the Acropolis, as well as at night when it is lighted up. It is a very dramatic sight. The staff was very pleasant and helpful and we would definitely stay here again.

author: LucieBlue
title: Found a Gem
text: It's always disturbing to hear about reservation snafus, because they can happen to anybody. That was a concern I had when making three reservations for our party of seven. But I booked directly with the hotel via e-mail, guaranteed the reservation with a credit card, and verified the reservations in writing via fax. Even when I had to make last minute changes by canceling two of the reservations the day before the scheduled arrival, there weren't any problems, such as a fee for canceling less than 24 hours in advance. When my friend and I checked-in with the remaining reservation, the hotel clerk reduced our rate for the last night because our departing flight was leaving so early we would not be able to have breakfast in the morning. We found the location ideal for walking around Athens - close to Syntagma Square, Parliment Building, National Gardens, the Ermou shopping district - and one block from Aristokratikon, a well-known chocolate shop. There were also quite a few other very interesting shops, including a great "dry goods" store that had a dizzying array of bulk and packaged nuts, dried fruits, cookies, and candy, and a store with lovely embroidered linens. The hotel is also very close to the flower market and within walking distance (at least for us) to the Athens flea market. As far as the hotel goes, our experience was similar to those who actually stayed there. The price was right for what we received: a great central location very close to a Metro station, a room that was a nice size by a European standards and very clean, and a bathroom with hot water and good water pressure. While we didn't have a view of the Acropolis, that was okay with us, as we already had our view from a stay at another hotel during an earlier portion of our trip. Because of its location (sort of an inner courtyard position without an actual courtyard) the room was very quiet, which was appreciated, and we received a nice fruit basket upon our arrival. Each of us also receive a coupon for a free beverage from the cafe next door, which we enjoyed while waiting to meet friends. The breakfast, while not as sumptuous as some others we had in Greece, was more than sufficient to start the day. Since our goal was to get out and around the city as much as possible, we didn't need a hotel with the amenities one would want if you intended to lounge and relax on the property. We found the staff to be courteous, professional, and helpful. They even called our tour service to confirm transportation to the airport for our very early departure. For us, staying at the Athens Cypria was a memorable way to end our first visit to Greece.

author: DayTrip12786
title: a quiet corner
text: We were in Athens for a few days in early June, staying at the Athens Cypria. It is a very clean pleasant, well priced hotel. The breakfast room is cheery and bright with sky lights. The people working in the hotel were very helpful and recommended some good dinner spots. Our room was on a lower floor facing out toward the back of other buildings(basically a big air shaft), but there was no noise and we could see the sky. Considering the shape Athens is in today, that was all good. Many of the other hotels we had thought about staying in were either being remodeled or had digs outside their doors. The Cypria is just off Ermou on a tiny street. It is very convenient to both the Plaka and Syntagma Square. But most of all , it is quiet and clean and the air conditioning works well. Athens is a mess. There is construction everywhere. Cement dust and compressor noise,exposed pipes and detours are a constant. Many sights and sites are closed for remodeling for the Olympics. If you have a choice put off Athens for another time.

author: Syswatch
title: Average little hotel for short stays.
text: I stayed here for 1 night on a business trip, where the hotel was not picked and paid by myself. The checkin was very fast, and the staff very friendly.. Great atmosphere. The hotel is very small, and it feels a little cramped. There is not elevator, and the stairs up to the rooms is very steep. Not for old people. The rooms is small, and feels like small apartments that you could rent through Airbnb. It was very clean, and everything worked fine. Even though the TV setup was old, and the picture not that good from the bed. Could be updated to a more modern solution. The hotel offers free wifi, and it worked very well. The breakfast room is also small, but thats okay... When I came in, I was still very tired, and at first I thought all the tables was used, and not cleaned, but when I looked again, it was the way it was placed with the chairs places across, and the napkins not lying flat and straight. Very strange way for presenting a room, but nevermind... it worked as supposed. The breakfast selection is very small, and I really missed some ketchup for my scrambled eggs. No bacon.

author: Ibely
title: Great location
text: Stayed here for one night in the split level room (small double), which has the bathroom downstairs from the bedroom. It is located next to the elevator, hence the split. I haven't heard the elevator at all, but the walls are thin and you can hear people talking through the ventilation system in the toilet. The bed is high (hip height) and very comfortable. There is a water kettle and tea/coffee in the room, or you can use the coffee machine downstairs. Small minor things: the paint in the bathroom is peeling, since the shower water falls on it every time, the escape plan was not on the wall but in a binder and only showed the way from the bathroom, which has its own exit to the hallway. However, the internal stairs are narrow and I would flee toward the hall from the bedroom. The room was small, no way to do anything there that doesn't involve sitting on the bed. Good selection of tv channels. Apple tv is available according to the information. Very friendly staff with 24/7 attendance at the desk. Did not try the wifi, but it is available. Nice breakfast bar and eating area. The city center is 20 minutes walking and the hotel has some discount deals with restaurants nearby. Same goes for a gym. A few days before my stay I was notified by reception about road work in front of the hotel and some alternative car routes, a nice service.

author: kat_ryb
title: Lovely hotel, great staff
text: Booked the hotel based on location to the offices I was visiting, and reviews. I stayed in a ‘Grand Suite’ which was not very expensive (it was in my company’s travel policy and anything other than the standard room is usually excluded as too expensive!) Good points: Small boutique hotel with plenty of character. Check in very efficient and staff helpful. My suite was a very good size comprising a bedroom, and a sitting room with dining table, microwave, fridge, nespresso machine, bose sound dock and TV. Bed was comfortable. Room was quiet. Impeccably clean. Huge bath and a separate powerful shower. Free and very fast wifi, had no problems connecting to my company’s VPN to work in the evenings. Good breakfast selection. Tea and coffee, biscuits and fruit always out in the dining room for you to help yourself to. Bad points: Funny lay out – the bathroom was in a strip along the edge of my bedroom. Fine for me staying solo but not sure I’d feel the same if I had a partner with me. Would also be quite disturbing if one was getting up before the other with the shower being in the bedroom. The toilet is in a cupboard off the sitting room, so at least that isn’t on show but the toilet door was a bit close to my knees. There was a small problem with the hot water while I was there but the hotel staff dealt with it superbly and even took off one nights cost which was very unexpected. The customer service really was the best I have had in any hotel for a while. I would certainly stay here again if I was in the area.

author: Babsie_K
title: Lovely little hotel
text: We arrived in the hotel at 14:00. As was mentioned on the hotel website, we could not check in to our room before 15:00, but that was not a problem for us. With free parking in the neighbourhood and a nice walk in to town, we were pleased to park our car and walk to the city center to do some shopping. At 18:00 we went up to our room at the third floor. Quite good exercise to walk the stairs, so when our room key did not work, I sent my boyfriend down for some help :-) The frontdesk lady was very helpfull with the key and offered to walk up with us to check if the spare key did work, so that we didnot have to walk down again. Luckily it worked the second time. Room was nice, but small. We did expect this, so no problems for us. The bed was excellent, had a good night sleep. Separate toilet from the bath room. Nice iPod docking station next to the bed. Good airco, nice Rituals toiletries. Breakfast in the morning was really good. Excellent coffee (free coffee and tea services provided during the entire day), nice fresh orange juice, warm bread, cheese, sausages, salmon, brie, sweets, etc. We would love to come back!

author: rato_11
title: Hotel Mozaik intimate & quiet
text: I truly do my homework before booking accommodation but this little hotel took me by surprise when I did get there from Schipol. 1. You have to press a buzzer to gain access! 2. The very small lift has to be pressed ALL the time as you wait for it & when you are inside.I was on the 3rd floor & with the steep steps I had to just take those vs.having to go through this nightmare 3. There is hardly any food - dinner menu is very scanty/limited. Thank God I was on a business trip with colleagues & so half the time I was eating out with them.The few groceries I did had to go to their fridge as there's no bar fridge in the standard room as has become routine at most hotels 4. There is no wardrobe - just a very small space with a few hangers-this amazes me no end! 5.The staff pick up the phone after a thousand rings - 1-2 staff at a time so I guess the reception area where the phone is unattended at times 6. I had 2 single beds with 2 very narrow duvets 7. City Centre rather far in wet/cold weather but ok-ish if you take the bus/walking in good weather The good: 1. Friendly staff - mainly ladies who allowed me to check in even before 12 as I had requested while still at home 2. Very close to my office - 5mins walk made up for it & stopped me from making a booking at the usual Novotel City Centre/The glorious Hilton. 3. Quiet area close to Embassies So for those who love small intimate/cramped spaces (25 rooms here) go for this standard room or upgrade to a bigger/non-standard room

author: Victor155032
title: Best service ever!
text: The service in this hotel is outstanding. From the moment you check in to the moment you check out you feel at home, more like a guest than a customer. It is difficult to put into words the concept of service, but I will try. We booked the "surprise room" for one week, this turned to be a luminous, super clean, medium size room. Breakfast was included with a remarkably good coffee selection (I still miss it). There is a DVD player in the room and they have movies downstairs. One day I asked for some Tabasco sauce, they said they did not have (hot food is not very popular in Holland) but they promised me to have it ready for the following day... and they did. Other day I went a bit late for the breakfast and there were no scrambled eggs left, I asked and they cooked 2 right then for me. But you have to try the salmon, that is the real deal. The day I arrived, I had a little problem with the internet. I needed a special type of connection (SSL using port 22) to connect to my server in Denmark. This is beyond email and web surfing which worked totally fine. They tried many things to fix it but it turned to be an issue of their provider. Anyway, the following day, as I returned to the hotel, there was a small bottle of wine and two glasses in a tray in the room. They sent it for the inconvenience. I do not drink wine, but that is not the point, the point is the high standard in service and care for the guest. So, do yourself a favor and book a room here as soon as possible and prepare to have a great time. One last comment: Do read the brochure they have in the room and request your favorite type of pillow :-)

author: deechka
title: Mosaic is what great customer experience is all about. Stay here!
text: We stayed one night at Mosaic and wished we could have stayed longer. From the moment the front door was opened to us we felt like the most important people to the staff. The attention to detail at this hotel is just amazing. While the decor, which is new and trendy, is not exactly our choice, that really didn't matter. A full tour of the kitchen/dining area and the wonderful coffee and tea facilities (available free all day) within the first 5 minutes of arriving, and we knew we had chosen to stay at one of the best hotels we've ever stayed in. All of the staff are incredibly helpful, friendly and highly professional. They are genuinely interested in you, that you have the best stay possible, and make you feel like you are at a home away from home. Our room was a "Light room" and indeed it was with a great view over the rooftops. The room was not especially large, but very well laid out and extremely comfortable. The bed and the linen were a joy to sleep in. The welcome booklet detailed everything you needed to know from the usual how to make a call, to instructions for the air conditioning. The welcome note from the owner described how running this hotel was her passion and that is extremely apparent from the attention to detail for the guest's stay. Breakfast was also very nice. Oh and I did I already mention the great coffee? The location is really nice - only a 10 minute walk down tree lined streets to get to the centre. The Hague is really not that large, so this feels just like being in the centre. Plus the staff are very helpful at orienting you where you need to go, as well as showing a genuine interest in what you have seen and done on your return. I can't recommend Mosaic highly enough. It's a great example of something done right. And it's rare to come across excellence in customer experience as you'll get on a stay at Mosaic.

author: MarcLAmsterdam
title: Excellent and surprising stay in a Hotel with character!
text: Our stay was absolutely fantastic! We simply booked the surprise room on internet. When we arrived we where really surprised because we got a big suite. Two seperate rooms. One with the bed, bath and the really big shower. Another room for relaxing. When we looked out of the window, we saw our bicycles (we also booked them in advance) ready for action. Within 10 minutes cycling we saw the sea! We had the best fish ever in the Scheveningse Harbour (Harbour Club!). We went to The Hague center for some after diner drinks. When arriving back at the hotel, we had a nice chat with the friendly door-keeper. The bed was big en comfortable. We want these pillows at home! When we woke up, we simply gave a ring to the reception for our Champagne breakfast. A few minutes later we once again where surprised by the excellent breakfast on bed. The Pink Champagne, salmon en freshly baked croissants gave us the best start of the day. No doubt this was one of our best stays at a really personal hotel. Next we're in The Hague we again will stay at this hotel!!

author: rahallny
title: Simply Extraordinary
text: Absolute five star performance. The service was flawless. The food choices were excellent. The room and the hotel's environment were heavenly. The beach was almost perfect. The spa was idyllic. The logistics of airport pick-up and drop-off were perfect. There are two points for potential travelers to note. The first is that all this perfection comes at a hefty price. The second is that the resort is built on the side of a hill. This opens up the spectacular vistas from the rooms and the beautiful and lush vegetation that characterizes the resort, and it also assures the privacy on the beach that is part of the attraction of the resort. It means, however, that most rooms are a few minutes (by golf cart) from the beach/the restaurant/the spa/the gym. It also means the beach is not a mile long and 50 yards wide. But that is a choice a traveler gets to make, of the Four Seasons or other "isolated" Samui resorts vs any of the resorts on one of the substantial beaches. Room hint at the Four Seasons -- Rooms 503 and 504 are fabulous

author: stone1980
title: Paradise once again
text: This was our second time staying at the amazing Four Seasons Koh Samui and it won’t be our last ! We are a family of 4, 2 adults and a 4 and 10 year old. Our latest stay saw us checking in for a wonderful 13 nights in a family villa. The staff were thoughtful enough to give us the same fabulous villa that we had 2 years prior. There is nothing that the staff won’t do for you ! Service is 110% at all times. From the buggy drivers to the wait staff at breakfast they all genuinely love their jobs and love interacting with you. The kids were at kids club all day every day enjoying the varied craft and sport activities. Who wouldn’t want to hang out in a tree house overlooking the beach as part of their holiday ! The resort pool is the best we have experienced and we have stayed at all the top resorts on Samui. The villa pool was just the right size for some splashing and playing for the kids. The beach is 100% private and sheltered. Food is varied and delicious. The Thai banquet is fantastic as is the beach bbq. The pastry team are commended for their amazing work and superb creations. Thank you Dustin. We were even given some macaroons and peanut butter to take home . Special thanks to : Tak, Tom, Supa, Ben (pool), Pun, Shen, Tina and Cookie. This was a wonderful stay and we took away terrific memories from our time here. Well worth the money for the level of service you receive.

author: LawrenceO418
title: Serene Samui
text: The Four Seasons Resort in Koh Samui is a serene tropical paradise. The rooms are tucked onto a jungle hillside with incredible views of the Gulf of Thailand. Our suite had an infinity pool with unobstructed views. Our room was spacious and warmly decorated. It had a huge bathroom with double sinks, a large walk-in shower and a soaking tub overlooking the beach.It had plenty of storage space with multiple closets. Although the suite had a pool, the resort has a beautiful, deceptively large pool on the beach and the beach itself is gorgeous. The resort has multiple dining options, the two main ones are Koh Thai Kitchen and Pla Pla on the beach. Both are outstanding due to the quality of the ingredients and the talents of Chefs Renato,Ivo and Jaeb. You can also dine in the villa or dine on the beach at Once In A Blue Moon. A secret hide away off the beaten path. Very private and very romantic.Or they will arrange a night in town at one of their recommended spots The service at Koh Samui is beyond belief. From the smiles and greetings from all of the Buggy drivers, to all of the servers at the restaurants, especially our friend Patty who always took care of us at breakfast and taught us a little Thai as well. I personally feel that what makes the place run as smooth as it did for us, is the management team of Sean (GM), Reza (resort manager) and Simone ( Director of F&B). They were always there for us making sure our stay was as perfect as possible. My wife and I thank them very much.

author: DannyJB80
title: Luxurious and Relaxing
text: The Four Seasons Resort Koh Samui is another of Thailand's truly amazing resorts. You arrive into the check-in area where you are checked in with a welcome drink in an open-air reception area with spectacular views of the property. The view is due to the resort being built into the side of the hills (which can be steep), which offers amazing views out over the ocean and towards the neighboring islands from what seems like every room on property. Rooms are bungalows or villas (whatever you want to call them), with either 1 or 2 rooms per structure. Units have their own private (unheated) pools and lovely pool decks. The pool decks can be used for dining and we had a wonderful bucket bar-b-que on ours, which was really fantastic and the best meal we had on property. Because of the dramatic slope and spread of the property, the resort ferries guests around in golf carts ("buggies"). The system worked well and we only one had to wait a minute or two for a ride, every other time the cart was available virtually on demand. We took a Muai Thai class at their spectacular gym facility, with an outdoor boxing ring perched near the top of the property with amazing views and a local Muai Thai fighter as our instructor. Together with the yoga classes and wonderful spa (which needs its own review), the resort provided us with plenty of options for fitness and activity, from intense workouts (Muai Thai), to the nice gym, to the relaxing (the spa). The beach is OK, not great, but there are plenty of water toys and activities. The pool is fantastic, it is large with plenty of seating options (and availability), decent "pool-side" food options, Definitely participate in one (or more) of the experiences they offer. I skipped a massage with my wife one day to do the rum library tasting, which was a real treat and something I would highly recommend. Between that, the yoga, Muai Thai, and bucket BBQ at our villa, everything we had the resort arrange was spectacular. I highly recommend and will definitely return.

author: 778ingridn
title: Superb resort and service...
text: I stayed for four nights arriving on my 60th birthday. I had the FS car service pick me up at the airport, great choice as I was given lots of information and tips on my journey to the resort. I booked a deluxe villa with swimming pool which was fabulous and had been decorated with a HP banner plus a cake and bottle of fizz were left for me. All the staff are extremely welcoming and provide excellent service, they always stop to greet you and ask about your day. I had in-room lunch on my first day, excellent service. I booked half-board which I was so pleased I did, you can eat in any of the restaurants but I have to admit the Thai was my favourite for both lunch and dinner and also the menu changes often so you have a variety of choices. Breakfast was amazing, so many choices and sitting outside to eat and enjoy the view was amazing. The F&B director was always around at breakfast and dinner chatting to guests and again offering tips. The concierge staff are also excellent. It's buggy service everywhere as the resort is huge and getting one was always quick - I did walk to the beach as this was downhill from my villa (403). The whole place is really amazing and I'm so glad I stayed there, there are also daily activities, yoga, cooking lessons etc. There is a weekly barbecue on the beach which I did attend which was lovely and included a fire show, there was also a cocktail reception hosted by the GM but sadly I missed that. All in all it's definitely a 5 star experience and I would highly recommend for all types of travellers. Oh and the spa is heaven, I had an amazing treatment there. My only feedback would be please get rid of the single use plastic toothbrushes in the bathrooms - bamboo toothbrushes would be a better option. The beach (sadly like most now) washes up plastic daily, yes they keep it clean but it's a big problem worldwide for everyone...

author: Fairreviews
title: One of, if not, the best
text: We stayed 3 nights and had a pool villa booked. On arrival at the cutest airport I've ever been to we were greeted by the Four Seasons resident representative at the airport and taken to our Mercedes transfer. Cold towels, water, Wi-Fi in the car! We checked in and were informed we had been upgraded to a deluxe pool villa - absolutely stunning. We were truly wowed! Service in the Far East is legendary, however the Four Seasons has taken that up several notches. They have a central communication system when you require a buggy or any service, and hey presto it's there. This service comes from the top, and we were fortunate enough to meet the GM. it is clear that he loves this hotel, and that flows through to the rooms, food, style, ambience and above all exemplary service. The beach is private and welcoming with water sports of all kinds, a button on your table to call for service (drinks or food). We felt the food offering was a bit restrictive so obtained a great recommendation from the concierge at the Fisherman's market. They honestly cannot do enough for you. This was a special trip for us having been to Singapore and Phuket before coming here. It was relaxing and the best choice for us and have no hesitation in recommending the hotel, its natural environment and grounds. Go and enjoy!

author: TravelingDuo2130
title: Meets all expectations and way more !
text: Wow, what a place. If you booked your stay here, you are in for a treat. If you are thinking about it, don’t hesitate. Whereas yes it is expensive and in some ways a bit much, once you are there you feel it was worth it. My wife and I were there in late October, luckily had great weather during the days we were there and got to be at the beach, which I recommend. I say this because you might be tempted to stay in your villa quite a lot considering they have their own private pool and sense of great peace and quiet. The place itself is amazing, every inch is carefully landscaped and very well maintained. The staff is just outstanding, they are there for absolutely every little thing you need or think you will need. A special thanks to “Kip” at the beach who when I asked for a band aid for my wife—she has stepped on a little rock in the water and hurt a toe— instead, he pick up a first aid kit and came over to our beach chair and perform a full blown sterilization and cure of her toe with amazing care so she keep enjoying the water. Strongly recommend to try the “Thai BBQ” they offer on their InRoom dining. Its a great experience and spread that they set up in your Villa for a cool romantic evening. All three restaurants in the hotel are very good and diverse so there is a bit of something for all tastes, even though the Thai one was our preferred. One caveat, wine could be Very expensive...be prepared to pay an average of $100 per you average wine that it would cost you $12 bucks back at home, but I guess is not surprising. Finally, if you can, do try the spa, it is just superb ! And well prices for what you will get. Amazing set up and service. All in all one of the top three hotels we have ever been in the world. Enjoy it !

author: X6387SUsamanthac
title: The same but better.
text: This was our third stay at FS Koh Samui after an 8 year hiatus. We hoped that it would be as wonderful as we remembered. In fact, it had the same incredible beauty, wonderful atmosphere and amazing staff that we remembered. But it also had more to offer too. The games room which my children loved. The pool and bar/ restaurant are fantastic. The spa is sublime. Our villa with a room dedicated to the children was perfect. The Muay Thai boxing was AMAZING. A couple of things which could be improved on only which do not impact on 10/10: the complimentary yoga class was more like a yoga lecture. The teacher obviously has his own method which I'm sure is great if you can spend time with him consistently. For an hour I just want to do some yoga, not a few excercises, listen to him talk and watch him do yoga. Not great. Second, the kids club: was very much for younger kids. Other than the games room, there are no activities for kids who are 7+. We will happily go back - again and again.

author: brittanypeterson3188
title: The best Four Seasons property by far!
text: The Four Seasons Thailand was hands down the best resort we have visited. As you walk into reception, you are greeted with almost a 360 degree unobstructed view of absolute perfection. Our room (deluxe villa 1 BR with pool) was amazing with everything we could possibly need. On our first night, we dined at Pla Pla and had the unique opportunity to meet Four Seasons Exectuive Chef Rizzi during our dinner. The next day we enjoyed the ammentities and activities near the perfectly manicured pool + beach area. We ate the Sunday Brunch (must do) and enjoyed even more views at KOH (onsite Thai restaurant) in the evening. Nicha, an A+ concierge assisted us with a boat tour through the Anthong National Marine Park. This was an amazing tour with impeccable beaches + views. The Monday evening Beach BBQ was an expereince we will never forget. We truly felt like the resort had so much to do/offer we didn’t need to leave. Aside from the amazing views, ammenities, and food - the staff honestly made our stay so memorable. Every single employee at the resort was friendly, and caring. The communication between team members was incredible. Every person seemed to know our names, and remembered our favorite coffee orders, and preferences. Koh Samui Four Seasons was a highlight to our trip. We hope to return soon!

author: 0lilyl
title: Mosquitoes Paradise
text: We stayed at their most expensive 5 bedroom villa No. 3, which is actually made up of 2 2 bedroom villa and 1 one bedroom villa. So it is not really a 5 bedroom. Therefore, it is quite a walk to each room. We are a party of 7 and 1 kid. We stayed there for 5 nights. We had a total of 76 mosquitoes bites, both around our villas and in the main pool area. The GM said "All resorts in the world have mosquitoes" ( I wonder how many he had been to). I had to cut the conversation short because he was too argumentative and not helping to alleviate the situation. And I was surprised that he approached me at the main pool to talk about this problem when I have already told him to meet in my villa after the swim. Rather, his staff were very nice and offered us ice and ointment. Of course it is not their fault for the mosquitoes, but I'd expect them to forewarn us when we made our reservations about them defogging 3 times a week. I always had a pleasant stay at other Four Seasons properties around the world for more than 45 years. This is the first time I complain and I hope it is my last time. Please improve. I want to come back.

author: RogerS673
title: 5 Star all the way
text: We had booked 2 villa’s, one for the kids in the resort and one for us (parents) at the top. We were kindly given 2 next to each other at the top and the view was very beautiful. Each villa has a private pool and a terrace with sunbeds. Rooms are decorated in Thai style. As where the bathroom is a bit more modern and large since its a combination with the walk in closet and makes the bedroom stand out a bit smaller. The resort is like most in Samui built on a hill and buggy’s whisk you around, but I walked up and down to room/pool several times, a good work out if up hill! Anyhow, the drivers on the buggy are good fun. They know after a day your name and where you stay, make fun with you and chat the drive away. In each and every restaurant we ate we were very happy. The quality of the food is excellent and if you had a request they would go all the way to manage. Wine was sold out, the next day they remembered and had bottles arranged for us and if we still wanted that same one. The resort restaurants, gardens, pool and beach are absolutely amazing. The resort is not very big and that makes it very personal. What makes the usual Four Season stand out, the extremely high level of service and eye to detail and this probity is no exception. I wrote down several names but decided not to mention individuals , it would be unfair to the rest as all were so damn good and hard working! What caught attention, and have never seen it to such extend in my many hotel visits during the years anywhere, was the on going presence from all the managers incl the GM and being informed about the smallest going on. One small advise, they are in the process of building a new villa and if you want to be sure your holiday is what you expect check if its finished in order to avoid possible disturbances.

author: VC360
title: Perfect tropical hideaway
text: Had a fantastic time at the Four Seasons Samui from the moment we arrived. Stayed in a beautifully decorated villa overlooking the ocean. Everything was perfect in the room (tho I do miss an iron and ironing board, however you can pay for your clothes to be laundered) and the pool area with beds under a canopy and sun loungers on the deck. Very private and a nice area for in villa dining. Especially liked the mosquito repellent lamps given the weather. Service was fantastic both in-villa and in all the restaurants and bars. Really impressed with the breakfast options and catered well for gluten free and vegan. Great range of water activities and nice private beach. Pool area was very chilled and not too crowded. Very friendly staff especially at the bar. Special mention to the guys driving the buggies who were super friendly and helpful. Spa is definitely worth a visit if you have the chance. Thoroughly enjoyed my 120 minute massage. Sunday brunch is a ‘must-do’ with great views and nice ambience. Would recommend even if you are not staying in the resort. Nice limo ride to airport where we were assisted by a very nice member of staff. Thanks for a lovely stay.

author: DaltonVaas
title: Amazing Resort in Every Aspect
text: Wonderful Resort, truly. I was awed by the sweeping view of this property when we first entered into the main check in area where we were greeted warmly and offered refreshments and cold towers after our journey from the airport. Our room was impressive, it was large, features a pool, veranda, outdoor bed and dining table, inside we have a large bedroom, large bathroom and dressing area. The decor was neutral, tasteful and calming. Many essential amenities were also provided and to a high quality. The small touches were very nice and they set this place apart. I was left a pack of screen cleaner and micro fibre cloth to clean my ipad and laptop screens with. I didn't ask for this was but given it and it showed the staff were attentive, my cables for my chargers were also wrapped up in Four Seasons cable binders and we were provided with a different selection of cakes and fresh fruits everyday. Jeff the general manager was a gentlemen, he invited us to the complimentary drinks and canape evenings he hosted and made effort to speak to us warmly, A classy affair attended to by classy hotel staff. We were also made to feel comfortable by resort manager Rom, she attended to us when my Wife was not well and also made sure we were content on everyday of our stay. The food here is fantastic! being in a isolated location you have to eat in the hotel and it is well worth it. The Thai food is fantastic and in my humble opinion offers great value considering the quality you are served. The same goes for the Mediterranean restaurant by the beach, where we were looked after by Bovy (who was always smiling and friendly) along with all of the other staff. The breakfast features a large and varied buffet serving continental and oriental food. You are however also able to order a la carte, the options were plentiful, the quality high. The head chef Simeone was also a very pleasant man, he tended out our dietary requirements throughout the trip. Many thanks to everyone at the hotel, a marvellous resort which I fully intend to visit again.

author: 740ozs
title: One of the best hotels
text: We came to Koh Samui in mid April the weather was awesome. What was more awesome was the stay at The Four Seasons. This was our first time staying at a Four Seasons resort, however, I do have some experience with higher end luxury resorts as we have lodged at Ritz Carlton Reserve resorts (namely Mandapa - Bali) which before I came here to The Four Seasons in Koh Samui I definitely thought it was the best hotel in the world (wrote a review in 2016 regarding that resort). This is a very similar resort as they cater to your every need, know everything about your stay and everyone that works for the resort knows your villa and last name which is very personal and nice during vacation.
