It has a small private beach cove next to the normal beach that is only accessible through a small path, so it guarantees maximum privacy and a beautiful setting for the picture-perfect beach wedding. Upon arrival we were upgraded to a beautiful deluxe pool villa with a gorgeous view onto the beach and the stunning palm trees that engulf the entire resort. The villa was completely private and the infinity pool was big enough to swim in. We had our breakfasts at the Koh restaurant which has a huge buffet and also a menu from which to choose anything special you would like. You can also ask for breakfast in your private villa if you prefer that. We opted for the Koh because there was simply more choice and the view was stunning from there too. We had lunch at the beach restaurant with our families which was lovely with the beautiful beach backdrop. The food was good and service was excellent as everywhere in the resort. The day of the wedding: I couldn’t believe how beautiful the the venue looked – of course you see photos and you decide on which flowers, colours you want, but actually seeing it live and walking down that isle is a whole different thing! The decoration was beautifully arranged, flowers, colours, arch and chairs, it was just like in a catalogue! It looked simply stunning and we couldn't have asked for a more beautiful set-up and location. We also had our wedding dinner on the private cove. The food was delicious and the service was out of this world. It was just that perfect blissful experience that we will cherish for the many years to come. Thank you to Khun Pat and the entire Four Seasons team for making this such an unforgettable experience. We will be cherishing the memories for many years to come

author: travellinggirl1312
title: Birthday trip - 2/5 stars
text: I stayed at the four seasons resort in Koh Samui from 11-14 Dec. The resort is beautiful, the location, design, amenities and room design is lovely. However, a few shortcomings are on my mind upon arrival back home. As I'm reflecting on the trip, unfortunately I'm left with a less than happy memory as a few things went less than perfectly as I would have expected of the four seasons. Firstly, I felt the restaurant menus were lacking some of my favourite classic Thai dishes. For this reason, I chose to have my birthday dinner outside of the resort. Also, a very unexpected thing happened - our villa lights were not working for 2 out the 3 nights of our stay!! By this I mean, literally we were in darkness and I had to use my phone torch to use the bathroom at night. This may or may not have had something to do with the torrential rain we experienced on the last 2 nights. When we complained about it, the technical people managed to put the lights back on, but the problem just reoccurred over and over again. This happened 4 or 5 times on our final night. It didn't help that I couldn't sleep at all due to the very loud sound caused by the heavy rain on the tiled roof of the villa. The concierge and night manager did apologise and offer to change us to a different room, but as it was late at night on our last night, we couldn't be bothered to change room in the pouring rain. I was also disappointed that upon check out, this problem we faced was not acknowledged at all. I expected a bit more from four seasons. I was very shocked that this kind of technical problem could happen in a 5 star resort like this. I hope that they will resolve it so that other guests don't experience the inconvenience that I did.

author: Fleetcat
title: Fabulous with a BBB (big breakfast but).
text: We love the Four Seasons. People comment negatively about the beach but I think it is breathtaking (but we don’t swim) with the longest, tallest palm trees ever swaying above you. We were upgraded to a beach view suite (thank you so much) and were very appreciative as we could drink in the picture postcard vista. The room was delightful and very comfortable. In fairness to the hotel our visit was slightly tainted by three days of dullish weather and quite a lot of rain. It is hard to entirely enjoy a beach trip without being able to sunbathe and having to duck and dive between golf carts every time you want to go outside. That said we’ve visited for meals regularly in the past and the real estate is IMHO the best on Samui. Location less so but depends on your personal agenda. So why not five stars? Well we had breakfast for three mornings of our four night stay and every day we had to wait to be seated, one day we had a windy table, one day we were seated next to a wedding party who were absolutely charming but noisy and basically took over the space and the final day we were in the ante room the service was desultory to say the least. English breakfast tea was returned two days as it was lukewarm and both times came back stewed – almost as if microwaved (surely not?) and undrinkable. Small cups of coffee were decent but getting a refill was always a challenge and was never offered – sometimes came with milk, sometimes not. Everything was buffet (a la carte seemed to be at extra cost but was not explained) and the food area was small and always busy. Food quality was excellent but the choice quite limited. Of the three hotels we stayed in on our trip this was the least good breakfast and the least pleasant experience. For us a leisurely breakfast with our (electronic) newspapers is a great start to the day and in the the FS fell short. In fairness we do think the wedding party and the rainy weather created a particular set of circumstances that might not be the norm. Lovely hotel and lovely staff. Best on Samui? Probably yes.

author: Alkatrunk
title: Top Notch
text: This is by far one of the best hotels I have ever stayed in. The resort is located in the best corner of the island, away from all the bigger resorts and touristy things. The premises of the resort are just fabulous, restaurants, bar, gym, spa, boxing ring, beach and castaway beach, are just exactly what you wish in every sense. The villa we stayed in had one of the most dramatic views of the resort, unobstructed views with almost a 180 degree angle. The room is big and spacious, great bathroom, outside you have your private small pool, an outside lounge area and table to have a meal or drinks. The amenities of the hotel are top notch, the food is the best I ever had in a resort, only comparable to city hotels such as the Four Seasons in Hong Kong, (Caprice, Lung King Heen etc...) Mr Alex Gares the Executive Chef is one of the most talented individuals I have ever met. He is passionate and delivers the real Thai culinary experience for those who are open minded and willing to indulge themselves in something very unique. I had the chance of taking the cooking class as well and I would also recommend this experience. The beach is very nice, clean, and amazing service is provided. I had the chance of eating in Koh and Pla Pla several times and both exceeded my expectations by far. Amazing food, outstanding service and a great quality of people together with a remarkable talent of those behind the scenes. A big thank you as well for Mr. Jose who is the the manager of Pla Pla who was always very nice and caring. The Castaway dinner is very nice and quite and the Breakfast is by far the best hotel breakfast I have ever been to. I understand the hotel is very pricey but I personally think that it is quite worth every penny. Again thank you for an amazing stay and I will definitely come back soon.

author: AdornoLou
title: You will want to stay in the room....
text: We arranged for the Four Seasons car service to pick us up from the hotel: an unnecessary luxury but very nice none-the less. The right turn into the property carves up the side of a hill and opens to a light filled apex, specifically dedicated to check in. While all Four Seasons service is nearly unflappable, they did ask for my credit card a bit too abruptly, which broke the spell of the Four Seasons magic for a bit. The manager then come to intro herself, give us her card, and welcome us to the property. They next take your photo- which they say is so you can have a copy- but its clearly so they have record of you and can continue that ‘magic’ of knowing your name nearly anywhere you go. Which is worth mentioning- we rarely said our name or room number during our entire stay- the care of us was immediate and intentional. The room was stunning and the pool was the perfect temperature. We spent a long time in our room, sunning, swimming, ordering room service, drinking champagne. We did venture to the beach for lunch, and to the beach bar for dinner. One night we had dinner in the oval lounge chairs on the sand. It was private and romantic, and not as stuffy as the ‘private dining’ experiences that are sold. The breakfast is served at an expansive peak in the resort where you get a birds eye view. The presentation is impeccable. The food was excellent. As noted- this is not a resort for walking--- you will take a golf cart everywhere. They arrive promptly and this generally lends to the ‘special’ experience. I agree with the others- the beach is 'meh'. It seems the most beautiful beaches in Koh Samui are public and not affiliated with resorts. We didn’t make it to the Thai Boxing classes that are offered—but next time for sure.

author: Lotus111
title: Simply Marvellous
text: From the moment you arrive to the, difficult to tear yourself away departure. The Four Seasons resort at Koh Samui, was simply a pleasure. Service is a make or break for any hotel or resort. At this resort it not only "made it", but surpassed it. The Thai people are generally wonderful people in nature and manners, combine this with the Four Seasons usual quality and you have the makings of a wonderful holiday. Room size, amenities and quality are all top notch. The location excellent. Just far enough away from the local towns to give you a sense of isolation, but close enough to help you feel like you are not on a desert island. Breakfast is a culinary treat. The optional one day a week, beach barbeque, one of those mouth watering delights that you will talk about for years, a must do experience. Even though the location of the rooms are spread down a hill side, it is not a hard walk to get around. But if you are feeling a little asthmatic then a call will have a buggy at your door within minutes, all hassle free. The beach is private and well catered for for all your needs, with loungers to spare. So highly recommended by yours truly. And a place that you would certainly recommend to your friends and one you'd go back to.

author: JessicaV592
title: Best Resort in Koh Samui
text: Another fantastic Four Seasons resort and I cannot find a bad thing to say. The setting is breathtaking, on a hillside with fantastic views. The villas are huge, beautiful and have everything you could ever want. You have so much privacy but equally staff are on hand for anything you might request. All villas have private pools, we stated in villa 304, which I would definitely recommend, it's not that near to the beach but has a fantastic view. Even though the resort is set on a steep hill, there is no need to walk anywhere and the staff encourage you to request a buggy to take you where you would like to go and these arrived in seconds! Breakfast was the best I have had in Thailand, everything was so fresh. You could order items from the menu and also help yourself to a fantastic buffet. We ate all our meals during our stay at the hotel and each one was outstanding. Both restaurants are very different, in terms of setting and menu, I can't decide which one I liked more. The beach and pool are beautiful, the beds are huge, the service here was outstanding. Water, fruit and other treats were brought to your beds throughout the day. We used the spa, which was a fantastic experience. I also made use of the other activities the resort offers including morning meditation and spiritual enlightenment. I could go on all day, I didn't want to leave and I cannot wait to return. I guess the only downside to this resort is the price. But in this case you get what you pay for and in my opinion it is worth every penny.

author: Mademois
title: It is in the little thoughtful details that this resort is exceptional!
text: The best experience staying at a resort I ever had. I don't know if this is just what you sign up for when you book yourself into a Four Seasons resort or just the exceptional Management, ethics and values which they have at this one but everything about my stay here was simply outstanding. We were welcomed by the assistant manager as well as other staff members on our arrival, I must mention we requested an early check in which was granted to us without a problem which meant a lot to us as we were treating ourselves to such a luxury for one day and night and wanted to maximize our stay there. Our one bedroom villa had breath-taking views which was not obstructed by any coconut trees which made for postcard perfect pictures. It is very ethical of them to have a policy in place not to cut any of their coconut trees and they have just over 800 of them all planted around the villa's. The villa was sparkling clean with complimentary little breakfast (pastries, orange juice and a fruit salad) very thoughtful of the staff to do that as we arrived at 10am and were actually hungry. You get complimentary wifi at all times during your stay which is handy as you want to upload everything you see at all times onto social media for people to get an idea why when they speak to you whilst you stay at The Four Seasons, you seem to be speechless. This hotel is thoughtful that even when we have been sunbathing and relaxing by the pool all day and then got ready for the cocktail party and dinner in the evening, we had the house keepers come round whilst we were out to tidy everything up, lay down towels by the bed and the sinks, change our dirty towels and put water by the side of the bed all ready for bed time. How unbelievably adorable! The whole time we felt like we were the only ones staying at the resort and not only that but that we were Royalty as every single staff member always greeted us with a genuine smile and the "WAI" gesture and it really does feel that people enjoy working there if they are gardeners, golf buggy drivers or the Management which makes such a difference to a person who is sensitive to peoples energies. I felt like it was a pleasure for them to be of service. Both of the restaurants are top class, the food is top quality and we also made use of the wine guru who chose our wines to complement our dinner. At breakfast the al carte menu is just full of goodies I went for the French toast with coconut shavings and cinnamon which was a whole experience in itself. I had the most magical 24 hours there where I felt lovingly enveloped in Thai hospitality, care and thoughtfulness. This is the ultimate place to pamper and refresh your soul and give into your desires to treat yourself, after all you deserve it and it is worth every penny!! Find my more detailed review of The Four Seasons and pictures on my blog http://worldwithinher.com/2014/06/01/my-happy-place/

author: ChicagoTravelpro
title: The Magic of Four Seasons continues.......
text: We are five days into our ten day stay here, and I am going to go ahead and write this. I often rave while I am at a property and get home and get busy and neglect to write when everything is wonderful! (Last year at Four Seasons Tented Camp being an example, A "once in a lifetime" experience that I highly recommend.) Anyway, back to this experience......the property is lovely, our villa (300) has a very large pool, (I brought a blow up float, and it's heavenly to float from one end to the other), every detail is attended to during morning cleaning service, and again at turn down. ( One of my pet peeves is to pay top dollar at a property and then have to call and ask to have something that should be automatically restocked brought to the room.) My husband had to leave for three days and I was here alone. The staff could not have been nicer, especially one employee in particular "Pi". She took me shopping, sighting seeing, and basically was at my disposal during her three days off. It was above and beyond what I would expect, and well appreciated. She also upon my arrival promptly replaced my embroidery scissors which had been confiscated at the Bangkok Airport. The food so far has been amazing.....we had a foie gras appetizer last night at PLA PLA that was probably one of the best appetizers I've ever had. I don't feel that for a Four Seasons that the prices are too terrible. The Koh is less expensive, but just as good. Service is superb. The problem with Four Seasons is that once you stay with them, you're hooked! I love the attention to detail from this property, the personal service, every person knows my name, and never misses an opportunity to greet me. I took a private cooking class and everything was arranged perfectly as I requested. Again, that pampered feeling. In a nutshell, no request goes unanswered, and staff and property are magic!

author: garysummerhill
title: Magical stay at the Four Seasons Koh Samui
text: My wife and I have justg returned from 7 days at the Four Seasons Koh Samui. The resort, the rooms, the food and the service are truly magical. We stayed in 205 which has an amazing view and was very private. From the villa its A 10 minute stroll downhill to the beach or 5-7 minutes to the main reception. Buggies are readily available within a few minutes to take you anywhere within the resort. The Villa was by far the most luxurious property my wife and i have stayed in. You really couldn't ask for more. . I would highly recommend the coconut bath which you recieve free of charge (1 per stay) Breakfast is served at KOH as is lunch and dinner. All are superb and high quality. The views are amazing! You can also eat/drink at the PLA PLA beach resturant which is also superb.. The service and attentiveness of the staff is something we will never forget. Every need is catered for. The Four Seasons staff are by far the warmest and friendliest people I have ever met at any hotel/resort my wife and I have been to. Yes it is expensive but worth every penny!

author: A8443XWmichaelj
title: Great View - Small Beach
text: We recently visited Thailand and the Four Seasons Koh Samui from California to celebrate a special birthday. Koh Samui, Four Seasons Resort is a beautiful tropical location isolated on a corner of the island perched high above a cove overlooking the Gulf of Thailand. The resort is in large part comprised of 40+ Semi attached rooms each with a refreshing Spool (Bigger than a Spa, but not a pool.) Each Unit appear well appointed though lacking common tropical resort feature amenities such as indoor/outdoor showers. The guest rooms are arranged along a steep lushly landscaped hillside with commanding views toward the gulf and on clear days also toward adjacent islands. Only two Units have direct Beach access the remainder rely on golf carts to ferry guests between the various amenities including Restaurants(2), spa, tennis courts, Gym and the Beach. The service and price at the resort is on par with other Four Seasons Resort experiences elsewhere in the world. As such the service is excellent. The Staff were helpful in celebrating our special day. Menu selections and execution at restaurants were adequate though not exceptional. Wine prices at the resort were 8-10 times US retail. A cultural emersion in Samui's culinary offerings take some efforts due to the relatively remote location of the resort. Aside from lack of direct beach access and absence of beach trails for a meaningful stroll, the most disappointing aspect of the resort was the very small beach. Their website manages to create the illusion that every room is just above the water with wide angled shots creating the appearance of the endless beach. The Beach does offer warm waters, white corral sand and activities including SUP, Kayaking, snorkeling, etc. A fun 17ft Trimaran is also available. The Four Seasons Koh Samui appear to cater to the forty-some year old crowd with small children. Parents we spoke to seemed happy with the Kids Club and room amenities. The resort does not offer an adult pool area and the 5 or so day beds set aside on the "quite" beach is anything but. The daybed next to yours is just as likely to look like a diaper changing table and trampoline as it is as a shaded location for cocktails. I believe the resort offers a perfect location and great amenities for families wishing a quick getaway from Bangkok and other bustling cities in the region; but I would not recommend it for adults looking for a beach destination traveling from across the world.

author: Doyoulikeourname
title: Outstanding
text: We has been to Koh Samui a few times some 10 years ago and this time we decided to try the Four Seasons. From the moment we stepped from our airport taxi into the hotel reception area, perched on a hilltop with amazing ocean views, we knew we were in for a treat. We had flown overnight and we were given a complimentary villa until our premier villa (standalone) was ready. Our villa was outstanding: large, private, excellent bathroom facilities, nice covered verandah, heart shaped infinity pool, beautiful landscaped garden and trees, and of course the views to the beach and ocean. Once settled in we had 8 glorious days mainly relaxing at the villa. We regularly used the well appointed gym, and took part in some of the activities organized by the hotel (e.g. Thai cultural and language class). We were never disappointed with the offerings. The buffet breakfast was of a very high standard with excellent choices. We also had dinner most nights at either the Koh and Pla Pla restaurants in the hotel. We were most impressed with the chef at the Koh restaurant as she prepared excellent ‘vegetarian’ options to suit our dietary needs. Also there was a lovely French sommelier on hand to advise on wine selections. Of particular note was the warm, friendly staff at every turn whether it be concierge, buggy drivers, food and beverage, cleaners, gardening staff. They were always on hand to help out, chat or just smile. You were made to feel so welcome and that you enjoyment was their prime focus. Just outstanding! It was with regret we left his outstanding resort.

author: JAR55
title: perfect. beautiful jungle like grounds. amazing views. small but very nice beach. great service
text: i broke up a business trip with a weekend with my wife at the Four Seasons in Koh Samui. What a perfect weekend. We never needed to leave. the room is great and very private. Luxurious in an understated way. The beach is very beautiful with comfortable chairs spread out with plenty of room. Water clear and beautiful. Staff throughout the property is friendly and helpful. Breakfast was legendary. great layout of delicious food. Fruit selection could have been more indigenous but great anyway. View from breakfast is breathtaking. There is nothing bad to say about this hotel. We had a great relaxing time and would return at the next opportunity. Really really nice. don't miss the barbecue on the beach. And wait for the surprise at the end. only down side of the resort is the very long ridiculous walk from the spa to the treatment room.

author: Luxluvva
title: Four Seasons fabness
text: A great short hop from Hong Kong, the fabulous Four Seasons provided us with the 4 night break we needed. Peace, service, wonderful food and light entertainment. If you are looking for the above, take your spouse in between school holiday breaks for romantic child free (almost) luxury. The kindness of the staff never fails at a Four Seasons resort. Eager to please and always smiling, but the ground staff should spend less time chatting on their mobile phones near the beach. The new Thai food restaurant KOH is wonderful. Food excellent if you have a good stomach for spicy dishes. The beach restaurant evening menu is full of marvelous international dishes too and a little more romantic with subtle cool blue lighting. We booked a beach villa this time. 908. Just a few steps from the beach and the gorgeous round blue beds are large enough to fit a small house! Even though this hotel is over 10 years old, the decor is still in good nick. The best beach villa is probably room 910 as the sun will be on it's terrace for longer in the day. The best cocktail is "Sea, Sand, Sun" and try the home made chocolate covered passion fruit sorbet Magnum lolly whilst swaying on the beach hammock. MMMMMMM! 10/10 We enjoyed an energetic sail on the hotel kat as the wind would pick up at various times during the day and then to slow the pace back down, a peaceful beach massage to the sound of soft tinkling chimes worked wonders. So, if you are looking for a quick fix, this is the place. Now back to the real world.........

author: spOiled12014
title: beautiful, but disappointing beach
text: THis resort was our last stop on a family tour of Thailand. The resort is stunning, the setting is private , away from the hustle and bustle of the rest of the island. The service was EXCELLENT. The food was very good, but VERY expensive...and alcohol even more expensive. I suggest you buy alcohol elsewhere and bring it to the resort. We were there for a New Years and the party they put on was spectacular!! Fireworks, bands, etc.... overpriced, but all new years parties all over the world always seem to be. Because we were there for the new years holiday we had to stay at the resort for a seven night minimum which was a bit long. But that could also be that we had already been traveling for several weeks. The villas all seem to have beautiful views. The plunge pool is not heated though, which was disappointing. We did not care for the island og KOh Samui, too touristy and a bit tacky. The Four seasons resort is like an amazing oasis on the island! A boat excursion to the national marine park is a MUST!!!!! Even tough I mentioned several negatives, this is no doubt a beautiful resort i But if you are looking for a spectacular beach this resort does not have it. Depending on the tide and time of day the beach is better on some days than others. Breakfasts are amazing:))

author: HelenaD723
title: Absolutely fabulous!
text: Absolute fantastic resort. Impeccable service on every professional level. Lovely rooms nicely camouflaged by shrubs an trees and with ocean view, A beautiful, extensive, very well kept garden. Breakfast is a dream with an abundent choice. Delicious food on high international level in both the Koh and the Pla-pla restaurant. The BBQ on the beach is a special treat, not to be missed. Excellent selection of international wines. The beach is very clean and staff there was especially helpfull moving umbrella's this way and that on our request. Fresh water is supplied and snacks like coconut caramels, icecream ,grilled bananas and fresh fruit are handed out with regular intervals. The Beachbar serves lovely tastefull drinks and a lunch menu. The buggies are ever available to drive the guest up and down the rather steep terrain. We have come to this resort every year since it opened and it has maintained the same high standards of management through the years. The entire staff is very dedicated and make the place feel like 'home away from home'. No request seems to be too difficult to fulfill; we were never disappointed. Even when fully booked it is still quiet and peacefull around the resort. We thank the whole staff for once again making our stay unforgettable.

author: Mazzy5983
title: Breathtaking Paradise - Not to be missed!
text: We came here for the first part of our honeymoon and were amazed at how spectacular the entire property was - I don't know how many times we had to pinch ourselves just to remind us it wasn't a dream. The staff was extremely attentive and helpful, they knew my love for "lady finger" bananas and brought them to my table for breakfast. Each day we had a new present in our room - something small but meaningful like a leather bookmark, iPod cleaning solution, fruit, flowers, etc. The buggy drivers were more than eager to shlep us around. The property is massive so it's easiest to travel by luxury golf cart. You never have to wait more than 5 minutes to pick you up. The manager Songpol deserves a shout out as does James, the beach manager. the breakfast buffet was outstanding. We did the "once in a full moon" dinner which brought me to tears. Sunday night there was a fantastic buffet with that entertainment and food that would satisfy any palette. The Koh and Pla Pla restaurants need some work but they have potential. We didn't venture off the property but there really is no need to. If you can afford to stay here, I would recommend a min of 5 nights (and that wasn't even enough). We were the youngest there but weren't treated as such, we made a lot of nice friends along the way and cannot wait to go back for a future anniversary. Don't even go to Bangkok just connect through there and some to Samui you will not be disappointed!

author: OTT12
title: Perfect Hotel on Paradise Island
text: We were lucky to spend a perfect week in The Four Seasons in Samui. This was our second visit to the hotel and if anything we liked it even more than the first time. The hotel in located 20 to 30 minutes drive from the local airport and it is located in a beautiful and private spot with all the villas built on a hill covered in lush forest and a gorgeous sugar white private beach. The hill is quite steep and although we did walk from the restaurant and bar to our villa and also the beach we left the coming up to the electric buggies as it was too much for us. Our villa was half way between the main reception area and the sea and very secluded. It has a huge bedroom which includes a sitting and work area, two wash areas with two separate wardrobes, separate bathtub area and separate walk in shower room. Our bed was super king size and extremely comfortable. This leads to a double patio and quite large plunging pool with again sitting area and sun loungers with amazing views the beach and the sea beyond. At the patio you have a coffee machine, fridge and a wine fridge/cooler and every day a platter was replenished with local fruits. The rooms were spotlessly clean and turned down again in the evening. The Thai restaurant at the top has extremely local food and it doubles up as the breakfast area in the morning. The variety and quality of the breakfast is fantastic. On the beach level, which also has the main pool also, you have again a very good good fish restaurant which also does lighter and European cuisine at lunch time. The beach bar is very very good and during the day they come around with various free goodies, like drinks, fruit etc. Buggies are always available to take you anywhere and are with within minutes of calling for one. You must not miss sun set in the evening! The colours are unbelievable and whatever I say will not be enough to describe it. The staff are smiling, friendly and extremely professional and really make your stay unforgettable.

author: ISKK8
title: Wonderful Hotel and Resort!
text: We stayed there for 4 nights and were upgraded to a 3-bedroom residence - near the beach. The residence was fantastic and the butler was excellent. We had our own pool, living and dining room and within easy walking distance to the beach. The hotel is set on a hill so walking up and down is not easy and the gym and spa were too far anyway. Fortunately the buggy service was very good so we did not really have to walk anywhere. The service was also top-notched and could not be faulted. The two restaurants served Thai and Western food and though the menu did not change, the food was excellent. We had a barbecue buffet organized by the hotel by the beach one night and the setting was wonderful. There was also some Thai dancing. The beach was very nice with clear blue water, and a reef not far away. Wonderful for a family and those who like swimming, snorkeling and any water sports. There were many beach staff which kept the place very clean. It was not too crowded perhaps because the hotel was not full due to recent unrest in Thailand. But it did not really affect us. Only slight concern would be for older visitors as everything (except the beach) is on the hill which makes walking difficult. And there is not much close by but who wants to leave the resort anyway... I wish the gym is a little bigger though. All in all a very relaxing, enjoyable holiday. I have been to many resorts/hotels in Asia and would ranked this as one of the very bests.

author: pjkmiller
title: Stunningly situated Resort
text: We (English family, 2 and 4 year old) spent new years at this resort and had a really fantastic time. The first thing that I think sets this apart from other great Asian resorts - Datai etc - is its design and layout. Each villa is a masterpiece in design, with your own pool and sun deck, and with a very beautiful and relaxing style. They have great family rooms where you can shut the kids off when they go to sleep but still have the run of the Villa in the evening. But even though the resort was full when we were there, you never felt like it was too busy or that this impacted you, and sitting in your villa you could be a world away from everyone and everything. The downside is that its a walk to get places but the golf buggy service is excellent and quick and we never had an issue. The design of the communal areas and restaurants as well is stunning. it is a very 3D resort since it is situated on the side of a hill but the architecture and feel of the place is really impressive. The food was very good and not ridiculously expensive, whilst the kids club and the effort that went into the guest experience was first rate. The beach is lovely with these wonderful circular day beds. The weather was not stellar (v warm but overcast) when we there but that is hardly their fault. The other element which stands out was the service and the attitude of the staff which was so good. I think an element of this is the fact that the Thais are just some of the world's most lovely people, and their approach to service is excellent. But even given that, the people we met were extremely good at their jobs and focused on us, with all the soft touches e.g. remembering kids names (which is such an easy thing to do but makes a big difference) and combined with the traditional four seasons' extremely high standards makes this a very relaxing experience. They are a very popular hotel with guests from all over the world, so whatever they are doing, it seems to be working! I remain a big supporter of the Four Seasons brand - they just seem to try harder than other hotel groups to make your experience the best it can be.

author: Hermes-Ro
title: A True Tropical Paradise
text: We have traveled here to relax on the beach after a few days in busy Singapore where we’ve spent the New Year, and boy! Were we right on the money with the choice! The place is spectacular; a true retreat paradise perched on a fast hill slope descending to one of the most iconic beaches you’ll see. It has this air of private residences park (and for a good reason: half of it is). At first it looks discouraging to be relatively away from the sea and up on a abrupt hill but, believe me, you would worry for no reason as the view is absolutely fantastic from up there, what you loose in beach closeness you gain in privacy and they are religious in picking you up in a buggy in a few minutes after you call and drive you anywhere on the property. It never failed! Needless to say the service is without reproach, the facilities (bars, restaurants, gym, spa) are very high in standard and luxurious, and the little details that make the difference from high-level service to legendary customer care are employed at every corner. This is one of the best hotels I have ever stayed in and, I have had my fair share of staying at some top-notch places. We never had any – even minor – argument. Everything was possible although sometimes we were probably pushing it a little. The staff is awesomely trained and genuine in their approach to service. Correct, efficient and Asian-style-courteous without overdoing it if you know what I mean. The rooms are vey private (an independent villa actually), lavish décor, featuring the right amenities and properly equipped, even having a mini-pantry with coffee and tea makers, a wine fridge and a full blown mini bar on the generous deck of one’s own private 10mx2m infinity pool along side it, overlooking the bay and beach below. It’s Paradise, I’m telling you! In departing I have understood the reason behind the superb service by meeting the resort’s GM, Mr. Barta, who treated me like an old friend he intended to please like if I was his houseguest, although I’ve met him then for the first time. Good job! We will come back and recommend the place to others.

author: Kapuku
title: The perfect place to stay
text: I stayed this resort on October 2013 with my family, as I held my wedding ceremony here (regrettably I spent only two night). Not necessary to mention about its great location, I have to emphasize great hospitality of all the staffs and quality of services. In terms of accommodation, I stayed in deluxe villa located on hillside with big private pool. Some people loves to settled close to the beach, however, beautiful ocean view from hillside villa was also breathtaking. Taking nap on outside sofa, with feeling slight breeze, was my perfect moment. Villa was consist of three section, bed area, closet & sink, and shower & bathtub. The room was big enough for two of us. Although the villa was distant from the beach, it was easy to get there by baggy service. On the beach, you can enjoy various activities such as snorkeling and sea kayak. Breakfast was also fantastic. Beside the accommodation what made our stay very special was intensive hospitality provided by all the staffs in the resort. Everybody knew our and our family member’s schedule, and all the services were provided one step ahead from what I needed. I can say that all the services were labeled as “Four seasons”. I was impressed by the attentiveness of the main consultant of our ceremony from the preparation phase, and it turned out to be in the real world once I arrived there. Everything was well arranged and prepared, thanks to my consultant and his team, and went as most smooth as I can imagine. Ceremony and dinner on the private cove was just perfect. I never forget everything I enjoyed in this resort, and would definitely like to come back there and stay much longer. I sincerely appreciate my consultant and his team, resort manger and all the staffs who helped us, for giving me such a wonderful memories and the place want to come back.

author: holidaymaker286
title: Outstanding service, truly world class
text: I'm writing this review as I'm waiting on my car for the airport, just after check out, not only because I have the time to do so, but because it is very well deserved. I have travelled all over the world having and I must say I'm converted from Hilton And Conrad's honours platinum to a Four seasons member. First of all let me congratulate you all at the Four Seasons Koh Samui for a dreamlike stay and personalised service you have provided over the past ten days during our stay. Some people we will remember that have made this trip one of a kind are resort manager Ram, helpful, kind, thoughtful and one of the best resort managers I have encountered over any other luxury hotels I have stayed. Waitress Ben was so lovely to talk to, sweet and charming and efficient at her job. Housekeeping... The best, twice a day service, to wake up your villa and to turn it down to ensure you have a good rest. All the touch ups and personal finishings were out of this world, thank you for all the help. Food throughout the resort, including in-villa dining, was extraordinary, not one bad meal or bad anything for that matter. Cakes and breakfast are delightful. Spa treatments were peaceful and relaxing. Starting with a complimentary light foot scrub and then the rest is a true awakening of the senses treatments. The whole team are hard working, and pro-active ensuring your stay is nothing but the best, nothing is too much trouble. Beach is wonderful and clean with activities, children seem to have fun too although this is a more romantic type setting, complimentary activities run everyday for adults too. I know this sounds like I work for the resort, the fact is I don't. I'm simply very greatful to have been a guest at the four seasons, and for sure a long standing customer from this day onwards. Thank you. Thank you.

author: HarshH
title: The best of Koh Samui
text: The Four Seasons, Koh Samui is one of the best beach resorts i have stayed in. It is spread out over a hill overlooking the sea and rooms are in form of villas. The villa where we stayed had a private lounge pool and had the best ocean views i have experienced. Infact the views from all places of the hotel is spectacular. The service is top quality and you live like royalty while here. Even though the villas are spread out, service time is prompt. we had breakfast in our villa a few days and must say they made an effort to lay out a mini buffet. The lobby has oversized loungers where you can play boardgames or read some books. Dining options are though limited at this property. the spa is heavenly. i tried the four hand massage, and must say was one of the best massages i have experienced. The resort is very upscale & posh. The villas are done in such a way to provide complete privacy. The rooms & toilets in the villa are exquisite done. For Thailand standards it is very expensive, but for the lucky enough this is a luxury resort worth experiencing. If one is afraid of tropical insects & animals, be careful. the villa where we stay used to be infected by various tropical insects, lizards and all sorts of animals post sunset. Although they would not enter the room but the outside area in the villa would be infected by these pests. We thought of this as a small inconvenience paid for one of the most wonderful resort experiences we have had.

author: oneseason
title: Perfect!
text: We recently returned from the Fours Seasons in Koh Samui on October 15. What a fabulous resort. My husband and I traveled with our 25 year old daughter for her birthday. The setting is wonderful but what makes it so special is the staff. Every staff member remembered our name and our villa number every time we got in a buggy or went to one of the restaurants. The beach is quiet and private. You are served refreshments on the beach throughout the day. Not one time did our water glasses get empty before they were refilled. I had originally thought we would want a beach villa but we decided to book a villa up the hill for the view and we were glad that we made that decision. We did do some walking around the resort but we also called for the buggy service and never waited over a few minutes. You feel that no one else is around and you are in your own private oasis. The food was excellent and we especially enjoyed the Thai food. We went on a private boat excursion with Scott and his boat the Siamese Dream. It was wonderful as well as Scott continued with the Four Seasons service. We snorkeled, hiked and cruised a few islands. I highly recommend Scott as well. We hope that we can come back and do it all over again!

author: Cheng168
title: A place like a dream
text: We spend the most wonderful week at Koh Samui Four Seasons - for our two person elope wedding and honeymoon. It is truly like we have escaped to a small paradise with a week in private villa with a private pool, with stunning view of the bay which was upgrade from a basic villa . Wartchapong the wedding planner was so right on each details and so responsive to my request so one reason for me to choose this property among many other top choices in the country. Upon arrival we were upgrade to a pool villa with even auspicious villa number that has a number eight in it ( for Chinese belief, and again Wachapong would take the extra step to make sure the villa choosen was perfect for us). Our private villa is beyond description comfortable , a truly luxury experience. .The service through our of stay was perfect- everyone was so tentative and every request was answered immediately. we were addressed by our surnames by each and every server which is exactly four season 's motto -they make each guests feel like they are the most special guest. The food was near perfection exp the daily breakfast on a breath taking ocean view terrace .Our Thai ceremony was so romantic, even it is just two of us - we did not felt alone among the most friendly stuff and Thai dancing entourage. Our beach side special dinner for two was so nice and enjoyable . The private beach was great place to just relax and hang out -with stuff bringing complementary cool drinks from time to time. There are all kinds sports one can do literally a week can be passed so fast here without wanting to go any where else. So if any one has an idea of elope wedding , this is the most perfect place you can choose. Our entire week is everything beyond our expectation that we decided to spend the rest of our honeymoon at Four Season Chaimai and Four Season Bangkok-and still something about both the property and people here at Koh Sumui that give us the memory of our live . Actually there is no royalty program at Four Seasons , the foot and beverage manager took extra care of us upon hearing we will go to anther four season property and we were taken good care of upon arriving Chan Mai . We look forward to go back there to our next anniversary there.

author: steveto710
title: What a place for wedding!
text: It was my first stay at a Four Seasons Hotel after keep hearing it from my rich relatives. I was impressed by the reception area and the view. The staff were exceptionally tentative and nothing was too much of a problem. We were gobsmacked by the villa and the provisions, the view over the bay was breath taking. Not accustomed to this level of luxury nor space in an hotel. We were determined to enjoy it while we were there. I loved the golf buggy rides on site, reminds me of the Prisoner - my number was 303. Breakfast was great and the view over the site was unbelievable. As we were there to celebrate my step daughter's wedding, there were a group of us there - family and friends. Four Seasons had pulled all the stops out to assist with the event. The actually ceremony went down a treat and to perfection. The after ceremony beach party and BBQ was just perfect with attentive staff on hand through out. We had the time of our lives at the Hotel and the wedding. Good job I didn't have to foot the bill. We are now trying to persuade the newly wed couple to going back every year to renew their vow! The only gripe I have was that there should be another fridge inside, I didn't fancied going out in the middle of the night to get a cold drink with the heat outside!

author: Amberlicious
title: Secluded and stunning hideaway
text: Built into a hillside, you drive atop the hill to an un assuming entrance, however, a few steps further, when you start approaching the lobby… WOW!!! the most breathtaking views of the ocean sprawled in front of you. Check in - we were escorted to the reception where we had to wait about 20 mins before someone attended to us as they were busy with another couple. Slightly annoying as we had arrived after an all night flight from India. Once that was done it was smooth sailing from the minute we arrived at our villa until we checked out. Villas - Beautilly perched on stilts on in a terraced formation giving each villa unobstructed views of the sea. beautifully appointed in a luxurious fashion. the highlight was the shell shaped bath tub that overlooks the ocean. Can slide the doors open to make it an out door bathing experience or slide the huge glass doors shut if you'd rather. The infinity lap pools gorgeous! Breakfast was served at the villa every morning. It was my 40th birthday and we had a beautiful dinner on the Beach where the staff presented me with flowers and a card and released lanterns into the sky. It was spectacular! Food- Was delicious. Especially the pad that and green curry in the in room dining! Over all a memorable stay .would highly recommend it for people who want to get away from the hustle and bustle of Koh samui nightlife and retreat to a place of quiet and elegant luxury!

author: kewpielovesyou
title: Paradise within paradise
text: the first thing you see about this property is the hilltop 'welcome'. go past these tall, narrow doors and you'd find yourself perched on top of a hill with the most amazing view! it is so so so impressive! it's hard to even describe without being there but if you talk about first impressions, these guys have got it right. everywhere you go, it pretty much requires a quick call to the buggy service to take you around. we've never had to wait more than 2-5 mins for it to come to our villa. it's not how i like to get around (i do love walking), but it is such a sprawling property that it's easier just to rely on the buggy service - my son also loves going down the steep hills in them! the rooms are generously sized. separately sleeping, dressing and bathroom areas... with floor to ceiling windows that let natural light in! best part is, the bathroom is all inside! none of that outside shower business which i tend not to prefer cos of the tropics (flies and mossies). service is attention and not intrusive. the restaurants onsite are also excellent and reasonably priced. the staff all knew my son by name from the get go and this really added a touch of personalisation to the whole trip. we loved every minute we were there. i am a four seasons convert!

author: Daalekuk
title: Peaceful Island Paradise
text: We visited the resort because my son and his Thai fiancee had chosen it to get married. The arrangements made for the wedding were faultless and it will long live in my memory as one of the greatest experiences of my life. That said..... Situated some half an hour drive from the airport, The Four Seasons Resort is not so much a hotel, but a paceful hillside village but with all the five star amenities that you need. The resort is situated on a steep, horseshoe-shaped hillside that leads down to its own private beaches. Transport is provided with an ample supply of golf buggies that are always available, day or night via a phone call from your room. In fact, they are not rooms but discretely separated bungalows that are slotted into the vegetation covered hillside. Each bugalow is exquiitely laid out with sensational views from the covered balconies and each with its own infinity pool. The beach has a pool, a bar and a full restaurant and sevice levels on the beach are outstanding. At the top of the resort is the front desk,another full restaurant with a large platform giving outstanding views over the resort and out to sea. If anyone could find a more beautiful location for breakfasting with the lovely light breezes and outstanding food, I would like to know where it is. Service levels throughout the resort are of the quality that you would expect from a Four Seasons establishment......outstanding. From buggy drivers to gardeners, the staff were always friendly and welcoming and certainly knew a lot more English than I did Thai, I'm embarrassed to say. This is a place to go for pure relaxation and to dismiss the cares of the world. My dodctor will be pleased to know that for the four days of our stay, my blood pressure was normal for the first time in two years! Need I say more. A must to return to.

author: Matthieu_1976
title: An amazing location but some areas for improvements
text: The main advantage of the four seasons is the fact that they own the entire hill, which makes it a very calm and secluded area. The beach therefore is great as isolated, therefore you can really benefit from it. The room we took was a premier bedroom villa for which we really appreciated the quietness, and the fact that it was separated from the other rooms. However there are a number of smaller inconveniences, but also concern to be aware of if you want to fully get value out of your trip at Four Seasons: - on the beach, the sand close to the beach tends to be a bit muddy, however you can go to a platform a bit further away by kayak which gives you access to a beautiful turquoise water and snorkeling area - the kayaks are scarce (only 3 x 2 people kayaks, plus a few single ones) so plan to get yours soon - the beach restaurant is outrageously expensive, especially at dinner time: we had one san pellegrino water, one sea bass and one "lamb" plate for 130 USD +. Both mains didn't have more than 2 or 3 vegetables. The plates were ok, but nothing overwhelming. When you know you can have a feast for this price on the island, this is just unacceptable. - make sure therefore to plan to eat outside or bring in snacks. It's also a budget to plan for (you can actually get a cab to Nam Mae at 15 mns drive at 300 Bahts if you take it outside, and 500 bahts through the hotel. Trip to Chaweng takes 35 mns and costs 800 bahts one way. Probably negotiable as well) Some other improvement areas: - it's disappointing we didn't get more than the "fruit basket" when arriving. Other equivalent or less high standard hotels offer chocolates, macarons, wine bottles. Not a huge investment for FS, and does help appreciate the service. They should also replenish the fruit basket when you stay several days (we stayed 5 days) - cleanliness is good, but we did get a coackroach on the last evening... - kind of strange that the toilet in the bedroom doesn't have a door. ok for us but might be an issue for others - sometimes an impression of FS being just a bit "cheap" in replenishing amenities: not a huge concern, but I remember other four seasons who would more rapidly replace cottons, shampoos, etc... - breakfast was good, but again, I had better buffets in other places (check the Mandarin Oriental in Chiang Mai!)

author: SCRTraveller
title: Exquisite Resort!
text: This would have to be my favourite place resort that I have ever been to. Not for any one reason, but for the entire experience you get at this resort. It is so peaceful and private, set in beautiful lush surroundings. The beach is gorgeous also very private. The food is excellent and breakfast is probably the highlight. There is such an enormous array of food to choose from all so well presented. I would often spend a few hours here each morning, not just eating but enjoying the serenity and view from the restaurant. The beach restaurant is also a highlight. They make incredible healthy lights salads for lunch (which is all you need after a few hours at brekkie). And a sundowner at the beach was always a perfect way to end the day. Lots of activities on the beach, kayaking, table tennis and a lagoon to swim out to. Or just chill in their beautiful day beds. The villas are gorgeous. The private pool and day beds by the pool were perfect for reading a book in the afternoon or for having a little nap. Location is also excellent, just a 15 minute a cab and you are back in the hustle and bustle of Koh Samui.

author: Jimbo1981
title: amazing, perfect honeymoon
text: spent 8 nights at the resort and did not leave once! it was so so good. service, room, food, beach, everything. calling for a buggy was no issue at all, one was always close by so no wait longer then 3 minutes. beach big enough to always get a bed and be able to pick a quiet spot if you wanted one. staff just so helpful and very very sweet. really felt like we were welcome guests at the resort. the rooms were huge and spotless, cleaned twice a day. mini bar was expensive but all hotels are. perhaps the hotel should offer more complimentary still water in the rooms as we often ran out and had no other option to take the crazy expensive Evian. restaurants were great, def get the option to have breakfast included as its substantial. lunch at PLA PLA... TUNA BURGER!!!!! the best thing on the menu. simply top drawer. spa was just the same, amazing and all that we wanted. the staff listened to what we wanted and suggested the perfect 90min massage and treatment. i just simply can not recommend more highly! cant wait to return for our one year anniversary.

author: YungO
title: An unmissable experience in Samui...
text: Fresh from a great experience at the W Retreat, we arrived at the Four Seasons expectedly spoilt and wondering how the Four Seasons would compare. Upon stepping out of our ride and into the entrance sala, our jaws dropped at the view that was presented to us. Checking in here is an unforgettable experience. You look out off the cliffs on the bay with a tasty welcome drink and cold towel, and Ram, the General Manager of the resort, herself drops in to introduce herself and welcome you. Just meeting her was such a great experience, the staff are obviously an extension of her wonderful attitude and personality. She is so warm and professional, and she made us feel like we were VIPs despite another two groups arriving at the same time. While we preferred the rooms at the W, the grounds here are astounding. It's a veritable tropical paradise of a resort built into the cliffs overlooking a private cove with a beach of soft white sand. We took a buggy down a steep incline which seemed at times like an exciting roller coaster! But the drivers here are skilled and careful and they always fill you with confidence. There are staff on the way to the villas working the grounds tirelessly, preening and pruning the flora. Everyone you pass stops for a moment to greet you and it makes the experience here even more magical. Our villa had its own private pool that looked out into the surrounding jungle and onto the bay below. We were surrounded by a friendly family of squirrels who seemed like they had gotten used to the fact they had to share their home with us and were dancing in the trees while we got changed and headed straight to the beach. We headed to the private area of the beach which was away from the kids. Over the 3 hours we spent there, staff treated us to trays of fresh fruit, cookies and other goodies, which made us feel like staying even longer to be pampered, but we wanted to explore the rest of the resort. There's a lot more to see here than just the beach and I'd suggest spending as much time in the resort as you can because most of Samui pales in comparison.

author: Lottie_NY
title: Did not want to leave
text: This was the third hotel in a recent round world trip and we were lucky enough to get a villa at the Hotel for 4 nights after the Bangkok Four Seasons help us secure a space. The car service picks you up from the airport making it very easy and it's a short drive to the hotel. Upon arrival you step out and walk through these doors to the reception area. Except it is not like any reception area I have ever experienced. A wooden deck with a view across the cliff / tree / sea that literally takes your breath away. You are seated and refreshed with an iced cocktail whilst they process your check in. A small golf cart then transfers you to your booked villa. The staff are discreet but friendly and nothing is a problem for any small request you may have. The villa is beautiful. We had the king bed, with walk in bathroom with egg shaped bath, rain shower and then long pool in front. All perched up on the cliff so totally private and surrounded by trees with a view to the bay below. Having your own pool with room is just brilliant. (I wish more hotels in the US would consider this concept for high end hotels!). The spa is beautiful and we had a few treatments and food / dining is great. I really recommend though also leaving the hotel if you can tear yourself away to see the local areas and explore the island. Although if your stay is short you may not want to!! The beach at the bay is lovely and a golf cart can take you down with a quick call to the butler service. If you plan to go down I recommend giving around 15 minutes notice so you aren't waiting for long. My one final recommendation is having the breakfast in the morning served at your villa. It's adorable and romantic!

author: AlexandraS457
title: A slice of heaven in West Koh Samui
text: The Four Seasons resorts like to pick out-of-the-way locations and this is what they have done with their Koh Samui location, which is in the Western, less-developed part of the island. As such, the resort has only a small beach surrounded by rocks: this makes for a dramatic scenery but is in contrast to the long beaches found elsewhere on the island. Because it is private, hotel staff constantly clean the shore to remove algae and any rubbish which is washed ashore (a bit of a weird sight I have to say). But you are guaranteed a pristine stretch of sand and Gulf of Thailand water. The resort is located on a very steep hillside. You check-in about 250 meters above the beach I mentioned and are then ferried to your villa in a golf cart and it is a vertiginous ride! As always with the Four Seasons, the environment is amazing to behold: luxuriant and yet perfectly tended vegetation surround you and all the villas are nestled among this tame jungle. No one walks there as the path is simply too steep and the heat too strong. Villas are superbly appointed. The decor, Turquoise-based with teak wood and carved beige stone, is magnificent and full of all the amenities you could dream of: shampoo, conditioner, shower gel of course but also toothbrush and toothpaste, after-sun gel, mouthwash and a shaving kit. The bed comes with a mosquito net and you need to be ready to use it as such dense jungle tends to foster mosquito growth. At times, it is difficult to be outside if you're not close to the beach as this is the only place they avoid. We got bitten a lot and noticed many other guests with the telltale red dots on their skin. Many villas come with a private pool and that this the height of luxury but it comes at a price. In fact, price is the one thing which is not easy at the Four Seasons where staff will go to great length to make you happy. It might therefore make sense to save the Four Seasons for a honeymoon or some sort of special occasion. But it is wonderful and well worth it.

author: travplaces
title: Incredible experience despite a hiccup
text: We have just returned from a 3 night stay at this hotel and I have to share our wonderful experience. We arrived from the Four Seasons in Chiang Mai and were quite sure nothing could match that experience but we were wrong. From the outset this place is also outstanding. You are welcomed with the ring of a bell and double doors open up to an open air reception and the most expansive and beautiful sea views I have ever seen. From there we were taken to our private pool villa which was secluded and lovely. The room amenities are top notch and the bed is so comfortable. Our first afternoon was great. We took the kayaks out and kayaked to the far end of the beach where it was private and beautiful. I highly recommend this, it gave you a clear idea of how special this location is. Here is the hiccup...I got severely ill the fist night there, so sick that my husband called the front desk and was going to take me to the hospital. We are not sure what it was but suffice it to say when hotel management found out about it the next morning they were all over it. They spoke with my husband and assured him that they would do anything we needed to make our stay comfortable and to help me in my quest to get better. They delivered black tea with ginger to my room immediately and asked my husband to call them and let them know how I was doing. l was not able to make it out of the room until late in the afternoon but when I did, Melville the food and beverage service manager seemed to know where I was at all times. He showed up at the beach with coconut water and fresh watermelon and took the time to speak with us and guarantee us that they were there to take care of us and his sincerity was evident. Everywhere we went the staff knew that I was not feeling well and did their best to make an unpleasant situation better. They took care of me everywhere. When I tried to eat and it was clear i was not able to, the hotel did not charge us for our meal. This type of treatment continued until the end of our stay I can't say enough about the experience. The entire staff was outstanding, but Melville and Nicholas in the dining area and Gabrielle in the spa were outstanding I am a person that does not like to revisit places I have been because there is so much of the world to see, but I can honestly say I would love to revisit The Four Seasons Koh Samui and I hope i am able to soon.

author: Pawnstar
title: Probably the best in Ko Samui
text: a slice of heaven on the north-western tip of the island. away from the most crowded parts but close enough to go out for meals. one rainy day we rented a car and drove around the island, stopping off to check out numerous other resorts including W, Banyan Tree and Nepasai. I can safely say Four Seasons is the best property, by far. Returning to the quiet luxury after a day out among the noise and hustle is wonderful. The private beach is superb - exclusive, clean, great service, although the sea can get rather rough on windy days. I'd love the pool to be a touch larger though. the villas are very well set out, with maximum privacy. you don't really see other villas around you. bathroom is extremely generous in size and we loved the free standing egg shaped bath tub and the fully openable glass doors so you can take a bath semi-open air. only two restaurants, one beach side and one next to concierge which serves decent thai fare. kind of limited so you probably want to eat out a few nights. kids menu food can improve somewhat - the mac n cheese was particularly poor (all cream no cheese). breakfast was great though with lots of healthy and not-so-healthy choices. nice range of fresh pastries with some creative touches. overall i would strongly recommend this resort, with the only proviso being you have to take golf carts everywhere because it's located on a rather steep hillside.

author: Heavenonearth65
title: THIS MUST BE HEAVEN
text: We are at a loss to understand how the Four Season's can rank 4th in terms of hotels on Koh Samui! We travel extensively and this is heaven on earth! The experience begins with the check-in process. You are welcomed in an open air hilltop building with astounding views of the resort and the water beyond. Everyone you encounter is warm, engaging and accommodating. Do not worry about the location of your villa. All have breathtaking views and allow for a tremendous amount of privacy. The beach and pool are secluded, quiet and allow for the perfect balance of sun and shade. Do not try and move your own beach chair! At least 3 people will come running to do it for you. Be sure to reserve a table for the Castaway dinner. You will dine at a private moonlight lit table in a secluded cove. Do not miss the spa. One of the best experiences of the entire trip. Finally, hats off to the resort manager. She was warm, engaging and continually asking if there was anything they could do to make things better. The answer was no. Everything was perfect.

author: WinePleaze
title: The Residences - Simply Astounding!!!!!
text: After staying last year and describing The Four Seasons as the best Resort I have ever experienced, we ventured back for another all too short stay. This time, our experience can best be described as mind altering. We upgraded to one of the Residences that had visually teased us when dining in the main restaurant last year. Well, my god, this is truly a bucket list experience. Your villa, is complete and I mean complete with everything you could need because, in residence, is your own personal Butler. We quickly forgot everything else in the world, absorbed in the true, effortless style of luxury that is Four Seasons. The restaurants with sublime food and suburb service could not tempt us away this time. Our Butler, Khun Pae, was a superstar and quickly infused our daily habits. She picked up on our style and would join in chats and then quickly retreat to bring some snacks or top up our wine. She catered all meals and maintained a curated mini bar of our favourites. She even learned that we liked a chilled Limoncello, always keeping 2 glasses in the freezer. Everything is a wow factor, and all just happens so easily. The Residences are huge and come in various configurations from 2 - 5 bedrooms I think, so even large families could be accommodated and I suspect you would have more than the one Butler! I just cannot pick anything negative. Knowing that these kind of places exist around the world is very motivating, I NEED MORE. Thank you to the GM Lubosh and the team for such a special experience.

author: Samuels66
title: Lunch was Excellent
text: What a fabulous setting. You arrive and are invited to enjoy the amazing vista. Just in the reception area you are surrounded by beautiful design features whereby everything around you has been crafted to exude opulence. The staff were professional and personable. There are two restaurants. One set high, against the cliff overlooking the bay and the other on the beach. After perusing the menu’s whilst enjoying the amazing view, we chose to eat lunch at the beach restaurant; at which point we enjoyed a scenic decent down to our chosen venue, courtesy of a golf buggy. The beach restaurant was very tasteful and the staff welcoming with witty personality. I ordered sea bass cooked in a banana leaf which was cooked to perfection and my husband, who ordered a burger could not find fault. Meaty, juicy and cooked just as he had requested. His only comment to add, was why were the beer glasses not chilled? If I am to name any negative comment, it was on the mosquito’s, who were lunching on us whilst we were lunching. However, a waitress did come to our rescue and really, it’s unfair to blame mother nature on our intrusion. However, I would also comment, please stop inserting a service charge and tax in the footer at the end of the page. Please include this in the overall price and then everything is plainly transparent. It seems very old fashioned. It’s just annoying, just name the price. Very enjoyable and a memorable experience.

author: JohnMLeeLondon
title: Simply the best
text: It starts and ends with the view. You walk in to this strange little hut perched on top of the Four Seasons estate - the views were idyllic and breathtaking. Then you get whisked off through a network of buggy tracks to your secluded villa. The landscape is such that you can be quite close to another villa but not be able to see them through the coconut trees. The rooms are great (particularly the signature four seasons bed – slept like a baby despite the jet-lag). The service is unparalleled – everyone is so kind and nothing was too much. Perfect example - ‘P’, on the concierge team, spent 45 minutes walking me through the different types of Thai street food. For me, this place was just what the doctor ordered - total relaxation and rest. With its perfect beach, great activities, I just can’t wait to go back. It felt like a boutique resort but had all the services you need to keep in touch and keep other aspects of life going. Comparing to other hotels on the Island: I went to the W hotel. Whilst it is a great hotel it could be anywhere in the world. I liked the younger, European vibe but only for a night. Same applies to Nikki Beach – great for a day probably don’t want to stay there for the whole holiday. Intercontinental and Conrad looked good – but still would not tempt me to leave the Four Seasons when I go again. Who should go: Perfect for honneymooners, families on a relaxed holiday, and well everyone who wants some downtime. The views, the service, the rooms, the food..... all outstanding. My new favourite hotel.

author: peekyboo
title: Only for peace
text: I am usually staying in hotels and this was the 1st time I was in a resort. It was our first time in KS,the weather was very hot the first day we were there.I had booked a van for 4 of us from the hotel transfer and when we came out of the hotel, there was the van waiting for us.The driver addressed my kids with names, something that had prepared for before.My kids were very excited.The resort is about 20 mins away from the hotel.When we reached the resort, the arrival hall,it had an excellant view of all the villas on the side and the beautiful sea.Welcome drinks were given, and the resort manager was very friendly.We were whisked away in a buggy to our villa, a 1 bedroom pool villa.It was clean and lovely.Pillows are too soft. First thing we noticed was there was no one on our left & right villas. It seemed that the occupancy wasnt much as throughout our 4 nights there,You cant move around without getting the buggy.The whole resort is very clean. There are only 2 restaurants there,Pla Pla by the beach and Lan Tania,near the concierge.Breakfast buffet was 700 BHT, without eggs,waffles,pancakes,If you want all these, it will be 1050BHT. I was very dissapointed that we have to pay for eggs and the breakfast buffet was limited. There were 2-3 types of doughnuts,some variety of breads,some cold meat, fruits, fresh milk,cereals, and 1 type of muffin.All the days ,it was the same stuff. The desserts are not so nice. Chaweng was 30mins away. We felt sort of trapped in the resort due to the limited choice of food.I Room service takes at least 30 mins,Housekeeping is fast.Aircon wasnt working so we had changed to another villa, Deluxe villa. The pool is longer & the room is smaller.There is no iron and ironing board in the room, so you have to ask for one, They can also provide you with universal adapters.The library had very old books.Kids club also seemed boring as there were no kids. Every staff you meet greets you with a smile.Service is very good here. At the beach,there are only non motorised sports and the beach is closed at 6pm.We only did kayaking.Beach has lots of rocks.I wouldnt recommend this resort if you have little kids, they would get bored.We went to Big Buddha but there is nothing there ,you can only see the statue and nothing else.Its not like the temples in Bangkok.We went for elephant trekking ,my kids enjoyed the thought of having a ride on them. The mahoots will take you for a short ride and back.Its not really a jungle. Our driver recommended Centara Grand.Maybe we will try next time.On the way to Big Buddha, there was KFC,lots of shops,Starbucks. Overall,I feel that Koh Samui,is only for those who need some quietness.I dont think I will be back here,Its like Bintan Number 2.I would rather prefer Langkawi. So if you have kids, I would rather you choose elsewhere.Weather wise, the first day it was very very hot.Next day was heavy rain, and the 3rd day was cloudy.Also, do take the taxis as they are spacious too and only charge 800BHT to the airport.

author: Ausfamily4
title: Met every expectation and then some
text: We just got back from staying at this wonderful resort and wish we were still there. The service is outstanding and if you're after a luxurious stay away from the hustle and bustle of Chaweng beach with it's shopping and markets which is only 30 minutes away by taxi (which the hotel can provide at a fair cost), this is it. The staff are so genuinely warm and go out of their way to meet every need you might have. From bringing you iced water, sorbets and refreshing towels and fruit treats while lounging on your deck chair by the beach to delicious food in each of their restaurants. We travelled with another family and each have two children under 9. The children are catered for with a fabulous kids club and other activities on the beach which our kids thoroughly enjoyed. From ping pong to soccer (football) and beach volley ball on the beach there's something for everyone. Our fondest memory is watching our son (7) playing a game of soccer (football) with people from Germany, Australia, Hong Kong and USA from 3 to 60 years of age together with Four Seasons staff. Just beautiful to see. The beach staff (Zak) even organised a Ping Pong tournament complete with trophy after my husband challenged everyone including Four Seasons Staff to a match. The luxurious day spa for all you ladies or men out there who enjoy a massage or a facial is a must. They even provide foot massages or mini mani's and pedi's on the beach on certain days. Thank-you Charles (Manager) for the luxurious and relaxing stay we had, we can't wait to come back and visit other Four Seasons Resorts of which we are now loyal fans!! Well done Charles, the kindness and genuine hospitality we experienced at this resort is unlike anything we have experienced anywhere else. Visit this place, the only thing you might regret is you didn't book it for long enough!

author: Vicandchai
title: Superb surroundings but restaurant disappointed
text: My partner and I decided to have my birthday dinner at the Lanteria restaurant last night (on the hill, not on the beach). We were very impressed with the high level of service from all the staff we that came into contact with. I have to say that the food quality was not so impressive. My starter was fine but my partner chose the pomello salad, which was blindingly spicy. My partner is Thai and has 8 chilli som tum salads, so when he says it was too hot...... My main course was beef massaman curry, which tasted rather over seasoned and the beef had a rather curious glutinous consistency and odd odor. I am sure it was beef cheek, which would account for the odd texture. My partner had the red duck curry, which he said was tasty but questioned the freshness of the duck. The staff were superb and presented me with a birthday chocolate bomb and even sang happy birthday to me! I ordered a frozen chocolate mousse tart, which was the oddest chocolate mousse tart I have ever eaten and again, had a 'stale' taste to it. We did not finish our main courses and were not questioned as to why. I also left most of my dessert, except the ice cream. Finished my meal with a perfect cappuccino. We then went down to the beach bar for a couple of drinks before heading home. As previously mentioned, an excellent resort in stunning surroundings with the best staff I have encountered in my 8 years on this island. You could see how happy and proud they were to be working at the Four Seasons. Has it put me off returning? No, but I think I would opt for the Italian menu on our next visit.

author: Anjuaradhya
title: Exquisite Rooms!
text: We celebrated our First Year Wedding Anniversary at The Four Seasons, Koh Samui, Thailand. Getting there, if you are driving there yourself can be a little tricky! You can easily miss the hotel name board! However, once you walk into the Hotel, from the Shiv Ling (Lord Shiva's idol) in the center of the landing to the vast expanse of the ocean beyond, you start feeling the excitement build up to start your 'second' honeymoon there! Food is FANTASTIC! Service, due to the long distances can be very slow! Rooms have a breath taking view of the ocean, with a plunge pool and a superb bathroom, planned for every convenience of the guests! Definitely recommend kayaking with your mate/partner/love!
