It is so much fun! But yes, do be careful in low tide as you can get easily stuck in the shallow waters. Enjoy lazing on the beach with extremely friendly service from the bar! Enjoy the evening at the bar again! They have a fantastically romantic setting with blue lights, sound of the ocean and lite Thai music! And do NOT forget to order the Thai Style Fried Rice! It is yummilicious! Spa - well, if you have the budget, it is great! But I think Thai massage can be a LOT cheaper and a LOT better than what they offered at their spa!

author: banjogo
title: Best weekend away after 13 years
text: I'm flying back to the states - writing this in Japan's United Club and quite biased coming off an incredible weekend at the Four Seasons Resort - Koh Samui in Thailand. My wife and I had a week of work in Bangkok, had to get away. We were actually looking at Phuket or Krabi, but flights didn't match up. We ended up going to Koh Samui and I think God had a plan for that one. If you're able - you need to choose this resort over any others. It's pricey, sure - but worth it. I'm now convinced on the experience of what you spend. We had a private pool, everyone knew our name, the food incredible, and didn't have to question a think. I always think people should get what we got - which was a drive in/out ride to the resort that included breakfast. Anytime I'm in a different country, I like to know my wife is safe - and they insured it... You just can't beat the service of the Four Seasons, everyone knows your name, knows the package you're on, knows where you need to be, takes care of every need. I think we've been at a Four Seasons a dozen+ times, and I'm now overly loyal due to the experience I had in Koh Samui. It will hurt my wallet maybe, but in the end I know it's worth it. When I left my bags with a bellman/buggy guy - I realized I really trust every employee at this Four Seasons. Thanks to Melville, Jose, Chai, Joy, and all the other incredible staff involved there.

author: WinePleaze
title: Don't hesitate, it's simply amazing!
text: Don't be too concerned by some of the petty comments you read on TripAdvisor, this is quite possibly the best Resort experience I have ever had. My Wife and I stayed with our toddler for 4 nights in November and we still suffer from having to leave. It truly is such an exceptional experience as Four Seasons are the masters of the "less is more" philosophy. The Rooms are spacious, elegant, thoughtfully appointed and uncluttered which I love, with views to die for. Service is exceptionally good and we were very impressed at how attuned they were to the family traveler. We were cautious at first because we did not want our little one to have a negative effect on others but the staff were just fabulous with him and he had a blast. We don't usually expect much from Kid's menus because they are loaded with fried food but we were truly impressed at how we could basically order him anything as a kids dish and it was provided without fuss. Food is superb, we ate every meal in the resort and from what I gather, their new Spanish Executive Chef has made quite an impact with new menus, again, simple dishes executed with a lightness of touch that elevates the food to a very high standard. Breakfast is sublime, its not a huge selection, again its the less is more approach but there is detail in everything and I dare you to try and eat just one almond croissant. Behind there curtain there must be one hell of a pastry team because they are producing world class pastries. To be expected, its more expensive that eating on the street but I have to laugh when people complain about pricing in such a resort, its akin to buying a Bentley then complaining about the cost of the tyres, its not the place to go and then expect everything to be free. Be aware that the resort is built on some very steep terrain and unless you like a hike from point to pint, you will be reliant on the buggy service. It did not seem to be too busy when we stayed and reading the reviews prior we would plan ahead and call for a buggy, but after the first few times, we learned that you basically call, collect your things, lock the door and by the time you have walked to the road, the buggy is there. Its effortless but you have just have to factor this in to your stay. Its worth every last cent they charge and I would go back in a heartbeat.

author: VickiM968
title: Four Seasons, Koh Samui, Absolute Paradise!
text: My husband and good friends recently decided to stay at Four Seasons, Samui to celebrate my 50th b-day. We wanted to go somewhere we had never been and somewhere special. WOW, we got a lot more than we bargained for. Upon arrival, we were greeted with lemon scented cool hand towels, welcome drinks and a view like I have never seen, absolutely stunning! A view of the entire Island, from the beach to the mountain tops, breath taking. We were then taken to our room, a Pool Villa with yet another beautiful view. The room was more than spacious, decorated to match the surroundings and the bathroom...I never wanted to leave! We then went down to the beach for cocktails and bubbles, to toast my special day. The staff and chef were at our disposal and we couldn't have asked for more. The following morning, we sat outside to partake of the buffet. A gentle breeze, an almost 180 degree view of the island, topped off with another glass or two of bubbly, made for one of my favorite memories of the weekend, however it's hard to pick just one! Deciding to join other hotel guest in the pool area, we had our own little piece of heaven, followed by another great meal. After lazing the day away, we made our way to our rooms to get ready for a 5-Star meal, being prepared by a Michellin star chef, Indian fusion as I have never tasted, words can't describe it. The icing on the cake regarding the entire weekend, the attentive staff. They were amazing and made the weekend one I will never forget. I hope that if I'm a lucky girl, I will be able to stay at this resort another time, hopefully someday soon!

author: hoonoo
title: What an incredible weekend!
text: From the moment we arrived it was fabulous. I've never been in a better reception 'room'. No walls, on top of a mountain with views of both sides of the island. Seamless service abounds. The property consists of individual villas nestled within the jungle. Though the room is worthy of description the bathroom is the real luxury. A tub with a view of the ocean and overlooking your own private pool. The first night there we experienced magic. We met our friends on the beach at sunset; champagne, appetizers and a fire dancer for our pleasure. Then dinner on the beach after the chef came to greet us. Wonderful food, beautiful view, great friends made our first night just about perfect. Breakfast the next morning was incredible. We sat on the deck with a view of the outlying islands and the jungle below as we enjoyed the buffet that included everything you'd ever want, I think we stayed for 2 hours, probably because of the bottle of champagne we needed. A wonderful day on the beach included a nap in the hammock being served cool towels and peach iced tea. Lovely. The second night we were there we had a real treat. A Michellin star visiting chef was on the property and we sat at a table for 24 and ate the most delicious gourmet dinner with just the hint of Indian flavoring. A treat that could never be duplicated! This was an incredible weekend.

author: jvcs112
title: HEAVEN
text: This place is heaven. The minute u walk in to check-in you're greeted with a welcome drink, and super friendly staff. Then a little golf cart, "buggy" they call it, drives u down to your villa. The bed there, is seriously, no joke, the most comfortable bed in the entire world, it totally moulds to your body. The staff will give u a tour of ur room, showing u also that there's already a bath ran and ready for you with rose petals in there. Food here is OUT of this world. Recommendations: Thai beef salad, red curry with duck, prawn cakes, fresh coconut, mango with sticky rice dessert. And by the beach: DEFINITELY the beef wrap, it is SO good. The beach is super nice, the staff at the beach is incredible, they feed u like every hour almost, from fruits to roasted corn and sweet potato, to coconut flavored popsicles, or thai ice-tea flavor, to setting up a little fire on the beach with a pot dangling on top with chocolate melted inside to make smores, they have these nice marshmallows and biscuits. Then at some point during the day they will have complimentary head and neck massage on the beach, it's like 5mins, but still super nice. Activities are: catamaran sailing, kayaking, football, volleyball, a box FULL of toy u can play with on the beach, a ping pong table. And they have a set itinerary for each day of the week ie. cooking class, movie under the stars, bbq on the beach on sunday nights, yoga on the beach, etc. And they can also organize day trips out to do stuff like elephant trekking, zip-lining etc. It's a MUST GO, I can't wait to go with my guy again.

author: DianeB282
title: Absolute heaven.
text: Hubby and I stayed at Four Seasons Koh Samui for 6 nights of bliss and perfection. The villas were absolutely perfect with excellent views of the ocean and tree tops. Very private. The infinity pool was a delight to swim in every day overlooking the great view. The staff were more than helpful and nothing was too much to ask, everyone of them remembered our name from the minute we got there - it was as if we were the only ones in the resort. There are buggys that take you anywhere you want on the resort as it does become too hard to walk up after a day chilling on the beach! They are always on hand and seem to magically appear so no waiting at any time. Melville John the food director was superb. We upgraded to full food package so we could sample the delights the restaurants had to offer without counting the dollars. Everything was always perfect and fantastic food and service. Only once was there a tiny error - mainly on our part, but Melvillle John rectified immediately followed up by a courtesy small gift of chocolates - absolutely unnecessary but this is the kind of treatment you get here. The food package worked out at approx 50 GBP per person per day - but SO worth it. Drinks are expensive and wine ridiculously expensive, but the whole atmosphere is so good you don;t need a lot of wine! The small private beach is exquisite and no one there only the guests. If you want hustle and bustle and bars, forget this resort as it is not near anywhere like that - a 20 min drive to Fisherman, but we got exactly what we went for - a peaceful part of heaven and felt completely well looked after and rested. Perfection on a stick. Will definitely return as nothing compares to this hotel for luxury.

author: Liuyihao
title: Will surely return
text: This review is long overdue as we stayed in the resort last December, but it's not fair to FS if we don't share the amazing experience we had there. The resort is STUNNING, this is the first FS resort that we "wow" on arrival. We got there late at night, the view of the resort from the reception was breath-taking. The reception is located on the top of the hill, with villas and varous facilities spreading along the hilll all the way down to the breach. The buggy ride down to the villa after check-in was a bit scary (to me only, my husband loved it) coz it's like 60-degree slope. The villa was beautifully and thoughtfully done - rose peddle bath was prepared and our daughter's name was put on the side of the bath tub. Huge curtains can be drawn around the patio so that there's absolute privacy. Diffrent fresh fruits were offered each day, and the villa was spotlessly clean all the time. The main restaurant is amazing, like a bird's nest elevated on the hill side with stunning view of the sea and the mountain. The staffs were nice, all of them remembered our daughter's name the next day and offered to look after her while we eat. Food (breakfast, lunch and dinner) was yummy, best Thai food we've eaten. We spent a lot of the time at the beach (FS has its own private beach). Free popsicles made of fruits grown in the resort were offered all the time, and we can see the staff from Kids at All Seasons playing with the kids on the beach all the time. On thing we are particularly grateful is the service. Shortly after our arrival, we realised that we took someone else's luggage (identical Samsonite suitcases), a bit of nightmare in the middle of the night and with a 2-year old. The resort gave us free changing clothes and toiletries, arranged people to go to the airport and checking with every single hotel in Koh Samui that night. The next morning when we got up, we were informed that our luggages were found and are on their way to the resort! To summarize: this place is beautiful, the size of the resort and quality of service are so good, that you can either be couples seeking for romance with great privacy or family with kids looking for relaxing breaks. We definitely would love to come back.

author: El_Mudo_11
title: Gorgeous but missing a few Four Seasons standards
text: Great and gorgeous hotel. The views are stunning and the rooms are beautifully appointed. Beach is gorgeous. Staff was lovely. Of course when you pay 700+/night and stay at Four Seasons you expect certain standards and a few were off here: --Food was good. Not excellent. --Service in restaurant in the evening was extremely slow. --System of "buggies" to get from room up to where breakfast is served--which one can walk but can be either inconvenient or difficult depending on where your room is located--does not yet seem to be spot-on. You call for one, it can take up to 30 minutes to arrive or does not arrive. --There were some guests staying at one of the houses on the property. It was more than obvious that when they were in the "public" spaces the management set out to speak to them, make sure they were OK, etc. They did not do this for the other guests. A little off-putting. The other parts of the hotel were lovely. There is a very clean and nice gym, the breakfasts were excellent and the beach, as mentioned before, is captivating. The best massage I have ever received was here. Excellent spa.

author: StevenC1234
title: Stop looking for paradise, this is it!
text: The Four Seasons Koh Samui is one of the most amazing places I've been to. My girlfriend and I decided to plan our vacation by visiting Thailand and fortunately for us the Four Seasons has four amazing hotels in this beautiful country. We also visited the Bangkok and Chiang Rai tented camps properties, both equally as spectacular. Once we arrived at the resort we immediately knew we were in paradise, the welcome reception is situated at the top of the cliff overlooking the bay in an open roof setting. We were then escorted over to our villa by the very kind front desk agent and bellman who made sure that all our needs were met before leaving us. The location of the villas are ideal giving you all the privacy you want when you're on vacation. The room was stunning and the most comfortable i've ever stayed at, everything you need is there and housekeeping service was always on point. The plunge pool was great to relax in and the temperature of the water was ideal for a hot summer day. What can I say about the food? Everything we ate was amazing and the care and attention from the service staff made each meal memorable. I highly recommend getting a table on the deck with views overlooking the bay and the rest of the resort, this will surely take your breath away. We can't stop raving about the food and had a very romantic dinner at their restaurant Pla Pla, I highly recommend the tasting menu they offered, a northern and southern Thai menu allowing you to taste a little bit of everything Thai food has to offer. The beach is ideal and much more relaxing than the crowded beaches located on the rest of the island, the privacy allows you to unwind and feel like you're on a deserted island with five star service. It was truly amazing seeing the care and kindness shown by the entire staff, from the hotel manager to the security staff, everyone always went out of their way to assists us in making sure that we had an amazing experience. Nang one of the bellman noticed that my girlfriend was getting a couple of mosquito bites and went out of his way to get her some anti-ich cream without even asking for it, this is just one of the examples we have about the outstanding service we received. Also, the buggy service to take you around the grounds of the resort was always so accommodating and showed up even before we asked for it, not sure how they did it but they always knew where to be when we needed a ride. We've been blessed to have traveled to many beautiful places around the world but this was the most memorable trip we have ever had and can't wait to return one day!

author: mamamo
title: Beautiful property but major management issues.
text: Four Seasons Koh Samui is a beautiful property. There is no doubt about that. The problem is that it is seriously lacking in management. Suprsing as this is a four seasons property. Service was a problem, but it was not the fault of the wonderful Thai people. The staff were clearly lacking leadership and guidance. Four Seasons is not doing a good job in bringing over their management expertise. The lobby restaurant was chaotic at dinner. Reservations were muddled. Orders were delayed. It took too long for cocktails to arrive, The staff were confused and seemed overworked. Food was good but even considering the usual premium one would expect at four seasons it was just way too overpriced considering the overall experience. Room service was slow, and it could take up to 10 mins for the buggy pick up to arrive (which is too long) The beach and adjacent pool area and bar is very nice (although the beach itself is nothing special in terms of sand and water quality) The villas are beautiful but the resort has made a major design error in the layout, there is practically no sun shine on most of the villa pool areas, so if you plan to sun bathe in the privacy of your villa, forget it. Spa is nice, but nothing special compared to other 5 start resorts in Thailand and you have to do a lot of walking to reach your spa villa from the spa lobby (which in my opinon kind of sucks) Overall the four seasons koh samui is gorgeous but management has a lot of work to do to get the service and operations up to international 6 star standards which is what they are charging for and what one is expecting.. next time we will check out the SIX SENSES

author: mrbompa
title: Four Seasons Koh Samui blows away any other Four Seasons Resort
text: Yes I said it this resort is amazing and trumps what I always thought was the best one (Hualalai). Right off the bat you know that this hotel is something special from when you arrive and see the view from the reception area at the top of the hill overlooking the resort. From this point on the resort is nothing but magic. The hospitality by the staff reminds me of what Hualalai was about 5 years ago before that location seems to have gotten snootier than the guest that go there. The manager Alex and Brent go above and beyond to make sure that you feel like the only person staying at the resort even when the hotel was at capacity during the Holidays. Within 2 days everyone at the hotel knew our name and always had that wonderful Thai smile when they greeted us. The spa is great and the walk to the rooms will blow you away while walking through the jungle. The beach was as clean as could be. Honestly people were sweeping the sand. I have never seen that in my life but I guess that is what you get when you stay at this hotel. The rooms I could live in one of them for the rest of my life and I would be more than happy. Now the downsides. I must say that really the only thing that was a negative was the plunge pool which I am sure when you look at any photos is the clincher for staying at this hotel. Every room has there own infinity pool that overlooks the gulf. Although the pool and deck are great the downside is there are no heaters for these pools. So if the sun does not heat it up they are very very cold. We actually swam maybe one lap then got out and never went back in it again. Also we could not find a jacuzzi anywhere on the property which I thought was sort of odd but such is life. All and all if you are going to Thailand you must stay at this hotel. I would take the 18 hour flight any day of the week to go back.

author: Mohi412
title: Exceptional location!
text: Having been to Koh Samui three years ago and having stayed at a hotel considered to be the top on the island then, I had my doubts about Four Seasons whether it would have managed to suprass it. Also, having had a so-so impression of the island then, (too many mosquitos, stink of sewage in the towns), we were rather off-put by the idea of Samui. But, being strict Four Seasons followers (for media purposes), we went exclusively for the hotel alone. Not only did it change our view of the island, as the location is probaly the best there could be, on an amazing densly vegatated hill, going down all the way to a private beach. The welcoming is on a wooden platform, vistually hanging off the top of the cliff into the trees below, providing breathtaking views of the Four Seasons residences to the left, and the rest of it's villas down below. The pathways leading to the villas are beautifully done, full of flora and fauna of the island (we've been told Four Sesons actually planted many of them!). The villas are done in the stylish interiors of the Four Seasons which is plenty of local wood, combined with glass, marble, and lovely linens. Lovely touches such as complimentary baked teddy bears for our kids made a difference! Also, a wooden low fence was actually screwed on the wooden deck outside the vllla to protect the children from falling off in the private pool. This is the first time we actually see this measure of protection in a private pool. The staff is excellent, throughout, but the best among all are the beach staff who actually took over our kids upon our arrival there, and got to show them fantastic games such as crab-catching and cooking mash mallows on an open barbeque on the sand. The approach of the Thais towards children has left us amazed. Never, in any country have we encountred such kids' loving people. The only minus, would be the options for dining within the hotel, as there are only two restaurants, and as there weren't many children there, we sometimes felt that couples might be annoyed at seeing two young ones near them in a quiet enviroment. The hotel claims to be child-friendly, and they were, but during dining times we felt awkard due to the two restaurants being mainly booked up by couples. The beach has a quiet zone too, which allows guests to enjoy their peace and quiet and that's appreciated when you pay such rates per night, to be entitled to relaxation. Mini compimentary massages on the beach are e great way to add some bliss and to entice one towards the Spa for more! The spa is also beautifully built, in the dense vegatation and the Thai masage I had was very good. Yes, I would rate this hotel as the top in Samui and by far suprassing it's predececors.

author: hoyasaxa00
title: Great Stay...
text: The four seasons is probably the prettiest hotel on the island. We traveled to Koh Samui for spring break with our two kids in march and absolutely loved it. The Four Seasons is a bit of a drive to town , but we rented a car and had not trouble finding our way around. You can drive around the island in few hours. There's really nothing bad to say about the hotel. If you are beach people, like us, you might be disappointed b/c the beach here is small and appears to be manmade. Everything else was spectacular so we overlooked that and we are absolute beach people. We drove to the other beaches on the island every day - didn't mind. The staff was fabulous of course. They brought fruit and popsicles to the beach every afternoon for guest to enjoy. The food was expensive, but not as bad as some reviews made it out to be. We really were expecting the worse, but it wasn't any more expensive than any other hotel we've been to. They also have a kids menu and everything was under $10. Kids club was free during the day and babysitting worked out to be about $15 p/h for both our kids. Would love to go back!

author: MWC
title: Good rooms, but no sun and overpriced
text: We stayed for 7 nights and didn't enjoy it at all. The rooms are really good, spacious and well equipped with a lovely bathroom with a quality bathtub facing out over the sea. The big downside is that the resort is north facing, so the sun comes up behind you and passes around the back of the villa before setting behind the hills at around 4.00. We got sun on the deck for about 45 minutes a day and even then you had to position yourself right on the edge of the deck to catch it. As a consequence the pool was a lot cooler than you would expect in a hot country. In fact the sea was warmest, followed by the pool on the beach and in last place was our pool. You also have to chase the sun on the beach as there are a lot of trees down there. We did take a canoe out to get a better view of the whole place and see if any of the villas got a better dose of sunshine, but with the exception of one or two of the really big ones they were all about the same. We only ate there only once and that was at the beachside restaurant on the first night, the food was fine but eye wateringly expensive - 2 simple main courses (a Thai curry and a risotto) with a (cheap) bottle of wine was £130. We did get an invitation to a beach barbie, but at £70 per head for food only we declined. Having just come from the Mandarin Oriental in Bankok (better service, reasonable prices) we really felt that we were being ripped off here. Generally the service was ok, a bit hit and miss though. We had breakfast in the hotel each day and sometimes your plates were cleared just after you finished, or before you had or never. We didn't have any goodies left in our room at night and it was a bit of a lottery as to how many tea bags we would have in the mini bar each day! We walked all around the resort and didn't find the hills too taxing. You do need a buggy if you are leaving the hotel and these came very soon after ordering. We hired a car and went out each day to find deserted sunny beaches and most evenings to eat at a number of really good restaurants around the island. We were really disappointed with our stay at this hotel.

author: luxuryvoyage
title: amazing rooms
text: What I loved most about the hotel was their big, luxury rooms. We had room 802 quite close to the beach with a nice beach view, sunny location and a large pool. I noted that some rooms high above are in the middle of palms and seems to be quite dark so ask for a sunny room before check in. The secluded beach is small, private and with white sand. The pool behind the beach was hardly used by guests. While staying at the beach, the waiter brought regularly cold water and cold towls. We especially liked the comfy beach bar loungers in the late afternoon for a sundower drink while listening chillout music from the bar. As for the food: breakfast selection (buffet and à la carte) is good. We once had dinner (special thai evening) which was solala but horrible expensive. Prices for food, drinks,massage and other services are above the limit. It is just to much for what you get. As for the hotel grounds, everything is perfect, luxurious and beautifiul. Also the staff is perfect - four seasons style. One word about the location: the hotel is far away from everything, no chance for walking, you need a car. Still, driving at night is not for everybody so we stayed at the hotel in the evening which was a pitty regarding the selection of nice local restaurants. Over all, I recommend this hotel for having some relaxing beach days in luxury and pretty surrounding. But expect to spend a big amount of dollars for food, drinks, massage etc. in the hotel!!!

author: DSS-Bombay
title: Loved It! Loved it! Loved It!
text: All earlier reports were correct! You feel you are Royalty as soon as you enter the resort. Check in was smooth and efficient. The electric Powered Buggy's take you to your room, The view is astounding! – Not easy to walk around the resort so we used the buggy to go all over. When you see any employee, they are extra courteous and always fold their hands and bow their heads to greet you! The food is good - mainly had the breakfast and ordered room service! Prices are not too bad for the food, we expected to pay exorbitant prices, I felt they over charged for the soft drinks / coffee example: 2 cokes cost you as much as your main dish! They have an incredible lavazza coffee machine in each room (with complementary lavazza coffee ) My Wife went for several massages and loved it - though again steep for Thailand standards. The internet connection though not complementary was quite economical at around 700 Bhatt for 24 hours. Each room has a DVD player and IPod dock - just Perfect. The plunge pool and the Deck area were the perfect place to spend the whole day! I was wondering what I did not like during the 3 night stay: a) The lights in the room were not enough (Not bright enough for my taste) even though we got an additional lamp put in our room , I personally found the low lighting to be depressing (I know they have tried to create an atmosphere in the room but with dimmers the patrons should be allowed to increase Intensity of Lighting. I read somewhere recommended standards were 300 Lux in a living room - this was way lower b) The Weather - Well that's not really in the control of the Hotel! November is the Monsoon Season in Samui

author: epicureanadventurer
title: Best on the Island, great with children
text: The Four Seasons Koh Samui is only 18 months old and reading some of the early reviews had a few teething problems like most new properties.....however that is well behind them now and they are firing on all cylinders. We spent 12 days at the hotel with our two children ( age 5 and 2 respectively ) and enjoyed it immensely. The facilities are the best on the island and the staff are equally as good. We visited all the major hotels and resorts and the Four Seasons staff were by far the best.....nothing was to much trouble and everything happened seemlessly. The hotel is on a steep hillside but the 'buggies' can easily ferry you around if you don't want to walk.....the drivers are great. The villas are beautiful...large and well thought out, we were able to place the extra bed and baby cot in the changing area and that kept the bedroom free for us. The outside sala and private pool area works really well. The gardens around the villas are immaculate and full of cocnut and plam trees. While the beach is not a great swimming beach it is ideal with kids...the water is shallow and safe and the pool located at the beach is a good alternative if you want to swim. The 'Kids For All Seasons' club is very well done with interesting activities for the children on the beach in the morning and at the club in the afternoon. The only slight negative is the variety of food on offer. The breakfast has a great selection and the quality of a high standard. There are 2 restaurants or in villa dining as your other options. The food is not significantly different at the two restaurants ( one on the hill, fine dining is a pricey version of teh other ) . I realise they are trying to please everyone but i would have thought that Four Seasons would have made the fine dining room the best Thai restaurant on the island instead of a 'half and half' Thai and Italian mix. Anyway the quality of the food was generally good. The FS is a little out of the way but we liked that and hired a car for our stay.......it is a lovely feeling to arrive back to the FS after a day exploring. Overall one of the nicest resorts we have visited in Thailand, we will certainly be back !

author: NYC134
title: Stunning!!
text: My husband and I stayed at this property on the last 5 nights of our Honeymoon and I agree 110% with previous posts - this place it is amazing! From the breath taking cliff side check, the villas, the food, the service, the spa, the beach (i could go on for days) - everything was flawless! I will say we had one negative experience with the "snorkeling" here which entailed us hiking no less than 200 yards off the beach through the reef and treacherous rocks to find that the water was way too cloudy and there was nothing to see! I have no idea why they would encourage guests to go out there as we were left disappointed and had to trek back having seen nothing! We spoke to Alex the hotel's GM (who was extremely friendly and you could tell went out of his way to befriend the hotel guests) and he mentioned they are looking into permits to excavate a portion of the reef but until then - DONT try going out there! The beach is beautiful but as many others have posted you can't really swim here because the water is very shallow all day long. It was a negative but by no means a deal breaker! We ate at the Beach Bar several times, I highly recommend the duck quesadillas and dinner and breakfast at the upper restaurant was always solid. We did go off property to rent ATVs through ATV Samui and had a blast! If you are the adventurous type this is well worth the 45 minute drive to the other side of the island for the two hour off road adventure. Take bug spray - I did get bitten here but its to be expected in this type of climate. In closing I really have to wonder about the people that had a terrible time at this resort. Either it was a fluke experience or these people really must not know how to have fun or appreciate the beauty of nature! DO NOT let the negative reviews discourage you from booking a trip here. I worried briefly about the buggies but we never waited more than 5 minutes and they were part of the fun and gave you a chance to chat with the wonderful staff. This is a wonderful resort and we had the time of our lives!

author: DeniseBee
title: Absolutely fabulous!
text: I wholeheartedly agree with a previous review that stated the view at check-in took my breath away. I also have forgotten about any of the admin, signing in etc. my mind and eyes were soaking up that view. What a start to a great weekend. The residence my mother and I shared with my brother, his wife and her family was stunning. Typical local wooden architecture, airy and decorated to a very high standard, in-keeping with the relaxed style of a beach resort but with surprising touches of hi-tech (ipod docking station etc). We had three villas and the use of the main residence in the centre, large infinity pool with more fabulous views over the tree tops to the sea and beyond. In addition we received excellent service from all the staff especially Khun Fah & Khun Ratt our Maebaan's (maid/butler). What luxury having our breakfast cooked and laid out by the pool every morning, they were always at hand in an unobstrusive way. We found the buggy's such fun and no inconvenience whatsoever. Travelling to and fro in these made the holiday even more of an amazing experience. Must mention that bath. It rained one afternoon and that is the day that I experienced bathing in it. Shaped like a shell in marble - wow! Private yet looking over the treetops whilst lolling in the bath. I could have stayed at this resort much longer than the three days I had booked but unfortunately reality beckoned!

author: Justybusty
title: On top of their game!
text: My wife and I stayed in February and could not have been looked after better. The setting is spectacular and the beach is completely private and clean. We did not have any trouble finding a sun lounger to sit on as some other reviewers had experienced. The resort is spread over a large area of steep jungle clad hills which made the setting all the more special. To get to the beach we had to call a buggy but we found they always arrived quickly. The food and drinks were excellent and we especially enjoyed our leisurely lunches at the restaurant by the beach. We even bumped into some friends from home which was a surprise. The food especially was a high point for us. The rooms are huge and very well laid out with a generous bathroom. My wife especially enjoyed not having to share a sink. The iPod dock is a great touch. The private plunge pool is quite a treat. We both had a full body massage in the spa which was amazing. The only down side was my wife nearly died with laughter when she saw me wearing my spa pants - skimpy pants made of see-through tights material. Sorry - no photo. The management and staff were genuinely friendly and the service was efficient yet unobtrusive as you would expect at a Four Seasons Hotel. Overall, we had a brilliant time and we will definitely return one day.

author: voyageur69
title: Four Seasons - Koh Samui
text: The setting of the resort is beautiful. About 30 minutes from the airport to a remote part of the island. The property is VERY hilly. Be prepared with comfortable shoes and the rooms are not easy to get too. While the rooms are incredible and relaxing, there is a screaming whistle for a good part of the day for detracting the mosquitos. The pool is tiny and if you forget something in your room when you are at the pool, it is at least a 30 minute walk back to your room. The management presence is minimal. The GM is very picky about who he talks too and fake with most of the guests. If he thinks he can sell you a property, he will talk to you. The service is slow. While there is really no place to rush off too, it is a good thing. The first morning I waited 1 hour for eggs at breakfast. Everyday after was at least 30 minutes. For me, I would not recommend this property at all. There are too many downsides. I have stayed a many Four Seasons and this was my least favorite!

author: Davies72
title: Don't waste your money
text: This hotel while physically beautiful is so incompetently run as to be almost comical. To get room service for your villa, order ice or a buggy takes at least 2 telephone calls and a wait of almost an hour and even then it still sometimes never happens. Once your food arrives you wonder why you bothered. An open club sandwich consists of a piece of what seems to be fried bread, a poached egg, a slab of chicken breast with two pieces of bacon on top. It also had bowls of olive and pepper relish on the side and some reddish oily sauce swimming around on the plate. Don't ask for your duvet to be replaced by a blanket - surely a not unreasonable or unheard of request in the tropics- you will be left with only a bottom sheet and a scratchy acrylic blanket that is too small for the bed and no other sheets! It will then only take 3 telephone calls and about an hour and a half to get the bed made properly. Even if you eat in the restaurants the service is hit and miss. You can order things which are never served but they still end up on your bill. Forget about getting a lounge on the beach too. Alhough you can turn up first thing in the morning and see a row of about 10 unoccupied lounges they aren't available because they are "reserved". Guest who are on the beach are expected to just sit on the sand or perch on the hotels catamaran while empty lounges wait for some special mystery guests to turn up. Although the resort has only been opened for 11 months the furniture, decking and handrails in the common areas are all looking pretty beaten up and tired. Maybe you could forgive all this - after all it is the tropics, Thailand and they have only been open 11 months - but this is a Four Seasons resort and they are charging over US$1,300 a night. I have stayed in a number of Four Seasons properties all around the world. While they are always expensive they still offer value for money because the service you receive and the experience is normally outstanding but Koh Samui just doesn't come anywhere near the Four Seasons standard. My advice is don't waste your money. There are a lot of beautiful resorts in Asia find one that is properly run.

author: MinetteD
title: Matter of Preference
text: Our holiday at Four Seasons Koh Samui didn’t start so well… when we arrived at the airport, there was no one to receive us, so we had to walk around in the rain with our luggage to try and find our driver. Luckily we found him and the trip to the hotel went smoothly. We booked a one-bedroom villa with a view of the bay, but the villa we got only had a view of some treetops with hardly any sun over the pool area and hardly any privacy as the villa next to us looked right over our pool. We asked for a different villa and were shown two others. We decided to go for 802, which had a lovely view of the beach, the ocean, and another little island across the ocean. This villa however, had hardly any privacy. Getting around the hotel is very difficult; you have to ‘book’ a buggy at least 15 minutes in advance before you can go anywhere (even to the beach which isn’t far). The interior design of the rooms is utterly stunning - this place could be paradise when it’s done. Unfortunately there were still a lot of construction going on while we were there, so instead of listening to tropical birds singing while we relaxed on our daybed, we were forced to listen to hammers, saws and drills. We were supposed to spend 8 nights there, but ended up checking out after just 1 night – the noise was too much to handle. The manager was kind enough to offer us 50% off our final bill if we stayed the 8 nights, we still moved to another hotel as the noise was seriously unbearable. Since we were only there for one night we only had 3 meals there, the service was good and the staff were all very friendly. If you like being spontaneous on your holidays, then I wouldn’t recommend this hotel, even though the villas are beautiful, it does feel like you’re ‘stuck’ in it. When you make your booking, make sure you book the view that you’d prefer (unless you don’t mind looking at treetops and nothing else). Btw. The hotel that we moved is called Sila Evason - do have a look at it. We absolutely loved it. All in all, I'd say its about preference, what kind of holiday you like and what you do on your holiday. This hotel certainly didn't fulfill our needs.

author: RandB1805
title: Excellent out of cbd paradise
text: Santorini mesotopos We chose Mesotopos hotel from its wonderful photos online and distance from CBD. From the transfer from the airport they organised to arriving at the hotel. The staff here were amazing. The reception is open from 0830 to 2030. And is run by either the mum or the daughter. Both are such beautiful ladies and so happy and welcoming to help you with what ever requests you have. They organised boat tours. Massages and transfers for us. The rooms are very private with a small wooden staircase leading to your bed up stairs. With a amazing balconey with a table and 2 chairs. With 2 sun lounges on the side looking down on the pool area. The room is very large compared to many others we seen here. The room does not have kettle and iron facilities but easy to ask and they lend to you from reception. The swimming pool is beautiful maintained with crystal clear waters and is so private to relax in and arround from chairs to lounge beds. As this place is only 3.5km from Fira CBD we hired a scooter and was easy to go in and out. Over all this hotel is bloody brillant in every way. I couldnt recomend staying here any higher from the location to the resort it self. A true please to be welcomed into their family for our stay here. Was sad to leave as we felt part of there family here.

author: wats16
title: Quick week away with 20 something daughter
text: Room was small but spotlessly clean. Flora hand delivered breakfast every morning, bear in mind it is the end of the season. There are 2 bakeries and a bar that serve breakfast every day so this can be a better option if you like your tea hot. Flora happily provided a kettle and mugs. Would recommend you go to the bakery if it is in season, a lot of things close down the last weekend in October Bathroom is 'eccentric' no shower curtain but the design If you are careful stops most but not all of the water. The bathroom was basic but it worked. Water pressure was a little low but there was no shortage of hot water. The weather means that everything rusts very quickly so a little rust on some of the fittings was acceptable. Keep in mind that to go anywhere from here you need transport. The hotel taxi was €10 to fira. Local taxi rank charged €8. Room was made up and cleaned daily again this may not happen in high season can't say for sure. You can't fault the welcome! Had to ask for a kettle and mugs but they were provided, IT WAS NOT THE ROOM I BOOKED, the pictures I saw on booking.com showed a small kitchenette. The room we has did not have this but I was told it was a better room?! For the most part Email enquiries were not answered except for the airport transfers. The view was spectacular. Walking distance to a bus stop, a very good coffee/snack shop/bakery/Mexican restaurant and most important a dive shop. Very clean and friendly place. Including the hotel cat!

author: mallowpuff_nz
title: Pleasant stay outside of Fira town
text: My husband and I stayed at Mesotopos for 3 nights in July. The hotel is about 15 minutes drive out of Fira. It is nice and peaceful being away from the crowds but you must hire a car or scooter to get around, or rely on the local bus service. The bus stop is a few minutes up the road and runs every half hour. The room was very spacious and tidy. It had a mini bar fridge and an extra sofa. We slept comfortably despite the heat as the room seemed very cool, even without the air con on. The bathroom towels were hard as cardboard and could do with replacing. As with many of other reviewers, we too did not have Wifi in our room throughout our stay. The hotel should not advertise that it has wifi available, when it is permanently not available. One evening we discovered the wifi was switched off when we tried to connect to it by the reception area. The outdoor area by the pool was very nicely set up. The hotel provides towels for the pool. The staff are helpful and friendly. Our hotel price excluded breakfast, but there is a cafe and bakery just up the main road. We wanted to be close to the main towns, but not pay the price for staying in the town centres. Overall I think this hotel was value for money.

author: enkab
title: Disgusting Hotel and Racist Owners!
text: Where do I start???? Just imagine the hotel from your nightmares or a horror movie. The only good thing about this hotel is the pool area, it goes downhill from there... Bathroom: the shower head is covered in mold, the silver coating has all chipped off and there is very little light in both rooms' bathrooms. The body soap was the size of a mint and the shampoo was 2 in 1. For the prices they charge they seriously can't afford separate shampoo and conditioner? Kitchen: All of the cups and plates in the kitchen were dirty and the tea pot had bugs and dust in it. Wifi: the "free" wifi does not work in any of the rooms. Our first room was right across the pool and I had to get out and stand by the pool for the wifi to connect. Then when we went to a room further down from the lobby it wouldn't show up at all. Employees: There were two women who helped us check in. One of them completely tries to rip you off. They charge 20 euro PER PERSON for a ride to the airport when it's a 12-14 euro cab ride. They also offer squad bike rental for twice the price of the stores in Fira. But the most unprofessional and offensive experience I have ever had at a hotel was when we asked the woman for advice on where she recommended we have dinner in Fira. She told us to visit her friend's place and then said "Do not ask the Albanians about anything, they do not know anything!" We are Albanian. She did not know where we were from originally because we spoke Greek and English. When working at a hotel with tourist from around the world, try to keep your rude opinions to yourself and do no speak badly of other nationalities. However, thank you for showing your true colors, I will not be returning to this hotel.

author: 396rupertov
title: Ruperto's adopted Greek Family !
text: The Mesotopos is a fabulas place, right on the edge of the caldera.It is ideal for a quite, relaxing stay. You can walk to the edge of caldera in 7 minutes for spectacular sun rises or sunsets. I have been coming for about 8years and it has never been a bad expirence.My adopted Greek family: Flora,Konstantina,Ignathios, Christos and papa Ignathios treats me like a lost son comiing back. Christos always make sure my moto is ready. Papa Ignathios calls me Son. He leaves fruits and vegetables fresh from their magical garden,after my island explorations.Ignathios has check my moto for optimal preformance.He loves motoclycles so I considering as my technical expert. Throught out the years my kitchen is properly stocked, so it is ideal for my personal cooking. Flora has shared different greek cooking receipes. She has cooked for me, her food is always delicious and unique greek cooking.So I dont eat in resturants. Flora is there always with the best advice such as local markets. The family always exceed in expectation and always provide execellent and quality service. Kostantina has guided me all the time for beautiful events in Santorini. She set me up on a catamang "The dreamer catcher" for a cooking class and sunsets from the Aegean sea facing Santorini. I even call my family from "the dreamer catcher" in Mejico.They would say, we can hear the waves! It was spectacular and magical.Kostantina is responsible for making these unforgetable events. I could have not done this without her. She is very fluent in Italian and English which makes very confortable knowing there is no communication issues.I strongly recommend come and stay at the Mesotopos and let my greek family provide you memories for a life time.Santorini, a magical place for sunrises and sunsets.Mesotopos will make this magic a reality, without my greek family .... Santorini will just be a dot on the map !

author: EsmeY
title: Pretty apartments with an island view
text: We stayed a week at this apartment complex on Santorini. It's not luxury accommodation but a pleasant small apartment complex, modern buildings designed in a traditional style. The complex faces across the island rather than towards the caldera, but the view is still very attractive. The pool is a good size and depth and kept clean. The pool area is attractive and sunny late into the evening. Our apartment was a good size and clean, with a little balcony over looking the pool area with a lovely view. We liked the mezzanine bed which is fine for a couple or family, but less good for friends sharing. Bathroom was a little basic, shower wasn't fixed to the wall and curtain didn't stop water getting everywhere. As there was fridge and kettle we didn't have the breakfast, preferring to make our own. It would be useful to have some bowls and a bottle opener in the kitchen. There are two supermarkets and a bakery within 20 mins walk so quite easy to part self-cater. Air-con worked well and wifi was a bit patchy in our room but fine outside. The guest information was useful and helped us with ideas of what to see. We knew it was a bit out of town when we booked, but did find it a bit difficult to locate it when arriving by car. There is a good bus service on the island, but we found it convenient to have a car particularly for going out for dinner in the evening. Quad bikes/ATVs also popular on the island. Good location to get to other places on the island. Overall, we had a relaxing and enjoyable holiday here and would recommend it.

author: donna792
title: Great Hotel
text: My boyfriend and I stayed at the Mesatopos for 5 nights in August . It's in a great position, away from the madness of Fira but close enough to jump on a bus and be there in 10 mins. We walked into Fira a couple of times , the walk takes about 40mins. The staff are lovely and very helpful. The pool area is idyllic, very clean and peaceful with views of Fira and the sea. We had lunch by the pool a couple of times which was great. Our room was quirky with the bedroom on a mezzanine level, very clean and sheets and towels were changed daily I think. Wifi could dip in and out but that wasn't a problem for us. As you leave the hotel and walk up to the main road, just across the road is the breath taking view of the Caldera . The bus stop is there, where the buses take you everywhere on the island . We went over to the beach at Perissa a few times. There are a couple of fabulous bakery's on the road that we used for breakfast and snacks . There is also a great Mexican restaurant close by. The staff organised our transport to the port at the end of our trip and waved us off. It's a lovely hotel on a truly wonderful island and would happily recommend.

author: lynnb667
title: wonderful family run hotel
text: My daughter and I stayed at the Mesotopos Studios and Apartments for 9 nights in June. We decided that we each wanted our own room when we made the reservations. I had studio 13 near the lovely pool. Flora and Constantina and family were absolutely wonderful hosts. They suggested and reserved everything from transfers, restaurants, beaches and rental car (delivered to Mesotopos) to vineyard and Caldera sunset sailing tours. Their first restaurant recommendation was so fantastic that we ate there most every night. Metaxi-Mas in Exo Gonia, give it a try. My studio was simple, roomy and very clean. The bed was very comfortable. We chose to shop for our own breakfast and coffee. And, we ate just outside my studio, poolside. A lovely way to start the day. One important thing to know about Santorini in general, is that it can get very crowded when the cruise ships disembark each day. For that reason, its important to get an early start to the beach or any other sightseeing if you don't want tons of company! Fira and Oia can get quite crowded and noisy. It was nice staying just outside Fira and feeling that we had the view to ourselves... Just a lovely stay.

author: SettaI
title: Don't waste your time
text: I have to say, the pool area is a nice, and the rooms are good also comparing to the trend in other hotels. ( besides the toilet that are small and no shower head, so water is everywhere ! ) BUT nevertheless, its definitely not worth the money you pay for. If you fall on Flora, you're definitely doomed to ruin your stay ! Owning a hotel is something, but managing it and being courteous is something else. We weren't provided towels in the rooms, and when asked the answer was we dont give you towels everyday. Although she had already taken the dirty ones from the room. When we asked for toilet paper, she asked for the room number to register that we even took one during our stay ! On another hand, they tell you there's breakfast in the morning till 10.30am ! Don't bother waking up for it, you are better off buying a nice pie from a bakery than paying 8 Euros for this ! A lady takes your order and places it on the table in front of your door but you end up with eggs not well cooked, old bread, cold tea, and the list goes on. After having stayed for 4 nights, and paid more than 80 Euros per night. We asked to leave the last day at 2 pm instead of 12 to be on time for our ship. Instead Flora, Very nicely ( of course ) refused and insisted we be out before 12:00 ! And she didnt forget to say: " If I remember well you owe me 8 euros each for your breakfast" Seriously ! Is this the way you make your guests come back !? All in all, dont bother ! the location is nice because its far from the noise of Fira and close to the port if you're leaving by boat. But other than that totally not worth the money !

author: Frank-Carol-Yeshua
title: Adaquite +
text: First, let me say that the grounds of this hotel are beautiful and are very well kept. The gardens and the pool are really make this place. But the down side from the beautiful gardens is that there are so many flying insects that you can't leave your doors or windows open because your room will soon be full of the pests. Another good part of this hotel is the owner and manager. Flora was very pleasant and helpful in all our needs. Another down side is that the Wi-Fi barely reaches the room. We had to sit on the balcony of our room to get 4 bars. Inside with the doors closed you get 1 bar connection. Next is the TV. If you don't speak Greek then the TV is useless. I would have liked to have satellite TV. Next is the water pressure in the shower...hardly any. There was more water pressure in the kitchen sink than there was in the shower. Another good factor is that this place is a few miles from the capital of FIRA and set out by itself, so the noise level is very low. As for if we would ever stay at this hotel again...probably not. I would rather spend a few extra euros and get a higher standard of room.

author: manuel_munteanu
title: Excellent cozy stay!
text: I spent a few weeks in and around this resort so i dare to share my experience with anyone interested: if you have your own transport and looking for a good deal for a holiday - this place is amazing! Location: The very name of the place says a lot about the location - mesotops (gr)=middle of the place. And you are indeed in the very center of the island, ideally located toward any direction you may feel like visiting the next morning. Just around the corner is one of the top5 bakery on the island, the best diving center store and one of the most important crossroads. The resort is sourrounded by vineyards and offers superb views to the east and especially incredible sunrises! Rooms: There are about 15 studios, 5 of them with loft - strongly recommended! We had a beautiful balcony with 180 degrees sea view attached to a decent living room, kitchenette and bathroom with shower, plus the loft. Everything was clean, cozy, comfortable, functionable, just as expected. Nothing fancy but its more than enough and certainly a good value for money. Some of the rooms have boiler but we never lacked of warm water around the day. Resort: Spendid shell-pool with jacuzzi area with bar and showers, tables, lounge chairs, very nice arranged and designed, rather friendly-familiar, with good taste - trees and alley, flowers, big garden and very important: no neighbours, which suited us very well. Maintainance: The people who run the place are the owners so imagine everything is going on smooth and easy. One of the peculiar things is the breakfast, which is being taken care by the lady of the house in person and in particular, be it served in the room or by the pool. All in one we had a very nice stay and it proved to be a good choice. Thanks again to Flora and Constandina for being such a good hosts.

author: allaroundtheworld1
title: good location, quite, nice swimmingpool and you can cook yourself because santorini is not cheap
text: I stayed here for 4 night and everything was nice. It's not easy to find. It's on the big road from fira to the old port. lidl shopingmarket is 500m away and ride in the streeks wit a big sign " wemcome" on it! when you come from fira it's left. Nice balcony with wonderfull vieuw. the bathroom is not realy new but clean. the kitchen is basic but everything you need! nice welcome with a good explanation about what to see and to do! i got a plate with cherrytomatos from there own garden as "welcome"! the vieuw from the swimmingpool and jacussi is magnificant and beds enough! very quite place! and close to fira ! they clean every day in your room and yout get new towels! one day even my dishes was done :-)

author: EG814
title: Outstanding!! Can't wait to return!! Perfect!!
text: One of the best experiences ever!!! Loved everything about Santorini Mesotopos. Family who run the hotel are fantastic. Professional, effiecient & warm & very friendly. Made us feel like family members. The studio we stayed in was perfect. Always kept very clean. Facilities like the fridge and stove gave us flexibility to cater for ourselves if we chose not to eat a some of the good restaurants nearby. Brilliant view of the caldera sunset from the top of the driveway. Pool is great! Great location a few minutes from Thira town. Airport pickup was professional & punctual. Loved every minute there? Will definitely return as soon as we can. Absolutely loved it!!

author: ChewInRI
title: Not as nice as expected. Strong smoke smell throughout hotel.
text: I recently stayed one night at the Swissotel in Foshan. I chose this hotel because some of my colleagues were staying there, and I have some standard loyalty to Accor hotels. The hotel is located in the middle of Foshan on a busy commercial street. The entrance to the hotel is actually quite tight and there were some cars backed up, but overall it was easy to find. Our check in was fast and the front desk staff spoke very good English. the lobby is large, but not particularly warm or modern. I would say the hotel felt older than other hotels I stayed out during my multiple city trip in China. My room was a larger king room, and it was actually very good size. For the most part the room was clean and comfortable, but there was a slight smoke smell throughout the hotel. Even though I had a non-smoking room, others nearby were smoking and it made its way throughout the hotel. The bed is VERY firm, but the pillows were comfortable and I actually slept quite well. The bathroom is large and modern and very typical of a Chinese hotel. In the morning, we had breakfast in the hotel restaurant. It is very strange set up and the restaurant area is actually quite small. There wasn't a massive buffet like other hotels, but it had all of the basics both Chinese and Western and there was a chef making custom eggs if needed. Overall, this was an okay stay, but not my favorite in China. The strong smoke smell in the hotel made it feel less fresh than other completely new non-smoking hotels we stayed in. I might choose a different property my next time in Foshan especially given this was one of the most expensive properties we stayed at.

author: Beaniee
title: Nice hotel and worth of value
text: We stayed 1 night in Swissotel Foshan. The building is tall but the logo is not as big as we expected. We reached hotel by walking from zumiao rd. Hotel is about 10-15 mins walk to Zumiao temple and Lingnan tian di. Guangfo metro is closer which can be reached 7-10 mins walk) from hotel. We select this hotel ‘cos of the location and price. The reviews from TripAdvisor members say that Swissotel is a newer hotel. We checked in at 8pm and upgraded to a bigger room. Room itself is not new but is not too old. Bed is ok. Room is spacious and at high floor with city view. Foshan is an interesting place to visit. It’s not a big city. It’s still a very Chinese city where English is not widely used. Tourist attractions also got no much English wording. Life is at slower phase. Living cost is cheaper than Guangzhou. People are friendly and happy to answer when we asked for directions. I will visit Foshan again in future and stay at Swissotel.

author: Riesst
title: Would be perfect Business hotel if the internet would up to standarrds
text: The Swissotel in Foshan is a modern business hotel. The rooms are set in the floors 36-49. On the 50th floor is the restaurant with panoramic view. The room occupied by me in the 48 floor is spacious and did not have a window, except in the bathroom. Only while sitting in the bathtub I could enjoy the fantastic view. The room is modern and comfortable, tailored to suit the needs of business travelers. A complete nuisance was the poor Wi-Fi reception, which did not allow reasonable work and communication over the Internet. In the middle of the night I could finally have some connection with my European headquarters. The breakfast buffet is rich and leaves nothing to be desired. The dinner is charged RMB 288.- and includes unlimited wine and beer. Hotel guests are given a discounted price for RMB 200. As a rather costly delicacy sea cucumber is offered. Unfortunately the seafood buffet was plundered at 07.30 PM and not resupplied. The hotel is centrally located with shopping and dining options nearby. A solution to the bad internet connection is a must, otherwise the hotel is unsuitable for a business trip.

author: coryd17
title: Nice Hotel that Could Use some TLC
text: I stayed here during a recent business trip to Foshan. Having never stayed in Foshan, I went off other users reviews rather than listening to my vendor. I should have listened to my vendor. I'll start with the good. The service was probably the best that I've experienced in China. Check in and check out was extremely fast and easy. The staff at the breakfast buffet was friendly and attentive. My room was spacious and had an incredible view of the entire city. Now for the annoying aspects. The furnishings and decorations need an update and some cleaning. The gym was like a giant sauna due to no air conditioning. Floors and equipment in the gym looked like they hadn't been cleaned in days and left my clothes with Black stains. The Italian restaurant was so-so and they definitely need to turn on the air in that space. It was so hot and humid that I was sweating at dinner. The bed was really hard even for a Chinese hotel. Felt like sleeping on plywood. Having to change elevators at the 36th floor got be quite annoying after the 2nd day. Especially when carrying samples from my vendors. Overall, not a bad place to stay but there are better in the region.

author: ALAN1001
title: No so good as expected but still ok
text: I visited this hotel due to many good reviews in Tripadvisor . First impression in lobby was good . Check in was fast and i get executive non-smoking room . First when i enter room there was a bad odor in room - after cigarets . The room was different as on pictures on hotel web site . Size of room is more on small size and im doubting if the size is same as shown on web site !? Bed was very hard and sleep was not so good . Breakfast was just ok - nothing very impressive . Happy hours in executive club was good and selection of drinks was good also . The executive lounge was good experience - mr Jack make really good impression and was willing to provide help . The concierge wasn't able in 3 days to book me train or bus ticket to Hong Kong !? Answer was always - tickets are sold out !? I was in hotel during Canton Fair and they provide shuttle bus from hotel to exhibition and back . But return was very late so i always took Metro - price was 7RMB and it takes around 1 hour . I will think if i will be ever back to this hotel since service and rooms are not spotless .

author: alhadraje
title: Great views but average experience
text: Location is fantastic. Views from the 37-50th floors are amazing. Rooms are well laid out. But after this point, everything is very average & not what one could expect from a brand like Swissotel. At least with a brand like this, one expects the staff to have working knowledge of English. But most of the staff is either completely English unfriendly & least bothered about it. This makes simple tasks very difficult. This is a high rise hotel & one does expect all the elevators to be in working condition. But during my stay 1/4 th of the elevator bank for the 36th (transfer floor) wasn't working. Aircon doesn't work consistently well. Breakfast experience was average at best & not worth the price. The staff here is English ignorant too. This makes even ordering one's eggs a task of epic proportions. I'd summarise that it's not worth paying the extra buck over other hotels in Foshan. Not recommended. Please book only if your getting a sweet deal on the tariff.

author: SamsonW885
title: Good International Hotel
text: We had a satisfied 2 night stay at Foshan Swissotel. Some international branded hotel seem to have difficulties to live up to their names when they franchised their name to Chinese hotel operators. In my experience, Swissotel is doing a decent job in keeping its name, though not excellent yet (may be due to my shorter period of stay). Even the standard rooms are quite spacious and efficient with a couch and working desk. After these basic furniture, there are still room for moving around. The room as well as the bathroom was kept very clean. The only complaint was the chair was without wheels (!) and made movements very difficult when you are working there. The hotel provide free wifi everywhere and connection was good. As others quests had shared, the location of the hotel is a bit away from the main road and need almost 20 mins walk to Lingnan Tiandi. There are several major bus lines stop at the front of the hotel but probably not useful for international guests. Some guests mentioned also the trouble of changing lifts at 36/F. The front desk staff at 36/F did a good job that she was very alert when there are guests coming out from G/F and offer guidance for changing lift or other services. The hotel management would like to consider putting some front desk staffs at G/F also because it seemed empty there during my 2 nights stay. I also want to comment that the breakfast at 50/F was also very good (compare with most hotels in China). The lay out of the restaurant is not very comfortable which is restricted by the building itself. The restaurant manager may want to keep track of the service level here because the waiter/waiteress were mainly young ones and service attitude need some brushing. They will fulfil your requests soon but with a bland and almost unwilling face. May be it was during National holiday there were a lot of screaming kids without control and made the breakfast less enjoyable . The spa facilities at 7/F is great and use it more if you have time.

author: mlwendy
title: Comfortable stay
text: Overall, my family and myself had an enjoyable stay in Swissotel during our holiday in Foshan. Many thanks to Mr. Andrew Brownrigg for managing my requests. We've arrived at Swissotel Foshan late around 10pm and therefore we've decided to have our first meal in Foshan in the hotel room. Called room service, and food was served in 30 minutes. Thumbs up for the tastiness of food! We had a very fulfilling dinner. The bathroom has a stunning view of the city scenery. It was mesmerizing. The room itself has little view though. Cons: We were allocated two rooms, although side-by-side but was separated with a door outside the room which require an access card to open. This has caused inconvenience especially our children always had trouble trying to go over to their grandmom's room. We stayed on level 49 which is supposed to be a non-smoking level. However, there were people smoking at the corridor and lift lobby. In many occasions, i felt that the staff in the hotel could be more polite. The basics of greeting guests are lacking.

author: Britny
title: Hotel that switches off its air conditioning Cooling Compressor when the temperature outside is around 20 degree celsius
text: We have just returned from a 4 nights stay in this hotel recently. The hotel was everything the other reviewers said, but we found out that the hotel has a very peculiar practices of switching off their air conditioner when the outside temperature is cold, unfortunately, during our visit, the outdoor temperature hoovers around 20-25 degree celsius, our room temperature was at 25 degree celsius, the air was stuffy, smelly and very uncomfortable, we cannot open the window as it was locked and with Foshan pollution level, not a good idea anyway. Neither my husband and I slept much on our first night resulting in both of us having splitting headache the next day. Even after I complained at 8am the next morning and after receiving a letter from the manager saying that they have "fixed" the problem, the temperature stayed at 25 degree Celsius at 8pm when we returned that night, it was only after a really unhappy call to the front desk that the room temperature finally dropped to 20 degree at 10pm, that was after 3 calls, 27 hours after checked in and 2 very irritated customers later… We found out subsequently from the service staff that the hotel will switches off their air-conditioning cooling compressor if the temperature outdoor hoover around 20 degree because they reckon the indoor temperature should be cold enough which is a flawed logic because building retains heat and whilst it was 20 degree outside, inside was much warmer at 25 degree. I would pose a question for the hotel management: Shouldn't the hotel guests be the one deciding at which temperature they are most comfortable with? What is the use of having the air-conditional temperature control in the guest room where the guest cannot adjust the room temperature? Will 25 degree in-room temperature with no ventilation be comfortable for anyone? 2. We stayed at the executive floor but found the toilet to be on the small side and the toilet door (solid wooden sliding door) was jammed upon our check-in. A maintenance crew came swiftly, he removed some nuts and screws and left swiftly saying that the door would not glide smoothly because solid wooden door is heavy. We have to tug and push the door to close and open it every time we have to use the bathroom, resulting in me finally broke two of my newly manicured nails, imagine having to nurse two broken nails at 2 am in the morning. After further complaint, the Hotel sent 3 maintenance man the next morning, brought in the ladder, tool boxes, took down the whole door, replaced the rollers and fixed it properly this time, which mean we also can't use the toilet while they were doing the repair work after our really nice breakfast and before rushing off to our meeting. 3. The iron provided in the room was leaking, both of us ended up wearing Polo shirt to our meeting as we did not feel right to call the housekeeping at 12 midnight for a replacement and there was no time nor privacy to do that with 3 maintenance crew in our room.. That being said, the good part of this hotel is their front line service staff, very friendly, apologetic when there is a problem and, we believe, sincerely aspire to be professional. Once the air-condition compressor was turned on, the hotel was pleasant, so maybe if you visit Foshan where the weather is not at the "Grey" area - around 20-23 degree celsius, where it is neither too hot nor too cold, this hotel is a good choice. Breakfast is fantastic (at the executive floor), very fresh, high quality and very well prepared. We unfortunately have a very rough start at this hotel because of a unconventional practice.. shame..

author: SGO007
title: Average but could be better
text: This is my second experience with swissotel, first was in Beijing which was really bad. Since I already pre paid for the hotel, I had no choice. The hotel is good, a little dated but again the service needs some work (or better training is needed). The Good: - Hotel as clean and good size - Free Wifi - The bright star of the staff would be the Chinese host at the executive lounge, on my second day he really went the extra mile to make us feel welcome. He took the time to chat with us to ensure we felt welcome. The Not So Good: - Hotel little dated - To get to your room you need to switch elevator The Service Issues: - After checked in I went to the executive lounge, they guy told me I didn't pay to have access even after check my room numbers. I check with the front desk and I did pay for it. - After checking in, was told they made a mistake and didn't process my credit card for room deposit. Which was ok, went back to take care of the issue on my way to dinner. - The Major issues was the deposit for my room. When I was checking out... I was told the lady at the front desk made a mistake. Instate of putting my credit on hold for deposit of $2500 RMB, I was fully charged the $2500 RMB. They said it is not possible for them to provide the refund back onto the credit card, because is been over 24 hours. After a long process I was refunded $2500 RMB Cash. - While checking out they charged me $30 RMB for laundry bag I accidently took. You think after make the $2500 RMB mistake they would over look the $30 RMB (I understand this is my fault so I paid it). The good news is that they gave us two free bottle of water because the whole process took so long (over 40 minutes).

author: Happytraveller2211
title: Reasonable hotel but needs improving
text: I have stayed at least twice year since the hotel opened. I always stay on an executive floor, After my stay in April 2013 I complained about several aspects of my stay. As a result the hotel offered to upgrade my room to a suite for my next stay, which they did. The first suite I had during my last stay was so cold I could not stay in the room. The hotel moved me to another suite. The temperature was fine but the hotel's idea of a suite and mine where quite different. The suite consisted of two very small rooms being combined by removing a wall in one of the bathrooms. In the first room all that was removed was the bed. The second room remained unchanged. The suite still had two doors to the corridor . Again I said I was not happy and was moved yet again to a proper suite on another floor. I would have been happy to have a normal room. Again this room was cold (but not nearly as cold as the first room) and the hotel put in a heater which was on all the time during my stay. I have never stayed in a hotel previously that required a heater to supplement the airconditioning. I think there is a serious problem with the airconditioning in the hotel.

author: hyppie_boy
title: Luxury hotel with warm personal touch - you get both
text: I always stay in this hotel for purely business trips. However, receiving a personal American Express birthday promotion (buy one executive room night and get one complimentary plus a birthday cake) and having a relative visiting me from Hong Kong for mid-autumn festival I decided to stay two nights to show my relative around Guangzhou and Foshan. As this is the first time I booked and check-in myself instead of having a local Foshan colleague handling everything for me, I decided to write another review. Before my visit I wrote an email to Mr. Andrew Bronrigg, Rooms Division Manager, who has replied my last tripadvisor review, to make sure I would get a twin bed room upon late arrival. I received an email reply, saying that my trip is being well taken personally. Then the fun and exciting part starts here: I checked in really late, and the front desk staffs Jane and Bella have been extremely helpful. First of all I was reminded that I have a complimentary birthday cake – and ask me the time I wanted it. The cake later arrived promptly with a card from Mr. Ferry Warnke, hotel general manager wishing me a good trip in Foshan. Secondly, I was reminded that my requested twin bed swiss executive room is ready, but if I want something more I could be upgraded to a suite (113m2) or a room that is not in their website (I believe this must be a serviced apartment as it had kitchenette and a washing machine).
