I was then being friendly advised that only king bed is available with the suite, and the “service apartment” is not with the same decorated as rooms I have been visiting – which from the staffs’ look I guess the room is not as luxuriously decorated. Now this is a big choice – for privacy or luxurious, which I picked the former, and did not regret even for a second. For at least 150m2, two rooms - one with double bed and the other with king, still luxury enough for me, is perfect for my stay with relative while maintaining privacy. Plus whenever a little more luxurious is in need one should always go to their executive lounge – The already excellent executive lounge has got even better – their colleague there, Jack, made me home there with his excellent knowledge of wine and kind hospitality. I am not repeating here their must-go 50th floor executive lounge and 51st floor Italian restaurant (please refer to my former review – their executive lounge is extremely nice and worth every penny you spend, because 50th floor is considered very high floor in Foshan surroundings so you get a spectacular look to the city). I was also offered to have breakfast in the 51st floor due to a group occupied the 50th floor on the first day I stayed – which was even better. All in all, Swissotel is a hotel that values their customers. I enjoyed every second I stayed. Too bad they have got only one hotel in China Guangdong province / Pearl River Delta where I get most of my business trips – otherwise most of my stays will be Swissotel - of course Swissotel is definitely my first choice in Foshan.

author: jackieeee
title: Very nice & child-friendly hotel
text: We spent 3 days over Easter in Foshan visiting relatives and wanted to stay in a very clean, high-standard hotel because of 3 young kids. So we went for Swissotel. IT's indeed very nice and clean. We had one premier room connecting to a Swissvantage room. The latter is very spacious and is really worth the extra money. The day bed is big enough to fit my 4 year old and the baby cot is nicely set up. We asked for a Kings bed, big enough for me, my hubby and the 6-year old. Everything is cool except the swimming pool is an outdoor one and not open till 1st April. So its not the resort kind you can imagine, but we are there mostly for the relatives, so its fine. At night after we tucked the kids in, we opened the connecting doors so my parents can keep an eye on my kids while me and hubby went out for a drink. Bar 51 in Swissotel 51/F got very nice and chic decor but no atmosphere even on a Friday night. However, the philippino vocalist of the live band is very very good. Drinks are at reasonable price too. Must try their breakfast buffet, only RMB 90 per head, very good value, and they didn't charge our 3 kids (1, 4 & 6) !! The only thing is it's a bit out from the tourist/night market areas, so if you need to shop or go for dinner, you will need to take a taxi to have more choices.

author: xmikex
title: No respect for non-smokers in the club lounge
text: Caveat: I have stayed over 50 nights at this hotel but not since early 2012 when I decided to base myself out of GZ when I need to do business in Foshan. I previously preferred to stay here out of Loyalty to Swissotel. To the point of my rating Swissotel Foshan average is primarily based on the lack of a non-smoking area in the club lounge and/or the lack of the Club Lounge staff and hotel management to enforce a non-smoking area in the lounge. Unless this has changed, I will never stay at this hotel again. Rooms: For the price and location the rooms are good sized and clean. However, the beds are on the hard side, and the internet is slow. Other than that, nothing really remarkably great or terrible about the rooms. Service: I think the service here is ok overall, and the lower level staff tries hard. In reference to my issue with smoking in the club lounge, I blame that on the senior hotel management not the lower staff. I had multiple incidents where at my request a lounge worker tried to ask a guest to stop smoking or move and it was clear to me the staff is intimidated. Especially when that guest spoke the same local language as them. I addressed this point to the hotel GM but over several visits after my first complaint nothing changed. No no smoking signs or signs to designate a no smoking area were ever posted. I was told one half of the lounge can smoke and one half can not. I asked them how a guest would know that and they said because they can only smoke in areas where this is an ashtray on the table. Well the ashtrays aren't nailed to the tables so they move around resulting in people smoking everywhere. Anyway, in my opinion that is a really poor response for an international brand hotel. One other thing I will note on the positive side to be fair is regarding room service. I stayed here a several times for several weeks at a time, and upon request room service regularly made a special order (not on the menu) dinner for me. Not all hotels are willing to go outside the menu offerings for room service, so I did appreciate that flexibility.

author: white100
title: Tallest Hotel in Foshan but short on style
text: Having stayed in Foshan many times over the past 5 years I decided on my recent visit to try this hotel rather than the Crowne Plaza where I usually stay. A mistake I am afraid! First impressions when you enter the hotel are not good as you enter a busy lobby with a small reception desk at the back which I have to be directed to. There is no guest area where you can meet people it is more like a office building than an hotel lobby. Once you check in you have to take the lift to the 36th Floor where you then transfer to another lift which takes you to the upper floors for your room and restaurant etc. I was on the 44th floor in an executive room giving me access to the executive club lounge which was always empty. My room was not in my opinion 5 star being very minimalistic with quite low quality furniture, Formica top tables, probably not Formica but that's how they looked. Everything was there you needed but by comparison with the Crowne Plaza and other 5 star hotels in China the room was quite basic except the bathroom which was lovely and spacious. I ate in the Italian Restaurant every night of my 3 night stay which is on the 51st floor with a terrific view of Foshan. I had a Pizza the1st night which was ok, the 2nd night I had fillet steak which was fantastic the 3rd night I had Veal and that was awful. Each time I ate in the restaurant I was the only person eating which I found bizarre for this size hotel. The bar was also quiet until after ten when it livened up a bit. Generally I found this an odd hotel with no where to meet and greet my suppliers or friends and if you like your own company then it's a good place to stay. The staff I have to say where lovely, everyone was very friendly and polite and are a credit to the hotel. Particulary the head barman and restaurant Manager Victor and his staff, very nice people and can't do enough for you. Having read some of the reviews I am a little amazed that people are saying it is comfortable they should try the Crowne Plaza just accross the road where at least there is a large comfortable reception area and good seating in the lobby plus an executive lounge which is really 5 star and ideal for meetings. Sorry but i will not stay at the Swiss Hotel again as the Crowne Plaza is far more comfortable and pleasant to stay in at the same price. Pity because the staff at the Swiss Hotel really made an effort and are better and more welcoming than the Crowne Plaza.

author: Dogroom
title: Tale of Two Stays
text: Stayed at this property twice during a recent 10 day trip to Costa Rica. Our first night we got a "dog room" on the 5th floor - old decor, not refreshed in decades, stained carpet with a view of air conditioning units. It also took four calls to the front desk over three hours to get an extra blanket. On our second stay, it was a completed different experience on the 15th floor - renovated room, bathroom amenities, robe (just one though), comfortable beds with duvets and a city scape view. Lesson learned - be sure to ask for a higher floor. During both stays we ate breakfast and dinner in the ground level restaurant. All of them were buffet style with plentiful food and choices. The beverages were hit or miss as the coffee was excellent but the fountain drinks were awful. There are other restaurants in the hotel. Apart from the effort it took to get an extra blanket on the first night, staff were helpful and courteous. The room cards were also hit or miss for getting them to work in the elevators or room locks. Most of the time they worked eventually. We also checked out but did not use the indoor pool. Nor did we explore the city around the hotel as we arrived after dark and were away early in the mornings. The guide books say the area is sketchy but it looks okay.

author: willsaveat
title: Honeymoon
text: The worst hotel, what I'm ever see! We are living here right now, we have honeymoon, 9we only choose 5 stars, and have never seen such service. Keys do not work all the time, in order to go up to your room, you need to go along with these cards to each guest. We change cards several times a day! the rooms are cleaned awful, just look at this mirror. the breakfast is just awful and every time we are asked for breakfast tickets, which we were not even given, every time there is some sort of clarification for half an hour, then finally they let us in! Is it really hard to just check our number without any tickets? Sower very bad, water is almost cold... Today my wife has a birthday, there is a piano in the hotel lobby, and I asked personal to play congratulations on the piano. I was not allowed, without explanation of the reasons. I am a professional musician, and just want to congratulate my wife ... how is that possible ??? I want to play for her just five minutes ... we live in a hotel for 10 days! and we have the right to play the piano! what is this attitude ??? this is not 5 stars, it is just a collective farm for the homeless. If we are not contacted as soon as possible and the situation is not corrected, we will ensure that the reputation of the hotel will be below the plinth on all world sites ... we are now in room 817, my phone number is 12156179972. Hope owner and management staff reading this...

author: StapletonFamily
title: Good value, good location
text: Costa Rica is still a third world (okay, second world) country so know what you are getting coming in. This Holiday Inn has a good location for the Central Avenue pedestrian mall for shopping and food options. Only three blocks and an easy walk. The onsite restaurant is nice treat (chicken caesar salad was very good). They go to a lot of effort to make sure you are happy. The breakfast buffet is ho-hum. Three kinds of cereal, watermelon and pineapple and some local food items and pastries. There is an ice cream shoppe (POPS) across the street and a convenience store. The nicest unexpected was the man in the lobby playing piano for hours each day. What a nice touch. There is a tour desk in the lobby also if you want to book a tour. Like many of the other reviews, we found the key cards and readers to be flaky but we managed to make them work. There is a pool but no hot tub. The rooms are a bit dated but comfortable and about what you would expect for a hotel at this pricepoint. We were very pleased overall with our stay. The staff was patient and helpful. We would stay here again.

author: Windansea2015
title: Friendly front desk, room need improvement, beware of travel partner
text: Hotel entrance looks great, very high ceiling, well decorated. Front desk very friendly and helpful. Good location, walk to downtown attractions. Guest room is dated, needs remodel, especially the bathroom, like the bathtub strips is so dirty... Comparing with other Holiday Inn (even Holiday Inn Express) we stayed later, a lot improvement could be done here. Beware of the travel agency Grayline, which Hotel partnered with. Here's our experience - we booked a 2:30 pm shuttle to La Fortuna, and was told it's about 2 1/2 to 3 hour drive. The shuttle didn't show up until 3:45 pm. Then it started going around the town, filled up gas, dropped off an employee, stopped to change the spare tire (didn’t know why, the replacement seemed even worse), picked up another employee and one more passenger, finally left San Jose by 4:30 pm , already 2 hours behind. At this point, we’re still hoping to arrive our hotel at La Fortuna by 7:30 pm. To our surprise, a nightmare just started, the shuttle stopped at a restaurant at Mi Finca at 7 pm, and we’re told to switch to a smaller van to continue another 2.5 hours’ drive to our destination La Fortuna. We're completely shocked, but no choices at all. Seems like Grayline combined our ride with a customer going to a different direction. These extra 2.5 hours was awful, very rough mountain road with sharp turns. The worst 20 minutes just like driving on “continuous unpaved, uneven bumpers”, made me very sick, almost thrown out. It's almost 10 pm when we got into our hotel, kind of feel lucky for arriving safe. According to our hotel staff at La Fortuna, the trip should be less than 3 hours if they drove directly from San Jose, Mi Finca located much further west, separated by mountain and a lake, which is definitely not along our route.

author: celinanjimenez15
title: Rental car gone missing
text: We arrived to the hotel and the valet was great. They were all very nice! When we went to check in, the front staff was not very friendly. But that's not why I gave this hotel a 3 star. We came back to our hotel real late one night from visiting family. There were no valet drivers in the front, no big deal. My husband went up to the front desk and let them know no one was there and that we wanted to drop our key off. The young man at the front asked for our room #, told us he would give our key to a valet, and told us to have a good night. The next morning when we went downstairs to get our car, the valet asked for our ticket. We explained what happened the night before, and they began to look for our key. It took almost 30 minutes for them to find our key. Which would have been okay. I'm reasonable, I understand that things happen and so do mistakes. However, the people at the front tried to tell us that we never left our key with them. Then the manager tried to tell us that the guy we left the keys with had sticky fingers. Now, there was no language barrier either, my husband is from Costa Rica and speaks fluent Spanish. Needless to say, we will not be staying here again.

author: satipatipatti
title: Comfortable, nice, requires some acceptance for where you are
text: We were happy with our stay at Holiday Inn Aurola. We stayed on the 'concierge level' on the 16th floor. First, the bed was very comfortable, the flat screen TV had very good reception and picture quality. The free breakfast was very good in terms of variety and quality. Our room and the building were clean. Our bath had plenty of hot water and plenty of towels and washcloths. The hotel is within walking distance of the most popular SJ attractions and borders the Amon neighborhood which is full of good dining options. There was no problem getting back to the hotel; all of our Uber drivers knew exactly where it was (by its old name, Aurola) and there are plenty of cabs out front. The entire 17th floor is meeting room and restaurant; our room was beneath the meeting room. One evening there was a meeting with very loud public address, so we could hear every word in our room. The front desk said that they would send security to the meeting to ask them to turn down the volume. We didn't notice the difference, but the meeting was over at 9pm. As I recall, the smaller room numbers were under the meeting room, the larger were under the restaurant. For this reason, next time, we might ask for a concierge level room on the 15th floor. We would stay here again. When we looked at all of the TA hotel reviews for the highest star-rated hotels in San Jose, we noticed that all of them had low marks for service, without exception. While this hotel has some review issues with the front desk (we had none), this hotel seemed to have more consistently higher reviews for service than the higher-priced hotels (see for yourself). Since this was our first trip to Costa Rica, we felt that service would be important if we had any problems with our touring/travel arrangements. Turns out we did not need to rely upon the hotel staff, but we felt that we could if we needed to.

author: frkgundogdu
title: disappointment , frustration
text: I am still staying in this Hotel with some of my friends . Absolutely wouldn't recommend it at all. Thank God that I am leaving tomorrow here , This Hotel even made me feel hate to Costa Rica. Look guys ,i I am traveling to all countries in the world because of my work .. I could easily say that this was the worst treating hotel I have ever been in last 5 years. You can absolutely get better service and respect in any 1 star hotel or hostel. Dont even think about it . Because of their trading of clients. Especially reception desk staff. I can even tell the name of the person works at the reception STEVEN , what a person acting and treating you like you are not even a client. It felt like you are someone came to his house door and asking for food. If you want to feel like homeless , come to Holiday in San Jose Aurola . and meet Steven , ,and another recommend is , don't even book your Hotel with Expedia. because this hotel don't like other agencies that you can book for . that why they are not even giving us breakfast that we paid for . I will be writing my commend to Expedia too. Be careful . and take another option to be happy.

author: EDDMaros
title: Good location. Awful customer service, rude people at the front desk
text: Every time I travel to San Jose Costa Rica I stay in that hotel for a week or more BECAUSE OF THE LOCATION. Las stay was last July 2017 13 days 11th floor same room. They didn't notice I was there twice and I had terrible experiences with customer service including rude people at the front desk and also good things to say about doormen and the restaurant. They don't know what is customer service about. Don't expect to be treated right for the price you paying. Bad things: There is not a customer service survey available to say what is good or wrong there. Be prepared to deal with rude people at the front desk, they treat customers like if they were doing a favor and nobody supervises them. If you really want to give a good value of your money, choose another place to be unless that you ready to deal with difficult people. Good things: The locations is really good, right in the middle of down town, everything is close by. The hotel has an acclimatized pool and the restaurant service is good. You can find around the area very nice places to eat like Barrio Escalante like 15 minutes walking from the hotel. I definitely will stay there again just for the location. I don't expect more from people that they really don't know what is customer service about. They need to be educated about it first. Good luck on your stay.

author: Brittishborn
title: Business for me, vacation for my wife.
text: Let me start by saying this is not a brand new looking hotel, but it is very clean and tidy. The lobby is well kept and furnished. As soon as you pull up outside, there is someone to valet your car (free 24hr) and the service continues to be excellent from beginning to end. There is a high priced restaurant on the 18th floor, you are looking at a $50 steak bill for one. However, they complement this with a reasonably priced restaurant on the ground floor, with a bar and separate menu on the second floor. There is a concierge level with free snacks and alcohol between 6-8 depending on if they are busy or not. The room was very clean and had Hi speed wifi for free. This is great to use the wifi calling feature on your cell to save large roaming charges. The bed was very comfortable and being a king, my wife was able to build a wall of pillows to lay on and there was still plenty of room. The in room TV did have a lot of channels that could be changed to English by using the audio button in the remote. Remember they charge for double occupancy, But it is still worth while for the location. As in all cities, one has to be careful, but there is a nice park right outside the front entrance, and you can frequently see jugglers and musicians etc near the main circular stage. Take good walking shoes with you, as there is plenty to see. The national museum, although nice, was not quite as good as the gold museum or jade museum that boasts 5 stories. Not all goods are cheap, for example a large suitcase that we went searching for ranged from over $200 to $48 for a very similar item. It pays to keep looking around. Finally, if you want the Costa Rican goods like coffee t shirts, hand made wooden gifts, there is a market next to the jade museum. You can haggle with these guys and get T-shirts at $6 rather than $15-$20 in the local stores near the hotel.

author: Ronin381
title: Good location, good wifi but need improvement
text: My wife and I stayed in this hotel for two periods, total of 8 days/nights, spanned Feb/March 2017. Our trip was a combination of business and pleasure. I am heading back to San Jose in four to five months time. Here is my observation: Location was good, great WiFi. Breakfast area on the main floor was dark, foods was not great with limited choices, coffee was poor (weak or burned), the placemats were reused again and again, very dirty. There is a cook prepari gneggs, such as omelette for customers USING a four burners electric cook-top. He constantly switched on/off and adjusting the elements, the solution is use a gas fired griddle style surface with different heat setting on different area so he can serve more than just a couple of customers at a time. There is a coffee machine located behind the food counter near the special orders cook is, a very narrow area with all the traffics. Every time a customer wants a special coffee, server has to stand there to make the coffee, took up time and space. The servers also walking around with coffee/mike jugs for refill, better solution is to have filled coffee/milk jugs on each table for customers to help themselves. Free up the servers to prep the tables for new customers. Many mornings the table settings are missing something, such as coffee cups, forks, napkins and knives etc. Same missing items, missing work also applied to house cleaning staffs. The cleaning staffs would knocking on each door asking if the customers have any laundry requirement, simple solution, like the rest of the world is to have a bag inside with check list for customers leave outside their doors or dropped off somewhere; thus free up cleaners for other duties. With a to-do check list for cleaning staff to check off each items, duties with each room; so other staff don't have to bring missing items up to customers after they check in.

author: daveb653
title: The little things......
text: I stay in IHG worldwide, Spire Elite status (oh er mrs!!!!!). Checking in.....ok, but cc not needed so go to bar, have a beer, check refused. Matched to reception by barman to set up account. Very embarrassing. Room all ok, envelope to tip the room maid . No, just pay decent wages you bloody tight guys!! Check out a nightmare . Dot matrix printer- remember them?? Can't see amount paid, Invoice for stay not printed, just expenses. CC charged in dollars, not asked for choice. Room not serviced on first day so maid obviously keen on second day so wakes me up at 8.30am on a Sunday. Executive lounge not open for breakfast, no water available...... Breakfast in main restaurant horrible (described as an American buffet), if it is the Yanks need shooting as it was horrible, although the omelette was good. Orange juice- the bane of my life in IHG hotels. They charge $14 for breakfast and the orange juice is some horrible concoction from a plastic bottle. For gods sake, we are in Costa Rica where you grow the bloody things!!! Good location for city, be careful though, dodgy area. Casino next door fun.

author: gardenergrl
title: Good hotel- not so much bfast
text: Had a great two nights. Roomy suite, clean and comfortable. Most staff was friendly and helpful. Loved that as HI members we had a happy hour. The pool is gorgeous and warm. Ordered breakfast in bed- the kids were so excited. Disaster - the order was not correct, and the food was terrible. Ordered croissants and got three crescent roll type items that were about a third the size of a crescent roll and well over cooked. Not close to a croissant. Eggs were rubbery and somehow the café con leche came without milk. When I called to ask for this they sent up powdered creamer. Bakery basket was tiny, stale items. After walking around the area and seeing so many bakeries we had much higher expectations. The buffet the next day was better, but not great. At least all the kids were free for the dining at HI. We notified the front desk at checkout about the room service and they said they would notify the staff. This is my first negative review on TA, I believe, but it was worth noting.

author: angelomariadaffonchi
title: Glad I Found the Way to San Jose
text: With the help of GoAhead Tours I was priviledged to stay at this lovely property. Rooms/bed comfortable, clean and had a good feel. First imressions are everything and Anita, Glorianna, Jocquin, David, Roy, Edward and Hector made me very happy, feel safe and taken care of. They like their jobs and you can tell. Happy and helpful are the magic words for front desk people and they;ve got it all. YYou guys are awesome! Downtown is quite congested on Saturday. The central mercado is fun and most everything is $2 and/or very reasonable. I can't wait to return the end of the week for another visit even tho it will mean back to the real world, I'll have the reminder of the kindness shown not to just me but all the guests at this facility. Patience is their virtue. Quite a popular tour stop over. Try GoAhead Tours through EF (Education First)-they know their stuff! Yea! Jaime, Raphael and Melissa! Thanks for the positive vibes the first day of a wonderful adventure! More to come!!

author: lidiam497
title: Average hotel-overrated at 5 stars
text: definetely need renovation; the quality of the room is a medium level; rooms are clean but with old furniture and features (olf TV set, the bathroom needs definetley to be redecorated) A big minus is related to the absence of ice machines; even there is an ice conteiner in the room (I wonder why); there is a locked !!! minibar containing some chcoclate bars but if you ever would like one you need to call the frontdesk to send somebodey with the key. The breakfast is interesting but expensive for the qualtiy of food. Avergae expensive food is offered in the restaurand for dinner. The restaurant at the lobby level definetely needs a redecoration, it looks and feels like a above average cafeteria. I had a 10th floor room, nice view but be prepared for a very slow wifi. They gave an additional router and finally I could use the wifi in a proper manner. i had to sign for the router so that they are sure that I will not leave with it. The magnetic card had to be reactivated almoste every single use... Which was unpleasent. The personell is polite but not really friendly, the tip is almost mandatory if you would like to have a smile from the hotel team, One of the maids just entered in my room without knocking on the door catching me half nacked. My fault I did not locked the door of course :) Limited communication in English. I had one dinner at 17th floor restaurant, nice but not exqusitie, definetely expensive for the services. Food was good. The pool area is nice but the pool is actually a larger tub and definetely not a swimming pool. Overall i would not come again in this hotel and i would not recommend it especially if you are in vacation.

author: BforBoy
title: Average hotel, great location
text: It's my first time in San Jose and I chose to stay at this property because of its location primarily. Also, I am an IHG platinum member and was hoping to get a nice room with my membership. I paid $ 100 US a night which was reasonable I guess. At check in, I was upgraded to the executive floor but a regular room which was ok. The executive lounge has soft drinks and limited bottles of water that don't get replenished often. The snacks they had during happy hour were like 10 pieces of crackers and cheese and when they're finished, that was it. I wanted to exchange some US dollar to colones. At the front desk, I was told that I could cash advance using my credit card and the rate was US 100 = 54500 colones but I had to pay 10% service fee ($ 10 US). I said ok well what if I gave them cash, then the exchange rate was dropped to US $100 = 51500 which did not make sense to me. I ended up going to an ATM which gave me a much better rate. The hotel location is very close to the main museums (a 3 min walk) and fast food places in case of hunger emergency! Uber is very convenient in San Jose, though I find it more expensive than regular taxi even with Uber X. Some taxi drivers tried to rip me off but luckily I knew what the usual rates were. Uber is more safer. The service at the front desk was acceptable. The staff weren't exactly friend but they weren't rude either. Overall, an average stay.

author: Jazzyjan12
title: A comfortable Downtown Hotel
text: We stayed here overnight. We were greeted promptly by the Bell Captain. Check in was smooth. The staff escorted us to the room with the luggage and filled the ice bucket. He also showed us how to operate the thermostat. We used the hot tub. It was lukewarm but relaxing. There is a nice pool and work out area. We dined at the breakfast buffet in the morning. It was average. They had an omelet chef. The price was quite high at 15.00 for breakfast. There is a nice gift shop in the lobby with reasonable prices. The staff parked and retrieved our vehicle. The service here was very good.

author: kenster99
title: Great Location, Terrific Staff, TERRIBLE INTERNET!
text: The location of this hotel is perfect. It's central to everything. There's nightlife, shopping, and restaurants all within a very short distance. The staff is also very well trained. They were professional, bilingual, and available to help with all of my needs. I was very impressed with all of them (ranging from the front desk to the bartender, to the bell man). All professionals. The pool is nice, the hot tub is great, the beds were super comfortable and the rooms were clean. My gripe (why I did not give the property 5 stars), as a business traveler I need Internet like I need electricity and water. I need to stay connected with my client base and when I stayed at this location I was unable to do so. The internet is very spotty in the rooms. It works on one side room and not the other, etc. Some rooms don't even have wifi. During the afternoon and evenings the Internet was virtually unusable because of the load of other users. The property needs to address this.

author: C2308UUdavidc
title: Response to the Nay Sayers
text: I really wasn't going to review this hotel until I saw some recent very negative reviews that I felt were unfair. We stayed here on the first two nights and then the last night of our trip to Costa Rica in March 2015. Our experience was completely positive. We found the rooms clean and comfortable. The facility did not appear threadbare to us at all. Admittedly we were there in the dry season, but there was no "musty" aroma. The front desk staff were courteous, efficient and helpful. They were happy to allow us to stay past the noon-check out time since we weren't going to be picked up until 1PM. . We did not go to the upper restaurant, but did eat several meals in the restaurant in the lobby which we found satisfactory and not terribly overpriced. We were booked into this hotel by the agency that arranged our trip and so had pre-paid. We did not have to pay extra for the breakfast buffet. All they wanted was our room number. I don't know if this was a special deal. The hotel is in downtown San Jose and is close to several museums. For example the Gold Museum is only two blocks away. Bottom Line: This is after all a Holiday Inn and the rooms were just like the those one would see in the U.S. We would stay there again.

author: PianoTuner
title: A Tour Of Costa Rica With "Caravan Tours."
text: Our first night was spent in downtown San Jose at the Holiday Inn. An interesting city in the daytime, but, we were advised not to venture forth at night. We were also warned to look both ways at cross streets, because nobody stops for the stop signs! A point to see is the businesses in Downtown San Jose - most all of them were covered with the same razor wire defenses that are put around prisons. The sights away from San Jose were absolutely fabulous! We visited both coasts and many places in between ... all the places we were interested in seeing. I wasn’t sure I wanted to visit Tortuguero, but it turned out to be one of my favorite destinations! Living in the jungle with the "Howler Monkeys starting to howl at pre-dawn - no sleep from then on!! This was an exceptional tour at an exceptional price. The guides were very eco-minded. We received a good education from them and their passion for preserving their environment was contagious. Our leader was not only a very experienced guide, but held a degree in environmental science. He was able to find curious little creatures in the jungle floor to show and explain to us. With the volcanoes, and sea shores, and monkeys all over the place, this was a great trip with a great company.

author: TonyM167
title: Rude, no guest allowed in room, followed by security
text: I visited this property May of 15 and upon check in I noted(written down on ck in papers) that I had one guests staying with me. The res. was for 2 adults no problems thus far. After walking around the terrible scummy city of San Jose we returned to the hotel with a friend who wanted to come to the room and have a drink. Upon entry security swarmed upon us, directed all 3 of us to front desk where the disrespect began. To be short I was told if I wanted a guest to visit me they must stay in the lobby for the entire visit. Next I was told I could pay $70 to have him go to the room. After requesting to speak to a mgr, I was told to wait a moment he would be right down...after 25 mins I realized Luis Aguayo(mgr on duty) was not coming. The front desk guy then says Luis is on the phone. After being told I signed the paper that states the visitor policy, I decided to read back the contract of the hotel-it said nothing about visitors or a FEE! Appalled at this point I asked for refund and was told NO! I asked for a copy of the contract with "my" signature on it and was told NO! I stated I would simply cancel charges via amex, and more security was called and I was told I was posing a threat. Amazed beyond belief by this point, my friend booked another hotel and we decided to leave. PLEASE BEWARE IF YOUR STAYING IN THIS PROPERTY! THE RESPECT LEVEL FOR AMERICANS IS VERY LOW!

author: Drealtalk
title: The WORST customer service
text: First I must start by saying I am appalled and disgusted with the level of service and professionalism I experienced. I went to visit a friend who was staying in the hotel and as soon as we returned from dinner I was escorted to the registration desk. Once there they told my friend that he must pay them $70 so I can come up stairs. After explaining that I have never heard of a holiday inn requiring a guest to pay for a guest to come up, the front desk person Allen went ahead and be came very rude and disrespectful to me and my party. From the time we got to the hotel, we felt like we were being watched and profiled. When we asked Allen to speak to the Manger, he lied and said that he was on his way. We later found out that the hotel manager was not even in the building, and he continued to lye saying that he was on his way when he wasn't. We ask for him to call corporate, he said "You have their number, you call them". Once we decided not to be disrespected anymore we decided not to stay at this hotel, he said that he is not going to cancel the reservations. We asked for a copy of the contract and he said no. He finally agreed to cancel the reservation and ordered security to follow us to the room to grab our belongings and leave. There was more that transpired, but I wanted to say that I would never be setting foot inside of a holiday inn ever again. I am going to starting now to make it my purpose to tweet, intagram, and send out my review about my terrible experience. I will make sure to share my experience with all of my friends and family. Not to mention I am on the end of my vacation and on top of that hearing news about my father dying. This just ruined my entire trip. Thanks

author: nohassle1956
title: On a mission trip with our church for a week in San Jose
text: My wife and I viasited in August 2014. We had a suite $174.00/night w/o tax. The suite was a nice size. It had two full bathrooms with a shower in each one. Plenty of towels and toiletries. A large closet with plenty of space to hang cloths and store things. There was a safe in the closet. The bedroom was nice and large with a comfortable king size bed, a desk and a chair, two bedside tables, a table with two chairs, and a nice flat screen tv. The living was good size with a couch, 4 chairs, a table, tv and some end tables. The coffee pot was in the living room. There were two separate ac units, one for the bedroom and one for the living room. Internet signal seemed weak in the room but worked well in the lobby. The internet was in the price of the room. Breakfast was included in the price of the room. It was a big spread with many items to choose from. We were on the 16th floor so it was very quiet and secluded. The hotel had a pool, casino, gym, spa, tour desk, front desk, restaurant, bar, business center, and plenty of space in the lobby to meet in. We used the conference room on the 17th floor to meet with our church for daily devotions and instructions for the day. All of the areas were very clean. This was a great hotel for this mission trip or for any other reason if you find yourself in San Jose.

author: btwatsvc
title: Holiday Inn Aurola
text: All in all it's a very nice facility. The staff were very helpful and had no problem with English. Clean and well kept. May have been a five star hotel a few years ago but is beginning to show some signs of wear and tear. Carpets are a bit frayed and thin. I had the Presidential Suite and it was a tremendous bargain. The first morning I had no hot water and the shower was certainly "refreshing". The second morning it was luke warm but manageable. By the third morning I had more hot water than I ever wanted. The flush button popped out on the floor which left the toilet running but was repaired post-haste. It was interesting that there was no soap dish in the shower. Had a good looking jacuzzi and sauna but I didn't have the chance to use them. I went down for breakfast one morning and the pans in the buffet were empty so I opted out. The Palma bar was friendly and the staff very helpful. I would recommend the hotel to anyone who is not looking for lush luxury but a good clean hotel with a helpful staff. The prices were very good.

author: Lubiere
title: Decent option in downtown SJO for less than 100$, but a bit drab
text: Booked via IHG for 79$. Arrived late evening to a lobby which was partially closed up for a cleaning of the carpets (not inviting at all). Check in was OK, not particularly friendly, but polite. Benefits provided to Gold members is a free drink per night at teh bar, no breakfast or bottled water. The room itself was decently sized with plenty of window, decent view of SJO, good king bed, nice clean bathroom, free wifi. The TV is old school CRT with decent selection of channels. The aroma of the room was unpleasant, musty, light cat pee, maybe due to tropical clime. Air conditioning helped a bit with attenuating the odor. The gym was decently appointed with ellipticals, treadmills, some weights. The pool was nice but again, some renovation work made the area unappealing to the eye. The Jacuzzi was OK. The location is good, with plenty of dinning options around (ask the bellboys), Auto Mercado is 2 blocks away for groceries...the immediate area is OK to walk at night (Morazan park is lively with youths hanging around) but if you walk to far, it can get a little iffy (you do get a warning). I did not partake in the breakfast at the hotel (15$ buffet). I did use my free drinks and the young lady serving me was very pleasant...go for the Pura Vida (anything with a lil. guaro is good). If this hotel could get some reno work and updates, it would be a really good option...I still recommend it.

author: afderoide
title: Conveniently located - No charm but as written on the tin
text: Always difficult to rate a hotel part of a hotel chain. Location is great, on a place with a bit of animation and 5 minutes away from Museul del Oro and pedestrian streets. Professional and smiling welcome from reception (did request internet access to book the room on hotel.com, no problem). Room was large, bathroom a bit outdated but no big deal. Swimming pool is of decent size. Breakfast was ok with fruits (which i asked to be made in a smoothie, done with a smile), eggs station (always appreciated), rice ... . The only drawback are the viennoiseries (croissants and alike) of very poor quality. I would kindly advise the chef to search for an alternate supplier .. you might get better quality for same price. Wifi worked fine (free) and parking as well (free). Did not try the dinner (went to Limoncello, see review, which Holiday Inn staff booked nicely for me) but I understand the restaurant has a nice panoramic view. At check out I asked if i could pay the aiport tax through them. Was possible for USD 34 I think, ie USD 5 premium compared with doing it straight at the airport. I would have paid USD 2 extra only for this so i queued just a bit at the airport. Overall no bad surprises, good experience.

author: StefaniLeo
title: Nice Rooms, Located in the middle of everything
text: My husband and I missed our connecting flight out of Costa Rica and were forced to spend one night in San Jose. Instead of staying at the airport, a local friend of ours suggested The Holiday Inn Downtown because it was in the middle of shopping and dining and night life. He also said it was a safe hotel in a safe area. It certainly lived up to his recommendation. There was a street festival with vendors selling handmade crafts the day we were there. It was great. The staff was friendly, the bellmen were all extremely helpful in suggesting restaurants and getting us a taxi. We spent the evening at Las Palmas Bar on the 2nd floor which overlooks the park. It was the best people watching. Orlando was the bartender and he was AWESOME! Friendly, he made great margaritas and caipirinhas which were on special for happy hour. I also really wanted a Caprese Salad from the nice restaurant on the 17th floor of the hotel but since we weren't planning on staying an extra night, I wasn't comfortable venturing up there in my tank top and shorts. But Orlando was happy to order one to the bar for me. It was delicious. Overall no complaints. The breakfast was mediocre but if it was free with your stay, it's fine. And most of the staff only limited English so knowing some Spanish is helpful.

author: ba31182
title: Very good hotel, even if it is not the newest one
text: Overall rating. ***** (out of max 5). Very good hotel, even if it is not the newest one Location ***** (out of max five). 5 min to walk to Plaza de la Cultura. A lot of restaurants, coffee shops, supermarkets and bus stations around the hotel Room. ***** (out of max five). Very nice large room with air condition. Infrastructure, Service (internet, reception, pool etc): **** (out of max five). Nice pool. Good gym. Friendly reception. Weak internet in the room. Very good internet in the lobby. The carpets on the floor and in the room are not the newest one but they are clean. Breakfast. *****(out of five) Good breakfast from 6:00 am – 10:30 am with handmade omelets, grilled bacon, corn flakes, fresh fruits etc.

author: ekinwilliston
title: Nice facilities, everything else average.
text: Modern building and very nice facilities overall. The hotel has two restaurants and one bar. It is very close to many, many places to eat and visit. The room is comfortable and clean. In fact, it might just be the cleanest room I've every stayed in in my travels. There is no complaint about cleanliness. The bellhop staff was always helpful and kind. I relied on them a lot. However, the internet doesn't work. It took one hour and a room change to get me hooked up to a non-wireless internet. For a modern hotel, the internet needs to work properly and rapidly. The desk workers were not always friendly. In fact, some were just rude. I did speak to the manager about the issues with some of the more unfriendly, non-smiling staff, and she promised me that my concerns would be addressed. Overall, not bad.

author: 871FrancescaM
title: Not good
text: We stayed in the Aurola holiday Inn on the final night of our trip before flying home. The hotel is OK - the area slightly dodgy and wouldn't recommend walking round after dark. We were warned about this by a local on the street as well! The main problem with this hotel is if you are unlucky enough to experience any problems. Unfortunately the door to our bathroom got jammed and we weren't able to get back inside. Maintenance were called but informed us that the door would take an hour to fix and therefore would we prefer to move rooms as we had told then we needed to get to sleep, having an early flight the next day. The front desk was very helpful at the time and got us moved fairly quickly. They did mention they would upgrade the room, however the room we were moved to was identical in every way to the original, but no matter as it was functional and we were leaving the hotel very early the next day. The main problem was that some of our possessions were trapped inside the bathroom. They left us with the key and told us to come back in an hour when the door would be open. We went to bed and planned to return the next day to pick up our things and this is where the big problem started. At 3:50am we returned to retrieve our things but the door was still locked and the TV in the room still on. Clearly nobody had bothered to go back and fix the door. We went down to the front desk to complain and they insisted they had no record (unfortunately the woman who had helped us move had left) of there being a problem. They weren't particularly bothered that our things were trapped in the room and we had an airport taxi waiting. In the end we had to leave and to this date some of our stuff might still be stuck in there. No apology, nobody bothered to record the complaint and the customer service was pretty poor. Suggest people stay somewhere else for the money.

author: LindsayD820
title: Nice escape
text: as soon as we arrived at the Holiday Inn, we felt taken care of. The staff were very friendly and always willing to help. Whether it be by recommending places to visit, or ensuring that you're prepared for a 3AM trip to the airport (Not just a wake up call, but providing someone at your door to help take luggage for you). Carlos was at the front desk for most of our stay and he was very informative about the area. Very nice and always had a smile. He even told us where to go to see a piece of the Berlin Wall! The rooms were clean and the beds were very comfortable. Perfect for a good night's rest after a full day flying. The rooms were nice and cool. Bathrooms were clean and well maintained. the breakfasts were extremely good. I loved that they provided a lot of authentic Costa Rican meals. They were fantastic! Make sure to eat at the restaurant at least once. Prices are fair and the portion size is awesome!

author: chinasonvacation
title: Wrong room type & lost luggage
text: We arrived around 4 and were told our King room was ready, given the key and off we went. Room key didn't work, had to go back to to reception to get that corrected. Luggage was to be brought up to our room so we walked around outside and the pool. The indoor pool was small but adequate. The inside areas were well kept and the location was good as it was in the downtown area of San Jose. Returned to our room around 5:15 and no luggage. I called down to reception to check on this since we had a 6:00 dinner reservation with a large group & needed our clothes. 30 more minutes & no luggage. I went down to reception to see what the problem was. The told me they would figure it out. 10 minutes later I was called in the room & told our luggage was on the way, that it was delivered to the wrong room/floor. The girl form reception along with a bell hop brought the luggage up with a simple "sorry". After all of this I wasn't about to tell them I booked a king room, not 2 doubles! Room & linens were clean & the room was a decent size. Breakfast was just ok. I wouldn't return...after the baggage issues.

author: Lorraine242
title: Exceptional visit!
text: We spent 2 nights here before joining a tour group. The service was impeccable. We arrived at 10:30 pm. The desk clerk was very friendly and helpful. The bellman provided us with exceptional service. Unfortunately I don't recall his name but kudos to him for knowing what customer service means. Our room faced the park in front. The room was a good size, very clean and the bed was very comfortable. We had breakfast in the restaurant on the main floor. It's buffet and was ok. Not sure it was worth $13 US. We dined in the restaurant on the 17th floor. WOW! Awesome view, food was incredible - it's fine dining so the price tag fit fine dining but was reasonable. The server, Rodolfo was super friendly, always smiling. He truly made our dining experience a good one. Thank you to all the staff for making our first trip to San Jose a positive one!

author: karenpammy2016
title: great central location place
text: We stayed here overnight as part of our tour package to Costa Rica. It is one of the highest buildings located in the busy central part of San Jose, right next to Parque Morazan which is quite busy during the daytime with a live concert going on when we arrived ~ 4p.m. on a Sat. in August. The check-in was quite efficient with our luggage delivered to our rooms within 1/2 hr after we arrived. Very convenient with 2 computers available to check on our departing flights and we were able to print out our boarding passes. The rooms are decent size and our room offered a view of Parque Morazan. Actually it is located at quite a busy intersection where there is a constant flow of traffic- public buses and cars so crossing the streets are a bit challenging but not a great problem. It is only about a 3 block walk up to the downtown area of San Jose. Our dinner up on the 17th floor at the El Mirador Restaurant was good- we had a choice of sea bass, prime rib, or free range chicken as the main dish. I would recommend staying here if you wanted to walk around the downtown San Jose without having to take any public transportation as everything including the National Theater, Gran Hotel, and Parque Central are just about a 10-15 min walk down. Lots of people for sure, but it's not a problem walking around. Need to be somewhat careful of the uneven cement crosswalks as they are not all that level. It is best to walk slowly than run. Anyhow with so many people around, it is difficult to run in the area. Also, despite having an early departing flight out the next morning, the Holiday Inn had a breakfast available prior to our 5a.m. departure to the airport.

author: ctamborra
title: Great location, looks like a great pool
text: First of all I am a Marriott Gold member and usually stay at Marriott properties, but choose this property due to location, free airport transfer if staying on executive floor as well as the fantastic pool. The day before I was due to arrive in San Jose, I called the hotel to arrange airport transfer. I was informed that there was a charge for that service, $22.00 not a big deal, but was told at 1 888- holiday that it was complimentary. I questioned charge. They also wanted to change my rate as they only had 1 person listed on reservation for 2 rooms. It took numerous calls to 888-holiday as well as calls to the hotel. Holiday Inn customer relations ended up picking up transfer bill. It was during one of these calls I became aware that the pool would be closed but would reopen on Friday July 26. I expressed my concern about not being notified about pool staus as we were had a pending reservation. Customer relations open up a case and informed me that the manager would contact us within 48 hours. I assumed he was going to contact us during our stay. It never happened. When I returned home I called customer relations about this and was told well you stayed at the property, there was nothing they could do. I would have booked into the Marriott San Jose but since I had prepaid for the Aurola so I didn't want to lose my money. All I wanted was for the manager to make arrangements for us to swim at another pool. Next time I will stay at the Marriott, yes it is farther out of San Jose, but I am sure the situation would have been handed different.

author: IschiahereIcome
title: Stinky Room
text: I arrived late on a Saturday night and I was leaving early in the morning. Otherwise, I would have asked for another room. It had a bleach plus something else odor. The windows don't open & the AC didn't help. The bathroom was brand new & nice. The room, nothing special, Breakfast was $15.00 pp. All I wanted was coffee & it was $2.00. This price in a coffee producing country. Absurd. I told the nice waitress that I didn't want it. She let me keep the coffee without charge. The customer service was very good & check in was quick. The doormen polite. I would have to say the staff is their strong suite. btw, even the breakfast area in the Lobby had the "odor" I sat outside on a bench to drink my coffee & wait for my ride. I paid $90. for the room with a United Airlines discount.

author: ChristinaB508
title: Spring Break Class Trip
text: The Holiday Inn in San Jose Aurola was a great place to stay for my class over this spring break. A group of 19 of us stayed here two weekends in a row and loved it. There was a little park type place right outside with a fesitval type thing going on. It wasn't too loud or too in the way. The view from the windows on either side of the hotel were breathtaking. A supermarket, restauraunts, and souvenir shops were within walking distance. The traffic was a little crazy but that is just the type of driving in Costa Rica. The hotel staff were very kind and helpful and did their best to understand us and help us in anyway possible. The decorations around the hotel were very simple, yet elegant. The bar was nice and quiet place to sit down for a drink after a long day. One thing that I was not too happy about was that the shower did not warm up very well the first time we went to shower. However, subsequent showers were fine and relaxing. I figure it to be user fault or a rare occurance. Also, the hot tub was not hot but warm. It was still relaxing but could have been warmer. Overall I would recommend this hotel to anyone asking my opinion. If I ever return to San Jose, Costa Rica I know where I will be staying.

author: Hilthd2000
title: GOOD EXPERIENCE
text: This Holiday Inn Aurola is very nice considering you are staying in San Jose. The rooms were modern, clean, had a safe and everything was in working order. The staff was friendly and helpful. People complain about the location. The hotel is in downtown SJ across from a busy park, but within walking distance to museums, etc. So that's a plus. People should realize that SJ is a city without a "WOW" factor - lots of barbed wire, rubbish on the streets, etc, so don't be shaken up by its looks. Its citizens are friendly and there are no more police officers there than any other large city in the U.S.A. My one complaint about the hotel is the bar - service was VERY SLOW and one male bartender was unfamiliar on how to make drinks listed on the menu. Service was also slow in the restaurant. These need to be corrected. If I were to return to SJ, I would stay there again. Oh - you will hear noises from the constant buses that travel the streets - this is the major mode of transportation in SJ. Don't be shocked! Enjoy the culture.

author: hermrc
title: Nice place for seeing a few sites in San Jose
text: Caught a taxi from the SJO Airport to the hote; cost about $30. Check-in staff was very polite and said we had a corner room on Floor 11, as requested. Room was clean and in good condition. Indoor pool was heated to 93degrees F. Almost too warm, especially if you want to swim. There was a pedestrian mall and central market a few blocks away. Nice to walk around after sitting on flights. Plenty of US fast food chains and local places to east at. I would suggest the pizza places for breakfast and lunch. Really good food that was inexpensive. The park across the street .... would not go there at night. Daytime on Sunday, it was nice to walk around. Small park in the middle of the city. Not much else to say.

author: hankTexas
title: Nice place in a worn out neighborhood
text: Vacuum used by maint crew for a plumbing problem was dirtier on the outside than on the inside. Hall carpets need better cleaning. Lavatory faucet in 611 was loose from the granite top. Thermostatic feature of shower faucet is not working. Often hot water came out of hot line and cold line at the shower and lavatory. Shower head does not have a good setting. Shower head needs to be simpler and more effective. Door key cards are unreliable. Food in Tropicana dining room can be good at times and very average to poor at other times. Breakfast was reliably good. Pool was good fun and relaxing. Dinner was variable. Final dinner on the 17th floor restaurant was good. Hotel very well adapted for service to the large Caravan tours. Drum beats from Cultural Center 3 blocks away can keep you awake at night until 3 or 6 am.

author: WeLoveCR1
title: Nice Stay
text: We stayed an entire week here. This is the hotel my parents stayed in 19 years ago for our wedding. It is still just as nice as it was then. We have family in CR and based here for visiting them. The hotel is very nice, very clean and the service is great. Valet parking, a gym and swimming pool, all of which we used. Nice bar, but the complimentary "cocktail" is actually non-alcoholic. We did not eat at the restaurants, as we know the city and went out for authentic Costa Rican food at much lower prices. We recommend La Criollita, a couple of blocks from the hotel, behind, near the INS building. Maid service slightly inconsistent (different maids do things differently, I am guessing), but not on anything important. Someone also comes around later in the day to check that you have everything that you need. If you are not in, she comes and does a turn-down service and leaves chocolates on your pillow. I assume that most of the staff speaks English, but we speak Spanish so I am not sure about everyone. Mini-bar is OK, we did not indulge, but did use the fridge. The area around the hotel has gone down hill in 19 years, especially at night. Parque Morazan is directly across the street and is quite pretty, even at night, but it seems to be in the middle of the red-light district. There are a LOT of police around, so we felt OK, but there were prostitutes on the corner (as someone else also commented on) and all the bars close by seem to be pick-up joints for sex tourism. It was not comfortable and we bought our own bottle and enjoyed a drink in our room instead of venturing out at night. If you want to buy souvenirs, the place with the best prices is the large Artesania, right in front of the National Museum. Avoid the Central Market and "La Casona" - both totally overpriced.

author: bluejean18
title: Quiet oasis in center of busy San Jose.
text: Stayed here at the beginning and end of a tour of Costa Rica. Enjoyed the very central location in the heart of bustling San Jose. The room and public spaces are extremely clean and comfortable. The hotel staff was helpful and personable, and we were relieved to find they also spoke English quite well. We had a lovely view from our seventh floor room, looking out over the adjacent park, the jumbled rooftops and the distant mountains. The streets adjoining the hotel are busy day and night, but the insulation was good and we had no problem with street noise. The food in the hotel is mediocre. You can do better by finding restaurants in the immediate area. After reading about San Jose, and the area around the hotel, we were a little intimidated to venture out on our own the day we arrived. However, with a very nice tourist map (provided at the hotel front desk) and a few tips on interesting things to see within walking distance, we thoroughly enjoyed exploring the local area. The pedestrian friendly Avenue Central is only a couple of blocks from the hotel. Leave your valuables in the hotel safe and go there. Visit the marketplace, the parks, and dine at the local eateries. We were so glad to get a feel for the city in this way. Our most treasured souvenirs were purchased from the stalls at the artist market only a few blocks from the hotel. San Jose is certainly not a vacation destination to recommend to friends and family. However, it is a necessary evil as a gateway to the rest of this beautiful and fascinating country. As such, I would not hesitate to recommend the Aurola Holiday Inn.

author: CarrollCollinsFL
title: Outstanding Service and Hospitality
text: August 4, 2010 I wanted to take a few moments and express my gratitude and appreciation for the concern shown to me by the staff at the Holiday Inn Aurola in San Jose. I have been coming to Costa Rica since the mid seventies, and have been staying at this hotel, while in San Jose. All of my adventures in Costa Rica have been terrific, up until this last trip mid July, 2010. I experienced every travelers nightmare of getting severely sick far, far from home! I was exploring the west coast, in Montezuma, a place I had never been before, traveling alone this trip, and I get sick! I was fortunate to make it back to San Jose, back to the Holiday Inn Aurola and with the kind help of The Holiday Inn Aurola staff, improved enough to get to the airport and fly home. Ana Sanchez, Aurelia, Raymond and Ms. Laura Rodriguez were so instrumental in getting me back on my feet. They definitely went above and beyond anything I would expect, to get me my medication,and special juices. I will never forget their kindness and concern and their quick action. They need to be applauded and recognized for their compassion and willingness to help. Thier hotel staff is always warm, inviting and respectful. The facility is always kept fresh, immaculate and safe. A terrific haven for the traveler, the tourist, the business person. I look forward to the day when they promote a casino on the penthouse floor again--what a treasure that view is up there! I truly thank them for the help they gave me when I really needed it. I told my wife that the willingness to help and to care was equal in every level of administration and staff, a true testament of the caliber of people in thier organization. Everyday I am feeling better and looking forward to returning soon to San Jose. Sincerely, with appreciation, Carroll Collins

author: peachome1
title: Good enough
text: Like others, I was a this hotel as part of a caravan tour - spent a total of 4 nights there. It's functional. The room was clean and had the amenities you'd expect and they worked. One challenge is the air conditioning. It seems it is either ON or OFF and On was pretty cold. That was frustrating. When it was on it was noisy but did the job. I agree with another reviewer that they should have a better business center with free internet there. They have free Wi-Fi in the rooms for those who can use that. The pool is inside, on the 3rd floor. They have some chairs and will serve you a drink there. as a hint for other..... No one was at the pool the afternoon we arrived, so we acutally used the area as a meeting place (didn't get into the pool) to hook up with friends since there is no lounge area except in the lobby which gets loud and crazy. I also think they have a missed opportunity for their bar area...dark and plain - not a fun hang out. The surrounding area is "iffy" - - we were advied to not walk down sdie streets. We just walked around the park in front of the hotel. But, others in our group did venture further and found a nice pastry shop. (they spoke fluent Spanish, however). Having said all that, I must admit we were happy to be there and have "modern comforts". Not top of the line but functional and seemed in line for the price.

author: joeconsumer
title: Unscrupulous
text: Ok, this Hotel is touristy and the staff was very superficial. Be aware of your surroundings at all times. The hotel is located in a portion of the city’s red light district, so be careful when venturing out. If you like soaking in highly chlorinated pool water, or lounging in an air condition environment, or dining on laxative ridden foods, then this Hotel is for you. I would like to warn everyone about the Message Parlor across the street from the Aurola Holiday Inn Hotel. Stay far away from it! I got a message there on the advice of the folks I was traveling with, because it was super cheap $15. Well my message experience turned into a living nightmare. I nearly ended up in a Costa Rican prison because I was being forced to pay more money than what I was originally told was the cost of the message. The guy behind the counter confirmed the $15 dollar price when I first walked in, then the price somehow changed upon exiting. Very shady! The hotel’s staff was completely callous to my pleas for assistance. The of course was after I had broke away from the irate monster of a woman who claimed to be the owner, and the two police officers she had flagged down during our quarrel over the bill. At the time, I could swear the Hotel's clerks and check in folks were in cahoots with the parlor and the whole affair frightened me to death! I was forced to get my wife to come down from our room with $65 in order to appease the cops and the message parlor's owner. All the while the Aurola Holiday Inn's Hotel staff were completely indignant and made me feel like the crook. The affair was nothing short of horrifying.

author: VEC24
title: Disappointed
text: We decided to stay in San Jose the final night of our trip in order to see the city. I figured that this would be a great finish to our trip, but I was disappointed. From the outside it had the trappings of a class hotel, but it missed the mark in many areas. No one helped us with our luggage upon arrival and checking in took longer than anyplace else in the country. Our room was nice but lacked the standard information you would expect in a hotel room. We had an ice bucket but never did find the ice machine. The hotel binder told you that there were two restaurants but not their locations, or menus. However, they did have paperwork outlining all the charges you would incur if items were found to be missing from the room. We ate at a local luncheonette and bought some muffins for our breakfast so we never did eat at either of the restaurants on the premises. I went on a hunt to find the fitness center and ran across it but I never did locate the pool. We were on the 8th floor and slept worse here than elsewhere in the country. We heard some gentleman coughing and car alarms going off all night. By 6AM we couldn't wait to leave. The only saving grace was going to NAMU located right around the corner. It's a store that sells local handicrafts and had a good variety of items.

author: Consumerguy1
title: A very disappointing finish to an otherwise terrific tour.
text: We toured Costa Rica with Caravan Tours, which put us in hotel after hotel that exceeded our expectations . . . until we came to the Aurola. In spite of its 4-star rating, this place needs a lot of improvement, except for its beautiful warm-water indoor pool. The food in its buffet restaurant was third rate. The air conditioner in our room, and the rooms of several other guests on our tour, sounded - as one of our fellow travelers put it - "like a broken tractor." We stayed in Costa Rica an extra day after the tour, so we asked for a change of rooms . The front desk staff was surly and indifferent. And with just one person ahead of us at the desk, it took 10 minutes before someone helped us, even though other staff saw the line growing behind us. In spite of a Do Not Disturb sign on our room door, housekeeping knocked at 7:40 a.m. On our first night - the final night of the tour - our pre-arranged dinner in the 17th-floor restaurant was mediocre at best. The food was rushed on and off the tables and its quality was poor to fair. The fitness center was not air conditioned. The final insult came when the staff missed our 3:45 wakeup call. Had I not set an alarm, we might have missed our plane.

author: Yoshi99
title: Adequate, but not ideal for layovers
text: I'm a little mystified by all the reviewers describing the place as "posh" and "upscale," but maybe it's all in the frame of reference (I note one reviewer was impressed with the fact there were two trashcans (!). Don't get me wrong, the place is fine. In any event, the positives: 1) clean, 2) no-hassle on-line reservations, 3) friendly staff, 4) quiet rooms, 5) very comfortable beds, and 6) free cocktail coupon upon check-in. Negatives: 1) location (more on this below), 2) no in-hotel ATM. To put it as kindly as possible: downtown San Jose is not exactly a luxury destination. The hotel is near the city theater and a large center square ringed with American fast food restaurants. If there was a place to get Costa Rican food, we didn't see it. We tried to find a local restaurant, but failed and ended up just eating at the hotel restaurant, which was fine (their marinated hearts of palm were pretty tasty). We needed to go to an ATM and the hotel staff gave us directions. "Is it safe?" I asked. The clerk looked up at the clock, thought about it for a second, and then said, "Yes ... at this hour." (We got cash without incident) The thing to consider is that the hotel isn't really near the airport. We took a taxi from the SJO airport to the hotel ($30) then to the small airport (Parva?) the next morning ($15). So given the transit costs plus the fact there isn't any compelling reason to stay in downtown San Jose, I'd recommend either staying near the airport or just timing things so that you don't have to stay in San Jose at all. If you're intent on staying in downtown San Jose, however, the hotel is definitely adequate and hassle-free.

author: femaleCalifornia
title: Most helpful staff in all aspects
text: We were in San Jose, Costa Rica the end of November. The hotel staff was courteous, helpful and beyond accommodating. They spoke English fluently and were more than happy to help in any and every request that we had: and we had many! There was a travel agency on the lobby floor who arranged a trip to El Arenal (volcano) which was much easier to do by tour just to get our "feet wet' and explore the city and streets enough to rent our own car and explore the rest of the country on our own. We used this particular hotel as a base to be able to travel around the country and return a few days here and there. If you're in Costa Rica, might as well take off to Panama which is an hour flight and very worthwhile. However, each time we wanted any information at all, the front desk was eager to help and didn't expect anything in return. It was like a home away from home. The one thing that was a "problem" for me was the fact that there were many rooms that had recently been painted, which was very bothersome for my allergies, making it impossible for me to sleep. The hotel was more than happy to guide us to several rooms and allow us to select one that was to our liking. A must do in Costa Rica; Manuel Antonio. Jaco is just average, but has a good location for the Canopy Tour. Keep in mind that if you're driving to any of these locations, it is a breathtaking drive, yet getting out of the city is very tricky if you're only used to driving in the U.S. Also, all, and I mean ALL the cars we tried to rent were stick-shift, no automatic in sight; meaning that not everyone can get themselves around. Last but not least; the people in Costa Rica are absolutely the nicest we have ever encountered, and we've traveled to more than 50 countries so far. They will go out of their way to help you, just because. Another must do: the coffee! It is to die for. Enjoy.

author: sachahuista
title: As good as it gets in Central San Jose
text: I stayed at the Aurola for 18 nights in February and I have to say, as hotels go, this is as good as it gets. Sure, the facilities were great, rooms comfortable, helpful staff and a really decent location, but it was the whole experience of staying there that made it good. You get a feel of things after such a long stay and, on the whole it's an overwhelmingly positive experience. For a start, its location is superb. San Jose can be a very noisy place and whilst there's heavy traffic outside during the day, it gets pretty quiet at night outside the hotel, and what's more, there's virtually no pedestrians outside. The same cannot be said for other hotels which are in much noisier neighbourhoods in downtown, and can be a pain to sleep in even at 11pm. No such problems at the Aurola though the park outside can be too quiet and a little bit iffy at night so beware of thieves or petty crime there. Tourist police are now a regular sight around, however. As for the rooms, they're pretty good - safe that fits in a laptop, bed was comfortable, good amenities such as cable TV (with US television), fridge, good gym, swimming pool (indoors so a bit weird), jacuzzi, helpful staff (except for buying the departure tax which they only do in late afternoon and there's always a long queue), free wi-fi, internet terminals by the lobby, and a good breakfast. I don't quite understand why people complain about the breakfast because it's pretty much standard continental, American (sausage, bacon, waffles, pancakes) and Costa Rican stuff (rice and beans, plantines etc) as well as cereal and omelettes. A big bonus was also free local calls so great for business though I can't vouch for leaving messages as I never used it. Good wake-up calls too. My only complaint would be that they don't provide any airport pick-ups or shuttle services, and that you can't open the windows in the room which can be quite annoying. Cleaners can be a bit too efficient in wanting to clean your room everyday, ignoring the 'Do Not Disturb' sign. And hot water can take a bit of time to kick in to the shower late night/early morning. Other than that, I would happily recommend this to anyone. Having also stayed at the Crowne Plaza Tryp Corobici, I can say that the Holiday Inn is cheaper, better-located (much better especially for finding food in downtown and personally, that's what made me choose this hotel) and just more happening in general. The Tryp Corobici was great, but just felt a little detached from all the action a little bit. With the Holiday Inn, you're never too far from somewhere to eat, or a bus to nearby suburbs.

author: yodabogota
title: A very nice Holiday Inn in the heart of downtown San Jose.
text: We stayed here with our Caravan tour at the beginning and end of our trip and really liked this beautiful hotel. The lobby staff are always busy, but helpful and accommodating. The food here is excellent at both the cafe and restaurant, and the cafe and restaurant waitstaff are very gracious people. The rooms are very nice and clean and if you're fortunate enough you might have a view of the mountains out your window. Being in the heart of downtown is very convenient, albeit a little bit noisy, but the rooms themselves are pretty sound-proof. There is a nice bathroom with bathrobe provided as well as soap, shampoo, bath mat and a coffee maker with coffee. There are key-cards that you use in the elevator to get to your floor for security purposes, but this is a nice touch. There is a pool, exercise room and bar. The hotel itself is very lovely (lots of marble), clean and well-lit. My only real complaint is that the first night we were there, we were freezing and couldn't turn on the heat. They came up to look at it but couldn't fix it and didn't have an explanation for it. Apparently other people had this same problem on our floor so I am wondering if the whole building had no heat since they never need it??? Anyway, if you're cold, turn off your air-conditioning or put it on fan ("dry"). If the fan function blows out nothing but cold air, shut everything off and just bundle up in pajamas. I was surprised at how cold we were that close to the equator, but then again San Jose is at a higher elevation (ie- cooler) and we stayed on both the 10th and 14th floors during our stay. Overall, this is a very posh and well-maintained hotel. I would definitely recommend it to others.

author: singermom4
title: Fine but non-descript
text: We stayed here as our starting point for a Caravan Tour. Although the location is central and close to main city attractions, it is a bit off the main road and next to a park so I would not want to be walking about in this area after dark. The securiy in the hotel is good - you need to insert your room key to access your floor. This is a good thing since alot of different types of clientele enter this hotel due to the casino. We saw many odd pairings of older men with young girls - if you get my drift. The rooms were of good size, standard holiday inn furnishings and small bathrooms. Most rooms have very nice views - it is one of the taller buildings in San Jose. The first night we arrived we dined in the 17th floor restaurant. The food was actually quite good and the price was very reasonable but all the food was served cold. Another night when we dined as part of our group tour, the food was excellent - one of the best (and largest!) filet mignons I've ever had. The casual cafe on the first floor is average at best. Good selection of fruit in the mornings and and omelet station but everything else was just okay. The buffet dinner on a Sunday was one of the worst meals we ate during our stay in Costa Rica. The dinner the next evening was thankfully better. Service could have been friendlier. I tried to have the front desk arrange a driver for us for a day to go to La Paz for our party of 3 adults and 2 kids and they tried to book me with a driver for $90 a person!
