Thankfully I happened to bump into our tour director and he arranged a nice van and driver for a grand total of $80 (not per person). This was my least favourite hotel on our tour.

author: HOTWINGS78
title: Definitely Not for Business
text: Stayed at the Hotel Holiday Aurora for 10 days on business last July/August 2006. The hotel itself is fine as well as the bell-hops who are quite helpful and are truly there in the best interest of the guests. Their advice is straight-forward and no nonsense. The room service was impeccable, efficient and first class. The management was not worth two flips especially insofar as resolving problems was concerned. There was no problem with the language as I am fluent in English as well as Spanish. Complaints that were brought to them was light putting up a stop sign in front of a hurricane. Getting messages was even worse. Since we were there on business, there were messages expected and left that were never received or even noted for that matter on checking with the person(s) that supposedly take the messages. This cost me one of the days by waiting for someone who had already left a message changing the date of the meeting. The icing on the cake was when they had arranged for a minivan to take us to the airport (courtesy of Holiday Inn) and after waiting ~ 20 minutes, they bell boy came out and said that our minivan was in an accident with a city bus ! Having lived in Mexico for ~7 years and familiar with the lies and garbage that they come up with, I simply "reacted" and let it all hang out both barrels. Another minivan was there in minutes (big surprise). On returning to the United States, I complained about this to Holiday Inn main office in the United States. While they were all apologetic, they sent vouchers for $100 for my next stay at Holiday Inn. Nice but did not alleviate the situation of having lost time on a short trip. Needless to say, I do stay at Holiday Inn without problems. I returned to San José in October and there was no way I would stay there: not even for free ! It was not worth the aggravation at all. I would trust that this was an isolated incident, but if incidence of whatever is 1 in a million and you're the one, then the incidence is 100%.

author: DownTheRoadAbit
title: Very Nice Hotel w/ great management!
text: 3 - 5 blocks from the national museum and pedestrian walkway(where there is EVERYTHING), 2 blocks from the pharmacy, 2 blocks from a giant casino.. It's a GREAT location!! I was a bit concerned when we pulled up as the Aurola is right downtown But, no need to worry... I felt safe and secure the entire time. You need a room key card to activate the elevator, there is plenty of staff in the spacious lobby area that all kept an alert eye out and everything was clean as a whistle. All the amenities are away from the lobby so there is no direct access to the public. For instance, the bar is on the 2nd floor and overlooks the park so it's not really a place where people would mosey in FROM the park. The pool area is also covered and away from the street access. The casino and restaurant are on the 17th floor with a fantastic view of the streets below, again NOT where people would drift in from off the street; so safety is figured into the plan here. I had a problem and it was handled quickly & kindly by Romero, the manager. He takes customer relations seriously and made certain that I felt completely understood. Though he was busy, he arranged to correct the problem and then followed-up with me to see if I was enjoying my stay. 2 weeks later when I popped in for a cocktail, he recognized me and though again he was clearly quite busy, he took a moment to offer his friendly hospitality with a broad genuine smile. Beyond his great sense of humor and voice of a songbird, Romero's style of management made my willingness to recommend the Aurola and easy decision. We found it to be upbeat, comfortable, and a pleasure. Oh yeah, depending on your room location, you will either have a view of the city lights, or on a clear day a view of Poas in the distance! Either is nice. "Mira Ramona"

author: viradanna
title: The security guard is a pervert peeping tom!
text: It pains me to write this review of Besakih. We stayed for 7 days and had a good time. We actually upgraded our room to a bungalow and enjoyed the clean beach, nice pool and decent breakfast buffet. We intended to come back to Besakih hotel our next trip to Sanur - until our last night. It was approximatley 10:30 PM when I came back from the lounge area and observed the security guard (who was wearing a large sweater over his uniform by the way) looking into our window and watching my husband, who was unclothed. I came back to the bungalow and immediately contacted the front desk and headed to reception. The security guard arrived and stated that he was "checking the doors" and that it was "standard practice" - an obvious lie considering that there were no lights on or around our bungalow except for our bedroom light, and the security guard had no flashlight. And "checking the doors" for what exactly? That question was never answered because it was obviously untrue. I was upset and disgusted and asked for a refund for the night and to be moved to a different hotel. It took an hour of arguing with reception and then arguing with the manager over the telephone for us to be moved to a different location for the night. While I am not blaming the receptionist for this, he was honestly nice and just doing the best he could about this disgraceful situation, I don't appreciate the fact that it took an hour of me yelling and hysteric in order for management to do the right thing. For the record they did actually refund us for the night the following day. I wish I didn't have to write this review, but I cannot in good conscience remain silent knowing that there is a security guard on the premises inappropriately observing people in the privacy of their rooms. It is sickening and dengerous, especially since there are plenty of children on the hotel grounds. Because of this I will publish my review on TA, Google and Booking to alert people about the security guard on the premises, I hope Besakih will do the right thing and put the safety of visitors as their top priority,

author: jnxd
title: Thank You
text: If you want modern western hotel then Besakih may not be for you but if you want real Bali then it’s perfect. We had villa behind doors Friends had suites and standard rooms, they were all comfortable. Gardens are lovely. Nice beach area. Good food with flavour. Cold beers. The pools are great the infinity pool with bar on the beach is a stand out feature. The number of people walking by stopping to take photos said a lot. Great location .. lots of spas, warungs, bars and restaurants to choose from. Last but not least were the beautiful staff and a heartfelt thank you to management and staff for allowing us to hold our wedding there.. even more so when short notice (less than 2 weeks) when other venue became difficult. The Besakih turned out to be a more than perfect venue. We will be back and so will our wedding guests some who had not been to Bali but have fallen in love. Thank You xox

author: oktadvisor
title: Good value for beachhotel
text: This hotel is right in the middle of Sanur. It is quite as the rooms and cottages are located in a green quite garden balinese style, far away from the bussy street. The beach is right at the back of the hotel. You have a nice view of the beach from the hotelrestaurant and the pool. There is a comfortable clean walkingpath along the beach with many (hotel) restaurants on one side and the beach on the other side. Rooms has that old classic look, with old furniture. Everything functions well. There is a fridge and a kettle but no safe. There is a seating area inside and a seating area on the balcony or terrace. Wifi is average and free. Buffet breakfast is very basic and almost the same each day. Waitress will bring you coffee/tea and ask how you want your eggs/bacon/etc. Nice touch, no selfservice egg-station like in most hotels. Good value for a beachhotel in this location! Hotel restaurant is overlooking the garden and the beach and serves good food for lunch and dinner. Staff is very friendly and helpful. Plenty of restaurants, eateries, shops just outside the hotel.

author: vermaderma
title: A family friendly experienced hotel right on the beach.
text: Besakiah Great location. Right on the beach. Nice pools. Both are small but they are nice for relaxing. The reception was very welcoming. We were offered cottage as well as room and we preferred the room. I would suggest getting rooms at the ground level. There is a lot of greenery and flowers everywhere. Large property. There is a nice restaurant near the pool which is where you have breakfast which we found very nice and welcoming. Nice fruit juice, fresh fruits, bakery items, sausages and bacon and eggs etc. The bacon especially was excellent and tender with the right crispness. However they limited it to only two rashers! That was weird! You had to pay for extra but both times we asked for some extra they gladly obliged with a smile. The last day we were late and they accommodated us but were really very very hospitable. The place is about 45 years old and I am sure has lots of repeat customers because of their attitude and also the location and prices. It a little run down and is aged but let that not deter you. Full marks for the location, reception, check in check out, courtesy and breakfast. But 2/10 for wifi.

author: gutsache
title: Not as good as it used to be.
text: My wife and I booked the top priced suite at the hotel but were disappointed with what we received. The suite was dated and in need of maintenance. Plaster and paint was peeling from the walls. During our seven night stay we lost the hot water supply on one occasion; both phones to the unit did not work and we had an issue with the lighting. The faults were rectified expediently by management. Like many Bali accommodation properties the suite was fitted with shiny slippery floor tiles (Bathroom, bedroom, front porch area and front step). When wet they became as slippery as ice. I slipped, once, on the front step and was lucky not to receive serious injury. I commandeered two extra rubber door mats from nearby (unoccupied) units and positioned them on the front steps of the unit for safety purposes. The large poolside spa was empty and had been for some time. I asked the pool attendant about the issue and he told me he had been making requests to management (at the request of guests) but nothing had come of his inquiries. Breakfast was the worst part of the hotel's service.......their system was to take the guests order at the table and serve - rather than the normal buffet breakfast. One could choose two eggs (cooked to your choice) and the choice of bacon, sausage or ham. A guest, at a nearby table asked for fried eggs with four of the small chipolata sausages - but was told by the waiter he was limited to just two of the sausages. The pre-cooked toast, in a bay marie food warmer was so tough, dry, thin and hard it was virtually impossible to eat. The fresh fruit and other breakfast items were very basic. I would have given the hotel a three-star rating but could not do so because the breakfasts were so bad. We have visited Bali 17 times so I did not have unrealistic expectations as to what to expect at the hotel.

author: chichy
title: Not worth the money
text: I was very disappointed with this hotel. The room was dark and semi clean, bed linen was thin and grey, the bathroom towels where very worn and stained. The shower was over the bathtub which will be an issue for some to climb in and out of, the floor was flooded after every shower. Breakfast is very basic not much of a selection if you want lattes or cappuccinos is extra - most hotels offer this in the price these days. One particular morning there weren't any tongs out for the fruit and you had to use your fingers to pick up a piece - not very hygienic. On arrival we were given a pool towel and after that you had to source your own towel from housekeeping they weren't available at the pool. No where at the pool to leave your wet towels you had to bring them back to your room so the cleaners could take them the next day. We had to use ours to mop up the floor in the bathroom after we showered! Asked the room cleaner if i could have another pillow as one bed had 2 and one had 1 - never got it , had to go to housekeeping myself to get one. Guest who had ordered room service put their dirty dishes out the door in corridor and they stayed there for 24 hours with uneaten food on the plates, thought this could have been collected by staff just not a good look when having to walk past it. I can only say that this hotel is directly on the beach and it is in a great location but so are many other BETTER hotels. On check out i asked the receptionist if i could print off my boarding pass and he abruptly told me to go to another hotel as he couldn't do that for me !!! I was speachless... Lucky i do have some very good Balinese friends who do work at another hotel who were more than willing to help me out. On the whole i found this hotel very old and in need of serious clean up and renovations, the staff seemed to lack enthusiasm this can totally change the vibe of the place. Friendliest staff were the ones in housekeeping/laundry room and the security guard at the entrance other than them i found the rest to be totally disinterested and miserable. If your not expecting much from a hotel then you wont be disappointed but after many years of holidaying in Bali i dont rate this hotel well comparing it the other hotels i have stayed in.

author: Lisasmart1
title: Run Down - No 'love' for customers.
text: We stayed 9 nights in a standard double room on second floor (room 235), after the first night I advised reception that there was water pooling on the bathroom floor due to leaking pipes under the sink and that we used all the towels to clean up the water, I complained 5 days straight and then demanded that they fix it or move us. They finally moved us to an identical room a few doors down (room 241) for our last 3 nights and this room had exactly the same issue only was leaking much, much worse. I told management again, but they really did not care... these rooms are in dire need of basic maintenance for the safety of its customers. The double bed was 2 hard single beds pushed together with a big crack down the centre, the sheets and bath towels were stained and just YUCK! On the positives?? Adequate air conditioning. We found the majority of staff to be typically lazy here and hard to find when you need something, daily there were no mattresses on sun lounges you had to get them yourself from the beach area, there were often dirty ashtrays, empty glasses and water bottles lying around the hotel pool and beach tables. Not once in 8 days did anyone come to the pool lounge or the beach to see if we needed a drink, we had to go to the hotel restaurant to order them as there was rarely anyone in the pool bar, also when staff delivered the drinks they didn't take away the empty bottles or glasses, we had to ask them to clean up, and most of the time we just walked our empty bottles up to the recycling bins on the beach. WiFi - Free but frequently not available for hours at a time, we went to the Santorini Hotel next door, bought a beer and used theirs free of charge. Day tours - There was no brochures and no help to book day trips from the Besakih hotel, we asked reception about a boat cruise to Lembongan, and they told us they could make the phone booking, but not responsible (and we had to find our own tour information). The Santorini hotel next door was far more helpful with brochures and guidance. We found a local tour guy in a booth on the beach who looked after all our needs (highly recommend, his name is Budi at Chantik Information Centre) chantik_tourbali@yahoo.com Breakfast was included and was basic but adequate (bacon and eggs if you ask for it, but very small serves), fruit, pancakes, croissants and soggy toast in the buffet. Salt shakers were always wet and never refilled with dry salt. The only positive attribute to this hotel is the location, situated directly on the beach at Sanur, however there are dozens of hotels along this strip all with very competitive food and beverage prices and every one of them we visited providing exceptional customer service in comparison. We ate and drank elsewhere opting to pay (and tip) for better service and a friendly smile. Summing up - Very disappointing Besakih Beach Hotel. Excellent location but definitely would not stay here again.

author: schezara
title: This place has all that we needed....
text: If you want a place where the staff is nice, helpful and friendly, the rooms and accompanying bathrooms are decently comfortable and clean, the breakfast is simple (pancakes, stir-fried noodles and bacon/eggs), it provides you access to Sanur beach, within walking distance to numerous nearby restaurants and bars in Sanur, and fits into a low-medium budget, then this 3-star hotel is the place. This is the kind of hotel where its reception staff still uses a typewriter and keeps a safety box at the reception (instead of the rooms). That's its charm. If you don't want any of these things, then go to one of the modern hotels that can be found along the Danau Tamblingan street. There were some comments about the staff on this board. The staff was responsive enough during our stay. I came with my partner who doesn't speak Indonesian. I found that they were more comfortable speaking with me (though limited Indonesian I had) instead of with my partner. It pays to be patient with them due to this language barrier. I once sat one afternoon at the reception while waiting on my partner. There were guests who talked down to the staff, and that was not cool. Politeness goes both ways, and Indonesians are the type that if you're polite to them, they will return the favour. Also, I'd like to thank the cleaning staff for finding and keeping my flight ticket. You're a life saver... Good job!

author: Sheppards28
title: Loved it
text: My husband & my mother & I spent a week at the Besakih Beach Hotel and loved it. The front desk staff are so friendly & helpful. The cleaners did a great job & all the staff were just super friendly. On arrival out air con was rattling & noisy so we were immediately moved to another room & offered the original again once it was fixed but we stayed in the new room. I will say don't get a room with an internal door as it means the noise from the next room comes through loud while we were trying to get to sleep which was annoying but we just put up with it. The restaurant is good, good & prices were great although we thought the price of the Bintangs too expensive. We loved the breakfast which was very fresh, well prepared & nice & the staff are lovely. We lived the sun lounges and the beach is fantastic. The massage ladies on the beach are adorable we had a foot massage every day. We used 2 drivers through the hotel Putra & Putu both of whom are fabulous. They have great driving skills are safe & well priced & have lovely personalities with great senses of humour. It was my birthday whilst there & the management left me a lovely basket of fruit. Nice touch. We will def be back again. Just loved this hotel.

author: sg721
title: Very old school hotel in a great location
text: Sanur is one of the original tourist destinations in bali, and this hotel feels like it must've been pretty impressive in its heyday. The gardens are quite lovely with water features throughout, some amazing old established trees and beautiful stone temples and shrines. At reception to summon a bellboy they use a great old gong! The standard rooms are part of an impressive old building and have some charm, despite very dated bathrooms. Modern comforts are limited. Wifi was awful. Bathrooms very old and had not at all been upgraded - taps quite hard to turn, steep narrow bath. Of course it is clean and staff are pleasant. The restaurant was hit and miss. Breakfast fine and the Indonesian food we ordered for lunch was lovely. Dinner (western style, as room service) was pretty ghastly. There are a couple of joined pools that are pretty cool, overlooking the beach pleasantly, a swim up bar and one pool even functions as kids pool as my toddler could easily stand up. But the pools are tiled and a bit slippery. One spa pool area was not functioning. I probably would come back because the location is great, right on the beach, and right across the road from Art Cafe which is excellent. Maybe I would get a more expensing room though.

author: johnnyo803
title: Not too bad
text: Hi there.. We only stayed here for 2 nights and were pleasantly surprised with the location of this hotel. For the price it was good. We didn't know that at the end of the hotel which fronts onto the beach there it's a bike/ footpath that goes about 2k in one direction and 3 : the other. Each way you go you go past heaps of other bars and restaurants from other hotels and locals alike and you can eat at any off them... Great. The pool is good with a little swimup bar. The rooms are adequate and clean although are a bit tired but ok for 3 star place. Only have 2 negatives the first being the air conditioning... During the day just not cold enough not too bad at night when you've cooled down. Second was taxi company used by hotel... We were quoted 200,000 to the airport.. On route the driver tells us it's another 50,000 for tolls... Then when we get to airport he says we got to pay 285,000 + tolls.. We don't pay... Lesson learnt is always make sure you agree on the price before getting in the cab.

author: wendyb228
title: The pool area makes up for other sins
text: There is no better pool in Sanur. I'm sure of it. I loved this pool so much - it was "sidewalk level" so not above looking down like most resort pools so it was such fun to watch the action at the beach and promenade. And the pool is GORGEOUS. Simply gorgeous. We had stayed in a villa in Sanur and discovered this hotel as we stopped their for lunch one day (I had the best juice I've ever had). We walked through the hotel to get out to the main road and were very impressed by the grounds. Thus, when we found ourselves in Sanur for one last day/night before heading to the airport it was our first choice. Simply put, the pool/grounds are the best thing about this place. And the pool/grounds is extraordinary. That's where it ends though. My room really stunk. The staff watched as I carried a 50 lb suitcase up the stairs. I had two single beds which was also weird as I was one person (we each had our own rooms). And the complimentary breakfast was average (actually, after a month of complimentary breakfasts in Bali...this one was hands down the poorest). But...the pool area makes up for all of the other less than stellar features!

author: CharlieS879
title: Old, but beautiful location
text: My husband and I celebrated our 22 year wedding anniversary last week at this hotel and enjoyed our stay very much. Having been to Bali several times before, but never staying in Sanur, we decided the attraction of this hotel was its location. Right on the beach with wonderful views. Beautiful clean beach and free of "sellers" of any sort. The hotel itself is very old and needs desperate upgrades in the bedrooms and bathrooms. The pool area is small, but lovely with direct views straight onto the beach. Pool swim up bar was a little disappointing as not always manned and I think this is probably got to do with the main clientele of the hotel who are not interested really in using it. I would say the average age of the regaular repeat visitor to this hotel would be aged bedtween 70 – 85 years old. Some have been going for 40 years which really intrigued me. Even though it was a much older age group to ourselves, all the guest were very friendly and we had a great time getting know some of them and listening to local advise on where to eat , shop etc. I had a sneak peek into the future of retirement and I really liked what I saw!!!! Would not recommend it for teenage children or 20-35 year olds as it is way too quiet and boring for them. We wanted five days of sun, good food and drink and a little down time which this hotels offers. Staff are very friendly and accommodating and Sanur streets are so clean and quite compared to hectic Kuta, Legian and other parts of Bali. If it is rest, relaxation and bathing in the sun, this hotel is for you. There are more modern hotels in the area and so many great places to eat that choice is abundant.

author: kevinsL5972RG
title: Great Location and Homophobic
text: We are a gay male couple and as the title suggests "the Besakih Beach Hotel" is Homophobic. We were booked in for 6 nights but only stayed the one because we were made to feel that uncomfortable. Upon arrival there was an older woman at reception. No one helped us with our bags or welcomed us. When the receptionist realized we were 2 men wanting one room she then told us we would have to purchase another room and another 6 breakfasts because 2 men could not share the same bed. She then offered a room with twin beds. We finally got a room with a king bed down the rear of the resort well away from the pool restaurant beach and other guests. The room was nothing like the photos. They are old and tired and need updating. The cleaners need retraining. The towels are old crispy thread bare and yellow with age. Large ants crawled through the bed while we slept. The rooms have no safe but safe deposit boxes are available at reception, however you aren't allowed to keep a key. The hotel doesn't provide fresh bottled water in you room. Only a jug, but where is the water poured from? Breakfast is expensive poor and scarce and restaurant staff don't care. On the up side the resort has a great location, though small,the pool is great right on the beach and the grounds are pleasant. On the whole most of the staff were ok. It was only one Homophobic woman that ruined it for us.

author: Leecam33
title: In need of an upgrade.
text: Stayed at the Besakih last week. We had booked an upstairs standard room. When shown this room, climbing the unsteady stairs (I was sure to break my neck on these), opened the doors to the reek of toilet sanitizer. Instantly I knew I could not stay there. Spoke to the manager and negotiated an upgrade to a bungalow. This was much nicer but still very old. The bed was very soft and the bathroom in need of a upgrade. Breakfast was included in the price. This was very simple with no changes for 8 days. The staff all very friendly and the location absolutely wonderful. Beach on one side, road on other. An abundance of restuarants to choose from. The main pool lovely, but the people reserving the pool chairs all day every day very annoying. I really feel the staff need to stop this. Also the pool is in the shade all day so was quite cool at times. As for location I loved this resort but everything else I feel it is overpriced for what you get.

author: chrissieisawesum
title: Balinese style
text: This resort ticked all the right boxes. Traditional Balinese styling, right on the beach, swim up bar overlooking the beach and a central location to shops and restaurants. Perfect ! The restuarant is also right on the beach which I loved every morning to enjoy the breakfast which is a limited buffet style, rice,noodles,fruit and pancakes but you can also have eggs with bacon and tomato to accompany the buffet. The restuarant is open style to appreciate the gorgeous views. There is of course a water sports agent and massage area on the beach in front too. The gardens are lovely and each style of accommodation is arranged so to promote maximum privacy. The shops, markets and restuarants are right there and spread in both directions. But the negatives are few, the pool bar service is aweful. We spent each day hunting for someone to serve us and when they did they would dissappear again. Very frustrating and they lost a lot of money as we (4people) got fed up and went for a drink elsewhere for 7 days. The restuarant staff are not overly friendly or engaging and again we had to keep asking for coffee. The rooms (standard) while spacious and clean were a let down when it came to the bathroom which were quite tired and rundown. But overall I will definitely return to Besakih for its outstanding location alone. But ill get a bungalow instead.Beautiful.

author: 422roberto
title: Good but could be better
text: We arrived in the afternoon October 15th. We had to transfer our baggage to the foyer while the reception staff watched on with no acknowledgement of our arrival.No welcome drink; no refreshment towel; no big smile of welcome. We then did the usual you can have this great room (we had booked a bungalow) that we walked into and straight out of. They then gave us a bungalow we had paid for. (Are we the only people who have this problem?) As the other reviews state the rooms are badly in need of refurbishment but they were clean and tidy. Breakfast was not the fancy layout that we have had at other hotels in bali,but still adequate with a reasonable choice from bacon and eggs to pancakes,fruit cereal etc. Some of the serving staff need a happy pill. Others were fabulous; that could be said of all the staff from the top down and I think that they are a bit complacent compared to other places we have stayed. The hotel is in a great location with plenty of places to eat (we did not have a main meal at the resort) in the area. It is nowhere near as busy as Kuta so it is good for relaxing without the hassles of sellers - there are locals who are selling but in a very laid back way and very friendly. The beach is good and there is a great path along the beach to walk and cycle on. There is a reef which protects the beach therefore the water in the available swimming area is not very deep, depending on tide . The hotel had wi-fi in the lobby and the restaurant and I think they were extending that as we left. We met some lovely people there, very friendly guests and now, knowing what to expect, would love to return. It is an older hotel without all the trimmings, however, judging by the conversations we had with other guests, many people return year after year.

author: JulSydney
title: A great place to stay
text: I love staying at Besakih. Its the whole environment that makes it so enjoyable. The rooms are not that great but good enough for a pleasant stay and the air conditioning works well and there's plenty of water in the shower. But its not the room that makes a stay here so enjoyable. Its lovely walking through the hotel gardens, over the little bridge and out to the beach path. The beach path near Besakih has lots of cafes and restaurants as does the main road. Along the beach path are various markets also. The pools are nice. Its nice swimming in the big pool looking at the ocean and watching out over the beach path.The beach in front of the hotel is very nice and spacious and there are always plenty of beach chairs. There is also both shade and sun for you to sit in. The big trees are lovely The nail and massage ladies and boat men out front are also nice and don't nag you. It is also lovely sitting at breakfast looking out over the beach. The breakfast is a bit disappointing though. Overall a very enjoyable holiday can be had at Besakih if you are not particularly looking for 5 star rooms. Will definitely keep returning.

author: DebraH994
title: Manager says "Go to another hotel if you don't like it "
text: This was my second stay here and unfortunately the last. On arrival everything was great. Then our airconditioner didnot work. Yes we changed rooms after 2days and alot of discussion. The cleanliness of the room and especially the bathroom is terrible after bleaching the toilet ect it was marginally better. Within the first week our shower drain was blocked and we reported it several times to be told yes we have fixed it. The basin sink my husband ended up unblocking it himself,the stuff that came out of it was enough to make you dry reach!! As for the clean bed linen that was a joke, especially on our second last night we go to get into our freshly changed sheets to find it covered in sand, small leaves and a few dead bugs!!! I reported this to the manager also telling him about the drains which were still had not fixed. I then had 6 of them follow me back to our room to see what the problem was. I showed him the stuff out of the sink drain and then the blocked shower which they finally put the plunger over it sucked a coulpe of times (It fixed now ) was the reply. Once again after using the shower it was still blocked and shrugged off again!!! Then on our last day you could not swim in the main pool as it was off. A very nice couple which we met up with over there and have also been staying here for several years reported this to the manger. The managers reply was that they knew about it and that the filter was broken, but not enough money to fix it, our friend said that at the end of the day it's not good enough as we are paying for facilities we can't use. To all of our disbelief the managers response was " If you don't like it go and stay at another hotel" We will be finding another hotel as there are several hotels alongside the Besakih which are the same advertised price and offer alot more for your money!!!!

author: sharkbait_two
title: good all rounder
text: After having been to Bali several times before ths was our first stay in Sanur. We decided to stay at the Besakih beause of the location and the reviews. We were met at reception by Sri and found her very efficient and quite helpful. The layout of the grounds is quite nice with 2 pools, one with a swim up bar. They are not big pools but do the job well . This suited us as we dont like the big resort feel. The restaurant faces the beach with some dining on the beach. The beer is cold and the food is tasty and cheap enough. Breakfast was cooked well and the coffee very good. The rooms are big enough and clean. The only criticism is that in the bathrooms there is obvious signs of age. Tiles replaced and the grout is not a good match. Bit of grime in some corners, however overall not too bad. The location is excellent. Just walk out the front and you are on the beach front walk way. This is much better than the Tanjung Benoa / Nusa Dua one. For the most part it is flat and tree covered. There are lots of good places to eat and some markets nearby. Hardys shopping mall is a 10 minute walk. Overall we liked it and would definitely stay here again

author: StephanieM611
title: Beautiful Gardens, Excellent Location, Great for young kids, Clean and Large Rooms
text: We stayed here during Nyepi, mid March. This hotel is really beautiful, with lovely tropical gardens, and in the right location. It's right on the beach and very close to restaurants, Hardy's Shopping Centre, laundries, Mini Marts etc. The Besakih gardens kept my young toddler and preschooler amused with their scattered fish ponds, turtles, lizards, statues and the resident cat and dog. The pool is great, very clean, and has a separate area for the young kids. Plenty of sunbeds, whether it be poolside or on the beach. Also the pool is in a sunny location, as the sun swings round there are nice shaded areas too, so it's great for anyone. We stayed in a superior stand alone bungalow, which was spacious and very clean. Even though we were right next to the reception and driveway, it was very quiet inside the room. The friendly cleaning staff did a great job, our rooms cleaned everyday, and tea/coffee replenished. Pool towels were supplied, and if we needed them swapped over for clean ones, all we needed to do was ask. Only negative was the restaurant staff, who were snobby and their table service was zero. We found this very strange as all the other staff were very nice and welcoming. The breakfast was great, fresh and hot. They had nasi goreng, mie goreng, toast, pancakes, fruit, juice, and cakes. No water is supplied, but shops are close by.

author: gambrinusmare
title: What a pleasant surprise!
text: We are a family of 4 from Italy and have just spent a fanastic week at this beach resort, it was our first time in Bali. I really can't understand why so many people are disappointed with the Besakih and write such negative reviews? On our arrival, kind & smiling staff gave us a warm welcome and immediately took the lugguage to our room. All the staff in the resort were very nice and always with a smile on their face. The restaurant is very cozy with amazing sea views, it was beautiful to sit and have breakfast basically right on the beach! We really enjoyed, every morning, the fresh homemade pancakes, fluffy scrambled eggs and the local fruit but there was also omeletts with bacon & sausage and always served quickly, so the breakfast was totally fine. The food in whole was always tasty and authentic, the noodles were delicious and we never once had a bad lunch or dinner. Our room was basic but very clean and of a decent dimension, the sheets were changed every second day and the towels daily. We knew we were not going to a luxury resort as it was not exspensive so we did not expect 5 star accomodation. However the air con worked great and we had a modern flat screen tv. The saftey deposit box was at reception and free of charge as was wi-fi, which was in the lobby & restaurant. The 2 pools were small but lovely and there were plenty of sunbeds & parasol's, but the great thing was that the pools and bar were right next to the beach so for us this was handy as the kids could go backwards & forwards and we, from the beach, could always have an eye on them! Lastly the gardens were well looked after, clean and with little ponds with fish & turtles. All in all we have fond memories of this small & friendly balinesse style hotel, with it's great location and would definately not hesitate to go back again. Lisa, Gianni & girls from Italy.

author: cbimages
title: Make sure you get the room that you paid for
text: stayed at Besakih 10-15 October, our room bought and paid for via Qantas Holidays. We had the choice of booking a standard room, or a superior bungalow and chose the higher priced bungalow. Price difference was around $80 for the 5 nights. A week before arrival, I e-mailed the hotel to confirm our booking/arrival time and requested an upstairs bungalow room if one was available. On arrival, check in was quick and we were shown to an upstairs room in a stand alone building which also had a downstairs room. The room was old, but had recently been painted and was reasonably clean. The bed was quite soft and a bit saggy, but OK. The main light in the room did not work. Upon request, we were given a spare pillow each and beach towels were brought to our room. Someone arrived very quickly to fix the broken light. Staff were helpful and pleasant. Breakfasts were OK, with a small buffet and cooked to order eggs/bacon etc. Wifi was free and available in both restaurant and lobby. The day before we were due to leave, we decided to return to the Besakih on our next trip, perhaps staying in a standard room, so went to reception to ask if we could look at a standard room, to help us decide about our next stay. We were most surprised to be told that we had been "downgraded" and were actually staying in a standard room as no upstairs superior bungalow was available for us. We had not been told this upon check in nor had we been given a choice of taking a downstairs room of the standard we had paid for. I have notified Qantas Holidays of this and am awaiting a reply. Otherwise, we did enjoy our time at the Besakih and will still consider returning nest trip......but will only pay for a standard room!

author: polly95
title: Awful Awful AWFUL!
text: Rooms are so out of date. We arrived at 1pm to be told that one of our rooms wouldnt be ready until 7pm. Not acceptable. I approached Reception on my own and was met with a VERY rude and sarcastic man telling me that there was nothing he could do and also telling me we were not checkin out until 6pm on our leaving date, I then explained that we had paid for late check out. That put him back in his box. The air cons dont work (we were in 3 rooms) the rooms are full of mozzies. The breakfast is CRAP! The location is perfect, the driver who sits in the hut out the front is wonderful, we used him twice. The Pool chairs get taken by all the oldies very early int he morning. If you are under 40 years old I would not reccommend staying here. I regret not listening to by fellow trip advisors warning me about this hotel. It left a very sour taste in our mouth. I have never come across such awfully rude reception staff in my time in bali. Please listen to this review. I would hate for you to regret your stay here like we did

author: Dorno
title: A Nice Hotel for the price
text: This was our 3rd trip to Bali but was our First stay at the Besakih Hotel. We enjoyed our stay very much and would have no trouble in staying there again. We stayed in a standard Bungalow and although the room was not what I expected because of the word bungalow it was still just your normal type of room . It was a basic room but comfortable and had all the things you need in a room. I wll have to disagree with earlier comments from others complaining about the beds because even tough I have had spinal surgery I found the bed reasonably comfortable. It was a great place to stay and is great value for a few reasons. The main reason is that it is right on the beach and there are not many hotels where you can swim up to the edge of the pool and be only a few feet from the sand of the ocean. Also it is only a short walk to the markets along the beach boardwalk where you will also find some great restaurants and bars. Another great thing for us was the fact that there were no hawkers on the beach in the hotels section of the beach so you could rest and sunbake in peace. There were however plenty of hawkers once you went outside the area designated to the Besakih hotel. Sun lounges tended to be hard to get but the staff were all extremely friendly and helpful with your needs and always managed to move things around and find you a spot. The Breakfast was a basic breakfast with bacon eggs and some other bits and pieces you generally get in a breakfast and was ok. Restaurant and bar prices were reasonable and I could not fault any of the meals that I had while staying in the hotel. They made the best Garlic bread that I have had at any restaurant I have eaten at in all my travels. So taking everything into consideration I think the hotel was great value for money and would certainly have no trouble staying there again. I think this is a nice hotel and the problem arises when people are expecting 5 Star accommodation at 3 star prices

author: 849RobertB
title: Putrid Bathroom, smart-mouthed Reception Man
text: My room was booked as 'Run of the House'. Very strange room classification. Anyway I received a 'Standard' room. Room was ok although very dated, and did not have a clean feel about it. Old paper-thin curtains, so a lot of early sunlight. There was a paper-thin back door and outside of that there were 2 very loud and noisy aircond. compressors that made sleep difficult. There was an electric jug, but no coffee/tea/milk and no complimentary drinking water. I thought that was just an error and so I queried it at reception only to get 'smart mouth' responses from man at reception. Anyway the result was that these are not included in a 'Standard' room. The worst thing about the room was that the bathroom was like something that you would find in a back alley in Mumbai. It was disgusting. White tiles cracked or broken, and the white grouting every colour of filth except white. I felt like I needed a shower after being in there. The resort grounds were pleasant, pool and restaurant ok. If you get a cheap deal and can handle noisy aircond and filthy bathroom, then I recommend book for the location/price. If you want modern, clean, polite, and classy, then I recommend next door at Griya, which I saw 'first-hand' because friends were staying there.

author: 281MichaelS281
title: Clearly 3 Star
text: Well our first night was a disappointment!!, as a couple!, still very much in love! we were given what can only be discribed as a Granny Flat with two single beds!! the bathroom had a hole in the roof and the tiles are filthy with grime from what era im unsure!! the bath leaks all over the floor! so you can imagine after flying 6000 miles i wasn't happy!!.....However after complaining the next day!, at first they were going to charge me more money!! to have a double bed!!! which was shocking! but after speaking direct to the Manager! she was very helpful even if she looked unhappy with having to change us, the room we moved to was far better it was clean but was still a standard room! so don't be fooled!! There are also NO Curtains!! in any of the rooms!!, just a thin effort of a blind that by 4am you will wakeup from the light shinning through" See Pictures " ,finally we could enjoy our Holiday, the grounds are well looked after and the staff that create this are very friendly and helpful, The resturant is nice for proper dinner etc but breakfast is a disaster!! and drinks are over priced but this is the case with most resturants!! its far easier to buy beer etc from the local shops and keep in your fridge at the hotel, the Beach is okay but the 8 days we were there it was never cleaned, but it is swimmable " See Pictures ", The whole resort is really for 60 years plus as you will see!! however everyone we met was friendly and age wasn't a problem for us but maybe for younger couples!!, THERE IS NO WIFI IN THIS HOTEL!!!! Just a poor connection in the Reception!! and resturant ONLY!!, also i advise you get a tshirt made saying NO I DON'T WANT TRANSPORT & NO I DON'T WANT A MASSAGE!! as this is all you will hear throughout your time in Bali.....if i can recommend anywhere it would be Nusa Dua Beach!! which is really Paradise and Clean and looked after and is only a short cab ride away "about 5 miles".

author: jessh423
title: Good starting point, but not for the young.
text: We decided to use Besakih as our starting point. The hotel itself is rather nice and suited us for the beginning of our holiday (we'd never been to Bali before) the staff were welcoming and helpful but once we got to our room we were a bit disappointed, the beds were twin beds not the queen requested & the bathroom was of a poor standard (we were scared to use the towels on offer). However we decided to let it go and enjoy the start of being in Bali. As it was a late arrival we stayed in the twin room and organised for the beds to be put together properly the next day, when we woke on our first day in Sanur we were shocked by the view from the restaurant. It was beautiful it didn't even bother us how bad the breakfast was we were to busy enjoying the view and admiring the pool area. The best thing about the resort is the pool area and the restaurant area, they are without a lie stunning and you instantly feel relaxed walking down to them. We had no trouble ordering drinks all day by the pool but after eating once there decided to give it a miss as the food isn't that good. However the pool bar menu is decently priced and you can easily get drunk hanging by the pool all day. The downside to the pool area is that someone must have told all the old pensioners and retirees that its cheaper to retire at this resort in Bali then it is in Australia because they are everywhere. And with nothing for them to do, they hog up all the sunloungers & complain about everything all the other holidayers are doing.I don't have any issues with the older generation being on holiday in fact its a great idea for them and some of them were lovely to have a chat with but then there were some that took it upon themselves to make sure no-one was going to have a good time, only themselves. In fact on multiple occasions we were confronted by these patrons over small things like moving someone's (who was using two) top to the sunlounger to use on an empty one. By the end of the stay we felt that we needed to really watch what we were doing, so we didn't evoke nosy people to give us their 10c of what we were doing. And being two young couples we felt we were watched constantly and as we spoke to other holidayers we found that it's become the norm at this resort & that there are groups of older patrons that stay months on end, know eachother and put their nose in everyone's business because they feel that it's their business. *tip bring down from the room the information paper that states no one can save a sun lounger for more then 2 hrs, you might need it to remind them that its a resort for everyone not just them. Because they honestly get to the pool area at 7am put towels down and head off doing whatever they do & come back in the later arvo when the sun loungers are in the sun but its getting cooler, once back they expect to have the sun lounger still waiting for them & the staff do nothing about it & if you tick the older patrons off you might get a telling off for doing nothing out of the ordinary at a resort. For young people I'd advise not staying here unless you are patient enough and can ignore the glares & rules concocted up from the older patrons, other then that and the bathroom its a great, cheap starting point that is of a good standard. The staff are lovely, the beach is beautiful and view from the pool area & restaurant are breathtaking.

author: sdpaine
title: Nice hotel and staff
text: This was our third time at this hotel and it didn't disappoint. It still has a beautiful garden, nice friendly staff and a wonderful private feel to it. All the rooms have either a balcony or patio. A nice touch is the clothes dryer/airer also all rooms have umbrellas available. The hotel has a town frontage (set back from the road) so all the restaurants, bars and shops are a short walk away and Hardy's is about 10 minutes walk. The rear of the place goes down to the beach where a swimming pool overlooks the beach. A path walk can be taken in any direction for a good few kilometres. Access along this path can be made to the main road at anytime by following the numerous side roads or taking a short cut through the many hotels. Breakfast is taken in the restaurant which looks out to the sunrise over Sanur Beach and is more than adequate, but is not of a buffet type (as has been intimated by some reviews). If you wanted to 'knit pick' perhaps the bathrooms could do with a makeover and some of the mould removed but this is Bali after all. Our air conditioner broke down whilst we were there but it was mended within a couple of hours. The hotel provides towels for the pool and beach, unfortunately people will always use these to reserve beach loungers provide on the adjacent beach. On this visit unless you were up by at least 6am. any hope of a lounger was gone in what might be called the shadier, cooler areas. Many of the selfish guests that were responsible for this practice didn't turn up until 9 or 10 later in the day. We even witnessed the unsavoury spectacle of a guest removing anothers towel from a reserved lounger and replacing it with his, culminating in a near fight in what in the past we have referred to 'a bit of paradise'. It did seem that there were a few guests that had been at the hotel for a prolonged stay and felt they owned their 'pitch' so to speak. The whole spectical reminded us of the old package type holidays in Europe, but in this case played out by some very arrogant Australian tourists. This should not distract from the hotels charm, although it did seem that some of the security empolyed by the hotel were complicit in the 'reservation' proceedure, which did shed some light on how the late arrivals in the morning managed to get their towels there so early. All in all though, no one should be disappointed with such a good choice of hotel in a good location.

author: PerthNataliePerth
title: Great First Trip To Bali
text: My husband and I went on our first holiday to Bali. We enjoyed 5 nights at the Besakih Beach Resort in Sanur and were very happy staying there. We loved Sanur as it was very quiet and none of the rush and pressure of Kuta which was exactly what we were hoping for. The grounds were kept immaculately and the ground staff should be congratulated on how clean and well presented they were. The staff were friendly and helpful. Our room was a standard room - basic but definately acceptable. The room was spacious enough, extremely clean and the bed was very comfortable. The bathroom was a little dated and probably in need of a revamp but thoroughly clean which was all that mattered. The breakfast was just ok and for this reason we didn't eat at the restaurant any other time. But there is a restaurant called The Village just down the road which is sensational and we ate there almost every night. One bit of advice, if you're going to do the white water rafting don't book through the hotel who one of the staff members "knows someone who is a bit cheaper" . Although it was a pleasant day with a really nice driver and people doing to rafting, it wasn't very long and along a fairly calm bit of the river. My husband and I are in our mid and late 40's and we would have been some of the youngest guest staying at the hotel. There were many many senior dutch people who come over for 3 months at a time. Whilst this didn't bother us in the least, if you were young people looking to mix and mingle this property probably wouldn't suit you for that reason. All in all we were very happy staying here. Would probably book a bungalow next time as they looked beautiful.

author: TonesterWA
title: We'll be back!
text: We've been regular visitors to Bali since 1984 - generally coming at least once a year for the past fifteen years. We prefer the relative peacefulness of Sanur over the hustle and bustle of Kuta, Legian and Seminyak. Whilst having walked past Besakih many times we had not stayed here before but, based on other travellers' reviews, we decided to stay for a week in early December. We're glad we did! We booked direct with the resort, no deposit required. When we arrived we received a warm welcome and no need to prepay for any nights at check-in. Our renovated standard room (#294) was fine - reasonably spacious with nice terrace and a clean bathroom. The room was in the section closest to the road but once inside we didn't hear any noise. The beds were comfortable, linen changed every second day and pool towels supplied to your room. The resort grounds are lovely with a nice garden and some small ponds (one with a couple of turtles). The TV had a very limited range of channels (no movie channels) but that wasn't an issue for us. As others have described, the pool and resturant is beachside - a great view to start each day. Whilst the choice at breakfast is limited it is fine and you can swap selections. We had no problems in securing poolside lounges but we preferred to sit under the big trees on the beach. We really liked the friendly staff at Besakih, many of whom are older and seem to have worked at the resort for many years. No request seemed too much trouble for them. Besakih's location is ideal for us - instant access to the beach and the beachside footpath, 10 minutes walk to the Sindhu Beach area (including the wonderful Lutu's Coffee Shop) and 10 minutes walk to Hardys supermarket. On the street side it is easy to catch a bemo or taxi and there is a good selection of resturants, massage places, laundries and shops in walking distance. All in all, we really enjoyed our stay and we'll be back.

author: miles_wa
title: Good location for the price
text: We stayed for a weekend at Besakih in a corporate group of 14 (a Christmas party for staff from Western Australia). We had seven standard rooms, all on the second floor. Overall, the hotel was adequate with what we wanted; a fairly central location where those who wanted to walk the neighborhood could, and those on motorbikes were able to venture further. Communications via email were good. Strangely enough, this is possibly the first place I have ever stayed in Bali (and this was my seventh visit to Bali) that didn't have any form of airport transfer. Fine by me, as we have a good driver we use, who was happy to arrange three vehicles to move us. First, the bedrooms. Adequate yet a little tired looking. They weren't the cleanest I have ever stayed in, nor were they the worst; an average score would apply here. Airconditioning was good, and having a balcony was great. The pool was nice, with wonderful views of the beach which was literally metres from the pool and restaurant, which are located right on the Sanur boardwalk. There was a pool bar which looked very unused; no staff or fridges, etc. Nice gardens with ponds full of fish, a large chess set and pool table available, along with shelves of reading matter. There was a manned security booth at the front, and the place was well lit in the evenings. We only had breakfast at the restaurant. The fare was average Western breakfasts, however we heard they do offer an Indonesian option, however didn't see it offered. Staff were polite but not overly warm. If you're looking for a fairly cheap spot to explore Sanur, then this fits the bill. If you are looking for super-friendly staff and a romantic location, you'd be better off finding somewhere else. Overall, I give Besakih an average score.

author: AnnieBundaberg
title: Lovely Hotel, Top Location!
text: Besakih Beach Resort was the last hotel of our 3 week visit to Bali. After staying at the beautiful Ubud Village Hotel for 1 week then on to the Kuta Lagoon Resort (which we did not enjoy very much) we were hoping that Besakih (for our final week) would at least be on par with Ubud Village Hotel. We were not disappointed! Besakih was beautiful. The rooms were large and clean, fitting 3 of us in comfort all on single beds. The staff were lovely and ready to help with any request. The restaurant serves a variety of food and each meal we tried was delicious (and it is set right on the beach so a lovely place to eat). The location of this hotel is spot on. Just about the best stretch of Sanur beach. I have stayed at other hotels along Sanur beach but this location is by far the best. Beautifully kept grounds complete this hotel. Be sure to wake early and treat yourself to a 'Sanur Sunrise' This is a truly spectacular sight and it is so convenient to walk out of your hotel room straight down onto the beach to enjoy this magical part of the day. There is also about a 5km 'boardwalk' along Sanur beach with plenty of other hotels and eateries along the way. There are hagglers here but it is all good fun and nothing like the pinching and poking experienced at Kuta. Heading out onto the street you can find plenty of other restaurants to eat at and the large Hardys Supermarket to stock up, a short walk to the left as you leave the hotel. Sanur is a 'quiet' part of Bali and a wonderful place to re-charge your batteries and Besakih Beach Hotel is a wonderful base to do that from. The photos I have included were taken on an Olympus palm size camera and no photo shopping has been done. The sunrises really do look like that!

author: Lasty
title: Great as usual like a second home in Bali
text: We have stayed at Besakih five times now. We spent another two weeks there in June. This time we stayed in Bungalow 277 which is up the back next reception. I twas a great spot the room had been renovated and was on the first floor. We sat outside most afternnoons on the balcony having a drink looking over the gardens. The only problem was the Frangipani tree in front of our room. Every afternoon we sat out there seemed to be the same time two pigeons started getting it on, and from all the fluttering looked like they were struggling. The resort is not the flashest but is in a great spot and has one of the best pools in Sanur which comes right up next to the board walk. All the stafff from the gardiners, to the waiters are friendly. This place has a charm to it. If you sit back you will see how many of the guests at the resort are repeat guests. Betsy the resort dog is still roaming around looking for free feeds and pats. She see seems to have an afternoon round when everyone if having afternoon drinks on their balcony. We also made friends with Ronnie the male dog who spends the day chasing the squirrels around in the tree's. We became pretty fond of Ronnie and he would sit with us on our balcony or come for walks with us down the road or beach. He even started waiting for us on our balcony in the morning.

author: sdpaine
title: Peaceful and friendly, true Bali.
text: The hotel was situated in central Sanur and on the beach. We had been there a few years ago so went with the trepidation it would not live up to our memories. It did. Since our last visit the hotel was having a upgrade. The rooms/ detatched chalets were new and clean. The showers, air conditioning and facilities were first class. All the rooms seem to have a balcony and offer some privacy (dependent on position). The breakfast is fresh fruit or juice, followed by eggs to order and toast etc. (part of the room charge). The staff were so friendly and helpful, and it was obvious many couples returned year after year, a recommendation in itself! All at budget prices! The hotel was close to the beach (only worth swimming at high tide) had a nice pool and adequate sunbeds. You walk out the front of the hotel into central Sanur, with many eating and drinking establishments. I recommend the RIB restaurant, turn left for about 200m. Nice Indonesian food and a good price. Don't tell too many people as we want to go back again next year. (Keep it a secret between us).

author: Luckett90
title: Thank you Besakih we will be back next year
text: Just returned from a week stay at Besakih and loved it. We traveled with four children under 12 and found that the location and environment offered by Besakih suited our family perfectly. Because of the location of pool right on the beach we could watch the kids to play while we enjoyed a massage or manicure. How good is that? The staff were friendly and I felt relaxed and comfortable at this resort. The breakfast was enjoyable and watching the sunrise as I at bananna pancakes was a great way to start the day. There was plenty of water sports available just in frount of the resort and lots of fun shopping to keep you busy. The rooms were comfortable and cleaned every day including clean sheets and towels. Water was avalible from the cooler near by so you could top up your water bottles everyday. Save buying all the time so that was helpful. We stayed in the section yet to be renovated so the bathroom was a bit tired but for the price and the fact that we didn't spend alot of time in the room it was hardly noticed. Lots of great placees to eat nearby and we had fun trying a different one each day. Ribs was great and yes I had the ribs. You must go to the Bali Safari and Marine Park and Water Bomb Park if you have kids a very different experience to any in Australia. Thanks Besakih we will be back for sure.

author: greygrump
title: Great value and location
text: Our first trip to Bali and the Besakih was recommended. We spent 4 nights there. For the price it was excellent value. Beautiful gardens. Room made up each day. Some have commented on breakfast, we found it very adequate and the bringing of our own cereal unnecessary and not used. The rooms don't provide tea or coffee, so bring your own. We also found small packets of long life milk helpful. There is a bar fridge with cold drinks available. There is also safe water provided for the kettle. The bathroom is a little tired, but fine. We found air conditioner didn't really cope to well. Great shaded area around pool. For $80 a night we would go there again. Also free wifi in hotel lobby was fast and easy to access.

author: jillybean66
title: Would stay again
text: We have just recently stayed at the Besakih Beach Resort. As previously said the rooms are fine. For the price compared to what you would get in Australia they are very comfortable. Things to remember if you come over are that they do not supply tea,coffee or sugar. Also no shampoo etc. They supply linen, towels, beach towels, shower caps and soap. So bring your own coffee if you can because theirs is very strong...even brands bought from the local shops. I would also recommend popping in a couple of coffee mugs if your a drinker. Cups supplied are very small. Breakfast is basic and wore a little thin after 10 days. But everywhere around supplies the same. Bring your on cereal as there isnt anything like that in Bali really either. Food can be bought in ok. Other than that the hotel surroundings are just beautiful. The pool location is suburb and we found the hotel restaurant really reasonable there are also many nice restaurants nearby. We met many lovely people while we stayed there and would definately come again...with a few extra home comforts:)

author: VessFlutterby
title: Great Location. Room OK. B’fast Basic.
text: The Besakih has a good location right in the middle of the Sanur Beach strip and the main road. It also has a lovely pool right on the beach front (ideal for quiet night time swims). The hotel is on the cheaper side, so if on a budget it is not bad if wanting a hotel on the beach. However we were disappointed with a few things. The rooms and bathrooms are very tired. The bathroom needs a really good scrub and upgrade. The rooms smelt a bit musty and it was a bit dark is there is no main room light. The TVs need replacing, to something larger than a postage stamp! The standard room did not include complimentary toiletries, tea or coffee, which is a first for us. I must mention though that the garden and room service staff were friendly and one of the maids asked if she could have my liquid lipstick that I had thrown in to the bin (it was rather new but I did not like the colour). I left her another one the next day. I wouldn’t dream of using someone else’s lipstick, but it obviously was something she couldn’t afford and liked. The older reception and restaurant staff members were not friendly at all and seemed quite disinterested. The older male staff member at breakfast did not explain the set menu breakfast options (very basic) properly so we were left a little hungry. After a few days, a younger male staff members was more helpful and we received a better breakfast. We were tempted to upgrade to the only suite available at the Besakih, however they said the upgrade would be $160 USD to upgrade. We had already paid $80 for the standard room, and the Suite was $200 per night, so thought it would have been $120 or slightly better, but not the case, so didn’t upgrade. In summary, the hotel has a great location and not bad if on a budget, however I wouldn’t feel comfortable recommending this hotel, especially to someone wanting a romantic getaway or a fun hotel for the kids.

author: delboyPerth
title: Besakih ! Stop the cut backs please.
text: My wife & I have just arrived back from a week at the Besakih. I have wrote reviews about this resort before and I have stayed here many times as recent as about 6 months ago listing good points about the location and staff blah! blah! blah! and so on but, I have noticed this time a real deterioration, cut backs to the point that it has lost the identity it used to have. Seemingly gone are a lot of the friendly old staff who made the Besakih the place it used to be. There are trainees everywhere basically cheap labour. They are all friendly enough but it's not the same. The resort of course still has arguably the best location on Sanur beach in combination with restaurants and shops on the main drag. The rooms are clean without frills and that's fine unless you like to spend your holiday in your room. Any reader of Tripadvisor considering staying here should book a room without breakfast. The breakfast has quite possibly become the worst of breakfasts of any place I have ever stayed, the choice is small and you will be eating the worst quality food you can purchase, that I can guarantee. The swimming pool is good but it is difficult to get a chair unless you go very early and put your towel on one to claim it for the day, whether you are sitting round the pool or not. I have never been able to understand the inconsideration of people who do this, but it was prevalent in the week we stayed.( This is the resorts fault to allow it to happen) Sorry to sound so negative regarding this. I am just trying to help the Tripadvisor readers the best way I can in making their decision to stay. So to Tripadvisor readers who are considering this resort my opinion is:- Location Excellent. Rooms Clean average 3 star. Staff Possibly the same as any other small resort.( This used to be the Besakih's strength) Pool Good but you may not get a chair. Breakfast The worst of the worst. Value for money Average, but guests want good value for money.

author: delboyPerth
title: The alluring Besakih.
text: My wife and I have just returned from staying at the Besakih. We have stayed here many times and every time we leave I say " next time we will stay somewhere different" The fact is we did stay at the Griya Santrian next door once but, we just get drawn to staying at the Besakih because the staff are so friendly and the location is so good. The rooms are as basic as you can get and that includes the newly refurbished ones. The rooms do get cleaned everyday and you get clean sheets everyday. The breakfast is not a buffet and the choice is very limited.There really are no luxuries here. There is nothing pretentious about the Besakih, they know they are not a four or five star and they don't try to be which is evident in their prices. The meals, drinks etc. are very cheap in fact cheaper than most of the restaurants on the main street. The Besakih has two wonderful swimming pools. One of the pools is located right on the edge of the beach, this is a great spot to relax and watch the day go by. You will find that many people staying at the Besakih have stayed there before. I was speaking to one guest who said it was the 38th time he has stayed there. The hotel is generally frequented by mature guests. I really don't think the Besakih is good for the younger or party animal types. If I do return to Sanur I am sure I will scour the internet looking for places to stay and probably finish up staying here again.

author: stick751
title: Perfect location - dated but friendly and clean
text: Stayed from the 22nd of December to the 2nd of January. To be honest we went expecting the worst and were pleasantly surprised. Yes the hotel is dated and could do with a refurbishment but they don't claim to be a 4 star hotel. Initially we were placed in a bungalow with 2 single beds and an extra bed for our 4 year old. Was a little squishy but the reception kindly gave us another bungalow with a queen and the extra bed. We had was with the aircon which they did try and fix promptly. It never really worked properly but it was still bearable. The only other qualm was that the room service menu said it opened at 10am. Feeling a bit off colour one day and not wanting breakfast we waited till 10.15am and were abruptly told we couldn't order because they were too busy! My husband then rang and was hung up on after ordering one item and then after ringing back was also told that we couldn't order as they were busy and we had to wait till 11am to order. We ended up going out, not that we felt like it. The breakfast is fine but after 7 days we chose to try other places. The grounds are lovely and the pool over looks the beach. Betsie the dog is a character as is the pet cat. The hotel is placed in the best location amongst lots of awesome restaurants. And yes, I would stay there again.

author: hailz19
title: Do not stay if you want a clean room
text: Oh my god! this was the worst place i have ever stayed. I have stayed in backpackers cleaner and newer than this. The resort is falling apart. We arrived at reception after spending a lovely few days in Ubud and was greeted with a snarl by reception staff. When my father pointed out that their reception area looked like it might have termites they replied with 'yeah, big problem here'. Why would you not do something about it. The friendliest member of staff we came across was a dog that greeted us when we got out of the car... There were termites flying all in the room. The room looked like it was 100 years old and as i was a 3rd person in the room i hade a rollaway bed.. it looked like the mattress was rotting. The bathroom made me think i would catch something if i sat on the toilet and the drain in the shower was filled with someone elses hair, so much so that the water didnt drain. The pub across the road was infested with rats, not just a few but a whole colony in the football jerseys pinned to the roof. This whole area is sleazy, dirty and vile. Would never go back to Sanur because of this experience.

author: KateCaringbah
title: Loved the Besakih
text: We have just returned from 7 days at the Besakih and I can highly recommend this hotel. It is situated on what I believe to be the best position on Sanur Beach. Close to shops, restaurants, convenience store and markets. It is on a lovely stretch of beach, whereas other hotels have very little beachfront when the tide comes in. The horizon pool is absolute beachfront and you can swim in the pool and gaze at Mt Agung in the distance. The hotel is frequented by regular older clients who have been coming here for 30 years. The advantage of this to my 2 teenagers was that they had the pools to themselves at most times, the older guests preferring to just laze about the beach or pool and read all day. There were a few younger couples and little ones about and all guests seem to get on well. The only downside was that the hotel is being refurbished at the moment and there was a fair bit of noise, for which the manager personally apologized for. Rooms are quite large with nice verandahs, but the bathrooms not so good, being very mouldy. I figured that I probably only spend 1 hour out of 24 in the bathroom, so it wasnt such a big deal, unfortunately they dont seem to have included bathroom renovations in the refurbishment. I believe they will be raising the prices by 10% when the refurbishment is complete. Staff were all lovely and we knew most of them by name after 7 days. They also have 2 pet dogs and a cat which made my kids feel like they were at home. We loved Sanur, a lovely way to settle into Bali, much quieter than the other side of the island. Would I return to the Besakih, definately and look forward to doing so in the future.

author: phillandsuzi
title: Love Sanur! Love Besakih Hotel! Love the shopping!
text: When our son told us he was getting married in Bali we were less than enthusiastic. However, we have just returned from 8 glorious - picture perfect - relaxing and stress free days in Bali. On top of that it was really inexpensive! The wedding was beautiful, the staff at Besakih Beach Hotel went out of their way to ensure that our new daughter-in-law had the day she had dreamed of. The Besakih was a great hotel, after a week most of the staff new us by name - and all had great joy teaching me snippets of Balinese! We had swims at midnight in the pool - surface covered with floating frangipanis (courtesy of nearby trees) - it was glorious. Lunch at the swim-up bar - didn't even have to get out of the pool! Everything was beautiful - I would be back there tomorrow if I could be! Some tips for good shopping - once you have purchased an item - like a necklace or a sarong - wear it next time you go shopping. The hawkers will try to sell you more - will ask how much you paid - and offer to sell for less. Tell them what price you want - we tended to get things for less than half the price we purchased the first necklace or sarong for! Was much easier than cold haggling - the hawkers knew we had some experience. They will often try to take you for a ride if they know you have just arrived. Just tell them you have been there for a week even if you have just arrived! And you have already bought too many/much. If it is your first purchase - aim to get the item for roughtly half their initial price. It really helped me to write a rough conversion sheet on a business card and kept it in my purse - so you know roughly how much money you are talking about when haggling. Work out in your head what you want to pay - but don't be too tough - these people are really struggling with the lack of tourists. Although several times I had to walk off before getting what I wanted for the right price.

author: Klcboyd
title: We Will Be Back
text: My husband, myself and two other couples stayed at Stella Maris this past January. We rented the Rainbow House which we found to be spacious, clean and well stocked. The view was spectacular as was the infinity pool. For the most part, we found the resort staff to be very helpful and accommodating. We were able to arrange a rental car which they had waiting for us as well as fishing guides. The food at the resort was very good and they had a nice variety. We found the prices comparable to other Bahamian islands. We also had a chef cook for us at home one night and frequented a local spot for dinner another night. You also have the option to order in pizza which we would like to try another time. We really enjoyed the rum punch party/steak night on Saturday night. Well worth it and a great assortment of sides to go with a generous sized steak. The band at the party was very entertaining and festive and all of the people whom we met were very friendly and welcoming. There was a liquor store and grocery store about 6 miles away and both were reasonably priced and fairly well stocked. We were also able to have some groceries ordered for our arrival which was great perk. I would definitely recommend renting a vehicle as we were able to travel around the island, explore different beaches etc. From a fishing point of view, our husbands liked the fact that they could do some do it yourself bonefishing from the flats /mangroves as well as have the option of guides. We are already planning to go back next year. Thank -you to Jill and her staff for a wonderful week:)

author: PJD591
title: Just press "Pause"
text: Working in a Nassau for a couple of months I decided to take a weekend to experience bone fishing and mark it off my "Bucket List". What I wasn't expecting was to fall in love with this beautiful, untainted piece of paradise. After landing at the airport I was greeted immediately by a taxi who was waiting for me....then a pleasant short drive to the resort. Check-in was friendly and warm. Immediately felt like a VIP but transported back in time where there was no television or work station in my room, no keys as no one locks the door and the staff greeted me by my first name. Of course after sitting back and taking in the view from my room I quickly decided that I needed to venture down to the water.
