There is a small parking place outside, but you hardly have the chance to ever find a free spot. The hotel has a very good, luxurious standard. However, breakfast is not served before 7 am (and sometimes, not everything is available at 7 am, like the scrambled eggs…), which for some business travelers may be too late. It is not understandable for a hotel of this category. Anyway, the breakfast standard is excellent, but allow enough time for it… In summary: all is OK if you have enough time. Everything seems to take a little longer than in most chain-hotels, like checking out, for example. Nevertheless, I still recommend it very much. I come back again and again, in fact I forgot exactly how many times I already stayed there. I hope my notes are not seen as a criticism, but as an opportunity to improve the standards. And I will be back in one week again. Friendly and helping staff, they are nice and pleased to help.

author: TerreyB
title: Great location poor facilities
text: Great location unfortunately does not live up to expectations. Room excellent, junior suite which was booked. At check in given a very derisory glance at our booking through dot com. Dreadful smell under nose! Lovely room beautifully appointed. Fan on and no cool through AC unit +35 deg outside, maybe 40 in our room. Engineer checked whilst we were at dinner, put it back on 23 deg turned it down when we came back to 16 deg to cool. Took all night to come to reasonable temp, dial at 18. Left in morning to sightsee with key in to keep room at reasonable temp. Cleaner took key out, came back to hot stuffy room. no water or gowns provided with only one lounge chair to sit on. Truly for money paid for a three night stay not acceptable. Pool also not open until July, stifling hot outside, what on earth do they think. Breakfast buffet paltry to say the least. Staff terrific, good parking underneath. Unfortunately would not stay again in a sweat box in Spain in summer.

author: Spyns
title: Top Marks for Spyns Running of the Bulls Tours
text: Spyns offers hotel package tours to Pamplona's annual bull run festival. While I have worked with the Tres Reyes for over five years, this is the first time I have written a review as both a guest and tour operator. First: location. The hotel has the best location to enjoy the annual San Fermin festival. Spyns former Pamplona clients always love the easy access to the fiesta, bull run, and bullfights. Located on the very edge of the old town, it is roughly 5 mins from the bull run and yet just far enough away you won't be up all night because of fiesta noise. Second: rooms. The rooms are spacious and functional, however, renovated rooms like mine are rather standard without a lot of personality. My room was impeccably clean and I found the bed very comfortable (I am a bit of a bed snob). Third: service. This is where the hotel has made great strides. I was never prompted to write a review in the past because I had nothing positive to write about the highly professional but rather stuffy and aloof reception staff. Well all of that changed in July 2014. With the arrival of a new manager, we and our Pamplona tour guests were treated like royalty. What a difference! In addition to the new manager, there were several new front-line reception staff. They all went out of their way to make Spyns Pamplona 2014 trips a success. Our clients were over-the-moon happy and we look forward to working with the hotel again in 2015.

author: LondonTraveller848
title: Great room & location, rubbish service
text: We arrived at Pamplona on 5 July ahead of the San Fermin festival and stayed at Tres Reyes two nights. The room was great, the staff was not. GENERAL Easy access by car, great location close by to the old city (a 2 minutes’ walk), parking available (at under €20 / day), nice and plentiful selection at breakfast and great view of Pamplona from our room’s window. Reception had kindly booked a balcony for us for the Running of the Bulls (€120 per person) and we were given the red San Fermin scarf as a gift. The room and bathroom were spacious and it was clean. NO tea and coffee facilities in the room unfortunately, which was unfortunate as the festival starts really early and we couldn’t have a cup of tea. LOW RATING DUE TO SERVICE The Manager was very caring and most of the staff were friendly and helpful with the exception of several incidents, one of which involved a rude and unprofessional member of staff in the Cafe who upset me greatly. The bar tender in the English Bar ignored us for quite a while and then when finally acknowledged us he was not friendly nor helpful. Also at breakfast we were made to wait and queue in spite of the huge amount of available tables. Lastly, reception had to be asked twice before they sent an engineer to fix the air con. Some of the hotel’s staff just seem to LOVE to make guests waste their time, they’ve been very consistent doing so! Which is why my rating is low; given the room charge, which was inflated due to the San Fermin Festival (at over €377 a night), I had expected a pleasant and smooth stay in a professional hotel. Also, the hotel hosts so many San Fermin visitors, they can be a bit considerate and offer their guests at least a cup of something hot during the festival at 06:00 a.m. in the morning, when one has to set off to their balcony (the streets are shut well before the start of the running at 8 so one must get to the balcony by 06:30 a.m.). We asked at reception and were told we can come back for breakfast after the running, which we did, but the hotel could have put a kettle and tea facilities for the early risers on such a special occasion. Surely the cost of our 2 cups of tea would have been covered by the inflated room rate we had paid!

author: 321uktraveller3
title: Good overnight stop or longer stay
text: Stopped here mid afternoon on our way South. The hotel was in a good location for walking to the old town. The girl at reception who checked us in spoke exceptional English. Having booked in advance, everything was ready for our arrival - so smooth check in. Secure parking was available for the car in a locked garage under the hotel and was valet parking only, which meant we didn’t have access to the car if we had forgotten anything. This came at a price of course – we paid 9 euros for overnight and even this was at a 50% discount. Two bottles of water had been put in the car for our onward journey when it was brought back to us. A nice touch. Receptionist and concierge were helpful. Our room and bathroom were large and clean with well kept furniture but although supposedly a garden view we were on the 4th floor which was higher than the trees and looked directly into flats opposite. The bed was good size and the bathroom had a separate bath and shower with various toiletries. The shower tiles were beginning to show signs of wear and needed a bit of re-grouting. No tea or coffee making facilities in the room although there was a minibar. The hotel public area lounge is large but the bar doesn’t open till 7pm each evening and the restaurant doesn’t open on Sundays. There is a café belonging to the hotel which serves good coffee and where you can get beer, wine and good tapas etc., as well as breakfast croissant and pastries in the morning as breakfast in the dining room is expensive. Free wifi in the room and public areas which worked satisfactorily. All in all quite a good place to stay for a short visit.

author: www00man
title: The Holiday House was no "Holiday"!
text: Actually, because of a series of problems and unfortunate circumstances, we checked out and left after our first night. We were expecting to stay four. Thanks to the understanding and cooperation of the onsite staff we were granted a full refund. We were to stay in the Holiday House, which is one of two detached cottages. Initially, we were extremely happy with "house"; lots of room, full kitchen, private back deck/yard with nice view. Then the problems started... barking dog from the next door cottage, TV did not work (found out later the cabling was incorrectly wired), tank-less water heater was barely functional and to top it off the "after hours" contact phone number was not active. So, calls, emails and texts asking for help went unanswered. Consequently, after the accumulation of problems we asked for and were granted a full refund and left. Too bad and unfortunate. The barking dog belonged to the Monarch owners... not good. The correct after hours contact number should have been available to deal with the TV hookup. And, the tank-less water heater needs to be replaced before this house is rented again. For those reasons... we checked out after one night.

author: GoingPlaces111
title: Beautiful grounds but interior needs upgrading
text: The address of Monarch Cove Inn is very confusing, the property is at the very end of El Salto Street, but before one can reach the Inn (620 El Salto), there are properties numbered in the 600's and 700's. It will be helpful if there is a sign further down the block to help visitors find the place. The grounds is lovely and very well maintained, overseeing the coastline and the ocean. It relaxes you right there and then. The location is very quiet, no street noise. We slept with the windows open, and all we could hear was the rustling sound from the trees and the chirping of the birds. Even though there are neighbors occupying other rooms of the inn, everyone was respectful and nice. We had a pleasant stay. Breakfast was sumptuous (fresh orange juice!) and it was brought into our room in the morning. We could eat in the patio or in the room. We did both. We stayed in the Lilac Room. We liked the bed, it was very comfortable. However, the carpet is old, as well as the furniture -- some of them need to be replaced. The bathroom needs some serious upgrading (the shower head is loose), the ironing board is wobbly, I had to be super careful whenever I put the iron down. No AC, but with the ocean breeze, it was fine, just have to keep the windows open.

author: MonicaLcsw
title: Gorgeous retreat!
text: What a lovely area to stay in alternate to Santa Cruz. This bed and breakfast is on a bluff overlooking Monterey Bay in small town of Capitola which has a beautiful beach and cute town. On weekends though consider parking in the lot outside of downtown and take free shuttle in; I had no problem coming in on Sunday. Monarch Cove Inn felt luxurious with its great setting and flowering gardens. I heard the ocean from my room and the continental breakfast was fresh with good coffee/cream. I came by myself and hope to bring my partner next time- very relaxing and romantic. The room was easy to heat the 2nd night with the cold coming in and the bed comfortable. The room infobook wrote of this being a place where Al Capone and Mary Pickford stayed. THis is a wedding site with pavilion at the bluff. Tall eucalyptus and pine are on the edge of cliff. Google map took me to the doorstep with no complication. The office staff was welcoming and friendly and parking was nearby and easy. It was also easy not to run into anyone so very private. I drove 5 min to New Brighton State Beach- beautiful. An added plus was finding the Well Within in downtown Santa Cruz. All I was looking for was a hot tub and found an oasis. Outdoor private hot tub w/ shower and 1/2 hr massage- = $65. Great way to start my first vacation day. Monarch Cove is on my return list.

author: Ellie9193
title: Beautiful and Breathtaking
text: For the most part, a relaxing getaway for two. This was a very romantic setting. No complaints about the staff they were extremely friendly and hospitable. The grounds are beautiful. The views are breathtaking. The place is a Victorian so it is old but kept nice. The only downside was the family who was staying above us was very loud. They had several children or atleast it sounded like they did. If your going to bring your whole family PLEASE consider your neighbors. Bed and Breakfasts are meant for peace. This place is so romantic I can’t really imagine why you would want to bring your whole family..... Besides this my experience was amazing. I will definitely return the next time I’m in Capitola. This will now be the only place I stay. <3

author: jmarkar
title: charming, unique country Inn Coastal style. New England style
text: Great location. Very romantic setting on peaceful overlook far away from traffic noise but very close to downtown. Really remarkable. We went the first time on a Groupon type of discount, but came back again at normal rate because we just loved our stay. Built out on a point overlooking the Pacific. Feels like you are staying in a beautiful, airy guest room at a county estate. Continental Breakfast delivered to your room each morning at your desired time. Big fluffy bed a little soft for our taste but not a problem. Just a wonderful escape setting, and close to Monterey, Carmel, Santa Cruz, and set in Capitola, a great old beach town with lots of interesting little shops, fascinating history as the first resort on the Pacific Coast (1800's). Plenty to do: Santa Cruz for the younger set, Whale boats at Moss Landing, Kayaking and everything else in Monterey Bay, music and night life in Santa Cruz... and ... this is California: Good food discoveries everywhere. Monarch Cove Inn just makes it better because you can just hang out and walk around lazy and feel fulfilled.... We'll be back. Would give it 5 stars if the breakfast was a little healthier and the bed a little firmer.. clearly earns 4 1/2 Stars

author: DiaNoor
title: Wedding Wonder Mary helped make our special day amazing
text: I had my wedding here and it was absolutely perfect. We rented the whole property for the weekend which made it a nice retreat. My parents catering the rehearsal dinner made me pretty stressed but Mary was there to make it ok. We were looking for a rolling pin that they didn't have, totally ok. Mary offered to go back home and let us borrow hers. She adamantly insisted but I couldn't let her do that. But I wholeheartedly appreciated it. This property is simply picturesque and everyone had a wonderful time. The cons were that neighbors and other people felt like they could pass through anytime they wanted. This REALLY pissed me off. I kicked out a few people. We paid for the whole property so it was ours for the weekend, no exceptions! The other con was that cleanliness was not their strong suit. I had to ask them to clean the build up on our shower head and vacuum under the bed. They replaced the shower head but they forgot to vacuum...

author: beachster56
title: Away from it all, but just a walk away from Capitola Village.
text: Just up from the little town of Capitola by the sea. Good restaurants, fun atmosphere, lots of shopping and the beach. At the Monarch Cove and is a property that has been there since the late 1800s. Nestled at the end of a residential street along the Pacific coast. I believe it became a hotel in the 1940's. Fun history you should check it out. We stayed in a cute little bungalow. Super comfortable bed, really nice little secluded deck. Actually your own little private backyard .Darling kitchenette also place to serve you a nice breakfast. Which is included. Very charming, not modern. Things are a bit old but very well taken care of in my opinion. Very fresh.The doorknob to the bathroom may be an original, but it's so cute and fun. We really liked the property, the service was excellent. We will definitely go back.

author: deezeee2
title: Amazing Ocean Views!!!
text: You are literally right on top of the ocean! Gorgeous views from our bay window (Victorian Room) --- ocean in all 3 directions. The inn sits atop a cliff, so if you want to get your toes wet, it's worth the nice walk into town (and down 83 steep steps.) Lots of good places to eat in the delightful town. Continental Breakfast delivered to your room each morning (8:30 - 10:00 AM) consisted of high quality pastries, bagels, fruit and yogurt, plus a carafe of hot coffee. Our room was large, comfortable and completely clean. We enjoyed the large round glass top table in the bay window. The bed was comfortable and the pillows were OK. The bathroom could use a remodel as well as a more thorough cleaning. The bathtub was old and stained/scratched (and small!) I could see where plumbing repairs had been done because a large block of tiles near the on/off shower spigot were white, and did not match the other tiles around the tub/shower. When I lay down in the tub, I could see that the area under the soap tray was filthy with mildew - yuck! (I didn't take a bath the next day because of that.) There wasn't always enough hot water, and it took a long time to become hot. There was a ventilation fan in the ceiling (also dirty) but there was no switch to turn it on! The bathroom walls and mirror were dripping wet by the end of a shower. (No window in the bathroom, either.) We hope to return again --- even if they don't remodel the bathroom. The positives far outweigh the one negative.

author: scotbet
title: Spectacular Location
text: We loved the location of this inn. It's in a quiet residential neighborhood a short walk from Capitola village, making it easy to pop down for lunch, coffee, or happy hour. In fact, the walk, along a cliffside pedestrian path, was even better than the destination. We loved experiencing the view it at all times of day: morning, sunset, and moonlight. The inn itself is beautiful and there's a breathtaking view from the grounds. We were there on a very cold winter weekend, so we didn't linger too long, but if it were summer I could spend all day out there with a book. Lastly--butterflies! Although the butterflies were not out in full force, several were flitting about during our stay. We were in the Butterfly Room, which was, as advertised, small. It was nicely decorated though the carpet was a tad worn and the curtains did not cover the windows completely, letting in electric light at the top. The walls are thin. We could hear voices from the rooms surrounding us. It was only really an issue when a woman got in a phone argument just on the other side of the wall. Inngoers, please speak softly! I think that if we go again I would spend for for an upstairs room or a cottage. Breakfast was simple but ample, and it was nice to have it delivered to our room.

author: OnklReisendeMac
title: Scenic getaway
text: I loved staying here the night before heading for Carmel Valley. We came from camping in Yosemite, and needless to say it was a great contrast. The sun was shining and I was standing forever soaking in the view. The house has so much exciting history, and I especially liked the thought of mafia boss Scarface Capone walking around the property with high class people back in the day. Maybe he stayed at the Lilac Room? The lilac room had a perfect location with a veranda. We had planned on having our breakfast there but it was way too foggy in the morning. Speaking of the breakfast, it was very refreshing! Fresh fruit, yoghurt, something sweet. What else would you want? I was not able to eat it all. So, don't worrry about breakfast not being good enough. It is! The lilac room was very cosy and tastefully decorated. The bathroom was cute but would have been even cuter with a bit more updated bubble bath, or what?! We did not hear the other guests apart from when they were showering. Not a problem. It was a 10 minute walk to the village and we enjoyed walking around there but did not have a bath as the beach was packed with people. Sundays are not the best day for a quiet bath down there for sure. All in all, we enjoyed our stay to the full and would go back here if in the area!

author: DavidAndSonia
title: Have to second the Starthur review...
text: “Good location in beautiful setting, terrible breakfast, very dated rooms” somebody wrote in July. Unfortunately, we have to second this. The setting in the garden is very charming, plus there are not many B&Bs or small inns beyond Santa Cruz. The rooms are spacious and comfortable but with dated ambiance. The breakfast is a disgrace. What's really upsetting is that there had been complaints about the breakfast prior to our visit in May, but we hoped that it was an exception rather than a rule, or that it would have been improved. And now we see that as of July, there still are similar complaints, even though we expressively complained about the stale pastries and completely dry and burnt bagel. We were told that "it is always fresh and had never happened before". We also complained that 1 bagel, 1 muffin and 1 (very) sticky bun seemed to be an odd number of items to share for 2 people, and that most people do not eat sticky buns anymore. The next day the pastries were more fresh and the sticky bun was replaced by a small croissant, but still only 3 items to share. We asked for butter with the bagel - they don't have it, only a tiny package of cream cheese which was hard to open without scissors and which had traces of the cream cheese outside. Only one (1) miniature tub with some jam. OJ tasteless, definitely not freshly squeezed. In short, any motel has a better and more generous spread in the reception area in the morning. Weddings or other events is a different story, especially if they bring their own caterers.

author: Roo11
title: great location, tired property
text: If you like to stay at your Grandmother's cottage, then this is the place for you. I am not opposed to older properties with history, as I have stayed at numerous B and B's that have history and are not "new," I prefer B and B's because of their character and charm. This property is in a fabulous location with a great view. It is charming. The rooms are equipped with a refrigerator, microwave and coffee/tea maker and heated by an electric fireplace. It is an easy walk to downtown Capitola. We stayed in the Lilac room, which has a fabulous water view and deck, however, the deck is peeling and in need of painting. The room's carpet, unfortunately, is stained or bleached. Not sure what caused it., but it is distracting and looks bad. We were served promptly each morning in our room with a continental breakfast, consisting of orange juice, coffee, yogurt, fruit and some pastries. Unfortunately, the pastries did not seem fresh. Perhaps the age of this property may explain the lack of privacy between rooms. It was easy to hear activity in the room next to us as well as the room above us. Maybe having an upstairs room or a cottage might be a better choice for less noise. We did experience two different encounters with the office staff. Mary was very nice and helpful and was genuinely interested in how we were enjoying our stay. Jacqueline, who I spoke to on the telephone, was not quite as friendly. In sum, I am glad that we tried the Monarch Cove Inn, but feel that it is not a property that excites me to return.

author: clarabakus
title: Excellent B&B plus great prices!!
text: I decided to take a trip to Santa Cruz with my boyfriend and best friend and since we're on a budget we wanted to share a room in a motel (since that's all we could really afford). So I had compared motels and inns on different websites and the ones that cost about $150 for one room had absolutely horrible reviews. My mom recommended the Monarch Cove Inn because I guess she'd stayed there with a friend and my sister and I when I was an infant. I checked out the website and figured "this is way too nice it's got to be expensive." But it was right in our budget! I couldn't believe such a nice place is so cheap. I originally booked the Butterfly Room but I was told that the Monarch Grove Room would accommodate three adults a little better so I paid a tiny bit more for an even greater room. I am giving this place five stars because there is nothing I would improve about our stay. We stayed in the Monarch Grove Room and the room was clean, smelled pleasant, had an electric fireplace, a huge TV, a giant bathroom with an amazing bathtub. It was all so clean and fresh and had beautiful views and tons of windows with this unbelievably comfortable round chair. Plus the staff is so sweet and understanding. And the cutest comforter, this place has the sweetest little butterfly-garden style too. I had accidentally hit the corner of my sedan on the car port on our way in and the woman that was working at the time was completely understanding and apologized even though it was completely my fault. (I was able to buff out the white paint from my car with a rubbing compound). Anyway, I would highly recommend this inn to anyone visiting the Santa Cruz area. It's a short drive to the boardwalk and even a nice walk to great restaurants and shops in Capitola. Before you book a motel by the boardwalk for around $150 a night, please check out the rooms at the Monarch Cove Inn. You'll get way more than what you pay for. I'm definitely coming back here someday.

author: PackMySuitcase2015
title: Romance & Charm
text: This is a perfect place for a romantic getaway, proposal, wedding, renew vows, etc. Beautiful B&B overlooking Monterrey Bay. The Inn is located in a residential neighborhood so it is very quiet. However, it is close walking distance to the cute beach town of Capitola. The grounds are well manicured and the building is a very cute Victorian vacation home. The location is atop the bluffs & has panoramic views. Next door is a Monarch grove where you can see many butterflies migrating. They bring a fantastic continental breakfast in the morning. If you are a little adventurous, you can walk along an unmarked trail, through the monarch grove, along the bluffs & end up on a very private, sandy beach (New Brighton I think). I did this & walked on the sand all the way to the "concrete ship". We stayed in the 2 bedroom Ocean Mist which had amazing views from the Master bedroom. I slept with the curtains open & was awoken by the sunrise of the bay & mountains. I highly recommend this room. My only issue is I stayed with my 3 children. They are kids and they don't walk with soft feet. It's an older facility so the floors are thin. The occupants staying below us pounded the ceiling when my kids were making too much noise at 8pm. They were kinda jerks & there behavior frightened my kids. Next time, I will stay on the lower level to avoid this issue.

author: 474meredithe
title: Flowers Galore! Convenient location to Monterey, Carmel, and Santa Cruz
text: I loved my stay here so much that I am considering having my wedding here. The property like the other reviews suggest is gorgeous and flowers and ocean views abound everywhere. I stayed here in late July and the weather was perfect (70s). Wish I could have stayed here when the butterflies were also over to visit! There's always next time! It's about 20 minutes from Natural Bridges State Park (tide pools! check to see when Low Tide is, usually around 4:00 pm) and about 30-45 minutes away from places like Carmel and Monterey. I am not ashamed to say that I took advantage of the location's picturesque qualities to shoot a lot of self portraits (best time for this is around 6:30 to 8:00 am when the sun has just come up, because after breakfast the clouds set in). I had the Ocean View room and it was gorgeous. Room was clean. Breakfast is served around 9:00 am and included pastries, fruit, juice, and yogurt - delicious! Free Wi-Fi as well and free parking on the lot. The staff was super nice and helpful but the desk is only open until 6:00 pm so try to get in contact with them if you plan to check in afterwards! I checked in after 6:00 pm but was able to make arrangements so that checking in was a breeze. Love, love, love this place! It was a true gem. I felt like a Disney Princess. Can't wait to come back!

author: BernadetteG343
title: GREAT PLACE
text: If your looking for a fabulous retreat and a place back in time, the Monarch Inn, in Capitola, Ca. is the place to go. We just returned from this Mid-1800 year old Bed and Breakfast property, it's nestled among Eucalptus and pine trees, old world roses, flowers and charm. The walking paths take you to serene sitting area's where water fountains give you a tranquil moment. A walk down by the ocean may just give you look at the whales and dolphins swimming by. The surrounding landscaping fits the time and era of the property. The rooms have great ocean views, and their decor pleansantly gives you the comfort and look of days by gone. The rooms have sitting area, eating erea, fireplace, comfortable canopy beds, and their own bathrooms. There is so much window space, the views are breathless. Breakfast is brought to your room, you can eat in your inside eating area, or simple go outdoors to your own patio sitting area. You are served fresh fruit,coffee, orange juice, yogurt, jams, cream cheese,butter, and wonderful very large pastries. The property is very quiet and serene, the staff is very friendly and helpful. It's also a very great place to have a Wedding. We will go back again. The Warren's from Lodi, Ca.

author: alicem985
title: Management takes advantage of the view and location
text: The only good thing about this place is the location and the view. We stayed in one of the best rooms the Ocean View Room with indeed a stunning view. The room was furnished with flea market furniture. The mattress was soft, the room dirty, a big gap under the entrance door causing a draft when you were inside the room. The sheets had holes. The bathroom had mildew, no hooks for your clothes, no towel racks, the toilet was wobbling and loose. The pressure of the shower very low - and the shower curtain had hooks missing. Motel 6 would have been luxurious. Our first breakfast was also a big disappointment. Frozen fruitsalad, stale and cold rolls, warm coffee. For the two of us we had to share our food on one plate. The second morning we left (the same identical breakfast) and went to Gayle's Bakery for a wonderful meal with fresh rolls and juice. No staff was on the premises to complain to only the cleaning staff who did not speak english. We travel a lot all over the world but this was a huge disappointment. Shame on the owners to charge so much for so little.

author: KellieSwann
title: If you like worn Victorian, you'll love this.
text: Let me begin by saying the location is beautiful. You cannot see the water from your room, but you might be able to hear it. Walking around the grounds, you'll smell the trees and hear the water- but you won't get close to either really. The property is fenced - distorting the view and the most appealing part of the place. I stayed here with several girlfriends and they all loved it. I found it to be creepy and worn. The rooms are decorated in an attempted Victorian style, but everything including the sheets are old (mine had holes). The bathroom was enormous, but the toiletries were laughable. Here is the thing- if I'm going to stay in a place like this (a small, locally run - more of a bed and breakfast type) I need it to have something more than what I would expect at a Rodeway Inn. The breakfast was weird. I've never said that before. We received a glass of OJ, fruit bowls and a plate of bread. The bread included one onion bagel, a chocolate croissant, a soggy plain croissant and some type of weird banana bread. Really? Then they threw in some jelly. Actually, this pretty much sums up the place- they think of a decent idea (breakfast in bed) to offer guests, and they disappoint. I love older places with character- but I didn't find this to be one of them. It has a lot of potential, but it's definitely not there yet. Small touches, like screens in windows or flowers in the bathroom would go a long way here. Give it a few years - I could see it becoming charming.

author: sanity-seeker
title: Has lots of potential but...
text: The hotel location is amazing, however the accomodations and service are certainly lacking. Our key was in an envelope tacked to the office door when we checked in at 2 PM, and that was the last we saw of any inn employees. There was hispanic man that was cleaning the room when we got there who was the same one who brought us breakfast the next morning, but he spoke no english so we couldn't ask questions. There are no phones in the rooms, no numbers to call for assistance. The bottom of the wall heater kept falling off (a little dangerous with 3 small kids). No extra pillows, balnkets. We had a cottage with a kitchen although no napkins. The kitchen window was stuck open, and we couldn't find anyone who worked there to close it. Appearantly no inn employees live there. Good thing there was no emergency. Our cottage had a hot tub in the back altough we weren't sure if it was for the entire inn or just us (again no one to ask). Old wedding arbors with lace still in them were in the walkways. On a good day this is a charming "rustic" property. On a bad day is is some serious need of TLC, both in maintenance and in staff. Come prepared to be on your own!

author: cupi
title: Stay way from staying at Holiday Room
text: We stayed at Holiday room during this Labor day weekend and it was terrible. We absolutely loved the location by the water, but the facility needed lots and lots of work. I am not sure how they justfy charging us over $200 per night for the room when the whole cottage was falling apart. We arrived on Sunday early afternoon and we were told that there was a wedding ont he ground. The wedding did not end until early am hours. People were drunk, yelling and honking, we could not sleep at all. When we lifted the bedding, the right side of the sheet was wet and left side was damp, we told the B&B lady, but she didnt do much. We put the heater all the way up, but the room was so cold at night, I ended up catching a cold. The toilet was not bolted to the ground, so it moved everytime one of us sat on it (carefully). The bathroom was very small and the sink was very small, old and dirty, and 2 faucets for cold and hot water, so it was very unpleasant to use it. The bathroom had no air fan, so the steam would spill over to the room, make it even more damp. The cottage had a kitchen, but the old refrigerator was so loud, it would wake us up (when we finally fell alsleep after the wedding paries quiet down well after midnight) everytime it got turned on. The room did not have proper curtain, so people can see you from outside. The outdoor ground lamps would shine down on your eyes if you sleep on your right side (like I do). The room furnitures were falling apart... We requested breakfast to be served at 8:30am, but didnt come well after 9am. I can go on and on...... but I'll stop here. We loved the beaches there and next time we are in Capitola, we'll stay away from Monarch B&B.

author: MC7894
title: Modern, Clean, no frills hotel with excellent location near central train station.
text: The Metropol is a modern, clean budget hotel. Rooms are modern and very clean. Rooms are quiet with only one double insulated window. Furnishings reminded me of IKEA. No bar or restraunt on premises but many nearby. Small lobby. No fitness center. No individual temperature controls in room. No USB ports in room for charging. No Netflix or other internet TV. No room service. No amenities other than generic shampoo and soap. If you are familiar with Marriott fairfield inn brand this hotel is similar. Location near central train station is convenient. I stayed here solely for location which is walking distance to a meeting I was attending.

author: vovelle1789
title: Lovely views from the breakfast room!
text: I was very happy with this hotel! I arrived early and left my bags at the reception, and they took them to my room when it was ready. The young gentleman at the reception also gave me useful information about how to get to the cathedral (including maps of the city and transportation), which came in handy. The hotel is located about two minutes away from the train station, so I did not have to take a taxi (expensive in Switzerland!). With your tourist card you get free transportation in Basel, and there are lots of trams operating from there. You can also walk to the tourist centre (10 minutes or so). Breakfast was included in my room price, and the options were basic but nice. My only complaint was with the coffee. Both times I ordered lattes and got black, strong coffee (a whole teapot of it), but this is really insignificant. The "superior" room was clean, spacious, and comfortable, and I had a nice view. I will definitely stay here again and would not hesitate to book a room. Basel is excellent for a three/four-day break, if you like museums, historic centres, and walking in general. On a sunny day, it is fantastic to wander about the Rhine and the tourist attractions. There is a supermarket (COOP) nearby, if you do not feel like eating out all the time. Keep in mind that you do not need to carry your luggage up the entrance staircase - open the black doors at ground level, to the right of the staircase, and an elevator is hiding there!

author: dmhinsf
title: A very fine place to stay in Basel
text: The Swiss really know how to do hoteling as an industry. The Metropol is a good example of this. The hotel management and staff clearly uphold the highest standards to ensure a quality stay for their guests. My room was on the back of the hotel making it quieter as a result. It was nicely appointed and clean. The bed was comfortable. There was a mini bar and coffee/tea service though I did not use these. Each day a bottle of water was refreshed. The Wi-Fi worked well as did the TV, mini bar, etc. - everything in good working order. The bathroom was clean and well maintained as well and there was a "green" approach to soaps, shampoos, etc. The hotel is not large. The common areas including the reception area and hallways, lifts, etc.were clean and well maintained. There is a nice breakfast area on the 8th (top floor) with nice views of Basel SBB and surroundings. The breakfast area did get a bit overly crowded and busy on one day of my stay. But in general, it was a relaxing place to start the day with wonderful breads, cheeses, cereals, yogurt, fruit, etc. The customer service at the hotel was top notch as well. For example, they were willing and generous to print out a few documents for me and were also gracious and kind with greetings and welcomes. The hotel is VERY close to the train station as well as many tram lines and the 50 bus that will take you to the airport. All-in-all, this is a great hotel and I would gladly stay here again should I return to Basel.

author: Edinburghgardener
title: Great Value, Brilliant Location
text: Fantastic location round the corner from the main Rail Station and the bus terminus from the airport. The Tram Station is between the Rail Station/bus stop, and the hotel....couldn't have asked for a better location. ***The Hotel provided free transport 'hop on' 'hop off' tickets for the duration of our stay - including the 15 min journey in from the airport (on request) - which was a significant asset. We could walk slightly downhill into the City Centre (including the River) as far as we wanted to and catch the tram back when we were tired, right to our doorstep. This is a comprehensive tram service all over the City....nearest 'stop' never far away. Hotel room was immaculately clean and kept at that standard for the 4 nights we were there. Very comfortable. We requested a quiet room and that was provided. Rooms are sound proofed. We sacrificed a view but it was worth it because we never heard a thing. Breakfast on 8th floor was great value for money....15 Francs pp if booked when you get there. Very good cold buffet. Everything wonderfully fresh. Try the soft boiled eggs. The Swiss have devised a way of keeping them warm and soft which you will find interesting. Prices for food and drinks around the City are high,so this is actually a great way to start the day on a finite budget. There is also a VG Co-op round the corner near the station which would be great for buying food and drinks for lunches as there is a lovely small grassy park, with seats, across from the Hotel, where you would enjoy 'eating out'. Reception staff were helpful. Great value for money hotel. Wouldn't stay anywhere else if we were to go back to Basel.

author: johne275
title: Affordable Swiss Quality
text: Myself and my dad stayed here for two nights, mid July, this year after trying to find a reasonable and convenient place to stay for our short stay in Switzerland in order to visit Lucerne for a football match. As anyone looking at practically anything in beautiful Switzerland knows, you can expect to pay a tidy sum for whatever you need, so we were pleasantly surprised to discover this hotel just a stones throw from Basel train station. And at just £100 each for the two nights we were both very happy. As I have said the Metropol is only 150yrds or so from the station and all tram stops and while it may look fairly unassuming from the outside you will find a bright modern reception area through the front door and this décor continues throughout. Reception staff upon checking in were friendly and informative as they provided us with a map of the city marking out our location as well as other areas which may be of interest for the duration of our stay. Not forgetting of course the free travel cards which appears to be a standard bonus throughout the area and something that I wish was adopted back home. Surely it's beneficial to enable tourists to see the sights? The twin room we booked was bright with a bath/shower en-suite and although a little smaller than the photos suggest, the room was immaculately clean and comfortable with plenty of storage, a free safe, flat screen t.v and hairdryer, which if either of us were blessed with a full head of hair would have been much appreciated. The view from the large window overlooked a road towards the small park at the front of the building - the road incidentally posed no problems as regards noise even with the window open, which was really handy considering that the temperature outside was a fabulous 30degrees. We both found the beds to very comfortable. During our time here we only had one problem when the safe refused to open but the girl on reception, whose name I unfortunately didn't catch, came up immediately and sorted it out. I should say that I think the safe was working perfectly and the blame can probably be laid firmly at the door of my dad who I suspect used the wrong code when my back was turned!!! He of course denies all responsibility. Because of our schedule we didn't get a chance to sample the food which was a shame as having seen the pictures of the view from the restaurant it would have been a lovely way to start the day. Overall, while perhaps not for a full holiday, we felt that the Metropol was a great find in a brilliant location at a reasonable price with everything you'd need for a stay in Basel either as a base to explore further afield or to simply enjoy the city - highly recommended.

author: 881victoriab
title: Surprisingly lovely hotel
text: Note: If you want to park your car there, you must call the hotel in advance. They kindly accommodated us after wheedling a bit, but it's not very prominent on the website. The website says "valet parking - contact the hotel". Well, perhaps they are unclear about what valet means...we arrived ready to park our own car, and they winced at the fact we hadn't contacted them beforehand. They need to change that from "valet parking" to just "parking". But in the end, they were able to give us a space, which was very kind of them! (18CHF per night). Outdoor parking is virtually non-existent in that area, just so you know. Anyway, the hotel rooms were very comfortable, and clean. Excellent breakfast service - one of the waitresses spoke German, French, and English fluently, which was helpful to our mixed group. However, even with the restaurant space, they do not serve lunch and dinner, which was fine for us because we hit the town. (There is a huge Starbucks next door, for those who are obsessed with Starbucks) We stayed in a basic room on the first floor which we were surprised to find was just as roomy and comfortable with lovely amenities (coffee/tea tray, slippers, bathrobe) as one of the superior rooms our friends stayed in on the 6th floor. Free local train/tram tickets got us around the town and down to the Christmas Market which was our intention. Hotel staff was nice, even with a few irate customers (I don't know what they were upset about but at checkout time a few people came down to scream at the receptionists). They remained courteous and respectful and seemed to be trying very hard to help them. Overall I was very happy with the visit and this would be my first choice hotel if I end up back in the area.

author: cillierabbit
title: Great if you need to be by the train station
text: I stayed here one night because of a late flight into Basel, and needing to hop on a train first thing the next morning, wanted to stay close to the station. I booked the cheapest room category and was pleasantly surprised. The room looked like it had recently been updated. It was small -- typical of Switzerland and maybe even smaller than average -- though very practically laid out and all the necessary functions/amenities were there, including a decent-sized flat screen tv, robe, hair dryer etc. The bed, pillows, and bedding were all very good quality and comfortable. Breakfast was included in the rate, and it was solid. A decent selection of cold cuts, cheeses, breads, fruit, yogurt etc. There weren't any hot options, though I was more than fine with what they had. The coffee wasn't as good as what's typically offered at other places. Internet access was included in the rate, which is a great bonus in Europe. Speaking of the rate, the Metropol was easily the least expensive of the options around the train station (though I didn't check Ibis). One thing I didn't like about the hotel was the stairs leading to the lobby. This was not a welcome sight when I had a carry-on and two checked bags. Another annoyance is the shower/bath has one of those doors that only extends halfway the length of the tub. I hate these. Maybe I'm just dumb, but I can never manage to shower without getting water all over the place. The Metropol is a solid choice if you need to stay by the train station. I probably wouldn't stay here for an extended stay, but it serves it was great for my purposes.

author: salbilla
title: Do Not Stay Here, Dirty Rooms and Incompetent staff
text: Please don't stay here if you like cleanliness. When I arrived there were stains on my sheet. I called the recptionist and she sent housekeeping to change it. Great! After housekeeping left, I went to the bathroom and the shower and sink looked like it was not cleaned in months. The toilet smelled foul like it was just used with a particle in it, so I called the reception again and asked why the room wasn't cleaned. She was defensive and kept telling me it was cleaned. I told her to give me another room, she agreed. I told her I would prefer to check the room first when I did, that room was also not cleaned. There was hair in the shower and towels on the floor which suggests that it was cleaned. Suffice to say we end up cleaning the bathroom after the housekeeping only cleaned the toilet. Also, I paid for breakfast which was at 7 am, I had to leave at 6:00, breakfast was already laid out, asked the receptionist if I could just grab something from the table since it was ready and he refused to allow me. Kept saying breakfast was at 7 am. At the end, even though there are not a lot of hotels in this area, you be better off staying in the park or parking lot than being traumatized at this nasty hotel. Even the bathrooms at the close by ferry station were cleaner.

author: D6989MYcristinad
title: Not a nice experience in AC. I will not come back to this brand
text: Good location and breakfast. Non friendly personel, not a good hotel service, not clean properly, non speaking english personal attending the phone... Before I start... I work as Quality Manager in a Hotel in Amsterdam and I know this industry from inside to outside. When we arrived there was a problem with the reservafion that was solved really quick and friendly. We got a room in the 1st floor although I wanted a room in a higuer floor but I understand the hotel was fully book. The room was big with 2 bathrooms, living room and bedroom but was super dirty. I found bread from the previous guest all over the sofa and carpet, the floor was not hoover and mop at all (sand everywhere), super dusty and bath dirty. During the stay improved a bit... amenitties were replaced every day, always hoovered and bed change every 2 days. In four nights we were staying... only once we got a greating as good morning. We asked for a couple of spoons to room service, they did not speak a word in english and they said that they will not bring them to the room that If we want them we have to go downstairs and get them... non a service for a 4 stars hotel.... The breakfast is good. Nice coffee and variety of juices...breads....eggs and bacon...cereals... I think was the only thing I cannot complain about. In the end, It was not the service I was expecting in a 4 stars AC. Although the situation of the hotel in the city was good... I will not come back to this brand anymore.

author: FarAway802738
title: A Very Nice Modern Hotel
text: I spent 3 nights recently at the hotel. The hotel itself is very excellent. It is modern, new, very clean, and the room was excellent. I stayed in a suite on the top level with a great view. The staff is very knowledgeable & helpful & they all speak English. I have some critical comments -- (1) The breakfasts are adequate & meet European standards, but are not up to American standards in a Marriott hotel. (2) Huge shipping terminals are nearby & there is a constant & irritating noise from them. I got somewhat used to it. Be sure to bring ear plugs. (3) There are essentially no services in the immediate area. If you walk about 1 mile you will find shops and restaurants. But this is a relatively poor area and the services are not excellent. (4) There is absolutely no public transportation at the hotel. You must use a cab. I chose this hotel for my visit to Gibraltar & I am glad I did. It is newer and nicer than the hotels I saw in Gibraltar. It is 25 min & 30 euro from Gibraltar by taxi. I made the round trip daily and was glad for it.

author: travelwithpeggy
title: Not suggested - to avoid
text: When we arrived driving two cars, there was no safe place to unload close to the entrance. The street in front of the hotel is very busy and narrow with really no parking even to unload. We had to drive around to the other side to off load and then lug our bags. The front desk was not friendly. I had booked 3 rooms with half board over the Internet. When, we arrived she informed me that none of the rooms would have dinner included. The restaurant and bar were both closed didn't even open until 7:30 and my group wanted something to eat then. You could buy a beer at the font desk but no food. The group ended up walking around and not finding a place to eat nearby. We ended up near the university. So, that wasn't nice for us. I found the hotel staff not caring. Even in the cafe at breakfast, not helpful. I would NOT return to this hotel at all. I can not even believe it has the Marriott name attached.

author: elisel366
title: Fabulous staff, nice rooms, amazing restaurant
text: The staff here was very nice, and extremely helpful. We had a number of chances to find out how good they were over the course of our 3-night stay- we got restaurant recommendations, ferry service information, cabs, directions, and pretty much anything else we needed. They handled it all easily and with aplomb. The rooms were good, but not great. Nice, modern decor with clean lines, but the wall paper was peeling a bit and there wasn't anything particularly amazing about them. The breakfasts were fairly standard - fruit, some cheese and meat, a lot of pastries. for the price, you can do better, but it wasn't bad. The real stand out, though, was the hotel restaurant for dinner - it was a total surprise. The chicken with vegetables was insanely good. The vegetables were grilled perfectly, leading to some of the best grilled asparagus I've ever eaten. The chicken had a hint of sherry or something similar, and was perfectly juicy and tender. My husband had a pizza, and it was an excellent version of a thin-crust pizza. My daughter's club sandwich was also well-prepared (it's a club sandwich though, so not exactly complicated). The waitstaff were really lovely and the entire dinner was an excellent experience. It made me a bit regretful we hadn't eaten there prior to our final night. Overall, a nice hotel but not outstanding, but with an excellent staff and a truly surprising restaurant.

author: wirtravel
title: Not the best experience
text: First of all, the location of the AC Marriott in Algeciras isn't picturesque. Sure you can see Gibraltar there, but the hotel is located in the industrial part of town near the port. Once you get past that, you have the inept staff and less than spectacular accommodations. It all started with our room that smelled of old hotel cigarette smoke even though we requested a non-smoking room. They informed us that is is and was a non-smoking room, but apparently it was right next to rooms that are smoking rooms. The entire floor smelled of cigarette smoke and that was totally unacceptable. Because of that, we had to open our window in the 95-degree heat, which was not ideal. As for our TV, we received only three to four channels that did not have static. We mentioned that to them, but they did nothing. As for the breakfast, we asked them how much it was and they said six euros per person. When we checked out, they said it was 9 euros per person and that there was no way that someone would have told us that it was 6 euros--essentially calling me a liar. After a bit stern conversation, they set it at 6 euros. I have no problem paying 9 euros if that was what they had initially told me. During the day, they have complimentary espresso, sodas and water in the lobby. I helped myself to an espresso and it was delicious. I went back for another cup a bit later and an employee was beginning to put everything away. I reached for an espresso packet, but she said I couldn't have one because it was "closed." It's a freaking espresso packet that was free just moments earlier. Not a big deal, but it was just another situation where the AC Marriott was unable to accommodate or provide what a hotel of their stature should -- hospitality. I would not recommend this hotel or even a stay in Algeciras for that matter. Unless you visit Gibraltar, stay far away from the AC Marriott and Algeciras.

author: MarkOlsen
title: Best hotel in town
text: I stayed at the AC Algeciras hotel in late August 2009 on a trip thru Portugal and Spain. I specifically stayed in Algeciras because I came in on the bus from Seville, left on the Renfe AVE train to Madrid and took a ferry across the strait for a day trip to Tangiers, Morocco. Also, there are few hotels in Gibraltar and all were expensive so Algeciras, for me, seemed like the logical place to stay. Algeciras, in my guide book, is described as a "gritty industrial city" yet I found it to be the most real Spanish city I visited as all the other cities were heavily touristy i.e. Seville, Madrid, Ronda, Toledo, Gibraltar, Segovia, etc. The hotel isn't in the best location as it's about a 20 - 30 minute walk from the train station, bus station and port and there isn't anything of interest nearby. I walked from downtown to the hotel several times and wasn't worried about my safety as the hotel is on a main road with plenty of traffic at all hours of the day and night. This would be a good hotel if you have a car as there is plenty of free on-street parking and a garage. If going to Gibraltar I'd suggest taking the bus for only 2.05 Euros as it ends in La Linea and you don't have to worry about the cost or hassle of parking your car. The AC Algeciras is, in my opinion, the best hotel in town. It's clean, new and modern. The room I had included a free minibar (soda and water), a nice big soft bed, no view, in-room safe and a flat panel television with 1 English language station (CNN). The room, overall, was quiet but there was some noise (voices and footsteps) from the hallway. Breakfast was not included in my room rate but could be purchased for 8 Euros or 4 Euros if purchased from the front desk when checking in. My only complaint, other than the location, was the lack of a full-size barrier in the shower which resulted in water getting all over the floor. There were 2 free Internet PC's in the lobby which I did not use but there seemed to be at least 1 always available. In all, a nice, clean and new hotel within walking distance of the bus, train and ferry port. I saw some of the other hotels in town and this is definitely the best. While the location is not perfect it is still easy to get around by walking, taking a cab or bus.

author: fluffnfold
title: A Wise Choice in Algeciras!
text: We loved the AC Algeciras! Everyone said not to stay in Algeciras, but it worked well for us (day trips to Gibraltar and Tangier) between stays in Seville and Granada. We booked a business class/executive room, which was awesome! A sitting are with sofa, desk and flat-screen TV, a very modern (glass) bathroom, and a separate bedroom with king-size bed and another flat-screen TV. But the best part was the ENORMOUS terrace! It's definitely worth the extra money (which wasn't much) to upgrade from the standard or superior rooms. I found a better rate contacting the hotel directly than on the AC Hotels website, and that appeared to be the only way to book the business/executive room anyway. Free mini-bar at the hotel, too, which was GREATLY appreciated! The lobby/lounge areas of the hotel were very hip and modern, and the restaurant was quite good. There weren't a lot of other restaurant choices within walking distance. We did have a great meal at La Posada de Millan, recommended by the hotel, which gave us an authentic view of Spanish life. A grocery store and gas station (with mini mart) were just a block away. It may have been possible to walk to the ferry and bus/train stations, but I think it was just a bit too far for us. Cabs to any of them cost about 5 Euros each way, well worth the convenience. Have the front desk call a cab for you--it will arrive in mere minutes. I was very happy with this hotel, and will check out their counterparts (it's a chain) in other cities in Spain.

author: Avril60
title: Great location
text: Hotel is located within 15-20 mins walk to Old Town & main train station. There’re many restaurants and supermarkets a couple of buildings away from the hotel, including the classic Imperial Cafe and low cost Lidl supermarket. Check in was easy and reception staff friendly and helpful. We asked if they could print some documents for us and they readily offered for free. There’s a gym and swimming pool which are free to use for guests. Bedroom was sizeable with plenty of table space to put things. I booked a triple room for my friends and were pleasantly surprised that instead of getting a bedroom with 3 single beds, they were given a 2 room unit (just like a suite) with a room with a king sized bed & an attached room with a sofa bed that opened up to a queen sized bed with a TV in each room. A couple of news channels are in English. Beds are a little soft but comfortable. Rooms come with a mini fridge and tea/coffee making facility although I only received coffee on the first day and subsequent days, only tea was refilled with no coffee. Rooms are not air conditioned but hotel placed a fan in each room for use. Windows are double layered so sound from tram and traffic is not so bad. But in summer can be hot if you do not open the windows. But noise can be unbearable if windows are opened, not only from traffic but from party goers along the road too. Breakfast spread is good. They do bother to change a few items over the 3 days we were there. They offered to pack breakfast to go for the day we intended to leave early for excursion. I’ll recommend this hotel and will definitely return on my next visit to Prague if it’s not in summer.

author: bluebear1905
title: PLEASANT EXPERIENCE AT THE AXA HOTEL
text: We stayed at the AXA hotel during a two night stay in Prague in March. We found the hotel to be spotless, tidy and well organised. All the staff members were pleasant and helpful. Check in was quick and easy (check in was after 2pm and check out was 11am) and breakfast which was served between 7am and about 10.30am was well cooked and plentiful. The room and bathroom were well decorated, clean and tidy. They had tea and coffee making facilities and also a small fridge. However, there wasn’t a safe deposit box in the room. Although we never used the facilities, the hotel has a gym and swimming pool which were included in the price. There was also a bar which served food and guest at the hotel were given a reduction of 15% off the bill at the time we stayed. We were really impressed that the hotel had made the effort to contact us through E-Mail before we left for our break to ask if we had any special requests etc to make our stay more enjoyable. They also made the effort to contact us after we returned home to thank us for staying with them, which we thought was a really nice touch. The hotel is well situated for tram and metro links across the city. The nearest metro station was Florenc which was about 5 mins walk away and the tram and bus stops where right outside the hotel. There are also plenty of shops, chemists, fast food outlets, cafes and restaurants close by. We really enjoyed our stay at the AXA Hotel and we will definitely stay there again if we return to Prague.

author: StockholmKindaGuy
title: It Didn't Live Up To My Expectations.
text: LOCATION: The area where this hotel is located has gotten nicer since the last time I was in Prague. While not the prettiest area of the city, there are plenty of cafes, restaurants and places to get a drink. There's also a tram stop near the hotel. HOTEL/CHECK-IN: The hotel has a small lobby, but it's nothing you would want to hang out in. They also have a bar, although I never had a drink in it. While check-in was fairly quick, I didn't find the staff overly pleasant. ROOM: The contemporary room has a Bauhaus feel with all the tubular steel furniture. The bed looked to be a full size bed, but was really two twin beds put together with thin mattresses that weren't comfortable at all. Considering the room rate, I would have expected better. My desk chair had a big disgusting stain, that should probably be replaced. The curtains on the windows weren't wide enough, allowing too much light to filter in at night and in the morning. The bathroom was modern with a spacious shower and hairdryer. Overall, I didn't find the room as quiet as I would've liked. BREAKFAST: Breakfast was included with the room rate and offered a lot of choices. STAFF: I honestly didn't find the staff here all that pleasant. They always seemed a bit moody. CONCLUSION: For me this hotel didn't live up to the rate being charged.

author: Hollie151
title: Great stay!
text: Just home from a 3 night stay at hotel AXA. Thoroughly enjoyed ourselves! The hotel is great if you want to visit Prague on a budget. If you're looking for something luxurious, then this probably isn't the right hotel for you. That being said, the rooms were very spacious and modern and had everything we needed. The rooms were huge, and we actually had a separate living area and bedroom! The room size was probably my favourite thing about the hotel. Breakfast was good. There were a lot of options to choose from, so something for everyone. Regarding the location, this was another excellent point about the hotel. It was very Central and close to everything. 10 min walk into old town square which was great. There also was a tram stop right outside the hotel, but we did not use this as we travelled everywhere on foot. Overall I was very pleased with this hotel. I think it provides great value for money and would highly recommend it to anyone who wants to visit Prague on a budget! When booking, it seemed to be the best available hotel that fitted our budget. The only negative thing I would say about the hotel is the reception staff. I did not find any of the reception staff to be particularly friendly or helpful. A smile goes a long way, and I would've felt more welcome had the reception staff been more warm and welcoming. However, despite this, this is a great hotel and I would recommend it.

author: gemmal553
title: Good value hotel in a great location
text: Email correspondence with the hotel prior to arrival was answered efficiently and they arranged for a car to collect us at the airport. As promised when we entered the arrivals hall there was a smartly dressed driver with a card with my name waiting. We checked in on the 30th November and checked out at 4am this morning. We travelled as a family of four, myself, husband, 10 year old and 8 year old. Check in was efficient and the staff were very helpful when they established that we had never been to Prague before, lots of information offered on public transport and tours and pointing information out on the map. We were in room 301 and upon entry to the room were pleasantly surprised at the amount of space, there was a cloak area, an absolutely huge bathroom with a shower which could hold around 6 people easily(!), two sinks, loo, bath and hairdryer, and two bedroom areas - one with a sofa bed and one main room. The kids room had a desk and chair, tea making facilities (but no milk) and a cupboard and lamp, and the main bedroom had bedside tables, with touch lamps, chairs and a large wardrobe and a wee fridge. The rooms were basic but absolutely spotless with two towels per person provided. There is a tram and bus stop right outside the hotel and whilst there was some noise heard as a result of this during the night it in no way hampered our stay. The radiators had adjustable thermostats so we were able to control the temperature in the room. The WiFi was really good and we had no connection issues with it at all during our stay Breakfast was basic but adequate, there was something for everyone and no one went hungry and any point. We settled our bill the evening before check out as we were leaving the hotel at 4am and the staff again organised a taxi transfer for us (it was 600czh or €24 euros each way.....to give some context, I was quoted €35/45 by Uber, so I think represented good value for money) and the taxi arrived at the exact time requested. The hotels location is great with brilliant public transport links right at the door, and the metro station is a short walk away too. There are plenty of bars, restaurants and shops nearby - both for a bit of retail therapy or the odd grocery item such as bottled water- and a 10 minute walk will take you to old town square. All in all a really pleasant stay, with friendly helpful staff, would definitely consider using this hotel again when we return to Prague.

author: EdJ843
title: Prague...what a city
text: Did not want to travel there but had to follow my wife. Not sorry I did. What a beautiful city. A lot to see, spacious, clean and good food. Can't ask for more. The hotel was nice, breakfast included (fantastic variety) and close to transportation, restaurants and a ten minute walk to shops and stores galore. The hotel had the IKEA type of furniture and comfortable, one hick.... no outside telephone calls. There are two restaurants you must visit and one of them is across the street in the building of Bila Abut. It's on the top floor and here is what you get. A soup, main meal, desert and a beer (you get beer everywhere) for $5.95 US. Next one is just a 3 or 4 minute walk from the hotel called Hybernia (Pilsner Urquel Art Restaurant) Hybernska 7, Praha 1, 110 00. Very good food with beer of course at moderate prices. More expensive than the Hybernia but worth it. Good food is found everywhere in Prague. A city to see.

author: Mell848
title: Spotlessly clean, great location, great value for money!
text: POSITIVE : - Spotlessly clean! The cleaning ladies are VERY good at their jobs. - Towels were white and clean. A little small though. - Great location. Right next to Lidl for snacks, plenty of fast food restaurants around, currency exchange across the road, tram stop right out front and the international bus stop is a minute away. Walking distance to touristy things. - Helpful staff including assistance with printing travel tickets. - Good value for money. NEGATIVE: Minor issues. - Noisy surrounds when the windows were open, which was sometimes required as there is no aircon. Quiet when the windows are closed. They do provide a little fan which was of use. - No safe in the rooms. - Breakfast was average but it is a 3 star hotel so I suppose it is adequate for what you pay. Overall we were happy with this hotel.

author: mari_thetravelous
title: Perfect affordable place to stay in the center of Prague
text: So the saying goes, you cannot please everybody, and all of us has different expecations. But then for the price that you pay for a place in the center of Prague - i believe that what AxA offers is more than enough. The room is always clean when you come back and all your valuables are safe even if there is no safety deposit box in the room - thank you Housekeeping Team, i didnt meet you but you did a great job. Staff at the reception always acknowledges you when you pass by and they have an answer to all your inquiries which matters a lot. The breakfast is very good for the price that you are paying for, two times i tried breakfast outside the hotel to see and it costed me from 250 to 350 czk and the food is almost just the same as what they have in the buffet in AXA. As for the limited number it can accommodate it really gets busy from 9am onwards so I tried to go earlier and it was perfect. Their is only a small fan in the room but it didnt create any incovenience at all as you can keep the window open which is more fresh and the area of my room, i got lucky as I was not bothered by any noise at all. There were sockets/plugs for your chargers everywhere.. In the toilet, on each sides of the bed, and 2 more around the room which was super cool. And the best plus? Wifi works so fast in the room and anywhere in the hotel. The arrangement of my airport transfers done good, the drivers very polite and helped with my luggage. Thank you. And special mention to one of their Lobby Security PAUL, he was always greeting guests and talks to them if they have to wait when the receptionists are busy, this is a plus as it keeps the waiting guests busy talking to him and this avoids that they get annoyed waiting - in his own way he is doing an excellent customer service ( this i know as am a Head Concierge, i know a good service when i see one ) Plus and plus point for this place? Aside from being affordable and the good team? The location is very convenient and you can explore the whole Prague just walking - i didnt use the metro even once on my 8days stay. Thank you AXA Team keep up the good work.

author: GiakouM
title: Minimalist hotel, newly renovated, within easy walking distance of all the sights
text: A group of 10 friends booked to stay in the hotel Axa because it was cheap and within easy walking distance of most of the sights of Prague. On arrival we were pleasantly surprised as the rooms were well sized, newly renovated and clean. I shared a suite with 3 other girls and this was fantastic. Two rooms, one with two single beds and the other with a very large sofa bed. Both rooms had flat screen TV and we also had coffee and tea making facilities. There was one bathroom to share but again we were pleased to find that it was huge, with two showers, one in the bath and another in a cubicle. We were on the second floor and had been worried about street noise as the hotel is on a large main road, but there was no noise at all. Breakfast was also pretty good. Plenty of choice, hot and cold and re-stocked regularly. Really nothing to complain about at all. The staff were all helpful and the cleaners were brilliant..whenever we asked for anything (coat hangers, extra pillows, etc) they brought it straight away. The location was also good as there is public transport available right outside the hotel. There are also a few bars and restaurants nearby but the hotel is only about 800m walk from Republic Square and the Old Town. If you are looking for something cheap and good value then this is ideal. I would definitely stay there again if I returned to Prague.

author: Ytoh2809
title: Average hotel
text: We stayed here for a night on 17th Sept. The hotel is close to Old Town Square and Billa and Albert Supermarket. So sightseeing and buying your basic stuffs were very convenient. The only thing was getting to the hotel via the Express Bus from airport. They dropped us at the namesti republicky stop and it was cobbled streets all the way to the hotel (about 700meters away). So we had to carry our suitcases as pulling the suitcase on cobbled streets were very damaging to the wheels. Better to take a taxi directly from airport The room is very basic. We stayed on the 4th floor and with the windows open, we can everything happening on the streets including trams, cars, people , garbage truck , etc etc. Try to request for a room NOT facing the main road. No toiletries given except a shampoo and soap and towels. No toothbrush kit , shaver , comb or shower cap. The pillow was too soft and not comfortable. Bed was ok. No fridge in the room. A kettle and tea is provided. The hotel staffs are very friendly and can speak good English. For a one night stay, it was okay but I wouldn't stay longer than that.

author: W503BFandrewh
title: Good value but has issues
text: So I needed a hotel for a long weekend in Prague. This hotel pooped up in the right location and budget. It's located in amongst a row of building along a main road. Check in was quick and polite. I was told then that the pool was out of use ( that information would have been key to booking another hotel for me, so would have been useful at the time of booking) Rooms are small but not cramped. The style is modem and clean. Good use of space with handing rail and shelve space the photos on the website are a good representation of my room I had read previous reports about how hot the rooms get. However, these reports are true. The rooms are extremely hot and there is no way to cool them. As I arrived, the window was open to keep the heat down. But the window open to a communal balcony which is insecure. I live in Dakar and I'm used to the heat. But I struggled to sleep Good bits .. Nice design overall, funky bedside lamp, plenty of wall sockets , good breakfast, great location with shopping centre 5mins walk Bad bits .. Hate paying for a double room to find to small beds placed together ( straight out of Spanish 80's package holidays ), no air conditioning or fans, no lock on the window in order to leave open , TV is very small (21") positioned on the wall some 20 feet from the bed. The concrete corridor outside rooms amplifies every sound , high heels, chatting , doors closing etc etc, Overall ok, but I've not sleep for three days properly so disappointing I guess Maybe the management will aim to fix the cooling issue soon

author: Hoppetussa
title: Clean, functional hotel with great bathrooms
text: We stayed 3 nights at Hotel Axa and was very satisfied with that choice. The hotel was newly renovated, and the room had real nice, functional interiors, and a lovely, big bathroom. The bathroom did not stand back for any other bathrooms in much more luxurious hotels. The beds were ok, and we all slept well. The breakfast was ok with a variety of hot and cold dishes, coffee, juices and cakes. But the dining room itself was not the cosiest I've seen. We chose Axa partly because of the swimming pool, but I must say that was not what I expected. We wanted a swimming pool where the kids could have lots of fun, but this was anything but. If you want a swimming pool for work out I guess this is perfect, but it's really not kid-friendly. When we entered the swimming area it felt like we came out of a time machine that brought us back to the sixties or even further. The swimming pool is run by a different company and you pay 1 kr pr minute. We visited the swimming pool just once. After that the kids preferred to spend time in the bathtub instead :) The hotel is located about 400 m from the city center, and the tram and tube are close by. We thought the location was real good, and so was the price. Hotel Axa is a good choice.

author: katslife1
title: Birthday in the sun!
text: Wow! What an amazing place to escape to! We spent six months anticipating our stay at Makanda By The Sea and the hotel did not disappoint. The staff was absolutely amazing. Alex, Amanda and David along with everyone else who takes care of the guests making it seem so effortless. Alex who always seemed to be there ready to make sure we had the perfect drink, a towel when we arrived pool side or to make sure we were taken care of at breakfast. Amanda, thank you for finding a candle for me to blow out on my birthday while we sat poolside and had dessert and wine. David for always having a wave of hello as you went by or a where to? As you took us to the beach or our room. The gentlemen at the beach who made sure the lounge chair was exactly where we wanted it to be and the drinks were ready when we wanted them and you were engaging throughout our time. To the staff that somehow always knew when we were out and they could come in and clean the room. To everyone at Makanda. Thank you. The resort is beautiful and lived up to all of our expectations and the staff made the stay memorable. We are looking forward to staying with you again.

author: hornswin90
title: Paradise found!
text: We stayed in Villa #7 which we feel has the best view on the propery! The room was beautiful, and well decorated. The balcony was HUGE, and had a lovely always hot Jacuzzi and we were welcomed by all of the wonderful jungle wildlife including a variety of monkeys, parrots, and more! Just an amazing experience. The hotel staff is very friendly and accommodating. The food was absolutely outstanding. Arbol restaurant is some of the best food we've ever had at a hotel. The pools are incredible. We'd like to point out how much we enjoyed Alex at the bar. He was great and made us feel at home! We had a few small issues, but nothing that would prevent us from returning. The hotel is going under some renovations, so there is some construction noise during the day. We would highly recommend this hotel, but keep in mind, if you are looking for a cheap option this is not the place. This is an exclusive boutique hotel, and is priced as such. But if money is not an issue, and you love to be spoiled. This is your place!

author: Rach29100
title: A very special hotel
text: Makanda is an amazing hotel for adults only. The accommodation is a mixture of 27 large suites and villas. The accommodation is in the jungle and is on steep slopes.
