One whole wall was glass sliding doors which led out to a verandah with two sun loungers and a jacuzzi (the heating element did not work and it wasnt covered, so full of leaves and we didn't use it). The view was incredible- jungle and the beautiful pacific ocean. It really was beautiful. We saw monkeys, toucans, lizards, vultures, just while sitting on the deck. The room was large and well appointed with a huge bathroom that had a glass wall so you could look out over the jungle while showering (there is a blind if you want privacy). As other reviews have said, the technology was a little unnecessary- an astounding combination of mood lighting options, the non functioning jacuzzi etc, but I can imagine that some people may enjoy that. We wanted to relax here and we did! We ordered room service every day which came fairly quickly; the only drawback being that plates were not collected so we had to rinse them off in the sink to avoid attracting flies! The surroundings are beautiful and you can walk down the road to little shops and restaurants if you want to get out of the hotel. I think price and location of the hotel are certainly 5*, however I think the following would improve it: - Collection of plates/somewhere outside the room to leave them after breakfast & room service. If there is no option to take breakfast in the restaurant (which didn't bother me) you should be able to get the plates out of your room asap...with only 11 rooms surely they could be collected? - Turning off, or at least turning down the music that plays quite loudly from 6am to 10pm. We booked a hotel in the jungle to hear jungle noises! - If there is to be so much technology, it should all work This place was genuinely beautiful and I loved it, however I did feel it was slightly missing the mark, and I can't put my finger on why. I don't imagine you would be disappointed by booking here; the wildlife alone compensates for any (minor) drawbacks there may be; on our last morning a troop of about 20-30 squirrel monkeys were playing in the trees above our verandah. It was absolutely great. Overall I'd say go, expect 4* rather than 5, and expect the view from your room to take your breath away!

author: rogeroldfield
title: Arrogant owner's attitude ruins stay
text: The arrogance and ignorance of the Russian owner spoils what is a beautiful hotel in a stunning location, holding itself out as a 5 star hotel. 1. Owner insists that loud music played at dinner inspite of all the diners asking for it to be turned off, to enable us to hear the sounds of the jungle at night. 2. Red wine served at 9c, on owners instruction against advise of apologetic and courteous staff. The day we left a cabinet was delivered to store it at between 12 and 15 c. Too late for us! 3. The only English speaking TV channel was HLN, which gushed parocial US News. 4.Inspite of a $500 per room price only one cup of coffee per day, to be drunk in the room, included in the price.You have to pay for another! 5. Seriously undercooked mahi mahi, which had to returned to the kitchen. 6. No turn down service at night to remove the bathroom rubbish of the day. That will be understood by those who have visited Costa Rica. The location and the stunning pool area are compatible with a 5 star hotel, but the above provided a bitter disappointment at the end of an amazing 18 day holiday in Costa Rica. The owner needs lessons in Hotel Management and civility. She declined my request for a meeting to discuss the above, which confirms her unbelievable arrogance. I cannot speak for Russia, but in other countries the Customer knows best.

author: Lorac
title: Disappointed
text: We saw Makanda under construction some 20 years ago and ever since, have stayed there in different villas. Makanda, nestled into the jungle, has been a wonderfully designed small hotel situated for appreciation of nature. Guest comfort has always been paramount, as has been serenity. A new owner is intent on making Makanda something it was not; a trendy, music filled hotel with increased numbers of guests filling newly constructed facilities. Some will like the changes. We did not, finding the new decor at reception and the restaurant to be gaudy and not unlike 1970s beauty salon atmosphere. Music at the pool masks the sounds of nature. A word about service. Staff members were courteous, friendly and helpful, for the most part. Drinks at the pool ought to be served with napkins. They were not. Music at the pool, a major distraction, ought to be optional at turned off at guest request. It was turned off, but then inched back on... Nothing stays the same. We will have the former Makanda to look back to, but not the new one.

author: PingLondon
title: Hotel is under construction
text: This hotel was our first encounter with Costa Rica. A truly beautiful setting on the hill overlooking the ocean, in the middle of the rainforest. Come in good shape and bring walking shoes because everything (the villas, the beach, the pool, bar, restaurant, office) is a hike (15 minutes to the beach) or a minimum of 40 stair steps away; we enjoyed that very much, but it is not for everyone. The villas are private, spacious and the view from the balcony is breathtaking. The forest and wild life is all around .The pool area is stunning and the food is really good. It is probably going to be a wonderful place to vacation, but at this moment it is under construction. We were the only guest together with another couple. Having Christmas dinner in the restaurant all by ourselves felt a little weird. When we arrived, the room of our 3 kids was under construction so they put them in a 2 person room with one 6.2 foot boy on the couch. After 2 days the kids room was ready and without our consent they packed their stuff in plastic bags and moved it to their new villa. The villa was stunning, but not finished. The private pool (!) was empty and the was no railing along the balcony. Our villa had not been upgraded yet, is was situated under the pool which meant that we woke up every morning by the noises of the cleaning crew above. My advice is: wait a little until they are done with the construction. When the construction is finished, and the service is up to par, I would probably give it a 5.

author: alexandraa233
title: Stellar views
text: My husband and I stayed here for three nights and had a wonderful time! The ocean view from our room was perfectly framed by lush jungle. We sipped coffee in the mornings on our porch/balcony and watched toucans in the trees. The private beach here is amazing as well and the hike to get to it makes it even more special. The service was wonderful. Everyone was very friendly and personable. Also, their 2 for one happy hour is a fantastic way to relax by the pool (which also has an incredible ocean/jungle view) and watch the sunset. The food here was really well done although I felt their dinner menu was a bit limited and on the pricier end. I rated this hotel very good instead of excellent for a couple reasons. First, we lost power two of our three nights. It happened late at night, probably around 1 or 2 am so it wasn't a big deal but it did wake us up. Second, although the room was beautiful, it could benefit from an upgrade. Little things like new fixtures, flat screen TV's, etc... just a little more posh and "polish". Finally, the bed was incredibly noisy! Any time we turned over or adjusted in our sleep it would creek so loud it would wake me up. Overall, Makanda is a fantastic hotel and we would definitely return.

author: 597nikih
title: Perfect Villa in Manual Antonio
text: We love Makanda by the Sea. We were very pleased with the location, the room, the food and the service. Marvelous Marvin was our favorite and took great care of us during the trip. I can understand why some are bothered by the walk and stairs, but we are fairly young and in shape, so it really did not phase us. We loved the walk down to the public beach and the private beach, and walked up the hill to the main road most every day for a stop at the supermarket or one of the many fantastic restaurants. On food, I must say that the food at Makanda is fantastic. The breakfast every morning was probably my favorite. Two words: French Toast. (My husband also loved the Huevos Rancheros, but I am love sweet stuff in the morning). The fresh juice they brought was always so fresh and unique. We had lunch there twice and thought it was great as well (great portions and so fresh). We stayed in Villa 10 and found it to be clean and comfortable with an incredible view. The amenities at this place are so well thought-out: huge closet, large bathroom, nice kitchen, ipod docking station, free reliable internet and phone. Most importantly, we felt very safe at Makanda. There was always someone at the front gate and they got to know us quickly. I felt like they paid attention to where we were going - if we were getting in a cab, etc. (Not is a weird way, just a respectful manner of taking care of their guests). Thanks to everyone at Makanda for making our first Costa Rica experience the one that we will never forget.

author: 104jaym
title: Truly Paradise
text: My wife and I stayed in a studio room for 6 nights in April. It was the best hotel experience we've ever had. Pros: -stunning view, just incredible. You will never just get used to it. -room was beautiful with floor to ceiling windows facing the ocean -breakfast is personally delivered to your room after you order off menu by phone. Loved the privacy. -Infinity pool/jacuzzi was incredible with amazing view overlooking forest and ocean. We never use the pool at hotels when there's an ocean nearby but it was so nice there we used it everyday. Mostly at night. -the Drinks! Oh man. I had almost all of the tropical mixed drinks on the menu & they were all absolutely incredible! The staff would cut up fresh tropical fruit. God they were tasty. Daquiris,pina colada, caiprinha -food was good, breakfast & dinner. -the staff were incredible, very attentive & helpful. Usually I just write "staff was nice" in reviews but these people really show you what good customer service looks like Cons: You have to leave.

author: JeanneFromCt
title: Place to be
text: We loved our room with a beautiful view of both the jungle and ocean. Loved the architectural details of the wood and glass doors you could throw open to the outside. The fans and air conditioning assured you were going to be comfortable. So did the bed and sofa and the hammock that had my name on it. You do climb a lot of steps up and down to get from reception or restaurant/pool area to your room though and that can be taxing. Our room was always clean and the extra touches of fresh flowers was nice.Breakfast was brought to your room and even though we had an early excursion and check out time, someone was able to serve us. Choices were good and all included fresh fruit.There was a kitchen and you could cook if you so desired. Coffee staples were provided and appreciated. The food at the restaurant was good and the service excellent. Everyone was very helpful and friendly at the resort no matter what position they held. Loved the pool. There was cable but we were on vacation and really didn't bother watching. . This was a very pleasant, peaceful time. We didn't venture into the downtown but stayed at the resort except for a excursion to the National Park. What a lovely beach Manuel Antonio is. We were glad out agent choose this as they do inspections of the properties and would not put us where they would not stay.

author: SagehenTraveler
title: Outstanding room, very dated feel
text: Let me start by saying that my wife and I were off the beaten track for 12 days and then came to Manuel Antonio to have a 5 star lux, on grid experience before going home so we may be a bit tainted. First off, M.A. is so touristy - it's like a prettier cabo or cancun so expect crowds, crime, and panhandlers... This hotel's room (studio 11) was unbelievable and we spent 90% of our time lounging on our patio and taking in the breathtaking sunset and daytime view. Breakfast on the balcony on order was pretty legit and delicious (huevos rancheros for me, french toast for the wife were both amazing) Okay, so the cons (at least for us): The average age of guests is 60+. We felt very young in our 30s. I couldn't imagine honey-mooning here as some guests mentioned The private beach is actually shared with a family resort and has kids and dogs on it. It's small but great warm water for wading or swimming. The pool, while infinity, feels dates. The primary color scheme (purple, yellow, red) and the matching tables reminded my wife of a Williams College reunion (see pic) vs a fancy resort...I tend to agree. The welcome cocktail (the makanda) tasted like a jolly rancher. We're not drink snobs, but it was undrinkable. The welcome intro was like "Ok guys, come on in guys, sign here guys. Ok, here are the rules guys." It felt like a tour...which my wife and I despise.. Anyways, this place is great and just wasn't the right fit for us. It's perfect (with its pool noodles, and pool floatation rafts) for the golden-year crowd looking for nice rooms and a simple place to take in a exquisite view of the MA bay and sunset. All in all, M.A. is overpriced and touristy and Makanda seemed like a very solid if not great choice for that market.

author: JazzManSeattle
title: Great place to stay
text: During our 12 day vacation in Costa Rica, we stayed in 6 hotels. Makanda by the Sea was by far the best hotel! The rooms are set within the jungle with spectacular views. The pool, unlike others, gets deep! there are few guests due to the small size so it is quiet. Also, there are no children allowed. The restaurant is but a tented/open area by the pool that served the best meals we ate in the country. Actually, I visited the area 15 years ago and stayed at another hotel. My wife read about Makanda's restaurant so we decided to try it. It was so good that we went there the next night as well! The issues we had is that you need to walk quite a bit on gravel and up hill to get to your rooms. This is unavoidable due to the layout of the property. The air conditioners were set so that they blow right on the bed so we had to turn them off at night which defeated the purpose! The rooms have steps down to the bathroom and both my wife and I tripped on them. There is an awesome beach that is nearly private at the end of a short walk. We loved it!

author: Social_Velcro
title: Beautiful, intimate boutique hôtel
text: Stayed in Villa 6 and loved it. Truly a sanctuary with comfort inside and out. Gorgeous veranda with a bit of an ocean view, and surrounded by trees, birds, all sorts of wildlife. A/C inside was worth the occasional respite from humidity. Fabulously appointed room, canopy bed, sitting area, luxury bathroom, kitchen. Look at the site's pictures - it's for real. Staff seemed really friendly and helpful. Delivered breakfast to us early as we wanted to leave for Manuel Antonio by 7:30. Loved the small pool area, with infinite view overlooking jungle, and Pacific Ocean framed by luscious foliage. Really good restaurant with about 5-6 tables on the far side of pool, served tasty, decent quality food. The place feels like a semi-private sanctuary, and with only 13 villas/rooms (I think), the property feels quietly enjoyed and appreciated. We did drive into a few other hotels to check them out; some have more units and are inevitably louder and busier. Given the crowds at Manuel Antonio, it was really refreshing to have such a deluxe home away from home. All of the hotels along here are high up on the cliffs, only one on this ridge gets some beach front access - but that property involves either walking or driving up and down a lot. While Mariposa has killer views from the restaurant (worth a meal there), I think the rooms are nicer at Makanda. We'd go back. Not with the kids tho - too quiet for teens. Perfect for couples. Below, where reviewers click to select ratings in categories, I've put value at average - only because at $400, it's about what you'd expect for that price. If it was $200 for this property, I'd give it an "excellent" in that heading.

author: WidaM
title: Beautiful and elegant small hotel on a large property
text: The Makanda by the Sea is sited in the book Elegant Small Hotels listing the best small hotels around the world. That says a lot for this beautiful hotel set amongst tall trees and lush landscaping. We were greeted at the gate with a golf cart to take our luggage and ourselves to the reception desk where we were served a welcoming drink. The hotel consists of 11 villas some of which are attached but provide all the privacy and security you would want. Our villa had a large room with a built in sofa at the foot of the bed. There was also a view of the ocean from our terrace. The room even had a large vase of fresh flowers. There was also a small kitchenette with a refrigerator so we could store cold drinks, coffee maker, 2 electric cooktops, sink and dinnerware if you wanted to prepare something. The bathroom had a huge shower. The swimming pool had an infinity edge making photography especially inviting. It was relaxing to sit by the pool and occasionally dip in. The tree surrounding the pool had a sloth in it the day we arrived. The eating area is located at the edge of the pool. Service is exceptional with the waiter explaining the various items in detail and making suggestions. The shredded pork sandwich is huge and the salads are great. There are several other good restaurants in nearby hotels as well but i would recommend taking a cab since the hill is narrow, steep and curvy with autos speeding up and down. You can take a 15 minute walk through the woods down the hill to the beach which we did once but the hotels pool was just fine for relaxing.

author: 476alisonj
title: Favorite hotel in Costa Rica
text: Fantastic & romantic boutique hotel. Loved it from the second we arrived - pictures don't do it justice. All the rooms are private & wonderfully integrated w/ the jungle. Only 12 or so villas and studios- so very private. Loved the walk to the beach and running the quiet streets in the morning for exercise. Monkeys and sloths all over the place. Pool was amazing. Drinks at pool were great, too. Breakfast is great, as everyone else says, too. For our last night, Makanda was booked, so we moved to Arenas Del Mar. Down the street from each other. Arenas was nice too but Cheryl different. We preferred Makanda without a doubt. Walk to town for dinner was very easy. Flashlight in the room - 15 mins tops. .

author: Boggg3312
title: VIEW! Beautiful rooms & pool property
text: My Fiance and I stayed at Makanda towards the end of our Costa Rican vacation and loved it. If you're looking for good service and an amazing view - this is your place! The view from the infinity pool & rooms is to die for - absolutely breathtaking. The pictures don't do it justice. We were also extremely pleased with the upscale rooms on the property. The beds were extremely plush and comfortable and the bathrooms were expansive and clean. We enjoyed our sitting out on the balcony in the mornings with breakfast delivered to the room. Try the pancakes - they are amazing. The restaurant on the property cinsists of 4-5 tables on the pool deck. It was just OK, our food for dinner took a good 45min and wasn't necessarily worth the price paid. But it was perfect for lunch by the pool, where we got pizzas, sandwhiches and salads (all of which were excellent). The drinks at the poolside bar were wonderful - as was the friendly bartender. We saw a ton of wildlife from the pool area: white faced monkeys (pictures attached), howler monkeys and sloths. Really neat. The small beach is a bit of a hike (200+ stairs down and back up). I would suggest the beach off of Quepos for swimming and sunbathing. In all, we had a wonderful stay and would recommend Makanda to anyone visiting the MA area!

author: itsmedeepti
title: Horrible Experience!! Do not stay here!!
text: Makanda was the only hotel in Costa Rica who charged our credit card the full amount in advance. We reached this place late in the night. The check-in took a while and they put us in a villa. The lights in the villa did not work to begin with. Someone had to come and fix the lights which took 30-40 mins. We were tired from the drive from Arenal and called the restaurant on the hotel property. They told us not to come as it was raining and the place was under water, so we ordered on the phone. It took more than an hour for our food to come and quality was so horrible, I almost puked. I am a vegetarian and the pizza they made was burnt badly. We were pretty bummed and tried to get some sleep. All night, there were these fruits dropping on our villa and making really loud noise..forget relaxing, we hardly could sleep even for a minute.I also got some skin allergy dont know from what at this place, my guess is some insect bites. We decided to move to another hotel due to this and asked for our money back for the rest of 2 days that we were not going to saty there. They charged us $300 for one horrible night here!! and never gave us the rest of the money back. Its been 4 months.Finally, we called our credit card compnay to dispute this charge against Makanda.

author: MaggieC1102
title: What a gem
text: My husband and I spent five nights at this hotel in early July. We actually booked the room at the last minute as we had changed our travel destination within CR. What an amazing place. We stayed in suite 11 for the first four nights and had to switch to another room the last night because suite 11 was booked to other guests. We were then upgraded to an amazing villa ( number 1). At first glance, the villa was unbelievable but we loved suite 11 more because it had a porch with comfy wicker chairs and a hammock. Villa1 did not. We saw wildlife on a daily basis and the breakfast was delivered to your our each morning. There was however one downside to this. Being very outdoorsy, we loved to get going early in the morning on our excursions. If you wanted to leave before 7:30 you could only get the continental breakfast which was not that plentiful. But, this was a very minor inconvenience. Big bonus, no children. Don't get me wrong, I love kids. However, being a teacher, it's nice to get away from them when on vacation. I would certainly opt for this hotel again.

author: Alex7210
title: Nice, but overprices
text: The hotel has several different suites and 'villas'. They all have different views of the sea. One room we saw, a senior suite nr 9, was very dark inside and you had to climb much stairs to get there. It smelt a bit moist. The sea-view was limited because of all the trees. We decided to take suite nr 3, which was much lighter, had a better sea view and was better reachable. Inside it looked more modern. Unfortunately it had a suite on top with a connecting door between them. This meant that you could hear almost everything the neigbours were saying if they had a bit of a loud voice. The pool was beautiful, a real iinfinity pool, although it had some bushes sticking out at the infinity edge. And we could see monkeys and sloths almost every day from the pool, which was very cool!! The hotel does not ly on the main road, so you have to climb 600 meters up hill to get to the main road where you can find other hotels, restaurants and the bus to the Manuel Antonio National Park. They offer a free shuttle to the park, but that is only once a day and only one way. There is free wifi, but only at the pool area. They don't offer a free shuttle service to the airport. We have spent the night in other much cheaper hotels in costa rica and Manuel Antonio that were much cheaper and offered more free services. So overall, it was a nice hotel, but overpriced.

author: kocheroni
title: Excellent staff and location
text: My wife and I went to Makanda by the Sea in early May, 2012 on our honeymoon. The first location we stayed in Costa Rica was Nayara (near Arenal volcano), which set the bar high. After flying into Quepos airport (recommended to save driving time), we got to the hotel. On first impression, the pool and grounds were incredible. We can't say we were disappointed with any of the staff, the food, or the common grounds. Our room (room #9) was a bit of a hike from the common area, which didn't really pose a problem for my wife or me. If you have a disability, you may want to ask for a closer casita, or something with less stairs. In regards to the room, the setup was great. All the doors opened up so that you could truly enjoy being surrounded by nature. The whiteface and howler monkeys were common sights on the grounds. The only real complaint about the room was that it had a musty smell which lingered on our luggage / clothes even after we left - the hotel should check out the air conditioning unit to see if it's something that can be resolved. The food at the resort was great - breakfast delivered to our room each morning. Everything is freshly made (including the juice). If you go to the Quepos / Manual Antonio region, riding on the bus is a definite if you don't have your own car. It costs approximately $.50 US per person, which is a steal. The bus runs regularly from Quepos all the way to Manuel Antonio. Also, go to Manuel Antonio National Park - not only is the wildlife great, but the beaches are some of the best in the area. Over the four nights we stayed at Makanda, we got close with Jorge and Daryle - both great guys who have been working at the resort for a long time. Overall would recommend to any person who likes being surrounded by nature, but with a luxurious feel.

author: meredythm2018
title: Wonderful experience
text: Had a wonderful time in MA, mostly due to our stay at Makanda. We were on a week+ long trip to CR, ending with 5 days in MA. We also planned to elope there. True to many who choose to get married this way, we wanted something simple, romantic, beautiful (and most of all...stress free). We could not have imagined anything more perfect than our wedding turned out to be...we had a sunrise service with a photographer, florist and lawyer at a beach location, all coordinated by Leo. (and huge thanks to Leo!!!...we will forever be grateful for making this exactly what we wanted). Makanda will always be a special memory for us. Makanda was perfect. Our villa (#5) was beautiful with a great view, breakfast was good and filling, we ate at Sunspot twice (once on our wedding night) and the food was very good and reasonably priced. I think you will find that many MA restaurants are "meh" and overpriced for what they are, and I personally found Sunspot to be worth going to twice (the exception to this is Cafe Milagro, which we loved). The entire staff is lovely and gracious. The tours coordinated by Makanda seemed to have the most talented and informative guides (e.g. the MA tour...our guide was great). If you're debating about going to Makanda, GO!! We'll be back for sure!

author: hezzer
title: Beautiful, Relaxing, just plain old Great!
text: I have a lot of reviews to do for our 5 night trip to Manuel Antonio but I wanted to do this one first because we loved Makanda so much. We stayed two nights here, two nights at Arenas del Mar and one night in SJ. For us, an early 40s couple with no kids looking for a relaxing, beautiful, authentic, unpretentious but upscalish experience, Arenas del Mar didn't even come close (I'll be doing a review of that as well) and was a lot more expensive. We had Villa #1 - it is a gorgeous, huge room with a kitchen, massive closet and great living area including a hammock and huge sliding doors that open to let the outside in. This villa doesn't have a balcony, but it does have an absolutely amazing (AMAZING) view. We talked to others who had monkeys on their balconies quite a lot so it's a trade off as this villa is a lot bigger than another we saw (#6) but we were happy with our choice. Oh - and the bed was super, super comfy. Breakfast is brought to the room and is fresh and yummy (they could improve how they bring it so it's a bit hotter). The food at the poolside restaurant is excellent and only second to the fantastic drinks. The whole poolside area is gorgeous. The infinity pool with the amazing view over the jungle and ocean was crazy cool. There's just little better than lounging around (or in!) the pool with a drink enjoying the sunset and the monkeys that come to play in the trees. All the staff was excellent. The only slight blip we had was being told one tour would pick up at 10 but when I called at 9:10am for breakfast and checked on the time for the tour it was actually 9:30 causing a bit of a rush but it all worked out in the end. It's hard to really convey the experience at Makanda but we really wished that we had spent all four nights in Manuel Antonio at Makanda and when we return wouldn't think of staying anywhere else.

author: 912am
title: Just What I Needed- Full Experience
text: Travelled to Manuel Antonio on several occasions. You can't beat the location and beaches. Always wanted to stay at Makanda. In the past would come up from the beach and dip into their awesome pool and enjoy drinks with a sunset. Rooms offer privacy and open verandas. Was kindly upgraded to a villa and enjoyed a large room, bathroom, comfortable lounging areas, and low key and attentive service. A bit dated as most hotels seem to be in this area, but nothing of poor taste as you might find in Hawaii. Hotel is walkable to main and more secluded beaches. Also a nice walk to the main road. There are many options in Manuel Antonio. What I like about Makanda is the location and the fact the let the "guest" be a guest. The energy of the hotel allows you to ease into a wonderful vacation. Could easily have stayed longer. Can't beat the sunsets framed by beautiful trees. Food is great and breakfasts were plentiful. Had a bit of a rough time traveling in Nicaragua and had no doubt my escape to Manuel Antonio would relieve my memories from the week before. Thanks Leo and Darian for a great stay.

author: newsak
title: An amazing stay!
text: We stayed for three-nights in Villa #10 and was totally blown away. The views from this villa are unbelievable. Our first day we went to MA National Park (booked through the hotel) and the only thing we saw were two sloths - no monkeys, no frogs at all. We got back to our hotel and there were monkeys everywhere! We saw spider monkeys and had an interesting experience with a group of white-faced monkeys while on our patio. They had us running into our room and even tried to open our door. Where else can you get this up-close and personal?! The pool area was very relaxing, the food at the restaurant was very good, and the breakfast delivered to our room every morning was a huge treat. The hospitality is above and beyond. We appreciated the mosquito netting around our bed, the coffee maker with unlimited ground Costa Rican coffee, the friendly and attentive staff, the huge room with ample storage, comfortable table, chairs, hammock (the monkeys loved this, too), and other amenities. It felt like our home. We did notice that the mattresses of all the hotels we stayed at were on the hard side and this hotel was no exception. It reminds me of europe in that way, but I was able to sleep despite this. Other posters have written that there are no curtains on the windows and this is true. We were always up early so this was not an issue for us, but it may be if you like to sleep in later. All I can say is this place is top notch, particularly if you are looking for an adult only atmosphere. SO beautiful and serene. We loved it!

author: MagnoliaBlossom
title: Perfect place for us, a couple needing to getaway
text: This place was fabulous. Adorable villas nestled in the jungle. There were so many terrific places to choose in MA and I'm so glad we chose here. Exactly what we were looking for. I loved the concept of our own little villa (we had #11) where we can relax and enjoy the scenery. This trip was for some adventure and relaxation and we definitely got both. The resort is very clean and well maintained. Daily breakfast was terrific. So glad we did not have to venture out for breakfast. The pool was pretty too, and overlooks the sea. The restaurant food and drinks were excellent as well. The staff is friendly. I honestly can't think of a single complaint, not even a little one. This was our first trip to CR and we loved Makanda as well as MA. I could go on and on. Since we were looking for a place that is more than just a hotel room, a place we could just relax, this was exactly what we needed.

author: mg1305
title: By far the best hotel of our trip... and ever!!
text: Makanda-by-the-sea hotel is truly paradise. We stayed here for 3 nights and it was honestly a struggle to ever leave the grounds! This was our "splurge" stay of the trip and was worth every penny. Despite being their most basic offer, our "studio" room was spacious and beautiful, with an awesome bathroom and a king-sized bed and a couch looking out to our balcony. The private balcony had a tremendous view of the sea and was the perfect place to sit and watch the sunset every night. Another guest pointed out to me - correctly - that while every hotel in Manuel Antonio has sea view, they are not all situated facing the right direction for the sunset! Makanda was the first one built in its location in 1985, thereby assuring the best location in the area! The in-room breakfast was fantastic (some of the best french toast!). Happy hour 2-for-1 drinks by the pool was great! The level of service in general was outstanding - particularly by Max at the bar and Leo the manager. We could have stayed at the infinity pool forever. Every day we saw tree sloths and iguanas, and at night we were lulled to sleep by the sounds of tree frogs and cicadas. Because this is an adults-only hotel, there are only a few guests and you are sure to make friends with the other couples by the pool. We had a car, but still were able to walk 15 minutes to several good restaurants nearby. A definite recommendation - don't stay anywhere else!!

author: jnollett
title: A Tropical Dream
text: We went to Makanda for our honeymoon, and loved it. Room- Our room was beautiful, with a big birds of paradise flower arrangement, expansive views of the jungle and the sea, and most importantly, a really comfortable bed. It was very clean, quaint, and modern. They have lightweight robes, which are PERFECT for sitting on the balcony in the morning. Each room has its own path to the door, and you cannot see another room from yours or from the balcony. It has a very intimate charm. Staff- They were so warm, and bi-lingual for the most part. The pool/restaurant staff was very attentive and brought cold scented washcloths around to people at the pool. The staff also was very proud of the local wildlife, and would always stop to show you a monkey, or a toucan, etc... Beach- It was a hike to get to the beach, and more of a hike back from the beach, but well worth it. The beach is spotless, large, and rarely had more than 5 people. At one point, we were the only ones. We spotted monkeys, hermit crabs and other types of crabs by the dozen on the beach. Because of the 4 tide changes throughout the day, you have to pay attention, because at high tide, the beach is gone, and the ocean meets the jungle. It is pretty cool! Area- Great. Really, not more more to say, just amazing. We will be back!!!!

author: Shmalyson
title: Monkeys, ocean views, luxury villas, jungle & outstanding service
text: Went to Makanda by the Sea with my husband for our honeymoon in June of 2010. We stayed in Villa #6. The room is amazing. The bed with mosquito netting and a daily towel art sculpture was so romantic. The villas are situated to give you almost complete privacy. It is an adult-only place with ~12 villas, so the most people who can stay there at once is ~24. We felt like we had the place to ourselves. We went to dinner at their restaurant our first night and we were the only ones there. The food was AMAZING and reasonably priced. Everyone who works there is really nice and are at your service. We saw two types of sloths and 3 types of monkeys at the hotel. Two of the types of monkeys we saw were from our beautiful balcony overlooking the ocean. The walk to the beach is pretty far down a hill, don't forget your sunscreen if you go because you won't want to go back up for it. Breakfast served in the villa was really nice, but many times my food was a little cold. There aren't any shops near by, but you can get shuttled up the hill where there are a handful of restaurants to choose from. We ate a Barba Roja and it was very yummy! The hotel will shuttle you to Manuel Antonio park, but not back again. I suggest shopping near the park. I wish we took the shuttle twice: once for the park and once for shopping, lunch and beach time. If you become a fan on facebook, you can get a discount.

author: farrar99
title: From check-in to check-out...better than advertised!
text: Just returned from a fantastic week at Makanda by the Sea and beautiful Costa Rica! It is hard to return stateside/work after this wonderful vacation. Makanda, from check-in to check-out, was better than advertised. Each and everyone of the staff, from the desk clerks, to the waiters who brought us breakfast each morning to the entrance guard were helpful and friendly. The rooms were clean, well designed, private and the view from our suite was breathtaking. Extremely comfortable bed! Delicious breakfast every morning was served fresh and hot to our room at designated time. Staff gave us great recommendations on mangrove kayaking tour, white water rafting and "local" cuisine (try Soda Salsa in Quepos). Evening meal at Makanda was the best we ate all week. Hike down to the beach was a "hike" but worth it. Saw monkeys, sloths, iguanas and beautiful flora on the grounds of the Makanda. Very peaceful, relaxing and romantic setting. We thoroughly enjoyed Costa Rica. Beautiful country. Take the time to view and learn about the rice, palm oil and coffee plantations and the native flowers and animals. Manuel Antonio Park was ok, more touristy than desired but had a nice beach. Riding in cab, bus or van was an everyday adventure but fun even if your fingers were tired from clutching the arm rest. Extremely impressed with the friendliness of every Costa Rican we came into contact with.

author: DougStevens
title: Over The Top
text: We absolutely loved this hotel. The location between Manuel Antonio Park and Quepos was very good - although the final mile into the resort is a pain. We stayed four days in late-April to May 1. Rates were reasonable, food was fantastic and the rooms Divine. We were in Villa studio 11. And, like several others, we picked out the hotel from a guide book on the day of arrival. This was up there on the top of all hotels we've ever stayed. This place will knock your socks off. We were surrounded by forest with an unobstructed view of the bay. Given the time of year, we experienced a few pretty dramatic rain storms. Yet, sitting on the front porch or swinging in the hammock was very relaxing. The delivered breakfast was a huge plus. Wildlife was great. From the parking lot to our room we spotted three white faced monkeys playing in the trees above us. Spotted a sloth on the property. And, the constant birds and insects assured us we weren't at home. Hard to describe in terms other than it was Over the Top. We felt this hotel made the difference in a fabulous vacation versus a good vacation. Highly recommended.

author: TravelswellNewJersey
title: Morning Paradise!!
text: This review is a little late as we stayed at Makanda in February 09, however I'm sure not much has changed since then. Let me start with our arrival. We arrived in the dark since we rented a vehicle and did some sightseeing on the way. The staff greeted our family of 6 and showed us to our rooms. I stayed in villa # 1 and my sisters stayed in Villas #3-4 which was located under villa # 1 and was very convenient. Viilla #1 was extremely spacious with a large glass sliding wall looking out to the jungle and beach. At night you couldnt see a thing but as the sun came up it was MORNING PARADISE!!!! The view from this room was to die for. We saw a variety of monkeys and birds while sipping freshly brewed coffee supplied by Makanda. If your up for the challenge take a long stroll down a few hundred steps to the beach. Its a very strenuous hike back up the steps, but worth the trip if you stop and look closely for sloths,monkeys and beautiful foliage. We found ourselves sitting in the infinity pool on numerous occasions taking in the sunsets and watching troops of monkeys make thier way through the trees. I'm an early riser, so my brother inlaw and I would walk up the street to a small Cafe and grab a coffee and the best bananna bread ever, before heading back to Makanda for the day. The breakfast was always delivered promptly by Marvin, who was always in a very good mood and could not do enough for you. Get the french toast and chorizo!!! Delicious! You cant go wrong at Makanda!! Location,views,cleanliness and staff. Go for it.

author: RichardJWW
title: Stunning rainforest experience, but helps if you're fit!
text: The Makanda was perfect for us but as the gentleman who wrote the very useful 5th of July review points out, it's not for all tastes. If you want a secluded, rainforest experience, are happy to be unbothered by the professional and unfussy reception staff (mostly dealt with Leo and Alban who were both excellent), and have no difficulty climbing stairs and steep slopes up to the main road, then this is the place for you! Something that hasn't been emphasised enough is that I think Makanda are looking to give you as "authentic" a rainforest experience in Manuel Antonio as possible. Makes sense as it's the rainforest and national park that have drawn you here in the first place! Each studio is set apart from the next and you are completely enveloped in the rainforest. We had a troop of howler monkeys right next to our studio, white-face monkeys within a few yards of us, all manner of birds etc. and all this can be experienced lying in your hammock on the porch! The studios are fabulous, all with stunning views through the teeming rainforest to the ocean, the pool is one of the nicest i've seen; very stylish and very clean, and again, with the same great view. Breakfast was excellent and delivered to your door. People seem to travel from distance to get to the Sunspot restaurant - probably because it gets into the "top 10 places to eat in Costa Rica" list in the Lonely Planet - and it is very good indeed. It closed at 8.30 each night though which i found strange and a little inconvenient but i'm not sure if that only happens in the rainy season. It's worth bearing in mind that if the restaurant is closed it's a 10 minute steep uphill walk to the restaurants on the main road (though the Mariposa Hotel's restaurant was excellent and is just short of the main road) or a 5 minute walk down the hill to the nearest hotel. During the day they're happy to ferry you in a golf cart up the hill but they won't pick you up. As others have said, forget the Makanda's private beach. Not worth it at all. The public beach all the way at the bottom of the hill is nice but it's a good 25 minute walk and a heck of a climb back up! To give an idea on price, we were there at the end of November and just made it in time for the last part of the rainy season discount period. Studios were advertised out front for $120 though these prices soon double and then more from mid-December on.

author: beachtraveler10
title: Jungle Paradise
text: My husband and I spent a week at Makanda in October and were very impressed and pleased. We stayed in Villa #5, which was huge and kept very clean. You can open one wall directly to a beautiful view of the jungle and the ocean. Every day we saw monkeys, sloths, and beautiful birds hanging out in the trees right outside our balcony. There are mosquitos, so be sure to bring bug spray and you'll be fine. The service at Makanda really set it above the rest for us- from reception, who took care of everything we needed from tours to transportation, special requests, etc, to the folks at the restaurant and pool bar who were extremely friendly and hospitable. Makanda has a very pretty private beach you can hike down to - we did this once and it was worth the trip, but we ended up spending most afternoons when we were not out exploring lounging by the pool and enjoying beautiful views. There seemed to be many other couples our age at the hotel, so it was nice to meet people while hanging out in the pool with some tropical drinks - go for the house drinks, both were great. Although it was rainy season, we mostly only experienced rain at night. The restaurant staff was willing to serve us dinner in our room if we were not up to venturing out in the rain, which was a great service. The highlight of traveling in the low season was avoiding lots of crowds - my husband and I took three tours and on two of them we were the only people signed up, so we got lots of personal attention. Manuel Antonio is a beautiful desination, so get out and see it. Go to the national park, where there are lovely beaches -if you hire a guide they will point out all of the wildlife for you. We also took the mangrove and atv tours, which were a lot of fun and gave us a chance to see lots of wildlife and beautiful country scenery. I would highly recommend Makanda as a place to make your base in Manuel Antonio - immaculate rooms, awesome service, and a gorgeous environment to be in - what more could you ask for?

author: monart77
title: In a Jungle with Ocean Views
text: We just spent 9 days in Costa Rica visiting the Arenal volcano, San Jose and Manuel Antonio. Manual Antonio was the highlight of our trip in large part due to the Makanda by the Sea hotel. We stayed in a studio room, which had a small kitchen and a nice balcony. The view was spectacular! Jungle and beach both on the same picture! We will definitely recommend this hotel to couples looking for a peaceful escape...breakfast was included, like most hotels in CR, however, it was delivered to your room every morning and it was delicious! Not just Pinto (rice and beans), eggs and toast like others. The food in their restaurant was great...we ate there the first night, ate out the second, and decided to make sure we ate there again because the food was the best we had had during our trip. The prices were ok...comparable to the States if not a bit more...but totally worth it! On the negative side, you are really far from everything...they advertise they have a beach, and although it is a nice hike up and down in the middle of the jungle towards the beach (might be hard for some but we happened to love it because it is something we do not get to walk through at home) their private beach is really not close. You can't quite spend time there, it is not comfortable. If you do not have a car it might be uncomfortable to go in and out of the place. Taxi cabs are cheap, so I guess that could help. We had a rental and it was the best...after all we did not go out much but it was nice to have the freedom to do so if necessary. Whatever was in the mini bar or on top of the dinner table, was priced way too high...will recommend you take a quick trip to the local supermarket to get your snacks...the nice kitchen could be helpful if you like to cook at all. The pool was very nice and the service was great...we enjoyed some overpriced drinks but the time and the views were worth it ,once again! I think it is very fair for us to say that Makanda by the Sea was the cleanest, nicest room we have stayed at...and we have traveled quite a bit! We will go back in a heart beat!

author: BFDStein
title: Superb - hope to go back!
text: This was one of the most romantic places my wife and I have ever been. We went to the park one morning and actually came back because the hotel was so much more pleasant than the beach! The restaurant had delicious food, great ambience, and excellent service. It was also affordably priced, which was a surprise. The room (studio 3) was outstanding. The view of the sunsets was priceless. We relaxed in the pool for hours and hours every day. Breakfast is very fresh and included a lot of options, all of which were included in the room price, and lunch was cheap and delicious. You can order food and drinks at the restaurant or to your room basically from 7am through 10pm. The staff were very friendly (almost "friends"!) and at out our beckon call, but yet provided us with total privacy. The rooms are simply beautiful (not outdated by any standards). We felt VERY safe. There was a very active staff and guards on duty at all times. We kept our valuables locked up in a safe the whole time. We didn't need even so much as a watch or a wallet here. You can charge everything to your room and why worry about what time it is in paradise? We definitely hope to go back!

author: jmb872
title: Secluded and romantic resort
text: Makanda was a worthwhile splurge. We stayed in studio #9, and it was perfect for a romantic getaway. Our room overlooked the jungle and the ocean. The outside porch was the perfect place to eat breakfast or relax in the hammock. The restaurant food is good, and the prices are on par with other places in the Manuel Antonio area. (The food is also better and more reasonably priced than at the nearby Mariposa hotel.) The private beach was beautiful, though a bit rocky. You need to have a sense of adventure to stay here. It's quite a ways off the main road, down a rocky and pothole-filled road. The hotel does provide a free golf cart ride up to the main road. It's also quite a hike to get to the private beach... at least 300 steps down a cliff. But the trail is well marked, and you're well rewarded once you get there. We went on the tour that Makanda recommended of Manuel Antonio National Park. While this tour was more expensive than hiring a guide at the park entrance ($45 vs $20), it included transportation to/from the park and hotel, the park entrance fee, and fresh fruit at the end. Plus our guide was amazing... the other park guides were following him because was finding all of the animals. The staff was very friendly, always asking what they could do for us.

author: Ksp48a
title: Magical
text: There are a total of 11 gorgeous rooms. Ours was 950 sq. feet. overlooking the jungle and the sea without another soul in sight.One day my wife was "chased" in from the terrace by a troop of Capucin Monjey's coming through. Most days we had the infinity pool to ourselves (adults only in any event). Imagine floating in the pool, watching the sun disappear into the Pacific with a troop of 15 Howler Monkeys in the tree immediately overhead. It was magical. It was romantic. it was wonderful. The food is excellent. The service is very good. Its close to Manuel Antonio Park (well worth a guided visit). Its also close to some very nice restaurants if you tire of the Sunspot on the property (which is quite romantic). The Jungle Canopy Zip Line is terrific . Oh, and a massage in a "tent" by the pool was wonderful also. Frankly, we had not expected to love it as much as we did and we would love to return.

author: honest0112
title: The best MA has to offer!
text: This was our second time at Makanda, having also stayed at Si Como No and Mariposa during previous stays, and having spent a fair amount of time at the Gaia property during this last trip. Makanda is still by far and away my strong preference, for all of the reasons that many have noted in previous reviews. While I was impressed with the Gaia property, it just doesn't quite seem to fit in Manuel Antonio, it doesn't have that Costa Rica charm. Don't get me wrong, it is a beautiful property and they execute well but the Euro/South Beach feel to the property just seems a little out of place. If that type of style is your preference, then it would certainly be a very good choice. We enjoyed our dining experience there, the spa was the best in MA, but I'll take Makanda for the privacy, personal service, room style and size and overall accommodations. Makanda is a very well run property, with a fantastic and experienced staff and a sense of intimacy that is unmatched at Gaia, La Mariposa or any of the other main upscale hotels. It has a sense of understated luxury and exclusivity about it, while not ever trying to be something it is not. The pool area is sheer beauty, with what now seems to be a resident Sloth and a (perhaps sometimes overly) healthy monkey population. The sunset views are incredible. Makanda offers a unique feeling of privacy, seclusion and romance without losing the Costa Rica/Manuel Antonio feel. The rooms are all very tastefully done, we stayed in Villa 10 (our favorite) and also spent a few nights in Villa 5, which was also very nice. A very good breakfast is brought to your villa each morning and that really is a fantastic way to start the day. The mosquito netting over the bed seems to be more for the charm than any real necessity, and it does add a certain charm. The restaurant is very good, although with so many choices around MA we opted only to eat there one evening. The staff at the restaurant is superb and very accommodating whether for dinner or just some poolside refreshments. Our next trip to MA we will be back at Makanda and already can't wait.

author: lovehawaii37
title: Amazing hotel, wonderful staff
text: We were at Makanda for one week in Villa 5. I can't say enough about the wonderful staff at Makanda. Everyone there made us feel like family. Melissa and Junior are wonderful, Gloria also took great care of us and had a different animal with flowers arranged on our bed each day. It was a treat to see what she would come up with each day. Yes, the road to the hotel was a challenge, but nothing that would keep us from returning. The breakfast each day was amazing, set up on our balcony. It is not a large hotel, only 11 Villas, so at the beautiful pool there were only a couple of people each time we were there. The view from the pool and Sunspot resturant were amazing and staff there were the best. We were joined each day by Whitefaced and Titi monkeys which was great, but please don't feed the monkeys, it is not good for them. I just can't say enough about the incredible level of service we experienced while at Makanda. My husband and I have traveled extensively and found the people of Costa Rica to be the warmest and most friendly of anywhere we have visited. We never felt unsafe while in Costa Rica. Worth the trip up the road was Cafe Milagro for their great coffee and banana bread. They also have a great breakfast and lunch. The park tour is a must do, as well as the canopy tour with Canopy Safari, great ziplining. Staff at Makanda arranged our transportation to and from the airport as well as all of our activities. We look forward to staying at Makanda again.

author: linners07
title: Nice Hotel
text: We stayed in both the deluxe studio #11 and standard studio #3. The studio's in general were a little more rundown than all the more pricier rooms. It seems like the studio's didn't get as much of the renovations as some of the other more expensive rooms got, such as newer flooring, tiles, paint job. So if youre staying in anything above a studio it might be worth your money, but the studio's themselves needed some work. We also had some issues with insects which is kind of expected in this area. I imagine all the hotels in the manuel antonio rain forest area have this issue to varying degrees. Normally it was an occasional ant or spider, but once we found a big cockroach in the bathroom. Our friends in studio #2 had issues with some kind of insects in their bed as they woke up with tiny red bites all over their leg. Not sure if other hotels would've been better sealed from insects. Location is remote and the pool is one of the nicest. There aren't that many guests around so you feel like you have to place to yourself. The area is decently landscaped but I was definitely more impressed with Si Como No's common areas. It was very well constructed with manicured walkways between rooms and pools, whereas in Makanda you had to walk down a dark road at times within the hotel property to get to the office or pool. The pool staff was great, provided towels and cushions right away. The check-in staff along with the check-in office was very minimal and looked like a 1-2 star hotel. The check-in service wasn't that impressive, they just did their job but didn't really provide any great service above and beyond giving you your key and taking your key back at checkout. I'd probably stay at Si Como No if I went back for the same price range.

author: MdWeekender
title: Great Views and Privacy
text: The view from our room is the cover picture of our album. It is simply gorgeous - bannana tree right in front of the porch. Beautiful ocean view. We stayed in Villa #7. It's an easy hike to the pool. The open shower is way cool - you'll love it. Housekeeping leaves towels in shapes - swans, teddy bears, hearts - very cute. It was great to be in a couples only place - we left our two kids home for our anniversary trip. Monkeys came right down to the pool one afternoon - it was very exciting. We also saw them cross the monkey bridge one morning as we were waiting for our tour bus. The hotel is down a long bumpy road and requires a taxi - which is about $7 each way to the beach. Infinity pool is great; as is the pool side restaurant. We walked down the steps to the beach at low tide. We weren't sure if we should turn around or not because we didn't know how far. We were brave and went all the way down. It was easier coming back up than we expected. The beach is black and rocky - no umbrellas or chairs - and nobody else around - if there was an emergency - you would be out of luck - but we were glad we went on the adventure - the kids loved the rocks and coral that we picked up on the beach.

author: tori9054
title: Enjoyed our stay...
text: We stayed in Villa 10- King sized very comfortable bed, huge wrap around comfortable couch, TV with cable, large kitchenette, nice bathroom with great toiletries. The best part about this hotel was the balcony. Very large, comfortable chairs on the balcony along with a table and chairs and a hammock. As soon as we got there a few Squirrel monkeys came to visit us. We also saw White faced monkies from our balcony. The view of the ocean is OK- no view of MA park. It was a perfect spot for the sunset- we had front row seats, unobstructed view of the most gorgeous sunsets! We didn't use the pool, didn't appeal much to us. Ate lunch at the poolside restaurant which got great views in travel books. We thought it was ok, very expensive. They serve you breakfast in your room, it was pretty good. The beach accessed from inside the hotel grounds is not appealing at all, besides, it was a steep 10 minute walk though a path in the jungle to get there. There was another beach down the road past La Mansion Inn and past the new condos being built called Playa Besanz (sp?) that we went to- 20 minute at the most from Makanda - beautiful water and sand and you can snorkel- if you go, bring water shoes. Almost the entire floor of the water is large stones. This hotel is a 10-15 minute cab ride from MA park- that is where we really enjoyed the beaches although they were a bit of a hike to get there and there is almost no beach during high tide, MA beach is the most gorgeous beach with the clearest water. Animals on the property were abundant...saw tons of iguanas, two sloths pointed out by the nice man at the front gate two different times, and lots of monkeys. They took us by golf cart to La Mariposa for dinner/drinks one night (Tuesdays their one and only restaurant is closed) which was a nice service. We were floored by the the fantastic view here and the pool area...I think I would stay there next.

author: KristaNyc
title: paradise, really
text: There is not space (or time) enough to share every detail of our incredible stay at Makanda, but I'll attempt to convey how outstanding the experience was nonetheless... We stayed in studio 9 for 7 nights. We felt as though we were in in absolute seclusion the entire time (only rarely detected the presence of the upstairs guests in Villa 8). Our view was breathtaking; we looked forward to returning to Makanda every day/evening to relax and enjoy the view. The pool was never crowded, despite my concerns that March is high tourist season. The jungle location never stops being amazing... even after 7 nights. The hotel blends seamlessly with its surroundings so that the monkeys and sloths that we readily spotted (and heard) went about their business as if we were not even there. Incredible. But, maybe most importantly, the staff at Makanda is simply the best. From booking our stay with Melissa, to Marvin delivering breakfast, Willy at the pool, Manfred serving dinner, Marco and Leo at the font desk, Gorge at the front gate... we did not meet a person who we did not genuinely enjoy. We walked down to the Makanda beach only once, preferring to walk over to Playa Espadilla on the border of the park. We took cabs too/from Quepos and Manuel Antonio; cabs seems to be a necessity for most staying in the area, even those at hotels less secluded and easier to get to than Makanda (unless you rent a car). Regardless, we always found transportation easy. This was definitely a vacation I hope to repeat at some point in the future. Manuel Antonio was gorgeous and Makanda was unquestionably the best place we could have stayed. As if its not obvious, I highly recommend it. I attached some photos of our room/view for those interested.

author: mesu802
title: Great Large Rooms, Shady Hotel Employee
text: The stay itself was great. We loved the large room, complete kitchen, balcony that overlooks the forest and ocean, and the in-room breakfast which is included. I especially liked the lovely king-sized bed. The sheets were divine. However, when we got back to the States, we noticed that there was an extra charge for $107.24. I emailed the hotel and they said the charge was for a cash advance. I did not make a cash advance nor did I sign for it. They emailed me the signed receipt and it was indeed forged. I know it was a hotel employee who forged my signature and took off with $100. I am in the process of getting my refund back. Be sure to check all credit card charges. Whoever forged my signature and got a cash advance is going to be fired immediately. Also, the roads there are horrific. The owners of these hotels should step up and finance paved roads in front of their hotels. These hotels are supposedly the best hotels in Manuel Antonio. Paved roads is a no brainer.

author: Trav1964
title: Best hotel in Manuel Antonio
text: I have been to Costa Rica many times and have stayed at Makanda several times. I think Makanda is cool and a good overall Costa Rica experience. The villas are very large, nicely done and great views. They are well placed with good privacy and jungle feel. Breakfast delivered to your room is a nice touch. The bathrooms could be a little nicer, but minor. Although the pool is fun, it could be done better. It is a little dated. The only large miss here is the restaurant. It’s a tent off the pool. The food has always been good, but the environment isn’t. They should really put some effort into creating a nice restaurant and bar. Oh, there isn’t a bar. Just bar service. Overall, if you stay at Makanda you won’t regret it. One of my favorite hotels in Costa Rica.

author: Gamero
title: Makanda was amazing! Everything we had hoped it would be ...
text: Like another reviewer said, I also loved Makanda by the Sea so much that I feel it is necessary to give them an excellent review. Out of the three hotels we stayed in during our 10-day trip to Costa Rica, Makanda was our favorite hotel by far. The rooms were beautiful and had everything we needed. We stayed in Villa 5 and really appreciated the fully-stocked kitchen, the great selection of television channels, the beautiful view and balcony, and also the yummy bath products that were refilled everyday. Every morning we enjoyed watching a large troupe of monkeys make their way toward our balcony, and of course the amazing breakfasts were also something to look forward to in the mornings. My favorite was the pancakes with banana coconut toppings and also the fresh fruit juice. As to the grounds, the pool is beautiful and has a great view of the ocean and surrounding areas. I also recommend making the trek (and boy is it a trek going back up to the hotel) to the beach. It is very secluded and beautiful. The restaurant, Sunspot Grill, at Makanda by the Sea is also not to be missed. We ate dinner there almost every night and couldn't believe how delicious and fresh their fish was. Their desserts are also wonderful. Everyone on the wait staff was so hospitable and nice as well. In fact everyone in general, from the front desk staff to the person who monitors the front gate, was very gracious and nice to us our entire stay. One thing I would also like to comment on is the safety of the place. There are signs EVERYWHERE reminding people to lock their doors and keep a close eye on their belongings, and the hotel makes it clear that it is the individual's responsibility to keep tabs on his/her things Let's face it people, it's Costa Rica and things have been known to happen, so please take their warnings to heart. From everything we could see, the security here was great, and even at night we saw people keeping an eye on the parking lots and just perusing the grounds in general to make sure everything was safe. We felt completely safe and at ease at Makanda, and we would return to this hotel in a heartbeat! It really was one of the most relaxing and romantic hotels we have visited.

author: FellowTraveler12797
title: Perfect
text: We loved this hotel for our honeymoon! The staff is WONDERFUL. We chatted with the American owners several times and they are nice, too. We called every morning and had breakfast delivered to our room. The order was always correct, the food hot...fresh mango and papaya every morning! We always felt safe here as there's a "guard" at the front of the drive. The room was bright, spacious and comfortable. The balcony was perfect for afternoon naps in the hammock or morning coffee. Beautiful and fragrant flowers everywhere...the reception area, the rooms, the paths, the restaurant. This hotel is the ONLY place we saw monkeys. We didn't see them on the canopy tour, at El Avion, in the National Park..only here! And one morning the howler monkies woke us up EARLY. But the sun wakes ya up around 5:30 AM anyway. The pool area was very clean. The only one complaint I have is too much Bob Marley. I'd rather hear Costa Rican music, not Jamaican music. Oh, well. I would definitely stay here again and would definitely recommend this hotel to any couple.

author: Journey16694
title: The Truth about Makanda
text: My new wife and I stayed at Makanda from May 8th to the 14th. We stayed in Villa 7 which is located below the Sun deck by the pool. We had read many reviews about Makanda, some good some bad. All and all we had a great stay at the Makanda. My only complaint was walking more steps in a week than we had all year. Remember folks this is Costa Rica, not Hawaii. This a 3rd world country and not for the faint of heart. The service at the restaurant was great and the poolside service was above and beyond; including frozen towels to cool off and small servings of ice cream. We would have liked to see a little more wildlife (Monkeys and Sloths). In reading all the reviews that rated Makanda poorly I believe some people are snotty "international travellers" who think that any hotel staff needs to bow down and thank them for gracings the hotel with their presence. I had a great time with the staff including the grounds crew, who did a great job keeping the Makanda beautiful, not to mention always pointing out weird creatures for us to see. If your going to Makanda tell Manuel I said hello. He is the smiley character with the Machete. We would definately go back to Makanda. Last word of advice; if you are frightened by bugs, crabs or lizards this place may not be for you. If you are looking for adventure Costa Rica definately offers a variety of exciting tours. We really reccommend the ATV tour in the rain forest....Very Cool! Good luck and happy travelling.

author: leverhart
title: Beautiful view, pleasant service
text: We just got back from Makanda after spending 3 nights in Villa #1 and 2 in Villa #6. Both were nice, but I preferred #1. It is open-air, and I was a little leery, but it was wonderful. A few lizards (small) dined in the rafters, but they were cute. There were no bugs to speak of, and I didn'y even open my repellant even though mosquitoes love me. I found the staff very friendly, helpful and attentive. They got our breakfast order exactly right every time and it arrived promptly. The view from #1 was spectacular and it was very quiet except for the early morning wakeup call from the howling monkeys- otherworldly! #6 was a little less quiet because it is near the gate and there is a lot of foot traffic going by. The MA Park tour arranged by the hotel was very good. If we'd gone without a guide we wouldn't have seen most of the wildlife. The beaches inside the park are very nice. The hotel also arranged for us to go on the Titi canopy tour, which was excellent. The guides were very friendly and helpful and VERY safety conscious. Booking early is important or you won't get what you want in the way of accomodations.

author: marian12
title: Beautiful Setting
text: My husband and I stayed at Makanda by the Sea Hotel on the Pacific Coast of Costa Rica during the first week of January 2006. The hotel is approximately equidistant between the town of Quepos and Manuel Antonio National Park. The setting is absolutely spectacular! The rooms are all situated to maximize privacy and all oriented toward the ocean. Each has its own terrace or balcony. The grounds are very lush and attract a wide variety of butterflies and birds. There are also many monkeys on the property. It is quite a show to sit on your terrace and just watch the wildlife! The staff is incredibly attentive and will cater to your every need and desire. Although I think they are very reluctant to tell you no something can't be done or that there is a delay (I found this to be true of most Costa Ricans that I met). They will arrange any tours for you that you might want to take (e.g., national park, rain forest, etc.). This makes activities away from the hotel very convenient. The service in the restaurant is excruciatingly slow (I'm not talking about leisurely, gracious dining -- but painfully and tiresomely slow). We ended up going out to eat most nights; fortunately there are many nice options in the vicinity. However, they deliver breakfast to your room each morning. This is a nice touch and a great (and relaxing!) way to start the day. The rooms are showing a little wear (at least, ours was). But they are fairly large and comfortable, and the view can't be beat! However, they aren't very well lit so at night it is a little hard to see or read in the room. All in all, it was a great vacation and I wasn't ready to come home at the end of the week.

author: FrequentFlier26853
title: Thinks it's better than it is
text: The room was stunning, but a couple of things detracted from our enjoyment. This hotel is so "exclusive" that our personal guide was not allowed onto the premises. This is an uncomfortable and undemocratic rule in an otherwise friendly and egalitarian country - we (British) were astonished. I realise they are trying to make it "special" but we were embarassed to have our guide wait at the gate for us - we had to go out to share a drink with him and plan our next day. The evening meal was very good and the poolside location very romantic. The staff were very friendly and sweet. The breakfasts were really not up to scratch though - delivered to your room in a cool box and not very generous portions. No sense of luxury about that! Especially as you make your own coffee and they charge you for the milk. Why not a proper tray with linen? I loved looking out over the bay from the bed and the privacy was quite good in spite of being open on all sides, but there are a lot of hotels crammed onto that hillside - you are not out on some lonesome promontary. The bathroom was good with flowers everywhere, but the lighting was too low, and frankly, as a woman on holiday by the sea, I need to be able to see to shave my legs! There are too many "luxury" hotels that give no thought to this - men have lovely well-lit mirrors and we girls end up balancing with one foot in the sink! Kind of detracts from the sense of being pampered! We mostly enjoyed our stay but would not choose the hotel again.

author: GreenTraveler
title: Makanda was fabulous!
text: We arrived at Makanda in the early evening after a long and stressful drive. Once we got there is was dark and raining, so we had no idea what beauty lied ahead. The room is tastefully decorated, nicely laid out and strewn with fresh flowers (a cute touch). You can light the room in 50 different ways, which we thought was kind of funny. The best part of the room are the french doors, which span one entire wall and provide the most amazing view. We ordered room service that evening and had the most amazing food- costa rican trout with almond, basil sauce, grilled calamari, yummy bread, and a spinach salad. The coconut creme brulee was delicious, as well as the chilean wine. This meal was under $50 and the best of our trip- not to mention in the comfort of our room. In the morning, we woke up to the most amazing view of the ocean and the sounds of monkeys in the trees. Each morning you call in your breakfast and it is delievered to your room. The fresh fruit, coffee, french toast, granola, etc was to die for. You don't even have curtains on the windows, as it is not needed for privacy. The service, food, location and accomodations were all excellent. It would've been nice to have a bathtub, the shower head was a little weak and there were some ants in the kitchen (as is normal), but those things did not impact my impression at all. We loved this place and plan on coming back!

author: Daydream15735
title: Private, Exotic, Wonderful
text: We wanted to find a hotel that made us feel like we were a part of the jungle yet enjoy all the comforts and luxury that small boutique hotels can offer, intimate, well tended and excellent service - and we were very satisfied with the Makanda by the Sea. We stayed in Studio #11 for four nights - and loved it. The entire wall that faces the ocean is a series of glass and wood doors that open up. The entire room is strategically placed facing the ocean, framed by trees that provided us with the perfect view. We woke up to the sight of Capuchin monkeys eating in the tops of the trees - just by openning our eyes from sleeping! The space was well designed in a nice simple modern/japanese style with touches of tropical prints and fresh flowers and local wood accents. It had a small kitchenette, a well stocked mini-bar (not free - but convenient), kimonos, and most importantly, two of the most efficient fans, one on the patio, and one over our bed - PLUS an air conditioner. Temperature wise - we were provided with exactly what we needed to be very comfortable, and bug-wise, I guess we went at a good time of year, because we had no bug problems except for one small spider in the bathroom. Front desk service was excellent. I let the front desk know that the CD player was not working and by the time we came back from dinner there was a new one set up. Our breakfast was brought to our room each morning, the room was kept very clean, we came back one day to delightful petals sprinkled on the bathroom rug and by the sink. The restaurant was good - certainly well recognized and respected by everyone in the area (whenever we told anyone we were staying at the Makanda, they always remarked on the restaurant). We had two dinners there and they were good, but not the best we had in the area. It was very private, the only place we saw other guests were by the pool/restaurant and the parking area. I have included a photo of the beach at the Makanda. It does consist of quite a series of steps the lead down the hill to the beach - it is a little more difficult going back up - we had no problem with it - but it might be an issue for others. The beach below is still that volcanic grey color - dramatic and lovely, but Manuel Antonio offers lovely white sand beaches nearby so you can enjoy both. My one tiny comment is that when we first checked in, our room had a lingering smell of cigarette smoke - after openning up the doors and running the fans the smell cleared and was not an issue. Overall, we enjoyed what felt like a very special room and would definitely recommend it to people who are looking for such a lovely private place.

author: tannins
title: Eaten Alive
text: Maybe the most beautiful place we have ever stayed. BUT..... But i wouldn't agree to stay on the moon if it meant dealing with all of the bugs. Bugs in the shower, bugs in the couch, bugs in the bed. All kinds of them. Little red spiders, ants, mosquitos, alien looking things would all be fine, if you could keep them outside of the room. Heck, outside of the mosquito net around the bed would have been acceptable i guess. Three days into our week after one of us had to sleep in pants, socks (on her hands, too) and a hood, drenched in bug repelant and STILL had dozens of bites in the morning, we got fed up and booked ourselves a room up the road at an airconditioned hotel (that cost less than half the price) with no bug issues. The management at Makanda offered no refund or solution or assistance in paying for our additional hotel room. They only offered to move us to a smaller villa that was under construction and too noisy. The food was great. The scenary amazing. The rustic beach beautiful. The management disgusting, rude and irresponsible. I would never give another penny to this establishment.

author: Ross9000
title: Lovely Room, Great Staff & Nice Breakfast. 5 stars!
text: My Girlfriend and I stayed here just last week for three nights. We booked the bigger of the double room options. The staff were so friendly and helpful and the lady that greeted us helped us to feel very welcome! The room was lovely and tidy, and had daily cleaning service, with a well stocked and very reasonable priced mini bar. Good location ... 5 mins walk from the Spanish Steps, and around a 8 min walk to the Trevi Fountain. The breakfast was great for our tastes. a nice contintental section of quality bread, hams and cheese, fruit, croissants, jams, orange and pineapple juice as well as cereals. It came served by the staff with one of the tastiest coffee I have had! To be honest I was doubtful of the room before I turned up as it was so so cheap. To be fair we came out of season, but it really was a great deal. The rooms are so nice, although they do have an echoey acoustic due to the floor, so there is a possible sound issue, although we heard nothing else from any of the other guests during our stay.
