If you want to rock up here and make a load of noise and party in the hotel room all night then look elsewhere! We had the TV on for an hour before sleep and in the morning with no fuss whatsoever, and heard nothing else during our stay. Book ahead, and make sure you watch the video on how to find the room. We loved the Elevator! In short it's 5 stars from me. I hope the hotel reads this and can feel my heartfelt thanks for a wonderful stay.

author: JustJo29
title: Comfortable bed, good breakfast
text: We were very pleased with this hotel and would definitely stay here again. We did not rent a car for our time in Rome. We took the bus (8EUR return) and walked for a few minutes. The location is great and there were a lot of restaurants to eat at. We love to walk and found a lot of the iconic tourist stops to be within walking distance. The hotel itself is great. You really must watch the video of how to find the front door, otherwise it's unlikely you will ever find it. The receptionist greeted us on the 3rd floor and check-in was very smooth. The room was on the small side, but very clean. There was a mini bar and a kettle with coffee or tea. The aicon worked very well. The pictures of the bed are misleading - often in Italy, the beds are rock hard. The pictures led us to believe that it was a standard ridiculously firm bed, but we were surprised to find that it was the most comfortable bed we've experienced in Italy. The wifi was very good and worked in the room. The shower was warm and the pressure was good. When running the shower, the mechanism that drains the water is very noisy. Breakfast was delightful. We had cappuccinos and fresh fruit. There was also cereal and many kind of cakes and bread. Jam and nutella was available on the table.

author: MECindylou
title: Excellent value, small, quiet, great location!
text: I recently stayed at the DG Prestige Room for 7 nights and would definitely stay there again. Marina and Giuseppe could not have been nicer. I was traveling alone and they made me feel completely at home. My room (18) was on a quiet inner courtyard and I was never disturbed by noise, inside or out. My room was large enough that I did not feel claustrophobic (decent as European standards go), in perfect condition, and immaculately clean. The bathroom, though small, was bright and modern, with a heated towel rack, hair dryer, shower, bidet, good-quality towels (replaced daily, as needed), a shelf under the sink for toiletries, and an amenities basket with shower gel/shampoo, soap, etc. There were numerous electrical outlets, a desk, a TV (not much on, but they have a collection of DVDs you can borrow), a spacious closet (with a safe and an extra blanket), and a mini-fridge. The window to the courtyard opened easily, so I could get fresh air. The breakfast room was pleasant and the breakfast was very good, with lots of choices. Along with breads and pastries, there were coffee or cappuccino, juices, fruit (stewed prunes and peaches, apples), hard-boiled eggs, granola and other cereals, milk, meats and cheeses, mozzarella balls and cherry tomatoes, yogurt, jams, Nutella, and butter. Via Lombardia is quiet, but you’re only 5 minutes or so walking distance from Piazza Barberini where there’s a metro station (short rides to Termini or Cipro (Vatican Museum), for example, and buses. Other walking distances: Borghese Gallery is 10-15 minutes, Spanish Steps are 5-10 minutes, Termini is 20-25 minutes. Bear in mind, the area is uphill from Barberini, Via Veneto, and the Spanish Steps. It didn’t bother me, but it’s something to think about if that concerns you. I did exhaustive research; if you want an affordable place to stay that’s safe, clean, pleasant, and conveniently-located for walking to many sights in Rome, look no further!

author: Robdavies88
title: 3 bad nights
text: I stayed here for 3 nights, and I’ve just had 3 terrible nights sleep. The location is right in the middle of the red light district, so very easy to find, but the street outside is extremely busy, especially at night. I’m in an 18 bed dorm which gets roasting hot and stuffy, so having windows open is a must, so get used to sleeping with people shouting outside at night, then lorries and delivery vans first thing in the morning. There is no curfew here, so expect people turning up in your room every hour of the night. Due to it being the cheapest hostel in the area, most of them aren’t the type who respect others, so they will be loud and they will smoke weed by the window as I found. On my last night, at some rediculous hour, the staff even dragged an extra mattress into the room so a 19th person could sleep on the floor. Again, no effort to keep voices or noise down, and this was a member of staff. The beds themselves aren’t great - I ended up with a top bunk...it had no ladder up or any bars on it, so there was a straight drop down if you rolled off. Toilets aren’t great either. There’s a separate shower/toilet room on each level for males and females, but given 18/19 people sleeping in this apparent ‘mixed’ dorm are all men, there is always a long wait in the morning. WiFi is terrible. You need to register with your Facebook account which posts on your account. When you do get access, it is very slow. My 3G data is about 2-3 times faster to put into perspective. There’s no plugs for laptops in the rooms - the only plugs in here are USB plugs for charging phones. I found people were sitting on the stair wells to use their laptops. The only positives from this is that it is in a good location and easy to find, and it is cheaper than other hostels in the area, although across Europe I have stayed in my hostels that have been much cheaper than this, but with better facilities.

author: thegreatpumpkin
title: I think I was a bit too “old” for this hostel
text: On the positive side - this was in pretty fantastic location, especially if you are planning to take advantage of the red light district. The price is low compared to a lot of Amsterdam hostels. I had only good interactions with the staff, everyone was nice and friendly and willing to chat when it wasn't super busy. The 2.5 euro breakfast was a great deal, drinks and snacks at the bar are cheaper than anywhere around it. But unfortunately I can't say I'm a huge fan of this hostel. It's old, dark, dinghy, in serious need of an update. The bathrooms had missing ceiling tiles, hair everywhere, a distinct smell of mildew. My bunk bed had gum stuck in more than one place. The rooms were quite cramped, the beds in my room were so close together that two people couldn’t pass between them at the same time. The rooms only offer USB chargers, no real outlets, so it charges smart phones super slowly. If you want to use a real outlet, you have to go to the bar area where they have powerstrips on the tables which I guess is a good way to get you out of your room to socialize. But was kind of a pain when there are two large and loud stag parties taking up the whole bar. Also, my wi-fi access was blocked my first night due to file sharing activity (I wasn’t doing any file sharing, I didn’t even download anything) and no one could unblock me. As someone in her 30s, I think I was a bit too “old” for this hostel. If all your planning to do is sleep and party, this is probably a good bet. But I think If I return to Amsterdam, I’ll spend the extra few euros for something more modern.

author: QiaoLingHo
title: Central location, basic hostel stay
text: The location of the hostel is perfect. Just few minutes from the central train station and few minutes to the red light district. I stayed a night. The mattress are really thin and sunken in the middle. I am fine with it. But if you are looking for somewhere comfortable, you probably won't appreciate it. You got to pay for the locker if you need one. The receptionist are nice and bartenders are all fun loving bunch. The hangout area is pretty chill and it's open 24 hours which was great. The toilets are clean. The breakfast is not really worth it I thought. It is cheap thou, 2.50 euros but I do think that you could get better food along the street with maybe 3 euros. Well, that is personal preference. I am very easy with food and sleep so the hostel is really good cause all it matters to me was the location. :)

author: Jemmotsk
title: Warm & welcoming
text: I arrived to Amsterdam on a Saturday (July 18th)morning during peak tourist season without anywhere to stay. Everywhere was telling me that a last minute Saturday night would be 60€ and there were two night minimums and I thought I'd be homeless in Amsterdam until I found hostel meeting point. I showed up and there was a sign on the door that clearly said they were booked, but in my desperation I asked a gentlemen who was cleaning about availability and he told me to come back at 11 am and check to see. I return at 11am and a lovely lady named Rita (I think) is working the front desk. She seems very organized knows exactly what's going on and keeps people flowing in and out of the lobby. I asked her about availability and she tells me that I can wait a few more hours until she has people checked out and rooms clean and then she'll let me know what's available. And she tells me the price of the dorms, €30 on a weekend night which is half of what anywhere else was telling me. She was so kind and let me wait in the lobby and didn't even mind me asking a thousand questions. They were my last hope and she came through ! She had one bed left in an 18 person dorm and got me all all checked in even though the room wasn't clean I told her it didn't matter is stay out of the way. I only stayed one night but the whole time I was there everyone was super kind and helpful. When I checked out the next day they let me leave my luggage there for free so I didn't have to haul it around with me all day which i really appreciated. The only slightly inconvenient thing I can think of is that there are only outlets and wifi in the bar area. I guess this promotes the "meeting people" vibe but I know a lot of people are used to their phones changing right next to their bedside. The beds were clean, showers were clean. Lockers available for 2€ with a 10€ deposit. They serve breakfast and you're guaranteed to meet amazing people. Thanks for everything Hostel Meeting Point!

author: KadieZ
title: Amazing location!
text: Stayed here for two nights with my boyfriend during our recent interrailing trip and we were both impressed. We slept in a dorm with six other people who were all friendly and considerate. We each had our own locker, so we could rest assured that all of our things were safe. I could not fault the location: it is genuinely perfect. It's only a five minute walk from central station and the street stays reasonably quiet at night so it's easy to get a good night's sleep if you so wish. The room was clean as were the shared toilet and shower facilities. The hostel has its own bar which is reasonably priced and it also has its own smoking room which is pretty chill. There was free wifi in the room which was great but I would have liked to have had plug sockets in the room too. They were available downstairs in the bar area though. We'd totally forgotten to bring towels but we managed to rent some from the hostel which was nice. The staff are also friendly and helpful. I think the only thing I could fault with this hostel is the stairs... We were on the top floor, there is no elevator (so don't stay here if someone in your party is disabled. it isn't accessible at all.) and the stairs are extremely steep - not something you look forward to after a day indulging in all the city has to offer... Regardless I'd definitely recommend this hostel to any young backpackers, it was exactly what we were looking for and it was certainly worth (if not better than) what we paid for it.

author: L1quidator
title: Pursuing the plug
text: We stayed there in 8-beds room because of only reason there were no places in other hostels for that days available. Actually, I don't know the prices in other Amsterdam hostels (damn expensive city), but we paid about 30 EUR/per night (after 4-5beds rooms costed 25 in Cologne and 22 in LuxuryBourg with breakfast included). Position is great (near the central station and tourists attractions), but it was not a big deal for us because we traveled by Eurolines (train station Amstel) and still had to go by metro. Stuff is nice (they gave us back forgotten in the bar mobile). You can leave your luggage for free in hostel (with no guaranties though) after checking-out. Breakfast for 2,5 EUR is helpful in Amsterdam. It contains 3 toasted big pieces of bread, jam, boiled egg, cheese (1 piece), butter (enough for 1,5 toast max), 200 ml cup of tea/coffee. So I's better to have something with you for 1 piece of bread or eat it as "dry food". Tea was not enough for me, so we BOUGHT HOT WATER there for only 50 cents and had our sugar-steaks and tea-packets (from LuxuryBourgian hostel :) ). Wi-fi is only available in that bar, I don't have it in rooms. Actually, you have nothing in rooms except of 2level beds and lockers (available for 2EUR/per day +10EUR deposit): no plugs, no hangers, no shelves, no chairs - so you don't have possibility to charge your modern phone (you have to charge every day) and photo-camera except you are sitting in the bar or staying in the toilette; you don't have anything to put your closes or goods on except of your bed. These two made us feeling really uncomfortable. In the city we used to look for eating place with plugs only, this made us pay more in cafes and loose our time to find appropriate one's. I saw a guy, who was vacuum-cleaned the rooms in the afternoon. He did nothing, just a 30 second's "work" in every room. And no locks on rooms is the third bad thing. We had no locker (because of rent-payment) and had to have shower in order. 100 inhabitants + friends is not the guaranty of your things safety even if it's hard to go inside the hostel from the street. And good thing, 8beds rooms on the 3rd flour had a view on the channel and central station - it's really nice. The same has half of 18beds rooms on the 1st and 2nd flour, you should ask during booking for that view.

author: frankm928
title: Just ok....
text: Stayed here last weekend. Was not what i was expecting to be honest. Its location is ideal. Not far from the train station and all the hotspot Amsterdam has to offer. Checked in and the reception staff were all very nice. We were asked if we wished to get a locker. Thought it wouldn't be a bad idea so we did. The locker is basically an oil barrel with a lid you can padlock. Thought they were trash barrels when i first saw them. Rooms have no locks on them was a big concern at first. Anyone can walk in to each others room. The rooms themselves are not that clean. Linen is fresh but the general state of the dorm rooms was not in good condition. Also our room was on the Third floor. With no elevator it can be a bit exhausting at times. Down stairs there is a bar, smoking room and internet hub. The bar is nothing to write home about and generally service was quite slow despite there not being that much going on. Didn't have breakfast.

author: hexalite2k5
title: Ok but quite a few shortcomings
text: You better have your expectations right before getting there otherwise you risk being disappointed. My room was unlocked or open day and night, there was no key. As it is the case with most other hostels in Holland there is no elevator so expect to carry your bag up the stairs. But the location is great; the price is also high but cheaper than most alternatives. Sleep quality was ok, my room was facing a pretty large canal so although there was some noise from outside, it was ok overall. There were lockers in the room but you couldn't use your own padlock with them. You have to rent a key from them for 2 Euros and also leave a small refundable deposit. There were no sockets in my room. From talking to the staff I understand this is done on purpose to minimize the chance that electronic devices get stolen while left to charge. Even so I understand thefts happen every few days, especially during the night when people leave valuables by their bed-side. While I understand their reasons for not providing sockets in some of the rooms, I think having the freedom to charge my own devices is important and necessary. The solution they provided seemed insufficient to me. They have a few extension cords (I counted 2-3) in the lobby area but unless you sit on the chairs next to them you probably won't be able to use them. During the night I put a few valuables (including the locker key) under my pillow. The quality of the WiFi was very poor. It wasn't only my phone that had issues, a lot of other tourists that I talked to had the same problem. The signal was very weak, my phone kept disconnecting. You had to go to a specific place in the lobby (basically sit on 1 of 2 chairs) to get full strength signal but even that didn't really work well. They do try to keep the place safe, you get a piece of paper when you check-in and if they don't recognize you when you want to re-enter later, they will ask for it.

author: Neags
title: Fantastic location, the 'lobby' smells though
text: I just want to start off saying that we paid next to nothing considering the euro rate at the moment so knew what to expect. For the price you pay the location is fantastic. You're more or less are in the heart of the action. 5 mins from the train station, round the corner from the red light district, the sq is at the end of the road and all the bars and coffee shops are just outside. You couldn't wish to be in a better location. The bathrooms are very clean and modern but the facilities are very average. The dorms for example. Lockers are provided but don't seem very secure i.e. it would take someone to kick it quite hard and the door would come off. So i would suggest to check out the locker before you use it but for 2 euros it was fine. The beds and carpet seem clean but are quite hard though it's quite warm in the rooms which is good. The bar area though does smell a bit and not very inviting. The menu and breakfast also is a bit bland with their 2 boiled eggs and bread. If you're travelling on a shoestring then fine but there are much better places about. The drink prices are okish but if you look around you can find better places with better atmosphere and the computer to use the internet look like it was bought in 1990. But the staff are absolutely fine. Overall this is a fine place for location and for a cheap budget break that doesn't mind sharing in large dorms. The bar was a let down but if you take the attitude of it's a place to lie your head down then its ok. you need to remember you get for what you paid for!

author: luramu
title: The Meeting Point is made for hanging around
text: The hostel has not very clean rooms. The carpet and matressess has many not definable blotchs, so I recommend you to take your own sheet with you. But you have enough space for your luggage. The bathroom is rather clean. The staircase, which you have to use when you came into the hostel through the bar and to your room, is very cliffy. The hostel is very near to the central station (by walk 1 min.) and the red light district. Next to the hostel are many coffeshops and smartshops too. It also has a very cheap and good wok restaurant next to the hostel. But the hostels pick of the bunch is definitive the bar. It looks like an old british pub, with to big flat tvs which always playing football. It has really cheap beer and a pool table. In the bar room it has 5 large tables on which it is allowed to eat food which is bought outside (takeaway). It has also a smoking room with a beautiful view on the amstel, or another big river (i'm not quite sure about that). In the smoking room its allowed to smoke weed with tabaco, not like in the coffeshops where it's only allowed to smoke pure joints. In the night the smoking room is closed and its allowed to smoke in the bar, which is 24/7 open. The employees are very friendly and helpful.

author: Cosmopolitan7639
title: soo good
text: amazing amazing amazing . loved it . loved the people the staff the barr the cats the service the atmosphere the location .the beds the view , i couldnt have asked for anything more . i would recomend this to everyone . im not a big fan of stairs but i didnt care it was to amazing to care. beautifull white cats climbing evertwhere . good music . nice breakfast . completley secure to keep anything you wana bring . i took my own sleeping bag just incase but didnt need it . but yea the lockers are top . really did me good . best place ever going back as soon as possible . also nice and cheap, cant wait to go back . met some amazing people .

author: LisaLiaw
title: Good value and great hospitality
text: We stayed for 5 nights and from airport pick-up to check in and check out, it was of great experience. Staff were generally friendly (except for one or two housekeeping staff merely looked our way without expression). The 2 bedroom apartment was well maintained and with beautiful furnishings. The kitchenette, washer and dryer were very useful. Staff came to do housekeeping every late morning. The gym was opened 24 hours, equipped with water, smoothie and modern equipments. Their daily activities is a big plus that included Muay Thai and Zumba. A big shout out to Apple for teaching me Muay Thai and Nadia for her upbeat Zumba dance. Both were very friendly. There’s also an air-conditioned lounge with pool table, mahjong table, table soccer where we totally enjoyed the facilities. It’s a place to hangout after check out but before time to leave for the airport. The only thing we wish is different is the size of the swimming pool. It’s kind of small and usually crowded. There are many restaurants just outside the resort at Turtle Village and a supermarket if you want to cook some simple meals. Overall, we will definitely return in the near future.

author: darrenoh888
title: A 'Peace' of Heaven in Phuket
text: This has been our family's favourite resort for many years. The resort caters to all ages. From computer games to fat wheel bicycles, billards to zumba dancing, swimming to mini golf course, the resort has it all. With the new strip mall and many restaurants located within walking distance, we can basically stay within the resort area and fully enjoy the facilities offered by the resort as well as JW Marriott which offer a couple of excellent dining choices. We particularly like Cucina for its selection of pizzas and pastas. Spa treatment is rather expensive but you can find a couple of really good Thai massage places within 15-20 minutes. Our current favourite is Mai Khao Thai Massage located close to Holiday Inn. Look for Paew - the owner. Pen & Lek were the best masseuses we have for a long time. If you are looking for halal seafood, try Tao Kun Seafood which is located about 20 minutes by car. Great ambience by the sea, fresh seafood home cooked and the owner, Khun Sunee is very hospitable and generous. Finally, have to give tremendous credit to the housekeeping team for keeping the room in such excellent condition. Team of Kai, Aor & Yora deserves mentioning. They will create nice art pieces from towels every day for us to enjoy. What a nice personal touch !

author: muzaneeshah
title: Everything is there
text: Stayed for 4D3N last Thursday. Apartment with 2 bedrooms. Located at Mai Khao Beach, northern part of Phuket with other resorts. The review is just on the hotel stay, not the membership. Pros: (1) Staff were good and attentive. Can speak good English and address your needs and queries in line international standards of Marriot. (2) Apartment is spacious and it has everything : 2 rooms, 2 bathrooms with bathtub, kitchen with induction stove, pot & pans, culteries, dishes, washing machine & dryer, ironing board, living hall, TV (3 units - each bedroom & living hall), patio. (3) As for the bedroom, its has twin bed (queen size each) (4) Facilities: 24 hour gym, pool, wading pool (covered), bar nearby the pool, golf putt putt, bicycle (2 hours usage), kids playroom, lounge, etc.. (5) Places to shop very nearby - Turtle village (2 mins walk), Mai Khao plaza (2 mins drive) (6) 7E Convenience store nearby. Family mart is just within 2-3 mins drive. (7) In the morning there is also small stalls selling local delicacies & thai coffee & tea (just opposite turtle village) by the side of the road. (8) Buggy services to the beach at the next door hotel. (9) Accessibility to other hotels/properties. (10) Location : quieter part of Phuket (Mai Khao beach - longest beach in Phuket) (11) Nearby to the airport : 15-20 mins drive Cons: (1) Location: Far from the happening areas of Phuket Town, Jungceylon, Bangla Road, Patong Beach. About 1 hours ++ drive from the resort provided no traffic (2) The shower at the 2nd bedroom has slow flow and looked old. I suggest to stay here for people who wants to chilax, relax and its also best place for family to hang out as well - STAYCATION - For me the resort has good facilities. The whole resort is quite integrated and well-equipped with facilities.

author: _kevinfpa
title: As Expected
text: This resort is a no brainer. Super easy with no stress. Stayed here with family 12 days. Everything one would need when traveling with young children. Kids enjoyed the kids club. 2 bedroom apartment very well equipped with good quality and quantity items. Washer and dryer. No dishwasher. Lots of bottled water. Mini golf, bike rentals and pool great source of entertainment. The gym is well equipped. Lots of walking paths. Great internet. Tips: Rent a car Decline the breakfast and use Turtle market for groceries. Use Coffee Club in nearby strip mall. Use the restaurants at the nearby JV Marriott for special occasions. Endure the sales pitch (1 hour) to get your 6,000 Baht cash vouchers. Will definitely stay here again and recommend to family and friends.

author: 276deang
title: Don't be blackmailed into joining!!
text: We accepted a complimentary 3 night stay promotion in return for attending a 90 minute Vacation Club presentation. Due to airline delays that were out of our control, we missed the first night ( we kept the Marriott informed at all stages of the delay). The airline was good and allowed us to rebook the return flight one day later, therefore allowing us to still maintain the 3 night stay. However, the hotel would not allow us the same courtesy, telling us that they were fully booked and we would have to pay the walk in rate to stay the extra night. We challenged this because if they were fully booked, then how could they offer us the same room if we paid?? We had no choice but to pay the extraordinary amount (12,000 thb for 1 night)!! We upheld our end of the bargain and attended the 90 minute presentation, that went for 120 minutes. We told the sales rep about our situation, He and his superior were shocked and said that at the very least we should only be charged a members rate. They said they would sort it out for us. HOWEVER, at the end of the presentation they said we could have the cost refunded ONLY IF we accepted the vacation package!!! The most disappointing factor, apart from the blackmail tactics, is the fact that all throughout the experience, emails were answered promptly until the minute the presentation was over. At the time of writing this review, we have not had ANY contact from the representatives of the hotel. BEWARE of the deceitful tactics this chain will do to secure your custom. On another note, although the beach is nice, the location is very far away from all other parts of Phuket. Taxis are extremely expensive and you have limited option of things to do.

author: effortleslie
title: Just like home with friendly staff and comfy rooms
text: We have chosen Marriott Mai Khao to spend our December vacation over the years. Each time we come away satisfied and refreshed. We're always greeted with warmth by everyone on duty at the Front desk area. There was Chat, Puu, Yean, Tanya and Kate -just to make a few. Then there is the Japanese staff Aya, who has worked many years to look after the guests. The bunch of guys who welcome us are full of smiles. They are on hand to help you with your luggage or take you around in the buggies. It was a wonderful 'I've come home feeling.' To keep the guests fit and health conscious, there's Nadia who organises activities like pilates, Zumba and aqua gym each day. The hotel has a host of programs for the young and adults. The children are well taken care by the Kids Club team. One favourite activity is the pond fishing and fish feeding. Pia, Kitty, Jenny and Popcorn teach us how to make papaya salad, or coconut leaf folding, vegetable carving and others. Staff from the Mandara Spa taught us how to make body scrub. Each day the housekeepers made a different towel folding creation. We were impressed with little notes they left for us too. What a lovely touch! It was truly a wonderful vacation and we were so reluctant to leave the people we've come to call our friends and our comfortable room at Marriott Mai Khao.

author: JennyZeng21
title: A cheap (not necessarily a good) option
text: Haven't been here for 7 years, I came back and mostly negatively surprised by a few factors. First of all, vacation club members staying at this property, unlike the Marriott's Phuket Beach Club right next door, have no access to the main facilities at the hotel, including three pools. So basically as a customer you are stuck here with one pool, a small gym, and some basic facilities. Secondly, while it is a property for family vacations mainly given the size of the rooms, which apparently are all two-bedroom apartments with standard Marriott vacation club layout and designs, the hotel staff apparently are not used to see single travelers, particularly single women travelers. The reaction most of the staff have when they found out that I was traveling alone by myself this time was as if I were abandoned by my family of sort...then why don't they just put on a board saying 'no single allowed' to make everyone's life easier? I would guess it is a lack of international staff here. Can't blame the locals as Thailand remains primitive when it comes privacy and equality. However, shouldn't it be a basic requirement for anyone in hospitality business to be cognitive of the uncomfortness triggered by their comments? Three, the property has no character whatsoever. It can be anywhere in South East Asia, or even outside of Asia. So if you think you come here (WITH YOUR FAMILY PLEASE) for something different, don't bother. It is just another MVC property. Well, always two sides of a coin. Now the positives. One, it is cheap and has abundant availability for last minute decisions as a Marriott Vacation club member. Two, the buggy service to the beach is efficient. Three, the pool in the property is not that bad, with reasonable width and depth for adults, and slides and activities for kids; Four, if you come with a big group of family members with three generations, I guess the service is quite good. I notice that staff here are generally quite attentive to kids and elders within a group. And hence I give it 3-star, otherwise it could have been a two.

author: 137fritzp
title: Peace and tranquility
text: I have been a Marriott vacation club member for several years and have been to Thailand many times but not making use of my points. So I took the opportunity to travel with my Daughter during her September Singapore school holiday. We absolutely love the resort and how it’s kept up to date. The 2 bedroom apartment is spacious and has everything you need. We are very familiar with the resort and enjoyed everything. The staff are very pleasant, nice and always willing to make sure you are enjoying your stay. The manager there Gee was a great and always made sure we were comfortable. Invited us to the members cocktail and my daughter to the kids Golf and other events. One thing to note is that Mai Khao is further up north and about 45min away from Patong. If you want busy, shops and partying.... stay elsewhere. This is where folks wanting to relax, not go anywhere and enjoy the property. There is a little turtlemart shop within walking distance but also suggest that you just order groceries online if you want. The restaurants are great but will always be pricier than the local places. Nonetheless, the food was great and we will definitely be back.

author: 991micheles
title: Anniversary Dream
text: This is our 4th year in a row we have celebrated our Anniversary at the Mai Khao. It was an amazing two weeks here. We brought our daughter and boyfriend this year and they fell in love with Thailand too. The staff here are all the best from the Bell boys, Pool staff, Front end cashiers, restaurant workers at Delights or Zest and best housekeepers ever. Even the managers, Pu, Aya, Gee, K. Coke are the most accommodating you will find. The 2 bedroom rooms are modern and clean. You need to go to the JW Marriott for the beaches and more restaurants, which the Marriott Cafe, Cucina and Kabuki and Siam Deli serve great food. You must try the buffets at Zest and the Marriott Cafe. So good. We enjoyed the Phi Phi Islands, James Bond Island, and Elephant Sanctuary tours. Also a must see, Patong Beach, Central Festival, 2 Night Markets, Phuket town and Jung Ceylon. We love riding the free bikes here and exercising at their gym. They made our Anniversary so special, with flowers champagne and chocolates and decorated our whole room. Thank you for your generous hospitality and great service. You won’t be disappointed if you stay here. Highly recommended.

author: Plumer3
title: Phuket Heaven
text: Where do I begin? I have now stayed at each of the three (3) Marriott properties in Phuket and every single time it’s been an amazing experience. The exceptional Customer Service began as soon as I contacted the hotel to confirm my reservation. The staff promptly answered my questions and worked extremely hard to provide my requests. This was our first “family vacation” so I wanted to make sure that it was an exceptional experience. If you’ve stayed at any of the other Marriott properties in Phuket, you’ll find the floor plan familiar. I reserved the two-bedroom unit. Each bedroom had its own bathroom. The kitchen is more than adequate and allowed us to make breakfast each morning. The living room and bedrooms each have a tv. The property is about 10 minutes from the Andaman Sea and a beautiful beach. There is a beautiful swimming pool with early and late hours if you’re looking for privacy. A grocery store is available at a small strip mall called Turtle Village. Prices are high, but the option is a 30-minute taxi ride to a grocery store. There are two restaurants on this property. One of them would more likely be called a café in the U.S. All in all it was a fantastic vacation. I would highly recommend this hotel to any of my friends and colleagues.

author: ChesterClaret
title: Loved it!
text: My wife and I stayed for two weeks at this resort in a two bedroom apartment with two friends. The location is about five minutes walk from Mai Khao beach. The resort does have some renovations ongoing at present but this couldn't detract from the superb levels of comfort and service on offer. The staff are just lovely and nothing is too much trouble and the rooms are spotlessly clean and extremely well equipped and comfortable. If you want a relaxing holiday in a tropical location look no further than this resort. The towel displays are lovely. (See photos) There are two restaurants on site both offering tasty, freshly cooked food at reasonable prices. There is also a poolside bar which is convenient but prices were on the high side. It's better to wander down the beach and find a "Bushbar" offering great sunset views across the Andaman Sea and far cheaper prices. There is no convenience store on site but right next door to the resort is the "Turtle Village" which has a small supermarket. Be warned prices are high and better value can be found at the "Tesco Lotus" north of "Sarasin Bridge." I hired a car for a week via the hotel staff and it was well worth it as it gives you the ability to shop elsewhere, eat at different restaurants and see a bit more of Thailand. I found driving reasonably easy as long as you take it slow and keep clear of Patong! Motorcycles are your biggest problem. Complimentary cycles are available on-site and there is a small lake nearby with a paved track around the perimeter which is a nice leisurely cycle route. The JW Marriott is a short walk from this resort and offers a great selection of upmarket restaurants. Prices are on the high side but you get what you pay for as the food is very good.

author: 7shasha7
title: Impeccable service, awesome private beach
text: We came here during the CNY period. Upon entering the resort, we noticed that there were some construction going on. It’s great if they are expanding. The place itself is not huge. There’s a small kid’s pool for very young children and an adult pool area. There is a kids’ playroom area, a small courtyard for ball games and a small lounge area with one pool table and seating places. Truth be told, we were not wowed by the facilities. However, the service, the room and the easy access to the beach itself made up for the lack of awesome facilities. The staff was always smiling and friendly and can answer queries well. The room was amazing with a small kitchenette which they gave brand new scouring sponge, dishwashing liquid, full cutlery, crockery etc. The best part was the washing machine AND dryer. This is awesome when going to an island with a family! The walking distance to the beach was a big plus. The beach was really beautiful and you can catch a full on sunset! Magnificent Mai Khao beach! The location of the place itself is not a big draw because even to get out to a restaurant nearby cost us 1700 THB for the six of us. But if you are just a family intending to chill at the club with an additional trip out to Phi Phi islands tour (which is a MUST) without going anywhere else in Phuket, then this is a definite family friendly place. Ps:/: we saw lots of other developments under construction so soon there’ll be more entertainment and dining options!

author: effortleslie
title: A place you’ll call home
text: If you’re looking for a resort to relax in, Marriot’s Mai Khao Beach in Phuket offers you that much needed break from the busyness of life. From the moment you arrive, you’ll be greeted with smiles. From the front desk to our room, Peach and Joe made us feel warm and welcomed. I, along with many guests I’ve spoken to, have stayed here several times over the years. Every single staff is so friendly, it’s as if you’ve come home. It helped that we spent the New Year there and saw the fireworks on the beach. You’ll never be bored with the range of indoor and outdoor programs most of which are free. I must commend the staff in the daily children’s programs. Ticktock and her cheerful team include Bling, Kitty, Popcorn, Nicha,Jenny, Pia and Deer. They work tirelessly to make the kids want to come back to the activities. There are fun things like marshmallow roasting, cupcake decorating and balloon art making. The kids loved the fishing by the pond- catch and release. All the parents have only praise for this group of young ladies. The adults can choose to attend classes like animal towel folding, Thai lessons and how to make body scrub. My favourite activity is the aqua gym workout with Nadia who is so passionate in getting everyone to get active in the pool. The spacious villas are so comfortable with a well equipped kitchen. The housekeeping staff give the extra touch by folding towels animals for each villa. I highly recommend the Marriot’s Mai Khao Beach.

author: peterbrewmaker
title: Vacation stay at the Marriot Mai Khao beach
text: First of, the positive. The two bedroom suite was excellent and my family of four enjoyed the stay as far as this part of the facility is concerned. The second was the friendly wait staff who try their best (but largely fail due to reasons below) to convey a sense of local Thai hospitality and ambiance. Beyond that, this was a disappointment for various reasons. The Marriot rep immediately went into an upselling mode as soon as we arrived after a long flight. She wanted us to attend a 90 min presentation for a 10% discount. (Please at least give us some time to settle down). If you did not know better you would easily mistake the facility being located somewhere in the US. Most of the people you see are people from North America with kids. (I have two so no bias against kids. Love them) A few from UK perhaps. The food is very expensive (western pricing) because Marriot takes advantage to the hilt of the facility being located far from other places to eat. The quality of the food itself leaves much to desire. Over all there was a lot of nickle and diming. After paying $450/night, I expect more class. In contrast when I attended another event there people from all over the globe (Father-daughter from Norway, a couple of Germany, another from SoCal) but at Marriot it is just the same kind of people. Families can get the same resort experience without leaving the US.

author: gramazingtravels
title: Average & Poorly Maintained for a 5 Star Hotel
text: This was a group couples trip with a total of 8 of us living in two villas! Upon arrival, this place seemed grand, luxurious and wonderful - however the moment we entered the room we were swamped with tons of mosquitoes inside. Note: there is a huge pond at the back of the hotel and I think this attracts a lot of bugs and breeds a lot of mosquitoes. The room was good, clean and spacious. Bed was very comfortable as well. We had room service - ordered tons of food but only the Phad Thai was passable and nice. Our private pool was disastrous however. Tons of dead bugs, insects, mosquitoes and even a dead frog (photo as attached) was found!! I don’t think they bother cleaning up the pool at all, because it was just so dirty and full of weird things at the bottom. Tried to inform the hotel staff but they just smiled and said okay but never bothered to attend to it. Maybe there was some language barrier, but clearly a problem if they don’t even bother occasionally checking on the pool themselves. Service was overall average. Also, I think this place is only good if you just need a complete respite from the city and mainland. Otherwise it is very costly to get out to go to more happening places like Phuket Town or night markets. Water sports is also not available here, seemingly. Beach has a nice sunset though.

author: AmandaR5726
title: We had a brilliant family holiday
text: My husband and I had a great 3 night stay here with our two children (aged 5 and 3 years old). It's really well set up for all the family to have a good time - our kids loved playing in the kids pool and splash area and we were able to sit nearby and watch them. They also enjoyed the kids club and we utilised the babysitting service so that we could leave our youngest there too for a couple of hours (minimum age to be left unsupervised is 4 years old). We also took bikes out one morning and had a lovely cycle along the road stopping off at the JW Marriott for a drink on the way back. Although you can't use the pools and kids club at the JW Marriott, you can access the restaurants and bars there and the spa. I would highly recommend the spa, it's expensive compared to what is available outside of the hotel, but it's a beautifully designed space and I really enjoyed my whole experience there. Breakfast was good - it's a relatively small hotel compared to some resorts so don't expect an enormous spread but we found it perfectly adequate and the coffee was good. We ate lunch at Delights and were very impressed with the food choice and quality there. We ate at the Andaman Grill at the JW one evening and had the most delicious steak. We ate in Zest another night from the special Thai menu - the food again was great. We had one of the ground floor apartments with a pool and there was more than enough space for all of us, it was huge. It was nice to be able to sit on loungers by our own pool whilst the kids were napping in the room. Also the direct access from the gate of our terrace to the pool area and restaurants was really convenient. The room was very clean and well-equipped and we always had plenty of towels etc. My only complaint would be that it smelt very strongly of damp and you could even feel the damp when sitting on the sofa. Also all of our clothes smelt when I was unpacking our cases when we got home. I guess it was because the room was a little dark as it was on the ground floor and it has been rainy season. Perhaps it wouldn't be so bad in dry/high season. Overall though it didn't adversely affect what was otherwise a great experience for the whole family.

author: Caro371
title: Awful customer service, worst hotel I have ever been to, bar none.
text: Without a doubt, the worst hotel I have ever stayed in. Upon arrival, there were no rooms available as they had over-booked, and were moving guests to another hotel nearby. I was with my 4 month old baby, and they had no rooms for us, so suggested we sleep on the sun lounger outside by the pool. That's right, a newborn baby should sleep on the sunlounger. After an hour of arguing with a manager, we relented and had no choice but to stay outside until the morning. About 10am, we were finally given a room. A casual 6 hours after arriving. No apology. No awareness for all the mosquitos outside. For the most part, the staff are very friendly and nice, but none have any responsibility and keep saying to call Head Office....which is in America. So while the office staff in the States are safely tucked up in their beds cosy and safe, they leave guests and their newborns to stay outside. They did suggest that we book another hotel nearby, and even offered us free wifi so that we could google somewhere to stay. But we had to sort our own transport. Obviously. Because offering a half decent service would be too much for them. I'll never stay in a JW Marriott again, and will be telling everyone to avoid this hotel like the plague.

author: edh804
title: Great family holiday
text: Great for our family of three adults and a two year old. We were able to relax and had everything we needed. If you're looking to save a little money: -There are two "local" restaurants, JJ's and Singh's, just near the tennis courts, both with decent mains for 150THB. You can walk to these -There is another restaurant Kin Dee which is not walking distance, although they may offer shuttle of sort. -There is an on-site mall (Turtle Mart) where prices are 30-50% inflated vs normal Thai prices. Good for the odd item -Tesco Lotus delivers to the resort. The resort staff helped us liaise with Tesco for the delivery. Good for the essentials. We did a big shop at the start of the week. -The closest quik-e-mart type place for booze that isn't marked up 2-3 times is JPs on the main road. -Consider hiring a car. -Massages can be had on the beach accessible via the shuttle. There are four stops, and the stops at the JW Marriott and Ginja restaurant \Phuket beach club are the "beach" stops. Just walk through the resorts. A massage on the beach is 500THB\hr which is expensive by Thai standards, but well worth it in my opinion. The experience of the sea breeze coming through the Salas whilst getting a very good massage was a trip highlight. The resort itself Pros -There are a myriad of activities, mainly aimed at kids, and good standard. -The in room Wi-Fi is exceptional. -The rooms are spacious and well maintained - The kitchen is handy (no proper oven but the microwave has an oven mode) -The bathroom in the master suite is pretty impressive Cons (more accurately just things that weren't perfect) -The air conditioning is a little on the loud side (remember they're big rooms) -The room service food was good but not amazing -TVs only carried analogue Overall a really fantastic stay. We will definitely come again.

author: JoeT2000
title: Amazing Property and friendly Service
text: This is one of the best resorts I have stayed in. During check-in, after our arrival from Phuket international airport, we were offered a free drink before being taken by a golf cart with our luggage to our spacious and immaculately clean room. The appartment was huge and included a balcony, a small kitchen having all the utensils and appliances to cook a full meal or b/f. The apparment consisted of two en suite bed rooms, a large sitting room cum dining room. The master bedroom had an enormous king size bed, with a huge bathroom with a great shower, separate toilet and oversized bath. We were there for 7 nights. The property has an outstanding with a range of activities - including classes - yoga, Pilates and ab workouts. The gym also has a sauna, huge locker room and very good quality bicycles for rent. This area can be used for changing, chill out, etc in case your departure flights are in the evening. Our property also had a washing machine with a dryer, in case ... The property is just immense with lush gardens, a path in front of the beach and a few pools to select from. The gardens are just amazinh throughout the property. There are a range of of restaurants in the resort, pricey for Thailand, however food and service was near to perfect. Only negatives that we faced was the fact that the property is far out from other local areas to get local massages, real cheap local food and small shops around. There are a couple of super markets nearby, however prices reflected are not those of other places in Phuket such as Patong beach. The service provided throughout our stay was faultless. Since we wanted to chill out, our stay was just about perfect for relaxation. The staff were always smiling and greeting the customers and the service be it at the bar or the restaurants, or buggy rides were perfect. We had a wonderful 8 day experience.

author: mujergato
title: Great vacation, looking forward to returning!!
text: We had a fantastic family vacation. The food, the staff, the accommodations, just wonderful. We enjoyed being up North as we avoided the "adult entertainment " that's predominately down South. Look forward to coming back!!! Must stay for families that have friends who have kids but want to vacation together. PROS - Great 2bdrm villa with plenty of room. Nicely furnished, cleaning staff was great. - Concierge was beyond fantastic. Oy arranged life changing tours, so glad we didnt book online, her feedback was invaluable - Kids pool. Tip, bring your own music and inflatables. They have an air pump. Happy hr 1630-1730 is pretty laid back and not crowded, bonus! - The adult pool was also not crowded and relaxing, you can hear the waves crashing - Marriott cafe offered such a variety, also packed. Tip, eat breakfast at Cucina, a little cheaper and not crowded - Staff at kids club, they offer babysitting service since under 4 needs a parent to stay with (200 bht) an hr - Buggy service to rooms and shops - We are up North, definitely quiet and relaxing, not crowded and bch to yourself - Kabuki Japanese restaurant was a splurge, kid enjoyed the show and Japanese beef worth it - Not far from airport (apprx 20 min) use metered taxi, with 100 baht airport fee it was 400 baht total CONS - You are going to pay resort prices pretty much at every restaurant except Siam Deli which is expected but at Cucina, service needs work, lots of work - You are going to pay Four Season prices at spa but right by adult pool is a make shift spa that offer 500 baht massages vs 3400 baht. Its pretty criminal what they charge especially for being in Thailand. Probably the most disappointing thing was the cost of spa services. 1700 baht for a pedicure, not when I can walk down street and get it for 650 baht - Most activities are down south so transportation is going to cost you. The travel time to marina was an hr, makes for a long day with little kids. Tip, you can use uber here

author: Z8555UVruthm
title: Faultless Marriott Mai Khao Beach
text: Got home today from a wonderful three nights at the Marriott Mai Khao Beach. The staff were outstanding - every one of them. Nothing was too much trouble. We have two kids - five and seven. They loved kids club (mostly free) and begged to be there from first thing in the morning until last thing at night. The kids also loved the golf garden - a free, really fun nine hole mini-golf. Tips: JJs for authentic, rustic roadside Thai. Go passed the kids court, guest car park, weave your way passed the massive laundry buildings, passed the security guard and across the road - about five minutes walk. Smile sweetly and one of the staff may just drive you there in a buggy. :) We had green chicken curry, spring rolls, fried rice, several beers and another curry for less than 1000baht. Swimming pool - ideal options for toddlers and competent swimmers. Powerful jets go from 9am to 7pm in the main pool. Kids and adults lacking in confidence might not enjoy it much (in fact there were women wearing giant floaties). Thai sun - we were warned in advance and found that we were much quicker to burn than in other parts of the world. We'll be back - I doubt anyone could do it better.

author: nissan11
title: Lovely room and great family place
text: We were two couple traveling with infants. We were booked in a 2 bedroom apartment which was excellent. It had a large master bedroom with a super sized bath tub twin basin and a balcony. The apartment had a fully equipped kitchen and washer dryer. The apartment was clean each day so it was with full service The hotel was very nice with a large pool and a nice kiddie pool and enough loungers and cabanas It had a kids club with activities for infants to older kids. They offer free cycles (very nice cycles) The beach was a short buggy ride away. Just outside the property there was also a large convenience store and few shops. The beach was lovely with clear water and clean sand. The hotel has a small shack outside the beach and offers free kayaks, surfboards, loungers and ice water Cons: While you are allowed to go to the adjoining Mariott resorts for meals you can't use their pools There isn't much in the area for food options other than the 3 large resorts and couple of sea food joints. Cabs are prohibitively expensive to go anywhere. JW had the best restaurants, we are most meals there and few outside This is a 5 star resort so be prepared to pay prices for the services and being in a remote area you should make the most of the hotel and its facilities rather than trying to venture out much. Tips: some tips to save There is another convenience store in mai khao plaza next door which is slightly cheaper than the one attached to the hotel There is a fruit vendor who is much cheaper than the stores There are couple of restaurants Singhs kitchen and JJ Bar which have decent food at a reasonable price. There is also a food court about 10min walk on the main highway attached to the gas station There is a good massage joint on the beach which is much cheaper than the hotel (still more pricey than elsewhere). They also had an in room package which was slightly more but totally worth it. The room massage felt no less than a spa at much cheaper prices.

author: dis-spirited
title: Don't get trapped in the middle of nowhere!
text: Our family of 4 recently booked into this resort as part of a trip of a lifetime but were so disappointed upon arrival. It is in the middle of nowhere - an $80 round trip taxi ride to anything you want to see or do in the Phuket area. You are basically trapped there. It is not on or near the beach. You have to take a golf cart or walk to the front of the other Marriott, where you can sit on their beach, but NOT use any of their pool or beach chairs. You CAN of course use their restaurants, but expect to pay LA or New York prices. Yes, in Thailand! You might be thinking - well we will just use our kitchen and cook a bit. The only grocery store is owned by them and again, prices double and triple what you would pay at home. You are basically held hostage there. There are so many choices in Thailand and in the Phuket area. Keep looking and don't bother with Marriott Mai Khao. Not worth the huge sums of money! (IF you have already booked and can't get out of it, go online and order your groceries from Tesco Lotus and have them delivered. Great service and cheap!)

author: tusharanand1
title: PHUKET 2017
text: Our family of 7 had an enjoyable 5N/4D in this resort hotel. Stayed in a 2 bedroom villa Loads of activities for kids. the hotel is surrounded by J.W .MARRIOTT and once more hotel . well the resort is equipped with everything in the room and also the hotel is very clean . it has daily room cleaning service which is not possible in other villa hotels . the water bottle are complimentary. i noticed one thing which is very interesting, the room kitchen is equipped with every small thing needed to cook and u will also find washing machine and dryer for your daily use. the restaurants is also good but i didn't liked the preparation of food as i visited J.W hotel next to this which is far more better in taste . i visited the coffee shop in both the properties. The rooms are updated with all the essentials . the bathroom and toilets are also very clean and soap , shampoo, shower gel are of very good quality. The nearest super market is Turtle Village mart but its over priced which they should they have to look and should reduce bec on the main road there is a shell patrol pump and u can find 24 hr mart with prices which are acceptable and after that there is 7eleven store , all these store are easily accessible by cycle which u can get from Marriott. u get buggy service every 5-10 min if u need to go to other marriott resort which is free. u should try food of J.W coffee shop. the swimming pool of this resort is far more cleaner than J.W as in J.W people come directly from beach and enter the pool which makes it dirty. the night swim in Marriott is very good. as the water is not cool. overall the villa is very good for the people who loves making food and want to party and relax . The beach is beautiful & quietened very clean (not heavily populated like Patong) its very near to airport and there is complimentary pick-up and drop from hotel. the staff is very friendly and very supportive round the clock thanks tushar

author: sgktraveller
title: Great Vacation home for family
text: Booked a 2 bed room apartment for my family vacation. Rooms were clean and spacious. Only set back is the main bedroom does have a musky smell, the front desk responded immediate for the housekeeping to attend to us and they place a burner with scent oil to improve the situation. This was definately appreciated though it did not and will not solve the root of the problem as musking the smell is not a long term solution. I suggest the resort seek n professional to work on the airflow, humidity and air quality inorder to resolve the issue as I believe that other rooms will have the same issue as well. Other then the issue of the smell in the room, rest were all well. Service staff is friendly and you never fail to see a smile on their faces. Apartment comes with a fully equip kitchenette where you can prepare your own breakfast and simple meals. There is a grocery store just mins walk away so it make it even more convenient. However, items at the store is much pricier then those you find in town. The main pool is nice with plenty of deck chair. Children pool, play area, table tennis, game room, snooker room are all available. Food at the restaurant is not too bad, otherwise there are restaurant mins walk awayas well at the turtle village. All in all, a nice property especially for family. I do not recommend this resort for couples or honey mooners. If not for the smell, I would given it a 5 star rating.

author: DavidC7873
title: Great place for kids! Wonderful service
text: We had a great time with our kids (6 & 2) at the resort. The kids club had lots of great activities throughout the day like fishing, balloon twisting and mocktail mixing as well as some fun craft activities (only ones with additional cost). The staff at kids club were wonderful, and the kids had a great time with them. Bling was especially great with our 6 year old and encouraged them to have lots of fun with the activities and each other. Popcorn, Litta and Kitty were friendly and fun too! Always ready to help the kids with various activities! Go was also great and had a mini impromptu climbing contest at their small climbing wall that my Son loved. Our 2 yo loved the many pretend wooden toys like the dollhouse and cooking set and cars! He also loved feeding then fish! The kids also loved the pool and the small kids sprinklers and slide were a great hit with both of them! Service was wonderful throughout the stay and Karn at the deli/restaurant was great and went out of her way to fulfil special food requests. She was also great with the kids. Tony at the front desk was extremely helpful and helped arrange our car rental, liaising with the company to fulfil our special request of returning car at the another resort! He was also very patient with our many requests and helpful with food recommendations! Overall a great place for kids with lots of activities and great service!

author: JaniceFifi
title: Very good stay!
text: We had a 2 bedroom villa, villa was very spacious and comfortable. It has a small kitchen with everything you need, utensils, crockeries, pots and pans. Very well maintained property. There is washing machine and dryer in the room, they even provided detergent powder. Services provided by the hotel was excellent, everything is top notch. Nothing to complain about. Since it was a rainy season when we went, hotel actually has quite a lot of activities for us to participate, we enjoyed the yoga, pilates and aqua gym very much! Champ was a good instructor! He took care of everyone, not forgetting first timer like us whom may have limited flexibility. We love attending his class! Hotel offers shuttle service to JW Marriott. Food served was great! The air cond unit in the living room tend to be a little noisy. Convenience store is available just next door, but things are a little pricey. Overall, it was a good stay!

author: highimpactuk
title: Great family resort
text: The resort is located about 20 minutes from the airport and for those acquainted with the Marriott resort brand, you will not be disappointed. The apartments are well kitted out and have all the home-from-home things you would expect such as laundry facilities, good size kitchen, large-screen TV's, DVD player, etc. There is no dishwasher though. This hardly mattered as all the dishes left in the sink are taken care of by housekeeping daily. Every unit had a balcony and some of the ground floor units had their own dipping pools. There is a supermarket near the resort (in the shopping complex) which is useful for the odd item. We found it easy to use the Tesco Lotus delivery service and had our shopping delivered directly to our unit - twice. Delivery is free and we spent less than £30 on each occasion - at a fraction of the rates near the resort. For those interested in making suits/formal dresses, there is a good tailor at the Turtle shopping complex (A Prime) which is handy as I had 2 fittings there before collection. It was simply a case of walking across. Even if you could get it cheaper elsewhere, you need to factor in the convenience of getting fitted locally into the overall price - which in any case, compared favourable to the rest of Phuket. Do not waste your time buying water on the first day (guilty!) as you will be provided with 8 litres of bottled water by the resort everyday. Our 9 year-old used the kids club a few times and enjoyed himself. Other things you'd like here include the gym (good size and plenty of kit) and the swimming pool area - where we enjoyed a few games of water polo late into the evening with other guests. There is a shuttle to the other Marriott resorts nearby - which we took advantage of - to use restaurants/beach. Also worth noting that between noon and 4pm everyday, on the main road by the Turtle complex, there are hawkers doing food including BBQ chicken - from as little as 40 bahts. The one gripe I had was the occasional waft of sewage - which seemed to occur most evenings. It was mentioned that some works were taking place. Management need to look into it as this smell (although it did not spoil our experience) is not what one would expect in a 5-star resort.

author: YongBin
title: Great family resort!
text: Well thought out and well run resort. The 2 bedroom apartments were spacious and well appointed, with all the amenities you would need for a comfortable stay. Loved the self-sufficient kitchen (minus groceries), washer and dryer with a free packet of detergent, and the ample supply of towels. That being said, the living room could do with a fan and the carpet (in our room- 4333) with some cleaning as there was a mild odour. The resort itself isn't very big, but had a lot of activities for the kids and teenagers/adults. There was also a regular shuttle service to the bigger JW Marriot and the beach. Turtle village, with its supermarket and limited shops + restaurants is just a stone's throw away. The kids club was fantastic, had great service staff and fun activities. My favourite was fishing with the kids at the pond with a simple rod and hook. The gym was a big draw as well, spacious and well equipped for all sorts of workouts. The food options at the resort were limited but the quality was quite good. Breakfast had a decent variety but the cheeses were my favourite. Would have been nice if they had some fresh juices. Overall my family of 4 had an enjoyable stay at the resort and would visit again! What we liked about the resort: 1) Kids club 2) Gym 3) Service 4) Large, self sufficient 2BR apartments What we didn't like so much 1) No access to beach 2) Mosquitos

author: aussie_fireblade
title: Great place to wind down and relax
text: Great place to wind down and have a bit of relaxation. All apartments are two bedrooms and two baths. Master bedroom on the ground floor can lead straight into the private pool. It also has a huge bath. Other room is in the front and you would need to keep the blackout curtains closed for privacy. All rooms come with a flatscreen TV and dvd player to keep you entertained. Comes with a small kitchen and fridge. Drinking water is provided everyday. Free wifi throughout the whole resort, which is very strong no matter where you are. The main pool is relatively large, with plenty of space for everyone. Many lounge chairs available. There is a poolside bar (not exactly a pool bar). Different treats are provided daily at set times (example fruits at 3pm, water at 11am, cool towels at 1pm etc). Kids club has many activities. There is also an outdoor theatre that they run on Tuesdays and Thursdays (I think). Overall, this is a great place. Will definitely recommend to anyone who wants to be away from the crowd of Patpong and the mad traffic of Phuket town. Be aware that you are pretty isolated and getting into town can cost quite a lot.

author: Raj_Tee
title: Top notch Vacation Club experience
text: Overall an excellent resort run to very high standards throughout. In Summary: 5/5 modern apartment which is light and airy. Request a high floor for great tree top views. 5/5 Bathroom and well equipped Kitchen. 5/5 spacious and covered balcony which is ideal for relaxing during the rains or in the evenings. 4/5 Pool. Great but is mainly for kids. 4/5 gym which is well equipped but no sauna. For excellent local food, I'd recommend eating at JJs which is a 2 min walk from the resort (outside rear service entrance). Even better was ordering a takeaway from JJ and dining al fresco on the balcony - perfect ! 'May' on the front desk was excellent along with all the staff in the resort. No aggressive Sales tactics from any Marriott staff. But... watch out for the Sales Reps from the next door Anantara resort - they are certainly persistent. For Vacation Club owners, Darren and Olivier (Guest Relations) assisted us during our stay and were excellent throughout. For owners, I recommend you seek and touch base with these guys at the owners drinks night. Only real downside is the property is not directly on the beach front and requires a 2 min walk which means you have to navigate past the Anantara Sales reps on the way.

author: luxk69
title: Excellent, perfect for families
text: Convenient location next to Turtle Village with small super market and some air conditioned eateries if you don't want to go to local beach/street restaurants but don't want to renounce on air condition, as Hotel restaurants are always more expensive. But you can also use all the restaurants in the 3 Marriott hotels and put it on your room charge. The resort has much improved since my last time there, 6 yrs ago. There is a lot of entertainment all day long, from morning yoga, zumba, water aerobic, muay tai classes. In the evening 2 x live band by the pool, fire show, kids' movie by the pool. The staff from the gym/pool were so friendly and greeted me by name every time I met them. I felt the attention was much more personal and intimate compared to the Phuket Beach Club as it is much bigger. We were there end of February and always had plenty of available beds and not crowded at all. The only critique I would have, are that the sunbeds could use lounge cushions like the Phuket Beach Club next door, that would make the beds much more comfortable. Guests would not want to leave the resort as I had the impression that people returned to the resort late afternoon. The resort has a convenient buggy bringing you to the beach and back on demand even though the distance can also be done by walking, which we did. A free shuttle coming every 10/15 min drives to the adjacent Turtle Village-JW Marriott-End of Phuket Beach Club, very convenient if it's too hot or raining. But we chose to walk as it is a good exercise after lunch. The 4 stars only instead of 5 because it is not as luxurious as the Phuket Beach Club as that one is integrated into the JW Marriott. Would and have recommended to my friends/family, we had a really relaxing vacation.

author: Kaalo
title: Relaxing resort
text: Rarely do we stay in a 5 star resort, let alone a two bedroom villa. Yet an opportunity arose so we seized it. We were expecting not to enjoy it that much. Usually large resorts mean overinflated prices, indifferent staff and the resort not being what is made out to be. We were wrong on this occasion. The staff were friendly, efficient and welcoming. Each and every person would greet you with a smiling face and a quick chat. Particular note should be made of "Champ" who conducted the yoga and other fitness classes. Always smiling and made sure we had a great time. The meals were not at exorbitant prices. Obviously a little more than you may get normally, but the quality was exceptional. And a variety of choices. Not a lot outside of the resort however except for one beachside "hut" restaurant which did serve great food at bargain prices. Unfortunately we were there only guests. There is a small supermarket on the lower level of the Turtle shopping centre which is central to the resorts in the area. A great place to stock up on any essentials. (Such as cheap beer!) The rooms were incredibly spacious, clean and well thought out. So overall, a five star review in all aspects for the 5 star resort.

author: MTQTT
title: We Keep On Coming Back!
text: There are reasons why we came for the 3rd time even if there are a lot of choices around. We felt the great hospitality the moment we arrived. I must say that Marriott's Mai Khao Beach staff are fantastically warm and they're the friendliest. Even the Management Team was extremely helpful and polite. The apartment we had was crazy massive, very clean, complete kitchen equipment and there's nothing more you could ask for! We always appreciate that they welcome us with a bottle of champagne, goodies, sweets, etc. Really thoughtful! Our plunge pool was of the right size :) anyway, they have a huge pool which we really enjoyed too. The beach is a 15 minute walk. It is huge, fantastic and quite uncrowded but we haven't enjoyed it as it was always on red flag whenever we visit. You can get a buggy to take you there. We love the food in all their restaurants! Wide and good selection with a very reasonable price to think you're inside a 5-star resort. You may also cook by yourself as there's a small supermarket in the Turtle Village. You'll never get bored inside this resort as there are several activities for adults and children too! Highly recommended! We'll definitely return :)

author: cheekyvic
title: Amazing, relaxing family holiday
text: I recently stayed here with my husband, almost 2 yr old son and my parents. The resort is beautiful and the staff are so friendly and helpful. They have pretty much thought of everything and ideal for children of all ages. There are plenty of activities to keep everyone entertained with a fantastic kids club. The kids pool with the slide was a hit with kids and adults alike. There is a shuttle that takes you between the other marriott resorts in the area. The blue bar is a must for a drink at sunset! There is also a buggie that takes you the short 5 minute walk to the beach another definite must. We went most mornings when there was more shade on the beach. The room was fantastic with all you could want and a good size. Daily housekeeping was great and all you drinking water was provided (andyou can order more as you need it). The food was great at all the restaurants we ate at (only tip would be if ordering around the pool order early as the food took a little while to arrive). A couple of special mentions Nadia who does the fitness side of things is awesome and would recommend the bike ride as a nice way to get out and see the surrounding area. Joelle was also super helpful and friendly and very kind to us and our son. Pia who was around the pool while we were there was just beautiful with our son and made a real impression. A definite asset to the team. Overall fantastic holiday for all.

author: 97s_lr_ns
title: ABSOLUTELY FANTASTIC!
text: What a fantastic resort. Marriott has done it again! We stayed at Marriott‘s Mai Khao Beach for 10 days over the Christmas holidays – family with two seven years old. Our first time in Thailand and our first time at this resort,. When we arrived we were greeted with very friendly staff and the word "Samanika“ or welcome/hello was the word you heard all the time. We stayed in a 2 bedroom apartment and it had all the equipment you would need – and the space – ahhh that was nice! They provided us with drinking water every day and everything was so clean and well kept all around the resort. The pool was an endless source of play for children and adults as well and I have to mention the Aqua Team at the Pool bar. They were fantastic and knew exactly all your needs – even before you thought of it :). Thank you Tiger, Ton, Black, Pla, Gung and Bao. And a special thanks to Nadia who made sure we had a workout in the pool and Funny who provided us with cold water and towels! The only downer (not a bad one though) is that the resort is not located near any "downtown“ area but there were plenty of restaurants in the resort and the resorts nearby – JW Marriott and Anantara Spa. The local restaurants I would like to mention nearby are Kin Dee and Mai Khao Seafood – fantastic food! We did not rent a car but there was very good service with taxis and shuttles if you wanted to go anywhere. The beach is nearby – only 10 mins walk or with a buggy from the hotel. Absolutely loved this resort and thank you for making our holiday a memorable one!

author: bew11000
title: Luxury
text: We had a two bedroom apartment which had everything you needed, except the food. The quality of furnishings and kitchen equipment was excellent. It included a washing machine and dryer and even the washing powder. In the kitchen everything you would need to self cater was there: fridge freezer, microwave with grill, hob, toaster, coffee machine and kettle, pots and pans various plates glasses etc. I even discovered a liquidiser and plastic containers if you wanted to pack a picnic. The resort also provided dishwashing liquid etc. On arrival we were given ice cool towels to freshen up with and a refreshing drink whilst we booked in. The reception staff were lovely and very accommodating. The place was immaculate. The resort provided plenty of activities throughout the day, and you can get a buggy to the JW Marriot to enjoy the restaurants there plus the beach facilities on offer, such as kayaking. During your visit to the pool you may be lucky and get free drinks and fruit if you time it right. The resort has links to the the shops in the Turtle Village (which is in front of the resort), where there is a mini mart, pub, cooking school and other restaurants and gift shops. There is also a tourist travel agents for booking local trips, often with extra discounts. We found all the staff friendly and helpful. The resort is situated north of the airport, around 20 minutes away. The main tourist areas are about an hour's taxi drive away, but to be honest, the hotel, pool and beach offer much more than the crowded touristy areas do unless you want a hectic night life, in which case go to Petong beach instead.

author: tony12cu
title: Luxury Living with Attention to Detail
text: Marriott lives up to its motto of "Service and Quality". Hotel: The hotel is a short ride away from the airport and situated along the Mai Khao beach (11km of it). The location is secluded from the public. It forms one of the 3 properties that Marriott is operating in the same area, offering guests plenty of premises to visit during the stay. Room: The apartments are designed for long stays, complete with dryer/washing machine as well as all the kitchen utensils and cutlery that any family will need. All quality stuff. Several types of rooms are available including rooms with private pools. Facilities: The main swimming pools is surrounded by great landscaping. It offers a myriad of activities, all complimentary. It also offers a great child center that will take care of your kids while you enjoy some private time. Service: Staff is very friendly and helpful. One of the most memorable gesture that is hugely appreciated is their offer for shower, even after we have checked out (as we have a late flight out of Phuket). Thank you Marriott. Meals: The buffet breakfast offers a decent spread with good quality food, although not the big one. The waiting staff is great. If there is any fault to pick, it is something that the hotel cannot change, being too close to the high power tension cables/pylons.

author: yuryd571
title: 2** facilities hotel with 4**** service
text: Just returned from vocations from Marriott's Mai Khao Beach - Phuket. Stayed in a 2 Bedrooms Suite with private swimming pool. 1. Beds: master bedroom mattress was in a terrible condition - we felt like we slept in an L-shape chair. On both sides of the mattress. 2. Aircon: aircon can't constantly maintain temperature - it's either ON, or OFF.
