We put on the aircon on +24C and woke up together with the baby every 1.5 hrs as it was either very hot in the room, or it was very cold in the room. 3. Private swimming pool: upon arrival it was a 40cm hair circle floating in a swimming pool. The floor was with stones and sand. Called maintenance to clean it. Hats off - they arrived fast. After they cleaned and left - still hair was floating in the pool... Decided not to swim at all. Otherwise the service is 4**** as advertised. I would NOT recommend it as a family hotel, there are plenty of good hotels at the same price range on Phuket.

author: Stenvoid
title: Beautiful property, good facilities, impressive
text: We visited here for a week's holiday as part of a BA Holidays package. We were very impressed. We had a two bedroom ground floor apartment with plunge pool and it was huge. The furnishing quality and style was excellent, the plunge pool and private garden/courtyard lovely. The kitchen was really well stocked and dining area was pleasant. All in all an excellent room with some lovely touches - e.g. his and hers giant bathroom of the main bedroom. The cleaning staff would always leave a selection of folded towel animals for the children as well - which made them very excited on returning from the main pool each day. On that subject the main pool was huge, tastefully appointed and along with the children's water play area, was genuinely fantastic. There was a range of seating including daybeds/cabanas and the pool bar was also conveniently placed. We loved the pool. We used the Kids Club a number of times, but felt this was perhaps the area where the hotel let itself down. There is little point having a timetable of great pasttimes if you then never actually stick to it - in a tropical destination blaming the rain in monsoon season is silly, but also even the indoor activities weren't always stuck to, and when we asked to pay a small amount extra for the children to make fans we received completely blank stares as if this request was from an alien. In short we got the impression the childcare facility was more of a "love them and leave them" offering where children ended up playing video games, and that wasn't what we wanted. That said, the holiday was fantastic and the accommodation lovely. The grounds are very well kept and make for an interesting walk. This isn't a beach-front property, and that should be borne in mind. However, there is a buggy transfer to the beach which doesn't take long and it is also a lovely stroll. Overall highly recommended.

author: bboymsia
title: Nice accommodation for families, but there might be safer beaches elsewhere
text: lovely accommodation, shame about the location. Located near Phuket Airport, by Mai Khao beach, this is a apartment hotel catering to families. The two bedroom apartment that we stayed at was very spacious, well equipped, clean and everything worked. There were three flat TVs, two DVD players (you can borrow DVDs from the Kids club by the lobby), a fully equipped kitchen, hobs, coffee maker, kettle, full sized fridge, and even a rice cooker! Throw in a washing machine (soap powder included) and a dryer and the only thing it lacks is a dishwasher! Getting food from the local Lotus Tesco supermarket is easy online, and they deliver to the hotel. The pool is adequate with lots of activities for young children, and a bit for the teenagers and grownups too. Bikes can be borrowed for short trips around the hotel strip (Anantara, Phuket Club resort, and Renaissance). The disadvantage is that you are not right at the beach as it is about a 500m walk, although there is a buggy service to bring you there. And the sea was pretty rough when we were there. Not really safe for paddling or swimming unless you are a seasoned and strong swimmer. Maybe August is not the calmest month. We explored some restaurants outside of the hotel, and JJs was the closest, just next to the rear exit or tradesmans entrance. Cheaper and tasty Thai food if you need an alternative venue from the hotel restaurants without having to take a taxi out. There is not much to do in the evenings apart from visiting the neighbouring hotels unless you take a trip out to Patong or attend one of the evening attractions (eg. Phantasea) nearby.

author: GihanJay
title: Amazing hotel and service
text: Marriott hotels are my favorite hotels, period. So when I choose a country to visit, I first check out the Marriott hotels in the area. When in Phuket, Thailand, we chosed this vacation club property. It was a truly a wonderful experience. On arrival, at 1am, we were greeted with a cold towel and a watermelon drink, which we all enjoyed. The front desk staff were extremely friendly and took the time to explain all the different facilities and activities at this vacation club. The villa was beautiful and extremely spacious. The beds were very comfortable and we all slept very well. The pool was the perfect size and very well maintained. The restaurant, which serves breakfast, lunch and dinner, had some of the best meals available at any Marriott Vacation Club property. The staff at the restaurant were equally nice and very friendly. The beach is a short buggy ride, which is also provided by the hotel. If you like to take pictures at the beach, it is best to stay a little longer to take beautiful pictures of the sunset. We all enjoyed this property and would come again, when in the area. One word of advice, call the hotel and book the shuttle from the airport before you arrive. It cost about 1300 Thai Baht each direction and fully worth it.

author: M7155NFdavidr
title: Clean, Comfortable, Complete, Costly
text: I have been a repeat visitor to this resort, and it's one of my favorites. Multiple pools, multiple 5-star restaurants, large rooms and bathrooms, beautiful grounds, good facilities, multiple activities, good concierge, excellent staff, and probably the best beachfront on all of Phuket Island. An occasional bad smell from an overworked wastewater treatment system and some postponed maintenance items, but it it a large complex. Some people mistakenly think Thailand should be avoided int the rainy season, but even the rainy season it rarely disrupts anything you can;t postpone or reschedule, and even the rain is beautiful in Thailand.. There are some cautions, however. In the off season, it it possible to find a room at a reasonable rate. I can assure you only want to be here when the hotel is lightly booked. It is unpleasantly overcrowded otherwise- fight for a chaise lounge, pool space, a seat at the bar, a reservation at a restaurant, etc. etc. etc. Not a place to visit when it is anywhere near capacity. Worst of all, prepare to pay New York prices for EVERYTHING except the room. This problem is worsened by few choices of other adjacent non-Marriott facilities to escape the cost trap. A nice cultural event to witness is the fire show at sunset about once per week. The breakfast buffet is certainly a great experience, and make certain you include it in the room rate!!! Additional compliments to a long-term staff member, Supaporn Toluang. Ms Toluang has moved from the Sala Bar supervisor to the Marriott Cafe brunch buffet supervisor. The service was good before and even better now. Ms> Toluang is always friendly, accommodating and service oriented. You shouldn't expect any problem but if you experience one, she will certainly correct it., She is representative of the overall excellence in the Marriott staff.

author: NickyP_13
title: Best holiday ever ... Can't wait to return
text: I spent a wonderful week with my husband and two kids (Aged 6 & 8 years old) at the Marriott’s Mai Khao Beach Club and we loved every minute of it. The Resort The Resort is lovely with well maintained grounds and beautifully kept gardens The Villas All the villas are gorgeous & very spacious with 2 bedroom, 2 bathroom units with a lounge, dining room, fully equipped kitchen with oven & stove top, kettle and coffee machine, fridge/freezer, toaster and utensils. There is also a laundry/utility cupboard with a washing machine and tumble dryer which was great. The units are of a very high standard and the master bedroom with a huge stunning bathroom was pure luxury. Our unit was thoroughly cleaned daily and they even supply you with bathrobes, slippers, toiletries, washing powder, tea, coffee, sugar etc . We upgraded to a ground floor unit with a private pool that we all loved and made good use of. We absolutely loved our villa and this made for a perfect holiday. The pool was great and the kids loved the daily activities around the pool. One of the highlights was the movie nights in the pool – such an awesome idea and the kids loved it! Bar, restaurant staff were good and the ladies at the coffee shop were great, all so friendly and welcoming. Aew (Receptionist) was lovely, super friendly, professional and really went out of her way with guests. Lick from the pool towel hut was great with the kids and Joshua still tells everyone about him. The Kids club staff were not very friendly at all, this was on all 3 occassions when we dropped the kids off. Overall, this was one of the best holidays we’ve had which was due to the superb villa, great activities and fantastic staff. We will definitely be back

author: quiescent
title: Relaxing getaway in a beautiful property
text: Firstly, the villa we stayed in was gorgeous and spacious. We felt right at home immediately. One of the highlights would be the bathroom in the master bedroom. It had a spa bath, 2 sinks and almost as big as a room. A villa would be nothing without a spectacularly matched bathroom in my opinion. And of course, there was the private plunge pool. The rainy season wasn't gonna stop me from using it. We had so much fun in it on our last night ;) Secondly, I love that there were so many activities around the resort! I dragged myself out of bed for a refreshing morning workout, went for a thai papaya salad making workshop, a towel folding workshop and a refresher tennis course! Would have gone for more if not for time constraints.. The staff I've encountered were exceptional. Much love goes to the guy who hosted the morning workouts and tennis sessions. He was really accommodating and friendly. Lastly, the resort may be small but you can always hop on over to the other Marriott resort to use the bar or sit by the much bigger pools. Or like us, you could borrow bikes for free and ride there and explore the area where the locals live. There's a free buggy shuttle as well. The possibilities!

author: SiewChoyM
title: A slice of paradise
text: My family stayed here and also at the Marriott Phuket Beach Club so I'm able to compare the two. The Marriott Mai Khao Beach Resort has huge apartments complete with a full kitchen and washer and dryer. There must be over 2000sf of space. The apartments are more modern than the Beach Club and if you're on a high enough floor you can see over the tops of all the palm trees to the sea beyond. The view is better than the Beach Club where trees prevent you from seeing to the horizon. I like the fact that the resort is small as well, which makes it feel cozy. Everything is within a short distance, especially the pool and kids club and, therefore, the resort feels a bit more private than the Beach Club.On the other hand, there is only one pool whereas the Beach Club has a choice of three. Marriott Mai Khao Beach is also not directly on the beach but they have buggy service on call all the time to take you so its not much of a problem. Nevertheless you don't the beach resort feel of being right on the beach. Since the resort is smaller it also doesn't have the lush sprawling gardens over at the Beach Club. The kids club has all sorts of activities for kids, teens and adults. This was one of the highlights for my kids. Do borrow the free bikes and ride around outside. One great thing about the resort is that its right next to Turtle Village so you can eat there anytime for a fraction of the cost of eating in the resort. Everyone is extremely friendly and helpful. I would have no qualms in going back and recommend it highly.

author: John_Teh_TB
title: Nice apartment but everything else quite ordinary
text: Stayed here with 2 other couples, and found the 2-bedroom apartment to be comfortable, well equipped and spacious enough. We did quite a number of island and beach excursions, so the housekeeping staff was superb in bringing us extra towels at our beck and call. The beach, Mai Khao, is lovely and quiet, though we found an even more outstanding beach at Nai Thon not very far away. I was a bit disappointed to learn on arrival that the use of JW Marriott's faciities is restricted to the restaurants and the spa only, which is sad considering JW's pools were much nicer. My group had breakfast at JW one morning and found it to be of very high standard, in terms of quality, variety and service. There are some serious drawbacks with this resort's location though. It is quite remote, and a distance from many Phuket attractions such as Patong and Phuket town, both more than an hour by taxi and hence, much costlier than any of past experience in Phuket. We would have loved to spend more time at the resort itself but this is not a beach fronting property and compared to other resorts I have been to, there isn't much to do or places to hang out within the resort itself. The Turtle Mart is very expensive. I can only surmise that this shop is taking advantage of the area's 'remoteness' i.e. no other shops nearby. I would have loved to rate this resort more highly but unlike the experiences of other travellers, I didn't think the service was quite up to scratch. The Concierge desk was not particularly friendly when I sought recommendations for trips, restaurants etc., particularly needed because of the resort's location. Except on check-in, we didn't get much help lugging 'stuff' on other occassions. In case you find this comment unfair, I say this only because in Phuket the 5-star treatment you get from other resorts is usually outstanding but here, I have to remind myself this is a vacation club property, not a hotel. I also have reservations with the early check out time (10 am). The consolation though is the resort does provide a shower room, which we required since we took a later flight out. I found this arrangement adequate, though couldn't help but be slightly annoyed when we were handed the key we had no help with the luggage despite bellhops just standing around.

author: Itrytotravel
title: Vacation club stay was excellent
text: We stayed there for 3 nights with my parents, hubby and two kids. Awesome service, kids loved the plunge pool, my mom loved the kitchen and the laundry area. The magic door as they call it was very useful especially with kids and all the beach activities . For activities we stayed at the club... The beach is awesome with non motorised water sports on the house. Every hour there was some activity for kids and adults. I did pilates and my kiddo went for the kids club but mostly we swam as we all are human fishes. The turtle village next to the club is very convenient. We got our snacks etc from there. They have restaurants as well and are cheaper than the club. One breakfast we had at JW MARRIOT. It was nice and very filling. Shuttle service to everywhere is very convenient after a long day out at the beach. Room service:food served at the room is good and served hot. Recommend their Rogan Josh and satays.

author: RYWsg
title: High end but far end
text: My family and I (6 adults and 1 baby) had a relaxing stay at this property in Jul 2014. Their villa apartment is so spacious, we could probably bring 1 or 2 more adults (but they just have to sleep at the sofa). Their 2-bedroom villa apartment is well equipped with facilities to take care of your everyday needs. The master bedroom has a king size bed, while the other room has 2 queen size beds. We were pleased to find that they even prepared a playpen for our baby. Each bedroom has en-suite bath and toilet, the master bedroom has an additional bath tub. Also, each room has its own TV and thermostat control to the air-con unit. Within the wardrobe of each room, you will find the usual bathrobe and slippers. Only the master bedroom has a safe for your use. The lounge has a larger TV and the sofa is comfortable to sit in. Dining area has a beautifully designed glass round table (but we were more attracted to the elephant-shaped napkins that was placed on the table most of the times). You will find that the kitchen has things you need to cook up a storm (cutleries, cooking wares, dinnerwares, induction stove, rice cooker, oven, fridge, etc.) once you purchase your ingredients (and leave the cleaning up to others!). Personally, I like their in-villa washing machine, dryer, iron and ironing board. It means I can bring less clothes and save that couple of kilograms of luggage space to bring back more goodies from Phuket. Their ground floor apartment has a private swimming pool which I feel that families with kids or those who want more privacy will prefer to have it at a cost. One minor thing which they can improved upon is to equipped their apartments with multi standard sockets, which some lower star hotels provide. There are many activities which you can engage in within their property and the surrounding: swimming, dining at their restaurant, play games (table tennis, snookers, basket ball, etc.), cycling, gym, shop at next door Turtle Village, go to the beach for a stroll, take their free shuttle bus to visit their 2 other properties, etc. I feel the only big down side is that it is located far away from Patong beach and Phuket centre if you are a shopper.

author: petsaloz
title: A Great Experience in Phuket
text: Mai Khao Vacation Resort is part of a larger Marriott Complex which includes the Vacation Club facilities, a JW Marriott resort hotel, another holiday village complex and Anantara Resort. While each resort is independent they are linked through the Marriott brand and you get access to restaurants, pool and other facilities although not all. It makes your choice for restaurants etc much broader and you can charge to your room in the resort you are staying at to ensure your reward points are secure. There is also a small shopping plaza nearby (walking distance) where you can obtain basic provisions and other resort shopping. There are regular shuttle services throughout the complex and so, even though all is within walking distance, you can ride if you prefer. If venturing further afield there are local buses and taxis available and street food vendors just outside the resort boundaries. Massages are available at reasonable prices on the nearby beach. We stayed in a 2 bedroom apartment in the Mai Khao Centre. It was on the 5th floor and gave a view over most of the resort from the extra large balcony. The rooms were similarly large and well appointed. There was provision in the kitchen to prepare your own meals, if desired. However, the range of restaurants available allowed choices from top end to deli cafe style so you could eat economically or go upmarket. The Japanese teppan restaurant was excellent on the high end dining. Rooms were serviced daily and the staff did a great job seeking to please in every way. We were met at the airport and delivered back as part of our package arrangement and this was all arranged very efficiently. The whole experience was excellent and certainly a resort I would look to come back to.

author: Ahmed_Elmadani
title: Lovely days
text: We arrived at Marriott Mai Khao for our first visit in Phuket not knowing what to expect and we were welcomed by a nice surprise. The villa was spacious and very clean and fully equipped with everything you will need for your stay, washing machine, dryer, fully equipped kitchen, you name it. Also the bathrooms were fantastic, specially the bath tub. The hotel is located in the north of the island so its near to the airport, 20 minutes, but its far from city centre (Patong). The Mai Khao area is relatively prestigious, with other 5 star hotels Anantra and JW Marriott located in the same area so its a 5 star district if I may say. The pool is nice but better is to have a shuttle take you to the beach and there you'll find the multiple pools for JW marriott. Marriott Mai Khao beach and JW Marriot are integrated together in some sort and some of the facilities and the activities are shared by both. The staff were professional, not very friendly as compared to our next hotel in Phuket, but overall they were nice. There is a nearby shops area called turtle village, nice too, with Bill Bentley pub which we liked, it also has a pricy supermarket and money exchange, so basically most of your needs will be met. On the downside is that it is very far from everything so you have to take a 75 minute, 1200 Baht taxi to patong one way if you like to see the city centre. No shuttle service provided by the hotel which is a bummer. Also the food was not that great, don't get me wrong, it was good, but nothing extraordinary. Also they My advice is to go to the beach and have a massage there, its an awesome experience. This resort is for relaxation, if you are looking for explore the island this one is not for you. Finally, I would visit again if I get the chance.

author: enochho
title: Good experience
text: Marriot's Mai Khao Beach is a well-organized resort with lots of activities for everybody. We had a 2 bedroom ground floor suite with a private plunge pool, however, the pool was simply too deep to utilize (1.8m!) so we spent a lot of time in the common pool. The suite itself is well-equipped with a kitchenette and all the cooking utensils you could ask for, and a laundry room with a washing machine and dryer. The small bathtub in the second bathroom could have been better taken out and replaced with a shower area, however, that's just a small quibble. The staff also leave little cute animals made from the towels, and it's definitely a delight for the little ones. There is a full day of activities every day and there is plenty for everybody, from the young kids to the adults. The Director of Recreation, Gee, made sure that everybody was having a good time and his friendliness and enthusiasm definitely made a positive impression. If you hang out at the poolside, every few hours they bring around little treats like fruit platters and ice lollies, which is an amazing plus under the hot Phuket sun. There are also a few kiddy pools to choose from, with varying depths. The only minus point, again, was the depth of the main pool, which also went to 1.8m. What is the point of such a deep pool anyway? Food there was good, we managed to get 30% off the buffet breakfast one morning and it had a good selection of food and fresh fruit juice, with the discount it's worthwhile trying it out once in a while. We didn't try the rest of the food during other meals, but there isn't a whole lot of options around Mai Khao Beach anyway. In the late morning till the afternoon there are some little mobile stalls that set up shop just outside Turtle Village, the open air mall right outside this resort, and you can pick up fruits, barbecued chicken and other things there. The Bill Bentley Pub in Turtle Village has really good food and we ate there a few times. Marriot's Mai Khao Beach was a great experience and we will definitely be back again. One huge minus I would say would be that the check-in is at 4pm while check-out is a mind-boggling 10am, although they try their best to offer a shower room for you to use if your flight is much later.

author: Alexvonw
title: Lovely relaxing holiday
text: We had 4 nights at this resort and it was very relaxing. I believe all the accommodation is in 2 bedroom apartments which are very well equipped, including a kitchen and washer and dryer. Our kids had a great time at the kids club and in the pool and on the beach. It is a lovely beach although better for playing in the sand rather than swimming as there are some waves (but not suitable for surfing) and currents which could be dangerous. There is a good supermarket next door to the resort which has everything you could need, although prices are comparable to Australia/Singapore or even more for imported items like cheese. In the same shopping centre as the supermarket are also some restaurants and a pub. These are all quite good although not very cheap - roughly a third to 3/4 of prices in Singapore or Australia. You can get Thai dishes in all the restaurants although it seems silly to pay so much for them! The only downside to this resort is that it is 45 minutes to 1 hour by car from Phuket town. Therefore you are somewhat limited in your meal choices unless you want to make a long journey. But the flipside is that this resort is very serene and peaceful. You will not be accosted by touts and hawkers. The hotel does its best to give some local flavour to the place, but you could quite easily forget you are in Thailand altogether. Finally, the naming of the Marroitt's resorts in this area is very confusing and difficult to work out which one is which. They are almost next door to each other and the facilities are similar but this one is smaller, more intimate and more family oriented. If you are organising your own transportation from the airport, make sure you are clear about which place you are going.

author: celadoncatz
title: Best Resort in Mai Khao
text: I first visited Marriott's Mai Khao Beach (MKB for short) in 2008. At that time, it was a very new resort and had almost no amenities hence it was quite a hassle for us to take the buggy to the adjacent JW Marriott and Phuket Beach Club for the facilities there. There was also no Turtle Village nor any other options in terms of dining. Resort was lovely but we were literally held hostage to pay Marriott prices for food. Our next visit came in 2010. Once again, lovely resort and this time there was Turtle Village. Made a huge difference to the pocket for us to be able to buy groceries (albeit at 30% above the prices of Tesco Lotus) to prepare simple breakfasts. Between 2012 to 2014, we have visited the resort at least once annually, as we eventually became MVCI members. We love it there. The one time we actually stayed at the Phuket Beach Club instead of MKB, our kids begged us to never book PBC again. The reason? The MKB staff in the fitness centre and the kids' club are just above and beyond wonderful. They make every effort to get to know every single guest and subsequently, call every one by name. It's like coming back to a huge family. Gee, the American guy in charge of the fitness centre and kids' club activities has really done a bang-up job of organising so many fun activities for both the adults and kids. The guys and girls who work under him are happy and outgoing. My kids feel so welcome and happy being there that it's hard to tear them away from the kids club! In terms of the food around the resort, there's Kindee (they deliver), JJ's Bar (walk through the laundry buildings and out of the Anantara Staff entrance) and the huts nearer to the Renaissance and Sala resorts. If one cycles or walks out, there's a whole bunch of cheap(ish) local Thai food to satisfy every single Thai food craving :)

author: Kshitij2003
title: Overall ok experience
text: The resort is quite beautiful and very peaceful since it is in the quiet part of Phuket, an hour drive away from Patong which is the City Center in a way. We had two bedroom apartment with our own plunge pool which was a great advantage since the kids could enjoy swimming at any time of the day. The layout of the apartment was good with a huge bathroom attached to the Master Bedroom which had a king size bed while the other room had two queen size beds ideal for a family of four with 2 teens. The kitchen had all the utensils required for cooking and daily housekeeping services took care of cleaning. There were quite a few downsides though. This resort has the worst check-in (4PM)/check-out time (10AM) that I have come across in my 20 years of travel experience. This in a way takes away one day of stay considering most other hotels are quite flexible in giving early check-in late check out while Marriott was quite rigid in this regard. On our last day of stay, we requested for a 12PM check out since out flight was at 4PM but the hotel did not budge and extended the check-out only by an hour. This was in sharp contrast to Grand Mercure (where we had stayed in Patong before moving to Marriott) which had no issues in extending the check-out time from 12PM to 3PM. Marriott's attitude here was very disappointing. Also the Turtle village which is nearest grocery store is extremely expensive with rates for most items more than double of what you will pay in the city. Actually the two good things that we experienced were both outside the resort. First was Kindee Restaurant which is a 5 minutes drive from the resort. The taxi service outside the resort takes 500 THB for a round trip to this place which provides excellent thai food at reasonable prices. We went to this place almost every day of our stay. The second one is the massage at the beach (outside JW Marriott Hotel) which is not only much cheaper than ridiculously priced Mandara Spa at the JW Marriott but also much better. Since the hotel is in a middle of no where, commuting is a major issue since the taxi service outside the resort ask for very high charges to go to any place in Phuket. Luckily we found phuketshuttle.com which was easy to use and much cheaper. Also our favourite place for poolside drinks and snacks was JW Marriott rather than Marriott Mai Khao since we could enjoy our drinks with the beautiful view of Andaman Sea. There is really no view at Marriott Mai Khao.

author: Ricoy
title: Great Property! A Haven for family vacation
text: We have enjoyed staying in this beautiful property through our exchange program with Interval International -- having to enjoy a week long of fun and excitement. The property is a good 20-minute ride from Phuket International Airport. Though the property seem small from the main entrance but the property extends beyond what we have expected. Our room (4342) was very big with a foyer, two toilet and baths , 2 bedrooms ( 1-master bedroom with huge toilet and bath -- with big bath tub and 1- bedroom with 2-queen sized beds also with a decent sized toilet and bath -- regular sized bath tub) , it has its own kitchen complete with cooking amenities like cooking pan, fry pan etc. , included are glasswares, plates, utensils, and free bottled water everyday! Inside our room is a dining table good for 6-people , a nice cozy living room and 3-TV (1-for the master's bedroom, for the 2nd room , and the living room). We also got to enjoy a relatively nice balcony. Not to mention that there is a washing machine and dryer inside the room!! Plus, ironing board, flat / steam iron and detergent soap for the laundry. We enjoyed their facilities and daily scheduled activities like, zumba, aqua aerobics , biking, and other outdoor activities. Best of all, the property is very near to good restaurants and small quaint stores -- the Turtle Village -- which is a mere 2-3 minute walk from the Marriott. A grocery store is also within reach and you can buy necessary grocery items if you feel like cooking inside your unit / room. Marriott Mai Khao is also a near to JW Marriott and Anantara where they have different ambiance and restaurants. Moreso, I would also like to commend all staffs who are very accommodating, kind, respectful and very professional. Overall, the place is fabulous. We truly enjoyed our stay here. We will surely be back here on our next visit to Phuket. Thank you Marriott Mai Khao for making our family vacation a very memorable and happy experience.

author: dseptkon
title: Stay here if you want peace and quiet
text: We stayed here 4 nights. The rooms themselves were wonderful as the other reviewers have pointed out- almost everything was taken care of and it really felt like a home away from home. From the DVD player with DVDs from the kids club, the brand new washer and dryer (missing a dishwasher though), microwave and fully stocked kitchen, the hotel managed to check all the boxes. Thumbs up to Phoo at the front desk who managed to get us into our beautiful rooms early from our red-eye flight despite the official check-in time being 4 pm. Our room was located on the corner on the second floor of the first block and that made it very convenient for getting to turtle village. It also offered plenty of privacy unlike rooms along the corridor which were in full view of passers-by. What let the hotel down was the beach- or rather lack thereof. Granted it was low season when we visited but the pounding surf coupled with the 20 foot stretch of creeper-covered sand ensured that this was to be our first beach holiday where we never set foot on the beach. This is not a family-friendly, or child friendly set up. The weather held up wonderfully despite our fears of the rainy season and so we spent most of our time at the pool. At least there were lots of inflatables there that everyone was free to use so the pool noodles, inflatable tyres and balls kept the kids busy. The kiddie pool with slide was really way too small- most of the time there were also plenty of adults in it minding their children! The quality of food poolside was good but the prices high and we realised that there was often a midday exodus from the pool as people trotted over to the restaurants at turtle village or anantara next door to have lunch! I'd recommend you rent a car if you stay here. We did and it turned out to be a great decision as other than Turtle Village, there isn't much else to visit nearby. It's great that Thai roads are easy to navigate- fairly straight, smooth and roadsigns are in Thai and English. Thalang is only a 20 minute drive away and the Tesco Lotus there provides some retail therapy and more variety in stocking up your hotel room refrigerator. Further afield, there is Central Festival Market with a nice supermarket and in Patong, there is Jungceylon. While in Patong, we got the sense that Mai Khao was really "out of the mainstream" and could not help comparing this with our previous stay in Phuket. We appreciated the hotel's proximity to the airport (a short 10 min ride away) but if you really want to experience Phuket and its beaches, then this is not the hotel for you.

author: Lasereraser
title: Lovely place!
text: I loved the smiles of all the staff I met! From the concierge to the driver! And all the small touches that we experienced, like ice water being served at the pool, updated and current magazines to read with a reinforced plastic cover in case they get wet and the shuttle service to and fro the two Marriott establishments. We arrived at 930am in the morning and check in was at 4pm! But luckily since we had called the day before to let them know this, our room was ready for us when we arrived. They were also kind enough to extend our check out by an hour as our flight was a little later on. Much appreciated! We also took the bus twice into patong and central shopping mall. Patong is a tourist trap and very busy. We won't be returning. Central was okay lots of Japanese food options. But not sure if worth the hour's ride to and fro. Patong certainly wasn't. The food at Marriott is pretty decent. One of the best Thai meals I've had is definitely at Ginja, their Thai place The rooms were great and spacious. I had some bug bites on my arm from leaning on one of their cushions/armchairs but I didn't sit there anymore after that, probably due to age/not cleaned. But that was the only little thing! everything else at the Marriott was very pleasant. I'd recommend it to anyone who's not looking to do anything but relax in the sun by the pool for a few days!

author: SingaporeCbu
title: Lovely hotel but smaller than the Marriott next door.
text: We recently stayed here on a referral from a friend who has taken out the Marriott Vacation Club package. The room we were given was a lovely, big, spacious 2 bed apartments that could sleep up to 6 people. We felt very spoilt as there was only 3 of us. The kitchen is well equipped with just about everything that you could want to cook a decent family meal. We were given 4 large bottles of drinking water each day and the apartment was spotlessly clean. I couldn't fault it. We were a little disappointed that the facilities and grounds were not as big as the Marriott next door. Although they had similar things on offer (pool, kids pool, play kids club, gym etc) they were a lot smaller. We weren't allowed to use the big Marriott's facilities either which was a shame as our 3yr old would have had an absolute field day in the larger, much more entertaining kids pool, grounds and kids club. The beach from this hotel was a short buggy trip away unlike the other Marriott, where is right on their doorstep. Although this didn't cause a problem for us I can see why it might put some people off. It's easy to get to (the hotel will take you on demand which was great) but there is no return buggy, unless you walk to the shuttle bus pick up point which is easily a good 10-15 minute walk away (so you might as well walk home). It might not be too easy with tired kids at the end of the day. There is a booth set up on the beach for towels, but this shuts at 5pm. Finally, food at both the hotels can be expensive and the supermarket close by is also expensive. We paid for a little more baggage allowance on the way out, took our own food and just bought basics when we were there. Overall the Marriott Mai Khao Beach hotel is lovely, the staff were cheerful, the room was great, but we thought that it did feel like the smaller, less important Marriott compared to the one next door.

author: jpoon99
title: Perfect for families with children
text: Stayed here for 4 nights in a 2-bedroom pool villa. Perfect for children. Free bicycle rental, free shuttle to travel to JW Marriot and you get 4,000 baht voucher if you attend a 60 mins. Marriot Vacation Club presentation. Points to note: 1. If you want to go to the beach, take the shuttle to JW Marriot. Remember to take the blue towel from the front desk first as JW Marriot will not provide towel to Marriot Mai Khao Beach guests. 2. I rented a 7-seater for 1,600 baht per day. I can then travel freely to the restaurants nearby, to and from the airport (20 mins.), go to Tesco's food court for lunch.... 3. Buffet breakfast is 5-stars. 4. Only that the A/C is not very comfortable. Either too cold or too hot. 5. Swimming pool has a water slider for kids. Pool bar has buy one get one free from 4:30pm.

author: Catherine0404
title: A family resort!
text: We just came back from our 5 days 4 night trip from Marriott Mai Khao beach resort (MVCI) and overall experience is very good. We are a family of 4 with two kids age 7 & 12. We are here by the invitation of the marketing promo of the vocation club membership and we did not regret it. The resort is fully equipped with kitchen facilities and washing machine and dryer so it really make it very convenient for us to do our laundry after every trip to the beach. We love the big rooms and my kids especially enjoy the big bath tub in the master bedroom. The pool area is nothing to rave about as it is quite small in my opinion and the restaurant there is a disappointment as there is only 1 major restaurant and if you need variety you need to travel to JW Marriott for their restaurant. And the food there is really expensive in local standard. We only had the breakfast and a Japanese dinner (Kabuki restaurant) in JW and the rest of meals we ate in the restaurants at Turtle village. In comparison the price are also expensive compare to local standard thus we have engage a personal driver to drive us out to shop in Phuket Town and eat at leam hin seafood restaurant. Overall, the stay is great perhaps this resort is meant for marketing purpose on the Marriott vocation membership so it doesn't provide the full resort facilities as JW Marriott offers. The beach is a 30 meters walk and you need to carry the towels all the way as this resort don't have the beach area. One thing to mention is that as we are traveling in peak season and we notice that the restaurant are very very full in JW Marriott (Marriott cafe for breakfast and Kabuki) We waited about 15 mins to have our table for our breakfast at 9 am. The food replenishment is very slow given the high volume of guests and we need to remind the staff for our coffee and my son's hot chocolate is never been seen even we reminded them for two times. It is a common sight to see beelines at meal times in most restaurant. My suggestion is to go early or prepare to wait. No reservation is allow for breakfast. We did not sign up the membership as it does not fit our travel lifestyle for flexibility and hotel location is also our top priority. Most Marriott hotels are far from city and in a serene secluded places.

author: hunter_partyofive
title: Beautiful property, away from the chaos
text: The Mai Khao Beach Club is nice for our family of five. They have nice two bedroom apartments, with a king and two queen sized beds. Also with a fully equipped kitchen. Bottom floor apartments have great private pools to get away from the bustle of the main pool. A yoga pavilion is currently under construction and will be a nice asset to the property. Only a ten minute walk to the beach down a path or a shuttle service every 15 minutes to JW Marriott, which is a beach front property. This is really not bad considering the larger resorts require the same amount of walking to get to the beach and they have beach front property. Staff was very friendly. The atmosphere at Mai Khao Beach club is good for families. Lots of good energy and activities for the kids. There was even a trapeze club at the JW property. For 1100 baht pp the kids reserved an hour slot for trapeze lessons. This activity was the highlight for them. To my surprise there were lots of small, open air Thai massage huts along the beach so if you don't want to pay a fortune at the spas you have other options. Our only complaint is the lack of development lends itself to limited food options. We stayed here 8 days and have eaten at every local resort, plus the two options at Turtle Village. Food is pricey. There are a few restaurants on public property outside the resorts but again,only Thai options and they are expensive by local standards.

author: AusBoo
title: Great resort, but it's not the J.W.Marriott! And beware of the sales pitch
text: this resort is very nice, villas very comfortable, pool nice, we really enjoyed our time here. But be aware that it is not the J.W. Marriott , we thought the resorts were side by side, but they are 2 separate resorts and you need to catch the courtesy bus over to J.W. The names are a bit confusing too - there's the J.W. Marriott which is hotel style accommodation, set in the grounds of the Marriott's Phuket beach club! and then there's the resort we stayed at the Marriott Mai Khao Beach Vacation Club. Also, this resort is not set right on the beach, you need to walk or get a buggy, only a 5 min ride, but still not on the beach! We were also led to believe (not by Marriott staff) that by staying at Mai Khao Beach vacation club we could still use the facilities at J.W (ie. the beautiful pools at J.W. ) but it turns out that you can't use the pool at J.W., you can only use the restaurants and bars, which was a big disappointment! We were interested in buying a membership to the Marriott club, (we figure that's about the only way you can ever get to stay at the J.W.,) but decided not to go ahead... so just a word of warning - make sure you understand the credits system - 23000 points ( the minimum you can buy) is not enough to get you a week basically anytime between Nov thru to April. The meals can be pricey in both the resorts, so we often ate at a group of local restaurants near the beach, much more relaxed and better value. Plus the local restaurateurs are so welcoming! If you are self catering , say for breakfast, there's a Tesco Lotus supermarket about 30mins south on the main highway No.4. Much cheaper than turtle mart and much more variety. the staff are wonderful, they really go out of their way to make your stay as pleasant as possible. We would stay here again, but at least we now have a clearer understanding of the different resorts and how they are set up.

author: EugenioP661
title: Be prepare to pay dearly for everything here.
text: I guess this is a very decent place for families with kids prepared to stay the whole time in the same place and pay 10 times more for food and drinks than elsewhere in Thailand. Is definitely not for young couples. If you want a more decent place nearby with less noise from kids shouting in your hears, head to the JW Marriott just next door which has an amazing swimming pool. Be aware of the monopoly that the resorts in this area are creating: 1. Forget going anywhere for less then 500 Bt per person, if you are lucky. The hotels here charge ridiculous prices for going just about anywhere. Even to go to a restaurant nearby the asked 500 Bt when the ride would be 10 min. 2. All the restaurants are overpriced to a point of desperation. I have read of others who went to some supermarkets nearby and that might be the solution, but given I have experienced quite a bit of Thailand, I would have expected more reasonably priced eateries in the area. 3. If you come with the timeshare program, do your research about it carefully. There is a lot to learn on internet about all this program. The sales people have very powerful psychological techniques to get you to make a very rush decision on the spot. Do not give in! Take your time and do the research very very carefully as you might sourly regret it sooner rather than later!

author: Filumel
title: Marriott Mai Khao Beach
text: Nice resort located just 20 minutes from Phuket airport. Got a 2 Bedroom suite with 2 Bathrooms, Kitchen, Washing Machine and tumble dryer, cutlery dishes and all you need during your holidays. Resort is clean , housekeeping washes even your dishes. Beautiful pool with Jacuzzis , kids pool and playground , Kids playhouse, Gym, soccer/basket court; definitively a good choice for a family. The downside is a poor restaurant choice (just 2 and not attractive restaurants) , but OK for Breakfast , and a quick lunch. Next door a nice complex (Turtle Village) with a Supermarket (not cheap) , café , pub and Ice Cream Shop. Now, if you want luxury , book next door property JW Marriott! This place is stunning , majestic decoration , bars , restaurants a wonderful pool , a huge bakery , kids playground ; absolutely impressive and very elegant. Another good choice is the other next door resort called Anantara. They provide pool villas in a very ZEN environment. You will be offered to purchase Vacation ownerships either by Marriot or Anantara. Both Hotels unleash staff around the turtle village offering free tours , spa service , hotel rooms in exchange of your attendance to a 90 minutes presentation with a salesman who will do everything to sell you a vacation ownership. Is worth a try especially for the free gift , but be prepared to get brain washed by the salesman. We purchased such package from Anantara. Conclusion: JW MARRIOTT OUTSTANDING ANANTARA EXCELENT MARRIOT MAI KHAO BEACH VACATION CLUB , VERY GOOD

author: mel-man-india
title: Excellent Stay at Mai Khao with Family
text: We had an excellent stay at Mai Khao with family in Nov'12. A 4 night referral offer was taken up by us and we were pleasantly surprised at the quality of the property. The villas are exceptionally well maintained and the staff is quite good. Lots of fun activities for the kids - its a place designed for a family vacation. We were aware that the place is far from the city centre (Patong) however it was a conscious decision to stay here. Local car hire for the duration was cheap and extremely convenient for our trips into the city. The villas are equipped with all amenities including cooking facilities. There is a small convenience store next door (though prices are 2-3 times of regular marts) for supplies - its better (if you have a vehicle) to go down to supermarts and pick up stuff. The room dining was average as the choices are very limited. The Mai Khao beach is amazingly quite and serene. The JW Mariott next door is nice (though crowded and noisy - I prefered Mai Khao resort any day). The sales presentation (if you are on a referral trip) is mandatory and they do try and do a hardsell (buy-now or loose offer type). We did not take it up and they did seem a little miffed. Nevertheless, overall the trip to Mai Khao was excellent (try to get a room with the plunge pool - its on the ground floor, but I suspect they may want to reserve it for members or paying guests instead of referrals). Don't forget to hire a car if you plan to stay here (the hotel guys arrange it for you)

author: whoisw
title: Possible food poisoning, customer service didn't care
text: I'm posting this story since the normal way of notifying a business of a bad experience (customer service) was such a fail that it deserves to be publicly called out: We tried out the Marriott on a discounted 4 day 3 night trip to decide if the vacation club package would be a good buy for us. Since this was a family trip including my parents and a small child, we spent the whole time on premises for all dining and activities. The Good: facilities are nice, the staff friendly and helpful, and the rooms some of the nicest we've stayed in by vacation club standards. The Bad: food quality is inconsistent- a lackluster buffet our first evening followed by much better room service breakfast, cafe lunch and then a evening buffet all from the same kitchen. We suspected there was something wrong with dinner as the next morning 3 of us came down with day-ruining diarrhea - hence possible food poisoning. The Ugly: When my wife and I explained this to the customer service rep, a borderline dismissive expat, the complete lack of empathy was shocking. He couldn't care less that part of our trip was ruined by a break down in food safety standards on Marriott's end. He even remarked that other people also had similar issues with the same restaurant and that "they take these things seriously and would certainly look into it"... wtf?! To make matters worse, we were harassed and insulted by an overly aggressive sales manager, and when we mentioned this, the rep cared more about defending the sales manager than even bothering to listen to our story. Adding final insult to injury, the rep's way of "making up for this" was to slash the sales tax on a last last chance package to enjoy the same Marriott club again (obviously we chose not to buy into the club nor will we ever be returning). In conclusion, if Marriott is in the business of selling a memorable experience and great service, they've certainly hit the mark for us with this trip. Our family will definitely remember this experience and the wonderful lack of guest empathy. 1 star for our stay and experience. 1 extra star for the wonderful local staff, who we would like to acknowledge

author: iamhey
title: A wonderful time at Marriott!
text: The villa is fantastic and well equipped. There are washing machine and dryer which can be used for free. There is also complimentary internet access in the villa and across the resort. We chilled out at the resort most of the time during our four-day stay. The pool is great and we spent a lot of time there. Staff are friendly and helpful. Since the resort is in a remote location, dining options are quite limited. We had a dinner at Ginger Taste at JW Marriott (connected to Marriott by free shuttle bus) which was quite nice but not spectacular. We also had in-room dining which was affordable and quite good. We also called for delivery from Kin Dee Restaurant which is near Marriott. The food was more authentic but the fried rice was disappointing. We also took a bike ride around the resort area (bicycles are available for use for 2 hours daily on a complimentary basis). We cycled to a small old town near the lake area to have lunch at a local restaurant there. The food was great and authentic but there were just too many flies! The Mai Khao Beach is just okay so we did not spend much time there. We only went there to see the sunset.

author: MrO330
title: Great for rich families and boring couples
text: This hotel is far from the Phuket's action spot, Pataong Beach. Distance to Pataong beach from this hotel is about a 1 hour drive, though the hotel is very close to the Airport, 6 k.m. Having said that, they have roundtrip pick up and drop facility available to the Pataong on chargeable basis(1200 baht). If you only want pool, quiet surroundings and expensive food(breakfast is 720 baht each)... you can consider this hotel. There are very limited to no other food options around. Theres a small market connected to the next property, but has inflated prices as well. If you come out of the hotel and make a left, right at the employees cafeteria and follow that road, it leads to JJ's bar. This is where the employees eat and half the price of anything at the hotel. Along the way you will see signs deterring tourists from going down that road, but ignore those. Also, do not get confused with the name and consider this hotel as a beach front hotel. This hotel has no beach access. They have access to the neighboring JW Marriott hotel and have shuttle every 15 mins to drop you off to the beach. Also during the rainy season, the riptides are severe and they recommend you not one going into the water. Villas are huge and very well maintained. All amenities are available with kitchen, cutlery, oven, washing machine, dryer and so on. Perfect for long stay with a family that has disposable income. Stayed October 2012, traveled with couples and friends

author: PrincessMia
title: members referral hotel
text: We were guests of Marriot Vacation club and invited for a stay here with another couple sometime in August. The catch for this complimentary stay was to attend a 90 min session sales presentation for the vacation club membership. All well and good. We discovered that Mai Khao is where all the referred guests were placed.Not in the Marriott Resort and vacation club which was a 5 min buggy ride away....(sadly) Since 2 couples were sharing the apartment, obviously only one couple would get to use the master bedroom with a king bed and a bathroom with a tub and the bathroom was as big as the room itself! but not a chance for us to check out the bathtub. Had to settle for a small bathroom with a standard bath tub.. We were in the 2nd bedroom which was intended for children of a family. The 2nd room was tiny with 2 super single beds squashed inside although I was told that there are 2 queen sized beds. I was misled. We felt that The vacation club should have offered us another unit of apartment so that we can experience the master room - although it was only the referral resort.On top of this, the Mai Khao has no beach and we would have to take a buggy to the beach if we wanted to. It was not the most convenient. There was no breakfast provided and we felt that it was a basic necessity which would have been taken care of as it posed another inconvenience to us during our stay. Otherwise the set up and facilities were reasonable but it would have been better for us to be allowed to stay in the Marriott Resort and Vacation club proper so that we can consider the membership more seriously. Worse still, we were not even allowed to use the facilities ie pool and gym in Marriott resort and vacation club. I wrote to the sales person Ms Suleemart on a few of my concerns but she never got back to me and this level of service is not quite acceptable. There is certainly room for improvement here if the vacation club wants to improve its membership sales!

author: JetsForFunJourneys
title: Very Nice MVCI Property
text: We recently stayed at this location for the first time after getting a great deal. We stay in a 2BR unit with private plunge pool. The resort and room were to Marriott standards. Our early arrival was warmly accepted with cool towels and juice. The room had three 1L bottles of water and there was free internet available in the units. I agree with other contributors that it is best to go out and buy some food for your villa. It is much cheaper than the resort food. The breakfast buffet is almost US$30 per person which is expensive by Thai standards. The resort is quite a distance away from the major attractions, so some pre-planning is needed. The fitness center had good equipment in it and the kids' club had plenty of video games/activities available for the little ones. The pool area is beautiful and expansive. I would agree that the baby elephant interaction twice daily was a hit! If you plan to do cooking classes, go offsite to a school down in Patong or Phuket City areas. The resort charges a hefty THB2,500 per person for a fixed menu. If you go elsewhere, prices start around THB1,000 and you get to shape the menu. Be aware that you will probably be approached at check-in to do a timeshare presentation if you are already not an owner. For the 90 minute presentation, they will give you 20,000 Rewards points or THB4,000 to spend at the overpriced Turtle Village shops or on overpriced resort food. Keep in mind that these units start around US$17,000, but are much lower if you by from a reseller.

author: Greyman003
title: Very pleased, will visit again, recommended.
text: I visited recently with my wife and son. Our arrival was very late at night due to a late flight arrival, however the staff on duty were very good and attentive to our needs. We were shown to our villa and provided an overview of the services available and the villa. We ventured to breakfast at the Delights cafe at the resort the next morning. Again the service was very good and the food tasty. The pool is fantastic and big enough to enable me to find some swimming space without bumping into people. The pool is cleaned daily and is surrounded by lounges and day beds. The pool side bar staff brought guests complimentary water, fruit and small drink samples. The recreation staff were brilliant in assisting my son by providing him towels, goggles and pool toys. Of great interest to us was the twice daily visit to the pool area by a baby elephant. The handler encouraged guests to play with the elephant and was patient while we all took photos. Our interaction with all the staff was brilliant. They would always welcome us with a big smile and were very helpful. I have no complaints about our stay and recommend you all visit in future. The rooms are cleaned daily if you wish and restocked with towels, water, coffee and tea. You can save some money by buying bread, milk etc from the Turtle Beach supermarket. The only downside was the distance to Patong Beach, Phuket Fantasea and other activities. If you don't want to leave Mai Khao Beach, you wont be concerned. Otherwise, expect to travel 1 hour each way through maniac Thai traffic. The novelty wore off very quickly.

author: KLMalaysian
title: 4 Days 3 Nights Complementary at Pool Villa
text: We stayed this hotel complementary 4 days 3 nights by members reference packages. The conditions is must attended 90 minutes presentation by the Marriott Vacation Club. The presentation took about 120 minutes but the sales representative is friendly and good presentation. We all 4 adults with 1 infant arrival at this hotel. Welcome drink and souvenir upon arrival. This packages included complementary round trip airport transfer. The hotel staffs are very nice and friendly. We requested baby chair and baby play pen all prepared nicely. Everyday 3 bottles 1 little mineral water. Complementary free wired internet and free WIFI. We bring our own laptop for movie and surfing Internet. We rental a private Taxi for half-day 5 hours from Marriot to Patong, Tesco Lutos, seafood restoran, local products about 2000 bath for round trip. The hotel is far from town about 40KM one way. We order dinner from Kin Dee restoran, food is ok and delivery on time but the portion is too little for every order. We can said just enough for 2 persons. The price for Kin Dee is acceptable. We recommended order more if you have a big group. Overall this hotel is great if you want for relaxation and away from town.

author: qqtraveler
title: Love the private pool!
text: We stayed at the pool villa in the hotel for 2 nights. The hotel gave us very home feel, it was an apartment with a guest room and a kitchen, it was good for a max of six persons, though only two of us stayed there. What was special was a private pool which was half-covered. In fact, we were so relaxed as we spent most of our daytime there enjoying the cooling water with the hot sunny sky and beautiful trees. A good place to enjoy privacy and recharge our energy... Other merits: Free wifi, three 1 liter of drinking water daily, nearby Turtle Village for shopping and food. Coffee Club there serves good food at reasonable prices. We were lucky we got early check-in, otherwise, we would need to check-in at 4pm. Fyi, check-out time is very early at 10am.. There are free shuttle bus every 15 min around the hotels under the Marriott Group. You could also arrange hotel transport to Patong, cost THB700 per person round trip. It takes about 1 hr one way. Boyfriend said he wanted to have a house with a pool like this. I said it was better to come here whenever we wanted..that is more convenient and efficient! Haha!

author: CarloRago
title: Check-In & Check-Out Time Needs Improvement
text: We stayed at this resort from April 2 to 5 2012 at a two bedroom villa with a plunge pool. Each bedroom has a bathroom with tub; so my ten year old daughter was overjoyed as she was able to take a bath in each of the tubs, aside from having her own private pool. The villa has a living, dining, and kitchen area as the intention is for guests to feel at home. Being located at the northern part of the island, far from the more commercial and touristy area in the south, makes it all the more important if the guests do not want to travel far. A plus is the Turtle Village (mini) mall which is situated right beside as there are shops and two restaurants and a grocery at the basement; just in case you want some change in scenery. Over-all, the facility is five stars! The major drawback is the check-in and check-out time. We arrived at the resort just before two in the afternoon. Unfortunately, the check-in time was 4pm so they asked us to wait as the villa had to be cleaned up. We decided instead to spend time at the Turtle Village mall and as we walked passed our villa, we noted that there were no longer occupants. Upon our return at 4pm, we passed by the villa again and noticed that there were no cleaners and that the cleaning had not yet started. When we checked with the front desk, they told us that the room would be available at 530pm. I could not understand this because the villas and rooms are regularly cleaned every day; so why was it taking so much time for them to make the room available considering that the required check-out time, on the other hand, is 10am? In fact, when we checked out three days later, a family of four were getting irritated as they had arrived in the morning; only to discover that their accommodation was still not available. Definitely needs improvement!

author: CalvinOng1982
title: Fully furnished 2-room apartment, quiet with mini shopping complex
text: Took a 4 day, 3 night FOC package under the Mai Khao Marriot Vacation Club plan, after referral by a friend, on condition that spouse and myself attend a 90 minute talk. Went with 2 other friends, all with 2 kids, aged around 4-7. Apparently, breakfast is included only for non-peak periods. Do remember to ask for plunge pool which is only available for the 1st floors. If impression serves me right, the resort are all 4 levels high, or there or about, with only the 1st floor with a pte pool, which we did not used at all, for some reason. Mai Khao is near the airport and up north and we made the mistake of renting 2 cars for 3 families with kids. Should have stayed in the resort and perhaps take a cab out. If you prefer the crowded Patong, this is no good, but if are prepared to cook, arrange activities yourself in the resort and make use of the kids' club/activities room, which I think you should, then this is good. The kitchen is fully furnished and stocked, right down to clothes, detergents and they even have washing machine and dryer with detergent. Just 30 seconds walk away, is a mini village, Turtle Village which has a Swenson (only gelato), a Coffee Club (which sells pretty excellent East/West food) and a minimart, which is slightly more expensive but carries extensive grocery items and you can just go to resort empty handed and get ready to cook some simple breakfast and maybe light lunch. For dinner, we went places but one of the best was a delivery order, apparently from a restaurant outside but near the resort. You can google for the name and food was good, costing about THB3,200 feeding 3 families of 7 adults and 6 children. Can't remember the name though. Pools in resort are great and clean. The 90minute talk was at JW Marriot, some 300 metres away and the resort looked much more exclusive. The salesperson comprises different nationalities and rather professional. They will assess your travelling needs/patterns and make recommendations accordingly. Pros and cons of signing the package you will have to assess yourself but Marriot has a brand name to protect and uphold. Overall, quite a good stay, provided you are intent on staying in the resort, which is some 20 kilometres from the main shopping areas although along the way, there are 2 TESCOs, a most overpriced Premium Outlet and a rather clean and uncrowded shopping complex call Central Festival.

author: AlvinTSingapore
title: Very spacious rooms with individually equipped kitchen and laundrette
text: Very courteous staffs who are all ready to smile and help. Service enquired were all promptly attended to. Rooms are very very comfortable and spacious. Full equipped kitchen with readily placed utensils. There is also a washing and drying machine in the room. Housekeeping is very attentive and left smiley messages which are a delight. Free and paying activities at all times readily available for guests to participate. I rented a car from a private vendor who delivered it to the hotel rather than directly from the hotel. Save me a 400$THB per day through this way. The only gripe is that resort is very far from Patong or the major supermarket and shopping malls; at least 30km away. If its raining, it takes even longer as road markings are difficult to see as well as water ponding challenges and roads are not so well illuminated in the night; this all makes it a dangerous drive especially if you are unfamiliar with the road and driving on a rented. I had to sit through a 90mins time share presentation as part of the package conditions; as the room nights were given complimentary to me. However, be up front with them if you had no intention to buy. They will be appreciative of your honesty and will instead just run you through the time share benefits and not hard sell or pressure you to buy. Thank you for that! It was an enjoyable stay in a nice property overall!

author: yahooHk
title: Go if you get the deal, otherwise skip it
text: I just went to this hotel on the marriott vacation club referral programme, where you get a 2 bedroom villa for free for 3 nights including airport transfers, the only catch being that you must attend a 90 minute sales pitch on day 3. You can also add extra nights for $150/night. Pros: The room was great for a family as there was 2 bedrooms, kitchen, living room & laundry room available. The hotel was small, so it wasn't a long walk to the pool. There was a kids club and gym. Cons: The food, beverages & service was very basic. If you do go, I suggest you plan to cook or you only eat at the coffee club at the turtlemart next door. Even breakfast! You are allowed to use the JW Marriott restaurants next door, however the food was not great there either. Front desk and concierge service was quite substandard and sometimes rude. Also service varies based on the serving staff - we received no welcome drinks or welcome gift, whereas my sister who arrived earlier in the day did. And staff could not explain why and did not care to apologize for any inconveniences caused. Concierge staff seemed uninterested in advising about packages available. Daily activities are available, but again not so organised. Diving class was supposed to start at 4 on the schedule, but didn't start till 5 as they were still setting up and it appeared that they only started once the guests arrived! Note the hotel is also about 45 minutes away from Patong and there isn't much going on around the hotel. The beach is at the main JW marriott and is on a slope. I certainly wouldn't go for the service or the food. But if you are going in a big group - the villa is great as it accomodates 6 people and is a good deal if you get the free package.

author: rbbgator
title: Fantastic Getaway
text: This hotel has very spacious rooms with a open air balcony. We shared the villa with another couple and had plenty of space. The master suite was very large with both a large tub and separate shower. Everything your need for the kitchen is provided (except for the food and alcohol of course). The second room has 2 queen beds so not to worry about out fitting multiple people. As for the hotel's location, it is very far from the rest of Phuket. We noticed most of the families just stayed around the resort or went over to the JW Marriott or the beach. They said you can't swim in the JW's pools but looked like you could just jump right in. As for the beach, it was low season so the waves were very rough and there were signs saying no swimming. You can get a local Thai massage on the beach for 400 baht (or $13.50 usd) It was great but just don't worry about all the flys around. You can get a golf cart ride to the beach but you could take about a 5 min walk. We had a vehicle so we left the area almost everyday including a trip to Tesco Lotus in town for food which is cheaper than the Turtle Village. Many of the day trips we did through the concierge at the hotel and I would recommend going through them since they were so helpful. The hotel did everything for us and most of the trips provided transportation. We did 4 excursions including 2 full day speedboat trips to Koh Phi Phi and Krabi, John Gray Sea Canoe, and Siam Safari elephant trekking. These were all fantastic and I would also recommend a trip to Fantasea and Simon's Cabaret. The restaurants were all good and reasonable along with the ones at JW. We did find an amazing restaurant at the resort Sala down the road. It is outdoor next to the beach and great for sunsets. In all, if you are looking for something different than Pa Tong and a place to relax with your family this is the place.

author: robnadcol
title: Family-friendly digs
text: As other travellers have said, accommodation here is best described as apartment-style, rather than the advertised villas. We were upgraded to the ground-floor apartment, which gives you a plunge pool and yard, instead of a balcony. My 3 kids (aged 9, 11, 13 years) loved the freedom of running in and out of the unit to the pool and resort grounds. We were also a stone's throw from the resort pool and Turtle Village next door. The deli and restaurant are right in front, as well. Very convenient! It is a compact set-up. There are 4 blocks of apartments - we were in Block 4, nearest to the shopping complex and beach access. Blocks 2 and 3 are facing the pool, reception area and kids club. Block 1 is closest to the laundry block and local eatery Uncle Lern's. For families with young children, it is an ideal arrangement. The apartments have everything you need. A fully-equipped kitchen and laundry facilities, comfortable living space, 2 bedrooms (1 king, 2 double beds), 2 bathrooms. Otherwise, it is nothing special. We noticed that only families with very young children hung around the resort pool and clubhouse. It is definitely not a 'happening' scene, and remote from all the action, nightlife and shopping of Phuket. Would we return? Not likely, when there are so many more exciting choices to be had.

author: Madeng
title: Very nice, but not exactly our type of holidays
text: We stayed for a week in the hotel. As we went by referral of a friend that had a Vacation Club program, we were offered 3 free nights in exchange for a 90 minutes presentation of the advantages of Vacation Club and we extended the stay additional 4 .We stayed not on the main hotel area, but in another area reserved for the Vacation club, but with exception fo the pool and kids club, all hotel facilities could be used by us. Just as clarification, what Marriot calls "villas" are not exaclty villas, but apartment blocks 4 storeys high. Good: -The size of the apartments is huge and they are completely equipped with all facilities, including washing and drying machine; -Cleaningless; -Adult and kids activities -They have a wide array of activities for adults, family and kids; -Service-Very kind staff Not so good: -Location-It is very far away from everything resembling local life. It is very secluded and the transportation is not cheap (see "taxi mafia"below) -Transportation-There is a "taxi mafia" that rips you off whenever you want to go out of the resort area. A return trip to phuket town will cost you 1400Baht , not negotiable because you don't have any other viable option (besides renting a car in the airport or so). You can also rent a bike at 250 Baht for 2 hours, but this is only good for small trips Price of restaurants-Absurdly expensive for thai standards Beach-Very steep and the sea is strong, whihc doesn't allow any swimming attempt and it is kind of dangerous for kids. In one of my bike trips I managed to find a couple of local restaurants that are more or less walking distance and that you can eat for reasonable price. You have to take the shuttle bus from Vacation club to Ginza (they have a shuttle bus connecting their different properties) and then walk in the road for around 5 minutes in direction of a lake. You will see a couple of local restaurants. Unfortunately, they are already accostumed to the foreigners and despite our attempts asking them to put the spice in the food to local levels, it still came very midl. But the taste was quite good. There is also a mini market nearby where you can buy some fronzen ready made food and fruits, but with limited choice. The Vacation club rpesentation didn't take 90 minutes but almost 2.5 hours, but Goran (the tall swedish guy that tried to sell us the vacation club membership) was always very correct and nice, even if in the end we didn't make business. In final, a very nice place if you like to go for a resort and stay in the pool all day, with a 5 star service, but for us, that like to make contact with local life and go around to see people, we had the feeling of "golden prison".

author: 2mchfn
title: Unbelievably Opulent - a Real Treat!
text: We exchanged our timeshare and stayed here for a week. It was so indulgent! The staff is very attentive, the rooms are beautiful, the property is designed well and allocates space to families, children, and adults (mostly), very well. They installed wireless in the room the week we were there and it worked perfectly. The beds are very, very comfortable! Our room was quiet. There are many restaurants to choose from; we eat at the Thai restaurant one night. The food was excellent, the service impeccable, the price-very, very high. We cooked for ourselves 3 nights, one night we ate at the cafe at the Turtle Village just down the street from the hotel; it was reasonable and the food was good, and one night we ordered take out from Kin Dee's; they delivered and it was excellent and very reasonably priced. The workout/spa staff organizes a bike ride; this was fun and if you like to bike, I recommend this. My sister and I also took the towel folding class which was a lot of fun. I took several yoga classes and really enjoyed these also. We did a Phuket City Tour with an operator, arranged through the concierge. I would recommend paying a little bit more, hire a taxi driver, and then you can go at your own pace, and have a better a lunch than the one provided on the tour (which was awful). We also did a long boat tour to Phang Nga Bay; it was beautiful with limestone islands, caves, etc. We also booked this through the concierge but you could hire a taxi and arrange your own long boat once you reach the dock (there were plenty) and all the taxi cabs know this location. We paid way too much money for this adventure, although we loved it, it was way over priced.

author: YorkshireCelticTiger
title: Very nice resort
text: We stayed at the resort for 5 nights. The room was lovely, clean and very well equipped. The his and hers sink was a welcome treat.The staff were friendly and helpful. The Marriott hotel next door is very nice for a drink or a meal but you can't use the pool if you are staying in the Mai Khao beach apartments. We enjoyed the lovely pool we had anyway. The sea is too rough at this time of the year for swimming but interesting to watch! The food at the resort restaurants is very expensice and the quality does not match the cost. The Coffee Club in Turtle village is excellent value for money and good quality to match. Turtle village on the whole is very well equipped to meet your needs in this quite isolated resort.We had a car and were mobile. It is easy to drive in Phuket but watch out for the motorcycles they are the biggest danger to any driver.We drove all around the island and the Big Buddha is worth a visit. I can recommend the Matoon Seafood restaurant which is on the mainland.The food was wonderful.We didn't try Kin Dee which has been recommended several times here. A taxi driver from the resort will take you there and wait for you while you have your meal for £12....excellent value. I can recommend the Siam elephant safari. The elephants are very well cared for and we enjoyed the trek. We also went to Phi Phi island on a speed boat. At this time of the year this is not for the faint hearted......you have been warned!We had a wonderful holiday in Phuket at this resort.

author: Bangkokmangoman
title: A Beach Resort Not on The Beach
text: Rooms are big. Service is good. Staff well trained but its location is bad. You have to take a golf cart or walk 15 minutes to get to the beach of this "beach resort". Also, by being isolated you have no choice but to eat at their restaurants with its over inflated prices. Just for fun, we compared the same hot fudge sundae at Swensons in Phuket Town with the hotel's, and the hotel was 40% more. Also usual BS: we wanted a cup of water but they only have $2 bottles. There is also a taxi-mafia concession which means you must use the guys parked our front who charge the highest prices in Thailand. Not phuket. THAILAND! $20 for a 20 minute ride!! In Bangkok it would cost $3. Hmmmmmmm. Who has their fingers in that pot? I don;t think it is worth it; we won't come back.
