One last point is that I have not slept as well as I have here in years...so stars for that

author: Gypsy2829
title: New but used with no soul
text: Moving to this new property from the Marriot Phuket Beach resort just down the road the first thing that struck us was the obvious signs of wear and it has only been open since March 2010! The units themselves are virtually the same as the other resort but the 'modern' aproach seems out of character for Phuket and the light coloured walls are unforgiving on the marks and bumps that would be expected in a family oriented resort. The units were spacious with a large open balcony overlooking the pool. For a resort of this size having only 1 pool is a mistake especially if there are couples and adults looking for a quiet relaxing cool space away from it all. The large balls used to accommodate children for 'running on water' fun are far too big for the one pool and more secluded space is required, preferably a deeper 'adult' pool. Being so new the grounds are still being established and given time these will be much improved. The service at this Marriot property was exemplary and the staff are too be complimented on their attention to detail and ensuring guests were well catered for. The restaurants are expensive but the coffee club in turtle village, immediately adjacent to this resort, provided good meals at a great price. Delites cafe made excellent coffee and the pastries after 6 at half price could be bought for a quick breakfast next morning. The groceries from the turtle mart are expensive, as described by many others but the cost of a return trip to another supermarket probably makes it just as cost effective to eat at the coffeee club. Staying at this resort allows you to use all of the facilities at the Marriot Phuket Beach Club except the pools. In peak season we suspect finding a quiet space by the one pool would be very difficult. From here we booked two trips - one bus tour around Phuket Island to see a range of sights and John Gray's Hongs by starlight. We chose to do a private tour to ensure a 'quiet' and informative trip. The trip was good but we were charged an additional fee on top of that quoted as there were less than four people in our party - we were not informed this when we booked. The 'hongs by starlight' trip was as good as the brochure said and is highly recommended with good English speaking guides on the kayaks, informative commentary and great Thai lunch and dinner. We would recommend this resort to friends with families but only in the low season.

author: Hongkong123
title: Playing Hide-and-Seek inside the flat
text: A true 5-star standard resort hotel targetted for families or larger group sizes. All accommodations are 2-bedroom flats in 4 to 5 storeys villas. A very spacious accommodation - one master bedroom with own DVD and TV and a big bathroom with an oversized bathtub and a shower box at the same time; and a twin bedroom which comes with its own standard bathroom - with separate dining / living area, kitchenette, large balcony and a washing room. Equipment/Facilities include 3 LCD TV sets, 2 DVD players, a full set of kitchenware and tableware. One of the activities, we have with our two young kids is playing hide-and-seek in the flat. It usually takes quite a few minutes before you can thorough search the whole accommodation - a number of times our kids just couldn't find either one of us without giving them hints - imagine the size of the flat. The pool is not huge but of a good size with everything, from bubble bed to kids slide, jacuzzi to training pool. There are enough sun beds but a bit too crowded in some parts. One main restaurant, The Zest, (buffet is served here) and one bakery, Delights, (kids will love the waffle buffet here) and one pool bar (besides pay-for drinks, cold water is served for free here) only. Kids Club is not huge either but the games variety is good for different ages. Organized bike tour to nearby locations is provided daily. You can also borrow DVDs and books here. The resort is just 15-minutes drive from the airport towards the north end of the island. It is situated near a beach which only shared by one other resort. However, it is quite far away from most other parts of the island, eg Patong Beach and Phuket Town.

author: nsfranky
title: Perfect escape into quiet, peaceful nature
text: My husband and I stayed in the 3 bedroom Mountain View chalet for 2 nights. The shoulder season prices were wonderful. We brought our own food and were impressed by how well equipped the kitchen was. We enjoyed the wood fireplace, hot tub, bbq, comfortable living space, heated tile bathroom floors and huge windows to enjoy the view! We walked on the trails to the waterfall and got lost on some mountain biking trails. We saw a total of 3 other humans during our stay and it was wonderful! Just what we needed to relax and recharge. My only suggestion would be to sign the trails a bit better, or create a new map, we never did find the rockabout loop other than a black diamond cycling trail and I’m not sure if we did the right waterfall trail because it didn’t seem like it was 4 km. We tried the easy hike too but it wasn’t well signed and it seemed like we could have walked along the power lines forever. We followed all the signs we could and we aren’t new to hiking so it was a bit of an adventure trying to figure out where we were! We weren’t in a hurry though, so it was fine and fun. I would recommend this place to anyone and would love to come back again. Maybe we would bring the kids next time. Or some friends. Or both! Thanks to Darrin for his hard work and hospitality!

author: MsKerriZ
title: Family visit for my sisters elopement
text: My family and sisters fiancés family and the newly weds stayed here for 3 nights for their elopement weekend. My parents and I stayed at the mountain view chalet. And let me tell you, that is some mountain view. Beautiful patio. Huge hot tub. I didn’t want to leave. Also I have to add, I love the that there are per friendly chalets there . I looked around the garden chalet and the Lower level of the larger chalet and all chalets were comfortably decorated and had everything we needed. I would suggest to the owners to put heavier throw blankets for late afternoon naps on the couch ;p My sister got married at the viewpoint and it was breathtaking. If you want a quiet area, this is the place for you. We had dinner at the restaurant that night and everyone loved their dishes. Ordered a few appies for the table and loved them all and then everyone picked their own dish. The main courses were huge !! I ordered the duck leg, and tried the lamb and short rib. Equally tasty. It was the perfect ending to a perfect day for our families. Looking forward to visiting again.

author: EdmTraveller101
title: Fantastic Property!
text: I'm a little late in writing this review as stayed at the property last summer in 2017 for a 5 night stay. As I arrived later in the day, reservation docs and info was left for me to access my cabin once the office was closed. Easy to do and great set up. The cabin itself (I stayed in the Garden Chalet) was incredible with all the amenities you would need to make your stay perfect!. It was a 1 bedroom with a loft area as well that also contained a king bed. Full sized kitchen and in-suite laundry were definitely a bonus as well as the BBQ on the large deck along with the amazing hot tub! Beautiful views from both the cabin and the large deck couldn't be beat and as the weather was incredibly hot while there, I spent alot of time outside throughout the day. The property advertises as being pet friendly and did not disappoint throughout my stay as I did travel with my small dog who thoroughly enjoyed the property and the bonus of a few visits with the resident dogs there! In terms of booking, I did email the property directly and booked that way-it was the best way to get all the information I needed and Kristen was an amazing help throughout. I had to make some changes and she was prompt and thorough with that. She was able to offer suggestions as to which cabin would best suit my needs and provided all the answers I needed to make the stay great! Thanks Kristen! If you are truly looking for a mountain getaway with a few "extras", this is the place to do it. Unfortunately I did not eat at the on-site restaurant so can't comment on it but it seemed to be steadily busy and looked nice on the outside. Would definitely recommend and will certainly be back!

author: KiwiandCanuck
title: Fantastic and accessible
text: This is a belated review only because I forgot! We spent a fantastic week in the Mountainview cabin, which was made mobility accessible to us with a ramp (it has mobility bathroom facilities too) Cabin was spotless and well appointed ... forgot Qtips? No problem. Hot tub has a fairly deep step up but we added a portable platform to make it three steps and family member who walks with two canes was able to use it with care. Glorious views, perfect privacy, good close access to town, which has pretty good grocery shopping. Our only regret was not eating at the on-site restaurant (lingered too long taking sunset pics in national parks every night!) but we preordered a charcuterie plate which was waiting on our arrival that was spectacular (mmm that duck confit) and had obviously had the attention of a talented chef. Staff were fantastic with booking, too. We will definitely be back. Oh, iPod music system was great but uses older non-lightning connection ... we are old with a pre 2010 iPod so had no problems. You will need an adapter to use your iPhone. Great access to national parks from here, and we were treated to a 2 am aurora display in late September, early October. Forget those chain hotels on the main road that charge almost the same price, this is the real deal ... locals who care.

author: iel0820
title: Always a pleasure :)
text: This is our second time staying in this magical place. And this won't be our last. The Cedar House has a special place in my heart as this is where my husband, Ben proposed to me in 2012. Since then, we decided that this is going to be our own romantic getaway. This time, we enjoyed the trail for a hike. Dana was informative with sharing about other guests' experience with the hike to Mt 7. Unfortunately, we did not reach the summit as it was still a bit snowy up there for my liking to hike. The hot tub was definitely a bonus to come down to after the hiking. The Green house was amazing. It had a lot of room. Everything we could possibly need, it was there. We cooked our own meal which we enjoyed doing and brought our own wine to share. We enjoyed our home-cooked meal, the view and each other's company on the deck basking in the sun setting. The one thing we liked about this place is being able to create a great bonding time. Whether it be the selection of DVD to enjoy or the board games available, it is just enjoyable as the surrounding of The Cedar House. With our short trip, we opted the restaurant this time but I'm sure my husband could have been easily convinced had we not bring our awesome food. But reviewing the menu was making us drool and we'll definitely go back there again sometime. All in all, this is a great place to stay as always to get spoiled. Thank you again.

author: bozzy20142014
title: Cedar house chalets in Golden BC , Canada( pet friendly )
text: This is a gem!! seriously ... if you want relaxation... privacy with outstanding views , this is the place to come to ! The cabins are luxurious.. everything that you need with the best quality of amenities. included are a hot tub , barbeque ... huge deck .. satellite TV ... on and on .. My husband and I stayed in September of this year , along with our dog. So an excellent place for the fur babies too... Service was impeccable.. !! Restaurant is five star!! and not a far walk from your cabin.. The town of Golden is very close by .. so not a far drive either...check this out ,, it will be worth your while....

author: wintersummer
title: Best Place We Stayed During Our Entire Trip
text: We recently spent two weeks in the Canadian Rockies. The Cedar House Chalets was the best place we stayed during our entire trip! All cottages are named and ours was the "Cedar Chalet", a very spacious and super-comfortable one bedroom, with big living area and kitchen. It had absolutely every single thing we could ask for. Dayna, the manager, was so helpful and friendly. We loved Dayna! This experience was topped off by the restaurant on the property, the Cedar House Restaurant. I'll review it separately - but the meal was the best of our entire trip! Chef Corey makes wonderful food. Annie served us and made us feel so comfortable. Chef Corey also made us a breakfast basket for the next morning (charge was just added to our dinner ticket). The breakfast was the best, with care and attention and much thought put into making a varied breakfast, with awesome presentation and lots of variety. Can you tell we really love the Cedar House Chalets and Restaurants? Our only regret is we were only able to stay one evening. It was perfect.

author: tjhouse87
title: Awesome! Awesome! Awesome!
text: I took my girlfriend to the Cedar House Resataurant and Chalets as a surprise trip the beginning of January. From the minute we arrived we were in awe. We stayed in the adventure chalet. I could live year round in one of these! BBQ and hot tub on the balcony and only a short drive to kicking horse ski area. For the price of the chalet and considering that the chalet is self contained I find this a far better , cheaper , alternative to staying right on the hill if you are skiing kicking horse. Chalet came with a nice little woodstove that heated the cabin excellent! The private atmosphere is also a bonus. There are other chalets/cabins in close proximity but when out in the hot tub , and even being inside the cabin we felt like we were by ourselves in the middle of the mountains. We went for dinner at the restaurant and hands down the best meal , and service I have ever experienced. The chef was the only person working as the servers were caught in a snowstorm in Calgary. So the Chef not only cooked for us , but he also was serving and cooking for the other 4 couples in for dinner including us. I have stayed with Fairmont Hotels and Resorts in the mountains. Overpriced for the product you receive. If you are looking for great bang for your buck , friendly service , great private atmosphere , and delicious dining then look no further! make Cedar House Restaurant and Chalets your next stay!

author: 207pl
title: Excellent accommodations breath taking mountain views
text: Couldn't ask for better.... Great for adults and children.... Lots of snow for play and skiing at Kicking Horse... Great hot tub... Built campfire and cooked hot dogs in the snow. Great beds. Fully appointed kitchen. everything was very clean...tubs showers bedrooms... Lots of room. 4 adults 2 toddlers.... Absolutely not one complaint or problem. Roads and driveway was always clean... We shoveled our own deck to be outside! And the view was fantastic! Great heated floors and wood burning stove. Everything was modern and up to date... High efficiency washer and dryer. Have stayed in Banff and Canmore this was my favorite!

author: 231AudreyS231
title: Beautiful any time of year
text: Stayed in the Mountainview Chalet in December with our son and his wife. Can't even describe how perfect this place is. The décor is modern but sports a slight country style, with everything available that you could need (coffee pot, coffee, tea, toaster, frying and baking pans, cutting board, all dishes and utensils, and an assortment of wine and champagne glasses). The bedrooms are spacious with comfortable beds boasting high-end bedding and bathrobes for everyone. This is a 3 bedroom unit. One bedroom has an king bed with an ensuite, plus there is another full bathroom as well. There is plenty of room for 4 or 6 people to cook, play games or relax with a cozy wood-burning stove ready to light, and lots of wood to keep things toasty. It's nice to know there are laundry facilities on-site (including soap) if needed. The view is spectacular, it truly feels as though you are here alone. We stayed in the Dragonfly Chalet in June 2013 and thought that was the best one, but obviously Darrin and staff have provided many beautiful chalets to offer their guests. The units are immaculate. It's obvious that a lot of pride goes into building and caring for these chalets. We felt so spoiled and pampered while we were there. We did not eat in the restaurant this trip, but had fantastic food and service during our June trip. We have again booked this unit in September, and can't wait to return.

author: CarryLove
title: Perfect place for a family reunion!
text: Our family had chosen Lake Louise as the destination for a family reunion, and I was in charge of the planning. I looked at many options for lodging all around the area, but it wasn't until I found Cedar House Chalets on tripadvisor that I was excited to consider any of them. We had four families with a total of 18 people attending. Three stayed in Sun Suite; 7, in Green Chalet; 4, in Dragonfly; and we 4 stayed in Mountain View. The four accommodations (in 3 buildings) are situated together on the property farthest from the restaurant. They gave us the togetherness we desired but allowed privacy when we wanted it. For a budget traveler like myself, the cost made me cringe a little, but now that I've experienced the well appointed chalets and the spectacular views that were ours for the 5 nights we were there, I feel that it was totally worth the price. I'd even say that it was a good value. We shared most of our dinners at either Mountain View or Green Chalet where the spaces could allow for our numbers. For our last night, I made special arrangements for us all to have a fancy meal at Cedar House Restaurant, which was a real treat! Golden and its environs offered a wide variety of activities that provided great entertainment for everyone during our days. We all made our ways to Lake Louise at some point during our stay where we enjoyed the beauty and various activities, but we all returned with the same feeling that we were happy that we weren't staying there with the hordes of tourists. We all agreed that I had found a perfect place for our family reunion at the Cedar House Chalets! The only reason that I am not giving this spectacular property a 5 star rating is because of a few glitches with my dealings with the office staff. They were all small infractions, but together, they added up to some feelings of disappointment and mild frustration for me as the planner of our gathering. Also, Darrin said that we could pay later during our stay when we arrived. This was all fine and good, but the lack of any posted office hours made the task of settling our bills more difficult than it should have been. It proved to be a challenge to luck into finding the office open and staffed. I understand and appreciate the laid-back nature of the place, but just the slightest bit more attention to detail on the business end would have made our stay a bright, 5-star experience.

author: rachelt212
title: A relaxing Getaway!
text: We stayed from Jan 16-19 in the Adventure Chalet. From everything we read, we had high expectations, and it was more than what we thought it would be! The restaurant's food was amazing! Great flavour and presentation. The chalet had everything we needed (minus a whisk and a steel to sharpen knives) :) The loft was fun as we felt like kids having to climb a ladddar up to bed. It was great! The woodburning fireplace had a never ending amount of firewood (shed out back) and was constantly burning while we stayed there. It was great to just turn off the furnace and have a natural setting the entire time! The hottub! For all the germaphobes out there, you have nothing to worry about. It's clean and clear. They have the dipsticks, so if you know how to read them...maybe we weren't allowed, but we used them, and felt comfortable being in the tub knowing it's balanced. We did have someone stop by to test it during our stay which was nice too! The neighbouring chalets, you can't even tell they are there. This place has organized and built the chalets in a way that you have full privacy. It's honestly the best place to go! Just do it! We will be back for sure. I can't imagine what this place is like in the summer!

author: RuthBoldt
title: Superb Choice for a Family Reunion
text: We recently rented the Cedar House Chalet property for a 3-day family reunion to celebrate our mother’s 80th birthday. It couldn’t have been a more perfect venue. The Chalets are absolutely beautiful—they are well-built, tastefully decorated and very clean. Each Chalet is unique and has its own character, some are a little more quaint and rustic and others a little more spacious and luxurious. All are comfortable, cozy and high-end. Every Chalet had everything we needed and more (including fully equipped kitchens, wood burning stoves, washers & dryers, irons & ironing boards, flat screen TVs, DVDs, Wi-Fi internet, card games, hot tubs, bathrobes, slippers, extra towels & bedding, etc.). The owners have really thought of everything! Our mother stayed in the Sun Suite, which was spacious and perfect for congregating in because of the additional sun-filled Sun Room. The outdoor views are scenic and we were able to get some really great family photos that we will cherish. If there was anything we needed, we were just a short 5 to 10-minute drive to town. We particularly liked the outdoor fire pit area with 13-log log stumps for sitting that is a near exact replica of the one our father built on his farm in Saskatchewan. (He built his with 13-logs stumps so there was one for mom and him and each of their 11 children). He passed in May so this was a reminder that he is forever near and close to our hearts. Our only regret is that we weren’t able to try out the Cedar House Restaurant. We are impressed the owners grow their own organic produce for use in their dishes. Fortunately for us we have family members who live in Golden so we have an excuse to return for eats. The owners left us a lovely bottle of red wine that we will be sure to enjoy. Thank you Darrin and Shannon for helping to make our family reunion a success! Ruth Boldt & family

author: LaceyL116
title: A Second Home
text: My fiancé brought me to the Cedar House Chalets on one of our first out of town dates. Everything about the place was magical and will always be considered another home in my heart. The layouts of the chalets were cozy and the atmosphere made it feel like home. The beds were extremely comfy and the fireplace was perfect. Just walking into our "home for the weekend" took every bit of stress away instantly. It managed to capture the feel that it was just us there. Darren made our stay even better. His hospitality was over the top and absolutely genuine. He went to every extreme to make sure we were happy and comfortable. Not only was the chalet the first place where I realized I wanted to spend the rest of my life with my fiancé (boyfriend at the time), but it was also the first place that we got to experience together. We have stayed there a couple of times since the first time, and every time was just as magical as the first. This is the perfect romantic getaway, and the perfect place to make memories with family and friends. The grounds are absolutely gorgeous and the view is unreal. I would not change a single thing about this place and it will always hold a little something special in my heart. Best mini vacation ever.

author: exploringismypassion
title: AMAZING
text: So we were looking for a place that we could go, take the fur baby, and relax. We found it and did NOT want to leave! From the moment I booked the cabin to the moment we left we had an exceptional experience. We spent a while looking for a pet friendly, private cabin. My husband found this place and after reading reviews we decided to spend a little bit more and book this place. And it really is worth the money. The cabin we stayed in was called the Garden Cabin. As we entered our new home for the weekend we were amazed at how clean, tidy and the fantastic quality this cabin offers. Shannon had left us a note explaining about the local bear that had been seen that morning so we were extra careful around the grounds as we had our dog with us. After we had settled in we went to the office and met Shannon in person. She was extremely polite and friendly. Nothing was too much bother. Shannon made us a copy the walking map and told us the best paths to explore. She even offered the can of bear spray just in case. After a nice walk and some hot tub time we did nothing but relaxed. So much so that we didn't want to get ready for the meal at the restaurant. I am glad we managed to find the motivation to go as the food was excellent. All in all a perfect getaway and we will be returning.

author: JohnB379
title: When is a destination not just a destination?
text: When is a destination not a destination? …When the accommodations are just as spectacular as the destination! Once I checked into my chalet, I must admit, it was hard for me to leave. Cedar House has 5 Chalets and I spent two nights in the Garden Chalet. Never once did I see any neighbours, I had all the privacy I could wish for. What I did see was a beautiful property teaming with tall evergreens and majestic hardwood trees. From the Jacuzzi Hot Tub on my balcony I saw snow capped mountaintops, and running streams. The interior of the Garden Chalet was nicely furnished, spacious, and clean. The kitchen came equipped with a full size fridge, stove and dining area. In the living room I found a most comfortable sofa, rocking chair and a wood stove that eased me into peaceful quiet evenings. And for anyone so inclined, as I was, you will enjoy the full size flat screen wall mounted television and complimentary wireless Internet. I slept upstairs on the 2nd floor loft. The space is absolutely surreal. Spacious is another word that comes to mind, but then, so do the words “peaceful” and “serene”. The bed was comfortable, the linens crisp and clean. The Garden Chalet was all and more that I could have asked for: private, spacious, clean and with friendly staff and lovely amenities. I look forward to visiting again soon. John B

author: Jezebette
title: It was nice.
text: My family and I recently stayed in the Sun Suite. It was adequate for one night. The unit is clean and well equipped. It was very hot when we arrived so we turned on the portable A/C unit in the futon room. While that room was comfortable the other two bedrooms were extremely warm. There is only one bathroom so you will have to decided if this will be an issue. You share the building with the unit upstairs so it is semi-secluded and the view nice. You see more trees than mountains. We had dinner at the restaurant that night. The food was excellent but service was extremely slow considering there was our party of five and two couples on the deck. We waited with dirty appetizer dishes in front of us for almost an hour. Our meals came almost two hours after ordering. As I said the food was very good and tasteful. The menu is limited so check it online before you go. It was a nice dinner but after all the reviews I had expected more.

author: AprilU90
title: Private Anniversary Celebrations
text: We were celebrating our wedding anniversary - looking for private accommodations and were attracted by the hot tub on our own deck. Upon arrival, we were quickly greeted and toured the Cedar Chalet. At first we were underwhelmed by the 'privacy' as the restaurant was right next door and the hot tub on the back deck had views of two other chalets. But we were pleasantly surprised as shortly after we settled in, we did not see or hear other persons our entire two night stay! It was wonderful! A great place to spend our anniversary. Our own kitchen allowed us to save expenses and travel time, by dining in. The restaurant next door proved a tasty choice for a celebretory supper. We especially appreciated the non-alcoholic beverage list. The Cedar Chalet itself was comfy with everything we needed, and we spent much time hustling out the patio door to soak in the hot tub. That was our favourite part. Cable was nice to relax on the couch. We both enjoyed our weekend, and would return in the future. Also appreciated the environmental consciouness of the owner. Great rates.

author: KimBottles
title: We were tempted to just move in and stay
text: We stayed in both the Sun Suite and then Adventure chalet on Sept 21 and 22, 2011. The sun suite was brand new and even almost too spacious for just the two of us -- but we managed! Full kitchen very well supplied with the necessary utensils and tableware. Excellent wi fi connection in the suite.Nicely furnished. Very deep bathtub But we fell in love with Adventure Chalet. Cute, cozy, charming, with everything close at hand --even leather place mats! Owner Darrin had laid a fire in the wood stove to welcome us back from our day in Yoho (but there are electric heaters as well). We didn't use the complete kitchen for dinner that night as we went right next door for an excellent dinner at the on-site Cedar House restaurant. Max and Sabine were charming, and the food was first rate -- the filet and a pork chop, well matched with by-the-glass suggested wines. The bed in the chalet is up a ladder in an under-the-roof loft, Very comfortable -- we are in our 60s and had no trouble negotiating, but the toilet is downstairs and older folks might think twice unless they are very spry. No one should think twice about using the hot tub on the deck -- super private and with a view of the Purcells. We are not enthusiastic hot tubbers when needing to share with strangers, but we loved this one and its privacy! Darrin is continuing to expand the property. It already has nice landscaping and excellent maintenance, but we could see the vision that will make this even more lovely. We would definitely recommend it to everyone wanting a warm welcome, a quiet place to stay with all the comforts. You will not find nicer people than Darrin, Max and Sabine!

author: Casado182
title: Perfect - Can't say enough good things
text: Stayed in the Adventure Chalet at Cedar House. Perfect getaway for the family. Great chalet with a quaint little loft, full kitchen, full bathroom, wood burning stove, living room under loft, and available hot tub. Learn to stoke the wood burning stove properly and it's atmosphere makes for a great night. Lots of room for my wife and I and 2 yr/old. The scenery was awesome with Kicking Horse right out the main window. A few trails around for walking or hiking. The staff was amazing as well. Friendly, personable, and accomodating. They shared with us their dreams for the future of the land. Loads of potential. They were willing to take us on tours of their other chalets and answer tons of questions about their new Green Chalet (which is "green" environmentally). We always had wood waiting for us on our porch without even asking. Little details were everywhere. Because of the time of year the restaurant was not open for us but we hear good things about it and look forward to returning when it is open. We will definately be returning in the future.

author: Beaugosse33
title: Almost great
text: Overall very good experience, but not perfect. Few of my complaints were: İn general breakfast was fine, except for the quality of tea and walnuts. They were poor. i booked a superior room and it was great. my only complaint there is the toilet paper. İt is very thin and not very good quality. Sunday morning after breakfast i went to the lobby to have a coffee and enjoy reading the newspaper. But at 11 am vaccum cleaning was done at the lobby ! very noisy, hence could not relax. Management should pay attention to cleaning hours. Spa employees should respect the duration of massages. İ took the Sultan scrub and massage which was supposed to last 45 min. However lasted only 30 min. İ don't care how busy the spa is. They work on appointments and charge 5 star hotel fees. Mr.Tezcan (spa employee) tends to rush treatments.

author: HOSTAN
title: Sometimes it is not sufficient
text: We stayed in Crowne Plaza Bursa, with our 1.5 years old daughters in two annexed rooms. We also had the exclusive floor option. The hotel is new and comfortable. The front office is very welcoming so are the staff in the exlusive floor. On the other hand you do expect also a good standard for the Spa and technical service. For ex; The door between the rooms had a problem, we called the technical service. The reply was; "the technical service is allowed to come to your room when you are there". It means that you should spend your time waiting for the handy man to come to your room to fix the door :) The time of the arrival is ambigious. Oh yes... That's why I am on holliday, for waiting the technical service instead of enjoying my day somewhere else. Insisted in an undecent tone, we persuaded the fixing to be done when we are away. Then in the spa. We had a problem with the appointment. As the guy responcible to take it, was not listenening to me, he gave the appointment to someone else on the phone. Then he tried to fix it saying that, he'll try to recontact the other customer to persuade him to change his appointment. Oh yes... That's why I am on holliday, for waiting the other customer's decision. The next day when arrived to the pool there were no towells. Solved quickly but It gave an idea about this area of the hotel. So, the hotel is new, well furnished and have features and facilities but sometimes it is not sufficient as it comes to a management approach.

author: Forensic99
title: Very nice but a little far from downtown
text: We had a nice couple of days in the hotel. We'd been staying in budget hotels (as recommended by guide books) in Turkey and wanted to finish the trip with a couple of days in nice surroundings. My brother was keen to stay in an upmarket hotel that had a pool. Well the Crowne met all of these expectations. The room was nice, wifi good, the restaurant was quite good with a wonderful view (you might ponder at the heavy freeway traffic at 8 pm that you can see from the terrace). The hotel is situated near a large shopping mall that you can easily walk to (hint you can buy your grog/alcohol at the large department store and have your cocktail hour in the hotel room). We enjoyed the hot spa pool and the indoor pool, it was nice to relax after the rigors of travel. The breakfast was also nice, the best we had in Turkey, it consists of the usual international hotel fare. In particular the young woman at the help desk, was, as the title suggests helpful. She organized cabs to out of the way places etc. She even said 'goodbye' as we left. A nice touch. The only minor grip was the hotel is situated about a 15 minute (~20tl) taxi trip out of downtown. As far as I could figure there is no public transport to and from the hotel - could be wrong about this though. Overall, very nice but a bit out of the way.

author: toddrI172MD
title: AVOID AT ALL COSTS
text: This was the most infuriating experience I’ve had traveling in many years on the road. I arrived at the hotel at 2:30am after a long day of travel only to have no one there to check me into this hotel with a “24hr” check-in policy. I waited outside along with another guest who was locked out after a night on the town. Both of us rang the buzzer and repeatedly called the front desk with no luck. Finally after repeatedly shouting for someone to let us in, a third guest woke up and opened the door. I was then left for additional hour in the lobby with still no help. While there, I was forced to play door man and let 5 other guests in.....luckily for them because they would have been locked out. Finally, at 4:30am, someone from the hotel came to check me in without an apology and with nasty attitude. I asked for the managers phone number or email address and she gave me the wrong address. I stayed in the dingy, unclean, and out of date hotel with for a grand total of 5 hours before waking up and checking out. The man at the desk in the morning was nicer, but also no help. He did give me the correct email address which I used to send an email that still hasn’t gotten a response. I can’t overstate my anger with the management of this place. If you’re looking to have awful customer service at an even worse hotel, go ahead and book. However, dont be angry when you are locked out only to hear that the person at the desk stepped out to “get something to eat” at 2am.

author: Suyling
title: Last Resort Hotel
text: Let me just start out saying the best thing I can say about this hotel (if you can call it that) is that it is very close to the beach. We realize that San Juan is still recovering from the recent hurricane, but most of the conditions in the hotel were not related to any weather issues. At check in I wouldn't say the person was out and out rude but he was very short. The elevator did not work properly, you have to step up or step down to get in/out of it. The room was very barren. I'm not sure the floors were cleaned as they were very gritty. The TV did not work (looks like it took rain damage at some point). There was no phone and the safe was a rusted box with no lock. There was no smoke detecter in the room and my husband was very concerned about this as he is a volunteer fireman. The bed was like sleeping on a piece of plywood. We got no sleep. We thought breakfast was included, but sadly no, we did eat at there little cafe and the food was okay. They told us after the fact that check out was 11 am but the website stated 12 pm. Its a good thing this was only booked for one night as I'm not sure we would have survived staying longer. It is very sad that the hotel is in such condition, because it could be so much better. Also, surprising was the fact that FEMA workers are staying there, in those conditions.

author: cassandraa815
title: You Get What You Pay For
text: Pros: -The hotel itself was right on the beach. I loved being able to go outside and be there. -The staff were able to be personable with me and very welcoming. They were extremely nice and helpful, as well as honest. -They allowed us to check in early which was a PLUS! -The price was good and cheap. -You are in the heart of Condado with lots of things to do in the area. Cons: -They have elevators to take you up, but you have to take the stairs to come down. The hotel has three floors and we were on the second. While this was fine for me, this may not work for someone with bad knees. -They say they have free wifi, but the wifi DOES not work in the rooms. It only works on the first level where you checkin and outside where they serve breakfast. That was inconveinent because you want to be in your room relaxing and using wifi, not downstairs. -They say they serve free continental breakfast, but it is more of a bed and breakfast. The free meal on consists of your basic eggs and toast with a side of bacon, boiled or scrambled eggs, eggs and a side of meat, or frenh toast with bacon. Those are your four free options. If you want something other than that, you will have to pay. That was sad to find out since they advertised continental breakfast. -The area accross the street has a sewer hole that overflows with smells of sesspoo and bathroom backup. Nothing they can control but it's nasty.

author: Jsm10029
title: Not as described
text: Booked this hotel for a couple of nights before leaving to my cruise. Upon first sight, looks alone would've made me cancel if it wasn't too late to do so. The hotel is run down and looks dirty. Staff was ok but only seemed like one person was running the whole place. My room was located on the lobby which was way too basic. A bed and a tv and a tiny bathroom. No fridge. The AC was located on top of the bed and dripped water all night. Woke up to a water bed. I was however credited back some money. The restaurant located inside the hotel didn't look clean. The beach is located a few steps away from the beach. No pool. The waves at the beach were rocky. Definitely not for the smaller kids. If I had to choose, I wouldn't stay here again. For a couple of more books you can stay across the street to a much better view, room, refrigerator and pool which is what I should've done. This hotel needs a major improvement but for just a night or two I guess it would be ok.

author: sarahelizabeth000
title: Sandy beach motel san juan
text: Let me start off by saying this is not an upscale hotel by any means. So dont go expecting this. However! it is a cute little motel only a few feet from the water. Me and my roomate went for a week and paid about 89$ a night for a single twin bed room. It was all that was available and due to uncontrollable circumstances we were not able to stay in the hotel we actually booked for the week. It was literally a few steps from the beach. Very small room but this did not bother us. We are from Michigan and in February it is covered in snow. So anywhere warm would do for us. Also we are 25 and 26 so sleeping together in a twin bed didnt bother us either. They did have bigger rooms but we wanted to save money. It was right in the middle of the tourist area. We have never been anywhere like this and she had never been out of Michigan, they front desk was extremely friendly and helpful. They pointed out many things for us to do, and our last day there our flights werent until late in the evening so instead of having to pay for another day they let us leave our bags behind the desk and we just walked around and hung on the beach for the day.They even let us use a shower to wash off and get dressed to go to the airport. We are planning another trip soon but taking our little ones and will absolutely be looking into staying here again just a bigger room. It was by far better than a 89$ room here, and and way more doable than the 300$ a night room a block away. If you are looking for something fancy this is not for you. However if you are just going to be a beach bum i saw nothing wrong with the place.!!

author: mim2000
title: Good location, but worn out
text: We stayed for a week. The location is good, right next to the beach. But the place is worn out. Our air conditioner smelled of mold. There is no fridge in the room. You can grab ice from the icemachine at the ground floor. One evening it was very windy outside. The seiling plates in our room were lifting themselves and bits of insulation material was falling down all over the room. The room is cleaned every day. There are 3 desk clerks working in shifts. One is very helpfull, one is friendly and one doesnt care. There is a common area where you can sit and eat your own food. There is a microwave oven that you can use. Outside is a small resturant where you can have breakfast. If price is your priority, this hotel is fine. For my preference, I would rather have payed a little more if they would maintain the building better.

author: Jesssell
title: If you are looking for a hotel in Condado, keep looking
text: If you are considering this hotel, you should really keep looking. Let me start by saying the walkway to get up to the hotel is horrible. Try carrying luggage up this ramp while its wet, impossible. The only good thing about our stay is that the front desk clerks were helpful and friendly. Once inside the room, we couldn't believe how rundown and beat up everything looked. The AC unit was literally about my head about a foot while I slept. By the end of our 3 night stay my throat hurt. There was a poster dated 95' hung on the wall...that just shows you the last time the furnishings were updated. The TVs volume would randomly stop working. So you'd turn it up to max and nothing would come on, then when you'd turn the TV on the next night you were in for a rude awakening when it decided to work. Surprisingly there was a safe in our room. $2 a day to get the key and a $50 deposit. The funny thing is if someone would kick the safe it would probably bust open cause of how rusted out it was. Oh and good luck with the Wifi. They kept saying apple products just wont connect to it meanwhile no one could. This definitely is a budget hotel. We didn't expect it to be anything special for the price and location, but it could at least be clean without stains everywhere and dirt in the rooms. This hotel is in major need of renovation!

author: CynthaDelTorro
title: Inexpensive, mostly clean, perfect location
text: We stayed here for 5 days in February. The location is perfect. Steps from the beach, a block from Condado Ave and a short bus/cab ride away from Old San Juan. Our room was small but had everything we needed. The room was clean, but the bathroom could have been cleaner. I actually bought a sponge at the Walgreens down the street to scrub the sink myself. As in FYI: no wash cloths, no blow dryer. The window air conditioner was old and a little loud, but it cooled the room well. The closet was large, but there were only 3 wire hangers in it. We got more from the front desk. Our room, 301, was on the south side of the hotel (not the ocean side). The noise from the bar next door was very loud on Friday and Saturday night. I would recommend a room on the other side of the building. We travel with ear plugs so that solved the problem. The wifi router was right outside our door so the signal was great. Overall we had an excellent stay at the Sandy Beach. The staff was friendly and the price and location were great. This is definitely a budget hotel. We just needed a place to sleep on this trip and this hotel fit the bill perfectly.

author: ktwldwomn
title: Overall "Okay"
text: Spent two nights of a 5 night vacation here. The staff was wonderful and very helpful with tips and suggestions for a first time single lady traveler in Puerto Rico. If you're looking for chain hotel amenities this is not the place to stay. If a very basic room for a place to sleep and shower is what you need then this will be just fine. The location is fantastic...just steps from the beach where you can rent a chair for $5.00. Walking distance to restaurants and shops. Walgreen's was a handy 1/2 block away for purchasing forgotten items and snacks. The area is lovely and I felt safe at all times-even at night on the beach. The breakfast was somewhat "continental" if cereal and grocery store pastry is considered as such. The only entrance to the room is the hallway door so if you're looking to enjoy some outdoor space you'll need to head up to the open air terrace on the 4th floor. Wasn't impressed with the cleanliness of the room. Areas of the bathroom could have used a more thorough scrubbing. Felt encouraged to spend as much time out of the room as possible which of course is what the vacation was intended for. But after 2 nights the room started to feel incredible claustrophobic with no private balcony, etc. so decided to move to the Caribe Hilton for the remainder of the trip. Now that place is amazing! But another review...

author: JennyK843
title: Dirty!!
text: From outside, very quaint & attractive. Beach is only a few hundred yards away, very close. No parking. Room small but dirty. Outdated doesn't bother me, dirt does! Dusty, mirrors & pictures look as if they hadn't been cleaned for months. Ratty towels, no bathmat. Floor dirty & some bugs. Dirty finger prints on bathroom tiles. Footprints on my pillow cases! I requested for fresh sheets & pillowcases and changed it myself. Bed was crappy. Pillows were very stained, luckily had my own to use. Didn't use bedspread for cover, I would only skieve (gag). Dusted the top of my headboard myself. Lamp shades dirty & disgusting, with bugs. Continental breakfast ok. It's a shame, the place is quaint, very close to beach and potentially could be so much better. As I said, quaint and outdated doesn't bother me, but dirty, there is no excuse for that!

author: Heather886
title: Good for its price and location
text: It’s a decent budget hotel in a good location. It’s one block from a 24-hour Walgreen’s, Starbucks, Charlie car rental office, and the Marriot (the latter where we saw a live salsa band and dancing late Saturday night). There are lots of restaurants of all kinds in walking distance. It’s a good neighborhood with other hotels and condos. The fact that the hotel is one building away from the beach and not directly on the beach is irrelevant for beach access, because it’s on a dead-end street that opens out onto the beach. The hotel even has an outdoor shower, for its guests to rinse off the sand. If you want an ocean view, however, that may be difficult. (It’s not the best beach for swimming because the waves are kind of big. It was also very windy. But it was still clean and pleasant.) If you need a parking space at the nearby pay lot ($10), you can request to reserve a space. The breakfast is minimal but better than nothing: cold cereal, milk, pastries, white bread (and toaster), butter, jelly, orange juice, and two kinds of coffee, but no tea or hot water. Free wifi was accessible from our room. A rollaway bed fit into our room. The owner is friendly and helpful. There was some noise of music from the pub/restaurant nextdoor, So, I recommend requesting a room not on that side or just close the windows and use the A/C. (We like fresh air so we had the windows open.) The A/C fan is a little loud.

author: KayinKy
title: One night stay before cruise
text: My husband and I stayed one night before a cruise. This hotel was a great value for this purpose.Much less expensive than other hotels in the area. It's about halfway between the airport and the ship port area.( Ten minute cab ride for each portion). It is just steps from the beach and night life. Although we were only there from 9pm to 11am we were able to have a great dinner at the Green Tree restaurant (highly recommend) and enjoy the beach the next morning. We felt very safe walking in the area. The hotel itself is quite old and old style (small lobby and hallways and elevator), and a bit worn. However, we found it to be clean and the staff very friendly and helpful. As mentioned in other reviews, the towels were a bit worn and mismatched, but smelled fresh and clean, as did the sheets. Room and bath were very basic, but did have flat screen, wall mounted tv and again were clean. Comfortable, newer mattress.Slept well, but a bit of noise from next door nightclub and window AC unit. Small outdoor courtyard for breakfast. Light, minimal continental breakfast. Cab station within steps to grab taxi. Would stay again for a night or two, but not extended stay. Great value as long as you can deal with basic, no fancy frills.

author: 137kayb
title: Poor hote choice
text: I stayed at this hotel for one night only and i was only too happy to check out . The name "hotel" is a misnomer since there is none of the usual amenities of a hotel. Just the room and a small place to have breakfast. The place is very untidy ,the linens were dingy and when we arrived there was a man in the room assigned to us fixing something in the roof of our room. he left all the debris on the bed and floor . We demanded another room and it was granted. That room was somewhat cleaner but the towels were still dingy. Better towels were provided when we asked. A little bit of paint and attention to the potted plants will go a long way to improve the ambience. I was dismayed to see all the plants dried up or partially dried up! The TV did not work well as we kept losing the signal. The A/C was very noisy. The saving grace of this hotel is its location about 15 minutes from the airport and from Plaza Las Americas. It is on the beach so the sea air is refreshing though swimming will be a challenge for all but very good swimmers. The breakfast was satisfactory as continental breakfasts go! The staff was cordial . The Sandy Beach Hotel should be renamed Sandy Beach GUEST HOUSE. This will prevent disappointment.

author: Bomby211
title: Great value for the money!
text: We went to Puerto Rico on a tight budget. Knowing we would not be staying at our hotel to just sleep, wanted to find a hotel in San Juan that was clean and beds were comfortable. This fit the bill. The continental breakfast, was okay. Plenty of Puerto Rican coffee. I booked through Booking.com and got a great rate if $85 per night. The hotel is a stones throw from the sandy beach of Condado. You can walk to a number of shops and restaurants. As for parking, this was very limited. They have two spaces available at near by gates parking for $10 per night with deposit. You've got to ask for that parking. Otherwise, you pay $18 a night to park at Marriott across the street. Our room was back up to the bar next door. The bar next door played music till all Hours but was muffled by the air conditioner, so did not keep me awake. I'd recommend if your looking for an inexpensive, friendly staff, hotel where you can sleep at night.

author: bigfern
title: Don't expect much & you won't be disappointed . . .
text: This is a back-packers paradise! Great rates & right on Condado Beach. However, very limited ammenities, so don't expect too much. The rooms are clean although they are dated. Beds were very comfortable. Hotel staff was eager to assist in any way they could. I would call this hotel "quaint". When I was a child, my family used to stay in side-of-the-road hotels, and this hotel is reminiscent of those days. Plenty of restaurants near-by, bus stop about 1/2 block away, within walking distance to a lot of things, beaches, etc. All-in-all, we really enjoyed it. Was it a five-start, no. But what it lacked in elegance, it made up for in character. Will I stay there again? If circumstances were the same, yes. We stayed pre-cruise for 4 days & bunked with another couple, so we had fun. However, if we stay longer in Puerto Rico, we will go with finer accomodations.

author: Asanchez61306
title: Don't be fooled
text: It was in a very nice location. Close to beach and main street. However, don't be fooled by the pretty pictures. You have to pay extra for parking and the parking is around 2 corners and halfway up the block. Not convenient at all. Front desk gave us a key for room 303 that didn't work. Had to go back down stairs on the rickety elevator. Got the correct key and up we go. Once in the room we found 2 large dead palmetto bugs and one crawling on the AC. We turned the AC on and the sound was horrendous. It sounded like a truck motor in the room. Back down we go. Got switched to another room. This one had no bugs but smelled musty. I pulled back the comforter only to find blonde AND brown hair on my pillow. I was so disgusted we had to sleep on top of the comforter. I would never recommend this place.

author: jazapsu
title: Not What I Imagined
text: First, if you look at the picture of the hotel, you will realize that the building on the left has been eliminated. The hotel is close to but not ON the beach. Usually, I'm just happy with a clean room for the price. Not this time. I booked the Sandy Beach for pre- and post-cruise nights. The first night, I was in room 303. The bathroom sink had no plub, the towels were so threadbare that you could almost see through them, the shampoo containers had broken seals and were half full. The windows were filthy, there was sand on the floor, and the room smelled musty despite the window air conditioner. The final night, I was in room 102. No phone. When blowing the thick dust off of the clock/radio, I sneezed. No phone. The room is located right next to a common area where a party was going on until late at night. Since you can hear through the walls...enough said. To print out my boarding pass, I had to give all of my information to the desk clerk. A new printer had been installed, and the clerk didn't know how to use it at first. I left to have dinner, and when returning, the desk clerk said that he needed my information again. I did get the pass. Next time, I will pay the extra and stay at a hotel not billed as a "cozy bed and breakfast." That's a misnomer unless the definition of "cozy" means something different to different people.

author: RickyB
title: When you aren't paying for five stay quality, don't expect it.
text: Stayed here from January 13th - 15th. Was way too late for booking a hotel in Old San Juan so that we wouldn't have to drive or pay expensive taxi rates to go to Las Fiestas de la Calle San Sebastián, the Carnival in Old San Juan. Fortunately, Sandy Beach had an opening for a quadruple room. Plus tax, we each paid $60 for a two night stay... which is reasonable considering the taxi to the area where we live would pretty much be the same and much more of a hassle. It's a small hotel, no frills. It's true what they say about the elevator, too many people and you might break a toe when stepping out of it (it wont be level with the floor). The room had the essentials, we bought water across the street at Wallgreen's and kept in the room for emergencies (no fridge or anything of that sort in the room). Flaw: service. We had a quadruple room but it only brought 2 towels... asked for two more and it took two hours and a few calls for them to actually bring them. Would I stay here again? Yeah. Again, if you aren't paying for five star quality, don't expect it. You get what you pay for, and a bit more considering it's in such a great spot in the heart of Condado.

author: Susan964
title: Deeply disappointed
text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel several times when it was El Canario by the Sea and we were very pleased. Based on those experiences, we recommended the hotel to friends. We were very embarrassed to see how the hotel had deteriorated in a few short years. Where to begin? We and our friends booked identical rooms yet when we arrived they had a mini-suite and we had a room so small we could barely walk around the bed, which was almost in the doorway. After protesting, we were provided with a larger room almost identical to our friends' but lacking a small writing table. After many requests, I gave up asking for the table, but we had to argue with the desk as to whether we "deserved" the larger room. By the way - the large room was no treat. There was little hot water, the room was cleaned only occasionally, and we had to keep asking for towels. Oh yes, and the ceiling tiles kept falling down. A continental breakfast was provided but, after the first day, pastries and bread were never replenished so that by our third day everything was stale. Pluses? The hotel is steps from Condado Beach, half a block from the bus to Old San Juan, and quite convenient to Condado night life, restaurants, and shopping. The rooftop terrace offers a wonderful view of the beach and is very relaxing after a long day of sightseeing. Still, unless you are willing to see this hotel as simply a place to change clothes and sleep, you should avoid it. There are plenty of other options in Condado.

author: adonald291
title: "What a dump"
text: As guests who have stayed in this hotel under the previous management, we booked our stay in May for eleven days and requested the same room which we had stayed in for the past ten years.We were very dissapointed when we arrived and were told that our room was not ready. We were put in another room which also was not cleaned. The room had dried blood stains on the floor, the shower had hair and other debris in it, towels were dirty and smelly , the mirrors and wall were dirty and the quilt on the bed had a big hole in it. We had to clean our own room in order to feel comfortable in it. The next day we were then given the room we originally requested however, there were no towels. When we complained to the hotel manager she told us she was only the secretary, apparently she was too embrassed or ashamed to admit that she was the manager, and said "these things happen and an early reservation does not guarantee a specific room " eventhough the it says in the computer " do not move guests from this room" .. Our reservation was made with the niece of the owner who was the one who noted that we were not to be moved from our requested room. Over the next ten days we had to clean our own room and change the linens and towels. The one maid they had came in when she felt like it or not at all, one day she showed up at 5 PM to start cleaning and only stayed for half an hour. There was garbage left in the halls, the ice machine was broken and kept beeping all night which kept you up along with the noisy air conditoners. The guide books that gives guests ideas as to where to go, and what to see were in the rooms but were dated from 2008, the current copies were hidden in the emergency stairwell and not even displayed in the lobby. Then you might not be able to read them while in the lobby because the front door was so salt encrusted I was surprised that any light filtered in from the outside. I could go on and on but there isn't enough space to tell you how disappointed we were with the place. It got to the point that we were recommending other hotels to guests who were about to check in. After hearing our horror story they fled. The only plus was the front desk staff who were plesant. If you want a pleasant experience while in San Juan avoid this dump at all costs. I would recommend looking at any of the other Canario hotels which this one used to be. To quote Betty Davis "WHAT A DUMP"

author: brodycooper
title: Very disappointing experience!
text: My sister and I had booked onto a Princess cruise out of San Juan and needed a one-night stay in a hotel hoping to do some sight-seeing before boarding the ship the next day. I had booked one night on-line for Feb 6th 2 months ago secured with my Credit Card and confirmed by El Canario By the Sea. It looked like a very cute and cozy B&B right on the ocean and was very reasonable in price. Unfortunately our flight from Toronto was delayed due to storms in the U.S. causing us to miss our connection in Newark, and we arrived very late in San Juan at almost midnight. We were hot and tired and after a $25 taxi ride we arrived at El canario where we were told there was no room for us despite having the e-mail confirmation with us. There was no explanation for this and we were told we would be sent to another "sister" hotel called Coral By the Sea which was back at the airport area. They even wanted us to pay for the taxi ride again but we insisted they should pay the driver at the very least. Needless to say we were very angry and disappointed. The hotel they sent us to was in a very run-down area and looked terrible from the outside. There was no water pressure at all from the shower and the floors were uneven, there was not even a matress cover. You can be sure I searched high and low for signs of bedbugs. All in all a very unprofessional establishment - we were never even offered anything for our trouble and inconvenience. I would definitely not recommend this hotel to anyone as it seems they cannot be trusted to honour their e-mail confirmations. C.S. & J.B.

author: PatMcS
title: Never Again!
text: I have been to Puerto Rico numerous times and will always go back. BUT I will never stay at an El Canario Inn. This practically ruined our trip. The price looked good for our budget this trip. Well, we got less than what we paid for! The elevator never stopped properly so you always had to watch your step. Our room was very small and has not been updated in 50 years! Drop ceiling that would flap up and down if we opened a window. Cracks in the wall. No hangers in the closet. Broken unusable safe. Beds not made properly, with sheets never changed, we knew this because there was always sand in our beds. Old tile floors never vaccumned. Tiny, tiny bathroom with no counter space and very weak shower pressure. A bag with new toiletries was taken! We had to ask for toilet paper everyday of our stay!!! I can go on but I won't...False advertising!!!!!!!

author: Jeannie1717
title: Exceptional Location
text: We stayed here for two nights while traveling throughout Puerto Rico. I am a "clean freak" and was a little nervous about booking a "Non chain" hotel. We were pleasantly surprised to find this hotel more than met our needs. The location in San Juan can't be beat for beach, restaurants and shopping. The only down side was the extremely limited parking. We ended up having to park at the Marriott across the street which was 18.00 a day. El Canario is not a true 3* hotel by US standards, but was clean and met our basic needs. If you stay here, there is an awesome Italian restaurant right down the block that is quite interesting. It is a very busy, not fancy at all, but excellent food and fast paced atmosphere. There are other choices nearby but we noticed that this place always had a crowd. We liked it so much we went back twice! The service is excellent also, Back to the hotel. It is an older building so the rooms, bathrooms, etc. are a little outdated, but workable. Small bathroom, limited space, but clean. I would recommend this hotel if you are on a budget and want a clean, safe place to stay while in San Juan. If in the mainland, I would rate it a 2*.

author: TejasTraveller
title: Don't Expect Anything Special
text: Stayed there three days with a friend and everything was fine until the last day. Our toilet did not flush and we contacted the person at the front desk who told us to go get the plunger across the hallway. We walked across the hallway and didn't find a plunger. We told the person at the front desk this and said that we would be out for the next few hours and that they could come into the room to fix the toilet. When we came back, we asked if our toilet had been fixed and the guy at the front desk said that it was still not fixed but that he had called the manager. They then came to our room later that night to give us the plunger. Then left us to fix it ourselves. No manager came. No repair person came. Just the same person at the front desk. Since this was late at night and we were leaving in the morning, we decided to just tell the manager in the morning that the toilet was not fixed. When we told the manager about how unhappy we were about our room that night, she said that we should have told them that the toilet was not fixed (we did more than 5 different times that night) and that it was OUR fault for not asking for another room. All we wanted was an apology for the inconvenience. This place is ok if you don't mind the loud noise from others in the hotels, the strong smell of bleach everywhere, and substandard service. For twenty more dollars, you should try to stay at one of the other hotels in the area.

author: srafnel
title: Don't Expect Four Stars
text: I stayed at El Canario with my mother for the weekend of March 29-April 2. The hotel was exactly what I expected. Yes, it has its bad points: -Age: It is an older hotel, and it shows. The rooms are outdated and open to outdoor hallways surrounding a courtyard. -Size: The rooms are small, and the bathrooms are cramped. -Breakfast: Limited options. If you are planning on using the breakfast as a full meal, forget it. For a cup of coffee and a pastry, it is perfect. -Insects: We saw a few palmetto bugs, but this is a tropical location. The bugs disappeared after the first night and we never saw them again. However, the plusses outweighed the minuses for me: -Price: About $200 cheaper than nearby hotels -Location: The beach is just steps from the door. It is in the middle of Condado with shops, restaurants, and a bus line to Old San Juan within 3 blocks. -Staff: The second shift staff was FANTASTIC. They were able to book a snorkeling excursion for us and reccommend the best ways to go to Old San Juan (the bus), the Bacardi Factory (the ferry and a publico), and El Yunque (car rental on Ashford Avenue). Add to that, they were very friendly and seemed to recognize everyone staying in the hotel (a plus for security!). In summary: This is a fine place to stay. If you expect a luxury experience, you will be disappointed. If you are on a budget and do not mind an older hotel (with its inherent problems) you will enjoy El Canario.

author: readytogoSoOregon
title: Motel 6 with older hotel charm
text: We chose this motel because it was reasonably priced ($134) and not far from Old San Juan and the pier for our cruise ship. This was not a room you would want to spend much time in; very small, no comfortable chair, tiny portable TV, noisy air conditioner, but it was not dirty. We never could get the safe to work. Our friends' room was better all the way around although price was the same. I was kept awake the first night by a screaming woman. The next morning we found she lives there and just goes off occasionally. There was a lot of construction going on in the area, so there was that noise as well. The beach was about 100 feet away, but we were advised that it was not safe because of the winter surf. There were only a few surfers on the beach. The continental breakfast consisted of cereal, rolls, fruit and juices. Good, but no protein. The patio was small and thankfully walled which helped soften the noise. The location was convenient, with the bus stop being only a block away. The fare to Old San Juan was only $.75 and even less for seniors. At age 75 you ride free! (Taxis were $12.) Within just a few blocks were the usual fast food places (Burger King, Wendy's, Baskin Robbins). Walgreens is just 2 blocks away and has a food section. I would stay there again if my plan was to sightsee all day and just sleep there. If you plan to spend much time in your room, this is not the place for you. El Canario by the Lagoon which is very close looked nicer and might be a better choice.

author: Rizzie_02
title: Infested and bad customer service
text: I recently stayed at this hotel for 4 days 3 nights after finding that the Marriot was completely booked. It had to be my worst experience ever in a hotel. There were roaches crawling in the clock as well as on the bed, when I aproached the front desk with this information they apperared very nonchalant as if this happens all the time. He stated he would call the manager and let me know what he could when she called back. After speaking with the second person at the front desk later that night they told me they could change my room assignment. I went to look at the second room and there were roaches in the bathroom. The person at the front desk informed me that maybe the second floor was infested(both rooms were located on this floor). So I was then told to look at a room on the third floor. (It was 10:30pm on a Friday night and there were no rooms available at the surrounding hotels) This one was okay and the front desk personnel changed me to this room and told me to speak with the manager in the morning, he warned me that she was awful with customer service and he was right this was the worst experience with customer service I had ever seen. The manager had a thousand excuses why there were roaches in the room (i.e. other guest brought them, this is the carribean what do you expect, etc.). She informed me that all hotels had roaches and it was no reason to be upset. She was very rude, hostile and unprofessional. And to top it off she began making smart comments about the situation to guest checking out, as if it was a laughing matter. She did give me a 10% discount for 2 of the 3 nights I stayed (she stated she would not give a discount for the third night because I did not see roaches that night, just baby lizards in the room). All and all spend the extra money to stay at the marriot and book early they fill up fast. Maybe the other Canario hotels are better I can only judge this particular hotel's customer service. Also the hotel is pretty nasty and needs some major repairs. The good thing is that it is steps from the beach, but I would rather walk blocks than to stay here.

author: Travel-n-Buppie
title: It wasn't horrible
text: I read almost every review before I left for my trip. But I went against the reviews and decided to stay there anyway, I need to see for myself. I stayed for one night before my cruise, and I paid less than a hundred dollars. The room was so tiny, the bathroom was almost non exsistant and I took a shower with my filp-flops on. It was what I expected, based on the previous reviews. The area is an up and coming area in San Juan. The beach is extremely close and beautiful. The area is nice, going thru a renavation though. In a few years it will be hard to get a room here, because of all the new hotels and resorts they are building in the nearby areas (within walking distance). Old San Juan is really close, either a $.75 bus ride or a $12 cab ride. Old San Juan is nice, lively on the weekend, especialy on Sundays. I stayed in the Sheraton in Old San Juan after the cruise ( I wrote a review there as well). If you are staying for a night or two, I think it is worth the money. And if you just plan to use your room as somewhere to sleep then it is not that bad. If you like the luxury of the a nice room as part of your vacation, then I would not recommend it. The worst part of this whole El Canario Inn/Sea stay was that I orginally reserved my room at the "Inn" and when I called to confrim my resevation two days before my arrival, I was told that my resevation was moved to the "sea." The "Inn" was closed for vacation. And no one contacted me about the move. I am glad I called. AND when I wanted to cancel my reservation at the "Inn" for after my cruise, I wasn't able to do it at the "Sea" I had to wait and do it myself when they opened.

author: WisconsinVagabond
title: Best Price, and on the beach
text: This was the most inexpensive hotel in the Condado beach area that had acceptable reviews on TripAdvisor. For our Dec. 8-11, 2005 stay, we paid the [--] Internet rate of $80, plus $3/day Energy Charge, 9% tax, and $2/day for room safe key. It was clean, and well located. There is only one condo building between this hotel and the beach, but that tall building blocks the ocean view from all rooms except those on the front of the hotel ($90). Our room was somewhat small, but adequate. The continental breakfast in the courtyard offered abundant sweetrolls, muffins, bananas, coffee and fruit juice. Our credit card was not charged until checkout. Limited overnight parking on the street in front of hotel. The only downside of this place is that there is no luggage storage room for pre-checkin post-checkout. You are to leave your bags sitting in a lobby room, which all guests pass through going to and from their rooms. Although it is next to the front desk, the receptionist can not see into the room to watch the bags. A sign says you can leave bags there, but they are not responsible. We would stay here again. FYI - there is a cheap Internet cafe about 1/2 block north of the hotel on Ave. Ashford.

author: missmlock
title: A little slice of heaven!
text: A group of friends rented a cottage at this resort for a week and it was one of my best decisions! We enjoyed the beachfront family cottage, loved the resort grounds, and the beach! Often found myself looking around, to realize that I am the only one on the entire beach! I enjoyed the Amihan winds in Feb. It was perfect weather while we were there. I learned how to kite board with Donald, and it was an amazing experience! Instructor Donald was so patient with me, and taught me how to do a water start. We spent many hours around the pool, pool table, dining area, beach, hammocks, sun chairs, and the porches. Not much time in the cottages other than sleep, but we definitely enjoyed the outdoor shower. The outdoor shower was one of my favorite things! The staff was very friendly and nice, the manager, Pete was very helpful with setting up activities and transportation into El Nido. The staff of this resort are superb. I was definitely really sad to leave this place. ...*still sad. Thank you for sharing your happy place to the world! In order to write a full review, I must include some Cons: 45 min drive into El Nido, $80 taxi round trip... Didn't necessarily mind the drive, I think $80 for transport might be a little excessive. Dive tours and island hopping limited to weather, especially during Amihan wind season. You may want to consider priority of activities with weather when booking this resort.

author: Lessismaura
title: Simply wonderful!
text: This place is paradise! We were a little worried about being an hour away from town for four nights, but it turns out we had the perfect balance of activity and relaxation here, and never felt we needed to go back into town (though we hope to go back to explore more someday). The days were long, relaxing and fulfilling, with yoga, reading, swimming, SUPing, kiteboarding, massages, games and more. The yoga space even has TRX straps and kettle bells, so we could do yoga in the morning and another workout in the evening. We took the boat out for snorkeling and a private BBQ lunch on an island and it was lovely— a great meal and totally worth the reasonable price. After doing an island hopping tour in Coron (surrounded by other boats and tourists) it was great to have a quieter island experience. Apart from the beautiful, impeccably maintained grounds and villas, the other winning feature of this place is the staff. The service was perfect, literally, and the employees seem to truly take pride in their work and feel shared ownership for this place. This is not always the case when a resort pops up in a rural fishing community, and is a testament to the thoughtfulness of the owners and managers, who were very present, pleasant and helpful. It is also very sustainably run, with solar power and other green features. Because outside food is not allowed (no cooking facilities in villas and lots of critters around the grounds) we were also worried we’d be stuck eating the same thing from a mediocre overpriced restaurant (per poor experiences elsewhere). Not the case! The Qi restaurant was excellent, reasonably priced, and had plenty variety and lovely fresh ingredients. Even after four days, there were plenty of things we still wanted to try. And, unlike other resorts that gouge you to constantly buy bottled water, our cup runneth over at Qi. They would constantly refill our glasses and brought cold pitchers of purified water to our room at least twice a day, alongside twice a day cleanings. For our departure, we had an early flight out of El Nido but they arranged to pack us a sandwich to go, and brought coffee to our villa as part of our wake up call. They truly went above and beyond to make our stay wonderful. If you like nightlife and don’t love the idea of vibrant hummingbirds flitting around your outdoor shower, this may not be the place for you. If you like comfort and serenity in a wild place and appreciate attention to detail, Qi Palawan is for you!

author: mermaidgaby
title: Low price value
text: The room is bamboo wall and wood NOISY FLOOR. We understand that is wood and it could be noisy, but you can fixed it actually, the floor it was not even they made the floor that is why it was noisy, we have wooden floor in my resort but we do not have noisy floor even the house is too old. Good point is Quite, design are good, food is very Expensive but at least tasty. Service was very good in our first arrival, I like the reception lady who welcome to us buy she forget to inform us about the SAND FLIES...
