Everything from handicrafts to apparels to foodstuff are sold here by the local kundasang villagers as well as nearby other nearby district traders...plus the landscape around the tamu is equally breathtaking... My room was very clean though though basic. No fan or AC was necessary at all throughout the night as the area was chilly but comfortable. One thing to remember: bring snacks and food of your own as minus the Friday tamu, there is absolutely nowhere to find food (except of course if you order room service or go to the resort restaurant). The restaurant caters more of chinese-styled cuisines (and halal) and if you want western meals, you need to let them know. The prices are pretty steep but you will not have much of a choice if you're hungry...Small portions are at RM 15.00, medium is at RM21.00 and large portions are at RM 26.00 per plate (as at May 2012). The breakfast at the resort is so-so...eggs, toast, sausages...the usual fried noodles with tea/coffee and juice.... Other than that, for entertainment, there's a TV avaliable with local channels but HBO, ESPN and CNN if you decide to just do nothing but relax in your room. Make prior arrangements to the kinabalu park and other attractions if you like on your own. I requested the reception to make arrangements to the park on my behalf and i must say it was very expensive. A whopping RM95 return trip from the kinabalu park to the resort. Overall, I did enjoy the entire trip and I plan to visit again. This time with friends and with preparation regarding trips and snacks....oh...did I tell how spectacular the view is in the morning?...;) Enjoy your stay...

author: bugsy12
title: Good place to chill out..
text: Kinabalu Pine resort is a good place to come with the kids and just chill. Its very different from the rest of KK so having done the beach, islands, city, animals etc, this was a welcome change. Weather is pretty cool (around 18 - 21 degreed when we were there) and the little "chalets" are really quite cute with big large porch to enjoy the view. Interior however, is very basic. The rooms are really small and come with two small twin beds. Bathroom was pretty ugly although fairly clean. I had to add an extra bed and it did not leave much room for moving around. The room rate comes with breakfast and dinner for 2 at the Pines restaurant. The breakfast was acceptable with a small buffet spread. We upgraded our dinner to the "steamboat" (cooking your food by dipping hte food into hot water) that night which was pretty fun. Staff at the restaurant are very friendly and helpful. Spectacular views of KK mountain more than made up for everything. Get up early to watch the sun rise and see the mountains from your chalet. It really takes your breathe away and the kids enjoyed the change in climate and environment. Travel around the area and check out the Kundasang area. It is completely different from the rest of KK, with fruit farm, milk farm, tea plantations etc - its a lovely area and very different from the rest of KK. You can drive and park here as I saw a lot of local families drive in with their cars and park.

author: sg_globetrotter89
title: Lovely View and Cosy Cabin
text: My friends and I drove up to Pine Resorts and were charmed by the cosy cabins, well equipped with hairdryer and electric kettle. As the resort does not have any supermarket nearby at night, an electric kettle is imperative for boiling water to cook cup noodles! We spent one night at this resort We arrived there in the afternoon and had a convenient parking lot right in front of our doorstep (rented a small car). On a side note, please rent a car to get up there instead of taking a taxi as you would want to explore the area (Dairy farms, fruit markets, war memorials, strawberry farms) in the day. The resort also has a small rabbit enclosure for children to get close to the rabbits. Do ask the reception area for a map so that you can get around. Woke up early next morning to catch the sunrise and it was really cold! Bring warm clothing. We managed to catch a glimpse of the hues only, as the clouds were blocking the sun. Nevertheless, that was beautiful enough and we had a great view of Mount Kinabalu's peak from our cabin's balcony. The view from the cabin is lovely, unblocked, and you suddenly feel like you are in some other winter country (See photos)! One warning for people afraid of insects: the bathroom's panels are not airtight and insects and bugs do make their way into the bathroom at night. You could try to prevent this by spraying repellent around the window, or just turn the light off so that they will not be attracted to it. There was also a cat which kept meowing right beside the bedside window, which kept us awake, but went off after a while. Breakfast was buffet, nothing fancy but nothing to complain about either. Checkout was likewise a breeze, and on the whole it was a pleasant experience, especially for the very reasonable price!

author: burnerz
title: Superb place to stay to have scenic view of Mount Kinabalu
text: My family made this trip in December 2010 and I chose to stay in this hotel. I have never been to this part of Malaysia before nor had I been this hotel facilty. What attracted me to this hotel is that it's well described promotion and it's among the cheapest during that season. The best part is that I can choose which block I want to stay. So I chose the one facing the mountain view. I have no regrets staying there. The room was clean and neat. It did not come with an air conditioning unit (why need one when the air is cool 24/7) and it was comfortable even during day time. Parking area is sufficient although you may need to drive up steep path to your parking bay. However, I have an issue with food. It's quite difficult to find shops offering food that I am familiar with. The hotel itself has a cafeteria but has limited choices. My advice to those planning to stay here: bring along some hot beverages sachets and make some simple sandwiches. Unfortunately, cooking is not allowed in the room. What I liked best: LOCATION What I liked the least: FOOD That's all I have to say about Kinabalu Pine Resort. If you are coming for the view, this is the hotel I recommend for you! Have a nice vacation!

author: pteropus
title: The one disappointment in an otherwise great holiday
text: My expectations for this hotel were probably too high before arrival (having read the reviews on here and looked at the website) but having climbed the mountain and stayed in very cheap (10GBP) hostel type accommodation the night before I was expecting more of the Pine Resort for 30GPB/night. For one thing, this place should not have resort in the title as it is very misleading. It's very small - approx 20 log cabins on a hillside, one small restaurant (more like cafe), one very small shop, which was generally closed, and a bar, that was always closed. The restaurant only serves chinese food, which is very cheap but was very poor in comparison to the hostel food we'd had the night before. Be very careful if you are vegetarian as there are very few options and even things like vegetable soup invariably have chicken in. Also don't expect to be able to order a beer as the only restaurant is Halal. Unfortunately there are no other options for food or drink nearby so you must rely on the hotel for this. The rooms are very basic with very old looking bathrooms. You need to plan ahead with a shower as the hot water needs half an hour to heat up but will then only last long enough for one person, which was really frustrating. The walls and ceiling are very thin and you can hear every thud of a person walking around in the room above. The tv only has 3 malay channels, which all have pretty poor signal. If the weather is bad there is nothing to do here but sit in your room. Internet access is not available in the rooms but there is one hotspot near the shop. The hotel can organise a taxi for you but it would be cheaper to walk left out of the main gates and up to the main crossroads to arrange a taxi youself. This hotel really only has two things going for it - a fantastic view of Mount Kinabalu on a clear day and the war memorial, which is a 20min walk from the hotel and well worth a visit. Overall it was a real let down due to its isolated position, poor food with very little choice, basic accommodation and staff who barely acknowlege you're there.

author: kukuhamster
title: nice view
text: The room was so-so.... but the view is magnificent. the resort has full view of mt kinabalu. Its a bit far off from kinabalu park, but i bet u cant have full mountain view from kinabalu park resort. Do ask for block P, its the standard room block but its the best block facing the mt. during my stay, the peak covered by clouds. only during dusk and dawn we could see the peak. but it was great... really breathtaking, its a must do thing when u go to kota kinabalu. To go to kundasang, its a 2 1/2 hr drive, we took a cab. From hotel they wanted to charge us rm 180++, we turned it down and decided to walk to merdeka field (taxi station) from our hotel at kk ( 10mins walk). The Taxi driver in merdeka field only charge us rm 20/person to get to pine resort. WOW!!! from pine resort also we asked the reception to arrange for us sharing taxi from ranau, so it only cost us rm 20/person. If not pine resort wanted to charge us rm 163.

author: DoraemonCute
title: Horrible experience
text: This was a most lousy hotel in my life I have ever stayed. Hotel scenery and view was nice and quiet. However, many flies I can see in restaurant. When I took my lunch in Pine restaurant, we were sitted in open area but our seat was under roof. It real a good scenery but many flies were around us. Food was nice also. However insert was dropped to my soup when we suddenly heard things drop inside soup. We looked up to roof there have many lizards!!! I have no intend to check what was inside my soup as it was a horrible experience. This was not the worse issue. The main problem was our bedroom..We were stayed in room N2. We feel happy and relax when we entered our bedroom. Pine resort was cool as around 15 degree. We thought we will have a wonderful night…Who’s know that we feel hundred of itch in our body. We keep applied insect repellent but that itch cant be remove and it more worse hour by hour. I guess it was bug or called "pasat"....I think Pine resort shouldchange their matteress and bed as it too dirty. It was a horrible night for us..

author: mrsflorencegoh
title: Great views of Mt Kinabalu
text: This is a 2-star hotel. It has won many awards, especially for landscaping. We stayed here for 2 nights in June 2007. When Mt Kinabalu is not shrouded in cloud, we can see this majestic mountain while lying on our king sized bed, watching TV, sitting at the balcony of our room, or just walking around the beautifully landscaped hotel grounds. It's worthwhile to come to this hotel just for the great views. On top of that, you get peace and quiet. An entrepreneurial massage/spa company drove its van to the hotel and we chose 2 masseurs to give us foot reflexology and body massage right in our hotel rooms (no hanky panky). Location: If you come from Kota Kinabalu, you'll pass the Mt Kinabalu national park entrance/turnoff, then Kundasang village, then the hotel. At the village, you can buy fruits, vegetables, etc. But they did not taste very sweet. Cleanliness: The hotel room is clean, the hot water works. The whole Kundasang area has lots of flies. This was the only thing that bothered us. Other services: We booked at 3D/2N package and were chauffered around to visit Mt Kinabalu National Park, Poring hot springs, War memorial, etc by no less than the Hotel Manager himself! We ate all our meals at the hotel and even though it was a 'conducted tour', we decided what to eat, and also told the driver when we wanted to come and go.

author: 277shereneb
title: Much better then the first time
text: This was our second time around staying at Le St Martin Laval. Two years ago we also stayed here for 5nights. This time it was only 3 nights but we had a Grand executive suite that was superb! We had a few complaints last time but they were handled very professionally! The only reason I didn't give 5 star review is because we felt that the reception staff was a bit distant. Checking in went well but was very short and to the point... No friendly smile... It was more like taking care of business and who's next.... Checking out we were not asked how are stay was and if everything was to our liking. Again a kind of distant approach. A pity because guests like to feel welcome and cared about during their stay and that's where they missed their mark. Apart from that everything was top notch. Room was beautiful, clean, enough space. Breakfast is as mentioned, good but not a lot variation. A lot of great restaurants in the area especially at Centrepolis.

author: Desaril
title: 2nd and 3rd visit all in one trip
text: So I had a reservation for a grand lux room with the whirpool tub in it for 8 nights. This part of my stay was great. We were happy with the room, I was a bit put out with the tub, I think I had higher expectations for it, but it was great once we got it working. So overall, this part of my stay was 4-5 stars. Now, the rest of the stay. I had an issue with my airline, and my flight was delayed to go home, so much so that I ended up staying over in Laval one extra night and leaving the next day. The front desk agent was great, she was able to get me into a room on short notice with me just giving her my name since all of my info was already in the system. Check-In was a breeze and I was able to relax for my unexpected stayover. Now on to the issue: Around 10pm, my boyfriend and I had taken showers, and were preparing for bed. I pulled the bedclothes back and there was a.....stain, on the sheets. It looked like someone had passed gas, and left a mark. I called down to the front desk, she was apologetic, and offered to send someone up with new sheets. The houseman was very confused when he arrived and thought the sheets were for the pull out couch bed, and I had to show him the stain. He was also very apologetic and offered to help me change the king size sheets since my boyfriend was still in the shower. We were able to get them changed and he stated multiple times that he was going to let the front desk know what the issue was etc. When I left the next morning, my boyfriend handled the checkout since the night was on his card, and when I was looking at the receipt, it seemed we were still charged full price. I guess I was just disappointed that there was not even a small discount for the dirty sheets. I would like to say, that this was overall my second time to stay at this location, and I had stayed at the Montreal location 3-4 times as well, and this is the first time anything like this has happened, so this is not a common occurrence with this hotel, I guess I just had higher expectations because of previous visits.

author: 2monkeys
title: Very Enjoyable-Would definitely return
text: We stayed at this property for 1 night on March 16th while travelling to Montreal. It is very conveniently located right off the highway. Check-in and check-out were most efficient. We were greeted with very friendly bilingual staff. We were given a very good Government rate. This Hotel shows beautifully inside and out. We had a room with 2 queen beds that was spacious and nicely decorated. The beds were comfortable. Lots of pillows and nice bedding. What I loved about this hotel room was that there were lots of bath towels in the bathroom...unlike a lot of hotels that just give you 2 bath, 2 hand and 2 facecloths. They also provided hair condtioner that you don't always see in other hotels. The room had a stocked mini bar with beer, wine, Baileys, pop, water as well as chocolates, peanuts, snacks to purchase. The hotel provided free parking, wifi and breakfast which was included in the price. The breakfast area was very well organized and run. The two ladies replenished food items regularly. It offered scrambled eggs, boiled eggs, waffles,3 different types of bread for toasting, bagels, yoguart, croissants, cereal, tea, coffee, juice, fruit and loafs. Check out is normally 11:00 am but we thought we may require an extra hour or so, as we were there to pick someone up who had an appointment in the area and they graciously allowed us a later check-out free of charge. We ended up not requiring it but we appreciated the fact that they were willing to accomodate us. This hotel is in an area that has many restaurants, stores, malls all within walking distance or a very short drive away. I would definitely stay at this location again and I wouldn't hestitate recommending it to others.

author: patrickcV3628UE
title: Horrible service
text: Simply horrible and robotic service. I have to admit the room was very nice and comfy bed. But our Experience was completely ruined by how bad we were received. It seems when my girlfriend and I arrived they took us for teenagers despite our thirties, with the condescending looks and the way ALL staff spoke to us. Even the manager. After check out we go up to the room and find the maintenance guy removing all the alcohol from the minibar and putting it in his garbage bag!!!!! He was called by reception to remove all commodities. He took the little welcoming chocolate from the bed table!!!!!!! We didn't say anything as we had our own champagne and were planning an evening out anyway, but my significant other was insulted. The next day we go for breakfast and come back up to the room to find our access cards not working. We go back down to activate them, the manager at the reception explains with a fake smile that it happens sometimes (for both cards at the same time!!). To be honest it is such a nice hotel. But the service and client experience doesn't seem to be a priority. Third time we go there and always a horror story. It was the last!

author: LarryLFL
title: Quiet, Convenient, but not without frustration
text: Upon check-in after a 6-hour drive I really wasn't in the mood to even be here. A large wedding party was taking place and a misunderstanding on my part caused a great deal of frustration concerning the noise level. All said and done, we got to the room and found the sleeper sofa opened and fully made, ready for someone to sleep. Of course the chair is in the middle of the floor and it's hard to get around. Why this was, I have no idea. This only added to the frustration. A call to the desk brought someone to put the sleeper sofa back together. The beds are comfortable, the price is good, the location is excellent, although the GPS built in to the car did not recognize the address. Google maps, however, finds this hotel right away. Breakfast, included, was disappointing...toaster waffles, lots of bread/pastry and cereal, standard powdered scrambled eggs but NO MEAT..."sorry we are out of bacon, sausage, ham or whatever... Parking is more than adequate and the room has a single serve coffee maker. If you drink coffee like I do, that's simply not enough and at 6:30 in the morning, your only choice is the "oh so convenient" McDonalds just on the corner very near the hotel. The staff is...in my own words...cordial. The stay, at least for me, was pretty typical, but I've certainly stayed at other properties that were much more pleasurable. Will I stay here again? Probably not, I'll most likely try to search for a different hotel on my next visit to the Laval/Montreal area.

author: VeberC2
title: Great hotel in Laval!
text: First of all I want to say that this is a great property and I want to comment on some other reviews. Staff is very friendly if you show some common courtesy. I actually spent time with a few of them in the front desk and the breakfast room with a great conversation. Very nice and always available to answer any questions with a smile one their face. The cream cheese does not have pork in it. There are plenty of packets of cream cheese in the basket to the right of the pork condiments. All countries have different condiments and different tastes for what is considered appropriate. I have been to different countries and there are some items that I did not like but I would never criticize another countries culture or tastes because it is was not what I am used to. The best part or travel is meeting new people and experiencing new cultures. The outdoor pool is actually a oversized jetted tub. It is not the size of a couch. When I was there, there were 14 of us in there and I would say it was about 1/3 full. As far as only given 5 minutes to move your vehicle, I would say that that is all it should take. Driveways should never be blocked. There are two large shopping centers very close to the hotel for all of your needs. Yes they try to sell items but it is not any different that any full service hotel or cruise ship. I will end my review here, but if you have any questions please contact the me. I will give you an honest answer for any question that you may have. Would I stay there again......absolutely!

author: VarshaG551
title: Looks can be deceiving
text: I was actually impressed by the size and looks of the place at first. It was well furnished and nice-looking. That faded a bit when we went up to the front desk. The guy there was pretty rude and got upset when he realized we parked our car near the front of the hotel, when it wasn't even near the entrance. He gave us 5mins to move it. The room was comfortable, but way too expensive and everything had a price. I was surprised when a small chocolate placed by my bedside was priced at $5. Breakfast the next morning was in a buffet form, and was pretty decent. (Cereal, oats, buttered croissants, bagels, eggs). The lady in charge of the breakfast was very rude. I bumped into her and apologized, and she glared and walked away. I asked her what was in the white packets, and she said cream cheese. I opened one and found it to be full of pork! The lady also started cleaning breakfast up 10-15 minutes before the assigned time. The service was very dissatisfying. When we went to see the pool, it was very well decorated but the actual pool was the size of a big sofa. I was very unimpressed by the experience.

author: Lets_Cruise_13
title: Great Place to Stay
text: The St-Martin Hotel Laval is situated at 1400 Maurice Gauvin Street in Downtown Laval. It is considered a modern boutique hotel and is very close to the main highways 15 and 440. On November 28th 2014, my wife and I stayed for one night on a 5th floor King Classic room. As advertised, the room is stylish and includes a king size bed, an armchair, a working desk with Wi-Fi, a small fridge mainly for drinks and a mini-bar that we did not use. It also has a very small coat closet. The colour scheme of our room was of golden beige with darker buffs which makes it rich looking. The king bed was very comfortable with its four pillows. The large screen Samsung HDTV is very nice and clear but make sure to keep the volume under 8 because it is easily heard from the corridor. The free outside parking is ample enough and well lighted at night. The view from our room was directly above the parking lot and of the commercial and financial areas of Laval. The modern washroom is of a good size and has a large glass shower. It has a granite counter, a wall attached make-up mirror, a Keurig coffee maker and provides all the main washroom necessities. The hot tub/pool area is near the reception desk; that area is cozy but the pool is small and the water could have been a little warmer. There are no restaurants in the building or stores of any kind. On the main floor is the continental buffet breakfast area; the next morning our gourmet breakfast was delicious, warm and plentiful. At $120.00 CDN plus taxes for a King Classic room with free Wi-Fi, free parking and with a continental breakfast makes it a reasonable and a good choice for travelers or shoppers in Laval or for the central Montreal area. We would certainly recommend Le St-Martin Hotel Laval to friends and family. Their toll-free telephone number is 1-866-904-6835, the local is 450-902-3000 and the web site is available at www.lestmartin.com.

author: Jake427
title: Nice suburban hotel
text: Stayed 3 nights in Laval. First time to the area so I did considerable research prior to selecting this property. Research paid off. Hotel is very clean, quiet and beds were very comfortable. The setting is nothing to write home about as the property is next to a car dealer, McDonalds and a couple local restaurants. A car is likely needed here as metro is fairly far and only a few restaurants within walking distance. Other restaurants nearby near mall and Centropolis short drive away. Breakfast was excellent. Eggs, while not cooked to order, are real eggs scrambled. Variety of other breakfast items including some healthy options. Front desk staff was friendly and greeted me with a smile. Hotel GMs should understand the importance of a good team at the desk. This sets the tone for the stay. The staff here was good including housekeeping. I would stay here again without hesitation.

author: NancyDayton_Ohio
title: Excellent!
text: Its a great place. Its a small hotel. Room 133. It was quiet. Room clean, updated. Shower very clean. Oldish style with dim light. Newest coffee machine in the room. Big screen TV. They have no restaurant, only a bar but walking distance (3 minutes) they have McDonald and Burger King. Our room had a frig full of drinks and snacks, a little expensive. Small jaccuzi we didn't use but look inviting. French-kind-of-breakfast, it was one of the few clean breakfast table I saw in a long time. Scrambled eggs, waffle, fresh fruits (apple orange banana), wheat and white bread, bagels, croissants and a slow coffee machine. I thought it was a great presentation. We would go back.

author: Vito_Andolini_C
title: "With Class and Savoir Faire" The Chapiteau a must experience in Laval
text: Stayed at this property in 2 weeks ago for a family wedding and had the time of my life. I travel all around the world for work purposes and stay in hotel very often, but this property does it with class and professionalism. The property looks and feels like a European castle. Upon arrive the front office staff was very welcoming. I had booked a suite in the executive tower, it was very impressive,clean and comfortable. We attended our family wedding that was held in the Chapiteau in their hotel garden. The setting is beautiful, bellisimo!!! They have this large tent they call the Chapiteau for weddings and parties surrounded with palm trees, Jacuzzi pool, decorated garden. It is something to see, a real oasis for weddings. The wedding was out of this world, the food was fantastic, the banquet staff was professional with a 5 star service. If you get a chance go see the bartender he really know how to make is drinks. We had the time of our life. I have not attended a fantastic wedding like that in years. I would definitely have my wedding there. The gourmet breakfast was very good the next morning. I loved their lounge/bar, its relaxing and you can enjoy a drink while watching the hockey game on the giant screen. All in all the hotel was excellent. They know how to host and take care of their guests with a lot of "class and Savoir faire". Great Hotel, I would without a doubt recommend it to every one looking for an upscale place to stay. Bravissimo

author: bobs582
title: Excellent value for your money...
text: All: I have been traveling between Toronto and Montreal on business and pleasure for some time now. While at Montreal, I always make a note to stay at the Le Saint Martin hotel in Laval. The rooms are outstanding, all amenities are provided, beds are comfortable and the down-filled plows are fantastic! Lately, they have added even iPod/iPhone docking stations and I am elated playing my own music while on the road! What surpasses the above is the customer service. Staff are always available to help, deliver on-time and, during my last trip, they even made a downtown Montreal itinerary for me for best restaurants and clubs. I asked what is good and the staff provided me with locations, phone numbers and directions. Thanks to them, my Montreal evening was amazing, thanks to their gusto and suggestions. While they all deserve a round of applause, It would be a disservice not to mention at least two names: Alex is always available for a chat and a good conversation late in the evenings. Crystal at the front desk, she's always available to meet and surpass demands with customer requirements square and centered. Congratulations for excellent customer service to all the staff at Le Saint Martin. Kudos to the hotel's senior management team for excellent choice of human resourcing. They all make you look great! You have earned a loyal and repeat customer. Bob Sachsenidis

author: mmv686
title: nice hotel but ...
text: We have stayed at this hotel a few years in a row for my husband’s Christmas party which is held in a near-by reception hall. I will echo what others have said concerning no sidewalk. The drive way slopes down to the road and the road also slopes down to the main road. This can be very slippery in the cold weather and difficult to walk on. The breakfast is now advertised as a gourmet breakfast. I would call it an enhanced continental breakfast with boiled and scrambled eggs. Very nice but gourmet is overstating it. The room we had this year had a dingy carpet. Rooms we have stayed in the past had nice wood floors. In the past bathrobes and slippers were provided – something they seem to no longer provide. As others have mentioned the wooden legs on the beds are a danger. We both hit our shins on them. We did not sleep well due to noises coming from the hall. We were woken up several times. Someone mentioned stairs leading to the breakfast room from the lobby. There is an elevator right next to the stairs that take you to the breakfast room so it is accessible to a wheelchair. It is a nice hotel but we don’t sleep well in it.

author: andrewc623
title: Good Value for a Great Hotel!
text: Hotel Le St. Martin was an overall great experience. The hotel itself was very warm and inviting. The staff was also very helpful and spoke both English and French. The room was clean and it included a fully stocked bar. We booked this hotel about 1 week in advanced and were still able to get a good deal. We found that booking just outside of Montreal one could get more bang for your buck. BE WARNED though that your cell phone [if it is an American Carrier i.e. Sprint, Verizon] WILL NOT WORK once you cross the border without incurring additional fees. This means that your GPS will not function either. Your first order of business should be getting a map! The hotel also included free breakfast every morning which consisted of Croissants, bagels, cereal, eggs etc. and also Free WIFI, which is a savior if you are using a smart phone. Bed was great, food was great and the staff was very helpful. Would stay here again if I am ever in the area.

author: AlbertaDaisy
title: Nice hotel small workout room
text: Stayed here twice now for business. It is a very comfortable hotel. Free parking for those who are driving. Service is great - there were umbrellas to borrow when it was raining outside. Breakfast is included. The bar in the evening is nice as well with a fireplace, large television and lots of seating to relax. If you are looking for a restaurant, you will need to venture out of the hotel. Beds are very comfortable. Bathrooms are clean and modern. They have nice seating areas and include a throw to keep warm while curdled up in a chair to watch TV or read a book. I also liked the Keurig in the bathroom and must remember to bring some of my K-cups for my next stay. The only downsides to this hotel was that the WiFi doesn't work in all rooms, as there are two sides to this hotel. The first time I stayed, I had great WiFi reception but was in the older portion of the hotel. In the newer section which is quite far from reception, does not receive the WiFi signal. I was ok with it as I have a good plan with my cellphone carrier. The service is excellent and I would definitely stay here again if I am staying in the area.

author: Ruby5549
title: ALL BUCK no bang... Fend for yourself!
text: We were looking forward to this overnighter at teh St.Martin in Laval as our house was being painted and my husband who has terrible respiratory condition had to leave for 24 hours. well at first we upgraded to GrandLuxe,room was clean looked great we had access right away from parking ,the tv(circa 1980's) is very fuzzy the remotes don't work well and the concierge says not to worry they are upgrading to plasmas in Dec.. that doesn't help us.. after going out for supper returned to find ELEVATORs from 4-6 don't work. had to walk long lobbey to get to other elevator to go to 3rd floorwhich stops at 3rd as we were in the new addition and then my husband had to walk up two flights of metal stairs to access room. after that we smelt \woodburning stovesmoke coming from hallway. NIght auditor was no help and quite rude!offered to vacuum the air from our room. in the morning, YEP had to ask front desk to call us when the elevator would be working as we couldn't go down for breakfast without taking the stairs. Gourmet complimeatray breakfast was nothing great,cold eggs and no one even cleamed our table from previous guest, BY the way everytime we asked to speak to a MANAGER there was no one to help! he\ll be in next Tuesday is the reply. LOng story short I had to haul all my luggage from the 4th floor down to check out of this nightmare! recoomend this ??? only if you like pretty things that don't work. even shower was hot and cold......can't wait to speak to the MANAGER on Tuesday. very uncooperative staff there.

author: Jess_H-Town
title: Very nice hotel for a 3-3 1/2 stars and very good value
text: It was a long weekend get away. Our family was at the Le St-Martin for one night and it’s was a very enjoyable stay through out our time at this hotel. Both the exterior and exterior of this hotel is nice and very clean. I love the outdoor pool and the indoor hot tub. It would have been nice to also have the indoor pool. However, the outside pool is very nicely designed. The beds are very comfortable. The staffs are very helpful and friendly. Continental breakfast buffet is also including with the stay so that is a bonus. Not too many hotels would offer this without extra charge. The only down side about this hotel is that it's too far form Montreal downtown. Other then that, it was a very nice stay and I would come back the next time I’m in Montreal. After we left this hotel, we went to Quebec City where we stayed at the Times Hotel & Suites and this hotel is rated a 4 star but it's sure does not look or feel like one. This hotel can not be compare to Le St-Martin. The Times Hotel & Suites looks like it was cheaply made. It’s definably not a 4 star hotel.

author: lbmmoh
title: Nice option outside of Montreal, esp if you have a car
text: We booked two rooms here for a 4 day period with my family memebers. The hotel is about a 10-15 minute drive from downtown Montreal, so keep this in mind. Its in a suburb town of Laval, which really doesnt have too much going on. Imagine a hotel off the side of the freeway in the states. After some exploration we did find a shopping mall, but the eating options were a bit lacking. Now for the room, we had the upgraded suite, so the wood floors and the walk in shower were great. Bathroom is very clean, and water pressure made bathroom tasks pleasant. The bed was good, but not great like some raved here. The curtains in the room do NOT close. You just have a thin see through linen curtain that closes the middle of the windwos. This is OK, but would prefer better privacy and light blackout when sleeping...the views are worthless as well. The biggest problem we had was the AC/Fan in our room made an incredibly loud noise when the compressor kicked on. We already moved our room twice, so we didnt bother to complain...so we just turned the fan on and ignored it. Hotel staff was good and friendly with English. The hotel breakfast was your average continental breakfast with bagels, toast, bread, fruits, coffee, juices. There is a staff that takes your dishes away if needed....they could have been friendlier wih the service, but not a huge deal. We would stay again, if we drove a car to Montreal. Oh, and the free wifi is a nice touch as well.

author: tristan_rao
title: Nice place to stay!
text: I would highly recommend this hotel. We had booked a queen suite and upon arrival, were asked if we wanted to be upgraded to a king suite for which we gladly accepted. The room was spacious yet cozy with a kitchenette which was very convenient since I had two small children. My kids loved the hotel and called it their "castle home." The buffet breakfast was quite good. Just simple food items like bread, bagels, croissants, cereal, yogurt, fruit, boiled eggs. Just enough for breakfast. We visited the hot tub which was nice, very relaxing. I noticed there were busloads of tourists staying at the hotel. A very busy hotel indeed. There was ample parking space. The staff was friendly. The premises was neat and clean. Only amenity it lacked was an indoor pool. As the hotel does not have a restaurant, we had to eat out which was alright as there are loads of restaurants within the area including McDonalds which is next door. There is Centre Laval (a huge shopping mall) which is across the street and the Carrefour Laval (the largest mall in QC) which is very close by. The hotel is beautiful from the inside and outside. We enjoyed our stay and will definately return next time we visit Laval/Montreal.

author: Katelyn000000
title: Awesome Hotel
text: We only stayed at this hotel for one night but it was a lovely stay. We had booked one of the King Suites. When we first drove up our daughter thought we had driven into a fairytale. She called it a castle for the entire trip. The bed was one of the most comfortable beds we have ever slept in. There were lots of things nearby, stores, restaurants, etc. Some of the other reviews talk about the staff not caring, we called down because there was a circus tent set up as we came off the highway. We asked if they knew if it was open and for some details. The attendant that answered didn't know and suggested we check on the internet. I told him we didn't have a computer. He apologized and that was the end of the call, ten minuted later our phone rang. It was the front desk attendant and he had got all the details of the circus for us - how much it was, when the show started, what the circus was about, it ended up being a horse circus. I was really impressed. We went during a windstorm so we didnt go to the outside whirlpool but the one inside was reallllly nice. The hotel wasn't all that busy when we stayed and we pretty much had it to ourselves. All and all we will definatly go back.

author: Bricksie
title: Shame about the St. Martin
text: The Good: The hotel itself is lovely, and in a convenient location. It's right off Route 15, and there are plenty of restaurants and stores nearby. The rooms are very nice: comfortable beds, nice (though dark) bathrooms, pretty furnishings. You can usually get a decent price if you book through Expedia. We stayed here for two nights, one at the beginning and one at the end of a trip to Quebec province. The Bad: The staff is pretty incompetent, and though not openly rude, could clearly care less about you. The first night we stayed was not exceptionally bad, but we were given a cramped handicap access room (which we didn't request) right next to the elevators and linen supply room. I think if we had needed this type of room, it would have been great (wide doorways, large bathroom, close to the elevator), but we didn't, so it was more of an annoyance. It was a very noisy room. The high-speed internet died right after we arrived, and remained broken throughout our stay. When we arrived back a week later for a second night, the hotel was experiencing "electrical problems," so the elevators were out of service, the TVs emitted a high-pitched whine, the internet was down, the refrigerators didn't work, and there was an unpleasant smell of burning electrics/ozone that made us slightly nervous. When we notified the front desk, we were dealt with rudely, and the guy responded by complaining about how hard all of this was for him. (Since we were the ones paying to be there, we weren't terribly sympathetic.) No apologies were offered, and while we didn't necessarily expect compensation, it would have been nice if a free drink or something had been given, since so few of the amenities were actually functioning. We couldn't wait to leave! It's a shame, since the rooms are so nice. This could be a top-notch hotel!

author: pauldC4994DG
title: Budapest
text: Stayed at Ibis Styles Budapest City for three days. While this hotel is a lower budget, it is very clean, has a great buffet breakfast, and very comfortable beds. Also complementary coffee/tea 24hrs. Took 200E bus from airport (3-day bus/metro pass for 14 Euro ea) to end of line, then M3 metro to Corvin-negyed stop. Walked 10 mins to hotel. Could also take another bus/tram to hotel, but wanted to walk since was so close. We are big walkers, so the hotel location wasn't too far from tourist areas down town - 30-40 mins. Bus/tram is just outside hotel door, and metro is 10 mins walk. Breakfast is great! Eggs, meats, veg's, cereals, yogurts, cheeses, and wonderful breads (included with hotel stay) 6:30 am start (7 am weekends). While a bit of a walk to major attractions, cost of hotel made the walk worth it. Many options for lunch/dinner nearby hotel within 5 min walk. Hotel is just across street from Danube River. Walk up River to bridges that cross into Pest, and all the Buda attractions. Note- charging U.S. cell phone didn't work until I found an European adapter with a 2.4 amp USB port. 1 amp USB port didn't work. If you need your phone for GPS (helped for walking) - ensure you have right plugs. Would certainly stay here again - great visit.

author: YvonneRobinson
title: Good Hotrl
text: Just returned from a 4 night stay at this hotel. Check in was fast and dealt with professionally and friendly. We were a group booking of 15 adults. Rooms were ready earlier than expected. Rooms are basic, but clean and modern and of a good size. Bright and airy. Toileteries are very basic, but we took our own so no problem there. Staff throughout the hotel are friendly and efficient. Bar open until midnight daily. Breakfast was good with varied hot and cold food and beverages. Tables cleared quickly by serving staff. We had a double room on level 3 at the front of the hotel, looking over the river danube, with a balcony. Unfortunately we did find the street noise very intrusive, obviously with the balcony door shut it was better, but still noisy. The room was very warm as the a/c was not available, so we needed the door open to cool the room down, evening noise not too bad, but by 5.30am the noise of teams and cars was very bad. However overall a good stay here, a 15min walk into the city, but tram (no 2) nearby takes you into the city and run regularly. Would stay here again. Very reasonably priced.

author: lharr0w
title: I always can depend on the Ibis brand
text: Comfy beds, cozy comforter and nice pillows. Clean and simple. Breakfast had a nice variety. The coffee/tea all day is a nice touch. Location at first seemed disappointing then realized that it was perfect for transport to the centre of the city. Number 2 tram is constantly running. Catch it right across the street . Takes 10 min. We also walked on the path beside the Danube into the city centre. Takes 45 min. Beautiful scenery espically at night. Caught the Hop on Hop off bus 5 min. away the second day. Not a lot of dining choices in the area but the Thai restaurant next door was resonable and delicious. Its also licensed. Grocery store nearby. This hotel is great value. The Ibis brand is always consistent and thats why we choose it.

author: eg77on
title: Average hotel
text: Advantages: 1. Good location 2. Good scrambled eggs 3. Complimentary tea, coffe and water in the lobby. 4. Smoothie prepared on the bike - it was fun. Disadvantages: 1. Not carefull cleaning - for example room was not vaccumed for 2 weeks despite I explicitely asked. 2. Poor selection and quality of products for breakfast. During almost 2 weeks of my stay butter was available only 3 days - the rest of the time only some spread and margarine. Vegetables are not fresh. Coffe awfull. The only bright side of the breakfast were scrambled eggs. 3. Smoking area on the steps to hotel - to enter the hotel you have to hold your breath. It should be moved 20 m from the entrance. 4. You cant leave your plates during breakfast even for a second because they are immediately taken away despite you have not finished.

author: 130kathc
title: Style over substance
text: This hotel is in a great location. Trams to the city centre are just across the road and buses are close by. The hotel is close to a busy road, so it can be noisy. There is a cycling theme to the hotel. For example, the coat pegs are handlebars. It's Aa very modern hotel. My room was quite small, but the bathroom was great. It was stylish but the clothes hanging space was exreamly small. There was a bean bag. I would have preferred a chair. Breakfast was poor. The choice was very restricted. We ate in the evening and it was not good. We were told that this was because they brought food in. It's a very stylish hotel but they need to get the basics right.

author: FORSYTH6
title: Great visit: Disabled friendly
text: We visited Budapest for an International Skating competition, this was the official hotel. My mother travelled with us who is disabled and I can safely say this was the best facilities we have ever had anywhere! Brilliant wet room! Great room with room for the three of us with privacy. The beds were very comfy! My mum needs extra pillows as can't sleep lying down and the hotel gave an extra two pillows plus the bean bag.. meant she slept well for the 4 night stay! Brilliant! The free coffee was good only downfall was the cups are tiny! The breakfast is varied! It's not the UK so obviously they are catering for a wide variety of people, there is something for everyone! Unless you are very fussy. Certainly none of us went hungry! Only negative is the cost of snacks in the hotel lobby which is a tad steep but you can easily nip to a local shop to avoid this. Staff friendly and efficient.

author: ps151061
title: By far the best IBIS around
text: This is definitely the best IBIS hotel that I have ever stayed at - Why? The new IBIS styles is obviously different to the IBIS that I have become accustomed to for many years now, but this particular hotel sets the bar for all the others within this category. The layout of the hotel was as you would expect. It is the theme that is delightfully catchy - bicycles! Everywhere you go you will find a bicycle or parts of one game-fully employed as a coat rack, stool, lamp holders, etc. There is even an exercise bike in the reception and another where you can make your own smoothie for breakfast. The hotel is very clean, tidy, well maintained and the decor is soft and fun. The rooms are standard as rooms go, but again, clean, tidy and well maintained. Our room had a small balcony that had a good view over the Danube. The bed was comfortable and the shower water temperate did actually adjust from freezing (which I personally prefer) to very hot. There are two lifts and despite the size of the Hotel, we did not find ourselves waiting too long at any time of the day. What also impressed me was the well-equipped children’s corner which kept one very active toddler happy. The breakfast was by far the best that I had experienced at any of the IBIS hotels that I had stayed at over as many years. There was a good selection of local delicacies as well as fruit, cereals, salads, cold meats, breads. The hot food was limited to just scrambled egg, mini frankfurters, pasta. There is free coffee and tea available 24/7 (self service) in the reception area. Adjacent to the reception desk is the bar serving beer, spirits and freshly made coffee. The staff are polite, efficient and helpful. The hotel is well located for business people and tourists, has a very nice theme and layout and is therefore very good value for money.

author: paulcX8740WY
title: On Heat
text: This hotel has an unhealthy obsession with bicycles. Bikes and bike parts are everywhere, sprinkled around the lobby and integrated into the corporate 'art' that hangs on all the walls. The hotel gurus who designed this probably wanted to get real, get down with the kids or something. But it's very fake. Main problem, however, is the heating system. My room was over-heated, so before retiring I set the fan to max and turned the thermostat way down low,. At 2.30 in the morning I was woken by truly oppressive heat. Drenched in sweat, heart pounding and head splitting, I groped for the thermostat controls only to discover that they were entirely for show. Nothing worked. I had finally arrived in hell. I crawled naked across the floor of my fan-assisted oven, wrenched the window open and staggered onto the balcony, much to the amusement of a rabble of late night taxi drivers. I had to be up early for a working breakfast. You know those mornings when you really need good coffee? On the plus side, the coffee at Styles hotel is free. On the debit side, it is undrinkable. In fact, the breakfast is very poor overall. So what is good about Ibis Styles? Their staff. Keen, smart, great people.

author: L5043QZemmab
title: Good but maybe not great
text: Just arrived back from a four night stay here with my partner. All very clean and nicely decorated. Given a room on the top floor as requested. A little on the small side for two people plus luggage in all honesty but it did the job. Very comfortable bed and extra pillows available. Hairdryer in the room isn't the strongest so id advise taking your own if you have thick or long hair. There is also a free to use safe in the room. Only real issue with the room was how warm it was. Air conditioning was quite poor and just not sufficient for the summer weather. No fridge or drinks facilities in the room but there is a coffee machine, teas and water available for free in the reception area 24/7 as well as a snack bar. There are also two Spar shops very close by. Breakfast was continental buffet style with a reasonable amount of choice. The hotel is a little out from the city centre but walkable if you are able or want to. There's also a tram stop and bus stop right in front of the hotel. However, the underpass you need to use to get anywhere can feel a little dangerous. Lots of homeless people and loud drunks in it all the time and it did feel quite intimidating at times. Other than that, decent hotel with lovely staff in a decent location but if you want luxury or to be in the heart of it all maybe increase your budget a bit.

author: AnisaS16
title: Great hotel, great city!
text: The hotel has very convenient location, it is 20 min by nice walk next to Danube river to the city centre, bus station, tram station (lines no. 2, 4, 6), metro station just in front of the hotel, so you do not need your car at all for moving around Budapest. We got family connecting room - one with double bed and the other room was single room with large closet so you can place all your luggage there. Room very clean and tidy. The rooms have very nice and interesting interior, my kid love it! At the lobby, there are few bicycle installations so you can sit and ride to prepare smoothy for breakfast - cool idea! All day free coffee and water available at the lobby. The staff were so kind and willing to answer all your queries. Breakfast was very good, always fresh with lot of choices. There are few available parking slots, we were not charged for parking our car there, very nice touch by the hotel staff. It should be noted that during the weekend, parking at public places in Budapest (if you find one) is free (there is few parking slots just behind the hotel's corner, so if you are staying during the weekend, I m sure you can find some free parking slots there. Budapest is a great city, very warm, a lot of things to explore and visit. Food in the city centre is tasty, I would recommend to try local food (Hungarian goulash, onion soup etc.), prices are around EUR 5 and you get large dish. During our visit, the weather was pretty nice, so we were outside all day, otherwise, in case of bed weather, this hotel maybe miss a nice indoor pool to give it 5 star rate. :)

author: fezojk
title: Room with magic view on city
text: Hotel is situated on very busy place but reward is fantastic view on Statue of Liberty and Castle. After dusk it is totally beautifull. You can also have a room in the quiet side of hotel but you will see nothing. Check-in and check-out was very quick. Staff was nice and profesional. Breakfast were very good - good choice of bread, vegetable, fruits, cereals, eggs, teas. There were also typical hungarian sausages and hot meals - pasta, boiled vegetable, etc. I missed more types of cheeses. There was also a food corner where you can buy something to eat/drink anytime 24/7. Great was also tea corner where you can make for free tea or coffee as much as you wish. There was also water with lemon. Wifi connection was for free and very good. Room was very nice decorated with beautifull details - lamps, table for breakfast from bed, wallpapers,.. Bed was great - it would be paradise to have this kind of bed in every hotel in the world. The same I can say about towels :) Comparing the rates we paid, it is very good choice. But if you need piece in night for sleeping, ask for a quiet room on the quiet side of hotel.

author: 339danielp
title: Um...depends what room you get
text: First let me say the staff here is GREAT. The brunette manager that speaks French was very nice. The breakfast is also great. Now for the bad..which the hotel has less control over... If you get one of the rooms facing the street (a VERY busy and noisy street) I was literally surprised by how busy and noisy you will be inhaling all of the pollution if you need to keep the balcony door open for fresh air. I was here in March and thanks to global warming it was uncharacteristically (according to the staff) warm. They said they don't turn on the AC till May so I had to leave my balcony door open to cool down the room. I eventually got used to the noise but woke up with my throat hurting and eyes burning from the pollution. THEN,.,just FYI to all my fellow Americans who did not know this as I do now. In March to April every god dam Italian high schooler gets some sort of free vacation around Europe and they fill up all the hotels like ants...loud, immature, boisterous ants. So if you are traveling in Europe during March to April I highly recommend going with an Air bnb if you would like to sleep. If you would like to be woken up by sixteen year old mom as boys literally laying and hanging out in the hall way outside your room, feel free. That's right..it turns out the only thing worse than huge groups of American teens is a huge group of Italian teenagers. OH and they love to stay up all night in each other's rooms because they're so young they can't go clubbing. THEN after not sleeping all night and having the staff do almost nothing about it. You will be shuffling through forty or so spoiled smelly and sleeps teens during breakfast because they all go at the same time. Air bnb for life. That said, I'm grateful to the staff for accommodating me and moving my rooms when I nearly ripped them a new one because I didn't sleep all night. In my opinion this is why air bnb is destroying hotels. If IBIS had any sense they wouldn't accommodate these large groups of students Oh and this is an excellent location you can walk to everything

author: 418carloc
title: A magnificent introduction to Budapest!
text: We arrived into Budapest a few days ago with the intentions of finding an apartment for a few months. We decided to stay in in the Ibis Styles city hotel because 1) We heard it was a nearly opened hotel chain in the city and 2) The photos of the hotel looked pretty impressive. It was also the first time we stayed in an Ibis Styles hotel so we were looking forward to having a comfortable base in the city while we explored it for a few days and also find an apartment. The first thing you'll notice upon entering the hotel is the vibrant yellow/green colours that greet you. Each of the 300+ Ibis Styles hotels around the world have their own unique character/decor. This hotel incorporates bicycles and healthy living into their decor (which you can see from the photos). Apart from the warm colours, we also felt a great sense of friendliness from the staff - who genuinely took an interest in making sure we were 100% comfortable during our stay. The hotel itself is situated smack bang in the centre of the shopping/business area of the city which makes it easily accessed to the tourist and cultural attractions. Each of the 130 rooms are sound proof, have a colour tv with a bunch of channels and free open WiFi (no annoying passwords to worry about). Why can't every hotel have open WiFi in this day and age? We're not really breakfast people, so we didn't sample the breakfast but it looked very tasty. Bottom line is that we enjoyed our stay here and couldn't find anything negative to say about the hotel. We were so intrigued by the design that we took the tram to the Ibis Styles centre hotel (About 10 mins away) to check out it's decor - which is based on the 1980's "pac-man" computer game! It brought us right back to our childhood. Hopefully this gives anyone contemplating staying here a little information about what our stay was like.

author: thorntonem
title: Excellent Customer Service
text: Both front desk clerks that I interacted with during our stay (Chris and Bob) were engaging, professional, and made check-in/check-out quick and easy. Chris gave us a coupon for a free appetizer for Applebee's. The Microtel is approximately 15 minutes from the Illinois State Fairgrounds. There are multiple restaurants within walking distance of the hotel. Breakfast is included with your stay, from 6:30 - 9:30 AM daily. The fare includes make your own waffles, fruit, cereal, juice, milk, eggs, pastries, bread, English muffins and sausage. Our room had two queen size beds. There was a stain on one of the comforters. My wife called to get it changed. The staff responded quickly. The beds were comfortable. There was also a bed time in the window. Our 9 year old son thought it was so cool that he slept there. In addition to the stain on the bedding, the room could have been cleaned better. I had poor reception for internet in my room., and I couldn't connect to the free wifi. The customer service was great, but the cleaning could be better, and the food did not taste good. We will be back in Springfield the same time next year for the state fair. Have not decided if we'll stay here again.

author: S1478OPamandak
title: The front desk staff was nice and professional but...
text: The front desk staff was nice and professional but apparently was left on her own after only one day of training. Issues with the room: 1. The room smelled like cat urine which was nauseating. 2. The floor did not look clean enough to walk without shoes on. 3. One of the pillow cases was smudged with makeup and wrinkled which clearly indicated it was not changed after the previous guest. 4. The shower wall had some hair on it that was not mine or my husbands. 5. There was no fridge as advertised so I couldn't keep food that I brought. 6. Curtain wouldn't stay shut. 7. The chair in the room had a big, gross looking stain on it that my dog kept wanting to sniff [yuck] which confirmed it was something disgusting or food related. 8. Design flaws would include the non existent counter space in the bathroom and the tacky mirror along the entire back wall of the room (made me think it was a hooker hotel from the 70's) just something to think about with renovations. This room probably should be a complete gut because it was pretty gross. Unfortunately we got in at midnight and this was the last room available in the entire hotel so we couldn't switch rooms and we were too exhausted to try to find another hotel so we stayed and left as early as possible.

author: MHer101
title: Terrible night sleep
text: The walls are paper thin. Yes it was New Year's Eve, but we could hear everything and no one was monitoring. I would have expected better from a Wyndham brand. The doors no not have any stop so they slam automatically. The beds are rock solid and I'm guessing old. Pillows small. Furnishings worn. Room was clean. When I complained about kids crank calling our room and the revelers waking us at 4:45 due to thin walls, I was offered a shrug if the shoulders. Also, same revelers smoking in non smoking hotel. Yuck! Again I know it was a holiday evening. We stayed in a timeshare last week and our time ended New Year's Eve so we were forced to stay in hotel en route back home. But as I said I would have expected more from a Microtel. I thought they were a decent level Wyndham property. Breakfast also not great. And only three tables to sit.

author: natep952
title: Disgusting
text: We booked 2 adjoining rooms. They were available to check in early, and the front desk was friendly. Good start. The rooms were among the shabbiest I've stayed in. Seriously worn down. Old gross peanuts under the bedside table. Graffiti on the door connecting the 2 rooms. Grubby, chipped doorframes and walls, with sheetrock tape coming off around the shower. I've never stayed in a hotel that feels the need to present the tv remote as "sanitized" in a plastic bag. And in the morning, a roach in my kids' bathroom! Awesome. On checkout, I mentioned to the desk clerk and the only thing he seemed concerned about was the graffiti. No attempt to try to make it up to me. He suggested I might not know what a roach looks like, as beetles are coming in when it gets cold - which also would be unacceptable. I really expected more from a Wyndham branded hotel. The management should be ashamed.

author: lsusand
title: For a No Frills Motel, Visit Here...
text: I've been sampling various Wyndhams, and this is below Baymont. No luggage cart...they have 1 for 3 floors, not seen during entire visit. Must have been visiting inside a room. Ice machines on floors 1 and 3. Inside the room, clean. No chair or sofa, padded window seat. Accessible room had tub. Furniture by Sauder. No outlets in nightstands. 3 pillows for bed. Shampoo, no conditioner or lotion. This is a Continental Breakfast in the am, done by your Night Desk Clerk. Danish, muffins, cinnamon toast, and a toaster. Tiny yogurt. Psst...IHOP is next door. Across the street are good restaurants. Red Lobster, Outback, Smokey Bones. On the way out of Springfield, Toronto Rd. next to Cracker Barrel, is a Baymont. We'll check that out next trip here.

author: aa2marti
title: OK but nothing spectacular
text: Place is unspectacular but gets the job done if you are looking for a simple place to rest on a road trip. Cons: Carpeting is stained and old and could use replacement. Sound insulation to the hallway was poor; I could hear everything being said in the hallway. If you are sensitive to noise, I'd suggest getting a room as far away from the elevator as possible, as sound tends to decrease the further away you are from the elevator. Sound insulation to neighbouring rooms was better, but I could still hear the TV and muffled conversations. There is only a single elevator and it is a bit slow. Mattress was creaky and springy. Room air conditioner was somewhat noisy. Pros: Staff was friendly and helpful. On checkin, I got a coupon for a free appetizer at the nearby Applebee's. Free parking and free breakfast were nice touches. Location was convenient - just off the I-55 and I-72. In summary, 3 out of 5. Probably what you'd expect in this price range. I would stay here again.

author: R2715YWkevins
title: Midnight Rider
text: Rolled in twice to this place on back to back nights after 11 PM. Found the hotel clean and quiet. The front desk was excellent both nights. The beds weren't the greatest but efficient. A little firmer than I prefer. Pillows were really nice. Rooms were clean. I did find a badge of one of the staff members under the bed but I'm assuming she just dropped it while cleaning. I stayed in a single one night and then the next night with a AAA discount got a really nice double room with a kitchenette for about the same price. Breakfast? it was there. Good thing there's an eating establishment across the parking lot out of the front door. Breakfast was continental but I don't know from which continent. Maybe one of the starving countries? Just a few rolls, a little cereal, some coffee, some really sticky oatmeal and that's about it. Skipped it twice. Cable is basic in the rooms but there is about four or five movie channels included. I like the place because of the security, the location, and it was clean. I can skip breakfast.

author: ntsmom
title: Just Right!
text: This hotel was a great spot for my family during a visit to Springfield. It was inexpensive and had everything we needed. We had a room with two queen beds. The beds were very comfortable. They offered what they called a, "continental" breakfast. Really, I felt it was a little more than that. There was flavored oatmeal packets, french toast, bagels and other breads for toasting. They also had 4 types of cereal, hard boiled eggs and yogurt. There were even muffins and danish along with juice, milk, coffee and tea. The pool was small, but enjoyable. The walls in the bathroom needed a little attention. The paint was looking a little damaged in some areas. The remote needed to be replaced too. Really these were the only negatives. We would recommend this to friends.

author: YG01
title: Dirty Dirty
text: The rooms were dirty! The first room I had, had a black smudge on the bed, white stains, and what looked like gum on the window bench. The carpets were disgusting, you could definitely tell that it was well used and traveled on. It really could have used a deep cleaning. I asked for a different room, the guy at the desk asked me if I had used it. Just in case it was needed. Uhm. Gross? I'm sure he didn't do a walk around or fix the issues with the room. My second room was an upgraded suite. It smelled better than the previous room but....there were crumpled up chips on the floor! The carpets were not very clean nor did the room smell clean either. The bed was clean but I had a hard time sleeping since the room temperature kept fluctuating from hot to cold. Breakfast in the morning was ok. Do not be fooled my the previous good ratings. I was fooled and wish I hadn't spent the night here. Also the website's pictures of the rooms did not look anything like the actual room.

author: AlohaPammie
title: Accomodating, Clean, Comfortable & Friendly!
text: I stayed here on business several times years ago when it was brand new. This time I stayed over traveling with my two dogs. To my amazement it was still clean, comfortable, & friendly just as it was when it was new! Carpet a little worn now but so what?! Immediately, Carlos at the front desk greeted me by name & acknowledged my request for ground floor with the two dogs without my asking about it. He was glad to tell me that not only was I on the ground floor, he thought I'd like being right next to the side door for easy dog potty & car access. I could not have been happier!!! I've made this request to numerous hotels & finally someone listened, accomodated, & even went an extra step! The room was spotless. Usually you find water spots or even mold on the ceiling in hotel bathrooms, but not here! The bathroom was bright white and possibly freshly painted. Coming in late I appreciated the 10% discount at the IHOP right on the grounds to conveniently carry-out din-din! The breakfast area was neat & well maintained with a good variety for continental breakfast. This is the second Microtel I've stayed at with great results. I'll be seeking them out in the future. Thank you again, Carlos!

author: blackpupjean
title: "Micro"tel fits perfectly
text: The first night - The name of the hotel "Micro"tel is perfect, because everything at the hotel is small. We had a queen size bed room, and the room was tiny. Never staying in such a tiny room. The pool is so small that don't bother bringing your swim suits unless you have little kids. They should just renovate it into a hot tub. It would be a nice big hot tub. The evening desk clerk was very nice as was the morning one. The morning breakfast was lacking a lot, but it was still free. The second night - This was on our way back home after vacation. I had forgotten to make a hotel reservation, so I thought I would just go to Microtel again. The desk clerk was awesome. He gave me the one remaining room left for a reduced rate. It was a double queen size room, which is a decent size. If I am ever in Springfield again, I will probably try another hotel. The Microtel was okay, but I thought it was a little steep in price for what you get.

author: liverpool1023
title: A good option
text: My go to hotel in the Galleria area is usually the Mariott which has superb facilities (good gym, great food and comfy rooms). I’ve also stayed many times at the Hotel Derek, which although is very good, has a major downside as it is very difficult to walk to the Galleria or nearby shops. The Sheraton provides a good alternative. It is well located and short walk to shops, mall and nearby restaurants. The staff are friendly and provide good customer service and make a really positive impression. I stayed in a small suite on this stay which was comfortable with an extremely comfy bed. The room was relatively quiet with little noise from the freeway close by. The room was well stocked with bottled water. There is safe, bathrobes, ironing board available. There are a couple of annoying aspects however. The breakfast buffet options are the most limited I’ve seen in the hotel of this kind of rating (although there are some typical al a carte menu options). Why not stock the minibar and put some fruit in the rooms? Strangely there is a lack of information in the room; where is the gym and what are the hours? Where is the club lounge located? Get some nicer shampoo etc instead of the crappy motel standard stuff. The hotel could therefore do with a bit of sharpening up to bring it in line with its competitors in the immediate area.

author: BarbaraSS
title: It's the Personnel That Make This Place
text: I came back to this Sheraton again because while the rooms are comfy and large, the personnel are amazing. Checked into my room with Amanda at the front desk. As a gold member, we had been upgraded to use the Sheraton Club. My sister had checked in earlier and Amanda remembered her name. Went up to the room and oh boy did it smell. Went down to the lobby and asked Amanda if they allow animals in the hotel and she said, just dogs. I told her one of them had left his mark! She was most apologetic and with no questions asked, gave us another room. We had to wait a bit, no worries. While waiting, Yanos (I believe he was one of the managers), went above and beyond to make sure we were fine while waiting - some drinks and food. So nice and totally not necessary. This hotel would get an excellent save for some things: one of the stalls in the downstairs bathroom took almost 2 days to fix, stuff that was left outside of rooms took all weekend to be taken away - the leftover food was removed, but the plates and glassware were left on the floor. When the a/c in our room went off, there was a loud noise. The Club still is just adequate. Food was average and sometimes cold; plastic utensils one morning. They did away with happy hour in the lounge downstairs, but it was still more pleasant to have a drink there than in the lounge. Again, I want to reiterate that Amanda at the front desk was EXCELLENT! She deserves a raise, a promotion or whatever they can do to make sure she stays with Sheraton. I don't know how she remembers our name everyday, remembered we were going for a manicure and asked to see them. I will stay again at this hotel - rooms are comfortable and the personnel are great.

author: tracytex
title: Football Weekend
text: We stayed here over Labor Day weekend for a football game in Houston. I went through Priceline and got a fabulous rate, even though I am a SPG member. I am use to staying on the SPG designated floors, however, this time it was not offered. I have booked through Priceline before at a SPG property and have always stayed on the designated SPG floor. I am unsure if it was because they were booked up or because I booked through Priceline, or maybe they simply didn’t have one. The room was ok. The TV in the living room did not work, but they were very quick to fix it. Our view was of a rooftop, but that’s okay! We did arrive late and there were a couple of football teams in. We were on the 2nd floor and down the hall from what seemed to be a daycare. I have never heard so many little ones screaming in unison. It did tend to quiet down, because I am sure they passed out from exhaustion. 😂 but all in all, the staff was absolutely fabulous, the bartender in the bar was fantastic and Valet was quick and incredible. I will probably pick a property downtown next time because the traffic around this property was insane. This is totally not Sheratons fault though! I gave it 4 stars simply for the outdated room, but the service was impeccable.

author: NikyCW3
title: Not a Four-Star Hotel
text: I am currently in the middle of my stay. I spent a great dela of time researching hotels before choosing the Sheraton because it is a familiar brand. The front desk staff is excellent and they respond to questions quickly. The room is okay, but the hotel is old and there is very little attention to detail for small things that could be resolved with paint and basic maintenance. I am in my secong room and the bathtubs are stained because they are old. The tub in the first room would not stop a steady stream of water and the it was clear that it had been going for while based on the tub stain. The sink handle easily came all the way off its pedestal if you tried to turn on water. The paint on the ceiling was curling and hanging in the bathroom. I was out for a funeral when the front desk sent maintenance. They repaired the sink and tub and it appears that they attempted to scrape or sand paper the hanging paint. They left all of the white powered debris from the work all over the bathroom and they tracked it through the carpet as they departed. Attention to details is a key attribute at a four star hotel. Not sure if the positive reviews here are from people who don't travel much, but I travel often. This hotel would be worth the price if you intended to pay LaQuinta Inn prices. The bathrooms need an overhaul. Basic caulking and replacement bathtubs and tiles would really make a difference.

author: BarbaraSS
title: Mostly Good, but Not Very Good
text: I had the most amazing front end person - Chris. He could not have been more personable, helpful, sweet...and a wickedly dry sense of humor. Actually remembered my name throughout the entire stay. Marta, the bartender in the WildPlum Lounge was quite sweet. Rooms were fine, bedding, as usual, very comfortable. They need to have a few more outlets, though. Club Lounge was less than adequate. Hors d'oeuvres were really sad looking and tasting. Proper utensils weren't in place...needed to ask. We didn't go back our second night, but went to the lounge in the lobby instead. They offered a happy hour - why wasn't there one in the lounge which is pay as you go for liquor and, because of happy hour pricing downstairs, triple the price for a glass of the house wine. Breakfast was average, truly not impressive food. We also never saw a Club Manager. Parking rates are ridiculous - truly didn't know you had to pay. We have been staying at the Westin across the street in the Galleria - no parking fees. Would probably not go back. The only thing going for this hotel is the personnel - again, specifically, Chris and Marta and the ability to spread out in the room

author: shong425
title: Inattentive Staff, Facilities Old
text: Stayed here for two nights. Two main issues: 1. I've never had so much difficulty getting in touch with the front desk than at this hotel. Anything basic that I needed (extra towels, room service) or even the extraordinary (reporting a mysterious bag outside my door) -- not once did I get in touch with anyone on my first try. I had to call an average of 3-4 times spaced 10 min apart to get in touch with anyone. I've never experienced anything like it at any hotel level. 2. While I enjoyed the room layout, the facilities are all kind of old and need to be updated. It gave me the sense that things weren't clean. Things may have been clean but the fact that everything was kind of dated gave off an unclean feeling. Perhaps I was just in an older room? Extra: This last note has nothing to do with my review but also reflects poorly on the hotel, generally. There was a fire drill during my stay. Obviously that is not a knock against the hotel but how it was handled quite poorly. They told everyone to go outside and wait until the fire dept arrived and gave the OK to go back in. For the next 90 min or so the entire body of hotel guests wandered in and out of the hotel in their pajamas, with no announcements or specific direction from hotel staff as to whether it was OK to stay in the building or not, or to go upstairs or not. After some time, guests got fed up and were using the elevators to go up, and while the hotel staff saw all this, when people asked staff directly "hey some people are going up, is it OK to return to the rooms?" they said "no, it's unsafe." What if there was something seriously wrong? Shouldn't there have been protocol in place to deal with the guests in such a situation?

author: Ariesgurl
title: Birthday Getaway
text: We checked in late on Friday after attending a comedy show. Yonas is really nice, friendly and knowledgeable. I forgot to pack my jammies and he told me where the two nearest 24hr drug store were. Check in went smooth and i was really pleased with how spacious the room was. You could get to the restroom from the hallway and the bedroom. The beds were comfy. Our room had a view of the freeway. The hotel is in a good location especially if you're a walker. There is Le Beep and CVS across the street/highway. Down the street is old navy, Nordstrom and a lot of other high end stores. The vanity area in the room is huge and has a full length closet mirror. The restroom itself was somewhat small. They had excellent water pressure but the hot water did not get as hot as i would have liked it. I had the dial turned all the way to the max hot setting and it was just a little hot. The faucet kept dripping in the shower as well.
