It wasn't loud enough to disturb us and you only noticed it when you were in the restroom. They had the AC set on the perfect temperature we never had to adjust it. Breakfast was $20 and parking $22 per day.

author: K5890TItims
title: Combines Friendliness with Comfort
text: I go to Houston, TX on business visits. I normally stay in either of the two Westin hotels by the Galleria Mall but this time I thought of staying in Sheraton Suites, two blocks from the Galleria as construction work is in progress at Westin Oaks. My stay at Sheraton Suites was a pleasant surprise, the personal touch and feel made me wonder why I did not make this hotel my first choice during previous visits. The reception staff were friendly and they gave me and my colleague good suites on the 15th floor with Sheraton Club lounge. The East facing suites are though noisy with the bed rooms right on the highway with nonstop traffic throughout the night. My preference next time will be for the West facing suites. This did not take away the impeccable quality of the room with a king size bed and independent sitting area. The suites are well appointed, clean and self-contained. Sheraton club in the same floor serves to elite Gold and Platinum members breakfast in the morning and snacks in the evening. I would suggest that the breakfast hours are extended from 6 AM to 9:30 AM instead of the current hours of 6:30 to 9 AM on weekdays. The Fitness center has Life Time elliptical that need some attention from maintenance, the touch screens did not respond . I also enjoyed a quite swim on the inhouse pool. The restaurant and bars were never crowded, the meal choice was limited but the preparations were tasty. The concierge desk was handled by Rex and Raul both very friendly and resourceful. The Hotel offers free shuttle service to Galleria mall and nearby areas, which I thought was a convenient option. This morning when I checked out we found some big charges on the bill for a few long-distance calls made inadvertently, but Matt Davis, Director of Operations called me back even before I arrived in Detroit to inform me that he would reverse the charges. Chris Mendoza is another young man in the reception who helped me during my stay. All in all, this Sheraton facility is guest focused and will not disappoint anyone who is looking for a friendly comfortable place to stay in Houston. This place will be my first choice when I go to Houston next time.

author: jasoncrh
title: I'd rate this 3.5 stars - solid hotel
text: I stayed here this past Thursday night for one night. Overall, it was a solid business hotel in a good location in Houston. It's close to the Galleria, and it's close to many of the attractions/ restaurants in mid town/ river oaks. Hotel itself is solid and clean, if a little dated in its decor. I was happy that my Amex SPG card got me access to the club level where I had breakfast. Solid continental breakfast with good selection and friendly service. In addition, there is a full breakfast buffet in the Sage restaurant that I didnt try, but for $15 it sounded like a good deal. My room was good. Comfortable bed, good water pressure in the shower. Nice to have the space of a suite. I will echo others - my room was on the east side overlooking the freeway out front, so there was a constant din. If you want more quiet request a room overlooking the back. There was a large line when I went to check out. I didnt have time to wait but the bellman took my key and said that they would send me the receipt. They didnt and I had to call back twice to get it, but I finally did. Overall, this is a solid hotel in a good location.

author: Moedot
title: First time at Sheraton
text: Found a good deal on Groupon and stayed here as a couple for Thanksgiving holiday and overall it was a pleasant stay! We checked in rather late and the room we got smelled super smokey/mildewy. Went back to the front desk and they immediately gave us another room which was great. The room was spacious and bed was comfy. We did have a stain on our sheets and called housekeeping. Took awhile to get new ones and after talking to the housekeeper she advised she was the only one on duty (poor woman!). We aren't the snooty type so instead of waiting for her to remake our bed, we happily took the linens and did it ourselves. Food was pretty good and prices for room service weren't over the top. The breakfast buffet was worth the money. The bartender downstairs was amazing and friendly! Guys at the front desk were comical, valet attendant were friendly, parking garage wasn't bad. we did have a lot issues with our room keys, but the front desk were more than happy to help each time. Also, there are two TV's in the room and while watching one, it would randomly turn off and the other would turn on. Weird. It's walking distance to the Galleria (we personally didn't go due to Black Friday madness) and there are some restaurants and a gas station literally at the corner. Would definitely stay here again if ever in Houston for an extended period of time!

author: E2994RCpatrickb
title: Avoid this Hotel!! Aggressive Security and bad A/C.
text: I stayed at this hotel with my family for a long weekend. The lady who checked me and was very nice and hospitable. Unfortunately the first room I was sent to had not been cleaned yet. So the second room I resent to, the furniture was turned on its side and it also smells like smoke. The lady apologized and sent me to a third room with an attendant to make sure everything was OK which it was. The rooms were large with a sweet like two separate rooms which was nice. Later that night when we came back from dinner the hotel seemed to be having some type of load party going on. There was beer spilled and drinks in the lobby and even in the elevator. No big deal I was a kid wants so I went to my room the retired for the night. My room would not cool down at all in maintenance guy said the AC was broken so they told me that they could move me to another room. A few minutes later as I'm packing my stuff up to move rooms an agree security officer come to my door and accuses me of smoking marijuana. I tell him he is lost his mind and that I'm with my family and that there are kids coming up and down the hall ways which time he leaves. He shows back up three minutes later with the police officer and tells me I'm not allowed to move rooms anymore. The next morning I went downstairs to the desk and they had charged up $400 smoking fee to my room. The management apologized and said that the officer tends to be very aggressive and they comped my parking for the trip. From check-in to check out this whole experience at this hotel was a bazaar disaster.

author: TheMayfs
title: SPG Members Beware
text: Second time extended stay at this hotel. Good location for access to freeways and access some restaurants in walking distance but for us it ends there. You're hardly recognized as an SPG member and frankly any kind of comps or upgrades are hard to come by at this location. Room was not very clean on check in. Dust all over the place along with somebody's dirty socks (not ours) next to bed. Selected Green program and when requested a couple more towels they were delivered to room still damp. Wi-Fi free plan we were offered limited to THREE devices, (Had to make sure to shut devices off when done in case of phone calls otherwise charge was $14.95 per day) Wi-Fi signal very weak. $20.00 per night self park and on weekends if hotel is holding an outside private event good luck in finding a parking place even though you will be charged $20.00 for that night. TV's in room clicked off at any time. Room AC control seemed to be mal-functioning. Room décor very dark. $20.00 breakfast buffet was not a good value and you have to EXTRACT from wait staff other food options that are included that are not on the buffet line. Toast, Omelets, etc. Purchased ONE bottle of domestic beer in Club Room cost over $6.00. (Should have gone to corner store about one block away). Pool and Hot Tub are small. Room does have small sink and fridge. Room rate was a decent but will look for a better place to stay next time in Houston. Staff is friendly.

author: Janty1202
title: Weekend trip with the grandson
text: One of the best hotels I've ever stayed in! I've stayed in tons of hotels over the years including some in the $300-$400 a night range. This hotel ranks up there with the best. The ladies at the front desk were awesome and super friendly. It was my 10 year old grandson's first trip to Houston and he wanted to be as high up as possible. The front desk staff made certain we got a high floor. Upon walking in to the room, a lady from the front desk called just to make sure everything was in place and we were happy with the room. I can honestly say that I have never had a hotel do that, not even the high dollar ones. Terrific customer service! Parking was a breeze and the hotel and room were super clean and beautiful. The room was a suite and very spacious. The beds were some of the best I've slept in. All in all, it was honestly one of the best hotel experiences I've ever had. The only bad part was that we were only there for one night. I would love to spend more time there. I will absolutely recommend this hotel to anyone that asks!

author: AAEXPFlyer
title: Very disappointing: Poorly maintain & cleaned
text: I seldom provide negative reviews of hotels. This is an exception. On the positive side, the front desk staff and restaurant team is very friendly, the lobby is in good condition and appears to have been recently updated. The hotel location is quite convenient. The beds are comfortable and meet standard Sheraton standards. Unfortunately that's where the positives end. I understand that hotels age and that renovations are planned to upgrade the condition of the hotel. However, I do expect that Sheraton hotels would provide decent levels of hygiene and that basic care to maintain the condition of the hotel would take place. The condition of this hotel was one of the worse that I've seen in a long time. Considering that I spend roughly 125 nights a year in a hotel, that should say a lot. A few items that demonstrate this lack of care and systemic failures to maintain a property: - Rusting bath that could easily have been fixed (see photo) - I've only seen this once at a respectable chain hotel; - Accumulation of dust that was never vacuumed probably over a significant period of time (see photo) that brings into question how often this room is actually cleaned between guests; - Broken windows (see photo) that were not addressed during stay; - Someone else's hair in the sink when I checked in (no photos) which brings into question as to whether the bathrooms had been cleaned. And this was apparently in an upgraded room because of my status with Starwood Hotels. I expect much better from a Starwood hotel, particularly at this price point. I also stayed at the Marriott down the street which is also an older hotel being upgraded. The one significant difference is that this hotel has been meticulously maintained and feels clean (review to come). I would not recommend this hotel and will not be staying here again... at any price point.

author: TexasEx91
title: This hotel is like the mailman...always delivers!
text: I am in Houston almost weekly on business. For years, this has been the hotel of my choice. It is in a great location, offers reasonably priced self-parking, the staff is amazing, every room is a very nice suite and everything is well maintained. I am a Starwood Platinum member and most of the staff recognize me as soon as I come in. They make sure I have everything I need, and if I have any issues, big or small, they are EXTREMELY responsive. The rooms are large. Sitting room with a couch and work area and nicely sized bedroom. There is a sliding door in between for privacy. The air conditioning is quiet, cool and consistent. The wi-fi is amongst the best I experience as a 'road warrior.' The lobby an community areas are very well kept. I would definitely say this property is ideal for a business traveler or group. The Club Room is nice. I do wish they had a bit of a better 'on the go' selection of health food. Maybe some breakfast bars or more fruit. Otherwise, it is terrific. When it comes to business travel, this is about the best value you are going to find. Other hotels in the area are MORE expensive and NOT as nice! How can you go wrong?

author: 402cp
title: Great Stay
text: I stayed at the hotel with an alumni group. The lobby smelled so good. David checked me in (was nice & pleasant) and was very accommodating to my requests. My king room was great - nice modern furniture, very comfortable bed, two televisions and doors separated the different areas of the suite. I was on the interstate side but that did not bother me. If you are a light sleeper, ask for the other side of the hotel. I was a little surprised about the iron (felt broken & did not steam well) and ironing board cover (did not fit). Also, it seemed like I could not get the water to turn completely off in the shower. I normally iron my clothes before traveling so my clothes were not too bad. I did not report at the time of my stay. I am sure the staff would have taken care of it. It is in a great location but you have to go up to the next exit and circle back to the hotel. Easy access to the interstate, Galleria Mall, other shops, restaurants, self parking is $16 and valet $26 (in/out). The valet staff was very nice (friends did valet). You have some covered parking and it is easy to get from the garage to the hotel lobby. I also loved the key card access on the elevator to get to your room. I would definitely stay here again.

author: Moostro
title: Maybe 3-stars
text: I needed one night in a hotel, and Houston seems to be a very expensive town. I used hotwire for the first time and thought for $82 a night, you can't go wrong with an advertised 4-star hotel. Well, I would give this a 3-star. To start, the parking garage is directly behind the building and not included - nickel and diming. You then walk in the heat to the un air conditioned elevator to go the ground floor and walk past the pool to the entrance of the hotel. Lobby staff was very friendly and even verbally confirmed that I had pre-paid by Hotwire. The hallways were not air conditioned, and that is stifling. When I went to get ice from the machine, I am not exaggerating that It was 105F+ in the room. The room itself was fine, but not 4 stars. The faucets were not of high quality. There was plenty of space to have a double sink, but only had 1. The shampoo and amenities were most definitely 3-star. The closet doors were mirrored sliding doors which did not function well. 2 flat screen tvs were nice., Free internet was nice. Room service was quick, but not cheap. At check out, one of the printers was broken so she had to switch to a different machine. Starbucks coffee in the room was nice with the little machine and a refrigerator. I slept well, but it was not 4-stars. I cannot imagine paying full price for this place.

author: momtomonkeys
title: Excellent hotel, staff, just so-so
text: Beautiful suites, comfortable beds! My only area of concern with this hotel, is their lack of commitment to their jobs. The valet guys seemed to always be missing. The staff seems to stand around chatting amongst themselves, rather than projecting a professional upscale image. Then there is the luggage cart issue. They only have 3 for the whole hotel?! We were traveling with 3 kids and a TON of bags. No one offered to help me carry out the luggage. They just said "sorry-no luggage carts", and went back to talking to eachother. I was so mad. I hurt my back trying to carry all that luggage and bags down. (We were on a 10 day trip with 5 people. Lots of bags. ) It would have been nice for someone to offer to help carry bags. Clearly, the management needs to be present and lead the staff better. Hotels are a service business. If you just want to chit chat--be a telemarketer.

author: Hawaiiantaco
title: Nice Little Hotel; Nice Little Price
text: We stayed here one night. We found the hotel to be clean, well organized, and updated. The staff was helpful and friendly. The room was well appointed, with a nice bathroom. There were plenty of towels, pillows, and toiletries. The bed was very comfortable. We had a good rest. We were tired so decided to try the restaurant, The Plum, in the hotel. This place was supposed to be gourmet, but was really just expensive. We ordered fried tomatoes, and they were pretty bad. The braised short ends were excellent, but there was not much of them. Dessert was just average. Service was adequate, but not particularly good, and there was just one other group eating at that time. I can't recommend the place, but also would not say to steer clear. The cost of the hotel was really reasonable. I do recommend this hotel.

author: ShazaamIam
title: Pleasantly surprised
text: We stayed at this hotel for one night--a Thursday. In general, weekday hotel rates are expensive, so I took a leap of faith and reserved a room on Hot Wire--was given the Sheraton Suites. I have not been pleased with the Sheraton hotel chain in general in the past, so I was VERY apprehensive. Until I entered our room. Spacious, nice, clean, and very comfortable. The fact that it was a suite with a separate living space was a great bonus. We chose not to eat in the hotel, as there are many restaurants nearby. Parking was $16/day. With that said, most all of the hotels in that area charge for parking. TV channels were mostly sports and news, with a couple of other random channels, as well as the local stations. Would have been nice to see some add'l tv channels. When you first turn on the TV, you have to click around to avoid all the pay-per-view stuff. That was annoying--it took a while to find the free cable channels. And you had to go through it all over again each time you turned on the TV. Even so, I would definitely recommend this hotel.

author: 2Texas_Travellers
title: The good and the bad
text: I'm staying here for a conference after not staying here for ~ 1 year. The good news is that the renovation is complete. The bar is in place and the club on the 15th floor is finished. The remodel is nicely done. The good: nice, attentive staff. The restaurant manager checked on me in the bar after I vetoed the restaurant because it was I too loud due to a happy hour taking place in the back. I like the chilled, bottled water offered in the lobby. The bad: the club lounge. I went up on Monday night and there was no food and the server informed me that the wine would be $19 a glass ( while she as pouring the wine). The following morning, I went up for breakfast and found a very limited menu followed by a ticket to sign with a spot to add gratuity. I've stayed at Sheratons all over the world and have never had this happen. It was tacky. If they can't afford to pay their staff, then don't offer the club. In the room, there wasn't a robe. The management would be wise to consider what is offered at other Sheratons nearby and offer a comparable product, especially when they charge more per room.

author: cincoMcBrides
title: A stay with Kids
text: I have stayed here twice now; a 7 night stay this past summer and a 18 night stay this Dec with a family of five with three kids under 5. I choose to stay at this hotel again in Dec because of the layout of the rooms and the price of the rooms. However, the staff are not the best. The good: 1. Rooms- The rooms are suites in which you can have a king bed and a sleeper sofa. The thing that brings me back to this hotel with my family is the ability to close off the bedroom from the living room to create two rooms. 2. I'm usually able to get this rooms around $100 per night which is a great value for the room you get. The Bad: 1. Parking- I hate the fact that the hotel charges for parking. 2. I actually had a valet attendant honk at me and told me not to block the front drive when I was trying to load my family into my car. 3. The maids failed to clean my room one day during my stay. 4. The lounge for SPG Platinum members should not be labeled a lounge by SPG standards.

author: gracemarini
title: Overall really good. Can work more on the details
text: The hotel is clean and comfortable. It was recently renovated and they did a good job. A couple of things I suggest they work on: the room service is menu is very limited. It has less than a handful of salads and no soups. Breakfast is very expensive for such slim pickings. Coffee and a bagel go for about $19. Same menu at Starbucks around the corner goes for $6. I stayed here for 3 weeks. On the first weekend I went downstairs to have breakfast and the buffett service wasn't laid out. Another detail. I had requested the green option for room cleaning but nobody told me it also meant my toiletries didn't get replaced! I had to request then at the from desk and the next morning I found two sets of shampoo and conditioner while I still had 10 days left in my stay. Toiletries didn't get repalaced after that. They either tell you about this upfront or instruct the staff that not cleaning the room doesn't mean no toiletries. I will go back because I like the hotel overall and the attention is great. But I would love to see these two aspects taken care of.

author: EMF60
title: Great hotel
text: We liked this hotel right away. Very nice front desk staff and friendly. Our room was super nice and newly renovated. Everything was new. Very clean and pretty. Two complaints: pool and hot tub were filthy. I told the desk staff but nothing changed. It was still gross when we checked out. Also, the door that connected to another guest room was as thin as paper. Scary, because we heard every word from the room next store. Not interested in crying kids and their conversations. Oh well. Also the restaurant Sage was really great. Such nice wait staff, good food... loved the bar too. Overall, a super hotel steps from the Galleria.

author: Pastordsg
title: Remodeling
text: The hotel is under remodel. The ice machines do not work. Couldn't get hot water in the sink this morning but eventually got it. Parking is $13 extra per day, but that seems customary for the hotels in the area. The staff is extremely accommodating and were apologetic about the remodeling. I had to change rooms the first night because the traffic on the freeway was keeping me up, but they quickly changed me to an inside room (I am a very light sleeper). The suites are quite nice and roomy. The king sized bed is very comfortable, and I slept well. It is hard getting in and out in the traffic around the Galleria. The furniture is outdated, but again, they are remodeling. The fitness center is very nice. The price was right for the value you get. The area is very safe. The Galleria is only a couple of blocks away. Lots of restaurants nearby. I would stay here again, especially after the remodel.

author: texascouple25
title: Not fancy, but nice enough
text: My husband and I went to Houston last week for business. The hotel is nice and the front desk was very helpful and welcoming. Our room had a living room and a bedroom so that was nice. One thing that was really, really wierd was after we went to bed, the tv in the living room (1027) came on by itself. So, naturally, we got up and turned it off again. Then before 7 a.m., the tv in the bedroom AND the tv in the living room came on. Thankfully we were about to get up anyway. We thought that this was quirky. That morning while visiting with other attendees, I was telling them about the TVs and one said that their TV did the same thing! The decor of the hotel does need a facelift. It's basically a tan-colored interior. Another review calls it 'tired'. I'd agree with that. Not bad....just tired. We'll probably stay here again for business, but never as a couple get-a-way.

author: P2Pro
title: Great staff, but needs Improvement
text: I have stayed at this hotel on business twice in the past year or so. It was not booked on choice, but on proximity to the job I was doing. The layout of the rooms is nice, since it's a suite layout, with a living room area, a bedroom, and the bathroom/closet. My room had 2 flat screen tv's, one in the bedroom and one in the living room. The bed was comfortable, and the room was quiet, which was my primary need. The bathroom had terrible lighting, just one fixture and it using a eco bulb that took so long to "warm up" that you were finished before the light came on. The wallpaper was peeling off the walls, and the ceiling had some stains. As an added bonus, a dirty towel was hanging on the door hook. Not a great start. There is a small pool and hot tub, but it borders a parking lot. Not very appealing to me. There is also a restaurant in the hotel, but I skipped meals there. There is a 24 hour Starbucks within walking distance. The front desk and concierge staff of this hotel saves it. The hotel has a small shuttle that with a little advanced planning will take you around the city for free. I found the valet and bell hops to be attentive and friendly as well.

author: MrsRKC
title: Although it may be in the heart of the city...
text: I would give this particular Sheraton a thumbs down for family friendliness, bed comfort, water temperature, and parking. All which are very important! First, my family and I have been to many of the Starwood Hotels for business and pleasure; Westin, Four Points, Sheraton, etc., but this particular Sheraton's walls are so thin you can hear what ever drunken person has to say at 2:45 a.m. We felt like we were at a Motel 6. This latest stay we were awaken by the sounds of screaming, moaning, and calling out to God, it was disgusting, to say the least. We asked if someone could come up and ask our neighbors to cool it or take it down a notch so that we could get some rest but that didn't happen. Trust me, you DON'T want your kids at this hotel or if you are in town to take chemotherapy treatments at MD Anderson, choose another location! Second, the parking is $13 a day if you park yourself, are you serious? Or $20 a day if you want valet. Excuse me, I'm paying $154+ a night and you also want me to pay you to park? Never again... Lastly, you want to make sure you take a shower at night because in the morning there is NO HOT WATER, and don't bother calling and asking about it because it won't change anything. You will get a, "Yes, thank you so much, we will change that right away." But, don't expect any change. The BED WAS HARD AS A ROCK, this was not the Sheraton, or Westin sweet sleeper bed that we are accustomed to having when staying at Starwood hotels. Over all I would have to give this hotel a 2 on a scale of 1-10. The employess were friendly but everything else was not so great.

author: TravelDJ1981
title: Better than average hotel where efforts at service were made
text: I really enjoyed my time in Houston and this Sheraton Suites hotel was a main contributing factor. I loved the way this property was set up and the suites are a pretty nice size for the price. When I arrived, check-in was fairly swift and the fact that I enrolled in the "Starwood Preferred Guest" program allowed for my wife and I to have a room on the "Preferred Floor." The parking was a little odd to get to (and be prepared for the overnight $13 charges) and the spaces were a little limited on the floors in the garage that had covering so there were cases when we had to park on the roof (and it happened to be raining). That being said, I have traveled a good deal and have seen my share of suites and this one was better than average. The way the sitting area was closed off from the bedroom and bathroom allowed for us to have company but still maintain privacy. The bathroom included a magnifying mirror with a light (which my wife enjoyed) and their selection of bathroom amenities (body wash, shampoo, lotion) were more than expected. They do include a wet bar and a mini-fridge (surprisingly missing a microwave) in the sitting area which helps the feel of the suite. The staff is eager to assist each time you need something. When I went down to the front desk to grab a toothbrush and some toothpaste, they delivered it right to my room. I did have a problem when I pressed the guest services button on my phone to request extra towels and while they were more than willing to help, I did have to head downstairs from my room to the front desk three hours later to repeat my request before they finally delivered. Other than that, the breakfast buffet that came with our room package was fair, but not overflowing. It came with some meats, cereal, powdered eggs, oatmeal, biscuits, fruit, juice, coffee (all the regular stuff) and you could also get an egg prepared to your liking along with toast. So that was pretty good considering the only thing that we were responsible for was the gratuity. The location is literally two blocks from the Galleria, however I wouldn't walk there unless walking is your thing. And there's a ton of dining on Westheimer Road and other things to do in the area, so if you drive you should take full advantage of getting out and seeing what's out there. Overall my experience was great. They even returned the money to my debit card the day after I checked out (even though you sign a paper that says that it could take up to 10-14 business days). It was a great hotel for the price and if that's one of your considerations when you travel, I would recommend this one highly.

author: DayDreamerTraveler
title: Disappointing experience and very impersonal service
text: I had kind of high expectations regarding Sheraton Hotels, and I was glad when I learned that on my next business trip I was going to be able to stay there. Though my whole stay was fine, some aspects of the service were disappointing for me. Although I had a reservation, when I arrived in the morning they told me that the hotel was sold-out and I that I will have to wait. It was OK because I arrived way before the check-in hour. However, they told me that there were rooms available but the housekeeping staff started working at 10:00 am (It was 8:00 am at that moment). I went for breakfast in the meantime and came back at 11:00, but the room wasn’t ready yet. Finally, I had to wait until 5:00 pm to have my room. After a 14 hour flight, it’s not a good first impression. The lobby and the restaurant (Omaha Steak House) are less than average in comparison with the majority of the business hotels I’ve been to. The rooms, supposedly renewed recently, are also average. The decoration is totally impersonal, with an incredibly uncomfortable couch, a more than limited space to work, and poorly illuminated. The amenities kit was regular and, as the great majority of the hotels, with no particular consideration for women. I mean, some hotels provide make-up removing towels, shower gel and other feminine details as part of the amenities, etc. The bath tub and shower were very good, instead. I only used the restaurant for breakfast, which was kind of expensive for the kind of food they offer. There was not a great variety of dishes, just standard American breakfast, which people from abroad find sometimes too heavy and full of fat. Besides that, there were very few low-calories options. I’ve always had the idea of Sheraton being hotels of excellence; instead, I found it’s just no more than a regular hotel.

author: David5131
title: Perfect hotel, def worth staying here!!
text: I read TONS of reviews about hotels in the Galleria area (we were coming just for a couple days),and after looking at lots of reviews we settled on this hotel, and boy was it impressive. First it was easy to get to off the interstate, we got there around noon and figured what the hell lets try to check in early, walked in and within 4 min had the room keys ready to drop off luggage. Room was HUGE and very very nice. Bed was king size and incredibly comfy, two flat screen tv's, nice bathroom with vanity, the works. Only downside about room was the main couch, I felt it awkward and not too comfy, but def manageable. The site claims its a block away from the galleria mall, and I guess technically it is if you don't mind cutting through parking garages, other places, etc. But if you walk along the sidewalk like we did, more like two blocks. But still easily manageable. Now for the most impressive part. We get back from the galleria and wanted to go check out Dave & Busters restaurant. Walked in the lobby and I go ask the concierge about possible cab service. He asked where we needed to go, I told, and he said no worries, he will bring us in the hotels shuttle! So I told him when we were ready, he pulled it around, and for free (of course we tipped him) he drove us to the front entrance. Was perfect. He said he will come pick us up at anytime before 10:45, they stop at 11, and we were still drinking and playing games then so an $8 cab ride back the hotel and no worries about drinking and driving. Also, parking, while it is $12/day, is in a secure guarded parking garage which is very nice not to have to worry. Worth the money in my opinion. Overall, if you are looking for a clean, safe, and nice place close to EVERYTHING, stay here. Rooms are more than affordable and extremely nice. Also, I am a 26 year old male who stayed there with my girlfriend, also 26.

author: 1_brit_1_yank
title: In a great shopping area
text: Stayed at this hotel as we are spg members and collect the points. We stayed in a suite on the 15th floor and, facing the freeway. Other comments had mentioned traffic noise, but with the curtains being closed and the AC on, you couldnt hear the road. Room was spacious and clean, seperate living area with a fridge and sink. The decor in the room was nothing super-fancy, but the bed was comfy and me and my partner had two very relaxing nights. We ate at the Omaha steak house on our first night, pricey as most sheraton eateries are, but the steaks were done too perfection. Hubby enjoyed a well done sirloin, while i had a very tender filet. i wasnt too keen on the mash, thought it was a bit gummy, but hubby loved it, so, personal preference i guess. If you order extras, such as sides or dessert, the portions are HUGE! i had a side of broccoli, which was practically a tree, and a piece of chocolate cake to go. The piece of cake weighed atleast 2 lbs and took me 3 days to eat it! thankgod for the fridge in the room!! The area is nice and feels safe. The galleria is well worth a visit, and is right on the doorstep. Wear comfy shoes!! Also FYI, we flew into Hobby and took a taxi to the hotel, they charge an extra $6 ontop of the meter price, because its in a "downtown area", it came to about $45. Avoid yellow cabs if possible. This hotel may not look the fanciest from the outside, but did not disappoint. Clean, modern, comfy, convenient.

author: loveluxuryholidays_9
title: Excellent 4 star hotel
text: Went to Houston in April 2010 to attend a wedding and there were 6 of us (3 couples) staying at the Sheraton. We found the hotel to be excellent value for the price, the staff extremely friendly (particular Rex at the concierge desk) and we would not hesitate to stay here again if we came to Houston. Rooms This is an all suite hotel, and whilst there were not great views from any of the rooms (you don’t go to Houston for the views!) the rooms are large, with a separate living area, huge bed, bathroom, and separate sink and dressing table area. The suites also have complimentary tea and coffee making facilities and a decent sized fridge. The hotel does give out shampoo, conditioner and soap, but not shower gel. So if you want shower gel- remember to bring your own! Food We stayed on a room only basis and every morning we had breakfast in the Omaha Steakhouse. Full breakfast buffet costs approx $16-20 per person and offers a huge choice of hot and cold food, and they will make you eggs/pancakes/omelettes etc to order inc with the price. Room service was quick and efficient. Some of our party ate dinner in the hotel one night and said the service was slow. Other facilities The hotel has free wifi which was very handy. There are also 4 computers in reception with free printers that are very useful for plane check ins (and for keeping up with the volcanic ask situation). I did not use the gym but others in the party did and said it was nice. The pool looked old, unloved and was always empty so we stayed clear, the pool is the only negative I have about the hotel. Getting to the Galleria mall You can walk to the Galleria mall and it is only 5-10 mins away. You can walk along a path all the way and there are traffic crossing where you can wait and safely cross the road. The hotel will drive you to the mall for free if you prefer. The Galleria mall also contains restaurants and a food court if you want to eat there. Altogether excellent value for money stay!

author: Pharmarep1979
title: Not the best...
text: This hotel is nothing more than ok. It isn't really bad, but not great. The room was actually quite nice and was designed pretty well. The housekeeping staff appeared to be excellent. That's the good. The bad while not horrible, would keep me from staying here ever again. First, the traffic is pretty bad around here. If you don't mind that then, it will be ok. The lobby area had a bad smell to it, somewhat like raw sewage, but it came and went throughout the week I was there. There was a hotel power outage, that literally only affected the hotel. The guy at check-in was a little perturbed when I changed my mind about what credit card I wanted to use for incidentals, because I forgot about the parking charge. It really shouldn't take an attitude to change my mind about something they aren't going to charge me for until after I check out. I also had to go back to the lobby, after hauling everything to my room, because the key didn't work after I checked in. Also, my internet in my room was very spotty. It worked for one of the days, but not on the others. I called the desk to see if they could give me the IP address, (my computer uses Xandros Linux, and no one knows how to connect it, but by getting the correct IP, I can manually fix the problem), but they have an in-chouse computer tech and they couldn't give me an 800 number to a tech support person like the Hampton Inn or Hilton does. So I said, "ok send him up", but he never showed up and I figured it was more trouble than it was worth, and just used the computers that they have in the lobby, which were excellent. Free internet should work, though, otherwise, what's the point. Overall, wouldn't be a first choice, but would stay there in a pinch.

author: Algesoft
title: Pleasant stay
text: Great location. You can walk to Galleria, the famous Mecca of shopping. The rooms are ample, apartment style, with a mini refrigerator. Reception desk is staffed with excellent personnel. Very good gym with enough exercise equipment and enough to more than one person in the gym – not a small feat comparing with gyms of many “high end” hotels. The parking is extra, although not very expensive, and so is the breakfast. There is a two hundred dollars penalty for smoking in the room but my take is that the penalty is not enforced judging that I needed to change the room because the initial one was reeking of stale smoke. There was no problem in having my room changed. My only pet peeve is about the “shuttle services”. The hotel advertises for free transportation in a two and a half miles or so radius. Good luck to you! I tried to catch the shuttle about three times during my two days stay. Every time the concierge gave me a standard answer: “the shuttle will be back between five and ten minutes”. It never happened. You better take a taxi - unless you are the type of person who wins the lottery. What I found aggravating was that at one time there were two shuttles parked in front of the hotel with no drivers attending while people were waiting. But heck, that’s a small inconvenience for an excellent deal at this hotel – providing that you prepay the room.

author: chicagotraveldiva1
title: Questionable cleaning practices!
text: I stayed at The Sheraton Suites at the Galleria from 4/30-5/2. The hotel was ok for the rate (79/night). Rooms look a bit dated with old wallpaper. The fabric on the couch was rough and felt like an SOS pad & the cushions were so flat and worn that you felt like you directly on the bed underneath. Dont plan on sitting on the couch relaxing. Free wi-fi was nice. A microwave would have been helpful. Parking should have been free. All that being said, the accomodations were ok for the $$$. BUT here was my major issue, I found a "little blue pill" on the floor in the sleeping section of my room. After examining it closely w/the help of the internet, I realized it was VIAGRA. It was left there by the previous customer. The pill was clearly visible and had housekeeping vacumned thoroughly as they should after each customer, then they would have found it. I was concerned because my 4 yr old son was playing on the floor. He would have been very ill had he injested the pill.Hotel manangement's response? "We will waive your parking charges." Gee thanks Sheraton! Makes me wonder where else the cleaning staff took shortcuts. I would not recommend this hotel unless that rate was low.

author: 1travel5MV
title: Large Suites, Great Price, Nice Views/Location
text: My son and I stayed at the Sheraton Suites Near the Galleria for our visit to Rice University in Houston for my son. The hotel is very nice and either new or newly renovated. The lobby is a warm with wood walls and marble floors and the check in desk was very friendly and quick. We were on the 15th floor at the top for the Starwood Preferred Guests were there were some cookies, snacks, and water by the elevator for complimentary use. The best part of the hotel is the larger room size. It has a living room area with a LCD TV and then a bedroom, in our case two double beds, also with a tv. The bathroom had granite counters and the separate shower and toilet area had marble walls. In all I was pleased with the apperance and style of the room. It was an elegant look and the views on floor fifteen were very pretty, especially at night as the galleria area lights up. We did not eat at Omaha Steakhouse nor did we use the pool/gym. Free wireless internet in the rooms was a great plus. Be cautious when you exit the freeway from the north because the hotel is right there and you have to dart across four lanes of traffic. Look at a map to be safe and try to arrive not at rush hour. The location is walking distance to the Galleria mall though. I also appreciated the late check out as we were at Rice University during regular check out. The hotel just gave us new room keys for use after 12PM and let us leave at 2PM. All in all, a very good experience.

author: diva23
title: Spacious Suites
text: Just returned from a 3 night stay at Sheraton Suites and found it convienient to all shopping in the Galleria and other venues. Room decor is peaceful and spacious. Bed was very comfortable and loved the pocket doors that separated the living and sleeping areas. Check-in was without incident and no problem with keys to room. Breakfast buffet was varied with the best orange juice I've had in a long time. Staff for the most part were pleasant. The one shortcoming was the jacuzzi. Only in operation once during my stay.The water or jets weren't hot or strong enough. Problem in pool and jacuzzi area: Children used the jacuzzi as a wading pool because jacuzzi wasn't in operation!!!!!! Entire pool area was taken over by kids yelping and throwing things while some adults tried to get some sun or read. Maybe they should allow times for adults and kids to use pool/jacuzzi area. No shuttle from hotel to airport. They will take you to the Galleria which is within walking distance and pick you up. If you stay in your room for your entire stay it's a good place to rest. Diva 23

author: Chris_CNY
title: The devil's in the... details?
text: OK, let's start off how we should -- with the positives. As others have said, and really goes without question, this is a nice, well-appointed, very clean newer suite room that is sure to please just about anyone, especially when booked through and at the price this room can often be found on Hotwire. So that being said, two things bothered me, one a bit more than the other. I will let you decide -- for you -- which that is. 1) A missing VIP toiletry item: No, not shampoo or conditioner or the like, but maybe the most important of all -- this category's namesake... paper. At the critical moment, you reach, you look... nothing. You curse yourself for not noticing beforehand as you improvise. I understand that mistakes are made, but this can be (and was) a critical one, and has, in hundreds of hotel/motel stays, never happened to me until now. 2) Ordered an expensive bourbon neat in the lobby bar (which as they come, was for some reason I can't put my finger on, quite depressing), and was served what could subjectively be called a very exacting portion in what could ONLY be called an extremely dirty (in multi-hues) glass. When I politely pointed this out, the bartender got a clean glass, and started to pour the drink from one to the other. Yea. So when I slightly less-than politely balked, he (while nervously looking over his shoulder) poured another one that could have been a 4th grade lesson in surface tension out of that jigger. What bothered me most (aside from the attempted dirty-to-clean transfer) was that he conveyed a management dictate that it was more important to keep costs inline than make good on/make up for a mistake -- and show a bit of love in the process. The bartender seemed more concerned about controlling portion size than the hideously soiled glass. As I always say, YMMV.

author: TravelSheryl
title: Great Accommodations and Good Value
text: This hotel provides a great value. There is free wireless high speed in the rooms which isn't too common at full service hotels. During the first 45 minutes I was here, the high speed kept going down, then up, then down. I had to call for service 3 times. The engineer came up promptly and was very nice. They never could find the problem but it eventually corrected itself. A properly working Internet connection is very important to me. The room is lovely and very spacious. It has a refrigerator and a wet bar. Self-parking is $10/day. Valet parking is now $18/day. It's very quiet and the garage was almost empty when I arrived and throughout the weekend. I ordered room service twice while I was there and both times they met their 30 minutes or less delivery commitment and I was pleased with my order. In the afternoons, they provide free popcorn from a popcorn machine in the bar. You can get a bowl and take it back to your room. The only negative was the traffic to get to the hotel and to leave the hotel. The Sheraton Suites sits on a feeder road of a major freeway and it's a half a block to one of the busiest intersections in Houston. The traffic backs up really bad and there is only one entrance and one exit to/from the Sheraton Suites. I would definitely stay at the Sheraton Suites Houston Galleria again.

author: TheThreeOfUs
title: Very Good Value Here!
text: LOCATION -- You can walk to the Galleria, though the hotel will provide a shuttle within 3 miles. STAFF -- Accomodated an early check-in request after an early flight, with no problem. ACCOMODATIONS -- Everything was in great condition. Tastefully decorated, smartly-designed rooms (and, yes, the bureau drawers *are* in the dressing area, not in the bedroom area. We liked the arrangement. ) Probably the best black-out curtains of any hotel I've stayed in recently. The beds are comfy and the linens are of good quality. There's a fridge and a bar sink in the rooms, along with coffee maker and hair dryer. VALUE -- Free wireless access. Parking is $10 self, $15 valet per day. We didn't eat in the hotel restaurant, because there are so many other choices nearby, but in quickly scanning the Room Service menu, the prices seemed reasonable. We got it for $45 on Hotwire, and were *very* pleasantly surprised by the quality for the money. RECOMMENDATION -- The hotel itself was very, very quiet, but I'd recommend asking for a room on the back side of the hotel. A major freeway is adjacent to the hotel. If the hotel isn't crowded (which it wasn't when we stayed there), I have no doubt the staff will 'make it so.'

author: Gaff313
title: Home away from home
text: Our experience with Marjorie's began with correspondence with Alexis, who provided invaluable information for planning the trip. On arrival, the accommodations were exactly as described. The rooms are not large, but are certainly large enough for two. The lanai was more than large enough (we stayed in the Valley View unit), and does have a very nice view. Sarah is a most gracious host. Whatever you need, she will help you with. We stayed for ten days, and like to travel light, which means we need to wash clothes. We were able to use the washer and dryer, as long as we worked around Sarah's schedule. The breakfast was a high point each day. Great opportunity to sit with the other guests and chat over a good meal. On days where you are leaving too early for the breakfast, Sarah puts up a breakfast for you, which is left in your refrigerator the evening before. The location is very convenient to the beaches at Po'ipu, and is about an equidistant drive to the sights of the Waimea Canyon and the North Shore. The Inn is about 600 feet above sea level, with good exposure, so there's a cool breeze all the time. We never once even thought about using the AC in the room. Going forward, we wouldn't stay anywhere else.

author: 584beauk
title: What a Jewel!
text: From the time we made our reservation (several months ahead) and throughout our stay we felt comfortable and welcome, like we were meeting old friends and visiting their home. But it was so much more. Our accommodations were spacious, clean and well-appointed. And the view of the Lawai Valley was beautiful! We saw rainbows almost every day and parrots that perched in the lush vegetation that graces the grounds of the property. What a treat. Breakfast was always delicious, every morning with gourmet baked goods that you just couldn’t get enough of! The owner-hosts, Alexis and Mike, were so helpful with recommendations for interesting hikes, the best beaches, local restaurants, and suggestions/directions to anywhere you might want to go. During our stay the weather was against us, but our stay was really wonderful despite that. Coming back to Marjories, after a day out and about, felt comfortable and warm, like coming home. And sitting on the lanai watching the sun disappear – a serene ending to any Hawaiian day. And did we forget to mention how well we slept? Well – it was restorative, divine. We’ll come back, for sure. Thank you, Alexis, Mike, and Sarah!

author: AlanandCarla
title: Fantastic
text: A great inn consists of two components. First, it must have a good physical appearance and ambiance.Second, and equally important, is the service and hospitality provided. This Inn was exceptional in both regards. The property is beautiful, sitting on the edge of a cliff. We stayed in the sunset view room, which afforded breathtaking views, along with its own lanai and hot tub. The property also featured a beautiful 50 foot saltwater pool along with a gazebo. Sunsets and rainbows were abundant and fantastic. The service and hospitality were outstanding. Although Alexis and Mike, the owners, were out of town, we were exceptionally assisted by the innkeeper, Sara, who went out of her way to make us feel at home and welcome. She fixed gourmet breakfasts and allowed us to make sandwiches to take with us for the noon meal. Sara was attentive to every detail and request that we made. She is one of the best innkeepers we have ever met in our many travels. Overall the Inn was fantastic. It was one of our best trips ever. We hope to return.

author: TahoeTravler
title: A taste home
text: We stayed here for our 10-year anniversary trip last May. They didn't have availability for the entire duration so we ended up staying here one night, 2 nights at another B&B, then here 3 nights in a different room. Alexis makes the most amazing pastries and breakfast items. We were excited to rush upstairs and discover her daily treats. She even made us Lattes each morning! Breakfast is served buffet style and you sit with the other guests. Everyone we met was super nice and we shared tips and ideas about things to do. Alexis, Mike, and the occasional neighbor would sit and eat with us. (No joke, random people would come in to say "hi" and hang out. They have a liberal open-door policy that reminds me more of a small farming community than a world-renowned vacation town :) Mike and Alexis truly open their home to people even though the house is designed specifically as a B&B. They let you borrow chairs, towels, snorkel gear, snacks, water, and more. We had an evening flight but they had to flip the room for another guest. They apologized for the "inconvenience" and let us store our suitcases in the garage, swim in the pool after checking out, and even use their private bathroom to shower and change. They helped us book a sunset cruise which turned out to be in the top 2 favorite things we did in Kuai. We would have never of gone if it wasn't for Alexis' recommendation. This catamaran company actually parked under the waterfalls and went part-way into a sea cave. No other boats were getting this experience (wish I remember which company it was, ask Alexis, she probably knows)

author: miaaco
title: An exceptional bed & breakfast - highly recommended!
text: My wife and I recently enjoyed a 7-night stay in the Valley View Room at Marjorie's Inn. Everything about this inn is remarkable. The room was very comfortable, extremely clean, and had a huge lanai with a spectacular view. Breakfast was served between 7:30 and 9:00 am on the upstairs lanai and always included both continental items as well as a delicious hot entree. Neither my wife or myself are very extroverted people, but we both really enjoyed chatting with the other guests over breakfast - in fact, we enjoyed it so much that we often got a later start than anticipated to our day's activities! What makes this inn truly special, however, is the warm hospitality of Alexis and Mike, the owners. You could not ask for more friendly and accommodating hosts. They are always willing and available to provide a wealth of information on the island, activities, places to eat, things to do, etc. They have a garage full of items for guests to use, free of charge. We made good use of the beach towels, beach chairs, and coolers during our stay. Alexis was always willing to pack lunches or food-to-go. Most importantly, they really treated us like family during our stay. On our last day on the island, we had a late night flight from the airport, and Alexis offered to let us use the entire inn (except our room of course) for the whole day, including offering up her own futon and shower. While we didn't take her up on this offer, we really appreciated the thoughtful gesture. The kindness and hospitality of the hosts made our stay very relaxed and enjoyable. We enthusiastically recommend Marjorie's Inn to anyone looking for a quiet, comfortable, and unique bed & breakfast experience. This place is really a gem. When we travel, my wife and I specifically seek out bed & breakfasts like this one, as we enjoy the quiet, personal, and intimate atmosphere that is generally not found at hotels and resorts. However, it seems like there are very few true B&B's on Kauai, so for people like ourselves, being able to stay at a really exceptional B&B like Marjorie's Inn is a great reason to travel to Kauai. We look forward to staying here again if we ever return to the island.

author: amibelmont
title: Amazing beautiful luxurious getaway.
text: We had an absolutely amazing stay at Marjorie's inn. My husband and I stayed there in March of this year. We have traveled all over the world and this by far was one of very favorite places. This inn has the perfect combination of luxury and comfort, with amenities to make you feel right at home. It had the warmth of being invited into someone's home, yet the privacy of a hotel. The owners Alexis and Mike, as well as the manager Sarah, make this place truly exceptional. The accommodations were well-kept, beautifully appointed, with many little details to keep us comfortable (e.g., extra towels, robes, slippers). We had the room with the private hot tub, which offered gorgeous views of they valley and made for relaxing ends to the days. They have an amazing garage full of any/all beach and travel accessories you could dream of (sun screen, aloe, toothpaste, as well as a plethora of snorkeling sets, beach bags, magazines, beach chairs, etc). Alexis and Sarah are eager to suggest and help you book whatever activities you are interested in (sailing cruises, helicopter flights, hikes, etc etc) I could rave for days about the breakfasts. Every day there is a fresh baked absolutely delicious bread and a rotating sweet item (e.g., chocolate cherry cake, blueberry clafoutis, mini bundt cakes). There's always a fresh fruit/vegetable juice, served in a champagne flute and fresh fruit/yogurt galore. There's also a breakfast item of the day, like waffles or quiche. Whats more is they make extra and encourage you to take it with you, which is great when you have a hike planned. On a more personal note, my husband and I really enjoyed getting to know Alexis and Mike. They are down-to-earth, engaging, and have many fascinating stories to tell. It was truly a pleasure getting to know them, as well as the warm staff they have hired. I cannot recommend Marjorie's Inn more highly!! Stay here, it will be the highlight of your trip!!!

author: 784nilsw
title: The perfect choice for our last days on Kauai
text: We spent the last three nights of our Kauai trip at Alexis' & Mike's house and we can only tell you this: Go there, if you're on the Garden Island! The rooms are just perfect and equipped with everything you need. Each room also has a big lanai with view over the rainbow valley (unbelievable in the mornings, so many rainbows to see). Alexis & Mike were wonderful hosts, giving us great tips which hikes to do or where to go to in the evening. The breakfast they prepare is outstanding! There's always fresh juice or smoothies, homemade bread and cake (Alexis even baked a Gugelhupf for us Germans), cereals, eggs, fruit, something warm (e.g. one day Mike prepared crepes with goat cheese and tomatoes that were absolutely delicious) and more. Both were just super kind and let us even prepare sandwiches to take for our hikes. We have never experienced that in any other B&B. Simply perfect. And: You can ask Alexis for anything you might need, I am pretty sure she has it available in the house (cooling boxes, sunscreen, snorkeling gear etc. etc.). Super well equipped house! We really could not have chosen a better place to stay for our last nights on Kauai and felt very welcome the minute we walked into the house. Thank you for that, Alexis & Mike!

author: AliFromBedford
title: The Most Luxurious B&B We've Ever Experienced!
text: Alexis and Mike have worked diligently to make Marjorie's Kauai Inn a resounding success. Their B&B overlooking the Lawai Valley is breathtaking and the birdsong is beautiful. They keep the 3 ensuite rooms spotless and there are fresh towels and sheets daily. We are sharing the Sunset View Room with our teenager and the room is spacious enough for a very good extra mattress they've put onto a frame and we've simply kept up for our stay. We also have a lovely lanai with a private hot tub that we've used frequently. Their buffet breakfasts are delicious and plentiful: cut fresh fruit, hot freshly baked bread, a different savory dish daily, and so many other taste treats! Yogurts, cheeses, meats, and coffee and tea are available, too. Breakfasts are shared on the large lanai, right next to their state of the art kitchen. And as you enjoy your breakfast, it may rain a bit. Then come the rainbows. There's much to see and do on the South Shore and both Alexis and Mike and Sarah are more than eager to share their recommendations and experiences. They provide so much information and it is so helpful. They are enthusiastic and kind and they mean it when they tell you to think of their place as your home. Their garage is filled with more towels, beach chairs, sunscreen, ice packs, coolers, and a washer and dryer, which is so handy. Really nice not to have to find a laundry and take time away from the fun stuff. Remember though, that some of that fun is right here at the Inn. Their 50' salt water pool is heavenly and the Bali Hut - from Bali!- provides shade and coolness even during the hottest part of the day. Spending time reading, writing, or simply listening to the valley and watching the changing clouds and verdant foliage is well worth it. Relaxation at its best.

author: RichandBarb
title: Gorgeous Valley View Rural Scenery
text: We enjoyed our 3 night stay in the Valley View room which was very comfortable. It even had a small AC unit which cooled the room from the afternoon heat; did need need AC in the evening or at night to sleep. The breeze and rural night sounds were very welcoming. The room has a large scenic corner lanai where we could enjoy "happy hour" and even "take out" one night. A great place to stay for a rural Hawaiian feel; so much better than busy hotels. There was a welcoming tray of sweets, fruit, and nuts in our room refrigerator. Coffee and teas were also in our small kitchenette for early risers. Sipping coffee on a beautiful lanai in the cool morning breeze, PERFECT. Our host, Mike, was very gracious, informative, and accommodating. He has a variety of beach equipment for guests to use. Even let us use the washer and dryer which was a big help. His gourmet breakfasts were outstanding. Delicious baked treats, cereals, fruits and home made juices along with various egg dishes served on the upstairs lanai. Sorry we did not meet Alexis who was unable to be there. Mahalo Mike.

author: TravelBugTennessee
title: Comfortable Inn. Lovely hosts, amenities & view. AMAZING breakfasts...
text: Based on Trip Advisor community ratings, we booked 4 nights in the last room available at MKI. SO glad we did! The directions to the Inn were good (it's located a ways from the airport - yay!) and though it was after hours, there were clear instructions on room access and a surprise. :) The bed was comfortable and the fan and in-room air conditioning appreciated. There was a nice breeze but we'd just come from snow... Kauai has been populated with wild chickens/roosters for years now, so there is abundant crowing at all hours. They are all over the island so you'll see/hear them on your adventures. The a/c and fan noise as well as ear plugs were helpful. We live in the country so their presence made us feel more at home. :) We met the hosts and other guests in the main room upstairs next morning and what a breakfast spread. YUMMO! Every day was a different main course, but they ensured a few faves daily, including various freshly squeeze juices. (The husband & wife team live on property.Their 35+ years of inn keeping experience shows.) The hosts gave us tips on where to go and what to do, and provided a nice cooler too. There is a gorgeous pool on property and 2 hot tubs. (If there is a negative, it is the *steep* driveway slope to access the Inn. They made accommodation for an older couple to park near the entry which was good. There are only 3 rooms so we worked out the parking to everyone's satisfaction I think. As I say it is VERY steep but if your group walks/hikes like we do, it's not much of an issue.) Really wonderful stay, great hosts, thoughtful abundant breakfasts... Perfect for our Kauai visit. Highly recommended!

author: Graphiker
title: Wish I could have a house like this on Kauai
text: I loved the warmth and serenity of Marjorie's Kauai Inn. Built on a hillside, all 3 rooms overlook a valley. Our room was attractively decorated; all 3 rooms had lanais. Air conditioning was a plus, for several reasons - keep reading. What makes this B&B a standout is the superb breakfasts; Alex is a great cook. She also made reservations for dinner for us at local restaurants; those were the best meals we had during our trip to Kauai. The Inn is fully stocked for trips to the beach - you don't have to bring anything. Boogie boards, coolers, ice packs, chairs, towels - I probably jhave overlooked something. I got great photographs of Japanese White-eye birds in the garden. The roosters - chickens overrun Kauai - did not wake us. Again, another advantage of an in room air conditioner. Guests have access to the Inn's washer & dryer. There's a beautiful garden surrounding the Inn; also a long, narrow salt water pool, excellent for doing laps. A great place to stay to explore Kauai's magnificent Waimea Canyon and the local beaches. The only down side was the quantity of mosquitoes outside (we were there in November, could it be different in other months?). Not a problem at breakfast on the main floor lanai, but afternoons on ours were interrupted by these troublesome insects. We went forced to retreat to our room and turn on the A/C. We recovered from our itchy bites quickly, thanks to Alexis who came to the rescue with calamine lotion.

author: oneyearoff
title: The inkeepers thought of everything
text: We stayed in the Trade Winds room (see photos) for 2 days in late January. I loved the quilt on our bed so much that I Googled Palm Tree Quilt and found it at Macys.com and ordered it before we went to dinner! Everything you could possibly need is provided at Marjorie's. The kitchenette was well supplied, and they can lend you any kind of beach equipment, including coolers, fins, hiking poles, etc. you could possibly need. A beautiful snack tray was waiting for us on arrival, and the breakfasts prepared by Ina and Rob were outstanding. We went to Hanapepe for the Friday night art walk and had dinner at one of the restaurants serving outside. This restaurant was known for its Hula Hula chicken and the line proved how popular it was. Tip: order ONE order for two people. It's a huge, half a chicken with sides and way too much for one person. Cash only. Then find the pie stand and get a fabulous piece of lilikoi cheesecake. It was a beautiful way to spend an evening, full of tourists and locals alike - a real sense of community. Check out the used bookstore - excellent titles. We didn't use the pool at the inn as it was a bit breezy, but I imagine it's a perfect spot on a warm day. When you go down the driveway, bear left, or you end up at another house. Once you get to Marjorie's, it feels secluded and cozy, with a beautiful view over a canyon. Highly recommended!

author: sophiad853
title: Quite simply the best b&b I've ever stayed in..
text: It's hard to have the words to describe my short experience at Marjorie's. From the moment I arrived in Kauai, I was taken care of by Alexis and Mike (the owners). I felt totally at home immediately, and as a lone traveller, less daunted by my experience, knowing Alexis and Mike were so helpful. I didn't have a car, and my plans fell through, so Alexis tried to organise everything for me without me even needing to ask. She was calling around car places, and trying to find me another place to stay once I left there. Totally above and beyond the call of duty. The b&b itself is beautiful, with gorgeous views, and it's really clean. Every morning, you get the most delicious breakfast, and everyone sits around chatting before they start their day. Every detail is taken care of. Advice about the island is given freely, and nothing is too much trouble. The only downside for me, was that I didn't get to stay longer. These guys get booked up, so I'd suggest getting in quick to avoid disappointment! I'll be back for sure. A massive thank you to A&M for being such lovely people, and wonderful hosts. X

author: slisse
title: Perfect B&B
text: The 4 nights that we stayed in the Sunset Room were wonderful! The room is cosy, romantically decorated and offers amazing views from the spacious private lanai. We also enjoyed our very own hot tub, from which we could witness the sunrise in the morning are the bright stars in the evening. Alexis is a great hostess. She made us feel so welcome upon arrival, although we were very early. She gave us tips and tricks for places to see as well as restaurants to go to. They indeed turned out to be as good as she promised! She also immediately arranged the reservation for a boat tour and made it clear that we could use all of the stuff in the garage (snorkel gear, towels, surf boards, cooling aids,…). We feel that the breakfast is of course a very important aspect in a B&B. Describing it as “good” would be an understatement, to say the least. The choice was abundant and every morning Alexis made a different hot dish herself, which was even better. On Sunday, when there is no breakfast served, she prepared a basket which again included all kinds of delicious treats, which we could enjoy at our private lanai. We didn’t even have to ask for it – it was prepared and put in the fridge the night before! This was our very first B&B experience and we feel it will be pretty tough to beat this one, as the bar has been set really high! Thank you, Alexis, for your kind attention and care! Mahalo!

author: 336keni
title: Great service; unique location
text: Marjorie's is a wonderful B&B. It is the last property on a road above the Lawa'i Valley. It was neat to go onto our lanai just before the sun rose and watch the valley wake up. First the white cattle egrets could be seen down below flying up the valley. Then mynah birds, doves, and cardinals arrived in the trees close to us. There were often rainbows over the valley. One morning the rainbow lasted for more than 40 minutes! The sun sets on the far side of the valley. One evening we were treated to a lightning show in the direction of Kokee State Park. Normally vacation diet is pretty basic. Activities are a higher priority. But we looked forward to the gourmet breakfasts that Mike and Alexis served on their lanai. Also they would spend time visiting with us about what we had seen and making suggestions about other things to do. They said "We want this to be your home on Kauai. How can we help you?" We always had the pool and whirlpool to ourselves since there are only three units. We loved this place!

author: P7117CJmaryp
title: B&B/Inn Review Fabulous
text: Warm and welcoming from the moment we arrived! This place exceeded our expectations. Alexis's thought of everything that a guest could possibly need and more! The view of the valley is breathtaking and calms your senses immediately. She was great at suggesting local places for great dinners and setting up reservations for us. She had maps and ideas for any type of day activities we might be interested in. We thoroughly enjoyed the activities she suggested. The Allen gardens were beautiful. We had the SunView room with the hot tub on our deck, which we used every night gazing up at the stars. Loved it! The breakfast was just fabulous and Alexis was every bit interested in pleasing individual needs. Met some lovely people visiting there as well. We will definitely visit this place again. Warmest thanks Alexis for a wonderful stay! Mahalo!

author: DarrP
title: Should've stayed all 7 nights here! Excellent!
text: Stayed in the Tradewinds Room 3 nights in early May. Spent 4 nights elsewhere. Why? Can't think of a reason now! The Inn's price is right. Room very comfortable for a couple, clean, modern. Inn location allows easy access to rest of island. Mike's breakfasts and conversation--great! Lanai view over the valley at breakfast--fantastic. Plenty to do in the vicinity. Good advice from Mike regarding touring options. Beach and related gear available for guest use. All pros, no cons from our perspective. Made our stay on Kauai all the more memorable. Thanks, Mike.

author: 509michelleg509
title: First night in Kauai and we were blown away!
text: I randomly ended up calling this Inn and I am sooo glad I did. When we got to the island we called the Inn to see if we could possibly drop out stuff off while we explored the beaches. She said thay would be fine so we headed up. the inn keeper we so nice and accommodating! She offered us water and refreshments while she got to know us and showed us all around the property. They have everything you could think of needing... Beach towels, chairs, ice chest, snorkel gear, boogie boards, sun screen.... Everything! So we left for the after noon and when we came back we checked into our room and it was so cute! A perfect Room with a view of the whole valley. It was sooooo peaceful and beautiful. In the fridge she left snacks for us. Bottled water, home made banana bread, cheese and fruit, chocolates.... It was so great. We slept with all the windows and doors open that night and waking up to the sun and roosters was so peaceful. I would come back here in a heartbeat over the crowded resorts down at the ocean just a few miles away!

author: 899elainer
title: Our Vacation
text: My husband and I stayed in the Sunset Room from 12/25/13 until 1/1/14. We were so sad to leave because we were returning to a foot of snow back in New York! The room was clean, had a great view and we loved the hot tub. At times, we could hear the roosters and sometimes people in the adjoining rooms, but that is part of staying in Kaui and at a bed and breakfast. We didn't have Alexis or Mike but to our surprise guest innkeepers Luanne and Gary. They were very nice. Gary makes a good fruit salad and 4x as a bonus he made a hot treat for breakfast mainly for husband who loves eggs, pancakes and French toast. Gary also spent a lot of time each day giving us suggestions of things to do. I took advantage of many things in the garage a day pack, water shoes, and chairs (thank you for providing them). I also used the washer and dryer before leaving for New York (Thank you Luanne). I am a "walker" and felt very safe in the neighborhood walking around. I even met an 82 year old man on their block that gave me tangerines from his tree, and JR the landscaper that told me all about the property. My only suggestion which I related to Luanne was maybe if a guest innkeeper is substituted the arriving guest can just receive an email stating so. I like Gary very much, but was unsure of who he was until he further explained himself. However, please only take this as a suggestion. Overall ...great place we will be back to visit and thank you again! Elaine and Wayne Long Island New York :)

author: Dam0007
title: A great find and would love to go back
text: Majories was 5 nights well spent. As first time visitors to the island we were very happy with the choice. After we arrived Alexis was able to provide great advice on where to go as well as places to eat. Lots of tips that made things a little easier and that much more enjoyable. The garage is full of gear that you are able to make use of. There is also a washer and dryer that we were able to use. We talked with Alexis about a helicopter flight around the island. A company was recommended and Alexis took care of the booking for us. All part of the service. Breakfast was plentiful and great quality. Mike does a great job here. Eating out on the Lani was very comfortable. Lovely views. It is a great time to meet up with other travellers. We met people from Germany, various states of the US and fellow Aussies. We particularly enjoyed sitting with Mike and Alexis, chatting and enjoying a coffee. Some people we met were staying a few nights on either side of the island. We found basing ourselves at Marjories for the duration of our stay worked just fine. Mike and Alexis are fantastic hosts. Thank you.

author: jmjbrtw
title: Excellent Hospitality
text: We stayed 5 nights at Marjories while visiting Kauai on our Hawaiian vacation. The location is very convenient to explore the island of Kauai. Its about a 10 minutes ride to the beach. It is tucked into a residential neighborhood. Mike the host, showed us excellent Hospitality while there and was very helpful with sightseeing information. The rooms were extremely clean with views to die for overlooking the valley. Breakfasts were great, plentiful and healthy. We saw a rainbow every morning while eating breakfast on the covered deck chatting with Mike and the other guests. They had boogie boards and coolers and other stuff for guest to use which was nice. They even allow you to use washer and drier which helped on amount of clothes we needed to pack. There is a pool and hot tub which was nice to use after hiking. There are plenty of chickens there just like the rest of Kauai. We even saw a couple wild pigs eating the mangoes that fell off Mike's trees. The gardens at Marjories are beautiful. We highly recommend a stay at Marjories when Visiting Kauai. We like staying at BBs rather then hotels when we vacation, we feel we get a more authentic experience.

author: Aellsonatc
title: Amazing!!
text: We decided to try a bed and breakfast during our honeymoon and we are so glad we tried Marjorie's!! We were met by Mike and he took us into our room that had a kitchenette and amazing lanai!! We had such a great view! We had to leave the next morning early for a catamaran tour and they put a breakfast basket together in our fridge since we would be missing breakfast! We loved the salt water pool, and the hot tub! Great views of the valley to enjoy! We loved the lanai and loved enjoying the nights and mornings in it! We had access to snorkel gear, beach chairs, and boogie boards. Alexis and Mike even let us use their laundry as we had been traveling for over a week! Breakfasts were awesome! Such great meal and foods! Lots of fresh fruits that we had never tried! It was fun to chat with the other guests and hear their stories! We loved staying at Marjorie's and will be staying there again when we visit Kauai! Thanks Mike and Alexis!!!!

author: ChainsawJim
title: Just returned from my third stay
text: I can't imagine staying in a hotel in Kauai as long as Marjorie's is available. We have now celebrated our 20th, 25th, and now 30th anniversaries on Kauai, staying at Marjorie's each time. To echo previous reviewers, it just keeps getting better each time we stay. Leisurely full/hot breakfasts on a spacious lanai overlooking the lush Lawai valley. In tune with the local culture, Mike is "very organic" in his shopping habits, so we always enjoy the healthiest and most flavorful breakfasts with fresh fruit and cheeses with a different smoothie every day (the pineapple/pear/ginger is my favorite). We always stay in the very spacious Sunset View room with a private lanai (west facing with beautiful sunsets) and jacuzzi. Staying at Marjorie's is a bit like coming home... the garage is jam packed with coolers of every size, chairs for the beach, snorkel stuff, just about anything you would have in your own garage if you lived a few minutes from the beach. Mike is also great with local restaurant, beach and cultural advice. Wonderful conversations with other guests from all over the world at breakfast.
