Peaceful tradewinds that lull you to sleep at night. Bottom line... Marjorie's is everything and more that I hope for in a B&B experience. Is there a down side? There really isn't one, but in jest I will just say: Wow...that driveway! Marjorie's is literally carved into a hillside so yes, the steep sloped driveway will remind you of San Fran or Boston. The turnaround to get back out is tricky the first few times, but well worth mastering.

author: worldflyer74
title: Heaven
text: This was our second time visiting Marjorie's and it was as fabulous this time as the last. Our first stay was back in 2000 when Marjorie owned it. We couldn't imagine what it would be like with new owners. Wow! Alexis & Mike took what Marjorie started and improved it...which I didn't think was possible. Mike & Alexis are the best hosts you could hope for. If you are thinking it might be strange to stay in a house with strangers while on vacation isn't for you, please think again. When you arrive, they treat you like family. They take you to your room and then invite you up to their floor to show you around and give you pointers on where to go. We were there for our 10th wedding anniversary and knew which restaurants we were thinking of trying but didn't know for sure. Alexis was able to give us her thoughts and then called the restaurant and made a reservation for us. The garage of items to borrow make your vacation so much better. Besides the beach chairs, beach towels, mats, snorkle gear, coolers, water bottles, etc... It makes a trip to the beach or a hike so much better when you have your gear and don't have to pay to rent and deal with the lines. The rooms are as nice as any resort I've ever stayed in. We always stay in the smaller room which does get really hot when the sun sets but you get to see the beautiful sun set over the mountains. It has a TV, fridge, chairs & bookshelf (with books left behind from others) in addition to the lanai with comfy chairs. I highly recommend this place to first time and seasoned visitors to Kauai. It's a nice way to start and end a trip with friends.

author: AlexandraN222
title: Best Place to Stay
text: My husband and I took a week vacation and stayed here at Marjorie's Inn. We arrived in the afternoon and have to admit that when we first got there were actually weren't sure about the place. I really seemed like someone's home. Fred and Veronica met us in the driveway with smiling faces and showed us around the property. We stayed in the Valley View room and it was unbelievable. As soon as we walked in (from our private entrance) our eyes were immediately drawn to the view from our private lani (which all rooms have). Our room was so cute and cozy and the bed was so very comfortable. We sat in the jacuzzi every night with a glass of wine/beer listening to the sounds of nature watching the sunset. Couldn't get any better... until the breakfast. This was my first time in hawaii and the food is not that great! Aside from the few delicious meals we had breakfast was by far our favorite. Fred and Veronica would set up everything fresh in the morning by 730. We had a whole selection of fresh fruit, pastries, yogurts, homemade granola from the island and an assortment of delicious French cheeses. If that weren't enough, Fred and Veronica would make fresh homemade juice and one special main, such as crepes,french apple tatin, and quiche.Between the hospitality and Marjorie's Inn everything was wonderful and we didn't want to leave. If we ever find our way back to Kauai, Marjorie's Inn will definitely be the place we stay!

author: robins504
title: Do one fun thing everyday
text: My husband and I were celebrating our 25th wedding anniversary with another couple who were celebrating their 29th anniversary. What drew us to the place was the view and the pool. My girlfriend and I were training for a triathlon and needed to do some swimming. They have a fabulous lap pool that was so refreshing and perfect for us to keep training. The motto at the inn is to"do one fun thing everyday". In the pool on the tiles on the bottom of the pool, the motto was written. Therefore it became our challenge everyday to do more than one fun thing everyday. Certainly Mike and Alexis' breakfasts were the first fun thing of the day. The food was healthy and delicious. The rooms were clean and the lanai was great. We watched the goats and horses in the fields below during the day and watched the stars at night. The inn is on the south part of the island and it is easy to get to the south shore and Waimea Canyon. If you've read anything about Kauai, you know that the roosters are prevalent everywhere, and they make noise at anytime of the day or night. However there were no roosters that were very near to Marjorie's (you could hear them in the distance). Hot tip was that if you put the fan up on the table (they have them in every room) and turn it on medium or high, you'll drown out the rooster noise almost completely. We thought we were enjoying ourselves on vacation as it was, but when we arrived at the inn, our whole attitude changed and we started seeking out not only what was good about Hawaii, but what was quite memorable. It makes you want to sit back and smell the ginger.

author: Roams-A-Lot
title: Paradise in Paradise!
text: My wife and I recently spent 5 wonderful days at Marjorie’s Kauai Inn. This is easily one of the best B&Bs that we have ever stayed in! The room was spacious and had all the amenities. It opened onto a large balcony overlooking a serene, lush, green valley. Below is the large salt-water pool, hot tub and barbecue. All of this amid a beautifully landscaped property. Once at the Inn, you are totally secluded from the hustle-bustle of the island. It is quiet and beautiful. You truly feel like you are in paradise! The garage is stocked with everything you could need for your holiday - boogie-boards, beach mats, towels, snorkel gear, etc. - all available for the guests. And one of the highlights, of course, was the expansive breakfast. This was prepared each morning by our wonderful guest-hosts Fred and Veronica. In addition to a selection of breads and cereals, there was always fresh tropical fruit, scones, AND freshly prepared items ranging from crepes to French toast to waffles, etc., as well as freshly-squeezed juice. Breakfast was served on the lanai overlooking the tranquil valley below. Really an amazing experience! We couldn’t have been happier with our visit to Marjorie’s. Fred and Veronica were “over-the-top” hosts who made an outstanding visit even better! Highly recommended!

author: Rainahune
title: A wonderful experience
text: We had a truly delightful experience here and ended up making a friend. We could only stay for two nights because of limited availability and wish we could have stayed the entire trip here. Marjorie's is conveniently located at a short-distance drive from Poipu. We stayed in the Tradewinds room, which was spacious, clean, and tastefully furnished, with a wonderful view of the valley from our lanai. Our favorites were the pool and hot tub overlooking the gorgeous Lawai Valley. We felt it was more charming to stay here compared to choosing a hotel in Poipu. The inn has a nicely equipped stock room filled with boogie boards, snorkels, bug spray, etc and things you might need out on a day at the beach or hiking the rugged mountains of Kauai. I guess there is a possibility of hearing your neighbors as in any B&B but this being Kauai, people seem to get to bed early enough and it was quiet. Overall, after a long day being out and about, this is a great place to come back to relax in the hot tub and pool before hitting the bed (which was comfortable). This review would be incomplete without talking about our inn-keeper, Veronika. She made it easy to look forward to starting the day with a cheerful greeting and wonderfully fresh, hearty, and healthy breakfast. She took a lot of trouble to help plan our day with activities and all the bookings, making it a point to give us all the information, vouchers and maps that we needed. She even went way above and beyond her calling to help my girlfriend out with some unfortunate car trouble. Veronika's warmth and sense of humor made our stay in Kauai all the better. Note: Watch out for speed traps on Poipu road (15mph and 25mph speed limits). I got a ticket for doing 36 at 6AM. This was even in the guide book (which I read a little too late).

author: MasTadesse
title: Perfect Retreat!
text: From the very start, Alexis and Mike delivered on everything they said we were getting. The description of their home is spot on. This home has all the amenities we would expect from a B&B. The innkeepers, Veronika and Fred were very friendly, accommodating and greeted us at the door with a smile! Marjorie's Kauai Inn is very clean; we had fresh linens, towels and living space. We had a mini- fridge which held leftovers, wine, and beer. We also had our own mini-coffee pot, microwave and counter space in the TradeWinds Room. There is a Gas Grill which we did not get the opportunity to use, but a washer and dryer which we needed. The grocery store is a few miles away. We found many boogie boards, snorkel gear in the garage. We spent our early mornings on the porch in patio chairs overlooking the valley. Having rented a lot of vacation homes over the years, Alexis, Mike, Veronika and Fred are great people to work with; they made our stay in paradise! Veronika and Fred were so helpful with booking our excursion; they even printed turn-by-turn directions so we knew how to get there. Breakfast is continental; fresh fruit, baked breads, and something warm like crepes, or specialty omelette with pecans, tomatoes and cheese. We could not be happier and would love to stay again! We plan on honeymooning in Costa Rica and if the timing works out we hope to stay at Alexis and Mike's other property! After staying at a resort for five days before arriving here, we were thrilled to stay at this B&B--they get it!

author: OntarioHappygal
title: A Wonderful Experience
text: After many years of resorts, we decided this year to use a B&B for our stay from Feb. 13-20, 2012 and we were not disappointed with Marjories! The "Welcome Tray" was an appreciated touch after long hours of travel. The view from the lanai is breathtaking and expansive! Guest hosts, Gary and Luanne, were the ideal hosts ( quiet, generous and informative). As stated before, breakfasts were delicious and had enough variety to satisfy even the pickiest of eaters. The fresh fruit and freshly squeezed juice along with something new off the stove every day along with the breads, croissants and cereals were enough to satisfy well into the day. We appreciated all the beach gear that was available for our use, including a cooler and ice packs, as well as the advice on what not to miss while on Kauai. The kitchenette in the room was an added bonus as was the fantastic lap pool. A BBQ is available upon request, but eating out or cooking in costs about the same, so we decided to eat out. Since we were going on to the Big Island for a week, we also were glad that laundry facilities were available for our use. It is true that it can be a tricky place to find in the dark, even with the directions given, as the road signage is on a slant and is not totally reflective and the mailbox is black and up against a hedge. A word of advice: BOOK EARLY. We had wanted the Valleyview Room, but even though we booked in Oct. were not able to get it. Our stay was in the Tradewind Room (the smallest of the three) but quite adequate as we were out and about every day. A wonderful stay!

author: gf_lynn123
title: paradise and rainbows in the hills
text: My husband and I just returned from our trip to Kauai and truly are home sick for our home away from home! Alexis was so warm and welcoming we really did feel like we were staying in the home of a relative.The house was clean and quiet and had gorgeous valley views from every room. Upon settling into our room we found a wonderful welcome platter complete with homemade banana bread, nuts, and fresh island fruit. So sweet! The room had a comfortable bed, a separate seating area, a tv (which we didn't use throughout our entire stay), and a fridge, microwave, and prep sink area. Oh, and a coffee maker which we used every morning. Adjacent to our room we also had access to a private hot tub. Every day, we came back and took a quick dip before turning in for the night. Marjorie's also has a 50ft long salt water pool that is cooled and a separate hot tub for guests to use. Both were fantastic for relaxing after hiking around the island. Alexis also gave us access to snorkling gear, beach chairs, beach towels, sunscreen, and even her laundry machines while we were there! The location was great. Easy access to both sides of the island, quiet, hidden, and gorgeous valley views. Every morning we woke to the sounds of the local birds and saw beautiful rainbows in the valley. Breakfast every morning was delicious and nutritious. My husband can't have anything with gluten (typically wheat, rye, or barley), and Alexis went WAY above and beyond going so far as to get us gluten-free breads, muffins, and macaroons. We had wonderful buckwheat pancakes, eggs benedict, potato and egg caseroles, scambled eggs with quinoa and beans. Each morning we were also treated to fresh fruit smoothies which she juiced and blended to order. Everything exceeded our expectations and we can't wait to get back there.

author: KarinlovesKauai
title: Secluded and quiet, but close to everything
text: We just returned from a lovely stay at Kauai at Marjories Inn, where we celebrated a belated 5 year wedding anniversary and our first stay away from our 3 year old. We stayed in two different rooms during our stay, one with a huge lanai with a stunning view of a mountain valley, and the second room was larger and had it's own hot tub. The breakfasts were incredible....a variety of local, fresh fruit from farmer's markets, yogurt, granola, cereal, coffee, tea, toast and pastries, hard boiled eggs, fresh squeezed juice (from Mike the raw food guru!), and one special thing every day like buckwheat pancakes or eggs and sausage. All of this served on the lanai overlooking the aforementioned incredible valley view. The inn includes it's own pool and palapa for lounging, which we enjoyed immensely after enjoying many of the adventures Kauai provides. The hosts could not have been more courteous, helpful, and accomodating. They were full of tips of things to do, and had any possible bit of gear you might need on your adventures to use. Not to mention that each of the three rooms has it's own refrigerator, microwave, tv, and wifi - and there is a laundry machine on hand, perfect after a red muddy hike.(I highly recommend a muddy hike - especially in Waimea Canyon. INCREDIBLE!) There's only three rooms, so the establishment is quiet, and if you like your privacy, you are perfectly able to stay in your room - or if you like visiting, the guests we met were all interesting and great breakfast-mates, and Alexis and Mike also were super fun to chat with. Too bad we are an ocean apart - I could easily enjoy them as friends instead of just great hosts! So if you are staying down south, stay at Marjories. Why stay close to the water with everyone else? It's a 5-10 minute drive away to a myriad of beaches, super cute Koloa town, and close to the main hwy to take you anywhere else you want to go on the island. Oh yah and the beds and pillows were SUPER comfy. Scott and Karin

author: Archiegirl35th
title: Fantastic B&B for a relaxing Hawaii vacation!
text: My husband and I stayed at Marjorie's for a week for our honeymoon--we chose Kauai and Marjorie's because we wanted to go somewhere not too touristy, a little out of the way and private, but also somewhere that would have fun and interesting things to do when we got tired of relaxing all day! Marjorie's Kauai Inn was absolutely the perfect choice for our honeymoon. Situated in a beautiful spot overlooking the Lawai Valley, we were afforded spectacular views without the crowds and noise you might find elsewhere. We were just a short drive away from the beautiful beaches at Poipu, and since the island is relatively small everything else also felt pretty close by. We stayed in the Sunset View room, which was amazing. It was very comfortable, well equipped, clean, and spacious. It got lots of sunlight, but was never very hot because of the breeze; there's also an A/C unit in the room which we used once for a short time in the afternoon. We spent many evenings on our private lanai enjoying the view and the private hot tub! can't get much better than that! Also the kitchenette was very handy--we were able to save some money by spending a few evenings in and using the microwave to heat up some food. We also wanted to mention how well-stocked the garage is! There were all kinds of things we could borrow--snorkeling gear, beach chairs, bug spray, aloe, coolers, tons of beach towels, and probably more that I can't remember! Incredibly convenient and thoughtful! The breakfasts we had while we were here were definitely one of the highlights of our trip--I'm still craving Mike's buckwheat waffles and pancakes! We also appreciated the personal touch we experienced--Mike took requests for breakfast, and spent time during breakfast chatting with us and other guests. Mike was a fantastic resource for us while we were there--he directed us to an excellent small company for a helicopter tour of the island (unbelievable--definitely recommend this!) , and had lots great suggestions for other fun outings. Overall we loved our stay here, and we're already dreaming about coming back to Kauai and staying at Marjorie's!

author: JamesFrench
title: Peaceful, Comfortable, Relaxing B&B. Thoughtful Host
text: I came to Marjorie's as a solo traveller after reading the reviews on Tripadvisor, and I was not disappointed! Mike, my host, gave detailed driving instructions, so I was able to find the place easily. When I opened the door to my bedroom, I was blown away by the sweeping valley views from my four-poster bed and my very own private deck! The room was decorated with tasteful island-style furnishings, and had more facilities than I was expecting, including a fridge, coffee maker and microwave. The fridge was filled with fresh fruit salad, juices and other treats, which I really appreciated since I was still exhausted from my 14-hour flight. After I arrived, I took some time out to relax. When Mike gave me a tour of the cottage, I was amazed by all the things that he offers – not just wireless internet and a washer/ dryer, but also guide books, snorkels, ice boxes, bicycles, insect repellent... Mike was very helpful with travel advice. I arrived in Kauai with no idea of what I should do. Mike gave me a detailed map of the island and spent over an hour with me helping me plan my trip. I'd recommend Marjorie's to anyone wanting a comfortable, relaxing stay in a peaceful B&B. You’re a million miles away from stress, but it’s only a few minutes’ drive to shops, restaurants & beaches. The views are amazing, the pool is long & has many deck chairs, and I slept very well because the B&B is so quiet and secluded. Mike is a helpful host who makes great breakfasts! He is keen to help with anything you'd like to ask, and his living room and garage are thoughtfully stocked with many things to make your stay fun and easy.

author: Picalilli
title: Comfortable stay with a great host.
text: We stayed in the Sunset View Room for the final four nights of 2009 on our honeymoon. Our only complaint is that we had to leave. Our innkeeper, Mike, has possibly the best job on the planet and it comes through in his demeanor. He was a gracious host, from the moment he met us in the driveway on arrival until he saw us away to the airport. It was great to know that Mike is always available to provide tourism advice, relaxed conversation, and help if you get yourself into a jam (as we did). Mike, if you're reading this, we really appreciated your help that night. The rest of you will have to ask Mike when you arrive at Marjorie's :-) In addition to our host, we were fortunate enough to share a healthy breakfast each morning with the fascinating people staying at the inn. Now, Marjorie's can't guarantee that you'll meet new and exciting people, but those extended breakfast interactions may have been our favorite part of the stay. If you're not feeling social, breakfast is casual and there's plenty of space to have some privacy. The room in which we stayed was awesome, with a private hot tub, comfy bed and a fantastic vista off the private lanai (veranda). We snapped a picture of the largest rainbow either of us has ever seen right off that lanai and we're told it's not uncommon after a little rain. I was very happy to learn that the land in the valley below is zoned for rural use and the view will never be ruined by some huge condo or other development. The rest of the property is as beautiful as the rest of Kauai, and it would have been great to just lay around doing nothing. Though we didn't have enough time to lay around for days, we did enjoy a refreshing dip in the salt water pool one morning. If we ever win the lottery and have money for a pool, we're doing salt instead of chlorine. Wait, no - if we win the lottery, we're going back to Kauai... and staying at Marjorie's.

author: TripAdviserFan2
title: Exceptional B&B
text: We stayed at Marjorie’s Kauai Inn five nights at end of December 2009. While using B&Bs, if possible, in our every vacation we find this place an outstanding value. Consider this: you arrive late evening after 9 hours flight and are treated with a snack and glass of wine. In the morning and every morning after that, you are treated with exceptional, REALLY, breakfast. One time - buckwheat pan cakes. Another time - just made quiche, and so on. This is in addition to fresh fruits, juice, yogurts, breads, muffins, coffee and teas. The host, Mike, current owner, is friendly, helpful and a good cook. Read farther… If you forgot your snorkeling gears, surf boards or sun lotion – everything is available for you. You can wash there your dirty cloth, after a long day hike, as well. If you rather watch movie, a collection of some 70 movies is for you. All these are for …free and are offered with a pleasure by the owner. Overview that opens from the rooms’ balconies is pictureous, too. Down below you would see a small green valley with private houses spread within it. The somewhat remote (few miles) location from the closest beach is easily compensated by all the above, if you aren’t willing to stay in crowded condo and hotel complexes and pay $300-500 per night. The only limitation would be for people with physical disabilities since the house is located on a hill and one have to climb the driveway to get in, otherwise, visit there.

author: baylorsf
title: No pity on the deposit
text: My spouse and I were very excited about spending the first 2 nights of our Kauaii vacation at Marjorie's. We sent a $160 deposit to secure the reservation. Unfortunately we received some pretty bad medical news and had to cancel our vacation plans due to a surgical procedure I must now have. I had to cancel my reservation at Marjorie's- 30 days prior to our reservation date. For the record- Marjorie's cancellation policy states that to receive partial reimbursement for your deposit you must cancel 31 days prior to the reservation. So essentially I was one day off from canceling and receiving some money back- however I could not control the timing of my medical diagnosis. Regardless, I had to cancel and offered my sincerest apologies. I asked Marjorie's to tell me how much I might be able to recover from my deposit. A woman responded- AGAIN- not the owner but as friend of the owners- stating that I was out of luck on the deposit. She also stated that she would need to keep the deposit as she was sure that they could have other guests fill the spot and they passed up on them because of my reservation. Wow. Now- given that this is a holiday season, I am quite confident Marjorie's will have no problem filling the reservation. So in essence, they are making a little profit off of my deposit. Please also note that the other 2 B&B/Inns that I had to cancel were extremely understanding and sympathetic to our situation- offering full refunds and inviting us back when we are able to travel again. I understand that business is business, and everyone needs to keep their business afloat. But really- one day off on the cancellation policy and you can even offer $20 back? A little disappointing to say the least, especially given our unfortunate circumstances.

author: olallaalum
title: A refuge after busy days exploring the island
text: We chose Marjorie's for our honeymoon after reading so many great reviews on TripAdvisor. We were not disappointed. A bit about us: Newly married, in our early 30s, Marriott/Westin kind of hotel people with an occasional boutique hotel thrown in, we like great food and cultural experiences. We decided to go the bed and breakfast route this time because it sounded so peaceful and a good change of pace from the mega hotel experience. And it so was. Marjorie's is tucked along the side of a lush valley where seemingly everything is green. We loved listening to the trade winds rustle the tropical leaves as we drifted off to sleep at night in the aptly named Tradewinds room (when we return in the future, we hope to snag the larger, hottub included sunset room). Our room came with a comfortable queen-sized bed, our own roomy deck, a fridge and sink and that nice view of valley -- a lot like staying in the nicely appointed guest room of a family friend. We loved waking up each day of our week on Kauai and not having to think about where to have breakfast, because upstairs Mike, the host, had created yet another bountiful spread of local granola, eggs, fresh fruit salad, yogurt, buckwheat waffles, etc. Mike knows pretty much everything about Kauai and is a great resource for planning adventures. We appreciated the garage full of equipment for our excursions, including snorkeling gear, beach chairs, towels, straw mats, etc. Lawai is near Poi'pu and Hanapepe, so great dining and the Friday art night are just abotu 10 minutes away in either direction. It's also a good spot if you plan to spend a lot of time exploring the Waimea Canyon (about an hour's drive away). It took us a little over an hour to reach Hanalei Bay and a bit more to get to Ke'e Beach on the north shore, which turned out to be our favorite. It was great to be able to walk downstairs and jump in the pool when we wanted a quick swim or a break from the beach. We look forward to returning and would recommend Marjorie's to those who want tranquility when they visit this stunning island.

author: Regina-TRIP
title: Best Vacation Ever!
text: If you are searching for the picture perfect rainbow, then at Marjories Inn on the island of Kauai is where you will find it. Our 8-night stay at Marjories Inn was our first experience at a B&B and we couldn’t have been more pleased with the accommodations, beautiful weather and our hosts Daniela and Michael. In terms of customer service and value it was second to none. We stayed in the Valley View room, which included a very comfortable bed and quality linens. Our private lanai was more than you would ever get at a large resort; approx 15 ft x 30 ft, with a lounge chair as well as two tables and 4 chairs; plenty of room to relax and enjoy breakfast, take-out dinner and bottle of wine or just breath in the fresh island air. The extra amenities at no extra charge included the use of mountain bikes, boogie boards and even an ice cooler if you want to pack a lunch for the beach. The view of the valley was majestic and the grounds were impeccable. The continental breakfasts were also very good and Daniela even made crepes one morning with their homemade mango jam.......excellent! Its worth a mention the mangos were picked just outside our room door from the most spectacular mango tree. The fresh grown Kauai coffee was so good we purchased some from a local store to bring back home. We wanted a more personal experience which is why we decided to try a B & B and happily we got exactly what we were hoping for. Last but not least, our dear hosts Daniela and Michael certainly contributed to our "Best Vacation Ever". From the time they greeted us when we first arrived at the Inn, they both made our stay truly comfortable. (I don’t know of a large resort that offers you a glass of wine when you arrive or asks if you’re hungry after such a long flight). If any of you are wondering if a B&B is the way to go, at Marjories Inn, it definitely is! [-]

author: Neepaconejo
title: A Perfect Place to Stay in Kauai
text: We stayed a week at the inn and it was a perfect stay. This is the place to be if you want close proximity to attractions but want to start and end your day with a peaceful location. There is a long driveway that takes you completely away from the road which has little traffic. We stayed in the Valley View room. All three rooms have private entrances but I think The Valley View Room has the best view and most privacy of the three. I also liked the fact that we had a great view of the valley from the bed. Taking a peek at the moon and stars in the middle of the night was an extra treat. Our kitchenette had a sink, microwave, frig and dishes. Wireless internet access from the room was also a big plus. As mentioned in the other reviews, Alexis and Mike are the perfect hosts. They even supplied us with beach gear and coolers. We started every morning with a light breakfast and they kept a cookie jar on the counter with home made chocolate chip cookies which they let me stock up on every day. I enjoy staying at b&b's but sometimes the hosts are a bit too intrusive. Mike and Alexis made sure the guests had their privacy but were there when we needed assistance. The only thing to note is that trip advisor says the rate averages around $90. When we stayed there and according to their web site, the rate ranges from $120-$160 per night.

author: ShannonNYC
title: This place is Gorgeous inside and out!
text: STUNNING! FABULOUS!! When we arrived at 'Marjorie's Kauai Inn', I was so relieved to see this would be 'home' for the next few days. The bed and breakfast is built on the side of a cliff over-looking a beautiful lush valley with horses and goats milling around the fields far below. We were warmly greeted by the owner Alexis who promptly made us feel at home. She was anxious to assist us with our activities (i.e. Helicopter tours, a luau, and restaurant recommendations.) She was happy to make all of the arrangements, making our trip effortless. Her inn is so quiet and peaceful. There's no noisy traffic, just breezes flowing throughout. Occasionally, a light rain would water the lovely tropical flowers and palms surounding the property, than quickly gave way to the Hawaiian sunshine. The inn has wonderful covered porches, all facing the valley. It is immaculately clean and modern with very comfortable beds and linens, and tasteful furnishings and appointments. All of the rooms have kitchenettes with mini-fridges...really nice! (especially if you've doggie-bagged your left-over pasta from the night before :) Nestled into the hillside just below the porch is the gorgeous swimming pool and tiki bar (for happy hour.) The torches are lit at night to greet late arrivals, adding to the Hawaiian embiance...(tastefully done.) We awoke our first morning to fresh tropical fruit, Kona coffee, juice, and delicious breads...HOW WONDERFUL!!! We decided to visit Kauai to celebrate a birthday (our first trip to this island.) We stayed at a big resort on the beach the first night, but wanted a more intimate experience, so we checked-in to 'Marjorie's.' By the way, 'The Garden Island' lives up to it's nickname, not nearly as developed as the other Hawaiian Islands. Skip the other islands and visit the real Hawaii. And do yourself a favor, check into this inn!!! WE WILL DEFINATELY BE BACK!!!

author: CfromV
title: Great place
text: Our family of four stayed for four nights at the beginning of our trip. Nice hotel, recommend getting the buffet breakfast, it was a little different everyday. The pool on the rooftop was awesome. Always a lounger. There was rooftop drinks service although they didn’t come around much. That said, they didn’t bat an eyelash when I gave up and went and brought my own. Super nice staff and the guy who arranges the taxi or tours was great. I liked how he told us to cover up more for the temples (but said it in a respectful way). Note you have to give1000 baht deposit when you check in. So leave yourself a few minutes to check out because they go check the room before giving it back to you! Air con was super cold. Showers super hot. Clean room. Safe neighbourhood, great location. Rooms were super quiet. Beds amazing.

author: inverness-uk
title: Probably the worst hotel experience ever
text: I am writing this review at the airport, after spending 3 nights in what can only be described as my worst hotel experience ever. The reason I did not make a review while I was there, is that the hotel apparently has a habit of finding things you have damaged, torn towels, chipped cups etc, and making you pay heavily for them. I managed to escape without charge, however if I had complained, I wouldn’t have been so lucky. On first look, it’s a new hotel, and looks ok. It’s clean, has comfortable beds, and is in a good location, a few minutes walk from bts. That’s where the good bits stop. The walls are paper thin. You WILL hear everything your neighbours are up to. It’s impossible to sleep when there is so much noise, both in the corridors and from adjoining rooms. The breakfast is the absolute worst I have ever seen in years of travelling. A cold buffet of fried eggs, chicken sausages and beans. (All cold) freezing cold. Fresh hot food is available everywhere in bkk, why can’t they have some here too? As a final note, if you are still reading, the hotel responds to critical reviews with a standard response. (Just check the other bad reviews) so it’s not as though they don’t know the problems, they just choose to ignore them. Please don’t stay here, it’s an amazing city, and there are so many good hotels for not a lot of money, I just wish I had listened to the reviews!

author: sipniprelish
title: Nice place to stay
text: This lodge is really nice if you are looking to stay in Bangkok then go for it. We booked this hotel online. Booking amount was not much as of other nearby hotels. We checked and compared prices of other hotels too and found that this is providing good rooms and facilities in reasonable amount. This hotel has very nice swimming pool at the terrace where you can spend some good time. Their restaurant was also nice. We had breakfast and dinner there. They had variety in breakfast and dinner. Staff of this place is very humble and polite. They will treat you well. Rooms were also nice with nice bed and bathroom. Only one thing I think they need to improve that is seating area for visitors as the benches they have kept at reception are little hard and the chair which are kept outside the hotel are mostly occupied by the smokers. It is easliy approachable from market area. You will find many shopping mart and restaurants nearby. You will have easy access to taxis if you want to go anywhere. I will highly recommend this place.

author: uclatraveller
title: Excellent Location and Good Value. And Good Value.
text: Was just at this hotel from March 25, 2018. Stayed for 5 nights. Location was very good. It is close to Nana Station. There are some reviews that suggest that it is super far from Sukhumvit street. That is not the case. It is about 5-10 minute walk to get there. People from the U.S. are so use to driving and treat a 5-10 minute walk as somehow being a massive journey. It was close to everything, public transit, shops, food etc. There are two sections to the hotel, I stayed in the back part of the hotel, where the reception area was located, so I did not have any street noise. Had comfortable bed. Hot shower, room was clean. A/C worked great. I had limited interaction with the hotel staff, but everytime they were nice and helpful. Room had a mini fridge. There was free wifi in the room. They offered breakfast, however the package, I bought did not include breakfast. This was fine with me, as there are plenty of options right outside the hotel. Would definitely use this hotel again!!

author: AdrianCCCCC
title: Mixed bag.
text: Let me get this straight, the hotel is located at a very good location, new, nice small little sky pool and a tiny little gym. Room is comfortable and design is good. Location - 10/10 for me. Right smack in the center of tourist district. Facilities/amenities - 8/10 - restaurant is good, gym is small but has free weights and treadmill, pool is more for relaxation then actual swimming but rooftop pool. Room - 8/10 - comfortable, not to the extend of posh but definitely no complains. Service - 0/10 - the thing that really puts a damper on this hotel is the front desk people. Before we checked in, over the span of 5 minutes, 3 front desk personnel mentioned the words “ pay upfront” more than 10 times despite us reassuring them that we will. Since we had one person doing the booking for a big group of people, some arriving of a later date, the hotel kept on mentioning that all the rooms should be paid upfront, Though some guest are arriving on a later date. When we ask questions, front desk was rude and not helpful at all. The moment we paid and I ask for the invoice , the front desk say we get the invoice only When we checkout and they will not prepare it now. So all in add, asking for money too many times, after which no invoice till u checked out. Quite unfriendly I think because they are very busy and any question we ask seems to annoy them. That is on TOP of telling us we got the best price in the market since we book for 3 -4nights for 20+ people, just to find out that someone who booked 1 room later on got a cheaper rate ( we chatted on the lift). I personally won’t return.

author: RTM2289
title: Great hotel in Bangkok! Good rooms and excellent location!
text: We enjoyed our 3 night stay at Travelodge Sukhumvit 11! The location is great and within walking distance to many restaurants and shops. We walked around every evening and were able to find some great restaurants for dinner in the area. Our room was located in the older tower that is not attached to the main lobby. Our room was very small but we managed. The rooms are nice and have updated modern furniture. My only complaint about the room was that our air conditioning did not work the second night and our room was very hot. It was just very uncomfortable to sleep without air conditioning for 1 night. My parents received a room in the new tower which is attached to the main lobby. I would definitely recommend requesting a room in the new tower, it’s a little more updated. The hotel has a buffet breakfast each morning which is included in your room rate. The breakfast buffet is AWESOME!! We loved the options each morning! Overall we really enjoyed out stay at Travelodge Sukhumvit 11 and would stay here again. The nightly rate is priced really well and the location is excellent! I’d recommend to other travelers!

author: FCB1
title: Comfortable hotel with friendly staff
text: This is a new hotel located at the end of Soi 11 off Sukhumvit Road. Good size room, sheets and towels are replaced daily. Excellent cleaning service. Don't forget to leave a small tip for the cleaning lady. There is a Tuk Tuk service on an hourly basis. If you need a ride, just go to the Tuk Tuk 5 minutes before the hour and have a seat. Bear in mind that walking to the main road can take up to 10 minutes which can be unbearable in Bangkok hot weather. I had a very nice stay at this hotel. The front desk staff, restaurant staff and cleaning crew are very friendly and helpful. Breakfast buffet is available for around 150 Bahts. Minor issues : only luke warm water in the shower and the AC is centrally controlled. You can adjust the temperature but you can not turn it on or off from your room. This can be a deal breaker for some people. I had to cover one of the vents with tape and newspaper. Although I recommend this hotel, I'm not sure I will be back for the issues mentioned above.

author: 603adamw
title: Great Hotel
text: Travelodge Hotel We ended up staying here twice on our trip to Thailand. I wanted go to give this hotel 5 stars for everything but our second stay let us down. We stayed in building B (building with reception) on our first stay and building A (Building with the pool and gym) on the second trip Pros: all the staff are friendly and helpful. Rooms are spacious. Bed is big in comfortable (I’m 6”3 15 stone). Interned is very fast. Tv works with some English channels. Prime location. Free hourly Tuk Tuk to nana BTS Station. Free bottles of water daily. Soap and shampoo in the bathroom. Free safe. Pool is a sun trap. 7 eleven across the road. Food is resonantly priced and tasty Cons (only applies to building A) There was a putrid sewage smell from the bathroom (we arrived late and could not be bothered to ask to move room witch we regret as it was very off putting to sleep in) In the early ours in the morning there was a very loud noise witch I thought was thunder and rain but it was the plumbing running above our room. It was honestly so loud me and my parter both woke up and ran to window thinking there was a storm happening. Would I stay In this hotel again ? definitely as long as I was in building B or they fix the issues above with building A. When I Mentioned to the staff in the morning about the smell they seemed very apologetic and called someone straight away to investigate.This was great hotel and the value for money was second to none.

author: 892eh
title: Large clean room helpful staff and offers excellent value
text: First you have to remember this is a Travelodge and not a resort hotel. That said we stayed for 8 nights and found the hotel in a great location handy for the Nana skytrain which will take you anywhere in the city. It was far enough away from the main road to allow a quiet time but close enough not to miss out on atmosphere. There were hundreds of restaurants and bars all around but the hotel itself offered pleasant evening meals and a small drinks menu should you wish to stay in-house. The rooftop pool is a nice touch and we always found plenty of room so sit or swim. NB. They could use a few extra sun umbrellas as there were too few i feel. There was a roof top gym with some free weights and 4 cardio machines. Breakfast was pretty good, always breads eggs preserves fruit and pastries. Added to this was a variety of sausages stir-fry noodles or hash brown on different days as well as fruit juices and a very nice fresh coffee. All self service and eat as much as you like. The room was VERY clean fresh and spacious. The bathroom had a roman shower and plenty of power for a nice shower experience. The air con worked very well and was quiet. Large bed with really comfy pillows. All in all for the price you can't do better than this for a city hotel. Thanks for a wonderful stay.

author: glennstuarth
title: it was ok
text: "New" is what it mostly had going for it. Location is a walk. Tuk only every hour unless they dont feel like it then it is every day. Maybe. You guess the time because they wont tell you. The restaurant had lousy service and over priced food. "New" is its main attribute and that will wear off soon. Pool deck was cool. Get there early and be polite and pick up your towel when you leave. There are too many loser travellers that think the world is there to pick up after them. Fitness center is OK and better then none. its tiny. Don't go at a peak hour and be prepared to clean up the last persons sweat. Again travelosers abound everywhere now. People also like to be loud in the hallways. They dont understand the concept of what a hotel is about but you had better not interrupt them. Slam the door a few times at 5AM. LOL

author: atrain2
title: Amazing stay, amazing price!
text: The hotel is about an 8 minute walk from the Nana Station (green line, BTS). The traffic in Thailand can be so bad that you often resort to taking the trains for quicker transport. I note this first, because I highly recommend positioning your hotel stay as close to a train station as possible. That being said, 8 minutes was a fairly long walk in the Thai heat, but our party was there during the cool season which I can only compare to May heat in Houston, TX - humidity and all. The hotel itself was new, clean, and extremely comfortable. We opted for the free breakfast which was a served in the restaurant next door. The buffet spread was better than the average hotel fare. I would recommend getting it. The location was great, long walk to transport not withstanding. Located in the foreign district, it was close to many bars. The staff was extremely friendly. Word of advice - if your flight departs late (say 10pm like ours), I'd recommend booking for another day, as the thai heat can be terrible. However, the lobby will hold your bags for you even after checkout. The rooms were spacious for Asia standards. If you are debating about whether or not to upgrade, I would say do it if you spent some nights in smaller hotel rooms. The extra space was a nice reprieve after several nights in a cramped hotel room. Otherwise, the standard room is fine, if not on the small side. We got a great deal and paid less than $60/night for our room + breakfast. It was a steal. I would come back any day to stay here again.

author: brownPeter
title: Pleasant but we did not need the ants
text: We were upgraded to room 2214 (slightly larger with an inter connecting door) by a very lovely and efficient receptionist. The room was basic, the bathroom was a fair size. Only 1 roll of toilet paper and very few tissues with no obvious replacements.The toilet was a brand but unless you really pushed the button really hard the flush was not good. By the time our one night stay was over both toilet roll and tissues were gone (thank goodness for our own supply. The bed was comfortable and we had a view over a garden (of weeds) For one night and the Travelodge being only open for 1 month and 4 days it was as expected except we had a team of ants visiting us. They were running around the bathroom, the counter shelf and while not a mass they were there. We live near Hua Hin (4 hours bus south ) and my wife kept finding them in her bag,and through the book she was reading. When we got home she had to empty the bag to eliminate any travelers. We paid for bed and breakfast and that was in The Lodge. Who ever designed the set out for breakfast obviously eat else where. A nice set out of table and chairs ( inside and out) but the plates were kept under the bench that held the food and so you wre gigging through peoples legs to get a plate A choice of fruit juices . There was a toaster, pasties (that did not feel over fresh) Hot food was a fried egg with a form of sausage and a some asian dishes The eggs were next to the pastries and the same tong went from eggs to pastries, I would not consider that healthy. Fruit was on a table around from the bench (as an after thought) and the designer should have carried the counter to include this space. Not well thought out at all. My breakfast was 3 pastries and a coffee not were the price. Being in a good location for 7/11 type of shop and restaurants I would have found a better breakfast elsewhere. Not what we were expecting and teething trouble allowed I don't think we will go back.

author: missvtravels
title: Comfy Bed, New and Clean, Great Value
text: Stayed here for 2 nights, booked a Standard Room for USD51/night including breakfast, service charge and tax. Location wise, pretty convenient, 10 mins walk to Nana BTS station along a busy tourist-filled street with many hotels and restaurants. 7-11 and Family Mart closeby to pick up drinks and snacks. Check-in was quick, I arrived 2 hours before check-in time and was given room right away and also 2 key cards despite travelling solo which was great. They require THB1,000 cash as deposit. Re the room, decent size. Given the hotel opened for less than a month, everything is new and clean as expected. I like that the floor is non carpet. Top marks for the super duper comfy bed, plus large tv. Air con works great, with kettle, hairdryer and safe in a drawer (good size as I can put in my small laptop). Shampoo, shower gel and great smelling fluffy towels. No slippers and mini bar (but there is a vending machine in the lobby). Breakfast is really basic but no complaint since the rate with breakfast is only USD4 more for 2. Fast lifts. A small outdoor swimming pool and gym. Return of deposit upon check-out. Staff helped with stored luggage and also ordered a Grabcar for heading to the airport. Overall, nice stay and great value for the room.

author: TravelDG
title: Great stay in Taipei
text: We are a family of 4 and stayed at the Cozzy hotel for 3 nights. The location of this hotel is great. As others have mentioned, subway station is right next to the hotel. There’s always taxi at the door waiting and it’s relatively cheap. The staff at the hotel are all polite and fluent in English. The room is modern & simple and it’s a decent size for Asian standard. The bed is indeed a bit small but you can ask for an extra bed with additional charge. All toiletries are provided and the room is very clean. All drinks in the mini-fridge are free and they also provide an mobile phone with free internet access and international call which can be used as your mobile phone while you are staying with them. Breakfast is included and the choices are more the sufficient. They do offer typical Western style breakfast plus Asian style. The only recommendation I have is instead of asking each person their room number, just issue voucher for breakfast which can save some time & hassle. We also hang out at the lounge in the evening. It’s a nice place to chill and relax plus they offered free drinks such as juice, coffee & tea. They also have one computer that can be used by guests. A Starbucks is attached to the hotel and the staff there also offer excellent service which we do get in North America. It’s the personal touch that made a difference. Overall we are very happy with our stay at Cozzy and will surely be return.

author: dhlchung
title: MODERN ELEGANCE
text: For my personal taste, I find this hotel to be one of the most pleasant one that we have stayed due to its blend of Asian and European modern elegant designs and layout. The only negative comments we can come up with are the room without a view facing the back even on the 9th floor. I would have preferred rooms facing the street or between 10th and 12th floor. The mattress is is on the firm side and the breakfast had few choices of breads. The high points are as follows: Location: super location 50M from MRT Line 5 which connects to any part of the city. Room: very compact design but very efficient. The room lightings are great and the twin beds are super big with soft down pillows and comforters. Air conditioning is easily adjusted and very cool. The closet is big enough for longer stays with a nice safe. Mini frig also works nicely for some cold drinks and water. Bathroom: not huge but again comfortable without feeling cramped. The shower works great, lots of volume and pressure. All the personal hygienes necessities are provided nicely in the drawer. Lighting is very pleasant. Breakfast: area is very spacious with comfortable seating and nice modern decor and lighting. Coffees are delicious! Just a nice place. I would have rated the hotel 10/10 except for the non-view room!

author: yun3101
title: Cozy :-)
text: We stayed for 4 nights in March. It was overall a very comfortable stay. The hotel location is excellent, barely 2 minutes from the shan dao si stop, which is one of the commonly used train lines for us. The room we stayed in was large, even with a cot, there was adequate space for my toddler to move around. They do not refill the mini bar though. Bathroom was spacious, and had both a tub and shower area. The breakfast buffet was average. I think we have tried more interesting breakfasts in other taiwan hotels. They have a "happy hour" in the evenings there they serve a small selections of local dishes. It was nice to just chill there with a warm drink if you don't feel like heading out. You can also bring the mugs in your room to the same cafe for hot drinks anytime you want, and drink it in the comfort of your room. Service was nice and fast. When we requested for a cot, they prepared a tub along with a stool and thermometer for the bath. We borrowed umbrellas from the front desk every day before we head out. Will definitely consider this hotel the next time we head back to Taipei.

author: zhaobao
title: Charming boutique hotel at convenient location
text: The hotel is situated right at exit 6 from Shandao Temple Metro station on the blue line, (2 stations east of Ximending, and 5 stations west of City Hall station). It is a much quieter location compared to Taipei Main Station. Because this station only has one line, once you enter the gates and go down the escalator, you are basically at the train platform. This is unlike Taipei Main Station which is a huge interchange and therefore I personally find navigating from any building down to the train platform at Taipei Main Station a bit confusing. There were plenty of taxis outside the hotel during my stay (New Year long weekend) for those who do not prefer taking public transportation or those going to the airport. Not sure if this would apply normally during the week. Taxi fare to/from Taoyuan airport would cost around TWD 1120 to 1200. The interior decor has a soft colour hue and there is a lot of natural lighting on the second floor (where the restaurant / lounge is) which makes it very homey. There is not a lot on offer with the complimentary snacks (mostly sample bread items from their bakery), but you can get unlimited tea, coffee, Perrier and soft drinks, so that's fine. Of course, you can always catch up on the newspapers of the day in the lounge - helps if you read Chinese. The breakfast items are geared towards the local Taiwanese palate. For fruits, they basically have a nonstop supply of grapefruit and combination of apples, melon, pineapple. On 2 of the 4 days, I stuffed myself with plates and plates of passionfruit. The room itself - big enough for two people, with heated bathroom and heated toilet seat. Nice touch given that it can be quite cold in the evening during winter. They seem to have a very strict check in time at 3pm, or the hotel was very full because of the New Year holidays. Arrived at the hotel at 230pm, and was told to wait for the key at the lounge and they would come deliver. Surely they did deliver the room key at 3:10pm. Unlike their sister property at Minsheng, Cozzi Zhongxiao does not have a gym.

author: sneaky_123
title: Wonderful stay!
text: Stayed at Hotel Cozzi Zhongxiao for 3 nights in a recent trip to Taipei. Great location, right next to Shandao Temple Station, which was a quick 1 stop away from the main Taipei Main Station. Very convenient to get around. Even with cabs, as long as you give the cab drivers the address, they'll be able to drop you at the door step. Hotel staff was friendly and very helpful. Room was well designed and spacious enough for 2. Loved the extra huge double bed (i think they pieced together 2 super single beds which made like a super KING bed). Toilet was well designed too. Had a standing shower as well as a separate bath tub. Breakfast is served till 10am daily on the 2nd floor. I suppose they have a relatively good spread except that we always turned up at the tail end of service... We did encounter the slight issue with the room - i don't think they really vacuum the sofa as there were some stains and hair on them... Small tip for travellers: There was a super long queue at Fu Hang Dou Hua shop just opposite the hotel. Queue starts at 5.30am and ermm...it just keeps getting longer...on weekend the queue spills over to the next block! I think it must be really good but...queue was too long for us to try anyway.

author: 166anneh
title: Very disappointed
text: I found this hotel in web, as it's just opened in Oct and fotos shown on official web are nice, and super convenience (1 min to subway station), so i made my reservation at the official web. confirmation was received successfully. nightmare happened during check-in. THEY COULD NOT FIND MY RESERVATION. they said they didn't receive the ID no. from me.........so they cancelled my booking without any notifications. hey, i wasn't asked for that at all. it wasn't a big deal if the rooms were available. but it was fully booked. they allowed me to stay for 1 nite only but i needed 2. the worst part is, i ordered a buy-1 night-get-1 night-free package. in this case, i would b charged the same price for just 1 nite :( i managed to get in the room, and was told to look for another room by myself as per their suggestion. all rooms (which were within my budget and distance) in town were booked. i had no choice but to yell at the reception to find me a solution. it wasn't my fault, why i had to be responsible for their mistake. in short, new hotel, new reservation system, new and inexperience staff and poor CS can drive u crazy. no matter how good the hotel is, in terms of location, cleanliness, rooms, price. at last i packed my things and left the room.

author: Vegas-Queen666
title: Beautiful Building, rest was poor
text: I booked two nights here on how pretty it looked, however the bedrooms do not live up to the outside impression. Downstairs is quite pretty and the breakfast was ok. The bedrooms were the big let down. I always book the largest room as I like a king bed. This was the first room in a very long time where I could sit on the loo, wash my hands in the sink and my feet in the shower at the same time, absolutely tiny! I had to open the single person tiny square shower tray, shower door to bend down to pick up the shampoo! I am a UK 14, chunky but not huge! The sliding door to the bathroom was the first clue of how an ensuite had been squashed into very small space. The whole room was dated and a bit tatty. Terrible decor like an old school 80's B&B stuck in time. It was clean, but terrible for the price paid £150 a night! I was so let down I drove home a day early and skipped the second nights stay. No offer of refund, which was fair enough with leaving last minute however on check out I was not even asked why I was leaving a night early. My answer would have bee, 'my own bedroom is better decorated and more comfortable!' I have been back to Wrexham a few times since and will never stay here again. I would rather stay out of town and drive in daily. Shame as the place has so much potential, it looks like the owners ran out of money when they started the bedroom refit and had to make do with a much smaller budget than downstairs on the decor and layout. It could be fabulous with some money spent on a bedroom refurb. However the spanking new Premier Inn literally around the corner at a third of the price will probably effect their takings. Shame as I like to support independent traders.

author: JuneP139
title: Second very disappointing meal here
text: I've eaten here twice from their main menu and once on an afternoon tea. Afternoon tea was fine, however they seem to be unable to produce food from the kitchen quickly despite how few people are in the restaurant. The first time I went was just 2 of us and it took for ever to get the meal. The second time was this week and there were a party of 12 of us and there was just 1 other person in the restaurant when we ordered shortly after 7pm. It took an hour for the food to arrive, and my gammon was salty and nothing special but the side of onion rings were quite frankly burnt and the onion was like the outer skin.. nothing of it, it just shattered. Deserts are really expensive as are the mains. The worst thing was the time we waited for food yet again. Having arrived at 6.30 we got out of there around 10pm only having 2 courses and in total 2 other people came in and ate during all that time. I can only think the menu is so pretentious that even the chef gets confused and can't cook everything to come together as part of my meal was cold anyway. I really just wanted to get out of there by the end of the night as everything was almost in slow motion. No sense of urgency whatsoever. The one waitress is lovely, the other younger one is a little dizzy and can't even explain the ice cream choices (I think you're supposed to guess what they have on offer) or bring the drinks in a timely manner. I won't be back again and my purse won't be £100 lighter for 4 average quality meals. Only good thing I can say is the place is lovely and has so much potential but the meals are poor.

author: Peanut66Kent
title: Disappointing
text: Was very much looking forward to eating here. Would not return. Ordered meal then advised no steak of choice available a few minutes later. Steak was not rare as requested. Waiting staff argued it was rare and we should have ordered it blue. The steak was definitely medium. My duck was supposed to be pink, it wasn’t. They took the steak away. 20 minutes later new steak arrived. This time minus the new potatoes originally ordered and now served with chips. Steak still medium. My meal was finished by then. Very frustrating. No point in trying to reason with them. Paid bill and left. Have since heard similar stories and would not return here.

author: K1906CMclairew
title: Awful!
text: We’d been wanting to try this place for a while. Perfect opportunity as my 88 year old mother and grandchildren were staying with us for Christmas. First impressions were good, lovely looking from the outside and inside. Located the disabled toilet to find it was locked! The waitress said she didn’t have a key to open it but it could be opened with a spoon!! This failed and I had to take my mother to the other toilet. Perhaps this would have been a good time to leave. We ordered 3 fish and chips, one salmon, and a child’s portion of sausage, chips and beans. One portion of fish and chips and the child’s meal was ok. As for the other meals they were extremely poor. The chips looked more like batter bits, the battered fish was like cutting into fresh air! No fish at all, had better from our local fish and chip shop. The salmon was over cooked and the veg limp. The waitress could only apologise for the poor quality of food and reduced the bill accordingly. Will not return not even if it was free!

author: A3917EBchrisw
title: Lovely restaurant gone to the dogs.
text: We used to visit The Lemon Tree regularly but we won't be visiting again for the following reasons. (1) inconsistent service, a couple of the staff have been lovely and attentive. However we have had some who were really rude and obnoxious. (2) some meals have been lovely, but some have been terrible. Tiny portions, Luke warm food and meals not matching the description provided. Twelve we would be giving a 5* rating. (3) breakfast £10, not worth it at all. Facebook page shows a well laid out breakfast table with fruit, pastries and various continental choice. Not how it was in reality. (4) extremely long wait for food and service when the place was virtually empty, if there were problems these should of been communicated before food orders were taken. Don't expect excuses after 40 minutes of waiting, and this was for sandwiches at lunch time. (5) I always give praise when due, however I will also give constructive criticism when necessary. The Lemon Tree will quickly respond to positive comments on Facebook, but you give polite but constructive comment or post an enquiry they will just ignore. (6) you used to be able to use gourmet card at the location, but after you had eaten they would try to change the terms so that you paid more. Not a chance. They don't accept now. We will not return, shame as it is only around the corner.

author: Nurstin
title: Good roast dinner. Accommodation and service average.
text: My boyfriend and I booked to stay here as we were running the local half marathon. The car park was full when we arrived on Saturday evening, we were told we could use the Citizens Advice car park next door as their office is closed over the weekend. We were shown "the long way" to our room as the quick way that took us via the corridor to the toilets as was not so nice. We were in room 12, above the toilets, the room was fine, clean with a comfortable bed but the noise from the hand dryers in the toilets below was very disturbing. The kettle was faulty (as I have since read in other reviews) requiring the switch to be held down for some time. When we requested extra teabags, milk and sugar be left in our room the following day we returned to find around 15 sachets of coffee, about 10 teabags yet only 6 pots of milk...... A bottle of sparkling water was left in our room each day, but no still water. We only ate one meal in the restaurant during our stay. We both had a roast dinner on the Sunday after our run. There were many tables free in the restaurant yet we were sat right next to another couple in a small conservatory type room. The main meal was very good for a restaurant roast dinner, the beef was pink in the centre and nicely browned on the edges, succulent pork with crackling, homemade yorkshire puddings, tasty gravy and al dente vegetables, all very very good. The menu offers a free dessert with any roast dinner and I am glad it was free as I would not have been happy to pay for it.... described as sticky toffee pudding with a rum toffee sauce and ice cream arrived as a slab of dry cake with a drizzle of sauce and for some reason the ice cream was sat on a pile of popping candy. I enjoyed popping candy as an 8 year old in the 90s but it had no place on the plate of this dessert. We paid for our meal before returning to our room. I can't complain about the attitude of the staff as we had very little interaction with them, they did not check back to ask if our meals were okay and they did not enquire if we had enjoyed our stay when we came to check out. Upon check out we were told there had been a meal charged to our room, a meal we did not have. The member of staff disappeared, presumably to check with a manager, returned and said "well, I'll take it off anyway then"..... I should think so too as we had not had a meal and charged it to our room.

author: nmj
title: Second Visit
text: This was our second stay at the Lemon Tree Let me review by listing positives and negatives, and then you can make your mind up on whether it is suited for you?! POSITIVES Great check in by very friendly female member of staff who is a credit to the Lemon Tree. Lovely restaurant area/bar, Well decorated, relaxing and good ambience. Very well presented meals at dinner time and tasted delicious, I can highly recommend dinner here. Not silly money either! Again great service at dinner, with the same friendly member of staff very attentive and hard working. Request for soya milk was aknowleged and was at breakfast as requested. Much appreciated. NEGATIVES Our King room 2 was at the front of the hotel and above the bar area, which made for a noisy room until the music went off at about 11.30pm. No heating in room until we switched radiator on. It was freezing outside, so felt this should have been on. Small bathroom in room 2 needs a shelf within the shower and by the sink, and also a hook somewhere to hold up dressing gown/clothes etc. Breakfast was a disappointment compared to the lovely dinner we had the previous night. The poached eggs were as hard as rocks -very overcooked for both myself and husband. School boy error which is such a shame. Tomatoes were uncooked/cold. To recap - there are more positives than negatives. I would happily return and would hope that the breakfast next time would be better, and that the constructive criticism about troom 2 would have been addressed and rectified.

author: Jayne469
title: A little jewel
text: Stayed one night with work colleague.. Staff were friendly and approchable . Booked two single beds in one room but on arriving bed was a double... Raised our issue and was dealt with prompt, friendly and professionally. Ordered food from the menu till 5.30pm.. Had soup of the day, red pepper and tomato served with a nice touch of a warm bread roll.. Absolutely delicious.. Went for the cheese Burger and triple cooked chips... Very scrumptious... Had chocolate and lavender moouse for dessert ..seriously good... 3 course with a drink just over £20...given the quality of our meal was pleasantly surprised at the price... Ended the evening sharing a bottle of prosecco.. Great quality. Room was clean, with tea and coffee facilities in room... Breakfast was lovely ...choice of juice, cereal, fruit etc... Had cooked English which was great Bacon, lovely sausage and came with two poached eggs and two chunky slices of toast.. Lots of top ups of coffee.... Great little find as hotel our conference was fully booked... Which was great for me as I have found a real little treasure... Will be back with hubby for a night in the near future

author: Y7096DPmartinb
title: Lovely but...!
text: Myself and my wife stayed for two nights over 20th and 21st August, the second day being her Birthday. We did a package where we stayed on B & B on the first night and bead, breakfast, afternoon tea, free bottle of wine and £30 off the evening meal. £65 for the both of us on the second night - brilliant value! I booked room 3 which is the best room and has a window over the bed, its the one they use in the advert on the website. We knew there would be some traffic noise as the room is on the front of the hotel which is situated on a traffic island. When we got to our room it was very nice but I noticed that one of the windows could not be closed as the catches were missing. This wasn't too much of an issue at that time as the room would be nice and cool although there is a bit of a security issue. Once we had gone to bed we realised just how much of an issue the window was. The noise from the road was quite bad and the occasional 'boy racer' woke us up with a start so we woke up and didn't feel that we had had a good nights sleep, this was true of both nights. This is a 10 minute job for someone. The other downside was the rather out of date bathroom (no bath) with a small shower that you couldn't bend down in and notary to put anything on, no doubt because you would probably keep banging into it. The toilet itself was raised on a large piece of wood and was very uncomfortable and the bathroom mirror had been set to high for most people to use efficiently, there was no extractor fan either, just a couple of air bricks. The staff were great and the breakfast on our first morning was superb, the afternoon tea was huge and really nice and our evening meal was cooked to perfection, other guests were also making comments about how good the food was. Breakfast on our second morning just didn't come up to the standard of the rest of our meals, it was nice but simply not as good - overcooked poached egg and my fried egg was just not as nice as the two on the day before. This is a nice place and as the name suggests, it is a restaurant with rooms. The food and service come first and the rooms seem to be a bit of an afterthought. Good range of beers and wines and not expensive. The dearest thing on the menu was a fillet steak at £22.00 so, if you get £30 off, it is brilliant value. I would love to give this place 5 out of 5 but, for me, the room, although spotlessly clean (as was the rest of the hotel)just seemed a bit under par. We would certainly go back.

author: michaeldemp
title: Chef certainly knows what he is doing
text: We stayed for one night to enable us to attend a funeral. They seem to expect a lot from their staff - there seemed to be only one person on duty at any one time and in the evening Holly was doing bar, reception, taking restaurant orders and serving till quite late. She did it all splendidly and with a happy demeanour. Our room was reasonable, quiet and fully equipped. The biscuits were amazing! The only thing was that, even with windows open, it was a bit hot and the duvet was a thick winter one so it was very difficult to get cool. The restaurant was a real surprise. We hadn't been overawed by the menu but the reality was very different. I had perfectly cooked asparagus with a perfectly poached duck egg and hollandaise. Then I had braised beef cheek with green beans. It must have been a large beast because the cheek was enormous. But it was really delicious. My wife had lamb rump, served pink as requested and thoroughly delicious. Maybe a bit on the large size again. My wife had ice cream but I had lemon and pistachio semi freddo which was lovely. The pistachio added texture rather than flavour. We also had a bottle of Malbec for under £20 which was amazing for that price. We have plans to take all our local relations there for Sunday lunch one day. We would happily introduce them to the restaurant. Chef Mike Peters should be proud of his little restaurant - beautifully furnished and decorated, incidentally.

author: mariadelmaradrover
title: Big disapointment
text: I've stayed at this place for 2 nights this Feb 2016. I had been to the Lemon Tree in 2013 and the reason I booked it again this time was because I had a very positive experience in 2013, both the cosy hotel rooms and excellent restaurant. This time my experience was not good at all. I think it had recently changed managers. When I returned to the hotel at 5pm following the first night stay (I was out in a course aal day 9am to 5pm) my room had not been serviced. One of the members of staff explained that because I had taken the room key away with me they didn't have an spare key and they could not enter my room. The member of staff asked me if I needed anything to be done and I asked her if they could get me toilet paper and make the bed while I went for a jog. My surprise on my return was that she had made my bed in a completely careless way (I attach picture), but even more so when she completelly dismissed my opinion about the bed as she didn't think there was anything wrong with it. She went to say that they don't change the bedding unless a client requests it at which point I said I wasn't talking neither asking for change of bedding but just for a bed to be made up to a hotel service standard. She went to say that making beds are not part of the room service at the Lemon Tree since "how would they know how clients prefer their bed to be made...folded duved, tucked in..." at this point I realised there was no point in further discussing this with this member of staff and ask her to see the manager and she told me "I am the manager". Her attitude was at all moment completely the oposite of what you would expect from a person working in hotel/restauration services, not even considering the clients point of view and completely dismissive. I found out the later she was not the manager Unfortunately the following morning when I went for breakfast I left my key inside the room and the door had to be forcefully opened with a screwdriver to access the room by one of the only 2 members of staff available in the morning at the hotel despite breakfast being busy. At the exception of the member of staff in charge of breakfast in the morning, the rest of staff at reception/bar and restaurant although nice were unprofessional and looking lost . The issue with the particular member of staff that argued with me about the bed and pretended she was the manager goes far beyond this. In general the Hotel appears run down, not very clean and with a poor service compared to 2013. The food at the restaurant was reasonable, deserts particularly good but not at all to the standards as before ( artisan bread is just posh supermarket heated rolls, the olive oil and balsamic deep is vegetable tastless oil -for sure not the virgin olive oil as it says in the menu-... I 'd never formally complained before of a hotel/restaurant! I hope the "real manager" can address these issues and The Lemon Tree can become again that special hotel/restaurant with rooms it once was.

author: tt1960
title: Probably okay for an overnight, but room was too small for anything longer.
text: Spent two nights in the Lemon Tree while visiting family in Wrexham. Staff were friendly and helpful and the free wifi was fast and worked everywhere. The bar was well stocked with both standard beers and a few more esoteric versions. So why won't I be going back? Well, I like to be able to unpack and get at my stuff when I'm staying away, and our room was minute. We had a double bed and there was about two feet of width on one side, and 18 inches on the other. At the foot of the bed there was room to walk round to the bathroom. When I came to wet-shave, my left shoulder was touching the shower and my right shoulder was touching the wall. It didn't stop me shaving, but it didn't make it easy. Add to which the state of the bathroom extractor fan, (lots of fluff and dust), and the noise from the kitchen fan outside our room (okay, that's always going to be a problem but I expect the other rooms don't suffer from it); and it wasn't ideal. Breakfast was average. I had the full english on day one, and ended up leaving about half of it. Day 2, I asked for scrambled egg on toast. I got two rounds of toast, unbuttered, next to a plain omelette sliced up. It's not the same, guys! Overall, it wasn't the disaster it sounds like when I read this back. The staff WERE friendly and helpful. The Wi-Fi- WAS strong and available. The location IS nice and central. and the Wrexham lager IS cold and well stored :-) But I'm getting old, and I like my creature comforts, and I don't like hunting through a suitcase every time I need something, so I'll choose a hotel with a bit more room next time I visit Wrexham.

author: ButtyBach67
title: Saturday Afternoon at the Lemon Tree.
text: My Wife and I called in at the Lemon Tree on a Saturday afternoon for a bite to eat. The Lemon tree is within easy walking distance of the town centre. Lovely decor and furnishings. I was suprised that the restaurant was very quiet for this time of the day. We were greeted by a friendly waitress who showed us to a table. We chose off the two meals for £10 menu. My Wife chose the red pepper, red onion and mozzarella vegetarian burger. This came with a side salad, french fries and coleslaw. I had the battered haddock with hand cut chips. this came with a side salad and tartare sauce. The meals arrived piping hot. The quality of the ingredients was very good. Both meals were very tasty and excellent value for money. Washed down with two pints of Wrexham lager. Two meals for £10! You cant go wrong. Give this place a try. Im sure you will enjoy it.

author: DaiJEvs
title: OK, nothing more
