text: When I arrived I discovered that my pre booked room had just been given to another guest with the same Christian name. I was not too perturbed about that as they simply gave me another room. I am not so sure what would have happened if the hotel had then been full however. The radiator in my room did not work. As it was late at night I could not really be bothered in making any fuss about it. The shower head holder had one available height - low. I tried to adjust it upwards but it immediately slipped back down. OK I suppose if you are short but I am 6'4". At breakfast my order was taken immediately. However, my omelette was then brought as I was half way through my cereal. The omelette was overcooked on the outside and undercooked in the middle. That said, I have stayed here before and had good experiences. I will try it again. It is in a good location and is clean and tidy. Oh, and although I could connect to the internet (or so it told me), the thing was so slow I gave up.

author: Sarum_Castle
title: It's really a restaurant with rooms, rather than an hotel, but was a fair deal for the price paid.
text: This review covers the accommodation at 'The Lemon Tree', my review of my meal will appear in the Restaurant category. Colleagues who have been to Wrexham on business recommended staying in Chester, but only having been through the town previously by train I decided that I did want to stay there. One must judge anywhere by its price: £65 for bed and breakfast anywhere in the UK is difficult to achieve nowadays, but that's what I paid (and this wasn't any special deal). That is more a B&B price, which is really what I got. I did have a very comfortable bed, with clean sheets and towels, good tea and coffee makings and a television which remembered the radio station previously used. So far, so good. There was nowhere to sit in the room but on the bed (which isn't easy if trying to work), the hanging cupboard lacked a door and there was nowhere to hang a dressing gown (in the room or the bathroom). The small bathroom was again clean, but the cold tap needed to be re-secured to the basin. The reaction when I reported this problem suggested that the problem was well known. I'd asked for (and I think been given) a quiet room, although there was still some traffic noise. The over-loud music from the restaurant was clearly audible in my room, but luckily went off in good time. I don't usually have a cooked breakfast, but the selection of cereals, etc wasn't inspiring, so on this occasion I did have something cooked. The staff were very pleasant, with two Wrexham ladies on duty when I arrived and Portuguese ladies covering the morning shift. The Lemon Tree is walkable from Wrexham General station if you haven't got too much baggage. As I have observed, I got a reasonable deal for what I paid, but I wouldn't have wanted to be sharing the room with my wife or staying for more than one night.

author: WelshyGirl11
title: Made my night!
text: I travelled up to Wrexham recently for work. The staff there were great from the moment I walked through the door with their chirpy, happy attitudes - definitely what I needed after a very long commute! I was shown up to my room by Jess and she made sure that I was settled and that she was available if I needed anything. Not long later I had to dash to a meeting, but had a disaster where my phone had only 8% battery left, and my charger would not work. Sam, one of the staff lent me his charger to take to the meeting as I was in a rush - a god send, I was in a new place all on my own with little idea of where I was going, the thought of not having a phone in an emergency. He assured me it was fine to take and bring back. He also made sure I had a rough idea of where I was going in case my phone did die on the way! Exceptional service, in my eyes. When I returned 4 hours later, I thanked Sam and gave him back the charger. He poured me a lovely glass of wine, which I then took up to my room to enjoy while winding down after a long day. My room and bed were really comfortable, the shower was lovely and hot and everything about the room and bathroom were immaculate, with big large towels to wrap up in after a lovely shower. I had a better sleep here in the Lemon Tree than I have done at home for weeks! I hope I'll be making another trip to wrexham soon, just to visit them again! The restaurant looked lovely, I didn't get a chance to eat there in the evening unfortunately, so hopefully next time I can enjoy that there too. Thanks again to all the staff there. You made my trip!

author: JosieHart123
title: Avoid if you want a pleasant quiet stay
text: We arrived at the hotel and was advised that we would have to sit in the snug and wait as they were busy with another party booking. The snug is a long table in the opposite room and was not very welcoming. After waiting nearly 40 minutes we were finally shown to our room which upon entry was freezing cold. The room was really shabby and faced the busy road so was also noisy as its an old building (charming) that does not have double glazing. We asked to move rooms to be away from the noise, we were moved however the wifi did not work in the next room so we had to be moved again..... The next room was just as cold however we were advised that the heating was on a timer and it would come on around 3pm. The room was really really small and the bathroom was not heated so the room was again freezing cold. You can see from my photos it needs a lot of updating. We had to keep the bathroom door shut to keep the cold air out of the room. The staff were not at all helpful and as they had a large dinner booking they really did not want to help us in any way at all. You can really tell that the money is in the restaurant and that the hotel seems to be the thorn in the side. We had a really poor sleep due to the pillows which were flat and all the noise from the restaurant and the constant banging of the entrance door below. People going in and out to smoke etc. We went down to breakfast in the morning and the girl that waited on us was pleasant and the breakfast itself was OK. When we went to check out I was asked if my stay was OK and I replied that it wasn't and that the noise and the unpleasant bedding etc had kept us up all night and was met by, 'Well OK thanks for letting me know.' I was so tired I just paid and left. I wish I had not paid the full amount and complained further as the attitude towards my complaint was met with a total brick wall. If you want comfort, cosy and friendly environment go elsewhere. I travel all over the place and this is not written without true honesty.

author: LakshmiP896
title: Hidden gem in Venice
text: I stayed overnight at Ca dei Polo and though it was a short stay, it was a memorable one. Perfect location to explore venice. it is a 5 minutes walk from Piazza le roma where the ATVO takes you directly from the airport in 25 minutes. Piazza le roma is a good transportation hub from where you can take buses, land and water taxis to centre of venice. The hotel is also just 8 minutes walk from the Santa lucia train station from where you can take trains to explore the rest of Italy. I had a single room which was tastefully decorated and enough space for 1 person including cupboards and a work-desk. The best thing is that unlike many other venice hotels, there is an elevator so you don't have to trudge up with heavy luggage. Wifi is free and fast. There are good restaurants and shops in walking distance from the hotel. I will particularly recommend the one diagonally opposite (operated by a chinese family) for coffee or a quick breakfast. The highlight was really the service. Francesca who manages the hotel is one of the friendliest people I have met and gave me wonderful suggestions for sightseeing, food and transportation. I forgot my phone in the room and left for Verona. Francesca contacted me by email and co-ordinated the return of the phone to me, even though she had to open the reception early for this purpose. I was floored by this service. I would definitely recommend this hotel for anyone who is planning a trip to Venice. For further improvements, I would suggest to put a signboard with the hotel name outside as it is not so easy to locate with just the building number and to install a holder for toiletries in the shower area.

author: FelicityB477
title: Ants! Black hair. And rude management to top it off.
text: I booked this place because the reviews were nothing short of fabulous. I cannot actually believe I'm writing this review. But my experience was so terrible I can't not. The establishment does not deserve its high rating. There was a misunderstanding with check in times, communication wasn't clear however those things happen and it's fine. However the manager was terribly rude about it. There are no staff overnight so by the time I finally managed to get into my room and discovered ants all through the bathroom and creeping into the room, plus long black hairs all through the bathroom (i've got fair hair) there was nothing i could do about it because there were no staff to help me! So I wrote an email overnight to the manager and had to sleep, I'm not joking, with ants in my bed, crawling on me. So disgusting. In the morning I went to discuss it and to be frank, he was flat out rude to me. I said the place was disgusting (ants and hair), he didn't even come to look at the room and said "If you think it's disgusting you can go elsewhere." No apology, no offer of another room, no nothing! I was flabbergasted. The only thing he did right was to not charge me for the night or for cancellation when I did indeed go elsewhere. But incredibly difficult as it was Easter Sunday and last minute accommodation in Venice was through the roof. I paid much more elsewhere, but I couldn't stay in that filth with rude staff. The money was better spent in cleanliness and polite company. I do have photos and video evidence of this, but will not share it here. Overall - a disgrace.

author: 814susang
title: I am torn-- half the staff was GREAT, the other was terrible...
text: I am really torn about this review - I had a great experience dealing with the woman who part owns the B&B before we arrived, she was so sweet and helpful. However, when we arrived we could NOT for the life of us figure out how to get from the public parking area to the B&B with all of our luggage and baby- I called the B&B and spoke to a man who was beyond unhelpful- he was actually mean and rude. He told us to "find a porter and/or find an information booth for help". I was shocked that the place we were paying to stay could not help us get to said place. We spent 45mins in the hot blazing sun with a baby trying to find a porter or information booth. No such luck. I called back and he would not help us and basically told me there was nothing he could do-- which came off as "F off..". Finally we decided to leave the luggage in the car (only one hour parking) and try to find the B&B. When we finally found it the man I had been speaking to was hanging out outside of the place chatting up a chick and seemed like he had to be somewhere and was irritated by our arrival (which was during normal business hrs). Let's just say this left a BAD taste in my mouth about the place. However, after the arrival drama our stay was very pleasant. The woman handled breakfast most days, which was delightful and so was she. I suggest eating on the roof terrace! The rooms were clean and tidy- although a bit misleading about canal views- we did not have any views (just of the backyard). Rooms were quiet. No highchairs for dining. Small elevator. Great location- just very hard to find.

author: katc672017
title: Hidden Treasure
text: We stayed at Ca dei Polo for one night before our cruise. This B&B was a little hard to find due to the house number being worn off in places and it is part of an entire row. It is located very near to the Plazzo Roma and we only had two bridges to cross (the larger one had a ramped side). It is owned by Francesca and Massimiliano, brother and sister. It had a rooftop patio for relaxing, eating, and seeing parts of Venice. The building was exceptionally clean and decorated in true Italian style. I gave the sleep quality average because the mattress was hard and the pillows flat. I need to give a Bravo Zulu to Francesca. She went above and beyond in securing our travel bags from Venice airport. Our bags missed the flight and did not arrive with us. She worked endlessly the day of our arrival to get our bags delivered allowing us to go and enjoy her beautiful city. She recommended a few eateries to us and the essential places to see since we only had a day. We highly recommend this location for your lodging needs. Thank you Francesca and Massimiliano for your hospitality. Rob and Kathy

author: TravelH33
title: One very important detail missing.
text: The hotel is very well situated (south end of Fondamenta dei Tolentini). The air conditioning was very good. The room was clean, the bed was comfortable and all hotel staff I encountered was very friendly. There was even a mini fridge in the room which is great. I never managed to keep my room free from mosquitoes though, resulting in several bad nights. One night I even had sort of a big centipede (6cm) in my room. Nevertheless I was very careful to keep the windows and door closed. I even put up notes for the cleaning staff to keep the windows and door closed. Only on the last day but one I discovered the reason. The bathroom was fitted with an electric fan high up in the wall to move air out of the room to outside, which is great. But the conduit in the wall for the fan was not covered with fine mesh (flyscreen) at all. So at night I would switch off the bathroom light, which would also switch off the fan. And from then on I would have an open conduit between my room and the outside world. Which in summer in Venice is asking for problems. So before the last night I covered the ventilator with paper and tape just before I switched it of. No mosquitoes or scary insects in the room that night. I discussed this in detail with one of the hotel staff and urged her to check the ventilator conduit in all rooms. You really can not have an open conduit between a room and the outside world in Venice. I think this was simply overlooked during construction, but should definitely be corrected before I ever would return.

author: 279carolynk
title: Adorable place to stay on a side canal!
text: Amazing place! We arrived before check-in to store our bags for a tour we had booked. Max buzzed us in and said our room was already available for us and we checked in. Max showed us to our room, informed us of how things were run there at the property, including how to operate the front door, the reception times and what time breakfast was served. Max also gave us a map of Venice and answered every question we shot his way...with great English as well. Wifi was perfect, never had any problems with it at all. The room was impeccably clean, beautiful views of the canal below, large sitting area with large comfortable bed! Room was quiet and we slept like rocks! We didn't find the place hard to find like reviewers mentioned. You have the number of the place and by looking on the map, it's easy to see which canal it's on from the grand canal. The location of this property is perfect. Very close to the train station and right on a side canal from the grand canal. So anytime walking around the island, once you would get to the grand canal, it was so easy to find! Terrace was quant and offered a beautiful view below! Loved our stay here: friendly staff, perfect room, perfect location!

author: audrao2015
title: Beautiful B&B very near to transportation hubs, short walk to main attractions
text: Very clean and beautifully decorated B&B in a great location. We had a room on the first floor with an internal garden view which was very serene, and there's an elevator so you don't have to worry about carrying heavy luggage up the stairs. But as we arrived Venice by train, carrying our luggage over the bridge in front of the train station was quite a work-out and the porter touts charge exorbitantly (between 5-10 euros just to carry over the bridge!) so ignore them at all cost. Be sure you note down the address of the B&B - no. 203 as that is what you'll have to look for since there's no signboard, otherwise you'd definitely be walking up and down the street clueless. Giovanni was great with his warm hospitality and even helped us with our luggage. The B&B's strategic location also means that taking the Piazzale Roma and Ferrovia waterbus stops, which are the main stops for cruising the Grand Canal or for going to the lagoon islands of Murano and Burano just to name a few, are just a stroll away. St Mark's Square and Rialto Bridge are also about 15-20 mins walk away. So convenient. Be sure to also visit the Cannaregio area (same side as the train station) just across the bridge from the hotel, surprisingly lively with plenty of cafes and local shopping! Truly living up to its B&B status, you get served breakfast in bed if you wish to - croissant, bread, crackers, muesli & yoghurt, juice and a delicious cup of cappucino. Just lovely. Bathroom was huge and very clean, nicely heated, so was the bedroom. Free, strong wifi in the room with fast connection was very useful. We left for Marco Polo airport by bus from Piazzale Roma - two small bridges to cross but not an issue with wheeling luggage as the second bridge to the bus station has ramp while the first was just a small bridge - just a 5-min walk to Piazzale Roma with heavy luggage, 2-min without luggage, so it's really close by. All in all, really love our stay in this quaint B&B. Highly recommend it!

author: bkmac
title: Lovely Bed & Breakfast
text: We found this Bed & Breakfast via--where else--Trip Advisor. We needed a place to stay for two nights at the end of a cruise. We were looking for value, location, charm and modern amenities. We got all four at this small B & B. After leaving our cruise ship, we got on the People Mover, an elevated train from the cruise ship dock and rode the 5 minute ride to Piazzele Roma. We followed the hotel's directions to cross over two bridges (one with a ramp; one with only steps), finding the hotel after a couple of missteps. As others have noted, it's not well-marked, but once you know where it is, it's easy to find. We were traveling with friends, and both of us had large, comfortable rooms with king size beds (twins pushed together). There was room for a small table and two chairs; a large armoire; a desk and chair; and nightstand. Our view was of the courtyard, which wasn't quite as nice as a view of the canal enjoyed by some rooms, but was quiet. The bathroom was spacious, with a jetted tub/shower combination and vessel sink. A couple of added bonuses made Ca dei Polo an especially good choice for us--an elevator for schlepping lots of cruise ship luggage, a rooftop terrace (where we enjoyed wine we had purchased elsewhere), and a small snack-like breakfast, with items such as yogurt, croissants, and cereal. The two staff members we met were professional and helpful. One arranged transportation for us to the airport at the end of our stay, at a price of 60€ for four people. The area is lovely, with nearby restaurants and snack bars, but not much shopping. The train station is about a 10 minute walk. Two Grand Canal vaparetto stops are also fairly close by. All-in-all, I would stay here again and would recommend it to others.

author: HarishP553
title: Quaint and comfortable....super location.
text: The biggest thing this place has going for it is the location. Minutes from the station, it could not get any more central, for a wonderful stay in Venice. The staff, are all awesome. Sandy was great with breakfast and keeping the place real clean and cozy. She even opened up the terrace for breakfast, which was sweet of her. I hate myself for this, I cant remember his name, but Massimiliano's assistant, young guy.. was very nice too. Helped me out with directions and pointed me to some nice local digs. Now for the rooms. Large and very comfortable. Original Italian furniture and having all the luxuries one could want. The bathrooms are clean, and well kept. The toiletries super. My only beef with the place is that they need to do a little bit more for the "included breakfast". If the management spruced that up a bit, even improve the coffee and the breakfast pastries a bit, I think it woudl be incredible. When you pay 200 euros a night, a great breakfast is demanded. At minimum, fresh baked croissants an authentic Italian coffee. All said and done, I would recommend this place.

author: ladydog1010
title: Perfect Location xx
text: We recently stayed at Ca dei Polo and loved it, we stayed there the night before we joined our cruise ship. It is a perfect location, only 2 bridges from Piazza Roma where the transport hub is, but also right on the canal and 30 minutes walk from St Marks square. We loved the fact it was a bit further out and quieter than new the main centre of Venice. it was so easy to get to with our luggage 10 minutes walk max. it was also very near the people mover that links the cruise terminal. When we arrived we were greeted by Francesca, her sons and the dogs. We were shown to our suite, basically a larger room over looking the canal. it was beautifully appointed. There was no kettle being Brits we love a cuppa, but Francesca said the tourist board won't allow them to have kettles in the rooms and they dictate that the breakfast items have to be pre wrapped. She also told us they aren't allowed a sign outside because it used to be a private house. she was so helped with everything we asked. Francesca also booked us a Gondola ride with Luca, he was based in the Jewish quarter and it was lovely being in the quieter canals of Venice. the ride was expensive 80 euros for 30 mins, but so worth it. Luca, sang to us and pointed out lots of things on the ride, he also said the prices were governed by he tourist board, so everyone has to charge the same. The hotel had free wifi which was a bonus, but lots of cafes offered it too. I would highly recommend this lovely bed and breakfast a real gem, if you like walking and being a little further out its perfect, Venice is a small place and its very easy to find your way around. If you want to be nearer the centre or in a big hotel it is not for you. I hope we will stay there again soon.

author: wildflowers94
title: Much improvement needed
text: I am convinced that people who write an outstanding review of this hotel is either a friend/family member/ or has been compensated in some way. I had a reservation here in June, 2014. I found the location okay and had confirmed I would be there the day before. However, upon arrival the door was locked & I buzzed for someone over & over & over. A nearby neighbour had come out & enquired if he could help me at all. He telephoned the hotel and eventually spoke with the man that ended up checking me in, but he had been on the roof terrace. He showed me my room, which was sufficient, it was clean and tended to daily. This is the only nice thing I can honestly report. He did not tell me anything about the breakfast included in my rate nor any other service/facility that I have since read about. I was awakened every morning to noise down the hallway, but I did not get up to investigate- I was in bed. Only after checking out and thinking about my experience here, did I surmise that must have been the breakfast room that I was not informed about. I was not informed about the roof terrace either- like how to find it. For the three nights I stayed here, no one was ever around to ask any questions to, so I left with a very negative opinion regarding this accommodation. I would go to Venice again, and although I choose to stay near the train station for convenience sake, I would stay elsewhere because life is just too short and I would stay on the same side of the street that the train station is on to avoid carrying luggage over yet another bridge. Not impressed, nor would I recommend to any person I liked.

author: 567leannn
title: Great hotel in Venice!
text: I spent no less than 11 hours researching options for hotels in Venice. Having never been to Europe, much less Venice, the options overwhelmed me. I finally landed on Ca dei Polo based on location (on the water, but not in the more touristy part of the Grand Canal), price (again, not in more touristy area, so more affordable) and of course, on it's fantastic traveler reviews. If anyone is in the same situation as me - blindly trying to find a place to stay in a foreign city that you have basically no knowledge about - trust these reviews and stay here! It's all true! Stefano is fantastic, the building is wonderfully charming, and the rooms are very comfortable and clean. The area around the hotel has several restaurant options and an amazingly casual, laid back vibe. Additionally, this hotel is very close to the Piazzale Roma (5 minute walk?) which made getting into (via bus) and around (via water taxi) the city very simple. It's also very close to the cruise ship port, which was an added bonus for us. Really can't say enough nice things... Stop your searching, stay here! Note! The building was kind of difficult to find at first. Ask Stefano for directions and follow them to a tee - they are perfect... just don't expect to find a large sign for the hotel. It is a tiny little sign on the wall next to the door (not even on the door itself). It's very easy to miss!

author: CRAFTYCRUISER
title: Pleasant Surprise
text: We arrived at around 9:30am after a cruise and because it was too early for check in they held our luggage for us. When we returned at 1:00pm our bags had already been delivered to our room. We were more than happy with our room. Much larger than we expected. Very clean and nicely decorated. The bathroom was large and had a jetted bathtub which was a nice surprise. It was a little warm in the room but the mosquitoes came in when we opened the window. Internet worked fine. Breakfast was very good. Even had cold meat and cheeses. Elevator available so no dragging luggage up the stairs. Good idea to go on internet and see what outside of building looks like. There is a small name plate on the inside of the door frame but no name from a distance. It is directly across a small canal from Hotel Papadopoli so if you can spot that you are close. Easy and close to get to from bus and train station. Staff very nice and helpful. Would definately stay there again if ever in Venice. Beautiful place. Owner spared no expense in decorating.

author: DerKommisar
title: Reasonable accommodations for Italy
text: The Good: - We had a Deluxe King Suite overlooking the Grand Canal which was quite exceptional. - The room was rather large, complete with couch, table, two chairs, and a mini-fridge. - The staff provided 2 free bottles of water in our fridge (carbonated or still, we just needed to specify). - The restroom was nice, as it had a european-style urinal and toilet and an elegant sink. The Bad: - Breakfast was absolutely HORRIBLE. I seriously couldn't stand it and that is saying something given that my wife and I had been in several countries and hotels and all of their food was at least edible. If you like regular lunch meat with bread, some tough croissants, dried out cakes, and a fruit basket - this is your gig. If it wasn't for the hardboiled eggs, I wouldn't have eaten anything. - The shower was okay, although it's only 1/2-way glassed in which means water gets ALL over the floor. The soap/shampoo wasn't that great either, but it's typical for a hotel. The reception guys are nice, however there is only one staffed at a time and reception closes early (no 24/7) and therefore no wakeup calls. Would we go back again? Maybe, if all other hotels in Venice had awful breakfasts. That honestly was the most disappointing thing I experienced. Lastly, the location is great with respect to the rail station (<10 min walk) and for getting to the buses that head to the airport (<10 min walk). It's poor with respect to the city centre and St. Mark's Square, as it takes nearly 25 minutes to get there (and even longer if you aren't used to the Venetian maze!)

author: Kacee211
title: A memorable stay!
text: We stayed at Ca' Dei Polo on May 9, 2013 for one night before our cruise. What a delightful surprise! I emailed Stephano with our ETA and had just a little difficulty finding the place-because it was closer to the bus terminal, train station and People mover than I thought. Once you go over the second bridge, there will be a building with restaurants in front of you. Make a left, go 25 yards and the place will be right before the wine bar. Stefano saw us coming because he was enjoying a coffee at the outdoor café run by an Asian family. It's a great place to enjoy snacks, coffee and wine while people watching. Stephano showed us around the hotel. He takes great pride in the decorations and furnishings and authentic woodwork. We had a front bedroom to the canal. It was quite lovely. The bathroom was modern and much larger than others that we had encountered in Europe. The rooftop terrace was comfortable and quaint. The breakfast was delightful. I LOVED the location of the place. We were in the quiet section of town and could roam and discover many little niches and shops. We enjoyed the perfect romantic first evening in Venice. It seemed that the whole world was smiling and laughing with us. Thank you, Stephano, for the lovely place. And thank you Venice for the wonderful memory!!

author: Chris_and_Britt
title: Wonderful and Quaint Bed & Breakfast with Great Staff
text: We started our Italian holiday in Venice and were referred to Ca dei Polo by several friends. As other reviews have stated, this is a wonderful place to stay and experience Venice. We stayed for 2 nights, April 20th-22nd. We arrived early in the morning and our room wasn't ready, but the owner led us to the cafe across the canal and bought us a cappuccino while we waited for less than half an hour for them to prepare our room. The location is very convenient to the grand canal, train station and shops and restaurants. It is not marked with a sign so make sure you have the address and/or phone number. Any water taxi or cab service knows where it is. There is a wine bar next door, can't remember the name, but they have a great bar that opens up at 5:00 pm. The cafe across the canal is also good if you want an English style breakfast, but the the buffet at Ca dei Polo is also very good and more than adequate to get your day going. You're less than a five minute walk from the train station and the nearest public water taxi stop. The staff were all great, but we can't say enough good things about Stefano. Friends we were traveling with lost their luggage (the airlines couldn't have been less helpful). After two days of getting the runaround from the airlines - Stefano got involved and like a miracle worker tracked down their luggage (which was mysteriously in route to Florence). He stayed well past the time he should have gone home and instead waited while a courier service he arranged to bring the luggage showed up. As Americans on their first trip to Italy with nothing but the clothes on their backs - you can not imagine how grateful we all were for Stefano's assistance and generosity with his time. It was one of those things you will always be thankful for. One of the pictures below is the courtyard view from our room - so peaceful and quiet. The second picture is a scene of Stefano in a gaggle of luggage delivery men - if you look closely in the lower right-hand corner you can see our friend literally hugging her luggage bag with joy. Great place and great experience in Venice. Thank you!

author: maureenSunshineCoast
title: Venetian Elegance & Comfort
text: Booked this hotel as travelling on a budget.. price & location looked okay...Not just "okay" but what a thrill and delight to stay here. Walking distance to the train or bus terminus, water bus .Piazzale Roma! No matter where i walked the signs leading back to Piazzale Roma were prominent an easy to follow. The hotel itself is sheer Venetian elegance and hospitality. A family treasured/ rebuild/ reproduction from yesteryear. Classy Venetian decor, good size room , comfortable bed, quality fittings through out make this a hotel to relax, feel pampered and secure.. as I was travelling alone.. a priority met. Continental breakfast is more than adequate... Would totally reccommend the hotel.. once the exterior sign is in place ..Hotel will be easily recognised.. .. Hotel only has Street number above black wrought iron gate/ door , and name on intercom at this stage. A very minor issue. (Many thanks to Stefano..).

author: Yi-Jie
title: Awesome!!!!
text: I rate this place 9/10!(There's nothing perfect right? this is the closest i can get :D) Y so? Was in Venezia last week, and was arranged for a night in cà dei polo. As many other reviews mentioned, this palce is just a stone throw away from Piazzale Roma, what more can be better then this? Everything was a breeze from checking in to checking out. Was very welcomed by the lady owner, Miss Polo. After a no more then 5min check-in, she personally showed us to out individual rooms. was really surprised by this act! Once in room, everything was in order, spick and spant. Rooms were very clean and tidy. Not to mention the European feel of the room. Not like other hotels i have been to, its more like a home then a hotel. Arrangements were very personalized and i believe all rooms are of different setup.(Cause i managed to see 3 different rooms). Was ready to head out and as a foreigner, we seeked advise from Miss Polo for food and places of interest. She was more then passionate to introduce to us all the stuffs we could possibly do in Venezia. All in all, i would totally recommend cà dei polo to people who intends to visit Venezia for a place to stay! A ptiy that we only stayed for one night. Cudos to Miss Polo!

author: garryo8893
title: Truly a dream in Venice
text: Our visit here is truly far exceeded our expectations. From the moment we arrived in Venice we were lost, maps are poor at best but you soon learn that's just the way it is, take it in stride, relax and have a good time. We called the B&B after trying several times to find their location even though it's centrally located near the bus station and the train station, not their fault by any means, they can't add a sign to the outside of their building since it's a B&B it's technically a house and.... added to being so overwhelmed with the beauty and the excitement of actually being in Venice we were just flat lost. Anyway to make a long story short Massimiliano one of the owners came and found us and personally escorted us to their inn...turns out we were only a few doors away, pretty funny actually. And that began our fabulous adventure at a truly lovely, warm and gorgeous B&B. Please review the included pictures to get real idea of just how beautiful our suite was. Yes we paid for a suite and it was worth the cost. First class accommodations from the Murano chandeliers and sconce's to the marble bathroom, it was first class in our eyes. We read many times that hotel rooms in Italy are small and ill appointed so walking through the 17th century door into our VERY large suite was truly overwhelming, simply put we loved it and hated to leave after our three day stay. Breakfast was great, yogurt, crescents, various pastries, prosciutto, cereal, coffee (Italian of course, strong and the BEST!) sorry..... there are no ham and eggs, no egg McMuffin, if you want that kind of stuff, don't leave the US after all! Great air conditioning, the bed was large and very comfortable, a little on the firm side which is exactly what we like and to our surprise it was very quiet all night until about 7am when the canal outside our window came to life, it is after all the "road" if you will and thats how goods get delivered etc....so get up and get going on your tours, you shouldn't be sleeping any later anyway! Another of our hosts Stefano Vio is one truly lovely guy, so polite, so caring about their guests a true pro and has the experience to prove it treated us like royalty, what a wonderful guy. You can probably pay less and definitely you can pay more but we cannot imagine any better Euro value than this fabulous B&B and if you don't like it there, sorry, just don't know what's wrong with you...maybe your one of those people who leaves an unfair and negative review because a lightbulb was burned out, seriously what some people can complain about is just unreal. The folks that run this place are absolutely invested in taking care of you like your family...as Massimiliano said more than once "if you're happy, we're happy" guess what he MEANS it, stay here you'll not regret it. We would return in a heartbeat without one second of thought! And yes we are gushing in our review...this place deserves it! You'll soon learn that service in Venice is a little sketchy sometimes, you should know/learn quickly that if you want service you will need to ask...well push a little for it, it's just how's it done in this tourist driven place but NOT at this dreamy place, they can't do enough for you EVER....

author: mer16
title: Una bella Casa
text: Ca dei Polo is much more than a hotel, it is just like home away from home. The location of the hotel is very near the bus station, train station and boat rides very convenient for those with big luggage. It is easy to find if you will only consult a map before going and ofcourse the locals are usually friendly to guide you to the spot. It a place where I guarantee your satisfaction considering you are in Venice . The room we occupied is just the right size for a couple with a table, chairs, cabinet and ofcourse a TV set but who would like to watch TV anyway when there is lot better to see in Venice. The room is charming with their Morano lights and floral decorated ceiling. But what impressed me with this hotel is having the concern of all your needs from bathrobes, slippers, toiletries like bath soap, shampoo, bath gel, lotion, cotton, cotton buds and even foot lotion are little extras that you won't usually find in other B&Bs and even 3 star hotels. There is even a tray of fresh fruits in your table, eating utensils and glasses for your needs. And most of all the room is always kept clean. The breakfast is superbly served by Sonia from coffee, fresh fruits, bread, eggs, ham, cheese, cereals and others. And their roof top is captivating too where you can enjoy the early morning sun and even have the fresh breeze of the night. I tell you that what you would like in Venice is to have a quiet, fresh and friendly atmosphere after a long day in a crowded San Marco area and to have a good night rest. For food it won't be a problem too because there are restaurants, cafes and even a coop grocery just walking distance from the hotel. I am not wrong choosing to stay in Ca dei Polo and I highly recommend it too. Thanks to you guys, to Steffano, Massimilliano and Sonia for a very memorable and pleasant stay in Venice. Will surely choose to stay here again.

author: BazzaT
title: Fabulous place to stay in Venice
text: We have spent 3 nights at ca' Dei Polo, and it has been marvellous. It's location is excellent, 10minutes easy walk to the bus and train stations. Right beside a side canal, in sight of the Grande Canal. Oh so quiet at night. Our room is very large, very clean, quiet aironditioning, and has a large spotless bathroom. Very modern bathroom too, where as the bedroom has just a lovely venetian charm. Beautiful. Breakfast has been delightful, continental with oh so fresh fruit and croissants, cold meats, expresso coffee, juices. Friendly staff, especially Stefano, trying to make sure our stay was the best it could be. They succeeded!! We love the place. There is a modern lift too, to make bag moving easy. And there is also a roof top terrace where you can sit under large shady umberellas in comfortable chairs and watch the sun sets. Sounds great? It is!!

author: m1508
title: Very comfortable, very quiet: just very nice
text: The B&B is located very close to the Piazzale Roma, which means it's only a short walk from the bus station, the train station and the car park. At the same time, it also means you're either in for a bit of a walk to the Rialto or the San Marco square or have to take the boat there. The B&B is located next to a small side-canal of the Canal Grande in an old, but very nicely restored old mansion. The hotel is small, which gives a it very nice quaint feel. Staff are competent, friendly and helpful and speak English well. The rooms are very quiet and have a safe, a TV, a minibar and air-conditioning. Free WiFi is on offer. Breakfast is served in the authentically restored breakfast room and offers a (for Italian standards) wide choice of cold cuts, cheese, fruit juice and yoghurt. The roof terrace offers a nice view of the canal and the street below. This being a B&B and not a hotel, no drinks are served at this terrace, which is really a pity. In short: the B&B is really very good, very authentic and very tastefully restored. So why no 5 stars? Well, for that a couple of (admittedly small) things would have to be changed. For example: some electrical wiring was sticking out of the wall in our room, the safe wasn't fixed to anything, of the 114 TV channels not a single one was non-Italian, the hotel was almost impossible to find (no sign on the outside) and I find a deposit for key-cards and remote controls something more for a youth-hostel than for a place like this. Yes, I admit this is complaining at a high level, but at 200 EUR a night, I feel I'm allowed to. So in short: great B&B, wholly recommended, but some small improvements can still be made.

author: LyudmilaM_12
title: The best choice to stay in Venice
text: When looking for a hotel in Venice maybe you could find a cheaper options (as well as for more expensive ones), but!!! I doubt you could find the same comfort and great service in other places. The hotel is newly renovated and opened just last year. Even though it’s quite small it has an elevator, so you won’t have to carry your suitcases up by stairs. The rooms and the bathrooms are specious and spotlessly clean. I love the wooden floor and amazing chandeliers from Murano glass. The bed and the pillows are very comfy, good quality linen and terry towels. The little dining room is lovely and the breakfast is great. I really liked the location as it’s only couple of minutes’ walk from Piazzale Roma (where the bus station is), so once you arrive you won’t have to wander the streets and bridges of Venice with your heavy suitcases looking for your hotel. And it is just 15 minutes’ walk from San Marco and all the attractions. Or if you’re a bit lazy to walk, then the Vaporetto stop is just near the hotel as well. I really liked that the hotel is located in a quite area, so I could avoid all the noise of the central streets and have good rest at night. The staff is very nice and friendly. Stefano, the manager of this lovely property, really knows what hospitality is about and gives personalized service and attention to every guest. His advices on exploring the city are very useful and his attention and care really made me feel welcomed and…just like at home. If I’m ever coming to Venice again, I certainly know where to stay :o)

author: TheGliicks
title: Great Value, something not often found in Venice
text: After half a dozen less than satisfactory hotel stays in Venice, my wife and I took to renting a delightful apartment near the Frari church for week-long stays. "Been there; done that" set in a few years ago; so Venice became a destination of fond memory rather than yearly destination. Venice reentered our travel plans this year when we opted to ski in the Brenta Dolomites making Marco Polo airport the flight destination of choice. We chose to spend the last couple of days of the ski trip in Venice to try to recapture the magic of La Seranissima. Ca' dei Polo made it work. As of early February, it had been open only four months and it sparkled like new. Rooms are large, very well decorated as are the expansive common areas. Decoration throughout is exceptionally tastful. Bathroom facilities are high quality and there's lots of hot water. Unlike every three star and most Italian four star hotels, the reading lamps actually enable you read in bed, something the snow on our second morning dictated. The location is especially suited to a guest who wants easy access to railway station and Piazzale Roma. This does mean a long walk or a vaporetto ride to most of the most popular tourist attractions. But it also means the neighborhood is quiet when you want it to be quiet. Breakfast is lousy; but in a couple of dozen visits to Italy, we have never had a breakfast worth looking forward to. The 135 euro price was the biggest hotel bargain we've ever found in a popular Italian city.

author: simonpinkstone
title: Good base for short stay in Vienna.
text: I felt I had to write this review to counter balance the previous review which could worry you if you are booked into this hotel. My wife and I booked holiday through secret escapes and checked reviews on trip advisor on each hotel we were staying at in Prague, Vienna and Budapest and they were all pretty good on average over 4 out of 5. Then just before we left we read the latest review giving 1 out of 5 and therefore were dreading this hotel. Now we are fussy especially the wife and we would say this hotel is absolutely fine. I would agree that the area of Vienna is not the best but have not seen any evidence of red light district and have not felt threatened in any way. That is probably because we only walk about 70 metres to tube station and then can be in centre of Vienna St Stephens Cathedral in 15 mins. There is also a tram station just metres from tube station so a little rough but great location for transport into the sights of Vienna. Room is very large a little on the bland side but clean and tidy. Separate toilet and bathroom with shower and bath look newly refurbished and clean and towels were changed daily. Room is warm no air conditioning and a bit noisy if you keep window open. Daily temps have been in low 20 degrees. The hotel reception is a desk but the manager has been very helpful with any questions we have had and the dog is lovely. Breakfast is pretty good cereals breads cheese ham freshly cooked eggs with bacon in a ramekin. Pot of tea or coffee which is fresh. So in summary for a relatively cheap hotel it is a good base for spending most of your time visiting the best areas of Vienna.

author: Maggitay2014
title: The Bates Motel....
text: Arrived at this hotel early evening with my friend, and was greeted by Norman Bates himself on reception. Well to clarify, reception was a desk in the middle of the floor and the man was very weird to say the least, unhelpful, and very unwelcoming. We asked if we could get a drink and we were told they only had beer or wine so we had a beer. After unpacking, we asked where in the area we could get something to eat, and the man told us there was an Austrian restaurant round the corner. Which corner, I have no idea as we walked for an hour and a half round the roughest area I have ever seen, full of brothels and street walkers, drunks and druggies and finally found an Italian run by an Indian. At this point anything would have done so we settled on a couple of omelettes to be on the safe side. As previously mentioned, there is no air conditioning at this hotel and the outside temperature was 37 degrees that day. The room was like an oven and the fan did nothing but circulate hot air. There is also no fridge or tea and coffee making facilities. The room itself was disgusting, see pictures below. The toilet and bathroom were dirty, paper coming off the walls, damp growing on the ceiling and the towels were filthy, full of brown marks, before we had even used them. The television was the oldest, biggest tv I have ever seen and took up half the room. I have to say the breakfast was ok and plenty of it, but we only got that on two days as the hotel had no electric on our second day for over twelve hours from 2200 hrs until after 12.00 noon the next day. Therefore, in the extreme heat, the fan wasn't working either, no lights and no hot drink or food for breakfast. We were on a trip staying in Budapest, Prague and Vienna and as a travel agent, I have travelled the world and stayed in hundreds of hotels. However, I can honestly say, this hotel takes the prize for being the worst I've ever stayed in, in over thirty years in travel, and the area makes any slums look like the Ritz. Whatever you do, avoid this hotel like the plague - one of the worst, if not the worst, hotel experiences I've ever had, and believe me, I've had a few! I would add that the other two hotels on our trip were fine.

author: 539janetg
title: 'Interesting'
text: The previous reviews give every kind of comment and in some ways they were all recognisable! The reception area is an office desk but no less efficient for that. Jonny the dog did' welcome us but we became friends before long. The courtyard garden was sadly peopled with smokers but provided an outside area for a drink. Beer and wine both served by mine host at v reasonable prices. Our room(s) were huge. A sitting room and a bedroom with red curtains and carpet - both + the heat were more than enough to beat the little domestic fan into submission. Bed comfortable, shower small but efficient and if you are plastered there's a little step to trip you up between the bedroom/lounge and the loo. We saw no signs of brothel activity but it wasn't an area a single lady might find comfortable - v close to the ATM and the metro/tram into the city centre. Breakfast was OK. Lots of sweet cake/bread and when some areas are full the spaces between tables can be a challenge! We enjoyed our stay and the good humour of our host. We would probably stay closer to the city centre next time as we prefer to walk rather that public transport. If you like quirky this is for you. If not - stick to chain hotels.

author: ZoeOfShalott
title: Prepare to enter the 19th century
text: We arrived on a very hot day in Vienna. The hotel is about 4km from the centre and we've racked up some great step numbers walking to and from the old town! I mention the heat because, despite the spacious rooms, pretty courtyard and ornate furnishings, we realised straight away that there was no air con, which made the room really muggy. A floor fan helped us to sleep (but kept one of us awake with the noise). I have the feeling that the whole place is a bit stuck in the 19th century. The loo is separate from the main bathroom (on the other side of the rooms, so you have to trail back through living and bedroom to wash your hands) There is no air con. There is no fridge. There was an ice bucket in the room, so we looked for ice. No ice. Why an ice bucket, then? Reception girl replied with a shrug. The breakfast (which is very nice) was served by men in normal attire but women in lady-hosen which seems quite sexist to me. Finally the worst aspect is that we can't get WiFi in the room at all. I am sitting in the lobby to work and access the internet which is far from ideal. What kind of modern hotel doesn't have room internet?? We literally can't do anything (booking tourist activity online, moving money to our travel card) in the privacy of our huge, chintzy suite of rooms. In conclusion, if you want to travel back in time, this hotel is perfect.

author: BristolLights
title: This is an unwelcoming hotel in an unwelcoming part of the city.
text: The hotel is described as traditional Viennese but is more like tired and shabby and in great need of an update. On arrival at the hotel we were met by a growling dog at reception with a proprietor who was just as unwelcoming. The room was large but shabby with no fridge and no hot drink making equipment. There was 1 bottle of warm, fizzy water provided but this wasn't replenished the next day. The local area was equally run down with a brothel right across the street from our room. The metro station was very close but at the pedestrian crossing by the metro you were harassed by gangs of youths. The burger stand by the station was frequented by a bunch of good natured drunks but approaching the stand was a bit intimidating at first. The breakfast in the hotel was very good with good service. The area outside the dining room was piled with catering supplies for the 2 days that we were there. On the first night we came back to the hotel at a reasonable time after dinner in the city and thought we'd have a liqueuer nightcap. However, the only thing available was Schnapps. Interesting but not quite what we wanted but the proprietor seemed to imply it would be unreasonable to expect anything else . We didn't eat in the restaurant other than for breakfast so can't comment on this. Overall the hotel was more like glorified B&B than a hotel. We would not stay there again.

author: drskdas
title: Classy, convenient location, but old and dated
text: We were booked as a family into this hotel as a part of a package holiday. We were disappointed to be given two double rooms on separate floors, room 207 and 307. Rooms were quite large. Room 207 had a pedestal fan and 307 had AC. Both the rooms had a shower room with handbasin left of the doorway and a WC with nothing else in there on the right- rather inconveniently. The rooms had hairdryers but no tea/coffee making facility. Room 207 had a flat screen TV, but 307 had an old CRT, both had poor quality reception of some local channels only. The furnitures were old but would go with the rest of the decor. The decor of the rooms and rest of the hotel was rather dated, with faded carpets and peeling off wallpaper. It smelt musty in places. Could not operate the security safes as per instructions. The internet was flaky, but just enough for basic browsing or a little WhatsApp. The breakfast was good and varied with some individual attention by the waiters. When we enquired of the filter bags used in the teapots to contain the loose tea, we were very kindly given a box of the 'tea filters' we have not seen anywhere before. A nice touch indeed! Public transport in nearby, with underground and trams within 2 minutes walking distance. City centre and the new regional Train station Hauptbahnhof are a bit far away. Overall, convenient for public transport and good breakfast and service, but lacking in modern amenities and needs an updated decor. It's your choice.

author: TulaKitty
title: Enjoyed Our Stay
text: This hotel is not in the city center, but that is okay as there is a station right across the street where one can jump on the subway. We stayed there in August when it was 99 degrees. The suite was huge, but it was also very hot. No a/c and no fan. We had to leave the windows open all night long and as Vienna is a large city, it was very loud all night long. Under normal conditions, we would have enjoyed the large suite more. The bed was very comfortable. The hotel has an elevator for luggage, which was very helpful. However, the wi-fi was very weak as we had to sit by the front door of the suite just to get it to work. The breakfast was excellent with a good selection of cheese, meats and bread. Loved the sparkling wine and orange juice too. There is a formal dining room or outdoor courtyard where one could eat breakfast. There is no free parking, but parking is available at 15 euro per day. We never used the car and appreciated having a covered area in which to park the car. We enjoyed our stay and would more than likely stay here again if we were in Vienna. The subway system was very easy to use, so being out of the ring of the tourist area was not a problem.

author: 786marinab
title: Great hotel
text: When we checked in and we rushed back to the reception to make sure it was a room for us. Had to rush again to confirm a price. A 3rd time we wanted to pay quickly before they changed their minds. Im telling it because I was pleasantly shocked about the room: big and luxurious room and couldn't believe we got such room for such reasonable price (was afraid they put prices up, lol))) Huge bath and shower, separate toilet. Room was split in a bedroom and launch which was very convenient. I like the walls and the chandeliers which are very elegant. Breakfast is a viraety of ham, cheese, juices and teas, even champagne if you wish. I liked baked an egg and ham, pastry is nice as well. Even a blue rock cheese. While having a breakfast you are enjoying a classic music, which made my day. Breakfast is more than enough, making you fool till the evening. Guy who was serving a breakfast was very polite quick and professional: cleaned tables very quickly so was no dirty tables around at all, when bread or something else was finished he quickly replaced it. Thanks him a lot for doing his job properly. The owner is the most charming man, can speak different languages, eager to help and patiently explains the direction, was a pleasure to talk to. One evening when we were sitting in a lobby complemented us with a glass of wine, which was very kind (thank you very much). You can see he puts his heart to his hotel.

author: smart_traveller00
title: Character & Convenience
text: Such a delightful place to stay! Oozing with character and positioned in a very convenient location. I stayed here with a friend for 4 nights and we had a great time. You can catch the train across the road at the end of the street and it's only a short ride to the centre of the city. The room itself had fairly old decor, but that wasn't high on our list & you can choose a more fancy room if you have a bigger budget. We had a view over the courtyard and there was even a closet to put all our bags in. Having a separate toilet to the shower was handy too. The hotel itself has some beautiful features, and was a bit eclectic which I loved. The breakfast dining area made for a gorgeous setting with a large variety of food including hard boiled eggs, specialty cheeses, great vegetable platters, a few cereals and meats, coffee, juices and champagne with orange juice which was a bit special! There is also a lovely cellar which you must check out too. The staff were very knowledgeable and helpful with our arrangements prior to our arrival, answering all my emails punctually. It was also great that they offered parking right out the front of the hotel for a fee (and I think they offer garage parking too). I would definitely stay here again. It was the best value for money we could find in such a central location with so much charm. Also, it is worth getting the Vienna 5-day pass if you are both adults and plan to see a few of the main attractions or shows as you will save $. You can conveniently buy them from the reception area when you check-in. Vienna was a lovely city to explore too. I highly recommend you see the Spanish Riding School, Belvedere and pay to climb the tower at St Stephen's Church to capture a awesome view over the entire city.

author: Mel_Summerwine
title: So and so
text: I've been traveling with another 2 friends (couple). I booked a single room, they booked a double one. They got a huge apartment with living room and dinning space and separete bedroom. I got an aweful small room, in the form of a L, on one side of the L there was a very worn couch and on the other side of the L was the bed. Aside of it, there was a closet , decently spaced for one person, a small night table with lamp and another small table with an ancient TV, as well very very small (sport model if rings a bell to anyone). Needless to say that there was no space to put things needed on hand or any space to work/use laptop. Internet was anyway not working most of the time. The bathroom was decently spaced for one person, but shower was quite clogged so the water was not pouring properly, making it quite a challenge to wash properly. In some days, I got all 3 towels replaced, in some days they just left 2 towels instead of 3, therefore it was funny again to step out of the shower, since the ceramic is quite cold in winter. From a cleanliness point of view, the service was OK-ish, tho the ancient furniture being so worn out would not give any feeling of cleanliness. Breakfast-wise, if you are the first in the morning, then you have the full selection on hand, if you come later probably there will only be leftovers. They refill only after the serving dishes are empty. There is no fridge in the room, so keeping some fruits or yogurt for late evening is not easy. The staff is generally polite and pleasant. Location-wise, it's cross the street from subway, which is fabulous in Vienna. but needs to be changed twice to get to the city center. However this is not a big inconvenient , as subways are fast and very frequent, even in the evening or during holidays. No A/C. Not needed when I traveled as it was winter and the heating was very good, but might be necessary in summer.

author: sortilegus
title: Eclectic and worth a stay
text: I stayed at the Altwienerhof in October and will return in late November. The area is a bit out of the way. From the metro, you will probably have to change trains at least twice. Nevertheless, the hotel is very nice and well worth the price. My first night, I stayed in a room with two single beds and it was more apartment than a room. I left Vienna and returned to the hotel and got a small (and I mean small) room. It was fine because I was leaving in the morning. The breakfast is elegant and complete. The owner/receptionist is Mr. Sorin Panus. He is most helpful and polite. The area is a bit seedy but, personally, I don't mind that too much. There are a lot of Bosnian and Serb bars around and they are Yugo inexpensive. However, there are some red light massage parlours and the like in the area that look more like people trafficking houses. It's depressing.

author: attolug
title: NOT HAPPY
text: Let me start by saying that the manage-owner? of this hotel, Mr. Panos- couldn't be nicer. Unfortunately, it ends there as the property is a hard sell. We booked this on Trip Advisor reviews, but we were very disappointed. (We moved to another hotel as soon as we could.) The rooms were huge - even by US standards, with a huge bedroom and an huge adjoining sitting area that included a couch, chairs, and dining table. However , the furniture looked like bad castoffs, and the room had a Wuthering Heights feel to it with old massive curtains and a morbid feel. There was no quaintness. The door was a key lock, and you had to lock yourself in to close the door at night - which made me think that might be the best option in a fire. The outlet and hair dryer in the bathroom didn't work, so a mirror was placed by the dining area so my wife could dry her hair. The room was noisy as it was on the first floor- we had requested the courtyard when booking, but didn't get it. Breakfast buffet was marginal. There was a charming courtyard, and unfortunately the weather prevented its use. Lastly, the area leaves much to be desired, as the neighborhood surrounding the hotel was marginal, and the metro stop - which was very near the hotel - was horrific. I think you get the picture.

author: GinaSanseverina
title: Clean, courteous and full of old-world Viennese charm
text: This beautiful hotel had bags of character (painted ceilings in the breakfast room, beautiful marble floors, large pleasant rose garden, old Viennese furniture). I stayed here with my daughter on a trip to celebrate her 18th. We had a large double room with shower room (great shower) and separate toilet, all very clean and neat, comfortable and we certainly didn't find it noisy. This hotel is a little way out as some have said, but very easy to get to - Airport bus to Westbahnhof and then one stop on the brown tube line (U6) south to Gumpendorferstrasse. Don't get out of the bus too early, at Meidling, as we did - as you will have to get the tube from a different direction. When you get out of the tube make sure you exit the station on the correct side to save yourself walking a long way up the wrong road like we did! You should be able to see a zebra crossing with a small pizza shop opposite and to the right of that a bar boasting of its "schattiger Garten". The only problems were very small - we couldn't get the wi-fi to work and also the tv didn't seem to come on at all - we did mention the tv to the host but he told us it should be fine and we thought it was probably just us. Same with the wi-fi which we didn't mention as it could have been us being untechnical - and anyway wasn't that important - who needs tv and wi-fi on holiday in Vienna?! The room was not airconditioned so if you arrive during a heatwave like we did, you're going to be too hot. That wasn't the hotel's fault of course, but we weren't expecting to escape the English weather to that extent!. But in the evening it was lovely to come back to a complementary glass of wine as we did, apparently there is a great wine cellar there and wines are available for sale at this hotel although I didn't have time to check it out/buy any. Had a fabulous time, saw everything we wanted to - Vienna is compact and easy to get around although quite hard to find places among the little streets - we had a terrible time locating the Spanish Riding School and had to ask about 5 people for directions when we were only 30 yards away! I recommend the Schoenbrunn, the Riding School, Belvedere ( very rude waiter who could have done with a lesson in politeness from the lovely Altwienerhof staff) the Kapuziner crypt and the St Stefan's tower. Fantastic, and thoroughly recommend the hotel

author: kmarch
title: A Very Comfortable Value with Outstanding Service & Wonderful Breakfast
text: Altwienhof is spotlessly clean, in an older building very convenient to the Metro (a short 3 stops away from the train station) On arrival we were greeted by the broadly smiling Melanie - - It was like we had a full tourist office to ourselves. She grabbed a map, and began marking it for us with Metro stops, her favorite "do not miss" things to do in the city and restaurant recommendations. Nice! The night desk was occupied by Sorin. Again always upbeat and eager to serve a beer or wine or hot tea from the bar if needed, while using the computer in the lobby. The rooms are classic Austria. Spotlessly clean, with the perfect white fitted sheets and one individual feather-bed per person, and big fat feather pillows. We had a room that faced the courtyard. It was very quiet. I would guess rooms that face the street would be noisier. Breakfast was the best - - again with excellent service. A buffet of Muesli, fresh Zemels and other great breads, a meat and cheese area, and warm wieners. Again - classic Austrian breakfast. And of course great coffee served with warm milk upon request. ALL Included with your room cost. The breakfast adds to the excellent value for this Hotel.

author: VictorNeamtu
title: Very stylish centrally located hotel in Vienna for people that want a more vintage experience
text: The hotel is quite unique being decorated in an old fashioned style that really gives you a taste of what life in Vienna used to be like. I've rated each key point separately on a 1-10 scale and explained my thoughts: -Location: 9/10 The hotel is located in the center of Vienna, at about 5-10 minutes walking distance from Mariahilfer Str.. There's also a subway station at 2 minutes walking distance so you can get pretty much anywhere very easily. -Accommodation: 9.5/10 As soon as you walk into the hotel you will be very pleasantly surprised by the old fashioned but very stylish interior design and decorations. Rooms are very spacious and clean and each of them is somewhat unique being decorated with genuine antiquities that really give the place a great vintage feeling. If you like experiencing cities with tradition as they once were you are going to love this place. Bathrooms are very clean and well equipped with everything you need. Also there is free wireless internet both in the lobby and the rooms. The hotel also has a small interior yard with a beautiful garden where you can relax and enjoy a beer or a glass of wine. -Staff: 10/10 The hotel staff is simply great. The manager is a very open and friendly guy that will gladly help you with anything you need, give you advice regarding tourist objectives, restaurants, bars and anything else you might need. If you somehow do manage to ask him something he doesn't know he will gladly look it up online for you (or you can use the computer in the lobby to do it yourself). He speaks english, german, french, italian and romanian and usually handles the reception. The other receptionists are very open and helpful as well and from what i've seen speak at least 3 languages (english, german and french). Overall very professional yet very friendly staff that won't disappoint you.

author: Ambassador22821
title: We will never be going back
text: We stayed here for three nights on the basis of the good reviews from 2004, particularly for the restaurant and the wine cellar. On arriving (during the evening), we noted the various restaurant and wine plaques and awards around the reception, but were very surprised that there was no one in the restaurant. The room was well past its best; Peeling wallpaper, worn furniture, TV not working properly, yellowing net curtains. The general decor of the public spaces also looked shabby. On the plus side, the receptionists were friendly and helpful, but seemed very surprised when we asked to make a reservation in the restaurant. The next morning, breakfast was terrible. Not enough food on the buffet, overstewed, lukewarm coffee, and appalling service. By this stage, we knew something wasn't quite right (given the sparkling reviews we had seen on this place from the previous year), and a brief conversation with one of the receptionists revealed all. The previous owner had passed away, and the hotel had changed hands. The best part of the superb wine cellar had been sold, the restaurant had a cheaper menu and a different chef (all of the aforementioned awards related to the resaurant before it changed hands, and we felt it was misleading having them on the walls), and it was clear that no investment had been made in the place by the new owners. We immediately cancelled our dinner reservation, but decided to stick it out for the last two nights rather than move to another hotel (which in hindsight we should have done immediately). The last straw was on the final morning at breakfast when we saw one of the staff smoking in the entrance to the kitchen, right beside a No Smoking sign. I went to the reception and asked to see the manager to complain. It turned out the smoker in question was the manager! Needless to say, we will never be going back.

author: DesmondO29
title: Average hotel
text: Location is decent, walking distance to old shanghai street, yu yuan garden and cheng huang temple. there's also a starbucks just across the street and a small convenient stall. it's 10 minutes walk to the bund but it is at the end of the bund where the view isn't great. u have to walk a farther 500m at least to the middle of the bund where the view is great. the room's air con seems to not be working. no matter what temperature i choose it always remain at 23 degrees. wifi is slow. staffs are nonchalant. the concierge only help me with my luggage on my check out day most likely for tips. the first day i checked in, no help, the few days i stayed there, not a single greetings from anyone. powerpoint on the wall is loose. i plug in my charger and the thing came loose. there's also sparks coming out from it when that happens. location is hard to get a taxi as well. overall for the price u pay it is pretty decent. but i wont recommend it to any of my friends, and most probably won't be going back.

author: stc200
title: Lovely hotel - with a view of the river!
text: Hotel is part of the Virgin Splendours of China Tour - the first one - and was a perfect introduction to China. The room was of a decent size, bathroom large and comfortable. Bed was a bit on the hard side (which we prefer anyway) - we had twin double beds. There was also limited views of the river - the higher you are the better. The room did smell faintly of cigarette smoke - window was wide open when we got in! The room could do with refurbishing but would be difficult as it is almost full all the time and would be costly to close a floor to get it done. It was not an issue for us. The shopping centre is just round the corner - we had the rest of the afternoon spare so went there. It was a good way to experience everything for the first time. We did go there again with the official group but only had limited time so go on your own if you can. Breakfast - we knew there was a mixture of Western and Chinese but - WOW - It was definetely an experience. Usual coffee, juice, breads, fruit AND noodles, soup, cauliflower with bacon, golden cake, rice, shredded beef, steamed buns, dumplings etc. Had to check watch to see if it was lunch time! This was the norm for the rest of the trip with local differences. There is no bar but local shop round the corner - turn right on exiting the lobby and right again. 4 beers, crisps for 5Y.

author: 1955Westy
title: Lack of English speaking staff.
text: Completely underwhelmed with this complex ! When attempting to book in at their reception we had to wait while they went looking for a staff member who spoke English ! Eventually we got through this process and directed to our room on the 12th floor. The room was very spacious and the ensuite passed muster. The matress was rock hard and after staff fitted two mattress protectors, it was still rock hard ! Management advised that all the beds were identical. We were both tired so we endeavoured to rest and catch up on some sleep. Woke up around 9.30pm to discover that the room service menu was very limited, ordered two bowls of chicken and corn soup. The waiter delivering the soup was surly and didn't recieve any reward because of his attitude ! Buffet breakfast is served in the ground floor restaurant and was not good ! The orange juice was in fact orange cordial, the luke warm toast was as hard as rocks, bacon was inedible, sausages were even worse, scrambled eggs were cold and the dining room staff started clearing the food away at 9.40am (advertised closing time 10.00am) All of the restaurant staff were surly, couldn't or wouldn't understand English. Their coffee was excellent but when I went back for seconds the coffee machine had been removed - a full ten minutes before official closing time ! We never bothered to visit the hotels restaurant again during our three day stay. . Fortunately, there is a 'Starbucks' coffee shop across the square - the food and service was excellent !

author: Oamaruvian
title: Barely suitable
text: We stayed 2 nights here. A good location to the water front but not much of a river view. Most rooms had none. English was not widely spoken with hotel staff, so be ready for some frustrations. They were difficult at times. We arrived after a 12 and half our flight. Got to the hotel by 8.50. Would not let us check in because check in is at 9.00am. At 9.55am we needed some food. Told the restauramt could mot serve us or even let us sit down as lunch wasnt available until 10.00am. Not good at catering for tourists needs. If you lke sleeping on a block of concrete then the beds will suit you. Otherwise the rooms were well appointed with large bathrooms. Taxis are everywhere and cheap. To be honest, you could probably find somewhere more comfortable and accommodating.

author: micaro3030
title: Hotel "ok" - be awere of the Bad Driver
text: We arrived at Riverviw at 12:45 am - the lobby is very nice. A lot of people have been there to take care. The staff does speak english but not that well. So if there would be a problem for example you don't understand how your invoice is created what irritated us than it can be very difficult to discuss it. The first room they gave us smelled very smokie. So we told them to get a non smoking room. That was no problem so we got our room in the 19th floor for one night. You get there two bottles of fresh water a free tea and some canes in the minibar. TV is good, a lot of channels, climatic device works well, the beds are very hard, and when I say very I mean very very. But the very best the Hotel can offer is the location. You are not stressed from carnoise or something like that and you are in 5 minutes on the bund by foot. Unfortunatelly we had a very bad experiance: We ordered a taxi and the driver cheatet us. We suspect that the personal and he know each other. First he drove in the complete wrong direction and we made a complete unnecessary loop to the north before we turned and go with a cupple of unnecessary arcs to Pudong Airport. We were very awere about it because with maps.me you could follow your route. We tried to make him clrear that he's wrong but the chinese are not able to understand englisch german frances or spanish! When we arrived at the airport he wants the dubble price. Because of his "shortcut" we were very late for check in, so we pay without any argue. You can never be sure that you are right Especially not in China. My suggestion to Pudong Airport: Take the Transrapid, very impressive good and solid german technology and than order from longan Road a taxi to the citycentre or try to get a Hotel with a fix price shuttle service.

author: berkshirejane
title: Family holiday visiting daughter living near Shanghai
text: Great location. Nice view of Bund. Excellent overall. Breakfast ok for price. No bar to speak of. Drinks got delivered to lounge area. On river front so two minutes waslk to Bund. Not any atmosphere. City Hotel. We had two rooms. Fine. Toiletries and robes provided. Adequate for price. Very near old town. and Bund.

author: rambo37
title: Hot stuffy room
text: Arrived at the hotel after a scary taxi ride from the airport. It was very late at night and very we were tired from the plane trip. The gentleman at reception was quick and helpful. We went to our room and was met with a very hot and stuffy room. After trying to get the air conditioner to work it kept defaulting to heat. With a temperature of 35 degrees on the pad I rang reception to complain. I was told that there were no other rooms, but an electric fan would be brought up. The hotel actually tries to keep the rooms warm. It would have been about 28 degrees in the room. We found out the next day that you could open the windows a little. Fan did help a little. Beds were not comfortable. The bed was like sleeping on a stone. No bounce in the mattress. I think you may have broken something if you did try to bounce on the bed. Breakfast was cold as the heaters under the hot food were not turned on for the 3 breakfasts we ate there. The manager did help us get our luggage for us.

author: deborahh598
title: NOT UP TO 4 * Standards!
text: We got a very reasonable deal through Agoda but that is no excuse for the Hotel not being up to scratch! When you stay in a 4* Particularly in a major city like Shanghai it is imperative that the Air conditioning works properly.
