The 1st day when we arrived at 1.45pm we had to wait 45 mins to before room(no.1819) was ready. 30 mins after check In time we asked the hotel assistant manager to lower our air conditioning which was set at 22 degrees. He said that the hotel is set at the same temperature throughout. We accepted this but we were surprised that whenever we opened our door, the corridor was far cooler. On the 3rd day I pointed out to the cleaner how hot it was in our room, she too, told reception that there was a problem. They then accepted there was a problem and would we like to change rooms? This was at 5pm and we were due to leave the next day so we declined. Everything we had used from our bags was damp because of the atmosphere in the room. Having used the gym on a few occasions the staff did not know how to set any of the running machines which seemed to be fixed on manual. It is a real shame as this was a lovely hotel and from a review on TripAdvisor before, we had either got the short straw and stayed in the same room or they are keeping the air con high in order to save money. NB. I noted that one of the photos above, shows the temperature set at 30 degrees. Why the photo? unless others have experienced the same problem!

author: sambruce
title: Great value in Shanghai
text: I just finished a 3 day stay at the Riverview Hotel and was very satisfied. The location is great. The Bund, Old Shanghai Street and the Yuyuan Gardens were all easy walks from the hotel. I ate in the hotel restaurant only once, ordering dumplings and mo po tofu from the room service menu and both were very tasty. For the more adventurous persons, there is plenty of tasty food to be had along Old Shanghai Street at very affordable prices but be prepared to eat like the locals. A little further away is even more food at the YuYuan Gardens with more variety and higher prices. The room was clean and not noisy. The bed was unusually hard but comfortable. Housekeeping was a little stingy with water and coffee but they were willing to send someone up with more of both when I asked, no problem. There's an in-room safe but read the instructions carefully before using! I did not and I ended up having to ask someone to come up to open the safe for me. There's a little red button on the inside of the safe door that you have to press first to get it to work. Taxis were readily available and the trip to the Pudong airport ran almost RMB 200, so be prepared. Staff speak pretty good English. Free Wifi. Book through Agoda or Priceline to get a very significant discount and save alot of money!

author: Roams-A-Lot
title: In a downward spiral!
text: I have stayed at the Riverview Hotel many times in the past few years. And I have seen it in a steep decline. The hotel used to be frequented by independent tourists as well as tour groups and the hotel used to be bustling. Now it is like a tomb and you feel like you are the only one staying there. The hotel location is the key positive feature - it is a short walk to the waterfront, to Yu Gardens and to Old Shanghai. However, this positive is overshadowed by the discomfort of the rooms. The central air conditioning is set and not adjustable in the room. This is, of course, to save them money. The problem is that the rooms are uncomfortably hot. Add to that the fact that the beds are the worst I’ve ever encountered (anywhere!) means that this hotel is not a good choice! Obviously others have made the same decision. As the hotel has lost guests, they have not downgraded services gracefully. The breakfast buffet used to be extensive and quite good. You often had to wait for a seat at breakfast as the buffet was that popular. Now you may only see two or three other people present for breakfast. As they have scaled back, the breakfast is now just barely tolerable. The selection and quality are greatly reduced. The orange juice is just orange-colored water. The croissants were paraded out each day, but were days old and hard as a rock. There are many other hotels in the Yu Garden area - and any one of them has to be a better choice than the Riverview Hotel!

author: SensorCEO
title: 4 stars for China, 3 for anywhere else
text: First, most taxis have trouble finding this hotel, so be prepared with address card and instructions. I wouldn't say it's close to the Bund--15-20 minute walk, so requires taxi if you want breakfast outside the hotel. Carpets are dirty & rooms other than yours are unheated, but that's common for China, as are hard beds. Tiny closet, bigger one in my biz partner's room, but his heater was broken, so was on non-stop, making for a balmy room. Difficult if you're planning to stay more than a few nights. Breakfast is pretty good, but mostly Chinese dishes...at least we had boiled eggs, which is kinda steep at $9USD/pp. Coffee is horrible, so bring your own Starbuck's Vias for use with the hot pot provided :) Laundry is outrageous for China, so plan to wash your own, or skip it. There is a new construction starting on the City View side, and they work from 6:30am, so it can be noisy for those trying to sleep in. Make sure you get a room above floor 10 or you won't see the river. Staff were helpful & kind, but do expect to tip, about $1-2 for a taxi or bags. The fitness room isn't heated until you arrive, but they had some free weights and aerobic machines. Private rooms for business are nice, but like anywhere, including the "non smoking" rooms, smoking is allowed everywhere, and they keep the windows open to air it out. There is NO wifi anywhere, so be prepared to plug in if you need access. All in all it's a nice looking hotel with good staff, but don't expect 4-star level like America. But when I consider what I paid...what should I expect? It's still a decent value.

author: LSmithTO
title: Great hotel, good location
text: My family stayed in this hotel very recently for three nights. Our rooms were very large and the bathrooms were spacious and clean. The amenities in the room were very nice. We were on the 8th floor with limited river views. Next time I would ask for the highest floor possible for incredible views. Service was friendly and prompt. Twice we called housekeeping for ice and it was brought to us without delay. Housekeeping did an excellent job cleaning the room daily. Buffet breakfast was fine with an omelet station. Concierge was very helpful and friendly giving us directions to Old Shanghai (about three blocks away) and also the ferry terminal for the night cruise which was very close by. Yuan Gardens are an easy walk. Subway was about a 15 minute walk away. Nanjing Road shopping area was just one stop on a very clean subway line. The Bund is 1 km away. There is a small gift shop in the lobby with quality products, very reasonable prices and friendly staff.

author: Max_O6363
title: Ready for a cold shower – I wasn’t.
text: Unfortunately things did not go well to start with where the hotel lost all hot water and failed to get a trade’s person onsite quickly to fix the problem. All guest either showered / washed in a cold shower of went elsewhere. No apology offered, no notification received until I asked and only offered a response of ‘it’s never happened before’. This type of event could have been handled far better taking into account the hotel’s guests best interests. I’ve stayed numerous times at this hotel as do like the location and ease to walk to town, restaurants and cafés. There is limited and tight car parking available, it’s free but need to be extra careful when manoeuvring around the narrow car park area to save damaging other cars or your vehicle. I parked one night on the road due to the lack of space to fit a medium-sized sedan onsite. The rooms are very clean and tidy yet are quite dated. This hotel really needs a huge upgrade to bring it alive into the real world where you find up-market competitors these days. This is where Copthorne use to sit in the old days. The lift between 3 floors seems like the slowest lift on the planet, both waiting for it to arrive and while using. It’s easy to get lost in the maze of corridors to rooms so read room direction signs as you leave reception to get to where you need to. The room is comfortable, the aircon isn’t overly responsive as did not seem to alter to temperatures I set and can be noisy on higher fan settings. There was no opening outside window in the room, but found the room very quiet which is a bonus to a good night’s sleep. There is a Sky Decoder in the room with access to sky movies plus sports being great along with free Wi-Fi (password given at check-in). From that aspect the hotel does well. With usual kettle, mugs, sachets of hot beverages there is also a mini bar and snack basket yet with a Service Station across the road you could save a small fortune and grab some snacks and non-alcoholic drinks from there.

author: DeanM8013
title: Nice and easy for an overnight stay
text: My second time for work in New Plymouth had me staying in the Corpthorne Central Hotel. There was freeing parking for my rental car. Note that there are limited spaces. The check in was easy and friendly. I was in a standard room with a Queen/King size bed. Very comfortable and clean. The room had the standard facilities like TV (sky), mini fridge, spa bath etc. This room had a desk and some comfortable sitting chairs which was very nice. The gym was ok. A bit more than a home gym but not quite as many things as I've come to find in a hotel chain. I ordered room service a bit before 8pm as I was out exploring the centre city as there was a Hot Rod convention on. The nice person advised that it was a 40 min wait which I didnt mind as it gave me a chance to shower and change. The water pressure was fantastic. My dinner when it arrived was hot, yummy and filling. I had a good night sleep in the bed without hearing any outside noise. I went down for breakfast and it was very nice. They don't have a hot food buffet, just a cold food one. You order your hot breakfast and they make it for you. Overall a nice place for an overnight work trip.

author: Max_O6363
title: Half Good Half Not
text: Set in the heart of the CBD – easy walk to everything including the walkway along the sea front. Finding your room in this 3-story hotel is a maze of corridors, finding the restaurant is even harder – faster to go out the main entrance and walk around the side of the building into the restaurant. There are numerous car parks available – just log your car registration at the reception area when checking in. The room is small yet extremely clean and tidy, well-appointed and quiet. There is no opening external window for fresh air which is a bit of a let-down. My room had a mini bar of sorts, tea and coffee and the usual over-priced snack foods though there is a BP service station directly opposite. One interesting comment is the spa bath where a small notice on the wall indicates the spa motor starts up without warning in a self-clean process. I did not use the spa tub save the shower which still activated the auto self-cleaning which gives you that ‘what the hell’ when it starts up and runs for a minute or two on two occasions. Enjoyed a very comfortable sleep – great bed and did not require the ‘inhouse’ air-conditioning on that night which can be a bit noisy for older hotels. The restaurant became a disappointment expecting a buffet type breakfast but was informed there were not enough guests so order from the menu. That’s all good accept if you want the continental and a full cooked breakfast you are facing a bill of around $42. I’ve never experienced anything like this before and when enquiring was informed I could have a cooked breakfast plus a filter coffee (bottomless cup) for an additional $3.50 or a flat white for $5. A fruit juice was I think another $3.50 or cereal and fruit add another $5. How bizarre. Scared to ask how much for an additional piece of toast and butter might cost. Did not get my tick of approval and think their method is way off the mark compared to other hotels (numerous) I’ve stayed in across the country. Of interest there is a very inviting café right next door though doesn’t open until 7.30am. I would return and stay at the Copthorne as was very comfortable though unless their dining policy changes I would go to the café next door.

author: 668DavidM668
title: Thank goodness for Maureen
text: We booked this hotel having previously stayed in the sister hotel in Rotorua (Millennium hotels) The difference was like chalk and cheese. Maureen gave us a warm and friendly welcome with good directions to the centre and seafront. A short walk from the hotel. We had asked for a quiet room and we were put in a room to the side of the building. The first night we were kept awake by an adjoining air conditioning unit. Breakfast was served in the basement. Not many people in for breakfast (breakfast ended at 9 far too early for a hotel at weekends) and the waitress appeared as though she didn't want to be there. Second night we returned from a night out not too late (before 10) only to enter our room and have the noise of a party taking place on the roof opposite with what I can only describe as boom boom music. Went to reception and fortunately Maureen was still on duty and we were moved to a quiet ground floor room. On returning to our original room in the morning to pick up our belongings the adjoining room to ours was playing loud music. This guest continued to play his ghetto blaster through the corridor to reception. We checked out after them and the receptionist stated how rude they were. Reluctantly we paid for our 2 nights but we feel on reflection a refund should have been provided. Very grateful to Maureen for all her efforts. Very much appreciated.

author: CherieM127
title: Disappointing Visit
text: Arrived at hotel after a long day and trip at about 730 pm. Although the website stated the hotel restaurant would be open on 10 January (this was 11 Jan), I was told by reception the restaurant was closed, The chef apparently 'had a problem'. I was invited to walk into town to get Subway but as I'd had a long day and an early start the next morning I decided against it and flagged dinner. My room, 208, was a disappointment. It was dark and small with pretty basic furnishings. The toilet cistern ran all night. I couldn't find a compendium and had to ring reception twice; once for tv instructions (they'd just changed the Sky and there was a sequence to get the tv to work. How people would know that without instructions I have no idea). I also had to call to get a 0430 wake up call. Which I never got. Good thing I was awake anyway with the toilet constantly running. The bed was comfortable and the room was clean. However the bathroom was old and the room lacked ambience. I stay in a lot of hotels nationwide and the staff Copthorne Grand could do with furnishing upgrades (of my room anyway) and customer service enhancements. It was certainly not up to the standards of it's partner hotels around the country.

author: Katsolo
title: A new favourite
text: Stayed here two nights and really enjoyed it. Good parking (free) which is handy if you want to walk around the city. 10-15 min walk to Pukekura Parks. 5 min to the new Len Lye building 5 min to the museum and foreshore. Room. Perfect! Supremely clean. Bed was so comfortable. Reception. Provided a warm welcome and speedy check out. Room service. Faultless. Yum! Noise. Triple glazing meant a super quiet night. Wiifii was good and easy to access.

author: KatheJTP
title: A fabulous stay - EVERY time!
text: I have spent more time in New plymouth this year, than I have in my lifetime! I chose this motel for it's proximity to the city. On many counts, I was not disappointed. From the moment I stepped into the reception area, the likes of Jasmine greeted me with a warm, friendly and inviting smile. Within moments. I was guided to my room where I walked into a light, spotless and beautifully set up space. (Spacious, clean and luxurious!) When I headed to the restaurant to work and eat, the staff there Logan (greatest chef ever!) Lara (the personable, bubbly and very friendly gorgeous blonde) and Faiz (the warm and friendly general manager) made me feel sooooo welcome. It was not hard for me to decide to keep coming back here time and time again! I have had no need whatsoever to look elsewhere. Just this past week on maybe my 6th? 7th? 8th? visit to this motel this year, it felt like I was returning home! While the menu had changed for this Spring season (and I am so boring that I like repeating my order!) Lara and Faiz kindly asked Logan (maybe I tried to bribe him too!) to whip up a seafood platter for me to nibble on. Suffice to say, for as many times as I am in New Plymouth, the Copthorne Grand Central motel is my pick of the bunch! (By the way, I move around the country a little bit and this motel is definitely my favourite one) Thank you Copthorne Grand Central for taking such good care of me. I feel VERY spoilt! :-)

author: Strickes
title: Lovellace to stay, very central to CBD
text: My husband and I have just spent two nights here. First time at the Copthorne in New Plymouth. Lovely rooms, decor etc all in ex condition. Excellent range of items supplied, sewing kit, cutton buds, shampoo etc. Very impressed. Bed was very comfortable. Only downside was room we were in (322) had a bit of traffic noise from early approx 5.30 each morning. Traffic going to work. Other times didn't really notice it at all. Staff were all very welcoming, both in reception and restaurant where we had buffet breakfast each monring. Good range available, a little different from other places, where you chose from the menu for hot part of buffet and rest was on table. Great anyway. It was nice to step outside and be able to walk to town in a few mins, or the Coastal Walkway another few minutes. Very central. Would definitely stay here again. And free parking, some of it undercover.

author: Greenfieldsontour
title: Faulty Towers
text: A bit of a comedy of errors, is the best way to describe my stay at the Grand Central. The hotel is a bit of a rabbit warren, but the corridors are signposted and newly decorated, so I suppose that is something. I walked past all the 200 rooms on the second floor only to find room 229 (?) on the 3rd floor - go figure. The room was tidy and fairly recently refurbished, however when I arrived there was a foul smell coming from the bathroom (possibly through a floor vent). A liberal spray of Ralph Lauren Blue fixed that problem. The only natural light in the room came from a little square window, so high up I couldn't see out of it (see my photo). I liken the room to a prison cell in an attic. After having a shower, every 10 minutes for the next 40 minutes a motor went off for about 10 seconds. It sounded like the spa bath and the first time it gave me the fright of my life. On ringing reception to report a maintenance issue I was told it was the self cleaner on the spa bath. A notice on the wall would have alerted me to this. I went to order room service and the auto dial on the phone didn't work, so was transferred via reception. The next morning when trying to order breakfast the receptionist cut me off 3 times when transferring then called me back to say she was having problems and gave me the extension, which was still incorrect. Finally i noticed the room service number was noted on a complimentary slip with the newspaper, but in frustration and now running late, I ended up flagging breakfast. All in all, a memorable stay, but not one I would repeat.

author: erntravels
title: Dumpy and fraying everywhere
text: Our travel agent had booked us into a "run of the house" room (#230) in this dumpy, frumpy chain hotel, probably because we had wanted to see Mount Egmont National Park and this was the closest location for lodging. The whole place is weird: the layout of the hotel (various halls and stairs) as well as the room. The room was VERY dark, with a strange triangular shaped window at the upper right edge of a high ceiling. I could not tell which direction we were facing, but it was not noisy, at least. There was a very small closet with iron and ironing board, a suitcase bench, a stocked fridge with TV, a very small table and chair, and a frumpy double bed on dark "carpet." The small bathroom had, of all things, a hot tub/shower combination. Again, curiously, the amenities included a shoe mitt (the first in all of NZ), tissues, soap, shampoo, and a sewing kit. The hot tub made strange, gurgling noises after we used the shower, probably for some sort of cleaning purpose. The room did not smell, but it was certainly not inviting at all. It was so dark! The hotel is within easy walking distance to "downtown" New Plymouth, which did not seem to have too much to offer other than a splendid path along the seaside, a "wind wand," a few bars and restaurants. There seemed to be other, perhaps better hotels nearer to the sea than the Copthorne. The clerk let us have an internet username and password, which otherwise would have been $15 NZD. Parking was included. The included breakfast the next morning was in the hotel's ground floor restaurant, with a mediocre "buffet" and cooked to order, acceptable but not generous hot breakfast. We had eggs and bacon with toast. Based on our experience, this hotel would be a 1.5-2-star in Europe.

author: Samwisely
title: Really good location.
text: The location is just right for a walk down to the waterfront and to the restaurants. Free parking in a city hotel is always a winner in my book. Please don't change this. We decided after checking in and seeing the rooms that we would stay another night as it was quite comfortable and the weather was looking good. The aircon was a God send on our second night as it got so warm. Our family in the room next door had left their window open instead and experienced a bit of the Saturday night crowd. We didn't hear a thing with the Windows closed. The view wasn't spectacular but that didn't bother us. We didn't find time to use the spa bath but the bathrooms were well equipped if you had forgotten anything. Silly complaint but its only a little one but the tissue paper could have doubled for sand paper. The 2 different receptionists we dealt with were very friendly and very helpful and town maps are always good to have. We decided to have breakfast in the restaurant the morning we were checking out. We only wanted a very light breakfast which wasn't on the menu but the staff were very accommodating and we were able to just have tea and toast instead of the full cooked or large continental that was on the menu. The addition of this to the breakfast menu might be an idea. Would definitely recommend and stay again.

author: Kiwis-two
title: Comfortable Hotel in Convenient Downtown Location
text: Our "average score" doesn't mean there is anything terribly wrong with this hotel. It's just not an outstanding place but is quite comfortable. We were in room 35 which looked out over some roofs and the car park. That wasn't of concern for us. The room was clean although at first we thought it had a faint stale smell but a few minutes with the window opened changed that. The colour scheme was in autumn tones. The bed was quite comfortable but unremarkable. The room had a small round table and casual chairs and a work site for computer and other activities. The bathroom was just practical with a shower over a corner bath tub with spa jets in the bottom. Our check in experience was slow while we waited for the lone receptionist to answer phones and assist an enquiry from another guest. We dined at the house restaurant and found service to be very slow despite only about 4 other diners present in the restaurant. My chosen main, pork belly, was dry and not up to the standard that I have experienced with similar dishes at other restaurants. But our waitress was friendly and welcoming. There is hotel car parking available and it is without charge. I suspect that if the hotel is heavily booked the parking facilities would not cope with a full house but we had parking options to choose from. The Copthorne Central is well located to walk around the corner into the main street of New Plymouth. And there is a good selection of dining options within easy walking distance. We would choose to stay again because of the convenient location.

author: JandJfromNZ
title: One place to not stay
text: We had a function at this hotel and then stayed overnight (15 Nov 12). The events manager (Hillary) was very good, but the rest of the stay was a bad experience. We decided to eat in, but on arrival at large restaurant found the place was empty! Foolishly, we opted to stay. Ordered bread for starters - still cold in the middle and spreads were very ordinary. Considered quitting then but too wimpy, and when mains arrived - my colleagues looked like vomit from a giant animal. Contained lumps of fatty tissue and was inedible. I had lamb shanks - meat fine but the vegetable pile had fibrous parsnip and lumps of inedible leaf (think it was old Rosemary leaves). Colleague's meal taken away and offered a second - neither of which we were billed for. Had to book out at 6am for early flight so rang reception at night to check on check out times - fine as "reception staff arrive at 6am". Ordered breakfast for 5.30am - but it was not delivered until 5.45am so it was too late to eat it. Went to book out at 5.55am but no one around. At 6.10am with 4 guests waiting to check out a girl arrived and rang night porter to take payments. Night porter arrived at 6.12am but unable to use computer and take payment so hand wrote credit card details - no receipt given. Left at 6.15am but still no sign of reception staff. Rooms spacious but tired. Service is slack and food is crap. Found out later that hotel is well known in local community for its poor quality of service and relatively high rates. Many hotels around with good service and with similar or cheaper rates.

author: gohomemumbai
title: A perfect choice for us
text: I really researched a lot of accommodation options for St Petersburg. In the end, due to its close proximity to the Mariinsky theatre and its great reviews we selected Alexander House. What a great choice! From the moment we arrived at the airport being met by their driver and whisked off after 26 hours of flying it was a relief to arrive to our beautiful room with a view of their internal courtyard - we stayed for 5 nights. The staff were all just amazing, just couldn't select one person to praise. The food was excellent and we ate dinner there 4 out of the 5 nights. The breakfast was substantial with variety each day, but I must admit I went for the salmon and herring every morning, it was delicious. Eggs any way as well as three different types of porridge. The location was perfect, we are walkers. Started the day with a taxi to our first choice destination then walked back at the end of the day. There is a bus #181 which gets you into town easily. Just pay the conductor on the bus. There is an ATM close by as well as a supermarket that sells great German and French wines if you want a bit of a tipple in your room. The theatre is also 10 minutes walk away. The boutique hotel (an old converted mansion) is amazing and we loved the open fire in the evenings. Tried lots of Russian vodka with cranberry juice - lovely. Nothing was too much trouble for the staff and there was always someone there to help even late at night. Thanks Alexander House

author: 21gracebk
title: Russian hospitality with a smile.
text: This was our first visit to St. Petersburg. We travelled with our teenage daughter and stayed in the Amsterdam room. Before arriving I had many correspondence with the hotel, and they had set up our room with an extra bed as well as our tour and our ride from and to the airport. The room was spacious, AC worked great(during the record heat week), and the breakfast was yummy every morning. We had so many questions and requests, and they answered all of our questions and met our requests with a smile every time. We had arranged for a tour through the hotel for three days and the tour guide and the driver were wonderful. For one morning, we had to start our tour earlier than the breakfast time at the hotel and they prepared our food for us before the time they were open. So nice of them. They were so thoughtful with every offer and suggestions they made. We asked for restaurant recommendations and they gave us many choices and sent us to yummy restaurants. We mainly used Uber, so not being near the subway station wasn't an issue when we wanted to go farther than the areas around the hotel. We really enjoyed our stay at the Alexander House and would recommend anyone going to St. Petersburg to stay here. We had a wonderful time.

author: sanjeevah
title: Great stay !
text: Wow what a stay at Alexander house, St Petersburg. It was the most amazing experience. I stayed at the hotel from 24th June to 26th June and I had the best stay. Check in and check out was simple and hassle free. They have 24 hour staff at the reception so, can check in at any time. Staff are the friendliest I have met anywhere in the world. They all speak very good enlgish and will go out of their way to help. I forgot about my check out and was about 2 hours late for check out. Despite this the staff were very considerate and polite and even apologized to me when it wasn't their fault !!!! The staff are just amazing ! Very clean hotel and rooms. The ambience is of a large manor house and there are two communal areas (one library and one social area) which gives the impression that you are actually in a european village manor rather than a hotel. I am not a fussy breakfast person, but the breakfast has both continental and english options with a variety of yummy russian baked stuff. Dinner is a la carte and will be made on request in a short amount of time. There is a outdoor area with bird songs where you can enjoy the meals in serenity. Quite close to city. Unfortunately there is no health fitness facility in the hotel but there is ome about 1.5km away. Great boutique hotel and will definitely stay there again

author: dagtj
title: One of the best places we've ever stayed in
text: It's rare to find absolutely nothing negative to say about a living place. We came to explore the old city centre. We had walking distance to all major attractions on this side of the river (15-45 minutes). The Mariinsky is just down the street, or rather, the canal. The stylish, old house is situated in a quite street, no noise night or day. The staff is super-friendly and helpful with good English. We felt they sincerely wanted all our best. All rooms have different interior. We choose Deluxe with spacious living room and bath room. It felt fresh and clean. Very good value for money. Food was very good. Service 24 hours. Fireplaces in the evenings (this was winter). Can highly recommend to all good people. Staying here was a considerable contribution to make a very pleasant stay in St Petersburg. It's a truly rare find!

author: mortytarg
title: a most fantastic stay
text: We stayed at the Alexander House for 8 days at the beginning of June. The hotel is in a very convenient area near the Mariinsky theater. Given that the center of St Petersburg is relatively small, we easily walked from the hotel to the center of town in half an hour or we took the convenient buses to the downtown area. The room was beautiful, large, clean and very well taken care of. The bedding and towels were always perfect. The hotel had extra spaces for a library and a meeting room. But, what puts this hotel above many others we have stayed at is the service of the staff. They all spoke excellent English and were always there to help, even throughout the night. They helped in every way possible, usually without our asking. They greeted us every time we came in or left. They carried our luggage to our room and out when we left. They gave us umbrellas when it was raining. The breakfast was really fine. Since we stayed more than 4 nights, they arranged for a free pickup at the airport, which for us was very important. As we came out of customs, an English-speaking gentleman was there with our name on a sign. Since this was our first trip to Russia and since we do not speak Russian, not having to worry about how to change money or find transport from the airport to the hotel was a very big help. At the hotel, they told us where to change money at a very good rate and explained to us how to navigate the bus system. They supplied us with maps, directions and any other arrangements we needed. They took care of our special needs in a manner above and beyond our expectations. I can highly recommend the Alexander House without any hesitation.

author: ExPattyO
title: My First Perfect Review!
text: From my first contact with the hotel ... calling for reservations, to my last goodbye every moment of dealing with the staff at the Alexander House Hotel was wonderful. Everyone on the staff seemed to really enjoy their jobs and dealing with the guests ... they were friendly and helpful while still being extremely professional. When asked if there is one staff member who stands out (on the usual review forms) I would have to list every one of the people I had the pleasure to deal with! The room we stayed in was lovely (the Marrakesh) it had a great seating area with comfortable couches. The bed was extremely comfortable (we truly hated leaving it behind!). The bathroom was well outfitted with robes, slippers and very good quality toiletries. The breakfast was fantastic ... some same items but always enough variety in the hot foods and sweets to keep us wondering what was to come. We were lucky enough to stay here to celebrate my husband's 50th birthday. I informed the hotel of this in advance and when we got back from a day out on his birthday we got a knock on the door and were presented with a bottle of sparkling wine and bonbons. The young ladies from the restaurant and front desk who delivered it seemed truly happy to be making the day more special for us (which it did!). All of the concierges that we dealt with went out of their way to help me to find that special gift that I was searching for (thank you Valentin!) and to point us in all the right directions. My husband and I are expats and travel quite a bit ... this hotel stay is the best we have ever experienced ... a memory that will truly stay with us. I can't recommend them highly enough!

author: SouthernSkyAdv
title: One of the best hotel stays I've ever had
text: Just finished spending 3 nights at the Alexander House after being referred by a friend. Old historic building with modern amenities and a staff to rival the Ritz Carlton. I stayed on the 2nd floor in the Stockholm room and had a beautiful view of the church nearby. The room was spotless, minibar was well stocked and the daily cleaning service was efficient. The breakfast was large in offerings. The dinner menu was ample and the food was delicious. The ambience of this property is a real draw at being only 20 rooms. However, the greatest attraction to this boutique hotel is the staff. There is a reason this property is ranked #1 of over 300 offerings in its class in St. Petersburg and that reason is the staff. The entire staff was highly professional, helpful, courteous and engaging. The Ritz Carlton has nothing on this group of employees. Well done. The property is very well located to all the major city center attractions of St. Petersburg. Make haste to this property. You will not be disappointed. I will be back soon.

author: hwcii
title: Didn't want to leave!
text: The Alexander House deserves its #1 rating on TripAdvisor. I visited Russia before in organized tour groups, but this was the first time on my own. I was concerned about the language and transportation. No worries at this lovely hotel. I felt welcomed and taken care of from the moment I walked in. The desk and concierge staff are fantastic. I was fortunate to have the St. Petersburg room, which was large and well appointed, with a huge bathroom. I enjoyed the hotel's breakfast, and had a nice dinner twice. Took me about 15 minutes to walk to the Mariinsky Theater. The concierge was super helpful and patient while educating me on bus and metro options. His guidance was perfect and I used public transportation with no problems. It's true to say it's a long (long) walk to a metro station, but you can pick up various bus routes a block away. I highly recommend a visit to the Russian National Museum, before or after the somewhat more famous Hermitage. On two occasions, the concierge arranged a driver for me, and everything worked beautifully. This is an A+ hotel. Top recommendation, and I'd love to visit again.

author: LVarro
title: Excellent choice in a quiet part of town
text: I spent six nights at this hotel in late October 2015, and I was quite impressed by the quality of the services. My room, Bali, was more a suite then a room, tastily furnished and exceptionally well maintained. Its windows opened onto a courtyard on one side and a narrow ally on the other, ensuring that in exchange for the lack of views I had guaranteed quiet nights without any disturbance. The room was equipped with a safe large enough to store my 15-inch laptop and large SLR cameras, had independent heating/cooling system, and a bathroom with heated floor. There was also a fully stacked mini bar, but I missed tea/coffee and hot water in the room. The restaurant is open 24 hours and serves super delicious dishes. Most of these are traditional Russian or Ukrainian fares, giving travelers a chance to sample local cooking in a very cosy environment. On most evenings we had the fire roaring in the fireplace. Breakfast has the usual cold selection laid out on tables, with a wide range of cooked options to be ordered. The hotel is relatively small to ensure personal treatment. I found the staff members very friendly and attentive to all my needs. They all spoke excellent English, and were more than happy to play along as I tried to use my limited Russian. There is blazing-quick wifi in the entire building, and the common room is equipped with a laptop and a connected printer. The location may not be to everyone's liking, but I enjoyed being in a quiet side street somewhat away from the usual tourist spots. The Winter Palace complex is about 30 minutes on foot. The nearest subway/metro station is a good 15-minute walk, but there are bus and tram stops only 100 meters away. I was lucky with the weather and this allowed me to walk pretty much to everywhere, but I suspect on rainy days I would have taken advantage of public transport more frequently. Overall I am quite happy that I chose Alexander house and not one of the more usual hotels.

author: sj99ad
title: Calm, Friendly, Wonderful Hotel
text: We booked Alexander House because it was top in Trip Advisor and because the photographs and reviews told a very good story. Our expectations were exceeded. This was our first visit to Russia. We had a transfer arranged from the airport to the hotel, which was organised by the hotel. Perfect. We stayed in room "London". A very nice room, nice bathroom, overlooked the canal, air con etc. Simply perfect. The staff were very welcoming and friendly. Breakfast was excellent. A huge choice from the buffet and they always offered a cooked option as well. Metro is 1.5 km walk, or you can get a bus. We mostly preferred to walk since the location was in a nice district and there were plenty of sights to see on the way. We stayed five nights, but honestly St Petersburg has so much to offer we could have stayed twice as long. Will definitely come back and would for sure stay at this wonderful hotel again.

author: ChairWell
title: Oasis Connected to Town Center by Bus 49
text: Alexander House is perfect for travelers seeking a top quality boutique experience in a secluded lovely location at the confluence of two canals, crowned by a view of cerulean cathedral domes covered with gold stars. Right down the street the old and new Marinsky Theaters with online ticket purchasing service will fill your nights with convenient world class entertainment, A 10 minute walk left on the Fontanka takes you to Caravan Restaurant for delicious Georgian food. You are a long (about 45 to 60 minute) walk from the center, but just two blocks from the bus stop where you catch the 49 bus to the center. Get a good map (Eyewitness Guides have a great one) and follow the streets as you bus to town and you will avoid taxi fees and hassslles. We booked nine nights in the Marrakesh room, a large room in the standard category and recommend it highly. There is some construction noise, but the view of the domes makes up for it and windows when closed seal out most noise. Staff is young, learning, caring, eager to please, and available 24 hours a day to serve meals and assist. They need better maps for clients (the standard maps are small print and hard to follow). To catch the 49 bus, go out the front door, turn left, turn left at the first big street, go down one and one half blocks and you will see a bus stop (do not cross the street). The 49 stops here. Will get you to near Spilled Blood in about 15 minutes. I did not try this until late in trip and wasted much money on taxi fares (about US$10 per trip). Nice walk to center walking straight past Marinsky Theaters then turn right on Moika canal to center (40 minutes). If you have quite a few nights, I recommend staying at Alexander House for half the stay then stay near Hermitage for the other half. You will enjoy the best of both worlds! Because the only disadvantage of Alexander House is not being able to access the fantastic plazas near the Hermitage by just walking out your door. Nickolas Cathedral across the canal from Alexander House is a lovely place to go to early in the morning. I went in about 7:30am and there was a small choir, people standing around lighting candles and praying, a close encounter with spiritual Russia. Grounds around church are lovely.

author: AndyandCathy
title: Good but away from the main action
text: This is a nice small hotel. The staff are friendly and helpful. It is about 40 minutes walk from the Hermitage and main shopping district. Nonetheless if you have time and like walking you will enjoy the canals and architecture of the city as you navigate you way to places. A taxi to town is about $10. Getting one to get you home without getting ripped off is a bit trickier. Order one from the hotel or from a restaurant if you can and agree the price first. There is an excellent souvenir shop nearby. The rooms are spacious. The breakfast room is cosy and has a nice ambiance and a decent breakfast choice. We had dinner there but it was expensive for what you got - good home cooking really. Lamb is generally expensive in Russia and their meat cannot compare to a place like Australia - I recommend dishes like borscht, beef stroganoff and dumplings which are better priced and Russian dishes. We had the Mexican room which we liked. We were not allowed our wine into the dining area as suggested by another Tripadvisor guest. Romeos is a nearby Italian restaurant which is okay if you are looking for somewhere different else close to eat. My best eating experience was the Russian Empire. If you want to walk out of your hotel and be in the main action of Saint Petersburg this is not the place for you - if you like a boutique quieter experience a little distance away then this is a good choice.

author: waiyee1
title: Friendly and stylish
text: When we met up with our guide, she asked who booked the hotel. Then proceeded to shake my hand to congratulate me on a good choice. We started to suspect that is the case as this is a serious Russian teacher of 3 generations from St Petersburg. The hotel is small (20 room), part of the Small Luxury Hotels group, situated in a converted old "house" in a quiet, but relative central part of town. You will need either public (a bus then metro) or private transport to go to the main tourist points. It is right where 3 canals converge, lending it a calm and typical St Petersburg feel. The hotel was well furnished, each room having a "theme" in accordance to its name. Ours was Copenhagen so furnishing was Scandinavian in style while my sister's is Nairobi hence decked out in a wooden 4 poster bed. Compared to a formulaic big hotel, service may seem a bit disorganised but the staff are all very friendly and willing to go out of their way to help. We have a 7 year old and they quickly pointed out which of the two rooms would be more suitable for an extra bed - which was nicely set up when we returned from dinner - with no extra charge. Our requests for drinks to be served in the living room, dinner at a relative late hour and an early morning departure (4:45) were all met with a smile. In addition we were asked if we wanted sandwiches for our morning departure. Nice touch which became even more impressive when we discovered that they were all freshly toasted with two different fillings for choice. We like small hotels for their characters and personal touch. This might not impress those who expect everything to be visible and work on rails, but we found everything we needed just as we need them or ask for them. Staff was very discrete - sometimes we actually felt as if we were staying in someone's house - albeit a large one with a team of trained staff. One still likes to keep the illusion that we are invited house guests, and not tourists.

author: John1450
title: Decent enough hotel let down by service
text: The hotel is comfortable enough, quiet comfortable rooms of a reasonable size. Unfortunately the hotel is badly let down by front of house service : 1/ We were in St. Petersburg for five days. The breakfast menu became boring and repetitive by day three. The breakfast offering does not change and is not very interesting (tinned fruit, industrial pastries). 2/ The food at the restaurant is ok, but again the menu never changes. We only ate there twice, but if the menu was more interesting and changed then we might have eaten there more. 3/ The service is very, very, slow. Simple drinks ordered from the bar take an eternity to arrive (20 minutes for lemonade and a glass of wine ! ), even though the hotel was not busy. 4/ The staff seem to change daily, no consistency. 5/ Arrived at the airport, had pre-booked a car through the hotel.... nobody at the airport. After numerous phone calls to the hotel we ended up having to take a taxi and get it refunded by the hotel. 6/ Arranged some taxis through the hotel. On both occasions the price was agreed in advance with the hotel. But the taxi driver insisted on wanting to charge us more money than was agreed.

author: karlkkm94
title: Unsatisfactory stay at this hotel
text: We stayed at this hotel during our trip to Russia. We chose the hotel based upon reviews. Unfortunately our experience was less that satisfactory. First of all the hotel is located out of the way, it is a good 45 minute walk to the main street Nevskiy Prospekt. The day we checked in we were assigned a room on the main level overlooking the garden. The room was recently painted. From the smell of the paint it was likely in the past 2-4 days. The smell of oil base paint was unbearable and we requested a change of room which could not be accommodated till next day. Next we were assigned Koyoto room which probably is no more that the width of a double bed. One has to climb the bed from foot end. Needless to say that it was quite cramped. The staff also forgot to transfer the welcome fruit basket to the next room. We had some issue with our visa and I was appalled to know that hotel knew of the requirement but did not proactively helped prior to our stay i.e. at the time of reservation. The friendliness of staff was patchy. Even tough we did not find any major cleansiness issue, the place felt more like being in a cottage in the back woods. Some of the earlier posts in fact stated that the Koyoto room was spacious !! They must be in a different room than our Koyoto room!! Yes the breakfast was plenty with a lot of choice.

author: KristinaGar
title: The best boutique hotel in St.Petersburg
text: What I liked: Staff was so nice,attentive and helpful. Check in and out was fast and easy, no waitings. No deposits at check in. Room (Mallorca) was very nice, cute and comfy. It was on the first floor with the views into the garden, where the outside terrace are in summer times. Might be in summer time there not much privicy, cuz out the window are tables of the restaurant's terrace. But during winter time it's perfect. But anyway the room was great. Fast wi fi for free, complimentery 2 bottles of water, complimentery small champagne and small chocolates for wamans day (8 of march) Breacfasts are great, lots of choices. For such a small hotel it's a really suprise! Location near the water, with the views to the canal from some rooms, with the nice promenade , especially in summer time. For about 10-15 min walk city center. Finally, we really liked the place. No complains. Definitelly stay there again when we'll be in St.Petersburg again. What I disliked: Nothing really.

author: lauralovesit
title: Homely, superb staff, historic building
text: This is a lovely hotel set on the banks of one of St Petersburg's famous canals. It has been sympathetically restored into a boutique hotel with a moderate number of rooms, cosy dining room, living room and library where all guests are welcome to relax. It's a little out of the way for the main sights of the city and slightly bizarrely located in amongst a host of construction/renovation projects (surely a sign that the area is rapidly gentrifying), but the Mariinsky Theatre and Holy Trinity Cathedrals are within easy striking distance. The service sets it apart from the rest of the city (in part because the surly Russian service in most places takes some getting used to!) and the staff are genuinely helpful. I had issues with my visa the first time I tried to get to St Petersburg and they were very understanding in issuing a voucher and assisting on numerous occasions with a rebooking. The breakfast is hearty, generous and delicious. The rooms themselves are large and comfortable with good-pressured, hot showers, toiletries and large towels. The beds are wonderfully comfortable and we slept soundly. In fact our room (Copenhagen) was more of a suite than a room, with dressing area, study area, sofa, and separate bathroom. The decor, however, is not quite what you'd expect of one of the city's premier boutique hotels. Although impeccably clean and maintained, stepping into our room felt almost like stepping into the guest bedroom at your (albeit wealthy) aunt and uncle's house... who last decorated in the 90s. It just looks a bit dated. The relief wallpaper needs updating and you'd really expect a flat-screen TV in an expensive hotel these days. The wifi doesn't work in all of the rooms and not even always in common areas. Again, a hotel of this calibre should really have boosters so you can access the net from the comfort of your room. I'm fussy, I know, but there are just a few small aspects holding Alexander House from receiving the full force of my praises. The service is spot on, the breakfast is excellent; sort the wifi and refresh the rooms and you have a world-class boutique property. I would definitely recommend it.

author: travjourno
title: Excellent hotel, great staff, superb kitchen
text: The staff were helpful before we even arrived; they helped organise our visa invitation and book various restaurants, as well as a very reasonable airport transfer. We arrived and the staff were just as friendly in person. The hotel is about a 15-minute walk from Sennaya/Sadovaya metro station so bear that in mind when booking, if you'd rather be nearer the Hermitage/Nevsky Prospekt, think about an alternative. Though from Sennaya/Sadovya you are only one, or a few stops away from all the sights. The hotel restaurant is open 24 hours' a day and we chose to eat there on our first night. It lived up to the hype on here. Good quality and traditional. I was surprised that there was so much variety on the menu. My boyfriend had stroganoff and it was very good. I had a stuffed pepper with rice and meat, again it was very good. Our room (Helsinki) was large with a comfortable bed, clean linens, sofa, TV, more than adequate bathroom and number of bottles of shampoo, shower gel etc. There were robes and slippers for those that want them. We booked through Small Luxury Hotels of the World - so that's the sort of level of hospitality we were expecting. The hotel certainly delivered.There's a lovely library and lounge area. Staff will even make you up a fire on a cold day which is a lovely treat. There's not much way in terms of noise at night so we slept well. I'd not hesitate to recommend this hotel. There's no lift and two flights (of small stairs) - though they helped carry out luggage but worth bearing in mind if you have limited mobility. There is a good restaurant called Karavan nearby. It serves Uzbeki, Azerbaijani and Georgian cuisine.

author: SidraE
title: A Haven in Saint Petersburg
text: Not only was the Alexander House the single most important fact of our trip to St. Petersburg (February 13-19, 2012), but it would be the single most important reason for returning to St. Petersburg. The city, which is so fascinating and diverse, is also, like most of Russia, very unwelcoming to tourists from the West who do not speak Russian. To be illiterate in the Cyrillic alphabet means that a tourist can’t make out the word for ‘restaurant’ even if it is transliterated from French or English. The same is true of the wall texts in most of the museums and other public spaces, though one can arrange for personal guides to such places and a number of them have audio guides in English and other languages. The Alexander House would have been a haven in any other part of the world, but in St. Petersburg, especially in the frozen month of February, it becomes a refuge and an absolutely necessary intermediary to the environs. The accommodations are splendid, as good as any of the most indulgent hotels in the world, but there is something else: a kind of personal attention to very individual needs that doesn’t usually coincide with way-stations that are, by their nature, impersonal. There are fireplaces in the restaurant, which is available 24/7 for dining, and also in the warm library, and these are lit for the asking. No request is too great for the dedicated staff. The art on the walls and in every nook and cranny reminds one of the sumptuous conditions in which the czars and the Russian aristocracy lived for centuries, but with a democratic flavor. The rooms are appointed with an eye to artistic and geographical integrity—representing various cities in the world—but not at the expense of comfort. From planning your journeys to ordering taxis and making sure the drivers don’t gouge the tourists-- to tailoring your accommodations to all your needs, the Alexander House is at the top of my list of recommended boutique hotels of the world. A word of caution: one can get addicted to herring and vodka in front of the fire on a cold St. Petersburg night! Sidra Ezrahi and Bernard Avishai

author: travelourNyc
title: Escape to Shape Goes to Russia
text: This was beyond my expectations. It was a dream vacation. I had never been to Russia before and I was a wee bit nervous. But, let me tell you-it was beyond belief. This hotel was so clean, so interesting, so well staffed. The trip was filled with so many surprises. Arriving there in the early afternoon, we had lunch and then a Russian sauna with eucalyptus leaves brushed all over your body for at least 15 minutes. This was in the hotel! So invigorating. We had a fun-filled week ahead of us. Did almost everything there was to offer. Saw almost all of the sights. Learned a bit of Russian. Had great food. The owners of Escape to Shape are flawless! Erica is like this travel goddess who is so calm, beautiful, organized and accommodating. Her partner, Francesco, is a dream come true. He would almost tuck you in at night and gently wake you up in the morning, if need be. I felt so taken care of. I would go back in a second.

author: brish
title: A real gem!
text: I don't know why this hotel has been re-catagorized - it really is a proper hotel - albeit with only 14 rooms and 2 suites. It has a bar and a restaurant which is open until 1am in the morning. Very useful when you have been to the Mariinsky and want something to eat before or after. We were delighted with the small garden patio area - with private seating areas where guests can just relax or have a meal served. We had the St Petersburg room which is enormous with a small lobby and large shower-room - more like a suite - with a good sized lounge area - all for about £130 per night including breakfast and in the middle of the White Night season. The service was outstanding in every way. In addition there was a lovely lounge area and on the top floor a library. The whole place was extremely tasteful with exposed brick walls and high ceilings. The drawback for us - we are in our 70's - was that it is a good mile and a quarter from Nevsky Prospect - about a 45 minute walk. However, rather than get a taxi via the hotel - about 300 Rubs. we would walk up to the bridge and get a mini-bus, the 212, which runs fairly frequently and goes to Nevsky. The cost was 12 Rubs. or alternatively we went native and waited until a passing car stopped and asked us whether we wanted a lift. We only took a car that had a lone drive - it always worked beautifully and cost us 100 Rubs (about £2). The immediate area is a little bit run down but great if you are going to the Mariinsky - less than a10 minute walk - but once you get inside it is so peaceful and feels like an oasis after a day of sightseeing. We met many other tourists and not one of them was as satisfied with their hotels - from 5* down to a basic B&B. We would certainly return - perhaps next time in the Winter, when the tourists sights are not so frenetic - and swap the garden for the joy of an open fires in the hotel.

author: mool
title: Great value for money, classy, a bit away from Nevskiy, but not too far either
text: I have stayed there twice in two consecute years. It's a great hotel which feels like a home. The staff is polite and courteous and speaks good English. Restaurant is ok, more sea food choices. Breakfast is included in price. Breakfast is standard. But maybe I expected more. The only trouble with this place is its distance from Nevskiy. If I were the owner, I'd offer a courtey shuttle a few times a day. They have cars for rent which are lower cost than other hotels. I rented the car once and it was very reasonable. Rooms are exquisite and unique. While wi-fi is not free, a ethernet cable connect was. This is not a criticism of this hotel but the staff in Russian hotels always seems a bit tense to me, and don't offer chit-chat and make hotel guest feel a bit at easy. Just my opinion maybe, but I always find the staff stressed in comparison to western countries.... I recommend this hotel if you don't feel you need to be near Nevskiy Prospect two three times a day..

author: Adventurer803149
title: Just perfect
text: I stayed in Alexander House for three nights at the end of August. I booked it through hotel’s web-site; next day they confirmed the reservation and arranged a transfer from the airport. My room (St. Petersburg room) in reality appeared even better than on the hotel’s web-site pictures. It is light, spacious, with lovely furniture and good sized wardrobe. The bathroom is huge, although with no bath tube. Room’s and hotel décor is outstanding, the owners considered all little details. Breakfast is included into rooms’ rate and you should not miss it. They serve freshly brewed coffee, home made pastries (there are only two types but they are delicious), pancakes with caviar/sour cream, sausages, fried bacon, eggs, etc. Their little garden is something special – a perfect place for morning coffee and newspaper. Staff is helpful and friendly and their attitude makes you feel at your best friend’s house. Reception may help you in arranging sightseeing tours and general advice about the city. The hotel is located on the channel’s bank and surrounded by nice historical buildings; the street is quiet with almost no cars. It is a bit far from the tourist attractions - about 40 minutes walk to Hermitage but only 10 minutes from Mariinsky Theatre. I was surprised that they charge for WiFi because their web-site was advertising that WiFi is included into the room rate. Anyway, it was only one minus, which could not spoil the overall impression about that beautiful hotel.

author: iheartvegan
title: Charming place, charming staff
text: We got a massive corner room with a huge ceiling which was lovely. Lots of space to spread out! Views over the snowy courtyard are nice. You can adjust the heating accordingly by turning the radiators off or down and opening windows. Lovely thick curtains as well. The bed was very very comfy and we never struggled to sleep at all. Yes some of the decor is tired, but honestly we didn’t care. It was so clean and the place felt very comfortable and had a lovely vibe. Shower was lovely and hot too. The sulphur smell takes some getting used to but honestly I found it a novelty bathing in hot spring water! The cold water from the tap is also high quality spring water and very special so don’t buy bottled! The most important thing to note is how amazing the staff are. They might be the friendliest hotel staff we have ever encountered! They are so helpful no matter how busy they are. Always happy to chat and talk so well about their country too, from an honest place. Was an absolute pleasure staying there. Very close to the main shopping street too.

author: StEw115
title: Not up to standard
text: Stayed here for three nights. The hotel is in good location close to relevant places in town. All is walking distance. The check-in was smooth and without issues. If you wish to exchange f/x at the reception they charge 8% commission (?!?). So better rely on your ATM card - which will work very well. The room was small - really small even for Iceland standards. The bed was uncomfortable and the first good sleep I had was the night after we left the Fosshotel. The bathroom was small and of old standard. Amenities were provided. The room was generally clean. Breakfast is included but just about average. Paid about 250 USD - not worth it. I know and accept that Iceland is expensive; but even Hilton is cheaper. Not coming back.

author: Discover563852
title: Horrible room
text: This was our second last stop in Iceland. We had been all over Iceland via the Ring Rd and had stayed in the remotest of Spots. All were four to five stars I had a hard time giving this even a one star rating. We travel quite a lot and have stated in many different city's around the world. We thought that by staying here it would be like the Foss Hotel at Glacier Lagoon that we had stayed in, it was the very opposite of that hotel. This hotel is conveniently located in the downtown area so our expectations were that it was representative of the capital city of Reykjavik. It was not. The room was small cramped when yiu opened the front door it hit the bathroom door. Getting bags in was a challenge. Getting them back out even more so. The bathroom was very small you couldn't swing a cat in there and they had plastic cups, everywhere we had been had glass more environmentaly friendly and not gross to drink out of. The tv was up on the wall to the left side of the bed a horrible angle to watch. The worst was the bed it squeaked and made noise everytime you moved plus the springs were digging into your back we had the worst sleep since getting here and we stayed in an old farmhouse which was amazing. The room itself creaked and cracked all night long and was extremely stuffy. Note to morning staff as we were leaving we noticed that some travellers had put out their do not disturb signs the staff that was cleaning vacated rooms near them was very noisy and oblivious if I had been still asleep I would have been extremely upset at their inconsiderate behaviour. All in all this hotel is a never go back to for us. Dear staff up your standards you represent your capital city and your beautiful country Iceland if they can do this right in the remotest of areas what is your excuse?

author: I453SKkates
title: Great staff and perfect location
text: My friend and I describe ourselves as "2 mean biddies" not in the nasty sense, in the financial sense. We chose this hotel as it was a good price for the location and offered twin beds on the date we wanted (you'd be surprised how hard it can be and as she snores and thrashes around like a beached trout and I'm like a "corpse, it freaks me out" it can impact on our break ) We didn't book transport from the airport as we thought we would get a shuttle or cheap bus, as we usually do. This proved to be wrong as the only busses are Greyline and another local one that name escapes me. They all charge roughly the same about 2600 ISK which is about £16. Upon arrival at the Fosshotel, we were given a room that was a double and a bit dark, to be honest but when I showed our booking confirmed a twin room they called housekeeping and shuffled a room or two and found us a twin on the 2nd floor which was light and bright and looked out over the main road. We didn't book B&B (mean, see) but thinking we would find a cafe or similar for our breakfast. We did, in fact, find a nice cafe at the end of the main road on the right, a fish and chip place but it did breakfasts and lunches as well. We had booked the Northern Lights tour before we went, which was not able to go ahead on both nights due to the weather but we did book The Golden Circle with the hotel, which we did during the Tuesday of our visit. Jorge (please excuse my spelling if incorrect) was so helpful and as he was new to the job, trying hard to to please us and complete the paperwork correctly. Also, my friend woke up with a vile headache on the morning of the trip and he went out of his way to find her some pain killers, which she replaced when we left. You cannot buy paracetamols in the supermarkets only pharmacies btw. We also choose the hotel based on location as well as I have a bad back, so need to be able to get back to my room to rest if necessary, the Fosshotel was only a 10 min walk from the lovely shops and restaurants, so was perfect for me. The rooms were basic but had all we needed plus a kettle, which was great as many don't. The showers are not particularly hot, but plenty of water. Every member of staff we met were so polite and helpful and we would have no regrets in recommending this hotel to anyone, in fact I have already suggested it to my cousin and her husband for their break to Reykjavik next March.

author: TravelerACJ
title: Best Hotel Home Base
text: Fosshotel Raudara is the best home base hotel for staying in Reykjavík! You are a 3 minute walk from the main shopping street Laugavegur, a 5 min walk from the Sundol local pool/bath, and a 10 minute walk to the church. The front desk staff could not be nicer—thank you Valentina, Kolbrun, and Benjamin! They will call you a taxi to anywhere, help you arrange tours and transportation to the airport, answer your questions about the area, and otherwise just make your stay comfortable and nice. The hotel has been recently renovated. We stayed in a beautiful, modern room. When you book, call the hotel and confirm you can get one of the renovated rooms. It is worth the modest extra fee. Excellent shower and bathroom, extremely comfortable beds and bedding, and in-room tea kettle for tea or coffee as well as a fridge. It was perfect for starting and ending days filled with adventures in Iceland. The breakfast is hearty and includes a few traditional US-style foods, but mostly excellent European and Scandinavian-style foods. It was enough that we were not hungry until lunch—a *huge* savings as food here is so expensive. Snacks, beer, wine, and beverages are available in the lobby for purchase, including a full bar that has a happy hour. There is a computer and printer to print tickets for tours and airlines. They offer plenty of maps, coupon books, tour brochures (all free) and post cards and stamps (reasonable) for purchase. I booked this hotel through Bookings.com. The photos there do not do it justice; it is a great property and and even better staff. Feel confident booking here!

author: Bugenhagen1096
title: Simple, clean, comfortable
text: The hotel is located just off of Laugavegur St so the location is great for walking around the commercial area. The light switches were upsides down from what I'm used to (U.S.). There is also a master switch that turns on all the power in the room. Fail to turn that on and you can guess what happens. The refrigerator was on the master switch in my room but the alarm clock was not (there was one switch always on marked 'Refrigerator' that the clock used). I'm guessing the stag got tired of resetting the clocks all the time but it means if you turn off master power your food goes bad. The room was flawless but very simple. Clean and no frills. Small. I slept great there. Be warned that hot water in all Iceland smells slightly of sulfur. You get used to it quick. It can also come out of the tap very hot sometimes so don't just jump into the shower. In Iceland don't expect napkins anywhere, including this hotel. They have them, but you have to look for little bar napkins.

author: abetterfitlife
title: Eek
text: Only reason I stayed at this hotel was because it was booked for me through the "Guide to Iceland." They don't exactly give you a list of potential hotels and what it may be like. Checking in was ok, but once I walked into my room, I kind of got scared. I booked quality accommodations through the GTI and when I walked into the room, this seemed to have a hostel feel/dorm room. There was a single full bed, horrible view and extremely hot room. I was sweating bullets all night. For the most part out of a week that I stayed here in total and ironically the 2 times I checked in, I was put in the same exact room. What are the odds. For the most part, staff was nice, breakfast buffet was blah. Go out and get a real meal at a nearby restaurant. Unfortunately when I checked back in the 2nd time, not only did the room smell like a septic tank, reeked of marijuana and I found pubic hair in random spots of my bed, making me think, if the sheets were ever changed and therefore my low rating. I did not say anything to housekeeping or front desk because by the time I checked back in, I was only there for 2 nights and couldn't wait to get home as I was exhausted from my vacation. I just cleaned what I saw and tried not to think about it and slept on top of the covers. Females- they have a cheap in wall dryer which all its good for is give your hands 2nd degree burns. I asked if they had a handheld pistol and they told me they did not. I explained how it didn't do the job I needed it to do and burned me, told me they would send maintenance to check it (this was when I checked in first time). When I checked in 2nd time and put me in same room, it still did the same lousy job. In other words ladies, bring a blow dryer.

author: RonP967
title: UNRELIABLE
text: I've given the hotel a poor rating for one reason only. My wife and I needed to be at the airport by 06:00 on the morning of 03 February 2018 and asked for an alarm call to our room for 04:00. I watched the receptionist write this in the diary, My request was top of an otherwise blank page. I also asked that a taxi be booked for 05:00. At 04:45 I woke naturally, there had not been an alarm call. My wife and I quickly dressed and went to reception, our taxi was waiting for us, the driver was standing in reception with a "complimentary" cup of coffee. All I got from the receptionist was "I forgot". Ha!! the diary was still in the drawer behind him. Two "if's", 1. If I had not pre ordered the taxi and, 2. If I had not woken naturally my wife and I would have missed our flight. This event spoilt an otherwise decent stay at a pleasant hotel. Be Warned. Do NOT rely on pre booked alarm calls from this hotel.

author: GaryR2312
title: A friendly hotel
text: Arrived on a raining Friday night, 40 of us arrived at the same , we were all booked in within 10 minutes, great staff at reception. We had room 212 which had twin beds for me and my teenage daughter, the room was tiny. It faced onto the main road . The windows weren’t double glazed so the traffic kept us awake practically all night! The following morning (still half asleep) I asked for another room not facing the road, within 15 minutes we were given 217 room which was much quieter & spacious. The shower compartment is tiny even for a slim person like me! If you get 412 room you are very lucky as far as I’m concerned. Cold tap water is fine to drink just let it run for a while until the eggy smell goes. Beds were comfy. Breakfast; fantastic assortment whilst we stayed there for 3 nights, the juices weren’t very tasteful some mornings. The staff were quick to clear tables and replenish food. Location of hotel is brilliant, 15 -20 minutes walk to Perlan,10-15 to the church. 15-20 to Sun Voyager landmark. Overall a great hotel that’s only rated 3⭐️⭐️⭐️. The staff were friendly & very helpful.

author: SanjayRJain
title: OK hotel and OK Rooms, Staff partly good
text: We stayed in this hotel from October 31 to November 1 and again from November 6th to November 9th. This hotel is far away from the Keflavik International airport ( about 50 Kms distance). So I am not sure, what is at the outskirts, the airport or the hotel? There are many varieties of Standard rooms. Though everyone pays the same price for a Standard Rooms but you got to be very lucky to get a good room. Same Standard room could be 100 Sq ft or 150 or 200 sq ft depending on your luck ( Excluding the bathroom area). The bathroom could be 25 sq ft to 100 sq ft depending on your luck. Breakfast is good enough. However the bar section is right at the reception. This gives the feeling that it is more like a boutique hotel. very compact. Front office has a mix of staff. Most of them are very sweet and helpful. Very polite and courteous. However their manager is different. If someone is looking for a budget hotel then this hotel is Ok otherwise there are many other luxury hotels close by as well.

author: P6301PHcharlesk
title: Disappointing
text: ***Visited here last November... The hotel room itself was nothing like the photos, being dated, plain and dismal.*** We were instructed via email to pay in euros cash for our room, which we brought with us, but when it came to checking in and paying for our room, we were told that this was incorrect and were told we would have to pay the full price by card, despite this complete blunder, the reception staff were helpful in booking us a last minute northern light excursion. The reception area seemed nice, with a small bar area a small fridge with sandwiches and drinks... Though already prepared to pay Icelandic prices, was not expecting to pay almost £9 for a canteen standard sandwich and a bottle of drink. As expected the water in Iceland is sulphurous, but the bathroom had a funny smell which beyond that, hit you every time you opened the bathroom door. The room was maintained, replenished and cleaned everyday. Despite the dullness of the room, it was clean. Breakfast was included in our stay... Which was a good point to our stay. It was hot and fresh, a buffet with wide selection of fruits, continental, cooked foods and hot and cold drinks. My partner had stayed at another Fosshotel down the road, and was impressed with the standards there, but was disappointed to see the contrast in ascetic between the two hotel rooms. Within certain seasons in Iceland, daylight is a sort after thing. You'd think the rooms would be bright and inviting, to compensate for this. Between the excursions and eating out at local restaurants, I found myself sleeping a lot in our room. It's dark interior left me feeling tired and lethargic. The little black boxed TV was only good for about two channels before waves of static would eventually take over the screen and render it useless. For the price we paid for the room, we expected something a lot nicer. I'd stay at a Fosshotel again, just not this one.

author: Beerwolf2014
title: Basic three star hotel
text: The location of the hotel, in a residential area, is only a short walk from Hallgrimskirkja and the main streets with bars and restaurants. We stayed for 5 nights and, after the initial surprise of the soulless room with its challenging spiral staircase leading to a mezzanine bed area, and the constant unpleasant smell of sulphur from the hot water tap, we soon acclimatized to its quirks. A few cheerful cushions and throws would make the room more homely until the management completes the hotel refurbishment. Although very dated, the room (see hotel photos room 429) and bathroom were clean. The thin plastic tea/coffee cups were very poor – surely they could stretch to “proper” crockery. The bed was comfortable but, although there was a bedside table on one side, there was nothing on the other which meant placing personal items on the floor. The breakfasts were adequate but not great. Consisting of cereals, continental style meat and cheese, some pastries, rollmops (for those with Icelandic tastes!) and basic cooked breakfast of baked beans, small frankfurter sausages and rubbery scrambled egg. However, there was plenty to eat and the bread was delicious! The hotel only uses the restaurant for breakfasts and the reception/bar area is very small which makes it rather crowded at busy times. It would be an improvement if the restaurant was utilised as a bar and lounge area as well. We found the staff pleasant, friendly and ready to assist, even at their busiest times. They were most helpful and informative with tour bookings. We were there during the heavy snowfall (51 cm) when some of the tours – particularly the Northern Light trips – were cancelled and had to be rearranged. Iceland is a wonderful country with spectacular scenery and delightful people. We loved Reykjavik and hope to return one day but would choose somewhere else to stay.

author: elmapp
title: Poor service
text: When we arrived and went up to the desk the 2 women on reception were quite off and not welcoming at all. We had 2 rooms booked; a double and a triple. The double was on floor 2 and the triple on floor 3. We weren't told where the breakfast bar was or how to even get to our rooms we were just given the key. Found the lift and went up to our room to discover just 2 beds and a sofa which we assumed must have been a sofa bed. They hadn't made it up for us so we went to ring reception to find we didn't even have a phone. We made it up ourselves and to our horror discovered blood on the mattress and the thinnest most ripped mattress topper ever. It looked like a float you use at a swimming pool. There wasn't even any sheets or covers for the sofa bed. We went downstairs to complain and we were told they would come and make the bed up for us.
