However we did not want to sleep on a blood stained mattress, therefore my sister had to stay in her own room on floor 3 that night but only for that night as it was booked in for the next day. It was a really bad start to our holiday. The hotel itself was okay but we found the staff extremely rude and unhelpful. On our last day when waiting for our pick up another man checked in and the man behind reception had failed to tell him how to get to his room which was through the breakfast place and on the other side! The staff just seemed to assume we would know our way around the hotel and were less than helpful. As we left we didn't even get a goodbye or a thank you from the reception man which we thought incredibly rude as we had stayed there for 3 nights! Would never stay here again.

author: Cazzan
title: Hotel in good location
text: We stayed here for 4 nights during a recent trip to Iceland. The hotel was nice, and adequate. We had 3 rooms between 9 people but were spread out on different floors and at different ends of the building! My room was the one with a spiral staircase which was very nice and spacious for 3 people. In fact all our rooms were spacious and totally fine for what we wanted. The rooms were also hot! We had to turn the radiator off. The bathroom shower did smell, but we were expecting that. The cold tap water however also smelt and tasted of sulphur!! After 2 days of drinking 'eggy' water I discovered one of our other rooms tap water was lovely! Breakfast was continental style with hot food of beans, mini sausages and scrambled egg. It was kept well topped up. The breakfast room never seemed busy either, even though it was fairly small. The reception area could have been bigger as it was very crowded when there were people waiting for a tour coach pick-up, plus people arriving with luggage. This area also doubled as a lounge/bar and I think it might have been good to have a separate bar area. Location of the hotel was perfect. Only a 5-10 minute walk and you were at the waterfront which had beautiful views of the mountains, and a 5 minute walk into the main street for shops and restaurants. All in all, a good hotel and I'd stay here again.

author: Wienprater
title: Fosshotel Raudara - request for newly renovated rooms
text: We chose this hotel as a base for 2 nights. It used to be called Best Western Reykjavik. Not directly in the city centre but we could walk to the main shopping street in just 5 minutes and Hallgrims church in around 10-15 minutes. We read from reviews that the hotel had recently renovated some rooms. Upon request, we were given one of the newly renovated rooms located on the ground floor. Understand that only a handful of rooms were renovated. I must say that our room was considered huge with a large walk-in area, a bedroom and a huge bathroom. Bed was very comfortable, there's also a mini frige and safe box in our room. The bathroom had both bath tub and a separate shower area. Eventhough our room was near the breakfast area, the soundproof was good and we hardly heard any noise at all. Frontdesk staff were friendly and helpful. Breakfast was nice. Lots of complimentary parking space inside the hotel indoor carpark. Only thing is that you will need to request the front desk staff to open the carpark shutter entrance for you when you drive your car in and out of the carpark. Wifi signal was on & off in our room. We had to go to the breakfast area or near to the lobby where the signal was much better. This hotel was one of the pickup locations when we joined the Northern Lights Tour with Reykjavik Excursions so it was very convenient. Overall we enjoyed our stay at Fosshotel Raudara and would definitely return again. Tip : Ask for the newly renovated rooms.

author: LaurenN912
title: Old and tatty rooms, good location
text: A friend and I stayed at Fosshotel Raudara for 3 nights in December. We chose this hotel because of the good location and relatively cheap price. Upon arrival, our room was already ready which was good however the receptionist didn't show us a map and explain where we were/wifi details etc. We had to ask for this which was a bit disappointing. We went to our room on the second floor and found that our room was one that hadn't been refurbished yet. The room was average size, could have been slightly bigger but had a lovely big window which was nice. That is about the only positive about the room unfortunately. The bedding was unclean and there seemed to be some sort of blood stain on the actual duvet which they had just tried to cover with a duvet cover. There was also black hair on my friend's bed - we are both blonde. The bathroom was also disappointing as there was a bad leak from the sink - the housekeeping were obviously aware of this as they had placed a towel on the floor to soak up the water. After a while a puddle had formed on the floor which was unsafe and not really acceptable. I don't really see the point of having a massive television in the room when there are no useful channels - for example one english news channel maybe. The breakfast was a standard hotel breakfast buffet which was average - we mainly ate the croissants. Overall, this hotel is fine if you are planning on just using it for a place to wash and sleep. We did not spend much time here so it was a good base as it is in a good location. We may have had a bad experience as our room was one that hadn't been refurbished yet - but I think a leak in the bathroom and bad housekeeping is avoidable so this was a shame.

author: Samwhiplash
title: Very dated, very basic but a good bed & good location
text: We stayed in Room 203 which is on the ground floor despite getting the lift up one floor. Decor very dated, probably from the early 1990's. Room small but clean. Bathroom tiny but functional. Very comfortable bed. No iron or ironing board. Tv to side of bed instead of at end of bed. The safe worked well. Whole hotel was REALLY hot - we had no heating on in our bedroom & with the window open it was still hot (while 8 degrees outside). Avoid the juice - it's some kind of massively watery cordial. The coffee machine and toaster weren't working on our first morning. There were never enough bowls/plates - ppl were always waiting for these to be replenished. Fruit, pastries, breads all good. Enough to fill up on but definitely a LOT of room for improvement! The area to sit in the lobby does not make for a comfortable place to relax with a drink with friends. Location was great though- just off the Main Street. If your happy with dated but clean & basic then you will be happy here.

author: Allyalexmch
title: Perfect for our needs
text: A great stay in the very lovely room 317. So many windows!! Very large by European standards. The bathroom was smaller with a shower stall but did the trick. Comfy queen size bed. Very quiet room. Didn't hear neighbours at all on our stay. The breakfast was awesome and saved lots of money not having to go out. Lots of options for every taste. Every staff interaction from front desk to housekeeping and breakfast room staff was positive and friendly. They are doing something right at this hotel! The only thing I thought could be improved was newer pillows. We could walk everywhere we wanted in the city centre. Thanks for a great stay! We will stay again next time we are there and will recommend to everyone!

author: G1846ISmaxg
title: Spartan and overrated
text: After a recent stay of 3 nights at the Best Western Hotel Reykjavik, I strongly recommend staying elsewhere. A short list of the most serious drawbacks: (1) The rooms are so small that when you book a room with two beds, what you get is a room designed for a queen or king sized bed with two twin beds positioned adjacent to one another. You may as well be sleeping in the same bed as your roommate - which can be seriously awkward, suffice to say. (2) There is no room in the bathroom for a tub, and the shower enclosure - which doesn't even appear to be secured to the bathroom floor - is a flimsy plastic contraption that looks and feels like a shrunken telephone booth. The end result is a shower experience that is absolutely claustrophobic You won't want to linger in this shower. (3) The complimentary wifi is so weak that it's impossible to get usable signal in your room. This forces people to congregate in the lobby or stairwells to get internet access. (4) The room I was given didn't have a television or a telephone. I can forgive the lack of a telephone in this age of mobile phones, but a hotel that lacks televisions in all of its rooms is automatically deserving of a 1-start rating. No effort was made to cover the conspicuous holes in the wall where a television had been mounted at some point in the past. (5) The hotel has as an adjacent parking garage, but access is controlled through an industrial type overhead door that must be activated from the front desk. Thus, to get in or out of the parking garage guests are forced to pull up to the overhead door, and and then walk to the lobby to ask someone to activate the door so you can get in or out. Definitely not a convenient arrangement. On the positive side, the hotel's front desk staff all spoke respectable English, and were genuinely helpful in terms of directions, activities, and nearby restaurants. Overall, the Best Western Hotel Reykjavik is a 1-star hotel. While it has a stylish lobby, the rooms are cramped, poorly appointed, with wifi that is functional only in the common areas. For the money, there are better accommodations to be found in Reykjavik.

author: PDWood79
title: Some really great features for an average hotel.
text: Reykjavik is a small capital city but has everything among the ever changing sky line. There for old and new mix for the mean time. The Best Western has a great location and is not far from the city center with plenty of shops along the way. The lobby is new and modern with a great staff at the front desk. The breakfast is continental with a few extras that make it as hardy as you want it to be; it is more then acceptable. You can tell it is a slightly older building by the size of the elevator and the condition of the rooms. They are very clean and the house keeping staff keep it that way. The rooms are laid out well but mine was showing wear in the carpet and wallpaper. On TV was flat screen and the other was still a CRT TV (old style). Your TV choices are very limited here as well. Would I come back here? Yes! It is a 3 star hotel so bound to have a few miner issues. The things I mentioned don't really bother me just pointing things out for the review. The whole staff are great and helpful and friendly as most of the Icelander are. Enjoy the location and Reykjavik!

author: roytan1947
title: Basic hotel
text: We were here for 3 nights. This hotel is a neighborhood that is about 3 blocks from the Main Street. You cannot compare these hotels to American hotels. The room was a nice size. The bathroom was small. The hairdryer was labeled "basic" and it certainly was. When I went to dry my hair the top popped off and the air hose was flying all over. It is mounted on a wall. It certainly was different. We had to go buy 2 electrical converters so we could charge our IPads. Then you had to crawl under a desk and nightstand to plug them in the outlets. Breakfast was an Icelandic breakfast with meats, cheeses, herring, eggs and bread. The bread was very good. In America when you return to a hotel after a day's outing and the clerk is there, they usually greet you and welcome you back. Do. Ot expect this in Iceland. People are very quiet and usually don't say anything unless asked. We found this with the receptionist's in the hotels and bus drivers. All in all, it was a place to sleep and served it's purpose.

author: Turk_H
title: Very good/Great staff
text: The staff is wonderful-especially Mr. Bradley Cooper look a like :). Seriously, everyone was very nice and helpful. The bar is right in the lobby and is super small-like the size of a counter with a couple of chairs. The lobby is small. Who cares--you don't stay in the lobby. The breakfast area is nice and the breakfast was good. American free breakfast is so lacking compared to other countries! I had a single room for a couple nights. Very small room with super small bathroom. Shower was like a camp shower to me. Moved to a larger room which was much better. The location was a few blocks up from the main shopping street and the bus terminal. I was happy here-rooms and hotel were very clean. I didn't spend that much time in my room. I was in Iceland!! :) I'd stay here again..it wasn't fabulous, but it is a good hotel.

author: Natwill27
title: Good base for our Iceland trip
text: This hotel was booked by my boyfriend as part of a surprise holiday for us and therefore had no idea/expectations as to where we might be staying. When we arrived at the reception (which also doubles as the hotel bar) the hotel receptionist was very friendly and helpful and by chance our room was ready for us to check into, even though it was before the stated 2pm check in time. Room facilities were perfectly fine for us, nice big bed, bathroom was a bit on the tight side but manageable for the four days we were there and plenty of toiletries and tea/coffee making facilities that were restocked daily. We did find that there was a problem with the wi-fi in the room when we checked in but this was due to them upgrading the connection. After this had been done it was fine for the rest of our stay. Breakfast area is a lot more modern decoration wise than the rest of the hotel and it may be that they gradually update the rest of the hotel in the near future. Plenty of space, even at fairly busy times. Lots of pastries, bread, meat and cheeses along with yoghurt and cereals. There was a hot section containing eggs, sausages and beans but we found that this was often fairly lukewarm or cold so maybe they could look at how they keep the breakfast warm for improvement. Hotel staff were very friendly and helpful, we used the reception to book our bus back to the airport and to check on the aurora forecast every day to help us decide whether or not to book a trip. Location wise- the hotel is at the far end of the main shopping street, and i would estimate that it is a good ten minute walk from the hotel to the area of the main shops/restaurants. We walked to the harbour one night and that took us about 20 minutes at a leisurely pace. So fairly close but not right in the middle of town. I imagine the secure car park at the hotel is a massive draw for those that are renting vehicles to drive around Iceland. I would stay here again and recommend to friends as a good place to base yourself whilst in iceland.

author: 172peggym
title: Perfect Location, Wonderful Hotel
text: First off, we'd definitely go back to this place. We were very tired, and knew arriving at 7 am that our room would not be ready. But the desk staff were lovely, directed us to some local coffee shops that had nice breakfast rolls and bagel sandwiches, and then somehow managed to get us in our rooms by noon (check-in time not being until 2 pm). Our room was in a newly renovated area, that they were just finishing up, so the only downside was to get really good wifi we had to go to the lobby. BUT the wifi in the lobby was both free and good. Breakfast was included, and it was also very good – eggs, meats, cheeses, veggies and good bread, and really great coffee – even latte! YES. Beds were comfortable, and we’re pretty picky. Pillows were also good. And service was fine or better than fine – nice products, and the room was kept quite clean. We liked the décor, and the staff were pleasant. They hook you up with the major tours, and you can be picked up at the hotel for hot springs, grand circle of the island tours, Northern lights tours, etc. The location is probably the best part (although the comfort is not to be minimized). Armed with maps we probably would not have even needed, we headed out each day to see the city. Turn right out of the hotel, the left on Laudevegar and you’re in the heart of the shops and restaurants. Just down from that (we discovered, looking to our right) is the harbor, and on a clear day you can see the mountains/glaciers and it’s incredible. We walked along the harbor, took pictures of everything, enjoyed finding the church which is a city landmark when we headed “inland”, and found myriad coffee shops and places with wonderful fish stews, amazing vegetables, and little groceries where we could buy fantastic cheeses and amazing dark chocolate as good as anything Europe has to offer. Yes, food is expensive but we were very impressed that it was so good! Both in groceries and in restaurants. We will definitely go back, and we will likely stay at this same hotel as we really loved it, and it’s hard to imagine a better location unless you have a very high end room overlooking the harbor.

author: Amolta
title: Dated hotel, OK for one night, but ultimately, book elsewhere
text: We were pretty disappointed in this hotel. We paid extra for a 'superior' room, and when we arrived it looked EXACTLY the same as the standard room advertised on booking.com. We went down to mention and they assured me it was a 'deluxe'. I had requested a double bed through the booking process and this room had two singles pushed together and, again, was EXACTLY THE SAME as the standard one advertised which was cheaper. On principle, I was a bit annoyed as why pay the extra money? They offered us one of the new renovated rooms, but the bed was a large single. Then eventually offered us the Junior Suite. While we took up on this offer, I am not sure we should have. Other than it being a bit unusual and on two floors, this suite is very dated and I would pity anybody who pays extra for it. I hope it's used as a reserve room only nowadays. Bed was rubbish, shower too. Loads of space, but useless space and I couldn't find a hairdryer/iron etc. This Best Western is clearly going through some updating, and it needs it badly. There are plenty of places to stay in the city (we stayed in a newer hotel with smaller rooms but way more comfortable earlier in the week) so I would recommend elsewhere. Pretty shocking they can charge what they do, but it's Reykjavik. There are just plenty of better places on offer. We picked this because of the car parking, and it was fine. Staff were friendly so not complaining about that, but overall, expect a dated budget hotel for not so budget a price. The city has better.

author: Naush187
title: Fit for purpose
text: This hotel was exactly what we needed for our bank holiday trip. We needed a clean room, central to Reykjavik with breakfast. This hotel has a 24 hour reception which is great and needed as we are leaving at 2:45am. They were even kind enough to arrange breakfast earlier than the time stated. This will be a sandwich and a drink. They have a great selection for breakfast. Fresh croissants, cold cuts, cheese, breads, fruit, cereal, milk, coffee/tea machine, fresh juices, yoghurt, sausages, beans and eggs. I'm sure I've missed some more items. Room we got was big, I think as a result of a late checkin. Next door is "Harrys" grill... you must go there (see my review) currently top 20 restaurant here. Lounge has a small bar, snack fridge and nice seating. Receptionist are all very freindly and will help. Walking time to main town 10 minutes. Ooh! Beds are bigger than UK king plus very comfy. Can't fault it for what we needed, it exceeded our expectations. Surrounding the hotel it's a bit of a dump due to graffiti and building work but you get that in this area. Excellent budget hotel.

author: herbf808
title: Good hotel, but right now the area is in transition
text: I liked the hotel premises very much. I now find most rooms for 1 person are smaller then in the U.S. As long as it clean, warm or cold depending on season and the employees are efficient it is good for me for my short visits. I enjoyed the front desk personnel and the maids were efficient. The room very clean and the view I had from the top floor (4th) was nice. The daily breakfast buffet is better then many others I have stayed in. The area: this will be much more exciting in the future. The main street is under construction as well as side streets. When I went to the harbor area it is totally different. Had a great trip, and the employees were pleasaint and mapped the places I wanted to go to. Made it very easy. Mostly everyone I ran into spoke English. They said it is mandatory from 9 ys of age and up to learn it in school. What a great idea. The airport is number one, as well as Icelandic Airlines, and Flybus connection busses were great. This country is not to be missed any time of year. The views and tours were outstanding even though it is March 2016. Next time will try it in summer as it is very different. Warmer then I thought also!

author: cableknit
title: Cozy & great location
text: We stayed at Best Western Hotel Reykjavik for about a week March 2016. It's in a very good location, walking distance to downtown Reykjavik (you're about 1-2 blocks away from the beginning of what I assume is the 'main street' of their old downtown, and steps away from restaurants; also there are shuttle buses that pick you up outside and you are right across the street from a bus station. About 1 km from a major thoroughfare that takes you to their highway system as well!). They have a great breakfast buffet in the morning (from I believe 7 to 10 a.m.) with super attentive staff! They were constantly picking up plates, cleaning tables, restocking food; very, very attentive. You can also ask the hotel to make lunch (we never did) and they have lunch/snacks/drinks available at the hotel bar & refrigerated case when you walk in. They have a gated parking garage which was wonderful since we rented a car and self-drove most of our trip. The only problem is that someone always had to get out of the car and either go into the office or use the call box inside the garage to get out (and when you go into the office, I stood for upwards of 10 minutes while people were chatting with the 'bar' patrons before even being acknowledged, which is disappointing when you're just trying to park your car). The room we rented had 2 twin beds and was nice and warm! My boyfriend is 6'4" so sleeping on a twin was a little challenging but oddly the blanket/comforter they put on the bed is very small. Fortunately (for him) they keep the standard room temp. at around 70-75 degrees at night (I wish that was something we could've adjusted as I don't sleep well in warm rooms but my boyfriend was very happy since his blanket didn't cover more than his chest). We noticed upon arrival that the room hadn't been swept of the prior occupants dirt/dust (has wood/laminate floors) and throughout our visit that remained the case. In general the room was nice. Large wardrobe, has a safe, nice bathroom (a little small but we like small bathrooms so it worked for us).

author: BristolWayne
title: Good location
text: Stayed here for 5 nights the end of Feb. Check in was nice and simple. Staff very helpful. Small bar and a cooler with sandwiches etc. Though at £10 each pretty expensive ! For the money it cost to stay here I was disappointed with the room. It was just ok, I expected a lot more. Room tiny with small bathroom with a shower and a tiny sink. Cleanliness was ok. Best thing about the room was it was lovely and warm. Wifi a bit hit and miss. T.V waste of time, not that we were in Iceland to watch TV. Breakfast was ok. Though the hot selection was cold every day ,So stuck to continental. Tables always dirty had to clean up and stack dishes before I could sit down. If you could find an empty table to start with. Had to wait for clean cups and cutlery most days. To be honest it's pretty chaotic most mornings.Always people waiting for a table unless you get there about 7 am. Close to town though, a five minute walk. Would I stay again, NO

author: 988jand
title: It grows on you
text: From our arrival we were more than a bit disappointed. We arrived quite early as do many flights from the states. They gave us no encouragement for an early check in, nor did they offer us breakfast. Suggested we walk "5 minutes" to a pastry shop. Ok... So we did, in the pitch dark (2 women), more like 15 minutes. We hardly saw anyone out and about until we got close to the pastry shop, but incredibly, we never felt unsafe. Since we were so far from the hotel we decided to keep going and did a lot of sightseeing before finally heading back to the hotel about 4pm. Then we saw the incredibly tiny room. Oh boy. Nothing we could do. Made the best of it. But as the week went on and we got to know the hotel staff, they really were very nice and helpful. Perhaps they could start out that way, first impressions. The room size really didn't matter after awhile and in the end we left with a positive feeling about the hotel. It is more than 5 minutes from city center but walk it, you can justify vacation eating that way If you use Reykjavik excursions, you are at the beginning of their pickup and drop offs, that is good late at night

author: kelse1990
title: Nice rooms but sometimes a long wait at reception.
text: I stayed here for 2 nights. Being an insomniac I always request rooms away from a lift. I received my room card and was disappointed to be given a small room right opposite lift. I went straight back to reception and asked for a room change, this was dealt with very quickly. I was told it was only a single room but it was superior, I accepted. The room was very nice and at the end of the hotel in what was a converted brewery. The bed was much bigger than a single so I was happy until time for bed. Extremely noisy family above thumping back and forth along the floor and not only that it seemed to vibrate after the thumping like someone walking along a wooden floor and a glass cabinet rattling. I am only describing how it sounded to me. I always wear earplugs but the noise was unbearable. The room was very clean and modern and with tea/coffee facilities and comfy bed. After around 1 hours sleep I went back to reception the following morning and explained they were very noisy above and I needed to change rooms. I was told at reception they could do this but it wouldn't be until after 2pm. That was fine with me. I went back but reception is usually very busy with mainly one person on reception and sometimes kept waiting for a long time. I was however given a different room quite a bit later and was very happy to be given a much quieter room with no room above and at end of hotel . It was huge, I had a family room just for me, perhaps above the room that was above me originally. Breakfast was quite good but typical European style. Basic but quite a choice. Mixed feelings overall so probably would not stay here again.

author: 353littleb
title: Good base camp
text: Our party of 6 stayed at the Best Western, which is well located just a short walk from the centre of Reykjavik (although most places are only a short walk from the centre!) in January 2016. First off, we arrived very late at night and the staff accommodated our out of hours check-in without complaint and the look of the reception area/bar was very promising. Free wifi throughout the hotel, though perhaps not with sufficient speed or capacity for the number of users, was also a definite plus, as is the fact that most, if not all, of the major tour providers pick off and drop off at the door. Although we each had a single room at the same rate, we noticed that they varied considerably; some were much larger than others, some had much older/newer bathrooms, some had chillers/fridges while others had nothing. Some, like mine, had a very drafty window and no light switches or working lamps anywhere near the bed. Beds were not luxuriously comfortable, but quite acceptable, especially after busy days of touring the local landscape. All the rooms were clean, although suffered slightly from a lack of doormats or rugs as we constantly came in with snowy boots, however hard we wiped at the front door - I wet my socks in several puddles over the course of my stay! . Breakfast came in the form of a buffet and was varied and plentiful, we were certainly well set up for our days stomping about in the cold. Breakfast room staff were very diligent. My only previous experience of a Best Western (in the UK) was exceptionally good, so I was expecting good things here. In honestly, I was a little disappointed with this hotel. However, we just needed a base during our 4 days in Reykjavik and didn't spend very much time in the hotel, so the facilities at this Best Western were perfectly adequate for our needs. At the equivalent of £77/€100 per night it seemed averagely priced for the area. I wouldn't book up if you're interested in a luxurious stay, but if a no frills base camp is what you're looking for, this is your place.

author: s_awomirt
title: Good location
text: Main pros: 1. Fantastic location 2. Very friendly staff (and it seems most speaks Polish). 3. Clean. 4. WiFi is fast and free. Cons: 1. Breakfast is good. But limited choice. The same every day. 2. Rather old hotel. 3. The room was quite small (single).

author: heidi-ann75
title: Clean and comfortable
text: Stayed 4 nights last week. Ideally situated, close to bars and restaurants. Usually first collect/drop off for tours. Room - clean and comfortable very warm, but you can control by turning down radiator or open window. Bed was large and comfy. Tea/coffee making facilities in the room.free safe and fridge to use if needed. Room cleaned daily. Complimentary toiletries restocked. Free WiFi worked well in our room (last rom on 3rd floor). No trouble with noise. Breakfast - often cold, but very good if hot. Self serve buffet style - eggs, sausages, cod meats and cheese, yoghurt and fruit. Bar- happy hour from 5pm to 7pm each night. There is no restaurant in the hotel, but loads within walking distance. Staff- all were polite, friendly and willing to help. Would use this hotel again.

author: HelenDavis84
title: Very average should be better
text: I didn't stay here for pleasure which may impact my review as I had to come out to Iceland at the last minute as my dad was admitted to hospital. The price I paid was approximately £130 a night which I know by Iceland standards is quite reasonable but I wasn't very impressed. I stayed here for a week which felt like a long time in this hotel. The room was fine. I had a single room on the 4th floor. It was quiet and clean apart from the floor which was filthy and I felt I kept getting grit and stones on my feet as the floor hadn't been cleaned in days. I couldn't get my TV to switch on but due to the staff being pretty unhelpful (see below) then I really couldn't face asking them to fix it. The sheets were very worn and bobbly so not particularly pleasant. The Internet was intermittent and often went off around 9pm at night which I assume was due to volume of users. The staff were very average. I had various problems with my booking, getting taxis to the hospital etc. Considering I was staying here at a stressful time they didn't really provide any support and in fact made my life more difficult. They stated they couldn't help me extend my stay on a Sunday as their office staff didn't work, then as I was always at the hospital I was never able to sort anything as again they only seemed to be able to deal with things between 9-5. This is very odd for a hotel to not be able to help people with things such as extending their stay outside of "working hours". There was often a big queue of people attempting to check out as there only ever seemed to be one person on reception. This was poor. Breakfast was fine. Overall I've stayed in worse places but I expected much better from a Best Western. If you don't need to deal with reception at all during your stay and expect basic conditions then you'll be fine

author: Gershwin12
title: Best Western Hotel Reykjavik
text: We chose this hotel based on the description and positive reviews from my fellow tripadvisor contributors. Thank you again for the great advice! This hotel was a good choice for us on our final night after a three week expedition to the Arctic and Iceland. The quiet, convenient location allowed for a much needed nights rest before the fifty minute drive to the airport and our flight home. Daniel checked us in, he was polite and efficient. Thor the manager made our stay extra special with an upgrade to a beautiful junior suite facing the court yard. We slept well in this quiet, comfortable, clean, double bed room. Oh, a brief description about what a double bed is in Iceland; it is about equivalent to a Queen size bed and there are usually two comforters. One for each sleeper, so no stealing the blankets from your partner! The room had everything we needed, including a refrigerator, hair dryer, iron/board, toiletries, including hair conditioner, coffee maker, tea/coffee, TV and much more. The hot water is that wonderful mineral geothermal water. After bathing I felt so refreshed and surprisingly clean in spite of the sulfur odor of the water. Surprisingly our skin did not retain that odor. We had a short, pleasant walk, just a few blocks away from this residential neighborhood to the heart of the city and visited the intriguing Phallological Museum. A superb restaurant called Resto is just a few steps away from the hotel. We had our dinner at Resto and enjoyed every bite! Breakfast was more than ample and offered both traditional Icelandic and American breakfast items that included; scrabbled and hard boiled eggs, herring (two types), tuna salad, a variety of breads, toast, cheese, salami, cucumber, tomato, yogurt, juices, cottage cheese, fruit and coffee/ tea. Wi-Fi was free and fast. On site parking was secured behind a locked gate and was complimentary. I recommend this hotel and would stay here again when in Iceland.

author: PD_tripadviser
title: Mediocre Western is closer to the truth
text: I was not optimistic about being booked into this place by our tour provider as I have previous experience of this chain, none of it inspiring. This hotel was no exception as once again it did not fail to disappoint. When we presented our voucher there was a lot head-scratching, mouse-clicking and keyboard clattering before the reception staff gave us room cards - this only took about seven minutes!! When we got to "our" room, I opened the door to be confronted with a gentleman with no trousers on. I was fairly embarrassed by this, but he was very welcoming, saying "Yes, please, come in"! We beat a hasty retreat back to the lobby, and were eventually allocated another room. As they had no more double rooms, we were upgraded to a suite "at no extra charge, sir". I mean, seriously, no extra charge because they were overbooked?? The suite turned out to be a split level affair with a sofa-bed downstairs and a double bed on a sort of landing accessed by a steep spiral staircase with a very frayed carpet. My partner was not impressed as the bathroom was downstairs, not a great arrangement if you need a pee in the middle of the night. Fortunately, it is light all night at this time of year, so there was a good chance of not breaking your neck negotiating said spiral staircase in the wee small hours. As it turned out, the flush on the loo was jammed and we had to get onto reception to sort it out. They offered us the key to a single room with an allegedly fully functional toilet, again terrific for late night use! The reception staff were clearly embarrassed, but working for massive hotel chain like this, there was not a lot they could do, and what they could do, they did. My final gripe was that the bath tub was so narrow that it was impossible to have a shower without the flimsy shower curtain sticking to some part of the anatomy.

author: teammakesthedream
title: A Lofty Hotel
text: The Best Western is a small hotel within blocks of the water, great shopping, and nice cozy restaurants. It offered a lot ease and comfort in its well functioning room and great views. Our mini suite with had a spiral staircase to bedroom which was different and unique. Both areas had a cable ready flat panel television sets and a comfortable bed and sleep sofa, To make things just a little sweeter, the suite actually had a window that open in the living room area. It was so nice to get real air. Unfortunately, the bathroom was small and only had one bathroom requiring a person to climb down the spiral stairs to use the bathroom. It was inconvenient in the middle of the night. The breakfast buffet was great! The offered so many different variety foods including hard boiled eggs topped with shrimps, tuna salad, fresh breads, sausages, beans, ham, assorted cheeses, fish and so much more. The food was nicely presented. However, the dining area became very crowded during the hours of 7am and 8am. The hotel offered a very small selling area that had snacks and drinks. Although small it had a nice selection of items at a reasonable price. I especially enjoyed the wine selections. Although the hotel did not have a pool or hot tub, I would definitely stay there again. I walked everywhere and loved the restaurant next door. It was an Icelandic hotel with a warm southern American feeling.

author: Horsemules
title: Five Nights in Reykjavik
text: First time in Iceland and I LOVED it. Did a trip with Gate 1 and had a wonderful experience. They had everything arranged without being on an escorted tour. The hotel was a little out of the city centre but very easy walkng distance and a short walk to the harbor. The girls behind the desk were very nice and helpful. Lobby and room was a little small but that is by American standards. European standards.... was normal. The hot water shower is out-of-this-world. It is plentiful and you never run out as it comes from way underground from the volcano situation. We had a two story room with lots of light from a wall of windows. Bed was comfortable. Breakfast was very good and the area was very nice with lots of windows. I would highly recommend and would stay again myself. ICELAND IS PHENOMENAL.

author: SarahKnowsThisOne
title: Functional.
text: I stayed here in March 2015 during what I was persistently told was " the worst weather in fifteen years". Despite the heavy snowfall and subzero temperature, the hotel was always warm and cosy. It's located about ten minutes walk from the city centre and the tour companies all run pick ups directly to the door. The night staff were very friendly and helpful, even after my flight was delayed by eight and a half hours and I didn't arrive until 1.30am.The day staff were a little less cheerful, but were very efficient and more than happy to organise tours and taxis. As I was travelling alone, I was allocated a tiny room on the fourth floor (it was either 406 or 407, I can't quite remember). The dark decor made it feel even smaller than it was, but it was perfectly adequate for me. Although other people have commented that the rooms on the front of the hotel get a lot of traffic noise, I can't say I noticed it. The room did have a lino floor, so I'd probably recommend taking some slippers and something to wear indoors - as I mentioned, there was heavy snowfall during my stay so the floor was constantly wet. The bathroom had clearly not been updated for quite some time, but everything worked just fine. The shower curtain was in pretty desperate need of a good wash; it was gross enough that rinsing it off with the shower didn't have any effect. Despite that, the shower itself was really good. You just have to adjust to the slightly odd smell. Breakfast runs from 7am until 10am in the bar area. You get a massive selection of hot and cold food, so I'd definitely recommend filling up before you go out. They do also offer a limited selection of breakfast foods on request from 4am for anyone with an early flight. Other than breakfast, the food situation is a little grim - there's a small case in reception with a few overpriced sandwiches and bottled drinks, but that's it. I bought a sandwich once, which contained brown lettuce and ended up in the bin. Overall, other than a few minor issues, this hotel has everything you'll need for your stay and I would definitely recommend it. Good points: good breakfast selection, efficient staff. Bad points: could use a deep clean.

author: Cats_123
title: Ideally Located
text: About a 10mn stroll to the main shopping area, this hotel is ideally located for tourists. There are several good restaurants in the vicinity. 5mn walk to the bus station. Built in the 1970s style, there is a small reception with a self service vending cabinet with sandwiches, soft drinks and alcohol. Further on is the main breakfast area which also has a small bar (but we never saw it open). Our bedroom was on the 2nd floor overlooking the street. It was a junior suite style with room for a sofa, coffee table and two chairs. Ensuite shower/wc and tea/coffee making facilities. There was also a fridge and a safe. The room was very warm (but then it was very cold outside) and there was a fair amount of noise from passing traffic and when the coaches pulled up outside the hotel. Having said that it was quite comfortable and maid service was very efficient. Good Wi-fi available throughout the hotel free of charge. Reception staff were very pleasant and always willing to answer questions/provide advice. Breakfast was at times like a bun fight, but at other times quite a pleasant experience. The hotel caters for `coach loads' and regularly has 50-100 guests staying any number of nights. So, everyone needs to breakfast at the same time. On two mornings (out of 5) there were queues to gte tables, but no more than a 5-10mn wait. Kitchen staff cleared the tables regularly and refreshed the food etc. There was a wide variety of buffet food available to meet most tastes, fresh fruit juices and hot beverages. We chose this hotel as a 3 star price range and it fits the bill perfectly.

author: MDGodwin
title: Bucket list trip
text: We booked this trip through a contact at Travel Counsellors. Julie got us 4 nights for the price of 3. I knew being a Best Western it wasn't going to be a 4 star hotel but I knew we weren't going to spending a lot of time in our room. This hotel is ideally located for the main drag of the cities bars and restaurants. You are literally less than 5 - 7 minutes walk away. If you want access to the main part of this buzzing city stay here. We stayed in room 325. Our room was clean spacious with underfloor heating in the bathroom. Room was warm and well appointed to a good basic level. Good tea and coffee making facilities and fridge which is always welcome to store the booze. Our friends room was not so great room 229 had mould in the corner of the room and no where to hang their clothes. It was an odd shape a weird triangle shape. Had I got that room I would have complained but our friends were more easy going that I am regarding rooms. The breakfast every morning was plentiful and we found we had room to sit as we got down early but it gets busy. The hotel receptionists were all very helpful and confirmed our trips for us when needed which is imperative you do the night before. We were blessed we saw the Northern lights so our stay was magical. We didn't spend much time in our rooms but I will be recommending this hotel as a good option to all my friends who are booking to go soon.

author: JellingtonFishly
title: Great location; excellent staff
text: We were here for my wife's 50th birthday, 16-20 February 2015 and this hotel suited us perfectly. Whilst not a grand or plush hotel, we were upgraded to a (ground floor) 'character room' in a part of the hotel building extended into the neighbouring former brewery. The room was quirky, retaining features of its original purpose, with sections of bare block or concrete wall and iron doors that, one assumes, served an oven or some sort of hopper for brewing ingredients (I'm guessing here). The bed was comfortable and the room had a wall-mounted tv and a fridge, which came in handy for drinks. The bathroom was lovely, with both a bath and very efficient shower. Do remember the hot water supply in Iceland smells 'eggy' due to the suphur - we were expecting it and it still took us by surprise! The only downsides to the bedroom was that the hotel wifi failed to reach us and also traffic noise, not least of all because of the bus stop outside our window. That said, passing vehicles were occasional rather than frequent so this really didn't bother us. Breakfast was an extensive cold buffet, plus some hot food such as scrambled eggs and sausages, and fruit, cereals and a choice of delicious breads. We also helped ourselves to juices and coffee. The best features of our stay were the location (10 minutes walk from the main shopping street and a further 30 minute stroll down to the water front, harbour and concert hall) but especially the staff. Without exception they were really helpful, booking taxis, recommending and booking restaurants and excursions and answering our many questions! When seeking a restaurant, one of the reception staff went to the trouble of printing off 2 or 3 menus from restaurant websites and brought them down to our room to help us make a decision. The hotel manager should be proud of his/her team of staff, who really enhanced our stay in Reykjavik. In summary, a mid-priced, well-located hotel, with excellent staff.

author: Jetset891
title: Lovely Short Break
text: Myself and a friend stayed at the Best Western Reykjavik from 16th-19th January. Our room was large and the beds were very comfortable! I had a great nights sleep every night. I'd read previous reviews and expected a great breakfask... It was okay... The hot food wasn't hot, so I stuck to toast and the cold breakfast which was very nice and filled us up until lunch. The hotel was quite central but I think I'd of prefered to have stayed at the other side of the main street towards the Harbour. The staff were very helpful if without a smile.... Overall great value for money! We were very lucky and saw the Northern Lights... be prepared for a long night though!! If you can get on a coach with a guy called Swan he's brilliant!! Very informative and funny, we were out until 1am however other groups the night before were out until 3am. The Blue Lagoon is a must, such a different experiance and great fun smearing mud all over your face. One resturant I must recommend is the Fish and Chip Shop on the Harbour front, there are two close together but this one was also part of the volcanic museum... very very yummy, with freshly caught fish.... Iceland was amazing and I'd love to go back!

author: alexo734
title: Never again!
text: This place is awful. Beyond awful. I don't care how cheap it is, it's not worth it, trust me! I have never stayed in a best western before, & I hope sincerely that I never have the misfortune to stay in one again. After almost booking the Radisson Blu our travel agent recommended this hotel... It is safe to say I will never use said travel agent again. I have no idea why he hates me this much!! The reception staff I can only assume are lazy as they don't seem to care you're staying there. One morning we sat in reception for 45 minutes waiting for our tour bus, to be told when we asked that it wasn't coming, that the tour company had called three hours ago to cancel it. Thanks for telling us! The hotel generally is in need of an update, with a carpet resembling a throw back from the 1980s. Our 'double room' was two singles pushed together with separate bedding on each (which we were told is just how it comes!) that slide around on the wooden floor as they are on wheels. The walls are so thin I could actually hear the man next door snoring/talking/sneezing and the floor boards creaking... And don't even get me started on the breakfast. They don't even have enough tables so for the two out of three mornings we decided to torture ourselves with awful food we had to sit on uncleared tables with other couples. They should be ashamed to say they offer cooked breakfast - chicken sausage and baked beans plus hard boiled eggs that you have to peel yourself does not constitute cooked breakfast. Oh and don't let anyone tell you it's in the city centre - it is about a 30 to 40 minute walk to the harbour. NEVER AGAIN!

author: Hooliethetraveller
title: Basic but great location
text: Hotel wasn't the cheapest in Reykjavik but had a great location. Close to the restaurants and shops. Plus as it was near the main road the excursion and shuttle bus would pick and drop us right in front of our hotel. Unlike others who had to walk in the freezing cold weather. Hotel was basic. The beds were really small. The duvet covers weren't great quality. They were really thin and small. I'm 170cm which is on the boarder line of average and a tall female. I'm wondering how taller people fit on those beds. They were somewhat comfortable but not great standard for best western. The water really smelt, we were told this was because something about the volcanic ash or lava. Can't really remember. But it really really smells. Breakfast was ok. Staff were very friendly and helpful. Plus loved the Scandinavians in general. They are extremely friendly and welcoming. If your going to do excursions it's best to book and print them online as you can get a discount after a few bookings. All excursions are same price more or less everywhere.

author: DeepakTailor
title: Excelent Hotel!
text: Lovely hotel to base yourself in Reykjavik. Very close to the centre of town. Walking distance to the main shopping street. You are around 4-5 minute walk from a local supermarket. Rooms inside the hotel are of a good standard. Maybe slightly dated and a bit old, but we had no problems. Breakfast was great. Lots of variety. There is eggs, sausages, cereals, breads, fruit and juices. Will be suitable for most people. Free WiFi coverage is good throughout the hotel. Reception staff were very helpful. Kolbrun was the best person on the front desk. She was fantastic at helping us organise all our tours, coaches and helping with rooms. Would stay again at this hotel without hesitation.

author: dawng344
title: A great location, but don't leave anything behind as you won't get it back.
text: We flew with WOW and the flight was brilliant, on time both ways and a really friendly crew. This hotel is about 3mins walk from the main shopping street. It is very clean and compact and just what we needed for our 4 night break. The safe, and tea and coffee making facilities were a bonus as well. There are plenty of toiletries in the bathroom so you don't have to bring a lot with you. The breakfast is buffet, with the normal continental breakfast as well as cooked, which was normally, scrambled eggs, baked beans and sausages. There was also lots of variety of breads and pastries, as well as different teas, coffee and juices. Considering this was included in the price of the hotel it was definitely good value. The in room wifi can be slow at times. We did not find the reception very helpful towards excursions on the 2/3 times we asked. They pointed at the leaflets on the desk. There are a couple of tourist shops on the Main Street and we booked with both of these, which included pick ups from the hotel lobby. Whilst in Iceland we did the Pearl tour with the Mountineers, which I would recommend, the Blue Lagoon, hired a car and the northern light tour which was unsuccessful on both occasions. My only grievance with this hotel, is that I left an item of clothing when we departed. I know exactly where I left it, however when I arrived home 8hrs later and emailed the hotel, they advised me that no item was left which is very untrue. I would therefore be very wary of leaving anything valuable lying around and if you leave something behind, don't expect it back. I know I should have had a better look around before I departed, but I would have expected a lot more from the staff., because of this I will not be returning to this hotel but would definitely return to Iceland as 4 nights was not long enough.

author: the_weekend_warrior
title: Great location for short trip
text: We stayed here for 2 nights in November as part of a stopover package en route to USA. We had asked our travel agent for an inexpensive middle of the road hotel and this is what we got. The airport transfer was door to door with Flybus. On arrival the hotel receptionist, Thora (forgive my spelling please) went far above the call of duty helping to sort out our trips. This example of customer service is outstanding. We took the hotel lift to our allocated room, 419, a family room with a double and 2 single beds. The shower room/toilet was very small but clean and did the job. The water smells strongly of sulphur so top tip is to let the water run for a few minutes and leave the door open before taking a shower or brushing teeth. The room provided tea/coffee making facilities, hairdryer, shampoo, conditioner and shower gel, safe and fridge. The hotel also provided free wifi which was brilliant. Unfortunately the bedroom had many velux type windows which were not well fitted and the noise of the rain, traffic etc was pretty bad. Breakfast was buffet style - tea, coffee, toast/bread, croissants, fruit, cereal, scrambled egg, sausages, cold meats, cheese etc. The breakfast room was clean and tidy and the staff were quick to replenish and clear tables. The hotel was ideally located to walk around the city centre and we thought for the price it was excellent value for money. We would return however would request a room at the back of the hotel.

author: janetrA6858IF
title: Great hotel to stay
text: Stayed for five days in room 101. Very large modern separate shower bath and toilet. Stayed for five days. Double bed ,desk and chair,two seats and a coffee table. Sachets available to make hot drinks. Radiators can be switched off or on easily. Plenty of wardrobe space and drawers. You push the drawers to open not pull. Overall very impressed. Breakfast was continental were you help yourself but they do have warm sausage or scrambled eggs if you need it. There again to help yourself. The tea and coffee at breakfast is from a flask. There is a selection of tea bags to choose from. I have no problem with this as breakfast is included in the price of the room We felt it was a very fair price as it is more expensive eating out in iceland. If you want a decent ground coffee or tea there are plenty of places to go in Reykjavik cafe or restaurant . Harry's restaraunt next door is very good. If wanting a cheaper option there is a good local pizza place on the corner by the bus station. Take away or sit in on a stool and afterwards cross over the road to the donnut stand small but very tasty

author: LolaLanes
title: Overall very good stay.
text: We were booked into this hotel for 3 nights through a travel agency package to Reykjavik. Our flight arrived into Reykjavik at 6:30am so arrived at the hotel by 8:30am. We knew we could not expect to get a room upon arrival so we checked our bags by the front desk to plan out our day. First, we were welcomed with a really wonderful breakfast--hot and cold items and so traditional local dishes. Given the very expensive cost of eating out in Iceland, this was a great way to save some money. After breakfast, we returned to the front desk to inquire about approx. time that our room would be available. To our great surprise, there was a room available immediately. The room was very clean and comfortable. Nothing fancy but definitely did the job of providing a good night sleep and a shower. We found the front desk staff to be exceptionally helpful and friendly. They provided some good recommendations for restaurants and places to visit. The only slight downside for us was that the location of the hotel was a bit removed from the heart of the downtown core. Fortunately, we did not mind walking around but definitely,it was not a location to drop by whenever you needed a break. However, every tour we took pretty much picked us up or dropped us off back to the hotel.

author: Powertrip1
title: Slightly Disappointed
text: Upon arrival for my reservation, the hotel informed me that they did not have my booking. I made the reservation on www.booking.com, and they claimed they had never received the information from booking.com. It came across as "this isn't our fault, its theirs". Well, if they agree to a working partnership with them, then it is their responsibility for the situation at that time. The quickly endeavored to put together a room for my group of 3, of which was satisfactory. Upon checkout the next morning, I politely asked for a possible discount because of the stress and inconvenience that was caused by the error. They declined at first, stating they had met our initial rate and provided the exact room we had booked. They asked if there was anything wrong with the room, to which I said no, but I insisted they offer something, as a kind gesture for the incident. They agreed to a 10% discount. I was a little turned off by this initial arrogance the evening before, and then during checkout. In my business, if there is an incident it is mandatory for me to offer something to my clients, regardless of outcome or situation. - Breakfast was good and the setting was comfortable. - Rooms were small but comfortable and maintained. - Parking was confusing and unexplained to me. I was stuck for 10 minutes trying to exit because there was no was to open to exit door. I had to put my car in park and run into the lobby of the hotel and ask them to open it. - Price, as with everything in Reykjavik, was not worth the value. That is just the economy in Iceland though.

author: roadwarriorla
title: Great Front Desk. Horrible hot water.
text: What no one tells you about Iceland is that the wonderful geothermal energy means that the hot water smells like sulfur. I am not kidding. If you go to take a shower or wash your hands you smell the distinctive smell of rotten eggs. It is rather disgusting. The Best Western Reykjavik is about what you can expect for a 3 star hotel. Very clean and comfortable. Average continental breakfast included. Not a great location.. a bit of a walk from central Reykjavik. The front desk is very helpful and accommodating (They are VERY GOOD). They offer an early check in for 5000 IKR which is a nice thing. The room is ok..not great. Don't get your hopes up about seeing the Northern lights. But that's more about the Gray Line tours...I will review that separately. But the hot water is truly indescribable. Who wants to wash their hair in rotten eggs ?

author: markaD2023FD
title: Convenient Location with Helpful Staff
text: Summary: Walking distance to downtown and staff that goes above and beyond when making recommendations and reservations. Reynir and Thora were especially helpful. Pros: 1. Daily Breakfast (meats, cheeses, breads, yogurts, croissants, hard-boiled eggs, coffee, tea, apple/orange juice) and the staff comes by regularly to refill and clean up. 2. Overall clean place and helpful staff. 3, Fast, free wireless internet (~15Mbps down and up) 4. Front doors lock late at night to prevent random people/drunks from wandering in. 5. 15-20 minute walk to the end of the main street (Laugavegur) 6. 2 for 1 happy hour at the breakfast room/bar from 5-7 (i believe) 7. Walking distance to the bus stop and a late pizza shop, Devitos, that closes at 1pm. Cons: 1. The room (1 Queen) was a tad on the small side, but nothing terrible (just an observation) 2. Need to get ice at the bar and no ice buckets 3. The main lobby gets quite crowded around check-in/out time (probably because of its popularity) 4. No gym, but you get a lot of walking done when you walk around the area.

author: Cazanda
title: Clean, Convenient, and Amazing Staff!
text: Such a great location! Short walk to downtown Reykjavic. This is also one of the main hotels that most tours will be able to pick you directly up from. Our room was small - but you're in Iceland! Why would you want to stay in a hotel anyway?! However small, it had everything we could need - a small fridge, cozy bed, and a super hot shower. Our room also had a balcony, which was great! We were able to enjoy sunrise/sunsets, see the water, and have a great view of the mountains. We were even able to see the Northern Lights the first night we were in! *Breakfast is complimentary - typical continental style. *Happy Hour was from 5 - 7, where the special was Gull. This is perfect if you're doing the late Northern Lights tour! The best part of the hotel though? Þora! She was so incredibly helpful and helped us to find our way around town, suggest restaurants, and book extra excursions. If traveling back to Iceland, I would book here again solely for the fact that Þora was so great. Almost like your own personal travel guide! We had a great stay here and would love to return!

author: Charlotte061287
title: Friendly staff and good location
text: The family room was spacious, comfortable and clean. We had everything that we needed plus more such as a kettle, tv, hairdryer and bathrobes. There was also free wifi. There was plenty of choice at breakfast ranging from cereal, toast, croissants, fruit, meat, tea, coffee and fruit juice. Breakfast is also served for a few hours which is good if you want an early start or a lie in. There is a bar in the hotel but it was rather pricey for 2 glasses of wine so would recommend drinking in town. The staff were all friendly, polite and very helpful. The girl who worked on reception when we arrived on the Thursday evening was extremely friendly and lovely to talk to. She provided us with lots of information about the Northern Lights and places to visit in Iceland. The location of the hotel was very good as only a 10 minute walk into all of the lovely cafés, restaurants, shops and the Cathedral. There is also a supermarket nearby which is very handy. The hotel is set on a quiet street so you won't be disturbed by people leaving pubs late at night. Finally, the hotel also has a secure car park which is great if you are renting a car. Only downside is that you have to get someone on reception to open it to get in and out. Overall, a great place to stay in Reykjavik.

author: Pstreet1
title: Friendly People, Location a Little Out of the Center of Town
text: The Best Western in Reykjavik was a good choice: the rooms were clean and adequate. Each had a small refrigerator and the beds were fine. We were placed in a triple, 3 twin beds, which would not have been our choice, but it was fine. The rooms are warm, maybe a bit too warm, but that can be remidied by opening the window. The floor of the bathroom is heated, and that is very nice. The highlight of the hotel is its breakfast, which in included in the room rate. They served hard boiled eggs, ham, cheese, yoghurt, fresh fruit, freshly baked bread, muffins, juice, cereal, milk, good coffee--and probably more that I've forgotten. They also have half price drinks for happy hour each day, and the setting is pleasant. Everything in Iceland is noticeably expensive, and this breakfast buffet would cost a great deal if purchased elsewhere. All of the front desk people are extremely helpful. They switched one tour we were scheduled to be on, they gave advice about nearby restaurants, and were happy to chat about Iceland. They were unfailingly cheerful. We were very pleased with our stay. The center of town is several blocks, which would be a pleasant stroll in any season except winter, when we were there. We didn't stroll; we moved right along at a pretty brisk pace, but even with the cold, it wasn't far.

author: spamfred
title: Great Location, Basic Hotel, Friendly Staff
text: We booked this hotel as a bit of a budget option and we weren't disappointed with what we received. Bearing in mind how expensive Iceland is, I was happy with this hotel choice. I stayed with my sister in a twin room and the room was small, the beds were fairly small and the shower room was also rather compact. In our room we had a kettle and complimentary tea and coffee which was nice. We had a TV that worked, as well as a clock radio. WIFI is also free in this hotel which is great. In the shower room, washing your face using the basin can be a challenge as there is a shelf immediately above the basin which gets in the way. It can also be tight getting round the toilet into and out of the shower. However, we had hot water and there were also some complimentary toiletries if you wished to use them. We had breakfast included in our stay, it's a basic continental type breakfast but perfectly adequate. Not a great selection if you need to follow a gluten-free diet but there is cheese, some fruit and some meats. The reception staff were fabulous, really friendly and keen to ensure you enjoy your stay. One of them even rushed out to our coach for our day trip as I'd left my hat on a sofa in the lobby. The hotel is located in walking distance of the main street for restaurants, etc. albeit at the "wrong" end but it takes about 25 mins from the hotel to walk the entire length of the street so it's hardly far. I'd definitely recommend this hotel to anyone on a budget who just wants somewhere friendly to rest their head at the end of a day. If you're a light sleeper, perhaps take earplugs as there's a little street noise and I found my eye mask useful to block out street light which seeped around the edges of the blackout curtains.

author: benmychree
title: Not bad for Iceland, not great compared against elsewhere
text: I stayed for 2 nights on arrival in Iceland and 1 night on departure. For Iceland it is not bad, or so I am told by veteran visitors there. On arrival I was in 214, described as a "good room" by the receptionist. It was certainly very spacious, almost like a suite compared to the other rooms, some of which my fellow travellers described as pokey. The safe didn't work but everything else did. It has a basic, homely, slightly cheap feel to it. Not much more to say. It did the job, and for the money I think the quality was reasonable. Breakfast was a continental style buffet. Nothing spectacular but not bad. On departure I had a much smaller room. That was after a room change because some inconsiderate and ignorant person had been smoking in the first one, despite it being a no smoking floor. The lift was also went out of order as I got into it, and there are no staff other than a receptionist so it wasn't much fun taking my heavy bags up 3 flights of stairs. A good cardio workout in the absence of a gym however! The hotel is only a few minutes' walk from the centre of the town, so the location was pretty good, but that is true of nearly all hotels in Reykjavik. The area is not particularly inspiring - some pretty drab and run-down housing is the view from your window.

author: DP_Canadian
title: Good location for walking downtown
text: We stayed at Best Western Hotel Reykjavik for one night at the end of a week trip to Iceland. We chose this hotel for two reasons - I had a BW gift card to pay for the room, and we liked the location for walking distance to downtown. The room we had was spacious, with a large sitting area as well as the large size bed (two oversized twins?). It overlooked the road in front of the hotel, so there was some road noise, but not enough to keep us awake. If you are a light sleeper ask for a room at the back - buses run up this street regularly. The area looks a bit rundown, with graffiti on some of the apartment buildings, but you're not far from the main shopping street, and we felt perfectly safe. We were also just downhill and about 10 minutes walk from Hallgrimskirkja, and 10 minutes drive from Perlan. I liked that we had underground parking for free. Breakfast at the hotel was very busy, and the layout isn't the best (constantly bumping into people around the food area). We were down for breakfast just after the start time, and were very lucky to find a seat. Variety of food was good though, the typical Icelandic continental breakfast with breads, cheese, cold cuts, cereal, boiled eggs, fruit. There is no restaurant in the hotel, but Harry's next door (Asian and Icelandic items) was excellent - probably the cheapest and best meal of our entire one week trip. My husband had a chicken curry, I had garlic grilled haddock, and we shared spring rolls. Including a beer, the bill was less than $65 and we had food leftover. I would stay here again - the location was good, price was reasonable and the staff were very helpful.

author: Leanne_Bear
title: How do you overbook & bump a reservation made 4 months ago?
text: We arrived in Reykjavik on an overnight flight Friday October 11, 2013. Got in at 5:15 a.m. After a hassle with the rental car, in the pouring rain, we made it to this hotel. We were first told that th room was not ready but they would try for between 8:00 and 9:00. In the meantime, we could have ONE cup of coffee each, only, we waited. At 8:30 we were advised that they had 'overbooked' and that they would not be able to accommodate us. What?! We booked this hotel through our travel agent in July/August. Had a voucher. We think this was the issue - why accept a pre-paid voucher at a lower rate when you can get other guests to pay more? They contacted Hotel Leifur Eiriksen - right across from the big church in downtown central - to put us up. We went there - again, room not ready. They allowed us to have breakfast - but we insisted on checking the room first. Not acceptable. Back to the Best Western. This time we were directed to the Grand Hotel, where we stayed. Only worked out because we had a rental car. Never saw the rooms ar the Best Western, so can't comment, and the front desk clerk did get us sorted - finally - to a decent hotel - but I would exercise caution in booking this hotel ever, and if you do so, book directly with them, get an email confirmation from them, don't book through a travel agent and get a voucher. We had no problem with the voucher system in Australia last year but Iceland is - obviously - different.

author: 560sandys
title: Small
text: The location is excellent and close to most things. On first checking in the young man at the desk was friendly, if not really very helpful. Was taken aback at the size of the room for two people. If you have the standard 22" luggage it is very hard to find room for two and still be able to walk around. The bathroom was tiny and lacked anyplace to put toothbrush and paste, let alone any make-up that one might need in there. Fortunately, neither of us used much. With a little imagination some shelves could be added in the bathroom. Same for the other area. I know that duvets are standard in most if not all of Europe. But, perhaps a single sheet placed in the cupboards for warm days would be possible. One young woman was extremely pleasant and helpful at the front desk; was able to give directions to places and suggestions. An "older" man that was at the desk some of the time seemed to have absolutely no interest in customers. The breakfast was adequate and nothing more. The girls in the kitchen were pretty surly. The same surliness was evident in the housekeeping group; never a smile when addressed with a "good morning" from the guests. The room was clean and was made up each day. A couple of times one towel was taken and not replaced until a call was made to the desk. For $200 American I would expect a bit more.

author: Landican
title: Nice basic hotel from a reliable chain
text: Medium sized hotel in this well known chain. Clean and comfortable but no frills. My single room was of a decent size with all the usual amenities. In reasonable decor, warm and comfortable. Two radiators which were both adjustable and I also had a small balcony - no view, but a balcony nonetheless. Bed was OK, although new pillows would be a bonus - mine had lost their umph! Bathrooms was OK - rather dark though which made the application of make-up challenging, particularly as the bedroom also lacked a decent light. A full length mirror would also have been appreciated. There is a reasonable choice of TV - although a flat screen placed in the extreme corner of the room is not particularly conducive to easy viewing! Although the receptionist was very helpful indeed, and very welcoming, I was not impressed that my room did not have it's tea and coffee replenished on the first morning of my stay, and even less impressed that there appeared to be no housekeeping in my room on the second morning at all! Breakfast was a trifle disappointing with no hot option at all. The one domestic toaster is woefully inadequate for a dining room full of guests and I gave up in the end. The cold options were also not that exciting. The hotel is well placed for the town, being a few minutes walk away and there seemed to be no end to the activities that could be organised from there, although I did not partake of these myself. So, all in all, and OK stay but some little things could be improved with a minimal effort.

author: E22S
title: Iceland Honeymoon Trip
text: We stayed at the Best Western Hotel Reykkjavik for our honeymoon in January 2013. The first room we were given was on the small side and did not appear to have been made up to the usual Best Western standard. The following morning after informing the reception staff we were promptly moved to a room on the top floor, which was much more spacious, with a balcony and refubished bathroom. This room was great and a perfect base for exploring Iceland. The staff were all very friendly and of course everyone in Iceland speaks English which made our trip easier. The hotel has an abundance of information on local excusions and Iceland must-do's so if you dont have your schedule already mapped out you can do so when you arrive. Staff we also very accomodating when confirming excursion pick up times etc. The hotel was clean and tidy and the buffet breakfast had a good selection, although my husband was disappointed there wasn't a 'full English' on the menu! We ate in the Pizza restaurant on our final evening - the food was fantastic and the staff were really friendly. The only slight complaint we had was that the bar didn't seem open in the evenings during our stay - maybe there wasn't enough demand but I'm not sure. The hotel is ideally located close to the town so it wasnt difficult to seek out bars and restuarants, which we did. We went on the whale watching tour, which was a bit of a let down as it was exremely cold and didn't see any whales only dolphins. Of course this wasn't their fault but I dont think I would book this trip again in the cold winter. We were lucky enough to see the northern lights during our stay and we are delighted to have done this by super jeep - they were fantasic and the jeep experience is not to be missed! The Golden Circle tour was my faveourite day and I dont think anyone should visit Reykjavik without booking on to this! On our final day we visited the Blue Lagoon, which despite the rain and fog was a great end to our busy trip. Many thanks to this hotel, its staff and Iceland for making our honeymoon so special! This really was the holiday of a life time for us and we would recommend it to all! If we are ever lucky enough to return to Iceland we wouldn't hesitate in booking the Best Western.

author: hidee97
title: No Northern Lights for us
text: Our family of three stayed at the Best Western-Hotel Reykjavik for three nights late September. Our room (313), located at the end of the corridor, was very good and spacious. Good tv, the (free) wifi worked well, beds and duvets were very comfortable, and the bathroom was well equipped with lots of amenities. The mini fridge had three bottles of glacier water and the heavy curtains kept out the outside lights. Coffee and tea were also available in the room and restocked every day. We had to ask for washcloths the second and third day. The staff were helpful and pleasant and speak English very well . Kudos to our night receptionist for his sense of humor! Breakfast was more than adequate (included), memorable was the huge bowl of hardboiled eggs, still warm. Walking distance to the Iceland National Museum is 15 minutes, and less than 5 minutes to the waterfront. Across the street is a delightful little restaurant, Harry's, run by a young couple, which should not be missed. Good food, pleasant atmosphere, excellent service and reasonable prices. (Harry will take your coats and hang them up.) We used the Scandinavian 3 Nights Holiday Special of 338 euro's, which I found an extremely reasonable price and value. Everything is within walking distance, just bundle up and brave the wind and cold. We had a great time, even without the Northern Lights!

author: sudhgarg
title: Nothing short of excellent!!!
text: We stayed there for 5 nights through Icelandair package. I must say that everything was simply fantastic. The hotel is well-located with a bus stop & 11to11 (supermarket) nearby. We had our own rental car & thus did not use the bus service. The hotel is clean & offers very good value for money - free wi-fi, free parking, great buffet breakkfast are additional value-adds. The reception staff is really friendly & Jon Arason was of great help. He is a fantastic guy & I had some great conversations with him. We were given a deluxe double room which was really large for european standards (something like 25 mtr sqr). We simply loved iceland and are already planning our next trip! Some tips: - The northern lights coach packages (from most companies) are a complete rip-off. - Hire a rental car & explore the country - its amazingly fresh & beautiful - On your own car, a fantastic place near Reyk to watch the Northern lights, is Seltjarnanrnes (Grotta beach) which is like 10 kms away only. - Northern lights appear better to your camera than your naked eye - generally appear as vertical green patterns - Routes in single digit & double digits are safe to drive in winter (we had a a Hyundai i20 & faced no issues). Avoid highlands with such vehicle or go for a 4X4 - Sunrise & sunsets are pretty amazing - you feel as if you are on another planet - Its realy windy out there & wet as well - so prepare yourself accordingly - There's a very modern looking church in Seltjarnarnes a couple of kms away from the Grotta beach) on a small hillock which offers great views of Reyk. We met a great gentleman from the church there who offered us free coffee & great knowledge on iceland - thank you sir! - Keep an eye on weather at all times - it keeps changing - we were fooled twice by it. - We drove from Reyk to Akranes - not the tunnel but around the peninsula - some breathtaking views worth dying for - take this lesser known route on a clear day from some real mountainside panoramic views - return to Reyk via the tunnel from Akranes - And last but not the least, MUST try the geothermal pools - they are real dirt cheap at 3 euros in Reyk - we tried Laugar***, which closes at 10 PM (very refreshing after a hard day out in the fields) And thanks once again to Jon & his team at the reception, without whom the trip would not be as memorable as it is!

author: LondonJay73
title: Warm Welcome in a Cold Climate
text: Greeted with a friendly welcome. Reception staff very helpful. Rooms are clean, comfortable and warm. Has tea making facility in the room.
