Breakfast is contienental but lots of choice, toast, croissants, cereals, fruit salad, hard boiled eggs, a selection of cheese and ham, yogurt. Choice of coffee,tea, orange, apple juice. Hotel is attached to La Luna restaurant so very convenient if arriving late and wanting a quick bite to eat without having to go into town. The main shops are about 10 minute walk. Many restaurants to choose from. Would recommend Caruso and Pomoddorosa, great food. The hotel will book the Flybus coach for you when requested. Nothing is too much trouble. Icelanders make you feel so very welcome. Take full advantage of all the excursions - particularly the Blue Lagoon (hot spring) and the Superjeep Tour for the Golden Circle. Best trip though was to see the Northern Lights - no guarantee, was cancelled twice due to weather conditions, however, got lucky on our last nite and saw the most amazing light show on earth - will stay with me forever!! Had the best time in Iceland! X

author: PGGUk
title: Space is at a premium
text: The twin room was tiny. Beds had no headboard so pillow kept sliding down behind the bed. No drawers to store anything. No bath. Wash hand basin so small you had to twist abnormally to rinse your teeth. The ordinary sized bath mat took up all available floor space in the (bath?)room. Socket on far side of room meant moving the desk across the floor for computer to be used. Safe didn't work but was fixed (next day as handyman not available every day). Phone didn't work (ditto). TV worked but not the interactive part of it (alarm etc.) and this was not fixed. Beds very narrow singles. Breakfast OK but no hot breakfast and unless you got in early the fruit sald consisted of browing apples (+melon if there early). Good points: internet access was included in room price and reliable. Got early (4.30am) breakfast on day of departure as early flight. 3 for 2 beers in bar in evening Happy Hour.

author: boltondriv
title: provides a roof over your head, clean warm but lifeless.
text: perfectly adequate if you just want a room. room service doesnt happen unless you request it. two tea bags and two coffee sachets is not really drink facilities in my mind. Easily obtain more at reception, but this is the issue for me. No loo rolls, so ask at reception. wet towels, so ask at reception. one small skylight window in the room, so really hard to get any air flow. That said it was mainly clean, bar the black mould in the bathroom tiles and the leaking tap in the sink. Staff were adequate, i don't think we had one moment of genuine welcoming except for the morning cleaner who was always cheery!. i would use this again, but we stayed at the fosshotel baron ealier this year and the friendliness and attitude was way above this and yet the same calibre of hotel. Yes use it, but in my mind it is purely some where to sleep. a negative note. Breakfast giggling and playing silly games in the kitchen which can be heard at breakfast ending in one silly girl staff member bumping into the buffet table, then bumping into a diner then the table and then the same diner again!. Giggling and laughing and not even apologising, quite frankly had that have been myself a huge complaint would have been wagered against the management. Plus point. literally next door is 'harrys' restaurant, which they recommended and with good reason. Excellent food good prices, book as soon as you can though. oriental with icelandic charm!

author: g00dall
title: Great location, excellent staff - would stay here again
text: I stayed with my son for 5 nights and had a great trip. Room was basic but clean and functional (and I think we had one of the smaller rooms). We were hardly in our room so it was fine. Big plus is the location - quiet, but close enough to shops, harbour and tourist attractions. And also the staff , who were very friendly and helpful. Continental breakfast provided was plenty and kept us going for most of the day, and we got an early breakfast for our return flight. We ate in Harry's restaurant just outside the hotel which I can't recommend enough - it has added to the hotel's rating for me as it was great to just nip out the door to get an excellent meal at a reasonable cost (around £10 per main course which was a huge portion). Worth a visit even if your hotel is further away. Great area - felt very safe to walk around and check out the area. Very close to indoor thermal pool (5 mins) which is worth a visit. We also used superjeep.is for northern lights tour and the guys are brilliant! Much better than a bus tour in my opinion (which we also did for a day trip). Overall a great place to visit, and this hotel is a great base for a short trip. It's not a luxury hotel but it doesnt claim to be and doesn't charge luxury rates. I would definately stay here again.

author: MarkandFay
title: Great base for your Reykjavik trip and don't miss Harry's Restaurant next door!
text: We have just returned from a 5 night stay at the Hotel Reykjavik, Raudararstig 37, Iceland. The Hotel is basic, but clean and comfortable, with friendly and accommodating staff. Breakfast is an added bonus (continental style - cereal, toast, ham, cheese and fruits, with fruit juice and tea/coffee) as most Icelandic Hotels do not serve breakfast. For early flights, breakfast can be pre ordered from 4.30 am onwards. The room we stayed in had a large bathroom (bath and shower) and a reasonably sized bedroom, with double bed, wardrobe, dressing table, pre stocked fridge and tea/coffee making facilities, which are replenished every day. However, looking at the Hotel room plan, we were fortunate as there are some smaller rooms on offer, which other reviewers have alluded to. Reception will assist with booking trips, exchanging currency, pre booking your Flybus seats to the airport etc. Just one word of warning, we missed one trip as Reception failed to pass a message on to us from the Company in question to say our trip pick up time had been brought forward by 3.5 hrs, which was disappointing. However, given it was the Hotel's fault, they happily sent an email to the Company to explain this and sought a refund for us. Remember to check for messages when you're in Reception!! The Hotel is situated out of Reykjavik Town Centre and requires a brisk 10-15 minute walk to reach it. However, it's position means that it is quiet and aids a peaceful nights sleep. We enjoyed a number of Trips including: the Golden Circle (book with David, at Horizon, for a real insight into Iceland, in the comfort of a small tour Group/bus (all the reviews about David being a great tour guide are spot on), the Blue Lagoon and Snorkelling at the Silfra Fissure (Dive.is). All of which we would recommend. A hidden gem is Harry's Oriental Restaurant and Cafe, adjacent to the Hotel. It's a family run restaurant, which offers excellent food, a friendly service and affordable prices compared to other Reykjavik eateries. We ate there on a number of occasions and the menu included dishes such as: Fish and chips with fresh salad; Deep fried shrimps with salad and sweet chilli sauce; Panfried haddock with salad and lemon garlic sauce; Pork, or beef with veg in stir fried oyster sauce cooked in a wok pan, philippine style; Crispy Chicken with fresh salad; Hamburger; Phillipine noodles with fresh veg/chicken, or tofu. Pay it a visit during your stay, you won't be disappointed - the food is delicious! There is so much to do and see in Iceland that we will be returning and would have no hesitancy in returning to Hotel Reykjavik.

author: arhy
title: Friendly and Helpful
text: My fiancée and I stayed here over the new year of 2008/2009. The hotel was clean, tidy and in a great location. All the staff were very polite and helpful. Breakfast was sufficient and in the form of a cold buffet. There was also a small selection of cereal. We ate an evening meal in the snack bar on two occasions. On both occasions it was only manned by one member of staff. Despite this, she still managed to serve us in reasonable time with a very positive attitude. All members of staff had very good English. They were always helpful and provided us with local knowledge regarding food and places to visit. In terms of location my fiancée and I walked to the Perlan, the BSI terminal, Hallgrimur's church and thought nothing of it. All in all, we had a great holiday and the hotel provided a good place to set up camp. I would certainly stay here again. Quality wise, the hotel is certainly better than a travel lodge and slightly worse than the outer London Hilton Hotels. My only complaint was that the room was a bit dark.

author: Universal22
title: Just above a budget hotel
text: A very un-impressive hotel. We did not stay there by choice; we stayed as part of a tour group. I would not choose this hotel; to me it was just above a budget hotel. The good points for the hotel are location; it was a few minutes walk to the start of the main shopping & dinning street, with a good restaurant a few buildings away & the buffet style continental breakfast was very good, the usual cold meats & cheese, sliced tomatoes, fruit, cereals, yoghurt, hot hard boiled eggs, toast, rolls, sweet pastries, tea, coffee, water & juice. The down side to the breakfast, there is no where near enough seating. The food is served in the bar/snack area and most days the only table we could get was a small table best suited to having a drink & not a meal! The area the hotel is situated in is not the best, right next to the hotel there was a bar/restaurant, with a few locals that looked as though they spent a fair amount of time there, and this may not be a comfortable area to come and go alone at night, not that we experienced any problems, but it could make some people uncomfortable. As for the hotel rooms! This is probably one of the smallest rooms I have stayed in, (I have had bigger rooms in New York), and for a European room you expect more space! The tea & coffee provided = 2 tea bags & 2 coffee sachets per day, so if you don’t like one or the other drink you have one free drink per day if two of you are in the room! There were no toiletries provided in our room, just a shower cap and a soap dispenser by the sink, nothing for the shower, (although the chamber maid cart contained bars of soap, shampoo, conditioner, and body lotion our room and many of our party never saw any of these items). The sink overflow obviously wasn’t ever cleaned, it was black & had a build up of dirt, the shower cubicle had rust on the bottom of the door, I don’t think it had ever received much of a clean as the door and all the shower fittings had a build up of lime scale all over them, defiantly need to wear flip-flops in the shower. The TV was wall mounted and fixed in the top corner of the room and did not make for comfortable viewing. In all the time we were there the bed was never made, on one occasion the quit was folded over at the edge, but that’s as far as it went, most days the bed & pillows were as we had left them! Would I recommend this hotel to other travellers, no, you can do a lot better.

author: brancepethdli
title: an OK hotel
text: Booking was awkward, in that their web site said they had no rooms, yet they were able to book us in by direct email contact. Worried us a little but it worked out OK. Location is OK, just beyond the far end of Laugarvega, near the bus station, a good place to start walking through the shops, about 10-15 minutes walk to the main square. A few reasonable restaurants around, a cheap local pizza place is two buildings away. Good safe free car parking at the side entrance by reception, but need to hassle the reception staff at times to open gates to get out again. Back entrance from car park would benefit from small ramp to get trolley cases over door thresholds into building. Accommodation is fairly standard western traveller style, rooms were a good size compared with some other capital cities in Europe. Just accept the fact that the hot water is very sulphurous in smell, the cold water tastes delicious. Smoking does still appear to happen, judging by the odour on entry to some rooms. Breakfast buffet was fine, standard chain hotel stuff in Iceland, but nothing exciting. Good news was that they had an early breakfast available at 4.30 am to help travellers going for an early flight. There is a snack bar, but frozen pizza or cold sandwich was all that was available. Staff varied in quality, from friendly and helpful (e.g. night reception man) to downright rude. A couple of staff didn't seem to realise that we were there to be served, even though we did not ask for anything out of the ordinary. Value for money is OK for Reykjavik, about £170 for a double room with breakfast per night in July 2008. Overall, this is a hotel I would return to, but I would want to check a few alternatives first.

author: drluch
title: Great yet lousy
text: Spent three nights here during the long summer month of June. Rooms were fine, as we didn't stay there often. Although the location was a little far from the city center, it was close to several attractions we visited. The food was enjoyable and different, and the wait staff, and the bartender at night, were pleasant. The desk staff were pretty helpful, and led us to the downtown without problem. We went on a tour that was recommended by the staff and were very impressed with the geysers, waterfalls and the Blue Lagoon. Very enjoyable. Here's the problem: We left for the airport in a hurry after a tour, and I left my keys in a drawer the room, along with some money and some coins that were very sentimental to me. I called back and emailed back asking them to ship them to me as I would gladly pay for the shipping as well as the trouble taken to mail them. The first response I received was very helpful, as they said they would send them back immediately. After several days, I emailed back a couple of times and received no response. I ended up having to spend $150 for another programmable key for my car, not to mention the value of the money I left and more importantly the sentimental value of the coins I left. The bottom line: don't leave any valuables in this hotel, and don't expect any help if you happen to leave them. I'm sorry to have to leave a bad report, but I'm sure travelers understand my concerns. Don't let this keep you from Iceland - it is a beautiful country.

author: alekn
title: Nice hotel fro Iceland
text: In general, hotels in Iceland are not the same as a typical hotel in the US. Thus my review is based on a typical hotel for Iceland (I had a chance to stay in another hotel before). This is a good and very clean hotel. We booked "3 beds room", but got a double bed with roll-away bed instead. The roll-away bed was quite hard; it's not for people who got used to plush beds.Since they gave us a different room, they charged us less than the original estimate; we didn't have to even ask about it. The room was very clean and cozy. The room and hotel looked like recently renovated. The included breakfast was good. It's a real steal for Iceland where everything (especially now, with weak dollar) is so expensive. Make sure you eat you breakfast, lunch, and dinner in the morning :-) to save some bucks. The hotel is located near city center: 10-15 min. walk to the heart of the city. Ask hotel for a trip to Blue Lagoon. It's a really nice place to spend 2-3 hours, especially before your plane departure (they offer such option). Make sure you book the earliest bus. By the time we were leaving (1:30 PM) Blue Lagoon, the line to get inside was huge.

author: jclaire
title: Wonderful, friendly hotel near town centre
text: We have just returned from a 4 night stay at this hotel. I agree with previous reviews and would like to make the following observations: - Hotel was a short distance from the centre of town. There was a supermarket nearby where you could buy provisions. Don't bother to buy water, the tap water is perfectly safe. - We found a Thai restaurant very near by, just off the main road, where you could eat quite cheaply. As previous reviewers have noted Iceland is very expensive - make the most of your breakfast in the hotel as it's hard to find meals/snacks for less than £10 per person. - The hotel reception were extremely helpful about booking tours. Sometimes suggesting a cheaper alternative to the one that we chose. We went on the shortened Arctic Circle tour, the South Island tour, the Blue Lagoon and we were also lucky enough to see the Northern Lights on our last night there. Reception check at 6-7pm each evening to see whether the weather conditions are OK for this last tour. And then will book you on if it's going. - Rooms were small, but quite adequate. Sometimes noise carried from one room to another but it didn't bother us unduely. - The hotel has a restaurant next door and also will provide snacks and food. Overall I thoroughly recommend this hotel as a good base for exploring the surrounding area.

author: ISPpilot
title: Clean, quiet, convenient and an overall great value
text: Found this gem of a hostal from the Rick Steves guide and we were very satisfied with our stay. For a vibrant city like Madrid where basically all you need is a clean, quiet, comfortable and affordable place to stay, Acapulco is all of the above. I can highly recommend this place. The location is convenient to El Corte Ingles (go for the Gourmet Experience on the 9th Floor and pick up groceries in the basement 0.39 eurocent bottle of 1.5 L water), Gran Via, Puerta del Sol and the San Miguel Mercado. For Rick Steves readers, his easy to follow walking guide tour starts less than 5 minutes away at Puerta del Sol. The staff are friendly and welcoming and it is a pleasure to be welcomed back after a long day. I am a light sleeper and noise was never a problem. We ate at La Mallorquina, a long established bakery on the Puerta del Sol twice for breakfast. Really good pastries as well as espresso type coffee drinks. We were curious about the long lines outside of Takos, a Mexican taco joint on the corner. Despite the long lines, we ate here twice. Can't beat 1 Euro tacos. My favorites were the arrechera and chorizo. The red sauce was nice and spicy. I really enjoyed Madrid and if my travels ever take me back, I would not hesitate to stay at Hostal Acapulco again.

author: DaveandJaniece1999
title: Fantastic Value in a Fantastic Location!!!
text: Our room faced the little plaza in the front of the hotel. Interior and exterior noise was not an issue. Plaza quiets down after 10ish. Our room looked exactly like photo on web site.....two twin beds. Room size worked for us. In room refrigerator was nice. Bath a little small but it was OK...When you are only paying 59 Euro per night in a big city like Madrid you can over look some of the little things. Rooms needed to be updated, but I'm sure if that was done a higher rate would be paid. Rooms and bath were very clean. Location is perfect to connecting to train station ( 5 minute walk from Metro) and airport shuttle bus (a 15 minute walk) Also, a 5 minute walk to Plaza del Sol. Owner Javier is a great hotelier. He was very responsive during and after the reservation process The best advice he gave us was to eat at the Restaurante Puerto Rico which is directly behind the hotel.....a fantastic inexpensive family run place. The rest of the staff was very friendly and had great restaurant and transportation advice. I would definitely stay at the Hostal Acapulco again and again and again. Thanks Javier! BTW...If you stay 3 nights they will do your laundry for free....and fold it nice!

author: dannymal2504
title: Probably the best Hostel in Madrid
text: I stayed here for 3 days in May 2016 .It's a great price can't beat it. I got more than what I bargain for. The hostel is cheaper than mid-range. This Hostel had everything I was looking for. I had a private room. I had a large bed, t.v in room , phone, and a private bathroom with a shower and tub. I love that the bath water comes out really thick not like sprinkles. It's centrally located it's a block away from the main thoroughfare Gran Via. A subway stop is a block and a half away. I love that the staff spoken excellent English and are knowledge about the city. There's free wifi and a guest computer available to guests. The hostel doesn't have a lot of rooms that was a plus to. The hostel is very quiet at night. I picked a winner and you will to, if you stay here. Final note if all goes well I may return to Madrid either solo or with a friend in September 2016 and I already know were I'll be staying !!!!

author: EdS172
title: Very Good Hostal, only one negative
text: We stayed here for three nights on our trip to Spain. We arranged the room prior to leaving home and Javier was very helpful and thorough. The price was excellent. The hostal is on Plaza del Carmen very close to the Puerta del Sol and the action of downtown Madrid. It is located on the fourth floor (there is an elevator) of a building that contains about three other hostals. The reception and check-in was quick and easy. We arrived off the red-eye from the USA so were there very early. They kept our luggage while we toured and waited for the room to be made up. The room was small but not overly so. There was storage and a small desk. Also a small balcony facing the plaza. The bathroom was more than adequate. The room was spotless. Wi-Fi worked very well. The beds were comfortable. Staff were extremely helpful and friendly. There was no breakfast or restaurant but tons of places in the immediate vicinity. The only downside was the night noise, especially on Friday and Saturday. Plaza del Carmen has some "nightlife" and people were out and about way past midnight. Earplugs are a must.

author: Aurora03
title: No frills hotel in a fantastic location at a great price!
text: Ditto to everything others have said - fantastic location, clean rooms, real bathrooms (unlike little four square feet cubicles you sometimes find in Europe for bathrooms), and really cheap prices. When we travel anywhere, especially in Europe, the location of the hotel is the most important thing along with safety and cleanliness and then we try to balance the budget. We were staying in five different hotels in five different cities/towns in Spain on our recent trip (just got back 4 days ago) with the longest stay of 5 nights in Madrid. This hotel fit the bill for location and the cost trumped everything else in deciding to stay here. Of course good reviews here were necessary to make that choice. We had a triple room with 3 single beds and a small balcony overlooking the small square - Plaza Carmen. One of the beds was a hard and a little uncomfortable but my daughter didn't mind. A full size marble bathroom is a luxury in Europe. Small refrigerator in the room was really helpful to store water bottles etc. as it was quite hot when we were there. Hotels this size and price don't usually have refrigerators so it was a pleasant addition. Free wifi is pretty standard everywhere now but again for the price it is appreciated. There was no noise if the balcony door was closed completely and AC was on. Staff was responsive in answering questions but not particularly friendly or jovial. As others have said, this is a very basic hotel best served as a place to sleep in a great location at a great price. Minimum continental breakfast of croissant and coffee even if we have to pay for it would make it convenient to start the day of site seeing.

author: duggem
title: Solid Budget Choice
text: This small hostal (hotel in Spain) is located on the 4th floor of a classic old building just a block off of Gran Via, the main drag in Madrid. It has a small lift. It is about 5 minutes from the Gran Via metro station and about 10 from Sol, the main square. The main train station is a couple metro stops away (as is the Prado). Royal Palace is a short walk. Rooms are quaint and fairly small, but adequate. Staff is very helpful. Beds and bath were fine. A couple of issues: The walls are quite thin so it is easy to hear your neighbor. The room has a small balcony overlooking a lovely plaza, but it can be noisy at night. This is not a problem if you close the window. However, it was warm enough when we were there that the room became stuffy. Yet is was not summer so the A/C was not turned on. So we either could leave the balcony window open to the street noise or suffer a warm room. Nevertheless, a solid budget choice with a great location in Madrid. And they alway kept the chocolate jar full in the lobby! No breakfast.

author: 275deepaka
title: A lovely, superfriendly and convenient place
text: We stayed in Madrid for a few nights in November of 2014. If I had to sum up our stay at Javier's place in 2 words, it would be: AWESOME & CONVENIENT! Right from the time of making a reservation till the time of departure, we had only positive experiences with Javier and his team at Hostal Acapulco. Javier's responses while making the reservation were timely, clear and extremely helpful. When we arrived, his brother Jose Luis was super-friendly and helpful in first getting our car parked and then informing us about the city in general and the sights. The room we stayed in was pretty nice. The location of the place is so convenient. Within a few minutes of walk, you have all the hip and cool places within Madrid. Once we had parked our car, we didn't need it for the rest of 3 days! When the time came to leave, I was amazed to see how caring and thoughtful they all were. Jose Luis had already made arrangements for getting our car back from the parking! He even brought the car back from the valet (although he didn't have to do it). We will certainly stay at their place again, when we visit Madrid. Thanks, Javier, Jose Luis and your entire team! :)

author: Woodhenge
title: Do Not Confuse Hostal with Hostel
text: The two of us stayed 5 nights in February. Booked online via website, good feedback via e-mail with advice on arrival from airport etc. Two changes on metro are needed but hotel is close to 2 or 3 stops. Hotel is very central near Sol and mant sites are walkable form here. Place is on the 4th floor with a small elevator, staff are present 24/7 and are helpful and speak reasonable English. As we stayed for more than 3 nights they did our laundry for us at no charge (hand in one day, delivered back the next). They also let us leave a bag in a locked closet when we went to Barcelona for 5 days before returning to Madrid for one night. They sell cold beer and sodas at reception. Rooms are spotless but basic. Towels are not big and fluffy but there was plenty of hot water. They provide basic toiletries which I was not expecting at these prices. Blackout blinds reduce light and noise. I am a light sleeper but did not have issues. Rooms away from street are quieter but have a view of a brick wall. Wall heater/AC takes a few moments to kick in so be patient. Once it's on it does a good job of warming the roomFloors are marble tile which make them cold in winter but very nice and cool in summer I would think. Would stay here again with no hesitation. Do not confuse a Hostal with a Hostel this is a real hotel, albeit a basic one. Great value for a safe, central location.

author: jolem11
title: Absolutely outstanding
text: There is nothing better than feeling at home. And Javier made it possible. Everything was perfect. EVERYTHING. Of course, taking into consideration that you go to a Hostal (do not confuse with Hostel, which normally has bunk beds, and you might as well have to share rooms and/or bathrooms with other people), the services provided there were completely impeccable. Take this advice as a rule: If you go to Madrid for touring, go to this hostal. After a long day of walking around the city and taking pictures, or enjoying the beautiful weather while having some tapas, all you need is a warm shower and a comfortable bed. Rooms + Sleep Quality + Cleanliness: 5 stars. Free internet and printing service are available, so if you need to do an online check-in and print your boarding passes, I'll have you known you are able to do it here. Plus, there is Wi-Fi, as well. Service: 5 stars. Locationwise, it's literally 3 minutes to Puerta del Sol and 1 minute to Gran Vía. Several Metro stations surround the area, restaurants all over the place, as well as the main national touristic places. Location: 5 stars. Last, but not least, the price. Basically, having this location, this service, and this added value that Javier grants to your experience, I'd reckon this is priceless. 5 stars OVERALL. Javier, please, I beg you, DO NOT CHANGE. Cheers and see you soon, Joel

author: mumontherun09
title: Lots of character and a fantastic location.
text: We were promised a room with a balcony overlooking a quiet plaza in the centre of Madrid and that's exactly what we had. The hotel comprises the fourth floor of quite an elegant old building - just going up in the lift takes you to another time and place. The beds were comfortable - latex mattresses, I think - and our air conditioned room was airy and light. The bathroom was cramped but very clean, everything worked and the water was hot. The wifi was excellent and we could print out tickets etc from the computer in the lobby. The staff were very efficient and helpful - for example in making a booking for us to go to a flamenco and giving directions. When we stepped outside the front door we were just a few minutes away from Gran Via, Sol and Plaza Mayor. Walking the city was easy and a great pleasure. We didn't need to use them but taxis were just meters down the road. There's are restaurants and bars in Salud and in Plaza del Carmen just at the front door - great for a drink or a meal but not open for breakfast. The place for that is just next door, on the right as you exit the building. Took us a while to notice this place but it's really good. Just wish I could remember its name. Ask Javier - he's sure to know. When we're next in Madrid, we'll be staying at Hostal Acapulco.

author: efsch
title: Great central location, nice rooms, friendly staff, reasonable prices
text: (Remember that in Spain “hostal” refers to a small hotel, not a youth hostel.) Hostal Acapulco is centrally located, between the Gran Via and Puerta del Sol (km 0 for all of Spain) metro stations. It is on the quiet Plaza del Carmen, but only 3 minutes in either direction to Madrid’s main shopping streets. It is a safe area, excellent for transportation connections, shopping, and people watching (especially during the evening promenade). To get to the hostal from the MAD (Barajas) airport on the metro takes two changes of subway lines, but it is easy if you do not have too much baggage (there are stairs in some stations). Be aware that some subway cars have station listings for several different lines, so if the listing in your car does not match the line you think you are on, do not worry. A transit pass is very useful for metro and bus routes all over the city, and is a bargain if you take several trips a day. Unfortunately there are no bus maps of the city, but the local tourist information offices can point out some of the most useful bus routes -- a great way to sightsee. As always on public transportation in Europe, watch out for pickpockets (I had no problems). The hostal staff is very helpful, even by email, and they will give you directions and answer any of your questions. The hostal is quite small, taking up the 4th floor of a multi-hostal building. There is a caged elevator so stairs are not a problem unless someone has forgotten to close the cage door when leaving. Rooms are basic but comfortable, with an empty mini-fridge for snacks. El Corte Ingles, the large Spanish department store chain, is 5 minutes away near Puerta del Sol and has a large grocery in its basement. The hostal has no breakfast service, so ECI is very useful. For sightseeing, I strongly recommend the current editions of Rick Steves guides. They are well worth in investment and will save you time and money. I spent several days at the Acapulco, and will happily stay there again on my next trip to Madrid. I hope this is useful. Enjoy your trip!

author: aclarinet
title: Location, location, location
text: You know the old real estate adage about location? Well, Hostal Acapulco is dead center for walking EVERYWHERE in the old town! Javier is blindingly fast with replying to any questions or giving advice that you may need. Even though we didn't meet in person, because he was at a conference, I felt welcome before arriving. I like to travel as much like a local as possible, and the transportation options in Madrid are great and very close to Hostal Acapulco - you can get most anywhere in no time~ The room is spacious by European standards - with a mini-fridge in the room. a nice, functional lift (it's on the 4th floor). The Wifi - is FANTASTIC . . . they also have a guest computer in the lobby. We loved the local food - Abrasador across the street and RESTAURANTE VEGETARIANO ARTEMISA Sol Gran Vía was so amazing we went TWICE!! Also - not to be missed is Casa Alberto - casaalberto.es We felt safe and secure in this clean central location and even though there is no breakfast, you will NOT go hungry in Madrid! Beds and pillows are great - there's a remote for the heat/ac, and tv (parents please monitor channels as we had some "surprise" skin shows) Can't say enough about the extra kindness and help from Javier for the first time traveler to Madrid - his tip for the Paseo de Arte pass was to buy it at the lesser used (but fabulous) Museo Thyssen . . . and he was spot on~ Thanks

author: orchid55
title: 4 star quality at 3 star price
text: Recently we stayed at Hostal Acapulco for two nights on our first trip to Madrid. I can't say enough about how good and comfortable our stay was. First of all I chose this hostel after reading reviews and made the booking by email. Javier who communicated with me gave us very clear directions as to how to get to the hostel from the airport. Based on this info we put some of our luggage at the airport storage locker & took the airport bus paying just 2 euros each. We got off at the third stop and just walked to the hostel which was pretty easy to find. The hostel is just off Gran Via in the best location. We didn't get to meet Javier but his brother I think who was at the reception received us and showed us the room. The room was really lovely with three beds even though we were only 2 had a balcony from where we could see all the little stalls in the square outside. The bathroom was spotlessly clean with all the toiletries, towels etc like in a 4 star hotel, the room was well furnished with lovely rugs on the floor, a plasma tv, fridge etc. The location was simply fantastic. We could just walk around and do a lot of shopping in just one day. Before doing that we booked the hop on hop off bus and did the two blue and green line trips just to get our bearings of the city. We bought the tickets online paying only 15 euros each instead of 20 euros. Plenty of eating places around the hostel. Our stay was great because of which we enjoyed our short trip to Madrid. Would definitely recommend it and would definitely stay there if we went there again.

author: cutandsew
title: Service extended even before we got there
text: This place sure stood out before we even got there. Even when we were a continent away, Javier helped us with our AVE train reservations for Sevilla that I was concerned with being a Semana Santa Week. He also will send you directions on how to get to the hostal, and that makes it easy to find. We chose the subway from the airport as we only had our carry-on luggage to roll around. Use the elevators if the heights of the escalators in the subway bother you! The exit is Puerta del Sol and you just head to your right to find Calle del Carmen which will lead you to the Plaza del Carmen and the hostal is across it. We stayed here for 2 nights before we travelled on to Sevilla and another 2 nights after. The front desk clerks spoke English very well, are very courteous and helpful with how to see Madrid (they have free xeroxed copies of the main part of the city). All the major landmarks are within walking distance of this hostal that we will surely come back and highly recommend the place. It has free internet usage which my travel companion readily used. The rooms we stayed in were very clean, beds are comfortable and the bathrooms were very clean also and you are given toothbrushes and toothpaste just in case you forgot yours! The rooms had a small refrigerator where you can store drinks and other quick snacks. For a reasonable price you can buy drinks from the front desk clerk. If you are a light sleeper you might ask for a room away from the street as it is in front of a plaza, and the garbage collectors come early in the morning. We liked the rooms by the street because it had a small terrace that looks into the plaza.There is also a nice restaurant with good food and service, and at a reasonable price, 2 doors away down the street. And if you are into ballroom dancing, there is a club next door to the restaurant that you could go to. We felt safe here as during the evening the entrance door can only be opened by the clerk thru a buzzer. Oue stay here helped us enjoy Madrid to the fullest!

author: shoegazer
title: Mediocre
text: I had chosen this hostal based on all the positive reviews on this site, but for the first time I felt I could not rely on the rating here on Tripadvisor. Positives were: - Location (smack bang in the centre, walking distance to all the attractions/areas) - Price (good value for Madrid) Negatives: - I found the staff at the front desk uncommunicative and not very friendly. If you don't say hello to them, they won't say anything to you. I did not get to meet Javier, which is a shame because in his emails he seemed very friendly and helpful. - The front door of the building is locked at siesta time (around midday to 3pm) and between the hours of 10pm and 9am. We found this quite an inconvenience to be honest, because you had to ring the bell each time you were coming in. At night it seemed like whoever was buzzing the door for us was getting annoyed. We were almost feeling guilty about coming back late at night, but Madrid is a city where people don't even eat dinner until around 11pm, let alone have drinks or go out to bars and clubs. - Cleanliness. The room was extremely clean on day 1, but for the following three days, it felt like they were just making the bed and not cleaning the room or giving us any clean towels. There was a stain on the pillow case and there were hairs on the floor. - The computer at reception was usually occupied by some person playing Solitaire. We had iPhones with us but the hotel's WiFi often did not work. - Last but not least, we were subjected to Whitney Houston at ear-splitting volume EVERY single morning! All in all, it was a disappointing experience.

author: biryani_lover
title: One of our best travel experiences
text: I cannot say enough good things about Hostal Acapulco. My family were stranded in Madrid due to the volcanic ash cloud and we were lucky to get a last minute room at this establishment. We were able to do this with an English speaking receptionist over the telephone at the airport. Upon our arrival (and subsequently each time we passed the front desk), we were warmly greeted. No matter who was working, the host or hostess was always very kind and had a smiling hello for our two year old. When we explained our situation, they offered us a triple at 79 euros/night (a great last minute deal) and unbelievably, did our laundry for free. Yes, free. They could have easily taken advantage of us, but instead took us in and helped us out. In a world where we are bombarded by news of crooks and swindlers, this fine place sets a fine example of how businesses should treat their customers. The room itself was comfortable and nicely located on the Plaza Carmen, just a few minutes from Puerto del Sol and a number of subway stations. There are a ton of good restaurants nearby as well - including one pricey but amazing Argentinian steak house. The hotel is on the fourth floor of the building, but has easy elevator access. They also sell cold sodas and water at the desk, so you don't have to go out late at night if you are parched. There was free internet (WIFI) in the room and cheap printing at front desk. If we ever go back to Madrid, we will be staying at this hotel again.

author: pricegals
title: All the ammenities but not the warmth
text: When we first arrived, I was all excited to meet Javier and get the low down on Madrid. Instead, we were greeted (NOT) by a stern woman who was not helpful at all. I really have no idea how much English she spoke but if she spoke it, she sure didn't want to use it. She opened the door to our room and I thought, oh no, what have I gotten myself into, the room was tiny and dreary. Things perked up when there was a shift change and we met Marco who came on at 4 PM. He spoke English and was quite helpful. He helped me secure tickets to an Atletico Madrid soccer game which could only be navigated in Spanish. Kuddos to Marco. The end result, the room was fine, the beds were fine, the location was great, 24 hour access to a modern computer, the AC was fabulous and the shower was to die for!!! Of the 3 places that we stayed in Spain, this was by far the best, quite a value for 59 euros. As for Javier, never did meet him. As for the Puerto Rican restaurant that several people raved about, we were not impressed. It was not PR, it was Spanish. The waiter overcharged us for our meal and when I questioned him, he blew us off. However, the Sangria was indeed good. I can recommend a fabulous (and I do mean fabulous) Argentinian restaurant on one of the corners of Plaza de Sol called Le Mario. We split a chorizo appetizer (served with french bread and 2 wonderful sauces), lemonade slush with cava and a plate of broccoli (steamed, we were dying for veggies after 8 days in Spain) and potatoes all for 13,5 euros. We were full and happy when we walked out. The place was clean as a whistle, well priced and wonderful.

author: Krzlioness
title: You must stay here!
text: We had heard about the Acapulco through some coworkers and even though we were not very sure what we would find (after reading all those horror stories). When we got to the location we were a bit unsure especially when we had to get on a 1900 style elevator that fits only one person and a piece of luggage. Wow to our surprise the personnel was awesome! They were very friendly the reception area small but very cozy. We were taken to our rooms and to our surprise -yet again- the room was nice and clean, it had a balcony, there was plenty of room to walk around - there were three girls in this room and we still had room for luggage, stretching and keep clutter out of the way. The bathroom was big! Shower with tub, plenty of room to use toilet and sink. Again the staff was welcoming, willing to help and gave us great tips, where to go what to avoid, what to bring with us and what should stay in the hotel for our safety. -oh yeah they had a safe in every room. The best advice we got from every front desk person was to go to the Puerto Rico Restaurant around the corner...it was THE BEST and can not wait to go back there. There were two waiters...one very sweet the other kind of grumpy looking but very sweet - if you spoke the language. The food was great, AHHHHHH the SANGRIA is to die for we had at least one pitcher every time we were there...some times two and only because it was late and we HAD to go to sleep. The Acapulco and Puerto Rico are situated in the heart of Madrid. We walked all over the place, the Corte Ingles, Museo del Prado, La Puerta de Alcala, El Parque del Retiro, La Plaza Mayor, Gran Via but if you do not wish to walk that much there are taxi services outside the hotel or around the corner and the metro is a short walk away. We felt very safe and we were out at 1, 2 or 3 in the morning! The front rooms could bring in the outside noise but the comfort is worth it. Last minute booking is not recommended but you could try. We stayed here when we arrived and return here when we departed (Visited Madrid, Toledo, Paris, Venice, Florence and Rome) out of all our rooms this was by far the best.

author: mplsfamily
title: Great staff, great location
text: Hostal Alcapulco was a great place to stay. It is completely charming and the staff is warm and friendly. They were nice enough to speak English (probably because they couldn't stand our Spanish!) and helped us find good places for dinner. We had two rooms, one with a double bed and a single bed, and the other with 3 triple beds. The triple room had a nice balcony with a good view. The room was a good size with plenty of room to walk around. The double bed room was smaller and had no view but met our needs. My hairdryer broke the first day and the staff had one that I could use during our stay. They have free internet in the lobby which was helpful when we wanted to find info on where to go or directions. We took a shuttle from the airport (go to ground transportation at the airport. We didn't have a reservation and they had a van for us in 5 minutes. 46 euros for 6 people) and the driver knew right where the hostal was. The kids got a kick out of the old fashioned elevator even though it was so small that we usually ended up taking the stairs. The location is fabulous. Just a couple minutes walk to 2 different metro stops although we rarely needed the metro since we were in the heart of the ciy. Just two blocks away was the giant department store, El Corte Ingles. The bottom level is a grocery store and we were able to stock up on gluten free snacks for our kids. We were also a 15 minute walk from the restaurant Da Nicola which had an extensive gluten free menu. I would definately recomment Hostal Acapulco for a budget minded traveler to Madrid.

author: DonNewYorkCity
title: Acapulco Is A Gem!
text: We stayed at the Hostal Acapulco in Madrid for over a week (after reading the great reviews on Trip Advisor). The Hotel will not disappoint. Javier is friendly (even before we arrived in Spain, he provided me with directions for the metro - subway to hostal - and boy was he accurate!) The Hostal has the three "C's" - CLEAN, CENTRALLY LOCATED, AND CHEAP. The rooms, while not large, are spotless. The bathrooms are modern and clean. (Rooms have cute balconies!) The rooms have a little refrigerator ...which is perfect, since there is a Cortes Ingles (supermarket, in the basement of the store) literally down the street. You can buy food and save a little on some meals. The location truly is PERFECT...walking distance to everything - from the great Museums, to the Palace, metro around the corner for any longer trips (to the zoo for instance). Yes, there is noise in Madrid, but the windows when shut, siphon it out. One night we could hear the people in the room next to us, but every other night it was quiet. You will use a FUN elevator when you arrive, and take it up to the higher floor where the Hostal is located. It's a riot. The older gentlemen (midnight to early morning shift) does not speak English, so if you don't speak Spanish (and I don't) you can simply settle your bill the night before you check out. Easy. You cannot beat the price, or location when staying in Madrid. Clean, comfortable and inexpensive. We will stay there again when returning to Madrid.

author: jobabes
title: Clean Room, Noisey but a great deal
text: For the price it was above average. The rooms were clean and of good size. They had the best shower - hot water and strong. We had a mini fridge, large closet, balcony and TV. The staff was very helpful. Javier responded to any question I had prior to booking the room. The room was nothing fancy but definetly a good deal and you did not feel uncomfortable or unsafe for a hostal. The room overlooked a square and it was loud. Do not expect to sleep before 1am. You can close the shutters but then you'll need to use the AC. Happily they have an AC. The old elevator was a hoot. One has to close the wood/glass doors and then the iron gate. Free internet. Great deal for the price. Centrally located to all.

author: Jeannegirl
title: Great location
text: We stayed at this hostal for 3 nights. Since it was called a hostal we thought it might be like a youth hostal but it was far from this. It was a 3* hotel. It gets the word hostal because it does not have a street frontage. After ringing the bell, someone opens the door and you take the antiquated elevator to the 4th floor. providing the last person out of it closed both doors. The rate was 55E and for Madrid this was a great rate considering it is one block off the main street of Gran Via in the center of town and quiet as well. Breakfast is not available here but we went to the store and bought juice, fruit and pastry and put it in the supplied refrigerator. Javier was most helpful at the front desk. It also had free internet. in the lobby. It is one block from the Gran Via Metro. My advise is to not ride the Metro with your suitcases as we were a group of 4 and pickpocketers were at work on us. Someone was in my purse, luckily I stopped the hand from taking anything. One person in our group got his wallet taken from a zipper pocket on his leg and his camera taken from the bottom of his backpack. We did use the Metro when we were in Madrid but again don't use it for traveling with your suitcases as you are a target and they work in groups, especially if it is crowded, you will get pick pocketed. We are experienced travelers and it seemed like there was nothing we could do as the train was overpacked and lots of shoving went on. Take the airport shuttle to the last stop at the Metro and then take a taxi and you will be safe. Use the taxi with the red stripe on it.

author: errant
title: Great value, great people
text: I really liked the Hostal Acapulco. It is central to EVERYTHING -- you can't beat the location. It is clean. Yeah, it's spartan but you're not paying for the Ritz. It is safe. I had no problem with the concept of leaving stuff in my room. The people are wonderful. As many have written, Javier and Ana are the kindest, most thoughtful people. They go out of their way to help you out. My only complaint was the ambient noise outside. Madrid is a noisy city. You don't go there for a good night's sleep, that's for sure. But that's not the Hostal Acalpulco's fault. Value for money? You bet. I'd highly recommend it. Clean, safe, reasonably priced accommodation in the heart of Madrid? This place offers it.

author: madridtripper
title: Central Locale, Friendly Staff
text: LOCATION: Excellent. The nearest metro stop, Gran Via, is just 2-3 minutes' walk. Other nearby metro stops were Callao and Sol (both ~5 minutes' walk). A ton of restaurants and shops are within 5 minutes' walk, including tapas bars, a Starbucks, McDonald's, Zara, El Cortes Ingles, etc. SERVICE: This is a family-run establishment and everyone was friendly and helpful. They even sent me an email before I arrived telling me how to get to the Hostal from the airport and that I shouldn't change money at the airport because high commissions are charged there. However, some of the staff members' English is pretty basic, so save your really complicated questions for the internet. ROOMS: I stayed in 2 rooms during the week-long stay. Both were very similar. Very clean but basic. The air conditioning in one room smelled like urine (common, I guess). The hot water also stopped working in this same room a few days after I checked in. INTERNET: Free access via a terminal in the lobby. Not sure about wireless for laptops, but I did see one guy who was using his laptop in the lobby, so wireless may have been available and free as well. NOISE: No outside noise seeps in, but you will hear people walking down halls and opening and closing doors. Also, you will hear the conversations of others from rooms near yours. TV: Only Spanish channels are offered. MISC: Lots of guidebooks and magazines are available in the lobby for you to peruse (e.g., Rick Steves', Frommers, and Michelin guidebooks).

author: dcnative
title: Great Value in Madrid
text: I was a little nervous staying at the Hostal Acapulco as I had incredible difficultly making the initial reservation. Via the Internet, I received friendly emails from Javier telling me space was available. But when I called, I was told nothing was available and was hung up on (3x). But being persistent paid off. Javier promised that the room would be available and ready when we arrived--and he didn't ask me to provide a credit card to hold the room. Of course, I was the skeptical traveller so I hedged my bet with an alternative reservation at the Hotel Plaza Mayor. Before leaving Barcelona, I called the Hostal Acapulco, confirmed my room and canceled my other reservation. It was the right decision. The difference in price between the hotels was 20+EUR/night. While Plaza Mayor was in a more quaint area, Acapulco's location was very central. The A/C worked well and kept away the fish smell from the fish store on street level. We actually enjoyed the Spanish TV, using our rudimentary language skills to learn more about a big murder case that was gripping Spain (the accused was a young and good looking flamenco dancer). Getting to the internet access took persistence as there were a lot of teenagers traveling with their families but that wasn't an issue. There was an elevator which made it easier after a long hot day of walking. And the best find of all was an amazing vegetarian restaurant within 10 steps (Artemesia). It's out the hotel, across the little plaza to the next ajoining road, and hang a left toward Grand Via. I'm not vegetarian but my traveling companion was and I suggested going back a second time. It was that good (and there are a couple chicken dishes for those inclined). For those looking for a clean, comfortable room at a good price, I would recommend this hotel.

author: 306rp
title: Excellent location, good facilities with very few nags
text: Excellent location. Less than 5 mins walk to the St. Mark's square, the key tourist attraction in the town. And about 10 mins walk to the Realto Bridge, another tourist puller. Finding the hotel just before midnight wasn't easy, but that is true for any place in Venice if you are visiting first time. With the help of Google map and a restaurant staff nearby, we arrived without great difficulty. Were lucky to find a staff at reception, but otherwise the protocol is that we should call their sister hotel. However he let us in and gave keys to the room in this same hotel. Room was clean and looked recently renovated. Over next 3 days it got cleaned and beds made every day. My only complaint is that they kept taking our basin soap away and replacing it with a sealed one every day! What a waste. Please give option to guests if they would like to reuse their opened soap and towels. Breakfast was good too. Available between 7am and 10am, it offered good selection of apricot croissants, rolls, cereals, biscotti, jams with hot tea/coffee. Other things I would have liked is a kettle and tea/coffee kit, and drinking water. Not a big deal but would have been a good finish over an already pleasant stay.

author: I9157NPmarias
title: Wonderful location- and not much else
text: Don't be fooled- it's situation is wonderful, but it's devilishly hard to find the first (and even the 10th time). You had better ask the nearby shops for the exact location of the entrance. On the comodities it's an average hotel, with furniture that shows its age but well-cared for. Some stains and such. We asked for a double bed, got two joined twins instead. There are no black-out curtains, only thin ones and small portico-like doors at the windows to cover some of the light, but hardly all of it, and the ones at the bathroom were in a very poor state. The Wi-Fi was okay. There is music in the halls and corridors all day from the audio system, which may be a bit annoying but will not be a big nuisance if you come back for a midday nap (at least, not for us). It is NOT worth its full price- get it with a considerable discount or you will be sorely disappointed. The recepetion is hardly 24 hours, and you are informed so upon arrival. They allow you to leave your baggage at reception if you arrive too early for sign in. Paolo was wonderful, but I can't say the same for the rest of the staff we met. We had a medical emergency and couldn't leave our room- upon asked for a call-in doctor's number, or to ring in the hospital for us- my partner was sent back to our room with the name and number of one of the hospitals (when we called no one spoke anything other than Italian). Ended up trying to get to the hospital by foot, and collapsed not half a street away from the door (got an aquatic ambulance called in by a pizza-by-the-slice place next to the hotel, who were wonderful to us, give them a shot!). Other than that: literally all main attractions are within walking distance, as well as a couple of supermarkets, convenience stores, restaurants and the likes. I can't speak for the most expensive rooms, but if you don't mind average accomodations and are looking for a good location AND get a big discount, I say go for it.

author: hrdmapl
title: Not at all impressed with customer service
text: If I could give this place a 0 rating I would. I booked it for a stay in about 10 days (late March). I booked through booking.com. I received a notice that there was a problem with my credit card, so I resubmitted my information. I then received a note that the information was ok. I naively thought all was good....until yesterday morning I received an email from the hotel that my reservation had been cancelled. Thankfully I was not en route to Venice expecting to arrive and stay there last night. I called booking.com and the agent took my information. He called the hotel. They said the reservation was cancelled, but could not tell him why. He asked if the reservation could be reinstated...the answer was no. If I wanted to stay there I would have to rebook at the current rate which was roughly double what I had planned to pay in the original reservation. The agent at booking.com found me comparable accommodation, with a better rating, at a similar price to the original booking. I am not at all impressed with the way this matter was handled by Hotel Citta di Milano. I share this as due warning to others so they will not experience similar. Definitely business practices and customer service at this establishment could improve.

author: lorreg77
title: Wonderful find in the heart of Venice!
text: The reviews worried me a bit about this hotel, but the location was great and the price was in our budget, so I took a leap of faith. Thankfully, my faith paid off. This was a quiet, small hotel with rooms that were larger than expected and a staff that offered wonderful suggestions for restaurants and gondola rides. They also had free wi-fi and breakfast. My family had one bedroom with four adults and one bedroom with three adults, and did not feel cramped at all. Do not listen to the porters at the water boats, the hotel is easily within walking distance of San Marco station - even my older parents managed the walk with suitcases. We would not have found the hotel without directions posted by other readers, so I am posting them again. Print them out! We had no problem locating the hotel! Take the water bus to San Marco. Walk through the San Marco piazza and under the blue clock arch. Continue straight until you see a yellow sign on a wall saying "Per Rialto" with an arrow pointing right. Turn right. When you reach the doors of the church, turn left and enter a little alley at the church. This alley takes you to a piazza with a well in the middle. Cross the piazza diagonally and walk down the alley beside the restaurant. Immediately turn left and left again (more small alleys), and the hotel entrance will be on your left.

author: Emilylouise145
title: Will stay again if in Venice!
text: I was worried about coming to the hotel after reading reviews. I informed the hotel about our late arrival in the evening and they said it would be no issue as there was a night porter around - which there was and he was very welcoming to us. He also gave us a map of the city. I can see how the hotel is a little difficult to find as there is a lot of small streets, but we used google maps on our phone and didn't have any difficulty. It is about a 5/10 min walk from Rialto water bus stop. We stayed for 3 nights at the hotel, and it was perfect for everything we wanted! Somewhere to sleep and a shower. Don't understand why people moan about the size of the room, you go away to see a different city not stare at a tv or walls in your room?! And it was a perfect size for our stay. Every staff member came across as friendly and welcoming, always saying hello and asking if we had a good day. The breakfast was simple and basic, but plentiful. The lady also makes a lovely coffee! All in all, I'd say don't judge a book by its cover.. Make your own judgment. I enjoyed our stay at the hotel, and we will definitely be back if we are ever in Venice again!!!

author: nicklyt
title: A bad option
text: The hotel is not 3 stars. We had a superior double room but we could not spend much time in the room because : a. the ambiance is very dull. Room decoration is very glum and the rooms not bright b. there is no insulation. You could here everything form adjoining rooms or the rooms on next floor. You could also stay awake due to the traffic from the busy streets outside c. the shutters from windows could not close, hence the morning light could wake you up from 6am. Although we booked for two nights, we left the second day, even though we had prepaid the entire staying. Could not stay there any longer! Cleanliness was ok, but the beds had not a duvet, but a blanket ! I doubt whether it is washed frequently. We also had requested a double room, and we were given a twin - the receptionist said that all rooms have single beds only! The only good thing with the room was its size (about 20 sq.m., which is good by the venice standards) Breakfast was very basic, even less than what you would expect from a budget hotel. Staff was ok - not rude but not very helpful. Finally, the hotel is hard to find - and if you are carrying suitcases, this is a nightmare! The only good thing about this hotel is its location - a 3min walk to St Marco square. In a nutshell - book this hotel if you want to be close to St Mark square and you are a budget traveler. Avoid if you are a couple and want some romance or if you are a family with kids and need some comfort.

author: adrialvarez
title: ***AVOID***
text: Dont go, you will be played. We booked the hotel via hotels.com at 12md and we arrived at 4pm... it was super hard to find, even with google maps. Once we did, the guy said our room was "outside" and asked us to follow him and we did, for about 100mts to another hotel, the Antica Panada. They did the check in and then drag us througj a laberint of floors and elevators and several buildings until we arrived to our "suite". The A/C was not working, TV broken, and a paper blocking the sun from the window in the roof fallen. I then went on to read the reviews on tripadvisor and hotels.com and it seems is very often that customers get switched from Cittá di Milano to Pananda because they belong to the same group.... so curios as I am i went on to check the prices and what a surpise!!! You pay the expensive one €134 per night... and you sleep at the cheap one, €83! We went to the reception and they said "that is normal", if a hotel is overbooked they switch you! we said that we booked it 4 hours in advanced! but they insisted it was normal. We asked for a refund on the difference and day say it was not possible, nor a change of rooms as they are fully booked. We ended up callinf hotels,com who refunded us the difference and canceled the extra night we had booked as we did not like what happened. So, avoid!!!!

author: Bee2109
title: Good location
text: Originally we were scheduled to arrive at the hotel at midnight. I'm glad we didn't get there until the next morning ... because even having been to Venice 3 times previously and knowing the area where the hotel was, there is NO WAY we would have found this in the dark. We really struggled the next day in the light and that was with sat nav, a map and previous knowledge! It took us ages!! When we got to the hotel we were told there was a flood and we would need to go to the Antico Pananda instead. Initially I was pleased because I'd stayed at the Antico Pananda before and once we insisted on a room as per the hotel photos (we were first put in a "sister hotel") it was gorgeous. Not this time! Again we were put in one of the sister hotels - it was so dire I refused to stay. Nothing like the pictures (or the Antico Pananda I'd stayed at before). We then got shown to two further rooms and not wanting to waste any more holiday time settled on the second room. It was ok, but dark and so hot because the air con didn't work. We made the mistake of opening the windowns at night to let some air in ... 50 mosquito bites later, we didn't do this again! The bathroom was lovely and the breakfast was nice enough and the hotel was well situated for us, being right in the heart of the St Mark's area. If the air con had worked it would have been sufficient. If it had been like the picture ... it would have been fantastic!

author: Coffpau
title: Perfect location
text: Myself and my wife have just returned from a 4 night stay in this hotel. It was everything the website said it was. The air con worked, bathroom was big with jacuzzi bath etc etc. The bedroom was smallish but very adequate and it is Venice afterall !! The staff were friendly and helpful. The breakfast was ok, pre packed croissants, cheese breadrolls, cereal, juice, tea, coffee. The restaurant in the square beside the hotel was excellent and resonably priced. The location is perfect. It is literally 3 minutes from San Marks square and 5 minutes from Rialto bridge. I would recommend this hotel to anyone. As a sub note.. Beware of the mosquitoes. If possible bring a net so you can sleep at night, also The tour to Murano Torcello and Burano with Ililaguna tours is not worth the money. You only get 45 minutes at each stop. On Murano you will see a glass blower making a horse and then you will see the shop and that is it. On Torcello there is nothing to see even and On Burano there is plenty to see but no time. You can get the vapporetto to Burano for €7 and spend a few hours there. Far better value. Also the service from IliLaguna is terrible and the guides are very poor ( in my opinion ).We loved Venice !!!!!

author: travelmyh0bby
title: great location, but...
text: In total I liked that hotel, although not everything about it was very good. But starting from the positive points: you have a great location. Few steps away from the famous st marc square, as well as from the bridge rialto. Not easy to find this hotel, so you better keep in mind how does it look on the photo which you see on this website. We finally asked a staff from this restaurant which you also see, because the entrance to the hotel is quite hidden, but Venice is like this ;) I liked also our room, feeling a bit like in a queen room. The great surprise was waiting in the bathroom: bath with jacuzzi. I don't know if you find it in every room. I booked just a double room not some superior one, so we were really nicely surprised. Maybe after renovation they furnished each room with jacuzzi...? About the bad points: no lift - for us not a problem, but maybe for somebody else it would be. Breakfast: one of the worst you can imagine. Nothing fresh, packed croissants (disgusting), basic corn flakes, packed biscuits and that's all. I don't know about wifi. Once I asked at the reception but the lady didn't really speak English so finally I have no idea. But in Venice you will find many restaurants with free wifi. So when I forget about the horrible breakfast, everything else was really OK. The price was quite high but when I was searching for a room in Venice I found some with shared bathroon which were even more expensive (100€) so the one we got (less than 90€) and with private jacuzzi was really worth.

author: xtenkfarpl
title: good location, otherwise just adequate
text: It's approximately between St Marks square and the Rialto Bridge, about 5 minutes to either. Easy enough to find: use the directions on their website. It's just off San Zulian square, which may be the easiest landmark to locate on a map. Room was quite large. Room, bedding and bathroom were adequately clean. Cons. No elevator: would be a deal-killer for anyone with mobility problems, obviously. Apparently some rooms don't have AC. However, while there WAS an AC unit in our room, even on its highest setting it only produced a barely perceptible sigh of air. Wasn't a problem for us in October, but I wouldn't put any faith in its ability to deal with real summer temperatures. Water pressure was barely adequate, and for a time one evening there was no hot water. It was an adequate base for a first-time visit, but price seemed rather high for what you get, even allowing for the fact that it's central Venice. On any future Venice trip I would economize by looking for better value somewhere less central, especially now that I've figured out that the vaporetto system is fairly simple to use. (Tip: buy a multi-day ticket rather than individual trips: it will rapidly pay off. Don't even THINK about the water-taxis unless you're Bill Gates)!

author: HunterDanny
title: This hotel sucks!
text: Was there for a night in June. Booked with expedia. Services are bad. I agree with most review here. No Aircon! A lots of mosquito and we are feeding them. Counter services sucks! Breakfast was terrible! The prepacked foods are not palatable at all! Not even a good fan. We were given a small century old fan which I can't feel the breeze at all! Pls don't stay here. Another Chinese customer from France actually knock into my door to compliant about the room! They book through booking.com. All written condition like aircon were not the actual services provided.

author: TashaAust
title: Absolute rubbish!
text: We agree with most comments of other Advisors; this hotel sucks. While it is situated in a great spot, that's about all it has going for it. The management are woeful, with barely the charm to muster a smile. Our air con didn't work. They didn't care. Our bathroom was on a noticeable slant with a big leak covered by towels. They didn't care. The toilet seat was broken, to the point where I slipped off and almost cracked my head. They didn't care. The breakfast is as described; not fresh, with everything pre-packaged. We ate out. There is NO downstairs restaurant, contrary to other posts. They've got the wrong place. An absolute nightmare to find, as it surely must be one of the most inconspicuous hotels in Venice. Pay attention to the poor reviews; the majority is certainly right and we doubt the management care about that either.

author: arifeign
title: Great location to be in Venice
text: I booked a room at this hotel online and was promised with a double bed, an en-suite bathroom, along with a flat-screen TV. When I finally arrived at the hotel, I was instead given a horrible small room with a twin bed and a sink. No bathroom, no TV. After making some noise with the receptionist and showing my booking, insisting that the booking is a good enough contractual agreement between both parties and that the hotel should honour our contract, she called her boss and gave me a much bigger room on the top floor, this time with the private bathroom as promised. The flat screen TV was there as well, but probably for display purpose, as no single channel or program is available. The bathroom was big, with a shower area, sink and lavatory. Also, the double bed is actually 2 twin beds placed side by side. There is a cafe in the form of a small room, fit for a few tables, opened in the morning for breakfast, with breakfast being cereals and some off-the-shelf bread still wrapped in plastic bags. I don't suppose they actually cook anything there. So don't expect much if your booking comes with breakfast. The location of the hotel is extremely good. It is very much near the Piazza San Marco and is right in the middle of where the action is. Only that finding the hotel can be a bit tricky as it is hidden from view, no big signs anywhere and only the entrance door is visible. The picture indicated on tripadvisor.com and booking.com is in fact, the building opposite it! You can buy a wifi plan for only €2/day. Network is excellent. This is a 2-star hotel and is quite pricey, probably due to its excellent location. However, its rooms, service and facilities here can be improved.

author: Gade_Siraprapa
title: Great Location with an Acceptable Level of Facilities
text: I only had less than 20 days to plan everything about my 5-days trip (Wed-Mon) at Venice prior to my departure. So, almost every affordable yet beautiful hotels at San Macro were all booked out for Friday and Saturday nights. So, after reading many reviews on the internet, I finally decided to book this hotel with no expectations more than just to find a place to stay at the lowest price in San Macro area to stay during the weekend and stay at another hotels that I desired on the weekdays when their rooms were available. However, this hotel turned out to be beyond my expectations. The hotel location is very great since it is close to go to San Macro so. it's very convenient to do many things e.g. go see the sun rise in the morning at the piazza when there is almost no one there, walk through the area until at late at night and still can find a place to eat, come back to the hotel to take a short break for using toilet and resting my legs for a while when I feel that I cannot walk anymore during the day and easily access to both Rialto port and S. Macro port, etc. So, I think this hotel is perfect for people with limited budget who only want a place to stay in San Marco with an acceptable level of facilities and do not want to stay in the hotel room for no more than just the normal 6-8 sleeping hours. Besides, the hotel staffs are also nice and the hotel location is not that hard to find when you googles the hotel location before you go. You can walk to find this hotel on your own without having to ask anyone. For the cons, the room I stayed was so small that the door panel hits the bed if I open the door wider than 40-60 degrees and there is no elevators. Even though I have no problems with tiny spaces and the large luggage, I still don't like this smallness of the hotel room because you can find a lot larger room with a lot better facilities at a lot cheaper prices at somewhere else in Venice. Moreover, there are no meats, vegetable or eggs in the breakfast menu at all (Almost 95% of the hotel breakfast is CARB w/ tea, juice, milk or coffee) but I was OK with this because I usually do not eat breakfast anyway. So, if the nice, healthy breakfast is the MUST for you, I would suggest you find an additional breakfast meal on your own.

author: thetravellerstoo
title: Beware
text: I stayed at the Citta di Milano in early June. Although difficult to find, once you do, it is in an excellent location close to Piazza San Marco. The staff in the breakfast room is very friendly, as well as the woman who cleans the rooms. Unfortunately, that's as far as it goes. It was very hot, damp and humid in early June and the mosquitoes were more numerous than the tourists. We got eaten alive. I had reserved for twin beds, but the room had a double bed. I didn't want to make a fuss because the hotel was full. It was only for two nights. The ceiling fan, which would have made all the difference for the quality of a night's sleep, wasn't working. To the desk clerk's credit, he offered me an electric fan. It didn't make a difference though. I asked for a compensatory discount at the front desk and I was told to write to the hotel's e-mail address. I did this twice and never received an acknowledgement of any kind. I would definitely not recommend this hotel, nor would I return.

author: KJLovey
title: Left out in the cold!!!!
text: I knew that our flight times would mean that we wouldnt be on venice Island until atleast 11.30 - 12 midnight so I called our contact at needahotel to check if this would be problem and was assured the hotel were aware and everything would be ok! Unfortunately there was a delay at the airport, due to hand luggage restrictions, which meant we got to the Rialto at 12.45. After finding the hotel, approx 1am, there was no one available to let us in! The lights were on but nobody home!! We rang the doorbell constantly...even the next door neighbour came to their door! Rang the hotels phone, atleast 5 times and tried the emergency number...no luck!! So what do you do at 1.30am in a strange city!!!?? We managed to find a nice hotel called the 'Panada' that although they only had a single bed available were very accomodating. In the morning we headed over to the hotel to confront the manager, Mr Alviso, who was very unhelpful and unsympathetic. He showed us our room but after all the hassle I had had with this man and his 'so called hotel' I wasnt prepared to stay there. So we headed back to the Panada where we were offered a double bed and put the experiences of the previous night behind us to enjoy this beautiful city. I am currently dealing with needahotel over my complaint but Mr Alviso is adamant that he did everything he could to assit us!! He explanaition that his night porter had gone home doesnt wash! He says that he tried to get to the door!! I doubt it! I was confused because they take your keys off of you before you leave the hotel, so no partying past midnight in this hotel! I have asked for a refund of the night missed in the hotel and the additional 100 euros I incurred in the Panada, as a fair settlement to this fiasco....the story continues!! In conclusion, I would never recommend this hotel to anyone and wont be offering to buy Mr Alviso a bellini anytime soon!!

author: gasezer2
title: hotel is nice but the management is...
text: The hotel web site is a little bit exaggerating the reality. The decoration of the hotel is nice. The location of the hotel is good if you are not trying to find it via a rent car or a SUV. Because it is located at the old part of the city where the roads are tight and you need to find the correct approaching spot in order not to enter the road from the wrong side. We arrived around 8 pm, where there was heavy traffic and we struggled a lot to find its place. But the neighbourhood is quite and the rooms are also quite if there is no one shouting in the corridors. The room they have given us was supposed to be a standard room but it was very small (room number 102 and 101) that with our luggage and camera gear it was hard to fit in. Then we realised that the bathroom was not cleaned. The shower space had the hair left from a previous guest, and there was a dirty towel at the closet below the lavatory. We ordered room service, that arrived very late with missing cutlery. When they have completed everything our meal was cold. We left the trays outside the door and at 9:30 am it was still there.
