And when we came back from breakfast at around 11:00 our dirty dishes were still staring at us. And the waste bin of our friend who came from Germany was full of cigarets she didn't smoke as she was a no-smoker. The day after we made a complain and they cleaned our rooms. Suggested a change but we were settled and we refused to change our rooms. On the 3rd day the rest of our team have arrived and they had the same dirty bathroom problem. In the restaurant at the 1st floor (Ziyade restaurant where the breakfast was survey) the staff was friendly. At the roof restaurant the service was poor and the kebap (simple lamb shish ) arrived cold. So in summary the hotel is nice but they have serious management issues, and therefore they don't deserve the four stars.

author: rjoneskb
title: Fantastic location for a hotel
text: We stayed here as we were attending a concert in Bolton Macron stadium, hotel was immaculate and rooms clean and tidy. Staff in the hotel were very helpful and polite. Breakfast is great value for money and delicious. But what makes this hotel extra special is the attached restaurant! Oh my! Incredible place! Staff are fantastic! Location is beautiful! The decked area to sit on is lovely and so is the area next to the canal! The food was top class and served quickly! Not overly priced but excellent value for money and the best I have ever had! They provide lots of little touches to make things great like blankets in a hamper by the canal side if you get cold and a hamper of toiletries in the loo's for you to use! I would absolutely return again in a heartbeat!! Please be aware though if staying here when visting the Macron Stadium for a concert, we had a really hard time getting back to the hotel after the concert as no taxi firm would pick us up due to the poor infostructure around the stadium, roads were gridlocked for hours, and no trains were running! We eventually managed to get back after flagging down an empty cab in the middle of the road but if you are using the hotel as a base and can drive into Bolton you will be fine

author: 657maestro
title: Below Premier Inn Standard
text: Premier Inn main selling feature is an acceptable standard throughout the chain. In this respect Chorley North falls short. 1. The rooms have not been remodelled. 2. Lift did not work 3. Problem in the bedroom with lighting going on and off. 4. Breakfast and meals are served in the adjacent Chef and Brewer and the standard is not the same as a traditional Premier restaurant. 5. No Costa Coffee 6. Food selection at breakfast poor. 7. Closes at breakfast at 9 am. I saw a guest refused at 9:06. 8. Evening meals poor in quality, My advice drive on further there are better Premier Inn choices.

author: Anon186364
title: Double check before requesting the top floor !!
text: Stayed with my husband on Sunday night whilst visiting family in Chorley. We usually treat ourselves to a more upmarket hotel but as we were having a meal at Malthouse Farm pub next door anyway it seemed the obvious choice. After reading the reviews on TripAdvisor I called ahead and booked an upper floor with a canal view, as these appeared to be the best rooms. Both our requests were granted HOWEVER what we didn't realise from the other reviews is that looking at the hotel from the front it looks like a two storey building but part of it has 3 floors (and the lift wasn't working). On a Sunday night in December the hotel wasn't even half full and we ended up having the full 3rd floor to ourselves !! Bliss you may think... No it was like a ghost town and quite scary. There were times during the night I would've loved to hear the noise of people walking past our room or in the adjoining rooms !! There was obviously other people in the hotel as we saw the lights on in their rooms and there was quite a few people at breakfast. It would've been nice if the staff would have told us when we checked in that we'd be on our own up there and then we would have changed rooms. Our room was 202 which was quite large just for the two of us and up to the usual Premier Inn standard. One added bonus that I did like is that the TV swivelled right round and due to the positioning of the bathroom door you could actually leave it open and watch TV in the bath!! On the whole the hotel is very nice and I can certainly recommend the pub next door, but you will need to book in advance as it is popular with locals as well as hotel guests ,it is far better than the usual mass produced food chains that are normally connected to Premier Inns ! The staff are very nice and we were given a warm welcome. Adam on the reception seemed very knowledgeable about the area and if we weren't familiar with it ourselves we wouldn't hesitate to ask his advice on the best places to visit etc. If you want cheap and cheerful in the Chorley area you won't get much better than this hotel.

author: Fireball14017
title: Usual Premier Inn high standard
text: We decided to book into the Premier Inn for 2 nights over Christmas. We booked online which was straightforward enough and prices were £32 per room per night. Easy to find, just off Jct 8 of the M61 motorway; the hotel is actually tucked away in a quiet location- great if you want peace and quiet ; but not if you want a central town location. On check in, the staff were extremely friendly, courteous and helpful. The whole check in process took less than 5 minutes. The room itself was Premier Inn standard fair I.e Well proportioned, very clean and with extremely comfortable bed. On the whole, we both slept well apart from the audible snoring through the adjoining bedrooms wall. Perhaps this is down to the lack of soundproofing here or just the thinness of the walls. We stayed in a similar Premier Inn in the Midlands last year and this suffered from the same fault- Thin walls; so maybe this is a fault of Premier Inns in general. In addition; one downside here is that the hotel is made from barn like outbuildings as opposed to a single structure. This means that the simple task of popping to reception or breakfast entails you having to step outside and brave the elements and walk across an open courtyard. Breakfast itself is served in the adjoining Pub/restaurant at £8.75 per person. For this you effectively get a continental breakfast with the option of a cooked bacon & eggs, toast etc. The breakfast is all self service but we felt the breakfast little disappointing for the additional price. Overall, this Premier Inn is a great place to stay in the Chorley area if you want a cheap, clean and very comfortable room and nights sleep. Braving the courtyard in the morning to get to breakfast may not be worth it - particularly if it's pouring down with rain as it tends to do in the North West!

author: lindsayeb
title: Fabulous room and service, disappointing breakfast
text: We had two rooms booked, both were very large, one in particular was a corner room and extremely spacious. Check-in was friendly and efficient, the rooms were spotlessly clean - even for my children who like to pretend they're on Four in a Bed!!! Rooms well furnished, bathrooms smart and modern - with the bonus of a swivelling telly so that you can watch from the bath - very excited daughter! Beds were large and firm - a bit too firm for me but everyone else was happy. Heating and air-conditioning easy to operate with very clear instructions on the desk. All in all, a great night. However, breakfast was a complete let down. We were really looking forward to it, we know the quality of breakfast that we expect from a Premier Inn and this fell well short. We waited for ages to be greeted and seated. When someone did come they were short and brusque - the exact opposite of the hotel staff. At the hot buffet, every tray was almost empty with a couple of slimy bits of almost raw bacon in one and fried eggs that had almost solidified in their fat. It was badly set out, there were lots of people in a very small area and we were in each other's way. Staff were impossible to find. An experience that we were looking forward to was very much ruined and we left much sooner than we normally would from a breakfast. Even the children (12 and 9) who normally love to wander back and forth to a breakfast buffet, were keen to leave. Sorry Malthouse, as ever we had a wonderful weekend in Chorley, but we do feel a little disappointed.

author: mikolavict
title: Just a normal business hotel
text: Was there for work just the one night. My employer had booked the room for me so I didn't have the details of my booking. When checking in I was asked for my passport as they would not accept my ID card. I was lucky enough to have taken it with me, but did mention the fact that in countries with ID cards people may not neccessarely have a passport too. I happen to do because I've lived int he UK for so long, but most other Spaniards will not have it. The receptionist said that it was company policy and that ID cards were not accepted. I very much doubt it and consider that this was due to a misguided employee. I've been to other Premier Inns before and used my ID card to check in. The facilities were good and clean, the bed was VERY comfortable and the room a good size. Coffee/tea making facilities, flat screen and wifi in the rooms. The windows weren't double-glazed so some noise from road traffic did get in, but not too much. Breakfast was served on the adjacent building housing the restaurant. It was good and plenty to choose from. Checking out was fuss-free, unlike checking in. There's a David Lloyds next door but there's no direct access from the hotel, you need to walk for about 5 min on the access road. You also need a car or you'll be grounded as this hotel is in the middle of nowhere (relatively speaking). I had not hired one so dinner options were limited to the hotel's restaurant or a sandwich in my room.

author: Raikeswood
title: Staff helped to abate heat and noise
text: We enjoyed a three night stay at the Premier Inn, Chorley North in late July 2014. On arrival we were told we had Room 140, a larger than average room on the first floor at an adjacent additional accommodation building. Unfortunately the room was a lengthy walk from the entrance and it was also overlooking the outside seating of the adjoining public house. We had been told at reception that by 10pm each night drinkers were encouraged to vacate outside seats and return to the pub. We enjoyed a warm and, as promised, peaceful first night. The second night was even hotter and the small fan in the room was unable to make any noticeable difference to the feeling of 'cooking'. Additionally the noise from the pub made any thought of an early night impossible - it was nearly midnight by the time the noise subsided. My wife didn't sleep in the night and I was uncomfortable all night long. As we set off in the morning I decided to mention this at reception and see if it would be possible to get a different room, away from the pub and hopefully on a lower floor. The receptionist was very kind and she found us a room in the main block. Although it wasn't a ground floor room it did prove to be somewhat less hot than our first. The housekeeping and reception staff at this Premier Inn are excellent. We found they always had time to say hello and despite the very warm weather - which they were clearly feeling the effects from as well - remained cheerful and efficient throughout. I'm not sure what the answer is with the very hot rooms on upper floors - on the fourth night we stayed at a Premier Inn in Nottingham and 'cooked' overnight in an upper floor room at that location. I appreciate substantial investment would be called for to provide working air conditioning, but I wonder how many times each day staff are refunding entire or parts of bills as a result of customers being unable to get the promised good nights sleep? The no nonsense return of monies when sleep has been impossible or sparse shows honest intent by Premier Inns. That and their ability to attract and retain excellent staff ensures our continued loyalty and affection for the company.

author: gvh67
title: Not up to usual Premier Inn standards
text: We stayed for 4 nights, selecting this Inn based of the positive reviews and our previous experience of the PI chain. Unfortunately it didn't live up to our expectations. In fairness, the front desk staff were very attentive and we received two nights' rebate of our room cost due to the problems encountered - but we'd have preferred a trouble-free break. For us, the mattress didn't come up to the usual high PI standard and our first night was not as comfortable as it might have been. Front desk staff arranged for additional duvet covers as padding (and the first of our rebates). But our main problem was with the housekeeping service. Returning to our room late on the first afternoon (around 4:30) we found that the room had not been made up. Having reported this to the reception desk, the housekeeping staff arrived but asked us to vacate the room while they worked. Now, Premier Inns are not renowned for providing comfortable lounge areas so we had to spend the next 15 minutes sitting in the reception area - not good. And when we were allowed to return to our room we were not happy with the standard of cleaning in the bathroom. However, we let it pass without further comment. Imagine our surprise then on returning late the following afternoon we found exactly the same scenario! Another wait in reception while the housekeeping was attended to (albeit with better cleaning this time) and second night's room cost returned! And it's such a pity because the inn has a lot going for it. The location is superb (just off the M61 but absolutely no noise), there is a lift to help with getting cases to the upper floors, the rooms are a good size, the double beds are not linked twins, the full-size bath fills quickly with plenty of hot water, and they offer reduced prices for continental breakfast. All right, it would be better not to have to walk across the car park to get to the breakfast table but that seems to be fairly standard for many Premier Inns. But we came away disappointed because, however helpful the staff were at resolving our problems, they need to understand that prevention is better than cure and that no amount of discount can make up for a bad experience.

author: 860DavidL
title: Not the best Premier Inn
text: I have often stayed in Premier Inns, and until this one, have had no complaints. I have a slight disability, so have difficulty walking upstairs, with bags. Unfortunately, they had me booked into "The Stable Block" - entrance is not close to the car park, and then I had to walk upstairs. Unlike previous reviews, I did not notice any outside noise, at all! The bed, as always, was very comfortable. Staff were friendly. The total lights in the room did not let me read, which was very disappointing. No telephones in room, as Premier Inns have apparently just decided to remove all the phones. This is pathetic. I actually was shown a large box, with all the phones in, waiting to be sent to the third world. My alarm call had to be made by sending someone to the room, to hammer on my door. This is not good for staff. I booked the breakfast, for £8.50, which was inconveniently served in the pub next door, only between 7-9am. Arriving at 7:15, imagine my surprise that all the eggs were cold (both fried and scrambled), and although the tomatoes and mushrooms were hot, the hash browns were cold, and even worse, were soggy. Shower was too low in pressure. Unfortunately, I had to be in this area, on business. I had to pay £63, which is much more than this experience was worth. I will not stay at this hotel again.

author: gentlefrench
title: Excellent value
text: Arrived at the Premier Inn to a warm welcome. We were staying at the Premier Inn to attend a family wedding and were surprised at how Premier Inns have improved. We had a very spacious and perfectly clean room, with a kingsize bed and a very tidy bathroom - no horrible grout!!!! Lots of space to put things away. Towels were changed as requested. Tea and coffee were provided in the room. Shower gel and soap in dispensers in the shower and by the sink. No hair conditioner so bring that along!!! Parking was easy - lots of spaces! The hotel is next to the canal/river - lots of lovely walks nearby and cycle paths! Breakfast was available at the pub next door - the food was excellent, the evening meals looked fab too! the staff once more very friendly. On entering and leaving the hotel the staff passed the time of day with you and made you feel a valued customer - more than most of the expensive hotels we stay in. The deals are fabulous at the Premier Inns and we plan to look for more deals and go away for the sake of it. Just go!!

author: Gmas0n
title: Lovely property - shame about the noise
text: Exceptionally well-maintained property in a very attractive location. Our room was in the converted building right opposite the pub, so we were concerned about the noise factor however, it was not an issue. The double-glazing was extremely effective and the room was quiet. Friendly staff and efficient service. Well-appointed rooms with plenty of space and immaculately clean. Large, comfortable beds, a pillow choice - all nice touches let down perhaps by poor quality, thin towels in the bathroom. The lack of a room-phone is not a problem as most guests will use their mobiles, but Premier Inns, please provide guests with a standard number to call. No one appreciates premium charges to call reception. In terms of a good night's sleep, it felt like we had about 17 minutes of sleep on the first night. Constant thumping around in the room directly above to the point we thought they were moving furniture or perhaps redecorating the room or training circus elephants. This went on way into the wee small hours and started again before dawn, so no real sleep. We did sleep the second and third night in that the guests above went to bed at reasonable times, but you do hear every single footstep. The ceiling creaks with movement the sound reverberates below. This is clearly an issue as other guests have highlighted it, so the solution is to stay on the top floor. No noise from adjoining rooms, so it is primarily up-down as opposed to sideways. There is a newer building, so it is possible the situation only exists in the renovated section. Liked the property, but the 3-night say was marred by the lack of sleep and noise on the first night.

author: Manj11_11
title: Fabulous Location
text: We stayed here in July. What a perfect location right by the canal. The setting is wonderful. Ducks accompany you across the car park. The bedrooms are very good. Plenty of space and super bathrooms. The only downside is that the dressing table mirror has very limited adjustment – a minor detail. The check in on arrival was very efficient and friendly. The lady could not do enough for us. It was a very hot evening and she searched the hotel to try to find us a fan that did not make a noise when in use. The next day, whilst we were having a coffee outside after breakfast, we were impressed to watch two gardeners. They worked so hard and cleared all the cuttings up after them. Not even a blade of grass was to be seen! Not an easy task in temperatures of 35c. We would definitely recommend this hotel and will be certain to book again when in Chorley.

author: JamNHoney
title: Lovely clean and comfy room but shame about the breakfast service
text: I like staying at Premier Inns as you know what to expect and they are good value. This Premier Inn is in a nice location and the buildings are pretty. We were allocated a room in the 'stable block' which was clean, modern with a comfy king size bed and nice clean bright bathroom. We did hear a little noise from people revving car engines around midnight which was probably from people leaving the pub opposite. The rest of the night was lovely and quiet. We had stayed in another Premier Inn in West Didsbury the previous night which had set a high standard expecially when it came to breakfast and this one was no where near the same standard. We had to wait some time by the 'please wait to be seated sign' before a member of staff appeared. We were then allocated a grubby table. I dont know whether there was a shortage of staff as the whole experience was completely unorganised. Almost most things we wanted had to be asked for e.g. teaspoons, cereal spoon, coffee, orange juice, white bread for toast. The whole buffet area was completely uncared for and needed replenishing although we were there 45 mins before the end of the time that breakast was due to be finished. The staff need more training on customer service and how to keep the area looking 'cared for'. This was in complete contrast to the West Didsbury Premier Inn breakfast which could not be faulted. Maybe the staff from Malthouse Farm should be sent to West Didsbury for some staff training! The few staff that were there seemed to be running back and forth from the kitchen with items that other customers were also requesting. When they did replenish items they would only bring out a bare minimum which meant they had to keep returning to the kitchen for more. Why not put more out to save the extra trips? I would certainly recommend the hotel and feel that it offers good value for money but I think if we were to book here again we would not bother with breakfast and would eat elsewhere.

author: mummysquadge
title: Lovely place to stay
text: We stayed here for two nights on the 12th and 13th October. The staff are very welcoming and were very helpful and polite. We had a family room and were down the corridor from the main reception. My heart sank when we were told that was where our room was as I had read other reviews about the noise but we heard very little noise. Our room looked out over the Canal which was lovely and far better than the view over the car park which some of the other rooms had!. The only snag was that we left our windows slightly open during the day on Saturday and came back late evening to find our room had been invaded by mosquitos ( much to my partner's concern!!). He " dealt " with them and they didn't actually bite any of us! Our room was a family room and the big bed was BIG!!! It was lovely and comfortable and the biggest bed I have ever slept in ( and mine at home is a Kingsize!). The children each had beds on the floor which they said were very comfortable although the way they had been put meant that they children risked bumping their heads on the bedside table so we moved the one which was at the wall end to the opposite end of the room but couldn't move the other as it would have blocked the bathroom - this didn't leave very much room but as we were only staying in the room at night time, it wasn't a great problem. The breakfast is served in the MaltHouse which is across the courtyard. This was very nice, however I don't eat meat and had been looking forward to trying the vegetarian sausage. On the first morning I was told that they didn't have any and the second morning when I asked, I was told I would have to wait 15 minutes for it to be cooked to order - which would have been fine, had they told me that when we first came in to breakfast and not when everyone else I was with was already tucking into their breakfast and we didn't really have time to wait. The cooked breakfast is already cooked and iit's on a serve yourself basis. Breakfast was much much busier on the Sunday morning than on the Saturday morning when it felt like a bit of a free for all as there was nowhere to put the lids from the metal dishes ( of which there were four) and the table had been set so that people could only serve themselves from one side of it - so there were queues, things were running out and nobody was checking on them- the beans ran out and the waiter was asked for some more, he brought out a bowl full which probably was just two tins worth of beans which were pretty much gone straight away and when someone asked for some more he complained that he had only just brought some more out and checked as if he didn't believe them! There is one toaster which you place your bread in and it moves through the machine, which is ok if there aren't many people there, but there was a queue about 7 people long all waiting to use the toaster which either burned the toast or didnt do it well enough and so the bread had to be put through again which just made the wait for toast even longer!! On the whole the breakfast was nice, I just feel that the logistics of it all needed thinking through more. The last time I went there was a few years ago but they cooked your breakfast to order then. All in all, it's a lovely Premier Inn, and we would stay there again and would definitely recommend it as a family friendly hotel.

author: chrismastree
title: A Lancashire Delight
text: We stay at the Premier Inns fairly often and therefore know their standards. Chorley North didn't let us down although despite the good experience it can improve even more. Reception greeting could be a little warmer although adequate for what it was. The desk was sometimes unattended which didn't create a helpful impression. The standard of accommodation for a budget chain is pretty good. A good nights sleep is guaranteed with premier inns but the room in the stable block here wasn't as nice as the rooms in the main block. With having a corner room the available light from the maln window was less than ideal but it was adequate. The bathroom would have benefited from a wall light over mirror but in the main the room was reasonable. The adjacent restaurant was very busy given the number of rooms at this hotel. We were within the time limits set for breakfast although towards the end time. The food was therefore limited and had clearly been there for some time. Staff though were very helpful and pleasant. We will return to this hotel in future and have no hesitation in commending it to visitors. Although comments above might appear critical, they are intended to be constructive and no way imply any sense of poor standard. The hotel staff do a good job and the premises are clean and well attended.

author: BoardingPass784093
title: A hidden Gem along the river
text: For the past 30 yr we have been travelling as 6 couples on a fall weekend. We have been to many memorable spots and Samuels ranks as one of he best. It is located beside the Maitland River just north of Goderich. Half the rooms have a patio facing the river. The rooms are spacious with all the modern amenities. Free Wi-Fi is available and all the rooms have a small fridge with complimentary water and chocolates. The staff are amazing. No problem in checking in all the couples. We chose to eat in the adjoining restaurant and a square table was set up for us so no one was left out of the conversation. The food was outstanding using mostly local ingredients. I had the duck and it was the best I have had in a long time. The wine list includes some local wineries and is decently priced. In the morning a continental breakfast is available in the lobby and can be eaten in the restaurant. It includes juices, cereals, yogurt, toasts and sweets. Complimentary cupcakes are always available in the lobby. There is a lot to see and do in the Goderich area and the staff will gladly suggest an itinerary. All in all it was a delightful stay and I would highly recommend Samuels if you are in the Goderich area

author: trainfan2000
title: Lovely Quiet Boutique Hotel
text: This is a lovely little hotel minutes away from downtown Goderich. The staff are helpful and the rooms are nicely appointed. The rooms all have a sliding door that opens onto a small patio with a couple of chairs and a table so that morning coffee can be enjoyed at the room. The rooms at the back have a partial view of the Maitland River. The rooms have laminate flooring and are furnished in a contemporary style. The AC is quiet and very efficient. Breakfast is available, either a continental one (boiled egg, toast, pastry, yogurt, cereal) or, for a reasonable charge, a full breakfast of eggs or french toast. If you are arriving late, the hotel will leave your key in a lock box at the front door so a late arrival is not an issue. There are chargers for electric cars. The hotel is clean and quiet and there is lots of parking available. Free DVD's are available for in-room use and the WiFi is excellent. Delicious little cupcakes are available at all times near the front door for guests which is a nice touch. My only issue is that the beds are low. If you have trouble (knees or other) getting off low chairs or beds you will find this a concern. The management knows about this and they say they are working on it. Other than this, the hotel is great place to stay - quiet, comfortable beds, good breakfast and helpful staff.

author: chrishA8378PT
title: ... and cupcakes to die for!
text: We really enjoyed our stay at Samuels! Saltford is north of Goderich by about a kilometer and provides for a very quiet area. Our queen room faced the parking area. You never heard any vehicles unless you had the patio doors open or if you were sitting in our patio. The Continental breakfast (included) was truly exceptional. The waitstaff brought us pots of hot water to brew our tea in. We did not get a chance to enjoy any other meals there this time -- but will make sure we do next time! All of the staff members were great to talk with, they offered great service plus suggestions of local areas of interest. My ball cap fell out of our vehicle after we left, they immediately phoned us, and we returned to pick it up ... wowzers ... now that is service! In the corner of the front foyer, was a shelf with a plate of cupcakes under a glass cloche. What an incredible marketing idea; made even move incredible by the fact that these cupcakes were to die for!!!! suggestions of what we might see, where to find things in town, how to access some of the excellent walking trails in the area and even adding a little local history to the mix. Samuels had not been our first accommodation choice in the area but I feel fortunate that we found it and quite sure that it is the only place I would want to stay on my next Goderich visit.

author: snowbird1954
title: Supper
text: We went out to supper with friends to check out the fare at Samuels, on a quiet Saturday night. Just us and one other young family of 4 there who finished up shortly after we got there. Our food was beautifully presented and was good. We tried 2 appetizers, one per couple to share which was great as the appetizer salad was large as was the other appetizer we ordered. The place is decorated nicely and clean, but unfortunately doesn't have much of a view of the river. All was fine until we received our bills, which was apparently divided up not as the 'men' on one and 'women' on the other. That was caught and we asked that the bills be corrected so each couple was reflected in the bill. The bill went back, at that point 2 new couples came into the restaurant at was very close to their closing time. Our bill came back a few minutes later and the guys looked at it, not real closely, but close enough to see that the correct entres were correct now on the bill. We tipped the normal 15%, and left. Next day we ( both couples) both discovered on looking at the bills, that they, our bills still were made up I correctly. One bill had an extra glass of wine $5 added onto it and the other had an extra $12 started added onto it. So we both paid for extras that were wrong, plus we had tipped on them, and tipped on the tax also, which was probably due to the way the tipping works on their machine. Because we both live in Goderich, we decided then to go back and ask for a credit back as we were annoyed that a total of $17 + tip was overpaid. I was a little surprised that the owner who was there and was the one who had waited on us & made up the original bill the night before, wasn't really apologetic at all. He did give us the credit back, plus the tip of the credit back also after it was mentioned to him, but I was expecting more, after all we had to go back to the restaurant the next day and wait for the correction and credit, so offering us a credit for a coffee & desert or a glass of wine at our next outing there would have been nice. If the restaurant had been really busy, the I can see maybe 1 mistake, but it wasn't busy, and too many mistakes on the bill were made to my liking.

author: LifeTravel2011
title: Genuinely friendly, peaceful, relaxing vibe
text: Pretty river view room with small outdoor patio and patio door with screen. New, easy to open. Very comfortable foam mattress for King Bed (no box-spring) and best pull-out couch with foam mattress we've ever found, anywhere!! Very quiet location, just outside Goderich with genuinely small-town friendly atmosphere, owner Kim and staff. Generous sized room for family of 4. Clean grounds and rooms; loved large shower space; great showers! Plenty of towels!!! A bit tight for toilet in shower room. Vanity/ sink separate from shower room (great idea!) with coffee maker. A/C user-friendly; plenty of comfort options; not noisy. Plenty of hangers; enough drawers or cubbies to store belongings. Small fridge (no freezer) came in handy; nice touch w/ electric fireplace. Breakfasts suited us all; very good continental menu w/ best yogurt!! freshly baked breads, muffins, small pastries, cereals or option to order a la carte. Very pretty bright dining area, never rushed; and comfy club chairs in small front reception area where we enjoyed playing cards at night. Small goldfish in glass bowel nice touch. Loved the home-baked treats for guests at front entrance!!! Free DVDs! books and area pamphlets next to ice machine. Adults and teens all enjoyed our stay:) Great location for travelling to Goodrich beach areas (10 minutes drive) or as home base for travelling along the coast to other beaches.

author: LaurelJohnso1
title: Modern, Quiet & Accessible.
text: The best part about Samuels is that it's on the edge of town close to the river. It's so quiet, serene & calm. I have stayed at Samuels on multiple occasions now for business and I will keep returning. They have been very accommodating to my needs at work, (receiving packages for me and placing them in my room for my return, booking last minute & leaving after-hours key box for me). Rooms are huge, modern, updated & clean! I've stayed in most rooms on the bottom level and I've been impressed with the modern decor and the comfort of the beds. All the rooms have a patio door & area with chairs for smokers etc. Most rooms & bathrooms are spacious and accessible if you have mobility issues. The suite on the top level is fabulous for large groups or families (two bedrooms). It has its own private deck with patio furniture which is super nice on sunny evenings. If you're coming for business or pleasure, Samuels is so much more than just a bed. It's a beautiful, friendly & quiet place to stay. The downside; Small number of rooms means you need to book well in advance. The cheaper rooms book up really fast and leaves you with a choice to spend more or go to another hotel. They have been booked solid on a few occasions when I have called.

author: flyingmg
title: Comfortable warm contemporary room with excellent services
text: I am a refugee from Benmiller inn due to freaking cold room there. What a nice surprise at Sumuels !! Room has both heater and an electronic fireplace. They warm up the room fast. Its working desk is on the small side but adequate to work on it. Two seat leather sofa is a plus. Hardwood floor makes it more modern. Microwave and fridge are very convenient too. Don't let hotel's ordinary exterior fool you. As a frequent business traveler, I rate it A+. The best part of this place is its services. From reservation, to check in, and check out, everyone is so professional and friendly. Upon learning my next day will start earlier than their breakfast time, front desk prepared my breakfast the night before and delivered them to my room. They did it again without asking the next evening. I wish I had time to chat with and know these wonderful staff more ........ I am highly impressed and really appreciate your helps!! Definitely stay again next time.

author: defib64
title: Christmas Luncheon
text: This afternoon 6 ladies got together to enjoy camaraderie, laughs, and celebrate Christmas, an upcoming milestone birthday and being in each other lives! Most of the ladies have never been to eat here before. We made reservations to be on the safe side as it is a very small intimate location. We were met by Sarah who was very friendly and a great server. The daily menu of soup and quiche or sandwich was on the board and was offered to us right away. We were also given a rather extensive bistro menu. I had the brie and the curry quinoa salad. The portions were fabulous, the presentation was amazing and the taste was superb. All freshly made and very tasty on the palate. I also had a nice glass for merlot!! Some of the ladies had the daily special and others ordered off the menu as well. The dessert menu was very good as well. I enjoyed the nice homemade baklava. This is a hidden gem for sure!! After lunch, of which we not once, felt like we were rushed, the owner Kim, took us to see one of th e rooms overlooking the MIghtly Maitland River. Very tastefully decorated and cozy rooms. Thanks to Kim and her staff for making our lunch a wonderful experience!! Highly recommend checking out Sameul's Hotel.

author: kipkat574
title: Don't overlook Samuels when visiting Goderich!
text: My wife and I were very impressed with this hotel after spending Thanksgiving weekend (2013)in Goderich. The hotel is situated on the north side of the Maitland River just off HWY 21 on Saltford Rd. which has wonderful views of the river and valley especially this time of year. The rooms are chic and modern with comfy beds, fireplace, flat screen TV, bar fridge, and a small sitting area. Floors are wood laminate, which add to the modern updated rooms. The bathroom is small, consisting of a toilet and a walk-in shower. The vanity with mirror and sink are just outside the bathroom. The room was spotless upon arrival and everything in its place. There is a cozy dining room where you can enjoy the continental breakfast included in the room rate. Breakfast consisted of bagels, toast, cereal, muffins & pastries, yogurts, fresh fruit, juice and coffee. You can also order breakfast from the menu at an additional cost. Lunch and dinner is also served in the small bistro dining room. When booking a room, I would strongly recommend booking a riverview room. Sliding glass doors open onto a small patio and a grassy area that extends to the riverbank. The grounds were well manicured and flowerbeds surrounding the complex were weed free as they do a very good job maintaining the outside as well. Staff were very friendly and helpful which also adds to an enjoyable experience at this hotel. Keep up the good work. Hotels like yours are hard to come by these days.

author: Torontocargo
title: Goderich 2013/2014
text: I am soooo happy we paid a visit to this place. We have been here 3 times and stayed at Samuels Hotel every time. There are trails near-by, The Downtown area is really cool. You got to get a free map and the Goderich book. It will help you with any places to eat, bowling,music shop etc etc. One night we stayed in the King size bed with the Hot tub for a little extra cash and it was worth it. Each time we go, we try and plan out what we will do next time we come back. People need a break and this is the place to go. There is a lot of History in Goderich and the Samuels Hotel. The food from Samuels is amazing. I had the French Onion soup at night for a snack. Breakfast is the best. I think the owner or Her Husband have went to Culinary School. They have just added some more items to the Menu. The Hotel is the best I have seen there, very frendly place.

author: 300karenl
title: Lights out!
text: Our stay at the Samuels was a de-light. Literally. We checked in. Very nice, clean comfortable room. Beds very comfortable. We went to the dining room and ordered our food. While it was being prepared the lights went out in Goderich. The owner called her husband and he arrived quickly with a generator. Our meal was prepared and served in the dark. (With battery lights so we could eat.) Every effort was made to be sure we were comfortable. Electricity was restored later. I enjoyed the history of the Samuels Hotel. We were a group of 10 on motorcycles. Lovely setting. Liked the outdoor seating in each room. Would love to come back and utilize the second floor suite with deck. Very nice stay in spite of difficulties beyond the owners control. Thank you for a wonderful evening.

author: ih516
title: Ontario's Finest Inns Lowering Qualification Criteria
text: My wife and I always stay at Ontario's Finest Inns whenever we have an opportunity to travel. We recently tried Samuels for a change of pace. The hotel is clean, has good beds, friendly staff and has recently been renovated. It was a motel in its previous lifetime from the looks of the layout...one floor, one long hallway. After enjoying other inns in the Ontario's Finest Inns group there are a few things we did not expect. The tailgate party in the parking lot for two nights was a bit off putting.....cooking with a gas barbq on the truckbed over the gas tank. OMG. Needless to say we kept our heavy drapes fully closed in case of an explosion. The nagahide couch in the room was very uncomfortable and we kept slipping off onto the floor. There was also no proper reading light(s), just two very small bulbs in the lights beside the bed. Another dangerous fixture was the glass wall between the toilet and shower. Hit my head a few times.....needs some stripping so you know its there. Shower also leaks all over bath floor onto the hardwood (hardwood in the bath?). If you like an upscale motel for a night this place fits the bill. If you are a VIP member of the group do your research and take nothing for granted. Motels in the area are likely half the price with just your basic room.

author: 146bettinah
title: Not worth the money
text: Online this property looks stunning. Less so in reality. I booked a junior suite and thought i was going to enjoy 6 days of luxury in an airy , classy environment. When i arrived the room was small and not user friendly and the so called balcony was only standing room only. The most disappointing was the view of the hospital carpark next door - not the city view as i thought i was getting! lol I went downstairs to be told that garden view room would cost extra. I insisted i was not happy and she begrudgingly gave me a garden view room. The view was definitely better and quite soothing. Unfortunately it was dirty and tired. the couch had marks and stains that meant there is no way i would sit on it, The Aircon had old water damage on the walls . The bathroom was dirty and the table had something sticky on it. I went to make a cup of tea and the cup was dirty. At this point I did not want another room. My Expedia booking said 'no changes or cancellations' but i felt the Residence at Thonglor did not live up to their end of the agreement. The positives are that the lobby and breakfast areas are beautifully decorated and have a relaxing ambiance. The pool is beautiful and the onsen (hot tub ) though a reason why i booked the hotel was only lukewarm. The bed was very comfortable and i had a great nights sleep. I will say that Expedia requested a refund and it was gratefully approved so I was able to go to another hotel without loosing money. To summarize your money will go a lot further at many other places in Bangkok

author: pwelch
title: Good value, panorama room is great!
text: Checked in here for 4 nights. You need to go to floor 2 for reception. The security guard kindly helped with luggage as all the concierge staff were standing chatting on the 2nd floor. I was swiftly acknowledged and checked in. I was upgraded to a one bedroom panorama apartment. This was a few categories above what I booked. The room is absolutely lovely. Windows all around - sure is a panorama with great views from the 8th floor. This was a great first impression and left me with a positive feeling about the hotel. It is right above a Family Mart which is really convenient for late night snacks and anything you need. The washer / dryer machine was particularly useful to catch up on all the laundry. Breakfast is truly nothing special and caters more for Asian guests rather than western, but staff are helpful and keen to look after their guests. Not worth the 300 baht fee but mine was included. The rooftop pool was lovely at night with views across the city. It was disappointing that the Onsen wasn’t at the proper temperature. The free internet can be slow at times and the free shuttle to Thonglor BTS even left us behind one morning so there’s a few things that could be improved. Saying that I’d happily stay again at the right rate given the 65sq metre room. Location is fairly good for nightlife!

author: canadianj2015
title: Loved this place
text: I visited Bangkok with my husband and my 1 year old. Upon arrival, we got help from 1 of the bell boys with our many luggages (traveling for a month and with a baby). Check in was pleasant with very polite front desk staff. We requested a crib at check in and it arrived as we got to the room delivered by housekeeping. The hotel was in a good location with lots of restaurants around. Convenient store just downstairs and full grocery store about 8 minutes walk away. The room was very impressive (we got a garden view 1 bedroom suite on the 5th floor) as I wanted a place that felt homey since we were staying for 2.5 weeks and with a baby we needed a kitchen and washer/dryer. The room looked clean but I am a bit more picky compared to others as my 1 year old likes to crawl around. So we requested our floors to be mopped at night when we realized it was a bit dusty. They sent someone up right away even though housekeeping was done for the day. (awesome service) The housekeeping staff was so pleasant and friendly and loved playing with my baby and always making her laugh. The free shuttle to the BTS was great as the hotel is located pretty far in (would be about a 25-30 min walk) and they even pick you up at the BTS (just make a call to them 5 mins prior to arrival at the station) but only until 9pm. Note that the shuttle will drop you off anywhere on that street leading up to the BTS, which worked out great for us since we have a baby and I am currently pregnant with a 2nd one! The rooftop pool is so lovely and especially beautiful when you go during sunset. I noticed some other reviews complained about the noise from the street but it wasn't really a big deal to us as we have been to Bangkok many times and is aware this is just the norm in Bangkok. Our baby never got bothered by it during her sleep either. The security staff at the front was always very helpful and friendly and assisted us when we needed to flag a taxi down. My last positive review would be for the new front desk manager who accommodated us for a late check out as our flight wasn't until 6pm. She realized we had been staying for 2.5 weeks and that we had a 1 year old baby and that it would be hard for us to kill time around Bangkok in the heat, plus being pregnant and all! So she let us check out at 3pm at no extra charge (so grateful!) We will definitely be staying here again when we return to Bangkok in the future (as a family of 4!).

author: 2806MAT
title: Excellent value & location
text: This is the second time I'd stayed here during my two month holiday in Thailand. This time for a week. Booked last minute via Agoda I got a great deal at around £50/€60 for a one bedroom apartment. Which in this location on Thonglor is amazing value for money. The rooms are modern, spacious and clean and fully equipped. Cold and quiet AC. Good bathroom, fridge/freezer and washing machine too. Breakfast was good and plenty of choice for Western/Asian palate. Nice pool on the roof which each time I used it is had to myself. Well equipped gym and even a golf simulator (which sadly, I didn't get to use). Check in was quick & easy thanks to the very nice Ta. As for location. Well if you like your restaurants and bars you cannot beat Thonglor. And some good shopping malls less than B60 in a taxi. Useful shuttle bus (free) to the BTS too. I changed from a one bedroom to a studio half way through the week. Only downside to the studio is there is a bath only (no shower). Which was a bit of a downside for me. But at £30 a night amazing value. Thoroughly recommended

author: lshapspro
title: Second stay and worse than the initial stay
text: This is my second stay at The Residence thong lo. I stayed for 3 nights in October 2016. I remember my first stay as much better than expected, so I was somewhat surprised that my experience this time was less pleasant. The problem already started at reception where the girl (Apple) was quite unfriendly, but someone I remember as being quite friendly during my first stay. I want to point out that after this initial cold reception, she was much more friendly and helpful (maybe just a bad day). When I got to my room, the room was still being serviced, so we had to go back to the reception center and after some discussion I was given a new room, which seemed smaller than the room I had on my first stay, even though I booked the same room type (Junior suite). Still, the room was of ample size and I had no complaints about getting a smaller room. The room comes with a complete kitchen, which is nice if you want to cook or use the micro. It has a washing machine/dryer in one unit proved useful since I was in Bangkok 3 days before coming to The Residence. The location in my view is not that good as it takes about 30 minutes to walk to the nearest BTS station (Thong lo station). However, there is a reliable free shuttle service that will take you to the BTS station and other areas close by. The shuttle service will even pick you up at the BTS station so you don’t have to walk back or take a taxi. The immediate area has several restaurants and massage shops not too far from the hotel (the massage shops are about 10-15 min walk from the hotel). Tops market (very good supermarket) is about a 20-min walk. There’s a second (more upscale, at least in terms of prices) market about a 15-min walk from the hotel. I bought some strawberries at this market, paying about 250 baht (I believe it was 125g), and later saw that Tops market was selling them for 125 baht. The hotel has a restaurant (high prices not much atmosphere), a swimming pool on the roof and a not so well equipped fitness center (no spa). While the room is completely okay, I was bored at the hotel (no pulse, few people) and I see that already the furniture and floors, etc. are starting to look worn out even though the hotel is quite new (cheap material). But I paid only about 2000 baht/night so I feel that this property is still good value for the money.

author: 486eliciac
title: Comfortable
text: We had the most basic standard room on level 2, same as reception area. The room was good enough for 2 pax. We had a sofa area, pantry, queen bed and bathroom with bathtub. We stay in the apartment for 3 days. The place was clean ok the 1st day. However subsequently, realized that the bathroom rug was not changed. Anyways, there's a complimentary shuttle service to thonglor area ( mainly along the same street of the building ). The pick up from thonglor bts is at the Maevaree mango store. The apartment is not really walkable distance. I would say a good 30 mins walk from bts. Drive is about 10 mins. There a nice pool, gym, golf area at level 9. You can enjoy the beautiful sunset from there. So near yet so far. The area was cozy. If you are looking for a place with not many tourist, this is it. So nearby the apartment, there are many nice restaurants around. Japanese, Italian... The place I frequent most over the days I stayed is The commons. Shuttle service is able to bring you right there to the door step!

author: monicaxox
title: Great place to relax!
text: We arrived at 12.30PM, however we weren't able to check-in as they were still cleaning the rooms. We were advised to leave our storage in the lobby and utilise the free area shuttle; however, the driver was out to lunch so we stayed in the lobby until 2PM and he took us to Thong Lo BTS station. Later, we called the hotel and he picked us up from the station pretty quickly, despite the busy peak hour traffic. We entered our room on the 6th floor and were pleasantly surprised to find that we were upgraded to a Junior studio room, complete with a kitchenette, cutlery and dishes, a washing machine and fridge, complimentary water bottles, a bathtub, TV, slippers, a DVD player, rainfall shower and luxury toiletries - not to mention a small balcony with city views. - Location: Far away from the city centre but the free area shuttle can drop you off at Thong Lo station where you could reach Siam, Ratchathewi etc. within 15 minutes. There is a 7-Eleven directly across the street with cheap street food stalls in front of it. Some restaurants are about a 10-minute walk away. The area is fairly quiet compared to the city centre and few locals spoke English. - Staff: The staff member who served us was very friendly, helpful and always smiled at us, unfortunately I didn't get her name. The shuttle driver and ground floor security were also friendly but they didn't understand much English. - Amenities: On the 9th floor there is a nice rooftop pool with beautiful views of the city. Sun loungers and extra towels were provided nearby. There's also a mini golf area, a spa tub and sauna (strangely in the men's bathroom.. I hesitated to go in there!), small gym and a dining area. Overall - great staff, very nice amenities inside our room and in the hotel itself. Great value for money. This was one of my favourite places to stay in Bangkok, despite its distance from the city centre. They also provided free luggage storage. :) Will definitely be back!

author: lshapspro
title: A bit far from the nearest BTS station but great value
text: I stayed 8 nights in July 2016 for business. For all 8 nights, I paid around 13,500 baht! The Residence is new and very clean and well maintained. The gym was great and there is a small, outdoor pool. There is even a golf opportunity but I’m not sure how that worked! There was a restaurant with reasonably priced food, but I preferred to try all the many restaurants close by. The Residence is quite far the Thong lo BTS station, a good 30-minute walk. However, the property offers free shuttle service both from the property to the BTS and from the Thong lo BTS back to the property. The biggest problem, besides the distance to the nearest BTS station, was the key card, which often did not work and one was required to press it against the card reader several times (this was a bit annoying). I was given a free upgrade and found the room to be spacious, clean and with enormous space for clothes, etc. The one thing I noticed was the large number of electrical outlets in the room (there were 30)—never stayed in a place with so many outlets! The bathroom had a bathtub and separate shower (rain forest and European style). The only issue was the pressure (too low). My impression is that the building material is of rather poor quality and I could imagine that after 4-5 years this building will not be so attractive as it is now (hope I’m wrong). The Residence was a truly great value (about 1700/night). If you don’t mind the distance from the BTS, I can highly recommend this property. There are many restaurants nearby, although I was surprised at the rather high prices for rather simple food in an ordinary restaurant. I think this is because the Thong lo area is rather upscale, with many of the well-to-do Thais hanging out here.

author: nnovak_11
title: Has some rough edges despite beautiful photos online
text: We stayed here four nights at front end of our trip to Thailand. The staff is courteous but there are language challenges. I wrote everything down in English so they could translate later. Our room was nice and clean, but lacked sufficient towel sets for three guests. Nice to have in room laundry but hard to get from hotel the laundry soap. We had two incidents that resulted in our request to move to another higher floor room. The two incidents were 1) too noisy neighbors next door for two nights, 2) early morning piercingly screams and yells in English from our floor. I called security/front desk, it turned out to be a domestic argument in a room three doors down, Very Unsettling. We were told the hotel was fully occupied but rarely did we see other guests, except a few in the lobby or restaurant. Perhaps the hotel is fully booked with companies or longer stay occupants who come and go? It gave us an slightly eery feeling of being by ourselves in a large, new, hotel. We did enjoy the onsite restaurant with very friendly and attentive staff each am for breakfast. Delightful menu and very delicious and attractive presentations. Fitness room is small, appears to be Very lightly used. no free weights less than 10 lbs 😳 Location is far from Skytrain, but walkable in early morning. Taxis are hit or miss depending on time of day. Would not stay here again as there are many other comparable priced, higher end hotel options in a better central location in BKK.

author: familymatriach
title: Beautiful spacious Hotel, great amenities
text: A group of us four female friends, visited different parts of Thailand in celebration of one of our friend's birthday. While in Bangkok we booked two rooms at the Residence in Thonglor. A new, very comfortable, well equipped Hotel. Modern décor with high ceilings, plenty of closet space, gorgeous bathrooms. It's on the outskirts of Bangkok in an upscale area. Hotel offers shuttle to the BTS station and other places in Thonglor. We used the shuttle to go shopping in the area, go to the spa, restaurants and to be dropped off at the BTS station. The stuff is very polite and friendly. The receptionist, Ta, was particularly very helpful, eager to offer guidance and highly professional. I even witnessed her remain unusually calm and professional while being assailed by a churlish, unruly and disrespectful guest. The residence on Thonglor has a restaurant in house but with plenty of diverse restaurants in the area we did not dine here. Since the rooms are equipped with a lovely kitchenette, we prepared our own breakfast during our week long stay. We took the shuttle to buy a few groceries at a big well supplied supermarket recommended by the staff. Joke, one of the staff members, was very patient and kind to us while shuttling us around and providing advise and guidance. We were able to communicate well enough with the staff. None of us speak thai and they were able to offer us the help we needed by making a great effort to communicate with us. The hotel offers a beautiful infinity pool, hot tub and sauna which we enjoyed tremendously. The place is very clean, with a lovely ambiance.

author: Thakkii24
title: New Hotel with warm staff!
text: The hotel is relatively new and so the property looks fantastic. What we loved most about the hotel is the staff, everyone from security, front desk to housekeeping is very welcoming and hospitable. The food at the restaurent is over priced and was not upto the priced charged. (eg, hot chocolate brought was luke warm, milkshake was too sweet, a sandwhich ordered had an utterly hard and somewhat burnt bun!) Housekeeping needs to improve more, the housekeepers seem to rush and many times I had to personally ask to empty some trash cans. But as the rest, everyone was wonderful with the service delivery. We loved and enjoyed the roof top pool, the ambiance of the hotel is chic, the amenities were great, wifi was strong. Would be a good to add more english channels to the current list. A Seven Eleven is right across the hotel and for those on medicals, BKK hospital is about less than 10 mins away (in taxi). Many restaurents near by as well. So the location is convenient. We had a glitch at check out. Half way through our stay we had paid for the nights stayed and kept the remaining days to be paid on check out. However, the front desk had no records of our payment and requested to pay full. Luckily had a reciept of the initial payment and all was sorted. And the key card also kept having issues. We would definitely recommend this hotel and would stay there ourselves again. Hoping that such little glitches will be dealt in the future. We enjoyed our stay! :)

author: neilbert
title: Excellent Stay...considering
text: The hotel is so very new. Everything is pristine. Our 5 day stay was fabulous, so we feel very sorry for the guy who gave the 3* reference here. We would have been staying there at the same time and did have some problems with the Wifi on one day. They had to reboot the system a number of times, but as an IT Systems Support Director I see this as very positive. Someone was at least trying to get it working. And they did...eventually. The only other complaint I could offer was the hot and cold water to the shower. Somehow, this plumbing was a bit of a mess. Hot was cold, cold was cold, intermediate was hot. By playing with the lever you could get it right...but it changed during a shower so you had to keep changing the lever. Annoying, buy nothing more. These things happen in a new hotel, and I for one will put up with that for a very nice room at a very reasonable price. Oh, one other thing, the advertised Golf Simulator is an added cost. That is not made clear in the literature. I almost dropped a star from my rating because of this. To the management: You need to put both these things right

author: Kenyalang
title: Nice, new, spacious serviced apartment on Sukhumvit Soi 55
text: This serviced apartment is new one on Sukhumvit Soi 55. It is not very close to train stations, but there is a complementary shuttle to the nearest BTS station, Thong Lo, so the distance to the station would not be a problem at all. Taxis are readily available as well. The building as well as room are of course very new and functional. In the building, there are a lot of common space and facilities that you can use such as coffee shop, meeting space, library, gym, rooftop swimming pool, patter range, and panoramic onsen (hot tub). We stayed in a junior suite, which was quite spacious and had everything you need including fridge, washing machine, microwave, hot water pot, cable TV, DVD... The bed and couch were also nice. The room had both dinning table and working desk, so we got enough space to work as well. And a bath tub to add. Seven eleven is just across the street, so you can have your necessary supplies easily even after late night drinking. Basically not much to complain for the price we got (USD80 inclusive of tax on Agoda), but some points for improvement would be: (1) WIFI: extremely slow. It needs to be significantly faster. (2) Gym: a water server and hand towels should be installed. Currently only machines. (3) Onsen: this is only open for men? My wife could not enjoy it. (4) New apartment smell: this was not a big problem for us, and it might go away after a while, but some others might not like it. It's a kinda strong smell at least for now. All in all, good property. If we can get the same price, we would come back to this serviced apartment again!

author: SuavesTrips
title: Good Bang for your Buck!
text: I stayed at the Residence Inn Los Angeles Downtown Burbank for 4 nights while there on business. We got the government rate, which was surprisingly hard to find in anywhere that wasn’t downtown LA. Every room has a kitchen with a full size fridge, dishwasher, stove top, and microwave. They provide all the basics, stone ware and flat ware, etc. I stayed in a studio, which was spacious and accommodating. There was a living room area, a dining table with 2 chairs, as well as a king size bed. There was coffee and water in the lobby and in the evenings, they put out oatmeal raisin and chocolate chip cookies. Breakfast is served daily and is included in your rate. It’s a great spread, with something for everyone! They have eggs and some kind of breakfast meat (bacon, sausage, etc), there’s a waffle station, a variety of breads, oatmeal, fruit, and cold cereals. I observed a wide range of people staying there, with some of them appearing to be there long term. It was located near shopping and food options. The hotel service was really good. They brought me some ice, even though there are icemakers in the suites. My colleague asked for an upgrade, as a rewards emember and was accommodated as soon as they had a vacancy.

author: H9965FSjeanf
title: Love this hotel!
text: Check in: Mariana was awesome! She was by herself at the front desk, handling all the activity going on around her with ease and a smile! She checked us into room 544, with a great view of the pool/courtyard area. She mentioned the evening reception and the food truck that was in the parking lot! She was also able to recommend a near by restaurant for dinner the first night and a delicious pizza place that would deliver the second night, when we didn't want to go out after a long day being tourists. (Mama and Papa's, which we really enjoyed. Fast delivery and the pizza was piping hot when it arrived) The room: The rooms are very spacious, with designated space for everything--cook, work, relax or sleep. Especially nice was being able to open the windows to let in fresh air. You can hear the freeway with the windows open, and while we thought it would be a problem, we didn't even notice after 5 mins. The only suggestion I would have would be to have some of the great smelling lotion in the bathroom and perhaps an additional trash can near the desk. The hotel: Conveniently located just a few short miles from the Burbank airport, easy to find. Also close proximity to the activities we had planned (TMZ tour :) Jimmy Kimmel and the Farmers Market. The free buffet breakfast is incredible, a huge selection with something to please everyone. OH and free wifi! All in all, a great little vacation. We wouldn't hesitate to stay here again and highly recoomend it.

author: EatVegJohn
title: No Love for Platinum Marriott Rewards Members - Dishonest
text: First, I was not recognized as a platinum rewards member upon checkin. I stay 75+ nights at marriott hotels around the world to achieve this status. As a platinum guest, I and generally provided certain benefits due to my loyalty. I had requested an upgraded suite at checkin, and was told the hotel was "sold out". I have stayed at this hotel nearly a half dozen times, and not once have I been upgraded to a larger room than was originally booked. I understand that being a plainum member doesnt guarantee any type of room type upgrade which I respect.. I do not respect, when the hotel is DISHONEST and says "they are sold out" so there is no upgrade vs. saying honestly, we do not upgrade platinums. Today I was told the hotel is sold out, but I can go on marriott.com and book a one-bedroom suite (3 of them on one reservation). I do not appreciate dishonesty at any hotels. If they dont want to upgrade platinums to suites, thats fine, just be honest. Other than that, they charge $16 for parking which is pretty much all the hotels in the area. If you have more than one car, they will charge you $16 per each car per night. The other thing is that they do not replace the dish brush after every guest, so it can be nasty and unsanitary. Most residence inn's provide sealed sponges. Other than these things, the property is clean and tidy and in good shape otherwise. So if your a platinum and expecting an upgrade. Stay elsewhere.

author: liliudlesofaloha
title: Front Desk Staff Needs Class in Customer Service
text: My family and I stayed here while having a fumigation in our home. This is a fairly new facility and very clean. The downfall is the noise from the freeway if you are on that side of the building. Very loud! Also the front desk person, a female, was not very receptive in checking in and tried to overcharge. Luckily I had the email stating the rate, but she had to honor what was on it. She had an attitude and when checking out, I needed some help with luggage. This same woman, answered the call for my request and nonchalantly said “if I can find someone”.. total attitude. Some time went by and I called again.. she said “I’ll send someone”. She sent a maid, who spoke very little English. The maid was very nice and helped me get my things to the car, even though when entering the lobby area, the front desk attendant (same person), blurted “she can’t help you to the car”. I didn’t like this front desk attendant’s attitude towards me. Will never stay again!!!!!

author: 879philippeg
title: Good rooms and great customer service
text: I booked that hotel because at that time of the year in Burbank ( end of July), all hotels are overpriced and full of tourists and families. This one was in the middle range of price I wanted for a one night business trip. The location of the hotel is both good and bad, thanks to its being right by the 5 freeway. When I pulled in, I noticed that many rooms are facing the freeway, I just hope I would not get one but they did give me a room literally on top of the freeway and despite the reinforced sound isolation on the windows, I had to ask for another room. The noise was such that I knew I would not sleep through the night and I needed my sleep in preview of my next day meeting. I explained all that to the front desk and they said they were sorry but they could not help, the hotel being fully booked. I was not happy. 30min later, the front desk called me telling me that they had a room for me, having just had a cancellation. I was the very happy. So in a nutshell, that hotel has rooms that are all small suites with everything to cook a meal in ( no restaurant ). They also offer free breakfast and parking is reasonably priced for LA. For one person, the rooms are large enough. And the exercise room is well equipped. I would recommend that hotel for price and convenience but be careful when you book and ask for a room that does not face the freeway! The staff is very nice and professional.

author: davidjD7521VE
title: Everything you need except a movie deal!
text: I was in Burbank to pitch a television show to WB studios in Burbank in 2016. I know that's a long time ago but I didn't want to let this stay go un-raved about. When we arrived we were greeted with top notch customer service. The hotel was meticulously manicured. The rooms were excellent. Great size and the layout was outstanding. I got a comfortable nights rest before the big day and woke up to the nicest wake-up call ever! Car service that they set up for me was right on time and I left the hotel for my meeting feeling confident! Too bad the producers I met with didn't stay at the Residence Inn because if they did I might have made a great deal. Oh well... Can't win them all. I had a nice cry in the soft pillow when I returned to my room and a dip in the pool was a refreshing break from the "reality". Thanks, Residence Inn Burbank! Hopefully, I will be able to come back again.. who knows.

author: BeckyK548
title: Perfect locale for sightseeing
text: We chose this location for its close proximity to all the places we wanted to visit. It is close to both Universal Studios and Warner Brothers, and allows for quick access to the freeway to travel to farther destinations. The hotel itself is within walking distance to a couple of restaurants, and is a short drive to a Ralph's grocery store. I actually walked to Ralph's. It's a few blocks away and took me about twenty minutes to get there. We had a corner room which was spacious. I wasn't real fond of the layout of the room, however. The bed faces the bathroom which has a separate sink and vanity area, but no door to it to provide privacy. Also, there is only one TV that swivels between the living area, which has a sleeper sofa, and the bedroom area. We enjoyed having a kitchen with a fridge to keep drinks cold. A hot breakfast is served every morning. Eggs, biscuits with gravy, fruit, cold cereal, and waffles are some of the food items offered. The breakfast area was never crowded and there was ample seating available during the times we were there. All of the staff we encountered were friendly and helpful. I would recommend that if you are a light sleeper that you request a room away from the freeway. The noise did not bother my husband or son, but it was very noticeable to me.

author: Sunny-waters
title: Good Place to Stay with Everything Under Excellent Control
text: We only stayed two nights, but, it was amazing how everything was run so smoothly in this hotel,...from the friendly and helpful staff to the clean, comfortable room. We had a studio king room and we loved the comfortable layout. The swivel tv stand was an excellent idea. The front desk staff was always friendly and helpful always answering questions with a friendly smile. It was a nice touch to leave a message on our phone asking how we like our room. The breakfast had a good variety to satisfy all different appetites. However, some of the hot items were cooked pretty poorly. For example, the breakfast sausage patties and potatoes had no taste and tasted like cardboard. The cantaloupe and pineapple tasted old on the second morning. The orange juice tasted watered down. One thing we missed in our room was a room safe. Would be nice to have one. Liked that they slipped our bill under our door on the morning of check out so that we don't have to check out at the front desk. This hotel ran like clockwork. Everything was in place. Everything was clean and neat. Had a wonderful stay.

author: bornnorb
title: Great location, comfortable stay, great service staff
text: This was our first trip to L.A. - decided on Burbank which turned out to be a great location to travel from when going to all areas of L.A.; Warner Brothers tour (right in town), Universal Studios (5 miles away), Disneyland, Getty Center museum, Santa Monica Pier, LA Zoo, Hollywood walk of fame, etc. The hotel has plenty of parking and our room was very comfortable. We stayed for a week and the entire staff was always friendly and accommodating. The breakfast crew worked especially hard and remained cheerful and helpful all through the crazy morning rush. The breakfast buffet had a decent variety; scrambled eggs, potatoes, sausage, canadian bacon, biscuits, salsa, fresh fruit, yogurt, muffins, toast, bagels, danish and make your own waffles with various toppings-berries, chocolate chips & whip cream. There was orange juice, soda, decent coffee and a good selection of teas. The pool was nice and there were plenty of lounges, chairs and umbrellas. As a bonus we were greeted each time by an adorable little "resident" lizard that our daughter named Kevin! When you come back after being out all day there is fresh lemonade and cookies waiting in the lobby. They also have "evening socials" in breakfast area the first couple of nights of the week and have light food for guests - burgers,hot dogs,tacos,soda,chips,candy etc. Our daughter played games (uno/blokus) with a lovely family and thoroughly enjoyed herself. - a nice touch, Marriott! We are Marriott Rewards members and have never stayed at a residence inn before. This was a wonderful experience for us and we will definitely stay here again when we come back to L.A. A special thank you to Joseph (front desk) for making our stay memorable - he helped us find the perfect room and gave us great suggestions on where to eat and what to see.

author: drdmromeo
title: One of the Best Residence Inns
text: when my family travels, we love staying at the Residence Inn since it is perfect for a family. Yet it's also perfect for business travelers as well.This hotel was so much more comfortable to me than glitzy 4 star hotels I have stayed at while working in LA. It feels private, and relaxed, definitely not a place that tries to be "cool and hip" and a place to be "seen." I had a large studio type living space, with everything I needed. I had coffee maker, microwave and free microwave popcorn, cook top, kitchen table and chairs, large couch and comfortable chair for reading, full size bridge, flat screen TV, even a dishwasher. A desk with lots of ports. High speed internet. super comfortable Marriott bed. Great natural lighting, too. Free breakfast in the morning and excellent exercise facility. There was also a really nice outside seating area, with comfy outside stuffed couches and chairs, a fire pit, and pool that had lovely landscaping. Free parking! I particularly appreciated the front desk -- great service, really. I asked for a later check out and received it free of charge. I asked for help securing a ride back to LAX and they set me up with a town car for the same price of a taxi (cray, it turned out to be a stretch limo with full bar). It is also in a terrific location, close to downtown Burbank.

author: MARIE1960
title: Wonderful Stay in Burbank, CA
text: We stayed here for 3 nights while traveling through California on Spring Break in April and we were so happy with everything this hotel offered us! First, I want to say how nice and courteous the front desk staff were. We so appreciate them helping us with directions, etc. Also, I am a clean fanatic and always take my Lysol wipes and spray with me when I travel and you can leave them home if you stay here! The rooms were so comfortable and clean and spacious. Loved them! There is even candy in a candy dish! Very nice touch. I can't say enough about the receptions that they have for guests on Mon-Wed. They have complimentary wine, beer, soft drinks and appetizers that can substitute for a light dinner! The complimentary breakfasts were great! They had everything from eggs, breakfast meats, hash browns, cereals, fruit, yogurt and waffles! If you are traveling in the L.A. area, this hotel and Burbank is where you want to stay. Burbank is a great location because you can avoid the freeway traffic and still visit Hollywood and Beverly Hills without traffic! Thanks to everyone at the Residence Inn Burbank, CA !!

author: AmandaK131
title: Fine if you like your breakfast disposable
text: We stayed in one of the studio apartments - a room with a king sized bed and a good sized kitchen with living area. There was a lot of furniture in the space which made the room seem cramped somehow. The internet was free and fast, the shower was nice, there were plenty of little amenities in the room. The pool was fine for splashing around in. The car was safe in the car park. The reception staff were extremely friendly and professional. The business center worked perfectly. The little shop saved us when we arrived at midnight without dinner. The main downsides were - a mysterious repeated noise throughout the night which sometimes ascended into a loud "crack" - I didn't investigate but wondered if it was the fridge de-icer. The bed was ridiculously uncomfortable (hard). The door didn't close properly on its own (running the risk of leaving it ajar without realizing).
