The worst downside was the breakfast which was (a) not that inspiring and (b) used so many disposable materials (plates, bowls, cups, cutlery) that I actually felt uncomfortable eating there because of the waste generated. And at the weekend the breakfast area was completely trashed because so many people were trying to get food. There was cereal all over the bench, waffle mixture pouring out of the machine, and the acrid smell of burnt toast. We will be staying here again (work's hotel of choice) but I'm not certain I'd come back by choice.

author: Travelsaloth
title: Great Place to Stay!
text: This is a very nice hotel. Our room was clean and quiet. We were staying for a couple of days and wanted to cook, so this was a perfect choice. However, Black Angus was an easy walk and there were a great many other dining choice close. I didn't use the outdoor pool, but it was heated and others were enjoying it. The fitness room was well equipped. We enjoyed beverages around the fire pit in the evening. The full breakfast was better then most. Eggs were good, the oatmeal wasn't runny. The only one who couldn't find something they liked would be a non breakfast eater. The staff was friendly and more then willing to help us with anything we needed. Parking is $15/day, but considering the location this is pretty normal. I liked the main stairway down to the lobby. I kept picturing someone making an entrance if they so desired. My only complaint was the bed was a bit hard for me. It didn't feel as luxurious as other Marriott beds. However, this definitely is individual choice and does not affect the fact that this hotel deserves and excellent rating.

author: 672donaldm
title: Great Hotel, Convenient location
text: We stayed here in early January for about a week as we were visiting family in LA. Loved this hotel and will stay here again, next time we are in California. Great room, a little different from typical Residence as this hotel is a high rise. But you still have a kitchenette, so you can have meals in room if you want. But they also have an awesome free breakfast in the morning, but get their earlier to get all the best stuff. We also used the fitness area. It's small, but there are a couple of treadmills, a bike and a weight machine on the second floor. They also have a great outside pool on the second floor. The location is very convenient, close to all major roadways, and the city center is easy walking distance. We walked to many local restaurants and my wife went shopping, all within easy reach of hotel. They have underground parking (as well as outside), which is also where you check-in. We used the underground parking because it was so convenient, especially packing and unpacking the car. The staff was great and very friendly. We are so happy we decided to stay here as it was closer to our family than other places we had tried. In fact when you pull out of the garage you can go left or right directly onto I-5!

author: kasens
title: Great Stay for Business or Families
text: Recently stayed at this hotel for a week in January. It was part business and part leisure. The hotel is conveniently located in downtown Burbank with easy walking to San Fernando Blvd with a ton of restaurant options. The mall is just a bit further down, but still a nice walk. Also, there is Target, Best Buy, and other restaurants within a short drive. The hotel room is clean, nicely furnished and equipped for the long term traveler and worked well for us traveling with a toddler. The kitchen is well equipped and they will even go grocery shopping for you! It's nice to stay at a hotel that actually has proper black out curtains, which make the room very dark during the day so my son could nap! Breakfast is included each morning and was changed up slightly each day. Three days a week, the hotel offers a reception with snacks and drinks. As others have mentioned, the hotel is right on Hwy 5. If possible, ask for an interior room. I can only imagine that the outer rooms will hear the traffic. If you are concerned with the noise, either bring earplugs or a sound machine in case you cannot get a different room. However, others in our party that did have an outer room said they did not hear the traffic. We did hear a train a few times, but it stopped by 9pm. The staff was courteous and very helpful with all our questions. The only negative issue I had was the door to the bathroom did not block out any sounds. Which could be, ummm, disruptive.

author: cynsmith61
title: Great Residence Inn
text: This is the 4th time we have stayed at this Residence Inn in Downtown Burbank. It is a great Marriott property. The customer service is always friendly, courteous, and helpful. The rooms are always fresh, clean, and well stocked. Even the Studio has plenty of room!! My only criticism is the breakfast. We attempted to eat their on a Monday and there was still 20 minutes left, and everything was getting put away. And we were not getting very welcoming looks from the breakfast staff. THIS is highly unusual for a Residence Inn. But that would not make me not want to return. I would happily stay here anytime I was in the area. It's in a great location, quiet and you have a view of the Burbank side of the Hollywood Hills. You are very close to the studios and just a hop off of Cahuenga Blvd to Hollywood. You really don't have to travel a freeway to get to Hollywood, Santa Monica, or Beverly Hills. Which is a plus in my book. And parking at only $15 and no tipping required (no valet) is another GREAT thing in this area. This property is great for business, couples, and families.

author: jordan57
title: You are kidding me?
text: Hotel is in great location . Pool is fine, breakfast is fine. Not impressed by anything else. First full day room was not cleaned . Complained and they apologized and sent someone to give towels . Next day housekeeping came and didn't leave toilet paper for one of the bathrooms. Oh by the way no lotion at this residence inn. Last but not least no blanket for pull out couch . We called to get one and they said there was one in the closet but we could come down and get one. Not one in closet . I was going to call down again but so angry for such bad service decided best not to at this time. . One more day in this low class Residence inn . Mr M would not be happy. Will be complaining to corporate. . Management obviously not the best .

author: Global_Thinker
title: Some good, mostly bad
text: I've stayed here before and this was my first choice for when my business brought me here again. However, this stay left much more to be desired. When I booked they didn't tell me that the only handicap room they had available was on the same floor and facing the pool. So, when I arrive with my friend (who is handicapped) they didn't have any handicap rooms available - except the noisy one facing the pool! We finally got them to find us a different room, but this one faced the I-5 freeway. We had to sleep with earplugs every night. The manager at least listened to our allergy concerns, however, I had no idea this was a pet-friendly hotel. They told us they only accept pets up to 50 lbs, however, while leaving for a meeting one day, a huge black lab that easily weighed over 120 lbs. (I'd understand if it was a service dog, but it wasn't.) The dog caused my allergies to severely act up and made me miss and have to re-schedule several meetings. Another issue was the maid. I don't want maid service when I stay at hotels, and it's good I didn't. One of the days I left around 10 am and the maid was cleaning the room just across the hall. When I returned at 6:30 pm that same maid was still "cleaning" the SAME room!!! Don't know what she was doing or why it takes that many hours to clean ONE room. When we brought this concern to the manager, he thankfully took proactive action. I'm not sure what he did or said to the maid, but I didn't see that maid on our floor for the rest of our stay. The last issue was noisy people on the floor above us. The front desk staff and the manager were the only redeeming qualities of this hotel. They were kind and professional. Overall, I most likely won't be coming back to this hotel.

author: JJHII568A
title: Good Location and Convenient to Hollywood attractions.
text: I chose this hotel because of it’s proximity to Hollywood, not too close and not too far away. It’s quick drive to the Hollywood Blvd. and Highland Ave. parking garage. I was not disappointed with the surrounding area, it was very nice and I felt safe walking around at night. Also, there are several restaurants within walking distance. As for the hotel itself, the staff was very helpful and professional and they made my wife and I feel welcome as their guests. Check in was expedited quickly and courteously not much else to say about that. I was not surprised in regards to the charges for self parking, it was a minimal charge. The room was a studio type with a bed, kitchen, bath, and a small sitting area with a couch. The room was very clean and appeared to be updated recently. The bed was a bit harder than I remembered Marriott beds to be and was not comfortable for my taste. The air conditioning system was a bit difficult to adjust, it worked great but was not easy to maintain a constant comfortable temperature. It was very quiet during our stay we did not hear any construction noise. The breakfast was adequate and had plenty of choices in my opinion. The area was clean and organized. All in all staying at the Residence Inn Burbank Downtown was a good experience and I would stay there again...

author: SamiGalaxy
title: A terrific spot in the heart of BURBANK!!
text: Chose this new RI for a 'staycation' in the LA area and really enjoyed it .. .. Freeway access (off and on) was easy with lots of parking (paid) .. .. Stayed in a lot of RIs but this room was really attractive with new Kohler fixtures and even visiting family members commented on hos nice the property and rooms were .. .. Even the sofa pullout bed seemed more comfortable .. .. The lobby/breakfast area is very attractive and the Mon-Wed Social hour was greatly appreciated > Loved the Fajitas, Rice & Beans .. .. ;))) Most of all though, the staff was top-rate > The PM desk staff were happy to greet me and JOSEPH even caughte me later to return a bag I had left on top of my car - Thanks Joseph!! I lve staying in RIs, but this one seemed exceptional .. .. Lots to do in the area with a BLACK ANGUS/BJ'S right next door with tons of restaurants one block up on San Frnando Road .. .. Greek, Hawaiian, Indian, you name it .. .. And, IKEA & In-N-Out further down the street .. .. I'LL BE BACK!!!

author: travelalotwithfamily
title: Glad we stayed here!
text: We stayed for 5 nights at the beginning of August. Great location. It's close to many of the tourist attractions, like Universal Studio, Hollywood, WB Studio Tour, Griffith Observatory etc. This hotel didn't look nice from the outside when we first saw it from the freeway exit. It's too close to the freeway and too low. However, when we get inside, it's nice and quiet. Check-in was smooth. Staff was cheerful with good manners. We used 80,000 Marriott Rewards points for our stay in a Studio. It's such a great value! It was much more spacious than we thought. Small full size kitchen came in handy. Complimentary breakfast is the main reason I chose Residence Inn, even though the breakfast area could get cramped at times. I'm glad I chose ths place for our short stay in LA. Glad we used our points for it.

author: JCKEW54
title: Nice Stay
text: We had a very nice over night stay at The Residence Inn. It was very close to many restaurants and shops in downtown Burbank. Our one room suite was very clean and comfortable. The bathroom, with Paul Mitchell amenities, was spacious and bright. A definate plus as far as I'm concerned! There was a full kitchen, which was nice to have. We had a long cross country road trip begining the next day and it was great to be able to buy water/soda for the drive and have a frig to put them in. Check in was easy and the staff was very attentive. Just had two minor issues: We called the front desk to ask them to contact the room above us. For about 45 minutes we listened to someone, very heavy footed, walking ( almost stomping ) back and forth across the room. They said they would take care of it. The pacing continued to the point where we had to call again. At this time the staff at the front desk informed me that there was no one in that room... I found that a little confusing & eerie. It eventually stopped. The other, as Platnium Elite members we would have appreciated a room with a view better than a brick wall and a parking lot. We would stay here again but would ask for a different room.

author: AI961
title: Nice hotel but beware of credit card overcharges!!!!
text: We stayed here for 10 nights and found the hotel very clean and well looked after. Everything in the room was perfect and located perfectly within walking distance to shops and restraunts. HOWEVER.................. When we first checked in they incorrectly charged our credit card $1000. They admitted this was a mistake on their part and reversed this. They then charged the card TWICE for $2500. We asked them to explain and they told us that it was a hold for any incidentals that occur during the stay. We thought $5000 was a bit extreme as our stay in total only came to $3200. They told us that is was be reversed before we checked out and our friends and I could split the room charges at the end of the stay. The next day we got a call saying that they tried to charge our card again for another $1000 but it was declined. We contacted the bank and they informed us they had now overdrawn our account because of all these charges. On the 10th day after various attempts to try to get the staff to fix this, we spent 1 and 1/2 hours in the reception area trying to check out but they wouldn't let us as their was $600 outstanding but we couldn't pay this as they STILL had not reversed the charges. They Finally admitted that the $5000 was a mistake on their part again!!!!!! They agreed to let us go and charge the account in a few days when the other charges had been reversed. we also then had problems checking into our accommodation in Las Vegas as they stuffed up our card. This experience ruined our stay in america as this was our first time here and made it extremely frustrating and stressful. It was unnecessary as all they had to do was do they accounting properly! They have a lack of communication skills and just blame other staff members when problems arise. USUALLY customers are always put first right?........... We recommend everyone be very cautious when staying here!!!

author: Gestur_Traustason
title: Great stay.
text: Stayed there two nights on our California Road-trip (San Francisco to San Diego). I drove past twice before seeing the entrance to the hotel. It’s more like an entrance to a parking lot. I will admit that once I found the entrance I noticed it was well marked but driving a busy street in a big city for the first time. Plenty of parking but you pay for it (reasonably priced). The reception was excellent. Quick check-in, free coffee, ice-water and cookies. The staff was very friendly and always had time to offer great advice and hints to make our experience better. If you are visiting LA for the first time then I strongly recommend you ask the staff for advice and hints on your planned activities. We went to Six Flags and the advice we got from the very friendly man in reception saved us both time and money (tip reg. online rebate). The two rooms we had were fantastic. Marriott tends to have good rooms but these were larger and better furnished than we had experienced. The kitchen was well equipped. The rooms were very clean, the beds great and we had a very enjoyable stay. Breakfast was good. Plenty of options and the staff very diligent in filling up. We used the self-service laundry, spent time at the pool and cooked steaks on the gas-barbeque in the courtyard. We also took part in a wine-tasting/mingle for guests. Overall this was a very enjoyable stay and I would not hesitate to visit there again or to strongly recommend this hotel to friends and family.

author: Carmen1318
title: Efficient and Excellent Value for 2-Bedroom Suites
text: stayed here with family. we had 9 people total stay in 2 separate suites. each suite came equipped with a kitchen, microwave, stove, refrigerator, and coffeemaker. There was a TV in each of the 2 bedrooms and a sofa and TV in the community living room/kitchen area. The bedrooms were a little small, but is very efficient for larger parties. the sofabed mattress was thin and not very comfortable. somehow i managed to fall asleep on it because i was exhausted that night. each of the 2 bathrooms has the sink area isolated from the bathroom, which is kind of inconvenient, if you are sharing the bathroom with the people in the bedroom. our room was also facing the freeway. there was a little noise from the traffic which would bother light sleepers. i am a heavy sleeper, so it didn't bother me. there is a pool on the 2nd level along with a fitness center. i used neither. parking is available to guests on the ground level. it is a garage built into the footprint of the building. not sure if it is extra. it is not gated and allows for easy, but unsecure access. we had a complimentary breakfast buffet the next morning. it was very good. they had scrambed eggs, sausage, milk/cereal, waffle makers, french toast, orange/apple juice, and fresh fruit.

author: jpinedo
title: Good Extended Stay
text: I would give this place a solid 4, not because it is a luxury property or anything but because it does a good job at what it needs to do. I stayed two weeks recently while moving to the area. The hotel overall was fairly new, though some of the furnishings looked a bit worn as if they might have come from another property. The front desk was very helpful and friendly and accommodated all requests I had, they even scanned and emailed documents for me. There is free wifi and the computers and printers in the lobby are also free. They welcomed my dog (40 lbs) with a $100 per stay pet fee. Not a bad deal considering some places charge you per night for your pet. The included breakfast was nothing special but it was nice that it was there and there were a broad range of options: cereal, oatmeal, eggs, potatoes, yogurt, granola, fruit, waffle station, breads. On site coin laundry for a reasonable fee ($2.25/load) was very convenient for extended stay guests. It was an easy 10 minute walk to many shops and restaurants in Burbank's little downtown area, and access to the 5 freeway was convenient. I did not notice the freeway noise but I will say that my place in Chicago was located near both the el train and expressway so it is possible it is loud and I just didn't notice. There was a loud noise that I did notice above the bathroom, it sounded like the air conditioner or something like that, but it was only intermittent and did not bother me. Parking was $15/night which was sort of annoying, but expected for most hotel parking. So overall minus one for the meh breakfast, the a/c noise, and having to pay for parking. Everything else was great!

author: cynsmith61
title: A Beautiful Hotel and Excellent Location
text: My 76 year old mother and I took my sons ages 18 and 20 to California and stayed at the Residence Inn Downtown in Burbank. It was a beautiful hotel. So fresh and new. Beautifully decorated and the most comfortable beds we have ever slept on. The staff was friendly and helpful. The location is terrific. Downtown Burbank is a fun town filled with wonderful restaurants and stores. The breakfast at the hotel is really nice. The waffles are yummy and they try to switch up the eggs a little every day. Yes, they are always scrambled but some days they are served with sausage, some days sausage gravy and biscuits and other days with taco shells with all the fixings. And the home fries are also very good. They have a nice assortment of fruits as well. I really cannot say enough good things about this property. We stayed in a 2 bedroom suite and I truly feel that the price was a very good deal for what you get. I would absolutely stay here again. We travel frequently to this area, and this is by far the best value for your money.

author: gallopar
title: good overall but some issues
text: Chose hotel on basis of revews on trip advisor. This is a summary of good and not so good points; Good looking hotel that looks new and modern. Had a 2 bedroom (smaller size) apartment that adequately catered for our family of 5. 2 bathrooms was a big positive for a family with teenagers as was the 3 flat screen tv's. Our room was facing side street and did not encounter any problems with outside street noise or noise from adjoining rooms. We stayed for 4 nights and i would rate housekeeping as good. On the negative side reports of noisy airconditioning are very true. We were lucky in that we did not need to run aircon for long periods of time as it would have been impossible to sleep with that noise. Quality of breakfast is poor and Hotel closes breakfast down at 9am on weekdays. I have never heard of such an early finish time for breakfast however after making the effort to get up early one day we decided we were not missing much and didn't bother there after. Breakfast area is very tight. Hotel doesn't have a restaurant however many food outlets in the area will provide delivery to your room. It is about a 10-15min walk to downtown shopping area. The Burbank area that Hotel is situated in is serviced by a cab company called city cab. We were ripped off by a cab driver on our first trip from the hotel so I would suggest caution if you are a tourist and to get a quote up front for the approx cost of your trip or use an alternative private transport company. I do not blame Hotel for this situation and they were most apologetic after it occurred. After making a complaint to the cab company they refunded the amount overcharged which was appreciated. Overall a fairly good experience. .

author: Bo94114
title: Great find
text: Hi, Stayed here for 1 night. I found the location to be very close to everything we needed. Room was of good quality. A bit tight on space around one side of the bed. As mentioned previously the air con is a problem here. I tried opening the windows and the freeway noise was too loud. When the window was closed it was not an issue. full sized appliances. Breakfast was good with plenty to choose from. comfortable bed. Parking was plentiful under the hotel and outside. Plenty of restaurants nearby as is shopping. Harry's Family Restaurant was a nice find down the road with excellent prices and good food. This hotel is a good value when compared to my last stay at the Hilton in Glendale. I will stay here at the Residence Inn when I come back here next year. This was not much further of a drive to where I needed to be.

author: Antoinella
title: Works Well For Family Stay in L.A,
text: The Residence Inn in Burbank is a year old property that still has some of the freshness of a new hotel. Beds are comfortable, linens are very nice, quality of towels fluctuated (some were thick and soft, some were thin, older and scratchy). The hotel management needs to watch to make sure that this hotel does not lose its newness too soon. I stayed with my family of four in a two bedroom unit that was smaller than other Residence Inns we had stayed in previously(yet was decorated with more style), but worked very well for us during our stay in the L.A. area. The Residence Inn concept of having a full kitchen (microwave, cooktop and oven, dishwasher and stainless steel sink) and living room (albeit small) with three large screen TV's (one in living room, one in each bedroom) and free internet access makes traveling with older kids terrific, as everyone has a bit of space to themselves after returning from a day of sightseeing. It was great to bring food back to the suite to heat up, or to prepare simple lunches when we were tired of eating out. There is one main drawback to this hotel. The many comments in Trip Advisor about the noisy/overly cool/strongly blowing gusts air conditioning system are all true .Our A/C system made it difficult to converse from one bedroom to the other. The highway noises directly behind our suite were a loud tradeoff when we cut the A/C. While no one in our family was kept awake by the various sounds, it was a distraction when we tried to talk with visitors to our suite. . Still, the positive aspects of the Residence Inn Burbank outweighed the noise problems for us. If management can work out the noise and A/C issues, and keep the hotel from aging too quickly, it could become our favorite L.A. hotel for family vacations.

author: club22
title: 2nd best Residence Inn I've been to
text: First of all, I'm glad Residence Inn have come a long way, from old musty properties (we stuck with it bec of the kitchenette). I am a Marriott member for 5 years so I have been to A LOT of different Marriott properties (from Renaissance to Marriott to Courtyard). This property has modern/contemporary decor and larger suites. I read the reviews before making my reservations. For me, this is 2nd best Residence Inn (I vote the one in Denver City Center Residence Inn as #1 altho they have no pool in Denver, I left a review for that property). Anyway, we stayed for the weekend (fri-sun) to go to Universal Studios so I only heard the train once Fri night past 10pm. I requested for a room facing the courtyard to avoid the freeway noise (although I did still hear the cars when the AC was off). There were just some kids at the pool/bbq pit late at night that were noisy. We were on the 5th, the pool on the 2nd (so don't stay on the 2nd flr unless you want immediate access to the pool but it also means more noise) I didn't complain bec, hey, its summer! Also bring your own towel from the room to the pool, they go fast and it took them more than an hour when we informed them there were no more towels left. The AC is strong but the vents were properly adjusted facing up the ceiling, it does hit the person (on the 1 king bed suite) on the head I just blocked it off w a pillow. It took a while of adjusting the temp (I set it to LO 76 instead of AUTO bec that would turn on/off which would make you wake up more) it helps filter off the sound of the kids and cars outside. If you are a light sleeper then maybe this is not the place for you but for the location (4 blocks to downtown eateries) its not a bad deal considering you get free breakfast whereas other hotels in the area may not offer breakfast (it all adds up). My other choice was Beverly Hills Residence Inn but I read their rooms were smaller. I guess if you stay during the weekend the noise from the freeway may be less frequent and more during the weekday rush hour. I was not charged for parking so I don't think the parking fee is strictly enforced (unless its peak season). Staff were cordial and I would consider staying here again if I am to return to the area.

author: ballerina
title: great hotel noisy air conditioning
text: this is a great suite hotel. we have 2 young kids and booked a 2 bedroom suite. it was not the more expensive corner ones (which we did stay in the first night as the hotel was overbooked), but the basic one. the room was very clean, comfortable and just what we wanted. although the busy street was outside we didn't hear it at all. The staff were generally friendly and helpful. The parking was great. The free breakfast was pretty good, although a bit too unhealthy for my liking. The situation of the hotel is great, you can easily get to supermarkets and the shopping mall, and good restaurants nearby. Room internet free access really good. the pool was on the small side but very warm and clean and we were in it every day and really enjoyed it. I only had 2 problems with the hotel were 1/ the terribly noisy air conditioning. i like to have fresh air at night but just couldn't turn it on. it was so loud. 2/ there is a great self laundry but there was no washing power. when i asked at reception they said they wouldn't be getting any for 3 days...

author: vickier
title: Beautiful new hotel
text: My 17 year old son and I stayed at this hotel from March 21st until March 24th. We wanted to stay at a hotel that was near both the NBC Studios and Universal Studios. We stayed in a studio room with a king size bed. This is a new hotel that opened in October or November of 2007. The rooms were gorgeous. There was a flat screen HDTV in the room and very nice furniture. There is a small kitchen area in the room complete with pots, pans, plates, cups and utensils if you want to eat or cook in your room. You can really tell that this is a new hotel by the improved lighting and furnishings of older Residence Inns. The pool area was nice, but there is no hot tub and I thought that was a bit unusual for a new hotel. Sam (who checked us in) was fantastic. He was friendly and efficient. This hotel is in a good location, but it was right next to the freeway and it was noisy at night. I asked for an inside room, but that didn't help with the noise factor. You could hear trains every day as well, so this hotel was near the train tracks, too. If you are a light sleeper, this may not be a good hotel for you. Otherwise, this hotel was great.

author: ahnion777
title: Absolutely Fantastic and Brand New
text: I've got to say that this is probably one of the nicest hotel's I've been to due to the brand new design and push that Marriott is doing with their new Residence Inns. Ritz, 4 seasons, and Waldorf may have spa style bathrooms and roomservice, but that's the only thing better than a hotel like this. The decor of the hotel room was literally like a very well furnished apartment with artwork on the walls, glass center pieces on coffee tables, and espresso brown colored dinning table and chair sets. The kitchen area was granite or marble and the refrigerator was stainless steal. I could literally live here and be happy for many years. The bed was extremely comfortable and bathroom had a glass shower door. Honestly, an extremely comfortable stay with absolutely no hassle. In fact, when checking in, an irate and extremely rude guest berated the front desk manager in front of me. I was extremely impressed on how she held her bearing and remained polite. Even after letting the guest stay at the hotel's best room with no upgrade fee, the guest was extremely rude to the manager, even asking how old she was and demanding to speak with someone other than her. She calmingly replied that she did not need to tell her how old she was and if she wanted to speak with someone else, that she could call in on Monday because she was the person in charge. Although she was young looking, she handled herself with poise and maturity. I was impressed. Only drawbacks was that because the hotel was so new, there was no shuttle to the airport. But all in all, the hotel could have easily been a new and hip apartment complex in an up and coming neighborhood like Seattle, Austin, and other cities that caters to young professionals.

author: vyasjh
title: First time in Bangkok in hotel season
text: The hotel is booked by the travellor, we stayed for 3 nights with family. Average hotel with average restaurant. Restaurant is not good for vegetarians. Tripadvisor rating is 3.5 star but according to me it is 2starhotel. Nothing special in staying except the location of hotel for those who want to some shopping. Bangkok famous Indra market (10 min walk) palladium and platinum fashion mall (20 min. Walk)for all short of garments is very near. Hotel rooms are neat and clean but area wise small rooms. WiFi- Hotel provide free wifi and it is good. Restaurant : Average Hotel location for shopping: Very good ,BTS train connectivity is also near. Near by station is Phaya Thai. Hotel service : Not tried Toiletries : They are providing some toilatories Refrigerator in room is full of beverages and liquor but double the cost from market. They are also placing the condom in the room if you are travelling from conservative country like India than your kids first question is What is this? And you have to answer. I ask to remove from the room but the denied.

author: 17SUN2014
title: Good enough
text: Decent and clean hotel. Helpful staff. Excellent breakfast. Good aircon in rooms (you will value this in Thailand) Check-in was quick. 1000 Thai Baht deposit required at check-in. I've learnt that this is common practice in Thailand. I can vouch for The Seasons Bangkok Siam Hotel and say that they actually do return your deposit without any complications or scams. Very easy to get to from Bangkok Airport - take train (40 Baht) from airport to Rajaprarop station. It is a short walk from there. Or u can take a taxi/tuk-tuk from station to The Seasons hotel (very cheap as it is a very short distance). Good location - very easy to get to places of interest. Many taxi/tuk-tuk drivers wait outside hotel. Beware, these drivers will exploit the fact that you are a tourist. A short stroll down/up the street will get you much better taxi fares. Metered taxi is very cheap - if they actually use the meter. Be sure to insist on this.

author: sanjosems
title: Good and budget friendly
text: Actually this review is already very late. Nevertheless, I feel like I need to share. My family and sister-in-law stayed in this hotel last year (5th May 2013). I booked 2 standard double rooms for 5 days and 4 nights. All-in-all we are 4 people. The hotel is simple, but it is clean and the staff are very friendly to the guests. The room is equipped with a small fridge, a little sofa, TV, and a digital safebox (which I see as very important to have). They do housekeep the room everyday and replenish the fridge with bottled water for free. The toilet and bathroom is well maintained as well as the room itself. The location is just a short walk to the famous Pratunam Market where you can buy a lot of cheap and good items from clothing, bags, etc. The hotel is strategically located alongside the road where public buses travel and is also a walking distance to train stations which makes roaming around the major places of Bangkok quite easy. It serves good buffet breakfast which cater to western, local, and Indian people. We checked out noon time. Our flight back home is at 8pm but the hotel allowed us to safekeep our luggages while we had our last hours roaming and shopping at Bangkok. I really appreciate this gesture by the hotel staff. I didn't have any problem during my stay. In fact this is my 2nd time on this hotel. The first time is with my workmates few years back. I wouldn't mind coming back to this hotel and in fact, I recommend it to friends and people who would like to have a convenient location to stay in Bangkok.

author: stratcat11
title: Hmmm, yeah ok
text: Ok, well, it wasn't bad. The room was ordinary, but clean, with a fridge, bathroom and tv. All you need really. Like I said, not bad. No wifi in the room. There is wifi in the foyer, and you can buy an internet card to use on their computers. The food... Hmm. Ever had a spicy bruschetta? Neither had we! There was chilli on it, and more vinegar than a drunken sailor.! Don't have the bruschetta! Service was very slow, especially considering we were the only 2 in the restaurant (until an entire extended family arrived). A vegetarian pizza was served, with chicken on it. Hmm. 'Nuff said about that. The front desk staff were nice however. We had all we needed, and got what we paid for.

author: whi1989
title: Not very good
text: We stayed for 3 nights during our visit to Bangkok. Our impression. When we first came in, we got a free welcoming fruit punch juice. Was quite ok except too sweet. The receptionists were friendly. The guy who took our luggage to keep was very friendly. The services were good except that they wanted to charge us 8 bahts for a phone call to our tour guide. The lobby was ok except it was thronged by Indians. Freaking noisy and talk loudly spoiling our trip. The hotel room was ok except that during the noon, the shower will be freaking hot while at nite and in the morning, the water will be very cold. Hope the hotel can do something about the shower and noise pollution. Breakfast was ok, nothing too fancy. Sausages and hams as usual. Wifi-ed at the lobby thus usually crowded in the nite. Location wise, 20mins walk from BTS, very near 7-eleven and pizza hut. 20mins walk to Baiyoke Tower. Go there because the B-Gallery sells good things at low price. You'll be amazing. Overall, there are better places but if you're not high on budget and don't mind the indians shouting at night, this is a good place.

author: pco_13
title: Horrible, sleepless nights in Bangkok
text: Pictures perfect on the reservation website, but it's like going for a blind date. Once you saw her from far, you wanted to turn around and head back home. Lousy and cramp lobby with too many hotel guests and their luggage all over the place. The hotel seems to serve a particular group of clientele; even the restaurant has a special section for them and the advertisement in the elevators confirms the fact. Shower head in the bathtub was dirty and moldy. The towel was stained; I understand that the price we paid, you got the used towels from other AccorHotel, but come on...when the towel was stained, wouldn't it be time to retire the towel? The wall between the room was thin. The guests next door happened to leave for their international flight super early in the morning; I heard all the bang on the doors and the drag sound on the floor. The hotel is not located near the Skytrain or subway stations. You need to walk a few blocks if you don't mind the sun during the day. I used to stay in the crowd shopping areas and I think next time I will stay in those areas again. This hotel is a bit too far from the action. Anyway, we won't stay here again. Price-wise, you can find a better place. We don't recommend this place. It's deceiving!

author: cool_marvz
title: Good value for money
text: Hotel - we were given a room on the 5th floor but with the next door building's wall as our view, not that it really mattered as we only wanted a bed for our backs. The room was neat, clean and tidy as is typical of accor hotels. The hotel is generally clean but the carpeting on the hallways is worn out and faded. Refurbishment is in the pipeline I hope. Location - the hotel's location is ideal as it is along a thoroughfare so buses, taxis, and tuk-tuks abound in the area. You can easily go to any part of the city without any hassle except of course for the horrendous traffic that Bangkok is infamous for. It's also walking distance to the train and sky station as well as the Victory Monument. The Pratunam Market is also easily accessible. My friend and I walked to and from Pratunam market due to bad traffic. The MBK, Isetann and neighbouring malls are also readily accessible. Food - the breakfast buffet in this accor hotel is by far the best I had seen compared to the buffets I've tried in accor hotels in Europe. All Seasons Bangkok's offering is lavish compared to its counterparts in Europe so if people are complaining I don't really understand. There is enough choice for everyone - mostly Asian food (noodles, rice, soups, a wide selection of fruits, etc.) which should be expected. Service is okay, the staff are generally polite and accommodating. We arrived early and left our belongings with them to explore Bangkok while we waited for our room to be ready. They were very helpful with directions although they (staff at the main restaurant) struggled explaining in English. Overall, I would say it's good value for money and would recommend for those who are looking for a decent and affordable hotel in Bangkok.

author: /undefined
title: Horrible hotel do not stay here
text: We checked in at 12:30 AM we were so tired from a 20 plane ride. The room is so out dated and frumpy it does not look like the pictures on the hotel web site. My bed linen had yellow stains on it looks like excrement and some some sticky stains which looked like body fluid. I politely called the front desk if I could have new sheets. They sent me one and I even helped to make the bed feeling sorry that I'm causing a fuss, I tipped the guy who change the linens. The front desk person however, was very curt and unfriendly. Then maybe to get even they called us at 4AM mind you we'd just got to bed at 1 AM. I called the next morning to ask why they set up a wake-up call that was not requested they denied that there was one. We were 2 people in the room and we were awakened. The tour package they offer in the hotel was for 5,000Baht, the travel agent next door only charged 1,100Baht for a whole day tour. Also, the web-site says that it is only a 5 minute walk to the Victory monument BTS station. It's more like 20 minutes away to walk there, and you have to go up the overpass bridge to cross. There are no good restaurants or banks near this hotel. The towels and sheets are so old they are grey and murky instead of white. The walls are so thin that you can hear the people in the next room. I stayed here for 2 nights, never,, never stay here. You will walk a lot to get somewhere or pay for taxi everywhere and be stuck in traffic.

author: DelhiNeeraj007
title: EXELLENT LOCATION FOR INDIANS
text: good hotel with best location. indian food are easily available near the hotel. hotel serves very limited variety of indian food. breakfast was not good. we had just coffee and bread butter jam. close to indira market. (best market for indians who wants to buy lcd and led). taxi's are easily available. tuk tuk charges more than taxi's. so its better to take taxi. nice clean rooms with good bathrooms. staff was very friendly. they kept our led in the store room without any charge. wi fi service is free in lobby only. reccomand this hotel specially for Indians.

author: PritpaulSingh
title: Shopping!!
text: This hotel is on the main road, close to the shopping area (10-15 minutes walk) and most of the people know it so hiring a cab/tuk tuk is not a problem. I recommend this hotel to all travelers desiring a cheap accommodation, in Bangkok for Shopping in nearby market -- may find it worth the price. The bathroom appears recently renovated but the fittings are not replaced – which makes it untidy. From my room, I requested cold (regular) drinking water – they refused to provide it – they wanted me to either buy mineral water or use the complimentary (regular) water bottles provided by the hotel. One will perhaps never like to use this water because it is kept in the bathroom –next to the toilet. I approached the front office, who also refused to serve drinking water. The idea of keeping the drinking water bottles in the washroom –next to the toilet is just too filthy. The attendant brought my luggage to the room and I said “Thank You”. He started walking around bouncingly and repeating the words “Thank you . . . Thank you . . . “. It was his style for asking for a tip. The mattresses are not so good. The room walls/passage walls are dirty. As I said earlier, if you are at this place, just keep in mind that you are there for a cheap accommodation.

author: SunSport
title: A good hotel and worthy of consideration.
text: This is my hotel of choice when I'm in Bangkok. This is not because it is particularly outstanding in any way but because its location suits me well. There is not a lot I need to write about this property because it does everything well. This is not to say there are no problems with the hotel. First of all the rooms are really too small for western guests. You will need to be smaller than Miranda Kerr to manoeuvre yourself into the shower cubicle without causing a nasty injury. The room itself is not going to be comfortable for a couple. I will stay here again as I can put up with the cramped conditions. The restaurant is fine and the breakfast offer is perfectly ok. At least they know how to make good coffee! There are good local restaurants close by and there is a 7/11 for water and other necessities. Two ATMs are outside the 7/11. The hotel does its best to warn and protect its guests from the criminal taxi touts who occupy the pavement outside the hotel. Be warned - do NOT enter into any conversations or arrangements with these unsavoury characters. If you need a taxi the hotel's security staff will flag one for you and ensure the driver uses his meter. There is free Wi-Fi in the lobby / cafe area which is very good. It is turned off during breakfast time to prevent guests occupying a table just to use the Internet and so prevent other guests finding a table for breakfast. Such is the ignorance of many that this step had to be taken by the hotel. I will stay at this hotel again as the benefits far outweigh and negatives. I should also mention that most hotels in the Makkasan / Pratanum area are very popular with guests from India so the All Season's small lobby area is often filled to capacity with Sony wide screen LCD televisions waiting to accompany their owner's return to Mumbai!

author: Pontychild
title: Small and practical and easy access to / from airport and shopping centres
text: I choose this hotel mainly because of the location, it's near the airport link station (Ratchaprarop station), it's only by walking distance around 10 minutes, and also near the pratunam market (which is a benefit to my business). We arrived at night time (around 9 PM) the check-in process was quick, with a little smile, quite friendly for a busy hotel. (I noticed several group tours during breakfast) There are computers with internet in the lobby and elevators for easy access with luggages. The room is clean and quite spacious and with standard amenities such as cable TV, fridge, snack bar, and free coffee / tea making facility. The only problem was the linen / bed-sheet. There was a permanent stain on my bed sheet just under the pillow, which was only found the next morning when I woke up. I thought they will change it, but instead they flip the stain to the feet position. I can understand the environment policy, but they should not re-used a permanent stained bed sheet. The bathroom is clean with standard amenities, soap, shampoo and hot / cold shower. The thing I like is the breakfast, it's delicious and plenty of choices, from Chinese, Thai, Western, and India food. The restaurants staff is quick, tactful, and friendly. The other thing that I don't like is the carpet on the hallway, as soon as we step out of the elevator, there is dirty carpet along the way to the room. Fortunately, there is no carpet in the room. I used to stay in other small hotels around that area, about the same price, but All Season has more value for money. Other than the bed linen and hallway's carpet, all other things are Good. I will certainly be back...

author: Seat01A
title: Bad experience, I would not recommend this hotel.
text: I booked this hotel because of its proximity to the airport, I wanted to stay just one night before leaving Thaïland and I had a bad experience in this hotel. First of all, I enjoyed the possibility to connect the Railway Station (located 5-10 minutes away from the hotel) for the airport. Rooms were quite clean and with enough space. Buffet breakfast was OK, but there is no enough room in the "restaurant", you will certainly have to take your breakfast outdoors with the noise and pollution of Bangkok's streets ! The first room we had was on the 4th floor, we had no safety-box in the room, the walls have many scratches and windows was so thin that the noise was insupportable. We asked the reception to change and we had a second room on the 6th floor, noisy but less than the other one. You have to know that reception staff speak only a little English ... it doesn't correspond to the Accor standards. We asked for Post Office, and they were not able to give us information about that. Moreover, we wanted to leave our lugguages in the hotel and there was a lack of organization because the lugguage room was full so our lugguages had to stay in the lobby, so everyone can take it away ... I kindly asked the manager if the hotel was full responsible for any damages or losses and he didn't answer, this is not serious and professional ! There is no room available to take a shower before leaving for airport, which is a little disappointing. The hotel staff wasn't able to told us where we can take a shower in the surroundings. If you want to visit Bangkok, this is certainly not a good place to stay. We asked the staff reception and told us that it will only take 10 minutes by walk to reach the SkyTrain. Actually, there is more than 1.5 kilometers to reach the nearest station (Victory Monument).

author: krishnamurthyr2017
title: BAD LOCATION/ TOURIST TRAP
text: It could have definitely been worse, but the rooms were slightly better than gutter quality. We had taken three rooms, so I can confidently say that my room was not an exception. Pretty lame inside, with poor quality bedsheets, depressing views from the windows, itch causing seating, inadequate airconditioning, ancient TVs and dubious towels. Had booked this through a travel agent, as part of a tour package that we purchased last minute. Did not know this was the kind of hotel that served as a dumping ground for tour groups. The hotel is poorly located and one has to walk a few kilometres to find public transport. Not great if you want to independently explore the city. To add to bad rooms and poor location, the staff were quite rude on occassion and even refused to give additional glasses to our rooms, saying that glasses would be provided only after payment of additional fees! This was when we had not even broken a glass in the room, to justify such a charge. We were also stuck there on the wrong date, during Buddha's birthday. There was only a skeleton staff and to add to our woes of most things in the city being closed, there was one person waiting on a full restaurant at the hotel. Naturally, things were forgotten or delayed unreasonably, people lost their temper and the usual hassles ensued. In the sum of things, I came back much more stressed than, I had been. This hotel really has to get it's act together. If you are looking for relaxation or a great base to enjoy the city from, this is NOT the place the go. This is ok if you are part of a tour group and do not care about where you are staying.

author: runvrun
title: No frills, basic, clean, well located
text: The All Season Siam Bangkok Siam hotel is a basic, no frills, budget hotel. It's great for business travellers or tourists looking for a clean room with basic facilities. I was quite shocked when the hotel asked me for a deposit of 1000 baht on checking in even though I had paid for my room in full advance. No other hotel I've ever stayed in asked me for this - and nor was I informed about this prior to my stay. This wasn't the most welcoming gesture. The rooms aren't too big nor are they cramped. The toilets though are a little cramped, especially compared to the other hotels I stayed in in Thailand. The minibar is expensive. In fact, most of the additional facilities in the hotel are - and aren't worth the money. Internet for example is charged at 120 (or something like that) baht an hour whereas there are 2 internet cafes a minute away which charge only 20 baht an hour. The food is on the pricey side and not worth the money. It's edible but not great. Their breakfast spread in the morning too is pretty basic. In fact, they also served some items such as noodles and rice which I'd rather have for lunch that breakfast. The hotel is quite centrally located and is a 5 minute walk to the Pratunam market and other shopping malls. A decent hotel to stay in if you want something pretty basic and relatively cheap.

author: mark0007
title: A decent hotel for the money
text: I have stayed in this hotel several times. It is well located, near Pantip, Siam Paragon, and Central World. Easier to get in and out of town, than Sukhumvit, which is very congested. There is alot I like about this hotel. Rooms are clean, service is good, the breakfast is exceptionally good, and so is the food in the lobby restaurant. Free internet is another bonus. Great value. The only issues I had are twofold. First, the shower heads are the worst in Thailand. They should have been replaced years ago, and offer a pathetic trickle. Second, there is a dog that lives in one of the houses on the even side (rooms -20, -22, etc) that barks ALL NIGHT. He should be taken out of his misery, or relocated to a suitable home. Those are my only complaints. Ask for an odd numbered room, in the interior, in the rear, or on the other side, that does not face the sol on the side of the hotel. That dog is a nightmare. Bring earplugs.

author: ryben01
title: Breakfast disgusting, poor location, but good staff.
text: We just got back from a 4 night stay here, the initial check in drama ..... staff didnt read the booking and provided my brother and children with king bed rooms instead of twins and then had to relocate floors and rooms at 1am grrrr.... We woke after our 1st night to be stiff and sore .... now before I get shot down I have travelled Thailand many many times and know it is well known for hard beds but these ones here at All Seasons or my room at least made the floor and a pillow look good not only were they hard but lumpy and could feel springs or something poking you. The breakfast just topped off a wonderful check-in and 1st nights sleep ... not. OMG I have not experienced a worse breakfast anywhere else in the world than here and for an international chain of hotels they should be disgusted and embarrassed for what they offer!! Sweet & sour fish, fried half raw eggs, cold noodles (from nite before), cold chinese donuts (lumps of greasy batter deep fried) stir fried vegetables, boiled ham,potato bake, curry meat and rice, rice congee, soup, white or grain bread, salad stuff, pineapple or watermelon platter and 2 selection of cakes banana & date!! There was nothing remotely inviting about this brekkie at ALL and every day was the same the reason I say it was leftovers from the night before was because after having it for dinner the same was for breakfast. The indian/pakistan/burmese tour groups were overwhelming boisterous, loud and rude, and topped off a memorable stay here. I admit the price here is cheap but being a Accor member would of expected a better standard of their chain of hotels. On the good side however the staff spoke good english at reception, were helpful and accommodating, one thing we found amusing was the wooden icecream stick provided in our room to make coffee etc and when asking for a proper spoon from the kitchen had our room number name etc recorded in case we stole it OMG lol. The staff at reception suggest you ask them to get a taxi for you because of touts etc camped out front....they radio the security guard to hail you a taxi meter and tell the taxi driver where you want to go and ensure the meter is on we loved this service that the hotel provided as it made it easy for us as a family of 5 needing 2 taxis to go anywhere. All in all the rooms were ok small window in some rooms and large bay like window in our family suite. The bathroom grout was mouldy but everything else worked and was presentable. Wifi was free if you used your laptop in the foyer otherwise was expensive in room by memory 150baht for 1 hr in room. Would have to say the breakfast ruined it for me here, and the location is remote the short walk they say on their website is more if yr a jogger or speed walker. Would not stay here again.

author: samdevau
title: great little hotel
text: Booked this hotel as we wanted to be close to friends and the shops of Pratunam. Staff are incredibly friendly and helpful. Enjoyed it that much we stayed another night after travelling around northern Thailand. Both times the rooms had safes (but not all rooms do) and we were located on non smoking floors. Bangkok has heavy traffic, and the hotel is on a busy main road, so if you need to sleep when it is dead quiet, best go elsewhere. The upside to being on a main road is that the buses that stop out the front (73 and 214 from memory) go to Chinatown - great for shopping too and travel past MBK as well and cheap as well. MBK 12 baht and Chinatown 14 Baht. Most of the buses that go by will take you past the main shopping areas of Pratunam or Big C. Plan your trips to avoid peak hour congestion. Breakfast was satisfactory, but had a great little espresso machine, which is the most important part of my breakfast. Some reasonable restaurants close by from the street BBQ stall between the hotel and 7/11 and the Chinese restaurant in the opposite direction. Just walk to the next overhead bridge, cross there and it is just past another 7/11 Lots of people from Northern Thailand live in this area of Bangkok, so many of the restaurants close by serve Northern Thai dishses. This is especially true of the street that runs past the new King Power duty free shopping centre. Avoid the restaurants at the end of the street closest to the hotel and eat at the other end of the street past the park and close to the BTS. If you want a convenient place to shop Bangkok that is value for money, then this could be the place for you

author: db527
title: Great small hotel - good value.
text: Arrived here at 7 AM via an early morning flight. The front desk staff gave me a room immediately. Other hotels can make you wait till 9 AM as a room may not be available at that time. The rooms are fair sized with not much of a view. But everything is very very clean and comfortable. The buffet breakfast is just ok as not much choice and the same thing every day. First night was on the second floor towards the front where at night it was very noisy due to traffic at the front road. Next day complained and they gave me a room on the 8th floor towards the rear where it was quite. The lobby is very small compared to many other hotels in BKK and the small restaurant next to lobby only does breakfast and later in the day becomes a bar with snacks. The location is not that great as nothing nearby. There is a chinese restaurant next door where the food and service was terrible. The nearest skytrain is about a 15 mins walk and you can also do a leasurely walk to the Pratunam market (Indra mkt) in 20 mins. Overall, the hotel is nice and the front office staff is always smiling and ready to help for anything. It was a bargain for US$38 per night. Taxi is easily available at any time.

author: khrisng
title: Good for value?
text: We stayed in Ibis Siam Bangkok hotel previously a couple of times and find it very good for value. However, my lastest stay change my perspective. My family stayed from 17th - 18th of May 08, My wife and I stayed in Room 508 while my parents were in Room 507 which are next to each other. The room was as expected before, everything neat and clean. There is also a little balcony, only accessible by the window, where the air conditioner compressor seats. In the early next morning , I received an alarming phone call from my parents asking me to check if my window to the balcony was locked as they heard some noises at their balcony. Later in the morning, after some clarifications with my parents, I found out that about 4:30am my dad heard some rustling of the curtains and immediately woke up and shouted (to scare off anyone who maybe there), only to realise that the window was partially opened. He mentioned that one of the window lock was out of order and cannot be locked. Hence, he suspected that someone may have attempted to enter the room from the faulty window. I told him that he should have informed me on the faulty window when we checked in. Nevertheless, upon checking out, we informed the front desk of our unfortunate encounter and were utterly disappointed when the front desk only accepted the information but did not make any obvious effort to check with the security guards or log book. They also did not make any effort to retain our contact information for follow up. I also could not help but notice the number of female and young travellers staying in the hotel which I cannot even imagine or describe the consequences if the intruder succeed in entering any of the rooms. On hindsight, I admit that it is our mistake for not informing the front desk on the faulty window during checkin. But in an establish hotel chain, I could not help but question if they have a checklist of things while cleaning up the room? Especially if it concerns security and safetyy of the guests? I also expected more professional front desk to handle such incidents and lead the investigation. Anyway, no point crying over spilt milk but an advice for the fellow travellers, pls check the room properly especially the window locks are functional upon checking in. As for me, I really doubt that I will recommend this hotel to my friends or stay there myself in the future.

author: eddibabyyeah
title: Good Value - No frills
text: Myself and friend stayed in this hotel last week. We only stayed one night in Bangkok as we were moving to southern Thailand the day after. The hotel was nice and clean and what you'd expect from an IBIS. The breakfasts were good value. The bar seemed to be open all night (it was at 4am from what I remember). The hotel was about 30 mins taxi from the airport which cost 1000baht. There are plenty of cheap taxis/tut tuts outside the hotel which will get you round Bangkok cheaply. And take you to the airport for about 300bath. I found Bangkok itself to be extremely busy and found getting around the city very slow and time consuming due to traffic. We seemed to spend hours in taxis getting nowhere. I plan to return to Thailand soon, but doubt I will bother with Bangkok. Its just too busy and smelly due to fumes from traffic. One point to note. On departure we got a taxi to take us to the airport for our next adventure in Phuket. On arrival at the airport we were told by Thai airways staff that we were at the WRONG airport. Luckily, we got another taxi to the correct airport (about 40 mins) and made the flight. So a word of advice for all concerned. Make sure you got the correct airport.

author: pattayainsider
title: Probably Bangkolk's best value hotel
text: I regularly stay at the Ibis Siam Bangkok, booking the "hot rate" on the hotel's website. It has to be the lowest price of any chain hotel in Bangkok. Room is fine, restaurant food is good and reasonable. Cable t.v. has many international channels, including BBC news in English. Bed is comfortable, air conditioning is individual controlled, and works great. Water pressure in bathroom is fine too. There is no pool here. The onl problem for me is that it is about a 15 minute walk to the Victory BTS skytrain station, which in the Bangkok heat means you'll be very hot after only five minutes. But the savings you get at the hotel means you can take an inexpensive taxi to the Siam shopping area for only about 45 baht, which is about $1.30. Lots of taxis pass in front of the hotel. Staff were very friendly. I booked at tour at the lobby tour desk, which was a little overpriced, but you can negotiate with them. The breakfast buffet is fine, 150 baht including tax, about $4, with just about everything. There is a 7-11 a few doors down from the hotel, which is convenient.

author: PhilLondonUK
title: Great hotel for the price
text: I booked into this hotel having stayed in the Lotus Novotel last year, but being unable to afford it this year. I booked it via Precision Reservations (usually a but cheaper than Asia Rooms and very reliable) at the last minute after being frustrated having stayed at a 4 star hotel near Kao San Road earlier on this trip - hard to get to and from using the skytrain which is my preferred method of getting round Bangkok these days. All I can say is that I was immediately impressed - the staff were polite and friendly, happily accomodated my request for a 2pm checkout for no extra charge - the room cost 20 US dollars per night without breakfast but the breakfast buffet is only 150 baht. The room is pretty much what you get at higher star rated hotels too i.e. a good quality, solid Queen sized bed, sofa, desk, fridge, cable TV etc. The bathroom is tastefully decorated and spotlessly clean - as was the room as a whole aside from the carpet which had a few holes and marks. There is however no bath, just a shower. Tea and coffee making facilities are provided, there is a safe in the wardrobe and an individually controlled AC unit so you can get the room temperature just right. The only drawback (and its not a drawback at all when you consider a 24 hour 7-11 is about 2 doors away!) is that the fridge is not stocked with anything aside from 2 small bottles of water. At hotel minibar prices I usually stock up at the 7-11 wherever I stay in BKK. Some people have complained about noise at this hotel - I didnt have any problems, thought quite clearly the doors are thin and you can hear what people are saying clearly if they are stood outside your door. As I say, this is not generally going to be a problem but I did get disturbed when trying to lie in one morning, by screaming kids running up and down the corridor - not sure if this would have disturbed me in a higher star rated hotel with thicker doors and walls. Its about 10 minutes walk to Victory Monument BTS station and there are various internet cafes around as well as a few cheap eateries and a couple of neon lit karaoke bars if youre into that sort of thing! Good price, reasonably good location, clean and friendly. Highly recommended and a bargain for the price - will be my first port of call when I return to BKK Next year.

author: Tweety2004
title: A great budget hotel
text: A newly open budget hotel in Bangkok, the first by an international hotel chain I think! The hotel is located in the Pratunam area, about 15 minutes walk to the nearest BTS station which namely is Victory Monument. This may not be the most conveniently located ('cos BTS is my most used mode of transporatation in Bangkok to avoid the terrible traffic jams in this City) but it does have a bus station right in front of the hotel, and all buses which stop there would take you to the Central World Plaza area, and from there, you're only 5 minutes from Chitlom BTS station or the shopping malls and restaurants in the area. Rooms are clean in terms of the price paid. The only complaint was that there were ants on the bed the first night, but after my compaint to the reception the next morning, the problem has been dealt with swiftly. Being a budget hotel also means that there is no swimming pool, no mini-bar in the room (though there is an empty fridge in my room - I was upgraded to a superior room for free because of some misunderstanding at booking, as a compensation) and there is no in-room safe which could pose some level of inconvenience because one can't leave the valuables in the room. However, there was an individual air-conditioner in each roo, so you can regulate the temperature according to your personal liking rather than stick to one temperature because of the use of central air-conditioner in other budget hotels. The bathroom, like most budget hotel, has no bath tub, but is clean enough. The only complaint is that the water pressure wasn't very stable at times and so the water temperature would vary when you take a shower. However, it didn't post a big problem with the weather being so hot in Bangkok. Breakfast is standard fare but being a buffet is more than adequate in itself. There is a tour desk but mind you, the price is not cheap although this is a budget hotel. I ended up finding other travel agents outside of the hotel for our day tour to the Floating Market. In general, I would recommend this hotel if one doesn't mind its distance from a BTS station for the price is more than just reasonable (I paid 1,200B per night net, but I heard there is a promotional rate of a prepaid rate of 950B net per night directly from the hotel's website until August this year) ! !

author: 345teril
title: Absolutely perfect!
text: Bob and Sande were incredible hosts -- staying with them truly made for an unforgettable trip to Maui! I surprised my boyfriend with a trip to Hawaii for his birthday. I didn't plan much except the flight, rental car and the bed and breakfast. Bob and Sande were very helpful right from booking, with detailed directions to their home and even a rental car discount from their website. We arrived late on a Wednesday and woke up early Thursday for breakfast with our hosts. They were so excited to hear about our travels and how the surprise went! They served us a perfect Hawaiian breakfast outdoors, where we enjoyed views of the ocean and got to know our warm, kind, and gracious hosts. They are lovely people and seem to really enjoy getting to know everyone who visits. We asked Bob and Sande for recommendations for our short stay, and they did not disappoint. You can walk to the beach from their home (which we did and which was beautiful!), but because we were looking for the best snorkeling nearby, they gave us a great recommendation for a different beach down the road. From amazing restaurants to gorgeous hikes, memorable outings for a rainy day and even the best way to do the Road to Hana, they helped transform our quick trip into an unforgettable adventure. We stayed in the Coral Room, which has its own entrance on the side so you are allowed as much privacy as you'd like. We were out and about for most of the day but our room was a perfect place to relax when the time came. The private lanai is wonderful for coffee in the morning or a glass of wine at the end of the day, the bed was big and comfortable, and the room itself was very clean and tidy with a private bathroom, refrigerator, AC if you need it, TV, along with a cooler, beach chairs, umbrella, and towels to take to the beach! Do yourself a favor and choose this adorable bed and breakfast for your Maui vacation. Bob and Sande would love to host you on their beautiful island, and you will not be disappointed!

author: SPerreault
title: Felt just like home, can't wait to come back!
text: It was our first time at B&B so we were pretty nervous and we spent a lot of time choosing and reading all the reviews carefully. Ocean Breeze Hideaway originally was not our first choice but they responded the fastest and were the most helpful with our requests so we decided to give it a try. Before we arrived, we got an email from Bob & Sande informing us that they were not going to be there. So we got very worried because all the good reviews are because of them. But as soon as we arrived, we fell in love with the mango tree, the garden, the private patio and the room itself right away! Then, best of all, we were greeted by Jody, the inn sitter, who turned out to be one of the reasons why our trip was so amazing! We truly enjoyed her company and she gave us all the good tips on things to do (e.g. farmer market, First Friday, beaches). We would have missed a lot of these cool events if it was not because of her. Everyday when we came back from a long, full-packed day, we truly felt like we were coming back to our home. There were two suites but there was nobody else in the other suite so we had the whole house for ourselves, the kitchen & the cozy living room! We like going out for breakfast to try great local food but we never had a chance to go out because the breakfast here at B&B was just too good to miss! My husband is more picky but he loved everything, the fresh fruit, the pastry, the coffee, and all. We will definitely come back and stay here when we come back to Maui. We totally can't wait! Thank you again, Bob, Sande and Jody, for making this a perfect trip for us! See you again soon!!! :D

author: 519Marla519
title: "Best Choice"
text: Our experiences at B&B's spans over 12 years. After staying at my first one in CA in 2000 it is always my preference to find one anywhere my trip takes me. Innkeepers are a wealth of information about the local areas and the hidden finds they share make your vacations even more memorable. Taken with the B&B experience we became innkeepers ourselves meeting people from all over the world..... thus leading us to Maui for our 10th anniversary as one of our guests said a trip to Hawaii had to be MAUI. We knew we had chosen a great place even before we arrived, as months before we landed we shared many emails and calls to Bob and Sande. They always were happy to share their suggestions about local attractions and even helped book them for us. Once we entered the garden at their paradise we felt it, "we were home!" We enjoyed eight nights in the beautiful Coral Suite.. Bob & Sande have given lots of thought to the needs of travelers and offer it to their guests as many have mentioned before us. These extras were much appreciated and made our stay even nicer. The most memorable was the time spent with Bob and Sande over the scruptious breakfasts. We looked forward to our time with them each morning! Our time at the Ocean Breeze went by far to quickly and before we knew it, it was time to leave. With tears in my eyes I said goodbye to our new friends... These innkeepers have by far exceeded any other B&B experience we have had. Mahalo Bob & Sande!!!!!!!!!

author: Dony243
title: What a great place to stay in Maui!!
text: We will always have wonderful memories of our stay at Ocean Breeze Hideaway (B & B). We stayed in the Ocean Room. What a lovely room! Bob and Sande thought of everything to make their guests feel at home! It was an " Aloha" welcome. The Ocean Room has a fountain flowing just outside our door which we found very relaxing. There was a patio table and lawn chairs for us to sit outside and enjoy their beautiful yard and the warm breezes of Hawaii. We appreciated Bob's and Sande's knowledge of the sightseeing tours and the Island foods served at the different restaurants in Maui. Besides being great hosts, Bob and Sande are very accommodating people. We couldn't make the breakfasts that Bob and Sande serve on their lanai during the week day because we had to leave the B&B around 7 A.M. every morning to take care of our Grandchildren while their Mom and Dad attended a Dental Conference at the Fairmont Hotel in Wailea. Sande would provide us with a breakfast of fresh fruit, yogurt, muffins/banana bread and put it in our little fridge so we could have it the next morning. Mahalo Sande!! You are very special people Bob and Sande! Mahalo for making our stay so memorable in Maui. We will return!!

author: GiniGL
title: Real island hospitality in a home away from home.
text: We returned from Maui this morning, refreshed and relaxed. The Coral Room at Ocean Breeze Hideaway was our perfect home away from home. We originally chose it because we eschew high priced hotels, preferring to spend the bulk of our vacation dollars on food and adventure. But our choice was perfect! We arrived at night and were greeted by twinkling lights, a lit garden path, and a warmly lit private room. We were home! Both Sande and Bob are charming and helpful, with great tips about island food and activities. They showed genuine concern when I suffered an injury, and exuded interest in their guests and the island. The room was charming, very"Hawaiian decor." the bed was über comfy, the bathroom serviceable if a bit outdated in decor, but nothing that would make me stay elsewhere. Sande and Bob have thought of everything you might possibly want or need: beach chairs, boogy board and noodle floats, umbrella, cooler, extra luxurious beach towels, an outdoor clothesline, refrigerator, picnic ware and plastic glasses. The list goes on and on. The ONLY possible downside is the scheduled breakfast. We were Unable to avail ourselves of the sit-down breakfast more than a few times (and those times it was delicious) because we tend to get up and going early. They did offer to pre-pack a breakfast for us. But I would appreciate it more if the schedule could be more flexible- say, from 8 to 9am, instead of exactly at 8:15. That said, my complaint is minor. I would stay there again in a heartbeat!

author: DiverMom18
title: Very nice little Hawaiian "Hideaway"!
text: The owners, Bob & Sande were always quick to reply to our emails/questions. This cute little B&B is conveniently located in North Kihei, which allows very easy access to Piilani Hwy & Kihei Road, so if you're headed to Lahaina/Ka'anapali or to South Kihei restaurants or beaches, it is easy travelling. It is in a pretty residential neighborhood and was fairly quiet, with the occasional loud vehicle or motorcycle. (we travel with a noisemaker so we didn't hear much at night) Private parking was great to have as was the private entrance. The beach is about a 10-15 minute walk, but it is a nice walk especially in the mornings. (I think it's Sugar Beach) This is a great beach to walk on, but for beach-bumming during the day, I'd recommend other South Kihei beaches for that. Our room (Ocean Suite) was very clean and comfortable, and had everything we needed. This room did not have A/C, but we had cooler nights and with the ceiling fan and a floor box fan, we kept plenty cool! We loved going to sleep at night with the sounds of the fountain they have in the little sitting area just outside the door-truly felt like we were in our own little "hideaway"! It is beautifully landscaped, very peaceful and calm. We also appreciated VERY much the items to use:cooler, boogie board, umbrella, beach chairs & towels.The highlight for us was the delicious breakfast each morning with a wonderful host, Lisa. (owners were gone, but Lisa was gracious, helpful, accomodating & fun to visit with!) Even though it consists of yogurt, granola, fresh fruit, juice and varying breads everyday, we loved it. We eat yogurt, granola & fruit every day at home, so this was perfect for us and we didn't tire of it. On the mornings we were gone, Lisa sent us with a baggie of breakfast food to take with us, which was very helpful & appreciated. We very much enjoyed our stay here and felt well taken care of - a big Mahalo to Lisa! (and Bob & Sande for sharing their beautiful place with us!)

author: Beate5
title: For our next stay we will definitely choose this hotel again
text: This B&B is located in a quiet neighborhood area. There are two suites: Coral Suite and Ocean Suite. We stayed at the Ocean Suite but got a chance to look at the Coral Suite as well. Even though the latter is somewhat larger, the Ocean Suite is perfectly fine for two people to spend a week. Ocean Suite offers access to two terraces that are nicely located between coconut palms and blossoming bushes. These terraces have not to be shared with the people occupying the other suite. The suite was very clean and offered all the facilities required for a comfortable stay (e.g., hair dryer, ironing plate, TV, DVD player, refrigerator, coffee making facilities etc.). Complementary beach towels, beach chairs and a sunshade were also available. Numerous excellent restaurants as well as grocery stores are within easy reach (by car). The beach is within walking distance. We found this beach the quietest and nicest along the shoreline between the "Big Beach" and Lahaina.
