Sande and Bob are excellent hosts: always friendly and extremely helpful when required, but at the same time discreet and unobstructive. Every day, they offered a very tasty breakfast. They regularly accompanied us during breakfast, and we found these relaxed chats very enjoyable. In summary, this place is really a "hideway" for people wanting to enjoy the beauty of the island and to get some rest from their business life.

author: TimeProfessor
title: Was a great fit for us
text: H and M K. We stayed at the Ocean Breeze Hideaway Ocean View room in September 2010. I understand this is the slowest month for traveling in Hawaii--although if you saw the crowds in Pali up near Hana in the North...well, you'd never know it. (Sorry, I never got my true bearings of Maui or later on Oahu....could never tell if I was going East or West). Nice dual parking area, you are given set of keys for the gate, room, leisure room. Breakfasts were great, Sande would have some muffins or scones and they had fresh papaya...yes, that was very nice, plus the morning conversations with Bob and Sande were extremely helpful on where to go...best snorkeling...Bob told us of the Pali Fish market and I admit it was busy and the food was very, very good. Cat's name is Coconut I think. Yes, simple room, ceiling fan/floor fan/bathroom. Nothing fancy but hey, you're gone all day aren't you? The use of the beach chairs/umbrella/ boogie board was a huge help. Small mini-refrig. in room in closet also was a major bonus, keep your drinks cold or some food you might have gotten at a restaurant. Also free wi-fi...but I think wife's Droid is better than my laptop. Nice people, nice area, great location to base yourself to explore the island. Did I mention I liked the breakfast?

author: MrSvensson
title: More than a just B&B
text: We stayed there for 20 nights. Our room was the Coral Suite. Bob and Sande – the hosts– were very obliging and helpful. They managed so much for us in advance. As we arrived, everything we asked for was arranged and set up. They made us feel so comfortable and welcome from the second we unlocked the gate to our suite. They did not treat us like guests but friends (and still do ...). Both have a huge repertoire of Tips, that they are willing to pass on to their guests. Breakfast was great/delicious all the time. We could choose from different kinds of cereals, fresh fruits and juices, selfmade smoothies, Sande´s bread, scones or muffins. Everyday there was a new choice. The whole house is very clean and comfortable. As they only rent two rooms, the place is not over crowded and quiet. High-Speed Internet (Wi-Fi) is available for free, so is Off-Street-Parking. We do recommend this B&B to everyone who wants to have a fulfilled and inexpensive stay in Maui. We will be back, that is for sure! If that is not enough information and you want to know more, do not hesitatte to contact us.

author: gatorman4321
title: Excellent Stay
text: This was an excellent place that really contributed to a great vacation. Bob & Sandee were great hosts. Everything was convenient. The location is central for exploring the island. The cooler, beach chairs, umbrella, towels, glassware, and fridge right in the room were convenient. The WiFi is very fast. The parking is very convenient. The breakfasts were very good when we made time for them. Its easy to get going early and be busy for days straight in Maui, but we found it very relaxing to sleep in a few days and do breakfast w/ Bob & Sandee. The gardens create a great buffer on the 2 sides of the room. The 2 sliding glass doors always provide a cool breeze for the room we stayed in (Ocean Suite). We stayed 5 nights in late March and would love to return one day. The 2 nights we had in Waikiki afterward were not that enjoyable compared to our time on Maui. i always look for value when traveling and I can't see how you can beat this place for value. Thanks Bob & Sandee Nick

author: Lunzinho
title: Wonderful B&B
text: We stayed 3 nights in this lovely B&B and we definitely enjoyed our stay. I read a lot of the other reviews and I can confirm the laudatory facts like the perfect breakfast and the great hospitality of Sande and Bob and so I don´t want to repeat all of them. So maybe I use these words to comment on the few not so perfect reviews that we cannot understand. For example some people complained about not having an A/C in their room and therefore the need to sleep with open windows and the assosciated noise. BUT there is the possibility to have an A/C because one of the two rooms has one. So if you book the Coral Suite you will have an A/C and can sleep with closed windows. So you will definetly have a quite night in a well tempered room. (Only as a side note: this was the only B&B we had on Hawaii (and we had a lot) that offered the convenience of an A/C). We would definitely recommend these B&B to all our friends because it is a really great place to explore Maui and get in contact with people living on Hawaii. There is only a small disadvantage for people from europe that do not book by a travel agency. Because the advanced payment with paypal was quite expensive for us. We had to pay the fees of paypal AND the credit card (because paypal charges the credit card). In all the other B&Bs we gave our credit card number as deposit and paid cash during our stay. That was much more convenient for us. But never the less Oceanbreeze Hideaway was worth the money. Markus and Kerstin

author: traveler820
title: Great hosts and amenities - but we didn't sleep so well
text: First the good. Sandi and Bob were both very friendly, welcoming, and eager to offer advice such as things to see, places to eat, etc. The personal insight was very helpful. We also definitely made use of the refrigerator, beach accessories, and other provided extras - it was great to have beach chairs, a beach umbrella, a cooler, and a flashlight/jacket for Haleakala. Finally, the breakfasts were good - fresh fruit, yogurt, bread, etc. Unfortunately, we were only able to take advantage of the breakfast on 2 of the 5 mornings we were there - b/c of our trip to Hana, sunrise at Haleakala, and an early flight. Our biggest complaint was that we couldn't sleep so well. We stayed in the Ocean Suite, which doesn't have air conditioning. There are two glass sliding doors and an overhead fan which combine to create a pretty decent cross breeze. (It was still a little warm/humid, but definitely manageable.) The only problem is that in order to take advantage of the cross breeze, we had to leave the doors open all night which meant (1) limited privacy and (2) (more importantly for us) we could hear EVERY outside noise. I'm usually a pretty heavy sleeper, but even I had issues. We heard cars driving by, dogs barking, and - by far the worse - roosters cock-a-doodle-dooing at various points throughout the night (11pm, 2am, 4am, etc.). (Apparently wild roosters are a problem in Maui.) We tried closing the sliding doors to make it quieter, but that made the room really hot/stuffy. Overall, for us, the lack of sleep was a deal breaker for future visits, but perhaps a set of ear plugs would minimize the issue for others. Or the Coral Suite may be a good alternative, since it is air conditioned. There were definitely a bunch of perks to this place if you can handle the noise and lack of air conditioning/privacy.

author: mrandmrsdoc
title: What a Great Experience!!
text: This was such a great experience for us that we referred our son and his fiancee' to this lovely place. They are coming to Ocean Breeze in October for 7 nights on their honeymoon. We found Bob and Sande to be friendly and helpful hosts. The coziness of our room was so special, we just loved it...The garden area just outside our door was wonderful and the singing of the birds we truly enjoyed. And to top it off we were close to the beach area where we jogged every morning. We felt that here we were centrally located for all areas of interest. This was our second time on the Island of Maui and discovered that this is the place we will come back to on our return. The accommodations were clean. The bed was very comfortable. Bob and Sande take special care to make the experience special. Bob is very good at giving directions and suggestions for places to eat and see. The breakfast is a must! Plentiful and healthy we looked forward to eating and visiting every morning. You can see the ocean from the eating area. Another aspect of the home which we appreciated is the privacy Bob and Sande have designed. We could have our window curtains open all the time with the security of privacy. Enjoy!

author: charlenean
title: You are going to LOVE this B&B!
text: This is my second stay at Ocean Breeze Hideaway and I will never stay anywhere else on Maui! Bob and Sande are knowledgable and fun hosts with excellent suggestions of things to do on the Island that you might not otherwise hear about in a guidebook. Their service is unobtrusive and perfect. Waking up to the sound of birdsong; having breakfast every morning looking out over the Ocean and eating delicious food with great company is the best way to start a day! (Did I mention the fresh fruit and flowers grown on the property?) The room is clean and comfortable. They even provide jackets for cold morning trips up to Haleakala, a cooler, beach chairs, etc. It's like being at home while on vacation at the same time. The location in Kihei is also perfectly central for just about every place you want to visit on the Island and just minutes from some of the best beaches in the world. One thing I truly love is what I call the "Kwan Yin Garden" outside my room, with two fountains and lush landscaping. I have a picture I use as my screensaver that takes me back to Maui and Ocean Breeze every time I look at it. As much as I love the Island and all the things there are to do? I have to admit, some of my best memories are just laying out in the private yard, soaking up the sun, listening to the fountain and birds while reading a good book and relishing the peace and quiet. Perfect place to meditate and just get away from it all. There is an energy about this place that is unmistakable. Combine that with the great value, super service and location? You can't go wrong with this one! ** I've attached some pix but please note the date was wrong in the camera. These are recent taken in April 2008!

author: Bubbavon
title: A great B&B with lots of value and convenience
text: We stayed here for 9 days in Feb-March 2004. We were very pleased. Because we stayed over a week we only paid $83US a night. A Hawaiian bargain. We stayed in the Coral Suite. A very large room with a king sized bed. Included, ceiling fan, AC, TV, Cable, VCR, lots of closet space, a private bathroom, fridge, hair dryer, clock, coolers, mats, and healthy breakfasts. It was Bob and Sande our hosts that made it home. They were always friendly and helpful. We had off the street parking which is important in Kihei. (little street room). We always felt safe and relaxed. With only one other room for guests it was never over crowded. It is well located in Maui not far from anything but not really at anything either. It was perfect as we saw and did many things all over the island so we did have to travel to everything but never very long as oppossed to those who choose the north west corner. We hope to return and will reccomend it to others.

author: PippaL594
title: Cool artwork in a dirty, overpriced hostel
text: Wow, what a disappointment!! Positives: The location is in a great neighbourhood near the Lepanto metro stop and walkable to the Vatican. Building security is good. Artwork is kind of cool throughout. Rooms have lockers. Negatives: Everything about this place is dirty - it is barely cleaned. Beds are terrible!!! Paper thin and my sheets were ripped with bloodstains on them. The bed above me has ripped open and also had blood stains for me to stare at in bed. Rooms have air conditioning but the remote wasn’t there so we couldn’t use it. Bathroom is dirty and sticky with no ventilation. Showers have no pressure and the water is lukewarm at best. Kitchen is so small and very dirty - I would not at all want to use this. Tv room only has seating on a couch for two which is also covered in stains. Rooms don’t lock and sometimes in the bathroom it was hard to open the lock to get out again. No atmosphere, very little common area space and surprisingly few people staying here speak a word of English. For a hostel in Rome, the location is great but the price for a dorm bed is more like a budget hotel. Don’t forget that you will need to pay the city tax in cash on arrival in addition to your room price. It is a better place to stay than the area around Termini but in Rome I’d recommend that you pay an extra $20 per person/night and stay in a budget hotel.

author: Christophe_SB
title: Amazing stay
text: This hostel is by far the best one i've seen in Europe for that kind of price. The staff is very nice and helpful as they will help you with any problem you have. They will also be able to give you hints about museums, attractions, transport or good restaurants. The place is very clean (every room get cleaned every day). There is good A/C in every room and the wifi is fast. The kitchen is a bit small, but at least you have enough equipment to cook easy stuff (there is no oven). The place is very original as you can find many cartoons/comics/game related furnitures. I was sleeping in a 6 bed mixed dorm and we had our private bathroom. There is a nice living room with a flat screen TV and a PS3. There is many DVDs and PS3 game that you can enjoy. The place is in a very good location, about 10 minutes walk from Vatican City and about 3 minutes walk from subway station. There is a supermarket at 5 minutes walk from there. Just ask the reception guy for that info. The people that stayed there was mostly young (from 20 to 30) but there was also a family. I would recommend that place to anybody that want a nice stay in Rome!

author: DiscoDonald
title: Clean, good location but quite noisy
text: Me and my boyfriend stayed here for 4 nights in April 2014. We were in the double en suite Dylan Dog room. Room - spacious and clean. However, we did get a couple of flea bites which I think may have come from the rug in the room but I cannot be certain. Bathroom - nice and clean. Great shower. Toilet made a very loud strange noise for about 20 seconds when flushed which was a little annoying. The walls are VERY thin and you could hear everything the other guests were doing or saying in their rooms and in the corridor. On our first night there was some loud people drinking and watching tv in the common room down the hall and as the walls are quite thin, they did keep us awake until 2am. However, our other 3 nights there were much quieter. I would highly recommend taking ear plugs with you. As a very lightsleeper, I probably wouldnt have got much sleep without them. Also, a lot of the other guests would wake up about 7am and you could hear them showering and getting ready. The staff are very helpful and friendly and speak great English. We asked them to book us a transfer to the airport and they did so no problem. The location of the hotel is also good. You can either walk around the city and explore or there is a metro station 2 mins from the hotel which is very handy. We got a shuttle bus from the airport which took about 45 mins. At 15 euros per person it is much cheaper and faster than getting the train/metro. I would highly recommend.

author: Rages_64
title: Just not my lucky days
text: We were at this hotel as a group of business travelers. The rooms of all others were a little bit outdated and not as clean as you expect at a 4 star hotel. My room was in terrible condition and it had a viwe to walls and a roof, instead to the park as advertized. When leaning out of the window I could see a bit of the park. When I've opende the wardrobe door it fell on me and hit me at shoulder and head. Most srews were missing and some were now laying on the floor. The screws stayed on the floor as well as the toe nails from a previous guest until I've checked out. My experience is, they did not vaccum clean this room before and during my 3 day stay. The wardrobe was fixed on day to as well as the telefone. The non-functional air condition was not fixed although one of the front desk staff has checked it. At first and again at check-out they blamed me for the non-functioning aircondition because it doesn't work it the window is open. Well it was checked and a failure was confirmed. The bathroom was clean and in good shape, expect for a loose metal bar on the floor at the entrance. After fixing the wardrobe I've found a small bottle of liquor in my room to compensate for the unconvenience. The cardboard package of the bottle and the bottle itself were previously opened. No a nice guesture! At check-out I payed my bill and the man behind the counter started to make fun of what happened to me in this room. I was not happy about his attitude and I told him that. As a consequence He refused to hand out the final receipt and he refused to call a taxi. Neither from a 4 four star hotel nor from a Mercure would I expect any of these things.

author: 457eltonm
title: Perfect end to our trip
text: The last stop on our amazing trip through Europe and especially Italy. My wife is a teacher and wanted to stop at R.E. being the "Mecca" for early childhood education philosophy. The Mercure was fantastic. We booked a balcony room for eur5.00 more. (95.00 all up). Overlooking a very large park in the town centre, very peaceful. The park needed the grass to be cut (looked like it gad not been done for 3 or 4 months? ). They had parking available. The room was spacious, the bed very comfortable. Breakfast was included and extremely tasty. Plenty of variety. It had a gym, but was limited and hours only 10am - 9.30pm? No good for me as an early riser to train. I just ate more for Brekky thinking how long it will take to get back in shape when we get home?! (Possibly years?!). It looked like they were hosting a conference also, the hotel handked the volune of people well and the staff were courteous at every turn. Thoroughly recommend the hotel.

author: sandyw1969
title: 2ND Time Stay
text: I have just recently returned from a trip to Reggio Emilia area of Italy. I stayed in the Mercure Astoria and was originally booked to stay for 3 nights... we ended up coming back to stay an extra night because we enjoyed the hotel so much. The staff were really friendly and efficient from the very start. Our check in was smooth and quick.We were told about all the facilities and offered free wi-fi codes. the room itself was perfect, I had contacted the hotel a week before I arrived and asked for a room overlooking the park. They answered me the same day and said they would do all they could, I got the exact room i had asked for on arrival. The room is spacious, spotless and well appointed. I really have to highlight the team that are working there the reception staff were all lovely and extremely pleasant always saying hello and goodbye as we were entering or leaving the hotel. I must give a special mention to the lady working in restaurant for breakfast she was so attentive making sure we had everything we wanted and telling us about the various coffees. The hotel is a great location within Reggio we drove to it with no bother from Bologna airport and availed of the free car parking provided in front of the hotel. It is 5 minutes walking distance to the main squares and shopping areas of Reggio. If you are staying in the Reggio Emilia do not go past the Mercure Astoria for a place to stay. Definate 5 out of 5 from me ....... will be back

author: LeaFrancis
title: Nice staff, good rooms, quiet and comfortable.
text: We arrived by car and parked our car in the underground car park. Nice big spaces, clean and well lit. Fully secure and out of the searing heat of the day ( we arrived in the June heatwave). Rooms a good size, with a mini bar, TV with CNN and BBC channels as well as local Italian channels. Free Wifi in all rooms. Good sized bed that are comfortable. Our room was quiet and cool ( with a/c). The bar serves lighter meals and drinks, and the bar man was friendly and helpful. We used the restaurant on one evening and found it to be fine. Typical Italial fare with pasta, pizza and a few fish dishes. Good staff that are obviously used to serving in a good restaurant. Front desk staff are very helpful and polite. They all speak good English. Its a 7 or 8 minute stroll into the main town, although there is not too much to see. A nice stay. We had no complaints.

author: Spanna52
title: Lovely room. Overpriced, poor quality food. Inconsistent service.
text: I stayed here for the first International Summer School. (It was a 10-15 minute walk to the International Centre from here.) I was pleased with the room itself. I booked a superior room and it was a great size with a balcony. Always very clean. Annoyingly they put plastic sheets on the bed and pillows which meant it was an uncomfortable sleep. The sound proofing was not good between rooms and from the corridor, especially as the heavy doors slammed. The service was inconsistent and really depended on who served you. Some of the reception staff were good and seemed professional. Others gave incorrect information and were less professional. The most disappointing issue was the food. Very overpriced and of poor quality. It's got to be bad when you order pasta in Italy and you hear the microwave ping!! For 10euros I'd expect more. Same for the breakfast - buffet 12 euros, too expensive for what you get! The biggest plus was the free internet in the room. Another plus was the location. Very central and set in the park. Beautiful.

author: 529julietf
title: Great family room great location
text: I really liked this hotel. The family room has a double bed downstairs (2 singles joined) very comfy. Up a spiral staircase, on mezzanine are two more beds for the children. The room was quiet and cool despite visiting Granada in a heatwave! Air con great but actually only needed for initial cooling blast then the room was fine as it is quite dark. We took the bus from the airport, the hotel is a one minute walk from the bus stop. No need for a car. Cheap 3 Euros each. Great location close to the cathedral. We ate breakfast out as there are cafes nearby. There is a handy supermarket so we bought milk and had a cup of tea etc in the room. Staff are friendly and helpful. It is a pretty hotel with some original features. It is cool and relaxing after a hot day sightseeing. You can walk to all the old town easily. Even up to the Alhambra, it would take half an hour and it is uphill but we went around 6pm and it was doable. Lovely area to walk around up there.

author: ARB1615
title: Lovely hotel in a great location
text: We had a double room with two windows and a beautiful coffered ceiling. There were electrical outlets on both sides of the bed to charge phones. Very nice bathroom with shower. The furnishings were lovely and the room comfortable. There was A/C in our room. The wifi was free, but didn't work very well. Very nice breakfast and breakfast area. The hotel was classy and the staff were friendly and helpful. The best part of the hotel is its location! You can walk to everything you want to see and do. It is also close to bus stop if you need to go a farther distance. Lots of shopping and restaurants nearby. Great hotel. Would love to stay here again. Our only problem was some street noise.

author: pok1961
title: It was the people that make a hotel
text: Female receptionists are stars of the hotel. They were super helpful, friendly and professional and deserved 10 stars. They went out of their way to help us find tickets for Alhambra because we came unprepared during the high seasons. Although the attempt was not successful it was highly appreciated. They speaks a few languages fluently. We were comfortable in this hotel. Bedrooms and corridors are lovingly decorated. There was one elevator and it functioned well. Windows insulation was good and kept street noise away. The down side, which is not the hotel's fault, is the driving and parking situation. Granada is full of tight grid roads and if you want centrally located, value-for-money hotels, parking is the first thing you have to trade off. We were sweating our way driving there just on Easter Monday afternoon. It took over 30 minutes to find it due to some roads being one-way traffic. We had to drive through pedestrian zones on top. There is a temporary loading area in front of the hotel to ease unpacking the car. The hotel has arrangements with nearby parking so that we could get reduced parking fees. It was not the easiest parking one can find but we won't complain for the many lovely attractions that are just a few steps away from the hotel and parking house. We highly recommend Anacapri for its value for money and high staff efficiency. Those travel with cars must keep steel nerves when driving into Granada inner city.

author: Xplor138
title: Friendly, quiet, great location
text: Like us, the majority of folks who stay here are visiting Alhambra. And it's a great location. 20 minute walk or five minutes in a cab. Also close to all the night life in the old Muslim quarter. Situated down a quiet side street but a short walk to great tapas bars and restaurants. Posh shopping district equally short walk. The hotel is three start but has most amenities you'd want for a night or two. Good size rooms. Well appointed. Aircon. Ours had a huge private patio / balcony. Importantly, staff are super friendly and helpful. Finding the hotel was challenging but if you follow the hotel's instructions carefully (ask for them before you travel) you'll find it ok. I confess it took us a couple of attempts having missed a turning. Also, an important tip, ask the hotel to book the Alhambra well in advance of arrival. We heard guests pleading with the reception staff for tickets to enter the Alhambra palaces. They'd come from all over the world to find they couldn't get access to the main attraction because it's booked up weeks or even months in advance.

author: C8046NJemmar
title: A simple, no frills hotel in the centre of Granada. Would benefit hugely from getting rid of the air 'freshener'.
text: Our experience is a bit mixed. We booked the hotel as it was in the heart of the city. It's very close to the wonderful shops, restaurants and markets and the Morroccan quarter, which feels like you are actually in Morrocco! The choice of restaurants in the area is great, with amazing food and ambience. Anacapri is a simple (basic) and clean hotel. The beds were very comfortable and the room/ensuite very clean. The receptionists were very friendly and helpful. Not so good points: Why all the air freshener? It's not good to breathe in all those chemicals!!! I just think it's really unnecessary and I feel sorry for the staff who have to breathe it in all the time. There aren't any tea/coffee making facilities and the 'cafe' was actually the breakfast area, which is out of use other than at breakfast time. This really wasn't too much of an issue, as there are so many nearby cafes, but it would have been nice to have had the option. There are so many wonderful teas for sale in the area and it would have been nice to have been able to sample them during our stay. There is no water or glasses provided in rooms, but glasses were provided for us when asked. There is free wifi, although it is a bit slow.

author: LivingInWien
title: 3.5 stars - good hotel but pros and cons
text: We had a good stay but it was our least favorite hotel out of four cities. Definite pros and cons. Pros: Location was amazing and perfect. Close to the Plaza Nueva, cathedral, footpath to Alhambra, and road to Albayzin. We took a cab to the Alhambra and walked down. We also took a cab to Sacromonte and walked down. Walked all around town. Front desk was helpful and very friendly. Lots of good bars and restaurants close by. Parking was easy to find and worked well. Cons: We didn't love our room. We were in a family room that was recently renovated. It was on the first floor and had a loft so kids slept in twin beds downstairs and up a narrow spiral staircase was a double of two twins pushed together. It was a noisy ground floor room with low ceilings on both levels (I'm tall) and no natural,light. Bathroom was fine but shower water got everywhere and no ventilation. Aside from the room we loved the hotel.

author: GoMars
title: Good location, adequate rooms and breakfast
text: The hotel is in a great location for easy access to the Alhambra, the cathedral, and the Albayzin (Moorish quarter) and for other tourist sites in and near old town. That said, when we rounded the corner towing our suitcases and saw the street on which the hotel is located we were greeted by several abandoned graffiti covered storefronts and a couple guys on the curb having a smoke and a few beers who ignored us (thankfully) as we clicked by towing our luggage. The appearance of the hotel lobby was much more reassuring, and I felt completely vindicated for choosing the place when I noted a posting indicating that a Rick Steves group was in the hotel as well --- it was his guidebook that led me to the hotel in the first place. That said, I expect Rick may reconsider his enthusiasm for the place, or at least room 317. (Directly across the narrow street from the hotel lobby is a Segway tour office offering a fun and safe variation on walking tours. We tried it for the first time on this trip and quite enjoyed the experience. Guests of the hotel get a discount.) Ours was room #311 and, frankly, I would not recommend it. On the plus side, the room was clean, had a functional small desk, a small closet, and a free safe (pick up key at front desk), and good electric lighting a bidet and a huge bathroom sink. On the downside, the bed was hard and uncomfortable and along with the poor pillows made for less restful nights than we would like. The one window in the room opened to a view of two nearby walls and offered poor ventilation. The a/c while it worked well, could not be adjusted to blow anywhere except at the head of the bed. And there appeared to be no venting of any kind in the bathroom. And now for the most unusual fixture: the shower head location and the even more bizarrely designed shower door. Take a look at the picture accompanying this review and you'll see an arrangement that makes no sense that I can figure. The shower head is up high in the middle of the long wall in the tiled tub enclosure, and it thus faces outward into the rest of the bathroom. This location is bad enough for several reasons, but it is made laughable by the freely swinging (both directions!) shower door that only extends halfway along the tub's length. I pointed the obvious problem out to the clerk who, herself, found the design bizarre, but only said I should mention it in a review, and said we may need a few extra towels to clean the flooded floor which didn't have a drain. Finally the breakfast was adequate, with a couple choices of (stale) cereal, a good selection of standard fruits to include bananas, orange juice, good bread and some cheese and meat. No bacon, eggs, potatoes...nothing hot.

author: p0intersister
title: Do not drive your car here
text: While the directions to the hotel seemed clear, actually driving to it was anything but. Street signs are non existent in Granada, and the hotel is on such a small street ( we drove right by it because we were sure it was an alley). We finally found it. I jumped out of the car as there was no room to pull in, and my husband drove around the block 3 times while I checked in. He ended up double parking so we could unload our bags. Needless to say, after taking our car to the recommended parking garage (Trex), we left it there for the next 3 days. The hotel is in an excellent location. Everything you could want to see is within walking distance ( Alhambra 15 minutes, Albycin 10 minutes, cathedral 5 minutes). Our room, a standard double, was on the small side, but adequate. The bathroom was quite tight, with an awkward shower set up. Wifi was slow. The air conditioning worked well. Front desk staff spoke English and were very helpful. We did not opt for the breakfast, as there were several cafes close by that we felt were more reasonable. Overall, the hotel was fine for a few nights.

author: 401danr
title: Great Location but noisy rooms
text: Stayed here with friends and family as part of our tour of the different cities in Spain and Portugal. Couple of great things about the hotel. 1) the location is fantastic! It's near shopping, restaurants and virtually all of the 'must sees' of Granada. The Alhambra is a short bus ride away. The bus to the Alhambra can be taken from plaza Isabela Catolica which is a 2-3 minute walk away. 2) the front desk staff are amazing! All the front desk people were helpful in arranging yours and tickets for the Alhambra and flamenco shows. Their suggestions were spot on. 3) the breakfast is great! The croissants and the Jamon served during the breakfast were really great. I only wish I could have brought some with me. Now the reason why I can't give the hotel 5 stars is because: 1) the rooms were poorly sound proofed. The street noise from bars outside and the hallway could be heard inside the room. At night the sound of the partygoers down the street made sleeping difficult. Overall a great hotel with an excellent location. If you're a light sleeper, try other hotels

author: Elle1971
title: Super budget hotel in a great location
text: This hotel is located between the main Gran Via and the Arabic quarter. Everything we wanted was well within walking distance. The staff were excellent, and nothing was too much trouble. We would have happily spoken Spanish throughout our stay but the staff all spoke English. The American lady was especially helpful... providing ides of places to go in the evenings for good tapas and drinks. We stayed in room 103 which overlooked the Atrium so was nice and quiet. you do hear people in the corridor but noise was certainly not an issue. The room was spotlessly clean and well maintained. It was fairly small but more than adequate for a couple. The breakfast was basic but tasty. Ours was included in the price of our stay. Would we stay there again? Yes, absolutely! Thanks again to the staff who made our stay in Granada very enjoyable.

author: ARealMother
title: Great location, helpful staff
text: We chose the Hotel Anacapri based on recommendations here and Rick Steves' book and stayed here 2 nights. This was an excellent location near the Plaza Nueva and a quick bus ride to the Alhambra. The staff was extremely helpful booking our trip to the Alhambra in advance as well as the Arab Baths. They were very friendly. Free W-Fi was included but the strength of the signal wasn't great in the room. The room was small, clean, and comfortable and adequate for our family of three. It was functional but not fancy. But in reality, who spends that much time in the room on vacation? We were located on the 4th floor but could still hear the street noise but it did not keep us awake at night. There was a simple breakfast available each morning which included a selection of rolls, yogurt, meats, cheese, and coffee. Quick and convenient. We arrived by car and were provided detailed directions on how to arrive. After doing a little research, we decided to park at the Alhambra lot (guarded) and take the bus to the hotel so we didn't have to navigate the restricted traffic zone and narrow streets. The cost was about the same and when we left Granada, we were able to quickly get on the highway and avoid the city streets. The location and helpful staff make the Hotel Anacapri an excellent choice and a superb value.

author: WC-Travelers-75
title: Great Stay / Great Bargain/ Great Location
text: We stayed here for three nights, arriving on the train from Madrid. Had a room with two large twin beds on the first floor, one level above the street. At 50 euros/ night, the room was a great bargain. Plenty of room, the A/C and WiFi worked well, safe for valuables is provided in the room. Bathroom was somewhat dated but more than adequate. Room was quiet. Great location and close to all major sites - the Alhambra, the Albayzin, the Cathedral as well as restaurants around Plaza Nueva and its restaurants. Breakfast was 10 euros per person but was a very good buffet - a bargain if you take advantage of it. Front desk staff was very efficient and helpful. They were able to book us into Carmen Mirador de Aixa on short notice. Tips 1. The taxi from the train station took the long way around the Plaza Isabel since he "had to turn around to come in the right way", which cost us a couple more euros since we sat in traffic. Have the taxi driver drop you off at the cathedral on Gran Via de Colon and walk unless you have a lot of baggage. 2. Do not use the laundry service at the hotel. It is an outside service and expensive.They lost some of our clothes and gave us someone elses clothes.The hotel straightened it out but we received our clothes right before departure.

author: dnsnmnd
title: Non-smoking - great people, location, and price
text: We started our search for a Granada hotel for June 2014 during the summer of 2013. Our requirements were a non-smoking room, a room for two adults and a teenage boy, a central location, and a reservation that could be cancelled with no penalty. It did not take us long to learn there are not many non-smoking hotels and not many rooms for 3. We used Booking.com since its search criteria included non-smoking. We wanted a 3 star or above and a rating of 8 or above. The Hotel Anacapri had a rating of 34 out of 129 hotels in Granada and was recommend by Rick Steves. Now with regard to our stay. When we arrived we were upgraded to the family room which was huge. It had a living room with a sofa and 2 twin beds and a bedroom with two twin beds. The location was close to everything. The Alhambra was a short walk away and since we already had tickets, we were able to use the Justice Gate entrance. The staff was great and spoke English. We took the Renfe from Sevilla and flew from Granada to Barcelona on Vueling airlines. We planned on taking a taxi to the airport since there was a stand a block away at Plaza Nueva. We asked the front desk how early we needed to arrive at the airport and they told us there are only 12 flights a day, and there is an airport bus that runs once an hour and takes 40 minutes. And the stop was only a 5 minute walk away. We decided to take the bus which was quick, easy, and cheaper. The airport was small and modern.

author: jdcoach
title: Roberto is the "MAN"-Great customer service!
text: The hotel is centrally located 1 block from the Cathedral. 1 block from the #30 bus stop that takes you to the Alhambra front gate. Hotel is nice, comfortable and clean. Now my kudo's!! Roberto is "the Man". Realized I had a mistake on my next booking in Seville. Roberto got on the phone, called the hotel I was going to stay at, and fixed my problem. It took about 1/2 hour but, he diligently went about a fixed my reservation. Went above and beyond "good customer service". He and his coworker Stefamie were helpful finding us a place to eat to try the local flavor. Sent us to spots, they eat at. Customer service is sometimes more important than all the extra stuff you look for in a hotel. This was the case today! Can't say enough good things about the front desk staff. When staff save your vacation the hotel needs to know and future customers need to know that they will have a good stay. Only negative is that the walls are a bit thin but, everything else is great. Next time I'm in Granada, this is where I am staying.

author: whitesheilagh
title: In the heart of the city
text: We stayed in this hotel for 3 nights and thought it was excellent value for money. The hotel is situated in a quiet little side street off the main street up to Plaza Nueva and is so handy for shopping, bars, restaurants, the Cathedral and the Alhambra. The bus for the Alhambra and the city tour bus both set off from a stop about 2 minutes walk from the Anacapri. We were two ladies spending a long weekend in Granada and it was so handy to be 2 minutes walk from restaurants and bars at night. Our rooms were both used as single rooms but since they had double beds they could presumably be given out to couples which would be a bit cramped. The bathrooms had a shower, bath, bidet, WC and basin and although a little tired decor wise were spotlessly clean. We were delighted to have an excellent signal for wifi in our bedrooms on the second floor, and not just in reception area. The staff were exceptional especially Kathy in reception an American lady from Iowa who was so helpful and efficient. She went the extra mile for us and booked our tickets for the Alhambra. What were the down sides? Our terms included continental breakfast so we ate there and thought the choice was good, the room pleasant, the bread and rolls freshly baked and there was plenty to eat, but the coffee and tea tasted bitter. The main downside for us was the walls were paper thin, there were no soft furnishings in the room to absorb noise and the noise from other rooms travelled easily. We were there at the same time as a group of college students who came in late and although they tried to be considerate we were wakened at 5am with the noise of doors clicking shut, toilets flushing and water running! Would we recommend this budget hotel? Absolutely. Would we stay here again? Certainly.

author: hyunshim
title: Nice reception and strange management
text: Overall, it was a nice and decent budget hotel. Cleanly maintained with friendly and helpful staff was one good thing about this hotel. Location was ideal to visit anywhere in Granada. What made me embarassing was their policy; they said I could get free breakfasts with my Rick Steve's Spain. I confirmed it via email. --At first, I reserved it through booking.com and when I requested about it, they emailed me: 'to get free breakfast, you should reserve directly in our website.' So, I cancelled the former one and did it through their website. They replied 'Perfect. you can get free breakfast with the book.' So, I never doubted about it. But when I got there, they told me that I should pay higher rate to have breakfasts. I would happily pay surcharge if they have informed me beforehand. It wasn't a bad hotel at all to stay and the rate was quite good. But their attitude wasn't right to accept. I am 60 and travelled quite extensively all over the world. So, I stayed in various accomodations.- from 4,5 star hotels to B&B's. But this kind of happenings never have occurred. I hasitated to write this review because Cathy at the reception was so helpful. But I decided this kind of procedure must be straightened up. Hope this wouldn't make people hesitate to go to this hotel. Just check out their rate applicable before you get there.

author: RichR970
title: Clean boutique hotel in the heart of the city!
text: We stayed at the Anacapri for 9 nights in January 2013. We were in Granada to visit our children who were studying at the University of Granada for the winter semester. The location is wonderful. Half a block from the Plaza Nueva, and within walking distance of the Alhambra (although you may want to take a taxi or bus since it's uphill all the way!) Minutes from the charming Carrera del Darro, and Mirador de San Nicolas, there is certainly a lot to see and do right there. There are also many little restaurants for drinks, tapas, and dinners. We reserved a triple room, and the first night they put us in a quad room which was up on the fifth floor. As was mentioned in another review, the hotel elevators only go up to the fourth floor, so we had to climb a flight of stairs with our luggage to reach this room. That was the only down side. The hotel staff arranged with us to have our luggage moved to our regular room while we were out and about. Rooms were cleaned every day and we couldn't complain about service. Our subsequent room was on the first floor, and we were often able to get the wifi from within the room. We opted for the daily breakfast, which is served from 7:30 to 10:30 a.m. It consisted of yogurt cups (room temperature), fresh fruit, rolls, pastries, sliced meats and cheese, orange juice, and a coffee machine which made various types of coffee. There were plenty of tables in various rooms off the lobby. The front desk staff were very helpful with directions, bus information, and ideas for activities. They even called a barber shop for information for my son who wanted to get his hair cut. Yes, the noise from outside can be bothersome, but we found that many people go out to the bars and restaurants, and don't leave until 3 or 4 in the morning. If you're a light sleeper, you may want to request a room on a higher floor, or one that doesn't face the street. All in all, I think this hotel was a very good value for its price.

author: DianaP_12
title: Pleasant hotel with very helpful staff
text: We enjoyed stay at the Anacapri for two main reasons--the very helpful staff and the great location. The person who was most helpful was named Stefanie (I hope I have remembered her name correctly). She went above and beyond the call of duty with all of our questions and requests. She helped us get our Alhambra tickets, instructed us about catching the bus, got us a taxi to the train station, recommended bars and restaurants, etc. She also tried very hard to help us purchase train tickets, but the RENFE website doesn't like American credit cards. Since she couldn't help us accomplish it, she left a note with her co-worker on the next shift to check in with us and help us try again later. She was this helpful with everyone! I heard her talking to several other guests, and offering information catered to each person/group. Other employees were very helpful too, so this hotel clearly has a very strong customer service ethic. Our room was clean, although very small. The bed was a little hard, although it seems from some recent reviews, they replaced the mattresses right after our visit. We didn't eat the buffet, as it seemed very small for the price. (We had just come from a hotel with an amazing buffet that was included in the hotel price.) Also, given the great location of the hotel, we had no problem finding a more affordable breakfast nearby. The hotel is near lots of great tapas bars, and a short walk to the Albaicin (Moorish quarter), the river walk, and the cathedral. It was great to be able to walk out the front door of our hotel, and immediately be in the middle of lots of things we wanted to do. It really saved on time and on taxi/bus costs.

author: S8297VJandrews
title: Perfect hotel in the heart of Granada
text: Just returned from 6 night holiday and overjoyed we stayed at this marvellous hotel. It is in the perfect location. Close to the cathedral and its nearby plazas and the plaza nueva. Great food, cafes and restaurants close to hand. The room was excellent for our needs. We had the only fifth floor room, which is up a flight of stairs. The lift goes to the 4th floor. There are four beds – two in the large living space and two past a partition on the way to the bathroom. This is a perfect arrangement for ourselves and our two children. The room was clean – faultless daily service. There are two air-conditioning unit, one in each of the sleeping areas and two TVs, if you need them. We chose to have breakfast at the hotel for the sake of convenience and so pleased we did. Good choice of pastries, ham, cheese etc constantly topped up by the staff. The staff are all amazingly obliging. Without exception the staff were professional, helpful and obliging. Highly recommended.

author: scienceteech
title: Great room for a family in a wonderful town
text: Our family of four booked the 'family room' at Hotel Anacapri and couldn´t have been happier. We arrived at 8:30 am on a Sunday from the trenhotel overnight train from Barcelona ( a whole different adventure ) and of course our room wasn't ready. We were able to store our luggage and wander to a nearby bakery Pan y Chocolate for some yummy pastries to munch in Plaza Nuevo as the town maintenance crew cleaned up from the night before. The hotel staff worked hard to get us a room but we gave them a break and went to mass at the Cathedral, and when we returned at 11:30 we were able to move in. We had Room 501, the only room on the fifth floor, because the 5th floor is really just this room. Kind of like the penthouse -- kind of. The room was large, with a couch sitting area, tv, two chairs and coffee table, then 2 twin beds, and in a separate area 2 more twin beds with a desk and flat screen TV, and then a very well appointed and clean bathroom. There was a bidet, a toilet, and a shower-bath. There were air conditioners in both bedroom areas with separate remote controls. The rooms were very clean, the linens in very good shape, including towels that were soft. I noticed that other reviewers had some trouble with street noise but we never had any.. maybe because we were up so high. We did not take the breakfast so can´t comment on that, although it smelled very good each day as we were leaving. Our trip to Spain consisted of visits to Barcelona, Granada, Toledo, and Madrid, and the Hotel Anacapri was our hands down favorite hotel and Granada was our favorite town. We could have spent a week there.

author: Cherpig
title: 5-star Location!
text: We (2 couples) spent 4 nights at Anacapri. Would HIGHLY recommend as a home-base in Granada! Anacapri is PERFECTLY located for accesss to Granada's sights and transportation. You are only 5 minutes walk from many popular restaurants. Plaza Nueva--3 minutes walk--offers frequent buses to Alhambra for only 1 euro per person. Rooms are very basic with outdated furniture and baths that could be remodeled. Generally clean. Staff was friendly. Internet is expensive at hotel (NO FREE Wi-Fi), so, we used the internet cafe, located across the street, for VERY CONVENIENT and CHEAP internet & international phone calling! Did not eat breakfast at hotel. HINT: There is one airport that services Granada. The taxi cost from airport to Granada's Old Town Center is about 28 euros ($41 USD.) Instead, we used the AIRPORT(aeropuerto)BUS--which serves approximately 5 pick-up/drop-off points throughout the city. The cost is 3 euros (about $4.50USD/person) A BARGAIN! No reservations needed. Show up and pay the bus driver. The bus is VERY comfortable with plush seats and huge baggage storage beneath--like a touring bus. The nearest stop to Hotel Anacapri is less than 2 minutes walk! Located across from the Cathedral/Royal Chapel...use bus-stop "Gran Via."

author: pgrwrx
title: Overnight stay
text: Stayed at this hotel on the way to Inverness. Has on-site parking which is a real bonus. Reception staff were welcoming. One night stay so didn't get to experience much. Close to the city centre but on a side street. Unfortunately my room was on the street side and subject to the afetrnoon sun which made the room a bit warm. Given the location no air con but wasn't too bad. Had dinner at the in house restaurant. Excellent selection of dishes. I had the fried camembert and brie cheese on a ceasar salad. Interesting but very rich. Also had fried kushrooms for starters. Yummy! The young lady who looked after us in the restaurant was very helpful but not intrusive. Breakfast was ok. Would stay again. .

author: Egg1950
title: EXCELLENT - AS ALWAYS !
text: Another very enjoyable stay at The Brentwood, on one of my regular trips back to Aberdeen, to watch my favourite football team in action. I received a delightfully warm & friendly welcome from Jane in Reception. My room, as always, was clean & tidy, with a very comfy bed and an adequately sized en-suite bathroom. I'm always pleasantly surprised by the fact that, despite its city centre location, the bedrooms I've had have always been quiet, ensuring a good night's sleep. I was joined for dinner & a few beers by a pal of many years . . . . he enjoyed the spicy salmon . . . . I had an excellent curry which, at my request, Chef had "cranked up" to my preferred HOT. Dinner was served in a nice relaxed manner by Christine, who was back to serve me a very tasty "full Scottish" breakfast the following morning. The barman Andy was one of the most pleasant & efficient I've encountered in a very long time, helping to make my evening of chat all the more enjoyable. I've stayed in The Brentwood a fair number of times now, either alone or with my son, and have yet to score it anything other than 5/5. HIGHLY RECOMMEND

author: Diez66
title: Not Perfect but Really, Really Good, Really enjoyed our stay
text: OK, not 5 stars but so close. Close and easy to find but a little uphill from the station. It is as good as it looks on this site, lovely building almost residential location and when we were there it was nice and quiet. On arrival it was cold and unfortunately the room was very cold as there was no heating on, until we arrived. It took a while to warm up which was a pity as we wanted to have a rest after a long day on trains getting here. The only other down was the bathroom, which seemed cold throughout our stay and some black on the ceiling above the bath. OK, that is all the bad stuff, now the GOOD. Staff, fantastic, really nice and helpful made checking in easy and any time we saw them, a cheerful encounter. The room was quite big. It had tea, coffee, chocolate and biscuits; nice. Shower; if the shower is good I am a happy bunny, it was great, thanks "The Brentwood". They have a bar and restaurant, the bar looked good and full of happy people, we chose to eat in the restaurant the first night and what a good decision that was. Food, really good, both our choices left the other feeling slightly jealous. We had to share. I live in Spain so wine in the UK always seems so expensive, it was quite pleasant to get the, nice, house wine for under a tenner; nearly went back the second night on the strength of that alone but, a new city you have to try other places? Breakfast, in the same place and once again really nice. fast and fresh. The staff, just like the reception staff, really good, even more jolly that we are first thing in the morning. We enjoyed Aberdeen, we will go back again and we will try to stay at here again. Perfect for our 48 hours stay

author: B7580QHjohnb
title: EXCELLENT HOTEL IN BRILLIANT LOCATION
text: This excellent hotel has a brilliant location in the centre of Aberdeen. The main train and bus stations are both less than a five minute walk from the hotel. Airport link buses depart from this bus station. The main shopping street, Union Street is only a few minutes’ walk away. Although Union Street is so close by, the hotel itself is situated on a very quiet street and there is no street noise. The hotel has its own private car park to the rear of the premises. This is a bonus if you are travelling by car as many city centre hotels do not have such a facility. The hotel has an excellent restaurant and a nice bar area which has a great ambience to it. Bar prices were very reasonable. The restaurant has an extensive menu and again prices were very reasonable. Breakfast was excellent and cooked to perfection. The room that we stayed in was very well appointed and was spotlessly clean. The bed was very comfy and there was no street noise to disturb any sleep. The room was supplied with a hairdryer and tea and coffee making facilities. There was also a small fridge in the room. Free Wifi was also supplied. One of the outstanding things about this hotel is the attitude of the staff. They are all exceptionally helpful and friendly and nothing is too much trouble for them. In my opinion the Brentwood is an excellent all round hotel in a prime location. It goes without saying that I would highly recommend this hotel to others as I intend use it for all my future stays in Aberdeen.

author: evrynameistaken
title: Nice and Clean
text: Welcoming friendly reception staff. Very clean rooms. Decent amount of tea coffee and hot chocolate. Fluffy towels, nice soap, extra little extras! Free wifi. I just don't know why every other hotel charges for it. Toast barely browned, like all other hotels. Waiting staff under pressure as everyone went to breakfast at the same time! Much more friendly than the other one down the road on the opposite side. Good breakfast available, although I just had cereal, toast and tea. This is my number one choice when I visit Aberdeen now. Didn't have a car with me. Room was at the front. There was no traffic noise on this Saturday night. Terrible view of a wall and the extraction pipes a few feet away from the window of this single room. Extractor fan runs all night from kitchen, so noise has to be expected with the window open, but I was tired and it didn't keep me awake for long. Queen size bed was firm after a memory foam mattress, but not uncomfortable. Pillows were comfy.

author: NatashaS79
title: Good location - I wouldn't pay full price
text: I got a room here discounted as a last minute deal and for I paid it was adequate. At first I found the staff a bit aggressive and threatening. I checked in and then went for a walk. When I came back a member of staff (a large build man)followed me up the stairs and demanded to know what room number I was in. As a lone travelling female I found this a bit scary. When he explained he worked there and he had not realised I was a resident things were a bit better. I later appreciated the fact that these staff were actually very protective of their residents and made me feel quite safe there despite the fact the hotel is just off one of the busiest tourist/ stag party stretches The room is ok but if I had paid the full amount (equiv of £120/120 E) a night, I think I may have been disappointed as despite the convenient location, the rooms are not of the quality for that price. There was a good variety of breakfast I had problems with the lock on my door. Every time I left my room and came back I had to get a new key as it stopped working- not sure if my room was just a bit odd or if it was something I was doing, but it was a little bit annoying. There wasn't any lighting in the hallways either which made it a bit of an adventure trying to navigate to your room after dark :) The hotel advertises itself as overlooking Charles Bridge- it is 2 roads back from the bridge and there is no way you can see the bridge from the hotel. I however got a view of the air con unit :) I often travel with disabled people but was not this time. However this would not be a good option for disabled people. There are lots of stairs throughout. There is a lift but as others have said, you have to go up two flights of stairs before the lift is accessible. The doorways are also very narrow. The hotel had a feel of the old culture, with many of the old fittings and style- which I personally love , but I appreciate it is not everyone's taste

author: johnhM6435IW
title: Mid week city break
text: Hotel Liliova is a converted apartment block. Newly refurbished, very clean. Right in the centre of the old town, 5 minute walk from Charles Bridge, Bethlehem Chapel and 10 minutes walk from old town square. The entrance is down a side street off a square that is very busy. I was concerned about the noise but with triple glaze windows we were not disturbed. Reception staff were very pleasant. Access to the rooms would be difficult for those with mobility issues. Even the lift is up a few small flights through a few short narrow corridors. Breakfast was downstairs from reception in the basement. Some reviews did mention the breakfast refills. For us it was adequate. A small hot option with 2 items changed each day. There was cereal yoghurt, breads, fruit, cheese and ham, juices teas and coffee. There was enough to choose from and did get replenished. My only concern was the table cloths remained the same each day. Not sure if that's a bit custom. Nice convenient location. I would stay again.

author: Kansenji
title: Location, Location, Location & Good Value.
text: I stayed in Room 14 (1st floor, front) for 7 nights from 11th April 2012, with my wife. The hotel's own transfer service collected us from the airport & returned us at the end of our week's stay; it is well worth using their own, very efficient service. The hotel's location is absolutely superb for tourists; very close to the major attractions yet in a quiet (now pedestrianised) cobbled side street. The reception staff are excellent & all speak English too. Our room was a bit smaller than expected (about 17 square metres) but appears to have been completely renovated in the last couple of years. The very high quality bathroom was a very pleasant surprise though (can I have one like that at home please?) :0) The room was very clean & attended to daily by the chambermaid. Furniture was plain but functional, with timber framed beds and very comfortable memory foam mattresses. Do take care not to bruise your feet & legs though, as space between the desk/chair & beds is restricted. An LCD television was provided, but only Czech language channels were available. A fridge was in the room, plus a safe. The window was TRIPLE glazed (outer double-glazing, plus a third pane on the inside); the heating worked very well & air conditioning was provided (though seemingly switched off for the winter). Hotels in Prague do not generally provide tea & coffee making facilities in guest rooms & The Liliova is no exception. There are numerous restaurants nearby though (The nearby TGI Fridays serves food until midnight) and refrigerated drinks can be bought from the hotel reception area. We were very well attended to at breakfast on our first morning by a very helpful man, in contrast to the attitude of the female staff member on subsequent days of "everything is too much trouble"; she made us feel unwelcome. The breakfast food was adequate, though I would have liked a better range of cereals to choose from. CONCLUSION: An excellent hotel for the price, especially taking account of its location. The breakfast service though, does need some attention from management; it is the only thing that lets the hotel down.

author: Bradys1
title: If you are looking for the ideal base for your trip to Prague this is it!
text: We have just returned from a long weekend in Prague, our first visit to the city, and we loved it. Your hotel is often the first impression you get about the city and it's people and the hotel liliova did not disappoint. Situated on a very quiet street we were a bit worried when we seen the sign for a table dance club which shares an entrance lane (do not let that deter you please. We were here for 3 nights and saw no-one and heard nothing from the club) We were met by a more than helpful receptionist who was more than happy to assist us and answer questions. The hotel itself was immaculate and we had a very spacious, clean room with very comfortable beds. We were also given a discount card to use inthe restaurant on the ground floor where breakfasts would be served. We dropped our luggage off in the room and headed for some lunch and were pleased to be met with such lovely friendly staff and an extensive international menu. Really did make an excellent impression on us this hotel. LOCATION Ideally situated in the old town. Walk around the corner and you are at Charles Bridge, walk round the opposite corner and you have a straight 3 min walk to the astronomical clock and the old town square. About 10-15 minute walk to Jewish quarter. Couldn't have asked for more! 2 doors down from the hotel there is a TGI Fridays. Hagan Daz shop round the corner as well as a mini market. All in loved Prague, it's very welcoming people and this hotel was a real find. Thank you to all staff at the hotel liliova for making our stay so stress free!

author: JK68
title: IN Old Prague
text: We stayed for 2 nights, left to go to Cesky Krumlov for 2 days and came back for 5 more nights. We were able to leave our luggage while we were away. For the two nights we had a smaller room on the back, very quiet, no view. For the later nights we had a front room with a distant view of the castle and a good view of rooftops and a bridge tower. When the trumpeter played in the tower we could enjoy it. I never tired of the view. There were only a few moments when loud people in the street below disturbed us. In warm September we mostly left our windows open. The location worked very well for us. We could actually be on the bridge in 5 minutes. We could follow the crowds and stroll the shopping street, arriving at the square in just a few minutes. We kept finding new places to eat, or for a beer , nearby. The staff were efficient, pleasant and helpful. The breakfast was good, with a choice of hot eggs along with a pretty good spread of bread and cheese and meat. We had no complaints and thought that having a week to wander Prague was a great luxury.

author: Arkansastraveler69
title: 22 miles and an hour due to traffic from the beaches
text: Traffic is ALWAYS bad any where near Tampa/St. Pete. I've driven in every major city in America and due to lack of controlled access connectors to the Interstate (I-75) it is a bad here as anywhere. Takes forever to get any where more than a couple of miles away. For us, the location was central to the beaches to the West and the wild life management area and bird sanctuaries I wanted to photograph in. The facility is clean and well appointed. Rooms were nice and the beds comfortable. Still no charge for pets but rumor has it, that is changing. We had planned to stay a whole week but stayed only four days - 3 nights due tot eh lack of a HOT breakfast. We have stayed in La Quinta Inns all over the Country. One of the reasons is the wonderful HOT breakfast we always, until now, received. “Brightside” certainly implies a HOT breakfast. Cold hard boiled eggs, cold cereal and muffins, and cold frozen waffle slices warmed in a toaster (and lukewarm coffee) is NOT a “brighside” hot breakfast. For all the positive things we can say about this location and management, a hot breakfast is not one of them. We have stayed in motels for half the price that served a hot breakfast and were also pet friendly: Hot eggs, bacon, sausage, biscuits and gravy and piping hot coffee.

author: nrajk757
title: Needs major renovation and some cleaning
text: We drove from Miami for my son’s soccer tournament. The location of the hotel is perfect, around restaurants, movie theater, shopping etc. Unfortunately the location of the hotel can’t make up for what’s inside. This hotel is in a major need of some renovation and TLC. The hallways look like they haven’t been vacuumed in ages, the smell is of mold, mildew and just plain old smell of an old building. The elevator was super dirty and looked like someone literally smeared something (it was like that from Friday night to Sunday). Our room was a good size with comfy beds, but again smelly, old looking. The worst was the bathroom. Our tub had a glued on anti slip mat that was peeling in the corners. Underneath you can see the dirt, buildup and rust. I had a 5 year old and wouldn’t let him sit so had to bathe standing up. On the floor of the bathroom you literally had a pile of dirt build up and it looks as if it hasn’t been cleaning in a long time. Does management ever do walk through of these rooms? The breakfast was good. It was a simple and quick continental breakfast. Clean area and the staff were always near by to clean and replace anything that ran out. Front desk was also super friendly. All in all, staff is great, it’s great that breakfast is included but I’d much rather spend $20-$30 more a night on the newly renovated la Quinta down the road (they were sold out when we tried to book).

author: GingerH952
title: Shining Light Whenever it was NEEDED!
text: Last time we visited Florida was in 2015, and decide in the Fall to make plans for the last full week in Dec. 2017. First stop was to visit St. Augustine, and stay 2 nights in Ormond, Fl. and head back to Tampa, Fl. for 3 night...On Nov.28-29 research and finally decide to make a room reservations for 2 nights in Ormond, Fl. at Ocean Crest Motel for Dec. 27-28th. We decide to visit son in Harrisburg, Ms on 12.26 and the next day [12.27]drive all the way to Ormond Beach. En route around 11:48 AM; hubby wanted me to call the motel, informing them - we would be a late arrival. Whoever answer the phone HAD NO RECORD OF US FOR A RESERVE ROOM at 11:51 AM. Here my hubby and I are driving to a place on the other side of Florida and if Hubby didn't suggested me to call- can you imagine the 'pickle' we would had been in? This is WHERE LaQuinta comes in! Thankfully we had already prearranged 2 nights reservations at LaQuinta Brandan West, in Tampa for Dec. 29-30. Thank the good Lord- LaQuinta Inn had a extra room for that same night. There we were driving along I-20-toward St.Augustine, called Ocean Crest Motel to let them know of LATE ARRIVAL - only to find out we didn't even have a room to spend the night. LaQuinta Inn was our SHINING LIGHT BECAUSE IT WAS NEEDED- DESPERATELY!

author: phughes1956
title: Lack of attention to details
text: Made reservation for my family in their name using my credit card to hold. When family arrived, there was no room reserved for them and they were advised to go to the other LaQuinta close by. A couple days later i discovered a charge on MY CREDIT CARD for the cost of the room that was never used. (the same thing happened last year, but too much trouble to pursue at the time-not this time). After returning I went to inquire about the missed reservation and was told it was reserved in my name. After some resistance and misunderstanding on part of the desk clerk, she finally acknowledged that the error was hers, she submitted the refund and was told my account would be credited within 48 hours. That was 6 days ago and I haven't gotten the refund yet. Suffice to say I won't be recommending this motel again - two errors in two tries. When I made the reservation on a Sunday afternoon, I asked for a confirmation. He handed me a hand-written number on a piece of note paper. There as another lady, whom I won't name, working the desk with him. The date was 2/4 for a 2/5 reservation. There are plenty of suitable lodging locations in the area. In case anybody wants to know, I will be contacting the home office with my concern. The refund invoice number is 249180, supposedly processed on 2/19/18. Any business can provide a clean bed, TV, continental breakfast, etc. It's the little things, the attention to detail, that keep customers coming back. La Quinta was my family's choice of lodging. Not again.

author: vedamargaret
title: New Management is the WORST!
text: Stayed at this location last year when here on business and had a great stay. My husband and I stayed with our 2 dogs for 3 days during hurricane Irma as our home was in her direct path. People standing at each and every entrance/exit smoking cigarettes ALL day and ALL night making it impossible to go in or out without walking through a cloud of cigarette smoke. Since I am allergic to cigarette smoke, I get instant throat, ear, and sinus irritation, using means of egress makes it difficult! Not to mention, who wants to take a shower and put on clean clothes to walk through cigarette smoke! At one point, people were standing IN THE HALL smoking because it was raining. There are signs at each door not to smoke within 25 feet. When brought to the General Managers attention, Sharon Quinonas (sp), she said "They can do what they want". They locked doors when winds were picking up and loudly and rudely shouted, "We are on lockdown for the storm and you can go out at your own risk". I advised they cannot lock us in and that the dogs must go out or they will go on the floor. Sharon yelled, "Then we'll charge ya". Upon returning, from taking the dogs out, I contacted LaQuinta corporate while asking for the manager's name. The manager was rude adn said "do what you gotta do". I advised her attitude was poor and she needed to act accordingly. She told us to go back to our room as we were "causing problems". Another guest got involved and said we were told the procedure about entering and exiting (which this conversation had nothing to do with that). The guest who later apologized to for imposing and said he was wrong to do so as he didn't know the whole story. The manager had no control over the situation; luckily for us, I recorded the whole thing. Another guest made small talk with us who was outside while we were walking our dogs the next morning and she mentioned how nice the lady named Cathy is and said, "But boy, that manager is rude!" "She apparently cannot handle stressful situations (hurricane) well" Will not stay at this location again while this manager is there. Reported to Corporate and have not heard back.

author: ashleymY9145VQ
title: Hostile Front Desk Agent!
text: I wasn't even able to check in. I was waiting behind a mother and son TRYING to check in and the front desk agent named Mattie was being very hostile toward them. I was confused as to why the agent was yelling at them when the agent claimed that their "system" was down. If your system is down and you can't check anybody in, why are you being hostile towards your guests? I just don't understand, she should've told the guests something along the lines of... "I apologize we are experiencing issues with our computer system would you mind waiting in our lobby until we figure out and ETA as to why we are having this issue and as soon as we get our system back up we will check you in, thank you for your patience" instead we were told "You can't check in! I don't know when it will be back up, it's been down all day" UNACCEPTABLE! I left right after I witnessed this happen, I did not want to encounter the same problem so my husband and I just left. I am not going to stay at a property that allows this type of customer service! I have worked in customer service for YEARS and I have NEVER not ONCE treated a guest like this lady, she does NOT need to be in customer service if she acts like this toward the guests. Being rude and nasty to the guests when it's not our fault that your system is down is completely unacceptable! I even witnessed Mattie throw the ID and credit card back at the gentleman and mother trying to check in, I am just astonished that I witnessed such unprofessional behavior from a front desk agent. If your trying to lose business and money then I would say your going in the right direction keeping this lady. If your trying to keep your business going I would suggest bringing on a an agent that is more attentive to the guests and their needs. Even just a simple smile goes a long way, this lady had a resting b face since we walked through the doors. If I could have given this place a 0 I would have.

author: TSOfan
title: A Place to sleep...sorta
text: My friend and I recently stayed at this La Quinta for three nights while on a Spring Training baseball trip to the Tampa area. We decided that we didn't need to spend bid dollars for bigger chain, after all, we wouldn't be in our room that long.That said, the rate was very attractive. Ironically, we stayed one night prior to arriving here at the LaQuinta in Lakeland, FL. Two properties from the same family couldn't be more different. This facility is due for an overhaul. The carpet in the halls and rooms looks dirty, drab and old. Unlike Lakeland, there was no refrigerator in the room. And the straw that broke the camel's back literally was just that...the mattress that I slept on was awful. Three nights sleeping on it left me in pain that hampered my enjoyment of the rest of my weekend activities. I told myself that I wasn't going to complain. But when I got home, I read several other reviews that point out the same issues. It is my hope that management might take notice. This is clearly not an isolated incident. It's time for a change. It's too bad. Our stay in Lakeland was very pleasant, so clearly this isn't normal for the chain.

author: keefe506
title: Good enough.
text: We were there as Spring Break was beginning to happen in the Tampa area. This hotel was reasonably prices on a Friday and Saturday. It is a comfortable room with a nice bed, lots of pillows, good wifi, a nice size refrigerator, and microwave. One of the best features of the hotel is the pool. You might miss it if you don't look around. It is on the other side of the parking lot. It is well located and gets good sun. Very comfortable place to sit outside and catch a few rays in the afternoon. Best outdoor furniture of all the hotels we stayed at in Florida. This is not a deluxe hotel. There is a free breakfast with waffle makers but not much else. Some good oranges and hard boiled eggs, cereal and a few other items but you won't be looking forward to breakfast. The halls are narrow, odd colors and paint that looks like it was done by the managers kids. We were off for the day on Saturday and returned to the room at 5:00. Surprised to find that the room had not been made up. They did get it done after we notified the woman working on our floor. She said she had been very busy that day. I was actually mostly satisfied with this hotel. Not a pretty face but they seem to provide the basics.

author: 47MaineYankee
title: Bad Choice
text: Jan 17-19th 2015 The Hotel was easy to find and well kept and clean. The staff was harried by guest complaining of no hot water when we were checking in. The staff assured everyone a new hot water heater had been installed that day and it would take a while for the water to heat up. When I took my shower the next morning it was warm and turned to tepid before I finished. The second day my wife had a cold shower. They said a plumber would be in the next day to fix it. Seems they were not willing to pay weekend rates to get it fixed right away. The room is nice but the shower and toilet are in a room (closet) about 6 feet by 8 feet. The lavatory, hair dryer and makeup mirror are just outside the bath area next to the door opposite the coat closet. There was a refrigerator and microwave in the room. However, the refrigerator was all iced up and not cooling much. Much of the space in the room is taken up by an oversized desk. The bed is a bit soft and I hate those Chicklet sized pillow. The WIFI internet connection was fast. Breakfast was below average on a scale of 1 to 10 with 10 as the best it was a 3. The coffee was terrible, the juice was watery, there was cold cereal, pastries and waffles available. I have had various problems this year with LaQuinta I am about ready to write them off as a lost cause.

author: destiny4me2
title: Hotel good but staff made it worthwhile
text: Having spent 30 straight days at the Tampa Brandon West, I feel I probably know the hotel better than any other guest...so here it goes. I had just driven across country with my two dogs and arrived at the hotel a bit earlier than expected. Initially, I was asked by the young lady at the Front Desk to come back in a couple of hours as my room was not ready for occupancy.
