As I walked back to my car, totally exhausted, she came running out, yes running out and asked that I wait 10 minutes and she would arrange to have her the staff prepare my room. I requested a room on the first floor so I could have easy access, in and out the building, with the dogs...no problem. I asked for non feathered pillows, due to allergies and received some. I have to say the hotel does have its faults, but they are not due to the staff, just the age of the facility. Although the hotel is clean and continually maintained (painted, landscaping, vacuuming, etc), the walls and floors are a bit on the thin side, so if you are a light sleeper, you may hear your neighbors, next door and above. But, if you lodge a reasonable complaint with the staff, which unfortunately I had to do because of some very loud, inconsiderate guests, the Front Desk will comp the night for you...they will also make a point of providing an alternate room, should you wish to relocate. They want you to be happy. The Housekeeping Staff was also very accommodating. Having two dogs, I needed to take them out each morning to do their business. I was able to get Housekeeping to make up my room, approximately the same time each morning, while I was out with the dogs. That is customer service. As far as dogs, there is a policy that they are not be left unattended. Unfortunately, there were 2 ocassions where guests chose not to abide by the rules and left their dogs in the room alone....barking and barking and barking. Once the Front Desk was made aware of the problem, they immediately contacted the owners and told them to get back to the hotel as their pet(s) were disturbing the other guests. Breakfast is included and they provide a nice variety of items; hard boiled eggs, bagels, cream cheese, assortment of breads, waffles (you make them), fruit, coffee, tea and juices....always fresh and always replenished. A special shout out to Cornelius (GM) and Jessica (Supervisor).

author: 760natashas
title: Great staff! Rooms just ok.
text: Upon check-in we had to wait, even though we were an hour late. Friendly staff greeted us with a smile. Upon entering the room it stank of cigarette smoke. They didn't ask if we wanted a smoking room. They did tell us, however, that the hotel was fully booked. For this reason we did not request a room change. It was only for 2 nights. Breakfast was standard for La Quinta and the breakfast attendant, Minnie, was superb! She was absolutely caring and very helpful. She made sure that the breakfast was fully stocked even at the busiest of times. On our first night we noticed the floors had candy on them and under a bed was an empty beverage bottle. I guess housekeeping isn't as thorough as I would like. Check-out was smooth and easy. No major issues and good for the price. The rooms just need to be better maintained in my opinion.

author: NiharShah
title: Good hotel, courteous staff
text: I had stayed here from 20-Nov-2013 to 19-Dec-2013, that's a month. So I had this property as my home for a month. When I arrived, the room was well prepared. The staff had me checked-in in no time.The house-keeping staff was very courteous and did a sincere job in keeping the rooms and the premises clean. The front-desk staff was also helpful. The breakfast essentials could be little better managed especially during weekends when the rush was more. Nonetheless, there was no deficiency of materials. Coming to the most important part of the stay, the rooms. My room was well-spaced. I was staying solo so had 1 king size bed. The office table, the bath etc was well spaced. No issues at all. Although I would have liked that bed linen to be *changed* everyday, not just cleaned and arranged. The AC worked really fine, no problems whatsoever. (which I learned are very frequent in the competitive hotels). The manager and front-desk staff was well conversant with the processes of rewards and free nights and I also enjoyed some 2 free nights during my 1 month which was a welcome saving. Looking forward for some more savings (or perks) Mr. Manager ! ;) Overall - the experience of staying at this property was very good. I would recommend this property in the neighborhood.

author: my5sonburns
title: After reading all of the other reviews, I was surprised...
text: I wanted to start off and say that I am a frequent traveler. I usually stay at Hilton, Marriott and Priority Club properties. However, my company recently changed to a per-diem program that allows a set amount to be spent on hotels and we get to keep the amount that we save on the rooms. Add to the fact that this hotel was a couple of miles from where I was working and it was right across the street from a bar that I could drink at and walk back to the hotel, so I decided to give it a try. I read the reviews, and they didn't look promising, so I decided to drive by first. I walked into the lobby and it was very clean. There were no smells and a nice young lady greeted me immediately. I asked her for availability and she quoted me some prices. I told her that I saw them cheaper online and asked if she could give me a better rate. She apologized and said that I could use the lobby PC to book the room. I thought that was a great compromise. I realize the desk clerks don't have authority to change rates. I booked my room and within a few minutes I was checked in with keys and a very nice, clean comfortable room. I have to say, I was pleasantly surprised. Super Cheap rates for Tampa area. It was about the quality you would expect from a newer Holiday Inn Express. I enjoyed my stay and Cornelius (General Manager) greeted us every morning for our waffle, oatmeal and coffee breakfasts! Great property, I would definitely stay again.

author: Josie313
title: Horrible Experience
text: Upon arrive on October 8 at La Quinta Inn, the room reeked of mold and mildew and the trash was full of beer bottles, that had not been removed from the previous guest. Was taken to another room because we could not re-locate to another hotel, because we book our reservation through price-line.com, and not through La Quinta direectly. Second room also smelled of mildew not as badly as the first room but we had no other alternatives but to stay. The refrigerator was not working, we lost food and drinks because it was not getting cold. It was replaced by another refrigerator that did the opposite, it froze everything. Again we lost food and drinks. The light on the table would not work properly, it went on and off and it was finally replaced. The toilet wasn't flushing properly. Sometimes it would flush, sometimes not. Our last morning in the hotel we were getting ready to leave for the airport, had to take a shower in cold water! NO HOT WATER!! On October 16th, 1 day after returning home, Mr. Corneleius Mathis, General Manager from LaQuinta Inn and Suites in Tampa Bay Brandon West, called me, apologizing for the bad experience we had and offered to give us a refund for two days (out of the seven we were there) but stated we would have to contact priceline.com, explain everything to them that occured at the hotel and give them Mr. Mathis phone number and also tell them he was giving priceline the OK to refund us for two days. He said to tell priceline to contact him and he would speak with them, about everything.

author: patrickvS7020II
title: Budget Hotel
text: Fast check in. Staff were friendly and helpful. Hotel needs updating especially the elevator. My room was an executive. Room needed updating but was clean and comfortable. Bed was excellent. 2 HD TV's with NO HD channels. In room fridge and microwave. Didn't notice any noise from adjacent rooms. The price I paid was very reasonable. If I had paid any more I would have rated this hotel 2 star. Bob Evans is next to the hotel but is very busy. McDonald's is across the street. WiFi signal was very strong but the speed was terrible. Continental breakfast was very basic and the tiny breakfast room is always busy.

author: patrickvS7020II
title: Budget price gets you a very budget hotel.
text: Did not have the room I booked. I did get a King Executive room which had a large desk, sofa bed, microwave and fridge. On the 3rd floor at the very end of the building. Sofa had stains all over. Cigarette burn marks on the carpet. Windows open but had no screen to keep out the bugs. The wifi signal was strong but the speed was ancient. Was not able to use YouTube or Netflix. In the bathroom, the paint was peeling everywhere and the water pressure was terrible. This property is located on a very busy & noisy highway that connects to the interstate. OK some positives: bed was comfortable. 32" HD TV was great although the CW channel 6 never worked and the on-screen channel guide was never accurate and way too many sports channels. 3 channels of Showtime was nice. The staff I dealt with were friendly. Overall, I would not stay at this location again because of the room mix-up.

author: Mobile402813
title: Wonderful Staff
text: I have now stayed at this hotel twice and I have not had any significant problems with the location. On my first stay in Sep. there was an incident with a car alarm at 1 in the morning but the guy at the front desk was very willing to help and moved me to two different rooms so that I could get away from the noise. The second stay in Oct. was completely uneventful. The hotel is very close to I-75 which is a big bonus with my job. There can be some difficulty getting out of the hotel durring rush hour if you have to make a left onto Falkenburg Rd. and I did resort to turning right and then making a u-turn a few times just to get out. There are a lot of places to eat close by including a Bob Evans across the parking lot. It is also close to a lot of Tampa attractions. The rooms are clean. No stains on anything and no bed bugs. Everyone on the staff has been very friendly and helpful. The location is well lit outside which is important to me because I work late into the night and I always felt very secure returning to hotel. In the months to come while I'm working in Tampa I will continue to stay at this hotel and recommend it to anyone seeking a hotel in the area.

author: SometimesTravel
title: Too much $ for too little
text: Wow, where to start! Good thing first -- staff was friendly and our requests were met (i.e. shaver, area information, etc.). Now to bad -- room was very dirty. Bathroom had dozens of strands of hair along tub and a dirty mark in the toilet. And the fan wasn't working. Vanity area floor was so dirty that when I wiped up some water I spilled, the paper towel became black. The bed was fine until we had them change the linens on the third day and then it was only partially made when we returned and one of the pillows was missing it's case! Carpet had many little bits of debris on it (we had a baby with us, I was down there!) and it was obvious that they hadn't vacuumed under the bed in some time! There was a smear of something on one of the night tables and the fridge had some food debris in it. There was also a lot of dust and bits under the TV which had terrible reception, we couldn't even watch most of the channels. They do have free Wi-Fi but you can't print out your boarding passes as they don't offer that service. The breakfast was fine except the hot water had debris in it! The pool is outdoors and unheated, brr! Also, site proclaims you can walk to restaurants -- don't do it after dark. Hubby smokes and when he went out after dark he was panhandled and heard another patron reporting that he was accosted by a man who tried to open his car door in the parking lot on our last night there. Down the road to the right is the county prison!

author: famezzz
title: Super 4 star hotel - Had anything we needed!!!
text: Stayed for 4 days. It is located in a very convenient location. 2min walking from tram, bus stop, and 10min walking fro Wawel castle. Hotel has very modern design. Rooms/bathrooms are also very modern. We had a Standard room with a very nice view of the Castle. Cleanness was not perfect, but it was good enough , no complain. Hotel has Free wifi everywhere. Check-in and check-out were easy and fast. Requested for double bed and an early check in and they satisfied our request. Staff was very good and helpful. Breakfast was really good. Generally their restaurant was very good. We had a very nice staying. More than highly recommended!

author: udihc
title: Torn About The Review
text: I would have given a raving review of the hotel apart from a very embarassing incident we had. Rooms are lovely. Breakfast was excellent. Position of the hotel is also very good. The hotel staff was most friendly ( but the one incident), and so was the service. We were a group of 11 visitors attending the March of the Living. We are orthodox observing Jews and as such cannot operate the lift or use the electronic keys on our Sabbath. On Friday evening we approached he front desk and asked them if they would hold on to our room keys and when we return in the evening would operate the lift for us as well as open our room doors. All was done with a smile. The following morning we asked for the same assistance. They promised the same. When we returned to the hotel in the early afternoon, the desk was manned by one person only. He had no idea what we are asking of him. He called the manager in charge who told us that this is not a service they provide and will be extra service we will have to pay for (!!). All our explanations of the holy Sabbath would not be accepted. This was most embarrassing as well as annoying and went of for at least ten minutes. Finally, we asked one of the employees of the restaurant if he could help and he did it with a big supportive smile and no issue. I am ashamed even to write this but given the humiliation and lack of any willingness to understand and provide this simple assistance has brought me to do so. In all my travel I have never had such an experience.

author: dpprod02
title: If you want a cheap comfy hotel, this is the one for you!!
text: I chose this Hotel for one reason, that was the price!! I needed two rooms, Price for two rooms for two nights in the height of summer was £226. Which I thought was a great price!! If I hadn't of taken the children I would have definitely stayed in the old town. The Old town is great!!, loads of restaurants and bars, plus plenty going on - at all times. The walk to the old town from the hotel is about 20-25 mins. The Hotel itself. Check in was quite slow, Plus didn't even inform us where our rooms were, it wasn't difficult to work out for ourselves. Room was a nice size, bed was lovely and comfy. Room was very clean. Shower room was very modern and clean, plus dove shower gel was provided.. Very nice I thought. Shocked that the power of the shower was terrible, considering it was newly fitted. The view was terrible. The bar staff were great, prices for drinks were a bit pricey considering we are in Poland,, Don't Know what it is in Poland every time we bought a latte coffee we always got cold milk, one good advice learn how to say hot milk in Polish!!!!! Krakow is a fantastic city we absolutely loved it!!!!, we will deff be going back. I won't come back to this Hotel, only due to the location and that's the only reason. Thank you Park Inn for a comfy stay Mr & Mrs P

author: GlobeTrekker98
title: Perfect
text: This was the first time I have been to Krakow and the first time staying at a Park Inn. I would usual stay with Radisson Blu, but I wanted to see if this property had the same standard for a lower price...It does. This hotel really lived up to expectoration. I found the stay were so lovely and so accommodating. The restaurant has a good menu selection and the food is so good. I do not usually eat in hotels as I like to experience a cities lifestyle scene but the restaurant was very appealing. The breakfast has a large variation on offer as taste as good as it is presented. The rooms are large and very comfortable. I would not call them basic as they still had all the appropriate amenities, which were restocked daily. I especially liked the bathroom as it was light, modern and to a high standard, but most importantly it is very clean. The whole hotel in fact is kept to a high standard. The hotel is not a far walk to the main square and is perfectly located for bus, tram and taxi network. The hotel is just across the river from the castle in which you can see from certain floors. Overall very impressed. Although cheaper than its sister brand Radisson, you would not notice as the standard is still very high. Thank you Park Inn Krakow, I hope to return to you in the future.

author: roctourer
title: A Very Pleasant Surprise -- Super Experience
text: Chose Park Inn without too much analysis and it turned out to be a very good decision! It is a very modern hotel situated on the Vistula, close to Wawel Castle. You can get rooms with gorgeous views of the castle -- ask for one! The amenities are excellent. Our room for three was HUGE and had three regular beds and very nice furnishings. Modern, chic bathroom. Our price included breakfast, which is superb -- amazing choices are laid out and you can even have omelettes made to order. And get real espresso! The place is set back a bit from the road and is hence very quiet. We did not drive and so I have no idea about the parking. The staff is very, very good. Very friendly, helpful and efficient. (While I waited my turn, one of them helped out a guest who did not seem to have any idea of a SIM card. The person at the desk installed the card and made sure that phone was on the network.) They also arranged for out taxi to go to Auschwitz -- the rates and service were clearly explained and it all worked out perfectly. The bus stop is just right across the road to get to the Market Square, but one can walk there if one has the time. Same with the Wawel Castle. But, I would suggest taking the bus as part to the walk involves going through a somewhat beaten up and dreary neighbourhood. All in all an excellent hotel and if you are not dying to be on the Market Square, this one offers great comfort and a very reasonable price. Yes, there is nothing do outside other the amble on the riverbank, but everything is just a 10 min bus ride away.

author: catsforkids
title: Lovely stay
text: I stayed at the Park Inn Krakow for 3 nights and enjoyed my stay. The hotel is well situated on the #18 Tram line to Old Town and is an easy 30 minute walk to the Town Square passing the lovely Wawel Castle and crossing the Vistula River on the way. The staff are helpful and friendly. The room is roomy enough, clean and the windows do an excellent job at keeping the street noise out (I was on the 2nd floor facing a 4 lane highway and never had a noise issue). There is no real "view" from the hotel. The bathroom has a shower only, with limited counter space and soap/shampoo dispensers only. The bed was very comfortable and the air conditioning worked well. Good lighting and 2 outlets on the desk. There is a hot water kettle with instant coffee/teas and a mini-refrigerator. There is a safe and the Wifi works very well and is fast and secured with a log-in provided. It is a non-smoking facility so the room was fresh. I did not use the bar or restaurant, for meals other than breakfast, as the hotel is so close to many good restaurants in Old Town. The breakfast buffet had a good variety of foods hot and cold, fresh real juices and the eating area was bright and very clean. Great pastries! I would definitely stay here again in the future.

author: Sliver2907
title: 10 out of 10
text: I am a flight attendant and travel quite a lot. Sometimes I find a hotel that I think meets my expectations and this hotel does. The front end staff were friendly and helpful. The hotel is very clean and has that just built smell. It is located in walking distance to the old city, and as a matter of fact you can easily see the old city from the hotel, so no need to worry about getting lost, it is right there. It is also across from the the trams, so transportation is easy. If you arrive in the main train station by chance, you can take tram number 52 to the hotel, going in the direction of the old city. A cab cost me about $6 from the train station, since I didn't know which tram to take at the time. The travel time from the train station is about 10 minutes on the tram. The old city can be walked in about 10 minutes. The hotel was well decorated, had a small refrigerator and a tea/coffee pot with lots of tea, coffee and condiments. The hotel has a breakfast buffet, for about $16 USD, which I didn't use. I could not comment on the food. The main train station has a large mall attached to it, so I was able to buy some groceries, keep them in the hotel refrigerator and then just eat breakfast in my room. My only suggestion, if you are going to the salt mines, do NOT use public transportation. Get a tour, only for the fact that finding the bus stop for the salt mines is so difficult, even with directions. The stop on the route is not really marked and we wound up having to double back on another bus after we passed the correct stop. This is one hotel that you should not hesitate to book,

author: VoyageVogage123
title: Blown away by beautiful Krakow
text: We flew to Krakow with easyjetholidays at the end of October for 2 nights and were pleased with our choice of hotel: - It is in a good location next to the Congress Centre and within a stone's throw from the impressive Wawel Castle, which we could see from our room. If you walk on from the Wawel Castle complex, you get to the beautiful Market Square in about 10 minutes, enjoying the cobbled streets, cafes and shops along the way. - The breakfast offering was really good - nice to have soft boiled eggs as a change from scrambled and plenty of hot and cold offerings, range of breads, cereals and tea, plus coffee and juices. We enjoyed sitting by the window watching everyone busily going about their business in Monte Cassino, with the tram stop across the way. - The room was standard but had everything in it, including a hair dryer. The free in-room safe was an added bonus and there was bottled water in the fridge on arrival. There was no separate shampoo and soap, but just an all-purpose dispenser, which wouldn't suit everyone. - It only took 20 minutes to get to the hotel from the airport, and I had prebooked a transfer rather than using public transport to save time as there is a lot of building work going on at the moment (I think they are doing a new train link to the airport and they are also building a new runway). Weather wise, it was cold - you need your winter coats, gloves and scarf. There was also fog which was around in the morning, before lifting and descending again in the late afternoon. Apparently, this is quite common October time and didn't prevent us from getting out and about. It did mean though that we did not venture out in the evening and ate instead in the hotel's restaurant. We tried local Polish dishes on the first evening, but the dumplings were an acquired taste (!), so we opted for spaghetti carbonara on the second evening. Local beer was reasonably priced at around £2.50 for half a litre. Krakow is one of the most beautiful European cities we have visited and there is plenty to see as well as a great atmosphere. You can do hop-on hop-off buses or go on city tours in mini multiple-seat transporters or do what we did, which is to get a map and walk everywhere. We did the main square area (from where guides wait to take you on a guided free tour), then walked out through the park area to the big upmarket indoor shopping centre before coming back to the main square via the old city walls and Florian's Gate and going for a horse and carriage ride (about £24 for 30 minutes for up to 4 people). We did walk to the Kamierz old Jewish district, but found it was grittier. Apparently, it has a good vibe in the evenings though. All in all we enjoyed our city break and would recommend Krakow, as well as the hotel.

author: 415shubhams
title: Excellent place to stay in Krakow
text: Travelling to Krakow (Poland) from India was a long and tiring journey but, a very warm welcome by the hotel staff and a basket full of fruits and a welcome note was a pleasant surprise. The room had a beautiful view of the Wawel Castle just across the river. Thee room was comfortable, clean, soothing, even though I would have loved to watch an English channel other than BBC World ;), but, the internet connection was good enough to make you not switch on the TV. I would like to appreciate the front desk staff as they were super co-operative and every time patiently tried to answer my wide spectrum of questions ranging from places to visit, things to buy, train station, tram stations, tours, maps, and what not. And they always helped with some good information and always kept that wide beautiful smiles. :) .. Thank You so much for that, it was really helpful. Getting a taxi is something they help very quickly. Travelling to the main square is a 15 mins walk or 5 mins tram ride from hotel. So, good in terms of connectivity to other areas. Morning breakfast was good, but monotonous each day. This is one thing that needs innovation i guess. Being Indian and finding a dish named "Madras Vegetable" in the menu was a pleasant surprise. After tiring day at work, it was always good to see some surprises waiting for you in the room. For instance, the first day a basket of fruits, on the Friday evening cake and cookies, on the day just before leaving some more cookies with apple were waiting with the thank you note. It was really good. Overall a nice experience, Krakow is a place worth visiting, and I would recommend Park Inn to stay in Krakow.

author: ReneD460
title: Clean and friendly
text: I have stayed at the Park Inn by Radisson in Krakow on a number of business trips this year and it serves me perfectly well. The rooms are clean and the wifi is free. A lot of hotels in Krakow offer free wifi but the connection is not great. However, there are no problems here. The bathroom is modern with a walk in shower - no bath. The rooms are decorated to a modern standard with bright colours and pine desks and wardrobes. Some of the rooms do not have a wardrobe but they do have hanging rails. The rooms have twin beds which is common in Central Europe. The breakfast is really great and caters for everyone's tastes: fruit, yogurt, a selection of meats, cheese, amazing breads, sausages, eggs, cereal, pastries, coffee and juice. It is really worth it just for the breakfast. I keep going back because it is a reliable, no frills hotel in a good location half way between downtown and my place of business. It takes around twenty to thirty minutes from the airport, depending on traffic. All rooms have hair dryers, which is a must for me. And if you need an iron and ironing board they will send one up to your room. Taxis are usually available outside the large, modern lobby but, if not, reception will happily call one for you. There is a restaurant and bar next to the lobby but I have not eaten there except for one late night snack which the kitchen staff rustled up for me. Each room also has a mini bar with a range of snacks and drinks. I've never had a bad room here and never heard any noises outside my room at night. Can't complain!

author: MJSellers
title: Friendly and efficient staff. .
text: Spent three nights at the Park Inn Krakow as part of a pre-cruise extension with Grand Circle River Cruises. This is a fairly new hotel with moderate sized rooms, modern in decor, rather basic rooms but comfortable and very clean. The hotel has a small lobby connected to a bar and dining room where breakfast, lunch and dinner are served. The included breakfast buffet had a full range of good quality choices. Hotel staff was friendly and helpful. The hotel is located on a main road and has no nearby stores or restaurants. However, directly in front of the hotel is a tram station with a tram taking you to the Old Town in about 10 minutes. Some young family members walked to the Old Town in 20 minutes. The Old Town was not destroyed in WW II as was Warsaw's and for me, it rivals Prague's Old Town. There are a number of large squares each having numerous bars and restaurants surrounded by historic sites and old churches. .There are many streets leading from the main squares which also have restaurants and shops. Behind the Church of St. Barbara, we found a large outdoor barbecue grill serving grilled sausages, breads, etc. at good prices. And of course, also beer. We enjoyed our stay at the Park Inn and Krakow which offers so much to see.

author: dusgruntledg
title: Park Inn by Radisson Krakow: a dishonest experience
text: We were engaged by an agency of the Polish government seeking to execute a multi year project, which brought me to Krakow and the Park Inn. Arriving at the hotel which was only accessible via an unpaved gravel road,I was promised at the front desk that I would collect their loyalty program points for my stay and "yes" there would be no problem extending my stay if necessary. My first interaction following the front desk was with housekeeping where I had to INSIST on a piece of soap which turned out to be a 1" square soap. Period. The housekeeper seemed as if that piece of soap was coming out of her own pocket. A couple of days later when I did try to extend my stay I was notified that only the hotel manager Micheael or Michel, had the authority to do so and I was told that he'd be in by 8:30am the following morning. I delayed my day to be at the front desk by 8:30am, only to be told he'd be coming in at 9:30am. At 9:30am I was told he was busy having breakfast in the hotel restaurant and couldn't be disturbed. An hour later I was told he couldn't be disturbed again, because he was in a meeting with the general manager. The following day I found him based on his physical description as indicated by others at the hotel. He never introduced himself, never presented a business card and only grunted when I repeatedly asked whether he was the hotel manager. When I asked for a stay extension he offered me a rate almost triple what I was already paying, suggesting 140 euros per night and that he was giving me a big discount. The price of online computer access at this hotel: first I was told 5 euros + tax per minute then the manager said 2.99 euros + tax per minute, assuring me I wouldn't find "a single" place in Krakow to offer computer access for less. He was correct, I didn't fine ONE place; I found TWO places which offered free online access plus free printing, right there in Krakow. And when I contacted Radisson about my missing loyalty points, I was presented with a series of "sorries" that NO they wouldn't be issuing me the promised loyalty points and that on my next trip I had other options of where to stay other than Radisson. I am amazed at how easily this hotel organization dismisses what would have been hundreds and hundreds of annual room nights in Krakow for our staff of accounting, architectural and engineering professionals and their own staffs. I'd love to know which business school the director of marketing for Radisson, attended.

author: Marie_LH2013
title: Two night stay - not as high standard expected
text: We stayed in the Park Inn for two nights of our trip to Krakow. The location is a taxi journey out of the city - the reception advised us that we could walk but did not offer any directions. They were helpful in booking a taxi for us. On arrival (at 23.30) we asked where was best to visit in the city (as in what area of the city should we ask the taxi to bring us to) for some late night food and a drink - the receptionist was quite rude and just gave us a strange look and did not answer our question insisting that if we wanted food or drink their bar was open and refused to give us any other information. We were informed that if we wished to have breakfast we could pay an extra 50pln (€12.50); we politely declined this offer. However, on our last day there we had a tour booked which was picking us up from the hotel at 10am. We were down stairs at 9.45am and asked if we could purchase some bread (or a croissant) from the restaurant explaining that we did not have time for the full breakfast but wished to take something light with us. The staff refused to accommodate our request stating that our only option was to purchase the full breakfast and sit in the hotel and eat it. We once again highlighted that we did not have time for this and we were only looking something light asking if we could purchase some fruit - once again this suggestion was declined. We then asked for directions to the nearest shop and we were told that there were no shops in the surrounding area. Not very accommodating. The hotel itself was nice - clean and modern. The rooms were tastefully decorated. Basic necessities such as tissues, shower caps etc were not provided however. The hotel boasts WiFi however only one device can avail of the WiFi at a time and actually connecting to it was very troublesome. One great thing we noted was that the hotel were involved in an energy efficiency scheme which aimed to save water and reduce carbon footprint. Overall the hotel itself was quite nice and comfortable. However, generally speaking the hotel staff let the hotel down and made us question its worthiness of a four star rating

author: Loves2Research
title: Modern hotel in Krakow
text: We stayed at the Park Inn for three nights, travelling with a group. Check-in was quick and the room was adequate. There were no closets, just hooks on the wall across from the bed and there was only one towel in the bathroom. Very disappointed with the cheap liquid soap and shampoo in dispensers in the shower and glad we provided our own soap and shampoo. We had to open the window for fresh air and it was very noisy as there is large construction project taking place next door and the train runs across the street. The bar is a couple of tables in the dining area and not adequate nor welcoming. It is also in the middle of the lobby which is very noisy. The business center is around the corner from check-in, in the hallway outside the handicapped bathroom and you must use your credit card and pay for access. Breakfast was okay, not many choices of healthy items but managed to find a cup of yogurt each morning. The fruit was hard as nails. The biggest drawback of this hotel is the location. It is on the "other side of the river" from downtown Krakow. This is not within walking distance unless you are a "long distance" walker. We utilized taxi cabs for transportation to and from the main square. This hotel had multiple tour groups constantly coming in and leaving which turned the lobby into much noise and mass confusion and long lines at the two elevators. I would not return to this hotel for the many reasons listed but mostly for the location. There were many beautiful hotels in the center of Krakow in the heart of the city that I would stay at for a future return visit to this beautiful and historic city.

author: UncleDom
title: Acceptable choice - not quite 4 star
text: First time in a Park Inn and somewhat underwhelmed. The first impressions are good, the lobby is modern with clean lines and a very busy vibe. Checkin was efficient and allocated room on the 5th floor facing the road. Thankfully with the windows closed there was no noise from the trams or traffic but it is a very busy junction so take care when crossing the road into the town. Room itself was modern, clean and well kept. IKEA comes to mind when trying to describe the furniture style.The wardrobe was small and you had to hang your clothes facing as opposed to on a rail. The bed was firm, clean and comfortable. Bathroom was a tad small, unforgiving light over the mirror and no tub, only a wet shower with limited space. The towels were not very soft. Kettle for tea and coffee and fridge under the desk space for water and juices. Breakfast was included in the rate and was average buffet style. It is a very busy large breakfast room. Cooked items were so so as were the pastries and bread. Good choice of apples and bananas to take away The juice was not of a good quality. If you only wanted something light you would be happy with the breakfast. The location is fine but the walking time to the town square may bite into your vacation/tour. There is a lot to see and do in Krakow so use your time wisely

author: Parren75
title: Fabulous New Hotel
text: We really enjoyed our stay here. The hotel is brand new and looks great. Its really, really clean & comfortable. The staff were first class and we felt well looked after. They worked hard to make sure that we had a good holiday. The location was good, lots of options for transportation near by. We enjoyed the breakfasts each morning. Apart from full English and the usual cereals, bread, pastries, meat, cheese, yogurt, etc. you can also have fried eggs, omlettes or waffles made to order. I can personally recommend the waffles! We also ate lunch here and it was very good and fairly priced...so was the beer. The rooms are modern and have everything that you could want with air conditioning to boot which is really needed in Krakow during the summer. I don't normally have very good experiences with companies that offer a world class customer service to its customer's these days, but the staff at the Park Inn really made an impression that will stay with me for a long time. Nothing was too much for them and this hotel deserves a great recommendation. We would stay here again in a heart beat. This is the only place that has truly impressed me for a very long time.

author: nmaidwell123
title: Excellent hotel
text: From walking through the door to leaving every thing about this hotel was excellent. The warm welcome checking in set the scene for a great stay. Our room was massive and immaculate. The bed was huge and the bathroom was gorgeous. Air con was very good and the balcony view was great. Plenty of storage for clothes in a well equipped room. The pools were very well maintained and plenty of sun beds. The upper floor heated swimming pool had great views of the sea and massive sun beds. The main pool was large and the pool staff were 1st class. The bar staff could not do enough for you. Breakfast was brilliant and had a huge range of foods available. The egg chef was lovely and so friendly. All the food was delicious throughout our stay. The beach was a just outside the gates. Wonderful stay & gorgeous setting.

author: ianwalker555
title: Is it really 5 star
text: Just back from two weeks at this hotel. Is it 5 star? I don’t think so. The hotel is well situated literally a stones throw from the beach. Estepona old town and Puerto de le Duquesa only short taxi rides away €10-12. Reception staff top notch as are most of the team but there are some seriously miserable people waiting on in the buffet restaurant. A smile and cheery face costs nothing. Not so the lady who seemed to run the buffet restaurant, she was brilliant. Hotel very well presented indeed we liked it enough to think about going back later this year. We had a junior suite our friends a premium double both with sea views, disappointedly if you sat on the balcony you could not see the sea because of the high wall which formed part of the balcony. Our biggest disappointment was the food in particular the grill. Certainly no complaint about quantity but different meats and fish piled high either side of grill is hardly appetising. Some entrecôtes if not most were mostly fat and very small. Salad bar and cold meat and fish offerings were absolutely excellent. Another thing we found annoying was the volume of people smoking in the restaurant. You could not get away from it. Yes of course you want to eat outside in the buffet restaurant but why not have smoking and non smoking areas. Would I recommend the hotel, yes I would in the hope the team will now smile more. Would I single out anyone for special praise, yes indeed, don’t know her name but she was working in the pool bar on Sunday afternoon, what an asset to the hotel. So many thing are good at this hotel but with just a little few tweaks it would be at another level.

author: Freebird_71
title: Excellent family choice in Estepona
text: We definitely made a good family choice here! We spent around 10 nights here this months, and the overall feeling was very good. The room is big, comfortable, good beds, clean, nice modern bathroom and non-slippery shower. LG Tv allows easy USB connection. The restaurant/buffet is really good! You have almost anything you can imagine, with good quality food and cooks preparing stuff for you on the go, in front of you. Kids enjoyed the mini club, in fact the animation team was great and really devoted to kids' happiness (thanks to Manuel, Cristina, Paloma). The swimming pool is really big and sunny, great relaxing area with a family atmosphere (young groups looking for perpetual happy hour and teen excitement, this is not your place). I would remark some negative aspects too: - the beach in front of the hotel is just a few seconds away but it's not a superb sandy beach, it's kinda rocky. However, free sunbeds and really wild, not a lot of people really. - not easy to find a spot to park. Luckily, front desk guys will park your car and give you the keys back as soon as you need the car. - the hotel management should find a system to manage the pool sunbeds. As a guest, you can't just leave your towel first time in the morning and pretend to be back in the afternoon, preventing other guests to use that particular sunbed for almost 90% of the sunny hours. When I found myself in the situation where I did find no available beds (around 11.00 am, yes a little late), pool guys told me that due to recent incidents they were not allowed to remove guests' towels from the beds. I just did it myself, took the risk and nobody came to claim the beds. Anyway, I know it's tough to control, so I just leave that as a suggestion. It's not that difficult to find a sunbed, don't get me wrong. Anyway, an overall very good experience, I do recommend it, you will not be disappointed.

author: rpproperties1
title: Awesome hotel
text: My family and I were visiting Spain for the first time and had decided we wanted to stay in Mallorca. However upon contacting a travel agent in Spain he said he highly suggested we avoid Mallorca in July because it would be extremely busy. He suggested this hotel as he and his family had stayed at it last year. He nailed it. We ended up getting a suite on the fifth floor I believe the room number was 515 and it was awesome! The breakfast which was included was very good for European standards. It was very large. However they are missing American bacon and sausage. Otherwise the breakfast was awesome! We also got massages and we’re pleased and paid for the family spa/ indoor pool service and relaxation area, which we all really enjoyed. It was very relaxing. Our weeklong stay exceeded our expectations. One nice thing about staying here is if you take an hour ride south you can jump off for a day trip in Morocco which is what we did and thoroughly enjoyed that. One negative I will say about where this is located is that the beach is very rocky and it is difficult to walk in the water because of the rocks. But there’s so many positives about this area that the rocky beach was a small thing. I would highly suggest this city and this hotel!

author: frappe-uk
title: 3 star hotel charging 5 star prices
text: One may think that if you pay over £250 per night and than some extra to upgrade to a balcony room , you will get a decent level of service, facilities and food. We paid to upgrade to a Junior suite specifically to have balcony with sun lounger. The room 614 was on top floor which also happens to be the same floor on which they keep huge ventilating and air conditioning units. The room was so noisy we couldn't sleep, with a closed balcony doors the noise lever was still comparable to a hairdryer. Balcony itself was unusable unless you like to hear rambling sound 24/7 versus the sea waives. In the morning we asked to change the room, they had nothing available in the whole resort apparently, reception staff was not considerate or apologetic around the noise, they just said some guest don't mind it. We did and after wasting an hour and a lot of nerves they found somewhat quieter room on middle floor, room 402, but we had to wait until the evening to move into it. Not exactly 5 star service. Room 402 was the same type, room was big, bathroom too but shower and bathtub old with mold present. The balcony was small and had tiny squeezed 2 lounger chairs which I specifically wanted but it was in the shadow for 100% of time. So couldn't use it, we paid for the upgrade and got nothing from it. I would not bother with doing so, as we chatted with a couple in nearby room 401, which had massive terrace, it's the same type room and they were upgraded for free as apparently hotel was quiet at the time. Overall tips: Room and bathrooms are big but not particularly clean Food is expensive and a low standard They service bottle of wine for £16, same you can get across the road in Aldi for £2 Swimming pools are ok, again could be cleaner Lounging chairs are cheap, plastic and half of them were broken on chipped. Very tacky. Beach is horrible, the lounging chairs are chained to the umbrellas and so dirty my tower chained from beige into brown, horrible! Mini bar in the room is very expensive and they don't even offer complimentary water. Overall for the price we felt mugged. Photos on the website have nothing to do with how this place actually looks and operates. Avoid!

author: Ramalamadancer
title: Not 5 stars!
text: The front reception staff were exceptionally helpful. Our room was big and clean. I had requested 2 twin beds and that is what we got. Our room overlooked the garden which had a loud live performance until 11:30 each evening. It was so loud, we could clearly hear it in our room. When I called to ask about it there was no offer to change rooms even though I asked. The pool, although big, had mold growing on the sides and tiles that were coming up around the edges. There were activities at the pool throughout the day. There was only one choice of a la carte restaurant during our stay. The staff there were not very friendly or helpful. Additionally the restaurant was run down with tiles missing and railings in terrible condition. The food was good but overpriced. There was a buffet as well which cost 30 euros for adults, 15 for children for lunch, 40/20 for diner. Again the food was Ok but nothing that tasted amazing. The restaurant manager was friendly and let my daughter eat free one evening as I think he realized what a rip off it was for us. The spa was able to fit us in for pedicures one day of our stay. The treatment was good and staff there were helpful but again it was rundown with paint peeling and mirrors not cleaned. Overall the hotel was ok but not worth the money and definitely not 5 stars.

author: Maryj51
title: Isolated without a car.
text: We upgraded to a junior suite with a sea view, which was worth it as we had plenty of space and could hear the sea even in bed! Some maintenance issues particularly in the bathroom. I hope my photos work as they illustrate these. The piano bar showed no sign of opening and this was July. The restaurants rotated their opening. We ate there a couple of times and the food was OK but uninspiring and expensive. The evening entertainment was awful. We gave up on the juggler as he kept dropping things and the dancers were amateurish. We travelled into the town by taxi as it was impossible to walk. There was no path to go anywhere apart from the immediate vicinity of the hotel. On two occasions there was a long wait for a taxi and on one of these, several people gave up queuing, including ourselves. Don’t stay here without a car. We had an issue with a noisy group of women who stayed next door to us for two nights. They were playing loud music with a bass ( clubbing music) on the balcony and at 3:30 in the morning. The receptionist with whom we dealt came up to listen, sniggered and said they were having a good time. When I said that we weren’t, he reluctantly asked them to turn it down. His attitude was not good and we watched the General Manager take him to task over discarded bottles so it wasn’t just us! Lovely adults only pool and the gardens are a real joy.

author: 888paml
title: A last minute three generation break...
text: Our son, wife and three of our grandchildren have recently moved to Gibraltar and as the weather was wet for the weekend we made a last minute booking to this delightful hotel. There were 9 of us...six adults and three children - ages from 70 down to 4. We were accommodated in 3 large sea view rooms and each of us had a child in with us in good sturdy put-u-ups (children were free). Two of the rooms were interconnecting allowing for the children to be in one while we chatted, read in the other. The rooms and large bathrooms were very spacious, although with glass doors in the bathrooms it was a slight worry with the children...I have to say that Granny managed to walk into one of the doors and was fine! There were bathrobes, slippers and very good sized bottles of shower gel, etc. + toothbrush sets and a comb and there was the usual minibar, hairdryer, safe and everything was immaculate. The first night we ate downstairs and had the buffet which was excellent - plenty of choices of each course - the kids and adults all found plenty to tempt them! Children especially liked the ice cream cart to assemble their own cones! We then went up to the bar/reception area where there was some light entertainment from a chap singing ‘rat pack’ type songs for his first set followed by an Elvis tribute once he’d changed into a black leather ensemble! The kids danced as did several adults...very enjoyable evening. Night two...we ate in the bar - we felt like a more laid back earlyish meal with the kids. Still excellent and the staff were attentive and efficient. Breakfast was included in the room rate...another superb buffet with everything one could possibly think of to eat...omelettes and fried eggs made to order... I would highly recommend this hotel for a weekend break. The family utilised the indoor pool (towels provided) and when not raining we managed a walk along the beach accessible through the gardens. Have no idea what it would be like in the height of the summer though. Would hope to repeat the experience again at some stage when visiting Gibraltar.

author: I1285AZjanicem
title: Friends get together
text: Had such fantastic time . Staff are fantastic. So helpful. So friendly. They always make u feel so welcome . Hotel big boss . So welcome chat to u. Ask if everything ok . Food is so delicious. Rooms so clean and tidy. They have lovely spa. Which I enjoy. So relaxed., this my fourth visit. Enjoy each visit. So much to in Estepona.

author: Maudepam
title: Lack of customer service
text: Hotel room was clean and comfortable with a sea view. The pool area was pleasant and again spotlessly clean with access to the beach. However, it most certainly does not warrant five star status. We have stayed at many 5 star hotels in Spain and this hotel is inferior in many respects. We stayed on a B&B basis and the breakfast lacked variety. The coffee was undrinkable, bread and pastries were of poor quality and the service was inconsistent. Now to the main point of my review. On day 5 of our weeks stay we requested late checkout as our taxi transfer was not due until 5pm. We were told that the whole hotel was being taken over, we had to checkout at 12 and that from 1pm they could not keep our luggage in the luggage room, no hospitality room was available and that we could not have lunch in the hotel or even get a drink after that time! At this point we were dumbfounded. The staff were adamant and didn’t recognise the difficulties that this would cause us. Their whole attitude intimated that they didn’t care. I am a wheelchair user and my husband and I were quite upset. Our travel company also contacted the Hotel who remained unreasonable. Their only concession was to agree to keep our luggage until 3pm. Rather than ruin the last 36 hours of our holiday we checked out of the hotel and booked another hotel for our last night. I can highly recommend the Kempinski, truely a 5 star establishment who couldn’t do enough for us.

author: Timbob23
title: Five star halo slipping...
text: Wife and I have just come back from a weeks stay at the Elba hotel in Estepona. We stayed here last year too as we liked it so much first time around. Unfortunately I have to say that sadly standards there have slipped a bit since the last time we visited last year. The rooms are beginning to look a bit tired and our particular one was in need of a spruce up, new wallpaper and paint definitely required at the very minimum. There were mosquito "splats" over all the walls and ceiling and when I looked at the wall above the desk area it was covered in dust! (I took a photo it was so bad). The sink in the bathroom had a hairline crack that had discoloured (not really 5 star is it?). Worst of all was our bed sheet had a hole in it and wasn't changed for FIVE DAYS! In the end my wife went to reception and complained about the hole in the sheet and the fact our bedding had not been changed for so long. The receptionist was extremely apologetic and the sheet was changed the very same day. The balconies are also not very private either, which is a shame with just a small privacy glass panel (with large gaps) between you and the next door room... The pool and facilities are very good, we very much like the breakfast facilities (except in the overflow area) and access to the (limited) beach facilities is nice too. The gardens are superbly maintained (unlike the hotel rooms lol). The breakfast dining area was very busy during our stay and there is an (overflow) area at the far end for use when the main seating area is very busy, which was regularly. Unfortunately the 'overflow' area is poorly attended and equipped - there are not even enough salt and pepper pots for each table - so try to avoid sitting in this area if you can! Finally I have to mention the terrible smell of cooked fish that regularly prevails throughout the reception area and a lot of the hotel too, it really is bad and the hotel urgently need to review their food smell extraction systems from their kitchens to prevent this stench going forward. Will I stay here a third time? the answer for now is probably not as the 5-star rating is not currently deserved while there are so many issues with regards to shabby-looking room (deterioration) issues, poor housekeeping etc. When the management there pull their collective fingers out and re-decorate the rooms, sort housekeeping out and get rid of that awful cooked fish stink in the hotel I might reconsider, but until then it's a "no" from us.

author: finian29
title: Up market hotel
text: We recently enjoyed a week's holiday at this hotel. . WE thought our deluxe room was outstanding with a comfortable bed and a huge bathroom.. Great sea vistas from the terrace but a word to management it would have been nice to have had sun beds instead of chairs on this large terrace! Food. The buffet food was arguably the best we have eaten in any of the large hotels we have stayed in. Congrats to chef Victor and his team. We rarely see Turbot or entrecote steaks cooked to order each night in any hotel. We did use the a la carte restaurants and found both the service and cooking top class. Abraham looked after us there in an admirable way. One slight complaint though, Management should rethink the snack menu to put some tapas on it. It is Spain you know. Room service was not up to 5 star service as on many occasions our tea and milk sachets were not always topped up. Visitors to the hotel should remember that it is a taxi ride into town. The pool area is lovely as are the gardens although some of the beds are showing some wear and tear. We loved the indoor pool area with superior beds. We did enjoy the Spa, very relaxing. All in all a very enjoyable holiday.

author: strolling8
title: Just be sure this will suit your needs
text: Estapona is a really lovely place for a holiday. However, to keep it authentic all the large hotels such as this one are located a distance out of the town itself and there are no suitable footpaths even if you did want to walk. As a result unless you are patient with bus timetables you are going to have to budget for taxis which are excellent and will cost between €8 and €11 each way dependent upon time and destination (port is nearer and it's a nice 15 minute walk along the front into the old town). Taxi to Puerto Banus cost €33 each way - again a bus is possible from the town. Apart from a few meters at the front of the hotel there really isn't anywhere to stretch your legs around this hotel. The hotel itself is good. Our larger sea view room was excellent with its own patio and sea view. Breakfast buffet was fine and all the staff were friendly. It is expensive. A beer and glass of cava is €5 in town. It was €8 here. We took the advice of other reviewers and on day 1 visited the supermarket over the road for water at 16 cents a bottle. This hotel will suit if you like to spend your days by the pool and you don't mind being restricted to food choices at a hotel. It is a nice hotel and kept really nicely but it's location won't suit everyone. On reflection we don't so we would have been better placed booking one of the smaller hotels in the town. No real facilities but as we don't use them that's not a problem! The old town is a great place just to wander around and we enjoyed the walk around Puerto Banus looking at the very flash cars, even flasher boats and window shopping.

author: jowanm2016
title: Great rooms
text: Well let me start by saying that the staff are brilliant, can't do enough and very helpful especially Pablo the man in charge of the adult and teen day entertainment, he's very considerate and helpful. All staff work really hard even though not all speak the best of English. Would rate this as 4 star at the most. What disappointed us was the fact that the pool is not lifeguarded most of the time and therefore we had to keep an eye on our 10 year old. All other hotels we've stayed at before had great constant lifeguards so we didn't have to watch the kids like a hawk. Also this hotel does not allow any kind of floats or lilos in the pool so our kids couldn't play and partly spoiled our holiday and these two are the main reasons why we wouldn't return (as well as food below). Also bit annoying as all bins only one side of the pool so had to keep walking all the way around and if we left our cups on the loungers they'd be blown away and nobody removed them form the area. Location is not bad as 7 minutes from Estepona Old Town and about 10 Euros one way. Aldi near by which is handy too. Rooms are lovely and large and comfortable and we had wonderful sea view. Although the walls are very thin and you can hear neighbours and anyone in the corridors. Breakfast not the best and we are glad that we didn't book half or full board as the buffets choice is limited and pretty similar every day. Lunch a la carte is very limited small menu (although the price is reasonable for a hotel). Internet free however works best in the room and reception and not really that well by the pool. Wouldn't recommend this hotel for kids over 9 years old.

author: Dwrox1664
title: Relaxing holiday
text: We had a lovely week at the hotel. It's spotlessly clean everywhere, but it's not a 5* hotel. It's a big building with an unusual layout and they have people on different meal plans and deals, so we spent the first couple of days a little confused about where we were and what we were doing. The room was good, not particularly luxurious for 5*, but clean and comfortable. The bathroom was fabulous and ceiling fan great. The third bed was a proper bed but didn't have a duvet like the others. It was a room for 3 people but only had 2 cups, bathrobes, chairs on balcony etc. The food everywhere was excellent. A large variety and we appreciated the quieter adults breakfast and specialist restaurants. Both swimming pools are great, but a little chilly and you can get clean towels daily. The adults sunbathing area was fabulous. All the staff were lovely but this is where the hotel really doesn't live up to its 5 stars. There just aren't enough of them. We often had to wait quite a while to be served in lobby bar and reception and trying to place an order for food at adults breakfast took some time. The hotel is out of the way with nothing around it and the beach is not very nice. The hotel really doesn't deserve 5 stars but we had a lovely, relaxing holiday and enjoyed ourselves

author: CarolK309
title: Extremely disappointing
text: I brought my parents for their anniversary. Made my reservation on booking. Upon arrival I was requested to pay the whole stay. Never seen this in a so called 5 star hotel... We were given rooms at the pool level (-2) with limited sea view. Decent size but outdated. Beware of mosquitos...zillions of them dead on the walls. Zillions flying in the rooms. Called housekeeping. The lady was very friendly and did her best but the overall impression of the rooms is a general lack of maintenance. This is definitely not a 5 star and is very disappointing. Bar service is nice but the setting is appalling. A motel bar. Buffet breakfast is average. The restaurants 'a la carte' are fine but somewhat expensive for the food quality. Sun beds are old, uncomfortable and dirty. The only good sides of this hotel are (in the right order) its beachfront location and its overall friendly staff. You will however need a car for the nearest restaurant. Next time we will choose a real 5 star hotel.

author: JonHerd
title: Good, but read the fine print!
text: Good points - Rooms very spacious and clean (if a few signs of wear). No outside noise. Breakfast included and plentiful. Hotel Amenities are all very good, pool not too busy, quiet if a little small. Service pretty good. Drinks expensive as standard! But this is advertised as a 5 star. Its not, its a 4. Dont eat the buffet at night for a whopping 40 euros a head, virtually same as lunch buffet that is 15 euros. Food is ok but not 5 star, not close! Better off getting a 7 euro taxi to marina or old town for more value and better food. Location is poor. Right by dual carriageway, 2/3 miles from marina and the town and isolated completely. Beach at front is dark shingle and rock, i saw not one person sun bathing on it and nothing else there. Much better 2/3 miles down the coast in the town with restaurants, bars all on the sand. If this was a 4 star hotel is would be excellent but there are just too many holes to merit that 5 star status. Good but not great.

author: 55PaulR
title: Beautiful but.....
text: This was the second time we've been to this hotel in 2 years. We booked a junior suite again as the rooms are just lovely. Huge bathrooms, fantastic bedrooms and enormous balconies! The staff are brilliant especially Pablo at reception for whom nothing is too much trouble. I really enjoyed our visit but it claims to be a 5 star hotel? These are very minor quibbles but the difference between 2 years ago and now was noticeable. The breakfast choice was much more limited. Muesli ran out on day 2. The fried breakfast choice was disappointing to say the least and why do you get coffee served at the table but have to get tea yourself? Moving on it seems that the standards have just dipped. Our balcony door handle was loose as were a couple of electric switches. A replaced part of the wooden floor hadn't been stained to match the rest. Grouting on some of the bathroom tiles was missing. Nothing major but I feel they need a new eye to walk through the hotel and point out all of the details which need correcting. Despite this it is a beautiful hotel and we had a great holiday!

author: oliastu
title: Poor Location
text: Deluxe room was nice and spacious, beautiful balcony view (although the he balcony furniture was poor) and great bathroom. Plenty snags though; the patio door wouldn't lock and we reported this but it wasn't fixed. The safe broke and this was promptly fixed and the kettle wouldn't work. The reception staff were great and even prepared us breakfast for two at 5.30 a.m.for early departure. The bar staff were rude on one occasion when they forgot our drinks. Gym was good but didn't use the spa. Two big complaints though.. Firstly the price of the buffet - at lunch it was 15 euros each but became a staggering 40 euros each in the evening and there was barely a change in the menu! The location of the hotel is awful. The prom walk cuts out at rather end of the hotel and you can't go further. There is virtually nothing around and you can't walk to town as the busy main road does not have a footpath. Even the bridged walk to the local Aldi is not pleasant ere is no proper footpath on the other side. Tried to walk to the marina (2 miles) on the beach, as recommended by staff but it is pebbly and the waves come right up to the wall at certain points so it is pretty much impossible. The buses are infrequent and taxi prices a complete rip off! We paid 7 euros to the marina and 10 to return in the evening. You can walk to the old town from the marina though to save a few euros. By the way, the Internet availability was unreliable in the room. If you just want to chill in the hotel then it has got an element of luxury and you should be fine but don't expect anything more.

author: BroonieEdinburgh
title: Lovely Hotel - Nice location
text: Just spent a couple of nights here and was impressed by the size of the Junior suite we had. The bed was a super King with a fantastic mattress and good quality pillows. Room 614 on top floor with huge terrace including x 2 luxury sun loungers + Table and chairs. Magnificent view right out to sea and along the bay. Bathroom has a separate shower room and bath with shower as well a large wardrobe and safe. The staff here were all hard workers and very attentive. Food was very good and there is something for everyone. Particularly good seafood which could be cooked to order within the buffet and also a large assortment of shellfish cold or grilled.The staff were very pleasant and attentive and all looked like they enjoyed working there which was nice. On the downside, the Sun loungers by the pool were disappointing and not very comfortable so I bought a LiLo / airbed as I have a bad back but was not allowed to use this in the pool which seems ridiculous and an unnecessary rule as the pool was very quiet and mostly empty. If your looking for a good beach please be aware that the beach in front of the hotel is public and does not have any sun loungers and is all pebbles and rocks. Entertainment in the evening was poor and I think for a so called 5 star hotel they should really lose the Elvis tribute act as he was irritating most of the audience rather than entertaining them. !! Past his sell by date I think. I would not recommend doing all inclusive here for more than two or three days as it there are only a couple of a la carte restaurants and you can generally get what you order here also in the buffet. 7 days or 2 weeks of this would be hard to bear. We tagged this on to a trip to Marbella and Seville and it was a nice finale to a lovely week in Spain. I would definitely recommend this Hotel for people travelling on a short break or a week but probably not for 2 week holidays unless you have hired a car as you need to get out after a while. Overall this is a lovely hotel with many very nice aspects which out weigh the negatives.

author: bethanm597
title: Family holiday
text: 3 night stay as a family of 4 with children aged 8 and 10. Very friendly staff - welcome cava on arrival . Hotel has stunning views. Indoor heated pool fab with plenty of sunbathing areas just around the covered area. Outdoor pool not heated but close to 50metres in length so very good for swimming. Pool towels provided - you can swap them at reception for fresh ones. Breakfast choice excellent - friendly chefs cooking omelettes, eggs and pancakes on demand. Free cava at breakfast ! Coffee from machines not great but the waiter will make you a proper coffee if you ask.We were half board - again chefs with meat and fish grilling fresh superb, hot vegetables not so great, plenty of salads. Good choice of puddings and plenty of fruit. Family room for 4 had 2 singles and a large king size bed. Very spacious room with large bathroom and terrace leading out to the pool. Small fridge in room with minibar but space to put some of your own bits - Aldi and mercadona opposite hotel useful for snacks and drinks. Hotel fairly quiet - not in peak season yet . No evening entertainment - bar quiet in the evening . Plenty of comfortable sofas for children to chill out late in the evening. Would be very happy to come back to stay here. Staff very friendly. Good relaxing start to our Andalucia road trip!

author: Ek24
title: Excellent service
text: We've just returned from and over night stay in the Elba. It was my husband's birthday and I wanted to book a 1 night stay somewhere relatively close by to where we live (about 20mins away). We've stayed in lots of hotels along the coast and we'd highly recommend this one. The service was great, which sometimes is a downfall in many hotels in Spain. Upon arrival we were offered a welcome drink of cava which was a really nice touch and kick started a lovely relaxing stay. We then were shown to our room. I paid €168 for it and it was like a junior suite which I didn't expect. The staff could not be more helpful and friendly. We then used the Spa which in my opinion is better than many other more expensive spas I have used. My husband also got a 50 minute massage which only cost €58, I thought this was very reasonable. We went to Estepona old town for dinner which was really beautiful. There's lots of little bars and restaurants there and it's only a 5 min taxi journey away. We had breakfast included in our room price which was an extensive buffet and really good. The hotel is located on the beachfront and is really lovely. We'll definitely be back to the Elba. We enjoyed our stay tremendously and we applaud the hotel and staff for doing such a good job!

author: BobbieR275
title: A little bit of luxury
text: We spent 9 days here all inclusive last month and thoroughly enjoyed it. Staff very friendly and helpful although a little under staffed on the bar at night. They made lovely cocktails from scratch but as they are time consuming to do another barman/maid would have helped to stop people starting to get grumpy. There was a singer every night, all quite good, but the entertainment was in the lobby bar adjoining reception where people were booking in which was a bit weird. We thought it would be a good idea to move the entertainment to one of the themed restaurants on the floor below and use that bar as well, much more enjoyable for the artistes I would think.There are 2 a la carte restaurants but they were only used on alternate nights so why not open one every night and just alternate the menus? It made sense to us and fellow guests. Our room was beautiful with a balcony looking out to sea and a huge comfy bed. Lots of space, 2 armchairs and a table, bedside tables, fridge,TV and tea & coffee making facilities. The bathroom was immense, I've never stayed anywhere with 3 showers! There was also a bath, bidet, toilet and twin sinks. The wardrobe is in the sink area so a bit awkward if one of you wants to use the bath etc as the doors are glass and there is no door at all into the bathroom but these are small niggles. Great hairdryer by the way that is not fixed to the wall as usual. The buffet selection was good with always 4 meats and 4 fish to cook while you wait and an extensive salad bar. The choice of pre-prepared hot dishes was more limited but ok. Lovely gardens and access straight onto the beach. Great indoor pool on the 2nd floor with comfortable loungers looking out to sea and the outdoor pool was nice too and a decent size. We had a car so the location was not a problem for us but the road is really too busy to walk into Estepona but tear yourself away from the hotel because it is beautiful there and good walks along the prom (Paseo Maritimo) and make sure you explore the quaint back streets as well. La Duquesa up the road in the opposite direction is also worth a visit - small marina and lots of bars and restaurants and a decent walk along the seafront.Enjoy!

author: E4601GKstephens
title: Honeymoon
text: Recently returned back from our honeymoon. I would like start firstly by saying after reading other reviews on there own personal stay I am really not sure what there going on ( the negative ones) made me laugh especially the person who wrote about the coffee machine. It really wasnt difficult all you had to do was place your cup under the machine when you had place your plastic coffee in the machine and then guess what you only have to add milk which is warm in a metal container. How easier does it get PLEASE . On our arrival at 1.30 in the Morning feeling tired it was nice to see that food ( cold buffet) had been put in the room for us was a nice touch. Also the free cava and free upgrade. Thanks again for this .During our entire stay the room we stayed in must have been.cleaned at least twice daily. The rooms were spacious and clean and had everything need .I do agree the mini bar in the room was a little pricey. But guess what there is a lidl just across the road hmmm not as expensive. The food in the.Hotel was great both at breakfast and evening. The swimming pools were cleaned daily and if wanted a bit more peace then use the adult pool which fab. The main town of estapona can be reached by walking on the beach takes about 40 mins. We would often walk there and get a taxi back which would cost about 8 euros. The staff at the hotel were always polite and very helpfull towards us and I noticed they were the same to others. The managment team especially who ran the buffet reasturants are doing a great job always smiling and always helpfull I would strongly reccomend to stay here. Not sure.I would all inclusive though knowing that Lidl is near by lol. I would do Half Board. Thanks again to all the staff at your Hotel who made our Honeymoon even more special

author: wendysB8192GT
title: Overall a most enjoyable stay....
text: I have just returned after 15 nights with my son, on all inclusive basis. Many highlights with the facilities and staff, not least of which was celebrating my son's birthday with a cake thank you Pippa! Agree with many statements in relation to this hotel and you have to research the locality (Google earth to properly understand the location and busy dual carriageway); we ensured we were all inclusive as the location is remote in terms of other restaurants bars etc. However we wanted a chilled all emcompassing break next to the sea with associated facilities. I agree that the hotel could do with some remedial work cosmetically particularly with broken/missing tiles to the spa and pool areas which leaves it short of awarding 5 stars to the accommodation, but more making good rather than needing a complete refurb! We upgraded mid break to a prestige suite to enable us both to have our own rooms/space, well worth the investment and enhanced the holiday massively! For our purpose this hotel and location was perfect but many people failed to check out the surrounding area beforehand and they did not want to pay 5 star prices for drinks etc. If you have not budgetted for this, you either need to invest in a car to travel to other restaurants or allow for taxis to Estepona, coming in at around 18 euros return. This can mount up, especially as the walk from the beach to Estepona was not doable for many people given the tough and unpleasant siltiness of the coastline, very difficult to walk on other than in trainers. The resort and facilities were superb for our needs, having an indoor adult pool, with no child access and the spa, was awesome. The gym was poorly equipped in terms of cardio and the beach was not really suitable for running being very silty, so beware if you are runners, we had to go inland and not very scenic! Only real complaint would be the room upgrade which included a jacuzzi was not cleaned out before and I had two nights with brown sludge coming from the pipes (most unpleasant), so make sure the jacuzzi has received a proper clean out before taking a bath. Also we were constantly charged for items we did not take from the fridge, having identified eventually that staff put items in the fridge or in the cupboard meaning there appeared to be a shortfall .... we had to resort to checking our bill daily as a result. Overall very good but only because we researched what for some was a disaster due to location mostly. We will go back for a weekend in New Year!

author: magical13
title: after hen weekend relaxation
text: lovely large rooms, with fab extended en suite bathroom . large balcony on 2nd floor with lovely sea views. clean throughout the hotel, staff are very welcoming. a little dated in some parts of furnishings in lobby but does not deter the place itself. food is good, not a great selection but what they have is okay. the la carte menu in other restaurant is lovely, much different from buffetstyle in main restaurant.... As there where alot of children there when we arrived we chose to go to the buffet breakfast on the 1st floor which is adults only and very nice.... drinks are expensive we were only half board, it is worth going AI if possible because of this. Aldi is across the road for anything else. otherwise not much around till the town about 2 miles away. overall an excellent stay possible return. Last but not least i must mention the housemaids who are very thorough in the rooms and very trustworthy, so much so that i accidently left my mums watch on the day of leaving,not realising till i was at the check in at the airport it was not packed away... i rang hotel and it was passed to reception for me. luckily we had friends staying in their apt locally who collected it for me... so a big THANKYOU to the staff at the Estepona for this.

author: w0lram
title: Another good stay
text: This was our families second time at the Gran Elba and we all came away relaxed, having had a lovely family holiday. The hotel is not perfect and I am sorry it is not 5 star...... but it is very nice indeed. Checkin was smooth and we were offered a choice of a soft drink or Cava. Our suite and interconnecting room were spacious and offered a perfect view of the sea and we started to relax immediately. We were on an all inclusive package which does include pretty much everything, but you must eat all your meals (except one) in the buffet. You get a voucher to eat in one of the a la Carte retaurants. The buffet is extensive but after a while does get a bit repetitive. (I also wish they would use separate utensils for raw chicken) but the food was always fresh and well presented. Service was excellent most of the time. The kids club is not a creche to check your kids in to a forget about them.
