text: We have just returned from a one week break at the Althea Village Hotel, we stayed half board. We had an excellent time at the hotel and we were so sad to leave. We found every member of staff to be extremely friendly and helpful, they were happily willing to provide us with guidance no matter what we asked. There was always a good choice of food morning and evening, when the food ran out the catering staff would swiftly top up. The only criticism would be with the food labeling especially during the evening which I found to be occasionally misleading. Vegetarian dishes were not specifically marked as being vegetarian but you would expect at least one vegetarian dish on the menu. Mostly it wasn't a problem but I did find on a couple of occasions the main vege choice did contain either ham/bacon, which was a little disappointing. Overall, the choice was good and the food was always very fresh. The rooms were a good size and kept very clean. The pools were also very clean, and there was always plenty of space on the loungers. For us the location was perfect, it wasn't too far from either the beach or Chania. It was lovely taking an evening stroll through the village, and meeting some of the locals, which we found to be extremely happy and friendly. We went on two excursions which the hotel kindly organised for us, they were on the Little Fun Train, the tours varied and there was something for everyone. The cost was 17 euros each children 8 euros. The two we travelled on lasted approx 3.5 hours, we all found them to be very informative and fun, the guides were very knowledgeable, we thought they were certainly worth doing and good value. We had a wonderful time here and we do hope to return soon. Fond memories which will last a lifetime!

author: pani0202
title: Decent hotel, good value for the money
text: We stayed at Althea Village in early July. The rooms are dated and they're in need of some TLC (I think the hotel was built in the mid-late 80's) but overall they're clean and in decent shape. The grounds are looked after well and the swimming pools are clean and spacious. The (wonderful sandy) beach is quite far from the hotel, so if you don't have a car you'll be stranded at the swimming pools. If you're staying at Althea you should make every effort to rent a car for a few days and visit the beaches of Agii Apostoli and Chrysi Akti. Both sandy beaches and extremely clean and only a short 5-10 minute drive from the hotel. Also, make every effort to visit the beaches of Elafonisi and Falasarna. They're both well worth the (long) drive! Food: We stayed half-board and we were not overly impressed with the food. The breakfast was pretty basic, while dinner choices were very limited and the food was uninspired to say the least. Even though it makes sense from a financial perspective to go with the half board or all inclusive options I'd strongly advise against this. If you've set your heart to book a room at this hotel then just book a regular room and choose to eat out. Crete tavernas offer excellent food at very decent prices. If you're only in Crete for a week or so it's certainly worth to spend a few extra euros and enjoy the amazing Cretan cuisine. I'd say that on average you should expect to pay between 20-30 Euros for couple to eat out, and that would include drinks, salad and main dish. Pretty affordable. Service: Where Althea Village shines is when it comes to their service and friendliness. I found all staff I spoke to (from the people at the front desk to the servers and cleaning stuff) very polite and friendly. In general we found people in Crete extremely helpful and polite, wherever we went.

author: KatieE506
title: A lovely relaxing holiday with great food and in a beautiful setting
text: My boyfriend and I returned from a lovely week at Althea Village three days ago and we are very sad to be back home. We went All Inclusive which was incredible value. The food is gorgeous and largely traditional greek; at lunch and dinner there are about 5-6 main dishes to choose from along with a selection of side salads and (of course) chips for the more fussy eaters. Admittedly there was often only one choice of dessert but, to be honest, even with my sweet tooth I was usually too full up on the amazing main courses to care about the dessert. There was also a great choice of drinks included with the All Inclusive and the beer (which was self-service, on tap) tasted great. Shots of ouzo and raki as well as glasses of wine were also included with the All Inclusive. The staff were very friendly and helpful when organising trips. I'd recommend the coach trip to Elafonissi beach which you can arrange at reception- the coach also picks you up outside the front of the hotel. Nikos was also very attentive in the restaurant area and seemed to always be there- you deserve a day off Nikos! There are two pools to choose from and there were always enough sun beds. I also enjoyed the absence of entertainment teams dragging people from sunbeds or playing loud booming music while trying to relax. On an evening there isn't any entertainment provided, however the outdoor dining area is so nice that we enjoyed taking our time over our meals and a few glasses of wine. There is also a games room which kept us entertained with free table tennis as well as an ice hockey table, pool table and some computer games. The hotel location isn't a particularly lively resort, although there is a shop that is owned by a lovely lady at the end of the road and the bus stop to get to Chania is only a few minutes walk away. There is also a large children's play facility that includes go karts, mini golf and bowling by the bus stop. The beach is about 10-15 mins walk away but it's actually quite a nice stroll and the two beaches we visited (Sunset Beach and Iguana Beach) were lovely. There is also a handful of restaurants within a few minutes walk of the hotel which seemed like good value, although the food provided by the hotel was so good that we didn't eat out. Overall, we went to this hotel with pretty low expectations given our reduced budget this year and some of the reviews on here. However I'm happy to say that in the end we were blown away by the beautiful gardens, the quality of the room, the pools and especially the quality of the food. I wish I could be back there now!

author: Shellmomma24
title: Garden Hotel
text: Just come back from Althea Village and had a wonderful time there. No complaints with room or food, always soup or salad, pasta, fish, meat every day - we went all-inclusive - although there was usually only one pudding plus fruit available. Staff were excellent, especially Nikos (when does that guy get a day off?), always very helpful with good English spoken. Rooms were cleaned every day but Sunday, towels changed every couple of days, sheets also, you also got your clothes folded up and things tidied neatly. The location of the hotel we found was great, slightly out of the way, but still only about 10/15 minutes walk to the beach and we like walking anyway so that suited us. The main selling point of this hotel was the fanastic grounds with beautiful plants and trees and flowers which smelled wonderful, you could see the gardener most days doing his work. The only thing we found not quite as good as expected was the range of drinks included on the all-inclusive. You got beer and soft drinks on self-service, but the only spirits were local brandy, ouzo and raki, and these finished at 22.00, cocktails were not included. Wine only seemed to be available at mealtimes. The weather on Crete is amazing, hot and sunny every day we were there which was late May/early June. Sun beds were always available during our stay and there was a pool bar so you could help yourself to beer or soft drinks all day right there. We found the trips to be quite expensive, eg., 24.00 euros each to go to Samaria Gorge, plus another 5 each for entrance to the Gorge, plus another 8 each for the ferry back from Agia Roumelli, where you end up after your walk, to get to Sougia where the coach picks you up again for a 2 hour drive back to hotel. Having said that, the whole trip was amazing with fantastic scenery, shame to be in Crete and not do it, but the "path" consisted of stones/boulders for most of the way so be warned! Trip to Elafonissi beach was also 24.00 each, car rental started from 35.00 euros per day for small car and there are lots of places to hire from in the village so this may be a cheaper option. Bus to Chania cost 1.10 euros each, each way caught from near to the BMW garage down the hill from the hotel. Journey takes about 15 mins and drops you off near the square. Chania is a very picturesque place, especially the harbour area, and it is a maze of narrow streets with lovely shops to browse in the old town area, selling a lot of leather goods, bags, belts,shoes, etc. We got approached by restaurant owners trying to get us to eat by the harbour but no real pressure, we just walked past them. All in all a wonderful relaxing holiday, would recommend this area and this hotel.

author: ALHP
title: Lovely setting compared to rest of the area, hotel a little dated.
text: After reading great reviews of the hotel on here and other sites we figured this was a good choice when finding a deal for a couple of weeks staying at The Althea. After being messed around a lot by the holiday company we finally arrived at the hotel. After initially feeling disappointed with the area we'd chose to stay in we were pleasantly surprised with the sweet looking "village" that was Althea. We were taking to our suite by a slightly abrasive receptionist. We were a little disappointed by our room and its lack of views (a tree) resulting in no sun! Very dark and a little depressing. Maybe this was why it was quite cheap. They could make the room feel a little more comforting. Very dated décor with stained pillows and single beds. It was a mission to make the maids realise that our attempt to fill the gap to make it a double was intentional. Daily they were pulled apart. However the bathroom was lovely, very modern, nice shower. Did they miss refurbishing the rest of the room when they did the bathroom? The pool's were lovely. So were the gardens, some amazing flowers, plants and fruit trees.The Bar was a little pricey. The barman was friendly. Had one snack in the restaurant on the first day, didn't try it again as we were very disappointed. For snacks, the takeaway pizza place around the corner is the best!! Breakfast was standard buffet quality. We thoroughly enjoyed our holiday so where we stayed didn't massively bother us as it was only a place to sleep just a shame about a few things.

author: ImogenCornwall_11
title: An excellent choice
text: Have visited this hotel 3 times in the past year so I think that speaks for itself. Rooms are clean and modern and set in beautiful grounds with lots of lemon and olive trees. The two pools are beautifully clean and ther are lots of sunbeds and brollys. There is a busy road close by but we didn't find it a problem at all. Staff are so friendly and do their utmost to make sure you have an enjoyable stay. If you need anything at all the reception staff will organise it for you. Lovely drinks served in the bar at the hotel and we lunched there on many days. The pizza and spag bol was particularly good and Nikos gave us gorgeous complimentary deserts and shots. Breakfast was really nice. We didn't eat dinner here as we love to go into the city of Chania as the food there is the best we've had in Greece and really cheap compared to other islands. The city is about 3km away and is 1 euro on the bus which goes from close to the hotel. We found all the Cretan people to be exceptionally friendly . There are 3 beaches nearby, I'm not too keen on a couple of them but one is acceptable with clear water for swimming. Sunbeds are 3 euros. Al in we had a brilliant time and we will definitely return.

author: Jonathan50
title: Shame about the location
text: First of all I'll say we had a very enjoyable week in Hania at the Althea. The public areas are very clean and well presented. The gardens are very well kept and the rooms are very generous in size (although I think we had a family room for 2 people) and well presented. The pool areas are very pleasant, and beds are available anytime throughout the day. The weather in mid September was very pleasant, although we did have a morning of rain. However there are a number of negatives, which I don't think, have been emphasised before. The hotels location being the main one. The hotel is only metres from the island's main road. At the upper pool a wall has been built and has been turned into a waterfall wall to help disguise the noise. This helps, but there is no getting away from the traffic noise as you sit around the pool. Also, as the traffic runs through the night, it means that room windows need to be kept closed at night if you are a light sleeper. The majority of the guests at the hotel are German / Dutch / Swedish. Only one other British couple arrived on the same day as us. All taverna's in close proximity are all on busy roads. We went on a boat trip to Gramvousa. We were told by the Simply rep that it was a big boat, but foolishly we didn't ask how big. It was more like a ferry, with a capacity of 1200, and it was certainly was full the day we were on board. The trip stops at 2 pretty beaches, which would be excellent locations, but when 1200 people descend onto a small area, it soon get a little claustrophobic.

author: KateP1
title: Great little hotel
text: The Althea Village hotel is small blocks of rooms and apartments set in lovely gardens. Our room was large with 3 beds, air con, a fridge and a large bathroom. The rooms and the whole hotel were very clean. We stayed on a B&B basis - the breakfasts were good continental style food. The restaurant had an a la carte style menu or a buffet in the evenings. We tried the buffet and is was pretty good value - all you can eat for 9 Euros. We found the staff very friendly and helpful. The hotel is a few km from Chania and there is a frequent bus service into the town. Chania itself is lovely - not too touristy at all. We eat in the restuarants one street behind the waterfront - they are better value and the food is great - espaecially Tamam. There are quite a few tavernas close to the hotel if you don't feel like venturing far. The hotel had 2 pools and it was always easy to get a sunbed. It is quite near to a busy road so you do get some background noise from that but it's not too bad and you don't notice it after a while. The beach is a bit further than the website states - about a 10 or 15 minute walk. It's in a quiet little cove and the sunbeds are cheap to hire for the day. We would recommend walking the Samaria Gorge as it's beautiful - but make sure you wear good shoes or trainers and take plenty of water and a hat! We thoroughly enjoyed this holiday and would definitely return to Crete and recommend the Althea Village.

author: Flyer33200
title: my best trip ever!
text: Calimera! (Hello in Greek) Me and my family arrived Althea Village late in the evening June 2003. Because of the reason that it was dark, we didn't see much of the hotel that night, but the hotelroom was just fabulous! It was on 2 floors, and got 2 balcons, 2 bathrooms, livingroom and kitchen and bedroom! I had never expected it to be so nice, and the price of it was really cheap, when I compare it to other hotels I've been to. When I woke up next morning, I could finally see how it was outside the hotelroom. I've never seen anything like it!! It had 2 big pools, a restaurant and bar, and the waiters, cleaners, receptionists and gardeners were really nice to us! The food was really good, and I recommend you to try different types of typically Greek food if you ever go there.. I spent my time down there at the beaches, by the pool at the hotel, and took taxi or the bus to visit the centre Platanias and Xania!.. one day we went to th huge waterpark Limnoupolis with waterslides for both children and adults. It was so fun that I had to go back the next day too!If you want to go shopping, you can just go to the markets and streets in the cities, where the shops are full of everything!! (for example clothes, shoes, souvenirs, etc..) The time just flew away, and suddenly the day we had to go home arrived. But one day I'm going back to the island with the big mountains, warm waterside and the kind and friendly people! c",) V.F.N.

author: ButterflyThursday
title: Vegan Sunday Lunch
text: My partner is veggie and I'm vegan. We were visiting Westonbirt Arboretum for the day, so I googled 'vegan Sunday Roast' in that area and could not believe my luck when we found this place! It's just ten minutes away. I don't think I've had a roast dinner out since becoming a vegan in 2016. Service was very good and the lady who served us was so friendly and enthusiastic. The pub itself is also gorgeous (open fireplace- hello!). We both had the nutroast and my boyfriend added cauli cheese and a Yorkshire pud. The nutraost was delicious- I think full of beetroot and and some spices, and as weird as it sounds, not too many nuts! The veg was my favourite part- I'm a sucker for sprouts and everything was cooked perfectly. The roast potatoes were a bit of a let-down, to be honest. They were quite dry and not at all crispy, but maybe this was because it was a quiet day? We also had DESSERT! We both had warm ginger cake and I had mine with coconut ice cream. So delicious and the best vegan cake I've ever had. LOVED this place and we wish we lived more locally. We will definitely be visiting again!

author: NewOldGit
title: GOOD PUB GRUB
text: Myself & Mrs NOG stayed for a couple of nights late September. On arrival we were shown to our room (6) at the end of the 1st floor by a young man from reception who suggested to avoid carrying our bags from the car park, we might like to reverse our car near to the steep stone steps to our room, so as to make the transfer of bags a little easier. At no time did he offer to help with the bags.! Dinner began with a couple of G&T’s (no Gordons) in what is the small cosy pub section, before we transferred to the upstairs restaurant for our meal. We both started with the confit chicken terrine accompanied by a delightful chutney. Main for Mrs NOG was a mackerel special while I opted for the ribeye. The starters were very tasty whilst both mains were satisfactory. The serving staff were pleasant and efficient. Our room was spacious & comfortable with an additional pair of single beds on a mezzanine level and a bath in the lounge adjacent to the window. The ensuite was modern with a superb rainfall shower accompanied by upmarket bathroom products. Cons included, no shaving mirror (particularly galling for my wife’s application of makeup), no bedside lockers (nightstands), no clock & I couldn’t find a phone. However, the best part of our stay was breakfast which is served in the bar. Not a lot of choice is on display but on asking virtually any request is available served with a smile. For e.g. my wife asked for slices of avocado garnished with smoked salmon & scrambled eggs and got it!

author: carolinerF6595YG
title: Acorn Cottage Tetbury
text: We have just returned home from a long weekend at Acorn Cottage Tetbury. Recently renovated this immaculately presented, four double bedroom cottage, is the perfect country retreat. The white washed walls, mixed with oak beams and natural stone walls, give a sense of calm and tranquility, making you relax and unwind as soon as you walk through the door. The country style shaker kitchen is equipped with everything you need (bean to cup coffee machine, range-master fridge with cold water dispenser, dishwasher, toaster, and range oven) Sitting pride of place in the centre of the dining room is a beautifully crafted square oak dining table with benches, which easily fits 8-10 people for dinner. The first double bedroom can be reached by the staircase off the dining room. A large double bedroom with its own stylish ensuite. Fluffy towels, hairdryers and deliciously smelling Bramley hair and body products can be found in all the bathrooms to use at your convenience. The living room with two large grey comfy velvet sofas, was the ideal place to get the children off their electrical devices and participate in playing some good old fashion board games. Our particular favourites were Chess and Dog Bingo - great for all you dog lovers out there! From the living room, another staircase leads to a further two bathroom and three bedrooms. All with crisp white covers and extra padded mattresses - I challenge anyone who has the pleasure of staying at Acorn Cottage not to have the perfect nights sleep. The Wall Art light installation on the first floor hall is something you would find in the hippest of hotels in London or New York but looks perfect on the stone wall backdrop. What stands out about this house is the attention to detail. Everything you could ever need or want and more. If you do want to leave the house, you've only got to walk across the road to the Royal Oak pub where you'll find guest real ales and delicious organic food. Thank you for such a wonderful holiday.

author: Compass802831
title: Excellent. very welcoming
text: The staff at The Royal Oak are patient and always happy to help. After us having to cancel our stay due to our second grand daughters birth. Then to rebook again. they were so patient with us. When we arrived we were welcome with a congratulations on the birth of our grand daughter. Emma was lovely and showed us to our room. Although on the small size it was lovely decorated and clean. The toileteries were good to the point we ordered some for our selves. We were offered fresh milk if we wanted it. The bathroom room was clean. Nice powerful hot shower The food at The Royal oak was great especially the fish and chips. we had dinner there both nights and we thought it was of a high standard. Our breakfast was very good. You don't go hungary, if you do its of your own doing. The eggs were very fresh. My husband had poached eggs and salmon and there was plenty. On the first morning the house keeper Wendy asked if we were happy with our room and if we required anything. Our stay was excellent. Could not find any faults. Highly recommend

author: Alman130150
title: One of the best!
text: Just returned from a mid-week break at the Royal Oak, which I booked for an annual reunion of college friends and partners. Our group of six received a warm welcome and were personally shown to their rooms. The accommodation, which is in a separate building from the pub and restaurant, has thoughtful touches. Filtered water, tea and coffee-making facilities, accompanied by gluten-free and sugar-free biscuits, all replenished each day. The toiletries were high quality (Bramley). The bathroom had underfloor heating with an easy, operable shower. The breakfast, (served in the bar from 8:30 to 10:00am on weekdays) is varied and uniformly excellent, ranging from continental, smoked salmon to full English. All the food is freshly cooked and the tea, coffee and hot water is continually topped up The bar is popular with locals (always a good sign) with a selection of real ales and open throughout the afternoon. The large garden, with parasoled picnic benches, is an added bonus. It overlooks a valley with an excellent circular walk that begins outside the Royal Oak along a disused railway line. Although the hotel is only a five minute walk into Tetbury's centre, you feel you are in the countryside without any sense of isolation. Finally, all the staff are extremely attentive. They enter into conversation without being intrusive. Moreover, they are local with a fund of knowledge about places to visit and eat out in the area. We began our yearly reunions in 2000 and our visit to Tetbury has been one of the best.

author: Jumbosue
title: Outstanding staff and accommodation.
text: On entering the Royal Oak we were immediately made to feel welcome. The staff were friendly and keen to make sure that our stay was going to be a pleasurable experience. Lisa showed us to our room and pointed out the range of facilities, how various things worked and other relevant information about the accommodation. Our room was not large but was snug and contained some nice items of furniture. The ensuite room was warm (underfloor heating) the shower was easy to use and like the bedroom, spotlessly clean. I was very impressed by many small touches - quality toiletries, a choice of tea bags and coffee, a large bottle of filtered water, plenty of milk and gluten free biscuits. Breakfast was served between 8:30 and 10:00am in the bar, the menu was quite extensive and food was freshly cooked to order. The "full English" was very full - sausage, bacon, black pudding, mushrooms, tomato, baked beans and eggs. I expected my choice - scrambled egg with smoked salmon, to be similar to how I make it at home but it was better! Slices of salmon arranged on a plate accompanied by a portion of perfectly scrambled egg - delicious! The team at the Oak really know what they are doing, I couldn't fault anything. They care about their customers and clearly enjoy their work. They couldn't have been more helpful, obliging and cheerful. We have stayed in many hotels and pubs, both here and abroad and this was an outstanding experience. Thank you for making our stay so enjoyable

author: SamH296
title: Brilliant food, service, drinks - HIGHLY RECOMMEND!
text: After looking for good restaurants in Tetbury this one was ranked number 1 and there is good reason for that. In fact it was so good we returned the next day! We visited this Saturday with 3 other couples and with the lovely weather sat in the cobbled stone court yard surrounded by properties that the pub rents out. The Royal Oak is a freehouse and there are at least 6 ales on draft and plenty of other choices to boot. The food was fantastic. I chose the homemade beef burger with blue cheese, homemade PROPER chips and a homemade coleslaw relish. The portions were big, the quality excellent and the price very reasonable (approx. £12 for the above). We were served by Leah who was friendly, keen, helpful with good knowledge of the menu. Other friends’ foods included the prawn salad and fish and chips. Both were highly recommended! We went back for Sunday lunch but after a large breakfast at our hotel (20 minutes away but wish we’d stayed here!) we weren’t up for a full roast. We were sat in the beautiful open upstairs dining room with exposed beams and oak floors and hops hanging from the ceiling. We all shared a plethora of dishes including charcuteries, maki rolls, salads and Yorkshire puddings with gravy followed by chocolate terrine with berries, apricot etc. All again was fantastic and once again, we were served by Leah who was excellent at every stage of the meal. You’re lucky to have staff like this Royal Oak! We were all big fans of the ‘make your own bloody Mary/virgin Mary’ that was on the bar and had a large assortment of accompaniments to go with the dish. Refreshing, unique, reasonable and fresh! We will certainly be returning to this pub, hopefully to stay next time. FIVE STARS.

author: EllenRN
title: AVOID this place
text: We booked a king no-smoking room about a month in advance of our overnight stay. When we arrived, my husband used the bathroom after our long drive. Not only did the toilet not flush, but it immediately overflowed! The clerk informed us that, since it was a Saturday, nobody was available to fix the problem and she would have to give us another room. It was at the far end of the property and honestly looked like it had been neither used nor cleaned in months. Plus it had 2 double beds rather than a King. Plus, it smelled of smoke although we were assured it was a non-smoking room. The toilet worked, but the tub was a dirty mess. The bedspreads and carpet had large black stains. None of the lamps or the TV were plugged in, and in doing that myself, I saw a GROSS amount of dirt in the carpets. The furniture was shabby, dented, and dusty. I will say the beds were comfortable, the TV and fridge worked, the wifi worked and was free. Standard breakfast choices. We were in town for a very specific event and I had no time to argue with the clerk about our bill, but it seems to me that given the circumstances (downgrade, horrible room) we should have been given a credit on our bill without me having to negotiate for it. VERY poor property.

author: 550pattyw
title: Needs freshening up
text: This is our second stay here in eight months. Check in was great .. quick friendly .. buttered popcorn cooking in the lobby for guests.. nice atmosphere . The room .. 118.. not so much . First observance was the dirty carpet .. actually tacky under my bare feet.. immediately put shoes back on . In the bathroom later I realized a damp used bath towel had been left on the door hook making me assume the bathroom hadn’t been cleaned.. as a fresh towel wasn’t replaced . The bottom of the tub was grey with overuse . Internet was slow, furniture chipped, decor dreary.. tv sound was poor .. non clear .. I won’t stay here again despite the good location and attractive reception center. BW needs to redo this one ..

author: LordandLadyPenelope
title: Peace and comfort... probably not
text: First impressions were great, out of the main part of the town, and easy to find. The welcome was warm and effusive. We felt quite special! The pub has undergone complete renovation at huge expense in the last few years. The main part of the pub is interesting and atmospheric. It appears to be popular with locals as well. Dinner was good however the service was rather frenetic, intrusive and somewhat incompetent at times. But the handmade chips were really good! Unfortunately the rooms let The Royal Oak down. Our room was quite small with a small but fab shower room. But the bed was as hard as concrete with bricks for pillows. Sound proofing is non existent and we were disturbed by very noisy neighbours to one side, frequently going in and out of the room slamming doors, shouting at the TV and singing along (very loudly) and 'entertaining' us until the early hours with some mild S&M!! (Yes really!). The couple in the room above us also 'tested' out the bed springs. It might have been funny in other circumstances. I appreciate that The Royal cannot control guest behaviour or antics but they could have made sure that the rooms had the highest spec of sound proofing given no expense spared in other areas. Breakfast was excellent and as with dinner its obvious that great produce is used. I would recommend the Pub for a meal and would eat here again but I could not really recommend it as place to stay.

author: GeoffH106
title: Great place to stay..........provided you're not in a rush!
text: For this weekend six of us booked in for a weekend at the Royal Oak. It's an annual event when we choose a part of the country to visit and walk. This year we chose Tetbury. The Royal Oak is a brilliant pub. Loads of atmosphere and very, very friendly staff. We arrived on a sunny Friday afternoon and the place was buzzing with lots of people enjoying themselves in the garden. After a bit of a wait whilst the keys to the rooms were found we were shown in. Good rooms. Our was a bit tight, and it's just as well that neither of us is large, but well equipped and comfortable with one exception. We arrived by motorbike and to be honest, four coat hooks with coat hangers is not a really good substitute for a wardrobe and cupboard space. Yes, there was a chest of drawers but because of the size of the room it was a bit of a chinese puzzle to use it when we were both in the room. We ate in the restaurant for both nights of our stay. This is where we do have a bit of a gripe. We had booked in for 8 on the first evening and had to ask twice before we were shown up. We had to wait a further hour before we were actually fed. The food however, when it did come, was superb and the menu very varied both in choice of meal and in price. You could have a mains ranging from under £10 to £25. Yes, the waiting for access to rooms and the wait for food was a bit annoying, as was the lack of accessible storage in the room, but that is all they are, minor annoyances. I would not hesitate to stay here again.

author: CoachD29
title: Didn't live up to expectations
text: I have stayed at this particular BW for 4 years now for an annual golf trip to the area. Although a bit dated.. I have always been very pleased with the service I received, the cleanliness, and the attention to detail at this particular BW. I must say that this time was a disappointment. Strictly speaking for the room I was assigned (177) , This facility is in need of a major upgrade... There were major scuff marks all along the wall. There were zero electrical outlets near the night stand which made charging my various devices a problem. The room in general was not as clean as I have been accustomed to. There is build up of dust along the baseboards behind the nightstand and beds, which I discovered looking for an electrical outlet. There was a spiderweb in the bathroom, with a spider, and a large spider in the tub the morning I checked out. I checked in on Saturday, June 30th. After coming in from my morning round of golf I noticed my room had not been cleaned. Later that afternoon as I headed out for my 2nd round of the day I stopped by the front desk to report the issue and request some clean towels. I told the desk clerk that I would stop back by the desk after I returned from my round of golf to collect the clean towels.. I'm not sure if the fact that it was a Sunday and they may have been short staffed as to why my room was not cleaned. The wifi was weak and inconsistent. I constantly had trouble accessing google maps to get directions to courses and restaurants. All in all if I had to rate this stay on a scale of 1 to 10, I would have to give this one a 5 at best... There just wasn't the attention to detail that I am accustomed to when staying at a BW...

author: lindaf925
title: Old but okay in a pinch
text: We made the reservation the night before. We called several places in Pinehurst but they were all booked. The place looked like it had been a motel; it's 2 stories. All the rooms are entered from the outside. And because of the configuration, you may not be able to park in front of your unit. If you have a lot of stuff, try ti get a fist floor room. The room was old -- old rug, old beat-up furniture, old bathroom. The bathroom was tiny. But the sink (granite) was outside so that helped. The counter was tiny also. There was no tea in the room and we discovered in the morning that the pullout tray in the coffee machine was missing. While we were at breakfast, the maid came in and took all our towels. It was obvious that we hadn't left yet. I had to go to the front desk to get a hand towel. On the plus side, the rooms seem to have been freshly painted. -- inside and outside. There were lots of plugs in the lamps to charge our phones. And there was a microwave and a mini fridge with freezer. The lobby was being renovated.

author: KarenB100
title: Worst Room Ever!!
text: We booked for one night at the Best Western Pinehurst Inn to visit friends nearby. I frequently book at Best Western because they have a pet friendly policy and don't charge more for the pet than the cost of the room as some motels do. Plus the room is usually clean and comfortable. We arrived around five o'clock and checked in. The motel was not crowded. As I requested, our room was by the pool. Anxious to get our dog outside for some quick play time and to get her accustomed to the room before we left for dinner, we didn't inspect the room closely. We did notice an odor but it wasn't strong. We put our dog in her crate and left for dinner. When we returned, I took my shoes off and noticed that the rug felt damp and looked stained in a couple of places. My husband took a shower and said the tub didn't drain leaving him standing in dirty water. The worst discovery came in the morning when I saw that the bed had no mattress pad and only a sheet between us and the mattress! That is disgusting! Think of how many people have slept on that bed!! Gross! Total negligence on the housekeeping staff! First time ever to not leave a tip! We couldn't wait to leave! I told them at the desk and the reply was, "We're sorry." We would have definitely changed rooms had we discovered everything earlier. You just don't expect that from Best Western, at least I didn't!

author: Joebella
title: Great B&B!
text: We've stayed her twice in the last few months, we're actually getting married in Tetbury and so have been staying here when visiting to do wedding plans. The first time we stayed we were downstairs - I have attached pictures. The room was beautifully decorated, modern and simple. it was also a decent size with plenty of space. Everything was also really clean and tidy. The second time we stayed we were upstairs in the room next door to Oak Lodge. I was really surprised by how small this room was compared to the one (pictures of small room also attached) we'd been in previously, you only just had enough room to open the door and walk around the bed. Again, the room was decorated lovely and really clean etc. But it just was a bit too small and if staying again i'd ask for a different room. The other issue we had is you could hear absolutely everything going on in the rooms next door, particularly the side that Oak Lodge was on. We didn't have this problem when we were downstairs, so was a bit of a shame. The food here is really great, breakfasts are delicious and you have a good choice. We ate tea here one night too and it was lovely. The staff are also really friendly and helpful. It also has free parking and is a short walk from the town centre. The rooms are also really good value for money, we paid £75 for weeknights and i think it was £90 or £95 for a weekend. I've given this place a 5 because of the first time we stayed, the food and staff. If i'd just stayed in the tiny room then it may have been a 4. I would recommend this place to anyone wanting to stay in Tetbury, just maybe specify one of the downstairs or larger rooms if available. We are actually coming back to stay here in Oak Lodge for a couple of nights after our wedding in March and really looking forward to coming back!

author: Dinlos
title: Scrupulously clean, friendly & delicious.
text: We decided to make a trip out to Tetbury to eat here; as we have booked all the rooms for 2 nights & the upstairs restaurant for the rehearsal dinner. Our daughter will be leaving from here to get married at Westonbirt in the summer. So, a lot was riding on how we would enjoy the Royal Oak. Any apprehension was assuaged immediately by the incredibly friendly welcome we received the moment we stepped through the door. There is a lovely selection of local ales on draft…and of course cider! My husband and I enjoyed a thoroughly Gloucestershire-based meal of a Gloucester old spot sausage sandwich made with local baker Hobbs House bread and fish and chips with probably the nicest rustic fat chips I've ever eaten. We both had local drinks my husband; Uley Ale and I had a still Seven Cider. The food was fresh, fast, hot and very tasty. Great accompaniments and a happy relaxed atmosphere. Papers to read and dogs are welcome. As I mentioned in my title we both needed to use the rest rooms and they were scrupulously clean. The makeover of this pub, which neither of us had ever been to before; is a high specification and it shows. A great deal of flair mixing the Cotswolds style with modern amenities has been applied, & it definitely works. If I was to levy one tiny criticism it would be a sign for the car park would be helpful. So much looking forward to visiting you again in August and being able to take advantage of the lovely courtyard garden area...as I have booked a perfect summer's day for my daughter's wedding, obviously! Finger's crossed. :-)

author: sheilac684
title: Stunning!
text: Beautifully restored pub, dining room and buildings across a courtyard which house B & B accommodation. Our room (no 1) was tastefully decorated and well furnished. Although not a large room, it was beautifully appointed and had a lovely shower room. Staff are very friendly and helpful and they enhance the whole experience. Breakfast, which is served in the pub, is excellent with generous portions. The sausages are amazing! The upstairs dining room was busy and buzzy. Service couldn't be faulted. Although the evening menu isn't huge it is varied and fresh local produce is used. We saw the delivery of beautiful fruit and vegetables this morning! Try the ice cream! Staff are knowledgeable about the menu and origins of produce. Lunch menu is also varied. Good choice of local beers and cider. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay and our trip to Highgrove which is about 2 miles away. No problems with parking. Spaces are available behind the garages below the pub or in the Rail Yard free car park which is just a few more steps away.

author: Philpedia
title: Pub/Food review: Nope - I disagree
text: When this place finally opened we felt we had a winner. The decor is simple and quite stylish and the drinks selection is both comprehensive and reasonably priced. The food however..... We have now eaten here three times. The first within a week of it opening and it was good. Nicely constructed dishes and flavours but served in a cold upstairs restaurant - so cold we asked to be relocated in the bar which was a lot better. We visited again a couple of months later and the food has taken a big downturn. The burger was dry, hard and tasteless it was like MDF! The chips were frozen offerings. All very poor. Having read all of these glowing reviews about the food, we thought they had perhaps turned over a new leaf - so we tried again. We wished we hadn't. Sausage and mash was 3 nice sausages on some pitiful looking (and miserly) mash and a jug of instant gravy - no veg, no love and no imagination. It was a dish produced to 'feed' not impress and it didn't impress at all. The other dish was a pork chop which was dry and on the same dire mash also failed to impress. Don't get me wrong, these were edible plates of food but they are most certainly not of the quality to make you want to visit for dinner. These were more like school dinner quality (no offence to dinner ladies) and not worthy of the prices being charged. I really do question the palates of the people who describe this food as excellent - perhaps they don't get out very often. The pub is great and the outdoors space is very nice, worth a visit to those reasons alone but leave the food well alone!

author: DennisL418
title: Three days in November 2014
text: My wife and I travel twice a year to Texas and North Carolina. We stay in motels for two weeks, and we visit restaurants that are local or belong to a chain not located in our hometown. We visited the Best Western Pinehurst Inn in Southern Pines, North Carolina, for three days, because of its proximity to Fort Bragg, where our son is stationed. It’s a two-story motel, easily reached on US-1, with all rooms accessed from the outside. We’d asked for a first floor room. Ours was located with door access to the parking lot, so we parked right outside our room and had minimal luggage drag. Our room was nicely appointed with dark cherry or mahogany colored furniture and complimentary wall and floor color schemes. As with most Best Western Hotels we’ve visited, the furniture included desk, large TV, dresser, queen beds, table and chairs, refrigerator, microwave, and adequate lamps. The beds were very comfortable. There was a closet nook with several hangers and an adequate half bathroom. Between the closet and half bath was a counter and sink. The half bath was adequate but not spacious. The shower head had a pulsating stream with good pressure and temperature. Breakfast was mostly what we expect of Best Western. It was served 6:00 to 10:00 in a nice large room with comfortable chairs and spacious tables. The breakfast counter was outside the dining room at a far edge of the lobby. There were yogurt, cereal, instant oatmeal, waffles, bagels, toast, biscuits, muffins, cream cheese, jams, gravy, microwave breakfast sandwiches, coffee, several juices, bananas, and apples. My wife enjoyed a breakfast sandwich and coffee. I enjoyed a breakfast sandwich, bagel with cream cheese and jam, coffee, and juice. Near the motel were a McDonald’s, Arby’s, Wendy’s, and Dunkin Donuts.

author: amanda_sid72
title: Great hospitality
text: My husband and I have just returned home after spending two nights in this lovely guesthouse. We picked room 6 after viewing the photos on their website. We were not disappointed, stunning room and plenty big enough. It has two single beds upstairs (mezzanine) thus would also be a great room for friends or family to stay too. The room is kitted out with quality furnishings and the decor is tasteful. We enjoyed two lovely evening meals in the dining area of the pub. Good value for money and cooked very well. The menu has good choices with some good old fashioned English food with little twists to make them interesting. They also provided a good selection of breakfast. We chose the English breakfast which was great and well cooked. The pub is lovely and charming with a great beer garden well thought out. Since we were lucky with the weather we took full advantage of it with lazy afternoons and evenings sat underneath a parasol sipping cider. We choose this guesthouse as it was also close enough to the Fairford air tattoo which we were attending. We are so pleased we found this place and will definitely be returning - but will stay longer next time. This is an excellent base to explore both Tetbury and the surrounding area. This is probably the most important information about this review: all the staff members are incredibly friendly, helpful and nothing was ever too much trouble. It's rare to visit a place today where you immediately feel relaxed, at home and well looked after. Much thanks royal oak. . See you again soon!

author: MelvinNewportGwent
title: Great choice made !
text: After looking over many places to stay in Tetbury for a night away for my wife`s birthday i decided to stay here going by the reviews, could not have made a better choice. Very friendly welcome when we arrived and were shown to our room straight away, what was mentioned in an earlier review was the room was not very big, size is not everything! The room had all you needed,lovely large comfy bed, good beverage tray, great lighting and a good flat screen tv, okay no wardrobe but the hangers were ample for the usual length of stay by most people. The bathroom was as good as any i have ever come across, top end spec. A word of warning though, dont turn the power shower on full as it will hit you across the bathroom as it`s that good a shower. Plenty of extra`s as in shampoo, conditioner, bath crystals etc,etc. We decided to eat there as the menu and restaurant looked really nice. We started off with a shared plate of different slice of cold meats, homemade sausage roll, gherkin, salad and piccalli, really nice food presented well. My wife then had a really good burger with blue cheese topping and chips which she really enjoyed. I had the pick of the bunch though, creamy mash with spinach folded in with belly of pork, with "twiglets" of pork crackling on top, this came with a cider and apple jus, this really was as good as it gets, if possible i would have had it for breakfast the next morning if i could have as well. Good cooked breafast the next morning with a vegan option as well, good coffee also. Spoke to the owner Kate whilst there and you could see her passion for the place when she spoke, she was thrilled to bits when we said we really liked the place, she also has one of the nicest dogs you have ever seen, also the largest as well HA!! Great beers as well with great staff, proper traditional pub. As someone who does a lot of reviews one maybe looks for the odd thing wrong but on this occasion i did not have a hope! Will return again without a doubt.

author: CaroandJon
title: Fantastic hospitality for a traveler with mobility issues
text: From the initial booking, the friendliness and general air of wanting you to have the best experience with them shone through. We were looking for a spring break to brush the cobwebs away and offer hospitality that is attractive to two mobility impaired 40 somethings with a wish for beer, good food and good company. Usually the old fashioned hospitality of pubs and inn's are off limits as their rooms are up stairs which we cannot climb. The Royal Oak has had a massive refurbishment in the last year and they have converted an outside building to rooms, with the Garden Room in particular being designed to accommodate those with mobility issues. We loved the decor which has been designed with luxury and comfort in mind, I envied the tv that is a mirror! We noted that the owners were adding the extra things as and when finances allowed that makes it stand out ( good art on walls) and were also very open to recommendations from guests. The short hope across the courtyard - was heaven for my husband who so often the car driver had well kept ale on tap, and foodie heaven for me ( as well as fine wine the rose was sublime). From other reviews there was mention about quality of the food, breakfast, set you up for the day, fresh and plentiful. We ate both nights we stayed from the pub menu and it was glorious we loved the chips with skins on, appreciating them being non processed. Meat was melt in the mouth and supplied from a top quality supplier whose name I knew. Sadly we could not access the restaurant being upstairs, we could have had the restaurant menu down stairs but as the pub menu was so good no need. I have stayed in many places where owners have spent large amounts on the decor and products but customer service lets them down. This is where The Royal Oak stands out, from the help we received on arrival ( a wheelchair push was required from the car park) to the young lady with a beaming smile at breakfast, to the bar staff who made sure we had a table each night, throughout the evening making sure beer and food was flowing to our table and good conversation about beer and wine, it made for a terrific stay. The marker of a good pub/inn is what the locals think, each night it was packed with them and their four legged friends! When we were shopping in Tetbury, the shop owners when enquiring where we were staying had nothing but praise Yes, its not completely ideal for two people with mobility issues..... car park is definitely a scooter journey (down a steep hill) the bathroom although adapted is not an all singing or dancing utilitarian wet room. Life is not perfect, we are use to adapting.... and so appreciated actually not feeling "disabled" and this was so 99% perfect for us, we are already planning our return..... see you soon

author: steffifritz11
title: 5 stars in every way - plus fab entertainment in their pub!
text: I have had the pleasure of being asked to perform at this wonderful Pub/Inn/B&B twice since it opened and i can honestly say that it is my favourite place to stay over and perform in. Firstly the rooms are decorated so tastefully and with such quality that it really feels like 5 star accommodation. The rooms may not be massive (apart for the amazing room 6!! Amazing!) but you're only really staying there for 1 or 2 nights so I'd take the huge and oh-so-comfy-its-rediculous beds over that little extra floor room any day. The bathrooms are my favourite...so classy, and all British made fittings. Everything at the Royal Oak has been put together with love and it really shows, everything has been carefully chosen, locally sourced and carefully installed, so there's no bad workmanship anywhere (I've checked!) Even the shower gel and shampoo stuff is gorgeous...plus you can buy it. Which i did. Let's put it this way...the towels are so good that it took me 20 seconds to realise that i was drying my face with the foot matt....(true!!) So then there's the pub...with the nicest and sweetest staff going. Genuinely friendly and interested in their customers...and all ready and willing to help you have a lovely stay. The food is amazing, fresh, tasty, healthy and well presented...including the breakfast in the morning where one can get pretty much anything they want! The beers are local and different and change regularly as all good pubs should. The main thing that I noticed on my two separate gigs here was the loyalty and genuine support of their locals. Which just speaks volumes about the atmosphere, quality and warmth that this pub and it's landlady Kate gives out to anyone who walks through those doors. If you're planning on stopping over anywhere in the area...I really cannot recommend this place enough...you will not be disappointed in any way. And if you're a performer and Kate asks you to play and stay over...say "yes please!"...it'll be a lovely gig and she'll make you feel like royalty!

author: chrisp390
title: Affordable luxury
text: My wife and I stayed here for one night in the middle of the week in the dog friendly room downstairs with our not so friendly Puli! Our first impression was that of an old coaching house nestled in a very pretty Cotswold village, and this is exactly what it is, but with a twist. The Royal Oak has been fantastically and sympathetically renovated to a very high standard which equals the standard of many hotels that we've stayed in for 3 times the price. The room was very large that we could have stayed there all week and not felt enclosed. We were greeted by Lucinda who ensured we had everything we needed and even gave us a little tour of the rooms and the bars. We were introduced to all the staff who were conveniently around but not intrusive. In the evening we ate in the restaurant meeting my elderly mother and grown-up children for dinner. The meals were large enough for my big appetite and we all had something a bit different showing the variation of dishes and choices available. Although we had booked a time for dinner and there were many other diners, we were not hurried so were able to have a drink in the entertaining bar beforehand. After the meal we retired downstairs and sat by the log fire which was the perfect location to exchange and open Christmas presents. What a lovely thing to do in the glow and smell of a winters fire. Even some of the staff joined us when invited giving the whole experience a personal touch. Breakfast in the morning was sumptious with lovely local food and again unhurried. We felt extremely well looked after and thank Kate and Chris for making us feel special during our stay at the Royal Oak Tetbury. A special thanks to Lucinda, Leah and Sharry for looking after us during our stay. We cannot recommend this establishment enough. There is now only one place to stay in the Cotswolds. Well done, A 5/5 experience.

author: rmksmk
title: Great accommodations for a short stay
text: We spent a couple days in the Pinehurst area decided to stay at this Best Western, mainly to take advantage of their spring special (Rent 3 get one free). We were pleasantly surprised. Loved the first floor room (no steps needed) with a king bed. The room was comfortable and clean. The refrigerator was big and had a freezer section which let us keep our ice paks frozen for during our travel. The breakfast bar had a great selection and well maintained. We were able to get a healthy variety! The only thing that disappointed us was that while we went to breakfast, housekeeping came in to clean our room. We weren't expecting that and hadn't put all of our stuff away. Also, they had to drop off towels later - we were still there so we had to set up. By doing that, they also neglected to give us new coffee packets for the next morning - of course we didn't realize that until we went to make the coffee. We got dressed quickly and ran up to the breakfast bar to get some. The location was great and easy to get to. They also were partnered with The Sly Fox restaurant and pub where we got 20% off food because we were staying at the Best Western. We took advantage of that and had a delicious dinner! I would definitely select this hotel again.

author: CGNY53
title: PInehurst Inn - great stay
text: In August, seven of us traveled to Pinehurst, NC, for the 100th birthday of our aunt. We wanted a place that was clean and updated but not overly expensive. The Best Western Pinehurst Inn fit the bill - and then some! The rooms (we had 4) were all super clean and very comfortable. The pool area was immaculate. Three members of our party had canes and one had a walker and the hotel staff was very accommodating to get their rooms near the lobby where the breakfast was served every morning so it wouldn't be difficult for them to walk there. And what a great breakfast! It included make-your-own waffles, an assortment of breakfast biscuits (sausage and egg, bacon and egg, etc) that you could microwave, cereal, different types of juices, fruit, coffee, tea. Everyone was very happy with the breakfast. Also, on some nights they have what's called a manager's reception at 5:00 where they serve snacks and wine (I think this may only be during the week, which is when we were there). A nice extra. I also found the housekeeping staff to be very respectful. The BW Pinehurst Inn is located right on the main drag in Southern Pines and close to many restaurants, stores, etc. It goes without saying that golf is very close by. I would definitely stay here again and so would the rest of my group. Highly recommend.

author: cymmiller
title: Nice place, just a few quirks
text: This place is hard to find, even with directions on Google maps. This is on the 3rd floor of a private residence building. There is no signage on the outside, and the building numbers are very small. It is directly across the street from a gas station, and that's the best place to park to go check in, daily parking is €15/day. There is a buzzer panel beside the door, ring it, and they buzz the door open for you. There is a small elevator, which is nice with bags. The woman who runs the B&B is really nice, she shows you the room, the remotes, how to work the widow shutters. The breakfast is served in the room, it's delivered at the time you arrange with them, and your choice of coffee. We stayed in the blue room. The room itself is very good sized, especially for Europe, and so is the bathroom. The shower is small, and the door leaks at certain spots, so you have to be careful on the tile floor. Plus, the shower drain was really slow. There's an electronic kettle in the room, and teas, and small fridge. One morning we woke up and there were ants all over the wall, and desk, where the kettle was. It only happened once though. Overall this is a good property, nice staff, and good rooms. The difficulty finding it, the slow shower, and the ants are the only reasons I gave it four stars, instead of five. The people are really nice, I was sick when we arrived, and they offered to get me a doctor, and told us where to find a pharmacy. I would recommend staying here, just be aware of the quirks.

author: BoardingPass237415
title: Excellent place
text: We would like to thank Emily for our wonderful stay at Emily Suites in Sorrento. The room was spotless clean, spacious, nice and colourful. Delicious breakfast was served in the room, prepared by Emily's mother,with fresh eggs coming from Emily's farm (which we actually visited). The room cleaning service was excellent.The elevator is cute,stylish and unique. Laundry services can be found in the building next door. The location of Emily Suites is very convenient, pretty close to "the Cuore di Sorrento". Emily is a great host. She organised our stay perfectly. We were able to visit most of Sorrento, Capri, almost all of the Amalfi Coast, Salerno and her family's gardens and farm in Sant'Agata. Most of these tours were private with Domenico as our driver. Domenico is a very polite,respectful and punctual person. He drives carefully and safely (we had a little child with us).He stopped at every viewing point in order for us to take pictures, while he enthusiastically explained all kinds of interesting facts and stories. The last day, he was courteous and kind enough to help us push and carry our heavy luggages onto the dock right in front of the ferry. You feel very much at home and very welcome at Emily Suites. We highly recommend Emily Suites without reservation. Roula, Hadi and Georges.

author: MandD018
title: Wonderful host and a great place to stay!! Highly recommended.
text: We booked Emily Suites based on the excellent reviews we had read. Before we arrived we had regular email communications that were always prompt and courteous and Emily arranged our transfer from the airport for us. I got a call from her the day before se set off to explain about the driver and getting into the apartment and to ask what time we would like breakfast on our first day! Our stay was excellent. The room was spacious, modern, comfortable, exceptionally clean with a tv, free wifi and air conditioning. Each day we were asked what time we would like our breakfast and this was brought in on table and was always a lovely way to start the day. The real gem at Emily Suites is Emily and her staff. She is very passionate and caring and goes out of her way to look after you and make sure you have all you need. She really does love what she does and the satisfaction of her guests is top priority. Nothing was any trouble and we even had a decorative ornament given to us on our last day that Emily made herself, as well as a heart-felt hug! Our room had a balcony but if you chose to sit out on it, it was a little too noisy with the traffic as you are on the main road towards the centre. However, with the patio door shut you could not hear anything much. The suites are on the third floor (there is a lift) of a fairly unimpressive residential building and its a 15-20 minute talk to Tasso Square. That said, there are bars and restaurants nearby if you wan to avoid the hordes of fellow tourists. Don't let the walk or the comment about the noise from the traffic put you off though, these things are very minor indeed and are dwarfed by the wonderful time you will have staying here and its superb value. : )

author: FionaZak
title: Wonderful Stay!
text: Emily the lovely owner already texted me on my phone via whatsapp before our arrival so that I could contact her if I needed to. How considerate was that! She greeted us warmly upon our arrival and showed us our beautiful blue room (for triple) and checked what we liked for breakfast the following morning! She was really on the ball. She and her mom served us breakfast in our room. It was such a treat. She was so eager to please and wanted to make sure that we were comfortable. She also arranged for a car to bring us to Naples train station when we had to check out. We slept well for the two nights we were there. The room was spacious and very clean, and the bathroom was huge. There was a lift so it was great for our luggages. The guest house is centrally located and just a 10 minute walk to the town centre. There are shops and restaurants where Emily Suites is. We will stay at this guest house again! Thank you Emily for your handmade gift and for a memorable stay.

author: Yogi535
title: Excellent price and location. Great family environment.
text: We are family of four and stayed in Mid March for 4 nights. Nice size and clean rooms. Beds were comfortable and sheets and towels were clean. Roomy bathroom comes with a roomy shower space and even a bidet! Even the kids beds are comfortable. Emily (the owner who has 3-4 rooms on the 3rd floor and shares the building with other B and Bs and tenants in the same building) was very hands on and helpful. She went out of her way to help us. She helped us with the laundry (laundromat is 2 doors down). She helped pick it up after it was done and put in our room while we were out on a tour which was great. She suggested us to use Whatsapp to communicate via smart phone and that saved us money on communication (text and calls on whatsapp are free if you have data plan). Overall a great value as it is affordable, clean place and is 12 minutes walk to main (Piazza Tasso). Hotels and B and Bs can be expensive in Sorrento depending on time of year. Emily and Ana work hard and go out of there way to help make your stay very comfortable. The breakfast gets delivered to your room and it can be a little tight in there with four people eating. The suggested time is 830AM for breakfast but they deliver it early (we got it at 715 AM one morning and night before one morning) if you ask one day ahead of time. Breakfast got delayed one morning by 20 min and we almost did not make our tour (most tours start 7am or 8am). Also the train tracks are right behind the hotel and train runs from 6AM to 1030PM and can be an issue if you are not used to noise of train. One other issue which I don't think was the fault of B and B completely, is our tour of Capri got cancelled because of sea conditions and the tour operator (Travel etc) did not notify us directly but the B and B directly via email one day before but that did not get conveyed to us till later in the evening around 730 pm and that was too late to make any changes to our itinerary. Hence the reason for four stars. In summary, a great value for the money you spend, near central location, a family environment and wonderful warm people.

author: DavidWren66
title: Excellent accomodation in Sorrento
text: I highly recommend Emily Studios for anyone who is looking for bolt-hole in Sorrento, or indeed anywhere on the Amalfi coast. Emilia is THE perfect host, always willing to assist and genuinely concerned that you are having a good time. We received a room upgrade after I contacted Emilia to inform her that we were celebrating our silver wedding anniversary in Sorrento. The room was perfect, kept spotlessly clean (cleaned on a daily basis) and breakfast was served in the room at whatever time you requested it. Plenty of choice for breakfast too with coffee, juice, fruit, a selection of pastries, yoghurt and toasties all available. Emilia or Anna are usually around at the apartments for anything you need from around mid-morning to between 6 or 7 in the evening. You can change your breakfast choice whenever you wish by informing Emilia or Anna the day before. Emilia also booked all our trips for us while we were there. I can highly recommend the trip to Capri, the Amalfi coast tour and the trip to Pompeii & Vesuvius. Very convenient pick up and drop off right outside the apartments and the trips were excellent. We had a superb week in Sorrento and I must give a lot of credit to Emilia for making it so memorable. She was an extremely good source of local information for getting to/from places and recommending good places to eat (try Soul and Fish restaurant in Marina Grande for a special occasion). The apartments are located on the main road into Sorrento about a 10 minute stroll into the centre. There are some excellent cafes and local restaurants on the way into town. Don’t bypass these in a rush to dine in the restaurants on the square. On the whole, they offer excellent/good value food. 10 out 0f 10…… Meraviglioso!

author: 265sylviaa
title: Incredible Stay"
text: Our first trip to Italy. I found Emily Suites online, wasn't sure what to expect but the reviews were all great. Before leaving Toronto Emily and I exchanged several emails and a phone call. Just from our conversation I felt good about my decision to stay there. When we arrived in Sorrento Emily came to pick us from the train station. Right away I felt a connection, she was lovely. My husband and I both felt very comfortable and welcomed into a beautiful bed and breakfast. Big, beautiful and clean rooms. Breakfast was brought into our room every morning. Emily went overboard in ensuring our stay was comfortable, helping me book excursions, restaurants, giving us tips on what to do and where to go in Sorrento and getting to Salerno in time to catch our cruise. :) Emily is a wonderful lady with such a big heart! She really does everything to ensure her clients have a wonderful stay. You can feel her passion and love for her work. I've made a friend for life! Thank you Emily, we miss you!

author: 377deannac
title: Amazing stay!
text: It was such a pleasure to stay at Emily Suites in Sorrento! We were lucky enough to stay there for 6 nights so we could enjoy Sorrento and the Amalfi coast. The room was a nice, clean, modern design, very lovely and comfortable. Nice, private, attached bathroom, also very nice and clean. All decorations for a room (we stayed in the blue room) are coordinated to that theme color, including tile in the bathroom. Very refreshing change from a lot of older, heavier style Italianate furnishings. Breakfast was very filling, a change from the sometimes skimpy continental breakfast we were offered as we traveled. Not only did we get our meals, which included croissant filled or plain, and a basket of zwieback type toast and jellies, we also had made for us each day a "toast" which is sort of like a grilled cheese with or without something else; in our case ham. It made for a nice start to the day before venturing out. But what really made Emily Suites different as an accommodation was the owner Emilia and her assistant Anna who were delightful. Always helpful, they booked tours for us and arranged a last minute pizza-making class. When we had issues or needed help they were there for us. Anna was on duty until 8PM in the evenings so we always had someone to turn to morning to night. While we stayed there, another couple had a health issue requiring a hospital stay, and believe it or not, Emilia accompanied them to the hospital and stayed with them there overnight until all was resolved. Now that's what I call a personal, caring touch. I would not hesitate to stay again with Emilia and if we ever have the pleasure of returning to Sorrento, look forward to staying with her again. If you want something that's not a hotel, can't afford the "belle epoque" accomodations along the shore, but want a nice, comfortable place, with a wonderful host, at a reasonable cost, Emily Suites is the place for you! Thank you Emilia and Anna for the great stay! - Deanna and Stephen Kaufman

author: L4U
title: Emily went the extra mile to make our stay special...
text: Emily really goes beyond expectations to make your stay special. The place is a little hard to find (it's just next to the pharmacy and opposite the Esso garage) so make sure you take Emily's number so you can ask for help if you need it (she came to meet us outside). The rooms and clean and tidy and the shutters on the windows make for a wonderful nights sleep. Our room looked out across the lemon grove. Breakfast is served inside your room at a time you select. This is a wonderful idea and means you can have breakfast in peace in your pyjamas if you choose (more B&B's should do this). Our first morning in Emily Suites was my thirtieth birthday, and I was overwhelmed to find Emily had bought a birthday cake along with our breakfast. Such a thoughtful gesture (and delicious cake). Emily also arranged for dinner at a gorgeous restaurant in the hills for us (Vino Vero) which made the day truly special. There isn't someone always available in the apartments, but we did not find this a problem. Every morning Emily or one of her staff would greet us and ask if we needed anything. We left early in the morning on our last day, and Emily kindly packed us a breakfast the night before for the journey. The walk into town took us less than 10mins, which we found pleasant after gorging on wonderful Italian food. I would thoroughly recommend Emily Suites. It's not a swanky hotel, but the price you pay is not a swanky price. It's a comfortable and pleasant B&B made unique by the level of service offered by Emily. Hope to return one day....

author: 838emilyk
title: Exceeds Expectations!
text: We had a wonderful stay at Emily Suites. The B&B is a little bit of a hike from the center of town, but it's really not bad at all. In fact, you'll be glad you have a walk after eating all of the delicious food that Sorrento has to offer! The rooms are impeccably clean and really large for Italian hotel rooms. What my husband and I loved most were the black out shades on both the bedroom and bathroom window- it made it SO much easier to fall asleep. The absolute best part of this B&B is the hostess- Emilia. She is the warmest, kindest, most thoughtful person. She really wanted to make us feel as comfortable as possible and made sure we did not hesitate to ask for anything we needed. She really went above and beyond our expectations by driving us to the ferry station in Capri, as well as the train station to go to the airport. When you arrive at Emily Suites, Emilia will ask you what time you want breakfast and details on what you want to eat. It then comes delivered to your room on a beautiful tray and set up on a table for you to enjoy. Our breakfasts consisted of freshly picked strawberries, a banana, yogurt, biscuits and jams, delicious croissants, hot coffee, and juice. Compared to other breakfasts in Italy, this one is definitely much better. On the day that we were leaving and didn't have time to eat breakfast, Emilia packed up a to-go breakfast bag for us--so sweet of her. Overall, my husband and I truly had a magical vacation here in Sorrento, and we would 100% go back to Emily Suites!

author: goldseal1972
title: AWESOME HOSTESS!
text: Anyone who stays at this little family B&B would not be disappointed. I arrived about 1hr. late on the airport express bus and was very touched that Emilia returned to collect me from the station. Emilia is a very warm and friendly person she cares very much about her guests concerns and goes out of her way to ensure your stay is a comfortable and that you get the most out of your trip. On check in she enquired the time that best suites you for breakfast, recommends great place to visit and eat. Her assistant Maria is always happy and full of life...HATS OFF TO HER, she makes great coffee. I stayed 4nights and then went on to the Amalfi and when I returned Emilia drove me over to get the bus to the airport. Each morning Emilia shared with me something from her home, a lemon, mozzarella cheese (made by her boyfriend), it was always such a joy to interact with her and she is within easy reach via telephone. The B&B is within walking distance from everything Sorrento has to offer, even the marina to catch the ferry to Capri or any of the other places. The shopping in the area is great and plentiful with many cafes along the route. You don't have to worry if you have to go out at night as the area is safe and always busy. When you're in for the night you do not even know you're in a busy part of town as its so quiet and peaceful. In my opinion and without a doubt, the service received at Emily Suites is better than that received at the big hotels. I will never regret choosing this HEAVENLY little B&B and would certainly return. Thank you Emilia and Maria for taking care of me during my stay.

author: Indygirl50
title: Very Happy with this B&B !
text: I've traveled a lot internationally and I found this B&B to be terrific. It's tiny...only 4 rooms, but the owner Emilia puts a lot of personal touches into her establishment. Talk about service....she picked me up from the train station! She then shuttled me to & fro the station when I went on my Pompei excursion. She's bright, she's cheery, she's full of great tips and information. She made me feel right at home. I had the Blue room. It was plenty spacious, as was the bathroom. Clean too! I appreciated the little frig, and hot water maker for tea. There's free wifi ...oh, and a laundry mat next door. (It's pricey...cost me 10 euros to do a load. But I needed my traveling clothes washed...so oh well! )The Suites are on the 3rd floor...thankfully there was a elevator! Within walking distance are plenty of restaurants and shops. I'll stay here again. Emilia is wonderful proprietor!

author: Pinklady0214
title: Trusted
text: We were welcomed by Nino and his wife as we arrived. He explained every detail about the room and provided us the city map. The room was the one of the biggest one within our stay in Italy. They had Kettle, hairdryer, safe box and wifi etc. in the room. The amazing thing was the intercom on the ground floor could connect to Nino's mobile. We didn't need to worry about there's no 24hour reception. We were running out of hot water for shower in the morning. Nino could solve the problem so efficiently. Nino drove us for free to catch the boat to Capri. He even waited for us in the car until he knew we had our boat tickets to Capri since we were quite late at that time. After checking out, he drove us to train station. He asked us about our next destination and reminded us to get off one stop earlier which was so important to us. They took care of us in the last second. I could feel how much effort they put to run Emily suites. I felt so warm and grateful to stay in Emily suites.

author: katie0688
title: Spotless, good breakfast, lovely staff. Excellent restaurant Il Ritrovo two blocks away
text: Stayed here with my partner for 5 nights in April. We stayed in the turquoise room which was really big and had all of the facilities that we needed. The wi-fi was excellent and very fast and the fridge and kettle were also well used and very handy to have. I was really pleased that there was a full length mirror in the wardrobe and a large mirror in the bathroom. As with all hotels and b+bs that we have stayed at I found that there were not enough coat hangers in the wardrobe but this was not a major problem and this was one of only two things that I could possibly complain about. The only other issue was with the hot water supply, this was limited as the rooms run off a tank. I found this slightly difficult as I have long hair and my partner wet shaves every day so we had to try and conserve hot water otherwise there was not enough for both of us to have showers, me to wash my hair and him to have a shave. These were two minor niggles and did not cause us any discomfort and overall they in no way affected our experience of Emily Suites. The best thing about Emily Suites was the staff, Emilia, the owner was absolutely lovely. She spoke excellent English and went out of her way to resolve our hot water issue and give us information about the area and the transport options to the airport. Emilia’s father was also lovely, he offered us free lifts down to the port and our day of departure offered to drive us to the station with our luggage. He also very kindly gave us a bag of huge lemons to take home with us. The cleaning lady was wonderful, she made lovely breakfasts which were very substantial, it varied each day which was much appreciated, we received a platter of fruit on our first morning, strawberry cocktails on another and a selection of meat and cheese on another. She went out of her way to accommodate our plans and was really friendly.
