She thoroughly cleaned the room everyday to an excellent standard – cleanliness is really important to both of us and so we were extremely happy and satisfied with the standard at Emily Suites. We would definitely stay here again if we return to Sorrento. I booked our trip to Italy as a present for my partners 50th and was really pleased with my choice of accommodation, it really added to what was an excellent holiday.

author: pempya
title: Don’t waste your money
text: My girlfriend and I arrived to Smart Hotel a little late (around midnight) due to flight delays. We checked in normally and everything seemed to be okay. The problem began when the concierge told us we are in room 100 and he would show us to our room but did not give us a key. We had two large suitcases and a few carry on pieces with us and the employee told us to climb the stairs expecting us to carry all of these items with ease up a narrow staircase. After getting a few steps up we asked for an elevator and the employee did not seem very pleased that we were being an inconvenience to him. We got in the elevator and went to floor #1 since our room was #100. After waiting 2 minutes to find out where the concierge went, my girlfriend went a floor down to look for him where she was getting YELLED at by the conceirge for going to the wrong floor. Turns out our room was on a floor where the elevator doesn’t even go, it did not even have a room number and it was right beside the main breakfast buffet (which gets very loud around 8am). We tried to talk to the conceirge to get us a different room as the room was not at all what we had paid for; however, he continued to be frustrated with the situation and told us that we got a good deal since it’s a three person room and there’s two of us. Needless to say the first impression on the hotel was terrible and ruined our first night in Milan. We talked to a lady at the conceirge desk the next morning and she was very understanding of the situation and apologized to us about the employee during our check in as this seems to be a frequent problem with that employee. She upgraded our room and gave us a 20% drink coupon for the inconvience. The next room we got was defintely an upgrade except for the shower. The shower head in the shower comes off as soon as you turn the shower on and it floods the whole washroom since there is only one piece of glass on the shower. Again, we went to the front desk 3 times to ask for someone to clean the floors or to give us some more towels so we can place them down but he was not willing to help out in the slightest. The water ended up leaking into the main room and we had to just try and walk around it to not make any more mess until it either dried up or leaked through the floors by the morning. Overall, the experience was very bad and was more stressful than enjoyable. There are other places in the same area for a much better value.

author: tt03xz
title: WORST Hotel Experience EVER!!!!!!! 29/12/2017 - 02/01/2018
text: My gf and I booked a 4 night in a “1 KING Room” over the new year period (which wasn’t cheap btw) Only to find it's the SMALLEST room I have ever been in. As for the so called King Bed… it was 2 SEPARATE single beds they pushed together. I went down to speak to the receptionist (one particularly RUDE, arrogant old lady) who kept saying that the bed was a king size bed frame with 2 single mattresses on it and that the entire hotel is like that and so there is nothing she can do about it...that as long as the frame is King size then that's what they advertised and that's what we got !!! (That was a lie btw, as the bed FRAME was 2 singles beds…which kept separating themselves as you lay on them - you can almost fall through - we hadto keep waking up and pushing them back together!). I pointed this out to her and she effectively called me a liar, saying the frame itself was 1 solid king bed frame… even though I have pictures to prove otherwise – which she refused to look) The middle bit where the 2 single beds meet is sooo RIGID and HARD it’s actually PAINFUL to lay on it. So my GF & I ended up being forced to sleep separately on the single beds. If we wanted to sleep separately we would have booked 2 single beds!!!! This lady didn’t seem to understand that or simply didnt want to. While we were arguing with her about this... ANOTHER COUPLE came down with the same issue (they had booked a DOUBLE ROOM – but ended up with 2 singles as well (like the lady said the entire hotel is like this) – She dismissed them completely and they were saying they were not getting what they paid for..nor value for their money which is true but this rude arrogant lady didn’t seem to care. So I asked her WHY they advertised “1 King Bed” room if in fact it’s 2 singles pushed together and pointed out that if we knew beforehand we wouldnt have booked. She blatantly said and I quote “we don’t have to specify that on the website” I said maybe it’s cos you know people would NOT pay a lot of money for a King if they knew they would end up with 2 singles? She kept repeating “we don’t have to specify that”… “we don’t have to put it on the website”...dismissing us as if we were wasting our time - we're talking over a THOUSAND pounds here we want value for money!!!! It was like arguing with a wall, so we left it at that …my GF and I were fuming …they almost ruined our new year but we chose to look past it. Apart from that..the walls are so THIN you can hear noises from the next room and corridor - 1 night we woke up in a shock cos a loud bang from the next room, it was like the wall was falling on us. One thing is for sure .. I WOULD NOT RECOMMEND THIS PLACE TO MY WORSE ENEMY!!!! – DO NOT GO THERE!!!!

author: italynotes
title: Absolute worst hotel experience!
text: We booked a double room with a queensize bed (151-180cm on Booking.com). This is what we got: - A 100cm, or maybe 120cm bed (see photos). That’s definitely not a queensize bed. Not even a bed for two persons.. We went downstairs to ask if they accidentally gave us the wrong room, but no. According to the man behind the counter these are the standard rooms for two persons. - The bathroom was a nightmare as well. In the sink there was dirty, smelly water. It seemed that the (lever of the) drain was stuck because there was no possibility to flush the water. Nothing was done about it. There were also no excuses for the horrible smell. The toilet is situated inside the shower. This means that, unless you want wet clothes/shoes, the toilet cannot be used for a while after you’ve taken a shower (see photos). When we called Booking.com about this situation we were lucky to get an additional one person room to solve the ‘bed-problem’. Unfortunately the hotel didn’t offer this themselves and a one hour phone call with Booking.com was necessary. In the past years I’ve slept at multiple hotels in Milano. My advice is to stay away from this one. Don’t get fooled by the hotels (wide angle lens photo’s) and enjoy your stay in another hotel :)

author: elavrushina
title: Horrible!
text: To start with I was given a single room even though booked Double for Single use just because I did not want the small single. So the key word is double. This is the type of room one books. Not for the hotel though. If you book single use, you get a single. The receptionist tried to convince me that it was a double. The bed is 1 meter wide! The official site says double bed is 131-150. (So again, this is a single). It is not a double and the room itself does not even show on any of the hotel´s official photos. He tried to tell me they do sell those for couples! And since I was "single use" this is what I get. The toilet is in the shower, literally! And the shower itslef has not seen a cleaner since the renovation. Absolutely disgusting. Yet, "no, we do not have more rooms available tonigh"t, and you are "single use", "you can try to change, tomorrow but you wil get the same answer". The booking was for a double and it does not matter what use I am. Plus, Do not recommend at all.

author: headshot6868
title: Boutique
text: When booking a hotel in Milan, we wanted to be close to the Central train station. This place is 5 minutes walk. Easy peasy. We arrived early and had to leave our bags. no problem. About a 25 minute walk to the tourist sightsee spots. not bad. I think there was a Metro station a block away as well. When we got back, we checked in no problem. The room was clean, modern. The only negative thing was the shower. It had no enclosure. Europeans and American shower differently, I get it. Not a bad thing. Just cultural differences. So if you're the type who likes to get in the shower and splash water about yourself. You're in for a flooded bathroom! Complimentary breakfast in the morning was plentiful. Grazie!

author: loganmountstewart
title: Filthy room
text: Possibly the worst hotel I have stayed in for a decade. Our aircraft, which was scheduled to land in Pisa, had to make a diversion to Milan airport. On arrival, we wanted to find an inexpensive yet clean and safe place to spend one night before travelling the next day. We booked the hotel online about an hour before we arrived at about midnight. We checked into a triple room which was situated on the top floor. The check in was brusque but efficient. The room was frankly disgusting. There were splashes either of blood or nail varnish on the headboard; the pillow cases were stained; the sheets were well worn and felt grubby. The beds were uncomfortable and the room generally dirty throughout. There were holes in the plaster board walls for crying out loud! What on earth are these people peddling? The room was roughly Euro 150 so it’s not like we paid for a Bangkok style hostel hovel. Quite incredibly all the toiletries in the bathroom had been USED. The only positive thing I can say about this hotel is that it is very close to the train station. That’s it. I ended up vomiting all night (not, I might add, because of the room but because of a stomach bug) and so didn’t have the energy to demand a change my friends equally didn’t have the strength to deal with the matter. In hindsight, we should have demanded a change of room. I honestly cannot believe that this hotel has not been investigated by the Milan tourist board. The reviews on other sites (including those used to book rooms which we reviewed) misrepresent this hotel as do the photographs.

author: JaymePollock
title: Great Hotel and Location, Just Watch Out for the Showers!
text: GREAT location. I cannot stress this enough. To have a hotel so conveniently located to the train station is wonderful. The facilities were very clean and modern. Though the rooms are small like most European hotels, it felt like there was a good amount of space. Great breakfast options too! My friend and I loved how fresh everything was. Staff was polite as well. The one downside however had to do with the shower facilities. I know that the bathrooms are smaller in Europe, and though ours was a good size, the shower was very tiny. We didn't initially think this was a problem until after my friend got out of the shower--it had flooded unlike anything I've ever seen before! The entire bathroom was soaked and so was the entry way into the room. Luckily, the staff was super attentive and helpful--they came mop in hand to clean it up. We really appreciated their quickness to resolve the issue however, we were too wary to take another shower afterwards. Overall, if you are traveling and need a clean hotel with great access to the train station--this is your place!

author: wave_babe210
title: ...or Nah?
text: Needed a room just for one night, literally just needed a place to sleep and this was one of the few hotels available this evening in the location I was looking for. A skip away from Milano Centrale. I checked in after a work day at around 18:00. First thing I noticed was that the front entrance didn't have a ramp for luggage or accessible persons. No bell man or greeter either. Fine for me because I just had a small carry-on trolly but might be an important missing feature for some guests. Lobby looks decent and the welcome staff was friendly at check in but afterwards didn't bat an eye except for the intern at check out who was professional. The elevator is miniscule and the floors are dark. There is no double lock on the room door so for safety reasons I had to barricade the door with my luggage. The bathroom window didn't have a sufficient drape or light blockage. You couldn't take a shower in the evening without being on full display to the neighbouring building and all their guests....I actually showered in the dark! The shower leaked water all over the floor and was uneven. The bed was decent and I slept well but the room was very dingy. The breakfast wasn't appetising and I didn't try much for fear I might 'pay for it later'..If you know what I mean. Our rate wasn't cheap either. We paid 300€ for one night. I would suggest paying even 100€ more for a better hotel. Location was great and it served it's purpose but I would not go back.

author: ChristinaD350
title: Decent Hotel
text: I stayed at Idea Hotel for 3 nights in a double bed room. The hotel is within walking distance of Milian's Central Train Station. About a 30 minute walk from Duomo Square. The property is within walking distance to shops, small grocery store and restaurants. The lobby is very nice but the breakfast buffet is limited and does not include include eggs like mentioned on their website. All items are served at room temperature. The room included a mini-fridge, safe and tv with English channels. The walls are not soundproof, I heard other guests through walls, ceiling and door. The bathroom was very small, especially the shower, the water will splash everywhere. The hairdryer can only blow air for about a couple minutes, then shuts off. In about 5 minutes the hair dryer "recharges" and will blow again. This routine continues. The lighting in the bathroom is also very poor, almost in the dark. The one item that is most important to me is WiFi. I would consider the connection poor. The WiFi was slow and continuously disconnect, I had to sign-in over and over again. The front desk told me the password would work on two devices and that was false. If you are low-maintenance I would recommend this hotel for you.

author: 579darrenl
title: Great location... that is all
text: We stayed here in September, due to the superb access for Centrale Train Station. We arrived on Friday and left on the Monday evening, using the hotel as a base whilst we went to the Italian F1 GP. This hotel had some staff that cared and others less so. The reception staff were courteous and helpful, however the breakfast/food staff were beyond grumpy... and that's coming from an Englishman. Not once did they smile, help or refrain from mopping around our feet as we ate what can best be described as 'a breakfast you'd expect in economy at 30,000 feet'. I guess it was partly the drink from the night before, but we couldn't stop laughing. I've travelled to a number of European countries, but this took the biscuit/really dry continental pastries. After the culinary 'double dare' of breakfast, we found ourselves bloody hungry and awaiting a packed train journey to the race... awesome! Our room too, bore evidence of the lack lustre approach we were coming to expect by the 3rd hour in. Pushing the button for the toilet, for example, ended up with my arm halfway through the wall and into a remarkably spacious cavity behind the cistern. I appreciate this is perhaps what some people might seek when booking a hotel, but i was on this trip to get away from home maintenance and light repair. Value? well it's fairly cheap i guess and it is located close to the station. I would recommend it for GP goers that's for sure, just be prepared to have breakfast elsewhere. As with all things, it's only as big a deal as you want to make it. Joking aside, We are lucky to go to such places and get a roof over our heads.

author: Naaone
title: Definitely not a great Idea!
text: We booked to stay here for 2 nights as we were taking the train and travelling across Italy. As soon as we stepped into the hotel we knew right away what a big mistake we made. Although the entrance and first floor was well decked out, the service or lack of service you got at reception was beyond horrible. Receptionist was not friendly, she doesn't even look at you when she is checking you in, doesn't explain anything feels like she doesn't want to be there herself. Upon checking into our room we discovered that the bin was not emptied from the previous guest. We had also noticed that the bathroom lights were not as bright. We called reception right away to tell them that the bin was not empty and that if someone could check the lights in our room. The receptionist sent someone up to our room that did not speak much english. She had a look at our room and our bin and did not say much. She then called reception they exchanged a few words and then handed the phone over to us. We were told nothing can be done for the lights and that she will send someone up to change the rubbish bin for us. 4 hours later when we came back to our hotel room the bin had not been touched. The next day after we got our room cleaned we noticed that our mini fridge had a new chocolate bar placed in it, we realised it was the same chocolate bar that was in the bin when we checked in. When checking out Idea hotel tried to charge us for it and that was when we pointed out that our bin was not emptied and that the chocolate bar was already in the bin when we checked in, it was obviously eaten by the previous guest and was not properly charged for. We also continue to put through a complaint (as nice as possible as we also understood that it was not the young gentlemen's fault) that service had been poor and that upon checking in it would be nice to have been explained about the city tax, breakfast or anything at all about the hotel! The hotel does not provide free wifi. They charge you 7euros for 24 hours per device. For a hotel that does not have much going for them, charging wifi is ridicules. Only good thing I can say was that breakfast was decent. Do yourself a favour and don't ruin your trip by staying here.

author: purplesteffi
title: Excellent location and sleep quality!
text: The third stop on our northern Italy adventure was Milan and the Idea Centrale. We booked it the day before and took advantage of a very good "last minute" price, one of the best in Milan, which isn't cheap generally! When we got there we found it very easily, close to the main railway station. We found the reception staff here to be very friendly and helpful. It transpired that the reason for our good price was partly down to the fact that booking.com (with whom we'd booked the room) had listed our room as a double when in fact it was a "double for one person". The lady on reception told us that this had happened several times and they honoured the booking. The double height entrance lobby is modern and stylish and the room was also attractively decorated. The big room numbers on each floor were a nice touch! The room was very small, probably the smallest we've stayed in, but still perfectly adequate. The bathroom has the toilet in the shower cubicle which saves space and was well stocked with toiletries. One negative point though was a substantial amount of pigeon droppings around the window. The breakfast was fine. There was a free, code operated safe in the room. The staff kindly looked after our bags after check-out. Possibly our main annoyance here was the cost of using the Wi-Fi at 7€ for 24 hours. Even then you can only use it on one device! Overall, we thought it did the job at a good price, even though it's in a busy area and our room fronted onto the street, the sleep quality was excellent. We would stay again and recommend the Idea Centrale.

author: m-town2185
title: small and noisy
text: three times i've been there. hope last time. first two where ok. but now. room was very very very small (room 205 if i remember correctly) just above the entrance. toilet INSIDE the shower. litterly inside the shower. my shoulders where touching both walls when i wanted to view the mirror (i'm 1,76m and 80 kg) you have to stand sideways to brunch your teeth and drink some water. because room was so small i had to unplug the minibar otherwise it was inpossible to sleep (the light from the minibar where to bright in your face) when you opened a window, to much noise from the street. when you close the window, to much noise from airco inside the room. and i could not change the temperature myself. so it was way to hot in the room. i've been here 3 times. rooms where getting from really big, to really small. close to metro 1 min walk so that is nice.

author: Ora90210
title: Awful room (or closet), rude staff, ok breakfast, SKY satellite TV nice
text: This hotel is close to Milano Centrale, that's the only good thing! The staff was so rude at check in! I specifically asked for a bigger room, and she cut me off and insisted that I have on of the bigger rooms in the hotel. My room was a closet! I would imagine that most Americans (unfortunately to say because many are obese), would have trouble actually physically fitting into the bathroom. I'm a 5'5'', 130lbs woman, and as I would wash my hands in the sink, my shoulders were touching both walls, that's how small the sink is! And the other interesting thing that I've NEVER seen before if that toilet was in the shower!! AWFUL!! The breakfast was ok. The only good thing is its near Milano Centrale, I would advise to get a day metro card (5€), because Milan is a huge city, so I wouldn't advise walking to the city center, its much easier to take the metro. I never waited longer than 3 min for any train, and I felt safe in all the metro stations. They also have satellite TV SKY, which is nice... but definitely did not make up for the room! Another negative was that there was a loud humming, buzzing sound that went on constantly, I thought it might be the elevator, but when I opened my room door and went into the hallway to listen, it would go away! It made it very difficult to sleep!

author: MarcoDLS
title: Good hotel, shady area
text: We had a one and a half day stay in Milan before going to Rome. We enjoyed Milano Centrale hotel. One of the front desk attendants, Ursula, goes above and beyond what Ive seen in any other italian hotel. Her hospitality and eagerness to help is a without equal. She is an assest to any hotel, she even hugged us goodbye. The hotel itself is very chic and modern. Everything looks pretty much new. The room was perfect with modern touches and a comfortable bed. The shower had plenty of hot water. The breakfast was the best yet. However...........the area is pretty shady. Its only steps from the train station. You can walk there in about 30 seconds. The area right before the street looks like an abondoned bank (or something) and has about 3-5 homeless persons living there with mattresses and all. About 30 yards from the hotel entrance. The entrance itself however looks safe. The shady area smells of urine. So basically.....the hotel is nice and chic. Nice room and bed. Roberta and especially Ursula were very nice, but areas nearby kinda shady.

author: R0shanna
title: Close to Milano Centrale, quiet and functional!
text: Ok, my first impact with concierge was brusk but afterwards very accommodating. You need something, you get service rapidly. I liked that, same regarding taxis, they suggested calling only when you need it or you get tapped for an extra chunk of change. Good advice. Helpful. Room was quiet and clean. Too bad it is so small but it works. Watch the toilet push, gentle hands only or it goes through the wall. Happened to me but it is a. Easy repair a d a good chuckle! Not a problem. Great restaurant suggestion nearby, Mamma Rose. Yum. Perfect transition neighborhood, you are safe. There is a supermarket nearby if you prefer to eat in. Breakfast okay, nothing memorable.

author: SenLee
title: Basic but good
text: We made a brief stopover in Milan, thus we have selected this hotel which situated very near to the main train station. It is a mere 5 minutes walk away. We were also happy to find that the Swiss Railway (SBB) ticket office is right opposite the hotel, exactly where we need to go too. As we know, this hotel was recently renovated and refurbished. We booked the hotel very much earlier plus they've got the renovation works going on that time, hence we got it at a really good rate i.e. EUR58 for a night inclusive of breakfast. The interior is modern. The check-in process was quick, front desk staff speaks fluent English and very helpful. She gave us maps and showed us where to visit, shop and eat. Wifi is chargeable. Yes, the room is small but clean. Tiled floor. Small bed but comfortable. Bathroom is clean with adequate supplies. But the shower design is not practical. Same as mentioned by other travelers, we experienced the same flooding problems. Breakfast is good, buffet style with fair variety. Alternatively, the restaurant next to the hotel (Fashion 2 Pizzeria) serves delicious food at reasonable price.

author: BradfordAgent
title: Good stay but could do a bit better!
text: Stayed here for a 1 night stay. This is by far not the worse hotel I have stayed in and I would stay here again. It just could do so much more of the smaller things and probably gain an extra star. The hotel is near the central station. The staff were friendly. Our room was on the 5th floor. The overall hotel is very modern. When we got to the room the door was very stiff and you had to bang it to open/close. The rooms are very modern and were clean. Just a few small things, the towel rail had fallen off - easily put back on the wall but probably with the banging from the door. The safe was not fastened down at all, could walk out with it. The shower flooeded from the bottom out, the soap dish was "no more nailed" to the wall, the tv had bad reception even though it was SKY and went off a few times. Apart from that (dont be too put off) the beds were comfy, rooms soundproof, modern and clean. The breakfast had a large choice of things and was good enough. As I said before I would stay here again but just attention to detail needs adding!

author: Dave_Ball2007
title: OK for the price, shame the rooms don't reflect the reception
text: Located close to the main station, area is quiet nice with decent restaurants and bars close by. Reception staff helfpul and friendly and the public lounge very nice, however no bar or restaurant in the hotel, but there is an Continental Shop opposite where you can buy alcoholic and soft drinks, snacks etc. The mini bar is very limited - so buy your own. No parking - on the next street and the cost is €24 per 24hrs. Room was very small for two people, just about ok for one person really. Only two sheets on the bed, no duvet, beds a bit hard and only one pillow so not the best. Air con is managed centrally which means you have to call reception to turn it on or off. Decor a little plan, plasma on the wall with all the sky TV's. Limited storage space for hanging clothes. Rooms cleanish. Safe in room, but pointless as it is not attached to anything and you can just pick it up. Bathroom nice with walkin shower, but again quiet small but rooms do vary in size as do the bathrooms. They had a tendancy to ration the toilet paper, which was cheap and brown! Does have toiletries though. Breakfast was uninspiringly dull. Generally OK, nothing special, ok for one person for a short stay, but definately better options of places to stay.

author: julia499496
title: What a shock
text: we arrived 11.30 am on 14th feb to find a building site. we climbed over the rubble through scaffold etc. to find the reception. We were met by exceptionally freindly and apolegetic staff. They guaranteed the hotel would be completed by that evening as not just ourselves were booked here but many Tottenham supporters. The area manager then kindly took us for coffee. Later that day we returned to find vast improvements although the builders were still with us.. The reception area was bright and modern. our room although at this point not completely furnished was clean with a very comfortable bed and a large bathroom. The restaurant just serving breakfast was sleek and modern. The food on offer ranged from cereals, fresh fruit, cooked breakfast cold meats and cheeses. Along with a large selection of very excellent freshly baked cakes. The location of the hotel is perfect for a visit to Milan just 200 hundred metres from th e main station where the airport buses stop. The metro staion is just outside the hotel door with just a couple of stops to the Duomo or if you prefer a 15 minute walk to the centre. There are plenty of bars and restaurants in the surrounding area We enjoyed our stay and felt it was good value for money. We say well done to all for completing the hotel and thank the staff for their help and hospitality. As a result of this stay we booked another night at the Idea Hotel at malpensa airport which was equally as good.

author: withacy
title: Stay here to relax and enjoy the island
text: My husband and I stayed at San Juan de la Isla over Christmas and it was a beautiful place to enjoy the holiday. The staff is super friendly, speak great English and are very responsive. This is the kind of place you will love if you are looking for a relaxing vacation right in the middle of natural beauty. If you are looking to go in and out of town a lot, you may feel a bit secluded. We stayed in one of the cabins on the lake. It was clean, quiet, nicely decorated and had hot water in the private bathroom. The wind is intense though, and we heard it throughout the night - but that's what makes this place special! We brought a mosquito net with us and I would recommend you do the same if you are sensitive to bugs. You are in nature, so there will be bugs. We ate the majority of our meals here and we enjoyed it. The food is pretty good and while a bit higher priced than in other areas, it's fresher and healthier for sure - worth the money. We took advantage of the bikes they rent (really good quality bikes) and we rode out to see some of the towns, beaches and to take a dip in Ojo de Agua. It was a great way to see other parts of the island. Oh! And we saw monkeys right outside our window one morning. It was such a treat. Thank you to the staff for a wonderful place to spend Christmas.

author: Rrupandaway
title: Love this place
text: You will say "wow" the second you arrive. Stayed only 2 nights. Wish it had been more. Log cabin right on the beach. Great view from bed. Staff were amazing and helpful and friendly and thankfully for us spoke good English. There are chairs and umbrellas on the beach to use or 20 or so hammocks to lie in. So beautiful and comfortable. I happily fell asleep in one in the afternoon reading my book. It's a place to stop and unwind. They helped us choose what to do and we chose to go to the nearby fresh water pool and have an amazing swim. They can drive you there and back. Love this place. Bed is on the harder side but it's fine. You can leave doors open at night (fly screen shut and locked) but the breeze is amazing. Out of bed and in about 20 steps you're in the fresh water of the lake. Food is great and good prices. I want to go back. We've moved to another place on the pacific coast but wish we had stayed there longer.

author: EddieDean99
title: Decent restaurant, poor hotel experience.
text: Maybe we arrived at a bad time (Dec 1), but we did not have a great experience. The hotel only had maybe 6 guests and most of us were bunked in a back bungalow. Even knowing they were there, we rarely saw anyone. The first day was earily devoid of any other people other than the at the restaurant. We had hot water the first night we arrived and then not again. The whole farm was overrun with noseeum type bugs. Harmless, but overwhelming nonetheless. The beach area was dirty with garbage and dead fish. The restaurant was good, but a bit pricey compared to similar restaurants in the island. The rooms were sealed with screens over the window, but on our second night, I found a spider the size of my palm on the bathroom floor. Usually I am fine with spiders, but I was shocked at how something so big could get into a supposedly sealed room. I killed the foul beast and had an uneasy sleep as the power cycled on and off through the early hours of the morning. The desk man let us pay and leave a day early with no qualms. He apologized as best he could, while not fully relating to why we were so upset. Overall, the hotel is overpriced for the facilities it offers and for the relative remoteness of its location. Being 3km off the main road, when a ride costs $20 (no matter the destination), is not feasible without your own vehicle.

author: TravelWithAnn
title: Tranquility at its absolute best...
text: A Nicaraguan friend had referred me to Finca San Juan de la Isla. Her opening words, "It's just so peaceful." And that it is. We walked along the beach, explored the grounds, and relaxed. The refreshing lake breezes were perfect. Along with two colleagues/friends, I was on Ometepe for the first time to explore the island, look at some lodging options, and assess if all would be suitable for an annual women's trip that I lead each year. Within a few hours of arriving at this lodge, viewing the volcano, and watching the shore birds play, I knew that I was at a very special place.... I have only one piece of constructive criticism. When we were at the lodge, it was at just about full occupancy. Dinner service was quite slow as there were not enough people servicing the dining area. Simultaneously, since many people arrived at the lodge at about the same time, Daniel, the wonderful man in charge of greeting and orienting the guests, etc., was pulled in way too many directions at the same time. He was always smiling and incredibly helpful and gracious, but I think it would have been easier for him and also for the guests if he and the restaurant had had some additional assistance during this peak period. I hope this issue of insufficient staffing was a one evening "anomaly". If not, I hope the lodge will consider my suggestion. One more word about Daniel-- he gave us a wonderful tour of the lodging and grounds. It was very helpful and contributed to my decision to return to Finca San Juan de la Isla in the future!

author: 697elizabethm
title: Amazing volcano views
text: This resort was everything we were hoping for. We checked in after dark, so we couldn't see much of the resort, we walked to dinner and we're delighted to find a play area for children set up near a few tables. Our party was myself, my husband, our four children, and my brother in law with his girlfriend. Our meal that night was perfect! I had the refried black bean appetizer, and it was incredible, and the guys raved about their steaks. Even though we were exhausted after a long day and a late dinner we just couldn't pull ourselves away from that patio! We sat for hours, talking and enjoying the warm breeze coming off the lake, and the sounds of the wildlife. That night we ran into an issue with our room, and the next morning we were moved to a very large cabana with the most amazing volcano view. There was a kitchen, beautiful living area and very large bedroom. This is the room to book! We spent our couple days here walking the beach and swimming, but mostly we just relaxed and enjoyed the gorgeous Finca. And eating! We ate so much! Everything was incredible, each meal better than the last. I'm still fantasizing about all the plantains. If you are looking for a quiet destination, one that is a true escape from the norm, this is your spot.

author: BetuliaEriksson
title: By the lake and right after the banan plantation
text: Ometepe island is a beautiful place to visit. Stayed at the San Juan de la Isla. Some of us were given small rooms and some of us were given huge rooms. But that was totally fine since we were inside very little of the time we were there. We enjoyed the garden, the beach and the common areas. We enjoyed talking to Juanito and Douglas. The rest of the staff was just as friendly, wonderful and helpful. The brise was always blowing lukewarm and everything was bathed in light of the full moon. The food was good. Breakfast is always a la carte, which was weird but doable anyway. We shared drinks at the bar overlooking the lake and never tired of looking at the fantastic sculptures done by the locals and for sale at the common area. Our room was number 11 which is a real beauty. Prefect place to relax . Not easy to find since it is hidden between banana plantations and milking cows. Loved it all around. Worth a visit.

author: RosEngland
title: Check your room
text: We were part of a group and so we had a look at most of the different types of room. Unfortunately we were given the smallest room- think it was room 7. We were very disappointed. It was dark and the bathroom was tiny. Having seen the other rooms, we asked to be moved. We moved to room 6 which was much better. The block of rooms had a very sunny veranda at the back with a view of the volcano. The room was fine as was the bathroom. We had plenty of hot water and a decent shower. We did sneak a look at the bungalows which looked a notch up- especially the bathroom. The waterfront bungalows were lovely with a really nice bathroom. They also had a fridge and coffee maker. Luck of the draw! The hotel is set in a banana plantation and we really enjoyed it. We walked the beach to the next village and had lunch at a hotel there. We went in January and there were a lot of annoying non biting midges in various places but it didn't spoil our enjoyment. The common areas were lovely- with games and books etc.

author: 572ritaz
title: Nice place, lousy service
text: We chose Finca San Juan de la Isla based on the experience of friends. We were very pleased with the accommodations. And if you come with your own car and/or driver, you'll probably be OK. Unfortunately we did not. We came by cab and expected to use cabs to get around. Alas the hostess - the only person on the grounds who spoke English -- made it virtually impossible to get off the grounds without hiring the hotel's in-house driver. (No English.) She would not even call a cab for us when it was time to leave. We were very put off the night before it was time to leave -- at about 7 p.m. -- when we asked if she would arrange for a cab to pick us up at 8 a.m. the next day. Her response: "That's kind of short notice." It was short notice for her because then she had to find an in-house driver. We made it clear we intended for her to simply place a call to a cab company, but she refused. Before that unpleasant encounter, we had accepted her offer of a day-long tour of the island for $90. We didn't know that our "guide" wouldn't speak English. And part of the tour included a trip to a coffee plantation -- where no one spoke English, so that was a total waste. Another reason to have a car: breakfast is included but you'll want to eat your dinner elsewhere...

author: 158caseyj
title: Acceptable Stay on Ometepe
text: Unless you choose to stay at a hostel, you don't have many hotel options on the island, so I booked this since it appeared to be somewhat decent. You will need a taxi/motorbike to get here. No one was at reception to check us in so we asked some Americans if they knew where to go, and one individual turned out to be the owner. He was very polite and talkative, and we were shown our room. There are private, lakefront rooms or apartment-style rooms, with an open-air common area and "kitchen", along with hammocks. We had an apartment type room, and it was basic. About 10' x 10' and the bathroom had no toiletries. Wi-Fi was only available in the restaurant. We were near a marsh-type area so bugs (harmless) and birds were abundant (they were somewhat loud all through the night). The owner let us use the jet-skis for a short time free of charge which was nice. The restaurant food was pretty good although the almond cake was a bit old/dry. The beach view is nice but not much shore, and the bugs were so overwhelming it was difficult to enjoy being outdoors (obviously not the hotel's fault, but rather its proximity to the water/vegetation). Hotels.com also lists a coffee/tea maker in-room but after I inquired about it, I was told there weren't any available. Overall, the stay was acceptable, but not a place I'd stay again or recommend. My volcano tour guide mentioned he had a place he rents out, so I would look into that before booking this hotel.

author: Marcela79
title: Inconsistent Quality
text: We were looking forward to our two-night stay at the Finca San Juan de la Isla; its website surely makes it look like a very nice place. In reality, only some parts of it are nice. We booked a standard room with a volcano view. When we arrived, we were severely disappointed at the room: * It was barely cleaned, and sparsely decorated. * The bed and its linens were old and dingy. * The windows had no glass, meaning the room's titular view could only enjoyed if the room was kept uncomfortably hot. * The bathroom did not seem clean, and was appointed with plain and mismatched bathroom fixtures. * The bathroom had a weird door to the outside hall; we were not able to figure out its purpose. * The shower was not cleaned properly; we wore flip flops to shower. * The bathroom windows only had wooden slats that did not close, compromising the room's ability to get cooled by the A/C unit mounted on the room's wall. Others in our party booked the lake front cabins. The quality of those cabins compared to the standard room was like night and day. The cabins not only were bigger and had more amenities (which was expected), but the overall quality of the bed, linens, and bathroom (nice fixtures, slate floors, actual glass on the windows), highlighted the difference between the cabins and the standard rooms. By comparison, the standard rooms gave the impression of having been former staff quarters haphazardly changed into guest rooms. The rest of the hotel is nice enough, with great views. The staff at the restaurant evidently works hard to please the guests. It's worth noting that meals (except breakfast) are not included even thought there are little to no competing options for meals around the property. All in all, our stay would have been much better if the standard rooms were of the same quality as the more expensive rooms. The baseline quality should be the same across rooms, more expensive rooms should simply be larger and/or with more amenities.

author: Likewater4chocolate
title: Lovely Getaway on beautiful Ometepe Island
text: Finca San Juan de la Isla is located on a quiet serene spot right on the shore of Lake Nicaragua. My room was quite comfortable and the grounds were lovely. Staff were kind and accommodating. Food was lovely. I met the owner who was very friendly and welcoming. There were two highlights for me: I swam in Lake Nicaragua for the first time. Delicious! My first evening there I had an Avatar type of experience. I had forgotten about the fireflies (we do not have them in the Northwest). When the sun went down, the grounds and grass were lit up by the luminescent insect life like miniatures flares everywhere! Then a thunderstorm rolled in with lightening and thunder on side of the sky and the moon was rising on the other side of the sky. Fireflies lit up the beach at the same time. It was magic! I highly recommend this modestly priced hotel. You won't regret it!

author: efatzergarcia
title: Wonderful Finca San Juan !!!!
text: We splurged in this place and it was worth every penny. Finca San Juan de la Isla is a Plantain Plantation and lies on the east side of Ometepe directly on Lake Nicaragua with a superb view of Volcano Concepcion. A lovelier spot would be hard to imagine! Excellent accommodation with either lake - or volcano view. The 3 of us choose a cabin with volcano view. It had a large bedroom, 2 very comfy queen size beds, separate living room, kitchenette, dinette, huge bathroom, hot shower, this is a winner! I can not forget to mention the lovely porch where we spent many hrs. early in the morning and evening listening to the birds, howler monkeys, cicadas, admiring Concepcion sometimes shrouded in clouds other times reviling its beautiful classic shape. Meals are served depending on the breeze from the lake in an open Veranda or in the bar area. The food is delicious, no matter what you order. Ernesto, the chef surprised us on two evenings with a typical Nicaraguan creation. It was sooo good we asked for seconds. The beach is lovely, the water is nice and warm and when you sit under a palapa with a Tonia ( local beer) in your hands your fooled to think that you're on the ocean. There is always a breeze on the miles and miles of sandy beach, take a walk and you'll experience the real rural Nicaragua. Nicas walk, bike, horseback ride, play, swim, bath on the beach and water, women and men standing waist deep in the warm water are busy washing their clothes on a big slab of rock, can't think of a nicer laundry room, dryer or cloth line, what is that? Bushes and trees will do. Cattle and horses guided by cowboys will come to the lake for a drink and disappear in the trees again. Time has stood still We had booked for 4 nights but decided to stay the whole week. Finca San Juan and staff you are simply the best! Thank you for a magic stay.

author: ArjunaS
title: Great secluded hotel
text: Stayed here for three nights. The ace is pretty big but we had almost the entire hotel to our selves when we were here. The place is very secluded, with rooms facing the lake, conception or cottages raised up facing the lake as well. For dinner and breakfast, there's a lovely terrace facing the lake. We really enjoyed having breakfast and dinner there and then hanging out on the hammocks sipping piña spiked with aged flor de cana. The rooms themselves were nice, clean bathrooms and had AC. The hot water didn't work but we didn't bother to get it fixed as it was so hot outside anyways. The food was great for the most part. Mixed pinchos - various grilled meats were our favorites, followed by the churrasco and the grilled chicken. I had the fish the first day and thought it was too salty. Breakfast was great; great coffee, surprisingly good French toast. The fruit plate with honey and the "Finca" with two eggs, rice and beans, and platoons were also good. Staff were kind and courteous and spoke a bit of English. The grounds were really nice as well, just a few bugs flying around, which you'll see anywhere on the island. Also note that this place is about 2 km off the main road on a very rough road. Mountain biking out will take you about 15 minutes.

author: composertim
title: Just paradise
text: I just had an amazing three night stay here in one of their new Lakefront cabins. There are so many positive things I can say about this beautiful Finca that I don't know where to begin. Perhaps I'll start with the thoroughness of the staff in helping me plan my trip (from my arrival and departure to the tours I wanted to take while staying here), as well as making me feel confident the kitchen staff would be able to handle my dietary restrictions (gluten free, Celiac). Marianela, who greeted me upon arrival, was immensely kind and very caring, often talking to me about my stay and helping me with getting around the island, one day showing me on the map how I could walk to the Ojo de Agua, a nearby and not-to-be-missed attraction on the island, and the Pena Inculta, a beautiful old forest preserve which I unfortunately did not make it to. She even ensured that, when I hiked the Concepcion volcano, that I had a gluten free lunch to carry with me. To me this was above and beyond and she deserves to be commended for her hard work. The kitchen and wait staff were very kind and thorough as well; Martin, who also drove me to the Finca on the first day, always remembered how I liked my rum (con hielo y limon). The food on the menu, though limited, was plenty satisfying and I was able to thank the chef personally for taking care of my dietary needs and preparing the best tostones con queso I had on my trip (they make their cheese on the farm and it's amazing!). Now I have to say more than a few words about the beauty of the grounds and the hotel itself. A short bumpy ride past the plantain farm and you enter an amazingly beautiful and secluded place. You have stunning views of both volcanoes and immediate beach access. The beach is beautiful here (you may hear people around here talking about it being dirty but I just didn’t see that) and the grounds themselves are well kept and there are plenty of birds and wildlife as well as local cattle being herded down the beach daily. You can take horses, kayaks, bikes, even scooters for rental. And the cabin I stayed in was an amazing place to relax in the middle of my trip. They are very well built and incredibly comfortable for the rustic locale, each equipped with a full bath and a mini bar, as well as porch overlooking the beach. I couldn’t have found a better place on the island honestly. Stay here, you won’t regret it.

author: neilhalper
title: Quiet, clean, very nice
text: I stayed at this hotel in Feb 2015 and it was great. I stayed in one of the rooms attached to the main building. It was clean and quiet. The bed was very comfortable and the water in the shower was nice and hot. The wifi was ok. If I would recommend one thing to the hotel, it would be to reset the wifi on the daily. By the end of the day it was very slow...so slow we had trouble paying. The beach is very nice, long, and quiet. The hotel is a short walk from Ojo de Agua - which was awesome - they arranged a guided hike for us up Maderas - which was also awesome. The food was simple but tasty. The prices of each meal on the dinner menu was around 14$ US. I would recommend this hotel. It was really great. If you are going to hike Maderas do yourself a favour and wear proper footwear. I was in ACG shoes and would have benefitted from an actual hiking boot. It took us 3 hours to walk up and 2:40 to get down which the guide said was exceptional time. He said he typically plans on 5 hours up and down. Also, it gets COLD and wet at the top of the volcano. Tank top on the bottom, jacket on the top.

author: ELKEH22
title: Beautiful place, friendly staff, delicious food
text: My husband and I stayed 2 nights at this wonderful finca in a beachfront cabin, located right at Lake Nicaragua and from where you could see both volcanos on Ometepe (Maderas and Concepción). We loved our cabin. It was very well equipped with A/C, ceiling fan, complimentary toiletries, and a fridge. The room itself as well as the bathroom was spacious and the terrace facing the lake was huge. We loved to sit there and enjoy the view. It was a little windy (normal for the season) but not too bad. The advantage of the wind is that there are no mosquitos. The finca is in a remote location but that makes up its charm. Birdwatching, going for a hike on the property, enjoying the delicious food at their restaurant, friendly and attentive staff – we couldn’t have asked for a better place to explore Ometepe. They also help you plan excursions and rent scooters and bikes. We had all our meals at Finca San Juan de la Isla. They prepare everything with fresh ingredients and we liked everything we tried. The only thing I could complain about was that we had only 2 nights there. We would have loved being able to stay a little longer. Finca San Juan de la Isla was one of the highlights of our trip, very relaxing. We would definitely stay here again when in the area and highly recommend this place.

author: Captschoch
title: Great location and friendly staff!
text: I am an airline pilot and have stayed at many hotels and can tell you Finca San Juan de la Isla is fantastic. My new husband and I recently visited Finca San Juan de la Isla for our honeymoon for 2 nights. We live in Nicaragua and wanted a location that was secluded and unique but not too far away. Finca San Juan de la Isla was perfect. We stayed in a cabin on the water. It was updated, clean and had a perfect view. We enjoyed the convenience of a mini fridge in the room, coffee maker and dish ware. The breakfast was fantastic. I can not comment on the quality of the other food because we went to a nearby town to eat dinner. I did notice the prices for food and beverages were similar to those found in the United States but not outrageous. The staff was excellent as well. Maria was a huge help! She provided many suggestions and speaks very good English. She made the check in process very quick and easy. The other staff members were very helpful also. Our car would not start on our last day and we needed to catch the ferry. The staff members helped my husband troubleshoot the problem and got the car started within an hour! The location is definitely a bit out of the way for nightlife and stores so I would suggest this location only for people looking to disconnect for a few days. There is no television in the room (which was great!) The wi fi works at the main building but cell phone service is not good. Overall this location is perfect and we will definitely be back soon!

author: TravelKAM13
title: Rustic island get-away
text: We spent two nights at the Finca San Juan de la Isla on beautiful Ometepe Island. It is definitely remote and has a more rustic feel compared the places we stayed in Granada and San Juan del Sur, but we loved our time there. The room was not our favorite part of the experience. It was average but still a little camp-y compared to what we are used to (You could hear the people in the room next door, bedding wasn't that nice, etc). But it was clean, had a decent shower, had an A/C unit in the room, and was adequate considering the other benefits of being at the Finca. We loved the hammocks and rocking chairs outside on the porch. Our favorite part was the view of the lake and the sounds of nature, along with the amazing food. We sat outside on the porch and were served some of the freshest, most delicious chicken and fish we had during our time in Nicaragua. We also loved the tostones so much that my husband asked Ernesto to teach us how to make them. Despite the language barrier, we had a great time and this was one of our best memories of the trip. Ernesto even made us an early breakfast and sack lunches for the morning we were going to hike Concepcion Volcano. One morning after breakfast, he brought out a special treat of "guacamole" Nica-style which we are still drooling over and hope to try to re-create at home. He is a great cook! All of the staff members were extremely kind and helpful. It was incredibly relaxing sitting outside over a delicious dinner, reading in a hammock, drinking coffee with the sounds of the lake and birds, being surrounded by the tropical island farm environment, and just being away from the busy-ness of life. We are definitely glad we went to Ometepe and would recommend staying at the Finca for a unique experience.

author: HCB_11
title: Unusual, tranquil, great food
text: We enjoyed one night at Finca San Juan. The finca primarily grows plantains. We had a small new room with a private bathroom. This room is in block of four rooms, and it appears that the finca is building at least one additional block of these rooms, if not two. From the hammock on the back porch we had a beautiful view of the Concepcion Volcano, which was magical at sunset as we listened to howler monkeys in stereo. Then there was a massive infestation of massive ants. They came from nowhere! We were afraid they would get in our room, but they didn't, however, they could have. It seems as if they were just marching through to see what was there. We then sat at the bar and chatted with the person I assume is one of the managers. He is from the island. His English wasn't great and my Spanish wasn't great, but we managed to have some conversation and he was very nice. Our dinner was marvelous. I had a fish dish with capers and olives and my husband had beef. perhaps the best beef of our trip, though we ate a lot of beef, so it's hard to say! They were kind enough to accommodate an early breakfast for us the next morning at 5:30 as we were departing at 6am to hike Maderas. Really nice unusual place to stay.

author: trvlbug04
title: A Treasure!
text: Peace, serenity, tranquility. . . all of these feelings spring to mind when I think of Finca San Juan de la Isla. It was truly one of our favorite experiences while in Nicaragua. Private and tucked away behind acres of banana trees, this beautiful property is truly something special and unlike anywhere else. The rooms were very nice and comfortable, but we spent most of our time outside of the room relaxing in a hammock or rocking chair on the beautiful porch overlooking Lake Nicaragua or walking up and down the beach taking in the nature around us. I still can't get over just how gorgeous this property is. You truly feel as if you've escaped from the rest of the world. It was also a real pleasure getting to meet Cesar, the owner and his lovely wife. They made us feel at home and we did not want for anything. Cesar has done an amazing job of restoring this property and encouraging responsible tourism in Nica. We also loved Cesar's staff: Catalina and Ramon, who took great care of us during our stay. We hiked to the San Ramon Waterfall and really enjoyed the company and humor of Neftali during the tour. Ramon drove us around the island and he had an excellent eye for spotting wildlife along the way including howler monkeys, iguanas, and all sorts of beautiful birds. He was gracious enough to pull over so that we could hop out for some great photo opportunities along the way as well. The food prepared on site by Catalina was delicious and some of the best during our entire trip. I loved having our meals outside on the porch feeling the breeze on your face and the sound of the birds in the trees. It's not everyday you come across a place to stay like Finca San Juan. Some of our best memories were made here.

author: ellybellycat
title: A little slice of heaven.Fantastic food,service,location and scenery.
text: This place is beyond wonderful. Marvin is an exceptional cook & host. He uses fresh herbs, fruits, vegetables & grilled meat/ fish to make sensational meals which are served on the veranda of the renovated farmhouse. Fantastic chicken soup--it's a meal!The property is an explosion of nature from birds,butterflies,horses, flowers,monkeys, plantains,orange trees & frogs, to the beautiful lake and the spectacular volcanoes. The beach is steps away. The stars are brilliant since there is nothing else nearby. It was so relaxing and felt so comfortable. The room was very large & comfortable with screens/nice breeze. We never had to use the A/C. Hot shower with unreal water pressure (it felt like a spa treatment). All the staff were friendly,helpful & provided excellent service. Breakfast is included & it is a full, complete meal. They arranged transportation to/from ferry. If you want to experience a spectacular visit to Ometepe, it MUST include staying here. You will not want to leave the finca. We miss you Marv! Be sure to go to the "eye of water" for the day...it's a neat mineral spring/pool nearby

author: AmazingJourney
title: The Best accommodations on Ometepe!
text: My husband and I had the pleasure of visiting Ometepe Island for the first time this year. I read all the reviews of hotels/B&B's on the island, and decided Finca San Juan was the logical choice. We had a driver waiting for us when our ferry arrived at Moyagalpa on Ometepe. It was a good half hour drive to Altagracia, and then off the main road through a 168 acre plantain farm. Once we arrived at the Finca we were very impressed with the compound. This Finca was totally rebuilt a few years ago, and a lot of details went into the construction of the main lodge and the separate casitas. We opted to rent the casita, rather than the main lodge. It was a very nicely decorated free standing unit with AC, the hottest water and pressure I have experienced anywhere in Nicaragua, and a very private patio complete with hammock. Since it is a fair distance to the actual town of Altagracia we ate all of our meals on the main patio overlooking the impressive Lake Nicaragua. This is the first lake I have seen with it's own surf! If you are a bird watcher, then this place is for you also. We saw dozens of different species of birds everyday.One of the most interesting is the blue magpie.They were very social birds, and quite comical to watch.Many Howler monkey's, grass lizards and iguanas too. I did notice a few flying insects after the sun went down, but brought a good insect repellent ,so no problems there.In my opinion we were fortunate enough to eat some of the most delicious meals during the 3 days we were here. Marvin is the Head Chef, and took a great deal of pride in his creations.We were never disappointed with any of our meals.I would most certainly recommend Finca San Juan de la Isla to anyone looking for an "upscale" retreat off the beaten track! I will be back again next year for sure :-)

author: vacaciones71
title: Nice Hotel
text: I stayed in one of the cabanas for 3 nights in early March 2011 . The cabana was spacious and clean with a wonderful hot shower everyday. The staff was very friendly, helpful, accomodating and professsional. Marvin, Cesar and Ramon were very courteous, kind and made my stay very comfortable. The rest of the satff was also excellent but I do not remembe their names. The food at the hotel was also very good and plentiful. I didn't walk away from any meal feeling hungry. The hotel and farm is pretty and pictoresque and there is a black sand beach on the lake in front of the hotel with nice views. The hotel is located in a remote area, but the hotel offers transportation to get around with a SUV (driver provided) and bicycles for rent. It is a very peaceful and tranquil place to visit. The only thing that wasn't pleasant was the numerous small flying insects that happened to be all over the place during the time I stayed there. I heard that there are certain times of the year when these bugs are every where on the island. I wasn't aware of this ahead of time so initially it did scare me a bit, but then I got used to them. Of course, this is no poor reflection on the hotel itself, but simply something new to me and slightly uncomfortable. I would recommend this hotel to others

author: StardustCharly
title: perfect getaway from NYC
text: My boyfriend and I just returned from Nicaragua a few days ago and I am missing the fantastic time we had at Finca San Juan de la Isla. Everything everyone has said in other reviews is true. It is paradise and it is remote. As we were driving through Nicaragua for about a week, we rented a car (with 4wd!) and brought it with us to Ometepe. For us, the car was crucial. We mostly took it easy, but we did get out to explore the island. Marvin is amazing - he really made our trip special. He's a super-nice guy and a gracious host who put up with my mediocre Spanish. He also cooked us delicious meals. He set us up with a great guide (Neftali) who took us hiking on the volcano, then to a local rodeo and baseball game. There is lots to do on Ometepe, but I will echo others in saying our favorite thing to do was nothing. There are hammocks and rocking chairs everywhere you look and the little beach right outside the fence is a perfect place for looking out at Lake Nicaragua. There are bugs, for sure - bring bug spray. Or, take a lot of vitamin B1. It's worked for me, though I know others it hasn't worked for. If you really hate bugs and little lizards, don't go to Nicaragua. We stayed in a cabin that wasn't attached to any other rooms and it was $90/night. That's not cheap for Nicaragua, but it was a great value. (and about 1/4 or the price of another place we looked at on the mainland...)

author: teacherblue
title: Highly recommend!
text: We stayed two nights, in two different rooms due to my booking and changing plans. This gave us a chance to see two types of rooms. The first room was in the motel part. We had a main floor king room. It was large, had a fridge and patio doors that we could walk out to the pool. We had a bit of trouble at the beginning when the bed wasn’t made when we walked in but Patrick the manager took care of us immediately! Excellent service. The walls were a little thin but tolerable. The next night we stayed in a king room in the tower. Wow! Room was much bigger , bathroom is huge, robes for the pool were in both rooms, balcony overlooked the city. Room was much quieter. The breakfast is one of the best I have seen at a Best Western. We are Diamond plus members so we stay at a lot of Best Westerns. The hotel is about 7 minutes to the main beach and downtown but it was the best price and an excellent stay. We will be back!

author: christinedG2005ZR
title: This place sets the standard for the Okanagan!
text: Will be hard for Kelowna to compete with this place. Customer service is top notch at this hotel. Very Friendly staff that genuinely look like they love being here. The rooms are very clean, the location is perfect. We had to have an extended stay (3 mos) at this hotel due to a house fire, so had the luxury of trying all their room types. Each room exceeded my expectation. They are roomy, bright, and very clean. The housekeeping and maintenance staff always had a smile on their face, and they were very friendly. The front desk staff were also friendly and personable, trying to make efforts to know their customers names. They made each room change seamless and made our extended stay easy to be displaced from our home. I cannot say enough about the the breakfast staff ... they were very personable, and they genuinely seemed liked they cared about the visitors at the hotel. Managers would come down and query visitors about their trip, their stay as well as treated their employees with exemplary attitudes. Treating this environment much like their family. True customer service starts from within and this hotel exudes that. All hotels should aim as high as they do! I will definetely be highly recommending this hotel to all that come and stay and anyone questioning where they should stay.

author: russellc770
title: Poorly managed and unfriendly staff
text: This hotel should be avoided. It did not meet Best Western Plus standards. The old section in this hotel has a very small service elevator, but it was almost unusable with limited weight restrictions. The front desk staff did not advise us that we would have to lug up our luggage otherwise. It was so bad it was almost funny. Many of the staff were unfriendly with the exception of a couple of housekeepers. Additionally we accidently left an expensive clothing item behind which was not returned. This item could not have been mistakenly discarded and should have been turned over to their lost and found who we had almost immediately notified. The room had very poor lighting and should have at least on bright light by the bed for reading. The guest room had a heavy perfume smell when we arrived which we discovered later was intended to cover up an bad odor from the toilet. There was also a trip hazard in the room where new tile was installed by the room entrance but not level with the carpet. This may sound like a small thing, but it really was a trip hazard and poorly designed. While the room had been clearly remodeled, it was still an old section of a larger hotel and not especially attractive. We would not stay here again and probably would try the other Best Western Plus in West Kelowna. We are BW Reward members and this was our first unsatisfactory experience with BW. Our stay in Revelstoke had been perfect so our expectations were already established...thus our disappointment to an otherwise wonderful 10 day vacation.

author: tshep42
title: Very Nice Hotel
text: Clean, comfortable and spacious rooms. Staff were all very friendly. Rooms have all the usual amenities including a mini fridge. Ours on the 6th floor had a nice view of the surrounding mountains. We had a balcony on our room. Location is right on the 97 highway but we didn't hear any traffic noise. Lots of shopping and dining around the hotel. There is an onsite restaurant as well. They have a pretty good complimentary breakfast with all the usual items: waffles, scrambled eggs, bacon, etc. It's in a large room so it doesn't get too crowded. It wasn't lined up at all when we were there around 8 AM but it was a little lined up when we walked by around 9 AM. They have a small fitness centre, business centre, pool and hot tub. The pool is right beside the breakfast area and it's all glass the breakfast goers are watching you swim. Also, you're walking through the lobby to get to the pool. There is a roof top terrace but it was locked when we tried to look at it. 4 rating might have been a 5 had they brought up the extra pillows I asked for.

author: Demi_8
title: Impressed!
text: This was our second stay with the Best Western Plus chain (first a few years ago in Florida but satisfaction level was not too high). We decided to try BWP again on a recent trip to Kelowna based on plenty of positive reviews here on Tripadvisor. Our family of four spent two nights in a standard room (2 queens) in the tower (8th floor). At first, it was hard to choose between a tower or courtyard room because they both sounded nice and different. The room was clean, modern, good view of the city/mountains, beds comfortable with the right amount of firmness, and the bathroom had a nice set-up with adequate light and counter space. I loved having one of those lighted wall mount mirrors that extend out of the wall (I wish all hotels had these) – great for the ladies when doing make-up. With plenty of counter space, it was possible for two people to use that part of the bathroom at the same time without feeling too crowded. There was one sink but the other person had room to do their hair or whatever. The parking lot had plenty of spaces that were not too tight. We have a larger-size truck and it was nice to have that one area along the curb where many other trucks seem to favor as well. We had some expensive bikes attached (locked up well), but still the concern of being in an unfamiliar place and worrying about theft or damage at night – fortunately we encountered no issues. The hotel is centrally located in town but the area appears to be good. We had stayed at a few places on this trip through the Okanagan (all with complimentary breakfast) and the best breakfast award goes to this hotel! There was a good variety (other reviewers have posted selections so I won't repeat) but it is the small touches that put this breakfast at the top. Some of these minor additions are simple things like the strawberry sauce for the waffles and having extra toppings for the oatmeal, etc. We look forward to choosing this hotel again the next time we are in Kelowna and perhaps trying a courtyard room next time.

author: NGolamco
title: Nice stay
text: We had a nice stay at the best western in Kelowna. It's a good location, lots of restaurants and shopping near by. We had a deluxe room and it was nice for our family of 4, 2 toddlers. We also asked for a playpen and actually got a real crib which was nice for the baby. We spent 3 nights there. The pool was great but very warm and not refreshing at all, it felt like bath water. They had 2 outdoor hot tubs as well which were nice. They have loungers outside by the pool/hot tub and they were nice to soak up some sun. The courtyard area by the pool is wonderful and they have BBQs you can use. They give a free breakfast which is more than adequate, it doesn't change much but it's free. They have scrambled eggs, omelettes, bacon or sausage, breads, pastries, fruit, cereals, milk, juices, waffle station, yogurt, hard boiled eggs, oatmeal and coffee/tea. So more than you need. Staff was friendly and helpful. We did a load of laundry there as they have coin machines. We would definitely stay again.

author: Purpleceltic
title: Absolutely Fabulous!
text: Regrettably we only had an overnight stop at the Best Western in Kelowna. From the warmest of welcomes right through to the the moment we regrettably had to leave, our experience was top notch. Our room was generous in size with a large balcony and quality fixtures and fittings. We had a fridge, coffee maker and kettle and the bed was possibly one of the most comfortable I have slept in. Air-con undoubtedly aided that sleep on what was a very hot day. We had planned to skip across the retail lot to The Cactus Club for dinner but read in the reviews that the hotel's attached pub was good so tried that instead. It was better than good! The prices were reasonable and we ate from the specials menu for that evening which featured British favourites with Canadian flair. The very tasty fish and chips deal came with a glass of beer and represented very good value for money. Our friendly waitress gave good advice on what beers would best suit our tastes and she wasn't wrong. Breakfast was hearty and complimentary. Loved the oatmeal and there was a full cooked breakfast including make your own fresh waffles for those that wanted it. Didn't try the pool but it looked good for laps. Would recommend this hotel in a heartbeat as a good out-of-town touring base. Hope that helps.

author: lemon910
title: Weekend wedding visit
text: Our check in was oddly off- putting with comments we found to be in poor taste and offensive. Despite the shaky start, we were afforded a playpen in very short order. Our room on the main floor had an outdoor sitting area to a common green space. Our pool experience was not a highlight due to rambunctious youngsters frolicking loudly and the slippery floor of the change room. One of our room robes, which we appreciated, was worn through. Breakfast was good, especially with fresh fruit, waffle and porridge stations and a selection of typical hot and cold breakfast items enjoyed in a spacious, airy space between the pool and lobby, which is suitable for group gatherings. The pub was awesome with friendly service, lots of options for craft beer and appealing- looking food. A free shuttle service is available to the airport and downtown. We noticed several dogs and heard them during the night. Our room was clean and maintained acceptably. Coffee pods and tea variety were good. Checkout was friendly and without concerns. The rooftop wedding had a great view. Location is close to shopping and restaurants. There are charging stations for electric vehicles.

author: FLORIDAMAGA
title: BEST WESTERN PLUS KELOWNA-SURPASSED MY EXPECTATIONS
text: As a traveler who has frequented many hotels in North America, I can't rate them all. I will rate this one, because everything thing about the property and staff exceeded my expectations. Most properties I frequent are ok, but my stay here went above the usual hotel stay. I stayed 3 nights. The airport shuttle is included in the cost and run by professionals. the lobby of the hotel is quiet and the check in staff are more than kind, they really show they care about their guests stay. My room was very clean, very quiet and soundproof. I could not have wanted another room, it was perfect. the sheets towels furnishings are all in good condition, no wear and tear...nice ! all surfaces in room and bathroom were clean. the breakfast area is divided into 2 sections, I found it relaxing during breakfast, none of the usual frenzy and chaos at some properties I have stayed at, and all areas are clean as well. The lap pool was warm, quiet with a nice view of the trees and sky and well maintained clean showers and change rooms. internet was fast, all computers and printers in the business center worked well. The staff were the greatest, thanks Sarah and (front desk staff as well) for making my stay the best I could have hoped for. If ever you want to pay for a hotel and feel like you actually belong there, stay here ! I have paid for many hotels and felt like a stranger on the property, not here! I could not have had a nicer time. thank you all for making jan 5th 2017 a memory I will cherish :)

author: SylviaMacD
title: Hotel was fine
text: I stayed here with my family during my dad's heart surgery in Kelowna for four nights. The hotel was clean overall and there was lots of room in the queen deluxe room we stayed in on the first floor that had two queen beds and then there we requested a cot at an additional cost. Breakfast was fine, but we did wait for about 15 minutes one morning for the hot items to be re-filled as there were sports teams that were cleaning out the trays - not a big issue as we weren't in a hurry. There was a tournament of some sort in town as there were numerous teens in the hotel however this was not a constant issue but did result in literal screaming in the hallway outside of our room and loud thumping from above between the hours of 9pm and 1030pm - we called the front desk which addressed it immediately. We never had any issues with parking or the front desk. There is a pool and hot tub that my daughter used - it was fine. There is also a small spa that offers massages, pedicures, etc but I did not have time to use it. It is attached to a pub and restaurant. Not sure if the restaurant is open anymore as we only ever noticed the pub open so had to order food in or go out as my daughter could not go into the pub. There was a strange smell in the room, not sure what it was from. Didn't complain about it as we only noticed it every once in awhile - almost musty - maybe the room also allowed pets? Not sure. Also, there was no microwave and the fridge was so cold it froze our fresh vegetables and fruit even after we turned it down which was a bit odd. If you upgrade to a better room then you get a microwave. Overall it was good for the time we were there.

author: E7513THnancyk
title: Spacious clean rooms
text: Upon check in, you are welcomed by a spacious lobby and an inviting front desk. The rooms are spacious and the beds comfy. Each room, if you are in the tower, have a balcony. There is a separate area in front of the bathroom for your coffee maker, a fridge etc. The bathroom is "tight" but very clean and acceptable. The only negative factor was I was unimpressed with the "free breakfast".........It was a hot and cold offering, you could do either. I found the hot items very unappetizing, there looked to be breakfast sausages but I couldn't accept the way they were presented, it was ghastly. There are hotel staff but this is a self serve so they were there to clean up the tables. The morning I was there, I was horrified to see that there were ten year olds trying to use the waffle makers. Batter spilling everywhere and just a disrespectful conduct with no parents around. When I mentioned this to the front desk clerk upon checkout, I got a "that's too bad". There was no offer to rectify the situation as I told her both mornings we refused breakfast entirely. Plus on top of it there were kids running around like it was a school playground.
