We seem to pay a lot for what in effect was coffee, a Danish pastry and a slice of toast. We tried to get a hotel one day from outside the hotel using the concierge and we were told this particular taxi driver didn't take 'foreigners'! Fortunately my daughter can speak Chinese so could understand everything the driver was saying which wasn't pleasant! Anyway he eventually said he would take us but wasn't happy about it! Felt really safe in the area. The major shopping areas were around 15 mins walk away. Really enjoyed Beijing and it was an easy city to get around using public transport. It was also very cheap in my view. Would definitely come back to Beijing again.

author: Budge45
title: Big Rooms- Great location
text: It is always a nice surprise when the hotel is better than expected. We were on the 12th floor and had a nice large room. In fact two rooms. There was a living area and the bedroom, both of more than adequate proportions. The bathroom had a shower and separate bath. The room was clean and the bed firm but comfortable. The room didn't smell of smoke which is a pleasant change. Love the location. We have stayed in this vicinity 3 times now and enjoy having the subway within about 5 minutes walk. The walk to Wangfujing is about 15 -20 minutes. Checkin/Checkout was smooth however the minibar security payment was a bit extreme. Free wifi was only in the lobby. We were a bit disappointed that there was no washing machine in the room as indicated in the listed room features online. It was one of the reasons we had selected this hotel. Overall though we were more than happy.

author: Gus116
title: Rooms served warm and Breakfasts served cold
text: Walking into the impressive and expansive lobby, with excellent reception staff, who were kind enough to upgrade us, one had high hopes for this hotel, but sadly it was a letdown. I have hence upgraded my experience from Poor to Average , in thanks to reception team, The rooms were dated from the mid eighties, with everything, especially the badly nicked wooden surfaces, clearly showing their age. It was very hot in Beijing and the aged central aircon struggled to cope. I woke up every night drenched in sweat.A complaint was made, but nothing was done about it. The breakfast restaurant was abysmal. The restaurant itself was impressive, and appeared newly renovated, with lovely views over the central courtyard and pond. The buffet selections were numerous, and well topped up, but all the hot food was stone cold. . The burners at the bottom of the hot pans were insufficient to come with the volume of the food in there. The service staff were clueless, and there did not appear to have any manager or supervisor in control. We were led to our table one morning , and when we got up to pick our selections from the buffet, our table was given away to another guest. Tea and Coffee had to be requested, and served without teaspoons. It took long minutes of miming, and gesticulating for the waitstaff to understand what a teaspoon was, and then only one was proffered on a table of 2. More than poor English skills, there appeared to be poor comprehension skills among the staff, There is no shortage of wait staff around, but all appear to be roaming around in circles, quite clueless, We were not tempted to try any other outlets for meals, given the chaos we experienced at breakfast. The wi fi in the room worked sporadically, and appeared to be free. Our driver also experienced issues with the car park attendant to charged him for entering the premises to pick us up. Apparently only the first few minutes are free, and they then start charging for parking. Housekeeping did a great job with what they had to contend with, and our room, and all common areas were always clean. Checkout was a breeze, and no issues were experienced there.

author: HosseinShamloo
title: a 3.5 Star Hotel, dirty breakfast, don't Stay at this Hotel !
text: me and my mother stayed 7 nights there because we could not book another good Hotel. a 3.5 Star Hotel ! very Old Hotel, Staff don't know English at all except reception, dirty breakfast. 0- Hotel Staffs can't speaks English, you ask : is this water ? in Chinese you here something that she means I don't understand. you ask is Tap water drinkable ? you hear what ?? 1- Breakfast was very dirty, lots of bugs (fly) on foods, the waiter who clean's others finished dishes, same person serve's fork, knife and plate for you with same wet hand ! 2- If you missed your military service, try Beijing International Pool. you are not 1 minute alone, one personnel is chasing you at all time. you can not enter without cap (that it is a good thing) you think, wow what a good quality, but there are blood on the towels of the sauna. they ask you to take off your swimwear to enter to the cold jacuzzi (it was not hot, wrote 45 degrees centigrade , was 20). Bath tub was for 100 years ago ! Water Tap, you have to be Rocky to open it and you will get wet by compliments. Lobby is very noisy, you can visit 100 people each time you enter the Lobby. --------------------------------- Positive : Very Fast and Good house Keeping Services. 5 minute to Metro Station but you have to go down 182 Steps, there is no Escalator !!!! There is an automatic money Exchange Machine in the Lobby.

author: L0la2003
title: We were treated awful
text: We booked a double room with an extra bed, and put a clear remark to have three beds. Once we were at reception they said there were only rooms with queen bed and an extra bed with no space to have another extra bed. They said there was no twin room available. We complained but not succeeded. After that, the offered a twin room with an extra bed by paying 24 euros more per night. Is there now an available room when we pay an extra money? We felt as we were being rip-off, but they did not accept any other solution and we paid for it. No breakfast included, if you want breakfast you have to pay 20 euros per person. In the room you have some expensive drinks available, for example; bottle of 1 litre of water 8,5 euros. Wi-fi internet worked horrible. There is a cable to connect to internet in the room but you have to pay for that service. After spending four nights, when checked out we tried to use the swimming pool but we were not allowed. In this five-star hotel, we were treated awful. The hotel is among huge avenues with nothing interesting around. Definitively, I would not recommend this hotel at all.

author: bmarie_01
title: Imperfect but endearing
text: We stayed here for 5 nights during our stay in Beijing. I'd have to agree with some of the other reviewers in that the hotel is outdated! Our 16th-floor room was clean enough with daily room service, but the carpet (an unappetizing brown), doors, furniture, and accents were clearly worn and haven't been replaced for some time. Notably, the bathroom had no ventilation system (no fan!), so taking even a brief shower steams up the room and tends to create the perfect incubator for mold. Considering how steamy Beijing can get, I'd say this is a major con. We also had some difficulty getting the air conditioner to work, and we were never able to blast really cool air when we wanted -- however I'm not sure if that was just a fluke or us being inept at figuring the little cooling/heating button pad out. We visited in May, just before the weather becomes unbearing-ly hot and humid, so I hope ya'll have better luck with this! Needless to say, the coolest (literally) place to be in the hotel is the downstairs lobby, where my aunt and I hung out quite a bit. There is only free wi-fi downstairs and the quality of connection was unpredictable; we'd spend at least ten minutes each time before being able to connect. It is a little disappointing that in-room wi-fi is extra charged; however I admit that it was refreshing and different to have an excuse to chillax in the lobby and watch other guests and business people come and go. Another con for me was the gym/pool services. If you intend to work out at this hotel, be prepared to have your first workout be the successful completion of the roundabout maze you will undergo to first find the gym, which is located in the "basement". You have to take a certain staircase up to the second floor and then take a certain elevator to the basement, and then ask the staff where to go next. The gym itself is poorly ventilated (read: Stuffy!) and just the basics. The pool costs and extra 99 yuan to use. To be fair, it is a pretty nice pool. The travel services and concierge desk staff were extremely helpful and friendly, despite the sometimes-limited English of some. They helped us arrange a day-long tour of the Badaling section of the Great Wall and the Ming Tombs for about $384 yuan per person; although our tour included the requisite stops at a huge Jade Gallery, silkworm factory, and a tea house (definite tourist traps--let me tell you, the Jade Gallery is very cleverly spatially-arranged to trap you inside with a melange of jade jewelry and sculptures), our guide was down-to-earth and did not push us to buy, although stressed that these places could at least ensure quality products. Lastly, location. It is about a 20-30 minute walk west to Tiananmen Square, and is within 7-10 minutes walking distance of the nearest Metro Station.

author: DHWShanghai
title: Well Past its Former Glory
text: The only reason I stayed in this hotel is because the buses for the Great Wall Marathon were leaving from here at 3am. This meant I could sleep till 2:45am and would not have to worry about catching a taxi. This hotel is the best example of a Chinese 5-star hotel. It probably was a 5-star hotel in 1980 before there were other true global 5-star hotels around. In fact, the 4-star Crowne Plaza or 3-star Holiday Inn are several notches above this hotel. The only thing it had going for it was that it only cost $100 / night. And I guess we got what we paid for. The inside appearance was typical for a Chinese interpretation of 'grandness' but ruined by the use of cheap materials and the usual lack of proper hygiene and maintenance. The hotel had a run-down feel everywhere for the lobby to the rooms. Everything was shabby and well-worn. My room had a very strange layout where the top of the bed (with the pillows) looked straight into the shower. The bedside table was so close to the entry door of the bathroom that I really hurt my left toe walking from the bathroom back into the bedroom. Thank goodness it was after the big run. It was sore for a full year after that. The breakfast buffet was good for American standards where you get only bagels and jam at most hotels. But again, it does not compare to global standard 5-star hotels in China or across Asia. So, I got what I paid for, just.

author: Zanzie
title: Large hotel, met all expectations
text: I just spent 11 nights at the Beijing International for a work conference followed by several days of sightseeing around the area. The hotel is clean and the staff is friendly and speaks enough English to make the stay comfortable for this non-Chinese speaking guest. Breakfast, included with the room, is a large buffet breakfast filled with Asian and Western items, including omelette bar. You won't leave hungry, that is for sure. The best restaurant in the hotel is probably the Tan Restaurant on the third floor; although you should certainly check out the rooftop lounge just for the city views. The hotel is about 30 minutes walk from Tian'an Men Square and (in the opposite direction) the Silk Market. The closest metro station is about 10 minutes walk. Taxis are extremely hard to get in Beijing -- traffic control measures ban them from stopping during weekday business hours on busy streets, including the one the hotel is on. The staff will call and make arrangements for a cab for you, but don't expect to just jump into one from the hotel cab stand. We often had to wait 20 minutes or more at the stand without calling ahead. The fitness room is functional, with four treadmills, free weights, a rowing machine, stair stepper and bike. There's a sauna and nice, large spa and swimming pool. You can get a 45-minute foot massage for about US $60. There is a clean, well-stocked grocery store in the Henderson Mall across the street -- take the underground tunnel to the mall entrance, go down to B2 level and stock up on bottled water, sesame peanuts, candies, tea -- as well as the more exotic yak bone marrow protein powder and tripe. And of course, Peking duck packaged in pretty red bags.

author: MickeyDV
title: Pleasantly Suprised
text: After a failed booking at another hotel, we were offered a room at this one. We were immediately impressed by the grand lobby - based on earlier reviews, they must have finished the renovations sometime before we got there. We stayed two nights in a comfortable and quiet room that showed signs of having been renovated. We chose to eat our first dinner at a wonderful Japanese restaurant in the shopping mall across the street. The second dinner was at one of the inside restaurants - good but very over-priced in our opinion. The breakfast buffet was really good, with a large selection of foods but lacking variety from one day to the next. On the second morning, we decided to make use of the pool which is located in the gym in the conference area next to the hotel. Now, that was a treat! Upon entry, ladies and gents were separately and quietly ushered into well-furnished changing rooms, supplied with towels, gowns and bathing caps, before being led to the large pool. Afterwards, we were led to showers where soaps, shampoos, combs, moisturisers, etc. were available for use; even our feet were toweled dry for us! This is a must if you visit this hotel. We walked to the subway, not too far away, to get around Beijing. Tianmen Square and the Forbidden City were within 2 stops away. Getting to the airport was also relatively simple, with 2 transfers, the last being the airport fast train.

author: Ozjane
title: Tired but very convenient
text: We stayed here in two separate visits for a total of 8 nights in January 2012. Our agent got us an excellent deal so the cost per night was excellent. As other reviewers have said, it is a bit tired though we had what we think were re-furbished roooms on the 10th and 11th floors. Apart from very poor lighting and a showerhead that poured out in an almost single stream, the room itself was very comfortable. Plenty of room for two of us to potter around in without tripping over each other and/or our bags. The staff, by and large, were ordinary, service not seeming to be a preoccupation. Standing at the front desk waiting for someone to finish texting and no apology when they finally looked up was a bit much. HOWEVER .. the big winner for this place is the location. Our rooms (1014 and 1114) faced the main street and we were able to stand and marvel at Beijing happening below us. Across the road is a brilliant supermarket, department store and specialty stores (just use the pedestrian walkway under the street) and a bit further along a number of food stores. As we were there in winter we tended not to go out too much at night so these stores were great. Hotel food average at best. We could see Beijing Railway Station which given that we were there during Lunar New Year was fascinating. We loved watching the people, cars, buses and everything else heading toward the station on their way home for New Year. In fact one evening we walked over and joined them just to experience the good will and general happiness people seemed to be feeling as they headed off for their 7 days holiday. There are 3 subways in easy walking distance, one to the left as you exit the hotel, one to the right and of course one at Beijing Railway Station. About 15 minutes walk from Weifujing Street and a little further (or 3 subway stops) from Tiananmen Square. Strangely I would recommend this hotel - not for the service, or the food, or the general environment. The position is the real winner.

author: Avid_Reader_10
title: Very nice! Excellent service! Great Location.
text: As a 1st time traveller to Beijing, wasn't sure what to expect. Booked through expedia, not as a tour. Rate was below $100CAD per night for deluxe biz rm incl all taxes & fees; stayed 1 week. Shuttle service available to/from airport, min cost. As the in-room staff was not bolted in, staff changed us to another room but on finding that room was smoking, they upgraded us to an even better room, separate bedroom suite with 2 bathrooms. Excellent response and service. Concierge service always the best in answering our Qs and getting us info. Housekeeping staff kept room very clean and always replaced amenity items or brought extra if requested. King bed very comfy. Location is excellent as hotel is between 2 subway stations with 1 having 2 different lines so with a bit of research, we were able to get to Beijing sites with little effort. We do not speak any Chinese whatsoever. Hotel is also on main thoroughfare that you can get to the $$$$ shopping area (10-15 min) and to Forbidden City & Tiannamen (20-30 min) with just walking if you like exercise. Lots of buses on main front road too. Across street & surrounding hotel were lots of places for huge variety of food that was both inexpensive and good. If we wanted to venture farther for food, it was easily done. Booked 1 tour through the hotel for Great Wall and it included Ming Tombs, jade & silk & tea shops. Tour from start to finish about 12 hrs and our group of 7 were the only ones so it was private with the rest of the 20+person bus empty. Tour leader spoke in English. About $60CAD cost pp, lunch included. Our group comprised of us travelling as a couple with 5 family members (booked other rooms at hotel).

author: aryna
title: Good value for money; amazing swimming pool
text: I have been in Beijing several times; each time we take another hotel. This time it was the Beijing international hotel. First, I arrived early at 11am, but nevertheless got a room. The room itself is relatively big, with two beds, a big seat, a desk, a fridge, and a TV set. There is also a tea boiler. The bed was comfy, and I slept very well. There was no noise from outside. The bathroom itself had nothing remarkable, but there were combs, toothbrush, etc... available for 2 people. I can only say that the shower was quite powerful - you would be awake in no time. Maybe the water could be a little warmer but I like it really hot (more than 40°C, so I am not a reference here) You had internet available in the room, but there is also free wifi in the lobby (and also in my room as I was on the 4th floor), but it was weak. When I came back from meetings, they were doing my room. It was not finished but I wanted to rest. When I came back later in the afternoon, the work had been completed. To note: the water is NOT drinkable, and I actually consumed water bottles that were available on the desk (some are for free, but not all). There is a supermarket on the other side of the road (and a Starbucks) They have an amazing swimming pool that unfortunately I was not able to test as they were cleaning, but was at least 25 m long. I tested the gym however, there was nobody there but it was well equiped and open up to 11pm. Everything is brand new. The only downside is that this is hell to get a cab so plan to ask the concierge in advance!

author: Wende888
title: Loved this hotel; many amenities and friendly, English-speaking staff.
text: I lived in Beijing, at this hotel, for a total of 39 nights while working the Olympics. The staff was friendly and helpful from the moment I checked in. The rooms are comfortable and clean, and I appreciated the twice-daily housekeeping. The restaurant downstairs had a fabulous breakfast buffet which would please anyone as there were almost too many choices. The staff speaks excellent English, and the concierge even found a place for me to go play foosball one evening. As my stay was so long, the concierges did direct me to many places I needed to go, and were instrumental in making my stay a very comfortable one. I felt right at home and safe in this hotel. There is a money exchange right there in the lobby, and it is centrally located. I was able to walk to a very popular shopping area called Wafujing Street. (While you are on Wafujing Street, I suggest visiting Carpenter Tan's as they have some amazing wooden combs and jewelry. They do not barter there but their items are very good quality.) There is apparently a rotating restaurant atop the hotel, which was closed during my stay. Just a reminder to travelers: don't drink the tap water or even brush your teeth in it. It's gritty. There are signs in your bathroon reminding you of this. The hotel did generously provide 2 bottles of water every day to the room. I would absolutely stay at this hotel again and am so glad this is where I was put up during such an extended stay.

author: springrollz
title: Great hotel and service, location is awesome!
text: Of the three hotels I stayed in during our China tour, Beijing International was the best in staff service, comfortable rooms and breakfast buffet. We went through Friendly Planet's Taste of China and it was definitely worth the money. Unfortunately we had a lower floor so there wasn't much of a view but the floor to ceiling windows made the room feel even bigger, but I didn't spend much time in the rooms besides sleeping anyways. Since we were 3 in room, we had a cot which by cot standards wasn't bad at all. My friends took the beds and they had no complaints either. The bathroom was marble and very clean. The rooms were kept very clean the entire time and no noise disturbance. The American and Chinese items at the breakfast buffet were plentiful and very good. I have a very adaptable stomach so I was able to enjoy the foods I wouldn't normally see in a U.S. breakfast bar. My favorite was congee with pickeled vegetables and the mini seafood steamed buns. The best thing about this hotel is the staff service and location. The staff is very knowledgeable, and if you stick to the front desk staff, they speak English well and even if you're not sure of where you want to go and can't exactly remember how to say it in Chinese, they'll figure it out and even write it in Chinese for your taxi driver and in English for you. I had problems locating a wholesale eyeglass shop (much cheaper then home) I wanted to visit and the front desk was extremely patient and helpful in locating the store and the doormen explained to the taxi driver how to get there. Also, since most taxi drivers do not speak English, tell the doormen where you want to go and he'll translate and you're on your way. If the doormen doesn't know, he'll ask the front desk. Their location across the street from a good shopping mall that included a Watsons Pharmacy and an Internet Cafe, which I was extremely thankful for, was also very convenient. You can also walk to Wangfujing Street which took about 20 minutes and if you need the metro, its about 3 blocks away. We also ordered McDonald's to the room a couple times, delivery time no more than 10 minutes, the fries were still hot :)

author: LearningForAll
title: Home away from Home
text: Just read a few reviews and honestly am quite disappointed with some opinions. But then everyone has their freedom of speach. Working and teaching in the Hotel field for over 25 years, I can be really objective about this particular hotel. True, it's big, old and due for renovations, which I was informed will be done this year. Actually a new section is under construction right now that will offer a new Reception area and lobby amongst other public areas. The existing lobby will be closed for renovations shortly. I encountered no mould or foul odours in my room. My room was spacious and comfortable but not extavagant for a 5* hotel but then again the price was right compared to other 5* hotels around the world. Some collegues got cards under their doors offering outside services but not I. And I heard of no knocking on doors offering after hours extra services from my group. The public areas were very clean, how many hotels do you see around the world with an employee constantly passing a dry mop in the lobby? This hotel has a staff of over 1200 employees and they are very present and pleasant. The trouble with some travellers is that they expect everyone in every city of the world to speak their language perfectly, especially the Americans! Wake up, open your eyes, ears and hearts to these foriegn destinations, the majority of employees working in the Toursim sector do their darnest to please the foreign traveller. At this hotel, they spoke much better English than I did Mandarin and I appreciated their effort. By the way, this hotel was just presented the presitgious 5* Diamond Award by the American Academy of Hospitality Sciences. This should say something about the Beijing International Hotel.

author: mmyk72
title: Hotel & Location are ok
text: Stayed at this hotel as part of tour package. It's rated 5 star, but it isn't as nice as a true 5 star in Western countries. I probably wouldn't stay here if I had to pay for the room (cheapest I found was US $130 for Nov). The location is great - 1 block from the main train station and subway. The airport shuttle also departs from the hotel parking lot. Looking at a map of Beijing, it seems like this hotel is only a couple of streets from the attractions. However, be aware that city blocks are long, so walking 2-3 blocks can take a while. However, taxi is very cheap (typical fare is less than US $2). Our room was a standard with 2 twin beds. The linen and towels were fresh. The temp in our room was very hot. There seemed to be too much central heating as we had our thermostat turned off. We had to cool the room down by opening the windows, but it was difficult to control how wide the window gap we want. One more thing I didn't like was that the room was very dark even with all the lights turned on. There is a small refrigerator in the room. You get 2 small bottles of water for free, and there is a water kettle for boiling water before drinking. I think this is a decent hotel if not for the high price. There are a lot of other hotels that are cheaper and just as nice.

author: JTeruelJax
title: PERFECT!!!
text: This hotel is 2-3 blocks away from the old city. It takes maybe 15 minutes walking to the Cathedral. And most other attractions are inside a 30 minute walk. We even walked to the Monte Del Gozo so we could walk the last 5 kms of El Camino. We also walked to El Corte Ingles mega store. Maybe a 25 minute walk. The hotel has no parking, but they work with one location across the street for 9 euros a night. Be aware. That parking does not open until 6 or 7 am. If you need your car earlier you will need to park in a 24 hour location a block away. Just in case you have an early flight. There is a large supermarket next door. There is a pharmacy across the street. There are multiple locations to eat nearby. Hotel staff is great. Very modern bright and clean rooms. Would I stay here again. Absolutely yes.

author: bostonbased
title: twin beds tucked in separately
text: Overall, the hotel is fine, but if some of the missing amenities are important to you, look elsewhere. Pros: the room was clean, and the a/c worked well. Plenty of closet space in our room, and luggage storage, but someone else in our group had a much smaller room where that was not the case. Good shower, and good coffee machine at breakfast. Cons: we've stayed in many European hotels where 2 twin beds are pushed together, but you are well and truly separated from your partner/spouse in the beds here. There is no mattress pad/sheet to connect the two beds, and the blankets are tucked in tightly around each twin bed. The beds aren't held together in any way, so a widening gap separates them if you are inclined to try and get closer to your traveling partner. Some photos seem to show a bed with one large blanket on it, but we specifically reserved a double room and were given 2 twin beds pushed together but not connected in any way. Very thin pillows. Additional pillows were delivered the next day upon request. The soundproofing is poor, allowing hallway and neighboring room chatter to reach us clearly. Breakfast may be traditional and tasty, but there are very few healthy options. If you eat everything and are not trying to be health conscious, you'll be fine with the many types of meat, cheese, white bread, pastries, and full fat yogurt/milk. There are hardboiled eggs (overdone) and sliced fruit, as well as whole fruit, along with sweetened fruit juice. I will start bringing oatmeal with me on future trips, as we went to two of the nearby groceries for snacks every day. No kettle in the room. We were given one at the front desk, but then had to get special permission to unlock the dining room so we could get hot-beverage coffee cups. No tea bags were offered with the kettle. Already had some in the suitcase.

author: LTMiranda
title: I WOULD STAY HERE AGAIN
text: I stayed here as part of a pilgrimage group. The hotel is conveniently located and is within 5-minute walking distance to Plaza Galicia, which is where the cathedral is. The hotel looks new, if not newly renovated, and clean. I like the black and white color scheme. The reception staff was very nice and patient. She didn't look overwhelmed, even if she had to attend to a group of 56 people. The room is of good size with clean bathroom. Our room had a bathtub which is perfect after a day of walking around. Food was excellent. I don't know if we had to pay extra, but we had a buffet dinner with bread, soup, salad, and a good variety of main course and dessert. We also had red and white wine on our tables. The wait staff were attentive and accommodating. We had to leave early the next day and they packed us breakfast to go. They also have free Wi-Fi. I would definitely book here if I were to go back to Santiago de Compostela.

author: hersheya2014
title: Wonderful Week in Habana
text: My wife and I stayed with Jose Antonio at Casa Eclectica in February 2017 and had a wonderful time. It always helps to speak Spanish (which we do), but the staff and Jose Antonio speak decent English and we did not have any communication issues. Everyone was incredibly friendly, hospitable, and the breakfast each morning was delicious (there was always fresh bread, fresh fruit, and eggs any way we wanted them). We are pretty casual and relatively low maintenance travellers, and Casa Eclectica was perfectly fine for us. The location n Centro Habana was very nice and essentially put us in the middle of the two areas we wanted to walk to on any given night (about 15 minut walk to Habana Vieja or 15 minute walk to Vedado), and it was just a few minutes walk to the Malecon. The energy in the neighborhood was indescribable and the are and vibrance of the community made our stay a wonderful one. With respect to the accommodations, the room we stayed in had 2 double beds (we only used one) and a nice bathroom with a shower. It was always clean and relatively comfortable, and there was also a fridge and safe available for our use. There was air conditioning, which we used, but we could have also opened up our windows and likely gotten a decent breeze. There was a balcony and common area that looked out onto the primary street that we were located on (Neptuno), and there was music playing almost all the time. With respect to the staff, I always felt like there was someone there in the Casa if we needed anything, and it felt very safe (as with most all of Habana). Yanelis and Daniel were incredibly kind and fun to talk to throughout the day and morning, and always gave us tips on what to do, if needed. We could not have asked for more from the Casa. If you are looking for a 4 star hotel experience, this is not for you, and honestly neither is Cuba, really. But if you are looking for nice accommodations, with a welcoming staff, and vibrant location, then this spot is perfect. Thank you again to everyone at Casa Eclectica for giving us a wonderful experience. We miss it! - H & V

author: paulamA1188GI
title: Elegant and Comfortable Casa in Centro Habana
text: This beautifully maintained Havana apartment is owned by Jose Antonio Alvarez Fernandez who lives on site. After showing us our room he gave us a bit of an orientation to Havana and answered any questions we had. His advice and assistance was very helpful. We asked about a good place to eat locally and Yanelis (who worked at the casa) walked with us the few blocks to a good paladar in the area. Yanelis prepared and served the beautiful breakfasts at the casa and went above and beyond to make our stay the treat it was. She went to the neighbours to find a corkscrew and came to work extra early to prepare and serve breakfast for us on the day we left. The casa itself is beautiful with soaring 12 foot ceilings, walls painted in lovely pastel colours and a beautiful veranda overlooking Calle Neptuno a busy one-way street in Centro Havana. The casa has 3 well furnished rooms to rent out. Our room had one double bed and one single bed and they were comfortable and clean. The veranda proved to be a great spot to meet the other guests and we enjoyed spending time there watching the old cars and people of the neighbourhood come and go. We could easily walk to Capitiolio and Parque Central as well as Habana Vieja and the Malecon was a few short blocks away. We were very happy with the accommodations and would return. Room 30 pesos, breakfast 5 pesos. Advice to travellers: Note: the rooms are on the third floor of the building. If you arrive by Viazul bus get off at Liberte Station (the main bus station) not Habana Vieja. Buy your return ticket when you get there, so you don’t have to take a taxi back to the station 2 days or so before you leave to buy a ticket. Hotel Inglaterra offers a hotel to hotel bus to Varadero for 25.00 pesos. We had problems with bicycle taxi operators at the Habana Vieja stop, we did not realize we were hiring bicycle taxis and they insisted on increasing the agreed upon price dramatically when we got to the casa.

author: prestonthompson7
title: Stay at Casa Eclectica 1925!!
text: All in all I stayed with Jose Antonio at his beautiful Casa for seven nights spread over two and a half weeks. I stayed with two different groups of friends and also by myself. I think that when your travelling to a place you've never been to before, you want to feel safe and when you step into someone's house you want to get along with them. This exceeded any expectations I had by miles. Staying at the Casa Eclectica was such a joyous experience and that was all down to Jose Antonio and his wonderful family. Located in Central Havana and just a few blocks away from the waterfront, you really feel like you're in the middle of this wonderful and vibrant city. Old Havana is just a fifteen minute walk away and although I went there a lot I was much happier living in Central Havana. I stayed in two different rooms, both spacious and beautifully painted with high ceilings and air conditioning. I slept better here than I do at home. The shower has hot water although with the heat outside it is hardly necessary and the water pressure was the best I experienced in my stay in Cuba. Breakfast was delicious and the staff were charming. It rained a few days, which I thought would be disappointing but Jose has one of the best balconies so reading there was a treat. When I was by myself, Jose made such a lovely effort with me. Seeing as my Spanish is embarrassingly poor, he talked to me in English and was full of recommendations. I also found it fascinating picking his brain on all things Cuba. If you get the chance to stay here, don't think twice. Book it.

author: KatharinaK378
title: Perfect Casa to stay!
text: We spent 3 days in Havanna. After our first Casa just cancelled our room we had no place to go. We fortunately got a room in Casa Eclectica 1925 and Jose and his wife helped us with so many things like all the tourist information, taxis and they were really friendly to us! the casa is amazing, very clean, beautiful furniture, lovely decorated! We loved our room! The breakfast was also really good! What we liked the most was the beautiful terrass! Having breakfast in the morning or just sitting and relaxing, enjoying the atmosphere was perfect. The location is very good, just 10-12 minutes walking to the capitol, a supermarket close and some nice restaurants. We wanted to thank Jose again for his help after we've been stranded due to another casas cancellation. In the moment of having no room we were really angry but afterwards we were really happy because we spent our nights in Casa Eclectica which was for sure much better! :) Dear Jose & family thank you again! I will recommand your casa to my friends who are coming! All the best from Austria! Katharina

author: skimber1949
title: Hidden gem in Centro Habana
text: The first time I stayed in Casa Eclectica 1925 was in 2009, and it was by accident. My original choice was only available for the first two days of my week's stay in Havana and that casa owner had suggested I complete my visit at his friend José Antonio's Casa Eclectica. My first view of my new digs was not encouraging. When you opened the door on busy Neptuno, you looked up a long, dingy unpainted staircase with more than a few cracked marble steps. I dragged my suitcase up one flight and then a second, wondering how quickly I could find some place else to stay, when I turned a corner and arrived suddenly in a beautiful airy, well appointed apartment. To your right as you enter, there is a large dining and seating area that leads to a comfortable deck overlooking Neptuno. To your right is a hallway with three private, reasonably quiet rooms off to the side, each with air-conditioning, a small fridge and a modern bathroom and shower. Ever since, I've stayed here whenever I come to Havana. The casa, halfway between Habana Vieje and the University of Havana (La Rampa area) and not far from the Malecon, is conveniently located and safe. I have wandered the neighbouring streets at all hours and never once felt threatened. Indeed, people have been kind and welcoming. Including, of course, José, the casa owner, who is helpful for everything from things to see to arranging taxis to the airport. At the same time, José is happy to give you your privacy if your prefer. The casa offers an optional breakfast of eggs, any style, bread, fruit, fruit juice and coffee for 4 CUC. The generous portions make it well worth the price (and the substantial breakfast often provides leftovers for snacks or lunch you can keep in your fridge.) Since I've begun coming here, José has managed to fix up the entrance with paint and repaired steps. It's still a climb up those stairs but well worth it when you get to the top!

author: 75jamesS75
title: Great Casa and People
text: We stayed with José and Gladys for 5 nights in their casa in Centro Habana. Great people. I felt that myself and my belongings were safe in this Casa. The casa was built in 1925, consists of beautiful architecture, and is in excellent shape. Small but reasonable sized room with 2 single beds, A/C and a private bath with shower. José was very helpful in providing some Havana guidance and advice. Gladys is the quiet one, but also very helpful. We had breakfast ($5 CUC each) on their gorgeous balcony every morning, and spent a little time out there in the evenings too. Thanks to Julie for providing our breakfast each day. Centro Habana is very interesting. We were two females and felt perfectly safe after the 1st 2 days adjusting to the difference between our city streets and those of Centro Habana. This is a bustling area with many friendly people. The hustlers don't kick in until you arrive in Habana Vieja. The walk to Habana Vieja is about 15 minutes and we walked back and forth each day. So many amazing buildings, but sadly deteriorating. The city must have been stunning in it's prime. Great hosts, great casa, great location. Thank-you José and Gladys for opening your house to us. The Gemelos - Carol and Jane E-mail: joserentroom@gmail.com Site: http://www.casaeclectica1925.com/index.php?option=com_contact&view=contact&id=1&Itemid=5&lang=en

author: JamesBisset
title: Quirky menu, but good room and location
text: I may be wrong but my perception and experience of 'restaurant with rooms' usually promises delightfully diverse and tasty menus leaving you spoilt for choice and often with a hankering to return (e.g. Sutherland House Southwold, Barley Bree Muthil, Rock Salt Folkestone) Arrived via Skye for 2 nights after fantastic stay in Lonbain on the Applecross Peninsula. Very friendly and helpful staff and re-assured that table for dinner reserved for guests of the lodge. The garden room was spacious, clean and comfortable with superb shower pressure and plenty of hot water. Dinner at 7:30 and somewhat disappointed to find that all the specials had been wiped off the blackboard, astonishing given that the restaurant only opens at 6 p.m. for dinner. There was an enigma of a seafood platter but, a) it wasn't cheap, b) it contained smoked mackerel? probably the least exotic Scottish fish you could put on a platter, c) going by the noises off by a couple who weren't convinced they'd had a meal despite having a platter each, it paled by comparison to other less pricey and more representative of the fantastic diversity of Scottish seafood available up and down the western seaboard. So with no choice but the limited menu my wife and I opted for a fantastic prawn cocktail (curiously not prawns but delicious langoustines) and mussels, nicely cooked in a delicious broth as starters. Sad to say the mains were average, well 1 was and the other sticky-chicken thing was devoid of imagination and skill albeit strong on monotone flavour. Breakfast was cheery and friendly but as an echo of the lack of 'restaurant' skills from the night before, the smoked salmon and scrambled eggs arrived with another enigma in the shape of a large wedge of lemon. No chives, or dill, or fennel even.. just scrambled eggs, salmon to the side and a chunk of lemon. Deconstructed? We stayed another night, Arisaig has a lovely quiet charm all of it's own, and the roads lead to some wonderful scenery but, having spied that the specials on the board were non-existent, we decided to eat elsewhere... Maybe the chef was on holiday? Maybe there was limited seafood available? Maybe...

author: 819IanF
title: Hundred pounds a night and no hot water!
text: Sadly we didn't have a good experience. The rooms are dated and in need of an upgrade. The spare blankets stank of dogs. Wifi was patchy and in the morning not available at all. The door on our room could not be locked from the inside. I thought this must be a recent glitch until I saw the problem was mentioned on Tripadvisor last August. Clearly fixing it is not a priority for the owners. Worst of all was the cold shower. It started hot and then went stone cold and stayed that way. A very unpleasant experience - and absolutely unacceptable for a room costing a hundred pounds. I mentioned the problem in the morning and was thanked for bringing it to their attention! I was told they were having problems with the boiler. After our visit I wrote pointing out the issues we'd had and asking them to consider a refund. Although I e-mailed twice, they did not have the courtesy to reply. I guess this sums up their attitude to their visitors. This place is in a fabulous location, but sadly it is absolutely not worth the money. I reckon seventy pounds a night would reflect what they offer.

author: namenotgiven
title: Memorable breakfast but a little disappointing overall
text: Breakfast was the best part. The toast was hot and tasty, the smoked salmon was plentiful and excellent quality, and the porridge was very good and served at just the right temperature and consistency. The choice of hot drinks was good and our waitress was truly helpful and friendly. The dining room is a little chilly and dark and gloomy in the morning though quite atmospheric for an evening meal. The location is excellent, just metres from the sea, and Arisaig harbour is very pretty with fine views to the Small Isles. In good weather the outdoor seating would be very pleasant. We were a little disappointed with our dinner. The service was again excellent and the food was very imaginatively presented and looked great, but unfortunately the taste didn't quite match its looks. To be fair, we had seen all the good reviews and were expecting something special, so perhaps our expectations were too high. We stayed in the annexe at the back, which has very dated furnishings and sentimental pictures that made me wince a little. You might feel more at ease if you have a tiny bit of nostalgia for the 1980s! But on the good side we were able to access our room from very early in the day, it was extremely clean and spacious, the beds were comfortable and it was nice to have a bath with plenty of towels. It was also very easy to nip in and out through the garden, and felt quite private. We couldn't hear what our neighbours were saying through the walls though we were aware of their presence. Unfortunately one of them snored very loudly - still, with earplugs, no problem. Contact with the owners was very limited, to the extent that without TripAdvisor we wouldn't have known when to turn up for breakfast. To be honest, we felt a little out of place, if not precisely unwelcome thanks to the excellent waiting staff.

author: erntravels
title: Lovely room and location on the way to Skye
text: (My reviews are a bit fussy. I would really rank this a 4.5 out of 5. A very very nice inn.) We picked this "Inn" (it is really more than a B&B since it has a restaurant) as a stopping point before taking the ferry to Skye. Our room (#5) faced the water per our request; the other rooms have little balconies looking out to the owner's garden.) The room included a wardrobe, dresser, small table and chair, the usual tea kettle. It was very quiet in spite of being over the dining room, probably because the dining room closes early. The bathroom had tissues, a small soap, hair dryer, and good counter space. The shower door was a bit awkward to use as it opened on the left right under the shower head itself.... so you run the shower to get the water warm, close the door, and then open it again to get in while the water is running. The view over the water is charming. The owner and his staff are very hospitable and based on our email exchanges in advance, we made our ferry reservations for the following morning so that we would have plenty of time for breakfast. Dinner was excellent. The dining room is small, but the food was great! We were offered choices for breakfast so I had scrambled eggs with salmon and my husband had kippers. Toast, juices, cereals, and coffee/tea were included. Parking is across the "main street" and wifi is included. This would be a lovely place to stay and explore the glens and lochs.

author: IanCarnoustie
title: Somewhat disappointing
text: Arriving in Arisaig last Saturday in the rain and mist, we received a warm friendly greeting from mine host, and our room was as advertised, looking out through the mist and rain westwards to what is on a clear day a glorious view. The evening meal however was somewhat disappointing. The Dining room was not overly warm, the heat from the stove effectively blocked to the whole room by a table right in front of it(lucky people sitting there.) There was also a constant draught from behind the bar area and door leading to the toilets, as I had to get up a few times to close the door during our meal. Irritating. The menu looked promising with specials advertised. However, everything seemed to be done at high speed. No offer of a pre dinner drink while perusing the menu, and my choice of wine by the glass caused a problem, as it initially was not available, until pointed out that the wine list specifically stated it was.The friendly waitress took our order, prawns in filo starters, although suspiciously industrial, were tasty enough. No sooner had we finished, than the vegetables arrived, very bland bowl of potatoes, carrots and sugar snap peas, which accompanied every dish. My wife's Mallaig haddock in Dunsyre Blue cheese was apparently well cooked, but rather smothered by a heavy sauce. My pork loin in apple and brandy was not good, covered in an indifferent sauce, lacking any tenderness or flavour. I explained to the waitress it was tough, and she said it would be mentioned to the chef. Nothing of that was heard. The dessert menu appeared thereafter at breakneck speed, as if everyone had to be out by 8.30pm. We managed to stall our selection for a while, and to be fair, when ordered, the sticky toffee pudding was excellent. We managed to get a move away from the draught later, and were asked, about 9.30ish if we wanted coffee, before the urn was turned off. A strange way of doing. So for the meal maybe 6/10, as it was also somewhat overpriced. The real disappointment probably lies with the innumerable reviews that say how good this establishment is -foodwise for us, sadly it was not quite what other reviews had promised.

author: LyndaGPearson
title: Fantastic Short Break
text: My friend and I have just returned from a visit to the Old Library in Arisaig. On arrival the hotel the owner Robert came out and took our bags to our room and made us feel very welcome. Our twin room was very comfortable and very clean. We were booked in for our evening meal and what a treat we were in for! The meal was excellent! Some of the best fresh sea food I have ever had. The menu was varied and the food beautifully presented. The staff were very polite and friendly. We decided the following day that we would like to book in for our evening meal again as our first night was so good, but thought that we might struggle for a table. We asked Robert if there were any tables free and he said that he had already kept us a table - just in case we wanted to eat there again so that we would not be disappointed! He said that he always looked after his guests first. I would definately recommend that you go and visit The Old Library. It is right on the sea front and just a few miles from some beautiful beaches. This is my second visit to this lovely small hotel. It certainly won't be my last!!

author: SophieJasmine
title: Peace, quiet and five star service
text: I had a fantastic two nights. Beautiful, peaceful village. The Lodge is right on the sea front in Arisaig next to the shop, post office and a stone's throw from the local pub and pier for the island cruises. I was looking for silence. I certainly found it here. Robert was extremely helpful and friendly...patiently meeting me in the street to carry my bag in when I called from about 30 seconds away...unsure of where I was. I was the only person staying on the first night - end of the season. Nevertheless I was made to feel extremely welcome: I had dinner in the dining room and it was all set up with tea lights and i received really attentive service. Delicious food. On my first morning, Robert helpfully rang to find out whether the island cruises would be going out and booked my place. He also lent me a map of the local area on my first afternoon so I could go out for a walk around the beautiful bay. He advised me too on the local bus routes. One of the staff let me know about the bag lock up in Mallaig too so I didn't have to lug a heavy bag around there after my departure from Arisaig while waiting for the steam train. Wifi in the room, a good size TV and a bath in the ensuite bathroom all made for a really enjoyable stay. Tasty breakfast with good choice of local food on the menu. I was surprised to find such a gourmet place in a tiny village! Thank you to all at the Old Library for such a great stay. I hope to return someday.

author: TadaGanIarracht
title: Book with Confidence
text: On arriving I was shown my room by Robert. He was very relaxed and easy to get on with, The room he took me to was MASSIVE. I was really happy with the room. There was the usual kettle with coffee and tea in the room, lots of storage for clothes and things you may have with you and a good wall mounted tv that was handy for watching films from my netbook.. The shower was great, it had a good pressure behind it and was nice and relaxing. The dinner I had after arriving was great as were the other two meals that I had. The portions were generous, and it was well presented if thats what you are after. I had chicken in a white wine sauce with wild mushrooms on the first night, I think the second it was grilled trout with a roasted red pepper sauce and the third it was a venison pie. Breakfast was very filling if you wanted it to be and on at least one day meant that I was not hungry at lunch time. Locally I did not need much but there was a wee shop right next to the Lodge so if i needed anything I had forgotten or wanted maps etc I only had a matter of yards to walk. As soon as you leave the lodge you are treated to a view of the bay and moored boats. One evening Robert and a chap staying at the lodge were playing guitar so I was treated to a good playlist of music and singing! Another evening Robert mentioned a walk which I did not go far in but bumped into four stags and what I think is a buzzard sitting on a tree stump. Lovely. All in all a great visit and a shame that I didnt have the day time to spend relaxing (too busy with work). Next time work takes me to that area I will book here again without hesitation.

author: I7987WJbriang
title: Lot of fun
text: Great place to stay. It’s quiet, safe and nice but then again so is the whole town. The pizza place next to it is awesome and walkable. It’s right outside the National park and worth it for anyone going. Go directly through their website or call them to make your plans. Don’t go through a third party website, they’ll give you a better deal. First off the room. It’s clean, roomy and safe. Perfect for a family. They have an in Ground pool but it was to cold to use when we went. They have a playground and tons of games. My kids LOVED the shuffle board and tether ball. At night there was a fire and we got to hangout with some people and even the general managers came to sit and talk with us for a while. It was a nice personal touch. The continental breakfast was really good. The coffee was great and I liked the eggs and potatoes. I didn’t catch the name of the young man working breakfast this morning but he was very friendly and hardworking. He also gave us a great tip about parking in Boulder which ended up really helping us. Overall I loved this place. It’s definitely where we’ll stay when we go back someday.

author: Jamil_Sayed
title: Great hospitality and very pleasant experience
text: This hotel is at a distance from downtown in a quiet area. There is a lake a few steps away from the hotel. We stayed here for 2 nights from the 29th September 2018. We booked one apartment with two bedrooms.We were allotted room No. 359. The beds and pillows were comfortable. Linens and towels were new and spotless. Everything was neat and clean. Really unbelievable in such a small town. The house keeping lady is sweet person with smiling face from probably Mexico. she does not know English, but she is a great & kind woman. She supplied more towels and she was up in a jiffy to deliver them. The suite was very clean. The WiFi was good. Definitely we will stay here again. The staff was super friendly and easy check in and out. Love the hospitality!!! The complementary breakfast was great at this place. Very pleasant experience.

author: fishonMi
title: Cozy, Quiet and Friendly
text: We started going to Estes 8 yrs. ago because we like The Rockies and the elk. Each year the elk come down from the mountains and take over the town for 5/6 wks. They congregate on the golf course as well as wherever they want. So exciting. The first year we stayed at the Murphy’s Lodge and this time Murphy’s Resort. One is closer to downtown and the resort outside of town. The managers are friendly as is all the staff. They make you feel at home. They are updating the resort and the rooms are nice. Big, spacious area inside. Good beds as far as mattress and pillows. Clean bathrooms and another area with sink/mirror. Window in this area to let in the sunshine and view of Estes Lake. The resort has many things to do for families but in the warm climate. Hot tub open all year. Reasonably priced and I understand discounted in the fall. We had beautiful weather and good time.

author: F8120LManitam
title: Very good experience
text: Stayed 5 nights in Sept while visiting RMNP. Rooms were comfortable for the two of us. Liked the fact that the A/C could be put in fan only mode to provide a steady background sound to mask out any snoring noises, etc. We both slept very well. We used the hot tub and laundry facilities. Hot tub are was too hot during the day with the hot sun baking you through the enclosed glassed in area with no ventilation. I did not measure the temperature but it seemed like about 110 Fahrenheit. But it was great at night without the sun beating down on you. If you use hot tub during the day consider sun screen and sun glasses and drink liquids so you do not dehydrate. There is one washer and one drier. I think the drier is not heating properly - maybe a heating element is out. The dryer does not get near as hot as my 20 year old home dryer. So the clothes never got dry. It was not because we overloaded it, but again the dryer just did not get very hot. We ate breakfast there all 5 mornings.It was not what we are used to at other motels. It would be nice to have had scrambled eggs, potatoes, sausage or bacon, cooked oat mill (not the instant individual serving kind), and perhaps a waffle machine.The last morning, Sunday, Sept 23, they did serve scrambles eggs and potatoes. Dave was wonderful as the breakfast area attendant. He kept the eating area spotless and was very personable. All in all, I would probably stay here again if I return to Estes Park. .

author: KellyW3138
title: Nice Stay
text: We booked at the last minute as was surprised we were able to get two rooms. Rates seemed reasonable at the time of booking. They also do vacation rentals. This was a quick stay and didn’t get to see much that evening. Our day was spent exploring town, horseback riding and the Stanley Hotel and a nice dinner at La Cabana Mexican Bar Restaurant. Upon arrival there was a sip and painting class going on. Looked fun but didn’t know about it prior. Rooms were clean and nice. There is a pool and spa, picnic area, fire pit, games outside for kids and dvd rentals and a breakfast in the morning. We left early and did not partake in this. No alcohol in picnic areas. You can drink it outside your room. There is a table and chairs outside your room. Located a few blocks from town. Enjoy.

author: jenniferfG2699OR
title: We will not be returning
text: It was nothing like we expected, it was so much less. Upon arrival we quickly realized it looked nothing like the pictures online and was in fact a cheap motel not a resort. We went with Murphy's because it claimed to be pet friendly however, at check in you sign a paper stating that your dog will not go on any part of the property except inside your room and a disgusting rock covered area where your dog has to use the bathroom. If you leave your dog in the room alone it has to be crated. The room itself felt dingy and cheap. The carpet is directly on the concrete and is 1/4 inch thin, your comforter is stack of 4 sheets, and I am 5'6 and the shower head did not go up higher than my chest. During our stay we spent several hours listening to the sound of drilling, and sawing as they did repairs to the siding of our room. Management was called and they did not care one little bit and did nothing to resolve the issue. Breakfast if you want to call it that consisted of mini plain bagels, danishes, bananas, and rotten hardboiled eggs. Most people staying in Estes were there to hike and several guests including ourselves were confused as to why there were no protein or healthy carb options for breakfast. The hotel offers overpriced smore kits you can purchase. We did so and were given the old display bag and a single cheap roasting stick and that was it. They had nothing to start a fire and we had to ask around until we found matches. We were very disappointed with Murphy's Resort as this was our first time in Estes and we expected a lot more. We will not be returning.

author: JenDugieMac
title: Just ehhhh
text: We booked Murphy’s to take a one night “staycation”. We were mostly excited about the large hot tub they have & the fact that they advertised a bar/snack area with lots of games. When we checked in we were told our kids, age 4 & 6, are not able to use the hot tub because it’s 18 & older. We were able to use the heated pool at their sister property which was fine but they clearly have a wasp problem judging by all the wasp catchers up in the pool area. It’s also a drive to the other side of town to get to the sister property. After swimming we decided to check out the bar/snack area. It offered seating for 5 people (3 seats at the bar & a love seat) with no room to play games. The bar offered beer or boxed wine (Franzia) by the glass.....or plastic cup rather. The snacks were frozen hot pockets or frozen cheese burgers. We were looking for a place to hang out outside of our room, and this area lacked space & wine offerings. Dominos is the only restaurant that delivers. They do offer a large selection of movies that you can check out which we enjoyed. The rooms were clean & comfortable. Breakfast the next morning left much to be desired. It was store bought muffins, cereal, bagels & hard boiled eggs. The manager on duty did offer a free bottle of water upon check out with a note encouraging us to give them a 5 Star review......I’m sorry but I just can’t give them one! I’m sure this hotel has a lot to offer families in the summer but we won’t be returning for another winter “staycation”!

author: MyLifeofAdventures
title: Great value and super dog friendly
text: I stayed here for a few days before Christmas with my boyfriend, his mother and sister, and our two dogs. We had booked it a few months in advance since everything else in the area had ridiculous minimum booking restrictions and we only needed 2 nights, not 5. The hotel itself is nice and comfortable. The room we had was just big enough for the 4 of us (plus our 2 dogs), but we fit comfortably enough. The couch in the living room pulls out into a bed, although they could use some mattress support because it was your standard couch bed with a terribly uncomfortable bar that hangs out by your back. It was also a little disappointing that the fireplace works on a timer so you only get like 10 or 15 minutes before you have to get up and turn it on again. The room is obviously heated so it's not necessary, but who doesn't love a nice fire when it's snowing outside? We were thrilled to have a kitchen, though. It has the basics - 4 plates, silverware, some pots and pans to cook with, and some salt and pepper - as well as a two burner stove. Very simple, but better than having to eat out every meal! The staff was wonderful and helpful whenever we needed anything. They even had treats for our pups, and have one of their own in the office occasionally. The breakfast is continental, but the had hard boiled eggs in the fridge which was nice. Location wise, Murphy's is about a 5-minute drive to town, so it's very convenient. The view is awesome as well! Overall, Murphy's is nothing spectacular if you're looking for fancy, but if you want functional for a reasonable price, this is a great choice!

author: mboston1129
title: Holiday vacation at Murphy's Resort!
text: It is so hard to find starting point when reviewing Murphy's Resort because we had such a great experience. We had an extended vacation so we were able to stay at 2 locations Murphy's has to offer but the experience started at check in with a staff more than happy to help you and even give some pointers on things to do and places to see while visiting Estes Park. The first place we stayed at was a very nice and newly renovated house that had privacy and all the personal touches your own home would have (this place was referred to as "clover") a home that within a couple of hours of getting situated felt like your own home. It was spacious had everything we needed and the staff made sure to let us know if we needed anything they would bring it right over. Awsome first week of our vacation. The second week we wanted to be a little closer to the resort (btw when staying at off property locations you can still use the resort and lodge pool and hot tub amenities!) So we stayed at "summit view" an on property apartment/house (3 bed 3 bath apt...basically a house lol) this one was my wife's favorite because it had a real fire place and a lake view. Even though it was part of the resort it felt like a separate house because it had it's own entrance but you still had direct access to resort amenities and the awsome staff who didn't blink an eye if you needed something! For a family it was a great vacation not just because of the great service and amenities, but because you could tell there was family value and comfort behind It! My wife and myself are very busy people and the little things we found at both locations were a refreshing dose of family time. There is a collection of board games at both locations that we stayed at (we played a lot of games haha) and you have those at home but don't think how much they connect a family until you have some time to play and have fun. And then there's the massive DVD collection over 100 at both places, I think we had more fun going through the dvds and arguing over what one to watch than actually watching them! There was cable or satellite too of course, but no commercials with dvds! Too many little things to list like kids toys, box fans, etc....all the things you wish you had on vacation. Last but definitely not least the thing we all take For granted, a good night's sleep! The beds and pillows are amazing! Not sure what brand they are but there's was comfort in mind for sure! I could rant forever but Murphy's is my "go to place" in Estes Park!!

author: russkwtx
title: Great place for families
text: We stayed here for two nights in August 2017 and had a very enjoyable experience. The hotel ("resort") is not luxurious but it is very convenient and comfortable; plus it is quite affordable compared to some other places in Estes. I should say right off that we were a couple but this "resort" is absolutely perfect for families with children. The resort really offers a lot of activity to keep the little ones busy. There are board games, free DVDs, a pool, outdoor games, and a hot tub. Plus the marina is minutes away if the family wants to go on the lake. Our experience: the room was clean and the bed was soft. We had a view of the mountains and the lake. The room price includes free continental breakfast, which was convenient and adequate. The room had a flat screen TV and DVD player. My quibbles: the walls are thin so you can hear people next door walking (the buildings are one story but it sounds like they are above you). The check in time is late at 4pm and the check out is early at 11am. Our room had a fly swatter but no box of kleenex. The staff was friendly and helpful. Overall, we enjoyed our stay and I would consider returning the next time we are in Estes.

author: DanMeg1
title: Great place for famlies!
text: We stayed here the week of the 4th of July while visiting family and we couldn't be happier. We stayed in a lake side view room. The room was spacious with mini fridge, microwave, coffee maker and tv. Beds were comformable and the a/c worked very well. The grounds were kept very clean by a friendly and hard working staff, all of whom were great! There was everything to do, as has been stated in other reviews. Pool is big and pool toys are provided. Kids loved being able to use bikes that are provided. Breakfast is provided with something for everyone! The owners are really involved and friendly. They were there everyday checking the grounds and helping the staff, very impressive. Best of all, they are pet friendly, my 90 lb German Shepherd was very welcomed. After spending a week at Murphy's, I can honestly tell you that you don't have to look any further, this is the place to stay!!! We will be back and we highly recommend. Thank you to the owners and staff for an amazing week!

author: nicolediane
title: Great option in Estes Park
text: Room was clean and the beds were comfortable. The small window air conditioner did the trick even though it was very hot. Had everything you needed, coffee pot and fridge. Had a fireplace which we didn't use. An old fashioned drive up to your room motel spot like a lot in Este Park. Lots of activities for kids. Nice, clean pool. There was playground equipment and games outside, a fire pit and picnic tables. Board games in the lobby in case of rain or for after dinner. Big indoor hot tub for adults. happy hour specials on drinks in the lobby bar area. Free popcorn in the afternoon. Bottled water and treat at checkout. Lots of extra little things that made it nice. Fair price too. We thought breakfast was the only thing that could have been done better. Not much to choose from. Milk was in gallon jugs in a little fridge. Coffee left a lot to be desired. One morning we opted to eat in a restaurant.

author: ypw22
title: First Visit to Estes Park
text: I took my 18 year old son on a trip to Colorado at the beginning of June. This was our first time visiting this great state! We knew we wanted to visit Estes Park, but having never been there before had no idea where to stay. We found Murphy's on tripadvisor and it had great reviews so we decided to give it a try! We were SO GLAD we did!! Murphy's is a very clean and fun place to stay right outside the city of Estes Park, very convenient. We were always greeted by very friendly and helpful staff each time we went into the office. There is a fun map of the city and the desk workers were more than willing to give suggestions for dinner and things to do when asked! The breakfast each morning was simple but good. Our lake-view room was very spacious and clean, A/C worked well, and there was a refrigerator. Each night at dusk a fire was made in the fire pits and it was so relaxing to sit outside by the fire and enjoy the sunsets and cool breezes after a long day of sightseeing. We also enjoyed the free DVD "rentals"...tons to choose from! We didn't have time to use them, but there were several bikes and games and picnic table and grills to use as well. The pool/hot tub areas were clean, even a ping pong table poolside. The hot tub is inside a greenhouse type structure, would have preferred it to be outside as it was very warm in the building and not very many of the windows could be opened. Loved this place and would definitely go back!

author: WendyBillingsMcCoy
title: Great time!
text: I won a free 2 night stay here. We added on an extra night and an extra room. 4 of us went up. We had car trouble so Ubered up from Lyons. The staff was so awesome! We told them our trouble and they helped us out a lot. Rooms were newly renovated and new beds. So comfortable. Mini fridge and microwave. We've stayed here before and they are really updating everything. The grounds are nice. Picnic tables, grills, fire pit, play ground, etc. Free breakfast, dvd's, to watch. Small wine and beer bar for Happy hour. They let us check out late because our shuttle wasn't picking us up till 12:30. All of the staff was great!

author: fawnkhess
title: We are coming back to visit Murphy's Resort
text: I am over the moon excited that we have planned our second trip to Estes Park. My 40th birthday is in October, yes I am getting my butt over that hill and my daughter's 5th birthday is the day after mine, we decided what better place to celebrate than Estes Park and of course stay at Murphy's Resort again. We stayed there July 2016 to celebrate my parent's anniversary. We fell in love with everything about it. My dad is 80 and my daughter was 3 at the time and it was perfect for the whole family. There are so many places to choose from at Estes Park. Murphy's Resort has everything and it's the most family friendlies along with the nicest place to stay. The pull out sofa bed is the only thing my daughter will sleep on. Even though the King Rooms say on 2 people, you have the sofa bed that pulls out. When we made our reservations my daughter told me she wanted the sofa bed again. It's perfectly located especially if you want to be close to town and everything, but away from the craziness and traffic. Beautiful Lake Estes views and mountain views. We were there in July and a heard of the Elk just decided to come to the resort and welcome all the guest. Can't wait to celebrate my 40th birthday with our Murphy's Resort family! See you in October!

author: EmMirW
title: Great Value, Great View
text: My husband and I stayed one night using a Living Social promotion. The price was low enough to make me a little nervous about what we might find. However, there was absolutely nothing to worry about. We got exceptionally friendly service when I called to make reservations, when I called about a late arrival, and each time we interacted with the front desk. I haven't made a reservation by phone in a while, but the person I spoke to made it a pleasant, quick, and easy experience, even with a Living Social voucher to apply. It's a medium-sized complex with several one story units of outdoor entry rooms. Our room was about average size for a king room, maybe a little larger, but the furniture was a bit more homey than a typical hotel's. The bathroom was a decent size with newer fixtures. Ours had only a standup shower, but we were specifically informed of that when we made reservations. The decor was a little eclectic, but the room was clean and welcoming. The bed was comfortable, and it was an incredibly quiet place, so we had wonderful sleep after a long day of traveling. We did have to turn on the air even though it was February, as we woke up far too warm, but that did the trick. The mountains are visible from almost anywhere on the grounds, and there were elk on the property in the morning. There is a complimentary breakfast, offering a few cereals, muffins, breads, yogurt, juice, coffee, and hard-boiled eggs. It's not fancy, but it was plenty for us to get our day started. We didn't get a chance to use the hot tub or borrow any of the many board games or DVDs available in the office, but would have liked to. If we are fortunate enough to get back to the area, we would be glad to stay there again. I wouldn't call it fancy, but it was clean, comfortable, and cozy.

author: biancas61886
title: Relaxing family fun
text: Stayed in the queen suite with a jacuzzi tub. Both rooms were large and clean. Jacuzzi tub was exactly what we needed. Rented a movie from the office and had some free popcorn. We also borrowed a game since it was chilly outside. If it had been warmer there were multiple locations on the property to sit outside and enjoy a fire or a rest in a hammock. Gazebos, gas grills picnic tables, teather ball places, shuffle board, ladder ball, bocce ball, bean bag toss, horseshoes, and gigantic jinga games were available for play outside. There were also two different playgrounds for the kids. This is a great place for families and couples. Very quite and everything within walking distance. The bar on sight has a good variety however no local beers. There is a liquor store next door. For restaurants Fajita Rita's and the Hunter's Chop House is next to it. The pool was closed for the season but looked large and had lots of seating in the poolside area. The hot tub was inside where the vending machines were and was very large. However kids are not allowed so we stuck to our jacuzzi tub in our room. The office staff is really friendly and helpful! The continental breakfast was a perfect start to our day. I would recommend this to anyone looking for a down home place away from home.

author: sjderosia
title: September at Murphy's
text: We stayed at Murphy's resort on our recent trip to Estes Park. My husband, myself, and our dog, Tango stayed 3 nights and had a wonderful time. The property was open and clean and had everything we might want or need, including a hot tub, barbecues, lots of picnic areas and best of all was right on the lake!. When we checked in around 5 pm we were greeted like family and even had a nice happy hour beer & wine with Jake, who checked us in and made us feel very welcome. When we checked our room we opened the curtains to find a perfect view of lake and mountains with nothing but a field to disturb that view. The sun was beginning to set and there were 15 elk in the field!!! What a welcome!! We spent 4 days hiking and driving through the park and we also kayaked at the lake. The marina at the lake rents kayaks, canoes, and boats and is within walking distance from the resort. The lake is small and quiet, perfect for kayaking. There is a playground at the lake as well. There is a paved walk all around the lake that is perfect for morning and evening strolls. They were very dog friendly with areas for doggy business with pick up bags supplied. We were only going to stay for 2 nights but decided right away to add a night and Jake was very helpful with this. Tango was introduced to the owners dog Stella, a beautiful standard poodle! We loved this resort and will definitely be back for a longer visit soon.

author: dustyparker
title: Very Pet Friendly
text: Stayed here for 2 nights in a King room. Room was very clean and they are very welcoming to dogs. You can rent a crate for $5 a night. Room was large with a king bed and a sofa, coffee table, and a table and two chairs, microwave and small fridge.. Staff were very friendly and helpful. Some rooms have a lake view, although the property is set back. This seems like an older motel that has been refurbished to some extent. No stairs which was great for our older dog and why I choose the property. One disappointment was the hot tub which I knew was inside a separate building, but I did not realize how warm the room would be! Yikes it was warm in there. Used one night but not the second. It would likely be very nice in the winter, but it was fairly warm in the evening that we went. Easy access parking. I think it would be a nice setup for families and family activities. They have games and movies you can check out. I would 't choose it for a romantic getaway, but if you want a clean, inexpensive place to stay or you have a dog, this place will be fine. Also, it is on the east side of town. It's on the highway but it was quiet and away from the hustle and bustle. You can't walk to town though, if you're interested in doing that.

author: gossettmk
title: Their Grand Estates Property was everything we imagined and more!
text: Find this property on VRBO #867486. The photos for this property truly depict reality! This home was beautiful and comfortable for our group of 9 people (2 families).
