(Extra tip: they have some very capable ladies stationed at the front desk who also happen to be very cute) Third, the Verona Roofdeck is as chill as it gets. The view of the metal skyline is just magnificent. Perfect for an afternoon coffee or apéritif. Also a great place to have a late meeting followed by a couple of drinks. Lastly, the rooms. The rooms are pretty good too! What really made our event legendary was the epic attentiveness of the staff. These guys surely understand what it takes to run a hotel and to please its customers. Cheers, Privato! We'll be back

author: 18vinm
title: Mother's day staycation
text: Room - small but okay. Bed is great very comfym should have more pillows but okay. Tv is great. Blower is nice. View of the city is fab! Room space is a little bit small. Should have more table. Restroom - okay but easily gets dirty but okay. Love the shower. Towels arent soft. Pls invest on it. Pool - great for kids not for adults. But dtill nice. I love where its located. Service was good. Not for a 5 star one but definitely worth the price of 2100. Ü

author: ilocanotraveller
title: For the price we got, it's bang for the buck
text: We got a really good deal from a discount website. One night came out just $40. For that amount we got two comfortable queen size beds, a hot shower, a working A/C, an LCD TV with USB socket, and free WIFI. Check in and check out were both a breeze. Less than a 5 minute wait. Having said that, you get what you pay for. Here are some caveats to look out for, unless you already know them from previous posts. Parking is limited. The parking floors can accommodate not more than 8 cars per floor, which we found such a waste of space. I might be nitpicking already, but the floor is not carpeted. This being the case, we could constantly hear the footsteps outside our door. Also, the shower stall does not have an enclosure. The shower head is pointed towards the wall, so it's not necessarily messy, but if you're not careful, you might end up having a wet bathroom floor. The window only has a single curtain, instead of the usual double, which means when you open it, the people across the other building can see you inside. Lastly, they only give you one key card, which makes leaving the room turned on a challenge. Since the key card is needed to turn on the lights and A/C in the room, and also to operate the elevator, one has to sacrifice electricity in the room if one has to use the elevator. Either I leave the key card in the room so my family can continue watching TV and I just ask someone to wave their key card in the elevator so I can use it, or I bring the key card with me and leave my family in the dark. I wish they just gave us two key cards to lessen the hassle.

author: little_traveller731
title: Good Price, Good Location, Average Service
text: We stayed here during the Holy Week season and here are the good things about this place: 1. Rooms are reasonably priced 2. Bed sheets, pillows are clean 3. Rooms are generally clean 4. amazing view at the roofdeck ; nice place to chill and have a few drinks 5. Free wifi 6. Lots of restaurants near the area - Capitol Commons or the Kapitolyo Area The not so good: 1. most of the housekeeping staff during our stay were interns; if you ask them for certain policies, they wouldn't know what to say. we had to supervise them when they cleaned the room. 2. There were no towels at the pool area, they blamed it on the high occupancy rate, c'mon! 3. there was a smell of sewage coming from our room toilet and bath 4. parking is a pain! limited slots and horrible space 5. Nothing special with the food served at the roof deck, a bit pricey 6. small pool with ledges on top, if you want to sunbathe, then this is not the place to go to In general, this is a nice place to stay within the metro, reasonably priced, good location and nice roof deck. The flaws are forgivable given the positive sides mentioned above. Enjoy your stay!

author: BarnesPerez
title: The Latest Modern Hotel in Pasig City
text: Since it opened, I've always wanted to try this hotel in Pasig. By sheer luck, I was able to book it for a night due to a "secret special deal" in Agoda. I am quite surprised to see that it only cost less than PHP 2,000 (exclusive of government tax and service charge) for a "3.5-star hotel" (there goes your tip - *wink*). Perhaps it's because I booked it one day before the visit. Going there by car, parking was quite easy on this Christmas time on a weekend, but limited (4 parking floors with about less than 10 slots per floor) for all 117 rooms. Elevator though is quite slow. They only have 2 (can you believe that?) servicing more than 20 floors! No wonder staff were very courteous and accommodating because it is being managed by Enderun Hospitality Management (of Enderun Colleges in BGC), which is a well-known third-party management company. Staff named "DJ" addressed our request to have 3 boxes of edible food to be stored in their kitchen cold storage overnight without any additional charge. I'm not sure if this applies to all guests though so better ask them. If your peeve is noise at night, then you might want to reconsider because it's very near Capital Commons, which had big loud speakers at this very same night we visited. We did not avail of their breakfast, but it's optional. Although I think you will be eating within the same lobby floor. This might be a problem for those people who don't prefer this set-up. I'm not sure if they will permit you to bring your food inside the room, but they might consider it since they allow you to make your own coffee inside. The only downside (or upside perhaps) is that they have given me a Deluxe Double Queen room instead of Executive King that I booked online. I'm not sure if this was a courtesy upgrade or an honest mistake. Nevertheless, I was not complaining. :) The room is new, with a small fridge for canned and bottled drinks only, cable TV (SkyCable), Wi-Fi (good for at least two devices simultaneously), hot and cold water, clothing cabinet, a safe, two pairs of slippers and dental kits, and other pertinent toiletries. Overall, this was such a pleasant experience and will definitely go back or refer this to others.

author: staycationista0610
title: Excellent service, so so room
text: We checked in at this cause it's new and we have a run at bgc. When we first came in immediately the bell boy welcomed us even though we're still at the parking area getting off from the car. He took our bag and ushered us to the reception are. The was well designed as seen from their website, the couches were clean and new. There were two elevators and both have an attendant, which were courteous as the bell boy who assisted us. When we got to our floor (10th Flr.) the hallway was not ventilated or doesn't have air conditioning as should be expected in a hotel, I was a bit disappointed by that. When we got to our room and the bell boy opened it, as what the others say on their reviews there was still a distinctive smell, because it's still new. The room we got was so cramped, but for the price that we paid it was okay I guess (2699 without breakfast) but I was expecting a little bit of more room space. There's no place for you to eat properly, although there were tables they were not meant for eating. The head board was a good touch, my boyfriend liked it, the bed was good and relaxing but it's missing the mattress topper for that extra comfort. The bathroom was okay but when you shower it gets flooded easily, the drainage was located directly from where the water from the shower falls. The toiletries were okay although I always bring my own stuff, for some reason I forgot to bring my brush and they don't have a comb included in their kit. The tv was a bit small, but the mounting of the tv was okay. All in all the experience was okay but not the great, their price is still at introductory price until August. There is still a lot to improve at this hotel, when they charge their regular price it will be considered as over priced.

author: FIdes2013
title: Good choice for the budget
text: The hotel lobby and facade has an impressive design. Well-lighted and clean. It is relatively new and the room paint still smells. We requested for freshener but were transferred to another room instead. The room size is just right. Twin beds were big enough and comfortable. The room and bathroom are clean and clean linens and toiletries were provided. The bathroom is small but clean. Cable tv and signal is great with a lot of program choices. We checked in at about 2am and we requested for a late check out. We were extended until 6pm. That was very accommodating of them since most hotels do not allow that. Location is along the main road. Near fastfood restos. Easy to get taxi except on rush hours. Many jeepneys ply the area. Room service is good enough. Staff are very polite and accommodating.

author: DrBK
title: soft opening still underway, but great promise
text: Stayed as a couple in a King Executive Room. Facilities extremely new and clean, airconditioning powerful. Late check-out given easily. Check-in also a relatively seamless process. Bed size generous and welcome in room. More on the firm size, consistent with most in SEA. Shower "open" style with no door or curtain completely closing, making for a large mess. Furnishings modern and spotless. TV works wonderfully with many cable and local channels available. Gym basic consisting primarily of cross-trainer and treadmill. Pool deck not open yet, and not open for viewing, on our stay. Facility seems overstaffed and under-advertised at this stage, understandable given soft opening and not at full capacity. Often see staff standing around talking, waiting for jobs (gives somewhat of an unprofessional feel). However, always polite service. Location very convenient and close to transport. Ample parking (at this stage) available. Fantastic value at this stage for business stays while still at the soft opening stage. Shows great value. Will certainly be back as a (currently) budget hotel with upmarket studio apartment feel.

author: mervynr49
title: Superb
text: It is difficult to write a review of this fine Hotel On arrival, the welcome from the reception staff was excellent. We were registered very efficiently. They took our baggage from the car and we parked our car in there large underground garage – free of charge. It was > 100m from our room. They then took us to our room, which was very large. They then brought our baggage. This hotel is privately owned and is almost 100 old. However, the original building has been rebuilt and now there are five houses. We were very surprised with the spacious restaurant. There were different dishes for both breakfast and dinner. It fact one evening there was 127 different cheeses to choose from. The hotel has extensive water faculties at least five pools and at least 12 saunas / steam rooms in a fine naturist setting. We stayed 11 nights and found all the staff to be always very pleasant and helpful. This was especially true for the reception staff. It was one of the best hotels we have stayed at and as a former UN Consultant I visited > 60 Countries. One the problems with the hotel is its size it was almost five minutes walk to the restaurant! It is one a hillside so there are many lifts (two broke down whilst we were there)! However, there is no lift to the swimming areas – only stairs! The latter is the only real complaint!

author: lparker
title: Fabulous stay again at the Post Hotel!
text: This is my second stay at the wonderful Post Hotel and everything was fabulous! Highlights include: Wonderful meals - so much choice at the buffet in addition to the “specials” offered at every meal (ask your waiter). Also a v good wine list. Spa and pool and all other facilities wonderful. My room was modern and stunning (room 428). So quiet, clean and beautiful. Very modern and stunning. There’s a free pass for the bus around the region - ask at reception - and free bikes to explore the lake. We also had a free make over (“make up tips” session at the spa on the programme). Staff are kind and attentive. If you are an English speaking only visitor I’d also suggest: Ask for a tour of the hotel at the beginning of your stay. This makes it easier to see everything that’s available and for the staff to explain the nude only areas, the sports programme, what’s free, what’s not etc. All signs and information for the hotel is in German. They can also book transfers, help with the bus times, times for the cable car etc. There’s two local supermarkets if you want to buy anything and a local cafe (not that you will need it - there is more wonderful food than you could ever consume at the hotel). Thanks Post Hotel and your staff!

author: ValarieA728
title: Worth a trip just for a small mountain village
text: I had the opportunity for a short vacation after a conference in Innsbruck and I chose Posthotel after reading about the horse back riding in Alpine trials on Lipizzaners. In this part of Tyrol, hikers are everywhere with their poles and backpacks. Even bikers navigate the mountain roads and have special lanes in the city People learn English in school and are helpful if you ask for directions which is a good thing since often signs are only in German. My hotel room had a view of the Alps and a cosy bathrobe for frequent trips down the hall to the spa for facials and massages which eased any sore muscles from the variety of exercise possibilities. The pools, salt and fresh indoor and out, are heated to 30 or 35 C. What a surprise to find that salt water pools swell up from far below the Alps! Even some rain isn't a problem since there is tea time in the lobby with a sumptuous selection of pastries and a huge bowl of whipped cream to dollop on everything.. Lunch is a buffet with a soup and salad bar. Everything is included,even a spa menu. Dinner, however, is too luxurious to forego. Daily activities include organized hikes, bike rides, hotel tours with highlights that might include bread baking or a demonstration of room preparation. Of course, horse back riding lessons or trail rides are available. The exercise rooms are open and the classes range from Pilates to Zumba. A Chinese instructor for tai chi, qi dong, and meditation, gave a demonstration of sword skills for an evening reception that introduced the Reiter family who began the stables and major staff members. The village has little more to offer but nothing else is necessary to restore a sense of well being even if you are traveling solo.

author: TravelDocKleen11
title: Austrian Charm
text: A very beautiful and scenic drive coming from Italy, leave the Brenner at Achensee. You are rewarded with the most spectacular panoramas of mountains, lakes and below lying villages!! The Post Hotel Achenkirch visit was a Pistop and gee what a pit-stop. Vettel could not wish for more!!. We parked the car across the street (below the hotel) on the church grounds. The charming waiter (Maxim) informed us that dining on the Terrace was reserved for hotel guests only. He joked about how busy the terrace was and gallantly (Austrian Charm) took us to a table, promptly our glasses of champagne appeared. A bit too chilly for this time of the year, the external heating was on and soft blankets readily available. The magnificent alpine air instilled huge appetite and we were excited about our order of flank of veal steak and grilled Samlet. It did not disappoint!! Hmmmm....pity we had to skip the wine as we still had some driving to do to our destination in Germany. However, I had a "teaspoon"of Grappa Paola Berta, at €22.00, the finest Grappa after an opulent dinner. Maxim did well in enticing us into having the chocolate bomb (-chen) tiny, accompanied by local berries and homemade ice cream...hmmmmmm, is all I can say. Girls.....get over there. Armed with the hotel Brochures etc, we left happy, contented, spoiled and with an aftertaste for more, we booked there for next September.

author: traveller90210
title: The Lipizzaners!
text: We planned a two week driving trip in Germany / Austria and my wife looked very hard to include a chance to ride horses in the Alps. We chanced upon Achenkirch and their stable of Lipizzaners. After all, a few days later we would be in Vienna to see the stallions perform at the Spanish Riding School. Great choice. My wife did have the ride of her life in the Alps and said it was fantastic. She would love to do it again. We came here for the riding and it did not disappoint. The hotel itself was excellent. It is a beautiful resort and spa in a beautiful setting. Although we didn't take advantage of the spa or swimming pools I imagine that it gets many repeat customers who come for a weekend get away. The rooms were spacious and comfortable. Staff excellent and friendly. Meals were outstanding. We were given a table for our first dinner and then each subsequent meal we were seated at the same table. Would definitely do it again. The one thing that I would like to see improved is the wifi. It was not available in our room.

author: Midorosan
title: Read My Shirt
text: We have stayed in many wellness hotels in Austria and we looked forward to this new experience in a different location on the basis is it always good to see other places. We should have known better and we should have checked with Trip Advisor first. I have just read a few reviews which clearly reflect similar views. This is a family hotel like many Austrian hotels and full of the fake hoflichkeit that one often encounters. The service was poor from our first arrival at reception until the day we ended our stay four days early. We were prepared to put up with the poor service and the very average food as we just wanted a nice break in the Tirol but things went from bad to worse. The much vaunted Wellness area is miserable in comparison to some of the great wellness hotels, the facilities are poor and the staff minimal with one major exception. Tired of the limited facilities in the family area which we had to share with small children and grannies we decided to check out the Undergound Temple where all the so called good stuff was. I, my chinese wife and my married daughter went together to the sauna/steam area, a notice on the wall said this was a quiet and naked area. We did not want to go naked so we attempted to enter one of the small steam rooms while wearing our swimsuits. Suddenly a man appeared fully clothed who told us that we must take our clothes off, we declined and tried to enter the steam room whereupon he seized the door which I was holding and wrenched it from my grasp almost throwing me to the floor and seriously wrenching my shoulder. I suggested he go and get his boss and it was then that he told me in the most arrogant way I have ever encountered from someone in the hospitality industry that he was the boss and to prove it asked me to "Read my Shirt" on which was printed across the back Sauna Meister. If it hadn't been so serious I would have laughed but at 72 years old I was still smarting from the pain in my shoulder. We gave up the fight and told them we would like to see a manager, I was passed off with a receptionist but later that evening we met in the bar with the very young son of the owner who sadly did not have any idea how to deal with the situation and tried to convince us that it was all our fault and that naked was the way it was in this and all wellness hotels in the region which of course is nonsense as my Austrian son-in-law was quick to point out. He would not make the slightest concession and when we said we would checkout in the morning he made no attempt to apologise for this extraordinary experience. The hallmark of a good hotel is how they deal with a problematic situation for it is this that will remain in the memory of the guest. This hotel like base metal does not have a hallmark and I would not recommend it in anyway.

author: HingLaw
title: A Hostel with a Sense of Commune
text: First thing first, everyone from the staff to the volunteers at Hostel One Sevilla was very pleasant, efficient, and helpful. More than often they went beyond the call of duty in assistance. Housed in a vintage townhouse about 20 minutes from Catedral de Sevilla on foot and literally next door to Plaza de la Encarnacion, the hostel offered a much original, at home, and maybe Bohemian atmosphere seasoned globe backpackers could have found familiar back in the 1970s. There seemed to be a number of guests staying longer than the usual tourists would while some of them even volunteered in upkeep works around the premise to the point that it felt somewhat more a commune than a short-term accommodation. Facilities at the hostel were apparently in medley of basic, eclectic, and dated items. The four-bed room we stayed featured 2 steel bunk beds in a space of approx. 110 square feet in size. Interestingly, the bathroom was quite spacious, up to 90 sq. ft. The room situated on the ground floor, right between the main hall and a patio out from the kitchen, two main areas where all the folks congregated, dined, and chatted. What's going on around the room was clearly audible. A vintage locker cabinet similar to those in U.S. public schools provided secured storage. Yet the thin cabinet sheets rendered every moving items in or out like hitting a steel drum. This was the most expensive hostel among a total of 4 in our Spain trip. For some reasons, the charges were more than twice for others with better facilities in both Madrid and Granada.

author: MefdeBef
title: Great hostel to meet people
text: I stayed in the hostel one Centro in Sevilla at the end of July and I really loved it there. Since I had problems with my credit card at the time I could not make a reservation beforehand so I just showed up and it was no problem at all. The staff was very welcoming and friendly. I loved the group activities they offered. The first day I arrived we went with a group to the plaza España which was impressive and a great way to meet fellow travelers. They offered free family dinners. Since I stayed for two nights, I had the dinner twice, the first night was bad but the next night was really good. If you're on a budget, it will still fill you up at least and again a great way to meet people. They also offered a trip to see a free flamenco show which was alright. The rooms were cleans as far as I can comment on it (I was in a 4 bed down with one other guy). The room had it's own ensuite and an AC unit. The AC was pretty powerful so you should be advised to talk with your roommates about the desired temperature as I was very cold the first morning since my roommate set the AC on 17°C. The hostel offers laundry service for 7 euros. You give it to them j. The morning and your clothes will be clean and dry in the evening. A special shout-out to Anna, Heidi and the other Danish girl at the reception whose name I just can't seem to remember (sorry!!).

author: dreameurotrip
title: Disappointing staff
text: I didn't like the staff lying to me. When I checked-in I asked the guy at the reception if I can sleep at a bottom bunk bed. He said all are taken so I said okay I'll take the top bunk. Fifteen minutes later, he comes in with a new guest who just checked-in and showed her her bottom bunk bed. And I was like WTH? He just told me all are taken earlier. So whatever. When I came back later that night, someone took over my bed. It has a lot of stuff on it. So I went to the night-shift receptionist and told him. When we came to them room I saw 2 more bottom bunk beds were empty and I told him he didn't need to move the stuff out and I will just sleep in one of the empty bottom bunk beds. He agreed. I was already in my bed cozy and all ready to sleep when the night-shift receptionist came to me and said there was a mistake. Someone was supposed to sleep in this bed and I have to move back to my original top bunk bed. I was annoyed but it was already 1AM so I just moved out the stuff on my bed and slept there instead. The next morning, I woke up and the bottom bunk beds were empty and looked fresh because no one slept in them. I was super pissed. I don't get why they won't just give me the bottom bunk bed.

author: Demirjian
title: Great hostel for Semana Santa! Home away from home!
text: I stayed at Hostel One Sevilla Centro for six nights during Semana Santa and had a wonderful visit!! The hostel is centrally located and offers a walking tour every morning to all the major sites. The design of the hostel is great with a patio, rooftop, kitchen and sitting room. I stayed in a room for 4 women, I appreciated the privacy curtains on the beds and the bed itself was quite comfortable. The bathroom was cleaned every day. This hostel was especially great for Semana Santa as many processions pass nearby or even through the plaza that is in front of the hostel! You can watch the processions from the rooftop or if you're lucky with your room assignment, as I was, from the balcony of your room! Waking up during the madrugada at 4:30am for "El Silencio" was a very cool experience. Free dinner made by Chung is NOT to be missed!! Chung is a master chef and the food he cooks is by far, 1000%, the best food I've ever had in a hostel. I had a lot of fun on the pub crawl one night led by volunteer Ben (the King of the Crawl) and accompanied by 15-20 other hostel guests from around the world. After staying there for almost a week, I was quite comfortable here. I made a lot of friends here that I continue to keep in touch with. There is a great group of people running this place- the owner Ariel, Chung and the volunteers/staff were all so personable. Hostel One Sevilla Centro is my home in Sevilla and I can't wait to return someday soon!!

author: escad59
title: Worst value for money ever!
text: Absolutely no value for money. It can almost be described as a scam. There is simply no words to describe the worst hotel/hotel experience we ever had. One of us have traveled extensively to several countries and have never experience such a degree/display of carelessness towards "guest experience". Overall hostel experience was the worst of all places we stayed in Spain where we also visited Barcelona, Cordoba and Madrid. Size of Room: Bare minimum to fit one bed for two people and the bathroom. Nothing more. Cleanliness: Bed sheets had not been changed from those used by previous guest staying in the room. They were only changed at our request after two nights. The bathroom had a stench worst than any public washroom that we visited in our two-week travel to Spain. We actually have to buy air freshener (out of our own pocket) to reduce the stench. The toilet became plugged during our visit and the cleaning personal never noticed and/or took any corrective action, which goes to show the thoroughness with which the room was cleaned. The fan in the bathroom was as noisy as anyone can imagine. Laundry: Not only you have to pay for it, and not allowed to do yourself; but also there was too much laundry detergent put on to wash our clothes. This resulted in a adverse allergic reaction which was the direct result of excessive amount of detergent left in the clothes after washing. Internet access: Wi-Fi access had to be continuously reset/reconnected. Food: Not the greatest when one considers that, supposedly, breakfast and dinner are included in the hefty price to stay. The experience of sharing the place and meals with other people traveling was great and we truly enjoyed interacting with those staying at the same place. However, the rest of our experience left much to be desired. We do not recommend this place to anyone wishing to get value for money while having a decent time at a place to stay.

author: trevvorw
title: Had potential
text: This is my first review on trip advisor. I was compelled to submit this because this was by far the worst hostel I experienced on my 2 and a half month Europe trip. The hostel itself had lots of potential, the building is noce, layout is well done and the room are adequate. Most of the staff is quite welcoming as well, with one main noticeable exemption.. Julien, I believe his name is, can only be classified as a jerk. Before we had even been given the keys to our room he threatened to call the police on us if we made any noise whatsoever after midnight. He gave us 2 keys for a room of 4 people although we were not altogether, because he said he didn't trust any of us... That meant we were sharing a room with 2 other people WITHOUT locker access with people that he didnt trust, or our roommates were. Side note, our roommates were very nice people. While resting my feet upon a chair, he came by and pushed them off. A polite 'can you please put your feet down' would of sufficed. The looks we were consistently given by this Julien were not welcoming at all. I did find it somewhat funny though because his appearence reminded me of dimitry martin, but i digress, he is the wrong type of person to be in charge of a hostel catering to youth. Aside from this Julien fellow, problems at the hostel included poor heating. Despite the 20 degree weather, the hostel was always cold. Wifi was useless, no point in advertising wifi here at all. Frequently had to use the starbucks nearby for their free wifi. Would not recommend at all, you can easily find a better place in Seville, which is a lovely city.

author: MochaChoca
title: Great staff, cool atmosphere, comfortable
text: The best thing about this hostel is it's friendly staff, central location and comfortable rooms. My friend and I stayed inthe 4 bed ensuite female dorm, and since we were the only people it was like having a private room at dorm prices. We were glad of the heating as Seville is quite cold in winter! The room was comfortable, the shower hot and we had lockers to store our valuables. There is also a communal kitchen if you want to self cater but we found Seville cheap for food and drinks. Ariel checked us in, even though we arrived late and there was free dinner (a simple paella) wating for us on on our first night. There was also free sangria on the second night. This is a really sociable hostel and the staff take those guests who want to go out at night. We went to some local underground bars with Julian who is an amazing host. The staff really go above and beyond to make you feel comfortable, give you travel advice and take you to bars that they like, not just because they have an incentive to do so. There is free wifi in the hsotel, but my only gripe is that the wifi signal was poor in my room, so I would need to use it from the common area. I would definitely recommend this hostel and wouldn't hesitate to come back next time I'm in Seville. TIP: Book directly with the hostel and they may offer you a discount! We booked on the day of arrival and secured a discount. A cab to the airport costs around 25 Euro, but you can also take the tram and walk 15 minutes.

author: abhijit89
title: Comfortable stay, nice location, great staff!
text: First of all, Seville is as pretty as a picture - and so is this place. Also, you can cover the whole city (along with Triana) just by walking - so we didn't really stay in much. It was more of a place to freshen up \ sleep. Considering you plan to travel over town, make friends - this is a very ideal place. Ariel received us at the hostel - who was extremely welcoming and seemed outright happy to have us. He gave us all the details of the city, places to go, the secret to catching a real flamenco show (for free!) et. al. The folks there arrange pub crawls and trips over the cities. So you really can skip the part where you have to figure out the things to do in Seville. We stayed in an 8 bed dorm - and it was very spacious. Big lockers for each of us where you can stuff your backpack and other stuff right in. A big plus was they had a separate shower and a big washroom attached to a dorm. The rooms were very clean at any time of the day - so clearly the staff was doing a good job. The common room is pretty big - they have a few computers to get online, a lot of maps and pamphlets for the things that are going on in the city. They have a nice kitchen where you can go in and make your breakfast. I even think they have bikes for hire. All in all - given how much we were paying, a sweet deal :)

author: Peitho
title: This is how you hostel
text: Great staff. Fantastic location. Comfy beds. Clean bathrooms. Tons of hot water. Amazing rooftop terrace. Clean rooms. Big lockers (bring your own lock). Cold AC. Warm blankets. Historic and lovely building. Affordable and lovely restaurants in the square just outside. Only complaint: during peak hours (evenings), more wifi capacity would have been awesome. With all of Seville: take the map with you! You'll get lost but discover awesomeness along the way :)

author: gardinerfam2010
title: Great Pool, friendly staff
text: We loved our stay. We had a family room on the 1st floor with amazing views of the mountains. Pros: Amazing Pool. Very clean. Lots of extra towels. It can get quite busy the staff is helpful and the service was great. The front front desk was helpful with finding us a babysitter through a babysitting service. They also were helpful with transportation questions. Also Anthony at the Bar was awesome! Lots of free parking is available daily. Cons: We has an issue the 1st night with our key not working. The staff was helpful and changed some batteries and fixed it. There also were not many english channels on the TV, but that’s not a deal breaker or anything. The restaurant was yummy but expensive in my opinion. There is also a playroom/kids area in the hotel which is great but was closed for 2 of our 4 days we were there. Kind of a bummer because my kids loved the playroom. We would definitely stay there again!

author: KAMERM
title: Ski holiday
text: Got a great deal on this through Anna voyage prive. Hotel is lovely, large room with double aspect and balcony, which didn’t get any sun. Great bathroom, lousy storage! No where to hide away your luggage, and on a skiing trip you need place to put all the bulky suits! Bring swimwear as it’s needed for the jacuzzi and steam room. Breakfast was good, but half way through our week the fresh fruit changed to tinned peaches! Everything else on offer was great, best croissants ever! Dinner was ok, nothing spectacular! We were on half board basis. Position of the hotel wasn’t good. You had to walk about 200 meters to catch a bus going either way. Our first few days most of the Resort was closed due to bad weather and avalanche risk, so only LES Houches was open and therefore really crowded. Unfortunately the hotel had a couple of seminars going on so the lounge area and children’s room was unavailable to guests for a couple of days, not good for a 4 star place! Staff were all friendly and helpful, most spoke very good English. Think the hotel could do with a courtesy bus as it’s so far away from ski lifts and town centre, especially as it claims to be a 4 star.

author: 504fredo
title: Stunning scenery, super friendly
text: From the moment we arrived to the moment we left we felt looked after. Nothing was a problem and everything was comfortable. We were snowboarding Chamonix and the hotel was out of town but that's its charm. Links to the slopes was by bus or train. If you take the train it is jaw dropping scenery as you snake through the mountains. The hotel has a spa, which was great for us after a day of boarding. And they have a board room with heated lockers.... Breakfast was three courses and you could fill your boots with all the food groups. Fruit and yogurt for starter's, bacon eggs and sausages for main and pastries for pudding. And they have a great coffee machine so you can make your own cappuccino variables.. Breakfast for winners. Hotel bar was busy and a great opportunity to talk to guests and staff about Chamonix. The local mt blanc beer was fab. Our room was a great space, little on the small side but plenty of cupboard space. TV channels were a little limited but we didn't spend too much time as the spa was opposite and the jacuzzi overlooked the Cham valley. Hotel has a comfortable contemporary feel. It's warm without being stuffy. Staff were lovely and relaxed.

author: ecbj-61
title: Ok but overpriced restaurant
text: We booked a family room and got a room with a minimal oval window facing a wall! It was room 171. When we asked to change it was not possible but after some more complaining we got a room with a balcony. Same price apparently, strange! Comfortable beds and fresh bathroom but very little storage for clothes in the second room. Not even hooks to hang jackets or shelf for bags. Difficult when having all ski clothes etc. The breakfast is great! The dinner was varying. Starter lovely, main coarse tasteless but beautiful and desert ok. Too expensive though! A bottle of water is 7 Euro and house wine 30 Euro. They don't server tap water even though it is good quality 😕. Staff is friendly and atmosphere nice but spa is very small. Wifi poor and English TV channels not working. The hotel is not in Chamonix centre. Bus 3 km. We will probably try a new hotel next time.

author: jules232004
title: Great views, wouldnt return
text: Visited Chamonix 7th Sept 2016-17th Sept 2016 Staying at the Excelsior Hotel Chamonix. Having read other guests comments I was concerned but decided to be open minded, their comments were justified. Had booked a superior room with balcony, we were disappointed & even questioned the grade of room. Balcony came with added extras of previous guests toe nail clippings. Room did not appear to be hoovered at all during our 10 night stay. Quality toiletries & towels. Breakfast-road side cafe!!!. Tables very rarely cleared of used plates/cutlery etc. 2 Hot drinks machines only one working-self service, staff member just shrugged her shoulders. Had to request replenishment of hot food options at 9am despite breakfast being served until 10.30am Every piece of crockery came with multiple chips/cracks. "Fine dining french cuisine" for evening meal, set menu = 1 started/1 main/1 dessert - very restrictive.Yes they did accomodate & substitue with an alternative. Only 2 staff "working" at breakfast & dinner, understaffed to say the least especially when coach load of tourists arrived. Great views of Mont Blanc. Peaceful quiet location. Local bus into Chamonix centre runs every 30mins, free with Valley Card provided from hotel. Hotel info stays hotel transport available into Chamonix, has to be pre booked the previous day & only available on days a member of staff is available. Also hotel info states mineral water in room for arrival, none there, spoke to reception, never arrived. Loved Chamonix. Would not recommend or stay at this hotel again.

author: Missy2008
title: Room with a view to die for....spectacular
text: What a wonderful hotel. I cannot think of one single negative about this hotel.Yes, it is outside of Chamonix but you would know that already when you're researching hotels in the area, for us it is a positive. There are a couple of places to eat nearby, but we didnt try them as their menu wasn't to our taste, we did venture into Chamonix several times & there is plenty of choice for all budgets and tastes.There is a train station and bus stop nearby if you prefer public transport. The staff on the front desk, the bar staff, the restaurant staff as well as the spa staff are all very good at their jobs, and go above and beyond to make sure your stay at this hotel is relaxing and memorable. The whole hotel is modern and spacious and extremely clean. The reception staff are very helpful and knowledgeable and gave us tips on where to go and what to see. There is free parking and free wifi. Our mountain view bedroom was on the third floor over looking the pool, with a shared balcony. What a view!! There is a room safe, plenty of hanging space with dressing gowns and slippers. There is also a kettle, and a good quality coffee maker along with teabags and coffee and creamer. Plenty of power outlets, an alarm clock with docking station. The bed is so comfy, we slept in late a couple of times as we had such a deep sleep and the sheets are top quality too. The bathroom had a great hairdryer, toiletries and a shower cubicle. I have rarely seen such a clean bathroom, the housekeeping team here really know their jobs. We ate in the restaurant one evening, Ben looked after us very well. The food was exceptional. The heated pool is awesome, plenty of sun loungers, deck chairs and a sofa too. What else could you want, a spectacular view, the photos really dont do it justice a pool bar too. The whole experience from beginning to end exceeded our expectations.

author: NorJerseyDad
title: Short notice business trip
text: I booked my room on short notice for $80/night. Driving up their narrow gravelly short driveway, which looked residential, with some construction, I was concerned. However, upon rounding the last curve, I saw the hotel and was very happy. It's a older style building and from the outside looked very well kept. Inside was very nice and modernized. The receptionist was super sweet and very professional. She had a really positive energy. My room was modern, comfortable, and clean. Not small for a European hotel room but not large. My view was great. I did not have to adjust the thermostat in the room and I slept well. I ate dinner in the restaurant and it seemed that the menu was priced to push toward the prix fixe menu (or to speed a lot). As I mentioned, I booked this last minute with price a main concern...so I ordered the three course fixed menu for 29 euro (escargot and rabbit pictured) and found it excellent. The bread they brought one piece at a time but it also was excellent. All in all I would certainly recommend it- especially it the price I paid-although I suspect they will charge more in-season.

author: RandyR796
title: Still Nice Place To Stay, Still Tricky To Get To
text: Have been staying here every Memorial Day for the past 4 years for grandson's b-day. My Garmin has a hard time getting me there even. Look for the KFC from the road and aim for it. Motel is next door. Very clean establishment and very quiet. Noticed new carpeting. TV selection OK. Internet on middle of 2nd floor was good with no need for a security code to be entered. King bed had 4 small pillows. Could have used two more. Breakfast area was busy with Memorial Day travelers. Breakfast was OK but could have used a few small improvements. Area was very clean. Did not use the pool, but there was a number of people using it. Will stay again. Look for the KFC.

author: Mrswanderlust88
title: Discrimination against Americans
text: Do NOT stay here if you are an American. I can’t believe I have to write this but we were SHOCKED at the treatment we received by the staff. Please read the whole review. First, when booking we paid an “extra fee” to have a penthouse to have a view of the Eiffel Tower, which was “guaranteed” to us. We had already been to Cairo, Santorini, and Rome before arriving to Paris. 1 day before our arrival, we received an email from the hotel telling us they gave our room to a different guest! We would have booked at the Shangri La for the view because money is not an issue for us, but this place seemed quaint and romantic and I regret giving it a chance. After They gave our room with the view away, there wasn’t enough time to cancel the reservation with out being charged the entire amount ! So we HAD to stay here. Upon arrival, the front desk worker got up to help us with our bags, but as soon as he saw that we were American, he promptly went back inside and sat back down at the counter, leaving us to bring in our own bags. Not that that’s a problem but it was noticeable that he purposely did not want to help us. Once we checked in, we asked for recommendations on tours and restaurants and asked if the concierge could help us set it up, he said “I am the concierge” but was so short and annoyed that we are asking what activities and places to eat at he actually waved us away to end the conversation!! I have NEVER in my life been treated with dismissal moments after checking into a hotel! And if you are all still reading, my husband and I couldn’t have been any nicer, realizing that being rude back would get us no where with this staff. Our morning breakfasts weren’t not any better l, the waitress would not come wait on us, after waiting for 10 mins for her to come to our table, watching her wait on all of the French guests, I finally got up and went and tapped her on the shoulder asking if we could order coffee veeeery politely, as nice as I possible could, and she would only speak back in French with an attitude and never brought us coffee. I could go on about other incidents, but the worst was at the end when we had requested a car service to the airport a DAY in advance, but they never arranged it for us and we almost missed our flight trying to get an Uber to come pick us up. This place made us never want to ever go back to Paris, which maybe that’s what they wanted, for Americans to stay out of Paris! WORST HOTEL WE HAVE EVER STAYED AT.

author: ellieh0llyw00d
title: Convenient, Cozy Hotel. Great for families!
text: This is an adorable little hotel within walking distance of the Eiffel Tower. The hotel was well decorated and clean. We were two families traveling together, 2 Adults and 4 children. We took two adjoining rooms and it worked out well. The rooms are smaller compared to American hotels. But, they was still enough room that we were not on top of each other. The staff was welcoming, friendly and helpful...Thank you to the breakfast staff for always greeting our large family with a smile.... The breakfast was European, which we were fine with. Espresso, sliced ham, croissants, crepes and cheese..ummm, yea. There are restaurants, of all kinds, within walking distance and pastry shops everywhere. If you like lemon, go get a lemon tart at the bakery ( patisserie) shop next door. Delicious!!! The taxi stand is right down the street, as well as the Metro. This hotel really could not be any more convenient. Don't believe the stories of the French being rude to Americans. We walked miles everyday and ate crepes and many little crepe stands. We tried the food at many different restaurants right next to the hotel. And everyone, everywhere was kind and helpful. Of course there are sometimes language issues, but patience always helps. Remember this is their home, it is only proper to be polite when invited to someone's home.

author: groupking
title: Walk to Eiffel Tower, DO NOT USE HOTEL TO BOOK AIRPORT TRANSFERS
text: Booked this hotel for 1 night due to its proximity to the Eiffel Tower. It is walking distance to the ET and the Passy Metro station. We took the Metro to other major sites and it was fine. Metro is a little crowded so if you are not a Metro person, use UBER or taxi. Hotel is a bit expensive for what you get. The family site is actually 2 connecting rooms and priced as such. Staff was very nice. They provided free bottled water in room and a smart phone for your use. The big issue we had was that we had problems with the airport transfers both from the airport to the hotel AND the return trip. The transfer companies they use are awful. We would've missed our return flight if we had not called an UBER at the last minute. Typical city hotel as far as location, street noise etc. We did not and I would not recommend the breakfast. Much better options nearby as their are plenty of food options within walking distance. Overall hotel worked for us as a family of 5 for 1 night. If planning a longer stay, I would shop around for better deal and larger room.

author: Mavsmurf
title: A hidden gem
text: I just returned from watching the tennis tournament at Rolland Garros. I do NOT ordinarily take the time to write reviews. . . but I felt compelled to write of my experience at Maison FL. The location of the hotel makes it walkable to Rolland Garros (or 10 minutes by bus or metro). We did both. This is the place to stay if attending the tournament. After a full day at the tournament, it was so nice to be able to wander into neighborhood bistros of high quality (reasonable priced) food. Beyond location, the hotel itself is fabulous. The room size is very large by European standards. The bed was one of the most comfortable that I have encountered in my travels. It felt like sleeping in my own bed. The room was lovely! The breakfast was so delicious and far beyond my expectation! The staff could not have been more friendly and so very helpful! This is the place to stay!!!

author: elenasparkle
title: Good location, clean and comfortable room, good breakfast
text: I stayed here for work because it was close to my meetings - a 15 minute walk to the OECD. I find it a bit more upscale than some other hotels in Passy yet still reasonably priced. The hotel is also well located for tourists - a quiet neighbourhood and yet a short walk to the Eiffel Tower and other top tourist spots and very close to the metro. The room was spacious for Paris (although there are smaller rooms in the hotel). The bed was big, and comfortable and clean. The bathroom was very spacious and again clean and well appointed (including a heated towel bar - a nice touch). The bathtub was fantastic and clean enough to actually use for a bath - I am very picky about that! The staff was really nice and it was the same small team all week so they felt very familiar by the end. They seemed to be a lot nicer, more caring and accommodating than other hotel staff I've experienced. The breakfast was perfect with good choices for food, fresh and tasty. Surprisingly, for a relatively small hotel, there was also room service, which I tried and found the food quite good as well. The food came quickly also. I was right next to the elevator which worried me at first but I never heard it. There was some traffic noise from the road but for Paris this was very quiet - it's on a small, one way street in a mostly residential area. Very unlike many hotels in Paris near bars and restaurants which can be brutal with so many outdoor patrons. That said, there are a few nice restaurants nearby, a pharmacy, a small mall down the road on rue Passy with a starbucks and a toy store, and other fancy or chain store shops along this fairly upscale street. Overall a really nice experience and I will likely come here again - certainly for work and maybe one day for holidays too.

author: tramonteL
title: Very good choice
text: I was pleased with the choice of Maison FL, perfectly located at few steps away from Passy Metro. I love the neighborhood and the fancy consignment stores all around as well as the restaurants and shopping options. It is really the perfect spot to explore Paris. The hotel is quiet and spotless. Great staff and interesting style. I mean, it is a bit on the over decorated side, but does not bother. One mistake I made is that I booked a single room rather than a double. I did not do the booking myself, as I generally take into account that a double in Paris is small, so a single is like be buried alive. The single was more like a boat cabin than a room, but everything was there, and also strategically designed. So, no complaint. Except that the view of my room was a set of stairs, at about 3 mts from my windows.People could see me getting dressed from the windows in the hallway. As the room is tiny, the only way to be private was to pull the curtains down and obscure the room. So, this is a downside of possibly a cheaper room.This was really unpleasant. Overall, I would say that if I choose myself and booked a double, I would have had a better experience. In general, the hotel is really nice. I almost forgot; i did not have breakfast, so I cannot judge whether the 20 euros would be well spent. I preferred eating at the various amazing bakeries that surround the hotel.

author: Audrius999
title: Overrated hotel!
text: The hotel looks great from outside, however it is highly over rated for the following unpleasant experiences that we had: 1. On the second day of our stay, we planned some sightseeing in Paris. After we came back to the hotel, the staff members were in our room doing some maintenance. 2. When we got back from town, we went for a nap. While we were sleeping a member of staff came to our room without even knocking or letting us know before hand. But then he quickly left straight after. My wife was shocked and got really frightened. This irresponsible behaviour of the hotel staff is totally unacceptable, as it made me feel unsafe whilst staying in our room. 3. On the last day of our stay we booked a transfer from the hotel to the airport through the hotels reception. A member of staff confirmed that the taxi will arrive in the early morning and has issued the invoice for the service that we booked. However, the taxi didn’t turn up and caused us a lot of stress as we had to rearrange the pickup on the spot. This is definitely something that you don’t want to experience in the early morning before going to the airport to catch a flight. All in all, the staff weren’t dealing with the problems we had at all. They were ignoring our arguments. When we tried reporting this behaviour to the hotel manager, our feedback was completely ignored. This is not something that the hotel rated this high should be doing. So to all of view planning your stay at this hotel - don’t get tricked by looking at the hotel ratings as they may not represent the true experience that you might have.

author: Coellum
title: Pleasant little hotel
text: The hotel is about a 15 minute walk to the Eiffel Tower. Our room did not had a view of the Eiffel Tower but it did have a balcony. It was nice to look out onto the street even if it was winter. The room is small but nicely decorated. The bed was good quality. The bathroom was also tight but had a good sized shower. Tiles were attractive. The whole room had a modern light look. It was convenient to be close to the Passy Metro, a 5 minute walk. From there, it was just one transfer to go to the Opera area. To go to the Champs Élysées, no transfer is required. Within the area of the hotel, one can shop along Passy Street. There is even a little mall with a Monoprix and a Massimo Dutti. The breakfast was adequate. There were cheeses and cold cuts. One could boil eggs. The lobby is a pleasant spot for a meal. The next time my husband has to attend a conference in the area, I will choose this hotel again,

author: Yuriy_Zaremba
title: Not bad, but will think twice before visiting again
text: I was choosing the hotel for our Paris trip veru carefully, and thought that I chose best quality/price hotel, but actually it was not completely so. Let's review it step by step: 1. The staff was very helpful and flexible when I arranged the booking and payment via email, but upon check-in they were not very friendly. 2. The breakfast is very overpriced. Right accross the road there is a great French cafe, where you can have a really nice french breakfast two time cheaper. I would strongly recommend not to pay for breakfast at the hotel. 3. The rooms are clean and really stylish. There are some defects and dirt in the corners on the cealing or near the doors, but generally, everyshing is fine. The bathrooms are great. Sheets and towels are changed every day. 4. The thing that made me the most uncomfortable is the fact that it is very quiet in this hotel. No music at reception, no people in the halls or lobby. 5. Location was perfect. I hope this review was helpful.

author: tomasz34
title: nice hotel in good location
text: We have spent 3 nights in Maison FL in early October. Hotel is OK. LOCATION Pretty good location despite our initial concerns. Metro station is 300 metres away, Trocadero is in a walking distance. In principle you may reach every major attraction in 20 minutes - using metro or taxi. ROOM We took a Junior suite and it was fine in terms of size. Unfortunately no balcony. Windows were overlooking the street which was very noisy. In general soundproofing does not exist - noise from outside was permanent but we could also hear our neighbors and people on the corridor. I would say that lack of soundproofing was a major weakness of the room. Bathroom was large and very nicely decorated. Bed comfortable, pillows were quite OK. RECEPTION All our requests submitted before arrival were fulfilled. Everything was fine, including smooth check-in and check-out. Hotel is nicely decorated, staff was professional and friendly, room was of good size. The only real weakness - although I am possibly oversensitive - was a lack of soundproofing. If you are not too noise sensitive you may seriously consider this hotel.

author: LolaZee
title: Lovely rooms, good stay, good location
text: I just got back from my stay at Maison FL. The rooms are lovely, I couldn't have been happier with the decor. I had a window on the street that opened up. It is about a block to the Passy metro station and there is also a taxi stand around the corner. About a block away is a Monoprix for all the stuff you forgot to bring. It is about a 5 minute walk to Eiffel Tower. I loved the location (except on Friday night when the neighbors across the street decided to party LOUDLY with their windows wide open) but that has nothing to do with the hotel itself. The room itself was plenty big for me, the bathroom was comfortable with good water pressure and temperature. There is a mini bar with some drinks if you are dying of thirst, otherwise avoid it, its pretty pricey. 4.50 Euros for a small Coke. There is an excellent hair dryer along with a robe and slippers, should you desire. The bed was comfortable, if not a little on the firm side. Overall, I was VERY pleased with my stay, when I come back to Paris, I will stay here again. I came solo and felt very safe in the neighborhood and its closeness to transportation as well as ability to walk to the tower definitely sold me on this place. I hope to be back soon!

author: EinStein_Norway
title: A nice place for kids!
text: Quality hotel&resort is a nice big hotel which has a good location, its easy to find, if you are on a low budget, you have 3 supermarkets and a grill (kinda fastfoodrestaurant) only about 300 meters away. The hotel has 500 free parking-spaces so you will always find place for your car. The reseption is clean, tidy and the staff is very friendly and welcoming! The hotel has a big aqualand with a stream-canal, big massage-showers, mushroom-waterfalls (one of them is 3 meters deep), you'll find a big waterslide and for longdistance-swimming you have lanes for that too. The relax-department has a strange age-limit and that is 16 years, BUT if you are a parent with one or more kids under the age of 3, you can access the relax-department. We had an 8 year old son who is far less noisy than kids of age 2-3 so that was a little disappointing that we couldn't enjoy the relax-department because of the age-restriction... The bolts attaching the ladders to the pool were loose (kinda half of the bolts) so I hope the security-manager reads this and secure them immediately, for me who ways 140 kilo it was a nervevracking experience to descend down that half-loose ladder... The superland is cool for kids! Here you can be like an "american ninja warrior" and you can do it very safely due to a safety-wire you are attached to so its impossible to fall down! The 10 meter tall "rock-climbing wall" was very cool to climb in for our son, but it should have been talkum-powder there to avoid sore hands ore maybe they can have climbing-gloves that the climbers can borrow. The "Cafe sulten" was very nice and they even have soft-ice! You can also enjoy pizza here and its not expensive! The hotelroom we had had no refrigerator, but I just went down to the lobby and the cute and top serviceminded reseptionist gave me a big bucket of ice-cubes! The big double-bed was very comfy and we slept like rocks! :-) The restaurant has everything you need for a royal breakfast and the staff there were friendly and helpful! The food was delicious and on most of the hotels I've been to they start to take away the food BEFORE the breakfast ends BUT not on this hotel! Here you got fried eggs and soft boiled eggs fresh from 6:30 to 10 o'clock! At other hotels they tend to run out of juice, BUT NOT on this hotel! Here I could drink all the juice I wanted and even all the smoothies I liked! So to sum it all up: We were very pleased of the stay and we will surely be back!

author: KeithHewitt
title: Rather sad experince
text: It started badly - no TV remote in room so asked reception to send one up at 6 15pm. After 30 minutes went to reception and asked again. She didn' t seem to know what to do. I suggested get one from another room. At 7 pm I phoned reception and said this is totally unacceptable. Wanted to watch BBC news at 6pm UK. Eventually one did arrive. Of course the fault is with the chamber maid not doing the job to standard in the morning. The other aspect that I dont like is the almost complete lack of pictures. None in the room. None in the corridors. Few if any all over the hotel. They even have pictures in prisons ( so Im told ☺) On a positive note - full marks for the breakfast. I was able to speak a bit of Vietnamese with the omelette chef. Thanh, which seemed to surprise her.

author: Tablefortwo
title: The nicest thing about this hotel was Holly the housekeeper
text: When I checked in a man with a maintenance name badge checked me in. The entire time he was face timing a young child. The room was clean and the bed comfortable. I looked for the card with the housekeepers name on it and found it. The next morning I sought out and found Holly. Very nice and seemed to care about her rooms and guests. The hotel itself is dirty in the public area. Build up by vending and ice machine and pool didn’t look clean. I opted not to swim. One very thin blanket on the bed which made a cold night even with heat turned up. Remote control for TV was useless. You have to hold it at a certain angle to get it to change channels or to adjust volume. Over flowing ashtrays on the porch. Two breakfast attendants the next morning worked hard to keep things replenished and tables wiped off. At check out no one was visible. Several people waited. I chose to leave with the express check out option. The encased pillow in our room has an out dated promotion in the bag for Summer a year ago. Hard to find another hotel in area as everyone else was booked. Not worth the 200.00 plus for one night.

author: 899kerryf
title: Not up to Country Inn standards!
text: My husband and I stayed in this hotel for two nights! Right from the check in we were not happy. Needed to try three rooms before we found one that was okay. We are Carlson Club members and were initially put in a handicap accessible room that had a toilet that would not stop running. We went back to the desk and the attendant checked two other rooms before she finally gave us a room that she felt was acceptable. When we went to the room it was a two room suite with a wall air conditioner in the one room and was extremely warm. Had to open the windows to cool down the room. The room had two nice flat screen TVs, however it only had analog cable and it was terrible. Furniture was cheap, home furnishings. Broken lamps, stains on carpet. Housekeeping didn’t vacuum, empty ice bucket or remove garbage from tables. Just not the experience that we are used when booking a Country Inn. Also, outside doors didn’t lock which is a security issue. If going to York book a different hotel because this is not worth the price. At check out we weren’t even asked about our stay. Only tells me they know they have major problems and really don’t care!

author: tdobish
title: Visited family in the area
text: We could have stayed at a hotel closer to family, but chose this hotel because it had a pool. We checked in around 6 p.m. and went to the pool that was EXTREMELY COLD. 2 other families were there and in the hot tub because the pool was too cold to swim. We told the front desk clerk, who was very apologetic and said she would alert maintenance. The next morning, same cold pool. We tried to check out and waited for over 10 minutes for the desk clerk to return from outside (Smoking a cigarette). There was also another man waiting before us to check out. As we checked out, we again alerted the clerk that the pool was still cold and we were not happy with our stay. She said she had no idea about the pool because someone called off and she had to come to work, otherwise she would not be there. She was not one bit friendly and did not appear to care about our concerns, or the concerns of the man in front of us. I answered a survey that was e-mailed to me. AGAIN- I feel like I was brushed off. This is the response I received: Dear TRACI, Thank you for taking the time to complete our guest satisfaction survey. On behalf of our entire staff at Country Inns & Suites we apologize for the concerns you shared about your experience at this hotel. I have addressed your concerns with our team, and I assure you we are working diligently to ensure a similar situation does not occur again in the future. we do not charge extra for the pool. We appreciate the feedback and will use it to fine tune our operations in the hope that upon your next visit we can exceed your expectations. Sincerely, ANTONIO REYES Manager Country Inn & Suites 717-747-5833

author: SandyB1121
title: Poor service but updated room
text: Every time I called this hotel (and I was a group organizer) there was a problem or a delay or a confused person. Computers were often down too. Upon check in, I was greeted with a sign at the front desk telling me they were helping another guest. Not a good way to start. There is only 1 elevator at this hotel-always had to wait. Breakfast was nothing special-very basic. I skipped it since nothing was appealing. My TV remote was low on batteries so when I went to the front desk I told them. They asked me what room I was in so later when I got back, I expected it to be in my room and working. Not the case! When I checked out I told them again and they told me the guy left the new remote for me at the desk. Well how was I supposed to know that? And why did he ask for my room number then? Also, the sink was not fully functional which I reported at check out. Positives: Room was newly updated. Cookies always at the front desk. I would not stay here again or recommend for my groups.

author: musicman85
title: Pleasant Stay
text: I recently stayed here with a few friends over Labor Day weekend. I have stayed in different Country Inn & Suites in PA, and was interested to see how this one was. I arrived late Saturday after a full day of sightseeing and was checked into the room promptly by the nice lady at the front desk. The room was very spacious! A pull out couch with a mini fridge, microwave and sink. In the other room was a nice size bed. Both rooms had televisions and the bathroom was accommodating. In the morning they do offer a free hot breakfast which consisted of pastries, bagels, cereals, yogurt, oatmeal, eggs of some sort, sausage and another hot item (french toast, hot english muffins). There was also the make your own waffle machine. The breakfast was very nice and the lady working in the area was always wiping spills and making sure it looked clean and re-filling it. Another nice perk is that there was all day coffee/tea. One perk which was very accommodating was that the pool and hot tub didn't seem to close early and was open later then most hotels I've ever stayed at which was nice. After sight-seeing all day, the hot tub was a very much needed way to relax at the end of the day. I do have a few minor issues to address: The air vent in the front room took a while for the room to cool down while the bedroom towards the back where the air was controlled was nice and ice cool. While the hotel wasn't close to Amish country where I was touring, it was still a very clean and accommodating hotel and I would recommend this to anyone.

author: lifesabeach39
title: Everything is neat and very clean
text: Even while under renovation we found this place to be very neat and clean. The staff is friendly and helpful. We were told our room had brand new beds. They were firm, but comfortable. We were missing a coffee pot, but the front desk promptly brought one up - no big deal. The water pressure is actually good in the shower. The toiletries are name brand - appreciate that! We enjoyed the pool which is a good size, not small. The breakfast had different eggs, meats, home fries daily; along with what you'd expect. The gem of the breakfast room is their hostess - very nice lady. Cookies and fruit and coffee and tea are always on hand. There are are lots of restaurants available within a 1/2 mile. There is a Ruby Tuesdays right next door that you can walk to. We chose this hotel for its location half way between Lancaster and Gettysburg. We would return and we recommend.

author: 705sarahd
title: Clean room, comfortable bed - lacks amenities
text: Stayed here for one night - 6/27 - in a king suite. Although I arrived at noon amd understood the room may not be ready, I decided to check-in upon arrival. The male at the check-in desk informed me that check-in wasn't until 3pm. I acknowledged that I was early and requested to check-in and wait for the room to be ready. He hesitantly took my information and, after checking me in, informed me that my room was, in fact, ready. The room was clean and spacious. The bathroom was clean with a tub/shower. There is no closet in the room, however, there is an armoire for storage. I found the king-sized bed to be quite comfortable, however, the pull-out sofa for my son is in dire need of replacement. Breakfast was mediocre. It had the usual hotel breakfast offerings-scrambled eggs, bacon, make-your-own waffles, and assorted pastries, muffins, and breads. It's free so not too much to complain about here. The hotel itself lacks a pool and a small convenience shop for purchasing snacks and forgotten items. There is, however, a gas station with a large convenience store across the street. We did not experience the highway noise others have commented on. Our room was quiet and we slept comfortably.

author: Nicemeany
title: Keeping it Real!
text: First time stay but not the last! Great location just off Rt 83 yet very quiet area. Next to Ruby Tuesday Restaurant. Giant Supermarket located nearby. Greeted by Lisa at check-in. Big genuine smile that made you feel very welcomed. Of course the fresh Chocolate Chip Cookies at the Front Desk helped too! Our room was very clean and comfortable. We found the King-size bed to be firm to our liking. As this was a last minute stay we brought no toiletries. The hotel offers toothpaste, toothbrush, shaving cream, razor, deodorant and other such items for FREE. Nothing fancy but when you have nothing and you are very tired it was great to get these much-needed items without having to go shopping. But the best feature I found was the sumptuous breakfast selections. From make your own Egg McMuffin, to make your own waffles, to oatmeal, fresh fruit, cold cereal selection, coffee/tea and several juices to choose from I was quite happy. And all this with REAL silverware and china. Did I mention LARGE glasses for your juice too. I left quite content and with a wrapped Raspberry Danish and Chocolate Muffin for a treat later on of course. Thank you CIS for 'keeping it real"...and not styrofoam plastically!

author: live2vayk
title: Good one night stay
text: In a trip to drive my 80 year old father back to his summer home from the South back to New England, we stopped in York, PA. We stayed one night at the Country Inn & Suites in York, as it was convenient. We reserved a suite, as he really needs his own room. I slept on the pull out in the living room section. Check in was easy, and the desk person was helpful and pleasant. The room was well appointed, and clean. It had everything we needed, and the Ruby Tuesday restaurant in the same parking lot made dinner easy. The one complaint I have is the rooms next to us had people who were loud until about 1 pm. They must have been friends with the people across the hall, because the doors kept slamming, and I could hear loud voices. My father wasn't bothered, I am guessing because he was back into the bedroom part of the suite, but it also could have something to do with hearing loss, the man is 80. I never like to call the front desk to complain, so I waited it out hoping it would stop, and by about 1 am or so it did. I can't fault the hotel for this, but come on people, have a little respect for fellow guests. The breakfast was decent enough. There was fruit salad, cereal, waffles, and the like. All in all for a one night stay, it was fine. I would stay here again.

author: Coolcoil
title: Clean, Low Price But Needs Fridge and Flat Screen
text: I stayed at this hotel for 12 days while I was working on a project team at my employer's office in York. Our rooms were booked as a block, so we had a good price, but I know that many of my colleagues regularly stay here when they come to town. That said, I thought the stay was OK, but not great. The property is a little out of date. Positives: - Friendly staff. I found them to be energetic and helpful. - Low cost washer/dryer ($1.00 each per load) - The indoor pool looked nice, though I did not use it. Negatives: No mini-fridge. This is not a big deal if you are there one night, but when you are there a while, you like to have snacks or a place to keep a six-pack cold. I would not stay there with my small children, as we definitely need a fridge to keep milk cold. Old-school cathode ray TV. It's been a long time since I stayed in a hotel without a flat screen. Slow standard internet. The standard internet speed is way below today's standards. You can upgrade to a very good speed for only $3.00, which is well worth the money if you want to stream video. None of the above was a deal breaker for me, but one of my colleagues did move to another hotel as he is a big TV and mini-fridge fan. I was a little annoyed to have to get ice to cool my beer. I would stay here again if the price were significantly lower than nearby hotels and my kids were not part of the trip.

author: SharonD61
title: Very clean, wonderful service, great breakfast
text: We were traveling south from upstate New York to southeast Virginia and it was getting late, so we checked the reviews on this hotel and pulled in for the night. We were not disappointed. Our suite was very clean, with comfortable beds and extra pillows. The refrigerator and microwave worked well, and the bathroom was very clean with everything in working order. Evita (at the front desk) was courteous and took care of us promptly, and Diales (sp?) set us up with a crib for my granddaughter. The fold up crib was easy to set up and had a good, clean mattress. The hot chocolate, coffee and cookies that are available in the lobby were a nice touch. We thoroughly enjoyed the breakfast. Many hotels now offer a complimentary breakfast, but this one was several notches above most that I have seen. Sausages and scrambled eggs (not the yucky egg patties), with warm tortillas available and ham, salsa, and shredded cheese, in case you want to make a breakfast burrito. Also fresh fruit or cut up melons and grapes, a nice variety of breads, muffins, and bagels, cereal (including hot oatmeal, with fixings like brown sugar, cinnamon, blueberries). There were highchairs available as well. Traveling with an infant is sometimes a challenge, but they made our stop truly pleasant. We were able to get back on the road feeling refreshed. We will definitely stop again when traveling through York.

author: Sirius4565
title: Adequate; somewhat disappointing
text: Stayed here 3 nights. Room had nice bed with extra pillows, small desk, small stuffed chair, coffee pot. No fridge nor microwave. I had specifically requested a fridge and microwave, but on arrival they said those rooms were sold out -- off to a bad start. Room was a reasonable size. Everything was very clean, though the carpet was remarkably sticky everywhere in the room. Everything throughout the motel was reasonably new and well-maintained; nicely decorated. Our room had some maintanence issue when we walked in, but a call to the front desk and it was quickly corrected. Good housekeeping -- helpful and attentive. Noise: even though my room faced away from the freeway, there was plenty of freeway noise. Its located a little too close to I-83 with no sound barriers. Good exercise room with lots of machines. Indoor pool looked very nice, though did not have time to use it. Wireless internet was easy to use, but had frequent drop outs and disconnects. Breakfast bar was very nice -- eggs and sausage in warming trays, lots of bagels, make-your-own waffles, muffins, cerials, yogurt, fruit, juices. Excellent 24 hour coffee available. Location was convenient to many locations in York. Many places to eat within 1/2 mile. Ruby Tuesday across the parking lot. Excellent Maple Donuts up the street.

author: graymom
title: Great place to stay!
text: My family of 3 stayed one night in a nonsmoking one-bedroom suite with a king bed and sleep sofa. The hotel is conveniently located just off I-83, minutes from downtown York and just a 6-minute drive to the local skating rink – which was our draw to the area. Despite being close to the highway, our room was very quiet. The front-desk staff was friendly and helpful. We arrived early and were allowed to check-in immediately. The hotel, its carpets and furnishings, showed wear but was very clean. The bathroom was exceptionally clean. There was a nice indoor pool and spa to relax in at the end of a long day. As far as dining, Ruby Tuesday shares the same parking lot as the hotel. Within a 5-minute drive, there are numerous full-service and fast-food restaurants, as well as a grocery store. The complimentary breakfast included bagels, cereals, hard-boiled eggs, fruit salad, and make-your-own Belgian waffles. The breakfast room was very busy during out stay, but the staff did a great job keeping up, bringing out fresh bowls of fruit salad, etc. The only drawback was the cooling system. The air conditioner was located in the bedroom at the back of the suite. Although there was a switch in the front living room labeled “fan”, all it seemed to do was cause a rumbling in the vent, but no movement of air. The living room quickly became quite hot if the bedroom door was closed. Thankfully, we always bring along a floor fan when we travel by car. By keeping the bedroom door open and setting up our floor fan in the doorway, we were able to pull cool air into the living room and keep the entire suite comfortable.

author: CCCLady
title: Great hotel for the price
text: This was our second stay at the Country Inn and Suites in York, PA. We stayed this past weekend for the Family Weekend for York College. The hotel is located about 3 miles from the college. The college is very easy to get to--only 2 turns. We were in a King suite. The room was very clean. My daughter stated the sofa bed was not comfortable but I have not found a sofa bed yet to be comfortable. The breakfast was great. A waffle maker to make fresh waffles.
