Planet Dailies serves a good breakfast and the head chef on premises is happy to whip up something you like even if it is not listed on the lunch/dinner menu. Service is very good and the staff are friendly and helpful. A few small touches here and there will add to the overall experience being even better. One major suggestion to the hotel is that they equip all rooms with a welcome mat so residents can wipe their dirty shoes on it before entering the room. Being a beach resort, this is a must! This establishment is surely going to be superb once all facilities are up and running. Best wishes to the team.

author: 699amandak
title: Gross, gross, gross
text: This hotel convinced me to write my first review ever. I'm a fairly frequent and low maintenance traveller. A clean, secure room is all I'm really looking for. This place was gross! The walls and carpets are horribly stained. We wore shoes the entire time. The bathroom had little bugs. Door handles were broken off. The bathroom door wouldn't stay closed unless locked. Hair dryer didn't work. TV didn't work. We heard everything from all the rooms around us. Reception kept our room key every time we left the building. Don't waste your money here. This was by far the worst hotel I've ever stayed in.

author: 718laurav
title: Lovely Little Pit Stop
text: We booked this hotel as part of a 3 day trip to Paris to take in the sights and culture of Paris… this hotel is exactly what we wanted. Situated a minute walk away from the St George metro station, the location could not be anymore perfect for those looking to visit the tourist hotspots and explore Paris with the Sacre Couer & Moulin Rouge within a 30 minute walk and a single metro stop away. It is also placed comfortably within the centre of a hub of bars, restaurants and tabacs, however not too close that it is annoyingly noisy. On arrival we were greeted by a friendly, English speaking receptionist who explained all the required information on our stay there and offered to help show us all the ‘must see’ places on our handy travel map, even advising us of each metro station closest to each attraction in order to get us there easily. We found this very helpful! Wifi is available here... however chargeable. Prices are shown and explained on checking in. The rooms themselves, although fairly worn, are very pleasant, clean and spacious, which is exactly what you want if on your feet all day exploring! Beds were very comfortable and the bathroom was surprisingly sizeable. They are cleaned daily with fresh soap and towels, which was lovely. On exiting the hotel, you must give your room key to the receptionist, which does leave you feeling something of an annoyance should you be in and out fairly regularly or over small intervals. It also meant that we were very wary of leaving valuables in our room while we were out as they key was not on our person. Although we understood the rule, and it meant we didn’t have to worry about losing our key… however for a security purpose, we didn’t feel entirely comfortable leaving expensive goods/passport/money in our room whilst out and about. (May have been just our personal preference however?) Breakfast option is available and although it looked lovely, we found it expensive compared to the other resaurants and cafes closeby therefore opted not to stay for this. As a whole, our stay was lovely, comforable and very welcoming. This is not the kind of hotel you would visit should you be wishing to spend the majority of your time there however for a place to stay whilst soaking in the sights of the city, it is perfect and EXCELLENT value for money! Televisual choices are limited and French language only (subtitles and audio change to other languages did not work although the option was on the settings?) and other than providing a comfortable bed, a relaxing bath and a place to store your things… it offers little else. All in all… a lovely little pit stop with friendly staff!

author: jackandangus
title: Centrally Located!
text: My husband and I have been going back to Hotel Antin Saint George for the last ten years. This hotel is very special to us. However, when I returned in March with family, I was very surprised to see the rooms needed some maintenance. I switched rooms with my cousin as the room I was given had a street view, she was given room 200 which has a view to the hotel laundry room/kitchen down below. The floor to room 200 needs some repairs, very uneven. Bathroom tub had dangerous rust on the edge. Another thing, I didn't like the vibe in this room at all. So much so that at night I would sleep with bathroom light and tv on. My cousin was originally put in this room but we switched. She also mentioned the heaviness of the atmosphere. She said "you don't have to stay there, you're welcome to come and stay with us".....I didn't want to make a big deal of it so I stuck it out in that room for another night. Now having said all this, this hotel is always very clean. Rooms need some updating but very, very clean and I guess that is what matters right? Breakfast selection is always lovely. The only thing I don't like is that wifi is not free. You get free wifi in just any hotel these days. Metro, restaurants, shops, bars at your doorstep.

author: FireFlyChick
title: Awesome Location on a Budget
text: My sister and I picked this hotel based on location and price. The location is absolutely perfect. You have the option of either walking or taking the metro (the hotel is literally above the metro) to anywhere in Paris. Also, it is dirt cheap so you're able to spend your money elsewhere... You are in Paris after all... Good shopping, food and wine. This is a perfect place to stay if your intentions are to spend as little time in the hotel as possible. It's a very tiny hotel and like other reviewers have said... the rooms are very small and definitely older and the hotel could definitely use an update as the decor did look a little grungy. The receptionists were always very nice and were able to answer any questions that we had. They even spoke English and went out of their way to help us get to the French Open, offered us umbrellas on a day when it was raining and even hooked us up with a cab back to the airport when were checking out (which is apparently hard to get in Paris). One thing to note: This hotel doesn't have air conditioning but I stayed there over the summer and with the windows open the room stayed nice and cool. Granted, since you are over the metro and in the middle of the city, it can be noisy at night, but it's just like being in any other big metropolitan city. Bottom line: Great location and cheap. Perfect if you plan on spending as little time as possible in the hotel.

author: BL1P1982
title: Avoid Avoid Avoid
text: I stayed in this hotel with my partner on 5 February 2011. All i can say is thank god we were only there for one night. I booked this hotel through a agency website (cant remember whcih one) and from looking at the pictures and descriptions of the rooms the hotel looked very good value for money. The hotel is situated in the north of the city and is a ten minute walk from the Moulin Rouge. As such, it was pretty good in terms of location. Upon arrival the reception appeared presentable and the receptioist was very helpful with our questions. However, things changed quickly when we got into our room. The first room we were allocated was on the first floor overlooking the road. Someone had just finished comking a ciggy in there and it STUNK of stale smoke, really disgusting. The room was tiny, no joke, one of us had to sit on the bed whilst the other was moving around the room. The bathroom was filthy with mould and mildew everywhere (stomach churning in fact), the bed was really lumpy, pillows were not worth having they were so flat and to top it off there was some pub hair left in the bed which suggested the sheets had either not been changed or cleaned properly. The receptionist was helpful and very apologetic and helped us changed rooms. The second room was slightly bigger and cleaner although still not what i was expecting from having looked at the hotel's website. Sleep quality would have been a bit of an issue had a not had a fair bit to drink at the Mouin Rouge that night. To be frank, i loved Paris but you would have to pay me to go back to this hotel.

author: This_Is_Us_2009
title: Small, interesting hotel close to Moulin Rouge
text: Stayed a week. The reviews I read on this hotel were dead on for the most part. Few complaints: no alarm clock in the room, the walls are paper thin and I could hear everything in the room next door (and I mean everything..........especially the young couple doing the "deed"). My room faced the street, so I had to leave the windows open for air since there is no AC. You will not get any sleep. Nothing but loud traffic and people talking/yelling on the street all hours of the night! The floors squeaked and the carpet looked old and never vacummed. And, I would recommend skipping the 10 euro breakfast. Just buy street food and pay a fraction of the cost. Spend your $$$ on eating at bakeries and eat baguettes and simple foods. Avoid the classy, overpriced restaurants cuz if you end up staying at this hotel, you're most likely on a budget! And now the good stuff................the bathroom was very clean and so was the bedding. Comfy bed (granted European rooms are smaller than North American). The decor was modern and clean. Nice, small flat screen TV. The young girl with glasses at the reception was very nice and helpful. The hotel is only a 10 min walk to the Moulin Rouge and close to little restaurants and cafes. And the metro station is a 30 sec walk so easy to get around Paris. I would give this hotel a 7 out of 10. Enjoy Paris!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

author: Abie18
title: would recommend and come back again
text: I had very low expectations coming but I was pleasantly surprised! Very near Saint Georges station in line 12 of Metro which makes it really accessible to everything - just don't attempt to walk to them if you're not really familiar with the streets. From the Eurostar station at Gare du Nord you can take 3 short trains - line 4, line 2 and line 12 and a 2 minute walk. We had no trouble finding it when we got off the Metro station. The staff was pleasant and speaks good English, they are very much willing to be of assistance to us for any weird/ silly queries about Paris. The rooms albeit small are clean, (from day one to the last) the TV was flat screen and mounted (and actually has CNN), the breakfast was a buffet and enough to last you till lunch time. For the price we paid I believe this hotel is a good value for money. Our room was on the first floor and facing the highway and being summer, we had to keep our windows open when we were there (it turned out we had to go back between sight seeing to nap and rest our feet) and the noise from the street made it hard for me to sleep and rest, I can also hear the Metro trains passing 2 floors below which was a bit freaky. Having a glass of wine during dinner helped these so in the end they weren't that big a deal. The shop/supermarket along the same street was very convenient and we bought a 6-pack of bottled water for around 1.63 euros. (it can go up to 2 euros near the sights for 1 bottle) We also bought some fruits and some exquisite cakes on the next street parallel to the hotel and they were cheap and a must for a night cap. You can bring food into your room and even borrow utensils/crockery from the hotel kitchen. (just ask reception and bring it back clean afterwards) The hotel doesn't have it's own restaurant but the area has loads to choose from - even if you get hungry around 10:30 at night like we did and decide to go on a prowl. Some of the cafe's/restos nearby can be a bit pricey so be sure to lookout for something more budget friendly. I enjoyed my stay enough to say that I would recommend it to anyone on a tight budget and has the right expectation. You get what you pay for. I would definitely consider coming back to this hotel unless I get lucky enough to afford something more luxurious. Overall, it was a really lovely stay.

author: mxu
title: Better than expected, good location and good price
text: 30s walk to Station St-georges of Line12. Ok lobby ok reception ok doorway. Met 3 staffs, the girl was the best and was willing to spk En. The lift was out of order at our arrival in the late eve, so we had to carry our 18kg bag by the stair. But the lift was repaired the next day, surprise, so no carry-down for check out. We didn't expect high so the room was better than our expectation. The room 530 was about 9 square meter, with a 4 squre meter bathroom and a small balcony. In addition, there's one narrow desk and one 19inch LCD on the wall. The closet is at the door way separated by a two-side door, door to close the doorway and to close the bathroom. The window glass was two-layer, but a little noisy from the stree still can squeeze into the room, but no bother. We stayed there for two nights and the room was enough confortable. Shower cabine was a bit too small but the water was good, good German equipment too. There's no wifi, but I didn't have mood for internet at all after arriving such a city as a tourist. 10euro for breakfast was too much even though a lot of people was there eating, some were from neighborhood? The living zone where the hotel locates offers lots of cafe, boulancherie, boucherie et marche. We had out breakfast out there and packed salad, meet, drink, fruit for pic-nic at Versaille.

author: wissaw
title: Great Cheap Hotel in Paris Super close to Metro
text: Great small boutique hotel in Paris. This hotel is right near the Montmarte area. It is just a few steps from the St. Georges Metro stop. It is in a quaint little neighborhood. All of the desk staff spoke some English and we had no problems. The room was very small, but had a large bathroom. The elevator was tiny, not big enough for the two of us and all of our luggage. Not much storage in the room besides a little closet. Room was cleaned daily and provided fresh towels. Everyone was helpful and friendly. The breakfast was not included since we purchased online, but we enjoyed a little bakery around the corner. The metro couldn't have been easier with it stopping just steps from the hotel. Neighborhood was quaint, but just a few minutes walk from the red light district. We didn't have any problems, though. The room was not air conditioned but had big windows that opened onto a teeny tiny french balcony. This hotel was just perfect for us! I would definitely stay there again!

author: 175cynthiat
title: More Hostel than Hotel
text: We stayed at this hotel for 2 nights during our visit to Petra -- and I'm glad it wasn't any longer. It's a very basic accommodation and cost us around 35JD (62 CDN) total which we paid upon arrival. PROS: Cheap! That's all this place has going for it -- even then I'm sure there are more comfortable options around. The staff were nice and they try to help out however they can. Wifi was OK -- not fast but it worked. They offer a basic breakfast for a small fee. CONS: Rooms are VERY basic -- florescent lights made the room look even more depressing, the lock on the door didn't feel secure, no safe in the room. The beds were too soft, and I wouldn't bet money that the bedding and towels were 100% clean. The bathroom smelled wet and the shower was terrible. After a long day of hiking and being in the sun, the best part is hopping into a nice, relaxing shower ... don't count on that here. No water pressure AT ALL, no warm water either. That was the deal breaker for me. We decided to go to a local hamman for a scrub and a decent shower instead. Oh did I mention, there were rolling blackouts??? We experienced the power going out on our floor TWICE! The man at the front desk told us that it happens occasionally and we would have to just wait in the dark until it came back (which thankfully wasn't too long). Petra Gate might be good for some people who are on a budget and have minimal requirements from an accommodation other than a place to lay their heads. But I wouldn't recommend it.

author: lsen
title: Very simple hotel/hostel with a very good service (meals) and a nice view of Wadi Musa”
text: GOOD: The hotel is more likely hostel, quite good for bagpackers. It has a good location a lot of restaurant near by where you can eat. It is around 20 -30 minutes by walk to the Petra Gate entrance (on the return trip it is a really a hill but even after a full day walking you can make it. Some people také taxi from Petra gate in the afternoon - it costs 20-30 JD). The greatest benefit is service - especially cost of meals. They provide simple buffet breakfast for 3,5 JD, lunch packet for 3,5 JD and a diner (1 main typical dish and a buffet mezze and sallads - EXCELENT ). These prices for Petra are really unrivalled. We arrived in the morning around 10:00 and we got a room. It was very pleasant. BAD: The hotel is more likely hostel, quite good for bagpackers. It has a good location a lot of restaurant near by where you can eat. It is around 20 -30 minutes by walk to the Petra Gate entrance (on the return trip it is a really a hill but even after a full day walking you can make it. Some people také taxi from Petra gate in the afternoon - it costs 20-30 JD). The greatest benefit is service - especially cost of meals. We arrived in the morning around 10:00 and we got a room. It was very pleasant.

author: retrospektive85
title: Can't agree with all those good reviews
text: We stayed in that hostel for nights. We decided for the Petra Gate Hostel because of the good reviews we've read. First I want to say that the hostel mananger and the other person who's working there (we haven't seen any more people there) are really helpful and friendly. But besides that the hostel itself isn't in its best years. for 10 JD we got a small room with a double bed. The whole interior was very old, the bedding including the towels weren't the cleaniest. We only had one blanket for two people and it was that big, so one of us had to deal with an old woolen blanket without having any cover on it. In the bathroom there isn't hot water, our entire stay the water only get lukewarm and the shower was badly calcified so the water was only dropping out of it... The shower and toilet is in one room and the shower is directly next to the toilet which means when you taking a shower the whole floor is flooded because the water can't drain properly. They don't provided floor mats so after the shower the whole toilet and the rooms is getting wet because you'be got no chance to dry you feet. In the room there is no aricondition or heater, at night it's getting really cold this time of the year so you'll need to wear a warm jacket unless you don't care to freeze. You can order breakfast for 2 JD per person which wasn't the best deal. We expected a nice breakfast but it's more a buffet consisting of sliced sausage, boiled grey smelly eggs, kind of jam, butter, processed cheese, some olives and sliced tomatoes and cold hard pita bread. Unfortunately we paid for the breakfast in advance. Last but not least the wifi connection in our room on the first floor was really bad and slowly. I can only give 2 stars because of the kindliness of the manager. But the whole building including the rooms definetly need a renovation!

author: melaniepostbox
title: Unexpected Treat! Generous Jordanian Hospitality!
text: We stayed at the Petra Gate Hotel in March 2016 as a group of 7 from Canada. Our entire trip to Jordan was organized by Nasser at the hotel. A taxi was waiting for us at the Eilat/Aqaba border. We had a delicious, home cooked meal at the hotel on the first night and purchased additional tickets to see Petra at Night (which was amazing!). The next day we enjoyed breakfast and were given a packed lunch (egg, pita, juice box, cucumber, tomato, cheese and a few packaged sweets) for our day at Petra (we had bought the Jordan pass which included our admission to Petra). That evening Nasser arranged for us to go to the Turkish Bath close by. What an experience! The next morning Nasser arranged for a taxi cab to take us to Wadi Rum where we met with our next host. We enjoyed a 5 hour jeep tour of the desert (including sand boarding on a giant red sand dune!) and then we were welcomed at the Bedouin camp where we spent the night. The dinner in the camp was so delicious and cooked in the earth! The next day we were delivered by taxi to the Aqaba border once again. We felt very taken care of and enjoyed the kind hospitality of Nasser and all those who worked at the hotel. Highly recommended if you don't mind a budget accommodation. Free wi-fi worked great. Rooftop terrance was charming. Overall very clean.

author: JenTravelsNow
title: Like staying with a family friend.
text: I've already reviewed Nasser and the Petra Gate Hotel on Booking, but I want to do it here as well. I recommend this hostel! The price is unbeatable, and although the lodgings are not luxurious, I would choose to stay there again. I felt cared for. Dinner was prepared every night and served communally, and was excellent. Any time I needed a ride one was found for me, often with family or the owner himself. I once came home unexpectedly early after getting tired (I was in Petra exploring for almost 4 full days) and within an hour they made a multi-course delicious lunch even though it was just for me! I felt safe there, and I am a woman who was traveling alone on this trip. I saw some negative reviews on Booking and I want to say that I think those may have been from folks who thought this was going to be Petra Gate Guest House. It is not, and if you are looking for that experience you may not be in to Petra Gate Hotel. But trust me - you can be in a resort hotel anywhere in the world. In Petra, you want to be in a place that gives you good information to support deep exploration of the city, that makes you feel like family when you come home at the end of the day. This is that place. Please support this small locally owned non-chain hostel. I am sure they will take good care of you.

author: jasonl54
title: Dirty / Cold Rooms & Two-Faced Management
text: Initially, Nasser and his family seemed nice, however, they quickly turn against you if you have any issue with their hotel. You can tell from other negative reviews on this site that they readily trash talk you if you didn't have a good experience. Nasser accommodated a late arrival and helped arrange transport for me from the airport, which was great. However, upon arrival, things quickly went south. The room was very tiny, dirty, and dark with only a single power plug. The bathroom floor was covered in water and there appeared to be a leak and it smelled of sewage. Also, the bedsheets and blankets were very gross / dirty. I notified Nasser about the water in the bathroom and he mopped it up. However, it continued to leak and smell horribly. Later, when I discovered the dirty sheets, I went down and told a younger man at the front desk and he just shrugged at me when I asked for clean sheets. Additionally, the room was frigidly cold despite an old rickety heater going at full blast. At that point, I walked down the block and found Al Rashid Hotel, which offered an identical rate, for a very clean, warm and modern hotel room. I went back to Petra Gate Hotel and informed the guy at the front desk I was leaving due to the aforementioned issues with the room. He didn't protest and I left. They didn't offer a refund for my stay. After posting the review above on another travel site, Nasser went on to trash talk me saying that I expected a "5 star experience at a 1 star price". By no means did I expect a "5 star experience" at Petra Gate, but I did expect basic sanitary conditions and a comfortable room, neither of which was provided even given my multiple communications to the front desk. I would strongly urge you to avoid this hotel during your visit to Petra. You can find vastly nicer hotels for identical prices in the immediate vicinity.

author: onimity
title: Avoid at all costs; Dangerous for solo female travelers
text: I stayed at the Petra Gate hotel based on reviews here and was horribly disappointed. I will skip over the detail on the minor stuff, room not as promised, door didn't lock, packing tape holding the sink together, no heat in December, dirty room... that is all undesirable but "you get what you pay for" and this is a cheap place to stay. However, the man, Yousef, in the lobby suggested as restaurant where a man there wouldn't leave me alone. Because there was no heat in my room, and the WIFI didn't reach my room, I was in the lobby that evening after dinner when the man from the restaurant drove by and saw me. I hadn't said anything about where I was staying. Yousef let him in to talk to me, and when I started heading upstairs they broke into a fight, which almost came to blows. The guy left, and Yousef tried to persuade me to come back downstairs. He had been talking my ear off and telling me that he 'felt something special' for me, so I took it as a good chance to get away. However, he didn't stop. I had complained earlier about my room being cold, but when he asked if I wanted more blankets I said no. I had 2 warm blankets, but I really just wanted HEAT for when I was sitting on the tile floor trying to get my e-mail -- the only alternative to being harassed by him in the lobby. However, he kept knocking on my door, bringing blankets (no thank you) then beer... It made me especially nervous since the wood around the door lock was barely in place, it could easily have been forced open. The next evening, the man from the restaurant saw me walking back from Petra and followed me. It was at this point I decided that I was not really safe there and decided to check out. The owner decided to charge me for the following night as well, though, to be fair I argued him out of it and he was not aware of all the circumstances as Yousef was there while I was checking out and I didn't want to put myself in further danger by angering him; he'd already told me about how he'd been shot, been in jail...etc. Petra is amazing and the people there on the whole are phenomenal, but as long as this man is employed by the hotel I don't recommend it to anyone, least of all women traveling alone.

author: jinnssy
title: A truly budget hotel
text: If you want value for money to stay in Petra, this hotel is the place for you. Remember it is a budget hotel/hostel so don't expect to get nice plush accomodation and 5 star amenities. Free wi-fi available. The room that we had is downstairs with a view over the town. The room look old and the bathroom that we had is.. worn. The heater works intermittently and there is no closet to put your stuff in but please, don't let all of these things keep you away from this hotel. What you will get is a 5 star service from it brilliant staff. The breakfast is cheap (JD2) and nourishing. They can pack u a simple packed (JD5, i think) lunch for your whole day trip in Petra. The owner (Mr Naseer) is kind enough to ferry us to the main entrance, advise us on all the best dining places (cheap and good) and treat us like old friends rather than guests. Ms Leia, her warmth and kindness light up the place during those cold winter days. The staff are all very humble, sincere, honest, easy going and hardworking folks. If i may, upgrade your bathroom so it looks more cosy, invest in a more reliable system for the heater and hot shower and put in more racks inside the room so at least, guests might be able to hang their clothes more so that they are able to air dry them. Even if you guys put them in place and had to charge us a bit more in the future, we will have no qualms about staying with you guys again. Petra gate hotel really made our trip to Petra worth it.

author: Elsiora
title: The best hotel in Jordan??? Are you Blind?
text: I chose this hotel because of excellent reviews. But it is the worst place I've ever been before in reality. Staff is good, I agree with it, but conditions are awful!!! Very-very dirty carpet surface, blankets are full of holes, there is no any door between toilet and room space. I asked to change the room and got another one with something like plastic screen in the toilet. But when I try to close it, it fell out with all screws! Oh! The curtain is hanging on two clips instead of 10 I think. The mosque is nearby. It means you wake up at 5 a.m. And the last one. How I understood the breakfast is included, but it is extra. And you will be surprised of total invoice. I am very disappointed with my stay in Petra Gate Hotel & Hostel! Please be honest in making your reviews. I hope I save future tourists from the mistake choosing!

author: LarryWastoday
title: budget hotel, simple but welcoming
text: We stayed here a few nights in an ensuite room. The hotel is simple, a little dated but the owner and his staff are very welcoming. All in all we had a positive experience. The room was relatively small, was simply decorated and some of the finishing left to be desired. The ensuite bathroom was a wetroom with shower. Hot water was generally available but there were a couple exceptions. Heating was sometimes slow to come on. Breakfast was the simple Jordanian meal that you get in most budget hotels, although you could get a fried egg (which replaced the usual boiled egg). On some website the hotel was described as being within a 10 minute walk from Petra. If you are not Usain Bolt and are not sprinting all the way to Petra, you may want to allow 30-40 minutes (and it is all uphill on the way back). On the other hand, the owner typically offers a lift. On the other hand, the hotel is easy to find and in the town centre, close to most restaurants and shops. Parking (on the street) is not a problem. The hotel has a few compute is available for use at a nominal free. Wireless connectivity is also available. If we were to go back to Wadi Moussa, we would take a look at the other hotels but we would probably go back to the Petra Gate.

author: SanDiegoRichard
title: Nasser is great, place is rundown and dirty.
text: My son, his girlfriend and I took a triple room. They are 26, I am...older. They have traveled the world for 18 months and stayed in all kinds of hostels. The Petra Gate was below any standard they define as OK, and I quote: "It was probably the worst hostel we've stayed in, at least in the past several months. Just falling apart, bugs everywhere... and the bed literally did fall apart and was never fixed while we were there so I just had a mattress on the floor. That said, it is cheap and the owner is extremely nice and helpful...". I have to agree. Hotel owner Nasser is a prince, marking out the preferred walking routes at Petra, giving restaurant suggestions in town, serves a decent breakfast, and he personally drives his guests to the Petra entrance. But one has to adapt to the hostel's dirt, a few bugs, broken and battered fixtures, and see it through. Whatever breaks there that is not absolutely critical, stays broken. They must only repair the most essential items, and then just barely. It’s doubtful that Nasser owns a vacuum cleaner. And yes, my bed collapsed, twice. They "fixed" it once by reattaching the bed rail locking brackets to the bed frame, but the locking clips were old, worn and bent and did not hold. A real repair was needed. So when the bed failed again, my son slept on the mattress on the plywood on the floor so I wouldn't have to do so on my birthday.

author: lippy84
title: A fantastic time with a fantastic host
text: When I arrived in Petra, I was expecting to find it full of tourists and I expected the price to be triple of what it was in Amman. However, when i stumbled on the Petra Gate hotel, I found it to be really fantastic. When I go travelling, i look for somewhere that I can afford and somewhere where there is an atmosphere of the country that i am staying in and not a sterile environment. I was not expecting a five star hotel with maids looking after me, but I did expect a place to be clean and neat. I was able to get my money's worth and more. My room was clean and tidy, the sheets were clean and my bathroom was spotless and hygeinic. The shower had a lot of hot water and the food was great. There was a wide variety of dishes. However, these are things that a lot of hotels with have. The one thing that I have not found in many hotels is a host who is genuinely out there to help. Nasser, the owner felt like he understood me and what I needed as well as all sorts of travellers. He was always interested in what I had to say and any feedback I would give him. He helped me and a lot of other guests with what to do and see, and he was able to save me money on taxis and tours aftewrads to Wadi Rum. He is a very friendly guy and will go out of his way to make sure you enjoy yourself, and the whole time, i felt like i was in Jordan chatting with a Jordanian and not a sterile hotel. I would highly recommend this hotel. I felt like I wa

author: FordPrefect421
title: Adequate nights sleep
text: My parents like staying here. No idea why. For my mother’s 70th birthday we had a trip down to London and stayed here for their sake. Family room for 2 adults and 2 kids (14 and 12). The room was clean but TBH tired and cramped. Dingy decor and poor lighting. The bathroom was huge however! Beds were comfy although my wife said the pillows were not. The shower was intermittently cold and hot and had a screen that, concertina in nature, failed to stay shut consequently flooding the floor. Nothing to really moan about but things that need addressing. Breakfast was poor, overpriced and lacking choice. Undercooked sausages and burnt croissants were the house special. A choice of two cereals, bacon, hash browns, eggs etc but hot breakfast is served in a different room to continental breakfast. Since my wife and daughter wanted continental we had to split up. You can carry your food from the cooked breakfast room to the other restaurant if you wish. A total of £36 which included a £2 per person guest discount voucher. I slept well and the location is convenient but it’s in dire need of refurbishment. Shutting down, gutting it and starting again.

author: 11SariL
title: Good location, close to Lambeth North Station, ok stay for three nights
text: My daughter and I spent three nights at this hotel. We found our room on the 5th floor to be clean and comfortable, although a bit small. The biggest minus in the room was that there was no safe deposit box (those were available on the ground floor, in a corridor). Our room faced Lambeth Road, so there was some noise from traffic, but on the fifth floor, earplugs helped with that nicely. The hotel had two elevators close to the reception. One of them was broken all through our stay. Our room did not include breakfast, but it was possible to pay for it daily. 2£ discount coupons were available at the reception. You could either choose continental or full English breakfast, and these were available in different rooms. The room for the full breakfast was pretty small, but we found a table every morning. I found the English breakfast buffet to be well worth the money spent (£7.90 per person with the discount). The buffet included, for example, scrambled and fried eggs, fried tomatoes, bacon, two kinds of yogurt, toast, fresh fruit salad, and different kinds of pastries. I found the hotel's location to be very good - a short and easy walk from Lambeth North Station. Would I return to the hotel? I would if they had safe deposit boxes in the rooms. I did not feel comfortable using a safe deposit box that was located in a corridor. As it is, I had not noticed that they didn't have them in the rooms when booking the hotel. Otherwise, I was happy with our stay.

author: 548brettp
title: Fantastic staff
text: Arrived here Saturday 23rd February. Only to be told by the man at the desk we didn't have a room as the company we booked through (gala hotels) hadn't paid them and that they had gone bust. No fault of the hotel, but obviously abit stressed they looked for an alternative hotel on their computer for us to see if they could find us anything cheaper than their last room as it was £119 to stay there. Obviously there isn't much out there on a Saturday in London so we decided to take their offer. They looked after us by giving us breakfast and parking for free as we were already out of pocket a very nice gesture from them. All the staff were friendly towards us and the room was perfect. Only a 30 min stroll into the town. Bar prices were excellent and again bar staff were friendly and made sure we felt welcome. The breakfast was just perfect a good selection was on offer very busy but was prepared to wait. Wish I could remember the staffs names (sorry) as they truly deserve a mention. Overall fantastic stay and if we visit London again I wouldn't hesitate to book again. Also a few nice pubs within 1 minute of the hotel very handy. Oh and happy hour 6pm till 8pm very nice touch. Well done to all at the hotel. Thank you.

author: Happiness13114037043
title: The restaurant! :/
text: My mother and I came to visit London for a couple days, and wanted somewhere convenient and not too expensive to lay our heads for the night. We found this, and at first, weren’t too disappointed. Beds seemed okay enough, and the bathroom wasn’t bad. However, as the time we spent there progressed, it gradually got quite a bit worse. We came here about 2pm to check in and drop off our bags, the staff seemed friendly and even though we were on the 5th floor, the elevator made it so we weren’t too bothered. Yet, after coming back not more than 4 and a half hours later, both lifts were out of service, and a lady informed us that she had to use the stairs, even though she had a torn ligament in her knee, and so walking up and down stairs caused immense pain. On top of this, when we went to the restaurant, the steak I had (granted I asked for rare), was hardly cooked at all, and cold upon serving. It cost £16. And didn’t even come with chips. The brownie for dessert looked pre-packaged, but was warm. And the ice cream served with it wasn’t bad. Although, to top it off, a man near us asked for a prawn starter, and was served the prawns with the shells on. He commented this to one of the staff, whom proceeded to take his plate, put it on the empty space on the table, and pick the shells off! Bare handed! The rooms aren’t bad if you’re looking for a place to rest your head, and the public bathroom downstairs was surprisingly clean. But, on top of the lift being broken, despite working fine a few hours before, and the really poor restaurant, I can say I would not stay here again, especially not for the price. I think I’ll go back to Travelodge.

author: AlwaysTravelling01
title: Perfect stay
text: Stayed here with a few friends for one night. First time ever stayed in a Days Hotel and have been extremely surprised how good the stay was. Reception staff were friendly and check in was efficient and quick. My room was a double on floor three. The room had a modern bathroom with shower and the bed was comfortable. It’s not 5* but it was not basic. I have stayed at a lot worse for much more cost. There was tea/coffee making facilities with biscuits. A fan is also in the room which I can imagine in summer months would be used all the time. There is an alarm on the bedroom door if it is not closed fully which is first time I’ve ever seen this and good for those safety conscious guests. The bar/lounge area was comfortable and drinks are available until 2am. Breakfast is well worth it and of good quality. Public areas were very clean. Daily newspapers are free at reception including Sunday times. Impressive to have these included. Tube Lambeth North is 2 min walk away and about 10 min walk to the river. Overall, I will definitely return to this hotel.

author: TanithPanic
title: An even nicer stay than my first visit
text: I'd been looking forward to my stay at Days Hotel again, having stayed here a couple of years ago. I did wonder if the standards would have dropped, which sometimes happens with a good hotel, but I had an even better time on this visit. I was given a room on the ground floor which was more than helpful, and so was the disabled shower room that I had. There were grab rails everywhere, which made me feel so confident and the shower was so easy to operate - no wasting valuable time adjusting temperatures and volume with this hotel! I've seen one or two comments about rude staff but I found the staff were lovely. And it might be worth remembering that with some members of staff, English isnt their first language so what the complainers might see as rudeness I just saw as a natural reserve when speaking. I had to ask the lady on reception who booked me a taxi on Sunday night one or two questions twice but no way does that mean she was rude. I decided to try the continental breakfast on Sunday and was really happy with it. Vassilim was so helpful as I find it hard to balance and go round with a tray. If anything he was a little over-generous with the food but it meant I could take my bananas back to my room to enjoy later. Oh, and my bed? I lay down for a quick catnap on Saturday night and was so comfortable that I was soon 'away with the fairies' as they say. The Internet was a bit pesky to work out at first but once it came through I was able to enjoy a good Wifi service all weekend. Thanks to Elina (I hope I've spelt her name properly) for her valuable help there. I'll just end with a disclaimer here. No, I'm not related to any of the staff. I just genuinely enjoyed my stay in this hotel and would like to come back again.

author: 402alisonh
title: Needs modernising.
text: Due to corporate budgets not matching London pricing at this time of year I’ve stayed at this hotel a fair bit recently. I’ve always found the reception staff efficient and personable. When you spend as much time as I do in hotel rooms it’s really nice to have staff who treat you as an individual and have a brief conversation that’s related to you as opposed to sticking to the script. Sadly the same cannot be said for the staff who man the breakfast room. They can barely be bothered to ask your room number let alone say good morning. I’m always glad to get out of the lifts as I’m never convinced that I’m not going to become stranded in one between floors. The bouncing sensation when the lift stops at one of the floors does not add to that confidence. The rooms are adequate but could definitely do with updating. The reason I’m submitting my review now as opposed to any other time is because the lack of aircon is causing me to have to listen to the noisy traffic because the window is open, listen to a noisy fan that only seems to be blowing warm air around, take the quilt out of its cover because separate sheets aren’t provided and it’s too hot for a duvet and try to sleep with a wet towel around my neck because all other attempts to cool myself down are not working. A good nights sleep is always important but most especially when you’ve got to go to work the next day. Thank goodness for the bottles of water but it does seem to be hit and miss as to whether you get those and the fan. The shower cubicles are way too big for the tiny bathrooms and trying to get in and out of them requires squeezing past the sink. I’m not slender but I’m not overly large either and it’s a struggle to get in and out safely. I’ve only eaten here once in the evening and I was pleasantly surprised by how lovely the food was. So all things considered I wouldn’t refuse to stay here but they aren’t my hotel of choice either.

author: darrylm731
title: poor
text: We stayed in this hotel I late june to early july 5 days. This was in the heat wave and no a/c, I can't find this fact in any ads for this place. First, the front desk had staff who were poorly trained, the young lady that checked us in barly spoke english. She tried hard but everything we asked she had to ask someone else this led to a 35 minute check in. The lifts were a joke firstly the walls were badly beat up, the floor was so bad you felt that you should wash your feet, the second lift was out of service the whole time. This meant while staff tied up the lift to do their jobs you could wait up to 15 minutes. While doing the refreshing of the rooms the towels and bedding were thrown in the halls and I mean thrown right across the hallway. I am handicapped and use a cane to get around and it made it very difficult . I mentioned this but nothing changed. The diningroom was a bright spot the food was good althought the prices are high. At breakfast we had ask for salt and pepper everyday we, we gave up on the 3rd day and got our own. Our flight home wasn't until 6PM so when we checked out we ask to keep our bags and were told there was room, it was suggested they could keep them behind the bar and there was a $1.00 pound charge for this service. I have travelled quite often and have never seen a hotel as cheap as this. I spoke to the manager who apologized but said it was policy. It upet us to the point where we left with our bags never to return. There was one young lady who work the front desk, the bar and the dinning room she was from Lativa I think and was a delight to deal with. I wish I could remember her name so I could say thank her personally. The hotel is in a great location, a little more TLC and care would certainly go a long way to change the customer experience. Darryl Middleton their .

author: Phillygirlagain
title: Stay somewhere else
text: I stayed here because it was just about the only place that had a room available. I now know why it had the room to spare. This hotel is cheap - not in terms of price, sadly, but in terms of quality. First of all, it is not very centrally located. It’s a bit out of the action, making it necessary to use public transport to get around. That wouldn’t be so bad (I’ve done it before to save money), but usually, when that’s the case, you get a nicer hotel for a lower price. Not here. The hotel seems old and dingy. Everything is cramped and shoddy. The room was actually a good size, but it was not air-conditioned, so you have to leave the windows open, which means you contend with lots of noise while in the room - especially while trying to sleep. If you come here in the summer, you will have a hot, stuffy room waiting for you at the end of a long day of touring. Not nice. The lack of air-conditioning wasn’t the only problem. The WiFi was so weak, I struggled to do the business I needed to online and couldn’t make a FaceTime call to my husband to set up arrangements for my return home. The faucet on the sink was very old, so it was hard to turn on, and once it did come on, it could only go to full blast, which meant water got everywhere, including all down the front of me every time I wanted to use it. There also aren’t any outlets near the bed, so no using your phone in bed if you want it to be charged for the next day. The one positive thing I can say is the staff was nice. So, there’s that. Presuming my WiFi signal is good enough to submit this review (I am checking out now, getting to the airport several hours early because that’s better than being here), I will encourage you one last time to exhaust all other options before staying here. This place is better than sleeping rough but only just.

author: 306mayaw
title: Average
text: My friend, my 12 year old daughter and my self stayed at this Hotel for four days from 9th April to 12th Apri. We had booked this Hotel because it is located near to all the attractions. We booked a triple room, with 1 double bed and 1 single bed: We got three single beds! Even though we were on the 5th floor, noise if traffic through the night was horrendous. Shower was very tiny. And the shower made weird noises through the night and shower would just turn by itself!!! Honestly, at first I thought this shower or room was haunted!!!! Spoke to reception about it and they said, they'll sort it. And it wasn't sorted. We were three people for four days, and the wardrobe space was probably the size of average person's thighs!!with only five hangers. We had to request for more hangers to hang our coats and clothes... Breakfast was ok. On a positive note, staff were friendly, polite and very respectful. We had dinner at the hotel's restaurant and food was delicious and their Panna cotta is to die for!! We did not enjoy our stay at this Hotel all!!! I hope, no one from here books room 530!!! Honestly,traffic noise from that room isn't good. And shower is tiny, wardrobe is really really tiny!!! Maya

author: tamulizabroad
title: Very good location and good staff
text: I had a course to attend near London Eye and booked this hotel after reading reviews. Glad I did. This hotel is located 5 mins walk from Lambert North Tube station. This hotel has its own car park if you driving to London. I didn’t drive there, so didn’t enquire the parking fees. Check-in was quick. Provided the WiFi password and £2 discount breakfast voucher. I booked a double room, but they gave me a twin room. I didn’t complain as I was alone anyway. Has lift access to upper floors The room was clean, warm and the bathroom was very spacious. Didn’t hear any noise at night and I had good night sleep. Two breakfast options available. Continental and Full English. Average breakfast. Free WiFi available both in the lobby as well as in the rooms. In my room there was no fridge, but kettle to make coffee and tea. The hotel is 15 mins walk away from London Eye. Imperial War Museum is 5 mins walk away. I found it very centrally located to walk most nearby london attractions. The TV had most freeview channels Overall: Cleanliness- 4.5/5 Location- 5/5 Value for money - 4.5/5 Breakfast- 4/5

author: GaronP
title: Recent stay
text: We recently had to stay in London for a few days as one of our Grandchildren was in hospital. We did not want to spend a fortune on a hotel as it was only for a short while. We managed to find this hotel that offered us a very reasonable price for a two night stay. We phoned the hotel to ask if there was any parking available on site as I am disabled and needed ease of access, we were told that there was parking available and due to me holding a Blue Badge there would be no charge. This we thought was very good and was correct as when we arrived we were issued with a ticket that authorised us to park free of charge. On entering the hotel it was evident that this was not one of the more expensive and upmarket hotels, however the reception and bar area were clean and tidy and had very welcoming and polite staff. We were told that there was a small lounge area, 24hour bar and where the continental or full English breakfasts would be served. (Full English £10) however we were given a £2 off voucher each. The room that we had was small and basic, but offered all that we required for our short stay. Tea and coffee making facilities, flat screen TV, small desk area and small hanging space. Full length mirror and hair dryer. The bathroom was very clean and offered a good sized shower cubicle. Although basic this hotel offers you a friendly service, clean room, buffet breakfast and on site parking. Thanks to the nice staff we will return to this hotel for further visits to London, as it also offers very easy access to the Underground Station at Lambeth North or a short walk to the Elephant and Castle stations. You are also literally two minutes from the Imperial war Museum by foot, and a six to eight minute walk from the Londo eye.

author: szy59l
title: Minimum
text: The lobby, the bed, the bathroom, the toilet, ... everything was there. It was clean and everything was working properly (also the WiFi). So you get the minimum you need to spend the night, But that's about it. The reception staff was pretty unfriendly and not very welcoming. I could see they didn't like their job. I couldn't book a room with breakfast, only without. Breakfast had to be paid on the spot... Don't ask the hotel to call for a taxi. You'll get some dubious 'private' taxi driver who charges different rates (the hotel gets a fee) and doesn’t accept credit cards. If you’re as unlucky as I was, you’ll get a driver who doesn’t know his way around the city. It's better to go out and just stop a taxi on the street. London centre is pretty expensive, so I chose for a cheaper hotel (still above 100 EUR/night), that probably explains a lot. "If you pay peanuts,..." The neighborhood is what it is: Waterloo. Not were you want to be, but only 5 min walk to all the nice places. The hotel has a private parking which could come in handy if you arrive by car.

author: CheekyKB
title: Excellently located but require thicker walls!
text: The hotel is set in a prime location in Waterloo. Great for site seeing and transport is on your doorstep. The hotel is about a 15 minute walk into central London and passing over the bridge you can view the London eye as well as other local attractions. On arrival at the hotel I was greeted by 2 receptionists. I provided my details for check in and was handed a key card. No explanation of the hotel facilities or how to get to my room. I asked where I was going and was advised the lift would take me to my floor. The hotel is clean but basic but since I was only staying here for 1 night it was fine. Bathroom facilities could have done with a re-vamp but this is a standard hotel. Again facilities were clean and shower gel/shower cap was present. Nice clean fluffy towels too. The room itself was very small but I was a lone traveller with a double bed to myself. Décor was slightly tired but it was clean. Team and coffee making facilities were present in the room which was a nice addition after my long day. There was a TV present also. Locating a plug socket took me a while but eventually I found it and was able to charge my phone. I chose not to purchase breakfast in the hotel as I could get something else nearby at a better rate. I also chose not to use the hotels facilities as my visit was a flying visit. My only complaint of the rooms would be the paper thin walls. I’m still feeling slightly scarred by the whole experience!

author: DublinGirl2011
title: Just what we wanted
text: Came to London for a long weekend to see a west end show, as we had never been to london before we wanted to stay somewhere very central to allow us to see the sights. We chose the days hotel for various reasons 1) we thought it to be central and close to transportation links, 2) we have stayed in the days inn hotel chain before and enjoyed it, 3) the price and it didn't disappoint on any of those factors. The hotel was a 2min it's walk from the bakerloo line and another 5min walk to Waterloo station, which is fantastic for all tube connections. We also loved how close it was to the rail lines as we could use this method of transport to get to/from Gatwick airport. From this hotel we could walk easily to the London eye, big Ben, Westminster and Buckingham palace, in fact we found it easy enough to walk to most places within London. On arrival we were early for check in so the lovely receptionist kept our bags to allow us to go explore and see our show. When we finally did check into our room we were happy with the amenities in the room. As usual there were tea/coffee making facilites, a tv, and the bathroom equipped with fresh towels and toiletries. The bed takes up most of the space in the room but it's a great room for a base camp. When we checked out we had to pay a 1pound fee per bag to keep in the room we had used for free on check in to allow us to continue exploring. We didn't eat in the hotel but the menu looked delicious and the prices were reasonable. The only bad this i would say is that the lift does not feel safe at all. Any time you step into it the lift drops a couple of inches. After the first few times using it I decided to use the stairs up and down to the fifth floor until we had to use it again with our bag. I'm sure it is perfectly safe but it just freaked me out so much the first time that I couldn't use it.

author: jebndelorus
title: So-so
text: Stayed for a night on business in October 2017. Good location, a few minutes walk from Lambeth North station. Hotel is on a busy junction, right opposite the Imperial War Museum. Check in was busy, but staff worked quickly (efficient rather than welcoming). My room was on the fourth floor. Welcome couple of bottles of Evian, tea coffee and speculoo biscuits. I ate at the pub behind the hotel, a specialist beer and burger pub, which I'd recommend. Room was quiet but very warm, even in October. An annoying fan in the bathroom ran all night. One of the halogen lights in the bathroom was hanging down by the wire. It all felt a bit rough around the edges and under cared for. Breakfast the next day was disappointing. It's served in a small room off reception (no idea why not in the restaurant...?) Quality was poor, particularly the bland, soft, grey sausage. I'd be cross if I'd spent the £10 they charge for 'full English'. I was also disappointed to see they charge £1 per item for left luggage - surely this is a basic offer from a hotel?

author: SeanMK55
title: Very Comfortable Stay
text: This was our first stay at the Days Hotel in Waterloo. The hotel is an older property but quite well presented and is clean and welcoming. We were warmly greeted by the staff. We had pre-booked and the registration process was seemless. My room was of an older style but comfortable. The bathroom was modernist and there was plenty of hot water. The bed was very comfortable. Wi-Fi was free. The hotel has a lounge area by reception and there is also a small bar area and dining area. The room rate does not include breakfast which cost £8.50 and there was plenty on offer. There is limited seating in the small breakfast dining area so guests also sit in the lounge area and dining room. A bit disjointed. The Days is a budget hotel and provides perfectly good value for what you pay. Pleasant staff, a comfortable bed and plenty of hot water...everything I needed. I would not hesitate to stay there again.

author: AnnabelM161
title: Perfectly adequate for a two night stay.
text: Chose this for the location, it is very good to get to the Imperial War Museum and Waterloo Station, just a one tube stop away from Lambeth North, which is a few minutes down the road from the hotel. Staff really good. Room, small, but adequate. Dripping shower head though! Bed comfy. Hairdryer, mirrors, TV, shower wash fixed to shower, not mini bottles, but never-the-less toiletries included. Breakfast good, choice of cereals, hot & cold drinks (well, tea, coffee, apple or orange juice), cooked brekki for full English. Make your own toast machine. Yoghurts, butter, cakes. All fine. Limited seating in breakfast area, but they opened up restaurant seating, or you have the option of sitting outside. Staff all very accommodating. Security boxes by Reception, not in rooms, but free. £1 charge for leaving luggage for safe keeping, which we used as we had checked out, but were not leaving London till later in the day. Had a ground floor room, which is probably not a good idea, it was very hot and you couldn't open a window for security reasons (being ground floor), a desk fan was supplied, which was noisy (if you're not used to them), no traffic noise though, and plenty of trees and bushes outside to shield your view of a busy main road. Good value overall. I would book again, but not if I was staying a week or more.

author: 205colleenc
title: Customer service is terrible!
text: If you value your priceless items and then accidentally forget them, don't plan on getting them back. When we were already on a train out of London, my daughter realized that she had left her two most precious and priceless belongings behind in the bed. She has had these items since she was a baby. I called the hotel immediately and was hung up on the first time. I called again and reported the left items and was told to call back in the morning as the hospitality staff had already left for the evening. The staff member barely understood what I was saying and I spoke very plain English. I called the next day and was told to email my concern, which I had already done, but received no response...book@hotelwaterloo.com doesn't work. She then gave me another email address and I forwarded the message I'd already sent earlier. She then responded rather quickly that there was nothing left in the room and apparently she thought this was enough work on her part. So to make a long story short and 9 emails later, the items have not been found, so either they were thrown away (WHY) or they've been lost at the laundry facility. I believe all of this could have been avoided if more action had been taken immediately, not after 9 emails. I would rate this hotel's customer service as terrible. My daughter and I stayed in the hotel for two nights. The room was stifling and one window barely opened, but it was clean. Breakfast was overpriced and terrible.

author: MarkOlsen
title: Hotel near Waterloo station
text: I stayed at this large (162 rooms over 5 floors) hotel in late April 2017 during a visit to London. I arrived on a train at the Waterloo station and simply walked from there to the hotel in about 15 minutes with a large piece of luggage. The Lambeth North tube station on the Bakerloo line is also very near (2 blocks) the hotel if coming from Heathrow airport - take the Piccadilly line to the Piccadilly Circus station and then transfer to a brown Bakerloo train (destination; Elephant & Castle) four stops. This hotel is across the street from the free Imperial War Museum and walking distance to the Westminster Bridge, Big Ben, Houses of Parliament, London Eye, Aquarium, Dungeon and city center. The hotel room had a very small TV with a limited number of channels, desk, chair, closet, hair dryer, full length mirror and shower but no tub. The windows were double paned but I was able to easily heard police sirens and the blackout curtains really weren't effective in keeping out the early morning light. The bed was comfortable with a choice of pillows but had a single futon instead of the sheets and blanket I prefer. There was a continental breakfast for £7.95 or full English breakfast for £9.95 that I didn't try so I can't comment on the quality. There was a very lively bar and restaurant on the ground floor open nightly till 10:00 pm. There also were 4 PCs in the lobby to check e-mails at a cost of £2.50/hour and you could leave your luggage for £1.00/item for the day (not overnight) for early arrivals or late departures. I saw a very limited number of parking spaces (~15) in front of the hotel (£20/24 hours or £10 from 9:00 am - 5:00 pm) and some street parking. Check-in was a very late 2:00 pm and check-out a very early 11:00 am. The hotel had two elevators that were the slowest of any I've ever seen and were barely able to handle the five floors. This is a older hotel that is centrally located and is good as a place for storing your luggage and sleeping. The room was very small and the furnishing were dated and in need of replacement but everything was clean. If looking for a reasonably priced hotel in an expensive city this would be an acceptable choice.

author: greatholsDevonUK
title: OK Hotel Good Location
text: I have stayed here quite a few times and it has been ropey at best, but work like it because it is cheap. In the past I have found the food to be so bad that I have just not bothered and eaten out. This time I was pleasantly surprised. Bottled water in the room was a big plus ++++ The room was standard days inn fayre but well stocked with tea / coffee and clean and tidy. The room was well serviced during my stay and towels etc were replenished each day. Breakfast has improved somewhat since my last visit and I have to admit that it really was ok! The staff were very good. Polite friendly and helpful. On check out I realised that my car, which was in the overflow carpark at the rear, had taken a direct hit from what I can only assume to be a flock of albatross! Seriously bad. Having paid £20 a day to park my car it was annoying to have to pay to get it cleaned so that I could drive home. The Hotel Manager offered to have maintenance get some of it cleared off. Unfortunately I could not wait as she had trouble locating them but at least she tried. Definitely would be worth erecting shelters over that particular area due to the overhanging trees! The improvement in customer service and breakfast is great news for this hotel and I hope it continues :-)

author: Skywalker714
title: Fantastic Stay!!
text: Just back from a two nights stay in London and so pleased we chose this hotel to stay. We were booked on a bed and full breakfast option. Upon arrival the reception staff were very friendly, the girls English wasn't so clever but we got over the language barrier. We stayed in room 120, two doors from the lift. Our room had a double bed, dressing table area, small and compact wardrobe and some drawers. Ideal for what we needed the room for. Pros for the hotel - small bar area which isn't overally priced. Small breakfast area for b+b residents which was fantastic. Breakfast consisted of rolls, toast, pastries, fresh fruit and fruit salad. Yoghurt, cheese portions as well as jam marmalade and Nutella portions. There were croissants, selection of cereals and of course the hot options which consisted of fried and scrambled eggs, hash browns, beans, mushrooms, bacon and sausages also. Selection of tea, coffee and hot chocolate too. The hotels in an ideal location wherever you choose to visit in London. The nearest underground station is Lambeth North which is five mins walk away. Public transport links for this area are plentiful and the hotel is located in an ideal part of London. Cons- we couldn't get to stay longer 😔

author: xxjadexx2015
title: Great hotel, all you need to explore the City
text: Positives: Room was absolutely perfect for what you need; comfy bed, comfy pillows, TV, kettle and refreshments and very nicely done bathroom facilities. Opted for breakfast every day which was lovely as on site. Got a voucher for money off on the first morning too which was a nice touch. Negatives: Housekeeping incident: As most people do we put the sign on our door for it to be cleaned. We went out all day and came back around 6 - 7 pm to find our room door was ajar. The housekeeping had been and cleaned it however had left the door open afterwards! We were horrified as all our belongings were inside and we had been out all day. I phoned down to reception to let them know but if i am honest they did not seem too bothered. I then went down to reception to explain the situation to be told 'a note had been left for housekeeping'. I argued that i was really not happy but still had no apology or anything - it felt more like i was being a hindrance explaining this situation which was not a nice feeling. This was very disappointing. We stayed for 3 nights and did not want anyone to clean our room again. I was just upset at how the reception staff gave us no feedback, apology or anything. We would very much so like to stay at this hotel again but am just frustrated at this response. We, as many people do, put our trust into the hotel and they broke it without any interest in resolving the problem.

author: lkb59353
title: Good location. Modern and clean.
text: Just minutes from the Waterloo, N Lambeth, tube stop, this hotel was everything we needed. Friendly staff, comfortable beds, clean and spacious bathroom. It's an easy walk to many sites, just minutes across Westminster bridge to Parliament and Big Ben. Also not far from the Bourrough Market, London Tower, Tower Bridge, or The Globe theatre, we walked to these locations but took the tube back after a performance at the Globe. There are also some excellent pubs nearby, The Three Stags has great burgers and traditional food. The pub right behind the hotel was good, too. Never tried the Hotel restaurant but heard good reviews from others staying there One night we walked around the area near the hotel and enjoyed seeing the gardens near the Lambeth Palace. Visiting with the locals in the area is one of the best reasons to stay here. They were all so friendly. Unless you are set on staying right in the middle of things this hotel is a great value. No complaints at all. Really, by tube or bus you can be at many major sights in less than 10 minutes, about the same as on foot. We went to Hampton Court by train and it was a very easy train ride only about a half hour ride. Can't say enough good things about the staff, either. 24 service at the desk.

author: iidael
title: Will stay again
text: Stayed for six nights with my boyfriend. The hotel was in a good area, about 10-15 minutes walk to Waterloo station, where it was easy to take the tube to pretty much anywhere. Approximately 15 minutes walk to the London Eye and Big Ben, too. The Imperial War Museum is just across the road. Good restaurants and grocery stores nearby. The room was clean, beds were ok, nothing bad to say about it. It could get a bit cold during the night. We tried to get the heating system on, unsuccessfully. Luckily the blanket was warm enough. The staff were both friendly and unfriendly. We didn't really need any services so it didn't matter that much. Breakfast we had once and it was average, although a bit pricey. The elevator was a bit creepy, because it was a bit shakey and the doors took a while to open. We got used to that, though. Also, the hotel room door was sometimes a bit of a headache. It was hard to open, because the card didn't seem to work well every time. We didn't really mind that because usually it worked on the second or the third try. I will probably choose this hotel the next time I visit London. It's not luxurious but it's worth the money. We had a good stay at Days Hotel Waterloo.

author: /undefined
title: Great location
text: Rooms are small, but my sister & I were able to manage ok, as we weren't here to spend time in room but sight see. So this hotel was a great location for that. Wasn't much closet space, so we didn't unpack but manage out of our suitcases. Hotel has no AC, but there was a fan in room. The bathroom was an odd shape & shower stall was small. The bath towels were large (which I like) but a little on the old side with edges starting to fray & a little rough. Also nice to have a place to eat at hotel, even though we only ate breakfast there a couple of times, as we were out during day & eat supper before returning most times. Plus there are a few places close by to eat at, as well as a small grocery store for snacks that was open until 11pm. Only small issue we had was when we booked original through Expedia we booked before flights were booked & after booking flights realized they were booked for day after we checked out. So we had contacted hotel & booked extra night. They had both reservations on check in, but said to come back on end of 1st reservation to check in again. And when we did at first they had us booked in different room. Weird, but the desk person was able to fix that for us. I think they should have had that arranged before we got there as they had both reservations, as I had given them Expedia # when asking for extra night & they were both attached together when we got there. But it all worked out in the end.

author: Gusse
title: Convenient
text: Knowing that the hotels in London is pricey and with cramped rooms, this hotel surprised us in a good way. Using a wheelchair and in need of more space we were happy to be given a spacey room with a spacey bathroom. The beds were extremely soft, but we had a good sleep comfort. The hotel is situated in a area without the most traffic noise, but there were double glassed windows. The room had carpet, like most London hotels, and this was not really clean, but other than that we felt the cleaning was satisfactory. The heating panel worked fine, but there were little light from the lamps. No problems for us, as we just wanted to sleep there. Bathroom was ok, but with an insane little sink. Towels changed every day. Had breakfast once, but that was really not worth the money. Extremely limited choice. So we went to a cafe nearby to eat a better breakfast for the same price. Reception staff was friendly, and check-in and -out went fast. Good location, with several restaurants nearby. Waterloo train statin 15 min walk away. Lambeth North tube station around 5 in walk away. We used mostly the bus, that stopped at several stops 2-5 min away. Recommended hotel if you are a wheelchair user, but can walk a little. It's not fully adapted.

author: susanaquerida
title: Horrible airless room
text: I really haven't give many bad reviews before, but this place was so bad, we moved out after 2 bad nights. There is no air circulation in the room, so they provide a desk fan. But there is no counter space, so you can't open 2 suitcases at the same time. Only 2 drawers and a tiny closet to put things away. The bed was so bad, lumpy and soft that I have been in pain all the next day from it. The room temperature was even hotter than outside, which was already hot at 27. Couldn't sleep from the heat, with the fan going, which just blows air around. Room is dark and you have to turn the light on even in daytime to see anything. Did I mention how small the room is? Only 1 person at a time can walk past the bed or into the bathroom. The shower stall was full of mildew. I took pictures and brought them to the front desk, who reported it to housecleaning. Some improvement on day 2, but lots still remained behind the shower door. Disgusting. This is a budget hotel that is no bargain if you value a decent nights' sleep. Didn't have breakfast there because of other poor reviews.

author: kristinm730
title: You Get What You Pay For
text: My family and I stayed at this hotel for a week during a surprise heat wave in mid-July, and it was unbearably hot. There is no AC at this hotel, and we couldn't leave our window open because people were partying/talking loudly and smoking in the courtyard outside our room (we were on the first floor) until all hours of the night. The fan did nothing more than blow hot air. The showers were the tiniest we have ever seen, and we have traveled to other European countries. Furthermore, the continental breakfast was beyond boring and the same exact thing every morning. We could tell that some of the fruit salad (mostly apples) had been recycled for far too long. The hotel employees were cordial when you asked for assistance, but did not go out of their way at all, and didn't even greet us when we entered the lobby each day. The bed sheets and towels felt like Brillo pads, but the maids were very diligent about leaving fresh towels each day. Like most who vacation in Europe, we booked a room based on the fact that we would only be sleeping there, but when you can't take a shower and get out of that room without sweating like crazy, or return to that room until after 10 PM (when it's cooled down), it's a problem. Finally, we were not aware that the Lambeth Tube station (closest to the hotel) would be shut down for repairs throughout our stay, so it took even longer to get to the places we needed to go. Waterloo is an ok area to stay in when that station is open. On a positive note, we really enjoyed some of the restaurants near the hotel (easy walk) such as the Steam Engine Pub, The Three Stags, and Cotto. There were also 2 convenience stores, a pharmacy, Costa coffee, and the Imperial War Musesum within a very short walking distance. If we could do it all again, we would upgrade our hotel without the breakfast included to have a better location and AC/cooler room. There are many restaurants that serve a delicious full English breakfast for 5-6 pounds.

author: PaulB589
title: Great location at a modest price
text: Overall the hotel exceeded our expectations: * Location - convenient for the city centre, you can walk if you're feeling fit or there are bus stops just outside the hotel and taxis are easy to hail from the street. We walked from the hotel across Westminster Bridge, via Parliament and up to Trafalgar Square and then back across Charing Cross Bridge to the hotel - circa 90 mins including a stop for a beer! * Room - the beds, pillows and linen were very comfortable, the room clean and room amenities in line with the cost of the hotel. We asked for a quiet room and that's what we got, helped by having an outer and inner window. No air conditioning but a fan was provided, however we found that with the window open we were fine. * Catering - we opted for continental breakfast (pastries, rolls, toast, jams, cheeses along with freshly cut fruit which was chilled and excellent. There was a bar area and seating both inside and out. There are also pubs and bars nearby e.g. across the road. * 'Nice Touches' - we felt the hotel staff were excellent, smiling and welcoming. There was a bowel of apples available throughout the day. There was a choice of 2 newspapers (complimentary). We purchased a couple of tickets on line and needed to get them printed out - the reception staff were very accommodating and there was no charge. Complimentary wifi. We overheard that they provided a complimentary left luggage service but we did not use this facility. We stayed there to spend a short break in the city and found the hotel to 'punch above its weight' and we will certainly consider returning the next time we visit London. We could have doubled our cost by staying in a 5 star hotel but preferred to save the expense and have 2 trips! Thank you Days Inn - great job for exceeding our expectations, Paul

author: nyalpi
title: Surprisingly good hotel at a very central location, cheaper than other hotels in central London
text: Stayed one night. Paid about £85 which is cheaper than all other hotels in central London. Surprisingly good -- I looked at another hotel in the vicinity for the same price but didn't have windows and didn't provide towels! Easy walking distance to Waterloo Station, Houses of Parliament etc. The building is dated, the elevator is slow and old, but surprisingly (despite the TripAdvisor reviews) the room did not look dated, but was clean. Room was not big but it was not at all cramped (I've been in many very tiny city center hotels). The bathroom had been renovated recently so it was modern and clean. Dove soap and shampoo provided. Hairdryer in room. No fridge in room. English and Continental breakfast available for purchase in the lobby, but I didn't have any. Double glazed window that looked through many trees, so minimal noise from the street. The whole place seemed quiet and peaceful. Free wifi (despite what is said on the hotel website). Overall I was very pleased and I certainly recommend to other tourists to London who want to stay in the city center but not pay a fortune.

author: 310lainec
title: Great location, horrible day-time service.
text: Perfect location to the tube and comfortable room. My problem lies with the daytime staff. I noticed a bag of purchases made on my vacation missing my last day. It was obviously mistaken for trash. I noticed the evening before my departure and notified the nighttime staff (night manager and Frank).
