Those two went above and beyond helping search for my items but because it was more than a day the items were missing, they were not in the trash. They assured me the daytime staff would look for me and followup as to what to do next. I talked with what I think was a French front desk woman who proceeded to care less about my problem. She did check with housekeeping but no one had any idea where the items were. I emphasized that I didn't believe the items were stolen (my electronics, including iPad were safe) and it truly was a mistake, though housekeeping should not throw away trash other than what's in the bin. After learning I had over 100 pounds gone, I was immediately told to file a police report. I said it was obvious what happened and she again could care less. I did not even get an apology. I loved London and am sad I won't have the several items both me and my husband found to remember our trip. I'd certainly stay here again, so long as I would o lay deal sigh the nighttime staff who obviously cared. I give service only 1 star which should be for Frank, who stood with me at 11 PM looking through a dumpster.

author: Z6385RDdawnb
title: Family weekend
text: Arrived they gave us room 12, I'm really not one to complain at all but felt I had to. The room was tired and small and noisy as it only had single Windows and was on the ground floor. It was almost like a hospital room. I went to reception and they said they would change us next morning. The next morning we had breakfast which was lovely everything you could ask for. They changed our room to 301 which was perfect and more what we expected. Really happy lovely bathroom comfy beds. Plenty of space. We would defiantly come back to this hotel. It is ideally situated two mins walk from tube. And 5 mins from the London eye. Some lovely pubs and a great Turkish restaurant just outside the hotel. The steam engine pub does the best burgers ever. Great hotel for family's staying for weekend as you have lots of amenities just outside the hotel. Also shops and a chemist.

author: shannonzetajade
title: Family room
text: Room 401 stayed 17th till 19th February. Disappointed as bed lights above my children head were faulty and dangerous. As they was not secured probably and fell in my daughter's head while sleeping. Which injured her head with nasty bump. Went to put light back a sparked a blue spark. Very dodgy electrics. Not safe to have as family room. Then discovered after having lovely day out for my daughter birthday with special needs. That when come back her London snow globe had been moved and dropped by cleaners. M6 daughter was so upset. Seems cleaners don't care if they damage guests stuff. The room was freezing cold could only get heater to work for a few minutes. And the staff so miserable at reception. Don't recommend it here you be better off paying a extra few pounds more. Where you get treated better.

author: Cymr0Gwiri0n
title: You get what you pay for.
text: Let's start by saying - this isn't an expensive hotel. That should be taken into account above all else I suppose. This was a business trip. My third visit to the hotel. It is centrally located, and as mentioned - affordable. Let's start with the good. Location as I said. Food is good. Bar is well stocked. Staff on the whole are friendly. The bad - The room is small, but it was clean. Only a small heater in the room was inadequate for heating the room. The TV has a very limited selection - however, you wouldn't to stay long in the room. No Air con. So you get what you pay for. I will visit again - for business purpose, on my own - yes. With my family. No!!

author: Barrblue
title: Brief London Break
text: This was the second time we had stayed in this hotel, the previous time having been some five years ago. We found that the reception area, dining area and bar had had a comprehensive re-furb. and all was pristine. The rooms, though a bit on the small side, are spotlessly clean and comfortable. The bathroom was likewise spotless and there was an excellent walk in shower which made it ideal for people who have difficulties stepping into a bath. When we were there previously, there was a fair bit of noise from police carsetc. because Kennington police station is just across the road. On this visit, we found that the widows had been fitted with secondary glazing and this cut down noise levels dramatically. The staff were all wonderful, friendly and went out of their way to be helpful. Notble staff members were Joanne, Melodie and Amina. The Breakfasts were very good with a choice between continental or full English. The dinner menu looked excellent but we didn't eat there in the evening as there is a terrific gastro-pub directly across the road called The Three Stags. (food to die for). For the location, so close to Westminster, it is marvellous value. All in all, a very enjoyable stay, the only real criticism was that the bed was a bit soft and the mattress had seen better days.

author: K7610IMkenm
title: Why pay more!
text: I selected this hotel because of an excellent price on bookings.com and it's proximity to Lambeth Palace. .. 10 minutes walk! Arrived just after noon and was given immediate access to my room... almost 2 hours early! The room was adequate. .. all I was doing was sleeping in it! Staff were attentive and efficient. Breakfast was not in the price but another £9.95 remedied that and was self service. ..so as much as you like! They stored my luggage on the day of my leaving for no extra charge. Downside... looking tired on the outside but that's picking. Overall... excellent for just under £100 Inc. Breakfast. .. don't forget to get best prices though... walk in tarrif is £199 per night!

author: lochnagar
title: Good value, clean and comfortable
text: Spent three nights bed and breakfast at this establishment. Right across the road from Imperial War Museum and just a fifteen minute walk from Westminster Bridge and the London Eye. We had a twin room which was quite clean and comfortable and the bathroom in particular was large although the shower cabinet would be tight for the larger (more rotund) person. We were on B&B - continental style breakfast which was more than adequate. Choices of croissants, pastries, bread, fresh fruit, yoghurts etc but cooked breakfasts also available. There is a reasonably stocked bar and the prices also very reasonable (for London). No complaints there at all. Just two points to be aware of - the hotel can do something about one of them but nothing about the other. There are two lifts to the upper floors - they work perfectly well but sometimes creak alarmingly. Maybe a bit of oil or grease wouldn't go amiss? The hotel is situated very close to a Police station and there are regular "blues and twos" sirens plus there is a busy crossroads junction to the front of the hotel. Quite a bit of regular traffic noise. If that doesn't bother you - fine, but if you like little traffic noise then perhaps not for you. We were on the 4th floor and didn't mind the traffic noise but probably wouldn't stay in one of the lower rooms. Overall, a very pleasant stay and we will return.

author: 212ChrisM212
title: Good couple of nights
text: I stayed at the Days Hotel for a couple of nights at the start of October using some of the Wyndham Rewards points that I had accrued over the last couple of years. They had a deal where you paid with a combination of points and cash which I thought was quite a good deal. The hotel is located only a few minutes walk from Lambeth North station on the Bakerloo Line whilst there are also a few bus routes stop right outside the door. The 59 goes up to King's Cross via Trafalgar Sq and Piccadilly Circus whilst the 159 goes to Marble Arch via Oxford Street. In the opposite direction both buses go to Kennington, Oval and Brixton. I arrived early afternoon and was able to check-in straightaway with a friendly member of staff. My room was on the third floor and was clean and comfortable with no visible problems which was good. The bed was perhaps a little soft but that personal preference rather than a problem. I had a good nights sleep on both nights and there was very little noise which was good considering the hotel is on the corner of a busy junction. There is a bar and restaurant in the hotel. I didn't eat at night, however I did have breakfast one morning and it was pretty good. Nothing too fancy but fresh and a decent start to the day. There is a couple of nice pubs - one opposite and one behind the hotel which were quite nice. On the whole it was a really good stay and I was quite surprised. I'd definitely stay again although I noticed that all the points and cash deals that I booked with have disappeared for the remainder of the year which is a real shame.

author: Queenofsun
title: Nice budget hotel!
text: We were pleased with our stay in this hotel. The price was good, and it covered all our needs. The room was basic but clean. Beds were comfortable. Reception staff was helpful. Good speed Wifi was included. There is a restaurant and a bar in the hotel. We had continental breakfast included. It was ok, but not a lot to choose from. It’s possible to book English breakfast instead of continental. This is served in another part of the restaurant that is situated on the opposite side of the reception. There are small supermarkets and cafes/ restaurants in the same street as the hotel. Location was good. It took us about 10 minutes to walk to London Eye. The Lambeth north underground station is only a 2 minutes’ walk away from the hotel. There are also good bus connections from directly outside the hotel. The Imperial War Museum is a couple of hundred meters from the hotel – well worth a visit!

author: IDRick
title: Unexpected overnighter (Retrieving left luggage from Waterloo Station)
text: Quick check-in. Reception chap, not that helpful on arrival. But other staff were. Good location. £110.00 including breakfast was an ok price. Breakfast not that great, but adequate. Would have prefered to not have had it to be honest, but it was already paid for. Waitress hovered, uncomfortably. The ice machine was a welcome find - because the room was stuffy and extremely hot. We had a view of the top of the Shard and the high street below. Nice. Clean shower and bathroom, bed comfy. Easy checkout. And they allowed us to leave our luggage there, free of charge for the day. Would visit again.

author: Ignottus
title: Room was way to HOT HOT HOT!
text: I am usually a nice rater, but not this time. The hotel is well located, and clean, I will give them that. However, the facility is not equipped with central air conditioning and it is too hot. I mean it; too hot. It's August in London, and still we have a nice 18 degrees C, outdoors. Inside our room however, its like the desert of the Sahara. Can not sleep due to the extreme hot. My wife and I turned off all lights lo lower the heat source a bit, and worked on our cellphones lights. It is that hot. They know it because they give you a portable fan as part of the room furniture. Yes... a small portable fan for you to cool down the place a little. Windows cannot be fully opened due to safety/security reasons, they said. Mattress was rubbish and the lamps within the bathroom are falling apart. Not acceptable for a hotel of this category.

author: kersuz
title: Days Inn, Waterloo, London
text: Visited this hotel from 1st-4th August, 4 of us split between a double room & 2 single rooms for 3 nights. This hotel is excellent, first time we have stayed on this side of the Thames but it was so convenient to everywhere. The closest tube station is Lambeth North which is literally less than 5 minute walk to the hotel. The hotel itself although on Kennington Road is on the corner of Lameth Road & is less than 10 minutes walk to Lambeth Palace. The rooms were so clean and comfortable. Beds have 2 pillows each which were big fluffy pillows, small wardrobe to hand clothes plus 1 drawer, 2nd drawer stored spare pillows and towels. TV in room & only drawback was no air conditioning and it was so hot that the window had to be kept open which meant lots of noise for my particular room as a police station was across the road & sirens were going a lot however the other room we had which was only 3 doors away was completely quiet as looked out onto a different road, we were on 5th floor. The lift seems to be quite old & was slow but we got used to this. The bathroom was lovely, dove shower gel/shampoo dispenser is attached inside the shower & lux liquid soap dispenser attached beside sink, towels provided and changed daily & bins emptied daily also. We paid extra for 2 out of the 3 mornings for the continental breakfast & it was worthwhile & there was plenty to eat, toast, croissants, danish pastries, yoghurts, range of fruit, grapefruit segments, fruit cocktail, choice of 4 breakfast cereals, orange & apple juice, tea & coffee. We did arrive at 11 am so tried to check in early, the girl at the desk was not overly pleasant, just said check in is 2pm but we were able to leave our luggage in the room supplied, go away and come back again to get the rooms. This was all fine but member of staff could have been more pleasant, same girl was there most of our stay & I would recommend a customer service course for her, this did not impact on our break or our attitude to the hotel as it can happen, rest of the staff were so pleasant & cheerful. On our departure we left our bags again in the luggage room at 11am check out time & collected again at 3pm. We were able to walk from the London Eye, across Westminster Bridge along South Bank down to Lambeth Bridge & up to the hotel all within 30 minutes going at a leisurely pace. We have stayed in Travel Lodges & Comfort Inns before in London & would definitely try to book this hotel again as first choice, I feel you get more than the price paid. The only other recommendation I would make to Days Inn in general is to include an option for a breakfast per person within the price when booked, even it is means adding a few £s more on as it would be very convenient, I made the mistake of thinking the breakfast was included but realised a few days before my break. The lounge in the hotel is beautiful with large leather couches & chairs, breakfast room for continental breakfast is off the lounge & is not overly big but large enough in my opinion & separate breakfast room used for cooked breakfast. All in all a fantastic stay.

author: Evy_Adams
title: clean, decent hotel
text: The lady at the check-in on Tuesday looked like she wanted to be somewhere else.. We couldn't really understand her either. The room was great! Clean, cosy, modern, everything we could ask for. Breakfast was very good too. On Thursday there was a tube strike. We were informed in the underground to be prepared for this inconvenience. I looked up some information on the internet and it said you could buy one day bus tickets at 4,000 shops in London. When asking the staff at the front desk if they knew any shops were we could get these tickets, none of them knew... I looked up on the internet again and there was a shop just around the corner. Instead, they wanted to send us to Waterloo station (a 15 min walk from the hotel, with our luggage) to buy tickets there. We thought it was a pity they didn't prepare for these questions as it was so easy to find this information. For us it wasn't a problem, but there were several other guests who didn't know. There was a police station across the street and sirens would pass several times a night. We knew London was a bubbly city, but we thought it would settle down at night. On Thursday morning a fire alarm went off at around 8am, we hurried out of our room to check what was wrong, but it seemed like only we were a bit worried. As no one (visitors nor staff) was seen in the hall way, we presumed everything was OK.

author: frankl933
title: Thank You For The Day's
text: We stayed here for three nights late July and early August. We arrived early and our rooms were not ready as check in is at 2pm. We were allowed to leave our luggage free of charge and also were informed that on check out we could also store luggage FOC for a whole day. When we did finally get to check in the receptionist was a little bit dreamy and not very responsive to questions. We had to fill in a compulsory data card with our passport numbers and additional silly nonsense. After arriving at our room we were pleasantly surprised to find two complimentary bottles of water and some biscuits. All rooms have Coffee and Tea making facilities. The bedroom had plenty of space except for hanging clothes. The area for this purpose was a little claustrophobic alley built into one corner and extremely difficult to use. The bed was very comfortable but the room lighting poor. The on suite bathroom/shower area was well presented and equipped with all necessary amenities. A hairdryer is supplied and a long wall mirror encourages a fast turnaround when getting ready for a night on the Town. This Hotel is within walking distance to the West End, South Bank and Lambeth North tube station is a very short walk up the road. The interior of the Hotel is a little bit shabby but fresh towels are supplied and your room is cleaned every day with fresh biscuits added for your coffee break. The bar is close to the reception desk and does very little for atmosphere and never had many people partaking of the beverages. Overall the staff are very helpful and obliging with requests for directions and general London queries. Price wise the Hotel is good for it's location and easy accessibility and this would encourage me to stay again. Improvements would be in the bar area and corridors and lounge seating.

author: LittleRachD
title: Our second stay here. Excellent location.
text: This is our second stay here for theatre trips to the capital. We find this hotel very good value for money. Conveniently situated for the Southbank Centre, London Eye, NT, Waterloo, The Globe Theatre and the Imperial War Museum. We stayed two nights on our trip this time. Staff always welcoming. Hotel in general and the rooms are always clean. I've stayed in other 4 and 5 star hotels that don't come even close to this little gem. One personal favourite thing of mine about the rooms is the proper sized mugs you have for tea and coffee. Thank you. But could do with real tea and not the cheap Tetley rubbish you get! Oh well. The noise from outside is nothing you wouldn't expect from a capital city. It's fine. No air con in our room but we had a cooling fan which was absolutely adequate. Shower in our enquire was nice and big with plenty of hot water. Top tip let the shower run for a minute or two to get the hot water coming through! Enjoy folks.

author: sandra020
title: Budget hotel, good location 1st impressions not good.
text: Stayed two nights first impressions were not great - outside the hotel there are wooden tables and chairs which have seen better days, they just need painting as they look really scruffy. Reception staff were efficient but not welcoming. On the way to the room (we were on the ground floor, may be different upstairs) I noticed there was no security door where guests swipe to gain access to the corridors where bedrooms are located like a lot of other hotels have. This means anyone can walk in from the street passed reception and then wander around the corridors.As I was with my partner I wasn't too concerned but as a single female traveller I wouldn't like this arrangement. We then walked past two very dirty cream coloured armchairs in the corridor. By this time I was thinking we had made a mistake booking this hotel. Luckily the room was although small, clean and the bed and pillows were very comfortable. Bathroom was clean but as it was small and the shower door was large and swung across the loo, guests who are on the larger size may find it tricky accessing the shower. If the hinge to the shower had been put on the other side of the door there would be no problem, bit of poor planning and design. The bedroom on arrival was very hot and as there is no air conditioning and we were on ground floor we had the fan on all night but the next morning we opened the window for some fresh air and the room was more comfortable. On reflection the room was sufficient for the time we spent in it which was not much. It worked out £80 per night without breakfast which by London prices is reasonable. The location was good, 5 - 10 mins walk to London Eye, Big Ben, Underground station very near by. Local supermarket, nice little bakers/cafe very close where you could have breakfast. Probably wouldn't stay here again as would opt to spend a bit more and stay elsewhere but as they say you get what you pay for. If the hotel painted the outside wooden furniture, front staff learnt how to smile and the hotel removed the two dirty chairs from the ground floor corridor, first impressions would be greatly improved.

author: str8trippin2019
title: Just ok, not great
text: The location is good, within walking distance of the Houses of Parliament and a couple of tube stations. The Imperial War Museum is across the street if you want to check that out. It's also next to a police station, so we heard sirens quite often. However there were some negatives such as one morning it looked like the housekeeping tried to clean the room as fast as they could. The duvet was just thrown back over the bed and not even straightened and the towels were just thrown onto the rack. Have never come across that before at a hotel. The elevators are extremely old which means they are tiny and wobbly and they take forever to move and then to open the doors. Was quite annoying. We ate in the restaurant the first night we got there, and we were standing waiting to be seated when the man working there barked at us to sit down. It was extremely rude. We then proceeded to sit there for 15 minutes without any acknowledgment, no menus, and no water before someone finally noticed us (the restaurant was completely empty besides us and one other table). If we hadn't been travelling all day and were exhausted and starving we would have gotten up and gone to find something else. On top of that, the food was not good. My husband's fish and chips came with the fish skin still on it inside of the breading. I've eaten a lot of fish and chips and have never seen that. It's disgusting. The room was very tiny. You could tell the bathroom had been renovated but the room part was not. Overall it was just ok, a place to rest for a couple nights.

author: GeorgeP333
title: Best Budget Hotel
text: If good value is what you are after in London, this is the place to go. My wife and mestayed here recently as part of a Christmas gift to see the excellent musical, Thriller. The location is superb. It is about 2 minutes walk from Lambeth North tube stop on the Bakerloo, that will connect you directly to Waterloo, Westminster and shopping/theatre districts. Waterloo main station can be reached on foot within about 10 minutes if preferred. The surrounding area is pleasant and not overly congested. The hotel itself is reasonably modern and basic. The room was spotlessly clean and warm, but very small. Those after a bit of space may wish to avoid, but will suit fine if just wanting a place for a comfortable night's sleep. The bed was nice and spacious. A full english breakfast buffet was included in our package and was very fresh and tasty. I would recommend adding this onto you package if not included. We are due to return to London at the end of this year. After a thorough search of somewhere to book, this proved to be by far the cheapest option for a hotel as central as possible. We will therefore be going back and are looking forward to it. Whilst having no major 'wow' factors to give it 5 stars, this place is perfect for somewhere to stay is travelling to London for a short break.

author: trurogirl
title: Five Stars for value and service
text: We checked in early which was no problem at all and left our bags with them to collect later on the day of departure. The welcome and the service from the staff was excellent and they greeted you every time you walked passed the reception desk which was nice. The continental breakfast was perfect especially taking the cost into consideration. The breakfast manager was most helpful and polite. The room was comfortable and very clean with a modern new shower room, tea and coffee making facilities with a biscuit. The lighting is poor but this is often the case in hotel rooms for some reason. The location is great, convenient for most things. You can easily walk to the tube at Lambeth North which is on the Bakerloo line and goes direct to Paddington. There are many buses passing the hotel. You can walk to the Tate Britain in about 30 minutes, the same for Tate Modern. The walk to Selfridges on Oxford Street passing by the Houses of Parliament took 50 minutes but it was a pleasant walk. The hotel is opposite the Imperial War Museum which has free entry and is well worth a visit. There is an amazing app available called 'citymapper' which is so helpful. If you want to get to a particular place you type it in and it tells you what bus to get, the cost, the number of stops, where to get off and best of all, when it is due - 2 mins, 10mins and 12 minutes for example. It was so helpful. The hotel also has free wi-fi in all areas and a bar which serves evening meal for about £10. This is the second time I have stayed there and will definitely go back there. I was there for four nights.

author: LittleRachD
title: Excellent Hotel
text: My husband and I stayed here this weekend just gone. It is not in our ideal location but nevertheless it is a great place and close to the tube and bus routes. It also very easy and close to walk to Waterloo and the Souhtbank / London Eye. The hotel staff we very polite. We were twenty minutes early for checking in and they found us a like for like room immediately. Bravo. The room was an excellent size, well equipped and very clean. No air con but a table fan was in the room and served us well. Breakfast was available at additional cost but we were handed money off vouchers on checking in. So we used them the following morning. Breakfast was lovely. The usual choice of continental or cooked. A great bound of being served in two separate dining rooms. Not every one likes the smell of an english cooked breakfast first thing. A great wee bonus. On checking out we were able to leave our luggage whilst we went off and did some more sight seeing, exploring and shopping. The staff at all times were very pleasant and the hotel comes highly recommended. Would use again. Thank you.

author: hsinghjhaj
title: good central location
text: stayed here for two nights booking with superbreaks . very good location within five minute walk to Westminster bridge and all the attractions . rooms well furnished clean and modern fittings , comfortable bed and lots of good pillows . shower room very clean and on the wall soap and shampoo dispensers . double , double glazig so very little noise from outside . staff all very helpful ad cheery . small dining area for evening meal with varied menu and reasonable prices esp as we were given a two pound off token each for main course . despite being bank holiday and well booked the restaurant in the evening was not overcrowded and the food was well cooked . my compliments to the chef . drinks reasonable London prices . breakfast in two areas ...one for full English and the other for continental breakfast . can get busy but easy if you take a seat in lounge area and they will call you . the servers at breakfast and evening restaurant were all very efficient . car park small with ten places and extra to or disabled . 20 pounds for 2.00 pm till 2.00 pm the following day . we did not use this but there were always spaces available . we were told harder to find spaces at weekdays but easier at weekends . would I stay here again when visiting London ? ....... yes !

author: Carol-and-Pete
title: Value for money
text: A really good reasonably priced base for a short break in London. Take comfy shoes and all the sights are within walking distance. If you prefer tube travel, the hotel is only a very short walk to Lambeth North for Bakerloo line, £18 for 2 day travel tickets. The room (407) was very clean, refurbished shower room, comfy double bed, bedside tables, small dressing table/desk, small hanging area, couple small drawers. Windows opened, glad they did as quite warm. Fan provided but no air con in room. Not a problem in April. Tea/coffee replenished daily. Room serviced daily. Lux soap provided in shower and sink, fixed to wall. Quiet room, reading light fixed in desk area, bedside lights and full length mirror with hair dryer fixed nearby. Reception area very comfy, plenty of seating, good bucket chairs and 2 seater sofas, good areas for groups with coffee tables and bar. Alcohol was reasonable price, not a 'rip off'. TV in reception. Staff very helpful and friendly. Free luggage area locked and secure to leave cases if you need to travel home late ( checkout 11am) We had B&B rate, for what we paid the breakfast was very good. Grapefruit and mixed apple fruit salad, cereal, yoghurt, toast, pieces of fresh fruit, croissants, rolls, full cooked breakfast included bacon, sausage, hash browns, fried or scrambled eggs, beans, grilled tomatoes, mushrooms. It was a good choice for all tastes and replenished throughout the service time ( until 11am). Free taxi phone at reception with direct dial to Waterloo cabs, the firm were excellent with professional drivers who engaged well and were a pleasure to travel with. All in all we had a very good deal here and would use again.

author: noeld733
title: good hotel but sharper staff diversity training needed: homophobic attitudes obvious
text: Stayed here on Tuesday 4th March with my partner on a business trip as we were attending an event that evening at London Film Museum. The hotel facilities for the price in central London are good. If you like mattresses as soft as a water bed then you'll love it - we didn't but that would be the only complaint about the facilities. Don't bother paying good money for the cooked breakfast though - it's awful: over cooked, cheap ingredients and tepid, I stayed in a Premier Inn the following night and paid cheaper for a far superior breakfast. My real issue is with the homophobic staff and the evident lack of training for staff coming from very different parts of the world. I don't mind if people have homophobic attitudes, particularly if coming from countries less open, tolerant and liberal than the UK. However Days Inn - their attitude has no place behind the reception desk and it's your responsibility to make sure they know that. In a cosmopolitan metropolitan western city like London then the predominant cultural attitude is one of respect for people of all backgrounds. The room was booked through Otel. It was for for myself and my partner and for a female friend who was booked into a solo use double room. Somewhere down the line someone had decided that two men couldn't possibly share a room and changed the booking so my partner and female friend were booked into a room together. When it came to checking in the reception staff also looked perplexed and disapproving that the bookings had to be changed to accommodate two men. For this to happen once would be bad enough but it happened twice, with two different members of staff, My partner and I had to check in separately and we both experienced the mix up (my partner was actually sent to the wrong room) mixed in with a homophobic disdain. We were both made to feel as have the mix up was our fault and both asked if we were sure that the two of us were going to share one room. When this was confirmed we were both again met with looks and sucked teeth that left us in no doubt what those members of staff thought about the arrangement. I don't need the aggro to challenge outdated homophobic attitudes in a place I don't expect it. That's your job Days Inn - sort it because it will rightly loose you money. By the way, if you link to your review page had actually worked then this review would have gone there but it didn't so it's going here instead.

author: FrugalF444
title: It does what it says on the tin
text: So here I am, another night in London, another hunt for a decent priced hotel. I haven't stayed in a Days for a million years, so long I barely remember.......... So given the chance to stay for £66 including breakfast with my supper this night also on the Bakerloo Line........... so it seemed all the stars aligned. As it turned out my supper was cancelled at the last minute so I arrived much earlier than I had expected. The check in was busy but not annoyingly slow. I loved the idea of free rosy red apples on the reception. I had an odd shaped room, a bit like a short corridor, with two singles at one end and a bathroom at the other- but I like it, it was like sleeping in a VW Camper. I liked the room, the bathroom, the sharpness of it all. Yes the shower was a bit cramped, there were no fancy toiletries (not that I was expecting it) the shower cap was a nice touch and the Dove shower gel welcome. I decided to opt for snack supper - which the staff kindly popped on a tray for me so I could return to my room. The bed was comfortable, the pillows not a friend. I like to sleep with two - one wasn't enough and two - too much. I slept well the room quiet, both inside and out. The Days Inn at Waterloo isn't at Waterloo but a Lambeth North. Don't forget that Embankment tube is closed until November 2014 so this may make your trip tricky. However it is very easy to find from the tube (as long as you head across the road when you arrive towards the road with the shops in) its not much more than two minutes walk. Downsides - well none really. I liked the restaurant menu, the option of a snack menu to take back to your room, coffee and tea facilities and free biscuits, range of tv channels and the free apples. I didn't take the breakfast in the end - wasn't feeling hungry so went for a coffee, a biscuit and an apple 'to go'

author: Seasonedtraveller028
title: Great Value
text: Stayed in Days Inn for three days and not a problem. Arrived two hours prior to check in time but was facilitated immediately. Front of house staff friendly, efficient and capable. Room perfectly clean, comfortable bed (very), room nice and warm, bathroom spotless and recently tiled etc, hairdryer, tea &coffee makers and even a fan available for the long hot summer nights. Flat screen TV with good choice of channels. Absolutely no noise on any night. Had the full English breakfast on one morning and was very good although the toasting machine is very slow and got me a bit of a dressing down because I mistakenly skipped the queue. Didn't use the restaurant but had a nice lunch across the road in the Three Stags .. nearby Indian is so-so only. Courtesy newspapers available and free Wi-Fi. Location is really good ... nearest tube station Lambeth North a few minutes away ... London Eye and Southbank about a ten minute walk away and if you walk across the Jubilee Bridge from the Eye you are practically in Trafalgar Square. Imperial War Museum is just around the corner. Chose the Days Inn because of the price which is very good for a centrally located hotel and will definitely use the hotel the next time I visit London. Final point the Hotel is in a very safe location.

author: dcln
title: Brilliant Stay!
text: We have just returned from a night away in London and was surprised by how good our stay was. From the reviews i was a bit worried, but when we checked in the staff were polite and pleasent, they gave all guests a FREE apple!! and in the rooms more FREE water!! the rooms were modern and clean. The bathroom was super clean and again up to date. Breakfast was really nice, they had lots to choose from i guess the only downside which has been previously mentioned is the room size, for a hotel that big, the breakfast room had about 10 tables! and then a separate bar area with about 15 tables! So it's hit or miss whether or not you get a table. However the food was lovely, they kept restocking things, so it was fresh. The one thing that let our stay down was the bed. It was soooo bouncy and soft. i didn't feel supported at all, and we both kept rolling into the middle! But other than than. it was a great stay and i would recommend this to everyone!! We have finally found a great and cheap hotel in LONDON!!

author: GTEastMidlands
title: Great room, poor breakfast
text: Stayed here with 2 work colleagues in early September. The check in process was painless enough, and I was given a room on the first floor. The room was a little small if I'm honest, but clean and tidy. The bathrooms - we were told - are being refurbished in a number of rooms, mine included. Well, it looked brand new. Probably was. My room had quadruple glazing - double glazed windows and secondary double glazing. I slept pretty well, a few sirens but not too bad. Normal road noise is totally eliminated. Bar prices weren't too bad either. What I have to take exception to is the breakfast. We paid £7.95 each for a cooked breakfast, which should have been billed as an overcooked breakfast - the fried eggs looked like albino hockey pucks, the sausages rather hard. The bacon was okay. It just didn't look that appealing, I'm afraid. I would advise guests take a look first, then decide if you want to pay. Maybe I got the kitchen on a bad day. For the money though, good value, and friendly staff.

author: Daleweaver
title: A very honest review, 2 day stay
text: To start the hotel is in a great location and the price we paid for 2 night stay is very good for the location it is in. 5 minute walk from a tube. On arrival we was not greeted just looked at by the reception staff, we was early for check in so we was very great full for the luggage room that they provide. I thought to myself it was very weird welcoming from reception staff. I felt intimidated, but I was not going to let them spoil my holiday. The room was nice bathroom was very pleasing for myself, like other reviews the room was hot but I was happy that a fan was left, I was in London for sight seeing not sitting in room. Bed very comfy and plenty of pillows and towels unlike other hotels. Slept well. In the morning my partner opened the curtain and it fell down, these things happen ! As we was leaving I waited by the reception and was greeted by a "yes?" I double looked to see the the member of staff was talking to me and I said "good morning" at this point I was stunned and totally forgot what I was doing at reception ! How rude to be greeted on your holiday by YES ? The curtain was temporarily fixed until the maintenance team was in the next day. Breakfast was nice and plenty to choose from, again the staff need some customer service training in this area too. Overall a good hotel to stay at, just get rid of the staff or spend a little time training how to work with people. I will be returning to this hotel on my next trip to London I just hope the customer service will have improved by then.

author: lilianm659
title: Good hotel!
text: I've stayed at this hotel about 5 or 6 times over the years.. It's a good hotel... if you're looking for somewhere central and basic but comfortable.. then it's the place to go. The only problem for me on my recent stay was the lack of air con. It was a boiling hot week in August and it was way too hot, even with the fan on. This hasn't been a problem before, but it was very, very hot that week. Also, if you're a light sleeper, insist that you get a room high up at the back because it can get quiet noisy.. my room was on ground floor at the front... I did ask for a room at the back when I booked, but when I arrived, they assured me it was double glazed and I'd have no problems, but it was still quite noisy, so had to buy earplugs which did help. If you ask for a room at the back, high up you'll have no problems and a good nights sleep. So yeah, besides that, I love this hotel, and will definitely return. It's in a perfect location, staff are friendly, breakfast is great (the woman who works in the breakfast room of a morning is lovely..), very reasonably priced...! I've been going here for about 6 years now, and probably wouldn't go anywhere else. I love London!

author: klpopp
title: You get what you pay for. Pay more.
text: Supposedly, very seldom does it get hot in London. By the standard of where we live, 80 degrees is not hot, but it is in your room at this poorly designed and appointed Days Hotel. The morning sun greeted us at 5:AM. Because the windows are not Low-E the heat quickly builds. The curtains are not blackout and they effectively transmit the heat to the rest of the room. You are basically forced out of your room by 8:A.M. or so. An oscillating fan is supplied, and if you place it in front of the window you can move some cooler air into the room, the fact that the window only opens about 3" retards the process. There is no air conditioning in the hallways or rooms. The rooms are very small. No closet, except for about a foot wide hanger area and there were two drawers. There was space for a single suitcase. The bathroom was small, but efficient. The management of this hotel is so cost concious that the styrofoam cups at the only ice machine are left out of the dispenser. You need to request the cup. The common areas of the hotel are air conditioned, but even if the A/C is needed, it is likely not to be used. The elevators are creaky, slow and scary. On top of that they are likely to be very warm (see previous paragraph). My bottom line advice is to not choose this "hotel."

author: towelobsessive
title: Disappointing
text: A first visit to this hotel. I was looking for somewhere close to Waterloo where my husband and I could stay with our teenage son sharing the room. We knew this was a budget hotel, but reviews seemed quite good s thought we would give it a try. First impressions getting out a Lambeth North tube station weren't great as the area looked pretty run down. Walking into reception the Hotel looked a bit tired and in need of refurbishment. Reception staff were very friendly and check in efficient. Entering the lift to go up to our room I thought how grubby the carpet looked. I asked for a quiet room away from the lifts and again this looked tired. Three single beds had been made up and fitted into the bed space. We had to shuffle these around a bit so that 2 of us wouldn't bang our heads on the fitted bedside lamps! Then shower was quite powerful, but tiles and grout, stained and mouldy. Breakfast wasn't included, but we were offered a discount voucher of £2 off if we decided to eat breakfast there. I'm afraid none of us slept well. My bed was hard and uncomfortable and the pillow was like a brick. To round all this off, having asked for a quiet room, we were put at the front of the hotel, but unbeknown to us the Hotel is located opposite Kennington Road Police Station and police sirens were going all night. It was impossible to sleep and too late t do anything about it. I appreciate this is a budget hotel but I am sorry Days Inn your staff are friendly but I won't be staying again.

author: rtpresident
title: Don't judge by the name of your hotel
text: We visited london on April 23 and stayed for 1 night. I was totally surprised how nice it was. Normally in this kind if cheaper hotel you never know what to expect but we figured it was only for 1 night anyway. Normally they make you check in at 3pm. They checked us in at 11am. I had made reservations for 2 single beds because that was the cheapest. When we got into our room it was beautiful, it was so clean, spotless. We would definetly stay there again and we recommend it at the highest. They also had a restaurant at this hotel and it was very reasonable. Breakfast was 7.95 pounds an which they gave us a coupon of 2.00 pounds off the price and they also had dinner there for 9.95 pounds in which they gave us another 2.00 coupon to apply to that price. We did not eat there, we were on our way to see as much as we could. Everything was in walking distance. It was beautiful. By the way I thought I was arriving in the Waterloo train station which was right across the street from days Hotel. Found out that the Waterloo train station was closed for some reason??? Picked up a taxi from the euro train station in which I taxi was about 20 minutes away, price was 14.00 pounds. Have fun, Take your rain ponchos or unbrellas just in case. We didnt have to use them.

author: PinkieLinz
title: Short stay, good base in ideal location
text: We have just today come back from a two night stay at the days inn. We went for a cheap short break for a few days for my birthday to see a show and do abit of sightseeing. Which may I add if you're looking to see a show while you're in London "Bodyguard" is absolutely amazing and well worth a watch!!! We only wanted somewhere cheap, clean & in a good location to use as a base and that's exactly what we got. The hotel is ideally located two minutes walk away from Lambeth North tube station based on the (brown) bakerloo line which interconnects with all other tube lines. The London eye & embankment attractions are only a short ten minutes walk away from the hotel too. The rooms are quite small and very basic I'd say the standard is somewhere inbetween a premiere inn and travel lodge. Very basic facilities. Very good powerful shower but disappointingly no bath, & after walking the streets of London a nice hot long soak in the bath would have been awesome. But never the less. Not a great deal of hanging space in the wardrobes and if there's two of you I'd definately advise taking a few of your own hangers. We found the staff to be very friendly & helpful. Especially in a morning at breakfast. Which might I add if you're staying here I'd definately opt for the breakfast as it's lovely. We had full English and there were also croissants, toast, bread rolls, fruit, cereals, cheese, cheese spread even chocolate spread. Our train got us into London slightly earlier than we expected so we arrived at the hotel a good hour before check in which wasn't a problem at all our room was ready for us immediately. :-) I'd say if you want the ritz don't stay here, but if like us you're not going to be spending much time there and you just want somewhere to use as a base this place is ideal!!

author: staceygibson83
title: Great location, but dissapointing room
text: I stayed here one night. It's a great location but at a cost of £99 a night is very high for what you get. The room was very very small. I usually don't mind this but it was so small it was awkward to get in and out of bathroom and around end of bed! The bed was squeaky and the mattress very broken in parts. The staff were just average. Not friendly in any way and continued their conversations before helping you at front desk. The shower pressure was terrible and not hot enough. No toiletries just that annoying combined shower/shampoo in pump. The noise in hall was very loud, doors banging and the noise from outside was awful. It was a Saturday night I stayed but you could here too many people drunk outside late in the night. London prices are always high but I don't think this hotel warrants £99 a night. I'm sure you could find somewhere better for that price. I wished I'd payed £30 extra it was to stay on premier inn Waterloo around corner. I won't stay again.

author: 413DavidL
title: Hotel well located but noisy
text: Days Hotel Waterloo is very well located. Not really at the center of London but closed to the underground station "Lambeth North" and that's a very good point. The hotel itself is not too bad. I would say it could be comfortable but actually too much noisy. Insulation of room window is probably not enough efficient. We reserved a family room for 4 people. One of the bed was very flexible... too much for me. Our friends reserved also a family room but got 2 standard rooms not communicating instead of when we arrived. The hotel team found a solution the day after when a family room became available. ---- L'hotel Days Hotel Waterloo est très bien situé. Pas vraiment au centre de Londre mais très proche de la station de métro "Lambeth North". C'est vraiment un très bon point. L'hotel lui même n'est pas mal, il pourrait être considéré comme confortable si il était pas aussi bruyant. En fait l'isolation des fenetre de la chambre n'est sans doute pas assez efficace. Nous avions réservé une chambre familiale pour 4 personnes. Un des lits était vraiment mou. Nos amis avaient aussi réservé une family room mais ils ont eu, à la place, 2 chambres non communicantes. Le personnel de l'hôtel a trouvé une family room dès le lendemain.

author: 847ChrisT
title: Decent Digs
text: Stayed here whilst down on quick buisness Trip. Walking distance from Waterloo Station. Around 15-20 mins. No dark lanes , all well lit up main streets. Reception was very friendly and quick to attend to. 3 min walk to Lambeth North Tube. Then London is yours to enjoy! The rooms were basic and tidy enough , sure the showers could do with a re-grout , but wasnt a problem. Beds and pillows were 9-10. Very comfy. Food was fine , although only had 1 meal in restaurant. They left a wee bag with fruit and bottle of water. That was a wee treat. Next to a few food/drink shops, so if you fancy a wee bottle of plonk in your room or nibbles , your sorted.Didnt spott many restraunts nearby , but was a quick trip as i said. Ironing room on 1st floor, 4 irons and small boards. Irons were actualy really good. But if you took a few items to iron , then had to hand then on the floor. Maybe Management can sort that out. Put hangers on the rack? All in all , for the location and price and comfort, this was a great wee hotel.

author: RoyE
title: Always a good stay.
text: Hotel is located about a 5-10min walk from Waterloo station and 5mins from Lambeth North (Bakerloo Line) underground station. Arrived early, before midday, but the Receptionist checked and found a room that was ready and let us book in, at no extra charge. We stayed in Rm 413, it had everything we required for a night stay, warm room, comfortable bed, tea & coffee making facilities. The view overlooked the Imperial War Museum and The Shard in the distance, also overlooked a road junction but the double glazing absorbed most of that noise so it was negligible overnight. After dropping off our luggage we left for our day in London. Returned late and had a comfortable sleep. Easy to operate the wall heater to the required temperature. Shower pressure was good with easy controls. We hadn't previously booked breakfast but decided to have some and purchased tickets. Since our last visit the dining arrangements had changed, it had been split into two areas, continental and full English. Trouble was the cooked breakfast area did not seat many, and when busy filled quickly, so we had to sit in the other area. This meant we had to cross the reception area with trays of food, not the best situation. Also the kitchen was next to the continental breakfast area so full trays of cooked food had to cross the reception area as well, not what I thought was best practice. Hopefully the hotel is trying different scenarios before deciding the best option. The cooked breakfast was plentiful and a good choice, it set us up for the day. After we booked out, the hotel stored our luggage till our train later in the day, again free of charge. All the staff were polite, helpful and cheerful. Would definitely recommend and stay at this hotel again. Other similar hotels could learn a thing or two from this one. Couple of pubs nearby, also restaurant, coffee shop and convenience store.

author: refinnej89
title: Good base in London
text: Stayed for 2 nights. Short walk from Lambeth North tube station, easy to find and the area is nice. I felt safe here. I was very pleased on arrival. Easy check in, room was ready early so went up straight away. I have noticed some reviews ststing that the staff are rude, not very helpful etc. I have to disagree. Rooms are small but there was plenty of space for us. Shower worked well and the bathroom was fine. Extra pillows and towels in the room which is always good. Bed was ok, slept well both nights even thought the rooms are noisy. Breakfast was ok. Had cooked breakfast on the first morning but did'nt ejoy all of. The sausages are a bit odd! But everything else was fine. Second morning consisted of pastries and fruit, which were fine. The only thing I was not comfortable with was the size of the breakfast room, very small and when busy is too crowded. Good base for exploring London due to it's location. Would stay again.

author: jaynew767
title: Great location
text: Just back from a two night stay at this hotel. Check in was easy and quick,however, and I urge everyone to double check this, be careful when it comes to including breakfast with your booking. We always, and I mean always, book breakfast with every hotel stay. The receptionist however said we hadn't booked breakfast and so would be an extra charge of £9.95 per person per day (this was for full English breakfast, continental was cheaper). On checking our hotel booking confirmation sheet it shows "meal plan" - this does not mean you have booked breakfast. I feel like I've been ripped off slightly here so if you have the time to find somewhere else nearby to have breakfast then I suggest you do that. The westend is only a 10 minute bus ride away (no 59). The hotel breakfast was okay but for £9.95 per person I would have expected fresh mushrooms and not out of a tin. The "restaurant" is really really tiny. You are forever trying to get out of someone's way. Our room was on the first floor and yes it was noisy from the traffic outside but then you are in central London. Pack ear plugs. The room was tiny, very tiny. So was the bathroom. No air conditioning, instead you have an electric desk fan to use! Room and bathroom were clean but the bed was very uncomfortable and the door on the shower did not close properly. The hotel has five floors but only two very old lifts. Take the stairs, they are more reliable and quicker! The location of this hotel is the best thing about it. 15 mins to west end and 20/30 mins to the Oval cricket ground.

author: Raven9267
title: Good location, fine for a budget hotel but beware of traffic noise at night.
text: I stayed for 1 night for business. I picked the hotel because it was close to Westminster and it cost around the £100 mark. Check-in was efficient and friendly. My room on the 4th floor was clean, had what I expected to find and everything worked as it should. It had a shower (but not a bath), the water was hot and the pressure was reasonable. Reasonable selection of chanels on the TV (no Sky Sports though). There is WiFi downstairs and in the bedrooms for a small charge. In the lobby there are about half a dozen PCs with chargeable internet access. I had an evening meal in the small restaurant; service, food and prices were good. Between 6 and 8pm there's a 'happy hour' at the bar and a pint of beer will cost around £2.25 which for a London hotel is incredibly cheap. I had full English breakfast in the morning. Reasonable choice and quality. The only serious drawback with this hotel, as other reviewers have pointed out, is the traffic noise at night. The hotel is almost opposite a major police station and also on the junction of several busy roads. Load sirens are a regular occurence day and night - great if you're watching a police drama and you want to feel part of the programme but otherwise not good. The room I was in didn't have aircon (that may be the case for all the rooms) which means if you'll be staying on one of those rare hot days during the English summer, you'll have to decide whether a noisy /hot room is better than a breezy /extremely noisy room! To be honest, the windows seem inadequate for keeping the noise levels to a reasonable level so opening them might not be too much worse. Would I stay again, maybe but not if I've had a very long day or will be making an early start. I need my sleep!

author: rtsoule
title: Excellent location for attraction on a very noisy street
text: My wife and I and our son stayed here for 5 days in mid-December. As the other reviewers note, the location near the North Lambeth (Bakerloo Line) Tube Station and a fifteen minute walk from the London Eye and Waterloo train station. The staff tries very hard to meet any additional need you might have and the restaurant/bar in the lobby with Sky Sports on a big screen is very nice. I paid £20 for one week access, which would not have been bad if the speed were acceptable (it was not). If I had to do it all over again, I would have paid for just one day as a test and then not another day. The speed of the free WiFi at the Train Station bar/hostel right behind the hotel is MUCH better. There are several dining options available close to the hotel (including the £6.95 pizza at the Train Station), but having the option of eating at the hotel was also good although £9.95 for a full English breakfast is a bit pricey. If you are a light sleeper, this might not be a good area of town for you because there are sirens blaring on the street in front of the hotel several times a night. This is not the hotel's fault to be sure and perhaps you can ask for a room in the back, but we could not sleep with the window open (nice for a little ventilation even in December) because of the noise. An alternative to consider is the Tune Hotel that is right across the street from the Tube Station. The Tune Hotel is very non-frills according to its web site and the reviews on Trip Advisor are mostly positive. The Days Hotel was nice, but definitely pricier than the Tunes Hotel and I am not sure the extra price was worth it for my family (I am very frugal when traveling). I wish I had known about the Tunes Hotel when i was making my arrangements so I could at least consider it.. This is no reflection on the staff. They are very friendly and helpful and certainly contributed to the pleasure of our stay.

author: chooseygirl
title: A good budget hotel
text: Positives first - booked through Travel Republic on a really good deal for twin room with breakfast. Staff really friendly and helpful. Changed our double to twin without any bother. Clean and fairly comfortable room with tea and coffee making facilities. Breakfast was plenty and good. Hotel is on 59 bus route so easy to get to from St.Pancras/King's Cross/ Euston stations. Nearest underground is Lambeth North - short walk from hotel. South Bank, London Eye and Westminster easy walking distance. They have a good safe room for leaving cases before or after check-out. A few negatives - NO AIR CON!!! We were there during the late September HOT SPELL! There is a fan in the room but it was still very hot! No safe or much room for clothes storage so not ideal for a long stay. En-suite is very basic and practical looking and has shower but no bath but towels and soap/shampoo are provided. Hotel will give you other toiletries in request. Overall - for the one night stay we had it was adequate and we got what we paid for - a good clean budget hotel in a good location for sight -seeing.

author: civicwagon1990
title: A convenient value
text: As part of a longer stay in London, I stayed here three days on arrival. Most of the previous reviews were correct. The location is a block and a half from the tube, very convenient. An Oyster Pass can be purchased a half a block away at a minimarket. The purchased continental breakfast (sometimes it is included in the room rate) was adequate but high priced. The double bed room was very small; it would be hard to see how two people with luggage could survive. As a single, I occupied all of the space (I pack heavy). It is noisy since it is on main road with emergency services close by. Bring ear plugs. The good news is that the south bank of the Thames and Parliament are withing reasonable walking distance Some mention in earlier reviews of a smell in the bathroom. I traced it to the sink trap that needs to be cleaned out. I reported that on my departure. Otherwise, the cleaning staff is quite effective but there is some staining in some remote corners of the shower. The staff is very knowledgeable, helpful and cooperative; they are the strength of the facility. It is more than adequate place for a value stay in London.

author: pope_jakob
title: Rude staff...
text: I stayed at this hotel with a girlfriend and it was a bit of a disappointment. The room was in poor condition (curtains almost fell down, had holes in them, the drain in the bathroom zink did not work etc.). It was clean though. The worst part of our stay was the very rude staff. From the second we arrived we felt like a burden and as if we were not welcome at all. We tried smiling at the receptionists every time we walked by, but got ignored. Every single time. When we politely asked for an extra duvet (since we were not a couple but friends) they reluctantly agreed to give us one. Same thing with the toilet paper and towels. The only time we saw any of the staff smiling was whes she was counting the cash in the register. When we checked out, the receptionist took our keycards and said: "Everything is fine" (since we had paid in advance), and that was it. No "Goodbye", or "Hope you enjoyed your stay". Nothing. He just answered the phone and left us standing there. The area was kind of rough but it only takes about 5 minutes by bus to Westminster Bridge, so it was OK.

author: Trentholme
title: Don't chose this Hotel
text: I had stayed at a Days Inn Hotel in London before and was impressed, so I booked the one at Waterloo for one night, thinking we would get the same kind of Hotel. Far from it. Apparently this is a franchise and the standard of each Days Inn Hotel depends on the Owner/Manager. The Hotel was dingy and on arrival the lift did not work. We were given a room on the ground floor. Not a problem, except the room was for someone Disabled. The Sink in the Bathroom was tiny, at thigh level and had no plug. Only good for washing hands after using the loo. The Twin beds had a reading light each, but unfortunately this was so low and situated towards the middle of the headboard that sitting up in bed was impossible. No air conditioning meant that we had to sleep with the windows open, which let in the noise of people having a drink outside our windows in the garden and also the heavy all night traffic. From early morning the low flying planes on their way to and from the airport could also be heard. Sleep was virtually impossible. Continental Breakfast consisted of either a stale roll or croissant with butter, jam, Philadelphia Cheese or a small piece of Pre-packed soapy cheese. No cold cuts. 2 types of Cereal and tinned grapefruit could also be had, as well as the cheapest Joghurt on the market. Most of the staff did not speak English very well and had difficulty understanding a simple question. All in all, a very disappointing stay.

author: LBurnie
title: Take ear plugs!
text: At the beginning of this review it's only fair to state that the main reason we won't be back is probably beyond the hotel's control. There is no a/c in the rooms and they are small and stuffy so you will have to open the small window (and our's had a failed double glazing unit). The road noise was really invasive. We were to the front on the fifth floor and the road noise included lots of sirens throughout the night so we had restless sleep on both nights we were there. The check in process was quick friendly and efficient, bar area looked fine as did the small restaurant area. Room was small,it felt worn out but very clean. Bed hopeless, mattress soft, worn and plastic protected like a hospital bed. Four pillows supplied were thin and cheap. Towels almost threadbare and not changed for our second day, despite being obviously still damp. Room very small but well designed. Shower hopeless,low pressure so you'll have to walk around it to get completely wet. Area around the hotel seemed quite safe and under five minutes walk to Lambeth North tube station, about ten minutes to Waterloo and you can be on Westminster bridge easily in fifteen minutes. Location is pretty good. We saw Tune Hotel nearby too, it looked worth a try and a even closer to all the aforementioned. So, we won't be back, at £99 per night, did not feel good overall value. Pay an extra £20 or so and get much much better elsewhere.

author: Crantock10
title: Very good overall, value for money
text: The Days Inn was perfect for our three day break on a budget. The main criteria when we searched for a hotel were that it was centrally located, of reasonable quality and most importantly wouldn't break the bank. Of course, It's not very easy to meet all these criteria, and at the end of the day you are gambling somewhat. Happily, the Days Inn proved a decent gamble afterall. We were guranteed the location we desired by checking beforehand on a map - 3min walk( 400yards) to Lambeth North for the tube network, and Waterloo International only a further 4mins. It's only a quarter of an hour to the London eye opposite Big Ben. The reception staff were friendly enough, and check-in was stress free and very fast. The room itself was small, but clean, tidy and modern. There was a decent flatscreen TV, hairdryer and tea/coffee facilities. The ensuite was again small but functional and the shower was good. The only complaints are that there was not enough space to hang clothes (5 hangers, and no room for more even if you brought/requested more!), the bed was a bit small and the curtains inadequate for blocking out the light from the busy street, which was also very noisy without double glazing - but then the centre of a major city is always gonna be fairly noisy I suppose. The continental breakfast came with the price of the room, and was pretty standard fare, but easily good enough for our needs. One other bonus was that the imperial War Museum was literally right outside the hotel, which is handy if you like that sort of thing. The price was very reasonable for London standards - it was £117 for two nights, all in. Overall, very satisfied. Would come again.

author: paulieceee
title: Comfort, Location and Value = Days Waterloo
text: Firstly lets look at the product offered; it's a budget hotel from a reputable budget hotel operator in Days so clearly the key deal breaker with people staying here is going to be price. Clearly a number of reviews here are less than complimentary though I venture that it is as a result of expecting too much for what you pay for. London is an expensive city to stay in and should you wish your hotel to be relatively luxurious then expect to spend in or around £150+ per night on a Hilton etc. The hotel itself; it is a basic 3 star hotel that is quite comfortable. I paid £60 for one midweek night and considering that breakfast was included I find it excellent value. The location is about 5 mins walk from Lambeth Tube Station on the Bakerloo line which will bring you into Oxford Circus [i.e. London City Centre] in approx 10mins. It is also across the road from London's best attraction in my opinion; The Imperial War Museum. The bar area and breakfast are is small though so it may be a problem if the hotel was at capacity. The rooms themselves are small but practical. Tea/Coffee making facilities are a bonus as is the high quality shower. Again functionality is key; if you're staying in your hotel room a lot then spend more on it. Breakfast was good, excellent selection for continental but it is worth the £2 upgrade for the Full English. Again the dining are is small so when the hotel as at capacity it may be advisable to head down early to breakfast. Staff do their job; heater wasn't working in my initial room and they had no problems moving me - they were at the standard I'd expect. The hotel is a touch noisy so it may be advisable to bring ear plugs if you are a light sleeper. Overall; go in with your eyes open into this one. Anything less than £90 per night is a super rate for what you get considering London is high on price and low on value in the hotel market. If you intend on spending large amounts of time in your hotel room and the hotel itself then spend the money on a 4 or 5 star hotel. If you're like most people here to either sightsee, on business or going to a match or concert and you only need a comfortable place to rest your head then look no further.

author: zzanne
title: Come on, a HOT SHOWER at least!??
text: Stayed here for a night - we have twins and the in-laws were babysitting so we could go to a gig/club and have a lie in. We booked it for the night of our evening out and the next night so we could have the room until we felt like leaving the next day. I live in London, so don't do this often, but I can't BELIEVE that you can't get more for your money. We paid over £200 for the honour of the most nondescript room in the world, a bit shabby - the curtains circa 1982. The bathroom was "clean" thought the shower could have used a good bleaching session. Speaking of which, the shower. Honestly, they have this device attached to it so you can't make it really hot. What???! I like my showers HOT. Especially after a loooong night out and feeling rough. So tight. Plus the hair dryer (thankfully I brought my own) has this stupid button you have to hold to keep it going instead of just staying on until you switch it off. Did they think we were going to heat the room with it or something? I was just trying it out and it shorted out after about 30 seconds. Glad I had mine... We did this last minute, so I reckon if we had done more research we could have found better in London.

author: CarannSheffield
title: Impressive for a budget hotel
text: I'd stayed the previous week at the St Ermins, which gave me an uncomfortable, wobbly single bed in a small room for £120 pn - the Days Hotel gave me a comfortable double bed in a nice sized room for £90 pn. The St Ermins tv only had 9 channels, 4 of which were foreign language; the Days Hotel tv was larger, had a better quality picture and had 36 channels, only 10 of which were foreign language. The Days Hotel had extra towels and pillows in a drawer without having to remember to ask for them. Not a huge amount of clothing hanging space, but perfect for a week's clothing. Both check-in and check-out were very quick and efficient. The room (actually everywhere) was very clean. Nice powerful shower, torrents of hot water. Security chain on the interior of the door, which is a good point for single female travellers. Breakfast was a good English breakfast (served, not a buffet) or a buffet selection of cereals, yoghourts and pastries. The restaurant section is fairly small, but as I was up early for meetings, I'd finished my breakfast before any queues built up. Yes, it's a little noisy as it's on a main road, but that might be alleviated by asking for a back room and I still got a better night's sleep than in the St Ermins wobbly single bed. The "Waterloo" name is slightly misleading, as the nearest tube station is actually Lambeth North, but it's still fairly central. Didn't get a wake-up call on my second day, but it wasn't a big problem as I'd got an alarm on my mobile 'phone. Biggest drawback - Nescafe coffee sachets provided in the rooms, Kenco's better if you have to have instant (okay, I'm a coffee snob, but at least they provided drinks in the hotel, which some budget hotels don't - and the breakfast coffee was very good). I thought it was very impressive for a budget hotel and would happily stay there again.

author: georgedoull
title: Decent Value Hotel
text: Stayed 4 nights in this hotel in early October on a family trip to London. Had it as part of a Superbreaks package holiday and got what seemed a very reasonable price, £560, which was for 2 adults and a teenager with full english breakfast AND included the return rail fares from the east of scotland. Taxi from Kings Cross to hotel only £13 (had been expecting £20). Reception staff very pleasant. Room reasonable, perhaps slight foosty smell. Beds fine. Shower a bit weak but ok for a few days. Downside as has been widely reported is noisy road. Location very good, 10 mins to London Eye/Thames/Westminster. Most attractions walkable though the nearby tube station will whisk you anywhere you want quicker. Imperial War museum across from hotel definately worth a visit. Breakfast in hotel very good, most people had full English which was cooked for you and brought to your table. All normal tea/juice/rolls etc also available. Breakfast area sometimes a bit busy. Had evening meal in hotel twice which on a slightly limited menu is still worth a look for good value eg mixed grill with chips/salad under a tenner. Had a couple of beers in bar, pleasant not too expensive. Couple of computers guests can get on interner for an hour for £2.50. hotel allows you to leave bags in safe room, so day we left were able to spend a few hours in area before returning for bags to return to train station.

author: stevehullEngland
title: Great location & service, friendly staff
text: We booked four rooms at Days Inn Waterloo through an internet hotel website which was cheaper than booking directly with the hotel. We arrived at the hotel at just gone noon, and although we knew we were earlier than the stated check in time, the staff were extremely efficient and friendly, and we all had access to our rooms within five minutes of arriving. The rooms are fairly small, but well equipped with plasma tv etc. The bathroom was clean with again a fairly small shower cubicle. But if you are in London for the weekend, you are only using your room to get your head down in the evening anyway!! The Lambeth North tube station is just five minutes walk from the hotel along a very nice street with shops and various restaurants, all in all a nice, safe feeling area. (Probably helped by the huge police station directly opposite the hotel). You are just four tube stops from Picaddilly Circus so a great location for seeing all of Londons sights. The 24 hour bar has a happy hour (£2.50 a pint for Stella) and they serve snacks right through until 4AM. After getting back from the West End we all had a pizza which is served with a beer for a very reasonable £7.95. There is also a restaurant serving all manner of evening meals. Continental breakfast was included in our hotel price, you can upgrade to full english by paying a £2 supplement. I opted to stick with the continental (still full of pizza) and had croissants, fresh bread rolls, toast, cereals, all great quality. Some of our party upgraded to full english, and unusually this was not buffet style self service, every one was cooked fresh, which I thought was very good. The only negative on this hotel is two of the roads it is situated on are fairly busy, so a little traffic noice can be heard. All in all, this hotel is superbly located for seeing the sights, has a great bar and food menu, the staff were all friendly and efficient, always smiling. I would not hesitate in recommending this hotel for the price, we paid £80 for a Saturday evening per double room. In fact we intend to book this hotel again for future visits, so that says it all I think. Enjoy your stay if you visit.

author: dreamingofstars
title: Good Location, thats it
text: Getting to the hotel is easy, its a short walk down from the Lambeth North station, and literally just across the road from the Imperial War Museum! We arrived quite early in the day, and the hotel got us into a good quickly and easily. Thats where the good news stops. Our room, like another reviews, was close to the Police Station. And also a kareoke bar, which was just behind the hotel. Trying to sleep was a nightmare! Our room was tidied, but never cleaned. The sheets weren't changed, originally had stains on them. Floor never hoovered, and the bathroom was never properly wiped down. The hairdryer also hiccuped constantly, on for five seconds, then off. Very annoying to use. The room comes with a tv, but the only channels you could reasonably watch were cartoon and music ones. As to the staff, the women that we dealt with were fine, helpful and kind. A couple times we came down for advice, and the gentleman who helped us seemed to care more about the computer he was sitting in front of than dealing with us. We didn't have breakfast, £6.95 seems a bit steep for continental! Stayed for three nights, and while we got a good price and a great location, would not return.

author: memphis4lmw
title: Listen out for the police sirens!!!
text: Stayed at this hotel for a 2 nights. Check in was ok but staff seemed bored and disinterested. Room had three single beds (travelling with two other family members, shared room to keep down cost), it was slighty depressing but beds were comfy and room seemed clean. But if you are wanting a goodnights sleep, beware!, our bedroom faced the front of the hotel, opposite was the Waterloo police station, and several times a night the sirens would blast out, waking us all up. Also, on our first night, my family member went to have a showe,r but could only spend 5 minutes in there, as the water didn't drain and her feet were swimming in water, nearly spilling over the shower tray. We then had to wait 20 minutes between showers for the water to drain. I did report this problem to the staff and it was dealt with the next day. Breakfast was ok but nothing special, the restaurant staff were very friendly. Get there early though as it get so busy you don't get a table. BEWARE: Do not use the hotel direct line to the taxi service. They are a rip off. Booked taxi which took us to Westminser abbey, charged £10. Got a black cab straight back from Westminster and they only charge £5.20. Made complaint to taxi company and said they would investigate. I have stayed in better hotesl in London, for the same price so I would be staying here again.

author: Canadiancouple15
title: Good location, not the brightest staff
text: We stayed here for 2 nights in August. We arrived very late due to our flight and checked-in at 2am. Room was small as is typical in many European hotels but clean and comfortable. It's in a pretty good location. only 10mins walk to big ben, 20mins walk to Buckingham palace and 30mins walk to the London bridge. There is a station for the underground located about a block away, but it's 4 Pounds a person at the exchange rate was about $8CAD each so we just walked instead. The room has no a/c but did have a small fan which worked well, but don't open your window as there is a huge amount of police activity in the area. Seems like a safe area, I think there must be a police headquarters near by because sirens are always zooming by every 15-20mins. On our last day I had to return to Canada early (6am) but my girlfriend was remaining in London to visit friends for another week. I told the front desk I was leaving but NOT checking out as my girlfriend would be there another few hours sleeping until her friend came to pick her up at which time she would check out. Our friend called the hotel asking for my girlfriend that morning but the staff told them there was no one there by that name or under my name for some reason.
