A bit confused our friend called several other hotels with similar names and naturally was told we weren't there either. She called back and the hotel insisted they had never heard of us. In the end our friend showed up at the address to the hotel we had given her and waited outside for 2hrs (she couldn't park anywhere in the area without getting ticketed) finally my girlfriend who had been waiting in the lobby to hear from her friend for 2 hrs discovered her waiting in the parking lot. They confronted the hotel staff about the issue and they said they were sorry but as they couldn't say who had answered the phone that was that and just shrugged the incident off. Aside from the poor customer care by the front desk, the hotel is a decent choice. Although it won't be my first choice now next time we visit.

author: JNeail
title: Just don't expect to sleep.....
text: If you'd like to gain that authentic prison living experience then please stop here! Three dull buildings with row up-on row of small windows give this hotel that typical prison look. Once inside, it gets no better. The in room live action entertainment taking place in the streets outside, included for me nightly appearances of the police helicopter hovering just out of eye sight, but must have directly outside above my 5th floor room, various sirens at all hours, continuous thunderous traffic noise, screaming and shouting locals late in to the night/early hours of the morning, all something to be marvelled. I thought you only got experiences this realistic at Disney..! Food... A none starter.... transport cafe style plastic moulded tables and seating, no atmosphere, a combined dining/bar/reception area just awful... Breakfast served from cheap plastic combo plates, juice and coffee from a push button machine all self-service and nothing on offer that didn't visibly look like it had just spend 10 mins either in the microwave or fryer beforehand or was served from a vast catering pack of some sort. The room was tiny, but did what it said on the tin I suppose; after all I wanted to SLEEP there! Struggled in the shower for a guy of normal proportions as it was so small, who knows how over-sized people would get on? Room was carpeted, but covering in stain patches, so keep you shoes on! Bathroom was OK, but all look very tired and in need of a desperate refit. Heating seems to be on full blast, I’d say at almost sauna levels causing you to need to keep the window open despite the continuous commotion outside, as there is no air-con. As this was a business trip, the ability to work from a desk was important, but unfortunately no real desk space provided, just a part of a pre-moulded unit with a rather un-comfy chair, no WiFi, no Ethernet, even my personal 3G let me down as I couldn't get a signal (although as much as I want to, can't blame the hotel for that). My best advice to anyone other than those looking as I said for that authentic Prison like experience... never stay there, ever. If you had no choice like me (due to my usual hotel being fully booked) then insist in a room which is facing the rear of the hotel as they are a little quieter I understand from the girl on reception who said I was too late to get one of those... Best of luck!

author: U2nyd
title: An American hotel in London
text: This was a pretty decent hotel for the money. We got a great deal through Expedia (about $100 a night for a double room w/ bathroom). The hotel is reminiscent of a United States budget hotel. However, in London, that gave us some nice amenities such as a larger than average room, roomy bathroom, and an ice machine (rare in Europe!). The amenities were above par - comfortable bed, nice tv, fan in the room, blow dryer, nice shower, etc. The location of the hotel isn't spectacular. It is on the southbank, near the Lambeth north tube stop. The only tube line that travels to that station is the Bakerloo, one of my least favorite lines to use. The waterloo station is a bit farther away but gives you access to the Bakerloo and Northern lines. One plus of being on the southbank however is the fact that things (for the most part) are cheaper. Instead of eating the hotel's pricey 7 pound/person breakfast, I would recommend finding something to eat locally. There is a great bakery called Gregg's by the waterloo station. One downside of the hotel was the staff. Though we only had to interact with them a handful of times, their English was poor and they were not friendly. The internet was good but a bit costly. Overall, if you can get a good price, this hotel is worth it.

author: Bob1949
title: It was OK!
text: I needed to stay near Watereloo for train connections and most hotels were priced totally over the top for a mid week overnight stay. The Days Inn at Waterloo was £110 for a double room for single occupancy including breakfast so it seemed cheap!! Days Hotel is a 10 minute walk from Waterloo Station and is opposite Lambeth North Tube station. Area is OK by day, I used taxis by night. A few small shops and bars in close proximity but there is an outside seating area at the hotel with uncomfortable picnic benches instead of chairs. The bar had reasonable prices and the breakfast was adequate enough with not very good machine coffee. On arrival they mixed up my room as I requested a higher floor with a quiet room but was give a ground floor room on the main road. This was quickly sorted and I received a long narrow twin bedded room on the 4th floor. It was basic with single beds, no air conditioning and a basic yet functional bathroom. It was just 3* which is what the hotel advertises itself as. I slept with the fan on all night and the windows open and in fairness, even though there were sirens etc is was not disruptive. The carpets and decor in the corridors are a bit grim and need replacing but it was clean. There is nothing much else to add really and this is not the sort of hotel I would normally book for business or leisure. However, it served the purpose, was cheapish for London, was convenient for Waterloo station and had reasonable facilities. Would I stay there again, probably not unless I was desperate but it seemed full of business and leisure travellers so it must be doing something right.

author: Krissy80
title: A decent budget hotel
text: I am a teacher and 4 of my colleagues and I accompanied a group of 27 high school students for a week trip in England. We stayed at the Days Hotel for 6 nights. Even though our group was large, the check-in was efficient. The rooms were clean and comfortable. The location of the hotel was good and it was only a 2 minute walk to Lambeth North tube station. We even had a view of the London Eye from our room which was especially pretty at night. I recommend asking for a room facing the London Eye! The buffet breakfast was well stocked and very tasty. The choices included eggs, bacon, sausages, beans, grilled tomatoes, freshly baked pastries, croissants, and rolls, a variety of cheeses, yogurt, fresh fruit, and cereal. There was also a coffee/hot chocolate machine and juice and milk available. The breakfast room was busy but we always found a seat. The breakfast was definitely worth it! My one complaint about the hotel was the shower. The water in the shower was never hot enough (it was just lukewarm), and the drain seemed clogged. However, the staff was accommodating and even let us use another room to shower one morning when there was no hot water. This was a great place to stay with teenagers, and it seems to be a popular place amongst tour groups,which might not be good if you are looking for an absolutely quiet hotel experience. Overall, the Days Waterloo was a clean, well-situated no-frills hotel.

author: FarAndAway2006
title: Awful welcome, excellent stay.
text: I was on a 2-day stopover in London, while flying between Marseille and Canada, and before leaving, I booked two nights at the Days Hotel London Waterloo. It was an internet booking made through the Days Inn website, and seemed to be a good deal at 48 GPB/night. Arriving at 1 pm to check-in, having come directly to the hotel from Gatwick after an exhausting flight, I wanted to grab a quick shower and head off sightseeing. I ended up having to wait for almost two hours before a room was free, despite the fact I had contacted the hotel notifying the staff of my arrival time. The woman who dealt with me was excessively rude and abrasive to the point that I seriously considered going elsewhere. Luckily, my room was ready before my patience wore out. Once in my room I was very glad I had decided to stay. Everything from the bedspread to the bathroom fixtures looked new and while not huge, the room was larger than I had expected. No bath, but an excellent shower, and everything was very clean and of good quality. My room faced a busy intersection and as a result was at times quite noisy. Also, the hotel is very close to a police station so I was a little bothered by the occasional siren. Overall, though, I quickly got used to the noise. The location is convenient if you are arriving or departing from Waterloo rail station. If not, the area is not very interesting. Just a 5-minute walk along a busy road to the underground, though, so you can still have easy access to the best of central London. While the quality of service at the hotel was terrible, the room was excellent and the area convenient, if a little removed from the main shopping / sightseeing / restaurant areas of the city. I would definetly stay here again as long as I could get a comparable rate, and I'll make sure to arrive after 3 pm or prepare myself for another fight with the staff at the front desk.

author: kevinlM5947PC
title: Location, clean, prof.
text: I and my wife stayed in this hotel last November. We tried three different hotels in Hong Kong. This was the best out of three. Perfect location in Tsim sha tsui except smokers in the restaurants on the same street. But it is like that everywhere in busy tourist streets in HK. Staffs were very helpful. Great English. Can't remember his name but.. Tony? Very helpful. He could speak little bit of Korean and fluent English. Very helpful. Breakfast bar was small but great and nutrient enough. Various yoghurts, Nespresso capsule, pancake and etc. Very ideal as we want to save money on breakfasts that we hardly eat. Sanitary/hygiene kit was better than other normal HK hotels (butterfly hotels, kowloon harbour front hotel). Love to visit again. Please do not increase the price. Lol

author: Iris_LTH
title: Spacious room for HK standard
text: Stayed one night here recently and here's my observation. LOCATED near TST station (Kowloon Park exit), not accessible by car so if you're arriving by taxi, you need to drop off at Mira Place (opp entrance to The Mira hotel), walk up a steep slope & walk pass a few restaurants/bars to the building to The Perkin (lobby at 5/F). Note that this is not a full fledge hotel with full suite of services, e.g. no bell boy, no room service. There's a security guard at the door at ground level, he's always there to open the door for me except when away on patrol. Check-in was swift and reception staff was polite. ROOM was spacious for HK standard with free mini bar (3 cans of soft drink + 1 packet lemon tea) for 1st night. The room and shower area were clean. A handy phone was included in the room which you can use to navigate around town. You can also make free local and international calls from the handy phone. It doesn't allow hot-spot tethering though, so you cannot share with your companion. Breakfast was simple with bread (toast them yourself), hard-boiled egg, cheese, jam & sausages. There's also coffee machine which has steamed milk for your tea if you like. They even have yuzu tea. My request for late check-out was swiftly given. Again, reception staff was friendly & polite at check-out. I'm overall happy with my stay though think it's a bit pricey. But again, it's all about location, location, location.

author: Loubbyloulou
title: Excellent hotel - clean and good service
text: We visit Hong Kong every two months and have stayed in quite a few hotels over the years, The Perkin is one of the best we have stayed in. We had two rooms as my parents were with us on this visit and the hotel did not disappoint. As mentioned in other reviews, the location is a bit difficult to access with bags and taxi, but a short walk along Knutsford Terrace isn't too arduous. The check in process took quite a while but everything was explained well by the staff on reception. The rooms were immaculate, very quiet due to the layout of the rooms and the number of rooms per floor. Two small issues - there is only one bin in the room, located in the bathroom; there should really be a bin in the main bedroom area as well as the bathroom otherwise you find yourself carrying rubbish (or the bin) in between the rooms. It doesn't cost much to have an additional bin and it just makes things a little easier. The second issue was the internet - it was terrible. We don't know what it is with hotels in Hong Kong and the internet, but for a business orientated city it's uniformly terrible. A guy from Reception had to come and try and reset the router in our room which didn't make any difference at all - the signal was very weak and the connection was unstable. We ended up having to pay for internet on our phones, as business travellers, we need good, stable access to the internet, so this is the main reason for the 4 star review. It doesn't take much effort to make sure the internet is decent, so this is a major mark down from us. Breakfast was basic continental and the breakfast area was so busy on the first day, we didn't bother the other days as people were fighting for places to sit as the area for seating is so small - not our idea of a relaxing breakfast. The toaster ovens didn't work properly and took ages to toast bread - it would be far simpler to buy a couple of toasters to speed things up rather than having to rely on the slow toaster ovens. Overall we had a nice stay and would return to The Perkin again on another trip as the location is excellent and the rooms were great and spacious for Hong Kong.

author: SBSBD
title: Excellent boutique hotel in Kowloon
text: We stayed a week at the perkin hotel for a holiday. The hotel is situated in tsim sha tsui which is a busy neighborhood in Kowloon (across the bay from HK island). While the hotel is in a busy street and area, the rooms were very quiet, with only 3 rooms per floor. We stayed at a higher floor (18th) and did not hear anything from the busy streets below. The room we stayed in was spacious for HK standards and very comfortable. Cleaning service was timely and efficient. The lobby is on the 5th floor of the building and that's where they have a small breakfast in the morning or coffee/snacks mid-day. It was about a 5 min walk to the nearest subway (MTR) station and from there you can go pretty much anywhere in HK within minutes. It was also a good base to walk from in the Kowloon area. Around the hotel there are literally hundreds of restaurants, shops and bars, and more in less than a mile radius. Kowloon has a more down to earth busy vibe than the main HK island (which is a bit more higher end and has a business feel) so be sure you prefer that prior to booking this hotel. To summarize, If you're looking for a comfortable hotel to stay in at reasonable budget and in a good area, this is a very good pick. It's small, simple, no frills but very comfortable, convenient and affordable. If you're in to high end amenities this is not for you. Overall would recommend for both business and holiday.

author: guillaumeandria
title: Cozy place on Knutsford Terrace
text: The Perkin describes itself as a hotel that provides 5-star service without all the unnecessary 5-star stuff. And it is indeed different from other hotels. The Perkin is located inside a building on Knutsford Terrace, with lots of restaurants and bars downstairs. Past the small entrance, you'll see a doorman, and the front desk will be on the 5th floor, facing the lounge. Staff was courteous and professional. The shared space is clean, well-designed, but rather small (though standard for Hong Kong). The lounge has a few tables and gets very crowded during the breakfast run. We enjoyed the simple but delightful breakfast buffet. You can get drinks and stuff all day long at the lounge, too. Our deluxe room was facing the garden on the 9th floor and was very quiet. It wasn't small by Hong Kong standards, but the long and narrow design of the room might not appeal to everyone. The design was grey-ish, sober and modern. The handy smartphone is useful. Knutsford Terrace is a great place for food and drinks. Very crowded in the evening, we enjoyed happy hour much more. Kimberley road and the surrounding areas are right at the heart of Tsim Sha Tsui and very convenient for shopping/getting around.

author: minatraje
title: We love Perkin Hotel!
text: We had a great stay in Perkin Hotel. .. In fairness, the reviews are true... It's a small hotel but our stay was very comfortable and comparable to other big name hotels in hongkong. We liked the lounge for the free drinks. Very nice to know that when you get home after a long day of walking there are available drinks in the lounge even if you have coffee and tea in the room its nice to relax in the lounge. My only concern is that there was no cabinet in the room that they gave us .. only a small one where the safe and ironing board is located and where you can hang your clothes. .. there was no space to put your luggage and other stuff. We loved taking a shower, the water pressure was very strong and the temperature was very easy to adjust. The water temperature once you've adjusted it is constant. The bathroom was clean. We loved that the drinks in the refrigerator although limited is free for one time, no other hotels provide that so that's an additional bonus with the free drinks and snacks in the lounge. Would definitely go back! But its not a hotel for the elderly because you have to walk a lot of steps to go to the hotel. Thanks perkin hotel! we would be back :)

author: catherinecF4551PI
title: Great Stay!
text: Our AirBnB got cancelled, so we ended up staying here for 11 nights in the Deluxe room. Room was clean, quite big and comfy. There was plenty of room for our luggage (3 suitcases, 2 backpacks). It was a bit stuffy in the hallway and elevator, but the AC worked great in the lobby and the room. Front desk was super helpful and friendly. Breakfast options were a bit limited (toast, english muffins, ham, egg, cheese, coffee, tea, apples, cereal, yogurt) - given our long stay, a bit of variety would have been nice. We did appreciate the free soft drinks and snacks during the day though. No issues with noise at all, despite all the bars/restaurants downstairs. We took the A21 bus from the airport to the hotel and it was easy to find. Just get off at the 12th stop (Kimberley Road & Nathan Road), continue walking south and turn left at Kimberley Road (where the Furla store in Mira Place One is). The steps/escalator to get up to Knutsford Terrace are at Kimberley Road/Carnavon Road, while the ramp is just past this intersection (can't miss it). It's a bit steep, but a great way to work off the yummy food in HK. Alternatively, you can get to Knutsford Terrace from Mira Place One - take the escalator up to L1 and follow the signs to Mira Steps - just go past the Jill Stuart/Cath Kidston stores, and exit the brown doors beside the Starbucks. Head up the short stairwell and you'll hit Knutsford Terrace. Definitely would stay here again if we came back to HK. Location is fantastic and super convenient - MTR Jordan, TST, and TST East are all within walking distance.

author: 526shaynea
title: Almost perfect except...
text: Very nice boutique hotel in a very good location! Reception at night could be better. Arrived late at night and Was promised an upgrade thru email since it was my friend's bday but was not honored. Have also asked for am extra pillow that we are willing to.pay for but was not provided. The guys in the morning shift were more accomodating and helped us more with our other concerns. they always take immediate action. Room is cozy and spacious by HK standards. Housekeeping is also great. Handyfone and the free mini bfasts and afternoon tea is a really great add on. Really very easy to walk everywhere. The bars surrounding the hotel served good food and drinks. Will stay again but I hope they honor their promises. Overall, really great value for our money. Almost perfect. Wouldve given a 5 rating if not for the broken promise.

author: BHC46
title: Good Location Modern Hotel
text: Situated in a very handy area near many interesting restaurants and good shopping. About 15 minutes walk to the nightly light show. Friendly helpful staff. This seems quite a new modern hotel. Compact well designed room (802) . Air conditioning adequate, however the duvet was too warm in my opinion: had to throw it off during the night , then got cold. Bathroom good, however, toilet roll holder bad design: paper kept falling off. Tap lever kept falling off. Good towels. Good supply of toiletries renewed each day. There was a pod coffee maker in the room with 2 pods and one small milk pod. On second day we did not receive more coffee pods: I was told at reception that you are only supplied once: if you want more coffee you can make one at reception. This seemed rather ridiculous. There was a "smart" phone supplied with the room which you could use in the room and take it with you touring for maps , local calls, etc. unfortunately it was too "smart" for us to use properly. Also the TV was quite technical and difficult for me to navigate. A couple of times I tried to contact reception by phone, but they never answered. I had to go down in the lift to contact them personally. I would use this hotel again as it was well situated and quiet, but would hope the problems I have would be rectified.

author: Traveler_1983_10
title: A good experience
text: Stayed at the Perkin for 4 nights for the New Years celebrations. Arrived at 10am but was told that the check in can only happen at 3pm?!? Not sure why so late.. Anyway, we stepped out to go around till such time.. The hotel is in the heart of downtown and is on a street that has tons of pubs and restaurants.. Must say it is a very lovely place and the noise level was minimal.. There are some Chinese restaurants nearby as well and a must try if you like Asian food. The hotel is pretty close to the airport shuttle drop off point, the only drawback is that one needs to drag their bags uphill a bit to get to the hotel.. The rooms are clean and new with the a very decent sized bathroom. The rooms comes with consumable mini bar which is stacked before you arrive at the hotel. Overall the room was pretty good for two people. They serve snacks, coffee and sodas at the lobby for all guests through the day, which I felt was great even if we didn't use consume much. The hotel is non smoking so one needs to step out to smoke each time. The staff at the hotel is friendly and very helpful. Kudos to Crystal for being hospitable and give helpful recommendations to go around. Overall a pretty good stay.

author: liyug2013
title: Nice location, Roomy for Hong Kong.
text: The hotel can be accessed by car from the street (Kimberly?) parallel to Knutsford Ter. Then you have to walk up a slope with your luggage. The subway station is close enough for daily sightseeing, very convenient. Knutsford Ter is occupied with western style restaurants, pubs. But you can't hear a thing at night in hotel rooms. The Perkin Hotel Lobby is located on the 5th floor of a building. The lobby is tiny, clean and modern: basically a desk as front desk and several sofas, tables to enjoy free food any time of the day. The food includes: dinner rolls, muffins, candies, apples, Nespreso coffee and lemon water. I couldn't eat these as breakfast, but they satisfy me in the afternoon as snacks. The room I stayed in was spacious, at least much bigger than the hotel rooms in Osaka. There are some free snacks, a fridge, a nespresso coffee machine, a desk, a sitting area. The wifi speed is fast. It's very comfortable. An adapter is attached to one of the outlets next to the bed. Enough for me. To/From the airport: The airport express (a subway train) runs from the airport and Kowloon station. Between Kowloon station and the Perkins hotel: there's a complimentary K4 shuttle bus. K4 stops on the street next to Knutsford Ter (See Paragraph 1). The shuttle stop is "The Luxe Manor".

author: AmberLDB
title: Could be incredible...
text: My husband and I recently stayed at the Perkin for 3 days. It is a chore to find this place and it would have been nice to have been informed of their recommended taxi drop-off points either via email or being able to access it on their website before arriving in Hong Kong and being dumped on the side of a road close to Knutsford Terrace (which is a pedestrian only street). They actually have the suggested points printed on business cards in the hotel lobby, but this isn't much help after you've been hauling your luggage up, down and around the general area before someone points you in the correct direction! This aside, The Perkin is a relatively new hotel, so the rooms and common areas are still in great condition. The rooms themselves are very modern with clean lines and finishings. The bathrooms are quite small but functional, and most importantly, clean. The complimentary mini-bar is a bit of a joke.. I think there were two cans of soft drink and a children's juice box in there which you are told, very strictly, will not be replenished for the duration of your stay. I think the person checking us in revisited the mini-bar situation 3 times! If you're looking for amazing service and facilities, this hotel isn't for you. Whilst there are numerous restaurants along Knutsford Terrace, the hotel offers no form of room service. As for the staff, I couldn't refer to them as warm, welcoming or particularly helpful; but nor could I say that they were horrible. In all honesty, because they did nothing, they left absolutely no impression. No assistance was offered to help with our luggage upon check out, and it's not like you roll your suitcase straight out the front door and into a taxi... you have to navigate the stairs past some charming garbage bins. It's the attention to the small details which The Perkin lacks, which is a shame because it could be an incredible hotel.

author: keigrant
title: Nice Place to Stay!
text: My wife said, "I liked it." I'll agree with that. You'll find the location to be at the Convention Center complex just off Interstate 2; you'll be super close to nice restaurants and stores if you have to pick up something that was forgotten. We stayed here for several nights while we visited birding locations; also returned to this hotel on our final night to be close to the McAllen airport for our flight home. You'll be pleased with the appearance of the area, exterior, and interior. The appearance makes it appear to be relatively new. The décor is pretty modern which kind of surprised me given the geographic location; there are lots of bold colors. The folks were very welcoming; very pleasant. We were given the usual set of information regarding room location, breakfast, etc. A surprise was a set of welcome drinks at the bar for both of us and a reminder of "wings" for happy hour. The hotel and room were incredibly clean both in appearance and odor. Being a tall person, I found the shower to be fantastic with an interesting and upscale door. Noise with the Interstate being so close?--not a problem at all. The breakfast area was clean and had all the servings one usually finds at these setups--cereal, fruit, yogurt, drink varieties, waffles, eggs and hot items, hard boiled eggs--something nearly all would find satisfactory--plenty of breakfast seating area. The folks at the desk were very friendly and willing to engage in conversation; their smiles and demeanor were real. Yes, we would stay here again if we would ever find ourselves in McAllen. Oh, yes -- we had no concern with the safety of the area, being in the parking lot, going out in the evening, etc. In fact, being a northerner, we left with a much changed conception of not only McAllen, but the entire Rio Grande Valley.

author: TexasNurseMom35
title: Impressed.
text: We have stayed at many La Quinta hotels over the years. And this one is by far the bast yet. I don't know if it is just because it is new or not. It opened this year in April I was told by the desk clerk. Clean, modern, and new! Breakfast is great. Many choices and all made fresh in the hotel. Free breakfast is always nice, but good free breakfast is even better. There is also a bar in the lobby that is open in the evenings. It seemed pretty busy when we walked through. Comfy beds, nice pillows. Modern bathroom with large walk in shower. Our room didn't have a tub, just a shower. No big deal for us, but might be for others. Would stay here again if we were in town.

author: TheBlueDuck
title: This property has aspirations and therefore has to be measured against them, could do better.
text: The room was a good size and nicely furnished. In the bathroom there was a good sized bath and separate shower and all the plumbing did what it was supposed to. The property has two pools, recommend the larger one at the back unless you like being the floor show for reception and the restaurant. There is also a Jacuzzi next to the larger pool with a nice big on / off button next to it. The trip we requested to Mt Popa was efficiently handled as was the airport transfer. The issues here relate to a lack of care. Here are some examples: 1) At lunch time requested that the sauna be available at 6pm as it needs a two hours notice to heat up, returned at 6 and it had not been turned on. 2) At dinner the pork in the pork curry dish was so hard it had to be retuned, and the 2nd attempt was still sub-standard. This was not an issue in other restaurants where similar dishes were ordered. 3) Minor, but the complementary banana in the room was unripe. 4) The eggs used of the omelette for breakfast were not freshly opened. 5) In general the breakfast was uninspiring. A property has to be measured against the price it charges and this is not a cheap property. Had the rate been half as much then the attention to detail would have seemed less of an issue. For a property of this quality expectations were high and frankly they were not met.

author: Aporo
title: Perfect for a stay in Bagan
text: These well equipped semi bungalows are large, clean & peaceful. Sun loungers on verandah and two pools situated in large well tended grounds. A peaceful spot to return to after hot & tiring days sightseeing in Bagan. Good breakfast spread and more than adequate dinners, both in beautiful setting beside main pool, chef really tried with presentation. Plenty of restaurants a cheap return taxi ride away, which can be easily organised at reception. (We tried Seven Sisters in New Bagan & La Terrazza in Nyaung U - both recommended). 2 for 1 Happy Hour on drinks from 4 - 7pm. on a wide range of drinks. But drinks not overly expensive anyway around $5 - $7. The Bagan archeological zone is amazing, well worthy of hoped for UNESCO World Heritage Site status. Just hope the powers that be don't spoil it by building hotels in the temple area (killing the goose which laid the golden egg!). Good spa and credit to them the only one I attended in Myanmar where I was asked to fill in a health questionnaire. Every member of staff was fantastic, Manager Oliver, Chef who sought out a jar of jam I had particularly liked at breakfast, reception staff who organised taxis & tours, bar staff who remembered our drinks each night and housekeeping staff who left a little surprise gift on leaving. A special thanks to tour guide Thein who speaks good English and over 3 mornings showed us most of the best sights in Bagan and made sure we had plenty of photos to remember our trip. He was extremely patient & helpful with my husband who has some mobility problems. Overall a great choice to stay in Bagan and would not hesitate to recommend.

author: Claudiojns
title: An amazing experience right in the middle of Bagan
text: We had a wonderful time at Bagan Lodge. We spent two weeks in Myanmar and chose Bagan Lodge to relax a little bit as Bagan was the final destination of our trip. We couldn’t have chosen a better place to stay. Facilities: two amazing outdoor pools, a fitness centre, a spa, jacuzzi and sauna, just to name a few. Restaurant: amazing food if you are too tired to go to the city center (where you can also find many beautiful tea houses). Many Burmese, Indian delicious dishes, but also occidental food. Breakfast with plenty of choices! Staff: the best! Very helpful, kind and welcoming, always ready to help in everything you need. We also met the hotel manager, Mr Ed Franco, who made sure with had a pleasant stay!!! The rooms are very clean, spacious and with the most wonderful decoration! I miss everyone and everything at Bagan Lodge. We will definitely stay there once we return to this beautiful country. Bagan Lodge made our stay and this country even more magical!! Thank you for making our stay so pleasant and joyful!

author: Harry_R001
title: Excellent Hotel, Fantastic Location
text: After travelling through Myanmar for 2 weeks, we decided to stay at the BAGAN LODGE to relax and unwind before going back to Europe. We could not have chosen a better place... Upon arrival we were warmly welcomed by the staff and General Manager. We stayed in a Suite, very spacious with top-quality amenities, spotlessly clean, from the first minute we felt like "home". Amazing pool (very clean and perfect water temperatur) and Jacuzzi, surrounded by a beautiful garden. The hotel staff was extremly friendly and very responsive. Just a little example: Our booked hot air balloon ride was cancelled due to wrong wind directions, no chance to book for the next days because they were fully booked. The Front Desk with Kiko and Olivier, managed somehow to get us on a balloon the following day. Special thanks to you guys for an unforgettable experience. The restaurant offers very delicious meals (Burmese, Indian, Chinese, European), we had 3 evening dinners in the hotel and it's a shame we could not try all the meals.. I guess that is a reason to come back! Service was excellent, very attentive and friendly. The breakfast was also the best we had in Myanmar. The General Manager Mr. Ed Franco made sure that our stay was perfect. All in all, impeccable service, beautiful location, delicious food, and everything in between. If you visit Bagan, the Hotel Bagan Lodge is the best place to stay and you will be well looked after.

author: montemaranne
title: Enjoyable stay
text: Since we were arriving shortly after 9.30 am, we were a bit worried that we might have to hang around for hours waiting for our room. Quite the opposite. We were welcomed by the staff with towels and drinks and then escorted to our very nice bungalow. Like most of the other reviewers, we were impressed by the size of the room, the lovely clean bathroom with fluffy, new towels and good products and, above all, the fact that the room was equipped with three ottomans/benches where we could open our suitcases. On our trip through S.E.Asia, there was generally only a rack for one suitcase and the other one had to be left open on the floor. The grounds of the hotel were beautifully planted and very well maintained. It was a real pleasure to sit on our terrace and admire the view. Since this was our second visit to Bagan, and I came down with flu, we were quite happy to relax in the resort and enjoy the wonderful swimming pool. Happy hour by the pool was enjoyable as was dinner the first evening when we were able to sit outside by the pool. The next day it rained heavily. Breakfast was OK but not great. I did like the hot tray to keep the croissants and danish pastries warm. Otherwise, nothing special. The front desk staff was helpful. When we wanted to book a car to take us to Mandalay airport the next day, they advised against it because of the heavy rain and flooding, explaining they would "worry about us" and the journey could take anything from 4 to 6 hours. Thank goodness for the Internet - we managed to book a flight from Bagan to Mandalay that cost less than the taxi would have, and when we saw the flooded countryside from the plane, we were glad we had taken their advice. We enjoyed chatting with the General Manager Ed on both evenings and wish him all the best for the future.

author: breweruk
title: Wonderful experience
text: We had three nights at Bagan Lodge and it's been a wonderful experience. We arrived early in the day having caught the morning flight from Yangon and were expecting to hang around for check-in, but no, they gave us cool drinks, face towels, and showed us to our villa. This gave us an extra day touring the pagodas, temples and monasteries. Thank you Bagan Lodge. Everything here is high quality from the furniture and fittings through to the food and staff. They have happy hour on the terrace by the small pool from 4-7. There is also a larger pool on site, which we used each afternoon. The lodge hires electric bikes out by the half day ($5) and full day ($10) and we took them for each of our days here riding down dusty roads visiting sites off the beaten track. Each evening we ate at the lodge, and used the bikes to try other restaurants in the area for lunch. We recommend Sanon, a training restaurant for disadvantaged youth. Wonderful food. It's 7Km away. Also try The Village House Restaurant (delicious food and beautiful setting) which is 1.5km away - or five mins on an electric bike. Bagan Lodge is a total experience and a real treat. Recommended.

author: Bigkabloona
title: Almost Perfect
text: The greeting was typical Myanmar—cool towels, cool drink, warm smiles. Our room was very spacious, modern, and well-equipped. King-size bed, comfortable seating area and a fabulous bathroom with separate WC and walk-in shower. Everything was really great. So, where did they fall down? Well, the breakfast buffet was good, but not great. We’ve had better in Myanmar. However, the main reason for losing a five-star rating was a familiar one. If you have read any of my reviews, this is a common problem in many hotels. They hang/post signs stating that if you wish to reuse your towels in order to “help save the planet”, you should hang them up. I dutifully hung up my towels and the housekeeping staff dutifully replaced them with fresh towels. How many of us get fresh towels everyday at home? I consider this a management issue, not a problem with the housekeeping staff. Clearly, management has not explained the policy sufficiently to make it clear to the staff. That said, I would stay here again next time I’m in Bagan. You should, too.

author: CarloC159
title: Exceeding Expectations!
text: For my solo trip this year, I chose Bagan because of so many great reviews about this destination. As I was searching for the perfect place to stay, I came across Bagan Lodge. I have to say the photos of the hotel are stunning and it is highly recommended by guests. When I arrived at the hotel, the place was amazing because the place was much better in person and adding to it was the friendly and accommodating hotel staff. The villa where I stayed was impressive. I have loaded some photos to help other travelers looking for the right hotel in Bagan. Trust me. This is the best in Bagan just like what other guest reviews say about the hotel. It will only take you 5 minutes or less to get to the hotel from the airport and almost the same amount of time to get you to the famous pagodas/temples of Bagan coming from the hotel. After a tiring day of going around Bagan, they have two big pools and a jacuzzi to cool you down. Just beside the pool near the reception is the restaurant that offers a variety of cuisines including some local favorites. They also have menu for vegans! Menu is reasonably priced and quality of food is above average. For gym addicts like me, there is a small functional gym to keep you active while you're on vacation. I visited their spa to get some Swedish massage and it was good enough to make me fall asleep. I forgot the name of the therapist but she really has strong hands. It was good 60 minutes for USD 50.

author: RWJanssen
title: Truely a perfect base for exploring Bagan
text: Enjoyed our stay tremendously as a family of 4 at Bagan Lodge. Very comfortable rooms with perfect showers, beds and airco. Very well put together and maintained resort opened in 2014 but kept up to look as new. Great pools & Manicured gardens. Very nice spa. Truely a perfect base for exploring Bagan Pagodas and Temples. Staff is amazing and food and drinks are fresh and well prepared. Rent an e-bike, explore a sunrise and sunset and even in July the weather was very good. Too bad the weather apps reflect the wrong predictions of the weather is Myanmar which is often much more pleasant than indicated on the apps. Ask for Mr U Wen or Mr Chan Myae Aung as a Licensed Tour guide Bagan, Myanmar 🇲🇲. We got a pickup by private van from Mandalay Airport flying in from Bangkok on Bangkok Airways. note there are now also direct flights to Bagan on Bangkok Airways on selected days. Will try that next time. We spent 4 days here and it felt like we relaxed for twice that amount of time. Don't miss the sunrise and sunsets from a neighboring temple. Truely magical.

author: sharonkI8533DX
title: A memorable trip to Bagan
text: We stayed at Bagan Lodge for three nights in July. We made the most of our stay while we were in Bagan and Bagan Lodge provided the perfect place to do this. It was low season so there weren't many guests at the resort. The resort itself is big and built to look like a safari lodge. Our lodge was comfortable and we found the double vanities very useful (not having to share vanity space with my husband). The aircon was nice and strong. Much needed in the Bagan heat. The only things that could be improved on re the villa are the noise from the birds that seem to be able to nest on the roof due to the openness of the roof covering and the smell from the drainage that comes out and is very obvious when you enter the villa after being out. The staff at the resort were friendly, polite and helpful. In particular, we found the driver service the resort offered to be very useful. Our driver Aung was so sweet, patient and polite. He was our driver for 2 days and he recommended local spots and made our lives so much easier by ensuring everything went smoothly with transport and pickups. Our stay included breakfast and we thought the options were sufficient. We had dinner at the resort on one night. Everything is priced in $US so it is definitely more expensive than local options but the food was nice enough and the wine was very good.

author: TeamMiller
title: Lovely time in Bagan
text: We stayed for 4 nights in a two bedroomed safari lodge suite. Lovely bedrooms and bathrooms. The sitting room dividing the bedrooms is a large room with two throne chairs. Slightly dysfunctional as no comfy seating nor a focal point. Shame as it's a nice space. The gardens are very well maintained and the outdoor space is very nice and relaxing. Swimming pools lovely. Breakfast had a good range of foods. Happy hour limited though adequate. Dinner was fine. Have read differing reviews but you do have to remember you're in a different country and things are just not going to be the same as back home! They were able to cope just with gluten free and omitted sauces etc. Stuck mainly to Asian foods though the Greek salad was very tasty. Husband and daughter had pizzas, satay, vegetables, grilled sandwiches. All of which were fine though pricing is not local. Very current American prices. Hotel staff couldn't do enough for you. Very helpful. We were able to hire electric bikes very easily from reception and then we were off to see the temples and visit Bagan proper. Great stay!

author: OnoO
title: A Mostly Great Stay with a Few Minor Flaws
text: We had a good stay here, with just a couple of minor flaws. The rooms were very comfortable and spacious, and were styled after African Safari lodges. Plenty of room in the large bathroom with two vanities, a tub, shower and separate toilet room. The staff is great, and the laundry service was perfect and on time. During the evening turn-down service, a different sweet was left each night in a wicker basket. I looked forward to the sweet surprise each night. The other good things include the ability o rent motor scooters and helmets at the hotel, and there is also an ATM machine outside (didn't use it though, so can't attest if it works). The cute outside bar also offers a 2 for 1 wine, cocktail and soda special for a few hours each night. We did this each night before heading into the restaurant for our evening meal. The couple of minor annoyances were that the resort had installed tacky light strings blinking garish colors at night (aka bad disco) all over the property. I am a fan of lights at night, but not all blinking off sync with each other. The included breakfast buffet was very marginal, as was the restaurant for dinner. The walls of the rooms are thin as I could hear loud music playing all night from an adjacent property. I was not able to sleep that night. Though it was not the fault of the Lodge, the rooms could have been better sound-proofed. The location of the hotel was a little off the beaten path which means that there were not off-property restaurants that could be walked to.

author: Eric1313
title: Probably best in Bagan but not value for money
text: Expensive resort-type place. Don't compare this place to any of Asia's best resort hotels (which we couldn't help doing), although quite a nice place for Myanmar, and probably the best in Bagan. Free airport shuttle and nice early check-in (we arrived at 10:00 a.m. and our room was ready at 10:45 a.m.). Clean, nice staff, pools are wonderful and enough sunbeds around. Massage in the spa is excellent and at reasonable prices (high for Myanmar but ok for international travelers). We also enjoyed playing pool (billiards) at the reception area. Close to temples, maybe sometimes too close (one day and night we had to endure a loud novitiation ceremony). Nice big rooms, good airco, LCD TV, fridge and free waters (often restocked), fresh fruit, large bathroom with two sinks, bath tub and separate shower. Beds were a bit small though. Food was good, both breakfast and dinner (we had Asian food, as they are obviously best at cooking that, and didn't have any issues that other reviews noted). Now the issues. Our most expensive hotel in Myanmar, so we expected more. I had to get an additional child bed as the existing two beds were too small for even an (8-year old) child to fit with us; for this they charged a whopping $70 per night extra (!!!) - I paid less in five star hotels, well, pretty much anywhere. Also, the outside open restaurant makes it very hot there for lunch and still warm and full of mosquitoes for dinner. Although there is a good child menu (only one we found in Myanmar), the prices are high/almost the same as the adult options. Some side-issues: the table football game was old and broken and the business center was just an empty small booth, maybe for the future? All in all, pretty good but let down in value for money.

author: samoncao
title: Very nice place. Still needs improvements
text: On our trip to Birmânia we choose Bagan Lodge to stay in Bagan. The offer in Bagan of 4 and 5 stars hotels is quite narrow. The positive points. Accommodation. The rooms are spacious and well decorated. The pool area. Very nice. The spa treatments. Very nice and quite affordable. Free airport pick up. The let downs. Breakfast. Poor. Service and food. Not at all Asian style. The jacuzzi by the pool. What a piece of bad taste..... ruined the view.... Still one of the best place to stay in Bagan....

author: Adore921
title: Lovely hotel
text: Hotel was really romantic. Big gardens with stylish villa n sidewalk give the stroll back to our room great ambiance every night. There are 2 pools at the hotel were beautiful and chilled. We napped by the pool a few times with the balance of fresh breeze and sunlight. It was a perfect rest place. 95% of the staff were a really nice. They were always cheerful and attentive. Greeting us and checking on our needs everytime. Comfortable n friendly interactions. The hotel even gave us thank you gift, very sweet and heart warming. The food was okay but a little bit pricey for Burmese standard. Their Asian foods were way better than their Western menu. But if you're are true food maniac, then probably the food wouldn't satisfy your taste buds. The location of the hotel was actually very close to the town (I would say it's walkable). But of course there are also electric bikes to rent. So no problem getting around at all. Overall I would say it's a very memorable experience at Bagan Lodge. I wouldn't hesitate to recommend to anyone.

author: jesssssssk
title: Relaxing Hotel Minutes from Temples
text: My husband and I stayed for four nights, but wish we had planed for more! The hotel is on a large property, and the bungalows are spread out making it very private and quiet. Even when the hotel is full, you never feel crowded. The hotel feels tucked away from the hustle of bustle of Bagan, but it really is in midst of where you want to be. The property is clean and makes for a relaxing stay. They have e-bikes for rent on the property, which we rented every day. This was one of the highlights of our time in Bagan. Waking up in the early morning, renting our e-bike and biking down to the temples just in time for sunrise. Something we will never forget. We ate our lunches out since we were sightseeing everyday, but ate all of our dinners at the hotel. They customized food for us, and were kind enough to give a recipe of a delicious vegan soup they made special for us. The staff were incredibly kind and always had the biggest smiles on their faces. I can never say enough how the people of Myanmar are the kindest of any country we've visited, and are the reason we will continue coming back. Cannot think of a single complaint or flaw of this hotel, and will definitely stay here again on our return to Bagan in the future. :)

author: xinmei55
title: Oasis in Bagan
text: Great stay if you're even considering it, just do it. We hesitated over a few for a while but we would definitely come back. Rooms are clean and spacious. We slept beautifully. Quite surroundings at night. Service excellent. V friendly. Beautiful lawns and property and the two pools are wonderful for a mid day dip in the scorching dry heat. Only down side is breakfast. Only western food, which is a shame for those looking for local flavours. Don't expect that here. Western breakfast includes average eggs pancakes cereals hot foods etc but not at a great standard which doesn't match the hotel. We did a breakfast box for sunrise at temples which included some stale pastries, one boiled egg and a banana. We did not eat here for dinner but hotel is a 10 min walk to the village and v accessible. Daily happy hour 4-7. Stay here!

author: flyboylee
title: Luxury in Bagan
text: This is a much nicer resort in real life than the pictures we saw before booking! The villas are spacious, luxurious and clean and little touches very thoughtful! The design of the accommodation is genius, cool during the day and designed to ward off the monsoon rain. We stayed for 4 nights and found the entire resort peaceful, quiet and the staff look after you really well. The restaurant is lovely, set by the first pool and easy access to the bars. Breakfast was served here too and sitting in the morning sun really set you up for the day! The evening menu was big enough to keep us occupied each evening as the hotel is a fair distance from restaurants or other places to eat. I would definitely recommend hiring ebikes. Go for whole day rather than 4 hours as you really can get totally absorbed in viewing the thousands of temples. The roads are quiet and safe and biking around on your own all day is a perfect way to see the amazing places Bagan has to offer. Sunset viewing is a must and its worth getting a list of the best temples to go to. Prepare for them to get busy and bus tours tend to rock up too. Many of the temples were damaged in the 2016 earthquake however it is still totally possible to get around and see them. Damaged ones are clearly signed and access closed if they are unsafe. Then after a hot and sticky day of sightseeing, either of the two pools at the lodge are a welcome treat. The hotel also has a spa. It was reasonably priced and the treatment ok.. a nice extra touch if you are on holiday. I would definitely recommend staying here and although a bit further out, we found the location to be perfect!

author: Guiyang26
title: Outstanding choice in Bagan - highly recommended!
text: We really enjoyed our stay here! Looked much better than the other options around town that we saw while riding around on the e-bikes. Our room was great, all staff were excellent, and hotel grounds were beautiful. There's also a nice pool. Food could have been better though. It's just average and expensive compared to the options outside (which is to be expected I guess). We also tried the spa. Service was good but staff were a bit unprofessional (whispering to each other, light giggling during our massage). If we ever come back to Bagan, we will stay here again! P.s. don't get conned by the sand paint sellers around the pagodas. We were idiots and paid 53,000 kyats for 2 on our first day, only to be quoted 10,000 for a similar 1 out of curiosity on our second day. Guess you can get them for under 10,000! Oh well you win some you lose some. Somehow we didn't have to pay the 25,000 kyat per person entrance fee on our way into Bagan.

author: SCORTAZAR
title: Spacious and super comfortable rooms... still need to work on the restaurant
text: We stayed here for three nights at the end of March during our Myanmar trip and used the hotel as a sightseeing base for the nearby temples of Nyaung U, Old and New Bagan. Check-in was pretty smooth, we were greeted by the staff with cold drinks and a cold towel and they allowed us to enter our room at around 10 am. The hotel architecture blends beautifully with its desert-like surroundings, featuring cabins that fit two enormous rooms each. Our room was probably one of the most spacious I've ever stayed at, had its own mini living-room, a desk and two armoires big enough to fit clothes for more time than you would need in Bagan. Furniture and lining was in a very good condition, bed was quite ample and not too soft or too hard. In summary, not a single complain from the actual sleeping product. Having said this, I've got quite a few "complains" in regard to the restaurant: - Fancy an espresso for breakfast?... They'll charge you for it. I find quite often that some hotels tend to have this annoying practice which, at least from my point of view, shouldn't be in place in a hotel which describes itself as a "Luxury Boutique Hotel". - Breakfast pastries were all pretty toasty, all the three times I had breakfast. Coincidence? Bad luck? Who knows, to me they were plain old pastries. - Food at dinner was just OK, you can easily have better food in many other places in New or Old Bagan, one's just to lazy to go to town again at night. Overall it was a great experience and I would totally recommend this hotel. I would just suggest guests-to-be to make an effort to have dinner outside.

author: TravelwithGar
title: Not all it's cracked up to be?
text: The biggest drawback for us on our visit was the fact that it is in an isolated area - there is nothing immediately around it, so if you want to venture out you need transport and taxis are not really an option on the outskirts of Bagan. We also found that everything closes down early in the hotel, including the restaurant and the bar, so there was little or no atmosphere there in the evenings. You can hire ebikes which, if you can handle the heat, are a great way to get about the temples during the day. However, be sure to check that they are fully charged, otherwise they will run out of juice as one of ours did in the middle of nowhere! We did not find the reception staff overly friendly or warm on our arrival just very officious , yet the grounds staff and others were particularly friendly. There are two pools on site, one beside the restaurant and the bar and the other in the middle of the complex with a very small pool bar which did not seem to be operational. The spa was reasonably good and again the staff here were very friendly and welcoming. On the occasion we stayed there was a hotel photo / drone shoot taking place for an updated brochure, so there was some disruption on site and the pool was not accessible on occasions. Perhaps what was more interesting was the extent of the 'changes' / props which were being put in place for the photo shoot. Not least of which were some fourteen torch lights around the pool in the evening, matching sun beds etc. I can't help thinking if this is how you want the hotel to look then why not put these things in place and not simply roll them in for the photo shoot?! If you are looking for a good base from which to explore the surrounding area, are happy with early nights and not too fussed about the limited dinning options, then Bagan Lodge may indeed suit you. The rooms are comfortable without perhaps the luxury touch, but that's fine and there is a verandah where you can sit out, not that there is anything to see. Just important to know the set up before you get there and to manage expectations. Not really our cup of tea.

author: 486StuartB
title: A very beautiful litte hotel, in a great location
text: I've just seen another reviewer title their review "Oasis in Bagan", and that's really exactly what this hotel is. When I stayed in Bagan (March, 2016) the area was incredibly hot, and very very dry. So when I saw the hotel, I was a bit shocked really. But in a good way. Bagan at this time of year seemed almost entirely brown, and dusty. The Bagan Lodge however has two massive pools, and was entirely green and lush. Really quite beautiful. The rooms are very large, and comfortable. The staff were super friendly and helpful. Oddly the wifi was great. And its location is ideal I think. One morning I was up early, and saw the balloons flying over head. I really can't think of one negative about this hotel or its location. I wish I still had the details of my tour guide there... he was amazing. So friendly and fun to tour around with.

author: Louisa718
title: Cool and tasteful oasis in a hot climate - recommended.
text: We traveled as a family of three, two adults and one young teen girl. We found the location easy, and the compound of green grass and garden areas a cool respite from the strong, dry heat of Bagan. Our daily routine was: out to see temples and pagodas early, mid-day break during the peak heat to relax and swim, back out with our guide around 430. Breakfast buffet was much like any of the nice hotels we stayed in during our Myanmar trip: some asian options, some western options. Kind and attentive service. The rooms are freestanding, adjacent with one other room, tented roof (under a wooden or metal roof). The beds do not have mosquito netting, but we had no issues with them unlike other travelers on this site. Perhaps we just missed them. The hotel does provide an insect spray in room...overall, bug management is an issue for western travelers in Myanmar. The overall feel of decor is "colonial", which can be a little odd if - like ourselves - you are not wistful for the days of colonial exploitation. Still, the rooms are fresh with robes provided, good working A/C, nice linens and towels. There is a small but decent gym should you want to run on a treadmill or use free weights. I opted not to! Very attentive housekeeping staff, and grounds people. Perhaps too much water is called for to keep the grounds green? Front desk also very helpful. Highly recommended.

author: annarenz_03
title: A comfortable hotel to stay in Bagan
text: Thanks to our friend for recommending Bagan Lodge. This hotel was simple but has a charm. The lodge are duplex style. The white tent/canopy over the roof made the buildings more attractive and unique. We even spotted the lodge from our balloon flight. Our room was spacious. T&B was simple but decent. AC works great and quite. The balcony outside the room was nice to relax also. The hotel has two big swimming pools. I like the swimming pool right by the restaurant and bar area. It's not only close to our room but easy to order food or drinks. Their breakfast buffet was good. At night all lights along the path from the rooms to the front of the hotel are well lit up. The buggy service was great as well. The wifi works perfect but sometimes inside the room doesn't. But over all, my husband and I had a wonderful stay. Of course, I should not forget the friendly staff at the front desk and restaurant specially Francis the manager/supervisor who made our stay memorable. We highly recommend Bagan Lodge.

author: Loke41
title: Bagan Lodge
text: Very recently my wife and I stayed at the Bagan Lodge just east of New Bagan which is in a great location as it is close to the city but without all the noise and traffic. When we arrived after dark and I was pleased to learn that there were electric golf carts to take us with our luggage to our “gold theme” suite. The short ride was just awe inspiring as we passed immaculately landscaped grounds and an outdoor Jacuzzi with near life sized statues around it plus a beautiful dome over it. We were told by the staff that they have 82 rooms and 8 suites at the “Lodge”. The “gold theme” suite exceeded our expectations as it was decorated in teak, teak carvings, lacquerware and Myanmar fabrics with of course gold highlights which gave one the feeling of what company executives and wealthy people experience. All the amenities were certainly more than needed. There was a mixture of Myanmar classic furnishings like a beautifully carved wardrobe to fashionable decorations. The “Lodge” has two swimming pools one of which is near the restaurant and the reception area and the other by the outdoor Jacuzzi. The beautiful pool near the reception area is made more attractive by elephant statues and decorations that are very pleasing and relaxing to the eye. The reception area is very comfortable and is decorated extremely well with everything that just balances together amazingly well. It is a great place to just relax and read a book in such comfortable surroundings or sip on a favorite beverage near the bar. Personally I just really liked the design, layout and colors of the “Lodge”. My wife tells me the “Lodge” has a world class spa, being of the male species I do not know of those things, but she does know and I respect her professional opinion. She also looked at the kitchen and talked to the chef and his staff at the “The Tiffin Box Restaurant”; the meals were very well presented and very good. All the Myanmar staff at the “Bagan Lodge” were very friendly, considerate, helpful, quick to respond when asked for help and professional with a good working knowledge of English and I expect at least German, French and Japanese as those were tourists nationalities that I encountered while staying at the “Lodge”. Late last year my wife and I stayed at a five star hotel in Athens, Greece and the Bagan Lodge was, in my opinion, was more comfortable and relaxing than that famous hotel near their Parliament Building. In my opinion the Bagan Lodge is first class and certainly must rank as one of the very top hotels in Bagan. On our next trip to Bagan we will most definitely stay at the Bagan Lodge. R J Löwecke

author: Cymbid64
title: Doesn't quite do it
text: Our accommodation was booked by our tour company but we were assured that everything was "5 star ". Now to be honest, I don't crave 5 star but I can live with it, but if it's rated as, the it better be! This is not. The rooms are cabins and these are good. Even great. Bathrooms stunning. Everything here worked. It fell down in the Resteraunt, and badly. Now our tour company had organized set menus for our lunch and dinner. I hadn't realized at the time but I let it ride. Well the curries were dried out bits of meat and tough. The menus uninspiring. The staff amateurish at best. We woke in the morning to lots of balloons floating overhead. That was a bonus. Bagan is fabulous. Not to be missed. I don't know how much it costs per night but just be prepared and eat in town.

author: 404kristinw
title: Not impressed...this will be the last time.
text: I really don't understand why a lot of people are raving about this hotel. First of all, the service was spotty, it's really a hit or miss depending on the person. While a few are nice and friendly, others especially the staff at the tiffin box restaurant and some of the reception were very disappointing. There's a particularly bad experience where one lady Server cleared the plates by throwing utensils into the plates and stacking them moodily and bodily with a smirk!!!! Some of the leftover from the plate flew out and landed on the napkins and table! To add insult to injury, our room has no view. Then we realized after a walk around the premises, that all the rooms / bungalows are built right next to each other with a maximum gap of 4 -5 feet. I dare not open my window at all as I'm worried someone will pass by and see me. When we expressed our unhappiness to the reception, there was no follow - up but fake smiles from reception. No sorries, no asking for feedback. And when I tried to call the hotel reception to book a taxi as we were out at a spa outside the hotel, no one picked up!! I kept trying every few minutes and gave up after 1 hour. We ended up having to ask around our spa who has kindly helped to arrange. Strange as every time I walked by hotel reception , there was always someone and how can no one picked up when I called??!!! I do not care for the overall service of the staff at this hotel especially when I'm paying good money for it. I have stayed in much cheaper hotels in Myanmar and never experienced such bad attitude from staff from a highly rated hotel on tripadvisor !!!

author: jwsmd3
title: THE lodge to stay at in Bagan !
text: 2 nights, hotel 2 of 8 on 15 night tour of Myanmar. Stylish and very roomy British safari style accommodations decorated with native longyis fabrics. Super comfortable beds, good lighting, closet space, etc. Didn't seem high occupancy when we arrived but I guess everyone is out touring because dinner was a very busy affair. Showed up for dinner first night without reserving and despite being very busy they instantly put a table together for us and were very attentive. Very good food with fresh pasta! Large grounds, occasional groups. They have golf carts but if you are of limited mobility securing a room close to reception should be considered. While not on their map there is a second (?new) large swimming pool and large Jacuzzi at the other end, a better evening choice instead of the main pool in front of restaurant. Plenty of loungers and towels but water was cold! Terrific breakfast spread with attentive staff. Spa was quite pricy by Myanmar standards and a massage was good initially but then got better. Considering the place has been here 3 to 4 years the plantings appear immature. Maybe recently redone or expanded. I found the two giraffe (in Myanmar? seriously?) topiaries taking form at the entrance kind of ridiculous as are the 3 dinosaur within the grounds. May I suggest elephants instead?

author: BrianH406
title: It is a must stay in Bagan
text: We stay here for two nights and we loved our stays. I believe that it is the best in Myarmar, after my stay in Sule Shangri-La and the Charium Hotel as comparison. You get a villa as part of your stay, the cheapest price for laundry. Massage price of $55 for 90 minutes. This is a must do. In the morning the air balloons are overhead. Two beautiful pools, however, the whirl pool was not heated. The restaurant served all kind of foods, from pasta (excellent) to hamburgers to Asian foods. Mostly good, at a fair price. Not much selection outside. The area around Bagan is amazing. Feels like Indiana Jones, with the thousands of Pogordas that looks like castles. Lots of Indian influences, with colors of gold, white, and brown, Some looks like the Tai . After visiting Yangon, Bagan is heaven. If I do it over again, I would skip Vangon and go directly to Bagan.

author: HH600
title: Stands Out in Many Ways
text: LOCATION - Located on the edge of New Bagan, the hotel grounds provide a welcome relief from the chaos of the village. Designed in the open, Southeast Asian style pergola architecture, the hotel lobby and reception area are at once a nice juxtaposition against the often haphazard and unremarkable new architecture one is subject to all over Myanmar. SITE PLANNING, MATERIALS, ARCHITECTURE AND INTERIOR DESIGN - It is clear that someone has paid deliberate attention to every aspect of design in creating this beautiful compound. Everything from the choice of materials, the layout of the cottages, landscaping, and even staff's uniforms are deliberately balanced to soothe the senses. Once you pass the welcoming front lobby and reception area, followed by an ourdoor patio bar and open dining hall flanking both sides of a glistening swimming pool, you are in an expansive garden setting, with the very large rooms paired together as duplex brick bungalows with a sweeping covered patio wrapping around each cottage. Dark colored, dense tropical wood meets the salmon colored brick structures and each cottage is shaded by a canvas shade structure carefully stretched to mimic oriental-style roofs extending several feet over the edge of each cottage. Once again, there is a wonderful balance of modern and traditional architecture and materials. The garden pathways are punctuated by antique carriages, bicycles, and life-size locally produced wooden and stone statues in a way that is neither kitsch nor garish. Inside each room, Burmese teak, wicker, and basketry come together with brick and cotton to remind you where you are. Maintaining the brick texture, with subtle details, the interior of each cottage is painted in calming neutral colors contrasting the dark tropical wood generously used all over. Each room has a vast bathroom with "his and her" sinks, a bathtub, an enclosed wash-closet and a shower area, using the same earthen brick. While each cottage embodies the balanced contrast of ideas and materials, the use of salmon-color brick follows the rhythm of the character-defining, beautiful brick pagodas and temples that make this valley a magnificent world-heritage site. One can only hope this balanced approach in design and site planning is maintained as this hotel - which is sure to become a favorite with the fast-growing tourist industry in Myanmar - is expanded. SERVICES, AMENITIES, STAFF - The hotel management has obviously gone out of their way to think about all accommodations their guests might need or desire. There is a wonderful spa, which we took advantage of the first day, bicycle and e-scooter rentals at reasonable prices, and the attentive staff will book any services you might need outside the hotel. The hotel restaurant provides a variety of Western and local foods. We were happy to include breakfast when we booked our stay.

author: travellerbirkdale
title: Good but not great
text: The first thing that annoyed me about this hotel is that it was by no means full yet they put us right next door to someone else, with an inter-connecting door which always affects the sound insulation of a room. I don't understand this mania hotels have for squashing guests into a small area: do the staff complain about having to go further to clean rooms or something? Fortunately the people next door left the day after we arrived and we were "alone" for the next 2 nights. The room itself was a good size and well-equipped with 2 stand-alone wardrobes and plenty of room for suitcases. The bathroom was large, with 2 separate sinks and a separate loo. The shower was in a separate "room", so plenty of space but be warned, the water is extremely hot and the taps in both the shower and the sinks were, for me, counter-intuitive and I nearly got scalded a couple of times. This was the only hotel we stayed in where having a shower didn't flood the bathroom floor. The soap bars were absolutely tiny - I realise that a lot of guests there only stay for a couple of days but seriously, could they not stretch to something a bit bigger? Also, the shampoo, conditioner etc were in bottles that were almost impossible to squeeze so it was difficult getting anything out. Breakfast was very disappointing: having heard that this hotel was French-run, I was looking forward to lovely crisp croissants, pain au chocolat and pastries. No such luck. There was a pretty poor choice available and the service was dire. One morning there were more waiting staff than guests and yet they still couldn't clear the table of dirty plates. We ate two nights in the restaurant and the food was good but, on the first night, we were annoyed to be moved from our table after being sat at it for several minutes, because it was reserved. Top tip - if a table is reserved, put a "reserved" sign on it, it's not rocket science. Happy hour was good and was my first chance to sample Myanmar wine - the sauvignon blanc was not bad, I've tasted worse! The pool is lovely and a good size and it wasn't busy while we were there. We went to the spa for a massage and facial: whilst the massage was good, I nearly had to remind the girl that my nose and ears were attached to my head, so it wasn't terribly relaxing. This hotel has the potential to be really good but someone needs to sort out the staff.

author: seoulsoulman
title: Oasis in Bagan x2
text: We arrived after a long journey and big smiles came to our faces as we walked into the reception area. The rooms are like little bungalows but all open concept. No separate bedrooms like in some other hotel suites. The resort is relatively new. If you walk the property you see construction crews adding to the facility by building new bungalows and a second pool. Amazing pool! Staff were great and friendly. They even took time out of their duties to entertain a temporarily unruly child. One downside is the resort is not walking distance to town. Our friends stayed at a more central hotel in New Bagan and were able to walk to restaurants. We we stuck at the Lodge. The second downside was the restaurant at the Lodge. The food was good quality but I didn't find the restaurant food up to expectations. I think they are trying to be too western and inadvertently ignoring their own culture. Local dishes were not really on the menu. I;d only give the restaurant an average review based on all the places we ate in Myanmar.

author: great_squasher
title: An oasis in Bagan
text: Great experience. Lovely staff. Spacious rooms. Good breakfast/kitchen. Had dinner there only the last day of our stay because we chose to go to the village (New Bagan, one kilometer away) for more atmosphere the other nights. Large pool and comfortable sun beds. Happy hours with two for one (USD3,5). The only remark I have, and it's not the hotel's fault I guess, is the taxi charge of USD5 one way to New Bagan. It is a fixed rate within Bagan but seems overpriced when you just drive three minutes. You would have paid the same going 20 minutes away to old Bagan. It's a taxi mafia system. It was too dark to walk at night with potholes and sudden rain but you can get locals to take you back on a motorbike for USD1. Hard to find taxis after dark (and they have same rate) so the best is to deal/agree drop-off and pick-up with the hotel's transportation service. Still this is a detail compared to the overall experience: heartly recommend this lodge. They also offer el-bikes (el-scooter) for hire at USD8/day. A great option when exploring this magnificent landscape.

author: TyE687
title: Super hotel, super surprise in Bagan
text: We stayed here for only one evening on April 22nd. This was such a total surprise for Bagan. Myanmar has really only been getting U.S. tourists for a few years so we were so surprised when we arrived. The hotel is a series of bungalows with very large rooms. The shower had a rain shower head with the bathroom having two vanities-one for each person. The unit we stayed in was very warm when we arrived as they don't run the power when not occupied. I was skeptical that the unit would cool down our bungalow so I put it on 18 C only to wake up that night freezing. The rooms were very clean and the bed was great. The wireless worked great as they had Many connection points. Several outdoor bars and a superb pool area. We had both dinner and breakfast there and they were both exceptionally good. For breakfast they had a make to order omelet station with make to order pancakes, various cereals, fruits and of course local fare. Not sure of some of the other negative reviews on the site as this hotel is good by Western standards. The staff was very friendly and helpful. I would have been happy just to hang out a few extra days to enjoy the place. I have travelled extensively and I must say that I was extremely surprised when we arrived. Fantastic place.

author: MONichols
title: A Calming Oasis
text: We traveled to Bagan in the end of the busy season, late March. We overnighted at the Bagan Lodge and my only wish was that I'd had more time there. I was part of a tour group that only stayed one night in Bagan, arriving in early afternoon and touring temples for several hours before arriving at the hotel after sunset. We had an excellent set dinner in the beautiful outdoor, poolside, dining area, then an excellent night's sleep before an early wake up call to head out again for more touring. The photos will explain it more thoroughly, the rooms are HUGE, each like it's own lodge. They look almost like African tented lodges with tented roofs, but are not tents. The decks have thickly padded loungers facing the courtyard. Inside a king bed, settee, ample closet space, desk, dual sinks, large soaking tub, rain shower room, toilet room. Plenty of hot water, a mini-bar and safe, and a can of insect repellant (to use yourself, since Buddhists wouldn't kill a bug), though I never saw any insects. It was quite a walk to the main pool/restaurant area, but there were golf carts running around gathering the older guests at meal times. The service was wonderful. Cold drinks and towels on arrival back from touring. The pool looked pristine, but we didn't have time to use it during our short stay. There was a small bar area, and folks from our party were able to order Margaritas, yes tequila in Myanmar. Loved this place and would stay again in a heartbeat. We awoke in the morning to chanting from the monks next door. It was lovely.

author: Mosquito2009
title: New charming hotel in Bagan
