text: I am a resident in Yangon and I spent a night at Bagan Lodge with my 5 year old child for a short weekend trip. Visiting Bagan after 5 years shocked me a bit with so many choices available! I selected Bagan lodge because of large swimming pool and excellent rating from Trip Advisor. None of my friends in Yangon stayed there before. My experience, though it was rather short was beyond my expectation. First, we were warmly welcomed by the reception people early in the morning. We arrived around 8 am but they accepted us to check in right away. The hotel also arranged a tour guide and transportation without any hustles and errors. The swimming pool was very large and well maintained. The room was so spacious and had a bathtub and a separate shower room, which were all maintained well. The compound was also well maintained with many flowers. My daughter and I enjoyed walking around in the morning when the weather was not too hot. For checking out, since our flight was late in the afternoon, the hotel arranged late check out so that we could enjoy their facilities till the last moment. The staff were all friendly and helpful, remembering our names. Before heading off to the airport, I also had a pleasure to try the spa. The therapist was well-trained and she told me that she had to go through one year training by a Thai therapist, which explained high quality of services! The only thing I could advise to the hotel is that the pressure for shower was too low (this happens a lot in Myanmar) to have good shower. If the hotel is seeking for excellence, I suggest that they improve this point for guests. Overall, I was really satisfied with the standard of services they provided and I would go back to Bagan Lodge if I have a chance to visit Bagan near future and would certainly recommend to friends and family members.

author: SandyC121
title: Who would have guessed?
text: Shock of all shocks, our group 40 checked into this new hotel after a whirlwind tour of temples, pagodas, and stupas plus a fantastic local market and a lacquerware factory. No sleep for nineteen hours. We would have been satisfied with a clean bed. Instead we pulled up to a clean, modern upscale lodge that was utterly charming sitting in a hot, dusty, venue that is the epitome of poverty and filth. Don't get me wrong, Bagan is fascinating, a land of 2200 remaining temples and stupas dating back to 850. The Bagsn Lodge is an oasis. The cottages dot a large area, some around the very large pool guarded by two golden elephants. The rooms are modern, well furnished and very comfortable. What a pleasant surprise. There is ample closet space, night tables, a desk, chairs and sofa and a very comfortable bed. The bath is modern with a large tub, a walk in shower and a separate area for the toilet. And, believe it or not, every amenity need from razors to dental kits, shower caps, soaps, shampoos, conditioner etc etc. One need not worry nor pack a robe and slippers as they are there for your use. Dinner was buffet style as was breakfast. Both adequate.

author: HanoiIG
title: Work In Progress
text: We heard that the Appletree Group had built this hotel and thought that Bagan was worth a third visit so we booked it. They provide free transfer from the airport. The setup is quite like other similar resorts in Bagan, Bali, Ninh Binh etc with open air reception area, a pool adjacent to reception together with restaurant and bar and guests housed in bungalows with two rooms to a building. The rooms connect so a family would be comfortable. Buffet breakfast was OK but not as varied as others we have enjoyed. The dinner was fine, as we ordered Myanmar specialties that were tasty and not expensive. Dining room staff is friendly and willing but not yet at A-level. Bar prices are quite reasonable and there is a two-for-one Happy Hour every night. The room was spacious and well equipped, and the bathroom had both tub and stall shower plus two sinks which is really a good thing. Both of the outings we arranged were professionally done and the horse cart and car both arrived right on time. Prices for these were quite cheap, compared to some we have had in the past. On our most recent previous visit to Bagan, we stayed at Aurem Palace which was somewhat nicer, though at a higher price. We used our time to relax and do minimal sightseeing but other guests seemed to spend most of the day out on excursions. The floor in our room had begun to buckle but it was otherwise in pretty good condition. My wife and I are much more city people than country so our view may be different from those who prefer resorts.

author: Ninimayo
title: Quiet hotel, some little improvements needed but overall excellent experience
text: The Bagan lodge is a quiet hotel, fairly remote location in Bagan, with some nice spacious rooms in lodges. The decor is nice. Everything is clean. The hotel is new so the garden is still developing. The pool is good size, clean - depends what you like but it is just near the hotel restaurant so no real pool privacy. However it always seems quiet which was very nice There is one restaurant - open air with nice food and good breakfast. The menu is fairly limited and a mix of international cuisine. Only a few local and asian dishes. It is overpriced but tastes good. Service is in general good although we had a couple of days where it can be very but very long and English is not always understood. For a place like Bagan and local standards - it is an excellent hotel, highly recommended. The spa is nicely built (expensive compared to others hotels we stayed in). The massages on offer are very limited - actually only one could be done out of the 4or5 possible. I have to say it was not the best I had and the facial was pretty bad. But hey ! Nothing to spoil the experience. The staff needs a little bit more training and practice. Big potential for the future

author: 888hamm
title: Simply Bliss
text: Bagan's three main areas are really coming on fast. And Bagan Lodge reflects that with chic standalone bungalows as your spacious and cool home. The entire resort is well done. Nice pool. Nice bar. Nice lobby. Staff are great and breakfast is also good. Located on the edge of New Bagan which I reckon is the best part of Bagan area. Quiet and within a five minute cycle of some really cool quiet and mostly abandoned pagodas and dirt tracks as your only guide. The hotel rents bikes and ebikes. There's an atm here as well. Some of the best lacquer shops are close by the Lodge as well. We stayed in Villa 56. Absolute bliss and although we did two full days of temple hopping. On the third day I just enjoyed the pool. We visited in the so called height of tourist season, New Year's Eve. But even so Bagan you can find quiet abandoned spots easily enough. E bikes are the way to go to cover the ground.

author: RoamingR0gue
title: Beautiful Retreat
text: The Bagan Lodge is a new-build lodge-style hotel, which means you stay in a separate lodge of your own, rather than a hotel complex. They're extremely large, very clean,beautifully appointed and quiet. Huge comfy beds, lovely pillows, and quiet - so that's really everything you need for a good nights sleep. The staff are fantastic, very helpful, attentive and welcoming. The food is excellent, the cocktails are great, and the pool is also lovely - especially at night. Now since this is Burma, and in particular, rural Burma you will experience power cuts, and the WiFi isn't great but this is the same everywhere in Burma - lets face it, if this is something you need to complain about then I'm afraid you're just going to have to suck it up. If you're well travelled you'll understand and not care anyway. Bagan is beautiful, and the people of Burma are wonderful people. You can hire an electric-moped at the hotel, but they won't let you hire a petrol engine as this is against Government regulations for tourists. Weirdly the locals are required to wear helmets by law, but tourists aren't! Another fabulous quirk of what is a fabulous country to travel in. If you're not used to being a bit outside you're comfort zone, you might not enjoy rural Burma, but back to the hotel. It's a lovely,clean, comfortable and quiet with good food and a lovely pool - oh and if you swim in it at night and the power goes off be sure to look up at the sky. The night sky out in Bagan is special. The Bagan Lodge is a fantastic hotel as well.

author: fun2travelCanberra
title: Long Walks to and from Reception
text: A modern hotel with its 82 rooms set in hectares of grounds. The lodge is so named because 2 adjoining rooms are set together throughout the grounds. A big drawback is the distance rooms are from reception. It is quite a hike: in the dark (take a torch) there are ground lights that tend to shine in guests eyes and so don’t help a lot; in the day time the walk is hot and humid. Staff in a golf buggy takes guests and their luggage to their rooms. The air conditioning worked okay (vital in Myanmar). No international phone calls can be made from a hotel room. If an international phone call is necessary, it must be made by going to reception and making the call from there. (Our mobile phones didn’t work in Myanmar.) Although the hotel’s dining room does have a roof, it is open air so there is no pleasant air conditioned dining, which is certainly needed when it is very hot and extremely humid. Also, the power in the room kept going off, only for short lengths each time but annoying just the same. There are no bedside tables on which to put things like a travel clock. There was a light on a shelf above the bed but that could only be reached by sitting up in bed. The lighting in the room was poor. Bottled water was ‘rationed’ to 1 bottle per room. I would definitely be staying elsewhere next time.

author: YYinMY
title: Fantastic hotel, great service but an very unfortunate incident
text: My friend and I had a wonderful time in Bagan Lodge. We stayed in the hotel for three nights ( 4th Oct- 7th Oct). It's far beyond our expectation: the hotel is wonderfully designed, room is spacious, modern and clean, each room has a small patio where you can lay in the chair and watch the sky at night. The location is okay, with an electric bicycle, old Bagan is only 15 mins ride away. Lovely pool and great breakfast, the most important thing is the staff is very friendly and helpful. In general, the hotel is very well managed. However, in the morning of our departure day, a very unfortunately thing happened--my friend left her bag and purse in the room when we had our breakfast as we thought Bagan is a safe place and it's okay to do so. But when we returned and about to give tips to the staff, we found around 400 USD and around 100,000 local currency (around 100 USD) was stolen! We paid for the electronic bikes the night before and didn't leave the room that night, so the only time my friend's bag was unattended was during the breakfast time. When reporting to the reception, they said it's the first time this kind of incident happened. After checking they said the only staff that went to our room that time was to check the mini-bar. They took our mobile and email address in case anything comes up after investigation. We genuinely hope we misplaced the money somewhere but we checked all our bags and luggage a and couldn't find it. We believe in this Buddhism country, a person must be desperate to do such a thing and if our money can help their family then let it help them. It's a great hotel but when you stay here next time, pls get your valuable things locked.

author: FrankCovey
title: Paradise in a rural setting
text: Stayed 3 nights at this wonderful hotel. Taxi from airport was approx $7 U.S. Hotel is brand new and everything is spotless. Rooms are located in 2 unit single storey dwellings. Rooms are very large with a sitting area, desk, 2 wardrobes, safe and mini bar as well as covered verandah with 2 wicker lounge chairs. Spacious bathroom with double sinks, tub and shower. Toiletries were replenished daily. Pool was spectacular with towels and lounge chairs provided. Poolside bar as well as lobby bar. Open air dining room overlooked the pool. Breakfast was not included in our room rate and was $15.00 person however it was buffet style with many western items. Dinner prices were more reasonable. Food was good. Spa was very good and reasonably priced, clean and had skilled therapists. Ms. Peerada, the spa manager was very helpful with local knowledge, friendly and her English was excellent. Front desk staff were accommodating and spoke reasonable English. Wifi was available in rooms however as with most of Myanmar (except Yangon) connectivity was spotty. if you are lucky and are up early, you will have an opportunity to see the Balloons over Bagan pass by the hotel.

author: MMHongKong
title: Quite a surprise!
text: The hotel is new (some units still being built). It is lodge style, with two rooms joined together. Perfect for families who need adjoining rooms. The rooms are spacious with a seating area, front porch complete w/ recliners and a large bath. Black out curtains ensure a good night's sleep and help keep out the heat. The staff is friendly and the front desk speaks very good English. Loved the spa - Great value for the money. Three 60 minute massages and a 60 minute foot massage - total bill (including s.c.) US$170. Happy hour - 5-7. 2 for 1 selected drinks. Not watered down like some places. Nice pool and seating area around the pool. On the other hand....the internet was slow and sometimes nonexistent. (Hotel or internet provider? Not sure) The food was so so. While we enjoyed breakfast but dinner was average. One of my complaints was the fruit - the melon and pineapple was hard, tasteless, not quite ripe.

author: pfkaa
title: Completely satisfied. Excellent hotel!
text: This hotel completely exceeded my expectations and was one of my top two favorite hotels in my latest trip to Asia. Two things stroke me the most: the rooms and staff. The rooms are huge, very tastefully decorated and with a lot of amenities. The bathroom was memorable and also gigantic. My favorite thing of all the room features was the 'rain' shower. The front desk staff was very attentive and welcoming. They helped to book a night bus ride to Yangon and also were friendly. The other thing that I loved about the hotel was the pool. It is very pretty and clean and very pleasing after a long day of temples and walking/cycling. Another good thing was that my booking didn't included breakfast and they didn't charge for it at checkout when I mention it. The only down sides are: (1) the property is a bit retired from the main sites, on the outer skirts of New Bagan. You can get to New Bagan by walking around 10-15 minutes or trying to get a ride in one of horse carts. If this place was more centrally located it would've been perfect. But even with its retired location there are some pretty secondary temples in front of the hotel. (2) The price is a bit high but I don't regret paying it and unfortunately most hotels in Bagan are overpriced so its price is not truly an outlier. I must also comment that when I stayed in the hotel has opened just two months before. I hope that the good conditions and attention to guests continue as is and this is not lost after the hotel gets more mature.

author: HarryB614
title: This must be the best hotel in Bagan, but the location can be awkward
text: We stayed for 5 nights. Positives: 1. The rooms/villas are very well designed and decorated, in addition to being large. 2. The service was of a very high standard with well trained hotel management professionals on duty all the time. We found all the staff spoke excellent English. Nothing was too much trouble and everything was done with a smile. 3. The open air design of the reception area restaurant around the swimming pool is attractive. Negatives: 1. The location is a good 15 minutes walk outside New Bagan. Taxis in Bagan seem to charge a lot of money relative to everywhere else. We thought we were being ripped off by them sometimes, as a result of which we found ourselves walking to and from the village too often. If you're not worried by greedy taxi drivers, this will not be a problem for you. 2. The blinds in our villa (No. 2) could not be raised without calling for a member of staff to do it, but this is just a teething problem for this new hotel.

author: russell898
title: Not the standard it should be.
text: This could/should be a class hotel but, only open for a few months, there are far too many teething problems. The major problem is Noise! The chalet style rooms are all linked to the chalet next door with interconnecting doors. But the connecting door is not sound insulated and too thin which results in the feeling you are sharing your accommodation with the people next door - which you are! If they have a conversation you hear every word and can join in; all their bodily functions are relayed to you and should they switch on the television then you must listen but without seeing the picture! We asked to be moved only to be told that they are all of the same design...why on earth? Because the chalets are spread out over a large area the maids and baggage staff have been provided with walkie/talkies and early in the morning you hear them chatting to reception. The designer ha! ha! has selected chic shades of dark seaweed green for the room decor but with insufficient lighting it is gloomy. No bedside tables are supplied - the room layout virtually forbids this - so you have to use the floor (or a ledge 18 inches above the bed) for glasses, books, clock etc. Sockets are in the wrong place and few hooks provided. The dining area is charmless and gloomy at night (I was provided with a torch to read my magazine). It feels like a canteen and desperately needs some plants/lanterns etc to cheer it up. Poolside loungers had no cushions and I wont mention the pungent septic tanks. I discussed all this with the charming manager who is well aware of the shortcomings and has requested an urgent meeting with the owner to tackle all these and other problems.

author: Trillyuk
title: Best hotel in Bagan
text: This hotel is very nice. Fantastic location , great room , very generous space inside , beautiful design , appropriate furniture. Impressive pool. Recently opened , you can see that they are doing a lot of effort to reach the 5 stars standard service. From my point of view , they should be focus on the service especially at the pool. Language is a lit a bit an issue. But with their smile and kindness you can enjoy your holiday for sure .The breakfast was very good. Thank you Valerio for your help . We were 7 and every day we had our table set for all of us with several different requests. They always did all the best to accommodate us. Thank thank you again and we'll come back one day. Last but not lest ...the spa. Very nice and peaceful. Thank you to all the therapists my friend and I we'll really appreciate the 2 hours treatment ... Ciao donatella

author: RickandGary
title: Beautiful Property with Great Potential in a crowded marketplace
text: Bagan is teaming with tourists so finding a 4 star property was next to impossible for our trip. Finally our operator was able to secure our rooms here. With only half the rooms built and only open for 2 1/2 months they are breaking in the local staff to provide the service this gem demands. And there are certainly bumps in the road. The property is gorgeous, the rooms are huge and comfortably appointed with a galley jack and jill bathroom that runs the length along the back of the room. Beds are very comfortable. International buffet breakfast was top notch. Infinity pool was perfect after a hot day of sightseeing. My rating could be so much higher but for the "new property pitfalls". Wake up calls that come when not asked for; shower handle not properly installed and falls off; the answer to everything is "yes" without consistent follow through; room had leftover cookies from previous guest and a note to those guests when we checked in; turn down service happens after 8:30pm so for us we never got it after first night. The list goes on. So if you are a persnickety traveler who demands perfection you may want to wait while they iron out the kinks. Expats from this company's other properties have been brought in to open this hotel and they are working day and night to teach the staff what needs to be done. They are the only hotel in Bagan with a computerized system for all aspects of service and teaching staff that have never worked a computer is a huge task. Also this property takes Visa and Mastercard so you can keep your cash if you want. Also a rarity in Myanmar. This property will get its act together and when they do it will be amazing. Would I stay here again... sure... they get a "A" for effort and a B-/C+ for execution.

author: Karlaleigh
title: Quite and peaceful paradise...
text: We had 4 nights at this hotel, the rooms are very spacious (pool side fale). There is a king size bed and two singles. We received a local juice which was a welcome refreshment when we arrived. If you are traveling as a couple my advise is sleep in the single beds unless you are used to sleeping on a plank of wood! The king size bed was so uncomfortable 😣 For the majority of the time we were the only people by the pool which was Amazing!! The food was a little on the Expensive side. Most of it was tasty especially the aranchini balls...yum a must try! There is nowhere else that we found to eat locally so we got a few bits a pieces from a local shop for our lunches. The breakfast which was included was just enough there were 3 choices on a menu which fir a 4 night stay was ok any longer and it would have got a little bit repetitive. There is also a choice of cooked at a price. The staff were very helpful when we were trying to organise A car for the day and infirmative about the local area. The local buses stop outside the hotel and cost 2.50 tala to the little town and market. You flag the bus down there are no bus stops, pay when you get off and tap a coin on the window if you want the bus to stop. Across the road where the beach is, is a long jetty where you can have dinner again at an extra cost. At night the lights under it show all of the lovely tropical fish 🐠. I got up early one morning to catch the sun rise this was beautiful!! and worth the early morning wake up! This was a very relaxing break...

author: Merri13
title: Fabulous staff
text: This is a lovely resort and the staff take it to the next level. Rooms are clean and beautifully presented. We stayed in a Family Poolside Villa. The room is split level with the King bed on higher level and 2 single beds on lower along with the lounge area. The bathroom was also 2 steps down so those with mobility problems could find this challenging. The outdoor rain shower was absolutely beautiful. The only thing missing were some draws or shelves in the cupboard to put belongings. The bed is built in and tile surrounded as is bedside 'tables', so no draws. We stayed 3 days in our month long holiday and really loved the feel of the place. Its beautifully presented and has the character you don't get from big chain resorts. We have 2 teens and had we stayed longer than 3 days we would have booked separate villas. The jetty and swim area across the road is a great spot to cool down if you prefer the ocean to the pool as we do. We saw some beautiful fish while snorkelling around the rocks at the base of the jetty. Food was great too. I especially loved the raw tuna 3 ways, Oka, Ika Mata and poke, yummo. We would definitely stay here again and highly recommend Amoa.

author: MaggieMax0426
title: Amoa Resort is the reason we WILL be coming back to Samoa!
text: Samoa is beautiful with magnificent landscape and wonderful people- a sacred treasure lost in time- Amoa resort captures this essence! It begins with a welcome pick up at Salelologa wharf, the driver Peter wears a warm smile as he escorts us to his van and starts our way towards the resort. Along the way he strikes up a lovely conversation and points out landmarks along the way. Recommend booking the wharf transfer they offer. As soon as we enter the clean tidy reception we are greeted with a sensational smile and welcome to Amoa by the awesome manager Elisabeth who gets us sorted at front desk with the help of Olivia and she has ice cold lemonade brought to us while we fill out paperwork. After this Joshua helps us to our room along with Elisabeth while she explains an event they are hosting for the local community encouraging climate change awareness at the jetty which we are welcome as hotel guests to the VIP area. This is the beginning of what was to be exceedingly excellent customer service everywhere in Amoa resort from everyone. Our room was absolutely stunning with traditional carvings on the post and handpicked fresh flowers on our bed and tables. The aircon was on full blast too! (we really needed that!) Tana was immaculate in presentation and ensured our dining experiences were unmatched. We recommend the jetty dinner complete with cocktails on arrival, beautiful leis and exclusive siva from the lovely Virginia. Breakfast was wonderful and even housekeeping and groundsmen were bright happy and acknowledging. The outdoor showers are solar powered and needless to say - refreshing! Amoa resort will keep a special place in our memories and can expect us back very soon! Highly recommended for first time visitors to Samoa

author: 380grahamj
title: Great spot for a wedding!
text: Our family group booked out the resort for a wedding. The accommodation was great. Food also. Staff were all very friendly. Lis and her staff took care of the wedding which took place on the pier which had just been built. The day started off with a large electrical storm but by the time of the wedding it had cleared up beautifully. Everything went exceptionally well. The reception was fantastic. All the facilities were top notch. Our rooms were spacious and very comfortable. The views over the water were really inviting. We enjoyed the outdoor shower. Our group included very young children, adults and some oldies. We all enjoyed ourselves there. When we were leaving Liz and all the staff lined up and sang us a Samoan farewell song. A nice touch. I would recommend this resort to everyone.

author: 169luciet
title: Amazingly Beautiful 😍
text: We came to savai'i for 3days and 2 nights... I am someone who likes to book everything in advance but my in - laws( who are samoan) said not to worry there will be heaps of places to chose from when we get there! Lucky I did listen to them and came across the breathtaking Amoa Resort... staff were incredibly helpful and found the best deal for our family of 8. The resort was very clean,comfortable and look amazing! And omg 😲 out door shower was awesome!!! My kids found out that the pool was opened 24hrs. This was the best news ever to them! They literally spent all the time they could in the pools. After breakfast and before and after dinner. Food at the resort restaurant was so yummy and delicious! We had complementary breakfast which was very enjoyable too... I really can't fault Amoa resort! We all had a wonderful and memorable stay! Thank you to all the staff at Amoa resort ❤️

author: KiwiMaz13
title: Wonderful, friendly staff.
text: My 12yr old son and spent spent 2 nights at Amoa (a night on our way to another resort, then a second night on our way back). Amoa's highlights are the staff, the food, the pool and the grounds. Our fale was by the road (but not too noisy). Clean, spacious, AC and we liked the quirkiness of the outside shower. Elizabeth and her team are really friendly and kind. We felt like treasured friends on our return stay. The first night was quite quiet as most other guests seemed to have cars and were exploring the island. By contrast, our 2nd night was really busy as a NSW rugby league team checked in at the same time as us. That evening (a Sunday) there was a buffet dinner with delicious local food. The staff and locals put on a really good cultural/dance show. We were really pleased as this was unexpected and we hadn't had the opportunity to see a cultural show at any of the other resorts we stayed at. We did venture across the road to snorkel. Clean, clear water but limited coral, fish life etc. The pool is a good size and has a swim up bar. The food here is typically pricey (it was the same as the other resorts) but it is of a high standard and really creative. Big thumbs up!

author: Natty2230
title: Excellent service
text: Wow where do I start, this hotel was absolutely amazing, what made it so perfect was the mosy extraordinary staff. I have travelled the world and have never ever experienced such genuine and wonderful service. We stayed at Amoa for one week, it was the most relaxing time. Travelling with our 9month old daughter, who is in a brace was difficult but nothing was too much for the staff here. Elisabeth was wonderful bringing in two of her own personal car seat for us to use and see what one our daughter would fit best in her brace. The staff also organised the most perfect suprise lunch on the jetty for my partner! If you stay here its a must surrounded by turquoise waters soaking up the view having the whole place to yourself. The beach out the front of the hotel was beautiful! Water was the perfect temperature and so clear. Food was good. Especially the bread and dips best bread I have ever eaten. The outdoor shower was pretty amazing. All the village walks and basket weaving, coconut show was amazing learning All the cultural ways at no extra charge. Every afternoon the staff would come and find us to see what our daughter would like made up for dinner(she ate around 5 so the would get it ready for her). The only one fault my partner had that didn't seem to bother me was the pillow where not 100%. We loved staying here and would highly recommend it to everyone. Thanks again Amoa team.

author: Dazza-R53
title: Glad we found it
text: We came across Amoa almost by accident on our way to another resort. We were so impressed that we came back a few days later and stayed 2 nights. The resort is not right on the beach but it is only across the road from a beautiful swimming spot. The rooms were very comfortable and spacious. They have a beautiful pool with swim up bar and waterfall which was very much appreciated with the weather being so hot. The food was especially good and it was nice to see a different menu with some variety after seeing virtually the same menu at every other place we visited. The owner's Italian background shows in the range of meals available. The staff were faultless. Nothing was too much trouble and their smiles and friendliness were obviously genuine. A special mention for the Manager, Elizabeth. From the time of our passing visit till the end of out trip she went out of her way to make us feel at home. She took us on a walk through th evillage and even invited us to lunch with her family in their Fala. Although the place wasn't overly busy she had a way of making you feel at home and nothing was too much trouble for her. We had left our booking of the ferry too late and it looked like we would get off Savaii in time for our next accommodation but Liz made a call and with the help of the owner Paul we managed to get on the ferry back to Upolu . We'll definitely go back when next in Smoa

author: jeanmaina
title: True Samoan Experience!
text: My husband and I recently spent four nights at Amoa Resort on Savaii and loved our time there. Elizabeth was so helpful in making sure that we had everything that we needed during our stay. She arranged optional activities for us, including a fishing trip, an island tour and a visit to a local church on Sunday. Her staff was attentive and extremely friendly, always greeting us with a smile. Service in the restaurant was very good and the food was delicious. The entire resort was spotlessly clean. Our room was large, quiet, air-conditioned and very tastefully decorated. We especially loved our beautiful outdoor garden shower. There is a beautiful beach just across the road from Amoa with crystal clear water for swimming or snorkelling. There was also a pool with a swim-up bar, but it was not operational when we were there. Maybe that was because the resort had been completely refurbished with its new Samoan decor and had just re-opened in August 2015. It was the atmosphere of Amoa Resort that especially impressed us -- from the layout of the resort to the décor, the appearance of the staff and the food. We felt like we were experiencing the real Samoa, rather than being at a resort that could have been on any South Pacific island. It's a special place! The fishing was our only disappointment as we did not catch a single fish of any kind after spending five hours of being on the boat despite the fact that we were trolling with 6 lines out at all times. Everything else about our stay was fantastic. We hope to get back soon!

author: nataliemN441QM
title: Five days in a tropical Paradise
text: We couldn't fault our stay at this wonderful resort and this was 100% due to the excellent service from all staff. It is obvious that a lot of effort goes into staff training. On our arrival we experienced a very warm welcome from Elizabeth and Beta and this set a high standard which continued for our whole 5 days. All the staff were friendly and very helpful, and nothing was too much trouble. This personal service made us feel very special. The food was delicious and of very high quality, and the restaurant staff were delightful. A special mention must go to Anna who was outstanding. Our poolside villa was quiet, spacious and very clean. The outside shower was a real bonus! Our villa was cleaned to perfection every day. A mention must also go to Warren Jopling a retired geologist who does very interesting natural study tours of the island. This was organised by Elizabeth. Thank you Elizabeth for running an excellent ship. The hard work you put in certainly shows! We have already been recommending this resort since our return home.

author: Credo505
title: Beautiful grounds and pool
text: We have just spent 6 nights at this resort. The beautiful gardens and the very clean and large pool area are a real plus. Our original bungalow had some shortcomings but we were upgraded for no additional price. It was clean,very roomy with king size bed, good air con and small fridge. There was a porch with table and chairs. Unfortunately there is no cable tv or Internet despite advertisements to the contrary. Admittedly the breakfast was basic but unlike a previous reviewer we did not experience any rotten or stale food. The lunch time sandwiches were deliciously fresh and there are no complaints about the quality of the lattes. Although the evening menu food was perfectly acceptable, it was limited, so we chose to eat at other resorts some nights. This meant going by taxi unless you were fortunate enough to get one of the few rental cars that are available on the island. We used the local buses during the day but they stop at 5.30.The restaurant and reception staff were polite and helpful when asked but were not proactive with suggestions for daily activities given that none of those listed in the room booklet were available. There was no attempt to link guests up to make a party to do anything local like a village tour. The standard response was that 2 people were not enough. We discovered other couples got the same response. We recommend checking out the options at Savai'i Travel before using the taxi drivers suggested by the Resort. We made friends with Umu, who owns a plantation behind the resort, and took us on a reasonably priced tour in his family taxi.Admittedly the beach is across the road and there are no chairs etc but we swam in the clear water,used the kayak and the snorkelling gear to see some beautifully coloured fish. We enjoyed our stay but had to work quite hard to make the transport options work and were disappointed that some of the expected facilities no longer operate. Having read some of the other reviews, people need to take into account that this is a Pacific Island so spiders, geckos and less than perfect beach access come with the territory.

author: sasa73
title: great pool
text: We have holidayed to Samoa 6 times but this was our first stay at Suifaga resort. We were really impressed with the pool, it’s huge and has a swim up bar, which we along with many of the other guests all made good use of! The rooms were nice, spacious, our room had a double bed and 2 singles, and also a lounge chair (although this was covered in plastic!), the rooms looked like the could use a bit of an update especially considering the prices per room we paid about $350 tala which included a basic tropical breakfast toast and fruit coffee/ tea. The rooms all had air con, fridge and tea and coffee facilities. The room was nice and clean and serviced daily. We ate a few times at the restaurant and the meals were a bit hit and miss, we had a pasta meal one day and out dish had about ½ cup oil in the bottom, we could not eat this dish. But then other time we had a pizza and this was nice. We have eaten here on previous visits to savaii ( while we stayed at another resort and the pasta used to be incredible, so we were disappointed with this). Another thing I found disappointing was the wine selection, they only had chardonnay! No sav Blanc! Very disappointing!! Considering most other places even small places had a better wine selection. The resort offered activities which we watched the coconut demonstration, this was $10 per person. The Beach across the road is small but gorgeous. The Staff were friendly and the resort grounds are nice. It was a very relaxing place to stay. Overall we enjoyed our stay at suifaga, and I think with just a few little changes this place would be really something special.

author: jessthefabulist
title: Wonderful
text: We had an awesome time at Siufaga. The rooms were beautiful and were spotless every day. They were spacious and felt like we were really some where magical. The cleaners did a fantastic job every day. Very impressed with the standard in which the rooms were kept. The pool was great. The pool bar was so convenient. Iosua and Taga made ordering drinks easy and they were reallllllly tasty too! However, the pool was filled with bugs and there was sand on the bottom of the pool. The restaurant wasn't too bad. There was a little bit of a language barrier but nothing we couldn't work around. The food took a while to come out but once it did it was delicious. The continental breakfast was great. The kayaking and snorkelling was amazing. The fish were beautiful and the reef provided great kayaking without too many waves. The beach was nice and clean and even had shade from the sun which was handy. The admin staff were awesome and everything went without a hitch. Overall, my stay was awesome and I'll definitely be back sometime.

author: bluegoldhighlander
title: Not luxurious but comfortable
text: We had a week at the Siufaga Beach Resort and found it very enjoyable. Our bungalow was spacious and comfortable. The outdoor shower is a fabulous treat. The bed was large comfy and there were not too many bugs in the room. The restaurant could use some improvement, although I do accept that it would be difficult to stay supplied in such an out of the way place. There were many items that the restaurant had run out of, including most of the wines. Seems there should be improvements in the ordering system or more storage for food and wine. The pool area was very nice. The pool was large and clean, with a lovely waterfall feature in the middle. There was a swim up bar that was not manned as often as one would like it to be, but it did serve frosty cold beer and nice drinks when someone was around. The staff are very friendly and helpful. We also had massages while we were there and they were very nice too. The beach across the road is small but nice. There are shops just down the road that can provide drinks and nibbles for you to keep in your room. The trip over from the main island is truly dreadful, on the most awful rust buckets that I had nightmare visions of the Tonga disaster running through my head the whole time. Someone from the upper level threw up over the side, which of course blew back in on all of us on the lower level. There are too many people crammed onto the ferry and too little seating. Samoa really needs to address this issue if they expect to draw tourists to them. All in all I would recommend this resort, it was very relaxing, friendly and comfortable and not too badly priced.

author: DaffyAKL
title: Shhh... don't tell anyone about this little secret
text: Savai'i is a well kept secret in the south pacific, and Siufaga Beach Resort one of the shining examples. The road through Faga beach is lovely, but you get no sense of the beauty of this resort, just a well-crafted sign, until you enter. The welcome is very warm; every one of the staff wants to know your name and welcome you as a friend. The rooms are wonderful, and set in a beautiful garden-like setting. Mine was on 3 levels, with a spacious living area, raised king-size bed and spotless bathroom. The piece de resistance is the outdoor shower. A high-walled enclosure filled with tropical plants, and shaded by banana palms. The floor is a beautiful turtle mosaic, topped by a generous 'monsoon' shower head. You will find yourself making excuses to shower! Central to the resort is a lovely pool, with swim-up bar. The staff here are mostly from local villages, and they take great pride in welcoming you. Management have taken bold initiatives in helping guests to become aware of Fa'a Samoa (the Samoan way of life) with many on and off-site activities at reasonable prices. You can visit local plantations, villages and cultural centres, without the usual pressure to buy stuff (though there are some great temptations). The resort owners are of Italian stock, so Parenzo's reataurant has a variety of pasta dishes, and pizza 3 nights a week. Otherwise the food is good, but fairly basic. Host Elizabeth is eagerly seeking feedback from patrons though with a view to lifting the standard. I recommend the sashimi. A local band entertains most nights with much enthusiasm and good humour. This is wonderful little secret holiday hide-out. Only tell your very best friends!

author: Laurie60
title: Fantastic Holiday
text: We have just returned from a wonderful 5 nights at Siufaga Beach Resort. We stayed in a standard bungalow which was great. Very clean and tidy. Staff were fantastic. Very friendly and genuine. Being a smaller resort, the attention from staff was more personal and individual . How often do you get a hug from the reception team when you leave!! Great pool complex set in a large garden complex. Bungalows were well spaced for privacy. There was a relaxed atmosphere as opposed to the usual bland standard style of resorts. Thoroughly enjoyed the village walk and trip to the local artist who’s artwork is on display around the resort. We also enjoyed one of Warren’s tours around the south coast. Restaurant was great. We enjoyed some of the best pizza’s ever. It was one of the best holidays we have had. We highly recommend it.

author: WellieAnnie
title: Beautiful Savaii, Beautiful Siufaga
text: We have just returned from a wonderful family holiday in Samoa. We were accompanied by our 15 year old daughter. After stayng on the mainland for a couple of nights we travelled across to the beautiful island of Savaii. We had been told that the ferry ride would be between 1 1/2 to 2hrs. Fortunately they have just put on a lovely new ferry, with airconditioning downstairs! The trip over took only 1 hr and it is another world. We had a hire car and travelled around to Siufaga Beach Resort. It took about 15mins from the ferry to the resort. We were greated on arrival by the staff and shown to our rooms. Gorgeous Poolside Villa ( not too close to pool for noise). The outside shower was fantastic! You stand outside and look up at the stars at night, just beautiful! The staff were wonderful and a special mention to the restaurant staff who are quick and efficient. The food was lovely pizza, pastas (as the owners are italian), as well as other selections. It is a small boutique Resort with wonderfully friendly staff. The pool was the biggest on the island and spotless! Elizabeth who was originally from Melbourne and has returned home to Samoa, takes visitors on tours of the villages and plantations, so we could see the real Samoa. If you are looking for a relaxing holiday in a delightful setting, this is the place for you! We will be back. Just remember, Samoa is on Samoan time, you need to relax, turn of the mobile, laptop and just be :)

author: Tomokinos
title: An exceptionally beautiful resort a true reflection of Samoan Hospitality
text: Wow, where do we begin, it was a true blessing that the original Hotel we were booked into, Jet Over double booked us, on arrival to Samoa I made contact with Jet Over and was told my room booking was no longer available, very disapoointing, upon this I had to search for other accommodation and fast. Upon finding Siufaga on Google, the resort looked amazing, so I booked my family in. Upon arrival to the resort, we were truly blown away at the landscaping of this heaven as well as the friendly smiles we were greeted with on arrival. From the Cleaner to the front desk ladies to the man sand papering the resort chairs, the atmosphere was calming & we truly felt we were on holiday the moment we walked through the tropical pathway leading to our Pool Side Villa. Although it may sound costly, its not until you experience it that you realise that what they charge is well below what they deserve. We have travelled to Savaii many times, and never expect 5 Star treatment, however Siufaga Beach resort, Staff and Resort, have changed that mentality for us. You pay for good service and you get that the minute you walk in. Elizabeth and Maria at reception are wonderful hosts, to Peta, Sefo, & Iosua (and all staff there) really will make your stay a memorable one. My kids loved the French Toast and lived in the pool. Highly recommend this resort to anyone travelling. We willc ertainly be back as we travel at least 2-3 times a year to Savaii for family gatherings, although our village is 1 hour away from Siufaga, we will continue to make to journey each day to soak in the warm hospitality of this Resort & its staff. Even other guests that were there, were people that had returned. We will now join this long list of returning travellers wanting to share in this wonderful experience. Highly recommended to all. It suits all types of Budgets, we extended out stay for a further 5 nights not wanting to come home. They deserve to named Savaii's number 1 resort 2010, I am the worst critic for Customer Service, and I must say, the team here were exceptionally Professional showing the true hospitable nature of all Samoan people.

author: Hazeyboy94
title: Relaxing & wonderful stay!
text: Always a great time here with the beautiful beach, friendly staff, great food & a superb pool & surrounding area. Would highly recommend to everyone. What's sad is all the negative comments written regarding this resort. I've lived in Samoa, Australia & live in NZ now so i know what to expect from all three countries. For a start, people have to realize that certain food isn't as accessible in Samoa as NZ or Aussie. E.g. Fresh veges etc. The prices in the market or food in general in Samoa are rising all the time causing people to raise prices on there menus just to break even or to just make a living. The locals because of living on a tropical island are obviously laid back & cruise. That explains their disappearing act at times from reception or other areas. Mind you, looking at the average wage workers in Samoa make, it's no wonder they cruize. How would you like to work your butt off for around $5 or less an hour?? You wouldn't even get out of bed!! So chill out on your negative feedback & understand the facts before ruining the good reputation of one of the best resorts in Samoa. The prices might seem excessive, but they are in Samoan Tala & that is nothing to the NZ or Aussie dollar. My chicken & chips & salad or (steamed veges) was 20 tala. Thats around $10 NZ. I couldn't get that at a restaurant in NZ for $10!! Loved my stay, loved the people & would go back anytime!

author: JoMillerAustralia
title: Good room, bad food
text: We ended up at Siufaga after being bumped from Le Vasa. We had no idea what we were in for but were pleasantly surprised by the rooms. They were huge with a modern bathroom and outdoor rock shower (which was great!). They were air conditioned, had a TV and fridge and were cleaned every day. The only problem was the food. Every day, at least four or five dishes were unavailable on the menu and when you are eating at the same restaurant for breakfast, lunch and dinner, you need some variety. The menu was very basic and most of the food was deep fried (ie frozen). We spent a lot of time on the toilet. Unfortunately there is really nowhere else to eat so you are stuck for choice. Luckily there is a shop up the road (across from the hospital) which stocks all the basics (and has some great ice cream cones). We bought our lunch supplies from here. There is a small beach across the road which you can only lie on at low tide. There are rocks in the water and it is a bit choppy, so not really good for swimming. The resort has a good pool. Hire a car but organise this before you arrive as there are only two companies and they only have six cars each. The blowholes and waterfall are worth seeing. But that is about it. There isn't much to do on this island. Especially if it rains.

author: zeroque
title: It's OK.
text: Like a few of the other recent holiday makers we found the place reasonable but lacking in some departments. On the up-side, the pool was great and the beach across the road was very nice. The staff were friendly. The rooms (beachfront deluxe bungalows) were good, fairly spacious and nicely appointed. The aircon worked well and the room had a nice outlook onto the pool from the front and the lagoon from the back. The TV didn't really have many recievable channels and the showers were very average in their temperature. But good pressure. My wife found them too cold and I found them marginal. From what I could tell they run solely on solar heating so if the sun is behind the clouds for most of the day like it was on a couple of days we were there then you get just a luke warm shower. It seems the reception is only sporadically attended by staff but whenever we wanted to speak with someone there was someone in the restaurant above the reception who could help. I thought the worst part of the resort was the restaurant. In Samoa it seems traditional that most places supply breakfast. I would have thought that a place costing as much as Siufaga (I think we paid about ST$450 per night which is about NZ$300) would put on a really super breakfast however it was the worst out of the three places we stayed. I also do not think the resort is worth the money overall when compared with other places we stayed. We tried the restaurant one evening for dinner and again found the food average for the price. We then went down the road to the Saviian Hotel, paid almost half the price and got really, really tasty food. It has potential but they need to sort out the restaurant and charge less for everything.

author: TinaAuckland
title: All it needs is a bit of effort from staff and management!
text: Pretty garden setting, well looked after gardens. Rooms had an ocean view if you looked out the back window! Why on earth didn’t they build the decks on the Ocean side of the bungalows! Beach pretty average and covered in rubbish and rocks. Much good be done by the management to make the beach more accessible, as to reach a good swimming spot on this beach you would have to climb over slippy and sometimes feet damaging rocks. (Not so good for the older guests). If as much attention was paid to the beach as there is to the gardens then it would make a tremendous difference. Bland flavourless food, menu lacking variety, cooked by a chef that obviously doesn’t taste the food or just doesn’t care. Mr Parenzo needs to get back in the kitchen to retrain the staff. The food was a running joke among guests. We were forced to self cater or travel into town, just to get a taste sensation. Staff ranged from very helpful(thanks Misi) to down right lazy (Barry). Pool bar was nice but bar closed & unmanned for first 3 days of visit. The cocktails sometimes seemed to be missing one or two ingredients. I do recommend the Lagoon Breeze, very tasty!

author: 321simons
title: Good but needs a tidy up.
text: We stayed here in the 3rd week of October. All the staff are amazing which make your stay here all the better. However some areas need improving. The door from the pool to the hotel reminds me of a service entrance. Some potted plants would make it a bit more welcoming. Many people have commented on the corridors and I agree. They look so plain and the fire doors have been bashed by the cleaners trolleys. There are only 2 lifts which can carry about 6 people so can take an age to arrive. We saw lifts of people waiting especially outside the dining room. We took the stairs which were dark and uninviting. They had timed light switches which you had to switch on. Sensors would be an improvement here. They are the only negatives. The room was lovely and cleaned every day. The bar area had a great atmosphere was subdued lighting and the entertainment wasn't too loud. Great service from the staff; you never had an empty glass. The pool was a good size and there were plenty of sun lounges.

author: 385stephent
title: Staff great, shame about the actual hotel
text: We returned from this hotel on the 28th Oct having had a week in the sun. On arrival this hotel doesn't have a welcoming look. The main entrance looks to have more in common with a hospital and there certainly wasn't a "Wow, this looks good" feeling. The reception staff, along with all other staff are friendly and welcoming and did their best to make sure you enjoy the stay. Our room (209) was light and airy and although the bathroom was a little on the small side, it served its purpose. However, the corridors of the hotel, all painted white most of which were bashed about and in need of redecoration coupled with the dated blue carpet, were more reminiscent of a 1970's office block rather than a supposedly 4 star hotel. The food was good with a wide variety of choices and again the restaurant staff always greeted us with a handshake and led you to our table. The grounds of the hotel, in our opinion, were in drastic need of some care and attention. The large grassed area resembled a worn out football pitch, the ground was uneven and vast areas were devoid of any grass and what grass there was obviously had not been cut for several weeks. The hotel is located on the waters edge but the beach immediately outside is not suitable for sunbeds as it is only a few feet in depth and surrounded by very slippery rocks. There is a nearby beach only a couple of minutes walk from the hotel but this is a Public Beach and you have to pay for Sunbeds. We had booked a 'Partial Seaview' room and on arrival we wondered why we had bothered. Our partial view was across the hotel car park. We roughly calculated that there were around 18-20 rooms in the hotel which had no view of the sea, the remainder would either have a full or partial sea view, therefore, if we decided to go again to this hotel, we would take a chance on being allocated a sea view room on arrival rather than pay £60-70 when booking. We stayed on an 'All Inclusive' package so everything was catered for. For quests on other deals there is very little directly outside the hotel, one Pub/restaurant and a couple of supermarkets. All other eateries are a short cab ride away. This was our 2nd trip to a Sensimar Atlantica in Cyprus since July this year and from both experiences we have decided that we will not be returning to Cyprus again. We have stayed in several others in and around the Greek Islands and they honestly leave those in Cyprus in the shade, this hotel and the other we have visited simply do not come up to the true standard. If it had not been for the staff and the fact that we had only booked a week, we would almost certainly have asked to be moved to another hotel.

author: CalvW1974
title: Fantastic holiday!
text: We stayed here for only a week but wished we had booked for 2. Having been on all inclusive holidays quite a few times now, this was the first adults only hotel we have been in and what a difference that made. Everyone was so chilled and relaxed. The hotel and the facilities were brilliant - we had a top floor room with a sea view, large balcony and a hot tub. It was a nice touch leaving us a bottle of champagne in our room on our arrival. The staff were very friendly and always helpful. Always plenty of sun loungers around, despite a minority getting up early to reserve them! (tip to hotel management - enforce your own policy of not reserving sun loungers). The local towns were a short bus ride away, costing 1.50 each way and a very regular service running 22hrs a day, so perfect for the party animals who want to go to local clubs. The food was great, always a wide enough choice. If i was being a bit picky, some of the evening entertainment could have been better - one evening we had a young lad with an electric acoustic guitar who was brilliant but only had a 45 min set. This was followed by a brilliant fire show. However, "Rod Steward" came on and he was terrible. The following night a Bon Jovi tribute was playing, who didn't do any Bon Jovi, until a track was requested as part of his encore. I can't really blame the hotel for the above but like I said, i am being picky. All in all, a great relaxing holiday.

author: fozy67
title: We enjoyed it
text: Overall some aspects of the hotel need an update which I belive they are doing this closed season. But on the whole a very enjoyable holiday made by the hard working staff. Rooms. Clean and well looked after every day by the cleaning staff. Negative don't see why you need a bath in a hotel these days a better shower would have been better ( room 411). Pool. A little cold.... The sea was warmer. But plenty of beds available. Restaurant. No complaints here... If people complain they are fussy, so much on offer. Bars. Pool bar and service excellent although they may need a few more staff as 2 is not enough to serve all those guests on sunbeds the two on worked really hard and done a great job. Top bar. Brilliant staff fantastic with amazing views, entertainment OK seen better. Summed up We were on the 4 floor looking west with a partial sea view, only complaint is service slip road for goods below could hear truck reversing beeps early most mornings, must have been worse lower down. Overall a great holiday with not many moans

author: JulieF206
title: Nice holiday
text: On the last day of my holiday and thought I'd give it a little review. Starting with the positives. Hotel situated next to a beautiful cove with lovely snorkelling which I adore. You can hire a sun lounger here but I was a little put off my the loud music so stayed in the garden of the hotel. Plenty of sun beds available at the hotel with a nice pool. The activities looked good. Our room was clean and pleasant but in hindsight it would have been worth upgrading to a sea view room. Ours was on the side of the hotel where the bin lorries wake you ( 6am) and staff also wake you talking loudly at 6.45 am. Apart from this the staff are fantastic, polite and hardworking. Cleaners were top notch. The pool bar staff come round offering water and ice creams which is a lovely touch. On the whole the food was nice but main course at dinner slightly boring. The al la carte meal was delicious and well worth a second visit. Had the best massage I've ever had in the spa. Location is nice but not a lot to do in the location. Plenty of trips on offer though. Will certainly visit beautiful Cyprus again but at another hotel a little closer to restaurants to enjoy a larger choice of Cypriot food.

author: GrandadandPat
title: Fantastic stress free week
text: Visited the sea breeze for a week from 29th September, had a wonderful time. We were delayed 2 hours so did not arrive until almost midnight, there were drinks and sandwiches and juice, water and two packs of sandwiches for us in the room. Safe and fridge free. The hotel is spotless and welcoming. Room spacious with plenty of room for clothes, cleaned and towels replaced as we requested. Great pool, as its adults only plenty of room to cool down, aqua aerobics, volleyball and inflatable, balls etc to use. Outside bar, at 10am Mark comes round with bottles of water, later mini ice creams, always checking if people wanted more from th bar, he never stopped. Whoever chooses the staff for the hotel needs a medal, they are helpful, friendly and always smiling. Food is good, even the most fussy eater is catered for, went to the restaurant and had stuffed mushrooms and fillet steak, fantastic. This is the second time we have been there and unfortunately the deserts have improved (was a little greedy,on a diet now). Two mins walk away is the most beautiful cove ever. Everything is there, novels, playing cards, quiz, different entertainment every night and even walking groups. On the way home we didn't leave until 5pm and forgot to ask to keep our room but they kindly held onto our luggage and allowed us to use a room to shower and change so we could make the most of our last day. Can't think of any negative comments at all. Would recommend this hotel.

author: bexiccle
title: Not what were used to, not what I expected
text: This hotel just isn't what I'm used to with 4* I am used to several food stations, 24 hour all inclusive, actual swim up bars, being on an actual beach, as many drinks as you like, unlimited towel replacements, people taking cups away pool side constantly, several restaurants and lots of activities to do. This place is selective drinks (orange juice not included except for breakfast), 1 cooking station with a salad bar, food during certain times unless you want a sad, sorry looking fruit salad from the bar, a bar at the pool but water so shallow it definitely isn't swim up, beach is down another path, directly outside the hotel is a pathway and rock, only selective drinks available on all inclusive, 1 restaurant and 1 a la carte (really not special either), I had my cups taken once poolside then the rest of the week I had to take them back, I watched plenty of people having drinks bought to them, not once was I ever asked if I'd like a drink. However this maybe down to the fact I am in my 20's and most people seemed to be 45+ maybe they deserve better treatment then other people paying the same price? no entertainment or activities available, and no one going round letting people know what was going to start and where. Rooms too small. Paid for a superior Jacuzzi room, absolutely nothing superior about it at all could hardly for 2 suitcases in it and move. However lovely laundry room by the spa!! Gents have to wear trousers at evening meal, why? It's a buffet! Towels can only be replaced 3 times in 7 days even if your in a Jacuzzi room!!! Night entertainment poor, one night a man was doing Bobby Marley, ermmm isn't it Bob Marley?? Overall, very expensive for what it is! Never going to a sensimar or atlantica again sorry. Ripped bedding all week too that just kept getting covered up with the purple fabric strip at the bottom of the bed. Not what u expect after paying the sort of cash for here! But not going to argue with staff. They are the only reason this hotel does well. Lovely staff and so so helpful!

author: Purple259
title: Quiet peaceful hotel
text: Had a relaxing time spent at this hotel. Very clean and comfortable. Interiors fresh and new looking. Staff very welcoming and accommodating. Had a sea view room which had amazing views looking across the pool/ sea and coast. Rooms kept spotlessly clean and very comfortable beds... didn’t want to get out of it! Food is good although it can be monotonous and depends on the type of evening dictates the culinary outcome. Had an amazing spa treatment although a little expensive. Entertainment was low key.. mainly quizzes then a singer or group. The bar closes around midnight which maybe enough for some! All this is classed as a four star hotel I’m bewildered why in this day of age you still have to place your toilet paper in a bin and not flush it away. Yes I know it may sound trivial to some but .... I’m sure not all hotels on Cyprus have the same problem.?

author: Chocnibbler
title: Very very nice hotel
text: Just stayed at the Atlantic’s seabreeze near Protaras Had a fabulous holiday. Rooms are cleaned every day, very comfortable beds. Only down side, we were above the service road, so had noisy lorries. But nothing to worry about. Food is excellent, good choices and plenty to tempt you. Service was excellent and very friendly. Cannot praise the catering team enough. They work very hard with a smile all day long. Entertainment in the evenings was good and varied. Every day they bring round a poolside puzzler to keep your brain ticking over. Like that touch never had that before. Liked the location from the beach, only down side is there aren’t many shops near the hotel. But directly outside is the bus stop which comes every 10-15 mins. Had a most enjoyable and relaxing holiday. Thank you seabreeze Special Mention to Spiros for bringing us drinks everyday to our sun beds. You were a star. Always had a smile and nothing was to much trouble.

author: ridley2015
title: The jewel in the crown of this hotel are the staff
text: This is a very solid, four star European holiday hotel. It is not favoured by being in the prettiest of locations but the staff, service and food are its great strengths. The hotel is roughly rectangular in shape, with one side facing west and the other side facing east. The best views are the sea view rooms which are north-east facing. The westerly facing rooms get sun all morning, whereas the easterly ones have sun all afternoon. Both sides of the hotel receive a fair amount of traffic, delivering either guests or goods to the hotel Without doubt the higher floors have an advantage and the best views. We had a Junior Suite (Room 434) on the top floor which was excellent, with a spacious bedroom, large sitting room, and a jacuzzi deck. The servicing of the room was excellent, we thought the maid was fantastic and always cleaned our room when we were out. The food was very good, lots of choice and we were fortunate enough to be able to eat outside on the terrace beside the pool, which we really enjoyed. There was always plenty of availability in the indoor dining room which some guests preferred, as it is air conditioned. Pre/post dinner drinks could be enjoyed on the outside bar terrace upstairs which overlooked the swimming pool and had good coastal views, but again, those who preferred the air conditioning, could use the adjacent bar/lounge area, which was well appointed. There were those guests who got up at 6am to place their towels on the very large sunbeds round the pool but there were plenty of very comfortable sunbeds on the grassed area and the breeze was stronger the closer you got to the coastline, which some guests preferred. So plenty of choice for all. There is a small public beach to the right of the hotel, which was very pleasant and safe for swimming, as an alternative to the pool. Chairside service from the pool bar was excellent with water being distributed every morning, plus fruit and regular visits by staff to take drink orders if you were reluctant to walk the ten steps to the bar! It is difficult to single out individual members of staff by name, because of the high standard of all, but just a thank you to the staff that we came into most contact with who were Maureen and Wills, Janice and Simon, Joanna, Johnny from the bar, George from the restaurant and Krista from the entertainment team who offered a wide range of keep fit activities. I particularly enjoyed the daily aqua aerobic sessions.

author: rexyworksop
title: Good holiday but hotel not for me
text: We have stayed in quite a few sensimar hotels and this has to be the most expensive one but sadly the weakest one we have stayed in. We booked in for 11 nights also our first visit to Cyprus. We arrived at the hotel late at night and the reception area was very nice, check in was quick given a welcome drink and told there was sandwiches in our room. When we got to our room there was a bottle of fizz waiting for us as we had just celebrated our 25th anniversary nice touch, but the hotel porter checked our fridge no sandwiches or drinks he apologised and went to get us some. Rooms are good but the bathrooms could do with a revamp very narrow bath with a tap fed shower,free safe ,kettle tea and coffee. Would have been good to have cans off drinks in your fridge as we had in other hotels. The hotel corridors remind me of an office block.The food in the restaurant was good but sometimes cold as was the plates. Would have been nice to be offered tea or coffee at breakfast time help yourself from a Nescafé machine. We visited the al a carte food was better in there and hot. The pool area was small with sun beds on a grassy area not nice waking on and being covered in bugs when trying to sunbathe Saw people spraying repellent to keep the bugs off. Pool service hit and miss with drinks, bottles of water or fruit . The pool could get very noisy especially when they had a pool party. The toilets need revamping as well broken tiles on floor and grubby no alcohol gel provided should have them outside the toilets only saw 1 in the restaurant. Service in the bar at night was ok but would be a good idea to put little bowls of nuts or crisps out every night on tables. Got offered them on our very last night really that was because the owner of the hotel was there. We had a good holiday with the help of some lovely people we met. We never met or saw the concept manager either walk around talk to your guests find out how there holiday is going. Would I return or recommend it sadly no don’t quite think it’s a good sensimar hotel

author: 348birgittas
title: Joyful holiday with a lot of touchy monments
text: We spent 12 days at the Sea Breeze Ressort and we met enjoyed really. Our room was just perfect, the whole facility was nice and we always had a perfect place to enjoy an exceptional sea view. The sport program, let be Kristin was just great. Yoga, functional training - all very good and mostly private lessons! Awesome and a big thank to Kristina. Love to have you here! The pool service - well, it was more than just pool service an Spyros did such a great job. I really don’t know how we managed to bring every time the right things! Thanks Spyros - you made every day a perfect job. The buffet - yes, all inclusive was a good choice - was great. All day we enjoyed various dishes, excellent salads and a lot of variations. High quality as always fresh. The most exciting people however are Maureen and Mark! Both made every day an exceptional job. If we ever come back - I hope both of them are still there. We had the feeling of meeting good friends and even at the not so nice moments of our holidays - when my partner fall down a rock and need to stay at the hospital - Maureen and Mark gave me the feeling have “not being alone”. Thanks for that. I also like to mention Katarina at the reception you helped me going through a painful night waiting to get good news from hospital. This place is just great. Many thanks to all making my holidays a good memory.

author: diverdaisy2018
text: I have never written a review before but felt the need to put a few things straight after reading some reviews on Here! It makes me wonder if I am at the same hotel. I cannot praise this hotel enough. Some one has said that Mark from the pool bar was rude and arrogant ( take a look at yourselves my fellow guests!!) and has his favourites. This cannot be further from the truth. That man is the best thing that has happened to this hotel in years. He runs around that bar like a man possessed to make sure everyone has what they need. And I mean everyone!!!!!!! Most of the staff are friendly and attentive. Yes you can see the lazy ones especially the girl at the pool bar(Vikki) but you will get that wherever you are. Some people treat these hard working individuals as their slaves. Another member of staff that stands out is Maureen who takes care of the outside eating area. She is efficient, friendly, always has a smile for everyone and makes sure the service there is second to none. You can tell when she has a day off! The bathrooms are adequate but may need walk in showers as some quests are elderly and find this difficult. Maybe a revamp is needed now but still very comfortable. Rooms have been redone though. The food is always plentiful and presented well and great selection for every meal. Very peaceful as away from main town but that's what it says in all the literature and what we like. I have stayed here for many years and will return again next year for our 14th visit and look forward to seeing everyone again.

author: FairyGlen74
title: 50th Birthday Celebration
text: We stayed here as a group of 9 of us ages ranging from 16 to 82 years old celebrating my husband’s 50th birthday. Food was fantastic at breakfast, lunch & dinner - lots of variety and some amazing salads! Stavros made sure we had our table reserved at every meal as we were a large group. He also went out of his way to make sure our visit to the a la Carte restaurant was most enjoyable. The pool area is very nice with very comfortable sun beds. Bar service around the sun beds is a bit hit and miss - Staff don’t ask everyone if they would like a drink. Bar staff at pool bar are very friendly and hard working. Pool was very warm. Entertainment during the day we found to be a bit boring. The aqua aerobics is very serious. Entertainment in evening was not always good. However we really enjoyed the blues brothers and we will rock you evenings - just a shame as most evenings we found that we had missed some of the entertainment while still having our dinner. Maybe the entertainment could start after 9pm when dinner has finished? Rooms are pleasant but not that large. Balcony quite small. We paid extra for a side sea view and 2 people in our group had a better view than us even though they didn’t pay for the upgrade. Hotel is a taxi ride away from Protaras approximately 5 minutes. We also took a taxi into Ayia Napa one evening - approximately 10-15 minutes.

author: donnacD5050OU
title: Top Holiday
text: This is our 4th visit to the Sea Breeze and still not disappointed. On arrival we checked in and went to room, but was disappointed as in a corner very much on top of other guests/overlooked, so off to reception to ask to be moved, we were informed by the staff that they were unable to do anything at the time as the Manager was not in, but would let her know in the morning and to come back by 10, which we did and to our delight they said they could move us later in the morning after guests checked out. This made our stay and couldn't be more thankful for the staff and their understanding. We could now unpack and relax. The rooms were as we previously seen no change, but always clean and spotless. The only let down was that the hairdryer was obviously meant to be attached to a wall and was in a holder (combined shaver) and so you could not detach it and so the unit would swing around and knock into you. Investment required to update these in rooms affected. Fresh water left in room everyday. Food excellent and improved on previous visit, which was never bad anyway, just better breakfast. Entertainment better than before. Quizzes were a laugh as Google came out and same couple always winning! Bar staff are what makes us come back, a huge shout out to Demis, Christos and John whose customers service makes us feel special, ensuring we were looked after as they do with all guests. We would like management to thank those specific staff members as a sign of our appreciation for what they do and how they made us feel. Sunbeds taken by pool early doors, which didn't bother us as you feel on top of each other, but plenty of beds on the grass area which is perfect as a bit breezier but more space. Pool bar/Garden bar staff excellent. The pool is perfect temperature all day. If you wish to go out and about, the bus is at the end of the drive and only 1.50 euro for a single journey. Or taxis are affordable and quick. We have nothing but happy memories of the Sea Breeze and its staff who are all friendly and accommodating.

author: tracyd568
title: Relaxing holiday
text: Had a relaxing week here mid August. Our room on the 3rd floor had a lovely sea view and pool view however the balcony was very small so never really sat out, not sure if it was worth paying extra for to be honest. Breakfast was ok but bacon and sausages were awful but plenty of egg choices, beans etc, fresh fruit, yoghurt, meat and cheeses. We quite enjoyed the lunch menu lovely salads, plenty of other dishes in fact we enjoyed this better than the evening meal. We usually love fish but was disappointed with the fish choice which tasted like cheap frozen fish to me. The snack bar which you ordered fresh from was nice and was pleasantly surprised. I wasn't that impressed with Al a carte and overall had better food at other sensimar hotel's we have stayed at. I can say the wine and local beer was nice however some of the cocktails wernt as good as others as some were straight from the bottle rather than freshly made. The evening entertainment was hit and miss some good some bad but each to their own. Sunbeds the the most comfortable I've ever laid on however the cleaning underneath wasn't good. The staff I've got to say were wonderful especially Maureen and her husband Will who are British and were always friendly and had time to chat. There was only one male pool bar staff who was a bit miserable. We enjoyed the pool which was lovely to cool down in and always plenty going on with aerobics water polo and the pool party was good. We had a lovely couples massage/ Indian head massage which I highly recommend and had a nail polish which was good. We normally like to keep fit but the gym was disappointing very small not much equipment so didn't really bother with it. Overall it was a pleasant holiday, we met some great friends which made our holiday and had such a laugh with but I'm not sure we would return.

author: Jenbabes81
title: Clean, great food and service!
text: This hotel is really quite lovely! It is so clean and bright! The pool and surroundings are relaxing and sun beds are plentiful with lovely cushioned backs so you can really relax. The food has been a delight; yes towards the end there were some similarities but no different to being at home! There was always a variety of salads, meats and fish dishes and some local dishes as well as British favourites. The food is fresh and topped up throughout the service times.
