She was full of endless advice and knows every restaurant owner on the island, which helps you get good deals! We stayed in a chalet out the back amongst beautiful gardens. We stayed for 4 nights, which was never enough on this brilliant island. In the mornings we'd have a nice breakfast on the terrace, where humming birds would come to drink at the water feeders. Aratinga is the name of a type of parrot that you can hear singing in the morning as you have your breakfast. In the evenings we would make ourselves a Caipirinha and chill out in the garden before going out for dinner. One of the many delights of the Aratinga is afternoon tea which comes included. Perfect to come back to after a day of surfing/lazing on the beach or trekking in the forests all day. Cakes, scones, biscuits, coffee and tea were laid out. Such a nice touch. The chalet room with en suite was always clean and tidy. One night, while in our chalet, we heard the local monkeys having a run around on the roof, which was funny. I have to say the Aratinga Inn was the perfect place for us to stay on Isla Grande.

author: Guido_Garcia
title: The perfect stay in a perfect place
text: Since I made the reservation for the room, I knew I had made the right choice. I have never seen a hotel/pousada with such a good reputation, and after I stayed at Aratinga, I could to see why. Rennie, the owner of the pousada, receives you as if you were a host in her own house, and makes it perfect to make you feel at home. She gives every guest directions, opinions, and even lends you any kind of things you might need for every day! (towels, umbrellas, surf boards, sailclothes, hiking sticks, and even a collection of over 600 dvds, invaluable for a rainy day!). She even wrote a "book" with all her tips for excursions, hiking trails, restaurants, bars, etc. I spoke to other people who were staying in other pousadas, and couldn´t believe we received an afternoon tea every evening. Before I travelled, I couldn´t find this service very usefull, but believe me that once you are returning from each excursion, all you are looking forward is for those tasty juices and those humid and soft cakes (I have never had such wonderful cakes ever!). During our stay, it was my girlfriend´s birthday, and Rennie got us a cake with her name on it, and got all the pousada guests to call her the happy birthday. Rennie was the main accomplice to give my girlfriend what was for her, the best birthday of her life. We stayed in 2 different type of chalet. Although one of them was a little big bigger and newer than the other one, both were perfectly cleaned up every day, and with much more of the essential things you will ever need. It is located not at the very center of the villa, but I saw this as a good thing. It is just a 2 minute walk, and you get far enought to avoid all the noises, and smells of each restaurant. The staff is very friendly and helpful. I could actually keep on going writing much more things, but it would take me forever. But trust me, this is your best option. It totally worths it. I had the luck to travel in many times, and stayed in the greathotels, and I have never felt more at home like in Aratinga.

author: M1075th
title: Our favorite place in whole Brazil!!!
text: We have just stayed at this beautiful place. From the very beginning, even just through email correspondance, we were very excited about meeting Rennie, the owner of this paradise. She seemed so lovely, warm, informative and helpful. And when we met her... She really was All that. And her place is a paradise. We have been traveling for almost a month now and this is by far our favorite place! The Rooms are personaly and cute, the flowers, plants and humming birds in the garden, made you relax and enjoy that you are on a tropical Island. When arriving you will recieve an "all you need to know" book, so nice, informative and helpful. The breakfast and the free afternoon tea and cake is lovely and nice to chat with Rennie and the other guests. Unfortunately we were sick when we arrived, but Rennie took so good care of us and looked after us like a mum:) we felt at home and safe and really didnt want to leave. Rennie is a cool, clever, strong and loving woman from Australia. We Will always be her thankful for everything she did for us. We miss her, her two lovely cats and Aratinga Inn already. Can not recommend this place enough!!!

author: BuenosAiresGer
title: PERFECT AND MORE!
text: After a brief search, I decided to go to Aratinga. And it was simply the best. Reenie is a wonderful host. She is very kind and helpful with all you need. The place is very beautiful, close to everything, and at the same time, away from noise. You feel in the middle of the jungle, but surrounded by beautiful details. The cabin was very clean, new, and comfortable. It has a private terrace for you. The breakfast is all what you need and more, and after beach, a perfect coffee with cakes and juice will be waiting for you. Also the staff is very kind and helpful. Reenie recommended some restaurants and trips. So, if you plan to go to Ilha, trust me. Go here, you sure will be happy. I saw other Pousadas that appeared to be nice, but were not located in good spots. This is the perfect stay for sure.

author: oakley75
title: Amazing Aratinga!
text: I don't even know where to begin. I had the opportunity to travel to Brazil last March, and am still blown away by my adventures. After travelling close to 10,000km...I arrive on Ilha Grande, my new favorite Paradise. Greeted by Rennie the owner of Aratinga, I felt "home" in a very odd way. Rennie's wealth of knowledge of the Island was awesome! So many little ideas and recomendations for daily activities!...back to her shortly. ;) The Inn is located a short walk from the main Pier (I arrived at one farther down the beach...added about 5 mins to the stroll. If needed, Rennie can have a porter meet you to help with any baggae you may have (if you have more than 1 piece, I recomend the service!, lol) The rooms are wonderful, each with it's own name and story (wait till you get there to understand) The entire Inn area is encopased with luch jungle trees, plants and wildlife...not just the two resident kitties, whom I became quite good friends with! hehe *hint, they love Whiskas Temptations!) Rennie has a beautiful breakfast/coffee/lounging area with a library of books, wifi access and an awesome selection of fruits,tea and cakes for breakfast. Also be sure to join Rennie for tea in the late afternoon! The staff are great, friendliest inn/Hotel employees I have ever met! Check in and out was a breeze. No need to explain that one. Back to Rennie...what a lady! She knows so much about the Island and it's little hidden gems! From hikes to great dinning, she'll have a recomendation for you! I know I'm forgetting stuff, my mind is racing with the memories from my visit to Ilha Grande. If you have any questions about Aratinga Inn or the Island, please feel free to message me! Can't wait to return..sooner than later!

author: lifes_an_illusion
title: Lovely homely place to relax
text: We really struck lucky with Aratinga. We booked in for 7 nights (after 4 in Rio) and wished it could have been 17; we didn't want to leave .. the island, or Aratinga+Hennie. The pousada/pension/inn is small and very pretty, friendly and very comfortable - in all respects. Although it's a little walk from the restaurants, beach, etc, (a five minute stroll) that's a bonus in that it's super peaceful. Ilha Grande was very quiet and uncrowded when we were there (end July/beg Aug), even though at the weekend the visitors doubled (locals popping across for a w/e break from Rio). But I imagine that during the Christmas/Brazilian Summer it could get quite busy .. and then Aratinga's quiet spot would be even more of a treasure. Nothing is too much trouble for Hennie and her lovely trio of staff, Josi, Lu and Regina. In addition to keeping the inn spotlessly clean they lay on a lovely spread for breakfast, and another for afternoon tea; the latter is really appreciated when you stagger in from a long day on the beach or trekking. Hennie (Rennie) is great fun! She's led a busy life, full of travel (well she's from Oz, what can you expect) and adventure; she's one of those people you could happily chat to and swap stories with all day. She seems to have thought of everything re running the perfect little inn ... though it seems she still has some ideas up her sleeve for making Aratinga even more appealing - if that's possible! As the island (and Aratinga) are so easy to get to from Rio we would definitely swing by Rennie's if/when we're in the area again. Lastly - I can't for the life of me get my Lopes Mendez sand to 'squeak' like it did when we were walking on that glorious beach just a couple of weeks ago ... I don't think I 'collected' enough to get the effect! And it's been baking in the Roman sun for the last few days to get it back to its natural talcumpowder state.... I'll just have to go back! I miss the jungle/forest-treks too!

author: CPVW
title: Perfect place to stay during your island retreat.
text: I could not agree more with the reviews above. From its location to its gracious host, Rennie and the staff at Pousada Aratinga, all makes for the perfect retreat on this island paradise. Set a few streets back from the maddening crowd, surrounded by lush tropical gardens, the well appointed chalets are a welcome oasis after a day of hiking, exploring and swimming. It is indeed a place to relax, unwind and enjoy the lovely teatime treats that the staff dish up late afternoon ( one of the many highlights of staying at Aratinga). We stayed in the newly built Chalet Azalea – lovely,clean,with all the modern amenities and a very comfy hammock on the front porch. Having injured my foot on the first day and being virtually incapacitated for most of the holiday, I had to spend most of my time at the pousada. Relaxing in the hammock surrounded by the lush garden and bonding with the very sociable cat was a marvellous substitute for exploring the island. Rennie went out of her way to make sure that I was comfortable ( even providing me with delicious lunch from the village Abraao). We would highly recommend Aratinga for anyone visting Ilha Grande. Make sure to read Rennie's book of recommendations as soon as you arrive. She provides extremely helpful suggestions from daytrips, hikes, beaches, restaurants and much more. And make sure to mention that you are staying at Aratinga to ensure you get a free Capirhina. Pousada Aratinga is indeed a unique gem, tucked away towards the back of Abraao - made even more special by the hospitality of Rennie and her friendly staff who always greets you with a smile. We will visit Ilha Grande soon again and ensure our accommodation at Aratinga is booked. Thanks Rennie and everyone at Aratinga!

author: Rob_S_in_Brooklyn
title: Perfect introduction to Ilha Grande!
text: We had an excellent four nights at Aratinga, which was the ideal base from which to explore Ilha Grande. Every morning started with a delicious, full breakfast, including plenty of fresh fruit and juice, and more cakes and breads than we knew what to do with. Each day we tried a new excursion, guided by fantastic tips from Rennie, the owner. Between our helpful conversations with Rennie and the big book she left in each room, filled with information and advice about the entire island, we were able independently to take advantage of everything within a day's walk of Abraao village, which was quite a lot - secluded and stunning beaches, waterfalls, amazing vistas, wildlife trails, rivers, and small, quiet villages where we sampled the Acai and tested our rudimentary Portuguese. At the end of each day's adventure, we were greeted by Rennie insisting we were not too late for tea, which offered all the pleasures of breakfast but with the added sense of reward for our exertions and the excitement of the tropical transition from day to evening. Rennie also filled us in on the best options for drinks and dinner, and even where to buy a good, inexpensive bottle of red wine (one of the comforts of home we had begun to miss), to bring to the delicious brick-oven pizza place in town. She was always enthusiastic, available to help us with our plans, and warm and congratulatory when we showed up sandy, sweaty and disheveled from our latest excursion. Aside from the ways in which the owner makes Aratinga perfect through her presence and all-out approach to service, the lodgings and grounds are lovely, secure and nicely situated between town/beach and the more forested, hilly center of the island. Our chalet felt private and secure, and was new and well-appointed with everything we could want. The shower was powerful, plenty hot when we wanted it, and clean and pleasant to use. The gardens were lush and beautifully kept, and our views from the chalet included both the shaded richness of the gardens and the bright blue expanse of the ocean below. The sounds and sights of colorful birds and small frogs reminded us that we were nestled alongside the Atlantic rainforest. Everything in town was a short walk away - no problem once we had dropped off our luggage. At the end of our four nights, Rennie could not have been more supportive about where we were going for our final few nights in Ilha Grande. We were very glad to have gotten to know the island through Rennie, and would strongly recommend Aratinga for anyone visiting Ilha Grande for the first time, or even anyone looking to get the most out of the community around Abraao, while enjoying the wilder, more secluded spots that can be reached on day trips. We can't imagine having had a better introduction to this memorable and special part of Brazil.

author: colleengrant
title: Awesome
text: Sorry this is sooo late, but this place IS the best pousada in Ilha Grande. Rennie, the owner, is a sweetheart. Very hospitable. My room was ready for me when I arrived. The room was clean and spacious. It was also cleaned every day. She served afternoon tea at 4, with some pastry. It rained most of the time I was there. Although this didn't prevent me from going out into the town (a five minute walk from the pousada), it did prevent from some hiking. However, on the rainy days, she let us watch movies without a charge. She had good recommendations on restaurants (try the biergarten). However, her talents really because useful when I needed to get to the Blue Lagoon (was staying at the Island Experience after Pousada Aratinga). She arranged a one way ticket for me, something I had difficulty on my own. She even coordinated with the owner of the Island Experience. I would definitely stay with Rennie at Pousada Aratinga again. Oh, and the cats are also awesome!

author: 335rikt
title: Really Nice Evening Staff - Room was Just OK
text: This hotel is really easy to find; just beware that some GPS software (eg. Google Maps) will lead you to the street behind the hotel with no way to continue to the hotel parking lot or even see the hotel from there. The evening staff dude that greeted me was very personable, spoke a slow French that was very easy to understand and gave me a great first impression. The room was a little disappointing; the queen bed was actually two singles (?) pushed together on a queen frame - which explains why I drifted toward the middle of the bed. Luckily, I was tired enough that it didn't matter, but it might make for some late night collisions if there were two in the bed. I also noticed that the one towel I used was frayed to the point that it probably should be recycled. Not a big deal - the towels, bathroom and bed seemed clean enough. The floor: not so much. The room was quiet, despite facing A-40, but that might also be my perception because I was tired enough to sleep through a nuclear attack and a rhino stampede. The breakfast was pretty lame. There were muffins (den't get excited about them, they tasted like plastic), bagels, bread, two kinds of cereal, juice, oatmeal, etc. Overall, I'd stay there again just because it's cheap and right off the highway that leads to the P. E. Trudeau airport. Just keep your expectations low.

author: ranitad2016
title: Terrible experience.
text: During the second day of our stay the lights stopped working in the room. They moved us to a different room. The second room was very unclean and dusty. It looked like it hasn't been used for a while and they did not bother to clean it before moving us in. Just because we were about to leave the next morning we did not complain and went to bed. I paid for a bigger room and with windows. This was much smaller and no windows. Room even smelt mold. During our move to the second room I left 2 of my expensive pants in the first room drawer. After I left the hotel I kept calling for 2 months and they will not respond. Someone told me to call back after she check with the house keeping. I called back and got another lady with heavy English accent who was extremely rude and just refused to help. During our stay we requested this same lady if we can check out half an hour late. She was very rude and completely refused to accommodate even after our terrible experience in the hotel. Another lady was sitting beside her and felt bad. She stepped in and said " thats ok, you can check out late." I visit Montreal every month but will never stay here again.

author: stolia301891
title: Worst nightmare and suffering
text: Worst service. The air conditioner in the room was not working. It was just on with the lights compressor was not working no cooling, no fan nothing. They didn't check the whole room before allotting to us. No refund and no transfer to the other room. They made us suffer whole night in worse summer with the heat and humidity inside. Worse reception, no technician. They just started when the renovation was going on. I don't know how they got the permit. No elevators. They didn't publish on the website. The senior person aged 70 had to carry their bags to the second floor. One person with the ligament tear on the wrist had to carry the bag. And the receptionist lying that the elevator is there and then she said it's going to be installed later. Manager was on a holiday when asked for the refund. Its was advance booking for the hotel online. Not the last minute.

author: JacquesC1266
title: Never stay there again
text: Horrible experience all around. The lady at check-in was nice enough but I thought a $200 security deposit was unusual. Went to my room down a musky smelling corridor. Room was big but had a wall air conditioner, dirty carpeting, a table that look like it was about to collapse. The TV only had less than half of the channels working and the wifi keeps kicking in and out. I went outside to get dinner and when I came back, my card would not let me open the back door. I went to the front desk and a new woman with a thick eastern european accent didn't understand what I was asking about my access to the door with my card. She took my card and looked into the computer and didn't say anything when she gave it back. I walked back to my room and found my card now no longer worked on my room. I walked all the way back to the front desk where that same woman now suddenly spoke English and told me I had to pay for the room. I told her I had prepaid in full 2 hours earlier as well as the $200 deposit. She repeated I had to pay. At that point the original counter erson came back and straightened her out and reactivated my card. I then went to my room and later called to ask for a 7:00am wakeup call....with the woman with the accent. I asked for her to confirm and she said "yea, yea" and hung up. No surprise next morning when I woke up on my own at 7:20am...no wakeup call. I called the front desk and was told "oh, sorry". Went to the continental breakfast which turned out to be a bunch of ready made toasts and bagels with jam, a coffee machine and a juice machine, some cereals and hard boiled eggs.

author: 553lindsayk
title: Just OK
text: We stayed here for a kids tournament. The hotel knew we were bringing a group of 11 year olds. They made our team move from the 2nd floor to the first after the first nights stay. Most of the team left. What hotel does that. Why book everyone of the 2nd floor to begin with. The lobby is nice. That is all... The elevator is super small. Our family couldn't all fit with the luggage cart... Yep we had to make 2 trips. Beds were hard as rocks. The room was clean but 5 days was just too long. We checked out a day early. Next year we will be booking elsewhere!

author: NearNorthernChris
title: Good Cheap Hotel
text: This hotel was chosen for the low price and little else as our group was attending a sports tournament. Both the room and the adjoining bathroom was clean with little else to speak for it. There was a hole in the wall from the room door handle and one "painting" was missing (judging from the faded paint outline on the wall). Classy. The room seemed to have little sound proofing as I could readily hear the surrounding rooms. The room was also very warm, even after turning off the heat. The breakfast included of bread and bagels for toasting, horrible coffee, and weak juice. It is also in a very small room which fills quickly and only opens at 7 am (which is a problem when attending a sports tournament). I could only find one distant ice machine. The ice was excellent. The customer service at check in and out was polite and professional. This is a great hotel for sports tournaments as it is very cheap. There is nothing around this hotel so be prepared to drive everywhere. Next time I am in Montreal, and not attending a sports tournament, I will spend a little more money to get a hotel that is on a Metro line. I can then park the car and take the Metro everywhere.

author: 299lorrie
title: Very poor communication with front desk clerk. Very rude and arrogant upon our arrival.
text: The hotel charged us twice for our 2 night stay and when tried to resolve this issue by telephone from Ontario, it was the clerk that I dealt with upon arrival. She again was very arrogant, rude and a lot of attitude. Kept insisting it was the bank's fault and not the hotel. It was very exhausting and time consuming trying to convince her other wise. She in fact called me about 2hours later only to advise that she had checked all receipts and again say that it had nothing to do with the hotel clerks mistake but all to do with our bank. I might like to add that we were 2 sets of family staying for a wedding. When my daughter arrived in their room, the urine smell in the room was overwhelming and of course asked for a change of room the next morning we were staying for 2 nights. Also, they made my son in-law come down to reception again to come give a deposit for possible damage. We were all extremely tired from driving from Toronto for 7.5 hours, so needless to say, this was not appreciated. We believe the night clerk who checked my daughter and son in-law in was possibly responsible this double charge on his credit card. Finishing my conversation with your clerk upon arrival back from Montreal, I advised her that I would get to the bottom of this situation and speak with a supervisor the next day when she would be on shift which I was told would be late afternoon. As it turned out, the next morning, not to my surprise, I might add, my son in-law had been reimbursed his money back to his credit card. I was very surprised that the clerk with whom I had been speaking with the day before did not take the time or opportunity to give an apology or explanation as to what had happened. It would have been a simple common courtesy to call back explain what had happened as it did not have anything to do the credit card or bank. I was unhappy with the whole situation and can tell that I would be in a hurry to recommend this hotel to any of my colleagues or friends. Sincerely Lorrie

author: 175fats
title: A fine place, but not 3 stars
text: This hotel served our purposes, but by no stretch of the imagination is this a 3 star property. The breakfast was on the lower end of what we've encountered on our 2 month road trip. Hard boiled eggs, croissants, toast, bagels, fruit, cereal, and oatmeal were the extent of the options. No waffles, no yogurt. And they were oddly strict about it. You had to have a ticket, given to you at check in, to get in, and there were signs everywhere telling you all food must be eaten in the breakfast room. I don't know what issues they've had before, but I can't imagine people are showing up to steal their Costco croissants. I'm glad I was able to drag my kids to breakfast that morning, and hadn't planned on taking a plate back for them. The room was small and strangely utilitarian. The furniture was fine, but the walls were totally bare; just plain beige paint over concrete (?) walls. The air conditioner did not cool the tiny room sufficiently, and seemed to randomly turn off and on. There was a fridge, but no microwave, and no closet type area, except over the fridge, I guess. That being said, the stay served our purposes. We were safe, comfy, and well fed in the morning. No strange smells, bugs, or noises. A perfectly fine 1.5-2 star stay. But definitely not 3. That being said, the stay

author: Madd555
title: Good for the price you pay
text: I stayed here once before with other members of my family for a wedding. We had 5 rooms booked, and the breakfast policy was very unclear, so some of us got breakfast, some of us didn't. It was all very awkward and embarrassing. I gave my feedback to the hotel, and they took my concerns very seriously and convinced me to try the place again on my next trip. The manager even called to apologize and get more information so she could fix the problems. We stayed there again recently and had a much better stay. They must have taken my feedback to heart because breakfast went a lot smoother. At both stays, the staff were always polite and friendly. The rooms are a little small, but we just needed a place to sleep so that didn't bother us. The beds are a little on the small side, but very comfortable. They wouldn't fit two people per bed though. My sister stayed in a Deluxe room and said they were much more roomier. So if I were travelling with my kids, I would probably do that next time. The location is quite busy, but we didn't hear any of the street noise, and it's close to many amenities, including a really nice park that was great for my morning runs. What impressed me the most though is the customer service and how important my satisfaction was to this hotel.

author: MidlandsRascal
title: In need of serious attention
text: I chose the hotel due to road links into the city centre and links to Quebec. For this, my choice was sound. Just about everything else was poor. The room ( a standard one) had a stained carpet and on arrival smelt of cheap room deodoriser, making me somewhat suspicious. The wifi fell off but was restored later. The bathroom was old but basically clean. There was no plug in the washbasin. Now when I go to less developed countries, I take my own plug, this really should not be needed in Canada! We were horrified to find our top bed sheet badly stained .This was replaced as requested. The front desk staff informed me there were issues with the housekeeping staff. The breakfast area was bleak with a limited choice and some rolls which were inedible. The feedback as above was given to the staff on check out and a small refund was offered and accepted. I have never stayed at a HO JO before and was not expecting much, simply clean and serviceable accommodation . On both counts I was disappointed. I could not recommend that anyone stay here.

author: JKaurT
title: Potentially the worst vacation we've been on
text: My family and I had two rooms here for two nights each near the beginning of July which we booked through Hotels.com. Now I dont know if maybe I expected too much because I myself work in a hotel but this stay was horrendous. The front desk agent that checked us in was great and she even let us check in early when we called. She was sweet as pie and I unfortunately did not get her name but everything after the moment we checked in was downhill. We only got breakfast for 2 people for each room but the agent told me to come down the following day and speak to the manager about breakfast which was totally understandable. When we came down the following day we were told that we only made the reservations for 2 people per room which was not true. The general manager asked us to e-mail our hotels.com confirmation to him which we did but he never got back to us. The "Manager" that we spoke to before speaking to the general manager was bare rude. She was possibly the worst part of the stay because we came and asked her regarding a follow up in regards to the e-mail and she said that the general manager was busy with other things both times and eventually we gave up on asking her because she just gave us attitude. The rooms were okay, kind of had a damp smell to them and the carpets were wet in the one room but again when we called down to see if we get a fan put in them or something she did not do anything. We paid for a cot for the room only to find out we also have to request sheets, pillows and blankets which I thought came with the cot. So when we came back to the room at 11:30pm with tired kids we ended up paying for a cot we couldnt use because sheets were unavailable until the next day. I would not recommend this hotel if you care about customer service. I would never treat a guest at my hotel the way that they treated us. It really put a damper on our little vacation which is quite unfortunate because we chose this place due to the great location. We will definitely just be staying downtown next time! I understand mistakes happen but this stay was more aggravating than relaxing. I never make comments or reviews unless I have good things to say but this was just a completely different story.

author: amber1027
title: The Hotel is actually a MOTEL ... but a good cheaper place to stay for those driving in Montreal
text: I am surprised about all the negative reviews of this place. Maybe I lucked out with my room? The Hotel is really a motel in a very tricky little location on a one way road beside the freeway in the outskirts of Montreal. The location (lack of public transport) and finding the hotel is probably the biggest negative. The best benefit.... free parking and about a ten minute drive from a metro stop if you don't feel like paying for parking in Montreal and getting lost. The lobby is clean and staff were great. Free breakfast I will give a descent rating as you could make your own waffles but otherwise standard continental. The room appeared to be completely renovated and clean. Even the carpet looked new. I didn't see any bugs, dust or dirt. The room was also quiet. Bed was clean & comfortable and linens were fine. Descent tv with several cable channels and not all in French. The room had AC although it seemed to be more difficult than it should have been to keep the room at a comfortable temperature. Bathroom was pristine with a stand up only shower and clean linens. Overall I would definitely stay here again it is far better accommodation than what is offered in the city center at the same price. Plus this hotel has free parking which appears to be a $10-$30 value per day for Montreal depending on where a car is parked.

author: tricksmom
title: Very much still under construction
text: Despite the motel's web site, they are still very much under construction. There were few parking spaces and I was even blocked in one morning (although the construction guys were great and helped me get out while shaking their heads that someone would block me in like this person did.) I was on the backside of the motel - quite a walk (3 exterior doors) so there was no noise but they were still tearing up the parking area and it appeared most of the rooms at the front were not ready for occupation. The reception area was simply a hole in the wall with two people in it. Nice, people though. The room was fine - I was "upgraded" which meant I had a desk and a couch. The desk was nice, I never used the couch, and there was no bureau to unpack into. The room appeared to have been redone recently - new paint, furnishings, tile, countertops etc. Nothing on the walls yet, but oddly, the bathroom ceiling was still stained and yukky. The walls and floors must be really thin - I was woken up two nights by someone above me doing nothing but walking back and forth - sounded like he was pacing, but I don't think he was really. Another morning I was woken by a child screaming down the hallway outside my room - the parents were trying to shush the child but I'd noticed him or her the evening before as he screamed down the hallway to their room. No "amenities" such as continental breakfast. Not even the usual book in the room describing the rules, the places nearby to eat, nothing. Maid service was terrific though - ask for more coffee, you get it! I would not recommend this motel until construction is really complete unless you get it half off - I paid over $100.00/night with all taxes included. It was much further from everything than advertised - unless you are a crow.

author: Teknisult
title: I have stayed in hotels across the world, and this was positively the worst.
text: Booked online, pleasant website. When I got there, it is located right beside a major highway on a off road in a dysfunctional quasi-commercial strip. Large empty parking lot (this should have been my first clue). Lobby coffee was disgusting and the building appeared very run down. There were old signs stating that they were under renovation that were dog-eared and dirty, obviously been there a long time. Check in was O.K., however the girl behind the desk appeared as if she was embarrassed to be working there. The room was small, broken and dirty. There was a strong odor of bug bomb and disinfectant. The washroom was small with no tub. There was an thin alternate door that allowed me to hear everything in the next room/hallway. The TV stand was broken and looked like it was re-glued by a 10 year old (although my 10 year old would have done a better job). The patio table that served as a desk, was dirty and when I put my laptop on it, a bunch of bugs fell off the from under the table and scurried away. I have stayed in hotels across the world in all sorts of rustic location, however I was not expect this from a 90.00/night hotel in Montreal Canada. When I went to immediately check out , the manager gave me a hard time, short of calling me a lier, and made me sign a waver stating that he inspected the room with me before he would give me a refund for the reaming 2 nights. They still charged me for 1 night, even though I was only in the room for less than 10 minutes, fighting off bugs. This is one hotel chain that I will not recommend to anyone. Very unpleasant experience.

author: jimmymarkbob
title: Stylish apartment
text: Great location and very good pricing. I haven’t stayed in an Aparthotel such as this before. Was uncertain how it would turn out. Though, we weren’t left disappointed. You get almost everything you would find in a small home. Shops are about 50 yards away. You can stock fridge and be like at home. Wasn’t sure if we should stay in hotel or see the city... :) Family and I were very happy. Not much to see out the window but that didn’t bother us. The staff are beyond friendly. I had a bit of a personal problem at check out. A miscalculation with transport to the airport. No problem... we were given exemplary service. All my requests were fulfilled without trouble. Couldn’t believe it. Public transport is incredible. I do recommend to get the day ticket. You can use every form of public transport for a very low price.

author: verushka2019
title: The Best!
text: First of all, it's location is prime. You are close enough to public transportation and far enough that there is peace and quiet. Our room was just perfect. Traveling as a family of 3 is sometimes difficult to get 3 beds, but this apartment accomodated 2 of us in the bedroom and one of us on a very comfortable sofa bed. Also, I just love the concept of getting the benefits of living in an apartment (kitchenette, etc.) and the benefits of a hotel (concierge, etc.) Sometimes we don't want to eat 3 meals out a day so having a kitchen where we can keep and make food as needed was so convenient. Also, I must remark on how clean, new and nice our apartment was. Everything was in perfect condition, looking and feeling great. The staff is also adorable. They let me practice my German and would respond in perfect English if I didn't quite get it. Last but not least - no hidden fees, costs or tricks. I paid half prior to arrival and the second half upon arrival. That's it. No secret taxes or unexpected charges. What a breath of fresh air! And, finally, the price is just right - the longer you stay, the less it costs. In conclusion, do not hesitate - this place is the best!

author: AlexKlaar
title: Fantastic aparthotel!
text: This hotel is fantastic - a short walk from Uhlandstasse U bahn station (500m). The staff are extremely helpful, really friendly, and made our stay perfect. We asked for 2 extra pillows...no problem. Our room was 219 - it was spotless and had a comfy bed that folds into a sofa (we didn't bother doing this). The bathroom had clean towels, toilet roll, shower gel and hand soap. The kitchen although small was superb- two hobs and plenty of cutlery pans etc. There is also a microwave. I made the mistake of going shopping before I looked at kitchen and made mistake of buying pizzas and part cooked rolls. Never mind! The fridge was also clean - you need to turn dial up for fridge to come on. The dishwasher worked well and tablets washing up liquid and a cloth are also provided. You can't use dishwasher unless you're in as once you take key pass out of holder by door all lights/electric supply is turned off. We were a bit worried the hotel was too far out the way but it really isn't- ten mins to center. The local shops are good too: Kaisers and Lidl are literally over the road. You can buy beer from a vending machine in the hotel foyer for 2 euros or buy them for 69 cents at either supermarket. I had to buy one from the vending machine for novelty value! The Story of Berlin museum is a short walk from the hotel and we'll worth a visit - included is a tour of an old Cold War bunker under the shopping mall! We will definitely visit Adiago again - having your own kitchen in your apartment is a real bonus and cuts down on costs overall. There is a luggage room at the hotel which we used as check out is 11am and we didn't fly until the evening. That way we were able to enjoy the day out and about in museums etc.

author: mulattokid
title: What an amazing experience!
text: I have always wanted to visit Berlin. I decided to do Xmas shopping with my son ans always look to stay in a place with a private kitchen as we are vegetarians and in any case, enjoy cooking. This place was amazing! Clean and bright. Well appointed. The room was amazing. I was expecting the larger apartment (Thanks to BA's advertising bumf) but it still had a separate kitchen with all the things you need for a short stay. On top of all that, the staff were wonderful and genuine from the moment we arrived. The manager was a wonderful Young man called David Berr. He attended to our every need. Clearly, no effort was too much for him or his wonderful staff. Our kettle was broken and replaced within minutes. We were also able to print important documents via David. They even stored a parcel fro me until I arrived. Our trip was tainted only by the terrorist incident just up the road at the Kaiser Wilhelm Market. We place candles and paid our respects every time we walked past. In fact, I am aiming to go back to this hotel in the Summer! I am not good in winter weather and being form a city that is almost 10c warmer than Berlin in winter (London) my hands and feet suffered terribly!

author: Patrickaclark
title: Very good location and well appointed hotel
text: Hotel is located one street back from Kurfurstendamm, near to Uhlandstrasse and Kurfurstendamm U-Bahn Stations, but Zoo station is within walking distance. Hotel is located behind another making for a quiet location. Arrived early but no issues in leaving luggage until check in time of 15:00. Rooms are compact but have everything you might need - iron, hairdryer, dishwasher, microwave, kettle, coffee maker, large fridge, crockery. Main room has 2 single beds and a large double that pulls down. Also a hifi but couldn't tune radio in so used free wifi for internet radio instead. Service was very good from reception. Didn't try any food from hotel. Only downside was room cleaning. 1-3 nights is daily, then it's once a week, so my 4 night stay didn't include any cleaning but wasn't really an issue. Complimentary toiletries in bathroom and a nice powerful shower. Would definitely consider staying here again. If you do go to Berlin, a trip to Poland is worth considering. For 29€ you can obtain a Berlin-Brandenburg ticket for up to 5 people after 9am on weekdays which includes unlimited travel on local transport and regional trains, including cross border to Szczecin. It's an inland port and about 2 hours away, and makes a nice (and cheap!) day out. Don't forget they don't take the Euro there, but you can get Zloty from one of many cashpoints. Never needed to show passport but advised to take it in case. Berlin is a great city to visit (flat!) and has really integrated transport system, and this hotel has everything you need in a good location.

author: AlonA_12
title: Very good hotel
text: We stayed at the Adagio for 5 nights, and had a great time. The hotel is close to the main shopping area in Berlin, with lots of available restaurants. The service at the front desk was good, and we got helpful answers whenever we asked. The room itself was medium in size, and included everything we wanted - a desk, a refrigerator, micro-wave, dishwasher, etc., so we took advantage of that and bought some groceries at the supermarket across the street and made ourselves dinner in two of the nights. The breakfast (for an extra charge) was standard - good assortment of meat and cheese, hardly any vegetables. The three problems we had were: 1. Cleaning service is not included, and in a stay of several nights it's a bit too much. Any extra towel costs money, which could be improved. 2. The shower is designed in a way that sprays outside a lot. So we asked for another towel, and for only 6 Euros we got one (the "just" was cynic, in case you thought otherwise. Later we found out that we could have bought one for less than that). 3. The hotel is not really close to the S-bahn or U-bahn, and you need to plan 5-10 minutes walk there (depending on which line you wish to take). All in all we had a good stay, enjoyed ourselves in Berlin, and would certainly recommend this hotel!

author: BernadetteN15
title: City Getaway
text: Me and my boyfriend stayed here for 3 nights in March. Check in was really easy and efficient, we were directed up to our room within minutes and we dumped our stuff ready to head out into Berlin. The rooms weren't too big but had enough space to maneuver about. The bed lifted up into the wall but left a couch to sit on underneath. The kitchenette had all facilities and equipment that you would need for a few nights. You won't be cooking up a storm or an Al a carte meal but cheese on toast is easy enough. The location is great. Close to ku'damn shops, underground and bus routes. We walked up to the tiergarten most days and used the transport from there. It's easy, once you get the hang of it. We didn't eat at the hotel, due to us having our own kitchenette but only heard good comments. We also left alot of money in the safe after check out. We realised at the airport. Which also only 20 minutes away, and theres a bus that stops just up the road from the hotel. Ive forgotten the number but the tourist desk speaks many languages so will be able to help. Anyways, we rang the hotel, he sent the maid who retrieved our possessions in full which doesn't always happen on some places, and it was returned to us when we arrived back at the hotel. Fab! Would return :-)

author: hrlga
title: Convenient , Clean and Comfortable
text: The Adagio is tucked away down a quiet lane just off the Kurfurstendamm....... the main shopping boulevard of Berlin. For 90 Eu per night our apartment had everything you could possibly need - a very comfortable bed, television, air con., well appointed bathroom, and tiny kitchen with electric kettle, coffee maker, 2 burner stove, fridge and dishwasher. We had a ground floor garden room which overlooked a charming courtyard space planted with lovely young oak trees and other greenery - such a delight to lie in bed and look out to a "mini forrest", and listen to the tweeting of little birds. Also, the ceiling was very high giving a feeling of spaciousness - rather than that awful "this is just like living in a box" feel. Another important point for travellers was the quietness of the room .... perfect for that all important sleeping after long flights. Clean? Yes, very. and there two excellent supermarkets are located just around the corner. Of course breakfast is available too. The staff at reception could not have been more helpful. The Adagio apartment hotel had not faults at all (and I am very fussy.) You will be happy if you stay here during your stay in Berlin. p.s. There is a smoking floor which may concern non smokers - the smell of cigarettes can be all pervading ( and necessitates an immediate check out) Our garden room was perfect - no smell what so ever.

author: 11hella79
title: Excellent Appartment Hotel in Berlin
text: We visited Berlin in a business trip. Adagio Aparthotel offered us a very nice studio, consisting of a bedroom, bathroom and a small kitchen. The room was pleasantly decorated and was quite new. The bathroom was excellent, equiped with a shower and an extra heating device very useful for the cold days of February. The studio is equipped also with an iron and iron table and a hairdryer as well no need to bring along! The kitchen was well equiped with anything we needed for a small stay to prepare our own breakfast. A small super market is around the corner, open until midnight, very convenient for our breakfast shoping. The kitchen is equiped with a heater, a coffeemaker, a microwave oven with grill and a dishwasher machine, providing also two tablets for the first use. The hotel is situated in a perfect place, very close to the Kufusterdam, the central shoping avenue of the city. Metro station is very close and the bus/strassenbahn/U-bahn network is very easy to use to arrive anywhere in the city. To arrive to the hotel we used the directions received from the information desk in the airport combining the Strassenbahn with a bus, getting off in a busstop 200 meters away from the hotel. Breakfast was only minimal for its price, only cold food, no eggs, for 13 Euros p/p so we preferred to make use of our kitchen in the room. The staff in the reception was very polite and helpful on our arrival and during our stay. Wifi is free and excellent in the room and all over the hotel. The price was very good according to the hotel quality.

author: JD_ELD
title: Strange cleaning policy
text: The hotel is very close to Kurfurstendamm. There are buses, U-bahn and S-bahn within 10 min walking distance. 20 min bus ride on line 109 will bring you to the Tegel airport. The room is clean, modern furnitures, kitchen with large fridge, microwave and a dish washing machine. However there is only 1 chair and no table for meals. The bed is rather hard but not uncomfortable. The pillows are uncomfortable. Breakfast is totally overpriced and there are other alternatives close by. What is most curious is that the rooms are cleaned daily if you stay 1-3 nights and if you stay longer, the next cleaning will be after 7 days. If you want to change towels you have to pay 6 Euros. I felt strangely warped back to my student days staying at youth hostels/camping cottages where I rented towels and bed sheets and cleaned the room upon leaving... The argument for the policy is that the rates are different. Well, the rates we got are not that cheap. At least they could have offered change of towels on a regular basis. I would rather go to a three star hotel with daily cleaning service.

author: NewDay-NewWay
title: Neat, quiet, great value
text: It was a very pleasant stay over a long weekend. We aimed to stay in that part of Berlin and we received pretty much what we were expecting. The hotel is very quiet, although I registered a hen party stayed there same dates as us. Great, very helpful and welcoming front desk staff!!!! The area around - quiet, slightly deserted in the evenings. Breakfast area - quite unusual with little cabins, although we did not go for breakfast there, it was interesting to see how it was arranged. Rooms have kitchenettes, if you are interested in cooking it warming up meals, teas, etc, it"s very user-friendly, incl dishwasher machine, fridge. The Place immediately around the hotel is clean and quiet, but not necessarily very touristy. There is Movenpik winecellar just behind the corner, great selection of wines. But for Ku'damm Stsse - 10-12 min walk. To KaDeWe - 20 min. S-Bahn - 15 min, U-bahn - 12 min. Schonefeld a/p - about 30 min, 37 Euro. Schiller Theatre (Staatopera) - 6 min , 6.5 Euro by taxi. Friedrichstat Palace - 30 -35 min walk-S-Bahn-walk. The overall score is between 3 and 4, with 4 being the venue and service, 3 - distances. Value for money - Yes! Pls watch for special deals! And enjoy your stay, we only got what we've come with!!!

author: jamieg917
title: Best way to visit a city
text: I love apartment hotels. Instead of the faintly regimented feel of ordinary hotels, your apartment is your own. Settle down, hang up your clothes, fry yourself an egg, make a cup of tea, pop to the supermarket and get some snacks for the fridge... it's a home from home. If you're used to hotels, it's a bit weird knowing that unless your stay is very short or very long, you won't get housekeeping. You have to dry your own towels, make your own bed and empty your own recycling bins. You even have to buy your own loo paper if you think you'll go through more than 2 rolls during your stay! But in return you get to come and go as you please, never listening for the dreaded 9am knock from a chambermaid keen to get your room done so he or she can get on. Horses for courses! Don't bother with the overpriced breakfast on the ground floor, by the way. There's plenty of good places to eat nearby. Walk the three blocks to Savignyplatz S-Bahn for a choice of cafes and bars, or head to Uhlandstrasse or down the Kurfurstendamm for more up-market eateries. Two supermarkets - EDEKA Reichart and Kaiser's - are nearby. Save yourself some money by shopping for a salad or a light meal and some beer to eat in - especially on your first or last nights if you've had/will have a long train or plane journey. Relax!

author: MarkB667
title: Almost perfect
text: We travel to Berlin at least once a year, having fallen in love with it when we lived there for a short period. We have used many hotels and apartments. As we use other hotels in the Accor group and we had our daughter joining us we thought we would try this apart hotel. Part of the reason for this was it's close proximity to U bahn stations and Kurfurstendamm bus routes. The hotel is actually down a little access road between a very nice apartment block and another hotel. From the start the hotel more than met our expectations. The booking in procedure was just as you would expect from an Accor hotel. We went to our apartment and both my and I were delighted with the large, airy and very light layout. A big bonus was the fact that the kitchen was linked to the lounge by a large serving opening which means that whoever is cooking can be connected with the others in the "lounge". We have stayed at apartments where the "kitchen" is actually in the hall!! The kitchen was equipped as you would expect and was very clean. What must be borne in mind is that we were staying in a family apartment which I believe is much larger than the standard rooms. The staff were very pleasant and efficient again as you would expect from Accor. I cannot comment on the breakfast as we eat in our apartment but the buffet looked plentiful. As my title suggests it was an almost perfect experience the ONLY fault I could find was that we had ordered a cab on the morning we left which had not in fact been booked, however, the night staff called a cab which arrived very quickly, well I had to find one fault!!

author: Adelaidian5052
title: Modern hotel with the full range of amenities
text: My family of four stayed three nights in this hotel at the end of September and were pleasantly surprise with the modern room which felt new. Our room was apartment style, complete with a kitchenette and separate room with a queen size bed and plenty fo room. The kids loved this hotel. Considering the kitchen facilities, we opted not to have breakfast, but to buy our own supplies from the supermarket across the street. Bear in mind, should you arrive on a Sunday, as we did, the shops will not be open and the gas station on the corner did not have breakfast supplies, so we ate in the hotel and paid the hefty breakfast price on the first day, which I didn't find to be good value for money, but our oversight really. There is free internet in the lobby, which we found convenient to use, and a coin-operated laundry for guests. However, arriving on a Sunday proved difficult, becasue the reception staff were out of change, and the gas station would not give us any either - bit frustrating. The laundry was such an appreciated service, but it would have been better had it been a token operated service as we found in other hotels, which would have taken the stress out of finding and keeping the correct amount and number of coins required. The front desk staff were good, although the language barrier was difficult at times, we were relieved when there was a good English speaker on the desk, as this was our fist time in Germany and our skills, though we tried, were bad.Overall, the reception staff we as helpful as they could be. Otherwise, the hotel is well located from the U-bahn and S-bahn making it easy to access points of interest. Train tickets can be bought at the station itself. You can even hire a bicycle from outside the main entrance if you are game. There is no restaurant in the Adagio, but plenty to be found close-by, the reception staff did provide us with some delivery menus for when we were too tired to go out again after a big day. That said, there was a great Italian restaurant near by- Capone's - which was just fabulous and seemed busy and popular. Great and friendly staff who paid particular attention to the children and tried to get a giggle out of them and who were very accommodating and forgiving of our very bad German.

author: stef933
title: a place to call home
text: The apartment was amazing. Everything looked brand new from the modern bathroom to the well equipped kitchen. The apartment was the right size for what we needed. The bathroom has a large shower, heated towel rail, shelf space, and is incredibly clean and modern. The kitchen is small but incredibly efficient and usable! it had a full sized fridge, dishwasher, sink, hobs, and all the cutlery and utensils you could need. There was also space to store and prepare food. The bed could fold into a sofa if you wanted a bit more space but we left the bed down the whole time and found there was plenty of room to move around still. There are cupboards, desk space, tv, stereo system, safe, luggage space, and even a hoover and iron in case you were feeling domestic :) We only stayed for 4 days so didn't get any free cleaning or towel change for the room..but it wasn't need or missed. I'm not sure if the hotel was quiet or if the sound proofing of the rooms is to a high level because we never heard any noise from the neighbouring rooms or the corridor. I would definitely recommend this hotel/apartment to anyone. The staff are helpful, and the complex is modern, clean and very welcoming. The location is also perfect. Just off a main road (behind another hotel) which means there is no road noise at night. Saying that, it is behind another hotel called the 'ABBA hotel' which could confuse you if unaware. There are signs to the hotel from the road though so don't let its location put you off, it is fairly easy to find. The area is full of shops (high end brands) and a short walk will lead you towards several lovely restaurants and bars. It is a very safe area to walk around at night. Also a short walk to the S bahn and the U bhan train stations which is perfect. As i say in the title, the apartment was a home from home, i loved it :)

author: sydney_CJ
title: Hello Berlin!
text: Stayed the Adagio for 4 nights in August and really enjoyed our stay. Hotel is located a few blocks from the tube station, so its very convenient to get around. Not the most exciting of neighbourhoods of all Berlin, but still a decent area to be staying in and has all the amenities a tourist needs, including a couple of decent neighbourhood supermarkets. Hotel itself is quite new, very clean and very inviting, with pleasant and helpful staff. The dinning and lounge area off from reception is quite social and had a few people there enjoying the free wifi (only works downstairs, not in your room). Rooms are apartment style with a good kitchenette, full size fridge, dishwasher, pots and pans, crockery etc. Even managed to cook a good steak dinner one night. The bed folds away into the way and opens up the living room if you want some more space. Don't be afraid though, the bed was very comfortable Air-con worked and we also had windows that opened - being set back from the road, there is no noise. Bathroom was a real highlight - absolutely loved the big shower, great water pressure and heated towel rail. All very nicely decorated too. There is a laundry onsite with Miele washers and dryers. One machine we tried to use was broken at the time, but reception helped out to get our washing done in the other machine and transferred our credit across no questions asked. Breakfast was pretty basic. Standard continental breakfast - nothing overly special about it. But considering you have your own kitchen in your room, I can't complain. Note - the servicing schedule is very random. We had no servicing as we only stayed 4 nights. But if you stay longer you get regular servicing.

author: SaraVila
title: A lovely place to stay
text: The Adagio Berlin ku'damm took me quite by surprise. From the photos on the website I expected that my apartment would be quite a bit smaller. I anticipated that in the studio apartment I wouldn't be able to walk the way around the bed with it down from the wall. This however was not the case. The apartment was well appointed and stylishly finished. I stayed in Berlin for four nights which provided great value. The little kitchenette was great for storing some drinks in the fridge and whipping up brekkie when I didn't feel like having a cafe breakfast or I had a tour on that day. There is a little grocery store just up the road too which worked out great. This particular aparthotel is situated only 5 mins walk from Kurfurstendamm; a very affluent and shopping oriented street. All your high fashion labels are here as well as some great restaurants. Only drawback I found was that it was a little far to walk from the main attractions. But then I walked pretty much everywhere while I was in Berlin. If you can master the transport system, you've got it made. Also just a note, if you are catching a taxi from the airport, let your cab driver know that it is behind the abba hotel. Mine didn't seem to know where the heck it was. As to whether or not he was just ripping me off is another question, but if you tell them this tid bit then you won't have the same issue. I also found that the bed was a little bit hard, though this seems to be the same in every hotel I have ever visited.

author: Kenny-Lyle
title: Handy apartments
text: My umpteenth visit to Berlin and another new hotel experience for me. I chose the Accor Adagio Hotel after receiving a promotion of 40 Euro a night in an email. The Adagio is described as an Aparment Hotel with each room being equiped with a small kitchen. This appealed to me as for 4 nights stay I quite liked the thought of having breakfast in the room and stocking up on some essentials if rweather dictated whether i woukld dine out or dine in. As it turned out, the weather was particularly wet this July and the facility of throwing together something hot and cooked was taken advantage of on a couple of nights. The rooms are amply big enough even with the folding bed permanently down and are erquiped with flatscreen t.v. radio/CD player and a writing desk. Peculiarly, for a modern hotel internet access is only available with ethernet connection but is free to use. The kitchen comprised of a sink. 2 hob stove, microwave, fridge and dish waher.No toaster which was a bit of an oversight I thought. The bathroom was again of ample dimensions and modern fittings. The hotel is in a good area surrounded by shops, bars and restaurants and is one block from Kurfurstendam and 10 mins walk to the nearest S Bahn (Savignyplatz) or U Bahn (Uhlandsrasse). I cannot comment on breakfast as I had stocked up for the mornings at the local 7/11 Staff were very efficient and helpful. The one thing that I found unfitting for a 4* hotel is their laundry policy.There is no cleaning or laundry replacement unless you are staying for 5 nights or more. This mean that 2 small bath towels and 2 handtowels are your lot for up to 4 nights stay. Had there been 2 of us in the room, this would have been far from adequate and seems such an easy thing to get right even if it is just by leaving clean towels at the door every other day. One other gripe was the building work goimg on directly beside the hotel. Work started around 8 o'clock and was particularly noisy one morning after a late night. All in all I would recommend the Adagio and would stay there again but still prefer the lower classed All Seasons Mitte which is also an Accor hotel but certainly not inferior to Adagio in quality.

author: Jes001
title: Small rooms, but good choice given the price
text: We stayed here for three nights and we were happy with the room, given the price we paid. When we arrived we were a bit disappointed by the size of the room, since it's really small. Actually the size of the room is very average, but because of the (small) kitchen, there is very little room left for putting your suitcases etc. when the bed is down. It took us some time to figure out that you can put the bed up into the wall. However small, the rooms are smartly organised. No space is left unused so they can give you the maximum amenities on a surface of about 20 sqm. The only thing we really missed in the room, was a coffeemaker. Other than that everything was there : microwave, iron board, stove top, dishwasher(!), fridge,... We didn't take breakfast here, so I can't say anything about that. Would I recommend this hotel to a friend? That depends. If you want to prepare your own food it's certainly a good option. If you don't plan on using the kitchen, I would suggest taking another hotel, because the kitchen makes the rooms a bit cramped. On the other hand the rooms are clean, modern, well appointed and not expensive so maybe it's not a bad choice after all. I doubted very hard whether to give the hotel a 3 or a 4 rating. Actually 3,5 would have been ideal. I decided for 3 because although everything was fine; nothing was really special or exceptional. Although there were no negative surprises, there were also no positive surprises.

author: mlcy
title: A bargain with a kitchen
text: My friend and I have stayed here for 3 nights as our last stop of the Germany trip. We booked a studio apartment and the room is very comfy and clean. Staff is helpful and nice. The open kitchen has a home size fridge, microwave oven, dishwasher and all the cutlery you need from making a coffee to cooking a meal. Toilet is clean and modern in design. One little thing can be improved is the shower, it will be better if there is a curtain to completely separate the shower space so the water won't be spilled out on the tiled floor. Another minor drawback is the Internet. There's free wifi in the lobby but you need a LAN cable in the bedrooms to connect free internet service. Fortunately I got my own LAN cable while the reception cannot provide one to us from a high demand of them. From the special offer from my booking I got complimentary breakfast. The continental breakfast choice is satisfactory and the food is nice. The little business centre in the lobby saves our trouble of finding a place to do print-outs as well. The hotel is just in a few minutes of walking distance to U-Bahn as well as a supermarket within 3 minutes walk. There are loads of hotels nearby with restaurants and local shops opening till at least 10pm so safety is not a concern when walking around the area (although there's a construction site next to the hotel, which is not affecting much). In general we had a very happy and nice stay which makes this hotel worth recommending.

author: arienne410
title: Don't think I'd stay there again!
text: My room was booked there by my company, as I was staying there with a group of co-workers. The room was supposed to be ready by 2 pm, but wasn't ready around 2:30, when my sister and I arrived. They said come back in an hour, but the room wasn't ready until 4:40. We had left our luggage locked up so we could at least get a bite to eat and the girl behind the desk just stared blankly when I asked her to get my luggage that had been locked up. When you haven't slept for over 24 hours, this is a problem. The girls earlier were very nice, as was a gentleman in the evening, but the rest of the staff was grumpy and not helpful. We weren't told that we would have the same towels for the entire stay, so some of the group were going to be charged for clean towels. Most of the group found the staff to be unhelpful and not very friendly. We didn't have a hot pot in our room to heat up water for tea or coffee, although some of the others had them. The breakfast was nice, there was an assortment to choose from and we enjoyed it. The rooms are a bit small and nothing fancy, but were fine, since we spent most of our time away from the room. The bus stop and subway stop were not too far away. There was shopping and restaurants a short walk away. The beds were very comfortable. The shower kept getting water all over the floor and the pipes were so hot, I burned myself. The wifi downstairs was almost impossible to hook up into and was a source of frustration. I was shocked that they didn't have free wifi in the rooms. It was free, but if I had to return to Berlin and have to pay for it myself, I would look elsewhere.

author: MagdalenaM912
title: Three weeks
text: I'm just back after over 3 weeks in the Adagio. The studio was fine, very modern, clean, the space was well used. It was sufficient for 1 maybe 2 people max. There were few maintenance issues, and everybody seemed to experiance some issues with internet conection. Once you arrive you should ask for a cable but you will only be able to use the internet at the desk. When it works its good, when it doesnt, it doesnt and i usually abandoned my computer for few hours. There is wifi in the lobby. I had some issues with cleaning. Sometimes i would be left with 4 towels, sometimes just two, sometimes there would be no bin bags in the bin. the electricity card would be taken out and laptop would go out of charge. Small things. The self service washing machine costs 6eur, you get a tablet/powder for it. Dryer is 3 Eur. It works on time so this buys you two hour use of each.The bed is big and comfy but the pillows are square and not great. I must admit the staff seems a bit not interested and wont go out of their way or anything but they are not rude. Over all despite the small issues described above I would recomend the hotel even for a long stay. Ps. there is a little Italian restaurant near hotel called Pizza Factory and its quite cheap but nice.

author: Dudel
title: At the end neither a bargain nor a winner - some issues to consider
text: We were disappointed with this hotel, for various reasons. Value-wise it is okay, but not a real bargain. First of all, the standard rooms are advertised as studio apartments with sleeping and living area - well it is a do-it-yourself "living" area, made possible through folding a foldaway bed and the placing pillows at the back of the cupboard. Speaking of the foldaway bed, it was uncomfortably hard with a foam mattress on a rudimentry statted frame not providing enough ventilation for a mattress of this kind. Sleeping quality was not good. Thirdly, though the kitchen was fully equipped, there was no coffee or tea provided for the guests. I asked if it was forgotten and was told that it is a self-catering hotel and that it has to be bought by the guests. I don't understand why for the cost of less than a Euro a day one would upset customers. Forthly, the staff was really kind and tried hard to be helpful, but every question we asked was answered with, "wait a second, I'll google it for you". It is okay for the most part, but when we asked how to get to the airport by public transportation we got the same answer. I would be amazed, if we were the first to ask this question. This hotel is rated as a 4 star hotel, well I am sure it meets all the criterias necessary, but it just doesn't feel like it. On the positive side, the small kitchen and the bathroom were very nice, even though the bathroom designer favoured fanciness over functionality, but okay. The rooms were tidy, and having a iron and a iron board in the room was handy. Location is good.

author: HolidaymadSolihull
title: Excellent apartment for the money
text: We first stayed at an Adobe apartment in Bordeaux and we impressed. I therefore searched specifically for an Adobe in Berlin. This is a modern aparthotel (street view actually shows it as a building site) and the facilities in the apartment were excellent. The staff were extremely helpful and when asked to recommend a restaurant for german food, told us of one a very short stroll away, which was exceptionally reasonable and good. There is a building site next door, but we were allocated an apartment as far away from it as was possible (without us asking). It was very quiet and we were not bothered by any street noise or from the building site. The apartment was clean, well equiped, warm and comfortable. The nearest supermarket is only about 100 metres away. A bus stop to catch the 109/110 to the zoo, where the S Bann runs to take your quickly to all the sights was only a 5min stroll away and a U Bann station no more than a few minutes more. We bought a 72 hour Berlin Card from which we got the full value from the travel and discounts. As we bought one which covered Potsdam, we also used it to return to the airport. I would certainly recomment the Fat Tyres Bike tour. It took us to all the main sites on very easy to pedal bikes and our guide was very knowledgeable and funny. All the guides, I think, speak English as their first language, so you get a full commentary. I certainly don't think we would have covered the distance on one walking guided tour. The whole thing, including a stop for lunch, took about 5 hours and was well worth the money.

author: Jaemi
title: Love the Adagio Hotels
text: We booked this hotel after having stayed at the Adagio in Vienna and loving it. We had an excellent experience in this Adagio too. This is definitely a chain that I would highly recommend! Rooms are very spacious, with a well equipped kitchen (including fridge, microwave, plates, etc), modern furnishings, comfortable bed and lovely bathroom (although the water from the shower ends up all over the floor). The shower gel and hand gel are beautiful. There is also a tv, free wired internet, a desk, and airconditioning. The windows are double glazed and the hotel is situated off the main street so is very quiet (although be aware there is currently a construction site next door - this did not affect me at all but my mother was a in a room closer to the site and she was aware of the noise. So maybe request a room away from the site). The hotel is well located between two metro stations although we used the bus to and from the zoologischer gardens (number 149). The stop is only 5 minutes away on the main street and buses come every 10 minutes. We asked at the front desk for restaurant recommendations and they pointed us to a road only 2 minutes walk away that had lots of excellent options. The hotel has one computer available for public use, and a printer. Breakfast is available for 11 euro but we chose to go to the nearby cafes instead. Our apartments were not cleaned during our stay but we liked this, as it gave us more privacy. This is a very clean, modern, comfortable hotel with excellent service and location. I would highly recommend it and would stay again.

author: Swheel
title: Serviced our needs
text: If I ranked this place based on the first room they gave us it would get a big fat 0. They had not cleaned the room and there was someone elses dirty underwear and socks laying about. The floor was filthy and the bathroom was vile, hair in tub and dirt, was disgusting. After we complained they rightly moved us to another room. The 2nd room had at least been cleaned. The room was small but did our needs, the kitchen was handy as we often like to lie in and not be in a rush in the am and want to eat on our time not on the time of any restaurant. So we did use the kitchen, as other has said there was dishwasher, microwave with grill in it, nice size fridge. Pots/pans, tea kettle, coffee maker, stove top with 2 burners, dishes, silverware, even dish soap and tea towel. Bathroom was nice size as well and lovely shower. The bed however was like sleeping on a slab of concrete!! never ever in my life have I been on a harder then a rock bed then they have here. Most beds have a bit of give when you sit or lay on it...not this one..so if you like a stone hard bed then you will love this. As we are not late night people we do like to get early nights, the only english they have on tv is either news or sports...that's it. so take a book It's about 15 min walk to the U train station... There is a computer you can use in the downstairs lounge free of charge and wired internet in rooms that is free. We would stay again just b/c of the kitchen

author: TriNicolino
title: Stunning sea views!
text: This was an interesting property. The lobby and hallways are almost like old-school glam - like you could just about picture the Kennedy's or Marilyn Monroe walking in front of out. I wouldn't call it luxury by today's standards, but this is a nice place. Our room was average, but when you opened the GIANT glass door leading out to a patio overlooking the ocean, the WOW factor definitely kicked in. The hotel is perched right on the ocean - like feet from the ocean, so that when you're in the room looking out, it's ALL water. Beautiful. We slept with that door open all night and listened to the waves lapping at the rocks below. We didn't have the chance to use the pool, but it looked great. Which is good, because the hotel has essentially no beach. I'm quite certain we could have found beach a couple of blocks away if we had wanted, but unfortunately we were just passing through this area. There was a very friendly older gentleman in his 60s that assisted us several times. Didn't speak a word of English, but that didn't stop him from communicating with us. He definitely gave off a grandfatherly vibe. Although there was another older gentleman who got a bit crabby with us as we were wandering around the property the next morning, checking things out. I must echo the others who say you MUST get a seaside room if you stay here. I thought about saving the extra $20-$30, but I'm SO glad I splurged. The view was worth every penny. I'd go back if I were in the area, and I wouldn't hesitate to stay a few days.

author: Anne123Waterford
title: A Gem.
text: Just back from a trip to Italy and stayed in Hotel Maga Circe, it made my holiday. The hotel is family run, and it shows, the staff were friendly, helpful and always pleasant. My room was perfect, I fell asleep to the sound of the sea and woke to the same sound every morning. The hotel itself is of an age, and I hope they won't change it! There is a magnificent seawater pool, and the pool area is again spotless, and has lots of poolside furniture. The food is good, freshly cooked, adequately choices and typically Italian. The old town is quite a climb, but worth the effort, it would take about 15 minutes to go up, and probably about 10 to come down. Likewise the walk to the shopping area is a very pleasant 25 minutes. The beach close to the hotel is clean and sandy and good for swimming. There is a local bus service, which I didn't use, so I can't comment on the service. It would probably be better to have your own transport if you wanted to travel around. I was on a tour, so we got to visit Rome, Naples and Pompeii and the gardens of Ninfa. I would be happy to recommend this hotel for a satisfactory and pleasant stay. Wifi is only possible in reception area. This was not a problem for me.

author: IanL507
title: Delightful Italian escape
text: This hotel is definitely worth staying in for the stunning views, the magnificent salt water pool and the delightful mix of Italian styles around the hotel from the 50s to the 80s. The hotel surrounds and rooms are kept clean to a high standard by the very cheerful cleaning team. Breakfast is standard continental, so if you want something hot, you will need to pay extra. Lunch and Dinner also available at the hotel, although we didn't take advantage of this as the hotel was very quiet when we stayed and we wanted a bit more atmosphere. There are a number of other eateries in the local vicinity if you choose to eat out. So, some things to bear in mind. Wi fi only available in the hotel reception and seating areas outside of the rooms, plus parts of the pool area. The pool is apparently seasonal, so check with hotel first if unsure. There is a small private walled beach as well. Most of the team are Italian speaking only. Having said all of this, if you are looking for a relaxing holiday to totally unwind and get away from technology for awhile, plus try out some Italian, which we found easier than we thought, and enjoy the sound of the ocean from your balcony, then this is for you. Came home totally chilled out and would definitely return. N.B. Rome is just 80 minutes away. Park your car at Tor Di Valle train station for free and get the train in, takes 10 mins from there...easy!

author: matts202
title: Beautifully positioned and appointed hotel that misses a trick
