text: We are a family of 5 (8,6 & 1) and can speak Italian. Hotel Maga Circe is a grand looking hotel that doesn't quite take advantage of its possibilities. As many other reviewers have written, the hotel is starting to show its age internally and still has the feel of a hotel from a bygone era. This is a shame because the situation of the hotel is simply fantastic. It literally sits on the sea, once you have ensured that you have booked a sea view room (you will kick yourslef if you don't), you can appreciated the totally uninterrupted views of the horizon with the sea stretching before it. Looking down you will find a small private beach which is perfect for kids and protected behind a sea wall. To the left is a salt water outside pool (approx 20mx25m) which is just incredible, beds are always available and infact reserved for you by the pool attendant for the entirety of your stay. Between the hotel rooms (below) and the sea is an incredible terrace where breakfast, lunch and dinner is served. OK so that's the good, now for the missed opportunity part: Half and full board options are horrendously over priced and it would be our recommendation to just get b&b and eat elsewhere. Breakfast is OK, but anything cooked is extra so don't expect eggs! We actually had lunch one day ala carte in the restaurant and were very dissappointed when the expensive fish was over cooked. The rooms have been repaired, but not painted, so there are patches of new plaster. In our room their were bare wires for the phone showing. There is no wifi except in reception (I think this is inexcusable personally), not at the pool, not in the restaurant and especially not in the rooms. The hotel bar was not well stocked and on one day the only beer they had was warm, additionally the gin was cheap and nasty and the bar attendant did not know how to make a g&t!! The hotel staff don't speak English, so be prepared to use your phrase book. We also found the staff to be a very mixed bag, the cleaning ladies were lovely as was one of the waiters and also, on occasion, the seemingly surly pool attendant. We enjoyed our week stay at Hotel Maga Circe, but felt frustrated that it could have been truly incredible with some fairly small and easy changes. At the end of the day it is not our hotel and these small changes could make this hotel significantly more expensive for its visitors, so I guess it's up to the owners if they want to do more of the same for the next twenty years or make the hotel the star attraction of San Felice.

author: threewinosItaly
title: Worth the visit if you get a deal.....
text: Stayed with friends for 2 nights, we meeting people with a rented home in Circeo. After alot of confusion about on-line prices, many phone calls to the hotel and explaining about an upgrade for customer service, it all worked out good. The place is old, needs a good clean up job and some decluttering if you want something new and expenisve looking. We were there at the end of May-beginning of June. Gardens at the back need a good clean up too. Especially off to the side. Price in our room double with one bathroom is a bit outdated € 750.00!! I do not think so.........not even close. We paid alot lot less. Not bad for what we got! Breakfast was a bit boring but a few home made cakes. The best thing about this place.......are the people. The couple at the front desk were Fantastic and helpful, cleaning ladies all very friendly, poolman was always busy......and our waiters...they helped make our stay very nice. We still don't know what happened at the restaurant......Saturday small portions at lunch, Sunday they made up for it. But once again not cheap.... I am sure it was gorgeous in its younger days.......

author: Johansoh
title: Great staff, hotel needs som tlc
text: Absolutely stunning location, this 60s style hotel has a lot to offer when it comes to bilingual service minded staff and communal areas. The staff is laid back, friendly and speak (by Italian standards) extremely good English. Very helpful with excursions and tips on where to go to eat. The open areas were well attended but not air conditioned. The reception was at times a bit sauna-esque. The salt water pool I right on the water with deck chairs and sunbeds free of charge. There is a private beach, but it is super small but has a sandy area great for kids. Some of the open areas were either under repairs or permanently off limits, but crudely done with red tape or some make shift gate made out of left over construction material. This takes away from the riviera style charm of the hotel. The big letdown was the room. Connected family room (two double rooms) was small. AC even on full blow in both rooms never got the temperature below 25 deg. Bathrooms were clean. Neither rooms or bathroom matched the charm of the open areas. The beds were hard, even by Italian standards. International clientele. The breakfast offers a large selection of cakes and drinks. Hot dishes are extra. During summer I would put this down as pricey for what you get in terms of room standard. + Charming hotel + Good open areas + Great staff with good English - Underwhelming room standard - Hot and stuffy inside - Hard beds even by Italian standards - Summer is pricey, a lot of things (like wifi, hot breakfast) comes at an additional charge

author: PatD484
title: Spectacular setting and facilities
text: We have just spent ten glorious days at this hotel. Having stayed here for three days last summer, there was never any doubt that we would be back. The rooms are very comfortable, but their crowning glory is their full wall window/door opening onto a private balcony. All overlooking the blue Mediterranean. Breakfast and dinner taste even better when eaten right by the sea and served by waiters in white dinner jackets. The swimming pool is large, clean and well maintained by the pool staff. There is no unseemly tussle for loungers. All is calm and well ordered. San Felice itself is delightful. Smart and with a plethora of shops. Particularly good for jewellery. We ventured away from this beautiful spot only once and that was to go to Pompeii. Next year it will be Herculaneum. So, we shall be back. How could we stay away?

author: LQuat
title: Bull-Ossum Cluster Bulldog Show
text: What a great dog show weekend!! As one of the show chairs of this cluster I highly recommend this facility for a dog show or family vacation. The ballroom is large enough to set up several rings, the rooms are updated, spacious and clean, the amenities are great - coffee shop, restaurant, bar, pool, game room, and many other fun family things to do. The staff is top notch and was available to us 24/7. I need to personally thank the employees that supported us and our exhibitors - Angela, Heather, and Cola who are at the front desk - greeted everyone with a smile and made sure everyone was well taken care of. Check in/out was very quick and easy. Our "HVAC" man, Jeff Ahner who kept our show room at just the right temperature all weekend Our "Maintenance" man Todd who not only provided my dogs with a daily greeting, but attended to our every need right down to changing ice/water in our rings between shows! Our event planner, Jenn Dyson who made this weekend stress free for me and my co-show chairs. Jenn truly listened to all our needs/wants and made sure our exhibitors were well taken care of. I don't think Jenn went home while we were there!! Chef Joe, Bartenders Melissa and Jennifer, and kitchen staff Anthony, Gianna, and Dante - Excellent is the only word I can use to describe them all. They all went above and beyond not only supporting our exhibitors, but our dogs as well. General manager, April Peregino took the time to truly understand what we needed from a dog show perspective and got it right! She made sure we had her entire staff at our disposal. Video night audit Rick and Security Steve, watched us closely as we walked dogs early in the morning and late at night. Our exhibitors felt very safe walking the hotel and grounds. On a personal note - I will be back with my family for a vacation. The hotel and grounds are beautiful with many things to do.

author: dbX6238FA
title: Nice Upgrades are in the making
text: I have to admit that the upgrades to this resort is an improvement.However, before I speak on them allow me to tell you about my wonderful stay. When I arrived I was greeted by the janitorial staff members who were attending to their nightly duties. I thought this alone deserved a star because many of establishments i have visited the janitors or maintainers do not speak to the guest unless spoken to. So kudos to friendliness. The receptionist was bubbly, personable and took an interest in my concerns and that made me smile. But when she gave me my room electronic room key and a physical key i became perplexed.she explained that the physical key was for the outside door. Smh this holding on to a physical piece of metal is not a 2000 thing, it must be done away with ASAP. Ok moving on. I was sleepier than a baby after eating so once i got into my room and prepared for bed, lights were out. I can say the bed was comfortable but i should of reserved a king size. The decor was not elegant, nor fancy however everything i needed to take care of my needs were there and clean. I went to the pool but it was closed for maintenance at 8Pm. So instead i went to the sauna which was very relaxing. The gym was up to par on machines that i use at my gym. I can do a full body work out with at least 3 machines for one part. The floor held at least 25 machines not including treadmills and bikes. I can honestly say that i will return whenever i am in town for a brief stay. However, i am asking that the owner would also consider my ideas i will share in a business letter i will submit by mail within a week. I see that upgrading is still in effect and hopefully i can suggest some key ideas from a customer's point of view as well as a person who has experience entertainment.

author: G1742ERjerryc
title: Disgusting place. Stay far away.
text: Stay far away. What a dump. Firstly, as you walk into this 'hotel' there is no one by the desk. The smell of mold filled the lobby and rotting smell permeates this place. Then was the first experience with one of the numerous broken thing in this place, the elevator. Finally got to the room and there is mold all over and smoke stench throughout. Dirty bathrooms and cold water in the middle of the winter. Absolutley horrendous. Even the heating system was broken and it had a rusty odor when it ran. Asked for help from the staff at the front and the guy refused to try to take a look at the heat in the room. Terrible attitude and upset employees work in this place. Dining room is atrocious. Dirty and cold. If you try using some of the 'amenities' here good luck. Ice cold, dirty pool in the middle of December, broken sauna and hot tub and no employees to help. If you want to have a terrible time and waste your money this is your place. Otherwise do yourself a favor and stay far away.

author: Lady_of_Mystery
title: Great stay in Riga - great location
text: We stayed 3 nights in this lovely hotel. The location is great, very close to old town and other attractions. Hotel is very clean, staff is very friendly, has a nice decor. Bottle of water has been replaced as a complimentary touch every day. Breakfast is great with a great selection of yummy food. Tea and coffee was replaced on a daily basis. We came to celebrate my friend's birthday and a very nice night club Coyote Fly is very near by as well, which was very convenient for getting back to the hotel. No uber, Taxify though is very cheap. The only little things that stopped me from giving this hotel 5* are: 1. the main shower head was blocked and water was running slowly and unevenly - i had to use a little towel to give a shower-head a good clean - which freed the wholes from blocked limescale and everything was working fine after that. 2. The second shower head with handle we couldn't get even to work, so we only had to use the main big one (looks like a huge sunflower) 3. the single bed was narrower that in any other European countries, i was scared that if i turn round i will definitely end up on the floor. 4. Pillows are very soft, which is uncomfortable, if you are used to hard pillows so it took me a 2 days to find a suitable position and you can imagine i was extremely happy to come back home to my comfy bed.

author: rajasukhdeo
title: Decent quality hard product, service and staff woeful. 4 star establishment at best.
text: I travel for work frequently and stay at various business and luxury category five star hotels in various countries. As such, I am not one to be easily impressed and my review is relative to some hotels of amazing standard. The hotel rooms, furniture, decor and interior were quaint and quite nice. Cleanliness was poor with our suite being dusty in pretty much all of the nooks and crannies. There was no improvement to this despite having complained. The service was poor. My family and another guest checking in when we did were both ripped off by taxies and there was little to no assistance from reception. The receptionists just stood behind the desk cowering unlike the stellar service in almost identical circumstances at some other establishments I've stayed at. There was only one porter who was doing a valet park when we checked in. As such, there was no one to help with our bags. Again, the 4-5 ladies at reception just stood behind their desk doing nothing. I spilled a drink at the bar when moving from the barside to a table because there was no service to assist. The waitstaff merely gave me some napkins to clean up... No help was offered nor a replacement drink. In conclusion, it was a decent premises, but the service was a joke (frankly speaking).

author: wolfgang333
title: Well-located boutique hotel outside of the old city - a 'breath of fresh air'
text: I did this as a pre-pay several months in advance of our first visit to Riga (or Latvia for that matter). Pleasantly surprised that we were upgraded without asking to a room facing onto the Park. We considered both the newly opened Kempinski and the also relatively new Grand Poet-- the latter turns out to be a wonderful 'value for money'. Grand Poet is a luxury hotel priced as a mid-range (does not happen often but I did a lot of research before I do these complicated trips to multiple countries-- they just don't have name recognition like Kempinski). Terrific room and a well-appointed bathroom with a good shower (why Euro hotels generally have small glass doors mounted on top of bathtubs and water splashes out is beyond me but I am not doing the cleaning up). The heated and sublimely quiet lap pool on the lower level was WONDERFUL (it was one of the reasons I booked this hotel). The buffet breakfast was extremely varied-- just super well-done-- almost to a fault so much on offer (hint-- sit in the quieter room across the way instead of the very busy and loud main room unless you must have your people-watching fix). In retrospect we are really glad we did not stay in the old town. Old town is wonderful for dinner and strolling-- but was glad to walk back to the hotel after our time touring and shopping. We had dinner one evening in the hotel-- almost by chance. Glad we did. The bartender is MARTINS-- turns out he bar-tended in the States in our town of Westport, Connecticut-- what are the chances? Really personable guy-- and we tried a number of gins (a sampled a few-- esp. a Dutch gin infused with vanilla invented by a guy from Reunion island off of Africa); he makes super terrific drinks-- one of which was a contemporized take on a Negroni. Just trust him-- you won't be disappointed. Usually you have to worry with the measurements in Europe which makes things crazy expensive/stupid so you usually stick to wine. Anyway-- I usually don't wax on about bartenders in Europe but this guy is a find. He likely won't be there when I return to Riga but I shall 'hope' (LOL)-- in any case, I may stay once again at the Grand Poet. They do an excellent job.

author: Katiestabler
title: A colourful modern gem
text: This is a truly delightful hotel, a very easy recommendation. It has a few little niggles (highlighted below) but overall it was a joy to spend a few nights in! STYLE: The reception is beautiful, I loved the eclectic decor, the bright and bold patters and colours. The rooms follow through with the same style, stylish and modern with beautiful accent pieces. COMFORT: The bedrooms have everything you need and are a joy to spend time in (Although Riga tends to do this weird thing where large beds have two single duvets on. This happened in both hotels I stayed in and I found it to be quite annoying on a night) FOOD: I only ate the breakfast here but it was one of the best hotel breakfasts I have experienced! It was buffet style and there was sooooooo much choice. It included an egg station, all the typical breakfast staples, lots of cheese, meats and fish. It even had FREE, help yourself champagne! The room service menu choice left little to be desired so didn’t tempt me. STAFF: Nothing but utterly helpful and friendly. FACILITIES: The gym has everything you need although us small. The spa was divine!! LOCATION: Situated close to everything! The park is right on the doorstep and it’s a mere 5 minutes walk to the shops, eateries and attractions. THE SMALL ISSUE: My bath was broken, the plug didn’t work meaning it couldn’t be filled but by the time I noticed this I was heavily unpacked and couldn’t be bothered to change rooms.

author: Likesholidays11
title: Perfect hotel
text: An excellent hotel from the moment we checked in. Very friendly and helpful check-in staff (despite having "trainee" on her name badge). We asked for a quiet room and were given a room on the 5th floor furthest away from the lifts which was perfect and very quiet. Our room was spacious and spotless. The bathroom was very clean and well stocked with toiletries that were topped up each day. The bed was clean and comfortable. The room had useful features such as a USB charging station, complementary water, robes and slippers. We also used the spa twice. Again, the staff here were helpful and friendly. Wanted to borrow a robe and take that back to your room? No problem. Need more towels? A locker? No problem. The spa was clean, with a lovely pool, jacuzzi, two saunas and steam room. It was well spaced out so both times we used this and didn't feel crowded by other people. Food at breakfast was also spot on - good selection of well cooked food and drinks with helpful staff. Highly recommend this hotel.

author: RodneyfromLondon
title: Luxury with limitations
text: I stayed here 13-16 September 2018. The Reception and other staff were welcoming and helpful. Several members (including me) of the group I was travelling with described this hotel as “More style than substance”. My room (541) was spacious (photo): it was dramatically furnished (for me, the carpet and shower room patterns were too strong), with a comfortable bed and choice of pillows, as well as dressing gowns/bathrobes and slippers. There was a big desk, with a very large number of power points, a television with plenty of channels and a mini-bar. There was the usual coffee-/tea making kit in the room. The air-conditioning was ineffective – at least I found the control incomprehensible. There were no lace/muslin curtains, so anyone opposite could see into the room when the curtains had been drawn. The luggage storage space was more than adequate. In the wardrobe there was a safe, but the wardrobe’s size was inadequate, and its sliding door was no substitute for three closing doors. The bathroom was generously equipped but had a noisy metal pedal bin. The hot water supply was slow. There was no anti-slip mat. The bath was dangerous, with narrow-topped, steep, deep sides. The hand rail was poorly positioned, as was the drain-away, which could easily be operated accidentally when getting in or out of the bath. It was for me extremely difficult to change the water source from the shower to the bath. Several people in my group reported that their rooms had not been made up at 17:00, but this did not happen to me. The breakfast buffet was copious and varied, but there was no hot chocolate and the tea was of poor quality. From many tables, there was a long walk to the buffet. The dinner buffet was excellent.

author: mother-of-love
title: Super Nice Hotel!
text: My two sisters, my mother and I had a lovely stay at Grand Poet. We where upgraded to such nice and big suite, and it made our stay even more perfect. The bath tub in the bathroom was a real gem for me, and we slept so good in the bed. There was a bit dirty in the toilet, and some forgotten garbage and dirt at the floor in the bedroom, but it was being taken care of by the understanding and smiling staff. Not a big deal, but still I wanted to mention it. The breakfast made a terrific start at our day with a good selection of eggs, bread, meat, fish, yoghurt, cereals, nut, fruit, juice, coffee and so on. We all had treatments at the Hedonic Spa, wonderful! I really recommend you to try a massage, and you can ask to make the massage where your body needs it most. Jelena was such a nice and calm person who absolutely knew how to make me and my body most relaxing and comfortable. My sisters and my mother was also super satisfied. The saunas and swimmingpool was a relaxing spot, and I had a good swim before breakfast. The hotel is only a short walk to the old city and other parts of "things to do" in Riga, and there are lots of parks just outside the door to make a stroll and have some relax time by your self. Take a boat trip on the river, it is just across the street, over a small bridge. We felt really welcome by every one of you, and I have only good things to say about all your staff. Keep up the good work! Hope to visit you again next time I travel to Riga.

author: ElectraCooter
title: Just delightful
text: This hotel was almost perfect. I loved the decor; the comfort; the vibe; the location; the breakfast and the spa / gym. I thought the hotel offered excellent value. I was able to check in at least and hour early and leave half an hour later than the very reasonable midday check-out time. On both occasions I was assisted by a friendly receptionist who spoke excellent English. My room was massive and the bed was huge and extremely comfortable. There was no coffee machine but there was Illy instant coffee- a favourite of mine. The bathroom was pristine and very tasteful. Overall, my room was so attractive, spacious and comfortable that I didn’t want to leave. Fortunately the beautiful old town is just across the park so I didn’t need to stray far. A canal / river boat tour jetty is even closer. I made good use of the spa facilities during my one night stay - one of the best such hotel experiences. Most of the time I had the pool to myself; it’s small but long enough for a decent swim. Breakfast was amazing! Friendly staff and everything you could want. The one problem was the toaster; I put my bread through it 3 times and it was as white as it was before its slow journey through a completely ineffectual machine. My only slight issue during my stay was that, on leaving, I wasn’t offered assistance with booking a taxi. When I discovered that my taxi app didn’t work in Riga, I was unable to book through the reception as there was only one member of staff available, and she was dealing with several newly arrived guests. This was disappointing, nonetheless The Grand Poet is definitely amongst my favourite hotel stays.

author: TheSavvyTraveller
title: Excellent property
text: Had a wonderful stay here. The property is almost brand new and everything is polished and perfect. The staff are friendly and helpful, breakfast was delicious and the food in the restaurant at dinner was absolutely perfect. They make very good cocktails too! I was upgraded to a junior suite which had loads of storage and an absolutely massive bathroom with great amenities. The hotel spa and pool area is spotlessly clean and upscale. The bed was extremely comfortable and I slept really well the entire stay. Housekeeping did a great job keeping my room spotlessly clean. The decor in both the public areas and in my bedroom really made the whole experience feel very special indeed. I had a small problem as the bedroom in my suite connected to another room in which the people were rather noisy, but checked out after my first night. The hotel very kindly agreed to block that next room for the duration of my stay which was incredibly kind of them and really went the extra mile in terms of service, although in the long term, I'd suggest they look at ways to improve the soundproofing between interconnecting rooms. I was also a little surprised that the towels were so small - everything else was extremely luxurious so this one is an easy fix. Would definitely recommend to anyone visiting Riga. It's a very short walk from the Old Town, opposite a beautiful park and has a great advantage of being a very easy venue from which to get a taxi. It's also great value.

author: micv2013
title: Pretty nice stay
text: It was a extempore trip to Riga. We choose this hotel because of the good rewievs. Location was nice and peacefull, next to beautiful park with a nice view. Old town was in a 10 minutes walk from hotel. Room was nice and comfy, bathroom was reasonable size and shower worked very well! 😅 How ever, even the breakfast was nice. It was not so pleasant event when we ordered omelets. They said it takes 25 minutes to get them. Terrible, all the chefs were a very nice persons, but they were extremely unorganized, nothing worked basically. Then some older lady with eyeglasses didn't understand a thing, i mean nothing. And it look like she was a superior. I said to them, please get few more stoves and pans, then some organising. You will do this "25 minutes" Job, in a 5 minutes, basic chef things!!! Other customers were not so happy aswell... Aaaand this was a big problem every morning. And im sure it was a problem today aswell.

author: gordonb386
title: All round terrific hotel
text: Where do I start. Check-in was quick and efficient. We were given a room which we had requested. High floor away from elevators and included a run down of what the hotel offers etc. All done by such a pleasant lady. The room is spacios and lacks for nothing, well lit with cute bedside reading lights etc etc. The windows could use some lace curtains as it looks into the rooms opposite. with an equally large bathroom/toilet. All shiny and new and maintained well, apart from the blind which could not be raised because the chain was lying on the window sill. for a 5 star hotel the towels were very much on the small side. We did not go to the spa which is free to guests. The unusual decor generally is of a very high standard. A big factor is the friendiless of all the staff, reminding me of cruise ships! When we were arrangng a taxi for an early morning ride to the airport, we were offered and given a packaged breakfast, which was more than sufficient with sandwich, fruit, pastry and a bottle of water. A first for us after many many years of travel. Buffet breakfast is more than ample with a variet of food to satisfy all tastes. The hotel is situated across from a park and about 200 meters from the old city. a very queit area which means sleep quality at its best. Windows are double glazed and doors and walls solid. Would definitely return there.

author: CurlyCar0l
title: Classy new hotel with relaxed atmosphere
text: The Grand Poet is situated in a perfect location for visiting the picturesque Old Town, taking a boat trip or strolling through the beautiful city park. Lots of fab restaurants in short walking distance too. Very good checkin and warm welcome especially from Mattis the barman with his cheerful philosophy. Beautiful decor and sumptuous furnishing and perfect if you like a firm mattress which 5 out of our party of 7 did. We like a soft mattress so asked Reception for a mattress topper. Unfortunately they don’t have them but have since advised me that they are going to review the situation as not everyone lined a “European Standard” firmness. Not the best weeks sleep but a wonderful short 5 day break nevertheless as Rīga is a city full of delights, both cultural and culinary. Breakfast was available until 10.30 which was good as Rīga is 2 hours ahead of BST so you don’t have to be up before dawn or starve. Although we didn’t partake there was Blanc de Blanc as well as the usual juices, excellent coffee and varied selection of teas. Chef will cook you selection of eggs -eggs benedict, florentine, fried, boiled and omelettes. Very good Continental breakfast also available. We didn’t eat dinner in the hotel as were out around the city with Latvian friends every evening. See my restaurant reviews for details. Small pool, jacuzzi and steam room but no treatments available yet although Reception said they could easily arrange a massage for me if I desired. Reception arranged taxis for us when required which were usually a little cheaper than taking them off the street with no haggling if it was just a short journey. Altogether an excellent hotel which I will recommend to anyone who has the budget for it. Definitely cheaper to book well in advance as when we found ourselves having to book an additional night 4 weeks beforehand (Wizzair cancelled our flight home!!!!) it cost about £30/40 more than our original nights booked 4 months earlier. Only improvement could have been USB charging points in the bedrooms, but we had bought a couple of European (same as Spain) just in case thankfully. Just thought as it was a brand new hotel they might be installed. Definitely a great place to stay..

author: Oscar8T
title: A 4 that could be a 5+
text: This is a brand new hotel with terrific rooms. I mention rooms because we began in the standard room which was spacious, clean, comfortable, top floor with nearly everything as promised. However, the shower leaked a bit and more importantly the air conditioning did not work so it was a hot and uncomfortable night. While the evening air was cool, the windows had no screens so they freely let in some rather large bugs and a great amount of street noise. The hotel was unable to fix the air conditioning and moved us to a larger room- a suite. It was on a lower floor and a terrific room. The air conditioning worked and we had a great night, except the shower leaked even more on the floor necessitating three bath towels to soak up the water which had covered over half of the bathroom floor. Some staff understood the problem and said they thought it had been fixed. The solution was to give us extra towels since it was the weekend and plumbers could not be obtained. The next day upon returning to our room we noticed that water had now flooded from beneath the tub which we had not used. With two plumbing problems we were again packed up and moved to an even larger suite, even more magnificent. We partially unpacked and after an hour noticed that the air conditioning did not work in that room. After some debate, we opted for the comfort of air conditioning with the chance of flooding in the bathroom. Luckily the water escaping from beneath the tub was limited and our stay ended in relative comfort. The staff, particularly Karina, was wonderfully understanding and worked very hard to make our stay comfortable. The included breakfast is fantastic with an abundance of delicious choices. Once the hotel figures out the air conditioning and the plumbing it will be a 5 plus star accommodation.

author: lightgreenmelon
title: Wow. Just wow!
text: I had their standard room, but even the simplest room was really something! The whole hotel and its interior is breathtaking. As I am the kind of person who likes to travel as light as possible, then existing toiletries were a plus. Spaa was also quite nice. Many different saunas and the pool was also okay. For gym enthusiast: they have gym. Location is also great! You can walk and explore the beautiful architecture without needing a car. Walking by itself is a good workout already. Don´t forget your camera! Only thing that is maybe a little bit confusing, is parking situation, so get acquainted with it beforehand. The hotel has its own parking sorted, but it will cost you extra 20 euros per day (with valet though). Service is great and the staff is friendly, so no problem here. Breakfast is great! You have endless options. Also, the coffee machine exists, so all of you, who love coffee, won´t be disappointed!

author: NIKEF2
title: Excellent stay
text: This is a new hotel and it appears that the company managing this chain has spent a lot of money on it (well done, loved the décor). Even non executive rooms are spacious, with comfortable beds and luxurious bedding. The bathroom was beautiful and spacious, with marble top to bottom and underfloor heating. The water pressure is not very good. Tea and coffee facility in the room, good selection of tv channels. Well controlled heating, air conditioning and radiators. The Hedonic spa in the basement is great too, loved the steam rooms, Jacuzzi and swimming pool. Breakfast was very good and what you would expect from a 4/5 star hotel. In my opinion, there is still room for improvement to make this a really 5 star hotel in terms of customer service. All the staff was brilliant but we had an incident that could have been handled better. A drunk client started banging on our door at 1 am, woke up completely disorientated thinking that something serious was going on and we had to evacuate the hotel. We informed reception and they said that they would send security. We were never called back to say what had happened and we were expecting that the management would provide at least an apology letter for the inconvenience. Really badly handled. They could also promote a bit more the restaurant by informing of any deals for customers. Despite this, I would stay again in this beautiful hotel.

author: Valmor
title: Good but not excellent
text: We had a pleasant week’s stay overall. There was nothing to complain in particular; if you adjust your expectations. This is not a 4-star resort hotel you may be used to stay in, on Canary Islands, Mallorca or Costa-something. Location is OK, 5 min walk from very nice beach. But to get to main “tourist” area of Noja (which is a very small place by itself), you need to walk for a good 20 min. Food was acceptable; but too boring after few days, no variety at all. Pool really small; 5-6 guests start to bump into each other. There is no huge lobby, or evening entertainment. If fact, the surrounding area is pretty dead after 8 pm. We stayed in “triple” room which is no bigger than double; just they squeezed third bed in it. That could have been OK for a city stay; but for week’s seaside vacation we felt a bit hampered. There was only one(!) chair in the room. In-house garage is convenient (considering no free parking in the area), but it cost 9 eur/night. (Advice: Unless you drive an SUV, don't try to park on "free" space across the hotel. Every day we saw some car stuck on it's belly when trying to get over the curb). Staff was friendly. Internet works OK in lobby area; but to get wifi connection in your room requires luck and patience. But in general, you get good value for money and won’t be disappointed.

author: thetaxwoman
title: smart hotel near beautiful beaches
text: We checked into the hotel on a last minute basis, and got a good deal through booking.com on bed and breakfast with a spa visit thrown in. Our room was smart and clean, with two double beds, a table and chair, and another easy chair, a small fridge, flat screen tv and nice smellies in the bathroom. Free internet access too - we couldn't get the wi-fi to work, but the hotel provided an ethernet cable which solved the problem. Parking in the hotel car park was €6 per night, but there was some free on-street parking around the place. There's also paying on-street parking, but this would be more expensive than paying to use the garage. Reception staff spoke good English and were very helpful. Most of the other staff spoke little or no English (and we know about the same amount of Spanish), but there weren't really any problems making ourselves understood. Breakfast was a hot and cold buffet - plenty of choice of the usual pastries, ham and cheese and so on. We ate in the hotel on two evenings, simply for convenience, as there didn't seem to be any other restaurants within reasonable walking distance that were open. Again there was a hot and cold buffet, so you could eat as much as you liked. The restaurant itself is quite clinical and brightly lit, as other reviews say, and the food was ok - nothing to write home about, but we had no complaints. At €15 a head it was pretty good value for money, as was the wine list with wines starting at €6 a bottle (ours were €9 and €12 and they were good quality). We used our spa visit, and thoroughly enjoyed it. It wasn't like any other spa we'd been to - you go to each of the treatment areas in turn, supervised by an attendant who spoke only a few words of English (but they were the right ones for us to understand each other!). You spend time in hydromassage pools, hot and cold showers and baths, a sauna and a steam room. It's all a bit of fun! There is a small and very sheltered outside pool which we didn't use, but which looked very pleasant, with plenty of sunloungers and a waterfall. There was a 5 minute walk to the beach, a long stretch of beautiful golden soft sands, interesting rocky coves, very unspoilt and quiet in September, though apparently it gets very busy in July and August when it's full of Spanish holidaymakers. The resort itself is a little soulless, with lots of newish apartment blocks which appeared to be shut up for the winter. We'd visit both this resort and hotel again, especially on a deal, but probably only out of the main season, because it's a lot cheaper (though on the other hand, many more of the local cafes, restaurants and shops would be open in season).

author: catalex1226
title: Very happily surprised!
text: We had a reservation here for two, but suddenly needed to change to three when our daughter joined us. Called the day before and changed from one room king to a two bedroom suite with no problem. Front desk workers were young, friendly, and efficient. Coffee and tea available in the lobby all the time. Much to our surprise when we checked in at about 5:00, we were told that a free dinner (!!!) was being set up and would be ready at 5:30! Our suite was two nice sized bedrooms, one with two queen sized beds and one with one queen sized bed. Each had its own bath. There was a fully-equipped kitchen with a 2-burner stove and microwave, and a very nice living-room. Both bedrooms and living room had large flat screen TVs. Comfortable beds, good towels, decent showers. Plenty of light for reading in bed, which is not always the case in hotels. In addition, it was extremely close to where we were going, which was a bonus! It also is very close to shopping areas.This would be a fantastic place to stay for a family with kids, especially in the summer as there was a very nice pool outside. Also noticed a man walking a couple of dogs, so it must also be dog friendly. Not noisy the night we stayed there. They also have a free breakfast. Didn't try either of the meals, so can't speak to that, but the area with tables was roomy and pleasant. We were very impressed!! Would definitely stay here again.

author: AzRat
title: Not a great experience
text: I stayed at this property for two nights as a caregiver for a relative recovering from transplant surgery as this was one of four locally approved hotels required by the hospital for post-op due to the properties 'awareness of the patients needs'. Post transplant patients need to be kept in a relatively clean environment. I spent much of my days (as did the other family caregivers who did there shifts during the relative's two week stay) wiping things down with sanitizing cloths and got a close up look at the housekeeping practices. Long story short - it just was not very clean. The property was worn down, the kitchen and bathrooms were not 'spic and span' or even close. The refrigerator, cooktop, and microwave would never pass muster in my home. The furnishings and carpets were tired and worn - I would have expected a lodging that apparently lobbied for this specific business to have more suitable flooring and easier maintenance furniture. The patient must bear the cost of the extended lodging and provide the 24 hour 'caregiver' and this property is pricy for a two bedroom suite. Given the overall room quality during this circumstance we probably would have been better off to lie to the hospital and find a much more economic air bnb property nearby. The patient couldn't eat the provided breakfast and evening happy hour offering so that was a waste also. Apparently little thought is given to patient room placement with this arrangement as the 'neighbors' children were noisy, sound carried thru out the suite from the hallways and other rooms plumbing, and the room was far from the elevator. My review must seem quite harsh for the normal traveler who would not be staying here under my circumstances. However the short comings of this property would affect most discriminating travelers at this price point for lodging. Of course we complained to the hospital about this property as one of their 'required' hotels for post-op, but I'm certain that fell on deaf ears. Not a good experience.

author: photobum
title: Great Value in a Great Area
text: We like to stay at Staybridge Suites when ever we can. The rooms are nice, clean and roomy. The kitchen is sufficient for our needs, which when we are on vacation are meager. They have a good breakfast and the evening food is always unique and sufficient. We were here 10/5-10/8 2016. This property is an easy walk to the Cherry Creek Mall which is a lavish up scale Mall. It also has several very nice places to eat. the rooms were clean and maybe a bit short of furniture. The rates for rooms at Staybridge properties are fare and affordable. The property is off the busy streets but not hard to drive to or find. There is a Super Target right across the street and several other grocery stores and restaurants close by. The outdoor living area at this property is very nice and quite large. It has outdoor cooking equipment, a large fire pit, a pool and hot tub. We enjoyed sitting by the fire during the evening. the weather was cool but the fire was just perfect. Using the breakfast each day we were her saved us a few dollars and was very handy. Nothing disappointing about this Staybridge and we will continue to use them when possible during our travels.

author: G5368RDmikeh
title: Don't stay for more than a weekend!
text: While the setting by the Cherry Creek trail and nearby shopping and restaurants is a plus, about everything else with the Staybridge Suites in Glendale has been negative. We had to move because rain was coming into our living room. We asked to get back into the room after the repair but another guest was moved in a few days later without the roof being repaired. We enjoyed the patio but we saw rats by the outdoor grilling area (three times). The patio is also the gathering place for smokers, which makes it hard for the rest of the guests to enjoy. Speaking of smoke, on three evenings we had to call the desk because marijuana fumes from adjacent rooms was coming into our room. The physical facility is in need of repair. During our 100-day stay we occupied three rooms. We had to have three leaky garbage disposals replaced and three of the phones didn’t work. Housekeeping was sporadic, as was the Internet. The TV doesn’t have a menu so you can’t tell what’s on or what’s coming next. I asked an online guide several times but nothing changed. I had business mail opened by the desk because they didn’t recognize the addressee. It was a check and they were going to send it to their office to figure out to whom it should go. The final straw was when my credit card was charged $1,100 when I put a hold on a possible additional week. They pulled the money for the week in advance, something I’ve never had a hotel do, and they didn’t tell me. There were other incidents but you get the idea. On site management didn’t do much to address our concerns. Some of the staff were attentive but others were just going through the motions. You might enjoy a weekend at the Staybridge but I definitely wouldn’t stay longer.

author: TravelerChriss
title: A Fine Stay
text: I traveled to Denver to meet some friends for a weekend visit. One of those friends lives near this hotel, so I purposely wanted a hotel in this area. For a personal trip such as this, I usually stay at a traditional hotel, but since I was sharing a room and there were others in our group, I decided to spend a little more and have the extras a suite provides. The hotel is across the street from a Target, and there are several other businesses and some restaurants nearby. This property appears to be a couple years old, but it's still in great condition. My room had two queen beds that were in a separate area from the sitting room/kitchenette. There were TVs in the sitting room and the bedroom. The couch was also a sleeper if we decided to add another person. The lobby was inviting. The outside sitting area was wonderful. The entire property was clean, quiet and secure. Breakfast was very good. Scrambled eggs, bacon one morning, ham the next, waffles, cereal, breads and more were offered. Everything was presented well, restocked often and the serving are was kept clean. I was very pleased with my stay here. Note that I reserve a full 5 rating for only truly exceptional stays, so my 4 rating is a high mark. I would gladly stay here again. (CS)

author: 707jennifert
title: Perfect for families
text: We're a family of 5 with kids ranging from 9-15. We try to stay in suite-style hotels if staying somewhere for more than a night or 2. We had a great experience at Staybridge. The 2-bedrm suite had two bathrooms, a nice living area, and small kitchenette. It was very clean. The ice maker in the freezer was a nice touch. Pretty decent breakfast included. Dinner was included as well but we did not partake in it this trip. The food looked good though. Another nice feature is the laundry facility on site is complimentary! No lugging quarters. The location is pretty convenient to the highway; getting to the city is about 15-20mins. Also located close to Cherry Creek neighborhood; a good shopping and dining area. And it's across the street (walkable) from a Super Target with Starbucks, which is very convenient. There's also a 4-mile trail outside the hotel-nice for morning or evening walks. There are a few un-family friendly places close by (adult "toy" store & 2 dispensaries) but I never felt nervous about walking around.

author: puglab
title: Absolutely adequate
text: We stayed two nights in July, 2016. The hotel is clean and comfortable and they took our dog. There are some repairs and refurbishing that is needed but overall we were comfortable. Breakfast was good on Monday but bad on Sunday. The eggs were good on Monday but very gross and inedible on Sunday. Pool was fine but water cloudy from sunscreen. Very nice trail behind the hotel with plenty of space to walk the dog... Only 1 pile of dog waste that I saw. The kids enjoyed our stay. Very convenient to Super target. The main AC wasn't working so they brought in these portable ACs that worked but were loud but we could easily sleep with them. Everything worked which is good. This isn't the Ritz but we'd stay again. Taxes are outrageous but they don't control that. Room maid service is only during the week. Expensive for what it was but hey, it's Denver.

author: MickyO100
title: They need to pay a little more attention to the details...
text: We had a two bedroom suite for our family. The suite came equipped with the standard Staybridge amenities. The bed was comfortable and the hotel was very quiet. The laundry area had plentiful washers and dryers that were free of charge. Now to the details- The hotel could use a good scrubbing. The laundry area was very dirty. Our bathroom was not as clean as it should have been. The floor was grimy especially behind the door and in the grout. The tub was discolored and the cabinet was a bit worn. The carpet was worn or had holes in places all over the hotel. The biggest improvement could be achieved by paying a bit more attention to the breakfast. The area wasn't clean, the English muffins and the butter were frozen solid, and the OJ was basically orange water. I was surprised to see packaged Otis Spunkmier muffins, foam plates and plasticware when there were containers for silverware- but they were empty. There were two stoneware plates that were stacked with foam plates. Another guest put her English muffin in the toaster whole so she could thaw it. There was no yogurt or milk. When guests complained the answer was a curt - We are out of milk. They had cereal but no milk. And this was at 8:00- breakfast had only been available for 30 minutes. If I were to be in this part of Denver again, I would stay at a different location.

author: DHaberer
title: Shuttle drivers were high and hotel smelled like pot. Don't stay here.
text: I have never been so unsatisfied and angry about a hotel stay. First there is supposed to be a shuttle running to the expo I was a vendor at, which is also another reason why I booked this hotel. We checked in and the clerk at the front desk could not answer any questions. Her eyes were bloodshot and she was high on pot. The shuttle was so unorganized and nobody could tell me anything. In our hotel room the carpet tacks that keep the carpet down next to the tile are sticking through the carpet and I stepped on the spikes numerous time. Very painful. The thing that makes me most angry is the same lady from the front desk came to pick us up and she was high on pot! She didn’t know how to get back to the hotel and did a big circle around the convention center before she got on the right road. I am a mother and absolutely do not like someone who is high, to be driving me around and putting me and my mom’s life in danger. Too top that off, getting back from supper and walking into the lobby of the hotel is smelled like pot. So strong that it is unbearable throughout the lobby and the first floor. The same hotel clerk is standing behind the counter with, who I believe to be the manager, with bloodshot eyes again and is high. There is supposed to be a kitchenette in the room but it was pathetic. There was not a toaster in the room. I went down and asked if I could use the one in the breakfast buffet area and they said they didn’t have one and the ones they rent out were taken or broken. Do not stay at this hotel, especially if you are traveling with children.

author: 44JEFFS
title: Great Family Value
text: We stayed in a two bedroom suite with two other families for a weekend of mild weather that included a Met-Rockies game at Coors Field. The room had 1 room with 2 queen beds, 1 room with a queen bed, and a pull out couch bed in the main room. It was very comfortable and it felt very adequate to handle the 6 adults, 2 toddlers, and a baby that we had there for 3 nights. The fact that there were 2 bathrooms really was great for the amount of people we had. I thought the location was great. Downtown Denver was very accessible via this hotel. We were able to easily access the Denver Zoo, the Children's Museum (near Elitch Gardens), and Coors Field with a 15 passenger van. None of it felt very far away. In addition, there is a Super Target right across the street which helped with any comforts from home we were missing. Snooze AM Eatery is also very close and worth some extra money for great brunch food! Amenities at the hotel included an outdoor pool, a good free breakfast, and a sport court with housed 2 basketball hoops. The outdoor pool and whirlpool are a little on the small side and not very deep- but they were clean while we were there. The sport court was fun. I enjoyed being able to close every day firing up free throws and playing 21 with my brother-in-law. Both pool and sport courts close at 10. The pool and sport courts are located in a wonderful courtyard that has some nice seating and a fire pit. This hotel was free wifi that was easily accessible in our suite and never down. There is also a business center on the lower floor.

author: BillD690
title: Best in a long time
text: I have been remiss of late in reviewing my business hotels, but this one deserves a writeup. I was assigned to this area of Denver for a 3 day job. I arrived extremely late at night, 11:45 PM. I had to be at the job at 6:45am the next day. A quiet room is therefore a necessity to get as much sleep as possible. I was first assigned to a top floor room, where I could distinctly hear the rooftop machinery resonating throughout my room. But the desk clerk was nice enough to re-assign me to the next floor below, where I could barely hear anything. Let me tell you, the location, accommodation, amenities, and staff couldn't have been better on this stay. Right next door to a Target with a grocery. In the area of many restaurants. A nearby trail to exercise outdoors, if desired, and a pool/hot tub (albeit outdoors). I wish these hotels were everyplace I had to go. So, I highly recommend this place. It is relatively expensive, I paid $136 a night, but that's ostensibly due to its location, an upscale neighborhood. And the rooms have a kitchen, yet there is also a breakfast provided. Best of all possible worlds.

author: dumomich
title: Great amenities OK rooms
text: Stayed at this hotel for the denver world lacrosse championships with our lacrosse team. Check in was smooth and staff friendly. Great amenities including free laundry and fitness room. Loved that they served free buffet breakfast daily and every tues, wed and thu have a social in the evening with free food and drinks including wine and beer. Outdoor pool was good, great barbecue sitting area. One of the other teams was able to do a barbecue there. Hotel overall was nice with lots of areas to hang around. Lots of restaurants and shopping in close proximity like target across the street, grocery store close by and cherry creek mall 10 min away. Also close to university of denver and zoo. Unfortunately I just wish our room would have been a bit nicer. Was very small for the 3 of us ( queen bed with sofa bed and kitchenette) sofa bed needs thicker mattress and new springs. Couldn't get restful sleep listening to creaking all night every time you moved in that bed. Everything in room was too close to each other made you feel closed in. Would stay here again but in bigger room. Was overall impressed with this hotel as it made our long stressful tournament stay very enjoyable.

author: JKWilson195
title: Above and beyond!
text: My wife and I stayed at Staybridge Cherry Creek two nights while visiting our son in Denver. It will be our ONLY hotel in Denver from now on! Check-in time is normally 3 p.m. (check-out time is noon), but after we arrived on an early flight, I called the front desk to see if we could check in around noon. "That shouldn't be a problem", we were told. Ultimately we changed our plans and didn't arrive at the hotel until about 9 p.m. When I called to tell the front desk about our later arrival, "Your room is all set when you get here". Very gracious. Our stay at the hotel was wonderful! The suite felt enormous, with a full kitchen. The complimentary breakfast was fantastic (I judge any breakfast by the coffee, and the coffee was great!). The breakfast room is huge and welcoming. The people are friendly. There's a Super Target store right across the street. Great hotel! Staybridge, well done!

author: drlahiri
title: A real home away from home
text: I was little apprehensive initally to get a room 4.8 miles away from the convention center. But once I reached 4220 E my unhappiness/ apprehensions evaporated. It took little over 30 minutes to reach the beautiful Cherry Creek area from the Denver International Airport. The check-in time is 3 pm. As there was no scope for an early check in I had to book it one day early. The huge two bedroom apartment was an overkill for a single customer like me who was not traveling with family this time.It was literally more than enough for me to be the sole occupant of a two-bedroom/two bath suite with a fully-equipped kitchen. The shuttle service to and fro the convention center(hotel is not responsible) was sluggish, so had to rent a cab(USD 15 each way) most of the time. The temperature was freezing(even minus 7 or 8 Celsius) outside but the whole building was nicely kept warm and comfortable. During happy hours (5.30-7.20 pm)on Tuesday/Wednesday and Thursday complimentary refreshment(with drinks) are served. Breakfast spread was nice, but bit monotonous which was probably expected. The business center and the convenience store is open 24x7. While the business center was free, the store was little over priced. But, when you have a huge Target just across the road why should you bother at all. I enjoyed my morning walk for a couple of days during my stay at Staybridge. They have a lovely walking trail around and the surroundings are very pleasant. The staffs are polite, helpful and cordial. I was especially touched one morning when I was waiting for my conference shuttle at the end of the corridor opening to the rear side of the hotel, the front desk girl came running to inform me that a cab has just arrived on the front side and as the shuttle service is uncertain, if I want, she can request the cab to wait for me. This kind of personal service we don't expect in many big 5 star hotels.

author: whitespruce
title: Perfect hotel near hospitals
text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel December 9 - 27th. I was being treated at National Jewish Hospital and University of Colorado Hospital. The Staybridge staff was extraordinary. Always nice and so very helpful. The room was a large one bedroom suite, with a very fair price for long term hospital stay. Kitchen was handy for us, as well as living room for viewing TV at different times and locations. They served a very nice breakfast each day and the bonus was dinner was served Tues, Wed, Thursday nights for free, with a wine or beer. I've never been to a hotel that served us dinner for free. We were able to meet people and visit next to the fireplace after a long day of appointments. The shuttle van took us to NJH each day and back, very handy. It goes 3 miles from the hotel. The van driver is super helpful and gave us a list of busses that would get us other places. There is a lovely walking trail outside of the hotel to get some fresh air, especially nice while recuperating. We did use the free laundry and there was a decent workout area, all nice and clean. I would absolutely stay here again--and I will at my 6 month check up. Thank you, staff, for making a tough time for us, a manageable stay. Leslie & Jerry from Alaska

author: MrsSJF
title: Great Location, comfortable rooms
text: My husband and I were in Denver for a business trip. I chose the Staybridge suites for the location and its favorable reviews. Our room was great- It was spacious and comfortable and clean too! It overlooked the Cherry creek Biking/walking trail. The outside courtyard/pool area was beautiful. I enjoyed relaxing by the pool a couple of times during our stay. The only negative was the strong cigarette smell in the lobby and hallways. Fortunately, the rooms did not smell. The hotel is in the midst of a renovation, and it is my understanding that the carpets in the lobby and hallways will be replaced....hopefully this will eliminate the odor....although I think they still are allowing smoking on certain floors. The location was perfect. We walked :to the mall, to eat, and to the grocery store. It was also very nice to be able to take walks along the Cherry Creek Biking/walking trail that was just on the other side of the parking lot. Staff were professional and ready to help in whatever way they could. The check in and Check out process was quick and efficient. I think once the renovations are complete this will be an awesome place to stay.

author: weyes
title: Would give 3.5. Service not as great as other Staybridge Suites...
text: If I could give a 3.5 I would. I've stayed at 3 different Staybridge Suites, two in Indiana and this one. This was not as nice as the one in Carmel, IN, but definitely a lot better than the one in downtown Indy. The room was nice and spacious and clean, like I expected. Breakfast the first day did not have bacon or sausage. The second morning they were out of every coffee except 1 and the cranberry juice was out. When people asked to re-stock the staff was somewhat rude. Granted, the hotel was busy for large event in town. The mall is within walking distance on the trail. My friend and I felt safe walking to the mall on a weekday morning. You can walk to Target from this hotel as well. Workout facility is sparse, 2 treadmills, 1 bike, 1 eliptical. Free weights consisted of 2 5lb and 1 8lb weight, I think the others were missing. Laundry facilities right in workout room if you needed them. Front desk was helpful in calling a cab for us.

author: freddie1933
title: Nice hotel with a Great Location
text: I stayed at Staybridge all last week for work. The hotel is very nice. It's a typical Staybridge Suites,with the studio room, small kitchen, free breakfast and a happy hour. The hotel is still in good shape but does show it's age in a few spots. I am not sure if it's a non-smoking hotel but you definitely can smell smoke in the hallways. The location of the hotel is perfect, especially for the price. I am a runner and chose the hotel strictly based on it's location to the Cherry Creek trail. It's literally on the trail. It's a little over a mile walk on the trail to the Cherry Creek North shopping/dining district. There's a lot of restaurants and shopping in this area. It's a higher end area that is very safe to walk. The Cherry Creek Mall is also there as well. The hotel is right across the street from a Super Target, Sports Authority, Applebees and several other retail businesses. The staff is very friendly and helpful. The maids do a light daily housekeeping and will only change the bed sheets once a week. This is pretty standard for business hotels like these so it wasn't really an issue for me. Overall, it's a good hotel with a great location.

author: ToniN606
title: Wonderful place for Family to stay!
text: Such a lovely time we all had there!! We had four rooms for our family of 16 from 3 cities and were so pleased. I'm sure we're all spoiled now to go back to 'just a room with a bed'. The staff was always ready with a smile and pleasant ways. The front desk staff was very accommodating to our check in needs. The rooms more lovely than the photos show and handy to have two bathrooms. The kitchen in the rooms well appointed and clean. A nice variety of choices at breakfast met the diverse needs of our group and lots of room to sit together. Somehow though - we'd been there two days before we found the room with computers (FREE!) and the DVDs to borrow for our rooms (a nice selection). We walked on the bike path a couple of times and walked to Target and the King Sooper nearby. The shuttle was new and nice and handy for a trip to the zoo. We do wish there was information available at the hotel about the light rail. Hmmm, maybe it was in the DENVER booklet in the rooms - that was very helpful. It would have been nice for some kind of discount available on the large suites. Recycle bins would have been a nice touch. I wish our group had used the shuttle more and tried the light rail. Denver is so lovely to observe instead of 'just driving and being busy with that.' SO, overall, we really enjoyed our visit and would readily come back to this or another Staybridge Suites.

author: AztecsU2
title: Not worth it
text: I attended the CEDIA Expo and the only reason I stayed at this hotel was because this was where I was assigned by the trade show. They block rooms at almost all the Denver area hotels and assign each attendee to whichever hotel they have available for you. I paid $189 a night and was very surprised that this was a the discounted negotiated rate! Sure it's not too far from the Convention Center (a 10-15 minute drive).... Sure, the room is spacious... but do you really need a kitchenette with a LOUD refrigerator? No. I stayed in room 313 and the regular air conditioning unit was broken so they had this portable floor unit that was so loud during the night. Without screens on my windows (after looking outside at other rooms, I honestly think mine was the only one without), I could not have the windows open at night for fear that bugs, mosquitoes, etc, would creep in. The bed was hard as a ROCK. I had so much trouble sleeping the two nights I was there. The pro's... the staff was friendly although they did not have any other rooms available to move me to. The breakfast is fairly adequate but I only stuck with cereal and toast. Business Center was free but the internet connection was SLOOOOOOW. Bottom line... overpriced and just NOT worth it. I'd only stay there again if I was forced to, like I was this time.

author: ShutterbugLisa
title: Not What We Expected
text: My husband and I booked a block of rooms for our wedding at this hotel. We were excited to offer our guests rooms that had kitchenettes. They were appreciative of that. Another reason we booked here was because they offered the best rate in the area. For what you get at this hotel, the rate was good. The issues came with the extras that we required as a wedding party. When my guests called to make reservations, they weren't always put on the wedding block. I had to call every week and make sure that they were given the discount and put into our block. Then, I asked if they could give each of our guests a gift basket when they checked in. They assured me that this was something they did often, and it would be no problem. I made beautiful baskets, but they weren't given to everyone. I had to ask for them back and hand them out myself when we visited with our guests. The worst was that they were supposed to have a room for us on our wedding night. When we showed up after the reception, still dressed in our wedding clothes, we were not greeted with a smile. We were instead told that our room was not available. The guy at the front desk could not find our reservation and was very rude to us on our wedding night of all nights! The rooms were okay, but the service wasn't. I would not suggest this hotel when there are others in the immediate area that cost just $10 more a night.

author: Jakentucker
title: Suite & Scary
text: First, Cudos to Brenda Osborne, Rep from Staybridge, for helping us with receiving a Hospital rate for the 2 bdrm suites (139 from 179/night); and with all helpful info. for our week in Denver at a developmental treatment center for our children. The room was nice enough, nice kitchen, bedrooms, and meals, etc., but it was the attention to detail and information that was, well, pathetic. We contacted the front office 4 days in a row to get our ice maker fixed....Nothing. Nothing. Nothing. We stopped asking. We asked two days in a row to stop paper deliver. Nothing, Nothing, Nothing. In one bedroom the backing of the carpet was showing and we would step on the nails coming up from the carpet -- one time drawing a small amount of blood -- based on our other attempts to discuss matters with the front desk, we didn't even bother to bring this up at the front desk -- as it seems apparent to us that these problems (incl. the ice maker) had probably been evident for some time. We asked for our DVD player in the room to get fixed. The 3rd day it started working. We don't know if they fixed it or not, because, you guessed it, we heard nothing, nothing, nothing. The breakfast and Supper's were very good and the location is great. Just don't come expecting anything that looks like attention and service from the front desk.

author: empathology
title: Old English country house
text: Stayed for 1 night after arriving on the ferry at Harwich (40 minutes away). With an evening arrival, it was hard to find in the dark - you should follow the instructions that the owner provides very carefully indeed! The owner made sure we were comfortable and that we had everything we needed, including that essential for English tea drinkers, fresh milk! Breakfast was splendid with every taste catered for (including gluten-free cornflakes - who knew such a thing existed?!). The bathroom had plenty of fluffy towels and ointments. And whilst the bed was most comfortable, the chairs in the room (and at the dining table for breakfast) were dismally old. As you sat down, you felt as though you might fall through. And getting up form some of the very low chairs required a black-belt in yoga! (Even the owner admitted they were a little old). They may be in keeping with the antique style of the house, but there comes a time when comfort comes first. The room also suffered from a mob of flies. Fortunately, I found a can of fly-spray close by and that did the trick but it kept us busy for 20-minutes. Country living in the fields was the response. Overall a very nice place to stay and the small town of Hadliegh down the road is utterly delightful. However, I'll pass on 5-stars as I feel there's a few fundamental items to pull it down.

author: BrendanMartin
title: A Suffolk B&B with that majestic touch
text: It's hard to think of Holbecks House as a B&B. It is a large 18th century manor house set in the Suffolk countryside at Hadleigh, about 12 miles from Ipswich. Set in its own expansive grounds Holbecks House offers stylish country living at a B&B price. (Not surprising really as it just offers B&B.) The rooms are spacious and en-suite. Well, ours was but our companions was not. But I think the adjoining bathroom was for their exclusive use. (Not sure about that.) Across the corridor from us was another large bedroom with massive bathroom but it also had a medium-sized sitting room. I'd call it a suite. Our bed was very comfortable and we slept well. In the morning we enjoyed a cooked-to-order breakfast from a wide menu. As well as the traditional full English and its component parts, we could have had porridge or kippers. They was also a well-stocked buffet bar or cereals, yoghurt, juices and home-made plum compote. The plums came from Holbecks House own orchard. Run by Perry Coysh and his friendly family, this really is a treat in which to stay. We were staying at Holbecks House as we were attending a wedding nearby but frankly, I would love to go back just to have a chill-out weekend in Suffolk. Check it out at www.holbeckshouse.com

author: 102emilyg
title: Peaceful weekend away in beautiful surroundings
text: Great place to go for a peaceful few days away. Beautiful house in stunning grounds. Perry is a wonderful host and the breakfast is delicious. Guests sit around big dining table with views of the lovely garden. We had the smallest room with a private bathroom but no ensuite. When we stay again we would endeavour to have one of the larger rooms with ensuite - the Constable or the Gainsborough. Both absolutely lovely and very large. A really cosy comfortable house and nothing is too much trouble for Perry. Minor criticism is hit and miss Internet access - mostly miss during our stay. Overall though would recommend this as a really lovely place to stay for anyone wanting a relaxing quiet break. Hadleigh and surround villages have plenty of great places to eat and drink. We ate in the Kings Head in Hadleigh the first night. Lovely meal and very reasonable. Also great beer. The second night we went to The Bildeston Crown, High Street, Bildeston. Lovely bar with big open fire and great meal with superb beer and wine. Looked like was going to be expensive but was in fact very reasonable.

author: DDdaddy
title: Just what the doctor ordered
text: Was thinking about writing a stinking review to put other people off booking. But the better part of me won out. Just. Not really a b&b as I conceive it. More of a cross between a boutique hotel and staying with friends at their country home (would that I had such friends). We were back in the UK for Christmas and New Year, mostly trudging between different parents/parents-in-law and wanted something a little bit special for a proper holiday. Holbecks House was perfect and exceeded our expectations (already high having read some of the earlier reviews). The room was large, great views across fabulous (and accessible) grounds and a wondrous bed. Bathroom huge and luxurious. Lots of very thoughtful touches (really nice range of teas in the room, genuinely interesting books you can pick up and read, relaxing and cosy drawing room with sofas, torch if you want to walk into the village) that speak of hosts who really care about their guests. And the breakfasts...I didn't think people really made that amount of effort any more. I suspect that the marmalades and jams may have even been home made. The fruit compote certainly was. If you have any requirement to find a B&B within 10 miles of Holbecks house you would be crazy to go anywhere else. It is worth 20 mins of anyone's driving time. If you are looking for a quintessentially British experience in gorgeous countryside in the care of people who know how to make you feel comfortable and make the effort to put you at your ease, then this is the place.

author: worldsnapzone
title: An unforgettable trip lifetime !! 😍😍
text: we wish to extend our sincere thanks to each and every member of Karma team, right from assisting in our bookings, to our enjoyable stay at Karma Chakra from 16th of March to 23rd of March 2019. The plans and bookings were made for our first stay, at such a short notice with the help of your team member, and that too by a senior. It was a never ending joy visiting God's own country and as we head towards our first home, we wish we could stay more at our second home in Chakra. There was no difficulty reaching the resort as the cab was waiting for us at the airport, we had a nice welcome drink on arrival and we moved to our nice room......which we never expected to be so special.....view of lovely lake and greenery makes the room so special...it can't be described in words. The housekeeping staff was really nice and we never had to tell anything to her. Everything was just perfect, from cleaning to changing towels every day. The maintenance staff was also very helpful...our air conditioner was not working and he came at odd hours to fix it. The chef prepares mouth watering food and the presentation was also too good, with smiling face of host. Not to mention, each and every staff member is really sweet, with smiling faces and ever ready to assist, approachable within minutes. To our surprise, holi was celebrated in a full fledged manner at the resort. Even everyday they called upon us to participate in the events organized by the team. We also spent time in the pool which was kept clean all the time. It was a relief from the heat sitting in the pool, in a quiet environment, with the sound of chirping birds and quak quak of ducks. We had a wonderful and best vacation we ever had. It was a relief from our hectic daily life. It's a pain now to get back. Thank you team Karma Chakra and everyone who helped us visiting Kerala. Thank you so much !! #experiencekarma #happycustomers

author: NormH14
title: A Peaceful, Out of the Way Setting
text: What an amazing week we had at Karma Chakra. From the first greeting, we could feel the peace and tranquility. Unhurried, friendly, very welcoming and helpful Managers and Staff were a pleasure to meet and to get to know. Chef Pratheese and the dining room staff were exceptionally welcoming, offering delicious options on their comprehensive menu and adjusting to the tastes and appetites of their guests with appreciative flexibility. Lijo George, Front Office Manager, was very visible and provided interesting and valuable suggestions and information. Antony and his housekeeping staff provided service above and beyond and we particularly appreciated the efforts of Minto in keeping our spacious, well appointed room, very clean. We had the pleasure of a 5-hour lunch cruise on Lake Vembanad. Karma Chakra owns it’s own houseboat and offers a variety of cruises to suit everyone. We appreciated the wonderful opportunity of not only cruising the 2nd largest Lake in Asia, but also enjoyed seeing, hearing and photographing the beautiful birds, interesting rice paddies and tropical lushness of the journey. No need to pre-book, line-up, or travel. The Houseboat, Captain Prinod and Cook Jayram are part of Karma Chakra Resort. The day was most memorable and the lunch was delicious. Set in beautifully landscaped grounds, the sparkling, clean, refreshing swimming pool was well maintained and very welcoming as was the entire Resort. Anju, Activities Coordinator, provides interesting opportunities and programs for all ages. We were very grateful for the opportunity to accompany Anju on a walk around the grounds as she provided the names and purpose of the unusual tropical plants. She also spent the time to write the English names of each one for us. A talented artist, Anju encourages artistic and creative opportunities. I personally enjoyed being invited to watch Chef Pratheese prepare Keralan Curry - a very informative and tasty presentation. We will savour our memories of the time spent at Karma Chakra and thank you to Jaison Anithanam, General Manager, and all his friendly, enjoyable and very efficient managers and staff. We would welcome an opportunity to visit you all again.

author: Vaishali0918
title: It’s the staff ALL the way!!!
text: We just got back from a five day visit to Karma Chakra Kumarakom. The property is small in comparison to others nearby but nevertheless wonderful and has everything one would want on a holiday. It’s just at the backwaters and the view is so soothing. They have a gazebo where one can just sit and stare out all day. Rooms are good in size with a balcony for each. They could do with a slight renovation with some walls, bathroom door knobs etc. Housekeeping was brilliant taking care of our needs. Food was great, whether at the restaurant or room service. There were enough vegetarian choices...though I strongly feel they could expand their menu especially for those who land up staying for more than four days. That’s probably the only reason I’m not giving this place a five star. Spa rates were reasonable and we indulged in a few very relaxing ones. There’s the swimming pool, gymnasium, badminton, table tennis and carrom for entertainment. Gym could use an upgrade in equipment’s for sure. There’s really nothin nearby except the bird sanctuary, a drift wood museum and a few spice shops. We did hire a scooty for the day visit to Kottayam. But above all, it’s the staff that makes this place a great visit. From the reception to the spa, restaurant, games organiser, housekeeping...they are always ready to help you and always smiling!
