This warmth is what made our vacay super! Thank you!

author: PriscilaP1514
title: Memorable
text: we recently returned from vacation where we spent around one week at this resort. There were hubby, my 6 yr old kid and myself. Room: Really nice, spacious and all what a family needs. The bed comfortable and it accommodates easily the family. lots of channels on tv....so great choice if we do not really speak the local languages. Amenities: nice pool, garden though small but it does not matter as it is a small resort and everyone gets its privacy easily. the spa small with only one therapist - unfortunately never had the slots to do it - this is something which can be improved. the recreation area, the gym, yoga rm all very nice....just need to ensure that the mosquito repellents are always present as this is very annoying. the wifi connection was not always good and it is an issue if u always need to be connected. restaurant - good service. nevertheless there is lack of typical kerala dishes on the menu...which unfortunately u need to drive to find in other restaurants, and this is not quite easy everyday. i would suggest a wider variety of seafood, duck and other local dishes. the staff over there are always welcoming and always ready to help. very joyful....very warming...very smiling....homely what! Overall a very pleasant stay and really looking forward for a second time.

author: heets1998
title: Amazing stay with a First-Class Service
text: I was here for a week in october, ie., 23rd Oct - 30th Oct 2017 and from my very entry to the resort till the moment we left, everything was excellent. We were given a warm welcome by the staff. Coming to the rooms, they were SPOTLESS !!! So far I've been to many resorts ranging from country club to sterling but none of the rooms was as good as these. We had two rooms and each of them was the same but a bit different when it came to view outside, both our rooms were on the ground floor and provided us with a damn spacious room and a patio in the backside with seating arrangement and gave us an enchanting view of Vembanad Lake, Kerala's biggest lake as what i heard from the locals. Also, the rooms were close to Swimming Pool. The resort is on the lake and hence to go from one place to another, bridges are provided everywhere. The scenics were at their best from the resort. Now, the resort is a bit far from kochi, munnar and other sightseeing places so take my advices, plan a trip in a way that you visit the resort last and complete all sightseeing before checking in here as Ms. Anju will take care that you and your family has tons of amazing activities to spend time, she has arranged amazing activities including karaoke night. The pool was kept so clean, you could actually see everything happening inside pool from the outside and leveled so well, everyone (except ones above 4'5") could enjoy the whole pool as the deepest point is just 4 feet so everyone could enjoy the whole pool. Also, at nights the pools looked just amazing. The room service was surely excellent and humble. If you're lucky, you might find a coconut in fallen in your patio, just call room service, they will break it open for you. The food in the waterside restaurant was amazing but I'll talk about it in the review z Lastly, the only thing painful is the fact that the resort has only 24 rooms and they are so much in demand, they don't accomodate walk-in customers and still do they have so much bookings that you have to plan out well in advanced to get a reservation.

author: harpal1266
title: Karma Chakra Kumarakom scenic and beautiful resort to stay with family.
text: It was my second trip to Kerala (Gods own country), but first in this resort. All of the staff members are fantastic. The food was very good. All the boys in restaurant are very enthusiastic and never hesitate in explaining the dishes and best of all serve with smile. Very nice lake view resort. A beautiful location adjacent to Vembanad lake. We enjoyed the serene and natural beauty by sitting on the bank of Vembanad lake, India's second largest lake. This is nicely build property. The food and recreation facilities are quite good and plenty in number. I may look for a good offer to be here but not at an extremely high price. The room on the ground first floor gives an awesome view of the lake. Room is quite clean and spacious. Food in the Restaurant is good but pricey. Beautiful Attwood's Bar, but unfortunately only beer and wines served which once again was very expensive so hardly anyone uses it. A good place to relax. If tthe food and liquour were more reasonably priced it would prevent people going to nearby seedy joints and end up with a bad stomach, but overall it was very awesome and beautiful stay there.

author: TAUAKATU
title: August break in laid-off Kumarakom village
text: We took a week break during the off-season in Kumarakom village to get away from the maddening rush of work life. I don't think we could have made a better choice than Karma Chakra. The resort is best located on the waterfront and you get an amazing view of the lake. It has all the facilities to keep you engaged or just stretch your legs and forget everything. The few rooms at the resort will give you a very exquisite feeling and you'll end up knowing everyone if you stay there for a couple of days. The staff is very courteous and always there to help you out. I'll rate them highly for being able to manage out the little niggle that we faced with hot water. If everything is working fine, it looks very artificial. The way they sorted out the issue shows how well they are prepared for anything not working fine. Everyday will start with a schedule of activities. This actually kept my daughter engaged and we could breathe easy. Activities for the grown-ups are in the evening and definitely, participate before you go for your dinner. We primarily dined at "The Waterfront". The Chef was very polite and treated us with some of the best local cuisines. We loved every dish we had there. To top it all, the meals were not costly at all as we normally see in a restaurant that charges a premium for being in a resort. Finally, I definitely recommend to take the BoatHouse and if possible, the luch cruise. It'll take you to some of the hiden treasures of backwaters, halt at some place where you can buy some fresh fish/prawns/crabs, and finally enjoy them cooked on the boat. Thanks for hosting us and a wonderful time!

author: 32riteshm
title: Amazing experience with family at Karma Chakra Kumarakom
text: We visited Karma Chakra Kumarakom May 13 to May 17, 2017 with my wife and son. We were greeted at the reception, served with complimentary drinks and led to our room. The room and the bathroom was very clean and bed nicely laid. The entire resort is beautiful, clean and excellently maintained. This is one of the best resorts on the bank of Vembanand lake. The staff is very courteous and cooperative. Every evening the staff makes sure they arrange activities like tambola or group games to keep families engaged. They have a spa inside which is state of art. Restaurant food is excellent and guests can either have food there or order from room. For us the best part was the houseboat ride arranged by the resort to Allepey, day ride for 5 hrs. This was a luxurious boat with very nice driver named Vinod and cook by the name of Saneesh. They took very good care of us and we had sumptuous spread of food including both veg and non veg. We als had a resort organised day trip to Munnar with driver Joseph. He is a very nice person who also acted as a guide for us and was a very good driver. Overall we enjoyed the beauty of the resort with excellent cooperation from staff and had a luxurious stay enjoying the facilities like pool, games, restaurant and spa. Thanks to the entire staff of Karma Chakra, Kumarakom for making our stay a memorable one.

author: 105ariesf
title: Awesome swimming pool, good food and clean rooms
text: Firstly, only reason I have given 4 is because the food pricing at the restaurant is very costly. Now let me add the information which made 4 stars. Location: Its right on the Vembanad lake, and the view is spectacular. My family loved the view and the place a lot. Rooms: Its awesome, very clean, excellent AC. Went has a family, booked 2 rooms (101 and 102). Room 101 is excellent. Big rooms, very spacious. Food: The restaurant is very clean and the food is very nice (tried the Appam - Chicken stew, Allepy fish curry, Chicken fried rice, steam rice, the Velmoute Chicken soup, pork coconut curry, and two desserts which I don't remember). All of them were very good, but, when we ordered prawns, highly disappointed. Staff and House-Keeping: Fabulous. Very cordial staff and house-keeping always came on time and kept our rooms very clean. There is also kids fun activities available, which will keep kids occupied during the afternoon and even in the evening. However, I would like to state this, the swimming pool is very good. My son enjoyed it a lot, both morning and evening. Its open from 8 am till 8 pm. Overall, we had a very relaxing time, and even booking taxis wasn't a problem as the front desk has all sight-seeing and taxi facilities. I am sure to visit this place once again (God willing).

author: g0wrishankaru
title: Awesome and Blissful Experience
text: My Third Visit to Grove within a year. It is a perfect place to relax and stay clam. I have stayed for a week in Feb which is just on the edge of the lake it was a wonderful stay. Special thanks to Jaison for having a such a wonderful team to take care of each Guest. We will be back every year. Food was excellent. Good place To stay for a quite and relaxing. The staffs was very friendly and care taking. Food in water side was too good with buffet breakfast and live appam, omelet counters. Staffs Chief Prateesh, Arun, Divya, Ashiq, Saneesh, Anju, Nitin, all we're taking friendly and made our stay memorable. Each and every one remembered us and greeted and spoke to us too friendly. Chief walked to your table every day and served us with delicious food. Daily evening we had fun games, Housie etc., which was good to play and learn. The swimming pool was one on the best just over looking the lake and a perfect place to be for sunset. Will be back....Again Soon..... Special thanks to everyone from Front office to Cleaners for have a such a wonderful place Clean and Clam to stay relaxed and Enjoy a peaceful Vacation.

author: Kamal1943
title: Nature Lovers Paradise with Modern Ammenities
text: We spent a week from 1st to 7th October in this picturesque resort along with our friends who wanted to celebrate their 40th anniversary quietly away from the chaos of Delhi. It gives me immense satisfaction to write this review and praise the sincerity and professionalism of the staff members in making my friends’ anniversary most memorable one and our stay in the resort very comfortable and satisfying. The resort is around 80km from Kochi airport in the midst of a typical village of Kerala, Kumarakom, on the bank of Vembanad Lake. Besides a number of other resorts and residences of the local people there are no shops or eating joints nearby till you reach the main road which is about 2km away. But there is no need to go out of the resort as there are number of activities to keep one busy – swimming, angling, indoor games, SPA and just enjoying the fresh air and the beauty of the lake all alone or with your friends and music. Of course one can go for the early morning walk in the surrounding village to get a feel of the rustic life, enjoy the choir in the nearby Church or appreciate the beauty of the variety of flowers on the roadside. Spending time leisurely on the lake side was a rewarding experience with a number of houseboats sailing along, the fishermen in catamarans catching fish or the flock of birds flying by. The nights changed the resort into a dreamland with innumerable lights, soft music, cool breeze from the lake and its waves dancing in the moonlight. The twinkling lights from the fishermen’s nets on the other side of the lake added to the nights’ beauty of the resort. The food served in the ‘Waterside’ restaurant was good and reasonably priced with variety including typical Kerala cuisine. The Chef took care of the requirements of each guest personally which added to the taste and flavor of the food of one’s choice. The candle light dinner with cake and flowers, organized by the staff for our friends’ anniversary was a unique experience for all of us. The nearest town from the resort is Kottayam, 15 km away, where one can go for shopping of silk sarees and spices or venture to try out different food in the restaurants. If you do not have a car with you like us, you can as well hire a covered auto-rickshaw, similar to a Nano car, for adventurous experience. Do not forget to taste the sweet water of green coconuts on the roadside. But be careful about the roadside restaurants. Finally if one loves Nature, a visit to Kumarakom and a trip in a houseboat in the Vembanad lake and its back waters is a must if not for overnight stay, at least for a few hours.

author: mohancp
title: Excellent!!!
text: We stayed for a week and no words to mention about the resort, absolutely amazing!!!. Best part of this resort is the way each and every staff takes care of you. They are very polite, courteous and gives atmost importance to you. When i was staying, it was overbooked and thanks to Mr Lijo who arranged a overnight stay in houseboat with all conveniences at no charge. When i complained about A/C not working, they immediately came and checked and replaced the faulty part in A/C immediately. Even in restaurant also when there is a delay they waived off the amount and they apologise which a very rare quality from restaurant folks. Food is great with both veg/non-veg in restaurant. I know these are one off instances but that also they took care of atmost priority for you to have a wonderful and excellent stay. Location wise, it is at great location, at the bank of Vembanad lake and overlooking at it. Special thanks to Anju who always kept engaging with her entertainment activities. We went to Athirapally waterfalls and its a must to see. Temples were good. Mr. Lijo helped me in booking stay at Coimbatore on my way back to Bangalore through Coimbatore. I would like to give more than 5 star rating.

author: 786sunils
title: A pleasant stay.....
text: We visited Kerala first time and choose this unit. As soon as we entered the property we can see the smile in our faces.... we stayed for 4 days from 1st July 2016 to 5th July 2016. All staff members were always ready to help... the best part of this unit was its design and location of its swimming pool. swimming in the pool and watching the lake was a nice experience. Restaurant and the food was good. Ms Divya helped us a lot from beginning to end. But I felt that the resort needs a paint and a high maintenance inside the room and bathrooms. The lawn door of the room was not fixed properly and had some space. We found some spiders in the room every day and called for removing them... if the hotel work out on maintenance, I am sure it will be one of the best unit in Kumarakom... We hired a house boat from hotel only and it turned out one of the best experience of our holidays ... and I suggest everyone to go for house boat as its a unique experience and in India this is the only place that have backwater. Overall a nice stay..... t from hotel only and it turned out one of the best experience of our holidays ... and I suggest everyone to go for house boat as its a unique experience and in India this is the only place that have backwater. Overall a nice stay.....

author: Sunil99
title: Very good
text: This is exactly what I had envisioned when I had become a member of the RGBC group 8 years ago. It has a feeling of the Taj group. I was very pleasantly surprised as soon as I entered the place. The photographs don't do it justice.The view is spectacular. The backwaters are within touching distance. The cleaning of the rooms could do with a bit of a lift. Our room had to be cleaned once again after we had checked in. The food is tasty but not authentic Kerala food. It has a bit of north Indian touch to it. I highly recommend the Balinese massage by Dinesh. It was one of the best massages I've had in a long time. The resort has there own houseboat for which they charge Rs 4500/2hours. There is a small Kerala restaurant a kilometer from the resort on the main road called Machinaria ( I think ) which serves traditional and absolutely authentic Kerala food. Auto's are a plenty to take you there. The only bummer is that you have to sit in the bar to have a drink. The other option is to have room service. I will definitely be visiting this place again and I recommend it to other members.

author: 853nitum
title: Memorable Kerala Trip
text: I finally take my time out to write a review of our stay at Royal Grove. It was our third holiday at the Royal resorts, and Grove turned out to be the best so far. We stayed from 11th Jan to 18th Jan 2016 at this resort, which I suppose is the best time to be there. The location of the resort is the biggest strength and the view of Lake Vembanad was breathtaking. The Royal welcome was much more than we expected. We were given a room at the pool side which overlooked the lake. I could spend hours only sitting at the balcony of my room. The kids loved it to every bits too. The room as expexted was luxurious. We spent 4 out of 7 days within the resort and didn't feel like going out at all, such was the coziness of the place. My son spent most of his time at the kid's section or at the pool. Food was good, but they can add more on the menu. The overall experience was overwhelming and we couldn't believe it was time already to bid adieu. I look forward to another such stay at Royal Grove in the near future. Thanks once again to the entire team at Grove for this pleasant and memorable stay

author: 128rahulc
title: Get all latest information here
text: The right time to go to this place is from Oct to Jan. I've been to this property and found the following points to highlight to all my readers... 1. The hotel/resort has 24 rooms (approximately), rooms are very good. 2. The rooms placed in the first block i.e. first block from the lake has an amazing view from the room, it has complete panoramic lake view. 3. Room services are good. Staff have pretty positive attitude to serve you and make your stay as comfortable as possible. 4. The don't serve buffet meals if the occupancy is less.This is to be considered and understood. 5. No 24 Hrs restaurant or room service. 6. Very important, the menu card has many options but disappointingly they are served as per the allotted timings. 7. They provide complimentary wifi and the speed was 256 kpbs You may opt for this property if you have their Timeshare membership or you can rent it through some member, the way I did. Good luck.

author: 408chaitanyar
title: Just the break I needed
text: Being an Emcee, its difficult to find a break in between events that happen on a regular basis. Finally, I combined a conference I was supposed to host in Trivandrum, with a holiday at Kumarakom. I've been a Royal Resorts member since 2006. I've always only traveled to Goa for a holiday and needed a different location. My wife, son and I flew from Mumbai to Trivandrum, and then drove down to Kumarakom in a car borrowed from a friend. Although the distance is 180 kms, it took us full 5 hours to reach as there are many small towns on the way making us slow down. It was a bit difficult to find the resort as the approach road to go to the resort is very small. Had to make multiple phone calls to finally reach the resort. The very first look and feel of the resort is very welcoming and cozy. The silence around made the back water waves sound very soothing. the check in was very smooth and the staff was very welcoming and cooperative. We quickly left our luggage in the room and headed to the restaurant on the premises. I was a bit skeptical about finding tasty vegetarian food but I must say I was pleasantly delighted to see that the food served was not only delicious, but very home like. Next 3 days were spent lazying at the pool, and roaming around the resort to nearby places. We took a few hours trip in the boat and also explored local cuisines. My 3 year old son enjoyed feeding the fish and running behind the ducks. I had to leave for Trivandrum on the 4th day as I had work commitments but my wife and son stayed back for another day and then took a train to Trivandrum from Kotayam the next day to join me. All in all, it was a well deserved break and I got to spend quality time with my family.

author: manhew
title: Ideal Retreat
text: Located adjacent to the Vembanad Lake, the property is quiet new. The rooms are spacious and offer a remarkable view of the lake. The view from the Pool, Restaurant and the Bar is again superb. The sunset should never be missed from the lawns of the resort. Facets that need improvement are the front office which should do good if they provide a list of local religious / cultural events that one can visit. The front office staff less the Manager need to be trained better. The Kitchen needs to improve on its Local Cuisine. In case you are not a member of the Royal resorts, i.e. either have come in on a Time share like I did ,or a walk in, the turn off is when they try to hard-sell the concept of Royal resorts. Advice to Guests:- 1. Try to get a bicycle/two wheeler to your disposal at all times. Four wheeler parking apart from the resort is difficult to find and taxis/autos expensive. 2. Sample the food at Kumarakom Toddy shop (Opposite Taj Kumarakom) for its authentic local cuisine.3. Depend on the State beverages outlet for your liquor the resort only serves Wine and Beer. 4. A Budget traveller should not be tempted by the glib talk for the resort house boat (Rs11,000 for a Night halt) or any other House Boat from the boat jetty (Rs 7000 for a night halt). Try out a motor boat which will cover equal distances as that of a house boat or better still follow the schedule I took. State Water Transport Department (SWTD) boat from Kumarakom Boat Jetty to Muhhama across Vembanad Lake >>> Auto to Kayyipuram >>>Shared Motor Boat to Pathiramanal Island>>> return to Muhhama>>> Taxi to Allapuzha>>> SWTD boat from Allapuza boat jetty to Kottayam>>> Auto to Kottayam Bus stand>>> Return from Kottayam to Kumarakom Boat Jetty by Bus. I got to cover all forms of transport that the locals use and interacted with them for a good measure.

author: HemanathD
title: Soul Soothing and Mesmerising view
text: A beautiful resort on the banks of the scenic Vembanad Lake, Asia's largest fresh water Lake. Our family stayed here for a short break during the month of May 2015. One can have a breathtaking view of the great Vembanad Lake from the vantage points gazing endlessly at the drifting weeds and houseboats. This boutique resort has a marvelous architecture, with every room facing the Lake. We stayed at room 105 which is right on the Lake banks. The resort has a SPA and a Houseboat of its own. Unlike other Karma properties this are hotel units with no Kitchen and no snack bars and grocery store. The nearest town is 3 kms away. The restaurant servers good meals but bit expensive. There are no eatery or shops near by. Polite and courteous Staff and very friendly GM. My kid enjoyed a lot at the kids pool and the 3 monkey's club activities. Feeding the fish was his favourite. The Resort and the Lake gives a spectacular and soul soothing view during rains. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LWjS22mhAo0 The Resort has a unique program of wine tasting for the owner members, its on all Mondays between 6 pm to 7 pm with free unlimited wine and beer. Kumarakam Bird Century and near by places are a worth visit. Would recommend a own vehicle for transport. We had a highly refreshing holiday and looking forward to visit again during rains. Do take a look at the below link for a short video of the resort. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jl_xTY1jwSk

author: Hitanshu_Agrawal
title: Nice place to relax
text: We spent 4 days at Royal Grove in last week of May'15. The resort is situated along the Vembanad river (the longest in the country) and adjacent to all the good resorts in Kumarakom. The place is around 5 km from the boat jetty. Overall the place felt new, nicely done-up and well maintained. Staff was courteous and prompt. Food was good, especially given the fact that there was no good option anywhere around the area. Backwater channels through the resort is a novel idea, though some parts of it were very stagnant and thereby unclean. Room was spacious and clean. We switched to an upper room from ground floor room allotted earlier, for the view. Only problem in the room was a/c - it would take around 2-3 hours for it to be effective at all. The playroom guy was very cheerful and lively. My kid had a great time there with all the spot activities. Gym and pool were average. I felt there is scope for improvement in pool cleaning. Also, the stairs and wall between kids and normal pool are badly designed; my kid hurt himself several times there; gentle gradient would have been better. Further, wifi never worked. Lot of scope for improvement in that regard. Overall good place for a nice relaxing holiday.

author: g0wrishankaru
title: Majestic At the Grove
text: My Second Visit to Grove within a year. It is a perfect place to relax and stay clam. I have stayed for 4 nights in room 101, 102 which is just on the edge of the lake it was a wonderful stay. Special thanks to Jaison for Arranging the rooms as requested. We will be back every year. Food was excellent. Good place To stay for a quite and relaxing. The staffs was very friendly and care taking. Food in water side was too good with buffet breakfast and live appam, omelet counters. Staffs Chief Pradeep, Arun, Divya, Marimuthu all we're taking friendly and made our stay memorable. Chief walked to your table every day and served us with delicious food. Daily evening we had fun games, noon class like cooking, towel design etc., which was good to play and learn. Daily events for kids. The swimming pool was one on the best just over looking the lake and a perfect place to be for sunset. Will be back....

author: Sac999
title: Beautiful Place with Awesome Food
text: We stayed here from 24th March till 27th March. Its a beautiful resort, neat n clean and nicely designed. It houses a decent Swimming pool. The check in was quick. Thanks Ms.Divya. The Chef and Stewards are very good at their job, throughly enjoyed the food ( pure veg ) made to our taste. The ambience of the restaurant is good and leisurely atmosphere. A special thanks to the Chef n his team for taking care of our special choices, and Mr. Arun for his services. The rooms are spacious, neat and clean, and nicely maintained. Each is a unit of 4 rooms, 2 on ground level and 2 on upper. Hot water is available 24hrs and the Air Conditioning works fine( which is needed).The rooms have a fridge and coffee maker and a decent balcony or backyard. They have a bar area with beautiful view and they also house a Spa. They do not have a vast open area, but considering the location its pretty adequate, with a good parking space. Its an Ideal place if you just want to relax and enjoy the Sunset and the birds. Enjoyed the mornings and the Evenings here with beautiful music of the birds. i would definitely recommend this place to my friends and Family. Thanks to everyone at the Royal Grove.

author: amrujay
title: great holiday retreat into the lake side Royal Grove Resort
text: Royal Grove, Kumarakom provided the most enjoyable holiday that we have enjoyed in recent times. Easily reachable from the nearest Kochi airport or even by rail to alight at Kottayam and a short road trip to reach the Royal Grove resort. The resort is ideally located on the banks of the Vembanadu Lake the largest lake in Kerala. The ambiance created by the very distinct architecture of the resort buildings and facilities itself is a refreshing change and a pleasant sight to behold during the night when the resort is aesthetically lit with clever and beautiful lighting. The guest rooms themselves are clutter free and brightly lit and embellished with tastefully designed furniture and fixtures. The ground floor rooms one of which was allotted to us open out into the grassy verandah where one could relax in the tranquil surroundings created by the lake waters and the welcome absence of nearby constructions. one could soak in the scene provided by the vast lake waters and the greenery. Royal Grove indeed provides very comfortable and clean living rooms and the unobtrusive maintenance staff allows one to relax in total privacy! The resort also has a nice swimming pool and one could really enjoy the warm / cool waters. We really enjoyed our time in the pool. The waterside restaurant is a good restaurant even though offers less choice of vegetarian dishes. the food is tasty and service is excellent. The whole experience has definitely rejuvenated me and my family. one highlight i wish to point out is the absence of large crowds and boutique like environment in the resort. I shall definitely return!

author: EnjoyUrHoliday
title: The Best Resort Till date I visited
text: One of the best stay of my life. The ultimate luxury hotel in the middle of nowhere. The hotel has been maintained very well. All room has lake facing balcony. One additional utility is there in every room but not mentioned anywhere ie a mini freeze. I have never seen any resort/hotel where all the staffs are too good. I can say blindly the resort staff has the capability to make your stay as memorable one. They will try to get you whatever you want. Even I have seen they went to local market to buy some fish as requested by some guest and prepared dish as they want. Since it is very small resort with 24 rooms you will get personal attention every-time. I suggest some scope of improvement to them which I am sure they will comply very soon. The Room service is not upto the mark. Also the Food quality is not at per with the food cost. But nevertheless a very good resort to be. I will definitely visit again.

author: TravellerPete53
title: Quiet and relaxing resort
text: You will love the Royal Grove if you are looking for a quiet and relaxing resort, but you should look elsewhere if you are looking for excitement and entertainment. The Royal Grove is small, clean and the restaurant serves food of consistently superb quality with a good range of choice. The staff are polite, friendly and attentive. A wide range of tours can be arranged at reception including houseboat tours, of varying length, in the resort's own excellent houseboat. The rooms are large with views overlooking Lake Vembanad, but the bathrooms need updating. Air conditioning was efficient and quiet and a large overhead fan is also provided, the king sized bed was comfortable and as Royal Grove is quiet at night we slept very well indeed. No kitchen is provided and local restaurants are some distance away, however the Royal Grove's restaurant is first class and reasonably priced. Whilst some have commented on slow service, I think this is unfair as the food is freshly cooked- this is not a fast food joint. We ate the excellent buffet breakfast outside watching the local egrets hunting for their breakfast! Watching the houseboats sail past was relaxing and watching the sun set over the lake was magical. We visited Kochi City and took the tour to Thekaddy both of which were enchanting. We would strongly recommend that you hire a small boat from the nearby jetty (take a tuk-tuk from reception) as the smaller boats sail on the narrow rivers. You will see people bathing, washing clothes, fishing and children swimming. Most smile and wave as you sail by. We saw a lot of birdlife including kingfishers along the way. We also hired the resort's houseboat for the afternoon. This is recommended for complete relaxation and the gourmet lunch was first rate (including crayfish we bought from a fisherman on the way). In short, this resort in God's Own Country is highly recommended for those seeking peace and quiet rather than excitement and entertainment.

author: chrisv293
title: Nice quiet resort in a beautiful but isolated location
text: As advertised in our Odyssey brochure, Royal Grove is set on the beautiful Vembanad Lake with the thatched roof houseboats plying past the resort all day. Our room was large and very comfortable, the air conditioner worked well and although the bathroom was on the small side it was adequate. The restaurant was quite good with great food and reasonable prices. Alcohol prices are elevated in Kerala due to taxes apparently. We did a few tours including: a trip to Alleppey with a backwaters boat ride for which we should have negotiated a better price; a tour to Thekkady which was very good; and a lunch tour on the resort’s houseboat with a very delicious lunch prepared onboard by one of the 2 crewmen. The beautiful horizon pool was great, but the lining is small tiles and many of them are coming loose so refurbishment is needed. Entertainment at the resort was limited basically to a full size billiard table but there was only one cue which didn’t have any cushion left on the tip, consequently the white ball was very pitted. So you need to make your own entertainment – or just enjoy the peace and quite. The staff were all very friendly and helpful, although there were some difficulties with my English communication. Reception was very helpful with arranging any transport required. We got an “auto-taxi” into Kottayam to check out the market area – very busy and crowded plus the journey through the rice paddy areas was enjoyable. The 86km trip from the airport, at 2030INR for a prepaid taxi, which we arranged upon arrival, was hair-raising. The resort staff told us it averaged around 2.5hours for the trip, but our taxi at 12:30 am took just 1.5hours! Kerala roads conditions are very different to Australia and relatively short distances take a lot longer – so allow accordingly. All-in-all we really enjoyed our first visit to India and consequently Kerala and will recommend the Royal Grove to our friends

author: Pipson
title: Serene atmosphere, beautiful views, authentic cuisine - unforgettable experience
text: The Royal Grove in Kumarakom is a beautiful and charming resort facing the Vembanad lake. In fact, the lake winds through the resort giving you a feel of living in the lagoon, rather than near it. You get uninterrupted views of the lagoon from your room and from the common areas of the resort. Much like a car in your garage, Grove’s own beautiful houseboat is docked against its shore, adding to the magical ambience. We requested a ground-floor room. If you prefer more privacy, you can opt for a first floor room. The rooms are very comfortable offering all modern amenities, including a mini fridge. Unlike other Royal resorts, the Grove does not offer a kitchenette. Instead, they offer great food. Chef Pratheesh will delight you if you ask for Kerala delicacies not included in the menu. We asked for Avial (a mixed-vegetable delight), Meen Peera (small fish that you typically eat with its bones, like anchovies, in a delicious dry masala of freshly grated coconut and pot tamarind), Tapioca-Fish Curry (a must-have combination in Kerala’s cuisine). You can try suggesting other items. Subject to availability of the ingredients required, the Chef and his team take sincere pleasure in making their guests happy. The Front Office staff is discreet, polite and attentive. The Spa services offered were also good by well-trained therapists. We’d definitely go back again and also recommend it highly to everybody.

author: arun_banerji
title: A Cool & Relaxing Week
text: Royal Grove met our expectations, almost 90%. After a long, bumpy &. tiring 2 & half hour drive from Cochin airport, reception at the resort was a welcome change and a great relief. The staff turned out to be proactively helpful & very welcoming . We spent plenty of time in the pool, which is well maintained . A good view of Vembanad lake is possible from practically any corner of the resort. Were lucky to get a room on the first floor, just overlooking the lake.Morning tea on the balcony, almost jutting into the lake, was truly special . Rooms are well-maintained and clean.Air-conditioning is perfect. There is a good Gym on the floor above the restaurant. The restaurant serves mostly Kerala cuisine, though North Indian food is also available. While the food quality is good, the service is an area that requires improvement. I also felt that the resort could organise some inhouse activities. The resort also helps in organising trips to nearby places. We took a days trip to Thekkady & the Periyar lake, which though tiring, was a great experience , especially the trip to spice garden. We also took the overnight house boat trip, arranged by the resort. Houseboat trip was truly amazing. A trip to Kumarakom is incomplete without the lake trip. On the whole we spent a very relaxing & quiet week at the Royal Grove. Would love to return. Chhanda &Arun Banerji arun.banerji@gmail.com.

author: nikhil817
title: Lovely, laid back place
text: Kumarakom is a lovely, laid-back lake district, and the location of this hotel encourages you to unwind and relax. There's not much to do in the resort itself except lounge, and it is located a bit out of the way (you need an autorickshaw which the reception will readily arrange -- to do any outdoorsie stuff). Activities in the resort: Right on the edge of the lake you can take in the serene view and sunbathe, swim (in the pool), lounge in the bar or just have a game of carrom maybe. There's a snooker table I missed trying. The resort houseboat is beautiful and well maintained -- comparing it with a third-person boat I rented from the private jetty. I'd recommend a shorter shikara ride in the backwaters too -- can be booked through the reception, and more satisfying than the day long ride really. A trip to the bird sanctuary in Dec-Jan might be nice. We hardly saw anything in mid-November. The heritage village tour would also be a good idea -- i missed doing that. Happened to spot a family of Indian Otter's on the edge of the lake on first day -- made my day - unfortunately didn't see them again. The rooms are nice and cosy -- the mattresses a little too soft for my comfort. The footbridge made of concrete beams leading to the rooms is a nice touch albeit requiring concentration for fear of stubbing your toe. The staff are very friendly and helpful. And the facility management is very responsive too. One of the highlights for us was learning to cook appams and vegetable mappas from the Chef. Very warm human being and very committed to his craft. Overall a good place to lounge, and have a laid back holiday.

author: dharamd18
title: Picturesque & Tranquil.
text: RESORT, LOCATION & MANAGEMENT: Scenic and peaceful location. Most of the Resort is virtually atop Water. Very Good rooms. Very nicely done Bathrooms. Amazing View of backwaters from the Balcony. Extremely helpful and friendly staff. Quick Room service, customer focused, all because of very good Management. Daily activities organised by the management for both adults and kids. The Resort Manager Mr. Jaison Anithanam is a great person to interact with, open to suggestions and willing to make your experience as rich as possible. FOOD:- A very good restaurant "The Waterside". Food was of very good quality, good portions, very tasty and priced reasonably, wide spread menu for both vegetarians and non-vegetarians. OTHER AMENITIES:- Nice Bar, a snooker/pool table, well equipped Gym. A Very Clean and a well maintained Swimming Pool. Free Wi-Fi at the reception, you may get some coverage from the room. Just the right place to escape the Busy City life to Rejuvenate and Recuperate. A must Visit!!!

author: maj0ra
title: The Grove....Royal Indeed!!
text: We returned after 2 years for the second time to the Grove with our yougest daughter Edel Socorro Ann to celebrate our 47th Wedding Anniversary on 18 Oct 14. Wow! what a surprise (Royal) reception accorded to us with gallends & welcoming drink. Later we went on a boat house (newly renovatedGlove's own) ride for the whole day. You have everthing you ask for. We were again given a warm welcome at the hoseboat with a birthday cake & wine to refresh our thurst. Amazing indeed!. 2 A/C bedrooms with everthing a *4 star hotel has. it was a slow ride on the cool waters of the Vembanade lake. The chef took us to a fishing village to buy local fish & lopster for our lunch. We enjoyed a tasty sumptious lunch. I went for a short nap while my wife Ruth & Edel watched a TV show and enjoying the beautiful scenery along the vilages. Later we took a rest at our beautiful room built on the stilt water. A great experince that one should not miss. Thanks to the Resort Manager Mr. Jason an enegetic & always smiling to welcome his guests with great enthusism at all time. God willing we will come by next year for my wife's birthday. God bless all the management staff & his crews.Also not forgeting the Resort's harworking Marketing Manager Babo John.

author: 19Joel63
title: Calm , Serene & Enjoyable
text: Stayed there from 27th July 2014 to 31st July 2014. Very friendly resort & well maintained rooms & bathrooms. I particularly liked the idea of the bathroom offset out to open sky with plenty of natural daylight at the same time maintianing full privacy. Rooms: Good & linen was well maintianed. However I feel the resort maintainence team should take additional measures to avoid small lizards creeping into the room through the gaps on the floor of the balcony door. An additional barrier & sealing will help. Tea & coffee makers were replenished everyday so were fresh towels provided. Refrigerator in room was an added advantage. Restaurant food was good & chef used to make as desired. However lacked the usual Idli & Wada both as breakfast & as anytime snacks. Absence of Tandoor items for lunch was also such a pity. Front desk staff was especially very helpful especially the thin, petite fair girl whose name I forgot( But I have mentioned it in my feedback) who even arranges a auto for you & who was always smiling & ready to help. Swimming Pool : Great though management must enforce strict rules of wearing swim wear for the pool as found a lot of people with regular cotton clothes in the pool. Activities: Great , Table tennis table should be added. WIFI boosters must be provided near each block of rooms as the wifi in the rooms further from front desk is terribly poor & cannot be used. Missed your Karma Spa. All in all a great stay & highly recomend this resort to anyone who likes to laze around the backwaters of Vembanand lake. Capt. Joel Joseph. Royal/ Karma Member since 2008

author: JAYESHPARIKH
title: The grove, kumarakom, kottayam, kerala
text: We have visited the grove from 27 jun to 3 jul. The resort ambiance is very very excellent. The layout of resort is very planned one. On one side of resort all the utilities of the resort and on other side residential room. It is ground + one stored structure well planned, well maintained, co-operative staff. Resorts have essential facility for recharge our human batteries. Rooms containing living room + attach bathroom and good viewing and good looking balcony approximately 510 sq feet. The use of stainless steel wire as a wall is really a very good and advanced concept. With the use of stainless steel wire the wall does not intercept the view and it add excellent view of the structure from outside and from inside the structure it gives excellent view of nature. The clean and fresh water at swimming pool does not hurt your eyes while swimming. The design of swimming pool is very excellent. The buffet breakfast item are mouthwatering. You can easily enjoy for seven nights at hotel without moving out of resorts. The staying at resorts really create an unforgettable memory in my whole life. Jayesh parikh 9820466993 mumbai

author: rimpuash
title: perfect vacation..
text: Our beautiful resort ‘the Grove’ rested exactly on the edge of the Vembanad lake, which is considered the largest fresh water lake in Asia. The lake water traversed underneath the passages of the resort. One could see the vast expanse of the lake while standing at the reception itself. The ‘infinity pool’ at the center of resort seemed to merge with the lake water. The resort itself gave the feel of one of the beautiful houses of Venice. we visited the resort in last week of February and had an amazing experience. we got the best room in resort '101' and i am thankful to the reception for that. first time happened to stay so near to a water body. the food was delicious and equally exciting were the extra curricular activities in resort. i attended a dance class, cookery class, towel-folding class and saw an amazing fire-dance show. my husband and 5 year old son stayed in the resort itself for all 6 days . our best time happened in the special 'Chickie-hut', where we spend most of our time either reading or getting inspired by nature. luckily bonded with some of wonderful guests in resort. the only draw back seemed to be the restaurant which the resort was working upon. all in all a beautiful place with friendly and helpful staff. will love to visit again.

author: T937FLjohnw
title: A relaxing, family friendly resort
text: My Wife & I stayed at The Grove for two weeks at the end of March 2014. A car from The Grove met us at the airport and took us to the resort 2 1/2 hours drive away. I would recommend this as the resort is out of the way and may not be straightforward to find. Our reception was very efficient and we were quickly shown our room where some, but not all of its functions were explained. The resort is in a beautiful, quiet setting and is generally well designed, being built around and above an artificial waterway. Its modern look fits nicely with the numerous coconut palms and other vegetation. Although it is fairly new to the Karma Group the resort is several years old and is in need of maintenance in some areas, but it is clear that there is a steady program of work to rectify the defects. The food at The Grove is excellent, and the menu has a good selection of less spicy dishes as well as traditional local ones. The waiters were very friendly and helpful with recommendations and tailoring spiciness to our tastes. The bar is upstairs above the restaurant, & my only criticisms are that service was a bit slow and access from the pool area is not easy. The infinity pool and sun loungers are key features of the resort and for the most part were not busy. There was a daily schedule of onsite activities to entertain children and a variety of excursions, both by car and by boat. The beautiful Lake Vembanad, its canals and villages offer some of the best excursions and the 5 hour Houseboat lunch trip was excellent. This is a very family-friendly resort with staff members happy to spend time playing games with children of all ages. Overall we had a quiet relaxing holiday and were well looked after. A lovely resort but not quite 5 stars as it was let down by a few minor niggles, such as the large sign at the lakes edge which spoiled the view of the sunset. The gardens were generally well-maintained and the in-house ducks provided some light entertainment! If you're looking for an activity holiday then this would not be the right resort for you. But if you're looking for sun, nice food and the chance to completely unwind then The Grove will provide the perfect get away from it all holiday.

author: Prashdsouza
title: Will come back.
text: We went here for a week’s stay. A well-deserved vacation and we returned back pretty rejuvenated. About the resort ... pretty much well documented below. My Highlights were 1) The most amazing sunsets. Clear till the last bit of the sun set on the far side of Vembanad lake .The view of the birds flying across the setting sun is pretty mesmerizing. 2) One of the places to view this sunset is the infinity pool which gives you the feeling that there is nothing between you and the sun. There are many other more vantage points to enjoy the beautiful sunsets. 3) The untiring staff that does every possible to keep you relaxed all the time. Special thanks to Mithun, He took care of my naughty son , engaging him with games etc . 4) Waterside restaurant had good waiters (Viraj Kumar , Arun and Co) who would do their best to get the meals. The breakfast buffet was ok and the a la carte menu had a good spread of food ranging from Keralite delicacies to North Indian items. Tandoor was only available in the evenings. The food would arrive in reasonable time as well except on the last day when the resort was fully booked. 5) The 2 hr + boat ride is also a must that passes through the water alleys of Kerala giving you some breathtaking sceneries… Palm fringed waterways… beautiful local birds.. Houses with their gates opening in the waterways… On the flipside the alcoholic menu was pretty expensive. Needs to be toned down slightly. I did not visit nearby places but noticed that there are not to many options.. Would definitely visit again .

author: Raospeaks
title: The Grove - A Nice Boutique Resort with a Big Heart :)
text: The Title says it all . We took a trip in Feb ( Our 5th Wedding Anniversary ) and Stayed from the 15th to 19th Feb. We reached the resort on the 15th noon and were welcomed with a nice lil garland and a refreshing Drink ( My 11 mom old baby got one too :) ! . The Check in was quick and the team had done great job in putting up some flowers , chocolates and balloon in room as requested .. We stayed in 104 ..very clean big room with all the necessary amenities.Bathroom Clean ( imp ). It had a sliding door overlooking the beautiful lake . Lunch was very nice ...we had Chinese.The rest of the day well was just Rest . The next day we lazed around the pool ..and baby pool which overlooks the lake and Isha ( my lil one ) enjoyed chasing the duck and the birds. The resort has it own House boat and a boat ..we took a 3hr trip on the boat on the lake ...the lake as such is beautiful and clean we met a very nice couple Chris and Maureen and chatted away for hrs ( Good part of being Royal resort members... ..) Other than that breakfast was good ...They even made me some Puttu ( Kerala specialty ) which was not apart of the Buffet ... There is room for improvement .a Sauna and Spa absoultely needed. more training for the staff ( very new ) some more activities like what they do in Hathi Mahal and other Royal resort ...gives us a chance to meet and mingle with other guest.Add more variety specially to the Veg menu. ( Big area for improvement ) Over all we had a fantastic vacation ..So Padmaraj/Arun ..s/Divya / Rajkiran and to all the other staffs and Chefs ..Thank you very much and Well done. .. The final verdict ..Not a five star but i would rate it a hotel with Five hearts !

author: amandap173
title: Blissful place to BE in Buzios!!
text: As an American traveling in Brazil, I was curious to see what is really going on (as opposed to what the media portrays.) I felt care from the staff at the gorgeous Perola Hotel from my very first step inside! The lobby was beautifully done & the staff was professional and helpful, above and beyond expectations! The facility had everything I needed to fully enjoy Buzios. The pool had lovely lounge with service that was approachable--Even an area for kids to play. Guests were sociable yet, not invasive. The relaxed atmosphere lent to spending the hottest part of the day under the tiki-covered beds and taking in the gorgeous view while being protected from the sun. Complimentary afternoon coffee & tea was a sweet touch too! The restaurant served some of the the best meals I had in Brazil! A proper breakfast started my day via BRUNCH BUFFET!!! This is a commodity in Buzios!!! I felt welcomed and the staff went above and beyond to ensure my comfort and dietary needs. There was a separate club for poker players which was modern gaming and a second bar. Great for those wanting to try there luck-- Yet discrete, not interfering with the families who may stay at the hotel. Truly, this is a great place to enjoy Buzios and it was not crowded! A gem of a find!

author: ski-fanatic-73
title: location location!
text: I think Perola is the only ‘good’ hotel with a decent size in the actual centre of Buzios. It gives you the opportunity to go ‘back home’ easily in between of activities. Being ‘home’ in the hotel feels nice. Not awesome, but still nice. There is a good size pool as well as a Jacuzzi. At the poolbar the barman (the tall bald one) makes excellent cocktails; which are very cheap during happy hour! Wifi is ok and free parking is handy as well in Buzios (if you want to see all the beaches). Room conditions are ok. They took the approach to use white and paint the wood white as well. It gives a beachy and crisp feeling; but if you look closer you see here as well that you are in a humid area. At least all the doors close well, so you will not be eaten alive by bugs. In our room, the matrass on the bed was on its end. We woke up after the first night with a backache. As all the rooms were booked, the offered to change the matrass: slightly better, but still not great. The breakfast was a bit of a let-down. Typical Brazilian hotel breakfast; but there was a bit of love an quality missing there. But hey, the location you just can’t beat; just outside of all the restaurants & pubs. There is even a supermarket across the road.

author: Ewappner
title: Awesome staff and service
text: Our visit began a bit slow. The hotel sent a third party transportation service to pick our party of six up. The car was over two hours late. We ended up hiring a taxi instead in order to get there. Four of us were only spending one night, and we had a three hour drive ahead of us. Upon our late arrival the manager and staff treated us with many apologies. They offered us champagne, lunch, and another drink as a welcome and apology. The staff was so awesome the entire stay. Communication is no problem as George (the manager) is originally from Manhattan. Edwardo at the front desk has great control of the English language and as very helpful. The rest of the staff especially Rose in hospitality and Phillipe the waiter/bartender were great. The facilities are very nice. The restaurant was awesome. We had the best fish of our entire stay upon our arrival. The breakfast was very lovely also with many options. The rooms could use a facelift. An easy fix would be a nice coat of paint to the rooms. The beds are comfortable and the shower was very nice. The pool and hot tub is lovely. We would definitely return to this lovely location.

author: FamiliaWilliams
title: Superb service, great location, an enjoyable stay.
text: We stayed at the Perola in late October with our friends who were on holiday from the UK, in all our group was 5 adults, 2 x 9 years olds and our daughter who is 7 months old. On arrival we were met by friendly staff who parked the cars and unloaded our luggage, car parking is free. The check in was very smooth and the staff super freindly and attentive, free glass of bubbly wine to greet us. The hotel is built around the pool area and has two floors, our rooms were on the top floor. The room decor is clean and simple with a beach / rustic style, our room had a loft bedroom with a double bed and two twin beds on the ground floor. we had requested a cot and this was all set up and ready for us in the room. The only negative comments rearding the the room; the tap in the shower was a little touch and go and actually fell off whilst we were there, the key card kept requiring to be re-booted and wi-fi in the room was non existant although it worked very well by the pool. Breakfast was excellent, lots of choice and lots of fresh fruit, breads, meats and cakes. Breakfast was large enough to keep us going for the day! The location is superb, walk out the door and turn left and your are in the heart of Buzios. If you decide to stay in the pool and hot tub area is a great place to relax, take a drink and read a book. without a doubt for us the jewel of the hotel were the staff, all of whom we dealt with were very friendly and helpful, nothing we asked for was an issue for them. The breakfast staff always set out a high chair and helped with our daughter, we couldnt have asked for more. Carlos at the pool bar was very friendly and mixed excellent Pina Colada's! In paticular a big thanks to Rose, her attention to our comfort whilst at the hotel was simply second to none. Personally we wouldnt hesitate to stay at the Perola again.

author: Christian_Taylor
title: It's all about the pool
text: This is a really lovely hotel - the central pool area is stunning, with a bar, plenty of sunshine, palm trees and a beautiful Balinese theme with lovely white drapes and dark timber. The jacuzzi is nice and warm, but the engine is loud when the jets are on. Bright orange is a colour that runs through the entire hotel's décor - I found it to be an unpleasant colour to look at after a while. Apart from that, our room was bright, clean and spacious. We had lots of storage space. I loved that concrete floors and large glass windows. Apart from the pool area, there aren't really any other common areas to relax and unwind in. The foyer isn't somewhere one would sit for long - it feels cavernous and empty. Good for when you're waiting for a taxi, but that's about all. Breakfast was lovely - plenty of options, but the plastic wrap was left on all the plates of food. Some people will like this - I found it a bit annoying. Coffee was nice and strong. Staff were great - many spoke English, which was really helpful. The hotel doesn't connect with the beach at all, which was a little unexpected. The location is good though - nice and central, close to downtown Armação dos Búzios but far enough away to escape the noise. If you're looking for a clean, trendy hotel with a great pool, then this a great choice!

author: lyjonne
title: Hotel garden
text: I stayed at this hotel for 4 days recently. The hotel was very comfortable with warm room and a breakfast every morning. There were some nice touches like the availability of toiletries and two free bottles of water in the room that were replaced every day. There were lots of plug sockets in the room, I counted nine in mine. There was also two separate usb charging points. We made use of the sauna where toiletries and towels were also provided. We also came across a laundry room where we washed and dried our clothes. What stopped me from giving this hotel 5 stars was three things. The first day we got up (a sunday) and went down to breakfast there was virtually nothing left and people were still coming down expecting a breakfast. My husband complained to a member of staff who said that there were a lot of guests and that they had simply run out of food. It annoys me to see people pile their plates with food and then leave half of it. We had a double bed, with a single quilt on it. We found another quilt and put that on the bed so that both quilts were lying across the bed and would cover us both. We spoke to the hotel receptionist and asked for a double quilt. We never got one and the cleaner would keep making the bed up with the two quilts side by side as if they were on two single beds even though we had left the bed made with the quilts the other way round. There was no tea or coffee making facilities.

author: SaraM9001
title: Less than i tought
text: Our room was super iper small (think that our luggage didn't fit well in it). The door in the shower was missing and when we arrived the shower was smellig of pee in a very strong way. I had to clean it... The sauna was supposed to open at 7 but it opened at 9. The breckfast was not good in the selection but also in the quality of food: not so fresh vegetables and scrambled eggs... The guy at the check in was very fliendly dough, but the one at our check out was terrible and mean. We check out in the morning but we leave there out luggage and stayed in the city for the all day. We had to take our return flight from copenaghen very early in the morning so we came back to the hotel to take our luggage at 11.30pm. We asked if we could stay a bit in the lounge room just to wait for our phone to charge and then to catch our train.. I was willing to consume something from the bar but in the beginning he said us that we didn't pay for that night in the hotel so we couldn't stay and had to leave!!! Than I became upset and said to him that we were guest the previus night and we had our luggage in the luggage room if he didn't trust and he replied to me that we had the luggage there as a favour since it would soon be a new day and said than that we could stay for one hour to charge our phone. Then i think he realized his mistake since he came back to us offering free stuff to drink or eat, but he never apologized. I didn't accepted the free food. We stayed then just one our to recharge the phone and we went to the train station to wait the rest of the hours. He looked very surprised of this and ask us to continue waiting there...but again, he didn't apologise for his previuse attitude. I don't accept to be treated like that. So we leave and we will not choose or advide this hotel.

author: L8903MZjanes
title: Great location , bit tired round edges
text: A great , reasonably priced hotel in excellent location with just a few things that let it down. Good friendly check-in and got into room at noon. Bed a small double and mattress a tad soft for me. Room quite small but only 2 of us so no real issue. Small bathroom, with strange feature of only half a shower door, not sure if Swedish thing or just removed. There was empty bottle left from previous occupants so some attention to detail missing. Luckily a fan in room as no AC and it was 30 degrees plus while we were there. The gardens are a little unloved and no set seating area so again just a little unloved. There is work going on to improve rooms though no noise or impact to us from this. Breakfast was excellent, big choice of local options. Staff friendly though some knowledge a little lacking - taxi to station , not 80 kr but set fee of 129kr and though info says can buy bus tickets from reception, you can't and no mini bar in room. Fridge would have been good as water left but boiling. For me it is a 3.5 rather than 3 but no halves on here. Water and coffee in reception a available free all day, great extra. Would definitely stay again and hope the small niggles ironed out with renovations.

author: K4080GElisas
title: Good hotel - beware of renovations
text: First things first: The location is really good, it's basically a 5 minutes walk to the city center, with supermarkets, shops, restaurants and bars close. Also, just about 10 minutes walk from Malmö Central Station. The room was not big, but certainly enough space for 1 person (I travelled alone). Honestly, a bit old-fashioned, but well-kept and very clean. In the bathroom, they refilled shampoo, shower gel, body lotion and conditioner, when I had finished it. My window went directly out to the gardens - nice view (but also, anybody who was in the gardens could look directly into my rooms, if I didn't keep the curtains closed). The breakfast was delicious, and certainly enough choice for different tastes. The staff was friendly. Despite my late arrival, I was welcomed heartily at the reception. Can't say much about the garden, as the weather wasn't inviting, but they seemed nice for spring/summertime. BUT: Unfortunately, there was quite a downside: they are currently renovating the rooms. While I understand the need to do that (maybe even without closing the hotel), they obvisously paid no attention to the noise. They rented out my room despite renovating the rooms directly to my left and my right. They tore out parts of the bathrooms, as far as I could tell. It was very loud and sometimes woke me up in the mornings. No chance to rest or work in my room during the day. That was a huge downside - I paid full price for my room and could only really use it during the nighttime. As this is not the staff's fault, but clearly a management problem, I only downrated "value" and "room".

author: EricH313
title: Quirky and Fine
text: I had a room with number 140-something, which was on the sixth floor at the end of about a 500m hallway. There's a garden in the courtyard on the sixth floor, which meant my room had a window opening right onto a public space. As the hotel was warm, I locked my valuables in my suitcase so nobody would climb in during the night. This also meant I was awakened by birds chirping several times during the night. The battered pillows didn't help, though the bed was otherwise comfortable. Staff was friendly, breakfast was nice, location is good. The whole place was much bigger than I thought it was. Would I stay here again? Maybe. Would I gladly recommend it? Nope. It was fine. Not great. Not bad. Just fine for one night and generally forgettable afterward.

author: PhilippMann
title: Not worth the price
text: We can't say we didn't know what we booked because on the website they tell you how small the rooms are (and you could book a bigger one), but the room size was still a disappointment. Especially when you see how small the bed is as well (which other hotel uses 80 cm mattresses?). The worst thing which made me write this review: Every morning I had to hear a dozen! cell phones vibrating for different directions (= probably used as an alarm clocks). Really annoying and something I hadn't experienced before. The electrical wiring in the rooms is from another age. You really have to look for the switches and then find out what they do. Needless to say that you can't turn off the ceiling light from the bed. The toilet dripped forever to fill up. Booth nights my room was quite warm and I didn't find a way to control the heating. The TV had only one (working) international TV channel: BBC news. On the first day, the breakfast room was quite crowded (which can be normal at certain times) but then I expect the staff to clean up which was not the case. Used plates were blocking many tables although waitresses were on site. The 2nd day it worked though. At the reception you surprisingly had to wait every time you wanted something. But the people were helpful and friendly. Parking is good/okay. Either you park on the street or in a public parking garage with direct access to the hotel. And of course due to the location, the hotel is steps away from the city center/shopping.

author: carmel187
title: great location, comfortable rooms
text: clean hotel. room basic but comfortable. booked superior room but was dissapointed with this as no uht cartons provided for milk and not available, and only specialty tea bags not English ones. never found sauna but to be honest was not a priority. breakfast provided was a plenty, great selection. and as for location could not have been better!! a very short walk from station, about 10 min max, and so close to all the restaurants, shops etc. although my room was right next to the lift, i did not have to worry about noise as it was so quiet. i guess my only problem was that i had a bath with overhead shower that had a fixed glass panel and it made getting in and out of bath difficult, especially as bath was unusually high off ground. recommend if you are staying there to ask for a room with only shower if you might have difficulties. and bring uht individual cartons and some tea bags if that's your preference. i would definitely stay again. and malmo is really lovely too. oh wifi was a bit hit and miss, but i did manage a few times. dont know if free for everyone or just certain room types...

author: TanyaBarrow
title: Perfect
text: This hotel came recommended to us by the travel agent who organised our week long stay in Iceland (we stayed in three hotels, this one was first) so we didn't know anything about until it was booked. The perfect location if you want to see Northern Lights. They even have an alarm system you can dial into to register if you want them to wake you up in the middle of night if there are lights visible. The staff were friendly and the rooms spotless. The room may be smaller than you are expecting but all rooms in Icelandic hotels are smaller than average as it keeps them warmer. This room was big enough for a desk though, and a large en suite. There are geothermal pools that are free for guests to use and they were perfect at the end of a busy day, and made for a stunning backdrop for photos. We did half board which meant we didn't have to drive anywhere to find dinner and thought the food was great. Buffet breakfast, pastries, and cooked. And dinner was three courses of the chef's choosing which meant we tried things we might not otherwise have done. All presented beautifully. And if these things matter to you, they are fab on social media. Sharing lots of photos and the joy of other guests seeing Northern Lights for the first time. if you are on Insta or Twitter, do give them a follow. Already booking for my parents to stay next year for their 50th wedding anniversary next year we loved it so much.

author: allenwkkwan
title: Hotel stay
text: I was travelling with my wife and another couple. We booked by internet . We had two rooms. They are good. It was clean and well equipped; specially with kettles and hairdryer . Good dinning. Good breakfast. Near the ‘into the Glacier’ shuttle meeting point. I drove there in 1 min after checking out. A good place to see the Northern night if there are no cloud. They have a wake up service for you if you want to see the Northern light. Unfortunately, the night we stayed was cloudy. They have a hot pool but it close at 7:00 pm. We managed to arrive at 6:00pm and just in time for a 30 min swimming . The water is about 25 degree but there are two other small pools up to 42 degree. There is a slider too and I saw adults sliding down safely. I would recommend to any one travellling around that area. And do not forget to join the ‘into the Glacier’ ... the tunnel to go into the Glacier is not going to last forever... once in a life time.

author: 159silasl
title: Disappointed
text: We booked this at the end of a 16-day trip around the Ring road. Of the nine places we’ve stayed in Iceland, this is the most disappointing. For the price, you can do far, far better. The pools close at 7 pm on weeknights. The rooms are basic and lack even blackout shades for Iceland’s 24-hour daylight. The staff lacks training and is not Icelandic for the most part — not the least bit authentic as an experience in the country. We were told we had to make a restaurant reservation for dinner and then told we couldn’t have our preferred time — but we were given 30 minutes earlier. During our entire dinner (2-plus hours of slow service by a trainee who meant well but had no idea what he was doing) we never saw the place more than half full. To be fair, the food was fresh and good. The head waiter, when he was around, was friendly and knowledgeable. But overall, it contributes to the theme. This place is over-marketed and over-priced. Stay at the Fosshotel Reykholt down the road. Far better value, bigger rooms and friendly staff. Sadly, Husafell doesn’t live up to its ambitions.

author: 99Martin
title: A spectacular hotel in a beautiful location.
text: Húsafell is a pretty spot and it is clear that well heeled Icelanders are building many second homes nearby. It is also a hub for the big Glacier Cave and Lava Tube trips and (in Winter) Snomobiles and all that kind of stuff. Plus hiking, fishing and so on. When we were there, the (extremely expensive) trips to the Lava Tube etc were all cancelled because the weather was so bad. We weren't bothered about missing those (although waking up in late May and finding everything completely white out with snow reminded us how far North we were! Still, we went for a nice walk, which was more 'our thing'. Anyway, the Hotel is impressive, the room, bed, bathroom were all fine, the view great (especially if you like snow) and the service friendly and efficient. We were there for three nights, although we spent one day in Borganes & Reykholt. The snag was that, although the Húsafell restaurant was good (if expensive, as usual), they only do four main courses. The lamb (which was nice) a Vegan option (which I don't do), Surf & Turf (which I don't like) or a Grilled Salmon dish. More specifically this is a decent piece of nicely grilled salmon with "Wasabi risotto, crispy soft shell crab, shiitake mushrooms, grilled spring onion and mango-wagame salad" Hmmm. I'm not sure whose idea that was, or whether they really thought all those flavours went together, but to us it was memorable in a bad way. Hey Ho. You can't enjoy everything. I'm lucky. There is really very little food I don't like. A pity they dropped on three out of a menu of only four options! So, a great hotel, but you may want to consider taking sandwiches....

author: JCNottingham
title: Land of Fire and Ice
text: We stayed here for 3 nights in March. What an absolute find! We booked a fly drive through Discover the World and after a 90 minute drive on almost deserted roads we came to this oasis. The Husafell Hotel is a modern, eco friendly hotel. Rooms are modern with lots of space, the bathroom was(well if I could have taken it home I would have!!) Beautiful attention to detail with shower gels and shampoos that are all Icelandic. We had done our research so knew the prices in the hotel, we stuck to starter and main so approximately £60 per person but it was totally worth it. The food is exceptional, taste buds will be totally satisfied! Lots of fish! And that does tend to be a little cheaper! I have to mention the reception staff who were all so friendly and happy to discuss trips and walks. The waiters in the restuarant were so professional and could easily have been in a top class London restaurant, however at no time did we ever feel uncomfortable as they were all so friendly. The hotel is close to Into the Glacier , well worth the trip in old army lorries converted into buses and the Volcano tunnel. Close by there are also beautiful waterfalls. All in all an amazing stay and without doubt if we can afford it we will go back! Thank you Hotel Husafell and your staff for making our trip to Iceland the best! And Yes the Northern Lights made an appearance!

author: Nelly59CR
title: Very nice hotel, but very, very expensive to eat and drink.
text: My wife and I stayed at the Hotel Husafell for three nights in November 2017. The hotel is an easy (even in the snow) 110 mile drive from the airport and lives pretty much in the middle of nowhere. The hotel is very nicely presented (it seems pretty new) and the rooms are very comfortable and sufficiently spacious. The staff (particularly the restaurant staff) were excellent. Very friendly and helpful. The location of the hotel is a bit of a double edged sword because on the one hand it's well out of the way so there aren't millions of other tourists around, but on the other hand you don't really have much choice other than to eat dinner in the hotel. We were on a B&B package and the breakfast buffet was excellent, with a good range of hot and cold food to choose from. Dinner was also excellent, but very, very expensive. If you order three courses a la carte you'll be looking at something like £80-90 per person, plus drinks, which will be around £10 each. Or you can go the whole hog with a five course meal (from the same menu), which also works out at about £90 per person, plus drinks. This would have been okay for a night, but was a bit painful for three nights in a row. My wallet is going to be in therapy for quite some time. But the food was very, very excellent. An unexpected high point was that the hotel offers an aurora watch service. Dial 555 on your room phone before you go to bed and they'll give you a walk-up call if the aurora comes out during the night, which it did for us one night despite the forecast being very poor due to low solar activity. Apart from the soul crushing cost of eating and drinking, we really enjoyed our stay at the Hotel Husafell and wouldn't hesitate to stay there again (if we win the Lottery).

author: 494aarone
title: Wonderful start to our Iceland trip
text: My wife and I stayed here our first night of our Iceland vacation. We rented a car in Reykjavik and had approximately a 2 hour, 30 minute drip to this Hotel. The surrounding area is absolutely breath-taking. The front desk, housekeeping, and restaurant staff were very friendly and gave the extra effort to make our stay more memorable. The restaurant on the premises had excellent service and the food is fantastic. The room was up-to-date and in my opinion was one of the nicest hotel rooms I've stayed in. The bathroom had a nice bathtub and shower. We never turned on the television, however, there were two nice curved screen TVs in our room. There was a nice patio area outside our room as well. This hotel is very close to several adventure tours in the area. We did the Langjokull glacier ice cave and snowmobile activity, which was a blast. Also, there is a gas/diesel pump open to the public on the premises. Gas stations are not as common in Iceland and you should fill up whenever possible if you are doing a self-drive vacation. The least thing I liked about this place was leaving. We really had a great time here. I would strongly recommend this location. My wife and I will stay here again in the future.

author: 339josephm
title: Didn't Meet Expectations - I was disappointed
text: The hotel is a great facility. Clean. Nice rooms and furnishings. The restaurant (different ownership) is excellent -- 5 stars. Loved the restaurant. Excellent food and excellent service. The front desk staff wasn't attentive and helpful in the way I would expect of a luxury hotel and this kind of put me off the place. They didn't seem well trained. Also, no vending machines or ice for after hours. No lobby store. No mini-bar in the room or stocked refrigerator for late night nibbles -- bring your own. And, they closed the pool and hot tubs at 8PM. The sun is out all night. We pulled in at almost 7PM and I was looking forward to evening soak. Disappointing at this price point. Three stars because it didn't live up to expectations of luxury hotel. I won't stay again.

author: Mattrick_Swayze
title: Excellent stay! Comfortable, luxurious, and great location!
text: We easily fell for Hotel Husafell and it's charm yet luxurious feel as well as it's exclusive location. When you make the counter-clockwise road trip around Iceland, you'll come to West Iceland near the end of the loop and Hotel Husafell is there for a exquisite yet comfortable stay and as the place to book some final adventures before heading home. Hotel Husafell has various sized rooms including suites and villas but judging on the excellence of our standard room, you know the standard at this four starred hotel is very high. Our room was very spacious and the room was modern yet thoroughly comfortable. The room had plenty of natural lighting and easy access to the courtyard.
