The bathroom was especially notable with an innovative shower system and stone floors that felt heated which kept us perfectly toasty during our visit in April. One of the highlights of our stay at Hotel Husafell is being able to take full advantage of their geothermal baths right on the premises and mere steps from our room. Hotel guests get free admission to the baths and you'll certainly want to utilize them. There are two pools, two hot baths, and even a water slide! We felt refreshed and invigorated after taking a dip in the baths. It's an Icelandic staple and the water if powered from surrounding natural environment. The hotel also boasts a first-class restaurant that people all over the area come for fine dining. Complimentary breakfast is tremendous and has a variety of pastries, including mini-muffins, that we thought were some of the best we had in Iceland. This is perfect place to satiate your hunger especially if you're using the hotel to help book adventures to the strikingly beautiful nature surrounding the hotel. You can book into the glacier tours as well as trips to the Hraunfossar and Husafell watefalls. Additionally, given the unique location embedded in scenic heart of nature, Hotel Husafell is the hub for multiple sightings of the Northern Lights. This is due to the remote location away from light pollution. The hotel even offers wake up calls so you can breathlessly witness this spectacular phenomenon. A trip to Iceland is not complete until you've seen the Northern Lights. Overall, we thoroughly enjoyed all aspects of our stay in Hotel Husafell from the mixture of Scandinavian decor with supreme luxury to the breath of nature that is infused throughout the hotel.

author: drsusan07
title: Luxury in Western Iceland
text: We had a couple of very relaxing nights in the Hotel Husafell. Our room was welcoming and comfortable. The bed had very nice linens and comfortable pillows. The bathroom was large and well designed. Everything was new and very clean. All of the staff was friendly and helpful. The lobby was great for a cocktail and conversation before dinner. We were especially happy with hotel restaurant. We had the chef's tasting menu the first night which was fantastic. We enjoyed our dinner so much we ate there again the second night. The high quality of the culinary technique was a pleasant surprise. Our favorite dishes: Goose breast, beef tartare, Surf and Turf( Beef filet and langostino). The service was also top notch. We used the geothermal pools next door to the hotel......really relaxing. The other activities in the area that we did: Lava cave tour and Glacier tour. Especially noteworthy: I accidentally left my new Brookstone travel makeup mirror at the hotel. Mariana, from the front desk, contacted me via email and then dropped it off for me at my hotel in Reykjavik the next day. That kind of above and beyond kindness is a rarity. We loved our stay at the Hotel Husafell and Mariana made us love it even more!

author: 35titusl
title: New hotel, nice scenery, good service, good food!
text: Was here for a short one night stay a couple of days back before moving to other parts of Iceland. The hotel compound looks modern and Scandinavian, and some parts near the carpark were still under construction. However, the main compound is nicely decorated. We had a room facing the mountains and could also see the heated outdoor pool from the window. Everything was good, and the toilet is pretty spacious, especially the showering area. It was a good stay and the staff were generally helpful in terms of making sure we had food to eat and answering our queries on road information and routes to take to the next destination. We were en route to laugarvartn from husafell, and we drove past the whale fjord area. One of the most beautiful and quiet region which is outside of the main ring road. Certainly worth a drive by and to see the locals picking humongous mussels from the beach. Food wise, the restaurant at the hotel serves above average food. The decor is also beautiful and simple, offering unblocked views of the mountain. The breakfast spread could have been better, but no complaints about the lunch and dinner. The prices are a little on the expensive side based on Iceland restaurant standards, but the portions are certainly enough to feel full. It was an enjoyable stay at this hotel on the whole. Would loved to have stay on longer if possible to enjoy the other facilities. Apparently the hotel provides some form of swim wear for those who forgotten to bring theirs for the outdoor pool. Good place to relax, enjoy the scenery and forgot about the other worldly happenings.

author: ChristieR182
title: Beautiful new hotel in gorgeous location
text: This was by far our favorite hotel during our latest road trip through Iceland. The hotel is new, having opened less than a year ago. The staff is delightful. Hotel restaurant is fabulous. There is an adjacent pool (complete with water slide for the little ones) and hot pot that guest can use just one flight of stairs away, below the hotel. The hotel is bright and airy with several seating areas. Rooms are bright, modern and very clean. Beds are delightfully comfortable. We had need for three beds. Our room included a king – which they pulled apart for two twin beds and also a pull out sofa bed. The sofa bed was comfortable for my 15 year old, but made the room a bit tight on space when it was unfolded – but it was just fine. Bathroom was large and bright – although there was no privacy in the shower area (was not separate and had no curtain – pretty typical though). Our only issue – the in room heating was hot – very hot. In the middle of winter we had a window wide open all night so we didn’t boil. Breakfast is served in the dining room – which is a wall of floor to ceiling windows on three sides and has sweeping views. Breakfast offers a very wide selection of foods – both continental (cold breakfast items), plus hot breakfast (eggs, has browns, sausage, bacons, etc) and a delightful assortment of pastries and fresh baked breads and jams. The hotel offers wake-up service for the northern lights. Put your name on the list and hope that the dance happens. It’s gorgeous and you need only to step outside the front doors for an amazing view.

author: chrisdknight
title: Amazing Hotel and Restaurant
text: Hotel Husafell is an Oasis in the Icelandic scenery. My friend and I shared a twin room for a night after self-driving our rental car. It is an easy and safe drive from Reykjavki (approx 2 hours) even in winter, including stunning scenery on the way and especially around the hotel itself. Hotel Husafell is a base for a number of excursions so there are day trips coming through around midday, but the rest of the time was a comfortable number of people. There is a golf course and spa facilities though we did not use these. Staff: They were simply amazing. Checking in and out was easy and the night porter took our details to give a wake up call if the Northern Lights appeared. The wait staff in the restaurant were attentive and knowledgable, plus happy to have a friendly chat and give advice on local attractions, names of mountains, and expert on their wine selection! But most importantly... THE FOOD! The restaurant at Husafell is the only place to eat in the area (at least in winter), but that is more than acceptable because the food was devine. From the amazing bread served with each meal all through to the multiple courses it was heaven. They served a wide range of local produce, meat and fish and it was all cooked to perfection with amazing flavours. The room was spacious and very comfortable with plenty of natural light. A large and well designed modern bathroom plus free wifi throughout the Hotel. There was underfloor heating throughout and it was very comfortable temperature even in mid winter. The cost is not cheap but it is most definitely worth it, in fact I would say it is worth more than what we paid as this was first class service and amenities. Everything you need is provided and there are a number of options to keep occupied in the area, we did the Glacier Tunnel tour the following day which begins at the Hotel.

author: bragibaldursson
title: Winter visit
text: I was invited with a group of people to stay at Hotel Husafell for 2 days. I am from Iceland and have visited Husafell on many occasions but never before in dead of winter and not after the NEW hotel opened. What a great visit it was. Felt really welcome by the staff and the room and bed was excellent. Since it is low season we weren´t expecting much in terms of service and food. Boy were we wrong. Staff were making sure all the time we were comfortable and things were to our liking. After the morning meeting we had a two course lunch starting with slow poured creamy vegetable soup and then an excellent cod dish. After wrapping up the meetings in the afternoon we were treated to the local swimming pool and spa. Enjoyed the dark skies and wind while soaking up all the heat from the hot pots. Dinner was a culinary journey starting with a small teaser of salmon roe, trout. This was followed by mussel and scallop soup. The second starter was crab claws on the barbie. The main course was a surf and turf beef and crab with gratinated potatoes, lobster, portabello mushrooms. The final course was almost too much after all this feasting but did not disappoint. Spices were a perfect match and all courses had mustard seeds which added a nice continuum. The wine selection is excellent and the prices are good. Surroundings are beautiful and the air is second to none. Recommend this place for meetings, nature lovers, or a weekend away.

author: DianeM92
title: NEW Modern Sleek Hotel near Ice Cave w Wonderful Pool & Hot Tub
text: Simply beautiful hotel with a high end restaurant/bar in it. This hotel seems to be built to coincide with the opening of the nearby ice cave that was carved into the Langjökull glacier. Comfortable beds, sleek, modern furniture and a high end bathroom with a rain shower head. Pool are was wonderful- a slide for young children, two pools and a hot tub. All the water was heated geothermally. Loved it! Pool area was open 10 am - 8 pm ( I think) FYI- Husafell is a very small town- about 50 km or 42 miles from Borgarnes. This hotel is tucked into an area with a campground, bistro, gas station and very small grocery store. When I booked this hotel, Borgarnes was listed on it and I assumed it was in the larger town Borgarnes. When in fact, it was an additional 45 minutes East. Consequently, we reorganized our site seeing and instead of driving west into the Snaefellsbaer peninsuala, we took the pricy Into the Glacier ice cave tour and we're glad we did. It was a highlight of our trip. As a teacher, my family and I were not interested in dining in the high end restaurant. We loved the bistro, just steps below the hotel. We ate dinner there twice and loved it. Free wi-fi The hotel room doors have alarms on them and they didn't close and click locked, so you had to push or pull the door shut harder than would you expect each time or the alarm would go off.

author: swift98b
title: Newly Opened and Very Nice
text: This property has only been open for a couple weeks. It is brand new construction. Our room was very nice. It was spacious, it had a nice desk, it had a very good shower and bathroom, it had coffee and tea service. It even had a small refrigerator. That is unusual for Iceland. One thing I found interesting was that there were lots of electrical outlets all over the room. The ones at the desk even included a USB connection so that you could charge your portable electronics. We found the bed very comfortable and got a good night's sleep. Being out in the country, it is very quiet here. The breakfast was better than average with hot offerings of eggs, bacon, sausage, potatoes and beans in addition to the usual cold offerings. There is in-room WiFi available. Being a new place, they were having teething problems with the guest routers. A quick trip to the desk, and we were online with the staff router system and everything worked just right. I like that the staff had a ready work around for this internet problem. These guys are off to a good start.

author: jk366
title: Find another hotel
text: Didn't realize it was a smoking hotel. Bath tiny. Broken tiles and plaster. Grout missing. Replaced poorly with caulking. Beds ok. A.C. adjustable. Small lobby. Staff friendly and helpful. Pool clean. Deck needs some help. We stayed in a room that did NOT have an updated bathroom. Our friends got that room! Bath light was dirty, dim and probably original construction. With many hotels in Rock Springs I would avoid this one!

author: misty_bee_Wyo
title: Good value, convenient location
text: Very conveniently located hotel with friendly check-in. I stayed here twice in April on two separate work trips. Very clean, nice linens and clean bathroom. Plenty of plugins and ports. Rooms have a fridge, microwave, single serve coffee, and hair dryer, and the ice machine is close. Quiet hotel off the interstate. Close to gas stations, fast food, and the mall. Had my reserved room ready before official check-in time. The window in the room opens wide for fresh air. There are no screens on the windows. One of my rooms had a safety lock bar so I was able to leave it open a bit at night for fresh air, but the other room was missing the bar, so I couldn’t safely leave the window open. This hotel does offer smoking rooms, they are separated from other rooms with a partition on one end of the facility, so non-smokers will not be bothered by any smoke smells. The first smoking room I had barely even smelled like a smoking room. No burn holes anywhere, etc. The second smoking room had more of an odor, but was still clean.

author: anitabE5059AC
title: Raelynn earned this for the hotel
text: Arriving exhautsed with my toddler, Sandy quickly lifted my mood, making me laugh while offering my daughter fresh cookies and fruit. Dylan was more than accommodating while helping me regain entrance to the building after misplacing my room key. The next morning, there is a knock on thedoor at 8 am. I open the door and a blonde females first words are, "not yet?" I said, "are you kidding? Check out is at 12, right?" She said, "I need to know when you're checking out." I went to shut the door. She stops the door and says, "well you need to put the dnd sign on the door then". After working several years at a 340 room resort and conference center, I knew this was incorrect. I called the front desk to inform them of this rogue housekeeper. Dylan was very empathetic and apologized immediately. Then the noise starts from the next room as if maliciously done. It was the same housekeeper. Walking to the front desk, I asked another housekeeper where the floor supervisor was and get the troublesome housekeepers name. At that moment, Raelynn charges toward us and yells her name. She then says, "by the way it's not 8 am its 9 because of daylight savings time!" There was never an apology for banging on my door and waking up my toddler after days on the road and a late night. We'd picked this place over another because of the noon check out. Raelynn, if the hotel continues to employ you after your aggression and blatant disrespect towards guests; perhaps you should use this unfortunate interaction as a stepping stone to understanding the hospitality industry and learn basic human interaction skills. Otherwise, Ana and Ashley were also fantastic!

author: candys947
title: Awesome Staff is Warm and Welcoming
text: I stopped at the Baymont Inn in Rock Springs last night while on a cross-country road trip. I was greated first by the delicious smell of cookies baking, and then by a delightful front desk clerk named Sandy! Sandy cheefully told me about each of the hotel's features, gave me a map of the hotel, and reminded me to come back in a few minutes because the cookies would be done! I talked to two more people on the front desk team later on - primary due to an odd credit card charge ( Expedia issue, not Baymont's fault). They were both as helpful as they could be - not a bit dismissive. In the morning I saw Emily at the desk - she too was solicitous and affable. Such a team of staff, who really do care about their guests, are rare enough that I felt I had to write this review to praise them! As for the room - it was nice enough. I think a remodel should include more electrical outlets. I wished the vending machine had coke products. The breakfast layout was standard. I can give top marks though to the strong and reliable wifi network. The point is, I left the hotel this morning with a smile on my face, because to me, a friendly, caring staff is the key to an enjoyable stay. The cookies don't hurt either. And the Rock Springs Baymont Inn has got that all figured out.

author: claudes307
title: Took me in at midnight.
text: Fell in off the interstate at midnight when the previous 12 hrs of the day fell apart and I was running well late. Dylan at the front desk was most helpful and found me one of the only three rooms they had left - mine was the only non-smoking room. Thanks, Dylan!! The facility is "average" at best - even though it is a Wyndham property, it has seen better days. The halls especially are dingy and run-down. The room was better, but signs of age and "can we keep this room open for one more year" were obvious. The beds were clean and well-made, and the room was clean - just "old". The room had a nice armoire - no closet - and a nice drawered cabinet with a microwave. There was a nice fridge, also. So - consider the room well-appointed for the average traveler. Breakfast was typical Road Warrior fare - but made all the better by the lady who was in charge of the food line. What a prize!! She was cheerful, happy, helpful, and made everyone's morning better. I only wish I had gotten her name to give proper credit. The front desk checkout personnel were also cheerful, helpful, and professional. I hope that at some point Wyndham can afford to put some upgrade money into the property.

author: K7920CDrobertb
title: Treating Guests Above the Rest
text: I wish I would have stayed with them from the beginning. My vehicle broke down in Rock Springs, WY. I stayed somewhere else the first few nights. The vehicle hit a snag and I needed to stay another night. This time, I chose Baymont Inn. WOW. What a difference. Nicer place, nicer room, better breakfast, wonderful manager, and LOWER PRICE. You cannot go wrong here. The manager, Robert Olguin, went way above and beyond. First he let me stay past time waiting to hear from the garage. Second, when it was time to go, Robert took me to the garage. WOW. He drove me the miles to my waiting vehicle. THANK YOU, Robert. Do not waste time checking any where else, stay with Baymont Inn. He knows how to take the edge off your trip. That is greatly appreciated.

author: rpg1ATL
title: Wasn't sure if I should stay, but glad I did
text: I hesitated in the ranking of 4 (very good), but based off the other reviews, I think it qualifies for one based off my experience and how much effort they're putting into improving that location. My wife and I hesitated in booking at this hotel, but we figured in this case, it's the destination, not the journey and this location was a perfect place to stop on our way to Florida. The hotel is definitely older and has seen some years. That being said, the outside is being repainted and maintenance and modifications are under way. The outside still needs some landscaping, but based off it's location, it may be a hard fix. When we checked in, they had cheese, fruit, crackers and cookies and beverages available. The lobby was clean, recently updated and decked out in Halloween decorations. The front desk agent was polite, smiling and professional. You could tell she enjoyed the upgrades available to the guests. Our non smoking room was neat, clean, no stains or smells. The bedding was good, not great. The cabinets were a little rickity, but the appliances were all in good shape. Bathroom was neat and clean. New granite and tiles. Plenty of dog poo bags in the back outside, but we took the dogs around the block for nice walks and potty breaks along the grass strips of the businesses (of course we cleaned up after them). In the morning, the bill was slipped under the door, nice touch. The breakfast was actually one of the better one's we've experienced at La Quinta. They had eggs, sausage, bacon, cheese and of course all the other usual suspects. All hot and plentiful. I'm glad we decided to stay after all, it was a very pleasant stay

author: 592lesliek
title: Make sure you don’t leave anything in the room!
text: If you ever stay at the La Quinta Inn in Rock Springs, Wyoming, make sure you don’t leave anything in the room! If you do, you’ll never get back it back! Here’s what happened to us. On Thursday, August 8, 2014, my wife and I drove from Salt Lake City to Rock Springs, Wyoming, and we spent the night at the La Quinta. We were on our way to Denver for a wedding. The next morning, we checked out; we didn’t realize we left our computer charger in the room until we arrived in Denver that evening. We called La Quinta as quickly as we could and explained the situation. They asked for our room and phone number and said they’d call back. We waited—but a call never came. On Sunday morning, August, 31, 2014, on our drive back to Salt Lake City, we stopped in Rock Springs to find out what happened. They had no record of our call. A heavy set woman at the front desk grudgingly showed me our room—there was no charger there. She next took me to their lost and found, which was empty. It had been “cleared out,” she said, without explaining what cleared out meant. The Inn staff was focused on renting rooms; they had no interest in our lost item. Tell me please, what kind of Inn is it that has no interest in returning lost items to its customers?! Answer: La Quints is the kind of Inn that gives its staff first crack at whatever’s left in a room. Beware if you stay there! A new Apple charger cost me $88—the price of the room was $124.

author: DonnaB953
title: Nice hotel but just missing something...
text: This is a nice hotel but the staff are a little lacking... We got in at 5:00 after a heck of a time with a rental car in SLC. They gave me my room key, we pulled around the side to unload. Grabbed our stuff and headed to the room. When I walked up, I knew something wasn't right because the door wasn't closed. It still wasn't made up or cleaned up. It was 5:00 p.m. and they were still cleaning rooms! I walked back to the front desk, they wanted us to wait another 30 minutes. I said NO WAY! We were exhausted and wanted a room to nap in now! They ended up exchanging our room for another. It just kind of bothered me that there were many rooms where the house keeping was still working on them. Breakfast was your basic free breakfast... but it was hot and tasty! Not sure if we would stay again. Beds were comfy though.

author: TrippingMaverick
title: The longest hallway outside of Versailles.
text: I arrived very late and tired. The clerk seemed like she was waiting for up for me and was fast and efficient getting me checked in and to my room. The long hallway leading to my room was disconcerting. My being tired, made the hallway seem to stretch out in front of me and I got a dizzy feeling. But the room was large and clean and most importantly the bed was large and comfortable. I slept like a rock. My morning shower was "invigorating" having little to no hot water. Apparently the boiler had broken down. The included breakfast was very good with sausage, bacon, eggs, waffles, cereals, yogurts, fruits and breads. The breakfast food area was very small, very busy, and very crowded. But there was another small adjoing eating area that was nice and quiet to eat in (1)(2). I had a room on a wing which was quiet and with access to the side entrance, parking lot and pool, and was able to avoid the long hallway. Overall a pretty nice hotel (3)(4). I would have given it a 4 but the broken boiler and no hot water demanded a demerit. (1) The La Quinta in Reno, NV has a similar small/split-up breakfast/dining area, but put the waffle-maker in the dining area, resulting in a huge crowd of noisy teenagers waiting on waffles and not quieter dining area. (2) Check out the La Quinta in Ely, NV. It has a much larger breakfast and dining area. Very nice, relaxing and enjoyable. (3) I recommend travelers use I-70/US-50 rather than I-80 and stay at the La Quinta in Ely, NV. (4) I recommend the hotel's owners/investors visit the La Quinta in Ely, NV when considering renovations.

author: MtnWeaver
title: Good - but needs some work
text: I did a late midnight check-in as I was on the road. I had reserved a King bed, and ended up with double queens. This wasn't horrible, as I was travelling alone. Both thin bedspreads were stained with black marks that looked almost like shoe polish. The furniture was older and quite beat-up. I thought the windows were frosted glass, however were just really dirty. They didn't have any light-blocking curtains, just thin off-white curtains in which you could see through. As I was a female travelling alone, this made me very uncomfortable. Plus, once the sun came out, I couldn't sleep, as it was WAY bright in my room. There was no "do not disturb sign" in the room, so housekeeping came by 3 times, starting at 7:00 am to knock on the door. So, not a very good quality of sleep. The room, hallways, and entry ways all smelled of stale smoke, which ended up giving me asthma issues. The refrigerator was plugged in but did not cool small water bottles over an 8 hour time frame. The toilet took several flushes to flush. The evening staff was very nice, but the morning staff was not very professional and sat there gossiping all morning and didn't re-stock the breakfast room supplies. The perks: the breakfast was actually pretty decent (waffles, sausage, bacon, eggs, biscuits & gravy) and the beds were very comfortable.

author: FL_iNsTaGaToR
title: Great Place!
text: My co driver and I stayed here for a week when our truck broke down and was being repaired. We both were very impressed and very grateful to have found this place. The rooms were very clean, great beds, nicely decorated and well equipped. This place goes out of the way to make you feel at home and comfortable. They have one of the best hot continental breakfast's I have seen at a motel. Allot of tasty choices from eggs, to sausage, bacon, waffles, pastries, fruit, cereal, etc, etc. The have fruit out 24 hours a day and every evening they baked a wide selection of "FRESH" cookies. The smell of them cookin reminded me of home, and would draw me out of my room every time! They also offered fresh cheese and crackers in the evening. We were unfortunate to have broke down, but I couldn't think of a better place for it to have happened. The best part of it all was the staff. I have never seen a motel go so over and beyond the norm to make sure your taken care of. They were the best! Can not wait to go back and see them... jus hope its under better circumstances! lol

author: JoshB678
title: Upgraded to a Suite!
text: The suite shouldnt be only the biggest room in the hotel, it should be the nicest. I might be being a little picky, but I am an Elite member, and I stay at LQ's across the US ALOT!!! The cords under the TV, which was on the desk, so I couldnt use it for working, were very "ratty". The couch had stains, the chairs, had stains, and the fridge was akwardly sitting in a corner. Overall the room was nice and big, but it was very poorly designed and had a bit of a messy look. The shower curtain was tattered, and the curtain bar was about to fall off the wall. For bfast, I noticed broken bowls being used to house the butter and cream cheese. Am I being picky? Maybe, but geez... but a dollar bowl! The bfast is always rather gross as well. I have stayed here multiple times, and the biscuits and gravy are horrendous, the eggs are spongy, and the sausage is rather mysterious looking. Still with a pastry, bagel, or bowl of cereal. I know this sounds like me just venting, however, the service is always top notch. All the ladies who work there go out of their way to make you feel wanted and comfy. I hope to see some changes, as I come here a lot, but will still come even if they dont change.

author: danicodd
title: Not for non-smokers!
text: If you are not a smoker, but LOVE smelling cigarette smoke in your non-smoking room, this is the place for you! The stank just bellows through the hallways and permeates your clothes, nose and pet's fur, just everything. Walking down the hall through clouds of cigarette smoke to reach our non-smoking room, makes NO sense! If we didn't just drive over 500miles, we'd leave right now. The super slow wi-fi is a bonus! Driving cross country and will be happy to spend a little more $ and pay the pet fees at a more upscale hotel from here on in. 20minutes later: The smoking down the hallway got so bad that we were totally disgusted and actually on line looking for other hotels that accept pets in this area, even though we are exhausted! Gave up d/t the slow internet and called the front desk instead to see this hotel can redeem itself and move us to a different room FAR from any smoking rooms. The woman at the front desk was very sweet and accommodating and didn't hesitate to move us. Thankfully there were a few rooms available or we would have packed up and moved regardless of our super long exhausting day. My throat is itchy, my nose is stuffed up and my head aches from breathing in smokey air for the past hour. Not a nice end to such a long day on the road. New room is much better, but unless you are an avid smoker, I still do not recommend this hotel. Time for a hot shower and nasal wash before bed! If you end up here and do not want to sleep in a room reeking of smoke, or walk through a hallway that stinks like a bar full of smokers, make sure you make it very clear that you want to be REALLY FAR away from ANY smoking rooms. 2 days later..... husband and I are still coughing, as if we actually smoked a pack of cigarettes that night, and I have a sore throat and feel like Im getting sick! Thanks La Quinta! Never again!

author: Maralyne
title: Pleasantly surprised! Will stay here again
text: I booked my room at La Quinta Inn of Rock Springs through a web site where the name of the hotel isn't revealed until after booking. This was rather scary, but saved me some money. I'll admit I was disappointed when I saw it was La Quinta, but I was very pleasantly surprised upon check-in and for the duration of my trip. Upon check-in there were fresh cookies as well as an assortment of cheese & crackers and freshly popped popcorn in the lobby area. My room was clean & quiet. The view out the window was of a courtyard type area with trees and grass - not at all what I had expected in Rock Springs. The room had a refrigerator, microwave and in-room coffee. The bathroom was good-sized and had a separate vanity area complete with hair dryer and plenty of counter space. There was a decent continental breakfast and for whatever reason the room was crowded and I was the only woman at breakfast. The evening before I had noticed a group of ladies playing cards just off the lobby area but I didn't see any of them at breakfast. I had booked and paid in advance for two nights but only stayed for one. My business wrapped up early so I actually left at 6pm of day two, but not because I didn't enjoy my stay. I travel so often and was close enough to home that I decided to leave early and make the drive over the mountains while I had decent daylight. I will be in Rock Springs again for business and I would not hesitate to book at this property. This place is much larger than it looks and I found the expansive parking lot to be on the dim side, so I asked permission to park on the side of the building towards KFC because the lighting there was brighter. As a single female traveler this was important to me and worth mentioning to others. I also noted there is a coin operated laundry facility available. I didn't use this, but would if i were staying for several days or a week.

author: TSR01
title: Its La Quinta lol
text: If you've stayed at La Quinta's before, then this one isn't much different. Good breakfast, Scrambled eggs, sausage, toast, biscuits and gravy, waffles, cereal, milk, yogurt, variety of juices, etc.. The pool, as you'll see is not open durring the winter, the business center DOES have a computer with "high speed" internet AND PRINTER, No extra charge for printing. The exercise room?? well... Hmmm its ok, I guess its better then nothing.. the treadmills are a bit warn out, and the universal....I guess its not really a universal weight machine, but hey, you can work your arms and legs etc sorta.. lol. The beds are.......older, but plenty of pillows, the bathroom is a bit small, but the sink and ironing board etc is in a separate area so its not really together. Good water pressure.. KFC / Long Johns Silvers, Kmart, C-stores, Mexican restaraunt and other places to eat are VERY CLOSE, with in 5 min walk from motel.. Cable TV ACTUALLY HAS more then 7 channels!! It has about 50 or so.. OH and free wireless internet.. (sorta, I think they need to update their wireless, its spotty, sometimes works sometimes doesn't..lol)

author: RMLtravels
title: Authentic old-school Chinese experience.
text: Took the family to this unique old-school Chinese hotel. It is full of charm and beautiful buildings, passageways and (bamboo) gardens. There are waterfalls and interesting signage. I felt this was a place of significance and history. Amongst the happiest visitors were older Chinese folk on family trips and reunions who looked happy and well catered for. The BGH did not cater well for young families and I would not recommend it for wheelchair, pram users etc... Rooms are ornate and clean but well worn and very small. All gadgets worked (fabulous computer console for light switches, which were only feet away!) Mini bar prices were staggering. The breakfast was pretty random but what you expect of a three star hutong hotel. Bathrooms clean, modern and in heat working condition. There were umbrellas...next to the toilet. Ok, here’s the bit that really upset me. The room we rented STANK OF SMOKE. And recent smoke. In the curtains, bed and gold wallpaper. This really changed my opinion of the place and maybe it’s a reflection of the older, local generation that stay there but for us, it ruined an authentic experience.

author: billbk
title: Let Down
text: Let Down We were looking forward to our stay as the internet pictures looked wonderful with a nice, Central garden Ching Dynasty single level buildings Close to Metro. The pictures of the hotel and grounds are not representative. Many of the ground floor rooms and suits have translucent treatment on the windows making the rooms very dark and dingy. The rooms are small and the bath rooms are even smaller and are totally enclosed with limited ventilation resulting in bad odours. All sorts of cleaning equipment, spare beds were left laying in the corridors. Scuff marks pealing paint etc. in may places and some very extensive. I developed a very bad back ache and finally realised the the bed mattress sunk excessively in the middle which probably was the cause of my problem. The furniture is Chinese style which is made from hard carved polished wood giving a nice appearance but making them very uncomfortable to use for any length time. All nicer outlook rooms are on the 3 rd floor and with no elevators they are not suitable for physically impaired people. Breakfast is definitely not worth it as the choice is limited with food quality being very poor. The service was equally the same as it felt like we were very privileged to being served. There were 3 staff pooled together talking and when I asked for the orange juice dispenser to be filled, I got a look that I cannot describe (all drink dispensers were empty) from then on we ate local Chinese or McDonalds which was a 5 minute walk. I need to mention that the Bell boy plus Housekeeping did a super job. We chose the hotel as it was in a good area close to the metro with nice central garden, However at a price of 800 RMB ($A180) a night we could have stayed at several 5 star hotels and many 4 star hotel which start at 520 RMB a night. Be careful when you book as the breakfast, tax and service charge is not included in the quoted price. There is a large choice of old style hotels with gardens at a much lower price which we will take advantage of on our next trip. Disappointed and let down.

author: bobasheville
title: The WiFi difficulties are no longer a problem.
text: I stayed here for a week and the place is great. The WiFi is not fast but you can have more than one device. This place is a little hard to find as it is in a Hutong which is all small houses and wide alleys. A car can go down the alley but everyone walking needs to hug the walls. To find the place remember the alley is right before you get to Mc Donalds and has a beautiful archway over the entrance to the alley. The hotel is large, beautiful grounds, decorated in all old china design/ Very clean, comfortable beds, marble baths with all American Standard fixtures. Big TV but only one news channel in English. Front desk all spoke great English. They change money at a better rate than the banks. They do not do tours. Restaurant just OK. Close walk to main street and Subway. I had a small room for one person $50 per night. On 3rd floor no elevators. Overall a great 3 Star hotel with much more charm than a 5 Star hotel.

author: willyard4
title: Decent hotel, lousy resturant
text: Housekeeping likes to leave the bottom dirty sheet when they change the bed but are happy to finish the job when you catch them. I is a decent hotel with a .nice atmosphere. The biggest deficiency here is the restaurant. They say they open at 7 AM but the buffet usually is not in place until 7:30 or later. There are signs all over prohibiting smoking but the cooks come into the restaurant from the kitchen smoking so they obviously smoke while preparing our food. The good side: the people are very friendly and mostly effecient although their wake up calls are usually late, if they call at all. The hotel is in a fairly quite location and several hundred meters from a major street that has abundant resturants and is near the drum and bell towers. It is a little pricy for a 3 star hotel. This is my 3rd trip to China using this hotel and probably my last. The quality and service have gone down while the price continues to rise. It reminds me of the old Russian hotels where there are a half dozen people doing a one man job. There are usually 5 or 6 staff hanging around the wing lobby but no one does much. There are lots of decent hotels in the area that are a lot more reasonably priced that will get my business on my next trip. I have started each of my trips with a week in this hotel and spent the last few days of my trip here also with a month in other provinces so I have spent 7 or 8 weeks total in this hotel. It can be great if you do not have high expectations. It does sleep well and the air conditioning works great.

author: ErikM185
title: Oasis in hectic Beijing
text: Bamboo Garden hotel is a located in one of the famous Beijing hutongs not far from the very center. Walking distance from the Belltower and Drumtower. The rooms are located in the back of a courtyard. Nice and guaranteed silence. The rooms are very clean and well maintained. The beds are close to European standard, comfortable and the right size. The bathroom also is very clean and well equiped. Nice products, good shower and a sufficient size tub. The rooms are equiped with a good working and silent airconditioning. The hotel has a good restaurant and the menu offers a variety of tastefull dishes. In the typical bamboo garden you will also find a nice terrace where you can enjoy a cold beer or tea. The staff speaks good english but a little more friendlyness would not hurt. All in all a very nice place to stay but mind that you are in a narrow alley where taxi drivers hate to come. They can but they try to avond it. The porter however helps you out finding transportation.

author: whiteroses
title: Don't judge a book by its cover - what a pleasant surprise
text: Right in the middle of a hutong, this hotel is so easy to miss. The nondescript gate does not give any clue to the haven beyond. First there is a the reception to negotiate...nothing spectacular, just your ordinary garden variety. And then someone helps you to the rooms. Oh my - walk along the garden paths with its lovely grounds and little pools on either side...and you sort of share your head wondering whether you were really on a hutong street just a few minutes ago. There are several buildings housing the various guestrooms. My room is in a pleasant building with a pleasant view of the gardens. Inside the building is a "common room" decorated, of course, with Chinese furnishings where guests can gather for pre or post dinner drinks. Very civilised! My room was quite spacious and had a computer in it. Television radio, telephone...all the usual bells and whistles...except they were all of the "antique" variety. Chinese furniture (rosewood) in the rooms were very impressive too. There is a restaurant in the hotel but the food was not what I expected. Maybe we only have the "westernised" chinese food elsewhere that is why I found the food here in Beijing not too my linking. I thought it was generally greasy. I had to wait until I got to Hongkong before I could satisfy my culinary cravings. If I had a chance, I would come back to the Bamboo Garden.

author: GlobalPassion
title: Pleasant Old Beijing near HouHai
text: This place was a great pick for us on this trip. In terms of access, it is within walking distance of the subway station---which is THE best way to get around all of Beijing. It is also close to western McDonalds, but local Chinese eateries as well. They have bike rentals on site--the preferred way to experience HouHai. It is a whole different way to see the city. Location is excellent, central in the city The ambiance of this hotel was built from an old Qing Dynasty residency. It had been a palace, and it still has that old ancient feeling. Once you cross the threshold, you enter into old China. We never ate breakfast in the hotel because it was way over priced, so we used the opportunity to eat the breakfast foods on the street. Perfectly wonderful! All along the way to HouHai are vendors and coffee shops...one of our favorite neighborhoods in Beijing. It was cool! The rooms are very comfortable-good pillows. The staff was attentive, excellent free wifi in the rooms-actually in whole complex. *There was even a computer in the room if you needed it* A plus if you don't want to drag your computer around with you. There is a restaurant on site, tea house--lots of grounds for walking around and contained from the hustle and bustle of the modern city. We were very satisfied with our choice. It wasn't a bare bones place, but also not a five star. We highly recommend it for families, especially with little children who need to wander about.

author: MacHope
title: nice view
text: We stayed here for 7 nights and booked a standard suite since it got a very good feed back and nice picture of the garden, BUT we were fooled by these things. Since we booked via agoda there is no chance to change room since you already checked in. We complained to the reception but they said that all suit are like this or worse. I did check at the lay out and our is the best on the floor hence they could not recommend a better one. Staff kept talking and smoking inside the building and nest to our windows so we could not open it or they can look onto our room. The door in the bed room open to the alley where people pass by can look into your room, or you can open small windows on top but you could hear the honking of the cars or electric bikes in the alley in front of your windows. Funny is if you book 2 5 seats cars for 8 passengers + 2 driver ( 150 each) it is cheaper than one 7 seater car for 6 passengers and 1 driver (400 RMB) where is the logic ?! Buut it is recommend to take the hotel cab and not a taxi since the cab driver intent not to go the shortest way. There is a Mc Don. fast food at the entrance of the alley where you can buy your BF since it is not included. Along the main road there are lot of restaurant for good price. On the way to the lake through the hutong you can find shops selling fruits for very little money. The walk to the subway is approx. 500 m from there it is the best way to go anywhere in the city. Pros - Staff is very polite - Room size ( 4.5 x 7.5 m for standard suite) - Car service for sight seeing ( 700 RMB for great wall and Ming tomb) - Two TV for standard suit - Bed draps - Location - Computer in room ( but no youtube or facebook due to governments restriction) - Near to small shops and supermarket - Wifi in room Cons - Almost no international or sport TV channel ( some with lower quality or not sharp) - Windows cannot be opened since walk-by people can look into your room ( standard suite) - Windows are not cleaned regularly - No breakfast - Price is high - view from room is terrible (standard suite) - Staff smoke in the corridor hence we had to insulated the door with wet towel - Slow internet - The bed light cabinet switched the light on uncontrollably during the night two times and we had to pull out the key card ! they repaired it but it come again

author: olefaithful
title: Second visit as nice as the first!
text: I booked the Bamboo Garden twice in 2011. First time for touring with with two grown daughters and a granddaughter. Its central location in Beijing is important from a tour standpoint. Second stay was with another adult. Both times, our suite was located on th first floor, facing the hutong alley. It was perfectly acceptable to us, as we spent little time in the room awake. No hutong noise bothered us while we were in the room, either. The room and bath have western-style amenities. When we had time, we walked around the beautiful courtyard. The morning breakfast buffet was wonderful, and the restaurant opened in plenty of time to get a full day of sightseeing in. Check in and out were simple and efficient. The Bamboo Garden has a unique history in Beijing lodgings...surf the 'net to learn about it! It is not a western hotel. And walking in the neighborhood was a wonderful experience, too. That's the best part of traveling, isn't it?

author: TorontoTim
title: Very good hotel
text: Just stayed 3 nights. Overall, very good. Location is great. Lots of interesting things within immediate walking distance (5 mins.), Drum Tower is very close, subway 5 min. walk away; we walked home from the Forbidden City (30 mins.?). Charming property, as other reviewers have described. Room was well decorated although a little small, not great for having to do any work at the desk (no chair, just a backless stool). And of course we weren't there to watch TV, but if you do want to relax in front of the TV after a long day, the English-language options are very limited -- only one channel, and even it isn't English all the time. Breakfast was fine but not excellent. We booked a car through the hotel to take us on a day trip to Mutianyu (Great Wall) and that worked out very well. Very comfortable car, good driver, fit to our schedule, reasonable rate. As for taxis to/from the airport, I disagree with those reviewers who say you need to book a car. We used taxis both ways for less than RMB100 each way, with no wait and no problem whatsoever. 30-second wait in line at the airport, and pre-booked waiting at the hotel for the return trip. Overall, some minor issues but we would stay there again. It was really nice to get a more authentic experience (hotel and area) than would have been the case in a big-brand-name hotel.

author: Jen78703
title: An oasis in the middle of concrete
text: I traveled to Beijing on a business trip and stayed for a few days of sightseeing- so I wanted a comfortable hotel that would fit my business needs as well as my preference for staying in a hotel with some local flavor. My colleagues all prefer the grand Western hotels so I was hoping they'd be happy here too. In the past I have had problems with getting a random taxi at the airport and having the driver find our hotel. Because there were 4 of us I prearranged (through the hotel) for a van to pick us up - it was simple to find the driver and he got us to the hotel easily. I loved this place. It's a walled in oasis- filled greenery- it was so pretty- green and lush- and I enjoyed walking around the small grounds. The food was tasty at the restaurant and the service wonderful- but no English was spoken here. There is a sweet little "house on the hill" where you can have massages. This came in handy latish one night (10pm) when one of my colleagues was having trouble with her neck/back- 30 min after calling the front desk a masseur arrived. She said there was some difficulty with the language but at all times the masseur was very professional. The tearoom/bar was beautiful but didn't offer much other than drinks- I was hoping for a larger assortment of tea food. Our rooms were all large and very comfortable, the internet access was better than many other places I have stayed at. The front desk spoke English quite well and I didn't have any difficulty dealing with them. Just remember if you're exchanging money- the currency has to look new for them to accept it- which is pretty standard here. There's a 24 convenience store at the end of the street with pretty much anything you want- from cough drops to yogurt to even Great Wall wine- for $3 a bottle. The day before we left I opted for a trip to the Great Wall while my colleagues slept in then wandered around the immediate area- they loved it. Lots of quaint shops, places to eat and a very pretty lake area to walk around. If you need a cab- be sure to order one well ahead of time. We had a dinner business meeting and didn't pre-order a cab- the front desk person told us that we would be better off walking to the main st and getting a cab there. Bad move- it took us more than 45 min to finally find an empty cab that would take us to the meeting.

author: KJA3
title: A mostly positive experience
text: I spent 6 nights at the Bamboo Garden, and had a mostly positive experience there. The location was great - about a 10 minute walk from a metro station and within walking distance of several wonderful sites within the city. The grounds are lovely and the rooms were nicely furnished, with some touches that went beyond the basics. My bed was very comfortable, and I really appreciated the free use of an in-room computer. The one problem with my single room was that it was poorly laid out, with no convenient place for me to put my suitcase, and for the size, I thought the single was overpriced. The garden-side restaurant looked nice and there is also a comfortable lounge in the compound. Other pluses included English-speaking desk staff, an on-site spa that offers guests a free 15-minute facial, and airport transport either to or from the airport for guests staying 3 or more days (more on that later). With one noteable exception, the staff (desk and other) were wonderfully helpful and welcoming. The exception was one young woman at the desk, who repeatedly refused to make reservations or place inquiries for me. I didn't make many such requests, and was surprised by her response. Fortunately, other staff were more than happy to assist, so I just returned to the desk when she was not there. As one example, I wanted a reservation for dinner at Dadong Kaoya, having read beforehand that reservations were essential; this young woman refused to even call the restaurant for me. I'm very glad I later asked someone else to try, because I would not have been able to eat at that restaurant if I hadn't had a reservation - it was very busy and they were turning people away. This same young woman did arrange my transport to the airport - but didn't arrange the free transportation that I had clearly indicated I wanted, instead arranging for a taxi. Not realizing the difference, I faced quite an awkward moment at the airport when I said the hotel was to pay the fare. The taxi driver called the hotel, and after I spoke to several different people at length, they agreed to pay him. (BTW, the driver was really nice about it.) To reiterate, though, all the other staff were very pleasantly welcoming and accomodating.

author: bheh1314
title: A hidden gem
text: We stayed at this hotel for 4 nights at the start of our holiday and again for 3 nights before returning to the UK. We chose this hotel as a change from the main chain hotels in Beijing which we have stayed in on previous visits. This is a lovely hotel within reasonable walking distance, through the hutongs, to the lakes Houhai & Quanhai. The metro line is a short walk from the hotel and taxis are cheap and plentiful on the main road near to the hotel. Despite being in a very busy part of Beijing the hotel is exceptionally quite and peaceful. We had a suite on the ground floor (room 407). The bed was giantic but, as with most Chinese beds, quite hard. The pillows were the best pillows I have ever slept on and the linen was spotlessly clean as were the rooms. The lounge room furntiure was classical Chinese carved wood, gorgeous to look at but not the most comfortable to sit on. We had a computer in the room with free internet acess which was a bonus. The rooms and the bathroom were spotless. Due to the position of our room there was not a lot of natural light. Breakfast was included in our deal and was ok. The main problem was that some of the food was not hot, in fact somtimes not even warm. That said there was a very good variety and the staff were helpful and friendly. All the staff were very helpful and we would highly recommend this hotel to anyone who doesn't wish to stay in a tall, concrete block where every room is the same.

author: English_Al
title: Excellent character hotel
text: We were delighted with this choice of hotel. It’s situated down a Hutong and takes you by surprise on approach. The road is a bit scruffy but don’t let that put you off. The hotel is a quiet oasis and a short walk from lots of restaurants and the old Bell and Drum towers. The reception staff were friendly (in contrast to some reports that I’d read) and spoke good English. The hotel buildings are set around a tranquil courtyard. The bedrooms are a good size and decorated in Chinese style. There was a huge, comfortable bed. The room was very clean with a nice bathroom and a good shower. There was even a PC in the room for free internet access! The air conditioning worked although I would have liked it to be a little cooler. The breakfast buffet was decent and had enough western food. We ate at the hotel one evening and found it to be very good value. We found it easy to navigate our way to this hotel as it is on the edge of the Hutongs. I would definitely stay here again.

author: indiancouple
title: Lovely boutique hotel, with good service
text: This hotel had character...genuine Chinese decor which was very pleasing, and a large campus, which we did not explore fully. The restaurant was very good, and everything we ate was well prepared and reasonably priced. There was always someone at the front desk who spoke excellent English, so there was never any problems of communication. The exchange rate offered for currency conversion was also very good. On request, they arranged airport pickup for 150 Rmb, which was a bit on the high side, but efficiently arranged (we managed the return airport trip in 100 Rmb quite easily by another taxi). They also arranged a taxi for the Great Wall for 600 Rmb, which again was slightly on the high side. We tried doing some flight bookings through their travel agent, but his quotes were very high; found much better rates on Ctrip. My only complaint is that the hotel seems to be trying to make too much money on the side by padding up taxi rates, travel agent fees etc. Their website says that they have a laundry room. I presumed that meant we could use the services of a washing machine/dryer. That is not true. They offer laundry services at prohibitive "per piece" rates, so beware. Location is central, but about a 10 minute walk from the Golou metro stop. Wish it was a little closer. Right in the middle of the "Hutong" neighborhood though. Overall good value for money in Beijing. Good rooms, decent prices, and overall quite comfortable. Oh yes, the free computer terminal in the room with internet was a big plus.

author: jado_and_kea
title: Memorable hotel
text: We stayed in Bamboo Garden Hotel during the Beijing leg of our China Tour primarily because we don't want generic looking hotels so much and we were not disappointed. It is located in the Hotungs and not very "famous" with taxi drivers but they were always helpful and we were able to go back no problem with help of the hotel card. The staff were friendly and very helpful. Simple service that feels genuine and none of those super trained 5 star hotel types. We went together with our 11 month old and 3 yr old kids. The staff were very kind and entertained them while we are waiting for some reception confirmation, taxi etc. The rooms are ok, clean with huge firm beds. My baby didn't like the crib they provided though( too small) so she slept with us. The huge bed was great! My 3 year old son loved the hotel so much. It's look, it's garden , with the blue birds and especially the red lanterns at night. Until now he still talks about the Bamboo Hotel and asks us to go back :) For my husband the best part is the massage. Really relaxing after a day of touring. The in room computer is also great as we didn't have room to bring our laptop with all the kiddie gear we had. There are several small eateries around but we didn't get to try them. The drumtower is also nearby and from the drumtower other places of interest are a stroll away. Definitely a good location especially if you love walking or biking around. We did not walk so much though with 2 kids in tow. But taxi was not hard to come by :)

author: kittymcgraw
title: Shaky start, great hotel
text: My first impressions of the hotel were not good - I'd booked the hotel's driver to collect me from the airport but was surprised to be asked at the hotel to pay the driver directly in cash rather than the cost being added to my hotel bill. I just had enough Chinese money with me to pay the driver. The hotel website said they offered currency exchange services so I tried to change $NZ but they wouldn't accept it, so "limited currency exchange" would have been more accurate - unless you have something like $US you're out of luck. The staff member I dealt with through this was not overly friendly or helpful. I had no problems from then on. The setting is great, very peaceful. I was shown to a lovely single room (411) full of character, with a fabulous bathroom and free internet access; later I booked an additional night and got a double room (416) which was just as good - no internet - but had a bit of drain smell in the bathroom - which as I later discovered you get in character hotels here as part of the package and is no problem if you close the bathroom door. The beds were the most comfortable of any I slept on during my trip. I ate a few dinners in the hotel restaurant and the food was OK - breakfast buffet just adequate - but also try the local street vendors and dumpling shops. Restaurant staff spoke very little English. I didn't try their spa; if you go left out the main gate and explore the hutongs you'll find the blind massage place - awesome - 2 mins walk. Make the most of the fabulous location. Most staff here speak limited English but are helpful. Ask them to write down your destination in characters to show taxi drivers, and also ask them to write in characters the hotel name and driving directions to it, as taxi drivers can never find it. This hotel was excellent value for money and offered a good balance between character and comfort.

author: 850brucen
title: Nice resort but average
text: This is a very beautiful resort. On the edge of the historical park, a world heritage site. That why we stayed here. The rooms are very modern and new and comfortable. The grounds are very attractive. Now the down side. Restaurant needs to be improved. I ordered three things off the menu before I got something they had. One friend ordered an entree that showed up more than half an hour after we had all eaten. We were actually getting ready to leave. The food was ok but really not the vibrant tastes and flavours you expect from Thai. Pretty bland actually. OK if you are in a cheap hotel but in a higher end resort not so good. This and a few other issues give you the feeling that they are not giving it their best effort. In this price range that's critical for success. There are a lot of other choices in the area. Not a bad hotel overall but with a few improvements, it would get a much higher rating, and be a much more memorable place to stay.

author: Aesp1
title: Noisy again
text: Having previously reviewed this hotel back in January, and saying I would not return, here I am. This is a hotel my company uses and I was unable to find another hotel in the price range that could offer the facilities we require - unfortunately. Last time, I described the setting as beautiful but 'bizarrely noisy' and could not identify the source of the loud music which was still blasting this time away well into the night and began again at 5am. Well, it's the hotel. The hotel literally blast music into your room from speakers around the perimeter of the grounds. I can't believe it. I rang reception to complain, the lady said "no speak English' and hung up. I went to reception to complain and with my little Thai and the security guard's little English, discovered that no, they won't be turning it off. I really can't believe it. Why do they think this is a good idea? I'm also shocked that no one else has mentioned this in a review. Well, this time, it's one star. This completely ruins this hotel for me, it's just awful. I'll be back in January and will really press them for an explanation/ solution and re-review then. If you can, just stay somewhere else that respects their guests and make the experience enjoyable, I don't have that luxury.

author: 751brettm
title: Lovely Hotel located between the historic park and Sukhothai
text: I spent three nights at the Sukhothai Treasure resort. The room was great, large and had a balcony that looked over the rice fields and mountains in the distance. Watching a storm rolling over the mountains at night was a immersible experience. The bed was firm (perhaps slightly softer than the traditional northern style), the bathroom was large with a shower and bath and there is an in room safe. The pool was perfect for cooling off after a day wandering around the ruins. It is large compared to other hotels and perfect for a couple of laps plus there is a smaller spa area. The grounds were immaculate and as mentioned by a previous reviewer there are mosquito's around, however this is not from the ponds at the hotel but rather from the abundance of rice fields in the region. I used a mozzie band on my backpack and hardly had any issues. Breakfast is the standard buffet type with a mixture of asian and western foods. There were occasions where the restaurant area was taken over by a bus load of tourist who were a little pushy (one even tried to take my Ipad off me!). I would recommend that they have tour operators put onto the larger tables and keep the smaller tables for other guests. Evening meals were more relaxed and even though there is a western menu I only order the local Thai food which was great. Expect general restaurant prices. I found that staff were generally very helpful, even driving me down to the historic park to hire a scooter. I tried the onsite massage (which seems to be constantly on sale) one evening and found it was extremely good. I guess that it comes down to the person giving the massage to you and their experience. I would get another massage there and it is priced at spa prices for Thailand. One thing to note - if you want to catch the airport bus run by Bangkok Air it is best organised when you are at the airport. It casts about 500B more using the hotel transport (however it is still a pleasant trip with the driver). It takes about 30 minutes to get to the airport.

author: GoBlueBoston
title: STUNNING hotel and location, but not the most pleasant
text: I want to give this hotel 5 stars so badly, because it is absolutely stunning and unlike any hotel I've ever been to before. It's situated in the middle of a rice paddy. Watching the sun rising over the paddy outside our bedroom window is an experience that I won't forget. The pool and common areas look like a spa, and we enjoyed relaxing with a glass of wine in the pool very much. HOWEVER, the open-air lobby area is surrounded by still-water pools that have no pumps or filters and have become an absolute breeding ground for bugs and mosquitos. Venturing out of your room after sunset nearly requires you to cover yourself in a net. It completely ruined the otherwise beautiful hotel for me. Also, we had lizards in our room, as did every one of our travel companions. It could be worse, but it wasn't the most pleasant feeling. If you happen to have a problem after around 10pm, do not expect to be able to speak with anyone who can help you. The English-speaking manager is off-duty fairly early and the ONLY hotel staff available is a security guard who speaks absolutely no English. The rooms are modern and pleasant but the television options are extremely limited for English-speakers, which was disappointing. The hotel is not particularly near anything but is a short tuktuk ride to a (very) small village that has a few little restaurants that hilariously compete with each other for your business. We ate at two of them during our time there and were pleased with both. And speaking of food, the restaurant at this hotel is pretty atrocious. Again, it's very nice to look at - great decor and modern design but the dinner menu is not great and the breakfast was the worst of our trip. As with many hotels in Thailand, they try to serve dishes that will appear to the many nationalities of their patrons. I laughed to see that spaghetti and tomato sauce was one of their homages to Western breakfast cuisine. There were occasionally eggs, if you could get them before they were cold. In sum, I'm glad we stayed here because it was so beautiful but it could just be so much better with a few minor changes.

author: Elle_01234
title: Beautiful hotel with major service issues
text: The hotel is very beautiful and modern with spatious rooms and well trimmed gardens. It is in the middle on nowhere so there isn't much to do at night. The restaurant offers good food for both breakfast and dinner although breakfast is almost completely asian (and even that with limited variety), westerners could have a bit of a problem (no croissant or any other pastry, just some bread and butter, no cheese). The free wi-fi is a joke since it goes on and off at will, with terrible reception in the meantime. My major problem with the hotel was the service. I stayed in a room with a connecting door to another room that didn't belong to our group. At 1am (so in the middle of the night) I heard someone knocking on my (connecting) door. I didn't pay much attention, I thought they would just stop. But they kept on knocking. After a while they started partying with very loud music and yelling. I tried calling the reception but no one answered. After three calls I woke up someone who spoke to me sleepily in Thai. Since I couldn't communicate with them I went down to the reception to have a personal word with them. I found two men sleeping in the reception couches. I woke them up and asked them to follow me to my room to end the next door party. They did, and they did ask the men next door to turn off the music (at least I think they did, because they all spoke Thai), but the party kept on going. Finally I started knocking on their door and they stopped the music around 3:30am. As I had to wake up at 5:30am I didn't get any sleep at all. Needless to say that no one apologized to me for my inconvenience. A hotel with international clientele in the middle of nowhere should have round the clock english speaking personnel that doesn't sleep while on duty and they should upgrade their overall services quality.

author: CarlaG403
title: Uninspired, unappetizing, unhelpful - but not unclean
text: Like a previous reviewer, we chose this hotel as it looked like it would be a cut above some of the other options in the area and because it was close to the historical park. We found the experience to be a real let down, although with improvements this hotel certainly could have potential. The location is about half way between "New Sukothai" (the centre of the current, modern town which is where all the restaurants and middle end hotels are) and Sukothai Historical Park. In reality, the two areas are about 15mins apart by tuk tuk. So staying at this hotel, you find yourself stranded at a fairly out of the way location which isn't significantly closer to the historical park than many other options. The restaurant is - let's face it - bad. We are huge fans of Thai food, and ate very, very well throughout our trip. The restaurant here was an exception, serving both the worst and the most expensive meal we had on our trip. The atmosphere at the restaurant is pretty grim, with a large space, wedding style round table and covered chairs, and bright lighting. The food at dinner is extremely bland Westernized Thai food. The food at breakfast is middle of the road to be charitable. If you stay here, recommend you go out to the city centre to eat. Many of the staff are eager to please, but a number seem very turned off by customer service and were not very helpful. The poor English of a lot of the staff was an issue, as well. On the plus side, the resort is very green, the design is new (although I agree with another previous reviewer who felt it all looked pretty cheap underneath), the rooms fairly clean, and the pool area nice. My impression was they had a lot of tour groups coming through, so perhaps don't need to work that hard to impress customers. Overall, I feel there must be better options in the area and probably at a better price.

author: HappyMoonChild
title: Nice and Calm Hotel
text: We stayed in this hotel in our way to the north of Thailand. There price was good and one can say that it is a good quality for money. Hotel has a beautiful open area entrance, especially at night. Hotel restaurant is good and with a modern decoration. We had made a mistake in our booking and had reserved our breakfast for only two but we were four people. Hotel was kind enough to provide all of us with the breakfast. Their breakfast is great. We were travelling with private van but it seemed like to be not easily accessible by public transportation. Room was specious and with modern decoration. Everything seemed to be new and room seemed to be renovated. We enjoyed the shower and the stylish bathroom in our room. We used the pool at the early morning and it was great. Hotel has a really nice spa but we did not have the time to use it. After checking-out we went to cite seeing at the historical park nearby in our way to the North, when we got a phone call from hotel. We were surprised to be informed that we have left a swimwear in lobby and they were kind enough to call us and we went back and pick it up. Hotel is surrounded by rice field with not fences. It is wild and beautiful scenery but a bit scary at the night. However, we noticed that guards were walking around and having watch over the hotel area around the clock. We enjoyed our stay.

author: chiangmaijim
title: Nice weekend
text: Had always wanted to visit Sukhothai. Chose this hotel for its location (we had a car) and the fact that it had a pool. Rooms very large, nice bathroom. Being low season it was pretty quiet. The first thing to say about writing a review on this hotel, is for you to IGNORE all the comments made at the time the hotel opened and be guided by latest postings. Upon arrival a member of staff ran over to the car to collect our case. We were offered a welcome drink at during checkin then taken by golf cart to our room by the pool. The pool is a good size but the water was warm. Free wifi everywhere. Breakfast was adequate and buffet-style on Sunday. Only comment on this was the fact that they failed to keep the food warm so I requested freshly made eggs as the fried eggs on offer were stone cold. Coffee was a bit stewed and sadly they didnt use the 'barista' type machines lying idle!! On non-buffet morning there was a choice of thai, asian or american style b/fast from a menu, all of which were freshly made to order. The location of the hotel means that you really need a car to get the the old city but thats true of all the hotels. All in all good value for the deal we got and I would have no hesitation recommending the hotel.

author: handyspanner
title: Did the job
text: We stayed here for one night during our tour of Thailand. The hotel is an open resort, which does not help when it is raining. The rooms are spacious with large bathrooms with separate shower. The main issue with this accommodation is the decor; it was all grey walls and grey tiles, which made the room really drab. We had a ground floor room that overlooked the pool. There was no soft curtain over the window, so everybody could see into the room. As stated in other posts the room contained a lot of insects and ants running every where. Another issue was that the drains in the bathroom were very unpleasant and we had to keep the door shut to limit the odour. As we were only there one night we did not ask to be moved. The bed was clean and provided a good sleep. There were coffee making facilities, but there were no coffee or tea provided. While we were at the resort there it did not appear that many of the rooms were occupied and the hotel appeared shut down. When we went for breakfast, for which there was not a lot of choice, there was only our table and two others laid out. Others we were travelling with had an evening meal and they were the only diners in the restaurant and the choice of food was apparently very limited. While we were here it rained most of the time and did not give the best picture for the hotel. Due to the drab decor, I would not stay here again if I was coming this way.

author: MKM2011
title: Peaceful location ...lots of bugs
text: We stayed at this resort as part of a tour of Thailand with Kuoni. It is a little off the beaten track which makes it a haven for relaxation and a great place to watch the sunset (or sunrise) over the surrounding rice fields. The resort is well laid out and staff helpful and friendly. A phrase book came in handy and our tour guide was also able to help us out with the language- so that we could practice our Thai. The manager also appears to take a personal interest in how guests found their stay. A welcome drink was well received. The rooms appeared modern, although lacked some of the finishing touches of some of the other resorts we stayed in during our trip, although from what our tour guide advised this was still one of the better resorts in the locality. The room was very hot during the night - even with the air conditioning on.The shower was great although we needed to ask for our towels to be changed as they were dirty. The staff dealt with this quickly and efficiently and brought us clean towels within minutes. There was a small area for preparation of drinks. Unfortunately, this area was infested with ants- which travelled with us to our next destination. There were also other insects and small lizards in the room which to be honest should be expected given the location. We were glad of our mosquito repellant and plug in - although even these did not stop us from getting bitten. The room looked out onto the pool area which was pleasant. It was good to have an in room safe. The resort we stayed in at our next stop had the same rating but was much better in terms of facilities and room quality. There restaurant area was pleasant and there was a good selection of foods for breakfast. Overall the resort was ok in an attractive location but could be improved by adding a few finishing touches. As a stop off as part of a tour this resort met our needs although would not recommend for a longer stay. Given the other available accommodation in the area we would potentially stay here again.

author: cherid1
title: Mostly Pros and a Few Cons
text: Our first visit to Scottsdale. Love the town! So clean and welcoming. This hotel was warm and inviting. The staff were very friendly and accommodating. We thoroughly enjoyed and took advantage of the breakfast bar and the evening reception. We used the shuttle service a few times and they were more than accommodating and helpful. The only downside to our time there was our room view. We asked for poolside room and received a room that looked out to a dental office. The pool was behind a fence to our right. I guess that could be considered poolside but in reality it is not and probably should not be advertised as such. We paid a premium price for "poolside". My husband and I are not complainers so we enjoyed what we were given as much as we could. We also had some issues with housekeeping. We tracked them down to receive fresh towels and dispose of our trash on three of our four day stay. Other than that we had a great time and would give this hotel another chance, as it has a lot going for it.

author: MarkfromtheIsland
title: Older HI Express. Good location but needs upgrading
text: Stayed here for 4 nights. We regularly stay at HI because they tend to be recently upgraded and a good experience. This one is older. The furniture in our room was badly worn and beat up. It needed replacement not repair. The linens, pillows, and towels were good - as is usual with HI. The staff were excellent - helpful and friendly. The location is very good - a 15 minute walk from Old Town. This HI has the same crappy breakfast as all the others we've stayed at (except DC which doesn't offer one). It offers something we haven't seen before, though. Happy hour with free wine, beer, and snacks in the evening. Yep - free. Granted it's cheap wine but it brought a lot of the guests out of their rooms and down to the lobby. The end result was that we met a bunch of nice people and had a lot of fun with them. They also offer a free shuttle within a certain radius which we used a few times to get back and forth to restaurants. Despite the age I think I would still recommend it - it's good value, a good location, and lots of parking.

author: NotGrlNextDoor
title: Long weekend stay and it was pleasant
text: I stayed at Holiday Inn Express Hotel and Suites Old Town for a long weekend. I had the suite which included a separate sitting area and bedroom with doors that close.
